title: docs: e2e API specification and implementation plan
body:
## Summary

Complete v0 API specification for `e2e` — the open-source, cross-platform, agentic testing framework. Spec only, no implementation: `spec/api.d.ts` is the normative contract, prose docs follow it.

> The last testing framework you will ever need.

## What's in

**Core design** ([spec/](./spec))
- **Control gradient** — three tiers, all cross-platform: `agent.act('goal')` (planning) → `agent.tap('the login button')` (AI locates, deterministic action, cached) → `screen.getByRole(…).tap()` (zero AI)
- **`screen`** — Testing Library queries (role/label/text/testId + state options) projected onto per-platform backends (ARIA on web, native accessibility on iOS/Android); a mapping layer, not an automation engine
- **Execution model** — code drives, agents are bounded: each `agent.*` call is an isolated sub-agent; continuity via the step ledger (compact handoffs, flat context cost); values move explicitly through code
- **Caching** — locate cache (instant actions → `screen`-shaped queries, committable/PR-reviewable) + path cache (act traces as guidance); agentic once, near-deterministic after
- **Resources** — `email.inbox()`, `credentials.user()` (secrets never enter model context), `webhook.capture()`, `files.from()`
- **Lifecycle** — `test.setup()` + sessions, groups/serial, `test.each`, sharding, `e2e dev` watch mode
- **Cross-platform targets** — one test runs on web/iOS/Android; `device` is the only platform-specific fixture
- **Drivers as packages** — public SPI (`e2e/driver`, `defineDriver`, `verifyDriver` conformance suite); official drivers as subpath exports (`e2e/playwright`, `e2e/agent-device`), community as `e2e-driver-*`; no backend object in the public API
- **OSS/Cloud boundary** — local-first; `runner: 'cloud'` is the only switch

**Deferred** ([spec/roadmap/](./spec/roadmap)) — PR testing, service emulation (designs preserved for later re-validation)

**Plan** ([PLAN.md](./PLAN.md)) — 6 phases: base API → caching/replay → dogfood on TesterArmy (local + GH Actions) → cloud + managed resources → iOS/Android → services

## Notes for reviewers

- Key decisions and their rationale live in [spec/01-principles.md](./spec/01-principles.md) (incl. non-goals: no backend escape hatch in v0, no homegrown automation engine)
- When prose and `api.d.ts` disagree, `api.d.ts` wins
- This is a living draft — we'll keep iterating on this branch/follow-ups

title: feat: deterministic runner, playwright driver, and web platform (Phase 1)
body:
## Summary

Implements the first part of the spec (Phase 1 of PLAN.md): the deterministic API, test runner, driver SPI with the reference Playwright driver, and the web platform. Sets the repo up as a pnpm monorepo so further packages (reference app, conformance suites) can be added.

Agentic execution, caches, HTML reporter, video artifacts, and mobile are intentionally out of scope: `agent` fixture acquisition fails with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` and mobile targets are rejected, both as specified.

## What's included

`packages/e2e` — the `e2e` package with exports `e2e`, `e2e/driver`, `e2e/playwright`, and the `e2e` CLI bin:

- **sdk-0.1** — `test`/`describe`/hooks/`test.setup` with synchronous-registration enforcement, `expect`, `credentials`, `defineConfig`; public types mirror `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`
- **runner-0.1 (deterministic)**
  - config discovery/validation, defaults table, CI mode, WHATWG base-URL normalization, origin policy, spec glob grammar, SHA-256/JCS `configDigest` (05)
  - collection with percent-encoded stable test IDs, duplicate detection, option resolution precedence, selection (tags, `.only` + CI rejection, platforms/capabilities, session producers, atomic serial closure) (11)
  - clean attempts in fresh execution realms, hook ordering, retries, flaky derivation, timeouts with bounded cleanup, serial groups sharing one driver session, AES-256-GCM per-run sessions (`session-1` envelope with JCS AAD), app process-group management, exit precedence `130 > 4 > 3 > 2 > 1 > 0` (11/06)
  - list reporter with trust notice; atomic, **schema-valid `report-1`** documents (13)
- **driver-1** — `e2e/driver` SPI: `defineDriver` branding/validation, `DriverError` with legal-retryability enforcement, `verifyDriver` stub for source compatibility
- **web-0.1 (deterministic)** — immutable locator expression AST, runner-owned polling/strictness, secure-field read denial, app/web fixtures (navigation, routes with the spec URL-pattern grammar, frames, cookies, dialogs, downloads, evaluation, keyboard/mouse), Playwright reference driver with storage-state capture/restore and screenshot/trace artifacts (08/09)
- **CLI** — `e2e run` with all spec flags and `e2e init` (commander + clack)

Notable: `tsImport` loads test modules in an isolated module graph, so cross-realm state (active collector, credential registry, locator internals, error taxonomy) lives behind `globalThis`/`Symbol.for` keys — required for the real CLI, not just tests.

## Testing

- 156 tests green (`pnpm test`):
  - 138 unit tests for the deterministic APIs: test IDs/JCS/UUIDv7, text normalization, glob grammar, URL/origin policy, route pattern grammar, config resolution/digest, registration/collection rules, selection, locator expressions, value matchers, driver SPI, error/exit-code mapping
  - 18 integration tests running fixture projects through the built runner against a live local app in real Chromium: queries, actions, polling, strictness, routes, dialogs, frames, cookies, sessions save/restore, serial groups, retries/flaky, timeouts, hook order, exit codes
  - every generated report validated against `spec/schema/report-v1.schema.json`
- `pnpm check` — spec typecheck + package typecheck clean (TS 7, strict, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`)
- CLI smoke-tested end to end: `e2e init` → `e2e run` against a live server → pass, report written
- CI workflow migrated to pnpm with SHA-pinned actions

title: test: harden test suite and pin the runner<->driver contract
body:
## Summary

Hardens the reference runner's test suite (129 -> 298 tests), pins the runner<->driver SPI contract at three layers so future changes cannot silently break it, and fixes a driver-error classification gap the new contract tests surfaced.

## Changes

### test: coverage for previously untested modules
- Unit: `internal/time` (deadlines, negation-grace polling), `run/retry` (full policy matrix), `credentials` (password plaintext never reachable), `report/list` + `report/write`, `realm-slot`, `regexp`, `package-version`, CLI arg parsing (runner mocked), `init` scaffolding idempotence
- Integration: `AppProcess` lifecycle — readiness polling, process-group teardown, SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation, spawn failure, startup timeout

### test: driver boundary contract (3 layers)
1. **Compile-time drift guard** (`tests/contract/driver-spec-drift.ts` + `check:driver-drift`): exact structural equality between `spec/api/driver.d.ts` and `src/driver/index.ts` for all 28 brand-free SPI types; wired into `typecheck` -> root `check` -> CI
2. **Runner->driver contract** (`tests/integration/driver-contract.test.ts`, no browser): instrumented in-memory `defineDriver` handle through the real runner — strict session serialization, close-always/dispose-once ordering, launch context shape, OperationContext discipline, session state roundtrip, stale-retry vs never-repeat-committed-actions, capability gates
3. **Engine<->driver unit contract** (`tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts`): retry-on-retryable semantics and the complete `DriverError` -> runner taxonomy mapping table

### fix: DriverError classification applied to every surface
`translateDriverError` was only applied on the locator path. DriverErrors from `launch`, `app.*`, `web.*`, `artifacts.*`, and state capture/restore were downgraded to category `test` — misreporting infra failures (exit 1 instead of 3) and letting them consume retry budget. The canonical spec 09-drivers.md mapping now lives in `internal/errors.ts` and `classifyError` is DriverError-aware; contract tests pin exit codes 2/3 and retry-budget protection.

### build: `.ts` import extensions
`allowImportingTsExtensions` + `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`: source imports name the on-disk files; emitted `dist/` keeps Node-ESM `.js` specifiers (verified byte-level, no bundler added).

## Verification

- `pnpm check` (spec typecheck + package typecheck + drift guard) green
- `pnpm test` — 29 files, 298 tests green
- `pnpm --filter @e2e/testbed test` — 30 dogfood tests green through the built CLI
- Drift guard verified with a negative test (detects a removed `DriverSession.close`)

title: feat: concurrent test execution across worker processes
body:
Implements the `workers` setting: execution now schedules file-target units across child worker processes per spec/11-lifecycle.md. Closes the "accepted but serial" gap documented in the READMEs.

## Design

**Scheduling (spec 11-lifecycle.md "Execution hierarchy")**
- Unit of scheduling = one file-target realm: all runnable pairs of one file for one target run on one worker, preserving realm reuse between passing non-serial tests and inline serial-group execution.
- Per target, setup units complete before ordinary units dispatch; the scheduler tracks failed sessions and emits `setup-failed` skips at dispatch time.
- Workers are bound to one target and run one unit at a time. A worker is discarded after any unit containing a failed/timed-out result, and on any infrastructure fault.

**Worker processes (spec 09-drivers.md driver concurrency contract)**
- Each worker re-loads the config module itself (configs may hold live driver instances/closures that cannot cross IPC) and verifies the resolved `configDigest` matches the runner's. This also yields exactly one driver instance per worker with strictly serialized sessions.
- Results/serial groups/run errors stream back over the IPC channel; `ResolvedTarget` never crosses the wire (results carry `targetName`, the runner rehydrates).
- Session state: the per-run AES key transfers once over IPC at worker init (never disk/env/argv); workers share the encrypted on-disk session store, so a setup produced in one worker restores in another.
- Worker crash mid-unit: the in-flight pair records a synthetic `WORKER_CRASH` failed attempt, unfinished pairs skip as `infrastructure-unavailable`, and a `WORKER_EXIT` run error is recorded (infra failures are not retry eligible). Two consecutive boot failures fail the target's remaining units.
- Interrupts broadcast over IPC (workers ignore direct SIGINT), with a `timeout + cleanupTimeout` force-kill budget.

**Fallback**: in-memory configs (programmatic `rawConfig`) cannot cross process boundaries and keep the sequential in-process path.

**Reporting**: serial groups are now sorted file → declarationIndex → target index like results, keeping report order independent of completion time (spec 13-reporting.md).

## Changes

- `src/run/units.ts` — work-unit planner (setup units, file units, immediate non-run pairs)
- `src/run/worker/{protocol,entry,handle}.ts` — IPC protocol, worker process entry, runner-side process lifecycle
- `src/run/scheduler.ts` — dispatch loop, setup gating, worker pool with target affinity, discard/crash handling
- `src/run/execute.ts` — `TargetExecutor.run` split into reusable `runSetupUnit`/`runFileUnit`; new `onSerialGroup`/`onPairStart` events
- `src/run/runner.ts` — parallel path for file-backed configs (all worker counts), fallback otherwise
- `src/run/sessions.ts` — injectable session key
- `src/report/build.ts` — deterministic serial-group ordering

## Testing

- New unit tests: work-unit planning, non-run/unstarted result shapes, wire round-trip
- New integration tests (real worker processes + browsers): distinct worker PIDs proven, cross-worker session restore, setup-failure gating across workers, atomic serial groups, worker crash recovery, interrupt → exit 130
- Full suite: 309 tests / 31 files pass; testbed 30/30 through the worker path, ~2.4x wall-clock vs `--workers 1`

Note: found a pre-existing ~10s process-exit lag (two lingering socket handles) that reproduces on the sequential path too — left out of scope, worth a separate issue.

title: feat: auto-install missing Playwright browsers on first run
body:
## Summary

Fresh installs of `e2e` had no mechanism to provision Playwright browsers: a missing executable surfaced as one `DRIVER_FAILURE` per test ("Executable doesn't exist ... please run playwright install") instead of anything actionable. This adds automatic first-run browser provisioning.

## Changes

- `src/playwright/install.ts`: `ensureBrowsersInstalled()` checks each required browser's `executablePath()` on disk and downloads missing ones by spawning the bundled `playwright install` CLI. Progress goes to stderr so JSON reports on stdout stay clean. Detection and installer are injectable for tests.
- `src/run/runner.ts`: new preflight step after driver validation, gated on the bundled `'playwright'` driver only (custom drivers manage their own binaries). Runs in the main process before any session launches, so downloads are never charged against `launchTimeout` and never race across workers. Failures classify as infrastructure errors (exit 3).
- `src/playwright/browser-pool.ts`: exports `browserType()` for reuse.
- README: notes auto-download + how to pre-provision in CI images.

No driver SPI changes (spec drift check passes).

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter e2e typecheck` (incl. `check:driver-drift`)
- `pnpm --filter e2e test` — 301 passed (incl. new unit tests for dedupe/skip/failure propagation)
- Manual fresh-machine simulation: moved `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1228*` aside, ran `pnpm test:testbed` — chromium auto-downloaded once, all 30 testbed tests passed.

title: feat: agentic located actions, judgments, and extraction (Phase 2)
body: Implements the non-planning agent tiers from `spec/02-test-api.md`: `tap`, `click`, `type`, `longPress`, `scroll`, `scrollTo`, `waitFor`, `extract`, `assert`. `agent.act` and `agent.login` still reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Both are planning invocations over the bounded `agent-tool-1` loop, so they land together in a follow-up. ## Design The runner owns everything the model does not. A model call returns one node reference or one boolean judgment against a closed grammar; it never returns a selector, coordinate, action, or error code. For a located action the runner: 1. captures one fresh atomic observation and redacts it, 2. asks the model to select exactly one node from that observation, 3. derives portable `screen` queries for that node, most portable first, 4. requires a query that resolves to exactly one node with the same role, name, and input purpose, 5. dispatches the predetermined action. Zero matches is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, several is `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, and a node absent from the current observation is a policy denial. A model that names a stale revision cannot act. ## Prerequisites landed here - **Real observations.** The Playwright driver's `observe()` was a stub with no tree. It is now an in-page semantic walker producing a single-revision tree with element-handle-backed `NodeRef`s, masked secure fields, and `href` reduced to origin and path. - **Config.** `agent` and `limits` were accepted but never resolved. Model (string, object, or `E2E_MODEL`), budgets, cache mode, and ambient context now resolve and validate; `--no-agent-cache` is wired through. - **Reporting.** Agent steps carry `metrics`, `model`, `events`, `cache`, `observationRevision`, and `explanation`; `limits` comes from resolved config and `usage` is aggregated. `web.setViewport` now reports its viewport, closing a pre-existing schema gap. ## Inference Vercel AI SDK through the AI Gateway, so switching provider is a model-string change: ```ts agent: { model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5' } ``` An adapter registry can replace the gateway for one provider, and `agent.model.endpoint` overrides the gateway base URL (HTTPS unless loopback). The credential is read at call time and never enters resolved config, the config digest, logs, or reports. ## Security Model input is the redacted semantic tree, the bounded prior-step ledger, and trusted project context. Never screenshots, raw HTML, cookies, headers, environment values, or secret values. Secret fills are authorized host-side before the value is resolved: registered handle, closed secure sink, allowed top-level origin, editable field with a compatible declared purpose. A `password` secret aimed at a `username` field is denied. Any secret fill leaves the viewport pixel-tainted for the rest of the attempt, after which `agent.assert` stops attaching screenshot evidence. Observations whose masking the driver cannot prove are discarded before reaching a model or disk. ## Not implemented - planning tier (`act`, `login`) - `cache-1`; every agent step reports `cache: bypassed` - screenshots are never sent to the model (semantic tree only) - observation covers the main frame only ## Testing 232 tests in `packages/e2e` (68 new): protocol grammars, config resolution, ledger compaction, observation redaction, query derivation, plus two integration suites that drive the real Playwright driver with a scripted model adapter and validate every report against `spec/schema/report-v1.schema.json`. New opt-in dogfood suite `packages/testbed/tests-agent` (`pnpm test:agent`), 11 tests, pinned to `google/gemini-3-flash` and overridable with `E2E_MODEL`. It is excluded from CI because it spends real model calls. Verified live, 11/11, on `google/gemini-3-flash` and `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`; grammars additionally verified on `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`. ## Cross-checked against tester-army's qa-agent Reading that implementation caught three real defects: 1. `href` query strings reached the model, violating the origin-and-path allowlist in `spec/10-determinism.md` and leaking tokens. 2. `agent.extract` guessed the output shape. The AI SDK can project a caller's zod (or converter-exposing Standard Schema) into a real provider schema, so extraction is now shape-enforced and costs one model call instead of two. Vendors without a converter fall back to text mode plus the validation-issue repair loop. 3. No post-action settle, so an observation could race a committing navigation. Its per-turn tool gating, repetition hashing, and transcript compaction were deliberately not copied: those belong to a tool loop, and in these tiers the model has no tool authority and no shared transcript. ---

title: ci: add oxlint, cover testbed in typecheck, split CI steps
body: ## What CI ran typecheck and tests but **no lint at all**, and testbed's typecheck was only passing by accident of step ordering. This fixes both. ## Lint There was no linter in the repo — no config, no script, no dependency. Adds **oxlint 1.75.0** with `correctness`/`suspicious`/`perf` as **error**, `pedantic`/`style` off. Three rules are disabled, each with rationale written into `.oxlintrc.json`: | Rule | Hits | Why off | |---|---|---| | `eslint/no-await-in-loop` | 39 | Sequential execution *is* the contract of a test runner. Parallelizing would be a correctness regression. | | `unicorn/consistent-function-scoping` | 6 | Would break `read-node.ts`, whose docblock explicitly requires helpers stay inline for Playwright serialization. | | `oxc/no-map-spread` | 1 | False positive against the conditional-spread idiom `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` forces (34 uses across 10 files). | **23 real violations fixed** across 18 files: mutating `.sort()`/`.reverse()` → `.toSorted()`/`.toReversed()`, `Array.includes` → `Set.has` on hot paths, redundant regex escapes, one dead import. ## Typecheck Root `typecheck` was `pnpm --filter e2e typecheck` — testbed was never explicitly covered. It only got checked because its own `test` script starts with `tsc --noEmit`, and that only passed because `pnpm test` had already built `e2e/dist` as a side effect. Run testbed's typecheck on a clean tree and you get 27 errors: ``` tests/smoke.e2e.ts(1,30): error TS2307: Cannot find module 'e2e' or its corresponding type declarations. tests/todos.e2e.ts(4,28): error TS7031: Binding element 'app' implicitly has an 'any' type. ``` Now: `pnpm run build && pnpm -r run typecheck`. Build ordering explicit instead of accidental. ## CI Named steps so failures are attributable in the UI: Lint → Typecheck spec → Typecheck packages → Install browsers → Tests → Testbed. Added `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress` on PRs. ## Two things worth flagging **`oxlint --fix` produced a broken edit.** It rewrote `const CATEGORIES: readonly ErrorCategory[] = [...]` to `new Set([...])` but left the array type annotation — a type error. Corrected to `ReadonlySet`. Worth knowing before anyone runs `lint:fix` unreviewed. **`pnpm -r run lint` exits 0 when no package defines a `lint` script.** The obvious wiring would have been a permanently-green no-op. That's why `lint` is a root-level `oxlint` call, not recursive. ## Verification Full CI sequence run locally, all green: - `pnpm lint` — clean - `pnpm check:spec` — clean - `pnpm typecheck` — clean, including cold after `rm -rf packages/e2e/dist` - `pnpm test` — 301 passed / 30 files - `pnpm --filter @e2e/testbed test` — 30 passed Both new guards verified to actually **fail** on injected violations (a stray `.sort()` and a deliberate type error), not just pass vacuously. ## Still open, not in this PR - `test:public` (real websites, `packages/testbed/tests-public`) still never runs in CI. Suggest a `schedule:` cron so it can't rot silently. - Whether this workflow is a *required* check before merge is unverifiable via API — `gh api .../branches/main/protection` returns 403 on a private repo without Pro. Needs a manual check of repo settings. ---

title: fullyParallel: schedule ordinary tests as individual work units
body:
## Problem

The scheduler's unit of parallelism is a **file-target pair**, not a test (spec 11-lifecycle.md; `run/units.ts` `buildWorkPlans`). A worker is bound to one target and executes one file unit at a time, running that file's tests sequentially.

Consequence: `e2e run --workers 11` against a suite of 10 tests spread over 3 files never runs more than 3 tests concurrently. For agentic suites this hurts badly — each test spends most of its wall time waiting on model calls, so per-test fan-out would give near-linear speedups.

## Proposal

Add a `fullyParallel` config option (Playwright-equivalent semantics), default `false`:

- `fullyParallel: true` makes `buildWorkPlans` emit one work unit per ordinary test instead of one per file
- serial groups stay atomic: one ordered unit with shared session and ledger, as today
- setup units keep gating ordinary units per target
- workers still re-import the file per unit (already the mechanism for child-process units), so module-level side effects run once per unit — this is the same trade-off Playwright makes and should be called out in the spec

## Touch points

- `spec/03-config.md` (or wherever config options live): `fullyParallel` semantics + side-effect caveat
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md`: unit definition becomes "file, or single test when fullyParallel"
- `packages/e2e/src/config/*`: resolve + digest the new option
- `packages/e2e/src/run/units.ts`: splitting strategy in `buildWorkPlans`
- report/provenance: none expected (units are not report entities)

## Notes

- Per-test units multiply worker boot + file re-import overhead; only worth it when test bodies dominate (agentic tests do)
- Consider a per-file override (`test.describe.configure`-style) later; config-level flag first

title: Visual tier: pixel-based assertions (assertVisual) and visual pointing/clicking
body:
## Motivation

The agent tier is currently semantic-only: observations are a runner-computed accessibility-style tree (`playwright/read-node.ts`), and `agent.assert` judges its text serialization — screenshots are report evidence, never model input. Locate never lets the model supply a selector, coordinate, or action (spec 10-determinism.md).

That breaks down on:
- apps with poor/no a11y semantics (canvas, WebGL, custom widgets, legacy DOM soup)
- visual properties no tree encodes ("the button is red", overlap, layout breakage)
- flaky flows where DOM timing lies but pixels don't

This is proven ground: tester-army (the precursor to this project) leaned on visual grounding heavily for exactly these cases.

## Shared foundation: pixel observations

Both features need the same substrate:

1. **Multimodal model calls.** Extend `ModelCall` / the gateway adapter (`agent/model/gateway.ts`) to carry image content parts alongside the prompt (AI SDK supports this today). Record image bytes in step metrics; images count toward per-call token/cost budgets.
2. **Pixel-taint policy (the crux).** Today any secret fill sets `taint` and pixel evidence is withheld for the rest of the attempt, because rectangle masking cannot *prove* redaction (see `captureEvidence`, spec 14-security.md). Sending screenshots **to the model** needs an explicit spec decision:
   - default: visual calls are denied once tainted (`POLICY_DENIED`, code `PIXEL_TAINTED`)
   - optional escape hatch: `agent.visual.allowTaintedPixels: true` config with best-effort masking of known secure-node rects, recorded in report provenance as a weakened guarantee
3. **Redaction before send.** Secure-node rects (already computed per observation) are masked in the screenshot before it leaves the runner. Screenshot resolution/scale capped and recorded (`observationRevision` pairing so pixels and tree refer to the same moment).

## Feature 1: `agent.assertVisual(assertion, options?)`

Smallest slice — no new response grammar:
- capture screenshot (masked), attach to an `agent-judgment-1` call together with the assertion; same closed judgment schema, explanation required
- runner maps `result: false` to `ASSERTION_FAILED` with the model explanation (same as `assert`)
- requires a multimodal model; non-multimodal providers fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` at config time if possible, else `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`
- report step records that pixel evidence was model input (new step field), not just an artifact

## Feature 2: visual pointing/clicking

Bigger change — inverts a core invariant, so it must be its own spec'd tier:
- new closed grammar `agent-point-1`: `{ protocolVersion, point: { x, y } | null, explanation }` (or a box); null = explicit no-match, mirroring the locate no-match semantics
- runner validation before dispatch: point within viewport, observation revision fresh, hit-test what's under the point and record the hit node (role/name if any) in the step for auditability; the model still never names an action — the API call predetermines it
- API surface: per-call grounding option (`agent.tap(target, { grounding: 'visual' })`) rather than new methods; optional `grounding: 'auto'` = semantic first, pixel fallback when the tree yields nothing (the tester-army pattern for low-a11y apps)
- determinism/caching: points do not cache like semantic locators; cache tier stores the hit-tested semantic node when one exists, else bypasses; `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED` semantics need wording
- budgets: visual calls are expensive (image tokens); default `maxModelCalls` unchanged, images count toward `maxModelTokensPerCall`

## Security summary (spec 14-security.md additions)

- model never selects error codes or actions; points are data validated by the runner
- pixels are untrusted evidence like tree text; prompt-injection surface grows (text rendered in the page is now readable by the model even when not in the tree) — policy wording must cover screenshot-borne instructions
- taint rules above; masked regions counted in `redaction.maskedRegionCount` (field already exists)

## Touch points

- spec: 02-test-api.md (methods/options), 10-determinism.md (visual tier + caching), 14-security.md (pixel policy), new `schema/agent-point-v1.schema.json`, report-v1 (step field for model-input evidence)
- runner: `agent/model/adapter.ts` + `gateway.ts` (image parts), `agent/invocation.ts` (visual observe path), `agent/index.ts` (assertVisual, grounding option), `playwright/session.ts` (masked screenshot capture), config resolve for the taint escape hatch
- testbed: a no-a11y playground page (canvas buttons) to dogfood both features

## Sequencing

1. pixel observation substrate + `assertVisual` (contained, no new grammar)
2. `agent-point-1` + grounding option + auto fallback

title: docs: add documentation site
body: ## Summary There is no user-facing documentation. This adds a Fern docs site under `fern/`, targeting `e2e.docs.buildwithfern.com`, written for the release rather than for the repo. Nineteen pages, two tabs: | Tab | Pages | |---|---| | Documentation | Introduction, Quickstart, Writing tests, Agents, Authentication, Web capabilities, Running tests, Configuration, Continuous integration, Coming from Playwright, Troubleshooting | | Reference | `test`, `expect`, `screen`/`Locator`, `app`/`web`, `agent`, `defineConfig`, CLI, Errors | ## Positioning The docs lead with the actual premise: a cross-platform agentic test runner where you turn a dial per step. The hero example is three lines at three levels of model authority, and the introduction then covers, in order: turning the dial, built-in caching, cross-platform by design, and what the runner owns. The workflow that framing enables is stated explicitly: draft with `agent.act`, pin the steps that matter to `agent.tap`, pin the assertions you care about to `expect`. At any point a reader can tell which steps still depend on a model. ## Documented as designed, gaps labelled Features are documented as they are meant to work, each followed by a `Not implemented yet` callout where the runner does not back them yet: - planned flows (`agent.act`, `agent.login`) — reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` - caching — `agent.cache`, the per-call `cache` option, and `--no-agent-cache` have no effect; steps report `cache: bypassed` - the HTML reporter — `html` is in the default `reporters` but nothing is written; reporter selection only takes effect via `--reporter` - video artifacts — `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT` before any browser launches - native targets and the `device` fixture — rejected rather than approximated No specification vocabulary appears anywhere: no `spec/`, no profile names, no conformance language, no `specVersion`. The docs describe behaviour as how e2e works. ## Accuracy Every signature is copied from `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`. Every default and range was read out of `config/resolve.ts` and `config/agent.ts` rather than assumed, which corrected a few things along the way: `APP_URL` is read by the runner (not only by the scaffolded config), `E2E_USER__USERNAME`/`_PASSWORD` exist, `--retries` and `--workers` bypass the config range checks, and `limits.maxObservationBytes` is not a `limits` key. Per-method agent budgets came from `agent/index.ts`, flags from `cli/index.ts`, error codes from `agent/error.ts` and `internal/errors.ts`. Examples are adapted from `packages/testbed`, so they are code that actually runs. ## Tooling - `pnpm docs:dev`, `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm docs:publish` - `docs:check` added to `pnpm check` - `fern-api@5.80.4` as a root devDependency, so CI and contributors use one version - `.github/workflows/docs.yml` runs `fern check` when `fern/**` changes, SHA-pinned like `spec.yml` - README gains a Documentation section and its stale "agentic execution is not implemented" paragraph now matches reality ## Verification - `fern check` — 0 errors; the only warning is the offline redirects check - `fern docs dev` — all 19 pages return 200, and each page's title plus its last section heading appear in the rendered HTML, which is what catches MDX compile failures - 0 broken internal links (every `/…` href diffed against the slug set), 0 orphan page files - 0 em dashes, and `accent-primary` is black on white / white on near-black at 21:1, so Fern raises no contrast warning - `pnpm lint` clean Note that Fern concatenates tab and section slugs by default, which produced URLs like `/documentation/writing-tests/tests/locators`. `skip-slug` on every tab and section pins them to the intended `/writing-tests` shape. ## Worth a second opinion - The hero example calls `agent.act`, which rejects today. It is the clearest statement of the premise and the caveat sits immediately below it, but if you would rather the hero be runnable, swapping that line for `agent.tap` is a one-line change. - Caching is described in the present tense as a capability with one callout. If the release ships before caching lands, we may want it less prominent in the introduction. - `e2e.docs.buildwithfern.com` must be claimable by the `testerarmy` org in the Fern dashboard. If the subdomain is taken, the fallback is one line in `fern/docs.yml`. ---

title: feat: harden the agent for production pages and add a wakacje.pl suite
body: ## Summary Dogfooding the agent against a real production travel site (wakacje.pl: heavy pages, ad iframes, consent walls, composite offer cards) surfaced a set of runner bugs and gaps. This PR fixes them, adds live debug tooling for iterating on agentic tests, and lands the opt-in suite that found everything. ## Runner fixes **Observation capture** (`playwright/session.ts`) - Frames outside `allowedOrigins` never enter observations: third-party ads/trackers are neither trusted UI nor the agent's to act on, so they stay boundary nodes and never reach the model. - Frame capture is time-bounded (3s per child document, 15s main). A stalled ad iframe used to hang `evaluateHandle` until the context-default timeout — exactly 30s per observe on the results page. Measured: **observe 30.4s → 0.4s**, whole test 86s → ~60s. **Locate on composite cards** (`agent/locate.ts`) - Observed names/texts past the driver's observation bound are matched as substrings and compared as prefixes, plus a whitespace/case-insensitive role-scoped prefix regex candidate. Offer-card links whose Playwright accessible name (includes image alts) never matches rendered text now locate reliably; for complete values the relaxed match still holds. - Locate failures now list every derived candidate query and why it was rejected (`no matches` / `N matches` / `resolved a different node`), so failures explain themselves. - Locate prompt pins the node id format; models returning bare-number ids get a precise repair message. **Timeout defaults** (`agent/index.ts`, spec 02) - `waitFor`/`scrollTo`/`extract`/`assert` defaults derive from config `actionTimeout` (30s floor) instead of hardcoded 30s constants. Model-latency headroom becomes one config knob; tests no longer need per-call timeout overrides. **Observation format** (`agent/observation.ts`, `playwright/read-node.ts`) - Role-less text holders drop the `generic` filler token, indentation is capped, hrefs bounded at 80 chars. ## Debug tooling - `E2E_DEBUG=agent` streams invocation phases, model selections, and per-candidate locate outcomes to stderr live. - `E2E_DEBUG=observations` dumps every observation exactly as the model sees it. Both were essential for diagnosing the issues above and are aimed at humans *and* agents iterating on agentic tests. ## New opt-in suite `pnpm --filter @e2e/testbed test:wakacje` drives a real booking funnel — consent dialog, destination autosuggest, offer listing, offer page — and stops at the booking entry point; nothing is ever reserved. ~60s / ~$0.23 per run on gemini-3.6-flash (measured comparison with gemini-3-flash documented in the config). Not in CI: live site, real model spend. ## Testing - `pnpm run check` (lint, spec typecheck, driver-drift) clean - 411 unit + integration tests pass - wakacje suite passing repeatedly end-to-end (headless and headed), including through the child-process worker transport ---

title: feat: vision tier for pixel evidence and visual pointing
body: Implements the vision tier from #9: pixel evidence as model input, and visual pointing for surfaces the semantic tree cannot describe. ```ts agent.assert('the chart trends upward', { vision: true }); agent.tap('the red pin on the map', { vision: true }); ``` Per the API decision in #9, there is no `assertVisual` and no `grounding` enum: `vision` is one boolean option shared by every model-backed method, defaulting to `agent.vision`, with a per-call value always winning. ## Design `vision` is **additive**. The masked screenshot joins the semantic tree; it never replaces it. Pixels-only is deliberately not offered: the tree is byte-budgeted and cheap, and its node references are what keep an action auditable. A vision `tap` on a real control still resolves to a node and re-resolves through a derived locator exactly as before. Pixel evidence **degrades rather than failing** a call. It is withheld, and the tree sent alone, when the viewport is pixel-tainted, when masking cannot be proven, or when the driver cannot capture pixels. The step records which. ### Pixels and the tree describe one moment `observe(operation, { pixels })` captures the screenshot *inside* the observation, so image and tree share one revision. Secure fields are masked before the bytes leave the backend, and `redaction.maskedRegionCount` is now real rather than hardcoded `0`. Clearance is checkable: every observed secure node must be covered by a masked region. An image reporting fewer masked regions than observed secure nodes is discarded like any incompletely redacted artifact (`MASKING_UNPROVEN`). ### The runner owns the coordinate Under vision, and only under it, the locate grammar accepts `target: { point: { x, y }, revision }`. A point answered to a tree-only call is invalid output, not an accepted coordinate, because pointing lives in a separate closed grammar. For a point the runner: 1. bounds it in the space the model was shown — the image, not the CSS viewport, 2. converts to CSS pixels, rounds, and clamps, exactly once, 3. hit-tests it against the same observation's node rects, 4. records the innermost node found there, or that there was none, 5. dispatches the predetermined action at the point. Out of bounds is invalid output worth one repair round, never a clamp: a normalized or percentage answer means the coordinate space was misread, and clamping would silently act on a corner. Hit-testing uses the observation's own rects, so there is no second driver round-trip and the answer is a node the model could equally have named. Dispatch is at the point, **not** at the hit node's center — retargeting would leave the pixels the model chose, which on a canvas is the whole surface. `hit` is the audit record, and per #9 it is also the natural cache payload when `cache-1` lands. Only `tap` and `click` accept a point. Every other method needs a node reference to hand the driver, so a point there is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` carrying the model's explanation. ### agent.visionModel Visual grounding is a materially higher bar than accepting an image, so the tier that needs it is pinnable on its own: ```ts agent: { model: 'google/gemini-3-flash', visionModel: 'openai/gpt-5.4', } ``` Overridable with `E2E_VISION_MODEL`; unset, vision calls use `agent.model`. Built on first vision call, so pinning a model whose credential is absent cannot fail a run that never asks for pixels. An invocation keeps one model for its whole lifetime, including rounds whose pixels were withheld, so one step reports one provenance and `waitFor` never switches models between rounds. ## driver-1 Additive, `spec/api/driver.d.ts` moved in lockstep with the drift guard: - `ObserveOptions { pixels? }` and `observe(operation, options?)` - `Observation.pixels`: bytes, media type, dimensions, and scale - optional `actions.tapPoint(point, operation)` — a driver without coordinate input simply cannot serve pointing `ObservationPixels.width/height` MUST be the true dimensions of the bytes, and `scale` relates them to the CSS pixels of `SemanticNode.rect`. The Playwright driver measures both from the PNG header instead of trusting `viewportSize()`. ## Security `spec/14-security.md` gains a pixel-evidence section. Pixels reach a model only when a test asks for them. Taint still wins: after any secret fill the viewport stays pixel-tainted and vision silently continues tree-only, recorded on the step as a weakened guarantee rather than a silent one. Pixels widen the prompt-injection surface, since text rendered in the page is now readable even when no node exposes it. Policy bumps to `policy-0.2`, which frames an attached image as data whose contents carry no authority. The model still never selects an action or an error code, and a coordinate is data the runner validates, converts, hit-tests, and records before dispatch. Image bytes count toward per-call token accounting via a patch-count bound rather than byte length: a blank screenshot is small and a photograph is not, while both cost the same number of patches. ## Reporting `report-v1` steps gain `visionInput`, `visionDegraded` (`PIXEL_TAINTED | MASKING_UNPROVEN | UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`), and `metrics.pixelBytes`. A pointed action records where it went: ``` the model pointed at (391, 253) for "the red pin on the map"; the runner hit-tested no semantic node there. The model explained: The red pin is the red circular marker in the map area. ``` ## Not implemented - `cache-1` vision semantics. Model identity is not part of the cache key and every step still reports `cache: bypassed`, so nothing diverges today; the point-vs-node keying from #9 lands with the cache itself. - Pre-run model disclosure remains unimplemented, as before this PR. The spec wording now requires a separately pinned `visionModel` to be disclosed too. - No config-time detection of a non-multimodal model: it surfaces as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. ## Testing 445 tests in `packages/e2e`, 5 files touched and 2 added. New coverage: the point grammar under both variants, hit-testing, PNG dimension reads, image token bounds, pixel clearance and withholding, pixel prompt framing, and `visionModel`/`E2E_VISION_MODEL` resolution. Integration coverage drives the real Playwright driver against a canvas fixture with no accessibility semantics and asserts, end to end: one image attached per call, masking counted, taint degradation keeping the tree, a pointed tap reaching the drawn target, out-of-bounds rejection without dispatch, a point refused for `type`, a point refused without vision, and vision calls routed to the pinned vision model while others stay on the main one. Testbed dogfood adds `/canvas` and `tests-agent/vision.e2e.ts`: 4/4 live, no env vars, `visionModel` pinned in config. Verified the audit trail records `(391, 253)` for a pin sitting at viewport `(392, 253)`. ## Rebased onto #11, and dogfooded on wakacje.pl Rebased on top of `feat: harden the agent for production pages`. Both branches rewrote `observeAndSelect` and `resolveSelected`, so the conflicts were resolved on intent rather than textually: - vision's point branch traces through #11's `agentTrace`, and the observation trace now reports pixel size, mask count, or the reason pixels were withheld; - `LOCATE_VISION_REQUEST` picked up #11's node-id wording (`exactly as printed after "#"`), which production pages taught the tree-only variant; - the masked screenshot is bounded by its own `PIXEL_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`, following #11's rule that a heavy page costs an observation a moment rather than the whole step. The tree is already captured by then, so a slow frame degrades vision to tree-only instead of failing the step. The wakacje.pl suite from #11 then became the real test. `agent.visionModel` is pinned there, and vision is on for exactly the two steps where pixels decide: **`waitFor("... visible and not covered")`** asks for something no accessibility tree encodes. A consent sheet or sticky promo overlaying the form leaves it present and named in the tree while hiding it on screen. **The offer-card tap**, which fails on `main` today: ``` no derived query uniquely resolved the selected node (role=link name="Lato 2026 Grecja / Zakynthos / Tragaki Caretta Paradise 06.10.2026- 13.10.2026 (8 dni / 7 nocy) Poznań, Katowice, Wrocław (+6) All Inclusive Grecos 8.3 Bardzo dobry 428 opinii od 5 680 zł za wszystkich SPRAWDŹ CENĘ") ``` One link's accessible name aggregates the entire card, so nothing re-finds it. Worth being precise about how vision fixed this, because it is not what I expected: the step now records `locate.identity allowed` and no point. Seeing the card, the model picks the small inner control it would actually click, and the runner still re-resolves that node through a derived query. **Vision improved the choice rather than bypassing it** — which is the argument for the tier being additive, and it leaves the result deterministic and cacheable. Pointing remains the fallback underneath, for when no node is re-findable at all. Full funnel green, 79 s, with routing confirmed in the report: the two visual steps on `openai/gpt-5.4`, the other ten on `google/gemini-3.6-flash`. ## Cross-checked against tester-army's qa-tools `vision_click` and the scene tools are the precursor to this, and reading them caught three things I had wrong: 1. **Screenshot dimensions must be measured, not assumed.** I was reporting `page.viewportSize()` alongside bytes captured separately. `getImageDimensions` exists in qa-tools for a reason: those dimensions are the space every returned coordinate refers to. Now read from the PNG header, with `scale` derived from it, which also makes a device-scale capture — the normal mobile case — correct for free via the same ratio their mobile path applies. 2. **The coordinate-space prompt is most of the feature.** Exact `[0, w-1]` and `[0, h-1]` bounds, plus explicitly ruling out normalized, relative, percentage, and logical-point coordinates. The CSS-pixel equivalence sentence is emitted only when the capture really is CSS-scale. 3. **Targeting rules.** Center of the control's hit area rather than nearby text, icon, card, or container; stay off borders and edges; only the top layer when a modal is open; a position given in the instruction outranks a better text match elsewhere; abstain instead of guessing. Deliberately not copied: the structured abstain enum (`foreground_layer` and friends). It earns its place in a planning loop that can act on recovery guidance; here a decline is a test failure and the explanation prose already carries the reason to the human. Clamping was also not copied — see above. The grounding-quality finding transferred directly. `google/gemini-3-flash` judges the drawn chart correctly and still points ~1.6x off in y; the same code and prompt score 4/4 on `openai/gpt-5.4`, the model qa-tools pins. That is what `agent.visionModel` is for, and the recorded point plus hit-test is how a bad grounding is told apart from a runner bug. ## Drive-by `spec/schema/fixtures/agent-locate-v1.valid.json` was missing the `explanation` its own schema requires — no test validates the spec fixtures. Fixed while extending that grammar, and point fixtures added alongside. Closes #9 ---

title: feat: locate cache (cache-1)
body: ## Summary Every agentic step currently pays a model call to resolve a target the runner has already resolved before. This lands the `cache-1` **locate** cache: a located action stores the portable semantic locator it landed on, and a later run resolves that locator directly for **zero model calls**. ```ts await agent.tap('the Pro plan card'); // cold: one model call, then getByRole('button', { name: 'Pro' }) // warm: cache hit, same query, no model call ``` Scope is the `locate` entry kind only. Path guidance (`agent.act`) ships with the planning tier, which has no producer today — `agent.act` still throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, so there is nothing to record. The store, key builder, and validator are kind-agnostic so `kind: "path"` drops in without a rewrite. ## The cache is never authority This is the property everything else is built around, and it is what the tests actually assert: - a hit still goes through **normal actionability and origin policy** — a cached locator cannot skip a check; - a stale, poisoned, oversized, foreign-key, or digest-mismatched entry is ignored, reported, and replaced by **one fresh locate**, so it self-heals; - a cache write failure never fails a passing test; - deleting `.e2e/cache/` cannot change what a correct test means. Worst case for a bad entry is one wasted resolve. Cached locators resolve with a **zero-poll deadline** so a stale entry cannot burn the caller's timeout — otherwise a warm cache would be slower than no cache. ## Identity `buildCacheKey` covers every field in spec 10-determinism.md, digested with RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256 (`internal/ids.ts` already had both): spec/schema versions, project, test, target, platform, driver id/version/SPI, method, call index, instruction, parameters, app identity, starting screen fingerprint, agent-policy version. - **Secrets never enter a key.** `agent.type` with a `Secret` contributes only its stable name and purpose, never its value — not even through a digest. - **Instruction normalization** is CRLF/CR to LF, NFC, outer-trim only; interior whitespace is preserved because it can be meaningful. - **Call index** is assigned for *every* agent call, cacheable or not, so inserting a non-cacheable call between two cached ones does not silently reindex their keys. - **Screen fingerprint** hashes the semantic tree minus node refs, geometry, secure values, and focus, plus URL origin/path/query and the exact viewport. A registered secret in a query becomes its stable name before hashing. `cacheKeyHash` reproduces the canonical `spec/schema/fixtures/cache-v1.valid.json` digest exactly, which independently confirms the JCS implementation. ## Security posture A committed cache is untrusted repository input, so `cache-1` is a closed union of semantic shapes with no free-form strings anywhere: - **no CSS/XPath selectors.** This is the security boundary, not a style rule. A semantic query can only address something a user could perceive; a raw selector could reach nodes the observation deliberately withholds (secure fields, hidden nodes, out-of-policy frames). Storing one of any syntax reopens that hole. - entry parsing is **closed**: unknown core fields, wrong types, and out-of-schema shapes are rejected rather than coerced (hand-written validator — Ajv stays a dev dependency); - the key hash is **recomputed** and compared against both the content and the file name, so an entry moved to another key's file cannot answer for it; - size is checked **before** read, capped at resolved `maxCacheBytes` and never above the 1 MiB wire ceiling; - the key hash is the only caller-supplied path component and must be a bare digest, so traversal is impossible by construction; - cached regexps are capped at 1,024 UTF-8 bytes with `u`/`v` exclusion and canonical flag order enforced on read. ## Consequences worth reviewing **iframe locates are `bypassed`.** Our frame chain is addressed by CSS selector (`agent/locate.ts` `scopeToFrames`), which `cache-1` has no node for and forbids storing. Payment/OAuth embeds therefore stay uncached. The iframe boundary node *does* already carry `role: 'iframe'` plus its title, so a semantic frame chain is a genuinely good follow-up — but it amends a frozen schema and deserves its own RFC with conformance vectors rather than being smuggled in here. **Verbs outside the `cache-1` method enum are `bypassed`** (`press`, `select`, `hover`, `check`, `uncheck`, `upload`, `dragTo`). `scroll` without `within` makes no model call, so there is nothing to cache. **No pruning.** Entries never expire, so a long-lived cache accumulates dead keys from deleted tests and changed screens. A filtered run cannot sweep untouched entries without deleting valid ones. Left out deliberately; documented; revisit during dogfood. ## Storage One file per key under `.e2e/cache/`, so merging two caches is a union of files — no shared index, no git conflicts. `e2e init` already left the directory out of `.gitignore`, so entries are committable as intended. Writes take an exclusive per-key lock (`wx` creation, with stale-lock stealing so a killed process cannot wedge a key), read the generation under it, and atomically rename a fsynced temporary file. Abandoned temporaries are swept. `CacheStore` is an interface with `FileCacheStore` as the only v0 implementation; entries are content-addressed and self-validating, so a TesterArmy remote store needs no additional trust and touches one file. ## Bugs found while testing - `cache: 'off'` reported `miss` with a real key hash and computed a fingerprint for nothing. Mode `off` is now a true bypass. - `explainActionFailure` said "the model selected …" on a cache hit, sending the reader to the wrong place. `LocatedNode` now records its origin. ## Docs `README` mandates docs land with behavior, so this removes the four "Not implemented yet" cache callouts and adds: - **CI**: `actions/cache` wiring for `.e2e/cache`, per-matrix-leg keys with `restore-keys` fallback, and the trusted/untrusted split (CI defaults to `read-only`, so a job that should contribute entries must opt in; a fork must never publish to a trusted store). - **The two settings that decide whether a cache travels at all**: `projectId` (falls back to a hash of the absolute project path) and the app base URL (contributes origin and path). Get either wrong and the cache is silently, permanently cold — this is the most likely reason someone reports "caching doesn't work". Cache mode intentionally gets **no new environment variable**: the recognized set is closed in spec 05-config.md, so the docs read `process.env` in `e2e.config.ts` instead. ## Testing `pnpm run check` clean. **517 tests pass** (411 before, 106 new). Unit — `cache-identity`, `cache-fingerprint`, `cache-locator`, `cache-entry`, `cache-store`: - key digest matches the canonical spec fixture; changes for all 13 identity fields; stable across property order - fingerprint ignores refs/geometry/focus/whitespace, reacts to role/name/text/states/structure/viewport/URL, and cannot be influenced by a secure field's value - selector and frame locators refused at any nesting depth; regexp caps measured in UTF-8 bytes - hostile entries: unknown fields, `__proto__` via `JSON.parse`, 2,000-deep nesting, bad digests, `path` entries, non-canonical flags - store: generation increments monotonically under 8 concurrent writers with no torn file and no leftover lock; traversal attempts, oversized files, directories-in-place, and foreign-key entries all fail closed Integration (`agent-cache.test.ts`, real Playwright, scripted model so "zero model calls" is countable, same project directory across runs): - all six cacheable verbs write distinct keys, then replay with **0** model calls — including `scrollTo` and `scroll` with `within` - a hit still performs the real action (the suite asserts the counter reached 1) - poisoned entry falls back to the model, is replaced, and surfaces a denied `cache.entry` policy event - a locator that no longer resolves misses and self-heals - `off` never writes or hits; `read-only` replays but never writes; per-call `cache: false` is honored - retry attempts bypass the cache - viewport change alone produces a miss, proving the fingerprint is part of the identity, and both entries coexist Not covered: the spec's interruptible-worker regexp evaluation (10-determinism.md:135-137). Cached patterns are validated and byte-capped on read, but evaluation still runs inline. Worth a follow-up. ---

title: Viewport-scoped observations + observation stats in reports and model input
Engineer the agent overlay and legible recordings
body:
## Problem

Our recordings are unreadable.

`web-0.1` requires video (spec 09-drivers.md) and the Playwright driver records it, but the resulting file shows a page mutating with no visible cause. The OS cursor is not in the compositor, so it never lands in the video. There is no indication of what was targeted, what the agent intended, or that an agent was driving at all.

That hurts in three places:

- **Debugging a CI failure.** A 40-second video of a form filling itself, then failing, tells you almost nothing that the report doesn't already say better.
- **Reviewing agentic steps.** `agent.act('complete payment with the test card')` expands into a plan we currently only see as report events. The video is the one artifact that could show the plan as it happened.
- **Trusting the tool.** "Code drives, agents are bounded" is our central claim (RFC). A recording where the agent's decisions are legible is the most direct evidence of it.

## Proposal

Ship an injected in-page overlay that renders the runner's intent as DOM, so it composites into the video.

Everything visible must be DOM. The real cursor cannot be captured, so we draw one.

### Layers

- **Cursor.** An SVG pointer at the resolved target's rect center. Animate with CSS transitions only — no rAF loop, no JS interpolation. Distinct easing per axis produces an arc rather than a straight slide, which reads as intentional movement rather than a teleport. Caller waits out the transition before dispatching the action, so the recording shows travel-then-act.
- **Caption.** A pill beside the cursor naming what is happening. This is where we have a real advantage: our locators are an immutable AST owned by the runner, and every action goes through it, so the caption can be the **actual semantic query or agent intent string** — not a guess reconstructed from user code. `agent.tap('the Pro plan card')` captions itself.
- **Click feedback.** Cursor squash plus an expanding, fading ring on dispatch. Without it, clicks are invisible in a recording — the single highest-value element and the easiest to omit.
- **Target highlight.** A border over the resolved element, re-polled on a fixed interval so it tracks reflow and animation rather than drifting.
- **Ambient frame.** A static inset border marking the viewport as agent-driven. Keep it static — a perpetual animation costs compositor work on every frame of every test for no benefit in a recording you scrub through.

### Recording integration

- **Overlay presence follows the video artifact, not headed mode.** If `artifacts` includes `video`, mount it. Headed is irrelevant. Gating on headed is the obvious mistake here and it produces exactly the wrong outcome: pretty local demos and useless CI recordings, when CI is where nobody was watching.
- **Cursor position persists across navigation** as viewport-relative coordinates, so it does not teleport to a corner on every page load. Recordings read as one continuous session.
- Overlay is torn down before the session closes, so trailing frames are clean.

### Hide policy is a design constraint, not a detail

The overlay must be absent from screenshots and from `observe()`, but **present** in video. Those are different lifetimes: video is continuous, captures are instantaneous.

A single hide toggle around capture means every screenshot blinks the whole overlay out for one or more video frames. So the layers need to be split by policy:

- capture-contaminating (cursor, caption, highlight) — hidden during capture
- recording chrome (ambient frame) — never in captures by construction, not by toggling

Full requirements are in #16, which must land with this.

### Security

Captions and highlights are model- and human-visible surfaces inside a recorded artifact, so they are in scope for spec 14-security.md:

- A caption MUST NEVER render secret plaintext. Credentials are opaque handles; a caption narrating a `fill` renders the **secret name**, never the resolved value. Otherwise we write secrets into a video we ship to CI.
- Secure-field pixel masking must compose with the overlay: an overlay element must not cover a masked region in a way that defeats it, and must not itself reveal masked content.
- Caption text derives from trusted test code and runner-owned locator ASTs. Model-authored strings reaching a caption are untrusted data and need the same sanitization as any other model output before rendering.

## Touch points

- `spec/09-drivers.md`: overlay/annotation as an artifact concern; hide-policy guarantee around capture
- `spec/14-security.md`: caption secret policy, masking composition
- `spec/05-config.md`: enable/disable, tie to the `video` artifact
- `packages/e2e/src/playwright/*`: mount, teardown, cursor updates driven from the action path
- `packages/e2e/src/locator/*`: surface the resolved query text for captions
- new: injected runtime bundle + its build step (see #16)
- conformance vectors land with the behavior, per PLAN.md

## Notes

- Build a **standalone harness page** that loads the built runtime and fakes agent scenarios. The overlay is otherwise only reachable by running a full test, which makes iterating on animation timing miserable. The harness doubles as the executable spec for the runtime API.
- Codegen the typed bridge across the page boundary: scrape exported names from the runtime entry at build time, generate an interface, and confine every cast to one small module. Otherwise every `page.evaluate` call is untyped by construction.
- Caption changes during typing need special handling: naive per-keystroke updates make any enter/exit animation strobe. Detect near-identical successive captions and swap text in place without animating.
- Deliberately out of scope for a first cut: numbered action trails, scroll-into-view of off-screen targets (mutates the page under test), context-aware cursor shapes.

title: Overlay isolation and hardening requirements (must not perturb the page under test)
body:
## Problem

The overlay in #15 injects our DOM, CSS, fonts, and JS into the page under test. That page is arbitrary, hostile, and the thing we are measuring.

Every requirement below is a specific bug class. Each one is cheap to satisfy up front and expensive to diagnose later, because the symptom is always "the tool is wrong about the app" rather than "the overlay is broken." An observability tool that perturbs what it observes is worse than no tool.

Treating these as a normative checklist rather than implementation notes, because several are conformance-visible: they affect `observe()`, screenshots, and reported performance metrics.

## Requirements

### 1. Style isolation both directions — shadow DOM + `all: initial`

Mount into a shadow root. On the host, reset inherited page styles (`all: initial`), then re-establish only what we need: fixed positioning, full inset, `pointer-events: none`, max `z-index`, `contain: layout`, and an explicit compositing layer.

- Without the reset, page CSS inherits into our overlay and it renders wrong on sites with aggressive global styles.
- Without shadow DOM, our CSS leaks into the page and we have changed the thing we are testing.
- Without `pointer-events: none`, the overlay intercepts a dispatched click and the action silently targets the wrong element. This is the worst failure mode in the list — it produces a *passing* test that did nothing.
- Without `contain: layout`, the overlay can participate in page layout.

### 2. `rem` → `px` at build time

`rem` resolves against the **document root**, not the shadow host. Shadow DOM does not isolate it.

Sites that set `html { font-size: 10px }` are common (it's a long-standing CSS convention), and every rem-derived value in our overlay silently shrinks to 62.5%. Post-process the built stylesheet and bake every `rem` to `px` against a 16px base.

Cheap to implement, effectively impossible to notice in review, and the failure is a subtly mis-sized overlay only on some sites.

### 3. Inline the font as base64

Ship the overlay font as a data-URL `@font-face` in the bundled stylesheet. No network request, ever.

- A font request appears in the page's network activity. We report on network activity.
- It appears in the performance trace. We report performance metrics.
- It is a real request to a real origin, which interacts with origin policy (spec 14-security.md) and would need to be allowlisted.
- FOUT in a recording looks like a rendering bug in the app.

Also disable font synthesis, or the browser faux-bolds the caption and it looks broken.

### 4. `display:none` + **forced reflow** before every capture

Hide the capture-contaminating layers before screenshots and before `observe()`, restore afterwards, unconditionally — restore must run even when the capture throws.

The forced reflow (reading a layout property after setting `display:none`) is mandatory and not optional micro-optimization. Without it the capture races the style change and the overlay intermittently appears in screenshots. Intermittently — so it passes review and fails in CI.

**Overlay nodes MUST NOT appear in `observe()`.** This is the requirement most likely to be missed, and it is the most damaging:

- Overlay nodes enter the semantic tree, so they burn observation budget (see #14) and appear as addressable nodes.
- A model can then attempt to target our own cursor.
- It pollutes model input with content that has nothing to do with the app.

Note the interaction with #15's hide-policy split: the ambient frame must be absent from captures **by construction** (separate host, never mounted into the captured tree), not by toggling — otherwise continuous video flickers on every screenshot.

### 5. Exclude overlay elements from performance metrics by attribute

Tag every overlay host with a stable data attribute, and filter on it in any `PerformanceObserver` we run.

A full-viewport painted element becomes the Largest Contentful Paint. If we ship an ambient frame and report LCP, we report our own overlay as the app's LCP — a completely fabricated metric, delivered with confidence.

Same class of problem for CLS and for any element-attributed metric. Attribute-based exclusion is the only approach that survives us adding overlay layers later.

### 6. Every overlay operation swallows its own errors

All overlay calls are best-effort and log at debug. An overlay failure MUST NOT fail a step, fail an action, or propagate.

Visual feedback is diagnostic. A test that fails because the *cursor* could not be positioned is strictly worse than a test with no cursor. This also covers the realistic cases: page navigated mid-update, context destroyed, CSP blocking, shadow DOM unavailable.

Corollary: the overlay must degrade to nothing rather than partially. If it cannot mount, the run proceeds silently with an unannotated recording.

### 7. Idempotent mount, and re-mount after navigation

Guard mount on the host already existing. Init script covers future documents; an explicit mount covers the current one; a load handler covers the rest. All three are needed and all three must be safe to run twice.

## Acceptance

- Conformance vector: overlay nodes are absent from `observe()` output on a page where the overlay is mounted.
- Conformance vector: screenshots taken with the overlay mounted are byte-identical to screenshots with it disabled.
- Conformance vector: reported LCP is identical with the overlay mounted and disabled, on a fixture where the ambient frame is the largest painted element.
- Fixture with `html { font-size: 10px }` renders the overlay at correct size.
- Fixture with hostile global CSS (`* { position: static !important }`, global font/color resets) renders the overlay correctly and is itself visually unchanged.
- Zero network requests attributable to the overlay, verified against the driver's own request log.
- Fault injection: overlay eval throwing at mount, mid-action, and during teardown leaves step status unchanged.
- Click dispatch through an overlay-covered region reaches the intended element.

## Notes

- Blocking for #15 — these are not follow-ups. Several are conformance-visible, so shipping the overlay without them means shipping a driver that misreports `observe()` and performance metrics.
- Requirements 4 and 5 are the ones that make this a spec concern rather than an implementation concern: they constrain observable driver behavior, so they belong in `spec/09-drivers.md` with requirement IDs.

title: fix: pin the selected node when every derived query is ambiguous
body: Fixes the failure surfaced while running the wakacje suite against a cross-sell page: six identical `Kup teraz` buttons stranded the locate sweep. ``` ✗ searches Greece vacations and reaches an offer [web] failed 150542ms no derived query uniquely resolved the selected node (role=button name="Kup teraz"): getByRole("button", name: "Kup teraz") -> 2 matches getByTestId("crosssell-btn-reservation").filter({ hasText: "Kup teraz" }) -> 3 matches getByTestId("crosssell-btn-reservation") -> 6 matches getByLabel("Kup teraz") -> no matches getByText("Kup teraz") -> 3 matches getByRole("button").filter({ hasText: "Kup teraz" }) -> 2 matches ``` ## This was never a lookup failure The model names a node id, the observation resolves it, and a live handle for it exists — the runner knew precisely which button was meant. `resolveSelected` refuses to dispatch until it can re-express that node as a *portable semantic query*, and the derivation vocabulary had no way to say "this one of several identical controls". The missing word is an index, and it was already in the vocabulary: `indexExpression` in `expression.ts` and the driver's `kind: 'index'` → `.nth()` projection both existed, unused by derivation. An ambiguous query is now pinned rather than discarded: ``` locate: resolved via getByRole("button", name: "Kup teraz").nth(2) ``` The action still dispatches through a query the report can show, not a raw handle. ## Index at resolve time, not at snapshot time Same idea as the `RefMap`/`nth` approach in tester-army, with one deliberate difference: the index is computed against the match set the query *actually returned*, not recorded during observation. That matters because the observation is byte-budgeted and need not contain every match, and the page can reflow between capture and resolution. An index measured against the live result is the only one that refers to the list it will be applied to. The node is then read and signature-checked before dispatch, so a page that reordered **fails the check instead of acting on a neighbour** — that check is what makes `nth` safe rather than hopeful. Matches are separated by signature first, then by observed geometry: two distinct visible controls cannot share a rectangle, and a reflow moves all of them and matches none, which reports ambiguity rather than guessing. Above 24 matches the sweep does not try — an instruction landing on dozens of identical controls needs rewording, not an index. Disambiguation is runner-side, so it costs driver reads and **never a model call**. ## Two bugs surfaced while testing this **An unresolvable locate reported a nondeterministic error code.** Once the clock ran out the sweep raced whatever else noticed, so the same page yielded `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` or `STEP_TIMEOUT`. A timeout is the worst of those: it sends the author after their timeout value rather than their instruction. A query that runs out of clock is now the sweep's own verdict, not a transport failure. **A sweep could begin with zero remaining budget**, which reaches the driver as "no timeout" rather than "give up now" — so the query hung and the step died of an outer timeout, discarding the diagnosis the previous sweep already had. The loop no longer starts a sweep on an expired clock. This is why the reproduction above burned 150 s. ## Ambiguity that survives indexing gets a remedy Some controls are genuinely indistinguishable. Those still fail, but no longer leave the reader to infer what to do from a list of rejected queries: ``` no derived query uniquely resolved the selected node (role=button name="Twin"): getByRole("button", name: "Twin") -> 2 matches indistinguishable from the selected node ... the page has several controls this instruction cannot tell apart; name what distinguishes the one you mean, such as the section or row it belongs to ``` Worth being explicit: indexing makes such a test *run*, not necessarily *correct*. If two real `Kup teraz` buttons exist, the model chose one; which one the test means is the author's job, and the message now says so. ## Tests New `agent-ambiguity.test.ts` against real Playwright on a repeated-row fixture: - acts on the selected row when every query matches all of them - **does not collapse to the first match** — two runs, same ambiguous queries, different rows. A `.first()` fallback passes the first test and fails this one. - records the indexed query it dispatched through - still fails, with a remedy, on two buttons stacked at one rect - asks the model exactly once per tap Verified these are not vacuous: with the disambiguation reverted, 4 of 5 fail (and that run takes 90 s against 31 s, which is the deadline-polling this fixes). The vision suite's fallback-escalation case relied on two buttons being indistinguishable in the tree; indexing separates those, so its fixture is now two buttons stacked at one rect, where neither a query nor an index can help and the tree tier genuinely strands. `pnpm run check` clean, 464 tests pass, ambiguity suite green 3/3 runs. ---

title: feat: agent.pixelScale to cut what a screenshot costs
body: Vision providers bill images by **area**, never by byte length. So the only lever that lowers the bill is sending fewer pixels — and `agent.pixelScale` is that lever. ```ts export default defineConfig({ agent: { pixelScale: 0.75 }, }); ``` At a 1280x720 viewport that is **700 billed image tiles instead of 1196**, a 41% saving on every call that sends pixels. ## Why not JPEG This started as "can we send something smaller and cheaper", and JPEG was the obvious candidate. It buys nothing: no provider charges for bytes. Measured across the wakacje suite, byte size stayed **flat** at 0.75 — 743 KB against 753 KB — because resampling introduces gradients that compress worse than the flat regions it shrinks. Meanwhile the billed area dropped 41%. Upload time was never the cost either: ~2 MB/s to the gateway, so the suite's images were ~170 ms of a 70 s run, and call duration showed no correlation with image size (`r = +0.21`; the three largest images were among the fastest calls). ## What is preserved The capture is untouched — still masked, still at CSS scale. Only the copy handed to the model is resampled, and **resampling runs after masking**, so no redacted region can reappear. Geometry is *measured from the bytes that come back* rather than computed from the requested scale, so `ObservationPixels.scale` stays true and a returned point converts back to CSS pixels through the path that already existed for device-scale captures. That conversion is the real risk of scaling — the model answers in image space, the driver dispatches in CSS space — so it is what the integration test pins down. ## Where the resize runs, and why not elsewhere In the browser, which already has an image decoder, instead of adding a native image dependency to the runner. Specifically in a **scratch page in its own context**. The bytes are a screenshot of the app, and resizing them in the app's own execution context would hand that evidence back to the page under test, which could hook `createImageBitmap` and read it. The scratch context is created on first use, only when a scale below 1 is requested, and closed with the session. Two mechanisms I tried first and rejected: - **`deviceScaleFactor`** — changes `window.devicePixelRatio`, which sites read for `srcset`. A screenshot setting would silently change what the site renders, and it would leak into tree-only steps that never see a pixel. - **CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` with `clip.scale`** — bypasses Playwright's screenshotter, which is what applies `mask`. Secure-field masking would be lost. A resizer that throws returns full-scale bytes, so a broken resize costs tokens and never correctness. ## Where it degrades Against 11-20px UI text with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`: | `pixelScale` | image | billed tiles | 11px text | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `1` | 1280x720 | 1196 | read correctly | | `0.75` | 960x540 | 700 | read correctly | | `0.6` | 768x432 | 448 | read correctly | | `0.5` | 640x360 | 299 | unreadable | It fails by **refusing** rather than inventing a value. Worth noting this had to be re-measured for this mechanism: an earlier measurement used `deviceScaleFactor`, where the browser *renders* text at reduced scale with hinted glyphs, which is a different and kinder operation than resampling a 1x capture. The conclusion held, but it was not transferable. Values above 1 are a config error — the capture is already at CSS scale, so upsampling would bill the model for detail the runner never had. ## Also The screenshot token reserve now derives from the configured scale as well as the viewport. Reserving for full scale would have handed the saving straight back to an untouched observation budget. ## Tests New `agent-pixel-scale.test.ts` against real Playwright: geometry reported to the model matches the bytes sent, masked-region disclosure survives resampling, and a point read off the resized image converts back to the right CSS pixels. Verified non-vacuous — with the resize disabled, 2 of 3 fail. `pnpm run check` clean, 470 tests pass. Verified end to end against the live wakacje suite with `pixelScale: 0.75`: green, and the pointed tap on the offer card still lands. ---

title: feat(mobile): freeze mobile-0.1 and add the e2e/agent-device driver
body: Implements PLAN Phase 5: `mobile-0.1` is frozen, the runner executes mobile targets, and `e2e/agent-device` drives iOS simulators and Android emulators behind `driver-1`. ```ts export default defineConfig({ targets: [ { name: 'ios', platform: 'ios', driver: agentDevice(), app: 'com.example.app' }, { name: 'android', platform: 'android', driver: agentDevice(), app: './app.apk' }, ], }); ``` Verified against real devices, not just fakes: **18 deterministic iOS tests, 5 Android, 7 agentic with a real model**, plus 579 unit/integration tests. The device suites are opt-in and never run in CI. ## Design The driver keeps e2e semantics and uses agent-device purely as a **device transport**. It captures raw snapshots and evaluates `LocatorExpression` itself rather than delegating: agent-device's `find` resolves *and* mutates in one call and its `wait` adds the hidden query retries `spec/09-drivers.md` forbids, and its default snapshot collapses off-screen content into prose summaries. The backend surface lives in one file (`src/agent-device/client.ts`) so upstream drift is a compile error in one place, and the version is pinned exactly because this driver derives its types structurally from a pre-1.0 wire format. `agent-device` is a **peer dependency**: web-only users pay nothing for it. ### The SPI needed only additive changes `DriverDevice` for the `device` capability, `DriverRuntime.device`, `states.offscreen`, and an optional `DriverContext.app.baseUrl`. Everything platform-specific was absorbed by the projection layer without leaking into the runner, which is the main signal that the driver boundary was drawn correctly. `report-1` target provenance became platform-family specific: a web target carries browser/version/origin, a mobile target device/OS, and neither substitutes a placeholder for the other's fields — provenance is what makes two runs comparable. ## What real devices changed Every one of these was discovered by running, not by reading, and each is a spec change plus a fix.
