This is the substance of the PR. **iOS lies about visibility and hittability.** `visibleToUser` is never sent and `hittable` is `false` for plainly tappable controls; I confirmed a `hittable: false` cell taps and navigates. Visibility and actionability now derive from geometry plus the backend's explicit occlusion signal. **iOS reports stale geometry for a scrolled-away row's descendants**, placing them where the row used to be (`y=116` under a parent at `y=1057`) and zeroing the innermost. Trusting that reported an unreachable node as reachable and handed the row's label to a node that could be neither seen nor tapped. Geometry is now validated against the tree, with scroll containers exempt because a `Table`'s rect is its *visible frame* and its off-screen children legitimately fall outside it. **A switch was a silent no-op.** iOS wraps a switch in a same-role container spanning the row, so the named node's center lands on the label; the toggle is elsewhere. Verified by tapping both rects. Actions dispatch at the innermost same-role descendant — a point *inside* the selected node, not a substitute for it. A silent no-op is worse than a failure. **Off-screen rows were unreachable.** `scrollUntilVisible` returned immediately because an off-screen node is visible, then the tap failed `NOT_ACTIONABLE` — a dead end. A node outside the viewport now reports `states.offscreen`, which the runner waits to clear and a model can read. **A repeated label belongs to its outermost carrier.** One Settings row put `General` on six nested nodes. The row is what a user taps; the copies are its internals. An observation now contains only nodes a derived query can address, which is what the agent tier requires — it rejected the model's own selections before this. Controls are always kept, because a container above a search field may repeat its label and the control is the only node carrying the role. **Android was a claim until it ran.** Device names change on boot (`Medium_Phone_API_36.1` becomes `Medium Phone API 36.1`), and Android selects by `serial` while iOS uses `udid` — the daemon rejects the wrong one outright. Android's tree is also shaped differently: labels on leaf `TextView`s with no ancestor duplication, `visibleToUser` always present, and a `Switch` with no value, label, or state, so `checked` cannot be derived there. The driver leaves it unavailable rather than reporting `false`. ### Two runner defects, mobile-visible rather than mobile-specific The direct-read surfaces encode "do not wait for a value" as an expired deadline, which reached the driver as a **1 ms I/O budget** — invisible against an in-process browser query, fatal against a 2.4 s XCTest snapshot. `timeoutMs` is the budget for one operation; the polling loop owns its own deadline. A `DriverError` thrown by a driver loaded from a config file was never translated, because it is a different class across module registries. That silently degraded **every third-party driver's** error taxonomy to a generic error. Detection is now structural. ## Deliberate gaps - **`state: false`.** agent-device exposes no app-container capture, and `spec/09-drivers.md` forbids claiming the capability on a partial copy. So `test.setup` and session reuse are unavailable on mobile. - **No `trace`.** No portable iOS/Android equivalent; configuring it is a pre-run `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT`. - **Pixels are omitted when a secure field is visible.** Mobile has no masking primitive, so the vision tier degrades rather than leaking a secret or forcing the runner to discard the observation. - **No implicit scroll before acting**, unlike web. A real portability seam, documented rather than hidden; `scrollUntilVisible` is the loop. - **`verifyDriver` is still a stub**, so the 24 `mobile-0.1` requirement IDs are not yet enforceable. The suites here are keyed to the implementation, not to requirement IDs. - **No reference app**, so `deepLink`, `setPermission`, `pushNotification`, video, and the default `clear-state` isolation path have unit coverage only. Settings actively obstructed this: it is a system app with no clearable data container. ## Working around upstream Two agent-device 0.20.2 bugs are compensated for: `apps.open({url})` drops the URL without an app, and `scroll` with `durationMs` is a **no-op on iOS** (measured a row's position with and without it). `tests/unit/mobile-backend-contract.test.ts` asserts each bug still exists, because a workaround that outlives its bug is silently wrong. Worth contributing back. ## Drive-by `browserVersion` was always `unknown` in reports: runtime provenance was read at launch, before any session could know it. It is now read as the session closes, which mobile forced because device geometry is unknown until then. ---

title: feat: split the Playwright driver into @e2edev/playwright
body: Every install of `e2e` downloaded a browser, including installs that never drive one. The driver was reachable from the runner by two static imports, so it could not be dropped without also dropping the runner's default target. ## What changed The driver now ships as **`@e2edev/playwright`**, and `playwright` leaves the runner's dependency tree. No separate SPI package was needed. `e2e/driver` is already the published SPI export, and `spec/09-drivers.md` already describes community drivers as `defineDriver` consumers of it — so the new package is simply the first-party instance of the pattern the spec documents. `cli/` stays in core because `bin` must ship with it. `agent/` owns the heavy `ai` dep but is not a leaf (it back-references `run/`, `config/`, `cache/`), so it is a future candidate, not this PR. `driver: 'playwright'` still works and is still the default for a web target. The runner loads the package on demand; a target that names it without the package installed fails config resolution with `DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED`, naming what to install. That is a configuration error rather than a launch failure on purpose: it is fixed by installing a dependency, so it must never enter the retry path. ## Spec change: `prepare` One of the two couplings was not a packaging detail. `runner.ts` called Playwright's `ensureBrowsersInstalled` directly, which put one backend's provisioning inside the generic runner and left every other driver to pay for its own setup out of a launch timeout. `driver-1` gains an optional `prepare` hook, run once before any session launches. Grouping is by driver **id**, not by instance, because provisioning is shared backend state: a download repeated per target is the same download. Drivers with nothing to provision omit it. Updated together: `spec/api/driver.d.ts`, `src/driver/index.ts`, `spec/09-drivers.md`, and the drift test. ## Two bugs found while testing 1. **A failing `prepare` was classified as a test failure** and exited 1. A backend that cannot provision has not failed a test. It now goes through `translateDriverError` and exits 3. Caught by the new contract test. 2. **The list reporter never rendered run-level errors.** A run that died during config, collection, or provisioning printed `no tests executed` and a bare exit code, with the reason reachable only by opening `report.json`. That predates this PR, but this PR makes it the most likely first run a new user sees. ## Release tooling Adds changesets and a release workflow — nothing existed, and two packages cannot be published by hand reliably. Peers point one way only. With `e2e` and the driver peer-depending on each other, changesets escalated **both to a major on every release**, and `0.1.0` would have shipped as `1.0.0`. The runner's reverse peer was redundant with the driver's own range, so it is gone; the driver's range is `>=0.1.0 <1` so a runner minor does not fall out of it. Both now land on `0.2.0`. The workflow needs an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. ## Verification `pnpm check` clean. 602 + 19 unit/integration tests, testbed 33 passed. Beyond the suites, both tarballs were packed and installed into a clean `npm` project: - runner alone → `✗ configuration error DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED … install it to run this target`, exit 2 - after installing the driver → passes, exit 0 Also confirmed pnpm rewrites `workspace:` correctly on pack, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is clean. ## Notes for review - `pnpm install` warns about a **cyclic workspace dependency**: `e2e` devDepends on the driver because 9 of its integration tests drive a real browser. Kept deliberately — the dependency is genuine, and root `build`/`test` are explicitly ordered so nothing relies on topological sort. The alternative (hiding it in root devDeps) trades an honest cycle for an undeclared import. - `@e2e/testbed` renamed to `@e2edev/testbed` for consistency (private, not published). ## Breaking The `e2e/playwright` subpath export is **removed**, not aliased. Install `@e2edev/playwright` and import from it, or keep using `driver: 'playwright'`. ```bash npm install --save-dev e2e @e2edev/playwright ``` ---

title: fix: resolve an ambiguous locate by reference instead of by geometry
body: Fixes the failure the wakacje suite hit one step past the one #17 fixed — this time on a reservation form with two `Nazwisko` fields: ``` ✗ searches Greece vacations and reaches an offer [web] failed 190829ms no derived query uniquely resolved the selected node (role=textbox name="Nazwisko"): getByRole("textbox", name: "Nazwisko") -> 2 matches indistinguishable from the selected node getByTestId("input-nazwisko") -> 2 matches indistinguishable from the selected node getByLabel("Nazwisko") -> 2 matches indistinguishable from the selected node getByText("Nazwisko") -> 2 matches, none of them the selected node the page has several controls this instruction cannot tell apart; name what distinguishes the one you mean, such as the section or row it belongs to at tests-wakacje/wakacje.e2e.ts:81:3 ``` The two fields are 347 px apart. The remedy is addressed to the test author, and there was nothing for them to fix. ## What actually happened Traced with a temporary probe in `pinOne`: ``` step "Dorosly 2 Name" selected y=1087.39 matches [740, 1087.39] -> pinned step "Dorosly 2 Surname" selected y=1175.39 matches [437, 784.39] -> "indistinguishable" ``` Both matches had moved by exactly 391 px — the page scrolled between the observation and the sweep that followed it. `1175.39 − 391 = 784.39`: the second match *is* the selected node. `sameRect` compares a live rectangle against one captured before the scroll, so it matched neither, and #17's terminal branch then suppressed the `addressByReference` fallback that would have dispatched correctly. `SemanticNode.rect` is viewport-relative (`getBoundingClientRect`). Geometry was being used as a proxy for element identity, and it is a proxy that collides on reflow and breaks on scroll. ## The change The sweep no longer tries to answer an ambiguous query. It drops it, and the `NodeRef` the model selected carries the step — re-read and signature-checked, as `addressByReference` already did for queries that matched nothing. Deleted: `pinOne`, `sameRect`, `MAX_AMBIGUOUS_MATCHES`, the `MatchOutcome` type, the `terminal` plumbing, and the read of every match that paid for them. `resolve.ts` goes from 330 to 227 lines. The index those reads produced was never durable. `storableLocator` already refuses a positional expression and stores the driver's selector instead (`locate-cache.ts:203`), so the geometry was buying a query the report could print, at the cost of failing runs that were never ambiguous. ## Consequences - **Identical controls are acted on, not refused.** The model chose a node, not "one of a pair", and the reference names it. #17's dead end is gone. - **`LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` now means the reference was gone too** — the only state in which nothing in the run knows what was meant. It still fails immediately rather than polling, which is the property #17 was right to add. - **`vision: 'fallback'` is unchanged.** Its tree-only pass runs `poll: false`, which still skips the reference, so a stranded sweep escalates to pixels exactly as before (`agent-vision.test.ts` unchanged and green). ## Tests New `/drift` fixture: two identically named fields on a page whose layout keeps moving, which is the wakacje shape reduced to its mechanism. It fails on `main` and passes here. The agentic step is paired with a deterministic check that the *second* field — named by position from the test, not by the model — is the one carrying the text. `agent-ambiguity` and the `driver-contract` block are rewritten to the reference contract: the assertion moved from `actions.tap(match-1)` to `actions.tap(node-2)`, which is the distinguishing one — a `match-*` tap means the runner chose out of a query's match set by position. Removed the stacked twin buttons from `/rows`: with the reference dispatching, tapping a deliberately obscured element just burns the action timeout on Playwright's actionability check. Stacked twins still live in `/twins`, where the vision suite uses them for something they actually prove. `spec/10-determinism.md:213` described the selector fallback as existing for a control "which resolves only by index"; that is no longer how such a control resolves. `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` (611) green. ## Verification The wakacje suite completes end to end for the first time. Benchmarked across four models, no cache, vision model held at `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`: | Model | Wall time | Model calls | Tokens | Est. cost | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` | 73.2s | 29 | 157,969 | $0.211 | passed | | `xai/grok-4.5` | 118.0s | 30 | 165,208 | $0.299 | passed (2nd run) | | `anthropic/claude-opus-5` | 165.1s | 29 | 213,616 | $1.083 | passed | | `zai/glm-5.2` | 237.8s | 26 | 155,868 | $0.187 | failed both runs | The two failures are model quality, not the runner: grok-4.5 tapped "Zarezerwuj wstępnie" instead of "Zarezerwuj" on its first run, and glm-5.2 selected the "Dorosły 2" heading instead of its input. ---

title: fix: report a step that ran out of clock as its own timeout
body: A slow page failed a `waitFor` with `APP_UNREACHABLE` — the code that means the app never came up. It was up the whole time. Reverting the source fixes and running the new test shows the old behaviour verbatim: ``` AssertionError: expected 'APP_UNREACHABLE' to be 'STEP_TIMEOUT' ``` The docs describe `APP_UNREACHABLE` as "the executable failed to spawn, the child exited early, or `readyUrl` never answered" (troubleshooting.mdx). None of that had happened. This makes reality match what the page already promises. ## How a slow page became a dead app An observation is handed whatever remains of the invocation deadline (`Invocation.operation()`), so one starting near the end cannot finish. Three things then compounded: 1. **The driver asked for an illegal error.** `captureDocument` raced the evaluation against that budget and reported ```ts new DriverError('OPERATION_TIMEOUT', 'observation capture timed out', { retryable: true }) ``` Legal retryability is closed to `NODE_STALE` and `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` (`09-drivers.md:258`), so the `DriverError` constructor silently rewrote the code to `DRIVER_FAILURE` (`driver/index.ts:227`) — which the runner translates to `APP_UNREACHABLE`. The spec already says a capture that ran out of budget is `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` and is not retried in place (`09-drivers.md:169`), and the driver's two other timeout producers (`support.ts`, `navigationStaleOr`) already reported it that way with tests to match. This one line was the outlier. 2. **The retry loop deferred to the transport.** `captureObservation` consulted the deadline only to decide whether to keep retrying, then rethrew whatever the driver said. Running out of clock is the step's condition, not the backend's, so the loop now calls `checkDeadline` first and reports `STEP_TIMEOUT`. 3. **`waitFor` lost its last judgment.** Its timeout message names the last thing the model concluded, which is the only part that says what the wait was waiting for. That message was built when the clock ran out *between* rounds but not when it ran out *during* an observation — precisely the slow-page case. Both paths now share one constructor. ## Diagnostics kept `checkDeadline` takes the failure being handled and attaches it as `cause`, so a driver error that lands just after the deadline is still recorded rather than replaced by a bare timeout. The report does not serialize causes today, so this only shows up in local stacks; it costs three lines and stops the runner from throwing information away. ## Tests New contract test drives a fake driver whose first capture succeeds — so the wait owns a judgment to report — and whose every later capture outlives the budget it was handed. It asserts `STEP_TIMEOUT` and that the last judgment survives in the message. Confirmed failing on `main` with the source changes stashed. The `session.ts` line is a one-word conformance fix: it has no dedicated test because the raced timeout lives inside a private capture path reachable only by blocking a real page's main thread, which buys a slow, timing-dependent test for an invariant `driver-spi.test.ts` already asserts directly ("coerces illegal retryable combinations to DRIVER_FAILURE"). The sibling producers are covered in `playwright-errors.test.ts`. `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` (612) green. ---

title: afterAll is skipped when a test fails or times out
body:
`afterAll` hooks are silently skipped whenever a test does not pass.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:139` — "`afterAll` runs after the last runnable member leaves each scope"
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:146` — every scope whose `beforeAll` started MUST run its `afterAll`
- Conformance: `RUNNER-HOOK-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:258` — `if (attempt.status !== 'passed') realm = null;` drops the realm reference **without** calling `realms.leave(realm)`. Every pending `afterAll` in the entered scope chain is skipped.
- Same at `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:210` (serial unit resets `realm = null` after non-serial tests ran).
- Only the pass path (`execute.ts:217`) leaves the realm.
- Secondary: `packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts:119-143` — `leave()` only runs at the end of the whole file unit and drains *all* pending scopes at once, so an inner `describe`'s `afterAll` fires at file end rather than when its last test finishes.

## Expected
1. `afterAll` for an entered scope runs regardless of the attempt outcome.
2. `afterAll` for an inner `describe` runs when that scope's last runnable member leaves, not at file end.
3. Failures inside `afterAll` are reported as secondary errors per `11-lifecycle.md:288`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `realms.leave()` is invoked on every exit path in `execute.ts`
- [ ] Scope exit is driven by "last runnable member of this scope", not "end of unit"
- [ ] Integration test: failing test in a nested describe still runs both inner and outer `afterAll`, in inner-then-outer order
- [ ] Integration test: timed-out test still runs `afterAll`

title: Session envelope algorithm is 'aes-256-gcm'; session-v1 schema requires 'A256GCM'
body:

## Expected
The literal `A256GCM`, plus a test that Ajv-validates a real produced envelope against the canonical schema.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `sessions.ts` emits `algorithm: 'A256GCM'`
- [ ] `tests/helpers/session-schema.ts` added, mirroring `report-schema.ts`

title: locator.fill(secret) bypasses all secret authorization checks
body:
`locator.fill(secret)` is one of the three closed secure sinks but performs **zero** authorization before resolving plaintext.

## Spec
- `spec/04-resources.md:22-26` — closed secure sinks
- `spec/04-resources.md:54-56` — credential `allowedOrigins` scoping
- `spec/14-security.md:74-83` — the six checks that MUST precede plaintext resolution
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-003`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:214-221` calls `this.context.secrets.resolve(value)` **eagerly, before any node read**.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:106-118` (`SecretResolver.resolve`) does no origin, role, purpose, or disabled check — it only sets viewport taint (`fixtures.ts:115`), and it sets that taint even when the fill later fails.
- The agent path is correct by contrast: `packages/e2e/src/agent/secrets.ts:17-69` checks origin, `EDITABLE_ROLES`, `inputPurpose`, and disabled.

Missing checks from `14-security.md:74-83`, on both paths:
| # | Check | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | handle authentic | partial (brand check at `screen.ts:46-51`, not re-verified in `secrets.ts:23`) |
| 1 | handle **unresolved** (single use) | **missing** — no consumed flag anywhere |
| 2 | requested sink is a closed secure sink | **missing as a check** |
| 3 | frame origin allowed | **missing** — SPI exposes no frame origin (see the frame-origin issue) |
| 5 | observation revision / node still current | **missing** — `secrets.ts` trusts `located.node` |
| 6 | no prior tool call transferred control to another origin | **missing** — no per-invocation origin ledger |

Also: `packages/e2e/src/credentials.ts:24` hardcodes `purpose: 'password'` for every secret, so `one-time-code` and `generic-secret` are unreachable.

## Expected
One shared authorizer used by all three sinks, running the full six-check sequence before any plaintext is materialized.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Single `authorizeSecretFill()` shared by `locator.fill`, `agent.type`, and `agent.login`
- [ ] Plaintext is resolved only *after* the node is read and all checks pass
- [ ] `POLICY_DENIED` when the top-level origin is outside the credential's `allowedOrigins`
- [ ] Secret handles are single-use; second resolve is `POLICY_DENIED`
- [ ] Taint is applied only on an authorized, attempted fill
- [ ] `Secret.purpose` is author-selectable, not hardcoded
- [ ] Security vectors: disallowed origin, non-editable node, wrong `inputPurpose`, stale observation revision, reused handle

title: Reference driver does not support the 'video' artifact required by web-0.1
body:
The canonical example config in `spec/examples/e2e.config.ts` cannot launch the canonical reference driver.

## Spec
- `spec/09-drivers.md:228-229` — `web-0.1` REQUIRES screenshot, trace **and** video
- `spec/examples/e2e.config.ts:22` — `artifacts: ['trace', 'screenshot', 'video']`
- Conformance: `DRIVER-ARTIFACT-001`, `SDK-TYPES-004`

- `packages/playwright/src/index.ts` declares `artifacts: ['screenshot', 'trace']`.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:347-353` throws `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT` for any configured artifact the driver lacks.
- `startVideo` / `stopVideo` do not exist in `packages/playwright/src/session.ts`.

So the reference driver is not `web-0.1` conformant, and `pnpm check:spec` type-checks the example while nothing proves it runs.

Reference driver records video via Playwright's `recordVideo` context option, honouring artifact size limits and taint (see the taint issue).

title: report-1 step and error 'source' locations are fabricated ('unknown', line 1)
body:
Every step in every report carries a fabricated source location.

## Spec
- `spec/13-reporting.md` — step records carry the authoring source location
- `spec/schema/report-v1.schema.json` — `source` is `{file,line,column}`
- Conformance: `REPORT-SEMANTIC-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:254-261` — `UNIMPLEMENTED_STEP_SOURCE = { file: 'unknown', line: 1, column: 1 }`
- `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:327` — serial group source is always `line: 1, column: 1`
- `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:59-66` — `ReportError` omits the schema's optional `error.source` entirely, so `13-reporting.md:99-100` is never satisfied
- Stacks are stripped at `build.ts:278-282` although the schema and `13-reporting.md:105` permit a sanitized one

This makes the code-frame renderer (`src/report/code-frame.ts`) and any future HTML report useless for navigation.

## Expected
Capture the call site at step registration (`Error.captureStackTrace` / `structuredStackTrace`), map to project-relative POSIX paths, and emit it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Step source captured at registration time in `src/run/steps.ts`
- [ ] Serial-group source is the real `test.describe` site
- [ ] `error.source` emitted, sanitized, project-relative
- [ ] Sanitized `stack` retained per `13-reporting.md:105`
- [ ] No path escapes the project root

title: Artifact paths are not contained, canonicalized, or symlink-checked
body:
Artifact paths are joined without canonicalization or containment checks.

## Spec
- `spec/13-reporting.md:15-18` — all paths relative POSIX, canonical, contained, symlink safe
- `spec/09-drivers.md:234` — driver artifact paths MUST be canonicalized, traversal and symlink escape rejected
- `spec/14-security.md:16-22` — artifact labels, filenames, and backend paths are untrusted input
- Conformance: `REPORT-PATH-001`, `DRIVER-ARTIFACT-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:36` — `path.join(dir, relativePath)`, unchecked
- `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:51` — `path.posix.join(...segments, relativePath)`, unchecked
- A driver-supplied `relativePath` containing `..` escapes the artifact root and produces a report value that violates `$defs/relativePath`
- No `realpath`/`lstat` symlink rejection anywhere in `src/`
- `sanitizePathSegment` (`artifacts.ts:64`) is applied only to runner-generated segments, not to the driver-supplied tail

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Resolve + `realpath` every artifact path and reject anything outside the artifact root
- [ ] Reject symlinked path components
- [ ] Reject absolute paths and `..` segments from drivers with a `DriverError`
- [ ] Security vector: hostile driver returning `../../etc/passwd` and a symlinked artifact dir

title: ArtifactRecord.redaction enum mismatches report-v1 and is hardcoded to 'complete'
body:
The report claims every artifact is fully redacted, unconditionally.

## Spec
- `spec/schema/report-v1.schema.json:82` — `redaction: complete | not-required | incomplete`
- `spec/13-reporting.md:142-144` — an `incomplete` artifact has no path/size/digest, is never persisted, and is never model-visible
- `spec/14-security.md:157`
- Conformance: `REPORT-ARTIFACT-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/run/records.ts:18` — `ArtifactRecord.redaction: 'none' | 'complete'`. `'none'` is not in the schema enum and `'incomplete'` is unrepresentable.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:53` — hardcodes `redaction: 'complete'` for every artifact kind, regardless of whether anything was masked.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:39-55` sets `redaction: 'complete'` but omits `path`/`size`/`sha256` when `statSync`/hash fails, which the schema rejects (`report-v1.schema.json:114-121` requires all three unless `redaction === 'incomplete'`).
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts` hardcodes `Observation.redaction.complete = true`, so the runner's `MASKING_UNPROVEN` gate (`src/agent/observation.ts:49-54`) can never trip against the reference driver.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ArtifactRecord.redaction` uses the schema enum exactly
- [ ] `complete` is emitted only when masking was actually proven for that artifact
- [ ] `incomplete` artifacts are deleted from disk and carry no path/size/digest
- [ ] Driver reports real masking results instead of a constant
- [ ] Hostile-report vector covers each enum value

title: HTML reporter is a default reporter with no implementation
body:
`html` is a **default** reporter but has no implementation; `--reporter html` is silently a no-op.

A local, single-file, zero-remote-asset HTML reporter with a strict CSP, rendering all untrusted strings as text.

title: Implement agent.act (planning tier)
body:
The entire planning tier is unbuilt. `agent.act` is the headline API of the project and currently throws.

## Spec
- `spec/02-test-api.md:102-124` — `act` semantics, `maxSteps` action accounting, schema repair loop
- `spec/api/e2e.d.ts:190-200` — both `act` overloads
- `spec/10-determinism.md` — control gradient, `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION`
- Conformance: `AGENT-TOOL-002`, `AGENT-TOOL-005`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts:235` — `act: (() => planningTierUnavailable('agent.act'))`, mapped to `POLICY_DENIED` at `src/agent/invocation.ts:758`
- `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:18-20` — `tool-proposal` step events explicitly deferred
- `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION` is declared (`src/agent/error.ts:27`, `src/types.ts:176`) but never thrown; no same-proposal / same-observation-revision duplicate detection exists

## Blast radius
`spec/examples/**` is unrunnable: `signup.e2e.ts:11`, `onboarding.e2e.ts:20,25`, `billing/checkout.e2e.ts:16`, `notifications.e2e.ts:13,15,21,37` all call `agent.act`.

## Depends on
The `agent-tool-1` grammar issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bounded observe → propose → validate → dispatch → re-observe loop
- [ ] Tool calls validated against `spec/schema/agent-tool-v1.schema.json`
- [ ] `maxSteps` counts **actions**, `maxModelCalls` counts model calls; both emit `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`
- [ ] `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION` on a repeated proposal at an unchanged observation revision
- [ ] Schema-overload variant returns required inferred `data` (`SDK-TYPES-002`)
- [ ] `tool-proposal` step events emitted into `report-1`
- [ ] Every `spec/examples/**` test that uses `act` runs against the testbed

title: Implement agent.login

`agent.login` throws. Every canonical example that declares a session fails at setup, which cascades to 8 of 10 example tests.

title: agent-tool-1: no runner-side tool grammar parser or authorizer exists
body:
`spec/schema/agent-tool-v1.schema.json` has **no consumer in `src/`**. `rg "agent-tool" packages/e2e/src` returns zero hits.

## Spec
- `spec/schema/agent-tool-v1.schema.json` — one closed discriminated union
- `spec/02-test-api.md:86-87` — each agent method receives only its documented tool subset and budget
- `spec/14-security.md:38` — method-incompatible actions are `POLICY_DENIED`
- Conformance: `AGENT-TOOL-001` … `AGENT-TOOL-006`

- `packages/e2e/src/agent/protocol.ts` hand-rolls locate/judgment grammars and never loads any canonical schema
- No per-method tool subset exists; there is no tool dispatch at all (see the `agent.act` issue)
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/locate.ts:536-540` returns `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` for a point answer to a node-only method; the spec requires `POLICY_DENIED`
- `spec/schema/agent-locate-v1.schema.json` and `agent-judgment-v1.schema.json` are likewise never validated against — only reimplemented

title: cache-1 path entries are neither produced nor consumed
body:
`cache-1` defines path entries; nothing produces or consumes them.

## Spec
- `spec/10-determinism.md:110-112`, `:282-299` — path guidance: reobserve, never restart after a committed mutation, `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED`, only a completely successful non-retry invocation writes
- `spec/schema/cache-v1.schema.json`
- Conformance: `CACHE-PATH-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/cache/entry.ts:40` rejects `kind: 'path'`, so a schema-valid path entry is reported `cache-invalid` (`src/cache/store.ts:107`) rather than merely ignored — a divergence from "an entry that fails is ignored"
- `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED` exists only in the error-code list (`src/agent/error.ts:24`)
- Blocked on the `agent.act` issue, since paths are `act` guidance

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Path entries written after a fully successful, non-retry `act` invocation
- [ ] Replay reobserves before each guided action
- [ ] Divergence before the first mutating action discards guidance and continues from the model
- [ ] Divergence after a committed mutation raises `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED` and never restarts inside the attempt
- [ ] Unknown-`kind` entries are ignored, not reported as `cache-invalid`
- [ ] Injected-divergence vector proves no committed action is duplicated

title: Prompt fences can be broken by untrusted page and model-derived text
body:
Untrusted page text and untrusted model-derived text are interpolated into the prompt fence with no delimiter escaping.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md` — prompt injection MUST NOT expand runner policy
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:68` — `<instruction>` interpolates the author string; a string containing `</instruction>` closes the fence
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:37` — same for `<project-context>`
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:91` — same for `<ledger>`, and ledger content is **model-derived** (`src/agent/ledger.ts:53` uses `step.explanation`), so this is a live untrusted → fence-break path
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:100` — the repair prompt echoes up to 2000 chars of prior model output back into the next request
- No injection-resistance vectors exist: `tests/integration/agent-policy.test.ts` covers stale revision / unknown id / closed grammar only; nothing feeds instruction-shaped page text, ledger text, or image-drawn text

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fence delimiters escaped or randomized-nonce delimited for every interpolated untrusted region
- [ ] Ledger explanations sanitized for fence tokens before packing
- [ ] Injection vectors added: page text, accessible names, ledger explanations, repair echo, and text rendered into a screenshot
- [ ] Vectors assert no policy expansion and no tool outside the method's allowlist

title: Secret redaction is observation-only; ledger budget excludes the omission line
body:
The ledger can exceed `maxLedgerBytes`, and secrets are redacted only on the observation path.

## Spec
- `spec/10-determinism.md:57-60` — the **complete** ledger context is bounded
- `spec/14-security.md:235-237` — redaction completeness
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-004`

## Current behavior
1. `packages/e2e/src/agent/ledger.ts:44` — the `[N earlier step(s) omitted]` line is `unshift`ed **after** the byte budget is exhausted, so the emitted context exceeds resolved `maxLedgerBytes` by that line's length.
2. `packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts:10` (`createRedactor`) has exactly one call site: `src/agent/observation.ts:59`. It is **not** applied to:
   - step `label` / `explanation` on the way into the report (`src/run/steps.ts:200-209` — no sanitize, no redact, no truncate)
   - serialized errors (`src/internal/errors.ts:219-229` strips control chars but does not redact secrets), including provider error text from `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (`src/agent/model/sdk.ts:262`)
   - terminal output (`src/report/list.ts:18-20`)
   - `agentTrace` lines (`src/internal/trace.ts:39`)
   - cache payloads (`src/cache/entry.ts`) — a recorded accessible name derived from a filled secret value would be persisted
3. No user-defined redaction patterns (`14-security.md:236-237`, SHOULD).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Budget accounting includes the omission line
- [ ] One redaction pass applied at every boundary that leaves the runner: report, terminal, trace, cache, errors
- [ ] Optional `redactPatterns` config
- [ ] Vector: a secret value appearing in an accessible name never reaches report, terminal, trace, or cache

title: Production opt-in does not block model-proposed raw-coordinate actions
body:
Model-proposed raw-coordinate actions are permitted against production targets.

- `allowProduction` is never consulted outside config resolution and report building — `rg allowProduction packages/e2e/src` hits only `src/config/resolve.ts:284-290`, `src/report/build.ts:374`, and a passthrough at `src/run/execute.ts:347`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Point capability is denied when the resolved target is production
- [ ] `POLICY_DENIED` raised before the first model call, not after an invalid answer
- [ ] `vision: 'only'` against a production target is a configuration error
- [ ] Vector covers both `vision: 'only'` and `vision: 'fallback'` escalation

title: agent.scrollTo under vision:'only' burns budget then fails MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID instead of POLICY_DENIED

`agent.scrollTo` under `vision: 'only'` fails with the wrong error code, at the wrong time, after burning model budget.

- So the call gets the `'point'` grammar (`locate.ts:143`), the validator rejects every answer (`locate.ts:238-240`), budget is consumed, and it ends in `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` (`locate.ts:536-540`)
