- [ ] `POLICY_DENIED` before any model call
- [ ] Test asserts zero model calls were made

title: Origin policy is not re-validated after redirects, and popups are unchecked
body:
Origin policy is checked only before dispatch. Everything after that fails open.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:53` — "A redirect outside policy is blocked before interaction continues"; origin checked before dispatch **and after redirects**
- `spec/08-platforms.md:169`
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-002`, `WEB-NAV-001`

## Current behavior
- Pre-dispatch only: `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:215,239,277` → `resolveNavigationUrl` (`src/internal/urls.ts:65-86`)
- `packages/playwright/src/web.ts:102-105` does a bare `page.goto`; no caller compares `page.url()` or the response chain against `allowedOrigins`
- **Popups are entirely unhandled**: `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:215` creates one page and there is no `context.on('page')` handler, so a popup is neither blocked nor origin-checked
- `resolveNavigationUrl` never inspects `url.username` / `url.password` (`urls.ts:65-86`); only the base URL is checked (`urls.ts:25`)
- An `allowedOrigins` entry of `http://example.com` passes validation (`src/config/resolve.ts:292-306`) and `web.goto` will happily use it — HTTPS is enforced only for `app.url` (`urls.ts:37-42`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Post-navigation and post-redirect URL re-validated against `allowedOrigins`
- [ ] Redirect chain inspected, not just the final URL
- [ ] `context.on('page')` handler blocks or origin-checks popups
- [ ] Navigation URLs carrying userinfo are rejected
- [ ] Non-loopback `allowedOrigins` entries must be HTTPS
- [ ] Vectors: cross-origin redirect, meta-refresh, `window.open` to a denied origin

title: Incomplete scheme denylist; no link-local, cloud-metadata, or DNS-rebinding policy
body:
The URL scheme denylist is incomplete and there is no IP-level policy at all.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:51-52` — link-local and cloud metadata denial
- `spec/14-security.md:54-55` — DNS-resolution IP recheck at connect time and after redirects
- `spec/05-config.md:159-163`
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-002`, `RUNNER-CONFIG-003`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts:59` denies only `file:`, `data:`, `javascript:`. Missing: `about:`, `chrome:`, `devtools:`, `view-source:`, `blob:`, `ws:`/`wss:`, `ftp:`, `intent:`.
- No check anywhere for `169.254.0.0/16`, `169.254.169.254`, `metadata.google.internal`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `::ffff:169.254.*`. `http://169.254.169.254` passes `allowedOrigins` validation today.
- No resolver hook, no connect-time or post-redirect IP validation. `rg '169\.254|lookup|rebind' packages/e2e/src` → nothing.
- `allowedOrigins` entries are only shape-checked (`src/config/resolve.ts:286-300`) — no private-range rule.
- `app.readyUrl` is completely unvalidated (`src/config/resolve.ts:311`) and `fetch`ed raw at `src/run/app-process.ts:57`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scheme allowlist (`http`, `https`) rather than a denylist
- [ ] Link-local, cloud-metadata, and (configurably) private ranges denied
- [ ] DNS resolution checked at connect time and re-checked after each redirect (rebinding)
- [ ] `app.readyUrl` parsed, origin-checked, and HTTPS/loopback-checked
- [ ] Vectors: metadata IP, rebinding host, `blob:`/`about:` navigation

title: No trace filtering; app.screenshot is neither masked nor taint-gated
body:
Playwright traces are started with full request/response and DOM snapshot capture and are then registered as `redaction: 'complete'`.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:125-127` — trace filtering
- `spec/14-security.md:121-123` — while tainted, screenshots are omitted from evidence
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-004`, `DRIVER-ARTIFACT-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts` starts tracing with `{ screenshots: true, snapshots: true }`. That records request/response bodies, `authorization` and `cookie` headers, DOM snapshots (including filled input values), and trace screenshots taken while the viewport was tainted.
- No filtering code exists anywhere. `spec/14-security.md:125-127` is entirely unimplemented.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:243-249` — `app.screenshot()` is **not** taint-gated; it calls `session.artifacts.screenshot` unconditionally and registers it as evidence. Contrast `agent.assert`, which is correctly gated at `src/agent/index.ts:619-622`.
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts` `artifacts.screenshot` passes **no `mask`**, unlike the observation path (`packages/playwright/src/observe.ts:42-53`).
- `ArtifactSink.register` accepts `'video'` (`src/run/fixtures.ts:44`) with no taint gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Trace post-processing strips `authorization`/`cookie` headers and request/response bodies, or tracing is configured to not capture them
- [ ] Trace segments recorded while tainted are dropped, or the trace is marked `incomplete`
- [ ] `app.screenshot()` masks secure regions and is suppressed while tainted
- [ ] Video frames discarded while tainted
- [ ] Vector: fill a secret, capture every artifact kind, assert the plaintext appears in none of them

title: driver-1 SPI exposes no frame origin, so frame policy fails open
body:
The runner cannot verify frame origin because the SPI does not expose it, so a non-conforming driver fails open.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:4` — the runner owns policy; drivers are untrusted
- `spec/14-security.md:74-83` check 3 — frame origin MUST be allowed before plaintext resolution
- `spec/08-platforms.md:183` — cross-origin frames are queryable only when their origin is allowed
- Conformance: `WEB-FRAME-001`, `RUNNER-SECURITY-003`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:121-124` — `SemanticNode` exposes `framePath` (CSS selectors) but **no frame origin**
- The only frame gate lives in the driver (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts` `isAllowedFrameOrigin`), on the observation path only
- The deterministic surface does no origin check at all: `validateFrames` (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:374-394`) and `packages/playwright/src/locators.ts:94`
- Consequence: `packages/e2e/src/agent/secrets.ts` cannot perform check 3 and does not attempt it

## Note
This is a `driver-1` SPI change — per `AGENTS.md` it must land in `spec/api/driver.d.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts`, `spec/09-drivers.md`, and the drift test in one review.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `SemanticNode` (and/or the frame descriptor) carries a serialized frame origin
- [ ] Runner enforces frame-origin policy for queries, actions, and secret fills
- [ ] Deterministic `getBy*` inside a denied cross-origin frame fails `POLICY_DENIED`
- [ ] `spec/api/driver.d.ts` + drift test + `09-drivers.md` updated together
- [ ] Vector: secret fill targeted at a node inside a denied cross-origin frame

title: Credential resolution: no env-only source, no name normalization, no pair validation
body:
`spec/04-resources.md` credential resolution is materially unimplemented.

## Spec
- `spec/04-resources.md:41-52` — resolution sources, uppercase-ASCII/`_` name normalization, env pair override
- `spec/04-resources.md:47-49` — nonempty validation, collision detection
- `spec/04-resources.md:60-62` — same normalized name resolves to the same record
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-003`, `RUNNER-CONFIG-003`

## Current behavior
- **Env-only credentials never materialize.** `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:421-438` iterates only `Object.entries(raw.credentials)`. A credential supplied purely via `E2E_USER_X_USERNAME` / `_PASSWORD` — resolution source #1 — is invisible.
- **No name normalization.** `packages/e2e/src/credentials.ts:39` does `registry.get(name)` with the raw string; `resolve.ts:430` keys by the raw config key. `credentials.user('Admin')` against `credentials: { admin: … }` throws `AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **No collision check** for keys normalizing to one name (`resolve.ts:425-436`).
- **No nonempty / partial-pair validation.** `resolve.ts:428-429` accepts `password: undefined` — which is exactly what `spec/examples/e2e.config.ts:25` produces when `MEMBER_PASSWORD` is unset. Failure surfaces much later instead of as a configuration error.
- **Env override is per-field, not per-pair** (`resolve.ts:428-429`), so an env username can be paired with a config password.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Env-only credentials discovered by scanning `E2E_USER_*_USERNAME` / `_PASSWORD`
- [ ] Names normalized before registration and lookup
- [ ] Collision after normalization is a configuration error
- [ ] Missing/empty username or password is a configuration error at resolve time
- [ ] Env override replaces the pair atomically
- [ ] Unit vectors for each rule

title: Nine resolved limits are reported but never enforced
body:
Nine resolved limits are echoed into `report.usage` as if active, but have no consumer.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:222` — resolved limits **and usage** MUST be reported; quota exhaustion cancels active work
- `spec/05-config.md:261-264` — `maxDiscoveredResults` fails **before result expansion** with a bounded config-error report
- Conformance: `RUNNER-CONFIG-003`, `REPORT-PROVENANCE-001`

## Inert limits
All resolved at `packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts:104-119`, echoed at `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:417-434`, never enforced:

| Limit | Note |
|---|---|
| `maxTerminalFieldBytes` | `src/report/list.ts:10` hardcodes `8192` |
| `maxArtifactBytes`, `maxArtifactTotalBytes` | `src/run/artifacts.ts:40` only `stat`s |
| `maxDownloads`, `maxDownloadBytes` | `src/run/fixtures.ts:466` registers with no counter |
| `maxReportBytes` | `src/report/write.ts:9` writes unbounded; `usage.reportBytes` emitted as constant `0` (`build.ts:451`) |
| `maxDiscoveredResults` | `src/collect/select.ts:166-172` expands unconditionally |
| `maxEstimatedCostUsd` | accumulated at `src/agent/invocation.ts:739`, never compared |
| `maxModelCallsPerStep`, `maxActionStepsPerStep` | inert — budgets come from `agent.maxModelCalls`/`agent.maxSteps` (`src/agent/index.ts:472-473`) |

`usage.maxTerminalFieldBytes` is also hardcoded `0` (`build.ts:445`), and `usage.downloads`/`artifactBytes` count only artifacts that happened to have a `size` (`build.ts:485-487`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each limit has an enforcement site and a typed error
- [ ] `maxDiscoveredResults` fails before expansion, with zero counts in the report
- [ ] `maxEstimatedCostUsd` cancels active work when exceeded
- [ ] `usage.*` values are measured, not constants
- [ ] One test per limit

title: Session store has no lease lock, maintenance lock, or startup scavenging
body:
Session storage lacks the maintenance behavior in `spec/11-lifecycle.md:221-231`.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:221` — owner-only storage; inability to enforce it is a configuration error
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:228-231` — advisory lease lock in the run directory, session-root maintenance lock, startup scavenging
- `spec/14-security.md:169`
- Conformance: `SESSION-CLEANUP-001`

## Current behavior
- No advisory lease lock; no maintenance lock — neither appears anywhere in `packages/e2e/src/run/sessions.ts`
- No startup scavenging: `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:207-208` just creates the store; nothing enumerates `.e2e/sessions/*`. Ciphertext from a crashed run is undecryptable but accumulates forever.
- `mkdirSync(mode: 0o700)` (`sessions.ts:109,172`) is best-effort only — no `stat`-back verification, no `ConfigurationError` on a platform that cannot enforce it
- No `fsync` of file or directory around the rename (`sessions.ts:172-173`)

Correctly implemented for reference: per-run random key held in memory only (`sessions.ts:92,104`), AES-256-GCM with a canonical-JSON AAD (`sessions.ts:154,206-208`), full binding validation (`sessions.ts:187-204`), expiry min(driver, +24h) (`sessions.ts:120-127`), atomic publish (`sessions.ts:170-173`), per-run dir removed at run end (`sessions.ts:236`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Advisory lease lock in the run directory
- [ ] Session-root maintenance lock
- [ ] Startup scavenging of expired/abandoned run directories
- [ ] `stat`-back verification of mode/ownership; `ConfigurationError` when unenforceable
- [ ] `fsync` file and directory before/after rename
- [ ] Vector: crashed prior run leaves ciphertext; next run scavenges it

title: Trust notice and pre-first-use model disclosure are never emitted
body:
Two ambient-authority disclosures required by `spec/14-security.md` have no code, and one is documented in a comment as intentionally absent.

## Spec
- `spec/14-security.md:24-26` — documentation **and CLI output** MUST state the ambient-authority trust model
- `spec/14-security.md:96-100` — pre-first-use disclosure of model provider, model, endpoint origin, and data categories
- Conformance: `RUNNER-SECURITY-005`, `REPORT-PROVENANCE-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:549-550` hardcodes `trustNoticeShown: false` with a comment asserting the notice is "never printed" — encoding a spec violation as intent.
- Model provenance is recorded **per step** (`src/agent/invocation.ts:699-714`) but nothing is disclosed **before** the first call, and `agent.visionModel` is never separately announced.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CLI prints the trust notice once per run (suppressible via a flag, still recorded)
- [ ] `trustNoticeShown` reflects reality
- [ ] Model + vision-model provider/endpoint origin/data categories disclosed before the first model call
- [ ] Remove the "never printed" comment

title: ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED is never raised; commit ambiguity is unimplemented
body:
The reference driver never raises `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`, so the entire commit-ambiguity contract is untested and unimplemented.

## Spec
- `spec/08-platforms.md:111-114`, `spec/09-drivers.md:141-146` — every mutator MUST distinguish precommit stale state from possibly-committed failure
- Conformance: `DRIVER-ACTION-002`

## Current behavior
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:475-495` (`classifyActionError`) emits only `NODE_STALE`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `DRIVER_FAILURE`. A click that timed out mid-dispatch is reported `NOT_ACTIONABLE` — i.e. as safe to retry when it may not be.
- Applies to every mutator: locator actions, swipes, app lifecycle, navigation, route decisions, drag.
- Downstream: retry eligibility (`packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts`) and cache path guidance both depend on this distinction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every mutator tracks whether dispatch began
- [ ] Failures after dispatch begins are `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED` with `retryable: false`
- [ ] Runner does not retry a possibly-committed action
- [ ] Fault-injection vector: abort mid-click, assert the classification and that no duplicate action occurs

title: Observation ARIA role and accessible-name computation diverges from the deterministic path
body:
The observation path uses a hand-rolled role table and name algorithm that diverge from ARIA 1.2 / AccName 1.2.

## Spec
- `spec/08-platforms.md:65-68` — ARIA 1.2 roles, AccName 1.2 names, `hidden` state
- Conformance: `WEB-QUERY-001`

## Current behavior
`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts:166-229` — a ~25-tag table. Missing: `form`, `section`→`region`, `aside`→`complementary`, `header`/`footer`, `article`, `fieldset`→`group`, `td`/`th`/`tr`/`thead`, `dl`/`dt`/`dd`, `p`, `hr`→`separator`, `progressbar`, `details`/`summary`, `figure`, `blockquote`, `search`, `menu`. `input[type=email|tel|url|number|date]` all collapse to `textbox`; `input[type=password]` is emitted as `textbox` (ARIA 1.2: no role). No role-ownership / required-owned-element rules.

`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts:245-298` — accessible name: no recursive `aria-labelledby` computation (uses `innerText` of targets), no `fieldset`/`legend`, no `table`/`caption`, no `::before`/`::after`, no `area`/`input[type=image]` alt. "Name from content" is a hardcoded role list (`:278-291`) missing `cell`, `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `gridcell`, `treeitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `tooltip`, `switch`.

`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts:300-308` — `isHidden` covers `aria-hidden` (self only), `display`/`visibility`, client rects. No `inert`, no `content-visibility`.

**Role fidelity is therefore split between the two surfaces**: the deterministic `getByRole` path delegates to Playwright (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts:36`) and is correct, while the agent sees a different, lossier tree of the same page.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Observation roles derived from the same source as the deterministic path (Playwright's ARIA snapshot / `role` computation) rather than a parallel table
- [ ] AccName computed per AccName 1.2, including recursive `aria-labelledby`
- [ ] `inert` and `content-visibility` honoured in `hidden`
- [ ] Reference vectors: the deterministic and observed role/name for the same node must agree

title: Web profile gaps: scroll/swipe gestures, frame cardinality, route.continue, evaluate errors, dialogs, downloads
body:
Several web-profile behaviors are approximated rather than implemented.

## Spec / conformance
`spec/08-platforms.md:127-141, 186-189, 196, 206-209`; `WEB-SCROLL-001`, `WEB-FRAME-001`, `WEB-ROUTE-001`, `WEB-EVAL-001`

## Findings

**Scroll / swipe** (`packages/playwright/src/support.ts:150-204`)
- Correct distance ratios 0.5/0.75/1.5 (`:188-191`) but **no durations** (spec: 250/500/250 ms)
- No 75%→25% start/end gesture points; viewport swipe never moves the pointer to a start point
- Distance not capped by remaining scroll range
- No two-unchanged-fingerprint termination (`08-platforms.md:133,140-141`): `packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:152-164` terminates on timeout only; `packages/e2e/src/agent/locate.ts:394-406` is budget-only
- `scrollUntilVisible` hardcodes momentum `'slow'` and always uses the **viewport** (`screen.ts:162`); no nearest-scrollable-ancestor selection
- `scrollIntoView` uses `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:443-445`) = "fully visible", but `08-platforms.md:127` requires success when **any** part is in the viewport

**Frames** (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:374-394`)
- `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` / `FRAME_AMBIGUOUS` are correct, but every selector in a nested chain is counted against the **top-level page** (`session.ts:379` `page.locator(selector)`), so inner-frame cardinality is validated in the wrong document

**Routes** (`packages/playwright/src/web.ts:160-162`)
- `continue()` is implemented as `route.fallback()`, which hands the request to the *next (older)* handler instead of continuing it to the network — a semantic divergence from "the first matching handler owns the request and MUST call exactly one of fulfill/continue/abort"

**Evaluate** (`packages/playwright/src/web.ts:121-134`)
- Page exceptions are rethrown raw and wrapped as `DRIVER_FAILURE`; `08-platforms.md:196` requires the message preserved and the source location mapped

**Dialogs** (`packages/playwright/src/web.ts:66-99`)
- Newest-first, attempt-scoped, idempotent disposer are all correct. Missing: "if an operation is active it rejects immediately" and "aborts pending waits" — currently only latched (`web.ts:52,57-63`) and surfaced on the next `requirePage()`

**Downloads** (`packages/playwright/src/web.ts:266-271`)
- `cancelDownload` drops the map entry but leaves the Playwright `waitForEvent` pending until its own timeout

**Other**
- `displayValue` candidate set is `input, textarea, select` (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts:46`) — excludes `contenteditable`; for `<select>` it compares `value`, not the selected option's rendered text
- `runtime()` hardcodes `scale: 1` (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:786`) and never reads `deviceScaleFactor`
- `generic-secret` `inputPurpose` and "explicitly registered secure custom field" (`09-drivers.md:176-180`) have no mechanism; `read-node.ts:442-447` can only emit `none|username|password|one-time-code`
- Authorization/cookie header redaction for routes (`08-platforms.md:211`) has no code — currently satisfied only by accident

## Acceptance criteria
Each bullet gets a fix and a vector. Splitting this into sub-issues per bullet is fine.

title: Driver primitives ignore timeoutMs/signal; resolve/read/observe add hidden waits
body:
`spec/09-drivers.md:91` requires every operation to observe both `AbortSignal` and `timeoutMs`. Several do not.

## Spec
- `spec/09-drivers.md:91`, `spec/09-drivers.md:120`
- Conformance: `DRIVER-CANCEL-001`, `DRIVER-QUERY-002`

## Current behavior — ignores deadline/signal beyond an initial `guard` pre-check
- `packages/playwright/src/web.ts:272-286` — all keyboard/mouse operations
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:528-531` — `actions.press`
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:367-371` — `screen.swipe`
- `actions.tapPoint`
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:436-438` — `focus` on a handle-backed target ignores the deadline

## Current behavior — hidden waits where the spec requires immediacy
`resolve` and `read` are specified immediate (`08-platforms.md:97-99`, `09-drivers.md:120` "MUST NOT add hidden query retries"), but:
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:320-322` — `inputValue({ timeout: 1000 })` inside `resolve`'s displayValue filter
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:344-348` — `locator.evaluate(..., { timeout: min(op, 5000) })` inside `read`
- Playwright locators auto-wait for attachment throughout
- `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:634-638` — `observe` performs a bounded `waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` settle, a driver-side wait not sanctioned by `09-drivers.md:148-173`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every driver operation threads `signal` and `timeoutMs` to the underlying call
- [ ] `resolve` / `read` use `{ timeout: 0 }`-equivalent immediate semantics
- [ ] Remove the `observe` settle, or move it behind an explicit runner-owned wait
- [ ] Cancellation vector per primitive: abort mid-operation, assert prompt rejection and no later mutation

title: Firefox and WebKit are never exercised; WEB-BROWSER-001 is unverifiable
body:
`WEB-BROWSER-001` requires the same vectors to pass on pinned Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Only Chromium is ever launched.

## Spec
- `spec/07-scope.md:77-78`
- Conformance: `WEB-BROWSER-001`

## Current behavior
- All three engines are reachable at runtime (`packages/playwright/src/browser-pool.ts`, target parsing, config validation) and auto-install works
- But: `.github/workflows/spec.yml` installs `chromium` alone; every testbed config declares `browser: 'chromium'`; Firefox/WebKit appear only in unit config/CLI-parsing tests
- "Pinned" is only transitive via `playwright: "1.61.1"` in `packages/e2e/package.json`. No per-engine version pin, and the pinned versions are not recorded in report provenance.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CI matrix runs the web integration suite on chromium, firefox, webkit
- [ ] Per-engine versions recorded in `report.target` provenance
- [ ] `target.browserVersion` no longer `'unknown'` (see the provenance issue)
- [ ] Engine-specific failures triaged rather than skipped

title: verifyDriver and the driver conformance harness are unimplemented
body:
`verifyDriver` is the entry point for `SPI-VERIFY-001` and the whole "Conformance" section of `spec/09-drivers.md`. It throws.

## Spec
- `spec/09-drivers.md:266-299`
- `spec/00-conformance.md:80-97`
- Conformance: `SPI-VERIFY-001`, `CONFORMANCE-*`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:570-582` returns a rejected promise: *"verifyDriver is not implemented yet: the driver conformance harness lands with a later Phase 1 milestone"*
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/driver-spi.test.ts:67-70` asserts it rejects — the test pins the unimplemented state
- No code anywhere produces a `conformance-1` document; `spec/schema/conformance-v1.schema.json` and `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` have zero consumers
- `DriverConformanceReport` (`src/driver/index.ts:538-564`) omits the schema's optional `extensions` and narrows `profile` to three of ten values

## Depends on
The reference web application issue and the requirement-ID harness issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `verifyDriver` boots the versioned reference application and runs the `core-0.1` / `web-0.1` / `driver-1` vectors
- [ ] Emits a `conformance-1` document validating against `spec/schema/conformance-v1.schema.json`
- [ ] Every manifest ID for the claimed profile appears exactly once with `passed` or `failed`; unknown/missing/duplicate/skipped IDs fail the run
- [ ] `DriverConformanceReport` matches the schema's `profile` enum and `extensions`
- [ ] `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` is the single source of the ID set

title: State restore: dead expiry affordance, lossy INVALID_STATE translation, untranslated web errors
body:
State capture works, but the SPI's expiry affordance is unused and error translation hides real causes.

## Spec
- `spec/09-drivers.md:198-208`
- Conformance: `DRIVER-STATE-001`

## Current behavior — correct
- Required `web-0.1` stores captured: cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:579` `storageState({ indexedDB: true })`)
- Replace-not-merge satisfied structurally: `restoreState` closes the context and creates a fresh one seeded with the state (`session.ts:587-601`)
- Format/version rejection present (`session.ts:589-593`)

## Gaps
- `restoreState` leaves the session **page-less**; the next UI op yields `INVALID_STATE`. Fine for the launch-time path (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:361-367`), undefined mid-test.
- No `expiresAt` is ever set on captured state (`session.ts:580-584`), so the SPI's expiry affordance is dead.
- `storageState` is cast through `as unknown as string` (`session.ts:156`) — the type is a lie about a Playwright union.
- `packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts:186` blanket-translates `INVALID_STATE` → `APP_NOT_OPEN`, so "session is closed", "unknown download waiter", "unsupported state format", and "unhandled dialog" all surface as a not-open app.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:274-478` calls the driver without `translateDriverError`, so raw `DriverError` instances reach test code for web ops; they are only classified at the attempt boundary (`errors.ts:203-205`).
- `packages/playwright/src/index.ts:22-40` — `launch` has no guard against being called while a prior session of the same instance is open (`09-drivers.md:73-78` assumes serialization).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `restoreState` defines mid-test behavior (reopen or documented `INVALID_STATE`)
- [ ] `expiresAt` populated from the state's own cookie expiries
- [ ] Remove the `as unknown as string` cast
- [ ] `INVALID_STATE` translation preserves the distinguishing cause
- [ ] Web fixture methods translate driver errors at the call site
- [ ] `launch` rejects re-entrant use

title: Implementation-only driver constants and helpers are invisible to spec/api/driver.d.ts
body:
Two normative-looking constants and one exported helper exist only in the implementation, so third-party drivers cannot see them.

## Spec
- `spec/api/driver.d.ts` is canonical for `driver-1`
- `AGENTS.md`: any change to `src/driver/index.ts` or `spec/api/driver.d.ts` requires the same change in the other

## Current behavior — present in `src/`, absent from the spec file
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:82-83` — `OBSERVED_NAME_LIMIT = 256`, `OBSERVED_TEXT_LIMIT = 512`. These are per-field truncation bounds that every conforming driver must apply, but they are invisible from `spec/api/driver.d.ts`, so observation truncation is not portable.
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:585-591` — `isDriverHandle` is exported from `e2e/driver` but absent from the spec.
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:511-536` — `defineDriver` performs runtime validation and `Object.freeze` + brand; the spec declares only "type-checks and returns". Spec-consistent with `09-drivers.md:36-37` prose, but spec-file-invisible.
- `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:227-231` — `DriverError` **silently rewrites** an illegal `retryable: true` to `DRIVER_FAILURE`/`false`. Consistent with `09-drivers.md:258-261`, but it hides driver bugs; `packages/playwright/src/session.ts:716-722` documents a real case where it did.

The structural drift test (`packages/e2e/tests/contract/driver-spec-drift.ts`) compares 31 types and catches none of this.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Observation limits declared in `spec/api/driver.d.ts` and documented in `spec/09-drivers.md`
- [ ] `isDriverHandle` either added to the spec or unexported
- [ ] `defineDriver` runtime contract documented in `09-drivers.md`
- [ ] `DriverError` rewrite surfaces a warning in the report rather than silently correcting
- [ ] Drift test extended to cover exported const values, not only types

title: No finalizer registry: acquisitions have no per-scope LIFO cleanup
body:
`spec/11-lifecycle.md:303-307` requires a per-scope LIFO finalizer registry. None exists.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:303-307` — "Acquisitions register finalizers immediately. Finalizers execute once in LIFO order within their owning scope."
- Conformance: `RUNNER-ATTEMPT-001`, `RUNNER-HOOK-001`

## Current behavior
- No finalizer stack anywhere in `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`
- The only cleanup is ad hoc: `driverSession.close()` (`src/run/execute.ts:395`) and `appProcess.stop()` (`src/run/runner.ts:313`)
- Routes, dialog handlers, downloads, artifact recorders, and dynamic resources have **no** registered finalizer and no per-scope LIFO ordering

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scope-owned finalizer stack; acquisitions register immediately
- [ ] LIFO execution, exactly once, on every exit path including cancellation
- [ ] Routes, dialogs, downloads, artifacts, sessions all register
- [ ] Finalizer failure is a secondary error per `11-lifecycle.md:288`
- [ ] Vector: nested scopes with acquisitions in each; assert exact teardown order after a failure

title: Timeout cancellation cannot terminate non-cooperative test code
body:
Timeout cancellation is cooperative only. User code keeps running in the same process.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:162-168` — abort proxies, wait the cleanup grace, terminate the realm, mark cleanup `forced`
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:9-10` — an isolated JavaScript module/worker realm
- Conformance: `RUNNER-CANCEL-001`, `RUNNER-ATTEMPT-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:518-531` — `withTimeout` only races the promise; nothing terminates non-cooperative user code
- `record.cleanup` is never set to `'forced'` on timeout (only `'failed'` on close error, `execute.ts:404`); the sole `'forced'` producer is the crash synthesizer (`src/run/scheduler.ts:549`)
- The "realm" is a same-process re-import with a `?e2e=<n>` cache-buster (`src/run/realm.ts:63-71`, `src/config/load.ts:51-54`). The test module's own state is fresh; its transitive imports are shared, and there is nothing that can be terminated.
- `op()` defaults to a **non-aborting** signal for cleanup calls (`execute.ts:177`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Attempts execute in a terminable realm (worker thread or child process)
- [ ] On timeout: abort proxies → cleanup grace → terminate realm → `cleanup: 'forced'`
- [ ] Host-side finalizers still run and partial results are preserved after forced death
- [ ] Fault-injection vector: `while(true)` in a test still terminates and reports

title: Hook ordering is declaration-order-global; afterEach runs for non-entered scopes
body:
Hook ordering is global-declaration-order rather than scope-depth order, and `afterEach` runs for scopes that were never entered.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:132-142` — nested hook order
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:147` — entered-scope teardown only
- Conformance: `RUNNER-HOOK-001`

## Current behavior
- `packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts:74-79` filters `registration.hooks`, one flat array in global declaration order. A top-level `beforeEach` declared **after** a `describe` block therefore runs inner-before-outer.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:507` inherits this via `toReversed()` for `afterEach`.
- `execute.ts:507` also takes the whole chain's `afterEach` hooks unconditionally, so an inner-scope `afterEach` runs even when the outer `beforeEach` threw before that scope was entered.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Hooks ordered by scope depth (outer→inner for `before*`, inner→outer for `after*`), declaration order only within a scope
- [ ] `afterEach` runs only for scopes whose `beforeEach` completed
- [ ] Vectors: hook declared after a describe; outer `beforeEach` throws

title: Workers are not discarded between retries or after cleanup-infrastructure failure
body:
`spec/11-lifecycle.md:98-99` requires discarding the worker after a target failure, timeout, or unhandled exception. Retries reuse the same worker.

## Spec
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:98-99`
- `spec/11-lifecycle.md:288` — cleanup-infrastructure failure row
- Conformance: `RUNNER-ATTEMPT-001`, `RUNNER-RETRY-001`

## Current behavior
- Retries loop **inside** the worker: `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:240`, `src/run/retry.ts:33`. The scheduler only retires after the whole unit (`src/run/scheduler.ts:421,450`).
- Cleanup-infrastructure failure does not discard the worker either: `closeSession` records a secondary error and leaves `status: 'passed'` (`execute.ts:403-406`), so `sawFailure` stays false (`scheduler.ts:421`) and the worker is reused.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:248` silently forces `workers: 1` for the in-process transport regardless of resolved `config.workers`.
- No `internal` category handling and no abort path for the "internal invariant → abort run" row (`11-lifecycle.md:289`); see `src/run/retry.ts:13-18`.
- `MAX_INIT_FAILURES = 2` / `failTarget` (`src/run/scheduler.ts:55,558`) is a runner invention with no spec basis.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A failed/timed-out attempt retires its worker before the next attempt
- [ ] Cleanup-infrastructure failure retires the worker
- [ ] `internal` category aborts the run
- [ ] `MAX_INIT_FAILURES` either removed or specified
- [ ] In-process transport worker cap documented or removed

title: Selection and serial-group divergences: skipped-group records, closure provenance, option restrictions, CLI precedence
body:
Several selection and serial-group behaviors diverge from `spec/11-lifecycle.md`.

## Spec / conformance
`spec/11-lifecycle.md:46,51-57,64-65,88,273-275`; `RUNNER-COLLECT-001`, `RUNNER-SELECT-001`, `RUNNER-SERIAL-001`

## Findings

**Excluded serial groups produce no record** (`11-lifecycle.md:273-275` — one record, `status: skipped`, zero attempts, every member referencing it)
- `packages/e2e/src/run/units.ts:78-83` + `src/run/scheduler.ts:172` — `plan.immediate` emits `nonRunResult` only; no `onSerialGroup`, and member results carry no `serialGroupId`

**No provenance for closure-included members** (`11-lifecycle.md:88`)
- `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts:294-296` reinstates `disposition: 'run'` and **erases** `skip`; nothing survives to the report

**Serial-group option restrictions are stricter than the spec** (`11-lifecycle.md:64-65` makes only `retries` a collection error)
- `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts:218-225` also rejects `session`, `platforms`, `requires`, `skip`, and `only`, so `test.skip(...)` inside a `serial: true` describe is an unauthorized hard collection error

**Top-level await in a test module is not detected** (`11-lifecycle.md:46`)
- Nothing in `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts` checks for it

**Registration synchrony is only partly enforced** (`11-lifecycle.md:30-32`)
- `Collector.assertOpen` (`registry.ts:75-81`) catches registration after module evaluation closes, but a microtask continuation resolving during the same `await load()` window still registers

**CLI `--retries` is beatable by a declaration** (`11-lifecycle.md:51-57` — CLI is highest)
- `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:162` folds `cli.retries` into `config.retries`, then `src/collect/select.ts:79` lets a test/group `retries` override it

**File-filtered tests vanish from the report**
- `packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts:129-132` filters before import, unlike tag/`only` filtering which reports `filtered`

**Setup option hygiene is type-only**
- `SetupOptions` omits `session`/`only`/`skip` (`src/types.ts:604`) but `registry.ts:322` spreads `rest` unvalidated at runtime

**Session restore is not a top-level step** (`spec/10-determinism.md:22`)
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:366` calls `restoreState` raw; `session.save` **is** a step (`src/run/fixtures.ts:173`)

## Acceptance criteria
One vector per bullet. Splitting into sub-issues is fine.

title: Config: unknown keys accepted on targets/credentials/app.command; capability checks missing or late
body:
`spec/05-config.md:4` says unknown keys are errors, but only five objects are closed.

## Spec
- `spec/05-config.md:4,110-111,126-130`
- Conformance: `RUNNER-CONFIG-001`, `RUNNER-CONFIG-003`

## Currently closed
top level (`src/config/resolve.ts:140-144`), `app` (`:247-254`), `agent` (`src/config/agent.ts:140-144`), `limits` (`agent.ts:187-191`), `agent.model` (`agent.ts:272-276`)

## Currently open / unvalidated
- `app.command` — `src/config/resolve.ts:302-307` checks only `executable`
- **target objects** — `src/config/resolve.ts:344-391` accepts arbitrary extra keys on `WebTarget`
- `credentials.*` entries — `src/config/resolve.ts:426-436`
- `command.startupTimeout` / `shutdownTimeout` / `args` / `cwd` / `env` — unvalidated, used raw at `src/run/app-process.ts:40,78,29-30`
- `app.readyUrl` — entirely unvalidated (`resolve.ts:311`); see the network-policy issue

## Capability validation gaps (`05-config.md:126-130`, "fails before launch"/"before collection")
- Driver **platform** never checked: `src/run/resolve-driver.ts:12-15` returns the driver without comparing `driver.platforms` to `target.platform`; `validateDriver` (`src/run/runner.ts:336-354`) checks only `spiVersion` and artifacts
- Driver **state capability** never checked for selected setups / session consumers — no check outside reporting (`runner.ts:365`)
- Artifact capability validation happens **after** collection (`runner.ts:182` collects, `runner.ts:214-220` validates)

## Glob grammar (`05-config.md:79-80`)
`src/internal/globs.ts` is largely correct (`!` rejected `:23`, `**`-inside-segment rejected `:28`, code-point sort `:96`, no directory-symlink following `:108`), but braces/extglobs are silently treated as literals rather than rejected, and `node_modules` is hard-skipped (`:109`), which the spec does not sanction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every config object rejects unknown keys
- [ ] Command timeouts/args/cwd/env validated
- [ ] Driver platform + state capability validated before collection
- [ ] Artifact capability validated before collection
- [ ] Unsupported glob syntax rejected explicitly; `node_modules` skip specified or removed

title: CLI: bound bypasses, scoped interrupt handling, exit-code precedence, dead config.reporters, non-atomic init
body:
Several CLI behaviors diverge from `spec/06-cli.md`.

## Spec / conformance
`spec/06-cli.md:8,88,105-111`; `spec/05-config.md:110,112`; `spec/13-reporting.md:153`; `RUNNER-CLI-001`

## Findings

**Bound bypasses**
- `--workers 0` is accepted: `parsePositiveInt` (misnamed) allows `0` (`src/cli/index.ts:9`), and `cli.workers` bypasses the 1–1024 bound (`src/config/resolve.ts:163-166`) → a zero-worker run. Spec: workers ≥ 1.
- `--retries` accepts any nonnegative safe integer, bypassing the 0–10 bound (`src/cli/index.ts:55` + `resolve.ts:162`).

**Interrupt handling is scoped to the scheduler only**
- Handlers installed at `src/run/runner.ts:238-239`, removed at `:301-302`. An interrupt during config load, app start, browser install, collection, driver pre-flight, or report write is unhandled → default kill, no `status: interrupted` partial report, no exit 130.

**Exit-code precedence**
- Report-write failure does not affect the exit code: `src/run/runner.ts:114-119` pushes a `report`-phase error *after* `exitCode` was chosen. Spec: report write failure is infrastructure, exit 3.
- Serial-group infrastructure failures collapse to exit 1: `resultExitCodes` (`runner.ts:369-388`) inspects only `result.attempts`, which is empty for serial members (`src/report/build.ts:352`, `src/run/serial.ts:122-137`).

**No report on config-load failure**
- `runner.ts:111` guards report writing on `config !== undefined`. A `--config` typo produces exit 2 with no `.e2e/report.json`, contradicting "every run writes report-1".

**`config.reporters` is dead**
- `rg '\.reporters' packages/e2e/src` → assignment at `src/config/resolve.ts:174` and three reads of `options.reporters` (CLI) at `src/run/runner.ts:85,122,142`. `reporters: ['json']` in `e2e.config.ts` still prints the list reporter and never emits JSON; `reporters: []` still prints list.

**`e2e init` makes partial changes after a conflict** (`06-cli.md:8`)
- `src/cli/init.ts:43-52` warns, then falls through to `:67-73` and creates the remaining files plus mutates `.gitignore`

**`--artifacts` is not contained**
- `runner.ts:390-393` resolves it without a project-root containment check, and the report lands in `dirname(artifactsRoot)` (`:113`) — for `--artifacts out` that is the project root, not `.e2e/`

## Acceptance criteria
One vector per bullet.

title: report-1 provenance uses fallbacks and constants instead of measured values
body:
`report-1` provenance is filled with fallbacks and constants where `spec/13-reporting.md` requires measured values.

## Spec
- `spec/13-reporting.md:51-54,60-65`
- `spec/09-drivers.md:100-102`
- Conformance: `REPORT-PROVENANCE-001`

## Current behavior
- `target.browserVersion` is `'unknown'`: `src/run/runner.ts:356` never queries the launched browser and `src/report/build.ts:366` falls back. The driver **does** return engine+version correctly (`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:782-785`) — `runtime()` is simply never called after launch, only after `setViewport`.
- `target.viewport` is guessed `1280x720@1` from config (`runner.ts:357-361`, `build.ts:367-371`) rather than read from the runtime.
- `driver` provenance falls back to `{ id: 'playwright', version: 'unknown', spiVersion: 1 }` (`build.ts:376`); `capabilities`/`artifactCapabilities`/`stateCapability` fall back to `['web']` / `['screenshot','trace']` / `true` (`build.ts:377-379`).
- Config digest (`src/config/resolve.ts:447-505`) correctly maps secrets/env/handles, but paths are **not** normalized relative to the project root and the digest is taken over the **raw** config rather than the **resolved** config (`13-reporting.md:60-65`).
- `usage.reportBytes` hardcoded `0` (`build.ts:451`); `usage.maxTerminalFieldBytes` hardcoded `0` (`build.ts:445`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `runtime()` queried immediately after launch; engine/version/viewport/scale recorded
- [ ] Driver provenance always real; fallbacks removed (absence is a bug, not a default)
- [ ] Config digest computed over the resolved config with project-relative paths
- [ ] `usage.*` measured

title: No requirement-ID harness: all 86 conformance IDs have zero mapped coverage
body:
No file anywhere in `packages/**` reads `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json`, and no test references any requirement ID.

## Spec
- `spec/15-conformance-matrix.md` — every manifest entry is REQUIRED; a report must contain every ID assigned to its profile exactly once
- `spec/00-conformance.md:80-97`
- `PLAN.md:135` — "Conformance tests land with each behavior, not after implementation"

## Current coverage: zero, for all 10 profiles / 86 IDs
`sdk-0.1` (6), `runner-0.1` (20), `core-0.1` (10), `web-0.1` (13), `driver-1` (8), `agent-protocol-1` (7), `report-1` (7), `cache-1` (6), `session-1` (5), `conformance-1` (4).

Indirect substitutes only:
- `pnpm check:spec` approximates `SDK-TYPES-001`/`004`
- `packages/e2e/tests/contract/driver-spec-drift.ts` is a structural drift gate, not a vector

## Proposal
A thin annotation layer so vectors declare the IDs they cover, plus a completeness gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests declare requirement IDs (e.g. `requires('RUNNER-HOOK-001')` or a title convention)
- [ ] A harness reads `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` and emits a `conformance-1` document
- [ ] Unknown, missing, duplicate, or skipped IDs fail the run (`CONFORMANCE-COMPLETE-001`)
- [ ] Overall status derived from requirement results (`CONFORMANCE-STATUS-001`)
- [ ] A coverage report shows which IDs are still unclaimed, so contributors can pick one
- [ ] CI job runs it and uploads the document

title: Five of seven canonical schemas are never validated; invalid fixtures are never asserted rejected
body:
Five of seven canonical schemas are never loaded by any test, and no test asserts that an `*.invalid.json` fixture is rejected.

## Spec
- `spec/README.md:39-47` — canonical wire schemas
- Conformance: `SESSION-SCHEMA-001`, `AGENT-TOOL-001`, `AGENT-TOOL-006`, `AGENT-TOOL-007`, `CONFORMANCE-SCHEMA-001`

## Current state
| Schema | Validated | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `report-v1` | yes | `tests/helpers/report-schema.ts` |
| `cache-v1` | yes | `tests/helpers/cache-schema.ts` |
| `session-v1` | **no** | — (and see the `A256GCM` bug) |
| `agent-locate-v1` | **no** | `src/agent/protocol.ts` hand-rolls the grammar |
| `agent-judgment-v1` | **no** | same |
| `agent-tool-v1` | **no** | never referenced outside `spec/` |
| `conformance-v1` | **no** | no producer |

Unused canonical fixtures (dead evidence): `report-v1.{valid,invalid}.json`, `session-v1.{valid,invalid}.json`, `conformance-v1.{valid,invalid}.json`, all four `agent-locate-v1.*`, `agent-tool-v1.*`, `agent-judgment-v1.*`, `evidence/sdk.txt`.

There is also **no negative test**: a schema could be vacuously permissive and nothing would fail.

Additionally, `report-v1`/`cache-v1` validation happens only as a side effect of integration tests — a run that skips those tests loses the gate entirely.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Standalone `schemas` test project that validates every `spec/schema/fixtures/*.valid.json` against its schema
- [ ] …and asserts every `*.invalid.json` is **rejected**
- [ ] Live-output validation for `session-1`, `agent-locate-1`, `agent-judgment-1`, `agent-tool-1`
- [ ] Runs as its own CI step, independent of integration tests

title: No versioned reference web application for conformance
body:
`spec/00-conformance.md:89` requires "the reference web application and fixture suite maintained with the specification". It does not exist.

## Spec
- `spec/00-conformance.md:89`
- `spec/09-drivers.md:285` — `verifyDriver` boots the **versioned** reference application
- `PLAN.md:43`

## What exists instead
Three unrelated ad-hoc apps:
- `packages/testbed/app/server.mjs` (491 lines) — dogfood playground on `127.0.0.1:4271`
- `packages/e2e/tests/helpers/fixture-app.ts`

None is versioned, published, addressable by `verifyDriver`, digest-pinned, or maintained with the spec. The testbed is `private: true` and lives in `packages/`, not `spec/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One reference application with a version identifier, maintained alongside the spec
- [ ] Covers the surfaces the vectors need: ARIA landmark set, secure fields, frames, dialogs, downloads, routes, storage, scroll containers, hostile text

title: Add an sdk-spec-drift contract test (types.ts vs spec/api/e2e.d.ts)
body:
`packages/e2e/src/types.ts` is currently a byte-faithful mirror of `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`, but nothing enforces that.

## Spec
- `AGENTS.md`: the driver drift test exists precisely because "any change to either requires the same change in the other"
- Conformance: `SDK-TYPES-001`, `SDK-TYPES-005`, `SDK-TYPES-006`

## Current state
- `packages/e2e/tests/contract/driver-spec-drift.ts` + `tsconfig.driver-drift.json` guard `driver-1` only
- `sdk-0.1` has **no** equivalent. A structural diff today shows only whitespace differences, so the guard can be added cheaply — before it drifts.

## Related divergence to fix while here
`packages/e2e/src/agent/error.ts:39` declares `AgentError extends E2EError`, but `spec/api/e2e.d.ts:177` declares `extends Error` and `E2EError` is **not exported** from `src/index.ts`. The emitted public `.d.ts` therefore references an unnameable base and leaks non-spec public members (`category`, and a public 3-arg constructor absent from the spec).

## Acceptance criteria

title: No reference semantic report validator (REPORT-SEMANTIC-001)
body:
`spec/13-reporting.md:156-172` requires a reference semantic validator. Only Ajv schema validation exists, in test helpers.

## Spec
- `spec/13-reporting.md:156-172`
- `spec/14-security.md:200-201`
- Conformance: `REPORT-SEMANTIC-001`, `REPORT-HOSTILE-001`, `REPORT-PARTIAL-001`

- Nothing recomputes identity, order, status, summary, references, or usage

title: SDK surface divergences: displayValue chaining, getAttribute allowlist, isVisible, ambiguity messages, assert screenshots
body:
Smaller SDK-surface divergences found during the spec audit. Each is small and independently pickable.

## Findings

**`getByDisplayValue()` cannot be chained**
`spec/api/e2e.d.ts:338` — `Locator extends Screen`, so every locator is a query scope. `packages/playwright/src/locators.ts:103-110` (`requireSingle`) throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` when a display-value projection is used as a scope or inside `filter({has})`.

**`locator.getAttribute` is allowlist-limited**
`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:328-331` reads `node.attributes`, populated only for `[testIdAttribute, 'type', 'autocomplete', 'href', 'role']` + `aria-*` (`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts:131,145,451`). Arbitrary attributes silently return `null`. Also `readGuarded(true)` (`screen.ts:407-416`) blocks **every** attribute on a secure node, while `spec/08-platforms.md:123` restricts only *value-bearing* attributes.

**`locator.isVisible()` on zero matches returns `false`**
`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:333-335,418-422` uses `Deadline(0)`, but `spec/08-platforms.md:82` says direct single-node reads *fail immediately* with zero matches. `textContent`/`inputValue`/`getAttribute` do fail correctly via `engine.read`.

**Ambiguity failure message loses the match count**
`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:98,116` reports `match count 0` because `assertSingle` throws out of `tryRead` before `lastSample` is updated. `spec/03-assertions.md:27` requires the final match count.

**`agent.assert` captures a screenshot on success**
`packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts:601-603` captures unless `screenshot: false`, spending a driver capture on passing assertions. `spec/03-assertions.md:60-62` scopes the redacted screenshot to the failure report.

**`agent.dragTo` is impossible for agent-observed nodes**
`packages/playwright/src/session.ts:460-467` → `unsupportedDrag()` (`support.ts:68-72`) whenever either node is observation- or handle-backed.

**Diff formatting is unpinned**
`spec/03-assertions.md:69` pins equality **and diff formatting** to `@vitest/expect` 4.1.10. `packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts:11-23` implements its own `format()`; only `equals`/`iterableEquality` are borrowed (`values.ts:3`).

**`toBeDefined` internal spec conflict**
`packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts:91-97` requires non-null **and** non-undefined per `spec/api/e2e.d.ts:725`, but `@vitest/expect` (pinned by `03-assertions.md:69`) passes `expect(null).toBeDefined()`. The spec contradicts itself; pick one and amend the other.

**Stale code comment**
`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:91-94` asserts "the store's own per-key lock", which does not exist and which `spec/10-determinism.md:316-318` explicitly says is not required (`packages/e2e/src/cache/store.ts:9-11`).

## Acceptance criteria
One fix + one vector per bullet. Sub-issues welcome.

title: Stale status prose: 'No implementation exists yet' and cache claims
body:
Status prose in two places is now false. `AGENTS.md` explicitly asks contributors to fix stale prose when they find it.

## Findings

**`spec/README.md:6`** — *"Status: frozen implementation contract. No implementation exists yet."*
Flatly false: `packages/e2e` (v0.1.0, publishable, CLI bin) and `packages/playwright` (v0.1.0) both exist and are exercised by CI.

**`packages/e2e/README.md:25-28`** — *"Not implemented yet: … locate/path caches (`cache-1`; every agent step reports `cache: bypassed`)"*
Stale for locate caching: `src/cache/{entry,fingerprint,identity,locator,store,index}.ts` and `src/agent/locate-cache.ts` exist, and cache-1 documents are schema-validated (`tests/unit/cache-store.test.ts:81`) and integration-tested (`tests/integration/agent-cache.test.ts`). Path caching **is** still absent, so the sentence needs splitting rather than deleting.

The rest of that list is accurate and should stay: planning tier, HTML reporter, video artifacts, step source locations, mobile targets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `spec/README.md` status reflects reality and points at the conformance coverage report
- [ ] `packages/e2e/README.md` distinguishes locate cache (landed) from path cache (not landed)
- [ ] Ideally the status list is generated from the conformance harness so it cannot drift again

---
*Correction: an earlier revision of this issue claimed the manifest was linked as `conformance/n.json` in three places. That is wrong — `spec/00-conformance.md:16`, `spec/README.md:51`, and `spec/15-conformance-matrix.md:3` all link `conformance/v0-requirements.json` correctly. No link fix is needed.*

title: Seven spec areas have no docs page; the public driver SPI is undocumented
body:
Seven spec areas have no corresponding docs page. `AGENTS.md` requires behavior changes to update the matching `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` in the same change, but there is nowhere to put several of these.

## Present (20 pages, all wired in `fern/docs.yml`)
`introduction`, `quickstart`, `writing-tests`, `agents`, `authentication`, `web`, `running-tests`, `configuration`, `ci`, `from-playwright`, `troubleshooting`, and `reference/{test,expect,screen,app-web,agent,config,cli,errors}`

| Spec | Gap |
|---|---|
