title: release.yml publishes without running the test suite
body:
`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `pnpm run check` (lint → check:spec → typecheck → docs:check) and then publishes. **It never runs `pnpm test`.**

## Current state
- `spec.yml` (PR + push to main) runs the full test suite — good
- `release.yml` gates publication on lint/typecheck/docs only
- So a release can ship with a red test suite if `main` went red between the merge gate and the release run

Related CI gaps, tracked separately but worth listing here:
- Firefox/WebKit never launched (see the browser-coverage issue)
- No conformance job (see the requirement-ID harness issue)
- No standalone schema-validation job (see the schema-validation issue)
- No fault-injection job for `07-scope.md:79-81`: forced realm termination, partial launch rollback, commit ambiguity, session corruption, hostile report/cache documents
- `test:agent` / `test:wakacje` / `test:public` are in no workflow, so `agent-protocol-1` is never verified against a real model — only `tests/helpers/fake-model.ts`
- Nothing detects a `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` or `spec/schema/*` change landing without matching suite-version and report changes (`15-conformance-matrix.md:37`)
- Nothing tracks the `07-scope.md:90` release gate (100 consecutive gating runs over 14 days)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `release.yml` runs `pnpm test` before publishing
- [ ] A scheduled workflow runs the agent suites against a real model with a repo secret
- [ ] A manifest-coupling check fails a PR that edits `v0-requirements.json` or `spec/schema/*` without touching the suite version

title: Spec conformance gap audit: tracking issue for v0
body:
Full audit of `spec/` against `packages/e2e` and `packages/playwright`, mapped to `PLAN.md` phases and `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json`.

**Headline:** the deterministic web runner is substantially built and largely correct. The three things that block a v0 claim are the **planning tier** (`agent.act` / `agent.login` throw), the **conformance harness** (zero of 86 required IDs have mapped coverage), and a set of **security fail-open gaps** (redirects, traces, secret sinks).

`spec/examples/**` is currently unrunnable end to end: 1 of 10 example tests executes, and only after removing `video` and the `member` session.

---

## P0 — blocks a v0 conformance claim

Correctness bugs
- #23 `afterAll` is skipped when a test fails or times out
- #24 Session envelope `algorithm` is `aes-256-gcm`; `session-v1` requires `A256GCM`
- #27 `report-1` step and error `source` locations are fabricated
- #29 `ArtifactRecord.redaction` enum mismatches `report-v1` and is hardcoded
- #47 `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED` is never raised
- #55 No finalizer registry
- #56 Timeout cancellation cannot terminate non-cooperative test code

Security fail-open
- #25 `locator.fill(secret)` bypasses all secret authorization
- #28 Artifact paths are not contained, canonicalized, or symlink-checked
- #39 Origin policy is not re-validated after redirects; popups unchecked
- #40 Incomplete scheme denylist; no link-local / metadata / DNS-rebinding policy
- #41 No trace filtering; `app.screenshot` neither masked nor taint-gated

Missing surfaces
- #31 Implement `agent.act`
- #32 Implement `agent.login`
- #33 `agent-tool-1` has no runner-side parser or authorizer
- #26 Reference driver does not support the `video` artifact
- #30 HTML reporter is a default reporter with no implementation

Conformance
- #63 No requirement-ID harness: all 86 IDs unmapped
- #64 Five of seven canonical schemas never validated

## P1 — required for v0

- #34 `cache-1` path entries neither produced nor consumed
- #35 Prompt fences breakable by untrusted text
- #36 Redaction is observation-only; ledger budget excludes the omission line
- #37 Production opt-in does not block raw-coordinate actions
- #38 `agent.scrollTo` under `vision:'only'` fails with the wrong code
- #42 SPI exposes no frame origin, so frame policy fails open
- #43 Credential resolution: no env-only source, no normalization, no pair validation
- #44 Nine resolved limits reported but never enforced
- #45 Session store has no lease lock, maintenance lock, or scavenging
- #48 Observation ARIA/accname diverges from the deterministic path
- #49 Web profile gaps: scroll/swipe, frame cardinality, `route.continue`, evaluate, dialogs, downloads
- #50 Driver primitives ignore `timeoutMs`/`signal`; hidden waits in `resolve`/`read`/`observe`
- #51 Firefox and WebKit never exercised
- #52 `verifyDriver` and the driver conformance harness unimplemented
- #57 Hook ordering is declaration-order-global
- #58 Workers not discarded between retries
- #59 Selection and serial-group divergences
- #60 Config: unknown keys accepted; capability checks missing or late
- #61 CLI: bound bypasses, scoped interrupts, exit-code precedence, dead `config.reporters`
- #62 `report-1` provenance uses fallbacks instead of measured values
- #65 No versioned reference web application
- #66 Add an `sdk-spec-drift` contract test
- #67 No reference semantic report validator
- #72 `release.yml` publishes without running the test suite

## P2 — improvements

- #46 Trust notice and pre-first-use model disclosure never emitted
- #53 State restore: dead expiry affordance, lossy `INVALID_STATE` translation
- #54 Implementation-only driver constants invisible to `spec/api/driver.d.ts`
- #68 SDK surface divergences (`displayValue` chaining, `getAttribute` allowlist, `isVisible`, ambiguity messages)
- #69 Stale status prose and broken manifest links
- #70 Seven spec areas have no docs page; driver SPI undocumented
- #71 The "named migration fixture suite" does not exist

## Already open, still valid
#8 `fullyParallel` scheduling · #14 viewport-scoped observations · #15 agent overlay · #16 overlay isolation

Note on #8: `fullyParallel` appears **nowhere** in `spec/`. It is a proposed addition, not a spec gap — per `PLAN.md:112` it needs a spec change first.

---

## Suggested pick-up order

1. **Unblock the examples** — #26, #43, #32, #31. Until these land, the canonical examples cannot serve as a regression suite.
2. **Close the security fail-opens** — #25, #39, #40, #41, #28. Each is small, self-contained, and testable.
3. **Make conformance measurable** — #64 then #63. #64 is a few hours and immediately catches #24.
4. **Everything else**, in whatever order.

Good first issues: #66, #69, #72, #64.

## Where the audit found the codebase already correct
Worth stating so nobody re-does it: cache-1 identity and locate replay, session crypto and binding, glob grammar, stable ID encoding, serial-group state sharing and retry-from-member-one, scheduler worker accounting, exit-code combination, assertion matcher set and negation grace window, `agent.extract` Standard Schema validation, closed locate/judgment grammars with observation grounding.

title: chore: release packages under the beta dist-tag
body: Follow-up to #20, which landed the changesets pipeline. This finishes the release setup so the first publish is not embarrassing. ## Beta channel The root `release` script now runs `changeset publish --tag beta`, so releases land on the `beta` dist-tag and npm's `latest` is never moved while the surface stabilizes. Two findings worth recording, both verified locally rather than assumed: - **`publishConfig.tag` is not enough.** `pnpm publish --dry-run` reports `with tag latest` even with `"tag": "beta"` set. The explicit `--tag` flag is the only thing that works, so that is where the setting lives. - **Changesets pre mode is the wrong tool here.** `changeset pre enter beta` produces `0.2.0-beta.0` for `e2e`, and a prerelease version does not satisfy the driver's `e2e` peer range (`>=0.1.0 <1`) under semver's prerelease rule. `onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange` then sees the peer as out of range and bumps `@e2edev/playwright` to `1.0.0-beta.0`, rewriting its peer range to `>=0.2.0-beta.0` and dropping the upper bound — exactly the failure mode AGENTS.md warns about. Plain 0.x versions on the `beta` tag keep both packages at `0.2.0` with the peer range intact. ## Registry metadata Both published packages gain `repository` (with `directory`), `homepage`, `bugs`, `keywords`, `contributors`, and `publishConfig` with `provenance`. Added the MIT `LICENSE` file that `"license": "MIT"` already claimed, at the root and in each package, so it ships in the tarball. Changelogs now go through `@changesets/changelog-github`, which adds PR links and contributor credits. ## Docs New `CONTRIBUTING.md`: dev loop, commit convention, when a changeset is required, how a release happens, and how to go stable (drop `--tag beta`). `README.md` gains a Releases section, and `AGENTS.md` records both findings above. ## How to test ```sh pnpm install pnpm lint pnpm exec changeset status # both packages minor, no phantom major pnpm --filter e2e run build cd packages/e2e && pnpm publish --dry-run --no-git-checks --tag beta ``` The dry run should report `with tag beta` and list `LICENSE` in the tarball. Running `changeset version` locally (then reverting) produces `e2e@0.2.0` and `@e2edev/playwright@0.2.0` with the peer range still `>=0.1.0 <1`. Note the release workflow needs an `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret, and Actions must be allowed to create pull requests. ---

title: fix: retry transient model provider failures up to five times
body: Rate limits and short 5xx bursts from the model provider were the dominant cause of spurious agent-step failures. The adapter left `maxRetries` at the AI SDK default of 2. ## Changes - **Transport retries per model call: 2 -> 5** (`src/agent/model/sdk.ts`). Only failures the provider marked retryable are retried, `retry-after` is honored ahead of the SDK's exponential backoff, and `timeout: call.timeoutMs` is merged into the signal the retry loop waits on — so the remaining step deadline, not the attempt count, bounds the whole chain. A healthy provider is unaffected. - **An exhausted chain now reports the failure that actually happened.** The SDK wraps it in `RetryError`, whose message names the retry *reason*, so `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` was surfacing the wrapper and skipping the `APICallError` branch. `translateModelError` unwraps to `lastError`, except for `reason: 'abort'`, which stays wrapped so a chain cut short by the deadline still classifies as `STEP_TIMEOUT`. This ports the transport half of the retry setup we run in tester-army. The other half there — retrying schema-invalid output with the previous attempt's issues fed back into the prompt — already exists here as the repair rounds in `AgentInvocation.ask`, bounded by `maxModelCalls` and the deadline. Not included: tester-army's gateway `fallbackModels` routing. That is model selection config, not retries; separate change if we want it. ## Tests Two cases in `tests/unit/agent-config.test.ts` drive a scripted failing model instance through the public adapter: - a permanent (`isRetryable: false`) provider failure is attempted once; - a retryable one is attempted 6 times and surfaces the provider's message, not the wrapper. Fake timers, so no real backoff wait. `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` pass. Docs row for `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` and a changeset included. ---

title: ci: gate releases on the test suite and schedule the agent suites
body: Fixes #72. `release.yml` gated publication on `pnpm run check` (lint → check:spec → typecheck → docs:check) only, so a release could ship from a `main` that went red between the merge gate and the release run. Closes the three acceptance criteria from the issue. ## Changes **`release.yml` runs the tests before publishing.** Adds the Chromium install, `pnpm test`, and the testbed run — the same steps `spec.yml` uses. The publish job now re-runs the whole gate instead of trusting the merge gate. **`agent.yml` (new) runs the agent suites against a real model.** Weekly cron plus `workflow_dispatch`; these suites are the only thing that exercises `agent-protocol-1` against a real provider instead of `tests/helpers/fake-model.ts`. - Matrix: `test:agent` (blocking — the playground is deterministic, so a failure is ours) and `test:wakacje` (`continue-on-error` — a live third-party site that changes and rate-limits under us). - A `plan` job resolves the matrix so a manual run can pick one suite (`all` | `agent` | `wakacje`); unselected suites never start, so the checks list reflects what ran. - Fails with a readable annotation when `secrets.E2E_MODEL_API_KEY` is unset, rather than surfacing `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` once per fixture. - Optional `model` input overrides `E2E_MODEL`. Passed through an env var and left unset when empty, because the configs treat `''` as a configured model id. - Uploads `packages/testbed/.e2e/report.{json,html}`: the only durable evidence of a model-dependent run. **`pnpm check:manifest` couples schema edits to the suite version.** `scripts/check-manifest-coupling.mjs` diffs the merge base against the working tree; if `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` or any `spec/schema/*` file changed, `suiteVersion` must differ. Implementations key their conformance reports to that version, so a silent edit makes existing reports claim conformance to requirements they were never run against (`spec/15-conformance-matrix.md:35-37`). Runs as its own PR job in `spec.yml` because it needs `fetch-depth: 0` for a merge base. Docs updated in the same change: `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the coupling rule, and `AGENTS.md` loses its now-stale claim that the agent suites never run in CI. Out of scope, still tracked by #72: Firefox/WebKit coverage, the conformance job, a standalone schema-validation job, fault injection for `07-scope.md:79-81`, and the `07-scope.md:90` release-gate counter. No changeset: nothing here is user-visible. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm run check` green - [x] `pnpm test` — 623 tests passing - [x] `pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test` — 33 passing; confirms the steps added to `release.yml` and the report path the artifact upload uses - [x] `actionlint` clean on all four workflows, all pinned by SHA - [x] `check-manifest-coupling.mjs` exercised in all three states: no coupled change → pass, schema edit without a bump → exit 1, same edit with a `suiteVersion` bump → pass - [x] suite selection verified for `''` (schedule), `all`, `agent`, `wakacje`, and an unknown value → exit 1 - [ ] `agent.yml` end to end — needs the `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY` repo secret; dispatch it once after merge ---

title: fix: emit A256GCM as the session envelope algorithm
body: Fixes #24. Every session envelope this runner wrote was rejected by the frozen `session-v1` schema: `state.algorithm` is `{ "const": "A256GCM" }` (`spec/schema/session-v1.schema.json:34`, `SESSION-SCHEMA-001`), but `sessions.ts` wrote Node's cipher id `aes-256-gcm`. ## Changes **`src/run/sessions.ts:35,149` writes the JWA name `A256GCM`.** The encryption is untouched — `createCipheriv`/`createDecipheriv` still take `'aes-256-gcm'`, which is Node's identifier for the same AES-256-GCM. Only the wire literal changes. Since the envelope-minus-ciphertext is the GCM AAD, `save` and `load` have to agree on it; the round-trip test below pins that. **Nothing validated a produced envelope against the schema**, which is why the drift went unnoticed — only `tests/helpers/report-schema.ts` and `cache-schema.ts` existed. Adds `tests/helpers/session-schema.ts`, mirroring `report-schema.ts` and exposing `isValidSessionEnvelope` / `specFixture` the way `cache-schema.ts` does, so a rejection can be asserted without a throw. **`tests/unit/session-envelope.test.ts`** drives a real `SessionStore.create(...).save(...)` into a `mkdtemp` directory, reads the file back off disk, and Ajv-validates the actual bytes rather than a hand-built object. Four cases: the produced envelope is schema-valid and carries `A256GCM`; it round-trips through `load`; `session-v1.valid.json` is accepted; `session-v1.invalid.json` is rejected. Compat: an envelope written by an earlier version will not load under this one. Sessions are per-run and the key lives only in memory, so nothing survives a run to be broken. Noted in the changeset (patch). No docs change — no page in `fern/docs/pages` documents the wire algorithm; the canonical statement is the schema itself, which was already correct. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm check` green (lint -> check:spec -> typecheck -> docs:check) - [x] `pnpm test` — 608 + 19 tests passing - [x] Reverting the one-line fix fails the new test, so the guard actually bites ---

title: feat: locate nodes no query can name, and widen what an observation sees
body: The playground app can only pose the problems it was written to pose. This points the runner at [seleniumbase.io](https://seleniumbase.io), the practice site the Selenium community uses for the awkward parts of the web, and fixes what that exposed. Two opt-in configs drive the same pages **deterministically and agentically**, which is the point: a gap in one tier is only distinguishable from a gap in the other if both are pointed at the same page. Neither runs in CI. ## What it found `deriveQueries` returns nothing for a node with no accessible name, test id, placeholder, or text — an unlabelled input whose only description is the table cell beside it. `resolveSelected` threw on that **before the loop**, skipping `addressByReference` 120 lines below, which needs no query at all. So the agent tier failed hardest on exactly the controls that have no deterministic address either. **8 of 10 agentic failures were that one guard clause.** The model had already selected the right node; the runner discarded it. ## What changed **The locate sweep falls through** instead of throwing. Two rungs, in order: 1. the driver's **platform selector** for the node, when it has an anchored one — recorded as the new `locate.selector` policy decision. This is the same construction `locate-cache.ts` already used for replay, so a selector trusted to re-find a node on a *later* run is now trusted on *this* one, and the located node is a real locator: cacheable, and usable by `dragTo`. 2. the observation's **reference** to the element. Both re-read the live node and require its recorded identity before acting, so a stale selection is still a miss rather than a blind dispatch. `poll: false` keeps its early exit for escalation. I left `id` out of the driver's anchoring attributes. The existing rationale holds — a framework that mints ids per render makes every stored selector single-use — so rung 1 fires for a test id or a form `name`, and rung 2 covers the rest. **Three observation gaps** close alongside it: - **Open shadow roots are walked.** A control that exists only in a shadow tree is now selectable. Slotted content is not double-counted: slotted elements are light-DOM children, and the shadow tree holds `` placeholders rather than copies. A closed root stays invisible, as it is to a person. - **`data:` documents are admitted.** Same trust class as `about:blank` and `about:srcdoc` — written by the embedding page, no network origin for an allowlist to match. Refusing them excluded the app's own inline frames rather than any third party. - **Empty painted rectangles are observed** with the role `box`: no children, no text, no role, no name, but a border, outline, or background of its own, and at least 12 CSS pixels a side. A drop zone, a swatch, a chart placeholder — the element class *defined* by being empty. An unpainted spacer of the same size stays out, because a person cannot see it either. **`dragTo` no longer requires a locator on both sides.** `Locator.dragTo` takes two locators, so a reference-backed destination made the verb unavailable for precisely the elements above. When either endpoint is reference-backed the driver drives the pointer instead, which is also what makes HTML5 drag-and-drop commit, since it needs a real `dragover`. ## A bug the `box` role exposed Assigning a role during the tree walk — as the pre-existing `iframe` branch does — **breaks the invariant that a walk and a single-node re-read describe a node identically.** The re-read returned `role=null`, `matchesSignature` rejected the node's own reference, and the box was selectable but not actionable. Roles are now decided in one `roleOf` that both read modes share, which also fixes the same latent bug for iframe boundary nodes. ## Where I stopped A drag whose **source** is reference-only still fails. I tried retaining one observation generation; the step trace showed why that is the wrong fix: `dragTo` takes **four** observations — a cache probe and a model input per locate — and each disposes the generation before it. Choosing a retention depth is a driver lifecycle decision that deserves its own review, so I reverted it and pinned the case. ## Verification `pnpm check` clean. **613** + **19** unit/integration, testbed **33**. New `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-unnamed.test.ts` — 11 tests, fixture pages for each gap. It asserts the two rungs *separately* (`locate.selector` for a node with a form `name`, `locate.reference` for an `` with no anchor), pins the drag case that is still blocked, and guards the `box` rule by requiring that an unpainted spacer of the same size never appears. Against seleniumbase.io: deterministic **55 pass / 4 skip**, agentic **17 → 26 pass / 1 skip**. ## The suites `tests-selenium/` and `tests-selenium-agent/`, opt-in: ```bash pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:selenium E2E_MODEL_API_KEY=... pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:selenium-agent ``` Every skip is a pinned finding naming its cause at the call site, and `packages/testbed/README.md` lists them. Still open, ranked: `Screen.locator` and nested `Screen.frameLocator` (3 of the 4 deterministic skips; the AST and driver already support both, only the public surface is missing), recording the resolved locator on agent steps, `toHaveAttribute`/`toHaveClass`, opening the 15-member `Role` union, a secondary pointer button, and a page-level response/console feed. The agentic suite also earns its cost: `/canvas` is a two-state drawn UI where vision taps a painted "Let's Eat" button, judges the burger it produces, and taps "Reset" — three steps with no DOM node involved, unwritable deterministically without hard-coded coordinates. ## Notes for review - **`Screen` has no `locator`.** Inside a frame there is no CSS escape hatch, so an unnameable control is unaddressable and a second frame boundary is inexpressible. Three deterministic tests are skipped for that, and the nested-frame test drops to `web.evaluate`. - **`getAttribute` reads a whitelist.** It returns `null` for `readonly`, `draggable`, `class`, `src` — indistinguishable from absent. With no `toHaveAttribute` either, attribute checks fall to `evaluate`. Worth deciding whether it should throw for a non-exposed name instead of quietly lying. - **`fill` on a rich-text host reports success and changes nothing** (TinyMCE reverts it). Reproduces in raw Playwright, so a driver-level hazard rather than an SDK defect — pinned as a test. A read-back after `fill` would turn it into a real failure. - **Exact-by-default string matching** (`spec/03-assertions.md:36`) inverts the Playwright and Testing-Library default and cost me three failures. Deliberate per the spec, but a docs callout would save every new author the same hour. - **The anti-bot page detects the reference driver.** `/hobbit/login` redirects to a block page on load; the aspirational test is skipped and the block pinned, so it fails loudly if stealth options land. ---

title: fix: recognize a driver error across module realms, and stop publishing stale dist
body: Three fixes to the runner/driver boundary. All are reachable today with the one driver that already ships separately, and none of them touch platform semantics. ## A driver error is now recognized across module realms `DriverError` was matched with `instanceof`. A driver imported by a config file resolves through a different module registry than the runner, so the two hold different copies of the class and the check misses. Every typed failure from such a driver then lost its taxonomy. The one that bites is `NODE_STALE`: backends raise it for an ordinary race whenever a mutation invalidates a node reference, and the runner is supposed to re-resolve and retry. Instead it became a generic driver failure, so a recoverable race failed the test. Detection is now structural, keyed on the closed `driver-1` code set, and the engine's three retry sites use it. ## `dist` is cleared before every build `tsc` only writes files. Output whose source has since moved or been deleted survives every later build, and gets published. Not hypothetical: after the Playwright driver moved out of `e2e`, a packed `e2e` tarball still carried the whole `dist/playwright` tree — 36 files belonging to another package. ``` $ tar -tzf e2e-0.1.0.tgz | grep -c dist/playwright 36 ``` ## `e2e/internal` shares the two text helpers every driver repeats `causeMessage` strips the terminal control sequences backends put in their messages; `sanitizeFilename` constrains a caller-supplied artifact label. Both reach the report, so two drivers disagreeing about them is a user-visible inconsistency. `@e2edev/playwright` now consumes them instead of keeping its own copies. ## Verification - The cross-realm retries are covered by a foreign `DriverError` constructed without the runner's class, and confirmed to fail on all three paths (resolve, read, perform) with the fix reverted. - The `dist` behaviour is demonstrated both ways: a planted stale file survives `tsc` alone and is removed by the new script. - `pnpm check` green; 611 runner + 19 driver tests; testbed 33 passed. ## Why separately Split out of the mobile branch because none of it depends on mobile: the failure modes apply to `@e2edev/playwright` as it ships today, and the stale-`dist` one is affecting published tarballs now. ---

title: docs: add a driver authoring guide
body: ## Why `e2e/driver` ships a full SPI with no user-facing documentation. Nothing explained `defineDriver`, the session surface, the `prepare`/`launch`/`close`/`dispose` lifecycle, or how a handle reaches `targets[].driver`. Writing a driver for a mobile or desktop backend meant reading `spec/api/driver.d.ts` and reverse-engineering `@e2edev/playwright`. Every existing mention of drivers in `fern/` is from the test author's side ("install `@e2edev/playwright`", `DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED`). This adds the author's side. ## What New page `fern/docs/pages/writing-a-driver.mdx`, under a new **Extend** section in the docs tab (slug `/writing-a-driver`): - **Ownership boundary table first.** The two rules it implies - no hidden query retries, no driver-side strictness - are the ones most likely to be broken, so they lead rather than trail. - **Eight-step walkthrough**: package layout (`e2e` as a peer dep), manifest fields, `launch` context, `screen.resolve/read/perform` with the `LocatorExpression` arms and `TextPattern`/`NodeRef` semantics, `observe`, artifacts, `close`, and wiring the handle into a target. - **Lifecycle table** covering the `prepare`-by-id vs `dispose`-by-instance asymmetry and the strict-serialization / one-instance-per-worker rule. - **Error table** with every `DriverErrorCode` and its legal retryability. - Optional surface (`tapPoint`, state, `web`, `capabilityFixtures`), testing notes, and the trust boundary. Cross-links added from `quickstart.mdx`, `introduction.mdx` (the native-platforms callout), and `reference/config.mdx` (the `DriverHandle` row). ## Two things called out as warnings Both are runner-enforced and neither is visible in the type signatures: 1. **Non-web targets are not schedulable.** `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:361` rejects any non-`'web'` platform with `PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` before a driver is instantiated, so a mobile or desktop driver can be written and unit-tested against `driver-1` today but cannot complete an end-to-end run. Better to say so than to let someone discover it after implementing a session. 2. **Retryability is a closed set.** `packages/e2e/src/driver/index.ts:214` silently downgrades `retryable: true` on any code other than `NODE_STALE`/`FRAME_NOT_FOUND` to a non-retryable `DRIVER_FAILURE`, so a genuine `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` loses its meaning in reports rather than throwing. ## Drive-by `fern/docs.yml` pointed its navbar GitHub link at `github.com/testerarmy/e2e`, which does not exist; the repository is `tester-army/e2e`. One line, and it would have propagated into the two spec links on the new page. ## Notes - No changeset: docs-site only, no package behavior change. - No spec, schema, or `suiteVersion` change - this documents the existing `driver-1` contract and does not amend it. Where the page and the spec could ever disagree, the page says the spec wins. - Prose is verified against `src/`, not against the README status lists, per AGENTS.md. ## Verification - [x] `pnpm docs:check` (`fern check`) passes - [x] `fern docs dev` renders `/writing-a-driver` (HTTP 200); callouts, step list, tables, and the new nav section all present - [x] No MDX compile errors in the rendered output ---

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## e2e@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- [#20](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/20) [`1e21658`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1e21658c949900be0191221a468647e43b6ddf2a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Move the Playwright driver into its own `@e2edev/playwright` package.

  `e2e` no longer depends on `playwright`, so installs that drive another backend
  no longer download a browser. `driver: 'playwright'` still works and is still
  the default for web targets; the runner now loads the driver from
  `@e2edev/playwright`, which it declares as an optional peer dependency.

  **Upgrading:** install the driver alongside the runner.

  ```bash
  npm install --save-dev e2e @e2edev/playwright
  ```

  A target that names the driver without the package installed now fails config
  resolution with `DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED` and exit code 2, naming the package to
  install.

  Also in this release:

  - Drivers can implement an optional `prepare` hook, run once before any session
    launches, for slow one-time provisioning. Browser downloads now happen there,
    so they are never charged against a launch timeout for any driver, not just
    the built-in one. A failing `prepare` aborts the run as an infrastructure
    error instead of a test failure.
  - The list reporter now prints run-level errors. Previously a run that failed
    during config, collection, or provisioning exited non-zero with the reason
    only in `report.json`.
  - The `e2e/playwright` subpath export is removed; import from
    `@e2edev/playwright` instead.

- [#78](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/78) [`61b31dd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/61b31dd95e431804e5bdb17a37da325d4dca10ef) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Locate nodes that no query can name, and observe shadow roots and `data:` frames.

  An agent step whose target has no accessible name, test id, placeholder, or text
  used to fail with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` before it looked at the page. The model had
  already selected the right node; the runner discarded it because no portable
  query could be derived from it — so the agent tier failed hardest on exactly the
  controls that have no deterministic address either, such as an input whose label
  is the table cell beside it.

  The locate sweep now falls through to the two paths that need no query:

  - the node's **observed reference**, which the driver backs with the element
    itself, and
  - the driver's **platform selector** for the node when it has an anchored one, in
    which case the located node carries a real locator instead of a reference and
    so survives into the cache and into `dragTo`. Recorded as the
    `locate.selector` policy decision.

  Both paths re-read the live node and require its recorded identity before acting,
  exactly as replay does, so a stale selection is still a miss rather than a blind
  dispatch. `poll: false` callers keep their early exit for escalation.

  One observation gap closes alongside it in `@e2edev/playwright`: **open shadow
  roots are walked**, so a control that exists only in a shadow tree is now
  selectable. Slotted content is not double-counted — slotted elements are
  light-DOM children, and the shadow tree holds `<slot>` placeholders rather than
  copies. A closed root stays invisible, as it is to a person reading the page.

  Empty painted rectangles are observed, and a drag can end on one.

  A drop zone, a colour swatch, a chart placeholder: an element defined by being
  empty carries no role, name, text, or test id, so the observation walk skipped it
  and no instruction could name it. An empty element that paints something — a
  border, an outline, a background of its own — and is at least 12 CSS pixels on
  each side is now reported with the role `box`. Nothing else changes: an unpainted
  spacer of the same size is still omitted, because a person cannot see it either.

  `dragTo` also no longer requires a locator on both sides. `Locator.dragTo` takes
  two locators, so a destination the agent reached through its observed reference
  made the whole verb unavailable — exactly for the elements that have no locator.
  When either endpoint is reference-backed the driver drives the pointer instead,
  which is also what makes HTML5 drag-and-drop commit, since it needs a real
  `dragover`. A drag whose _source_ is reference-only still fails: `dragTo` locates
  twice and every observation disposes the generation before it, so the source
  handle does not survive to the dispatch. That is an observation lifecycle
  question, not a drag one.

### Patch Changes

- [#77](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/77) [`9646852`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9646852104033c826faaeabfa4a2e334477a9f3f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Write the spec-mandated `A256GCM` algorithm name in session envelopes.

  Envelopes carried the Node cipher name `aes-256-gcm`, which the frozen
  `session-v1` schema rejects (`SESSION-SCHEMA-001`). The encryption itself is
  unchanged — still AES-256-GCM — only the wire literal is corrected. Envelopes
  written by an earlier version are not readable by this one; sessions are
  per-run, so nothing persists across runs.

  Produced envelopes are now Ajv-validated against
  `spec/schema/session-v1.schema.json` in the test suite, so this drift cannot
  recur silently.

- [#79](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/79) [`bc0f377`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bc0f377a0a2b5c9e9cea5cfffbcf94a1e8dcd7ae) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Harden the boundary between the runner and an out-of-tree driver.

  A driver's `DriverError` is now recognized structurally rather than with
  `instanceof`. A driver imported by a config file resolves through a different
  module registry than the runner, so the two hold different copies of the class
  and `instanceof` misses. Every typed driver failure then lost its taxonomy: a
  retryable `NODE_STALE` stopped being retried and surfaced as a generic failure
  instead of a recoverable race. This affects any driver package, including
  `@e2edev/playwright` whenever a project ends up with more than one copy of
  `e2e` resolved.

  Builds now clear `dist` before compiling. `tsc` only writes files, so output
  whose source has since moved or been deleted survived every later build and was
  published: after the Playwright driver moved out of `e2e`, the `e2e` tarball
  still carried a full copy of the old `dist/playwright` tree.

  `e2e/internal` additionally shares `causeMessage` and `sanitizeFilename`, the
  two text helpers each driver package would otherwise reimplement. Backend
  messages and artifact labels reach reports, so stripping terminal control
  sequences and constraining filenames happen in one place rather than once per
  driver.

- [#74](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/74) [`9334e8f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9334e8f35cbaacbe61b10b3489ea87a920aeb99a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Ship package metadata for the registry: repository, homepage, bug tracker,
  keywords, and the MIT `LICENSE` file. Releases publish under the `beta`
  dist-tag while the surface stabilizes, so `latest` is not moved.

- [#75](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/75) [`a1b80dc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a1b80dc1ff43589539181cb50a1fdf6cc254b9e7) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Harden agent model calls against transient provider failures.

  Transport retries per model call go from 2 to 5. Only failures the provider
  marked retryable are retried, `retry-after` is honored, and the remaining step
  timeout still bounds the whole chain, so a healthy provider is unaffected while
  a rate-limited or briefly 5xx-ing one no longer fails the step.

  An exhausted retry chain now reports the provider failure that actually
  occurred in `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` instead of the SDK's retry wrapper, and a
  chain cut short by the deadline still classifies as `STEP_TIMEOUT`.

title: chore: skip the private testbed in releases and pin publishes to the beta tag
body: Two release-plumbing defects surfaced by #81. ## The testbed is versioned as if it ships Changesets never *publishes* a private package, but it does *version* one by default. So #81 bumps `@e2edev/testbed` `0.0.0 -> 0.0.1`, adds `packages/testbed/CHANGELOG.md`, and would cut it a git tag — for a package that exists only to dogfood the built artifacts. `"privatePackages": false` in `.changeset/config.json` skips it outright (shorthand for `{ version: false, tag: false }`). The "dependent of a skipped package" validation only fires for packages that *depend on* the skipped one, and nothing depends on the testbed, so this is safe. ## The beta channel is not pinned to the packages `--tag beta` (added in #74, still unreleased) lived only in one root script string. Both publishable packages now carry `publishConfig.tag: "beta"`, so the channel travels with the package and a hand-run `npm publish` honours it. To be clear about which mechanism actually works: `--tag beta` still decides the channel. `changeset publish` always forwards `--tag` to the publish tool (`internalPublish`, `@changesets/cli@2.31.1` `changesets-cli.cjs.js:887`), and `pnpm publish` ignores `publishConfig.tag`. The manifest field is a backstop and a record of intent, not the enforcement. The prose now says so rather than implying the field is load-bearing. ## Verification Ran `changeset version` for real against the same six changesets #81 consumed: ``` M packages/e2e/package.json 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 M packages/playwright/package.json 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 ?? packages/e2e/CHANGELOG.md ?? packages/playwright/CHANGELOG.md ``` `packages/testbed/` untouched, no `packages/testbed/CHANGELOG.md`. #81 had both. The version artifacts were then reverted — `changesets/action` owns those. ## Two things that are not fixed here, because they cannot be - **`e2e` has no `beta` tag today.** Its dist-tags are `{ latest: '0.1.0' }`; `--tag beta` has never actually run. So `pnpm add -D e2e@beta`, which the README already instructs, 404s right now. Publishing 0.2.0 creates the tag and fixes it. No action needed, but worth knowing before #81 merges. - **`@e2edev/playwright` will land on `latest` once.** npmjs auto-assigns `latest` on a package's first publish *in addition* to the requested tag — documented in changesets' own source at `changesets-cli.cjs.js:805`. The driver has never been published, so its first release gets `latest` regardless of `--tag beta`, and `latest` can only be moved afterwards, never removed. Recorded in both docs as a known one-time leak. ## Prose correction AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md both said pre mode is avoided because a prerelease falls outside the driver's `e2e` peer range. True, but it understates the problem by implying a wider range would rescue it. It cannot: node-semver only lets a prerelease satisfy a comparator set when some comparator with the same `major.minor.patch` also carries a prerelease. Checked, not assumed — `0.3.0-beta.0` satisfies `>=0.1.0 <1`, `>=0.1.0-0 <1`, and `*` all as `false`. Both docs now record that so nobody retries the `-0` trick. ## Notes for review - No changeset. This is release configuration only; nothing in the shipped surface changes. Push back if you'd rather it be announced. - Docs-only prose beyond that, plus two JSON fields. `pnpm lint` is clean; the changesets config is validated by the `changeset version` run above. ---

title: feat: implement agent.act, the planning tier
body: Implements `agent.act`, the planning tier, plus `cache-1` path guidance. `agent.act(instruction, params?, options?)` plans and executes a bounded multi-action flow. One call is one invocation repeating a single cycle — observe, ask for the next action, authorize it, commit it — until the model concludes. The model answers with one `agent-tool-1` object per round and never reaches the driver: the runner validates every proposal against the action space and the security policy, then dispatches itself. ```ts await agent.act('complete the onboarding for Acme Inc'); await agent.act('sign in', { password: credentials.user('admin').password }); const { data } = await agent.act('read the total', undefined, { schema }); ``` ## Why a runner loop rather than AI SDK tool-calling Surveyed five loops across three prior-art implementations before deciding. Stagehand's `act()` and Midscene's `aiAct` are both runner loops driven by structured output; only Stagehand's `agent()` and testerarmy's QA agent use provider tool-calling. Midscene runs 100-step autonomous flows this way, so the shape is proven. It is also what the frozen spec describes — `10-determinism.md:36` "There is no outer agent loop" — and the only shape that permits the two things this change needs: a policy seam between proposal and dispatch (`execute()` *is* the dispatch, so there is nothing to interpose on), and a recordable action list for path guidance. ## The action space is one table `src/agent/action-space.ts` holds the vocabulary. The provider request schema, the prompt's action list, the response validator, the trail rendering, the cache derivative, and the dispatch are all derived from it: ```ts tap: action({ kind: 'tap', when: 'press a button, link, checkbox, tab, or menu item once', args: { target: node('the control to press') }, describe: (args, name) => `tapped ${name(args.target)}`, record: (args, locate) => ({ kind: 'tap', target: locate(args.target) }), perform: (context, args) => context.invocation.commit('tap', () => ...), }), ``` Adding an action is one entry and nothing else. That is asserted as a property over the whole space, so a newly added entry cannot sit unreachable: ``` ✓ declares every argument of every entry in the request schema ✓ offers every entry kind in the schema enum ✓ describes every entry in the request text ✓ reaches every dispatchable action through validation ``` Adding path guidance later exercised this: it needed two optional registry fields and three lines in the loop. ## Path guidance A successful flow records the actions it took; the next run is offered each one as the route that worked. It is **advisory** — `10-determinism.md:288` requires a fresh observation and a fresh decision every round — so it reduces wrong turns, not model calls, and declining it never fails a flow. Only locate hits skip a model call, and `--debug` now accounts for the two separately rather than crediting guidance with time it never saved. ## Bounded by construction - `maxSteps` / `maxModelCalls` / a deadline, all runner-owned. - No actions left → the grammar narrows to `observe` and `conclude`, so a flow that runs out reports what it found instead of a bare `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. - A repeated action against an unchanged screen is **not dispatched** — repeating a submit or a purchase is not safe to do on the caller's behalf — and the model is told the screen did not move. - A first `conclude: failure` with budget left is questioned once, then accepted. - A driver failure flagged retryable (a node the page replaced mid-dispatch) costs neither a step nor blame. - Every failure carries the trail, so a multi-action flow says how far it got. - Secrets: a `Secret` in `params` is disclosed as name and purpose only; the value is resolved host-side immediately before an authorized fill. ## `--debug` streams decisions Per-phase timings moved behind `E2E_DEBUG=phases`; seven lines per action became one, carrying the budget it spends. ``` [e2e agent] agent.act "complete the onboarding for Acme" - up to 8 action(s), 25 call(s), 60s [e2e agent] 1/8 tapped the button "Get started" - ok 22ms [e2e agent] 2/8 typed "Acme" into the node "Company name" - ok 4ms [e2e agent] 2/8 tapped a combobox - page moved, re-reading [e2e agent] 5/8 done success - the summary confirms Acme [e2e agent] agent.act end - 5 action(s), 6 call(s), 720 tokens, $0.0186 ``` ## Also fixed `No output generated` from a provider was classified as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (infrastructure, exit 3) and failed a run outright. `result.output` is an AI SDK getter that throws `NoOutputGeneratedError` — a different class from a response that parsed and failed validation — so the `undefined` check guarding it was dead code. It is now invalid output, which the existing bounded repair loop re-asks, re-sending the request unchanged rather than quoting a response that never existed. ## Testing - 683 unit + integration tests, `pnpm check` and `pnpm test:testbed` green. - 20 unit tests cross-check every accepted call and every recorded action against the frozen `spec/schema/agent-tool-v1.schema.json` and `cache-v1.schema.json`. - 20 integration tests drive real Chromium through a new `/onboarding` fixture (5 committed actions across 5 observations, which only passes if the loop genuinely re-observes) and a `/restage` fixture that detaches its own button mid-dispatch. - Verified live against wakacje.pl with `google/gemini-3.6-flash`. ## Docs `agent.act` callouts retracted across 7 pages; both budget tables gained an `act` row; `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION` added to the error reference; two new troubleshooting entries. `agent.login` remains the only `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. ## The agentic comparison `packages/testbed/tests-wakacje/wakacje-act.e2e.ts` reruns the existing located journey with `agent.act`: 26 `agent.*` calls become 8, 52 code lines become 41. It is **flaky** — observed passing outright, passing on retry, and failing both attempts — and leans on `retries: 1`. It flakes on "Kup teraz", where the offer page sometimes needs a room selection first; the located suite covers that step with `vision: 'fallback'` and a human's knowledge of the sequence, and is stable. Keeping both is the point. Neither gates CI. ## Not in this change - `agent.login` (still `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`). - `tool-proposal` report events. - `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED` is unreachable: nothing replays cached actions blindly, so the clause guarding a half-applied replay cannot trigger. Raising it when the model merely chose differently made the cache turn passing tests red. - No `agent.timeout` config key, so the 60 s planning default is per-call only. Every real-site agentic suite will hit that; worth its own spec discussion. ---

title: docs: RFC0001 — e2e v2 on the TesterArmy engine
body:
Supersedes RFC0000 and PLAN.md as implementation direction. **One document: `RFC0001.md`** — short and actionable: state of reality, the four layers, the socket contract, public/private line, business model, v0 plan, and nine open questions.

## The one-breath version

e2e is the framework for building testing agents: tests in code, one agentic API, a framework-owned action grammar with per-agent replaceable toolsets over swappable backends, a step-executor socket where anyone's brain plugs in, and the adaptive cache as the deterministic tier. Kitchen public, recipes private — `@testerarmy/agent` implements the same spec everyone else gets, and `qa-tools` is never published.

## Key decisions

- **agent.\* only in v0** — determinism is compiled by the cache, not hand-written; the v1 locator engine stays shelved.
- **Action grammar (framework-owned) vs toolsets (replaceable per agent)** — cache/policy/receipts are defined over the grammar; TesterArmy's production toolset fully replaces the public default and compiles to the same grammar.
- **Cache: mechanism public, judgment private** — format/store/adaptive-flow ship in the harness; relocation/divergence judgment sits behind a `ReplayPolicy` the paid agent tunes. Replay hit-rate becomes paid-agent value.
- **AI SDK native at the edges, e2e-owned at the seam** — `createAgent()` is the golden path; the executor type is e2e's (engine pins `ai@7.0.2`; skew is the adapter's problem, not builders').
- **Honest state (adversarial review, 2026-08-30):** legacy loop is what's proven; TestRunner is flag-gated; the cache merged 08-29 and is ramping — the RFC gates on that soak. "Mostly packaging" was wrong: v0 includes one real inversion (tools/budgets/policy/recording move out of `qa-agent` into the harness), bench-gated.
- **Business model:** agent → device leases → hosted third-party executors, on one substrate; public benchmark as the pricing-power requirement.

## For review

The nine open questions at the end are the decisions this PR does not make — the top one (review's Q1): where do v0 code tests run to earn receipts and PR verdicts before hosted executors exist. Also proposed: close PR #83 as superseded.

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2edev/agent-device@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- [#117](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/117) [`44ce280`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/44ce280e92772b452b6a958bf1a606b43e7cdba3) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Install builds on the device. The `appPath` backend option installs an iOS
  `.app` bundle or Android `.apk` once per worker, after boot and before the
  first attempt; without `app`, the installed bundle id or package becomes the
  app opened fresh per attempt, so `agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', appPath:
'./build/MyApp.app' })` is a complete target. The `device` fixture gains
  `installApp(appPath, { app, reinstall })` for tests that exercise upgrade or
  fresh-install paths, recorded as a `device.installApp` step.

  `BackendInitInfo` carries `projectRoot`, the directory relative config paths
  resolve against, so a backend option naming a file resolves the same way in a
  child-process worker and an in-process run.

### Patch Changes

- [#119](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/119) [`00cfc52`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/00cfc52bd5a9ab56f7fb2dad357ce325c9ce4817) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Hooks now run in the order the lifecycle spec defines. `beforeEach` runs outer
  scope to inner and `afterEach` inner to outer regardless of where in the file
  each scope's hooks were declared; before, a file-level hook declared below a
  `test.describe` ran after (or, for `afterEach`, before) the group's own hooks.
  A `describe`'s `afterAll` runs when its last test in the realm finishes rather
  than when the whole file ends, so one group's teardown no longer lands after a
  sibling group's tests. Sibling groups that share a title keep separate hooks.
  A failing `afterAll` discards the realm as the spec requires: later tests start
  fresh, and a serial group attempt ends with its remaining members skipped.

  Each `afterEach` hook gets its own `cleanupTimeout` budget with working
  fixtures: after a body timeout, teardown can still drive the app instead of
  failing with `operation cancelled`; a hook that overruns its budget fails, its
  fixture operations are cancelled, and the next hook still runs. The agent-device
  `device` fixture reads that signal per call, so it too keeps working in teardown.

  Suite-hook run errors carry a readable `scopeId` (`file` or the group title
  path); an `afterAll` failure at file scope no longer writes an empty
  `scopeId` the report schema rejects.

### Minor Changes

- [#117](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/117) [`44ce280`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/44ce280e92772b452b6a958bf1a606b43e7cdba3) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Install builds on the device. The `appPath` backend option installs an iOS

- [#113](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/113) [`6a2918c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6a2918cf98117d5c06a815422498923ee2c1c043) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Foundation work for executors that diff screens and replay long flows
  reliably; no behaviour of the built-in agent changes beyond its history hook.

  Chassis (`createToolLoopExecutor`): `prepareMessages(messages, turn)`
  replaces `compactMessages`. It runs between turns, its result carries forward
  to later turns, and it may return `{ messages, stop }` to force the
  conclusion when the executor has evidence the loop guards cannot see.
  `providerOptions` are passed to every model call. `createAgent` accepts
  `providerOptions` too. `isDefinedTool`, `toolAppliesTo`, `PreparedTurn` and
  `PreparedMessages` are exported from `@e2edev/e2e/agent`; `RUNTIME_CODES` from
  `@e2edev/e2e`. `ExecutorObservation` carries the current `path` when the
  backend reports one.

  Trace cache: a typed value that appears in neither the step's instruction
  nor its params was derived at run time and is recorded as a gap, so replay
  hands the step over before it instead of typing a value the app may not
  issue again. A trace records how long the recording run took to reach its
  end state (`endWaitMs`), and replay waits that long (plus a margin, bounded
  by the step clock) for the end anchors before it self-finalizes. Every
  targeted action records the key of the row or list item it sat in
  (`within`), and relocation requires it to hold, so same-named controls in
  different rows replay without a guess. The replay policy version bumps, so
  existing caches cold-start.

  Breaking for `createToolLoopExecutor` callers: `compactMessages` is replaced
  by `prepareMessages`.

- [#125](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/125) [`20c5d4a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/20c5d4ad404e90df8f54831e063d26536fae0073) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The harness is a notary, not an author: it witnesses and bounds what a step
  executor does and no longer decides what the executor's model reads.

  The executor context gains `attempt` (test id, attempt id, retry index, an
  end-of-attempt signal, and a per-attempt `memory` map the harness holds and
  never persists or reports), `step.index`, and `priorSteps` — the completed
  steps as structured, sanitized records beside the existing `ledger` string.
  `observe({ tree, pixels })` opts into the redacted node tree and masked
  viewport pixels; pixels are withheld with a reason after a secret fill, when
  masking is unproven, or when the backend has none. A `StepExecutor` may
  declare `cache: 'off'` so every one of its steps reaches `runStep` instead of
  a cached replay.

  The agent surface is layered like the AI SDK. `createAgent` is unchanged:
  the golden path, five options. `createToolLoopExecutor` is where the model's
  reading is shaped: `buildPrompt` may return a message history, and it gains
  `onConclude(ctx, { messages, verdict })` plus `loopGuards` / `windDown`
  policy. New primitives from `@e2edev/e2e/agent` compose with the chassis or a
  raw `ToolLoopAgent` and load no `ai` themselves: `createGrammarTools`,
  `createVerdictTool`, `trackModelCalls`, `conversationMemory`, plus the
  exported `serializeLedger`, `compactSnapshotHistory`, and
  `formatReplayedPrefix`. The chassis is rebuilt on those primitives. A model
  that remembers every step of a test is the chassis, the grammar tools, and
  `conversationMemory`.

  Spec chapter 10 now states what the ledger must guarantee (deterministic,
  bounded, never model-produced, never carrying secrets) instead of prescribing
  the serialization algorithm, which becomes the reference runner's exported
  default.

- [#115](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/115) [`b08a668`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b08a668eed39e3d68b5f5d15335eef9895bdb15f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Backends get a `prepare` hook: once per run and target, in the runner process,
  before any worker starts and outside every launch budget. The Playwright
  backend installs a missing browser there instead of inside `init`, so a
  first-run download is no longer charged against `launchTimeout`, no longer runs
  once per worker, and its progress streams as new `notice` run events. The list
  reporter prints those above its live status block, where before the block's
  repaint erased the download output written to a worker's stderr and a first run
  looked hung on a spinner.

- [#116](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/116) [`e73e4f2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e73e4f27ca8a4a863d2d142a2bc05983b2ae2057) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.url` and `APP_URL` no longer need a scheme: `tester.army` becomes `https://tester.army` and `localhost:3000` becomes `http://localhost:3000`. The `allowProduction` gate is gone and `app.environment` is no longer required for non-loopback hosts; it defaults to `test` for loopback, `.localhost`, and `.test` hosts and to `production` elsewhere, and stays a label for the report and the cache identity. `allowProduction` is now an unknown app key (`INVALID_CONFIG`), and the report target no longer carries it: readers that require `targets[].allowProduction` must drop that requirement. `e2e init` now scaffolds `app: { url: 'localhost:3000' }`, `agent: createAgent({ system })`, and one playwright web target, and warns when the `ai` peer dependency is not declared.

### Patch Changes

- [#118](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/118) [`749988f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/749988f923e7905a36c4898e0037b8af06eff23c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Ctrl-C now ends the run and tears the backend down. The first signal interrupts the running test immediately (it no longer waits for the test timeout when the body is not calling the harness), runs its bounded cleanup, disposes every worker's backend, and writes the report. A second signal forces every worker to dispose at once and kills it after the cleanup budget; a third exits on the spot. A worker whose runner disappears disposes its backend and exits instead of running on. The event stream gains `run-interrupted`.

- [#119](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/119) [`00cfc52`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/00cfc52bd5a9ab56f7fb2dad357ce325c9ce4817) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Hooks now run in the order the lifecycle spec defines. `beforeEach` runs outer
  scope to inner and `afterEach` inner to outer regardless of where in the file
  each scope's hooks were declared; before, a file-level hook declared below a
  `test.describe` ran after (or, for `afterEach`, before) the group's own hooks.
  A `describe`'s `afterAll` runs when its last test in the realm finishes rather
  than when the whole file ends, so one group's teardown no longer lands after a
  sibling group's tests. Sibling groups that share a title keep separate hooks.
  A failing `afterAll` discards the realm as the spec requires: later tests start
  fresh, and a serial group attempt ends with its remaining members skipped.

  Each `afterEach` hook gets its own `cleanupTimeout` budget with working
  fixtures: after a body timeout, teardown can still drive the app instead of
  failing with `operation cancelled`; a hook that overruns its budget fails, its
  fixture operations are cancelled, and the next hook still runs. The agent-device
  `device` fixture reads that signal per call, so it too keeps working in teardown.

  Suite-hook run errors carry a readable `scopeId` (`file` or the group title
  path); an `afterAll` failure at file scope no longer writes an empty
  `scopeId` the report schema rejects.

- [#126](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/126) [`15ebb46`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/15ebb465b883047b6afb0d126ab6c4a0cdaf9fb9) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A replayed step that navigates now waits for its recorded destination path
  before the end state is judged. A step that moved to another pathname records
  no anchors; the path is its whole postcondition, and the replayed tap that
  starts the navigation returns before the new document commits. The replay read
  the path once, right there, so every cross-page replay handed off as
  `end-mismatch` and the executor paid for the step again. The path is polled
  with the same settling backoff anchors use (100 to 3000 ms, 15 s cap, bounded
  by the step budget), and a navigation step self-finalizes zero-turn like a
  same-page one.
## @e2edev/playwright@0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- [#115](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/115) [`b08a668`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b08a668eed39e3d68b5f5d15335eef9895bdb15f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Backends get a `prepare` hook: once per run and target, in the runner process,

  backend installs a missing browser there instead of inside `init`, so a

  element the first time it is observed and reads it back afterwards, so an
  element keeps its id across observations for as long as it lives in the
  document, and an executor can diff two observations instead of re-reading

title: feat: agent.act() on a harness-owned StepExecutor socket (RFC0001 v0)
body: ## Summary Implements the simplest version of RFC0001's inversion: the harness owns each `agent.act()` step — observation redaction, the action grammar, budgets, deadline, origin policy, recording — and delegates only the thinking to a pluggable **StepExecutor**. Verdicts are ternary (`passed` / `failed` / `blocked`); blocked carries a blockable error code and maps to configuration/infrastructure exit codes, not test failure. No caching for act steps in this milestone. ## What's in here **The socket (`e2e/agent`)** - `StepExecutor` — one step in, one verdict out; valid to implement with no AI SDK at all - `createAgent()` — the built-in ToolLoopAgent executor over the grammar (`tap`, `type`, `press`, `select`, `scroll`, `navigate`, `observe` + `complete_step`) - `defineTool(tool, { replay, mutates, secrets })` — required annotations; undeclared semantics are rejected - config: `agent.executor` (worker-safe, structurally validated like model instances); model resolution is now lazy so custom-executor runs need no model **Fail-closed invariants** - Runtime hard stops (budget/timeout/cancel) outrank the executor's verdict - Closed verdict grammar (`MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` otherwise); runtime codes are runtime-assigned - Executor returning without concluding → `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION`, never a guessed success **Hardened against real models** (gateway/google/gemini-3-flash on the testbed playground; all flows passing) - Executor model accounting: per-turn model events + `StepModelInfo` provenance; `--debug` shows real calls/tokens - Stale screen-snapshot compaction in the tool transcript - Wind-down notice + forced `complete_step` on the final turns — verified live: missing credentials concludes `blocked` with `AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` instead of burning the budget **Docs/spec** - New `spec/16-executors.md` (philosophy, contract, invariants, whole-toolset replacement incl. an agent-device example) - `spec/02-test-api.md` act section, `agents.mdx` + `introduction.mdx` updated to shipped behavior - RFC0001: cache consolidation plan (v2 action-trace cache extends `cache-1`'s store/keys/validity; a locate entry is the one-action degenerate trace) - Removed `RFC.md`/`PLAN.md` (superseded by RFC0001) ## Testing - 634 e2e package tests + 19 playwright tests green, including 9 new integration tests: a hand-rolled no-AI-SDK executor over the socket against real Playwright, verdict mapping (blocked exit code, fail-closed budget override, closed grammar), and a scripted tool-calling model driving the real ToolLoopAgent path (`tests/helpers/fake-loop-model.ts`) - Full `pnpm check` green (lint, spec typecheck, driver drift, fern docs) - Real-model runs via AI Gateway: `packages/testbed/tests-agent/act.e2e.ts` (todos, wizard, sign-in) all passing with sane accounting ---

title: act-first: remove the located agent verbs and the locator cache
body: ## What `agent.act` becomes the one agent action API. The located verb tier and the locator cache are removed end to end — code, schemas, spec, docs, and testbed. ### Removed - **Located verbs**: `agent.tap/click/type/scroll/scrollTo/longPress/press/select/hover/check/uncheck/dragTo/upload`, `agent.login`, `InstantActionOptions`, `LoginOptions`. Sign-in is an ordinary `agent.act` flow over `Secret` params: the model sees a name+purpose placeholder, the runner fills host-side through the authorized `type_secret` path. - **The locate machinery**: the `agent-locate-1` protocol/grammar/schema, derived-query locators, node-reference dispatch, positional targeting, vision escalation for locates. `vision: 'fallback'` now behaves like `false` for `assert`/`waitFor`/`extract` — a judgment always answers from the tree, so there is no miss to escalate on. - **The locator cache (`cache-1`)** in full: `src/cache/`, `agent.cache`, `--no-agent-cache`, `limits.maxCacheBytes`, report `step.cache` + `usage.maxCacheEntryBytes`, `CACHE_REPLAY_DIVERGED`, the cache-1 schema and conformance profile. v0 performs no caching; runs are comparable through the report, not replay. ### Kept - `agent.act`, `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, `agent.extract`. - The deterministic tier (`screen`, `expect`, `web`, `app`), frozen as previously decided. - The executor socket, blocked taxonomy, loop guards, and Secret handling — unchanged. ### Coupled updates - `suiteVersion` 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 (`check:manifest` green); `cache-1` profile and `AGENT-TOOL-006` withdrawn. - Spec chapters 00–16, examples, README, RFC decision log; all fern pages. - Testbed: verb-based suites deleted (`tests-agent` verbs/interactions/credentials/frames/vision/wizard, all of `tests-selenium-agent`, wakacje). `tests-agent/act.e2e.ts` and the dogfood suite carry live coverage. ## Verification - `pnpm run check` (lint, spec typecheck, workspace typecheck + driver-drift, fern check): green. - `pnpm run test`: 452 e2e + 19 playwright tests pass. `test:testbed`: 33 pass. - Live on `google/gemini-3-flash` via the gateway: `test:agent` 3/3 (multi-action todo flow, wizard, **Secret sign-in**), dogfood 4/4 (async save, validation recovery, custom seed tool + confirm modal, select filter). Net: **−2,600 lines** across the two commits (64 files in the docs/spec commit alone at −1,693). ---

title: docs: collapse the guides to six agent-first pages
body: ## What A deep simplification pass over the docs. The value proposition now leads everything: **describe the flow, pin down what matters**. ### New docs tab (6 pages, ~870 lines total) | Page | Job | | --- | --- | | Introduction (74) | The hero test is agentic; `screen`/`expect` framed as the escape hatch. Why-this-shape in five short claims (resilient+exact, bounded verdicts, secrets, extensible brain, local first). | | Quickstart (107) | Install → model in config → an **agentic** first test → run. Model setup is no longer buried in a later page. | | Writing tests (172) | Goals (`act` + params/Secrets) → checks (`assert`/`waitFor`/`extract` + vision) → escape hatches (queries, gestures, `expect` in one tight section) → structure. Absorbs the judgment/extraction/vision content from the old Agents page. | | Your own agent (180) | Models/gateway, `defineTool` project tools, the `createToolLoopExecutor` chassis **with a device-toolkit example** (how you'd drive a computer-use/device SDK), full `StepExecutor` replacement, the ternary verdict, cost table. | | Authentication (181) | Unchanged content, links repointed. | | CI (156) | Unchanged content, links repointed. | ### Deleted (975 lines) `web`, `running-tests`, `configuration`, `from-playwright`, `troubleshooting` — every durable fact already lives in the reference tab (`app-web`, `cli`, `config`, `errors`). Redirects added for all five old slugs. ### Drive-by consistency fixes - `e2e init` no longer writes `.e2e/report.html` to `.gitignore` (the HTML reporter is gone) and the CLI reference drops its reporter row — config rejects the id. ## Verification `pnpm run check` green (lint, spec, typecheck, `fern check`), all 452+19 tests pass. Docs: 20 pages / 4,511 lines → 15 / ~3,170; the guides users actually read went from ~1,850 to ~870. ---

title: feat(reporter): live agent steps, tool calls, and model cost in list output
body: ## What The list reporter narrates agent runs live, and reports what the AI cost. **While a test runs** (TTY): the status block shows the active step under an animated spinner, with a rolling window of its latest model turns and tool calls: ``` ▸ runs a full reminders session: create, complete, delete [ios-simulator] ✓ agent.act "open the Reminders app, dismiss any welcome…" 18.6s · 1 model call ⠴ agent.act "add three reminders named …" click 2.8s model turn 6.3s · 9.0k tokens 0/1 done · 1 running · 0 waiting ``` **Permanent scrollback**: one collapsed line per finished agent step; test result lines and the run summary carry model usage (`ai 315.5k tokens · $0.0184`). ## How - New `progress` worker message (step start/end + step events) from `StepRecorder`, forwarded scheduler → list reporter. Plain data; serves child-process and in-process runners alike. - `ExecutorModelCall.estimatedCostUsd`: the tool-loop chassis reads the AI Gateway's per-request cost (`providerMetadata.gateway.cost`, `marketCost` BYOK fallback) per turn; act dispatch sums it into the step's `StepModelInfo`, so `--debug` tables and `report.json` provenance carry real USD. - `LiveStatus`: multi-line entries, spinner timer (unref'd), ANSI-aware width clamping so repaints never leave wrapped fragments behind. - All lines sanitized and bounded per spec 06; docs updated (`reference/cli.mdx`), changeset included. ## Testing - `pnpm check` green (lint, spec, typecheck + driver drift, docs). - 452 unit/integration tests green; reporter test updated for the spinner marker. - Dogfooded against the testbed device suite (separate PR) and synthetic TTY renders at 60/100 columns. ---
