title: feat(agent): adaptive trace cache (trace-1) with zero-turn replay
body: ## Summary Implements RFC0001's adaptive action-trace cache (the *cache-in* decision) as its own `trace-1` mechanism. Each passing `agent.act()` step records the grammar actions it performed — durable target descriptors captured at commit time, secret-free verbatim inputs, gap markers for project-tool mutations — and the next run replays them **zero-turn** through the same policed grammar (deadline, budgets, origin policy, secret authorization, recording all apply identically). A full replay self-finalizes the step as passed with zero model calls; any divergence hands the step to the executor mid-step via `replayedPrefix` and the step re-records on pass. Judgments (`assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`) are never cached. Measured on the new bench with real models (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`, three consecutive runs, stable): | Test | Live (record) | Replayed | Model calls | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Sign in with credential | 7.0s | **0.69s** | 0 | | 4-act expense journey | 24.8s | **1.95s** | 0 | | Stale-DOM (churning testids) | 9.5s | **0.60s** | 0 | | Revealed-target settings flow | 5.2s | **0.56s** | 0 | ## Behavior - **Opt-out by default**: unset `cache` resolves to `read-write`; CI is forced down to `read-only` (committed caches are untrusted input, CI never publishes what it learned). Opt out per project with `cache: 'off'` or per run with `e2e run --no-cache`, which wins over everything. Retries always run live and re-record. - **Write settlement is attempt-scoped**: a step's own passing verdict does not confirm its trace — the deterministic assertion after it does. Staged traces are confirmed by a later passed step or a passing attempt; an implicated trace's entry is **evicted** (a poisoned flow re-records instead of replaying forever); interruption (Ctrl-C) neither writes nor evicts. A consumed replay whose step settles non-passed evicts its entry directly. - **Store abstraction**: `.e2e/cache/` file store (atomic renames, traversal-safe digest-named files, 1 MiB wire cap) by default; any `TraceCacheStore` implementation (e.g. a shared Redis cache) drops in via `cache.store`. - **Conservative replay policy** (`conservative/2`): two-tier relocation — strict field match, then semantic-only when a recorded testid churned — exactly-one-or-diverge at both tiers, plus a pre-action settle wait so replay speed cannot double-commit a form the app is still clearing. Both rules came out of real-model bench failures. - **Executor contract**: `StepExecutorContext.replayedPrefix` carries prose summaries and a closed `stopReason` token — never descriptors or error objects. Grammar actions/observations now serialize in call order, fixing a parallel-tool-call race (observed live) where two mutations resolved against one stale observation and typed credentials into the wrong field. ## Spec (suiteVersion 0.4.0 → 0.5.0) 10-determinism's "No caching" clause is replaced by the trace-cache chapter; 05-config and 06-cli document the key, defaults, and `--no-cache`; 16-executors documents the hand-off and serialization; `report-v1.schema.json` gains `step.cache` with enumerated reason tokens; a `trace-1` conformance profile is added; `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` mirrors every new type, with example and type-test coverage. ## Bench infrastructure `packages/testbed/bench/` — a deterministic Next.js app (login/session, expenses CRUD, churning-id stale page, revealed-target settings; seeded in-memory store + `POST /api/reset`) with four agentic suites under `tests-bench/`. `pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed run test:bench` builds and runs it; `E2E_CACHE=off|read-only|read-write` selects the mode. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm check` (lint, check:spec, typecheck incl. driver drift, docs) and `pnpm check:manifest` - [x] 528 tests green: 7 new unit suites (entry format, identity, store, recorder, replay engine, relocation, config/settlement) + 13 cache integration tests over real Playwright (record → zero-turn replay → divergence hand-off → self-heal → poison-evict → read-only/CI/`--no-cache` postures) - [x] Real-model bench: record + two replay runs all green and stable; `--no-cache` smoke-verified via the actual CLI against a warm store (ran live, store untouched) Direction and phase history in `RFC0001.md` (cache-in decision) — next up: `ReplayPolicy` extension point, replay telemetry in the list renderer, bench parity vs the private fixtures, and the TesterArmy-side `StepExecutor`/Redis-store adapters. ---

title: fix(agent): settle executor-facing observations after grammar actions
body:
## Summary

Every executor-facing \`observe()\` now re-observes until the page shape holds still (75 ms poll, 1 s ceiling), through **one shared settle loop** (\`settleObservation\` in \`observation.ts\`) that replay's pre-action wait also uses — the pacing can never drift between the two paths. An executor observation is followed by a model call measured in seconds, so the bounded wait is noise there; what it buys is the guarantee that the executor never reads a snapshot the app is still reacting to. Replay is unaffected: it reads raw observations and keeps settling on its own schedule via the same loop, so zero-turn replay speed does not change.

## The bug

Observed live on the bench with \`google/gemini-3-flash\` (three consecutive reproductions on the approve-expense flow):

1. The executor taps \`Approve Taxi to airport\`. The post-action observation is captured **19 ms later** — before the app's fetch-round-trip re-render — and is byte-identical to the pre-action snapshot.
2. The next model turn reads that stale snapshot, concludes the click didn't land, and taps the same node again — which by now reads \`Unapprove Taxi to airport\`, toggling the state **back off**.
3. The following observation is again captured ~24 ms after the tap, showing the pre-tap-2 "Approved" state, so the model reports a pass. The deterministic assertion after the step correctly fails.

\`replay.ts\` had assumed *"the live run's pacing gave the app this settling time for free"* — a fast model disproves that: the harness captures the observation immediately after the action, and the model's turn latency can't help because the stale snapshot is already in its context.

## Design notes

- **Always settle, no dirty-flag mode.** An earlier draft settled only when an action had committed since the last observe; review flagged that the flag was step-scoped (a step ending in an action left the *next* step's first observe raw — the same stale-judgment failure one boundary over) and that the mode machinery wasn't worth one skipped 75 ms poll before a multi-second model call. Deleting the flag makes the invariant one sentence: an executor never reads an unsettled snapshot.
- **One settle implementation.** \`act.ts\` and \`replay.ts\` previously would have carried the same loop and the same constants twice; both now call \`settleObservation\`.
- The settle loop runs inside the step's single recorded observation event, so event counts and \`maxEventsPerStep\` accounting are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm check\` (lint, check:spec, typecheck, docs)
- [x] 424 unit tests + \`agent-act\`, \`agent-trace-cache\`, \`trace-replay\` suites green — record → zero-turn replay unaffected, observation event counts unchanged
- [x] Real-model bench (\`gemini-3-flash\`, cache off): the previously failing 4-act journey passes live; previously 3/4 with a double-toggle false pass

title: feat(run): the embedding-host surface — e2e/run, event spine, hosted-cache seams, secret providers
body: ## Summary Everything a hosted platform needs to run e2e as its core engine, shipped as generic seams with local defaults — no host is named anywhere: - **\`e2e/run\`** — programmatic \`run()\` (no \`process.exit\`, \`AbortSignal\` cancellation, full report-1 in memory) and \`RunOptions.onEvent\`: every lifecycle fact as plain JSON with an emitter-stamped \`seq\`. The stream is the runner's **single spine**: the list reporter consumes it through the same emitter (\`listReporterSink\`), so the CLI and a host dashboard can never render different stories — including run-level report-write errors, which previously reached neither. Sinks are quarantined independently. - **Hosted-cache seams** — a host-supplied \`cache.store\` is exempt from the CI read-only clamp (it is not a committed file cache; it states its own trust through \`writable\`), and \`app.identity\` keys cache/session identity by a stable logical app identity so ephemeral per-deploy origins (PR previews) share their recorded traces. \`buildTraceEntry\`/\`readTraceEntry\` are exported so a remote store validates with exactly the framing the file store uses. - **\`event.detail\`** — redacted, bounded prose on driver action events (\`tap button "Approve"\`, \`fill secret "member" into textbox "Password"\`), same wording as trace summaries. The action body returns its recordable descriptor: one value feeds the pure detail hook and the dispatch's trace-cache write, so evidence, prose, and recording cannot disagree. report-v1 gains \`event.detail\`; suiteVersion 0.5.0 → 0.6.0. - **Fill-time secret providers** — \`password\` may be a \`SecretProvider\` function, called on every authorized fill (vault lookup, fresh TOTP). The resolved value joins redaction the moment it exists through a \`SecretLedger\` (memoized redactor invalidated on register); \`E2E_USER_*\` env overrides win; providers never cross a process boundary. Proven under zero-turn replay: a replayed \`typeSecret\` re-runs the full authorization, so the provider resolves even at replay speed. - **A wired host demo** (\`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed run demo:host\`) — a test defined as data (natural-language step rows), materialized to a suite, run in-process via \`rawConfig\`, events streamed with action prose, artifacts enumerated at \`test-finished\`, zero-turn replay on the second invocation. - **RFC0002** — the host tool registry design (declared replay tiers over the policed grammar), the prerequisite for swapping in a host's own tool vocabulary without losing the trace cache. Stacked on #93 (the settle fix); retargets to \`main\` when it merges. ## Design notes Structured after an adversarial code-quality review; the decisions that came out of it: the event stream as the single dispatch spine (no reporter wired beside the emitter), always-settled executor observations through one shared loop, action bodies returning their evidence, \`RunEventResult\` built on the worker protocol's \`WireResultRecord\`, an honestly-async \`SecretResolver\`, and structural (not commented) redaction liveness. **Every commit in the range builds and typechecks standalone** — verified per commit. ## Test plan - [x] \`pnpm check\` (lint, check:spec, typecheck incl. driver drift, docs) and \`pnpm check:manifest\` - [x] 571 tests green: new unit suites (event emitter/quarantine, provider config) + integration (event lifecycle/ordering/JSON-cleanliness over real Playwright, provider fill with plaintext-free report, \`event.detail\` prose) - [x] Per-commit standalone build+typecheck across the whole range - [x] Real-model validation (\`gemini-3-flash\`): bench 4/4 live and 4/4 zero-turn replayed; \`demo:host\` recorded live (\$0.004) then replayed zero-turn (39s → 358ms, \$0.0007) with seq-ordered, JSON-clean events ---

title: chore(release): private npm phase — restricted publish with tarball-only rename
body: ## Summary Holds the public release: \`pnpm release\` (and the release workflow) now publishes both packages **restricted** through \`scripts/publish-private.mjs\`, which renames the core package to \`@e2edev/e2e\` **in the published tarball only**. The repo keeps the name \`e2e\` everywhere — the spec, the docs, the integration fixtures, and the package self-reference all depend on it, and the unscoped name is the public launch. ## Consumer contract (tester-army) \`\`\`jsonc "e2e": "npm:@e2edev/e2e@^0.2.0", "@e2edev/playwright": "^0.2.0" \`\`\` The \`e2e\` alias key satisfies the driver's peer range and resolves the driver's own \`e2e/...\` imports. Without the alias, pnpm's peer auto-install would fetch the unrelated unscoped \`e2e\` package from npm — every private consumer must declare it (documented in AGENTS.md). ## Safety properties - In-repo \`publishConfig.access: "restricted"\` on the unscoped name makes any accidental hand-run \`npm publish\` **fail outright** (unscoped packages cannot be restricted). - Provenance is off for the private phase (it requires public access); the workflow env documents the launch-day revert. - \`release:public\` preserves the plain changesets publish for launch day; the script is idempotent (skips already-published versions) and restores manifests byte-for-byte. Stacked on #94. Publishing needs an npm org with private packages enabled for the \`@e2edev\` scope and a granular \`NPM_TOKEN\` with publish rights to it. ## Test plan - [x] \`node --check\` on the publish script; \`pnpm lint\` green - [ ] First real publish after merge verifies end-to-end (needs the npm org + token — see PR body) ---

title: feat(run): the embedding-host surface — e2e/run, event spine, hosted-cache seams, secret providers
body: Supersedes #94 (auto-closed when the merged #93 branch was deleted; GitHub's stack metadata blocked retargeting). All review threads from #94 — Devin's five findings and two adversarial quality passes — are addressed here, plus a final structural pass (single emitter, state-derived exit code, reporter-as-sink, one action-description owner, store validation at the read). ## Summary Everything a hosted platform needs to run e2e as its core engine, shipped as generic seams with local defaults — no host is named anywhere: - **`e2e/run`** — programmatic `run()` (no `process.exit`, `AbortSignal` cancellation, full report-1 in memory) and `RunOptions.onEvent`: every lifecycle fact as plain JSON with an emitter-stamped `seq`. The stream is the runner's **single spine**: the list reporter is itself a sink on it (`ListReporter.handle`), so the CLI and a host dashboard can never render different stories. Sinks are quarantined independently — thrown errors immediately, async rejections when they settle. Config resolves before anything is emitted, so the emitter is built **exactly once** from the reporter set actually in force (config truth, CLI value only when config itself failed). The **exit code is a fold over run state** — every result, every run error, the interrupt — never threaded by hand, so a run error recorded anywhere (collection, the body, teardown, the report write) reaches it the same way. Teardown (session store, app process) always completes before the terminal `run-finished`; failures anywhere are recorded, never thrown. A failed report write is an infrastructure error (`REPORT_WRITE_FAILED`, exit 3) with `reportPath` withheld; the credential registry is cleared on every exit path. - **Hosted-cache seams** — a host-supplied `cache.store` is exempt from the CI read-only clamp, `app.identity` keys cache/session identity logically (PR previews share traces), `buildTraceEntry`/`readTraceEntry` are exported, and **every hit is re-validated at the single read site** (`StepTraceSession.tryReplay`) through the same trace-1 framing the file store uses — a remote entry can never be trusted more loosely than a local one, whichever store produced it. - **`event.detail`** — redacted, bounded prose on driver action events. `agent/actions.ts` is the **one owner** of the committed-action model: `describeAction` yields the durable target descriptor and the prose together, and the recorded trace summary, the live event `detail`, and the relocator's candidate projection all come from it, so none can drift. Action bodies return their `RecordableAction`; one value feeds the pure detail hook and the trace-cache write. report-v1 gains `event.detail`; suiteVersion 0.6.0 → 0.7.0. - **Fill-time secret providers** — `password` may be a `SecretProvider` (vault lookup, fresh TOTP per fill). A `SecretLedger` owns the attempt's values and a memoized redactor invalidated on register; **every value ever registered keeps redacting** (rotating TOTPs leave earlier codes on screen). `E2E_USER_*` env overrides win; providers never cross a process boundary. Proven under zero-turn replay. - **A wired host demo** (`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed run demo:host`) — data-defined test → generated suite → in-process `rawConfig` run → live events with action prose → zero-turn replay, with process-group server teardown. ## Behavior note Because the exit code is derived from every recorded run error, a failure during teardown (e.g. the app process refusing to stop) now yields exit 3 instead of the pre-teardown code. Previously it appeared in the report but not in the exit code — the same "a run error is not a footnote" stance the `REPORT_WRITE_FAILED` change takes. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm check` (lint, check:spec, typecheck incl. driver drift, docs) and `pnpm check:manifest` (suiteVersion 0.6.0 → 0.7.0) - [x] 585 tests green, including new suites: event emitter/quarantine (sync + async), reporter driven by events alone (full lifecycle + config-error shape), custom-store hit re-validation, secret-ledger rotation, provider config, trace-entry hostile inputs, report-write-failure lifecycle, credential-registry clearing - [x] Per-commit standalone build+typecheck across the range; every commit conventional and single-concern - [x] Real-model validation (`gemini-3-flash`), run before the final structural pass: bench 4/4 live and 4/4 zero-turn replayed; `demo:host` recorded live then replayed zero-turn (39s → 358ms) with seq-ordered, JSON-clean events - [x] Secret-hygiene audit across the whole range: no tokens or key material in any commit ---

title: feat(backend): the backend contract (RFC0002) - one seam, driver-less targets
body: ## What Implements RFC0002 Phase A (`RFC0002.md`, included): the executor socket becomes the one extension seam, with a typed, model-free **backend** as the body of a target. - **`e2e/backend`**: `defineBackend` - a validated manifest with capability grading (`observation`, `actions`), an `spiVersion` literal, the actions ⇒ observation dependency rule, and loud INVALID_CONFIG on any malformed member. Tools never live on a backend - all model vocabulary is agent-side `defineTool`. - **Backend targets**: `targets: [{ name, platform: 'ios', backend }]` - no driver resolved or launched, no browser, `app.url` optional when every target is a backend target. Honest platform in the run header and report provenance (`driver.id: backend:`). - **The adapter**: one `DriverSession`-shaped seam over the contract, so the agent tier, judgment tier (`waitFor`/`extract` now work off-web), trace recording, metrics, and fixtures run unchanged. Every undeclared capability fails `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` at the moment of use; `screen`/`web` gate the same way. - **Lifecycle**: `init` once per worker (device boot leaves step budgets), `dispose` at shutdown (cleanup-bounded, failure = run error). - **Config**: `agent: { executor, model, maxModelCalls, context }` - a custom brain composes with the options instead of forfeiting them. ## Dead surface removed (coordinated spec edits included) `MobileTarget`/`CustomTarget` (`Target = WebTarget | BackendTarget`), the reserved `Device` fixture, `DriverAgentActions.longPress`/`tapPoint` + `ViewportPoint` (runner never called them; playwright impls removed), the `'device'` capability literal, `frameExpression`, `@types/json-schema`, 13 over-exported symbols, and the `WellKnownDriverId`-collapses-to-`string` type bug. Sweep by a review agent; every removal verified zero-consumer. ## Testing - `pnpm check` green (lint, spec compile, typecheck + driver drift, docs) - 551 e2e tests + 19 playwright tests green, including a new integration suite driving a toy in-memory backend through the real runner (lifecycle, provenance, capability gating, schema-valid report) - Live iOS simulator dogfood: step 1 of the Reminders suite passes through the full new stack (observe metrics and per-step cost now populate); step 2 still iterating on the known Reminders off-screen-fill behavior - tracked as testbed work, not harness - Known follow-ups per RFC migration: grammar-2 (`open`/`back` verbs), chassis tool absorption, playwright-as-backend ---

title: feat(backend): neutral state capability for session save/restore (RFC0002 step 2', part 1)
body: Stacked on #98. First implementation increment of the playwright-as-backend migration: grow the backend contract with the platform-neutral capabilities web needs, expressed so no platform is privileged. ## What - `defineBackend({ state: { capture, restore } })` — a **platform-neutral** state capability. The snapshot is `{ format, version, data }` where `data` is opaque JSON the harness never inspects. A browser's storage state, a device's app state, and a desktop's window state satisfy it identically. - The backend adapter wires it to `captureState`/`restoreState`, so `test.setup` + the `session:` test option (session save/restore) now work on backend targets exactly as on drivers. The old `backend targets do not support saved sessions` guard is gone. - Capability name `state` joins the gradeable set; `requires: ['state']` gates at selection. ## Not web-shaped — the litmus Per the RFC correction: if a Limrun backend couldn't implement a member without contorting to a browser's shape, the member is wrong. `state` passes — opaque snapshot in, opaque snapshot out. ## Scope **Artifacts deferred** to the playwright-backend PR on purpose: correct artifact capture needs the attempt artifact directory plumbed into the capability (where the backend writes, how size is stat'd), and that should be designed against playwright's real trace/screenshot files, not a toy that returns a fake path. Shipping it half-wired would be the 'declared but unwired' smell we already cleaned out of #98. ## Testing - New integration test: a `test.setup` seeds counter state, saves the session; an ordinary test restores it and asserts — capture + restore round-trip through the neutral capability on the toy backend. - `pnpm check` green; 555 e2e tests + 19 playwright green. ## Next in the stack The playwright backend itself: `observe`/`actions`/`locate` from the existing session, `web` as a contributed fixture, artifacts with real files, `WebTarget` as sugar, driver SPI deleted. RFC0002 step 2'. ---

title: feat(backend)!: playwright is a backend; core knows no platform
body: ## Summary RFC0002 migration step 2': `@e2edev/playwright` becomes a backend built with the public `defineBackend`, and `e2e` core keeps only the backend contract. Core has no `Web`, `browser`, `page`, `route`, or `playwright` noun left (grep `packages/e2e/src`; only the `e2e init` scaffold names the package). **Breaking.** No zero-config web target and no driver SPI: every target names its backend. ```ts import { playwright } from '@e2edev/playwright'; targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright({ browser: 'chromium' }) }], ``` ```ts import { test } from '@e2edev/playwright'; // `test` typed with the contributed `web` fixture import { expect } from 'e2e'; ``` ## What changed - **Driver SPI deleted**: `e2e/driver`, `defineDriver`, `driver:`/`browser:` target keys, top-level `browser`, implicit web target, well-known driver registry. `targets` is required; a target is `{ name, platform, backend? }`. - **Web surface left core**: `Web`, `WebRoute`, `WebResponse`, `RouteFulfillResponse`, `Cookie`, `Dialog`, `WebExpectation` live in `@e2edev/playwright`. `expect(fixture)` routes to whatever a backend attaches through `BackendFixtureContext.expectable`. - **Contract grew, platform-neutrally**: `perform`, `swipe`, `artifacts`, `app`, `url`, `version`, observation pixels; `BackendInitInfo` carries base URL, allowed origins, `testIdAttribute`, `headed`. State duties (encryption, retention, restore-replaces) are stated on the `state` capability. - **Fixture contribution completed**: contributed methods are recorded steps with harness-owned bounds, sync accessors pass through, attachments land on the running step, undeclared fixtures fail at first touch. - **Tool scoping**: `defineTool({ platforms })` and `StepExecutorContext.target`. - **Wire**: reports and session envelopes record `backend` instead of `driver`, drop `browser`/`browserVersion`/`viewport` target fields, step events use kind `backend`, `DRIVER_FAILURE` is `BACKEND_FAILURE`. Spec `suiteVersion` 0.5.0 to 0.6.0. Spec chapter 09 and `spec/api/driver.d.ts` retire in step 5. - **Docs**: `writing-a-backend`, `reference/backend`, and updated config, test, expect, app-web, errors, quickstart, agents, READMEs, AGENTS.md, RFC0002. ## Review Two rounds of independent thermo-nuclear review; all MUST/SHOULD FIX items applied and tested (adapter-level error normalization, attempt cleanup on restore failure, placeholder base URL kept out of the contract, policy errors no longer swallowed into `BACKEND_FAILURE`, batched `locate`, download waiter deadlock, artifact attribution). ## Verification | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `e2e` unit / integration | 419 / 122 passed | | `@e2edev/playwright` | 32 passed | | testbed through the real CLI | 33 passed | | real model runs (AI Gateway): act suite on gpt-5.6-luna | 3/3 passed; backend observe avg 110 ms | | lint, typecheck (3 pkgs), `check:spec`, `check:manifest`, `docs:check` | pass | ---

title: feat(agent-device): @e2edev/agent-device is a backend with trace cache support
body:
## Summary

New package `@e2edev/agent-device`: the mobile backend for `e2e`, implementing the public `e2e/backend` contract (RFC0002) over [agent-device](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device) for iOS simulators and Android emulators. The testbed declares both as targets in one config, and the same portable tests run on each. It replaces the testbed's `fixtures/agent-device.ts` tool-loop shim. Core changes: none. The package contributes the `device` fixture and an agent tool pack the same way `@e2edev/playwright` contributes `web`.

### The backend

| Member | On a device |
| --- | --- |
| `observe` | Accessibility tree projected onto the role vocabulary (iOS `Button` to `button`, `TextField` to `textbox`, `Cell` to `listitem`; Android `TextView` to `text`, `EditText` to `textbox`, layouts to `group`), identifiers under `testIdAttribute`, switch `checked` state on iOS, secure fields without values, viewport, pixels on request with every secure node's bounds painted black (a package-local PNG codec); an image that cannot be redacted is withheld. |
| `perform` | tap, doubleTap, longPress, fill, clear, check/uncheck, Enter and single-character keys, node swipe, drag. A tap/check on a `switch` lands on its innermost control, because UIKit reports a settings row as a labelled switch spanning the row with the real toggle as an unlabelled child. Inputs pass `settle: true`. Everything else is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. |
| `locate` | Every `screen` query, plus agent-device selectors through `device.locator('role=NavigationBar id=About')`. |
| `url` | `app://device/<bundle id>/<screen title>` (title from the navigation bar on iOS, the collapsing toolbar on Android). This is what makes the trace cache work: a surface without a path anchor never writes a trace, and the cache compares pathnames, so the app identity lives in the path. |
| `app` | `back`; `restart` and `clearState` when `app` is pinned. Pinned apps relaunch per attempt, so a flow needs no agent-side tool and stays grammar-only. |
| `fixtures.device` | network, airplane mode, permissions, location, appearance, orientation, biometrics, open/close/foreground app, home, back, alerts, keyboard, clipboard, `locator`. |
| `/tools` | `agentDeviceTools(...backends)`: `open_app`, `swipe`, `type_text`, `alert`, `screenshot`, scoped to the platforms of the backends passed and dispatched to the one whose attempt is running. Main entry never loads `ai`. |

### Testbed

- `e2e.device.config.ts` declares an iOS simulator and an Android emulator target, each pinned to its Settings app, with one `agentDeviceTools(ios, android)` pack. `tests-device/about` and `device` are portable and run on both targets unchanged; `ios` and `android` hold the label-bound deterministic checks, scoped with `platforms`.
- New opt-in `e2e.reminders.config.ts` + `tests-reminders/`: four long agentic Reminders sessions (batch entry via `type_text`, completion, swipe-to-delete, list management, an interruption), each claim paired with a tree check.
- `test:device:cached` runs the Settings suite twice and fails unless every passed `agent.act` step replayed from the trace cache with zero model calls (`scripts/assert-cache-replay.mjs`).

### Docs

`reference/device` page, `config`/`introduction`/`writing-a-backend` updates, package README, changeset.

## Verification

Details and numbers are in the comments below, in order: the cold-cache double run (3 of 4 `agent.act` steps replayed zero-turn, the miss explained), the Reminders stress suite (4 of 4), and the two-target run (iOS 11/11, Android 8/9 with the emulator's unsupported clipboard write since moved to the iOS file).

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check:spec`, `pnpm docs:check`: clean.
- `@e2edev/agent-device`: 50 unit tests over a scripted client; 4 integration tests on a booted iPhone 16e simulator (`E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_SIMULATOR=1`), all passing.
- Devin review: five of six comments fixed in dad7af2 (secure-field masking for artifacts, the screenshot tool, and observation pixels; abandoned commands settle before the next attempt; per-app cache anchor; check/uncheck refuse unknown toggle state; focus limited to editable fields). The sixth (device targets advertising secret filling) is answered inline: `app://` has an opaque origin, so `type_secret` is denied before any plaintext reaches the device.

title: feat(cache): gate replay on recorded end state; confirm writes by verification
body: ## Why TesterArmy's cache rollout surfaced four failure modes: replays that declared a step passed with no verification, replays that resolved ordinal targets onto the wrong row, leftover cascades from fixed names, and a pool that learned from failed runs. e2e already relocated targets by unique identity and staged writes, but it shared the first hole structurally: a full replay self-finalized when the actions ran and the pathname matched, and the recording dropped the executor's final look at the screen. On a single-page app that check proves nothing about whether a save committed. It also confirmed staged traces on any later passed step, including another `agent.act`, and on the attempt passing by itself. ## What - **End anchors** (`cache/anchors.ts`). A passing step records the relocatable descriptors that appeared between its first settled observation and its passing one: the recording run's verification made mechanical. Recorded for steps that end on the pathname they started on (the path is the postcondition otherwise), capped at 8, leaves before containers, re-minted test ids ignored in the delta. A full replay self-finalizes only while every anchor is present again with **every recorded field equal, text included**. Target relocation deliberately ignores text when a node has a name; for an anchor the text is the effect, so that looseness is not reused. Otherwise the step hands off with `end-mismatch`, and the built-in agent is told to check whether the step took effect before acting. - **Verification-step confirmation** (`cache/context.ts`, `run/steps.ts`). A staged trace is written only after an `expect` assertion, a locator `waitFor`, `agent.assert`, or `agent.waitFor` passes after it. A later act or the attempt passing confirms nothing, so a trailing act nothing asserts on is never replayed blind, and a failing run confirms only what had been verified before the failure landed. - **Eviction after repair.** An `end-mismatch` hand-off that needed further agent actions evicts the entry instead of re-staging the failed flow plus its repair. A hand-off the agent settles without acting heals the anchors in place. - Replay policy bumps to `conservative/3` (cold-starts existing caches). Spec 10/16, `e2e.d.ts`, conformance `TRACE-ANCHOR-001` plus rewritten `TRACE-REPLAY-001` / `TRACE-WRITE-001`, `suiteVersion` 0.8.0, config docs, README, and the pending `trace-cache` changeset are updated together. ## Stress tested with real model flows (gemini-3-flash) | Suite | Record | Replay | |---|---|---| | testbed bench (4 tests, 8 acts) | 26 model calls | 0 model calls, every act self-finalized in 0.4–1.6s | | testbed agent suite (8 tests, 4 acts) | 26 model calls | 6 model calls, all judgments (never cached) | - Corrupting a recorded fill to `Taxi to airprot`: all actions replayed, the anchor check found the recorded row missing, `end-mismatch` hand-off, the agent deleted the typo'd row and re-added the right one, the assertion passed. The re-staged 7-action flow that resulted is what motivated eviction-after-repair. - Seeding a duplicate `Conference flights` row: the delete replay refused to choose (`target-ambiguous`), handed off, and the agent removed both. - The churning-id page replays zero-turn; its anchors went from 8 noisy toggles to just the effect texts after ignoring re-minted test ids. ## Verification - `pnpm check` gates: lint, spec typecheck, package typecheck, docs check, manifest coupling - Unit 469, integration 129, playwright backend 86, testbed default suite 33 ## Notes for review - Rebased onto main after #97 landed: `suiteVersion` is now 0.7.0 → 0.8.0, and the replay host, recorder, and moved `describeTarget` helper are adapted to #97's shapes. - Each cached act step pays two extra observations (baseline and passing screen). Removal-only steps and checked-state changes produce no anchors; downstream assertions own those. - Testbed runs across worktrees share app ports 4272/4273; concurrent real-model runs from two sessions cross-talk through the shared in-memory store. ---

title: feat(playwright): attach to a remote browser over CDP
body: ## Summary `playwright({ connect })` attaches to a remote browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol instead of launching a local one. This is the seam a hosted-browser backend plugs into: a per-run cloud session (Kernel, Browserless) whose endpoint is provisioned only once the run starts. - `connect.cdpEndpoint` is an **async resolver**, called at worker `init` and again on any reconnect, so an endpoint not known at config load resolves each time the pool needs it. - CDP attach is **chromium-only**; the factory rejects another engine as `INVALID_CONFIG`. - A local launch skips the browser-install step it no longer needs when attaching. - `dispose` detaches the CDP session; the remote process the host owns stays alive. - The `init` abort signal is honored before the endpoint is resolved. No TesterArmy/Kernel noun enters e2e: this is a generic CDP connect option. The private Kernel backend wraps it by resolving `cdp_ws_url` from its session pool. ## Test plan - [x] Unit: factory chromium-only guard; empty/throwing resolver fails `init` as `BACKEND_FAILURE`; pre-abort short-circuits before resolving. - [x] Integration (real browser): launches Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port`, attaches through `connect`, drives a full attempt (navigate + locate + url), and asserts `dispose` detaches without killing the remote. - [x] Full `@e2edev/playwright` suite green (92 tests); `pnpm check` clean; changeset added (minor). ---

title: feat(agent): defineTool replay tiers (RFC0003 phase 1) + RFC0003/RFC0004
body: ## Summary Adds the two `defineTool` replay tiers the full-vocabulary port needs, plus the design docs for the tool-replay and data-defined-test work. **RFC0003 (agent tool replay tiers)** designs `located` (input paths that are node references, relocated against a fresh observation on replay) and `fixed-model` (one recorded model call at replay). The harness owns tool replay, reusing the grammar's relocation and settlement — the lesson from the TesterArmy cache incident, where a host-side cache self-finalized without verification. **RFC0004 (data-defined tests)** designs file-less test identity so a host runs tests straight from data rows; the file-generation workaround (the materializer) stays the interim. **Phase 1 implementation (this PR):** `ToolAnnotations.replay` widens from `'deterministic' | 'none'` to a tiered union — `{ mode: 'located', locate: string[] }` and `{ mode: 'fixed-model' }` beside the two existing modes. The bare strings stay accepted as sugar and normalize to the object form. Validation: `located` requires unique non-empty input paths; `fixed-model` requires `mutates: false`. This phase validates and records the declaration; the located/fixed-model replay wiring lands in later RFC0003 phases, so a tool declared with either tier runs live until then, exactly as `none` does. ## Test plan - [x] 8 unit tests for the tiers (sugar normalization, located path validation, fixed-model mutates guard, unknown-tier rejection). - [x] Full e2e suite green (593 tests); `pnpm check` clean; changeset added (minor). - [x] `defineTool` is a layer-2 host API, not in the sdk-0.1 spec d.ts, so no spec/schema/conformance change this phase. ---

title: fix: deep-scan runner cleanup (lifecycle, hot paths, CLI) and fallow in CI
body: ## Summary A deep scan of the runner for speed, quality, and readability, verified finding by finding against `src/` and `spec/`, and validated with the deterministic suites plus the live-model testbed suite. Ten commits, each building and passing standalone. ### Correctness - **Suite hooks on every realm** (`run/`): `afterAll` now runs for a realm a failing or timed-out test discards, and before a serial group takes over a file. Serial groups and setup tests enter suite scopes (`beforeAll`/`afterAll`) like ordinary tests; a `beforeAll` failure inside a group skips members as `hook-failed` and fails the group without retry. A retry that hits a `beforeAll` failure keeps its attempts and reports `failed`, not `skipped`. A worker that cannot re-import a unit's module no longer drops the unit's tests from the report. - **Support layers**: a shared object reference in `agent.act` params or `web.evaluate` values is no longer rejected as a cycle; trace start/end anchors pass the secret redactor (a redacted path marks the trace non-replayable); the start-path precondition compares by pathname like the end postcondition; a platform-filtered setup test can no longer be promoted to run on a target it excluded; negated assertions with a sub-second budget can pass; `toHaveCount` polls within its assertion deadline. - **Playwright backend**: `web.route` registers on the browser context, so routes are attempt-scoped as the spec requires (they survive `app.restart()`, `clearState()`, session restore, and apply before the first page). One deadline bounds a whole observation including nested frames. An observation cancelled mid-capture no longer publishes its handle generation over the caller's live one. A dialog handler that returns without deciding has the dialog dismissed and fails the next step. Browser install and launch honour the init signal. - **Agent**: a `defineTool` tool that throws returns the failure to the model as text instead of failing the step as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`; mutating project tools are refused at the action ceiling before running; the wind-down window scales with the step budget (`min(60s, budget/4)`) instead of a flat 60 s that consumed half a default step; an executor bringing its own model no longer resolves the configured one; late accounting from an abandoned executor cannot land on the next step; transcripts are redacted before being written. - **CLI/config/report**: usage errors exit 2 (spec 06), `--help`/`--version` exit 0; `--workers`/`--retries` obey the config bounds (`--workers 0` used to deadlock the scheduler); a live `agent.visionModel` instance is reduced to its identity before the config digest; non-array `targets` is `INVALID_CONFIG`; `run.status` can be `blocked` for serial-only runs; `defineBackend` binds fixture factories; the live status block stops repainting after the run ends. ### Speed - Each worker imported every unit's test file twice; now the collect-time import is adopted as the first realm. Every import registered a new, never-removed tsx loader hook; one namespaced loader is registered per process. Session states are decrypted once per worker. Artifact size/sha256 are computed off the event loop. Work plans and registered-test lookups are map-based. - `locate` no longer derives a document-wide CSS selector per matched element on every assertion poll (nothing consumed it); the tree walk memoizes role/name/direct text per element and reuses the computed style it already holds; each document is read with one fewer protocol round trip. - Replay relocation projects nodes once per observation; wire regexps are compiled once; text sanitizing and UTF-8 truncation are single-pass; value matchers format failure messages only on failure; test discovery prunes dot-directories; `waitFor` no longer takes five throwaway observations per judgment interval; the initial screen tree in the step prompt is compacted like later snapshots. ### Readability and hygiene - `fallow` dead-code analysis is added as `pnpm check:dead-code` (part of `pnpm check`) and to the spec CI job (`.fallowrc.json`). Its findings are fixed: the dead `internal/backend-text` module, `selectorExpression`, unused getters and exports, one definition of `TextMatch`, `translateLocatorError` renamed off the core translator. - Shared helpers replace duplicates: `boundedOperation`/`recordPolicyEvent` (act and invocation tiers), `collapseText`, `config/validate.ts`, `samePathname`. `RefRegistry` is extracted from `PlaywrightSurface`; the attempt status rule in `runAttempt` is a named function. Docs and spec prose updated where behavior changed (`test.mdx`, `app-web.mdx`, spec 08/10). Changesets added for both packages. ## Validation - `pnpm check` green (lint, fallow, spec typecheck, package typecheck, fern check). - `e2e`: 626 tests (14 new: realm teardown, serial/setup suite hooks, retry+hook status, attempt-scoped routes, JSON DAG, CLI exit codes and bounds, fixture binding, decide/anchor rules, UTF-8 and control-char edge cases). `@e2edev/playwright`: 87 tests. Testbed: 33 passed. - Live model suite (`test:agent --no-cache --debug`, gemini-3-flash via gateway): 8/8 passed on the rebased build. Phase split: model 571.7 s over 26 calls, observe 2.2 s total (86 ms avg), action 0.3 s total. ## Follow-ons deliberately left Lazy element handles per observation, installing the in-page reader once via init script, the worker cap slot held by retiring workers, single-pass report aggregation, and splitting `act.ts`/`runner.ts`/`resolve.ts`/`build.ts`. ---

title: refactor(cache): the step session owns its probes; verification steps declare themselves
body: Stacked on #103. A code-quality pass over the end-anchor and verification-step work from that PR. Behaviour is preserved; the one intentional change is called out below. ## Why The hardening in #103 is right, but its structure spread each idea across two layers: - The baseline probe lived in the session and the passing-screen probe in the dispatch, with the same "rethrow hard stops, otherwise stage nothing" policy written twice and a `baselineUnavailable` flag plus two extra `stage` parameters to carry the result between them. - `flushStagedTraces` still took a three-valued outcome after the rule change made `'passed'` and `'failed'` behave identically. - `verifyAnchors` was `relocate` copy-pasted with a different predicate, and the anchor check re-projected every node once per anchor. - Whether a step verifies was inferred from api-name strings in `run/steps.ts`, even though every call site already knew. ## What changed - **`StepTraceSession.begin(host)`** captures the start path and baseline screen, then attempts replay. **`stage(summary)`** probes the passing screen and end path itself. One `probeScreen` holds the error policy. Deleted `baselineUnavailable`, `wantsStage`, the `endPath`/`endNodes` parameters, and the try/catch in `act.ts`. - **`ReplayHost`** exposes `observe()` raw and `observeSettled()`. Replay no longer settles raw captures on its own, so `ReplayObservation.shape` and the extra host method are gone. `relocate` and `verifyAnchors` share one `pollSettled` loop; `anchorsPresent` projects each observation once. - **`isRuntimeHardStop`** beside `RUNTIME_CODES` replaces five inline copies. - **`flushStagedTraces(context, lastVerifiedStepIndex)`**. `AttemptCacheOutcome` is gone; the runner skips the flush for an interrupted attempt. - **Verification declared at the source.** `StepRecorder.run(..., { verifies: true })` from `expect`, `locator.waitFor`, `agent.assert`, and `agent.waitFor`, read back as `steps.lastVerifiedStepIndex`. `isVerificationStep` is gone. - `withoutTestId` replaces the `void` destructure hacks, `evict()` dedupes the two deletion sites, and the anchor cap has one owner. ### Behaviour change `verifyAnchors` now treats a surface that cannot be observed as a mismatch (hand off to the executor) instead of throwing a cache error into an otherwise passed step. Hard stops still propagate. ### Report detail Replay's settled looks now emit one observation event instead of one per poll, since they go through the dispatch's own settled observe. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint` clean. - Unit: 486 passed. Integration: 142 passed. - Real model (gemini-3-flash via the gateway, ~100 s per act that night): | Run | Result | Model calls | |---|---|---| | Bench record (clean cache) | 3/4 passed, 7 entries confirmed | 25 | | Bench replay | 4/4 passed, 8 entries | 2 | | Bench, one recorded fill corrupted | passed via `end-mismatch` hand-off, entry evicted | 4 | | Agent suite record (clean cache) | 8/8 passed, 4 entries | 27 | | Agent suite replay | 8/8 passed | 6 | The bench record's long journey hit the 300 s test timeout on gateway latency; its last act was correctly left unconfirmed and recorded on the replay run. The remaining agent-suite calls are judgments, which are never cached. ## Coverage note The unit test for `'interrupted'` on `flushStagedTraces` was removed with the parameter. The rule now lives in `execute.ts` and has no direct test; an integration test that interrupts an attempt would restore that coverage. ---

title: feat(cache): gate replay on recorded end state; confirm writes by verification
body:
Replaces #103 and #108 as one PR. Same commits as the stacked pair, plus one structural commit on top; nothing here depends on either of them staying open.

## Why

TesterArmy's cache rollout surfaced four failure modes: replays that declared a step passed with no verification, replays that resolved ordinal targets onto the wrong row, leftover cascades from fixed names, and a pool that learned from failed runs. e2e already relocated targets by unique identity and staged writes, but it shared the first hole structurally: a full replay self-finalized when the actions ran and the pathname matched, and the recording dropped the executor's final look at the screen. On a single-page app that check proves nothing about whether a save committed. It also confirmed staged traces on any later passed step, including another `agent.act`, and on the attempt passing by itself.

## What

### Hardening (from #103)

- **End anchors** (`cache/anchors.ts`). A passing step records the relocatable descriptors that appeared between its first settled observation and its passing one: the recording run's verification made mechanical. Recorded for steps that end on the pathname they started on (the path is the postcondition otherwise), capped at 8, leaves before containers, re-minted test ids ignored in the delta. A full replay self-finalizes only while every anchor is present again with **every recorded field equal, text included**. Otherwise the step hands off with `end-mismatch`, and the built-in agent is told to check whether the step took effect before acting.
- **Verification-step confirmation** (`cache/context.ts`, `run/steps.ts`). A staged trace is written only after an `expect` assertion, a locator `waitFor`, `agent.assert`, or `agent.waitFor` passes after it. A later act or the attempt passing confirms nothing, so a trailing act nothing asserts on is never replayed blind, and a failing run confirms only what had been verified before the failure landed.
- **Eviction after repair.** An `end-mismatch` hand-off that needed further agent actions evicts the entry instead of re-staging the failed flow plus its repair. A hand-off the agent settles without acting heals the anchors in place.
- Replay policy bumps to `conservative/3` (cold-starts existing caches). Spec 10/16, `e2e.d.ts`, conformance `TRACE-ANCHOR-001` plus rewritten `TRACE-REPLAY-001` / `TRACE-WRITE-001`, `suiteVersion` 0.8.0, config docs, README, and the pending `trace-cache` changeset are updated together.

### Structure (from #108, then one more pass)

- **The session owns its probes.** `StepTraceSession` takes its host in the constructor, captures the baseline screen and start path in `begin()`, and probes the passing screen and end path itself. One `probeScreen` holds the "rethrow hard stops, otherwise stage nothing" policy. `ReplayHost` exposes `observe()` raw and `observeSettled()`; replay no longer settles raw captures on its own, and `relocate` and `verifyAnchors` share one `pollSettled` loop.
- **One write-side decision.** `conclude(outcome, summary)` holds the whole table: passed after a repaired end-mismatch evicts, passed otherwise stages, failed after a consumed replay evicts, cancelled does nothing. `act.ts` makes one call per branch instead of choosing between `stageTrace` and `evictConsumedReplay`.
- **One hand-off path.** `begin()` computes a single `stopReason` up front; the duplicated end-mismatch and divergence blocks collapse into `handOff()`, and the store read plus trace-1 revalidation moves into `readEntry()`.
- **Anchors reuse relocation.** `relocate.ts` exports `descriptorTiers`, `fieldsEqual`, and `describeNodes`; `anchorsPresent` is one expression over them, and `describeNodes` keeps main's per-observation projection cache (#107). The two deliberate differences (text always required, presence not uniqueness) are the only anchor-specific code left.
- **Verification declared at the source.** `StepRecorder.run(..., { verifies: true })` from the four verifying call sites, read back as `steps.lastVerifiedStepIndex`. The agent `step` helper takes it as its own argument. `flushStagedTraces(context, lastVerifiedStepIndex)` lost its three-valued outcome; the runner skips the flush for an interrupted attempt.
- **One path rule.** `samePathname` in `decide.ts` is a plain pathname comparison used at both ends of a trace; the two call sites that can see an unknown live path decide that case themselves. Main had already made the start-path check pathname-only (#107), so this is structure, not behaviour.
- `isRuntimeHardStop` beside `RUNTIME_CODES` replaces five inline copies; `withoutTestId` replaces the `void` destructure hacks; `evict()` dedupes the deletion sites.

### Behaviour changes beyond #103's feature work

- `verifyAnchors` treats a surface that cannot be observed as a mismatch (hand off) instead of throwing a cache error into an otherwise passed step. Hard stops still propagate.
- Replay's settled looks emit one observation event instead of one per poll, since they go through the dispatch's own settled observe.

## Real-model evidence (gemini-3-flash, run on the #103 / #108 code)

| Run | Result | Model calls |
|---|---|---|
| Bench record (clean cache) | 3/4 passed, 7 entries confirmed | 25 |
| Bench replay | 4/4 passed, 8 entries, every act self-finalized in 0.4–1.6s | 2 |
| Bench, one recorded fill corrupted | passed via `end-mismatch` hand-off, entry evicted | 4 |
| Agent suite record (clean cache) | 8/8 passed, 4 entries | 27 |
| Agent suite replay | 8/8 passed | 6 |

- Corrupting a recorded fill to `Taxi to airprot`: all actions replayed, the anchor check found the recorded row missing, `end-mismatch` hand-off, the agent deleted the typo'd row and re-added the right one, the assertion passed. The re-staged 7-action flow that resulted is what motivated eviction-after-repair.
- Seeding a duplicate `Conference flights` row: the delete replay refused to choose (`target-ambiguous`), handed off, and the agent removed both.
- The churning-id page replays zero-turn; its anchors went from 8 noisy toggles to just the effect texts after ignoring re-minted test ids.
- The final structural commit was not re-run against a live model; it is covered by the unit and integration suites below.

## Verification

Rebased onto `main` after #102, #104, #105, and #107 landed. Conflicts were in `step-cache.ts`, `recorder.ts`, `relocate.ts`, `decide.ts`, and `execute.ts`; main's redacted anchor paths, projection cache, `classifyAttemptStatus`, and pathname-only start check are all kept.

On the final commit:

- `pnpm check` passes: lint, dead-code, spec typecheck, typecheck for every package, docs check. Fallow's four unused-class-member findings and the zod dev-dependency note are identical on `origin/main`.
- `pnpm vitest run` in `packages/e2e`: 63 files, 669 tests passed (unit and integration).

## Notes for review

- Each cached act step pays two extra settled observations (baseline and passing screen) in read-write mode; read-only runs pay neither. Stated in the `step-cache.ts` header.
- Removal-only steps and checked-state changes produce no anchors; downstream assertions own those.
- The unit test for `'interrupted'` on `flushStagedTraces` went with the parameter. The rule now lives in `execute.ts`; an integration test that interrupts an attempt would restore direct coverage.

title: feat(artifacts): ArtifactStore — hand every artifact to a host store as produced
body: ## Summary The cloud seam for evidence, the way `TraceCacheStore` is for traces. Until now a host that wanted artifacts in its own storage had to read the report's relative paths back off the artifacts directory after the run. That was coupled to the on-disk layout, a needless disk round-trip, batched at run end so a live dashboard never saw a screenshot mid-run, and lost with the temp dir if the worker died. (This is exactly the hack the TesterArmy draft shipped with; this PR is what replaces it.) - `artifacts` accepts `{ kinds, store }` beside the bare kinds array. `store.put(artifact)` receives each artifact **the moment it is complete on disk** — bytes, size, sha256, mediaType, report-relative path, run/test/attempt identity, and the producing step — and returns its own reference, recorded on the `ArtifactRecord` as `ref` beside the local path. - The plug point is `createAttemptArtifacts`, where every artifact is already registered and hashed. With a store the file is read once, hashed from that buffer, and handed over; without a store the streaming measure path is byte-for-byte unchanged. - A failed `put` never fails the run: the record keeps its path and simply carries no `ref`. An empty ref is ignored. - A store is a live value: validated structurally like `cache.store`, kept out of the config digest so the array and object forms digest identically, and (like every live value) never crosses a process boundary. - report-v1 gains the optional `artifact.ref` (`suiteVersion` 0.8.0 → 0.9.0). Spec 05/13, the config and embedding docs, and `e2e.d.ts` describe it. No platform noun enters e2e. A TesterArmy R2 store is ~10 lines of `uploadObject`. ## Test plan - [x] Unit: the hook with a capturing store (bytes, digest, identity, step, ref), a failing store (path kept, no ref, no throw), an empty ref and a missing file, and the store-less streaming path unchanged. - [x] Unit: config resolution for both forms, unknown-key / non-store / unknown-kind rejection, `artifactsExplicit` semantics, and digest equality with and without a store. - [x] 676 e2e tests green after a fresh build; `pnpm check` (lint, spec, typecheck, docs) and `check:manifest` clean; dead-code gate exit 0 (its findings are pre-existing on main). ---

title: feat(agent)!: runner ships no agent; harness owns hand-off, replay fidelity, settling
body: ## Summary The agent layer in e2e is now the socket and the chassis only; the brain moves to a private package. Everything that makes the runner more reliable for *any* executor lands here: hand-off between steps, replay fidelity, settling, stable node ids. Measured on new long-flow, hand-off, hostile and cache benches with a repeat harness, across gpt-5.6-luna, gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3-flash. Three commits, each builds standalone: 1. `feat(playwright)`: stable per-element node ids, row/cell roles, select options as nodes, lenient option labels, request-aware settle. 2. `feat(agent)!`: `createAgent` removed; chassis gains `prepareMessages` (carry-forward, `{ messages, stop }`), `providerOptions`, temperature 0, tentative verdicts, `StepVerdict.facts`; ledger `did:/saw:/noted:/observed:` with value-based compaction; trace cache records run-time-value gaps, end state waited for on replay, and row keys for relocation (policy `conservative/3`); judgment-tier settling; gateway stall guard; `agent.judgments` config key. 3. `test(testbed)`: benches and `bench-repeat.mjs`; agentic suites load their executor from `E2E_AGENT_MODULE`. ## Breaking - `createAgent` is gone from `e2e/agent`. Set `agent.executor` (or `agent` to the executor). Without one, deterministic tests and `assert`/`waitFor`/`extract` run; the first `agent.act()` fails with `INVALID_CONFIG`. - `createToolLoopExecutor`'s `compactMessages` is replaced by `prepareMessages`. - Asserts route through the executor only with `agent.judgments: 'executor'`; the default is the model judgment tier. - Replay policy version bumped; existing trace caches cold-start. ## Numbers Long-flow bench (procurement cycle + one-step wizard), gemini-3.8-flash, cache off, before vs after the harness work with the same brain: 96 → 45 model calls, 877k → 186k input tokens, $0.56 → $0.16, 471 s → 124 s, both tests pass in every run. Repeat runs (`bench-repeat.mjs`): luna 10/10 runs, gemini-3.8-flash 8/8, jitter 8/8, cache-on long flows 6/6 after the replay fixes (was 1/6 before them), hostile suite 8/8 (luna) and 4/4 (gemini) cache off, 5/5 cache on with zero-turn replay of the library steps. ## Spec and docs Spec 02/05/10/16 and `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` updated (`ExecutorObservation.path`, `StepVerdict.facts`, `RUNTIME_CODES`, `agent.judgments`; ledger and trace-cache prose). Fern agents/quickstart/introduction rewritten around the chassis. Two changesets (e2e minor with breaking note, playwright minor). No `spec/schema` or conformance manifest changes (`pnpm check:manifest` clean). ## Verification `pnpm check` green; 633 e2e tests and 90 playwright tests pass. Private agent smoke-tested through `E2E_AGENT_MODULE` against the bench suite (4/4). ## Follow-ups - Port the removed agent-specific integration tests (observe wait, quiet-turn stall guard, batching) into the private agent package; they need e2e's fixture app and scripted-model helpers, which are not exported. - End-anchor hardening from the other worktree is partly superseded by recorded end texts; reconcile. - `agent.assert` re-judge on screen change (spec change) not done. ---

title: feat(agent)!: stable node ids, chassis hooks, stricter replay
body:
Rebased replacement for #112 (closed as stale). Reconciled with #110 (end anchors), #111, #114 (`@e2edev` scope) and the version-packages commit.

## Summary

Mechanism only, no policy. This PR gives executors a more faithful observation to work from and makes trace replay stricter about what it recorded. The built-in agent's behaviour is unchanged apart from the name of its history hook. Everything opinionated that came out of the long-flow work (screen-diff agent, ledger hand-off format, settling waits, temperature, stall guard, discarded batched verdicts) is left out; the TesterArmy agent carries what it needs on top of the public chassis.

Two commits:

1. `feat(playwright)`: stable per-element node ids (stamped on the element, seeded through the `RefRegistry`), `row`/`cell`/`columnheader` roles for tables, closed selects list their options as child nodes.
2. `feat(agent)!`: chassis `prepareMessages(messages, turn)` replaces `compactMessages` (result carries forward; may return `{ messages, stop }`), `providerOptions` on the chassis and `createAgent`, `ExecutorObservation.path`, exports (`isDefinedTool`, `toolAppliesTo`, `PreparedTurn`, `PreparedMessages`, `RUNTIME_CODES`). Trace cache: run-time typed values recorded as gaps, `endWaitMs` so replay waits for the recorded anchors as long as the recording did, and a row key (`within`) required for relocation. Replay policy `conservative/3`.

## Breaking

- `createToolLoopExecutor`'s `compactMessages` is replaced by `prepareMessages`.
- Replay policy version bumped; existing trace caches cold-start.

## Left out on purpose

The long-flow, hand-off and hostile benches, the repeat harness, the screen-update agent, the `did:/saw:/noted:` ledger, request-aware settling, judgment-tier settling, temperature 0, the gateway stall guard and tentative verdicts. The benches are parked on `t3code/testbed-long-bench` for a follow-up; the rest belongs in the agent that wants it, or comes back later as explicit options.

## Spec and docs

Spec 10 (`endWaitMs`, container keys, run-time-value gaps) and 16 (`prepareMessages`, `providerOptions`, `path`) plus `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`. Two changesets. `pnpm check:manifest` clean.

## Verification

`pnpm check` green; e2e, playwright and agent-device suites pass (counts in the PR checks).

title: chore(release)!: publish under the @e2edev scope as restricted packages
body:
## Summary

Private-phase distribution: every package publishes to npmjs under the `e2edev` org as a **restricted** package. This replaces the closed #95 plan (tarball-only rename to `@e2edev/e2e` plus a consumer-side `"e2e": "npm:@e2edev/e2e"` alias), whose alias key was the only thing keeping pnpm's peer auto-install from fetching the unrelated unscoped `e2e`.

- **Core package renamed in-repo.** `e2e` → `@e2edev/e2e`; `@e2edev/playwright` and `@e2edev/agent-device` keep their names; testbed → `@e2edev/testbed`. Entry points follow the name (`@e2edev/e2e/agent|backend|run`). Covers source, tests, the `e2e init` templates, spec + its tsconfig path map, fern docs, READMEs, pending changesets, workflows, fallow config, lockfile. The `e2e` CLI binary keeps its name.
- **Publish config.** `access: restricted`, `provenance: false` on all three (npm only attests public packages), `tag: beta` unchanged; `.changeset/config.json` is restricted too. `release.yml` drops `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` and the OIDC `id-token` permission; auth is the `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
- **Docs.** Every `npx e2e` becomes `npx --no-install e2e`: the unscoped `e2e` on npmjs is a foreign package that npx would otherwise download. CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS describe the private phase and the token requirement. A changeset records the rename as a minor on all three.

Before the first publish: the `e2edev` npm org needs a paid plan for private packages, and `NPM_TOKEN` must be a granular token with read/write on the `@e2edev` **scope** (not a single package) so first publishes of new names work.

Downstream: the TesterArmy app's `link:` deps and `e2e/...` imports become `@e2edev/e2e/...`; the alias goes away.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm run check` (lint, dead code, spec typecheck, package typecheck, fern) green.
- [x] `@e2edev/e2e` 678 tests, `@e2edev/playwright` 97, `@e2edev/agent-device` 50 (+4 skipped), testbed 33 — all green after a fresh build.
- [x] `pnpm publish --dry-run --no-git-checks --tag beta` in each package: scoped name, tag beta, restricted access; packed core manifest rewrites `workspace:*` to a concrete version.
- [x] `changeset status` resolves all three packages.
- [x] No bare `e2e` import specifier, `--filter e2e`, or `node_modules/e2e/` left outside the historical RFC0001 text.

title: fix(playwright): provision the browser in a runner-side prepare hook, narrated through the reporter
body: ## Problem On a machine without Playwright browsers, `e2e run` looked hung on a spinner for the whole download. The install ran inside the backend's `init` hook, in the worker, piping the Playwright CLI's progress to stderr. Since #89 the list reporter repaints its live status block every 120 ms with a cursor-up erase sequence, which wiped the download output underneath it as fast as it appeared. Reproduced under a pseudo-TTY with an empty `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Two more problems came with that placement: - The download counted against `launchTimeout` (60 s). On a slow connection the boot failed and, because init is memoized per worker, every test on that worker failed with it. - Each worker ran its own `playwright install`, serialized only by the CLI's registry lock. ## Change - **`prepare` backend hook.** Runs once per run and target in the runner process, after backend validation and before any worker starts, outside every launch budget. Only the run's interrupt cuts it short. Failures translate through the same taxonomy as the worker's lifecycle hooks (infrastructure, phase `launch`) and end the run before any test executes. - **`notice` run event** (`{ target, message }`). The runner emits it from the hook's `log` callback, so the CLI and host sinks see the same story. - **List reporter** prints notices as permanent lines above the live block, erasing and repainting the block around each one. - **Playwright backend** moves the install from `init` to `prepare` and forwards the CLI's stdout/stderr through `log` one complete line at a time instead of piping to `process.stderr`. - **Live status** treats a pty reporting `columns === 0` as unknown width rather than clamping every line to four characters. Docs: `prepare` row and `BackendPrepareInfo` in the backend reference, `notice` in the embedding event union. Changeset marks `@e2edev/e2e` and `@e2edev/playwright` minor. ## Verification - e2e: 682 tests pass; Playwright: 98 pass (unit + integration). New coverage: the hook is bound on the handle, the runner sequences `prepare` before `init` with its notices before the first `test-started`, a failing hook ends the run with no worker booted, the reporter prints a notice above the block, and the installer receives `log` and `signal`. - Full monorepo typecheck and `oxlint` clean. - Real first run under a pseudo-TTY with an empty browser cache: every download line prints permanently with the progress counter repainted beneath it. The first test's own duration dropped from 16.9 s to 2.2 s because the download no longer runs inside it. Before, the transcript showed each spinner repaint erasing the download lines: ``` Downloading missing Playwright browsers (first run): chromium... [2A[0J⠙ pl… 0/… ``` After: ``` e2e run 01a06977-… (targets: web) ℹ Downloading missing Playwright browsers (first run): chromium... ℹ Downloading Chrome for Testing 149.0.7827.55 (playwright chromium v1228) from https://cdn.playwright.dev/… ℹ |■■■■■■■■ | 10% of 171 MiB … ℹ Browser download complete. ⠋ playground renders and navigates [web] 0/2 done · 1 running · 1 waiting ``` ---

title: feat(config)!: schemeless app URLs, no production gate, agent-ready init scaffold
body: ## Summary `e2e init` did not work out of the box against a real host: pointing the scaffold at `tester.army` required adding `https://`, `environment: 'production'`, and `allowProduction: true`. This removes all three requirements and makes the scaffold agent-ready. - **Schemeless URLs.** `app.url` and `APP_URL` no longer need a scheme. `tester.army` becomes `https://tester.army`; `localhost:3000` becomes `http://localhost:3000`. The loopback check chooses the scheme, so plain HTTP still only reaches loopback hosts. `localhost:3000` parses as scheme `localhost:` under WHATWG rules, so only `scheme://` counts as explicit. - **`allowProduction` removed** from `AppConfig`, the resolver, the report target, `report-v1.schema.json`, and the spec API d.ts files. Passing it now fails as an unknown app key (`INVALID_CONFIG`). The report target no longer carries it either. - **`app.environment` no longer required.** It remains a label for the report and the cache/session identity digest. Omitted, it defaults to `test` for loopback, `.localhost`, and `.test` hosts and to `production` for every other host. `ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED` and `PRODUCTION_NOT_ALLOWED` are retired. - **Agent-ready scaffold.** `e2e init` writes `app: { url: 'localhost:3000' }`, `agent: createAgent({ system })`, and one `playwright()` web target, so a new project has an agent to shape from the first run. Because `ai` is an optional peer, `init` warns with the install command when `package.json` does not declare it. - Spec (`05-config.md`, `13-reporting.md`, `14-security.md`, conformance `suiteVersion` 0.9.0 to 0.10.0), fern docs (quickstart, CLI, config, errors), and the three testbed configs are synced. Changeset marks a minor bump for `@e2edev/e2e`. ## Breaking - Report `targets[].allowProduction` is gone from report-1; `environment` remains. Readers that require the field must drop that requirement. - `allowProduction` is rejected as an unknown key. Delete it from configs. - A non-loopback host without `environment` now resolves to `production` instead of failing. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run check:spec`, `pnpm run docs:check` clean - [x] `pnpm run test`: 680 + 97 + 50 tests pass across the three packages - [x] New unit tests: scheme inference (host, path, IPv6 loopback, query rejection), environment defaults, rejected `allowProduction` key, scaffold content - [x] Real CLI run with `app: { url: 'tester.army' }` and the scaffold example test passes repeatedly (`app.open()` + `toHaveURL('/')`) ---

title: feat(agent-device): install builds with the appPath option and device.installApp
body: ## Summary The agent-device backend assumed the app under test was already installed on the simulator or emulator. This PR lets it install the build itself, through the install commands the `agent-device` SDK already exposes. - **`appPath` backend option.** An iOS `.app` bundle or Android `.apk`, resolved against the working directory, installed once per worker after `devices.boot` and before the first attempt. Without `app`, the bundle id or package agent-device reports becomes the pinned app, so `agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', appPath: './build/MyApp.app' })` is a complete target and also declares `app.restart` and `app.clearState`. A failed install fails init before anything opens; a new worker installs again on re-init. - **`device.installApp(appPath, { app?, reinstall? })`.** A plain install replaces the binary and keeps its data. `reinstall: true` removes the app first, using `app` or the pinned app, and is `INVALID_STATE` when neither names one. Resolves to the identity to `openApp` the build by. Recorded as a `device.installApp` step like every other fixture method. - Docs: package README, fern `reference/device` and `reference/config` pages, and a minor changeset for `@e2edev/agent-device`. Deliberately left out: no `uninstallApp` (the SDK client at 0.20.10 only has it as a CLI command; reinstall covers the clean-slate case) and no agent tool (installing is a deterministic arrangement step, not something the model should decide). ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm --filter @e2edev/agent-device test:unit` — 54 passed, 4 new (init install with and without a pinned app, install failure at init, fixture install/reinstall and the no-app reinstall error) - [x] `pnpm check` (oxlint, dead code, spec, typecheck, fern docs) passes - [ ] Not run against a live simulator; `test:simulator` is the place for a live install case if we want one ---

title: fix(run): Ctrl-C ends the run at once and tears the backend down
body:
## Problem

Ctrl-C during a device run did not end the process, and the agent-device session was left running.

Reproduced with a fake file-logging backend and real `SIGINT`s to the process group:

- **First Ctrl-C only ended the test when its timeout fired.** The interrupt was threaded through harness calls only, so a body not calling the harness at that moment (a sleep, a slow device command) held the attempt until `timeout` — five minutes with the device config.
- **Second Ctrl-C hard-killed the runner and orphaned the worker.** The runner used `process.once`, so the second signal hit Node's default exit. The worker ignores SIGINT by design and kept running: the device kept being driven, `dispose` never ran, `sessions.close()` never happened.

## Fix

- `cli/signals.ts` (new): the Ctrl-C ladder is the CLI's. `SignalLadder` arms `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`: the first signal aborts `interruptSignal`, the second aborts `forceSignal`, the third exits 130. The state is the two signals themselves, no counter. `run()` installs no process handlers and never exits the process; a host passes `interruptSignal` and the new `forceSignal` option.
- `run/execute.ts`: on a worker process (`isolated`) the test body is raced against the interrupt, so the attempt ends immediately with status `interrupted` and moves to bounded cleanup; the abandoned body goes down with the worker. In-process `rawConfig` runs share the host's process and cannot abandon a body, so there the interrupt ends the attempt at the body's next harness call or its timeout, as before.
- `run/runner.ts`: bridges both external signals into the run, enforces forced ⇒ graceful once, emits `run-interrupted`, and keeps the bridges armed through teardown and the report.
- `run/scheduler.ts`: `forceSignal` and `forceGraceMs` are required options. A forced interrupt sends `terminate` to every busy worker (retired ones already hold a shorter kill) and kills it after the force budget; a terminated worker's exit is not reported as `WORKER_EXIT` (per-worker `terminated`, not a scheduler-global).
- `worker/protocol.ts`, `worker/session.ts`: `terminate` disposes the backend beside the running unit; disposal is memoized across shutdown/terminate.
- `worker/entry.ts`: on IPC `disconnect` (runner gone for any reason) the worker terminates itself; disposal is already bounded by the cleanup budget, and the outbox flush now is too.
- `run/in-process.ts`: `terminate` is the graceful close (no process to take an abandoned unit down); only `run-unit` is dropped while closing.
- `run/events.ts`, `report/list.ts`: `run-interrupted` event (`graceful` | `forced`), acknowledged immediately so a bounded teardown is not mistaken for a hang.

Docs updated in `reference/cli.mdx` (Signals) and `reference/embedding.mdx` (`forceSignal`, event union, in-process caveat). Changeset: `@e2edev/e2e` patch, noting that `run()` no longer handles process signals.

Not in scope: the agent-device daemon is a shared background service that outlives clients by design. e2e closes its session on dispose; stopping the daemon remains `agent-device daemon stop`.

## Tests

- `tests/integration/interrupt-signals.test.ts` (new): spawns the built CLI in its own process group and asserts (1) one Ctrl-C ends a sleeping test at once, disposes, exits 130; (2) a second Ctrl-C during a stuck `afterEach` forces dispose well inside the cleanup budget and still writes the report; (3) a SIGKILLed runner leaves no worker behind — it disposes and exits on its own.
- `tests/unit/cli-signals.test.ts` (new): the ladder's three rungs and handler release.
- `tests/unit/scheduler.test.ts`: forced interrupt terminates busy workers at once; a worker ignoring `terminate` is killed after the force budget.
- `tests/unit/report-list.test.ts`: the interrupt acknowledgement lines.
- `parallel-workers` interrupt expectation tightened (no longer accepts `timed-out`); `run-events` expects the new event.

`pnpm -w lint`, typecheck, `docs:check`, `check:dead-code`, unit (543) and integration suites pass. One integration test, `agent-act › forces a verdict when the model repeats itself`, fails identically with main's own sources at the rebase base (`44ce280`) in this environment and is unrelated to this change.

title: fix(run): run hooks in lifecycle-spec order with per-hook cleanup budgets
body: ## Summary `test.beforeEach` / `afterEach` / `beforeAll` / `afterAll` did not follow `spec/11-lifecycle.md`. Five defects, all confirmed against the built runner before fixing: - **Cross-scope order ignored nesting.** Hooks ran in file declaration order, so a file-level `beforeEach` declared below a `test.describe` ran after the group's own hook, and `afterEach` was mirrored the wrong way. Now `beforeEach` runs outer scope to inner (declaration order within a scope) and `afterEach` inner to outer (reverse declaration within a scope), wherever the hooks sit in the file. - **A describe's `afterAll` waited for the whole file.** Sibling describes A and B saw A's teardown run after B's tests. A scope now closes as soon as no remaining pair in the realm needs it. - **Same-titled sibling describes shared hooks.** Scopes were keyed by title path. They are now the registration's own group nodes. - **`afterEach` had dead fixtures after a body timeout.** Fixtures kept the body's aborted signal and expired deadline, so any `screen`/`app`/`device` call in teardown failed with `operation cancelled`. A new `AttemptBudget` gives each `afterEach` hook its own `cleanupTimeout` budget; the locator engine, the agent, and the SPI fixture context read it per call. The agent-device `device` fixture was snapshotting `context.signal` once and now reads it per call too; the SPI doc states the contract. - **Schema violation.** An `afterAll` failure at file scope wrote an empty `scopeId` (schema requires `minLength: 1`). Scope ids are now `file` or the group title path. Structural changes from the follow-up review: `RegisteredHook` is a discriminated union (`TestHook | SuiteHook`) so the executor and realm manager drop their `as TestFn` / `as never` casts; one `runHook` helper bounds every suite and teardown hook; the realm tracks entered scopes in a single ordered map; `LocatorEngine` takes the budget as a typed option instead of getters sprinkled through object literals. Docs: hook rows and a hook-order paragraph in `reference/test.mdx`. Changeset: patch for `@e2edev/e2e` and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ## Test plan - [x] New unit test `packages/e2e/tests/unit/realm.test.ts` pins the ordering rules on the realm manager alone (cross-scope hook order, scope close timing, same-titled siblings, failed `beforeAll` semantics, suite-hook timeouts and `scopeId`). - [x] `runner-lifecycle.test.ts`: the order test now mixes declaration positions; seven new end-to-end cases cover scope teardown timing with same-titled groups, serial member hooks with nested scopes, `beforeEach` failure, `afterEach` primary vs secondary errors, live fixtures in `afterEach` after a timeout, an `afterEach` hook overrunning `cleanupTimeout` while the next hook still runs, and suite-hook timeouts with a schema-validated report. - [x] New agent-device unit test: the `device` fixture reads the harness signal per call. - [x] `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e test` 702 passed; `@e2edev/playwright` 100 passed; `@e2edev/agent-device` 55 passed - [x] `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit` in all three packages, `fallow dead-code` (only pre-existing findings), `check:spec`, `fern check` ---
