title: feat(tmux): terminal backend for CLIs and TUIs, validated against OpenCode
body:
## Summary

New package **`@e2edev/tmux`**: a terminal backend that runs any CLI or TUI (OpenCode, vim, lazygit, your own `node dist/cli.js`) in a private tmux server and implements the public `@e2edev/e2e/backend` contract, the same way `@e2edev/playwright` does for browsers and `@e2edev/agent-device` for mobile. Core learns nothing new.

Demo target: OpenCode's TUI. The test agent drives a coding agent through a whole session: picks a model in the `/models` picker, switches agents, asks OpenCode to write a file and checks the disk, opens help, exits.

## What the backend does

- **Observation** is the pane text, captured in one tmux call (`display-message ; capture-pane`). One `application` root; one `text` node per printed column (rows split at runs of two or more spaces, the way TUIs draw columns, so `/help` and its description or `[ Yes ]` and `[ No ]` are separate nodes with cell rects); decoration glyphs (box drawing, rulers) dropped, even one space away from text; multi-column rows wrapped in a nameless `row`; the cursor column as a focused `textbox`; a `status` node once the program exits, with the final screen kept observable via `remain-on-exit`.
- **Actions**: `fill` types literally (`send-keys -l --`), `press` accepts browser key names (`Enter`, `ArrowDown`, `Control+C`, `Shift+Tab`) and tmux chords (`C-c`), `tap`/`doubleTap` write an SGR mouse click into the pane when the program has mouse reporting on and are `NOT_ACTIONABLE` otherwise, `swipe` sends wheel reports or page keys, `focus` is a no-op. Unsupported kinds fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.
- **Lifecycle**: `prepare` checks `tmux -V`; `init` starts a private server on a per-run socket with one session per worker; each attempt gets its own window running `command`, waits for `ready` text or a still screen; `dispose` kills the session. `app.restart()` relaunches. `url` mints `app://terminal/<program>/<pane title>` for the trace cache.
- **`terminal` fixture**: `text`, `scrollback`, `type`, `press`, `send`, `waitForText`, `waitForExit`, `exited`, `resize`, `cursor`, `title`, `cwd`.
- **`@e2edev/tmux/tools`**: `send_keys`, `wait_for_text` (one wait capped at 60 s so a wrong guess costs a minute, not the step), `scrollback`, scoped to the `terminal` platform.
- **`--headed`** on macOS opens a Terminal.app window attached to the session.

## Testbed

`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:terminal` (opt-in, not CI) drives OpenCode in an isolated workspace under `.e2e/` (own `opencode.json`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` redirected, `--pure`, edits pre-approved, sharing off). One test, one session:

1. Launch: prompt, agent, and model on the status line.
2. Agent opens `/models`, picks Claude Sonnet 4.5, status line proves it; agent switches back to Haiku.
3. Tab cycles Build and Plan (deterministic).
4. Agent asks OpenCode to write `hello.txt`; the test waits for the file on disk and reads it back.
5. `/help` palette and dialog open and close (deterministic).
6. `/exit`; the pane is dead and the final screen still observable.

## Verification

- Unit tests with a scripted tmux runner: 42 passed.
- Integration test on real tmux driving `cat`: passed (`E2E_TMUX_INTEGRATION=1`).
- The session above live against OpenCode 1.18: passes in about 36 s, 13 model calls, under half a cent.
- Live synthetic mouse tap on the `/help` palette row opened the Help dialog.
- `pnpm check` passes.
- Not exercised: `--headed` (opens a window on the operator's machine).

## Notes

- tmux 3.6b exits on the next `new-window` when `window-size manual` is set globally alongside another global option; the size is pinned per session instead (comment in `surface.ts`).
- String `getByText` is exact per the spec, so terminal tests name a whole column exactly or use a regex. `text` and `row` are outside the typed `Role` vocabulary, so those nodes are reached by text; `getByRole` works for `textbox` and `status`.
- OpenCode never shows the "Ask anything" placeholder again after a reply; the agent context says so, because a model waiting for it once spent a whole step budget.
- Docs: new `reference/terminal` page, nav entry, introduction callout, writing-a-backend mention; changeset `minor` for the new package.

body: ## Summary New package **`@e2edev/tmux`**: a terminal backend that runs any CLI or TUI (OpenCode, vim, lazygit, your own `node dist/cli.js`) in a private tmux server and implements the public `@e2edev/e2e/backend` contract, the same way `@e2edev/playwright` does for browsers and `@e2edev/agent-device` for mobile. Core learns nothing new. Demo target: OpenCode's TUI. The test agent drives a coding agent through a whole session: picks a model in the `/models` picker, switches agents, asks OpenCode to write a file and checks the disk, opens help, exits. ## What the backend does - **Observation** is the pane text, captured in one tmux call (`display-message ; capture-pane`). One `application` root; one `text` node per printed column (rows split at runs of two or more spaces, the way TUIs draw columns, so `/help` and its description or `[ Yes ]` and `[ No ]` are separate nodes with cell rects); decoration glyphs (box drawing, rulers) dropped, even one space away from text; multi-column rows wrapped in a nameless `row`; the cursor column as a focused `textbox`; a `status` node once the program exits, with the final screen kept observable via `remain-on-exit`. - **Actions**: `fill` types literally (`send-keys -l --`), `press` accepts browser key names (`Enter`, `ArrowDown`, `Control+C`, `Shift+Tab`) and tmux chords (`C-c`), `tap`/`doubleTap` write an SGR mouse click into the pane when the program has mouse reporting on and are `NOT_ACTIONABLE` otherwise, `swipe` sends wheel reports or page keys, `focus` is a no-op. Unsupported kinds fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - **Lifecycle**: `prepare` checks `tmux -V`; `init` starts a private server on a per-run socket with one session per worker; each attempt gets its own window running `command`, waits for `ready` text or a still screen; `dispose` kills the session. `app.restart()` relaunches. `url` mints `app://terminal//` for the trace cache. - **`terminal` fixture**: `text`, `scrollback`, `type`, `press`, `send`, `waitForText`, `waitForExit`, `exited`, `resize`, `cursor`, `title`, `cwd`. - **`@e2edev/tmux/tools`**: `send_keys`, `wait_for_text` (one wait capped at 60 s so a wrong guess costs a minute, not the step), `scrollback`, scoped to the `terminal` platform. - **`--headed`** on macOS opens a Terminal.app window attached to the session. ## Testbed `pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:terminal` (opt-in, not CI) drives OpenCode in an isolated workspace under `.e2e/` (own `opencode.json`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` redirected, `--pure`, edits pre-approved, sharing off). One test, one session: 1. Launch: prompt, agent, and model on the status line. 2. Agent opens `/models`, picks Claude Sonnet 4.5, status line proves it; agent switches back to Haiku. 3. Tab cycles Build and Plan (deterministic). 4. Agent asks OpenCode to write `hello.txt`; the test waits for the file on disk and reads it back. 5. `/help` palette and dialog open and close (deterministic). 6. `/exit`; the pane is dead and the final screen still observable. ## Verification - Unit tests with a scripted tmux runner: 42 passed. - Integration test on real tmux driving `cat`: passed (`E2E_TMUX_INTEGRATION=1`). - The session above live against OpenCode 1.18: passes in about 36 s, 13 model calls, under half a cent. - Live synthetic mouse tap on the `/help` palette row opened the Help dialog. - `pnpm check` passes. - Not exercised: `--headed` (opens a window on the operator's machine). ## Notes - tmux 3.6b exits on the next `new-window` when `window-size manual` is set globally alongside another global option; the size is pinned per session instead (comment in `surface.ts`). - String `getByText` is exact per the spec, so terminal tests name a whole column exactly or use a regex. `text` and `row` are outside the typed `Role` vocabulary, so those nodes are reached by text; `getByRole` works for `textbox` and `status`. - OpenCode never shows the "Ask anything" placeholder again after a reply; the agent context says so, because a model waiting for it once spent a whole step budget. - Docs: new `reference/terminal` page, nav entry, introduction callout, writing-a-backend mention; changeset `minor` for the new package. ---

title: feat(conversation): backend to test AI agents by talking to them
body:
## Summary

New package **`@e2edev/conversation`**: a backend that tests an AI agent by talking to it. The e2e agent plays the user, the agent under test replies, and `screen`, `expect`, `app`, and `agent` work unchanged. Built for [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev) v7 agents, implementing the public `@e2edev/e2e/backend` contract the same way the browser and mobile backends do.

This is "use our agent to test other agents": someone builds an agent with the AI SDK and points a conversation target at it.

## How it attaches

Name exactly one of:

- **`agent`** — an in-process AI SDK v7 agent, run through the SDK's `DirectChatTransport`. No server.
- **`api`** — a deployed `/api/chat` route speaking the AI SDK UI message stream protocol, driven with `DefaultChatTransport`. Tests what is shipped.
- **`transport`** — a ready-made `ChatTransport`.

The AI SDK is a lazily loaded peer dependency, so importing the backend never forces it on a project that only names it in config.

## What the backend does

- **Observation** is the transcript: one node per message, a `status` node per tool call carrying its state and input or output, a focused composer `textbox`, and `Approve`/`Deny` `button` nodes when the assistant pauses on a tool that needs approval (the composer is withheld then). The default agent grammar drives it: `fill` the composer and `press` Enter to send, `tap` Approve or Deny to answer a gated tool. No custom tools required.
- **Tool approvals** are the crux. An AI SDK tool with `needsApproval` pauses the turn; the backend reports `awaiting-approval`, executes nothing, and resumes on the answer. So a test can prove a dangerous action never runs until approved.
- **`app.restart()`** starts a fresh conversation; **`url`** mints `app://conversation/<agent>/<status>` for the trace cache.

## The `conversation` fixture

Deterministic control and structured oracles: `send`, `approve`, `deny`, `toolCalls`, `messages`, `lastText`, `status`, `awaitingApproval`. The guidance is to assert on tool calls and side effects, not wording, and pair each `agent.assert` (which judges meaning) with one hard check.

`@e2edev/conversation/tools` adds `send_message` and `respond_to_approval` for the e2e agent, scoped to the `conversation` platform.

## Testbed

`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:conversation` (opt-in, not CI): the e2e agent tests a small AI SDK bank support agent (`fixtures/support-agent.ts`) whose `wire` tool is gated on approval. Three tests, each pairing a judgment with a hard check on the recorded tool calls and a ledger of transfers that actually executed:

1. A balance question triggers the `balance` tool and moves no money.
2. A wire request pauses for approval, moves nothing while paused, and executes only after approval (driven through the fixture so the pause is observed deterministically).
3. A wire the customer denies never reaches the ledger.

## Verification

- 19 unit tests over a scripted transport with a mocked AI SDK.
- A live integration test against a real gateway agent: a gated `wire` held until approved, then executed (`E2E_CONVERSATION_LIVE=1`).
- The testbed suite live against a gateway model: 3 of 3 passing, ~10 model calls, about $0.003 per run.
- `pnpm check` passes.

## Notes

- A seeded `system` message is refused at config load: an AI SDK agent owns its system prompt via `instructions`, and a second system message in the prompt is rejected by the SDK. Seed prior `user`/`assistant` turns with `history` instead.
- Drive the approval gate through `conversation.send`, not `agent.act`: `send` stops exactly at the pause, where an `act` step is free to run past it and decide on its own.
- Docs: new `reference/conversation` page, nav entry, introduction callout, README and AGENTS entries; changeset `minor` for the new package.

title: feat(testbed): App Store readiness audit suite on agent-device
body: ## Summary An opt-in testbed suite that uses `e2e` + `@e2edev/agent-device` as an App Review rehearsal: the agent tours a third-party iOS app on a simulator, records a verdict per App Store Review Guideline it can observe from the UI, and a script renders a readiness report. Intended as a free first pass a team runs before submitting. ```bash AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... E2E_APP_PATH=build/MyApp.app pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:appstore AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... E2E_APP=com.example.myapp pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:appstore ``` ## What is in it - **`e2e.appstore.config.ts`** – one iOS simulator target; the app under review comes from `E2E_APP_PATH` (installed once) or `E2E_APP`, with Reminders as the smoke default. - **`tests-appstore/context/`** – the agent's knowledge as plain markdown. `reviewer.md` (how a reviewer tours an app, how to clear system sheets) goes into `agent.context`; `guidelines.md` (the rubric) is spread into every check's `agentContext`, because `extract` reads the test context and never runs through the executor. - **`tests-appstore/*.e2e.ts`** – nine checks covering 2.1 completeness and offline launch, 5.1.1 privacy policy / purpose strings / denied permissions / account deletion / login gating, 4.8 Sign in with Apple, 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 payments, 1.2 report and block, 4.2 web wrapper, 4.0 dark mode. Each is navigate → judge → conclude: `act` reaches the screen, `judge` screenshots it and asks `extract` for `{ verdict, summary, evidence }` against the rubric, `conclude` appends the finding to `.e2e/appstore/findings.jsonl` and fails the test only on a rejection-level violation. Verdicts are `compliant | violation | not-applicable | unverified`; advisory guidelines (4.0, 4.2, login gating) never fail the run. - **`scripts/appstore-report.mjs`** – joins the findings with the runner's JSON report into `.e2e/appstore/report.md` (scorecard, evidence, screenshots, coverage) and exits 1 on a rejection risk or a check that reached no verdict. `test:appstore` clears old findings, runs the suite, then renders the report. ## Notes for review - Testbed only; no change to `@e2edev/e2e` or the backends, so no changeset. - Not part of CI: every check spends real model calls and needs Xcode with a booted simulator. - **Not yet run against a device**: this machine has no iOS simulator runtimes and the gateway account has no credits. The report script was exercised on a synthetic run; typecheck, lint, dead-code and docs checks pass. - Things to watch on the first real run: whether permission alerts are readable for the 5.1.1(ii) check (it uses `vision: 'fallback'`), whether `app.restart()` after `device.setPermission` picks up the new state, and the cost of the 2.1 tour (capped at six screens). ## Review follow-ups (Devin) - The report script's exit code follows the runner too: no report or a run that did not pass exits 1, and the verdict line says why. - `test:appstore` clears `.e2e/report.json` with the findings before a run, so a launch that dies early cannot be read as the last run. - A merged check whose worst finding is `unverified` keeps that finding's summary instead of the clean one. - Ordering: `RANK` already sorts rejection risks first; no change. ## Review follow-ups (cubic) - Findings carry their test: `audit(title, tags, body)` hands each test a `conclude` that stamps the title on every finding, and the report matches findings to results by it, so two checks under one guideline no longer cover for each other, and a passed test with no verdict counts as incomplete. - Screenshot names repeat across retries; the report resolves each to the last attempt's artifact path. - The tour asserts the named section is showing before judging it, and files unreachable destinations and those past the cap of six as `unverified`. - Dark-mode teardown relaunches after restoring light, symmetric with the setup. - Rubric corrections: 3.1.3 exceptions to in-app purchase, the full 1.2 requirement set (posting included, controls anywhere in-app), the 4.8 advertising-consent condition; the README names the exact permissions denied. ---

title: feat(agent): the executor owns its context
body: ## Summary The harness is a notary, not an author. It witnesses and bounds what a step executor does and no longer decides what the executor's model reads. This is the brain-side half of the flexibility audit: the line is drawn as "the harness owns what must hold regardless of whose brain runs (budgets, deadlines, redaction, secrets, revisions, recording, verdict grammar); everything else is a library the brain may use." Two executors on the same socket can now manage context in opposite ways and both conform: one carries its whole conversation across every `agent.act()` of a test, another sends the model nothing but the instruction and the newest screen. ## Changes **Executor context** (`@e2edev/e2e`) - `ctx.attempt`: test id, attempt id, retry index, an end-of-attempt signal, and a per-attempt `memory` map the harness holds and never persists, reports, or shows a model. Serial-group members share one scope, like the ledger. - `ctx.step.index` and `ctx.priorSteps`: completed steps as structured, sanitized records (with cache participation) beside the existing `ledger` string. - `observe({ tree, pixels })`: opt-in redacted node tree and masked viewport pixels. Pixels are withheld with a reason (`PIXEL_TAINTED`, `MASKING_UNPROVEN`, `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`) and the decision is recorded as a policy event. - `StepExecutor.cache: 'off'`: the trace cache neither replays nor records this executor's steps, so every step reaches `runStep`. **Agent surface** (`@e2edev/e2e/agent`), layered like the AI SDK - `createAgent` is unchanged: the golden path, five options. - `createToolLoopExecutor` gains `buildPrompt` returning a message history, `onConclude(ctx, { messages, verdict })`, and `loopGuards` / `windDown` policy. - New primitives that compose with the chassis or a raw `ToolLoopAgent` and load no `ai` themselves: `createGrammarTools`, `createVerdictTool`, `trackModelCalls`, `conversationMemory`, plus exported `serializeLedger`, `compactSnapshotHistory`, `formatReplayedPrefix`. The chassis is rebuilt on them, so the verdict tool and accounting have one implementation. **Spec and docs** - `spec/10-determinism.md`: the ledger section states what must hold (deterministic, bounded, never model-produced, never carrying secrets) instead of prescribing the serialization algorithm, which becomes the reference runner's exported default. - `spec/16-executors.md`: the harness/executor line written down, a "Context is the executor's" section, and the new context fields. - `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`, `fern/docs/pages/agents.mdx` ("Three layers, like the AI SDK"), `AGENTS.md`, and a changeset. **Gotcha fixed on the way** - On Node 26, an `AbortSignal.any` composite with no listener stops following its sources after a GC pass. The attempt-end signal is a plain controller mirrored from the interrupt. ## Verification - `pnpm check` passes (lint, dead code, spec types, typecheck, docs). - `pnpm test` passes: e2e 71 files / 730 tests, playwright 10 / 100, agent-device 7 / 55. - New integration suite `agent-executor-context.test.ts`: attempt identity and memory across steps and tests, structured prior steps, tree and pixels on observe, cache opt-out, cross-step memory on the chassis, and a raw `ToolLoopAgent` with no chassis still policed and budgeted by the harness. ## Not in this PR Follow-ups from the same audit, each its own stream: runner seams (retry policy, reporter sinks, report opt-out, exported spawner, a real `test.extend`), backend seams (declared verbs, coordinate actions, harness context for `defineTool`), routing `waitFor` / `extract` through the socket, and the `trace-1` row missing from the conformance profile table. ---

title: fix(cache): wait for a recorded destination path before judging a replay's end state
body: ## Summary A step that moved to another pathname records no anchors; its destination path is the whole postcondition. `endStateMatches` read the current path once, right after the last replayed action, before the navigation had committed, so every cross-page replay handed off as `end-mismatch` and the executor paid for the step again (and, with a stale observation in hand, often spent the full `actionTimeout` on one tap before recovering). `pathSettles` now polls the path with the same settling backoff anchors use (100..3000 ms, 15 s cap, bounded by the step budget and the abort signal). Same-page steps with anchors are unchanged. Found dogfooding: the TesterArmy site suite (six agentic journeys) recorded at 32 model calls, replayed at 22 with every navigation step handed off. With this fix the replay is 7 calls, all nine `agent.act` steps `self-finalized`, only the `agent.assert` judgements call the model. ## Test plan - [x] `tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts`: two new cases (destination arrives on a later read → self-finalized; never arrives within budget → end-mismatch); 34 unit tests green across step-cache and trace-replay - [x] `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit` on the package - [x] Live: six-journey suite against tester.army, record then replay, all acts zero-turn ---

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2edev/agent-device@0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- [#142](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/142) [`02a73cd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/02a73cd3a53ebaecacca2424f3cb05a7e92097e9) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The app under test is declared by the backend that drives it, not by the
  config. The top-level `app` key (`url`, `command`, `readyUrl`, `services`,
  `allowedOrigins`, `environment`, `identity`) is gone, and so is the runner's
  `APP_URL` fallback: the browser backend takes the same fields as options,
  `playwright({ url, command, services, ... })`, and the device backend derives
  the identity from the app it pins (`agentDevice({ platform, app })`, or an
  explicit `identity`). Two web targets on one app each name it; services and
  commands declared identically by several targets start once.

  For backend authors, the `app` manifest of `defineBackend` carries the
  declaration (`BackendAppDeclaration`) beside its hooks, and the runner
  resolves it per target: navigation policy, cache and session identity, the
  report's target record (`baseOrigin` is now absent for a surface without a
  URL), and the app process all read from there. A device target can finally
  declare a stable identity without inventing a URL. `@e2edev/e2e/backend` also
  exports `obj`, the one-call replacement for the conditional-spread
  idiom when a declaration is built from optional inputs.

  Migrate by moving the `app` block into the backend factory:

  ```ts
  // before
  app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' },
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright() }],
  // after
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }],
  ```

### Patch Changes

- [#149](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/149) [`f810e23`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f810e2324b02b189cbbb6242a55da5d587285932) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Every `screen` query accepts `visible: true`, which drops nodes the platform reports as hidden before the exactly-one rule runs: `getByText('No memories yet', { visible: true })` resolves the copy a person sees even while a framework keeps a `display:none` twin in the document after a reload. Omitted or `false` keeps every match, so existing `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` failures still fire. The predicate is the node's own `hidden` state, the one `toBeVisible()` reads, and it composes with scopes, `filter`, `first`, `last`, and `nth`. `getByTestId` gains the same optional `{ visible }` argument.

  The backend contract's `SemanticQuery` carries the flag as `visible`; the Playwright and agent-device backends evaluate it from the hidden state they already report, and the harness holds a top-level query to the same predicate as a backstop.
## @e2edev/e2e@0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- [#142](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/142) [`02a73cd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/02a73cd3a53ebaecacca2424f3cb05a7e92097e9) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The app under test is declared by the backend that drives it, not by the
  config. The top-level `app` key (`url`, `command`, `readyUrl`, `services`,
  `allowedOrigins`, `environment`, `identity`) is gone, and so is the runner's
  `APP_URL` fallback: the browser backend takes the same fields as options,
  `playwright({ url, command, services, ... })`, and the device backend derives
  the identity from the app it pins (`agentDevice({ platform, app })`, or an
  explicit `identity`). Two web targets on one app each name it; services and
  commands declared identically by several targets start once.

  For backend authors, the `app` manifest of `defineBackend` carries the
  declaration (`BackendAppDeclaration`) beside its hooks, and the runner
  resolves it per target: navigation policy, cache and session identity, the
  report's target record (`baseOrigin` is now absent for a surface without a
  URL), and the app process all read from there. A device target can finally
  declare a stable identity without inventing a URL. `@e2edev/e2e/backend` also
  exports `obj`, the one-call replacement for the conditional-spread
  idiom when a declaration is built from optional inputs.

  ```ts

  app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' },
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright() }],
  // after
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }],
  ```

- [#151](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/151) [`d4489c0`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d4489c06be7b9b5270c29361af9830003da947bb) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Removes public API that had no consumer, was deprecated, or duplicated another surface, so what remains is what the runner actually enforces.

  - `ExecutorBudgets.recordToolCall` (deprecated): use `runTool`, which reserves the action budget before the tool body runs.
  - `ToolAnnotations.replay` and `ToolAnnotations.secrets` (deprecated, never read): `defineTool` takes `{ mutates, platforms? }`.
  - `StepExecutorContext.priorSteps` and `ExecutorPriorStep`: the ledger string is the executor's prior-step context.
  - `createToolLoopExecutor` options `onConclude`, `loopGuards`, and `windDown` (and the `WindDownPolicy` / `LoopGuardThresholds` types): the chassis keeps its own loop guards and wind-down policy.
  - The `@e2edev/e2e/agent` primitives `createGrammarTools`, `createVerdictTool`, `trackModelCalls`, `conversationMemory`, `VERDICT_RULES`, `serializeLedger`, `compactSnapshotHistory`, and `formatReplayedPrefix`: `createAgent` and `createToolLoopExecutor` are the two supported layers.
  - `blockedCategoryOf` and `BlockedCategory` from the main entrypoint.
  - The legacy fixture adapter: a backend fixture factory must return the surface it declared through `context.fixture`; a plain surface is rejected with `INVALID_CONFIG`.

### Patch Changes

- [#141](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/141) [`e26e1d8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e26e1d8fa9714930b9ea33f9a3bbadb7a1f89102) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - CI now demotes the trace cache to `read-only` only when the config left `mode` unset. An explicit `cache: 'read-write'` (or `{ mode: 'read-write' }`) is honored in CI as the project's own statement that it trusts the cache it restores, for example one carried between runs by the CI provider's cache service rather than committed to git. `--no-cache` still wins over the config, and a custom `cache.store` keeps stating its own trust through `writable`.

- [#143](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/143) [`57a313d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/57a313d021ad3f800188e07ffffd3f3d2209d17d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A backend's `command`, every `services` entry, and every service `teardown` accept a `log` path. When set, the runner appends the process's stdout and stderr to that file (resolved from the project root, kept inside it through symlinks, parent directories created) instead of discarding them, so a dev server that dies on boot or a migration that fails can be read back without wrapping the command in a shell redirect. Output is still discarded when `log` is unset. The file is unredacted, so `e2e init` now also adds `.e2e/logs/` to `.gitignore`.

- [#147](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/147) [`a3f9ad7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a3f9ad7190f2ce5212bd98e2f52d1b7b8f1e27b0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A backend's `command` and its `readyUrl` services accept `reuseExisting: true`: when the readiness URL already answers before the spawn, the runner attaches to that process instead of starting its own, reports `<label>: reusing the process already serving <url>`, and leaves it running on teardown (a reused service also skips its `teardown`). Off by default. CI ignores the flag with a notice. Setting it on a `waitForExit` service or a `teardown` command is `INVALID_CONFIG`.

  The runner now always probes `readyUrl` once before spawning, within `startupTimeout`. Without `reuseExisting` in effect, a URL that already answers fails the launch with the new `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` (infrastructure, exit 3) instead of letting the old server pass as the new command's readiness, so tests no longer run against stale code by accident.

- [#146](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/146) [`78f1e9b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/78f1e9b320ecea702f93df482eb07d85b73b4801) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e run [files...]` now accepts directories and globs, not only exact file paths. A directory selects every test file the config globs discover beneath it (`e2e run tests/agent`), a glob uses the config `tests` grammar (`e2e run 'tests/**/*.smoke.e2e.ts'`), and a file path still matches exactly. Positionals keep narrowing the config globs and must stay inside the project root. When nothing is left to run, the `NO_TESTS` message names each positional that matched no file, so a mistyped path is visible instead of failing silently.

- [#144](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/144) [`44ee0a2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/44ee0a2786fa1027bcc12eb6afddcf177899fd45) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.services[]` entries accept an optional `name`. Errors from a service that fails to start, never becomes ready, or whose teardown fails now read `service "postgres" exited with code 1 instead of 0` rather than naming the service by its position and full command line, which was unreadable behind a shell wrapper. The name defaults to the executable's base name; an explicit name must be a non-empty string of at most 64 characters and unique across the named services, otherwise `INVALID_CONFIG`.

- [#149](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/149) [`f810e23`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f810e2324b02b189cbbb6242a55da5d587285932) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Every `screen` query accepts `visible: true`, which drops nodes the platform reports as hidden before the exactly-one rule runs: `getByText('No memories yet', { visible: true })` resolves the copy a person sees even while a framework keeps a `display:none` twin in the document after a reload. Omitted or `false` keeps every match, so existing `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` failures still fire. The predicate is the node's own `hidden` state, the one `toBeVisible()` reads, and it composes with scopes, `filter`, `first`, `last`, and `nth`. `getByTestId` gains the same optional `{ visible }` argument.

  The backend contract's `SemanticQuery` carries the flag as `visible`; the Playwright and agent-device backends evaluate it from the hidden state they already report, and the harness holds a top-level query to the same predicate as a backstop.
## @e2edev/playwright@0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- [#142](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/142) [`02a73cd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/02a73cd3a53ebaecacca2424f3cb05a7e92097e9) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The app under test is declared by the backend that drives it, not by the
  config. The top-level `app` key (`url`, `command`, `readyUrl`, `services`,
  `allowedOrigins`, `environment`, `identity`) is gone, and so is the runner's
  `APP_URL` fallback: the browser backend takes the same fields as options,
  `playwright({ url, command, services, ... })`, and the device backend derives
  the identity from the app it pins (`agentDevice({ platform, app })`, or an
  explicit `identity`). Two web targets on one app each name it; services and
  commands declared identically by several targets start once.

  For backend authors, the `app` manifest of `defineBackend` carries the
  declaration (`BackendAppDeclaration`) beside its hooks, and the runner
  resolves it per target: navigation policy, cache and session identity, the
  report's target record (`baseOrigin` is now absent for a surface without a
  URL), and the app process all read from there. A device target can finally
  declare a stable identity without inventing a URL. `@e2edev/e2e/backend` also
  exports `obj`, the one-call replacement for the conditional-spread
  idiom when a declaration is built from optional inputs.

  Migrate by moving the `app` block into the backend factory:

  ```ts
  // before
  app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' },
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright() }],
  // after
  targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }],
  ```

### Patch Changes

- [#145](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/145) [`24a5763`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/24a5763e8bf234d481778d19f420f83335cc6e48) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `getByDisplayValue(...)` now supports `first()`, `last()`, `nth()`, and `filter({ hasText, has })` in the playwright backend, so a display-value locator can be narrowed, acted on, and asserted like every other query. Positions apply to the value-filtered matches, not to every form control on the page. Previously any refinement failed with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: displayValue queries cannot be used as scopes or filters in this backend`. The two compositions Playwright's locator chain cannot express remain unsupported and now say so precisely: a display-value query as the scope of a child query, and as a `has` filter.

- [#149](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/149) [`f810e23`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f810e2324b02b189cbbb6242a55da5d587285932) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Every `screen` query accepts `visible: true`, which drops nodes the platform reports as hidden before the exactly-one rule runs: `getByText('No memories yet', { visible: true })` resolves the copy a person sees even while a framework keeps a `display:none` twin in the document after a reload. Omitted or `false` keeps every match, so existing `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` failures still fire. The predicate is the node's own `hidden` state, the one `toBeVisible()` reads, and it composes with scopes, `filter`, `first`, `last`, and `nth`. `getByTestId` gains the same optional `{ visible }` argument.

  The backend contract's `SemanticQuery` carries the flag as `visible`; the Playwright and agent-device backends evaluate it from the hidden state they already report, and the harness holds a top-level query to the same predicate as a backstop.

title: refactor(device): replace handwritten PNG codecs

title: refactor(playwright): share one browser connection per worker
body: Each backend worker uses one browser configuration, but its browser pool maintained a keyed map of connections. Replace the map with a single pending connection shared across attempts. title: fix(agent): preserve model usage accounting provenance
body:
Executor steps could report provider-authoritative totals after a mixture of complete and missing usage, while judgment calls maintained separate accounting logic. Share the accumulator across both paths: a later complete response cannot erase earlier missing, partial, or estimated usage.

Sanitize model event counts and step totals before recording them. Cap token sums at the safe integer limit and mark their accounting non-authoritative; omit overflowing cost totals. Apply the same limits to run summaries so saved reports remain schema-valid.

Includes regression coverage for malformed provider counters, accumulation boundaries, and complete serialized reports, plus documentation and a patch changeset. This PR targets `main` independently of the other audit fixes.

title: fix(playwright): a page exception in web.evaluate is a test failure, not infrastructure
body:
`web.evaluate` now reports exceptions from evaluated test code as `EVALUATE_FAILED` with the page's own message. Errors and rejected promises are caught inside the page and returned in a tagged result. Playwright rejections retain the normal backend classification, including timeouts, closures, crashes, protocol errors, and lost execution contexts. Invalid source syntax is also a test failure.

The evaluation boundary preserves JSON argument/result checks and zero-argument calls. Regression coverage includes `Error`, `TypeError`, non-Error thrown values, page exceptions whose messages resemble infrastructure failures, prefixed protocol errors, and real page/context closures during evaluation. Includes matching documentation and a patch changeset.

title: fix(runtime): enforce session and operation ownership
body: Serial test members share a live session, but secret redaction and pixel taint were recreated per member. Project tools could also bypass guarded screenshot capture or consume their action budget only after dispatch. Keep secrecy state with the session, route device screenshot tools through guarded observations, and reserve mutation budgets before side effects through the same queue as grammar actions. Make operation ownership explicit throughout the fixture runtime: - Declare recorded backend fixture methods before invoking them, preserving object identity, mutable state, private-field receivers, and legacy fixture factories. - Attribute asynchronous attachments and events to their originating step, ignore late attachments, retain evidence attached before synchronous legacy failures, and mark contributed assertions as verification steps. - Expose guarded observation context to read-only tools and deprecate optional annotations whose replay and secret semantics were never implemented. - Share cancellation and cleanup helpers, preventing already-cancelled device commands from dispatching. - Bound retained device locator bindings, keep current observation references usable, and reuse location metadata from the same snapshot while explicit probes stay fresh. Includes regression tests, matching documentation, and changesets. The new fixture and lifecycle helpers require both reference backends to use `@e2edev/e2e >=0.4.0 <1`; core receives a minor release and the backends patch releases. This PR targets `main` independently of the PNG, browser-connection, and accounting cleanup PRs. It warns about the new backend peer minimum against the currently released core 0.3.0; the planned core minor satisfies that minimum. ---

title: feat(playwright): surfaceOf exposes the live page and context behind a handle
body:
## Summary

`StepExecutorContext` deliberately carries no session or handle, and `@e2edev/playwright` exports only `playwright()`, so an executor that brings its own browser tooling (spec chapter 16, "replacing the toolset wholesale") has no way to reach the page e2e opened. Attaching a second browser is not an option either: CDP is inbound only.

`@e2edev/agent-device` already models the sanctioned escape hatch with `surfaceOf(backend)`. This mirrors it: `surfaceOf(handle)` returns `{ page(), context(), claimDialogs() }` for a handle this module created, `undefined` for any other backend. `page()` and `context()` read the current attempt and throw `INVALID_STATE` before it exists.

`claimDialogs()` covers the one event both sides hear: a native dialog. Without a `web.onDialog` handler the router dismisses the dialog and latches an `unhandled dialog` failure for the next step, which is right for a test that forgot a handler and wrong for tooling that answers dialogs itself on the same context. While claimed, such a dialog is left to the claimant; a registered handler still wins; an attempt boundary releases the claim.

Core is untouched; the harness stays the notary and the docs say so.

Motivation: TesterArmy runs its full legacy agent (its own tools on a `Page`, including a dialog manager that holds dialogs open for the model) on e2e as the executor. With this seam it drives the same document as the deterministic steps, and its native-dialog checkout scenario passes.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/unit/surface-of.test.ts`: live surface for a playwright handle, `undefined` for a foreign `defineBackend` handle, `INVALID_STATE` from both accessors before an attempt, `claimDialogs` present
- [x] `tests/unit/dialogs.test.ts`: a claimed router leaves an unhandled dialog alone and does not latch; release restores dismiss-and-latch; a registered handler wins over a claim; reset drops the claim
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`
- [x] Docs: "Driving the page yourself" under Replace the executor; changeset (minor)
- [x] Live: TesterArmy legacy agent on e2e passing login, native dialogs, drag and drop, and hover menu scenarios

Three sentences cover the process-group spawn, the `readyUrl` 200-499 probe (defaulting to `app.url`), teardown on every exit path including Ctrl-C, the restricted inherited env (`PATH`/`HOME`/temp vars plus `command.env`, so secrets must be passed explicitly), and that `.e2e/report.json` is still written on `APP_UNREACHABLE`. title: fix(cli): init creates an ESM package so the scaffolded config actually loads
body:
Running `e2e init` in an empty directory produced an `e2e.config.ts` that the runner then refused to load: the TypeScript loader needs the package to be ESM, and there was no `package.json` at all. Even in an existing project you still had to know which packages to install by hand, and a CommonJS package failed with a loader stack trace instead of an explanation.

Init now sets up the package, not just the files. In an empty directory it creates a private `"type": "module"` `package.json`; in an existing one it adds only the missing dev dependencies and keeps versions, formatting, and module type intact, printing `npm pkg set type=module` when ESM is needed. A short wizard picks the backend (none, Playwright, or agent-device, defaulting to iOS on macOS and Android elsewhere) and whether to enable AI testing, then offers to install with the project's package manager. `--yes` keeps the old non-interactive behavior: AI on, no backend, no install.

Loading a `.ts` config or test outside an ESM package now fails with an actionable message.

Scaffold presets live in `src/cli/init/backends.ts`; AGENTS.md's "no backend nouns in core" invariant is updated to point there.

---

*Written by Claude Fable 5.1 in T3 Code (Claude Code harness) on behalf of Krzysztof.*

title: feat(config): app.services for dependency processes before app.command
body: > Proposal: this is a design proposal for dependency processes in the runner and is open to design feedback (field names, error codes, whether services deserve a `name`). Wire format is unchanged: no `spec/schema/*` or conformance edits, so no `suiteVersion` bump. ## Motivation e2e can start the app under test via `app.command` + `readyUrl`, but real apps need dependencies before they can boot: a database container, a cache, an auth emulator, a migration step. Today there is exactly one `command`, so users write wrapper launchers outside e2e (a real example: the TesterArmy dashboard has a 250-line script that runs `docker compose up --wait`, `pnpm db:migrate`, a WorkOS emulator, then `next dev`, tears everything down, and reimplements report writing for startup failures). The spec defers `globalSetup`/`globalTeardown` (`spec/11-lifecycle.md`, "Deferred"); `app.services` is the declarative alternative that fits the existing structured-command model. ## Design ```ts export interface ServiceConfig extends CommandConfig { readyUrl?: string; // HTTP probe, 200-499 is ready waitForExit?: boolean; // ready when the process exits 0 (migrations, docker compose up --wait) teardown?: CommandConfig; // run during teardown after the service is stopped (docker compose down) } export interface AppConfig { ...; services?: readonly ServiceConfig[]; } ``` - Services start sequentially in declaration order, before `app.command` and before collection. Each must be ready before the next starts. - Exactly one of `readyUrl` / `waitForExit` per service; neither or both is `INVALID_CONFIG`. `readyUrl` reuses the app's probe loop (`AppProcess` now takes a readiness object instead of a bare URL). `waitForExit` waits for exit 0 within `startupTimeout` (default 60s); a non-zero exit, signal, spawn failure, or timeout is `APP_UNREACHABLE`, and the message names the service as `app.services[i] ()`. - Teardown on every exit path (success, failure, interrupt): stop `app.command`, then stop started services in reverse (SIGTERM group, `shutdownTimeout`, SIGKILL, as today), then run each started service's `teardown` in reverse and wait for exit (bounded by its `startupTimeout`). A teardown failure is a `cleanup`-phase run error and never skips the remaining teardowns. A `waitForExit` service that already exited still gets its teardown; services never started get none. - Environment: service and teardown children inherit only the `app.command` allowlist (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP, SystemRoot, COMSPEC) plus their own `env`. In `configDigest`, every service `env` and teardown `env` value becomes `{ envName: key }`, like `app.command.env`. - `app.services` is allowed without `app.command` and without `app.url` (the app may be one of the services, or already running). - Small fix along the way: `AppProcess.stop()` now also treats a signal-terminated child (`signalCode` set, `exitCode` null) as already gone instead of waiting on an exit event that never fires. ## Spec / docs touched - `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` (+ mirrored `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`): `ServiceConfig`, `AppConfig.services` - `spec/05-config.md`: new "Services" subsection under "App process" (order, readiness modes, teardown order, env rules) - `spec/13-reporting.md`: `configDigest` sentence covers service and teardown env - `spec/11-lifecycle.md`: "Deferred" points at `app.services` for pre-boot dependencies - `spec/examples/e2e.config.ts`: postgres via `docker compose up --wait` + migration step ahead of `pnpm dev` - `fern/docs/pages/reference/config.mdx`: `app.services` table and example - `.changeset/app-services.md`: `minor` for `@e2edev/e2e` ## Verification - `pnpm check` (lint, dead-code, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check): passed. The fallow dead-code report lists two pre-existing class-member warnings and the `zod` dev-dependency note, unchanged by this PR, exit 0. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test:unit`: 56 files, 583 tests passed. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test` (unit + integration, Chromium installed): 75 files, 769 tests passed. - New tests: `tests/unit/config.test.ts` (readiness contract validation, malformed services, services without `app.url`, digest sanitization of service and teardown env); `tests/unit/app-process.test.ts` (`ServiceStack` ordering, reverse teardown, failure naming the service, teardown after a mid-stack failure, teardown failure returned not thrown, `waitForExit` timeout kills the child, abort stops starting and still tears down); `tests/integration/app-process.test.ts` (`readyUrl` service followed by a `waitForExit` step that depends on it, `readyUrl` timeout naming the service). ---

title: feat(report): junit reporter
body: ## Motivation e2e had two reporters, `list` and `json`. CI systems (GitHub Actions test summaries, Buildkite, GitLab, Jenkins) ingest JUnit XML, so users converted `.e2e/report.json` themselves - the TesterArmy dashboard's e2e launcher carries a hand-written `report.json -> junit.xml` converter for exactly this. A built-in `junit` reporter removes that. ## Design - New reporter id `junit`, selected via `reporters: ['junit']` or `--reporter junit`. Combines with `list` or `json` (only `json` + `list` stays `INVALID_CONFIG`). The list reporter is now enabled by `reporters.includes('list')` instead of "not json", so `--reporter junit` alone is silent on the terminal; docs recommend `--reporter list,junit` for CI. - Output: `.e2e/junit.xml`, written atomically (`writeTextReport`, shared with `writeJsonReport`) next to `report.json`, under the same artifact-parent rule, on every outcome where the report itself is written. It is rendered from the very `Report1Document` that was just written, never from runner state. A failed write is a `REPORT_WRITE_FAILED` infrastructure run error, like the JSON one. - Mapping (`packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts`, no dependency, XML built by hand): - `` root with aggregate `tests`/`failures`/`errors`/`skipped`/`time` (seconds, 3 decimals); one `` per test file, in report order. - One `` per result: `name` = title path joined with ` > ` plus ` [targetId]`, `classname` = file, `time` = final attempt duration. Serial members read their duration and error from the group's final attempt. - passed: bare testcase. flaky: passed testcase with `flaky: N failed attempts before passing`. failed with a `test`-category error: ``; any other category (infrastructure, configuration, internal, interrupted): ``. skipped: ``. A failed result with no error falls back to its status (`timed-out` -> failure, `interrupted` -> error). - Element text is `CODE (phase): message`. The report-1 document deliberately drops stacks, so only the message travels; nothing outside the document is read. - `run.errors` become one extra `` with one `` testcase per error, so `APP_UNREACHABLE` is visible in CI without opening the JSON. - XML escaping for `& < > "`, whitespace entity-encoded in attributes, control characters stripped via the shared `sanitizeText`. - `RunOutcome.junitPath` and the `run-finished` event's `junitPath` mirror `aiTracePath`; the list reporter prints `junit: `; `e2e init` gitignores `.e2e/junit.xml`. ## Spec and docs touched - `spec/06-cli.md` (`--reporter` row, Output prose), `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` and `packages/e2e/src/types.ts` (reporter union, kept identical). No `spec/schema/*` or `spec/conformance/*` changes. - `fern/docs/pages/reference/cli.mdx` (flag, Output table, init gitignore cell), `reference/config.mdx`, `reference/embedding.mdx` (`junitPath`), `ci.mdx` (workflow uses `--reporter list,junit`, uploads both files, short note on CI test-summary steps). - `.changeset/junit-reporter.md`: `@e2edev/e2e` minor. ## Verification - `pnpm check` (lint, dead-code, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check): exit 0. Fallow's two advisory class-member warnings and the fern "redirects check skipped: not authenticated" warning are pre-existing and unrelated. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test:unit`: 57 files, 588 tests passed, including the new `tests/unit/report-junit.test.ts` (status mapping, flaky note, escaping and control-character stripping, per-file grouping, run-level errors, serial members, empty run) and additions to `cli.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `cli-init.test.ts`, `report-write.test.ts`. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test` (unit + integration, Chromium): exit 0, 76 files, 774 tests passed (includes two new `runner-lifecycle` cases: junit.xml written beside report.json from the same document with escaped failure text and no temp files left; no junit.xml unless the reporter is selected). --- ## Review follow-up (059ab89) - Finalization reordered: junit.xml renders first from the built document, report.json is written once, last, so a lost junit.xml lands in report.json, `RunOutcome.report`, the exit code, and `run-finished` alike. New integration test in `run-events.test.ts` forces the junit write to fail after the JSON path works and asserts persisted and returned status and errors agree. - Sanitizer hardened: U+FFFE, U+FFFF, and lone surrogate halves become U+FFFD in text and attributes. Unit tests cover them, and every rendered document in `report-junit.test.ts` passes a strict XML 1.0 well-formedness check (no XML parser is a dependency here). - Re-verified: `pnpm check` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test`: exit 0, 76 files, 777 tests passed.
