title: test(playwright): fix stale fixture context stub failing CI on main
body: ## What The \`evaluate\` integration tests build a stub \`BackendFixtureContext\` with only \`operation\` and \`expectable\`. Since #132, \`createWebFixture\` registers the surface through \`context.fixture(...)\`, so every case in the file throws \`TypeError: context.fixture is not a function\` before reaching its assertion. This adds the missing \`fixture\` member as an identity passthrough, matching what the stubs in \`agent-device\` already do. ## Why \`main\` has been red since bc87f15 (\`check\` job, \`@e2edev/playwright\` tests). #132 itself was green because its own check ran before the merge picked up the surrounding changes. Every open PR currently inherits this failure (#134, #136, #137). ## Verification - \`pnpm build\` - \`pnpm --filter @e2edev/playwright run test\`: all files pass - \`pnpm --filter @e2edev/agent-device run test\`: all files pass - \`pnpm lint\`: clean No changeset: test-only change, no published package behavior changes. ---

title: feat(e2e): post-failure analysis with failure-time evidence capture
body: ## Summary A separate small model call that explains why a test failed, on top of the deterministic result. Two layers: **Failure-time evidence.** The moment a test-category failure lands (body catch, before `afterEach`, session still open), the executor captures a masked screenshot (when `screenshot` is among `config.artifacts`, a key that was previously a no-op) and the redacted accessibility tree as a `failure/observation.txt` `log` artifact. Both attach to the failing step. The attempt record carries `evidence: { screenshot?, observation?, url?, pixelsTainted }`. This runs whether or not analysis is on, so a failing run always leaves the final screen behind. **Analyzer seam.** New `analysis` config key (or `--analyze` CLI flag). After a failed pair's last attempt, the runner process builds a `FailureContext` (error, step timeline, previous attempts, redacted screen, failing source lines, optional screenshot) and asks the built-in analyzer for a closed-grammar verdict: classification (`app-bug` | `test-bug` | `environment` | `flaky` | `unknown`), confidence, summary, evidence, suggested fix. Hosts can replace it with their own `FailureAnalyzer`; its output is validated against the same grammar. The verdict streams as an `analysis` run event (after that pair's `test-finished`), renders under the failure in the list reporter, and is filed in `report.json` under `result.extensions['e2edev.analysis']`. The report schema already allows extensions, so no schema or suite version bump. ## Guarantees - Never changes a status, consumes a test's model-call budget, delays a retry, or fails the run. - A missing verdict is recorded as `unavailable` with a closed reason (`no-model`, `limit-reached`, `failed`, `timed-out`, `interrupted`). - Evidence is redacted through the session's secret ledger; the screenshot is model input only with `analysis.vision` and only when no secret was filled during the attempt (`pixelsTainted`). Verdicts are redacted again on the way out. - Only test-category failures and timeouts of ordinary pairs are analyzed. Serial-group members are not yet (attempts live on the group record). - Bounded: `maxFailures` (default 10), concurrency 2, 90 s per analysis, observation capped at 48 KiB for the prompt. ## Live validation Ran the new opt-in testbed suite (`packages/testbed/tests-analysis`, six deliberately failing tests with the expected classification in the title) against `google/gemini-3-flash` through the gateway: - 6/6 analyzed; every classification matched the title, with concrete fixes (e.g. naming the actual button label the screen uses). - Screenshot reached the model on 5/6; the credential-fill test correctly sent no image. - ~1.5–2k input tokens and ~$0.002 per analysis; 5–12 s text-only, 22–35 s with vision. Two things the live run caught and this PR fixes: Gemini's reasoning tokens exhausted a 1024 output ceiling (`finish=length`), so the ceiling is 4096 with one repair round; and in-process `rawConfig` runs have no source maps, so a frame whose column exceeds the line length is dropped instead of quoting a wrong line (the worker/CLI path maps correctly). ## Checks - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e test`: 782 passing, plus new unit tests (config, prompt/validation, repair round, PNG header) and a real-browser integration test (evidence artifacts, event ordering, report extension schema-valid, custom analyzer, `maxFailures`, throwing analyzer). - lint, typecheck, `check:spec`, `docs:check` clean. `check:dead-code` reports two class members and one dev dependency that predate this branch. ## Docs spec 05/06/13, `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`, fern `config.mdx` and `cli.mdx`, changeset (minor). ## Open question `analysis.source` defaults to `true`, which sends the failing test lines to the model. Flip the default if test source should stay on the machine. ---

title: fix(config): honor an explicit read-write cache mode in CI
body: ## Motivation CI demoted the trace cache from \`read-write\` to \`read-only\` regardless of the config. The rationale (a committed cache is untrusted input) is right as a default, but wrong as an override: when a project writes \`cache: 'read-write'\` it has stated its trust, typically because CI restores \`.e2e/cache\` from the provider's own cache service rather than from git. Today such a project has to hand-roll a \`TraceCacheStore\` just to get back what the default file store already does. The TesterArmy dashboard suite hit exactly this. ## Change - \`resolveCacheConfig\` tracks whether the config named a mode (string shorthand or \`{ mode }\`). Only a defaulted mode is demoted in CI. \`--no-cache\` still wins over everything, and a custom \`store\` still states its own trust through \`writable\`. - Spec prose updated in \`05-config.md\` (CI defaults table and cache paragraph) and \`10-determinism.md\`; the \`cache\` doc comment updated in \`spec/api/e2e.d.ts\` and mirrored in \`src/types.ts\`. No schema or conformance changes. - Docs: \`reference/config.mdx\` table rows and prose. - Tests: the CI demotion case now covers unset, \`{ dir }\` only, explicit string, explicit object, and explicit \`read-only\`. - Changeset: \`@e2edev/e2e\` minor. ## Verification - \`pnpm check\` (lint, dead-code, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check): exit 0 - \`pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test:unit\`: all passing ---

title: feat(config): the backend declares the app under test, replacing the top-level app key
body:
The config told two different stories about where the app under test lives. A web target put it at the root (`app: { url }`) while a mobile target put it on the backend (`agentDevice({ app: 'com.android.settings' })`). Same concept, two homes, and a device target could not even declare a stable cache identity without inventing a URL.

Now the backend declares the app it drives, and the top-level `app` key is gone. `playwright()` takes `url`, `command`, `services`, `readyUrl`, `allowedOrigins`, `environment`, and `identity` as options; `agentDevice()` derives `identity` from the app it pins (or an explicit `identity`). The runner resolves each target's declaration at config load and owns everything built on it: navigation and origin policy, cache and session identity, the report's target record, and the processes it starts. Services and commands declared identically by several targets start once. The runner no longer reads `APP_URL`; the scaffolded config reads it itself and hands it to the backend.

```ts
// before
app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000', command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev'] } },
targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright() }],
// after
targets: [{ name: 'web', platform: 'web', backend: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000', command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev'] } }) }],
```

For backend authors, the `app` manifest of `defineBackend` carries the declaration (`BackendAppDeclaration`) next to its hooks. The report's `baseOrigin` is now absent for a surface without a URL, so the report schema and `suiteVersion` move with it. Spec chapters, API declarations, docs pages, READMEs, the testbed configs, and a changeset (minor for all three packages) are updated in the same change.

No backward compatibility is kept, per the discussion that led here.

*Changes authored by Claude Fable 5.1 running in Claude Code (T3 Code harness).*

title: feat(config): command.log captures app and service output
body: > **Rebased onto `main` after #142 (2026-09-07).** The top-level `app` key is gone, so `log` now lives on the backend's `command` / `services` declaration (`playwright({ command: { ..., log } })`). Config plumbing threads `projectRoot` through `resolveTargetApp`; tests, spec prose, and docs use the new shape. History squashed to one commit; all Devin review threads were already addressed and stay addressed. ## Motivation `ManagedProcess` spawns the backend's `command`, every `services` entry, and every service `teardown` with `stdio: 'ignore'`. When a dev server dies on boot or a migration fails, the run ends in `APP_UNREACHABLE` with nothing to read. A real project (the TesterArmy dashboard suite) wraps every command in `sh -c 'exec ... >> .e2e/website.log 2>&1'` purely to see logs, and a CI failure of `pnpm db:migrate` could only be diagnosed after adding that wrapper. Capturing output should be a config option, not a shell trick. ## Design `CommandConfig` gains one optional key, declared identically in `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` and `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`: ```ts /** File that receives the process's stdout and stderr, appended, resolved from the project root. Omitted discards output. */ log?: string; ``` - Applies to the backend's `command`, each `services` entry, and each service `teardown`; they are all `CommandConfig`, so `ServiceStack` needed no changes. - `packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`: when `log` is set, `start()` creates the parent directories, opens the file in append mode, and passes the same descriptor for stdout and stderr (`['ignore', fd, fd]`). `stdio: 'ignore'` is unchanged when `log` is unset. The parent closes its copy of the descriptor right after `spawn` returns rather than on exit: the child already holds its own copy by then (libuv forks and execs synchronously inside `spawn`), so keeping ours open for the life of a dev server would only leak it. A log that cannot be opened (for example the path is a directory) fails with `APP_UNREACHABLE` naming the command, matching the spawn-failure path. - `packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts`: the shared `validateCommand` helper now also checks `log`, so `command`, services, and teardowns get the same rule and message shape (errors are prefixed with the declaring target, as every app-declaration error is since #142). A non-string or blank value is `INVALID_CONFIG` (`

title: feat(config): named app.services
body: ## Motivation `app.services` (#136) names a service in errors by its index and command line. Behind a shell wrapper that reads like `app.services[1] (sh -c exec ./node_modules/.bin/drizzle-kit migrate >> "/long/path/website.log" 2>&1) exited with code 1`, and the review on #136 already asked for a name. A `name` also gives the report a stable label for the startup phase. ## Design - `ServiceConfig.name?: string` in `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` and `packages/e2e/src/types.ts` (kept identical): "Label used in errors, reporter output, and the report; defaults to the executable name." - Resolution (`packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts`): the label is `service ""`, where the name is the explicit `name` trimmed, or `path.basename(executable)` when unset (so a `sh` wrapper is still `sh`, which is when you set one). `name` is lifted out of the spawned `CommandConfig` like `readyUrl`, `waitForExit`, and `teardown`. The teardown label is `service "" teardown`. - Validation: an explicit name must be a non-empty trimmed string of at most 64 characters, and unique across explicitly named services; both are `INVALID_CONFIG` with the offending `app.services[i].name` in the message. Derived default names are allowed to repeat (two `pnpm` steps, two `node` scripts) so existing configs stay valid. - `ManagedProcess` messages keep the exit code or signal and the phase (`failed to start`, `exited with code N before becoming ready`, `was not reachable at within N ms`, `did not exit within N ms`, `... teardown exited with code N instead of 0`); only the label changed. - No new run events or schema fields. The runner has no per-service notice today (the only `notice` emitter is backend init), so none was added; the name reaches the report through the run error message. - The now-unused `commandLine()` helper is removed (fallow would flag it). ## Spec and docs touched - `spec/05-config.md`: the Services section now states the service is named by its `name` (default: executable base name) and the validation rule. - `spec/examples/e2e.config.ts`: the example services carry names. - `fern/docs/pages/reference/config.mdx`: `name` row in the `app.services` table, in the interface snippet, and in the example. - `.changeset/service-names.md`: `@e2edev/e2e` minor. - No `spec/schema/*` or `spec/conformance/*` changes. ## Tests - `tests/unit/config.test.ts`: named labels, name lifted out of the command, trimming, the 64-character boundary, rejection of empty/whitespace/oversized/non-string names, duplicate rejection, repeated derived names accepted. - `tests/unit/managed-process.test.ts`: exact messages for a named start failure (`service "migrate" exited with code 2 instead of 0`), a named teardown failure (`service "cache" teardown exited with code 1 instead of 0`), and the default-name path. - `tests/integration/managed-process.test.ts`: exact readiness timeout message for a named service. ## Verification - `pnpm check` (lint, dead-code, spec typecheck, build + typecheck, fern check): passed. Fallow reports two pre-existing advisory class-member warnings in files not touched here. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test`: 77 files, 830 tests passed. ---

title: fix(playwright): first/last/nth on displayValue queries
body:
## Motivation

In the playwright backend, `screen.getByDisplayValue("...").first()` failed at runtime with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: displayValue queries cannot be used as scopes or filters in this backend`. `first()`, `last()`, and `nth()` are positional selection on the query's own matches, not scoping or filtering, and every other query supports them. The spec (08-platforms, "All query methods are equally valid") never carved out an exception. A real test in the TesterArmy dashboard suite hit this in CI when checking a textarea value after reload and had to fall back to `web.locator("textarea:visible").nth(2)`.

## What was impossible vs unimplemented

Playwright has no selector for a form control's *current* value (`[value=]` only matches the attribute), so the backend projects a `displayValue` query to the candidate set `input, textarea, select`, reads every candidate in one `evaluateAll`, and applies the value predicate afterwards. `requireSingle` then rejected any composition on top of that projection, which lumped together two very different things:

- **Genuinely impossible:** using a displayValue query as the scope of a child query (`getByDisplayValue(v).getByRole(...)`) or as a `has` filter target. Both need the value predicate *inside* Playwright's locator chain. These remain rejected.
- **Merely unimplemented:** `first`/`last`/`nth`, and `filter({ hasText, has })` on a displayValue source, in either order. Per-element filters that come before any position commute with the value predicate, so they compose natively onto the candidate locator. Positions do not commute (they are relative to the value-filtered matches), so they are recorded on the projection as post steps and applied after filtering. A filter that follows a position is recorded as a post step too and checked on the selected element alone (`candidate.nth(i).filter(options).count() > 0`), keeping Playwright's own `hasText`/`has` semantics. Actions and `expect(...)` assertions on the result work through the same `locate` path, so `toHaveValue`/`toBeVisible` on `.first()` follow for free.

## Change

- `packages/playwright/src/locators.ts`: `ProjectedLocator` gains `steps` (index or filter post steps); `project()` composes pre-position filters onto the displayValue candidate locator and defers positions and post-position filters; `requireSingle` becomes `requireComposable`, used only for scope and `has`, with the narrower message `displayValue queries cannot scope child queries or serve as a has-filter in this backend`. New exported `applyPostSteps()` applies the steps innermost first (`nth` past the end selects nothing, like Playwright; a filter step runs only on the matches that survived the steps before it).
- `packages/playwright/src/surface.ts`: `locate` applies `applyPostSteps` to the value-filtered candidates, with a filter step resolved as `projected.locator.nth(index).filter(options).count() > 0`. Refs still point at `candidate.nth(index)`, so a positional match acts on exactly that element.
- Tests: new `tests/unit/locators.test.ts` (projection shapes, error cases, `applyPostSteps` table and filter-step ordering) and an integration case in `tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts` on a new `/values` fixture page with three controls sharing a value plus a fourth that differs: `first` -> First, `nth(1)` -> Second, `last` -> Third, `nth(3)` -> none, chained positions, `hasText` before and after a position, `has` after a position, fill through a positional ref, and both unsupported compositions keeping `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.
- Docs: `fern/docs/pages/reference/screen.mdx` gains a callout under Refinement stating exactly what remains unsupported in the playwright backend. The limitation was never documented in `spec/` or the docs before, so this is an added note, not a narrowing; no spec declaration, schema, or manifest changes.
- Changeset: `@e2edev/playwright` **patch**. The spec already promised refinement on every query and the backend failed to deliver it, and no new API surface is added, so this is a fix rather than a feature.

## Verification

All run in the foreground on this branch at the latest commit:

- `pnpm check` (lint -> check:spec -> typecheck -> docs:check): pass
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/playwright run test`: 13 files, 139 tests pass (unit + Chromium integration)
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test`: 77 files, 827 tests pass

title: feat(cli): run accepts directories and globs; docs show app.services
body: > **Rebased onto `main` after #142 (2026-09-07).** The runner change merged cleanly; only the README and quickstart examples conflicted and now show `services` and `command` inside the `playwright({ ... })` declaration. History squashed to one commit; both Devin threads were already addressed and stay addressed. ## Motivation `e2e run [files...]` matched positional arguments as exact file paths only (`collect()` filtered on `normalizedFilters.has(file)`). `e2e run tests/agent` silently selected nothing and the run failed with a bare `NO_TESTS`, which is confusing: every comparable runner (Playwright, Vitest, Jest) accepts a directory or a glob. A real project had to keep an environment switch (`E2E_AGENT_SUITE=1`) purely to pick a suite directory. Separately, after #134 the README shows the backend's `command`, but `services` (#136) was only in the config reference. The quickstart and README now show the full "start your stack" story in one place. ## Change - A positional is one of: a file path (matched exactly, as before); an existing directory relative to the project root (every file the config globs discover beneath it, `.` selects all); or a glob (any `*` or `?`) compiled with the existing 05-config grammar (`compileGlob` / `matchesGlob` from `src/internal/globs.ts`) and matched against the discovered files. Positionals still intersect the config `tests` globs and never add a file they do not match; the outside-project-root rule is unchanged. A malformed positional glob is `INVALID_GLOB`. - Path normalization now runs through `path.posix.normalize`, so `./tests/agent`, `tests/agent/`, and `tests/../../x` are handled correctly (the last one is rejected; previously it slipped past the `..` prefix check). - `Collection` gains `unmatchedPositionals`; when `select()` raises `NO_TESTS` the message appends `(no test file matched: tests/agnet, tests/*.spec.ts)` so the user sees which path was wrong. Unmatched positionals are not an error on their own, they only narrow. - `e2e run --help` describes the argument as "test files, directories, or globs". - README and quickstart: the `playwright({ url, command })` example now also declares two `services` (a `docker compose up --wait` step with `waitForExit` and a `teardown`, plus a migration step), with three sentences on ordering and teardown and a link to the `services` config reference section. `ci.mdx` is untouched. No schema changes. ## Spec / docs touched - `spec/06-cli.md`: the positional-arguments paragraph is now precise about files, directories, globs, `INVALID_GLOB`, and the `NO_TESTS` detail; example command added. - `fern/docs/pages/reference/cli.mdx`: `e2e run` positional section rewritten, examples added. - `packages/e2e/README.md`, `fern/docs/pages/quickstart.mdx`: services example and prose. - `.changeset/run-positional-directories-globs.md`: `@e2edev/e2e` minor. ## Tests - New `tests/unit/collect.test.ts` covers `selectPositionals`: exact file (relative, `./`, absolute), directory (with and without trailing slash, `.`), glob (`*`, `?`, `**`), union with discovery order preserved, a file on disk the config globs did not discover is never selected, unmatched positionals reported as written, outside-root rejection, malformed glob. - `tests/unit/select.test.ts`: `NO_TESTS` message names unmatched positionals. - `tests/integration/runner-lifecycle.test.ts`: real run with a directory positional, with globs, and with two mistyped positionals asserting the full `NO_TESTS` message in the report. ## Verification - `pnpm check` (lint, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check): pass. The one fern warning is the unauthenticated redirects check, unrelated. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test:unit`: 58 files, 636 tests pass. - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test` (unit + integration, Chromium installed): 78 files, 838 tests pass. ---

title: feat(config): reuseExisting for app.command and services
body:
Stacked on #143; GitHub retargets to main when #143 merges.

> **Rebased onto the rebuilt #143 after #142 (2026-09-07).** `reuseExisting` lives on the backend's `command` / `services` declaration. Because the app command is now labelled `target "<name>" command` by `declaredProcesses`, the notice no longer sniffs an `app.command` label: it is `<label>: reusing the process already serving <url>` for commands and services alike. History squashed to one commit; both Devin threads were already addressed and stay addressed.

## Motivation

The backend's `command` always spawns the app. During local development the dev server is usually already running on that port, so the spawn either fails or double-starts, and worse, the readiness poll then accepts the old server and tests run against stale code. Playwright's `webServer.reuseExistingServer` solved this years ago: if the URL already answers, attach to it and start or stop nothing. This adds the same to e2e, off by default, and makes the stale-server case an explicit failure everywhere else, because in CI a pre-existing server is a mistake rather than a convenience.

## Design

- `CommandConfig.reuseExisting?: boolean` (identical in `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` and `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`). Applies to the backend's `command` and to `services` entries with a `readyUrl`.
- `ManagedProcess.start` always probes `readyUrl` once before spawning (same 200-499 rule), spending from the `startupTimeout` budget: the deadline is taken first and the probe timeout is `min(2 s, startupTimeout)`. HTTP readiness cannot tell which process answered later, so the probe decides up front:
  - answers, `reuseExisting: true`, not CI: mark reused, spawn nothing, `stop()` is a no-op, a `notice` says `<label>: reusing the process already serving <url>` (the label is `target "web" command` or `service "emulator"`, so one message form covers both). A reused service also skips its `teardown`.
  - answers, otherwise: fail before spawning with the new `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` (infrastructure, exit 3): `<url> already answered before target "web" command started; stop that process or set reuseExisting: true` (CI variant notes the flag is ignored there).
  - no answer: spawn and own the process exactly as before, same deadline.
- CI (`isCiMode`): the flag is ignored and a `notice` says so; an already-running app is `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` there too. Notices flow through the existing run-event channel (`target: 'app'`), so the list reporter prints them above the live block with no new schema fields. The hooks ride along `declaredProcesses` in `runner.ts`, so deduplicated commands and services get them the same way.
- Validation: `reuseExisting` must be a boolean; on a `waitForExit` service or a `teardown` command it is `INVALID_CONFIG` (nothing to reuse).
- `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` is added to both `AgentErrorCode` unions, the agent code table (`src/agent/error.ts`, same classification as `APP_UNREACHABLE`), the spec 06 exit-class table, and the errors reference. The report schema types `code` as a free string and the conformance manifest lists no codes, so no `spec/schema` or `spec/conformance` change and no `suiteVersion` bump.

## Spec and docs touched

- `spec/05-config.md`: app-under-test paragraph plus a `command.reuseExisting` row in the Local/CI defaults table. `spec/06-cli.md`: exit-class table row.
- `fern/docs/pages/reference/config.mdx`: `command` type, table row, explanatory paragraph; `services` note on where the flag is and is not allowed.
- `fern/docs/pages/reference/errors.mdx`: `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` row.
- `fern/docs/pages/quickstart.mdx`: one sentence where `command` is introduced.
- `fern/docs/pages/ci.mdx`: row in "What CI changes automatically".
- `.changeset/reuse-existing-app.md`: `@e2edev/e2e` patch (pre-1.0 policy).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/managed-process.test.ts`: URL answering + `reuseExisting: true` spawns nothing and stop leaves the server up; CI ignores the flag, emits the notice, and fails with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` without spawning; flag unset fails the same way; a slow server with `startupTimeout: 300` fails with `APP_UNREACHABLE` inside the budget; a reused `readyUrl` service skips its teardown while the following service still runs.
- `tests/integration/managed-process.test.ts`: `reuseExisting: true` with nothing listening starts and owns the app; a server another process already runs is attached to with the flag and fails the launch with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` without it, left running either way.
- `tests/unit/config.test.ts`: accepted on `app.command` and a `readyUrl` service; rejected on a `waitForExit` service, on a `teardown`, and when not a boolean.

## Verification

- `pnpm check`: green (lint, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check; the one fern warning is the unauthenticated redirects check).
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test`: 77 files, 836 tests passed.

title: feat(locator): visible option excludes hidden duplicates from screen queries
body:
**Stacked on #145** (`claude/displayvalue-nth`), which introduces `applyPostSteps` for positional selection and filters on display-value queries. This PR's base is that branch; merge #145 first.

## Motivation

e2e locators must resolve to exactly one node, which is the right default. Modern frameworks, though, keep hidden duplicates in the document: after `web.reload()` Next.js retains a hidden prerendered copy of a segment for a while, so `screen.getByText("No memories yet")`, `getByPlaceholder("Search memory...")`, and `getByDisplayValue(...)` fail with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` although exactly one copy is on screen. The TesterArmy dashboard suite (56 tests) needed five separate escapes to `web.locator('...:visible')` for this, which ties those tests to CSS and to the web backend. The screen query API needs a first-class way to say "the visible one".

## Design

- `TextMatchOptions.visible?: boolean` (so `getByText`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`, `getByDisplayValue`, and `RoleOptions` via inheritance), plus `getByTestId(id, options?: { visible?: boolean })`. Adding an optional trailing parameter does not break the canonical declaration, so `getByTestId` gets it too.
- Semantics: with `visible: true`, nodes whose `hidden` state is true are dropped from that query's match set before any enclosing scope, filter, index, or cardinality rule sees them. Omitted or `false` is unchanged, so hidden duplicates still make an unindexed query `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`.
- The visibility signal is the existing one: `SemanticNode.states.hidden`, the predicate `isNodeVisible`, `toBeVisible()`, `isVisible()`, and `waitFor()` already read. No new observation field and no wire schema change.
- Where the flag lives: `SemanticQuery.visible` in the backend contract, next to `states`. Only the backend can apply the predicate under a scope, filter, or index, and both backends already have the hidden state in hand at locate time:
  - Playwright: `locators.ts` narrows a visible query inside the selector with `filter({ visible: true }).locator(':scope:not([aria-hidden="true"])')`, so the predicate (including the `aria-hidden` half of the semantic `hidden` state) holds before any enclosing `first`/`nth`/`last`, `filter`, scope, or `has` runs. `surface.locate` additionally drops batch-read candidates whose `states.hidden` is true before the display-value predicate and #145's post steps, so `getByDisplayValue(v, { visible: true }).first()` takes its position among shown controls and a direct query agrees with `toBeVisible()` at the margin where the two predicates differ (a zero-size element with a layout rect). No extra round trips.
  - agent-device: `matchesQuery` drops `states.hidden` nodes for every query kind when `visible` is set.
  - Harness backstop: `createBackendSession.locate` filters a top-level `visible` query by the same predicate, so a direct query never resolves to a hidden node even with a backend that ignores the flag.
- `describeExpression` renders the predicate (`getByText("Save", visible: true)`) so ambiguity messages show it.

## Spec and docs touched

- `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` (canonical, mirrored in `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`), `spec/api/driver.d.ts` (`SemanticQuery.visible`, mirrored in `packages/e2e/src/backend/contract.ts`).
- `spec/08-platforms.md`: new "Visibility" subsection in the query model (the locator prose lives here, not in `spec/02`, which has no locator section; `spec/03` does not define query options, so it is untouched).
- `spec/09-drivers.md`: driver obligation for `visible` under scopes, filters, and indices.
- `spec/schema/*` and `spec/conformance/v0-requirements.json` untouched; `pnpm check:manifest` confirms no bump is needed.
- `fern/docs/pages/reference/screen.mdx`: "Hidden duplicates" example after navigation, updated signatures and option table. `fern/docs/pages/reference/backend.mdx`: backend obligation.
- Changeset: `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, `@e2edev/agent-device` as `patch` (pre-1.0 policy).

## Tests

- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts`: engine over the real session adapter and a backend that returns a shown/hidden twin pair for every query kind; `visible: true` resolves the shown node, omitted or `false` is `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, unknown visibility is kept, indexed expressions pass through to the backend unchanged, and the ambiguity message names the predicate.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/expression.test.ts`: flag propagation and description.
- `packages/playwright/tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts` with a new `/twins` fixture page (hidden copy first, then the live copy, plus `aria-hidden` paragraph and panel pairs): each query kind, role, `aria-hidden`, `first`/`nth`/`last` and `filter({ hasText })`/`filter({ has })` over a visible query, a visible test-id query as the scope of a child query, display-value `first`/`nth`/`last` and a filter after a position under `visible`, and acting on the surviving refs.
- `packages/agent-device/tests/unit/locate.test.ts`: hidden node dropped for text, label, role, and under an index.

## Verification

- `pnpm check` (lint, dead-code, check:spec, typecheck, docs:check): pass. The three dead-code items fallow lists (`LocatorEngine.assertionTimeout`, `SessionStaging.stage`, `zod`) predate this branch.
- `pnpm check:manifest`: no conformance manifest or schema changes.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e run test`: 77 files, 844 tests pass (unit and browser integration).
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/playwright run test`: 12 files, 125 tests pass.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/agent-device run test`: 64 pass, 4 skipped (simulator).

title: fix(deps): resolve high-severity Dependabot alerts
body:
## Summary
Closes all open high-severity Dependabot alerts (#1, #2, #3, #6, #8, #10, #11, #14, #19, #20, #21, #22). All affected packages are transitive, so this adds `pnpm.overrides` to the root `package.json`:

```

```

Overrides live in `package.json` (not `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) because the pinned `pnpm@10.2.1` ignores workspace-level `overrides`.

title: refactor(api)!: prune public API surface to what has a consumer
body: ## Summary Deep audit of every export on the public entrypoints (`@e2edev/e2e`, `/agent`, `/backend`, `/run`, `@e2edev/playwright`, `@e2edev/agent-device`, `/tools`), cross-checked against the real consumers: the TesterArmy engine and brain, the testbed, our two backends, the docs, and the spec. Anything with no consumer that is not part of the sdk-0.1 contract is removed. Adding later is cheaper than removing. ## Removed - `ExecutorBudgets.recordToolCall` (deprecated): `runTool` is the only tool accounting path. - `ToolAnnotations.replay` and `secrets` (deprecated, never read): `defineTool` takes `{ mutates, platforms? }`. - `StepExecutorContext.priorSteps` and `ExecutorPriorStep`: the ledger string is the prior-step context; the projection stays internal as the sanitization point. - `observe({ tree: true })`, `ExecutorNode`, and the tree projection: observations are text plus opt-in masked pixels. - `createToolLoopExecutor` options `onConclude`, `loopGuards`, `windDown` and the `WindDownPolicy` / `LoopGuardThresholds` types: the loop keeps its own guard and wind-down defaults. - The primitives layer on `@e2edev/e2e/agent` (`createGrammarTools`, `createVerdictTool`, `trackModelCalls`, `conversationMemory`, `VERDICT_RULES`, `serializeLedger`, `compactSnapshotHistory`, `formatReplayedPrefix`): the functions the chassis uses stay internal; `conversationMemory` is deleted. - `blockedCategoryOf` and `BlockedCategory` from the main entrypoint. - `ViewportPoint` from `@e2edev/e2e/backend` (reserved, unconsumed). - The legacy fixture adapter (`run/fixture-legacy.ts`): both shipped backends already declare through `context.fixture`; a factory returning an undeclared surface now fails with `INVALID_CONFIG` instead of taking a second, silent code path. Spec (`api/e2e.d.ts`, chapters 10 and 16), the agents guide (now "two layers"), the backend reference, and a changeset are updated in the same change. ## Kept on purpose `surfaceOf` / `PlaywrightLiveSurface`, `StepExecutor.cache`, `attempt.memory`, `isBackendHandle`, both `agent: executor` and `agent: { executor }` config forms, and the `ModelConfig` object form. Each is either spec-normative or the only correct way to do something a brain needs. ## Verification - `pnpm check` passes (the two fallow class-member warnings are pre-existing on main). - `@e2edev/e2e`: 822 tests passed. `@e2edev/playwright`: 124 passed. `@e2edev/agent-device`: 63 passed, 4 skipped. ## Downstream TesterArmy needs two edits before moving past `@e2edev/e2e` 0.4.0: drop `replay`/`secrets` from the `report_issue` annotations, and replace the post-execute `recordToolCall` in the brain's tool wrapper with a `runTool` wrapper around the execute call. ---

title: refactor!: rename backend to engine everywhere
body: ## Summary Deep rename of the "backend" concept to "engine" across the repo. The thing that drives a surface is an engine; "backend" reads like a server. - Case-preserving token rename in 219 files: `Backend*` → `Engine*`, `backend` → `engine`, `BACKEND_*` → `ENGINE_*`. - Moves: `src/backend/` → `src/engine/`, `cli/init/engines.ts`, the Playwright and agent-device `engine.ts`, every `backend*` test file and the fake helper, both fern pages, and the pending `app-lives-on-the-engine` changeset. - Articles fixed everywhere the noun changed ("a backend" → "an engine"). - Docs redirects for the old `/writing-a-backend` and `/reference/backend` slugs. - Disambiguation where "engine" previously meant something else: Playwright comments that said "browser engine" (chromium) now say "browser"; the locator engine is always qualified as such, its internal options type is `LocatorEngineOptions`, and the test helper is `makeLocatorEngineOverEngine`. `LocatorEngine` itself is unchanged. - Changeset: minor bump for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, `@e2edev/agent-device`. ## Breaking changes - `@e2edev/e2e/backend` → `@e2edev/e2e/engine` (`defineEngine`, `EngineHandle`, `EngineError`, `EngineFixtureContext`, ...). - Target config key `backend:` → `engine:`. - Error code `BACKEND_FAILURE` → `ENGINE_FAILURE`. - Report and session schemas: provenance field `backend` → `engine`. ## Deliberately untouched - The three `CHANGELOG.md` files, which describe released versions. RFC0001 and RFC0002 were renamed along with everything else since they are still draft design docs. Happy to revert those two if you'd rather keep them historical. ## Verification - `pnpm run check` passes (lint, dead-code, spec typecheck, build + typecheck, fern docs check). The two fallow class-member warnings and the zod dev-dependency note are pre-existing. - `pnpm test` passes: e2e 885 tests, playwright 142, agent-device 65 (4 pre-existing skips). ---

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2edev/e2e@0.6.0

### Minor Changes

- [`51ba502`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/51ba50207bd0fab811a56cd11cf7a97530a90190) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The package ships an agent skill: `SKILL.md` plus one reference file per
  topic (`setup`, `writing-tests`, `agent`, `running`, `debugging`) that
  teaches a coding agent to configure e2e, write tests, and read a failing run.
  `e2e init` installs it into `.agents/skills/e2e/` and `.claude/skills/e2e/`
  (a prompt on the first run, a silent refresh of the existing copies after an
  upgrade), `e2e guide [topic]` prints it for an agent that lacks the files,
  and `npx skills add tester-army/e2e` installs it from the repository.

- [#178](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/178) [`eb46707`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/eb467071b5b2e11a7c4e74dc6edb3c44490a4d43) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - `e2e cache ls`, `e2e cache stats`, and `e2e cache clear` read and empty the
  trace cache. Until now the only controls were `--no-cache` and deleting the
  directory, and a reviewer of a committed cache had no way to see what it held:
  entry files are named after the digest of their key. `ls` prints the test, the
  target, the instruction digest, the age, and the action count of every entry,
  `stats` prints the entry count and the size, and `clear` deletes the store's
  files and the directory. Recorded traces now carry the test, target, and
  instruction digest they were recorded for, which is where `ls` reads them
  from; entries written by an earlier version replay as before and list with
  `-` in those columns.

- [#171](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/171) [`fe569f2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/fe569f25ec3236c98751b6dc2628ff82763e62eb) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - `e2e list` prints the test-target pairs a run would select, one line per
  pair as `file › title [target]`, and exits without starting the app, an
  engine, or a worker. It takes the same files and selection flags as `e2e run`
  (`--config`, `--target`, `--tag`, `--tag-mode`, `--pass-with-no-tests`);
  `--reporter json` prints `{ "pairs": [...] }`.

- [#165](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/165) [`391f444`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/391f444ff6e1f399ab71d057aa32c90f6b06c6db) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The CLI has `--version` and a help worth reading. `e2e --version` (or `-v`)
  prints the installed version and exits 0. `e2e --help` opens with the version
  and tagline, lists the commands with examples, and points at the docs;
  `e2e run --help` groups the flags into Selection, Execution, and Output, then
  lists examples and the exit codes. `e2e help <command>` is the same as
  `e2e <command> --help`. Titles and flags are colored on a terminal and plain
  when piped or under `NO_COLOR`. A usage error now ends with
  `(add --help for usage)`.

- [#160](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/160) [`25a5838`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/25a5838512ebb0942d9c248cb2befc226c305e28) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `defineConfig` is gone. An `e2e.config.ts` default-exports the object literal
  and ends it with `satisfies E2EConfig`, which gives the same completion and
  unknown-key checks without a runtime import from `@e2edev/e2e`.

  ```ts
  // before
  import { defineConfig } from '@e2edev/e2e';
  export default defineConfig({ targets: [...] });

  // after
  import type { E2EConfig } from '@e2edev/e2e';
  export default { targets: [...] } satisfies E2EConfig;
  ```

- [#163](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/163) [`9e2519d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9e2519d1ed0c1b45d3c3cebed23de780c04ed617) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The first run of a new project fails with a sentence that names the fix, not a
  symptom. Walking through everything a first-time user does wrong:

  - `e2e init` without a terminal (a CI step, a pipe) used to wait forever on a
    prompt nobody could answer; it now exits 2 and names `--yes`. `e2e init
<directory>` scaffolds into that directory, creating it when missing, and the
    `next:` line starts with `cd`. An invalid `package.json` quotes the parser's
    position or the field with the wrong shape.
  - A Node.js older than 22.12 is told so, with both versions, before anything
    else loads.
  - `e2e run` with no config file is `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` naming the directory
    searched and `e2e init`, and calls out `e2e.config.js` (or another
    look-alike) when that is what exists, instead of `targets is required`.
  - A failing import in the config or a test file says what to do: a declared
    but uninstalled package ends with `run pnpm install` (or the project's
    package manager), an undeclared one with the add command, a wrong subpath
    with the subpaths the package exports, `defineConfig` with its replacement,
    and a misspelled export with the nearest one.
  - `NO_TESTS` says why: no file matched the `tests` globs (naming
    `tests/login.test.ts` and other look-alikes beneath the globbed directories),
    a positional matched nothing (with the nearest discovered file), a file
    registered no tests (its `test` is imported from elsewhere), or every test
    was filtered, skipped, or is a setup test.
  - Unknown config, target, agent, cache, limits, and artifacts keys, unknown
    `--target` IDs and reporters, and unknown fixtures all suggest the nearest
    valid name. Keys from other runners (`testDir`, `baseURL`, `webServer`,
    `use`, `projects`, a `url` on a target) point at where that fact lives here;
    `page`, `browser`, `context`, `request`, and `driver` fixtures are explained
    in terms of `app`, `screen`, and `web`. Durations name their unit and quote
    the value: `timeout must be a positive safe integer of milliseconds, got "30s"`.
  - A test failure carries its `cause` chain, so the scaffold's HTTP check fails
    with `fetch failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` rather than `fetch
failed`. `app.open()` against an address where nothing listens is
    `APP_UNREACHABLE` with the URL and the three ways to fix it, not an engine
    failure. A target without an engine says so when `screen` or `agent` is
    used, and names the two first-party engines.
  - A rejected model credential names the variable it was read from
    (`E2E_MODEL_API_KEY`, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, or the configured `apiKeyEnv`)
    rather than the gateway's own default, and ANSI color codes in provider
    messages no longer reach the report or the terminal.

- [#177](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/177) [`7e5b0cf`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7e5b0cffc2ce8a39e003ffc90ade25f8dd1e0a18) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - Judgments work on reasoning models. The judgment output cap is 8192 tokens
  so hidden reasoning no longer eats the answer, `agent.assert` has two model
  calls so a malformed response gets one repair round, and the adapter no
  longer pins `temperature: 0`, which reasoning models reject. A new
  `agent.providerOptions` config key sends AI SDK provider options (a reasoning
  effort, a thinking budget) with every model call of both the `act` and the
  judgment tiers.

- [#175](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/175) [`766cf52`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/766cf52c0db44be69d05079fa4f97726c3e5fa15) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - Node.js 22.12 is the floor. Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026; the
  `engines` field, the CLI's startup check, and the docs now all say 22.12.

- [#167](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/167) [`bbe8420`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bbe842042737f5df92766628429e5eb1cf67239f) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - Add `toBeFocused` and `toHaveAttribute` locator matchers, and make `getAttribute` read any attribute present on the element.
  Add `expect(web).toHaveClass(target, expected)` to the web fixture.

### Patch Changes

- [#162](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/162) [`203e938`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/203e9385a23a63d1ed103eb54804c4951a0c751a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The list reporter paints target badges on bright backgrounds. GitHub Actions
  renders the plain yellow background as dark brown, which made the first
  target's black label unreadable in CI logs.

- [#173](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/173) [`a312d5b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a312d5b9256e59470266d5e65e14289b5148c63c) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - `e2e init` prints a pointer to the new "Commit your traces" section of the
  config reference when it adds `.e2e/cache/` to `.gitignore`. Committing cache
  entries is opt-in; the section says how to opt in and what CI does with a
  committed cache.

- [#161](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/161) [`41612dc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/41612dcf44e6e395d578a23c09cf1dd451231095) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Package and CLI descriptions no longer call e2e a "standard".

- [#168](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/168) [`1ef5b00`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1ef5b003b62a588f554ad567f9d1f4540ffd8b35) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - READMEs and CLI help use the scoped package names (`@e2edev/e2e`,
  `@e2edev/playwright`, `@e2edev/agent-device`) on every install line, point at
  the Fern docs instead of e2e.dev, and describe e2e as an open framework for
  agentic end-to-end testing.

- [#176](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/176) [`cef82f8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/cef82f8e46c9f8ffbd79fa96b1dcc7843ea5dca5) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - A third Ctrl-C kills the process groups of every app command and service the
  run started before exiting, so they no longer survive the forced exit and
  fail the next run with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.

- [#159](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/159) [`2bd509d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2bd509d263b6b5a06d697261ab70d4df21926ba6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `Role` accepts the landmark roles (`main`, `navigation`, `banner`, `contentinfo`,
  `complementary`, `region`), `alertdialog`, and the structural and form roles the
  engines already report in observations (`searchbox`, `combobox`, `listbox`,
  `option`, `radio`, `list`, `table`, `row`, `cell`, `columnheader`). Scoping a query
  to the page's main content or a confirmation dialog no longer needs a platform
  selector such as `web.locator('main')` or `web.locator('[role="alertdialog"]')`:
  `screen.getByRole('main').getByText('Release website')` is portable. The Playwright
  engine resolves every role through Playwright's own accessibility engine, and the
  device engine matches the roles its node mapping produces; roles a platform never
  reports simply match nothing, as before.

title: feat(report): lay the list reporter out like vitest's default reporter
body: ## Motivation The `list` reporter printed one flat line per test-target pair as results arrived, with the error and code frame inline and a bare `8 passed` footer. With several workers the lines interleave across files, a failure's details scroll past in the middle of the run, and there is no sense of which files ran or how long the run took. Vitest's default reporter solves all of this and is what most of our users read every day, so this adopts its layout: file blocks, a `Failed Tests` section at the end, a padded summary, and a live window on a TTY. The reporter's own rules (8 KiB field cap, control-character stripping, permanent agent-step lines so a long agentic run reads in CI scrollback) are kept. ## Design - **File blocks.** Results buffer per test file and target and print as one line when the file's planned results are all in: ` ✓ web tests/todos.e2e.ts (6 tests | 1 flaky) 4.20s`, `❯` red for a file with a failure, `↓` for an all-skipped file, plus the file's `ai …` tokens and cost when a model was used. Tests are listed under the line, in declaration order, when the file failed, had a flaky pass, streamed agent steps, or is the run's only file (vitest's `renderSucceed` rule); a failed test shows `→ `. Files that never complete (an interrupt) print what they have at `run-finished`. - **Target badges** use vitest's project palette (black on yellow, cyan, green, magenta) in target-declaration order; `|web|` when colors are off. - **Failed Tests section** after the blocks: `⎯⎯ Failed Tests N ⎯⎯` banner, then per failure a ` FAIL ` label with badge, file and title path, `CODE: message` in red, ` ❯ tests/x.e2e.ts:7:5`, a two-lines-of-context code frame with a gutter (` 7| …`) and caret, and a right-anchored `[i/N]` divider. Run-level errors get a `Run Errors` banner the same way. - **Summary** with right-aligned titles: `Test Files`, `Tests`, `AI` (tokens, cost, calls), `Errors`, `Start at`, `Duration`, `Report`, `JUnit`, `AI trace`. Counts read `1 failed | 3 passed | 1 skipped (5)`; paths are project-relative. - **Live window** (`report/live-window.ts`, replaces `live-status.ts`): the reporter supplies the lines, the window keeps them painted below the log and repaints every 200 ms so elapsed times tick, wrapped in synchronized-output markers. It shows each running file with `❯` and `done/total`, running tests as `├──`/`└──` rows with elapsed time, the current step (`↳ agent.act "…"`) and its latest model or backend calls beneath, then the live `Test Files` / `Tests` / `Start at` / `Duration` counters. Rows are clamped to the terminal width and calls fold into a counter so the block always fits the screen. - **Agent step streaming.** With one test running, its agent steps still print permanently under a header naming the file and test; deterministic steps no longer print a header (the old per-test `▸` noise). In parallel mode a finished agent step prints prefixed with its test title, so CI logs of a long agentic run are not silent between file blocks. - **Colors** follow picocolors' own detection (TTY, `CI`, `FORCE_COLOR`) instead of TTY-only, so GitHub Actions logs are colored like vitest's. `ListReporter` takes `{ live, colors }`. - **Event stream.** `plan` gains `files: { file, target, tests }[]` (reportable pairs per file and target, unselected pairs excluded) and `test-started` gains `file`, so the reporter groups without a side lookup; the worker's `pair-start` message carries the file and `SchedulerEvents.onTestStart` gains the parameter. Both additive. The worker-joined title separator is now ` > ` to match. ## Docs and release - `fern/docs/pages/reference/cli.mdx`: the `list` row describes the new layout. - `fern/docs/pages/reference/embedding.mdx`: `plan` and `test-started` shapes, with a paragraph on `plan.files`. - `.changeset/vitest-style-list-reporter.md`: `@e2edev/e2e` minor. - `packages/testbed/e2e.mixed.config.ts`: the agent config plus the deterministic globs, for watching agent steps interleave with plain tests (`E2E_MODEL_API_KEY=… node node_modules/@e2edev/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.mixed.config.ts --no-cache …`). Opt-in like `test:agent`. ## Tests `tests/unit/report-list.test.ts` is rewritten around the new layout: banner; file blocks (single-line passing files, verbose single-file run, failed file with `→` line, flaky, skipped with reason, timed-out/interrupted labels, deselected results hidden, unfinished files flushed at run end, same file per target with palette order); failed-tests section (banner, `FAIL` entries, numbered dividers, ordering before the summary, no-error fallback); code frame gutter and caret column; summary rows including AI usage, run errors, and project-relative paths; solo vs parallel step streaming and deterministic steps staying quiet; live window contents, counters, notice ordering, no control sequences when off. `run-events` and `scheduler` fixtures carry the new fields. ## Verification - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/e2e exec vitest run --project unit`: 60 files, 696 passed, 1 skipped. - `tests/integration/cli-init.test.ts` + `runner-lifecycle.test.ts` against the rebuilt `dist`: 36 passed. - oxlint, `tsc --noEmit`, `check:spec`, `docs:check` clean; `check:dead-code` reports only main's pre-existing findings. - Testbed runs (non-TTY and under `script` for a real TTY) with a passing suite and with a temporary failing file to see the `Failed Tests` section and the code frame; TTY log confirmed the window erases before permanent lines and the summary prints after it stops. ---

title: docs(skills): add writing-pr skill and vendor unslop
body: Two project skills so PR titles and bodies come out the same shape regardless of which agent writes them. Same pair as tester-army/app#2290, adapted to this repo. - `writing-pr` (`.claude/skills/writing-pr/SKILL.md`): Conventional Commits title with `!` for spec or API breaks, bullets over essays, mermaid for runner and engine flow, code refs and snippets, before/after tables for CLI or reporter output and benchmarks, spec changes named with their `suiteVersion` bump. No "I ran tests" sections, no intermediate PR history. Blog-style body only for big or risky changes. - `unslop` vendored from `okwasniewski/dotfiles` and tracked in `skills-lock.json`. Auto-invoked (no `disable-model-invocation`), so it runs on any writing without being asked. `writing-pr` links it for the final voice pass. - `AGENTS.md` gotchas now point at both skills next to the existing Conventional Commits note, with the `npx skills add` line for non-Claude agents. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[agent drafts PR] --> B[writing-pr: shape] B --> C[unslop: voice] C --> D[gh pr create] ``` Both live as real directories under `.claude/skills`, the layout `unbox-ai` already uses here. ---

title: docker compose up --wait as a waitForExit service intermittently never exits under the runner (APP_UNREACHABLE after startupTimeout)
body:
## What happened

In the TesterArmy dashboard suite (`tester-army/app`, `packages/e2e-tests`), the first service is

```ts
{
  name: "compose",
  executable: "docker",
  args: ["compose", "--project-name", composeProject, "up", "--detach", "--wait", "--wait-timeout", "120"],
  waitForExit: true,
  startupTimeout: 180_000,
  teardown: compose("down", "--volumes", "--remove-orphans"),
}
```

On 2026-09-07, two runs out of roughly eight on one macOS machine (Docker Desktop, Compose v2) ended with

```
✗ infrastructure error APP_UNREACHABLE
service "compose" did not exit within 180000 ms
```

The same command, run directly in a shell right before or after the failing run, completes in about 1.8 seconds every time (four out of four attempts), including one attempt that reproduced the runner's conditions as far as I could: `env -i PATH HOME TMPDIR`, stdin from `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr redirected away from the terminal.

## Observations

- Not tied to the Compose project name or ports. One stall used the default project (`testerarmy-e2e`), the other a distinct project name with shifted host ports. While the default project was stalled inside one runner process, a second runner process started a second Compose project successfully at the same moment, so the Docker daemon was responsive.
- `docker ps -a` after the failed run showed no leftover containers for the project, so the teardown ran and either the containers never came up or `--wait` never returned.
- Re-running the identical command line immediately afterwards passes, so this looks like an intermittent interaction between the spawn (`detached: true`, stdout and stderr to `/dev/null` at the time) and `docker compose up --wait`, not a config error.
- Both stalls happened before `log` was set on the service, so there is no compose output from them. The suite now sets `log: ".e2e/services.log"` on the compose commands; the next occurrence will have the compose progress output attached here.

## Versions

- `@e2edev/e2e` 0.5.0 (pre-release build of main from 2026-09-05) and 0.5.1
- Docker Desktop on macOS, Compose v2, `postgres:16.4-alpine` and `redis:7-alpine` with `pull_policy: missing`

## Possible follow-ups

- A `waitForExit` service that is still running when `startupTimeout` expires could dump the last lines of its `log` (when set) into the `APP_UNREACHABLE` message, so a stall is diagnosable from the report alone.
- If the runner can cheaply detect that a `waitForExit` process is alive but silent, a notice at half the timeout ("compose has been running for 90s") would make the stall visible before the run is lost.

title: feat(locator): accept landmark, alertdialog, and structural roles in Role
body: - `Role` gains the landmark roles (`main`, `navigation`, `banner`, `contentinfo`, `complementary`, `region`), `alertdialog`, and the structural and form roles the engines already report in observations (`searchbox`, `combobox`, `listbox`, `option`, `radio`, `list`, `table`, `row`, `cell`, `columnheader`). - Type-only widening: the Playwright engine hands the role string to Playwright's accessibility engine (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts:36`), and the device engine compares against the role its node mapping produced (`packages/agent-device/src/locate.ts:85`). A role a platform never reports matches nothing, as before. - Same union in `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` and `fern/docs/pages/reference/screen.mdx`; no schema or `suiteVersion` change, since no wire output carries the union. - Motivation: a scope that means "the main content" or "the confirmation dialog" had to be a platform selector. The TesterArmy dashboard suite keeps six `web.locator('main')` / `web.locator('[role="alertdialog"]')` scopes for that reason alone. ```ts // before await web.locator("main").getByText("Release website", { exact: true }); await web.locator('[role="alertdialog"]').getByRole("button", { name: "Delete Project" }).tap(); // after await screen.getByRole("main").getByText("Release website", { exact: true }); await screen.getByRole("alertdialog").getByRole("button", { name: "Delete Project" }).tap(); ``` ---

title: feat(config)!: drop defineConfig in favour of satisfies Config
body: `defineConfig` was an identity function whose only job was type inference. `satisfies` does the same at the type level, so the helper and its runtime import go away. - `E2EConfig` is renamed to `Config`; there is no alias. - `e2e init` scaffolds the new shape, and the loader's `INVALID_CONFIG` message no longer names the helper (`packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts:93`). - Spec: `defineConfig` is dropped from `spec/api/e2e.d.ts`, and `spec/api/type-tests.ts` keeps the closed-union `@ts-expect-error` case through `satisfies`. - Docs: the reference page is retitled to Config with a new intro; nav, cards, READMEs, and RFC export tables follow. Changeset included as a minor bump. ```ts // before import { defineConfig } from '@e2edev/e2e'; export default defineConfig({ targets: [...] }); // after import type { Config } from '@e2edev/e2e'; export default { targets: [...] } satisfies Config; ``` ---

title: chore: drop the spec directory, keep the schemas and type tests in the package
body:
- `spec/` (17 chapters, `api/*.d.ts`, examples, roadmap, conformance manifest) had no consumer: the fern docs never cited it, there is no second implementation, and no conformance harness exists.
- It was already out of sync. `spec/api/e2e.d.ts` still exported `Web`, `WebRoute` and `DriverHandle`; `spec/api/driver.d.ts` described the SPI removed in #98. RFC0002 step 5 (reconcile the spec) never happened.
- `check:spec` could not catch any of that: `tsconfig.spec.json` mapped `@e2edev/e2e` to the spec's own d.ts, so the spec was typechecked against itself.
- Keeping it cost 27 commits in the last 30 days against 51 for `packages/`.
- RFC0001 and RFC0002 go too, for the same reason. The why now lives in PR descriptions and commit bodies.
- With no spec left, e2e is no longer called a "standard": the root and package `description` fields and the CLI `--help` header say framework, SDK, or engine instead. Patch changeset for the three published packages.

What stays, and where it moved:

| Was | Now | Consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/schema/*.schema.json` + fixtures | `packages/e2e/schema/` | `tests/helpers/report-schema.ts`, `session-schema.ts`, new `tests/unit/schema-fixtures.test.ts` |
| `spec/api/type-tests.ts` | `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts`, importing `../../src/index.ts` | package `typecheck` |
| `spec/14-security.md` | bullet list under Gotchas in `AGENTS.md` | agents |

Dropped outright: `RFC0001.md`, `RFC0002.md`, `conformance-v1` schema and manifest, `scripts/check-manifest-coupling.mjs`, `tsconfig.spec.json`, the `check:spec` and `check:manifest` scripts, and the `manifest` job in `spec.yml`. Every `(spec NN-chapter.md)` and `(RFC000x ...)` parenthetical in `src/` and `tests/` comments went with them; the surrounding sentences were kept or reworded, nothing else in those files changed.

Left alone on purpose:

- `.github/workflows/spec.yml` keeps its file and workflow name. Renaming changes the required-check names in branch protection.
- `specVersion: '0.1'` in config is a runtime API (cache identity, testbed configs). Removing it is a breaking change for another PR.

title: fix(report): paint target badges on bright backgrounds
