GitHub Actions renders plain yellow as dark brown, so the first target's badge was unreadable in CI logs while the cyan `RUN` banner next to it was fine. - The palette now uses the bright variants (`bgYellowBright`, `bgCyanBright`, `bgGreenBright`, `bgMagentaBright`), which stay light in the Actions log viewer and in regular terminals: `packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:63`. - Declaration-order assignment, the `|chromium|` no-color fallback, and the `RUN` / `FAIL` / `ERROR` banners are unchanged. | Target | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | 1st | `ESC[30m` on `ESC[43m` (yellow) | `ESC[30m` on `ESC[103m` (bright yellow) | | 2nd | `ESC[46m` (cyan) | `ESC[106m` (bright cyan) | | 3rd | `ESC[42m` (green) | `ESC[102m` (bright green) | | 4th | `ESC[45m` (magenta) | `ESC[105m` (bright magenta) | ---

title: feat(cli): first-run failures name the fix
body:
Walked a fresh `npx @e2edev/e2e init` project through everything a first-time user does wrong, then made each failure say what to do instead of what went wrong. - `init` without a terminal (CI step, pipe) hung forever on the engine prompt. It now exits 2 and names `--yes`. `e2e init ` scaffolds into a new directory and the `next:` line starts with `cd`. A broken `package.json` quotes the parser position or the field with the wrong shape. - `e2e --version` prints the installed version. `bin.ts` checks for Node 20.19 before loading anything, so an old runtime gets a sentence rather than a TypeError from inside a run. - A run with no config is `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, naming the directory searched and `e2e init`, and calls out a look-alike such as `e2e.config.js`. It used to resolve `{}` and report `targets is required`. - Import failures in the config or a test get a remedy from `packages/e2e/src/config/diagnose.ts`: a package that `package.json` declares but `node_modules` lacks ends with `run pnpm install` (the project's manager), an undeclared one with the add command, a wrong subpath with the subpaths the package exports, and `defineConfig` with its replacement. - `NO_TESTS` states its cause in `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`: the globs matched nothing (naming `tests/login.test.ts` and other look-alikes beneath the globbed directories), a positional matched nothing (with the nearest discovered file), a matched file registered no tests, or every test was filtered, skipped, or is a setup test. - Unknown config, target, agent, cache, limits, and artifacts keys, unknown `--target` IDs, reporters, and fixtures suggest the nearest valid name (`packages/e2e/src/internal/suggest.ts`). Keys from other runners (`testDir`, `baseURL`, `webServer`, `use`, `projects`, a `url` on a target) and the `page`, `browser`, `context`, `request`, and `driver` fixtures point at where that lives here. Durations name their unit and quote the value. - Plain test errors carry their `cause` chain, a navigation the network refused is `APP_UNREACHABLE` with the URL and three fixes, and a target without an engine names the two first-party engines when `screen` or `agent` is used. - `sanitizeText` strips ANSI escapes, so provider messages no longer reach the report and terminal as `�[31m` noise. A rejected gateway credential names `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY` (or the configured `apiKeyEnv`) instead of the gateway's own `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`. Where each diagnostic attaches on the first-run path: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["bin.ts
Node ≥ 20.19"] --> B["discoverConfig
CONFIG_NOT_FOUND, look-alikes"] B --> C["loadConfigModule
explainModuleError"] C --> D["resolveConfig
did-you-mean, foreign keys, units"] D --> E["collect
explainModuleError, near-miss files"] E --> F["select
NO_TESTS by cause, UNKNOWN_TARGET"] F --> G["fixtures
unknown fixture, APP_UNREACHABLE"] G --> H["classifyError
cause chain, ANSI strip"] ``` What the scaffold prints, captured from a scratch project installed from the built tarball: | Scenario | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `e2e init` in CI or a pipe | hangs on `Which engine?` | `e2e init asks questions and needs an interactive terminal; run it from a terminal, or pass --yes to accept the defaults (no engine, AI on, no installation)` | | `e2e run` with no config | `INVALID_CONFIG: targets is required: declare at least one target and the engine that drives it…` | `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: no e2e.config.ts or e2e.config.mts found in /app or its parent directories; run e2e init to create one, or pass --config ` | | `e2e run` before `npm install` | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: failed to load config /app/e2e.config.ts: Cannot find package '@e2edev/e2e' imported from /app/e2e.config.ts` | same, then `; @e2edev/e2e is declared in /app/package.json but is not installed: run npm install` | | `tests/example.test.ts` (wrong suffix) | `NO_TESTS: zero runnable ordinary test-target pairs; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched "tests/**/*.e2e.ts" under /app; found tests/example.test.ts, which the pattern does not match: rename to *.e2e.ts, or set tests in the config to a glob that matches; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this` | | `e2e run tests/exmple.e2e.ts` | `NO_TESTS: zero runnable ordinary test-target pairs (no test file matched: tests/exmple.e2e.ts); …` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched tests/exmple.e2e.ts (did you mean tests/example.e2e.ts?); the config globs discovered tests/example.e2e.ts; …` | | scaffold with nothing on :3000 | `ERROR: fetch failed` | `ERROR: fetch failed: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:3000; connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` | | Playwright scaffold with nothing on :3000 | `ENGINE_FAILURE: navigation failed: page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost:3000/` plus the call log | `APP_UNREACHABLE: nothing answered at http://localhost:3000/ (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED); start the app there, point the engine's url at where it runs, or give the engine a command so the runner starts it` | | `target:` instead of `targets:` | `unknown config key "target"` | `unknown config key "target"; did you mean "targets"?` | | `import { defineConfig }` | `The requested module '@e2edev/e2e' does not provide an export named 'defineConfig'` | same, then `; defineConfig was removed in @e2edev/e2e 0.5: default-export the object and end it with satisfies E2EConfig` | | `async ({ page })` on a Playwright target | `target "web" has no "page" fixture: engine playwright contributes web` | `target "web" has no "page" fixture; available: agent, app, platform, screen, session, web (engine playwright contributes web); there is no Playwright page: open the app with app.open() and find elements through screen; browser-only APIs are on the web fixture of a Playwright target` | | `screen` on a target without an engine | `target "default" has no engine capability for locators (screen)` | same, then `: the target declares no engine; add one, such as playwright({ url }) from @e2edev/playwright or agentDevice({ platform, app }) from @e2edev/agent-device` | | wrong `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY` | `the model provider failed: �[1m�[31mUnauthenticated request to AI Gateway.�[0m … set the �[33mAI_GATEWAY_API_KEY�[0m environment variable` | the same text without escape codes, then `the gateway rejected the credential read from E2E_MODEL_API_KEY (or the variable agent.model.apiKeyEnv names): check that the key is complete and belongs to the AI Gateway` | Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` gains the `init [directory]` argument, the non-interactive rule, `--version`, and a Diagnostics section; `reference/errors.mdx` widens the `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `NO_TESTS`, and `APP_UNREACHABLE` rows. Changeset: minor. ---

title: feat(cli): agent skill for coding agents, installed by init and printed by e2e guide
body: Coding agents working in a project that uses e2e need the config shape, the fixtures, the locator rules, and a way to read a failing run. That knowledge now ships as an agent skill on three paths: `e2e init` installs it into the project, `e2e guide` prints it, and `npx skills add tester-army/e2e` installs it from the repository. - `skills/e2e/` at the repo root: `SKILL.md` (overview, workflow, rules) plus `references/{setup,writing-tests,agent,running,debugging}.md`, one file per `e2e guide` topic. Root placement matters: `npx skills add` walks `skills/` and the agent directories and only falls back to a full scan when it finds nothing there. - The `@e2edev/e2e` build copies the directory to `packages/e2e/skills/` (gitignored, listed in `files`), so the published package carries it. `packages/e2e/src/cli/skill.ts` reads the package copy first and the repo source as the fallback, so unit tests need no build. - `e2e init` asks once where the skill goes: `.agents/skills` (Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Zed, and most other agents) and `.claude/skills` (Claude Code), both preselected. Later runs rewrite copies whose files differ from the installed version and never add a directory the project did not choose, so `init` after an upgrade refreshes the skill without asking. `--yes` writes both. - `e2e guide [topic]` prints the overview or one topic; an unknown topic exits 2 and names the valid ones. `e2e --help` lists it. - `fern/docs/pages/reference/cli.mdx`, both READMEs, AGENTS.md (the skill joins the "update in the same change" rule for behavior changes), and a minor changeset. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[skills/e2e in git] -->|npx skills add tester-army/e2e| A[.agents/skills and .claude/skills] S -->|build copies| K[packages/e2e/skills in the tarball] K -->|e2e init| A K -->|e2e guide topic| T[stdout] ``` ```bash npx --no-install e2e guide # overview and topic list npx --no-install e2e guide setup # one topic npx --no-install e2e init --yes # scaffold, skill into both directories ``` | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `init` writes package.json, config, example test, .gitignore entries | `init` also installs the skill, chosen in a multiselect on the first run | | No guidance reachable from the CLI | `e2e guide` prints the overview; `e2e guide writing-tests` one topic | Benchmark: fresh subagents configured e2e for a copy of the playground app (sign-in, todos, a wizard flow with one `agent.act`) from the same prompt, with `google/gemini-3.8-flash` behind the agent step. Baseline is the published 0.5.1 package; candidate is this branch's tarball with the skill installed. | Arm | Tests | Tool uses | Agent tokens | Errors hit | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Sonnet, published 0.5.1, no skill | 4/4 | 69 | 146k | 1 (`MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, missing `ai`) | | Sonnet, this branch, skill installed | 4/4 | 62 | 130k | 0 | | Haiku, this branch, skill installed | 4/4 | 44 | 42k | 0 | One run per arm, so read the numbers as a direction, not a measurement. The runs exposed gaps the skill now covers: `agent` may be omitted when `E2E_MODEL` is set, `ai@^7` is needed for any agent step, `{name}` placeholders in `act` are not expanded by the runner, `npx --no-install e2e init` when the package is already installed, `--yes` for a shell without a TTY. Pre-existing wart, unchanged here: `npx skills add tester-army/e2e` also lists the repo-internal `writing-pr` skill. ---

title: feat(cli): add --version and a grouped --help with examples and exit codes
body:
`e2e --version` did not exist, and `--help` was commander's default: no version, no examples, thirteen `run` flags in one flat list. - `e2e --version` and `-v` print the installed version, nothing else, and exit 0. - `e2e --help` opens with the version and tagline, lists the commands with examples, and links the docs. `e2e help ` prints the same text as `e2e --help`. - `e2e run --help` groups the flags into Selection, Execution, and Output, then lists examples and the exit-code table. - Titles are bold and flags cyan on a terminal. The help always carries color and commander strips it per stream when the output is piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, so stdout and stderr follow one policy (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:17`). - The `--tag-mode` and `--reporter` checks move out of the run action into commander parsers: `Option.choices` for the mode (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:146`), an `InvalidArgumentError` for an unknown reporter (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:43`). Every usage error now has commander's shape and ends with `(add --help for usage)`. Still exit 2; only the wording changed. - The CLI reference page gets a "Help and version" section. The changeset bumps `@e2edev/e2e` minor, like `--ai-trace` did. ## Before and after `e2e --help`, before: ``` Usage: e2e [options] [command] local-first agentic end-to-end testing Options: -h, --help display help for command Commands: init [options] scaffold an ESM package, e2e.config.ts, an example test, and .gitignore entries run [options] [files...] run e2e tests help [command] display help for command ``` After: ``` e2e v0.5.0 · local-first agentic end-to-end testing Usage: e2e [options] Options: -v, --version print the version -h, --help show help Commands: init [options] scaffold an ESM package, e2e.config.ts, an example test, and .gitignore entries run [options] [files...] run the tests help [command] show help for a command Examples: $ e2e init $ e2e run $ e2e run tests/signup.e2e.ts --headed $ e2e run --tag smoke --reporter list,junit Run e2e --help for the flags of one command. Docs: https://e2e.docs.buildwithfern.com ```
e2e run --help, before and after Before: ``` Usage: e2e run [options] [files...] run e2e tests Arguments: files test files, directories, or globs relative to the project root Options: --config explicit config path --target comma-separated target IDs --tag repeatable tag filter --tag-mode tag composition: any or all (default: "any") --headed request visible UI when the engine supports it --retries replace resolved retry count --workers replace worker count --reporter comma-separated reporters: list, json, junit --artifacts artifact root, default .e2e/artifacts --no-cache run without the trace cache, overriding the config --pass-with-no-tests allow zero runnable ordinary test-target pairs --debug print aggregated phase timings to stderr after the run --ai-trace record every model call to .e2e/ai-trace.json for trace viewers -h, --help display help for command ``` After: ``` Usage: e2e run [options] [files...] Run the tests the config discovers and write .e2e/report.json. Files, directories, and quoted globs narrow that selection, as do --tag and --target. Arguments: files test files, directories, or globs relative to the project root Selection: --config config file (default: the nearest e2e.config.ts) --target comma-separated target names (default: all targets) --tag only tests with this tag; repeat to combine --tag-mode how repeated tags combine (choices: "any", "all", default: "any") --pass-with-no-tests exit 0 on an empty selection instead of NO_TESTS Execution: --headed show the UI while tests run, when the engine supports it --workers parallel workers (default: from the config) --retries retries per failing test (default: from the config) --no-cache run with the trace cache off, whatever the config says Output: --reporter comma-separated reporters: list, json, junit --artifacts artifact root (default: .e2e/artifacts) --debug print phase timings and the agent step table to stderr --ai-trace record every model call to .e2e/ai-trace.json (unbox-ai) Options: -h, --help show help Examples: $ e2e run $ e2e run tests/signup.e2e.ts --headed $ e2e run 'tests/**/*.smoke.e2e.ts' --target web --tag smoke $ e2e run --reporter list,junit --workers 4 --retries 2 $ E2E_MODEL=provider/model-id E2E_MODEL_API_KEY=... e2e run --no-cache Exit codes: 0 every selected test passed, was flaky, or was skipped 1 a test failed or timed out 2 CLI, config, or agent policy error 3 engine, app process, model provider, or artifact failure 4 internal runner error 130 interrupted by Ctrl-C or a CI signal Docs: https://e2e.docs.buildwithfern.com/reference/cli#exit-codes ```
A usage error, before: ``` $ e2e run --tag-mode sometimes invalid --tag-mode "sometimes"; expected any or all ``` After: ``` $ e2e run --tag-mode sometimes error: option '--tag-mode ' argument 'sometimes' is invalid. Allowed choices are any, all. (add --help for usage) ``` ## How the groups are declared commander 15, already in the lockfile, has `optionsGroup`. The built-in help option keeps its own trailing `Options:` group. ```ts program .command('run') .optionsGroup('Selection:') .option('--config ', 'config file (default: the nearest e2e.config.ts)') .addOption(new Option('--tag-mode ', 'how repeated tags combine').choices(TAG_MODES).default('any')) .optionsGroup('Execution:') .option('--headed', 'show the UI while tests run, when the engine supports it') .optionsGroup('Output:') .option('--reporter ', 'comma-separated reporters: list, json, junit', parseReporters) ``` ---

title: docs: community files, public CONTRIBUTING, stability policy
body:
## What and why

Closes [ENG-697](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-697).

- `SECURITY.md`: disclosure channel (advisories or security@tester.army, ack in 3 business days, fix or plan in 30), supported versions, the trust model (code-trust vs untrusted model input, committed cache is code-trust), navigation policy with the two open gaps named honestly (top-level redirect re-check is still ENG-720 in backlog, popups unchecked), no telemetry plus the full outbound list.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` rewritten for the public flow. Inbound = outbound MIT, no CLA or DCO. The contract section follows #161: no spec directory anymore, so it points at the emitted `.d.ts`, the schemas, and the security invariants instead of `spec/README.md`. Private-phase and "stays internal" text is gone. New stability policy: what counts as breaking, six-month windows from October 1, 2026, how deprecations are announced, engine contract changes bump all three packages together.
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is Contributor Covenant 2.1 with conduct@tester.army as the contact.
- `.github/`: bug, feature, and docs issue forms (blank issues off, security routed to advisories), PR template with the changeset and docs checklist, `CODEOWNERS`, weekly `dependabot.yml` for npm (dev deps grouped) and actions.

Two things the reviewer should decide:

- The contact addresses `security@tester.army` and `conduct@tester.army` are assumed. Change them if those mailboxes do not exist.
- CONTRIBUTING now says packages publish as public, per the ticket. The manifests still say `publishConfig.access: "restricted"` and `release.yml` has no provenance. That flip is not in this PR since it is a release-day decision; until it happens the doc describes the target, not the current state.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: feat(e2e): preflight the model once; one canonical model configuration (ENG-703)
body:
## Summary

Closes ENG-703.

- `createAgent({ model })` fed only `act`; `assert`/`waitFor`/`extract` read `agent.model` or `E2E_MODEL`, so the quickstart config failed on the first judgment without a second model setting. `StepExecutor` now carries an optional `model`, `createToolLoopExecutor` sets it, and `resolveAgentConfig` treats it as the canonical model: executor model, then `agent.model`, then `E2E_MODEL`. An `agent.model` that names a different model than the executor's is `INVALID_CONFIG` at resolve time.
- `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` fired once per test because adapters were built lazily per call. `WorkerModels` (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker-models.ts`) builds the base adapter once per worker on the first `agent` acquisition (`createModelAdapter` validates provider shape and credential, no request). A failure is reported once through a new `run-abort` path and the run stops with the error's exit code (2), not 130; never-dispatched tests are `skipped`. A custom executor with no model skips the preflight; its judgment calls still fail on first use.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[agent fixture getter] --> P[WorkerModels.preflight]
  P -- ok, cached --> R[ModelRouter uses the same adapter]
  P -- throws --> E[TargetExecutor onRunAbort]
  E --> W[TargetWorker: local interrupt + run-abort message]
  W --> S[scheduler onRunAbort]
  S --> A["runner abortRun: recordRunError once, interruptController.abort()"]
```

```ts
// resolution, packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts
model: resolveCanonicalModel(agent?.model, executor?.model, env)
// executor model wins; agent.model naming another model -> INVALID_CONFIG
```

- `--debug` and the report already print `step.model` per step; with `createAgent({ model })` both tiers now show the same `provider/model`. Covered by `tests/integration/agent-policy.test.ts` (one run error for a 3-test suite; `extract` judged by the executor's model) and `tests/unit/agent-config.test.ts` (precedence, same-model acceptance, conflict).
- Docs: quickstart, agents, config and errors reference, `skills/e2e` references, scaffold comment, `AGENTS.md` gotcha, changeset (minor).

title: feat(config): E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT sets the model endpoint from the environment (ENG-705)
body:
## Summary

Closes [ENG-705](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-705).

- `agent.model.endpoint` was the only way off the hardcoded gateway URL, so an env-only setup (`E2E_MODEL` + a key) could only ever hit the Vercel gateway. `E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT` fills that gap; the gateway stays the default when neither source is set.
- Precedence mirrors `E2E_MODEL`: the config value wins over the variable. Both go through the same URL check (HTTPS, or `http:` on a loopback host), and the error names the source that supplied the bad value (`invalid E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT "..."` vs `invalid agent.model.endpoint "..."`).

```ts
// packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts
function resolveEndpoint(endpoint, env, label) {
  if (endpoint !== undefined) return validateEndpoint(endpoint, `${label}.endpoint`);
  const fromEnv = env.E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT?.trim();
  if (!fromEnv) return undefined;               // sdk.ts falls back to the gateway
  return validateEndpoint(fromEnv, 'E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT');
}
```

```bash
E2E_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.4-mini E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT=https://llm.example.com/v1 E2E_MODEL_API_KEY=... npx --no-install e2e run
```

- Unit tests cover env fallback, config-over-env precedence, blank values, and validation. Docs: `reference/config.mdx`, `agents.mdx`, the skill's env table, scaffold comment, changeset.

title: fix(cli): kill app and service process groups on the third signal (ENG-700)
body:
## Summary

Closes [ENG-700](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-700).

- The third Ctrl-C called `process.exit(130)` while app commands and services ran `detached` in their own process groups, so they outlived the run and the next one failed with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
- `managed-process.ts` keeps a module-level `live` set of spawned children (added on spawn, removed on `exit`) and exports `killManagedProcessGroups()`: a synchronous best-effort `SIGKILL` to every group still in it. Reused processes never enter the set. The group-signalling code `stop` already had moved into `signalProcessGroup(child, signal)` so both paths share it.
- `SignalLadder` calls it on the third rung, before `exit(130)`:

```ts
else {
  killManagedProcessGroups();
  exit(130);
}
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S1[SIGINT #1] --> I[interrupt: runner stops services/app gracefully]
  I --> S2[SIGINT #2] --> F[force: workers dispose now]
  F --> S3[SIGINT #3] --> K[killManagedProcessGroups: SIGKILL every live group] --> X[process.exit 130]
```

- New integration test in `tests/integration/interrupt-signals.test.ts`: a service that never becomes ready, ignores `SIGTERM`, and spawns a grandchild. Three Ctrl-Cs during services startup; asserts exit 130 within seconds and both pids gone. Fails on `main` (`timed out waiting for the service group to die`). The harness was generalized to `withRunningCli(fixture, body)` so the existing tests and this one share it.
- Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` Signals section; changeset (patch).

title: feat(cli): read and empty the trace cache with e2e cache
body:
## Summary

- The only cache controls were `--no-cache` and `rm -rf .e2e/cache`. Entry files are named after the SHA-256 of their key, so a reviewer of a committed cache could not tell what was in it. `e2e cache ls|stats|clear` is the missing half.
- All three resolve the store the way a run does: `discoverConfig` -> `loadConfigModule` -> `resolveConfig`, so `cache.dir` and `--config <path>` mean the same thing here as in `e2e run`. A configured `cache.store` is refused with an error instead of guessed at, since `TraceCacheStore` is keyed lookup only and has nothing to enumerate.
- `ls` needs provenance the entry did not carry, so a recorded trace now names what it was recorded for:

```ts
export interface TraceProvenance {
  readonly testId: string;
  readonly targetId: string;
  readonly instructionDigest: string;
}
// ActionTrace
+ readonly recordedFor?: TraceProvenance;
```

  Optional, and validated on read like the rest of the entry (bounded text, `/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`), so an entry recorded by an earlier version still replays and just lists with `-` in those columns. It carries no authority: all three fields are already in the cache key, so a mismatch is a miss before the file is opened. `StepTraceSession` fills it from `cache.identity` plus `instructionDigest(instruction)`, which is why `AgentCacheContext` grew an `identity` field, and `TraceRecorder.finalize()` requires it.
- `ls` reads through `FileTraceCacheStore.read()` rather than parsing the JSON itself, so the size cap and entry validation are the same code that gates replay. Output is one row per entry, sorted by test then target then recording time, and shows only the digest's first 12 characters plus counts. No action, selector, or model text reaches the terminal.

```
TEST                                TARGET  INSTRUCTION   AGE  ACTIONS
tests/billing.e2e.ts::upgrades      safari  eeeeeeeeeeee  <1m  1
tests/signup.e2e.ts::creates        web     dddddddddddd  2h   4 (truncated)
```

- `clear` deletes the entries, the unreadable digest-named files, and the writer's `.tmp` leftovers, then removes the directory. A file that is not the store's own is left in place and named on stderr, because `cache.dir` can be a directory someone else also writes to.
- `stats` counts and sizes readable entries, and reports unreadable ones on their own line rather than folding them into a number a reviewer would trust.

The ticket also asked for a `spec/06-cli.md` update. There is no `spec/` in this repo (`AGENTS.md`: "There is no separate spec"), so the CLI reference page and the `e2e guide running` skill topic carry the docs instead.

title: fix(collect): locate test declarations past the shipped source maps (ENG-699)
body:
## Summary

Every test in `report.json` reported `line 325, column 37` (or similar) because `captureSource` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts` skipped only frames under `dist/`, while the shipped `.js.map` files map the runner's own frames back to `src/`, so a runner frame won over the user's `test()` call site.

- `captureSource` now skips both runner code roots under the package root: `dist/` (what a shipped package executes) and `src/` (where the source maps point). This intentionally uses the two code roots rather than the bare package root: the package also holds files that legitimately declare tests, like this repo's fixture projects under `tests/`, which a package-root prefix would swallow.
- Frame paths now drop the `?e2e=...&tsx-namespace=...` loader query before matching, same as `userFrame` in `src/report/code-frame.ts`.
- `<testcase>` in `junit.xml` gains `file` and `line` attributes naming the declaration, so the location reaches CI test summaries too.
- Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/running.md` now note that `steps[].source` is `{ "file": "unknown" }` since per-step capture is a separate follow-up.

Verified end to end with the new `tests/integration/source-location.test.ts`: the built CLI runs a fixture project through the real tsx loader, and a test declared on line 5 reports `tests/source.e2e.ts:5:1` in `report.json`, `file="tests/source.e2e.ts" line="5"` in `junit.xml`, and a code frame on the throwing line in the list reporter.

Fixes ENG-699.

title: feat(cua): add the Cua Driver desktop engine (macOS, Windows, Linux)
body:
`@e2edev/cua` is the desktop engine: native, Electron, and Tauri apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through [Cua Driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua/tree/main/libs/cua-driver), against the same `defineEngine` contract the browser and mobile engines implement. Core is untouched.

- `cua({ app })` launches the app fresh per attempt, observes one of its windows as a semantic node tree (roles mapped onto the shared vocabulary, names, values, states, bounds in window points, redacted pixels on request), and quits it after.
- Every action addresses its node by the driver's per-snapshot element token, so a ref from an older observation is `NODE_STALE` and a partly delivered input is `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`, never repeated blindly.
- Secure text fields carry no value in the tree and are painted over in every image the engine emits.
- The contributed `desktop` fixture adds `locator(selector)`, `menu(path)`, `hotkey(chord)`, and `window()`.
- `@trycua/cua-driver` is pinned to an exact version: its tool contract changed five times in the three weeks before this PR.
- New reference page `reference/desktop`, root scripts, README and CONTRIBUTING entries, a minor changeset, and an opt-in testbed suite (`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:desktop`) that drives TextEdit with `screen` and `desktop` only.

Why this driver: it is the one maintained cross-platform accessibility-tree driver reachable from Node in-process (AX, UI Automation, AT-SPI, MIT). terminator ships Windows-only binaries and has been dormant since June; Scrapybara and Bytebot are gone; provider computer-use APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) are pixels in, coordinates out, so they belong to the agent tier, not an engine.

```ts
import type { E2EConfig } from '@e2edev/e2e';
import { cua } from '@e2edev/cua';

export default {
  targets: [{ name: 'mac', platform: 'macos', engine: cua({ app: 'com.apple.TextEdit' }) }],
  workers: 1,
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```ts
import { expect } from '@e2edev/e2e';
import { test } from '@e2edev/cua';

test('a new document takes text', async ({ app, screen, desktop }) => {
  await app.open();
  await desktop.menu(['File', 'New']);
  await screen.getByRole('textbox').first().fill('Hello from e2e');
  await expect(screen.getByRole('textbox').first()).toHaveValue('Hello from e2e');
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  I[init: check_permissions] --> S[startAttempt: launch_app]
  S --> W[list_windows until the window option matches]
  W --> O[observe: get_window_state]
  O --> P[project elements into SemanticNode tree]
  P --> A[perform by element_token: click, set_value, press_key, hotkey, scroll, drag]
  A --> O
  O --> E[endAttempt: kill_app]
```

| Contract member | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `observe` | `get_window_state` → `packages/cua/src/nodes.ts` projection; frames in screenshot pixels become window points; viewport is the window |
| `locate` | every `screen` query plus `screen.locator('role=AXButton label="Save"')` (`packages/cua/src/selector.ts`) |
| `perform` | tap, doubleTap, fill, clear, press, check/uncheck, selectOption by label, hover, dragTo, node swipe, focus on fields |
| `swipe` | wheel gesture at the window centre |
| `app.restart`, `artifacts.screenshot`, `url` | quit and relaunch; masked PNG; `app://desktop/<app>/<window title>` |
| not declared | longPress, scrollIntoView, setInputFiles, selectOption by index, `app.back`, `app.clearState`, state capture |

Errors map in `packages/cua/src/errors.ts`; the key vocabulary (`Enter`, `ArrowDown`, `Meta+Shift+k`) maps in `packages/cua/src/keys.ts`.

## Open before merge

- No live run yet. macOS attributes Accessibility to the process that runs the tests, and the authoring environment had no grant, so the engine was exercised through a scripted driver (`packages/cua/tests/unit`). To validate, grant Accessibility and Screen Recording to a terminal and run `E2E_CUA_DESKTOP=1 pnpm --filter @e2edev/cua test:desktop`, then the testbed suite.
- That run settles two assumptions: whether the driver's `elements[]` includes static text or only actionable nodes (which decides how well `getByText` works), and the exact per-element state fields on macOS. Windows and Linux field names (`control_type`, `name`, `rect`, `automation_id`) are handled but unverified.
- Draft until the live run passes.

title: feat(cli): e2e mcp gives coding agents a live session on the app
body:
`e2e mcp` is an MCP server over stdio for a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor). It gives the agent a live session on the app with the same tools the testing agent has, so the agent looks at the real screen and checks a locator before writing the test. Running tests and reading a failed run stay on the CLI, which the agent already has; run history belongs to the dashboard later.

- `open_session` grades and prepares the engine, starts the declared app command, boots the engine, starts one attempt, opens the app URL, and returns the first observation. `close_session` tears all of it down. One session at a time.
- The grammar tools are `createGrammarTools` output mapped 1:1 to MCP tools (`observe`, `tap`, `type`, `press`, `select`, `scroll`, `navigate`, `type_secret`): same names, descriptions, schemas, and "updated screen" results. Verbs the engine cannot honor are not offered. Project tools from `createAgent({ tools })` are served too, through the same `runTool` accounting; a project tool named like a built-in is not served, with a warning.
- `type_secret` is offered with every configured credential as a step secret, so a password is filled by name and never reaches the agent. Once a secret is on screen, `screenshot` is withheld (`PIXEL_TAINTED`), exactly as in a test.
- `locate` tries a semantic query against the live screen and prints how many nodes match, which, and the `screen.*` call to write; zero or several matches name the error a test would get.
- `--target` fixes the target; `--headless` hides the UI (sessions are headed by default outside CI). Sessions close after 30 idle minutes, after 4 hours, on client disconnect, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. An `open_session` that fails partway tears down what it started.
- Stdout is the protocol: the transport gets its own stream on fd 1 and every other `process.stdout` write goes to stderr for the life of the process. The integration test proves it with a config that calls `console.log`.
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is a regular dependency (6 MB installed); an optional peer would have meant an install step in every doc and a failure mode that exists only to explain the missing package.
- `e2e init` offers to register the server in `.mcp.json` (Claude Code) and `.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), merging into existing files. `e2e guide mcp` prints the new skill topic; the skill is also served as `e2e://guide` resources.

The session is one interactive agent step (`packages/e2e/src/agent/interactive-step.ts`): a recorded `agent` step whose executor is the host, opened on the attempt's agent runtime. Every MCP call runs inside the step, so budgets, origin policy, the secret ledger, pixel taint, stale-id rejection, and step recording are the harness's own. Nothing reimplements a verb.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as coding agent
  participant H as SessionHost
  participant Q as InteractiveStep.run (inside the recorded step)
  participant C as StepExecutorContext
  participant E as engine
  A->>H: tap { target: "n4" }
  H->>Q: run(body)
  Q->>C: actions.tap({ id: "n4" })
  C->>E: perform(ref, tap)
  C-->>Q: updated screen
  Q-->>H: result
  H-->>A: "Tapped #n4. Updated screen (revision b6): ..."
```

Runner changes that make this possible, all shared with the test path:

- `packages/e2e/src/run/standalone.ts` opens one attempt with the full fixture graph and no test body, reusing `TargetExecutor.launchSession`/`closeSession`. `launchSession` now takes the session name instead of the pair.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/provision.ts` holds `validateEngine`, `prepareEngine`, and `startDeclaredProcesses`, moved out of `runner.ts` so a run and a standalone attempt provision identically. A start that fails partway now stops what it started before rethrowing, which the inline runner code did through its teardown list.
- `createAgent` returns `DefaultAgent`, the executor plus its `tools`, so a host can serve the project's vocabulary. `projectTools` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/default-agent.ts` runs them through the step's accounting and throws; the model loop turns failures into text through its guard, the MCP server into error results.
- `createFixtures` returns the fixtures and the agent runtime behind them; `openStandaloneAttempt` exposes the runtime so a host can open steps itself.

Registration every client accepts:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["--no-install", "e2e", "mcp"] } } }
```

What `locate` answers, from the testbed playground:

```text
1 node matches getByRole("link", name: "Todos").
Use: screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Todos" })
- link "Todos"
```

Also in this PR: `tests/unit/cli.test.ts` still asserted the help tagline from before #168; it now matches the CLI.

Not exercised live: the agent-device tool pack over MCP (no simulator here) and the headed default (the smoke run used `--headless`).

Docs: `fern/docs/pages/reference/mcp.mdx`, the `e2e mcp` section of the CLI page, `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`.

## Review follow-ups (cubic)

- `close()` no longer wipes the credential registry a session opened during its teardown had just set; the registry is cleared only when no session is live or opening (integration test added).
- `serveMcp` resolves `closed` at once for an already-aborted signal; a failure after `launchSession` in `openStandaloneAttempt` tears the session, engine, and processes down before rethrowing.
- `planMcpRegistration` matches the server entry by `command` and `args`, whatever the key order or extra keys (unit test added).
- `runner.ts` consumes `prepareEngine` and `startDeclaredProcesses` from `provision.ts`; the shared starter takes per-kind hooks so the run still narrates services and apps as separate setup steps. The runner's own copies are gone.
- Code quality pass: the session's queue executor, synthetic agent, and unbounded budgets became the interactive step; `McpToolSpec` is generic over its zod schema (no casts, errors wrapped once in the server); the catalog and locate rendering live in `packages/e2e/src/mcp/catalog.ts`; `toModelOutput` rendering is typed from the SDK; the session's screenshot uses the same file part encoding as agent-device; `e2e init` shares one location prompt for the skill and the MCP registration.
- Session tools are `openWorldHint: true`; the read-only tool comment says what the set holds; the tour test has its own 300 s budget.
- Docs: MCP codes in their own errors subsection (tool or resource-read errors, never in a report), `--target` as a default that `open_session` overrides, `--config` reload versus the startup tool list, `type_secret` conditions, `init` offers to register, target-dependent tool list on the CLI page.
- The `observe` row keeps the path, qualified: the tool does print `at /path` when the target has one.

If you previously used prettier: false, migrate to format: false or remove the option to use automatic formatter detection.

  • #2190 96b65ee Thanks @​bluwy! - Move versioned prerelease changesets to .changeset/pre/ folder instead of accumulating in the root and tracking the versioned changeset ids in the .changeset/pre.json file. Existing pre.json will auto-migrate to this new structure on the next run of changeset version or when calling changeset status.

    This change allows easier management of versioned prerelease changesets (for the final stable release) and current queued changesets (for the next prerelease). Changesets in .changeset/pre/ can be edited or deleted depending if it's still relevant for the final stable release of a package. There's no need to synchronize the changeset ids in pre.json if certain changesets are deleted.

  • #2097 8c88f6a Thanks @​Andarist! - Packages with only prerelease versions published will now be published with the prerelease tag in the prerelease mode if the target registry doesn't auto-assign latest tag. npm registry itself does that and such packages will continue to be released with latest tag (and not with the configured prerelease tag).

  • #1655 db46911 Thanks @​bluwy! - Update @manypkg/get-packages which drops support for detecting packages in Bolt monorepos and adds support for npm monorepos

title: chore(deps): bump playwright from 1.61.1 to 1.63.0
body:
Bumps [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.61.1 to 1.63.0.
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

title: feat(report): print each file, test, and step once; live window carries the tree
body: ## What and why - One test rendered as two: the streamed layout printed a `❯ file > test` opener, the steps, the file line, then the test line again nested under it. Every name now appears exactly once. The live window carries the in-progress tree and the file block prints once, with agent steps nested under their test (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts`). - The `streamed` flags on the group, each line, the running test, and the set of streamed pair keys are gone. One rule remains: with a live window, finished steps accumulate in memory and print in the block, and a file that ran agent steps lists its tests even when it passed so the scrollback keeps them; without one (CI logs), they print as they finish, prefixed with their test. - The live window has a fixed-height running area (never shrinks during the run), so the summary below it no longer jumps as calls come and go. - Model turns read as `• Thinking (4.57s) (↑1.3k ↓156)`. The executor reports a turn in the AI SDK step-finish hook, after that turn's tools already ran, so the turn is inserted ahead of its tool rows and the window reads in causal order. The turn in flight shows a bloom indicator with a shimmering `Thinking`. - Tool calls read as the act the engine recorded (`› type "Buy milk" into textbox "New todo" (14ms)`). - The `RUN` banner names the configured model. The summary `AI` row no longer reads `AI ai …`. - Steps are held as records (`FinishedStep`, `CurrentStep` in `packages/e2e/src/report/list-model.ts`) and rendered where they print, so the file block and CI logs carry the whole label and only the live window clips it to the row (`packages/e2e/src/report/list-steps.ts`). The window body is its own module, `packages/e2e/src/report/running-tree.ts`; `list.ts` stays under 650 lines. - Wire, additive: model `StepEvent`s carry `inputTokens` and `outputTokens` beside `count`; `run-started` carries `model`. Schema updated; the report fixtures contain no step events to extend. ## Before / after Before, final output for one test: ``` ❯ web tests/example.e2e.ts > app opens ✓ agent.act "navigate to every page in the footer" 79.81s · 24 model calls ✓ web tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test) 82.94s ai 266.5k tokens · $0.0640 ✓ app opens 82.94s ai 266.5k tokens · $0.0640 ``` After: ``` RUN e2e v0.6.0 /Users/…/packages/testbed run 01a08107-5454-7034-922d-c478ff40c9f5 · targets: web model google/gemini-3-flash ✓ web tests-agent/tmp-stream.e2e.ts (1 test) 175.78s ai 15.1k tokens · $0.0096 ✓ todo flow streams 175.78s ai 15.1k tokens · $0.0096 ✓ agent.act "add two todos named "Buy milk" and …" 123.11s · 5 model calls ✓ agent.act "mark "Buy milk" as done" 26.93s · 2 model calls ✓ agent.assert "exactly one todo remains open" 25.21s · 1 model call Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) AI 15.1k tokens · $0.0096 · 8 model calls ``` Live window while running (TTY): ``` ❯ web tests-agent/tmp-stream.e2e.ts 0/1 └── todo flow streams 63.25s ✓ agent.act "add two todos named "Buy milk" and…" 52.84s · 5 model calls ↳ agent.act "mark "Buy milk" as done" • Thinking (1.56s) (↑1.4k ↓77) › tap checkbox "Buy milk" (10ms) ✢ Thinking Test Files 0 passed (1) Tests 0 passed (1) ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR S[step end, agent] --> L{live window?} L -- yes --> M[hold under running test] M --> W[window: test row, finished steps, current step] M --> B[file complete: block with steps nested] L -- no --> P[print now: test > step] P --> B2[file complete: block, tests only] ``` ## Checklist - title: fix(run): keep a first-run browser download off the run's clock
body:
## What and why - A first-run browser download ran after `plan`, inside the run's clock. The run that prompted this reported a 2.87s test as `Duration 17.45s`, with `Start at` stamped before Chromium was fetched. - The runner now collects and selects, grades each target, runs every engine's `prepare`, and only then emits `plan`, starts the app, and schedules tests. `plan` is where the clock starts: the report's `run.startedAt` and the list reporter's `Start at` and `Duration` are taken there (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:449`, `packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:283`). - The live window shows no clock rows until `plan`, so nothing ticks under a download. A run that never reaches `plan` (config or collection failure, failed download) still prints how long it took to fail, counted from launch. - Two consequences of the order: `NO_TESTS` and other collection failures are reported before any app command or service starts, and a missing browser is fetched before the app boots. - Event stream: `run-started` stays first; `notice` lines from `prepare` now precede `plan` instead of following it. No type changes; the JSDoc and `fern/docs/pages/reference/embedding.mdx` describe the order. - Stale prose fixed on the way: `packages/playwright/README.md` and `AGENTS.md` still said browsers install per worker in `init`. They have installed in `prepare` since #115. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before["main"] direction LR a1[run-started] --> a2[app start] --> a3[collect] --> a4[plan] --> a5[prepare
browser download] --> a6[tests] end subgraph after["this PR"] direction LR b1[run-started] --> b2[collect] --> b3[prepare
browser download] --> b4[plan
clock starts] --> b5[app start] --> b6[tests] end ``` Before, a fresh machine (`e2e-playground`, one 2.87s test): ``` RUN e2e v0.6.0 /Users/okwasniewski/workspace/e2e-playground ℹ Downloading missing Playwright browsers (first run): chromium... ℹ ... 276 MiB of progress ... ℹ Browser download complete. ✓ web tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test) 2.87s Start at 12:31:09 Duration 17.45s ``` After, the testbed smoke file with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` pointed at an empty directory (run launched at 12:58:33): ``` RUN e2e v0.6.0 .../packages/testbed ℹ Downloading missing Playwright browsers (first run): chromium... ℹ ... progress ... ℹ Browser download complete. ✓ |web| tests/smoke.e2e.ts (2 tests) 1.84s Start at 12:58:47 Duration 2.13s ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: fix(agent)!: drop the act options the runtime rejects
body: ## What and why - `Agent.act` had a `schema` overload returning `data` and took `vision` through `AgentOptions`, and `packages/e2e/src/agent/act-validation.ts` threw `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` on both, on every call. The compiler said yes, the runner said no. `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` even pinned the overload. - The type now says what the runtime does: `act(instruction, params?, { timeout?, maxSteps?, maxModelCalls? })` returning `{ ok: true }`. `AgentSchemaOptions` and `AgentResultWithData` are gone; `VisionOption` stays on the judgments, which honor it. - The runtime guard stays for callers outside the type checker; the type test now asserts that `schema` and `vision` on `act` fail to compile. - Docs and the README limitation list stop describing the options as "not implemented yet" and point at what works: `agent.extract({ schema })` for structured data, `vision` on `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract`. ```ts // before: compiles, then throws UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY at run time const { data } = await agent.act('read the total', undefined, { schema: z.object({ total: z.number() }) }); // after: the same intent, on the tier that implements it const { total } = await agent.extract('read the total', { schema: z.object({ total: z.number() }) }); ``` - Refs: `packages/e2e/src/types.ts` (`AgentOptions`, `Agent.act`), `packages/e2e/src/agent/act-validation.ts` (`rejectUnsupportedActOptions`), `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts`. The stability policy counts a removed export as breaking, hence the `!`. The removed forms never executed successfully, so I am proposing this as a type correction rather than a deprecation-window removal. If you would rather hold it for the October batch, the changeset body already names the replacement. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). No warning could land earlier: the old form never ran, see above. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(run): one status for the outcome, the run-finished event, and the report
body:
## What and why

- One run, two statuses. `report.json` derives `blocked` when every non-passing result carries a blockable code (`packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts`, `deriveRunStatus`), while `RunOutcome.status` and the `run-finished` event came from the exit code alone (`statusOf`) and said `failed`. A host that read the event and then the file saw them disagree.
- `finish()` now reads the status back from the report it just built, so the outcome, the event, and the file carry one value. `RunStatus` on `@e2edev/e2e/run` names the union, `blocked` included. `statusOf` keeps feeding the report builder its exit-code status; the derivation lives in one place.
- Review follow-up: `deriveRunStatus` used to ignore run-level errors, so a run whose only failing results were blockable but whose cleanup or report write failed came out `blocked` and hid the infrastructure failure. It now returns the exit-code status whenever the run recorded a run error; `tests/unit/report-status.test.ts` covers blocked, blocked plus a product failure, and blocked plus a run-level error.
- The list reporter prints paths and counts on `run-finished` and never branched on the status, so terminal output is unchanged. Exit codes are unchanged too: `blocked` is a status, not a new code.

```ts
// before
const status = statusOf(exitCode);        // 'failed' for an all-blocked run
const report = buildRunReport(exitCode);  // report.run.status === 'blocked'

// after
const report = buildRunReport(exitCode);
const status = report.run.status;         // the same value everywhere
```

Refs: `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts` (`finish`, `statusOf`), `packages/e2e/src/run/events.ts` (`RunStatus`), `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts` (`deriveRunStatus`).

`@e2edev/e2e/run` is host tooling and grows in minors (see the header of `packages/e2e/src/run/public.ts`), so this ships as a minor without a `!`.

title: feat(run): setup steps narrate collection, provisioning, and startup
body:
## What and why - Three PRs patched the same blind spot from different sides: #191 moved the clock past a first-run browser download, the first version of this PR narrated service and app startup with a `process` event, and #200 kept an interrupt before the plan from reading as "no test files". The run has a setup stretch between `run-started` and the first test, and neither the events, the reporter, nor the report knew it existed. This PR replaces #191 and the earlier version of itself with one model. - One additive event, `setup`, covers everything before the first test: `collect`, each target's engine `prepare` (`{ target, engine }`), and every `service` and `app` command, `started` then `finished` with its length and `outcome: 'reused'` for an attached process (`packages/e2e/src/run/events.ts`). A step that fails ends as a `run-error`; a step the interrupt cuts short reports nothing more. `SetupStep` is exported from `@e2edev/e2e/run`. - Runner order (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`): validate the process declarations, collect, grade each target, prepare each engine, emit `plan`, then start services and the app, then run. `NO_TESTS` and conflicting service declarations fail before any process starts or download begins, and a missing browser is fetched before the app boots. The `ManagedProcess` hooks from the first version stay (`packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`). - Accounting, stated once in the docs: `Start at`, `Duration`, and the report's `run.startedAt` count from `plan`. Collection and provisioning are off the clock; service and app startup is on it, split out as `(startup 3.14s)`. - List reporter (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts`): one handler for every step. title: feat(cache): positional targets, volatile-free anchors, and created-record paths replay
body: ## What and why Measured on the TesterArmy dashboard suite (20 `agent.act` steps, `e2e run tests/agent`, `.e2e/report.json` `step.cache` tallied per run). With every step verified and every input labelled, three replays still handed off on every run, each for a reason the runner could resolve itself: - **Twins the description cannot tell apart** replayed as `target-ambiguous` forever: one unlabeled `Set up` per integration card, one `Add step` per step gap, two `Add project` buttons on the projects page. The recorder now checks its own description against the recording screen (`describePosition`, `packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts`) and, when it matches several controls, stores the target's `position` among them. `relocateDescriptor` honors it only when the live screen shows exactly as many twins; any other count diverges as before, so a twin that appears or vanishes never becomes a guess. The action summary reads `tap button "Add project" (1 of 2)`. - **Volatile text as an end anchor** made a step hand off as `end-mismatch` on every run: an API-key row anchored on `sk_b1bccf4e03c5_...` and `6 days 23 hours remaining`, a memory row on `Added Sep 8, 2026`. `describeAnchors` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`) skips minted tokens, countdowns, dates, and clock times while any stable anchor remains; with nothing else it keeps them, since a replay that always hands off is still safer than one that passes on mechanics alone. - **A step that lands on a created record** could never replay: its `endPath` carried the new project's id, and the agent's repair clicks evicted the recording each run. `samePathShape` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/decide.ts`) matches the end path up to segments the app mints (uuid, hex or digit runs, long mixed-case or digit-bearing tokens), and a moved step now records the new page's first stable anchors as well, so the shape match is backed by content (`packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`). Trace entries written by earlier versions read as before; `position` is optional and validated (`readDescriptor` rejects a malformed one). Docs: the cache section of the config reference. Changeset: patch. ## Before / after Same suite, same machine, cache warm from the previous run: | Run | self-finalized | handed off / missed | model calls | cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.6.1, before app or runner fixes | 5 / 20 | 15 | 71 | $0.11 | | 0.6.1, tests verified + inputs labelled | 18 / 20 | `target-ambiguous` (Add project), `end-mismatch` (API key) | 10 | $0.0097 | | this branch | 20 / 20 | 0 | 2 (uncacheable `agent.assert` judgments) | $0.0021 | Pollution checks against the same recordings: a pre-existing group with the target name made the recorded `+ Create "…"` button vanish and the replay handed off `target-not-found`; a seeded twin row made the recorded unique target ambiguous and the replay handed off `target-ambiguous` before acting; the live agent then organized the wrong twin and the persistence check failed honestly. Neither false-passed. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(cli): anonymous usage telemetry, off with e2e telemetry disable
body:
## What and why

- The CLI sends anonymous usage telemetry to PostHog, on by default. Which commands, engines, cache paths, and models get used, and where runs fail, is what the roadmap needs and what filed issues do not tell us.
- Two events per invocation, sent in one request when the command ends, capped at two seconds: `e2e_cli_session` (command, flag names, versions, machine class, CI vendor, coding agent) and `e2e_run_completed` (the report's numbers: status, test and step counts, cache replay counts, engines, model provider and id, tokens, error codes). Builders in `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/events.ts`.
- Every property is a count, a version, or a closed vocabulary. A project's own engine name, platform, fine-tuned model id, or error code folds into `other`. The unit test feeds a report full of recognizable strings and asserts none reach the payload (`packages/e2e/tests/helpers/sample-report.ts`).
- Off means off: `e2e telemetry disable`, `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or a preferences directory that cannot be written. `E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1` prints each event to stderr instead of sending it. CI runs are attributed to `ci:<vendor>` with no file written and no notice printed.
- Telemetry is a CLI concern. The class is constructed in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts` (a commander `preAction` hook records the session event, `main` flushes in `finally`); hosts embedding `@e2edev/e2e/run` send nothing.
- Identity: a random per-machine id in `~/.config/e2e/telemetry.json`, a random session id, and the SHA-256 of the repository's root commit as the project id (a salted path hash outside git, none in CI without git). `$process_person_profile` is false, so PostHog keeps no person profiles.
- SECURITY.md replaces "sends nothing home" with the endpoint and what is never sent. README, the CI guide, the CLI and config references, the skill, and a new docs page say the same.
- `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/posthog.ts` carries the project's public ingestion key, the kind posthog-js embeds in web pages: it can add events and nothing else. The project lives in PostHog Cloud EU; a flags probe against both regions confirmed it, and the first batch sent through the built class came back `200 {"status":"Ok"}`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[command] --> B{opted out?}
  B -- env, saved choice, or no store --> Z[nothing queued]
  B -- no --> C[notice, once per machine]
  C --> D[queue e2e_cli_session]
  D --> E[command runs]
  E --> F[queue e2e_run_completed from the report]
  F --> G[flush: one request, 2 s cap]
  G --> H{E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG}
  H -- set --> I[print to stderr, send nothing]
  H -- unset --> J[PostHog batch endpoint]
```

The first command on a machine, with the payload it would send:

```text
$ E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1 e2e list --tag smoke
e2e collects anonymous usage telemetry to improve the framework: the command, the versions, the OS, and run counts. Never test names, app data, or credentials.
Opt out with e2e telemetry disable or E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. What is sent: https://e2e-docs.vercel.app/telemetry

[telemetry] {"event":"e2e_cli_session","timestamp":"2026-09-08T17:51:42.928Z","properties":{"os":"darwin","os_release":"25.6.0","arch":"arm64","cpu_count":10,"memory_gb":16,"docker":false,"wsl":false,"tty":false,"ci":false,"ci_name":null,"coding_agent":"other","node_version":"26.4.0","package_manager":"npm","e2e_version":"0.6.1","command":"list","flags":["--tag"],"distinct_id":"…","project_id":"…","session_id":"…","$lib":"e2e","$lib_version":"0.6.1","$process_person_profile":false}}
```

The switch:

```text
$ e2e telemetry disable
telemetry disabled; saved to ~/.config/e2e/telemetry.json
Status: disabled (switched off with e2e telemetry disable)
Nothing is sent from this machine.
Details: https://e2e-docs.vercel.app/telemetry
```

The run event for the sample report, whose titles, paths, origins, engine name, and messages all stay home:

```text
status: failed  exit_code: 1  duration_ms: 5000  flags: [--headed, --workers]
tests_discovered: 3  tests_selected: 2  tests_executed: 2  tests_passed: 1  tests_failed: 1  tests_flaky: 0  tests_skipped: 1
targets: 2  platforms: [other, web]  engines: [other, playwright@0.6.1]
steps_total: 5  steps_agent: 2  steps_locator: 1  steps_assertion: 1  steps_screen: 1
agent_steps_replayed: 1  agent_steps_partial: 0  agent_steps_missed: 1  agent_steps_vision: 1
model_provider: anthropic  model_id: claude-sonnet-4-5  model_calls: 4  model_tokens: 2850  estimated_cost_usd: 0.01
errors: 1  error_codes: [APP_UNREACHABLE, LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND, OTHER]
```

title: docs(quickstart): three commands to green with no key, typechecked snippets
body:
## What and why

Closes [ENG-715](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-715/rewrite-the-quickstart-around-the-five-minute-path).

- The quickstart now opens with the path the scaffold already supports: dev server up, `init`, `install`, the printed run command. The scaffold's `app opens` test goes green with no model key, since the runner only preflights the model when a test acquires `agent`. Rehearsed on a fresh directory with the local build: green in one run, then `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` (exit 2) once the agent test is uncommented without a key, then a real model call with `E2E_MODEL` + `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY`.
- Then, in order: add an agent step (one model, `E2E_MODEL` / `E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT` / `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY`), let the runner start the app (`command`, `reuseExisting`, `log`, pointing at the config reference for the rest instead of repeating the services block), a minimal CI job, and the ESM notes kept until ENG-727 has a home for them.

```mdx
<Code code={config} lang="ts" title="e2e.config.ts" />
```

title: docs(reference): complete the reference and gate error codes with a check script
body:
## What and why

- `scripts/check-error-codes.ts`, run as `pnpm docs:check-errors` inside `pnpm check` and as a step in `spec.yml`. It reads the `AgentErrorCode` union, `ENGINE_ERROR_CODES`, and every literal handed to the `E2EError` family in `packages/e2e/src` and `packages/playwright/src` (constructor first arg, `super('X')`, `code: 'A' | 'B'` parameters), then fails when a code is missing from `reference/errors.mdx` (engine codes: `reference/engine.mdx`) or documented there but raised nowhere. Runner codes are plain strings, so the constructor scan is the closest thing to a union they have. Today: 66 codes, all documented.
- `config.mdx`: `specVersion` row; the `agent` block's three shapes (options, options with `executor`, or the executor itself) and an `executor` row; `E2E_MODEL_ENDPOINT` in the variables table and resolution order.

- `app-web.mdx`: a Playwright timeout in `web.evaluate` surfaces as `ACTION_FAILED`, not `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` (that is the engine code it is translated from).
- New `reference/environment.mdx` from an inventory of every `process.env`/`env[...]` read in both packages: model, credential, run mode, diagnostics, telemetry (including the CI vendor and coding-agent marker lists), engine, and what an app process inherits. `config.mdx` keeps only the variables that change resolution and links there.

title: fix(agent): model step events carry the turn's start as startedAt (ENG-739)
body:
## What and why

- `recordModelCall` stamped the `model` event when the executor reported the turn, which in a tool-using loop is after the turn's tools ran. `startedAt` was a finish time, and report.json readers saw the turn after the engine events it caused.
- `ExecutorModelCall` gains an optional `startedAt` (ISO instant the request went out). `trackModelCalls` fills it from `onStepStart`; `ActDispatch.recordModelCall` uses it and falls back to the report moment when an executor omits it.
- The list reporter no longer splices each turn ahead of the tool events since the previous one. `CurrentStep.turnStart` is gone; `events` is in stream order. In the live tree a turn now prints after its tool calls, as it arrives. Anyone who wants causal order sorts by `startedAt`.
- `StepEvent.startedAt` doc in `run/steps.ts` states the semantics. Schema unchanged: the field was already a timestamp, only its meaning for `model` events was off.

```ts
// packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts
context.budgets.recordModelCall({
  startedAt: new Date(turnStartedMs).toISOString(),
  durationMs: Date.now() - turnStartedMs,
  ...
});
```

Closes [ENG-739](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-739).

title: fix(agent): clamp act observations, retry and timeout parity, real turn count
body:
## What and why

- `act` observations were capped only by `agent.maxObservationBytes` (1 MiB); the judgment tier already clamped to the per-call token ceiling minus the request's fixed cost. The clamp moves into `src/agent/observation-budget.ts` and both tiers call it: `Invocation` with `systemBytes + ledger.bytes`, `ActDispatch` with `contextBytes + ledgerBytes`. A dense screen now truncates visibly on an act turn instead of tripping the adapter's pre-flight.
- Default `agent.maxObservationBytes` drops to 262 144. Range and override are unchanged.
- The tool loop passes `maxRetries: TRANSPORT_RETRIES` (5, the judgment adapter's value) and `timeout: budgets.remainingMs()` to `ToolLoopAgent.generate`, so a hung provider ends with the step's clock. An SDK abort/timeout maps to `STEP_TIMEOUT` (before, `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`); `isAbort` is exported from `model/sdk.ts` for that.
- `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION` reported `maxTurns`; it now reports the turns the model used (`turnsUsed` of `maxTurns`).

Testbed (`test:agent --ai-trace --no-cache`, gemini-3-flash), unbox-ai `runs` totals:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| model calls | 25 | 25 |
| input tokens | 45.8k | 45.6k |
| act: todo flow | 6 gens, 12.0k in | 6 gens, 11.9k in |
| act: form + judgment | 3 gens, 5.9k in | 3 gens, 5.9k in |
| act: wizard | 6 gens, 10.7k in | 6 gens, 10.9k in |
| act: sign-in | 4 gens, 7.3k in | 4 gens, 7.2k in |

Playground pages are small, so the clamp never binds there; the differences are model variance. The change matters on screens whose tree exceeds a quarter mebibyte.

Closes ENG-711.
