title: feat: target name defaults to platform, agentDevice options accept undefined
body: ## What and why - A target's `name` is optional and defaults to its `platform`. One target per platform is the common shape, and the name always repeated the platform. `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts` settles the name after the unknown-key and platform checks, so a `platfrom` typo still gets its did-you-mean hint. - Names stay unique. Two unnamed targets on one platform fail with a hint to name them, and errors raised before a name exists point at the entry as `targets[0]`. - Every optional `agentDevice()` option accepts `undefined`. Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` a plain optional field rejects an explicit `undefined`, which forced `...(device ? { device } : {})` around every `process.env` value. The runtime already checked `!== undefined` at each read, so `packages/agent-device/src/surface.ts` changes types only. - The init template, the skill, and its setup reference drop the redundant `name: 'web'`. The config reference documents the default; the device page and README say env values pass straight through. - Not in this PR: the app declaration in `@e2edev/e2e/engine` keeps plain optional fields, so `playwright({ url: process.env.APP_URL })` still needs a fallback. Same one-line fix per field if we want it. A device config, before and after: ```ts // before const device = process.env.E2E_DEVICE; const iosAppPath = process.env.E2E_IOS_APP_PATH; targets: [ { name: 'ios', platform: 'ios', engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', app: APP_ID, ...(device ? { device } : {}), ...(iosAppPath ? { appPath: iosAppPath } : {}), }), }, ], ``` ```ts // after targets: [ { platform: 'ios', engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', app: APP_ID, device: process.env.E2E_DEVICE, appPath: process.env.E2E_IOS_APP_PATH }), }, ], ``` The new `INVALID_CONFIG` messages: ```text invalid target name "bad name" (defaulted from the platform); target names are limited to ASCII letters, numbers, "_", "-", and "." duplicate target name "ios"; a target without a name is named after its platform, so name one of them targets[0] requires a non-empty platform targets[0] has unknown key "browser"; a target is { name?, platform, engine? }; did you mean "engine"? ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent)!: act takes one options bag and resolves with what the step did
body: ## What and why - `act(instruction, params?, options?)` forced `act('open billing', undefined, { timeout })` on anyone who wanted a budget without params; the type test had to write exactly that. `act` now takes one bag: `act(instruction, { params?, timeout?, maxSteps?, maxModelCalls? })`. - A passing `act` returned `{ ok: true }`, an object whose only field was always true. It now resolves with an `ActResult`: the executor's `summary`, the `modelCalls` and `actions` the step spent, and `cache`, how the trace cache took part, the same `StepCacheInfo` the report records. A test can assert that a step replayed with no model call, or log what the model concluded. - `ActOptions` and `ActResult` replace `AgentOptions` and `AgentResult`. `AgentParams` is unchanged and still the type of `params`. - Runtime behavior is unchanged: params validation, secret projection, budgets, and the trace cache read the same values from the new place (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts`, `runActStep`). `ActDispatch.result()` reads the settled summary, the step metrics, and the cache session's info after the verdict settles. ```ts // before await agent.act('open billing', undefined, { timeout: 60_000 }); await agent.act('invite {email}', { email: 'ada@example.test' }); const { ok } = await agent.act('upgrade to Pro'); // after await agent.act('open billing', { timeout: 60_000 }); await agent.act('invite {email}', { params: { email: 'ada@example.test' } }); const { summary, cache, modelCalls } = await agent.act('upgrade to Pro'); expect(cache?.mode).toBe('self-finalized'); // replayed, no model call ``` Decisions D2 and D5 from the API audit. First of the pre-1.0 shape changes; the skill, the reference page, the quickstart, writing-tests, and authentication pages use the new shape. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Pre-1.0 shape decision, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent)!: named judgment option types; durations drop the Ms suffix
body: ## What and why - `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract` each took an anonymous inline option object, so nothing could be named in a signature or reused, and the shapes drifted: `maxModelCalls` on two of three, `screenshot` on one. They now take `AssertOptions`, `WaitForOptions`, and `ExtractOptions`, all exported from `@e2edev/e2e`. - `extract`'s `maxModelCalls` is gone. Its budget is fixed at two calls, one extraction plus one repair round, so the option only ever accepted 1 or 2 and rejected everything else with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `waitFor` keeps `maxModelCalls` because it polls; `assert` never had one. - Durations drop the `Ms` suffix, matching `timeout`: `waitFor({ interval })` was `intervalMs`, `longPress({ duration })` was `durationMs`, now typed as `LongPressOptions`. Every duration is still milliseconds. The engine contract's `LocatorAction` keeps `durationMs`; that surface is the 1.0 engine-contract pass, not this PR. - Stacked on #219, which reshaped `act`; this PR is the judgment half of the same `Agent` interface. ```ts // before await agent.waitFor('the export finished', { intervalMs: 500 }); await agent.extract('the plan name', { schema, maxModelCalls: 2 }); await screen.getByText('Row').longPress({ durationMs: 800 }); // after await agent.waitFor('the export finished', { interval: 500 }); await agent.extract('the plan name', { schema }); await screen.getByText('Row').longPress({ duration: 800 }); ``` Decisions D3, D7, and B3 from the API audit. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Pre-1.0 shape decision, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ## Review follow-ups - The runtime now rejects an option a judgment call does not take (`intervalMs`, `durationMs`, extract's `maxModelCalls`) with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the rename, so a JavaScript suite cannot silently poll at the default. One helper in `internal/options.ts`, unit-tested, serves `assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`, and `longPress`. - The three integration call sites that still passed `intervalMs` take `interval` (the red test job), and the opening `Agent` interface on the reference page uses the named option types (cubic). - No deprecation shim, on purpose: pre-1.0 shape correction, same call as #192 and #195. Replied on the Devin thread. ---

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2edev/agent-device@0.8.0

### Minor Changes

- [#291](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/291) [`abf1958`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/abf19588677070fb86234f735614c40b7677e755) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: follows the reshaped engine contract. Observations carry one `root` node (role `screen`, id `root`) over the device's windows and a `location` of the form `<app> / <screen title>` instead of an `app://` URL. Nodes carry `testId` from the accessibility identifier or resource id; the harness's `testIdAttribute` is gone. The engine declares the action kinds a device honors, so the agent is no longer offered `select` on a device. `press` accepts `Enter`, `Space`, and single characters; anything else fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. A discovered device pool reaches the workers through the `prepare` result's `env` instead of a write to the run's environment.

- [#294](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/294) [`c2c5df7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c2c5df7df94b25a8284b69dd6bc00a459b770a59) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The runner is published as `e2e`. `@e2edev/e2e` is retired and deprecated on npm; every import, config, and peer range now names `e2e` (`e2e`, `e2e/agent`, `e2e/engine`). The engines and the GitHub reporter declare their peer dependency on `e2e`, so a project on `@e2edev/e2e` must switch the runner to `e2e` when it takes these versions. The CLI keeps its `e2e` bin name.

### Patch Changes

- [#297](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/297) [`6fbf3c7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6fbf3c77606bfada21327e21d8279370040cfdd0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `@e2edev/agent-device/tools` no longer imports `ai` at run time. `ai` is an optional peer dependency, and the tool pack loads with the project's config, so a project without `ai` failed at config load with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` instead of getting as far as its own steps. The tools are typed the same way; nothing changes for a project that has `ai`.

- [#290](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/290) [`799b29f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/799b29fbfa0444589b66bc0e59ab0b83ededf50c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Origin allowlists are gone, everywhere. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` gated typed navigation only; a click, a redirect, or a popup reached any origin regardless, so the list guarded nothing and had to be spelled out for every subdomain a sign-in flow touched. `allowedOrigins` on a credential or a secret gated where a password could be typed; a secret is only ever typed into a field the step was handed, a password only into a password field, so that gate guarded against a model mistake at the cost of configuring every flow that leaves the app's domain, a third-party sign-in included. `app.open()`, the agent's `navigate`, and `web.goto` open any http(s) URL, `file:`, `data:`, and `javascript:` stay `POLICY_DENIED`, and a secret fills wherever the test or the step directs it. `credentials` entries are `{ username, password }`; `secrets` entries are a string or a provider, the `{ value }` object form is gone. `type_secret` now works on a device target too. What still keys on the site of `url` (its registrable domain) is invisible to config: the browser engine's `headers` reach the site and no other host, and child frames off the site stay out of observations. `basicAuth` answers a challenge from any origin, as Playwright's own `httpCredentials` does. Engine contract: `EngineAppInfo.allowedOrigins` became `site?: string`, `EngineAppDeclaration` lost `allowedOrigins`, and `sameSite`/`siteOf` are exported from `e2e/engine`. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` fails at config load. If a threat model ever calls for an allowlist again, it comes back as an opt-in.
## e2e@0.15.0

### Minor Changes

- [#291](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/291) [`abf1958`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/abf19588677070fb86234f735614c40b7677e755) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: the engine contract (`e2e/engine`) is reshaped as the locked, UI-only, cross-platform SPI for 1.0. What breaks and what replaces it:
  
  - `EngineSnapshot.nodes` is `root`, one engine-minted node with an id that stays stable across observations; `url` is `location`, an opaque address (a URL on the web, the foreground screen on a device) the harness treats as a URL only when it parses as one; `viewport` is required.
  - `Engine.url()` is gone; read `location` off an observation. `Engine.swipe` is gone; the viewport swipe is `perform(root, { kind: 'swipe' })`.
  - `Engine.actions` lists the action kinds `perform` honors and is required with it. The agent's tools and the `screen` methods derive from it, so a surface is never offered a verb it cannot do.
  - `Engine.app` is data only. The hooks move to `Engine.session: { open, back, restart, reset }` (were `app.navigate`, `back`, `restart`, `clearState`). `restart` and `reset` open nothing on an addressable surface; the harness reopens the app through `open`.
  - `EngineInitInfo.testIdAttribute` and `EngineInitInfo.app.baseUrl` are gone. `SemanticNode.testId` carries the node's test id and the `testId` query resolves against it. The root config key `screen.testIdAttribute` is rejected; set `playwright({ testIdAttribute })` instead.
  - `press` keys follow one grammar in Playwright spelling (`Control+a`, `Shift+Tab`, `Enter`, one printable character); `parseKey`, `KEY_NAMES`, `KEY_MODIFIERS`, and `LOCATOR_ACTION_KINDS` are exported for engines. An invalid key fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before it reaches an engine.
  - `OperationContext.origin` is required. `EnginePrepareInfo.env` is a plain readonly record, and `EnginePrepareResult.env` is the typed channel from a runner-side `prepare` to each worker's `init`, which reads it as `EngineInitInfo.env` (the run's environment plus that target's additions; other targets never see them).
  - Report: the target record no longer carries `testIdAttribute`; artifact kinds and usage counters are unchanged.
  
  `spiVersion` stays `1`.

- [#288](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/288) [`aa3b05b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/aa3b05bbbdd4534ef111e51b950002513998076f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Judgments are independent of the act loop. `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`,
  and `agent.extract` are shown the instruction and the current screen only:
  the prior-step ledger and the acting agent's summaries no longer reach a
  judgment call, so a verdict rests on what is on screen rather than on the
  actor's account of what it did. A new `judge` slot, `agents.<name>.judge` or
  `createAgent({ judge })`, names a separate model for the judgment tier;
  unset, judgments use `model`, and a config `judge` that differs from the
  executor's is `INVALID_CONFIG`. Each judgment step's `model` in the report
  names the model that produced the verdict. `createAgent(...)` counts as the
  built-in agent here, not a custom executor: its `agent.assert` calls now go
  to the judgment tier (one judgment call, `vision` and `screenshot` allowed)
  instead of through its own `runStep`, so the judge judges them. A hand-rolled
  executor still judges its own assertions through `runStep`.
  
  The judgment protocol is `agent-judgment-2`: the model answers `holds`,
  `fails`, or `inconclusive` instead of a boolean. An inconclusive
  `agent.assert`, one where the screen did not show enough to decide either
  way, fails with the new `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` code (category test, exit 1)
  and the model's account of what was missing; it is never a pass. In
  `agent.waitFor` an inconclusive round keeps polling until the deadline. The
  `agent-judgment-1` schema and its fixtures stay in the package, marked
  deprecated, for the stability window; the runner requests `agent-judgment-2`
  only.
  
  The report records the checkout under `run.vcs`: `commit`, `branch` when
  HEAD is on one, and `dirty` when git could say. Outside git the GitHub
  Actions variables stand in; with neither, the field is absent. It is what
  joins a run's verdicts to the pull request that produced the code.

- [#292](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/292) [`d486e40`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d486e40e73bfe23ac70a99f7938f05db0ba4e30c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A finished model turn in the live window now appends an excerpt of the
  model's reasoning when the model produced one: `• Thinking (2.84s) (↑7.5k
  ↓18) · The modal blocks checkout; closing it first`. Runs and explorations
  alike show why the agent acted, not just that it did. The excerpt collapses
  to one line and clips to the terminal; the full reasoning stays in the AI
  trace (`--ai-trace`). The same bounded excerpt lands on the report's `model`
  step events as `reasoning` (report-1 schema), and custom executors report
  their own through `recordModelCall({ reasoning })`.

- [#290](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/290) [`799b29f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/799b29fbfa0444589b66bc0e59ab0b83ededf50c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Origin allowlists are gone, everywhere. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` gated typed navigation only; a click, a redirect, or a popup reached any origin regardless, so the list guarded nothing and had to be spelled out for every subdomain a sign-in flow touched. `allowedOrigins` on a credential or a secret gated where a password could be typed; a secret is only ever typed into a field the step was handed, a password only into a password field, so that gate guarded against a model mistake at the cost of configuring every flow that leaves the app's domain, a third-party sign-in included. `app.open()`, the agent's `navigate`, and `web.goto` open any http(s) URL, `file:`, `data:`, and `javascript:` stay `POLICY_DENIED`, and a secret fills wherever the test or the step directs it. `credentials` entries are `{ username, password }`; `secrets` entries are a string or a provider, the `{ value }` object form is gone. `type_secret` now works on a device target too. What still keys on the site of `url` (its registrable domain) is invisible to config: the browser engine's `headers` reach the site and no other host, and child frames off the site stay out of observations. `basicAuth` answers a challenge from any origin, as Playwright's own `httpCredentials` does. Engine contract: `EngineAppInfo.allowedOrigins` became `site?: string`, `EngineAppDeclaration` lost `allowedOrigins`, and `sameSite`/`siteOf` are exported from `e2e/engine`. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` fails at config load. If a threat model ever calls for an allowlist again, it comes back as an opt-in.

- [#294](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/294) [`c2c5df7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c2c5df7df94b25a8284b69dd6bc00a459b770a59) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The runner is published as `e2e`. `@e2edev/e2e` is retired and deprecated on npm; every import, config, and peer range now names `e2e` (`e2e`, `e2e/agent`, `e2e/engine`). The engines and the GitHub reporter declare their peer dependency on `e2e`, so a project on `@e2edev/e2e` must switch the runner to `e2e` when it takes these versions. The CLI keeps its `e2e` bin name.

### Patch Changes

- [#296](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/296) [`f2f2e6f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f2f2e6fb1024ffb4cd481f7ea571c2d29be6d6d8) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The CLI starts without the optional `ai` peer dependency. The MCP bridge imported `asSchema` from `ai` statically and every command loads that module, so `npx e2e --help`, and `e2e init` in a project that has not installed `ai` yet, crashed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before reading a flag. The bridge now reaches the SDK through the same lazy loader as the agent, and an MCP session opened in a project without `ai` reports `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` instead.

title: feat(app)!: drop deepLink; open takes the absolute URLs it took
body: ## What and why - `app.deepLink(url)` and `app.open(url)` were the same call (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`, both mapped to `navigate`): same base-URL resolution, same origin policy, a different step label. The name promised a deep or universal link, but a custom-scheme URL has no HTTP origin and fails the `allowedOrigins` check, so it could not open one. - `deepLink` is removed. `app.open()` already takes an absolute URL within the allowed origins, which is everything `deepLink` could do; the two testbed suites and the origin-policy integration test now call `open`. - If a device engine ever opens app links, that is a new hook on the engine's `app` manifest with its own policy, not a rename of `open`. ```ts // before await app.deepLink('https://playwright.dev'); // after await app.open('https://playwright.dev'); ``` Decision C1 from the API audit. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Pre-1.0 shape decision, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. A removed method needs no type assertion. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(screen)!: visible is the one visibility option; drop RoleOptions.hidden
body: ## What and why - `getByRole` had two visibility knobs pointing in opposite directions: `hidden` (widen a role query to nodes hidden from the accessibility tree) and the inherited `visible` (narrow any query to nodes on screen). `getByRole('button', { hidden: false, visible: true })` needed the reference page to read. `hidden` is gone; `visible` is the one knob. - What a role query matches is now one sentence on every engine: never a node hidden from the accessibility tree. That was already Playwright's default (`includeHidden` is false) and the device engine's default; the removed option was the only way to widen it, and nothing in the repo used it. - The engine contract's `SemanticQuery.states` loses its `hidden` key (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`), so an engine cannot be asked for a state core no longer sends. Both first-party engines drop their handling of it; the device engine's unit test that pinned the widening is updated. ```ts // before: two knobs, opposite directions screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save', hidden: true }); // widen screen.getByText('Saved', { visible: true }); // narrow // after: one knob, one direction screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }); // never a hidden node screen.getByText('Saved', { visible: true }); // drop the hidden twin ``` Decision B2 from the API audit. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Pre-1.0 shape decision, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: refactor(agent)!: drop the E2E_DEBUG trace stream
body: ## What and why - `E2E_DEBUG=agent|observations|all` switched on a live stderr stream of agent phases, model selections, locate outcomes, and every observation the model saw (`packages/e2e/src/internal/trace.ts`). It was documented for one day, overlapped `--debug` and `--ai-trace`, and made the environment-variable set three ways to look at one run. - The variable and the module are removed, with the six call sites in `agent/invocation.ts` and `agent/phases.ts` and the two helpers only they used. `--debug` keeps the phase timings, the per-step transcripts, and the agent step table; `--ai-trace` keeps every model call for a trace viewer. - The config reference's environment table is back to the set the runner reads. Decision F2 from the API audit: remove the env stream rather than rename the flag. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Pre-1.0 decision on an `E2E_*` variable, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(screen): selectOption by value attribute
body: ## What and why - `selectOption` took a label (a bare string or `{ label }`) or `{ index }`, never the option's `value` attribute, which is what the form submits and what a test usually knows from the data model. `{ value: 'pro' }` now works beside the other two. - `SelectOption` keeps its mutual exclusivity: one of `label`, `value`, or `index`, and the type test pins that two together fail to compile. - The Playwright engine maps `{ value }` to Playwright's own `selectOption({ value })`; the device engine's `selectOption` stays `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` for every variant, so nothing changes there. - Stacked on #221 because both touch the `screen` types and reference page. ```ts await screen.getByLabel('Plan').selectOption('Pro'); // by label await screen.getByLabel('Plan').selectOption({ value: 'pro' }); // by value attribute await screen.getByLabel('Plan').selectOption({ index: 2 }); // by position ``` Decision B5 from the API audit. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(config)!: a target inherits its platform from the engine
body: ## What and why - `platform` was declared twice for a device target (`{ platform: 'ios', engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios' }) }`) and redundantly for every web target, and nothing checked that the two agreed: tool packs are offered by the engine's platform while `platforms: [...]` filters by the target's, so `{ platform: 'iphone-17', engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios' }) }` was valid config that silently dropped every device tool. - An engine now declares the platform it drives (`Engine.platform`, optional on the contract; `web` for playwright, the `platform` option for agent-device), and a target inherits it. With #218's name defaulting, `{ engine: playwright({ url }) }` is a complete target. A target without an engine still names its platform. A target that names one while its engine declares another is `INVALID_CONFIG` with both values in the message. - The scaffold, the docs, the skill, the READMEs, and the testbed configs drop the redundant label; the engine-less examples keep theirs. ```ts // before targets: [ { name: 'web', platform: 'web', engine: playwright({ url }) }, { name: 'phone', platform: 'ios', engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', app: 'Settings' }) }, ], // after targets: [ { engine: playwright({ url }) }, // named "web" { engine: agentDevice({ platform: 'ios', app: 'Settings' }) }, // named "ios" ], ``` Refs: `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts` (`resolvePlatform`), `packages/e2e/src/engine/index.ts` (`Engine.platform`, `defineEngine`), `packages/playwright/src/engine.ts`, `packages/agent-device/src/engine.ts`. Decision E2 from the API audit. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). A target whose label disagrees with its engine now fails; pre-1.0 decision, shipped without a window like #192. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `fern/docs/pages/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ## Review follow-ups - The config digest's engine identity carries `platform` (Devin, cubic): a named target inherits it, so two workers whose engines declared different platforms must not agree on the digest. Unit test added. - Both engines peer on `@e2edev/e2e >=0.8.0 <1` (Devin, cubic): an older runner rejects `platform` as an unknown key, and could still send `states.hidden` (#223 shipped without moving the floor, so this PR carries that reason too). Assumes these land in the same release as #221 (0.8.0); if 0.8.0 ships first, the floor moves to 0.9.0. - The engine header no longer claims "no platform noun appears here", and the targets docs name an engine that declares no platform as the other case needing `platform` on the target (cubic). - The target/engine platform mismatch stays an error, no shim: it was never a working form (tool packs followed the engine, test filters the target). Replied on both threads. ---

title: fix(agent-device): resolve text queries to the innermost match
body: ## Why On an iOS simulator every \`screen.getByText(x)\` against a React Native app fails with \`LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS\`. RN Fabric's \`RCTViewComponentView.accessibilityLabel\` returns the recursively joined labels of its children when a view has none of its own, so XCTest reports a \`Text\` as an \`Other\` host view and a \`StaticText\` child carrying the same string (often nested twice). \`matchesQuery\` matched both. Found while migrating react-native-pager-view's Maestro suite to e2e; the suite needed a \`getByText(x).last()\` helper for every text assertion. ## What - \`resolveExpression\` drops \`text\` matches that contain another match, the innermost rule a browser text selector already applies. Label, role, test id, and \`filter({ hasText })\` are unchanged. - Unit test on the existing \`SETTINGS_NODES\` fixture, which already models the echo (cell "About" over static text "About"). - Docs: \`reference/screen.mdx\` (new "Echoed text" section), \`reference/device.mdx\` locate row, skill \`writing-tests.md\`. - Changeset: patch for \`@e2edev/agent-device\`. ## Verification - \`pnpm --filter @e2edev/agent-device run test:unit\`: 70 passed. - \`pnpm lint\`, package \`typecheck\`: clean. \`check:dead-code\` reports two pre-existing members in \`@e2edev/e2e\`. - Built dist run against the pager-view example app on an iPhone 17 simulator with plain \`getByText\` (see comment below once done). ---

title: feat(web-benchmark): add hard-to-automate scenarios and e2e suites
body:
## What and why - `packages/web-benchmark` (`@e2edev/web-benchmark`, private) hosts the 41 scenarios from tester-army's `apps/web-benchmark`, each at `/e/`. They are local, deterministic pages that are hard to automate (shadow roots, a canvas-only UI, iframes, native dialogs, a second tab, a DOM that remounts every second, an accessibility tree that lies), and this is where we write e2e tests against them. The testbed's `tests-selenium` suite covers the same kind of pages on a third-party site that cannot gate a PR. - Eight scenarios plant one product bug each, and two more are traps with bug-looking artifacts and no bug. A test asserting the correct behavior has to fail on the eight and pass on the two, which is the check that assertions and `agent.assert` judgments catch real bugs without inventing them. `PLANTED BUG (do not fix)` marks each one in source. - Two suites, both gating every PR in `spec.yml`. `tests/` is deterministic. `tests-agent/` (one `agent.act` sign-in with the password as a Secret) spends real model calls through the repository's `E2E_MODEL_API_KEY`. - The Next app lives under `app/` with its own tsconfig, like `packages/testbed/bench`, so the package `tsconfig.json` stays the strict one and `next build` does not typecheck the suites a second time under looser settings. `next-env.d.ts` is ignored because Next rewrites it on every dev and build. - Scenario files are copies and still port both ways. Beyond four lint-driven lines (`sort`/`reverse` on fresh copies became `toSorted`/`toReversed`), five scenarios changed where the bot reviews found a way to pass without doing the hard part: the overlay trap accepted a Continue click that landed before the overlay existed, the deferred dialog queued one confirm per click, a shared `?q=` link ignored its own filter, the rich text check accepted bold that spilled into the previous word, and the shadow form rendered its error twice. Each fix has a deterministic test in `tests/`. - The agentic suite is pinned to `openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast` (`E2E_MODEL` overrides it). The sign-in seed passes in 8 s for 4 model calls and $0.0029; the same step on `google/gemini-3-flash` took 76 s through the gateway at the same cost. Layout: ``` packages/web-benchmark/ app/ Next 16 project: src/app shell, src/Examples/*.tsx, src/examples.ts registry e2e.config.ts port 4280, `pnpm run start`, reuseExisting, the `benchmark` credential e2e.agent.config.ts { ...base, tests: 'tests-agent/**', timeout, agent: { model } } tests/ deterministic, gates PRs (smoke, login form, overlay trap, deferred dialog, deep link, rich text) tests-agent/ agentic, gates PRs too ``` The authoring loop the package exists for: ```bash pnpm --filter @e2edev/web-benchmark dev # scenarios on :4280 cd packages/web-benchmark pnpm exec e2e run tests/login-form.e2e.ts --headed # reuses the dev server ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR T[pnpm test] --> B[next build app] B --> R[e2e run] R --> Q{port 4280 answering
and not CI?} Q -- yes --> U[reuse the running server] Q -- no --> S[spawn pnpm run start] ``` Open questions I did not decide here: - A code review suggested folding this into the testbed as a fourth app (`packages/testbed/web-benchmark/`) instead of a separate package: same next/react pins, same suite conventions, one fewer manifest. Kept separate as asked. A move later is mechanical. - The lint edits and the five scenario fixes should go upstream to tester-army so the copies match again. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat(agent): read action results after their effect and send screen changes
body: ## What and why Traces of the tester.army tour (`--ai-trace`, claude-haiku-4.5) showed the act loop paying for four things on every step: - A tap on a nav link returned the page it left. The observation settled on the old, stable screen before the route change committed, and the model repaired with a `navigate` it did not need: 2 of 6 steps, one extra action and two extra turns each. - Every action result was the whole tree again, 26 KB on that site, and the conversation carried two of them per turn. 331k input tokens for 8 actions. - The rules forbade batching because each mutation re-observed and invalidated the ids the model held, so a three-field form cost four turns plus the verdict. - A `complete_step` summary over 500 characters was rejected by the tool schema and re-asked. 2 of 6 steps paid a repair turn. This PR changes what an action result is and when it is read. - After tap, type, press, select, or navigate, the settled observation waits up to 2 s for the screen shape to leave the one the action was resolved against, treats an empty document as a screen in transition, then settles on stability as before (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts`). Scroll and secret fills leave no visible trace and do not arm the wait. Replay and the cache probes take the same path. - The opening prompt carries the screen once. Every later result lists the lines that were `added`, `changed` (with what they read before), or `removed`, keyed by the ids the engine already stamps on elements, ignoring focus (`packages/e2e/src/agent/screen-update.ts`). A screen that mostly changed goes out whole. Only the newest full screen stays verbatim; the one it replaced is elided, so the conversation prefix stays stable for prompt caching. A node that only moved to another depth is not reported, and a screen cut at the observation byte limit reports no removals. - Grammar tools run in call order with the loop guard inside the queue. Batched actions each report their own changes, and a hard stop skips what queued behind it. A failed action returns the failure together with the current screen. - Targeted actions are bounded by the smaller of `actionTimeout` and 15 s. A tap under a consent banner reports the element in the way within seconds instead of sitting in Playwright's actionability retry for the whole budget. - `complete_step` accepts 2000 characters and asks for a short handoff for the next step. - Engine errors are recognized structurally in the observation retry loop and in step events. An engine imported by a config file lives in its own module registry, so `instanceof EngineError` missed a retryable stale-node race during a cross-origin redirect and failed the action, and events recorded `EngineError` instead of the code. - The ledger hands later steps a replayed step's recorded verdict without the replay notice. - A targeted action whose node the engine reports stale is re-found by its trace descriptor in a fresh capture and retried, up to twice (`relocateStale` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts`). A list that remounts its rows between the observation and the action no longer costs a turn per attempt. - The `scroll` tool takes `times` (1 to 5, each one recorded action), moves three quarters of the box per swipe instead of the engine's half, and the observation after a scroll waits 500 ms for a windowed or lazy list to render. - Testbed pins move from `google/gemini-3-flash` (haiku on the tour) to `openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast`. `E2E_MODEL` still overrides every one of them. - The rules tell the model that a mostly changed screen arrives whole, headed `Current screen`, and replaces what it had; they no longer claim every result reports only what changed. Live before and after on the web-benchmark suite: 20/20 both, 81 against 86 calls, the difference inside one high-variance scenario. - Several actions issued in one turn keep addressing the screen the turn saw: an id the newest observation lacks is re-found by its descriptor in a recent observation, so batching works on an engine that mints ids per observation (agent-device) and across a remount. A mutating project tool arms the brief change wait; a secret fill's origin authorization runs under the 15 s bound; pressing a focus-only key (Tab, arrows, Home, End, Page keys) expects no visible change. - Three failed tool results in a row earn the model a notice to change approach; five force `complete_step`, the way five identical calls already did. Clock-like text (`12:05`, `0:59:59`) is ignored when comparing screen shapes, so a ticking timer neither ends the change wait nor blocks the settle. - `packages/web-benchmark/tests-agent/` gains a scenario table, one `agent.act` per tree-visible task scenario checked on its success message, with the scenarios the grammar cannot finish skipped with the reason, and three bug-book tests where the agent must report the planted bug. The benchmark config raises `agent.maxSteps` to 60 for the scroll-heavy scenario. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph main A1[tap] --> O1[observe at once] --> R1[whole tree, often still the old page] --> M1[model turn] end subgraph this PR A2[tap] --> W[wait for the shape to move, up to 2 s] --> S[settle] --> R2[added / changed / removed lines] --> M2[model turn] end ``` An action result on main, after tapping a header link on tester.army: ``` Tapped #n16. Updated screen (revision b4): #n2 document "TesterArmy: Test your app with AI, catch bugs before users do" #n3 navigation ... 480 more lines of the page the tap left ``` The same kind of result on this PR, after deleting an expense in the bench app: ``` Tapped #n19. Screen changes since revision b27 (now revision b30, path /expenses, 29 nodes): 5 removed. Every node not listed as removed is still on screen under the id you have. removed #n15 listitem "Conference flights — $320.00 (Travel)ApprovedUnapprove Conference flightsDelete Conference flights" removed #n16 text="Conference flights — $320.00 (Travel)" removed #n17 text="Approved" removed #n18 button "Unapprove Conference flights" removed #n19 button "Delete Conference flights" ``` Same suites, same flags (`--no-cache --ai-trace --debug`), same model in both columns: | Suite, model | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | tester.army tour, claude-haiku-4.5 | 23 calls, 8 actions, 329k in, $0.34 | 13 calls, 6 actions, 166k in, $0.17 | | tests-agent, gemini-3-flash | 25 calls, 43k in | 18 calls, 33k in | | tests-bench, gemini-3-flash | 26 calls, 38k in | 18 calls, 30k in | | tests-dogfood, gemini-3-flash | 29 calls, 52k in | 20 calls, 41k in | Every act step of the tour is now two calls, the action and the verdict. Gemini wall time moves on its own between runs and is left out. With the new default model the suites run in 29 s (agent, $0.011), 26 s (bench, $0.012), 54 s (dogfood, $0.010), and 82 s (tour, $0.046, including a consent banner the model had to dismiss). The new web-benchmark agentic suite, same app and model (luna-fast), main's act loop against this branch: | | main | this PR | this PR after the review round | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | passing | 19 / 23 | 20 / 20 active (3 skipped with reasons) | 20 / 20 active | | model calls | 197 | 86 | 86 | | tokens | 519k | 207k | 177k | | cost | $0.27 | $0.05 | $0.04 | | wall | 430 s | 202 s | 194 s | Stale DOM went from blocked after 20 calls to passing in 4; infinite scroll from failing at the turn budget to passing in 8 calls. The review round (Devin and cubic findings, see the comment below) kept the call count and cut tokens by keeping one full screen instead of two and comparing diff lines without indentation. The three skips need verbs the grammar lacks: a closed shadow root is invisible to the tree walk, a windowed table 4322 rows deep needs a scroll-to, and bolding one word in a contenteditable needs text selection. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat: device pools split a target's files across workers
body: ## Why A device target could only run with `workers: 1`: more workers shared one simulator and interleaved taps. Splitting a suite across simulators meant several `e2e run` processes with hand-picked file lists, colliding on the agent-device session and on `.e2e/report.json`. Maestro has `--shard-split`; e2e had nothing. ## What - **Core:** the scheduler hands each worker the lowest free slot among its target's workers (`TargetState.slots`, released when the worker's exit is observed, so a replacement takes over the slot of the worker it replaces). The slot travels through `SpawnUnitRunner`, `WorkerBootstrap`, `TargetExecutorOptions`, and lands in `EngineInitInfo.workerSlot`. Playwright ignores it. - **agent-device:** `device` accepts `readonly string[]`. `init` picks `device[workerSlot]`, boots it, and uses it for every open and install; the session becomes `e2e--` so pooled workers never share a session. A slot beyond the pool fails init with `ENGINE_FAILURE` and a message naming the fix, instead of silently sharing a device. - Docs: `reference/device.mdx` (option row, pool example replacing the "workers: 1" paragraph), `reference/engine.mdx` (`EngineInitInfo`), skill `setup.md`. Two changesets (minor each). - Tests: scheduler slot allocation and reuse; agent-device pool selection, session suffix, and the out-of-range error. Existing `EngineInitInfo` literals gained `workerSlot: 0`. ## Verification - `pnpm lint`, package `typecheck` (docs workspace typecheck needs its deps installed locally; CI covers it), `check:dead-code` (two pre-existing members). - Unit: e2e 893, playwright 145, agent-device 72, all passing. - On device: react-native-pager-view's 13-test suite with `device: ['iPhone 17', 'iPhone 17 Pro']`, `workers: 2`. 375 s on one simulator, 191 s on two, identical results. One worker was replaced mid-run (a failing unit) and the replacement reused slot 0 (`engine.init` count 3). ---

title: feat(artifacts): record every attempt as video with --video
body:
## What and why

- `artifacts: ['video']`, or `e2e run --video` for one run, records every attempt. Off by default, since it costs an encoder per page and about a megabit per second of disk.
- Video is never in the default set, so asking for it is a contract. An engine that cannot record fails before collection with `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT`; a recording that cannot be finalized is a cleanup failure in the report.
- Each artifact kind now resolves to a policy, `best-effort` for the default set and `required` for anything named in the config or added by the flag. The map replaces `artifactsExplicit` and the per-kind branches in `validateEngine`, `launchSession`, and `closeSession`; the executor starts and stops both recordings through one helper each (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`).
- The report records each segment as an artifact of kind `video` with `startedAt`, when the recording started, so `step.startedAt - artifact.startedAt` is a step's offset into the recording. `StoredArtifact` carries the same field for a host store.
- The Playwright engine screencasts the page at the attempt's viewport size. Recorder state lives in `packages/playwright/src/video.ts`; the surface calls it from its lifecycle hooks. A segment whose stop failed and left no file is reported at `stopVideo`, so a required recording never disappears with `cleanup: complete`.
- A screencast belongs to one page, so an attempt that opens a new one mid-way (`app.restart()`, a state reset) continues in `video/video-part<n>.webm`. The segment ends before its page closes, since Playwright writes nothing for a screencast whose page went away first. The video starts before the trace because a page's first screencast client sizes it and the trace's is capped at 800 pixels; for the same reason a restart under recording closes the trace as a segment and resumes it once the recording owns the new page. The lifecycle test decodes each segment's last frame in the browser and rejects grey padding.
- The agent-device engine records the device screen into `video/video.mp4` through agent-device's recorder, taps shown. It marks the recording before the start command goes out and clears the mark only after a successful stop, so a start that outlives its budget or a stop that fails is still stopped at `endAttempt`.
- `artifacts.video.retain: 'on-failure'` deletes the recording of every attempt that passed. The decision is made as the session closes, before the artifact is registered, so a configured store never receives a recording that is about to be deleted. Both executors settle the attempt's verdict before closing its session; an interrupt that lands during cleanup therefore no longer relabels an attempt that had already failed as `interrupted`.
- Video never enters the config digest, so turning it on cannot invalidate cached agent traces.
- A recording masks nothing, so it is recorded with `redaction: 'incomplete'`. report-1 keeps its conditional. An `incomplete` artifact may still omit `path`, `size`, and `sha256`, which a withheld artifact does, and may now carry them, which a kept recording does.
- The list reporter names the recording under each failed test, which needed `artifactsRoot` on `run-started`.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
export default {
  artifacts: {
    kinds: ['screenshot', 'trace', 'video'],
    video: { retain: 'on-failure' },
  },
};
```

```ts
// @e2edev/e2e/engine
export interface EngineArtifacts {
  screenshot(label: string | undefined, context: OperationContext): Promise<string>;
  startTrace?(context: OperationContext): Promise<void>;
  stopTrace?(context: OperationContext): Promise<string>;
  startVideo?(context: OperationContext): Promise<void>;
  stopVideo?(context: OperationContext): Promise<readonly VideoSegment[]>;
}

export interface VideoSegment {
  /** Relative to the attempt artifact directory. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** ISO instant the segment started recording. */
  readonly startedAt: string;
}
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as runner
  participant E as engine
  R->>E: startAttempt
  R->>E: restoreState (session tests)
  R->>E: startVideo
  Note over E: opens the page, so the recording sizes its screencast
  R->>E: startTrace
  R->>E: perform / observe / screenshot
  Note over R: verdict settled
  R->>E: stopVideo
  E-->>R: segments with startedAt
  alt retain on-failure and the attempt passed
    R->>R: delete the segments
  else
    R->>R: register video artifacts
  end
  R->>E: stopTrace
  R->>E: endAttempt
```

```json

  "id": "018f…:artifact:0",
  "kind": "video",
  "mediaType": "video/webm",
  "path": "chromium/tests_checkout.e2e.ts__pays/attempt-0/video/video.webm",
  "size": 1834112,
  "sha256": "…",
  "startedAt": "2026-09-09T10:00:00.000Z",
  "redaction": "incomplete",
  "producer": { "kind": "attempt" }
}
```

The failure recap gains one line per recording a failed attempt kept:

```
Error: nope

```

title: fix(playwright): names drop aria-hidden text, and an exact label query matches by that name
body: ## What and why - A field whose label ends in an `aria-hidden` required marker (``) was named `Display name*`. Every screen reader says "Display name", and the accessible name computation drops aria-hidden nodes, so `getByLabel('Display name')` and `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Display name' })` missed a field a person finds at once. Hit on TesterArmy's onboarding form, whose three required fields all carry the marker. - Names now come from `nameTextOf` (`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts`): a walk that skips aria-hidden subtrees and, like `innerText`, CSS-hidden ones, and that treats a control's own content as its value rather than label text. Screen text a person reads is untouched: `textOf` stays `innerText`, so observations still show the marker. - An exact `label` query is executed by Playwright's `getByLabel`, which also keeps hidden text, so the projection (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts`) now takes every labelable control in scope as candidates and the surface (`packages/playwright/src/surface.ts`) keeps those with a matching label. title: feat(report): name the configured model in the AI summary row
body:
## What and why

- The list reporter's `AI` summary row now ends with the configured models. A long run's header, the only place they were printed, has scrolled away by the time the summary lands.

body: ## What and why - `@e2edev/e2e/run` had one intended consumer, a platform embedding the runner in-process. title: feat(report): live window says Replaying while the cache has the step
body: ## What and why - The live window's wait row took every gap in an agent step for a model turn, so a step the trace cache replayed zero-turn shimmered `Thinking` for its whole length. Settle waits, relocation retries, and the end-state check all ran with no model in the loop. - `StepProgress` gains a `replay` phase, `{ phase: 'replay', api, active }`, at `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:163`. The step recorder emits it from `replaying(active)` and records nothing, since the step's `cache` detail already says how the replay went. The `@e2edev/e2e/run` entry grows by that union member, hence the minor changeset. - The trace session reads the cache entry before the baseline probe and takes the step as soon as it has one, at `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts:183`. It hands the step to the model only when a replay cannot finish it, after a decided miss, a diverged prefix, or an end-mismatch. A replay that finishes the step keeps it through the verdict and the re-stage, so the row does not flip back to `Thinking` for the trailing settled observation. - The window swaps the word at `packages/e2e/src/report/running-tree.ts:198`. Spinner, shimmer, and row layout are unchanged. - The reorder has one visible cost. On a `wrong-context` miss the row reads `Replaying` for one baseline probe before the model takes over. A clean replay still paints one `Thinking` frame at step start. The store read lands about a millisecond later and the next paint says `Replaying`. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["agent.act starts"] --> E{"cache entry?"} E -- no --> M["model runs, row says Thinking"] E -- yes --> T["replaying(true), row says Replaying"] T --> P["baseline probe, start-path decision"] P -- miss --> H["replaying(false)"] H --> M P -- replay --> A["recorded actions, end-state check"] A -- finished --> V["verdict, re-stage, step ends"] A -- diverged --> H ``` One frame of a zero-turn replay of a scripted `agent.act` in the testbed. Before is what `main` paints for the same state. Before ``` ❯ web tests-replay-demo/replay.e2e.ts 0/1 └── act replays from the trace cache on the second run 139ms ↳ agent.act "add a todo named "Write spec"" ✳ Thinking ``` After ``` ❯ web tests-replay-demo/replay.e2e.ts 0/1 └── act replays from the trace cache on the second run 139ms ↳ agent.act "add a todo named "Write spec"" ✳ Replaying ``` Relates to ENG-734. A record-then-replay demo GIF should not say `Thinking` during the replay. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(config): reporter objects in reporters
body:
## What and why

- The first step of the TesterArmy results reporter, and the only vendor-neutral one: a `Reporter` in `reporters` is how a run's outcome leaves the machine. The package that uploads to TesterArmy comes next and builds on nothing but this. Community reporters get the same seam.
- The three built-in ids are the first users of the contract. `list`, `json`, and `junit` are `Reporter` objects the ids name (`packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts`, `json.ts`, `list.ts`): junit writes `junit.xml` beside the report from `onRunFinished` and returns its summary row, json writes the document from `onRunFinished`, list implements `onEvent`. If the contract could not express junit, it would be incomplete; it took `FinishedRun.projectRoot` and nothing else.
- Contract on the main entrypoint beside `ArtifactStore` (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts`): a `name`, an optional `onEvent` that is one more sink on the run's event spine, and an optional `onRunFinished(run, signal)` that receives the finished run plus an `AbortSignal` (aborted on its timeout or a forced stop, so it cancels its own requests) and may resolve with summary rows of label and text. `Report`, `RunEvent`, and `RunEventOf` join the main entrypoint so an inline reporter types its handlers from one import. No new subpath until a package consumes one.
- `onRunFinished` runs last, after `report.json` and after the `list` summary. Every reporter runs at once, each awaited for one minute through the existing `withTimeout`, and abandoned by a forced interrupt through `withAbort` on the force signal. A throw, a timeout, a forced stop, or a result that is not rows is one stderr line and the run keeps its own exit code (`runReporters` in `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`). Rows print under the summary in its layout.
- Behaviour change, in the changeset: a `junit.xml` that cannot be written used to be a `REPORT_WRITE_FAILED` run error that flipped the exit code to 3. It is now the junit reporter's stderr line, the same rule every reporter gets. `junitPath` leaves the `run-finished` event and the outcome; the row replaces it.
- The document reporters and the outcome receive is the one written to `report.json`, rebuilt only when that write itself failed, so an upload ships the file byte for byte.
- `--reporter` replaces the built-in ids only. An object has no id to name on the command line, so `--reporter list,junit` in CI never drops the upload the config asked for (`resolveReporters` in `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts`).
- Live values leave the config before the digest's JSON clone, not after: a reporter or artifact store holding an SDK client with a cyclic object graph used to fail config load with a serialization error. Reporter objects never enter the digest and the ids digest as before, so adding a reporter leaves the trace cache valid.
- Folded in: `ManagedProcess.stop` cancels its shutdown timer once the process has exited, through the same `withTimeout`. It used to leave a pending 10 s timer that held the event loop, so the CLI lingered after the summary. A testbed run now exits ~0.4 s after `Duration` prints.

```ts
import type { E2EConfig, Reporter } from '@e2edev/e2e';

const upload: Reporter = {
  name: 'upload',
  async onRunFinished(run, signal) {
    const { url } = await post(run.report, run.artifactsRoot, { signal });
    return [{ label: 'Results', text: url }];
  },
};

export default { targets, reporters: ['list', 'junit', upload] } satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E[event spine] --> L["list.onEvent"]
  E --> O["upload.onEvent"]
  E --> F[run-finished: summary prints]
  F --> R["await onRunFinished on json, junit, upload  ≤ 60 s, until force"]
  R --> K[rows under the summary: JUnit, Results]
  R -. throw / timeout / force / not rows .-> S[one line on stderr, exit code unchanged]
```

```
   Test Files  9 passed (9)
        Tests  33 passed (33)
     Start at  17:06:54
     Duration  2.58s (startup 92ms)
       Report  .e2e/report.json

        JUnit  .e2e/junit.xml
```

title: fix(playwright): pin predicate-filtered matches to their elements instead of a candidate index
body: ## What and why - A match that a predicate selected (an exact label query since #234, a display-value query before it) is one element among many candidates, and its ref re-resolved `candidates.nth(index)` when the action ran. The exact-label candidate set is broad (every labelable control and every `aria-label` element in scope), so a page that inserted or removed an element between locate and perform shifted the index and the action landed on a neighbor. Seen on TesterArmy's settings page right after the bump: `getByLabel("Project Name").clear()` resolved to a button and failed as "Element is not an ". This is the deferred finding from #234, now with a real failure behind it. - `locate` (`packages/playwright/src/surface.ts`) now takes element handles beside the semantic read for predicate projections and stores `{ kind: 'element' }` refs for the matches, the identity observation refs already use. The two resolutions are compared by count; a mismatch means the page moved between them, and the read runs again (three attempts, then the positional ref as before). - Plain queries are unchanged: a single match keeps its strict locator, which re-resolves by the query itself and fails loud if it turns ambiguous. - Fixture: `/twins` gains an `Insert a field` button that prepends a labeled input. The lifecycle test locates `Display name`, taps the button, fills the earlier ref, and checks the value landed on `Display name` and not on the inserted field.
