title: docs: move the docs site from Starlight to Mintlify
body: ## What and why - Mintlify hosts the docs from `docs/`, so the site is now a `docs.json` and flat `.mdx` pages instead of an Astro project. Astro, Starlight, the Vercel adapter, the Shiki theme, the `PageTitle` override, and `vercel.json` are gone. Every page keeps its slug, title, and description; the nine Fern-era redirects move into `docs.json`. - The TesterArmy look survives in `docs/docs.json` (orange-300 accent, orange-100 in dark mode and orange-500 in light, Geist, dark code blocks in both schemes) plus `docs/style.css` for what the config cannot say: square corners, weights capped at 500, the orange rule over the title, a hairline above each h2, Geist Mono in code. - Starlight components map one to one. `Aside` becomes `Note`, `Tip`, `Warning`, or `Danger`, with the title as a bold lead line since Mintlify callouts take none. `CardGrid`/`LinkCard` become `CardGroup`/`Card`, `Tabs`/`TabItem` become `Tabs`/`Tab`, the npm/pnpm tabs become a `CodeGroup`, and the two `Steps` lists become `Step` components. - Mintlify cannot import a file into a page, so `docs/quickstart.mdx` carries verbatim copies of the four `docs/examples/` files. `scripts/check-docs-examples.ts` runs in `docs:check` and fails when a copy drifts; the examples stay typechecked against the built packages by the docs `typecheck` script. - `pnpm docs:dev` runs `mint dev`. `pnpm docs:check` runs the examples check, `mint validate`, and `mint broken-links`; `docs:build` is gone and `.github/workflows/docs.yml` runs the check. `scripts/check-error-codes.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.gitignore`, and the PR template point at the new paths. - `mint` 4.2.881 is a devDependency of `@e2edev/docs` rather than an `npx` call: `npx -y mint@4.2.881` exits 1 with no output (even for `--help`) while a local bin works. It pulls puppeteer, keytar, and sharp; the workspace's `onlyBuiltDependencies` already skips their install scripts. - Hosting still has to be connected in the Mintlify dashboard (GitHub app, directory `docs/`). Until a domain exists, the README, `packages/e2e/src/cli/docs-url.ts`, the skill, and the issue template keep pointing at e2e-docs.vercel.app. ```json // docs/docs.json { "theme": "mint", "colors": { "primary": "#ff8001", "light": "#ffb56c", "dark": "#b55b01" }, "fonts": { "heading": { "family": "Geist", "weight": 500 }, "body": { "family": "Geist" } }, "styling": { "codeblocks": "dark", "eyebrows": "breadcrumbs" }, "navigation": { "groups": [{ "group": "Get started", "pages": ["index", "quickstart", "writing-tests", "agents"] }] }, "redirects": [{ "source": "/writing-a-backend", "destination": "/writing-an-engine" }] } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[docs/examples/*.ts] -- tsc --> B[typecheck against dist] A -- verbatim copy --> C[docs/quickstart.mdx] C --> D[check-docs-examples.ts] C --> E[mint validate] C --> F[mint broken-links] D & E & F --> G[docs:check] ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent-device): discover booted devices as the pool, select UDIDs
body: ## Why Running a device target with no `device` on a machine with several booted simulators failed every test: agent-device refuses to guess between booted devices carrying the app (`Multiple booted iOS simulators have com.pagerviewexample installed`), and `prepare` only logged it. Pinning by UDID failed too (`No device named ...`), although the docs said "name or id". Consumers ended up shelling out to `xcrun simctl` in their config to build a pool. ## What **Core (`@e2edev/e2e`)** - `prepare` may return `EnginePrepareResult { workers }`: the cap the engine actually provisioned, `1` to `info.slots`. The runner validates it (an out-of-range value is `ENGINE_FAILURE`), stores it on the target's work plan, and the scheduler honours it over the declared `workers`. Engines that know their cap up front change nothing. **agent-device (`@e2edev/agent-device`)** - No `device`: `DevicePool` declares no static cap, so the run plans with `config.workers`; `prepare` lists the inventory (`client.devices.list`), takes the booted devices of the platform up to `info.slots`, boots each under its slot session, reports `{ workers }`, and writes the pool to `info.env` as `E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_POOL_`. A worker's `init` reads that variable; without it (no `prepare`), agent-device picks as before. None booted: one slot, agent-device boots one. - `deviceSelection` sends a simulator UDID as `udid` and a name as `device`. - Discovery log names the devices: `5 booted ios device(s); driving 4: iPhone 16e, iPhone 17, ...`. - Docs: `reference/device.mdx`, `reference/engine.mdx`, package README, skill `setup.md`. Two changesets (minor each). ## Verification - Unit: e2e 955, playwright 153, agent-device 81 (new: discovery with env handoff and worker read-back, slot-limited and cold-boot cases, UDID vs name selection; scheduler honouring a prepared cap). `pnpm lint` clean, package typechecks clean. - On device, react-native-pager-view's 13-test suite against this branch's dists: - no `device`, five booted simulators, `workers: 4`: `driving 4`, 108 s, same 12/13 as before (the failure is a known library bug). - `device: ['']`: boots and runs by `udid`. ---

title: feat(testerarmy): the TesterArmy reporter package
body: ## What and why - The conversion path from a local `e2e run` to a TesterArmy run page, as one package on the `Reporter` seam that #238 landed: `packages/testerarmy`, published as `@e2edev/testerarmy`. Nothing TesterArmy-specific enters `@e2edev/e2e`. - `testerarmy({ project?, apiKey? })` returns a `Reporter` whose `onRunFinished` runs the upload protocol (`packages/testerarmy/src/upload.ts`): `PUT /api/v1/e2e/runs/{runId}` with the report-1 document, the CI context, and the digests of the artifacts on disk (only files on disk under the artifacts root at the size the report recorded are offered); one direct `PUT` per digest the server lacks, streamed from disk with the report's size as the length so a recording is never held in memory whole, sending the headers the server named for it, which is how the pinned SHA-256 travels without the reporter knowing about checksums; `POST …/complete`. The run id is the report's own, so a retry is idempotent. Every request carries the reporter's abort signal; each storage PUT gets one of its own that follows it, so the streamed file closes however the request ends, and the first failed upload aborts its siblings. Anything the server does outside the protocol, a non-JSON body, an unknown or malformed upload entry, throws with a message the runner prints. - The key is read when the run finishes, from `TESTERARMY_API_KEY` (or the variable `apiKey` names) or from `~/.config/testerarmy/config.json`, the file `testerarmy auth` writes (used for tester.army only, so a config that redirects the reporter never carries the saved key with it). Without one the reporter sends nothing and the summary says so in one row, so one config serves a laptop without an account and a CI job with the secret. `TESTERARMY_BASE_URL` picks the host, the same variable the CLI reads; it must be https unless loopback, so the key never travels in clear text. - CI attribution (`packages/testerarmy/src/context.ts`): commit, branch (none on a tag build), pull request (CircleCI's URL form included), and job URL where the provider has one, from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite, or Vercel, sent beside the report rather than inside it. report-1 stays as it is until a second consumer wants those fields. - Options are two on purpose, `project` and the key variable name; anything else waits for a consumer. - The server side is tester-army/app#2310: new `e2e_runs` and `e2e_artifacts` tables, the two routes, and a run page that renders report-1. ```ts import { testerarmy } from '@e2edev/testerarmy'; export default { targets: [{ engine: playwright({ url: 'localhost:3000' }) }], reporters: ['list', testerarmy()], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as reporter participant A as tester.army /api/v1/e2e participant S as object storage R->>A: PUT /runs/{runId} {report, context, artifacts[sha256,size,mediaType]} A-->>R: {url, uploads:[{sha256, url, headers}]} (only digests the team lacks) R->>S: PUT bytes with the named headers, one per missing digest R->>A: POST /runs/{runId}/complete A-->>R: {url} Note over R: row under the summary: TesterArmy https://tester.army/… ``` ``` Report .e2e/report.json TesterArmy https://tester.army/dashboard/acme/projects/…/e2e-runs/0192c… ``` Docs: a new guide page, [Upload runs to TesterArmy](docs/testerarmy.mdx) in the Guides navigation, a Reporters section on the Environment variables page, a link from the Reporters reference, and a line in the running skill. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. New package, `minor` from 0.0.0. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/src/content/docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No change to `@e2edev/e2e`; the peer range is `>=0.9.0 <1`, the first release with `Reporter`. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(cli): e2e explore runs the agent toward a goal without a test file
body: ## What and why - `e2e explore [goal]` runs the agent against the app with a goal instead of a test file: it plans one charter at a time, drives the app, reports defects through a `report_finding` tool, and closes with an assessment. Use it before tests exist, on a branch to hunt for regressions a suite would not know to look for, or to find what is worth turning into a test. - No second brain. The explorer is `createAgent()` with exploration guidance appended and one tool added, so each charter is an ordinary `agent.act()` step under the same budgets, secrets, origin policy, and loop guards. The planner is one `agent.extract()` call between steps; the ledger carries state. - No second runner. The exploration is one test registered in memory (`RunOptions.tests`) and run in-process, so reporters, `report.json`, artifacts, `--video`, `--ai-trace`, `--debug`, and Ctrl-C are the runner's own. The report gains an additive `run.explore` block (schema updated, fixtures unchanged since the block is optional). - Outcome policy borrowed from TesterArmy's discovery runs: a failed step is a finding and the run goes on; a step that hits its budget ended at its limit and is not a failure; three failed steps in a row that reported nothing, the step cap (1 to 12), or the clock (3 to 15 min) end the run; `issue` findings fail the run (exit 1), `warning`s do not; zero steps and zero findings is `blocked`, never a pass. - `createAgent()` now returns a `DefaultAgent` whose `tools`, `system`, `maxTurns`, and `providerOptions` are readable, so explore composes on a project's `createAgent({ tools, system })`. A hand-rolled `StepExecutor` is replaced for the run, with a notice. - No `--model` flag: `E2E_MODEL` already does that for every command. ```mermaid flowchart LR G[goal] --> P[plan: agent.extract] P -- step --> A[charter: agent.act + report_finding] A --> L[ledger + findings] L --> P P -- finish --> S[assessment] S --> R[report.json run.explore] ``` ```bash npx --no-install e2e explore 'Explore checkout like a first-time buyer and report anything off' E2E_MODEL=google/gemini-3.6-flash npx --no-install e2e explore --max-steps 4 --video ``` ```text Explored 4 steps (4 passed); ended: the agent covered the goal Findings 10 issues, 1 warning S4 issue 'Add to cart' button for Dune is unresponsive / dead control (/catalog) S4 issue Removing an item from the cart removes the wrong item (/cart) S3 issue Account profile changes are not saved despite 'Profile saved.' status message (/account) ... Assessment Explored the Bookshelf online bookshop across all primary buyer flows ... ``` ## Benchmark `packages/testbed/app/bug-garden.mjs` is a bookshop with 11 planted defects (dead control, wrong calculation, wrong removal target, lost save, epoch dates, plain-text password, template token, negative stock, count mismatch, 404 link, typo). `scripts/explore-bench.mjs` runs `e2e explore` per model on its own app instance and scores findings against them. Eight steps, ten minutes, the same goal, final guidance: | Model | planted found | false positives | steps | cost | time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | google/gemini-3.6-flash | 10/11 | 0 | 3 | $0.13 | 131 s | | openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast | 6/11 | 1 | 4 | $0.03 | 112 s | | moonshotai/kimi-k3-fast | 8/11 | 1 | 5 | $2.57 | 510 s | | anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 | 3/11 | 0 | 2 | $0.42 | 130 s | | deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash | 2/11 | 0 | 3 | $0.03 | 526 s | | anthropic/claude-opus-5-fast | 8/11 | 5 | 5 | $13.63 | 530 s | What the rounds changed in the agent: the planner accepts a charter written into `title` alone (gemini's first runs died there), the sanity checklist is part of the default guidance (+2 defects for luna), findings so far travel as `params.reportedFindings` so nothing is reported twice, "passed" means the charter was carried out whatever was reported (luna had been failing productive steps and tripping the stuck rule), and a defect that only appears in a summary is called out as lost (haiku). The plain-text password is the one defect no model reports. Follow-ups, not in this PR: credentials in explore (`type_secret` needs step secrets), a planner step api so its long labels stay out of the ledger, finding gates for tool-error restatements, and mapping `explore` to `discovery` in the TesterArmy reporter. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(config)!: agents by name replace agent, and --agent picks one per run
body: ## What and why - `agents` replaces `agent`: a record of the same shapes the old key took (an options block, or the agent itself from `createAgent(...)` or any `StepExecutor`), by name. `default` is what tests run with, and it exists even when the config names none. - Other names are other brains for the same suite: a model that reads screens more carefully, a UX playbook with its own tools, a marketing lens. `e2e run --agent ` runs with one of them; the run summary and the `run-started` event name any agent that is not `default`. Names live on the CLI override path, so workers re-resolve the same choice. - One concept instead of one config block per feature. `e2e explore` (#243) will take `--agent` the same way once both land, and a per-test `{ agent: 'ux' }` option is the natural next step; neither is in this PR. - Breaking, while we are `0.x`: `agent:` is rejected with the replacement in the message. Every agent diagnostic now names its entry (`agents.ux.model`). `e2e init` scaffolds the new shape, and every config in the repo is migrated. ```ts export default { agents: { default: { model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast' }, thorough: { model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5', context: 'Verify every claim on screen before concluding.' }, ux: createAgent({ system: UX_REVIEW_PLAYBOOK, tools: { contrastCheck } }), }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ```bash npx --no-install e2e run --agent thorough tests/checkout.e2e.ts ``` ```text RUN e2e v0.8.0 /work/shop run 01a08… · targets: web · agent: thorough model anthropic/claude-opus-5 ``` Where it lives: resolution in `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts` (`resolveAgents`), the per-entry labels in `packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts`, the flag in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`, the event field in `packages/e2e/src/run/events.ts`. `ResolvedConfig` keeps `agent` as the selected agent, so nothing downstream changed; it gains `agentName` and `agents`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). No deprecation window: the packages are `0.x` and the policy starts at 1.0; the old key is rejected with its replacement. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. `E2EConfig.agents` and the optional `agent` on `run-started`; no report schema change. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(run): redact filled secrets out of the trace before it is registered or stored
body:
## What and why

- A filled credential ended up in `trace.zip` as typed: the `fill` action's params, every DOM snapshot of the field (`__playwright_value_`), and the login POST body and its resource. `report.json` still said `redaction: "complete"` because `run/artifacts.ts` hardcoded it per kind. Reproduced on the testbed login setup before the change. E2E-28.
- The runner now rewrites the trace in place instead of dropping it: a login setup is the trace most suites want to keep. Once a secret was filled on the session (`taint`), every UTF-8 text entry of every trace archive passes through the secret ledger before the trace is registered, hashed, or handed to an `ArtifactStore`: JSON records value by value (re-serialized only when something changed, so a secret that spells JSON syntax cannot break a record), other text as text. A binary entry (a screencast frame, a font) is carried byte for byte unless a secret's bytes occur in it, in which case it is dropped.
- `stopTrace` in the engine contract may now return every trace archive the attempt wrote. The Playwright surface returns its `trace-part<n>.zip` segments (a restart or a state reset cuts the trace) ahead of `trace/trace.zip`, and the runner registers and redacts exactly those paths. A returned path outside `artifactsDir` is refused before anything is touched.
- The redactor also matches the encodings a trace spells a value in: JSON string body (once and twice quoted), HTML-escaped, `encodeURIComponent`, `encodeURI`, and form-encoded. Observations, logs, and the cache get that for free.
- Labels are decided per attempt: `not-required` when no secret was filled, `complete` after a rewrite, and a trace registered without a verdict defaults to `incomplete`, so nothing can claim completeness by accident. A trace that cannot be rewritten is deleted with its segments and the attempt carries a `TRACE_WITHHELD` secondary error whatever the artifact policy; under a `required` policy the attempt's cleanup is also marked failed.
- `internal/zip.ts` is a small codec over `node:zlib`: reads by the central directory (Playwright's bundled yazl writes data descriptors), writes plain deflated entries, refuses zip64.
- Per-session ledger and taint moved from `run/fixtures.ts` to `run/secrecy.ts` so `closeSession` can reach them.
- Not done on purpose: `app.screenshot()` after a secret fill is still kept and labelled `complete`; it masks secure fields at the source. Withholding it, as the ticket text proposed, is a product call.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[engine stopTrace: one path or every segment] --> B{secret filled on session?}
  B -- no --> C[register each: not-required]
  B -- yes --> D[rewrite each archive, JSON value by value]
  D -- ok --> E[register each: complete]
  D -- fails --> F[delete the trace, TRACE_WITHHELD in secondaryErrors]
  C --> G[hash, store.put]
  E --> G

title: feat(github): the GitHub reporter comments on the pull request from Actions
body:
## What and why - `@e2edev/github`, a reporter package beside the runner: `reporters: ['list', github()]` posts one pull request comment per run from GitHub Actions and edits it in place on a rerun, keyed by a hidden marker naming the config's `projectId`, the workflow, and the job. The same text is appended to the job summary, pull request or not. - The comment is the report-1 document rendered once: counts in the headline, run-level errors above the table (an `APP_UNREACHABLE` makes every result meaningless), one row per test that did not simply pass with its error and the artifact kinds it left, source links at the PR head commit, passed tests folded away, and a link to the workflow run where `upload-artifact` put the evidence. Titles and messages are text a test wrote, so cells are stripped of control characters, escaped, and clipped; past fifty rows the table says how many more, and the passed list is dropped before the body reaches GitHub's 65536-character limit. - Actions only, on purpose. Off Actions there is no ambient token; a push has no pull request; a fork's `pull_request` token is read-only. Each case is one summary row saying so, and the run's exit code never changes. Posting from another CI, or as an identity that is not the workflow, is the TesterArmy reporter's job (#242), which the off-Actions row names. - `renderComment(report, { marker, artifactsUrl, sourceUrl })` is exported so the TesterArmy server can render the same comment from an uploaded report: the free comment and the hosted one read identically, and the hosted one adds video, checks, and history. - Nothing GitHub-specific enters `@e2edev/e2e`. Zero runtime dependencies: `fetch`, `node:fs`, `node:util`. ```ts title="e2e.config.ts" import { github } from '@e2edev/github'; export default { targets: [{ engine: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }], reporters: ['list', github()], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ```yaml permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write steps: - run: npx --no-install e2e run env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR R[run finishes] --> A{on Actions?} A -- no --> N[row: not posted, use testerarmy elsewhere] A -- yes --> S[append to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY] S --> P{pull request + token?} P -- no --> M[row: why, summary written] P -- yes --> L[GET issue comments, find marker] L -- found --> U[PATCH comment] L -- none --> C[POST comment] U --> H[row: comment URL] C --> H ``` What the comment looks like, from the sample in `tests/unit`: --- ### 🔴 e2e: 1 failed, 1 flaky, 2 passed | | Test | Outcome | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 🔴 | [tests/billing.e2e.ts:12](https://github.com/acme/shop/blob/1a2b3c/tests/billing.e2e.ts#L12) › billing › upgrades to Pro | **ASSERTION_FAILED** expected heading "Your cart" to be visible | [screenshot, video, trace](https://github.com/acme/shop/actions/runs/123) | | ⚠️ | [tests/todos.e2e.ts:8](https://github.com/acme/shop/blob/1a2b3c/tests/todos.e2e.ts#L8) › todos survive a filter round-trip | flaky: passed after 1 failed attempt | [screenshot, trace](https://github.com/acme/shop/actions/runs/123) |
2 passed tests - tests/example.e2e.ts › opens the app (850ms) - tests/dashboard.e2e.ts › the dashboard opens directly (2.1s)
Screenshots, traces, and recordings: [run artifacts](https://github.com/acme/shop/actions/runs/123). e2e 0.9.0 · 48.2s · 1 target (web) --- ``` Report .e2e/report.json GitHub https://github.com/acme/shop/pull/41#issuecomment-5 ``` Docs: a new guide page, [Comment on the pull request](docs/github.mdx), a section on the CI page, a Reporters section on the Environment variables page, a link from the Reporters reference, and a line in the running skill. Not exercised live against GitHub: the API calls are covered by the fake in `packages/github/tests/unit/post.test.ts`; a real workflow run is the next step once the package is published. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. New package, `minor` from 0.0.0. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No change to `@e2edev/e2e`; the peer range is `>=0.9.0 <1`, the first release with `Reporter`. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(playwright): reach protected previews with headers and basicAuth
body: ## What and why - `playwright()` takes `headers` and `basicAuth`. Before this, the only way to add a request header was a `web.route` handler inside a deterministic test, so `agent.act` and `e2e explore` had no way into a Vercel preview under deployment protection, an ngrok tunnel with its interstitial, or a staging host behind basic auth. - `headers` is not a pass-through to Playwright's `extraHTTPHeaders`. That option sends to every origin, which would hand a bypass secret to every CDN, analytics endpoint, and identity provider the page talks to. The surface registers one context route keyed on `allowedOrigins` and falls back to the network with the merged headers (`packages/playwright/src/surface.ts`, `installHeaders`). - The header route is registered before any attempt route. Playwright runs handlers newest first, so a `web.route` handler that continues still sends the headers and one that fulfills or aborts never reaches it. Routes are re-applied on every context the attempt opens, so `clearState` and session restore keep them. - `basicAuth` maps to Playwright's credential list with one entry per allowed origin, so the browser answers a `401` from the app and ignores a challenge from any third-party origin. - Both are validated in the factory: RFC 9110 token header names, no line breaks in values, a non-empty username without `:`. All `INVALID_CONFIG` before a browser launches. - Cost, documented: any route on a context turns the browser HTTP cache off, and a Playwright trace records request headers, so the bypass secret is in `trace.zip` (same family as #245). ```ts engine: playwright({ url: process.env.PREVIEW_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000', identity: 'storefront', headers: { 'x-vercel-protection-bypass': process.env.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET ?? '' }, }), engine: playwright({ url: 'https://staging.example.com', basicAuth: { username: 'preview', password: process.env.PREVIEW_PASSWORD ?? '' }, }), ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR R[request] --> O{origin in allowedOrigins?} O -- no --> N[network, untouched] O -- yes --> W[web.route handlers, newest first] W -- fulfill / abort --> X[done] W -- continue --> H[header route: fallback with merged headers] H --> N2[network] ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent): pin an agent per test, group, or call with the agent option
body: ## What and why - A suite pins its agent: `agent` is an option on `test` and `test.describe`, resolved like `agentContext`, innermost wins. A persona is then a describe block: an agent for how it thinks and, only when it is signed in, `session` for the state a setup test saved. Nothing has to be named a persona. - A call can name another: `act`, `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract` take `{ agent }` for one step under a different brain, with the attempt's ledger intact, so a buyer step and an admin step can share one flow. - `--agent` re-points what unpinned tests use and never overrides a pin. A pin is a statement about the suite; the flag is a statement about the run. - Unknown names fail early and by name: a pin at collection (`COLLECTION_ERROR`, before any process starts), a call before its step opens (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`). Every agent step records its agent as `step.agent`, so two personas in one test stay distinguishable in the report. - Follows #244, which introduced `agents` and `--agent`. ```ts test.describe('checkout as a first-time buyer', { agent: 'buyer' }, () => { test('pays for one item', async ({ app, agent }) => { /* ... */ }); test('applies a promo code', async ({ app, agent }) => { /* ... */ }); test.describe('refunds', { agent: 'admin' }, () => { // nested block, another agent test('refunds the order', async ({ agent }) => { /* ... */ }); }); }); await agent.act('approve the pending reorder', { agent: 'admin' }); // one step under another brain ``` ```text $ e2e run --agent thorough buyer browses ✓ agent.act agent: buyer # pinned, keeps its agent unpinned follows the run ✓ agent.act agent: thorough # re-pointed by the flag ``` Where it lives: the agent fixture resolves executor, models, and trusted context per call through `AgentContext.select` (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`), replacing the four attempt-wide fields the act and judgment tiers read before; `WorkerModels` (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker-models.ts`) checks each agent's model once per worker and shares adapters by resolved model; the pin travels as `ResolvedTestOptions.agent` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`); the step recorder takes `agent` in its run options and the report-1 `step` gains an optional `agent`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. `agent` on `TestOptions`, `DescribeOptions`, and the four call option types; optional `step.agent` in report-1, additive, fixtures stay valid. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(cli): load .ts config and tests as ESM in any package, pin the engine init installs
body:
## What and why - A fresh `create-next-app` project has no `type` in `package.json`. tsx types a `.ts` file by its package scope, so it treated `e2e.config.ts` as CommonJS and handed it to `require`, which tsx's ESM API never hooks. The run died on `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for a path carrying our cache-busting query, and `esm.ts` rephrased that as a demand to set `"type": "module"`, a change that also alters how every `.js` file in the app runs. - A resolve hook (`packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`) now marks the `.ts`, `.mts`, and `.tsx` files a project reaches by path as `format: 'module'`: the entry, `./helper.ts`, and tsconfig `paths` aliases, which tsx maps before calling the hook. Bare specifiers are packages, linked or installed, and keep the format their manifest declares; `.cts` files stay CommonJS. It is registered before tsx so it sits inside tsx's chain (last registered runs first). An outer hook cannot do this: tsx rewrites CommonJS-scoped URLs into its virtual-query form before an outer hook sees them. - The hook kind follows tsx 4.23.13's own choice per Node version (`tsxUsesSyncHooks` in `packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`): sync `registerHooks` on 22.22.3+, 24.11.1+, 25.1+, 26; async `module.register` otherwise. Chains only compose within a kind. Revisit when tsx is bumped. - `esm.ts` is deleted and `init` no longer warns about the module type. `init` still creates an ESM manifest when there is none. - `init` wrote engine ranges as `0.x`. npm and bun resolve a range to the registry's `latest` dist-tag whenever it satisfies, and our `latest` trails `beta` by several minors, so a new project got an engine whose peer range rejected the runner. The package build now records the sibling engine versions into `dist/cli/init/engine-versions.json`, and `init` writes `^0.7.0` for `@e2edev/playwright`. From source the range stays `0.x`. ```mermaid flowchart LR I[importModule
file:///app/e2e.config.ts?e2e=…] --> T[tsx resolve] T --> H[e2e hook
.ts outside node_modules → module] H --> N[Node default resolve
commonjs-typescript] N --> H --> T T -- format module --> L[tsx load: transform as ESM] ``` ```json // package.json written by e2e init in a Next.js app (unchanged type) { "devDependencies": { "@e2edev/e2e": "^0.8.0", "@e2edev/playwright": "^0.7.0", "ai": "^7.0.0" } } ``` Where it lives: the hook in `packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`, registration and the tsx version table in `packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`, the range in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts` (`engineRange`), the build record in `packages/e2e/package.json` (`build`). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(explore): configured credentials reach the explorer as step secrets
body: ## What and why - Configured `credentials` now reach the explorer, so an exploration gets past a real login wall. Every charter carries the credentials as step secrets under `params.credentials`, exactly as a test's `agent.act(..., { params })` would, so `type_secret` is offered by account name and the harness fills the value host-side. - The planner is told which accounts exist, name and username only, so it plans a sign-in step; the password never enters a prompt, a transcript, a finding, or the report. Once one is filled the run's screenshots are withheld, as in any test. - Two planner robustness fixes found on the way, with gemini-3.6-flash: the grammar accepts fields far past the report ceilings and clips afterwards (gemini poured a whole charter into `title`, past 2000 characters, and a rejection cost the run), digit runs a provider pads a field with are stripped, and one mid-run planner answer outside the grammar is covered by a continuation charter instead of ending the run. - Stacked on #243, which it extends. The bug garden's sign-in now requires the shop's one account, handed to the explorer through the testbed config, so the benchmark exercises this path and the plain-text password defect can surface through a refused secure fill. ```ts // e2e.config.ts credentials: { ada: { username: 'ada@example.test', password: process.env.ADA_PASSWORD! } }, ``` ```text Plan the next step ... Accounts the agent can sign in with (it fills the password itself, by name): - ada (username: ada@example.test) ``` Bug garden, 8 steps, the same goal, after these changes: | Model | planted found | false positives | steps | cost | time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | google/gemini-3.6-flash | 10/11 | 0 | 3 | $0.16 | 110 s | | openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast | 6/11 | 2 | 5 | $0.04 | 122 s | Both signed in with the configured account through `type_secret` and found the profile defect behind the login. The plain-text password field stays the one planted defect no model reports: the fill is authorized by the field's `current-password` purpose, so nothing looks wrong from the tree. Where it lives: `packages/e2e/src/explore/body.ts` resolves the accounts through the public `credentials.user()` once the run has the registry up and adds them to each charter's params; `packages/e2e/src/explore/plan.ts` lists them for the planner; the rules in `packages/e2e/src/explore/executor.ts` say how to use them. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. Extends the explore changeset. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No public type or wire change. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent): requests reuse the provider prompt cache and survive one context overflow
body: ## What and why - The agent loop now addresses the provider's prompt cache. Anthropic models get a breakpoint on the system prompt (it covers the tool definitions) and one on the newest message, moved forward each turn; OpenAI models get a cache key derived from the system prompt so every call of a run routes to the same cache. Other providers see the request they saw before. `agent/model/prompt-cache.ts`. - Superseded full screens stay in the history until they total 32 KB, then go in one batch. The old rule elided the previous screen on every turn, which rewrote the opening message and made the request prefix different each turn: Haiku wrote its cache on every call and read it on none. `agent/screen-update.ts`. - A request the provider refuses as larger than the context window is recognized (error catalog over twenty providers, ported from the pi harness, plus HTTP 413) and retried once with the history shrunk, on the same turn budget. A second refusal is the new `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW` code (blocked: automation) instead of `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. `agent/model/overflow.ts`, `agent/tool-loop.ts`. - The report carries the cache split so this can be measured: `model.cacheReadTokens` / `model.cacheWriteTokens` per step, `usage.modelCachedTokens` per run, `· 38% cached` on the list reporter's usage line, a `cached` column in the `--debug` step table, `model_cached_tokens` in run telemetry. - Text results from project tools are bounded to 400 lines or 16 KB, cut on a line boundary, with a notice naming what was left out. `agent/tool-output.ts`. - Testbed: `tests-agent/judgments.e2e.ts` used the removed `intervalMs` option and failed every run; `.e2e-*/` is ignored so measurement runs can sit side by side. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[prepareTurn] --> M[markLatest: breakpoint on newest message] M --> G[generate] G -- ok --> V[verdict] G -- overflow, first time --> S[shrink: elide stale screens, clip texts over 16 KB] S --> G G -- overflow again --> E[CONTEXT_OVERFLOW] ``` ## Evidence Live through the AI Gateway, trace cache off, baseline built from `c72b05e5` in a separate worktree, two rounds per cell. Every test passed on both sides; model time did not move. | Scenario | main | this PR | cache reads | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | tester.army tour, claude-haiku-4.5 | $0.149, $0.133 | $0.126, $0.130 | 0% → 43–56% | | tester.army tour, gpt-5.6-luna-fast | $0.042, $0.040 | $0.040, $0.037 | 33–36% → 53% | | dogfood suite, claude-haiku-4.5 | $0.095, $0.098 | $0.097, $0.077 | 0% → 13–27% | | dogfood suite, gpt-5.6-luna-fast | $0.008, $0.008 | $0.008, $0.008 | 83% → 86% | Why the gain is modest: most steps are two turns and the second turn brings a whole new screen. Anthropic bills cache writes at 1.25×, so on such a step the write plus the kept old screen roughly cancels the 0.1× read. Haiku 4.5 caches nothing under 4096 tokens, so the shared system-plus-tools prefix (~2k) never caches across steps on Haiku; Sonnet and Opus (1024 minimum) should. The mechanism pays on steps with three or more turns and diff-only results. The `--debug` table after the change (tour, Haiku): ``` step calls tokens in/out cached cost agent.act "open the Pricing page from the head…" 2 31076/141 38% (11805) $0.025964 agent.act "go to the web application testing s…" 4 43478/236 62% (27120) $0.024319 agent.assert "the page describes testing web a…" 1 7495/151 0% (0) $0.00825 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(collect): attribute a test's source to its test() call under source maps
body: - Every test in a report produced by the published package had `source` pointing at the runner's own `src/collect/registry.ts:328`, the `test()` wrapper, instead of the test file. The GitHub reporter turned that into a link to `node_modules/.pnpm/@e2edev+e2e@.../src/collect/registry.ts` ([example](https://github.com/tester-army/app/pull/2323#issuecomment-5619928520)); `junit.xml` carried the same location. - Cause: `captureSource` skipped frames under the directory the module runs from (`dist/`). tsx enables source maps, and the shipped `.map` files relocate those frames to `../../src/...`, a tree that is not in the package, so nothing matched and the first frame won. In this repository the module already runs from `src/`, which is why vitest never saw it. - `relativeSource` then either relativized the path (when `node_modules` lives inside the project, as with pnpm) or fell back to the test file at line 1. - Fix: skip both `src/` and `dist/` under the package root, and drop the loader's `?e2e=...&tsx-namespace=...` query from the captured file. - Regression test spawns the built CLI on a fixture project and asserts `report.run.results[0].source`. It has to be the CLI: inside a vitest fork, vitest's stack handling reports the raw transformed positions, while plain Node maps them as users see. ```ts // packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts const PACKAGE_ROOT = path.dirname(path.dirname(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)))); const RUNNER_ROOTS = ['src', 'dist'].map((dir) => `${path.join(PACKAGE_ROOT, dir)}${path.sep}`); ``` | | `report.run.results[0].source` | | --- | --- | | before | `{ file: 'tests/source.e2e.ts', line: 328, column: 37 }` | | after | `{ file: 'tests/source.e2e.ts', line: 3, column: 1 }` |

fix(cli): init lists engines by platform, runs through the package manager, and links the live docs
body: ## What and why - The engine prompt names what you test, with the engine as the hint: **Web** (Playwright), **Mobile (iOS/Android)** (agent-device), and **None** (HTTP tests or your own engine) last. title: chore(deps): move every workspace dependency to latest and the repo to pnpm 12
body: ## What and why - Every exact pin moves to its current release; `pnpm -r outdated` is empty. The notable jumps: pnpm 10.34.5 → 12.3.4, agent-device 0.20.10 → 0.21.0, zod 4.6.1, ai 7.0.97, react and its types 19.3.0, fallow 3.24.1, oxlint 1.82.0, @clack/prompts 1.8.0, mint 4.2.883. - TypeScript 7.0.2 was already latest and its `tsc` already is the Go-native compiler (the launcher execs `@typescript/typescript-`), so there is no separate tsgo to adopt. - pnpm 12 changed three defaults this repo relied on. Each is set explicitly in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with a comment: | pnpm 12 default | Effect here | Setting | | --- | --- | --- | | `minimumReleaseAge` 24h | Refuses anything published in the last day; `update --latest` writes a 31-entry exclude list instead of picking older versions. Would have held back zod, react, ai, fallow, mint, @types/react. | `minimumReleaseAge: 0` (one line to flip back if you want the guard) | | `allowBuilds` replaces `onlyBuiltDependencies` | The old key is ignored and unapproved build scripts are a hard error (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`) | esbuild allowed; scarf, keytar, puppeteer, sharp denied, matching what pnpm 10 did | | Workspace cycles refuse recursive runs | `pnpm -r run typecheck` fails with `ERR_PNPM_TASK_CYCLE` on e2e ↔ playwright devDependencies | `ignoreWorkspaceCycles: true` | - @clack/core 1.5 narrows `isCancel` to `typeof CANCEL_SYMBOL` while the prompts still resolve to `Value | symbol`, so the guard no longer strips `symbol` and five sites in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init.ts` stopped compiling. A local guard closes the gap: ```ts function isCancelled(value: Value | symbol): value is symbol { return clack.isCancel(value); } ``` - fallow 3.24 newly reports `LocatorEngine.assertionTimeout` and `SessionStaging.stage` as unused class members. The rule is `warn` in `.fallowrc.json`, so it does not gate; left for a separate pass. - CI picks pnpm 12 up from the `packageManager` field through `pnpm/action-setup`; no workflow edits. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent)!: the act model sees the screen; screenshot and tap_at bring pixels into the act loop
body:
## What and why

- The act loop sees the screen. Two grammar tools join the built-in agent while no secret has been filled in the attempt: `screenshot()` attaches the masked viewport to its result as an image, and `tap_at({ x, y })` taps a point in that screenshot's pixel coordinates. The act model receives the image itself: no second model, no localizer call, nothing lost in a description.
- `tap_at` routes onto the tree before it taps. The point is scaled from image pixels into the observation's CSS pixels and hit-tested: a listed, enabled control containing it is tapped by id, with policy, stale relocation, and the trace descriptor unchanged; a point on nothing listed reaches the new engine member `tapAt` as a bare point, recorded as a trace gap. The hit test routes, it never vetoes. `actions.tapAt` on the executor socket has the same routing.
- Pixel mode. Once a screenshot was sent, every action result carries a fresh one, so a flow on a canvas keeps seeing its own effects, and an unchanged tree is not reported as a failed action. A screen with no listed interactive node opens with a screenshot already attached. While the step shows pixels, the settle after an action watches the pixels too: a tap that redraws a canvas is read as soon as the redraw lands instead of waiting out the change window on a tree that never moves.
- Screenshots are compacted and sized. Older screenshots are elided in one batch once three are stale, keeping the newest two. Model-bound screenshots have their long side capped at 768 px by a harness-side box resample (pngjs), with `scale` carried through so the coordinate arithmetic is unchanged and masks stay black.
- Engine contract: optional `tapAt(point, context)` with the `pointer` capability and the `tapAt` grammar verb; `SemanticNode.rect` is pinned to the top-level viewport's CSS pixels for nodes inside nested documents, and Playwright now reports them that way. agent-device presses the point in logical pixels.
- The step dispatch is split so it stops absorbing every new concern: `act.ts` is wiring plus verdict mapping over `StepAccounting`, `ObservationFeed`, `ActionDispatcher`, and `OperationQueue`; point routing lives in `point-tap.ts`. `createAgent` now rejects a project tool that reuses a grammar tool name instead of silently shadowing it.
- Breaking: `ExecutorVision` (`vision.tap`, `vision.look`, `vision.tainted`) is gone, replaced by `pixelsTainted` on the context and `actions.tapAt` returning a `PointTapResult`; the `'fallback'` vision mode is gone (`VisionMode` is `boolean | 'only'`); `visionModel` serves judgments only.

## Why not a separate vision model

The first version of this PR had `tap_visual` and `look` answered by a pinned `visionModel`, TesterArmy's shape. Live runs showed it was a hedge for act models that cannot ground, not a win: with gpt-5.6 as the act model the localizer hop doubled a canvas step's time and cost, and `look` handed the model a lossy paragraph in place of the pixels. Measured on a ten-key keypad and an eight-screen wizard that exist only as canvas pixels, gpt-5.6-luna-fast, per run:

| Design | Keypad pass | Keypad calls | Keypad time | Keypad cost | Wizard pass | Wizard time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tap_visual through a vision model | 3/3 | 29 to 33 | 94 to 110 s | $0.030 to $0.036 | not run | |
| screenshot + tap_at, this PR | 12/12 | 13 | 28 s | $0.015 | 12/12 | 37 s |

Compaction settings were compared six runs each on both flows: keeping two screenshots and eliding at three stale was the fastest and passed everything; larger batches and no elision were about ten percent cheaper thanks to the prompt cache but slower, and lost four keypad runs of eighteen; keeping one screenshot doubled the turns. Screenshot size, four runs per cap on both flows: tokens per screenshot turn fall from about 1390 at full size to 960 at a 1024 px long side, 680 at 768, 580 at 640, and 500 at 512. Every cap down to 640 passed every run; at 512 the model misread the keypad display, needed retries, and once accepted a wrong code. 768 is the default: a full step of margin above that cliff at 35% less per run than the full capture.

Act models differ widely on grounding: gpt-5.6 luna and luna-fast pass everything (luna at half the price), Gemini 3.8 Flash passes but slowly, Claude Sonnet 5 hits the wizard's large shapes and misses the keypad's small keys, DeepSeek and GLM flash models give up and are billed tens of thousands of tokens per screenshot. The agent reference says so. Ordinary tree-driven flows never call the pixel tools; their only cost is the two tool schemas, mostly prompt-cached.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[screenshot] --> B[observe with masked pixels]
  B -- withheld --> W[text: reason, work from the tree]
  B --> C[image + changes to the act model; pixel mode on]
  C --> D[tap_at x,y in image px]
  D --> E[divide by scale, clamp to viewport]
  E --> F{listed control under point?}
  F -- yes --> G[tap by id: policy, relocation, trace descriptor]
  F -- no --> H[engine.tapAt point: trace gap]
  G --> I[result: changes + fresh screenshot]
  H --> I
```

Key paths: `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts` (`screenshot`, `tap_at`, pixel mode), `point-tap.ts` (hit test, scaling), `pixels.ts` (sizing), `screen-update.ts` (presenter, screenshot compaction), `observation.ts` (pixel-aware settle shape), `action-dispatcher.ts` (`tapAt` routing), `act.ts` (wiring), `packages/playwright/src/observation.ts` (`offsetTree`). Testbed: `tests-agent/canvas-flow.e2e.ts` and `canvas-wizard.e2e.ts` are the long pixels-only flows the numbers come from.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added for every changed published package.
- [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset names what breaks and what replaces it.
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR (`docs/reference/agent.mdx`, `docs/agents.mdx`, engine and device pages) and `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed through the build; `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` has no executor-socket or engine coverage today; the report schema is unchanged.
- [x] Engine contract change: changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: fix(agent): the act loop falls back to auto tool choice for models that reject a forced one
body: ## What and why - `agent.act` sends `toolChoice: 'required'` on every turn and forces `complete_step` by name on the wind-down turns. Claude Fable 5.1 returns HTTP 400 to any forced tool choice (`tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.`), so no step could run on it. Found while picking the arms for E2E Bench. - New `isForcedToolChoiceRejected` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/tool-choice.ts`) reads the provider's words through a gateway wrapper or a spent retry chain, the same way `isContextOverflow` does. Only a 4xx counts. - The refused request is sent again under `auto` with one rule appended to the verdict rules: reply with tool calls only. The refusal is remembered per model instance (`WeakSet`), so later steps on that model start in `auto` and pay no second 400. The refused request is not a counted model call. - Under `auto` the SDK loop ends on a turn without a tool call. Such a reply now stays in the history and is followed by a notice to act; it spends a turn like any other, so a model that keeps talking still ends in `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION` when the budget runs out. Nothing changes for models that accept `required`. - The forced-conclusion turns keep `activeTools: ['complete_step']`; under `auto` the notice does the forcing. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[generate, toolChoice required] -->|400 names tool_choice| B[mode = auto, remember model] B --> C[resend same request + tool-calls-only rule] C --> D{turn has a tool call?} D -- yes --> E[loop continues] D -- no, turns left --> F[append reply + act notice] --> C D -- no, budget spent --> G[STEP_NO_CONCLUSION] ``` Transcript of a step under `--debug`, on a refusing model: ``` --- the model rejected a forced tool choice before turn 1: retrying with auto --- --- turn 1 --- tool call: observe({}) ... ``` Not live-verified against Fable 5.1: the gateway key on this machine has no credits. The rejection message is the one Anthropic documents; the tests script it through the fake loop model (`tests/unit/tool-loop-tool-choice.test.ts`). - Also in this PR: the telemetry flush-deadline unit test hung on the Node 26 job (30 s timeout). Its hanging-fetch fixture only rejected on the abort event; when the git project lookup outlives the 50 ms budget on a slow runner, the deadline fires before fetch is called and no event follows. The fixture now rejects an already-aborted signal like the real fetch does. Test-only, no runtime change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(playwright): observe closed shadow roots and display:contents subtrees
body: ## What and why - Two kinds of content a person sees never reached the agent's tree. On a real Shopify store the agent could neither find the cart's checkout button nor a single checkout field, so every model scrolled until the step budget died. - Closed shadow roots: a context init script wraps `Element.prototype.attachShadow` before any page script runs and records each closed root by host in a WeakMap under `Symbol.for('e2e.closedShadowRoots')`. The reader consults it where it read `shadowRoot`, so closed roots walk like open ones. `packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts`, installed in `openContext` in `packages/playwright/src/surface.ts`. - `display: contents`: such an element has no client rects, which `isHidden` read as hidden and pruned the whole subtree. Shopify's `form#checkout-one-page-form` is styled that way. The element itself still enters the tree only if it carries semantics; its children now decide their own visibility. - Refs resolve through element handles, so `tap`, `fill`, and the other actions reach nodes inside closed roots. Playwright locators (`screen.getByRole`) still stop at a closed root, as before. - Screenshot masks follow the reader: a registered Playwright selector engine, `e2e-closed=`, matches inside the recorded roots, so a password field there is covered in observation pixels and artifact screenshots like any other. Registered once per process before the first browser in `packages/playwright/src/browser-connection.ts`. - Declarative `

title: feat(bench): E2E Bench runs the agentic suites across models and scores every report
body: ## What and why - `packages/bench` (`@e2edev/bench`, private) is E2E Bench: it runs a matrix of model arms across four tracks, scores every run from its `report.json` and `ai-trace.json`, and commits compact summaries under `results/`. Two questions from one dataset: which model is good at agentic testing (harness fixed, model varied) and whether e2e is getting better (model fixed at the PR-gate arm, release varied). Plan and arm research are in the session notes; the arms are in `src/catalog.ts` with the reason each is in. - Tracks and oracles: - `act`: web-benchmark `tests-agent` scenarios, one `agent.act` each plus the deterministic success check. Pass rate, reliability (passed in every repeat), failure-code histogram; declared gaps count as harness coverage. - `judgment`: new `packages/web-benchmark/tests-judgment/`. `bug:` tests assert correct behavior on the 8 planted-bug pages and are expected to fail; `clean:` tests assert true statements on working pages, the two traps included. The scorer turns outcome plus code into caught / missed / false alarm / correct / inconclusive. - `explore` and `explore-clean`: `e2e explore` on the testbed bug garden, and on the garden with every defect fixed (`BUG_GARDEN_CLEAN=1`, new). Recall over the 11 planted defects, precision over adjudicated findings, false positives, duplicates, stuck runs, time to first finding, evidence rate. Unplanted findings go through `adjudications.json`; the ones nobody judged yet are printed after every run. - Every row also carries model calls, actions, tokens in and out, cache-read share, reasoning tokens (read from the AI trace; the report has no field), provider-reported cost next to the same tokens at list price, wall time, and time outside harness events. - Runs spawn the built CLI in the track's package with `E2E_MODEL`, `BENCH_PORT`, `E2E_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` in the environment, `--no-cache --retries 0 --ai-trace`, one app instance per run on its own port. `packages/web-benchmark/e2e.bench.config.ts` and the testbed explore config read those variables; the explore config also gets its model back into `gateway()` (it passed a string, which the resolver rejects since #255). `explore-bench.mjs` retires; the bench covers it. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[catalog: arms] --> M[matrix: arms x tracks x repeats] T[tracks: suite + config + oracle] --> M M -->|spawn e2e CLI per run| R[.bench/label/arm/track/rN: report, ai-trace, cli.log, run.json] R --> S[score-run: tasks, judgment cells, explore recall] S --> G[aggregate per arm x track] G --> W[results/date-label.json + Markdown] ``` ```bash AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... pnpm bench run --arms luna-fast,gemini-3.8-flash --tracks act,explore --repeats 1 --label smoke pnpm bench run --dry-run # every command the matrix would run pnpm bench score .bench/

title: feat(run)!: run one test as several agents; --agent takes a list
body:
## What and why - A design partner wanted one suite run through several personas, not several brains for one suite. `agent` on a test or describe block now takes a list, and the test runs once per agent named, one result each, in one run. - `--agent` takes several names, comma-separated or repeated. Unpinned tests fan out over them. A pinned list narrows to the names both give; a pin the flag misses stands whole, which is the old "never override a pin" rule with a pin of one, so `--agent thorough` still benchmarks a model across unpinned tests while every persona stays itself. - The agent is a result dimension beside test and target, not a title suffix: `agent` on every result and serial group, the result id digests `{ testId, targetId, agent }`, artifacts land under `///attempt-`, and `test-started`, `step`, and `run-started` (`agents`, replacing `agent`) carry it. Test ids stay stable, so a dashboard can follow one test per persona. - A serial group runs as one unit per agent and its members must share the group's pin (collection error otherwise). A setup test runs once per target and pins at most one agent, enforced by the types and at registration. - Signed-in personas still pair a pin with a `session`, one per describe block, so that sweep is a loop over describe blocks; the authentication page documents the setup test that saves one session per persona and the loop that consumes them. ```ts test.describe('checkout', { agent: ['buyer', 'admin'] }, () => { test('pays for one item', async ({ app, agent }) => { /* runs once per persona */ }); }); ``` ```bash e2e run --agent buyer,admin # every unpinned test once per agent e2e run --agent admin # the list above narrows to admin; unpinned tests run as admin ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR P{pin?} -- none --> R[run agents from --agent, else default] P -- list --> N[pin ∩ --agent] N -- empty --> W[whole pin] N -- some --> S[the intersection, in pin order] R & W & S --> X[one pair per agent × target] ``` Resolution lives in `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts` (`effectiveAgents`, `assertSerialAgentsAgree`); the pair identity every keyed structure uses is `pairKey` in `packages/e2e/src/run/units.ts`. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ` ✓ checkout > pays 80ms` (one result, whichever agent) | ` ✓ checkout > pays [buyer] 80ms`
` ✓ checkout > pays [admin] 80ms` | | `` | `` | The tag appears only when the agent is not `default`, so suites that never name one keep their terminal lines and JUnit case names. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Title and changeset done; no deprecation window (pre-1.0 beta, result ids and the `run-started.agent` field change in one step). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. Not an engine change. ---

title: feat(report): tally the trace cache under the AI row of the run summary
body: ## What and why - The `list` summary gets a `Cache` row under `AI`, so a run says at a glance how much the trace cache saved: `9 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed`. Until now the only trace of the cache in the terminal was the transient `Replaying` indicator in the live window. - Counted by agent step from the `cache` detail each step already records (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:97`): `self-finalized` is replayed, `agent-concluded` is handed off, `missed` is missed. A run with the cache off records no cache detail and prints no row. - Prompt-cache reads stay where they were, as `N% cached` inside the `AI` row. title: docs: split guides and references by platform
body:
## What and why

- Split the docs into Documentation and Reference tabs, with Web and Mobile groups. Model setup, personas, project tools, executors, caching, app processes, and debugging each have a focused guide.
- Keep old links usable. `/reference/app-web` retains its section anchors and points to the separate App and Playwright references. The device reference redirects to agent-device, and the config reference retains `#commit-your-traces`.

- Use GPT-5.6 Luna in the examples, consumer skill, and generated `e2e init` configs. Keep the quickstart code blocks synchronized with the typechecked files in `docs/examples/`.
- Deny `app.screenshot()` after a secret fill, before engine capture or artifact registration. Secure-field masking cannot cover secrets echoed elsewhere on screen. Regression tests cover static and provider-backed credentials, pre-fill screenshots, and providers that return no secret.

title: fix(cli): run and list match a bare file name, and reject a flag passed as a file
body:
## What and why

- `e2e run saved-tests.e2e.ts` in a project with `tests: ["tests/regression/**/*.e2e.ts"]` ended in `NO_TESTS`: a positional that named no existing path only matched the whole root-relative path (`packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts`, `positionalMatcher`).
- A positional that exists nowhere now selects the discovered files whose path equals it or ends with `/` + it, so `saved-tests.e2e.ts` and `regression/saved-tests.e2e.ts` both work; with no `/` and no `.` it matches the base name with every extension dropped, so `saved-tests` works too. Exact and case-sensitive like globs, never a mid-segment substring (`ests/a.e2e.ts` selects nothing), never a file the config globs did not discover. Existing paths and directories behave as before.
- The `NO_TESTS` did-you-mean also compares the positional against the discovered file names, so `smoek.e2e.ts` gets `did you mean smoke.e2e.ts?`.
- `pnpm test:e2e -- --headed` reaches the CLI as `run -- --headed`; commander handed `--headed` to `[files...]`, the run went on headless, and the flag surfaced only as `no test file matched --headed` when nothing else matched. The TesterArmy docs told people to write `pnpm -C packages/e2e-tests exec e2e run ...` to dodge this.
- The `run` and `list` actions now check the completed positional list before the runner starts (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`, `rejectForwardedFlags`): a value that starts with `-` and names no existing entry relative to the working directory is a usage error through `command.error`, so it prints once with `(add --help for usage)`, exits 2, and the runner is never called. The hint keeps the whole tail from that flag on (`--tag smoke tests/b.e2e.ts` stays together) and names the detected package manager's script and exec forms. A file that really starts with a dash (`-smoke.e2e.ts`) still passes through to collection.
- Docs: `docs/reference/cli.mdx` positional rules and the `--` paragraph, `skills/e2e/references/running.md`, the `[files...]` help text, one clause in the quickstart. Changeset: `@e2edev/e2e` patch.

## Before / after

`e2e list smoke.e2e.ts` in the testbed:

```text
# before
NO_TESTS: no test file matched smoke.e2e.ts; the config globs discovered tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts, tests/board.e2e.ts, tests/dashboard.e2e.ts and 6 more; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this
(exit 2)

# after
tests/smoke.e2e.ts › playground renders and navigates [web]
tests/smoke.e2e.ts › screenshots capture evidence [web]
(exit 0)
```

`e2e run -- --tag smoke tests/smoke.e2e.ts` (what `pnpm test:e2e -- --tag smoke tests/smoke.e2e.ts` sends):

```text
# before
the run starts with tests/smoke.e2e.ts selected and --tag silently dropped;
with no other match: NO_TESTS: no test file matched --tag, smoke; the config globs discovered ...

# after
error: "--tag" is a flag, not a test file. It arrived as a file because a "--" came before it; "pnpm test:e2e -- --tag smoke tests/smoke.e2e.ts" reaches e2e as "run -- --tag smoke tests/smoke.e2e.ts" when the package manager forwards the separator. Run the CLI directly instead: pnpm exec e2e run --tag smoke tests/smoke.e2e.ts
(add --help for usage)
(exit 2)
```

title: feat(expect): expect.poll re-reads a value until the matcher holds
body:
## What and why

- `expect.poll(read, options?)` re-reads a value until a value matcher holds: the asynchronous form of `expect(value)`, in Playwright's shape.
- An agent step returns once the model has observed the app, which can precede the write it triggered, so every agent journey in the TesterArmy dashboard suite wraps its database read in a hand-written `eventually()` loop. This replaces those loops.
- `PollExpectation<T>` is a mapped type over `ValueExpectation<T>`, and the runtime matcher list is pinned with `satisfies Record<MatcherName, true>` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/poll.ts`), so neither side can drift from the value matchers.
- Each sample calls `read`, then runs the synchronous matcher and treats its `ASSERTION_FAILED` as not yet. A `read` that throws is one failing sample; a `read` that hangs is raced against the deadline, the way locator matchers cannot outlive theirs.
- The poll runs on the attempt's budget. The runner publishes the running attempt (its `assertionTimeout` and `AttemptBudget`) in a realm slot on `globalThis` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/attempt.ts`) when the fixtures exist and clears it when the attempt ends; `expect.poll` defaults `timeout` to `assertionTimeout`, caps its deadline by the attempt deadline (the test timeout in the body, the hook's cleanup budget in `afterEach`), and threads the attempt signal through the sleep and the read race, so a timed-out test stops reading at once instead of polling through teardown. Outside an attempt (a standalone script) it falls back to 5000 ms with no signal. One attempt runs at a time per process; `publishAttempt` refuses a second live one rather than trusting that.
- `interval` defaults to 100 ms (`POLL_INTERVAL_MS`); `message` adds a line to the timeout error. A non-finite or negative `timeout`, or an `interval` that is not above 0, is `INVALID_CONFIG` when `expect.poll` is called, before the first read; either would otherwise poll forever.
- `ValueExpectation.toMatch` now goes through `testPattern`, which resets `lastIndex`, so a global or sticky RegExp answers the same for the same value on every sample; without it `.not.toMatch(/done/g)` passed on an unchanged value.
- The timeout is `ASSERTION_FAILED`, worded like the locator matchers: the matcher line, `message` when given, then `last:` with the last matcher failure, the last read error, or `no read completed`.
- Not recorded as a report step: it touches no fixture.
- `expect` is now `export const expect: Expect`, `Object.assign` over the unchanged three overloads. `Expect`, `PollOptions`, and `PollExpectation` are exported from the main entry.

```ts
await agent.act('create a test named "AI checkout regression" described as {description}', {
  params: { description },
});
await expect
  .poll(() => getTest(workspace).then((row) => row?.title), { timeout: 15_000 })
  .toBe('AI checkout regression');
await expect.poll(async () => (await listTests(workspace)).length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
await expect.poll(() => readStatus(), { message: 'the batch never finished' }).not.toBe('running');
```

```text
expect.poll(...).toBe(...) timed out after 5000 ms
the batch never finished
last: expected "running" to be "done"
```

title: feat(init): say where the suite belongs in a monorepo, and warn when a new directory falls outside the workspace
body:
## What and why

- A coding agent scaffolded the TesterArmy dashboard suite as `packages/e2e-tests`, a nested install root with its own lockfile and `packages: []`, excluded from the repo workspace; the suite imports the app's ORM by relative path into `apps/website/node_modules`, root `test` and `typecheck` skip it, and two lockfiles drift.
- Nothing in the docs said where a suite belongs, and `e2e init <dir>` creates a private manifest anywhere without comment.
- `docs/quickstart.mdx` gains a `### In a monorepo` subsection under Project notes: the default is the app's own package (`e2e init apps/web`), a separate package only when the app is not a Node package or needs different major versions of shared dependencies, and then as a workspace member, never a second install root.
- `docs/reference/cli.mdx` says the same in one sentence on the `[directory]` row; `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` gets a "Where the suite lives" paragraph, since the skill is what the agent read when it chose wrong.
- `e2e init` finds the nearest workspace at or above the directory (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages:` list read line by line, or a `package.json` `workspaces` array or `workspaces.packages`), matches the directory against the globs with the runner's own glob grammar, honoring `!` exclusions, and prints one message before the confirm prompt: an info line at the workspace root, a warning when no glob covers the directory. The messages are informational; the scaffold itself is unchanged.
- A directory that already is its own install root (its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `packages: []`, the layout that prompted this) is judged by the workspace enclosing it, so re-running init there prints the outside-the-workspace warning naming the enclosing root rather than calling the directory a workspace root; with no enclosing workspace it says nothing.
- Detection lives in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/workspace.ts` as pure parsers and a matcher over file contents plus one fs walk. Silence is the default whenever the verdict could be wrong: a workspace file that cannot be read, a `packages:` key with no sequence under it, or a glob using braces, character classes, or extglobs (legal for pnpm and npm, outside the runner's grammar) all yield no message.

Output of `e2e init packages/e2e-tests --yes` in a workspace whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists `apps/*`, `packages/*`, `!packages/e2e-tests`:

```text
┌  e2e init packages/e2e-tests
│
●  add dev dependencies: @e2edev/e2e@^0.11.0, @e2edev/playwright@^0.8.0, ai@^7.0.0
│
●  add scripts: test:e2e (e2e run)
│
▲  packages/e2e-tests is outside the workspace at /repo (pnpm-workspace.yaml lists packages: apps/*, packages/*, !packages/e2e-tests); an install here will not share its lockfile. Add a matching entry to pnpm-workspace.yaml, or run e2e init inside the app's package
│
◆  created package.json
```

And `e2e init --yes` at the workspace root:

```text
●  this is the workspace root (pnpm-workspace.yaml); the suite usually lives in the app's package, e.g. e2e init apps/<app>
```

`e2e init apps/web --yes` prints neither line.
