title: fix(run): a stalled command or service reports progress at half its budget and fails with its last log lines
body:
## What and why

- Refs #158: `docker compose up --detach --wait` stalls in roughly 3 of 11 runs on one machine and the report says only `service "compose" did not exit within 180000 ms`. The Docker-side cause is still unknown; this makes the stall visible while it happens and diagnosable from the report alone.
- When `log` is set, a launch that fails with `APP_UNREACHABLE` (exit before ready, non-zero exit on `waitForExit`, or `startupTimeout` expired) ends its message with the last 20 lines appended to the log since the process started, terminal controls stripped, at most 4 KB. The log's size is read from the descriptor right before the spawn (`packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`, `unreachable` and `outputSince`).
- The quote lands in the report, so every `command.env` value of 4 characters or more is replaced in the quoted lines by the same `createRedactor` the trace and report redaction use, keyed by variable name (`<secret:DATABASE_URL>`), encoded forms included; the log file itself stays raw, as documented.
- The header reads `output in <log> since <label> started:` rather than claiming the lines as this process's own: services that share one log file share the tail, and an earlier `readyUrl` service still running can append to it. The docs say so. Piping stdout through the runner for per-process attribution was considered and rejected: it changes what survives a runner crash and the fd contract the child gets today.
- A process that wrote nothing gets `no output in <log>`; a command without `log` gets `set log on this command to keep its output`. Spawn failures (the `error` event) and `openLog` failures are unchanged.
- Once the wait passes half of `startupTimeout`, and that half is at least 5 s, `hooks.notice` fires once: `<label> still starting after <n>s: waiting for <readyUrl> | waiting for it to exit; log: <path>`. Until it has fired, neither a readiness probe nor a poll sleep runs past the half mark, so the notice lands at the mark instead of up to 2 s after it. The runner already turns `hooks.notice` into a `notice` event that the `list` reporter prints (the `reuseExisting is ignored in CI` line takes the same path), so no new hook.
- The error code stays `APP_UNREACHABLE`. Tests pin the exact tail for a readiness timeout, an early exit, and a `waitForExit` stall, the redaction, the two hints, the 20-line cap, and the notice at exactly half of a 10 s budget on a fake clock with a real child.

## Before / after

Before, with `log: '.e2e/logs/services.log'` on the compose service:

```
APP_UNREACHABLE: service "compose" did not exit within 180000 ms
```

After, the same stall, with one notice printed at 90 s while it stalls:

```
ℹ service "compose" still starting after 90s: waiting for it to exit; log: .e2e/logs/services.log
```

```
APP_UNREACHABLE: service "compose" did not exit within 180000 ms
output in .e2e/logs/services.log since service "compose" started:
   Network testerarmy-e2e_default Removed
   Image postgres:16.4-alpine Pulling
   Image redis:7-alpine Pulling
```

Without `log`:

```
APP_UNREACHABLE: service "compose" did not exit within 180000 ms
set log on this command to keep its output
```

title: feat(test): test.extend defines your own fixtures with setup and teardown
body:
## What and why

- `test.extend()` was type-only; a project that needed a per-test resource (a seeded workspace, a signed-in session) wrapped `test()` by hand and re-spread every base fixture.
- `test.extend(fixtures)` now takes Playwright-shaped definitions: everything before `await use(value)` is setup, `value` is what the test gets, everything after is teardown, run whether or not the body passed.
- `extend` returns a new `TestAPI` carrying the accumulated chain (parent's definitions first); every registration through it (`test`, `.skip`, `.only`, `.setup`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`) records the chain on the `RegisteredTest` / hook. The shared `test` is never mutated.
- Rule per attempt: the fixture set is the test's own chain; hooks receive the same fixture object as the body, whichever `test` they were registered through.
- Values land on the attempt's fixture object as own read-only properties (`packages/e2e/src/run/extended-fixtures.ts`), so the base accessors stay lazy and the unknown-fixture gate keeps rejecting names nobody defined. The engine-collision check is `Object.hasOwn`, so a fixture named `toString` is allowed.
- A setup the attempt timed out under is abandoned, not cancelled. Taking the teardowns marks the chain abandoned; a definition that reaches `use()` after that gets an immediately resolved `use` and no property, so the code after it (its teardown) still runs, detached from the run.
- Setup runs under the test deadline in phase `beforeEach`; each teardown runs after the `afterEach` hooks, last set up first, with its own `cleanupTimeout` budget and the same primary/secondary error rule as an `afterEach` hook. `runHook` takes a label so a timeout names the fixture.
- Fails: at import (`COLLECTION_ERROR`) for a non-plain-object, a non-function, an empty name, a core name, or a name an earlier `extend` defined; at the attempt (`TEST_SETUP_FAILED`, existing code) for a name the engine contributes, a definition that never calls `use()`, or one that calls it twice. No new error code; the report schema and `ErrorPhase` are unchanged.
- The zero-argument `test.extend<Extra>()` still returns the same object and types an engine's contributed fixtures.

```ts
import { test as base } from '@e2edev/playwright';

export const test = base.extend<{ workspace: Workspace }>({
  workspace: async ({ web }, use) => {
    const workspace = await createWorkspace();
    await signIn(web, workspace);
    await use(workspace); // hooks and body run here
    await workspace.cleanup(); // runs after the body, failed or not
  },
});

test('renames the workspace', async ({ workspace, screen }) => { ... });
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[engine fixtures] --> B[fixture setups, in order]
  B --> C[beforeEach hooks]
  C --> D[body]
  D --> E[afterEach hooks]
  E --> F[fixture teardowns, reverse order]
```

Types: `FixtureFn<Fixtures, Value>` and `FixtureDefinitions<Base, Extra>` are exported. Each definition is typed against `Base` only, so a fixture that needs another fixture goes in a chained `extend()` (the runtime defines values in order, but the type does not promise siblings). A key already in `Base` maps to `never`, so redefining `agent` (or `web` on the Playwright `test`) is a type error before it is a runtime one.

title: feat(playwright)!: playwright is a peer dependency, so an app keeps one copy and one browser cache
body: ## What and why - `@e2edev/playwright` declares `playwright` as a peer dependency, `>=1.63.0 <2`, and no longer installs it; the `1.63.0` pin moves to the engine's `devDependencies` for its own build and tests. - An app that already ships Playwright for its product (TesterArmy's website depends on `playwright 1.59.0-alpha`) got a second copy, a second browser revision to download, and an ambiguous `playwright install`; that is one reason its e2e suite lives in a separate install root. - The floor is 1.63 because `basicAuth` maps to the per-origin `httpCredentials` array that `browser.newContext` accepts since 1.63 ([release notes](https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes#version-163)); the next newest APIs the engine uses are `page.screencast` (1.59) and `storageState({ indexedDB })` (1.51). Everything else it touches (`connectOverCDP`, `selectors.setTestIdAttribute`, `context.route`, `tracing`, dialogs, downloads, `frameLocator`) predates those. - `e2e init` writes `playwright` next to `@e2edev/playwright`, at `^`; the `@e2edev/e2e` build records it in `dist/cli/init/engine-versions.json` from `packages/playwright/package.json`, and a source run falls back to `^1`. A project that already declares `playwright` keeps its version, since `addDependencies` skips declared names (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/package.ts:46`). - Browser provisioning resolves `playwright/package.json` with `createRequire(import.meta.url)` from the engine (`packages/playwright/src/install.ts:31`); under pnpm the peer resolves through the importer's `node_modules`, which the engine and runner lifecycle integration tests exercise. - Workspace consumers of the engine (`@e2edev/e2e`, testbed, web-benchmark, docs) carry `playwright 1.63.0` in `devDependencies`; pnpm reports no unmet peer, with `--strict-peer-dependencies` too. - Docs: the quickstart, `reference/app-web`, the engine README, the root README, and the skill's `setup` reference show the install line and a "Bring your own Playwright" paragraph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before A1[app] --> P1[playwright 1.59] A1 --> E1["@e2edev/playwright"] --> P2[playwright 1.63, pinned] end subgraph after A2[app] --> P3[playwright >=1.63] A2 --> E2["@e2edev/playwright"] -. peer .-> P3 end ``` Migration: `npm install --save-dev playwright` (1.63 or newer) in a project that does not already depend on it. A project scaffolded with `e2e init` from this release onward needs nothing. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). No deprecation window: the packages are `0.x`, where a minor is the breaking release, and a peer declaration has no runtime form to warn from. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. Not applicable: no exported type, schema, or wire format changes. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. Not applicable: the engine contract is untouched. ---

title: feat(app): url port 0 allocates a free loopback port for the run; {port} reaches the app command
body:
## What and why - A `url` on a literal loopback address with port `0` (`http://127.0.0.1:0`, `http://[::1]:0`) asks the run for a free TCP port. Port `0` on any other host is `INVALID_APP_URL`, `localhost` included: the name may resolve to `::1` while the command binds `127.0.0.1`, and a port free on one family says nothing about the other, so the URL must name the address the command will bind. - The runner picks the port once, in the main process, right after the config loads and before anything spawns (`packages/e2e/src/run/app-ports.ts`, called from `run()` in `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`); every port is held until all are chosen, so two targets never get the same one. - The port replaces the `0` in the resolved base URL, the default `allowedOrigins` entry (and an explicit entry spelled with the same host and `:0`), the default `readyUrl`, and the report's `baseOrigin`. - The default cache and session `identity` derives from the declared URL with `:0`, so trace cache entries do not churn with the port. - `{port}` in the command's `args` and `env`, in `readyUrl`, and in each service's `args`, `env`, `readyUrl`, and `teardown` expands to the port of the target's URL, allocated or fixed; the command must take the port through it. On a target without a `url` the token is `INVALID_CONFIG` naming the field. Expansion happens once, in `resolveTargetApp`, so `declared-processes.ts` dedupes on final values. - Workers re-resolve the config from the file, so the assignments travel in `WorkerBootstrap.ports` and go into `resolveConfig(raw, { ports })`; the digest covers the raw config only, so `CONFIG_NOT_DETERMINISTIC` stays quiet. The `e2e mcp` session allocates the same way when it opens. - Residual race, documented rather than closed: the port is free when chosen and handed to the command a moment later. Another process binding it in between fails the app's start with the usual `APP_UNREACHABLE`, which a retry of the run resolves. Passing the reserved socket to the child would need the app's cooperation and is out of scope. - Tests read the resolved URL from the new `app.baseUrl` (`undefined` on a surface without a `url`). Nothing else was added to `App`. - Scope is the app URL only: services keep whatever ports the config gives them and learn the app's through `{port}`. The TesterArmy dashboard suite can drop its hand-rolled `E2E_PORT_OFFSET` for the app once it moves to this. ```ts engine: playwright({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev', '--port', '{port}'], env: { PORT: '{port}' } }, }), ``` ```ts test('lands on the allocated origin', async ({ app, web }) => { await app.open('/'); expect(await web.url()).toBe(app.baseUrl); }); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A["loadRunConfig"] --> B["resolveConfig
base http://127.0.0.1:0"] B --> C["allocateAppPorts
listen 0 on the address, once per target"] C --> D["assignPorts
resolveTargetApp with the port"] D --> E["startDeclaredProcesses
command args and env, #123;port#125; expanded"] D --> F["WorkerBootstrap.ports"] F --> G["worker resolveConfig with ports
same digest, same URLs"] D --> H["app.baseUrl and report baseOrigin"] ``` Pending state: a config resolved outside a run (`e2e list`, `e2e cache`) keeps the `:0` URL and `ResolvedApp.portRequest.port` is `undefined`; `{port}` then expands to `0`, the same port the base URL still carries, so validation reads the same before and after assignment. Docs: `reference/config` gains a Free ports section under the app declaration and the `{port}` notes in the command and services tables; `starting-your-app` gets "Let the runner pick the port" with the sample; `reference/app` documents `baseUrl`; the skill mirrors the sample. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. Not applicable: `EngineAppDeclaration` is type-identical, only its doc comment grew.

title: feat(explore): the terminal shows the exploration step by step, each finding as it is reported, and a Findings section with the evidence
body: ## What and why - The old explore output was a test's output with four rows bolted under the summary: issue titles printed three times (glance line, `Failed Tests`, explore rows) while expected, actual, reproduction, and screenshot printed zero times. Planner calls showed as passed `agent.extract` steps, charters showed as clipped paragraphs, and a finding appeared live as `report_finding (172ms)`. - The exploration's progress now travels as an `explore` run event (`started`, `planning`, `step-started`, `step-finished`, `finding`, `finished`), emitted by `ExploreState` through the runner. Custom reporters get it on the same spine as everything else. - A new `report/list-explore.ts` view renders those events inside the list reporter. Live: the goal with a clock, finished steps by title (`✓ 1 Cart quantities 19s · 4 actions · 3 findings`), the running step's calls with findings interleaved, a `planning step N of M` row. Non-TTY: the same lines stream as they happen. End: the record, a `Findings` banner, one block per finding (grade, title, path and step, expected, actual, numbered steps, `evidence` screenshot path), the assessment, and `Findings` and `Steps` rows in place of `Test Files` and `Tests`. - The synthetic test's file block and `Failed Tests` entry are gone when the failure is the verdict (`ASSERTION_FAILED` with issues); a provider error or a run that explored nothing still prints as a failure. `explore/reporter.ts` is deleted. - Severity reads as a word: critical, high, medium, low, trivial. The finding tool saves its screenshot before recording, so the finding event carries the artifact id. - Prompts: step titles are two to five word headings; the assessment gives a verdict, names what was not reached, and says what to script, without restating the findings (they print above it). Finding fields ask for one sentence each and short imperative steps. - Testbed explore config used a string model, which the config now rejects; it uses `gateway()`. Validated live on the bug garden: gemini-3.6-flash 7 issues in 95 s for $0.12; luna-fast 9 to 11 issues plus 1 to 2 warnings in 135 to 176 s for $0.05. Before: ```text Explored 3 steps (3 passed); ended: the agent covered the goal Findings 8 issues, 1 warning S4 issue Negative stock quantity (-3) displayed for Neuromancer (/catalog) S4 issue Cart total fails to update after increasing item quantity (/cart) S1 warning Misspelling 'Recieve' in newsletter checkbox label on checkout page (/checkout) Assessment Explored all core areas of the Bookshelf web application, including catalog browsing, cart... ``` After (CI log, luna-fast): ```text ❯ web Exploring Explore this bookshop like a careful first-time buyer: browse the catalog, ... ⚑ medium issue Home greeting exposes an unresolved userName template (/) ⚑ high issue Neuromancer shows an impossible negative stock availability (/catalog) ✓ 1 Catalog browsing 31.46s · 7 actions · 4 findings ⚑ high issue Cart total does not update when Hyperion quantity increases (/cart) ✓ 2 Cart quantities and removal 19.47s · 4 actions · 3 findings ended: the agent covered the goal ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Findings 13 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ 1. high issue Cart total does not update when Hyperion quantity increases /cart · step 2 expected Increasing Hyperion from 1 to 2 should change the cart total from $25.25 to $39.25, matching $28.00 plus Solaris at $11.25. actual The screen shows Hyperion quantity 2 and line total $28.00, but the Cart total still reads "$25.25". steps 1. Open the cart with Hyperion and Solaris each at quantity 1. 2. Click the "+" button labeled "Increase Hyperion quantity" once. evidence .e2e/artifacts/web/explore__Explore_20this.../attempt-0/finding-5.png Assessment The exploration goal was covered: the catalog, cart, checkout, Account, Orders, and Sign in flows were exercised, including a successful order. The non-first Orders entry did not open a detail view. The cart quantity and removal flow is the highest-value flow to turn into a scripted test. Findings 11 issues | 2 warnings Steps 6 of 8 · 6 passed · the agent covered the goal ``` Left out on purpose: artifact directories derive from the test title, so explore evidence paths stay long; a short segment for explore is a separate change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(collect): a test declared through a helper reports the helper call in the test file as its source, never a runner or node_modules frame
body:
## What and why - The GitHub comment on tester-army/app linked every row's source to `node_modules/.pnpm/@e2edev+e2e@0.10.0_.../@e2edev/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts:328`; the CI `report.json` shows all 102 results carry that source, the passed list just prints `result.file` instead. - Two copies of the runner are on the stack during collection: the CLI's own instance (unmapped `dist/` frames) and the instance the test module imports through the tsx realm, whose `test()` frame Node source-maps to `src/collect/registry.ts` via the shipped `.js.map`. The 0.10.0 tarball on npm predates the `RUNNER_ROOTS` filter from #254 (its `registerTest` sits at line 328, matching 658b9c22), so that frame won. - With #254 alone, every TesterArmy test would instead point at the same line inside `support/test.ts`, because all of them go through a `dashboardTest()` helper and the first non-runner frame is the helper. - Now `collectModule` receives the file being collected and the source is the innermost frame in that file. Without one (the file imports a module that declares the tests), the innermost frame outside the runner and outside `node_modules` stands, so an installed package's frame can never be a test's source. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["new Error().stack"] --> B{frame under runner
src/ or dist/, or node:?} B -- yes --> A B -- no --> C{in the collected file?} C -- yes --> D[source] C -- no --> E{under node_modules?} E -- no --> F[remember first, keep walking] E -- yes --> A F --> A ``` | Declared as | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `test('…')` in `tests/direct.e2e.ts` | `tests/direct.e2e.ts:3` | `tests/direct.e2e.ts:3` | | `dashboardTest('…')` in `tests/wrapped.e2e.ts`, helper in `support/test.ts` | `support/test.ts:4` (0.10.0: `node_modules/.pnpm/…/registry.ts:328`) | `tests/wrapped.e2e.ts:3` | | `test('…')` in `tests/shared/declarations.ts`, imported by a test file | `tests/shared/declarations.ts:3` | `tests/shared/declarations.ts:3` | Verified against the built package installed through pnpm on macOS (Node 26, Playwright engine) and Linux (Node 22, `pnpm exec e2e run`). `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts` `captureSource`; call sites in `collect.ts`, `run/realm.ts`, `run/worker/entry.ts`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent-device)!: agent-device is a peer dependency, so a project keeps one copy and one CLI
body:
## What and why

- `@e2edev/agent-device` declares `agent-device` as a peer dependency, `0.21.x`, and no longer installs it; the `0.21.1` pin moves to the engine's `devDependencies` for its own build and tests.
- A project that already drives devices with the agent-device CLI (`npx agent-device doctor`, per the setup docs) got a second, pinned copy that could drift from the CLI it ran; now it keeps its version and one copy in `node_modules`. Same shape as the Playwright engine (#272).
- The range pins one minor line, unlike Playwright's `>=1.63.0 <2`: agent-device is 0.x and its minors break (confirmed with the maintainer: 0.20 -> 0.21 changed the API), and the engine couples to the client factory and its session semantics, the `normalizeAgentDeviceError` translation table, and the `agent-device/selectors` subpath grammar. Each agent-device minor moves the range with an engine release, the cadence the pin bumps already follow.
- `e2e init` writes `agent-device` next to `@e2edev/agent-device`, at the `<major>.<minor>.x` line the engine was built against; the `@e2edev/e2e` build records it in `dist/cli/init/engine-versions.json` from `packages/agent-device/package.json`, and a source run falls back to `0.x`. A project that already declares `agent-device` keeps its version, since `addDependencies` skips declared names (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/package.ts:46`).
- The testbed carries `agent-device 0.21.0` in `devDependencies` (it rode the engine's dependency before); the cli-init integration test links the peer the same way it links `ai`.
- Docs: a "Bring your own agent-device" paragraph in `reference/agent-device`, and the peer requirement in the skill's `setup` reference.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before
    A1[project] --> C1[agent-device CLI]
    A1 --> E1["@e2edev/agent-device"] --> C2[agent-device 0.21.0, pinned]
  end
  subgraph after
    A2[project] --> C3["agent-device 0.21.x"]
    A2 --> E2["@e2edev/agent-device"] -. peer .-> C3
  end
```

Migration: `npm install --save-dev agent-device` in a project that does not already depend on it. A project scaffolded with `e2e init` from this release onward needs nothing.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). No deprecation window: the packages are `0.x`, where a minor is the breaking release, and a peer declaration has no runtime form to warn from.
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. Not applicable: no exported type, schema, or wire format changes.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. Not applicable: the engine contract is untouched.

title: docs(cache): explain what a recording is, what must match, when it is written, and why a step was not replayed
body: ## What and why - `docs/cache.mdx` mixed the write rules, the replay rules, and the modes into one flow and never answered "why did this step miss". Rewritten from a pass over `packages/e2e/src/cache/*`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/replay.ts`, and `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`. - New shape: the `Cache` summary row and its three words, a four-step replay walkthrough, the key in plain words and what is not in it (the model, the rest of the config), which steps confirm a recording, every `step.cache.reason` with a cause and a fix, a real `trace-1` entry, then modes, committing, inspection, and a note separating it from the provider prompt cache. - Facts the old page missed: `expect.poll` and a plain-value `expect` are not recorded steps and never confirm a recording (`packages/e2e/src/expect/poll.ts` opens no step; confirmation is `verifies` at `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:185`), and neither does `agent.extract`. A test id is `::`, so `e2e cache ls` prints `signs%20up`; the sample in `docs/reference/cli.mdx` showed a space. - `docs/reference/reporters.mdx` pointed at a "config digest" as part of the trace cache; the key (`packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts`) never held it. `skills/e2e/references/agent.md` cache bullets now name the verifying steps and where the miss reason lives. The page's decision path, as it now reads: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[agent.act] --> B{entry for this key?} B -- no --> M[missed: agent runs live] B -- yes --> C{on the recorded start path?} C -- no --> M C -- yes --> D[replay actions] D -- control missing or ambiguous, action failed, tool gap --> H[handed off: agent continues] D -- all ran --> E{end path and anchors back?} E -- no --> H E -- yes --> P[replayed: 0 model calls] P --> W{verification step passed after it?} H --> W M --> W W -- yes --> S[entry written] W -- no --> X[entry deleted] ``` | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Sections | When a step is recorded, When a replay hands off, Cache-friendly tests, Modes, Commit your traces, Inspect the cache | How a replay works, What must match, When a recording is written, Why a step was not replayed, What a recording holds, Modes, Commit your traces, Inspect the cache | | Miss and hand-off reasons | named in passing | one table row each, with what to do | | Sample entry | none | a real one, recorded through the fixture app with a scripted executor and no model | | Words | 970 | 1714 | The sample entry was recorded through the real code path: first run `missed / no-entry`, second run `self-finalized` with 3 of 3 actions and zero model calls. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(config)!: secrets declares API keys, tokens, any value the model never sees
body: ## What and why - The only way to make a `Secret` was the `credentials` block, so the landing page's "Secrets the model never sees" covered passwords only. An API key a test pastes into a form went in as a plain string the model read. - A `secrets` block declares any named value: a string, a provider function, or `{ value, allowedOrigins }`. `E2E_SECRET_` overrides an entry per run, the same rule as `E2E_USER_*`. - `secrets.get(name)` from `@e2edev/e2e` returns the same opaque `Secret` a credential's password is. `locator.fill`, `agent.act` params, and the `type_secret` tool accept it unchanged. - One namespace: a credential's password is registered as the secret of the credential's name, so traces, the cache, and the ledger keep keying on the names they already use. A name under both blocks is `INVALID_CONFIG`. - Fill policy follows purpose. A `password` still fills only a password field. A `generic-secret` fills any editable input; the page shows it, so the ledger redacts it by name from every observation, action result, transcript, trace, and report, and the screenshot taint still applies. - New `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE` code for an unconfigured secret. `Secret.purpose` narrows to `'password' | 'generic-secret'`; nothing ever produced `'one-time-code'`. - MCP `type_secret` lists every configured secret, not just passwords. Explore still carries accounts only. ```ts // e2e.config.ts secrets: { 'stripe-key': process.env.STRIPE_TEST_KEY ?? '', 'webhook-token': { value: process.env.WEBHOOK_TOKEN ?? '', allowedOrigins: ['https://app.staging.example.com'] }, totp: () => generateCode(), }, ``` ```ts import { secrets } from '@e2edev/e2e'; await screen.getByLabel('Secret key').fill(secrets.get('stripe-key')); await agent.act('connect Stripe with the given key', { params: { apiKey: secrets.get('stripe-key') } }); ``` Where the value goes in the agentic form: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["act params: Secret handle"] -->|validateParams| B["model sees {kind:'secret', name, purpose}"] B -->|type_secret name| C{declared in step?\norigin allowed?\neditable input?\npassword field if password?} C -- no --> D[POLICY_DENIED] C -- yes --> E["resolve plaintext on host"] E --> F["engine fill"] F --> G["ledger redacts value by name\nin every observation, trace, report"] F --> H["taint: screenshot and tap_at withheld"] ``` - Resolver: `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts` (`resolveSecrets`, one map for both blocks, digest records names only). - Handles: `packages/e2e/src/secrets.ts` (renamed from `credentials.ts`; `credentials`, `secrets`, `setSecretRegistry(config)`). - Fill authorization: `packages/e2e/src/agent/secrets.ts` (purpose check is now `password` needs a password field). - Docs: new "Secrets that are not passwords" section in `docs/authentication.mdx` with the value path and the exact-match redaction limit; `secrets` in the config and environment references; landing bullet. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: perf(agent-device): settle actions in 150 ms by default, configurable per engine
body: ## Why Profiling a React Native suite showed reads are cheap and actions are not: `expect` steps take about 60 ms, every `tap` 1.1 to 4.8 s. The engine sends each tap, fill, and back with `settle: true`, and agent-device then re-snapshots until the tree has held still for its default 500 ms. Raw CLI timings on the same screen: | Command | Time | | --- | --- | | `snapshot` | 190 ms | | `press` without settle | 600 ms | | `press --settle` (500 ms quiet) | 1600 ms | | `press --settle --settle-quiet 150` | 1100 ms | | `press --settle --settle-quiet 0` | 785 ms | An alert tap paid 2.1 s and a screen push 2.8 to 4.8 s because the animation kept the tree changing through the window. With 8 to 12 taps per test, settle was roughly half of every test. ## What - New `agentDevice({ settle })` option: milliseconds the UI must hold still after an action, default **150**, `false` to skip the wait. Validated as a non-negative integer. - All ten action sites in `surface.ts` and the `device.back()` fixture read one `settleOptions` value instead of a hard-coded `settle: true`. - Rationale in the option doc: the runner already polls (`expect`, actions waiting for their node), so the wait only needs to keep the following observation off a transition frame, and every frame of a running animation changes the tree, so 150 ms still catches one in flight. - Docs: `reference/agent-device.mdx`, package README, skill `setup.md`. Changeset: minor. - Tests: default window on every action, custom window, `false` omits `settle`, validation. ## Verification - agent-device unit tests: 82 passing. `pnpm lint` clean. Dead-code: the two pre-existing members. - react-native-pager-view suite (11 tests, iPhone 17 Pro, release build), this branch's dist installed: | | Before (500 ms) | After (150 ms) | | --- | --- | --- | | Full suite | 190 s | 142 s, 142 s (two runs) | | Two-test sample | 29.1 s | 17.1 s | | Typical tap | 1.1 to 2.1 s | about 0.8 s | All 11 tests passed in both runs. No locator or assertion had to change. ---

title: docs: e2e is agentic testing first; quickstart for web and mobile; icons everywhere
body: ## What and why - The landing page, README, skill, and guides framed agent steps as an opt-in layer over deterministic tests and told CI to keep them off required checks. That contradicts the premise. Now: agents drive the flow, `expect` pins the outcome, exact values go through `screen`, and the trace cache replays passing steps so a suite pays for thinking once per UI change. - The CI page shows one job, with the model key in its env, that gates every pull request. "Keep model-backed tests opt-in" is replaced by what makes agent steps hold as a required check: commit the cache, small explicit goals, a recorded check after every `act`, CI retries once and reports flaky. - The agents guide and the skill's `agent` topic gain "Make the agent yours": the ladder from goal wording to `context`, `system`, tools, model options, executors, and `--agent` comparisons. The skill's writing-tests example now leads with agent steps. - The quickstart assumed a browser. It now runs one shared init/install/run flow with Web and Mobile tabs where the scaffold differs. Mobile snippets are mirrored from the init templates and checked by the examples sync script. The run transcript is a real 0.12.0 run. - Scaffold config and example test carry one comment each instead of five; the init test follows. - Every card and sidebar group has a Font Awesome icon, keyed by destination page. - "plain language" is "natural language" everywhere. Landing tagline: "Agentic end-to-end testing framework for any app." | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Tagline | End-to-end tests in plain TypeScript, with agent steps you can bound and inspect. | Agentic end-to-end testing framework for any app. | | Skill workflow, step 3 | Deterministic steps first. One `agent.act` per goal where the flow varies. | Drive the flow with `agent.act`, one goal per call, and pin each outcome with `expect`. Exact values go through `screen`. | | CI | Separate `e2e.agent.config.ts`, `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch`, never a required check. | One job on `pull_request`, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in its env, committed cache replays in CI. | | Quickstart | Web only; mobile is a pointer in Notes. | Shared steps, Web/Mobile tabs at scaffold and agent step. | ```yaml - name: Run e2e run: npx e2e run --reporter list,junit env: APP_URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000 AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }} ``` Left as is: the cache guide and the `init` hint still call committing `.e2e/cache/` opt-in, because `init` gitignores it today. The skill and CI page now tell users to commit it, so flipping that default is the follow-up product change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: perf(agent-device): deterministic steps act at once; settle is for the agent
body: Stacked on #281 (base is `oskar/settle-window`; retargets to `main` when that merges). ## Why #281 shortened the settle window every action paid. This asks the better question: why does a deterministic step settle at all? It verifies its outcome with `expect`, which polls. The only real hazard is tapping a control that is still sliding in: agent-device taps by coordinates read from the tree, and the tree reports the **model layer**, so a modal's button shows its final frame from the first animation frame while the view is still travelling. Sampled during a modal presentation: the submit button's rect was final at 23 ms and never changed; `hittable` is not reported. Screenshots as a stillness signal cost 340 ms each and static frames are not byte-identical, so that is out too. The one signal the engine already has for free: whether the control existed at the same place before the last action. ## What - **Core:** `OperationContext.origin?: 'test' | 'agent'`. The locator engine marks its calls `test`, the agent loop (`boundedOperation`) marks its `agent`. Absent means agent. Documented in `reference/engine.mdx`; changeset minor. - **agent-device:** - Actions with `origin: 'test'` carry no settle. `settle` now applies to agent actions only. - New `transition` option (default 500 ms): a control that appeared or moved with the previous action waits out the remainder of the budget, counted from that action's return; a control already in place in the snapshot the previous action was resolved from is acted on immediately. No snapshot or screenshot is taken for this. - `back` and `tapAt` follow the same rule. - Docs and README rows for `transition`, skill note updated, changeset minor. - Tests: immediate action on a pre-existing control, budget on a new control and on a moved control, no budget once elapsed, agent path unchanged, option validation, and the locator engine marking `test`. ## Verification react-native-pager-view suite, 11 tests, one iPhone 17 Pro simulator, release build: | Engine behaviour | Result | Duration | | --- | --- | --- | | 500 ms settle after every action (0.6.0) | 11/11 | 190 s | | 150 ms settle (#281) | 11/11 | 142 s | | no settle at all (experiment) | 10/11, modal case fails | 124 s | | this PR | 11/11, three runs | 116 s, 119 s, 118 s | Taps average 673 ms against agent-device's roughly 600 ms XCTest floor; `expect` steps average 215 ms because the waiting moved into them. An agentic test (`pagination-dots`) still passes on the settle path. Unit: agent-device 87, core 1236; lint and dead-code clean. ---

title: feat(report): a markdown reporter writes the run as summary.md, with an exploration's findings, and the GitHub comment renders from it
body:
- The pull request comment renderer moves from `@e2edev/github` into core as `renderMarkdownReport(report, options)` (`packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts`) and is laid out for a pull request instead of a failure table. `@e2edev/github` renders its comment from it and bumps its peer range to `@e2edev/e2e >=0.13.0 <1`; its `renderComment`, `CommentOptions`, and `MAX_*` exports are gone, since nothing consumed them. - New built-in reporter id `markdown`: writes the page to `.e2e/summary.md` beside `report.json`, the way `junit` writes `junit.xml`. Evidence is listed as paths from the project root, so a reader with the checkout, a coding agent in particular, pastes the result instead of retelling it. - The page reads what the report already holds and the old comment never used: agent steps, cache replays, model calls, tokens, cached share, cost on a spend line; per failure, the step it went wrong at, the agent's own explanation of what it saw, and the attempt's step timeline; one row per test file, worst first; every test folded under it, grouped by file. - An `e2e explore` run renders its record instead: goal, steps, each finding with expected, actual, reproduction and screenshot, then the assessment. The exploration's own failed result is the verdict the findings express and gets no block; any other failure (a provider error) still does. - `e2e init` ignores `.e2e/summary.md`. Docs: CLI output table, reporters, config, github (new sample), explore, coding-agents; skill references updated. Before: `### 🟢 e2e: 78 passed` followed by 78 flat lines, and a single table of tests that did not pass with the error message in a cell. After, the same run: ```markdown ### 🔴 e2e: 1 failed, 1 flaky, 2 passed, 1 skipped 3 agent steps · 1 replayed from cache · 17 model calls · 128k tokens (62% cached) · $0.31 **🔴 tests/members.e2e.ts › members › an email invitation is accepted by the invited account only** **ASSERTION_FAILED** expected heading "Welcome, Ada" to be visible Step 4 of 6, `agent.act` "Accept the invitation from the email", failed after 12 model calls in 38.0s: "The Accept button opened a page that still shows Sign in." Steps: ✓ open / › ✓ Sign in as the owner › ✓ tap Send invitation › ✗ Accept the invitation from the email › 2 not run Evidence: [screenshot, video, trace](…/actions/runs/9) · [tests/members.e2e.ts:41](…/blob/abc/tests/members.e2e.ts#L41) **⚠️ tests/todos.e2e.ts › todos survive a filter round-trip** Passed after 1 failed attempt; the last one hit **STEP_TIMEOUT** slow. Evidence: [screenshot](…/actions/runs/9) · [tests/todos.e2e.ts:3](…) | | File | Tests | Agent | Time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 🔴 | tests/members.e2e.ts | 1 failed | 2 steps · 16 calls | 1.2s | | ⚠️ | tests/todos.e2e.ts | 1 flaky, 1 skipped | | 6.4s | | 🟢 | tests/smoke.e2e.ts | 2 passed | 1 step · 1 call | 3.0s |
All 5 tests **tests/members.e2e.ts** - 🔴 members › an email invitation is accepted by the invited account only (1.2s) **tests/todos.e2e.ts** - ⚠️ todos survive a filter round-trip (6.4s, 1 failed attempt first) - ⏭️ not ready yet (skipped: waiting on the API) **tests/smoke.e2e.ts** - 🟢 opens the app (850ms) - 🟢 dashboard › opens directly (2.1s)
Screenshots, traces, and recordings: [run artifacts](…/actions/runs/9). e2e 0.9.0 · 8.4s · 1 target (web) ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR R[report-1 document] --> M[renderMarkdownReport] M --> S[.e2e/summary.md
markdown reporter, artifactsDir] M --> C[pull request comment
@e2edev/github, artifactsUrl + marker] ``` Size discipline is unchanged: thirty failure blocks at most, then how many more; two hundred file rows; the folded list goes first when the body nears GitHub's limit. Why now: a coding agent that runs e2e inside a review or a factory stage has only `report.json` to hand off, and a model summarizing a report in its own words is how false passes get laundered.

title: feat(explore): --baseline tells this run's findings apart from an earlier report: known, new, and not seen
body: - `e2e explore --baseline ` reads the findings of an earlier exploration and labels each of this run's findings `known` (reads like one the baseline holds) or `new`. Baseline findings nothing matched are recorded as not seen. `packages/e2e/src/explore/baseline.ts`. - Matching is word overlap, no model: Jaccard over title tokens at 0.6 plus Jaccard over expected-and-actual tokens at 0.4, stop words dropped, identical titles score 1, threshold 0.45. Each baseline finding is claimed at most once, by the first arrival that reads like it. Same two reports, same labels, every run. - The verdict does not change. Any issue still fails the run, baseline or not. The labels are a reading aid for whoever compares a branch with its base or a release with the last; what to do with them is the caller's call. - Report: `run.explore.baseline` (`source`, `goal`, `findings`, `known`, `new`, `notSeen[]`) and `novelty` plus `baselineFindingId` on each finding, additive in `schema/report-v1.schema.json`. A file that is not the `report.json` of an explore run is `INVALID_BASELINE` before anything starts. - Terminal: each finding is tagged as it is reported, the `Findings` section carries the tag, a `Not seen since the baseline` list follows it, and the summary gains a `Baseline` row. ```mermaid flowchart LR B[base checkout] --> E1[e2e explore] --> R1[report.json] H[head checkout] --> E2[e2e explore --baseline report.json] R1 --> E2 E2 --> K[known] E2 --> N[new] E2 --> S[not seen] ``` ```text ⚑ medium issue Counter starts at 0 with no label of what it counts (/) known ⚑ medium issue Increment has no keyboard shortcut (/) new ✓ 1 Counter 0.40s · 1 action · 2 findings Not seen since the baseline baseline-report.json trivial warning Footer misspells Receive Findings 2 issues Baseline 1 new · 1 known · 1 not seen · baseline-report.json ``` Docs: a `Comparing with a baseline` section in `/explore`, the flag in the CLI reference, the error code, and the skill's explore reference. The markdown page from #284 does not render the labels yet; that follows once both land. ---

title: perf(agent): replayed trace actions carry the test origin
body: Stacked on #283 (base `oskar/action-guard`; retargets when that merges). ## Why A trace replay executes recorded actions with no model reading the screen after them. The only thing that looks is the replay's own relocation, and it polls with its own backoff. So a replayed action is a deterministic step from the engine's point of view, yet it went out as `origin: 'agent'` and paid the settle wait after every action. ## What - `StepAccounting.replaying(active)`: the cache session's existing `replaying` hook (already used to mark the report) now also flips the accounting, and `actionOperation()` stamps `origin: 'test'` while a trace replays. - Docs: `reference/engine.mdx` (`origin` paragraph), skill `agent.md` (trace cache section). Changeset: patch. - Test: `step-accounting.test.ts` asserts `agent` by default, `test` while replaying, `agent` again after. ## Verification Same build, same test (`on-page-scroll`, one targeted tap then three swipes), record then replay, iPhone 17 Pro. The only difference between the two pairs is this change, toggled in the built engine: | Replayed action: tap the "Page 3" tab | Duration | | --- | --- | | Replayed with settle (before) | 1887 ms | | Replayed as a test step (this PR) | 1357 ms | About 530 ms saved per replayed action, the settle window plus its snapshots. Full replay with this PR: 27 s recorded to 15.6 s replayed, 8 model calls to 2 (the asserts). Note for anyone reading the raw runs: the recorded swipe sequence replays nondeterministically on this pager (it missed on one run in each pair, `target-not-found`), which is a replay relocation matter unrelated to this change. Unit: core 1237 passing; lint and dead-code clean. ---

title: feat(agent): a judgment sees the screen and nothing else, can run on its own judge model, and answers inconclusive instead of guessing
body: ## What and why - `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` no longer receive the prior-step ledger. The judge is shown the instruction and the current observation; the act loop keeps its ledger. A verdict now rests on what is on screen, not on the acting agent's account of what it did (`packages/e2e/src/agent/invocation.ts`). - New `judge` slot: `agents..judge` or `createAgent({ judge })` names the model for the judgment tier. Config resolves it to `model` when unset, so downstream has one rule: judgments call `judge`. A config `judge` that differs from the executor's is `INVALID_CONFIG`, the same way `model` already works (`packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts`). - Judgment protocol is `agent-judgment-2`: `verdict` is `holds`, `fails`, or `inconclusive` instead of a boolean. An inconclusive `assert` fails with the new `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` code (category test, exit 1) and the model's account of what was missing. `waitFor` keeps polling on an inconclusive round. Schema and both fixtures renamed to v2. - The report records the checkout under `run.vcs` (`commit`, `branch`, `dirty`), from git with a one-second budget, else the GitHub Actions variables, else absent. That is the join between a run's verdicts and the pull request that produced the code. The git runner is shared with telemetry (`packages/e2e/src/internal/git.ts`). - The run header and summary name the judge beside the model when they differ. Every judgment step's `model` in the report already named the model that produced it; it now names the judge. Why: the verifier literature's strongest single finding is that a judge which reads the actor's narration grades a story rather than a screen, and that a judge without a "cannot tell" answer guesses. Both were true here. Research notes in `.agent/research/verification-layer-for-software-factories-2026-09-12.md` (untracked). ```ts title="e2e.config.ts" agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna'), judge: gateway('anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'), }, }, ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before A1[act model] -- ledger + summaries --> J1[judgment: same model] J1 --> V1{true / false} end subgraph after A2[act model] -. nothing .-> J2[judge model] S[current screen + instruction] --> J2 J2 --> V2{holds / fails / inconclusive} V2 -- inconclusive --> F[ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE] end ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(e2e): opt-in post-run failure analysis says what went wrong, why, and how to fix it
body: ## What and why - A failure today is an error code and a locator name. This adds one bounded model call per failed, timed-out, or flaky test, after its last attempt, that says what went wrong, why, who should look, and what to do: `app-bug`, `test-bug`, `environment`, `flaky`, or `unknown`, with confidence, a two-sentence summary, the evidence each conclusion rests on, a fix, and a `suggestedLocator` the runner keeps only when the captured screen shows exactly that role and name. - Opt-in: `analysis: { ... }` in the config or `e2e run --analyze`. The model is an AI SDK instance like every model slot, falling back to `agents.default.model`. - Failure-time evidence is captured whether or not analysis is on: a masked screenshot (when `screenshot` is a configured artifact kind) and the redacted accessibility tree as `failure/observation.txt`, both attached to the failing step, at the one moment the screen still shows the failure (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`, before `afterEach`). - Three seams make it the project's own: `analysis.instructions` appends project knowledge to the built-in policy, `analysis.evidence` adds providers whose text joins every analysis (the diff under test, a server log), and `analysis.analyzer` replaces the analyzer wholesale. Provider output and a custom analyzer's answer are bounded, redacted, and held to the same closed grammar. - Read-only and post-hoc: runs in the runner process beside the remaining tests, two at a time, 90 s each, never a status, never a test budget, never a run failure, never in the config digest (turning it on keeps every cached trace valid). - Renders under the failure in the list reporter (a flaky test's after the failures), streams as an `analysis` run event, lands in report.json as the result's `e2edev.analysis` extension (no schema bump; extensions were already admitted), and joins the markdown summary the GitHub comment renders from. - Rebased onto main 2026-09-14: the runner package is `e2e`, the GitHub comment renders from `report/markdown.ts` (the analysis line lives there now), and the failure location comes from the observation's `location` since the engine SPI lock removed `session.url`. - Revives the 2026-09-05 prototype (ecca4236) as a rewrite on main: models are instances, secrets replaced credentials, events carry the agent, and the analyzer now reads per-step events and metrics. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[attempt fails] --> B[capture screenshot + tree] B --> C[afterEach, close session] C --> D[test-finished] D --> E{analysis on?} E -- no --> Z[report] E -- yes --> F[build FailureContext] F --> G[evidence providers, 15 s each] G --> H[analyzer: built-in or custom] H --> I[validate closed grammar + verify locator on screen] I --> J[analysis event, result.analysis, e2edev.analysis] J --> Z ``` ```ts export default { analysis: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast'), instructions: 'Controls carry data-testid; prefer it over accessible names in fixes.', evidence: [{ name: 'git diff', collect: async () => execSync('git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD', { encoding: 'utf8' }) }], }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` Live on the testbed bug garden (`pnpm --filter @e2edev/testbed test:analysis`), five planted failures, each classified as its title predicts, about $0.0002 and 3-7 s per analysis: ```text FAIL |shop| tests-analysis/failures.e2e.ts > test-bug: locator names a control the screen spells differently LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator matched no nodes within getByRole("button", name: "Add to basket").first() ❯ analysis test-bug · high confidence · gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast · 3.69s The test searched for a button named “Add to basket,” but the catalog exposes buttons named “Add to cart,” so the locator matched nothing. - Error message: getByRole("button", name: "Add to basket") matched no nodes. - Screen node #n48 (and #n54, #n60, #n66): the available buttons are named "Add to cart". fix: Update the test locator to getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().tap(). locator: screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add to cart" }) FAIL |shop| tests-analysis/failures.e2e.ts > app-bug: the Help link leads to a page that does not exist ❯ analysis app-bug · high confidence · gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast · 5.03s The Help link navigates to `/hlep`, where Bookshelf displays a “Page not found” page instead of the Help page. - Screen URL is `http://127.0.0.1:4275/hlep`, and the Help link has href `http://127.0.0.1:4275/hlep` fix: Fix the application’s Help link href and/or route from `/hlep` to the intended Help page. ``` Follow-ons, not in this PR: console and network diagnostics as an evidence source (the biggest gap for a confident `app-bug`), serial-group members (their attempts live on the group record), and counting analysis usage in the run's AI summary line. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(config)!: drop origin allowlists everywhere; navigation and secret fills are not gated by origin
body:
## What and why

- Origin allowlists are gone, everywhere. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` gated typed navigation only; a click, a redirect, or a popup reached any origin regardless, so the list guarded nothing and had to be spelled out for every subdomain a sign-in flow touched.
- The per-credential and per-secret `allowedOrigins` went with it. A secret is only ever typed into a field the step was handed, and a password only into a password field, so an origin gate on the fill guarded against a model mistake at the cost of configuring every flow that leaves the app's domain, a Google sign-in included. If a threat model ever calls for it, it comes back as an opt-in.
- `app.open()`, the agent's `navigate`, `web.goto`, and cookie targets open any http(s) URL. `file:`, `data:`, and `javascript:` stay `POLICY_DENIED` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts`).
- `credentials` entries are `{ username, password }`. `secrets` entries are a string or a provider; the `{ value }` object form only existed to carry the list and is gone too. `type_secret` now works on a device target, which the origin check used to block.
- The site of `url`, its registrable domain, survives where it is invisible to config: the browser engine's `headers` reach the site and no other host, and off-site iframes stay out of observations. `basicAuth` answers any 401, as Playwright's own `httpCredentials` does.
- Engine contract: `EngineAppInfo.allowedOrigins` became `site?: string`, `EngineAppDeclaration` lost the field, `sameSite` and `siteOf` are exported from `@e2edev/e2e/engine`. `playwright({ allowedOrigins })` fails at config load.
- SECURITY.md claimed link-local and cloud-metadata denies that never existed in code; the sentence is removed rather than the check invented.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before
    N1[navigate / open] --> A1{origin in allowedOrigins?}
    C1[click / redirect / popup] --> X1[any origin]
    S1[secret fill] --> A2{origin in allowedOrigins ∩ credential list?} --> A3{declared in step? editable? password field?}
  end
  subgraph after
    N2[navigate / open] --> B1{http or https?}
    C2[click / redirect / popup] --> X2[any origin]
    S2[secret fill] --> B3{declared in step? editable? password field?}
  end
```

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
// before
engine: playwright({
  url: 'https://tester.army',
  allowedOrigins: ['https://tester.army', 'https://www.tester.army', 'https://auth.tester.army'],
}),
credentials: {
  google: { username: 'tester@gmail.com', password: process.env.GOOGLE_PASSWORD ?? '', allowedOrigins: ['https://accounts.google.com'] },
},

// after
engine: playwright({ url: 'https://tester.army' }),
credentials: {
  google: { username: 'tester@gmail.com', password: process.env.GOOGLE_PASSWORD ?? '' },
},
```

The site heuristic has no public suffix list (`siteOf` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts`): last two labels, or three for `co.uk`-style suffixes. It only scopes headers and frame capture now, so an error is a missing bypass header or a dropped frame, never a refused step.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Title and changeset done; no deprecation window, removed outright by decision.
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No wire change; the SDK types file drops the `{ value, allowedOrigins }` secret form.
- [x] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat(engine)!: lock the engine contract as a UI-only, cross-platform SPI
body:
## What and why

- e2e tests applications through their user interface: web, mobile, desktop, TV, anything with a screen. The engine contract is the layer every platform shares, and it is being locked for 1.0. This PR removes the places where the web engine's world view had leaked into it, so the device engine no longer fakes web concepts to satisfy it.
- The snapshot carries one engine-minted `root` (stable id) and an opaque `location` instead of `nodes` and `url`; `viewport` is required. A device reports its foreground screen, a browser its URL; a location that is a URL anchors the trace cache on its path, any other anchors as the string it is.
- `perform` comes with `actions`, the kinds the surface honors. The agent's tools and `screen` methods derive from it, so iOS is never offered a `select` tool that can only fail. The viewport swipe is `perform(root, swipe)`; the `swipe` and `url` members are gone.
- `app` is data only. The steering hooks move to `session: { open, back, restart, reset }`. `restart` and `reset` open nothing; the harness reopens the app through its own navigate path, so a surface never learns the app URL and `baseUrl` leaves `EngineInitInfo`.
- `testId` is a field on `SemanticNode`. The harness stops knowing attribute names: `screen.testIdAttribute` in the root config becomes `playwright({ testIdAttribute })`, and the device engine sets `testId` from the accessibility identifier instead of synthesizing an attribute map.
- `press` keys follow one documented grammar (Playwright spelling, `parseKey` exported for engines). `OperationContext.origin` is required, `EnginePrepareInfo.env` is a plain record, the `download` artifact kind becomes `file`, and the recognized `platform` labels are listed.
- `defineEngine` moves to `packages/e2e/src/engine/manifest.ts`; `index.ts` is types only. `spiVersion` stays `1`: nothing has shipped as 1.0, so the literal marks the locked contract.

```ts
defineEngine({
  name: 'hyperdrive', version: '1.0.0', spiVersion: 1, platform: 'macos',
  observe: async (ctx) => ({ root, viewport, location: frontWindowTitle }),
  perform, actions: ['tap', 'doubleTap', 'fill', 'clear', 'press', 'swipe', 'dragTo'],
  locate, tapAt,
  app: { identity: 'com.example.app' },
  session: { restart, reset },
  artifacts: { screenshot },
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before
    A1[app.restart] --> E1["engine.restart → goto(baseUrl)"]
    S1["screen.swipe"] --> E2[engine.swipe]
    Q1["getByTestId"] --> E3["attributes[testIdAttribute]"]
  end
  subgraph after
    A2[app.restart] --> E4[engine.session.restart] --> H[harness reopens via open]
    S2["screen.swipe"] --> E5["perform(root, swipe)"]
    Q2["getByTestId"] --> E6[node.testId]
  end
```

- `EnginePrepareResult.env` is the typed channel from a runner-side `prepare` to each worker's `init`, which reads it as `EngineInitInfo.env`: the run's environment plus that target's additions, never another target's, in child, in-process, and standalone runs alike. The device pool used to write into the run's environment object and read `process.env` back.
- Verified live against the gateway: the agent testbed suite passes 11/11 on a cold cache (58 model calls) and the second run replays all 7 act steps with zero model calls; the deterministic testbed suite passes 33/33.
- Report wire format: `download` artifact kind is `file`, `usage.downloads` is `usage.files`, target records drop `testIdAttribute`. TesterArmy ingest needs the same rename.
- Fixed on the way: `screen.getByTestId` on the web ignored the configured attribute and used Playwright's process-wide default.
- Rebased on #290: `EngineAppInfo` is `{ site? }` only, with no `baseUrl` and no origin list, and secret fills carry no origin check on either path.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Title and changesets done; no deprecation window, this is the pre-1.0 contract lock.

title: feat(agent): Thinking lines show the model's reasoning
body:
The live window showed a `Thinking` line per model turn with timing and tokens, but never what the model actually thought. A finished turn now appends an excerpt of its reasoning, so a run or exploration says why the agent acted: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | 
• Thinking (17.29s) (↑7.7k ↓18)
› tap button "Close" (85ms)
| 
• Thinking (17.29s) (↑7.7k ↓18) · The modal blocks checkout; closing it first
› tap button "Close" (85ms)
| - The act loop reads `step.reasoningText` off each `ToolLoopAgent` turn (`packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts`); the judgment tier (`assert`/`waitFor`/`extract`, the explore planner) reads `result.finalStep.reasoningText` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts`). - Both tiers record through `reasoningField()` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/usage.ts`): trimmed, empty dropped, capped at 600 chars. The excerpt lands on the step's `model` event as `reasoning`, crossing worker IPC like every other event. - `eventLine` renders it after the token split, collapsed to one line and clipped to the row (`packages/e2e/src/report/list-steps.ts`). title: feat(e2e)!: the runner publishes as e2e; @e2edev/e2e is retired
body: ## What and why - The runner is `e2e` on npm. `import { test } from 'e2e'`, `npx e2e@canary init`, peer ranges on `e2e`. The scoped `@e2edev/e2e` was a private-phase name; the packages are public now and the unscoped name is ours, so the first build testers install is the one they will keep. - Every import, config, template, docs page, skill, and test names `e2e`, `e2e/agent`, `e2e/engine`. Engines and the GitHub reporter declare their peer dependency on `e2e`, which is why their changesets carry the break too. - `init` writes the runner's own dependency by the same rule as engines: caret for a release, exact for a prerelease. A canary engine names one runner build in its peer range, so a caret on the runner would resolve to a newer canary and fail the install. - The `e2e` name on npm already has a 2014 placeholder at 0.1.0, so a `--tag canary` or `--tag beta` publish leaves its `latest` untouched. ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { createAgent } from 'e2e/agent'; import { playwright } from '@e2edev/playwright'; ``` After the first `e2e` publish, deprecate the old name in one line: ```sh npm deprecate @e2edev/e2e "Renamed to e2e" ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`@e2edev/e2e/engine`): changesets for `@e2edev/e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: docs(reference): cut the slop from the Reference tab
body:
## What and why

- Every reference page ended in a four-card footer and most carried sections that lived on another page too (exit codes, `AgentError`, env var overrides, the MCP tour). The sidebar and cross-links already do that job, so both are gone.
- Justification prose and benchmark numbers left the reference pages. The agent page compared models and pixel sizes; the reporters and engine pages explained the reasoning behind every design choice; the CLI page had a changelog-style Diagnostics section and a signals essay. Reference states what a thing does. The why stays in guides and PR bodies.
- Every fenced type block is now the source declaration with its JSDoc, copied verbatim. The comment is the member's description, so the tables that repeated it row by row are gone. What remains as prose is behavior the types cannot carry: timeouts, thrown codes, merge rules, strictness.
- Members the source left undocumented (`E2EConfig` scalars, `TestOptions`, `CommandConfig`, `Reporter`, `SemanticNode`, and others) got one-line JSDoc, taken from the tables they replace. Comments only, no runtime change.
- Four tables became type blocks outright: `E2EConfig` replaces the top-level config table, `Locator` the action and read tables, `PlaywrightOptions` and `AgentDeviceOptions` the engine option tables.
- Three broken spots fixed on the way: the environment page had an empty Model table header, the engine page had a garbled sentence in App, and its Shared semantics table cited spec chapters deleted in #161.
- `reference/app-web.mdx`, a page of links to two other pages, is a redirect to `/reference/playwright` in `docs.json`.

Before, a member and its description lived apart:

```ts
export interface TestOptions {
  timeout?: number;
  retries?: number;
```

| Key | Type | Default | Valid | Merge across layers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout` | `number` | `config.timeout`, 120000 | positive safe integer | Innermost wins |

After, the block reads on its own:

```ts
export interface TestOptions {
  /** Attempt deadline in milliseconds; defaults to `config.timeout`. Innermost wins. */
  timeout?: number;
  /** Retries, 0 through 10; defaults to `config.retries`. Inside a serial group the group's value applies. */
  retries?: number;
```

title: fix(mcp): load the AI SDK lazily so the CLI starts without ai
body: ## What and why - `npx e2e@canary --help` crashed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'ai'` before Commander read a flag. Every command did, `init` included, and `init` is the command a project runs before it has installed anything. - `ai` is an optional peer dependency, so a bare `npx e2e` install has none of it. The one static value import of it outside the loader was `asSchema` in the MCP bridge, `packages/e2e/src/mcp/tools.ts:12` on main, and the CLI reaches that module for every command (diagram below). Every project that has run `init` has `ai`, which is why nobody hit it in the monorepo or in a dogfood suite. - The bridge now takes `asSchema` from `loadAiSdk()` and `aiSdk()`, the way `agent/model/schema.ts` already does, and `SessionHost.openSession` primes the loader before an attempt opens a browser, so the synchronous catalog render has the SDK. A project without `ai` that opens an MCP session gets `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` as a tool result instead of a crash at startup. - Two guards. `tests/unit/ai-sdk-imports.test.ts` fails on any value import of `ai` outside `agent/ai-sdk.ts`; type imports and prose that mentions the package pass. `tests/integration/cli-boot.test.ts` spawns the built CLI under a `module.registerHooks` resolve hook that fails `ai` and expects `--version` and `--help` to answer. ```mermaid flowchart LR bin[cli/bin.ts] --> index[cli/index.ts] --> cmd[cli/mcp.ts] --> server[mcp/server.ts] --> tools[mcp/tools.ts] tools -. before: static import, every command .-> ai[(ai)] tools -- after --> loader[agent/ai-sdk.ts] loader -. on session open only .-> ai ``` Scratch project with only the packed tarball installed, no `ai` anywhere: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'ai' imported from .../node_modules/e2e/dist/mcp/tools.js` | `e2e --version` prints the version, `--help` prints the usage, `init --help` renders | The rule the guard encodes is already written on the loader (`packages/e2e/src/agent/ai-sdk.ts:1`): deterministic suites never load the SDK, everything model-backed funnels through it, and a missing package is one `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` rather than a module-resolution crash. Two things left out on purpose. `@e2edev/agent-device` has the same shape (`packages/agent-device/src/tools.ts:10` imports `tool` from `ai`, with `ai` an optional peer there too), but it only loads from a project config at run time, where the default agent needs `ai` anyway, so it is not on the `init` path; same treatment in its own PR. The canary needs a re-publish after this merges. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

A local `deviceTool` typed against `Tool` with a type-only import does the same job, so each `execute` still gets its input type from the zod schema (`packages/agent-device/src/tools.ts:17`). - Guard: `packages/agent-device/tests/unit/ai-imports.test.ts` fails on any value import of `ai` in `src`; type imports pass.
