title: feat(agent-device): agent-device is a regular dependency again
body: ## What and why - `@e2edev/agent-device` installs `agent-device` itself again, pinned to the exact version it was built and tested against (`0.21.1`); the `0.21.x` peer requirement from 0.7.0 (#278) is gone. A mobile project adds one package, and `init` has one range fewer to compute. - `e2e init` writes `@e2edev/agent-device` only. `agentDeviceRange` and the `agent-device` entry the runner's build recorded in `engine-versions.json` are removed (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts`, `packages/e2e/package.json`). - The testbed drops its own `agent-device` devDependency and rides the engine's, as it did before #278. Nothing in the testbed imports the driver directly. - Docs: the peer paragraph in `reference/agent-device` and the setup bullet in the skill now say the engine installs the driver. - Changesets: `@e2edev/agent-device` minor, `e2e` patch. Not breaking: a project that added `agent-device` for the peer keeps working and can drop it. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph "#278 (0.7.0)" A1[project] --> C1["agent-device 0.21.x"] A1 --> E1["@e2edev/agent-device"] -. peer .-> C1 end subgraph "this PR" A2[project] --> E2["@e2edev/agent-device"] --> C2["agent-device 0.21.1, pinned"] end ``` What #278 solved comes back, and it is worth having in the open: with npm, yarn, and bun the driver hoists into the project's `node_modules`, so `npx agent-device doctor` runs the engine's copy. With pnpm it stays under the engine, so `npx agent-device doctor` (and `pnpm dlx`) fetch the latest release, which can differ from the pin. `doctor` only checks the toolchain, so that drift is harmless there. A project that scripts the CLI for sessions should declare `agent-device` itself at the pinned version, so one copy runs; the changeset says so. The upstream driver's own `ai` peer is optional (`^6 || ^7`), so the pin pulls no model SDK into a deterministic project. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(report): a failure hands off what the screen held, a page per failed test, and the line to look at
body: ## What and why - A failure message says what was asked; it cannot say what the screen held instead. Before this, a missing locator waited the full action timeout and the report kept only the message: no URL, no screen, no nearby nodes. Every step's `source` was hard-coded to `unknown`, and the failing line lived only in the stack, which never enters the report. - When an attempt fails with the session still open, the runner looks once more and records `attempt.failure`: the location, the redacted screen as the agent reads it (`failure/screen.txt`, a `log` artifact), a masked screenshot when the run keeps screenshots and no secret was filled, and for a locator that matched nothing or too much, the nodes closest to what it asked for. Best-effort, bounded to five seconds, never changes the verdict. - Every step records the test line it was called from as `source`; an error records the line it unwound through as `source`. Errors carry structured `details` beside the message: `expect` gives `locator`, `expected`, `observed`, `matches`; a locator failure gives `locator`, `role`, `name` or `testId`, `waitedMs`. - An agent step keeps its last twelve model turns as `turns` (calls and what came back, clipped), whatever the debug setting. The full transcript stays behind `--debug`. - The `markdown` reporter renders all of it, and writes one page per failed or flaky test under `.e2e/failures/`: error in full, the facts, the line to look at, every step, every kept turn, the screen text inline. The summary block links to it. The list reporter prints the location, closest nodes, and screen path under each failure. - Report-1 changes are additive: `error.details`, `error.source`, `attempt.failure`, `step.turns`; `step.source` is real now. ## Evidence Terminal, a locator that matched nothing: ``` LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator matched no nodes within getByRole("button", name: "Add todo item") ❯ tests-scratch/showcase.e2e.ts:8:3 8| await screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add todo item' }).tap(); | ^ ❯ at http://127.0.0.1:4278/todos ❯ on screen #n44 button "Add" ❯ screen .e2e/artifacts/web/.../attempt-1/failure/screen.txt ``` `summary.md` block for the same failure: ```markdown **LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND** locator matched no nodes within getByRole("button", name: "Add todo item") Asked for: button "Add todo item" · waited 3.0s Step 2 of 2, `locator.tap` "getByRole("button", name: "Add todo item")", failed in 3.0s Steps: ✓ /todos › ✗ getByRole("button", name: "Add todo item") Failed the same way on both attempts: **LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND** at step 2. Screen: http://127.0.0.1:4278/todos · closest to the locator: `#n44 button "Add"` Evidence: screenshot `…/001-failure.png`, log `…/failure/screen.txt` · Details: `.e2e/failures/…-f874d62b.md` · `tests-scratch/showcase.e2e.ts:8` ``` An `expect` failure reads `Expected: text "2 remaining" · Observed: text "1 remaining" (1 match)`. Failure page of an agentic step that could not complete (excerpt): ```markdown # ✗ agentic: the control does not exist **ASSERTION_FAILED** agent.act failed: Added the todo “Groceries” and marked it done, but the todo row exposes only a “Delete Groceries” button; no “Archive” button is present … Look at: `tests-scratch/showcase.e2e.ts:18` Failed the same way on both attempts: **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 2. ## Steps 1. ✓ `app.open` "/todos" (30ms) — `tests-scratch/showcase.e2e.ts:4` 2. ✗ `agent.act` "Add a todo named "Groceries", then archive it …" (12.1s, 6 model calls) — **ASSERTION_FAILED** ## Agent turns of step 2 **Turn 2** `tap({"target":"n200"})` > Screen changes since revision b4 (now revision b6, path /todos, 29 nodes): 4 added, 2 changed. > added #n210 button "Delete Groceries" … ## Screen at failure URL: `http://127.0.0.1:4278/todos` #n199 textbox "New todo" #n200 button "Add" #n215 listitem "GroceriesDelete Groceries" testid="todo" #n218 button "Delete Groceries" #n206 status "Remaining" text="0 remaining" ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: test(e2e): the suite accepts canary versions on main
body: ## Why Main is red since the two `chore: release` commits. Oskar releases canaries from now on, so main carries the versions a canary run writes, such as `e2e@0.15.0-canary-20260914095510`. Three tests assumed a stable version tuple: - `report-list`: the RUN banner regex only matched `v\d+.\d+.\d+`. - unit `cli-init` with `--yes`: expected a caret range on the runner, but `dependencyRange` pins a prerelease exactly, by design (a caret on a prerelease resolves to the newest prerelease of that tuple, which names a different runner build). - integration `cli-init`: same for the `@e2edev/playwright` pin. ## What The banner regex accepts a prerelease suffix. Both init tests derive the expected range from `dependencyRange`, so they hold for a stable and a canary runner alike. No runtime change. ## Release job With every changeset consumed by the canary, `changesets/action` runs `pnpm run release` on main. Every canary version is already on npm (checked the `canary` dist-tags), so `changeset publish` skips them and the job is a no-op after the gate. ## Verified - `pnpm run check`, `pnpm test`: all green locally on this branch (1595 passed, 1 skipped). ---

## @e2edev/agent-device@0.8.0

### Minor Changes

- [#365](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/365) [`f7f86d9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7f86d91e87b317dea9ae076f143e20f6ba8ed98) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `agentDevice({ device })` accepts a `DeviceProvider`: an object that leases one hosted device per worker slot when the run starts and releases every lease when it ends. The engine drives each lease through the agent-device daemon the lease names (`daemon.baseUrl`, `daemon.authToken`) instead of the local one, selects `device` inside it when given, and skips its own `appPath` install when the lease reports `installedApp`. Slots lease in parallel; a slot that fails releases the others and ends the run before any test. No vendor ships in the package; the mobile guide shows an example provider against a generic session API. `DeviceProvider`, `DeviceRequest`, `DeviceLease`, and `DeviceReleaseContext` are exported.

- [#380](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/380) [`54c0dba`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/54c0dba62fc47403564ece41ce503bb9b9ce9a08) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The engine declares the `swipeTo` pointer action and performs it as a coordinate swipe from the point to `target`, so `screen.swipe({ from, to })` works on a device. A directional swipe at a bare point is still `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`; `screen.swipe({ direction })` scrolls the screen root as before.

- [#349](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/349) [`3e0285c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3e0285c5e566abaa129ee167014f96c2a766d930) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: `agentDeviceTools()` no longer offers `type_text`. The agent's own `type` verb reaches the focused field without a target since the engine declared the `keyboard` capability, and a typed value goes through the grammar there, so the trace cache records and replays it; the project tool bypassed the grammar and ended every replay at a gap. A prompt that named `type_text` should say `type` instead. `alert` says to prefer a listed button, whose tap replays.

## e2e@0.15.0

### Minor Changes

- [#351](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/351) [`45c08b1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/45c08b123e52369257433da2e133a84f2d6bdfa7) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The built-in agent reads a phone keyboard the way the platform does. An action result says when the on-screen keyboard closed with the action, because on a touch screen the tap that closes it is often spent on closing it and the control under the finger did not react; the model is told to act on it again rather than read an unchanged screen as success. The execution rules now require the latest result to show the asked-for outcome before a passed verdict: a result reporting no change, or only the keyboard closing, means the decisive action did not land. `scroll` repeats up to 20 screens in one call instead of 5, so a long list costs turns in proportion to its length rather than five screens at a time.

- [#359](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/359) [`c1d23b2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c1d23b230b8c8502f551e869710ed26f606a7469) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A recording's starting and ending screens are compared as routes, not URLs. A location is reduced to its pathname with every segment that looks minted per record abstracted: uuids, hex and digit runs, long tokens mixing letters and digits, text with spaces. The query, the fragment, and a trailing slash are ignored; an app that routes in the fragment (`/#/companies/1`) routes by that path. A value the call marked with `unique()` is recognized in the slug an app derives for a record path, next to its percent- and form-encoded spellings. At the end of a step, two locations that still differ in one segment, a slug of a record the runner never saw, are the same screen when the recorded anchors are on it. The replay policy version changes, so existing caches start over.

- [#380](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/380) [`54c0dba`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/54c0dba62fc47403564ece41ce503bb9b9ce9a08) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Coordinate input for the deterministic API. `screen.tapAt({ x, y })` taps a viewport point with no node behind it, `screen.swipe({ from, to })` swipes along a path between two points (a touch swipe on a device, a pointer drag on a document platform), and `tap({ position })` on a locator (also `click`) taps at an offset of the node's box, scrolling it into view first when the engine can. Points are CSS pixels, the space `boundingBox()` reports in; a negative or non-finite coordinate is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and an engine without the matching pointer action is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before anything is resolved. Engine contract: a new `swipeTo` pointer action kind (`{ kind: 'swipeTo', target }`) carries the path swipe, and `TargetSession` exposes `pointerActions`. `Point`, `TapOptions`, and `SwipePathOptions` are exported.

- [#365](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/365) [`f7f86d9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7f86d91e87b317dea9ae076f143e20f6ba8ed98) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The engine contract gains an optional `finish(info)` hook: once per run and target in the runner process, after the last worker of the target is gone, on every exit path (pass, failure, interrupt, a `prepare` that threw part-way), within the cleanup budget and never cancelled by an interrupt. Release what `prepare` acquired for the run there. `EnginePrepareInfo` carries `projectRoot`, so a hook can resolve a relative option before any worker exists. Additive; the SPI version stays 1.

- [#382](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/382) [`2e18196`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2e18196b79ac724c2a274a27562ea06d7a316d02) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The locator reads and matchers a Playwright user reaches for on day one. `locator.all()` hands back one `nth(i)` locator per current match and `locator.allTextContents()` reads every match's normalized text; both resolve once, without waiting or the exactly-one rule, and answer zero matches with `[]`. `isHidden()` is the negation of `isVisible()` and `isDisabled()` of `isEnabled()`, with the same strictness and the same `POLICY_DENIED` rules on secure fields. `expect(locator).toBeAttached()` waits for one match to exist, hidden or shown, and negated passes once nothing matches. `toHaveText` and `toContainText` take a list: the match count must equal the list length and each match must satisfy the entry at its position, a string exactly, a `RegExp` by test; the failure lists every text observed.

- [#377](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/377) [`9f2b73f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9f2b73f9293d4cdee449bb04e4f8272477d22402) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Subscription sign-in ships inside `e2e`; the separate `@e2edev/oauth` package is gone. Import the model from `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`, `e2e/oauth/copilot`, or `e2e/oauth/grok` and install only the provider package it wraps (`@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, or `@ai-sdk/xai`). The constructors and the CLI are the whole surface; the `createOAuthFetch` library API of the old package is not carried over. `e2e init` writes those imports and no longer adds a sibling dependency, `e2e login` and `e2e logout` run the flows directly, and the `e2e-oauth` bin is retired; uninstall `@e2edev/oauth` from projects that had it. The `chatgpt()` fold for the Codex stream without a `content-type` header lands with it.
  
  `e2e models [provider]` asks the vendor which models a stored login serves and prints their ids. `chatgpt()` now tells the AI SDK that the Codex backend stores nothing server side, so a second turn carries the encrypted reasoning of the first instead of referring to it by an id the backend cannot find (`Item with id 'rs_…' not found`). The `CHATGPT_MODELS` constant is gone; the list is the vendor's.

- [#369](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/369) [`d746ce4`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d746ce4b3f568c00ac736c116a561ef4e4dc67df) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Telemetry tells a fleet from its users: a platform that runs e2e on someone's behalf sets `E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET=<name>` and its fresh machines are attributed to `fleet:<name>`, like CI, instead of each counting as a new user. Every event also carries the sandbox the kernel announces (`firecracker`), the JavaScript runtime and its version (`node`, `bun`, `deno`), whether the command created the preferences file, and the days since it was created (unknown for a preferences file from before this release). Every event also tells PostHog to skip its GeoIP step, so no location is derived from the request address, and the one-time notice shows again once because what is collected has changed.

- [#371](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/371) [`d7d843a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d7d843af9d241246d225795b7d2439cb98a27a8a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The run telemetry event now names the error that decided the status (`primary_error_code`), counts attempts and the tests that needed a retry, counts the agent's actions by the runner's own names with a project's tools folded into one `tool` bucket, files an engine, provider, or plain failure under a kind from a closed list read off its message (`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED:rate-limit`, `ENGINE_FAILURE:device`, ...) without sending the message, and says whether the provider priced the model calls (`cost_source`).

- [#370](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/370) [`bd2a9a6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bd2a9a6db7c23193be6a914f961c3fb178074d59) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The session telemetry event now says how the command ended: its exit code, its duration, and the runner error code when a run or a listing failed before it could start (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_CONFIG`, ...) or `CLI_USAGE` when the CLI rejected a flag. `e2e init` sends an init event with how it ended and the ids of the engine, the gateway, the skill, the MCP registration, and the install chosen; never a path or an endpoint typed at a prompt.

- [#354](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/354) [`91dcd30`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/91dcd30b535331d89d197f6c5f3e8ae984e92960) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Consecutive identical scrolls fold into one recorded action with a repeat count, so a list paged to its end no longer overruns the action cap and poisons the trace; replay repeats them with a settled look between, re-finding the list each time. A scroll target a device renamed and renumbered is re-found live by its role and place, and a lost list that covered at least half the viewport when recorded (`spans` on the recorded scroll) scrolls as the viewport, live and on replay; a smaller region hands off.

- [#355](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/355) [`ddf9747`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ddf97479d734b294f826b01b206e3b49cb7822bf) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A recorded point tap whose containing node matches several look-alikes taps the one the recorded point lies inside, on a viewport of the recorded size; a node that is gone hands off as before, and the bare point is never tapped on its own. The replay policy version moves to `conservative/5`, so entries recorded under the previous rules are re-recorded rather than replayed under the new ones.

- [#353](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/353) [`9fbba0b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9fbba0b34c4f6a387d62914d35fc756b84ba7f8e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A typed value is recorded as a run-time gap only when the step read it off a screen it saw (a code, a reference the app minted; a field echoing what was typed does not count) or when it is a date or time, or when the model had been shown a screenshot in that step, where a value may have been read off pixels the runner cannot check. A value the model composed itself, a name or an email for a form, is the flow's data and replays verbatim, where before any value absent from the instruction and params ended the replay.

### Patch Changes

- [#373](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/373) [`ca5e619`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ca5e6196b620165dcabc383c1aaf35c44cf22690) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Relicense from MIT to Apache-2.0. The package ships the license text and a `NOTICE` file.

- [#344](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/344) [`d438348`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d438348fda96a512cc03b51c41f1140353030003) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A `unique()` value is templated in a recording in every spelling a URL gives it: as typed, percent-encoded (`Acme%20Corp` in a path), and form-encoded (`Acme+Corp` in a search query). A step that ends on a search result or on a page whose path carries the value replays and passes its end check with the next run's value; before, the encoded form stayed literal and the step handed off after replaying every action.

- [#345](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/345) [`b9abd60`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b9abd60c435935fc96816249f48315885d8ac85f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A control with no accessible name, text, placeholder, or test id, an unlabelled input in a form, is now recorded with its place among the unnamed controls of its kind and relocates by it on replay. It is matched strictly, so an unnamed textbox never stands in for a named one, and a change in the number of unnamed twins diverges as before. Such targets used to be unrelocatable outright, so every replay through an unlabelled form stopped at its first field.

- [#342](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/342) [`ea27708`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ea2770804fe55857d105224355eef7b45453d665) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A recording replays on the page it began on up to the ids the app mints per record. A step that edits or deletes a record a previous step created starts on `/companies/<id>`, and that id is new on every run; the start check compared it literally and missed with `wrong-context` every time. It now uses the same shape comparison as the end-of-step check.

- [#343](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/343) [`195bd0d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/195bd0d14cc3f32440bfa140ed468dfa705d851d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Replays hand off sooner, and less often, on list pages. Pagination ranges (`Showing 1 to 9 of 9 results`), record counts (`12 items`), millisecond timings, and bare numbers such as a badge are no longer recorded as end anchors while a stable anchor exists: they grow with the data every run leaves behind and could never read the same again. A recording's end wait is now measured from its last action to the passing screen instead of from the step's start, so a replay no longer waits out the model's thinking time before handing off.

- [#368](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/368) [`da6b939`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/da6b939e4c306b5dba64088599961a666f680c9a) Thanks [@szymonrybczak](https://github.com/szymonrybczak)! - Use consistent sentence case for `e2e init` prompts and status messages.

- [#366](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/366) [`fb6e336`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/fb6e3363275991bf2baa3698f03a69574d93cb83) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The list reporter's live block now reaches the bottom of the terminal: the running tests take the rows under the log and the summary sits on the last rows, instead of the block stopping fourteen rows in and leaving the lower half of a tall terminal blank. The block gives rows back to the log as results print, and only once the log has grown down to the rows the running area needs does it scroll the log, as before.

- [#346](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/346) [`f09b69e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f09b69e90a8f76172ba5e5e006e7ec10dd99c172) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Clarify the bundled setup guide for subscriptions, API keys, and local models. Correct model authentication, judge selection, locator waiting, and cache guidance.

- [#375](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/375) [`f3d61e8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f3d61e8ce7a8ab9a40090ecd72c9f43557a12492) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A step call without `await` fails the test instead of the worker. A body that returned while a step it started was still running used to end the attempt under that step; the step then failed with nobody to catch it, and the unhandled rejection took the worker down as `WORKER_CRASH`. The runner now checks for running steps whenever the body settles, cancels them, and fails the attempt with `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`, the step recorded as failed and the code frame at the call that lacks `await`. A body that threw keeps its own error; the un-awaited step is recorded under `secondaryErrors`.

- [#366](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/366) [`fb6e336`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/fb6e3363275991bf2baa3698f03a69574d93cb83) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `console.log` and `console.error` in a test reach the terminal again. Workers wrote them straight into the runner's terminal, where the live window painted over them and left stale rows behind; the worker now sends each write to the runner as an `output` run event, and the list reporter prints it above the live window under a `stdout | target file > test` heading, one heading per source until another line intervenes. A line written in pieces prints once whole, and every secret value the worker has seen is redacted before the text leaves it. Programmatic reporters receive the same event with the test id, agent, target, and stream.

- [#367](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/367) [`e9c2914`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e9c2914c6d8f8d664d820b13a1fa454e9247e94b) Thanks [@szymonrybczak](https://github.com/szymonrybczak)! - Fix documentation links in CLI help, the init cache hint, and telemetry output to use https://e2e.tester.army/docs. title: docs: migration pages from Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Detox, and Maestro
body: ## Why Someone with a Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Detox, or Maestro suite has no page that tells them what changes and what to move first. The only trace was a `/from-playwright` redirect pointing at Writing tests. ## What Five short pages under a new **Migrate** group in the Documentation tab: - `migrate/playwright`, `migrate/cypress`, `migrate/selenium` for the web - `migrate/detox`, `migrate/maestro` for mobile Each page has the same shape: a config mapping table, one test before and after, an API map, the two or three behaviours that differ (exact text by default, two matches are an error, secrets are handles, no sessions on a device), and a "what to migrate first" paragraph. The Playwright page says the peer dependency keeps the user's Playwright version so both suites run side by side. The `/from-playwright` redirect now lands on the Playwright page. ## Verification - `pnpm --filter @e2edev/docs run check` passes: examples, `mint validate`, `mint broken-links`. - Every API named in the tables and snippets was typechecked in a scratch file against the built packages (`screen`, `web`, `device`, `app`, `expect`, both engine configs); the scratch file is not committed. - Not checked: the pages have not been viewed in a rendered Mintlify preview. ---

title: feat(agent)!: agents.<name>.timeout is the judgment budget; actionTimeout bounds engine operations only
body: Closes ENG-744. - `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract` ran under `max(30000, actionTimeout)`. Nothing in the config said so, and a project with a slow judge had to inflate the engine's per-operation budget to buy the model time. Every navigation and actionability wait then inherited the inflated number; the 15 s targeted-action cap in `step-accounting.ts` was a patch on that symptom, and PR #288's separate `judge` model made "one number for model latency" false anyway. - New `agents..timeout`, the judgment budget, default 30 s. Resolved in `packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts` next to `maxModelCalls`, read per selected agent in `packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts`. Per-call `timeout` still wins. - `actionTimeout` now bounds engine operations only. The 15 s cap stays; its comment no longer leans on the coupling. - Testbed suites that set `actionTimeout: 90_000` for the model move the value to the agent. The dogfood suite's bare `createAgent(...)` becomes `{ executor, timeout }`, the shape that already carries budgets. ```ts agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast'), timeout: 90_000 }, fast: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast') }, // 30 s judgments } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before AT[actionTimeout] --> EO[engine operation] AT --> JB[judgment deadline = max 30s, actionTimeout] end subgraph after AT2[actionTimeout] --> EO2[engine operation] T[agents.name.timeout] --> JB2[judgment deadline] end ``` Breaking for suites that raised `actionTimeout` above 30 s for the judge: judgments now get 30 s until the value moves to the agent. A suite that raised it for a slow page keeps it and loses nothing. Changeset included. ---

title: feat(engine): placeholder names in the tree and a truncated flag on the snapshot
body: ## What and why - An unlabeled search box observed as a bare `textbox`: the tree-mode attribute allowlist had no `placeholder` and `accessibleName` had no placeholder fallback (`packages/playwright/src/read-node.ts`). The `placeholder` descriptor that cache relocation already matches on could never be recorded. - The reader now names text-like inputs and textareas by placeholder in HTML-AAM 4.1.1 order: `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, label, `title`, `placeholder`, `aria-placeholder`. A search input observes as `searchbox "Search products"`, a labeled field keeps its label, and `placeholder` rides along as an attribute so a replay relocates by it. - The 3000-node cap ended a walk quietly. `EngineSnapshot` gains an optional `truncated` flag; the playwright engine sets it when the cap stops a document, or when an on-site child frame's document goes unread (no budget or time left, past the depth limit, a failed capture). Off-site frames are left out by design and never count. The device engine reads whole trees and never sets it. - The runner merges the engine flag with its own byte cut into one `truncated` on the agent observation: a marker at the end of the listing, a prompt line saying nodes past the cut are on screen but not listed, a truncated screen never reported unchanged, and the failure evidence header marking the listing truncated whichever limit cut it. - Docs: `reference/engine.mdx` carries the new member and what the runner does with it; `writing-an-engine.mdx` tells engine authors to cap unbounded trees, set the flag, and name nodes the way the platform's accessibility layer does. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[read-node walk] -- node cap hit --> T[truncated: true] C[captureDocument] -- no budget for a child frame --> T T --> S[EngineSnapshot.truncated] S --> O[prepareObservation] B[byte budget cut] --> O O --> M["marker + prompt line + never 'unchanged'"] ``` Before and after, the testbed's todo input (``): | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `#n7 textbox placeholder="What needs doing?"` | `#n7 textbox "What needs doing?"` | Tests: `packages/playwright/tests/integration/read-node-names.test.ts` drives the real reader for the name order, the attribute, and the flag on a cut walk, an unentered on-site frame, a frame past the depth limit, and an off-site frame that must not count; `packages/e2e/tests/unit/relocate-placeholder.test.ts` covers relocation by placeholder alone; `agent-observation.test.ts` covers the merged flag and marker choice. Agent testbed live: 11/11, unchanged. Closes ENG-712. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(release): canary publishes in its own step and refuses a stale dist
body:
## Why

Three canaries today (`0.15.0-canary-20260914081513`, `…095510`, `…132830`) shipped the same byte-identical `dist`, compiled before the package rename in #294. Their `dist/mcp/tools.js` still holds `import { asSchema } from 'ai'`, so every `npx e2e` command, including `init` and `--help`, crashes with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `ai`. The fix from #296 has been on main since 11:39 but never reached npm.

Cause: the publish was run as a bare `pnpm changeset publish --tag canary --no-git-tag`, because npm's two-factor prompt for a hardware key has to be answered at the terminal and the one-shot `canary` script did not fit that. That command packs whatever `dist` is on disk. Evidence in the tarballs: `dist/cli/init/engine-versions.json` names `@e2edev/playwright` `0.10.0` and still carries the driver key the build stopped writing in #298; `dist/collect/select.js` still says `@e2edev/e2e`; `package.json` in the same tarball is current.

## What

- `canary` now stops after the build (changeset, `changeset version --snapshot`, build). `canary:publish` runs `changeset publish --tag canary --no-git-tag` as its own interactive step. CI's `release` script is unchanged.
- `scripts/stamp-dist.ts`: every package build ends by writing `dist/.build.json` with the version it compiled for.
- `scripts/check-dist.ts`: each package's `prepublishOnly` compares that stamp with `package.json`. A missing or mismatched stamp fails `pnpm publish`, and therefore `changeset publish`, naming the package and both versions. `changeset publish` runs `pnpm publish` inside each package directory, so the hook fires for `canary:publish` and for a hand-typed `changeset publish` alike.
- CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS describe the two-step flow.

## Verified

- Fresh `pnpm run build` stamps all four packages; the check passes.
- Stale stamp and missing stamp both exit 1 with the message.
- `pnpm publish --dry-run --no-git-checks` in `packages/e2e` with a stale stamp stops at `prepublishOnly`.
- A fresh HEAD build packed and installed into an empty directory with no `ai` present runs `e2e --help` cleanly.

title: feat(playwright): web.frameLocator keeps locator and frameLocator inside the frame
body: ## What and why - `web.frameLocator` returned the portable `Screen`, so inside a frame there was no CSS escape hatch and no second frame boundary. A file input with no label or a drop zone that is an empty `div` could not be reached, and a nested frame needed `web.evaluate`. Two selenium testbed tests were skipped for exactly this. - It now returns `FrameScreen`: the same scoped `Screen`, plus `locator(selector)` and `frameLocator(selector)` bound to that frame. Both compile through the frame chain every query in the scope already uses, so actionability, settle, and `expect` retries are unchanged. An empty selector at any level throws `INVALID_LOCATOR`. - Playwright engine only. The portable `Screen`, `LocatorExpression`, and the engine SPI are untouched; the projection in `packages/playwright/src/locators.ts` already compiled `frame` around `selector`. ENG-708 asked for `screen.locator` on core `Screen`; keeping the hatch on the web surface matches `web.locator` and `device.locator` and keeps `Screen` portable. - The frame chain is a list of selectors, outermost first, folded once (`packages/playwright/src/web.ts`): ```ts function frameScreen(context: EngineFixtureContext, frames: readonly string[]): FrameScreen { const scope = (expression: LocatorExpression): LocatorExpression => frames.reduceRight((source, selector) => ({ kind: 'frame', selector, source }), expression); return Object.assign(context.screen(scope), { locator: (selector: string) => context.locator(scope({ kind: 'selector', selector: requireSelector('locator', selector) })), frameLocator: (selector: string) => frameScreen(context, [...frames, requireSelector('frameLocator', selector)]), }); } ``` - In a test: ```ts const result = web.frameLocator('#iframeResult'); await result.locator('#myFile').setInputFiles('fixtures/attachment.txt'); await result.locator('#drag1').dragTo(result.locator('#div1')); await expect(result.frameLocator('iframe').getByText('displayed in an iframe', { exact: false })).toBeVisible(); ``` - Testbed: both skipped iframe tests are un-skipped and the nested-frames test drops its `evaluate` workaround. Docs: `reference/playwright.mdx` carries the `FrameScreen` block and error semantics, `browser.mdx` says when to prefer role queries, and the skill's `web` table notes the hatches. Closes ENG-708. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(report): the run page is paragraphs a reader can skim; flaky tests and the file list fold away
body:
## What and why - The live comments on tester-army/app were a wall: a 17-row all-green file table, a flaky test rendered as a full failure block on a green run, a `Steps:` line of eight locator strings, two footer lines, and two comments per PR that read identically. - A green run is now the headline, the folds, and one line of small print. The visible file table is gone; each file's counts, agent work, and time sit on its heading inside the `All N tests in M files` fold (`packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts`, `fileHeading`). - Flaky tests fold under one summary, `⚠️ 1 flaky test passed on a retry`. The run is green and the headline counts them, so the block is there for the reader who asks. - A failure block is short paragraphs instead of five lines glued with hard breaks: the title; one lead naming the error and the step; what the error and the agent said, quoted; the facts as a list; the source link and the evidence. The file is named once, in the source link. - Cut from the block: the step timeline (the lead says where in the flow it was, the trace has the rest), the message line when it only says `expect.x failed`, the `Passed after 1 failed attempt` line under a fold that says so, and the loopback origin on screen URLs, which nobody reading a PR can open. - `MarkdownReportOptions.title` names the page in the headline. `github()` passes its `key`, so `github({ key: 'regression' })` posts `e2e regression: …` and the agent job posts `e2e agent: …`. - The failure page (`.e2e/failures/*.md`) picks up the same rules: locator labels as code, no facts line repeating the code block above it. All 78 tests…

title: feat(report): the live line says Observing or Acting while the device works, Thinking only for the model
body: ## What and why - The live line under a running agent step said `Thinking` between events, on the assumption that tool calls take milliseconds and the model is the one working. On a device that is false: a snapshot of a busy screen takes up to 16 s and a tap up to 10 s, and all of it read as model time. In an App Store audit of Bluesky, 117 s of a 235 s file were observation and 35 s were actions; the terminal showed `Thinking` throughout. - Step progress gains an `activity` phase. `instrumentPhase`, the one place every observe, model, and action phase of an agent step goes through, announces `observe`, `action`, or `model` as the phase begins; the `event` that follows ends it. The list reporter renders `Observing`, `Acting`, `Thinking`, or `Replaying` from that. A cache probe announces nothing. - Additive on the `RunEvent` stream: `{ type: 'step', progress: { phase: 'activity', api, activity } }`. Reporters that switch on `phase` and ignore unknown values are unaffected. Documented in the reporters reference. ## Evidence Before, during a 16 s device snapshot after a tap: ``` └── 4.2 is a real app, not a wrapped website or static brochure ↳ agent.act "get to the main screen of the app: past any splash, welcome, or onboa… › tap other "Discover" (10.44s) ✽ Thinking ``` After, the same moment: ``` › tap other "Discover" (10.44s) ✽ Observing ``` The `--debug` phase table that exposed it: ``` phase count total avg max agent.model 18 117.8s 6546ms 26.3s agent.observe 24 116.9s 4870ms 16.5s agent.action 10 35.3s 3525ms 10.4s ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(agent-device): a snapshot the runner restart could not deliver is asked for once more
body: ## What and why - agent-device restarts its iOS runner once per request when the XCTest accessibility capture fails, then gives up with `iOS runner was already restarted during this request and "snapshot" still failed`. The engine translated that to `ENGINE_FAILURE`, the observation failed, and the step died as `APP_UNREACHABLE`, ending the test. - It happens on screens whose accessibility tree is slow to walk: a live feed re-rendering under the capture. The runner log shows dozens of `kAXErrorIllegalArgument getting snapshot for element` in a row on Bluesky's home feed. The runner is back after the restart; the screen just had not settled. - The engine now asks once more after a 2 s pause, one extra request, which gets one more restart on a settled screen. A second failure surfaces as before. The sparse-tree retry ladder is unchanged and wraps the new single retry. ## Evidence The failure, from two independent App Store audit runs against Bluesky: ``` FAIL |ios-simulator| tests-appstore/business.e2e.ts > 3.1.1 and 3.1.2: digital goods use in-app purchase … APP_UNREACHABLE | snapshot failed: iOS runner was already restarted during this request and "snapshot" still failed, so agent-device stopped instead of paying for another runner boot. ``` The runner log behind it: ``` error: -[AgentDeviceRunnerUITests.RunnerTests testCommand] : Failed to resolve query: Error kAXErrorIllegalArgument getting snapshot for element {pid=87789} error: -[AgentDeviceRunnerUITests.RunnerTests testCommand] : Failed to resolve query: Error kAXErrorIllegalArgument getting snapshot for element {pid=87789} … (19 more) AGENT_DEVICE_RUNNER_COMMAND_COMPLETED command=snapshot ok=1 ``` Unit tests cover the retry succeeding on the second request and failing after two. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(agent): vision on act, a pixels-only vocabulary, and a keyboard engine capability
body:
## What and why

- `agent.act` takes `vision`, the option the judgments already had, with one meaning on both tiers: how much pixel evidence is pushed to the model. `false`, the default, pushes none; the act model pulls pixels itself with `screenshot` and `tap_at`, as before. `true` attaches a masked screenshot to every judgment call and every act turn. `'only'` does that and withholds the tree from the executor for the whole step: the model sees a screenshot and nothing else.
- The wait for an action's effect compares the tree alone on a screen that lists any interactive node (a focus ring otherwise moves the pixels before a delayed change lands), and `waitFor` skips judgments while tree and pixel digest are unchanged.
- Under `'only'` the built-in agent offers a point-addressed vocabulary: `tap_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, `select_at`, `scroll` at a point, `observe`, `navigate`. Every point is hit-tested against the tree the runner still holds (`actions.hitTest`), so a listed control is acted on by id underneath, recorded with a descriptor, replayed from the cache, and never named to the model by id.
- A pixels-only step refuses a `Secret` in its params and a tainted viewport with `POLICY_DENIED` before it opens: a fill would withhold the only evidence.
- Engines gain a `keyboard` capability (`type` into focus with opt-in `replace`, `press`, optional `dismiss`). It is the primitive for a field the tree cannot fill: drawn on a canvas, or flattened out of a platform's accessibility tree, the mobile case. The default `type` and `press` take no target on such an engine, a `type` by id on an unfillable node falls back to the focused field, `type_at` and `press_at` fall back to tap-then-type, and a device offers `dismiss_keyboard`. Parity with TesterArmy's `ui_fill focused/replace`, `pressKey`, and `ui_dismiss_keyboard`.
- The browser engine refuses focused typing when nothing that takes keystrokes has focus (body, button, link, select, non-text input), so keystrokes never vanish into the page.

```ts
await agent.act('enter the code 3141 on the drawn keypad and press OK', { vision: 'only' });
await agent.act('fill the drawn form: Name is Ada, City is Oslo, then press Submit', { vision: 'only' });
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[model: type_at x,y] --> H{listed control under the point?}
  H -- yes --> F[fill by id, descriptor recorded]
  H -- no, keyboard --> T[tapAt to focus] --> K[keyboard.type into focus]
  H -- no, no keyboard --> E[action failure the model reads]
```

Live on the testbed with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast`, no cache:

| Flow | Mode | Model calls | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drawn keypad, 5 digits + OK | only | 7 | $0.005 |
| Drawn 8-screen wizard | only | 17 | $0.013 |
| Todo page driven blind (`type_at` → `textbox "New todo"`) | only | 6 | $0.0035 |
| Drawn two-field form + Submit | only | 4 | $0.002 |
| Drawn two-field form + Submit | default (tap_at, then `type` without target) | 7 | $0.005 |

Key seams: `packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-feed.ts` (tree withheld, pixels forced), `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts` (`createPixelTools`, `typeIntoNode`), `packages/e2e/src/engine/index.ts` (`EngineKeyboard`), `packages/playwright/src/surface.ts` (`requireEditableFocus`).

## Checklist

A charter that passes, fails, or exhausts its budget keeps the existing issues-only verdict. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Exploration ends] --> B{Issue reported?} B -- Yes --> C[Failed] B -- No --> D{Every charter blocked?} D -- Yes --> E[Blocked with first blocker] D -- No --> F[Existing verdict] ``` ## Checklist - [x] Patch changeset added for `e2e`. - [x] Docs and the exploration skill reference updated. - [x] No public API, report schema, or engine contract change. - [x] No breaking change. ---

title: fix(report): identify live steps across retries
body: ## What and why - Live step phases lacked the IDs needed to distinguish retries and nested calls. Every phase now includes the owning attempt and step identity from the final report. - Serial members share their group's attempt ID and retain distinct step IDs. End phases carry the redacted step error and explanation so adapters can preserve blocked and cancelled outcomes. - `identity` is optional in the public type so reporters can still accept older event streams. No report schema changes. ```ts if (event.type === 'step' && event.progress.identity) { const { attemptId, attemptIndex, stepId, stepIndex } = event.progress.identity; // Indexes start at zero; stepId joins every phase to its report record. } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Attempt 0 / step A] --> B[Failed end with error] B --> C[Attempt 1 / step B] C --> D[Passed end] D --> E[Final report retains both attempts] ``` ## Checklist - [x] Patch changeset added for `e2e`. - [x] Reporter docs and running skill reference updated. - [x] Emitted declarations reviewed and compile-time assertions updated. - [x] No breaking change, report schema change, or engine contract change. ---

title: fix(agent): recover semantic timeouts with masked pixels
body: ## What and why - A semantic reader timeout prevented the agent from reaching screenshot fallback. One capture coordinator bounds the complete semantic read and reserves time for a fresh screenshot and an independent secure-field mask sweep. - Node IDs are reserved before a reader starts. Timed-out readers cannot cause another element to receive their IDs, and late captures cannot publish references after their capture or session has been superseded. - The engine contract marks unavailable semantics explicitly. Core normalizes semantic and pixel-only evidence separately. Acting steps receive the fallback image and reuse that opening capture once. Normal screenshots are requested through `observe({ pixels: true })` or model tools; judgments honor their vision settings. - Missing semantics reset the presenter's node history and stop trace caching for the step while preserving the captured screenshot and location. - Secret taint, failed masking, cancellation, and hard failures still stop capture. Agent-device keeps failing closed because its screenshot masks depend on the accessibility capture. - `report-v1` accepts a failed judgment capture before any model call without invented observation or verdict fields. Successful judgments still require evidence. The schema, both fixtures, and the agent reference document the condition; the report version remains unchanged. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Semantic capture times out] --> B{Pixels permitted?} B -- No --> F[Capture fails] B -- Yes --> C[Fresh mask sweep and screenshot] C --> D{Every mask probe succeeds?} D -- No --> F D -- Yes --> E[Explicit unavailable tree plus screenshot] ``` ```ts interface EngineObserveOptions { pixels?: boolean; pixelFallback?: boolean; } // A fallback snapshot carries treeUnavailable: true, only the stable root // reference, and fresh pixels whose masking was proven independently. ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changesets cover `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. - [x] Agent, engine, Playwright, device, executor docs and the consumer skill updated. - [x] Emitted declarations and compile-time assertions reviewed. - [x] Report schema and both fixtures updated. - [x] No breaking change. ---

title: feat(playwright): recover persistent CDP sessions
body:
## What and why

Depends on #317; merge the semantic-fallback PR first.

- A dropped CDP transport previously ended the attempt. `connect.reconnectEndpoint` enables recovery before the next operation, using the original persistent default context and page target.
- Ordinary Playwright contexts disappear on detach. The opt-in mode requires a fresh, dedicated browser per attempt and rejects reused contexts, missing pages, and replacement browsers. The host owns browser deletion.
- Each attempt owns its connection, references, and recordings. Recovery publishes the replacement binding after setup succeeds. Reads from an earlier connection cannot publish observations or satisfy the fresh-observation requirement for agent coordinate, root, and focused keyboard actions. Trusted `web.mouse` and `web.keyboard` calls use input supplied by test code. Recovery never repeats an operation already dispatched.
- Endpoint resolution, attachment, setup, and dispatch share the operation budget. Exhaustion raises `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`; caller or attempt cancellation raises `CANCELLED`. This mode does not support context replacement, session snapshots, `headers`, or `basicAuth`.
- Playwright 1.63 omits custom selectors from CDP default contexts. A contained compatibility adapter installs the closed-root masking selector through Playwright's context channel before publishing the binding. Unsupported channel versions fail the connection. Recovery also refuses documents that lost secure-field tracking while disconnected; it cannot reconstruct existing closed roots safely.

```ts
playwright({
  connect: {
    cdpEndpoint: provisionFreshBrowser,
    reconnectEndpoint: resolveExistingBrowser,
  },
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Transport drops] --> B[Next operation]
  B --> C[Resolve existing browser]
  C --> D{Same context and page?}
  D -- No --> E[Attempt fails]
  D -- Yes --> F[Restore handlers and recording]
  F --> G[Publish new connection generation]
  G --> H[Continue within the remaining budget]
```

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added for `@e2edev/playwright`.
- [x] Playwright docs, README, and setup skill reference updated.
- [x] Emitted declarations reviewed and compile-time assertions added.
- [x] No breaking change, report schema change, or `e2e/engine` contract change.

Scenario files stay line-for-line with the source so they port both ways. - Scenarios distilled from customer apps no longer name the company, trace id, or ticket (three files: FlattenedForm, SequentialOnboarding, the registry). The README states the rule. - App shell rebranded to `dev.e2e.benchmark`; EAS project link, EAS Update, and `expo-updates` dropped since they belong to the TesterArmy account. - `e2e.config.ts` + `tests/`: 11 locator-only tests. `e2e.agent.config.ts` + `tests-agent/`: one `agent.act` per scenario, with the scenarios the harness cannot finish yet skipped by reason and the Apple Pay ones scoped to iOS. - The Expo project sits at the package root (Metro, CNG, and autolinking read config from cwd) and stays CommonJS; the suites typecheck through `tsconfig.tests.json` with Bundler resolution. - Root wiring: AGENTS.md entry, `test:mobile-benchmark` script, fallow entries, lockfile. title: feat(agent)!: drop vision from act, the model asks for pixels itself
body: ## What and why - `agent.act` had three vision tiers (`false`, `true`, `'only'`) where `false` already meant "tree first, the model pulls pixels with `screenshot` when it needs them". The other two were config deciding what the model should decide. This removes the option from `act`, from `agents..vision`, and from the executor socket (`ctx.vision`), along with the pixel-only rules, the tree-withheld observation path, and the up-front pixel policy check. - The point verbs `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at` were only available under `'only'`. They are the fallback for a target the tree does not list, so they now sit in the default vocabulary next to `screenshot` and `tap_at`, offered while pixels may leave the runner and gone together once a secret taints the attempt. Every point is still hit-tested onto the tree, so a listed control is acted on by id underneath and replays from the trace cache. Before any screenshot they answer with the line that says to take one and spend nothing. - The rules gain one instruction: act by id whenever the screen lists the target, use the point tools only for a target it does not list, and take a screenshot before naming a point. - `vision` stays on the judgments (`assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`) with `false` as the only default; a visual assertion still needs it and the model cannot infer it. A custom executor's `agent.assert` rejects `vision` like it rejects `screenshot`. Default vocabulary of the built-in agent on the browser engine, before and after: | | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | id verbs | observe, tap, type, press, select, scroll, navigate, type_secret | same | | pixel verbs | screenshot, tap_at | screenshot, tap_at, type_at, press_at, select_at | | modes | `vision: false \| true \| 'only'` | none, the model decides | Errors: `vision` on `act` is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` naming the judgment options; `agents..vision` is an unknown key. The unreleased #314 changeset loses its vision half and keeps the keyboard capability and point verbs; a new changeset records the removal. Not done here: the six-month deprecation window the stability policy asks for. `agents..vision` predates #314, so this is a hard removal of a released config key; the changeset names the replacement. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). title: feat(engine)!: the pointer side of the contract is a vocabulary, finished before it locks
body: ## What and why - The audit of the engine SPI found one shape that could not grow after 1.0: node actions had 15 kinds, a bare point had one verb, `tapAt`. Desktop, canvas, and pixels-only bodies need the rest, and the sandbox engine already faked a `#screen` node to get fill, press, and swipe at a point. `tapAt(point)` is now `performAt(point, action)` with a required `pointerActions` list, the same shape as `perform` and `actions`. The adapter gates each kind; the agent's `tap_at` verb needs the `tap` kind in either list. The executor API (`ctx.actions.tapAt`) is unchanged. - `secondaryTap` joins the action kinds and `Locator.secondaryTap()` performs it: a right click on the web, a two-finger tap elsewhere. Context menus were unreachable before. - Nodes report `pressed` and `level`; `getByRole` takes both, so a toggle button and a heading level are queries on every engine. Playwright reads `aria-pressed`, `aria-level`, and the `h1` to `h6` digit; the device tree reports neither, so such a query matches nothing rather than everything. - `EngineSnapshot.viewport` drops `scale`. Every engine reported 1 and nothing read it; `ObservationPixels.scale` is the real image-to-CSS ratio. The report's step viewport and `attachViewport` keep theirs, so report-1 is untouched. - `Platform`, `ScrollDirection`, `Momentum`, and `SelectOption` move into `e2e/engine` and the SDK re-exports them: the contract owns its vocabulary instead of importing it from the test API. - `spiVersion` stays `1`; this lands before the lock, so no deprecation window. ```ts export type PointerAction = | { kind: 'tap' | 'doubleTap' | 'secondaryTap' | 'hover' } | { kind: 'longPress'; durationMs?: number } | { kind: 'dragTo'; target: ViewportPoint } | { kind: 'swipe'; direction: ScrollDirection; momentum?: Momentum }; defineEngine({ // ... performAt: (point, action, ctx) => surface.performAt(point, action, ctx), pointerActions: ['tap', 'doubleTap', 'longPress'], }); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[model: tap_at x,y] --> H{listed control under the point?} H -- yes --> N["perform(node, tap)"] H -- no --> G{"'tap' in pointerActions?"} G -- yes --> P["performAt(point, tap)"] G -- no --> U[UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY] ``` | Engine | `pointerActions` | | --- | --- | | `@e2edev/playwright` | tap, doubleTap, secondaryTap, longPress, hover, dragTo, swipe | | `@e2edev/agent-device` | tap, doubleTap, longPress | Key seams: `packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts` (`PointerAction`, `POINTER_ACTION_KINDS`, `pressed`, `level`), `packages/e2e/src/engine/manifest.ts` (`declaredKinds`), `packages/e2e/src/engine/session.ts` (`performAt` gate, `tapAt` verb derivation), `packages/playwright/src/surface.ts` (`performAt`), `packages/playwright/tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts` (every pointer kind read back from a page event log). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). No deprecation window: pre-1.0 contract, same as #291. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No wire change; `sdk-types.ts` pins none of the touched types. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(runner): single-file setup selection, runtime skip, more matchers
feat(agent)!: phone keyboards, replayable device flows, full mobile benchmark
body:
## What and why

- The mobile benchmark app did not launch: Expo's prebuilt `ExpoModulesCore` 57.0.10 imports a JSI symbol only `expo-modules-jsi` 57.0.4 exported, so any locally built JSI died at start with a dyld `Symbol missing`. `expo` 57.0.22 and `expo-modules-core` 57.0.18 pair with JSI 57.1.0 and launch unpatched on Xcode 27.
- The deterministic iOS suite now covers every scenario locators can reach (20 tests, one skipped: `doubleTap` never lands in the app's 300 ms window). The fixture drags the home list in quarter steps because iOS lists only rows fully on screen and reports final frames while a fling is still moving; forms dismiss the keyboard before a tap because React Native spends that tap on closing it.
- The built-in agent learns the phone keyboard from its own traces: an action result says when it closed the keyboard, `dismiss_keyboard` names the blank point that closes it when the device has no dismiss key, `tap_at` takes a viewport point before a screenshot, a repeated `scroll` keeps going when the device renumbers or renames the list under it, and the rules refuse a `passed` verdict on a result that shows no change. The agentic suite goes from 11 of 14 to 23 of 24, with the pixel-only screens, both Apple Pay sheets, Stripe, and the photo picker among the new passes. Rebased on #323: the scenarios pass no `vision` to `act`; the pixel-only ones tell the model the screen lists nothing and the model asks for the screenshot itself.
- The trace cache replays mobile flows: a typed value is a gap only when read off the screen or reckoned from the date, consecutive scrolls fold into one recorded action replayed with the list re-found per repeat, and a recorded point tap falls back to its point when the node is gone. `type_text` leaves the device pack because the grammar's `type` covers it and replays.

## Evidence

Agentic suite, iOS simulator, `gpt-5.6-luna-fast`, cache off:

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| scenarios passing | 11 of 14 runnable | 23 of 24 (three consecutive runs) |
| Sequential Onboarding | 17 to 20 model calls, ~190k tokens | 15 model calls, 149k tokens |

Record-then-replay pairs, steps that replay with zero model calls:

| | steps |
| --- | ---: |
| before | 9 of 23 |
| run-time value rule, folded scrolls, point fallback, no `type_text` | 12 of 23 |
| list re-found per repeat with viewport fallback | 16 of 23 |

Of the seven that still involve the model, four are by design (a coupon and a code read off the screen, a secret typed in plaintext, the device `swipe` project tool), two are timing and photo-grid ambiguity, one (Stripe) types a value the rule still flags.

Deterministic suite: 20 passed, 1 skipped, three consecutive runs. After the rebase onto #323 and #324 the agentic suite reran on the rebased build: 22 of 23 on the full run, the huge list failing on an exhausted action budget once the device renumbered the list mid-scroll, then both list scenarios green after the scroll fix above. Unit suites, lint, typecheck, and docs checks green on the rebased tree.

Follow-ups: a gesture family in the grammar (swipe, long press, double tap) would close Gestures, replay Async States, and remove the last device-pack gap; replay could wait for a debounced list before the next target.

title: feat(cache): unique() params keep the trace cache replaying across runs
feat(jev): step executor driven by TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model
body:
## What and why - Jev (`typesafe-ai/jev` on the AI Gateway) is an evaluation model: it answers typed questions with probabilities and generates no text. An act turn is that shape once the vocabulary is enumerated, so `packages/jev` plugs it into the public executor seam as `jevAgent()`. - One `experimental_evaluate` per turn decides `done`, `pending`, verb, target node, scroll region and value in parallel, in 300 to 1100 ms. Node ids come from the observation, never from the model. Values come from the literals the step quotes; an open value goes to a generative `fallback`, secrets go through `typeSecret`. - Assertions are one boolean question. Same harness budgets, recording and trace cache as the default agent. - `escalateTo` hands a step to a generative executor from the current screen when Jev gives up, stalls, picks without conviction twice, or runs the call budget down to a reserve. Jev's actions travel as an already-performed prefix. This is TypeSafe's confidence-routing pattern on a test step; eve's `autoModel` uses Jev the other way round, as a model router. - Research and iteration notes are in the package README; this is a private package and a benchmark arm, not a published API. ```ts agents: { default: { executor: jevAgent({ fallback: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna') }), model: gateway('openai/gpt-5.6-luna'), }, }, ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR O[observe] --> P[parse node lines into candidates] P --> Q{"> 255 candidates?"} Q -- yes --> R[evaluate: which page] --> E Q -- no --> E["evaluate: done, pending, action, target, scrollTarget, value"] E --> G{"done ≥ 0.6, pending ≤ 0.4,
no confident next action?"} G -- yes --> V[passed] G -- no --> A[dispatch verb through the grammar] A --> D[diff screen shape, quiet-screen rechecks] --> O ``` ### Web benchmark (`tests-agent`, cache off, 20 scenarios) | | default agent, `gpt-5.6-luna-fast` | `jevAgent`, Luna as value fallback | `jevAgent` + `escalateTo` default agent | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | passed | 20 / 20 | 17 / 20 (16–17 over four runs) | 20 / 20 | | run wall time | 232 s | 218 s | 249 s | | model calls | 91 | 152 | 149 | | run cost | $0.056 | $0.022 | $0.034 | | typical act step | 5–23 s | 1–5 s | 1–5 s, 25–55 s when escalated | - With escalation, 5 of 21 agent steps were handed over (`lying-labels`, `hover-menu`, `infinite-scroll`, `date-picker`, the wishlist bug-book step); 16 never left Jev. - Jev-only misses, same on every run: `lying-labels` (fills by accessible name, not visible label), `hover-menu` (follows the forbidden back link, loops to budget), `filter-deep-link` (taps the filled box instead of judging done). - `date-picker` was a false pass mid-iteration: done 0.90 with "Confirm booking" still pending. The `pending` question and the contradiction rule in `packages/jev/src/agent.ts` close it. - Scratch loop on TodoMVC and Sauce Demo: 11/11 steps, three repeats with identical trajectories; 16/16 assertions against one screen in a single 0.9 s call. ### Demo `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... pnpm --filter @e2edev/jev demo:headed` runs the TodoMVC suite headed with a video per attempt: 10 agent steps, about 20 s, $0.0015. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: fix(collect): glob forms that match nothing are INVALID_GLOB
body:
## What and why

- A config `tests` glob spelled in a form the grammar lacks is `INVALID_GLOB` with the fix in the message, instead of a pattern that matches nothing and surfaces as `NO_TESTS`: braces, character classes (`*.e2e.[jt]s`), extglobs, a backslash separator, an absolute path, a `..` segment, a trailing `/` or `.`.
- A leading `./`, a `.` segment, and a doubled `/` are dropped. `./tests/**/*.e2e.ts` used to match nothing, walk `.git` and `.e2e` (its `.` segment made every dot directory eligible), and then say "create tests/example.e2e.ts" beside the files it missed, because the near-miss scan rooted itself under `./tests`.
- Segments without wildcards compile to names, so the near-miss scan reads the directory a glob starts in off the segments (`literalPrefix`) instead of re-parsing a pattern string, and the positional "is this a glob" test is the grammar's own `GLOB_SYNTAX`.
- Positionals: an existing file or directory is selected by its path whatever its name is spelled with, and a positional that exists nowhere and carries braces, brackets, or an extglob gets the grammar's hint instead of "no test file matched". `./`, `..`, a trailing `/`, and absolute paths inside the project were already resolved for positionals and still are.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests: './tests/**/*.e2e.ts'` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched "./tests/**/*.e2e.ts" under /proj; create tests/example.e2e.ts (e2e init writes one), or set tests in the config` | the tests under `tests/` |
| `tests: 'tests/**/*.e2e.[jt]s'` | `NO_TESTS` | `INVALID_GLOB: character classes are unsupported, use ? or list one glob per alternative: tests/**/*.e2e.[jt]s` |
| `tests: 'tests/**/'` | `NO_TESTS` | `INVALID_GLOB: a glob names files, so it cannot end with "/": tests/**/; add a file pattern such as *.e2e.ts` |
| `e2e run 'tests/{a,b}.e2e.ts'` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched tests/{a,b}.e2e.ts` | `INVALID_GLOB: brace expansion is unsupported, list one glob per alternative: tests/{a,b}.e2e.ts` |

Behavior change worth knowing: a glob can no longer name a file whose own name contains braces or brackets; the path still selects it.

Code: `compileGlob` and `literalPrefix` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/globs.ts`; `positionalMatcher` and the near-miss scan in `packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts`.

title: fix(collect): validate tags and the tests globs where they are written
body:
## What and why

- `tags` is validated at registration, beside `timeout`, `retries`, and `agent`: a list of distinct names, none blank, with no comma and no leading or trailing whitespace, which is exactly what `--tag` can spell back (the flag splits on commas and trims). Inner spaces are legal, so `tags: ['Login Form']` as the mobile benchmark declares keeps collecting. A bare string is iterable, so `tags: 'smoke'` used to register the tags `s`, `m`, `o`, `k`, `e`; `--tag smoke` never matched it and `--tag s` did. Numbers, empty strings, and duplicates passed, and a non-iterable value threw a raw TypeError at selection.
- A registration error now names its file: `COLLECTION_ERROR: tests/b.e2e.ts: test options: tags must be a list of tag names, e.g. tags: ['smoke'], got "smoke"`. Before, `timeout`, `retries`, `agent`, and now `tags` errors named the option but not the module.
- `tests` is validated when the config resolves: a glob or a list of globs, each compiled there. A wrong type was a raw TypeError reported as a test failure with exit 1 (at config load for `tests: 5`, at collection for `tests: [1]`); it is `INVALID_CONFIG`, exit 2. A malformed glob was `INVALID_GLOB` only once a run or `e2e list` collected, so `e2e explore`, `e2e mcp`, and `e2e cache` accepted a config no run could use; they refuse it now.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test('x', { tags: 'smoke' }, ...)`, then `e2e run --tag smoke` | `NO_TESTS: 1 tests were collected but none is runnable: 1 carry none of the tags smoke` | `COLLECTION_ERROR: tests/a.e2e.ts: test options: tags must be a list of tag names, e.g. tags: ['smoke'], got "smoke"` |
| `tests: [1]` | `ERROR: pattern.startsWith is not a function`, exit 1 | `INVALID_CONFIG: tests must be a glob or a list of globs relative to the project root, got 1 in the list`, exit 2 |
| `tests: 'tests/**foo/*.ts'` with `e2e cache stats` | accepted | `INVALID_GLOB: '**' must be a complete path segment: tests/**foo/*.ts` |

title: fix(cli): --tag takes comma lists and NO_TESTS names the nearest tag
body:
Stacked on #333 (it reads the tags the identity carries). The base moves to `main` once #333 merges.

## What and why

- The list-valued selection flags share one parser (`parseNames` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`): `--tag`, `--target`, and `--agent` each take a comma-separated list or repeats, each name once, and an empty value (`--tag ''`, or `--tag "$TAGS"` with the variable unset) is a usage error with exit 2. Before, `--tag smoke,billing` looked for one tag literally named that, `--tag ''` failed later as `NO_TESTS` over an empty tag name, and an empty `--target` or `--agent` silently selected every target or the default agents. `--target` now accumulates on repeat, as `--agent` did.
- `NO_TESTS` blames the tag filter only for the tests it filtered. Pairs are `filtered` for three reasons (a file no positional named, not focused by `.only`, a tag mismatch); the old message counted all three as tag mismatches whenever a tag filter existed, so `e2e run b.e2e.ts --tag smoke` reported a test tagged `smoke` in another file as carrying none of the tags. The reasons are shared constants written by `classifyPair` and read back by `describeNoTests`.
- Under `--tag-mode all` the message reads `do not carry all of the tags smoke, billing` instead of `carry none of`, and every filter tag no test declares is marked, with the nearest declared tag when one is close.

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e2e list --tag smoke,billing` | `NO_TESTS: 4 tests were collected but none is runnable: 4 carry none of the tags smoke,billing` | the tests tagged `smoke` or `billing` |
| `e2e list --tag smok` | `... 4 carry none of the tags smok` | `... 4 carry none of the tags smok (did you mean smoke?)` |
| `e2e list b.e2e.ts --tag smoke`, `smoke` declared only in `a.e2e.ts` | `... 2 carry none of the tags smoke` | `... 1 file not selected by a positional argument, 1 carry none of the tags smoke` |
| `e2e run --target ''` | every target | `error: option '--target <ids>' argument '' is invalid. must name at least one target`, exit 2 |

Code: `parseNames` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`, `FILTERED_REASON` and `describeTagFilter` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`, `suggestionNote` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/suggest.ts`.

title: feat(report): tags travel with a test into e2e list and the report
body:
Stacked on #331: the tag-name rule it validates is what the report schema promises here. The base moves to `main` once #331 merges.

## What and why

- Tags stopped at selection: they were not in the report, either `e2e list` output, junit, or markdown, so no reporter could group by tag and nobody could see which tags a suite has.
- Registration derives a test's tags once (`declaredTags` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`, beside `titlePath`: the describe chain's tags outermost first, then the test's own, each once). `TestIdentity.tags` carries them across the worker wire and into every result record; `ResolvedTestOptions` no longer holds a copy, and the `--tag` filter reads the identity.
- `e2e list` prints each tag after the target, bounded like every other untrusted field; `--reporter json` gives every pair a `tags` array.
- `run.results[]` in the report always carry `tags`, `[]` when none, as every other array in report-1 is always present. Schema: a result gains an optional `tags` array, distinct, each item matching the tag-name rule (no comma, no leading or trailing whitespace, not blank); a targeted schema test and both fixtures cover it.

```console
$ e2e list
tests/billing.e2e.ts › checkout › pays [web] #smoke #billing
tests/billing.e2e.ts › checkout › refunds [web] #billing
tests/home.e2e.ts › opens [web]
```

```json
{ "id": "…", "testId": "tests/billing.e2e.ts::checkout::pays", "tags": ["smoke", "billing"], "status": "passed" }
```

Scope: `e2e list` and the report. The live list reporter, junit, and markdown are unchanged; a live reporter already receives `result.test.tags` on `test-finished`.

Code: `declaredTags` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`, `formatListedPair` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`, `serializeResult` in `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts`.
