title: perf(collect): walk only directories a tests glob can match beneath
body:
Stacked on #330 (both change the glob module); the base moves to `main` once that merges.

## What and why

- Every `e2e run` and `e2e list` read every directory but `node_modules` under the config's directory (`apps/`, `build/`, `coverage/`, and so on), then filtered the files against the globs. Discovery now lists the project root and enters a directory only while some glob still has a segment left to satisfy beneath it: `tests/**/*.e2e.ts` reads `tests/` and its subdirectories and nothing else.
- Matching runs a glob as a small state machine over the path's segments (`advance` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/globs.ts`): a state is the index of the segment to satisfy next, a `**` keeps its own state while it consumes parts and lets the segment after it start. `matchesGlob` folds a path through it; the walk carries each glob's states down the tree, so a directory costs one step instead of a match from the root. The previous recursive matcher and the separate pruning predicate are gone.
- A dot directory is entered only when a glob segment written with a leading dot matches it, which replaces the old whole-walk switch. Symlinks were never followed (a symlinked directory or test file was not discovered on `main` either); the config reference and the skill now say so.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["readdir(root)"] --> B{"any glob with a\nsegment left beneath apps/?"}
  B -- no --> C[skip apps/]
  A --> D{"beneath tests/?"}
  D -- yes --> E["readdir(tests/)"] --> F["file: state at end = match"]
```

| Tree (1.6k directories, 24k files outside `tests/`) | Directories read before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/**/*.e2e.ts` | every one but `node_modules` | `.`, `tests`, `tests/sub` |

Verified against oracles: the new matcher agrees with the previous recursive one on 200,000 random glob and path pairs, and discovery equals a walk-everything-then-filter brute force on 3,000 random tree and glob-set combinations. Pruning has no visible result of its own, so the unit test records the directories read through a `node:fs` mock; it reports `/`-separated paths on every OS and skips the symlink case where a symlink cannot be created.

title: feat(oauth): sign in with a ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, or SuperGrok subscription
body: ## What and why - An agent model no longer needs a pay-per-token key: `@e2edev/oauth` signs in to a plan the user already pays for and hands the runner an ordinary AI SDK model instance. The runner does not know the difference. - Three plans: ChatGPT Plus/Pro through the Codex OAuth client (browser PKCE on `localhost:1455`, or OpenAI's user-code flow with `--device`), GitHub Copilot (the GitHub CLI's token, or GitHub's device flow with `--client-id` for an OAuth App), SuperGrok / X Premium+ (xAI's RFC 8628 device flow). Claude Pro/Max is excluded: Anthropic's terms allow subscription sign-in only for its own applications. - No dependency: the deep search over npm and the OpenCode, OpenClaw, Kilo, Cline, and Vercel monorepos found no library that covers these three on AI SDK 7 without impersonating another client. The flows follow pi-ai's OAuth module and OpenCode's plugins. The package is fetch-based and self-contained so it can be extracted later. - New CLI commands `e2e login ` and `e2e logout `; `e2e init` offers the three plans next to the gateways and names the sign-in as the step before the first run. ```ts import { chatgpt } from '@e2edev/oauth/chatgpt'; // also: copilot from './copilot', grok from './grok' export default { targets: [{ engine: playwright({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }], agents: { default: createAgent({ model: chatgpt('gpt-5.5') }) }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR L[e2e login provider] --> F[OAuth flow: PKCE or device code] F --> S[(~/.config/e2e/oauth.json, 0600)] M[chatgpt / copilot / grok] --> P[vendor AI SDK provider] P --> X[createOAuthFetch] X --> S X --> R{expiring or 401?} R -- yes --> RF[refresh once per store and provider] RF --> S R -- no --> SND[provider.send: bearer, vendor headers, Codex URL and body, SSE fold] SND --> V[vendor API] ``` - `packages/oauth/src/fetch.ts`: the fetch every constructor builds. It captures the body once so the 401 retry can replay it, shares one in-flight refresh per store and provider across model instances (vendors rotate refresh tokens and reject the second concurrent refresh), and recovers a token another process rotated before reporting a lost login. - `packages/oauth/src/providers/openai.ts`: the Codex backend speaks only the streaming Responses API, so `send` forces `stream: true`, `store: false`, and `include: reasoning.encrypted_content`, and folds the completed event back into the JSON body `generateText` expects. - `packages/oauth/src/store.ts`: the file store locks its read-modify-write and drops a damaged entry instead of every login; `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` is a separate read-only store that refuses writes. - Live-verified: Copilot through the package with the GitHub CLI token (forced tool call over a screenshot on `gpt-4.1` and `claude-sonnet-5`), xAI's device flow issuing a code, the ChatGPT authorize URL and callback server. Not yet verified: a complete ChatGPT or SuperGrok sign-in and the Codex backend's answer to the folded request, both of which need a browser session. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: cache: template URL-encoded forms of unique() values in paths and URLs
body:
Follow-up to #327.

`templateText` matches a `unique()` value literally. A value that appears URL-encoded in a recorded path or navigate URL (`/companies/E2E%20abc`, `?q=Ada%20Smith`) stays literal, so the next run's replay performs the actions with the fresh value but the end-path check compares against the first run's slug and hands off to the model. Created-record pages often carry the name in the URL, so this hits exactly the flows `unique()` targets.

Fix shape: a second placeholder form, e.g. `{{param:/name|uri}}`, written where `encodeURIComponent(value)` occurs and filled with the encoded current value at replay. Longest-form-first ordering already exists in `templateText`. Trace-1 format gains one grammar variant; the cache starts over on the policy version bump as usual.

Raised by Devin and cubic on #327; left out of that PR to keep it reviewable.

title: cache: start-path precondition should tolerate minted id segments like the end-path check
body:
Found running the Open Mercato suite on canary 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813 with `unique()` params.

`decideTraceReplay` compares the recorded `startPath` with `samePathname` (exact), while the end-path check uses `samePathShape`, which forgives segments that both look minted (uuid, hex run, long token). A step that starts on a created record's page, such as "Rename this company" opened at `/backend/customers/companies-v2/<uuid>` or "add a custom line" on `/backend/sales/documents/<uuid>?kind=quote`, therefore misses with `wrong-context` on every run, because the id in the start path is new each time.

Three of the suite's 23 steps hit this in the replay run. Using `samePathShape` for the start precondition would make them eligible; the anchors and end check still guard the outcome.

title: cache: volatile-anchor filter misses result counts, badge numbers, and millisecond timings
body:
Found running the Open Mercato suite on canary 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813.

`isVolatileAnchor` skips ids, ages, dates, and clock times, but these end anchors were recorded and then failed the next run with `end-mismatch` after every action had replayed:

- `{"text": "Showing 1 to 9 of 9 results"}` (create category; the count grows per run)
- `{"text": "Showing 1 to 5 of 5 results in 321ms"}` (create role; `ms` is not in the duration pattern, which covers `s`, `secs`, `m`, `h`, `d`)
- `{"text": "11"}` (create product; a sidebar badge count)
- `{"text": "Last operation:"}` (create role; a status line that reads differently later)

Suggested additions to `VOLATILE_TEXT`: `\bms\b` durations, `\d+\s+(?:to|of)\s+\d+` ranges and `\d+\s+results?` counts, and bare numeric text anchors. Four of 23 steps in the replay run handed off on these alone.

title: fix(cache): replay on a start path that differs only by minted ids
body: ## What and why - Closes #340. Found running the Open Mercato suite on the 20260917213813 canary: 6 of 20 `act` steps missed with `wrong-context` on every run. - A step that edits, deletes, or extends a record a previous step created starts on that record's page, `/backend/customers/companies-v2/` or `/backend/sales/documents/?kind=quote`. The recorded start path carries the previous run's id, and `decideTraceReplay` compared pathnames literally, while the end-of-step check already forgave segments that both look minted. - The start check now uses `samePathShape`. Same segment count, every segment equal or minted on both sides, query ignored as before. Nothing else about eligibility changes; the relocated targets and end anchors still prove the screen. - No policy version bump: entries written before this change are valid and become eligible. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(cache): skip count-like end anchors and wait from the last action
body: ## What and why - Closes #341. Measured on the Open Mercato suite: six `act` steps replayed every action, then waited 38 s on average for end anchors that can never reappear, then handed off with one model call. The warm run took longer than `--no-cache`. - **Anchors.** The recorded anchors were `Showing 1 to 9 of 9 results`, `Showing 1 to 5 of 5 results in 321ms`, and a sidebar badge `11`. They were the screen's delta, so they were recorded, but they grow with the data every run leaves behind. `VOLATILE_TEXT` gains millisecond timings, pagination ranges, and record counts, and a bare number is volatile when it is all the anchor has to say. A named control whose text is a number, the `Counter` that reads `1` in the docs example, stays: that is the step's effect. `3 / 30 steps` and `v2.2.1` stay too, as the existing test asserts. - **End wait.** `endWaitMs` was the whole step's duration plus a 10 s margin, so it included the model's thinking time before the last action, 30 to 47 s on this app. It is now measured from the last recorded action to the passing screen. A replay does not think, so it has no reason to wait for it. - No policy version bump. An entry with a volatile anchor still hands off once, and the re-stage after an unrepaired end-mismatch writes it again with the new filter, so old entries heal on their next run. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(cache): template unique() values in their URL-encoded spellings too
body: ## What and why - Closes #338. On the Open Mercato suite the two search steps end on `/backend/customers/companies?search=E2E+mu62izb0c90h+Company`. Every action replayed, then the end-path check compared against the first run's literal query and handed off. - The placeholder grammar gains an encoding suffix: `{{param:/name}}` for the value as typed, `{{param:/name|uri}}` where `encodeURIComponent(value)` appeared, `{{param:/name|form}}` where the form-encoded spelling with `+` for spaces appeared. `templateText` looks for every distinct spelling of every marked value, longest first, so a longer value or a longer encoding is claimed whole. `expandText` applies the named encoding to the current value. title: fix(cache): relocate a target that has only a role by its place among unnamed twins
body:
## What and why

- Found running the Open Mercato suite on the 20260917213813 canary: 7 of 20 `act` steps replayed one action, the tap that opens a form, then handed off with `target-not-found` on the first field. The recording for that field is `{ "role": "textbox" }`. Open Mercato's form inputs carry no label, placeholder, test id, or a structural selector the engine could anchor.
- `isRelocatableDescriptor` required a test id, name, text, or placeholder, so a role-only descriptor had no tiers, `describePosition` found no twins to count, and the recorder stored nothing that could ever resolve.
- Now an anonymous descriptor is relocatable once it carries a position. `describePosition` counts its twins even when it is the only one, so `{ role: "textbox", position: { index: 0, of: 7 } }` reads as "the first unnamed textbox". Matching is strict for anonymous descriptors: a candidate must also lack name, text, placeholder, and test id, so an unnamed textbox never stands in for a named one. A change in the number of unnamed twins diverges as `target-ambiguous`, as positioned twins already do. Anchors are unaffected: they never carry a position, so a role-only anchor stays excluded.
- Three things the live suite then surfaced, fixed in the follow-up commits:
  - The trace reader rejected `position.of` below two, so every entry with an anonymous target counted alone came back `invalid-entry`. It accepts one.
  - A form still rendering shows fewer unnamed twins than the recording counted: the company form goes from 6 to 7 textboxes when its rich-text editor mounts. Ambiguity for a positioned descriptor now retries within the relocation wait instead of diverging on the first look. Ambiguity for a descriptor with no position still diverges at once.
  - The relocation backoff list ended after five looks, about five seconds, while `RETRY_TIMEOUT_MS` and the docs say fifteen. The last delay now repeats until the timeout, for every relocation.
- No policy bump. An old entry with a role-only target still hands off once; the executor repairs, the entry is evicted, and the next run records it with a position.
- Half of this is an accessibility finding for the app: inputs without labels are invisible to assistive tech as much as to the cache.

title: feat(agent): say when an action closed the keyboard and verify the outcome before passing

title: feat(agent): name the blank point that closes a phone keyboard when dismiss_keyboard cannot
body:
## What and why

- On an iPhone the engine declares `dismiss_keyboard` and then throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, so the model read "Dismissed the keyboard. failed: ..." and spent three turns per field working around it.
- This version answers the refusal with a screenshot and a blank point inside the focused field's scroll view, in screenshot pixels, ready for `tap_at`. `keyboard-escape.ts` computes the point from the tree. A `recover` hook on the verb kit lets one tool answer a failure with its own result.

## Draft, do not merge as is

The design is disputed and kept here so the work is not lost. Problems: the verb lies (declared, then refused at runtime), the runner computes the point but will not tap it, a tree problem is pushed into pixel space and recorded as a bare `tapAt`, and iOS layout knowledge sits in `e2e`'s agent layer.

Options on the table:

1. Engine owns it: `@e2edev/agent-device` implements `dismissKeyboard` on iPhone by tapping a listed non-interactive node inside the focused field's scroll container, the way Appium and Maestro hide keyboards. Delete this module, the hook, and the advice.
2. Model owns it: do not offer `dismiss_keyboard` where the engine cannot do it; one prompt rule says press Enter or tap a plain text node by id.

Stacked on #351. Split out of #326.

title: feat(cache): a typed value is a run-time gap only when read off the screen or reckoned from the date
body: ## What and why - Any typed value absent from the instruction and `params` used to end the replay as a gap. Every signup form the model filled with plausible values stopped replaying at its first field. - Now a value is this run's data only when a screen the step saw showed it as a whole token (a code, a reference the app minted) or when it is a date or time. A name or email the model composed itself is the flow's data and replays verbatim. - The observation feed remembers the name and text of every node its screens showed, leaving out editable fields (whose name is their value or placeholder) and the wrappers some platforms name after the field they hold. `isDerivedValue` checks against that set instead of parsing rendered screen lines. Rebased on main after #350 landed. Split out of #326. ## Evidence Record-then-replay on the mobile benchmark: this rule alone moved replayed steps from 9 of 23 to 12 of 23 with zero model calls. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package. - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/cache.mdx` `gap` row. - [ ] Contract change - [ ] Engine contract change ---

title: feat(cache): fold repeated scrolls and re-find a scrolled list by its place
body: ## What and why - A list paged to its end overran the 50-action cap and poisoned the trace. Consecutive identical scrolls now fold into one recorded action with `times`; replay repeats them with a settled look between, as the live loop did. - A device names a scroll view after its first visible row and renumbers the tree on every look, so the id the model scrolled a moment ago names nothing on the next screen and its descriptor matches nothing either. A scroll target is what sits where it sits: the same-role node whose box overlaps the old one by at least half is the same list (`scroll-target.ts`). A nested carousel never stands in for its list, nor the list for a lost carousel. - A lost list that covered at least half the viewport when recorded (`spans`) scrolls as the viewport, live and on replay; that is what scrolling the main list is. A smaller region hands off as before. - The dispatcher's targeted action takes an already resolved node, and the feed exposes `lookup` and `lastSeen` so the scroll policy lives outside it. `MAIN_LIST_SHARE` sits with the replay policy version. Stacked on #353. Split out of #326. ## Evidence Record-then-replay on the mobile benchmark: 12 of 23 steps to 16 of 23 with zero model calls, the two long-list scenarios among them. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package. - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/cache.mdx` `truncated` row. - [ ] Contract change - [ ] Engine contract change ---

title: feat(cache): a recorded point tap picks among look-alikes by where it landed
body: ## What and why - A point tap recorded inside a node (`tapAt` with `within`) handed off whenever the node's descriptor matched several look-alikes on replay, even though the recorded point settles which one it was. - `relocateDescriptor` now returns the candidate ids on `target-ambiguous`. Replay takes the look-alike whose live box contains the recorded point, on a viewport of the recorded size, and places the tap at the same fraction inside it. When the point settles nothing, or the viewport changed, it hands off as before. A node that is gone still hands off, and the bare point is never tapped on its own. - `hitTest` shares one `innermostAt` walk for the control and the node under a point; `containsPoint` joins the geometry helpers. - Replay policy moves to `conservative/5` (main took `conservative/4` in #359), so entries recorded under the previous rules are re-recorded. Stacked on #354. Split out of #326. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package. - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/cache.mdx` `target-ambiguous` row. - [ ] Contract change - [ ] Engine contract change ---

Out-of-process sheets (Apple Pay, the photo picker) say the sheet is not in the tree and the model asks for pixels itself. - Goals name the whole path to the success state. The login credential comes in as `params`, since the on-screen hint reaches the model redacted. title: feat(cache): compare a recording's screens as routes, not URLs
body:
## What and why

- Replaces the URL comparisons behind the replay precondition and postcondition with one model: a screen's **route**. #342 and #344 each fixed one URL shape; the Open Mercato suite showed the next app brings another (minted ids, slugs, encoded search terms, query state), and comparing URL strings pairwise does not scale. This PR is the model those fixes were approximating.
- `cache/route.ts` reduces a location to its route: the pathname's segments, with every segment that looks minted per record replaced by `:id` (uuid, hex or digit run, a long token mixing letters and at least two digits, text with whitespace), the query, fragment, and trailing slash dropped, and hash routing (`/#/companies/1`) read as the path it is. A non-web location, a device engine's screen title or a browser's own page, is opaque and compares as itself. An encoded slash cannot split a segment; a capitalized or dashed word stays a word.
- `compareRoutes` returns `same`, `different`, or `undecided`. Undecided means one segment differs at the same depth: a slug of a record the runner never saw the value of. **At the start of a step an undecided route is a miss.** A signature of the start screen was tried and measured on Open Mercato: the controls a start screen shows are the header and sidebar every screen shares, and different routes scored 1.0 against each other, so nothing recorded at the start can settle it safely. **At the end of a step the recorded anchors settle it**, because they are the step's own effect: present on the screen, the replay passes; not yet present when the path poll runs out, the recording-sized anchor wait decides as it does for a matching route. Two differing segments or a different depth are never the same screen.
- A `unique()` value needs no rule in the route: its slug joins its percent- and form-encoded spellings in `template.ts`, so the recording carries a placeholder wherever a path spelled the value and replay fills in this run's value on both sides.
- `samePathname` and `samePathShape` are gone. The observed path keeps its whole fragment; `route.ts` alone decides what a fragment means. The trace format is unchanged. `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` moves to `conservative/4`, so existing caches start over.
- Risk accepted knowingly: two records of the same type share a route, so "delete this company" recorded on one replays on whichever company the test opened. That is the intent, the test navigated there, and it was already true of the end check before this PR.

Validation on the Open Mercato suite is in the comments: four clean-cache replays at 18 to 21 of 27 steps replayed, zero `wrong-context` misses in every run, all tests passing.

title: reporter: run summary model label echoes the configured model, not the models that ran
body:
## What happened

CLI header and the final `AI` summary line print the run's configured model even when per-step report records show a different model did the work. With a custom executor (`jevAgent` from #329) driving every act and assert on `typesafe-ai/jev` and the configured `agents.default.model` only judging one extract, the summary printed:

```
AI  66.5k tokens · $0.0030 · 23 model calls · gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna
```

while `.e2e/report.json` per-step `model` records correctly showed 22 of 23 calls on `typesafe-ai/jev`.

## Workaround

Executor declaring its `model` (the `StepExecutor.model` seam) fixes the label - after that the line reads `typesafe-ai/jev · judge gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna`. That requires a structural AI SDK stub with a throwing `doGenerate`, which `isModelInstance` forces on non-generative executors.

## Proper fix

The reporter aggregating the models actually seen in per-step records (data is already in the report) instead of echoing resolved config.

## Environment

e2e 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813, jev executor from #329, agent-device engine target (iOS sim).

title: agent-device: iOS runner watchdog wedge persists across runs; next run fails at prepare with APP_UNREACHABLE
body:
## What happened

When an accessibility capture exceeds the execution watchdog on a heavy or animating screen (Bluesky home feed / post thread), the iOS runner is left broken and the NEXT `e2e run` fails immediately:

```
APP_UNREACHABLE: agent.act failed: snapshot failed: The iOS runner is still finishing a previous
command that exceeded its execution watchdog (usually an accessibility capture on a heavy or
animating screen).
```

The wedge survives the end of the run: engine prepare succeeds, the app opens, and the first observation fails. Needed manual recovery 4 times in one afternoon of iterating on a Bluesky suite.

## Expected

Engine `prepare` detects a wedged runner session and resets it (or the daemon recovers it) instead of poisoning the following run.

## Workaround

`agent-device daemon stop` + `xcrun simctl shutdown/boot <udid>` before rerunning.

## Repro

Bluesky iOS app (xyz.blueskyweb.app, simulator build), drive the home feed or open a post thread until a capture exceeds the watchdog, then start a second run.

## Environment

agent-device CLI 0.20.8, @e2edev/agent-device 0.8.0-canary-20260917213813, e2e 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813, iPhone 17 Pro sim iOS 26.2 (23C54), macOS Darwin 27.0.0.

title: agent-device: iOS snapshot fails with "regular iOS snapshot presentation requires a valid viewport" on Bluesky post thread
body:
## What happened

Opening a post thread in the Bluesky iOS app (tap a post in search results), the next observation fails:

```
APP_UNREACHABLE: agent.act failed: snapshot failed: regular iOS snapshot presentation requires a valid viewport
```

Reproducible on that screen. The step blocks and the attempt fails; this can also be the capture that triggers the watchdog wedge (filed separately).

## Repro

1. Bluesky iOS simulator build (xyz.blueskyweb.app), signed in.
2. Search for any term, submit.
3. Tap the first post in the results to open the thread.
4. Next snapshot fails as above.

Related app-side note: the same app's profile screen reached from search collapses the accessibility tree to a single `other "[object Object]"` node, so Bluesky is generally a good a11y stress fixture.

## Environment

agent-device CLI 0.20.8, @e2edev/agent-device 0.8.0-canary-20260917213813, e2e 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813, iPhone 17 Pro sim iOS 26.2 (23C54), macOS Darwin 27.0.0.

title: agent-device: keyboard.dismiss fails on iOS simulator ("Unable to dismiss the keyboard")
body:
## What happened

`dismissKeyboard` (executor grammar `dismissKeyboard`, CLI `keyboard.dismiss`) fails on the iOS simulator while the software keyboard is visibly up:

```
dismiss_keyboard on #n1736 button "szukaj" testid="Search" FAILED: keyboard.dismiss failed: Unable to dismiss the keyboard
```

Observed from a jev executor turn (#329 work): a needed control was behind the keyboard (`Ref @e72 is behind the visible keyboard and cannot be tapped safely`), the executor chose to dismiss the keyboard, and the dismiss itself errored. On iOS there is often no dismiss affordance, so this may need a fallback (tap outside, scroll, or the keyboard's return key) or a documented capability caveat.

## Repro

Bluesky iOS app, search screen with keyboard up (focused search field), call keyboard.dismiss.

agent-device CLI 0.20.8, @e2edev/agent-device 0.8.0-canary-20260917213813, e2e 0.15.0-canary-20260917213813, iPhone 17 Pro sim iOS 26.2 (23C54), macOS Darwin 27.0.0.

title: feat(agent-device): lease hosted devices through a DeviceProvider and release them in a new engine finish hook
body:
## What and why

- \`npx eas-cli simulator:exec "npx e2e run"\` works only because agent-device reads \`AGENT_DEVICE_DAEMON_BASE_URL\` from the environment. The session lifecycle then lives outside the run (nothing stops it on failure or interrupt), one session serves every worker slot, and the report never learns the device was remote.
- \`agentDevice({ device })\` now accepts a \`DeviceProvider\`: \`acquire\` leases one device per worker slot in \`prepare\`, all slots in parallel, and hands back the agent-device daemon to drive it through (\`daemon.baseUrl\`, \`daemon.authToken\`, optional \`device\` and \`installedApp\`). Every source of devices (configured list, discovered booted devices, provider leases) ends in one \`SlotBinding\` per slot, carried to child workers through one environment variable and warmed the same way before the run's clock starts. Leases are held as each \`acquire\` settles and released in \`finish\`, also when another slot's \`acquire\` failed.
- No vendor ships in the repo. \`docs/mobile.mdx\` gets a "Hosted devices" section with the contract and an example provider against a generic session API (create, poll, stop) as user code; the example is typechecked and verified verbatim by \`check-docs-examples\`. Any service that runs an agent-device daemon next to a device plugs in the same way.
- Engine SPI: optional \`finish(info)\` hook, once per prepared target in the runner process after the last worker, on every exit path (pass, failure, interrupt, a \`prepare\` that threw part-way), within \`cleanupTimeout\` and never cancelled by an interrupt; a hook that ignores its signal is abandoned with \`CLEANUP_TIMEOUT\`. \`PreparedEngines\` owns the prepare/finish pairing for both the run and the standalone \`e2e mcp\` attempt. \`EnginePrepareInfo.projectRoot\` added so a provider can resolve \`appPath\`. Additive, SPI stays 1.

```ts
agentDevice({
  platform: 'ios',
  app: 'com.example.app',
  device: hostedDevices({ serviceUrl: 'https://devices.example.com', image: 'ios-18-iphone-17' }),
})
```

Not live-verified against a hosted service. The provider path is covered by scripted-client tests (lease per slot, warm-up through the leased daemon, env hand-off to a worker, install skip, partial and synchronous acquire failures, release failure, size cap, no-lease fallback) and the runner's \`finish\` ordering and timeout by the integration suite.

title: fix(report): the live block fills the terminal and console output prints above it
body: ## What and why - The running area padded itself to a fixed 14 rows, so on a tall terminal the block ended mid-screen with the summary hanging over blank rows. The live window now counts the rows the permanent log holds above it (`LiveWindow.logged`, `packages/e2e/src/report/live-window.ts`) and hands the renderers the room left; the running tree and the explore view pad to that room, so the summary sits on the last rows. - Results printed above take their rows back from the block. Once the log has grown down to the rows the running area keeps, the block scrolls the log as before. Rows nobody counted (a worker's stray output, `--debug` on stderr) cause one scroll, after which the count is exact again. - `console.log` inside a test used to vanish: workers inherit the runner's streams, so the line landed under the live window, the next repaint covered it, and the cursor-up erase left stale rows. title: feat(telemetry): attribute fleets by name and carry sandbox, runtime, and machine age
body:
First of three telemetry PRs from reading the beta week in PostHog (Sep 14 to 21). Stack: this PR, then #370 (session outcome), then #371 (run detail). ## Why - Last week PostHog counted ~1480 distinct ids. ~1452 of them were Cloudflare Firecracker sandboxes running one `e2e run` each on a fresh preferences file. Real machines were single digits. - Nothing in the payload said "this is a hosted runner" or "this machine is new", and `node_version` read `24.20.0` for runs that were on Bun. | Cohort (7 days) | ids | runs | telemetry could tell | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Firecracker sandboxes | ~1452 | ~1452 | no | | CI (`ci:github-actions`) | 1 | 385 | yes | | people | ~7 | 20 to 144 each | only by hand | ## What changed - `E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET=` attributes events to `fleet:` the way CI is attributed to `ci:`: no preferences file, no notice, no salted project id. One concept, `statedIdentity(env)` in `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/environment.ts`, replaces the `ci` boolean in `Telemetry`; the id is the fleet, else the CI vendor, else the store's. - Every event carries `sandbox` (`firecracker` from the kernel release, else null), `runtime` and `runtime_version` (`node`, `bun`, `deno`), `first_run` (this command created the preferences file) and `days_since_first_run`. - The preferences file gains `createdAt`, written only when the ids are generated. A file from before the field is left alone and its age is null: `open` keeps its one-write contract and no existing user reads as installed today. `TelemetryStore.ageDays()` owns the arithmetic. `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/store.ts`. - `telemetry/token.ts` holds the plain-token and error-code folds that `events.ts` and `environment.ts` both used. `tests/unit/telemetry.test.ts` splits into store, events, and transport files. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[flush] --> B{E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET?} B -- yes --> C["distinct_id = fleet:name"] B -- no --> D{CI?} D -- yes --> E["distinct_id = ci:vendor"] D -- no --> F["distinct_id = preferences anonymousId
first_run, days_since_first_run"] ``` Debug output from the built CLI, machine and fleet: ```json {"distinct_id":"ce9ca4cd…","fleet":null,"sandbox":null,"runtime":"node","runtime_version":"26.8.2","first_run":true,"days_since_first_run":0} {"distinct_id":"fleet:testerarmy-cloud","fleet":"testerarmy-cloud","first_run":null,"days_since_first_run":null} ``` Under `bun bin.js list`: `{"runtime":"bun","runtime_version":"1.3.8","node_version":"24.3.0"}`, which is the shape the sandbox runs had in PostHog. ## Location PostHog's GeoIP step ran on every event at ingestion and stored city, postal code, and coordinates next to the machine id, while the docs promised "only the properties listed above". No IP was ever sent or stored; the enrichment happened server-side. Every event now carries `$geoip_disable: true`, so PostHog skips that step, and the docs and `SECURITY.md` say so. `NOTICE_VERSION` bumps to 2 so existing users see the notice once more. Verified against the live project: a test event sent with the flag landed with none of the `$geoip_*` fields, while all ~1078 unflagged events of the previous day carry city, postal code, and coordinates. Docs: `docs/telemetry.mdx`, `docs/reference/environment.mdx`, `SECURITY.md`. Our cloud should set `E2E_TELEMETRY_FLEET` once this ships.

title: feat(telemetry): the session event says how the command ended and init reports what it scaffolded
body:
Second of three telemetry PRs. Stacked on #369; #371 follows.

## Why

- A beta tester whose config failed to load, or who mistyped a flag, left no trace: the session event was recorded before the action ran and never learned how it ended. Last week `init` was run by three machines and one of them ran nothing else; we could not see whether it finished.
- `runToOutcome` and `main` printed `CODE: message` and recorded nothing.

## What changed

- `e2e_cli_session` gains `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, and `error_code`: the runner code of a failure that ended the command before it could run (`CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_CONFIG`, ...), `CLI_USAGE` for a flag commander rejected, null otherwise.
- `Telemetry` owns the session instead of queueing it as an event: `session(command, flags)` names it, `failSession(code)` records the first failure, `endSession(exitCode)` is the entry point's last word, and `flush` builds the event from those. `record` stays a plain push. `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/telemetry.ts`.
- The CLI names the session in a `preSubcommand` hook on every command that has children, before the subcommand parses its flags, and again with the flags in `preAction`. `e2e cache ls --nope` therefore records a session of `cache ls`. A `reportFailure` helper replaces the copy-pasted catch blocks in `run`, `explore`, and `list`. `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`.
- `e2e init` returns its outcome with the exit code; the CLI records `e2e_init_completed` with `result` (`scaffolded`, `already-initialized`, `cancelled`, `install-failed`, `not-interactive`, `invalid-project`), `yes`, `existing_config`, `engine`, `gateway`, `skill`, `mcp`, `install`. Option ids only, never the endpoint typed for an OpenAI-compatible gateway. The outcome types live in `telemetry/events.ts`, so the dependency points cli to telemetry. `packages/e2e/src/cli/init.ts`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as commander
  participant T as Telemetry
  C->>T: preSubcommand: session("cache ls")
  C->>C: parse flags
  alt flag rejected
    C->>T: failSession(CLI_USAGE)
  else action runs
    C->>T: preAction: session("cache ls", flags)
    C->>T: failSession(code) when the action threw
  end
  C->>T: main finally: endSession(exitCode), flush
  T->>T: flush: session event first, then the queue
```

```json
e2e_cli_session   {"command":"run","flags":[],"exit_code":2,"error_code":"CLI_USAGE"}          // e2e run --workers many
e2e_cli_session   {"command":"cache ls","flags":[],"exit_code":2,"error_code":"CLI_USAGE"}     // e2e cache ls --nope

e2e_init_completed {"result":"already-initialized","engine":null,"gateway":null,"skill":true,"mcp":true,"install":false}
```

title: feat(telemetry): the run event names the deciding error, counts retries and agent actions, and files failures by kind
body:
Third of three telemetry PRs. Stacked on #370, which sits on #369.

## Why

- Last week one tester hit `ENGINE_FAILURE` 42 times on iOS and Android in an hour and left. Hosted runs hit `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` 99 times. Neither code says what broke.
- 104 hosted runs passed with `STEP_TIMEOUT` in `error_codes`, meaning a retry rescued them; the payload had no attempt count to say so.
- `estimated_cost_usd` was null for every direct provider (`openai.responses` 1004 runs, `anthropic.messages` 349), which reads the same as free.
- `error_codes` is a sorted set, so breakdowns by failure were polluted by secondary codes.

## What changed

Built from the report alone, in `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/events.ts`.

- `primary_error_code`: the first error the run recorded. `errorsOf` now orders a scope's verdict, then its steps, then cleanup, so one walk serves `error_codes` and the primary alike.
- `error_kinds`: for `ENGINE_FAILURE`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, and `ERROR`, the code paired with a kind matched off the message against a closed list, as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED:rate-limit`. Lives in `telemetry/failure-kind.ts` with the precedence rule in its JSDoc (exact status before its family, protocol word before surface, surface before what was missing on it). Only the kind leaves the machine; the unit test asserts no fragment of the message does. The module says it is a stopgap: the exact facts exist on the cause chain at the raise site, and a kind carried in `ReportError.details` would replace it. That is a wire change for another PR.
- `attempts_total`, `tests_retried` across results and serial groups.
- `agent_actions`: counts by the runner's own action names from the agent steps' engine events (`{"tap": 12, "typeText": 3}`). The names are an allowlist, `GRAMMAR_ACTION_NAMES` in `agent/action-names.ts`, shared with the dispatcher along with the `tool:` prefix; a project's tools fold into `tool` and anything else into `other`, so the key set is closed.
- `cost_source`: `provider`, `none` (model calls nobody priced), or null (no model calls).

```ts
// agent/action-names.ts
export const GRAMMAR_ACTION_NAMES = ['dismissKeyboard', 'navigate', 'press', 'pressKey', 'scroll', 'selectOption', 'tap', 'type', 'typeSecret', 'typeText'] as const;
export const PROJECT_TOOL_EVENT_PREFIX = 'tool:';
```

Testbed smoke run through the built CLI:

```json
{"status":"passed","tests_executed":4,"attempts_total":4,"tests_retried":0,"agent_actions":{},"cost_source":null,"primary_error_code":null,"error_kinds":[]}
```

Not done here: a local price table for direct providers. Prices rot and a wrong dollar figure is worse than `cost_source: none`; that is a report feature, not telemetry.

Docs: `docs/telemetry.mdx`, `SECURITY.md`.

title: chore: relicense from MIT to Apache-2.0
body: ## What and why - The repo and all five public packages move from MIT to Apache-2.0. Same permissive terms, plus what MIT leaves out: an explicit patent grant from every contributor, a retaliation clause that revokes it from anyone who sues over patents, a trademark clause, and contribution terms in section 5 of the license itself. - No CLA, no DCO. Inbound = outbound stays the policy; `CONTRIBUTING.md` now points at section 5. - Done now because every contributor so far is on the team, so relicensing needs no outside consent. After launch it would. - Each public package ships `LICENSE` (full text) and a `NOTICE` file. `NOTICE` is added to `files` because npm packs LICENSE by itself but not NOTICE. - One changeset bumps `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, `@e2edev/github`, `@e2edev/oauth`, and `@e2edev/agent-device` as a patch so the npm pages read Apache-2.0 on the next release. ``` $ npm pack --dry-run # packages/github npm notice 11.4kB LICENSE npm notice 132B NOTICE npm notice 1.1kB README.md npm notice 1.7kB package.json ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. (No docs page or skill names the license.) - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(oauth): fold the Codex stream without a content-type and with streamed output items
body: ## What and why - Every `chatgpt()` call fails on `main` with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: Invalid JSON response`. The Codex backend answers its Responses stream with no `content-type` header, so `foldResponsesStream` passed the SSE body through and the AI SDK's JSON parser choked on `event: response.created`. - The same backend sends `response.completed` with `"output": []`; the items only arrive as `response.output_item.done` events. The folded response therefore had no text and no tool call even once it parsed. - The fold now recognizes the stream by its body (`parseSse` finds events) instead of the header, and assembles `output` from the streamed items when the final event carries none. A body with no events and no header is passed through as it was. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Codex 200, no content-type] --> B{application/json?} B -- yes --> C[pass through] B -- no --> D[parseSse body] D -- no events --> C D -- events --> E[collect output_item.done] E --> F[response.completed] F --> G["JSON: response + output"] ``` Observed headers on a live call, `packages/oauth/src/sse.ts` gate before this change: ```ts if (!response.ok || !contentType.includes('text/event-stream')) return response; ``` ``` 200 cf-cache-status, cf-ray, date, server, x-codex-*, x-oai-request-id (no content-type) event: response.created data: {"type":"response.created", ...} ... event: response.output_item.done data: {"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":0,"item":{"type":"message", ...}} event: response.completed data: {"type":"response.completed","response":{..., "output":[], "usage":{...}}} ``` The `openai.test.ts` end-to-end fixture now serves the stream the way the backend does: no header, one `output_item.done`, an empty `output` on the final event. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(run): fail a step call without await as STEP_NOT_AWAITED instead of crashing the worker
body:
## What and why

- `agent.act(...)` without `await` killed the worker. The body returned at once, the attempt ended and closed the session under the still-running step, the step failed with nobody to catch it, and the worker's `unhandledRejection` handler posted `fatal`; the scheduler answered with SIGKILL. The user saw `WORKER_CRASH`, `WORKER_EXIT (signal SIGKILL)`, and an `APP_NOT_OPEN: no attempt is running` run error, none of which named their line.
- The recorder now keeps each running step's promise and start stack. Whenever the body settles, `execute.ts` asks it to abandon whatever still runs: the step is recorded as failed at the line it was called on, its later outcome is dropped, and it is cancelled through the attempt signal (the one a test timeout already aborts the body with) and waited for within one `cleanupTimeout`, so teardown starts on a quiet session.
- A body that returned fails with `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`. A body that threw keeps its own error as primary and records `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` under `secondaryErrors`. A runtime skip abandons the step without adding an error.
- The promise the test holds still rejects once the step is cancelled, with nobody awaiting it. The recorder marks what abandoned steps rejected with, and the worker's `unhandledRejection` handler lets those pass instead of treating them as fatal.
- The error's stack is relocated to the step's start frames, so the existing code frame in the list reporter and `error.source` in the report both point at the call that lacks `await`. No reporter change.
- New runner code documented in `docs/reference/errors.mdx`, the skill's `debugging.md` and `writing-tests.md`, and one sentence in `docs/writing-tests.mdx`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[body settles] --> B{steps still running?}
  B -- no --> C[afterEach]
  B -- yes --> D[abandonRunning]
  D --> E[step: failed, STEP_NOT_AWAITED, at call line]
  D --> F[attemptAbort.abort, wait one cleanupTimeout]
  F --> G{body returned?}
  G -- yes --> H[attempt fails STEP_NOT_AWAITED]
  G -- threw --> I[body error primary, STEP_NOT_AWAITED secondary]
  H --> C
  I --> C
```

`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`, around the body:

```ts
try {
  phase = 'body';
  await (registered.fn as SetupFn)(fixtures);
} catch (cause) {
  const notAwaited = await abandonNotAwaited();
  if (notAwaited !== undefined && !isRuntimeSkip(cause)) secondaryErrors.push(serializeError(notAwaited, { phase: 'body', ... }));
  throw cause;
}
const notAwaited = await abandonNotAwaited();
if (notAwaited !== undefined) throw notAwaited;
```

Before, against a project with `agent.act(...)` un-awaited:

```
 × app opens 0ms
   → worker process exited during this test
 ERROR  test error APP_NOT_OPEN
no attempt is running
 ERROR  infrastructure error WORKER_EXIT
worker for target "web" exited unexpectedly (code null, signal SIGKILL) during file::web::tests/example.e2e.ts
```

After:

```
 FAIL  |web| tests/example.e2e.ts > app opens
STEP_NOT_AWAITED: the test body returned before agent.act "Go to contact form and submit it with dummy data" finished; put `await` in front of every step call
 ❯ tests/example.e2e.ts:6:9
      4| test("app opens", async ({ app, web, agent }) => {
      5|   await app.open("/");
      6|   agent.act("Go to contact form and submit it with dummy data");
       |         ^
      7| });
```

Not covered: a step that was un-awaited and had already failed before the body settled still surfaces as an unhandled rejection. The body has to be doing something else asynchronous for long enough for that to happen; the still-running case is the one people hit. The in-process runner has no rejection handler today and is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat(oauth)!: fold @e2edev/oauth into e2e as e2e/oauth, add e2e models, fix Codex second turns
body:
Sign-in to a personal subscription is part of the runner, not a package the user installs. `@e2edev/oauth` moves into `e2e`, and only the model constructors and the CLI stay public.

- `packages/oauth` is gone. Its source is `packages/e2e/src/oauth/`, published as `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`, `e2e/oauth/copilot`, `e2e/oauth/grok`. Each subpath is the only importer of its `@ai-sdk/*` package, now optional peers of `e2e`, so the CLI still boots without them.
- No library entry. The old package's `createOAuthFetch`, stores, flows, and provider factories were pitched for "your own product"; nothing consumes them, so they are module-private now. The constructors take `store` (a test and CI seam) and drop `userAgent` and `originator`.
- `e2e init` writes the new imports and adds no sibling dependency. `e2e login` and `e2e logout` call `runLogin`/`runLogout` directly; the `createRequire` shim in `src/cli/login.ts`, the `e2e-oauth` bin, and `runStatus` are deleted.
- `chatgpt()` forces `providerOptions.openai.store = false` on every call (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/chatgpt.ts`, `withoutServerStorage`). The AI SDK defaults `store` to true and refers back to a prior turn's reasoning as `item_reference`; the Codex backend runs with `store: false` and answers `Item with id 'rs_…' not found`. Told the truth, the SDK carries `encrypted_content` itself.
- New `e2e models [provider]`: each `OAuthProvider` gains `models(fetch)`, `runModels` prints one line per model (id, vendor name, notes) with terminal controls stripped from vendor text, and keeps listing when one of several logins fails.
- Default ChatGPT id in init, docs, and the skill is `gpt-5.6-luna`; the hardcoded `CHATGPT_MODELS` list is removed.
- Every workspace package pins `ai` 7.0.105. A mismatch makes `@ai-sdk/provider` types diverge between `e2e`'s emitted d.ts and a dependant's own `ai`, and agent-device stopped building.

```ts
import { createAgent } from 'e2e/agent';
import { chatgpt } from 'e2e/oauth/chatgpt';

const agent = createAgent({ model: chatgpt('gpt-5.6-luna') });
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[turn 1: SDK request] --> B[Codex backend, store:false]
  B --> C[reasoning rs_1 + encrypted_content]
  C --> D{SDK believes store?}
  D -- true, before --> E[item_reference rs_1] --> F[400 not found]
  D -- false, this PR --> G[reasoning rs_1 with encrypted_content] --> H[turn 2 answers]
```

```
$ npx e2e models
ChatGPT (openai): 3 models
  gpt-6-astra    GPT-6 Astra    reasoning medium/xhigh
  gpt-5.6-luna   GPT-5.6 Luna   reasoning low/medium/high (default medium)
  gpt-5.4-mini   GPT-5.4 mini   hidden in Codex
```

Not verified against the live vendors: the three model endpoints (Codex `/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=`, Copilot `/models`, SpaceXAI `/v1/language-models`) are parsed from the shapes their own clients use, with unit tests on fake servers. The first run of `e2e models` with a real login should confirm them; the Codex `client_version` constant has to track the Codex CLI or newer models stay hidden.

After merge: `npm deprecate @e2edev/oauth "folded into e2e; import from e2e/oauth/*"`.

title: fix(agent-device): keep the agent-device hint in translated engine errors
body: - `dismissKeyboard` on an iPhone keyboard is refused by agent-device on purpose: the keyboard shows no dismiss key and agent-device taps nothing outside it (callstack/agent-device#1606). Reproduced on the Settings search field with agent-device 0.21.8, it answers `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` with a hint naming the alternatives. - Our `translateError` kept only the message, so the model saw the refusal and nothing else. The hint the failure itself declares now rides in the same message; the normalizer's per-code default hint (CLI advice) stays out. - `docs/reference/agent-device.mdx` says why `dismissKeyboard` fails on iOS. ```text keyboard.dismiss failed: Unable to dismiss the iOS keyboard: the keyboard exposes no dismiss key, and background taps are never attempted (no tap outside the keyboard can be proven side-effect-free) Hint: An element whose center sits behind the on-screen keyboard is refused with tap_keyboard_occludes_target; one whose center stays above the keys presses normally. To end editing, tap the app's own Done/Cancel control, or use keyboard enter to press the return key when submission is wanted. ``` Closes #364 ---

title: feat(run): test.step groups the steps a body calls under one named step
feat(screen): tap and swipe by coordinates with tapAt, swipe({ from, to }), and tap({ position })
body:
Deterministic coordinate input, the gap every Maestro and Playwright migration hits (`tapOn: { point }`, `swipe: { start, end }`, `click({ position })`). Until now only the agent's `tap_at` could name a point.

- `screen.tapAt({ x, y })`: a pointer tap at a viewport point, nothing resolved, the page decides what it lands on.
- `screen.swipe({ from, to })`: a swipe along a path, beside the directional `screen.swipe({ direction })`. A touch swipe on a device, a pointer drag in a browser (it drags the testbed board card between columns).
- `locator.tap({ position })` (and `click`): scrolls the node into view when the engine lists `scrollIntoView`, reads its box, dispatches the pointer at the offset. The platform's enabled and covered checks do not run; the reference says so.
- Points are CSS pixels, the space `boundingBox()` reports in. A non-finite or negative coordinate is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; an engine without the pointer kind is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before anything resolves (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts`, `checkPointerAction`).

```ts
const map = await screen.getByRole('image', { name: 'Seat map' }).boundingBox();
await screen.tapAt({ x: map.x + 360, y: map.y + 70 });
await screen.getByRole('image', { name: 'Seat map' }).tap({ position: { x: 120, y: 48 } });
await screen.swipe({ from: { x: 300, y: 400 }, to: { x: 40, y: 400 } });
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["tap({ position })"] --> B{engine lists scrollIntoView?}
  B -- yes --> C[perform scrollIntoView]
  B -- no --> D
  C --> D[locate, read rect]
  D --> E{visible with a box?}
  E -- "no, past deadline" --> F[LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND]
  E -- yes --> G["performAt(rect + offset, tap)"]
```

## Engine contract

- New pointer kind `{ kind: 'swipeTo', target: ViewportPoint }` in `packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts` carries the path swipe. A second shape on `swipe` would have let `pointerActions` declare a kind the engine then refuses half of; a separate kind keeps the gate honest. It stays apart from `dragTo` because a device drag holds before it moves, and agent-device exposes swipe and drag as different gestures.
- `TargetSession.pointerActions` is exposed, mirroring `actions`.
- Playwright: `swipeTo` is a pointer drag. Pointer points are rounded to the nearest CSS pixel in `performPointDrag` and `dispatchPointerAction`: Chromium truncates a fractional coordinate, so a tap composed from a box at y 148.875 landed one pixel early.
- Playwright: `screen.getByRole('image')` never matched. The engine passed the contract's `image` spelling to a role selector that only knows `img` (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts`). Own patch changeset.
- agent-device: declares `swipeTo` and performs it as `interactions.swipe({ from, to })`.

## Also

- Testbed `/pointer` page and `packages/testbed/tests/pointer.e2e.ts`: tapAt, position tap, a hidden node failing as the engine reports, path swipe, and the board drag.
- Docs: screen and engine references, Maestro, Playwright, and Detox migration tables, the writing-tests guide and skill. Four changesets.

title: docs(migrate): sort every Playwright and Maestro feature by where it lives and whether it exists
