title: feat(locator): all, allTextContents, isHidden, isDisabled, toBeAttached, and list-form text matchers
body: The reads and matchers a Playwright user types on day one, composed from reads the runner already had. No engine changed. - `locator.all()` resolves once and hands back one `nth(i)` locator per match; `locator.allTextContents()` reads every match's normalized text. Both follow the `count()` row of the strictness table: no waiting, no exactly-one rule, `[]` for zero matches. `allTextContents` is `POLICY_DENIED` on a secure field like `textContent`. - `isHidden()` is `!isVisible()`, `isDisabled()` is `!isEnabled()`, same ambiguity rule and same secure-field allowance as their positives. - `expect(locator).toBeAttached()` waits for one match, hidden or shown; it rides the same spec table as `toBeVisible`, so `not` and the 1000 ms grace window apply and the negated form passes on zero matches. - `toHaveText([...])` and `toContainText([...])`: the match count must equal the list length and the match at each position must satisfy its entry (string exact after normalization, RegExp by test). The single-value path is untouched. The failure lists every text observed. - `tests/helpers/screen-fixture.ts` is the node-list `screen` fixture the attributes unit test used to build inline; the new unit tests share it. - One engine addition: `LocatorEngine.readAll` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts`) reads every ref of one resolve and re-resolves the whole set when a member went stale, the same race `read` already tolerates. Both the read and the list matcher sample through it. ```ts for (const row of await screen.getByRole('row').all()) { await row.getByRole('checkbox').check(); } await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toHaveText(['Write spec', /^Ship/, 'Release']); await expect(screen.getByText('Hidden content')).toBeAttached(); expect(await screen.getByTestId('todo').isHidden()).toBe(true); ``` Failure of the list form: ```text expect.toHaveText failed locator: getByTestId("todo") expected: text ["Item Alpha", "Item Beta"] observed: text ["Item Alpha", "Item Beta", "Item Gamma"] (match count 3) ``` ## Left out: `or` and `and` Both engines compile `LocatorExpression` themselves (`packages/playwright/src/locators.ts` projects it onto Playwright locators, `packages/agent-device/src/locate.ts` evaluates it over the projected snapshot), so a union or intersection kind is a contract change with two engine implementations, not a core-only addition. A follow-up needs: - `or` and `and` variants in the `LocatorExpression` union (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`), `describeExpression` and `expressionHints` cases, and `INVALID_LOCATOR` for a non-runner argument. - Playwright: `locator.or()` and `locator.and()` exist, but the visible-query self-selector and the `getByDisplayValue` post-filter in `locators.ts` have to compose across both branches. - agent-device: set union in document order deduplicated by node ref, and intersection, in `resolveExpression`. - The `e2e/engine` contract test (`tests/integration/engine-contract.test.ts`) and a docs note on which engines support it. ---

title: feat(locator): widen the closed Role vocabulary and accept img as a spelling of image
body:
`getByRole('img')` and the roles a ported Playwright test names (`tablist`, `menu`, `progressbar`, `toolbar`, `form`, `group`, ...) were type errors. The list is still closed; it is longer, and `img` is an accepted spelling of `image`.

- `Role` grows from 31 to 54 names: `tablist`, `tabpanel`, `menu`, `menubar`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio`, `progressbar`, `spinbutton`, `meter`, `toolbar`, `tooltip`, `group`, `separator`, `radiogroup`, `grid`, `gridcell`, `rowgroup`, `rowheader`, `tree`, `treeitem`, `article`, `figure`, `form`. None of the proposed roles was dropped; see below for why.
- `img` is a `RoleAlias`, not a `Role`. `roleQuery` rewrites it to `image` before the expression exists (`packages/e2e/src/locator/expression.ts`), so engines, the trace cache, and reports only ever see `image`. `'img' satisfies Role` is a type error and `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` pins that.
- #382 on main already translates the contract's `image` to ARIA `img` when the web engine locates. This PR adds the other direction: the reader turns `role="img"` (a `<div>` or `<svg>` with an `aria-label`) into `image`, so the observation and the locator agree.
- The reader derives the new roles from HTML the way HTML-AAM does, instead of dropping the element: `<progress>`, `<meter>`, `<hr>`, `<fieldset>`, `<details>`, `<address>`, `<optgroup>`, `<input type="number">`, `<thead>`/`<tbody>`/`<tfoot>`, `<th scope="row">`, `<figure>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, page-level `<header>`/`<footer>`, and `<form>`/`<section>` when they carry a name. `<menu>` is a `list`, not a `menu`; only `role="menu"` is a menu, and Playwright's own snapshot agrees. A `<legend>`, `<figcaption>`, or `<caption>` names its fieldset, figure, or table, so `toHaveAccessibleName` reads what `getByRole('group', { name })` matched.
- The mobile engine maps the composite widget types it has on both platforms. On iOS the buttons inside a `TabBar` or `SegmentedControl` become `tab` (XCTest reports them as `Button`; the parent says what they are), and `ProgressIndicator` moves from `status` to `progressbar` (`ActivityIndicator` stays `status`: a spinner says something is happening, a bar says how far along).

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('img', { name: 'Fixture logo' })).toBeVisible();
const tabs = screen.getByRole('tablist', { name: 'Filter' });
await tabs.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Open' }).tap();
await expect(screen.getByRole('menu', { name: 'View' }).getByRole('menuitemcheckbox', { name: 'Show grid' })).toBeChecked();
await expect(screen.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Formatting' }).getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Font size' })).toHaveValue('12');
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["getByRole('img')"] --> B["roleQuery: img -> image"]
  B --> C["expression role=image"]
  C --> D["cache, report: image"]
  C --> E["web locate: image -> ARIA img (#382)"]
  C --> F["mobile locate: node.role === image"]
  G["web reader: role=img, img alt"] --> H["node.role = image"]
```

## How each engine treated a role outside the list before

- Web engine. An explicit `role="tablist"` already passed through the reader verbatim, so the observation the model reads said `tablist` while the test could not type it. Implicit HTML semantics outside the reader's switch (`<progress>`, `<hr>`, `<fieldset>`) returned no role, so the element was a nameless node or absent. `locate` never checked the list: Playwright accepts any ARIA role.
- Mobile engine. Anything not in `ROLE_MAP` keeps its lower-cased platform type as the role (`segmented-control`, `stepper`, `picker-wheel`), so a `tablist` query matched nothing and `ProgressIndicator` answered as `status`. Unknown types still pass through verbatim; that is what makes `getByRole('tooltip')` on a phone a `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and not a crash.
- Core. `CONTAINER_ROLES` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/actions.ts` names `article`, `group`, `tabpanel`, and `INTERACTIVE_ROLES` in `src/agent/observation.ts` names `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio`, `spinbutton`, `treeitem`. The agent reasoned over roles the type refused to let a test write.

## Why nothing was dropped

The brief said to drop a role one engine truly cannot produce. Applied literally, the mobile engine fails that test for 11 of the 31 roles already shipped (`searchbox`, `listbox`, `option`, `alertdialog`, `banner`, `contentinfo`, `complementary`, `region`, `main`, `columnheader`, `cell` as a table cell), and it would fail for `tooltip`, `figure`, `form`, `tree`, `separator` here. The list has never promised a widget on every platform. It promises one spelling per widget, so a role reads the same on a browser and a device and a typo is a type error rather than a silent miss. A role the platform has no widget for matches nothing, which `banner` already did on iOS. The docs say this now, in `docs/reference/screen.mdx` and the skill reference.

## Mobile mappings added

| Platform type | Role |
| --- | --- |
| iOS `TabBar`, `TabGroup`, `SegmentedControl`; Android `TabLayout`, `TabWidget`, `BottomNavigationView` | `tablist` |
| iOS `Button` inside a `TabBar` or `SegmentedControl`; Android `TabLayout$TabView`, `BottomNavigationItemView` | `tab` |
| iOS `ProgressIndicator`; Android `ProgressBar` | `progressbar` |
| iOS `Stepper`; Android `NumberPicker` | `spinbutton` |
| iOS `Toolbar`; Android `Toolbar` | `toolbar` |
| iOS `Menu`, `MenuBar`, `MenuBarItem` | `menu`, `menubar`, `menuitem` |
| iOS `RadioGroup`, `RadioButton`; Android `RadioGroup` | `radiogroup`, `radio` |
| iOS `TableRow` | `row` |

`Group` and `Other` are untouched. The mobile benchmark's bottom tabs are react-navigation JS tabs with no native `TabBar`, so its `getByRole('button', { name: /Actions/ })` still holds.

Docs: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` (the `Role` listing, `RoleAlias`, the alias note and the HTML derivation), `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` (observe row), `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. `docs/migrate/*.mdx` is left for its own PR.

title: feat(locator): pressSequentially types into one node as keystrokes
body: - `fill` sets the value and fires no key events. An autocomplete, a search-as-you-type box, or a masked input wired to `keydown`/`keyup` stays cold under it. `pressSequentially(text, { delay?, timeout? })` resolves exactly one node (usual strictness and actionability wait), performs `focus`, and types through the engine's `keyboard.type`. Same name and shape as Playwright's. - Composed in core from what SPI 1 already has: the `focus` action kind and the `keyboard` capability. No new `LocatorAction`, no engine package touched, no SPI bump. `packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts` (`LocatorEngine.pressSequentially`), `packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts`. - `delay` sends one character per `keyboard.type` call (split by code point) with that many ms between them; without it the whole text goes in one call. The focus retries a stale node like any action; the typing never retries, since a keystroke may already have landed. - A target whose engine lacks `focus` or `keyboard` fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before any node resolves (same pre-resolve check `perform` does, keyboard presence read off `session.verbs.has('typeText')` as the agent already does). - A `Secret` is a compile error (`tests/types/sdk-types.ts`) and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` at runtime, pointing at `fill`. Secrets are filled, never typed as keystrokes. Typing a plain string into a secure field is allowed; reads on it stay `POLICY_DENIED`. - The step is `locator.pressSequentially` with the locator description as its label, like `fill`: the text is not in the record. - Trace cache and the agent's action dispatcher enumerate grammar verbs, not locator apis (`src/agent/action-names.ts`, `src/cache/recorder.ts`), so a test-code step needs no change there. Confirmed by reading both; the cache tests are untouched and pass. - Both shipped engines work with the composition as-is: Playwright `typeText` refuses only after a CDP recovery (`observed` starts true), agent-device `focus` taps a textbox and `typeText` lands on the focused field. No device run in this PR; the device hooks were verified by reading, so a live check on a simulator is worth one run before relying on it there. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[locator.pressSequentially] --> B{engine declares focus + keyboard?} B -- no --> C[UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY] B -- yes --> D[resolve exactly one node] D --> E[perform focus] E --> F[keyboard.type chunk] F --> G{more chunks?} G -- sleep delay --> F G -- no --> H[step passed] ``` ```ts await screen.getByLabel('City').fill('Wa'); // value set, no key events, no suggestions await screen.getByLabel('City').pressSequentially('Wa'); // keydown/keyup fire, suggestions render await screen.getByLabel('City').pressSequentially('War', { delay: 50 }); ``` Tests: `tests/unit/press-sequentially.test.ts` (fake engine: call order, delay, code-point split, empty text, missing keyboard, missing focus, Secret, malformed options), `tests/integration/press-sequentially.test.ts` (Chromium against a fixture field that renders suggestions on `keyup` only: `fill` leaves the list empty, `pressSequentially` fills it, delay shows in the step's `durationMs`), and a testbed forms case on a new City field. Docs: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` (interface, `fill` vs `pressSequentially`, Secret rule, `PressSequentiallyOptions`), `docs/reference/engine.mdx` keyboard row, `docs/writing-an-engine.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. `docs/migrate/*` left alone on purpose. ---

title: feat(mobile): open deep links and web links from a test with device.openLink
body:
Maestro's most used command, `openLink`, had no equivalent here, so a magic-link sign-in or a deep-link route could not be tested on a device. `device.openLink(url, { app? })` is that equivalent on the `@e2edev/mobile` engine.

```ts
test('a magic link signs the user in', async ({ device, screen }) => {
  const link = await fetchMagicLinkFromInbox();
  await device.openLink(link);
  await expect(screen.getByText('Welcome back')).toBeVisible();
});

await device.openLink('https://example.com/verify', { app: 'com.apple.mobilesafari' });
```

- The link is bound to `app`, the pinned app by default, and the session observes that app afterwards. That is agent-device's `open <app> <url>` model, not a foreground follow: on iOS a web link the app does not claim goes to Safari and the next observation brings the app back.
- iOS needs an app. An unbound `open <url>` there succeeds and opens Safari, but creates no app session, so the very next snapshot fails with `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; the engine refuses it up front with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of leaving the test blind. Android lets the OS route an unbound link and agent-device reports the package that took it, which becomes the location's app.
- `file:`, `data:`, and `javascript:` links are `POLICY_DENIED`, a relative or empty string `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The rule is a local copy in `packages/mobile/src/links.ts` because `context.app.resolveUrl` calls `requireAppUrl` first (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:317`), which a device engine never satisfies.
- Recorded as a `device.openLink` step under `config.actionTimeout` with the usual error mapping. The step label cuts the URL before its query and fragment, where a magic link carries its one-time token; `setClipboard` hides its text for the same reason.
- `apps.open` shapes come from agent-device 0.21.6's typings and source: `{ app, url }` bound, `{ app: url }` unbound. iOS launches the app first only for an `http(s)` link and then runs `simctl openurl`; Android runs `am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <url> [-p <package>]`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["device.openLink(url, { app? })"] --> B[linkTarget: parse + scheme rule]
  B -- file/data/javascript --> D[POLICY_DENIED]
  B --> C{app or pinned app?}
  C -- none, iOS --> E[INVALID_ARGUMENT]
  C -- none, Android --> F["apps.open({ app: url })"]
  C -- yes --> G["apps.open({ app, url })"]
  F --> H[identity = package that took it]
  G --> H
  H --> I[fresh id generation, location follows]
```

Live on this machine, iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) through `E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_SIMULATOR=1 vitest run tests/integration/simulator.test.ts`, session pinned to Settings:

| Call | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| `openLink('https://example.com', { app: 'com.apple.mobilesafari' })` | location `com.apple.mobilesafari / ...`, tree contains "Example Domain" |
| `openLink('maps://?q=Cupertino', { app: 'com.apple.Maps' })` | location `com.apple.Maps / ...` |
| `openLink('https://example.com')` bound to Settings (earlier iteration) | Safari opened, next observation re-activated Settings (status bar showed "◀ Safari"); hence the app-bound wording |
| CLI `open https://example.com --platform ios` with no app | `appName: "https://example.com"`, no bundle id; `snapshot -i` then failed `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` ("iOS snapshot requires an active app session"); hence the iOS rule |

Android emulator (Medium Phone API 36.1), CLI probes: `open https://example.com --platform android` unbound returned `appBundleId: com.android.chrome` and `snapshot -i` observed the foreground; `open com.android.chrome https://example.com` bound was accepted with the same identity. Chrome itself showed its first-run screen behind a "System UI isn't responding" dialog, an emulator artefact, so no Android tree content was asserted.

Not in this PR: an `open_link` agent tool. `mobileTools` is unchanged; the tool is a follow-up if a benchmark scenario needs the agent to open a link inside a goal. `docs/migrate/maestro.mdx` still says `openLink` has no equivalent; a separate PR rewrites that page and adds the row.

title: feat(expect): toHaveLength, toMatchObject, toHaveProperty, asymmetric matchers, and expect.soft
body:
Brings the value side of `expect` to what a Playwright or Jest user types without thinking, as runner code only. No engine changed.

Cut down from the first version on Oskar's call: the unit-runner matchers (`toThrow`, `toBeInstanceOf`, `toBeNaN`, `toStrictEqual`, `resolves`/`rejects`, `expect.extend`) are out. An end-to-end test checks what the app shows and what its API returns; those belong in the unit runner. Equality stays on `@vitest/expect` (`equals`, `iterableEquality`, `subsetEquality`) and the asymmetric matchers are its `Any`, `Anything`, `ObjectContaining`, `ArrayContaining`, `StringContaining`, `StringMatching` classes, so `toEqual` keeps the rules it had and the runner carries no equality code of its own.

## Matchers

- Three value matchers: `toHaveLength`, `toMatchObject`, `toHaveProperty` (dotted or array path, optional value through a rest tuple so "omitted" and `undefined` differ). Each works under `.not` and lands on `expect.poll` through the derived `PollExpectation` type; the matcher map in `packages/e2e/src/expect/poll.ts` gains the names and `satisfies` keeps the two lists equal.
- `expect.any`, `expect.anything`, `expect.objectContaining`, `expect.arrayContaining`, `expect.stringContaining`, `expect.stringMatching` as statics, honoured inside `toEqual`, `toMatchObject`, the collection form of `toContain`, and `toHaveProperty`. In a failure message one prints as `Any<Number>`, `ObjectContaining {"name":"Ada"}` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts`, `describeMatcher`), nested ones included.

```ts
expect(order).toMatchObject({ customer: { name: 'Ada' }, lines: [{ sku: 'a' }, { sku: 'b' }] });
expect(created).toEqual({
  id: expect.stringMatching(/^usr_/),
  createdAt: expect.any(String),
  roles: expect.arrayContaining(['member']),
});
expect(rows).toContain(expect.objectContaining({ status: 'paid' }));
expect(response).toHaveProperty('body.total', expect.any(Number));
```

## expect.soft

- `expect.soft(actual)` takes what `expect(actual)` takes: a value, a locator, or an engine fixture (`expect.soft(web).toHaveURL(...)` works). It is a Proxy over whatever `expect(actual)` returns (`packages/e2e/src/expect/soft.ts`, `soften`) that catches an `ASSERTION_FAILED` and keeps it on the attempt. The failure is classified with `classifyError` rather than `instanceof`, because an engine's matcher throws from its own copy of the error module.
- The runner opens a `SoftFailures` per attempt next to `publishAttempt` and closes it when the body settles (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`). Kept failures become one `ASSERTION_FAILED` whose message numbers them in order; its stack is the first failure's, so the report points at the first soft line. A body that throws or times out keeps its own error and records the soft one under `secondaryErrors`, the same shape `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` uses. A runtime skip drops them.
- After close, `expect.soft` throws like `expect`. That covers `afterEach` and a standalone script with no attempt at all.
- Report: a soft locator or `web` matcher is still a recorded `expect.<matcher>` step marked failed, since `steps.run` records before the Proxy swallows. A soft value matcher is not a step, the same as a hard one; its failure is in the final error only. There is no `expect.soft.poll`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["expect.soft(x).toBe(y) fails"] --> B{attempt collecting?}
  B -- no --> C[throw ASSERTION_FAILED]
  B -- yes --> D[SoftFailures.keep]
  D --> E[body runs on]
  E --> F{body settled}
  F -- returned --> G[one ASSERTION_FAILED listing every soft failure]
  F -- threw or timed out --> H[body error stays, soft error under secondaryErrors]
  G --> I["afterEach: expect.soft throws at once"]
  H --> I
```

```text
ASSERTION_FAILED: 2 soft assertions failed
1. expected "$40.00" to be "$41.00"
2. expect.toBeEnabled failed
   locator: getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' })
   expected: enabled
   observed: states: disabled (match count 1)
```

## Equality edge cases

The review on the earlier custom equality module raised four cases. Against `@vitest/expect` they land like this, and the regression tests in `tests/unit/expect-values.test.ts` pin the behaviour:

- Cycles in `toMatchObject`: terminate. At the point the reference comes round, Jest compares the pair for full equality instead of as a subset, so an actual with a property the expected lacks stops matching there.
- An iterable on one side only: fails the assertion, no native `TypeError`.
- Arrays that differ only in a non-index key like `'01'`: not equal.
- Set entries: Jest's rule lets one expected entry satisfy several structurally equal actual entries, so `new Set([{ x: 1 }, { x: 1 }])` equals `new Set([{ x: 1 }, { y: 2 }])`. Map entries pair key and value together and do not share this. Kept as Jest has it rather than diverging from what `toEqual` users expect.

## Types and docs

- `ValueExpectation<T>` gains the three matchers; `Expect` is now `ExpectCall` (the three call shapes) plus `poll`, `soft: ExpectCall`, and the six statics. New exported types: `AsymmetricMatcher`, `Class`, `PropertyPath`. `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts` pins what is easy to loosen (`toHaveProperty` path shapes, `expect.soft` having no `poll` or statics, the statics' argument types).
- `docs/reference/expect.mdx`: interface listing, `toMatchObject` and `toHaveProperty` rules, new "Asymmetric matchers" and "Soft assertions" sections, and one paragraph naming what is deliberately not there. `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md` lists the new names. Changeset: `e2e` minor.
- `docs/migrate/*.mdx` is untouched on purpose; a separate PR rewrites those pages.

title: feat(cli): select tests with --exclude-tag, --grep, and --grep-invert
body: First of a five-PR stack from the selection audit (2026-09-17): `--exclude-tag` and `--grep` were ranked first. Next up: `file:line`, then `--last-failed` + `--shard`, then `--max-failures`, then `--repeat-each`. - `--exclude-tag ` leaves out every test carrying one of the tags, whatever `--tag` or a positional selected. A serial group still runs whole when any member is selected; tag the serial `describe` to exclude the flow. - `--grep ` keeps tests whose title matches, `--grep-invert ` drops the ones that match. The text is the describe titles and the test title joined by one space (`checkout pays`), not the file (positionals do that) and not the tags (`--tag` does that). Bare pattern or `/pattern/flags`; repeat a flag for alternatives; a pattern that does not compile is a usage error, exit 2. - `run` and `list` declare the selection flags once, through `selectionOptions()` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`, so the two commands cannot drift. - `NO_TESTS` names what each filter removed: `2 carry one of the excluded tags slow`, `3 have titles matching none of /billing/, /admin/i`. ```bash npx e2e run --tag smoke --exclude-tag slow npx e2e run --grep checkout --grep-invert '/refund/i' npx e2e list --grep checkout --exclude-tag slow ``` ```ts await run({ excludeTags: ['slow'], grep: [/checkout/], grepInvert: [/refund/i] }); ``` Filter order in `classifyPair` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`): positional, `.only`, `--tag`, `--exclude-tag`, `--grep`, `--grep-invert`, then platform and capability. ---

title: feat(cli): select one test with a file:line positional
body: Stacked on #387. GitHub retargets this to `main` once that merges. - Any positional form may end in `:line`: `tests/signup.e2e.ts:12`, `signup:12`, `agent/signup.e2e.ts:12`. It selects only the test whose `test(` call opens on that line, the same line the report's `source` shows. - Several lines of one file add up. Naming the file without a line selects it whole. A serial group runs whole when a line names one member, as under `--tag`. - A positional that exists on disk as written stays a path, so a file literally named `a.e2e.ts:1` is still selectable. - When no test is declared at a named line, `NO_TESTS` says where they are: `tests/direct.e2e.ts:2 names no test (declared at line 3)`. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[positional] --> S{splitLine} S -- "path exists" --> F[file, whole] S -- "path:line" --> M[positionalMatcher on path] M --> L["CollectedFile.lines"] L --> T["test.selected = file selected AND source.line in lines"] ``` - The check runs against mapped lines, so its integration test spawns the built CLI like `tests/integration/test-source.test.ts` does; a vitest fork reports raw transformed positions (every test on line 1). - `PositionalSelection.lines` and `CollectedFile.lines` carry the named lines; `FILTERED_REASON.line` tells a line-filtered test apart from a file no positional named. ---

title: feat(cli): rerun with --last-failed and split a run with --shard
body: Stacked on #388. - `--last-failed` selects only the tests the previous run did not pass, read from the `report.json` this run overwrites (beside the artifact root, so `--artifacts` moves both). Did not pass means failed, timed out, interrupted, or skipped because a setup, a serial predecessor, a hook, or the worker failed. An explicit skip or a filtered test is not rerun. No report there is the new `NO_LAST_RUN` (exit 2); a run with nothing failed selects nothing, `NO_TESTS` unless `--pass-with-no-tests`. - `--shard ` runs one contiguous slice of the selected tests, cut once every other filter and the serial closure applied. Slices differ by at most one item, the first shards taking the remainder (Playwright's split), a serial group counts as one item and is never split, and each shard brings only the setup tests its own tests need because the cut happens before `applySessionSelection`. - `e2e list` takes both, so `e2e list --shard 2/3` shows what a job would run. ```bash npx e2e run npx e2e run --last-failed # the loop after a red run npx e2e run --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3 # one CI job of three ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR C[classifyPair: file, only, tag, exclude, grep, last-failed] --> S[applySerialClosure] S --> H["applyShard (contiguous slice)"] H --> P[applySessionSelection: setups the slice needs] ``` - `packages/e2e/src/run/last-run.ts` reads the report: `readLastFailed(reportPath)` returns the result ids; `select` compares with `resultId(testId, target, agent)`, so a test is named per target and agent. - Docs: `ci.mdx` gains a Sharding section with the matrix example and a note that merging shard reports is not implemented yet, plus a rerun section. ---

title: feat(run): stop a run at --max-failures
body: Stacked on #389. - `--max-failures ` (`RunOptions.maxFailures`) stops the run once that many tests have failed or timed out. Nothing more is dispatched, the tests running end as `interrupted`, the tests not started are skipped with the new cause `failure-limit` and the reason `run stopped after 3 failures (--max-failures 3)`. The exit code is the failures' own, 1, never 130. - The scheduler owns the stop. Every result now leaves through `Scheduler.report()`, which counts; at the limit it skips its queues and interrupts its workers the way the interrupt signal would (`interrupting` = signal fired or limit hit). - The interrupt message carries the skip as the abort reason (`interruptController.abort(skip)`), so the pairs a worker had not started say why instead of `run interrupted before execution`. `interruptedSkip(signal)` in `units.ts` reads it back; a plain interrupt is unchanged. - Reporters get a `run-stopped { failures, limit }` event; the list reporter prints `stopped after 3 failures (--max-failures 3): the running tests end as interrupted, the rest are skipped`. - Wire change: `schema/report-v1.schema.json` skip causes gain `failure-limit`. The fixtures are unchanged; the integration test validates a real report carrying the cause against the schema. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as worker participant S as scheduler participant R as runner W->>S: result (failed) #2 of 2 S->>S: skip queues as failure-limit S->>R: onFailureLimit(2, 2) R->>R: stoppedEarly, emit run-stopped S->>W: interrupt { skip } W->>S: running test interrupted, unstarted pairs skipped with skip ``` Left as it was: a plain Ctrl-C still drops a unit queued on a worker that had not finished starting without a result, which predates this PR. ---

title: feat(run): run every test n times with --repeat-each
body: Stacked on #390. Last of the stack. - `--repeat-each ` (`RunOptions.repeatEach`) runs every selected test that many times. `repeatEach(selection, n)` in `select.ts` expands each runnable ordinary pair into `n` adjacent copies with `repeat` 0 through `n - 1`; setup tests run once, filtered and skipped pairs are reported once. - The repeat is a dimension of a pair's identity beside test, target, and agent. It rides on `TestTargetPair`, `WirePair`, the pair-start and progress messages, `pairKey`, the `ResultRecord`, the `SerialGroupRecord`, and the report result and serial group (`repeat: 0` on every report from now on; optional in the schema so older reports still validate). - Ids stay stable. `resultId(test, target, agent, repeat)` digests the same three fields when `repeat` is 0 and adds `repeat` otherwise, so the first run's id is what it was; the serial group id does the same. - Later runs are titled `(repeat #1)`, `(repeat #2)` in the list reporter, JUnit, and the markdown failure pages, and their artifacts go under a `repeat-` segment so they cannot overwrite the first run's. - `test-started` and `step` events carry `repeat`, so a live reporter keeps each run's row apart. - `--last-failed` now keys the previous run's results by test, target, and agent instead of the result id, so a test is named once whichever of its repeats did not pass, and runs once on the rerun. ```bash npx e2e run --repeat-each 5 --no-cache tests/checkout.e2e.ts ``` With the trace cache on, the first run records and the later ones replay, so a flakiness hunt on an agentic test wants `--no-cache`; the flag's help and the docs say so. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[select] --> R["repeatEach(n): pair x n"] R --> U[buildWorkPlans: one file unit, repeats adjacent] U --> W["worker: pairKey(test, agent, repeat)"] W --> B["report: id = resultId(..., repeat), repeat field"] ``` ---

title: feat!: rename engine packages to @e2edev/web and @e2edev/mobile
body: ## What and why - Engine packages name what they drive, not what they are built on. Core already treats engines as a contract with no engine noun in `src/`; the package name was the last place the implementation leaked. Renaming after launch costs every user a migration, so it lands now. - `@e2edev/playwright` -> `@e2edev/web`, factory `playwright()` -> `web()`, engine name `web`, types `WebOptions`, `WebConnectOptions`, `WebBasicAuth`. - `@e2edev/agent-device` -> `@e2edev/mobile`, factory `agentDevice()` -> `mobile()`, engine name `mobile`, types `MobileOptions`, `MobilePlatform`, tool pack `mobileTools` from `@e2edev/mobile/tools`. - Kept on purpose: the `device` fixture (asymmetric with `web`, decided), `PlaywrightLiveSurface` (it hands out Playwright objects), option values like `browser: 'chromium'` and `connect.cdpEndpoint`, and the init hints "Playwright" / "agent-device" so a user still learns what is underneath. - `e2e init` writes the new packages; the build records their versions under the new keys in `sibling-versions.json`. Docs pages move to `reference/web` and `reference/mobile` with redirects from the old paths. - Existing changesets and the three from #380 point at the new package names so `changeset version` still resolves them. ```ts // e2e.config.ts import { web } from '@e2edev/web'; import { mobile } from '@e2edev/mobile'; export default defineConfig({ targets: [ { name: 'web', engine: web({ url: 'http://localhost:3000' }) }, { name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios', app: 'Settings' }) }, ], }); ``` Follow-up outside this PR: deprecate `@e2edev/playwright` and `@e2edev/agent-device` on npm by hand, the way `@e2edev/oauth` was, and publish the new names once. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it. No deprecation window: the packages are pre-1.0 and unreleased on `latest`. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: feat(agent): createAgent takes context, the app vocabulary every model call gets
body:
## What and why

- `system` and `context` are two different things and the built-in agent could only take one of them at construction. `system` is how the acting agent works: its persona, its caution, what it verifies before finishing. Only the act loop reads it, and the judges behind `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract` never see it, so nothing in it can talk a judge into a verdict. `context` is what the app calls things: screen and menu names, where a feature lives, which button submits a form. Every model call gets it, judges included, because a judge that does not know "plans are called tiers" cannot check that a tier was chosen.
- Until now `context` existed only on the agent's options object, so a complete built-in agent had to be written as `{ executor: createAgent({ model, system }), model, context }`, with `model` twice and the vocabulary split from the prompt it belongs next to. A real suite's config had exactly that shape.
- `createAgent({ model, system, context })` is now a complete agent. The executor carries the vocabulary the same way it carries its model, and config resolution uses whichever of the two places is set. Two different values for one agent is `INVALID_CONFIG`, the rule `model` already follows: joining or overriding would leave two vocabularies disagreeing without anyone noticing.
- Collateral fix: `HostExecutor` had a `context` promise on the class that stopped it implementing `StepExecutor`; renamed `opened`.
- Tests: config resolution for executor-only, equal, differing, over the byte bound, and neither; a fixture-graph test asserting the system prompt is byte-identical whether the vocabulary comes from `createAgent` or the options object, joins with test-level `agentContext`, and is absent when unset; `sdk-types.ts` pins `context` as one string. Docs, reference, and skill explain the distinction in the terms above.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat(sdk): stamp fixture and unique as a template tag
body: ## What and why - Open Mercato's suite wrote its own `stamp` fixture from `Date.now()` and `Math.random()`, derived six strings from it per test, and re-wrapped each in `unique()` at every `act` call; the skill still recommended `Date.now()` names in three places. - Core `stamp` fixture: `e2e` + start millisecond in base36 + 4 random chars, lowercase letters and digits only, one per attempt. The prefix marks records as test data and keeps the string a valid identifier start; the alphabet survives slug fields, URL paths, and file names, so a heading or route that echoes the name still matches. - `unique` as a tag: `unique\`${stamp} Company\`` returns the same frozen `Unique` as `unique(string)` and interpolates strings, finite numbers, and earlier `Unique` values. `unique(value)` is unchanged. No third surface: a tag on the fixture itself would hide the mark at the call site, and a derivation helper would be a string API the tag already is. - `stamp` joins the core fixture names `test.extend` and engines may not shadow; docs (`cache`, `writing-tests`, `reference/test`) and `skills/e2e` now show `stamp` plus the tag instead of `Date.now()`. - Tests: tag and `createStamp` units in `trace-template.test.ts` (through `validateParams` and the template path), fixture in `fixture-runtime.test.ts`, type assertions in `sdk-types.ts`, a testbed forms test that fills and reads back a stamped name (passed through the real CLI). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(run): add a cleanup fixture that runs test-registered teardown newest first on every verdict
body: ## What and why - Open Mercato's suite reinvented this in a fixture: `api.track(path, id)` after every UI-created record, then `for (const { path, id } of this.tracked.splice(0).reverse()) await this.request('DELETE', ...).catch(() => undefined)` in the teardown. The REST client is the author's; the lifecycle (LIFO, run after failures, own budget, reported) is the runner's. `cleanup.add(fn)` is that lifecycle. - Ordering: callbacks run after the `afterEach` hooks and before the `test.extend` teardowns. A hook still sees what the test created; a callback can still use the fixture that created it. Taken lazily, so a hook or a callback can register more. Runs on pass, failure, `test.skip` from the body, and timeout. - Budget and errors: each callback enters its own `cleanupTimeout` budget (same `runHook` + `budget.enter` path as an `afterEach`), so an overrun cancels that callback and the next still runs. A throw or a timeout is recorded under the attempt's `secondaryErrors` with phase `cleanup` and never becomes the verdict. `cleanup.add` after the attempt's cleanup ran is `TEST_SETUP_FAILED`. `e2e mcp` standalone sessions drain the same queue at close. - No new step kind or wire change: a callback's harness actions are steps like a hook's, and the error lands in the existing `secondaryErrors` field with the existing `cleanup` phase. Schema and fixtures untouched. - Tests: `tests/unit/cleanup.test.ts` (LIFO, add while draining, seal, non-function), `tests/integration/cleanup-fixture.test.ts` (order against afterEach and fixture teardown with the fixtures alive, run after failure/skip/timeout and from an afterEach hook, throwing and overrunning callbacks as secondary errors with the verdict kept), type assertions in `tests/types/sdk-types.ts`. Docs: `writing-tests.mdx`, `reference/test.mdx`, `reference/errors.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(web): pass Playwright context and launch options through web({ context, launch })
body: `web({ context, launch })` pass Playwright's own configuration through. Without them a project could not set a locale, a time zone, a color scheme, mobile emulation, `ignoreHTTPSErrors`, or `channel: 'chrome'` on its browser. - `context` goes to `browser.newContext` for every context an attempt opens, the one a state reset or a session restore replaces it with included. - `launch` goes to `browserType.launch` for the worker's browser. A launch naming `executablePath` or a release channel other than `chromium` skips the first-run browser download, since the managed browser is never started. - The engine keeps the keys its bookkeeping owns and refuses them at config load as `INVALID_CONFIG`, naming the option that stands in. - `context.viewport` and `viewport` are one setting, so a device descriptor spreads in whole and sizes screenshots and video too. Two differing values are refused. - New types `WebContextOptions` and `WebLaunchOptions` are `Omit`s over Playwright's, so the reserved keys fail at typecheck as well (`packages/web/tests/types/browser-options.ts`). ```ts import { web } from '@e2edev/web'; import { devices } from 'playwright'; export default { targets: [ { name: 'de-dark', engine: web({ ...app, context: { locale: 'de-DE', timezoneId: 'Europe/Berlin', colorScheme: 'dark' } }) }, { name: 'iphone', engine: web({ ...app, context: { ...devices['iPhone 13'] } }) }, { name: 'chrome', engine: web({ ...app, context: { ignoreHTTPSErrors: true }, launch: { channel: 'chrome' } }) }, ], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` | Refused | Use instead | | --- | --- | | `context.acceptDownloads` | always on, for `web.waitForDownload` | | `context.httpCredentials` | `basicAuth` | | `context.recordVideo` | `e2e run --video` | | `context.viewport: null` | a fixed viewport | | `launch.headless` | `e2e run --headed` | Guarded combinations: `serviceWorkers: 'allow'` next to `headers` (the site-scoped header route depends on the block), `launch.channel` on a non-chromium browser, `launch` with `connect`, `context` with `connect.reconnectEndpoint`. Validation and merge rules live in `packages/web/src/browser-options.ts`; the surface spreads `context` under its own keys in `packages/web/src/surface.ts` and hands the merged launch options to `BrowserConnection.acquire`. `extraHTTPHeaders` and `storageState` pass through on purpose: both are ordinary Playwright behaviour a project may want. Docs: new "Browser context and launch options" section in `docs/reference/web.mdx`, the browser guide, the viewports limits, the skill's options table, and the package README. Changeset: minor for `@e2edev/web`. ---

title: fix(agent): wait out a screen that says it is loading before judging, acting, or caching it
body: ## What and why - Measured on a Next.js admin app: a page whose content is `Loading product`, or a list showing a spinner, counted as settled. The next `agent.assert` judged the skeleton and failed as inconclusive, the trace cache's end check saw its anchors missing and handed off, and the baseline taken before the list rendered recorded the whole table as the step's delta. Consumers worked around it with `expect(screen.getByText(/Loading/)).toBeHidden()` before every assert. - `isLoadingObservation` names three signals the app gives: an indeterminate `progressbar` (no value), `aria-busy="true"` on the root or a landmark, or a content area of at most three text-bearing leaves outside the chrome (navigation, banner, contentinfo) with one matching `loading`, `please wait`, or an ellipsis alone. A paragraph mentioning loading on an ordinary page has too many neighbours to qualify. - `settleObservation` waits through such a screen for up to `LOADING_WAIT_MS` (5 s) after the change wait; judgments (`invocation.observe`) settle the same way with no stability wait; the replay end check takes the settled look first. A screen still loading at the bound is used as it is, never an error. The empty document stays transitional only: `about:blank` promises no content, and waiting on it would tax every `act` that starts before its first navigation (and every fake-engine test). - Tests: every rule with a realistic tree, positives and negatives; settle through a loading screen with and without a pre-action shape; the bound; the cache baseline and end check taking the settled look. Unit suite 1584 passed, `tsc`, `oxlint`, `check:dead-code` clean. Web benchmark agentic suite not run (no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in the environment). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## e2e@0.15.0

### Minor Changes

- [#380](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/380) [`54c0dba`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/54c0dba62fc47403564ece41ce503bb9b9ce9a08) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Coordinate input for the deterministic API. `screen.tapAt({ x, y })` taps a viewport point with no node behind it, `screen.swipe({ from, to })` swipes along a path between two points (a touch swipe on a device, a pointer drag on a document platform), and `tap({ position })` on a locator (also `click`) taps at an offset of the node's box, scrolling it into view first when the engine can. Points are CSS pixels, the space `boundingBox()` reports in; a negative or non-finite coordinate is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and an engine without the matching pointer action is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before anything is resolved. Engine contract: a new `swipeTo` pointer action kind (`{ kind: 'swipeTo', target }`) carries the path swipe, and `TargetSession` exposes `pointerActions`. `Point`, `TapOptions`, and `SwipePathOptions` are exported.

- [#394](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/394) [`4c93414`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4c934142bc4ef4002811eff2be20d463343dd381) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `createAgent` accepts `context`, with the value and meaning of `agents.<name>.context`: trusted project vocabulary prepended to every act turn and judgment of that agent. `{ executor: createAgent({ model, system, context }) }` is now a complete agent, so the options object around it needs no second `model` or `context` key. Naming a different `context` on both `createAgent` and the options object is `INVALID_CONFIG`, as it is for `model`; the same value on both is accepted. `StepExecutor` gains an optional `context` member for the same reconciliation.

- [#365](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/365) [`f7f86d9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7f86d91e87b317dea9ae076f143e20f6ba8ed98) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The engine contract gains an optional `finish(info)` hook: once per run and target in the runner process, after the last worker of the target is gone, on every exit path (pass, failure, interrupt, a `prepare` that threw part-way), within the cleanup budget and never cancelled by an interrupt. Release what `prepare` acquired for the run there. `EnginePrepareInfo` carries `projectRoot`, so a hook can resolve a relative option before any worker exists. Additive; the SPI version stays 1.

- [#417](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/417) [`a577da3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a577da3199c42402dfb9a04cd8452c5d89ab40dc) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `EngineInitInfo` gains `log(line)`, the same progress line `prepare` and `finish` already have: the runner streams it as a `notice` run event prefixed with the target and worker slot (`ios worker 1: ...`), from a worker process and an in-process worker alike, so a fact that only exists once the worker is up (the URL a hosted browser or device can be watched at, which simulator a slot got) reaches the reporter and every host sink. Additive; the SPI version stays 1.

- [#386](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/386) [`a583a88`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a583a88254cd80450f986174b022cf961442e7f0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Three value matchers a Playwright or Jest test reaches for: `toHaveLength`, `toMatchObject`, and `toHaveProperty` (dotted or array path, optional value), each under `.not` and on `expect.poll`. `expect.any`, `expect.anything`, `expect.objectContaining`, `expect.arrayContaining`, `expect.stringContaining`, and `expect.stringMatching` stand in for values inside `toEqual`, `toMatchObject`, `toContain`, and `toHaveProperty`; they are Jest's matchers with Jest's rules. The unit-runner matchers (`toThrow`, `toBeInstanceOf`, `toStrictEqual`, `resolves`, `expect.extend`) stay out.
  
  `expect.soft(actual)` returns the same matchers for a locator, a `web` fixture, or a value, but keeps a failure on the attempt instead of throwing it. Once the body has settled the attempt fails with one `ASSERTION_FAILED` listing every soft failure in order; a body that throws or times out keeps its own error and records the soft failures under `secondaryErrors`. Outside a test body, in a standalone script or an `afterEach` hook, `expect.soft` throws at once like `expect`.

- [#382](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/382) [`2e18196`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2e18196b79ac724c2a274a27562ea06d7a316d02) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The locator reads and matchers a Playwright user reaches for on day one. `locator.all()` hands back one `nth(i)` locator per current match and `locator.allTextContents()` reads every match's normalized text; both resolve once, without waiting or the exactly-one rule, and answer zero matches with `[]`. `isHidden()` is the negation of `isVisible()` and `isDisabled()` of `isEnabled()`, with the same strictness and the same `POLICY_DENIED` rules on secure fields. `expect(locator).toBeAttached()` waits for one match to exist, hidden or shown, and negated passes once nothing matches. `toHaveText` and `toContainText` take a list: the match count must equal the list length and each match must satisfy the entry at its position, a string exactly, a `RegExp` by test; the failure lists every text observed.

- [#384](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/384) [`0f864ad`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0f864ad3f3e7f5242ed957941e58e55e1a818aee) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `locator.pressSequentially(text, { delay?, timeout? })` types into exactly one editable node as keystrokes, so an autocomplete, a search-as-you-type box, or a masked input wired to key events reacts the way it does for a user. `fill` sets the value and fires no key events, which leaves those apps cold. The harness composes it from the engine's `focus` action and `keyboard` capability, so no engine changes; a target lacking either fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before any node resolves. `delay` sends one character per keyboard call that many milliseconds apart. A `Secret` is a type error and `INVALID_ARGUMENT` at runtime: secrets go through `fill`.

- [#413](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/413) [`2b9361f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2b9361ffea8e39d2c32a5b1e2a6a98c2da759380) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The markdown page's folded test list is one table: a row per file with its counts and time, worst file first, then a row per test. The agent column appears only when the run used the agent. The GitHub comment and `summary.md` both render it.

- [#390](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/390) [`2e4d40e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2e4d40eb0754f2558e5e89fe80b4b4933183d023) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e run --max-failures <n>` (`RunOptions.maxFailures`) stops the run once that many tests have failed or timed out: nothing more is dispatched, the tests running end as `interrupted`, and the tests not started are skipped with the new cause `failure-limit` and the reason `run stopped after 3 failures (--max-failures 3)`; the exit code is the failures' own. Reporters get a `run-stopped` event with the count and the limit. The report schema's skip causes gain `failure-limit`.

- [#377](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/377) [`9f2b73f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9f2b73f9293d4cdee449bb04e4f8272477d22402) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Subscription sign-in ships inside `e2e`; the separate `@e2edev/oauth` package is gone. Import the model from `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`, `e2e/oauth/copilot`, or `e2e/oauth/grok` and install only the provider package it wraps (`@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, or `@ai-sdk/xai`). The constructors and the CLI are the whole surface; the `createOAuthFetch` library API of the old package is not carried over. `e2e init` writes those imports and no longer adds a sibling dependency, `e2e login` and `e2e logout` run the flows directly, and the `e2e-oauth` bin is retired; uninstall `@e2edev/oauth` from projects that had it. The `chatgpt()` fold for the Codex stream without a `content-type` header lands with it.
  
  `e2e models [provider]` asks the vendor which models a stored login serves and prints their ids. `chatgpt()` now tells the AI SDK that the Codex backend stores nothing server side, so a second turn carries the encrypted reasoning of the first instead of referring to it by an id the backend cannot find (`Item with id 'rs_…' not found`). The `CHATGPT_MODELS` constant is gone; the list is the vendor's.

- [#392](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/392) [`f5e96d0`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f5e96d0cbea6bc26da1084ea3bbc49b7a7a16dd8) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The engine packages are named after what they drive, not what they are built on. `@e2edev/playwright` is now `@e2edev/web` with a `web()` factory, and `@e2edev/agent-device` is now `@e2edev/mobile` with a `mobile()` factory; the engine names in reports and telemetry follow (`web`, `mobile`). title: feat(web): seed configured cookies into every fresh browser context
body: ## What and why - Open Mercato's suite sets three notice-acknowledgement cookies (`om_demo_notice_ack`, `om_cookie_notice_ack`, `om_feedback_suppress`) by hand before every signed-out test and tells the agent to close the banners when they appear. `web({ cookies })` moves that into config: the `web.setCookies` shape, `url` defaulting to the app's `url`. - Seeded into every fresh context the engine creates: a sessionless test's, the one `app.clearState()` opens, and the one a saved session is restored into. Unavailable with `connect.reconnectEndpoint`, like `headers` and `basicAuth`. - Precedence: a restored session's cookie of the same name wins. The configured cookies are added first and the session's own written back after, so a value the app set during sign-in is never overwritten by config. - Validated at config load as `INVALID_CONFIG` naming the field: non-array, non-object entry, a name or value the `Cookie` header cannot carry, a `url` that is not absolute http(s), `url` and `domain` together, or neither on a target without `url`. - Tests: integration (first open of a sessionless attempt, after reset, session-wins on restore, default target origin and not another site) on a `/cookies` fixture page echoing the `Cookie` header; unit shape rejections; `tests/types/cookies.ts` pins the `url`-or-`domain` shape. `Cookie`/`CookieFields` move to `cookies.ts` so the surface and the fixture share one `addCookies` mapping. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

Updates `fallow` from 3.24.1 to 3.27.0
Release notes

Sourced from fallow's releases.

v3.27.0: every CI gate reaches the job, baseline staleness in CI, MCP verdicts

Features

  • Armed gates report their verdict in the JSON envelope. A run that arms a gate carries gate_outcomes, an object keyed by gate name. Each entry has status (pass, warn, fail or skipped) and enforced, plus observed, threshold and threshold_label where a comparison happened. The object holds only the gates the run armed: a dead-code run can exit 1 on the default severity rules with no object at all. The key set is open, and a gate name a consumer does not recognise means "some gate". (#2680, #2681, #2683, #2685)
  • Baseline staleness is in the envelope, and CI can gate on it. 3.26.0 put the stale-baseline advisory and --fail-on-stale-baseline on stderr only, which --quiet removes, and the GitHub Action and the GitLab template both run with --quiet. dead-code / check, the bare run, dupes and health carry one baseline_staleness object, also in grouped output: the entry counts, change_scoped, the advisory verdict and gate_trips. Both integrations show a stale baseline as a warning and in the job summary. On a pull request the main run covers changed files only. The integrations therefore re-read the baseline once over the whole project, which took 0.11s with a cache and 0.24s with type-aware analysis on an 870-file TypeScript project. The new fail-on-stale-baseline input and FALLOW_FAIL_ON_STALE_BASELINE variable decide whether the verdict fails the job. The pull-request comment and the merge-request note do not carry the advisory yet. Thanks @​cloud-walker for the report, which traced the gap through the action scripts. (#2673)
  • min-score is an Action input and a GitLab variable. Before this release it was reachable only through args: / FALLOW_ARGS. --min-score implies --score, so the integrations add --complexity when no health section input is set; the annotations, the SARIF upload and the pull-request comment stay populated that way. The CLI turns its own findings rule off for such a run and the integrations follow, which leaves the score to decide it. min-score and min-severity apply to command: health and exit 2 elsewhere. (#2682)
  • A run that analyzed no source file reports it. The run warns and passes by default; fail-on-empty-analysis: true (FALLOW_FAIL_ON_EMPTY_ANALYSIS on GitLab) makes it fail. The envelope carries a no-source-files-analyzed diagnostic and the new workspace_diagnostics[].degrades_analysis. When findings cover less than the whole project, the integrations print one combined warning with the diagnostic kinds and their counts. (#2686)
  • MCP tool results carry the verdict. The tools run the CLI with --quiet and turn exit 1 into a successful result, which hid every gate verdict from the agent. The root warnings array carries a stale baseline with the re-save remedy, every gate that reported fail or warn with its numbers, and one entry for a degraded run. The subprocess, Code Mode and typed routes all do this, and find_dupes with a threshold takes the route that can evaluate it. A response with nothing to report is unchanged. (#2676)
  • fallow report --from renders what each gate concluded, as a notice annotation and as a line in the job summary, the pull-request comment and the merge-request note. The line is informational and never fails a step. (#2684)

Changed

  • security-gate fails the job independently of fail-on-issues. In both integrations the security branch sat inside the fail-on-issues conditional, and fail-on-issues: false made it unreachable.
  • The Action's inline Check threshold step is gone. Its logic moved into the analyze step, and the gates-failed output names the gates that decided the verdict.
  • In combined mode the duplication threshold stands down, and the envelope carries enforced: false for it. Standalone dupes exits 1 as before. The default GitLab job forwards the threshold in combined mode; that pipeline warns and names the reason.
  • --fail-on-stale-baseline moves one wire member, gate_outcomes["stale-baseline"].enforced. Nothing in baseline_staleness depends on the flag, not even gate_trips.
  • health --report-only carries enforced: false on every gate it evaluated.
  • One stale baseline can produce two lines for a pull request. The Action's warning comes from its whole-project re-read. The gate line that fallow report renders describes the scoped run, where the gate stands down.
  • No envelope schema_version moved. gate_outcomes and workspace_diagnostics[].degrades_analysis are additive and optional.

Bug fixes

  • fail-on-regression, threshold, min-severity and the security gate fail the job. All four were documented as gates. Their verdict reached the integrations on stderr, which --quiet removes, or through an exit code that both integrations drop when stdout parses as JSON. The integrations read gate_outcomes instead: a gate fails the build when its status is fail and enforced is true, and only when the input that owns it was set. A flag passed through args: warns and cannot override fail-on-issues: false. (#2680, #2681, #2683, #2685)
  • Every failing gate is reported before the step exits. Both integrations stopped at the first failure, and a run with a tripped gate and findings reported one of the two. They print every reason, write the outputs and artifacts, and exit once. The security gate keeps exit 8, which outranks the generic 1.
  • The duplication threshold reaches the bare command on GitHub. The Action forwarded it on command: dupes only.

Upgrade notes

  • If you set fail-on-regression, threshold, min-severity or a security gate and relied on the job passing, expect failures. With security-gate and fail-on-issues: false, unset security-gate to keep the old behaviour.
  • Remove --fail-on-stale-baseline from args / FALLOW_ARGS, delete any separate unscoped gate step added as a workaround, and set the fail-on-stale-baseline input.
  • fail-on-stale-baseline with no baseline set, or on fix or security, exits 2.
  • Do not point baseline and save-baseline at the same file. The run saves before it compares, and such a baseline can never have a stale entry; the integrations warn about it.
  • If a workflow references the Check threshold step by name (continue-on-error, steps.*.outcome), point it at the analyze step and the gates-failed output.
  • With a pinned fallow older than 3.27.0, the integrations use the fields that version publishes. Gates it has no field for pass, with one warning.
  • TypeScript consumers of npm/fallow/types: HealthBaselineStaleness is now BaselineStaleness. The old name remains as a deprecated alias.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/compare/v3.26.0...v3.27.0

v3.26.0: stale-baseline gate, built-in exclusion diagnostics, rule overrides everywhere

Features

  • --fail-on-stale-baseline turns a rotting baseline into a failing build. The new global flag exits 1 when a loaded --baseline has any entry that matched nothing this run, on dead-code / check, the bare run, dupes and health, in every output format. A run that cannot judge the baseline (a narrowed scope, health --report-only, audit, decision-surface) stands down and says so on stderr. JSON output is unchanged. (#2637)
  • dead-code --baseline warns when the saved baseline has gone stale, in the same wording health --baseline has used since 3.12.0: when a quarter or more of the entries match no current issue, the run says so and points at the re-save command. Exit codes are untouched. Thanks @​cloud-walker for the report. (#2627)
  • A run can say which built-in ignore pattern removed source files. The walk attributes every excluded candidate to the pattern that removed it and records one excluded-by-default-ignore entry per pattern in workspace_diagnostics[] with the glob, an exact file count, the matched-directory count and a project-relative anchor. --explain-skipped prints the breakdown on check, dead-code, audit and the default run; without the flag, only a run that discovered no source files at all prints a two-fact warning pointing at the flag. (#2638)
  • Oxfmt is a built-in plugin. oxfmt.config.ts and its siblings are marked always-used and static imports from those configs are credited. Thanks @​uzosrc for the request. (#2614)
  • Expo Router's SuspenseFallback, getNavOptions and generateMetadata route exports are recognized. Thanks @​tilgovi for the SuspenseFallback patch (#2618).

Changed

  • The built-in build exclusion now matches at any depth (**/build/**), consistent with the dist and coverage defaults, so nested build output in monorepos no longer produces unused-file, unused-export, duplication and health findings. Five consequences are stated plainly in the changelog together with the remedy for each, including that hand-written source in a nested build/ directory is now skipped. Thanks @​michalius for the report. (#2622)

body:
Bumps [expo-audio](https://github.com/expo/expo/tree/HEAD/packages/expo-audio) from 57.0.3 to 57.0.5.
Changelog

Sourced from expo-audio's changelog.

Changelog

Unpublished

🛠 Breaking changes

🎉 New features

🐛 Bug fixes

💡 Others

58.0.1 — 2026-09-21

This version does not introduce any user-facing changes.

58.0.0 — 2026-09-10

🛠 Breaking changes

  • Paused time is now excluded from the AudioRecorder duration limit. (#49239 by @​stvrmrz and @​behenate)
  • [Android] Aligned the default audio focus request on Android 7.0–7.1 with newer versions by using transient exclusive focus when no interruption mode has been configured. (#49101 by @​behenate)

🎉 New features

  • [Android] Added support for keepAudioSessionActive. (#49108 by @​behenate)
  • Added the doNotMixPersistent interruption mode. (#49101 by @​behenate)
  • Added fileName option to RecordingOptions to allow specifying the recording file basename on Android and iOS. (#47265 by @​silwalprabin)
  • Support lockscreen controls with playlists. (#46020 by @​alanjhughes)
  • Added a fileSize field to RecorderState reporting the current size of the recording file in bytes. (#46808 by @​behenate)
  • Added startFileRecordingAsync and stopFileRecordingAsync methods to AudioStream for continuous WAV and PCM file recording alongside buffer streaming. (#46771 by @​behenate)
  • [iOS] Added allowsExternalPlayback option to AudioPlayerOptions. Set to false to keep the local player in control during AirPlay, fixing player.loop not firing. (#48366 by @​zoontek)

🐛 Bug fixes

  • Preserve recorder duration limits across pauses, consistently exclude paused time on Android, iOS, and Web. (#49239 by @​stvrmrz and @​behenate)
  • [Android] Pause audio players and playlists when headphones or Bluetooth audio devices disconnect. (#48151 by @​vivekjm)
  • [Android] Give the lock-screen MediaSession instances a unique ID so concurrent active players (and the basic session) no longer collide on the empty default. (#47101 by @​tsushanth)
  • [Android] Fix stale lock screen artwork when updating metadata without an artworkUrl. (#45738 by @​behenate)
  • [Android] Don't start playback when the system denies audio focus, and log a warning explaining that background playback needs an active media playback foreground service. (#46957 by @​alanjhughes)
  • [iOS] Create a fresh recording file each time prepareToRecordAsync is called, matching Android — repeated takes no longer overwrite the previous recording at the same URL. (#48002 by @​idoyana)
  • Fix player.replace(null) throwing due to a mismatch between native and TypeScript types. (#48219 by @​zoontek)
  • [iOS] Activate the audio session once and keep it active instead of toggling. (#48588 by @​alanjhughes)
  • [Android] Fix createAudioPlayer/useAudioPlayer throwing "Received 5 arguments, but 4 was expected" due to the native AudioPlayer constructor missing the iOS-only allowsExternalPlayback parameter. (#48655 by @​RasmusKard)
  • [iOS] Report denied instead of crashing the app when NSMicrophoneUsageDescription is missing. (#48840 by @​ahmadaccino)
  • [iOS] Resolve permission requests with denied and reject recording calls instead of letting the OS terminate the app when NSMicrophoneUsageDescription is missing. (#49162 by @​alanjhughes)

💡 Others

  • [Android] Removed outdated ExoPlayer changelog references and aligned Android media dependencies with AndroidX Media3 (1.9.1). (#45368 by @​saisreelasyaappali)

body: ## What and why - `ec52066c chore: release` wrote `packages/oauth/package.json` and `packages/oauth/CHANGELOG.md` back. That package was folded into `e2e/oauth` and retired; nothing else under `packages/oauth` exists and the lockfile has no importer for it. - On `main` today: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails (`importers["packages/oauth"]` missing), `pnpm -r run typecheck` fails in `packages/oauth`, and `check:dead-code` reports its seven declared dependencies as unused. Every fresh clone and every CI job hits the first one. - This removes the two files. The lockfile is untouched and a frozen install passes. - Found while rebasing the open PRs onto `main`. ## Checklist - [ ] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: feat(report): the folded test list is one table, a row per file above its tests
body:
## What and why - The folded `All N tests in M files` list on the markdown page rendered as a bold file heading with a bullet per test. On tester-army/app's 83-test regression comment that is 18 headings and 83 bullets of prose, not a grid a reader can scan by column. - It is now one table: a row per file with the worst glyph, its counts, and its time, then a row per test under it, worst file first. Flaky rows note `(1 failed attempt first)`; skipped rows carry the reason and an empty time cell. - The agent column is per run: present when any test ran an agent step, absent otherwise. A deterministic suite gets three columns instead of a blank column down every row, which is what the old always-visible table used to show. - The GitHub comment, the job summary, and `summary.md` all render from this one page (`packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts`, `allTests`). - Docs example in `docs/github.mdx` and the skill reference `skills/e2e/references/running.md` describe the table; changeset bumps `e2e` minor. ## Before, as GitHub renders it

title: fix(agent): read vocabulary from the built-in agent only
body: ## What and why - #394 let config resolution read `executor.context` from any `StepExecutor`, so a custom executor that keeps a `context` member of its own, a promise, a store, anything, had it treated as the agent's vocabulary: a string silently changed every prompt, a non-string was rejected as bad config. Devin flagged it on #394 after the merge. - The executor contract has no `context` field any more. The vocabulary comes from `createAgent`'s options alone, recognized through the brand `createAgent` stamps on its executors. The brand moves to `agent-brand.ts` so `config/agent.ts` can import it without the cycle `default-agent -> tool-loop -> config/agent -> default-agent` that the dead-code check refuses. - Tests: a custom executor with a string `context` and one with a promise both resolve to no vocabulary; the rest of #394's coverage is unchanged. `sdk-types.ts` drops the assertion on the removed field. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`. ---

title: fix(locator): a pause the deadline cuts ends pressSequentially, even when the timer fires early
body:
## What and why

- `pressSequentially` capped each pause to the remaining budget, slept, then read the clock to decide whether to stop. A timer that fires a hair early leaves the deadline unexpired by under a millisecond, and the next character goes out past the timeout. CI caught it as the unit test's promise resolving instead of rejecting: one matrix leg on `main` (4c934142), on #395, on #400, and on the first commit of this PR, with the other legs green.
- The cut now ends the typing by itself: when the remaining budget is shorter than the delay, the loop sleeps the remainder and stops, with no clock read in between. The end-of-budget check before each character stays for the case where the deadline passes during the keystroke itself.
- The test's wall-clock bound widens from 600 ms to the 1000 ms pause, since returning before the pause could elapse is the property; the typed-character log is the proof. Changeset `patch`: a character could be typed past the timeout.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/playwright`, and `@e2edev/agent-device`.

title: feat(mobile): a device lease carries agent-device client configuration
body: A `DeviceLease` can now carry `client`: agent-device client configuration the worker's client is created with, next to the `daemon` address, which becomes optional. - agent-device ships its own device-cloud runtimes (Limrun, BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm). Their daemon resolves a hosted device from the lease scope on each command: `tenant`, `runId`, `leaseId`, `leaseBackend`, `leaseProvider`, as `leases.allocate` returned it. A command without that scope falls back to the local inventory, and on a Mac with a booted simulator the test silently runs there while the hosted instance sits idle. - The engine's client only knew a session name and a daemon URL, so a provider on one of those runtimes had to put a proxy in front of the daemon that stamped the scope onto every request. Now it returns what `leases.allocate` gave it. - `client.stateDir` reaches a daemon the provider started for the run, so such a provider needs no `daemon` address at all. A lease names `daemon`, `client`, or both. - `client` is JSON data, since it travels to the worker through the environment under the existing 16 KiB cap. `session`, `daemonBaseUrl`, and `daemonAuthToken` stay with the engine and `daemon`; a lease setting them is refused at `prepare`. - `DeviceClientConfig` and `DeviceConnection` are exported. The mobile guide gains a second example, a provider on a device cloud through agent-device, typechecked like the first. ```ts const lease = await client.leases.allocate({ tenant, runId, leaseBackend, leaseProvider, platform, target: 'mobile' }); return { id: lease.leaseId, client: { stateDir, tenant: lease.tenantId, runId: lease.runId, leaseId: lease.leaseId, leaseBackend, leaseProvider }, }; ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR P[provider.acquire] -->|lease.client| B[SlotBinding in worker env] B --> F["createAgentDeviceClient({ ...client, session, daemonBaseUrl?, daemonAuthToken? })"] F --> D[daemon] D -->|lease scope on every command| H[hosted device] ``` Refs: `packages/mobile/src/bindings.ts` (`DeviceClientConfig`, `isSlotBinding`), `packages/mobile/src/provider.ts` (`DeviceLease`, `isDeviceLease`), `packages/mobile/src/engine.ts` (the client factory), `docs/examples/mobile/device-cloud-provider.ts`. ---
