- [#669](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/669) [`f5bc45a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f5bc45ac145718ec82396f28339d479c48d66612) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The limits of a persistent browser context fail early and name their cause. `app.clearState()` with `kernel({ scope: 'attempt' })`, any provider with `scope: 'attempt'`, or `connect.reconnectEndpoint` fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` naming that mode, instead of `engine web does not implement it`. A run whose tests consume a session on a target whose engine has no state capability fails with `COLLECTION_ERROR` before any test, instead of failing at `session.save()` after the setup test logged in.

- [#669](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/669) [`f5bc45a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f5bc45ac145718ec82396f28339d479c48d66612) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `browser.waitForDownload` works on a Kernel browser. It failed with `download failed: download.saveAs: canceled` on every hosted browser, which saves a download to its own disk. A `BrowserProvider` can now implement `downloads: { dir, read }`: the engine has the browser save under `dir` on its machine and reads the finished file back through `read`. `kernel()` implements it with Kernel's browser filesystem API. On a provider without it, a failed download names the provider and the missing `downloads`.

- [#669](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/669) [`f5bc45a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f5bc45ac145718ec82396f28339d479c48d66612) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A worker that dies no longer leaks its Kernel browser. With `kernel({ scope: 'attempt' })`, a crashed or killed worker left its attempt's browser running until Kernel's `timeout_seconds`, ten minutes by default; a replacement a worker leased in `worker` scope leaked the same way. A `BrowserProvider` can now implement `sweep(context)`, which the engine calls once per target when the run ends to release the run's leases a worker left open, and `kernel()` deletes every browser still active with the run's `e2e_run` and `e2e_target` tags. The reporter names each browser it released.

- [#670](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/670) [`0073644`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0073644863ef95fa264ee5e0d1ca63d3c86d5da9) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Unknown keys are rejected below the top level of the config too, naming the nearest known key when one is a plausible typo and the known keys otherwise. `app: { url, comand }` on a target is `INVALID_CONFIG` (the run used to go on and fail with `APP_UNREACHABLE`), and so are an unknown `web()` or `mobile()` option, an unknown key inside `connect` or `basicAuth`, and an unknown key in `app.command` (`command: { executable, arg }` dropped the arguments). An unknown test or `describe` option (`{ timout }`) is `COLLECTION_ERROR`, and an unknown query option (`getByRole('link', { nam })`) is `INVALID_LOCATOR` listing the keys the query takes. `e2e/engine` exports `rejectUnknownKeys(label, value, keys)`, the same check for an engine's own options.

- [#664](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/664) [`f67c49a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f67c49a3556616fd55250a017de6673af8d8c0c1) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A terminal Ctrl-C no longer kills a web worker mid-test. Playwright's own SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers are off, so the runner's interrupt ends the running test as `interrupted` with its attempt, runs its `afterEach` hooks, and disposes the browser, instead of the worker exiting 130 with `WORKER_EXIT` and the test reported `skipped`.

- [#669](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/669) [`f5bc45a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f5bc45ac145718ec82396f28339d479c48d66612) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A browser provider's progress lines reach the reporter from a worker too. Kernel's `browser <id>, watch at <live view URL>` line was dropped for every browser in `scope: 'attempt'` and for a replacement after a browser dropped; it now shows, prefixed with the target and worker slot.
## @e2e-dev/github@0.3.0

### Patch Changes

- [#682](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/682) [`e4fca9d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e4fca9debd85cc5be2b2df40357e9e071e92595e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `@e2e-dev/github` installs next to a stable `e2e` again. The published builds pinned their `e2e` peer to one canary build, so `npm install` refused to resolve it against a versioned runner.

title: fix(report): leave unselected results off the page and JUnit, link sources under the project path
body:
Regression seen on tester-army/app#2433: `e2e run tests/regression` posted `1 flaky, 82 passed, 24 skipped`, listing every agent test as `skipped: file not selected by a positional argument` and counting them in the headline. The failure's source link pointed at `blob/<sha>/tests/regression/settings.e2e.ts`, which 404s, and its evidence link landed on the bare run page with nothing to say which file to open.

- Since #332 a test in a file no positional named is a `filtered` pair, and the scheduler reports it as a `skipped` result with `selected: false`. The list reporter drops those, the rewritten markdown page (#413) and JUnit did not.
- Each result in `report.json` now carries `selected`, the flag the summary's `selected` count already used. The page and JUnit render only selected results and read a document without the flag as all selected. The schema and its fixture gain the field.
- `@e2edev/github` prefixes source links with the project's path inside `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so a suite in `packages/e2e-tests` links to `blob/<sha>/packages/e2e-tests/tests/...`. A project at the checkout root, or outside it, is unchanged.
- Evidence links end in `#artifacts` and are followed by each file's path inside the upload; the failure page names the path beside the kind. The docs explain the upload step the links rely on.
- `toBeHidden` observed `default states`, the node's state list; it now says `visible`.

```markdown
[tests/settings.e2e.ts:53](…/blob/<sha>/packages/e2e-tests/tests/settings.e2e.ts#L53) · Evidence: [screenshot, trace, log](…/actions/runs/123#artifacts): `web/tests_settings.e2e.ts__custom_env/attempt-0/screenshot-7.png`, `web/tests_settings.e2e.ts__custom_env/attempt-0/trace.zip`
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[pair: filtered] --> B[result: skipped, selected=false]
  B --> C[report.json keeps it]
  B -- before --> D[page + JUnit: skipped row]
  B -- now --> E[page + JUnit: left out, as list]
```

title: fix(run): long test ids get distinct artifact directories, sources resolve only under the project root
body:
Found in review of the artifact paths. `test.id` is `file::describe::title`, and `sanitizePathSegment` cut it at 120 characters with nothing to tell two long ids apart, so a monorepo path plus a describe plus a long title landed two tests in one `attempt-0/` directory. `mkdirSync({ recursive: true })` hid the collision, both wrote `failure.png` and `screenshot-N.png`, and the report's `path` and `sha256` pointed at the other test's evidence.

- `sanitizePathSegment` (`packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:158`) keeps the 120-character cap and, when it cuts, ends the segment in the first 8 hex characters of the sha256 of the whole original id, the way `failurePageName` already keys on the result id. A value within the cap is byte-identical to before, so cache keys and existing reports keep their shape.
- The digest covers the original id, not its sanitized form, so two long ids that only differ in a character the sanitizer folds (`a b` and `a_b`) get distinct directories too.
- Every attempt directory goes through this one function (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:744`, `packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts:188`), and the report path is `path.posix.join(...segments, file)` from the same segments, so the report, an `ArtifactStore`, and `@e2edev/github` (which reads report paths) agree without a second copy of the rule.
- `relativeSource` (`packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:369`) stripped the project root with `startsWith(projectRoot)`, so `/repo/app-shared/helpers.ts` under `/repo/app` became `-shared/helpers.ts`, a path neither rejected as absolute nor real. `userFrame` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/source.ts` tested `${projectRoot}${path.sep}` instead, which for a root of `/` or one ending in a separator builds `//` and matches no frame at all.
- Both now go through one `projectRelativePath` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/source.ts`): `path.relative(projectRoot, file)`, accepted only when it is not empty, not `..` or `..`-prefixed, and not absolute (another drive), then POSIX separators. A test source outside the root falls back to the test file as before; a step or error outside it names no line, as before.

Two ids that share their first 120 characters, before and after:

```text
before  apps_storefront_tests_checkouts.e2e.ts__checkout__a_returning_customer_with_a_saved_card_and_an_expired_coupon_on_file__
before  apps_storefront_tests_checkouts.e2e.ts__checkout__a_returning_customer_with_a_saved_card_and_an_expired_coupon_on_file__
after   apps_storefront_tests_checkouts.e2e.ts__checkout__a_returning_customer_with_a_saved_card_and_an_expired_coupon_-3e5074fa
after   apps_storefront_tests_checkouts.e2e.ts__checkout__a_returning_customer_with_a_saved_card_and_an_expired_coupon_-79c1bc32
```

- An integration test through the built runner and `createFakeEngine({ artifacts: true })` pins the user-visible bug: two failing tests under a describe long enough that their ids share 120 characters get two attempt directories under the target and distinct `path` and `sha256` in the report, each digest matching its file on disk (the fake screenshot now carries the attempt id in its bytes so two attempts can differ). `projectRelativePath` unit cases cover the root itself, a file above the root, a sibling sharing the prefix, and a root at `/` or ending in a separator. The other-drive shape (an absolute `relative`) is not tested: it only arises under `path.win32`, which the function does not use.

title: fix(web): evaluate runs functions with nested named bindings under the tsx loader
fix(web): a nested frameLocator chain resolves each frame inside the one before it
body: `web.frameLocator('#outer').frameLocator('#inner').getByText('Saved')` never resolved. Every poll failed `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` for `#inner` and the test ended in `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, while Playwright's own `page.frameLocator('#outer').frameLocator('#inner')` found the element. `docs/browser.mdx` shows exactly this chain. - `validateFrames` (`packages/web/src/surface.ts:736`) counted every selector from `frameSelectors` against the page. The inner selector lives in the outer frame's document, so its count was 0 and the runner re-resolved until the deadline. The projection in `packages/web/src/locators.ts:262` already walked the chain, so validation and resolution disagreed. - Validation now walks the same chain. The scope starts at the page, each selector is counted inside the current scope, and the scope becomes `scope.frameLocator(selector)` for the next one. A missing inner frame still fails `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` naming that selector, including when the page holds an element the selector matches, which before passed validation and then resolved to nothing. - `packages/web/tests/integration/nested-frames.test.ts` builds a two-level `srcdoc` page. The chain resolves and `tap` reaches the innermost button; `#outer` then `#aside` (an iframe of the page, not of `#outer`) rejects `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` for `#aside`. The runner-level `web-platform.test.ts` gains a `/frame-nested` page and a chained `frameLocator` test. - The testbed's `/frames` page has one frame level, so no case was added there. The docs already describe the chain and stay unchanged. - Follow-up: `nested-frames.test.ts` gains a three-level chain (`#outer` > `#inner` > `#deep`), which is the first depth at which the scope built by the last `scope.frameLocator(...)` is itself counted in, and an ambiguity case: two `.twin` iframes inside `#outer` reject `FRAME_AMBIGUOUS` (`2 frames match .twin`) while the page holds exactly one `.twin`, so the count is proven to happen inside the outer document. Before, for `web.frameLocator('#outer').frameLocator('#inner').getByRole('button')`: ```text FRAME_NOT_FOUND: no frame matches #inner (retried until the deadline) LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND ``` After, the button inside `#inner` is located and tapped. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[page] -- count #outer --> O[frameLocator #outer] O -- count #inner --> I[frameLocator #inner] I --> Q[getByRole button] ``` ---

title: fix(mobile): openApp and the open_app tool refuse a link before the device opens it as a URL
body: `device.openApp` and the agent's `open_app` tool handed the raw `app` string to `client.apps.open({ app })`, and agent-device opens any `scheme:rest` string as a URL. `open_app({ app: 'data:text/html,...' })` from the model, or `device.openApp('file:///...')` from a test, reached the device as a navigation no rule had checked; only `device.openLink` ran the scheme rule. - `surface.openApp` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:431`), the one place the tool and the fixture both reach, runs `assertAppId` (`packages/mobile/src/links.ts:57`) before the client call. A `file:`, `data:`, or `javascript:` link is `POLICY_DENIED` through the check `linkTarget` already used; any other link is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` pointing at `device.openLink`. A bundle id, package, or display name is unchanged. - `openApp` refuses a link instead of routing it: the method documents an app by id, `openLink` is the documented URL path, and `openLink` carries the iOS unbound-open check a link through `openApp` skipped as well. - The link shape mirrors agent-device's own test (`scheme:rest`, no whitespace, `packages/mobile/src/links.ts:22`), so `Notes: Pro` stays a display name. The message never echoes the input: a magic link carries its token in the query. - The `device.openApp` step label goes through `linkLabel` (`packages/mobile/src/device.ts:222`). The harness records a failed step under its label, so a refused link would otherwise have landed in the report with its query. - The `open_app` tool description tells the model the same (`packages/mobile/src/tools.ts:77`); the mobile reference, the mobile guide, the security page, and the package README say what the code does. - Follow-up (8f4c3f8a): `DevicePool.warm` opened the configured `app` with `client.apps.open` in `prepare`, before any attempt's `openApp` ran, so `mobile({ app: 'file:///etc/passwd' })` still reached every device as a URL. The surface constructor now runs `assertConfiguredApp` (`packages/mobile/src/links.ts`): a link-shaped `app` is `INVALID_CONFIG` at `mobile()`, pointing at `device.openLink`, whatever the scheme (config is trusted code, so a mistake, not a policy breach). A lease whose `installedApp` is a link, the other value `warm` opens, fails the lease. Tests pin the config-time refusal with no device command, the link lease, the `open_app` message naming `device.openLink` and its description saying "not a URL", and the `device.openApp` step label dropping a link's query. ```ts await device.openApp('com.apple.Preferences'); // apps.open({ app }) await device.openApp('file:///etc/passwd'); // POLICY_DENIED, no device command await device.openApp('myapp://orders/42'); // INVALID_ARGUMENT, points at openLink await device.openLink('myapp://orders/42'); // the link path, same scheme rule ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[openApp / open_app] --> B{scheme:rest?} B -- no --> C[apps.open] B -- yes --> D{file, data, javascript?} D -- yes --> E[POLICY_DENIED] D -- no --> F[INVALID_ARGUMENT: use openLink] ``` ---

title: fix(mobile): Android password fields read as secure textboxes
fix(report): the AI row names the models that ran, not the configured one
body: Closes #361 Seen on a jev-executor run (#329) against the iOS simulator: `.e2e/report.json` recorded 22 of 23 model calls on `typesafe-ai/jev`, the summary said `gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna`. - `run-started` carries `modelLabel(runAgent.model)` and `judge` from config (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:526`); the list reporter kept that string and reprinted it in the `AI` row beside token and call totals summed from per-step `step.model` records. A custom executor, an agent pinned to another model, or `--agent a,b` made the label wrong or absent while the numbers were right. - The row now comes from the same records as the numbers: `stepsModelTally` maps each step's `provider/model` to its calls (`packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts:274`), `testFinished` folds it into a run tally beside `runUsage` (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:647`), and `modelsText` renders it most calls first, with a count per model only when several answered (`packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts:292`). One model prints as before. The configured label stands in only when no step named one (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:797`). - The header under `RUN` still names the configured model and judge; it is what the run was configured with. A judge that ran shows in the row by its own label and count. - The `--debug` step table already derived its model from the records (`packages/e2e/src/report/debug-steps.ts`); it now shares the label helper. The markdown page names no model and `report.json` carries only per-step records, so neither changes and the report-1 schema is untouched. Before: ```text model gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna AI 66.5k tokens · $0.0030 · 23 model calls · gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna ``` After: ```text model gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna AI 66.5k tokens · $0.0030 · 23 model calls · typesafe-ai/jev (22 calls) · gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna (1 call) ``` - Follow-up: `stepModelLabel` returns undefined for a step whose model record lacks its provider or id, so the tally skips it and the row falls back to the configured label instead of `undefined/undefined` (the cache-tally fixtures carried such records and passed only by reading the next line). Pinned by a serial-group tally case, `tests/unit/debug-steps.test.ts` for the `--debug` table's `via` column, and two runner-level checks with the list reporter on (`model-usage.test.ts`: one scripted model on the row; `named-agents.test.ts`: two agents on two models, each with its call count). ---

title: fix(mcp): locate renders nodes through the secret ledger like observe
body:
A probe against `dist/mcp/catalog.js` after `call type_secret` of a generic secret into a plain textbox printed `textbox "API key" value "sk-live-SUPERSECRET-0000"`. The session's `locate` read the matching nodes straight from `session.read` and rendered `name`, `text`, and `value` raw, hiding a value only for a secure node, while `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` promises the plaintext never reaches the agent. A password fill followed by a show-password toggle leaks the same way, since the web engine projects `value` for every field that is not secure.

- `describeLocate` projects each read node through `projectTree(node, redact)` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts:252`), the projection `observe({ tree: true })` hands an executor, so name, text, and value pass the secret ledger and a secure node carries no value. `describeNode` renders that `ExecutorNode` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/catalog.ts:171`).
- The catalog takes the attempt's redactor, `attempt.agentRuntime.redact` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:182`), the same `SecretLedger.redact` that guards observations, the step record, and the transcript.
- `SessionHost.call` passes every text part a catalog tool returns, or the failure it raised, through that ledger before it leaves the server (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:139`, `packages/e2e/src/mcp/tools.ts:69`). An engine error or a project tool that quotes screen text cannot carry a filled value either. Image parts stay the pixel taint's to withhold.
- The docs said `screenshot` and `tap_at` "leave the catalog" after a fill. The catalog is built once at `open_session`; both stay listed and answer `PIXEL_TAINTED`. `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` and the `tools` description now say that, and both name the point tools as a group (`tap_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, `select_at`), which the catalog already served.
- `SecretLedger.redact` was a literal split and join per form, so it read its own markers again: with `secrets: { apiKey: 'api' }` the `call` boundary turned an already redacted `<secret:apiKey>` into `<secret:<secret:apiKey>Key>`, and within one pass a value that is a substring of another secret's marker (`Key`, or the word `secret`) mangled it the same way. `createRedactor` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts:19`) now cuts the text at the markers of the names it knows and freezes each marker it writes against the forms that follow, so redacting twice is redacting once. Only known names count as markers: a marker-shaped span of app text holding a raw value is still redacted, not skipped.

Before, after `call type_secret {target: "n12", name: "apiKey"}`:

```
1 node matches getByLabel("API key").
Use: screen.getByLabel("API key")
- textbox "API key" value "sk-live-SUPERSECRET-0000"
```

After:

```
1 node matches getByLabel("API key").
Use: screen.getByLabel("API key")
- textbox "API key" value "<secret:apiKey>"
```

title: fix(oauth): an expired sign-in names the login command to run
body:
A returning user whose ChatGPT, SuperGrok, or Copilot login was rejected saw either `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: ... ChatGPT token request failed (401: invalid_grant); sign in again`, with no provider id to type, or, for Copilot, a bare HTTP 401 from the AI SDK. Only the missing-login case (`NOT_LOGGED_IN`) named the command.

- `createOAuthFetch` owns the remedy for every case now. When `provider.refresh` throws `LOGIN_REQUIRED` and no other process stored a rotated token, it rethrows with `options.loginHint` appended, the same way `current()` does for `NOT_LOGGED_IN` (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/fetch.ts:106`). Without a hint it falls back to `sign in again`.
- A 401 on a token with nothing to refresh it (Copilot stores the GitHub token with `refresh: ''`) used to be returned to the SDK as is, so `refresh()` was never reached. It is now `LOGIN_REQUIRED` with the response detail and the same hint, and no retry (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/fetch.ts:133`).
- `requestTokens` and the Copilot provider drop their own `; sign in again` suffix, so the message carries one remedy (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/token-endpoint.ts:39`, `packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/github-copilot.ts:100`). `fetch.ts` is the only caller of `provider.refresh`.
- `docs/subscriptions.mdx` says what a rejected token or refresh token does.
- `tests/unit/oauth/login-required.test.ts` runs the ChatGPT and Grok cases end to end: `chatgpt('gpt-5.5')` and `grok('grok-4')` with the login from `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, expiring inside the skew, and a local server standing in for the vendor whose token endpoint answers 401 `invalid_grant`. `generateText` rejects with `LOGIN_REQUIRED` and exactly `` ChatGPT token request failed (401: invalid_grant); run `npx e2e login openai` `` / `` SpaceXAI token request failed (401: invalid_grant); run `npx e2e login spacexai` ``, after one refresh POST and no API call. Both fail against main's `fetch.ts` and `token-endpoint.ts`. The ChatGPT refresh test in `openai.test.ts` also pins the provider-level message, `ChatGPT token request failed (400: invalid_grant)`, with no remedy at that layer.
- The tests call the constructors with a model id alone. `useVendor` in `tests/unit/oauth/helpers/server.ts` stubs `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` and global `fetch` (path and query kept, host replaced by the local server); it is byte-identical to the helper #452 adds, so `helpers/server.ts` merges cleanly either way. The Copilot case in `copilot.test.ts` still calls `copilot('gpt-4.1', { store, baseURL: api.url })`; when #452 lands, that call becomes `vendor(api, { 'github-copilot': ... }); copilot('gpt-4.1')`, the shape #452 already gives the other Copilot test.

```text
before: ChatGPT token request failed (401: invalid_grant); sign in again
after:  ChatGPT token request failed (401: invalid_grant); run `npx e2e login openai`

before: (Copilot) HTTP 401 from the AI SDK, no e2e message
after:  GitHub Copilot rejected the stored token (401: Bad credentials); run `npx e2e login github-copilot`
```

title: fix(run): an interrupt reports every unstarted test once, so --last-failed can resume it
body: Two ways a run that stopped early misreported the tests it never ran. - `--max-failures` tripped by a serial group member reported the group's later members twice. `runFileUnit` consulted the interrupt before the serial-unit dedup, so once `runSerialUnit` had reported every member, members 2..n came round again as `unstartedResult`: five tests gave seven results, `report.json` repeated their ids, and `summary.discovered` disagreed with the plan. The dedup now comes first (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:304`). - A plain interrupt (Ctrl-C, or a worker's `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` run abort) dropped every queued unit from the report. `broadcastInterrupt` zeroed the queues and `retire` discarded a starting worker's `queued` unit, so those pairs never reached `results` and `--last-failed` after a Ctrl-C reran only the in-flight file. The broadcast now reports each of them as skipped with `INTERRUPTED_BEFORE_START` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:313`), whose cause `infrastructure-unavailable` is one `readLastFailed` already reads as work to run again (`packages/e2e/src/run/last-run.ts:11`); `retire` has nothing left to drop. - `stopEarly`, `failTarget`, and the broadcast share one `skipQueues` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:253`). The scheduler's rule is now plain: every pair a plan holds leaves through `report` once, an interrupt before dispatch included. - `assertValidReport` in the test helpers refuses a repeated result id, so every integration test that validates a report guards this (`packages/e2e/tests/helpers/report-schema.ts:33`). `buildReport` is left alone: a duplicate there could only throw and lose the report, or dedup and hide the bug. - `docs/reference/cli.mdx` Signals step 1 says the unstarted tests are skipped and land in the report; the `--last-failed` row was already promising that. ```mermaid flowchart LR I[interrupt] --> B[broadcastInterrupt] B --> Q[queued units] B --> S[unit handed to a starting worker] B --> W[busy worker: finishes its unit or is killed after the grace] Q -- before --> D[dropped] S -- before --> D Q -- now --> R["skipped: run interrupted before execution"] S -- now --> R R --> L[report.json, read by --last-failed] ``` Ctrl-C during `tests/first.e2e.ts` with `tests/second.e2e.ts` (two tests) queued behind one worker: | | before | now | | --- | --- | --- | | `summary.discovered` | 1 | 3 | | `second.e2e.ts` in `report.json` | absent | two `skipped`, `infrastructure-unavailable`, `run interrupted before execution` | | `--last-failed` selects | the interrupted test | the interrupted test and both unstarted ones | --- - `onExit` counts no init failure while the run is interrupting: the broadcast retires every worker still starting, and two of them exiting used to reach `MAX_INIT_FAILURES` and record a spurious `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` on a plain Ctrl-C. Scheduler cases pin that (`runErrors` empty, each pair skipped once) and the pre-aborted `plan.immediate` path (a filtered, a skipped, and a queued pair each reported once); an integration case covers the run-abort path: a run-level `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` lists the queued file's tests as `run interrupted before execution` and `--last-failed` runs them next.

title: fix(release): engine and reporter peers on e2e stay >=0.15.0 <1 after a canary, and pnpm check enforces it
body:
`pnpm run canary` runs `changeset version --snapshot canary`, and a prerelease satisfies no `>=x <1` range, so changesets treats the runner as out of range and rewrites each engine's `e2e` peer to the exact snapshot version (906e0b35 turned `>=0.9.0 <1` into `0.15.0-canary-20260914081513`). Every `chore: release` since has committed that pin, and the pending release PR #421 carries it into the first beta as `"e2e": "0.15.0"`. - With an exact pin, every `e2e` release patch-bumps and republishes `@e2edev/web`, `@e2edev/mobile`, and `@e2edev/github` with a new pin, and a consumer who updates `e2e` alone is left with an unmet exact peer that npm 7+ refuses with ERESOLVE. - The three peers read `>=0.15.0 <1` again (`packages/web/package.json:53`, `packages/mobile/package.json:66`, `packages/github/package.json:55`). - The published canary tarballs keep the pin they need: the snapshot step still writes it, and `scripts/restore-peer-ranges.ts` widens it back to `>= ` after `changeset publish`, so `canary:publish` and `version-packages` both leave a wide range in the tree. A peer already in that shape keeps its floor, so a runner minor that left an engine alone does not raise what the engine claims to need. - `scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` runs in `pnpm check` and as its own step in `spec.yml`, and fails on any `e2e` peer that is not `>= `, so a pin cannot land on main unnoticed. - `scripts/public-packages.ts` holds the package discovery and the range shape; `canary-changeset.ts` reads from it too. - AGENTS.md said a narrow or mutual range "forces changesets to bump both packages to a major". Against changesets 3.0.3 an out-of-range peer dependent gets a patch and a rewritten pin, never a major (`determineDependents` in `@changesets/assemble-release-plan` 7.0.0 patches `peerDependencies` like `dependencies`), and pre mode does the same with `>=0.16.0-beta.0 <0.16.0`. Both sentences now describe that, and the canary paragraph describes the restore step and the `chore: release` commit. - pnpm's lockfile records no peers of workspace packages, so the restore touches only the three manifests and `version-packages` needs no extra lockfile step. - #421 is untouched; the bot regenerates it from main once this merges, with the wide range in place of `"e2e": "0.15.0"`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[canary-changeset.ts] --> B["changeset version --snapshot canary
peers: exact canary pin"] B --> C[pnpm run build] C --> D["changeset publish --tag canary
tarballs keep the pin"] D --> E["restore-peer-ranges.ts
peers: >=0.15.0 <1"] E --> F[commit chore: release] F --> G["pnpm check
check-peer-ranges.ts"] ``` ``` $ node scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts packages/web/package.json: e2e peer is "0.15.0-canary-20260922135036", expected >= ; run `node scripts/restore-peer-ranges.ts` ``` ---

title: fix(web): contenteditable hosts are textboxes, icon buttons take their names from alt and aria-label
body:
A TipTap host (`
`) read as a roleless node, named only when it carried an `aria-label` and left out of the tree otherwise: the agent's `type` took the tap-then-keyboard fallback and reported "not an input", a secret fill refused it as not editable, and `toHaveValue` had nothing to read. An icon button read as an anonymous `button` because the name walk collected text nodes only, so `getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' })` resolved through Playwright to a node whose `name` was undefined and `toHaveAccessibleName('Search')` failed on it. - An editing host, `isContentEditable` under a parent that is not (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:290`), is a `textbox` whatever its tag: the check runs ahead of the tag switch, so an `
` is the editor, not an article. The blocks inside it keep no role. Chromium reports `isContentEditable` on any tag carrying the attribute, so `NON_HOST_TAGS` (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:194`) keeps a drawn or embedded surface (`canvas`, `svg`, `iframe`), a void element, and a native control (`a`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`) at its own role: the fixture's canvas map makes its canvas editable to collect keystrokes, and a reader that listed it as a textbox turned the pixel-tool tests' bare point into a listed control. Its trimmed `innerText` is its `value`, cut at the text limit in the tree projection (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:798`), so `toHaveValue`, `inputValue()`, and the agent's screen diff read the document as they read a textarea's text. - `aria-placeholder` names any `textbox` or `searchbox`, editing hosts included (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:585`). A host with no other name takes the `data-placeholder` on itself (Quill) or on its first empty block (ProseMirror, TipTap), `packages/web/src/read-node.ts:598`. - Name from content follows accname 2F the way Playwright's role selector implements it (`contentNameOf`, `packages/web/src/read-node.ts:470`): a descendant contributes its own `aria-labelledby` targets, else its `aria-label`, its `alt` for `` and ``, else its own children, else its `title`; hidden and aria-hidden subtrees still contribute nothing. So `` is `CloseIcon`. Tokens join with a space around block-level children and `
` only, read from computed style for SVG too, so `Go` reads `SearchGo`, the string Playwright matches (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:497`). - `aria-labelledby` is read before `aria-label`, accname 2B before 2C (`packages/web/src/read-node.ts:563`), and a target is read as Playwright reads it (`referencedNamesOf`, `packages/web/src/read-node.ts:441`): a hidden target (`hidden`, `aria-hidden="true"`, or inside a hidden ancestor) counts whole, its own `aria-label` wins over its text, a reference inside a target is not followed, and a `visited` set makes a self-reference, an ancestor reference, or a cycle contribute once. An `` is named by its `alt` on its own too. - Playwright's role selector has no rule for a roleless editing host, and `getByRole` resolves through it (`packages/web/src/locators.ts:69`), so a test reaches an editor by role only when the host carries `role="textbox"`; `getByLabel` and `getByTestId` reach it either way. The screen reference and the skill say so. - Follow-up (e643902c): a referenced target under an `aria-hidden` ancestor is read whole, as its own attribute would make it (`isReferenceHidden`, a local `closest('[aria-hidden="true"]')`, the same rule #445 gives `isHidden`): ` Shipping address ``` Before: ```text "Notes" text="Hello" button image "Search" button "Close" textbox "Address" ``` After: ```text textbox "Notes" value="Hello" text="Hello" textbox "Write something" button "Search" image "Search" button "Close" "Close" textbox "Shipping address" ```

title: fix(types): targets is required, ModelInstance carries doGenerate, referenced types are exported
body: Five places where `dist/index.d.ts` promised what the runner rejects, or named a type a consumer cannot import. Each now says the same thing in the type, the loader, and the docs. - `E2EConfig.targets` is required (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts:1151`). `resolveTargets` throws `INVALID_CONFIG "targets is required"` when it is absent (`packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:596`); the type said `targets?`, so a config without one compiled and failed at load. `tests/types/sdk-types.ts:70` asserts it no longer compiles, and every partial-config assertion there carries a target. - `ModelInstance` carries `doGenerate` (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts:953`), the member `isModelInstance` reads (`packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts:272`). `LanguageModelV2` through `V4` from `@ai-sdk/provider` and the `e2e/oauth/*` constructors assign; three id strings do not. - `RunStatus`, `RunExitCode`, `StepTurn`, `PointHit`, `PointTapResult`, and `ExecutorVerb` are exported from `e2e` (`packages/e2e/src/index.ts:30`, `:40`, `:41`). `FinishedRun.status`, `StepExecutorContext.attachTurns`, `ExecutorActions.tapAt`, `hitTest`, and `target.verbs` named them with no way to import them. - `agent.assert(..., { screenshot })` works under a custom `StepExecutor`. The runner takes that evidence after the verdict, so `ActDispatch.captureEvidence` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts:342`) attaches it to the step on a pass and on a failure, and `screenshot: false` opts out. `vision` stays `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` there (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts:107`): the executor decides what its model sees. `tests/integration/agent-executor-context.test.ts:233` covers the three cases. - Three more cases in that suite, one run. After the executor fills a secret through `typeSecret`, both following asserts record `assert.screenshot denied PIXEL_TAINTED` as a `policy` event and attach no screenshot, the attempt holds no screenshot artifact at all, and the runner's own failure capture keeps the screen text and no pixels either. `vision: true` under the executor is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` at the call: the executor never sees the instruction and no assert step opens; it is a `ConfigurationError`, so that one test makes the run exit 2, which the suite now asserts in place of the earlier exit 1. A failed verdict hands the test body an `AgentError` whose `screenshot` is the path inside the attempt's artifact directory (`screenshots/001-assert.png`); the suite appends it to the message and the test checks the step's screenshot record ends with it, and that `attempt.failure.screenshot` is a second capture of the runner's own. Report-1's `error` has no `screenshot` field, so the report cannot carry it there. - The abandon case in `tests/unit/fixture-runtime.test.ts` runs on fake timers instead of a wall-clock bound: the engine is asked for the screenshot with `timeoutMs: 200` (actionTimeout under a 2 s step clock), the assert is still pending at 199 ms and settled at 200 ms, with no artifact. - `CacheConfig.store` and `ArtifactsConfig.store` no longer describe `undefined` as a value; under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` it is not one. `docs/reference/config.mdx` shows the conditional spread for a key read from `process.env`. Compiled before, errors now: ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; export default { cache: 'read-write' } satisfies E2EConfig; // Property 'targets' is missing in type '{ cache: "read-write"; }' but required in type 'E2EConfig'. ``` ---

title: fix(telemetry): --help and --version record no command session
body: `e2e run --help` showed up in telemetry as a completed `run` session: `e2e_cli_session {command: "run", flags: [], exit_code: 0}`. The `preSubcommand` hook names the session before commander parses the flags (so a rejected flag still counts as a session of that command), and `--help` then throws a `CommanderError` with exit 0, which `endSession(0)` and `flush` treated like any other exit. - `Telemetry.discardSession()` forgets the named command (`packages/e2e/src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:182`); `main` calls it in the exit-0 branch of the `CommanderError` handler, which commander reaches only for `--help`, `help `, and `--version` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:777`). Usage errors keep their `CLI_USAGE` session. - `docs/telemetry.mdx` says the two flags send nothing, also when asked on a command. - The no-session test in `tests/unit/cli.test.ts` also covers `e2e login --help` (a command with its own flags; the old handler recorded it as a `login` session) and bare `e2e --help` (no command named at all). ```text before: e2e run --help -> [telemetry] {"event":"e2e_cli_session","properties":{"command":"run","flags":[],"exit_code":0,...}} after: e2e run --help -> (nothing) ``` ---

title: docs: the migration tables, mobile README, and skill match what ships
body: A read of the docs against `src/` on 2026-09-22 found claims that stopped being true as features landed, and shipped behavior no page names. Every fix below re-reads the cited source; no API changes. - `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` listed `toHaveLength`, `toMatchObject`, `toHaveProperty`, the asymmetric matchers, and `expect.soft` as "not yet"; all ship (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts:778-800` and `856-866`, `packages/e2e/src/expect/soft.ts`), and the value matchers number 17, not 15. `getByRole('img')` is an accepted alias (`types.ts:313`), and `maxFailures` is `--max-failures ` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:471`), which the CLI table further down the same page already said. - `docs/migrate/maestro.mdx` said there is no cross-machine sharding; `--shard ` exists (`cli/index.ts:162`) and `docs/ci.mdx` documents it. - `docs/starting-your-app.mdx` said to import `playwright` from `@e2edev/web`; the export is `web` (`packages/web/src/index.ts:11`). - `docs/telemetry.mdx` named the init engine ids `playwright` and `agent-device`; they are `web` and `mobile` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts:24,55`). - `docs/reference/agent.mdx`: `AgentParam` also admits `Unique`, what `unique()` returns (`types.ts:97-103`); `docs/cache.mdx` already documented the call. - `docs/reference/reporters.mdx`: the event union gains `output`, a test's console write (`packages/e2e/src/run/events.ts:127`), and `judge` on `run-started` (`run/events.ts:84`). - `docs/reference/cli.mdx`: the synopsis lists `models`; a cancelled sign-in exits 130, not 1 (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/cli.ts:168-171`). An unknown provider still exits 2, from commander's `choices`. - `docs/reference/app.mdx`: `screenshot` returns the attempt-relative path (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:476-477`), as engine.mdx and browser.mdx already said; only the report record is artifact-root-relative. - `packages/mobile/README.md`: `mobileTools` is `open_app`, `swipe`, and `alert` (`packages/mobile/src/tools.ts:74-107`), not five tools; `type_secret` fills declared secrets on a device (`packages/e2e/src/agent/secrets.ts:30-57`, no origin check since #290); identifiers are the node's `testId`, and `MobileOptions` has no test id attribute (`packages/mobile/src/options.ts`); the config example gains a `model`, since without one the first agent acquisition is `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`. - `skills/e2e`: the install lines say `@canary` like the quickstart (`@e2edev/web` publishes no `beta` tag); the MCP catalog lists `tap_at` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:353`); the web matchers list `toHaveClass` (`packages/web/src/web.ts:108`). - `packages/e2e/src/types.ts:850`: `expect.any(Object)` matches `null` too (vitest's `Any`), as `docs/reference/expect.mdx:275` says. - Shipped but undocumented, now on the page that owns it: `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` in environment.mdx (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/store.ts:15-29`; it holds the JSON itself, not a path); `secondaryTap` in the device's unsupported lists (`packages/mobile/src/actions.ts:14-27`); `createAgent({ maxTurns })` in agents.mdx and config.mdx (`packages/e2e/src/agent/default-agent.ts:82-83`, clamped to `maxModelCalls` in `tool-loop.ts:226`); `ctx.attachTranscript` and `ctx.attachTurns` in the executors context table (`packages/e2e/src/agent/executor.ts:390,397`); `StoredArtifact` as a type listing in config.mdx (`types.ts:978-996`); `mobileTools` takes at least one engine (`packages/mobile/src/tools.ts:48-50`). - Changeset: `e2e` patch, since the skill and the JSDoc ship in the package. ---

title: chore(ci): every job has a timeout, the weekly upload cannot fail the run, and the package ships its schemas
body: Five CI and packaging gaps, none of them code. - Every job carries `timeout-minutes`; only `benchmark.yml` did. A hung integration suite or testbed held a Blacksmith runner for GitHub's 6-hour default and, in `release.yml` (`cancel-in-progress: false`), blocked the next release behind it. Bounds come from the last 9 to 15 completed runs of each workflow: at least twice the observed maximum, with a 10-minute floor for jobs that install dependencies and a browser, since a warm-cache maximum says nothing about a cold one. | Job | Observed max | `timeout-minutes` | | --- | ---: | ---: | | spec / check | 1.1 min | 15 | | spec / test (22, 24, 26) | 5.5 min | 15 | | release / release | 5.3 min | 20 | | agent / plan | 0.1 min | 5 | | agent / agent, dogfood | 9.5 min | 30 | | docs / build | 0.7 min | 10 | - `.github/workflows/agent.yml` uploads the report with `continue-on-error: true` and `retention-days: 14`, the way `benchmark.yml` already does: a storage quota that refuses the upload must not turn a green suite red, and the run is weekly. - `.github/dependabot.yml` ignores `expo`, `expo-*`, `react`, `react-native`, `react-native-*`, `@react-native/*`, and `@stripe/stripe-react-native`. `packages/mobile-benchmark` pins Expo SDK 57 and `test:mobile-benchmark` never runs in CI, so one of these bumps merges green and breaks the app (#404, #405, #407, #409, #410, all closed). Dependabot's `ignore` is per update entry and the root entry covers the whole pnpm workspace, so the rule also holds `packages/web-benchmark`'s `react`; its `react-dom`, `next`, and types still move. - `packages/e2e/package.json` `files` gains `schema/*.schema.json`. `docs/reference/cli.mdx:294` and the `Report` JSDoc (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts:1091`) point at `schema/report-v1.schema.json` in the package, and `pnpm pack` shipped no `schema/`. The five schemas are in the tarball, the fixtures are not. Changeset for `e2e`. - `tests/unit/schema-fixtures.test.ts` pins the packaging: `files` names `schema/*.schema.json`, and that glob evaluated against the package root matches the same set of schemas the file's other cases enumerate, nothing under `fixtures/`. Drop the entry and it fails. The changeset no longer lists schema names, so #454 retiring `agent-tool-v1` leaves it true. - `scripts/check-error-codes.ts` scans `packages/mobile/src` and `packages/github/src` too, as its header already claimed. Every code they raise (`INVALID_CONFIG`, `POLICY_DENIED`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`) was on the errors page. ---

title: fix(cache): a replayed typed value is the flow's data, not a run-time gap
body: On an app that keeps state between runs, a cached `act` that typed a value the model composed (a todo "Buy milk", a note title) replayed whole once and never again: run 2 re-staged the step with a `type (run-time value)` gap where the `type` was, and every run after handed off to the model at that point. - Replay drives `host.actions.type(t, action.value)` through the same `runActionNow` as a live action (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts:368`), which asks `isDerivedValue` whether the value was read off the screen. The start-path probe had already published the first screen into the feed's shown texts (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-feed.ts:137`), and that screen showed run 1's value. - `StepAccounting` already tracked the span in which actions come from the recording (`replaying(active)`, used to stamp operations with the test origin). It exposes that span as a `replayingTrace` getter (`packages/e2e/src/agent/step-accounting.ts:218`), and the dispatcher skips the derived-value check inside it (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts:397`). `derived.ts` says a value the recording holds is the flow's data; the dispatcher now agrees. - A live `type` of a value the screen shows still records the gap. The negative test runs a fresh project against the same persisted list and reads `tool type (run-time value)` back from the entry, then a `gap` miss on the next run. - The fixture app gains `/todos`, a list the server keeps for the life of the fixture, so a run's first screen shows the last run's data the way an app with a database does. - `docs/cache.mdx`: typed values replay as recorded even when an earlier run left the same value on screen. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before A1[run 1: records type + tap] --> B1[run 2: replays, re-stages tool gap + tap] B1 --> C1[run 3: gap miss, model types the visible value, gap again] end subgraph after A2[run 1: records type + tap] --> B2[run 2: replays, re-stages type + tap] B2 --> C2[run 3: replays the same trace] end ``` ---

title: fix(expect): a negation that begins late in the budget passes, and a failure says how long it held
body:
`not.toBeVisible()` on a toast that goes away 4.5 s into the default 5 s budget failed with `observed: no node`, and `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 800 })` on a node gone at 200 ms failed at 800 ms the same way. Expected and observed agreed, and the message never said what was missing.

- `pollCondition` passed a negation only once it had held for `min(1000 ms, budget)`, and only inside the budget. A negation that began late hit the deadline first; under 1000 ms the window was the whole budget, so the node had to be gone at the first poll.
- The deadline now bounds when the negation must begin. Once it holds at the deadline, the poll runs on for what is left of the window and never past `timeout + window` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts:100`). A sample that breaks the hold after the deadline fails at once, and so does a sample that completes the hold after the cap: a slow read landing at 1700 ms cannot pass a 900 ms timeout with a 450 ms window, however long the negation held by then.
- The window is `min(1000 ms, budget / 2)` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts:61`), so a short `{ timeout }` keeps half of itself for the negation to begin. A one-poll flicker still fails.
- `evaluate` receives the deadline in force (`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:108`). Without it every sample past the deadline ran its engine reads on `timeoutMs: 1`, since `operationWithin` clamps an expired deadline to 1 ms.
- `onTimeout` receives `{ negation?: { heldMs, windowMs } }`, and `describeNegationTimeout` turns it into the last message line (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts:130`). The locator matchers (`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:114`) and `expect(web)` (`packages/web/src/web.ts:535`) both append it. The line has two forms: a hold shorter than the window reads `short of the window`; a hold at least the window long, which can only fail when the sample confirming it landed past the cap, reads `confirmed only after the window closed`.
- `e2e/engine` gains `describeNegationTimeout`, `PollTimeout`, and `NegationTimeout`; the two callbacks on `PollConditionOptions` gain a parameter, which an engine that ignores it still satisfies (`docs/reference/engine.mdx:871`).
- `docs/reference/expect.mdx:44` states the rule in one sentence, and "passes once nothing matches" now reads "for the negation window". Changeset for `e2e` and `@e2edev/web`.
- Tests: `pollCondition` under fake timers (window finishing past the deadline, halved window, hold broken after the deadline, late start with the held state, a hold completed by a sample past the cap), the matchers over a screen that changes mid-poll (`createScreenFixture(() => nodes)`), and a browser case in `web-platform.test.ts` that removes a node and renames the title 1 s into a 1.5 s budget for both `expect(locator)` and `expect(web)`.
- Follow-up (c69b40d7), runner-level in `web-platform.test.ts`: `not.toHaveURL('/')` after a `pushState` at 700 ms and `not.toHaveClass` after a class swap at 700 ms both pass with `{ timeout: 1500 }` (window 750 ms, finishing past the deadline). A `not.toHaveTitle` and a `not.toBeVisible` whose change lands at 1400 ms with `{ timeout: 1000 }` fail at the first sample past the deadline, and their messages carry no window line. The `held for ...` line cannot be produced deterministically through the web engine: every read is one shot (`resolveForRead`, `resolveOnce`), so no sample straddles the deadline with the negation newly holding; the unit test with a 200 ms read is where that line is pinned. Side finding fixed: `class assertions report the observed class on failure` swallowed its own error and was asserted by nothing; it now fails as written and an `it` reads `observed: class "card active"` from the attempt error.

```text
default budget 5000 ms, window 1000 ms, node gone at 4500 ms

        0                     4500      5000      5500      6000
        |---------------------|---------|---------|---------|
before                        gone      FAIL: observed: no node
after                         gone      deadline  PASS      cap = timeout + window

{ timeout: 800 }, node gone at 200 ms

        0         200       600       800
        |---------|---------|---------|
before  window 800 (the whole budget)  FAIL at 800
after   window 400           PASS at 600
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[sample] --> H{negation holds?}
  H -- no --> D1{past deadline?}
  D1 -- yes --> F[fail]
  D1 -- no --> W[wait 100 ms] --> S
  H -- yes --> C{held for the window, by the cap?}
  C -- yes --> P[pass]
  C -- no --> D2{past the cap?}
  D2 -- yes --> F2[fail, message says held vs window]
  D2 -- no --> W
```

Before, a node gone late in the budget:

```text
expect.not.toBeAttached failed
locator: getByRole("status")
expected: not attached
observed: no node (match count 0)
```

After, the same node passes. The line below shows on the cases that still fail while the negation holds. A negation that first held after the deadline (900 ms budget, 200 ms engine reads, node gone at 1000 ms):

```text
expect.not.toBeAttached failed
locator: getByRole("status")
expected: not attached
observed: no node (match count 0)
held for 304 ms, short of the 450 ms negation window
```

The same budget when the read that would have completed the hold lands past the 1350 ms cap:

```text
held for 600 ms, confirmed only after the 450 ms negation window closed
```

title: fix(agent): pixel-mode tool results feed the failure guard and screen elision
fix(mobile): a cut snapshot says so, a rejected lease is still released, screen scrolls settle
body: Three defects in what the mobile engine owes the contract and a device provider: a cut tree shipped as complete, a lease the engine refused was never released, and the screen scroll skipped the settle wait every other agent action gets. - `observe` never set `EngineSnapshot.truncated`. `RawSnapshot` dropped agent-device's `CaptureSnapshotResult.truncated`, and a tree still sparse after the three device-side retries went out unflagged. Core relies on the flag: the screen diff calls a cut screen unchanged without it (`packages/e2e/src/agent/screen-update.ts:133`), and the prompt's incomplete-listing line (`packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:77`) is gated on it. The trace cache is not involved: `truncated` under `packages/e2e/src/cache` marks a trace that overflowed the recorder's bounds, a different flag; the changeset said otherwise and is corrected. `isTruncated` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:114`) flags both cases; a whole tree carries no flag, the web engine's shape (`packages/web/src/observation-capture.ts:68`). - `isDeviceLease` threw before `held.push`, so a provider that allocated a device and returned `{ id }` without `daemon` or `client`, or with a reserved client key, kept the device billed: `finish` releases only `held`. `bind` now holds anything with a string `id` before the field check (`packages/mobile/src/provider.ts:184`), so `finish` hands the provider its own object back; the check still fails the run. An object without an `id` has nothing to release. - The root swipe (`interactions.scroll`) carried no settle for `origin: 'agent'`, while press, fill, longPress, and back all settled. It spreads the same settle options (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:746`). Node swipes and `swipeTo` go through `interactions.swipe`, whose `SwipeOptions` (agent-device `client-types.d.ts:458`) carry no `SettleCommandOptions`, so they are unchanged. - The root scroll keeps agent-device's default `amount` (about 0.6 of the axis) for every momentum and every origin, as on main, so `momentum` stays dropped there. An earlier revision of this branch sent `none` 0.5, `slow` 0.75, `fast` 0.8. agent-device centres the gesture on the viewport, so the finger starts at `0.5 + amount / 2` of the height: 0.8 at the default, 0.875 for `slow`, 0.9 for `fast`. A live iOS run of the mobile benchmark on that revision failed `sticky chrome: accept below the fold, then continue` (`packages/mobile-benchmark/tests/flows.e2e.ts:105`). `screen.scrollUntilVisible` sends root `slow` swipes, the finger started inside the absolutely positioned sticky footer (its top sits at about 0.87 of the viewport once the error line shows), the footer swallowed the drag, and the target never became visible in 30 s; main passes the step in 2.4 s. The one measured upside of the longer scroll, the virtualized-list scenario in 10 agent calls instead of 15, is given up for it. - The swipe on a node keeps its own table, `swipeWithin` (`packages/mobile/src/support.ts:60`): `none` 0.5, `slow` 0.25, `fast` 0.8 of the box, as on main. It is a gesture inside one control, and the mobile benchmark's `openScenario` fixture (`packages/mobile-benchmark/tests/fixtures.ts:27`) steps the scenario list with `slow` drags of a quarter of the list, shorter than any row, so no row is dragged past between stops. A revision that routed it through a shared three-quarter table failed `sticky chrome` and `web view coupon form` on the same simulator: the drags jumped past a deep row and the fixture's `expect.poll` timed out at 60 s. - Left alone: agent-device's per-node `hiddenContentAbove` / `hiddenContentBelow` (`sdk-contracts.d.ts:267`) mark a scroll container with content clipped off-screen. `SemanticNode` has no per-node slot, and folding them into `truncated` would flag every scrollable screen and stop the harness from ever calling one unchanged. - Follow-up: `provider.test.ts` covers one `prepare` with a good lease on slot 0 and `{ id: 'bad' }` on slot 1: the run fails, no device is booted or closed, and `finish` releases both, the bad one by identity. An interaction test with #443's snapshot retake (a presentation failure on odd `capture.snapshot` calls, a sparse tree on even ones, resolving `truncated: true` after six calls) needs that branch's `capture()` and is left for the branch that carries both. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[provider.acquire] --> B{string id?} B -- no --> X[fail the run] B -- yes --> C[held for finish] C --> D{daemon or client, JSON only?} D -- no --> X D -- yes --> E[worker binding] C --> F[finish: provider.release] ``` ---

title: fix(run): a session save failure fails the setup, a corrupt envelope is SESSION_INVALID, stale session dirs are swept
body:
A setup test whose `session.save()` the runner could not persist took its worker down. Seen with an engine whose `capture` returned a past `expiresAt`: the setup read `failed (WORKER_CRASH)`, the run listed `test/SESSION_EXPIRED` and `infrastructure/WORKER_EXIT` as run errors and exited 3, while `reference/errors.mdx` had `SESSION_EXPIRED` as a test failure at exit 1.

- The save loop ran in `runSetupUnit` after the attempt had returned, inside `runWithRetries` with no catch, so `SESSION_EXPIRED`, or an `ENOSPC`/`EACCES` on `.e2e/sessions`, reached `TargetWorker.runUnit` and `host.fatal`. The session contract check and the saves now run inside the attempt (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:1029`, `execute.ts:492`), after the teardowns and before the verdict: a save the store refuses fails the attempt at phase `body`, dependents skip as `setup-failed`, the worker lives, the run exits 1.
- Because the verdict is final before `closeSession` reads it (`execute.ts:623`), a setup that failed this way keeps its `retain: 'on-failure'` video; a status flipped after the close would find the recording already deleted.
- A `realms.create` that throws on a retry or a later setup (`execute.ts:365`, `execute.ts:454`) is recorded as a failed attempt at phase `collection` (`execute.ts:512`), the treatment `runSerialAttempt` already gave it (`packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts:216`), instead of ending the worker.
- `parseEnvelope` (`packages/e2e/src/run/sessions.ts:290`) checked only that `state` and `engine` were objects. A missing, empty, or non-string `iv`, `tag`, or `ciphertext` threw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`, `ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_IV`, or `ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_AUTH_TAG` outside the `try`, and `classifyError` turned a corrupt session into a test-category `ERROR`. The three fields are checked as non-empty strings (`sessions.ts:312`), and `createDecipheriv` and `setAuthTag` sit inside the `SESSION_INVALID` try (`sessions.ts:259`). No error message carries plaintext.
- A third Ctrl-C (`packages/e2e/src/cli/signals.ts:40`), a runner crash, or `SIGKILL` skipped `cleanup()` and left `.e2e/sessions/<runId>` behind with its memory-only key gone; nothing removed it. `SessionStore.create` (`sessions.ts:101`) now claims the run's directory with an `owner.json` naming the runner's pid (`sessions.ts:130`) and sweeps siblings (`sessions.ts:329`) that are both older than `MAX_SESSION_AGE_MS`, the 24 hours a session may live, and whose pid is gone (`sessions.ts:348`; `EPERM` counts as alive). A run still going after a day keeps its sessions, where an mtime-only sweep would have taken them and failed its later restores with `SESSION_UNAVAILABLE`. Sessions never leave the machine, so pid liveness is the portable check. The sweep skips the current run's directory, never follows a symlink, and swallows every error.
- `reference/errors.mdx` names the setup outcome under `SESSION_EXPIRED` and the malformed envelope under `SESSION_INVALID`; `security.mdx` and `authentication.mdx` describe the owner file, the sweep, and the save failure.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[setup body and afterEach passed] --> B[persistSessions: contract check, sessionStore.save]
  B -- ok --> C[verdict passed, dependents run]
  B -- throws --> D[verdict failed at phase body]
  C --> E[closeSession reads the verdict]
  D --> E
  E -- passed --> F[on-failure video deleted]
  E -- failed --> G[video kept, dependents skip setup-failed, exit 1]
```

`e2e run` on a project whose engine captures already expired state, before:

```text
 ❯ |demo| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 failed)
   × sign in 0ms
     → worker process exited during this test
 ↓ |demo| tests/dashboard.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 skipped)
 ✓ |demo| tests/public.e2e.ts (1 test) 1ms

 FAIL  |demo| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts > sign in
WORKER_CRASH: worker process exited during this test

 ERROR  test error SESSION_EXPIRED
state expiry is at or before creation

 ERROR  infrastructure error WORKER_EXIT
worker for target "demo" exited unexpectedly (code null, signal SIGKILL) during setup::demo::setup::tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts::sign%20in

 Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed | 1 skipped (3)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 1 skipped (3)
     Errors  2 errors
```

Exit code 3. After:

```text
 ❯ |demo| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 failed) 2ms
   × sign in 2ms
     → state expiry is at or before creation
 ↓ |demo| tests/dashboard.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 skipped)
 ✓ |demo| tests/public.e2e.ts (1 test) 1ms

 FAIL  |demo| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts > sign in
SESSION_EXPIRED: state expiry is at or before creation

 Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed | 1 skipped (3)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 1 skipped (3)
```

Exit code 1.

- Integration coverage through the built runner and the fake engine: a test file, and a setup, whose first attempt rewrites the file to a syntax error so the retry's `realms.create` throws (attempt recorded `failed` at phase `collection`, dependents `setup-failed`, exit 1, no `WORKER_CRASH`, the worker disposes its engine); a setup that never saves its declared session (`SESSION_CONTRACT`, phase `body`, dependents `setup-failed`, `retain: on-failure` video kept); and two runs on one project where the second sweeps a day-old `.e2e/sessions/<run>` whose `owner.json` names a dead pid and leaves a fresh sibling. A setup unit holds one pair, so the "later setup" branch of the `runSetupUnit` catch is reached on a retry, which is what the test does.

title: fix(mobile): device timeouts keep their message, a busy or wedged runner names the recovery
body: Seen on the Bluesky iOS suite (#362, #363): a capture that overran the runner's watchdog left the next run reading `APP_UNREACHABLE: agent.act failed: snapshot failed: The iOS runner is still finishing a previous command ...`, after `prepare` had opened the app fine and with the app blamed. A simulator boot that timed out reached the report as `operation timed out`, without the device, the app, or agent-device's hint. - `TIMEOUT_PATTERN` in `packages/mobile/src/errors.ts` re-coded any agent-device failure whose text said "timed out" (`IOS_BOOT_TIMEOUT`, `IOS_RUNNER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, an app launch) as `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`, and `translateEngineError` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts:293`) replaces that code's message with `operation timed out`. The pattern is gone: `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` means the harness budget expired, which `raceAbort` already reports, and a timeout the device itself reports stays `ENGINE_FAILURE` with agent-device's message and hint. - `RUNNER_BUSY` and `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT` reach the client folded under `COMMAND_FAILED` with the wire code in `details.runnerErrorCode`; `RUNNER_WEDGED` is the top-level code; the presentation failure ("requires a valid viewport") is `COMMAND_FAILED` with the failed check in `details.reason`, which is how upstream rethrows `IOS_SNAPSHOT_ENGINE_FAILED`. `translateError` matches all of them (`packages/mobile/src/errors.ts:74`, `:150`) and writes a message naming the runner, the session and device, agent-device's text, and the recovery. - The code stays `ENGINE_FAILURE`, the taxonomy's infrastructure code. Under the agent, core maps every infrastructure code to `APP_UNREACHABLE` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/error.ts:113`), so the message is where the diagnosis has to say the app is fine. - `warm` (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts:208`) rethrows a busy or wedged runner instead of logging "automation runner not warmed up": the first attempt could only meet the same runner and fail its first observation. A fail over a wait of up to the runner's 120 s recycle window, because the message names the fix and a silent wait in `prepare` would hide the wedge upstream wants reported; an app that does not open for any other reason is still logged and left to the first attempt. - A snapshot the runner acquired but could not present is taken once more (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:533`), as a sparse one is; a second failure propagates. `runCommand` and `staleOr` take an optional `where` (session and device) for the messages whose recovery is per device. - Docs: a Troubleshooting section on `docs/mobile.mdx`; the `APP_UNREACHABLE` rows in `docs/reference/errors.mdx`, `docs/debugging.mdx`, and the skill's `debugging.md`; the `device` fixture's error sentence in `docs/reference/mobile.mdx`. - Follow-up: agent-device's presenter rewraps `malformed-graph` as `invalid-presented-payload` (presented tree) and `invalid-quality-payload` (quality tree), and raises the former directly for a parent outside the payload or a disabled or off-viewport node marked actionable (`runner-presentation.js`); neither reason was in `PRESENTATION_REASONS`, so those captures got no retake and no runner message. Both are in the set, with one `errors.test.ts` case per reason agent-device raises or rewraps and a `request_canceled` reason that stays plain. Also pinned: the `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT` first move (`Rerun once it has drained.`), and, through the engine, a node tap (`interactions.press`, the `staleOr(..., where)` path) and the screen scroll (`interactions.scroll`) meeting a busy runner both naming `(session e2e-ios-0 on iPhone 17 Pro)`. The mobile package raises only documented codes; `scripts/check-error-codes.ts` scanning it is #437's. Before: ```text APP_UNREACHABLE: agent.act failed: snapshot failed: The iOS runner is still finishing a previous command that exceeded its execution watchdog (usually an accessibility capture on a heavy or animating screen). ``` After: ```text APP_UNREACHABLE: agent.act failed: snapshot failed: the iOS automation runner is still finishing a command that overran its watchdog (session e2e-ios-0 on iPhone 17 Pro): The iOS runner is still finishing a previous command that exceeded its execution watchdog (usually an accessibility capture on a heavy or animating screen). The app is fine. Wait a few seconds and rerun. If the next run meets it again, stop the daemon (`npx agent-device daemon stop`) and reboot the simulator (`xcrun simctl shutdown `, then `boot`). ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[agent-device failure] --> B{code} B -- RUNNER_BUSY, MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT, RUNNER_WEDGED --> C[ENGINE_FAILURE: runner, session, device, recovery] B -- details.reason invalid-viewport --> D[capture once more] --> C B -- IOS_BOOT_TIMEOUT, anything else --> E[ENGINE_FAILURE with agent-device's text] C -- at warm-up --> F[prepare fails] ``` Refs #362, #363. Upstream owns the wedge (agent-device 0.21.4 stops a draining runner on close); this is the engine's diagnosis. ---

title: fix(run): a reporter that throws on an event is named when it is quarantined
body: A custom reporter whose `onEvent` threw was quarantined for the rest of the run, as `docs/reference/reporters.mdx` promises, with nothing on stderr to say so. The user saw a reporter that stopped receiving events and no reason; an `onRunFinished` failure, by contrast, prints `e2e: reporter "" failed: `. - `createRunEventEmitter` takes `{ name, onEvent }` subscribers instead of bare sinks and writes one line when it quarantines one, for a throw and for a rejected promise alike (`packages/e2e/src/run/events.ts:269`). The runner passes each reporter's name and labels the host's `RunOptions.onEvent` sink `onEvent` (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:318`). - The line follows the `onRunFinished` style and carries the event type and the error message, so the reporter's author knows which handler branch broke. - `reporters.mdx` says the quarantine is announced; the run's outcome is still untouched. ```text before: (nothing; the reporter stops receiving events) after: e2e: reporter "loud" threw on run-started: bang; ignoring it for the rest of the run ``` --- - The integration test now also checks the quarantine is per sink and said once: the `loud` line appears exactly once, a second `onEvent` reporter beside it still receives `run-started`, `test-finished`, and `run-finished`, and a host `runOptions.onEvent` that throws is named `onEvent` in its stderr line.
