title: fix(agent): step labels, the AI trace, and executor screenshots go through the secret ledger
body: `docs/security.mdx` lists `report.json` as `complete`, but three paths kept a registered secret value in the clear when a test or config put it there: a step label, the `--ai-trace` file, and a screenshot an executor attached after a secret fill. Probed against `dist`: a value inside an `act` label survived `projectPriorSteps` and `serializeLedger` verbatim, so it reached the next `act` prompt. - `StepRecorder.run` stores the label through `options.redact`, which it already owned for errors and explanations (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:376`). ``agent.act(`use key ${key}`)``, `app.open('/reset?token=...')`, and `expect(screen.getByText(value))` now reach `report.json`, reporter events, the `--debug` step table, and the AI trace run name as ``. - `projectPriorSteps` takes the attempt's live redactor (`packages/e2e/src/agent/ledger.ts:40`), so the ledger the next `act` reads is redacted even for a value registered after the step was recorded, such as a provider-resolved secret. - `AiTraceRecorder` redacts each step's `input`, `output`, and `error` as it closes them (`packages/e2e/src/internal/ai-trace.ts:436`), with `processSecrets.redact` in both the worker (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts:223`) and the in-process runner (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:666`). The ledger matches the JSON-string form of a value, so a tool-call argument, an assistant message, or a `providerMetadata` leaf is replaced without walking the document, and the devtools shape is unchanged. The file is written with mode `0600` (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:439`), like the cache and sessions. - `attachScreenshot` throws `POLICY_DENIED` once the viewport is pixel-tainted and records the denial as a `policy` event on the step (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts:452`). The built-in path already withheld pixels; a `defineTool` or executor holding pixels from before the fill could still get them into the report and an `ArtifactStore`. - Docs: the security page's denied table, taint paragraph, and artifacts table, the executor context table, `tools.mdx`, the `POLICY_DENIED` row in `reference/errors.mdx`, and the skill's debugging reference. Still as written: the instruction of the step that spells the secret out reaches its own model call. This PR covers the label, the later steps' ledger, and every file the run writes. ```ts // packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts private async attachScreenshot(pixels: ExecutorPixels, label: string): Promise { if (this.runtime.taint.value) { recordPolicyEvent(this.runtime.steps, 'attachScreenshot', 'denied', 'PIXEL_TAINTED'); throw new AgentError('POLICY_DENIED', 'attachScreenshot() is denied after a secret fill because the app may display the secret outside a secure field'); } ... } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR L[step label] --> R[StepRecorder.run: redact once] R --> J[report.json + reporter events] R --> D[--debug table + AI trace run name] R --> P[projectPriorSteps: live redact] --> M[next act prompt] O[model output, tool args, providerMetadata] --> C[AiTraceRecorder.closeStep: redact] --> F[ai-trace.json, mode 0600] ``` ## Follow-up: gaps closed after the audit - `openStandaloneAttempt` builds its `StepRecorder` with the session ledger's redactor (`packages/e2e/src/run/standalone.ts`), so an `e2e mcp` session step spelling a secret out is recorded and announced as ``. `mcp-session-host.test.ts` opens a standalone attempt and an interactive step to check it. - Run-level errors pass the process ledger in `recordRunError`, before the record and the `run-error` event; the worker ships `runErrors` through its own ledger like its results. `outcome.results` passes `redactLeaves` at the seam the report does, the live target kept. `redactLeaves` drops functions and symbols as `JSON.stringify` does, which its doc already said. - Tests: the child-process trace run carries a configured secret, an echoing model, and a serial group whose label spells it (`ai-trace.json`, `report.json`, the serial-group members, and `outcome.results` carry the name); the scripted loop model can emit a text part and `providerMetadata`, and throw, so those trace columns are covered end to end; a `run-events` case checks the `phase: 'start'` label in `onEvent`; a leaky fake engine puts the secret in the failure location and a cleanup error, and `report.json`, the outcome, and the `run-error` event carry the name; the step's own prompt still carries the instruction as written. ---

title: fix(report): the live window clamps titles by terminal column, never inside a code point
body:
The TTY reporters measured text by UTF-16 code unit. A live-window title cut inside an emoji ended in a lone surrogate before the ellipsis (`abc\ud83d\^[[0m…` at 6 columns), which terminals paint as a garbage glyph; CJK and emoji titles were counted one column per code unit, so they wrapped despite the clamp and `rowsOf` undercounted the log above the block, and the `ESC[nA ESC[0J` erase then left stale fragments on every repaint; and the step label, reasoning excerpt, exploration header, and glance line were clipped by code point against a column budget, so a CJK label kept twice the columns it was given and pushed the duration off the row. A piped log changes too, only where it holds wide glyphs: `stepLine` prints permanent lines without a width, so `stepLabel`'s 72 budget now counts columns; the failure glance and the exploration step summary clip against the 80 columns a pipe reports; and the wrapped finding details count columns. A CJK label keeps half the glyphs it did (36, not 72); ASCII output is byte-identical.

- `graphemes(text)` in `packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts` segments with `Intl.Segmenter` and gives each cluster its columns: 2 for any emoji sequence (a ZWJ sequence, a base with VS16, a keycap, a regional indicator pair) and for the East Asian wide and fullwidth blocks and default emoji presentation; 1 with VS15; 0 for marks, format characters, Hangul medial and final jamo, and skin tone modifiers; else the sum of its code points. No new dependency: the wide table is wcwidth's, trimmed to whole blocks, and the zero-width set is `\p{M}` and `\p{Cf}`. `engines.node` is `>=22.12.0`, so the segmenter is always there.
- `visibleWidth` sums it, so `rowsOf` and every existing caller (the rule, the step labels, the explore header) count columns.
- `fitColumns(text, columns)` clips by column, whole clusters, ellipsis inside the budget. It replaces `ellipsize` wherever a width-derived budget applies: `stepLabel` and `reasoningExcerpt` (`packages/e2e/src/report/list-steps.ts`), the exploration goal and step summary (`packages/e2e/src/report/list-explore.ts`), the failure glance (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts`). `ellipsize` stays for markdown cells, which measure characters.
- `clampToWidth` walks clusters between ANSI sequences and drops one whole when it would cross the limit (`packages/e2e/src/report/live-window.ts`), so the painted rows match the rows the next erase removes.

```text
before: abc\ud83d\^[[0m…                (6 columns; malformed, one garbage cell)
after:  abc\^[[0m…                      (6 columns)
before: 日本語テスト -> 1 row, 6 code units        (10 columns; wraps, erase misses a row)
after:  日本語テスト -> 2 rows, 12 columns
before: stepLabel(60 CJK glyphs, 60) -> 120 columns, tail clipped away by the window
after:  stepLabel(60 CJK glyphs, 60) -> 59 columns + …, tail on the row
```

- Pinned: `tests/unit/live-window.test.ts` has caller-level cases for `stepLabel`, the reasoning excerpt through `eventLine`, and the exploration header and step summary with CJK input asserting the column budget, plus combining marks (`e` + U+0301 is 1), Hangul medial and final jamo (0), fullwidth forms (2), and `\p{Cf}` other than the joiner and the variation selectors (0); `tests/unit/report-list.test.ts` clips a CJK glance at 60 columns and clamps a wide-glyph `AI` row in the live window (59 columns on a 60-column terminal, since `WIDTH_MARGIN` leaves one for the ellipsis and one under the exact width; ends in `…`, no lone surrogate, printed whole in the final summary; it reads the header's configured labels until #428's per-step tally lands); `tests/integration/list-reporter.test.ts` runs the built runner with `quiet: false` and an `agent.act` label of 40 CJK glyphs, asserting the permanent step line shows 35 glyphs and an ellipsis at 71 columns.

title: fix(report): markdown cells cannot mention, autolink, or start a block, and all-dot names are rejected
body: A test title, an `Expected` or `Observed` value, the agent's explanation, a turn outcome, and an explore finding carry screen text from the app under test, and `cell()` let `@`, `#`, and URLs through to the `@e2edev/github` comment: `@someone` sent a notification, `https://evil.example/phish` was a clickable link, `#123` linked an issue, and an explore assessment beginning `# ` rendered as a heading. Separately, `.` and `..` passed the target and agent name rules and became artifact path components. - `packages/e2e/src/report/markdown-text.ts:24`: a whitespace-delimited token GitHub would link on its own (`@` before a letter or digit, `#` or `GH-` before a digit, `://`, `www.`) is written as a code span. Entities and backslashes do not do the job: GitHub's mention and issue filters run on the rendered text, so `@octocat`, `\@octocat`, `#1`, and `\#1` all still link (checked through `gh api /markdown -f mode=gfm`). `:` does break the `https://` autolink but not `www.` or an email address, and leaves `https://` in the local `summary.md`; a code span is the one rendering every filter skips, and it reads the same in the local file. - `packages/e2e/src/report/markdown-text.ts:31`: a leading `#`, `-`, `+`, `=`, `_`, or `1.` / `1)` is backslash-escaped, so a cell at line start (the explore assessment, a quoted message or explanation, a turn outcome line) cannot open a heading, a list, a rule, or a setext underline. This holds inside `> ` too, since a blockquote parses blocks. - `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:151`: target and agent names are `/^(?!\.+$)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/`. `..` was legal, and `createAttemptArtifacts` (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:744`) joins both names raw, so a target named `..` wrote beside `report.json` and its report-relative `artifact.path` began with `../`, which report-1's `relativePath` pattern rejects. The `INVALID_CONFIG` message names the rule. - `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:158`: `sanitizePathSegment` maps an all-dot value to `_`, a backstop for every other caller. One added line, so it rebases over #423's digest change. - `docs/reference/config.mdx` states the name rule for targets and agents; `docs/github.mdx` says what the comment does with app text GitHub would link. One hostile title, as the page writes it: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `ping @octocat, see #123, open https://evil.example/phish` | ``ping `@octocat,` see `#123,` open `https://evil.example/phish` `` | Rendered on GitHub, the first notifies octocat, links issue 123, and makes the URL clickable; the second is three code spans and no link. `http://127.0.0.1:3000` in an `APP_UNREACHABLE` line is the visible change on an ordinary page: it is now code. Still links: a full commit SHA and a repository's custom autolinks. Both point inside the repository, so they are left alone. - Follow-up tests: `packages/github/tests/unit/reporter.test.ts` posts a result titled `ping @octocat see https://evil.example #12` and reads the mention, the URL, and the issue ref back as code spans from `postedBody` (the package imports `renderMarkdownReport` from the built `e2e`, so this is a dist-level check); `tests/integration/report-markdown.test.ts` runs the built runner with `reporters: ['markdown']` and a failing test of that title, and asserts `.e2e/summary.md` and the failure page hold both inside code spans with nothing outside one matching `https://evil`; `tests/integration/config-names.test.ts` runs a target named `..` and an agent named `.` through `runProject`: the run ends with exit code 2 and one `INVALID_CONFIG` in `run.errors` naming the rule (the runner reports a configuration error that way rather than rejecting, as `explore()` does), and no artifacts directory is created; `report-markdown.test.ts` covers `+ item`, `_ under`, and `1) list` at the start of a quoted line and `+`, `=`, `_`, `1)` at the start of the assessment; `report-failure-text.test.ts` quotes a step explanation starting `# ` through `renderFailurePage`; `artifact-segment.test.ts` adds the post-#423 cases (`'.'.repeat(121)` is `_`; a 130-character id stays within 120) with the digest suffix asserted only when the cut segment carries one, so the test passes on this branch and after the merge. ---

title: fix(agent): a keyboard fallback is not blamed for an unlisted change, and an inconclusive judgment points at vision
body:
Two places where the agent was told the wrong thing about what it had just done or seen.

- `type` on a node the engine cannot fill (a focusable canvas, a widget with its own key handling) falls back to tap plus keyboard at `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts:406`. The keystrokes land, but the tree never lists that node's text, and `acting` presented the unchanged listing with `expectChange: true`, so the result blamed the control. The model retyped, or concluded the step failed. #433 removes the most common trigger (contenteditable hosts become `textbox`), not the mechanism.
- An action may now return `{ lead, expectChange }` (`primitives.ts:600`, `primitives.ts:631`); the fallback returns `expectChange: false` with a lead that says where to look instead.
- A mixed page (canvas plus controls) in pixel mode had the same shape: `changeShape` ignores pixels once any interactive node is listed (`observation.ts:372`), so a screenshot that visibly changed sat under a "did not change" verdict. `ScreenPresenter.attach` now digests each screenshot with the FNV the change wait already uses (`screen-update.ts:189`, `observation.ts:352`), and `renderUnchanged` says the screenshot changed instead of blaming the control (`screen-update.ts:256`).
- `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` carried the judge's explanation alone, while `docs/debugging.mdx` and the skill told the user to add `vision: true`. An inconclusive verdict reached with `vision` off now appends that sentence through `withHint` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts:89`); `waitFor`'s `STEP_TIMEOUT` carries it when the last round was inconclusive.
- The hint is gated on what the attempt knows about pixels (`index.ts:81`): none when the engine declares no `artifacts` capability, a secret was filled, or a completed step of the attempt has `visionDegraded`; firm once a completed step has `visionInput: true`; a condition (`if the engine captures pixels, ...`) before that. The SPI declares no pixel capability, only `artifacts`, and `observe` returns pixels "when requested and producible", so availability is known only after asking. `AgentContext` gains `engineCapabilities`, filled from `environment.target.engine?.capabilities` (`run/fixtures.ts:185`), empty for an engine-less target.
- `reference/errors.mdx` and `reference/agent.mdx` describe the hint and its gate; the skill's `agent.md` and both debugging tables say the message names it. Changeset: `e2e` patch.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` into an unfillable node | `#n12 is not an input; tapped it to focus it and typed through the keyboard.` followed by `The screen did not change within the wait after this action (re-observed as revision b2); the ids you have stay valid. If a change was expected, the control had no visible effect here: look for another way rather than repeating it.` | `#n12 is not an input; tapped it to focus it and typed through the keyboard. The tree does not list this node's text, so an unchanged listing says nothing about the typing: verify it through the app's reaction or a screenshot.` followed by `Screen unchanged since revision b1 (re-observed as revision b2); the ids you have stay valid.` |
| Unchanged listing under a changed screenshot | `The screen did not change within the wait after this action (re-observed as revision b2); the ids you have stay valid. If a change was expected, the control had no visible effect here: look for another way rather than repeating it.` | `Since revision b1 (re-observed as revision b2): listed nodes unchanged; the screenshot changed. Read the effect off the image (a focus ring alone is no effect); the ids you have stay valid.` |
| `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` without `vision`, no pixels seen yet in the attempt | `no order total or line items are on this screen` | `no order total or line items are on this screen; the judge saw the semantic tree only; if the engine captures pixels, pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels` |
| `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` without `vision`, after a step received pixels | `no order total or line items are on this screen` | `no order total or line items are on this screen; the judge saw the semantic tree only; pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels` |
| `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` on an engine without `artifacts`, or after a secret fill or a degraded pixel request | `no order total or line items are on this screen` | unchanged |
| `waitFor` timeout after an inconclusive round | `waitFor timed out; last judgment: no order total is on the About page` | `waitFor timed out; last judgment: no order total is on the About page; the judge saw the semantic tree only; if the engine captures pixels, pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[action returns lead or lead + expectChange] --> B[present]
  B --> C{listed lines changed?}
  C -- yes --> D[diff]
  C -- no --> E{screenshot digest moved?}
  E -- yes --> F[listed nodes unchanged; the screenshot changed]
  E -- no --> G{expectChange?}
  G -- true --> H[the control had no visible effect]
  G -- false --> I[Screen unchanged]
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  J[inconclusive, vision off] --> K{taint, or no artifacts capability, or a step degraded pixels?}
  K -- yes --> L[explanation alone]
  K -- no --> M{a completed step received pixels?}
  M -- yes --> N[pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels]
  M -- no --> O[if the engine captures pixels, pass vision: true ...]
```

- Tests through the built runner for what the unit tests alone had covered. `agent-act-pixel-tools.test.ts` drives `/canvas`, whose fixture now paints a tap count on every click, a repaint the tree cannot list: the same miss point twice repeats the status text and the result reads `listed nodes unchanged; the screenshot changed`; the blank margin twice reads `had no visible effect`. The two hint gates that had no test: `agent.test.ts` fills the password through `type_secret` and then judges inconclusive; `engine-contract.test.ts` asks for `vision: true` on an engine that declares `artifacts` but returns no pixels (`visionDegraded: UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`) and then judges inconclusive. Both carry the explanation alone. `reference/agent.mdx` says the hint is the built-in judge's: `runAssertStep` hands a custom `executor`'s `assert` its own explanation, never the hint.

title: fix(web): configured headers stay on one deployment of a shared host, not the whole vercel.app
body: `web({ headers })` on a preview at `myapp.vercel.app` sent the bypass token to every `*.vercel.app` host the page touched: `siteOf` kept two labels under a three-letter TLD, so the app's site was `vercel.app`, and the header route (`packages/web/src/protected-app.ts:38`) admitted any deployment on it. The same site check let an iframe from another `vercel.app` project into the observation as the app's own (`packages/web/src/observation.ts:220`). - `siteOf` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts:194`) reads one label deeper under a listed shared hosting suffix; the suffix itself stays a site of its own. The list (`SHARED_HOST_SUFFIXES`, `packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts:153`) is drawn from the PRIVATE DOMAINS section of the Public Suffix List. No PSL dependency: the list is hundreds of kilobytes that change monthly, and this rule only decides where configured credentials go, never where a test may navigate. - The longest listed suffix wins, so `up.railway.app` nests under `railway.app`. Under `amazonaws.com` every hostname is a site of its own: AWS nests service and region labels between the tenant's label and the suffix, so one label under it would make a whole region one site. - The two-letter country-code heuristic (`example.co.uk`), IP literals, and single-label hosts are unchanged. A shared host the list misses reads as one site, as before. - The `headers` docstring in `packages/web/src/surface.ts:158` still said "an allowed origin", the pre-#290 vocabulary; it now names the site rule. `docs/reference/web.mdx`, `docs/security.mdx`, `docs/starting-your-app.mdx`, and `docs/reference/config.mdx` state the rule and where the list lives. - A web unit test drives `installSiteHeaders` against a recording context: the header leaves for `myapp.vercel.app` and not for `other.vercel.app`. A browser-level check on a real `*.vercel.app` name is not possible over plain HTTP (the `.app` TLD is HSTS-preloaded in Chromium), so the existing integration test keeps covering the browser plumbing with `127.0.0.1` against `localhost`. - Follow-up (e7dbef82): the browser-level check does exist once no request leaves the machine. In `protected-app.test.ts` a real Chromium context gets a recording catch-all that fulfills everything, then `installSiteHeaders` (the same call the surface makes per context); Playwright runs handlers newest first, so the header route hands the request on and the catch-all reads it as sent. `https://myapp.vercel.app/` and a fetch to `api.myapp.vercel.app` carry `x-vercel-protection-bypass`, fetches to `other.vercel.app` and `vercel.app` do not, and HSTS never comes up because no name resolves. `observation.test.ts` captures a locally fulfilled `myapp.vercel.app` page with `site: 'myapp.vercel.app'`: the `api.myapp.vercel.app` frame's button is in the tree, the `widget.vercel.app` frame stays a boundary node, and without a site neither is read. `urls.test.ts` adds `now.sh` and `loca.lt` (the shared rule runs before the two-letter country-code rule, which would have read `myapp.loca.lt` as `loca.lt`) and an `it.each` over a mirrored copy of the suffix list, so a typo in either list fails; the list stays module-private because a test-only export is dead production API under `pnpm check:dead-code`. The `app.site` docstring in `packages/e2e/src/engine/index.ts` now states the shared-host rule. | Host | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `myapp.vercel.app` | `vercel.app` | `myapp.vercel.app` | | `a.b.myapp.vercel.app` | `vercel.app` | `myapp.vercel.app` | | `vercel.app` | `vercel.app` | `vercel.app` | | `bucket.s3.amazonaws.com` | `amazonaws.com` | `bucket.s3.amazonaws.com` | | `abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` | `amazonaws.com` | `abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` | | `shop.example.co.uk` | `example.co.uk` | `example.co.uk` | | `app.example.com` | `example.com` | `example.com` | ---

title: fix(locator): count, all, and isVisible answer at once when the frame is missing
body: A locator under `web.frameLocator('#widget')` whose iframe is not in the document yet made every non-waiting read wait or throw: `count()`, `all()`, and `allTextContents()` blocked for the whole action timeout (2041 ms at a 2000 ms timeout) and then failed with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, and `isVisible()` threw it at once instead of answering `false`. `docs/reference/screen.mdx` promises `0`, `[]`, and `false` for zero matches, so a `while (!(await widget.isVisible()))` loop against an iframe widget broke on its first pass. - The web engine reports the missing frame as a retryable `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` (`packages/web/src/surface.ts:740`), and `resolveOnce` retried every retryable error until its deadline. `isVisible()` handed it an already expired `Deadline(0)`, so the first miss was translated and thrown. - `resolveOnce` now takes what a missing frame means (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts:125`): `wait` keeps polling for it like a node that is not there yet, `empty` answers zero matches, since nothing under a frame outside the document can match. - `LocatorEngine` gains `resolveNow`, `readNow`, and `readAllNow` on the `empty` policy, used by `count()` and `all()`, `isVisible()` and `isHidden()`, and `allTextContents()` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:418`, `:445`, `:455`); the MCP `locate` probe uses `resolveNow` too. A stale resolve is still retried within the action timeout in all three: that repairs a race with a navigation, it does not wait for a match. - `resolveAll` and `readAll` lose their default deadline and serve the assertion poll only, so the next non-waiting read cannot pick up the waiting resolve by omission. Actions, assertions, and single-node reads such as `textContent()` keep polling for the frame. - The strictness table in `docs/reference/screen.mdx` gets a row for a frame that is not in the document; the frame test in `tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` reads under an absent frame with a time bound, and `tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts` covers the three new reads against the fake engine's `frame` step. - Follow-up (72db5777): a behavior change the first cut left unstated. `isVisible()` and `isHidden()` went through `Deadline(0)` on main, one resolve and done; through `readNow` they now re-resolve a stale node within the action timeout, as every resolve does, and a resolve still stale at the timeout throws `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` where before it threw at once. Three unit cases pin it (stale resolve then the node, 50 stale resolves against a 350 ms timeout, a stale read answered null with no second read), and the changeset, the intro above the strictness table in `screen.mdx`, and the skill's `writing-tests` line say exactly what a read waits for: a missing frame answers at once, a stale node is re-resolved, a value never. Runner-level, the waiting half: `frameLocator('#absent').getByRole('button').tap({ timeout: 800 })` fails `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` with a `locator.tap` step of at least 800 ms, and `count()` under `frameLocator('#outer').frameLocator('#absent')` on a new `/frame-nested` page (the same page #425 adds, so the two merge as one) is `0` inside 2 s. Before: `await web.frameLocator('#absent').getByRole('button').count()` waits `actionTimeout`, then `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`; `isVisible()` throws it at once. After: `count()` is `0`, `all()` and `allTextContents()` are `[]`, `isVisible()` is `false`, `isHidden()` is `true`, all at once. ---

title: refactor(api)!: drop the public exports nothing outside the runner consumes
body:
Nothing outside `packages/e2e/src` imports these names: a grep over `packages/*/src`, `packages/*/tests`, the testbed, both benchmarks, `docs`, and `skills` on 2026-09-22 found only the runner's own modules and its unit tests. The rule here is no zero-consumer public API, and an export whose only consumer is a test counts as one. Each name comes off the entry it sat on and stays exported from its module, where runner code still uses it.

- `RUNTIME_CODES` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/executor.ts:457`) leaves `e2e`. No consumer anywhere, not even a test; `agent/act.ts` and `agent/tool-loop.ts` import it from the module.
- `BLOCKABLE_CODES` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/executor.ts:479`) leaves `e2e`. One integration test and five runner modules import it from the module. A `blocked` verdict needs a code from the table the agent-steps guide lists, which `docs/executors.mdx` already points at, so the set was not documented instead.
- `buildTraceEntry` and `readTraceEntry` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/trace.ts:276`, `:285`) leave `e2e`. Unit tests only. `TraceCacheStore` stays documented and handles entries opaquely; `cache/store.ts` and `agent/step-cache.ts` keep the module exports.
- `isDefinedTool` and `toolAppliesTo` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/tool.ts:69`, `:64`) leave `e2e/agent`. One unit test outside `agent/default-agent.ts`, which imports them from the module.
- `store` on `ChatGptOptions`, `CopilotOptions`, and `GrokOptions`: zero consumers, and `CredentialStore` is exported from no subpath, so a user could not name the type. AGENTS.md keeps stores module-private.
- `apiUrl` on `ChatGptOptions`: the picked `CodexProviderOptions` field is marked a test seam in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/openai.ts`. `baseURL` on `CopilotOptions` and `GrokOptions` was the same knob under another name, "for a proxy", documented nowhere and used by one unit test each. Copilot's enterprise routing keys off the stored login and fires only on the default origin (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/github-copilot.ts:123`), so a custom `baseURL` would have bypassed it rather than enabled it. `chatgpt()`, `copilot()`, and `grok()` now take a model id and nothing else; the three option types are gone.
- `RUNTIME_EXPORTS` in `packages/e2e/src/config/diagnose.ts`, the list behind the missing-export hint that a unit test pins to the real module, drops the four names.
- The missing-export hint read every unknown uppercase name as a probable type, so `import { BLOCKABLE_CODES } from 'e2e'` would have been told to `import type` it, which fails the same way. A `REMOVED_EXPORTS` map in `diagnose.ts`, keyed by entry then name and consulted before the spelling and type heuristics, names the removal and what stands in for each of the six; `defineConfig`'s 0.5 message moves into it.
- The six hints name no release: `X was removed from e2e: ...` and `X was removed from e2e/agent: ...`. They first said `0.16` while the package is `0.15.0-canary`, and the version that ships the removal is the release job's to decide, so the text cannot lie about it; `defineConfig`'s hint keeps `0.5`, a release that happened. The diagnose unit test asserts the wording and that no `x.y` number appears.
- Pinned at the type level in `tests/types/sdk-types.ts`: `@ts-expect-error` on `import { isDefinedTool } from '../../src/agent/public.ts'`, on `import { BLOCKABLE_CODES } from '../../src/index.ts'`, and on `chatgpt('x', {})`, `copilot('x', {})`, `grok('x', {})`, next to the one-argument calls as positives. Each directive covers exactly one error (TS2724/TS2305, TS2554).
- Pinned at the dist level in `tests/integration/dist-public-exports.test.ts`: `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/agent/public.d.ts` mention none of the six names (and still export `renderMarkdownReport` and `defineTool`, so an empty file cannot pass), and each `dist/oauth/*.d.ts` declares `<constructor>(modelId: string): LanguageModelV4` with no `*Options` type and no `CredentialStore`.

The constructor tests handed a store and a URL through the removed options. They now sign in the way a CI user does, through `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, as `tests/unit/oauth/cli.test.ts` already did, and a `useVendor` helper beside `useServers` routes the process's requests to the local server with path and query kept. The constructors are called the way a user calls them, and no runner code exists for the tests' sake.

```ts
const serve = useServers(afterEach);
const vendor = useVendor(afterEach);

const backend = await serve(handler);
vendor(backend, { openai: login });
const model = chatgpt('gpt-5.5');
```

What `e2e run` prints for a config that still imports one:

```
The requested module 'e2e' does not provide an export named 'BLOCKABLE_CODES'; BLOCKABLE_CODES was removed from e2e: a blocked verdict carries any code the errors reference marks blocked, and the set was never usable outside the runner
```

Changeset: `e2e` minor. PR #434 adds type exports to the same `index.ts`; this one only removes lines, so the two rebase cleanly.

## Stability policy

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, "Stability policy", covers the exports emitted in `dist/index.d.ts` and says a breaking change to a covered surface ships with a deprecation first: the old form keeps working, prints a one-line warning naming the replacement, and is removed six months later, in a batch; the first window opens October 1, 2026, so its removals land no earlier than April 1, 2027. This PR removes covered surface with no deprecation: the four `e2e` exports are on that list outright, and while `e2e/agent` and `e2e/oauth/*` are not named in it, both are public. Two ways to land it, the maintainer's call rather than this PR's:

- Merge before October 1 as pre-launch cleanup, the way #392 renamed the engine packages under `feat!` on 2026-09-21 with no deprecation.
- Keep every removed name and option, mark each `@deprecated` in JSDoc with a one-line runtime warning on first use, and land the removal in the April 2027 batch.

title: fix(cli): init never writes the agent skill through a symlink
body:
Probe: `.claude/skills/e2e -> /tmp/elsewhere/e2e`, then `e2e init --yes`. The user's `elsewhere/e2e/SKILL.md` was replaced by the bundled one and `references/*.md` appeared next to it, with nothing printed. A skill directory linked to a dotfiles repo or a shared skills folder lost its content on every init.

- `findInstalledSkillDirs` took an `existsSync` hit through the link as an installed copy, and the write loop's `mkdirSync` + `writeFileSync` followed it (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/agent-skill.ts:49`, `packages/e2e/src/cli/init.ts:263`).
- `planSkillInstall` now `lstat`s every component from the project root to each file it would write, before reading anything, and records the symlinks it meets plus any file whose real path leaves the project. A location with links is never read and never written through.
- `--yes` skips it and prints one line naming the link and its real target; a dangling link shows the path as written.
- An interactive run asks `Replace the symlink <link> -> <target> with a copy of the skill?`, default no. Yes unlinks it and writes a plain directory, reported as `Replaced .claude/skills/e2e/`. The question is asked only when the link is the skill directory or inside it: a linked parent (`.claude/skills`) holds more than the skill, so it is skipped with the warning in both modes.
- The same walk catches a directory where a bundled file goes, or a file where `references/` goes. Such a copy is skipped with `Broken, not touching: .agents/skills/e2e/ (SKILL.md is a directory)` in both modes instead of throwing `EISDIR` mid-write: init removes nothing to repair a copy. The content comparison for plain copies treats an unreadable file as differing rather than throwing.
- `insideProjectRoot` and `realpathOfExisting` move from `packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts` to `packages/e2e/src/internal/paths.ts`, shared with the `app.command.log` check.
- `docs/reference/cli.mdx` gets the sentences on symlinked and broken skill directories.
- Tests in `tests/unit/cli-init.test.ts` for two more shapes. A dangling link (`.claude/skills/e2e -> ../../gone/e2e`): `--yes` prints `Symlink, not touching: .claude/skills/e2e -> <project>/gone/e2e`, the path as written and resolved against the link's directory, never realpath; the link stays and `gone/` is never created. Since `existsSync` follows the link, a dangling one is no installed copy, so `--yes` takes every location and `.agents/skills/e2e` gets the skill. Interactively, agreeing to the replace question unlinks the dangling link and writes the copy. The second shape is the `insideProjectRoot` branch of `findBlockers`: a file whose real path leaves the project with no symlink on its path. `firstBlocker` lstats every existing component from the project root down, so any link that could carry `.agents/skills` or `.claude/skills` outside is reported as a link first (`.claude` itself being the link is the parent-link case above); with the fixed `SKILL_LOCATIONS` the branch is reachable only through a direct `planSkillInstall` caller whose location escapes the root (`../shared/skills`). The test pins that contract: every bundled file is planned as a link to its real path outside, nothing as a write.

```
▲  Symlink, not touching: .claude/skills/e2e -> /Users/me/dotfiles/skills/e2e
```

title: chore(schema): retire the agent-tool schema nothing produces, and gate judgments on agent-judgment-2
body:
`packages/e2e/schema/agent-tool-v1.schema.json` sat in the AGENTS.md list of pinned wire formats with nothing behind it: no producer, no parser, and its only test was its own fixture pair. The judgment schema beside it had the mirror-image gap: `protocol.ts` says the schema wins on any divergence from `validateJudgmentResponse`, and no test compiled the schema to check.

- `grep -rn "agent-tool\|toolVersion" packages docs skills scripts .github` hits the schema, its two fixtures, and the AGENTS.md bullet; the remaining matches are the phrase `agent-tools-only` in `types.ts`, `resolve.ts`, `build.ts` and a `#agent-tools` docs anchor, none of them the schema.
- The schema's `kind` enum is `tap`, `type`, `scroll`, `press`, `longPress`, `navigate`, `observe`, `conclude`, and its secret fill is a `type` carrying `sensitiveName` and `purpose`.
- The runtime's grammar names (`src/agent/action-names.ts`) are `tap`, `type`, `typeText`, `typeSecret`, `pressKey`, `selectOption`, `dismissKeyboard`, `navigate`, `scroll`, `press`, and its tools (`primitives.ts`) are `tap_at`, `screenshot`, `type_secret`, `dismiss_keyboard`, `complete_step`; `longPress`, `conclude`, and `sensitiveName` appear nowhere in `src/agent`.
- The schema and both fixtures are deleted. `schema-fixtures.test.ts` globs `schema/`, so it needed no edit; the AGENTS.md Contracts bullet lists report-1, session-1, agent-judgment-2, and the deprecated agent-judgment-1.
- No tarball carried the file: `schema/` joins `files` in #437, still open. Its `.changeset/ship-schemas.md` first listed the five schema names, `agent-tool-v1` among them; as of 2026-09-22 it says every `schema/*.schema.json` ships and names none, and its test compares the glob's matches to the `schema/` directory, so the two land in either order with nothing to drop.
- `tests/unit/agent-judgment-schema.test.ts` runs 23 inputs through the wire schema, the provider-facing `JUDGMENT_SCHEMA` (the copy the model is asked to fill), and `validateJudgmentResponse`, and asserts one answer per input: both fixtures, every verdict, an extra key, a wrong enum, each missing field, the agent-judgment-1 shape, `null`, an array, a JSON string, and the 8192 boundary in ASCII, astral code points, and lone surrogates.
- The gate found one disagreement, and per `protocol.ts` the runtime was the wrong side: JSON Schema `maxLength` counts code points (Ajv's `ucs2length`), `asBoundedString` counted UTF-16 units with `.length`, so an explanation of 8192 emoji passed both schemas and was rejected by the runner as a policy error. It now counts code points; changeset `e2e` patch.
- Two integration cases in `tests/integration/agent.test.ts` run the gate through the built runner with the scripted judge answering the literal `agent-judgment-v1.valid.json` document, the shape a model still on the retired protocol would send. Answered once: one `schema` event, a repair prompt carrying `validation errors: unknown protocolVersion` and the rejected text, a valid second answer, the step passes with `modelCalls: 2`. Answered twice: `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`, category `test`, two model calls and no third, since `assert` is one judgment plus one repair round.
- The second case found the runner writing a report its own schema rejected. `report-1` requires `observationRevision` and `explanation` on an `agent.assert` step once a model call was made; the exhaustion path noted no explanation, so `assertValidReport` failed on `steps/1: must have required property 'explanation'`. This is on `main` too, for any assert whose repair round is rejected. `Invocation.ask` now records every rejected answer as a `schema` event (the extract path already did) and, with no call left, notes the rejection as the step's explanation before throwing; the step reads `explanation: "unknown protocolVersion"` next to its `observationRevision`. Changeset paragraph and a sentence in `docs/reference/agent.mdx` beside the capture-failure rule.

**Stability policy.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Stability policy" (#166) covers "the report, session, and agent protocol schemas in `packages/e2e/schema/`" and requires a deprecation before a removal; the first window opens October 1, 2026 and its removals land no earlier than April 1, 2027. This PR removes a listed wire format with no deprecation. Two facts say nothing can depend on it; the call is the maintainer's.

- No consumer: no file under `packages/*/src`, `docs`, `skills`, `scripts`, or `.github` produces or parses `agent-tool-1`, and its only test was its own fixture pair.
- Never published: `schema/` is not in the package `files`, so no tarball on npm has carried the file; #437 would be the first.

The alternative under the policy: keep the file, mark it deprecated in the AGENTS.md Contracts bullet and in the schema's `description` (as `agent-judgment-v1.schema.json` is), and delete it in the April 2027 batch. Say which and I will reshape the PR.

```ts
it.each(cases)('$name: the wire schema, the provider schema, and the runtime agree', ({ value, accepted }) => {
  expect(wireSchema(value), 'wire schema').toBe(accepted);
  expect(providerSchema(value), 'provider schema').toBe(accepted);
  expect(validateJudgmentResponse(value).ok, 'runtime').toBe(accepted);
});
```

title: fix(run): a worker failure is recorded once, and a stray rejection fails its own test
body:
Four worker-lifecycle defects, each seen on a real run. A target that could not boot reported `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` four times under `workers: 4`. A worker's fatal error came with a second run error for the kill the scheduler issued itself. A message to a worker whose channel had just closed took the runner down with `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: no report, the managed app left running, `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` on the next run. And a test that rejected a promise it never awaited killed its worker, so the next test in the file was skipped as infrastructure and `--last-failed` reran the survivors.

- `failTarget` records `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` once and still drains the queues on every later call: each worker still starting when the target failed exits after it and requeues its unit, and that unit needs its skip (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:750`).
- A `fatal` message marks the worker `killed` before `runner.kill()`, so `onExit` reads the exit as the one asked for and adds no `WORKER_EXIT` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:635`).
- `ChildProcessRunner.post` skips a child that is no longer `connected`, and the `error` listener is `on`, not `once`: `child.send` after `disconnect` reports on the next tick, once per send, and the second one used to escape as an uncaught exception (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/handle.ts:76`, `:91`).
- An unhandled rejection is charged to the test running when it surfaces, the rule Playwright uses too, since Node cannot name the test that created the promise. `TargetExecutor.strayRejection` (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:213`) cuts a running body through `attemptAbort` the way a timeout cuts it, or records the rejection against the phase a returned body was in. The attempt waits one event-loop turn after the body, since Node reports such a rejection once the microtasks drain, so a rejection the body left behind lands on this attempt and not between two (`:825`, `:991`).
- Between tests the rejection is the run error `UNHANDLED_REJECTION`, naming the last test that finished in the worker as the likely source, and the worker goes on; before any test has finished there it still ends the worker.
- A body cut this way keeps running like one past its `timeout`: the harness operation it is in is cancelled and its fixtures die with the attempt. `writing-tests.mdx` and the `TEST_TIMEOUT`, `UNHANDLED_REJECTION`, and `WORKER_EXIT` rows of `errors.mdx` say so.

Run errors, before and after:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` nondeterministic, `workers: 4`, 4 files | `CONFIG_NOT_DETERMINISTIC` x5, `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` x4 | `CONFIG_NOT_DETERMINISTIC` x5, `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` x1 |
| worker reports `fatal` mid-unit | the fatal's error, then `WORKER_EXIT` "exited unexpectedly (code null, signal SIGKILL)" | the fatal's error |
| `void Promise.reject(new Error('boom'))` in a body | `ERROR`, `WORKER_EXIT`; the next test skipped; exit 3 | none; that test fails with `boom`; the next test runs; exit 1 |
| a timer from test A rejects while test B runs | `ERROR`, `WORKER_EXIT`; B and the rest of its file lost; exit 3 | none; B fails with the rejection; exit 1 |
| a rejection surfaces between tests | `ERROR`, `WORKER_EXIT`; the worker's next file lost; exit 3 | `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` naming the last finished test; every test runs; exit 1 |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[unhandledRejection] --> A{abandoned step?}
  A -- yes --> N[ignored: STEP_NOT_AWAITED already recorded]
  A -- no --> F{attempt in flight?}
  F -- body running --> C[attemptAbort, body race rejects]
  F -- body returned --> P[recordFailure at its phase]
  F -- no, a test finished here --> U[run error UNHANDLED_REJECTION naming it]
  F -- no, none finished --> X[fatal: worker exits]
```

Tests: `tests/unit/worker-handle.test.ts` forks the real entry with a preload that severs the channel and holds the process open a second (the entry exits on `disconnect` by design), then posts two messages per turn until it is gone; the scheduler unit test gains a `fatalOn` fake and a four-worker boot failure; `parallel-workers.test.ts` covers the nondeterministic `projectId`, the stray rejection in a body, a late timer charged to the running test, and an `afterAll` rejection recorded between tests, end to end.

- `recordFailure` keeps the first failure and files later ones under `secondaryErrors`, so a persist or teardown failure after the body cannot replace the verdict; `cutBody` is cleared before the evidence capture, so a rejection surfacing during it is recorded. Tests through the child-process path: an uncaught throw is one run error and no `WORKER_EXIT` (exit 3); a rejection before any test finished ends the worker with the rejection itself as the run error and the pair on its way as `WORKER_CRASH` (the docs rows now say so instead of `WORKER_EXIT`); a rejection after a body failure lands under `secondaryErrors`.

- The `worker-handle` unit test hung on Node 24 and 26 (CI jobs ran past an hour and were cancelled; 30 s timeouts locally on 26). Its `--import` preload also ran in the module-hooks thread tsx registers, which has no channel and whose no-op `process.exit` kept the main thread's `exit(0)` waiting on it. The preload now severs the channel under `isMainThread` only, and the test kills a worker that outlives its second.

title: fix(types): the e2e and e2e/engine types compile without the optional ai peer installed
body: A project on the documented AI-SDK-free path (`agents: { default: own }` with a hand-rolled `StepExecutor`, no `ai` installed) fails its own `tsc` on `node_modules/e2e/dist/config/agent.d.ts: error TS2307: Cannot find module 'ai'` unless `skipLibCheck` is on. `e2e init` writes no tsconfig, so the project's settings decide. With `ai` installed and `skipLibCheck` off, the same project gets 18 TS2344 errors from the SDK's own `.d.ts` under TypeScript 7.0.2 instead. - `tsc --explainFiles` on `import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'` reached `ai` twice. `dist/config/agent.d.ts` typed `ResolvedModel.model` as `Exclude`, and `config/resolve.d.ts` pulls it in for `secrets.d.ts`, `run/records.d.ts`, `collect/*.d.ts`, and `report/build.d.ts`. `dist/internal/ai-trace.d.ts` names the SDK's `Telemetry`, and `run/events.d.ts` imported the worker protocol, which carries the trace snapshot, for `WireResultRecord` and `encodeResult`. - `ResolvedModel.model` is the structural `ModelInstance` (`packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts:33`). `SdkLanguageModel` and `asSdkLanguageModel` move to the loader, `packages/e2e/src/agent/ai-sdk.ts`, the one module the `ai` types enter from; `model/sdk.ts`, `tool-loop.ts`, and `explore/executor.ts` narrow there. - `SecretRegistry` names its two maps instead of `Pick` (`packages/e2e/src/secrets.ts:15`). - `WireResultRecord` and `encodeResult` sit next to `ResultRecord` in `packages/e2e/src/run/records.ts`; `run/events.ts` and the worker protocol import them from there, so the protocol and the AI trace leave the public closure. - `tests/integration/types-without-ai.test.ts` is the type-side twin of `cli-boot.test.ts`: a consumer-shaped project (`node_modules/e2e` linked, entry points resolved through `exports`) compiled with `--explainFiles`, failing on any file under `node_modules/ai` or `node_modules/@ai-sdk` with the imports that reached it. It fails on main with the chain below and takes about 200 ms on TypeScript 7. - `e2e/agent` keeps the `ai` types: `createAgent`, `defineTool`, and `createToolLoopExecutor` are the AI SDK executor builders, as the `e2e/oauth/*` constructors are the provider ones. - `docs/executors.mdx` says the `e2e` and `e2e/engine` types compile with no `ai` package installed. Before, on main: ``` node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts Imported via 'ai' from file 'dist/config/agent.d.ts' Imported via 'ai' from file 'dist/internal/ai-trace.d.ts' dist/config/agent.d.ts Imported via './agent.ts' from file 'dist/config/resolve.d.ts' dist/config/resolve.d.ts Imported via './config/resolve.ts' from file 'dist/secrets.d.ts' Imported via '../config/resolve.ts' from file 'dist/run/records.d.ts' Imported via '../config/resolve.ts' from file 'dist/collect/collect.d.ts' Imported via '../config/resolve.ts' from file 'dist/report/build.d.ts' dist/internal/ai-trace.d.ts Imported via '../../internal/ai-trace.ts' from file 'dist/run/worker/protocol.d.ts' dist/run/worker/protocol.d.ts Imported via './worker/protocol.ts' from file 'dist/run/events.d.ts' dist/run/events.d.ts Imported via './run/events.ts' from file 'dist/index.d.ts' ``` After, the same probe lists 37 declarations under `dist/` and `@types/node`, and nothing under `node_modules/ai`, `@ai-sdk/*`, `zod`, or `@standard-schema/spec`. ```mermaid flowchart LR I[dist/index.d.ts] --> E[run/events.d.ts] I --> S[secrets.d.ts] E -- before --> P[run/worker/protocol.d.ts] --> T[internal/ai-trace.d.ts] --> AI[ai] S -- before --> R[config/resolve.d.ts] --> A[config/agent.d.ts] --> AI E -- now --> RC[run/records.d.ts] --> R R -- now --> A2[config/agent.d.ts, ModelInstance] S -- now --> M[two ReadonlyMaps] ``` ---

title: fix(expect): toHaveValue compares the raw value and refuses a node without one
body:
`expect(textarea).toHaveValue('line1 line2')` passed against a textarea holding `'line1

line2  '`, and on failure printed `observed: value "line1

line2  "`, a string that was never what got compared. `toHaveValue('')` passed on a heading, and `not.toHaveValue(x)` passed on any node that is not a form control.

- The matcher table has declared `normalize: false` for `toHaveValue` since the first commit, but the flag only shaped the failure message: the predicate went through `matchesText`, which collapses whitespace on both sides (`packages/e2e/src/internal/text.ts:55`). `sample.node.value ?? ''` turned a node with no value into one with an empty value.
- `text.ts` gains `compareText(actual, pattern, { mode, normalize })` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/text.ts:65`), the one matching rule with normalization as an input; `matchesText` is its normalized `equals` form and `containsText` folds into the `contains` mode.
- Each `TextMatcherDef` is now a `TextComparison` plus the field it reads (`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:69`), so the flag drives the comparison and the message alike: `toHaveValue` compares the raw value, string or regexp, and prints it raw.
- A node's role decides what a missing value means. `packages/e2e/src/internal/roles.ts` holds the editable roles the secret fill and the observation feed already used, and the value-bearing set built from them plus `spinbutton`, `slider`, `listbox`, and `option`. A value-bearing role without a `value` reads as `''`, since the mobile engine drops an empty value from its snapshot (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts:303`) and a cleared field must still satisfy `toHaveValue('')`. Any other node keeps the poll waiting through a new `evaluableNode` hook on `MatcherSpec` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:41`), negated or not, and the failure reads `observed: no value (not a form control)`.
- `toHaveAccessibleName` also declared `normalize: false` while comparing normalized. It keeps the normalized comparison, as `toHaveText` and Playwright do, so the flag flips to `true` and its message now prints the normalized name it compared.
- `docs/reference/expect.mdx` names the exception under "Text comparison is normalized", `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md` mentions it beside the other matchers, and `tests/unit/expect-async-value.test.ts` covers the raw comparison, the message, the five control roles without a value, the heading, and the accessible name over the screen fixture.

Before: `toHaveValue('line1 line2')` on `'line1

line2  '` passes; `toHaveValue('')` on a heading passes.
After: the first fails with `observed: value "line1

line2  "`, the second with `observed: no value (not a form control)`; `toHaveValue('line1

line2  ')` passes, and so does `toHaveValue('')` on a textbox the platform reports without a value.

- `web-platform.test.ts` runs the chain in a browser: a `<textarea>` on the fixture home page holds `line1

line2  `; `toHaveValue('line1

line2  ')` and the regexp form pass, `toHaveValue('line1 line2')` fails with `observed: value "line1

line2  "`, so the web engine reports the raw value and nothing on the way collapses it. `expect-async-value.test.ts` adds `listbox` and `option` to the roles that read a missing value as `''`, and a `link`, whose name and text are not a value, stays unevaluable negated or not.

title: fix(agent): tool inputs are closed schemas, and the invariant says what happens to unknown fields, tools, and stale ids
body: Zod's default object mode strips keys it does not know, so a `tap` the model decorated with `force: true` or `selector: "#x"` passed validation and ran as a plain tap, while AGENTS.md and `docs/security.mdx` said unknown tools or fields are `POLICY_DENIED`. Nothing acted on the extra fields either way; the gap was between the invariant text and the code, with no test guarding either reading. - `schemaTool` closes the schema once for every grammar tool and `complete_step` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts:85`), so a tool added later cannot forget it. The MCP catalog's `observe` and `locate` and the server's four fixed tools get `.strict()` too (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/catalog.ts:82`, `packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:343`). The JSON Schema providers see is unchanged, though not because of zod: the AI SDK converts a zod 4 schema in input mode (`zod4Schema` in `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, `io: 'input'`), where zod 4.6.1 emits no `additionalProperties` for a plain `z.object`, and then its `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` pass writes `additionalProperties: false` onto every object. Providers got `false` from that pass before; with `.strict()` zod emits it itself, so the wire shape no longer rests on the pass. What moves is the runtime check. - The AI SDK parses each call before dispatch. An unknown tool name or an input outside the schema becomes an invalid call, gets a `tool-error` output, and never runs; the model reads the error as the call's result and its next turn is the repair. No harness model call is spent on it. - Refused calls count toward the failure streak: `extractToolResults` reads `error-text` outputs as failed by construction (`packages/e2e/src/agent/loop-guards.ts:174`), so a model that never gets a call past the schema is warned at three and stopped at five, like any failing action. Before, those results were skipped and only the turn budget bounded them. - The step's turns record a refusal as `[tap] error: ...` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/tool-loop.ts:580`); before, a refused call showed with no outcome. - AGENTS.md and `docs/security.mdx` say what the code does: refusals go back to the model, a node id not on the current screen is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` (an action failure the model re-aims from), and `POLICY_DENIED` stays for denied destinations, forbidden fills, and tainted pixels. `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` names the `INVALID_ARGUMENT` an undeclared `call` argument gets. What the model reads after `tap {target: "n5", force: true, selector: "#increment"}`: ```text AI_InvalidToolInputError: Invalid input for tool tap: AI_TypeValidationError: Type validation failed: Value: {"target":"n5","force":true,"selector":"#increment"}. Error message: [ { "code": "unrecognized_keys", "keys": [ "force", "selector" ], "path": [], "message": "Unrecognized keys: \"force\", \"selector\"" } ] ``` and after a call to a tool the step does not offer: ```text AI_NoSuchToolError: Model tried to call unavailable tool 'click'. Available tools: observe, tap, type, press, select, scroll, navigate, screenshot, tap_at, type_at, press_at, select_at, complete_step. ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[model tool call] --> B{name offered?} B -- no --> E[tool-error back to the model] B -- yes --> C{input fits the closed schema?} C -- no --> E C -- yes --> D[authorize, then dispatch] E --> F[next turn repairs; the failure streak counts it] ``` - `agent-grammar-tools.test.ts` pins the provider-facing shape through the SDK's own conversion (`asSchema(inputSchema).jsonSchema`): every grammar tool and `complete_step` carries `additionalProperties: false`, and zod's input-mode output carries it on its own; a control shows a plain object gets it from the SDK's pass alone. `mcp-tools.test.ts` refuses an undeclared key on the catalog's `observe` and `locate` with nothing dispatched; `mcp-session-host.test.ts` checks the four fixed tools' schemas through `toolSpecs()`, and `mcp-server.test.ts` shows the MCP SDK answering `Invalid arguments for tool open_session: Unrecognized key: "headless"` as an error result before the handler, with no session opened. `agent-policy.test.ts` runs one turn of `tap` plus `tap {force: true}`: the plain tap ran once and reported the change, the decorated one came back refused, and `step.turns[0]` lists both calls with `[tap] error:` beside the result. Both `POLICY_DENIED` rows in `reference/errors.mdx` name destinations, forbidden fills, and tainted pixels, and say an unknown tool or field is never this code. - A `complete_step` that pairs `status: "passed"` with an `errorCode` is accepted: the code is dropped and the turn's outcome reads `[complete_step] Step concluded; dropped errorCode ACTION_FAILED on a passed verdict.` An earlier commit on this branch refined the schema to refuse the pair, and live runs with `gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast` showed why that cannot hold: the model attaches `ACTION_FAILED` to passed verdicts about half the time, and each refusal had it resend the identical call 12 to 19 times (the conclusion tool sits outside the repeat guard by design) before it gave up with `status: failed` under a summary saying the step succeeded. The testbed agent suite went from 15/16 to 4/16 over 287 model calls; the web and iOS benchmarks looped the same way. The `errorCode` description still states the rule; a description steers, a refusal loops. Refused `complete_step` calls now count toward the failure streak: `extractToolResults` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/loop-guards.ts`) keeps the conclusion tool's `error-text` results and skips only its text, so three refusals warn and five force the verdict, and `loop-guards.test.ts` pins both thresholds. `agent-grammar-tools.test.ts` checks the pair validates, the body records a pass without a code and names what it dropped, and a `failed` verdict keeps its code; the pin that the sent schema is the plain object stays. `agent-policy.test.ts` runs a `tap` turn and then the contradictory verdict: the step passed on that call with no repair turn (`modelCalls` 2), the counter read 1, and the verdict turn's outcome is the dropped-code note alone. The verdict is its own turn because the SDK runs a turn's tool calls in parallel and an accepted conclusion wins that race: a `tap` batched beside it is refused by the loop's guard as already concluding, which is how the loop behaved before this branch too. `docs/agent-steps.mdx` says the code is dropped and noted. ---

title: test: login flags, option type assertions, an import allowlist, and no wall-clock bounds in mobile units
body: Four places where a regression would have passed CI unnoticed, each now a test. No production code changed. - `e2e login --device`, `--client-id`, `--from-gh`, and `--enterprise-url` had no test between commander and the provider flow: a renamed key in `toLoginOptions` (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/cli.ts:222`) would have parsed fine and reached the flow as nothing. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/cli-login.test.ts` runs `main(['node', 'e2e', 'login', ...])` with a provider double swapped in for `getProvider`, and asserts the flow got `{ method: 'device' }`, `{ clientId }`, `{ fromGitHubCli: true }`, `{ enterpriseUrl }`, that a flag meant for another provider is dropped, and that the file store holds what the flow returned. `--from-gh` with no `gh` on PATH runs the real Copilot flow: one line on stderr, exit 1, nothing stored. - Three mobile unit tests bounded a tap by wall clock (`toBeLessThan(200)`, twice `toBeLessThan(80)`). A loaded 4 vCPU runner turns that into a flake, and a tap that did wait still passes when the machine is fast. `tapsAtOnce` in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts` stops the clock with fake timers and asserts the press was recorded with no timer pending; a tap that waits out the transition budget leaves exactly one. The lower bounds stay, since timers never fire early. - `agents..judge`, `timeout`, `maxSteps`, `maxModelCalls`, and `maxObservationBytes` had no compile-time assertion, nor did `WebOptions.headers`, `basicAuth`, `viewport`, `testIdAttribute`, nor any `MobileOptions` field or the `DeviceProvider` seam. Widening `judge` to a string, `timeout` to a duration string, or dropping `password` from `WebBasicAuth` would have compiled. Assertions appended to `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts` and `packages/web/tests/types/connection.ts`; `packages/mobile/tests/types/options.ts` is new and listed in `.fallowrc.json` `entry` like the web one. - Only `ai` was kept out of core's runtime imports. `ai-sdk-imports.test.ts` becomes `packages/e2e/tests/unit/package-imports.test.ts`: every runtime import under `packages/{e2e,web,mobile,github}/src` is relative, a `node:` builtin, a `dependencies` entry, or a peer, and an optional peer (`ai`, each `@ai-sdk/*`) loads only from the module named for it. A devDependency or sibling package import resolves on this checkout, where the workspace hoists everything, and fails the first install of the tarball. Comments and template literals are stripped first, so the scaffold text in `cli/init/engines.ts` is not read as an import. The tree passes it today. - The two `@ts-expect-error` objects for `judge: 'openai/...'` and `timeout: '30s'` now carry `targets: [{ engine }]`. Without it, #434 making `targets` required would have given each a second reason to error, and a loosened `judge` or `timeout` type would still have compiled under the directive. Probed: each line fails for its one reason (`string` is not `ModelInstance`; `string` is not `number`). What the allowlist reports when it fails: ```text e2e/src/run/steps.ts: import { chromium } from 'playwright' (playwright is neither a dependency nor a peer of e2e) e2e/src/run/steps.ts: import('ai') (ai is an optional peer of e2e; load it from agent/ai-sdk.ts only) mobile/src/tools.ts: import { tool } from 'ai' (ai is an optional peer of @e2edev/mobile; import its types only) e2e/src/run/steps.ts: import path from 'path' (path is a builtin; import it as node:path) ``` ---

title: fix(secrets): the redactor matches every spelling of a value, refuses one under 6 characters, and redacts output across writes
body:
A probe against `dist` sent `%2f`, `'`, and `\u0027` spellings of a registered secret through the redactor and they came out intact, while `docs/security.mdx` said URL-encoded forms were covered. `E2E_SECRET_PIN=7` turned every `7` in a report into `<secret:pin>`. The worker redacted stdout one `write()` at a time, so a value straddling two writes reached the reporter in halves.

- The redactor is one pattern over every value, leftmost first and longer first at a position, matching each character in any spelling a serializer gives it (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts:37`, `spellings` at `:84`). A new scheme is a line there, not a form to enumerate and dedupe. Letters and digits keep one spelling, so a case variant of a value is not the value.
- A static secret or credential password shorter than 6 characters, counted in code points, is `INVALID_CONFIG` at resolve time, and a provider returning one fails the fill with the unavailable code (`packages/e2e/src/config/secrets.ts:83`, `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:113`). Refusing, not warning: a report that skips redaction for one secret is what the invariant forbids, and no documented use needs a shorter value (a TOTP is 6 digits). Hence `minor`: a config with a 5-character password loaded before this.
- The worker redacts stdout and stderr through a `StreamRedactor` that decodes bytes whole and holds back the tail a later write could complete into a value: the longest spelling less one character, or only the unfinished line, moved back to the start of the one occurrence the pass would rewrite across it, so what is held stays under two spellings and the pieces redact to what the whole does (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts:84`, `SecretLedger.holdFrom` at `redact.ts:178`). Held text is attributed to the pair that wrote it and leaves before the next `pair-start`, the `result`, and `unit-done`.
- The in-process path (`rawConfig`, in-memory tests) keeps no output hook: test code and the reporter share one `process.stdout` there, and a patched `write` would capture the reporter's own live window. `docs/security.mdx` names the exception, and lists base64, another normalization form, and a value spread over several nodes as out of scope.
- Four test fixtures used `'pw'` or `'v'` as filler passwords; lengthened.
- `holdFrom` also holds back a marker cut short at the end of a write (`<`, `<s`, ... `<secret:` and name characters with no `>` yet), bounded by the longest known marker less one character, so `write('<secret:api'); write('Key>')` reaches the reporter as one `<secret:apiKey>` (`unfinishedMarkerBefore` at `redact.ts:136`). The marker-preserving cut itself, which leaves an existing `<secret:name>` marker unrewritten, comes from #429; the two compose: this hold keeps a marker whole across writes, #429 keeps a whole marker unrewritten.

| Input | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `q=a%2fb%20c` | passes through | `q=<secret:path>` |
| `it's <ok>`, `it's <ok>` | passes through | `<secret:quoted>` |
| `{"v":"it\u0027s \u003cok\u003e"}` | passes through | `{"v":"<secret:quoted>"}` |
| `E2E_SECRET_PIN=7` | every `7` in the report becomes `<secret:pin>` | `INVALID_CONFIG: secret "pin" must be at least 6 characters (code points), not 1` |
| `write('token sk_live_gen'); write('eric_4242\n')` | `token sk_live_gen` and `eric_4242` reach the reporter | `token <secret:stripe-key>` |
