chore: integration check of #423 to #461, do not merge
body:
A merged build of the 39 review PRs so CI and live runs verify them together; this branch will be closed, never merged.

## Merged

#423, #424, #425, #426, #427, #428, #429, #430, #431, #432, #433, #434, #435, #436, #437, #438, #439, #440, #441, #442, #443, #444, #445, #446, #447, #448, #449, #450, #451, #452, #453, #454, #455, #456, #457, #458, #459, #460, #461

Each merged with `--no-ff` in numeric order onto `main` at b84fefb5. Four follow-up commits on top reconcile what only shows once the branches meet; none changes a PR branch.

## Conflicts

Every conflict was two additive changes to one region; both intents are kept unless noted.

- `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` (#429 vs #436): #429's `locate` and `screenshot` sentences plus #436's `type_at`, `press_at`, `select_at` rows. The two disagreed on a fact: #436 says the point tools "leave the catalog" after a secret fill, #429 says they "stay and answer PIXEL_TAINTED". The code (`mcp/session.ts` builds the catalog once at `open_session`; `mcp-server.test.ts` calls `screenshot` after `type_secret` and expects `PIXEL_TAINTED`) agrees with #429, so its wording stands, extended to all four point tools. `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` auto-merged with #436's sentence and was reworded to match.
- `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` (#427 vs #436): #427's Android password `textbox` and editable-type sentences, #436's `secondaryTap` in the not-declared list.
- `packages/web/src/surface.ts` `validateFrames` (#425 vs #445): #445's body, which already chains `scope.frameLocator` as #425 does and returns the outermost hidden boundary; #425's JSDoc sentence on why `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` is retryable folded in.
- `docs/security.mdx`, redactor paragraph (#429, #446, #460): #460's character-by-character matcher sentence, #429's never-rewrites-a-marker sentence, #446's step-label and final-pass sentences, then #460's two new paragraphs. Artifacts table: `ai-trace.json` row from #446, `sessions/<runId>/` row from #442. "Where redaction stops": #460's three new bullets, then #461's rewritten trace bullet and new download bullet.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts` `sanitizePathSegment` (#423 vs #448): #448's dot-only guard first, then #423's cap and digest.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/artifact-segment.test.ts` (add/add, #423 vs #448): one file, all four cases.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts` `failTarget` (#431 vs #455): #455's `if (!state.failed)` guard around the one-time run error, then #431's `skipQueues` helper.
- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-policy.test.ts` (#434, #446, #456, #458): imports unioned (`SdkLanguageModel` from #456's `agent/ai-sdk.ts`, #434's `StepExecutor`, #458's `nodeIdFor`); the three appended `describe` blocks (#446, #434, #458) all kept.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/agent-config.test.ts` (#434 vs #456): import union.
- `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts` (#439, #445, #457): imports unioned (#457's `compareText`, `TextComparison`, `isValueControl` replace `containsText`; #439's `describeNegationTimeout` kept); #457's `readField`/`printField` beside #445's `observedState` JSDoc.
- `packages/e2e/src/agent/loop-guards.ts` `extractToolResults` (#440 vs #458): #458's `GuardToolResult` shape; an `error-text` result (SDK refusal) is failed by construction, every other output goes through #440's `toolResultTexts`, so a screenshot-bearing result still counts. `tests/unit/loop-guards.test.ts`: #440's hoisted helpers, #458's title and refusal fixtures, #440's screenshot case adapted to the new shape.
- `packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts` (#429, #446, #460): #460's matcher is the base. Its single `replace` pass never re-reads what it writes, but a second pass over `<secret:apiKey>` with `{ apiKey: 'api' }` still matches `api` inside the marker, so #429's marker-cutting stays as a wrapper around #460's rewrite; #429's per-form `encodedForms`/`replaceForm` path is what #460 supersedes and is the only code dropped; #429's `markers` tests unchanged. #446's `redactLeaves` appended.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts` (#446, #455, #460): import union; in `emit`, #460's `flushOutput()` guard runs first, then #446's redacting `switch`; #455's `strayRejection` handler untouched.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/secret-ledger.test.ts` (#429 vs #460): import union, both appended `describe` blocks kept.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts` import (#455 vs #461): union.
- `packages/e2e/tests/helpers/fixture-app.ts` `startFixtureApp` (#438 vs #461): #461's `FixtureAppOptions` with #438's `todos` set; routes `/planted`, `/todos`, `/api/todos`.
- `.changeset/ship-schemas.md` (#437): named `agent-tool-v1`, which #454 deletes; the word dropped in the #454 merge commit.

## Follow-up commits

- `fix(agent)`: `act.ts` imported `recordPolicyEvent` twice after #434 and #446 auto-merged; tsc refused the duplicate.
- `test`: #430's Copilot `LOGIN_REQUIRED` case uses the one-arg constructor #452 left, through `useVendor`; #459's `judge` and `timeout` `@ts-expect-error` objects carry `targets` (required since #434) so each errors for one reason; one loop-guards case mixing a screenshot-bearing failure (#440), an SDK refusal (#458), and a text failure.
- `test(engines)`: #461 made `registerSecret` required on `EngineAttemptContext`; the attempt literals in tests from #425, #426, #443, #445 were written against the old shape and failed typecheck only once merged together.

## Results

Each command run on its own, exit code read directly, never through a pipe. Node v26.4.0, macOS arm64, pnpm 12.3.4.

- `pnpm run build`: exit 1 on the first try (`act.ts` duplicate `recordPolicyEvent` import, a merge artifact, fixed in a follow-up commit), then exit 0.
- `pnpm check`: exit 1 on the first try (four test literals missing `registerSecret`, see follow-up commits), then exit 0. Lint clean; fallow reports its advisory class-member rule only; typecheck, error-code check, peer-range check, and docs check pass.
- `pnpm --filter e2e run test`: exit 1. Test files 181 passed, 2 failed (183). Tests 2182 passed, 1 failed, 5 skipped (2188). Both failures analysed below; neither is a merge error.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/web run test`: exit 0. 34 files, 308 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/mobile run test`: exit 0. 11 files passed, 1 skipped (no simulator); 130 tests passed, 6 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/github run test`: exit 0. 3 files, 20 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:testbed`: exit 0. 10 files, 41 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: exit 0. 6 files, 11 tests passed.

### Failure A: `tests/unit/worker-handle.test.ts` > "drops messages to a worker whose channel closed ahead of its process" (30 s timeout)

#455's test; the test file and `src/run/worker/handle.ts` are byte-identical to #455's branch, and #455 is the only PR touching either. It reproduces in isolation, and with a fork harness outside vitest: the merged worker entry hangs, #455's own entry over the merged graph hangs, an empty `.ts` child with no e2e code at all hangs, an empty `.mjs` child exits at 1 s as intended. Mechanism, from a diagnostic preload writing to fd 2: `NODE_OPTIONS=--import <sever-channel preload>` is inherited by tsx's module-customization hooks thread; there `process.disconnect` is not a function, the thread's fatal handler calls the preload-neutered `process.exit`, and the main thread stays blocked in synchronous module resolution, so its 1 s real `exit(0)` never fires. Any `.ts` entry needs the hooks thread, and the unit test imports `handle.ts` from `src/`, so `resolveEntry()` picks `entry.ts` plus tsx. Environment-dependent: #455's own `test (22)` job (Linux, Node 22) passes; `test (24)` and `test (26)` were still pending. Not a merge error, not a cross-PR interaction; left as is. The hung child and its vitest fork outlive the run ("Timeout terminating forks worker") and were killed by hand.

### Failure B: `tests/integration/agent-ai-trace.test.ts` > "--ai-trace with the ledger as it stands when the files are written" (beforeAll ENOENT on `.e2e/ai-trace.json`, 4 tests skipped)

Cross-PR interaction, #446 x #460. #446's fixture declares `credentials.brace.password = '{'` on purpose (a secret that is JSON punctuation). #460 adds `MIN_SECRET_LENGTH = 6` code points: `isSecretValue('{')` is false and the config is refused with `INVALID_CONFIG` ("must be at least 6 characters (code points), not 1"), confirmed against the built `dist/config/secrets.js`; nothing runs, no trace or report is written, `readFileSync` in `beforeAll` throws. Reproduces in isolation (1 file failed, 6 passed, 4 skipped). Fix belongs in #446 (a punctuation-only password of 6+ code points, or a provider function, which #460 exempts) or in #460 (an allowance). Not patched here. No other merged test declares a static secret under 6 characters apart from #460's own negative cases.

## Observations

- Marker split across two `StreamRedactor` chunks (`<secret:api` | `Key>`): `holdFrom` measures value occurrences only, so the value inside a split marker could be rewritten. Only reachable if already-redacted text streams through the worker's stdout hook in pieces; no test exercises it. Noted for #429 and #460, not fixed here.


## Second pass (same day)

Every PR branch was re-merged in the same order after its follow-up commits landed; 15 branches had nothing new and merged as no-ops. Behaviour fixes now in: #446's brace secret is seven code points (clears the #446 x #460 failure below), #455 guards its severed-channel preload with `isMainThread` (clears the `worker-handle` hang), #441 restores the node-swipe quarter share, #426 validates `app` at `mobile()`, #434 asserts exit code 2 for `vision` under a custom executor, #454 records rejected judgment answers as `schema` events.

### Conflicts

Both intents kept unless noted.

- `.changeset/ship-schemas.md` (#437 vs my first-pass amend): #437 now says "every `schema/*.schema.json`", the same intent as my dropped `agent-tool-v1`; took #437's wording.
- `tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` (#439 vs #445; then #451 vs #425/#433/#439/#445): appended `it` and `test` blocks at the same spots, each side's last block closed before the other begins; the passing-titles list keeps both new titles.
- `tests/integration/engine-contract.test.ts` (#442 vs #423; #445 vs #442): import unions.
- `tests/integration/agent-policy.test.ts` (#446 vs #434/#456/#458): #446's `defineEngine`/`LOCATOR_ACTION_KINDS`/`RunEvent` imports kept; its stale `SdkLanguageModel` import from `config/agent.ts` dropped, #456 already provides it from `agent/ai-sdk.ts`; its new `describe` appended after #458's.
- `tests/integration/run-events.test.ts` (#446 vs #460), `tests/unit/artifact-segment.test.ts` (#448 vs #423), `tests/integration/agent-act-pixel-tools.test.ts` (#449 vs #440, three regions): appended blocks, first side closed before the second.
- `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` (#452 vs #434/#456/#459; then #459 vs #452): #452's value imports of `chatgpt`/`copilot`/`grok` and its `@ts-expect-error` imports with HEAD's wider `LanguageModelV2, V3, V4` type import; both appended assertion groups kept. #459's own `targets` fix auto-merged onto mine.
- `docs/reference/errors.mdx` (#458 vs #443/#434): #458's expanded `POLICY_DENIED` rows, HEAD's `APP_UNREACHABLE` row with #443's iOS-runner sentence, #434's "or an executor's `attachScreenshot`" folded into the second row.
- `src/internal/redact.ts` (#460 vs my first-pass resolution): #460's second pass adds `MARKER_OPEN`, `maxMarkerLength`, and `unfinishedMarkerBefore` in `holdFrom` (the partial-marker hold I flagged); it leaves `redact` as a plain replace, so my `known`-split wrapper for #429's idempotence stays and the two complement each other.
- Auto-merged and read: `loop-guards.ts` keeps #458's `GuardToolResult` with `error-text` failed and #440's point-verb `failed:` regex; `entry.ts` carries #446's `runErrors: redactLeaves(...)` inside the merged `emit` switch; `useVendor` (#430 vs #452) merged to one copy.

### Follow-up commit

- `test(mcp)`: #458's second-pass `mcp-tools.test.ts` builds a session catalog without `redact`, which #429 made required on `CatalogOptions`; the double passes a pass-through. Same shape as the first pass's `registerSecret` fix. All three first-pass follow-ups survived the re-merge.

### Results

Each command on its own, exit code read directly. Same machine as pass one (Node v26.4.0, macOS arm64, pnpm 12.3.4).

- `pnpm run build`: exit 0 first time.
- `pnpm check`: exit 1 on the first try (the `mcp-tools.test.ts` `redact` literal, see follow-up commit), then exit 0. Web, mobile, and github typechecks also run alone: all exit 0. Fallow reports its advisory class-member rule only.
- `pnpm --filter e2e run test`, first run: exit 1. Files 189 passed, 1 failed (190). Tests 2310 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (2312). The one failure is #440's second-pass loop-guards case asserting the pre-#458 `string[]` shape (adapted in the follow-up commit below, file rerun 14/14). No fork-termination timeout and no failed suite this time: #455's `isMainThread` guard and #446's seven-code-point secret cleared both first-pass failures.
- `pnpm --filter e2e run test`, rerun on the committed tree: exit 0. Files 190 passed (190). Tests 2311 passed, 1 skipped (2312).
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/web run test`: exit 0. 34 files, 316 tests.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/mobile run test`: exit 0. 11 files passed, 1 skipped (no simulator); 137 tests passed, 6 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @e2edev/github run test`: exit 0. 3 files, 21 tests.
- `pnpm test:testbed`: exit 0. 10 files, 41 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: exit 0. 6 files, 11 tests.

#455's own CI is green on Node 22, 24, and 26 with the `isMainThread` guard, which settles the first-pass note on the `worker-handle` hang as environment-only and now fixed upstream.

### Follow-up commit, second

- `test(agent)`: #440's second-pass "reads the message of a call the SDK refused" case expects `extractToolResults` to return strings; merged with #458 it returns `{ text, failed }`, so the case reads the refusal as text and marked failed, both intents kept.


## Third pass

Two regressions surfaced only under live runs of pass 2 and were fixed on their PR branches, then merged here (head `00d2330c`).

- #441 `0c194599`: the root scroll no longer passes an `amount` to agent-device. With `slow` at 0.75 the gesture started inside the sticky footer of the mobile benchmark's `sticky chrome` scenario and `scrollUntilVisible` moved nothing for 30 s (2.4 s on main). Settle options for agent-origin scrolls stay.
- #458 `a099567e`: a passed `complete_step` that carries an `errorCode` drops the code and notes it instead of being refused. `gpt-5.6-luna-fast` attaches `ACTION_FAILED` to about half of its passed verdicts; the refusal produced 12 to 19 identical retries per step and took the testbed agent suite from 15/16 to 4/16. Refused conclusion calls now count toward the failure streak so a refusal loop is bounded.
- Conflict: `packages/e2e/src/agent/loop-guards.ts` `extractToolResults` (#440 screenshot-bearing results, #458 refused calls, #458 refused conclusions). Resolved so an `error-text` result is a failure whatever the tool, the conclusion tool's own text is skipped, and every other result reads its text items. Both PRs' unit cases kept.
- Verified after the merges: `pnpm run build`, mobile package tests (137 passed), `loop-guards` and `agent-grammar-tools` units, `agent-policy` and `agent-act-pixel-tools` integration, `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit`. The full `pnpm check` and `pnpm --filter e2e run test` rerun follows the live suites.


## Verification on the third pass (`00d2330c`)

Gate: `pnpm check` 0; `pnpm --filter e2e run test` 0 (190 files, 2315 passed, 1 skipped); mobile 137 passed; web 316; github 21; testbed 41; web-benchmark 11.

Live suites, `gateway/openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast`, `--no-cache`:

| suite | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| testbed `test:agent` | 16/16, 98 calls, $0.075 | 16/16, 100 calls, $0.072 |
| web-benchmark `test:agent` | 21 + 3 planted, 90 calls | 19 + 3 planted, 2 gateway stalls (0 input tokens, 280 s aborted retry delay); both pass on rerun at 5 calls each |
| testbed dogfood | 4/4 | 4/4 |
| testbed dogfood-edge, dogfood-brain | fail by design | same outcomes |
| iOS mobile-benchmark deterministic (iPhone 17 Pro) | 19/1/1 | 20/0/1 |
| iOS mobile-benchmark agentic | 22/1/1, 171 calls, $0.20 | 19 comparable scenarios 123 calls, $0.12; the four rerun after the fixes 4/4 at baseline call counts |

Three regressions surfaced only in these live runs and are fixed on their PR branches: the node swipe stride (#441, `dcaccd65`), the root scroll amount (#441, `0c194599`), and the `complete_step` error-code refusal loop (#458, `a099567e`). One keypad step failed once on the same byte-identical screenshot and passed 3 of 3 reruns on both sides; three unanswered gateway requests between 21:41 and 21:47 UTC hit iOS and web alike and all pass on rerun.

title: test(oauth): port the Copilot 401 test to the vendor helper
body: Main fails typecheck and the unit suite on `tests/unit/oauth/copilot.test.ts`: `MemoryCredentialStore` is not imported, and `copilot()` is called with two arguments. ## What and why - #430 added the "GitHub rejects the stored token" test against `copilot(id, { store, baseURL })`. #452, branched before it, dropped that options argument and moved every constructor test onto `useVendor`, which supplies the login through `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` and routes fetch to the local server. Merged separately, main ended with one test written for a signature that no longer exists. - The test now uses `vendor(api, { 'github-copilot': ... })` and `copilot('gpt-4.1')`, the same shape as the vision test above it in the file. Assertions are unchanged: one request, `LOGIN_REQUIRED`, and the message naming `npx e2e login github-copilot`. Before: `tsc --noEmit` reports TS2304 and TS2554 at `copilot.test.ts:107-108`; vitest fails the test with `ReferenceError: MemoryCredentialStore is not defined`. After: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` pass, `tests/unit/oauth` passes (10 files, 64 tests). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: test(cli): the init test cancels with clack's own symbol
body: - `@clack/prompts` 1.8.1 (#465) types each prompt as `Promise` where 1.8.0 said `symbol`, so the init test's `Symbol('cancel')` no longer assigns to a mocked prompt's resolution and the `packages/e2e` typecheck is red on `main` since that merge (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/cli-init.test.ts:145`, `:326`). - The test now cancels with `clack.CANCEL_SYMBOL`, which the package re-exports, typed as that unique symbol so the const does not widen to `symbol`; the `isCancel` stub still recognises it, so the cancellation paths run as before. - Every PR whose CI ran after #465 fails `check` on the merge commit until this lands; #463 is the first. ---

title: test(run): the quarantine test waits on an immediate, not a zero timer
body: - `names a sink once when several of its pending promises reject` (from #444) rejects its promises from `setImmediate` callbacks and then waits with `setTimeout(resolve, 0)`. Node does not order a zero timer against the check phase, so under CI load the timer fires first, the quarantine line is not written yet, and the assertion sees an empty stderr (#455's `test (26)` run hit it). - The wait is now `setImmediate(resolve)`, queued behind the two rejections in the same phase, so it runs once they and their catch handlers have. Five local runs green; the assertion is unchanged. ---

title: feat: deterministic exercises for every verb on web and mobile, cached agentic gates, popups, closed roots, replay speed
body:
Every verb the runner exposes has a deterministic exercise on a real browser and a real device, a scripted engine drives the runner through every matcher without either, and the agentic suites gate pull requests by replaying a committed trace cache. The gaps those exercises exposed are fixed here rather than skipped: a second tab, controls inside a closed shadow root, replay speed, and a committed cache that rewrote itself on every run.

## Three tiers, all on every pull request

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph tier1[scripted engine, in pnpm test]
    S[scripted-* suites: matchers, reads, actions, polling, capabilities]
    C[trace-cache-replay + speed]
  end
  subgraph tier2[real web]
    T[testbed: 68 tests, 16 s]
    W[web-benchmark: 42 twins, 86 tests, 0 skips]
    WA[web-benchmark agentic: replays .e2e/cache]
  end
  subgraph tier3[real mobile, mobile.yml]
    I[iOS simulator: det + agentic]
    A[Android emulator: det + agentic]
  end
  F[@expo/fingerprint] --> B{cached app?}
  B -- hit --> R[repack JS] --> I
  B -- miss --> N[native build] --> I
```

- Testbed pages `/controls`, `/scroll`, `/browser`, `/speed` cover the verbs no suite touched: `secondaryTap`, `longPress`, `scrollIntoView`, a scoped and a viewport `scrollUntilVisible` over windowed lists, `waitForURL`, `isChecked`, `filter({ has })`, viewport and raw mouse, cookies, every state matcher, the negative paths. The playground server is five page modules and a generated nav (87 lines, from 1025); the speed floor is a ratio against a measured read cost.
- One deterministic twin per web-benchmark scenario (36 new files). `tests/support.ts` holds the shared helpers once (read a code off the page, the centre of a node, the error a step throws, the element beside a visible label); a planted-bug scenario asserts what the page truly shows, bug named in the title.
- `tests/helpers/scripted-engine.ts` is a configuration of `fake-engine.ts` over a reference locator resolver; five focused suites assert every matcher, `.not`, list form, read, dispatch payload, query kind and error code through the real runner. One `screenOver` builds every unit-test screen.
- `e2e/engine` exports `resolveExpression`, the reference locator semantics over a semantic tree (innermost match for `text` and `label`, scopes, filters, index), so an engine over a whole tree calls it instead of carrying a copy.
- Trace cache: record-and-replay tests for relocation by position, anonymous twins, placeholder and row; `unique()` in a value, a path segment, an encoded query; volatile anchors; start-path and route identity; a hand-off on a renamed control; `--repeat-each`. Seven Chromium runs; the re-keying, truncation, `--no-cache` and typed-value cases live in the unit and executor suites that already owned them. The fixture app is a routes table over six page modules (125 lines, from 1067).
- Mobile: a Control Inventory scenario and `controls` and `device-fixture` suites exercise every verb, read, matcher, refusal and `device` method on the benchmark app; the flows gained state matchers. The first iOS run of those suites found twelve defects; the engine-side ones are landing as follow-up commits on this branch (see below), the upstream ones stay as declared skips.
- `.github/workflows/mobile.yml`: iOS on `blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26`, Android emulator on x64 Blacksmith (KVM). One composite action (`.github/actions/expo-app`) keys the Expo build by `@expo/fingerprint`, keeps it in the actions cache, repacks the JS with `@expo/repack-app` on a hit and falls back to a native build; one `scripts/ci-run.sh` runs the deterministic suite and then the agentic one when the key is present, for this repository's branches.
- `packages/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` is committed. CI is read-only, so a step with no recording calls the model; a changed scenario is re-recorded locally in the same pull request. The mobile entries follow once the iOS fixes land; until then the Android side spends model calls on a miss.

## Agentic gate cost, web benchmark

| Run | Wall time | Model calls | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| record (first run) | 240 s | 84 | $0.042 |
| replay | 82 s | 21 | $0.004 |

Two consecutive replays leave every committed entry byte-identical. The six live steps per replay are by design: three planted-bug judgments (a failing judgment never records), one act that types a value it read off the screen and two that read a code (`step.cache.derived` names the rule: `minted-token`, `whole-node`, `pixels`).

## Replay speed

| Two-action step | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deterministic twin | 67 ms | 67 ms |
| replay | 417 ms | 154 ms |

Replay took two settled captures it did not need (a second look at the screen the start capture had just settled, and a re-capture of the end screen for anchors it already held). How far the screen settles after each action kind is one exhaustive `SETTLE_AFTER` table read by both the live loop and the replay. A step the cache replayed whole never rewrites its entry, and a re-recording of the same flow (a live run that typed a value read off the screen) is not written when only the summary and the measured end wait differ, so a committed cache stays clean across local runs. A typed value counts as read off the screen only when it equals a node's whole name or text or is a digit-bearing token the screen shows as a word; a plain word the model composed replays.

## Engine changes

```ts
const popup = await web.waitForPopup(() => screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Open terms' }).tap());
await expect(web).toHaveURL(/terms/);          // screen, web, and expect(web) follow the popup
await popup.close();                           // back to the opener

await screen.getByRole('feed').scrollUntilVisible(row);            // the feed pages, not the viewport
await screen.getByPlaceholder('Access code').fill(code);          // inside a closed shadow root
const file = await web.waitForDownload(() => download.tap());
await screen.getByLabel('Import').setInputFiles(file.absolutePath);
```

- `@e2edev/web`: a page stack inside the session state owns the active page; `waitForPopup` pushes the new tab (observation, screenshots, dialogs, video segment and CDP recovery target follow it), `close()` or the app closing it unwinds to the opener, out-of-order nested closes and a transport drop mid-popup recover. `Dialog.type`. Locators resolve inside closed shadow roots through an `e2e-roots=` selector engine that hands Playwright's own role, text, label and test-id engines every tracked root, with a zero-walk fast path on pages without closed roots and the six query kinds declared in one candidates table. `read-node.ts` is 153 lines (from 1188): the closed-root scripts live in `closed-shadow.ts`, the in-page reader in `in-page/read-semantics.ts`. `waitForDownload` returns `absolutePath`.
- `e2e`: `scrollUntilVisible` on a locator swipes that node, takes `momentum`, rejects unknown options; `filter({ hasText })` documented as the substring match it is.
- `@e2edev/mobile`: in progress on this branch: `getByLabel` ambiguous on every React Native text field (the label echoes up the host chain), an unlabeled field's value dropped when it equals its label, React Native roles that iOS has no trait for (checkbox, radio, tab, switch) carried in the value text and not projected, `closeApp` leaving the app running, a lost session reported as `ENGINE_FAILURE` instead of `APP_NOT_OPEN`, `foregroundApp` reading the session rather than the device.

## Skips that remain, each an upstream limit

- agent-device delivers a double tap as one tap on iOS (two presses arrive 400 ms apart, outside a 300 ms window).
- No focused flag on iOS text fields even with the keyboard up, so `toBeFocused` cannot pass on a device.
- The agent-device snapshot carries no placeholder or attributes, so `getByPlaceholder`, `getAttribute` and `toHaveAttribute` match nothing on a device (documented in the mobile guide).
- React Native flattens plain Views on iOS, so `filter({ has })` and scopes into a View with only a test id match nothing; ScrollView, TextInput and Text hosts nest.

## Follow-ups

- `getByText` exact compares full textContent while the tree prints the node's own text; `toHaveText` joins inline children with a space. Both trip Playwright users; docs or reader work.
- No console or pageerror API (`web.onConsole`); no CSS-content matcher; `toHaveValue` has no list form.
- An agent verb to switch tabs; `act` sees whichever page is active.
- A minor release of `e2e` re-keys every committed cache entry; re-record in the release pull request.

title: feat(e2e): scrollUntilVisible on a locator swipes that node, takes a momentum, and rejects unknown options
body: - `screen.scrollUntilVisible` on a locator swipes that node, so a feed or a table that is its own scroll container pages without the pointer having to hover it first; on `screen` the viewport scrolls as before. - `momentum` option, the swipe grammar's `'none' | 'slow' | 'fast'`, `'slow'` by default. An option the method does not take is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, like every other verb's. - `options.timeout` bounds the whole scroll. Each swipe used to get `config.actionTimeout` of its own, so a slow one could outlive the scroll by that much; the swipes now run under the scroll's deadline, and one it cuts short is the scroll's `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, with the engine error as its cause. - A locator made by another target's screen, or by an earlier attempt's, is `INVALID_LOCATOR` before any step: its expression would resolve through the wrong engine. `scrollUntilVisible`, `dragTo`, and `filter({ has })` share the check. ```ts await screen.getByRole('feed').scrollUntilVisible(row); await table.scrollUntilVisible(claim, { timeout: 240_000 }); ``` - Unit tests cover the scoped swipe, the direction, the momentum, a hidden target, the deadline (a hung swipe fails within the scroll timeout, on `screen` and on a locator), the step label, the refused option, and the same-screen rule on all three methods. Docs in the screen reference; changeset `e2e` minor. ---

title: test: deterministic exercises for every web verb in the testbed and one twin per web-benchmark scenario
body: Stacked on `oskar/scroll-until-visible-scoped` (the pane and infinite-scroll tests use the scoped scroll). Every verb the runner exposes gets a deterministic exercise on a real browser, so a red agentic run is the model, not the tools. | Suite | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | testbed | 41 tests, 10 pages | 68 tests, 14 pages, 16 s | | web-benchmark deterministic twins | 5 of 41 scenarios | 38 of 41 (the other three land with their engine fixes) | - Testbed pages `/controls`, `/scroll`, `/browser`, `/speed`, `/about` cover what no suite touched: `secondaryTap`, `longPress`, `scrollIntoView`, a scoped and a viewport `scrollUntilVisible` over windowed lists, `waitForURL`, `isChecked`, `filter({ has })`, viewport and raw mouse, cookies, every state matcher, and the negative paths (`LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_LOCATOR`). - The playground server is five page modules and a generated nav (`app/server.mjs` 1025 lines to 87); the speed suite pins a per-action floor as a ratio against a measured read cost. - One twin per web-benchmark scenario under `tests/.e2e.ts`, locators and `expect` only. `tests/support.ts` holds the shared helpers once (read a code off the page, the centre of a node, the error a step throws, the element beside a visible label); `tests/canvas.ts` the pixel reads. A planted-bug scenario asserts what the page truly shows, bug named in the title. - The twins for new-tab-flow, shadow-dom-form, and file-round-trip land with `waitForPopup`, closed-root locators, and `absolutePath` in the next pull requests of the stack. ---

title: feat(web): waitForPopup follows a new tab, dialogs carry their type, downloads report their absolute path
body: Stacked on `oskar/det-gates-web`. ```ts const popup = await web.waitForPopup(() => screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Open terms' }).tap()); await expect(web).toHaveURL(/terms/); // screen, web, and expect(web) follow the popup await popup.close(); // back to the opener const file = await web.waitForDownload(() => screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Export' }).tap()); await screen.getByLabel('Import').setInputFiles(file.absolutePath); ``` - A page stack inside the session state owns the active page. `waitForPopup` pushes the tab the trigger opened; observation, screenshots, dialog handlers, the video segment, and the CDP recovery target follow it. `close()`, or the app closing the tab, unwinds to the opener; out-of-order nested closes and a transport drop mid-popup recover. A tab that opens with no wait pending is left alone. - `Dialog.type` (`alert | confirm | prompt | beforeunload`) so a handler routes on the kind, not the message text. - `waitForDownload` resolves with `absolutePath` beside `path`, so a downloaded file goes straight back into `setInputFiles`. - Tests: `popup.test.ts` (strict and out-of-order nesting, a self-closing popup, a redirecting popup, video segments), recovery with a popup active, dialog kinds, the core kitchen sink. Web-benchmark twins `new-tab-flow` and `file-round-trip` land here. Docs: web reference, browser guide, migrate tables, security page. Changesets: `@e2edev/web` minor, patch. ---

title: fix(web): locators resolve inside closed shadow roots the reader observes
body: The observation has pierced closed shadow roots for a while, so a failure printed nodes no `screen` query could reach. - An `e2e-roots=` selector engine hands Playwright's own role, text, label, and test-id engines every closed root the page attached under the query root, so each element matches exactly once and the matching rules inside a root are the ones outside it. A page without closed roots pays nothing: the init script counts attached roots and the engine returns the query root alone at zero. - The six query kinds declare their candidates in one table in `locators.ts`; the exact-label path is no longer a second projection. - `read-node.ts` is 153 lines (from 1188): the closed-root scripts live in `closed-shadow.ts`, the in-page reader in `in-page/read-semantics.ts`. - Limits, documented: `web.locator(css)`, `frameLocator`, and `filter({ hasText })` keep Playwright's reach and stop at a closed root; `has` crosses it. Matches outside closed roots come first, then each root's; a test pins that order against the reader's. - Tests: `closed-shadow-locators.test.ts` (every query kind inside a root, nesting both ways, the visible flag, index, scope, `has`), the flipped lifecycle assertion, the engine source unit tests. The `shadow-dom-form` twin lands here, and the agentic scenario loses a gap that was already stale. Changeset `@e2edev/web` patch. - Two reads the reader stopped at the document, from review: an `aria-labelledby` id now resolves in the control's own tree root, so an exact `getByLabel` finds a labelled-by control inside an open or closed root and the observed tree names it; focus follows each root's active element through open roots and the recorded closed ones, so `toBeFocused` holds for a control inside a shadow root. Covered on `/closed-form` and in the reader names test with a same-id decoy in the light DOM. ---

title: feat(engine): resolveExpression is the reference locator semantics, and a scripted engine drives the runner through every matcher
body: Stacked on `oskar/web-closed-roots`. - `e2e/engine` exports `resolveExpression(expression, nodes, { selector? })`, the reference locator semantics over a semantic tree: query kinds, states, level, the visible flag, scopes as strict descendants, `hasText` and `has`, `first`/`last`/`nth`, with `text` and `label` answering the innermost match when a container echoes a descendant's text. An engine whose tree is the whole truth calls it instead of carrying a copy (the device engine adopts it next). Changeset `e2e` minor. - The scripted in-memory engine (`tests/helpers/scripted-engine.ts`) is a configuration of the instrumented `fake-engine.ts` over that resolver: a mutable scene, per-attempt timers, every action and pointer kind, keyboard, session hooks, stale and failing actions, typed call records. - Five suites drive the real runner through it in seconds: `scripted-matchers` (every matcher, `.not`, list forms, failure codes and messages), `scripted-reads` (every read, strictness, the secure-field refusal), `scripted-actions` (every dispatch payload, pointer actions, key grammar), `scripted-polling` (late nodes, growing counts, the negation grace, stale relocation, `scrollUntilVisible`), `scripted-capabilities` (every `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` path). - One `screenOver` builds every unit-test screen (`press-sequentially`, `filter-has`, `scroll-until-visible`, the screen fixture preset); `engineConfig` replaces the `as E2EConfig` casts. Unit tests for `isChecked`, `isEnabled`, `filter({ has })`, and the cache listing's truncated row. ---

title: fix(cache): replay reuses settled screens, one settle policy, entries that never churn, named derived-value reasons
body: | Two-action step | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | deterministic twin | 67 ms | 67 ms | | replay | 417 ms | 154 ms | - Replay took two settled captures it did not need: a second look at the screen the start capture had just settled, and a re-capture of the end screen for anchors it already held. Both are gone; the one settle before acting stays. - How far the screen settles after each action kind is one exhaustive `SETTLE_AFTER` table (`src/agent/settle-policy.ts`) the live loop and the replay both read, and one `SettleMode` (`raw | after-change | held-still`) threaded from replay to the observation feed, converted to a wait exactly once. - A step the cache replayed whole never rewrites its entry (staged entries are a `write | keep` union, one `switch` decides write and eviction), and a re-recording of the same flow is not written when only the summary and the measured end wait differ. Two consecutive replays of the web benchmark leave every entry byte-identical. - A typed value counts as read off the screen only when it equals a node's whole name or text, or is a digit-bearing token the screen shows as a word; a plain word the model composed replays. `step.cache.derived` names the rule (`whole-node`, `minted-token`, `date`, `pixels`) in the report and on the recorded gap; schema and fixture updated. - Tests: record-and-replay through the model path for relocation by position, anonymous twins, placeholder and row; `unique()` in a value, a path segment, an encoded query; volatile anchors; start-path and route identity; a hand-off on a renamed control; `--repeat-each`; seven Chromium runs, the rest at unit altitude. A speed test compares flow to flow and asserts replay within 3x of the deterministic twin and under the recording. The core fixture app is a routes table over six page modules (1067 lines to 125). Changeset `e2e` patch. - Rebased onto main after #478 and #479 merged. One fixture drift fixed on the way: the canvas page moved into `tests/helpers/fixture-pages/canvas.ts` from a copy older than main and had lost the tap-count repaint the pixel-tools test reads; the eight lines are back and all 15 of those tests pass. ---

title: test(web-benchmark): the agentic suite replays its committed recordings on every pull request
body: | Web benchmark agentic suite | Wall time | Model calls | Cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | record (first run) | 240 s | 84 | $0.042 | | replay | 82 s | 20 | $0.004 | - `packages/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` (19 entries, 72 KB) is committed. CI replays them read-only and calls the model only for a step with no recording, so the gate runs at deterministic speed and cost for this repository's branches; a fork's pull request has no key and is skipped as before. - Two consecutive replays leave every entry byte-identical. The six live steps are by design: three planted-bug judgments (a failing judgment never records) and three acts that type a value read off the screen. - The policy lives once in AGENTS.md ("Committed recordings"); the `.gitignore` files carry one-line pointers.
