A minor `e2e` release re-keys every entry. - Rebased onto main ahead of the cache work, at Oskar's request, so every later pull request runs against this gate. Re-recorded on main: 15 of the 20 act steps replay; five (lying-labels, iframe-form, async-states, the cart totals act, the wishlist act) still call the model here because their entries need the settled-screen replay #480 brings, which re-records them once it lands. The three planted-bug judgments spend one call each on every run; a judgment is never cached. ---

title: ci(mobile): iOS simulator and Android emulator gates for the mobile benchmark, with a Control Inventory scenario
body:
Stacked on `oskar/agentic-committed-caches`. Draft: the first iOS run of these suites found engine defects (label ambiguity on every React Native text field, an unlabeled field's value dropped, React Native roles carried in the value text, `closeApp` leaving the app running, a lost session reported as `ENGINE_FAILURE`, `foregroundApp` reading the session), which land in the next pull request; until then the iOS job shows those failures, and the Android job runs for the first time.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[@expo/fingerprint] --> B{cached app?}
  B -- hit --> R[repack JS with @expo/repack-app] --> D[deterministic suite]
  B -- miss --> N[native build] --> D
  D --> A{same repo and key?}
  A -- yes --> G[agentic suite]
```

- A Control Inventory scenario (plain controls, every state exposed) plus `controls` and `device-fixture` suites exercise every verb, read, matcher, refusal, and `device` method on a device; the flows gained state matchers.
- `mobile.yml`: iOS on `blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26`, Android emulator on x64 Blacksmith with KVM. `.github/actions/expo-app` keys the Expo build by its native fingerprint, keeps it in the actions cache, repacks the JS on a hit, falls back to a native build. `scripts/ci-run.sh` runs the deterministic suite and then the agentic one when the key is present (the emulator runner executes each script line separately, so the guard lives in the script). The booted simulator is handed to the config as `device`.
- Skips that remain, each an upstream limit: agent-device delivers a double tap as one tap on iOS; no focused flag on iOS text fields; the snapshot carries no placeholder or attributes, so `getByPlaceholder`, `getAttribute`, and `toHaveAttribute` match nothing on a device; React Native flattens plain Views, so `filter({ has })` into a View with only a test id matches nothing.

title: fix(init): the scaffolded config and the docs name the Vercel OIDC token gateway() accepts without a key
body:
## What and why

- `gateway()` from `ai` already authenticates with a Vercel OIDC token when `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is unset. `ai` re-exports `createGateway` from `@ai-sdk/gateway`, whose `getGatewayAuthToken` reads the key and otherwise calls `@vercel/oidc`. Nothing in e2e said so. The scaffolded config comment, the models, environment, config reference, and quickstart pages, and the agent skill all named the key as the only credential.
- The rule is stated once, in a new "Vercel OIDC instead of a key" section on the models page. Every other page and the skill say "or a Vercel OIDC token" and point there. The first draft restated the full rule in five places and had already drifted between them, so the review cut those to pointers.
- No runner code learns about OIDC. Core stays gateway-agnostic, and `credentialHint` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts` keeps its provider-neutral text.
- `ai`'s `wrapGatewayError` (`node_modules/ai/dist/index.js`, `wrapGatewayError`) replaces every gateway auth failure with a generic message that names only `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and drops the cause, so an OIDC problem never says OIDC. The models page and the skill's `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` row say what to check instead: the Vercel CLI login and `.vercel/project.json`.
- Testbed's dogfood-brain executor calls `createGateway()` instead of `createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY ?? '' })`. Same behavior, since an empty string is falsy in the gateway's key check, but it no longer reads as if the key were required.
- Checked with the built CLI from the testbed, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` unset, a `.vercel/project.json` in the project dir: an `agent.assert` passed on one gateway call from the worker, on a token the gateway minted and cached. Without the link file the same test fails `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with the SDK's generic key message, which is what the models page now says to expect.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[gateway model call] --> B{AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY set?}
  B -- yes --> C[api-key]
  B -- no --> D{valid VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN?}
  D -- yes --> E[oidc]
  D -- no --> F[mint for .vercel/project.json with the Vercel CLI login]
  F --> E
```

Scaffolded `e2e.config.ts`, before and after:

```ts
// The Vercel AI Gateway serves the model id and reads AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.
// The Vercel AI Gateway serves the model id and reads AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, or the OIDC token of a linked Vercel project.
```

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

title: fix(agent): an operation that times out within a poll tick of the step deadline is STEP_TIMEOUT
body: - `agent.waitFor` on a page that never changes polls the tree until its deadline, and the last observation gets the deadline's remaining time as its budget. Its timer and the deadline mark one instant on two clocks: the timer runs on the event loop's clock, which lags `Date.now()` under load, so it fired first, `deadline.expired()` still read false a few milliseconds short, and the engine's `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` surfaced as `ACTION_FAILED` "operation timed out" instead of `STEP_TIMEOUT` with the last judgment. `spends one judgment while the page it is waiting on does not change` flaked this way on the Node 22 job of #475, and on 2026-09-22 on an unrelated pull request. - `checkStepClock` reads an operation timeout within one poll tick of the deadline as the deadline reached; one with time to spare keeps its code, so a capture that fails on its own still hands off to the semantic fallback. Action failures go through the same check, so an action cut by the deadline reads the same way. A first cut keyed on whether the operation's budget was shorter than the action timeout and broke the fallback hand-off test, whose step timeout is 1.5 s: every operation there is shorter than the action timeout. - Unit tests: the clock check on an operation timeout with a few milliseconds left, on one with seconds left, and on another failure near the deadline. The errors reference names the case; changeset `e2e` patch. ---

title: agent: the act grammar exposes 5 of the 16 engine actions; hover, tap variants, drag, scroll-to, back, upload, tabs are missing
body:
The engine contract has 16 node actions. The web engine declares all 16, the mobile engine 12. The act grammar maps five of them (`tap`, `fill`, `press`, `selectOption`, `swipe`) plus keyboard input, a coordinate tap, and `navigate`. Everything else exists for tests but not for the model.

Evidence: the web-benchmark `hover-menu` scenario. Its menus open on `onMouseEnter` only. The recording that passes is three taps, which work because a click moves the pointer onto the element first. In the run on #475 the model believed the page's "hover only" hint, saw no hover tool, and concluded `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`. Whether the test passes depends on the model's reasoning, not on the tools.

| Engine action | Web | Mobile | Test API | Agent | What it costs the agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hover | yes | yes | `hover()` | no | menus, tooltips, hover-revealed controls |
| doubleTap, longPress, secondaryTap | yes | double + long | `doubleTap()`, `longPress()`, `secondaryTap()` | no | context menus, long-press menus, double-click to edit |
| dragTo | yes | yes | `dragTo()` | no | reorder, sliders, kanban, drag-select |
| scrollIntoView | yes | no | `scrollIntoView()` | no | reaching a named node is repeated blind swipes: infinite-scroll spent 7 model calls, sticky-chrome 4 |
| setInputFiles | yes | no | `setInputFiles()` | no | any upload flow is unreachable |
| check, uncheck | yes | yes | `check()`, `uncheck()` | tap only | a re-issued tap flips state instead of asserting it |
| back | yes | yes | `app.back()`, `device.back()` | no | any flow that has to return |
| popup, tab switch | no (#477 closed) | n/a | none | no | a new tab is invisible to the model |
| home, openLink | n/a | yes | `device.home()`, `device.openLink()` | no | deep links and app switching |

The agent has today: `tap`, `type`, `typeSecret`, `press`, `select`, `scroll`, `navigate`, `tap_at`, `typeText`, `pressKey`, `dismissKeyboard`, `screenshot`, `observe`, `complete_step`; on mobile also `open_app`, `swipe`, `alert`.

Proposed order, one pull request each, all on one pattern: a grammar verb in `VERBS_BY_ACTION` (`packages/e2e/src/engine/session.ts`) so only an engine that declares the action offers the verb, the tool schema and description, dispatch, trace-cache recording, docs and the skill reference, a testbed exercise, a benchmark scenario.

1. `hover`, plus a coordinate hover on web.
2. tap variants: double, long, secondary, as one option on the tap tool.
3. drag from one node to another.
4. scroll to a named node instead of blind swipe loops.
5. `back`; on mobile also `home` and `openLink`.
6. file upload under the project-root policy the test API already enforces.
7. tab switching, once the popup design (see the popups issue) is settled.

title: web: following a popup or new tab, dialog kinds, download paths for setInputFiles (design open, #477 closed)
body:
PR #477 built `web.waitForPopup`, `Dialog.type`, and `waitForDownload().absolutePath` on a page stack inside the web engine's session state. It was closed unmerged on 2026-09-23: the page-stack shape is not settled. The branch `oskar/web-popups-downloads` is kept for reference.

What still has no answer in the runner:

- A link or button that opens a new tab. The test cannot follow it, assert on it, or close it; the agent cannot either (nothing in the act grammar names a tab).
- A native dialog handler that has to route on the kind of dialog (alert, confirm, prompt, beforeunload) rather than on message text.
- A download that goes straight back into `setInputFiles`: `waitForDownload` returns a path relative to the artifacts directory.

Deterministic twins waiting on it in the web benchmark: `new-tab-flow`, `file-round-trip`.

Open questions before a second attempt:

- Where the active page lives: a stack the engine owns and every fixture follows implicitly (what #477 did), or explicit page handles the test passes to `screen`/`expect`, closer to Playwright's `Page`.
- Whether the agent follows a popup on its own (a new tab becomes the observed page) or needs a `switch_tab` verb; see https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/486.
- What `close()` on a popup unwinds to when tabs close out of order, and how video segments and CDP recovery follow the active page. Devin's review of #477 found three races there: video transitions during a self-closing popup, a popup's `url` after stack compaction, and a click whose only effect is closing its own page.

title: feat!: the app under test is declared on its target, engines keep only url, identity, environment
body: First of three: this moves the app declaration to the target and shrinks the engine's to the defaults it can know. Run-level `services` and a run-wide port view follow in stacked PRs. - `Target.app` carries `url`, `environment`, `identity`, `command`, `readyUrl`, `services`. Every field overrides the engine's default; the processes are the target's alone (`packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts`, `mergeAppDeclaration`). - `EngineAppDeclaration` is `url`, `environment`, `identity`. An engine declaring `command`, `readyUrl`, or `services` is `INVALID_CONFIG` at `defineEngine`; `web()` rejects them with a pointer at the target. - A target `url` on an engine that declares none is `INVALID_CONFIG`: `explore` and `app.open()` navigate whenever `base` is set, and a device engine cannot open an address. Metro for a debug build is probed with `readyUrl`; a release build has no `command`. - The config digest records the merged declaration once, so a URL on the engine or on the target digests alike, with command and service env values reduced to names either way (a run-level `DATABASE_URL` never enters the digest). - Foreign-key hints flip: `webServer`, a target-level `url` or `command`, point at `app`. The `e2e init` preset, testbed and web-benchmark configs, docs, and the skill follow. ```ts targets: [ { name: 'web', engine: web({ url: 'http://localhost:8081' }) }, { name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios', app: 'dev.example.app' }), app: { command: { executable: 'npx', args: ['expo', 'start'] }, readyUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8081/status', }, }, ], ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR E[engine.app: url, identity, environment] --> M[merge: target over engine] T[target.app: + command, readyUrl, services] --> M M --> R[resolveTargetApp] R --> P[processes, ports] R --> C[cache and session identity] R --> D[config digest, env stripped] ``` Why: the engine was the only place config could carry a process, so `web()` grew `command` and `mobile()` had no way to start Metro at all, and a web plus native Expo suite had nowhere to put the one dev server both targets share. Cross-target service dedupe stays in this PR so a shared mock still starts once; it goes when `config.services` lands. ---

title: agent: a screen that says it is loading counts as settled, so judgments, actions, and the cache see skeletons
body:
## Problem

- Measured on a Next.js admin app: a page whose content is `Loading product`, or a list showing a spinner, counts as settled. The next `agent.assert` judges the skeleton and fails as inconclusive, the trace cache's end check sees its anchors missing and hands off, and a baseline taken before the list rendered records the whole table as the step's delta.
- Consumers work around it with `expect(screen.getByText(/Loading/)).toBeHidden()` before every assert.
- Related: the web engine reports no value for a progress bar, so a determinate 75% bar reads like an indeterminate spinner.

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #398, branch `oskar/settle-loading-screens`, head af8a5f3b. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, both Devin findings fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- `isLoadingObservation` names three app signals (indeterminate `progressbar`, `aria-busy` on the root or a landmark, a content area that is only a loading notice); `settleObservation` waits through such a screen for up to `LOADING_WAIT_MS` counted from the end of the change wait; judgments and the replay end check take the settled look. The web engine reports a determinate progress bar's value.

title: fix(mobile): React Native controls read right on iOS, closeApp closes the app, a lost session is APP_NOT_OPEN, a discovered emulator boots by serial
body: The first iOS run of the mobile benchmark gates' suites (#498, stacked on this) found the first four; its Android job found the fifth. Landing these first is what lets that gate go green on merge. - A view with `accessibilityRole="checkbox"` or `"radio"` has no UIKit trait, so React Native spells role and state into the accessibility value (`checkbox, unchecked`, `radio button, checked`) and XCTest reports an `Other`. The node takes the spelled role, `checked` and `expanded` from the state words, and keeps only what follows as its value, so `getByRole('checkbox')`, `check()`, `uncheck()`, and `toBeChecked` work on a React Native checkbox or radio. - `getByLabel` answers with the innermost match, as `getByText` does: iOS reports a React Native `TextInput` as a labelled host view around the labelled field, which made every label query on a field `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`. A field whose text is also its label keeps its value; only Android's echo of a text view's label as its value is dropped. - `doubleTap()` sends two presses instead of agent-device's double-tap gesture, which reaches a React Native `Pressable` on iOS as one press. - `device.closeApp()` terminates the app before ending the session, so the next `openApp` starts it fresh, and `foregroundApp()` after it is `APP_NOT_OPEN` rather than `ENGINE_FAILURE`. `back()`, `home()`, `alert()`, `dismissKeyboard()`, and `setOrientation()` count as actions for the `transition` budget, as a tap does. - A discovered Android emulator boots by its adb serial. The pool bound a discovered device by the id agent-device lists it under and selected it through the name field; a simulator UDID was inferred as an id, an adb serial was not, so the Android job failed its boot with `No device named emulator-5554`. `SlotBinding.deviceId` now travels beside `device`, `deviceSelection` puts an id under the platform's field (`udid` or `serial`), and a configured `device` that reads as an emulator serial goes by serial too. - The fixture engine maps its errors through the runner's engine error table, so a fixture that throws `INVALID_STATE` reads as `APP_NOT_OPEN`. Unit tests: 142 in the mobile package, including serial selection for a discovered emulator, a configured serial, and a configured name; 39 in the runner's fixture runtime. The device suites that exercise every fix ran on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator against this engine code: 6 files, 50 passed, 10 skipped where agent-device or React Native has no answer yet, each skip naming why. #498 makes that run a gate. Docs: the mobile guide's troubleshooting section, the `device` option in the mobile reference, the engine reference. Changesets: `@e2edev/mobile` patch, `e2e` patch. ---

title: expect: a negation that begins late in the budget fails, and the failure never says how long it held
body:
## Problem

- A negated assertion (`not.toBeVisible`, `not.toHaveText`, ...) must hold for a window before it passes. When the negation first becomes true late in the budget, the assertion fails although the condition held from then on.
- A hold completed by a sample taken past the extended deadline passed, although the negation began too late to complete a window before the cap.
- A negation failure never says how long the condition held, so the message cannot tell a flapping condition from one that never held.

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #439, branch `oskar/negation-window`, head 7c095277. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, Devin's finding fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- `pollCondition` extends the deadline by one negation window once a negation begins, accepts a completed hold only at or before that bound, and `describeNegationTimeout` prints how long it held and the window it needed.

title: runner: a session save failure passes the setup, a corrupt envelope is not SESSION_INVALID, stale session dirs are never swept
body:
## Problem

- A `sessionStore.save` failure after a setup body passed leaves the setup `passed`; consumers then fail with `SESSION_UNAVAILABLE` far from the cause. Failure-only video retention has already deleted the recording by the time the failure is known.
- A corrupt or foreign session envelope surfaces as a decode crash instead of `SESSION_INVALID`.
- `.e2e/sessions/<runId>/` directories of runs that died are never swept.

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #442, branch `oskar/sessions-fail-closed`, head fb4976a4. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, both Devin findings fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- Staged sessions persist before the attempt's verdict, so a save failure fails the setup and retention sees it; a bad envelope is `SESSION_INVALID`; each run directory carries an owner file with its pid and the sweep removes only directories whose owner is gone, never on mtime alone.

title: web: a node under an aria-hidden ancestor reads as visible in single-node reads, so toBeVisible passes on text the snapshot never shows
body:
## Problem

- The tree walk skips an `aria-hidden="true"` subtree, but a single-node read checks the element's own attribute only, so `toBeVisible()` passes on text the snapshot never showed and `locate` disagrees with `observe`.
- A match inside a frame whose `<iframe>` is hidden reads as shown: the child document cannot see the attribute or style that hid its frame.
- `first()`, `last()`, `nth()` on a `visible: true` query are applied before the hidden filter, so a hidden shadow host holding the first match empties the result.
- A `hidden` verdict never says why (`states: hidden` for text plainly on screen).

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #445, branch `oskar/web-aria-hidden-visibility`, head 2ebdf32c. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, all three Devin findings fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- One hidden predicate serves the walk and single reads; `validateFrames` reads each boundary in the document that embeds it and marks matches inside a hidden frame hidden for the boundary's reason; positional steps on a `visible` query run post-read; `SemanticNode` gains optional `hiddenBy` (`aria-hidden`), so a failure reads `observed: states: hidden by aria-hidden`. Engine contract change: changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

title: secrets: step labels, the AI trace, run-level errors, and executor screenshots bypass the secret ledger
body:
## Problem

Four places a registered secret still surfaces in plaintext:

- A step label that spells a value out (`app.open('/reset?token=...')`, ``agent.act(`use key ${key}`)``) is recorded, reported, shown in `--debug`, named in the AI trace run, and handed to later steps as the prior-step ledger.
- `ai-trace.json` records what the model said verbatim: a tool call echoing a value, an assistant message, provider metadata.
- A value a provider resolves after a step was recorded or a trace step closed is never rewritten in `report.json` or the trace.
- An executor's `attachScreenshot` accepts pixels after a secret fill, where `app.screenshot()` is denied.

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #446, branch `oskar/ledger-covers-labels-and-trace`, head 46390b19. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, all four Devin findings fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- Labels pass the attempt redactor at record time and again in the prior-step projection; trace records pass the process ledger as they close and the whole document again as the file is written (`redactLeaves`, keys and structure intact); `report.json`, the MCP session step, run-level errors, and the outcome's records pass the ledger as it stands at write; `attachScreenshot` is `POLICY_DENIED` after a secret fill.

title: secrets: downloads are labelled complete without a scan, untainted traces keep configured secrets, restored cookies never join the ledger
body:
## Problem

Three artifact kinds carry a registered secret under a clean label:

- A download is recorded `redaction: 'complete'` without anyone reading it, so an exported CSV holding a configured API key reaches the report and the `ArtifactStore` as fully masked.
- A trace is rewritten only after a secret fill, although a settings page can render a configured value with no fill, and `web({ headers })` sends the bypass token on every request the trace records.
- A restored session re-sends its cookies on every request and the trace rewrite knows nothing about them.

## Fix, ready on a branch

- PR #461, branch `oskar/artifacts-honest-redaction`, head f505bb4d. Rebased on `main`, CI green on 2026-09-23, all four Devin findings fixed and resolved. Closed to clear the queue; the branch stays.
- Downloads are scanned when the attempt settles, against the ledger as it stands then, streamed through `SecretLedger.byteScanner` so a large export never sits whole in the worker; one holding a value is deleted, recorded `incomplete`, and explained with `ARTIFACT_WITHHELD`. Traces are rewritten whenever the ledger holds a value. `EngineAttemptContext.registerSecret(name, value)` lets an engine hand the harness what it puts on the wire; the web engine registers `headers`, the `basicAuth` password, and cookie and storage values of 16 characters or more, and refuses to start on a runner without the member when it holds one. Engine contract change: changesets for all three packages.

title: test(web-benchmark): the agentic suite replays its committed recordings on every pull request
body: Supersedes #481, which GitHub keeps in a stack with the merged #475 and #476 and will not retarget. | Web benchmark agentic suite | Wall time | Model calls | Cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | record (first run) | 240 s | 84 | $0.042 | | replay | 82 s | 20 | $0.004 | - `packages/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` (19 entries, 72 KB) is committed. CI replays them read-only and calls the model only for a step with no recording, so the gate runs at deterministic speed and cost for this repository's branches; a fork's pull request has no key and is skipped as before. - Two consecutive replays leave every entry byte-identical. The six live steps are by design: three planted-bug judgments (a failing judgment never records) and three acts that type a value read off the screen. - The policy lives once in AGENTS.md ("Committed recordings"); the `.gitignore` files carry one-line pointers. The root rules use `**/` so every package's run artifacts (`artifacts`, `sessions`, `report.json`, `ai-trace.json`, `junit.xml`, `summary.md`, `failures`, `logs`) are ignored, and no rule ignores `.e2e/cache` any more. - A changed scenario is re-recorded locally with `test:agent` and committed in the same pull request. A minor `e2e` release re-keys every entry. - Rebased onto main ahead of the cache work, at Oskar's request, so every later pull request runs against this gate. Re-recorded on main: 15 of the 20 act steps replay; five (lying-labels, iframe-form, async-states, the cart totals act, the wishlist act) still call the model here because their entries need the settled-screen replay #480 brings, which re-records them once it lands. The three planted-bug judgments spend one call each on every run; a judgment is never cached. ---

title: ci(mobile): iOS simulator and Android emulator gates for the mobile benchmark, with a Control Inventory scenario
body: Stacked on `oskar/mobile-engine-fixes` (#491), which carries the engine fixes the first iOS run of these suites found. Supersedes #482, which GitHub keeps in a stack with the merged #475 and #476 and will not retarget. With #491 underneath, the iOS run of this tree passes: 6 files, 50 tests, 10 skipped where agent-device or React Native has no answer yet (each skip names why). The Android job runs for the first time with the emulator selected by serial. ```mermaid flowchart LR F[@expo/fingerprint] --> B{cached app?} B -- hit --> R[repack JS with @expo/repack-app] --> D[deterministic suite] B -- miss --> N[native build] --> D D --> A{same repo and key?} A -- yes --> G[agentic suite] ``` - A Control Inventory scenario (plain controls, every state exposed) plus `controls` and `device-fixture` suites exercise every verb, read, matcher, refusal, and `device` method on a device; the flows gained state matchers. - `mobile.yml`: iOS on `blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26`, Android emulator on x64 Blacksmith with KVM. `.github/actions/expo-app` keys the Expo build by its native fingerprint, keeps it in the actions cache, repacks the JS on a hit, falls back to a native build. `scripts/ci-run.sh` runs the deterministic suite and then the agentic one when the key is present (the emulator runner executes each script line separately, so the guard lives in the script). The booted simulator is handed to the config as `device`. - Skips that remain, each an upstream limit: agent-device delivers a double tap as one tap on iOS; no focused flag on iOS text fields; the snapshot carries no placeholder or attributes, so `getByPlaceholder`, `getAttribute`, and `toHaveAttribute` match nothing on a device; React Native flattens plain Views, so `filter({ has })` into a View with only a test id matches nothing. ---

title: ci(mobile): iOS simulator and Android emulator gates for the mobile benchmark, with a Control Inventory scenario
body: The engine fixes these suites found are merged as #491. Same commit as #498, which GitHub closed when #491's branch was deleted, now rebased onto main. The iOS run of this tree passes on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator: 6 files, 50 tests, 10 skipped where agent-device or React Native has no answer yet (each skip names why). The Android job runs for the first time with the emulator selected by serial. ```mermaid flowchart LR F[@expo/fingerprint] --> B{cached app?} B -- hit --> R[repack JS with @expo/repack-app] --> D[deterministic suite] B -- miss --> N[native build] --> D D --> A{same repo and key?} A -- yes --> G[agentic suite] ``` - A Control Inventory scenario (plain controls, every state exposed) plus `controls` and `device-fixture` suites exercise every verb, read, matcher, refusal, and `device` method on a device; the flows gained state matchers. - `mobile.yml`: iOS on `blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26`, Android emulator on x64 Blacksmith with KVM. `.github/actions/expo-app` keys the Expo build by its native fingerprint, keeps it in the actions cache, repacks the JS on a hit, falls back to a native build. `scripts/ci-run.sh` runs the deterministic suite and then the agentic one when the key is present (the emulator runner executes each script line separately, so the guard lives in the script). The booted simulator is handed to the config as `device`. - Skips that remain, each an upstream limit: agent-device delivers a double tap as one tap on iOS; no focused flag on iOS text fields; the snapshot carries no placeholder or attributes, so `getByPlaceholder`, `getAttribute`, and `toHaveAttribute` match nothing on a device; React Native flattens plain Views, so `filter({ has })` into a View with only a test id matches nothing. - The iOS job boots the iPhone 17 Pro on the iOS 26.5 runtime, pinned by `IOS_RUNTIME` in the workflow. The runner carries four runtimes and the first match was 26.2, whose accessibility bridge reports no `selected` on a tab or radio and an empty field's placeholder as its value; seven tests that pass on 26.5 failed there. Bump the pin on purpose, after a local run on the new runtime. - What the first iOS runs found. With the same Xcode 26.6, iOS 26.5 runtime, and Release build as a Mac at a desk, the CI Mac serves agent-device snapshots without the simulator's accessibility bridge: a React Native radio carries `checked` but no `selected`, a tab no state, and an empty field reports its placeholder as its value (the failure screens are printed into the job log now, since the artifact quota is full). The engine reads a field that shows its hint as empty; the suites read a radio by `checked`, a tab by the section it reveals, and the reward claim by the message it leaves rather than the toast, which is gone before a snapshot lands. The microphone alert overruns the runner's watchdog on that host on every run and wedges the runner for whatever follows, so in CI that one test runs on Android only. - Android is advisory for now (`continue-on-error` on the job), tracked in #500: on the emulator no scenario opens, every deterministic test times out in `openScenario`, and the job runs into its limit before the other files start. The three refusal tests, which open nothing, pass, so the engine and the emulator boot are fine; the list scroll or the row lookup is not. No Android AVD exists on the development Mac, so this needs a machine with one. The iOS job is the gate; the script stops after a deterministic failure, so the advisory Android job spends no model calls. - Second iOS run on CI, deterministic suites: 6 files, 48 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed. The agentic suite ran live there (no recordings yet in that commit) at 22 of 23; its recordings are committed now (22 entries from a Mac, 14 replay on main's cache code, 8 call the model until #480), Huge Virtualized List is a declared gap (the agent scrolls blind on a list iOS renumbers every observation, #486), and Apple Pay Billing Address is a gap on the CI simulator only, whose Apple Pay sheet has no billing-address step. - CI time, measured on a Mac at a desk against the Release build. The home list is a two-column grid so a scenario is one tap away instead of five to ten seconds of dragging, the three-second transition budget that existed for the flung list is gone, and the iOS target drives a pool of simulators. Deterministic suite, 50 tests: 1090 s before, 444 s on one simulator, 283 s on two. A deep link was tried first and abandoned: `simctl openurl` raises the system "Open in" alert on iOS. In CI the iOS job is now two jobs, deterministic and agentic, each with two simulators (the picked iPhone 17 Pro and a clone), so the gate's wall time is one suite, not both. - CI on the final head (run 35909674621): `ios deterministic` green in 9 minutes (suites 359 s, two simulators booted in 137 s, app restored from cache in 10 s), `ios agentic` green in 16 minutes (786 s of suites, 20 scenarios pass, 4 declared gaps, 9 acts still call the model, $0.03), against a single 45-minute-plus job before. The flows file is split in two so the two workers share it, a moved control gets a second and a half to come to rest, and the scenario-open check reads the header title so it works on Android too: the emulator now runs the whole suite (28 pass, 19 fail on Android-only semantics, listed in #500) and stays advisory. - Android, 2026-09-24, from an emulator on a Mac. Of the 19 failures listed in #500, 18 were the suites' iOS spellings (the navigation bar's identifier as the home marker, `role=ScrollView` matching react-native-screens' wrapper too, tab buttons without ids, `CONFIRM` in capitals, a password sheet Android never shows, `check()` on a switch whose state Android does not report) or agent-device 0.21.6 facts the tests now name and run on iOS only (names from the content description, `checked` and `heading`, a WebView field's label, logical pixels, a clipboard read). The last one was an engine bug: the transition wait acted on the ref resolved mid-transition, and Android reports a sliding modal's frames in flight, so the tap went below the screen. The control is found again after the wait now (`@e2edev/mobile` patch), and `AbsListView` is a `list`. Emulator: 39 passed, 1 flaky, 10 skipped; iOS on two simulators: 48 passed, 10 skipped. The agentic suite's 17 Android recordings are committed (Stripe's Compose postal-code field takes no input from agent-device's fill, so that scenario runs on iOS only). The Android job is two jobs now like iOS, and the iOS boot step starts both simulators before waiting. Still advisory: on CI the `sequential onboarding` fill of the third step's number field failed verification in one run of two (the field stayed on its hint), and the permission test's relaunch after a grant lands on the launcher on its first attempt in every run; both pass locally. - Launching is explicit now, the Maestro model and the web's: an attempt launches nothing, the worker brings the pinned app up once in `prepare`, and a test calls `app.open()` when it wants the app fresh (on a device the runner serves it with the engine's restart; a path there is `APP_URL_REQUIRED`). A `launch: 'once'` option was built, measured, and reverted first: with the fixture popping back to the home list it lost time on iOS (308 s against 279 s) and gained nothing on Android, since a pop and the transition budget the first tap then pays cost as much as the launch. agent-device is 0.21.13; probing the skips against it moved four tests (`toBeFocused`, the two double taps, `foregroundApp` after `home`) to Android-only, where they pass, with the iOS runner facts kept as comments. Emulator: 44 passed, 6 skipped; two simulators: 48 passed, 6 skipped. The time audit lives in #500: agent-device's own startup is cheap, the per-attempt cost is the relaunch plus a cold first observation (about 2.3 s), and the CI simulator boots are now concurrent. - Run 35992430569 on this tree: all four mobile jobs green (Android 44 passed and 16 passed with one flaky, iOS 48 and 20). The judge had failed two Android pixel scenarios by contradicting itself over quote marks; it now explains before it decides and treats quotation marks as delimiters (`e2e` patch). The Android jobs gate from here; the remaining known items are the iOS runner episodes (#502) and `tap_at` recordings inside anonymous containers that never replay (#503). - The run script is gone: each mobile job runs one `e2e run` line whose `|| ... --last-failed` gives the failed tests a second pass before the job goes red, since agent-device's runtime has episodes of its own on the CI machines (#502), and a step prints the failure screens on failure (the artifact quota is full). Run 35999168302 on this shape: all four jobs green, the Android jobs gating; the iOS agentic first pass lost Modal Flow to `app 'dev.e2e.benchmark' is not running` and the second pass replayed it. ---

title: mobile-benchmark on the Android emulator never opens a scenario: every deterministic test times out in openScenario
body:
The first Android runs of the mobile benchmark gate (#499, `.github/workflows/mobile.yml`, `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`) never get past opening a scenario. Every test in `tests/controls.e2e.ts` fails the same way, about two minutes each, and the job runs into its 60-minute limit before the other files start:

```
× control inventory > a label query resolves a labeled text field 164.72s
  → expect.poll(...).toBe(...) timed out after 60000 ms
```

That poll is `openScenario` in `packages/mobile-benchmark/tests/fixtures.ts`: it drags `device.locator('role=ScrollView')` a quarter of the list at a time until `screen.getByTestId(<scenario name>)` is visible, then taps the row. On the emulator the row never becomes visible. The three `refusals` tests, which never open a scenario, pass. The engine prepares fine (`1 booted android device(s); driving 1: test`, boot by serial since #491).

Candidates, none verified yet because no Android emulator exists on the development Mac:

- `role=ScrollView` does not match the React Native list on Android (UIAutomator reports a `ReactScrollView` or a RecyclerView), so the swipe goes nowhere or to the wrong node.
- The home list rows carry their `testID` differently on Android (`resource-id` versus an accessibility identifier), so `getByTestId('Login Form')` never matches. The smoke test asserts exactly that and did not get to run.
- The rows are on screen but the emulator's tree marks them as not visible to the user.

Until this is understood the Android job is `continue-on-error: true`; the iOS job is the gate. The agentic Android suite spends no model calls meanwhile: `scripts/ci-run.sh` stops after the deterministic run fails. Reproduce on a machine with an AVD:

```bash
cd packages/mobile-benchmark && pnpm android   # builds and installs on the running emulator
node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --target android-emulator tests/smoke.e2e.ts
```

title: feat(agent): a tool for every engine action the target declares
body: Closes #486. - The act grammar mapped 5 of the 16 engine actions. Every declared action is now a tool: `hover` (and `hover_at` at a point), `double_tap`, `long_press`, `right_click`, `check`, `drag`, `scroll_to`, `upload`, `back`. A verb the engine does not declare is not offered; `check` needs both `check` and `uncheck` because it sets a state rather than flipping one. - One pattern end to end: the verb table in `packages/e2e/src/engine/session.ts`, `ExecutorActions`, the dispatcher, trace-1 record variants with replay (`relocatePair` re-finds both ends of a drag on one screen), the model tools built from one table per verb family, the `e2e mcp` catalog, docs, skill references. - `upload` is policy-gated before the engine sees a path (`packages/e2e/src/agent/upload-paths.ts`): project-relative, resolved inside the project root through symlinks, no hidden segment such as `.env`, `.git`, `.e2e`. A refusal is `POLICY_DENIED` and an `upload.path` policy event on the step; a missing file is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A page can talk a model into naming any path; the harness decides. - Web benchmark: drag-and-drop and kanban-board join the agentic suite with committed recordings; hover-menu is re-recorded as hover, hover, tap (the old recording was three taps, which passed because a click moves the pointer first). Testbed: `tests-agent/verbs.e2e.ts`, one live step per verb. - Left out: tab switching (no engine contract yet) and mobile `home`/`openLink` (device fixture only, outside the engine SPI). ```mermaid flowchart LR A[engine.actions] --> B[VERBS_BY_ACTION] B --> C[target.verbs] C --> D[createGrammarTools] D --> E[ActionDispatcher] E --> F[engine.perform] E --> G[trace-1 record] G --> H[zero-turn replay] H --> E ``` The vocabulary a web target offers, in the order the model sees it: ``` observe, tap, double_tap, long_press, right_click, hover, scroll_to, type, press, select, check, drag, upload, scroll, navigate, back, screenshot, tap_at, hover_at, type_at, press_at, select_at, type_secret, complete_step ``` The tap variants are separate tools, not a `kind` option on `tap` as #486 proposed. Offered as an optional enum, gpt-6-luna-fast filled it on ordinary controls and kept doing so after the description and system rule said not to; a double-click on a submit button submits twice. Live traces, same steps: | Step | `tap {target, kind?}`, two rounds | separate tools | | --- | --- | --- | | Accept terms (sticky-chrome) | `kind: "double"` | `tap` | | Rename menu item (context-menu-trap) | `kind: "long"` on every tap | `tap` | | Archive card (testbed board) | `kind: "double"` | `tap` | | report.pdf context menu (testbed controls) | `secondary`, then `long` | `right_click` once, 3 model calls instead of 4 | Live on gpt-6-luna-fast: hover-menu, drag-and-drop, kanban-board, context-menu-trap, sticky-chrome pass; the testbed verbs suite passes 8 of 8. The three new recordings replay read-only in under a second each. ---

title: iOS CI: agent-device daemon replaced as unreachable mid-run loses a worker's session; runner watchdog overrun wedges the agentic suite
body:
Run 35975626759 on `oskar/mobile-gates` (#499), iOS jobs on `blacksmith-6vcpu-macos-26`, agent-device 0.21.6, two simulators, two workers. The run before it on the same suites was green; nothing in the suites changed between them.

**ios deterministic** (3 failed of 48): the agent-device daemon was replaced twice as unreachable while the suite ran:

```
08:33:08 Replacing daemon (pid 2206, v0.21.6) in /Users/runner/.agent-device: unreachable
08:34:57 Replacing daemon (pid 12687, v0.21.6) in /Users/runner/.agent-device: unreachable
```

After the second replacement one worker's session had lost its device: `snapshot failed: 2 devices match this request equally; select one explicitly` (the new daemon had no session pinned to a simulator, so a request without a UDID matched both booted ones), then `open dev.e2e.benchmark failed: Invalid daemon response`, then `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT: starting an attempt on engine mobile timed out`. Both attempts of the three tests failed inside that window; the files after it passed.

**ios agentic** (2 failed of 20): `APP_UNREACHABLE: snapshot failed: the iOS automation runner is still finishing a command that overran its watchdog (session e2e-mobile-benchmark-ios-0 ...)` on Login Form, and the next scenario found the app still on the previous scenario's screen ("Stripe checkout closed. Open it again when ready."), so its home-list row was not there. Same shape as the microphone-alert watchdog overrun in #499's description, without an alert this time.

Neither reproduces on a Mac at a desk. Two things the engine could do about the first: pass the pinned UDID on every request rather than relying on the daemon's session (the pool knows it), and treat a daemon replacement as a lost session that is reopened before the next command instead of surfacing `Invalid daemon response`. The watchdog overrun is agent-device's runner; the engine already reports it as `APP_UNREACHABLE`.

title: trace cache: a recorded tap_at inside an anonymous container never replays (target-not-found)
body:
Seen on the mobile benchmark's Android agentic suite (branch `oskar/mobile-gates`, #499): the two scenarios whose tree is merged or hidden on purpose (Broken Accessibility, Vision Only) are driven by `tap_at`, and their recordings miss on every replay with `cache: { mode: 'missed', reason: 'target-not-found', replayedActions: 0 }`, locally on the same emulator that recorded them minutes earlier. CI shows the same (`5 replayed · 6 handed off · 8 missed` on the Android job).

The recorded actions:

```json
{"name":"tapAt","point":{"x":749,"y":1420},"within":{"target":{"role":"group"},"fx":0.4898,"fy":0.483}}
```

The container descriptor is `{ role: 'group' }` and nothing else, because the merged view carries no name or test id; a screen has dozens of anonymous groups, so `relocate.ts` cannot single it out and the step is handed to the model, which taps the same point again and rewrites the entry (only `createdAt`, `summary`, and `endWaitMs` change).

The Flattened Registration Form and Flattened Login recordings miss for a declared reason instead (`reason: 'gap', derived: 'pixels'`), which is by design.

Options, in the cache's own fail-to-miss spirit: record the viewport-relative point (`point` and `viewport` are already stored) as the fallback when the container is anonymous and the viewport size matches on replay; or record the container by its box in viewport fractions rather than by descriptor; or refuse to record a `within` that cannot relocate and store the point alone, so the miss reason names the real gap.

title: feat(cli): the e2e wordmark drops in on init and opens the help
body:
`e2e init` opens with the e2e wordmark written in the way a pen writes it, and `e2e --help` prints the wordmark at rest above the help.

- The lettering is the site's. Stack Sans Notch at weight 400, rasterized 20 px tall with two pixels per column and drawn in quadrant blocks: 53 columns by 10 rows. The bitmap is embedded in `packages/e2e/src/cli/wordmark.ts` with the recipe in its comment; no font ships.
- Each letter has a pen path over that bitmap: the `e` writes its crossbar left to right, then sweeps from the right side over the top, down the left, and around to its tail; the `2` sweeps its arc from the left over the top, runs the diagonal down to the bottom left, and draws the base. Every lit pixel takes the moment the pen passes its nearest point on the path, so the fill grows along the stroke. The next letter starts as the previous nears its end. About 1.3 s at 33 ms frames, time based, so a slow pty drops frames instead of stretching.
- Monochrome, in the terminal's own foreground, the way the site sets the word in white on dark. The ink just behind the pen is dim; the resting word carries no escape codes at all. The frame is the ten word rows, so nothing shifts when the wizard starts under it.
- Terminal only, at least 55 columns wide; piped output never sees it, so agents reading `--help` get the same text as before. `--yes`, `CI`, and `TERM=dumb` print the wordmark at rest. Ctrl-C while it is being written restores the cursor and exits 130.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[e: crossbar, then around the bowl to the tail] --> B[2: arc, diagonal, base]
  B --> C[e: crossbar, then around the bowl to the tail]
  C --> D[at rest: plain quadrant blocks]
```

| `e2e v0.15.0 · an open framework for agentic end-to-end testing` | the wordmark below, then the same line |

```
▐██▛       ▐██▌            ▗▄███▀     ███▘       ███
▀▀▀████████████         ▄▟███▛▀      ▝▀▀▜███████████▌
```

title: fix(agent): OpenAI requests store nothing, so zero data retention orgs run
body:
## What and why

- A customer on an OpenAI zero-data-retention org could not run agent steps: the second turn of every `act` failed with `Item with id 'rs_…' not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false`.
- Cause: OpenAI Responses requests went out with the AI SDK default `store: true`. With storage on, the SDK replays a reasoning model's earlier turns by item id and never asks for `reasoning.encrypted_content`. ZDR forces `store=false` server-side whatever the request said, so those ids never existed. Seen in `@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.71: `store` defaults to `true`, and encrypted reasoning is requested only when `store === false`.
- The runner never reads a response back from the provider (no `previousResponseId`, no `conversation`), so storage buys nothing. OpenAI and Azure OpenAI requests now carry `store: false` next to the prompt-cache key in `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/provider-hints.ts`; caller `providerOptions` still win. The ChatGPT subscription path already forced this.
- The prompt cache keeps working: ZDR orgs default to in-memory retention, and `prompt_cache_key` is unaffected.
- `failureHint` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts` names the remedy when the failure still shows (a caller set `store: true`, or a gateway dropped the option), beside the existing credential hint.
- The hints module is `provider-hints.ts` now, since it sets a storage policy as well as cache hints. It answers two questions per model, does it take Anthropic breakpoints and which key do OpenAI-shaped options go under, instead of a family union that doubled as the options key.
- `docs/models.mdx` gains a data retention section: the OpenAI default, and the direct-provider rule for Anthropic under a BAA (the agreement covers `api.anthropic.com` only, so `gateway('anthropic/…')` is outside it).

- Live through the Vercel AI Gateway (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, testbed `act` suite, cache off): 4 of 4 passed, 18 model calls, six turns in the longest step, prompt cache 79% hit. Every reasoning reply carried encrypted content, which OpenAI returns only when asked for, and the SDK asks only when it sees `store: false`: the OpenAI option bag reaches OpenAI through the gateway, so the documented default path works for a zero-retention org.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before [store: true, SDK default]
    A1[turn 1] -->|rs_1 by id| B1[turn 2]
    B1 --> C1{ZDR org?}
    C1 -- yes --> D1[400 item not found]
    C1 -- no --> E1[ok, 30-day retention]
  end
  subgraph after [store: false, runner default]
    A2[turn 1] -->|reasoning as encrypted_content| B2[turn 2]
    B2 --> E2[ok, nothing retained]
  end
```

What reaches OpenAI for a `gpt-6-luna` request, pinned by `packages/e2e/tests/unit/openai-request-shape.test.ts` against the installed provider:

```json
{ "store": false, "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], "prompt_cache_key": "e2e-…" }
```

Opt back in per agent:

```ts
createAgent({ model: openai('gpt-6-luna'), providerOptions: { openai: { store: true } } })
```

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

title: fix(telemetry): a source checkout of the repository sends nothing
body:
The CLI run from this repository, whether `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`, the testbed's `node_modules/e2e` link, or a fixture spawned by an integration test, counted as usage. Now it sends nothing.

- `runsFromCheckout(import.meta.url)` in `packages/e2e/src/telemetry/checkout.ts`: the checkout keeps this package's `src` beside `dist`, so `src/cli/index.ts` two directories up from the CLI module is the marker. No install or unpack ships `src`, wherever the package lands, so the marker is positive rather than an absence. `main` passes the answer to `Telemetry`, which reports it as the off reason after the two environment variables and before the CI identity.
- `e2e telemetry` prints `Status: disabled (running from a source checkout of e2e)`, and the first-run notice does not print.
- The CLI unit tests mock the detector so they keep covering an installed CLI; the detector's own test builds an install, a pnpm store path, a copy unpacked outside `node_modules`, and a checkout-shaped directory on disk.
- A `pnpm pack` tarball installed into a scratch project with npm, and the same package copied to a directory outside any `node_modules`, both report `Status: enabled`; the checkout and the testbed link report disabled.

Docs: `docs/telemetry.mdx`. Changeset: patch.

title: test(benchmark): every verb from #501 gates a PR from a committed recording
body: Follow-up to #501, which left `check`, `upload`, `back`, `right_click`, `long_press`, and `double_tap` with no PR-gating agentic test, and the mobile verbs untried on a device. - Web benchmark: a Control Inventory scenario at `/e/control-inventory`, one plain control per verb, each reporting its state in a status line: a checkbox and a radio group, a Hold me button that tells a 500 ms press from a tap, a Double-click me button that tells a double click from a click, a file list whose menu opens on right-click only, a file input, a details view one history entry deep, a footnote 1600 px down. Ours, like the mobile benchmark's Control Inventory (#499), not a copy from tester-army; AGENTS.md names the exception. - `packages/web-benchmark/tests/control-inventory.e2e.ts`: the deterministic twin, through `check`, `longPress`, `doubleTap`, `secondaryTap`, `setInputFiles`, `app.back`, and `scrollIntoView`. - `packages/web-benchmark/tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts`: one `agent.act` per verb, pinned by the status line, with six committed recordings. A red test names the verb. - Mobile benchmark: the Gestures scenario loses its gap ("long-press and double-tap have no grammar verb") and gets a recording from the iOS simulator. The card is a plain View the tree does not list, so the swipe goes through the device tool pack and is a gap in the recording: replay performs the long press and hands the swipe and the double tap to the model, about $0.003 a run. The Huge Virtualized List gap now says why `scroll_to` is missing on a device (no `scrollIntoView` declared) instead of pointing at #486. What gpt-6-luna-fast called on the first run, and what the recording replays: | Step | Tools called | Recorded | | --- | --- | --- | | check sets the checkbox and the radio | `check` x2 | check, check | | a long press and a double click | `long_press`, `double_tap` | longPress, doubleTap | | a right-click opens the file menu, Rename | `right_click` x2, `screenshot`, `tap` | secondaryTap x2, tap | | upload attaches the project files | `upload` | upload | | back returns from the details view | `tap`, `back` | tap, back | | scroll_to brings the footnote into view | `scroll_to` | scrollTo | | Gestures (iOS simulator) | `long_press`, `screenshot`, `swipe` x3, `double_tap` x2 | longPress, gap x3, doubleTap | The six web steps cost $0.0043 live and replay with no model call. On iOS the first `double_tap` did not register (agent-device presses 285 ms apart against the scenario's 300 ms window) and the second did; the hand-off gives the model that retry on every run. ---

title: ci(mobile): cache the Android system image and AVD boot snapshot
body: Both Android jobs of `mobile.yml` spent about 100 s before the first test on work that is the same on every run: the emulator-runner action downloads the API 36 system image (68 s on run 36047139133) and cold-boots the AVD it just created (34 s). - One `actions/cache` key holds the system image under `$ANDROID_HOME/system-images/android-36` and the AVD under `~/.android/avd` with its boot snapshot. The action's own AVD-caching recipe, with the image added to the path, since the runner image does not carry it. - A miss runs the emulator-runner action once more with snapshots on and no tests: its exit saves the `default_boot` snapshot, which is what the cache keeps. The suite step then boots from it with `-no-snapshot-save` and `force-avd-creation: false`, so it leaves the restored AVD as it found it. - The key carries the image, target, arch, and profile plus a suffix to bump when the snapshot should be rebuilt on purpose. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[restore cache] --> B{hit?} B -- no --> C[sdkmanager downloads the image] C --> D[cold boot, save the snapshot, stop] D --> E[boot from the snapshot] B -- yes --> E E --> F[run the suite] ``` | Step | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | system image install | 68 s | restore only | | emulator boot | 34 s | from snapshot | Numbers for the hit path come from this PR's second workflow run and go into the table once it is in. ---

title: fix(mobile): Android's status bar and navigation bar stay out of the tree
body: On the Android emulator, every agentic replay whose recording ended with a status-bar node among its end anchors handed the step to the model: run 36047139133 spent 50 model calls on Android for steps that all have committed recordings (Login Form 4, Modal Flow 1, Bottom Tabs 1, Async States 8, ...). - agent-device reports Android's system bars as windows of `com.android.systemui` beside the app's window: the status bar (clock, signal, wifi, battery) at the top edge and the three-button navigation bar at the bottom. Their labels follow the emulator's clock and radio: the same emulator read "T-Mobile, three bars.", "two bars.", "no signal.", and "signal full." across the nine committed recordings that carry `com.android.systemui:id/mobile_combo` as an anchor. - `projectSnapshot` in `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts` now leaves out a systemui root that hugs the top or bottom edge and is under a quarter of the screen tall, with its children. The notification shade, quick settings, and a system dialog are systemui windows too, but they cover the screen and stay. iOS reports no package on its nodes and is untouched. - The nine Android recordings lose that anchor; each keeps at least one anchor from the app (the success message), so a replay still checks its effect before it self-finalizes. - `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` says so in the `observe` row; changeset for `@e2edev/mobile`. What the emulator hands back for the status bar, `agent-device snapshot --json --platform android`: ```json { "type": "androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView", "bundleId": "com.android.systemui", "rect": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 1080, "height": 63 }, "depth": 0 } { "type": "android.widget.TextView", "label": "10:17", "identifier": "com.android.systemui:id/clock", "depth": 2 } { "type": "android.widget.FrameLayout", "label": "T-Mobile, signal full.", "identifier": "com.android.systemui:id/mobile_combo", "depth": 2 } { "type": "android.view.View", "label": "Battery charging, 100 percent.", "depth": 3 } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[snapshot roots] --> B{systemui window at the top or bottom edge?} B -- yes --> C[left out with its children] B -- no --> D[projected] ``` ---

title: fix(cache): a point tap inside a poorly listed control replays instead of handing off
body: Every pixel-driven step of the mobile benchmark handed its replay to the model, on both platforms, for the same recorded action: a `tap_at` inside a listed node. Run 36047139133 spent 13 model calls and 80 s on Broken Accessibility on iOS; Vision Only on Android took 47 s and 5 calls for three recorded taps. - iOS: the merged screen is a React Native host view and the view inside it, both named "Create your benchmark account, First name, ...". Relocation finds two, both hold the recorded point, and `boxWithin` wanted exactly one: `target-ambiguous`, nothing replayed. - Android: the merged screen is an anonymous `group` among groups (#503). A descriptor with only a role has nothing to re-find it by: `target-not-found` after the 15 s of settling looks, nothing replayed. - Several nested look-alikes that hold one point cannot be disjoint, so on a viewport of the recorded size the recorded point names the same pixel whichever of them was recorded. `placeWithin` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/replay.ts` taps that point, as a bare-point recording already does; a container that is gone or a viewport of another size still hands off. - The recorder no longer keeps a `within` whose descriptor cannot relocate (`isRelocatableDescriptor`, now exported from `relocate.ts`): the point alone is the honest record. An entry that still carries one plans as a bare point, so the committed Android recordings replay without re-recording. - `docs/cache.mdx` names the rule in the `target-ambiguous` row; changeset for `e2e`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[tap_at with a container] --> B{container re-found?} B -- one node --> C[point at fx, fy inside its box] B -- several nested, same viewport --> D[the recorded point] B -- anonymous descriptor --> D B -- gone or another viewport --> E[hand off] ``` Vision Only on the local emulator, same committed recording: | | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | cache | `missed · target-not-found` | `self-finalized · 3 of 3` | | model calls | 5 | 0 | | step | 35 s | 3.8 s | Broken Accessibility replays its first tap and hands off at the next action as designed: the code it types is read off a screenshot (`gap · pixels`). ---

title: test(mobile-benchmark): goals the recordings can replay, and the onboarding wizard runs on Android
body: Four steps of the mobile benchmark's agentic suite called the model on every replay for a reason in the goal text, not in the harness: a typed value the model composed after a screenshot counts as read off the image (`gap · pixels`), "any CVC" had it type the `123` the screen shows (`gap · minted-token`), and "pull to refresh" sent it to the device tool pack's free-form `swipe`, which no recording replays. A fifth failure was the scenario fixture's own. - Flattened Registration Form: the goal names the values (Ada, Lovelace, ada@example.com, Lovelace1815), so every typed value is the step's literal input and replays. Not the declared credential's password, which reaches the model redacted and poisons the recording. - Stripe PaymentSheet: expiry and CVC are named. The sheet itself still ends most replays in `end-mismatch` (it keeps state between runs), so this step stays live for now; the old recording is a dead key and goes. - Async States: "scroll up on the reward area to refresh it" names the grammar verb. On Android the model follows it and the step replays in 8 s; on iOS gpt-6-luna-fast still reaches for `swipe` after a screenshot, so that side stays live too. - Sequential Onboarding runs on Android, where three live runs passed and the recording replays in 8 s. iOS fails two of three: the fields the keyboard covers stay covered (agent-device cannot dismiss the iOS keyboard, and a tap while it is up only closes it), so the step is `platforms: ['android']` with the reason beside it instead of a skip on both. - Flattened Login keeps reading the hint off the screenshot: a secret can only be typed into a listed field, and this screen lists none. The comment says so. - `openScenario` in `tests/fixtures.ts`: the retry after a pop now waits for the home row to be back before tapping it, and a screen gets ten seconds to push. PR #510's iOS job lost Stripe twice to the old retry tapping a list that was not there yet (`LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: getByLabel("Stripe PaymentSheet. ")`). - Recordings: four new entries (Android Flattened Registration Form, Async States, and Sequential Onboarding; iOS Flattened Registration Form), five stale ones removed. Local replays of the committed recordings, same devices that recorded them, with #511 and #512 applied: | Step | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | Flattened Registration Form, Android | 44 s · 7 model calls · `gap` | 19 s · 0 · `self-finalized 9/9` | | Flattened Registration Form, iOS | 47 s · 8 · `target-ambiguous` | 38 s · 3 · 11 of 12 replayed, the trailing tap hands off once the form is gone | | Async States, Android | 47 s · 11 · `gap`, failed | 8 s · 0 · `self-finalized 2/2` | | Sequential Onboarding, Android | skipped | 8 s · 0 · `self-finalized 10/10` | ---

title: feat(agent): scroll_to reaches a node by its text, paging a list until it shows
body: Two benchmark scenarios were skipped for the same missing capability: a row hundreds of screens down a windowed list that the tree lists only once it is drawn. `scroll` moves half a screen a call and each repeat is one action of the budget, so the web `virtualized-table` (row 4322 of 5000) needed about 650 actions of a 60-action budget, and the mobile `Huge Virtualized List` lost its scroll target to renumbered ids around row 460. The deterministic API has had `screen.scrollUntilVisible` for this all along; the agent did not. - `scroll_to` takes `text`: the visible text of the node to reach. The list named by `target` (or the viewport) is paged screen by screen in `direction` until a visible node reading that text shows, then the engine brings it into the viewport when it can. One action of the budget however many screens; the cap is 800, and a screen that stops changing ends it earlier. Either is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, an action failure the model re-aims from. `target` keeps its meaning without `text`: the listed node to bring into view. - A node reads the text when its label is the text or holds it inside a label not much longer: a row label with a suffix ("Row 4322 - Golden Row") counts, the sentence on the same screen that says "Scroll to Row 0512 and tap it" does not. The first cut matched any label and declared the row in view on the screen that gave the instruction. - Each page moves as a grammar `scroll` does, three quarters of the list: a longer flick on a full-screen Android list starts in the gesture-navigation strip and moves nothing, and a page longer than the list skips rows between looks. Pages are read raw, since a device capture costs a second and the row is the row mid-fling; the screen the next action addresses is read settled. Three unchanged pages end the list, since a loaded device drops a swipe now and then; two unchanged pages of a named list hand the paging to the viewport, since a device shows two scroll views per screen and the model names the wrong one now and then, as does a list twenty pages down that neither name nor place re-finds. The record names what paged in the end. - A device engine declares no `scrollIntoView`, so it never had `scroll_to`; it gets the text form, unlocked by `swipe`. `target.verbs` gains `scrollUntil`. - Recorded as one `scrollUntil` action with the list it paged and how much of the screen it covered, like a folded `scroll`; replay re-finds the list (or pages the viewport for a lost list that filled the screen) and pages again. Telemetry, settle policy, trace reader and template mapping, and the fake executor context carry the new name. - The gestures fixture page gets a windowed ledger (400 rows, only the rows in the container's window in the DOM) with a hint sentence naming the row above it; `agent-act-verbs.test.ts` pages it to row 333 as one action, records it, and replays it. - The web gap and the Android side of the mobile gap come out; recordings for both are committed. iOS keeps the step out with the reason beside it, see the table. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["scroll_to({ text, target? })"] --> B[look at the settled screen] B --> C{a node reads the text?} C -- yes, engine has scrollIntoView --> D[bring it in, done] C -- yes, in the viewport --> D C -- no --> E{screen changed since the last page?} E -- no, or 400 screens --> F[LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND] E -- yes --> G[page the list, or the viewport] G --> B ``` Live runs with gpt-6-luna-fast: | Scenario | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | web `virtualized-table` | skipped: 60-action budget exhausted at row 620 | passed, `scroll_to` + `tap`, 3 model calls, 60 s; replays with none | | mobile `Huge Virtualized List`, Android | skipped | passed, `scroll_to` (49 screens) + `tap`, 3 model calls, 74 s; replays the paging on its own | | mobile `Huge Virtualized List`, iOS | skipped | still out, now as `platforms: ['android']` with the reason beside it: each page waits out a fling of a few seconds, the row is over forty pages down, and the step outruns its 300 s timeout (52 pages in 295 s on the simulator) | ---

title: test(mobile-benchmark): the Control Inventory shows what the device tells the app, and two device fixture skips come out
body: Three `device-fixture.e2e.ts` tests were skipped because the app had nothing that showed what `setNetwork`, `setLocation`, or a biometric prompt did. The Control Inventory screen gets a fourth section, Device, that prints what the device tells the app. - `expo-network`, `expo-location`, and `expo-local-authentication` join the app (SDK 57 versions, pinned like the other modules; the location and Face ID permission strings go in through their config plugins). The Device section shows `network: connected|disconnected` from `useNetworkState`, a Read location button that prints the position to four decimals, and an Unlock with biometrics button that prints the prompt's outcome. - `setNetwork and setAirplaneMode change what the app sees` runs on Android: wifi off, back on, airplane on and off, each read off the screen. On an iOS simulator agent-device's network settings paint the status bar indicator and the app keeps its connection, so the test is Android-only with the reason beside it. - `setLocation and clearLocation change what the app reads` runs on both platforms: the permission is granted up front, two positions are set and read back. The read asks for the highest accuracy, which is the GPS provider the emulator's fix feeds, and declines Google's "Location Accuracy" dialog, which otherwise covers the app on the first read. - `enrollBiometrics and setBiometrics answer a biometric prompt` stays skipped, now for a reason that names the blocker: agent-device 0.21.13 answers "Face ID simulation is not supported on this simulator runtime" on iOS 26, and the emulator's fingerprint answers only once a lock screen and a finger are enrolled by hand. The surface is there for the day either changes. - The native fingerprint changes, so the `expo-app` action rebuilds the app once in CI and caches it. Local runs of `device-fixture.e2e.ts` against the rebuilt apps: iOS 8 passed, 1 skipped; Android 8 passed, 1 skipped. The controls suite passes on both with the fourth tab. ---

title: feat(agent): the observed node carries its selected text, and press repeats a key
body:
The web benchmark skipped `rich-text-editor` with the note "selecting text inside a contenteditable needs a selection verb". It does not need a verb. The model needs to see what it selected, and to select eight characters without eight round trips.

- `SemanticNode.selection` (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`): the text selected inside the focused field or editing host. The screen line renders it after the value as `selection="..."` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts`), so a `press` of `Shift+ArrowLeft` reads back `selection="d"`, then `"ed"`, then the word. A secure field reports none, as it reports no value, and `projectTree` redacts it like one.
- The web engine reads it from an input's or textarea's selection range, and from the document selection inside a `contenteditable` host, for the focused element only; a collapsed caret reports none (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`).
- `press({ target?, key, times? })`: `times` presses the key 1 to 20 times in one call, each press one recorded action against the budget, as a scroll repeat is (`packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts`). With a target, the first press addresses the node and the rest go through the focused keyboard, since a targeted press refocuses the node and a repeated `Tab` would otherwise start over from it. The tool description says that Shift with an arrow extends the selection and that the screen shows it.
- `rich-text-editor` drops its gap and gets a recording under `packages/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/`.

Why feedback and a repeat count rather than a `select_text` verb: a verb would take character offsets the model does not have either. What a person at a keyboard has is the highlighted text and the ability to hold Shift and tap an arrow a few times.

What the model saw on the recording run (9 model calls in all):

```text
press({"target":"n7","key":"Control+Shift+ArrowLeft","times":1})
changed #n7 textbox ... value="release approved" selection="release approved"
press({"target":"n7","key":"ArrowRight","times":1})
changed #n7 textbox ... value="release approved"
press({"target":"n7","key":"Shift+ArrowLeft","times":8})
changed #n7 textbox ... value="release approved" selection="approved"
tap({"target":"n6"})   # B: the bold run becomes its own text node
changed #n7 textbox text="release" ... selection="approved"
added #n42001 text="approved"
tap({"target":"n8"})   # Check document -> "Document approved"
```

| `rich-text-editor` (gpt-6-luna-fast) | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| suite | skipped with a gap | runs |
| live, no recording | 24 model calls, 85 s, $0.021, failed: pressed `Shift+ArrowLeft` once per turn, lost count, bolded the wrong span | 9 model calls, 21 s, $0.004, passed |
| replay | none | 0 model calls, 1.3 s |

Two platform notes the tests carry:

- The recording holds `Control+Shift+ArrowLeft` then `ArrowRight` before the eight `Shift+ArrowLeft`. On macOS the first selects to the line start, on Linux the previous word; the `ArrowRight` collapses either to the end of the text, so the entry replays on the Linux CI runner as on the Mac it was recorded on.
- `Home` and `End` scroll the page on macOS Chromium instead of moving the caret, so the gestures fixture parks the caret at the end on click and the integration flow (`packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-act-verbs.test.ts`, "selects one word with a repeated press") taps, then presses `Shift+ArrowLeft` eight times in one call, and checks both the `selection="approved"` the model reads and the page's own `select` event.

Docs: `reference/engine.mdx` (the node field), `reference/agent.mdx` (`press` row and the selection paragraph), `reference/screen.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`. Changeset: `e2e` minor, `@e2edev/web` minor.

title: chore: move the testbed and both benchmarks to apps/
body:
- `packages/` now holds only what publishes to npm. `apps/` holds the private consumers: `testbed`, `web-benchmark`, `mobile-benchmark`. Package names, scripts, and `--filter` targets are unchanged.
- Committed recordings replay as before. The trace cache key is sha(`projectId`) + test id + target + call signature, none of which sees the package path (`packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts`). Both `projectId`s stay.
- The Expo build cache key (`mobile-benchmark-<platform>-<fingerprint>`) keeps its name, and `@expo/fingerprint` hashes relative to the project root, so a cached native build still hits.

```

apps/       testbed  web-benchmark  mobile-benchmark   private, consume dist
```
