title: feat(cli): init writes the skill once, .claude/skills/e2e links to the .agents/skills copy
body: - With both locations chosen (the `--yes` default), `e2e init` writes `.agents/skills/e2e` and makes `.claude/skills/e2e` a relative symlink to it: the layout `npx skills add` produces. One copy serves every agent, and a refresh touches one directory. - A project with two copies from an earlier version migrates on its next `init`: the Claude Code copy becomes the link when it holds nothing but the shipped files. Anything else in it keeps the copy, refreshed as before. - A `.claude/skills` already linked to `.agents/skills`, or a `.claude/skills/e2e` already pointing at the copy, needs nothing. The #453 rules stand for a link elsewhere: skipped with a warning under `--yes`, offered a replacement when asked, now the link instead of a second copy. When the `.agents/skills` copy is itself left alone (a link elsewhere, a broken tree), Claude Code gets a copy as before. - Windows gets a junction, as the skills CLI does. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[".claude/skills/e2e"] --> B{leads to .agents/skills/e2e?} B -- yes --> C[nothing to do] B -- no --> D{what is there?} D -- nothing --> E[link] D -- copy, shipped files only --> F[replace the copy with the link] D -- copy with other files --> G[refresh the copy] D -- symlink elsewhere --> H{"--yes?"} H -- yes --> I[warn, leave it] H -- no --> J[ask before replacing it with the link] ``` `planSkillLink` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/agent-skill.ts:133` makes that call; `init.ts` plans the copies first, then links only to a copy this run leaves current. Before: ``` ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e/ (8 files) ◆ Created .claude/skills/e2e/ (8 files) ``` After: ``` ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e/ (8 files) ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e ``` Follow-up, once the repository is public: write a `skills-lock.json` entry for `tester-army/e2e` so `npx skills update` refreshes the skill. The skills CLI refetches lock entries from GitHub and skips `node_modules` and `local` sources, so there is nothing it could sync against today. ---

title: fix(cli): quieter e2e init: no telemetry notice, planned changes listed one per line
body:
Two first-run rough edges in \`e2e init\`. - \`e2e init\` no longer prints the one-time telemetry notice. The scaffold used to open with the disclaimer, ahead of its own prompts. \`init\` joins \`telemetry\` as an exempt command in the \`preAction\` hook (\`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts\`); the first command after the scaffold, such as \`e2e run\`, prints the notice once as before. The init session event is still recorded. - The confirm prompt lists the planned changes one per line instead of joining eight paths into one sentence, and asks only whether to apply them. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | telemetry notice, then the prompts | the prompts | | \`◆ Update package.json, create e2e.config.ts, create tests/example.e2e.ts, create .agents/skills/e2e/, ... update .gitignore?\` | \`● Changes:\`
\` - Update package.json\`
\` - Create e2e.config.ts\`
\` - Create tests/example.e2e.ts\`
\` - Create .agents/skills/e2e/\`
\` ...\`
\`◆ Apply these changes?\` |

title: ci(mobile): each mobile benchmark job posts its run as a pull request comment
body:
- The web benchmark posts its two suites to the pull request through `@e2edev/github`; the four mobile jobs (ios, android, each deterministic and agentic) posted nothing. Now each does, plus the job summary.
- The workflow names each comment through `E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_COMMENT`, following the reporter's own matrix idiom (`key: process.env.MATRIX_BROWSER`): `ios`, `ios agent`, `android`, `android agent`. The agent config inherits the reporter through its spread of the base config, so one line covers both suites.
- The `--last-failed` second pass runs without the token and posts nothing, so each job has one comment: the first full pass. The report page lists only the tests a run selected (`packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts:472`), so a retry under the same name would replace a real failure list with its few passes, and a retry under its own name would outlive the failure that caused it. A green job whose comment lists failures is one the retry recovered.
- `pull-requests: write` on the workflow and `GITHUB_TOKEN` on the run steps. A fork's pull request still gets a read-only token, and the reporter says so instead of posting.
- Unset, as on a Mac, no key: the reporter prints why it did not post and nothing else changes.

```ts
// apps/mobile-benchmark/e2e.config.ts
const comment = process.env.E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_COMMENT;
reporters: ['list', github(comment === undefined ? {} : { key: comment })],
```

```yaml
E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_COMMENT: ios${{ matrix.suite == 'agentic' && ' agent' || '' }}
run: $E2E_RUN || env -u GITHUB_TOKEN $E2E_RUN --last-failed
```

This PR's own mobile jobs are the check: four comments should appear below.

Bumps the dev-tooling group with 6 updates: | Package | From | To | | --- | --- | --- | | [fallow](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow) | `3.27.0` | `3.28.0` | | [oxlint](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/tree/HEAD/npm/oxlint) | `1.83.0` | `1.85.0` | | [@ai-sdk/openai](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/HEAD/packages/openai) | `4.0.71` | `4.0.72` | | [@ai-sdk/xai](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/HEAD/packages/xai) | `5.0.4` | `5.0.5` | | [ai](https://github.com/vercel/ai/tree/HEAD/packages/ai) | `7.0.107` | `7.0.109` | | [mint](https://github.com/mintlify/mint/tree/HEAD/packages/mint) | `4.2.909` | `4.2.917` | Updates `fallow` from 3.27.0 to 3.28.0
Release notes

Sourced from fallow's releases.

v3.28.0: baselines carry a kind, request outcomes on every surface, Module Federation and Nuxt reads

Features

  • Every saved baseline now says which command wrote it. --save-baseline writes a top-level kind field with dead-code, dupes or health. Older baselines without it still load, and an older fallow still loads a baseline saved by this release.
  • Pointing --baseline at the wrong command's file is no longer silent. The run prints a warning with both command names and the path, and the file suppresses nothing. In the JSON output, baseline_staleness.unrecognised_format is true. The same warning appears in the pull-request comment, the merge-request note and the Check Run. The GitHub job summary shows the file path through the new baseline-path output, and fallow audit prints one warning per baseline it cannot use.
  • The JSON output says what narrowed a run. baseline_staleness.scope_reasons lists the reasons, for example changed-since or production. A narrowed run with a baseline also gets a recheck-baseline entry in next_steps, and the bare fallow command gets it too.
  • request_outcomes is now in the output of fallow flags, fallow suppressions and fallow security. The first two report their changed-since entry, and fallow security --sarif-file gets a sarif-file entry.
  • An empty diff no longer looks like a clean project. When a diff filter applies, its request_outcomes entry has a scope_size with the number of added lines. A diff with zero added lines reports scope_size: 0. The Action, the GitLab template, the MCP tools and the pull-request comment then all say that the clean result covers nothing.
  • hotspots-skipped now has a cause: not-a-repository, invalid-since or churn-file-unreadable.
  • A config that a plugin cannot read shows up in workspace_diagnostics. When a Module Federation exposes or remotes is not a static object literal, the run records plugin-config-unreadable with the plugin, the key and the reason. It sets degrades_analysis, so the Action and the GitLab template print it in their degraded-inputs warning. Nuxt has a related case: a components: or imports: shape that fallow cannot model. Such a project records plugin-effect-not-modeled, and that entry is silent.
  • The JSON output and both CI integrations report a run that widened to the whole project. They also report a --sarif-file that could not be written, and a format that cannot group results with --group-by.
  • fallow reads Module Federation exposes and remotes. It reads module-federation.config.* and inline plugin options in webpack, rspack, rsbuild, vite and Next.js configs. The plugin call can sit anywhere in the config: in a nested plugin array, in a variable, under tools.rspack.plugins or in a webpack(config) hook. Options held in a const in the same file are read, and so is the array form of exposes. Each exposes target becomes a runtime entry point, and each remotes alias counts as a provided dependency for the code under that config's directory.
  • Nuxt autoImports credits a global/ or islands/ component under the name Nuxt gives it. Each workspace root now gets its own verdict from its own config. components: true, imports: {} and imports: { dirs: [] } count as the Nuxt default. A name imported or re-exported from #components or #imports marks its file as used, and #layers/<name>/ works as a path alias.

Changed

  • fallow dead-code no longer exits 2 when the baseline belongs to another command. It warns and continues. --fail-on-stale-baseline fails the run on such a file. Saving over a baseline of another kind is refused with exit 2.
  • The GitHub Action and the GitLab template log why a JSON read failed. The cause goes to the debug log, and a green run gets no extra line.
  • fallow security --base warns when it cannot map the analysis root into the base worktree.

Bug fixes

  • A package name in a bundler entry is credited as a dependency. A value like react-hot-loader/patch or webpack-hot-middleware/client?reload=true in a webpack, rspack or rsbuild entry used to become an entry pattern that matched no file. The package then showed up as unused.
  • The MCP audit and decision_surface tools detect the base ref again. This regressed in 3.1.0. Thanks @​codingthat for the report and the reproduction (#2699).
  • autoImports: true works in a Nuxt project that turns the scan off. components: false, imports: { scan: false } and the other scan-off shapes no longer count as a custom layout, so unused convention files are reported. Thanks @​Tsuyoshi84 for the report (#2695).

Upgrade notes

  • A CI job that points --baseline at another command's file now fails when --fail-on-stale-baseline is set. Give each command its own baseline file.
  • A Nuxt project with autoImports: true and one of the scan-off shapes will see new unused-file findings. Add a file to entry when it is used in a way fallow cannot see.
  • If you switch on workspace_diagnostics[].kind, handle the two new kinds. Every new JSON field is optional.

title: feat(mobile): launch arguments, permissions at launch, clearKeychain
ci: run the benchmark suites only when a change can reach them
body:
## What and why

- `benchmark.yml` and `mobile.yml` ran all six suites (two Linux jobs for the web benchmark, two Mac jobs with two simulators each and two emulator jobs for the mobile one) on every pull request, docs, testbed, and runner-test-only changes included. Most pull requests here are one of those.
- A `changes` job in each workflow runs dorny/paths-filter over `.github/filters.yml`. The suites are skipped unless the change reaches the runner, that benchmark's engine, or the benchmark app. One filter file, so the shared runner list is written once.
- The six suites are the `Main` ruleset's required checks. A workflow-level `paths:` filter would leave them pending and block the merge; a job skipped by `if:` reports success. That is why the gate is a job, and why the comments and AGENTS.md say never to switch those workflows to `paths:`.
- The gate fails toward running. A `workflow_dispatch` runs the suites, and so does a run whose `changes` job failed (`!cancelled() && (needs.changes.result != 'success' || ...)`). A fork's pull request keeps its existing rule for the agentic suites.
- The mobile suites are four named jobs sharing their steps through YAML anchors instead of a matrix. A matrix job skipped at the job level reports as `ios ${{ matrix.suite }}`, unexpanded (seen on the probe PR #528), so the required checks `ios deterministic` and `ios agentic` would never arrive.
- A push to `main` is filtered the same way, diffed against the commit before the push. The Expo build cache is keyed by native fingerprint, so a merge that skips mobile leaves it as it was.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[pull_request / push to main] --> B[changes: paths-filter]
  B -- runner, engine, or app changed --> C[web, web agent]
  B -- runner, engine, or app changed --> D[ios x2, android x2]
  B -- nothing reached them --> E[skipped: required checks satisfied]
  F[workflow_dispatch] --> C
  F --> D
```

What reaches which suite (`.github/filters.yml`):

| change | web | mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/e2e/src/**`, root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `scripts/**`, the filter file | yes | yes |
| `packages/web/**`, `packages/github/**`, `apps/web-benchmark/**`, `benchmark.yml` | yes | no |
| `packages/mobile/**`, `apps/mobile-benchmark/**`, `mobile.yml`, `.github/actions/expo-app/**` | no | yes |
| `packages/*/tests/**`, any `*.md`, `docs/**`, `apps/testbed/**`, `skills/**`, `.changeset/**`, `spec.yml` | no | no |

Seen on GitHub, not just in a local matcher:

| path | run | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| docs-only pull request (#528, a trailing newline in README.md) | [mobile](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36119621420), [benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36119621422) | `changes` green, all six suites skipped under their required-check names |
| this pull request (workflows and the filter changed) | its own checks | every suite runs |
| `workflow_dispatch` on this branch | [benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36119207154) | filter step skipped, both suites ran and passed |

`ios agentic` is red here on the Stripe PaymentSheet scenario (`LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` on the sheet's label, 23 of 24 pass), exactly as on the last three `main` runs before this branch. Not from this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. (Repo CI lives in AGENTS.md, not on the docs site.)
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

fix(mobile): dismissKeyboard drags the keyboard away on an iPhone
body: - `device.dismissKeyboard()` failed on every iPhone: agent-device presses the keyboard's own dismiss key and refuses with `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` when there is none, by design (callstack/agent-device `packages/contracts/src/tap-keyboard-occlusion.ts`). The engine now does what a user does and what Maestro's `hideKeyboard` does: a short drag at the centre of the screen, which a scroll view turns into a dismissal. - The dismiss key stays first, so an iPad and Android keep the exact path. On a refusal: one capture (the simulator's "Speed up your typing" tip goes through its Continue button, as in Maestro), a 3 % drag, a fresh capture, and a second drag the other way if the keyboard is still up. A keyboard that outlives both fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` naming the app's Done control and Enter as the alternatives. - Horizontal first, vertical second, the reverse of Maestro. On React Native's default `ScrollView` a horizontal micro-drag is no scroll, so it counts as the touch outside the keyboard that dismisses under `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="never"`, while a vertical drag scrolls and dismisses only under `keyboardDismissMode="on-drag"`. Native scroll views that dismiss on a drag alone take the vertical one. Same outcome either way, one drag cheaper on React Native. - Both benchmark onboarding tests call `device.dismissKeyboard()` on both platforms; the title-tap helper is gone. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[keyboard.dismiss] -->|dismissed or already hidden| Z[done] A -->|no dismiss key| B[capture: typing tip? press Continue] B --> C[horizontal drag, 3% of the width] C --> D{capture: keyboard gone?} D -- yes --> Z D -- no --> E[vertical drag, 3% of the height] E --> F{capture: keyboard gone?} F -- yes --> Z F -- no --> G[UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY] ``` | `device.dismissKeyboard()` on an iPhone 17e simulator | per call | | --- | --- | | Maestro's order, vertical first | 9.3 s | | this PR, horizontal first | 4.9 s | | of which: the capture after the drag | 3.6 s | | Android emulator, dismiss key | 30 ms | - The 3.6 s is agent-device's post-gesture snapshot stabilization: the first snapshot after a synthesized `swipe` waits out its 3.5 s distrust deadline when the interactive tree looks unchanged, which it does once the keys are gone (`packages/capture-kit/src/post-gesture-stability.ts` upstream). A `keyboard dismiss` probe right after the drag reads a stale tree for over a second, so it cannot stand in for the capture. Upstream follow-up: the SDK exposing the `postGestureStabilization` request flag its Maestro port already passes. - Code: `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1030` (`dismissKeyboard`), `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1057` (`dismissKeyboardByGesture`), `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1085` (the typing tip). Tests: `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts`, "dismissing a keyboard that has no dismiss key". Benchmark: `apps/mobile-benchmark/tests/device.e2e.ts:46`. - Docs: the `dismissKeyboard` JSDoc in `reference/mobile.mdx`, the `hideKeyboard` row in `migrate/maestro.mdx`; changeset: `@e2edev/mobile` patch. ---

title: test(benchmark): network, location, and biometric surfaces for the device fixture verbs
body: ## What and why `tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts` declared three `device` verbs it could not exercise, skipped as "the app has no surface for this". The app gets the surfaces, the tests run where the tooling can, and what it still cannot do is declared with the reason instead of hidden behind a dependency that was never added. - Three scenarios in the mobile benchmark app, not hard surfaces, each printing what the OS reports the way Control Inventory does for runner verbs: **Network Status** (`expo-network`: type, connected, internet), **Location Reader** (`expo-location`: ask, read once, print), **Biometric Lock** (`expo-local-authentication`: sensor, enrollment, a vault behind the OS prompt). Deps pinned to the SDK 57 versions, permission strings in `app.json`. - `setNetwork` and `setAirplaneMode` pass on the Android emulator: Wi-Fi off moves the connection to cellular, airplane mode cuts it, both restore. On the iOS simulator agent-device 0.21.13 only overrides the status bar (`simctl status_bar override`), the simulator stays online, so that side stays skipped with that reason. - `setLocation` and `clearLocation` pass on both platforms. The reader watches for a fix newer than the tap: a one-shot `getCurrentPositionAsync` answers from the fused provider's cache on Android, the fix before the `geo fix`. Play Services' "turn on location accuracy" sheet is declined (`mayShowUserSettingsDialog: false`) so an unsatisfied setting is an error line, not a system dialog. `clearLocation` is a permission revoke on iOS (the app is relaunched) and `location_mode 0` on Android; no fixture verb turns services back on, so the Android test restores them through adb and says so. - `enrollBiometrics` and `setBiometrics` stay skipped, now for the real reason: agent-device drives Face ID through a `simctl biometric` subcommand no shipped Xcode declares (27.0 included). The skip is computed from `xcrun simctl help` at collection, so the test turns on the day the subcommand exists. The screen itself completes through `notifyutil` on `com.apple.BiometricKit`, checked by hand. Android fingerprint has no enroll verb at all. - `openScenario` waits up to 20 s for the home row: a debug build cold-starts in about ten seconds on the emulator while it fetches its bundle from Metro. README notes the release variant is the reliable local target, as in CI. Where each verb stands after this PR: | Verb | iOS simulator | Android emulator | | --- | --- | --- | | `setNetwork`, `setAirplaneMode` | skipped: status bar override only | passes | | `setLocation` | passes | passes | | `clearLocation` | passes (revokes, relaunch) | passes (services off, adb restore) | | `enrollBiometrics`, `setBiometrics` | skipped until `simctl biometric` ships | skipped: no enroll verb | ```ts test('setLocation moves the position the app reads', async ({ device, screen }) => { await device.setLocation({ latitude: 52.2297, longitude: 21.0122 }); await screen.getByTestId('read-location').tap(); await expect(screen.getByTestId('location-coordinates')).toHaveText('52.2297, 21.0122'); await device.setLocation({ latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522 }); await screen.getByTestId('read-location').tap(); await expect(screen.getByTestId('location-coordinates')).toHaveText('48.8566, 2.3522'); }); ``` The three scenarios are ours, like both Control Inventories, not a port from tester-army. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: test(mobile-benchmark): the biometric skip names the missing simctl subcommand and lifts itself when it ships
body: ## What and why Follow-up to #515, which brought in the Device section and left `enrollBiometrics` / `setBiometrics` skipped as "agent-device 0.21.13 refuses Face ID simulation on the iOS 26 runtime". That is agent-device's message, not the cause. - agent-device drives the simulator's Face ID through a `simctl biometric` subcommand (`biometric enroll yes`, `biometric match face`) and reports the runtime as unsupported when simctl rejects the subcommand. No shipped Xcode declares it, 27.0 included; the simulator itself still enrolls and matches through `notifyutil` on `com.apple.BiometricKit`, checked by hand against the Device section's prompt, so the gap is the fixture's, not the runtime's. - The iOS test's skip is now computed at collection from `xcrun simctl help`: skipped with that reason while the subcommand is missing, live the day it ships, no edit needed. The body leaves the simulator unenrolled again. - Android gets its own declared skip: the emulator's fingerprint answers only once a lock screen and a finger are enrolled by hand, and `enrollBiometrics` takes `faceid` or `touchid` only. - README: a debug build cold-starts in about ten seconds on the emulator while it fetches its bundle from Metro, longer than a suite that reopens the app per test allows; run it against a release build, as CI does. ```ts const biometricGap = simctlBiometricGap(); test( 'enrollBiometrics and setBiometrics answer a biometric prompt', { platforms: ['ios'], ...(biometricGap === undefined ? {} : { skip: biometricGap }) }, async ({ device, screen }) => { /* enroll, unlock, match, unenroll */ }, ); ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: fix(mobile): agent-device 0.21.15, and the tree reads what its Android snapshots carry
body: agent-device 0.21.15 puts on its Android nodes what the engine had to gate tests around: the content description, the heading flag, the role description, the checked state, and the field's hint. `@e2edev/mobile` reads them, and the Control Inventory tests that ran on iOS only run on both platforms. - `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`: `name` is the content description when the node has one, `text` stays the label, which is what the node shows. Before, an Android labeled text view or a filled field was named by what it showed and its `accessibilityLabel` never reached the tree. - `heading: true` makes the node a `heading`. A role description React Native writes for a role Android has no class for (`Tab`, `Tab List`, `Radio Group`) goes through the word table the iOS spelled value already uses (`describedRole`). - `checked` comes off the node ahead of the role/value guess, so `toBeChecked`, `check()`, and `uncheck()` work on Android instead of answering `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - `placeholder` lands in `attributes.placeholder`, so `getByPlaceholder`, `getAttribute('placeholder')`, and `toHaveAttribute` answer on Android. The iOS runner carries it in agent-device's next release (callstack/agent-device#2961), so that test and the tab-role test are `platforms: ['android']` until then. - From 0.21.15 itself: an Android `app.open` returns once the app is readable (callstack/agent-device#2895), and fill verification samples until a deadline (callstack/agent-device#2926), the fix for the CI-only `Android fill verification failed`. | Android raw node | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `TextView` label "Plain controls, every state exposed", contentDescription "Inventory heading", heading | `text "Plain controls, every state exposed"` | `heading "Inventory heading"` text "Plain controls, every state exposed" | | `EditText` label "Ada Lovelace", contentDescription "Name field", placeholder "Type your name" | `textbox "Ada Lovelace"` | `textbox "Name field"` value "Ada Lovelace" placeholder "Type your name" | | `View` roleDescription "Tab", label "Fields" | `group "Fields"` | `tab "Fields"` | | `Switch` checked false | `switch "Wi-Fi switch"`, no state | `switch "Wi-Fi switch" [unchecked]` | `tests/controls.e2e.ts` on the emulator with 0.21.15: | | main | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | tests not run on Android | 8 (6 gated to iOS by `NAMED_BY_LABEL` and `CHECKED_STATE`, placeholder and tab role skipped everywhere) | 1 (the React Native `View` flattening, both platforms) | | Android outcome | | 24 passed, 1 skipped | Whole Android suite: 53 passed, 2 skipped, the permission-prompt alert flake passed on rerun. Whole iOS suite: 47 passed, 2 skipped. `setOrientation` fails on this Mac's iOS 26.5 simulators with 0.21.13 and 0.21.15 alike (agent-device answers "Rotated to landscape-left", the app stays portrait), so it is the host, not this change; CI's iOS 26.2 passes it. Left for their own PRs: scaling Android rects and points by `pixelDensity`, iOS `appstate.state` for `foregroundApp`, the typed ref-miss reason in `errors.ts`, and the root type exports replacing the `Raw*` casts. ---

title: coverage: `e2e run --coverage` reports the routes a run reached, the browser code that ran, and the server code that ran
body:
### Problem

A run tells you which tests passed and nothing about how much of the app they touched. Three questions have no answer today:

- Which routes or screens did this run, or this `explore`, reach? `explore` records a path only on findings; steps carry no location, so it cannot say where it has not been.
- Which lines of the browser bundle ran? Playwright users copy a V8 coverage fixture from a blog post. Cypress users have `@cypress/code-coverage`. e2e users have nothing.
- Which lines of the server ran? The runner already spawns the app from `web({ command })` and owns its environment, but sets nothing that would make Node write coverage.

The cost angle is what makes this worth doing here rather than in a user's fixture. Agentic steps cost model calls, and a per-test coverage map is what a later `--changed` selection would read to run only the tests a diff can reach.

State of the code (2026-09-25): no coverage concept anywhere. Every observation crosses one seam, `TargetSession.observe` in `engine/session.ts`, with the engine's `location`. `cache/route.ts` already reduces a location to a route key and treats a mobile screen title as an opaque route. The `report-1` schema has an `extensions` bag on run, attempt, step, and artifact that no producer writes yet. Artifact kinds are a closed set: screenshot, trace, video, download, log.

### Proposal

Three layers, ordered by what the user has to set up.

**Route and screen coverage, no setup, core only.** A visited set of route keys per attempt from the observe seam, merged per run into route, hit count, and the tests that reached it. Written to the report `extensions` bag on attempt and run, one CLI summary line, and `explore` lists the screens it visited. Works the same for web URLs and mobile screen titles. No percentage in v1: a denominator needs a route inventory, and reading Next or Expo Router manifests is framework knowledge that stays out of core.

**Client JS coverage, web engine.** A new optional contract pair, `artifacts.startCoverage/stopCoverage`, declared like trace and video, driven by `--coverage` or `coverage: true` in config. Core records a new `coverage` artifact kind and never sees a page or a CDP session. The web engine implements it with V8 first (`page.coverage`, every page in the attempt's context, raw V8 JSON per attempt, zero app config, Chromium only). Istanbul mode follows on Playwright 1.64: PR microsoft/playwright#42684 (merged 2026-09-16) makes `tracing.start({ coverage: true })` harvest `window.__coverage__` into `coverage.json` inside the trace, in every browser, for an app instrumented with vite-plugin-istanbul or babel-plugin-istanbul. The engine already rewrites that zip.

**Server coverage, core.** When coverage is on and the target declares `command`, set `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` to a run-scoped directory in the app process env and register the files after teardown. Servers that exit on SIGTERM (Next dev, Vite dev) write their data. `reuseExisting` means no server coverage, and the summary says so.

**Rendering** lives in a separate reporter package, `@e2edev/coverage`, on monocart-coverage-reports: raw V8 and Istanbul to lcov, html, and a text summary, plus a per-test file map. Raw per-attempt files are always written; core without the package says where they are. V8 and Istanbul data are never merged into one report.

**Mobile JS coverage is a spike, not part of this.** Hermes CDP implements no `Profiler.*PreciseCoverage` method. The only route is babel-plugin-istanbul in Metro plus pulling `global.__coverage__` out of the app, possibly through Metro's inspector proxy with `Runtime.evaluate`. Native Swift and Kotlin coverage stays with xcodebuild and JaCoCo.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
export default {
  coverage: true, // or `e2e run --coverage`
  reporters: [coverage({ reports: ['lcov', 'html', 'text-summary'] })], // @e2edev/coverage
  targets: [{ engine: web({ url: 'http://localhost:3000', command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'] } }) }],
} satisfies E2EConfig;

// e2e/engine, additive and optional, declared in a pair like startTrace/stopTrace
interface EngineArtifacts {
  startCoverage?(ctx: EngineAttemptContext): Promise<void>;
  stopCoverage?(ctx: EngineCleanupContext): Promise<{ format: 'v8' | 'istanbul'; path: string }>;
}

// report-1: attempt.extensions and run.extensions carry the visited routes; artifact.kind gains 'coverage'
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Visited routes per attempt and run in the report `extensions` bag, CLI summary line, explore lists visited screens. Schema fixtures and report reference docs in the same review.
- [ ] Contract: optional `artifacts.startCoverage/stopCoverage`, `coverage` artifact kind, `--coverage` flag and config key. `writing-an-engine.mdx` and `reference/engine.mdx`.
- [ ] Web engine V8 collection across every page of the attempt.
- [ ] `@e2edev/coverage` reporter with the per-test file map and a docs page on source-map requirements per bundler.
- [ ] Server coverage on managed app processes.
- [ ] Web engine Istanbul mode on Playwright 1.64.
- [ ] Spike: Hermes counters through the Metro inspector proxy, go or no-go.
- [ ] Follow-on: `--changed` selection from the per-test map.

### Open questions

- `resetOnNavigation: false` is documented as discouraged and not guaranteed across navigations. If data is lost on cross-origin navigations, the engine restarts collection on `framenavigated` and concatenates.
- Where does a percentage denominator come from: a manifest the user points at, a framework adapter, or nothing?
- Reporter at run end in the runner process, or an `e2e coverage report` command over an existing `.e2e/`? Probably both.
- Playwright peer range is `>=1.63.0 <2`; Istanbul mode feature-detects the tracing option or raises the floor.

### Which surface

config keys, CLI flags, engine contract (`e2e/engine`), report or cache format

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today. All additions are optional; existing engines and configs keep working.

Research notes: `.agent/plans/code-coverage-plan.md` in the `t3code/8daff428` worktree. Sources: Playwright class-coverage docs, microsoft/playwright#42684, stevez/nextcov, cenfun/monocart-coverage-reports, cdpstatus.reactnative.dev.

title: cli: `e2e doctor` checks the machine, the project config, and the test tooling already in the repo
body:
### Problem

Setup failures surface one at a time, at run time, as errors. What has hit real first runs so far: Node too old, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` with no key or stored login, a peer mismatch between `e2e` and `@e2edev/web` after a canary, a leaked `next start` on the target port making the newest page 404, `.gitignore` missing the run output entries, a stale skill copy. Each costs a run to discover.

There is also no way to ask e2e what it sees in a project. A team with a Playwright or Maestro suite gets scaffolded like a greenfield project, though `/migrate/playwright` and `/migrate/maestro` exist. Coding agents setting up e2e have no machine-readable check to run before editing a config.

No web e2e framework ships a doctor. Playwright has `install --dry-run`, Cypress has `verify` and `info`. Prior art is `react-native doctor` (categories, `getDiagnostics`, `runAutomaticFix`), `expo-doctor` (project checks, exit 1, per-check opt-out), `appium driver doctor xcuitest` (per-driver prerequisites), and `flutter doctor -v` for the output shape. `npx agent-device doctor` already covers the mobile toolchain and our docs point to it three times.

Most of the probes exist in `e2e init` today (package manager from lockfiles, `package.json` validity, config presence, gitignore entries, skill drift, MCP registration), plus `collectEnvironment`, `Telemetry.disabledBy`, the OAuth credential store's offline expiry listing, and `loadProjectConfig`. Nothing detects the app framework or the dev command.

### Proposal

`e2e doctor` reads the project and the machine, prints one line per check with a fix, exits 1 on any fail, and emits JSON for agents. Each check is a small object: id, section, status (ok, warn, fail, skip), one-line message, fix as a command or docs URL, and whether `--fix` can do it. Offline by default; `--online` adds npm dist-tag and model endpoint checks.

**Machine.** Node against the floor. Package manager and lockfile agreement (a `bun.lock` next to a `pnpm-lock.yaml`). Chromium in the Playwright browsers path. On macOS, Xcode command line tools and simctl runtimes when a mobile target exists. Android SDK, adb, at least one AVD when an Android target exists.

**Project.** Config found, loads, resolves, with `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, `CONFIG_AMBIGUOUS`, `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`, `INVALID_CONFIG` as rows instead of a crash. Per target: engine package installed, its `e2e` peer range satisfied by the installed runner, Playwright inside the engine's range, `url` port free or answering, `command` executable on PATH, a warning when `url` names a loopback port nothing listens on and no `command` is declared. Test files matched by the config, zero is a warning. Model: an agent configured, a gateway key in env or a stored login that has not expired, `ai` installed. Secrets referenced in config whose `E2E_SECRET_<NAME>` is unset. `.gitignore` entries, skill copy current, MCP registration for the detected coding agent, a CI workflow referencing `e2e run`, telemetry state and its reason.

**What else is here.** Other test tooling by config files and dependencies, with file counts and a link to the migration page where one exists: Playwright, Cypress, Detox, Maestro, Selenium, WebdriverIO, Appium, Puppeteer, TestCafe, Nightwatch, CodeceptJS, XCUITest targets, Espresso `androidTest`. Informational, never a fail. App framework and dev port from dependencies and scripts (Next, Vite, Remix, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Expo, bare React Native), warning when the config `url` port differs from the framework default or the dev script's `--port`.

`--fix` handles only what init already writes: gitignore entries, the skill copy, MCP registration, the Chromium install. Everything else prints the command. `init` runs the project section first so a Playwright user hears about the migration page before scaffolding.

```text
$ npx e2e doctor
 machine
 ✓ node 26.6.2 (floor 22.12)
 ✓ pnpm 12.3.4, pnpm-lock.yaml
 ✗ chromium not installed            pnpm exec playwright install chromium
 project
 ✓ e2e.config.ts loads, 2 targets
 ✗ @e2edev/web 0.11.0 wants e2e >=0.15.0 <1, installed 0.16.0-canary…   pnpm add -D @e2edev/web@canary
 ! localhost:3000 answers nothing and web has no command   docs: /starting-your-app
 ✓ model: gateway key in AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
 ✓ skill .agents/skills/e2e current, MCP registered in .mcp.json
 - telemetry off (E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED)
 also here
 · playwright: 42 spec files, playwright.config.ts        docs: /migrate/playwright
 · next 16, dev on 3000

$ npx e2e doctor --json   # { version, exitCode, checks: [{ id, section, status, message, fix, fixable }] }
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Check runner and output: check type, sections, TTY and plain rendering, `--json`, `--verbose`, exit codes. Register beside `telemetry` in the CLI, section in `reference/cli.mdx`.
- [ ] Machine checks gated by the targets present.
- [ ] Project checks: config as rows, per-target engine and peer checks, url and command, test count, model and login, secrets env, gitignore, skill, MCP, CI workflow, telemetry.
- [ ] Other test tooling and app framework detection with migration links and the port mismatch warning.
- [ ] `--fix` for gitignore, skill, MCP, Chromium.
- [ ] `init` runs the project checks first.
- [ ] Skill and MCP guidance: agents run `e2e doctor --json` before editing config (`skills/e2e/references/setup.md`, `debugging.md`).
- [ ] One `doctor_completed` telemetry event with statuses by check id, no paths or messages; `telemetry.mdx` event table.

### Decisions to confirm

- Checks are data, not a plugin API. Engines do not register checks in v1; a contract member is an option if a third engine appears.
- Doctor never executes a project config other than `e2e.config.ts`. Framework detection reads `package.json` and known file names only.
- `--fix` never installs packages. The exact `pnpm add -D` line is enough.

### Open questions

- Probe the target `url` with a loopback HEAD in offline mode? Loopback is not the network, but a request changes state for some dev servers.
- Peer-range checks from `node_modules` manifests or the lockfile? Manifests are what loads.
- `xcrun simctl list runtimes --json` takes a second or two on some machines. Accept or cache.

### Which surface

CLI flags, config keys (read only), docs only for the migration links

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today. New command; `init` gains a pre-check but writes the same files.

Research notes: `.agent/plans/e2e-doctor-plan.md` in the `t3code/8daff428` worktree. Sources: react-native-community/cli healthChecks, expo-doctor, appium extension CLI docs.

title: fix(github): a --last-failed rerun updates the pull request comment as one run
body: On #534 every check was green while two comments said 🔴. The mobile jobs run `e2e run || e2e run --last-failed`, and the second pass ran with `GITHUB_TOKEN` stripped on purpose: the rerun's page lists only the tests it ran again, so posting it would have replaced 48 results with one. The comment therefore froze at the first pass. This makes the second pass update it as one run. - `e2e`: a `--last-failed` run hands its reporters the report it selected from as `FinishedRun.lastRun` (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`, `last-run.ts` now reads the document and derives the failed ids from it). Additive, optional, documented in `reference/reporters.mdx`. - `@e2edev/github`: `foldLastRun` (`packages/github/src/merge.ts`) folds the rerun into that report before rendering. A test the rerun left out keeps its first-pass result, a test that failed then passed is `flaky` with both runs' attempts, a test that failed again stays failed with all attempts, counts cover the whole suite, and the footer's duration spans both passes. The rerun's status and errors decide the outcome, since the tests it left out are exactly the ones that did not fail. - `mobile.yml`: the second pass keeps the token. Header comment rewritten. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[pass 1: full suite] -- fails --> B[pass 2: --last-failed] B --> C{lastRun?} C -- yes --> D[fold: carried + rerun] --> E[update comment] C -- no --> E ``` | Comment on #534 | before | after this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | ios (job green) | 🔴 1 failed, 48 passed, 2 skipped | 🟢 1 flaky, 48 passed, 2 skipped | | android agent (job green) | 🔴 1 failed, 19 passed | 🟢 1 flaky, 19 passed | A fold by `id` matches per target, agent, and repeat; a report from another project leaves the rerun as it is. `docs/github.mdx` gets a section on the one-step rerun. ---

title: fix(report): run page reads top down: source under the title, evidence kinds linked without paths, folded attempt runs, one target named once
body: The `@e2edev/github` comment for a mobile-benchmark run (workflow run 36149225389) was hard to read: the source link and the target came last, after three URL-encoded artifact paths per failure; four attempts that failed alike were retold one by one; every test row carried `(android-emulator)` although the file row above it said so, and the footer counted two targets when one ran. The mobile engine also appended agent-device's `Hint: Check command arguments and run --help for usage examples.` to every error. - Each failure block opens with the title and, right under it, the line to look at and the target (only when several ran). Evidence closes the block. - With a run page URL, each evidence kind is its own link and the paths inside the upload are gone from the comment: the download has one directory per test, named after it. `summary.md` (no URL, a reader with the checkout) keeps the paths. - A failed step that is not the agent's is one code span, the call it was: `expect.not.toHaveText getByTestId("location-status")`. - `attemptsLine` folds consecutive alike attempts: `Failed on all 4 attempts: **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 8, then at step 20 (3 times).` (`packages/e2e/src/report/failure-text.ts`). - The page's targets are the ones a selected result ran on (`ranTargets` in `packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts`), so `--target android-emulator` names it in the footer only, and a test row never repeats the target its file row names. - `@e2edev/mobile` drops a hint that is CLI advice (`CLI_ADVICE` in `packages/mobile/src/errors.ts`); a recovery hint still reaches the model. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | `**🔴 device fixture › setLocation and clearLocation change what the app reads (android-emulator)**` | `**🔴 device fixture › setLocation and clearLocation change what the app reads**` | | `**ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 20 of 21: \`expect.not.toHaveText\` \`getByTestId("location-status")\`, after 1.5s` | `[tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts:131](…)` | | `> expect.poll(...) …` | `**ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 20 of 21: \`expect.not.toHaveText getByTestId("location-status")\`, after 1.5s` | | `- Failed differently on all 4 attempts: **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 8, then **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 20, then **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 20, then **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 20.` | `> expect.poll(...) …` | | `- Screen: \`dev.e2e.benchmark\`` | `- Failed on all 4 attempts: **ASSERTION_FAILED** at step 8, then at step 20 (3 times).` | | `[tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts:131](…) · Evidence: [screenshot, log](…): \`android-emulator/tests_device-fixture.e2e.ts__device_20fixture__setLocation_20and_20clearLocation_20change_20what_20the_20app_20reads/default/attempt-1/screenshots/001-failure.png\`, \`android-emulator/…/attempt-1/failure/screen.txt\`` | `- Screen: \`dev.e2e.benchmark\`` | | `… · 2 targets (ios-simulator, android-emulator) · …` | `Evidence: [screenshot](…), [log](…)` | | | `… · android-emulator · …` | Docs: `docs/github.mdx` example and the artifacts note. title: feat(web): viewport: null follows the browser window
body: - The engine always emulated a fixed page size (1280x720 by default): `newContext({ viewport })` on the shared-browser path, `page.setViewportSize` on the persistent one. In a headed run or a hosted browser's live view (Kernel, reported while writing a cookbook against us) the page rendered in one corner of the window, and matching the two sizes by hand cannot fix it, since the window's tab strip and toolbar eat part of the height. - `web({ viewport: null })` emulates no size, like Playwright's own `viewport: null`. The page fills the window. `undefined` still means 1280x720; `web.setViewport` still fixes a size for the rest of the attempt. - Playwright reports no viewport of its own under `null`, so every reader of `page.viewportSize() ?? DEFAULT_VIEWPORT` went through one helper, `currentViewport(page)` (`packages/web/src/support.ts`), which measures `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` in the page when nothing is emulated: observation size and pixel scale, viewport swipes, drag reachability, and the video segment size at start. - CDP recovery restores the previous page's emulated size when one was set mid-attempt and otherwise leaves the reattached page at the window's size. ```ts title="e2e.config.ts" { name: 'hosted', engine: web({ ...app, browser: kernel(), viewport: null }) } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[viewport option] -->|undefined| B[1280x720 emulated] A -->|size| C[size emulated] A -->|null| D[no emulation, page fills window] D --> E["currentViewport: innerWidth x innerHeight"] E --> F[observation, pixels, swipe, drag, video size] ``` Docs: new "Fill the window" section on `/viewports`, the option's JSDoc in `/reference/web`, a pointer from the hosted-browsers section of `/browser`, and the skill's setup table. Changeset: `@e2edev/web` minor. ---

title: fix(runner): session file names keep target and session name apart
fix(locator): getAttribute and toHaveAttribute read own attributes only
fix(web): toHaveClass polls for a node that is not there yet
body: - Repro: `expect(web).toHaveClass(web.locator('#late-card'), 'card late', { timeout: 1800 })` on a node rendered 600 ms after load failed within a few milliseconds with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. `expect(web.locator('#late-card')).toHaveAttribute('class', 'card late')` on the same locator waited and passed. - Cause: the matcher decided "keep polling or fail" with `error instanceof TestError`. A project loads the engine from its config file in one module realm (tsx) while the runner's core runs in another, so the `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` the locator engine threw was a `TestError` from a copy of `e2e` the engine never imported. `name` and `code` said `TestError` / `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, `instanceof` said no, and the read error escaped the poll. - Fix: `isTestErrorCode(error, code)` in `packages/web/src/support.ts` matches by name and code. `toHaveClass` treats only `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` as one more poll; `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `POLICY_DENIED`, and every other code still surface at once. `isClassified` gets the same name fallback for `TestError`, `ConfigurationError`, and `InfrastructureError`, so a foreign runner error is never rewrapped as `ENGINE_FAILURE`. - The other `instanceof EngineError` sites in the engine (`operation-budget.ts`, `observation-capture.ts`, `surface.ts`, `provider.ts`) compare errors this package raised itself in the same realm, so they stay. - The existing `web-platform` suite never hit this because it passes the engine through `rawConfig` from the vitest realm, one copy. The new `tests/integration/web-class-assertions.test.ts` goes through a config file like a project does, and failed before the fix. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[toHaveClass poll] --> B[target.getAttribute] B -- value --> C[match] B -- throws --> D{name TestError and code LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND?} D -- yes --> A D -- no --> E[assertion fails now] ``` ```ts export function isTestErrorCode(cause: unknown, code: string): cause is Error & { readonly code: string } { return cause instanceof Error && cause.name === 'TestError' && (cause as { code?: unknown }).code === code; } ``` - Decision left as is, now documented in `docs/reference/expect.mdx` and the Playwright migration table: `toHaveClass('')` reads the `class` attribute, so it matches `class=""` and not an element with no attribute. Playwright accepts both. The contract speaks of the attribute, so this PR does not change it; a test pins the current behavior. --- - The fixture markup for these tests (late card, duplicate spans, `class=""`) is on its own `/classes` page. On the home page the late card landed between the MCP suite's two observations and turned its "screen unchanged" text into a diff, which is what the first CI run's Node 22 job tripped on.

title: fix(expect): value and text matchers refuse a secure field instead of judging its withheld value as empty
body:
- Repro: fill a `type=password` input, then `await expect(screen.getByLabel('Password')).toHaveValue('')`. It passed. `.not.toHaveValue('')` failed with `observed: value ""`. A test asserting a sign-in form was cleared passed with the password still in the field. `toHaveText('')` had the same gap.
- Cause: the engine withholds a secure field's value and text (`states.secure`, no `value`, no `text`), and `readField` in `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts` read that gap as `''`. Redacted is not empty.
- Fix: `toHaveValue`, `toHaveText`, and `toContainText` refuse a secure field with `POLICY_DENIED`, the same code and message `inputValue()` and `textContent()` already throw. The refusal runs right after each sample, before the predicate or the failure message reads the node, so it holds negated and in list form and never prints the value. `toHaveAccessibleName` and the state matchers still answer on a secure field; a plain empty control still reads as `''`.

```ts
await screen.getByLabel('Password').fill(secret);
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Password')).toHaveValue('');
// POLICY_DENIED: reading values from a secure field is denied: getByLabel("Password")
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[sample node] --> R{secure and matcher reads value or text?}
  R -- yes --> D[throw POLICY_DENIED]
  R -- no --> E{evaluable?}
  E -- yes --> P[predicate]
  E -- no --> W[keep polling]
```

- Tests: unit with a fake `states.secure` node (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/expect-async-value.test.ts`), scripted engine through the runner for value and text, plain, negated, and list form (`tests/integration/scripted-matchers.test.ts`), and a browser-backed password input holding a marker string with a plain `Email` input holding the same marker as the control (`tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts`); the report never carries the marker.
- Docs: `docs/reference/expect.mdx`, `screen.mdx`, `errors.mdx`, `docs/security.mdx`, and the skill's `writing-tests.md` and `debugging.md` name the denial.

title: fix(runner): artifact directories never collide for ids that sanitize alike
fix(web): an exact label query composes exactly as a has filter or a scope
body: - `rows.filter({ has: screen.getByLabel('Name', { exact: true }) })` matched a row whose input is labelled `Last Name` too, so `.first().getByRole('button', { name: 'Remove' }).tap()` removed the wrong row. Standalone, the same query matched one input. - Cause: `project()` in `packages/web/src/locators.ts` built the composable form of an exact label query as Playwright's substring `getByLabel`, since Playwright's chain had no selector for the reader's exact label predicate. The standalone path kept the predicate; the composed path lost it. - Fix: a third selector engine, `e2e-label=` (`packages/web/src/label-selector.ts`), runs the in-page reader on the labelable controls under its root, closed shadow roots included, and keeps those whose labels equal the value after whitespace normalization. That is the same comparison the surface makes standalone, so a `has` filter or a scope on an exact label now matches exactly what the standalone query matches. - Playwright's own `getByLabel(..., { exact: true })` was the shorter route and I did not take it: it reads a label's aria-hidden text, so `Display name*` would match standalone and miss inside `has`. The new test pins that case. - `SELECTOR_ENGINES` (`packages/web/src/selector-engines.ts`) is now the list both registration paths (launched browser, CDP context) read. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["getByLabel('Name', { exact: true })"] --> B{composed?} B -- "standalone" --> C["e2e-roots=<labelable> then surface keeps labels == 'Name'"] B -- "has / scope, before" --> D["e2e-roots= >> getByLabel('Name', substring)"] B -- "has / scope, after" --> E["e2e-label={value:'Name',...} runs the reader in the page"] ``` ```ts const rows = screen.getByRole('listitem'); await rows .filter({ has: screen.getByLabel('Name', { exact: true }) }) .first() .getByRole('button', { name: 'Remove' }) .tap(); ``` New browser-backed test: `packages/web/tests/integration/label-composition.test.ts` on a `/rows` fixture (`Last Name`, `Name*` with an aria-hidden marker, and a label carrying `"` and `>>`). ---

title: fix(web): a control inherits disabled from a fieldset and an aria-disabled ancestor
body:
- Repro: `
`. `button.disabled` is `false`, `button.matches(':disabled')` is `true`. The reader read the property, so `toBeEnabled` passed, `toBeDisabled` failed, `isDisabled()` answered `false`, and the agent's tree listed a dead button as a live one. Playwright's `toBeDisabled` passes on the same button. - Same for a widget under `
`: Playwright inherits the state down the tree, e2e read the element's own attribute only. - `disabled` is now the effective state (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`, `isDisabled`): ```mermaid flowchart LR A[el.matches ':disabled'] -- true --> D[disabled] A -- false --> B[own aria-disabled=true] B -- true --> D B -- false --> C{role takes aria-disabled?} C -- no --> E[enabled] C -- yes --> W[nearest aria-disabled up the chain, across shadow hosts] W -- true --> D W -- false or none --> E ``` - `:disabled` is the browser's own answer for a form control: own attribute, a disabled fieldset with the first-legend exception, nested fieldsets, a disabled optgroup. No hand-written fieldset walk. - The aria chain uses Playwright's role list (`kAriaDisabledRoles`) and stop rule (`aria-disabled="false"` cuts it), memoized per read so a subtree under one disabled ancestor costs one walk. - Own `aria-disabled="true"` still counts on any element, as before. Playwright limits that to the role list too; kept the wider reading so no existing `toBeDisabled` on a `div` flips. - `packages/web/tests/integration/read-node-states.test.ts` checks fieldset, first legend, second legend, nested fieldsets, aria ancestor, `false` cut, shadow root, and compares each case with Playwright's `isDisabled()` on the same page. The runner's kitchen-sink test gets a fenced button and a legend button so `isDisabled()`, `toBeDisabled`, and `toBeEnabled` agree through the CLI. - `docs/reference/expect.mdx` says what `disabled` means on the web. ---

title: fix(web): an editor's value keeps the whitespace it renders
body:
- Repro: a `contenteditable` editor with `white-space: pre-wrap` holding `" keep spaces "` failed `toHaveValue(' keep spaces ')` and passed `toHaveValue('keep spaces')`. A native input with the same value passed the first and failed the second, which is what `docs/reference/expect.mdx` promises for `toHaveValue`: the value as it is, spaces and newlines included. - Cause: `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts` trimmed the host's `innerText` before reporting it as the textbox value, to make the `


` an empty editor renders (which `innerText` reads as `"\n"`) read as `''`. - Fix: an editor with no text nodes (the `


` placeholder), or with only markup whitespace that `innerText` renders as that one newline, reads as `''`; anything else is the rendered text as is. Typed spaces are text nodes, so a pre-wrap editor holding `" "` keeps them. The zero-width no-break space Slate and Quill pad an empty line with is dropped, so an empty Slate editor still reads as `''`. `innerText` already follows the editor's `white-space` rule, so a `white-space: normal` editor still collapses its spaces and a `pre-wrap` one keeps them. The `textLimit` cut is unchanged. ```ts const rendered = textOf(el).replace(/\uFEFF/g, ''); const text = (el.textContent ?? '').replace(/\uFEFF/g, ''); value = text === '' || (text.trim() === '' && rendered === '\n') ? '' : rendered; ``` - Tests: the reader test in `packages/web/tests/integration/read-node-roles.test.ts` covers pre-wrap, two pre-wrap paragraphs, a normal editor, `


` under normal and pre-wrap, a whitespace-only pre-wrap editor, an empty host, empty and multi-line Slate documents, and a native input; the `/editor` fixture page gains a `Code` pre-wrap editor and `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` asserts `toHaveValue`, `not.toHaveValue`, and `inputValue()` through the runner. - Docs: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` and `docs/reference/expect.mdx` now say an editor's value is its rendered text, kept like a textarea's, and an empty editor reads as `''`. Playwright's `toHaveValue` does not apply to `contenteditable` at all, so there is no parity to keep here; the contract is e2e's own. ---

Dark mode

The agent tree lists an unnamed switch. Same for `role="checkbox"`, `role="radio"`, ``, `role="gridcell"`, a custom element with `role="button"` whose text is behind its shadow root, and ``. - Cause: `accessibleName` in `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts` named from content for a hand-picked role list, `childrenNameOf` read light `childNodes` only, and `reset` was mapped to `button` but only `button` and `submit` took the `value`. - The role list is now accname's, the same list Playwright's `roleUtils.allowsNameFromContent` uses, plus `listitem`, `status`, and `alert`, which the tree already named. `NAME_FROM_CONTENT_ROLES` in `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`. - Content collection follows Playwright's walk (`contentChildrenOf`): a `` reads its assigned nodes, a host reads its unslotted light children and then its shadow tree, a closed root from the record the init script keeps. A `` is `display: contents`, so both readers space it like a block (`* Custom`, not `*Custom`). - `submit` and `reset` read their `value`, else `Submit` or `Reset`, as Chrome and Playwright do. - Tests: `packages/web/tests/integration/read-node-names.test.ts` asserts the tree name and Playwright's `getByRole(role, { name, exact: true })` land on the same element for 15 cases; `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` runs `toHaveCount(1)` and `toHaveAccessibleName(name)` on one locator through the real runner for six of them. - Docs: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` names the roles and the shadow tree rule. title: fix(web): a response body the browser could not read rejects text() and json()
body: - Repro: a server answers `200` with `Content-Length: 1000`, writes a fragment, and destroys the socket. `web.waitForResponse` resolved with status 200 and `text()` of `''`, because the body read fell back to an empty buffer (`response.body().catch(() => Buffer.alloc(0))`). A test asserting an empty body passed, and a test wanting the transport failure had nothing to catch. - The read is still eager and the response still resolves once the body is known. `url`, `status`, and `headers` stay readable. `text()` and `json()` now reject with `ACTION_FAILED` naming the browser's reason, `net::ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH` for the repro, read from `request().failure()` since Chromium's own body error is a generic `No data found for resource`. - A genuinely empty body (`200` with `Content-Length: 0`, or `204`) still reads as `''`. - `ACTION_FAILED` over `ENGINE_FAILURE`: the app under test broke the transfer, not the runner, and the docs already file a `waitForResponse` nothing matches under the same code. ```ts const [response] = await Promise.all([ web.waitForResponse('**/api/orders'), screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' }).tap(), ]); expect(response.status).toBe(200); await response.text(); // rejects: ACTION_FAILED, net::ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH ``` Two behaviours to know about, both of which used to resolve `''`: a fetch the page aborts before its body finishes rejects `text()` with `net::ERR_ABORTED`, and a redirect rejects with Playwright's `Response body is unavailable for redirect responses`, since Chromium never keeps a redirect body. `status` is unaffected, so a test checking only the status keeps passing. A fire-and-forget `fetch` whose body the page never reads still resolves with the full body (checked up to 20 MB). `packages/web/src/web.ts` (`readResponseBody`), test in `packages/web/tests/integration/wait-for-response.test.ts` against a local `node:http` server. ---
