Audit 2026-09-25: findings that need a design decision
body:
## Decisions needed before a fix

Findings from the 2026-09-25 external audit (canary 0.15.0-canary-20260924194828, HEAD 7d93c085) that are by-design behaviors, API additions, or cache-key changes that would invalidate every committed recording. Each has a proposal; none is started.

### Cache: context identity (one decision covers all)

Any new key field turns every committed recording under `apps/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` and `apps/mobile-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` into a miss until re-recorded. Decide the shape once, ship one re-record.

- **B16** `agentContext` is not in the trace cache key. A test whose `agentContext` changes from "Daily" to "Monthly" replays the Daily recording. Proposal: digest of `agentContext` in the key.
- **B22** no session/account/role identity in the key. A recording made on account A replays on account B, so a negative access-control test passes falsely. Proposal: opt-in `cacheScope` (string) on the test or step, hashed into the key; document that persona tests must set it. No tokens in the key.
- **B21** query string ignored by `routeOf` (unit-tested on purpose). `/chores?audit=safe` recording replays on `?audit=unsafe`. Proposal: query participates by default, `volatileParams: [...]` on the target or test to ignore tracking params.
- **B26** origin ignored by `routeOf`. Same path on another host replays. Proposal: current origin in the start precondition, miss on mismatch; explicit allow list for real multi-domain flows.
- **B28** numeric path segment folds to `:id`, `/records/1` replays on `/records/2`. Proposal: keep the fold (it is what makes reseeded ids replay), but hand off when the instruction or params mention the id, or offer `routeSegments: 'exact'`.
- **D5** executor version outside the key by design. A policy change in a custom executor does not invalidate old traces. Proposal: `producer.version` compat rule, opt-in sharing across versions, hit/miss reason in the report.

### Cache: end-of-step evidence (one API decision)

The replayed click is real; only the effect check is skipped when the recorded end anchors are weak. Eight repros, one gap: anchors prove presence, not effect.

- **B20 / B27** no anchors recorded when the effect is a disappearance, a `checked` flip, or a same-node text mutation; replay self-finalizes unconditionally.
- **B23 / B31** `MAX_TRACE_ANCHORS = 8` in document order drops the ninth, business-critical leaf, including the one anchor an author added to disambiguate a route.
- **B24** a new `role=alert` beside the recorded success anchor is ignored.
- **B25** `isVolatileAnchor` drops `3 records imported`, keeps generic `Import completed`.
- **B29** an anchor already present before the action counts as proof.
- **B30** `endScreen` accepts an `undecided` end route when generic anchors are present.

Proposal: (1) never self-finalize on an empty anchor set, hand off to the executor instead; (2) record absences and state flips as anchors; (3) prefer identity-bearing anchors (text unique across the delta, route-specific testIds) when cutting to the limit; (4) an explicit `postconditions` option on `agent.act` for authors who need exact values. (1) to (3) are library changes with a replay-rate cost; (4) is new API. Pick which of these to ship first.

### Security defaults

- **D3** `web({ basicAuth })` answers a 401 challenge from any origin (documented). Playwright 1.63 supports `httpCredentials.origin`. Proposal: default to the target origin, `basicAuth.origins` for extras. Changes documented behavior in docs/security.mdx.
- **D4** `web({ headers })` is scoped by site, not origin; another port on the same host receives the preview header. Proposal: exact origin by default, explicit extras. Same doc.

### Runner semantics

- **PR #559 (B15)** carries the pixel taint across a session restore, so every consumer of a session saved after a secret fill (every post-login test) starts without pixels and its trace is rewritten. Alternative: carry only the ledger values and leave the taint per session. Decide before merge.
- **PR #548 (B17)** appends an 8-hex digest to every artifact segment that sanitization changed, so nearly every existing test's artifact directory moves once. Alternative: injective escaping, less readable.
- **PR #561 (B14)** adds a required `redaction` field to the public `StoredArtifact` type; a text download scanned with nothing to redact is labelled `complete`.
- **PR #558 (B7)** stops templating the recorded verdict summary, so a whole replay shows the recording run's unique value in its summary.
- **PR #560 (B4)** drops zero-size named elements from the agent tree while keeping their children; document root forced visible in tree mode.

- **PR #556 (B13)** fixes the lost callback error by adding an optional `settleAttempt(context)` hook to the engine contract (SPI stays 1, the hook is optional). Approve the SPI addition or ask for a runner-only alternative before merging.

- **D1** `skip()` after a failed `expect.soft` reports SKIPPED, exit 0, and a value soft failure leaves no trace in the report. Documented. Proposal: keep the soft failure sticky (FAIL), or a distinct status plus a CI flag; mark fail-then-skip on retry visibly.
- **D2** `artifacts.settle()` runs outside every budget and `store.put` gets no AbortSignal; SIGINT waited 12 s on a slow store. Proposal: `artifacts.uploadTimeout`, signal to `put`, `uploadStatus` in the report entry. API addition.
- **Store policy** `required` vs `best-effort` for CI evidence publishing.
- **B9** `waitForResponse` reads the whole body before returning; SSE and slow streams time out at the header stage. Proposal: return after headers, lazy bounded `text()`/`json()`. Behavior change to a public method.

### Matcher contract

- **toBeDefined(null)** fails in e2e, passes in Playwright and Jest. Proposal: align to `!== undefined`.
- **toContain({id:1})** on an array of objects passes in e2e (deep equality), fails in Playwright (strict). Proposal: document as a deliberate difference in a migration table.
- **toHaveClass('')** passes for `class=""` but fails when the attribute is absent; Playwright accepts both.

### Reporting and DX (P2, no repro of a bug)

- Passing `expect(value)` and `expect.poll` produce no report step; named checkpoints.
- A cache approval point after a chosen API or DB check (value assertions do not approve recordings today).
- Aggregated adaptation narrative in the report: first action had no effect, agent used an alternate entry, required route violated or unchecked.
- Distinguish "skipped by policy" vs "not configured" vs "write error" vs "overwritten" for a missing screenshot.
- Immutable run directories or a `latest` pointer when `--artifacts` is reused across runs.
- Native visual regression (`toHaveScreenshot`), popup control, clock, `addInitScript` for Playwright migrations.

## Shipped as PRs

| PR | Finding | Change |
|---|---|---|
| #544 | B18 | session file names encode target and name |
| #545 | B2 | attribute reads use own properties only |
| #546 | B12 | toHaveClass polls across module copies |
| #547 | B11 | value and text matchers denied on a secure field |
| #548 | B17 | artifact segments never collide |
| #549 | B10 | exact label stays exact inside filter has |
| #550 | B1 | disabled inherits from fieldset and aria ancestors |
| #551 | B6 | native checked and selected win over aria |
| #552 | B3 | editor value keeps whitespace |
| #553 | B5 | accessible names from content roles, shadow, reset |
| #554 | B8 | response body read failure rejects text and json |
| #555 | nits | service stack abort test waits for readiness, verdict wording |
| #556 | B13 | callback error survives attempt end, dialog keeps classified errors |
| #558 | B7 | cache refuses templating on colliding param values |
| #559 | B15 | session restore carries the secret ledger and taint |
| #560 | B4 | visibility reads boxes, svg, details, display contents |
| #561 | B14 | download redaction reports the truth, text downloads scanned |

title: fix(cache): refuse to record a step whose unique() value collides with another param
body: - A recording is text with no note of which param a value came from. `templateTrace` replaced every occurrence of a `unique()` value across the recorded fields, so a plain param that happened to spell the same text was stored as the marked param's slot. - Repro: `agent.act('fill the title {title} and choose frequency {frequency}', { params: { title: unique(title), frequency: 'Daily' } })` recorded while `title` was `Daily` stored `select('Daily')` as `select('{{param:/title}}')`. The next run, with title `Weekly`, selected Weekly and saved the wrong frequency. The recorded verdict `unchanged daily frequency` was rewritten to `unchanged weekly frequency` and shown as the recorded verdict. - The write side now refuses such a step. `templatesCollide` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/template.ts`) flags a `unique()` value that equals, is spelled inside, or is the URL-encoded form of another param's value, plain or marked. The step runs and passes as before, writes no entry, and `step.cache.notRecorded` reads `param-collision` (new optional field on `stepCache` in `report-1`, the valid fixture carries it and `schema-fixtures.test.ts` checks the rejected shapes). The next run, with a value of its own, records it. - The verdict summary is no longer templated. It is the model's prose about the recording run, not a replay input or an anchor. `expandTrace` still fills the slot older entries carry in their summary, so the committed web benchmark recording (`apps/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/e5c98b82...`) replays unchanged. The key derivation is untouched. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[step passed, actions recorded] --> B{unique value spelled by another param?} B -- yes --> C[no entry, step.cache.notRecorded = param-collision] B -- no --> D[templateTrace: inputs, descriptors, paths, anchors] D --> E[summary kept as recorded] E --> F[staged for the attempt-end write] ``` ```ts // unique title that reads like the plain choice: runs live, not recorded await agent.act('fill the title {title} and choose frequency {frequency}', { params: { title: unique('Daily'), frequency: 'Daily' }, }); // result.cache.notRecorded === 'param-collision' ``` Not in this change: tracking which action argument came from which param. That is the full fix; this one closes the wrong-value replay by refusing the ambiguous case. ---

title: fix(run): a restored session keeps the secret protection of the setup that saved it
body: - Repro: a setup test resolves a secret from a provider function, fills it with `Secret`, the app stores it, `session.save('acct')`. A consumer test restores `acct`, the app echoes the stored value, an assertion fails. The raw value landed in the failure message, the report, the failure screen, and the log, while the report still marked artifacts `redaction: 'complete'`. The same flow with a static config secret stayed masked. - Cause: the secret ledger and the pixel taint live per session (`packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts`). Static values are re-registered for every new session; a provider value joins only the ledger of the session that resolved it, so the consumer's session never learns it. - Fix: the saved session carries the name and value pairs the saving session learned beyond the static values, inside the encrypted payload beside the state data, plus the taint. On restore the consumer's ledger (and `processSecrets`, so it holds across workers) registers them and the taint is set. Nothing is written unencrypted; the envelope names the secrets and the taint in the clear as authenticated data. - Wire: `session-v1.schema.json` gains an optional `secrecy: { tainted, names }`; both fixtures updated. The ciphertext now holds `{ data, secrets }` instead of bare `data`; a session is only ever read by the run that wrote it, so nothing older can meet the new shape. - Docs: `docs/security.mdx`, Sessions. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[setup: provider secret filled] --> B[session.save] B --> C[envelope: names + taint in AAD, values + state in ciphertext] C --> D[consumer: load] D --> E[adoptSecrecy: ledger.register, taint] E --> F[restoreState] F --> G[app echoes value: redacted, pixels withheld] ``` ```ts // packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts export function carriedSecrecy(secrecy: SessionSecrecy, secrets: ResolvedConfig['secrets']): SavedSecrecy; export function adoptSecrecy(secrecy: SessionSecrecy, saved: SavedSecrecy): void; ``` One behavior change worth a look: a consumer of a session saved after a secret fill is now tainted from the start, so its agent steps get no pixels (`PIXEL_TAINTED`) and its trace is rewritten. Before, that consumer had pixels, static secret or not. Fail closed seemed right, since the restored state can put the value on screen, but it costs vision on every post-login test. Tests: `tests/integration/session-secrets.test.ts` (scripted engine, provider and static, asserts the mask in the failure message, the failure screen file, and the report, and the taint on the consumer) and `tests/unit/session-envelope.test.ts` (round trip with the new field, values absent from the file on disk). ---

title: fix(web): visibility reads the box, the style, and closed details, SVG included
body:
Repro: `toBeHidden()` failed on four elements Playwright's own `toBeHidden` calls hidden, and `isVisible()` said `true` for each. ```html
More
``` - The reader's `hidden` state counted client rects. An SVG skipped computed style altogether, a zero-size box still had one rect, closed `
` content still laid out, and `display: contents` returned visible before looking at anything under it. - `isHidden` now reads what Playwright's `isElementVisible` reads: computed style for any `Element` (SVG included), `visibility` other than `visible` or `display: none` is hidden, content of a closed `details` outside its `summary` is hidden, a box is visible only with width and height both above zero, and a `display: contents` element is visible only when some child element or text node is. `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts` - `styleOf` reads any element now, so the name computation's separate `nameStyleOf` is gone. - The same state feeds `toBeVisible`, the `visible` query filter's final check, and which nodes the agent's screen lists. The `isVisibleEmptyBox` floor (`MIN_BOX_SIDE`) is untouched. - The tree walk prunes on its own test, `hidesSubtree` (aria-hidden, `display: none`, `visibility`, closed details). A box with no size does not clip fixed, absolute, or overflowing descendants, so the walk goes on through it and only leaves that element unlisted. The testbed's `/canvas` page is the case: every control is `position: fixed`, `` lays out to zero height, and pruning there read the page as one node. The document root is listed whatever its own box. - Three role-mapping fixtures were empty zero-height blocks that only the rect-count quirk kept in the tree; they get a 1px box since those tests are about roles. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[aria-hidden=true] -->|yes| H[hidden] A -->|no| C{display: contents?} C -->|yes| K{some child element or text visible?} K -->|yes| V[visible] K -->|no| H C -->|no| S{display none or visibility not visible?} S -->|yes| H S -->|no| D{inside closed details, outside its summary?} D -->|yes| H D -->|no| B{width > 0 and height > 0?} B -->|yes| V B -->|no| H ``` `packages/web/tests/integration/visibility.test.ts` checks each case and its control against Playwright's `isHidden()` on the same element; the runner-level kitchen sink in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` asserts `toBeHidden`/`toBeVisible`/`isVisible()` through the CLI path. The `aria-hidden` ancestor case is #494 and stays as is. ---

title: fix(runner): a download is redaction incomplete unless the runner rewrote it
perf(web): reduce observation metadata transfer overhead
body:
## What and why

- Web observations spent more time transferring semantic metadata through Playwright than walking the document. Send that metadata as one JSON string and parse it in the engine, avoiding Playwright's recursive encoding of every node field.
- Pages with custom JSON serializers keep Playwright's structured transfer. Actions keep the same live element handles. Node references, masking, nested-frame capture, deadlines, and cleanup follow the existing path.
- Measurements on the local Chromium web benchmark, comparing `main` at `166f279b` with this change:

| Scenario | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Control Inventory capture, 52 nodes | 18.84 ms | 11.40 ms | -40% |
| Infinite Scroll capture, 67 nodes | 18.25 ms | 11.18 ms | -39% |
| Virtualized Table capture, 45 nodes | 12.91 ms | 8.59 ms | -33% |
| Iframe Form capture, 15 nodes across two documents | 18.56 ms | 16.07 ms | -13% |
| Control Inventory replay, 6 tests repeated 3 times | 15.76 s | 15.62 s | -0.9% |

- Whole-suite timings include fixture and settling noise. The same runs spent about 3.6% less time in observations.
- Capture means use 80 samples per version after 20 warmups, alternating versions and checking that their complete trees match. Replay means use two runs per version in alternating order, with all 18 tests replayed and no model calls. Settling and gesture delays limit the whole-suite gain.

```sh
node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run \
  --config e2e.agent.config.ts tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts \
  --workers 1 --debug --reporter list --repeat-each 3
```

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

title: perf(agent): skip a second change wait after scrolling to text
body:
## What and why

- Depends on #539 and targets `oskar/mobile-ci-deflake`. That PR repairs the Android permission, location, and long-press failures in the benchmark baseline. Merge #539 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.
- `scroll_to({ text })` already reads a settled screen after each page. On an engine without `scrollIntoView`, its final observation is the destination, but `ActionDispatcher.armAfter` arms another 500 ms change wait against it. The next look waits for a change that already happened, even when no scrolling was needed.
- Skip that extra change wait for this case. The next look still captures twice to check stability. Engines that make a final `scrollIntoView` adjustment keep their change wait.
- The regression fixture runs through the built runner, records the flow, and replays it with no executor call. It covers an already-visible row, two pages before the row, and a delayed final `scrollIntoView` effect.

| Built-runner fixture | #539 baseline | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Replay: row already visible | 696 ms | 156 ms |
| Replay: row appears after two pages | 837 ms | 308 ms |
| Captures in the observation after `scroll_to` | 9 | 2 |

- Timings are the `agent.act` durations from local reports with an in-memory engine. Each benchmark's committed recordings currently contain one `scrollUntil` action; these numbers measure the per-call fix, not a projected suite speedup.

| Native iOS replay, median of three runs | #539 baseline | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Observation after `scroll_to` | 1.255 s | 0.589 s |
| Full test attempt | 37.978 s | 36.320 s |

- Native runs used the existing Infinite Scroll List scenario on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator and one local recording that scrolls to Item 137, then taps it. All six replays passed with two cached actions and zero model calls. The final observation saves 666 ms (53%). Scrolling itself varies by more than two seconds, so the full-test difference is noisy and is not attributable entirely to this change. The measurement recording remains outside the committed cache.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Text found on settled screen] --> B{Final scrollIntoView?}
  B -- No --> C[Next look checks stability]
  B -- Yes --> D[Wait for adjustment, then check stability]
```

title: perf(agent): count capture time toward the action change wait
body:
## What and why

- Count the wait for a visible change from action completion in `packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-feed.ts`. Previously `settleObservation` started the entire window after its first capture, even when that capture or time before the observation had already spent the window.
- Keep the subsequent stability check. A slow capture and a delayed executor each still produce two matching captures before the observation returns. After an action, matching empty navigation captures without permitted screenshot evidence keep polling within the existing stability bound; blank initial screens and lone controls keep their usual behavior.
- Live iPhone 17 Pro measurements below use the benchmark's already-selected Home tab, which leaves the screen unchanged. Each result averages two measurements in alternating baseline/candidate order. These measure observation time after the tap, not the full suite. The delayed case waits 2.1 seconds after the tap before asking for an observation.

| Mobile observation | baseline (`166f279b`) | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Immediately after tap | 2,385 ms, 15 captures | 2,226 ms, 12 captures | -7% |
| After the action's wait has elapsed | 2,407 ms, 15 captures | 281 ms, 2 captures | -88% |

Three cached Infinite Scroll repeats on each revision all passed with zero model calls. Mean step time was 32.50 seconds before and 32.61 seconds after: no measurable whole-test improvement for that flow. The timings above isolate the wait this change removes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Action completes] --> B[Set change deadline]
  B --> C[Capture current screen]
  C --> D{Unchanged and before deadline?}
  D -- yes --> C
  D -- no --> E[Check consecutive captures for stability]
```

title: fix(locator): scrollUntilVisible owns the deadline whichever timer fires first
body: Fixes the flake red on main (spec.yml 36232357341, 36232177584) and on every open PR: `scroll-until-visible.test.ts` > `bounds a locator swipe by the same deadline` failing with `expected TestError: operation timed out: getByRole… to match { code: 'LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND' }`, and its viewport sibling failing with the raw `EngineError: swipe exceeded 250 ms`. - Each swipe of `screen.scrollUntilVisible` runs with the deadline's remainder as its operation budget (`engine.operationWithin(deadline)`). An engine honouring that budget reports `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` from its own `setTimeout`, which wakes up to 1 ms before `Date.now()` reaches `deadline.endsAt` (measured: 3-4 early wakeups per 400 on an idle Mac, more under load). The loop's `deadline.expired()` then read false and the swipe's error escaped instead of the scroll's `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. - Two timers raced for the same event, so the code that surfaced depended on scheduler jitter. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[tryRead] -->|visible| Z[return] A -->|deadline expired| N[LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND] A --> S[swipe with remaining as budget] S -->|ok| P[poll] --> A S -->|deadline expired| N S -->|OPERATION_TIMEOUT and remaining < 100 ms| N S -->|any other failure| E[rethrow as today] ``` - `packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts`: a swipe timeout with less than one poll interval (`MIN_SWIPE_BUDGET_MS = POLL_INTERVAL_MS`) of budget left is the deadline, whichever timer woke first; the raw engine error and the `ACTION_FAILED` the locator engine wraps it in are both recognised. An engine timing out on its own clock with the deadline far away stays `ACTION_FAILED`. - The agent's `scrollUntil` (`action-dispatcher.ts`) does not share this loop; it pages on a screens cap, not a deadline, so nothing changes there. - Tests: the two hanging-fixture tests keep the fixture and now assert the cause chain on both paths; new deterministic cases for the engine-timer-first ordering, for a swipe still dispatched with under a poll interval left, and for a genuine mid-loop engine timeout. 20 runs under 8 CPU hogs: 0 failures. - `docs/reference/screen.mdx` already says `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` "when the deadline expires first, a swipe it cut short included"; unchanged. ---

title: fix(locator): every action rejects an unknown option instead of ignoring it
body: ## What and why - Audit B45. Repro: `check({ trial: true })` on an unchecked box (or `uncheck({ trial: true })` on a checked one) from a JavaScript test, or with a TS cast. The box toggles and `click`, `input`, `change` fire. In Playwright a trial leaves the state alone, so a test ported from it silently commits a state change. - Cause: every timeout-only locator action in `packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts` passed `timeout` through and ignored any other key. Same hole for `doubleTap`, `secondaryTap`, `fill`, `clear`, `press`, `selectOption`, `focus`, `hover`, `setInputFiles`, `dragTo`, `scrollIntoView`, and locator `swipe`. `tap`/`click`/`longPress`/`pressSequentially` already rejected unknown keys. - Fix: those verbs go through one `LocatorImpl.perform` helper that validates the bag with `rejectUnknownOptions` before the step starts, so nothing resolves or dispatches. `fill` and `swipe` (different shape) call the guard directly. Trial support stays out of scope. ```ts private perform(verb: string, action: LocatorAction | ((deadline: Deadline) => Promise), options: ActionOptions | undefined): Promise { rejectUnknownOptions(verb, options, ['timeout']); return this.action(`locator.${verb}`, () => this.context.engine.perform(this.expression, action, options?.timeout)); } check(options?: ActionOptions): Promise { return this.perform('check', { kind: 'check' }, options); } ``` - Tests: `tests/unit/locator-action-options.test.ts` runs every locator action with `{ trial: true }` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, zero lookups, zero engine calls, zero steps) and with `{ timeout }` as the control. Integration on the real web engine (`web-platform.test.ts`): after each refused trial the checked state and the input/change/click count stay put; a normal check and uncheck still toggle and fire 3 events each. Both fail on main. - Docs: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` says an action takes only the options it names; `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` gets a row for `trial`/`force`/`noWaitAfter`. Changeset for `e2e`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: fix(expect): toContainText list matches an ordered subsequence, like Playwright
fix: a URL or text predicate is INVALID_ARGUMENT, not a match-all pattern
body: ## What and why - Audit B38. On `/items`, `expect(web).toHaveURL(url => url.pathname === '/other')` passed, `web.waitForURL(fn)` resolved at once, `web.waitForResponse(fn)` returned an unrelated response, and `web.route(fn, r => r.abort())` aborted every request, the document included. String and RegExp patterns behaved. - Cause: the public types take `string | RegExp` only, but anything that was not a string was read as a regexp. A function's `source` and `flags` are `undefined`, and `new RegExp(undefined, undefined)` is `/(?:)/`, which matches everything. Same hole in `expect(value).toMatch(fn)`; text matchers (`toHaveTitle`, `getByText`) crashed with a raw `TypeError` instead. - Fix: one validator. `toTextPattern` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/text.ts`, exported from `e2e/engine`) throws `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for anything but a string or a `RegExp`, checked with `util.types.isRegExp` so a RegExp from another realm still counts. `urlMatches`, `toMatch`, and web `route`/`unroute`/`waitForResponse` all convert through it. `toRoutePattern` and the web `testPattern` wrapper are gone. ```ts if (!types.isRegExp(match)) { throw new TestError('INVALID_ARGUMENT', `pattern must be a string or RegExp, got ${typeof match}`); } ``` - Tests: `toTextPattern` rejects a function, a `{ source, flags }` look-alike, `undefined`, `null`, and a number, and accepts a vm-realm RegExp; `urlMatches` and `toMatch` reject a predicate. `tests/integration/web-url-patterns.test.ts` runs the real web engine: a predicate is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` at `toHaveURL`, `waitForURL`, `waitForResponse`, `route`, `unroute`, and `toHaveTitle`, with a string/RegExp control both ways. - Docs: `reference/web.mdx`, `reference/expect.mdx`, `reference/engine.mdx` (`toTextPattern`, `urlMatches`), the Playwright migration table, `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. - `toTextPattern` and `urlMatches` are exported from `e2e/engine`, so the changeset bumps `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; title: fix(runner): a trace from a secret-filled attempt drops its screencast frames
fix(expect): toHaveAttribute refuses a secure field instead of reading its withheld value attribute as absent
body:
## What and why

Stacked on #547 (base `oskar/secure-field-value-not-judged-empty`). Merge #547 first, then retarget this to `main`.

- Audit B35. Repro: `<input type="password" value="marker">`. `getAttribute('value')` is `POLICY_DENIED`, but `not.toHaveAttribute('value')` passed and `toHaveAttribute('value')` failed with `observed: attribute "value" absent`. A text input with the same attribute and one without it both read correctly.
- Cause: the web engine drops `value` from a secure node's `attributes` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:946`), and `toHaveAttribute` in `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts` read that gap as absent. Redacted is not absent.
- Fix: `toHaveAttribute` refuses a secure field with the code and message `getAttribute()` already throws, for every attribute name, negated too. The refusal runs right after the sample, before the predicate or the failure message reads the node, so the value never prints.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByLabel('Secret')).not.toHaveAttribute('value');
// POLICY_DENIED: reading values from a secure field is denied: getByLabel("Secret")
```

- Shape: #547's `refuse` hook and `secureRefusal()` become one declarative `readsWithheld` flag on `MatcherSpec`. The value, text, and attribute matchers set it, and `poll()` calls #547's `denySecureRead()` on it. One guard for the getters and the matchers.
- Scope: every attribute is denied, `toHaveAttribute('type', 'password')` included, the same as `getAttribute()`. The engine contract (`SemanticNode.attributes`) does not say which attributes an engine withholds, and hardcoding the web engine's `value` in core would break the rule that core knows nothing of engine internals. Denying only the withheld attributes would need a contract field and changes in all three packages, for the getter and the matcher both.
- Tests: unit on a fake `states.secure` node, positive and negated, with and without a value, plus plain-field and no-attribute controls (`tests/unit/expect-async-attributes.test.ts`); browser-backed `/value-attributes` fixture with password, text, and blank inputs, the report never carries the marker (`tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts`).
- Docs: `docs/reference/expect.mdx`, `screen.mdx`, `errors.mdx`, `docs/security.mdx`, and the skill's `writing-tests.md` and `debugging.md`.

body:
## What and why - Audit D8, D9, D10, D11. The migration page claimed "same" for behaviors that differ from Playwright. title: fix(e2e): --last-failed reruns the scope of a failed suite hook
body:
## What and why

Audit B32.

- Repro: test A's body passes and its `afterAll` throws, B fails. Fix B, run `--last-failed`: A is left out, the rerun exits 0, and the GitHub fold (#537) drops the hook error. If A's hook is the only failure, the rerun is `NO_TESTS`.
- Cause: a suite hook failure is a run error that no result carries, and `lastFailedIds` (`packages/e2e/src/run/last-run.ts`) only read result statuses. The error named a display `scopeId` but not the file or target it ran in.
- Fix: the realm knows its project-relative file, so `beforeAll`/`afterAll` errors now carry a `scope` in the terms results use (`packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts`). `--last-failed` selects every selected test declared inside it:

```ts
function inHookScope(result: ReportResult, error: ReportError): boolean {
  const scope = error.scope;
  if (scope === undefined) return true;
  return (
    result.file === scope.file &&
    result.targetId === scope.targetId &&
    result.titlePath.length > scope.titlePath.length &&
    scope.titlePath.every((title, index) => result.titlePath[index] === title)
  );
}
```

- Title components are compared, not the ` › `-joined `scopeId`, so a describe titled `A › B` is not a child of `A`, and a describe titled `file` is not the file scope.
- Setups: a setup runs only for a consumer, so a setup whose `afterAll` failed while its consumers passed would never run again. `withSetupConsumers` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`) widens `--last-failed` to the tests that consume a named setup's session.
- The selection is read from the previous report only, so once a rerun's hook passes the error disappears and nothing stale is carried. An older report whose hook error has no `scope` selects every test. `packages/github/src/merge.ts` needs no change: the rerun runs the scope again and its own errors decide.
- Wire: `report-1` `error` gains optional `scope: { file, targetId, titlePath }` (relative path, non-empty target, describe titles; `[]` for the file scope). Schema, both fixtures, and producer change together. Additive.
- Out of scope: a filter that keeps the hook's scope out of the rerun (for example `--last-failed --grep B`) still drops the carried hook error in the fold. That is the chained partial rerun case (D6).

title: fix(secrets): redaction catches case-transformed and whitespace-collapsed secrets
body:
## What and why

- Audit B43 and B44. **Repro:** register `Tok-9f3aC0DeB1e7` and `first line 4417\nsecond line Qx`, fill them, and echo them on the page. A failed `toHaveText` on a `text-transform: uppercase` or `lowercase` echo reported `observed: text "TOK-9F3AC0DEB1E7"`, and on a `<pre>` echo reported `"first line 4417 second line Qx"`. That text reached report JSON, Markdown, JUnit, and the list output; the `<pre>` form also reached the model-bound observation. The plain echo was redacted.
- **Cause:** the reader returns text after the transform (`innerText` applies `text-transform`), and `normalizeText` collapses whitespace runs and trims. The redactor matched letters only in their registered case and whitespace only as written.
- **Fix (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts`, `valuePattern`):**
  - Each character matches every case form (default, full `ß` to `SS`, `tr`/`az`/`lt`), each in every existing spelling. The pattern gets the `i` flag, which also covers final sigma, titlecase digraphs, and upper-case hex, so `spellings` now writes hex in lower case only.
  - `character` drops any alternative the `i` flag already matches through another (`distinct`, keyed by ECMA-262 `Canonicalize`). No two alternatives match the same text, so a near miss stays linear. Without this, a 35-letter value one character off took 45 s to reject.
  - A whitespace run between two characters matches 1 to n whitespace characters, each raw `\s` or an encoded space or run character. That covers the run as written, a partial collapse (`\r\n` to `\n`), and the reader's single space. An edge run is optional when the trimmed value is still at least 6 code points.

```ts
function whitespaceRun(run: string): Pattern {
  const spelled = [...new Set([' ', ...run])].flatMap(spellings).filter((spelling) => !/^\s$/.test(spelling));
  const one = alternation([{ source: '\\s', maxLength: 1 }, ...distinct(spelled).map(exact)]);
  const count = [...run].length;
  return { source: `${one.source}{1,${count}}`, maxLength: one.maxLength * count };
}
```

- `packages/e2e/src/run/trace-redaction.ts`: a trace entry used to be redacted line by line, so a value spanning a line break in a resource survived. That already happened for multi-line secrets, and whitespace matching made it more likely. An entry whose every non-blank line is JSON is still redacted record by record, value by value. Any other entry is now redacted whole as text.
- Assertions are unchanged. Text that differs from a secret only in case is now redacted too, which replaces the "a case variant is not the secret" unit test from #460.
- **Tests:** `secret-ledger.test.ts` covers upper, lower, capitalize, `ß`, `ǆ`, Turkish `İ`, final sigma, encoded case variants, collapsed and partly collapsed runs, NBSP, `+`/`%20`, trimmed edges, the short-trim guard, the stream hold, and near-miss timing. `trace-redaction.test.ts` covers a cross-line resource. `transformed-secrets.test.ts` runs the real web engine against the observation, the failure message, the report, and every reporter file, with a passing `toHaveText` on the transformed text as the control.
- **Docs:** `docs/security.mdx` redactor paragraph and "Where redaction stops".

title: fix(web): re-resolve a match replaced mid-read instead of reading it hidden
body:
## What and why

- Audit B40. Repro: a visible input swapped for an identical clone every animation frame. On main, 100 `isHidden()` reads each by test id, label, and display value returned `true` 11, 26, and 17 times, and `toBeHidden()` passed while the field was on screen.
- Cause: `locate` queries the matches, then reads them in a second round trip. A frame in between detaches the queried element; a detached element has no client rects, so the reader reported `hidden: true` for it.
- Fix: the in-page reader reports an element that is no longer connected as `{ detached: true, value }`, and `locate` throws a retryable `NODE_STALE` (after disposing its handles) when a detached read could have been a match. The runner already re-resolves retryable locate errors within the caller's deadline.

```ts
// in-page/read-semantics.ts
return (element.isConnected ? describe(element) : { detached: true, value: describe(element).value }) as SemanticResult<Mode>;

// surface.ts, locate
if (reads.some((read) => 'detached' in read && (displayValue === null || matchesText(read.value ?? '', displayValue)))) {
  releaseHandles();
  throw new EngineError('NODE_STALE', 'a match left the document while it was read', { retryable: true });
}
```

- Which detached reads count: every element a query returns is a match, except a display-value candidate (display value still reads every input), whose held value says whether it was one. Exact label now resolves through the `e2e-label` engine standing alone too, not just in composition, so only controls labelled with the pattern at query time are candidates. A match that left re-resolves the whole set, so a count or a strict single match is never taken from what remains; a non-match that left drops out.
- Tradeoff: unrelated churn costs nothing. A stable field among 400 fields swapped every frame resolves at main speed, and an absent one reads hidden (the first PR head failed both with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`). A locator whose own matches are replaced every frame still retries until a query and read land in one frame, as by test id. A detached input loses its wrapping label, so a label candidate cannot be judged after the fact; that is why the label filter moved into the query.
- Tests: `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-replaced-nodes.test.ts` on a new `/replaced` fixture page. 30 `isHidden()` reads per kind must all be `false` (fails 3/3 on main), `toBeHidden()` must fail by test id, label, and display value, and a stable `City` field beside the churning one must read as shown. `/replaced-crowd` puts `City` among 250 fields swapped every frame: exact label and display value must pass `toBeVisible` and `toHaveCount(1)` five times at 1 s deadlines, and absent ones `toBeHidden` (fails 3/3 on the first PR head). title: fix(expect): Playwright matcher options are honored or refused, never silently ignored
body: ## What and why Audit B36. - Repro: `e2e run` transpiles without type-checking, so Playwright options reach the runtime. On main, `toBeChecked({ checked: false })` passes on a checked box, and the same goes for `toBeVisible({ visible: false })`, `toBeEnabled({ enabled: false })`, and `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`. `not.toContainText('error', { ignoreCase: true })` passes on `Error`. Playwright fails all of these. - Cause: every matcher in `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts` read `options?.timeout` and ignored every other key. The `expect(browser)` matchers in `packages/web/src/browser.ts` did the same. - Fix: the options Playwright documents that map cleanly onto e2e are implemented. The four state flags flip their matcher. `ignoreCase` works on `toHaveText`, `toContainText`, `toHaveAccessibleName`, and `toHaveAttribute(name, value)`: a string compares case-folded, and on a RegExp the option adds or strips `i`. Every other key, and any flag that is not a boolean, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before the first read (existing `rejectUnknownOptions`). The web matchers and `browser.waitForURL` accept `timeout` only. ```ts await expect(checkbox).toBeChecked({ checked: false }); // waits for unchecked await expect(banner).not.toContainText('error', { ignoreCase: true }); // fails on "Error" await expect(checkbox).toBeChecked({ indeterminate: true }); // INVALID_ARGUMENT await expect(browser).toHaveURL('/', { ignoreCase: true }); // INVALID_ARGUMENT ``` - Tests: `tests/unit/expect-async-options.test.ts` covers literal and computed option bags, negated text, RegExp flags, lists, a non-boolean flag, and unknown keys, with a true-condition control for each. `tests/integration/matcher-options.test.ts` runs the same cases through the CLI against a real browser, options built at runtime; on main all 9 of its tests fail. `sdk-types.ts` pins the new option types. - Docs: `reference/expect.mdx` (the interface, the flag semantics, the unknown-option rule), `reference/web.mdx` (`waitForURL` takes `timeout` only), `migrate/playwright.mdx` rows, and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. - `e2e/engine` exports `rejectUnknownOptions`, so the web matchers and `waitForURL` use the runner's check instead of a copy. The peer range stays `>=0.15.0 <1`: no stable 0.15.0 has shipped, and canaries pin the exact runner. - On top of #570 and #571: `ignoreCase` goes through the list matchers' shared `satisfies`, so the `toContainText([...])` subsequence folds case too, and it applies after `toTextPattern` validates the pattern. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web`; the export is additive and mobile does not use it. ---

title: fix(e2e): redaction catches a secret cut short by an observation limit
body: ## What and why - Audit B34 (truncation half). **Repro:** register a 60-char credential, fill it into a plain field, and echo it after filler so the web engine's observation limits (text 512, name 256) keep 59 chars. On main, `cut-secret-...Xn7u` reached the model input, `failure/screen.txt` (labelled `redaction: complete`), and the report. A plain value placed the same way was cut the same way. - **Cause:** the in-page reader cuts `name`/`text`/`value`/`selection` before the runner sees them (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:862`). The runner's redactor only matches whole values, so a value cut partway through no longer matches. - **Fix:** the page never gets the secret list. `SecretLedger.redactCut` finds the longest leading part of any value the text ends with (at least 8 chars, or half of a value under 16) before whole values are rewritten, so a value that starts with another registered value is not half rewritten as the shorter one; an occurrence running into that part joins its marker. `prepareObservation` runs it on every field exactly at its limit before indexing, so the model text, the executor tree, the trace cache anchors, and failure evidence all read the redacted tree. A longer field (a native input value, which no engine cuts) stays on whole-value redaction. ```ts for (const [field, limit] of CUT_FIELDS) { const text = node[field]; if (text?.length !== limit) continue; const redacted = redactCut(text); if (redacted !== text) changed[field] = redacted; } ``` - **Trace:** the Playwright trace keeps the page's raw read result (the evaluate call's `after` event), so after the fix above it still held the 59-char cut prefix. A tainted trace's text now goes through `SecretLedger.redactFragments`: whole values first, then any run of 8+ consecutive chars of a registered value becomes its marker. It builds the set of 8-char windows of every value and grows each match one window at a time, so it is linear in the text with no regex backtracking. Untainted traces are untouched, as before. - **Minimum length:** a 1-char cut prefix was masked, so a plain cut name ending in `o` became `name-c`: mangled text that also told the model the secret starts with `o`. Under 8 chars a prefix says little about a long value. A cut is one position, so for a value under 16 chars the minimum is half its length, which keeps most of a short secret masked without matching plain text by chance. The trace scan checks every position, so it keeps a fixed 8. - The contract JSDoc and `reference/engine.mdx` now tell engines to keep the start and cut the end, since the runner relies on that. - **Tests:** `redactCut` unit cases (59/40/8 kept, 1-7 left, half of a short value, whole values plus a trailing fragment, longest fragment across values, a value prefixed by another, a plain cut value and a mid-text fragment left alone), `redactFragments` unit cases, a trace-redaction case with a cut text and a selection in a read result, and a `prepareObservation` case with a whole-field control. New integration test `truncated-secrets.test.ts` uses the real web engine and checks that an 8-char prefix is absent from the model input, `screen.txt`, the report, and every file under `.e2e`. The shared `contentsUnder` helper now inflates every zip entry, so that scan covers `trace.zip`: before, it grepped the deflated bytes and missed the trace leak. The test also checks that the plain control still ends in its cut 59 chars, in the tainted trace too. It fails on main and on this PR's previous head (`trace.zip!trace.trace`). `trace-secrets.test.ts` uses the same helper. - **Docs:** `docs/security.mdx` redactor paragraph (the 8-char minimum) and trace bullet (fragment scrub), `docs/reference/engine.mdx` limits paragraph. - **Trade-offs:** a complete field of exactly its limit cannot be told from a cut one, so its trailing secret prefix is redacted too (`docs/security.mdx`). A tainted trace also masks plain text that shares 8 chars with a value: a secret holding `0123456789` masks every such run. That costs trace readability, never a leak. A cut prefix under 8 chars of a long value is still shown. - **Not in this PR:** the `selection` half of B34, in #581, stacked on this branch. - **Overlap:** #577 (B43/B44) edits `valuePattern` in the same file. The cut match and the trace fragment scan compare the value as written, so a case-transformed fragment needs a follow-up once #577 lands. The two merge without conflict. #495's branch appends `redactLeaves` to the same file, with no conflict. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: fix(e2e): observation drops the selection of a field holding a secret
body: ## What and why - Audit B34 (selection half). **Repro:** fill a registered 60-char credential into a plain `type="text"` field and select 40 of its chars. On main the observation lists `value="" selection="ecret-Kq7Z...a1eUo"`, so the 40 chars reach the model input, the executor tree, and `failure/screen.txt`. - **Cause:** the redactor matches whole values only. A selection over part of a secret never matches, and only `states.secure` suppressed `selection` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts` `formatNode` / `projectTree`). - **Fix:** `prepareObservation` drops `selection` from any node whose `value` or `text` holds a registered secret (cut-aware, via #580's `redactCut` for a field at its limit), or whose value or text was cut at its limit while the selection lies in neither, since it may come from the unseen rest. It runs in the same pre-index pass as #580's cut redaction (`protectSecrets`), so the model text, executor tree, and failure evidence all read one tree. No secret list reaches the page. ```ts function selectionMayHoldSecret(node: SemanticNode, selection: string, redaction: Redaction): boolean { const fields = [node.value, node.text].filter((text) => text !== undefined); const cut = (text: string): boolean => text.length === OBSERVED_TEXT_LIMIT; if (fields.some((text) => (cut(text) ? redaction.redactCut(text) : redaction.redact(text)) !== text)) return true; return fields.some(cut) && !fields.some((text) => text.includes(selection)); } ``` - **Tests:** `prepareObservation` unit cases (secret in `value` and in `text`; a cut value ending in a secret prefix; a cut value with a selection from the unseen rest; controls that keep their selection). New integration test `selected-secrets.test.ts` runs through the real web engine. It fills a plain value and then the secret into a field that selects chars 5-45, and checks that the plain selection still shows while an 8-char piece of the selected fragment is absent from the model input, `screen.txt`, the report, and every file under `.e2e`, `trace.zip` entries included (the shared helper inflates them since #580). It also checks that the plain selection survives in the tainted trace. The trace half is covered by #580's fragment scrub: the trace keeps the page's raw selection, which only that scrub masks. Both tests fail on main, and the trace check fails without the scrub. - **Docs:** `docs/security.mdx`, `docs/reference/agent.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`. - **Stacked on #580** (truncation half of B34). Merge #580 first; this PR's base then moves to main. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: chore(bench): pnpm bench:ab measures a branch against main
body:
## What and why - Perf PRs here each hand-built their own A/B loop (#562 alternated 80 samples, #563 and #564 took medians of three runs, #565 wrote a throwaway strict executor). `pnpm bench:ab` is that loop, measured the same way every time. - It builds the merge base with `origin/main` in a worktree under the temp directory (once per commit), builds the working tree, and runs one benchmark suite through each build's own CLI in pairs, in a seeded random order, until the suite's time change resolves or the pair budget runs out. Prior art: tachometer's auto-sampling, the TypeScript perf bot's paired comparison, hyperfine's warmups. - Behavior comes first: a test whose status, attempts, or step sequence (kind, api, label, status, error code, cache mode) differs between the builds, or between two runs of one build, is listed and left out of the timing rows. A perf change that changes behavior is not a perf change. - Timings are the median paired log ratio with a seeded bootstrap 95% interval, read against `±threshold` (5%) and an absolute floor (10 ms). Counters that should not move within one build (steps, events by kind, observed nodes and bytes, cache modes, model calls and tokens) are compared exactly. - Runs go with `CI=1` (read-only replay of committed recordings) and without `GITHUB_*`, so a bench run never posts a PR comment. - `scripts/tsconfig.json` makes `pnpm typecheck` cover `scripts/`, and `pnpm test:scripts` (part of `pnpm test`) runs the harness's unit tests under `node --test`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[merge base worktree
install + build once] --> C B[working tree build] --> C C[pair: coin-flip order
base run, head run] --> D{min pairs reached?} D -- no --> C D -- yes --> E{suite CI resolved
vs ±threshold?} E -- no, budget left --> C E -- yes / budget spent --> F[behavior diff
timings with CI
counters] F --> G[summary.md + result.json] ``` ```sh pnpm bench:ab -- tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts --config e2e.agent.config.ts ``` ## Evidence A positive control: #565 replayed from a worktree at `8601ad72` against `8601ad72~1`. The harness finds the rename step without being told where to look. | Metric | base median | head median | change (95% CI) | verdict | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | suite (sum of attempts) | 4.76 s | 2.52 s | -47.0% (-47.3% to -46.4%) | faster | | observe (events) | 3.17 s | 988 ms | -68.8% (-69.1% to -68.7%) | faster | | step agent.act | 4.06 s | 1.85 s | -54.4% (-54.8% to -53.9%) | faster | | rename test | 2.55 s | 346 ms | -86.5% (-86.5% to -86.4%) | faster | Counters: engine events 11 -> 10, observations 17 -> 16. The header says the suite differs between the sides (the recording changed), so each side ran its own. A/A control, this branch against its own merge base, same suite: every test the same steps, every counter equal, suite -0.1% (-2.9% to +3.1%), `same` after 4 pairs. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. Repo tooling only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; no product behavior changes. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: test(web): cross-check the tree against Chrome and Playwright
body:
## What and why - Most recent web engine fixes (#549, #550, #551, #553, #560) began as a hand-written repro showing the tree disagreeing with Playwright or Chrome. This check finds that class without anyone writing the repro: every node of the engine's tree is compared with two oracles on the same live page. - **Chrome**: `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` over CDP. Role, name, checked, disabled, expanded, selected, pressed, heading level, plus interactive nodes Chrome exposes that the tree left out (`missing`) and tree nodes Chrome has no node for (`unknown`). - **Playwright**: `getByRole(role, { name, exact })` must resolve to the same element, the round trip #553 did for 15 hand-picked cases. - Nodes are matched by tagging each element the engine published and resolving Chrome's `backendDOMNodeId`s back to the tag, so shadow roots match too. `packages/web/tests/crosscheck/crosscheck.ts`. - Two corpora: ten fixture pages, one per family of HTML and ARIA semantics (inputs, buttons, checked, disabled, expanded, landmarks, tables, names, hidden, shadow), under `pnpm test`, and every web-benchmark scenario in `benchmark.yml` after the deterministic suite. - Known disagreements are committed in `tests/crosscheck/expected.txt`, one line each with a reason, the way Playwright keeps its BiDi expectations. A new disagreement fails, and so does a listed one that stopped happening. `E2E_CROSSCHECK_UPDATE=1` rewrites the file keeping reasons and marks new lines `TODO`, which fails until someone writes one. - Deliberate vocabulary choices (a `listitem`, `status`, or `alert` named from content, `box`, an editor host as `textbox`, Chrome's `Iframe` and `ColorWell`) are policies at the top of `crosscheck.ts`, each with its reason. Without them the file had 113 lines. Now it has 9. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[captureDocument] --> B[tag each element
data-e2e-crosscheck=id] B --> C[Chrome AX tree
backendDOMNodeId to tag] B --> D[getByRole role, name, exact] C --> E[disagreements] D --> E E --> F{in expected.txt?} F -- new --> G[fail: unexpected] F -- listed, not seen --> H[fail: stale] ``` ## What it found | Page | Disagreement | Read | | --- | --- | --- | | inputs, control-inventory, file-round-trip | `input type=file` reads as `textbox`; Chrome and Playwright read `button "Choose File"` | bug, follow-up | | hidden content | an `inert` button is listed; Chrome drops it (Playwright lists it too) | bug, follow-up: the agent can aim at a control that takes no input | | disabled states | a disabled `fieldset` group is itself `disabled`; both oracles mark only its controls | kept, reason in the file | | disabled states | an option of a disabled `select` is `selected`; Chrome drops it, Playwright agrees with the tree | kept, Chrome quirk | Negative control: dropping `checkbox` from `NAME_FROM_CONTENT_ROLES` (the #553 bug) fails the run with `fixture: checked states | chrome name | checkbox "" | ours | theirs Custom agree`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. Tests and CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. `AGENTS.md`; no product behavior changes. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: feat(cache): --strict-cache fails a recording that no longer replays
body:
## What and why - A committed trace-cache recording that a change breaks is silent today. The replay hands off to the agent, the step passes live, and every CI run pays for model calls until someone notices. #584 was the example: making a file input a `button` broke the Control Inventory upload recording (`missed:target-not-found`), and the only symptom was 2 model calls and 8.8k tokens per run, found by `pnpm bench:ab` (#582). - `--strict-cache` and `cache: { strict: true }` make that a failure. A step whose recording exists but no longer replays fails with `REPLAY_STALE` before any model call. The report keeps `step.cache` with the reason. - Only the reasons that mean the app or the entry changed fail: `invalid-entry`, `wrong-context`, `target-not-found`, `target-ambiguous`, `viewport-changed`, `action-failed`, `action-uncertain`, `end-mismatch`. A step with no recording, a retry, a `gap` (a value read off the screen), and a `truncated` recording still run live (`STALE_REASONS` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`). - `REPLAY_STALE` is `configuration`, exit 2, so retries leave it alone. A retry never replays, so with a `test` code the retry would pass live and the run would read as flaky, not failed (`packages/e2e/src/agent/error.ts`). - The web benchmark's agent job now runs with `--strict-cache`. On `main` the whole agentic suite passes under it: 25 steps replay, and 6 steps run live by design (2 planted-bug acts that are never confirmed, 4 `gap`s). ```mermaid flowchart LR A[entry read] --> B{replays whole?} B -- yes --> C[self-finalized] B -- no --> D{reason} D -- no-entry, retry, gap, truncated --> E[agent runs the step] D -- stale reason --> F{cache.strict} F -- off --> E F -- on --> G[REPLAY_STALE, exit 2
no model call, no retry] ``` ```bash CI=1 npx e2e run --strict-cache ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. `docs/cache.mdx` ("Fail on a stale recording"), `docs/reference/{cli,config,errors}.mdx`, and the skill's `agent`, `running`, and `debugging` topics. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. `AgentErrorCode` gains `REPLAY_STALE` and `CacheConfig` gains `strict`. Both are additive. The report schema carries codes as strings. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: test(mobile): golden trees from real iOS and Android snapshots
body: ## What and why - Every mobile tree bug so far (#427, #491, #511, #534) was found on a device, and each was then pinned by a unit test with a hand-built snapshot. A hand-built snapshot has the shape its author expected, not the shape agent-device actually returns. Maestro's suite has the same gap. - This commits real snapshots: the benchmark's home list and every scenario's first screen, 26 on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) and 24 on a Pixel 7 emulator (API 36, CI parity), each raw agent-device 0.21.15 output. `packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/snapshots/{ios,android}/`, 888 KB. - `tests/unit/captured-snapshots.test.ts` projects each one the way `observe` does (`projectSnapshot`, then `screenRoot`) and compares the result with the committed `.tree.txt`: one node per line with role, name, text, value, states, test id, and attributes, no geometry. A change to `src/nodes.ts` becomes a readable diff of what the model and the locators read, on both platforms, in `pnpm test`. `E2E_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` rewrites the trees. - `apps/mobile-benchmark/tests-capture/snapshots.e2e.ts` (hand-run, `pnpm run capture:snapshots --target `) re-captures after an agent-device bump or an app change. It opens each scenario through the suite's own `openScenario`, waits for two identical snapshots in a row, and reads the session through the agent-device CLI that `@e2edev/mobile` installs, so the daemon version matches. ```text # android/control-inventory.tree.txt (excerpt) screen text "11:26 PM" text="11:26" #com.android.systemui:id/clock image "Wifi signal full." #com.android.systemui:id/wifi_signal group "T-Mobile, signal full." #com.android.systemui:id/mobile_combo ... tablist #section-tabs tab "Fields" [selected] #tab-fields textbox "Name field" text="Ada Lovelace" value="Ada Lovelace" #name-input placeholder="Type your name" ``` ## What the trees show - **Regression, fixed in the PR stacked on this one.** Android's status bar is back in the tree: the clock, the Wi-Fi and signal icons, the battery. #511 took it out, but agent-device 0.21.15 (#534) reports each status icon as its own top-level node rather than one edge-to-edge bar, and `isSystemBar` only recognizes a full-width bar. That is the same drift #511 fixed: an end anchor on "T-Mobile, two bars" hands the replay to the model once the signal changes. - **For later, iOS:** - React Native's section tabs read as `other "Fields" [selected]` where Android reads `tab "Fields"`. - A scroll container is named `Vertical scroll bar, 1 page`. - Static text nests a copy of itself. A negative control, mapping `button` to another role in `roleOf`, fails every scenario on both platforms. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. Tests and fixtures only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. `AGENTS.md`, "Golden device trees". - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: fix(mobile): Android status icons stay out of the tree
body:
Stacked on #587; retarget to `main` once it lands.

## What and why

- The golden device trees (#587) show Android's status bar back in every observation: the clock, the Wi-Fi and signal icons, the battery, and a notification icon. #511 took the bar out because its text follows the device: an end anchor on "T-Mobile, three bars" handed every replay to the model once the emulator read "signal full".
- The cause: agent-device 0.21.15 (#534) reports each status icon as a top-level node of its own, not as a child of one bar spanning the screen. `isSystemBar` only recognized the full-width bar, so every icon passed.
- Now a `com.android.systemui` node that lies wholly inside the top or bottom 8% of the screen and is narrower than half its width counts as the bar too (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`). A wide systemui popup in the same band, like a heads-up notification, stays, as #511's tests require.

```diff
 screen
-  text "11:25 PM" text="11:25" #com.android.systemui:id/clock
-  image "Android System notification: "
-  image "Wifi signal full." #com.android.systemui:id/wifi_signal
-  group "T-Mobile, two bars." #com.android.systemui:id/mobile_combo
-    image #com.android.systemui:id/mobile_signal
-  group "Battery charging, 100 percent." #com.android.systemui:id/battery
-    image
   group
```

The same seven lines leave all 24 Android trees, and no iOS tree changes. The Android smoke and controls suites pass on a Pixel 7 emulator (API 36).

fix(mobile): a worker that replaces a retired one opens the app before its first permission change
body: ## What and why - The scheduler retires a worker after a failing test (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:622`), and the retired worker's `dispose` closes its agent-device session. The next worker on that slot still read the warm-up's `sessionApp` from the environment, so `device.setPermission` skipped its open and sent the permission change on a session bound to no device. - With an iOS simulator and an Android emulator booted on one host, agent-device resolved that unbound request across both platforms and answered `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`. On one host the permission-prompt tests failed after any failing test before them. CI runs one platform per host, so it never showed there. - `init` now keeps the warm-up's app only while `sessions.list` still has the slot's session (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`, `resumedSessionApp`). Otherwise the app is unknown and the first permission change opens it, the path `setPermission` already takes for a session on no app. - The simulator integration suite (`E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_SIMULATOR=1`, not run in CI) drifted when the engine stopped launching the app in `startAttempt`: `beforeAll` now runs `session.restart`, which is what `app.open()` does. It also opened `maps://`, whose first-launch location alert outlives Maps and covers whatever the simulator shows next. It opens `shortcuts://` instead, which shows no prompt. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W1 as worker 1 participant AD as agent-device participant W2 as worker 2 Note over AD: prepare warmed session e2e-ios-0 on the app W1->>AD: test fails, dispose closes e2e-ios-0 W2->>AD: init: sessions.list AD-->>W2: e2e-ios-0 absent, sessionApp unknown W2->>AD: setPermission: open app (with device), then permission ``` Left for their own PRs: iOS 26 labels a pushed screen's navigation bar with its back button's title, so the screen title reads the previous screen (the integration test's General step still fails on that). `simctl pbcopy` writes nothing on Xcode 27, which fails the clipboard test on a Mac on Xcode 27, not in CI. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`. ---

title: feat(integrations): @e2e-dev/integrations/kernel, Kernel browsers for the web engine
body:
## What and why

- New package `@e2e-dev/integrations`, the home for official integrations with hosted services, one subpath each. Only a subpath imports its vendor SDK, and SDKs and engines are optional peers. The first is `@e2e-dev/integrations/kernel`, moved from `@testerarmy/e2e`.
- `@onkernel/sdk` goes from 0.68.0 to 0.113.0 (optional peer, `>=0.113.0 <1`).
- Docs get an Integrations sidebar section: an overview (`docs/integrations/index.mdx`) and the Kernel page (`docs/integrations/kernel.mdx`). The Kernel page answers Kernel's questions: how to fill the VM screen (`viewport: null` plus Kernel's `viewport`), and what each scope does with the browser's default context.
- Video is not in this PR. `--video` on a Kernel target records the web engine's screencast of the page, as for a local browser. A platform-agnostic video API comes separately.

```ts
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { kernel } from '@e2e-dev/integrations/kernel';

web({ url, browser: kernel({ viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 } }), viewport: null });
```

### Web engine fixes Kernel needs

- `scope: 'attempt'` failed at random on Kernel with `cdpEndpoint reused a browser from a previous attempt`. Kernel restores browsers from snapshots: a new session came back with the default context id of one created minutes earlier. A lease is fresh by the provider's contract, so the per-worker context check now applies only to `connect.reconnectEndpoint` (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`, `persistentBinding`).
- A persistent attempt's first page is the browser's own first tab, navigated to `about:blank` so the init scripts run. It used to open a second tab next to it (`packages/web/src/attempt-session.ts`, `nextPage`).

### Release scripts

- A canary snapshot pins the integration's `@e2e-dev/web` peer to an exact version, and `restore-peer-ranges.ts` only widened `e2e` peers. The check and restore scripts now cover every peer on a sibling package.

Measured on a headful Kernel browser with a 1920x1080 screen, and documented on the Kernel page:

| web `viewport` | window | page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ width: 1920, height: 1080 }` | normal, 1905x852 | 1920x1080, overflows the window |
| `null` | maximized 1920x1080 | 1920x993, fills it |

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- The packed tarballs of `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/integrations`, installed with npm into a fresh project. `e2e run --video` against real Kernel browsers, with `kernel()` in worker scope and `kernel({ scope: 'attempt' })`: 6 of 6 passed, including three attempt-scope attempts in a row, and each attempt left its screencast `video.webm`. The Kernel listing afterwards showed no `e2e_*`-tagged browsers.
- Before the fresh-lease fix, the same attempt-scope target failed on Kernel with `cdpEndpoint reused a browser from a previous attempt`.
- Docs rendered with `mint dev`:

| Integrations overview | Kernel page |
| --- | --- |
| ![integrations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6964266-eaa8-4b61-886d-ccb73e363dd9) | ![kernel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/766408e5-f80f-4dd2-ad3d-a7e9fcbc704f) |

Follow-ups, not in this PR: a platform-agnostic video API (Kernel replays can plug into it), switching testerarmy to `@e2e-dev/integrations/kernel` once published, and moving Limrun as `@e2e-dev/integrations/limrun`.
