title: chore(agents): agents verify, self-review, and babysit PRs to Ready for Human Review
body: ## What and why Agents hand over a PR that is already verified, self-reviewed, green, and has every bot thread handled. The human only reviews once the `Ready for Human Review` label is on. Ported from tester-army/app#2504 and adapted to this repo. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[implement] --> B[verify: built CLI on testbed / benchmarks] B --> C[fresh-context review] C --> D[PR with ## Verified] D --> E[babysit: conflicts, threads, CI, comments] E --> F[label: Ready for Human Review] F -- any push --> E ``` - `.claude/skills/verify`: a table mapping each surface (runner, reporters, `@e2edev/web`, agent and trace cache, mobile, `e2e mcp`, `init`, docs, `@e2edev/github`) to the command that proves it, plus how to collect evidence: CLI output, `--video`, and main vs branch for fixes. - `.claude/skills/ship-pr`: `pnpm check`/test, the `AGENTS.md` contract rules lint cannot see (changeset, docs and `skills/e2e`, `sdk-types.ts`, schemas, `filters.yml`), verify, a fresh-context review (`references/review-prompt.md`), open, babysit. - `.claude/skills/babysit`: the loop to the label. `scripts/pr-status.ts` returns one verdict (`READY | WAITING | ACTION | CLOSED`) with blockers. `references/review-triage.md` holds 13 code patterns taken from this repo's recent review threads and names no bot. - `.github/workflows/review-label.yml`: any push drops the label, so it always refers to the current head. It reads the live labels, not the event's snapshot, uses `pull_request_target`, and never checks out PR code. - `writing-pr` and the PR template require `## Verified` with `Ran it locally: yes | no - `. `AGENTS.md` gets a "Definition of done" section. - `.mcp.json` registers `e2e mcp` on the testbed, so `locate` and `screenshot` work in Claude Code. - `spec.yml` typechecks and tests the status script. `pr-status.ts` fixes three bugs in the app's `pr-status.mjs` (worth porting back): - `gh` reports a check that has not started as `startedAt: 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`. One queued iOS job made the push time year 1, and every old comment and review counted as new. - Comments and change requests posted before the latest push dropped out unanswered. Now a comment blocks until it has a 👍, and a change request blocks until that reviewer's latest verdict changes, matching GitHub's review decision. - `reactions?content=+1` decodes `+` as a space and returns every reaction, so any reaction counted as an acknowledgement. The query is now `%2B1`, and the reaction content is checked as well. - Smaller fixes from review: a `STALE` check counts as failing, a draft review with no `submitted_at` no longer crashes the sort, reactions are paginated, a thread keeps its root finding past 100 replies, and a deleted account's comment or review still blocks. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pr-status.ts` against the open PRs #582-#596. On #596, with `ios agentic` queued: ```text {"verdict":"ACTION","blockers":["conflict","threads:19","comments:6"],"headPushedAt":"2026-09-28T14:05:51Z","pending":[],"changesRequested":0} ``` - `.mcp.json` command over stdio from the repo root: `open_session` on the testbed, `screenshot`, `close_session`. Stdout carried only protocol frames. - `e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts --video` on the testbed: 7 passed, and the video landed at the path `verify` documents. - Not run: `review-label.yml`. `pull_request_target` runs from `main`, so it first fires on the first push after merge. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2edev/web`, and `@e2edev/mobile`.

title: fix(e2e): a secret cut short is redacted in any case
body:
## What and why

- Follow-up to #580, noted in its Overlap bullet. **Repro:** an editor under `text-transform: uppercase` echoes a filled 60-char credential after filler, so the text limit (512) keeps 59 of its chars. On main, `CUT-SECRET-KQ7Z...` reached the model input and `failure/screen.txt`.
- **Cause:** #577 made whole-value matching case-insensitive, but #580's `redactCut` (`leadingPartAtEnd`) and `redactFragments` (`fragmentOwners` / `rewriteFragments`) compare the value exactly. A secret that is both cut and case-transformed got past both.
- **Fix:** both now compare through a new `caseKey`: each code point lower-cased from its upper case, with the Turkish lower case used where the default one is longer. So `ſ`, `S`, and `s` agree, and so do `İ` and `i`, as in #577's whole-value forms. It keeps length (a mapping that would change it is skipped), so every index into the key is an index into the original, and the output slices the original. ASCII text takes a plain `toLowerCase()`. No regex, so the fragment scan stays linear.

```ts
const key = caseKey(text);
// ...
const owner = owners.get(key.slice(start, start + FRAGMENT_LENGTH));
```

- Not followed: a case mapping that changes length (`ß` as `SS`) and collapsed whitespace. Whole-value matching still handles both; only the cut and fragment paths skip them.
- The web reader reads an editor's value as rendered (`innerText`), so it comes back transformed. Tree text and names come from text nodes and stay as typed, so the fixture uses an editor.
- **Tests:** `secret-ledger.test.ts` covers an upper- and lower-cased cut part and fragment, a Turkish `İ` and a long `ſ` fragment, a 7-char upper-cased run that is left alone, and a timing case with a 160k-char near miss. `truncated-secrets.test.ts` adds the upper-cased editor echo to `/echo-cut` and checks that `CUT-SECR` is absent from the model input, `screen.txt`, the report, and every file under `.e2e` (trace entries included). It fails on main.
- Docs: `docs/security.mdx` cut paragraph and trace bullet.

## What and why

- Engines and reporter move from the `@e2edev` npm scope to `@e2e-dev`: `@e2e-dev/web`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, `@e2e-dev/github`. Private workspace packages (`testbed`, benchmarks, `docs`) follow.
- Covers package names, imports, `pnpm --filter` targets in scripts and workflows, docs, `skills/e2e/`, pending changesets, `.fallowrc.json`, lockfile.
- `e2e init` installs and imports the new names (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts`). The build keys `sibling-versions.json` by the new names too.
- History stays as it was: past `CHANGELOG.md` entries keep `@e2edev`, only the heading changes so changesets appends under the new name. `skill.test.ts` still guards against the retired `npx @e2edev/e2e`.
- `apps/testbed/scripts/explore-bench.mjs` pointed at the retired `@e2edev/e2e` bin, broken on main too; it now runs the unscoped `e2e`.
- Changeset: minor for `e2e`, `web`, `mobile`, `github`, with the steps to move.

Old -> new for users:

```ts
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';        // was '@e2edev/web'
import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';  // was '@e2edev/mobile'
import { github } from '@e2e-dev/github';  // was '@e2edev/github'
```

## Before merging the version PR

- `NPM_TOKEN` needs read/write on `@e2e-dev`. If it only covers `@e2edev`, `changeset publish` ships `e2e` and then fails on the scoped packages, and `init` would write deps that 404.
- First publish of each `@e2e-dev/*` package also lands on `latest` (npm does that on a first publish, already noted in `AGENTS.md`).

## After the first `@e2e-dev` release

```bash
npm deprecate '@e2edev/web@*' 'moved to @e2e-dev/web'
npm deprecate '@e2edev/mobile@*' 'moved to @e2e-dev/mobile'
npm deprecate '@e2edev/github@*' 'moved to @e2e-dev/github'
```

`AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` already describe `@e2edev` as deprecated, so they are only accurate once this runs.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `init`, packaging: packed `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web`, ran `e2e init --yes app` in `/tmp`, installed the tarballs, ran the scaffolded test against a static page:

```
$ cat package.json | grep e2e-dev
    "@e2e-dev/web": "0.11.0-canary-20260925150007",
$ head -3 e2e.config.ts tests/example.e2e.ts | grep e2e-dev
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
$ APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4391 npx e2e run
 ✓ |web| tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test) 140ms
   ✓ app opens 140ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

- testbed through the renamed workspace: `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test`, 68 passed.
- `git grep -i e2edev` hits only the retirement notes, the new changeset, old `CHANGELOG.md` entries, and the `skill.test.ts` guard.
- Fresh-context review: no code findings. It raised the two npm items above, which are listed as manual steps.

title: feat(run)!: video modes on the config, targets, the CLI, and tests, with provider recordings
body: ## What and why Video had one run-wide switch (`artifacts.kinds: ['video']` or `--video`) and a `retain` flag. This PR makes it a first-class, engine-agnostic option, adds retry-aware modes, and lets hosted services supply the recording. **How other tools do it** (the research that shaped the API) | Tool | Where it is set | Modes | Per-test | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Playwright | config, project, `test.use` per file or describe | `off`, `on`, `retain-on-failure`, `on-first-retry`, plus 3 added in 1.61 | describe only, because the video fixture is worker-scoped | | Cypress | config | on/off, delete in `after:spec` | none | | Detox | config, `--record-videos` | `none`, `failing`, `all` | none | | Maestro, Appium | in-flow start/stop | explicit | yes | | BrowserStack, Sauce, LambdaTest, Browserbase | session capability | on, or `videoUploadOnPass` | per session; a URL after the session ends | | Kernel, Limrun, Anchor | mid-session start/stop API | explicit | per session; bytes or a URL | Other runners bind recording to context or session creation, so a per-test switch would cost them a new worker or session. e2e starts and stops recording per attempt through the engine hooks, so a per-test override costs nothing here. **The API** ```ts export default { video: 'retain-on-failure', // config default targets: [ { name: 'web', engine: web({ url }) }, { name: 'kernel', engine: web({ url, browser: kernel() }), video: 'on-first-retry' }, ], } satisfies E2EConfig; test('checkout', { video: 'on' }, async ({ app, screen }) => { /* ... */ }); // innermost wins ``` - Modes: `off`, `on`, `retain-on-failure`, `on-first-retry`. They are Playwright's first four, and they cover the two patterns every tool converges on: record everything and keep failures, or record only the retry. - Precedence, lowest to highest: the config's `video`, the target's, `--video [mode]`, then a test or describe. Inside a serial group the group decides, as it does for `retries`. - Breaking: `artifacts.kinds: ['video']` and `artifacts.video` are removed, and using them is `INVALID_CONFIG` with the new spelling in the message. - Preflight: `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT` is raised only when a test that runs would actually record on an engine that cannot. - Step captions were prototyped here and taken out to be designed properly in #636 (the prototype is on `oskar/video-captions-prototype`). - Local screencast: `web({ video: { size, quality } })`. **Provider recordings, engine-agnostic** ```mermaid flowchart LR A[attempt starts video] --> B{provider has record?} B -- yes --> C[provider.record lease -> ProviderRecording] B -- no --> D[engine capture: Playwright screencast / agent-device] C --> E[stopProviderRecording: file in video/ or http link] D --> F[VideoSegment files] E --> G[report: path or url] F --> G ``` - `e2e/engine` exports `ProviderRecording`, `ProviderRecordContext`, `isProviderRecording`, and `stopProviderRecording`. `VideoSegment` becomes `VideoFile | VideoLink`. - `BrowserProvider.record` and `DeviceProvider.record` use the same seam. On mobile the worker now learns its lease id, so a provider can recover its lease. - Kernel replays are the first provider that records, saved as `video/replay.mp4`. Headless browsers and `replay: false` fall back to the screencast. - Schema: `report-1` artifacts gain an optional `url` (http(s) only), with both fixtures updated. The run page links a hosted video to its own URL. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `/tmp/video-smoke`, a fresh project using the packed tarballs, a local app, and `retries: 1`. Each target has `places an order` (passes), `fails on purpose` (fails on both attempts), and `keeps quiet` (`video: 'off'`): | Target | passes | fails (2 attempts) | `video: 'off'` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `video: 'on'` | kept | both kept | nothing | | `web({ video: { size: 640x360 } })` | kept, 640x360 | both kept | nothing | | `retain-on-failure` | dropped | both kept | nothing | | `on-first-retry` | nothing | attempt 1 only | nothing | - Real Kernel: an agent test with `video: 'on'` produced `video/replay.mp4`, the Kernel replay of the whole browser window. - `e2e mcp` on Kernel: `start_recording` / `stop_recording` saved a 1920x1080 Kernel replay to `.e2e/videos//1-todo-demo.mp4`. On a local browser the same tools saved the page screencast as `.webm`. - After taking captions out, the `/tmp/video-smoke` run again kept every video under `on` and only the failed ones under `retain-on-failure`, with no `.vtt` written and no `captions` field. - A fresh-context review found 8 issues and all are fixed (the eighth was about captions, which are now out): - Provider URLs and timestamps normalized to the schema's shapes. - `--video` no longer hides an invalid target mode. - `video` rejected on a describe nested in a serial group. - One list of modes. - One shared recording check for web and mobile. - A mobile lease's own `leaseId`. - The changeset note for stores. - Follow-ups, not in this PR: - `expiresAt` on links, because signed URLs expire. - Handing the attempt's verdict to a provider's stop, so `retain-on-failure` can delete the remote recording. - More Playwright modes if someone asks for them. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Removed without a deprecation window, by decision. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/819fe714-79ad-4d17-b9ac-a8a0061e79d2 ---

title: fix(web): a video started mid-trace fills the viewport
body: A video started while a trace is already running came out at the trace's screencast size, padded with grey. Playwright shares one screencast per page between tracing and `page.screencast`, and the first client sizes it. `e2e run` never hit this because it starts video before trace (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:581`). A host that starts video mid-attempt does: `e2e mcp` recording (next PR in the stack) starts it after the session's trace. - `AttemptSession.startVideo` splits a running trace around the start, the same split `restart` and `replace` already do: the segment so far is saved as `trace-partN.zip`, the video starts at full size, and the trace resumes on the video's screencast. The resume sits in a `finally`, so a video that fails to start does not leave the rest of the attempt untraced. - `VideoRecorder.stop` keeps handing finalized segments to the next stop after one that reported a lost segment; a new unit test pins that, since a host retrying the stop (the MCP recorder) relies on it. - No change for `e2e run`: video starts before the trace there, so there is no trace to split. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web engine, `vitest run tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts`: the new test (trace first, video started twice mid-attempt) fails on main with `video/video.webm padded: expected 0.6094552951388889 to be less than 0.01`, and passes here. The resume test fails without the `finally` (`expected [ 'trace/trace-part1.zip' ]`). - testbed through `e2e mcp` with the recording tools from the next PR, frame from the saved `.webm`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | ![main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9609b2a9-2056-4216-9398-e00b9be1c266) | ![branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ed3ca8e-9f1e-4e74-b2a3-9169a27f81f9) | - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web test` 386 passed, testbed suite 68 passed, web-benchmark 90 passed.

title: feat(mcp): record video of a live session on demand
body:
Stacked on #611.

A coding agent driving the app over `e2e mcp` had no way to record what it did. Evidence for a PR meant writing a test and running `e2e run --video`, or reaching for an outside screen recorder. The engines already record (`startVideo` / `stopVideo` on `SessionArtifacts`); the session just never called them.

- Two catalog tools, listed only when the engine records video:

  ```text
  - start_recording {name?}: Start recording a video of the app, for a person to watch: a demo for a pull request, or evidence of a bug.
  - stop_recording: Stop the running recording and save it: returns the absolute path of each video file, ready to attach to a pull request.
  ```

- On stop the files move out of the attempt dir to `.e2e/videos/<session>/<n>[-<name>].webm` (`.mp4` on mobile). Mobile writes `video/video.mp4` on every start, so moving is what keeps recording 1 when recording 2 starts. A web recording across a page restart returns `-part2`, `-part3` in play order.
- `close_session`, the idle timeout, and the TTL save a recording still running. It is saved after `step.done`, so a `start_recording` in flight at close settles first.
- A session no longer records from launch when the config asks for the `video` kind; that kind is for runs (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts`).
- Videos are not masked, as with `run --video`. A recording stopped after a secret was filled adds a line saying so. `docs/security.mdx` gets a `videos/` row.
- Recorder calls run one at a time, so the save at close waits for a start or stop still in flight. A failed start stops the engine best-effort so the next start is not stuck on mobile's "already recording"; a failed stop or file move keeps the recording so a retry or `close_session` saves it, without stopping the engine twice.
- `e2e init` adds `.e2e/videos/` to `.gitignore`. The folder is `videos`, not `recordings`, because "recordings" already means the committed step cache here.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as coding agent
  participant S as SessionHost
  participant R as SessionRecorder
  participant E as engine
  A->>S: call start_recording {name}
  S->>R: start
  R->>E: startVideo
  A->>S: call tap / type / navigate ...
  A->>S: call stop_recording
  S->>R: stop
  R->>E: stopVideo
  E-->>R: segments in attempt dir
  R-->>A: paths under .e2e/videos/<session>/
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, the built `e2e mcp` driven by an MCP client: `open_session`, `start_recording {name: "testbed-demo"}`, taps Home, Todos, Forms, `stop_recording`, `close_session`:

  ```text
  Recording 1 "testbed-demo" started. Act as usual; stop_recording saves the video, and close_session saves one still running.
  Recording 1 "testbed-demo" stopped after 4.6 s.
  - .../apps/testbed/.e2e/videos/01a0e9d0-.../1-testbed-demo.webm
  Session 01a0e9d0-... closed (closed by the agent); 6 tool calls ran.
  ```

  The attached video is that file: 1280x720 VP8, the three pages in order.
- mobile-benchmark on the iOS 26.5 simulator, same flow on `ios-simulator`: a 15 s 1206x2622 h264 `.mp4` showing the login form and keyboard. Android emulator not run.
- New tests: recorder unit tests (naming, move, parts, failed start and stop, taint line), session host on the fake engine (no recording from launch, save at close, bad name refused, no tools without video), and a real `.webm` from the web engine in `mcp-server.test.ts`.

title: feat(web): userAgent option sets the agent string every attempt sends
body: Actual Budget's app enters test mode (no auto tour, no news fetch, a direct worker instead of a SharedWorker) only when `navigator.userAgent` contains `playwright`; its `playwright.config` sets `use.userAgent`. `web()` had no equivalent, so that suite could not be ported. With this option, all 141 ported Actual tests pass. - `web({ userAgent })` passes Playwright's `userAgent` context option on every context the surface creates: attempt start, `session.reset`, session restore (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`). - Validated at config load: non-empty string, no control characters (`packages/web/src/engine.ts`). - A persistent context (`connect.reconnectEndpoint`, or a provider with `scope: 'attempt'`) can't take it, so it's `INVALID_CONFIG` there, same as `headers` and `basicAuth`. - Setting a `user-agent` entry in `headers` as well is `INVALID_CONFIG`. Site headers would override it only on requests to the app's site while `navigator.userAgent` reported the other value. - Docs: `reference/web.mdx`, `browser.mdx`, `migrate/playwright.mdx` (`use.userAgent` now maps to `web({ userAgent })`), the package README, `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. Changeset: `@e2e-dev/web` minor. ```ts engine: web({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:3001', userAgent: 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) playwright' }), ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project under `/tmp` on the packed `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` tarballs. The config sets `userAgent: 'Mozilla/5.0 e2e-probe playwright'`. A node server echoes the request `User-Agent` into the page, and an inline script switches to "test mode" when `navigator.userAgent` contains `playwright`, the same check Actual uses. The test asserts `web.evaluate(() => navigator.userAgent)`, the echoed header, and the mode text. ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 125ms ✓ |web| tests/ua.e2e.ts (1 test) 662ms ✓ the app sees the configured user agent 662ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) ``` - Failure paths, same project, exit 2 before any browser launches: ```text ERROR configuration error CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED (config) failed to load config e2e.bad.config.ts: web({ userAgent }) must not contain a control character ERROR configuration error CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED (config) failed to load config e2e.conflict.config.ts: web({ userAgent }) and a user-agent header in web({ headers }) conflict; set userAgent only ``` - `tests/integration/protected-app.test.ts` has a new case: the page reads the configured agent, and still reads it after `session.reset`. ---

title: fix(web): a descendant's title names a control only where getByRole reads it
body: Found while migrating Actual Budget's Playwright suite. Its month picker has: ```html ``` The tree named it button "Next month", but `getByRole('button', { name: 'Next month' })` matched nothing. So the test failed with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, and the "on screen" hint listed the exact node it had asked for. - Playwright's accname keeps a descendant's content untrimmed. The flex container blockifies the svg, the svg adds a space on each side, and the content is not empty, so the `title` step (2I) never runs. Chrome's AX tree names it "" as well. - `contentNameOf` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`) fell back to the title whenever the content *trimmed* to empty. It now does so only when the content is empty. - `referencedNamesOf` gets the same rule for `aria-labelledby` (2B). A non-empty untrimmed join of the targets ends the computation. Without this, a reference to a whitespace-only titled span would have fallen through to the button's own text, a name neither oracle gives. - New crosscheck fixture lines: `` and the whitespace `aria-labelledby` target. Two Chrome-only name disagreements are recorded in `expected.txt` with reasons (the tree follows `getByRole`). The axe conformance suite still passes. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/integration/crosscheck.test.ts tests/integration/conformance.test.ts`, with this branch's `fixtures.ts` and `expected.txt` copied onto an `origin/main` worktree: ```text main: + "unexpected": [ + "fixture: names | chrome name | button \"Blockified tooltip\" | ours Blockified tooltip | theirs ", + "fixture: names | playwright getByRole | button \"Blockified tooltip\" | ours match | theirs no match", + ], Tests 1 failed | 13 passed | 1 skipped (15) this branch: Tests 14 passed | 1 skipped (15) ``` - Built CLI in a scratch project (`web({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0' })`, page served with `web.route('**/*', r => r.fulfill(...))`). The Actual markup, then `screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next month' }).tap()`. It fails on both builds, since Playwright does not match that name. What changes is what the failure tells you: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `on screen #n3 button "Next month"` | no false "on screen" hint | | `failure/screen.txt`: `#n3 button "Next month"` | `failure/screen.txt`: `#n3 button` | - Not run locally: the web-benchmark `CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL` pass. Its fixed port collides with parallel work on this machine, so `benchmark.yml` covers it. - `pnpm check` fails only on `check:peer-ranges`, the canary pin `640a73ef` left on main. `spec` is red on main for the same reason. ---

title: fix(collect): a narrowed run skips an unselected file that fails to import
body: Porting Actual Budget's Playwright suite with several agents in parallel, `e2e run tests/transactions.e2e.ts` kept failing with `COLLECTION_ERROR failed to collect tests/mobile/settings.e2e.ts: Cannot find module ...` because another agent's file was half-written. The runner imports every discovered file on purpose (a selected test's session setup may live elsewhere), so any broken file blocked every run. Playwright only loads the selected files. - A run narrowed by positionals skips an unselected file that fails to import or register, with a `notice` (target `collect`): `packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`. - A selected file's failure, or any failure in a run with no positionals, still fails the run with `COLLECTION_ERROR`, exit 2. - A selected test whose session has no producer names the skipped files and why, since the setup may be in one: `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`. - The skip shows as a notice only; `report.json` does not record it. Unnarrowed CI runs still fail on a broken file. - Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` (positionals), `reference/errors.mdx` (`COLLECTION_ERROR`). Changeset: `e2e` patch. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[import file] -->|ok| B[collect] A -->|fails| C{positionals and file unselected?} C -- no --> D[COLLECTION_ERROR, exit 2] C -- yes --> E[notice, skip] E --> F{selected test's session has no producer?} F -- yes --> G[COLLECTION_ERROR naming skipped files] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project (`@e2e-dev/web`, page served by `web.route(...).fulfill`) with `tests/good.e2e.ts` and `tests/broken.e2e.ts` importing a missing module. Ran `e2e run tests/good.e2e.ts` on a main build and on this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | exit 2, `COLLECTION_ERROR` | exit 0, notice, test passes | main: ```text ERROR configuration error COLLECTION_ERROR (collection) failed to collect tests/broken.e2e.ts: Cannot find module '/tests/not-written-yet.ts' imported from /tests/broken.e2e.ts Test Files no test files exit 2 ``` this branch: ```text ℹ skipped tests/broken.e2e.ts, which no positional selected and which failed to collect: Cannot find module '/tests/not-written-yet.ts' imported from /tests/broken.e2e.ts ✓ |web| tests/good.e2e.ts (1 test) 188ms ✓ greets 188ms Test Files 1 passed (1) exit 0 ``` On this branch, `e2e run` with no positionals and `e2e run tests/broken.e2e.ts` both still exit 2 with the same `COLLECTION_ERROR`. A selected test whose setup file is broken: ```text ERROR configuration error COLLECTION_ERROR (collection) test tests/member.e2e.ts::member%20page consumes session "member" but no setup test produces it; it may be declared in a file that failed to collect: tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (Cannot find module '/tests/helpers/not-written-yet.ts' imported from /tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts), tests/broken.e2e.ts (...) ``` `tests/integration/runner-lifecycle.test.ts` covers all three runs (narrowed past an import error and a registration error, narrowed to the broken file, unnarrowed). `pnpm check` fails only on `check:peer-ranges`, the same failure `origin/main` has since the `chore: release` canary pins. ---

title: fix(config): workspace packages exporting TypeScript source load as ESM
body:
Migrating Actual Budget turned this up. A test importing `@actual-app/core/shared/months` (a yarn workspace package with no `"type"`, `exports` mapping to `./src/*.ts`, `#shared/*` subpath imports) failed at collection with `Cannot find module '.../loot-core/src/shared/months.ts?namespace=e2e'`, although the file exists.

- tsx's namespaced loader hands CommonJS-scoped `.ts` to `require`, which it does not hook. `esm-hooks.ts` forced `format: 'module'` only for path specifiers (#250), so a bare or `#` specifier into a typeless workspace package hit the same dead end.
- Now TypeScript a bare or `#` specifier resolves to outside `node_modules` is forced to ESM too, but only when the importing module carries e2e's tsx namespace (`packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`). A module Node loads itself, such as one a `.cjs` helper requires, keeps its format so Node's own type stripping still applies. Forcing it there broke `require` of a workspace package that works on main; the fresh-context review caught that.
- Installed packages under `node_modules` keep their declared format. For those, `diagnose.ts` now explains the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`: the file exists, its `package.json` declares no `"type": "module"`, and what to do about it.
- Plain `node --import tsx` loads the package fine. Only the namespaced loader has this problem.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[resolve .ts outside node_modules] --> B{path specifier?}
  B -- yes --> M[format: module]
  B -- no --> C{parent in tsx-namespace=e2e?}
  C -- yes --> M
  C -- no --> K[keep format, Node strips types]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Scratch pnpm workspace under /tmp: `packages/core` (no `"type"`, `exports: {"./shared/*": "./src/shared/*.ts"}`, `#shared/*` imports), an app with e2e tests importing it by name, a `.cjs` helper that `require`s it, and a typeless package copied into `node_modules`. Built CLI from main and from this branch, `e2e run --config <config>`.

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| test imports `@scratch/core/shared/months` | `COLLECTION_ERROR`: `Cannot find module '.../packages/core/src/shared/months.ts?namespace=e2e'` | `month: 2026-09`, 1 passed |
| `.cjs` helper `require`s the same package | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| installed typeless package exporting `.ts` | `Cannot find module '.../answer.ts?namespace=e2e'` | same, plus `.../answer.ts exists: .../package.json declares no "type": "module", so the file loads as CommonJS, which e2e's TypeScript loader does not transform; import the package's compiled JavaScript, or have the package declare "type": "module"` |

```text
# this branch, test importing the workspace package
stdout | |web| tests/months.e2e.ts > workspace package month
month: 2026-09
 ✓ |web| tests/months.e2e.ts (1 test) 112ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

- Same two workspace cases pass with `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ./noop.ts"`, which moves tsx and this hook onto the async `module.register` path.
- Adding `"type": "module"` to the installed package, as the hint says, makes that test pass.
- The new `cli-init.test.ts` case (a workspace import plus a `.cjs` require) fails with main's `esm-hooks.js` swapped into `dist`.
- The installed-package failure depends on the Node version: 24.19 and 26 hit it, while CI's 22.22 and 24.13 load that package fine. So the hint is covered by a unit test only.
- `pnpm check`: `check:peer-ranges` fails on the `0.15.0-canary-...` pins `chore: release` left on main, not touched here. Every other step passes.

title: fix(cli): init keeps an existing package.json in its own order
body: - `readPackage` parses with zod `looseObject`, which emits the schema's keys first. `serializePackage` wrote that order back, so `e2e init` moved `devDependencies` and `scripts` to the top of an existing `package.json`. On Actual Budget's `packages/desktop-client` that was a 200-line diff. - `serializePackage` now writes top-level keys in the original's order, new keys last (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/package.ts`). - `devDependencies` and `scripts` keep their own order and new entries go at the end. One exception: if `devDependencies` was sorted (the way package managers write it), it stays sorted, so `ai` no longer lands after `vite`. `scripts` never gets sorted. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project under `/tmp` whose `package.json` has `scripts` and `devDependencies` last. Installed the packed `e2e` tarball with `npm install --no-save`, ran `npx e2e init --yes`, then `git diff package.json`. Built main and this branch the same way. - Running init a second time on the branch leaves `package.json` unchanged. - Unit tests in `tests/unit/cli-init.test.ts` check key order for a sorted block, a hand-ordered block, and a sorted `scripts` block. They fail on main. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `package.json \| 25 +++++++++++++++----------` | `package.json \| 7 ++++++-` | main: ```diff { + "devDependencies": { + "@types/react": "^19.0.0", + "typescript": "^5.9.0", + "vite": "^7.0.0", + "e2e": "0.15.0-canary-20260928184528", + "@e2e-dev/web": "0.11.0-canary-20260928184528", + "playwright": "^1.63.0", + "ai": "^7.0.0" + }, + "scripts": { + "build": "vite build", + "start": "vite", + "test:e2e": "e2e run" + }, "name": "desktop-client", "version": "1.0.0", "private": true, "type": "module", - "exports": "./src/index.ts", - "scripts": { - "build": "vite build", - "start": "vite" - }, - "devDependencies": { - "@types/react": "^19.0.0", - "typescript": "^5.9.0", - "vite": "^7.0.0" - } + "exports": "./src/index.ts" } ``` this branch: ```diff "exports": "./src/index.ts", "scripts": { "build": "vite build", - "start": "vite" + "start": "vite", + "test:e2e": "e2e run" }, "devDependencies": { + "@e2e-dev/web": "0.11.0-canary-20260928184528", "@types/react": "^19.0.0", + "ai": "^7.0.0", + "e2e": "0.15.0-canary-20260928184528", + "playwright": "^1.63.0", "typescript": "^5.9.0", "vite": "^7.0.0" } ``` ---

body: - `640a73ef chore: release` left `@e2e-dev/web`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, and `@e2e-dev/github` peering on `e2e` at the exact canary `0.15.0-canary-20260928184528`. `version-packages` runs `scripts/restore-peer-ranges.ts` after `changeset version`; this release skipped it. - `check:peer-ranges` fails on main and on every open PR (`check` job), and `spec` is red for the same reason. - This is the script's own output, nothing hand-edited. title: feat(e2e): getByTestId takes a RegExp
body: - `screen.getByTestId` and `locator.getByTestId` take a `TextMatch`, as Playwright's `getByTestId` does. A string still matches the whole id, case-sensitive; a RegExp tests it. - Both engines already matched a regexp test id (`packages/web/src/locators.ts` `testIdSelector`, mobile `matchesText`). Only the SDK signature (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts`) and `testIdQuery` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/expression.ts`) forced a string. - A regexp test id adds no `testId` failure hint. Its source is not an id, so failure evidence would have matched candidate nodes against `^row-\d+$` as a substring. The locator label still shows the pattern. - Found porting Actual Budget's Playwright suite: its page models call `getByTestId(/total-budgeted$/)` and `getByTestId(/^budget/)`. ```ts await expect(screen.getByTestId(/^budget-row-/)).toHaveCount(2); await expect(screen.getByTestId(/total-budgeted$/)).toHaveCount(3); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project linked to this branch's built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web`, on a served page with Actual-style ids (`budget-row-food`, `food-total-budgeted`, `total-budgeted`, `total-budgeted-note`). `tsc` on the test file passes against the emitted `dist/types.d.ts` (`getByTestId(id: TextMatch, ...)`). - `e2e run --reporter list,markdown`: prefix, suffix, anchored, `i` flag, chained under a `filter`, and string still exact (`'budget-row'` counts 0). The second test fails on purpose to show what a user reads: ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 92ms ❯ |web| tests/testid.e2e.ts (2 tests | 1 failed) 1.51s ✓ getByTestId takes a RegExp 284ms × a regexp that matches nothing names it in the failure 1.23s → locator matched no nodes within getByTestId(/^missing-/) ``` - Mobile not run on a device; its `testId` query goes through the same `matchesText` it already used for regexp text queries. ---

title: docs(migrate): page objects, eager fixtures, and missing Playwright mappings
body: Gaps found porting Actual Budget's 145-test Playwright suite (page objects everywhere) to e2e. - `reference/test.mdx` said "Fixtures are lazy" and the migration table said `test.extend` is "same". Only built-in and engine fixtures are lazy (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`, `contributedFixtures`). Every `test.extend` definition in the chain sets up for every test of that `test`, named or not (`packages/e2e/src/run/extended-fixtures.ts`, `setUp`). Playwright sets up only what a test names. One migration agent lost 9 tests to this. Now scoped, and the row is marked `missing` - New "Page objects" section: take `screen` and `web`, typed with `Screen`/`Locator` from `e2e` and `Web` from `@e2e-dev/web`, handed out through `test.extend`. title: fix(web): waitForDownload says no download started instead of a bare timeout
body: - A `web.waitForDownload` whose trigger resolved but never started a download failed with `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out in web.waitForDownload`: `translateEngineError` drops the engine's `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` message. Hit while porting Actual Budget's settings export test. - Now it says `no download started within ms; the trigger resolved after ms`. The waiter's clock starts before the trigger runs, so the message names both numbers. - Only a timeout between the trigger resolving and the download event is rewritten (`packages/web/src/web.ts`). A trigger that throws keeps its own error; a timeout during the trigger or during `saveAs` keeps its old message. - New `web-platform` integration test; it fails on main with `"message": "operation timed out in web.waitForDownload"`. - `docs/reference/web.mdx` and a `@e2e-dev/web` patch changeset. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project (a node server on `http://127.0.0.1:0` with an export link and a button that does nothing), built CLI from main and from this branch: `e2e run tests/download.e2e.ts --retries 0`. ```ts test('a trigger that starts no download', async ({ app, screen, web }) => { await app.open(); await web.waitForDownload(() => screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Do nothing' }).tap(), { timeout: 1000 }); }); ``` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out in web.waitForDownload` | `ACTION_FAILED: no download started within 1000ms; the trigger resolved after 50ms` | Branch output, full file: ```text ❯ |web| tests/download.e2e.ts (4 tests | 3 failed) 2.46s ✓ export downloads a file 190ms × a trigger that starts no download 1.07s → no download started within 1000ms; the trigger resolved after 50ms × a trigger that throws 102ms → trigger broke × a slow trigger that starts no download 1.10s → web.waitForDownload exceeded its timeout of 1000ms ``` The other three tests print the same thing on main: the real download passes, a throwing trigger keeps `trigger broke`, and a trigger slower than the timeout keeps the harness's step timeout. `pnpm check` fails on `check:peer-ranges` here, same as on main (canary peers left by the release); #619 fixes that. Every other stage passes. ---

title: feat(artifacts): trace.record 'retries' records a trace on retries only
body: Adds `artifacts.trace.record`: `'all'` (default, unchanged) or `'retries'`, which skips the trace on attempt 0, like Playwright's `on-all-retries`. ```ts artifacts: { trace: { record: 'retries' } }, ``` - Found porting Actual Budget's Playwright suite (141 tests). The always-on trace was nearly all of the gap to Playwright, and there was nothing between "every attempt" and "never". - `launchSession` takes the attempt index (`execute.ts`, `serial.ts`, `standalone.ts` passes 0) and starts the trace only when `record` is `'all'` or the index is above 0. A serial group's shared trace follows the group's attempts. - Only a retry is traced: under `'retries'` a failure the runner does not retry (infrastructure, e.g. `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`) and an `e2e mcp` session (one attempt, index 0) record no trace. Documented in `config.mdx` and the JSDoc. - `closeSession` stops a trace only for a session that started one. Without that, a named (required) `trace` kind made every untraced attempt 0 a cleanup failure (`tracing.stop: Must start tracing before stopping`). - Public API: `TraceArtifactConfig` and `ArtifactsConfig.trace` in `dist/types.d.ts`, with `sdk-types.ts` assertions (closed union). Docs: `reference/config.mdx` (new `trace` section), `migrate/playwright.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. Changeset: `e2e` minor. ## Perf Actual Budget, full ported suite, 141 tests, 3 workers, `--retries 0`, same machine, interleaved runs: | config | run 1 | run 2 | load (1m) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default (trace every attempt) | 312s | 309s | 45.3 / 10.0 | | `artifacts.trace.record: 'retries'` | 274s | 263s | 11.2 / 12.8 | Run 2 ran at similar load: 309s to 263s, about -15%. Playwright's own suite on the same app: 246s. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `tests/integration/trace-record.test.ts` on the real web engine: with `retries: 1` and `record: 'retries'`, traces per attempt are `[0]` for a passing test, `[0, 1]` for a failing one and for a serial group, every attempt `cleanup: complete` with no secondary errors; the default stays `[1]` and `[1, 1]`. It fails with the gate removed, and failed on the cleanup assertion before the `closeSession` fix. - Scratch project (`web({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command })`, one passing and one failing test, `retries: 1`), built CLI, trace artifacts per attempt from `.e2e/report.json`: | config | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | default | passes `[1]`, fails `[1, 1]` | passes `[1]`, fails `[1, 1]` | | `trace: { record: 'retries' }` | `INVALID_CONFIG unknown artifacts config key "trace"` | passes `[0]`, fails `[0, 1]` | | `kinds: ['screenshot', 'trace']` + `record: 'retries'` | `INVALID_CONFIG` | passes `[0]`, fails `[0, 1]`, all `cleanup: complete` | ```text $ find .e2e/artifacts -name '*.zip' # record: 'retries' web/tests_suite.e2e.ts__fails-76bf31cc/default/attempt-1/trace/trace.zip ``` `pnpm check` fails only at `check:peer-ranges`, the canary peers the release left on main; #619 fixes that. ---

title: fix(web): setViewport works before the first navigation
body:
- `web.setViewport` before the first navigation failed with `APP_NOT_OPEN`. Playwright specs often call `page.setViewportSize` before `goto`, and I hit it porting Actual Budget's mobile specs: the port had to open at desktop size, then shrink. - The attempt session now keeps the requested size and applies it to every page it creates (`packages/web/src/attempt-session.ts`, `ensurePage`). An open page resizes at once, as before. No page is created early, so acting before `app.open` is still `APP_NOT_OPEN`. - Because every new page gets the size, it now survives `app.restart()` and `app.clearState()` too. Those used to drop back to the config size, though the docs already said the size lasts "for the rest of the attempt". - A size that is not whole, non-negative pixels now fails on the `web.setViewport` step itself, even with no page open to hand it to Playwright. The session stores a copy, so mutating the object afterwards changes nothing. - Video segments now take their size from their own page, not the config (`packages/web/src/video.ts`). A segment recorded after a resize and restart matches the page: `--video` gives `video-part2.webm` at 1280x720 on main and 390x600 here. - Docs: `viewports.mdx` (the agent example now resizes before `app.open`), `reference/web.mdx`, and the Playwright migration table. ```ts test('phone layout', async ({ app, screen, web }) => { await web.setViewport({ width: 390, height: 600 }); await app.open(); await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Mobile layout' })).toBeVisible(); }); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project on the built CLI of main and of this branch (`url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0'`). The app is a small node server whose script writes `first render width ` and picks its layout by width. Command: `e2e run tests/viewport.e2e.ts --reporter list`. - The three tests: resize then `app.open` (first render at 390, mobile heading, `innerWidth` 390); resize, then `app.restart()` and `app.clearState()` + `app.open()` (first render still 390); resize, then tap without `app.open`, which should still fail with `APP_NOT_OPEN`, now from the tap and not from `setViewport`. - The branch report records `"viewport":{"width":390,"height":600,"scale":1}` on the step. - On main, the new `web-platform` integration test fails with `expected 'failed' to be 'passed'`. It passes here. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | 
× phone viewport before app.open 137ms
  → no app page is open; call app.open() or web.goto() first
× phone viewport survives restart and clearState 5.32s
  → expect.toBeVisible failed
× setViewport without app.open is still APP_NOT_OPEN 12ms
  → no app page is open; call app.open() or web.goto() first
Tests  3 failed \| 0 passed (3)
| 
✓ phone viewport before app.open 156ms
✓ phone viewport survives restart and clearState 171ms
× setViewport without app.open is still APP_NOT_OPEN 8ms
  → no app page is open; call app.open() or web.goto() first
Tests  1 failed \| 2 passed (3)
| The third test is expected to fail on both. On main the error comes from `setViewport`; here `setViewport` passes and the tap raises it. `check` is red on main at `check:peer-ranges` (the release left canary peers); #619 fixes that, and this PR does not touch it.

title: feat(locator): tap, doubleTap, and secondaryTap hold modifiers
body: Actual Budget's "shift-click range selection skips hidden reconciled transactions" needs `click({ modifiers: ['Shift'] })`. e2e had no modifiers (migration table: missing), so the port faked a `MouseEvent` with `shiftKey` through `web.evaluate`. ```ts await screen.getByRole('row', { name: 'Transaction 1' }).click(); await screen.getByRole('row', { name: 'Transaction 4' }).click({ modifiers: ['Shift'] }); await row.doubleTap({ modifiers: ['Alt'] }); await row.secondaryTap({ modifiers: ['ControlOrMeta'] }); ``` - `tap`/`click`, `doubleTap`, `secondaryTap` take `modifiers` (the `KeyModifier` names of the key grammar, now also exported from `e2e`). The step label names them: `getByRole("row", ...) with Shift`. - Unknown, repeated, or non-array modifiers, and `modifiers` beside `position`, are `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any lookup. - Engine contract: the tap kinds of `LocatorAction` carry `modifiers?`. An engine opts in with a new `Engine` member, `tapModifiers: true`; `defineEngine` requires `perform` for it. - An engine without `tapModifiers` (mobile, any third-party engine written before this) gets `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before the node resolves (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts` `checkAction`, with `session.perform` as the backstop), so it never drops them silently. - `@e2e-dev/web` declares it and hands the list to Playwright's `click`/`dblclick`. - Changesets: `e2e` minor, `@e2e-dev/web` minor. No mobile changeset: its code is untouched, and the refusal is runner behavior covered by the `e2e` entry (mobile docs updated). - Docs: `reference/engine.mdx`, `writing-an-engine.mdx`, `reference/screen.mdx`, the Playwright migration table, mobile pages, `skills/e2e`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["click({ modifiers })"] --> B{valid list?} B -- no --> X[INVALID_ARGUMENT] B -- yes --> C{engine declares tapModifiers?} C -- no --> Y[UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY, before resolve] C -- yes --> D["resolve, perform({ kind: 'tap', modifiers })"] ``` Tests: `locator-action-options` (options, label, pre-resolve refusal), `engine.test.ts` (manifest), `engine-contract.test.ts` (fake engine with and without the flag through the real runner), `web-platform.test.ts` (click/dblclick/contextmenu observe shift, alt, ctrl in Chromium; fails if the web engine drops them). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project, a page of five transaction buttons with a Shift-click range selection (`node server.mjs` on `http://127.0.0.1:0`), one test: click row 1, Shift-click row 4, expect `4 selected`. Same test against a main build and this branch, `e2e run --reporter list`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: click options has no key "modifiers"; it takes timeout, position` | passes, `4 selected` | main: ```text INVALID_ARGUMENT: click options has no key "modifiers"; it takes timeout, position ❯ tests/range.e2e.ts:6:63 Tests 1 failed | 0 passed (1) ``` this branch: ```text ✓ |web| tests/range.e2e.ts (1 test) 227ms ✓ shift-click selects a range 227ms Tests 1 passed (1) ``` Steps in `.e2e/report.json`: ```text app.open | / | passed locator.click | getByRole("button", name: "Transaction 1") | passed locator.click | getByRole("button", name: "Transaction 4") with Shift | passed expect.toHaveText | getByRole("status") | passed ``` - The engine-contract test fails when the session gate is removed; the pre-resolve unit test fails (waits, `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`) without the `checkAction` gate. - Not run on a device: the mobile refusal is proven by the contract test's non-declaring fake engine. - `pnpm check` stops at `check:peer-ranges` (canary peers left by the release, fixed by #619); every other step passes. ---

title: fix(mobile): the iOS runner starts in prepare, not in the first open
body:
Fixes four causes of mobile benchmark flakes found by mining 45 recent `mobile.yml` runs and reproducing them on a Mac mini under load. Two more, in agent-device, are callstack/agent-device#3050 and callstack/agent-device#3051.

- **The iOS runner starts in `prepare`** (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`). A build the suite installs (`E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_IOS_APP`, i.e. CI) used to start the XCUITest runner inside the first test's `app.open()`, under agent-device's 90 s `open` envelope. A cold runner on the 6-vCPU Mac outlasted it. The timed-out `open` resets the daemon, so the other worker's session went too. That is every `open dev.e2e.benchmark failed: Daemon request timed out` in CI, always on a worker's first test (Login Form, control inventory's label query, `setAppearance`), plus the `2 devices match this request equally` / `Invalid daemon response` that followed in the same run. Warm-up now runs `prepare ios-runner` (240 s budget) per slot before any open. A runner that doesn't start leaves the slot unopened instead of retrying under the shorter budget.
- **A bare `locator.longPress()` holds for the engine's default** (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts`). The SDK filled in 500 ms before the engine saw the action, so the mobile engine's documented one-second hold never applied. A `Pressable` with `delayLongPress={800}` (the Gestures scenario) read it as a tap.
- **Async States re-taps Claim when the first tap met a settling scroll view.** A tap that lands while the scroll view still settles from the refresh stops the scroll instead of pressing the button (seen under load; the failure screen still shows Claim). A button still up with no toast gets another bounded tap; the claim is idempotent.
- **setLocation closes Play services' "No location access" warning**, which switching location off can put over the app. The read button stayed hidden and the poll ran out its 60 s (the Android `setLocation` flake).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[prepare: boot] --> B[prepare ios-runner, 240 s]
  B -->|up| C[warm-up open]
  B -->|failed| D[slot left unopened]
  C --> E[first test app.open reuses the runner]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Mobile benchmark, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --target ios-simulator` on two fresh iOS 26.5 simulators with agent-device 0.21.16 as pinned: `prepared 19.10s` (the runner start moved out of the first test), 51 passed. The one failure is the clipboard test, which fails on this Mac's Xcode 27 on main too.
- Cold runner: killed the runner `xcodebuild`, then ran smoke + login form. Both slots logged `prepare` finished ok, and the first test took 9.7 s.
- Android, device-fixture ×4 and setLocation ×10 on an API 36 emulator: all passed.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `longPress()` on the Gestures target, 4 runs | 0/4 advanced | 4/4 advanced |
| iOS warm-up log | `...awaits the suite's device.installApp(); the first attempt starts the automation runner` | runner prepared per slot, `prepared 19.10s` |

Not fixed here, found on the way:
- iOS double tap lands 284 ms apart, against the Gestures scenario's 300 ms window. XCTest reads a two-touch record as one gesture, so there is no quick fix in agent-device.
- Android `Android fill verification failed` on Sequential Onboarding: logcat shows `RemoteInputConnectionImpl: Session id mismatch header.sessionId: 0 currentSessionId: 1 while calling commitText`. The test IME still commits into the previous field's connection seconds after focus moved. This needs an IME-helper change in agent-device.

title: feat(mcp): parallel sessions, and a bug-bash skill topic
body:
`e2e mcp` can now hold several live sessions at once, so a coding agent's subagents can each drive their own browser. On top of that, the skill gets a `bug-bash` topic: run many `e2e explore` charters in parallel, merge what they find, and prove each finding with a repro test before calling it a bug. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[plan charters
routes + diff] --> F[fan out
e2e explore x N
--artifacts .e2e/bugbash/slug] F --> M[merge
run.explore.findings] M --> V[verify, one subagent per finding
own MCP session + repro test] V --> R{fails with
ASSERTION_FAILED?} R -- yes --> C[confirmed + repro test] R -- no --> X[rejected, with reason] ``` ## MCP sessions - `--max-sessions `: 1 to 16, default 4. Each session is its own attempt on its own engine. - `session` may be omitted only while one session is open. With several open, a call without it gets `SESSION_REQUIRED`, which lists the open sessions. - One registry record per session: `SessionRegistry` in `packages/e2e/src/mcp/sessions.ts`. - Each record moves from opening to live to closing, and keeps its slot, engine and config until its attempt has closed. A session that is still booting or still closing therefore counts toward the limit and keeps its claims. - Closing is idempotent. - On shutdown, the server waits for opens still in flight, closes everything, and admits nothing more. - Fresh config per session. Each session reloads the config's project-local module graph (`inGraph` in `packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`), so a config that spreads a base config still gets its own `web()` engine per session. Packages stay shared; a package-made engine that ends up shared fails with `ENGINE_IN_USE`. - One config at a time. Sessions open together share one config, because credentials and secrets resolve process-wide; a session on another config fails with `CONFIG_IN_USE`. The registry is now a hold stack (`holdSecretRegistry` in `secrets.ts`), so closing one session never leaves another without it. - One process-start flow. `startDeclaredProcesses` takes a `ProcessPool`, and a run uses `UNSHARED`. The MCP server uses `SharedAppProcesses` (`packages/e2e/src/run/process-pool.ts`): - It shares each service and each app command across sessions, whatever URL each target probes. - A shared process starts under the pool's own lifetime, not the first session's signal. - A restart waits for the previous stop to finish. - In a run, each service's teardown now runs right after that service stops (reverse order), rather than after all services stop. - Known limit: on mobile, two sessions on one simulator fight over it. The docs and the skill say to declare one target per device. ## Bug bash topic - `skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md`, readable with `e2e guide bug-bash` and `e2e://guide/bug-bash`. There is also a docs page, `docs/bug-bash.mdx`. - Fan-out: charters go in a `slug|target|charter` file, and `xargs -P 4` runs `e2e explore --target --artifacts .e2e/bugbash//artifacts --reporter list,markdown` for each. - Findings are read straight from each log (or its `summary.md`). - A finding counts as confirmed only when its repro test fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` on the assertion that encodes the bug. Repro tests are tagged `bugbash`, so gating runs can pass `--exclude-tag bugbash`. - `reuseExisting` does nothing when `CI` is set, and the skill says so: use port `0` there. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **MCP**: I drove the built `e2e mcp` with a real MCP client against the web benchmark, using `e2e.agent.config.ts` (which spreads a base config). The app was not running beforehand, so the sessions had to start and share it. ```text > open_session x2, concurrently, app not running Session 01a0ecaf-a8cc-... open on target "web" Session 01a0ecaf-a8d5-... open on target "web" > call observe, no session SESSION_REQUIRED: 2 sessions are open; pass session to name one: 01a0ecaf-a8cc-... on "web", 01a0ecaf-a8d5-... on "web" > observe each: A on /e/wishlist, B on /e/cart-totals > close A Session 01a0ecaf-a8cc-... closed (closed by the agent); 2 tool calls ran. > app after A closed: 200; B observes /e/cart-totals > call on A NO_SESSION: session "01a0ecaf-a8cc-..." ended: closed by the agent; call open_session for a new one > open_session on another config CONFIG_IN_USE: session 01a0ecaf-a8d5-... is open on config e2e.agent.config.ts; sessions open at once share one config, ... > close B > app after B closed: down ``` On main, the second `open_session` returns `SESSION_OPEN`. - **Fan-out as the skill writes it**: two charters against the benchmark ran in parallel in 19 s ($0.014 total). Each log listed its finding with the screenshot, `summary.md` held the same, and the video was under the charter's artifacts. Both planted bugs were found (cart totals, wishlist). - **Bug bash**: I ran headless Claude Code with the skill and this server in `apps/web-benchmark`. The app was treated as a black box: the agent was told not to read `app/` or `tests*/`. Model: `gpt-6-luna-fast` for the explorers. | Run | Scope | Planted bugs found | Confirmed bugs | Explore cost | Agent cost | Wall | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | 4 scenarios: cart, wishlist, addresses, promo | 4 / 4 (promo caught while verifying, not by its explorer) | 5 | $0.04 | $2.56 | 14 min | | B | 4 scenarios: orders, newsletter, reviews, checkout | 4 / 4 | 6 | $0.03 | $1.96 | 6 min | | C | 11 shopping/account scenarios | 8 / 9 | 10 | $0.11 | $5.24 | 21 min | Every confirmed bug came with a repro test that fails on its encoded assertion. Rejected findings were listed with reasons (for example: "a cart minimum of 1 is working as designed"). One gap: in the runs above, the agent verified findings one after another rather than handing them to subagents, even after the skill named the Agent/Task tool. Parallel sessions are proven by the transcript above and by `tests/integration/mcp-session-host.test.ts`, not by an agent-driven run.
