title: Video captions: show what the test and the agent are doing on a recording
body:
### Problem

A recording shows what happened on screen but not why. Someone watching a failed attempt's video has to line it up with the report's steps by hand (`step.startedAt` minus the video's `startedAt`). For agent steps the interesting part is not even in the report as a step: which action the agent took on each turn, and what it was going for.

We want recordings that say what the test and the agent are doing, as they play, without that text ever reaching the page the agent observes.

### What the #610 prototype did (removed before merge)

#610 shipped a first cut, taken out so this can be designed properly. The code is kept on the `oskar/video-captions-prototype` branch (8a3f8f07): `packages/e2e/src/run/video.ts`, `writeStepCaptions`, and its tests in `tests/unit/attempt-video.test.ts`.

- A WebVTT sidecar beside each kept recording (`video/video.steps.vtt`, `video/recording-<n>.steps.vtt` for a hosted link), one cue per step: `3. agent.act Sign in`, `- failed` on a step that did not pass.
- A cue runs from its step's start to the next step's start (or its own end if longer, at least 1s for the last), timed from the segment's `startedAt`. A step spanning a restart is captioned in both segments.
- Registered as an artifact of kind `other` (`text/vtt`, `redaction: complete`), linked from the video artifact's `captions` id; best effort, never fails a video.

What we learned:

- Out of the page is a hard requirement: Playwright's `showActions` / `showChapter` overlays are DOM-injected, so the agent would observe them.
- A sidecar plays in VLC, mpv, and a browser `<track>`, but GitHub's player ignores it. The PR demos needed captions burned in with ffmpeg, which e2e has no supported path for.
- One cue per step is too coarse for agent steps: an `agent.act` is one cue for 15 seconds of clicking.
- `e2e mcp` recordings (`start_recording`) got no captions, and there the coding agent is the brain, so e2e never sees its reasoning.

### Data we already have

- Steps: `startedAt`, `durationMs`, `api`, redacted `label`, `status`.
- Agent model calls: a `model` event per call with `startedAt`, `durationMs`, and `reasoning` (the provider's reasoning, redacted, max 600 chars; only when the provider returns it).
- Agent turns: `turns[]` with the tool calls (`tap({"target":"n12"})`) and the visible outcome, redacted, but no timestamp (turn N lines up with the Nth `model` event).
- MCP sessions: every tool call and the screen change it reported.

### Open questions

1. What a cue says: the step, each agent action as a person reads it (`tap button "Sign in"`), the model's reasoning when present, or a short intent the model states per action (a new tool field costs output tokens and changes the tool schemas; measure first).
2. Timing: add `startedAt` to `StepTurn`, or time cues off model events.
3. Delivery: sidecar only, a burn-in option for sharing (and whose ffmpeg), or a player in the report that overlays cues.
4. MCP recordings: caption them from the session's tool calls.
5. Shape in the report: a `captions` link on the video artifact, a new artifact kind, or derived on demand from the report instead of stored.
6. Redaction: reasoning and labels are already redacted and already in `report.json`; confirm nothing new leaks into a file a store exports.

### Which surface

report or cache format, public types (SDK), docs

title: fix(e2e): identify recorded controls by test id, labels only by shape
body:
## What and why

- Replay relocated a recorded control by its exact accessible name. In an app whose labels carry state (`Like (0 likes)`, a row named after its contents and `· now`) that handed every second step back to the model. Relocation now degrades from the strongest identity it recorded: test id, then an authored element id (web now projects the `id` attribute), then the exact label, then the label's shape, then place among unnamed twins.
- An element id counts as authored only when it is not a framework's counter: an id that ends in a digit (`mat-input-2`, `mui-3`, `headlessui-menu-button-1`) or reads like a hash (`:r3:`, `input-1739`) is skipped. A counter names whichever control rendered in that place this time, and an id rung that trusted it typed into the field beside the right one.
- A label's shape folds tallies and relative times only: a count governing a noun (`0 replies`, `3 followers`, `2 matches`) and `now`, `2m`, `yesterday`. A number that names something stays as it reads, so `Delete item 3` never finds `Delete item 4`, `Page 2` never finds `Page 3`, `Order #1234` never finds `Order #9876`. `now` is a time only on its own (`Bob · now`), not the adverb of `Buy now`, and a one-letter unit is lower case only (`3 M` is a size).
- Twins resolve by the recorded position only, never by whichever label happens to match now (the liked button is the one that stopped reading `Like`). Any rung that finds another number of them than were recorded passes to the next rung, and a lone survivor of a recorded set is ambiguous, not found: among label twins it is whichever one still reads as recorded, which after the step acted on the recorded one is exactly the wrong one.
- End anchors compare their labels as they read, with only relative times folded. A count is usually the very effect the anchor stands for, so a recorded `Count: 1`, `Step 2 of 3`, or `Cart (2 items)` does not pass on a screen left at `Count: 0`, `Step 1 of 3`, `Cart (1 item)`. Anchors are the leaves that appeared, ranked by durability, and skip relative times and social tallies; an unreadable end screen reports every anchor as missing; a stable container outranks volatile leaves.
- An `end-mismatch` hand-off names the anchors the screen did not show, in `step.cache.missingAnchors` and in the notice the agent gets. That is how the shell-chrome anchors were found.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile`: every settings request names the worker's device through one `settings()` helper. Without it the daemon resolved `clear app state` against every booted device, and one engine failure failed every later test of a run with "2 devices match this request equally".
- `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` goes to `conservative/7`; recordings re-record once on their next passing run.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[recorded target] --> T{test id recorded?}
  T -- yes --> I[nodes with that test id]
  T -- no --> E
  I -- none --> E{element id recorded?}
  E -- yes --> J[nodes with that element id]
  E -- no --> L
  J -- none --> L[label equal]
  L -- none --> S[label shape equal]
  S -- none --> N[not found: hand off]
  I -- one --> F[found]
  J -- one --> F
  L -- one --> F
  S -- one --> F
  I -- several --> P{same count as recorded?}
  J -- several --> P
  L -- several --> P
  S -- several --> P
  P -- yes --> F
  P -- no --> A[ambiguous: hand off]
```

`packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts` (`matchingTiers`, `labelShape`) and `packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts` (`anchorMatches`) share `SEMANTIC_ID_FIELDS` and `sameLabels`, so the two can no longer drift; anchors ask for the `times` fold, relocation for `counts`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Bluesky iOS suite on the published canary versus this branch, the three files with the most hand-offs (composer, home, thread; 10 tests), one recording pass then a replay pass on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator:

| Measure | main | this branch | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Steps replayed clean | 26 | 34 | +8 |
| Steps handed off | 8 | 1 | -7 |
| Model calls per run | 54 | 19 | -65% |
| Wall clock | 879s | 574s | -35% |
| `home.e2e.ts` | 228s, 4 tests with model calls | 67s, zero model calls | |

- The one remaining hand-off is pull-to-refresh, which the mobile tool pack records as an unreplayable `swipe` tool; a grammar action for it is a separate change.
- A stress probe through the real CLI against a scratch web app whose state drifts between the recording run and the replay run, on main, on the first version of this branch, and on this branch as it stands:

| Scenario | main | first version | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Increment` click is a no-op on replay, status reads `Count: 0` | handed off, agent reports the count did not move | replayed clean, anchor `Count: 1` taken by shape | handed off, agent reports the count did not move |
| `Delete item 3` recorded, only `Delete item 4` on screen | handed off | replayed clean onto `Delete item 4` | `target-not-found`, agent runs live and leaves item 4 |
| `Email` recorded with id `mat-input-2`; on replay that id is `Phone`, `Email` is `mat-input-3` | replays onto `Email` by label | replayed clean into `Phone` | replays onto `Email` by label, no model call |

- Web benchmark agentic suite with the committed `conservative/7` recordings under `--strict-cache`: 32 passed, 25 replayed, no `REPLAY_STALE`; the hand-offs and misses are the designed `gap` and unique-param cases.
- Testbed agent suite, a recording pass then a replay pass: 24 passed both times, 21 steps replayed with no action model call on the replay.
- iOS benchmark agentic suite re-recorded on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator under `conservative/7`, then a read-only replay pass: 22 passed, 13 steps from cache, 8 handed off (tool gaps, native sheets), the same profile the previous entries had in CI.
- `missingAnchors` in a real hand-off, before the leaf-only rule:
  `["other \"Test harness control, not part of the app\"", "other \"Home\"", "scroll-view \"Following\"", "other \"New post\""]` with the post text itself on screen.
- Mobile fix: a run with an iOS simulator and an Android emulator both booted no longer cascades after an engine failure.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(explore): short, stable artifact directory per goal
body: `e2e explore` artifact directories were named from the whole encoded goal, so every evidence path in the terminal, `summary.md`, and `report.json` repeated something like `explore__Starting_20at_20_2Fe_2Fcart-totals_2C_20...-8503b71d`. They are now `explore-` plus a slug of the goal's first words (32 characters at most) and a 16-character hash of the whole goal. - Explore sets a new internal `RegisteredTest.artifactName`, and `src/run/execute.ts` sends it through `sanitizePathSegment` as before. The test id, `report.json`, the report-1 schema, and paths for ordinary tests are unchanged. - The name is lowercased with accents removed, and Latin letters NFKD leaves whole (`ł`, `ø`, `ß`, ...) are transliterated, so `Łódź` reads `lodz`. A leading "explore" is dropped so the name doesn't say it twice, and a goal with no ASCII words becomes `explore-`. - Unit tests pin the exact name, that two goals with the same opening get different directories (including a pair whose first 8 hex digits collide), and accented, non-ASCII, and path-like goals. The explore integration test pins the full evidence path. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the built CLI against the testbed with a scripted model. The terminal, `summary.md`, and `report.json` all show the new path, and `report.json` passes the report-1 schema. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `web/explore__Starting_20at_20_2Fe_2Fcart-totals_2C_20change_20each_20quantity_20up_20and_20down_3B_20check_20every_-8503b71d/default/attempt-0/finding-1.png` | `web/explore-starting-at-e-cart-totals-change-05548d832bd70a7a/default/attempt-0/finding-1.png` | Two goals whose 8-hex digests collide (`...quantities 5885` and `...quantities 62140`) land in `...-after-5846d49d844ea116` and `...-after-5846d49df03de864`; `Sprawdź koszyk w Łodzi` lands in `explore-sprawdz-koszyk-w-lodzi-a4b90f83993c7ff8`. ---

title: docs: assert auto-dismissing toasts before slower checks
body: During a bug bash, a verifier writing tests against an app that uses sonner reported that `screen.getByText` could not see toast text. That was a test-writing mistake, not an engine gap. The docs now say how to assert a toast that dismisses itself, and the testbed pins the right pattern. - **Root cause.** Sonner removes a toast 4000 ms after it mounts, plus a 200 ms unmount. That is shorter than the default assertion timeout. The verifier's test first ran an assertion that could never pass, and that assertion polled for 5 s. By the time the toast check ran, the toast was gone, and the failure screen showed an empty `region "Notifications alt+T"`. - **The engine is fine.** On the live app, `getByText("Failed to update project")` passed `toBeVisible()` 5 ms after the tap. Sonner gives toasts no role, so `getByRole('status')` finds nothing. The toast is a `listitem` inside the named region. - **Docs.** `writing-tests` and `debugging`, in both the docs site and `skills/e2e`, now say to: - assert a toast right after the action that shows it; - find it by text, or by the region and then its list item filtered by the toast's text, since toasts stack; - remember that the failure screen is captured after the wait. - **Tests.** - The testbed has a new `/toasts` page with sonner's markup and timing: one list while any toast is up, one item per toast, typed `error` or `success` by the save's outcome. `tests/toasts.e2e.ts` reads the failure toast by text and by region until it dismisses, and checks that a successful save shows a `success` toast. - A `toasts` fixture was added to the web crosscheck. The engine, Chrome, and Playwright agree on it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Checked against the running app: the toast mounted 72 ms after the tap and was gone at 4274 ms. `getByText(...).toBeVisible()` right after the tap passes. - Reproduced on the testbed page with a scratch test. It failed three ways and passed one: - a slow check first: no node; - `count()` right after the tap: 0; - `getByRole('status')`: no node; - `toBeVisible()` right after the tap: passes. - Suites: the testbed ran 70 passed and 1 skipped. The web crosscheck passes, and `pnpm check` passes. Docs only, so there is no changeset, matching #574. ---

title: fix(web): show whole link targets in observations
body: The agent's view of the screen cut every link href at 80 characters and didn't mark the cut. In a bug bash, an explorer saw a link that ended exactly at 80 characters and filed a false bug: "link targets a truncated project ID". The real href held the full UUID. - **Engine (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`).** - Reports the origin plus the full path. A dropped query shows as `?…` and a dropped fragment as `#…`. - `data:` and `javascript:` hrefs come back as `data:…` and `javascript:…` instead of their whole payload. - `mailto:`, `tel:`, and `blob:` keep their scheme. `blob:` links used to come out with the origin doubled. Now the inner URL is rebuilt as origin + path, which drops any userinfo; a `blob:` with no inner origin becomes `blob:…`. - **Runner (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts`).** - A link on the app's own origin shows as its path. That form is shorter and complete, and `navigate` resolves paths against the same origin. - A link on any other origin keeps its full URL, so on an OAuth or payment page the model can't mistake a foreign path for an app path. - Anything still longer than 256 characters is cut with a trailing `…`. The cut happens after secret redaction and never splits a surrogate pair. - The same limit applies when the tree is handed to a custom executor (`projectTree`) and to MCP `locate`. The executor tree keeps app links absolute, but applies the 256 limit to the path after the app origin, so it keeps as much of the path as the line does. - Same-origin links no longer repeat the origin, so observations cost fewer tokens overall. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the built `e2e mcp` server against a scratch page, once on main and once on this branch, and called `observe`. Then I navigated to a second origin: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | long app link | `href="http://127.0.0.1:4391/dashboard/e2e-dc3cf837/projects/404b2532-9fab-44dc-b3d0-f0"` | `href="/dashboard/e2e-dc3cf837/projects/404b2532-9fab-44dc-b3d0-f0a1b2c3d4e5"` | | link with query | `href="http://127.0.0.1:4391/dashboard/e2e-dc3cf837/runs"` | `href="/dashboard/e2e-dc3cf837/runs?…"` | | data: export link | whole payload, up to 80 chars | `href="data:…"` | | link on a foreign page | (absolute) | `href="http://127.0.0.1:4392/dashboard/..."`, while `href="/dashboard"` stays on the app | - Tests: - New unit tests in `agent-observation.test.ts`: long same-origin and cross-origin links, query, fragment, `mailto:`, `blob:`, an origin lookalike, a foreign page, redaction before the cut, surrogate pairs, executor-tree bounds. - A new web integration test, including `blob:` with userinfo and an opaque `blob:`. - Suites: `pnpm check` passes, and so do the e2e unit tests, the web tests, and testbed `controls.e2e.ts`. ---

title: feat(explore): --session starts the exploration signed in
body: `e2e explore --session ` starts an exploration signed in. It runs the setup test that saves that session, then explores with the session restored. Why: in a real bug bash every charter had to sign in by filling a password with `type_secret`. Once a secret is on screen, screenshots are withheld, so none of the 21 findings had a screenshot. A project usually signs in once already, in a setup test, so explore can start from that. - **How it works.** Explore sets `options.session` on its in-memory test. The runner then collects the config's test files with none of them selected. Its normal session selection pulls in only the setup test that declares that name. This is the same path `e2e run ` takes, so there's no second way to do it. - **The setup runs as the project wrote it.** It keeps its own agents, trace cache, and retries. Only the exploration test runs as the explorer with the cache off. - **The explorer knows it starts signed in.** The planner prompt and the agent context both say so, and the body still calls `app.open()` after the restore. - **An unknown name fails early.** It fails in collection with `COLLECTION_ERROR` and exit 2, before any app process starts. The message now lists the declared sessions and suggests the closest one, and `e2e run` gets the better message too. - **Screenshots depend on how the setup signed in.** A restored session keeps its setup's taint. If the setup signed in by setting a cookie or calling an API, screenshots stay available. If it typed a password, they stay withheld. - `explore.mdx` has a table showing this. - I also fixed `authentication.mdx`, which wrongly said a setup test keeps screenshots available. - **Docs.** CLI reference, `explore.mdx`, `errors.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/explore.md`, and a changeset. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Live model** on the testbed (`gpt-6-luna-fast`, config with a live agent added): ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 207ms ✓ |web| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test) 228ms ❯ |web| Exploring Starting at /dashboard, look around the signed-in dashboard and report anything broken ✓ 1 Dashboard overview 7.17s · 1 action Findings none AI 22.7k tokens · $0.0035 · 5 model calls ``` The setup ran, and the explorer started on the signed-in dashboard without trying to sign in. - **Scripted model** on the testbed: - `--session admin-cookie`: the setup ran, and the finding carries `finding-1.png` as evidence. - `--session admin`: that setup fills the password, so the finding has no screenshot, as documented. - `--session admn`: `COLLECTION_ERROR ... setup tests declare "admin", "admin-cookie"; did you mean "admin"?` - **Tests.** - New integration cases: a deterministic setup, a tainted setup, an unknown name, and an agentic setup. - The agentic case checks that the setup's system prompt has no exploration rules and that it can't report findings. It fails if the explorer is swapped back in for the whole run. - **Suites.** `pnpm check` passes, the e2e unit tests pass, the related integration files pass, and so does the full testbed suite. ---

title: docs(skill): bug-bash lessons from a full-stack bash
body:
Lessons from a full-stack bug bash: 8 charters against a production Next.js dashboard with Postgres, Redis, an auth emulator, and per-charter seeded workspaces. Stacked on #634, which adds the `bug-bash` topic.

- **Prepare** covers what went wrong or cost time:
  - **Services with a teardown.** If the target declares services with a `teardown` (for example `docker compose down --volumes`), parallel explorers remove the database from under each other. Start the stack once and explore with an untracked bug-bash config that declares no services. A typechecked example config is included.
  - **Production build.** Dev-server compile lag produced a false "link does nothing" finding.
  - **One seeded account per charter.**
  - **Say what the local app can't do.** About 40% of that bash's findings were caused by missing email or AI keys and billing limits, so the agent's `context` should name them.
  - **Explore step budget of 40.** A project config tuned for 15-step test steps starves explore.
- **Signed-in charters.** Start them with `e2e explore --session <name>` (#641). If the setup signs in without typing a password, every finding keeps its screenshot.
- **New Triage step** before any test is written. Each finding goes into one of four buckets: environment, design, fixture, or candidate. Reading the source settled most of them in about a minute each.
- **Verify.**
  - One subagent per area, with 3 to 5 findings, reporting root causes as `file:line`.
  - Tests that disprove a finding move out of `tests/bugbash/`.
  - A charter that filled a password has no screenshots, so use its video.
- **Report.**
  - Rejected findings are grouped by reason.
  - Production risks found during environment triage are listed as unverified.
- **Docs.** `docs/bug-bash.mdx` gets the same points in short form.

## Verified

Ran it locally: no - docs and skill text only.
- The bug-bash config example typechecks: I placed it in `apps/web-benchmark/tests/` next to the real config, ran `tsc --noEmit`, and got no errors. A planted type error in the same file was caught, so the check really covered it.
- The approach was exercised end to end in that bash: 8 charters, 21 findings, 4 confirmed, each with a failing repro test.
- `docs:check`, and the skill and guide tests pass.

title: fix(explore): recheck the screen before recording a finding
body: `e2e explore` reported findings on screens that were still loading. In a real bug bash, the explorer opened a saved test during its React Suspense loading state and filed "lands on an empty test page" as high severity. A verifier showed the page renders fully moments later. Another charter reported a dead link on a dev server that was still compiling the route. `report_finding` now checks the screen again before it records anything. - **How it works.** - The first report on a screen takes its screenshot, waits 1.5 s, and looks again. - If the screen changed from the one the model had when it reported, nothing is recorded. A changed path counts as a change, and so does a truncated screen. The tool tells the model to report again or drop the finding, then shows the new screen, in full. - A report on a screen that was already checked records at once, whether it's the confirmation or a second finding on the same screen. - **It never loses a finding.** - If the model acted during the wait, for example a tap batched in the same turn, the finding is recorded against the screenshot taken when it reported. - With less than 6.5 s left in the step, the check is skipped. After the wait, only the confirmation itself (5 s) has to fit. A wait cut short by the step stopping still records. - If the next turn could only conclude (the turn budget, a tripped loop guard, a low clock), the finding records as reported. The tool reads this from a new tool-loop helper, `nextTurnWorks`, which uses the rule that forces the conclusion. - **Design.** - `report_finding` is now a host tool, added through a new internal `createHostedAgent`. It reads the model's screen directly, and its answer skips the size cap on project tools. - The project-tool path and `tool.ts` are unchanged from main. - **Explorer instructions.** A screen that is still loading is not a defect. Observe once before calling a page empty or a control dead. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Scripted model, built CLI, a copy of the saved-test loading page:** | | findings | exit | | --- | --- | --- | | main | 1 false "high issue: ... lands on an empty test page" | 1 | | this branch | none (the model got the rendered screen and dropped it) | 0 | - **Live model** (`gpt-6-luna-fast`) on the testbed's bug garden, which has planted defects, to check that real findings still get recorded: ```text ⚑ medium issue Neuromancer displays negative stock (/catalog) ⚑ high issue Cart total stays at $14 after increasing quantity (/cart) ⚑ trivial warning Empty-cart message contains a stray extra period (/cart) ⚑ trivial warning Checkout newsletter label misspells "Receive" (/checkout) ⚑ medium issue Order confirmation shows 1970 order date and earlier delivery date (/checkout) ⚑ medium issue Orders count says three but only two orders are listed (/orders) Findings 4 issues | 2 warnings AI 199.0k tokens · 87% cached · $0.0137 · 30 model calls ``` All 6 have a screenshot, and none was wrongly held back. - **Tests.** - The loading page stays loading until the test releases it, so no timer decides the outcome. - New cases: a report on a loading screen with only concluding turns left records at once; a report on a still screen records on the first call; a 450-line screen comes back whole with the instruction first; a report batched with a tap records; low step time, an aborted wait, and held-back-then-recorded are covered. - The explore integration file (18 tests after rebasing on main, including the new `--session` ones) passes locally and in CI. The `--session` secret-fill test now reports on the still `/storage` page: on the home page a button appears 400 ms after load, so a report made there at once is correctly held back. - **Suites.** `pnpm check` passes, and so do the e2e unit tests and the policy, MCP, and AI-trace integration tests. ---

title: test(mobile-benchmark): setNetwork asserts Wi-Fi handover, not a transient disconnect
body: ## Summary `device fixture > setNetwork and setAirplaneMode change what the app sees` flaked on Android: after `device.setNetwork('offline')` the app still read `network: connected`. It failed 1 of 6 full local runs, and once in each of rounds 1 and 2. Root cause: the test's premise is wrong on the emulator. `setNetwork` switches Wi-Fi alone (`svc wifi disable`, as documented: "Toggles the device's Wi-Fi"). The emulator also keeps a cellular link (`MOBILE[NR] CONNECTED` in `dumpsys connectivity`), which becomes the default network within about a second of Wi-Fi going off. expo-network reports `isConnected: false` only while Android still names the lost Wi-Fi network as active; once cellular takes over it reports connected again. So `toHaveText('network: disconnected')` passed only when a poll landed inside that sub-second window, and a loaded run missed it. The change: - The benchmark app prints its network type (`network type: wifi|cellular|none|...`) under the existing connected line. - The test asserts what `setNetwork` actually does: Wi-Fi goes away (`cellular` or `none`) and comes back (`wifi`). Airplane mode still asserts `disconnected`, a steady state since it cuts both radios. - The assertions that wait for a radio to come back get 30 s. Wi-Fi re-associates and validates before Android makes it the default network again, which took 5.5 s on an idle emulator, against the default window of about 5 s. JS only. CI repacks the new bundle into the cached native build. ## Verified - On the emulator, after `svc wifi disable`, cellular becomes the default network within about 1 s. After `svc wifi enable`, Wi-Fi becomes the default again after about 5.5 s. - The new test, 15 repeats in a row with 8 CPU-stress processes on the Android emulator: 15/15 passed. It passed in all 3 later full Android runs. - The first version, with the default timeout on "Wi-Fi comes back", failed 15/15 (`observed: network type: cellular`). That's why the reconnect assertions got the longer allowance. - `pnpm check`: passed.

title: feat(config)!: config shape, part 1: recording modes, output root, test-glob exclusions, renames, secrets in engine options
body:
First layer of the config redesign agreed after #610 (it replaces the closed #489). Stack: this PR, then #646 (agents), then #648 (the app on the target and services).

**Recording modes**
- `trace` and `video` share one `RecordingMode`: `'off' | 'on' | 'retain-on-failure' | 'on-first-retry' | 'on-all-retries'`.
- They can be set at the config root, on a target, on a test or describe, or with `--trace [mode]` / `--video [mode]`. Precedence, lowest first: config, target, CLI, test.
- Trace defaults to `on` locally and `on-first-retry` in CI. There's a notice when a retry mode meets `retries: 0`.
- A mode set at the config root or with a flag skips targets that can't record, with one notice. A mode set on a target or a test is required and fails with `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT`.
- `artifacts.kinds` and `artifacts.trace` are removed, and each old form names the `trace` mode it meant. Failure screenshots are always captured.

**Output**
- `output` (default `.e2e`, `--output`) is the one per-run root: report, junit, summary, ai-trace, `artifacts/`, `sessions/`, and MCP videos. `cache.dir` stays separate.
- `<output>/artifacts` is cleared at run start. The output directory is validated: not the project root, not inside the cache, not holding the tests.
- `--artifacts` is hidden and fails with the `--output` mapping.
- `artifacts` holds only `store`. The optional `ArtifactStore.putLink` receives provider-hosted video links, and its `ref` goes into the report.

```ts
trace: 'on-first-retry',
video: 'retain-on-failure',
output: '.e2e',
artifacts: { store: { put, putLink } },
targets: [{ name: 'kernel', engine, video: 'on', trace: 'off' }],
test('checkout', { video: 'on' }, ...);
```

**Smaller changes**

- `specVersion` is removed. A config that sets it fails with `INVALID_CONFIG`; the runner version is the format version. The report's internal `specVersion` is unchanged.
- `tests` accepts `!` exclusions (`['tests/**/*.e2e.ts', '!tests/wip/**']`). A list of only exclusions is `INVALID_CONFIG`.
- Renames: `TraceCacheStore` becomes `CacheStore`, "trace cache" becomes "replay cache" in docs and CLI help, and `web({ video: { size, quality } })` becomes `web({ screencast })`. `web({ video })` fails naming `screencast`.
- `secrets.get('name')` works in engine options:
  - At config time it returns a deferred handle that carries only the name. The config load checks the name, with a did-you-mean.
  - The worker resolves it per attempt through the new `EngineAttemptContext.resolveSecret`, and the value joins the redaction ledger first.
  - `web({ basicAuth: { password } })` accepts a Secret.
- `process.loadEnvFile('.env')` is documented as the way to load env files.

```ts
secrets: { stagingPassword: () => process.env.STAGING_PASSWORD! },
targets: [{ engine: web({ basicAuth: { username: 'staging', password: secrets.get('stagingPassword') } }) }],
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI in the testbed:
  - `--output .e2e-verify` wrote the report, junit and markdown files there and cleared a stale artifact.
  - `--trace=retain-on-failure` kept no traces for passing tests, and `--trace` kept `trace/trace.zip` per attempt.
  - `--output .` and `--artifacts` exit 2 with the expected messages.
- Built CLI in the testbed with a scratch config:
  - `specVersion` is rejected.
  - `!` exclusions select the right files, and an exclusions-only list fails.
  - `web({ video })` names `screencast`.
  - An unknown `secrets.get()` name gets a did-you-mean.
  - `e2e cache --help` says "replay cache".
- New `engine-secrets.test.ts`: a real config, workers, and a browser. A provider-backed basic-auth password echoed by the page is redacted from the failure message, the report, and the reporter files. It fails when the ledger registration is removed from the built `dist`.

title: feat(agents)!: plain-object agents entries; createAgent and limits removed
body:
Stacked on #645; #648 (the app on the target and services) is stacked on this. Each `agents` entry is now one plain object; `createAgent()` and the top-level `limits` are gone.

```ts
agents: {
  default: { model, judge, system: 'Prefer the keyboard.', context: 'Plans are called tiers.', tools: { lookupOrder }, maxSteps: 25, maxModelCalls: 25, judgmentTimeout: 30_000, maxInputTokens: 64_000 },
  thorough: { model: sonnet, system: 'Verify every total before finishing.', maxSteps: 50, maxModelCalls: 60 },
  custom: { executor: myBrain, model, maxModelCalls: 10 },
},
```

- **One place for every agent option.** Budgets used to be split between the entry and `limits`, and `system`/`tools` between the entry and `createAgent()`. Each entry starts from the built-in defaults, never from `default`'s values.
- **`executor` is for a custom brain.** `model`, `judge`, `context` and the budgets still apply; `system` or `tools` next to it are `INVALID_CONFIG`. `AgentConfig` is a union, so this is a type error too.
- **Removed keys fail naming their replacement:**
  - `timeout` becomes `judgmentTimeout`.
  - `maxTurns` becomes `maxModelCalls`, also in `createToolLoopExecutor`.
  - `limits.maxModelTokensPerCall` becomes the entry's `maxInputTokens`.
  - `limits` itself is removed.
  - A bare `StepExecutor` entry points at `{ executor }`.
  - Unknown keys get a did-you-mean.
- **Fixed internal limits:** `maxAgentContextBytes`, `maxLedgerBytes` and `maxEventsPerStep` are fixed at 16384, 8192 and 1000. The report's `run.limits` keeps its wire shape, filled from the largest per-agent values and the fixed ones. No schema bump.
- **Tools are validated at config load:** `defineTool` only, a real `execute`, and no built-in tool names.
- **`e2e mcp`** serves the entry's `tools`.
- **`explore`** extends the entry instead of building an executor.
- **`createAgent()` is deleted,** not stubbed. A config that imports it fails to load with an ESM missing-export error. That's acceptable pre-1.0, and the changeset, `config.mdx` and the skill name the new shape.
- **Built-in agent identity is unchanged** (`e2e-default-agent`/`2`), so committed recordings keep replaying.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI in the testbed:
  - Configs using `limits`, agent `timeout` and a bare executor each exit 2 with the new message.
  - A new-shape config with `system`, `tools`, `judgmentTimeout` and `maxInputTokens` passes `tests/forms.e2e.ts`.
  - `run.limits` in the report reads the max across agents.

title: feat!: the app is declared on its target; services are defineService handles
body:
Services are `defineService` handles, listed on the targets that need them. This is the second half of the config redesign, on top of #698 (the app on its target, now on main); it replaces the closed #489.

```ts
const db = defineService({ name: 'db', executable: 'docker', args: ['compose', 'up', '--wait'], waitForExit: true, teardown: { ... } });
const seed = defineService({ name: 'seed', dependsOn: [db], start: async () => { ... }, stop: async () => { ... } });
const webServer = defineService({ name: 'web-server', executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev', '--port', '{port}'], readyUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', env: { API: api.url }, dependsOn: [seed] });

targets: [
  { name: 'chromium', engine: web(), app: { url: webServer.url }, services: [webServer] },
  { name: 'firefox', engine: web({ browser: 'firefox' }), app: { url: webServer.url }, services: [webServer] },   // one shared dev server
  { name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios' }), app: { bundleId: 'dev.shop.app', appPath: './build/Shop.app' }, services: [seed] },
],
```

**One process model**
- A service is a process (`executable` with `readyUrl` or `waitForExit`) or a function (`start`, `stop`), never both. `dependsOn` orders services and pulls dependencies in; `defineService` copies and freezes its lists, so a cycle cannot exist.
- `app.command` is shorthand for a service named `app:<target>`.
- `{port}` is a process's own free port, and a process with more than one names them (`ports: { smtp: 0 }`, `{port:smtp}`). A service that uses `{port}` on a fixed port is `INVALID_CONFIG`, with a message spelling the new form (it used to mean the app's port).
- Address placeholders are plain strings holding a token: `svc.url`, `svc.port`, and `svc.urlOf('smtp')`, `svc.portOf('smtp')` for a named port, usable inside a longer string. The config resolves without ports, and `assignPorts` binds them, in the main process and again in each worker from the port list the main process hands down.
- Services live for the whole run. Function services get the addresses of their dependencies. Child processes inherit the runner's full environment, with `env` on top.
- Refused at load: two processes probing one fixed address, `app.command` beside a service URL, a placeholder outside the reader's graph, a placeholder in a `readyUrl`, an `app.readyUrl` on port 0.

**Layout**
- `config/services/` is four modules behind an index: `model` (templates and resolved services), `collect` (the graph and its start order), `template` (checking a process into a template, `{port}` and placeholder rules), `bind` (substituting the run's ports, keys, port requests, digest). An app command is a process spec that serves `app.url`; nothing in the template code knows a role.
- `ResolvedTarget.appUrl` carries `app.url` as the service resolution reads it; `ResolvedApp` holds only resolved facts. The services types live in `types/services.ts`, re-exported from `e2e`.

**`e2e mcp`**
- Sessions share a process when its key matches: name plus dependency keys for function services, the resolved command for processes.
- A session that opens while one that was assigned ports is still admitted reads the same ports, serialized across concurrent opens, so a fixed-port process stays shared when a service it depends on asks for a free one; once no such session is left, the next gets fresh ports. Before, the second session found the first's process and failed with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.

**Bugs found by live runs, fixed here**
- A hung function `start` ignored interrupts. Now the first interrupt aborts the start, and teardown runs. Function services also get a `startupTimeout` (default 60s).
- `teardown` ran for a service that never spawned, which could run `docker compose down` on your own stack. Now it runs only after a spawn.
- A throwing `stop` is named: `service "seed" stop failed: ...`, and a function service that never started is not stopped.
- A locator's reported `waitedMs` is timed on its own deadline's clock (`Deadline.min` anchors at now), so it can no longer read one millisecond short of the timeout.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI on the testbed: two chromium targets shared one port-0 dev server through `app: { url: webServer.url }`, with a function seed service and an API placeholder, on two workers. Both targets landed on the same port, and the seed's `start`/`stop` wrapped the run.
- A hung function `start` under the real CLI: the first SIGINT exits 130, and the log shows the dependencies stopped and their teardowns ran.
- The MCP port fix: `mcp-session-host.test.ts` opens two sessions at once on a fixed-port app command beside a port-0 service. It failed with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` before the fix and passes after.

title: test(mobile-benchmark): the agentic Gestures scenario runs on Android only
body: ## Summary iOS agentic `act completes Gestures` fails often on CI (for example 13 of the last 33 `ios agentic` jobs had it in their first pass; the `--last-failed` rerun hides it). The scenario needs a double tap inside the app's 300 ms window, and an iOS runner cannot land one on a React Native `Pressable`: - Two taps arrive 285 to 317 ms apart. `controls.e2e.ts` documents 284 to 285 ms on an idle host. - I measured the alternatives in agent-device's runner, with the app's `tap-count` readback (`N taps, M ms apart`): - two separately synthesized taps with XCTest's idle waits skipped: `2 taps, 300 ms apart` / `317 ms apart`. Each synthesis blocks about 300 ms, so the pair can't get closer; - two touches in one synthesized record (two pointer paths, or one path that re-presses, with 200 or 260 ms spacing): `1 tap`; - XCTest's own `doubleTap()`: `1 tap`, as `controls.e2e.ts` already notes. - The swipe step also goes through the free-form device tool on iOS: the card is a plain View the tree does not list, so the model picks the drag geometry and often misses the -80 threshold ("swiped the card left three times, but the screen did not advance"). `controls.e2e.ts`'s `a double tap lands inside the 300 ms window` is Android only for the same reason. This makes the agentic scenario match it, and deletes the iOS Gestures recording that no longer has a test. ## Verified - A deterministic probe of the same flow on iOS, 10 runs under CPU stress: long press 10/10, node swipe 10/10, double tap 3/10. That points at the double tap, not the swipe. - Android agentic `Gestures`: passed in all 4 local runs and on CI. - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile-benchmark run typecheck`: passed. ---

title: fix(mobile): a touch on a control under a sticky footer lifts it clear first
body:
## Summary

`sticky chrome: accept below the fold, then continue` flakes on iOS: 5 of 60 locally under CPU stress, and on CI (for example [this job](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36557530061), hidden by the `--last-failed` rerun). The failure screenshot shows the cause: `scrollUntilVisible` stops once the Accept button's rect is on screen, while the button is still mostly under the sticky footer. The tap at its centre lands on the footer, and nothing registers. The accessibility tree has no z-order or occlusion, and the footer's background isn't a node, so nothing flagged the button as covered.

The engine now lifts a covered control clear before a touch (`tap`, `doubleTap`, `longPress`, `fill`, `clear`, `check`, `uncheck`, `focus`, and a character `press`, which taps an unfocused field first):
- **Covered** means a named node drawn after the control's vertical list (so on top of it), sitting in the list's lower half, has a band that contains the control's centre. The band is the node's width, from its top minus the footer's padding (16 pt) down to the list's bottom, which covers the footer background that isn't in the tree. Layout wrappers as large as half the list don't count.
- **Lift:** a 400 ms `pan` (a controlled drag, no fling) moves the list up just far enough to put the centre 24 pt above the band, at most a quarter of the list, starting above the chrome.
  - After each lift, the control is found again near its old place shifted by the pan, so a row a virtualized list mounts in the old place doesn't take the touch.
  - Up to 3 lifts, stopping as soon as a lift leaves the control in place (the list is at its end).
  - The lifted snapshot becomes the action's before-state, so the next action doesn't wait out a transition that already settled.
- **Left alone:**
  - a control the snapshot lists more than once, since after a scroll the nearest match could be a neighbour;
  - chrome at the top, since pulling a list at its top could fire a refresh;
  - horizontal lists.
- **Cost:** the check reads the snapshot the control was just resolved from, so an uncovered control costs nothing.

A fresh-context review found the first version flagged any overlap (a FAB beside a row), could swap alike rows after the scroll, and swiped a fixed distance; those are the rules above. The bot reviews added the re-find by the pan's shift, the stop at the list's end, `press`, and the before-state.

## Verified

- Sticky chrome, 40 repeats on iOS with 8 CPU-stress processes:

  | Build | Failed | Lifted |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `main` | 5 of 60 | - |
  | first version | 0 of 40 | 39 of 40 taps |
  | review rules | 0 of 40 | 39 of 40 taps, one lift each (~0.8 s extra) |
  | this branch (after the bot reviews) | 0 of 20 | - |

  On `main`, the remaining taps passed by landing in the few points of the button above the footer.
- The full deterministic suite, iOS and Android at once under stress, twice each (first version): iOS 51/52 (only the Xcode-27-local clipboard test), Android 54/54.
- Unit tests:
  - the real iOS Sticky Chrome capture, with Accept peeking under the footer, is covered, with the band reaching the list bottom;
  - clear or edge-only overlaps are not covered;
  - a FAB beside a row, a header, a horizontal list, and a node in no list are left alone;
  - the engine lifts once with the computed pan and presses the re-found control (new refs);
  - alike controls are not lifted;
  - a list at its end gets one lift;
  - a row mounted in the old place doesn't take the press;
  - a character press lifts the field it focuses;
  - the next action on a lifted control goes out at once.

  Each fails on `main` or with its fix reverted.
- `pnpm check`: passed.

title: docs: add a Copy page menu with Markdown and AI assistant links
body: Every docs page gets a "Copy page" dropdown in the header, modeled on docs.expo.dev. - `docs/docs.json` enables Mintlify's `contextual` menu. Copy page, View as Markdown, Open in ChatGPT, and Open in Claude are Mintlify built-ins. - Open in Codex (`codex://new?prompt=`), Open in Claude Code (`claude-cli://open?q=`), and Open in Cursor (`https://cursor.com/link/prompt?text=`) are custom options. They use the deep links Expo ships, with Expo's prompt and the page's Markdown URL: `https://e2e.tester.army/docs$path.md`. - The Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor logos are in `docs/images/contextual/`, copied from Expo's icons. Mintlify renders a local path in `icon` as an ``, so `docs/style.css` inverts them in dark mode and matches the built-in icons' opacity. - The schema requires a `description` on every custom option. `docs/style.css` hides that second line so the menu shows titles only. The selectors depend on Mintlify's current menu markup, so a Mintlify redesign could bring the descriptions back. - The menu was never enabled before. title: refactor(kernel)!: rename @e2e-dev/integrations to @e2e-dev/kernel
body: ## What and why - `@e2e-dev/integrations/kernel` becomes its own package, `@e2e-dev/kernel`. Integrations are now one package per hosted service, named after the service, the same way `@e2e-dev/github` already works. - Each package can make its vendor SDK and engine required peers. Before, one package held every integration, so every SDK had to be an optional peer that nothing checks at install time. - Each service gets its own version and changelog, so a breaking change in one integration doesn't bump the others. - `packages/integrations` is renamed to `packages/kernel` and `src/kernel/*` moves up into `src/`. The package has only the root `.` export. - `@onkernel/sdk` and `@e2e-dev/web` go from optional to required peers. - The two pending changesets now target `@e2e-dev/kernel`. `@e2e-dev/integrations` has only been published as a canary, so no stable release is affected. - AGENTS.md documents the one-package-per-service rule and adds `@e2e-dev/integrations` to the retired names. ```diff - npm install --save-dev @e2e-dev/integrations @onkernel/sdk - import { kernel } from '@e2e-dev/integrations/kernel'; + npm install --save-dev @e2e-dev/kernel @onkernel/sdk + import { kernel } from '@e2e-dev/kernel'; ``` After the first `@e2e-dev/kernel` publish, deprecate the canary by hand: `npm deprecate @e2e-dev/integrations "moved to @e2e-dev/kernel"`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/kernel` into a scratch project in `/tmp` and installed `@onkernel/sdk@0.113.0` and `playwright`. The config uses `import { kernel } from '@e2e-dev/kernel'`. - `import('@e2e-dev/kernel')` exports `[ 'kernel' ]`. `@e2e-dev/kernel/kernel` fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. - With no API key set, `npx e2e run tests/home.e2e.ts` loads the config and reaches the provider: ``` ERROR infrastructure error ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) browser provider "kernel" could not lease a browser: KERNEL_API_KEY is not set while preparing engine web for target "kernel" ``` - Not run against a live Kernel browser: no `KERNEL_API_KEY` on this machine. Only paths and exports changed; provider code is untouched. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). title: fix(config): follow-ups to the config redesign: output data loss, engine-held secrets, migration messages, agents
body:
Fixes from a strict review and live breakage hunts on the config redesign merged in #645 and #646.

**Data loss**
- A run that stops before its tests start no longer clears `<output>/artifacts` and writes no report. That covers `NO_TESTS`, a collection error, `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT`, `NO_LAST_RUN`, an app or service that fails to start, and an interrupt. The last run's evidence and `--last-failed` survive a typo in `--grep`. A `--pass-with-no-tests` run with nothing to run still writes its report.
- The `output` and `cache.dir` checks resolve symlinks. `--output "$PWD/out"` works in a symlinked checkout, and a cache spelled through a symlink under `artifacts/` is refused instead of deleted on every run.
- `--output <existing file>` is `INVALID_CONFIG` at load.

**Secrets**
- Each session has one exposure level: `none`, `engine` (an engine option holds a secret, such as basic auth) or `filled`. One place maps that level to what is redacted or withheld.
- An engine-held secret is protected as text everywhere: reports, `screen.txt`, failure pages, text downloads, trace text, and everything the model and MCP read.
- The web engine also registers the base64 `Authorization` credential, which leaked when a page echoed the header.
- Pixels are not withheld for an engine-held secret. A page that renders the basic-auth password on screen is not masked in screenshots, and `security.mdx` says so.

**Messages that led users to the wrong fix**
- `artifacts: { kinds, trace: { record: 'retries' } }` now names `trace: 'on-all-retries'`. It used to say `'on'`, which silently traced every attempt.
- Old trace spellings at the root or on the CLI (`'retries'`, `'all'`, `{ record }`) name the mode they meant.
- The `--artifacts` hint only suggests an `--output` that is valid.
- Output errors name the default `.e2e` instead of printing `output undefined`.
- One notice covers trace and video when a retry mode meets `retries: 0`, with explore-specific wording (`pass --trace on`).
- Removed-key messages read `specVersion was removed: delete it; ...`.

**Agents**
- `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` names the agent that was selected, not `agents.default`.
- `e2e explore` fails before it starts when the explored agent has no model.
- A model used directly as an entry says to write `{ model: ... }`.
- The explore custom-executor notice names the agent key.
- A mistyped agent on a call gets a did-you-mean.
- Project tools can't take the names of the harness's own tools (`locate`, `start_recording`, `stop_recording`, `report_finding`, `complete_step`), which were silently dropped before.
- The config digest identifies tools, executors and `cache.store` instead of JSON-cloning them. A recursive zod schema or a circular store no longer crashes config load.

**Docs:** the bug-bash skill and doc use `--output`, and the JSDoc says `judgmentTimeout`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI in `apps/testbed`:
  - `--output "$PWD/out" --grep typo` exits with `NO_TESTS` and leaves the previous output untouched.
  - `--trace retries` names `on-all-retries`.
  - `--artifacts artifacts` suggests `--output .e2e`.
  - `--output <file>` is refused at load.
- Regression tests fail on the old source for the stopped-run, symlink, output and secrets fixes and the digest crash.
- `engine-secrets.test.ts` echoes the `Authorization` header and checks the base64 never appears as text in the report, `screen.txt`, failure pages, trace entries, the download, model prompts or MCP observe output.

title: fix(secrets): redact base64-encoded secrets in traces
body:
- With `web({ basicAuth: { username, password: secrets.get('BASIC_PW') } })`, trace redaction rewrote the `context-options` httpCredentials entry, but every request after the 401 challenge carried `Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)>` into `trace.network` untouched. report.json still labelled the trace `redaction: "complete"`. The MCP session trace goes through the same `redactTraceArchives`, so it leaked too.
- `redactFragments` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts`, used only by trace redaction) now decodes each base64 or base64url run (`[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{8,}={0,2}`). A run whose decoded text holds a value, or an 8-char fragment of one, is replaced whole by that value's `<secret:name>` marker.
- A run can open with text that is not part of the encoding, like `https://app.test/reset/<b64>`, `cookie=v2_<b64>`, or `tokenValue<b64>`. To catch those, each run is decoded from all 4 offsets a base64 group can start at. A `<secret:name>` marker that the decoded page text already contains counts as page text, not as a find. The same rule covers cookies and token segments that encode a secret.
- 5 new unit tests (`secret-ledger.test.ts`, `trace-redaction.test.ts`) fail on main. `docs/security.mdx` updated, changeset added.

```ts
// before
{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Basic YmJ1c2VyOlMzY3JldFBhc3N3MHJkLVhZWg==" }
// after
{ "name": "Authorization", "value": "Basic <secret:BASIC_PW>" }
```

## For the reviewer

- Cost. Each base64-alphabet run is decoded 4 times, and each decode goes through the same fragment scan the plain text does. That scan is slow on the non-ASCII garbage a misaligned decode yields (`caseKey`'s per-character path). The extra cost only applies to traces of attempts or sessions that hold a secret. Measured on `redactFragments` (median of 5, range across runs, on a machine shared with other jobs):

  | input | main | this branch |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 6.9 MB snapshot text with a 3 MB base64 data URI | 0.24s | 1.4 to 1.8s |
  | 16.8 MB snapshot JSON, no data URI | 0.49s | 1.8 to 2.3s |

  Decoding only at offset 0 cost about 3x and missed prefixed tokens. A prefilter could skip garbage decodes, but it would need a second copy of the spelling rules in `valuePattern`, so I left it out.
- Over-masking. A run is replaced whole, so a data URI or token whose decoded bytes happen to share 8 characters with a secret is masked in the trace. This matches the existing plain-text fragment rule.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, scratch config (`trace: 'on'`, `basicAuth` with `secrets.get('BASIC_PW')`, local app on 4281 that sends a 401 challenge, one page load, a fetch, and a link navigation), `e2e run --config e2e.bugbash-cfg.config.ts`, then counted `Authorization` headers in the trace zip:
  `unzip -p .../attempt-0/trace/trace.zip | grep -ao 'Authorization","value":"Basic [^"]*' | sort | uniq -c`
- MCP: `e2e mcp --headless` with the same config, `open_session`, `start_recording`, `navigate /two`, `stop_recording`, `close_session`. Same count over the session's `trace.zip` and `trace-part1.zip`.
- Main was built at 65ae4a75. The main commits since then do not touch redaction. The branch was rebased onto bb51ec1f and the CLI run repeated.

title: fix: Ctrl-C, --max-failures, and e2e mcp client lifecycle
body:
Fixes from the Oct 1 bug bash: Ctrl-C, `--max-failures`, and the `e2e mcp` server's handling of a client that goes away, plus two smaller MCP bugs.

- Ctrl-C with a web test running now reports the test `interrupted` and keeps its attempt. Before, the worker exited 130 with `WORKER_EXIT` and the test was reported `skipped` with 0 attempts. Playwright's own SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers are off (`packages/web/src/browser-connection.ts`), so the runner's interrupt is the one that ends the test. Its SIGHUP handler stays: the runner does not handle a hangup, and that handler closes the browser when the terminal goes away.
- A Ctrl-C that hits workers still loading is no longer counted as a boot failure (`WORKER_INIT_FAILED`). A worker that dies of SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP before it's ready is treated as interrupted when it was alive as that first signal landed (one Ctrl-C reaches every worker at once); a replacement that dies of a signal still counts as a boot failure, so a target that keeps killing its own workers fails with `WORKER_INIT_FAILED` (`run/scheduler.ts`, `excusedSignal`). The exit signal now reaches the scheduler through `UnitRunnerEvents.onExit`.
- `--max-failures` stops a running file right away. Each `run-unit` message carries `failureLimit` (`worker/protocol.ts`), and the worker counts its own failures against it, aborting as soon as the limit is reached (`worker/session.ts`, `countFailure`). The next test in the file is skipped with `failure-limit` instead of starting before the runner's interrupt arrives.
- When the MCP client goes away, the server closes every session, stops the app commands, and exits 0. It watches stdin `end`/`error` and stdout `error` (`mcp/server.ts`). An EPIPE on `process.stdout` now reaches the server instead of crashing it, and an EPIPE on stderr (a client that captured it) is ignored so the shutdown messages cannot kill the server first (`cli/mcp.ts`).
- MCP `open_session` on a second config fails with `CONFIG_IN_USE` before that config is evaluated. The config is found and claimed first (`mcp/sessions.ts` `claimConfig`/`claimEngine`, `mcp/config.ts` `locateProjectConfig`). Before, the second config evaluated `secrets.get()` against the first session's secrets and failed with a misleading `secret "..." is not configured`.
- A failed action no longer reads as done. Its result starts with the tool, its target, and the error code, e.g. `navigate file:///etc/passwd failed: POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: file:`. Before, the result started with the success text: `Navigated to file:///etc/passwd. failed: ...`. This text is what the testing agent's model reads and what MCP returns. MCP marks these results `isError: true` and still returns the screen the action observed afterward (`agent/primitives.ts` `failureLead`, `mcp/tools.ts` `actionResult`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[client ends stdin / dies] --> S[serveMcp: stdin end, stdout EPIPE]
  S --> A[closeAll 'client disconnected']
  A --> T[teardown: attempt, engine, app commands]
  T --> X[exit 0]
```

## Review these decisions

- The agent's check for a streak of failed actions (`isFailedResult`, `agent/loop-guards.ts`) now takes the tool name. A first line that starts with a lowercase word and contains ` failed: ` counts as a failure only for built-in grammar tools. A project tool's own text such as `build failed: 2 red` is not a failure; a project tool fails only by throwing (`Tool "x" failed: ...`). MCP's `isError` is also limited to grammar tools.
- Point-verb failures keep their old start (`tap_at (x, y) failed: ...`), apart from adding the error code for e2e errors. Only the verbs that target a node, a URL, or a key changed.
- `--max-failures` is now enforced in two places. The worker stops its own file using the run's count at the moment the file was dispatched plus its own failures since then. The scheduler still stops the rest of the run. A failure on another worker between dispatch and the local limit is only counted by the scheduler, so it cannot make a worker stop early.
- The mobile engine has no equivalent Ctrl-C bug and is unchanged. agent-device installs no signal handlers in the worker, and its daemon and device tooling are spawned `detached`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. Built CLI on scratch projects (web engine, app on ports 4311-4312), a real MCP stdio client, and `mcp-two-configs.mjs` on the testbed configs. main was a worktree at the merge base.

| Case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ctrl-C to the process group mid-test (`long poll`) | `rc 130`, `errors ['WORKER_EXIT']`, `long poll skipped attempts 0` | `rc 130`, `errors []`, `long poll interrupted attempts 1`, `afterEach done` |
| Ctrl-C reaches workers still loading | `errors ['WORKER_INIT_FAILED']`, `b skipped: worker process failed to start` | `errors []`, `a` and `b` skipped: `run interrupted before execution` |
| `--max-failures 1 --workers 1`, two tests in one file | `× would run next (interrupted)`, `2 failed` | `↓ would run next [run stopped after 1 failure (--max-failures 1)]`, `1 failed \| 1 skipped` |
| MCP client closes stdin, session open | still running after 20 s, app listening | `exit 0 after 1 s`, app stopped |
| MCP client closes stdin, no session | `exit 13`, `Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await` | `exit 0` |
| MCP client killed mid-call | `exit 1`, `Error: write EPIPE`, `Unhandled 'error' event`, app orphaned | `exit 0`, `Session ... closed (client disconnected)`, app stopped |
| second session on another config | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: ... secret "BASIC_PW" is not configured` | `CONFIG_IN_USE: session ... is open on config .../e2e.bugbash-mcp.config.ts` |
| `call navigate {url: 'file:///etc/passwd'}` | `Navigated to file:///etc/passwd. failed: forbidden URL scheme: file:`, isError false | `navigate file:///etc/passwd failed: POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: file:`, isError true |
| `call tap {target: 'zzz'}` | `Tapped #zzz. failed: node #zzz is not on the current screen ...` | `tap #zzz failed: LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: node #zzz is not on the current screen ...`, isError true |

After every run, `ps` and `lsof` showed no leftover app, browser, or worker processes.

New tests, each failing on main: `interrupt-signals.test.ts` (browser open in the worker), `scheduler.test.ts` (workers killed by Ctrl-C while loading), `parallel-workers.test.ts` (`--max-failures` in the running file), `mcp-session-host.test.ts` (config claimed before it evaluates), `mcp-disconnect.test.ts` (three disconnect cases), and `mcp-server.test.ts`, `loop-guards.test.ts`, `agent-act-verbs.test.ts` (failure text and `isError`).

The failure text is part of what the model reads, so I replayed the web benchmark's agent suite from its committed recordings: `CI=1 e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` passed 32/32 with no `REPLAY_STALE` and no cache changes. The benchmark's deterministic suite passed 90/90 and the testbed 70/70.

title: fix(output): only clear and write an output directory e2e owns
body:
`output` handling from #645 could delete or overwrite files e2e does not own. It could also lose evidence and misreport `--last-failed`. This PR fixes each case, and each fix has a test that fails on main.

- **Ownership.** A run only clears or writes into an output it can tell is its own. Anything else is `INVALID_CONFIG` naming what is in the directory (`packages/e2e/src/config/output.ts`).
- **Real paths.** The output checks compare real paths: symlinks are resolved first (`realpathSync.native` on the nearest existing ancestor), and names are compared without case where the filesystem ignores it (`internal/paths.ts`). A symlink to the root or outside the project, `TESTS`, and `.E2E/CACHE` are all refused.
- **Tests globs.** An output inside a directory a tests glob scans is refused. The check uses `scansDirectory` in `internal/globs.ts`, which shares its "does discovery enter this directory" logic with `discoverFiles`. `..results` is no longer treated as outside the project; one `isWithin` now serves both the config check and `run/trace-redaction.ts`.
- **`failures/`.** It is now in the list of directories a run owns, so `cache.dir: '<output>/failures'` is refused. Before, the markdown reporter deleted the cache there.
- **NO_TESTS runs.** A run that selects nothing no longer clears `<output>/artifacts`. After such a run, `--last-failed` names how that run ended instead of claiming "no failures" (`collect/select.ts`, `run/last-run.ts`).
- **Live `e2e mcp` sessions.** An `e2e run` no longer deletes a live session's trace. The clear keeps `artifacts/<target>/sessions/<attempt>/` while the attempt's UUIDv7, minted once the app is up, is younger than the session TTL plus its grace and an hour for launch and close (5 h 1 min). It removes older ones and never follows a symlink (`clearArtifacts` in `run/output.ts`).
- **`e2e list --output <dir>`.** Lets `list --last-failed` read the report that `run --output <dir>` wrote.

## For the reviewer to decide

- **Ownership rule.** An existing output is e2e's when it is any of these:
  - a directory that does not exist yet;
  - the default `.e2e`, owned by name whatever older versions left there (also when spelled `.E2E` or reached through a symlink);
  - a directory holding the `.e2e-output` marker;
  - a directory whose `report.json` is a `report-1` document;
  - a directory that is empty but for `cache.dir` (the fresh-clone case of a committed cache).

  File names alone are not trusted: a directory holding only an `artifacts/` e2e did not write is refused, since the run would delete it.

  `claimOutput` writes the marker before the first write of a run or a session into any output other than `.e2e`. `.e2e` gets no marker, so existing `.gitignore` entries stay complete. The `report.json` fallback keeps outputs written before the marker existed working, custom reporter files included. The marker is hidden, and a refusal message names it.
- **Refusing an output inside a tests-glob directory.** This is new. `output: 'results'` with `tests: '**/*.e2e.ts'` passed before and is now refused unless tests has `'!results/**'` or the output is a dot directory. The message names the exclusion. I changed the test from #645 that accepted it.
- **MCP session artifacts stay under `artifacts/<target>/sessions/`.** An earlier version of this branch moved them to `<output>/mcp/`. The fresh-context review caught that nothing would ever clean that directory and that older `.gitignore`s do not cover it, so the age-based skip replaced it. Session artifacts are still cleaned, by the first run after about 5 h.
- **A NO_TESTS run still writes `report.json`.** Hosts and CI get a report for every run. As a result, `--last-failed` right after a `--grep` typo has nothing to rerun, and it now says so: `which ran no tests (it ended error: NO_TESTS)`. Not writing the report would change what a run always produces, so I left that for you.
- **`apps/testbed/scripts/explore-bench.mjs`** now writes its `cli.log` beside the output directory (`.e2e/explore-bench/<label>.log`). Writing it inside the output before the run made the output a directory e2e does not own.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Rerun after rebasing onto `origin/main` at 77940082 (#663, #664, #666, #671, #672), against a fresh build of that commit.

- Built CLI from `apps/testbed` with a scratch config on port 4301: `e2e run` / `e2e list` with each bad `--output`.
- `e2e mcp` over stdio (port 4302) with a concurrent `e2e run` on port 4303 against the same output. The client then ends stdin without `close_session` (the #664 disconnect path), and a second `e2e run` follows.
- Main is the `origin/main` build. The extra cases were checked through `resolveConfig` in a scratch project: `src/app.ts`, `tests/`, `.e2e/cache/`.

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output bb-root-link` (symlink to `.`) | `Report bb-root-link/report.json`, `artifacts/user-file.txt` deleted | `--output "bb-root-link" is the project root`, file kept |
| `--output out-link` (symlink to `/tmp/...`) | `/tmp/e2e-fix-elsewhere/artifacts/keep.txt` deleted | `is outside the project root`, file kept |
| `--output TESTS-OSKAR` (macOS) | `tests-oskar/artifacts/keep.txt` deleted, report written into the tests dir | `holds tests-oskar, where the tests glob ... finds test files` |
| `--output app` | `app/artifacts/keep.txt` deleted, `app/report.json` written | `holds bug-garden.mjs, layout.mjs, pages and 1 more, which e2e did not write; ... create .e2e-output in it if the directory is e2e's` |
| `--output src` | accepted | `holds app.ts, which e2e did not write` |
| `cache.dir: '.e2e-oskar-c/failures'` | cache entry deleted by the markdown reporter | `would hold cache.dir .e2e-oskar-c/failures under failures/` |
| `--output .E2E/CACHE` (macOS) | accepted | `is the cache directory .e2e/cache or inside it` |
| `--output ..results` | `is outside the project root` | accepted, written with `.e2e-output` |
| `--output foreign` holding only `artifacts/build.zip` | accepted, `build.zip` would be deleted | `holds artifacts and neither .e2e-output nor a report e2e wrote` |
| `--output tests/results` | accepted | `is scanned by the tests glob "tests/**/*.e2e.ts" ... or add '!tests/results/**' to tests` |
| `run --grep typo` after a failing run | `artifacts/` wiped | `artifacts/web/...` kept |
| then `run --last-failed` | `2 did not fail in the last run, which had no failures` | `2 did not fail in the last run, which ran no tests (it ended error: NO_TESTS)` |
| `e2e run` during a live `e2e mcp` session | a file in `artifacts/web/sessions/<id>/trace/` deleted | kept |
| client disconnects, then `e2e run` | `trace.zip` saved at close, then deleted by the run | `trace.zip` saved at close and kept |
| `list --last-failed --output .e2e-oskar-c` | `error: unknown option '--output'` | `tests-oskar/a.e2e.ts › oskar fails [web]` |

The default `.e2e` still works with older content in it (`.e2e/bugbash/s1/notes.txt`), and it gets no marker. The testbed default suite (70 passed, 1 skipped), the web benchmark suite (90 passed), `pnpm test`, and the `@e2e-dev/eas` unit tests pass on the rebased branch. `@e2e-dev/eas` writes nothing under the output; the mobile CI's `--output .e2e/agent` is accepted.

title: fix(agent): resend a stalled model request; keep turns of a timed-out step
body:
One model request that never answered held an `agent.act` step until the step's own timeout. Found in a live `e2e explore` run on the testbed bug garden (`apps/testbed/scripts/explore-bench.mjs`): step 1 "Browse the catalog" ended `STEP_TIMEOUT` at 240 s, but the `--debug` step table added up to 23 s of work (model 19.4 s, observe 3.2 s, action 0.7 s). The Playwright trace showed the page idle for 220.4 s after the last observation. One provider request stalled, and the only bound on it was the step clock (`timeout: remainingMs()` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/tool-loop.ts`).

- `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/stall.ts`: `withStallGuard` wraps the model with the SDK's `wrapLanguageModel`. Each `doGenerate` gets a 120 s bound (`MODEL_CALL_STALL_MS`). When the bound fires, the request is aborted (and abandoned if the provider ignores the abort) and fails with a retryable `APICallError`, and the SDK's transport retries (`TRANSPORT_RETRIES = 5`, with backoff) send it again. A cancellation from the caller (step clock, run abort) passes through unchanged.
- The tool loop and the judgment adapter (`model/sdk.ts`) both send requests through the guard. The tool loop also notes each resend on the turn before it: `[loop] turn 2 got no response in 120s: sending it again`.
- A step the clock ended used to lose all its turns. `act.ts` races the step against its deadline and settles without waiting for the executor, but the loop only attached its turns when it returned. Turns are now attached as each turn ends and after each note, so a `STEP_TIMEOUT` step keeps them in `report.json` and in the `--debug` transcript.
- Loop notes now live in a separate field on the loop's own turn record. The report clips the outcome (600 chars) and the notes (1000 chars) separately, so a note appended after long tool results is no longer cut off. Tool output that happens to start with `[loop] ` is still clipped like any other output.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant L as tool loop
  participant G as stall guard
  participant P as provider
  L->>G: doGenerate (turn 2)
  G->>P: request
  Note over G,P: no answer in 120 s
  G-->>L: APICallError (isRetryable)
  Note over L: [loop] turn 2 got no response in 120s: sending it again
  L->>G: SDK transport retry (backoff)
  G->>P: request
  P-->>L: tool calls
```

## Design decisions to review

- **Why 120 s.** luna-fast's slowest call in the explore run was 6.7 s, and slow reasoning turns on big screens can take tens of seconds. The explore step budget is 240 s, so 120 s still leaves room for one full resend inside a step.
- **The bound covers the whole request, not time to first byte.** `doGenerate` does not stream, so a healthy request that needs more than 120 s for one answer (a slow local model on a large screen) is also cut off and sent again. After the retries run out it fails `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. `docs/reference/errors.mdx`, `docs/debugging.mdx`, and the changeset say so. A true idle-stream bound would mean moving the loop to `doStream`, which is a larger change.
- **Why a retryable `APICallError` instead of our own resend.** The SDK's retry keeps the loop state, reuses its backoff and the existing retry budget, and still stops at the caller's step timeout. A second retry path in the loop would duplicate all of that.
- **Not configurable yet.** The config shape is locked for this release. If a knob is needed, it can go on the agents entry after the release.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **Stall repro on the testbed** (`e2e run --config e2e.stall.config.ts`, a scratch config not committed). It wraps `gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast')` in a middleware that holds the 2nd request until aborted, then runs one `agent.act('open the Todos page and add a todo named "Stall check"')`.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| result | `TEST_TIMEOUT` at 240.15 s | passed in 129.27 s |
| model calls | 1 | 4 (1 stalled, resent after 120 s) |
| turns in `report.json` | 0 | 4, turn 1 carries the note |

main:
```text
   × a stalled model call is sent again > agent.act "open the Todos page and add a todo named "Stall check"" 239.96s · 1 model call failed
 ❯ |web| tests-stall/stall.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 failed) 240.15s ai 3.9k tokens · 97% cached · $0.0001
   × a stalled model call is sent again (timed-out) 240.15s ai 3.9k tokens · 97% cached · $0.0001
     → test timed out after 240000 ms in phase body
```

this branch:
```text

 ✓ |web| tests-stall/stall.e2e.ts (1 test) 129.27s ai 17.6k tokens · 97% cached · $0.0005

report.json turns (index, calls, loop notes):
[1,["tap({\"target\":\"n4\"})"],["[loop] turn 2 got no response in 120s: sending it again"]]
[2,["type({\"target\":\"n6027\",\"value\":\"Stall check\"})"],[]]
[3,["tap({\"target\":\"n6028\"})"],[]]
[4,["complete_step({\"status\":\"passed\",\"summary\":\"Opened Todos and added the todo “Stall check”; ...\"})"],[]]
```

- **Original bug, explore on the bug garden (main build).** The 240 s step spent 23 s working:

