```text
        agent.act exceeded its 240000 ms timeout
  step                                                               total   model  observe  action  calls
  agent.act "Open Catalog and inspect the listed books, including…  240.0s   19.4s   3180ms   688ms      9
```

- **No regression in the agent loop:**
  - testbed agent suite live (`--config e2e.agent.config.ts --no-cache`): 24/24 passed, 124 model calls. main was also 24/24.
  - web-benchmark agent replay (`CI=1 ... --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache`): 32/32 passed, no `REPLAY_STALE`.
- **Unit tests** in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/tool-loop-stall.test.ts`:
  - covered: the guard alone, a provider that ignores the abort or throws synchronously, a stalled turn resent with its note, a stalled judgment resent, turns kept on a step timeout, notes kept after the clip, and tool output that looks like a note still clipped.
  - fail on main: the step-timeout-keeps-turns and loop-note tests.
  - fail if the loop or the adapter stops routing through the guard: the loop and judgment wiring tests.

title: feat(mobile): declare command, readyUrl and services on the device engine
body: ## What and why - `mobile()` takes `command`, `readyUrl`, and `services`, the app process declaration `web()` already has. The runner starts Metro (or any dev server a development build loads from) and the app's backend services before the first test and stops them on every exit path; targets that declare the same command share one process, so iOS and Android start Metro once. - A device has no URL to poll, so `readyUrl` is required beside `command`; core already reports `INVALID_CONFIG` for a command without one. `services` without `command` stays valid: a release build embeds its JavaScript and needs only its backend. - Until now a device suite that needed these rebuilt the handle through `defineEngine` to splice them in (Bluesky's `__e2e__/fixtures/engine.ts`); that shim goes away with this. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run test:unit` (229 tests), package typecheck, `oxlint`, `docs:check`. - New unit test asserts the declaration with command plus services, services alone, and that undeclared values stay out of `engine.app`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ---

title: fix(agent): extract stops inventing data, clearer unchanged-screen feedback, stable committed recordings
body:
Four bug-bash fixes in the agent loop, the judgment tier, and the replay cache. One commit each.

- **`agent.extract` invented values.** The caller's zod schema went to the provider with its constraints, so `count: z.number().min(100)` on a page with 3 todos came back as 300 or 30366, and an absent phone came back `""`. Now the model gets only the shape (types, fields, required, items, enum/const; `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/schema.ts:63`) inside an `agent-extract-2` envelope `{ found, value, missing }` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/protocol.ts:89`). `found: false` fails the step with `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` naming what was missing (`packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts:217`). The caller's schema still judges the value, and the repair round may decline instead of bending a value to fit. The prompt no longer says the schema is hidden. Owner accepted the behavior change: a test that relied on `""` or `0` for absent data now fails with the existing `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` (no new code); asking for absence (`'the phone, or null when none is shown'` with `.nullable()`) returns `null`. `agent-extract-1` was an undocumented wire name (test helpers only), bumped to `agent-extract-2`.
- **Read-write runs rewrote committed recordings.** `flowOf` compared `actions[].derived`, which follows how the agent read a typed value that run (pixels vs a node) and never changes what a replay does (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts:95`).
- **Tree-only "no visible effect".** An action that left the tree unchanged told the agent the control had no visible effect even with no screenshot to compare, so on a PIN pad of drawn dots it abandoned working taps. That line now needs an identical screenshot; otherwise the result says no listed node changed and that a drawn change needs a screenshot. When the step can get no screenshot (a secret was filled, or the engine captures none) it still says to try another way (`packages/e2e/src/agent/screen-update.ts:323`). The act system rule defers to that wording (`packages/e2e/src/agent/default-agent.ts:36`).
- **`REPLAY_STALE` advice was hardcoded** to `--strict-cache` and `.e2e/cache`. It now names the knob that turned strict on (flag, `cache.strict`, or both) and the configured cache dir or `cache.store` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts:206`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[caller schema] --> P[shape only] --> E["envelope {found, value, missing}"] --> M[model]
  M -->|found: false| I[ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE + missing]
  M -->|found: true| V{caller validate}
  V -->|ok| R[value]
  V -->|issues| Rp[one repair round, may decline] --> M
```

Not in this PR: an earlier revision reported a tab the app opened to the agent through a new `EngineSnapshot.notices` field. That stopgap is dropped at the owner's call; a tab the app opens stays invisible (`docs/reference/agent.mdx`) until proper tab support lands.

## Decisions to review

- **Value rules are stripped for internal callers too.** The explore planner's `max(8000)` fields are now enforced by validation only, so a runaway field runs to the judgment output ceiling before the repair round. Keeping `maxLength` in the shape would let a provider truncate a real value to fit, the same bug class as `min(100)`.
- **Out of scope:** an optional field in the caller's schema is left out of `required` in the shape, which OpenAI strict structured output rejects. Unchanged from before.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on the branch rebased onto main after #663, #664, #666, #670, #671, #672, #662, and #678; the extract and strict-cache runs below were repeated after an earlier rebase; the gate and the strict-cache replay were rerun on this one with the same results. Real CLI, `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` through the gateway, `--no-cache`.

`agent.extract` on the testbed todos page with 3 todos (branch: same result in 3 runs):

| call | main | this branch |

title: fix(web,kernel): Kernel downloads, crashed-worker leaks, icon-font names, and clearer attempt-scope limits
body: Six web engine and Kernel bugs from the Oct 1 bug bash, one commit each. - **`web.waitForDownload` on Kernel.** It always failed with `download.saveAs: canceled`, because a remote Chromium saves the file on its own disk. `BrowserProvider` gets an optional `downloads: { dir, read }`. Before the download, the engine tells the browser to save the page's context downloads into `dir` on its machine (`Browser.setDownloadBehavior`), then reads the finished file back through `read` (`packages/web/src/downloads.ts`). `kernel()` (`@e2e-dev/kernel`) implements `read` with `client.browsers.fs.readFile`. A provider without the hook fails with an `ENGINE_FAILURE` that names the provider and the missing `downloads`. `downloads.dir` must be an absolute path in the POSIX or Windows form, else `INVALID_CONFIG` when the config loads. - **Icon fonts.** `` showed as `button "Login"` on screen, but `getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })` found nothing, because Playwright's name includes the `::before` glyph. The reader now includes `::before`/`::after` text in names, as accname, Chrome, and Playwright do, and turns each private-use-area glyph into a space in the name it reports. A role query with a string name matches the browser's name with those glyphs allowed where the name has a space or begins or ends (`packages/web/src/locators.ts:84`). Label text still leaves out generated content, as `getByLabel` does. - **Leaked browsers after a worker crash.** A worker killed in `kernel({ scope: 'attempt' })` left its browser running until Kernel's `timeout_seconds`. `BrowserProvider` gets an optional `sweep(context)`, which `finish` calls once per target after releasing the leases it holds (`packages/web/src/provider.ts:396`). `kernel()` deletes every browser still active with the run's `e2e_run` and `e2e_target` tags. Core still knows nothing about browsers. - **Kernel live-view line.** Leases acquired in a worker (attempt scope, and replacements) used a log that threw lines away. They now log through the worker's `init` log, so `watch at ` reaches the reporter. - **Clear errors for persistent-context limits.** In attempt scope, `app.clearState()` now names the mode it is running in instead of saying `engine web does not implement it`. A session consumed on a target whose engine has no state capability now fails selection with `COLLECTION_ERROR`, before the setup test logs in (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`). - **Kernel error text.** The trailing newline on SDK error messages (`401 Invalid or disabled API key\n`) is trimmed. The docs now list `userAgent` among what attempt scope rules out. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[prepare: lease worker-scope browsers] --> W[workers: attempt leases, replacements] W -- worker exits normally --> R[worker releases its own leases] W -- worker is killed --> X[its leases stay open] R --> F[finish: release the prepare leases] X --> F F --> S[provider.sweep: release what is still open for this run and target] ``` ```ts export interface BrowserProvider { // ...name, scope, acquire, release, record as before readonly downloads?: { readonly dir: string; read(lease, file, context): Promise }; sweep?(context: BrowserReleaseContext): Promise; } ``` ## Decisions to review - **Glyph names.** Glyphs count as content while a name is computed, as they do for the browser. They become spaces only in the name the tree reports. A control whose only content is a glyph (``) still reads as its `title`, as it did on main, so the agent can tell a toolbar's buttons apart. But the browser names that control by the glyph, so `getByRole` by the title still finds nothing. That is a known limit, listed with its reason in `tests/crosscheck/expected.txt`. I tried matching it by title too (`getByRole(...).or(... .and(getByTitle(...)))`), but that dropped matches inside closed shadow roots. A `RegExp` name is matched against the browser's name, glyph included. Documented in `docs/browser.mdx`, "Icon fonts and generated content". - **Reliance on a Playwright internal.** The engine finds the file on the remote disk by the basename of `download.path()`. That relies on Playwright naming its local file after the CDP download GUID, which is also the name the browser gives the file under `allowAndName`. That is a Playwright internal. `tests/integration/provider-downloads.test.ts` catches it against a real Chrome if it changes. - **Sweep behaviour.** The sweep is a backstop: when it fails, the reporter gets one line and the run does not fail, since Kernel's `timeout_seconds` still ends the browser. `kernel()` tries every delete and names both the deleted and the failed ones. The sweep is skipped when `prepare` failed and no worker started. It costs one Kernel list call per target per run. - **The plan-time session check applies to every engine.** It lives in core selection and uses only the generic `state` capability, so it applies to mobile and third-party engines too. It cannot name attempt scope in its message (it says `engine web, as configured, has no state capability`). Naming the cause would need a new engine contract field. The mobile engine declares no `state` with any device provider, EAS included, so a session consumer there already failed at runtime (restore and `session.save()` both raise `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`); it now fails at plan time instead. - **The reset hook is always present in attempt scope.** The web engine now always declares `session.reset` (what backs `app.clearState()`), and in attempt scope and with `connect.reconnectEndpoint` it rejects with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` naming the mode. Before, the member was left out, and core produced the generic message. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Rebased onto main at 77940082 (after #663, #664, #666, #671) with no conflicts. Main changed none of the kernel, provider, or selection files, so the live Kernel rows below stand as run. Re-ran after the rebase: `pnpm check`, the web and kernel suites (cross-check and conformance with them), `select.test.ts`, `engine-contract.test.ts`, `interrupt-signals.test.ts`, `parallel-workers.test.ts`, the testbed default suite, the web benchmark suite, and the cross-check against every web-benchmark scenario. This PR adds no launch path, so #664's `handleSIGINT`/`handleSIGTERM: false` still covers every local browser (the Kernel path is `connectOverCDP`, which starts no process). - Every pinning test fails on main and passes here: `tests/integration/provider-downloads.test.ts`, `tests/integration/icon-glyph-names.test.ts`, the new `generated content` cross-check fixture page, and new cases in `tests/unit/browser-provider.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cdp-connect.test.ts`, `packages/kernel/tests/unit/kernel.test.ts`, `packages/e2e/tests/unit/select.test.ts`, and `packages/e2e/tests/integration/engine-contract.test.ts`. - The cross-check `expected.txt` is unchanged from main: the new fixture page agrees with Chrome and Playwright on every node. The conformance expectations are unchanged too. - Live Kernel runs (hosted Chromium against the-internet.herokuapp.com), with main's and this branch's packages packed into scratch projects: | Scenario | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `web.waitForDownload`, worker scope | `ENGINE_FAILURE: download failed: download.saveAs: canceled` | `✓ download a file`, `downloads/001-test.txt` holds `Test file` | | `web.waitForDownload`, attempt scope | same failure | `✓ download a file` | | `getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })` on `/login` | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator matched no nodes within getByRole("button", name: "Login")` (the screen reads `button "Login"`) | `✓ font awesome login button by its name` | | worker SIGKILLed in attempt scope, then a leak check | `LEAK CHECK: active=1` (the attempt's browser, until timeout) | `ℹ kernel: released 1 browser(s) a worker left open: `, `LEAK CHECK: active=0` | | attempt-scope live view | no `watch at` line | `ℹ kernel worker 0: kernel: browser , watch at ` | | `app.clearState()` in attempt scope | `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: target "kernel" has no engine capability for app state reset: engine web does not implement it` | `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: app.clearState() is unavailable with browser provider "kernel" with scope "attempt": it replaces the browser context, and the attempt rides one persistent context; every attempt already starts on a fresh browser, and scope "worker" can clear one mid-test` | | `test.setup` + `session.save()` in attempt scope | the login runs for 20s, then `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: ... no engine state capability for session.save()` | `COLLECTION_ERROR: setup test ... saves session "tom" for a selected test, but target "kernel" cannot save or restore a session: engine web, as configured, has no state capability`, no browser leased | | bad `KERNEL_API_KEY` | `... could not lease a browser: 401 Invalid or disabled API key` then, on its own line, ` while preparing engine web ...` | one line: `... 401 Invalid or disabled API key while preparing engine web for target "kernel"` | - Worker scope with a SIGKILLed worker still releases its browser (`ℹ kernel: released 1 browser(s)`). Every browser these runs created is deleted (`LEAK CHECK: active=0`). - The testbed default suite and the web benchmark suite pass on this branch, and so does the cross-check against every web-benchmark scenario (`CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL`). - Reading `::before`/`::after` costs two more `getComputedStyle` calls per element on the name walk, cached once per element per read. `pnpm bench:ab` on the web benchmark (4 pairs) reports no change: every test ran the same steps with the same outcome, and every counter matched. | Metric | main | this PR | change (95% CI) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | suite (sum of attempts) | 109.11 s | 109.40 s | +0.5% (-1.8% to +1.2%), same | | wall | 110.45 s | 111.03 s | +0.7% (-1.9% to +1.9%), same | A direct reader measurement (an 800-row table plus a 300-item list, median of 10 reads, three alternating runs, machine under load) gave 916 to 1081 ms on this branch against 862 to 1110 ms on main.

title: fix(config): refuse silent config mistakes: secret references as strings, nested unknown keys, directory globs
body: Config mistakes that used to pass silently now fail at load, naming the fix. - **Bug-bash fan-out guard.** #653 switched the bug-bash guide and skill from the removed `--artifacts` to `--output`. Before that, every charter exited 2 into its log and the bash found nothing. `skill.test.ts` now fails any skill or docs paragraph that uses `--artifacts` without saying it is gone. The fan-out run below uses the guide's loop as it now stands. - **`secrets.get()` in config.** A handle read as a string became `[object Object]`, in `command.env` or in text such as `context: 'key ' + secrets.get('K')`. Now the config-time handle throws `INVALID_CONFIG` when turned into a string (`toString`, `toJSON`, `Symbol.toPrimitive`: `packages/e2e/src/secrets.ts`), and `validateCommand` requires `args` and `env` values to be strings (`packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts`). An `undefined` env value (`process.env.KEY` unset) is dropped, as `spawn` drops it. The config digest no longer JSON-clones `targets`, which it overwrites anyway, so an engine that holds a handle still digests the same. - **`createAgent` import.** It now gets a migration hint in `REMOVED_EXPORTS['e2e/agent']` (`packages/e2e/src/config/diagnose.ts`). It was the one runtime export #645/#646 removed without one. - **Unknown keys below the top level.** They are rejected through one helper, `rejectUnknownKeys` / `unknownKeyMessage` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/options.ts`. It names the nearest key when one is a plausible typo, and every known key otherwise: - `web()` options, plus the keys of `connect` and `basicAuth` - `mobile()` options, plus the permission names in `mobile({ permissions })` (a state other than `grant`, `deny`, or `reset` fails too) - the same permissions map in `device.openApp(app, { permissions })`, at test time with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, before any device command - `easSimulators()` options (`@e2e-dev/eas`, #671), whose two other option refusals are now `INVALID_CONFIG` as well instead of `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED` - command, service, and teardown keys - test, setup, and describe options (`COLLECTION_ERROR`) - `getBy*` query options (`INVALID_LOCATOR`, through the existing `rejectUnknownOptions` the locator verbs use) Each key list is written as `satisfies Record` (`Record` for the permission names), so the compiler keeps it equal to the type. It caught #671's new `videoTouches` on this rebase. `kernel()` is left alone: it passes Kernel's create body through. `easSimulators()` is checked: its options are its own, renamed onto EAS's create input (`device` is `deviceIdentifier`, `maxDurationMinutes` is `maxRunTimeMinutes`), not a passed-through body, so a misspelled `buildID` was dropped and the session started without the build. - **Directory entries in `tests`.** A `tests` entry with no wildcard that names a directory is `INVALID_GLOB` (the code a trailing `/` already gets), naming the glob to write. For example, `'!tests/wip'` excluded nothing; write `'!tests/wip/**'`. A positional that names a file a `!` entry excludes, by path (in its on-disk casing) or by name, is now `NO_TESTS` naming that entry, not "did you mean ", including when the exclusions leave nothing discovered. - **Error codes at evaluation.** A `ConfigurationError` thrown while the config evaluates keeps its own code (`packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`): `web({ video })` is `INVALID_CONFIG`, as `reference/web.mdx` says. A failed import is still `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`. ## Decisions to review - New public export: `rejectUnknownKeys(label, value, keys, code?)` from `e2e/engine`, so the web and mobile engines and `@e2e-dev/eas` run the same check as core. `code` defaults to `INVALID_CONFIG`; `'INVALID_ARGUMENT'` throws a test error, for an object a test passes to a fixture method. It is documented in `reference/engine.mdx`. - `@e2e-dev/eas` gains `e2e` as a peer (`>=0.15.0 <1`, as `@e2e-dev/kernel` has), to import that check from `e2e/engine`. It already needed `e2e` through `@e2e-dev/mobile`. - `device.setPermission(name, state)` is not checked here; its name reaches agent-device as before. - Only the config-time handle, created before any run exists, throws when turned into a string. A handle inside a running test (`fill(\`${secrets.get('x')}\`)`) still stringifies to `[object Object]`. Refusing that would take a test-time error code instead of `INVALID_CONFIG`, so it is left as a follow-up. - Errors raised while the config evaluates now surface with their own code, not `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`. That covers `web()` and `mobile()` refusals (`INVALID_CONFIG`) and a config-time `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`. Their messages lose the `failed to load config :` prefix. - Stricter checks that can break configs that loaded before: - an including `tests` entry that is a bare directory - `test.describe(title, { only: true })` (the docs already said groups do not take `only`) - a non-plain-object options argument to `getBy*` - misspelled keys that used to be dropped, including permission names and `easSimulators()` options - a non-string `env` value such as `PORT: 3000`, which `spawn` used to stringify (`undefined` is still dropped) - `test.setup` options are checked against `SetupOptions`, so `skip`, `only`, and `session` on a setup, which the type never allowed and which were silently accepted, are now `COLLECTION_ERROR`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. After rebasing on `origin/main` at 77940082 (#663, #664, #666, #671, #672; the head is now on 630c9879, which adds the docs-only #674), I re-ran every load- and collect-time row below (`comand`, `arg`, `env`, `context`, `createAgent`, `timout`, the `!` directory entry, `video`, and the new permission and eas rows) with `e2e list` on fresh builds of both; each matched. The run-time rows (`getByRole`, the excluded positional, the two passing configs, the fan-out) are from before the rebase. I used the built CLI from `apps/testbed` with scratch configs on ports 4321-4327, comparing a clean `origin/main` build with this branch. I also ran the bug-bash guide's fan-out loop, with the old `--artifacts` line and the current `--output` line (the testbed's explore config, without `--video`), against the bug garden with a real model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, two charters). | Case | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Bug-bash fan-out: old `--artifacts` line vs the guide's current `--output` line | `cart exit=2` `search exit=2`: `--artifacts was removed; write --output .e2e/bugbash/cart instead` | `cart exit=1` (7 findings, 30 model calls, $0.0167), `search exit=1` (3 findings); `report.json`, `summary.md`, `artifacts/` under `.e2e/bugbash//` | | `env: { API_KEY: secrets.get('API_KEY') }` | app receives `API_KEY=[object Object]`, run passes | `INVALID_CONFIG: ... app.command.env.API_KEY must be a string, got secrets.get("API_KEY"): only an engine option that declares secrets accepts a handle ...` | | `context: 'The API key is ' + secrets.get('API_KEY')` | loads; context holds `[object Object]` | `INVALID_CONFIG: secrets.get("API_KEY") is a reference to a secret, not its value ...` | | `basicAuth: { password: secrets.get('pw') }` | passes | passes (1/1) | | `env: { UNSET_KEY: process.env.FIXCFG_UNSET }` (unset) | passes | passes (1/1) | | `import { createAgent } from 'e2e/agent'` | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: ... does not provide an export named 'createAgent'` | same, plus `; createAgent was removed from e2e/agent: write its options as the agents entry itself: agents: { default: { model, system, tools } }` | | `web({ url, comand: {...} })` | `APP_UNREACHABLE: nothing answered at http://127.0.0.1:4324/` | `INVALID_CONFIG: web() has unknown key "comand"; did you mean "command"?` | | `command: { executable, arg: [...] }` | `APP_UNREACHABLE` | `INVALID_CONFIG: ... app.command has unknown key "arg"; did you mean "args"?` | | `test('x', { timout: 1000 }, ...)` | option ignored | `COLLECTION_ERROR: ... test options has unknown key "timout"; did you mean "timeout"?` | | `getByRole('link', { nam: 'Home' })` | `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS: locator matched 22 nodes` | `INVALID_LOCATOR: getByRole options has no key "nam"; it takes name, exact, visible, ...` | | `tests: [..., '!tests-fixcfg-glob/wip']` | `wip/w.e2e.ts` still listed | `INVALID_GLOB: tests entry "!tests-fixcfg-glob/wip" names a directory ...; write "!tests-fixcfg-glob/wip/**" ...` | | `e2e run ` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched .../wip/w.e2e.ts (did you mean tests-fixcfg-glob/keep.e2e.ts?)` | `NO_TESTS: no test file matched .../wip/w.e2e.ts (excluded by the tests entry "!tests-fixcfg-glob/wip/**")` | | `mobile({ permissions: { camerra: 'grant' } })` | loads | `INVALID_CONFIG: mobile({ permissions }) has unknown key "camerra"; did you mean "camera"?` | | `mobile({ permissions: { camera: 'granted' } })` | loads | `INVALID_CONFIG: mobile({ permissions }).camera must be one of grant, deny, reset, got "granted"` | | `easSimulators({ projectId, buildID: 'b1' })` | loads, `buildID` dropped | `INVALID_CONFIG: easSimulators() has unknown key "buildID"; did you mean "buildId"?` | | `easSimulators({ projectId, buildId, applicationArchiveUrl })` | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: failed to load config ...: easSimulators: pass ... not both` | `INVALID_CONFIG: easSimulators: pass ... not both` | | `web({ url, video: {} })` | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: failed to load config ...: web({ video }) was renamed ...` | `INVALID_CONFIG: web({ video }) was renamed web({ screencast }) ...` | The eas and permission rows ran `e2e list` from `apps/mobile-benchmark` on both builds. The docs' `easSimulators` config from `integrations/eas.mdx` (with `videoTouches: false` and an unset `EAS_BUILD_ID`) and a valid permissions map list all 53 tests on both. `device.openApp(app, { permissions })` is covered by a unit test on the fake client (no device command sent), not on a simulator. Also passing: every config in `apps/testbed`, `apps/web-benchmark`, and `apps/mobile-benchmark` still loads under `e2e list` (#671 and #672 added none). Two list with exit 2 after the load, the same on main: `e2e.capture.config.ts`, whose test resolves the old `@e2edev/mobile` name, and `e2e.explore.config.ts`, whose `tests-explore/` glob matches nothing. The testbed default suite passes after the rebase (70 passed, 1 skipped), and so does `pnpm test`. Both web-benchmark suites passed before the rebase (90 of 90 locator tests, and the agentic suite, 32 of 32, with `--strict-cache`); CI runs them on this head. A finding from the real bug-bash run, the planted "Recieve" typo: ![bug-bash finding](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c3cd675-e1b6-4e98-b4cd-41ae7a9a5d57) ---

title: feat(eas): @e2e-dev/eas, EAS Simulators for the mobile engine
body: ## What and why - New package `@e2e-dev/eas`: `easSimulators()`, a `DeviceProvider` that runs mobile targets on [EAS Simulators](https://expo.dev/services/simulators). One hosted iOS simulator or Android emulator per worker slot, driven through the agent-device daemon EAS runs beside it. It follows the per-service layout of `@e2e-dev/kernel` (#659). - It talks to Expo's GraphQL API with `fetch`, the same API `eas simulator:*` uses, so there is no SDK to install and `@e2e-dev/mobile` is the only peer. `EXPO_TOKEN` is read from the run's environment. - `buildId` or `applicationArchiveUrl` has EAS install the app. Without either, `device.installApp()` uploads a local build through the daemon. - Session lifecycle. The provider: - names and tags each session with the run, target, and slot; - pins the daemon to the agent-device version the engine pins, where EAS would otherwise run the latest; - defaults `maxIdleTimeMinutes` to 10 as the backstop for a dead run; - stops a session that errors, is cancelled, or is still booting after 15 minutes; - cancels the queued job of any session it stops (EAS otherwise starts that job later and it holds the concurrency slot); - fails fast when a session is still queued while another session of the run idles toward EAS's idle stop. - `@e2e-dev/mobile` changes, needed for video on hosted daemons: - `videoTouches: false` records without agent-device's touch indicator. On EAS iOS, drawing the indicator took about 2 minutes per recording and failed anyway, so every recorded attempt timed out. - Video now records with device scope. The app scope refused to start with no app open, which happens after `closeApp()` or before a fixture installs the build. When a stop reports that it ended the record-only session, the engine treats the session as closed. - `DeviceRequest.agentDeviceVersion` passes the engine's pinned agent-device to providers. ```ts import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile'; import { easSimulators } from '@e2e-dev/eas'; mobile({ platform: 'ios', app: 'com.example.app', device: easSimulators({ projectId: '', buildId: process.env.EAS_BUILD_ID }), videoTouches: false, }); ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as runner (prepare) participant P as easSimulators participant E as api.expo.dev participant W as worker R->>P: acquire(slot) P->>E: createDeviceRunSession (agent-device, buildId, packageVersion) loop every 5s P->>E: byId: status, turtleJobRun, remoteConfig end P-->>R: lease { daemon: url + token } W->>E: agent-device RPC through the session daemon R->>P: release P->>E: ensureDeviceRunSessionStopped (+ cancelJobRun if still queued) ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. I ran the mobile benchmark against live EAS Simulators: benchmark builds from EAS (iOS simulator build and APK), the built CLI, 1 worker, `--video=on`. Android, full deterministic suite, all passing with video: ```text ℹ leasing 1 android device(s) from eas-simulators ✓ mobile engine for target "eas-android" prepared 150.88s ✓ |eas-android| tests/controls.e2e.ts (25 tests | 1 skipped) 341.96s ✓ |eas-android| tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts (8 tests) 158.56s ✓ |eas-android| tests/device.e2e.ts (4 tests) 77.81s ✓ |eas-android| tests/flows-lists.e2e.ts (7 tests) 282.59s ✓ |eas-android| tests/flows.e2e.ts (7 tests) 107.99s ✓ |eas-android| tests/login-form.e2e.ts (3 tests) 56.70s ✓ |eas-android| tests/smoke.e2e.ts (1 test) 13.68s Test Files 7 passed (7) Tests 54 passed | 1 skipped (55) ``` iOS, full suite: 49 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped, with 52 videos. None of the failures come from the provider: - clipboard: fails locally under Xcode 27 too; - the WebView coupon text is missing from the accessibility tree on EAS; - the bottom-tabs button is reported as covered on EAS. The last two reproduce on every EAS run and pass on CI's local iOS 26.5 simulators with the same build; they are reported to Expo. Upload path: the same `.app` through `appPath` + `device.installApp()`, with no `buildId`. Recording starts before the app is installed, which only works with device scope: ```text ℹ a booted ios device: dev.e2e.benchmark awaits the suite's device.installApp() ✓ mobile engine for target "eas-ios" prepared 186.72s ✓ |eas-ios| tests/device.e2e.ts (4 tests) 159.46s ✓ |eas-ios| tests/smoke.e2e.ts (1 test) 38.48s Tests 1 failed | 7 passed (8) ``` The 1 failure was agent-device's "could not present the accessibility snapshot ... The app is fine. Rerun". The session reported `packageVersion: 0.21.16`, so the pin is honored. Failure paths: - 7 and then 4 workers on a 1-concurrency account: 1 session ran and the rest queued. The run failed with `still queued while a session of this run has been ready for 10 minutes ...`, and every session was stopped with its queued jobs `CANCELED`. - Ctrl-C while leasing stops both the queued session and the ready one. - A bad or missing `EXPO_TOKEN` fails the lease with `EAS: The bearer token is invalid.` / `EXPO_TOKEN is not set`. iOS recording (login form, sign in and out): ![ios](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff431be9-f7cb-4a7b-ac4b-f79aa7c757ab) Android recording (login form): ![android](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59e4ced1-ee98-4843-857b-23a23a9775c6) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ba282d0-836e-4e8e-bdf9-37f48c4d905f https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/350d3c79-2203-489e-aa15-af7998fa2409 ---

title: docs: add Mobile CI guide for GitHub Actions, EAS Workflows, Bitrise, Codemagic
body: ## What and why - Users asked how to run e2e on EAS Workflows, Bitrise, and the like. `ci.mdx` covered only a web job on GitHub Actions. - New page `docs/mobile-ci.mdx` (Automate > Mobile CI). Every service runs the same four steps: build Release, boot a device, install the build (`xcrun simctl install booted` / `adb install -r`), then `npx e2e run --target ios|android --reporter list,junit`. - Shared rules: one job per platform (hosted Apple Silicon Macs can't run the Android emulator), pin the iOS runtime (every iOS example runs `xcrun simctl create` on a named runtime and boots by UDID; Bitrise uses `OS=26.5`), cache `~/.agent-device`, upload `.e2e/` on every run, commit the replay cache, keep the model key away from untrusted PR code. - One iOS + Android example per service: - **GitHub Actions**: taken from our own `.github/workflows/mobile.yml` (KVM udev rule, `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner`) - **EAS Workflows**: `build` jobs feed custom jobs through `eas/download_build`, `eas/start_android_emulator`, and `eas/upload_artifact`; Android runs on `linux-medium-nested-virtualization` - **Bitrise**: a pipeline using `xcode-start-simulator`, `avd-manager` + `wait-for-android-emulator`, `custom-test-results-export`, with `.e2e` zipped into the deploy dir - **Codemagic**: `mac_mini_m2` / `linux_x2`, the image's preinstalled AVDs, `test_report` - `ci.mdx` and `mobile.mdx` link to the new page. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes (docs site). The YAML itself has not been run on EAS, Bitrise, or Codemagic. - `mint dev` + Playwright: the page renders and shows up in the Automate nav; `pnpm docs:check` passes (`mint validate`, no broken links) - Third-party syntax checked against vendor sources on 2026-09-29: Expo Workflows docs and `expo/eas-cli` build-tools (`eas/start_android_emulator` is documented only under custom builds and installs its system image with `sdkmanager`), `bitrise-io/bitrise-steplib` step.yml inputs/outputs and stack IDs, `codemagic-ci-cd/codemagic-docs` - A fresh-context review found 6 issues, all fixed: the page claimed Android works on macOS, `pod install` and prebuild were missing, the Expo build command was wrong, replay was overstated for judgments, a debug APK needs Metro, and the iOS runtime wasn't pinned - Not verified: which Bitrise Linux machine types support KVM (so `machine_type_id` is left out), and whether Codemagic collects artifacts after a failed script | Top | EAS section | | --- | --- | | ![top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4eda16c-52e4-460a-985f-bfe5626260a2) | ![eas](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39ba2cfe-3cf4-42a3-bfe3-6ef141d3f477) | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ---

title: docs: add PostHog analytics to docs site
body:
- Turns on Mintlify's [PostHog integration](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/integrations/analytics/posthog) for the docs site
- Reuses the CLI telemetry project key (`packages/e2e/src/telemetry/posthog.ts:17`); `$lib` tells the two apart (`web` for docs, `e2e` for the CLI)
- `apiHost` set to `https://eu.i.posthog.com`: the project is on EU cloud, and Mintlify's default proxy `ph.mintlify.com` forwards to US
- Session recordings off
- Consent: Mintlify's built-in consent banner is on in the dashboard (Cookies > Consent banner, a deployment setting, not in `docs.json`). It is the same c15t banner as tester.army and holds PostHog until the visitor accepts

```json
"integrations": {
  "posthog": {
    "apiKey": "phc_rT8h...",
    "apiHost": "https://eu.i.posthog.com",
    "sessionRecording": false
  }
}
```

## Open questions

- Docs events land in the CLI telemetry project with posthog-js defaults: autocapture on, GeoIP on. The GeoIP/aggregate claims in `docs/telemetry.mdx` are scoped to CLI events and still hold for them, but project-wide insights will mix both sources.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- docs site, `mint dev` + Playwright capturing network requests on page load:
  ```
  GET  https://eu-assets.i.posthog.com/array/phc_rT8h.../config.js
  POST https://eu.i.posthog.com/flags/?v=2&config=true&ip=0...   -> 200
  GET  https://eu-assets.i.posthog.com/static/surveys.js?v=1.302.2
  ```
- no `$pageview` capture on localhost; Mintlify's client only runs analytics when `IS_PROD`
- consent banner: `mint dev` does not read deployment settings, and prod shows no banner yet. After merge, check the banner shows on e2e.tester.army/docs, PostHog requests start only after Accept, and `$pageview` events arrive

It reads the repo source, not the build copy in `packages/e2e/skills/`, which `readSkillFiles()` prefers once a build has run. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI, `e2e guide running|bug-bash|explore`: 0 `--artifacts`, `--output` present in each. - `e2e run --artifacts out/artifacts` still fails with `write --output out instead`. - New test fails on main's `running.md` (`expected ... not to contain '--artifacts'`) and passes here. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ---

title: feat(email): email inboxes for tests and the agent, with maildev()
body:
Tests and the agent can now sign up with real email addresses and read the mail the app sends: verification codes, magic links, password resets, invitations. - `email` in the config takes a `MailProvider`. Tests get an `email` fixture; the built-in agent and `e2e mcp` get `new_email_address` and `wait_for_email`. - `maildev()` ships in core for a local app whose SMTP you control: [MailDev](https://github.com/maildev/maildev) runs as a service, addresses are made up, delivery takes milliseconds, and the SMTP envelope makes isolation exact (Bcc included). - Any other mail service plugs in as a `MailProvider`. `@e2e-dev/agentmail`, real inboxes for a remote site, is the PR stacked on this one (#681). - The runner reads no codes or links out of mail. `message.text` is the email as a reader sees it (HTML rendered, each link's URL after its label), the same text filters and the agent read; a test takes what it needs with its own pattern. - Inboxes only receive. Sending and replying were cut: nearly all email testing is outbound from the app, and sending was most of the security surface. ```ts // e2e.config.ts email: maildev({ url: 'http://127.0.0.1:1080' }), // a test test('a new account verifies its email', async ({ app, screen, email }) => { const inbox = await email.inbox(); await app.open('/signup'); await screen.getByLabel('Email').fill(inbox.address); await screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click(); const message = await inbox.waitForMessage({ subject: 'Verify your email' }); await screen.getByLabel('Verification code').fill(/code is (\d{6})/.exec(message.text)![1]!); await screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Verify' }).click(); }); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph attempt F["email fixture
email.inbox()"] --> M T["agent tools
new_email_address
wait_for_email"] --> M M["AttemptMail
(per session)"] end M -->|acquire / list / read| P["MailProvider
maildev()"] E["closeSession"] -->|release, own cleanup budget,
survives Ctrl-C| M T -->|values shown| V["evidence"] --> D["dispatcher: typed or opened
later = replay gap"] ``` ## How it holds together - One `AttemptMail` per session (`packages/e2e/src/email/mailbox.ts`): the fixture and the tools share addresses and "taken" emails; a serial group's members share them too. Addresses go back in `closeSession` under their own cleanup budget, so a timeout, a retry, an interrupt, or an acquire still in flight leaks nothing. A release failure fails the cleanup, never the verdict. - Every provider failure is the new `EMAIL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. A failed poll is retried within the wait's deadline unless the provider marks it `retryable: false`. - Agent safety (`packages/e2e/src/agent/email-tools.ts`): the tools read only the attempt's own addresses; each email reaches the model fenced as untrusted, with every field through the secret ledger before the body is cut. - Replay cache: the tools are mutating, so a call is a gap. What they showed is remembered for the attempt, so a later step that types a code or opens a link (absolute or as a path) from an email records a gap too instead of replaying last run's token (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts`). - The HTML renderer (`packages/e2e/src/email/message.ts`) is a one-pass tokenizer, linear on hostile markup, and drops hidden elements, comments, and Outlook-only blocks. - The email tool names join the harness's reserved tool names (`HARNESS_TOOL_NAMES`), so a project tool named like one is `INVALID_CONFIG` naming where the harness adds it. - The built-in fixture names now live in one list (`packages/e2e/src/internal/fixture-names.ts`); an engine may not take `email`, and with `config.email` set `test.extend()` may not redefine it. ## Web benchmark - New Email Verification scenario (ours, like Control Inventory): a Next.js route sends real SMTP mail with nodemailer to the MailDev the deterministic config starts as a service. `tests/email-verification.e2e.ts` covers the emailed code, a resend (two waits, two emails), an HTML-only magic link, an invite whose Bcc copy reaches only the sender, and a timeout that names what did arrive. - The agentic suite leaves MailDev and `email` out, and declares the scenario skipped: every email step runs live, so it would call the model on every run. ## Review A thermo-nuclear pass (three reviewers) and a fresh-context review ran on this branch; everything they found is fixed except: - Passing the mail through `StepExecutorContext` instead of an attempt-keyed registry: that context is public API, and the tools see only it. - A generic "tool evidence" set in the dispatcher: email is its only user today. - Moving recipient matching into core: which address a message went to is provider knowledge (MailDev's envelope, a hosted service's headers). - `MailContext.env`: a provider reads its key from `process.env`, like the fixture that calls it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The web benchmark through the built CLI, `e2e run tests/email-verification.e2e.ts --video` (MailDev 3.0.0 started as a service, real SMTP mail from the app): ```text ✓ service "maildev" ready 901ms ✓ target "web" command ready 656ms ✓ |web| tests/email-verification.e2e.ts (5 tests) 6.10s ✓ email verification > verifies a new account with the emailed code 763ms ✓ email verification > a resent code replaces the first, and each wait returns the next email 929ms ✓ email verification > signs in from the link in an HTML-only email 1.40s ✓ email verification > an invite reaches the teammate, its Bcc copy only the sender, and nobody else 563ms ✓ email verification > a wait for an email that never comes fails naming what did arrive 2.44s Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` - The whole deterministic web benchmark (42 files, 95 tests), the testbed (70 tests), and the web engine's crosscheck over every scenario, new one included, pass. - The app with no MailDev answers `503 {"error":"Could not send mail: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4281. Start MailDev (the suite does) on SMTP port 4281."}` instead of failing silently. - The replay fixes were each shown failing first: with the relative-link check removed, the new integration test sees step 2 `self-finalized` (last run's token replayed); with it, `reason: gap, derived: whole-node`. - A real model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`) through the built packages: - MailDev, web benchmark scenario (`--repeat-each 3`, 12/12): the agent signs up and types the emailed code, opens the link from the HTML-only email, invites a teammate and checks both inboxes (the Bcc copy included), and finishes a sign-up the test started with its own inbox. - Found and fixed: a Bcc copy's To header names only the teammate, so the model failed the step; `wait_for_email` now shows `Delivered to:` the inbox it read. - Seen once in 10 link runs: the model dropped the last hex character of a sign-in token when copying the URL into `navigate` (the email it was shown had the full URL). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4689a332-6c7e-4dfe-97b6-a6b6009ac318 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66dfa4cf-8495-4e81-9b17-7674d4db86a5

title: feat(cli): e2e feedback sends a report about e2e to the team
body:
## What and why

- New `e2e feedback` command so people, and coding agents working in their shell, can report problems with e2e itself: bugs, misleading docs or skill text, missing features. It follows `ta feedback` in TesterArmy (same types, fields, and limits), but e2e users have no TesterArmy account, so there's no backend. The report goes to the e2e PostHog project we already use for telemetry, as one `e2e_feedback` event (`packages/e2e/src/cli/feedback.ts`).
- The event also carries the anonymous machine facts telemetry sends (versions, OS, runtime, detected coding agent, CI). It never carries a person profile or GeoIP.
- Before sending:
  - the value of any env var whose name contains `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASS`, `_PWD`, `CREDENTIAL`, `AUTH`, `COOKIE`, or `PRIVATE` is replaced with `<secret:NAME>`, using the existing `createRedactor`. Values under 6 characters (`MIN_SECRET_LENGTH`, the same minimum config secrets use) are left alone so ordinary words don't get rewritten;
  - bearer tokens, credentials in URLs, private keys, JWTs, and common API key formats are replaced with `<redacted>`.
- `--dry-run` prints the exact event and sends nothing.
- Length limits count characters (code points), not UTF-16 units. Exit 0 means PostHog accepted the event. Exit 3 means PostHog didn't confirm it; the report may still have arrived, so the error message includes its reference id.
- Opt-outs:
  - a saved `e2e telemetry disable` does not block feedback, because feedback is only sent when someone asks for it;
  - `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` and `DO_NOT_TRACK` do block it (exit 2), so a CI job or fleet that opted out never sends anything, even when an agent runs the command.
- When telemetry is on, the event reuses the telemetry `distinct_id` so a report can be read alongside the sessions around it. When it's off, the id is a one-off `feedback:<uuid>`.
- The skill has a new Feedback section: when to send, never paste app data, and tell the user the reference id. Also updated: `reference/cli.mdx`, `telemetry.mdx#feedback`, and the outbound-connection lists in `security.mdx` and `SECURITY.md`.

```bash
npx e2e feedback --type bug -m "list ignores --grep" \
  --command "e2e list --grep checkout" --agent "Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5"
# Feedback sent to the e2e team, thank you. Reference: 01a0f1ce-930c-791d-8451-ae6d415e24a8
```

Not in this PR:
- An MCP tool for feedback. This is CLI only.
- Slack notifications. Those need a Slack destination on `e2e_feedback`, set up in the PostHog UI.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI from `/tmp`, the verify skill's scratch-project route.
- `e2e feedback --help` shows the Report and Output option groups, examples, and the docs link.
- `--dry-run` with `MY_API_KEY=supersecret123` and `TEST_USER_PASS=hunter22` set in the environment:

```json
"message": "run crashed with <secret:MY_API_KEY>",
"actual": "Bearer <redacted> <redacted>",
"agent": "Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5",
"coding_agent": "claude-code",
"$process_person_profile": false,
"$geoip_disable": true
```

- The PASS redaction and the prose check:

```json
"message": "login with <secret:TEST_USER_PASS> fails",
"task": "following the Basic authentication example",
```

- A real send was accepted by PostHog (reference `01a0f1ce-930c-791d-8451-ae6d415e24a8`, exit 0).
- With `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` it exits 2 and prints `feedback not sent: DO_NOT_TRACK is set, which switches off everything e2e sends. Unset it for this command to send the report.`
- Running without `-m` exits 2 with commander's required-option error.

title: docs: sync the package manager choice across every command snippet
body:
## What and why

- Only the quickstart `init` block had npm / pnpm / bun tabs, so picking bun there still left `npx e2e run` right below it. Every shell block that runs `npx`, `npm install`, or `npm ci` is now a `<CodeGroup>` with `npm`, `pnpm`, and `bun` blocks (51 blocks, 19 pages).
- Mintlify syncs code group tabs by title and saves the choice in `localStorage.code`, so one click changes every snippet on the page and on every page you open after it. No custom JS needed.
- Mapping:

  | npm | pnpm | bun |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `npx e2e …`, `npx agent-device …` (installed deps) | `pnpm exec …` | `bunx …` |
  | `npx e2e init`, `npx unbox-ai`, `npx vercel` (not installed yet) | `pnpm dlx …` | `bunx …` |
  | `npm install -D x` / `--save-dev x` | `pnpm add -D x` | `bun add -d x` |

- `scripts/check-docs-package-managers.ts` (run by `pnpm docs:check`) fails on a shell block with a package manager command that is not in a `npm`/`pnpm`/`bun` code group, so new pages can't bring the problem back. AGENTS.md mentions the rule.
- Out of scope: inline code in prose and tables (`npx e2e login openai` in the quickstart table), `console` output samples, and the CI workflow YAML in `ci.mdx`/`mobile-ci.mdx` (switching those to pnpm/bun would also need different setup steps). These still use npm.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `pnpm docs:check`: examples, the new check, `mint validate`, and `mint broken-links` all pass. On `main`, the new check lists every unwrapped block.

title: web: tab support in tests and agent steps (follow a tab the app opens)
body:
A tab the app opens (a `target="_blank"` link, `window.open`, an OAuth popup) is invisible to e2e today. The web engine keeps observing the attempt's first page, so:

- **Tests** cannot wait for the tab, assert on it, act in it, or close it. There is no `web.waitForPopup` or page handle (`docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` lists `page.waitForEvent('popup')` / `context.on('page')` as missing).
- **Agent steps** see a screen where "nothing happened" after the tap. `docs/reference/agent.mdx`: "Tab switching has no verb yet: a new tab is invisible to the model."

Seen in the Oct 1 bug bash:

- `e2e explore` on the web benchmark's `/e/new-tab-flow` filed a false high issue, "Open verification tab button produces no visible tab or code".
- `agent.act` on the same scenario ended `ACTION_FAILED` after trying `Control+Tab`, 4 model calls, 13-15 s.
- A stopgap in #668 reported open tabs to the agent through a new `EngineSnapshot.notices` field so it could end blocked with `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`. It was dropped before merge in favor of real support.

## Proposal

1. **Follow the new tab by default**, as a person does: when an action opens a tab in the attempt's context, the active page (what `screen`, `expect`, `observe`, and the agent read and act on) moves to it; when it closes, the active page returns to its opener. This covers most `_blank` and OAuth-popup flows with no new API and no new agent verb.
2. **A test API** for the flows that need control: wait for the tab an action opens (e.g. `web.waitForPopup(() => link.tap())`), read its URL, switch the active page back and forth, close it.
3. **An agent verb** (`switch_tab`) only if following the new tab turns out not to be enough.

## Open questions (from #487 and the closed #477)

- Where the active page lives: a stack the engine owns and every fixture follows implicitly (#477's shape), or explicit page handles passed to `screen`/`expect`.
- Tabs closing out of order, a click whose only effect is closing its own page, and a popup's URL after the stack compacts (the three races Devin found in #477).
- How video segments, traces, CDP reconnect (`connect.reconnectEndpoint`), and hosted-browser attempt scope (`kernel({ scope: 'attempt' })`) follow the active page.
- Replay cache: a recorded flow that crosses into a new tab has to replay into the same tab.
- Mobile parity: an in-app browser or a second activity is the same problem on a device; out of scope here but the contract should not rule it out.

## Done when

- The web benchmark's `new-tab-flow` has a deterministic twin in `tests/` and passes, and its agentic test completes the flow instead of ending blocked.
- `e2e explore` on `new-tab-flow` files no tab finding.
- Docs: `docs/reference/web.mdx`, `docs/reference/agent.mdx`, the Playwright migration table, and `skills/e2e/` describe the behavior.

Related: #487 (tabs plus dialog kinds and download paths), #486, #477.

title: feat(agentmail): @e2e-dev/agentmail, real AgentMail inboxes for config.email
body:
Stacked on #677 (core email seam and `maildev()`). Adds `@e2e-dev/agentmail`: real inboxes from [AgentMail](https://agentmail.to) for `config.email`, for a deployed site that sends through its real mail service, where MailDev cannot catch the mail.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
import { agentMail } from '@e2e-dev/agentmail';

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web({ url: 'https://staging.example.com' }) }],
  email: agentMail(), // reads AGENTMAIL_API_KEY
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

- Default `isolation: 'alias'`: every address is a plus-address of one shared inbox (`<inbox>+e2e-<hex>@agentmail.to`), created once per organization by `clientId` and reused, so any number of workers fit the free plan's three inboxes. An address reads only mail whose To or Cc names it exactly, and its mail is deleted on release unless another live alias also received it.
- `isolation: 'inbox'`: a new inbox per address, deleted on release, tagged with an expiry so a later run sweeps one a killed run left behind (six hours on).
- `inboxId` aliases an inbox you already have; `domain` and `displayName` for per-address inboxes.
- A 4xx or a bad key is `retryable: false`, so a wait ends at once instead of polling to its deadline. The SDK loads lazily, and every call runs under its own timeout.
- Release keeps mail that names another e2e alias (it may belong to another worker, which constructs its own provider); a background sweep, once per process, deletes alias mail older than six hours. `read` on an alias refuses a message not sent to it.
- Docs: the AgentMail sections of `docs/email.mdx` (provider table, setup, options, caveats), an integrations card, the package README, and a changeset.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/agentmail test` (9 unit tests against an in-memory AgentMail with offset paging) and `test:live` against the real API: an alias receives mail an inbox of its own sends, reads it, and both are cleaned up on release.
- A real model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`) through packed tarballs, against a scratch app that sends real mail from an AgentMail inbox:
  - The agent signs up with an address of its own and types the emailed code, verifies by opening the link from the email, and finishes a sign-up the test started with `email.inbox()`: 3/3 with aliases, 3/3 with `isolation: 'inbox'`.
  - A second run records `reason: gap` and types that run's new code, not last run's.
  - Afterwards the organization holds the same two inboxes as before, and no mail to the runs' aliases.
- After the review fixes (`9983e31a`, `222a0e60`): 13 unit tests (cross-worker release, the old-mail sweep, one shared sweep retried after a failed deletion, an hourly re-sweep for a long-lived process, confined reads), stable over 5 runs, with `fetch` stubbed so a call past the SDK mock can never reach the real API (one did, before the SDK loaded once per process). A read-only call against the real API confirmed the `before` listing the sweep uses. `test:live` was not re-run after this commit: its sweep would delete 47 alias emails older than six hours that earlier stress scripts left in the shared inbox.

title: docs(skill): bug-bash personas, explorer-artifact triage, and external-site rules
body: ## What and why - The bug-bash topic's config example now defines postures as personas: named agents sharing model and budgets with a different `system` stance (skeptic, fuzzer), picked per charter with `--agent`. The charter file grows an agent column and the fan-out snippet passes it. - New first row in the triage table: the "Explorer artifact" bucket - dead links that opened a new tab, copy that only reads broken in the accessibility tree, "Loading more" infinite-scroll sentinels, lazy-loaded media. Headless, `--max-steps 6`, 4-way parallel, gpt-6-luna-fast: | Recipe | Confirmed bugs found | Artifact false positives | Cost | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline: one default agent (current skill) | 3/4 | 2 (sentinel, new-tab link) | $0.23 | | personas only | 4/4 | 4 (split copy, lazy portrait, 2 sentinel) | $0.30 | | personas + artifact context (this PR's recipe) | 3/4 | 2 (both lazy-image, sentinel and split-copy eliminated) | $0.29 | - In the preceding uncontexted bash on the same site, artifact families were 14 of 27 raw findings (10 split-copy, 4 new-tab links); the verification pass rejected them all, which is what this PR moves up front. - The one bug the artifact-context recipe missed vs personas-only is single-run variance (a scroll-spy highlight; the same recipe's other runs caught it), not a suppression effect: the artifact context names only runner blind spots, none of which overlap that bug's shape. - `pnpm check` green, including `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` after the mdx edit. title: cache: context identity in the trace cache key (agentContext, scope, query, origin, numeric ids, executor version)
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, canary 0.15.0-canary-20260924194828). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `buildTraceCacheKey` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts:154-181` has no agentContext, scope, or executor field; `route.ts` still drops query and origin (`pathnameOf`, lines 62-76) and folds numeric segments (lines 45-51).

## Problem

Any new key field turns every committed recording under `apps/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` and `apps/mobile-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` into a miss until re-recorded. Decide the shape once, ship one re-record.

- **B16** `agentContext` is not in the trace cache key. A test whose `agentContext` changes from "Daily" to "Monthly" replays the Daily recording. Proposal: digest of `agentContext` in the key.
- **B22** no session/account/role identity in the key. A recording made on account A replays on account B, so a negative access-control test passes falsely. Proposal: opt-in `cacheScope` (string) on the test or step, hashed into the key; document that persona tests must set it. No tokens in the key.
- **B21** query string ignored by `routeOf` (unit-tested on purpose, documented in `docs/cache.mdx`). `/chores?audit=safe` recording replays on `?audit=unsafe`. Proposal: query participates by default, `volatileParams: [...]` on the target or test to ignore tracking params.
- **B26** origin ignored by `routeOf`. Same path on another host replays. Proposal: current origin in the start precondition, miss on mismatch; explicit allow list for real multi-domain flows.
- **B28** numeric path segment folds to `:id`, `/records/1` replays on `/records/2`. Proposal: keep the fold (it is what makes reseeded ids replay), but hand off when the instruction or params mention the id, or offer `routeSegments: 'exact'`.
- **D5** executor version outside the key by design (`identity.ts:10-13`). A policy change in a custom executor does not invalidate old traces. Proposal: `producer.version` compat rule, opt-in sharing across versions, hit/miss reason in the report.

## Done when

- Decision recorded for each of the six, key shape changed in one PR, benchmark recordings re-recorded once.
- `docs/cache.mdx` describes what participates in the key.

title: cache: end-of-step anchors prove presence, not effect (empty sets self-finalize, 8-anchor cut, volatile filter, pre-existing anchors)
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `verifyAnchors` returns true for an empty set (`packages/e2e/src/agent/replay.ts:366`), `MAX_TRACE_ANCHORS = 8` in document order (`cache/trace.ts:50`, `cache/anchors.ts:48-72`), `isVolatileAnchor` unchanged (`anchors.ts:98-110`), undecided end route still resolves via anchors (`step-cache.ts:411-422`). No `postconditions` option exists.

## Problem

The replayed click is real; only the effect check is skipped when the recorded end anchors are weak. Eight repros, one gap: anchors prove presence, not effect.

- **B20 / B27** no anchors recorded when the effect is a disappearance, a `checked` flip, or a same-node text mutation; replay self-finalizes unconditionally.
- **B23 / B31** `MAX_TRACE_ANCHORS = 8` in document order drops the ninth, business-critical leaf, including the one anchor an author added to disambiguate a route.
- **B24** a new `role=alert` beside the recorded success anchor is ignored.
- **B25** `isVolatileAnchor` drops `3 records imported`, keeps generic `Import completed`.
- **B29** an anchor already present before the action counts as proof.
- **B30** `endScreen` accepts an `undecided` end route when generic anchors are present.

## Proposal

1. Never self-finalize on an empty anchor set, hand off to the executor instead.
2. Record absences and state flips as anchors.
3. Prefer identity-bearing anchors (text unique across the delta, route-specific testIds) when cutting to the limit.
4. An explicit `postconditions` option on `agent.act` for authors who need exact values.

(1) to (3) are library changes with a replay-rate cost; (4) is new API. Pick which to ship first. Related: the state-drift probe testbed already exercises anchor relocation.

title: web: basicAuth answers any origin and headers are site-scoped; scope both to the target origin by default
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `docs/security.mdx:74-78` and `packages/web/src/protected-app.ts:46-53` document the any-origin behavior; `installSiteHeaders` is site-scoped.

## Problem

- **D3** `web({ basicAuth })` answers a 401 challenge from any origin (documented). Playwright 1.63 supports `httpCredentials.origin`. A third-party origin the app embeds can issue a 401 and collect the credential.
- **D4** `web({ headers })` is scoped by site, not origin; another port on the same host receives the preview bypass header.

## Proposal

- `basicAuth`: default to the target origin, `basicAuth.origins: string[]` for extras.
- `headers`: exact origin by default, explicit extras.
- Both change documented behavior in `docs/security.mdx`; needs a changeset and a migration note.

Related: #496 (headers values never join the secret ledger).

title: runner: skip() after a failed expect.soft reports SKIPPED and hides the failure
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, D1). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:1052-1058` drops the soft failure when the cause is a runtime skip, and line 1174 records `skipped`.

## Problem

`skip()` after a failed `expect.soft` reports SKIPPED, exit 0, and the soft failure leaves no trace in the report. A test that checks a value softly and then skips on a feature flag hides a real regression. Documented today.

## Proposal

Pick one:

- Keep the soft failure sticky: the attempt is FAIL, skip reason attached.
- A distinct status (`skipped-after-failure`) plus a CI flag to treat it as failure.

In both cases a fail-then-skip on retry must be visible in the report and the CLI summary.

title: runner: artifacts.settle() has no budget, store.put gets no AbortSignal, store publishing cannot be required
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, D2 and store policy). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `settle()` in `packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:201-206` has no budget, `ArtifactStore.put` in `types.ts:1087-1088` takes no AbortSignal, no `uploadTimeout` exists. The `best-effort | required` policy from #645 (`internal/recording-modes.ts:31-38`) covers trace and video recordings only, not the store.

## Problem

- `artifacts.settle()` runs outside every budget and `store.put` gets no AbortSignal. SIGINT waited 12 s on a slow store in the audit.
- A failed `put` never fails the run, so CI evidence publishing is best-effort with no way to make it required.

## Proposal

- `artifacts.uploadTimeout` (config), an AbortSignal passed to `put`, `uploadStatus` on the report artifact entry.
- Store policy `required | best-effort`, matching the recording-mode vocabulary from #645. `required` fails the run when a put fails or times out.

API addition to the public `ArtifactStore` type: changeset for `e2e`.

title: web: waitForResponse reads the whole body before returning, so SSE and slow streams time out
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, B9). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `readResponseBody` runs before `waitForResponse` resolves (`packages/web/src/web.ts:91-103, 410`).

## Problem

`waitForResponse` reads the whole body before returning, so an SSE endpoint or a slow streaming response times out at what should be the header stage. A test cannot assert on the status of a stream.

## Proposal

Return after headers; `text()` and `json()` become lazy and bounded (size and time). Behavior change to a public method: changeset, docs in `docs/reference/web.mdx`. #554 already made body read failures reject `text()`/`json()`, so the error path exists.

title: expect: toBeDefined(null) diverges from Jest, toContain deep equality undocumented in the migration table
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25). Verified on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `toBeDefined` checks `!== undefined && !== null` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts:129-131`); `toContain` uses deep `equals` (`values.ts:185`) while `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx:181` lists it as "same". `toHaveClass('')` was already decided and documented in #546, dropped here.

## Problem

- `toBeDefined(null)` fails in e2e, passes in Playwright and Jest. Proposal: align to `!== undefined`. Update `docs/reference/expect.mdx:211` ("Requires a non-nullish value").
- `toContain({ id: 1 })` on an array of objects passes in e2e (deep equality), fails in Playwright (strict). Proposal: keep, but document as a deliberate difference in the migration table instead of "same".

Two small PRs, or one. Both touch the migration table.

title: reporting: passing expect(value) and expect.poll produce no report step, no named checkpoints
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, P2). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `packages/e2e/src/expect/poll.ts` and `values.ts` record no step.

## Problem

A passing `expect(value)` or `expect.poll` produces no report step, so a test whose only checks are value assertions reads as "opened the page, passed" in the report. There is no way to add a named checkpoint either.

## Proposal

- Record value assertions and `expect.poll` as steps (`api: expect.toBe` etc.) with the same status and duration fields locator assertions get.
- A `checkpoint(label)` or equivalent for a named marker in the report.

Report schema change (`report-1` fixtures), `docs/reference/report.mdx`.

title: cache: an approval point after a chosen API or DB check
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, P2). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): traces are staged until the attempt ends (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts:71-77`, from #92); value assertions never approve recordings.

## Problem

A recording is approved when the attempt passes. A test that verifies the agent's work with an API or DB check after the step cannot make that check the approval point, so a false-positive step whose verification fails later still commits a recording if the attempt is retried into a pass.

## Proposal

An explicit approval point after a chosen check, e.g. `cache.approve()` or a `verify` option on `agent.act` that takes the check callback. Design open: whether value assertions inside the step approve by default.

title: reporting: aggregated adaptation narrative on agent steps
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, P2). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): nothing in the report aggregates adaptation events.

## Problem

When the agent adapts (first action had no effect, used an alternate entry, a required route was violated or never checked), the report shows the outcome but no narrative. A reviewer has to read `turns[]` to learn the test passed by a different path than the recording.

## Proposal

An aggregated adaptation summary on the step: list of adaptation kinds with one line each, surfaced in the CLI summary and the GitHub reporter. Report schema addition.

title: reporting: a missing screenshot never says why (policy, not configured, write error, overwritten)
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, P2). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30).

## Problem

A missing screenshot in the report has one shape: absent. The reader cannot tell "skipped by policy" (pixels withheld after a secret fill), "not configured", "write error", or "overwritten" apart.

## Proposal

A reason on the missing artifact slot, or a `withheld` artifact record with a reason enum. Aligns with the `redaction` field #561 added to `StoredArtifact`.

title: web: Playwright migration gaps: toHaveScreenshot, clock, addInitScript
body:
Split from #557 (audit 2026-09-25, P2). Verified still open on main 218e9ee7 (2026-09-30): `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx:179, 226, 229` list these as missing. Popup and new tab handling has its own issue, #680.

## Problem

Three Playwright APIs that migrations hit have no e2e equivalent:

- `toHaveScreenshot` (native visual regression with a stored baseline).
- `page.clock` (fake timers, time travel).
- `addInitScript` (a script that runs before any page script).

## Proposal

Decide each: build, document a workaround, or mark as won't do in the migration table. `addInitScript` is the smallest; the web engine already installs its own init scripts (`closed-shadow.ts`). Visual regression needs a baseline store decision. Clock may be an `app` fixture method.

title: feat!: the app is declared on its target; engines only drive it
body:
The app under test is declared on its target, and nowhere else. Engines only drive it. This is the first half of #648: the app move and the runtime fixes, without `defineService`, which follows in #648 on top of this branch.

```ts
targets: [
  { name: 'chromium', engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev', '--port', '{port}'] } } },
  { name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios' }), app: { bundleId: 'dev.shop.app', appPath: './build/Shop.app', permissions: { camera: 'grant' } } },
],
```

**The app on the target**
- `target.app` holds `{ url | bundleId, appPath, identity, environment, launchArguments, permissions, command, readyUrl }`.
- `web({ url })`, `mobile({ app })`, an app key directly on the target, and `services` anywhere are unknown keys: a plain break, no migration messages.
- `defineEngine` gets `validateApp`: `web()` needs `app.url`, `mobile()` needs `bundleId` or `appPath`, and `app.url` on a mobile target fails as not supported yet with a platform-specific note. `defineEngine({ app })` is an unknown key.
- `prepare` and `init` receive the resolved app as `info.app`.
- `requires: ['browser' | 'native-app']` is derived from the target's app, not declared by engines.
- Replay-cache and session keys are byte-identical to main, pinned by `packages/e2e/tests/unit/target-identity.test.ts`.

**Services wait for the next release**
- There is no `services` key in this version; the docs carry a callout in place of the old services sections. Nothing in the repo used them.

**Refused at load**
- a port-0 `app.url` with nothing to start on it
- `reuseExisting` on a free port: what already answers cannot serve the port the run assigns

**`e2e mcp`**
- A cancelled or disconnected `open_session`, or a server shutting down, aborts an open still starting its app command and stops what it started (`CANCELLED`).
- A shared start that every waiting session gave up on is abandoned, and the next session starts it afresh.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[target.app] --> C[checkTargetApp: shape]
  C --> V[engine.validateApp: what the platform needs]
  V --> R[resolveTargetApp: base URL, identity, command with port]
  R --> P[allocateAppPorts]
  P --> W[workers: assignPorts from the bootstrap]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Testbed, built CLI (`pnpm test:testbed`), its config declaring `app: { url, command }` on the target: `target "web" command ready 88ms`, 14 files, 70 tests passed, 1 skipped, the command stopped at the end.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/target-identity.test.ts` pins the cache and session digests of the same apps declared the old way.

title: fix(skill): rewrite the bundled skill against the runner; point tools refuse after a secret fill
body:
## What and why

- Every claim in `skills/e2e/` (SKILL.md and the eight references) was checked against `packages/*/src`; the skill ships inside the `e2e` package, so drift there is user-facing.
- Wrong claims fixed: reads fail at once on zero matches (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts:200`), `.not` holds 1 s (`internal/time.ts:54`), `clearState` has no serial-group limit, `onDialog` is async and an unhandled dialog is `INVALID_STATE`, `defineConfig` is `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED` not `INVALID_CONFIG`, the invented `backend` key is gone, the blocked `act` code list matches `agent/error.ts`, a per-call budget above the agent's limit is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`agent/call-options.ts:28`), EAS `maxDurationMinutes` is the account cap, `e2e guide` lists `bug-bash`, Ctrl-C writes a report only once tests started, the `Repeats` row wording matches `report/repeats.ts`.
- Gaps filled: `launchTimeout`, `cleanupTimeout`, `cache` object form, `testIdAttribute`, `screencast`, the `command` shape, `app.baseUrl`, `pressed`/`level`, bare `test.skip()`, route glob grammar, `login|logout|models`, `init [directory]`, `dismiss_keyboard`, `UNKNOWN_TARGET`, explore JSON `id`/`errorCode`, seven error-code rows.
- Slop cut: migration notes for removed shapes (the runtime already names the replacement), engine-internal paragraphs (CDP recovery, tree-capture fallback, settle policy), the secret-taint rule stated six times, ten-line table cells, the one em dash. Each repeated fact now has one home and pointers. 19676 words to 16613 before the #683 merge; bug-bash keeps #683's personas, artifact bucket, and external-site rules.
- Runtime fix found by the audit: after a secret fill, `tap_at`, `hover_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at` kept aiming at the pre-fill screenshot. The MCP catalog text (`mcp/session.ts:432`) and the docs already promised `PIXEL_TAINTED`. `pointOf` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts` now checks `context.pixelsTainted` first, so all five refuse with the taint line. The check runs inside the action queue (`atPoint`), so a `type_secret` batched ahead of a point verb in the same turn taints it before the verb resolves its target.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[point tool call] --> B{secret filled?}
  B -- yes --> C[PIXEL_TAINTED line, no action]
  B -- no --> D{screenshot taken?}
  D -- no --> E[take one first]
  D -- yes --> F[hit-test, act by id or bare point]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `pnpm --filter e2e run test:unit`: the new grammar-tools case builds the tools, flips `pixelsTainted`, calls all five point tools, and asserts the `PIXEL_TAINTED` line with nothing dispatched.
- A second case queues a taint-flipping body ahead of `tap_at` in one turn and asserts the same; both fail on main.
- `tests/integration/mcp-server.test.ts` against the built packages: `type_secret`, then `tap_at` answers with `PIXEL_TAINTED` and never taps.
- `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js guide bug-bash` prints the new topic; an unknown topic lists all eight.
- The bug-bash config example (personas, `satisfies E2EConfig`) typechecks under `--strict` against the built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` types.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `tap_at` after `type_secret`: `No screenshot has been taken in this step ...` or a tap at the stale point; the new unit case fails with `expected '...' to contain 'PIXEL_TAINTED'` | `No point actions: a secret was filled in this attempt, so no pixels leave the runner until it ends (PIXEL_TAINTED) ...`; unit and integration cases pass |

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`.changeset/point-tools-tainted.md`, `e2e` patch).
- [ ] Breaking change: none.
- [x] Docs: `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` already describes the fixed behavior; `skills/e2e/` is the change.
- [ ] Contract change: none (no public type, error code, flag, or wire field changed).
- [ ] Engine contract change: none.

title: fix(release): restore wide peer ranges the canary release pinned
