title: fix(mobile): agent-device 0.21.18, iOS clipboard writes under Xcode 27
body: ## What and why - agent-device 0.21.16 -> 0.21.18 in `@e2e-dev/mobile` and the docs site. - 0.21.17 writes the iOS simulator clipboard from the runner ([agent-device#3065](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3065)). Under Xcode 27, `simctl pbcopy` exits 0 and writes nothing, so on 0.21.16 `device.setClipboard` did nothing and returned no error. - 0.21.18: a live daemon gets probed again before being replaced as unreachable (#3050), and Android retries once after a device-offline refusal (#3055). - The iOS placeholder (#2961) and focus (#2925) fixes shipped in 0.21.16, but the benchmark still ran those tests on Android only and `docs/mobile.mdx` still called them Android only. Both tests now run on iOS too, and the two limitations are gone from the docs. - `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` also said `toBeFocused` never passes on iOS; that line is gone too. - I re-captured the golden device trees on 0.21.18 per AGENTS.md. The raw JSON only picks up the new `kind` field, key order, and clock or notification noise, and every projected `.tree.txt` is unchanged. I kept the old iOS Stripe capture: this simulator has no saved card, and the old one covers that state. - The capture suite had been failing to load since the scope rename (`@e2edev/mobile` import). That's fixed, along with the stale filter names in AGENTS.md. - The clipboard test writes a new string each run. With a fixed string it passed on main whenever the simulator still held the previous run's text. - The breaking change in 0.21.17 (Android permission ids, #3023) does not reach us: `setPermission` never reads its result. - I re-ran every other platform-limited benchmark test on the platform it skips, and the reasons still hold: an iOS tab has role `other` (the new `kind` field comes from the raw type), iOS `doubleTap` cadence, iOS `foregroundApp` after `home()`, Android clipboard refused, and Android web view fields have no names. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - mobile benchmark, `e2e run tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts --target ios-simulator --grep "clipboard reads back"` on an iOS 26.5 simulator (Xcode 27), with a new string each run: | main (0.21.16) | this branch (0.21.18) | | --- | --- | | `ASSERTION_FAILED: expected "e2e clipboard 42" to be "e2e clipboard 1790786955004"` (the write did nothing; this is the previous run's text) | `Tests 1 passed (1)` | - `e2e run tests/controls.e2e.ts tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts` on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator: 63 passed and 2 skipped. `a placeholder query and attribute reads find the field` and `toBeFocused follows the focus` pass on both platforms. - The one failure is iOS `setOrientation rotates the window the app measures`. It fails the same way on 0.21.16 on this simulator, so the bump did not cause it. - `tests/smoke.e2e.ts` and `tests/device.e2e.ts` on iOS: 5 passed. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ---

title: ci(release): publish through npm trusted publishing (OIDC)
body: Publishing now authenticates with npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC) instead of the `NPM_TOKEN` secret, same setup as callstack/react-native-bottom-tabs. Once the repo is public, npm attaches provenance automatically: the "built and signed on GitHub Actions" badge. - `release.yml` gains `id-token: write` and drops `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`; the OIDC exchange in `npm publish` (npm 11.5.1+, bundled with node 26) replaces it. - The `release` job moves to `ubuntu-latest`: npm rejects OIDC tokens from self-hosted runners, and Blacksmith registers as one ([npm docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/): "Self-hosted runners are not currently supported"). AGENTS.md records the exception to the Blacksmith rule. Timeout bumped 20 to 30 min for the slower runner. - `registry-url` removed from setup-node: its `.npmrc` template reads `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` and errors once the variable is gone. - `publishConfig.provenance: false` removed from all 6 public packages. Default is auto: npm skips provenance while the repo is private, attaches it once public. No changeset: metadata only, no behavior change. - All 6 packages (`e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, `@e2e-dev/github`, `@e2e-dev/kernel`, `@e2e-dev/eas`) already have the trusted publisher connection on npmjs: GitHub Actions, `tester-army/e2e`, `release.yml`, `Allow npm publish` checked. - CONTRIBUTING.md documents the per-package connection and the recipe for a new package (first publish by hand, then add the trusted publisher; npm has no org-wide setting). AGENTS.md's release notes updated to match. ## Verified Ran it locally: no - the publish path only runs on a release push to `main`, and OIDC cannot be exercised from a laptop (the token exchange only works inside the configured workflow on a GitHub-hosted runner). Checked statically instead: - `actionlint` on the workflow: clean. - Inputs validated against `action.yml` at the pinned `changesets/action` SHA: `create-github-releases` and `push-git-tags` default to true, the token input is optional; the action's `.npmrc` handling is OIDC-safe since changesets/action#545. - Runner and provenance constraints confirmed against the [npm Trusted Publishers docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/). - `pnpm check` green after the `publishConfig` edits. - Live proof is the next release publish; rollback is reverting this and restoring `NPM_TOKEN` (secret still set). Fresh-context review found 3 issues, all fixed here: the Blacksmith/OIDC incompatibility, provenance claims contradicted by the `publishConfig` pins and repo visibility, and the stale AGENTS.md release notes. ---

title: fix(cache): a failure where no model answered evicts no recording
body:
A read-write run with no model access deleted valid committed recordings. Replay handed a step to the agent (a `gap`, or a divergence), the provider rejected the request with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, and the cache treated that like a failed flow: the step-level `conclude('failed')` evicted the consumed entry, and `flushStagedTraces` deleted every unconfirmed staged entry, including an `act` that replayed whole before an `agent.assert` that could not reach its model. A failure where no model answered is a verdict on the provider, never on the app. It now evicts nothing, like an interrupt, while steps verified before it are still saved. - `AGENT_CODE_TABLE` marks the codes that mean no model answered: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (auth, rate limit, outage, the 120 s stall guard) and `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`. `isModelUnreachable()` reads that flag (`packages/e2e/src/agent/error.ts`). - Step level: `StepOutcome` `'cancelled'` becomes `'no-verdict'`, covering a cancellation and a model that never answered. `failedStepOutcome()` maps a thrown error to it, and `conclude` does nothing for it (`packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`). - Attempt level: `flushStagedTraces` takes an `AttemptSettlement`. When every failure in the attempt (primary and secondary, e.g. an `afterEach` assertion) is model-unreachable, `implicatesUnconfirmed` is false: steps verified before the failure are still written, and every unconfirmed entry (a new recording or one a step replayed whole) is left exactly as stored (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`). Interrupts keep skipping settlement entirely. - A model that answered with something unusable (`MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`, `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW`) or a step that ran out of time (`STEP_TIMEOUT`, even with a request still open, since the 120 s stall guard outlasts the 30 s judgment default) still counts as a failure of the flow: the screen it was shown may be what went wrong. The model cannot pick either code in a verdict (`MODEL_ERROR_CODES` in `primitives.ts`). ```mermaid flowchart LR F[step or attempt fails] --> Q{why} Q -- interrupted --> K[cache untouched] Q -- no model answered --> W[write confirmed, leave the rest] Q -- other --> E[write confirmed, evict unconfirmed] ``` Docs: `docs/cache.mdx`, `docs/coding-agents.mdx`, `docs/reference/errors.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web benchmark, no `CI`, no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`: `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.agent.config.ts tests-agent/scenarios.e2e.ts --grep 'lying-labels|async-states|shadow-dom-form|iframe-form'`, then `git status`. Both builds fail the 4 tests with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (`Cache 2 handed off · 2 missed`, exit 3); only main deletes recordings. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `D .e2e/cache/46163014...json`
`D .e2e/cache/d01c00f9...json`
`D .e2e/cache/ee64bc2d...json`
`D .e2e/cache/ffc271f6...json` | `git status` clean | - New integration tests in `tests/integration/agent-trace-cache.test.ts`: an `act` replayed whole then an `agent.assert` on an unreachable model, and a replay that hands off mid-step to an unreachable model, both fail on main with the entry deleted and pass here with the entry bytes and mtime unchanged; a fresh recording confirmed by an `expect` before the unreachable judgment is still written; a failing `afterEach` assertion after the unreachable judgment still evicts the replayed entry. - Mobile variant not run on a simulator; the replayed-whole-then-assert integration test covers the same path.

title: fix(mobile): never pin an install's file path as the app app.open() launches
body: A target with only `app.appPath` on Android: `device.installApp()` succeeds, then `app.open()` fails with `Android runtime hints require an installed package name, not "/.../benchmark.apk"`. CI never saw it because the benchmark always sets `bundleId`. ## Root cause (upstream, agent-device 0.21.18) - `install --json` returns `app: ` and no `package` when it cannot identify the APK (`src/daemon/handlers/session-app-deployment.ts`, `buildNonIosDeployResult`: `app || packageName || launchTarget || appPath`). - Its binary `AndroidManifest.xml` parser never matches aapt2 output: it requires a 36-byte start-element header and counts `attributeStart` from the chunk, but `ResXMLTree_node`'s header is 16 bytes and `attributeStart` is relative to `ResXMLTree_attrExt` (`packages/platform-android/src/manifest.ts`, `parseStartElementPackageName`). Its tests only use text manifests. - The fallback is the SDK's `aapt`, searched under `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `ANDROID_HOME`, `~/Android/Sdk`, so not the macOS default `~/Library/Android/sdk`. - The last fallback diffs `pm list packages` before and after install, which finds nothing when the package is already on the device. - Proof on this Mac: `resolveAndroidArchivePackageName(apk)` from `agent-device/artifacts` returns `undefined`, and with `ANDROID_HOME` set it returns `dev.e2e.benchmark`. - An upstream fix for the parser (a 10-line offset fix plus a test with a real aapt2-compiled manifest) is ready locally and not opened yet. With it, `agent-device install --json` reports `"package": "dev.e2e.benchmark"` with no SDK env. The bump comes in a follow-up PR once it is released. ## This PR - `installApp` opens by the id agent-device reported, else the `app` passed in, and never by `result.app` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`). With neither, it fails at the install with `ENGINE_FAILURE` naming `app.bundleId` or the `app` option, instead of pinning a file path that fails later in `app.open()`. - `app.open()` on a device now keeps the engine's own `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` reason. Before, core rewrote every one into "pin one with the target's app.bundleId or app.appPath", even with `appPath` set (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`). Core's message now covers only an engine with no relaunch hook. - The mobile restart message now reads correctly under both `app.open()` and `app.restart()`: "launching the app needs...". - Docs: `installApp` return rules (reference, README) and a Troubleshooting entry for the Android case (`ANDROID_HOME`, daemon restart, or `bundleId`). - Decision: a non-engine build installed with no identity and no `app` also fails, because `InstalledApp.app` has no honest value to return. Before, it returned the path. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Pixel_7_API_36 emulator, scratch project with `app: { appPath: '.build/android/benchmark.apk' }` and a test that runs `await device.installApp(); await app.open();` and then expects the home list. `dev.e2e.benchmark` was already installed and `ANDROID_HOME` was unset, the stress-test setup. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Android, no `ANDROID_HOME` | `installApp` resolves `{"app":"/.../benchmark.apk"}`, then `app.open()`: `ENGINE_FAILURE: open /.../benchmark.apk failed: Android runtime hints require an installed package name` | `installApp`: `ENGINE_FAILURE: installed /.../benchmark.apk, but agent-device reported no bundle id or package for it, so nothing can open it: name the app with the target's app.bundleId or installApp's app option` | | Android, `ANDROID_HOME` set (daemon restarted) | not run | `installApp resolved to {"app":"dev.e2e.benchmark","bundleId":"dev.e2e.benchmark"}`, `app.open()` launches, test passes | | iOS, `appPath` only, no `installApp()` | `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: app.open() has no app to launch on target "ios": pin one with the target's app.bundleId or app.appPath, or bring one up with device.openApp` | `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: launching the app needs the target's app.bundleId, or the build the target's app.appPath names installed first with device.installApp()` | | iOS, `appPath` only, `installApp()` then `app.open()` | not run | passes, resolves `dev.e2e.benchmark` | - Mobile benchmark locator suite on the Android emulator, branch build, `E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_ANDROID_APP` set: `54 passed | 1 skipped`. - No video: `--video` fails on this host with `start video recording failed: 4 devices match this request equally`, because iOS simulators were booted next to the emulator and the video start passes no device selection. That bug is on main too and out of scope here. ---

title: fix(init): let pnpm 11+ install the scaffold by skipping esbuild's build script
body:
`pnpm dlx e2e init` on pnpm 11+ scaffolds a project that cannot install: `e2e` depends on tsx, tsx on esbuild, and pnpm 11+ fails any install with an undecided build script (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: esbuild@0.28.2`). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI fails the same way. npm 11 only warns; bun is fine.

- esbuild's postinstall is not needed. It hard-links the CLI binary over the JS shim and prints the binary's version. tsx calls the JS API, and `lib/main.js` finds the binary in the `@esbuild/<platform>` optional dependency at run time. Checked: with the build skipped, tsx runs `.ts` files and the scaffolded example passes.
- So init records the build as skipped, not allowed: `allowBuilds: { esbuild: false }`. That is the least privilege and the shape `pnpm approve-builds` writes for a denied build. pnpm reads `allowBuilds` only from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (checked on pnpm 12.6: a `pnpm.allowBuilds` field in `package.json` still fails the install). pnpm 10.34 and 11.28 honor it too.
- Dropping tsx is not an option this close to the release: config and test loading run on its ESM API (`packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`).
- It runs only on pnpm 11+. The major comes from the `packageManager` pin, then the invoking agent (`pnpm dlx`), then `pnpm --version`. pnpm 10 only warns about ignored builds, and pnpm 9 and 10.2.1 refuse a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` without `packages` (`packages field missing or empty`), so older versions get no file.
- The new code is `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/pnpm-builds.ts`. It changes the nearest `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
  - missing: creates it
  - has no `allowBuilds`: appends the block
  - has a block `allowBuilds`: adds `esbuild: false`, keeping the file's indentation, comments, CRLF, and BOM
  - already sets esbuild to `true` or `false`, or has `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds: true`: leaves it alone
  - holds the placeholder a failed install leaves (`esbuild: set this to true or false`): sets it to `false`, so re-running init repairs a project main scaffolded
  - is a workspace root above the project, or has an inline `allowBuilds`: no edit, a warning naming the entry to add, and an outro that says the entry is still missing
  - names esbuild by version (`esbuild@0.25.0: true`) with no bare boolean: no edit, since pnpm lets a bare `esbuild: false` override a versioned `true`. The warning names the versioned entry to add (`esbuild@0.28.2: false`)
  - cannot be read: `invalid-project`, exit 2, before any write

```yaml
# e2e runs TypeScript through tsx, which calls esbuild's JavaScript API;
# that finds the esbuild binary without the build script, so pnpm skips it.
allowBuilds:
  esbuild: false
```

`pnpm dlx` still shows pnpm's own "Choose which packages to build" prompt while it fetches `e2e` into its cache. Enter (build nothing) works. That prompt is pnpm's and init cannot answer it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `pnpm pack` of every published package from main and from this branch, each set served by its own verdaccio (4410 main, 4411 branch; `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/*` not proxied). In a fresh `/tmp` dir, `pnpm dlx e2e init` (pnpm 12.6.0) with every prompt left at its default and Yes to install. Then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from an empty `node_modules`, then `APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4420 pnpm test:e2e` against a static page.
- Upgrade path: branch `pnpm dlx e2e init --yes` over main's failed scaffold changed the placeholder to `esbuild: false`, and install and run then passed.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile` on the branch's config installs clean, and esbuild is the only ignored build across web, mobile, and `ai`.
- Built CLI `init --yes` for each version: pnpm 12 writes the file and installs. pnpm 10.2.1 and 9 get no file and install (10 prints its ignored-builds warning). npm gets no file and installs.
- pnpm 12 installs every edited file shape the unit tests produce (placeholder, comment in block, BOM, 4-space indent).

title: fix(report)!: count interrupted tests apart from failures
body:
Interrupted tests were counted as failed in every output. Ctrl-C at 4s on the testbed printed `3 failed`, `summary.md` said `🔴 e2e: 3 failed` with 3 failure pages, and `report.json` had `summary.failed: 3`, all 3 of them interrupted. The report wire format freezes with the first stable release, so the count has to land now.

- `report.json`: `run.summary` gains `interrupted`. `failed` counts failed and timed out only (`packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts`, `computeSummary`). Schema, both fixtures, and a schema test change with it.
- `run.summary.skipped` counted the tests the selection left out (`--grep todo`: `skipped: 62` while the list said `7 passed (7)`). It now counts selected results only, so `passed + failed + interrupted + flaky + skipped = selected`, and the left-out tests are `discovered - selected`.
- `statusBucket` in `packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts` has an `interrupted` bucket, so every reporter counts it on its own:
  - `list`: `3 interrupted` in yellow in `Test Files` and `Tests` and on the file line. Interrupted tests are left out of `Failed Tests`.
  - `markdown`: the ⏹️ glyph, no failure block and no page under `failures/`. The headline is ⏹️ when the run was interrupted with no real failure, and 🔴 otherwise.
  - `junit`: `<skipped message="interrupted: ...">`, not `<error>`. JUnit has no interrupted outcome, and the test reached no verdict.
  - `@e2e-dev/github`: the `--last-failed` fold counts `interrupted`. A test that was interrupted and then passed reads as passed, not flaky. A test that failed and whose rerun was interrupted stays failed.
  - Telemetry gains `tests_interrupted`.
- Forced interrupt (two SIGINTs, which is what a GitHub Actions cancel sends as SIGINT then SIGTERM): `runReporters` abandoned every reporter, including the built-in `junit` and `markdown`. That left the previous run's `summary.md` and `junit.xml`, possibly green, beside the new `report.json`. Those two are no longer abandoned on force; the timeout still bounds them. Custom reporters are still abandoned (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`, `FILE_REPORTERS`).
- A test that failed and whose retry an interrupt cut short stays `failed` (`runWithRetries` in `packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts`), and every reporter tells the failed attempt, not the interrupted one. A serial group member keeps the verdict of the attempt before the interrupted retry (`packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts`).
- `--repeat-each`: a repeat the interrupt stopped or never started is listed as interrupted, not as a flake (`packages/e2e/src/report/repeats.ts`).
- The markdown headline shows ⏹️ whenever it lists an interrupted test with no failure, so a passing `--last-failed` rerun that carries a never-finished test does not read green.
- Exit codes are unchanged: 130 for an interrupt, 1 for `--max-failures`.
- Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` (summary counts, junit and markdown rows, signals), `reference/reporters.mdx`, `ci.mdx`, `github.mdx`, `telemetry.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/running.md`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed, built CLI, `e2e run --workers 8 --reporter list,markdown,junit`, sent SIGINT after 4s. Also `--workers 64` with SIGINT after 3s, `--config e2e.stress.config.ts --max-failures 2 --workers 4`, `--grep todo`, and a forced run: a green `tests/smoke.e2e.ts` run first, then the full run with two SIGINTs 20ms apart. Each was run on origin/main and on this branch.

SIGINT at 4s, `--workers 8`:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| list | `Tests  4 failed \| 48 passed \| 19 skipped (71)` | `Tests  3 interrupted \| 51 passed \| 17 skipped (71)` |
| `report.json` summary | `failed: 4`, all 4 results `interrupted` | `failed: 0, interrupted: 3` |
| `summary.md` | `### 🔴 e2e: 4 failed, 48 passed, 19 skipped` | `### ⏹️ e2e: 3 interrupted, 51 passed, 17 skipped` |
| `failures/` | 4 pages | none |
| `junit.xml` | `failures="0" errors="4" skipped="19"` | `failures="0" errors="0" skipped="20"`, each `<skipped message="interrupted: run interrupted in phase body"/>` |

`--max-failures 2 --workers 4` on the stress suite (2 real failures, 3 cut short):

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| list | `Tests  5 failed \| 4 passed \| 6 skipped (15)` | `Tests  2 failed \| 3 interrupted \| 4 passed \| 6 skipped (15)` |
| `summary.md` | `### 🔴 e2e: 5 failed, 4 passed, 6 skipped`, 5 pages | `### 🔴 e2e: 2 failed, 3 interrupted, 4 passed, 6 skipped`, 2 pages |
| exit | 1 | 1 |

`--grep todo`:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.json` summary | `selected: 7, passed: 7, skipped: 62` | `selected: 7, passed: 7, skipped: 0` (discovered 69) |

Forced interrupt after a green run:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stderr | `reporter "markdown" abandoned: the run was forced to stop`, same for `junit` | nothing |
| `summary.md` | stale: `### 🟢 e2e: 3 passed, 1 skipped` | fresh: `### ⏹️ e2e: 3 interrupted, 51 passed, 17 skipped` |
| `junit.xml` | stale: `tests="4"` | fresh: `tests="71"` |

Branch list output from the SIGINT run:

```text
interrupted: stopping the running test and tearing down (interrupt again to force)
 ❯  web  tests/controls.e2e.ts (15 tests | 1 interrupted | 11 skipped) 2.69s
   × controls > enabled state arrives late and every read agrees (interrupted) 180ms
   ↓ controls > check and uncheck move checked state, and one radio checks at a time [run interrupted before execution]
...
 Test Files  3 interrupted | 11 passed (14)
      Tests  3 interrupted | 51 passed | 17 skipped (71)
```

Failed first attempt, retry interrupted (`--retries 1`, SIGINT at 5s, a scratch test not committed): branch reports `failed: 1, interrupted: 0`, `### 🔴 e2e: 1 failed` with the `first attempt fails` block, junit `<failure message="first attempt fails" type="ERROR">`, exit 130.

New integration test `a forced interrupt still writes the junit and markdown files` (`runner-lifecycle.test.ts`) fails with the runner fix reverted: `expected '### 🟢 e2e: 3 passed\n'`.

# Releases
## @e2e-dev/eas@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- [#730](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/730) [`1554360`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1554360ba2b3d3aff5efeff443b16d8985a169ca) Thanks [@szdziedzic](https://github.com/szdziedzic)! - `easSimulators()` authenticates with the eas-cli login when `EXPO_TOKEN` is not set: it reads the session `eas login` keeps in `~/.expo/state.json` (under `USERPROFILE` on Windows) and sends it in the `expo-session` header, as eas-cli does, so a machine signed in to eas-cli needs no token. `EXPO_TOKEN` still wins when both are there. A session is stopped as the account that started it, even if the login changes during the run. Only the production login is read, since the sessions API is `api.expo.dev`. With neither a token nor a login, the lease fails with `EXPO_TOKEN is not set and eas-cli is not logged in`.

- [#731](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/731) [`88cef2c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/88cef2c26d0b095ce490e9f86c09221ce28d8fa9) Thanks [@szdziedzic](https://github.com/szdziedzic)! - `easSimulators()` takes `projectId` from the app config when the option is absent: `extra.eas.projectId`, the id `eas init` writes, read from `app.config.json` or `app.json` beside `e2e.config.ts`, or from a dynamic `app.config.ts` (or `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`) as the project's own `expo config --type public` evaluates it in the run's environment, without `.env` files, as eas-cli runs it. It reads the config once per run, before the first session starts; a config that links no project fails the lease naming the file. `projectId` is optional now and still wins when it is passed. Reading it needs the `@e2e-dev/mobile` that passes `projectRoot` to device providers.
## @e2e-dev/mobile@0.9.0

### Minor Changes

- [#731](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/731) [`88cef2c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/88cef2c26d0b095ce490e9f86c09221ce28d8fa9) Thanks [@szdziedzic](https://github.com/szdziedzic)! - A `DeviceProvider`'s `acquire` request carries `projectRoot`, the directory the config's relative paths resolve against, so a provider reads project files there instead of `process.cwd()`.

- [#740](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/740) [`bb904d4`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bb904d40d39d170a4ab38c4616552226bf77017f) Thanks [@NathanWalker](https://github.com/NathanWalker)! - `device.fold(pose)` puts a foldable iOS simulator (iPhone Duo) in a hinge pose: `'closed'` lights the outer display, `'half-open'` (a 130° book) and `'open'` the inner one. It runs agent-device's `fold` command, which sends the simulator's hinge event and reads the angle back from CoreDevice before it resolves, so the next observation reads the app on the other display. Like `setOrientation`, it counts as an action for the `transition` budget. A device without a hinge is `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, and Android is refused before any device command. The pose type is exported as `FoldPose`.
## e2e@0.15.2

### Patch Changes

- [#710](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/710) [`6b25a3a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6b25a3a4c8c8053151e6d323d0cc3079f1f6d90e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A failure where no model answered (`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`) no longer evicts replay cache entries. It says nothing about the app, so a read-write run without model access keeps every recording it did not confirm, including a step that replayed whole before an `agent.assert` that could not reach its model and a replay that handed off to the model mid-step, and still saves the steps verified before the failure.

- [#736](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/736) [`c9c3e14`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c9c3e14869f5ee50c97fc3b8fa9de3a527562f4d) Thanks [@programmrz](https://github.com/programmrz)! - Agent steps on DeepSeek's V4 models no longer fail on their first turn with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. In thinking mode, DeepSeek's default, the API refuses a forced tool choice with `Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice`; that refusal now reads as one, so the step retries with `auto` and the tool-calls-only rule, as it already did for Anthropic, and thinking can stay on.

- [#735](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/735) [`28b09f3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/28b09f3c1954d62ea14ee53fb280a9ff7da6297b) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e init` adds `zod` next to `ai` when it sets up a model gateway. `zod` is a peer of `ai` and every provider package; npm and pnpm install peers on their own, Yarn does not, so a Yarn project failed to load the generated config with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`. A Yarn project scaffolded with a model gateway before this fix needs `yarn add -D zod`.

- [#708](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/708) [`4ee772c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4ee772cc4ab800b1f2d4be4723bf28e2909b1edc) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The package ships the documentation pages: coding agents can read them offline from `node_modules/e2e/docs`.

- [#742](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/742) [`4f17480`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4f1748038014715b88942a366ec40461092f7683) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `expect(value).toBeDefined()` now passes on `null`, as it does in Playwright, Jest, and Vitest; only `undefined` fails it. It used to reject `null` too, so `expect(null).not.toBeDefined()` passed where Playwright fails. `expect.poll(read).toBeDefined()` follows: a read that returns `null` now passes on the first try instead of waiting. For the old non-nullish check, use `toEqual(expect.anything())`.

- [#739](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/739) [`8d38206`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/8d38206f460415b70706b45acb820bb0e24832ae) Thanks [@NathanWalker](https://github.com/NathanWalker)! - The agent loop handles providers that downgrade a forced tool choice instead of refusing it, as the AI SDK's Anthropic provider does for Claude models that reject forced tool use (Claude Sonnet 5.5 through `@ai-sdk/anthropic`). Such a request succeeds with `auto`, so the HTTP 400 path never ran: the loop kept asking for a forced choice, the SDK logged an `AI SDK Warning ... toolChoice` line on every turn, steps ran without the tool-calls-only instruction, and a turn the model answered in prose failed the step with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (the SDK's `ToolChoiceViolationError`). Now a `toolChoice` call warning switches the step to `auto` and gives its remaining turns the instruction, a prose answer under a forced choice is retried with `auto` like a refusal, and later steps on that model start in `auto`.
