body: Clears 4 open CodeQL alerts. No behavior change. - `packages/web/src/protected-app.ts:70` (#1, polynomial-redos): strip base64 padding with `/={1,2}$/` instead of `/=+$/`. Base64 pads with at most two `=`. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/report-junit.test.ts:8` (#2, redos): `XML_CHARS` matches code points with `/u` and a single class. No alternation left, and a lone surrogate still falls outside every range. - `packages/e2e/tests/integration/transformed-secrets.test.ts:23,49` (#4, #5, incomplete-sanitization): `replaceAll('\n', ' ')`, matching how `toHaveText` collapses every line break. The other 7 open alerts are false positives and get dismissed separately: - #3 reflected-xss in `oauth/callback-server.ts`: every value goes through `escapeHtml` in `renderPage`. - #6-#10 bad-code-sanitization in `closed-shadow.ts` / `label-selector.ts`: the `JSON.stringify` inputs are module constants, not user input. - #11 regex-injection in `internal/globs.ts`: every non-word char goes through `escapeRegexpChar`, and the source is the user's own CLI glob. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Fuzzed old vs new `XML_CHARS` on 200k random strings mixing BMP chars, lone high and low surrogates, valid pairs, and noncharacters: 0 mismatches. - Old vs new padding strip on 2000 base64 strings, lengths 0-8 (0, 1, and 2 `=`): 0 mismatches. - `report-junit` and `transformed-secrets` (real browser) pass, as do the `protected-app` unit tests. ---

title: fix(github): long marker fields keep a digest so distinct keys never share a comment
body: - `markerField` cut a long field to its first 200 encoded chars with no digest, so keys `android-<200 x>-A` and `-B` got the same marker and the second job overwrote the first job's comment. - A field over the limit now keeps a 183-char readable prefix (never cut inside a percent escape), then `#` and 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of the full value. `encodeURIComponent` always escapes `#`, so a short field can never read like a long one. Max stays 200 chars per field. - Short fields keep the exact marker they had, so comments already on open PRs are still found. A field already over 200 chars gets a new marker: one new comment after upgrading (noted in the changeset). - `findComment` matched with `body.includes(marker)`, so a reply quoting the marker counted as a match. It now takes only a comment whose first line is the marker, which is where the reporter has always written it (`\r\n` is tolerated for comments edited on the web). ```ts // packages/github/src/reporter.ts const digest = createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex').slice(0, MARKER_DIGEST_CHARS); const prefix = encoded.slice(0, MAX_MARKER_FIELD_CHARS - MARKER_DIGEST_CHARS - 1).replace(/%[0-9A-F]?$/, ''); return `${prefix}#${digest}`; ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the built e2e CLI with the real `github()` reporter against a local fake GitHub REST server (`GITHUB_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5401`). It made two sequential runs with keys `android-<200 x>-A` and `-B`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `GET, POST, GET, PATCH /comments/1`: 1 comment, B overwrote A | `GET, POST, GET, POST`: 2 comments | | `key=android-xxx...x -->` | `key=android-x...x#c979b70f80b6b575 -->` and `key=android-x...x#6ae6918f76a47dd9 -->` | - Backward compatibility, same fake server: main posted with `key=chromium`, then this branch rerun PATCHed that same comment 1. A long key run twice on this branch did POST, then PATCH on its own comment. - New unit tests fail on main (3 failures) and pass here: - two long keys sharing a 200-char prefix - a short key's marker stays byte-identical - the first-line match ignores a quoted marker, a marker buried later in the body, a longer marker, and a first line with trailing text ---

title: fix(config): refuse secrets or credentials sharing an override env var
body: - `envName` (`packages/e2e/src/config/secrets.ts:122`) uppercases a name and turns every character outside `A-Z0-9` into `_`. Two entries like `api-key` and `api_key` therefore both read `E2E_SECRET_API_KEY`, and `svc-a`/`svc_a` both read `E2E_USER_SVC_A_*`. Setting the variable to rotate one of them quietly replaced both. - `resolveSecrets` now groups the names in each namespace by the variable they read, before it reads any values. Any group with more than one entry fails with `INVALID_CONFIG`, whether or not the variable is set. The message names the entries and the variable, never a value. - Credentials and secrets are checked separately: their prefixes differ, so `credentials['svc-a']` and `secrets['svc-a']` can still coexist. Punctuation in names is still allowed. The engines' `targetName` env mapping in `packages/web/src/provider.ts` and `packages/mobile/src/bindings.ts` already appends a hash, so it does not have this problem. - Docs: `reference/environment.mdx`, `reference/config.mdx`, `authentication.mdx`, the `INVALID_CONFIG` row in `reference/errors.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/{setup,writing-tests}.md`. ```text ERROR configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config) secrets "api-key" and "api_key" share the override variable E2E_SECRET_API_KEY, so one value set there would replace all of them; rename all but one ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project at `/tmp/oskar-fix-secret-env-collisions`: the built CLI (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --no-cache`) running against a static page. The test fills `secrets['api-key']`, `secrets['api_key']`, `credentials['svc-a']` and `credentials['svc_a']` into four inputs, and the page reports whether each pair matches. All values are fresh random hex; "rotate" sets `E2E_SECRET_API_KEY` and `E2E_USER_SVC_A_PASSWORD`. No value appeared in the output or in `.e2e/`. - New unit tests in `tests/unit/config.test.ts` cover a collision in each namespace (with and without the variable set), groups of 3, providers, error text that leaves out values, and a control case with no collision. | config | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | colliding secrets + credentials, no env | exit 0, passes | exit 2, `INVALID_CONFIG` naming `"svc-a"` and `"svc_a"` | | colliding secrets + credentials, rotate | exit 1, page shows `keys same, passwords same` | exit 2, `INVALID_CONFIG` | | colliding secrets only, no env | exit 0, passes | exit 2, `INVALID_CONFIG` naming `"api-key"` and `"api_key"` | | colliding secrets only, rotate | exit 1, `keys same` | exit 2, `INVALID_CONFIG` | | control (`api-key-b`, `svc-b`), rotate | - | exit 0, passes (the rotation changes only its own entry) | ---

title: fix(security): allow only http(s) and about:blank on explicit navigation
body:
## Summary

- `view-source:file:///...` slipped past the `file:` / `data:` / `javascript:` denylist: `new URL()` reports the protocol as `view-source:`, and Chromium then renders the wrapped local file. `app.open`, `browser.goto`, and the agent/MCP `navigate` verb all go through `resolveNavigationUrl` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts`), so all three leaked file contents.
- Fix: `resolveNavigationUrl` now uses an allowlist and admits `http:`, `https:`, and the exact `about:blank`. A denylist can't cover browser wrapper and nested schemes (`view-source:`, `blob:`, `filesystem:`, `chrome:`, ...). WHATWG parsing already lowercases the scheme and strips whitespace and tabs, so case and padding tricks resolve to the denied scheme. A percent-encoded scheme is read as a relative path on the base.
- `about:blank` stays allowed because it loads no local or inline content and migrated suites use it. `about:blank#x`, `about:srcdoc`, and every other non-http(s) scheme are now `POLICY_DENIED` on explicit navigation. `setCookies` targets follow the same rule, and an `about:blank` cookie URL, which holds no cookie, is also `POLICY_DENIED` (`packages/web/src/browser.ts`).
- Mobile (`packages/mobile/src/links.ts`): device links legitimately use custom app schemes (`myapp://`), so it keeps a denylist, which now adds `view-source:`, `blob:`, and `filesystem:`. It stays a separate check because the web rule is now a different rule (an allowlist). Sharing it would also mean a new `e2e/engine` export, which would raise mobile's `e2e` peer floor.
- Docs and rule text: `AGENTS.md` security invariants, `SECURITY.md`, the `packages/web/src/observation.ts` frame comment, `security.mdx`, `reference/{app,web,config,errors,engine,mobile}.mdx`, `browser.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md` now describe the http(s)-only rule.

```ts
await app.open('view-source:file:///etc/passwd');
// main:   page renders /etc/passwd
// branch: POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: view-source:
```

## Tests

- `tests/unit/urls.test.ts`: each variant (`view-source:` file/http, upper case, leading spaces, tab/newline inside the scheme, `blob:`, `filesystem:`, `chrome:`, `chrome-extension:`, `devtools:`, `about:blank#x`, `about:blank?x`, `about:srcdoc`, `about:version`, `ftp:`, `ws:`, custom scheme) is denied with and without a base URL. Percent-encoded schemes stay paths. http(s) and exact `about:blank` controls still pass.
- `tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts`: `app.open` with `view-source:` (3 spellings), `blob:`, and `about:srcdoc`, plus `browser.goto('view-source:...')`, run against a real marker file in the project. All fail `POLICY_DENIED` before anything loads. `app.open` and `browser.goto` still admit `about:blank`. `setCookies` with `url: 'about:blank'` is `POLICY_DENIED`.
- `tests/integration/mcp-server.test.ts`: the MCP `navigate` verb refuses `view-source:file:`, `VIEW-SOURCE:http:`, and `about:srcdoc`.
- mobile `links`, `engine`, and `tools` unit tests: `openLink`, `openApp`, and `open_app` refuse the wrapper schemes.
- Reverting `urls.ts` to main fails 15 unit cases, the web-platform scheme test, and the MCP navigate tests.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Scratch project `/tmp/oskar-fix-nav-scheme-bypass` with a synthetic `marker.txt`, the real built CLI `e2e run` against a local http server, and a stdio MCP client that drives `e2e mcp --headless`.

| Input | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.open('view-source:file://…/marker.txt')` | page shows `marker-B63-SECRET-local-file` (leak) | `POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: view-source:` |
| `app.open('VIEW-SOURCE:file://…')` | leak | `POLICY_DENIED` (`view-source:`) |
| `app.open('  view-source:file://…')` | leak | `POLICY_DENIED` (`view-source:`) |
| `app.open('view-source:http://127.0.0.1:4901/')` | renders page source | `POLICY_DENIED` (`view-source:`) |
| `app.open('blob:http://…')` | `ENGINE_FAILURE net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (navigated) | `POLICY_DENIED` (`blob:`) |
| `app.open('filesystem:http://…')` | `ENGINE_FAILURE` (navigated) | `POLICY_DENIED` (`filesystem:`) |
| `app.open('chrome://version')` | `ENGINE_FAILURE net::ERR_INVALID_URL` (navigated) | `POLICY_DENIED` (`chrome:`) |
| `app.open('about:blank')` | passes | passes |
| `app.open('about:srcdoc')` | passes the denylist (not in the main run) | `POLICY_DENIED` (`about:`) |
| `app.open('file://…')` | `POLICY_DENIED` | `POLICY_DENIED` |
| `browser.goto('view-source:file://…')` | leak | `POLICY_DENIED` (`view-source:`) |
| control: `app.open('/')` + `browser.goto('http://…')` | passes | passes |
| MCP `navigate view-source:file://…` | `Navigated to view-source:file://…`, observe shows marker | `navigate … failed: POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: view-source:` |
| MCP `navigate /` | passes | passes |

- `pnpm check`, plus the `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile` test suites. The testbed (70 passed) and the web-benchmark (90 passed) ran on private ports.

title: fix(web): continue skips earlier routes, decisions take or reject Playwright options
body:
Four web routing bugs, all in `packages/web/src/browser.ts`.

- **`continue()` answered from an earlier route.** It called Playwright's `route.fallback()`, so a broad `fulfill` registered earlier answered instead of the network. It now calls `route.continue()`, which skips every other route. The site-header route (`web({ headers })`, `protected-app.ts`) was reached only through that chain, so `continue` now merges those headers itself, for the final URL's site only (`surface.siteHeaders`).
- **New `route.fallback()`** keeps the old chaining under Playwright's name. It takes no overrides: an overridden URL could take the gate header off-site.
- **Unsupported options were silently ignored.** `continue({ headers | url })`, `fulfill({ path | contentType })`, and `abort('failed')` all acted as if no argument was passed. New `route-options.ts` checks every key before the decision is taken:
  - `continue` now takes `url`, `method`, `headers`, and `postData`. `url` goes through `context.app.resolveUrl` (relative URLs resolve, `file:` is `POLICY_DENIED`) and must keep the request's scheme.
  - `fulfill` now takes `path` (relative to the project root, checked before deciding) and `contentType`. A `content-type` header wins over the type `json` or `path` would set.
  - Unknown keys go through `rejectUnknownOptions` from `e2e/engine` (#579), so the message matches the other browser options.
  - Any other key, two body sources, `abort(code)`, or `fallback(overrides)` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The request is aborted and the next step fails.
  - Header overrides follow the `web({ headers })` grammar (shared `headerProblem`): an invalid name or a control character is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
  - A Playwright decision call that throws after deciding now aborts the request instead of leaving it pending. Before, `fulfill({ json: 1n })` hung the page's fetch.
- **`waitForResponse` counted the body read against the match timeout.** Headers at 0ms with the body at 1200ms and `{ timeout: 500 }` gave `ACTION_FAILED`. The timeout now bounds only the match, as in Playwright. The body read still starts at once, and `text()`/`json()` wait for it on their own action budget, so an endless body fails as `ACTION_FAILED` instead of a test timeout.
- **`setCookies([{ url: '/' }])` threw `ENGINE_FAILURE`.** It discarded `resolveUrl`'s result and passed `/` to `addCookies`. It now sets the resolved URL, and still refuses an `about:blank` target (#722).

Routes still run newest first:

```ts
await browser.route('**/api/**', (route) => route.fulfill({ body: 'mock' }));
await browser.route('**/api/live', (route) => route.continue());   // network, mock skipped
await browser.route('**/api/chain', (route) => route.fallback());  // 'mock'
await browser.route('**/api/file', (route) => route.fulfill({ path: 'fixtures/quote.json' }));
```

Docs: `docs/reference/web.mdx` (routing, types, cookies), `docs/browser.mdx`, `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` (rows moved from missing to web only), `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. Compile-time assertions are in `packages/web/tests/types/routes.ts`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Ran the built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`) on a scratch project at `/tmp/oskar-fix-web-routing/proj` with `web({ headers: { 'x-gate': ... } })`, against a local server that counts hits per path and echoes requests. The same suite ran against main's `@e2e-dev/web` dist and this branch's.

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B53 earlier `fulfill`, later `continue()` | fail: `"earlier-mock"` | pass: `network-x` |
| `continue()` keeps the site gate header | pass | pass |
| `continue({ headers })` | fail: header missing | pass, gate header still added |
| `continue({ url: '/echo', method, postData })` | fail: original endpoint answered | pass, 0 hits on original |
| `continue({ url })` to another site | fail: original endpoint answered | pass, no gate header off-site |
| `continue({ url: 'file:///etc/hosts' })` | silently continued to the original | `POLICY_DENIED: forbidden URL scheme: file:` |
| `fulfill({ path })` / `fulfill({ contentType })` | fail: `["",null,null]` | pass: bytes, `application/json`, given type |
| `fulfill({ bodyy })` (typo) | passed silently with an empty body | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: route.fulfill options has no key "bodyy"; ...` |
| `fallback()` to the earlier route | fail: `Failed to fetch` (no such method) | pass: `earlier-mock` |
| B9 `waitForResponse` 500ms, body at 1200ms | `ACTION_FAILED: exceeded its timeout of 500ms` | pass, `text()` is `slow-body` |
| N53 `setCookies([{ url: '/' }])` | `ENGINE_FAILURE: addCookies: Invalid URL` | pass, cookie on `127.0.0.1` |

- New `packages/web/tests/integration/routes.test.ts` (27 cases) and 2 new cases in `wait-for-response.test.ts`. With main's `browser.ts`, `surface.ts`, and `protected-app.ts` swapped in, 25 of the 32 cases in the two files fail. On main, the non-JSON `json` case hangs until the 30s test timeout.
- Rebased on main after #722 (http(s) and `about:blank` navigation allowlist). On the rebased build, `continue({ url })` with `view-source:` or `data:` is `POLICY_DENIED`, and `about:blank` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (must keep the request's `http:` scheme). The repro suite gave the same results as the table. The `routes.test.ts` resolver fake now follows the allowlist, with cases for both.
- The testbed suite passed (70 passed, 1 skipped), run on a different port to avoid other local runs. The routing cases in `packages/e2e` `web-platform` and `web-url-patterns` passed (29). Did not run the web benchmark locally; CI runs it.

## Left open

- The configured `headers` reach an off-site redirect target. This also happens on main with no test route, because the site-header route's `fallback({ headers })` carries them onto redirects. It needs an owner decision on the invariant. See the escalated Devin and cubic threads.

title: fix(run): keep --last-failed reruns honest: failure-limit skips, carried debts, kept evidence
body:
Partial `--last-failed` reruns could go green on tests that never ran, forget a failed hook, and destroy the evidence the GitHub comment links to.

- **failure-limit skips rerun.** `failure-limit` joins the undelivered skip causes (`packages/e2e/src/run/last-run.ts`). Before this, `e2e run --max-failures 1 || e2e run --last-failed` reran only the failed test and exited 0.
- **Owed tests are carried.** A `--last-failed` rerun's report gets a new optional `run.carried` field (`report-v1.schema.json`, valid fixture, `sdk-types.ts`). It holds:
  - owed results the rerun did not run: left out by `--grep`, `--tag`, `--target`, `--agent`, or a positional;
  - the serial groups those results' attempts live on;
  - unresolved `beforeAll`/`afterAll` failures in their scope.

  `lastFailedIds` selects carried tests, so a test stays owed across consecutive partial reruns until one runs it. A hook failure resolves once a rerun runs any test in its scope without the hook failing. The rerun's own exit code and summary still count only what it ran.
- **The fold stays red.** `foldLastRun` (`packages/github/src/merge.ts`) shows carried rows in place of filtered ones and reads the previous run's carried rows as history. It appends carried hook errors and turns the page red while a carried test or hook failure is owed. A carried test the run before interrupted reached no verdict (#713), so it leaves the outcome alone and the page reads ⏹️, not red; the next `--last-failed` still runs it. Before, `...current.run` dropped the previous run's errors.
- **Evidence survives.** The rerun no longer wipes `artifacts/`:
  - it prunes the tree to the files the report it reruns names (`pruneArtifacts`, `reportArtifactPaths`);
  - it claims a fresh `artifacts/rerun-<n>/` (`claimRerunDir`, exclusive mkdir, numbered past any existing) and files its attempts there via `rerunDir` on the worker bootstrap;
  - no rerun attempt can overwrite `attempt-0` of the run it folds.

  A full run still clears everything and keeps the same paths.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R0[run: report 0] -->|--last-failed --grep B| R1[rerun-1: B ran, A carried + HOOK_FAILED]
  R1 -->|--last-failed| R2[rerun-2: A runs again]
  R0 -. artifacts kept .-> R1
  R1 -. artifacts kept .-> R2
```

Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` (`--last-failed`, `--output`), `reference/config.mdx`, `reference/reporters.mdx`, `ci.mdx` (the rerun no longer empties `artifacts/`, so one upload covers both steps), `github.mdx`, `debugging.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/running.md`.

Review findings fixed before opening (fresh-context reviewer):
- `--target`/`--agent` left no row, so owed tests on unselected targets or agents were dropped. They are now carried while the test is collected and the target still exists.
- A carried hook stayed carried after its scope reran and passed. It now resolves.
- A carried `failure-limit` skip left the fold green. Now anything carried turns the page red.
- An unneeded setup has no report row, so its failed `afterAll` debt was dropped. Existence is now checked against the run's collected test ids (Devin thread).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Scratch project `/tmp/oskar-fix-rerun-integrity` (rebuilt as `/tmp/oskar-724-repro` for the rebase) with the real built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`). An `api` project covers D7. A `web` project (`trace: 'on'`, `github()` reporter, faked `GITHUB_ACTIONS` env writing the job summary) has an `afterAll` that throws in A and a fixable B with screenshots.
- Each rerun's fold is `foldLastRun(report, previous)`. The "fold links" column re-hashes every artifact the folded page links and checks it against the report's `sha256`.

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D7: `run --max-failures 1`, then `FIX_T1=1 run --last-failed` | exit 0, 1 test ran, T2/T3 never ran | exit 1, all 3 ran (T2, T3 fail) |
| D7b: same, then `--last-failed --grep T1`, then `--last-failed` | exit 0, then `NO_TESTS` exit 2 | exit 0 with T2, T3 in `run.carried`, then exit 1 running T2, T3 |
| CI recipe `run \|\| FIX_B=1 run --last-failed`: fold links | 4 ok, 4 sha mismatch (overwritten), 2 missing (deleted) | 10 ok |
| CI recipe: first-run files after the rerun | 4 changed, 2 gone | unchanged; rerun files under `rerun-1/` |
| D6: `run`, then `FIX_B=1 run --last-failed --grep B`: job summary | `🟢 e2e: 1 flaky, 1 passed`, HOOK_FAILED lost, A's screenshot and trace gone | `🔴 e2e: 1 flaky, 1 passed` + `HOOK_FAILED (afterAll)`, all 10 links ok |
| D6: next `--last-failed` (hook still broken) | `NO_TESTS`, exit 2 | runs A, HOOK_FAILED, exit 1 |
| D6: `FIX_A=1 run --last-failed` | `NO_TESTS`, exit 2 | runs A, exit 0, nothing carried |
| Uncollected: `run`, break t2's import, `FIX_T1=1 run --last-failed tests/t1.e2e.ts`, fix t2, `run --last-failed` | (this PR before c4b0c69d) T2 dropped from `run.carried`, debt lost | T2 carried as failed, then the next `--last-failed` runs T2 |
| Interrupted carry (#713): SIGINT a run mid T4, then `FIX_T1=1 run --last-failed --grep T1`, then `run --last-failed` | n/a | rerun exit 0, T4 in `run.carried` as interrupted, fold `### ⏹️ e2e: 1 interrupted, 1 flaky` (status passed, exit 0), next `--last-failed` runs T4 |

New regression tests:
- unit: `tests/unit/last-run.test.ts`, `tests/unit/rerun-artifacts.test.ts`, the carried constraints in `tests/unit/schema-fixtures.test.ts`, and github `tests/unit/merge.test.ts`;
- integration: `runner-lifecycle.test.ts` (the failure limit and a filter carried across reruns, a hook carried until its scope runs, a test of a file a narrowed rerun could not import still carried) and `output.test.ts` (evidence kept byte for byte, `rerun-1/`, then `rerun-2/`, and a full run back at the root).

Re-run on the rebase onto main 7f9ee108 (after #713, #741, #727): every row above matches.

The new fold tests fail against main's `merge.ts`. Locally green: `pnpm check`, e2e (unit and integration), github, testbed, web-benchmark.

title: fix(expect): unawaited poll fails its own phase, slow first read counts toward negation window
body: Two timing bugs in assertion polling. ## Unawaited `expect.poll` (B58) - `expect.poll(...).toBe(...)` returned a promise the attempt never knew about. Without `await`, the test passed (exit 0 when it was the last test), and the poll's timeout rejected later. `strayRejection` then charged it to whichever test was running at that moment, or recorded it as `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` after the last test. - Each phase now owns the polls it starts through a `PollScope` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/poll-scope.ts`). The phases are the body (with fixtures and `beforeEach`), each `afterEach` hook or fixture teardown, and each `beforeAll`/`afterAll` hook. Ownership follows the async lineage (`AsyncLocalStorage`, shared through a `globalThis` slot so a test module's copy of `expect` reads the runner's context). A poll belongs to the phase that started it, not to whatever phase is running when it gets called. - When a phase returns with a poll still running, the poll is cancelled and the phase fails with `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` at the line of the call. This happens whether or not the poll would have passed, and it matches what an unawaited step does. A body that threw keeps its own error and gets this one under `secondaryErrors`. A suite hook reports it as `HOOK_FAILED`. - If work left running by a phase (a body past its timeout) starts a poll after that phase closed, the poll is cancelled before its first read and its rejection is marked abandoned. It never lands on the next test. - Fixture functions get a lineage that is handed to the teardown's scope when `use` is released. An awaited poll after `use` still works, and an unawaited one fails as `fixture "x" teardown`. - Polls are still not report steps. `runHook` (`packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts`) gives every hook and teardown its own scope. The abandoned-rejection set moved from `steps.ts` to `internal/abandoned.ts`, so steps and polls share it. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[expect.poll called] --> S{owning scope} S -- open --> R[runs, tracked] S -- closed --> C[cancelled before first read] R --> E{phase returns} E -- poll settled --> OK[nothing] E -- still running --> F[cancel + STEP_NOT_AWAITED on that phase] ``` ## Negation window with a slow first read (B41) - `pollCondition` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts`) computed `grace = min(1000, remaining)` before the first read, but started the "negation holding since" clock only after `evaluate()` returned. With a budget under 1 s and a slow first read, a negation that was true the whole time timed out. On a heavy page, `expect(screen.getByText('Loading')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 500 })` failed with `observed: no node`. - The window now starts when the read that first saw the negation was issued. A negation that held for the whole budget passes at the deadline on what it has seen, without a read past the deadline, where the engine's operations get a 1 ms budget. The protection the window exists for is unchanged: every pass needs the latest read to show the negation, and a positive read resets the window. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. Built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`) in scratch projects under `/tmp/oskar/fix-poll-drain-negation-timing/` (api target, and a web target on port 5201 serving N rows), with main built from `origin/main` 3a5651f6. | Scenario | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | only test: `expect.poll(() => false, { timeout: 100 }).toBe(true)` without await (api) | `✓` passed, exit 0 | `×` `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` at `alone.e2e.ts:3`, exit 1 | | same, web target | `✓` passed, exit 0 | `×` `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`, exit 1 | | unawaited poll (300 ms), then an innocent 600 ms test | poll test `✓`, innocent test `×` "timed out after 300 ms" | poll test `×` `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`, innocent test `✓` | | unawaited poll in `afterEach` / `beforeEach` / `afterAll`, then innocent test | owners `✓`, innocent test `×`, plus `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` blaming it | `afterEach` owner `×` (`the afterEach hook returned before...`), `beforeEach` owner `×`, `HOOK_FAILED (afterAll)` naming the hook, innocent test `✓` | | control: awaited failing poll | `×` `ASSERTION_FAILED` timed out after 100 ms | same | | control: awaited passing poll | `✓` | `✓` | | `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 500 })` on absent text, 3000 rows | `×` `observed: no node` | `✓` passed after 511 ms | | same, 20000 rows (first read ~570 ms) | `×` | `✓` passed after 567 ms | | control: `not.toBeVisible` on visible text, 500 ms | `×` | `×` | | `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 500 })` on absent text, light page | `✓` | `✓` passed after 502 ms | Regression tests: - `tests/unit/time.test.ts`: fake-timer cases for a slow first read (80 ms, then 10 ms) under 500 ms and 1500 ms budgets, fast reads (pass at the deadline, not before, with no read past it), and a positive read inside a short budget (still fails). Three of them fail on main's `time.ts`. - `tests/unit/expect-poll.test.ts`: scope close returns `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` at the call line, cancels the poll (reads stop), and marks the rejection abandoned, derived promises included. Also covered: a poll that would have passed, awaited polls close quietly, a poll started by a closed phase's leftover work is cancelled with zero reads and never joins the running phase, and the fixture lineage hand-over. - `tests/integration/expect-poll-scope.test.ts`: child-process workers covering body, body throw, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, fixture teardown (leaky and awaited), `afterAll`, `beforeAll`, and a timed-out body that polls while the next test runs. It checks that no later test is charged and no `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` appears. 6 of 9 cases fail on main. The timed-out-body case passes on main too, and guards against a poll joining the phase that is running when it is called. - Rebased onto main 7f9ee108 (after #726, #741, #713, #780). One conflict in `execute.ts`: #741 keeps only soft failures when the body skips; kept that, with the not-awaited list now spread (steps and polls). The "await every `expect.poll`" sentence followed the Goals section into `docs/goals.mdx`. Rerun on the rebased build vs main 7f9ee108: same results as the table; `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 500 })` passed after 501 / 510 / 556 ms at 0 / 3000 / 20000 rows (main fails at 3000 and 20000). With #726: `waitFor` `detached`/`hidden` (300 ms removal), and absent-frame `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 500 })` (503 ms, main 664 ms), `not.toBeAttached`, `toBeHidden`, `waitFor` pass the same as on main. - `pnpm check`, `pnpm --filter e2e run test` (3027 passed after rebase), `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run test` (462 passed), testbed (70 passed), web-benchmark (90 passed): green. ---

title: fix(expect): waitFor attached and detached, absence under a missing frame, toHaveProperty on primitives, toHaveURL ignoreCase
body:
## What and why

Rebuilt on top of #579, which landed the matcher option flags (`checked`, `enabled`, `visible`, `attached`), `ignoreCase` on the locator text matchers, and unknown-option refusal. This PR keeps only what #579 does not cover.

- `locator.waitFor` read every state except `'visible'` as `'hidden'`, so `'attached'`, `'detached'`, and typos passed at once on an absent node. It now supports Playwright's four states and refuses any other state, `null` included, or an unknown option key with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before resolving anything (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts`).
- Absence polls (`toBeHidden`, `toBeVisible({ visible: false })`, `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`, their negations, `waitFor` `detached`/`hidden`) waited for a frame missing from the document until the deadline. They now read it as zero matches: `tryRead(..., 'empty')` in `packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts`, used by `evaluableWithoutNode` specs in `expect/async.ts`.
- `toHaveProperty` reads a primitive on the path through its wrapper object, as Jest does, so `toHaveProperty('label.length', 3)` passes. `null`/`undefined` on the path are still absent (`packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts`).
- `expect(browser).toHaveURL` takes Playwright's `ignoreCase`. #579 refused it and listed it as missing. `urlMatches` in `e2e/engine` gets an optional fourth `ignoreCase` argument. `toHaveTitle` still refuses it (Playwright has no such option), and #579's integration test now checks that refusal in place of the `toHaveURL` one.
- Docs: `screen.mdx` (waitFor states), `expect.mdx` (zero-match forms, absent frames, `toHaveURL` options, `toHaveProperty` primitives), `engine.mdx` (`urlMatches`), migration rows (waitFor, `toHaveURL` ignoreCase), skill reference.

```ts
await screen.getByTestId('banner').waitFor({ state: 'attached' });
await screen.getByTestId('banner').waitFor({ state: 'atached' }); // INVALID_ARGUMENT
await expect(browser.frameLocator('#absent').getByRole('button')).toBeHidden(); // passes at once
await expect(browser).toHaveURL('/dashboard', { ignoreCase: true });
expect({ label: 'abc' }).toHaveProperty('label.length', 3);
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch project (web page on :6610: hidden node, a banner mounted and a spinner removed after 1200 ms) run through the built CLI against `origin/main` 84155791 (with #579) and against this branch. The 19 option cases from the original PR plus 3 absent-frame cases. Each asserts what Playwright 1.63 does (`pw-oracle.mjs`).
- main now: 8 of 22 fail. This branch: 22 of 22 pass. The 14 that pass on main are #579's cases (state flags, ignoreCase, unknown keys), so they are dropped from this PR.

| check | Playwright 1.63 | main now | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `waitFor({ state: 'attached' })` on banner mounted at 1200 ms | waits ~1.3 s, count 1 | returns in 18 ms, count 0 | waits 1.26 s, count 1 |
| `waitFor({ state: 'detached' })` on a hidden but attached node | times out | passes silently | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` |
| `waitFor({ state: 'atached' })` typo | throws | passes silently | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` |
| `waitFor({ state: 'detached' })` on spinner removed at 1200 ms | waits ~1.3 s | waits 1.27 s (as hidden) | waits 1.28 s |
| `expect(browser).toHaveURL('/dashboard', { ignoreCase })` on `/Dashboard` | passes | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | passes |
| `toHaveProperty('label.length', 3)` | passes | fails | passes |
| `toBeHidden`, `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`, `waitFor({ state: 'detached' })` under `frameLocator('#absent')` | pass | all three fail after 1 s | all pass, 443 ms total |

```
attached after 1264ms, count 1
OK(detached) threw LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator did not become detached: getByTestId("ghost")
OK(atached) threw INVALID_ARGUMENT: waitFor state must be one of attached, detached, visible, hidden, got "atached"
 ✓ |web| tests/frame.e2e.ts (3 tests) 443ms
 ✓ |web| tests/options.e2e.ts (19 tests) 7.91s
      Tests  22 passed (22)
```

- `pnpm check` passes. `e2e` unit tests: 2345 passed. `@e2e-dev/web` tests: 441 passed. The touched integration suites (`matcher-options`, `web-class-assertions`, `web-platform`, `scripted-polling`, `scripted-matchers`): 48 passed. `tests/unit/locator-wait-for.test.ts` covers each state with nodes added and removed after 1200 ms, plus the refusals.
- `pnpm test:testbed` (70 passed) and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` (90 passed) pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web`. `urlMatches` gains an optional argument, mobile does not use it.

title: fix(e2e): redact plain-string secret values in titles, labels, and agent input
body: A value registered in `config.secrets` (or a credential password) that a test passes as a plain string, not as a `secrets.get()` handle, leaked into model input, reports, and file names. Only error messages and observations masked it. `docs/security.mdx` promises every occurrence is redacted. ```ts test(`title holds ${process.env.KEY}`, async ({ app, agent }) => { await app.open(`/?token=${process.env.KEY}`); await agent.act(`inspect ${process.env.KEY}`, { params: { note: process.env.KEY } }); }); ``` On main the value showed up in: test title, `testId`, and step labels in `report.json`; list reporter output; junit testcase names; `summary.md`; the failure page file name; artifact directory names; the custom executor's `ctx.step.instruction` / `ctx.step.params`; the built-in agent's act prompt and judgment prompts; `agentContext`. ## What changed Redaction now happens once, at the place each piece of text is produced: - Titles: `collectModule` takes a title redactor and applies it as every `test` / `describe` title registers (`packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`). Every caller (runner collection, worker collection, `RealmManager`) passes `staticSecretLedger(config.allSecrets).redact`, a ledger of the static values built once per secrets map (`packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts`). Every process redacts the same way, so ids still match between the runner and its workers. Test ids, `--grep`, reporters, artifact dirs, and failure page names all come from the redacted title, so none of them needs its own fix. Titles are redacted before NFC normalization, and the 512-byte limit is checked again after redaction. Two titles in one file that differ only in a secret value raise the existing duplicate-title-path error. - Step labels: `StepRecorder.run` redacts the label before it records, publishes, or traces it (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`). Before a session opens, the attempt's redactor used to pass text through unchanged. It now falls back to the static values (`redactForSession`). The standalone (MCP) recorder had no redactor at all and now uses the same one. - Agent steps: `dispatchAgentStep` redacts the instruction and every string in the params (keys and values) before anything reads the spec (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts`). The executor, the built-in agent's prompt, the step label, the trace cache, and the ledger all get the same redacted step. Secret handles are already placeholders at this point, so `typeSecret` still fills the real value. - `unique()` templates follow their leaves: `redactParams` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act-validation.ts`) rewrites each template's pointer to the redacted keys and redacts its value too. A template with a secret in its key or value still slots into the cache key. - Judgments: `Invocation` redacts the system message and the built prompt (the repair text before its 2000-character cut). `agentContext` is redacted per step and per judgment against the live ledger, not once when the agent selection is cached. - Param keys: two keys of one object that redact to the same text are `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, not a silent overwrite. - `e2e explore`: the goal becomes the title, artifact name, report goal, and model context, and it is redacted once when the state is built (`packages/e2e/src/explore/index.ts`). - `--last-failed` after upgrading: a test whose title holds a secret gets a new id once, so the previous run's failure list does not match it. Out of scope, documented in "Where redaction stops": - A Playwright trace of a session no secret reached is kept as recorded, so a URL the test spelled a value into stays in the trace text. The exposure model decides this. - Titles are redacted at collection, before any provider runs, so a provider-returned value is not redacted from titles. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project (`/tmp/fix-plain-string-secret-redaction`) with a random 27-character static secret: a describe and test title holding it, `app.open('/?token=' + S)`, `getByText('missing ' + S)` (fails on purpose), `agent.act('inspect ' + S, { params: { note: S, ['key ' + S]: [S] } })` on a custom executor that dumps `ctx.step`, `console.log` / `console.error` of it, and a second test that types the secret through `secrets.get('probe')` + `typeSecret` and checks the server got the real value. Ran with the built CLI, `node dist/cli/bin.js run --reporter list,junit,markdown`, then grepped every output file and file name for the value. | surface | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | CLI list output (stdout lines with the value) | 6 | 0 | | executor `ctx.step` dump | instruction, params, keys, agentContext | all `` | | files under `.e2e` containing it | `report.json`, `junit.xml`, `summary.md`, failure page | none | | paths under `.e2e` containing it | 10 (artifact dirs, failure page name) | 0 | | failing assertion error message | masked | masked | | `typeSecret` through the handle | passes | passes | - New integration test `packages/e2e/tests/integration/plain-string-secrets.test.ts` (worker path plus the built-in agent in-process) fails 4 of 5 on main; the handle-typing control passes on both. The new explore and `redactParams` tests fail on main too. ---

title: fix(web): read visibility as rendered, null box, checkable values, embedded names
body:
Web reads now report what renders, Playwright's way, and keep accessibility-tree exclusion separate. Fixes bug bash B51, B52, N46, N48, N49.

- **Render visibility vs a11y exclusion** (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`): `isHidden` (`states.hidden`, so `toBeVisible`/`toBeHidden`/`isVisible`/`waitFor`/`visible: true`) no longer treats `aria-hidden` as hidden. A decorative spinner marked `aria-hidden` stays visible until it leaves. `hidesSubtree` still drops `aria-hidden` and inert subtrees from the agent's observation, and role queries still skip them.
- **`content-visibility: hidden`**: content under it (slotted content included) reads hidden. The element keeps its own box. The tree walk does not descend into it, and the element reports none of its own text, which matches its `innerText`.
- **N46**: text directly under a `display: contents; visibility: hidden` element reads hidden. It paints nothing, but Playwright calls it visible, so this is a deliberate difference, written down in the docs.
- **N49**: `visibility: hidden` no longer prunes the whole subtree in the tree walk, because a child can set `visibility: visible` and paint again. `display: none` still prunes.
- **`visible: true` narrowing**: a new selector engine `e2e-shown` (`packages/web/src/shown-selector.ts`) runs the reader's own `hidden` check inside Playwright's chain. It replaces `filter({ visible: true })` plus the old `:not([aria-hidden])` step, so `first()`, filters, and scopes agree with `toBeVisible()` by construction.
- **B52**:
  - `rect` is `null` when the element has no layout box. `boundingBox()` on a `display: none` node therefore returns `null`, matching Playwright, not `{0,0,0,0}`.
  - A checkbox or radio now reports its DOM `value` (`on` by default) in a locator read, whatever its checked state. The observation tree still leaves that value out, as it does for an option's.
  - `getByDisplayValue` no longer treats checkboxes and radios as candidates.
- **N48**: an embedded control now adds to an accessible name the way Playwright's role selector reads it:
  - a textbox or searchbox adds its value
  - a select or listbox adds its selected options
  - a range widget adds `aria-valuetext`, else `aria-valuenow`, else its `value`

  A secure field adds nothing. Label text, which `getByLabel` matches, still leaves values out. 9 axe-core conformance cases now agree and were removed from `tests/conformance/expected.txt`.
- **Docs**: `docs/reference/screen.mdx` now covers visibility semantics, a `null` box, and checkable values. A row in `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` now says `selectOption('x')` matches the label only, where Playwright matches the value or the label; the table had said "same". The skill text and a changeset are updated too.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The scratch project `/tmp/oskar-fix-web-visibility-reads/` runs the real built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --reporter list`) against a static server. `main` uses an `@e2e-dev/web` dist built from `origin/main`; the branch uses this branch's dist.

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B51 `toBeHidden` on an `aria-hidden` spinner that is removed after 900ms | `isVisible()` is false on the rendered spinner, so `toBeHidden` passes at once | passes after 959ms, count 0 |
| B51 button under `content-visibility: hidden`, `toBeHidden` | fails: observed visible | passes |
| B52 `boundingBox()` on `display: none` | `{"x":0,"y":0,"width":0,"height":0}` | `null` |
| B52 checkbox `inputValue()` / `toHaveValue('on')`, radio `toHaveValue('monthly')` | `""`, "not a form control" | `on`, passes |
| N46 `display: contents; visibility: hidden` text, `toBeHidden` | fails: observed visible | passes |
| N48 `toHaveAccessibleName('Flash the screen 3 times')` | `"Flash the screen times"` | passes, and `getByRole` finds it |
| `getByText('Save', { visible: true }).first()` with a hidden `display: contents` twin first | picks the invisible twin | picks the button |
| N49 agent observation (`e2e mcp`, `observe`) | `button "Child visible"` missing | listed |

The observation through `e2e mcp` on the same page:

```text
main:
 #n6004 text="Invisible text" testid="dc"
 #n6005 button "Flash the screen times" testid="flash"
  #n6006 textbox value="3"
 #n6007 text="Plan"
branch:
 #n6004 button "Flash the screen 3 times" text="Flash the screen times" testid="flash"
  #n6005 textbox value="3"
 #n6006 button "Child visible" testid="vischild"
 #n6007 text="Plan"
```

Tests in `packages/web/tests/integration/` check each case against Playwright as the oracle (`isHidden()`, `boundingBox()`, `inputValue()`, `getByRole({ name, exact })`): `visibility.test.ts`, `read-node-names.test.ts`, `read-node-checked.test.ts`, `lifecycle.test.ts`. Run against main's `src`, 12 of them fail. Also run:

- `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:testbed`, `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: all pass.
- Crosscheck against the benchmark (`CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL`): passes. `crosscheck/expected.txt` is unchanged.
- Web-benchmark `test:agent` replay: identical on main and this branch (`25 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed`, same 7 failures). The 7 come from no local `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, so no committed recording changes.

title: fix(e2e): keep secrets out of observed node fields and collapsed cuts
body:
Registered secrets leaked into model input and `.e2e/cache` entries through two holes:

- **B46**: `formatNode` printed `testid` raw, and `projectTree` passed `framePath` (an iframe `name`) through raw. Selectors and attribute keys were also never redacted.
- **B34/B44/B47**: an engine collapses whitespace, then cuts name at 256 and text at 512. `redactCut` only compared the cut against the value as written, so a secret like `letters\nletters` left a plaintext prefix of its collapsed form in observation text, the executor tree, and cache `endAnchors`.

## Fix

- `redactNode` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts`) runs once in `prepareObservation` and redacts every field of `SemanticNode`. It is driven by `NODE_FIELDS`, a mapped type with one entry per contract field, so a new field does not compile until it says how it is redacted. Keys that are not in the contract are dropped.
- `formatNode` and `projectTree` now take a branded `RedactedNode` and no `redact` argument, so a raw node no longer type-checks there. MCP `locate` and failure evidence go through the same path.
- Each string field is redacted as written and in its `collapseText` form. If only the collapsed form holds a secret, the field is stored collapsed and masked.
- `redactCut` and `redactFragments` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts` now compare on `readingKey`: case-folded, with each whitespace run read as one space, plus an index map back to the original text. This catches cut and fragment forms after LF, tab, CRLF, NBSP, or repeated spaces.
- Descriptors, end anchors, and relocation (`describeTarget`, `containerKey`, `describeNodes`, `relocateDescriptor`, `describePosition`, `describeAnchors`, `anchorsPresent`) take only `RedactedNode` and lose their own weaker redact pass, which redacted before collapsing and never applied `redactCut`. `ReplayHost.redact` goes with it.
- `readingKey` returns the text as-is when it has nothing to collapse. Otherwise it builds the key in typed arrays and keeps one offset pair per collapsed run, so a large trace text stays cheap. On a 22 MB newline-heavy text with one secret, main uses 98 MB, a naive per-unit map 954 MB, and this branch 262 MB.
- Before anchors are derived, the start capture is redacted again with the current ledger (`redactNodesAgain`). Otherwise a provider secret resolved mid-step would make an unchanged node look new.
- `describeAction` redacts each acted-on node again with the current ledger for the same reason, so a secret resolved inside the action (a provider-backed `typeSecret`) is masked in the recorded descriptor and summary, as main's `describeTarget(node, redact)` did.
- The container key an action sat `within` is redacted again with the current ledger too, as main's `containerKey(..., redact)` did at placement time.
- `docs/security.mdx`: the claim that cache entries are secret-free now holds. "Where redaction stops" no longer lists whitespace-collapsed cuts.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Real CLI with a deterministic `StepExecutor` in a scratch project (`/tmp/oskar-fix-observation-secret-leaks/proj-*`). A page with a secret `data-testid`, a secret iframe `name`, and six variants of a whitespace secret (letters plus LF, tab, CRLF, NBSP, or 3 spaces; hex plus LF), each padded so it is cut at 256 and 512.
- Two runs (record, then replay). A scan of the executor's `observe({ tree: true })` dumps, `.e2e/cache/*.json`, and the reports, looking for the raw value, its collapsed form, its first 24 chars, and a 30-char collapsed prefix.

| surface | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| observation text | probe raw; prefixes of all 6 whitespace variants | clean |
| executor tree | probe raw; prefixes of all 6 whitespace variants | clean |
| `.e2e/cache` entry (`endAnchors`) | prefixes of 5 whitespace variants | clean |
| report / junit / summary | clean | clean |
| replay | replayed | replayed (anchors still match) |

- New regression tests fail on main and pass here:
  - `secret-ledger.test.ts`: 16 of 86 fail on main. Covers LF, tab, CRLF, NBSP, repeated spaces, and hex, with the cut in the first part, on the collapsed space, or in the second part, plus fragments.
  - `agent-observation.test.ts`: every field redacted; cut at the 256/512 limits across text, tree, and anchors.
  - `trace-recorder.test.ts`: a secret registered after the node was captured is masked in the recorded target.
  - `agent-policy.test.ts` security invariant: a full record and replay run through the fake engine, asserting no value or fragment reaches observations, the cache file, or the report. It fails on main.
- Cost:

| measure | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepareObservation`, 5000 nodes | 8.7 ms | 18.8 ms |
| `redactFragments`, 22 MB text, single spaces | 668 ms / +98 MB | 590 ms / +98 MB |
| `redactFragments`, 22 MB text, newlines + indent | 709 ms / +98 MB | 746 ms / +262 MB |

  A size and memory regression test sits beside the linear-scan test in `secret-ledger.test.ts`.

title: feat(eas): authenticate with the eas-cli login when EXPO_TOKEN is not set
body:
`easSimulators()` falls back to the eas-cli login when `EXPO_TOKEN` is not set, so a machine where you ran `eas login` needs no access token. CI keeps using `EXPO_TOKEN`. - Same precedence as eas-cli's `SessionManager`: `EXPO_TOKEN` first, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; else `auth.sessionSecret` from `~/.expo/state.json`, sent as the `expo-session` header (`packages/eas/src/credentials.ts`, `packages/eas/src/client.ts`). - The home is the run's `USERPROFILE` on Windows and `HOME` elsewhere, then `os.homedir()`, which is where eas-cli writes the file. - Only the production login is read. eas-cli's `EXPO_STAGING` and `EXPO_LOCAL` logins belong to other API hosts, and the provider always calls `api.expo.dev`. - `release` stops each session with the client that created it (`packages/eas/src/provider.ts`). Before, it re-read the credential at the end of the run; with a file as the source, an `eas logout` or account switch mid-run would have left the session billed until its idle limit. - With neither credential, the lease fails with ``EXPO_TOKEN is not set and eas-cli is not logged in; run `eas login` or set EXPO_TOKEN``. A `state.json` that is not JSON fails with its path and without the parse error as cause, since that error quotes the text around the fault. - Docs: an "Authenticate" section in `integrations/eas.mdx`, `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` in `reference/environment.mdx`, the Expo API under "Outbound connections" in `security.mdx` with a note to set `EXPO_TOKEN` on CI runners, the package README, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. Minor changeset for `@e2e-dev/eas`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[acquire] --> B{EXPO_TOKEN set?} B -- yes --> C[Authorization: Bearer] B -- no --> D{"~/.expo/state.json
auth.sessionSecret?"} D -- yes --> E[expo-session header] D -- no --> F[lease fails: run eas login or set EXPO_TOKEN] C --> G[client kept per lease] E --> G G --> H[release stops with the same client] ``` Open question for reviewers: the provider now reads a credential file from the home directory without an opt-in, as eas-cli and Expo CLI do. If you would rather gate it behind an option (for example `auth: 'eas-cli'`), I can change it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Surface: this branch's `@e2e-dev/eas`, packed with `pnpm pack` and installed beside `e2e@0.15.1` and `@e2e-dev/mobile@0.8.1` in an Expo app with an EAS iOS simulator build. `e2e run` with `EXPO_TOKEN` unset and only an `eas login` session on the machine. - EAS created, leased, and released a real session, and the test ran on it: ```text ℹ leasing 1 ios device(s) from eas-simulators ℹ eas-simulators (1 of 1): simulator session 01a0f7d5-…, https://expo.dev/accounts/…/simulator-sessions/01a0f7d5-… ℹ eas-simulators: leased 01a0f7d5-… ✓ mobile engine for target "ios" prepared 108.57s ✓ landing opens the menu 8.85s ℹ eas-simulators: released 1 device(s) Tests 1 passed (1) ``` - `eas simulator:list` afterwards shows that session as `STOPPED`, so the release reached EAS with the stored login. - Failure path, the same project with `HOME` pointed at an empty directory. No session is created: ```text ℹ leasing 1 ios device(s) from eas-simulators ERROR infrastructure error ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) device provider "eas-simulators" could not lease a device: EXPO_TOKEN is not set and eas-cli is not logged in; run `eas login` or set EXPO_TOKEN while preparing engine mobile for target "ios" ``` - Not run live: `EXPO_TOKEN` winning over a stored login and the logout-during-run release. The unit tests in `packages/eas/tests/unit/eas.test.ts` cover both against the stubbed API, with a temporary home (`HOME` and `USERPROFILE`) so no test reads the real `~/.expo`. The release test fails when the per-lease client is removed. - Not verified on Windows. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(eas): read projectId from the app config when easSimulators() names none
body:
`easSimulators()` no longer needs `projectId`. When it is absent, the provider takes `extra.eas.projectId` from the app config, the id `eas init` writes, so most Expo projects configure it as: ```ts device: easSimulators({ buildId: process.env.EAS_BUILD_ID }), ``` - Static `app.json` / `app.config.json` are read as JSON, from under `expo` when that key exists (`packages/eas/src/project.ts`). - A dynamic `app.config.*` is evaluated by the project's own `expo config --json --type public` with `EXPO_NO_DOTENV=1`, the way eas-cli's `getExpoConfigInternalAsync` runs it. A `.env` file never picks the project. - The `expo` CLI is found by walking up the project's `node_modules`. `require.resolve` also searches `NODE_PATH`, which pnpm points at its whole store, and there it found some other project's `expo`. - One read per run and project root, shared by every slot and every `easSimulators()` target of the run. A failed read is not kept, so `eas init` and a rerun fixes it in a long-lived process. - `projectId` still wins. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[acquire] --> B{projectId option?} B -- yes --> S[create session] B -- no --> C{app.config.ts/js/...?} C -- yes --> D["expo config --json --type public
EXPO_NO_DOTENV=1"] --> E[extra.eas.projectId] C -- no --> F[app.config.json or app.json] --> E E --> S ``` `@e2e-dev/mobile` now passes `projectRoot` on `DeviceRequest` (`packages/mobile/src/provider.ts`), so a provider reads project files from the config's directory and not `process.cwd()`. Peer range: `@e2e-dev/eas` keeps `@e2e-dev/mobile >=0.8.0 <1`. A mobile from before this change sends no `projectRoot`. With `projectId` passed that is fine. Without it the lease fails with "needs an @e2e-dev/mobile that passes `projectRoot` to device providers; upgrade it, or pass `projectId`" instead of a `path` TypeError. I left the floor alone because `restore-peer-ranges.ts` owns those ranges; happy to raise it to the mobile version this ships in if you prefer. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/eas` from this branch's stack into a scratch copy of an Expo app (expo-enterprise/eas-sim-demo-app, SDK 57) whose `e2e.config.ts` has no `projectId`, and ran one test on a real EAS simulator. The session was created in the project `app.json` links, and released at the end: ```text ℹ leasing 1 ios device(s) from eas-simulators ℹ eas-simulators (1 of 1): simulator session 01a0f7d6-cca7-7692-b894-a029a166dd82, https://expo.dev/accounts/expo-enterprise/projects/eas-sim-demo-app/simulator-sessions/01a0f7d6-cca7-7692-b894-a029a166dd82 ℹ eas-simulators: leased 01a0f7d6-cca7-7692-b894-a029a166dd82 ✓ mobile engine for target "ios" prepared 97.73s ℹ eas-simulators: released 1 device(s) ``` The test itself failed on an app assertion (the build opens on its Cart tab), which is that app's test, not the provider. It ran with `EXPO_TOKEN` unset, so it also authenticated with the eas-cli login from tester-army/e2e#730, which this branch now sits on. - The built provider with `fetch` stubbed, against real configs and the real SDK 57 `expo` CLI: | Config | `appId` sent | | --- | --- | | `app.json` of the app above | `406cbecc-67d9-4b4b-a948-821e5444a947`, 2 ms | | `app.config.ts` reading `KAWA_PROJECT_ID` from the run's env | `dyn-1234`, about 4 s | | same, variable only in `.env` | lease fails: `app.config.ts (through \`expo config\`) has no \`extra.eas.projectId\`` (plain `expo config` there prints `from-dotenv`) | | no config | lease fails: `no Expo app config (app.json or app.config.*) in /tmp; pass \`projectId\` ...` | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cache): stop replays self-finalizing when the effect did not happen
body:
The replay cache could self-finalize an `agent.act` step with zero executor calls on a screen where the step's effect never happened, or for the wrong persona, query, or origin. A deterministic drift probe reproduced 14 such false passes on main. This branch fixes all of them in `packages/e2e/src/cache/*` and the key plumbing, and the replay now hands off to the executor in each case. ## What changed **Key identity** (`cache/identity.ts`, `cache/context.ts`, `agent/act.ts`) - The key now holds the configured agent name and `agentContextDigest`, a SHA-256 of the agent's redacted context (`context`, then the test's `agentContext`). A registered secret in the context contributes only its name. One persona no longer replays another's recording (B22), and changing `agentContext` causes a miss (B16). - The occurrence index counts per agent and signature, so another agent's call of the same instruction doesn't renumber this one's. - The executor stays out of the key and is kept as provenance. The OQ10 note is removed. **Route identity** (`cache/route.ts`, `cache/decide.ts`) - A route is now origin + path + query. A location on the app's own origin is compared as its path (`appLocation`), so a preview deployment that shares `app.identity` still replays. A page on another origin is a different route (B26). - Query values that look minted are read as `:id`, using the same rules path segments already use: digits, hex, uuids, long mixed tokens, prefixed record ids (`INV-2041`, from #777), whitespace, plus signed tokens, ISO timestamps, and dates. Every other value is part of the route: `?mode=safe` and `?mode=unsafe` are different screens (B21). - The end route must now match exactly, on every look the end wait takes. `undecided` is gone, so a link that lands on a lookalike page hands off (B30). - Locations are kept whole up to 4,096 characters. Longer ones poison the trace instead of being cut. **Anchors: the recorded delta** (`cache/anchors.ts`, `cache/trace.ts`, `agent/step-cache.ts`) - New `goneAnchors`: nodes the step made vanish. They must be gone again on replay (B20). - Anchors record `checked`, `expanded`, `pressed`, and `selected` states, plus a field's input value (redacted, never for a secure field). A switch turned on is no longer the same anchor as the switch left off (B27). - Announcements (`status`, `alert`, `alertdialog`) sort first, so the cap of 8 no longer drops the line that names the outcome (B23). - An `alert` raised during the replay that the recording never saw fails the end check (B24). Volatile parts of an alert's text are read as placeholders. - A count phrase is part of the effect when the step made it appear on the screen it acted on (B25, `3 records imported` vs `0`). It is still treated as volatile when it only moved, or when it sits on a page the step navigated to. - Evidence rule: at least one recorded change must happen during the replay. It is measured from the first screen the replay saw on its end route (B29: a status that already read `Submitted`). A field's value or a switch the step itself set counts only when nothing else changed. Before a free action (navigate, typed text, key), the replay looks at the screen until it reaches the end route, so the baseline exists. - A step with no observable delta and no route move is not recorded. If an entry was read for that step, it is evicted. **Unnamed controls** (`agent/actions.ts`, `cache/relocate.ts`, `cache/recorder.ts`) - When a row has no other text, its own label (`
  • Alpha
    • `) becomes the row key (B19). - An unnamed control among twins needs a named nearest row, list item, or group. Without one, the trace is marked `truncated` instead of replaying by order. ```mermaid flowchart TD R[replayed every action] --> E{end route same?
    origin, path, query} E -- no --> H[end-mismatch: hand off] E -- yes --> V{recorded change happened
    since first screen on end route?} V -- no --> H V -- yes --> D{appeared present, gone absent,
    states and values equal,
    no unseen alert} D -- no --> H D -- yes --> S[self-finalized] ``` `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` is bumped to `conservative/6`. Every existing entry re-keys and records again on the first run after the upgrade. Oskar accepted this. ## Committed recordings All 29 entries in `apps/web-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` and all 39 in `apps/mobile-benchmark/.e2e/cache/` are now unreadable (`no-entry`). I could not re-record them: this machine has no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and no `e2e login`. Until someone re-records them, the `web agent` job runs every step live under `--strict-cache`. A `no-entry` step is not stale, so the job should still pass, but it spends model calls. To re-record: `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web-benchmark test:agent` after `e2e cache clear`, then the mobile benchmark's `test:agent` on an iOS simulator, and commit the new entries. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Drift probe: a scratch http fixture where `PROBE_MODE=record|drift` changes the screen under each recording, and a deterministic `StepExecutor` that logs every call. For each case: record, then a drift run in read-write, `--strict-cache`, and `--no-cache`, reading `result.cache` and the fixture's own state log. Probe files live outside the repo and are not committed. - `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:testbed`, and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` all pass. - Rebased onto main `4ce01b29` (after #729, #725, #723, #784, #785, #779). #729 made every observed node a `RedactedNode`; the anchor delta now reads only those: an anchor's `value` is the node's already-redacted value (a secure field has none), `states` are booleans, and no local redact pass came back. The start capture (on record) and the replay's baseline and start captures (on replay) are redacted again with the ledger as it is now before the delta is derived or checked, and `redactNodesAgain` now relinks children so the gone side keeps its leaves-before-containers order. Checks and suites pass again, and the drift probe table below is identical on the rebased build. - Secret in an anchor: a `secrets` entry filled by `typeSecret` into a plain text field records the anchor as `value: ""` (and the echo as `Stored `), replays self-finalized, and no file under `.e2e` holds the plaintext. Drift run, main vs this branch. "Calls" counts executor calls for the step; "state" is what the fixture saw. | ID | Drift | main | this branch | `--no-cache` (reference) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | B16 | `agentContext` Monthly -> Daily | self-finalized, 0 calls, picked Monthly (test fails) | missed `no-entry`, 1 call, picked Daily (passes) | 1 call, Daily | | B22 | `agent: ['buyer','admin']`, admin refuses | admin self-finalized buyer's flow, approved | admin `no-entry`, 1 call, refuses | admin refuses | | B21 | `?mode=safe` -> `?mode=unsafe` | self-finalized, ran task in unsafe mode | `wrong-context`, executor refuses | refuses | | B26 | absolute URL on another origin | self-finalized on `localhost` | `wrong-context`, 1 call | 1 call | | B26 | preview URL, same `app.identity` | self-finalized | self-finalized (kept) | - | | B20 | delete is a no-op | self-finalized, Item A still there | `end-mismatch`, handed off | 1 call | | B19 | unnamed row buttons, rows reordered | self-finalized, marked Beta | self-finalized, marked Alpha | Alpha | | B23 | 10 rows + status `Report failed` | self-finalized | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B24 | `Payment saved` + alert `Card declined` | self-finalized | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B25 | `3 records imported` -> `0` | self-finalized | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B27 | switch click prevented | self-finalized, switch off | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B29 | status already `Submitted`, submit no-op | self-finalized | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B30 | link now goes to a lookalike `/profile` | self-finalized on `/profile` | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B31 | alert container after rows | `end-mismatch` (did not reproduce) | `end-mismatch` | 1 call | | B28 | row `Record 1` now links to `/records/2` | self-finalized, opened 2 | self-finalized, opened 2 | opened 2 | Under `--strict-cache` on the branch, every drifted ID above fails with `REPLAY_STALE` and 0 calls. On main every one self-finalized except B31. A record-then-replay run with no drift self-finalizes all 16 probe steps on both builds. The one exception is the branch's B22 admin step, whose refusal never confirms a recording. B28 is not a cache bug. Record ids are `:id` by design, and the live executor, given the same instruction, opens the same record (the `--no-cache` column). ## Behavior worth reviewing - A query value the recording did not have (`?tab=notes`, a tracking parameter) is now a miss. A slug that differs at the end (`/products/summer-sneaker` -> `/products/winter-boot`) now hands off instead of letting anchors decide. - A step with nothing to check never replays: a lone password fill, or a page-and-back round trip (`agent-act-verbs.test.ts`, `trace-secrets.test.ts`). - Integration fixtures pick their variant through `FixtureApp.setVariant` instead of `?variant=`, since the query is now part of the screen. - The evidence rule asks for at least one change rather than every change. Transient UI left by earlier steps (a toast fading, lazily loaded widgets) would otherwise hand off every run.

title: docs: agent prompt quickstart, why-e2e intro, separate API testing page
body: Introduction and Quickstart were almost the same page. Now the intro covers what e2e is and why to use it, and the quickstart opens with a prompt for your coding agent. - `docs/index.mdx`: you pick how agentic a test is (all locators, all agent, or a mix). title: docs(migrate): toBeDefined and toContain differ from Playwright
body: ## What and why - The "From Playwright" table listed `toContain()` as "the same" and said nothing about `toBeDefined()`. Both differ from Playwright, and #691 asks for the difference to be documented. - `toBeDefined()` rejects `null`; Playwright's passes it. - `toContain()` on a collection compares items by deep equality, so `toContain({ id: 1 })` passes on `[{ id: 1 }]`; Playwright's strict match fails it. String containment is unchanged. - Docs only. Behavior is unchanged and is already pinned by `packages/e2e/tests/unit/expect-values.test.ts`. This does not touch the `toBeDefined(null)` alignment proposal in #691, which stays a maintainer decision. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `@playwright/test` 1.63.0: `expect(null).toBeDefined()` passes; `expect([{ id: 1 }]).toContain({ id: 1 })` fails; `expect([1, 2]).toContain(2)` passes. - e2e `expect-values.test.ts` asserts `toBeDefined(null)` fails and `toContain({ a: 1 })` passes on `[{ a: 1 }]`. - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/docs run check`: build validation passed, no broken links. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset: not needed, docs only. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR. - [x] Not a breaking, contract, or engine contract change.

title: fix(init): add zod next to ai so Yarn projects load the config
body: - `ai` and every provider package `e2e init` adds peer on `zod`. npm and pnpm install peers on their own, Yarn does not. - A Yarn 4 (PnP) project scaffolded by `e2e init` failed on the first run with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: @ai-sdk/provider-utils tried to access zod`. - `createScaffold` now adds `zod: '^4.1.8'` whenever it adds `ai` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/scaffold.ts:48`). The range matches the zod peer range that `ai@7` and all four provider packages declare (`^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8`). - A project that already declares `zod` keeps its own range. When `e2e.config.ts` already exists, init still skips gateway deps, so a project scaffolded before this fix needs `yarn add -D zod` (noted in the changeset). Separate from this fix: for 24h after every release, `yarn dlx e2e init` resolves to the old `0.1.0` placeholder (`Binary not found (e2e)`), and `yarn install` reports every version in the scaffold's ranges as quarantined. That comes from Yarn 4's default `npmMinimalAgeGate` (1440 min), not from init. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - scratch project: `yarn init -2` (Yarn 4.18.1, PnP), `e2e init --yes`, `yarn install` (`YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE=0`, because 0.15.1 is under a day old), `APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 yarn test:e2e` | main (`e2e@0.15.1`) | this branch (built `dist/cli/bin.js`) | | --- | --- | | devDependencies: `@e2e-dev/web, ai, e2e, playwright` | devDependencies: `@e2e-dev/web, ai, e2e, playwright, zod` | | `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED (config)`: `@ai-sdk/provider-utils tried to access zod (a peer dependency) but it isn't provided by its ancestors` | `✓ \|web\| tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test)`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` | Yarn 1 (node-modules linker) already worked on main and still works. ---

title: fix(agent): retry DeepSeek's thinking-mode tool_choice refusal with auto
body: - DeepSeek's V4 models (`deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) think by default, and in thinking mode the API refuses a forced tool choice with HTTP 400 `Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice`. - `isForcedToolChoiceRejected` did not recognize that wording, so the act loop treated it as an ordinary provider failure: every agent step on DeepSeek failed on its first turn with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. - One pattern in `FORCED_CHOICE_PATTERNS` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/tool-choice.ts`) routes it into the existing fallback: the turn is resent with `toolChoice: 'auto'` plus the tool-calls-only rule, and later steps on that model start in `auto`. Thinking stays on; `@ai-sdk/deepseek` already passes `reasoning_content` back on every assistant turn. - A unit test pins DeepSeek's real 400 body; `docs/models.mdx` gets one paragraph on DeepSeek; patch changeset for `e2e`. ```ts import { createDeepSeek } from '@ai-sdk/deepseek'; const deepseek = createDeepSeek({ apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }); export default { targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:4791' } }], agents: { default: { model: deepseek('deepseek-flash') } }, // thinking at its default: on } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web target, a one-page app with "Choose Pro" / "Choose Free" buttons; test = `agent.act('Choose the Pro plan')` then `agent.assert('The page says "You chose Pro"')` - `e2e run --reporter json --ai-trace` with `@ai-sdk/deepseek` 3.0.58, `deepseek-flash`, thinking on (default), `ai` 7.0.126 | main (e2e 0.15.1) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `failed`, exit 1: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice` on the first agent step | `passed`, exit 0 | Model calls in `ai-trace.json` on this branch: | call | toolChoice | response | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `required` | 400 `Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice` | | 2 | `auto` | reasoning + tool call (taps "Choose Pro") | | 3 | `auto` | reasoning + `complete_step` | | 4 | judge (`agent.assert`) | reasoning + verdict: pass | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(expect): a negated assertion passes at the deadline when every sample held it
body: Fixes the `test (24)` failure on main in [spec run 36895132106](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36895132106/job/110480101344): ```text FAIL unit tests/unit/expect-async-attributes.test.ts > attribute and focus expectations > still judges the value attribute of a plain field and of one without it TestError: expect.not.toHaveAttribute failed locator: getByRole("textbox", name: "Blank") expected: not attribute "value" observed: attribute "value" absent (match count 1) ``` The test is right and the runner is wrong. The negation held the whole time and the assertion still failed. - `pollCondition` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts`) times the 1000 ms grace window from when the first sample returns. On main, a `{ timeout }` under 1000 ms shrank the window to the budget, but the window still started at that first return, so it ended after the deadline. Whether the assertion passed came down to whether a poll landed in that gap. The screen fixture's budget is 300 ms, and a slow first read or a stall under CI load put the last poll on the wrong side. - The same gap could fail `{ timeout: 1000 }` or any budget a slow read ate into, depending on how read latency lined up with the 100 ms poll interval. With 60 ms reads it failed every run. - A negated matcher now also passes at the deadline when every sample held it. A `true` or an unevaluable sample still resets the hold, and the 1000 ms window is timed as before, so one slow read cannot satisfy it early. - One tradeoff: a budget that a single read outlasts is now judged on that read. Main always failed it. - `docs/reference/expect.mdx` already promised the short-budget case. Its table row, the `not` JSDoc in `types.ts`, the `evaluate` JSDoc of `PollConditionOptions` in `e2e/engine`, and the `.not` line in `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md` now state the full rule. The skill used to say `.not` never returns in under a second. - `locator.waitFor` and `expect(browser)` in `@e2e-dev/web` go through the same function. New cases in `tests/unit/time.test.ts`, on fake timers: | negated poll | should | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 350 ms budget, first read takes 60 ms, never broken | pass | fails | passes | | 1000 ms budget, every read takes 60 ms, never broken | pass | fails | passes | | 350 ms budget, broken by the second sample | fail | fails | fails | | 3000 ms budget, first read takes 1100 ms and holds, then breaks | fail | fails | fails | ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Scratch project on the built CLI. Its engine, made with `defineEngine`, takes 60 ms per `locate`. Two tests run `await expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout })` on a screen with no alert, at 350 ms and 1000 ms. 10 runs per build: | test | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `{ timeout: 350 }` | 0 of 10 pass | 10 of 10 pass | | `{ timeout: 1000 }` | 0 of 10 pass | 10 of 10 pass | main: ```text × no error alert shows within a 350 ms budget 393ms → expect.not.toBeVisible failed × no error alert shows within a 1000 ms budget 1.04s → expect.not.toBeVisible failed ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.not.toBeVisible failed locator: getByRole("alert") expected: not visible observed: no node (match count 0) ``` this branch: ```text ✓ no error alert shows within a 350 ms budget 391ms ✓ no error alert shows within a 1000 ms budget 1.03s ``` - A second scratch project checks the change does not pass too much. The default budget, a first read that takes 1.1 s and sees no alert, then the alert on every later read: `not.toBeVisible()` fails after 5 s on both builds, `observed: default states (match count 1)`. - The CI flake itself did not reproduce here. `expect-async-attributes.test.ts` passed 174 runs on main under heavy CPU load on macOS. The scratch project and the fake-timer cases show the same gap deterministically.
