title: fix(agent): switch to auto tool choice when the provider downgrades a forced one
body: `@ai-sdk/anthropic` does not send a forced tool choice to Claude models that reject forced tool use (Claude Sonnet 5.5, for one). It rewrites `toolChoice: 'required'` (and `{ type: 'tool' }`) to `auto` on the client and reports that only as a call warning, `{ type: 'unsupported', feature: 'toolChoice' }`. The request succeeds, so the HTTP 400 path in `freeToolChoiceRetry` never runs. On main, with that provider: - The loop keeps asking for `required`, and the SDK logs `AI SDK Warning ... The feature "toolChoice" is not supported` on every turn of every step. - The tool-calls-only rule never reaches the instructions. - A turn the model answers in prose throws `ToolChoiceViolationError` inside `generateText` (ai 7.0.88+), which the loop reports as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. What changes: - `noticeToolChoiceDowngrade` reads `step.warnings` after each turn. A `toolChoice` warning switches the step to `auto` and remembers the model in `FREE_TOOL_CHOICE_MODELS`, as a refusal does. - `prepareTurn` returns `instructions` when the mode changed inside a generate call, so the remaining turns carry the rule. The Anthropic cache breakpoint rides along through `hints.instructions`. - `freeToolChoiceRetry` also takes a forced-choice turn that came back as a finished reply without a tool call: matched by error name `AI_ToolChoiceViolationError` (older 7.x releases export no class) and `finishReason === 'stop'` (a `length` or `content-filter` stop says nothing about the provider). That turn was answered and billed, so it is counted as a model call and a turn before the retry. - Test fakes: `scriptedResult` and `LoopResponder` answers can carry provider `warnings`. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[turn asks required] --> P{provider} P -- HTTP 400 tool_choice --> R[resend with auto + rule] P -- sends auto, warns --> W[step.warnings: toolChoice] --> A[rest of step and later steps: auto + rule] P -- sends auto, model writes prose --> V[AI_ToolChoiceViolationError, finishReason stop] --> R ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A NativeScript app's suite on `@e2e-dev/mobile` (iPhone Duo simulator), agent `anthropic('claude-sonnet-5-5')` from `@ai-sdk/anthropic` 4.0.71, `ai` 7.0.126: `e2e run tests/bookmarks.e2e.ts tests/search.e2e.ts --no-cache`, with the AI SDK's warning log left on. Main is the published `e2e` 0.15.1 (no `src/agent` changes since that tag); the branch is this build's `packages/e2e/dist` in its place. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `AI SDK Warning ... toolChoice` lines | 7, one per model call | 1, the first turn | | loop note in the report | none | `[loop] the provider sent auto in place of a forced tool choice on turn 1: continuing with auto` | | result | 2 passed, 7 model calls | 2 passed, 7 model calls | - The prose-reply path did not come up in live runs; it is covered by `retries with auto when a downgraded turn answers in prose`, which scripts a provider that downgrades and answers in prose. - Three of the four new tests in `tool-loop-tool-choice.test.ts` fail against main's `tool-loop.ts`; the fourth guards against acting on unrelated warnings.

title: feat(mobile): device.fold drives a foldable iOS simulator's hinge
body: agent-device 0.21 (the engine pins 0.21.18) can fold an iPhone Duo simulator: `agent-device fold closed|half-open|open` sends the simulator's hinge event and reads the angle back from CoreDevice before it answers. The mobile engine had no way to reach it, so a suite testing a fold-aware layout had to shell out to the CLI against a guessed session name (`e2e--`). - `device.fold(pose)` calls `client.command.fold({ pose })` through `screenCommand`, so it is a recorded `device.fold` step bounded by `actionTimeout`, and it counts as an action for the `transition` budget like `setOrientation`. - Android is refused before any device command, the way `clearKeychain` is. An iOS simulator without a hinge comes back from agent-device as `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`, which already maps to `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - `FoldPose` is exported next to the other device option types. - Docs: the device fixture section of `mobile.mdx` (with the `afterEach` fold-back, since the engine never resets the pose and a retry or the next test inherits it), the `Device` interface on `reference/mobile.mdx`, the package README, the skill's setup topic, and one known limitation: `--video` records the display that was lit when recording started, so after a fold the rest of the video is black. ```ts import { afterEach, test } from '@e2e-dev/mobile'; afterEach(async ({ device }) => { await device.fold('closed'); }); test('the list and the detail split across the fold', async ({ agent, app, device }) => { await app.open(); await device.fold('half-open'); await agent.assert('the list and the detail sit on either side of the fold', { vision: true }); }); ``` Left out: a fold tool in `mobileTools` for `agent.act`. The fixture is the deterministic half; the agent tool can follow if it is wanted. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, on an iPhone Duo simulator (Xcode 27.1, iOS 27.1), not on the mobile benchmark: its Expo app has no fold-aware layout. The surface was a NativeScript app that splits list and detail across the hinge in the book posture, run with this branch's built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` in place of the published ones. The model was `claude-sonnet-5-5`. `e2e run tests/fold-device.e2e.ts` (three tests: a passing fold, a test that fails while unfolded, and a test that checks it starts closed), steps from `.e2e/report.json`: ```text device.fold opens the Duo into two panes app.open passed 4.33s expect.toHaveCount getByRole("button", name: "go down") passed 1.08s device.fold half-open passed 10.77s expect.toBeVisible getByText("Theory of computation · …") passed 0.54s agent.assert the list and Alan Turing’s detail page … passed 5.83s device.fold closed (afterEach) passed 5.68s a failing test still folds back app.open passed 2.09s device.fold half-open passed 10.81s expect.toBeVisible getByText("A pioneer who is not …") failed 5.07s device.fold closed (afterEach) passed 5.70s the next test starts closed app.open passed 2.07s expect.toHaveCount getByRole("button", name: "go down") passed 2.05s ``` The simulator through one passing run (outer display, then `half-open` on the inner display, then `closed`): ![device.fold on the iPhone Duo simulator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NathanWalker/e2e/pr-media/device-fold.gif)

title: fix(runner): preserve failures when tests skip
body: - `expect.soft(1).toBe(2); test.skip('feature disabled')` drops the assertion failure and exits 0. A failed attempt followed by a skip on retry also disappears from the CLI summary. Related to #688. - Keep soft failures in the skipped attempt's `secondaryErrors` and show the original failure under `Skipped After Failure`, including retries and serial members. Exclude engine cleanup diagnostics that arrived after the skip. - Add `failOnSkippedFailure: true` to make these runs exit 1. The default stays `false` to preserve the documented skip behavior under the stability policy. Tests retain their skipped status and reason; clean skips and successful retries are unaffected. ```ts export default { targets, failOnSkippedFailure: true, }; ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the real CLI with a lifecycle-only engine in a standalone project, first with published `e2e@0.15.1`, then with this branch's packed npm package: `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`. No browser, app server, or model credentials. - The regression cases also failed against main at `28b09f3` before the fix. | Scenario | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Soft failure, then skip | Failure absent; exit 0 | Failure retained and printed; exit 0 by default, 1 with the option | | Failed attempt, then skipped retry | Original error hidden in the CLI | Original error printed; exit 1 with the option | | Clean skip with an engine cleanup error | Skipped; exit 0 | Skipped; exit 0, including with the option | The packed fix prints: ```text Skipped After Failure 1 SKIP |headless| tests/skip.e2e.ts > soft failure followed by skip ASSERTION_FAILED: 1 soft assertion failed 1. known regression: expected 1 to be 2 Warnings 1 skipped after failure ``` With the option enabled, `report.json` records run status `failed`, exit code `1`, test status `skipped`, and reason `feature disabled`. The app-backed testbed and benchmark suites were not run; verification stayed headless and service-free.

title: fix(expect): toBeDefined passes on null, as in Playwright
body: ## What and why - `expect(value).toBeDefined()` rejected `null` (`!== undefined && !== null`). Playwright, Jest, and Vitest only reject `undefined`. - The negated form is the risky one: `expect(null).not.toBeDefined()` passed in e2e and fails in Playwright, so a migrated test could pass silently. - Now `!== undefined` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts:133`). The JSDoc in `types.ts` and `docs/reference/expect.mdx` no longer says "non-nullish". - `expect.poll(read).toBeDefined()` uses the same matcher, so a read that returns `null` now passes on the first try instead of waiting. The changeset calls this out and points to `toEqual(expect.anything())` for the old non-nullish check. - Patch, not a deprecation: the signature is unchanged and one call can't carry both meanings. The changeset spells out the looser behavior. - `toContain` deep equality, the other half of #691, stays as it is: `toContain(expect.objectContaining(...))` is documented and depends on it. #734 documents it in the migration table. Closes #691 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, `e2e run` on a scratch suite with three tests: `expect(null).toBeDefined()`, `expect(undefined).not.toBeDefined()`, `expect(null).not.toBeDefined()` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `null is defined` fails: `ASSERTION_FAILED: expected null to be defined`; `null.not.toBeDefined` passes | `null is defined` passes; `null.not.toBeDefined` fails: `ASSERTION_FAILED: expected null not to be defined` | - The updated `expect-values.test.ts` case fails with the `values.ts` change reverted. - `expect.anything()` rejects both `null` and `undefined`, so the migration hint in the changeset holds. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: oauth: `e2e models github-copilot` lists ids that `copilot()` rejects with "The requested model is not supported"
body:
### What happened `npx e2e models github-copilot` prints model ids, each annotated like any other usable model (for example `OpenAI, tools, vision`), and the docs say each line is the id to pass to `copilot()`. For a signed-in Copilot plan, several of those ids fail the first agent step with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: The requested model is not supported.`, while other listed ids such as `gpt-4.1` work. Nothing in the `models` output tells a user which listed ids `copilot()` can actually use, so picking a model is trial and error. #### Expected Every id that `e2e models github-copilot` prints without a qualifier can be passed to `copilot()` and completes an agent step for that login, as docs/subscriptions.mdx ("Pick a model") states: "Each line is the id to pass to `chatgpt()`, `copilot()`, or `grok()`". Ids that `copilot()` cannot use are either omitted or visibly marked. #### Actual `gpt-6-luna` is listed as `GPT-6 Luna OpenAI, tools, vision`, but the first `agent.act` fails in about 0.5 s with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: The requested model is not supported.` The same project with `gpt-4.1` passes. Of nine listed ids tried, seven failed this way and two passed (table under Evidence). ### Minimal reproduction 1. In an empty directory: `npm init -y` then `npm i -D e2e@0.15.1 @e2e-dev/web playwright ai@^7 @ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and `npx playwright install chromium`. 2. Export `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` for every command below. 3. Sign in with the GitHub CLI already signed in to an account with a Copilot plan: `npx e2e login github-copilot` (prints `Using the GitHub CLI token` and `GitHub Copilot login stored.`). 4. Run `npx e2e models github-copilot` and note that `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-4.1` are both listed. 5. Add `server.mjs`, a one-file static server: `import http from 'node:http'; const html = '

Not clicked

'; http.createServer((req, res) => { res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/html' }); res.end(html); }).listen(4319, '127.0.0.1');` 6. Add `e2e.config.ts`: `import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { copilot } from 'e2e/oauth/copilot'; export default { agents: { default: { model: copilot(process.env.COPILOT_MODEL ?? 'gpt-6-luna') } }, targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:4319', command: { executable: 'node', args: ['server.mjs'] } } }] } satisfies E2EConfig;` 7. Add `tests/click.e2e.ts`: `import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { expect } from 'e2e'; test('click the button', async ({ app, agent, browser }) => { await app.open('/'); await agent.act('Click the "Click me" button'); await expect(browser.locator('#c')).toHaveText('Clicked'); });` 8. Run `COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-6-luna npx e2e run --no-cache` (red), then `COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-4.1 npx e2e run --no-cache` (green). Use `--no-cache`: a step recorded by a working model is otherwise replayed for a failing one and the failing id appears to pass. Which ids fail depends on the Copilot plan behind the login; any plan whose `models` listing includes an id that `copilot()` rejects reproduces it. ### Versions - e2e 0.15.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.11.1, ai 7.0.127, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible 3.0.62, playwright 1.63.0 - Node v22.23.2, macOS 27.0 (arm64) - Login: `e2e login github-copilot` reusing the GitHub CLI token, github.com (not Enterprise), a Copilot plan ### Engine not engine specific ### Anything else #### Affected area - `e2e models github-copilot`: `listCopilotModels` in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/github-copilot.ts` keeps every `/models` entry whose `capabilities.type` is `chat` (or absent) and prints vendor, `tools`, `vision`, and `preview`; it reads no other availability field. - `copilot()` in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/copilot.ts` returns `createOpenAICompatible(...).chatModel(modelId)`, which posts to the Copilot API's `/chat/completions`. - docs/subscriptions.mdx, "Pick a model" section. - Source read at `8d38206f460415b70706b45acb820bb0e24832ae` (main, 2026-10-01); these three files are unchanged from tag `e2e@0.15.1`. #### Evidence `npx e2e models github-copilot` (header plus the ids involved): ```text GitHub Copilot (github-copilot): 41 models gpt-5.6-luna GPT-5.6 Luna OpenAI, tools, vision gpt-6-luna GPT-6 Luna OpenAI, tools, vision kimi-k3 Kimi K3 Moonshot AI, tools, vision mai-code-1.1-flash MAI-Code-1.1-Flash Microsoft, tools, vision gpt-5-mini GPT-5 mini Azure OpenAI, tools, vision claude-haiku-4.5 Claude Haiku 4.5 Anthropic, tools, vision gpt-4.1 GPT-4.1 Azure OpenAI, tools, vision gpt-4o GPT-4o Azure OpenAI, tools, vision ``` `claude-sonnet-5`, the id the docs use in the Copilot setup example, is also listed (`Claude Sonnet 5 Anthropic, tools, vision`). `COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-6-luna npx e2e run --no-cache`: ```text model github-copilot.chat/gpt-6-luna ✓ target "web" command ready 91ms × click the button > agent.act "Click the "Click me" button" 590ms failed ... MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: The requested model is not supported. Tests 1 failed | 0 passed (1) ``` `COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-4.1 npx e2e run --no-cache`: ```text ✓ click the button > agent.act "Click the "Click me" button" 12.36s · 2 model calls Tests 1 passed (1) ``` Results with `--no-cache`, same project and login: | id passed to `copilot()` | result | | --- | --- | | `gpt-6-luna` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `mai-code-1.1-flash` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `gpt-5-mini` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `kimi-k3` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `claude-haiku-4.5` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `claude-sonnet-5` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ... not supported | | `gpt-4.1` | passed | | `gpt-4o` | passed | A plain `POST /chat/completions` with the stored login's bearer and e2e's User-Agent (one user message, no tools) returns the same error for `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5-mini`, `kimi-k3`, and `claude-sonnet-5`, and 200 for `gpt-4.1`, so the rejection comes from the Copilot API for that id and login rather than from the agent's tools or images: ```text {"error":{"message":"The requested model is not supported.","code":"model_not_supported","param":"model","type":"invalid_request_error"}} [400] ``` The raw `/models` entries carry fields the listing does not read, but on this login they do not cleanly predict the outcome: `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, and `mai-code-1.1-flash` report `supported_endpoints: ["/responses", "ws:/responses"]` with `policy.state: "enabled"`; `claude-sonnet-5` reports `/chat/completions` with `policy.state: "disabled"`; and `gpt-5-mini`, `kimi-k3`, and `claude-haiku-4.5` report `/chat/completions` with `policy.state: "enabled"` yet are still rejected. `gpt-4.1` and `gpt-4o` report no `supported_endpoints`. A fix based only on those fields may need a live check to be sufficient. #### Impact A user who follows the docs picks an id from `e2e models github-copilot` (often the newest or the one the docs show) and gets a provider failure on the first agent step, with no hint that the id itself is the problem or which listed ids would work. With the step cache on, a failing id can also look healthy if a working model recorded the step earlier. #### Additional context Red/green closure signal: for a Copilot login, every id that `npx e2e models github-copilot` prints without a qualifier completes the `agent.act` test above via `copilot('')` under `npx e2e run --no-cache`, and every id that would fail with "The requested model is not supported" is either omitted or visibly marked as not usable with `copilot()`; docs/subscriptions.mdx matches that behavior. Red today: `gpt-6-luna` is printed unmarked and fails. No existing issue or PR in tester-army/e2e covers this (searched "copilot", "github-copilot", "models", "e2e models", "not supported", "responses", "chat/completions", "MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED" on 2026-10-01).

docs(mobile): run Expo development builds on iOS simulators with launch arguments
body:
```ts
// e2e.config.ts
app: {
  bundleId: 'com.example.app',
  launchArguments: [
    '--initialUrl', 'http://localhost:8081',
    '-EXDevMenuShowsAtLaunch', 'NO',
    '-EXDevMenuIsOnboardingFinished', 'YES',
    '-EXDevMenuShowFloatingActionButton', 'NO',
  ],
  command: { executable: 'npx', args: ['expo', 'start', '--port', '8081'] },
  readyUrl: 'http://localhost:8081/status',
},
```

## What and why

- A development build (`expo-dev-client`) opens on the dev launcher, and the dev menu's onboarding sheet covers the app even when it is pointed at a server.
- On an iOS simulator, four launch-argument pairs fix that:
  - `--initialUrl <url>`: expo-dev-launcher loads the server directly (`initialUrlFromProcessInfo` in `EXDevLauncherController.m`).
  - `-EXDevMenuShowsAtLaunch NO`, `-EXDevMenuIsOnboardingFinished YES`, `-EXDevMenuShowFloatingActionButton NO`: the argument domain outranks the defaults `DevMenuPreferences.swift` registers.
- These go in the existing `app.launchArguments`, as a docs recipe. The first version added a `mobile({ expoDevClient })` option, which was dropped so the mobile engine stays framework-agnostic.
- Docs: an "Expo development builds" section in `docs/mobile.mdx`, plus a line in `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. Android opens the server with `device.openLink` and the `exp+<slug>://expo-development-client/?url=...` link.

## Verified

- With the earlier option, on an iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.5) running a blank `create-expo-app` on SDK 57 with `expo-dev-client`: with `--initialUrl` alone, the dev menu sheet still covers the app. With all four pairs, the app shows and the test passes. title: fix(web): read each locate match in the task that finds it
body:
## What and why

- `web-replaced-nodes.test.ts > never reads the live field as hidden through a detached node` flaked on loaded CI runners (PR #712, [run 36916290597](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/36916290597), Node 22): `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` "node became stale: getByLabel("Nickname")" from `EngineError: a match left the document while it was read`.
- Cause: `locate` found the matches in one protocol call and read them in a later one. The fixture page replaces the field every animation frame, so if a frame passes between the two calls, the read finds a detached element and `locate` throws retryable `NODE_STALE`. On a starved runner a frame passes every time, so `resolveOnce` retried until the action timeout. That is a livelock, not a timing tolerance problem. #578 named this ("a locator whose own matches are replaced every frame still retries until a query and read land in one frame").
- The pinned path (`getByLabel`, `getByDisplayValue`) had the widest gap: `elementHandles()` (query, `getProperties`, adopt), a client hop, then `evaluate`. The unpinned path (`evaluateAll`) is also two CDP calls inside Playwright (`queryArrayInMainWorld`, then evaluate on the array), so `getByTestId` livelocks the same way under heavier lag.
- Fix: a new `e2e-read` selector engine (`packages/web/src/read-selector.ts`). `locate` appends it to the projected locator. Playwright runs it inside the query call, so each match is read in the same page task that finds it. The read is stored on the element under a per-locate token, and `locate` takes it back from the returned elements (`evaluateAll`) or from the pinned handles. What was read and what is pinned are still one set of elements, and both now come from one instant.
- Every read now happens in a selector engine on a connected element, so the detached-read plumbing from #578 (`DetachedNodeData`, the reader's detached branch, `readManySemanticsFunction`, `readHandlesSemanticsFunction`) is gone.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as runner
  participant P as page
  Note over R,P: main
  R->>P: query (elementHandles / evaluateAll step 1)
  P-->>R: elements
  Note over P: frame: field replaced
  R->>P: read
  P-->>R: detached -> NODE_STALE, retry until timeout
  Note over R,P: this branch
  R->>P: query >> e2e-read (reads in the same task)
  P-->>R: elements, reads stored on them
  R->>P: take reads back from those elements
  P-->>R: reads from the query's instant
```

- One behavior change: a `*` capture before the last part of a `browser.locator` selector (`*css=article >> text=Hello`) is now `INVALID_LOCATOR`. Playwright rewrites a capture into `article >> internal:has=(text=Hello >> e2e-read)`, so the returned articles never pass through the read engine. Composing onto a capture was already broken on main: `locator('*css=article >> text=Hello').getByRole('button')` matched articles, not buttons. Documented in `docs/reference/web.mdx`, tested in `web-platform.test.ts`.
- `readOne` treats a stale `session.read` as `null` (hidden). That cannot cause this flake: `session.read` answers from the runner's located-node cache, so it is stale only when the ref was evicted (2048 newer located nodes) or cleared by a pixel-only observe between the resolve and the read. Left as is.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Repro: `web-replaced-nodes.test.ts` with the event loop of the process that drives the browser blocked in slices (`setInterval` busy loop), the way a starved CI runner is. `yes > /dev/null` x15 plus `nice -n 20` did not reproduce it on a 15-core Mac (0/15 on main).
- The new test `a field replaced every frame never reads as hidden on a starved runner` (20 ms `Atomics.wait` slices, 10 reads per locator) is that repro, committed.

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 ms slices, 30 reads | 10/10 fail, `getByLabel` stale (the CI signature) | 30/30 pass |
| 20 ms slices, 30 reads | 10/10 fail, `getByTestId` stale | 30/30 pass |
| committed starved test (20 ms, 10 reads) | 3/3 fail | 30/30 pass |
| unstressed suite | passes | passes, 6 s to 10 s for the file |

main, 5 ms slices:

```text
AssertionError: {"category":"test","code":"LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND","message":"node became stale: getByLabel(\"Nickname\")" ...
EngineError: a match left the document while it was read
    at packages/web/src/surface.ts:655:17
    at LocatorEngine.resolveOnce (packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts:163:16)
    at LocatorEngine.readOne (packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts:312:30)
```

fix(mcp): name the ai package an MCP session needs, and add it when init registers the server
body: Fixes #746. - `e2e mcp` needs the `ai` package even with no model: the catalog reads every tool's schema through the AI SDK's `asSchema` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/tools.ts:98`, `:170`), so `open_session` loads it up front (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:193`). - Without `ai`, that load failed with the shared loader message, which blames "model-backed agent calls" the session never made. `open_session` now rethrows with an MCP-specific message. The code stays `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, so nothing matching on it changes, and the shared message `e2e run` uses is untouched. - `e2e init` produced this broken setup itself: gateway "None" skipped `ai`, while registering the MCP server is a separate choice that still wrote `.mcp.json`. `createScaffold` now takes whether the server is registered and adds `ai` and `zod` for a gateway or the server. - Docs: the MCP setup page and skill reference state the requirement, the `init` table says when `ai` and `zod` are added, and the `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` entry covers a missing `ai` package. ```ts // packages/e2e/src/cli/init/scaffold.ts ...(gateway !== undefined || mcp ? { ai: '^7.0.0', zod: '^4.1.8' } : {}), ...gateway?.dependencies, ``` ## Trade-off for a maintainer A deterministic-only project that registers the MCP server now gets `ai` and `zod` as dev dependencies. The alternative from the issue is an MCP server with no `ai` dependency: replace `asSchema` with the project's own JSON Schema conversion and validation for zod and `jsonSchema()` inputs. That removes the dependency but adds a second schema path next to the one the agent uses, so this PR takes the smaller fix. Happy to do the other one instead if you prefer it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - MCP server, built tarballs of `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` in a scratch web project with no `agents` and no `ai`, driven over stdio (`initialize`, `open_session`, `call observe`, `close_session`). - `e2e init` driven interactively in tmux in an empty project: engine Web, gateway None, both MCP locations, install with npm. Then `open_session` on that project against a local page. - New regression test `refuses to open without the ai package...` in `tests/integration/mcp-session-host.test.ts` fails with the change to `session.ts` reverted and passes with it. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `open_session` without `ai` | `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: the "ai" package is not installed; model-backed agent calls require the optional peer dependency ai@^7 — install it, or configure an agent that brings its own model transport` | `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: an MCP session needs the "ai" package (ai@^7) to read its tools' schemas, even with no model configured; install it as a dev dependency` | | `e2e init`, gateway None, MCP registered | no `ai` in `devDependencies`; `open_session` fails as above | `Add dev dependencies: @e2e-dev/web@^0.11.1, playwright@^1.63.0, ai@^7.0.0, zod@^4.1.8`; `open_session`, `observe` (`#n2 heading "Hello e2e"`, `#n3 button "Click me"`), `close_session` succeed | | `e2e init`, gateway None, no MCP | no `ai` | no `ai` (unchanged) | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Next.js 16 dev target renders but never hydrates under 127.0.0.1 (allowedDevOrigins blocks /_next/*)
body:
## What happened

With a target like:

```ts
app: {
  url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0',
  command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['exec', 'next', 'dev', '-p', '{port}'], cwd: 'app' },
}
```

every page renders (SSR HTML + accessible tree are all there), but **no client JavaScript ever loads — the page never hydrates**. Locators resolve, clicks land (`:focus` moves), and React handlers never fire. Symptoms look like a timing flake; retries don't help because hydration never happens at all.

## Root cause

Next.js 16 blocks cross-origin requests to dev resources by default. `next dev` binds/identifies as `localhost`, and the run opens `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — requests to `/_next/*` (client chunks, HMR) get rejected:

```
Blocked cross-origin request to Next.js dev resource /_next/hmr from "127.0.0.1".
To allow this host in development, add it to "allowedDevOrigins" in next.config.js
```

## The trap

`app.url` with port `0` only accepts a loopback IP (`127.0.0.1`/`[::1]`) — `localhost` is rejected with `INVALID_APP_URL` — so the only fix is app-side:

```js
// next.config.js
{ allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1'] }
```

## Suggestion

Either document this in the web target docs (it will hit every Next.js ≥16 user running a dev target), or warn at runtime when the served app logs the Next cross-origin block. A sentence in the docs would have saved real debugging time.

Workaround confirmed working: adding `allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1']` to next.config restores hydration and the suite passes.

title: Keep the Codex `client_version` current so `e2e models` lists newer ChatGPT models
body:
### Problem

### Problem

`e2e models` (and so the ids I can pick for `chatgpt(...)`) lists models from `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models`, called with a hardcoded `client_version`:

```js
// packages/e2e, dist/oauth/providers/openai.js
const CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION = '0.155.1';
```

title: feat(run): screenshot after every step with screenshot: 'every-step'
body:
## What and why

- New `screenshot` option for the screenshots the runner takes on its own: `on-failure` (default, today's behavior), `every-step`, or `off`.
- `every-step` attaches one frame to every top-level step that passes, so a report (or a tool reading it) can show what each step left on screen without a trace viewer. Steps that keep their own frame (`app.screenshot`, `agent.assert`) and failing steps (the failure screenshot covers them) get none.
- Set like `trace` and `video`, innermost wins: config root, target, `--screenshot <mode>`, test or describe option. Kept out of the config digest, so it never invalidates replays.
- After a secret fill nothing is captured; each later step records a `PIXEL_TAINTED` policy event, the way `agent.assert` already does.
- A capture is bounded by `actionTimeout`; a failure becomes an `engine` event on the step and never changes its verdict. A step before the app is open has nothing to capture and records nothing.
- `@e2e-dev/web`: a screenshot no longer rethrows an error a route or dialog handler latched (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`). Without this, a frame taken right after the step that triggered a failing handler swallowed the failure and the test passed. `app.screenshot()` used to fail with that error; now the next step that drives the page, or the attempt's end, does, as `docs/reference/web.mdx` describes. Covered by `tests/integration/screenshot-handlers.test.ts`.

```ts
export default {
  screenshot: 'every-step',
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url } }],
} satisfies E2EConfig;

test('checkout', { screenshot: 'off' }, async ({ agent }) => { /* ... */ });
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[step body passes] --> B{top-level and every-step?}
  B -- no --> E[publish end]
  B -- yes --> C{secret filled?}
  C -- yes --> P[policy event PIXEL_TAINTED] --> E
  C -- no --> S[engine screenshot, actionTimeout] --> F[attach to step] --> E
```

The seam is `StepRecorderOptions.afterStep` (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`), run inside the step's scope so what it attaches lands on that step; the capture is `packages/e2e/src/run/step-screenshot.ts`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed, `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed run test`: 71 passed, 1 skipped. The new `every step leaves a screenshot` test reports one frame per step:

```
passed [ 'app.open:001-step-0.png', 'locator.tap:002-step-1.png', 'expect.toHaveURL:003-step-2.png' ]
```

The frame after `tap Todos` (`002-step-1.png`) shows the Todos page, the one before it the home page.

- The default (`on-failure`) is unchanged: `pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed -- tests/forms.e2e.ts tests/todos.e2e.ts`, 8 pairs, no test changed behavior and every timing row is `same` or unresolved within noise (wall -0.5%, 95% CI -3.1% to +0.6%).
- What `every-step` costs, same two files, 5 runs each, `--workers 1`, M4:

| Mode | Steps | Screenshots | Median wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `on-failure` | 102 | 0 | 7.1 s |
| `every-step` | 102 | 102 | 10.4 s |

About 32 ms per step on a fast deterministic suite, which is why it is opt-in. On agent steps, which take seconds each, it disappears in the noise.

- Also exercised from the stacked evidence PR (#754): `every-step` on live agent steps (testbed agent suite on OpenAI `gpt-6-luna`, 24 of 24 passed, an agent step's frame is the screen after its last action) and on iOS (mobile-benchmark suite on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, frames in points with the mobile engine's masking of secure fields).

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: not one. The default keeps today's behavior.

title: feat(report): write a sealed .evidence pack for every run
body:
Builds on #753 (the `screenshot` mode); review that first. Until it merges this PR shows its commits too.

## What and why

- Every run writes one sealed `.evidence` pack, `<output>/evidence/<runId>.evidence`, in the open, framework-agnostic format of [`@testmuai/evidence-cli`](https://github.com/LambdaTest/evidence-cli) (Apache-2.0, on npm). The same format other test tools produce, so an e2e run opens in the same viewers and tooling, as one file.
- On by default; `evidence: false`, `E2E_EVIDENCE=0`, or `--no-evidence` turn it off. Evidence takes no screenshot of its own and never changes how a run executes: the pack holds the frames the run already takes (`on-failure` by default). `screenshot: 'every-step'` (or `--screenshot every-step`, from #753) gives every step its frame.
- A built-in reporter (`packages/e2e/src/report/evidence/`), so it runs after the run and can never change its status or exit code; a pack that fails to write or validate is a line in the summary.
- The format's own library seals and validates the pack (`seal.ts` is the only importer), so this PR does not re-implement its rules.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[report-1 + artifacts] --> M[map.ts: planPack] --> W[write.ts: live dir] --> S[evidence-cli finalize: seal zip] --> V[evidence-cli validate L1]
  V --> Sum[run summary line]
```

How a run maps:

| Pack | From the run |
| --- | --- |
| `run.yaml` | run id, window, project, runner version, platforms, commit, models; token, cost, artifact-size metrics |
| `tests/t-<id16>/` | one per selected result, named from the result id, never a title (a test on two targets is two folders) |
| `result.yaml` | verdict, attempts, `flaky`, tags, final attempt's steps (`kind` = api, label, duration, cache mode) |
| `steps/<n>-<attempt>-<index>/` | `step.json` and `screenshot.png` |
| `failure.yaml` | on the failing step: error, expected/actual (matcher details, or an `agent.assert` instruction vs its explanation), locator, URL, failure frame, screen text |
| `logs/` | `steps.ndjson`, `agent.ndjson` (turns), the engine's trace when its redaction allows |

- Report format change (report-1, additive): each step records `argument`, what it was given beside its target (typed text, a key, an assertion's expected value). A secret is `<secret:name>`. Text typed into a secure field is `<withheld>`: the locator engine reads the resolved node once before typing and records the text only when that read says the field is not secure, so it fails closed. Schema, both fixtures, and `debugging.mdx`/`security.mdx` change together.
- Report format change (report-1, additive): each step also records `target`, where it acted in CSS pixels: the `box` of the node a locator action resolved to (read from the node the locator already fetched, so no extra engine call), the `point` of a positioned tap or `tapAt`, and for an agent step its last action's node.
- The pack's `step.json` carries the fields the evidence viewer reads (`summary`, `kind`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `url` on `app.open` and failing steps, `coordinates` and `element_rect` for the cursor and outline) with the report's step record under `e2e`. Titles read `Fill getByLabel("Username") with "admin"`, `Expect getByRole("alert") to have text "Welcome back"`, `Act: agree to the terms (check checkbox "Agree to terms" …)`.
- Engine contract (additive, `e2e/engine`): `EngineArtifacts.screenshot` may return `{ path, viewport }` in place of a path. The session normalizes it, so every existing caller still gets a path; the step frame records the viewport and the pixel scale (read from the PNG header) on `step.viewport`, which the pack writes as `environment.resolution`. `@e2e-dev/web` reports the page's CSS viewport, `@e2e-dev/mobile` the screen in points, so a step's box lands on a device screenshot taken at a higher density.
- CI: the testbed (`spec`), web benchmark and web agent (`benchmark`), and the four mobile jobs (`mobile`) upload their pack as its own artifact (`evidence-*`, 7 days, SHA-pinned `upload-artifact`) and write a viewer link to the job summary. The hosted viewer opens an Actions artifact URL directly (after a GitHub sign-in), so every CI run on this PR has a clickable pack. Both steps are `continue-on-error`, like the existing report uploads.
- Each test folder's definition (the file the format hashes as "what was tested") is a generated `test.json`: the test's id, title path, file, line, and tags from the already-redacted report. It is never the test's source, which can hold a secret value as a plain string (the case #727 now guards; `plain-string-secrets.test.ts` passes with the pack on).
- Verdicts: the format splits `failed` (the app was wrong) from `broken` (the check could not decide). Only `ASSERTION_FAILED` is `failed`.
- Secrets: only artifacts recorded `complete` or `not-required` are copied, so no video, binary download, `command.log`, or console output goes in; `agent.extract` values stay out. `contentsUnder` (the helper every secret-scanning integration test uses) now opens `.evidence` packs and the zips inside them, so `engine-secrets`, `agent-policy`, and the new `evidence.test.ts` all assert the secret is in no pack entry.
- The pack directory keeps the latest run's pack only (as `artifacts/` keeps the latest run's files); `evidence.outDir` is refused inside the cache directory or a directory a run clears. `e2e explore` writes none. `e2e init` and the repo `.gitignore` ignore `.e2e/evidence/`.
- `@testmuai/evidence-cli` is imported lazily in `seal.ts`, so commands other than `run` never load it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

**What was tested**

| Surface | How | Result | Pack |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit + integration | `pnpm test` on the branch rebased on `main` | 2,991 passed (one scheduler test flaked once, green 3/3 alone) | - |
| Web, deterministic | testbed suite, built CLI | 71 passed | valid L1 |
| Web, outcomes | scratch suite: pass, failed, broken, flaky, secret fill | each verdict mapped as designed | valid L1 |
| Web, AI steps live | testbed agent suite, `--no-cache`, OpenAI `gpt-6-luna` | 24 of 24 passed | valid L1 |
| Web, AI judgment failure live | planted `agent.assert` that must fail | `expected` = instruction, `actual` = model's explanation | valid L1 |
| Web, AI steps replayed | web-benchmark agent suite from committed recordings, no key | 25 passed, 7 broken (no model) | valid L1 |
| iOS | mobile-benchmark deterministic suite, iPhone 17 Pro simulator | 53 to 54 of 55 (see below) | valid L1 |
| CI path | fork run on GitHub-hosted runners: artifact upload + viewer link | 2 artifacts, both open in the viewer | valid L1 |

**Open the evidence** (GitHub Actions artifacts from [a run on GitHub-hosted runners](https://github.com/siddhant573/e2e/actions/runs/37025831023); the viewer asks for a GitHub sign-in to read an artifact, kept 30 days):

- [Testbed suite, 71 passed, tests named by title](https://evidence.lambdatest.com/?pack=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fsiddhant573%2Fe2e%2Factions%2Fruns%2F37025831023%2Fartifacts%2F11235192690)
- [Web benchmark agent suite from committed recordings, 25 passed, 7 broken for lack of a model key](https://evidence.lambdatest.com/?pack=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fsiddhant573%2Fe2e%2Factions%2Fruns%2F37025831023%2Fartifacts%2F11234279630)

- testbed, `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed run test` with defaults: 71 passed, 1 skipped; the summary prints `Evidence  .e2e/evidence/<runId>.evidence`. The format's own CLI accepts it:

```
$ evidence validate .e2e/evidence/01a0fb6c-…evidence --profile L1
ok valid (profile L1, evidence 0.1, status finalized)
```

- web-benchmark agentic suite from its committed recordings (`CI=1 … --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache`, no model key): the pack validates at L1; replayed `agent.act` steps map with their instruction as label and cache mode (`self-finalized`); steps that needed a model with none available map to `broken` with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. Live `agent.assert` judgments (failed vs expected/actual) were not exercised: they need a model key.
- Live agent steps: the testbed agent suite with `--no-cache` on OpenAI `gpt-6-luna` (`openai()` from `@ai-sdk/openai`), 24 of 24 passed, pack valid at L1. Agent steps read `Act: <instruction> (<what it did>)`, carry the cursor at the last action's element, keep turns in `logs/agent.ndjson`, and the run names the model. A planted failing `agent.assert` produced `expected` = the instruction and `actual` = the model's explanation ("The todo list shows one list item, not exactly three."). No secret value in any pack entry; `extract` keeps no extracted data.
- What it costs. Same machine, `tests/forms.e2e.ts tests/todos.e2e.ts`, `--workers 1`, 3 runs each:

| Run | Median wall |
| --- | ---: |
| `--no-evidence` | 6.25 s |
| evidence on (default, pack only) | 6.62 s |

The pack (write, seal, validate) adds about 0.37 s here, and about 2 s for the full testbed's 34 MB pack with traces on. Asking for `every-step` frames adds about 32 ms a step on top (#753). The full parallel testbed suite runs in 27 s either way. `evidence-cli` seals in memory and synchronously, so a very large pack blocks the event loop while it seals; a streaming seal belongs in that library.

- iOS, mobile-benchmark deterministic suite on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5), built locally with `expo run:ios --configuration Release`:

| Run | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `--no-evidence` (2 runs) | 54 passed, 1 skipped | 747 s, 795 s |
| evidence on (2 runs) | 52 and 53 passed | 872 s, 800 s |

  `infinite scroll` and `sticky chrome` fail with evidence off too (known simulator flakes). `toBeFocused follows the focus` failed in both evidence-on full runs and passed in both evidence-off ones, but passed 6 of 6 shorter evidence-on runs with the same tests ahead of it, so it is not reproduced on demand. It checks a field the app focuses one frame after mounting; a step frame's accessibility snapshot right after the tap is a plausible cause. Open, and worth CI's mobile job once approved. The pack validates at L1 with `resolution: 402x874` on every test and cursor boxes in points.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: not one by the API. It does change the default output and the default run time (see Verified); `evidence: false` restores both.

title: feat(oauth): add OrcaRouter with API-key and OAuth 2.0 + PKCE login
body: ## What and why - [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai) becomes a first-class model provider in `e2e`, with **two ways to authenticate**. Both end with the same ordinary `sk-orca-…` API key, so the provider request and the model catalog never branch on which entry produced it. - **API key** — `orcarouter('orcarouter/auto')` from `e2e/oauth/orcarouter` reads `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY`, or `npx e2e login orcarouter` stores a pasted key in the credential file the subscription logins already use. - **Connect with OrcaRouter** — `orcarouterAuth('orcarouter/auto')` from `e2e/oauth/orcarouter-auth`, after `npx e2e login orcarouter-oauth` authorizes in a browser with OAuth 2.0 + PKCE (RFC 7636). No client secret, no pre-registered redirect URI. The key OrcaRouter mints is durable, **not** a refresh token: there is no refresh grant, so a relay `401` is terminal reauthentication for the exact account and credential generation that was rejected, never a fake refresh. - **One credential seam.** Both providers return `OAuthCredentials`, `createOAuthFetch` swaps in the `Authorization: Bearer` header, and `orcaRouterModel` builds the same OpenAI-compatible model. `e2e init` offers both as gateways; `e2e models orcarouter` lists the ids. - **Two public origins, never derived from each other.** Auth is `https://www.orcarouter.ai` (`/auth`, and `POST /api/v1/auth/keys`); inference and `GET /v1/models` are `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1`. Swapping the hostname and appending `/v1` yields `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1/auth/keys`, which is a 404; the code never builds it. `ORCA_BASE_URL` is the shared self-hosted fallback, and the explicit `ORCA_AUTH_BASE_URL` / `ORCA_API_BASE_URL` win over it. A remote origin must be HTTPS; plain HTTP only on loopback. - **Flow A (loopback redirect) with an out-of-band paste fallback.** `e2e` runs on a developer machine with a browser, so `startCallbackServer` binds `127.0.0.1:0`, `callback_url` is `http://localhost:/cb`, and the code returns automatically; when the port cannot be bound, or the browser never comes back, the consent screen's shown code is pasted instead (`callback_url=oob`). `code_challenge_method=S256` is sent either way, because a code can always be handed to a person. The device grant (Flow C) is intentionally not implemented. - **PKCE invariants.** A fresh 32-byte verifier and 24-byte state per attempt from `crypto.getRandomValues`; the challenge is `base64url(sha256(verifier))` with no padding; the verifier never enters a URL, a log line, or an error; the callback state is compared in constant time before the code is used; denial, state mismatch, timeout, expired/reused code, `400`, `403`, `429`, and transport failures all end in one typed, actionable line with no hang and no hot loop. - **The model control is the live catalog**, filtered per capability from each record's own metadata — never from a model's name. A chat option needs `supported_endpoint_types` to intersect `{openai, anthropic, gemini, openai-response}`; a model offered for image input additionally needs `architecture.input_modalities` to declare `image`, so an undeclared capability fails closed instead of landing in a dropdown that cannot serve it. Embedding, image-generation, video, and rerank filters are implemented for the API's contract. A catalog outage falls back to a small seed verified against the live endpoint, marked degraded, and never merged into a live answer. - **Shown in the repository's own interface, not only the CLI.** The benchmark app gains the provider configuration scenario `/e/orcarouter-connect` (`apps/web-benchmark/app/src/orca/OrcaRouterConnect.tsx`): the API-key entry and **Connect with OrcaRouter** sit side by side over one masked credential, and the model control is a catalog-driven `

title: docs(starting-your-app): note Next.js dev origins for loopback targets
body: ## What and why - A Next.js 16 dev target under the loopback address the runner recommends never hydrates, and nothing in the docs says why. #751 reports it and asks for a docs sentence or a runtime warning. - The dev server blocks cross-origin requests to its dev resources. The browser origin is `127.0.0.1`, `next dev` identifies as `localhost`, and hydration never starts, so locators resolve and clicks land with no React handler behind them. - `docs/starting-your-app.mdx`: a `### Next.js dev targets` section beside the free-port recipe. It covers `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, names the `localhost` case that needs no entry, and shows the `next.config.ts` change. - `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`: the same fact in one paragraph under the app table. - Docs only. The runner and the web engine are unchanged. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project at `/tmp` with `e2e` 0.15.1, `@e2e-dev/web` 0.11.1, Next.js 16.3.8, `app.url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0'`, `next dev app -p {port}`: | Check | No entry | `allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1']` | | --- | --- | --- | | React attached to the button | 0 keys at 9s | 2 keys at 3s | | Click result | stays `0` | becomes `1` | | Dev server log | `Blocked cross-origin request to Next.js dev resource /_next/hmr from "127.0.0.1".` | no blocked lines | | `e2e run` | 1 failed | 1 passed | - `http://[::1]:4321/` hydrates with `allowedDevOrigins: ['[::1]']`, and `http://localhost:4321/` hydrates with no entry at all. - `pnpm check`: pass, including `mint validate` and `mint broken-links`. - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test`: 70 passed, 1 skipped. - Rendered in `pnpm docs:dev`: the section and the config block appear on `/starting-your-app`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset: not needed, docs only. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/starting-your-app.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. - [x] Not a breaking, contract, or engine contract change.

title: fix(mcp): open a session without the optional ai package
body:
Closes #746. ## What and why - `SessionHost.openSession()` called `loadAiSdk()` unconditionally, so `e2e mcp` in a deterministic-only project (no `ai`, no `agents`) failed `open_session` with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` before a browser opened. The MCP server only used the SDK to read tool schemas (`asSchema`). - `openSession` now loads the SDK only when it is installed (`loadAiSdkIfInstalled()`). Without it, `packages/e2e/src/mcp/tools.ts` reads the tool's Standard Schema directly: - `toolJsonSchema`: `schema['~standard'].jsonSchema.input({ target: 'draft-07' })` (zod 4 implements it); `{ type: 'object' }` when a schema has no converter. - `validateArgs`: `schema['~standard'].validate(args)`, issues rendered with the existing `describeIssue`, same `INVALID_ARGUMENT` message shape. - With `ai` installed nothing changes: both paths still go through `asSchema`. A schema only the SDK can read (`jsonSchema()`, lazy) still requires `ai` and fails with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` as before. - Docs: `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` say the server needs no model package. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `verify` surface: the built, packed `e2e` + `@e2e-dev/web` installed into a scratch project without `ai` (`e2e.config.ts` with `web()` and no `agents`), driven by an MCP SDK client over stdio (`e2e mcp`): `open_session`, `observe`, an invalid `call tap`, `tools {tool: "tap"}`, `close_session`. - `e2e run` in the same project passes on both (deterministic runs never needed `ai`). | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `open_session` → `isError=true`
`MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: the "ai" package is not installed...` | `open_session` → `Session ... open on target "web"` | | (no session) | `observe` → `#root document "Hello"` / `#n2 heading "Hello e2e"` / `#n3 button "Click me"` | | (no session) | `call tap {}` → `INVALID_ARGUMENT: call tap: target: Invalid input, received undefined; tools {tool: "tap"} shows its arguments` | | (no session) | `tools {tool: "tap"}` → description + JSON Schema; `close_session` → closed | - New `tests/unit/mcp-tools-without-ai.test.ts` mocks `ai` as missing and pins the catalog line, JSON Schema, valid call, and rejected call; on main its catalog and call cases fail with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`. - `pnpm check`, e2e unit + MCP integration tests, and `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` pass locally. - Self-review: no subagent available in this environment, so I re-read the diff cold against `.claude/skills/ship-pr/references/review-prompt.md` myself. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## e2e@0.16.0

### Minor Changes

- [#762](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/762) [`83c17e2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/83c17e261e1e6de043c6ae96b9251fecf05356d6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Anonymous telemetry covers `e2e mcp` and `e2e explore`. Each MCP session sends one `e2e_mcp_session` event when it closes or fails to open: the client's self-reported name and version, the platform and engine, how it ended, and its tool calls counted by the runner's own tool names with the error codes they failed with. `e2e_run_completed` adds `command`, counts and option ids of the config features the run used, and for `e2e explore` why it stopped and its steps and findings by kind and severity. Beyond the client's own name, no project names, paths, tool arguments or results, goals, or findings are sent. The notice shows again once; `E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1` prints every event, and the opt-outs are unchanged.

### Patch Changes

- [#760](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/760) [`b3c9832`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b3c9832aa78ac073ceeb4f11e21c833b8ed1e6f7) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - `e2e models openai` asks the ChatGPT backend for its model list as Codex CLI 0.160.0 (was 0.155.1). The backend hides models from clients it considers too old, so models unlocked since 0.155.1 now show up and can be passed to `chatgpt()`.

- [#767](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/767) [`5609f5e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5609f5e5f0e1a72d632c9cce185135f337d1b86d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e models github-copilot` marks the models `copilot()` cannot call: `not enabled` for a model your plan has not turned on, and `no chat completions` for a model Copilot serves only over other APIs such as Responses. These used to be listed like any other model and then failed the first agent step with "The requested model is not supported".

- [#579](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/579) [`c6c39ad`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c6c39ad3f631cc0a29d788af7d8e6b798ef5307c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Locator matchers honor Playwright's `{ checked: false }`, `{ enabled: false }`, `{ visible: false }`, and `{ attached: false }`, which flip the matcher, and `{ ignoreCase }` on `toHaveText`, `toContainText`, `toHaveAccessibleName`, and `toHaveAttribute(name, value)`. Before, these were ignored at runtime, so `toBeChecked({ checked: false })` passed on a checked box and `not.toContainText('error', { ignoreCase: true })` passed on `Error`. Any other option key, or a flag that is not a boolean, is now `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before the first read, from JavaScript too.
  
  `e2e/engine` exports `rejectUnknownOptions(api, options, known, code?)`, the check the runner's own fixtures use, so an engine refuses an option its fixture methods and matchers do not take the same way.

- [#759](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/759) [`0cda95d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0cda95daa72aa88874e2348942913f075f5df5a1) Thanks [@devin-ai-integration](https://github.com/apps/devin-ai-integration)! - `e2e mcp` opens a session in a project without the optional `ai` package. Without the AI SDK, the catalog and the argument checks read each tool's Standard Schema (zod's), so a deterministic-only project (no `agents`, `e2e init` with no model gateway) can `open_session`, `observe`, `locate`, and drive the page.

- [#727](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/727) [`dec903b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/dec903bd4c20a58cd01a4c09e7ab55ecae6a1cce) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A registered secret value passed as a plain string is now redacted in more places: test and describe titles (and the test ids, reporter output, and artifact and failure-page file names derived from them), step labels, `agent.act` and `agent.assert` instructions and params as executors and the model receive them, `agentContext`, judgment prompts, and an `e2e explore` goal. Error messages, observations, and worker console output already masked it. A test whose title spells out a secret gets a new id, so `--last-failed` from an earlier run does not select it once. Not covered: a value only a secret provider returns stays in titles, and a Playwright trace of a session no secret reached is kept as recorded.

- [#763](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/763) [`b573756`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b573756818d7d04088142d29e0e730cfbaf21b45) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Installing `e2e` pulls in 29 packages instead of 117 and takes about 31MB instead of 36MB. `e2e mcp` now runs on the split MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.2.0) in place of `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, which brought in express, hono, and the rest of an HTTP server stack that stdio never used. The server keeps the same protocol version, so existing clients connect as before. Packages are built and published without sourcemaps, which pointed at a `src/` that was never shipped. Stack traces show `dist/` positions.

title: feat(telemetry): report MCP sessions, explore results, and config features
body:
Anonymous telemetry was close to blind on two surfaces. `e2e mcp` sent a single `e2e_cli_session` when the process exited (`exit_code: 0`, `error_code: null`), even when `open_session` failed. `e2e explore` sent the generic run event, which never read `run.explore`. This PR covers both and adds which config features a run uses. Everything sent is still a count, a boolean, a runner option id, or a plain token.

- **New `e2e_mcp_session` event**, one per `open_session`:
  - the client's self-reported name and version, folded through `plainToken`
  - the platform and engine
  - `ended_by`: `agent`, `idle`, `step`, or `server`
  - duration and the number of other sessions open
  - tool calls by the runner's own tool names (project tools counted together as `tool`, anything else `other`)
  - failed calls and their runner error codes
- **Sent when the session ends, not at exit.** `Telemetry.sendQueued` (`packages/e2e/src/telemetry/telemetry.ts`) sends right away and reloads the saved preference before each send, so a mid-session `e2e telemetry disable` still stops it. The exit flush waits for sends still in flight. A client that kills the server loses only the sessions still open.
- **Error codes come from the error itself, not from result text.** The grammar now passes the cause of each failed action to a new `onActionFailed` hook (`packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts`), and the MCP host classifies that cause. Agent- or app-written text that looks like a code (`select "Order failed: VIP_TIER:"`) is never read.
- **`e2e_run_completed` additions:**
  - `command`: `run` or `explore`
  - `config_*`: workers, retries, number of agents, custom executor, separate judge (compared by provider and model id), number of project tools, credentials, secrets, cache settings, reporters, recording modes, app commands, app environments
  - on explore only, `explore_*`: why it ended, budgets, step counts by status, whether the agent gave an assessment, issues, warnings, and findings by severity
- `NOTICE_VERSION` goes from 2 to 3, so the notice shows once more. `docs/telemetry.mdx`, `SECURITY.md`, and `docs/security.mdx` list every new property and the extra request per MCP session.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[open_session / call / close] --> B[SessionUsage counters]
  G[grammar action fails] -- onActionFailed(cause) --> B
  B -- onSessionEnd(summary) --> C[server.ts adds clientInfo]
  C --> D[cli/mcp.ts sessionTelemetry]
  D --> E[mcpSessionEvent folds names and codes]
  E --> F[Telemetry.sendQueued: one request now]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- **Setup.** A source checkout sends nothing, so I packed `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` into a /tmp project (the testbed app plus the agent config). I drove `e2e mcp` with raw JSON-RPC (`clientInfo: claude-code 2.1.0`) under `E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1`.
- **The probe:**
  - an `open_session` on an unknown target
  - one session running `observe`, a `tap` on a missing node, a `select` whose value contains `failed: VIP_TIER:`, and an unknown tool
  - `close_session`
  - one more session left open, then stdin ended

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| one event at exit: `{"command":"mcp","flags":["--headless"],"exit_code":0,"error_code":null,"duration_ms":288}` | `e2e_mcp_session` `open-failed`, `error_code: UNKNOWN_TARGET`, sent immediately |

### Problem

### Description:

In E2E mobile testing, features that rely on the camera (such as biometrics, document verification, QR code scanning, and OCR) are notoriously difficult to test reliably in CI/CD pipelines due to the lack of physical hardware or static simulator camera feeds.

We propose adding native support for camera feed mocking, enabling developers to inject custom static images or video files directly into the emulator/simulator camera stream during test runs.

title: feat(testmuai): @e2e-dev/testmuai, TestMu AI hosted browsers for the web engine
body:
## What and why

- New package `@e2e-dev/testmuai`: `web({ browser: testmuai() })` runs a web target in [TestMu AI](https://www.lambdatest.com) (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Chrome or Edge on Windows and macOS. One session per worker slot, or one per attempt with `scope: 'attempt'`, like `kernel()`.
- A TestMu AI session starts when its CDP websocket opens and ends when it closes, so the provider only builds the URL (`wss://cdp.lambdatest.com/<route>?capabilities=…`). There's no SDK and no API call, `release` is a no-op, and `@e2e-dev/web` is the only peer, like `@e2e-dev/eas`.
- `LT_USERNAME`/`LT_ACCESS_KEY` are read from `request.env` and travel only in the CDP URL. The reporter line is `TestMu AI session "<name>" in build "<build>"`, never the URL.
- Options: `scope`, `browserName`, `browserVersion`, `platform`, `build`, `route`, `hub`, and `capabilities` for further `LT:Options` (video, network, tunnel, idle timeout). Unknown keys, a bad `route`/`hub`/`browserName`, or `capabilities` that would override what the provider sets fail with `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load. `idleTimeout` defaults to 600 s.
- `route` defaults to `/puppeteer`, which serves raw CDP on every account today. `/playwright-cdp` labels sessions as Playwright on the TestMu AI dashboard; the backend change that makes it serve raw CDP is rolling out, and the default can flip once it reaches production.
- No `record`, `downloads` or `sweep`: TestMu AI records its own video, downloads land on its machines, and a session a dead worker held ends at TestMu AI's idle timeout. The integration page documents all three.
- The hub host, `LT:Options` and the `LT_*` variable names keep the old brand because they are the service's live contract.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { testmuai } from '@e2e-dev/testmuai';

export default {
  targets: [
    {
      name: 'testmuai',
      engine: web({ browser: testmuai({ platform: 'Windows 11', capabilities: { video: true } }), viewport: null }),
      app: { url: 'https://staging.example.com' },
    },
  ],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as web engine
  participant P as testmuai()
  participant H as cdp.lambdatest.com
  W->>P: acquire(request)
  P-->>W: { id, cdpEndpoint } (caps + LT_* from request.env)
  W->>H: connectOverCDP(cdpEndpoint)
  Note over H: socket open = session starts
  W->>H: close
  Note over H: socket closed = session ends
  W->>P: release() (no-op)
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Packed the package (`pnpm pack`) and installed the tarball into a scratch project on `e2e` 0.15.1, so `exports`/`files` were exercised: the tarball holds only `dist/`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `README.md` and `package.json`.
- Real runs on TestMu AI production, `/puppeteer`, Windows 11 + Chrome, video on, 3 tests on the-internet.herokuapp.com (taps, assertions, evaluate):

| Scope | Result | Sessions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `worker` | 2/3 passed | 1 session for the worker |
| `attempt` | 2/3 passed | 1 session per test |

- The failing test in both is `add and remove an element`: the-internet.herokuapp.com stalls its jQuery for about 30 s on a fresh browser's first load, so the tap lands before the page's script binds. Session, connect and the other assertions are fine; the same test passes when the page is warm.
- Missing `LT_ACCESS_KEY` fails before any test with `browser provider "testmuai" could not lease a browser: LT_USERNAME and LT_ACCESS_KEY must be set`, and no session is created.
- No report, log or artifact file from any run contains the access key.
- Known limits, documented under Limits on the integration page: in `worker` scope about 25 workers per target fit the engine's 16 KB lease hand-off (`packages/web/src/provider.ts`, `MAX_HANDOFF_ENV_BYTES`; a unit test pins it), and hosts that take more than 60 s to provision (Edge on macOS, for one) fail with `connectOverCDP: Timeout 60000ms exceeded`. `BROWSER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS` is fixed at 60 s in `packages/web/src/surface.ts` and `launchTimeout` doesn't reach the CDP connect. Happy to follow up with a separate PR that lets it, if you want that.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: n/a, new package.

- [ ] Contract change: n/a, no change to `e2e` or `@e2e-dev/web` contracts.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): n/a.

title: docs(mobile): document physical devices
body:
Closes #766

agent-device 0.21 already drives phones plugged into the machine, and `mobile()` passes them through with no engine change. Only the docs said "simulators and emulators". This PR documents what works and what doesn't.

- New `docs/physical-devices.mdx` page under Mobile (with a short pointer from `docs/mobile.mdx`): listing devices, `device: '<name>'`, iOS signing env vars and Android USB debugging, and per-platform limits
- Name, not id: `deviceSelection` (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts:45`) reads only a simulator UDID or `emulator-<port>` as an id, so a phone's UDID or adb serial goes to agent-device as a name and fails with `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND`. The docs say to use the name and keep it unique
- Without `device`, a connected phone shows up as `booted: true` and joins the default pool
- iPhone limits come from agent-device: every `settings` call is gated by `requireSimulatorDevice` (`platform-apple/src/core/app-settings.ts`), so permissions, clearState, network, location, appearance, biometrics and keychain all fail, along with clipboard and fold. Older iPhones without CoreDevice also lose installs, video, links and launch args
- The `device` option wording is updated in the reference, the README, the `options.ts` JSDoc and `skills/e2e`

```ts
mobile({ platform: 'ios', device: 'QA iPhone' })
```

Follow-up, not in this PR: resolve a configured `device` string against `devices.list` ids so a phone's UDID or serial works, and phones that share a name can be told apart.

title: cache: short prefixed record ids like PROJ-016 are not treated as minted, so canvas steps never replay
body:
Follow-up to #340. The start-path check still misses on record ids that are short and prefixed, which is a common shape for human-readable ids.

## What happens

Our app's project URLs look like `/projects/PROJ-016`. `MINTED_SEGMENT` in `cache/route.js` (e2e 0.15.2) treats a segment as minted when it is a uuid, a hex run of 8 or more, a digit run, or a token of 12 or more characters with at least two digits. `PROJ-016` is 8 characters, so it matches none of them and stays a literal. Every recording made on one project therefore misses on the next run's project, and the agent takes over.

On a 4-step test that runs on a project canvas, only the first step (the one before the project exists) ever replayed. That held across 11 warm runs on three models. A run with `--strict-cache` stops at step 2 with `REPLAY_STALE` in about 20 s.

## Repro

1. Record an `agent.act` step that starts on `/projects/PROJ-016`.
2. Run again on a fresh project, `/projects/PROJ-017`.
3. The step misses as a wrong-context start.

## Possible fixes

- Treat `<letters>-<digits>` segments (for example `PROJ-016` or `INV-2041`) as minted.
- Or let a target declare id patterns, for example `cache: { idSegments: [/^PROJ-\d+$/] }`, so apps with their own id shapes can opt in without widening the default.

title: feat(testmu): add @e2e-dev/testmu device provider
body:
## What and why

This adds `@e2e-dev/testmu`, a `DeviceProvider` that runs mobile targets on TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) Android emulators, iOS simulators and real devices. It works through agent-device's TestMu AI plugin, [`@agent-device/testmu`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@agent-device/testmu) (callstack/agent-device#3118).

```ts
import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { testmu } from '@e2e-dev/testmu';

engine: mobile({
  platform: 'android',
  device: testmu({ device: 'Galaxy S22 Ultra 5G', osVersion: '14', app: 'lt://APP-id' }),
}),
```

- **Shape:** the package follows `@e2e-dev/limrun`.
  - `agent-device` and `@agent-device/testmu` are pinned dependencies at `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s version, and `acquire` checks `request.agentDeviceVersion`.
  - Each lease starts its own agent-device daemon in a child process. The process gets a temp state dir and its own agent-device home, with the bundled plugin registered there, so users never run `plugins add`. Its environment carries `LT_USERNAME`/`LT_ACCESS_KEY`, so the credentials never touch the runner's `process.env`.
  - Release runs `daemon stop --clean` and removes the lease's dir.
- **Leases:** each lease is allocated with `retainOnClose`, so e2e's session close between test files keeps the TestMu AI session. A 20 s heartbeat holds a 60 s lease TTL.
- **Options:**
  - `device`, `osVersion` and `app` (`lt://`, URL or local path) select the target, and `deviceType: 'real'` picks real devices instead of emulators/simulators.
  - `project`, `build` and `sessionName` name the session on the dashboard; the session name defaults to `e2e-<run id>-<target>-<slot>`.
  - Device options: `orientation`, `geoLocation`, `timezone`, `language`, `locale` and `appiumVersion`.
  - Unknown options fail at config load.
- **Video:** `record()` links TestMu AI's recording of the session.
- **Limits:**
  - A session is billed from lease to release.
  - An abandoned session ends after TestMu AI's 120 s idle timeout.
  - Device settings, alerts, logs and port reverse are not available through agent-device's WebDriver runtime.

Split out at review: the iOS `XCUIElementType` role fix is #1133, and TestMu AI hosted browsers (`testmuBrowsers()`) will come as a follow-up PR.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm check` passes, including `plugins:check`. Unit tests: `@e2e-dev/testmu` 65, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 262, `@e2e-dev/limrun` 14.
- I ran it end to end against a local fake TestMu AI hub with real agent-device 0.21.25. Allocation creates the session, a worker can snapshot, release deletes the session, and no daemon or temp dir is left behind.
- Live on TestMu AI production, with earlier revisions of this package: Android emulator with `video: 'on'`, iOS simulator, real Pixel 6 and real iPhone. The plugin itself was validated live at callstack/agent-device#3118's head. This child-process shape still needs a live run.
