## e2e@0.17.0

### Minor Changes

- [#779](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/779) [`6639bfa`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6639bfad711d131a3cb2d2bef88ff55289c211a8) Thanks [@fecolinhares](https://github.com/fecolinhares)! - `copilot()` reaches the models Copilot serves only over its Responses API, such as `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, and `grok-4.5`. On the first call it reads the plan's model listing and picks chat completions or the Responses API from the model's `supported_endpoints`; a model served over chat completions, or one the listing does not place, stays on chat completions. A listing that cannot be read sends that call over chat completions without remembering it, and a revoked login fails on the listing with the sign-in command. Responses models run through `@ai-sdk/openai`, which `e2e init` now adds for Copilot; without it the call names the package to install. Responses turns carry the same initiator and vision headers as chat turns. `e2e models github-copilot` marks what `copilot()` cannot call with `no chat or responses` in place of `no chat completions`, and a disabled model as `not enabled` only.

- [#794](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/794) [`c66176b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c66176bd04d79a0eb3391a603139aa10d9889569) Thanks [@neriousy](https://github.com/neriousy)! - Sign in with OpenCode Console to use OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go models for agent steps. `e2e login opencode-console` runs Console's device flow: approve the code, pick the workspace, and the login is stored and refreshed like the other subscriptions. `opencodeConsole('<id>')` from `e2e/oauth/opencode-console` calls a Zen model for a bare id and a Go model for a `go/` id (`go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`); on its first call it reads the workspace config to pick the model's API (OpenAI chat completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Google) and loads only that AI SDK package, so `@ai-sdk/anthropic` and `@ai-sdk/google` join the optional peers. Once the workspace config is read, a model it does not serve, or a Go model without the subscription, fails with `MISCONFIGURED` naming the fix. Each model sends one `x-opencode-session`, so a worker's calls stay on one upstream cache, and prompts cache the way e2e caches them for OpenAI and Anthropic directly: models served over Anthropic Messages get a breakpoint on the system prompt and, in agent steps, on the newest message, and Responses models get the system prompt's cache key. Reports name the model `opencode/<id>` or `opencode.go/<id>`, and chat models of both plans read provider options under `opencode`. `e2e models opencode-console` lists the enabled models tagged Zen or Go, `e2e init` offers OpenCode Console among the subscriptions, and `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, the variable OpenCode reads, takes a Console service account key in place of the stored login.

- [#741](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/741) [`bfa58c7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bfa58c77c252150f3a786cc4f2111a8a6c8527d4) Thanks [@Marve10s](https://github.com/Marve10s)! - Keep soft assertion failures in the report when a test skips itself, and show
  them in the CLI under `Skipped After Failure`. A failed attempt followed by a
  skip on retry also appears there with its original error.
  
  Add `failOnSkippedFailure: true` to fail the run with exit code 1 for these
  tests. The default is `false`, preserving the existing exit code. Tests retain
  their skipped status and reason, teardown still runs, and a skip does not
  trigger another retry.

- [#713](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/713) [`7ab80bc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7ab80bc61001dd102006ea020419b74b72ddf0c7) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: an interrupted test is no longer counted as failed. `report.json` gains `run.summary.interrupted`, and `run.summary.failed` counts only failed and timed-out tests. `run.summary.skipped` now counts only selected tests, so `passed + failed + interrupted + flaky + skipped` equals `selected`; the tests a filter left out are `discovered - selected`. The `list` reporter prints `3 interrupted` in its own column, `summary.md` shows them with ⏹️ and gives them no failure block or page, and `junit.xml` writes each one as a `<skipped>` whose message starts `interrupted:`. A test that failed and whose retry an interrupt cut short stays failed, and its failure is the one reported. A `--repeat-each` run the interrupt stopped is listed as interrupted, not as a flake. The telemetry event gains `tests_interrupted`. In `@e2e-dev/github`, a test that was interrupted and then passed on a `--last-failed` rerun shows as passed, not flaky.

### Patch Changes

- [#711](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/711) [`a3da00d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a3da00dcb147118ee64cdfbc2949225416e43b31) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `device.installApp()` no longer pins the build's file path as the app when agent-device reports no bundle id or package for it, which on Android made `app.open()` fail with "Android runtime hints require an installed package name". It fails at the install with `ENGINE_FAILURE` naming `app.bundleId` or installApp's `app` option; the mobile docs' Troubleshooting covers the Android cause (agent-device 0.21.18 reads an aapt2-built APK's package only through the SDK's `aapt`, which it does not find in the macOS default SDK location, or when the install added the package). `app.open()` on a device now keeps the engine's own reason it cannot launch, such as a build not installed yet with `device.installApp()`, instead of a generic "pin one with app.bundleId or app.appPath".

- [#732](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/732) [`3bf295e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3bf295e4a835a1aa7356487a26fb9bbe0f1f50f0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The replay cache no longer passes a step whose effect did not happen. Entries are keyed by the agent and a hash of its redacted context, so one persona never replays another's steps and a changed `agentContext` records again. A route now includes the origin and the query (ids, tokens, and timestamps aside), and the end route must match exactly. A replay checks what the step made appear, with checked or selected state, and what it made disappear, needs at least one of those changes to happen during the replay, and stops on an alert the recording never saw. A count the step made appear is part of the effect, and an unnamed control with twins needs a named row or group to replay. Every existing entry is re-recorded on the first run after the upgrade.

- [#713](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/713) [`7ab80bc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7ab80bc61001dd102006ea020419b74b72ddf0c7) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A forced interrupt (a second Ctrl-C, or a CI cancel that sends SIGINT and then SIGTERM) still writes `junit.xml` and `summary.md`. The runner used to abandon them along with every other reporter, which left the previous run's files beside the new `report.json`. Custom reporters are still abandoned on force.

- [#799](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/799) [`96ff11b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/96ff11bbc444751be144a3dcb3be9d8f9b333487) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A recorded step that removes a control while something else on screen keeps its text, such as a radio labelled "Express" replaced by a status reading "Express", now replays. Its recording used to fail its own end check on every replay (`end-mismatch`, or `REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`). Re-record such a step once to pick up the fix.

- [#726](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/726) [`f7c0756`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7c075666672d128f79ef2ec347fda67ea9e42ce) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `locator.waitFor` adds Playwright's `attached` and `detached` states and refuses any other state, or an option key besides `state` and `timeout`, with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Before, every state but `visible` ran as `hidden`, so `waitFor({ state: 'attached' })` and a misspelled state passed at once on an absent node. `toBeHidden`, `toBeVisible({ visible: false })`, `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`, and `waitFor` `detached` and `hidden` read a locator under a frame missing from the document as zero matches instead of timing out waiting for the frame. `toHaveProperty` reads a primitive on the path through its wrapper, as Jest does, so `toHaveProperty('label.length', 3)` passes. `expect(browser).toHaveURL` takes `ignoreCase`, and `urlMatches` in `e2e/engine` takes it as an optional fourth argument.

- [#784](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/784) [`cc54c6b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/cc54c6b72b40817c800ea5ad1e1ee80d57667e8e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Every model call now identifies e2e, whichever provider serves it: the `User-Agent` starts with `e2e/<version> (<platform>; <arch>)` ahead of the AI SDK's own, and `HTTP-Referer: https://tester.army/e2e` with `X-Title: e2e` attribute the traffic on the Vercel AI Gateway and OpenRouter. These replace an `HTTP-Referer` or `X-Title` set on the provider instance. Before, only subscription logins sent the e2e user agent.

- [#722](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/722) [`f0f9c8d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f0f9c8daaefd8751045e540007a09ba830147d48) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Explicit navigation now uses an allowlist instead of a denylist: `app.open`, `browser.goto`, and the agent's `navigate` verb admit `http:`, `https:`, and the exact `about:blank`, and every other scheme (`chrome:`, `blob:`, `about:srcdoc`, ...) is `POLICY_DENIED`. A wrapped scheme such as `view-source:file:///...` no longer loads a local file; it is `POLICY_DENIED` like `file:` itself. `device.openLink` and `device.openApp` also refuse `view-source:`, `blob:`, and `filesystem:` links. `browser.setCookies` refuses an `about:blank` cookie URL with `POLICY_DENIED`.

- [#729](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/729) [`4ce01b2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4ce01b29296bac02a7b7792069de3e0e9b8bd16c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A registered secret no longer leaks through the observed screen: a test id, an iframe name in a frame path, a selector, or an attribute holding one is masked in the model's text, an executor's tree, and cache entries, and a secret with a line break, tab, CRLF, no-break space, or repeated spaces that an engine collapsed and then cut at the name or text limit no longer leaves its leading part in observations or end anchors.

- [#798](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/798) [`02ad48a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/02ad48a94ef9f68befc89139694c519868d82853) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: `@e2e-dev/web` depends on `playwright-core` pinned to an exact version instead of peering on `playwright`. Projects no longer install Playwright themselves, and the engine always runs the Playwright it was tested against. Remove `playwright` from your dependencies unless your app uses it for its own tests:
  
  ```bash
  npm uninstall playwright
  ```
  
  Install browsers in CI with the package's new command, which runs the engine's Playwright: `npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium --with-deps` (`pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps` under pnpm) replaces `npx playwright install chromium --with-deps`. Open traces with `npx playwright-core@1.63.0 show-trace <file>` (`pnpm dlx` in a pnpm project). An app that also depends on `@playwright/test` keeps its own copy; the two share a browser cache only when their versions match. `e2e init` no longer adds `playwright` to a new project.

- [#725](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/725) [`9b93575`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9b93575faf35db1e309e0b6d5b421ffb6df14ede) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - An `expect.poll` that the test body, an `afterEach` hook, or a fixture teardown returns without awaiting is now cancelled and fails that phase with `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` at the line of the call; in a `beforeAll` or `afterAll` hook it fails the hook with `HOOK_FAILED`. Before, the test passed and the poll's timeout failed whichever test ran next, or nothing at all.
  
  The negation window of a negated `expect(locator)` or `expect(browser)` matcher now starts when the first read that saw the negation was issued, not when it returned, so a slow read counts toward it. With a `timeout` under a second, a negation that held for the whole budget now passes at the deadline; before, a slow first read made a true negation time out.

- [#777](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/777) [`79931d0`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/79931d081a1a687bcd003a70a13da21b905f9011) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - The replay cache abstracts short prefixed record ids as minted segments. A route segment of letters, a dash, and a digit tail of two or more (`PROJ-016`, `INV-2041`) now reduces to `:id`, so a step recorded on one record replays on the next instead of missing with `wrong-context` and running live every time. A single trailing digit (`page-2`) stays a route word.

- [#724](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/724) [`3a9667c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3a9667c0467f464bf542c50380d3468b0c222b17) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `--last-failed` no longer goes green on tests it never ran. It reruns tests `--max-failures` skipped, and a test or failed `beforeAll`/`afterAll` another filter leaves out stays owed in the report's new `run.carried` until a rerun runs it. A rerun also keeps the artifacts of the run it reruns and writes its own under `artifacts/rerun-<n>/` in the output directory (`.e2e` by default), so the folded pull request comment keeps its evidence and stays red while anything is owed.

- [#721](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/721) [`94ddbfe`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/94ddbfe46faa5cf7b9159fd0a604aa4317056051) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Two credentials or two secrets whose names map to the same override variable (`api-key` and `api_key` both read `E2E_SECRET_API_KEY`) now fail the config load with `INVALID_CONFIG` instead of both silently taking one value.

- [#800](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/800) [`b5dc0f8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b5dc0f87bb82dc878d1daeff06075c9e073c2688) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `--strict-cache` now fails a step with `REPLAY_STALE` when the cache directory holds its recording under another key, for example after an `e2e` or engine upgrade or a change to the agent's context. Before, such a step ran live and spent model calls with no error. The message names the old entry file. A step with no recording still runs live.

- [#786](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/786) [`f88233f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f88233fdce99ba57420e5f8d5c80e9254332f4d5) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - web({ locale, timezoneId }) sets the language and time zone every attempt's context runs in, as Playwright's `use.locale` and `use.timezoneId` do: `navigator.language`, `Intl`, the `Accept-Language` header, and local `Date` time. ### Patch Changes

- [#788](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/788) [`baa32c6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/baa32c68013215a62c31c25238926d4ee4300ada) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `check()` and `uncheck()`, and the agent's `check` tool, pass when the click removes the control or navigates away from it, such as a radio the app replaces with its selected view. The click landed, so the action is recorded and replays. What replaced the control is not read, so a test that needs it asserts on it. They used to fail: an agent step reported `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and left the action out of its recording, so the next run handed off with `end-mismatch`, and a locator `check()` timed out. Unchecking a checked radio and a click that leaves the state unchanged now fail with `NOT_ACTIONABLE` instead of `ENGINE_FAILURE`.

- [#726](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/726) [`f7c0756`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7c075666672d128f79ef2ec347fda67ea9e42ce) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `locator.waitFor` adds Playwright's `attached` and `detached` states and refuses any other state, or an option key besides `state` and `timeout`, with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Before, every state but `visible` ran as `hidden`, so `waitFor({ state: 'attached' })` and a misspelled state passed at once on an absent node. `toBeHidden`, `toBeVisible({ visible: false })`, `toBeAttached({ attached: false })`, and `waitFor` `detached` and `hidden` read a locator under a frame missing from the document as zero matches instead of timing out waiting for the frame. `toHaveProperty` reads a primitive on the path through its wrapper, as Jest does, so `toHaveProperty('label.length', 3)` passes. `expect(browser).toHaveURL` takes `ignoreCase`, and `urlMatches` in `e2e/engine` takes it as an optional fourth argument.

- [#722](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/722) [`f0f9c8d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f0f9c8daaefd8751045e540007a09ba830147d48) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Explicit navigation now uses an allowlist instead of a denylist: `app.open`, `browser.goto`, and the agent's `navigate` verb admit `http:`, `https:`, and the exact `about:blank`, and every other scheme (`chrome:`, `blob:`, `about:srcdoc`, ...) is `POLICY_DENIED`. A wrapped scheme such as `view-source:file:///...` no longer loads a local file; it is `POLICY_DENIED` like `file:` itself. `device.openLink` and `device.openApp` also refuse `view-source:`, `blob:`, and `filesystem:` links. `browser.setCookies` refuses an `about:blank` cookie URL with `POLICY_DENIED`.

- [#785](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/785) [`9844c30`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9844c30d1d320eecf51446f0100853d7310c564d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A string role name with a quote (`getByRole('button', { name: "Yes, I'm sure" })`) no longer fails with `InvalidSelectorError` once the locator is chained (`.first()`, `nth`, a filter, or the read itself). The same goes for a `u` or `v` flag RegExp with a quote or `>>` in `getByRole`, `getByText`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`, and `getByTestId`.

- [#723](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/723) [`cdc3a53`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/cdc3a53e816bcb8a5d8a4beb934b06b293d8c358) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Route decisions behave like Playwright's. `route.continue()` now sends the request to the network instead of handing it to an earlier route, and still carries the configured `headers` to the app's site; the new `route.fallback()` keeps the old chaining. `continue` takes `url`, `method`, `headers`, and `postData`, with `url` checked by the same rule as `goto`, and `fulfill` takes `path` (relative to the project root) and `contentType`. An option a decision does not take, such as `abort(errorCode)` or a misspelled key, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of being ignored. `browser.waitForResponse` resolves once a matching response's headers arrive, so a slow body no longer fails the match with a timeout; `text()` and `json()` wait for the body up to the action timeout. `browser.setCookies` with a relative `url` sets the cookie on the base URL instead of failing with `ENGINE_FAILURE`.

- [#728](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/728) [`7f9ee10`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7f9ee108dbdcbfab43cff2cdd9435b043a7035d1) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Web visibility and reads follow what renders, as Playwright reads them: an `aria-hidden` node that paints is visible, so `toBeHidden()` on a decorative spinner waits until it leaves; content under `content-visibility: hidden` is hidden; a child that sets `visibility: visible` under a hidden parent is visible and in the agent's observation; text under a `display: contents` element with `visibility: hidden` is hidden, where Playwright calls it visible, since it paints nothing. `boundingBox()` is `null` for a node with no layout box. `inputValue()` and `toHaveValue` read a checkbox's or radio's value (`on` by default) whatever its checked state. An accessible name reads an embedded control's value: `<button>Flash the screen <input value="3"> times</button>` is "Flash the screen 3 times".

- [#711](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/711) [`a3da00d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a3da00dcb147118ee64cdfbc2949225416e43b31) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `device.installApp()` no longer pins the build's file path as the app when agent-device reports no bundle id or package for it, which on Android made `app.open()` fail with "Android runtime hints require an installed package name". It fails at the install with `ENGINE_FAILURE` naming `app.bundleId` or installApp's `app` option; the mobile docs' Troubleshooting covers the Android cause (agent-device 0.21.18 reads an aapt2-built APK's package only through the SDK's `aapt`, which it does not find in the macOS default SDK location, or when the install added the package). `app.open()` on a device now keeps the engine's own reason it cannot launch, such as a build not installed yet with `device.installApp()`, instead of a generic "pin one with app.bundleId or app.appPath".

- [#791](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/791) [`b3e1fd1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b3e1fd1543300aa0c5c32a9ff1dc77b3b37ef1ef) Thanks [@DimaMishchenko](https://github.com/DimaMishchenko)! - Update agent-device to 0.21.20 so sibling-sized iOS toolbar containers no longer falsely mark nearby controls as covered.

- [#801](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/801) [`ae3dc64`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ae3dc645c9fba4b8fd2ed7341954ccc5e3ca16e3) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - Recognize agent-device's stale-ref refusals by their `details.reason` instead of matching their message, so a reworded message in a later agent-device release cannot turn a stale ref into an engine failure. Every ref-frame reason agent-device 0.21.20 sends is covered, including the three whose messages the old pattern did not match.

- [#722](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/722) [`f0f9c8d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f0f9c8daaefd8751045e540007a09ba830147d48) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Explicit navigation now uses an allowlist instead of a denylist: `app.open`, `browser.goto`, and the agent's `navigate` verb admit `http:`, `https:`, and the exact `about:blank`, and every other scheme (`chrome:`, `blob:`, `about:srcdoc`, ...) is `POLICY_DENIED`. A wrapped scheme such as `view-source:file:///...` no longer loads a local file; it is `POLICY_DENIED` like `file:` itself. `device.openLink` and `device.openApp` also refuse `view-source:`, `blob:`, and `filesystem:` links. `browser.setCookies` refuses an `about:blank` cookie URL with `POLICY_DENIED`.

- [#793](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/793) [`4db7d6d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4db7d6de4c32417099171485b4a8daca87c02225) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - `device.openLink` no longer echoes the string it refused in its `INVALID_ARGUMENT` message. A malformed link can carry a magic-link token in its query, path, or userinfo, so the message names no part of the input, matching what `device.openApp` already does.

title: fix(cache): treat short prefixed record ids as minted segments (#769)
body: ## What and why Fixes #769 - The replay cache compares screens as routes, not URLs: `routeOf` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/route.ts:81`) splits a location's path and replaces every segment that looks minted per record with `:id`, and the start-path precondition in `decideTraceReplay` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/decide.ts:47`) replays a step only when the recorded and live routes read exactly the same. - `PROJ-016` matched none of the minted shapes: it is 8 characters, so the 12-or-more-character mixed-token rule skips it, and it is not a hex run, not all digits, and carries no whitespace. It stayed a literal. - So a step recorded on `/projects/PROJ-016` compared its recorded route against `/projects/PROJ-017` on the next run: one differing literal segment reads as `undecided`, which is a miss at the start of a step, and the agent took over. Only the step before the project exists ever replayed (11 warm runs on three models per the issue), and `--strict-cache` stopped at step 2 with `REPLAY_STALE`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[replay starts] --> B["routeOf(recorded startPath)"] A --> C["routeOf(currentPath)"] B --> D{compareRoutes} C --> D D -- same --> E[replay] D -- "undecided / different" --> F["miss: wrong-context"] ``` - The fix adds one pattern to `MINTED_SEGMENT`: ```ts /^[A-Za-z]+-\d{2,}$/, ``` - Letters, a dash, then a digit tail of two or more: `PROJ-016`, `INV-2041`, `item-42`. It sits next to the existing shapes and inherits their behavior, so both sides of the comparison reduce to `:id` and the routes read alike. - The single-digit floor is deliberate. Both ids in the issue carry a zero-padded tail, while a single trailing digit is usually a route word a router owns (`page-2`). If you would rather follow the issue's `-` wording exactly, widening the tail to `-\d+` is a one-character change and the `page-2` control flips to `:id` with it. - What the pattern does not touch: `companies-v2` keeps staying a literal because no digit follows the dash directly, `Summer-Sneaker` and other dashed slugs stay literals, and `john_doe` stays a literal. Those controls now have test coverage. - Routes are computed at replay time from the stored raw paths (`trace.startPath` and the live path), so recordings made before this change benefit too: no cache version bump, no re-record, and no change to the `.e2e/cache/` layout the stability policy covers. - Docs: `docs/cache.mdx` already promises "the same route, whatever the record id"; this change makes the code keep that promise for prefixed ids, so no docs edit was needed. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The new assertions fail against main's code and pass here, in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-route.test.ts`: ```text AssertionError: expected '/projects/PROJ-016' to be '/projects/:id' AssertionError: expected 'undecided' to be 'same' ``` - Cache unit suites on this branch: `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/trace-route.test.ts tests/unit/trace-cache.test.ts tests/unit/trace-decide.test.ts tests/unit/trace-identity.test.ts tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts tests/unit/trace-recorder.test.ts`, 6 files, 116 tests passed. - The bug and the fix side by side, running `routeOf` and `compareRoutes` from `main` and from this branch: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `routeOf("/projects/PROJ-016")` → `/projects/PROJ-016` | `routeOf("/projects/PROJ-016")` → `/projects/:id` | | `routeOf("/projects/PROJ-017")` → `/projects/PROJ-017` | `routeOf("/projects/PROJ-017")` → `/projects/:id` | | `compareRoutes(recorded, live)` → `undecided`, the start precondition wants `same`, so the step misses and the agent takes over | `compareRoutes(recorded, live)` → `same`, the step replays | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`.changeset/prefixed-record-ids.md`, `e2e: patch`). - [x] Not a breaking change: no public API, config key, wire format, or `.e2e/cache/` layout change; the fix widens which paths read as the same route. - [x] Docs checked in the same review: `docs/cache.mdx` already describes this behavior and needs no edit; `skills/e2e/` does not describe the minted shapes. - [x] No contract change: no emitted `.d.ts`, schema, or fixture touched, and no engine contract change.

title: oauth: copilot() builds a chat model unconditionally, so models Copilot serves only through /responses (gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-luna) are unreachable
body:
Follow-up to #745 and #767, not a regression in the model-listing fix. The listing now
marks these models correctly; there is still no way to call them.

## What happens

`copilot(modelId)` in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/copilot.ts` returns
`createOpenAICompatible({ baseURL: COPILOT_API_URL, ... }).chatModel(modelId)`
unconditionally, so every Copilot model is called through `/chat/completions`.
`packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/github-copilot.ts` reads each raw `/models` entry's
`supported_endpoints`, and its own comment states the consequence: "A model the plan has
not enabled, or one Copilot serves without `/chat/completions`, is listed but marked:
`copilot()` posts to `/chat/completions`, which rejects both."

Copilot serves some enabled models only over `/responses`. On the reporter's login in
#745 those are `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-luna` and `mai-code-1.1-flash`, each with
`supported_endpoints: ["/responses", "ws:/responses"]` and `policy.state: "enabled"`.
Calling one through `/chat/completions` fails:

    POST https://api.githubcopilot.com/chat/completions -> 400
    {"error":{"message":"model \"gpt-6-luna\" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint",
              "code":"model_not_supported","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

The same request to `/responses` succeeds. Copilot's Responses direction is the vendor's
stated one: in github/copilot-cli#4337 a GitHub maintainer answered that "there is a
strong push for Copilot products towards the Responses API", that Copilot CLI/SDK and
Copilot Language Server already support it, and restoring `/chat/completions` access for
these models was closed as not planned.

#767 scoped this explicitly, and it is the request here: "That needs per-model endpoint
selection and `@ai-sdk/openai`'s Responses model, like `chatgpt()` uses. Copilot's
`/responses` returns 200 for gpt-6-luna, so it is doable as a follow-up."

## Repro

Text only, no engine, no agent step, no cache: the missing endpoint fails on the first
call. In a project with an existing Copilot login, on an installed build of this commit:

1. `npx e2e models github-copilot`, then pick an id enabled for your account whose raw
   `/models` entry lists `/responses` and not `/chat/completions` (`gpt-6-luna` is the id
   the maintainer tested in #767).
2. Save as `copilot-probe.mjs`:

```js
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { copilot } from 'e2e/oauth/copilot';

const modelId = process.argv[2];
if (!modelId) throw new Error('Pass a model id from your Copilot account.');
const result = await generateText({ model: copilot(modelId), prompt: 'Reply with OK.', maxRetries: 0 });
console.log(result.text);
```

3. `node copilot-probe.mjs gpt-6-luna` -> today this ends in the 400 above.
4. Repeat with an account-enabled `/chat/completions` model as a control; that one works.

For the same failure inside an agent step, run the suite with `--no-cache`.

This snippet is a proposed minimal reproduction. I did not run it against a live Copilot
subscription; the 400, the `/responses` success and the `supported_endpoints` values above
come from the linked reports.

## Versions

e2e 0.16.0 at f7c075666672d128f79ef2ec347fda67ea9e42ce; `ai` ^7.0.0,
`@ai-sdk/openai` ^4.0.0 (4.0.71), `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` ^3.0.0 (3.0.53),
`@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.18; Node 26 (the version in CI).

## Multimodal and tool continuation

A different URL is not the whole change. Two source-confirmed consequences of moving a
call to `/responses`:

- `sendCopilotRequest` decides the vision header by scanning for `content[].type ===
  'image_url'`. A Responses body carries `input[]` with `input_image`, so image calls
  would never set `copilot-vision-request`.
- The same scan sets `x-initiator`: `if (messages.at(-1)?.role !== 'user') initiator =
  'agent'`. A Responses body has no `messages`, so every turn would be labelled `agent`.

These are latent adapter problems visible in the source, not additional failures I
reproduced. They are why acceptance below covers image and tool-result turns: a text-only
200 does not establish that a screenshot step or a tool continuation works.

## Possible fixes

- Choose the protocol from the model's declared capabilities (`supported_endpoints`), the
  way the listing already reads them, and construct `@ai-sdk/openai`'s Responses model for
  a model served only over `/responses` (already a dependency of `packages/e2e`; no new
  package). Keep `chatModel` for everything that advertises `/chat/completions`, and
  decide the documented behaviour for entries with no `supported_endpoints`.
- Or expose the protocol as an explicit choice in the constructor, leaving the default as
  it is today.

Either way `sendCopilotRequest` needs the per-protocol initiator and vision detection, and
the multi-turn/stateless handling `chatgpt()` already does for the Responses transport
should be verified for Copilot rather than assumed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An account-enabled `/responses`-only model completes text, image, and tool-result
   continuation through the Copilot API, and existing `/chat/completions` models do not
   regress. Both `doGenerate` and `doStream` are covered.
2. Endpoint choice follows declared model capabilities rather than a vendor or model-name
   heuristic, with defined behaviour for missing metadata, disabled models, and endpoint
   sets this client does not support. Credential access and network I/O stay lazy.
3. Copilot authentication, enterprise-host routing, abort behaviour, and the per-protocol
   `x-initiator` / vision headers are correct, and stateless multi-turn handling is
   validated instead of assumed.
4. Deterministic transport/provider tests plus a built-package live check with secrets
   removed. Public declarations updated if the constructor surface changes; report/session
   schemas and fixtures only if those wire formats actually change.
5. Subscription/CLI docs, `skills/e2e/`, and the generated install instructions updated in
   the same PR, including any newly required optional peer, with a changeset.

I have not opened a PR or made changes; this issue is the diagnosis and the request.

title: fix(oauth): reach Copilot models served only over the Responses API
body:
Fixes #778.

`copilot()` built its model with `createOpenAICompatible(...).chatModel(modelId)` for every id, so a model the Copilot plan serves only over its Responses API (`gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, `grok-4.5`, `mai-code-1.1-flash`) could not be called: `/chat/completions` answers `400 unsupported_api_for_model`, while `/responses` succeeds. #767 marked those models in the listing and scoped the invocation as a follow-up; this is that follow-up.

## What changed

- `copilot(modelId)` stays synchronous and makes no network call while constructing. It returns a delegate that settles the protocol on the first `doGenerate` / `doStream` from the plan's `GET /models`, then hands the call to `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`'s chat model or `@ai-sdk/openai`'s Responses model (wrapped with `store: false`, as `chatgpt()` is).
- The protocol comes from the model's `supported_endpoints` only, as in `vscode-copilot-chat`. No endpoints or `/chat/completions` named means chat; `/responses` without chat means Responses; anything else stays on chat and the vendor's error explains it. Plan policy plays no part: `grok-4.5` and `gpt-5.3-codex` carry no `policy` yet work over Responses, and a disabled model fails identically on both endpoints.
- Only a listing that was read is remembered. An error status, non-JSON body, network failure, or the listing's own 10s timeout sends that call over chat and the next call asks again, so one blip does not pin a Responses-only model to chat for the whole run.
- One lookup serves concurrent calls under its own timeout; a caller that aborts stops waiting without failing the others.
- A revoked login fails on the listing with the sign-in command instead of being read as "no listing" and retried on chat.
- `@ai-sdk/openai` is imported lazily, only when a Responses model is called. Without it, the call fails with `MISCONFIGURED` naming the package. `e2e init` now adds it for the Copilot gateway.
- `sendCopilotRequest` reads the initiator and vision flag from Responses bodies too (`input[]`, `input_image`); before, every Responses turn was labelled `x-initiator: agent` with no vision header.
- `withoutServerStorage` moved to `src/oauth/responses.ts`, shared by `chatgpt()` and `copilot()`.
- `e2e models github-copilot` marks uncallable models `no chat or responses` (was `no chat completions`); a disabled Responses model now reads `not enabled` only.

## Verified

- `pnpm check` passes; e2e unit tests: 165 files, 2370 passed.
- Live, through `copilot()` against a real Copilot plan (`tests/live/oauth.ts`: image + forced tool call):

| Model | Endpoints listed | Routed to | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-6-luna` | `/responses` | responses | tool call ok |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | `/responses`, no policy | responses | tool call ok |
| `grok-4.5` | `/responses`, no policy | responses | ok with a 256px image; xAI rejects the 8x8 test PNG on either path |
| `claude-sonnet-5` | chat + messages | chat | tool call ok |
| `gpt-5.4` | chat + responses | chat | tool call ok |

- A 4-step reasoning tool loop over Responses with `store: false` completes on `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, `grok-4.5`, `mai-code-1.1-flash`.

## Open

- When a model lists both endpoints (`gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5-mini`), chat wins so working models do not move. `vscode-copilot-chat` prefers Responses there.
- `@ai-sdk/openai` decides "reasoning model" by name, so `grok-*` / `mai-*` get no `include: reasoning.encrypted_content`. `forceReasoning` from the listing's `reasoning_effort` works live but showed no measurable gain; left as follow-up.

title: docs(models): add an AI SDK provider picker to the Models page
body:
Users do not see that e2e takes a model from any AI SDK provider. This adds a provider dropdown to the Models page, with three setup steps that follow the selection.

- New section `## AI SDK providers` in `docs/models.mdx`: a dropdown, then "Install the provider package", "Set the credentials", and "Add the model to the config". Each step has a short text and a box that shows the install command (npm, pnpm, bun), the environment variables, or a full `e2e.config.ts` for the selected provider.
- 51 providers from the ai-sdk.dev provider pages: 25 `@ai-sdk/*`, 18 community, 8 OpenAI-compatible. Excluded: providers without a language model, models without tool calls (Perplexity, llama.cpp, QuiverAI), agent CLIs with their own tool loop, browser- and device-only runtimes, packages on the v1 model specification, and two packages that do not load as ESM or do not typecheck (Apertis 3.0.0, Requesty 3.6.2). The reasons are in the header of `docs/snippets/model-provider.jsx`.
- Six providers throw when the config loads if a variable is missing (Google Vertex, Claude Platform on AWS, AIHubMix, Cencori, Telnyx, Azure AI Foundry). Their environment box says that a missing variable stops all runs with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`.
- The four boxes are one component, `<ModelProvider show="select | install | env | config" />`. Mintlify evaluates each snippet export alone, so exports share no module scope. The instances share the selection through a store on `globalThis`, read with `React.useSyncExternalStore`. No wrapper component, so the step headings stay in the table of contents.
- Code renders with Mintlify's `CodeBlock`, which is available in snippets and gives the site's syntax highlighting and copy button.
- `docs/reference/config.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/agent.md` link to or state the same rule. The skill text lists example packages because agents do not see the dropdown.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Each of the 51 entries: installed its npm package in a scratch project, imported the entry's code, and constructed the model. All return a model with `specificationVersion`, `modelId`, and `doGenerate`.
- Each generated `e2e.config.ts` typechecks against this branch's `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` types (`tsc --noEmit`, 51 files, 0 errors).
- Constructed each entry under `env -i` to find which providers throw at config load. The six `readsAtLoad` entries match that result.
- `mint dev` with Playwright, light and dark: selected providers and package managers, and all four boxes updated with highlighted code. No page errors. The table of contents lists the three step headings.

| Light | Dark |
| --- | --- |
| ![light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b1ddbbe-414b-43b1-b75a-edd88503699b) | ![dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4cca739e-453a-46fd-a6d5-325e4ec5a5c7) |

Not verified: a real model call for each example model ID. The IDs come from each provider's AI SDK page. The page says that they are examples and that the model must support tool calls and images.

Review findings not taken:

- The install box does not sync with Mintlify's site-wide package manager choice. `CodeGroup` is not available in snippet scope (probed), so the box has its own npm, pnpm, bun switch.
- The offline docs shipped in the `e2e` package contain the `<ModelProvider>` tags without the data. The page links to ai-sdk.dev, and the skill text lists example packages for agents.
- The 51 config templates have no CI typecheck. The provider packages are not dependencies of the docs package, and adding about 45 of them for one check is out of proportion. I typechecked them by hand as described above.

title: `getByRole` throws `InvalidSelectorError` when the accessible name contains a straight apostrophe
A run downloads the full Chromium when only the headless shell is installed, and the install it spawns garbage-collects the shared Playwright cache
body:
## Summary

When a target uses the default headless Chromium and only `chromium-headless-shell` is installed,
`e2e run` decides the browser is missing and spawns `playwright install chromium` during `prepare`.
Two consequences:

1. The run downloads the full Chrome for Testing (about 190 MB on macOS arm64, 187 MB on Linux x64)
   that the headless run never launches. On our side this added 37 s to the first run and opened
   outbound connections in the middle of a test pass that is otherwise loopback only.
2. The spawned `playwright install` runs Playwright's browser garbage collection on the browsers
   directory. Revisions that no installed Playwright declares are deleted. With the default location
   (`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`, `~/.cache/ms-playwright`), this is the cache shared by every
   tool on the machine: on our workstation it removed Chromium 1234 and its headless shell, which
   another local tool launched through a hard-coded path. That tool was not a registered Playwright
   install, so the collection had no way to know the revision was still in use.

We would like the run to respect the browser that will actually be launched, and either respect a
declared location without collecting it, or document `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_GC`.

## Versions

- `e2e` 0.16.0
- `@e2e-dev/web` 0.11.2
- `playwright` / `playwright-core` 1.63.0 (Chromium 1243, Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12)
- Node 22.23.2, macOS 26 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0)

## Minimal reproduction

Any project with one `web()` target and one test that opens a page (we used the config of the
apostrophe report and this test):

```ts
import { test } from "@e2e-dev/web";
import { expect } from "e2e";
test("open a page headless", async ({ app, screen }) => {
  await app.open("/");
  await expect(screen.getByText("It's ready.")).toBeVisible();
});
```

A private browsers directory containing only the headless shell 1243, plus two older revisions that
stand for what another tool left in a shared cache:

```sh
B="$PWD/browsers"; mkdir -p "$B"
cp -R <an existing install>/chromium_headless_shell-1243 "$B/"
mkdir -p "$B/chromium-1234" "$B/chromium_headless_shell-1234"
echo marker > "$B/chromium-1234/INSTALLATION_COMPLETE"
echo marker > "$B/chromium_headless_shell-1234/INSTALLATION_COMPLETE"

PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$B" E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e run
ls "$B"
```

## Actual result

```
 RUN  e2e v0.16.0 …/repro-e2e
      run 01a10114-c17c-708d-b0cb-a3d2792ba317 · targets: desktop

ℹ Downloading missing Playwright browsers (first run): chromium...
ℹ Removing unused browser at …/repro-e2e/browsers/chromium-1234
ℹ Removing unused browser at …/repro-e2e/browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1234
ℹ Downloading Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (playwright chromium v1243) from https://cdn.playwright.dev/builds/cft/153.0.8010.12/mac-arm64/chrome-mac-arm64.zip
ℹ Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (playwright chromium v1243) downloaded to …/repro-e2e/browsers/chromium-1243
ℹ Downloading FFmpeg (playwright ffmpeg v1011) from https://cdn.playwright.dev/dbazure/download/playwright/builds/ffmpeg/1011/ffmpeg-mac-arm64.zip
ℹ FFmpeg (playwright ffmpeg v1011) downloaded to …/repro-e2e/browsers/ffmpeg-1011
ℹ Browser download complete.
 ✓ web engine for target "desktop" prepared 36.68s
 ✓ |desktop| e2e/headless.e2e.ts (1 test) 2.59s
```

Afterwards the directory holds `chromium-1243` (359 MB), `chromium_headless_shell-1243` (195 MB) and
`ffmpeg-1011`; both 1234 revisions are gone. The test itself ran on the headless shell.

## Expected result

- No download: the headless shell that the launch will use is installed.
- No deletion in a directory the user pointed the run to, or at least a documented way to prevent it.

## Where it comes from

`@e2e-dev/web/dist/install.js`, `isBrowserInstalled`, checks
`existsSync(browserType(name).executablePath())`. For `chromium`, `executablePath()` is the full
Chrome for Testing, not the headless shell that a headless launch uses since Playwright 1.49. The
missing list is then passed to `runPlaywrightInstall`, which spawns `playwright install chromium`
with the run's environment. That command installs both builds and, unless
`PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_GC` is set, removes every revision of the browsers directory that no
registered Playwright install declares.

## What we ask

1. Check the executable the launch will use: the headless shell when the target is headless and no
   `channel` is set, the full Chromium otherwise. Install only that one (`playwright install
   chromium-headless-shell` or `playwright install --only-shell chromium`).
2. Either pass `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_GC=1` to the spawned install when `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`
   was set by the user, or document the variable in the browser provisioning section, since a first
   run can delete browsers other tools rely on.
3. Optionally, an option or environment variable that turns the automatic install off, so CI can
   fail fast when browsers are missing instead of downloading in the middle of a pass.

## Workaround we use

We set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` to a directory owned by the project, `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_GC=1`,
install the full Chromium and its headless shell before the run, and point `PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST`
to a closed loopback port during the run so that any attempt fails in about a second instead of
downloading.

title: feat(agent): identify e2e on every model request
body: ## Summary - Every model call now identifies e2e, whichever provider serves it. Before, only subscription logins (ChatGPT, Copilot, SuperGrok) sent our user agent. Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints saw a generic AI SDK client. - `USER_AGENT` moves from `src/oauth/providers.ts` to `src/internal/client-identity.ts`, next to `MODEL_REQUEST_HEADERS`. - Both model call paths send the headers per call: judgments (`src/agent/model/sdk.ts`) and every act-loop turn (`src/agent/tool-loop.ts`). ```ts export const MODEL_REQUEST_HEADERS = { 'user-agent': USER_AGENT, // e2e/ (; ) 'http-referer': 'https://tester.army/e2e', 'x-title': 'e2e', }; ``` - The AI SDK appends its own user agent after ours (`withUserAgentSuffix`), so vendors still see the SDK version. - `http-referer` and `x-title` are the app attribution headers the [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/ecosystem/app-attribution) and OpenRouter read. Other vendors ignore them. OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini CLI all send one stable `name/version (platform; arch)` user agent the same way. - Groundwork for OpenCode Zen and Go, which ask clients to name themselves in the user agent. **Tradeoff:** call-level headers win over provider-level ones, so an `HTTP-Referer` or `X-Title` a user sets on their provider instance is replaced by ours. Documented in `docs/models.mdx` and the changeset. If we want an opt-out, it would be a follow-up `headers` option on the agent entry. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: web benchmark agent suite against the built packages, live through the Vercel AI Gateway (`--no-cache`, every step calls the model). ```text $ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.agent.config.ts tests-agent/login-form.e2e.ts --no-cache ✓ act signs in with the benchmark account > agent.act "log in with the given credentials" 5.83s · 3 model calls Tests 1 passed (1) $ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.agent.config.ts tests-agent/planted-bugs.e2e.ts --no-cache ✓ cart totals: a judgment catches the stale order summary ✓ checkout review: a judgment catches the broken copy ✓ wishlist: a judgment catches the lost saved items Tests 3 passed (3) · 8 model calls ``` Headers the gateway received on a real judgment call, captured with a logging `fetch` on `createGateway`: ```text url: https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v4/ai/language-model ua: e2e/0.16.0 (darwin; arm64) ai/7.0.107 ai-sdk/provider-utils/5.0.45 runtime/node.js/24 ref: https://tester.army/e2e title: e2e ``` `tests/unit/model-request-headers.test.ts` checks the same headers on the wire against a local server, for a judgment call and an `agent.act` loop. Both tests fail with the two `headers:` lines reverted. Not verified live: the subscription (OAuth) paths. No logins are stored on this machine. There the change is only the import location; `tests/unit/oauth/xai.test.ts` still asserts the `e2e/...` user agent.

title: fix(web): quotes in a string role name no longer break chained locators
body:
Fixes ENG-863 (4 `e2e feedback` reports on 0.16.0). - `getByRole('button', { name: "Yes, I'm sure" })` threw `InvalidSelectorError` once chained (`.first()`, `nth`, filter, or the engine's own `>> e2e-read`). Regression from #669: `glyphTolerantName` turns a string name into a `u`-flag RegExp for `\p{Co}`, and Playwright 1.63 `escapeRegexForSelector` skips escaping `u`/`v` regexes, so a bare `'` opens a quote in the selector parser and swallows the rest. - New `selectorSafeRegExp` (`packages/web/src/locators.ts:24`) rewrites quotes to `\x22`/`\x27`/`\x60` and `>>` to `>\x3e` in `u`/`v` regexes. Same matches, nothing for the parser to trip on. Keeps `\p{Co}`, so supplementary-plane icon glyphs still match. - Applied to the glyph-tolerant role name and every user RegExp (`getByRole` name, `getByText`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`, `hasText`, `getByTestId`), which had the same gap with a `/.../u` pattern. ```text heading[name=/^[\s\p{Co}]*Don't[\s\p{Co}]+... >> nth=0 >> e2e-read=... # before: parser opens a quote at ' heading[name=/^[\s\p{Co}]*Don\x27t[\s\p{Co}]+... >> nth=0 >> e2e-read=... # after ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, scratch test injecting `` then `expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: "Yes, I'm sure" }).first()).toBeVisible()` + `.tap()` - `tests/integration/icon-glyph-names.test.ts` new case (exact/substring name, `visible`, `u` and `v` text, `u` testId, all chained) fails on main with the same error, passes here - testbed suite 70/70, web benchmark 90/90 | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× role name with an apostrophe`
`ENGINE_FAILURE: locate failed: locator.evaluateAll: InvalidSelectorError: Error while parsing selector button[name=/^[\s\p{Co}]*Yes,[\s\p{Co}]+I'm[\s\p{Co}]+sure[\s\p{Co}]*$/u] >> nth=0 >> e2e-read=... - unexpected symbol ">" at position 74` | `✓ role name with an apostrophe 567ms`
`Tests 1 passed (1)` |

title: feat(web): locale and timezoneId options set the language and time zone every attempt runs in
body:
Closes ENG-871. Feedback: the browser is always en-US, so an app that picks its language from `navigator.language` needs a localStorage write and a reload in every test.

- `web({ locale, timezoneId })` passes both to Playwright's context options (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`), so they hold on every context an attempt opens: the first one, after `app.clearState()`, and after a session restore.
- Same semantics as Playwright's `use.locale` / `use.timezoneId`: context-creation options with no runtime setter. A target is the per-project unit, the same as Playwright `projects`. Per-test overrides (`test.use`) are a separate design question and left out.
- Config-load validation (`packages/web/src/engine.ts`) rejects values Node's `Intl` accepts but Chromium refuses at context creation: `und`, `x-private`, `+01:00`, `europe/berlin`, `utc`. Aliases Chromium accepts (`US/Eastern`, `GMT`, `Asia/Kolkata`) still pass. Best effort: Node cannot tell `us/eastern` from `US/Eastern`, so for that case Chromium's `Invalid timezone ID: us/eastern` at the first context is what the user sees.
- `locale` together with an `accept-language` entry in `headers` is `INVALID_CONFIG`, same as `userAgent` with `user-agent`: the header would win on the app's site while `navigator.language` reported the locale.
- On a persistent context (`connect.reconnectEndpoint`, or a provider with `scope: 'attempt'`) both options are `INVALID_CONFIG`, like `headers`, `basicAuth`, and `userAgent`. The error now names only the options that were set.

```ts
targets: [
  { name: 'de', engine: web({ locale: 'de-DE', timezoneId: 'Europe/Berlin' }), app },
],
```

Docs: web reference, browser guide, Kernel page, Playwright migration table (`use.locale` and `use.timezoneId` were "missing"), package README, skill setup table. Changeset: minor for `@e2e-dev/web`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI, a throwaway test reading `navigator.language`, the resolved time zone, and `toLocaleString()`:

```text
web({ locale: "de-DE", timezoneId: "Asia/Tokyo" })
{"language":"de-DE","timeZone":"Asia/Tokyo","formatted":"1.1.2026, 21:00:00"}
 ✓ page runs in the configured locale and time zone 182ms

web()  (control)
{"language":"en-US","timeZone":"Europe/Warsaw","formatted":"1/1/2026, 1:00:00 PM"}

web({ timezoneId: "Mars/Olympus" })
 ERROR  configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config)
web({ timezoneId }) must be an IANA time zone such as "Europe/Berlin", got "Mars/Olympus"
```

- Probed Playwright Chromium `newContext` with each edge value to set the validation rules above (Firefox and WebKit not installed locally).
- New integration test (`packages/web/tests/integration/protected-app.test.ts`) checks language, time zone, and UTC offset before and after a context reset in real Chromium.

title: feat(oauth): run agent steps on an OpenCode Go subscription
body:
## Summary - New `opencodeGo('')` from `e2e/oauth/opencode-go` runs agent steps on an [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/) subscription. `e2e init` offers it as "OpenCode Go subscription". - Go serves each model over the API of its family, at `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`. The constructor routes each model the way OpenCode itself does, from models.dev's `opencode-go` catalog, and imports only the AI SDK package that model needs: | Models | API | Package | | --- | --- | --- | | GPT, Grok, Muse Spark | `/responses` | `@ai-sdk/openai` (no server storage, like `chatgpt()`) | | MiniMax, Qwen 3.8 Flash | `/messages` | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (new optional peer) | | Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, MiMo, the rest | `/chat/completions` | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | - The key comes from `OPENCODE_API_KEY` and is read per request, so a config without it still loads. Each SDK gets a placeholder key, so none of them falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. A missing key fails the model call with `OPENCODE_API_KEY is not set; copy your OpenCode Go key from https://opencode.ai/auth`. - Go asks clients for [their own user agent and a stable `x-opencode-session` per conversation](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/). The runner now sends a conversation id on every model call as `x-session-affinity`: one per act step (`LoopRun`) and one per judgment (`Invocation`, shared across its repair retries). `opencodeGo()` copies it into `x-opencode-session`, next to the `e2e/` user agent from #784. ```mermaid flowchart LR step[act step / judgment] -->|x-session-affinity: uuid| sdk[AI SDK call] sdk --> go[opencodeGo fetch] go -->|Bearer key, e2e UA,
x-opencode-session: uuid| api[opencode.ai/zen/go/v1] ``` - Because the Anthropic SDK doesn't know Go's `/messages` models, two fixes: - It would cap a call with no output limit (every act turn) at 4096 tokens. These calls now get 131072, the models.dev limit for all of them. - `provider-hints` now treats a provider named `.messages` as Anthropic, so these models get the prompt-cache breakpoints Claude gets. ```ts import { opencodeGo } from 'e2e/oauth/opencode-go'; export default { agents: { default: { model: opencodeGo('gpt-6-luna') } }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` **Pending:** OpenCode lists the clients it has validated for Go. We're confirming with the OpenCode team that e2e can be one of them, which is why this is a draft. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, without a live Go key. A live run needs a paid `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, and Zen's and Go's free tiers refuse clients other than OpenCode. Real Go endpoints from a scratch project on the packed tarball, with a bogus key. Each API reaches its path with our headers, and Go answers with an auth error, not a 404: ```text gpt-6-luna -> POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses | ua: e2e/0.16.0 (darwin; arm64) ai/7.0.127 ... | session: probe-step-1 <- 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError","message":"Invalid API key."}} minimax-m3 -> POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages | ua: e2e/0.16.0 (darwin; arm64) ai/7.0.127 ... | session: probe-step-1 | x-api-key: true <- 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError","message":"Invalid API key."}} kimi-k3 -> POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions | ua: e2e/0.16.0 (darwin; arm64) ai/7.0.127 ... | session: probe-step-1 <- 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError","message":"Invalid API key."}} ``` With `OPENCODE_API_KEY` unset and `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-leak` set, all three fail with `MISCONFIGURED` and send no request. The built CLI on the testbed (`tests-agent/judgments.e2e.ts` with `opencodeGo('gpt-6-luna')`): ```text OPENCODE_API_KEY unset: → model provider failed: OPENCODE_API_KEY is not set; copy your OpenCode G… OPENCODE_API_KEY bogus: → model provider failed: Invalid API key.; the provider rejected the crede… ``` Unit tests on the wire, against local servers: - `tests/unit/oauth/opencode-go.test.ts` checks: - each API's path, the bearer key, `x-api-key` on `/messages`, the user agent, `store: false`, and the runner's session copied into `x-opencode-session` - a stable session per model instance outside the runner - `max_tokens` lifted to 131072 when the call sets none, and kept when it sets one - the cache breakpoint in the `/messages` body - no request sent without the key - `tests/unit/model-request-headers.test.ts` checks that both act-loop turns share one conversation and that a judgment carries its own. - Forcing every model to chat, dropping the session copy, or reverting the `.messages` hint rule each fails these tests. Not verified: a live agent step on a real Go plan. I'll run the testbed and web benchmark agent suites once a key is available.

title: fix(web): a check whose control the click replaces passes and replays
body:
## What and why

Fixes ENG-814. A user reported `check` failing with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` on a radio the app replaces with its selected view after the pick. The page did show the selection, but the action was left out of the recording, so the next run replayed only the earlier actions and handed off with `end-mismatch`.

- Cause: Playwright's `check()` clicks, then reads the element again to confirm it. If the click removed the element, that read throws `Element is not attached to the DOM`. `classifyActionError` turned this into `NODE_STALE` (retryable, "nothing dispatched"), even though the click had already landed. The agent then tried to find the radio again, found nothing, and threw `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. A locator `check()` re-resolved inside Playwright until it timed out.
- `check` and `uncheck` now run on a single element (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`, `setChecked`):
  1. read the state; if it's already right, do nothing
  2. refuse to uncheck a radio, before any click
  3. click
  4. read the state again. A control that's gone by now (detached, or its document navigated away) took the click, so the action is done. A state that didn't change fails with `NOT_ACTIONABLE`.
- A control that's gone *before* the click is still a retryable `NODE_STALE`.
- Unchecking a checked radio and a click that changes nothing were `ENGINE_FAILURE`; both are now `NOT_ACTIONABLE`.
- Limitation, by choice: whatever replaced the control is not read. If the app renders an unchecked copy in its place (e.g. a server rejected the change), `check()` still passes, the same as a tap. The next observation or assertion shows the real state. Documented in `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` and the changeset, and pinned by a test.
- Web benchmark Control Inventory has a new Delivery exercise: picking a radio replaces it with "Express delivery selected". It has a deterministic test and an agent test. The core gestures fixture page has the same radio, with a scripted-model flow that records the step and then replays it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[read checked] -->|already set| Z[done]
  A --> B[click]
  B --> C{read again}
  C -->|wanted state| Z
  C -->|element gone| Z
  C -->|unchanged| X[NOT_ACTIONABLE]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `packages/web/tests/integration/check-actions.test.ts`: real Chromium, both target kinds (locator, and an element pinned by an observation)
- web benchmark: `e2e run tests/control-inventory.e2e.ts` against a main build in a separate worktree and against this branch
- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-act-verbs.test.ts`: scripted model, `check` on the replaced radio, then a replay from cache

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-actions.test.ts` | 8 of 15 fail | 17 pass |
| benchmark: `getByRole('radio', 'Express').check()` | `ACTION_FAILED: check timed out after its input was dispatched` after 30s | passes in 182ms |
| agent `check` on the replaced radio | `check:failed`, and the replay needs 2 model calls | `check:passed`, and the replay makes 0 model calls |

```text
main:
 × control inventory > check picks a radio the pick replaces with its summary 30.15s
   → check timed out after its input was dispatched: locator.check: Timeout 2…
branch:
 ✓ control inventory > check picks a radio the pick replaces with its summary 182ms
```

The 6 existing Control Inventory agent recordings still replay with `--strict-cache` on the changed page.

The new agent step `check picks a radio the pick replaces with its summary` ran against the live model in this PR's `web agent` job and passed. Its recording is not committed yet: this machine has no model access. Until it is recorded with `test:agent` and committed, the `web agent` job calls the model for that one step.

title: Cache reader rejects recorded empty type action (REPLAY_STALE invalid-entry)
fix(e2e)!: load TypeScript with e2e's own oxc loader, so pnpm 11+ installs pass
body:
Every new pnpm 11+ user's first `pnpm install` after `pnpm dlx e2e init` fails today:

```
Error: ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS
  × installing dependencies
  ╰─▶ Ignored build scripts: esbuild@0.28.2
```

`e2e` loaded TypeScript through `tsx`, `tsx` depends on `esbuild`, and `esbuild` has a `postinstall`. pnpm 11+ fails on any build script the project has not decided on. The root fix is that nothing `e2e` installs runs an install script. Replaces the closed #712, which edited `pnpm-workspace.yaml` instead.

## What changed

- `tsx` is gone from `dependencies`. e2e loads TypeScript itself with synchronous `module.registerHooks` hooks (`packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`), compiles with `oxc-transform` (`config/typescript.ts`), and reads tsconfig with `get-tsconfig` (`config/tsconfig.ts`). None of the new dependencies has an install script; platform binaries come as `optionalDependencies`.
- One policy (`config/compiled-files.ts`): one extension table (`lang`, `format`, the extension an import writes) drives what is compiled, its module format, the `./x.js` swap, and implied extensions. `.ts .mts .tsx .jsx` run as ES modules, `.cts` as CommonJS. A project file compiles with the nearest tsconfig.json; TypeScript in an installed package compiles with defaults.
- Resolution: an import written in a compiled file follows TypeScript (`./x.js` and `./x` to `x.ts`, a directory's package.json `main` then index, tsconfig `paths`/`baseUrl` for project files); a `#` import or package export whose target is missing (`./x.js`, or `./x` with no extension) moves to the TypeScript file behind it, also when a lax resolver earlier in the chain returned the missing file. An import written in JavaScript gets plain Node resolution. `require()` specifiers are read as platform paths (`C:\app\helper` on Windows; `config/specifiers.ts`).
- `load` reads source through `nextLoad`, so other hooks in the chain still see the file.
- The tsconfig.json is the nearest one, or the referenced project that includes the file when it is solution-style (`files: []` + `references`, as Vite writes). One that cannot be read (an `extends` package not installed) is skipped with one warning per run (the runner hands the files it warned about to its workers, which warn only about others they reach). tsconfig and file lookups live in a view per module graph (`e2e-graph`): fresh for each `e2e mcp` session's graph load, read once otherwise (collecting 50 files parses the `extends` chain once). Outside a graph, file lookups go to the disk each time, as Node's own resolution does.
- Compiled CommonJS starts with `require = globalThis[Symbol.for("e2e.hooked-require.v1")](__filename);`, a `require` the loader registers: the `require` Node hands a CommonJS module an ES module imported skips resolve hooks before nodejs/node#62920 (24.18.0, 26.2.0; not in 22), and on every version once a `module.register` loader is in the chain (Yarn PnP, tsx in NODE_OPTIONS). Its `resolve` runs the loader's resolve hook, since `require.resolve` skips hooks before nodejs/node#62028 (24.15.0; not in 22). The statement joins the end of the last directive (found from oxc-parser's parse of the output), so the prologue and every mapped position stay put; with no directive it takes its own first line and the map gains one unmapped line.
- oxc helpers (`using` on Node 22, legacy decorators) come from e2e's own `@oxc-project/runtime`: the `from "..."` / `require("...")` specifiers oxc reports in `helpersUsed` are rewritten (oxc 0.152 has no option for it), so a project's own `@oxc-project/runtime` import is untouched.
- oxc appends `export {};` to CommonJS whose only imports were type-only, before any trailing comment; the loader finds it in oxc-parser's parse of the output and blanks it. Not reported upstream yet (`crates/oxc_transformer/src/typescript/annotations.rs`).
- Syntax oxc passes through and Node cannot run is refused before compiling, with `file:line:col` and the fix: auto-accessors (no oxc release lowers them), decorators without `experimentalDecorators`, and `import` declarations and value `export` declarations in `.cts` (`export interface`/`type`/`declare` pass, as tsc allows). The check parses only files whose text could hold them.
- oxc and oxc-parser load on first compile, so `--version` and `--help` run without the native binding; without it, a run fails with `TYPESCRIPT_COMPILER_UNAVAILABLE` (exit 3) naming the `@oxc-transform`/`@oxc-parser` bindings for the platform and npm/cli#4828; any other load failure gives its reason.
- Another loader earlier in the chain: a CommonJS load result with no source (Yarn PnP) is read from disk, and an inline source map it left is composed with oxc's (`@jridgewell/remapping`), so `file:line` still names the file on disk.
- Workers from source `--import` `config/register.ts`, which registers the hooks; it and `esm-hooks.ts` load under Node's own type stripping, so they stay erasable TypeScript.
- Removed what existed only for tsx: `tsxUsesSyncHooks` and its version table, the tsx namespace and `tsx-namespace` URL tagging, the `NODE_OPTIONS` inspection, and the diagnose hint for tsx's `?namespace=` CommonJS dead end. Config and tests now share the runner's module instances; the `globalThis` slots stay for a project that loads its own copy of e2e.
- A test's source location is read off the stack text, now with `at async ...` frames (a test file that awaits a helper declaring tests), and only `file:` URLs are decoded (`collect/registry.ts`); main throws on a `%` in a file name and loses the location at a `#`. `util.getCallSites` drops async frames and `Error.prepareStackTrace` gets no call sites while source maps are on, so the text stays the source.
- A type imported without `import type` that stays in the output (a decorated member's type under `emitDecoratorMetadata`, a re-exported type) fails at link time as before, but the error now names the importing line and `import type`.
- **Breaking:** Node floor is `^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0` for every published package (was `>=22.12.0`), as an explicit release-range model in `internal/node-version.ts`. `registerHooks` does not exist before 22.15, and before 22.22.3 / 24.8.0 a CommonJS file an ES module imported cannot `require()` an ES module the hooks load (nodejs/node#59679). The CLI refuses older versions naming the ones to upgrade to, and the Bun and Deno runtimes (Bun has no `registerHooks`; Deno has it but cannot load oxc's addon from a hook); `registerLoader` refuses them too (`NODE_UNSUPPORTED`). No async `module.register` fallback.
- Guards: `pnpm check:install-scripts` (in `pnpm check`) walks the installed tree of every published package and names the chain to any `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` or `binding.gyp` (on main: `e2e > tsx@4.23.14 > esbuild@0.28.2`). A new `install` CI job runs `scripts/install-smoke.ts` with pnpm 11 and 12: packs `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, installs them into a fresh project, installs again from the lockfile, runs a TypeScript test, and fails on a non-zero exit, `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`, or a written `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (on main: `pnpm install` exits 1).
- CI `pnpm test` runs on 22, 24, 26 (`check-latest`) and the floors 22.22.3 and 24.8.0. Vitest externalizes the workspace packages' `dist/` so integration tests load them natively, through e2e's hooks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["import / require"] --> W{written in a compiled file?}
  W -- no --> N[Node resolution]
  W -- "yes: ./x.js, ./x, ./dir, tsconfig alias" --> P[TypeScript file, from the graph's view]
  W -- "yes: # import / package export" --> X[Node resolution, retried on the x.js to x.ts swap]
  P --> N
  N --> F["format from the extension table; e2e-graph query"]
  X --> F
  F --> L{load hook}
  L -- "TypeScript, JSX" --> O["nextLoad source, oxc-transform, inline source map"]
  L -- "JSON, no type attribute" --> J["nextLoad as json, export default JSON.parse"]
  L -- else --> D[nextLoad]
```

## Parity with tsx

Each row has a test: `tests/integration/typescript-loader.test.ts` runs the built CLI on a fixture with all of them, in an ESM package and in a package without `"type": "module"`, with `--workers 2`; `tests/unit/esm-hooks.test.ts` and `tests/unit/typescript.test.ts` cover the rules one by one.

| Case | main (tsx) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| config + tests, `"type": "module"` | yes | yes |
| config + tests, no `"type"` (Next.js-style CJS scope) | yes | yes |
| `.mts` | yes | yes |
| `.cts` with `import type`, `import x = require()`, `export =` | yes | yes |
| `.cts` with ESM `import` statements | yes (esbuild converts) | no, see below |
| `.tsx` and `.jsx` (tsconfig `jsx`/`jsxFactory`) | yes | yes |
| enums, `const enum`, namespaces, parameter properties | yes | yes |
| `experimentalDecorators` (+ `emitDecoratorMetadata`) | yes | yes |
| standard (TC39) decorators | yes (esbuild lowers) | refused with `file:line:col`, see below |
| auto-accessors (`accessor x = 1`) | yes (esbuild lowers) | refused with `file:line:col`, see below |
| `.cts` with `export interface`/`type`/`declare` and `module.exports` | yes | yes |
| package `exports`/`imports` target without extension (`./src/*`) | yes | yes |
| tsconfig `extends` package not installed | yes (ignored silently) | yes, one warning |
| Yarn PnP (`module.register` loader in the chain), `.cts` | yes | yes (not on Node 24.8.0 to 24.11.0, see below) |

| top-level await | yes | yes |
| `.cjs` helper `require()`ing project TypeScript | Node type stripping | yes, through the hooks |

Behavior changes, all in `docs/reference/config.mdx` and the changeset:

- oxc compiles only legacy decorators. Standard decorators without `experimentalDecorators`, and auto-accessors, are refused with their `file:line:col` and the fix.
