title: mobile: worker replacement closes a provider-leased session and drops its device claim
body:
## Problem

A `DeviceProvider` cannot hold its device for the whole run on a local agent-device host. A worker replacement drops the device claim in the middle of the run.

agent-device ties host-wide device claims to a session that has an app open. A provider can take the claim by opening the slot's session (`e2e-<target>-<slot>`) in `acquire`, and the worker then resumes that session. But:

1. `e2e` retires a worker after **every failing unit** (`run/scheduler.js`: `if (worker.sawFailure) this.retire(worker)`).
2. `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s `AgentDeviceSurface.dispose()` calls `client.sessions.close()` on the slot session.
3. That close releases the device claim. Until the replacement worker reopens the session, another agent-device session can take the device or install over it.

The provider can't bridge the gap. It cannot hold a second claim-holding session, because that would block the engine's own session. agent-device 0.21.18 also has no lease that is independent of a session.

## Versions

`e2e@0.15.1`, `@e2e-dev/mobile@0.9.0`, `agent-device@0.21.18`, iOS simulator.

## Ask

When a slot is bound to a provider lease, have worker disposal keep the session (and its claim) open, for example by closing the app instead of the session, and leave closing the session to `finish`/`release`. Alternatively, add a provider hook that runs around worker replacement.

## Context

A per-checkout simulator provider that installs a workspace-specific Release build under the claim: https://github.com/nelearning/chat-app/pull/3012 (`e2e/native/checkoutSimulator.ts`).

title: fix(mobile): redact a malformed openLink's query from its error
body: `device.openLink` builds its `INVALID_ARGUMENT` message from the raw input, so a malformed link still echoes whatever query it arrived with. A magic link carries its one-time token there, and a link that fails to parse is exactly the one nobody has checked yet, so that message lands in logs, the report, and CI output with the token intact. ## What changed - `linkTarget` (`packages/mobile/src/links.ts:43`) now names the input through `linkLabel`, the helper that already cuts a link before its query and fragment for the step label and the report, so the message keeps the useful part (`got "not-a-url"`) and drops the part that can hold a token. - `assertAppId` in the same file already never echoes the link at all, for this reason, and `linkLabel` has been the shared way to show a link safely since `device.openLink` landed. This brings the one remaining message in the file to that standard rather than adding a second rule. - The malformed case is unchanged otherwise: still `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, still the same guidance naming `myapp://orders/42` and `https://example.com/verify`. - `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` states that a string which does not parse as an absolute URL is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and that its message cuts the query and fragment, next to the existing line about the report doing the same. - Patch changeset for `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ```ts linkTarget('myapp://orders/42?ref=mail'); // parses, query kept for the app linkTarget('not-a-url?token=s3cret'); // INVALID_ARGUMENT, got "not-a-url" ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built `@e2e-dev/mobile` from `upstream/main` and from this branch, then called the compiled `linkTarget` from each `dist/links.js` with the same input: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `got "not-a-url?token=s3cret-onetime"` | `got "not-a-url"` | - New unit test in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/links.test.ts` covers three malformed inputs whose query holds a token. It fails on main and passes here, and the existing `links` cases, including the ones pinning that `assertAppId` never echoes a link, still pass. - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run build` and `run typecheck` pass, and `oxlint` on the two changed files reports nothing. - `pnpm docs:check-errors`, `pnpm check:peer-ranges`, and the docs example and package-manager checks pass. - Not run here: the whole `pnpm test` for the mobile package, because this machine reports 55 failures under `captured-snapshots`, `engine`, and `provider` (Windows path and line-ending expectations) that reproduce identically on unmodified `upstream/main`. The `links` file this touches passes in full.

title: feat(oauth): sign in with OpenCode Console for Zen and Go models
body:
Adds OpenCode Console as a subscription provider, so agent steps can run on OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go models with one sign-in. ```ts import { opencodeConsole } from 'e2e/oauth/opencode-console'; const agent = { model: opencodeConsole('deepseek-v4.1-flash') }; // OpenCode Zen, workspace credits const goAgent = { model: opencodeConsole('go/deepseek-v4.1-flash') }; // OpenCode Go subscription ``` - `e2e login opencode-console` runs Console's RFC 8628 device flow (`/console/auth/device/code`, `supports_org_scope`). Approving the code binds the login to one workspace; its id is stored and sent as `x-org-id` to the Console API and `x-opencode-org-id` to inference. Refresh tokens rotate. - On its first call `opencodeConsole()` reads the workspace config (`GET /console/api/config`, the one OpenCode reads) and picks the model's API from it: chat completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Google. `@ai-sdk/anthropic` and `@ai-sdk/google` join the optional peers and load lazily, like `@ai-sdk/openai` for Copilot. - Every inference call carries one `x-opencode-session` per model, which Go requires and Console uses to keep a session on one upstream. - Prompt-cache hints match what the runner adds for OpenAI and Anthropic directly, which it cannot do here because the protocol is only known after the first call: Anthropic breakpoints on the system prompt and, in agent steps, the newest message; the runner's system-prompt cache key and `store: false` for Responses. - `provider` and `modelId` stay fixed (`opencode/`, `opencode.go/`) whichever API serves the model, since the runner reads them before and after the first call. - `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (a Console service account key, the variable OpenCode reads) replaces the stored login in `opencodeConsole()`. `e2e models` still reads the stored login. - `e2e models opencode-console` lists enabled models tagged Zen or Go, leaving out Zen's free models. `e2e init` offers OpenCode Console as a subscription preset. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["opencodeConsole(id)"] --> B{first call} B --> C["GET /console/api/config"] C -- "npm per model" --> D["chat completions"] C --> E["Responses: cache key, store false"] C --> F["Anthropic Messages: cache breakpoints"] C --> G["Google"] C -- "unreadable" --> D D & E & F & G --> H["opencode.ai/inference[/go]/…
x-opencode-session, x-opencode-org-id"] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `e2e login opencode-console` through the built CLI against a real Console workspace with a Go subscription; `e2e models opencode-console` listed 88 models (59 Zen, 29 Go). - Testbed agent suites (`tests-agent/act.e2e.ts`, `tests-agent/judgments.e2e.ts`) through the built CLI with `--no-cache --ai-trace`, on a temporary config using `opencodeConsole()`: | Model | API | Tests | Cached input | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `claude-haiku-4-5` (Zen) | Anthropic Messages | 9/9 | 83% (agent steps 85-96%) | | `go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | chat completions | 9/9 | 55% (misses are mostly the canvas step's screenshots) | ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 9 passed (9) AI 180.8k tokens · 83% cached · 30 model calls · opencode/claude-haiku-4-5 ``` - A forced tool call (what agent steps send) succeeded on `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `gpt-6-luna`, `go/gpt-6-luna`, `claude-sonnet-5`, and `gemini-3.1-pro`. - Two identical ~4.4k-token calls: Anthropic Messages went from 0 cached tokens on the second call without breakpoints to 4,416 of 4,419 with them; Responses (`gpt-5-nano`) read 4,352 of 4,422. - `OPENCODE_API_KEY` with a real Console service account key, a broken stored login in place: a Zen and a Go call both returned 200, every request carried the key as the bearer and no workspace header.

title: feat(web): init scripts run before the page's own, from web({ initScripts }) or browser.addInitScript
body:
## What and why - Adds init scripts, the same thing as Playwright's `addInitScript`. A script runs in every document before the page's own scripts, in every tab and frame. They're needed to mock a browser API (a wallet provider, say), seed `Math.random`, or set a flag the app reads at boot. Until now the migration table listed this as `missing`. - `web({ initScripts })` applies to every attempt. `browser.addInitScript(script, arg?)` adds a script for the rest of one attempt, after the configured ones. - A script is JavaScript source, a `{ path }` relative to the project root, or a function. A function is serialized the same way `evaluate` does it, with the same `__name` helper, now shared as `KEEP_NAMES_HELPER`. Its arg must be JSON, and a secret there is `POLICY_DENIED`. - Scripts are registered on the context, and the attempt's list is applied in the `configure` hook. So they're added again whenever the context is replaced (`app.clearState()`, session restore) and after a CDP reconnect (`reconnectEndpoint`, Kernel `scope: 'attempt'`), with no duplicates (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`, `startAttempt`). - Config files are read in `prepare`, so a bad path stops the run with `INVALID_CONFIG` before any test. Each worker reads them again in `init`, in parallel with the browser launch; a failed read is thrown only after the launch settles, so `dispose` owns that browser (`ConfiguredInitScripts` in `packages/web/src/init-scripts.ts`). - The step label is the file path, or `source` / `function`, never the script's code. - Not implemented: Playwright's `{ content }` (use a plain string), and a remover. Playwright returns a `Disposable`; ours returns `void`, so a remover can come later without breaking anyone. ```ts // e2e.config.ts web({ initScripts: [{ path: 'tests/init.js' }] }) // a test await browser.addInitScript((value) => { Math.random = () => value; }, 0.5); await app.open('/raffle'); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR P[prepare: read config files
bad path = INVALID_CONFIG] --> I[init: read again per worker,
parallel with browser launch] I --> S[startAttempt: list = configured] T[browser.addInitScript] -->|append + add to live context| S S --> C[configure: closed-shadow, then list
new context, clearState, restore, CDP reconnect] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Testbed, `e2e run tests/browser.e2e.ts`: the new test seeds `Math.random` through `browser.addInitScript` and reloads, and `/browser` shows that its own boot script read the seeded value. Full testbed suite: 71 passed, 1 skipped. - Scratch config with `initScripts: [{ path: shim.js }]`: the page sees the shim on first load and again after `app.clearState()`. - The same config pointing at a missing file: ```text ERROR configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (launch) web({ initScripts })[0] path cannot be read: .../apps/testbed/missing.js (ENOENT) Test Files no test files exit 2 ``` - `.e2e/report.json` step: `"api": "browser.addInitScript", "label": "function"`. The script's code (`selectedAddress`) appears nowhere in the report. - Integration tests cover order, frames, a `window.open` tab, `clearState`, carry-over within one attempt and no leak into the next, bad inputs, and CDP reconnect (`cdp-recovery.test.ts`). Breaking the line that re-applies scripts to a new context makes them fail. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: test(web-benchmark): re-record agent recordings for the conservative/6 cache key
body:
The web agent suite replays nothing on main. #732 (3bf295e4) bumped `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` to `conservative/6` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts:28`) and added the agent name and context digest to the key (`packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts:192-194`). Every committed entry sat under an old hash, so each lookup was `no-entry` and the step ran live.

- Re-recorded `tests-agent/` live: 29 new entries.
- Deleted the 29 entries orphaned under the old keys. None of them was rewritten by the new run.
- Cache JSON only.

## Not recorded, and why

| Step | Result | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cart totals `act` | missed | By design: the next step is an `agent.assert` that has to fail on the planted bug, so the trace is never confirmed (`flushStagedTraces`, `cache/context.ts`) |
| wishlist `act` | missed | By design: the act runs into the planted bug and fails, so nothing gets written |
| shadow-dom-form, iframe-form | missed at a gap | The value comes from the screen at run time (`minted-token`, `whole-node`), so the agent types it |
| lying-labels, async-states | handed off at a gap | Same, but at a later action (`pixels`, `minted-token`) |
| control inventory `pick Express delivery` (#788) | no entry | A recorder bug, details below |

The gap steps match main before #732, which had 25 replayed, 2 handed off, and 4 missed.

### `pick Express delivery` cannot replay (follow-up)

The recording stores `goneAnchors: [{ "text": "Express" }]` (the radio label) next to `endAnchors: [{ "role": "status", "name": "Delivery state", "text": "Express" }]`. `describeDelta` compares exact keys, so the label counts as gone. `deltaHolds` uses `fieldsEqual`, which skips fields the anchor leaves out, so `{ text: "Express" }` matches the status output. The recording's own end state fails its own check, and every replay ends in `end-mismatch`. Under `--strict-cache` that is `REPLAY_STALE`. I left the entry out, so this step runs live as it does on main. The fix belongs in `deltaSide` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`), in a separate PR.

`--strict-cache` also does not catch a key change: a `no-entry` step runs live by design. That gap is a separate follow-up too.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Web benchmark, `CI=1 e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` (read-only, same as CI), run twice on this branch.
- The "main" column is the recording run against main's cache: every lookup missed.

| | main | this branch, run 1 | this branch, run 2 | this branch, CI `web agent` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tests | 33 passed | 33 passed | 33 passed | 33 passed |
| Replayed | 0 | 25 | 25 | 25 |
| Handed off | 0 | 2 | 2 | - |
| Missed | 32 | 5 | 5 | - |
| Model calls | 126 | 20 | 21 | 21 |
| Cost | $0.0322 | $0.0035 | $0.0037 | $0.0035 |

title: feat(web)!: pin playwright-core and add a browser install command
body: `@e2e-dev/web` now depends on `playwright-core` pinned to `1.63.0` instead of peering on `playwright >=1.63 <2`. Same model as `@e2e-dev/mobile` pinning `agent-device`: the engine always runs the Playwright it was tested against, and it already reaches into Playwright internals (`cdp-selectors.ts` uses `_channel`), which only an exact pin makes safe. - All `packages/web` imports move to `'playwright-core'`. `playwright` (the test runner on top of core, ~5 MB) is gone from the lockfile. - `e2e init` no longer writes `playwright` into new projects (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts`, `scripts/write-sibling-versions.ts`). - New `e2e-web` bin, so users install browsers for the pinned version without having Playwright as a direct dependency: ```bash npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium --with-deps # npm, also bunx pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps # pnpm cannot exec by package name ``` - `install [chromium|firefox|webkit ...] [--with-deps]` only, chromium by default. It forwards to the bundled `playwright-core/cli.js` and passes SIGINT/SIGTERM on to it, so a cancelled CI job does not leave a download running (`packages/web/src/install.ts`). - The engine's `BROWSER_INSTALL_FAILED` message now points at the new command. - Docs (`reference/web#installing-browsers`, `browser`, `ci`, `migrate/playwright`), the README, and `skills/e2e` drop the peer-dependency story. The `check` CI job installs browsers through the built bin. Breaking for existing projects: remove `playwright` unless the app uses it for its own tests, and swap `npx playwright install` for the command above. Changeset included (`@e2e-dev/web` minor, `e2e` patch). Known gap: the trace docs still say `npx playwright-core@1.63.0 show-trace`, and nothing keeps that version in sync with the pin. Left on purpose: Playwright traces are slated for removal. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Packed `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` into a scratch npm project under `/tmp`: `e2e init --yes` writes no `playwright`, `npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium` fills an empty `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` with revision 1243, and the scaffolded test then runs on that cache with no download: ```text $ npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (playwright chromium v1243) downloaded to /browsers/chromium-1243 FFmpeg (playwright ffmpeg v1011) downloaded to /browsers/ffmpeg-1011 Chrome Headless Shell 153.0.8010.12 (playwright chromium-headless-shell v1243) downloaded to /browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1243 $ npx e2e run --video ✓ |web| tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test) 1.22s ✓ app opens 1.22s Test Files 1 passed (1) ``` - Same in pnpm (`pnpm exec e2e-web`, plus `npx @e2e-dev/web` inside a pnpm project) and bun (`bunx @e2e-dev/web`). - Failure path, download host pointed at a dead port with an empty cache: ```text ERROR infrastructure error BROWSER_INSTALL_FAILED (launch) playwright-core install chromium exited with code 1; run "npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium" (pnpm: "pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium") manually ``` - SIGTERM to the command mid-download: exits 143, the downloader's socket closes, no Playwright process left. `packages/web/tests/integration/cli.test.ts` covers this against a local server that never answers, and fails when the forwarding is removed. - Testbed and web benchmark suites pass on the built packages. - Docs page, `mint dev`: ![reference/web installing browsers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc095dde-689d-4219-9805-cdd195a5f668)

title: fix(cache): record a vanished node only when no end node matches its anchor
body: The web benchmark agent test `control inventory > check picks a radio the pick replaces with its summary` (added in #788) could never replay its `pick Express delivery` step. - Root cause: `describeDelta` decided which nodes vanished by exact descriptor key, while `deltaHolds` checks a gone anchor by matching only the fields it recorded (`fieldsEqual`). The radio label `{ text: "Express" }` was recorded as gone, the status `Delivery state` reading `Express` matched it on replay, and the entry failed its own end check every run (`end-mismatch`, `REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`). - Fix (`packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`): a start node counts as gone only when no end node matches its anchor the way `deltaHolds` checks one (`anchorIn`). The appeared side is unchanged: an appeared anchor always matches the end screen it came from, and dropping one that also matches the start screen would remove a real presence check. - The recorded delta now always holds on the screen it was recorded on. The radio `{ role: "radio", name: "Express" }` and the `Standard` label stay gone anchors, so a pick that leaves the picker on screen still fails. - Commits the one new entry for that step. No other entry changed. ```text before: goneAnchors [... {"role":"radio","name":"Express"}, {"role":"group","name":"Delivery"}, {"text":"Standard"}, {"text":"Express"}] after: goneAnchors [... {"role":"radio","name":"Express"}, {"role":"group","name":"Delivery"}, {"text":"Standard"}] ``` ## No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump - Matching and the replay check are unchanged; only which gone anchors get recorded changes. - The only anchors the fix drops are ones that match the recording's own end screen, so every entry carrying one fails every faithful replay already. An entry that replays today has none, and re-recording it gives the same content. - A bump would re-key every committed entry (what broke the benchmark after #732) to fix entries that are already broken. Read-write runs heal those on their own (the end-mismatch hands off and the step records again). Under `--strict-cache` they need one re-record, which the changeset says. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Unit: new `a radio the pick replaces with its summary` cases in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-anchors.test.ts` build the exact before/after screens. On the base build 2 of them fail (recorded delta fails its own check, `{ text: "Express" }` recorded as gone); here all pass. A replay whose radios stayed on screen still fails the check, before and after. - Web benchmark, base build (#796 head): recorded the step without `CI=1`, then replayed it read-only with `--strict-cache`: ```text × control inventory > check picks a radio the pick replaces with its summary > agent.act "pick Express delivery" 14.33s failed REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays (end-mismatch), and cache.strict hands no step to the agent ``` - Same on this branch: recorded once (2 model calls), then `CI=1 ... --strict-cache` replays it in 155 ms with no model call. - Whole `tests-agent/` suite, `CI=1 e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache`, read-only: | | main (#796) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `pick Express delivery` | missed, 2 model calls | replayed, 0 model calls | | tests | 33 passed | 33 passed | | cache | 25 replayed, 2 handed off, 5 missed | 26 replayed, 2 handed off, 4 missed | | model calls | 21 | 20 | The other 2 handed off and 4 missed are the same steps on both builds: steps the agent ends with a gap, which never record, and the cart and wishlist steps whose planted bugs fail them. ## Follow-up, not in this PR The appeared side has a related older gap in `deltaEvidenced`: a step whose only effect is a text-only node also matching something already on screen (a chip `Express` beside a status reading `Express`) records a delta that holds but is never evidenced, so it never self-finalizes. Fixing it means deciding what to record when no anchor can be evidence, so it is left out here.

title: fix(cache): --strict-cache fails a step whose key changed under its recording
body:
Follow-up to #796, which re-recorded the entries. This PR makes the next cache key change fail loudly.

`--strict-cache` let a cache key change through. #732 bumped `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` and added the agent to the key, so every committed web-benchmark entry became a `no-entry` miss. Strict runs `no-entry` live by design, so the web-agent job kept passing while spending about 120 model calls per run.

- On a strict `no-entry`, the runner now lists the file store and fails the step with `REPLAY_STALE` if an entry recorded for exactly the same step sits under another key. The listing is read once per worker and target, and only on a strict miss (`packages/e2e/src/cache/rekeyed.ts`).
- "Same step" means test, target, instruction digest, params digest, occurrence, and agent name. Entries now record the last three in `recordedFor`. The other key fields count as the environment: replay policy, engine minor, app identity, agent context, and project. A change to any of them makes the step stale.
- Older entries only record test, target, and instruction. One of them could belong to another call of the same instruction, so strict ignores them instead of guessing. A confirmed whole replay in read-write mode proves which step an entry belongs to, so it writes the missing fields in (`completeProvenance` in `cache/context.ts`).
- 25 of the benchmark's 29 entries are migrated in their own commit. I made it with a local read-write replay, no model calls, and only `recordedFor` and `createdAt` change. The other 4 are gap entries that need a live run.
- These still run live: a new or edited instruction or params, a retry, a truncated entry, and non-strict mode (no listing there, so behavior is unchanged).
- `CacheStore` is unchanged. Listing is a method on `FileCacheStore` only, so a custom `cache.store` is not checked.
- The message names the old entry file and repeats the existing re-record advice. It contains only a key hash. Provenance is compared in its redacted form.
- `AgentCacheContext.claimKeyHash` is now `claimKey` and returns the step's provenance. The unused `identity` field is gone.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[strict step] --> B{own key in store?}
  B -- hit --> C[replay as before]
  B -- no-entry --> D{file store holds an entry for exactly this step under another key?}
  D -- yes --> E[REPLAY_STALE, names the old file]
  D -- no --> F[run live]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. Surface: the `apps/web-benchmark` agent suite, run as `CI=1 node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` with no API key. A step that needs a model fails with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, which is how you can tell it went live.

No false positives on this branch with the real policy (`conservative/6`):

```text
      Tests  8 failed | 25 passed (33)
      Cache  25 replayed · 2 handed off · 7 missed
```

There were 0 `REPLAY_STALE`. The 8 failures are the steps that need a model, the same as on main: 3 with no recording, 2 gap hand-offs, and 3 `planted-bugs` judgments.

To simulate a key change I bumped `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` to `conservative/7` locally and did not commit it:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| every recorded step is `no-entry` and handed to the model (`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with no key, a silent pass with one) | all 25 migrated entries fail `REPLAY_STALE` with no model call; the 4 unmigrated gap entries and the never-recorded step run live |

```text
 FAIL   web  tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts > control inventory > check sets the checkbox and the radio
REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays: the store holds it under another cache key (3016a446bf7d9b426938366e1bb8cdd7968d34bb154707fda2509486765e685e.json), since the runner, the engine, the app, or the agent's context changed after it was recorded, and cache.strict hands no step to the agent; re-record it with a read-write run without --strict-cache and commit the changed entry under .e2e/cache
 ❯ tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts:20:5
```

Tests:
- New integration test in `trace-cache-replay.test.ts`. It strips a recorded entry down to the old provenance, and a read-write replay completes it. It then changes the agent's context: strict fails with `REPLAY_STALE` and makes no model call, a lenient run goes live and re-records, and strict replays after that.
- Unit tests in `step-cache.test.ts` cover a legacy entry (runs live), an edited instruction, other params, occurrence, agent, test, or target, a truncated entry, a masked secret in the title, and non-strict mode.
- A `trace-cache-config.test.ts` test checks the provenance completion on keep.

The fresh-context review and cubic both pointed at the old-entry wildcard: an unrecorded repeat could match an earlier occurrence's legacy entry. The fix replaced the wildcard with exact matching plus the migration. The review's other findings are also fixed: the message no longer tells users to delete an entry that may still serve another app identity, and the "once per run" comments now say once per worker and target.

title: fix(mobile): recognize stale-ref refusals by agent-device's typed reason
body:
## What and why

- `staleOr` decided `NODE_STALE` with a regex over agent-device's message. agent-device 0.21.16 gave stale refs a typed `details.reason` ([callstack/agent-device#2960](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/2960), added at this repo's request), and its ref frames refuse with four more reasons. The engine now reads the reason:

  ```ts
  const STALE_REF_REASONS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
    'ref_not_found',
    'ref_frame_expired',
    'ref_generation_mismatch',
    'plain_ref_requires_complete_frame',
    'ref_not_issued',
  ]);
  ```

- Three of the five messages never matched the regex ("minted from a superseded snapshot generation", "needs a complete snapshot", "was not issued by the current ref frame"), so those refusals would fail the action as `ENGINE_FAILURE` instead of re-resolving the node. The engine sends plain refs, so it rarely meets them today; the point is that a reworded message in a later agent-device release can no longer change the classification.
- It keys on the reason alone, not on `details.dispatched === 'no'`: agent-device refuses all five before the action reaches the device, but a drag's refusal comes back as `dispatched: 'unknown'` ([callstack/agent-device#3183](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3183)). Requiring `no` would stop retrying a stale `dragTo` that main retries today.
- The unsupported and no-session message checks stay as they are: a platform refusing a setting or permission e2e itself names (`siri` on Android, `faceid` on Android) still arrives as `INVALID_ARGS` text.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- iOS 26.2 simulator, agent-device 0.21.20 through the engine's client. Each refusal was captured live and passed through `staleOr` from main and from this branch (the pinned ref in row two is sent by hand, to get that reason):

| Refusal | agent-device sends | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `press @e9999` | `ref_not_found`, dispatched `no` | `NODE_STALE` (retryable) | `NODE_STALE` (retryable) |
| `press @e15~s708703` after a newer snapshot | `ref_generation_mismatch`, dispatched `no` | `ENGINE_FAILURE` | `NODE_STALE` (retryable) |
| `drag @e15 @e31` after a tap | `ref_frame_expired`, dispatched `unknown` | `NODE_STALE` (retryable) | `NODE_STALE` (retryable) |

- `E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_SIMULATOR=1 pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile exec vitest run`: unit and simulator integration tests pass on Settings.
- Not run locally: the mobile benchmark. This Mac has Xcode 26.2, which cannot build the Expo SDK 57 app; the PR's mobile jobs run it on iOS and Android.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: refactor(mobile): read agent-device's published snapshot, screenshot, and install types
body: ## What and why - The engine kept hand copies of agent-device's response shapes (`RawNode`, `RawSnapshot`, `RawInstallResult`, `RawScreenshotResult`) and cast the typed client's results to them. A copy drifts silently: #441 fixed one that had dropped `truncated`, so cut trees read as whole. - Each is now derived from what agent-device 0.21.20 publishes, narrowed to the fields the engine reads, and the casts are gone: ```ts export type RawNode = Readonly>; type RawSnapshot = Partial>; type InstallIdentity = Pick; export type RawScreenshotResult = Partial>; ``` - A field agent-device renames or retypes now fails `typecheck` here instead of reading as `undefined`. `InstallIdentity` still leaves `app` out, so reading the echoed build path (the #711 bug) stays a compile error. - No changeset: nothing in `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s emitted `index.d.ts` or `tools.d.ts` changes, and the emitted JavaScript is the same. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Compiled `packages/mobile/src` from main and from this branch with `tsconfig.build.json`: every emitted `.js` file is identical except `surface.js`, where only the parentheses of the two removed casts differ. - `captured-snapshots.test.ts` projects the committed real iOS and Android snapshots to the same golden trees. - `E2E_AGENT_DEVICE_SIMULATOR=1 pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile exec vitest run` on an iOS 26.2 simulator: unit and simulator integration tests pass. ## Checklist - [ ] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(web): provision the chromium build a run launches, and collect nothing in the browsers cache
body:
Fixes #783.

A first run provisioned the wrong thing. The check asked whether the full Chromium build was on disk, and a headless run launches Chromium's headless shell, so the run downloaded a build it never launched. The other way round, a machine holding only the full build — `install --no-shell` — read as installed and then failed to launch the shell it never got. The check now answers for the build the run will launch, the run mode reaches the install, and the install keeps `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_GC=1` so it adds what the run needs without collecting the revisions other tools share that cache with.

`EnginePrepareInfo.headed` is now required, as `EngineInitInfo.headed` already was, so an engine provisions for the browser that run launches.

Verified locally: `pnpm check` green, `pnpm -r run typecheck` 0 errors, 291 unit web, 2518 e2e, 231 mobile.

The `test (22)` failure was caused by the video-segment frame race fixed in #804, now merged into `main`. This branch has been rebased onto that fix; its own checks are running on the rebased head.

title: test(web): wait for a painted frame before closing a video segment
body:
Fixes the integration test that fails in CI with `video/video.webm inked: expected 0 to be greater than 0.0005`.

The failing test is "splits a running trace around a video started mid-attempt". Each segment stopped right after navigating, sometimes before the screencast delivered its first frame. Playwright writes a white frame for a segment with no frames, so the video ended blank. On Linux it failed 6 of 30 runs.

The test now waits for a painted frame before each stop, the same wait the per-page video test already had. Both tests share one paint observer. Since the mid-attempt test records two segments on the same page, the wait clears what the page painted earlier, so the second segment can't pass on the first one's frame.

Verified on Linux (node:22, 4 CPUs): mid-attempt test 0 of 40 failed, full `lifecycle.test.ts` 5 of 5 passed.

title: feat(cache): fallback relocation ladder and recorded replay pacing
body:
## What and why

- Replay matched a recorded control only when every recorded field still held. A relabeled button with a stable test id, a placeholder edit, a link restyled as a button, or `Like (0 likes)` becoming `Like (1 like)` handed the step to the model on every run, and the entry was refreshed only after a relocation failed.
- `relocateWithFallbacks` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/locate.ts`) now walks a ladder once the exact match finds nothing. The first rung that settles on exactly one control wins.
- Every rung still holds the recorded row (`within`) and the recorded place among twins. An ambiguous exact match never falls back, an anonymous control has no fallback, and a test id that points at one control while the name points at another hands off as a conflict.
- A fallback match is acted on only when the next look finds the same control by the same rung (`sightingKey` in `agent/replay.ts`), so a page still leaving is never clicked.
- A replay that needed a fallback re-records the step in `read-write` mode, unless only a tally or time in a label moved (that moves again next run and would rewrite the entry every time).
- `step.cache.relocated` (report schema, both fixtures), `· N relocated` in the run summary, and `agent_steps_relocated` in telemetry count those steps, so read-only CI shows what to re-record.
- Fixes from review: the tally fold reads only a leading count that agrees with its noun; nodes still carrying the recorded test id veto a name pick even when there are several; a test id and name conflict is retried while the screen settles and never resolved by a recorded point; a fallback must hold its place across both looks; an entry counts as consumed only once an action is dispatched.
- `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` stays `conservative/6`: the exact match runs first and is unchanged, so every existing recording still finds the same node. Committed benchmark recordings replay as before.
- `packages/e2e/src/cache/README.md` is the design doc: lifecycle, key, ladder, anchors, routes, templates, write side, testing map, and the audit below. `AGENTS.md` points at it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E{exact match} -- one --> F[act]
  E -- several --> H[hand off]
  E -- none --> T1[test id + role] --> T2[test id] --> A[role + name] --> R[name in role family] --> N[hand off]
  T1 & T2 & A & R -- one, same on next look, no test id/name conflict --> F
```

| Rung | Absorbs | Report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| test id + role, test id | copy change, role change | `test-id` |
| role + name | test id or placeholder change | `accessible` |
| name in role family | `link`/`button`, `checkbox`/`switch`, `textbox`/`combobox` | `role-family` |

### One locator for every lookup

- Action targets, live stale-node re-finds, a target's place among twins at record time, and end-state anchors all go through one lookup (`locate` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/locate.ts`): one projection per observation, the ladder, the container filter, and the test id veto.
- An anchor is split into identity and content. Content is its value, states, text, and its name when that is all the node says (a text node, a button that now reads "Following"). Identity walks the same ladder as a target; content is never loosened.
- A status found by its test id now holds after the region around it was relabeled or an iOS backend reports its role another way. The recorded reading on another node no longer counts while the node with the recorded test id says something else.
- An anchor with no identity left (an unnamed text node), or whose test id was re-minted, is matched on every field at once, as before. `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` stays: target matching is unchanged and anchors never act, and the committed caches replay as before (below).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[recorded descriptor] --> P[candidates: in container, carrying content]
  P --> X{exact tiers}
  X -- match --> V[test id veto]
  X -- none --> L[fallback rungs] --> V
  V --> T[target: exactly one or recorded place]
  V --> A[anchor: any match]
```

### Replay pacing

- A replay waited the full 2 s change timeout after every action whose effect the tree never shows (a right-click opening a native menu, caret keys, a tap that arms the next control), exactly as the recording did.
- The recorder now notes how each action settled: `ObservationFeed` reports whether any capture of the settled look left the action's starting shape, the dispatcher tells the recorder which action armed the wait, and an action that changed nothing is stored `quiet`. A note is dropped when it cannot answer for one action alone (another wait still pending, another action before the look).
- A replay gives a `quiet` action a 300 ms change wait (`QUIET_CHANGE_WAIT_MS`, `ActionDispatcher.withChangeWait`); held-still checks, relocation polling, and the end-state wait are unchanged. The pace is cleared once the call settles, so it never reaches the executor after a hand-off.
- `quiet` is a timing and never counts as a new flow. Entries recorded before learn it once, from the next recording or from a whole replay. A step whose entry did not serve it (anything but a gap) replaces the entry, so a stale mark cannot outlive it. The committed web benchmark entries gain their pacing in this PR.

### Found on a simulator and an emulator

- agent-device switches between two iOS snapshot backends mid-session, and they report one screen differently. A recording now keeps one end-state anchor per label (a wrapper `other "Flow completed"` around the status exists in one backend only), and an iOS screen is named by its navigation bar's identifier: its label is the back button's text on every pushed native-stack screen, so every scenario read as "Benchmark Examples".
- A snapshot the iOS runner rejects mid-animation (`regular-node-outside-cumulative-clip` and two other reasons the engine did not recognize) is retried after the transition lands instead of failing the step with `APP_UNREACHABLE`.
- A replayed action gets one more try, after the screen holds still, only when the engine proves no input was sent (`NODE_STALE`, `FRAME_NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`). An engine fault or timeout may have landed and hands off. agent-device's untouchable-target refusals (`covered_by_interactive_descendants`, `target_covered`, `target_bounds_invalid`) are now `NOT_ACTIONABLE` on mobile (`refusedOr`), which is what the debounced-search result tap hits; a web `check` whose click changed nothing, and a web `press` that timed out on the navigation its key started (log ends at `elementHandle.press(...)`), are `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`.
- A step that starts before the app reaches the screen its recording began on waits for it on the settling backoff (`awaitStartRoute`), then settles on it, instead of missing as `wrong-context`, keeping the step's hand-off reserve. Stripe's demo presents its sheet once a request returns.
- A tapped checkbox, switch, or radio records the state it flipped and relocates only onto the control in that state: a recording that undid an accidental check would otherwise check it.
- A list row was keyed by the list's first visible row (`Row 0499`), unreachable after any scroll; a container key that is a neighbour of the target's own role is dropped.
- The committed iOS and Android recordings were keyed under older engines and replayed nothing on main (about 130 model calls per CI run). Re-recorded: iOS on iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5, Android on Pixel 7 API 36. The web entries are main's (#833).

### Bugs from the audit, fixed here

title: fix(e2e): rewrite downloads with the full ledger pass, the way traces are
body: ## What and why The runner labels a redacted text download `redaction: "complete"`, and `docs/security.mdx` tells users a download is "rewritten the way trace text is". The code behind that label only matched whole secret values, so anything the whole-value pass cannot see sat inside a file that the report and an `ArtifactStore` export both treat as clean. The trace path does more. `redactFragments` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts:129`) runs three passes over the text: whole values, sliding 8-character windows of every registered value, and each base64 or base64url run decoded from all four offsets. `trace-redaction.ts:94` calls it for every text entry in an archive. The download path called `ledger.redact` (`packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts:285`), which is the first pass only, and it still stamped the record `complete`. Where the gap shows up in practice: - An observation cut. The screen reader clips a filled secret to `ad-secret-Qx7-`, the app serves that string later in a CSV export, and the fragment matches no whole value. The file keeps it and gets `complete` anyway. - A base64 copy. The scenario #663 fixed for traces, but served as a download instead of recorded in one: an `Authorization: Basic ` line in a served text export walks through untouched. - The label is what makes it hurt. #561 made the label honest by scanning before stamping, and a store that exports only `complete` files trusts that stamp, so a fragment under it ships. The fix is one line: `redactDownload` now calls `secrecy.ledger.redactFragments(text)`. The doc comment above the function already claimed trace parity, so it stays as it is. `docs/security.mdx` does not change either. It documented the behavior this PR restores, and CONTRIBUTING.md says that where docs and code disagree, the code is the bug. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[download lands] --> B{secret reached the session?} B -- no --> C[kept as served · incomplete] B -- yes --> D{text-like?} D -- no --> C D -- yes --> E["ledger.redactFragments: whole + fragments + base64"] E --> F[rewritten · complete] ``` The change itself: ```ts // packages/e2e/src/run/artifacts.ts, redactDownload - const redacted = secrecy.ledger.redact(text); + const redacted = secrecy.ledger.redactFragments(text); ``` And the test that pins the behavior, run through the real artifact sink (`createAttemptArtifacts`) rather than the ledger in isolation: ```ts const cut = SECRET.slice(6, 20); const encoded = Buffer.from(SECRET).toString('base64'); writeFileSync(path.join(artifacts.dir, 'downloads', 'export.txt'), `cut=${cut}\nencoded=${encoded}\n`); artifacts.sink.register('download', 'downloads/export.txt'); ``` The record says `complete` on both builds. What changes is the bytes on disk. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes On the old code the test fails with the fragment and the base64 run still sitting in the saved file while the record already claims `complete`: ```diff - cut= - encoded= + cut=ad-secret-Qx7- + encoded=ZG93bmxvYWQtc2VjcmV0LVF4Ny0yNzE4 ``` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `cut=ad-secret-Qx7-` left in the saved download | `cut=` | | `encoded=ZG93bmxvYWQtc2VjcmV0LVF4Ny0yNzE4` left in the saved download | `encoded=` | | record says `redaction: "complete"` | record says `redaction: "complete"`, and now the file earns it | - After the change, `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/artifact-store.test.ts` reports `17 passed`, and `pnpm --filter e2e run build` plus `pnpm --filter e2e run typecheck` both exit 0. - End to end through the real runner: `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/trace-secrets.test.ts` passes 9 of 9, including `downloads after a fill: a text download is rewritten, labelled complete, and stored clean` and `downloads without a fill: the file is kept as served and labelled incomplete`. - `pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed -- tests/browser.e2e.ts` against the merge base `b5dc0f8`, 14 pairs in random order: `Every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on every run of both builds.` and every counter matched. Timings resolve to `same`. | Metric | base median (IQR) | head median (IQR) | change (95% CI) | verdict | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | wall (process) | 10.81 s (10.58 s-11.13 s) | 10.61 s (10.08 s-11.00 s) | -2.0% (-4.1% to +1.9%) | same | | suite (sum of attempts) | 3.74 s (3.61 s-3.83 s) | 3.67 s (3.63 s-3.78 s) | -0.7% (-4.0% to +3.3%) | same | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`): `.changeset/download-full-ledger-pass.md`, a patch bump for `e2e`. - [x] Breaking change: no. `redaction` keeps its values and their meaning, the label semantics do not move, so the title carries no `!`. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/security.mdx` already describes this exact behavior ("rewritten the way trace text is"), so there is no prose to fix, and no `skills/e2e/` page covers the redaction passes. - [x] Contract change: none. No emitted `.d.ts` changes and no wire schema touched, since `complete` and `incomplete` already exist in report-1. - [x] Engine contract (`e2e/engine`): not touched, so no engine changesets are needed.

title: fix(run): charge stray rejections in in-process runs like a worker process
body: In-process runs (`rawConfig`, `e2e explore`) installed no `unhandledRejection` or `uncaughtException` handling, unlike the worker entry (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts`). A test body doing `void Promise.reject(new Error('x'))` was never charged to the test: Node's default handler killed the host process mid-run, so no report was written. - `InProcessRunner` (`packages/e2e/src/run/in-process.ts`) now adds both listeners when it starts and removes them in `end()`. They route the same way the worker entry does: abandoned work is ignored, a stray rejection goes to `TargetWorker.strayRejection` (fails the attempt in flight, or `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` between tests), anything else is fatal. - A fatal now ends the in-process worker the way a process dies. The runner marks itself crashed, drops whatever the worker reports while it winds down, and interrupts the unit. On exit the scheduler synthesizes `WORKER_CRASH` for the test in flight and skips the rest of the file, the same as a worker process. Engine disposal errors (`shutdown-done`) still get through, since in-process the engine really is disposed. - Scope: the scheduler keeps at most one in-process runner alive, so nothing is charged twice, and the host's own handlers apply again after the run. `standalone.ts` (`e2e mcp`) is unchanged because it has no test body to charge. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[unhandledRejection] --> A{abandoned?} A -- yes --> X[ignore] A -- no --> S{strayRejection} S -- attempt in flight / last test --> T[charged to test or UNHANDLED_REJECTION] S -- nothing to charge --> F[fatal] U[uncaughtException] --> F F --> C[run error + WORKER_CRASH in flight, rest skipped] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built dist. A host script calls `run()` from `dist/run/runner.js` on a fixture project, once with a file config (worker process) and once with `rawConfig` (in-process). It prints results, run errors, exit code, and the process listener counts before and after the run. - New `tests/integration/in-process-strays.test.ts` runs the same kind of host in a child process, because vitest's own handlers would otherwise catch the rejection first. It covers five cases: a body rejection, a rejection between tests, an uncaught exception, an uncaught exception with an engine whose `dispose` throws, and a rejection before any test finished. All five fail on main (the host crashes) and pass here. I mutation-checked it: dropping the `process.off`, the crashed flag, or the `shutdown-done` pass-through fails the matching tests. Body does `void Promise.reject(new Error('x'))`, followed by a second test: | | worker process | main, in-process | this branch, in-process | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | stray test | failed `x` | host crashes: `Error: x` on stderr, no report | failed `x` | | next test | passed | - | passed | | exit / listeners after | 1 / 0,0 | process exit 1 | 1 / 0,0 | Body throws from a `setTimeout`, followed by a second test: | | worker process | main, in-process | this branch, in-process | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | throwing test | failed `WORKER_CRASH` | host crashes | failed `WORKER_CRASH` | | next test | skipped | - | skipped | | run errors / exit | `ERROR` / 3 | - | `ERROR` / 3 |

title: fix(agent): a forced complete_step turn answered with another tool asks again, not MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED
body: On the last two turns of a step (and after a loop guard or a low clock), the loop offers only `complete_step` and forces it with `toolChoice: { type: 'tool', toolName: 'complete_step' }`. A model that still calls another tool, usually one it saw earlier in the history, makes the AI SDK throw `AI_ToolChoiceViolationError` before anything runs. On main that went through the generic catch and failed the step as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`: an infrastructure code with retries, for model behavior. #739 already handles the SDK throwing this error for a prose reply (`finishReason: 'stop'`, no tool call). That case means the provider downgraded the forced choice, so the loop switches to `auto`. A reply that calls the wrong tool is a different case: the provider answered with a tool call, and the model broke the protocol. So it is handled the way the SDK handles a call to a tool the turn does not offer: - the turn counts as a model call and a turn, like the prose case (`recordThrownTurn`, now shared by both) - the reply goes into the history as the SDK's own history would keep it, with text, reasoning, and tool calls plus their provider metadata (thought signatures). Each call gets an `error-text` result: `peek did not run: only complete_step is available now. Call complete_step with your verdict.` - the model is asked again on the same turn budget, still forced - once the turns run out, the step fails with `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION`, like any step that never concluded ```mermaid flowchart LR F[forced complete_step turn] --> V{AI_ToolChoiceViolationError} V -- prose, finishReason stop --> A[provider downgraded: retry with auto] V -- other tool calls --> E[error results, ask again] E -- turns left --> F E -- out of turns --> N[STEP_NO_CONCLUSION] ``` Code: `packages/e2e/src/agent/tool-loop.ts` `correctForcedTurn`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/tool-choice.ts` `isForcedToolCallMismatched`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A scratch project in `/tmp` with a stub engine and a scripted V4 model, `maxModelCalls: 3`. The model calls the project tool `peek` on turn 1, and calls `peek` again on the first forced `complete_step` turn. Ran the built CLI, `e2e run tests/wrong-tool.e2e.ts`, against main's `dist` and then this branch's. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: Model response did not contain a call to the required tool 'complete_step'.` (1 model call) | `✓ agent.act "look around, then conclude" · 3 model calls` | - Same project with a model that never concludes (`NEVER_CONCLUDE=1`). The branch fails with `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION: agent.act failed: the agent used 3 of 3 turn(s) without calling complete_step`. The `--debug` transcript: ```text --- turn 2 --- tool call: peek({}) [peek] error: peek did not run: only complete_step is available now. Call complete_step with your verdict. [loop] turn 2 called other tools in place of complete_step: asking again --- turn 3 --- tool call: peek({}) [peek] error: peek did not run: only complete_step is available now. Call complete_step with your verdict. ``` - Two new tests in `tool-loop-tool-choice.test.ts` fail on main with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. Mutation checks: dropping the out-of-turns break, the error result text, or the provider metadata on the call each fails a test.

title: fix(e2e): keep runner errors from a config-loaded engine classified
body: An engine loaded from `e2e.config.ts` comes from a second copy of the runner, so its `TestError` fails `instanceof E2EError`. `translateEngineError` only had the `instanceof` check, so it turned the engine's `INVALID_LOCATOR` (and any other runner code an engine throws) into an infrastructure `ENGINE_FAILURE` with exit 3. In-process runs were fine, which is why the in-process web-platform test never caught it. - `isForeignE2EError` becomes `isE2EError` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts`), the one predicate for "runner error from any module copy". It matches local instances too, since they carry the same `Symbol.for` marker. - Every runner-error `instanceof` in `packages/e2e/src` that can see a foreign error now uses it: `translateEngineError`, `translateProvisioningError`, `codedMessage`, `classifyError`, config load, engine session normalize, `expect.poll` not-yet, agent phase codes, `isModelUnreachable`, `toAgentError`, and collection (`isCollectionError`, keyed on `COLLECTION_ERROR`). - Collection had the same bug: a test file collects in its own copy, so its `CollectionError` was reported as `failed to collect : ...` instead of `: ...`. - `classifyAttemptStatus` drops `instanceof TestTimeoutError`; the `TEST_TIMEOUT` code check already covered it. - `@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` already fall back to `name` checks for foreign errors, so they are unchanged. Tests: `tests/integration/foreign-engine-errors.test.ts` runs through `runProjectWithConfigFile` and asserts the caught code, the reported code and category, and the collection message. A unit test pins `translateEngineError`. Mutation-checked: reverting either `translateEngineError` or `isCollectionError` fails them. Follow-up: `oskar/tests-integration` loosened the `*css=` case in `web-platform.test.ts` to assert the message because of this bug. Once both land it can assert `INVALID_LOCATOR` again, like the in-process version on main does. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, a scratch test running `browser.locator('*css=ul[aria-label="Todo column"] >> li').count()` on `/board`: `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-foreign-errors.e2e.ts` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `ENGINE_FAILURE: a selector that captures with * (*css=article >> text=Hello) is not supported: use filter({ has }) instead`, exit 3 | `INVALID_LOCATOR: a selector that captures with * (*css=article >> text=Hello) is not supported: use filter({ has }) instead`, exit 1 | - New integration test fails on main (both `INVALID_LOCATOR` cases get `ENGINE_FAILURE`) and passes here.

title: fix(run): serial group failures reach the exit code and the reporters
body: A serial group whose session failed to launch skipped every member and the run passed with exit 0. Serial failures also never reached the exit code's category fold, so an infrastructure error in a group exited 1, not 3. - Exit code folds serial groups too (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`, `verdictExitCodes`). Members carry no attempts, so the group's attempts are where the error category lives. - A group attempt that ends before any member runs (file load, session launch) fails the first member with the error; the rest skip as `serial-predecessor-failed`. An interrupt during that launch skips every member instead (`endBeforeMembers` in `packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts`). - A retry that never reached its members keeps the member verdicts of the attempt before it, so a launch failure on attempt 1 cannot erase attempt 0's assertion failure or blame a member that passed. - Worker crash during a serial member: that member fails with `WORKER_CRASH` instead of being skipped as never started (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts`). Stacked PR on top: a crash during a retry still drops earlier attempts, and a crash after a member's body ended (in an `afterAll`, the session close) is still charged to that member. Both are fixed there by streaming finished attempts from the worker. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Scratch project in `/tmp` with a custom engine whose `startAttempt` throws `ENGINE_FAILURE`, one serial `describe` with two members, run with the built CLI from `origin/main` and from this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | both members skipped, `exit 0`, report `status: passed` | `step 1` fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE`, `step 2` skipped, `exit 3`, report `status: error` | ```text # main ↓ |device| tests/wizard.e2e.ts (2 tests | 2 skipped) ↓ wizard > step 1 [device would not boot] ↓ wizard > step 2 [device would not boot] Test Files 0 passed | 1 skipped (1) exit 0 # this branch ❯ |device| tests/wizard.e2e.ts (2 tests | 1 failed | 1 skipped) × wizard > step 1 0ms → device would not boot ↓ wizard > step 2 [member 0 failed in this group attempt] FAIL |device| tests/wizard.e2e.ts > wizard > step 1 ENGINE_FAILURE: device would not boot exit 3 ``` Same project, serial group whose second member calls `process.exit(7)`, `--workers 1`: ```text # main ↓ wizard > step 1 passes [worker process exited before this test started] ↓ wizard > step 2 crashes the worker [worker process exited before this test started] ↓ wizard > step 3 never starts [worker process exited before this test started] # this branch ↓ wizard > step 1 passes [worker process exited before this serial group finished] × wizard > step 2 crashes the worker 0ms → worker process exited during this test ↓ wizard > step 3 never starts [worker process exited before this test started] ``` New integration tests in `engine-contract.test.ts` (launch failure, member infra error, interrupted launch, retry launch failure) and `parallel-workers.test.ts` (serial crash) fail on the pre-fix code.

title: fix(secrets): redact plain-string secret values from traces and text downloads
body: ## What and why - A registered secret a test passes as a plain string (`app.open('/?token=' + KEY)`, `fill(KEY)`) was redacted from titles, labels, and agent input since #727, but stayed verbatim in `trace.zip`. #727 left this out on purpose: trace rewriting was gated on the session's exposure level, which only a secret fill or an engine-held secret (basic auth) raises. A plain string raises neither, so the trace was kept as recorded and labeled `not-required`. - The gate assumed the runner sees every way a value reaches the app. It does not: a URL, a `fill`, or the app's own config never touch the exposure model. Traces and text downloads are now rewritten whenever the session's ledger holds a value (every static secret, and a provider's once resolved), the same way reports and observations already are. `redactsRecordings` in `packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts` is the one place that decides. - The `engine` exposure level only fed that gate, so it is removed. Exposure now decides pixels and saved-session taint only. Screencast frames are still dropped only after a secret fill: a plain string is protected as text only, like an engine-held secret. - Labels: a trace from a session that knows a secret value is now `complete` (scanned) instead of `not-required`, and a scanned text download `complete` instead of `incomplete`. `not-required` stays for runs with no secret value. - `tests/integration/plain-string-secrets.test.ts` now records a trace (`trace: 'on'`), adds a plain-string `fill`, inflates every zip entry, and asserts no plain, base64, or base64url form of the value (any case) remains. It fails on main on `trace.zip!trace.trace`. - Docs: `security.mdx` (Redaction, Where redaction stops, the artifacts table), `debugging.mdx`, `reference/engine.mdx`, `reference/errors.mdx` (`TRACE_WITHHELD`), and the AGENTS.md invariant. ```ts export function redactsRecordings(secrecy: SessionSecrecy): boolean { return !secrecy.ledger.isEmpty; } ``` ### Cost Every trace in a project with a secret is now scanned, not just traces after a fill. A trace with nothing to redact is still not rewritten (bytes untouched). Testbed (has `credentials`), full suite with `--trace on`, 70 traces, 9.4 MB: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | wall | 15.4s, 15.9s | 16.4s, 16.5s | | user CPU | 17.6s, 18.8s | 21.6s, 22.1s | | trace labels | 67 `not-required`, 3 `complete` | 70 `complete` | Roughly 55 ms CPU per trace. The scan is the existing `redactFragments` pass from #663; I did not add a prefilter, for the reason #663 gives (it would duplicate the spelling rules). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, scratch config (`trace: 'on'`, `secrets: { probe: 'plain-Zr8Kq2Wm5Tx9' }`) and one test: `app.open('/forms?token=' + S)`, `screen.getByLabel('Full name').fill(S)`, `toHaveValue(S)`. Ran `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.plainsecret.config.ts` on a main build and on this branch, then inflated every zip entry under `.e2e` and counted the plain, base64, and base64url forms of the value (case-insensitive). | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `trace.zip!trace.trace` | 20 | 0 | | `trace.zip!trace.network` | 2 | 0 | | trace `redaction` | `not-required` | `complete` | - Mutation check: putting the old gate back (`return secrecy.exposure.withholdsPixels`) and rebuilding fails the integration test on `trace.zip!trace.trace`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(mcp): redact secrets from open_session, close_session, and server logs
body:
`e2e mcp` returned engine and app errors to the client without secret redaction. `call` results passed the session ledger, but nothing else did. An `endAttempt` that throws with a configured password in its message put the value verbatim into the `close_session` "Cleanup:" line. A failed open did the same with the open error.

- Every fixed tool (`open_session`, `tools`, `call`, `close_session`) now goes through one wrapper in `SessionHost.toolSpecs()`. It turns a thrown failure into an error result and redacts the text with `processSecrets`, which holds every value any session resolved or derived (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts`, `redacting`). The duplicate catch in `server.ts` is gone.
- The config's static secrets go into `processSecrets` as soon as the config loads. Before this, a session registered them only after its engine launched, so an open failure had no ledger to redact with.
- The teardown text is redacted with `processSecrets` at the source. `closeAll` also writes it to stderr as the shutdown summary, and no tool boundary sees that write.
- Host log lines (engine notices, catalog warnings, sessions that end on their own) are redacted before they reach stderr and the client's `notifications/message`.

Text from a config that throws while it evaluates is not redacted: its secrets are not resolved yet, the same as for `e2e run`.

Out of scope: in the `e2e mcp` process, user code's own `console.log` / stderr output (project tools, config top-level code) still reaches stderr raw. `e2e run` redacts worker output with `StreamRedactor`, and the MCP command has no equivalent. That needs its own change.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/mcp-session-host.test.ts`: two new cases fail on main and pass here. One checks a secret in an `endAttempt` error, both through `close_session` and through the `closeAll` shutdown summary. The other checks a secret in a `startAttempt` error and in an engine `init` log line, before any session exists. Mutation-checked: dropping the static registration, the tool wrapper, the teardown redaction, or the log redaction each fails a case.
- The built CLI (`e2e mcp`) on the testbed, driven by a real MCP stdio client. The config wraps `web()` so `endAttempt` (target `leaky-close`) or `startAttempt` (target `leaky-open`) throws `... failed for admin:<password>`, with credential `admin` / `verify-pw-42`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `Cleanup: ENGINE_FAILURE: attempt end failed: endAttempt failed for admin:verify-pw-42` | `Cleanup: ENGINE_FAILURE: attempt end failed: endAttempt failed for admin:<secret:admin.password>` |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE: startAttempt failed for admin:verify-pw-42` | `ENGINE_FAILURE: startAttempt failed for admin:<secret:admin.password>` |

title: fix(run): bound failure evidence to one 5 s capture per attempt
body: - A failed attempt captures the screen and screenshot for failure evidence with a 5 s budget. When the capture came back empty (hung app), the runner tried again at every later capture point (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts` body catch, settle catch, finally), so a hung app paid 5 s per point: measured 11.3 s attempt for a 1.1 s step in `agent-act`, 11.7 s in `engine-contract`. - `captureFailureEvidence` awaited `observe` and `screenshot` without racing the budget, so an engine that ignores cancellation held the attempt forever. - Fix: capture once per attempt (`evidenceTried`), and abandon each engine call when the budget's signal fires (`withAbort`). The original failure is kept; evidence is just absent. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New fake-engine tests in `failure-evidence.test.ts` (hung `observe` that honors / ignores cancellation): on main the first takes 10.5 s with 2 observes, the second hangs to the 30 s test timeout. Branch: 1 observe, ~5.3 s each. Mutation-checked each half of the fix. - Existing slow tests: `engine-contract` "observation outlives the deadline" 11.7 s -> 6.6 s, `agent-act` "page that never settles" 11.3 s -> 6.3 s. - Real web engine, testbed scratch test: `app.open()` to a local server that never responds, `{ timeout: 3_000 }`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× fails on a page that never loads (timed-out) 13.08s` | `× fails on a page that never loads (timed-out) 8.08s` | Side finding, not in scope: on the web engine, `app.open()` to a never-responding server and a locator `tap()` on a frozen renderer (busy loop) both wait for the test timeout, not `actionTimeout`.

title: perf(agent): stop re-waiting for a lost list on every repeat of a replayed scroll
body: A replayed folded scroll (one recorded `scroll` with `times: N`) on a list that filled the screen re-ran the full relocation backoff before every repeat when the list could not be found. `pollSettled` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/replay.ts`) waits about 14s per relocation, so a recorded 4x scroll spent about 56s before falling back to the viewport each time. - `scrollOnce` now reports whether it scrolled the list, scrolled the viewport (list lost, `spans >= MAIN_LIST_SHARE`), or failed. Once a list is judged lost, the rest of the repeats in that scroll go through the viewport path: a settled `held-still` look, then a scroll, with no new relocation. - The list and viewport repeats share one loop now. - Unchanged: a smaller region (`spans` below the share) still hands off on the first miss, the count of repeats done before a miss is kept, and the cache key and recordings are untouched. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[repeat i] --> B{list still tracked?} B -- yes --> C[relocate, up to 14s] C -- found --> D[scroll list] C -- lost, fills screen --> E[scroll viewport, stop tracking list] C -- lost, small region --> F[hand off] B -- no --> G[held-still look, scroll viewport] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Unit: new test in `tests/unit/trace-replay.test.ts` uses fake timers to replay a 4x scroll whose list is gone. It asserts the elapsed clock (14000ms) and the looks: one backoff of 9, then one `held-still` look per later repeat. On main it fails with `expected 56000 to be 14000`. - Runner: a scratch integration test (not committed) runs the built runner through the fake engine on an `ios` target with `cache: 'read-write'`. The first run records an executor that scrolls `list "Feed"` (97% of the viewport) four times, folded to one action with `times: 4`. Before the second run the list is renamed (`Feed, row 13 of 40`, the way a device renames a scroll view) and the step replays: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | replayed `agent.act` step | 56369 ms | 14324 ms | | cache | `self-finalized`, 1/1 | `self-finalized`, 1/1 | | swipes / test | 4 / passed | 4 / passed |

title: test(e2e): integration suites on the fake engine, cut to what only integration proves
body:
The `packages/e2e` integration suite, trimmed to what only an integration run proves. Suites that don't read a page run on the fake engine, and fixed sleeps become event-driven waits. Test-only.

- Fake engine: runner lifecycle, run events, parallel workers, reporters, `expect.poll` scope, `expect.soft`, extended fixtures, and `runProject` without an app URL. A browser starts only where a page is read.
- Folded: `mcp-custom` into `mcp-server` (one server), the class and URL-pattern suites into `web-platform`'s config-file run, the stale `--strict-cache` run into the changed-screen suite, semantic fallback into `agent-fallback-handoff`, and serial artifact checks into `artifact-store-serial`.
- Dropped: integration cases that unit tests or the testbed already pin (each checked for a surviving test before the cut), the `trace-cache-speed` wall-clock gate (its replay check lives in `trace-cache-replay`), and line-by-line prose checks.
- Stronger: secret suites now read the model input and inflated `trace.zip` entries, not just the run result, and fail their deliberate tap in 500 ms instead of the 30 s action timeout. Project tool results and errors in MCP go through the secret ledger. `engine-target` asserts `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` and its category, not a message regex.
- New: Ctrl-C releases what `prepare` acquired, plus exit 3, `--shard`, and CI defaults through the CLI, and a timeout on the worker path.
- `engine-contract.test.ts` is also edited by #813 (`oskar/fix-serial-verdicts`). Whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase. Merged together, both are green.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes (full `packages/e2e` integration suite, `--maxWorkers=3`, on a shared machine)

| e2e integration | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tests | 622 | 535 |
| wall time | 240 s | 111 s (132 s on a loaded run) |

Mutation checks on the moved and rewritten tests. Each mutation was made in `src`, rebuilt into `dist`, run against the one test file, then reverted.

| mutation | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| absent-frame reads poll to the deadline before returning no match (`src/locator/engine.ts`) | `web-platform` absent-frame duration (< 3 s) |
| `abandonRunning` marks the step passed, or returns no error (`src/run/steps.ts`) | both `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` step tests in `expect-poll-scope` |
| a read on a detached node reports hidden (`packages/web/src/read-selector.ts`) | `web-replaced-nodes`, normal and starved; the 3-read starved case caught it 3/3 |
