The last five were cut first and then restored after self-review or bot review, because nothing else covered them. Fake-engine runs no longer inherit the caller's `APP_URL`. The MCP session TTL and idle polls also got a 5 s timeout: with a 500 ms TTL, the default 1 s poll left too little slack on a loaded runner.

title: feat!: drop Playwright trace recording
body: Playwright trace zips were the debugging artifact for a failed test, but an agent can't read one without a GUI viewer, the screencast is withheld after a secret fill, and devices have no trace at all. This removes trace recording. The failure pages in the stacked PR take its place. - `trace` in the config or on a target is `INVALID_CONFIG`, on a test, describe, or setup `COLLECTION_ERROR`, and `--trace` (bare or with a mode) on `run` and `explore` exits 2. Each names the replacement: the markdown reporter's failure pages, or `video` for a recording. - `video` keeps every mode and the config < target < CLI < test precedence. `trace-modes.test.ts` is ported to `video-modes.test.ts`, so on-all-retries, retain-on-failure, serial groups, and test-beats-config stay covered. - Engine contract: `startTrace`/`stopTrace` leave `EngineArtifacts`. An engine published before this (`@e2e-dev/web@0.11.2` allows `e2e >=0.15 <1`) still declares them, so the manifest accepts and never calls them (`packages/e2e/src/engine/manifest.ts`, `RETIRED_HOOKS`) and updating `e2e` alone keeps working. - report-1 drops the `trace` artifact kind, `trace` in `artifactCapabilities`, and the `not-required` redaction; `TRACE_WITHHELD` is gone. Schema, valid fixture, and producer change together. - Dead code deleted: `run/trace-redaction.ts`, `internal/zip.ts`, the ledger's `appearsIn`, the web engine's trace segments around restarts and CDP recovery, telemetry's `config_trace_modes`. `redactFragments` stays: text downloads use it since #806. - A video segment waits up to 1s for its first frame before it ends (`packages/web/src/video.ts`). Without the trace keeping the screencast busy, a segment stopped right after a navigation got no frame on Linux, and Playwright writes that as a white video: the `video.webm inked 0` failure `main` also hit. Reproduced and verified in the `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble` container. - The late route-handler tests route a script the page waits for (`/script-flags`) instead of a fetch it issues after load, which raced the end of the body once tracing no longer slowed it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, `e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts`: 7 passed, no `trace/` directory or zip written. `--video` still writes one `.webm` per attempt. - `trace: 'on'` in a copy of the testbed config, `--trace`, `--trace=on`, and `explore --trace off`: each refused, exit 2, with the replacement message. - The packed `e2e` from this branch with the published `@e2e-dev/web@0.11.2` and `playwright@1.63.0` in a scratch project: the config loads and the test runs (before the manifest fix it was `INVALID_CONFIG: engine "web": artifacts has unknown key "startTrace"`). ```text FAIL |web| tests/hello.e2e.ts > hello ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed Tests 1 failed | 0 passed (1) ``` (The failure is the deliberate assertion; no config error.)

title: feat: write a failure page per failed test with each step's actions, polls, cache decision, and app log
body: Stacked on #822. When a test fails, a coding agent (or a person) should read one file and know what happened. Today that file is opt-in (`--reporter markdown`), deterministic steps record nothing (`events: []`), the cache's decision never leaves `report.json`, and console errors and failed requests exist only inside the trace zip the parent PR removes. Every run now writes a page per failed or flaky test under `.e2e/failures/`, and each step on it says what it did. ```mermaid flowchart LR E[web engine: console, pageerror, requestfailed, 4xx/5xx] -- appLog --> R[StepRecorder: redact, file under the step] L[LocatorEngine: node acted on] --> R P[expect / waitFor: sample history] --> R C[step cache: stop point, write outcome, entry] --> R R --> J[report.json events] J --> F[runner writes failures/*.md] F --> T["terminal: ❯ details failures/x.md"] ``` - **Engine hook:** `EngineAttemptContext.appLog({ source, level, text })`. The session adapter checks each entry, holds it until a step recorder takes it, and files it under the step that started last, redacted then clipped (200 per attempt). The web engine reports console errors and warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and 4xx/5xx responses (`packages/web/src/app-log.ts`). - **Deterministic steps:** an `engine` event per action names the node from the resolve's own cache, no engine call (`tap button "Add" (appeared after 1200ms, went stale 1x)`); a point action names its point (`tap at (120, 48)`). `expect` and `waitFor` record a `poll` event with the readings in order: one value the whole time is a wrong expectation, changing values are a race. - **Cache:** `step.cache.entry` (the file), `detail` (`at action 2 of 3, tap button "Apply": ...`, or the recorded end state that never showed), and the report-only `write` (`saved`, `kept`, `unconfirmed`, `evicted`, `no-change`). New entries store their key's context, so a rekeyed `REPLAY_STALE` names what changed: `since the app's identity (app.identity, else its URL) or environment changed`. Existing entries are not rewritten to gain it. - **Also recorded:** the hook a step ran in (`step.phase`), loop-guard and wind-down notes on the agent's turns, and the message of a failed agent action. - **Output:** the runner writes the pages before `run-finished` (named `--<16 hex of the result id>.md`) and names them in the event and `FinishedRun.failurePages`. The `markdown` reporter keeps only `summary.md`, linked to them. A page that cannot be written is a stderr line, like `junit.xml`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, a scratch config with a scripted model (no provider key) and four failing tests: agentic, agent step then a wrong expectation, a missing locator, and a page that logs errors. `e2e run`: ```text FAIL |web| tests-audit/audit.e2e.ts > app: the page breaks while the test runs LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator did not become visible: getByRole("heading", name: "Todos") ❯ at http://127.0.0.1:4388/nope ❯ app 2 errors, 2 warnings logged ❯ details .e2e-audit/failures/audit-app-the-page-breaks-while-the-796fac5f.md ... Failures .e2e-audit/failures/ (4 pages: steps, cache, app log, screen) ``` The page's steps: ```markdown 1. ✓ `app.open` `/todos` (37ms in beforeEach) — `tests-audit/audit.e2e.ts:4` 2. ✓ `browser.evaluate` (3ms) — `tests-audit/audit.e2e.ts:24` - ✗ console error: `failed to load todos: TypeError: items is undefined` 3. ✓ `app.open` `/nope` (5ms) — `tests-audit/audit.e2e.ts:30` - ✗ uncaught error: `RangeError: render loop exceeded at eval (...)` - ⚠ network warning: `GET /api/missing 404 Not Found` - ⚠ network warning: `GET /nope 404 Not Found` 4. ✗ `locator.waitFor` `getByRole("heading", name: "Todos") → visible` (1.0s) — **LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND** - waitFor gave up after 11 reads in 1.0s: absent x11 ``` and for the agent step that passed before a wrong expectation: ```markdown 2. ✓ `agent.act` "Add a todo named Milk." (420ms, 2 model calls) - cache: no replay: nothing recorded for this step yet; recording saved (`.e2e/cache/1227d5a6….json`) - type "Milk" into textbox "New todo" (18ms) - press "Enter" on the focused field (4ms) 5. ✗ `expect.toHaveText` `getByRole("status", name: "Remaining")` (1.6s) — **ASSERTION_FAILED** - expect gave up after 16 reads in 1.6s: text "0 remaining" (1 match) x16 ``` - Second run of the same suite: `cache: replayed all 2 recorded actions, no model call; recording kept`. Changing the app port and running with `--strict-cache`: `REPLAY_STALE ... since the app's identity (app.identity, else its URL) or environment changed after it was recorded`. - web-benchmark agentic suite, `CI=1 --strict-cache` with committed recordings and no key: 26 replayed. The 7 failures are steps that call the model by design, and the failure pages said so (`no replay: a retry never replays`, `at action 2 of 3, tool type (run-time value)`). <!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. --> <a href="https://cubic.dev/pr/tester-army/e2e/pull/823?utm_source=github" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-no-image-dialog="true"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-light.svg"><img alt="Review in cubic" src="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-dark.svg"></picture></a> <!-- End of auto-generated description by cubic. -->

title: fix(run): kill a worker that blocks its event loop past the test timeout
body: A test body that blocks the worker's event loop (`while (true) {}`) never timed out: the test timeout is a timer inside the worker, which never fires, and the runner had no deadline of its own. The run hung until someone killed the worker process. Ctrl-C did not end it either. - The worker sends `attempt-deadline` (test timeout and `cleanupTimeout`) when an attempt's timeout starts, and `attempt-end` when the attempt ends (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`, `worker/session.ts`). - From the deadline on, the scheduler sends `ping` once per `cleanupTimeout` (at least 5 s). The worker answers `pong` right away, outside its unit queue. A worker that misses one is SIGKILLed through the existing crash path (`SchedulerWorker.watch` in `packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts`). A worker still tearing down a timed-out attempt keeps answering and is not killed. - The hung test is reported `timed-out` with `TEST_TIMEOUT` (exit 1, no `WORKER_EXIT` run error). The file's tests it never reached are put back in the queue and run on a new worker, as they would after a normal timeout. If the target failed meanwhile (workers could not boot), they are skipped instead of left in a queue nothing reads. - `worker/entry.ts` `send` now passes every message to the channel right away. It used to wait for the previous message's write callback, so an `attempt-deadline` sent just before a blocking body (for example a serial member right after the previous one) never left the process. - No watchdog for a worker with a debugger attached when the attempt starts (editor auto-attach, `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect=0`), so a paused breakpoint is not killed. In-process runs (inline config, in-memory tests) share the runner's event loop, so nothing can enforce the timeout there. The docs say so. - Builds on #837: the kill goes through its crash bookkeeping (`synthesizeCrashResults`). The attempts finished before the hung one stand, and the hung one is appended at its index as `timed-out` / `TEST_TIMEOUT`, with the id and start the worker sent in `attempt-deadline`. It is not retried. A hung serial member settles through `SerialGroupProgress.crashed` with status `timed-out`: earlier members keep their records, the ones after it skip. - The `send` change in `worker/entry.ts` was the same in #837, so there is one implementation now. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as scheduler participant W as worker W->>S: attempt-deadline (timeout, cleanupTimeout) Note over W: body blocks the event loop S->>W: ping (at timeout) Note over S: no pong within cleanupTimeout (>= 5 s) S->>W: SIGKILL S->>S: report timed-out, requeue unreached tests ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, a scratch `tests/zz-busy.e2e.ts` (a 2 s timeout test that runs `app.open()` and then `while (true) {}`, followed by a passing test), `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-busy.e2e.ts --workers 1` with the default 30 s `cleanupTimeout`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Hung. `timeout 120` sent SIGTERM and the run still did not end. It finished only after I `kill -9`'d the spinning worker at 212 s, with both tests skipped and a `WORKER_EXIT` error | Ended in 34 s, exit 1 | main: ```text ERROR infrastructure error WORKER_EXIT worker for target "web" exited unexpectedly (code null, signal SIGKILL) during file::web::tests/zz-busy.e2e.ts Test Files 0 passed | 1 skipped (1) Tests 0 passed | 2 skipped (2) Duration 211.96s (3m 32s, startup 86ms) ``` this branch: ```text ❯ |web| tests/zz-busy.e2e.ts (2 tests | 1 failed) 32.13s × blocks the event loop (timed-out) 32.01s ✓ runs after it 123ms FAIL |web| tests/zz-busy.e2e.ts > blocks the event loop TEST_TIMEOUT: test ran past its 2000 ms timeout and its worker stopped responding, so the worker was killed Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2) Duration 32.82s ``` (The branch output above was captured before the message wording changed. The behavior is the same.) After the rebase on #837, same testbed setup with `retries: 1`, attempt 0 throws, attempt 1 `while (true) {}`: exit 1 in 34 s, `report.json` attempts `[[0, failed, ERROR "first attempt fails"], [1, timed-out, TEST_TIMEOUT]]`, the next test passed. Tests: new integration tests in `parallel-workers.test.ts` cover a body that blocks immediately, one that blocks after a step, a serial member, and a slow teardown that answers pings and is left alone. The first one hangs on main, and the slow-teardown test fails if the worker's `ping` handler is removed. Scheduler unit tests cover the kill and requeue, and pings that are answered. Added for the #837 integration: the retry case above (integration and unit) and a target that fails while a worker hangs (unit, hung forever before the fix). Mutation-checked: dropping the kept attempts or the serial `timed-out` status fails them.

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- [#775](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/775) [`d1f2089`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d1f2089081219ab0a8a07d49adb0195623738b40) Thanks [@guhcostan](https://github.com/guhcostan)! - Add `@e2e-dev/decision`, an executor that runs `agent.act` and `agent.assert`
  through a decision model instead of an LLM. It takes any AI SDK decision
  model with choice distributions (`evaluationModel()` instances too) and
  decides through `experimental_decide`, so it needs `ai` 7.0.128 or later. One
  call per action fans out the operation and target questions; a small
  language model writes field values when the choice is `type`. Tests stay
  plain natural language with no params. Probability and confidence gates are
  off by default. A model id string or a language model fails config load with
  `INVALID_CONFIG`.
## e2e@0.18.0

### Minor Changes

- [#851](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/851) [`dc2afca`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/dc2afca0c02a882e2631a18f9d49768c4e4d84f2) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `e2e mcp` sessions are now headless by default, the same as `e2e run` and `e2e explore`, and the agent decides per session: `open_session {headed: true}` shows the browser or simulator, `headed: false` hides it. `--headed` makes headed the default for sessions that do not say. Before, sessions were headed outside CI and only the server's `--headless` could hide them; `--headless` is still accepted, since it now asks for the default, but it is no longer documented.

- [#790](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/790) [`0d1ed15`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0d1ed15871674aafd0ee3eff92c17eb39f6012bd) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Breaking: e2e and every `@e2e-dev` package now need Node.js 22.22.3 or newer on Node.js 22, or 24.8.0 or newer** (`engines.node` is `^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0`). Node.js 22.12 through 22.22.2, 23, and 24.0 through 24.7 are no longer supported, and the CLI refuses to start on them, naming the versions to upgrade to. Those releases fail when a CommonJS file a test imports requires TypeScript through the new loader's `module.registerHooks` (nodejs/node#59679 fixed it in 22.22.3 and 24.8.0).
  
  e2e now loads TypeScript with its own loader, built on oxc, instead of tsx. tsx brought in esbuild, whose postinstall script made every `pnpm install` on pnpm 11 and later fail with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` until the project approved the build; nothing e2e installs runs an install script now. Config and tests load as before: ESM whatever `package.json` says, `./x.js` and `./x` resolve to `x.ts` and `./x.jsx` to `x.tsx`, directory index imports, tsconfig `paths` and `baseUrl`, workspace packages exporting `.ts` source, JSX in `.tsx` and `.jsx`, enums, namespaces, `experimentalDecorators`, and source-mapped stack traces. JSON imported without `with { type: 'json' }` still loads. A test file whose name holds `%`, `#`, or a space now collects with its source location instead of failing with "URI malformed" or losing the location. Each file reads its nearest `tsconfig.json` rather than the one in the working directory. What changes: `import` statements in a `.cts` file are no longer compiled into `require` calls (write `import x = require()`); standard decorators without `experimentalDecorators`, auto-accessors, and ES module `import` and value `export` declarations in `.cts` are refused with their line (`import type`, `export type`, `import x = require()`, and `export =` work); the CLI refuses the Bun (`bun --bun`) and Deno runtimes (install with any package manager, run on Node.js); a type imported without `import type` that stays in the output (a decorated member's type under `emitDecoratorMetadata`) fails to load, with an error naming the import; a `.ts` file a CommonJS file requires runs as an ES module like every other `.ts`, so one written with `module.exports` needs the `.cts` extension; and an import written in a JavaScript file resolves as Node.js resolves it, without TypeScript's extension rules or tsconfig `paths`. TypeScript inside an installed package compiles without the project's `tsconfig.json`.

- [#840](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/840) [`b33398f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b33398fc380a1ecd8a0784d1c5c2fcbdeefaf841) Thanks [@Mohit20057](https://github.com/Mohit20057)! - `screen.swipe({ from, to, duration })` adds an optional `duration` for path swipes, controlling how long the gesture takes in milliseconds.

### Patch Changes

- [#834](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/834) [`8bc7d85`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/8bc7d850cb0082122100a20bb710f7f0c9691f25) Thanks [@Ray0907](https://github.com/Ray0907)! - A recorded step that types an empty value, which clears a field, replays instead of failing with `REPLAY_STALE` (`invalid-entry`). The cache wrote the entry but its reader rejected the empty `type` or `typeText` value, so such a step could never replay from a recording.

- [#806](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/806) [`f7f60ba`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7f60bae469b2febb984c27a97d9ad6920f02979) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - A text download is rewritten with the full ledger pass — fragments and base64-encoded forms of a secret included — the way trace text entries already are. The download path only matched whole values while still labeling the file `redaction: "complete"`, so a cut or base64 copy of a secret could sit in a download the report vouched for as clean.

- [#803](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/803) [`f2f9a53`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f2f9a5373d520c35514da713c3f0c18a343b96ff) Thanks [@fecolinhares](https://github.com/fecolinhares)! - `EnginePrepareInfo.headed` is now required, alongside the `headed` an engine already receives on `init`. A host that builds a `prepare` call now passes the run's mode, so an engine provisions for the browser that run launches.

- [#836](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/836) [`5603af1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5603af1bee11c55a6463769934b37a8f9d32e060) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - Run-level errors in reports (hook, collection, provisioning, and worker failures) are now redacted with the config's secrets.

- [#819](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/819) [`aeaca4f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/aeaca4fa4626c224cb3e84cfab10fd5bf87b889d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A failed attempt on an app that stops answering no longer waits 5 s for failure evidence at every capture point, or forever when the engine ignores cancellation. The runner captures the screen and screenshot once per attempt, stops waiting after 5 s, and keeps the original error.

- [#810](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/810) [`366766d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/366766df501cb75d817c2cc150092306883ee6eb) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - An agent step whose model answers a forced `complete_step` turn with another tool no longer fails as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. The call goes back to the model as an error and the turn is asked again within the step's turn budget; a model that never concludes fails the step with `STEP_NO_CONCLUSION`.

- [#811](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/811) [`8b552c2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/8b552c2f4cc6816ae1704e18ebe85187cd11b0e5) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - An error an engine throws with a runner code, such as `INVALID_LOCATOR` for an unsupported selector, keeps its code and category when the engine is loaded from `e2e.config.ts`. It was reported as an infrastructure `ENGINE_FAILURE`.

- [#809](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/809) [`9995932`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/99959329cd00cc905f4fc2838d7ace3f698ad8bc) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A run that executes in the host process, such as `e2e explore`, no longer crashes that process when a test leaves a promise rejection or an exception uncaught. It handles them as a worker process does: a rejection fails the test running when it surfaces, or is recorded as `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` between tests. An uncaught exception, or a rejection that surfaces with no test running before any test has finished, is a run error that fails the test on its way with `WORKER_CRASH` and skips the rest of its file. The handlers are removed when the run ends.

- [#911](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/911) [`7aafa00`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7aafa007e61a7a0d5e5460f219a3ec275e1f9c75) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `agent.assert` and `agent.waitFor` fail when the value they check is shown more than once and one place contradicts it, such as a correct order summary total next to a wrong pay button total. A claim about some item among several, such as `a todo is marked done`, still holds when one item matches.

- [#815](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/815) [`79497a7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/79497a7efe0ee7d0f40b3888fc091e62da84aaf6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e mcp` now redacts secret values from everything `open_session` and `close_session` return and from its log lines. Before, an engine or app error that carried a configured secret, in a failed open or in a `close_session` "Cleanup:" line, reached the client and stderr verbatim.

- [#894](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/894) [`9ae674e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9ae674e61603dbbeddce958552e64ee81f69675c) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Honor project tools' toModelOutput renderers for string results and preserve rendered error outputs as MCP error results.

- [#826](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/826) [`ac1c610`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ac1c61075d4d75ac48ac9a8506e29947a4cf304d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e mcp` now redacts secret values from what your code prints through `console`, `process.stdout`, or `process.stderr`, such as a `console.log` in a project tool or in the config's top-level code. Before, it reached stderr verbatim. Output printed while a config loads appears once the config has loaded; if the load fails, that output is withheld, since the config's secrets are unknown. An uncaught error or unhandled rejection is logged redacted and the server shuts down its sessions and exits with code 1, instead of crashing with the raw error.

- [#847](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/847) [`2e26ec6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2e26ec65510356508f680d70e85624d86a8c4c25) Thanks [@agammann](https://github.com/agammann)! - Include npm's argument separator in CLI hints so flags such as `--headed` reach the installed `e2e` binary.

- [#814](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/814) [`78e135a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/78e135a37227eb1ea6d6a93abb99ad4419e29ece) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A secret value a test passes as a plain string (spelled into an `app.open` URL, typed with `fill`) no longer stays in the Playwright trace. Traces and text downloads are now rewritten whenever the session knows a secret value (every static one, and a provider's once resolved), not only after a secret fill or an engine-held secret, so they are labeled `redaction: "complete"` instead of `not-required` or `incomplete`. Screencast frames are still dropped only after a secret fill. Like any secret trace, a rewritten one masks unrelated text that shares 8 characters with a value.

- [#902](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/902) [`032825f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/032825ffe11921c08555df19256c8e466377fd7e) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Preserve environment and client settings on existing e2e MCP registrations when rerunning init.

- [#820](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/820) [`a561f06`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a561f06eb31e735a3d6e245f335806e9ddd4b469) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Replaying a repeated scroll on a list that filled the screen, when the list can no longer be found, waits for it once and then scrolls the screen for every remaining repeat. It used to wait out the full relocation backoff (about 14 seconds) before each repeat, so a recorded 4x scroll took about a minute to replay.

- [#837](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/837) [`338378e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/338378ed484794de3617ae3621d54b91ec7ed93d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A worker that crashes during a retry no longer drops the attempts before it. Before, a test whose first attempt failed and whose retry crashed the worker showed a single attempt 0 with `WORKER_CRASH`, and the first attempt's error was lost. The report now keeps every finished attempt and adds the crash as the next one. A crash after the last attempt (in an `afterAll`) is recorded on that attempt instead of as a retry. For a serial group, the finished group attempts and the members that finished in the crashed attempt stay in the report, the member that was running fails with `WORKER_CRASH`, and a crash after a member finished fails the group attempt without blaming that member. A forced interrupt keeps the attempts that finished and the verdict they reach, `flaky` included.

- [#829](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/829) [`01b88d3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/01b88d3afd691d2bf2a3260966c48194e626a5ff) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e run` redacts secret values from what the config's top-level code, a test file's top level, and reporters print, as it already did for tests, including what a timer or a reporter the run stopped waiting for prints after the run. Output printed while the config loads appears once it has loaded, and is withheld if the load fails. With the `list` reporter, output printed during the run prints under `stdout | runner` or `stderr | runner`, on stdout like a test's output, so the live view no longer paints over it.

- [#813](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/813) [`87e75ae`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/87e75ae808d76fa07b66fba9e5c5f3a48be3c31c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A serial group whose session fails to launch, or whose file fails to load, now fails the run. Before, every member was skipped and the run passed with exit code 0. The first member now fails with the launch error and the rest skip with cause `serial-predecessor-failed`, so the `list` reporter, `summary.md`, and `junit.xml` show the failure. A retry that fails to launch keeps the members' verdicts from the attempt before it, so a member that failed there still fails. An infrastructure error in a serial group, at launch or in a member, now exits 3 and sets the run status to `error`, as it does for any other test, instead of exiting 1. When a worker crashes during a serial group, the member that was running fails with `WORKER_CRASH` instead of being skipped as if it never started.

- [#827](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/827) [`6f528be`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6f528be1a8681945b4002dd9c2e967f6fe3f8b1f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - After a secret fill, an agent step whose screen can only be read from a fallback screenshot (`act`, or a judgment with `vision: true`) now fails with `POLICY_DENIED` naming the secret fill, instead of the engine's timeout.

- [#888](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/888) [`5e032d9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5e032d95a903fe2fd190166bbe9aa78f81fb7d91) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Telemetry no longer sends a project id outside git or in a shallow clone, and a coding agent that sets `CI` outside a CI vendor counts as the machine it runs on. EAS Build, Bitrise, Codemagic, and Xcode Cloud are recognized as CI vendors.

- [#828](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/828) [`c83b86f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c83b86f4917d41cf5cf5941d909fb5f087916b88) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A page whose script never yields no longer holds a web test until its test timeout: a tap, a locate, or a navigation on it now fails with `ACTION_FAILED` at its action or navigation timeout, also while a trace records. A tap or keystroke cut off that way may have reached the page and is never repeated by a replay. `expect(browser)` matchers on such a page end at their own timeout instead of the action timeout.

- [#824](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/824) [`37806d7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/37806d7fc34b1c2532344a554d96bfcdb8ec2f7a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A test that blocks its worker's event loop (`while (true) {}`) no longer hangs the run until Ctrl-C. When the worker has not responded `cleanupTimeout` (at least 5 s) after the test timeout, the runner kills it, reports the test `timed-out` with `TEST_TIMEOUT`, and runs the rest of the file on a new worker. A worker with a debugger attached when the test starts (an editor's auto-attach, or `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect=0`) is never killed this way. Runs with an inline config or in-memory tests run in the runner's own process and still hang.
## @e2e-dev/eas@0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- [#790](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/790) [`0d1ed15`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0d1ed15871674aafd0ee3eff92c17eb39f6012bd) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Breaking: e2e and every `@e2e-dev` package now need Node.js 22.22.3 or newer on Node.js 22, or 24.8.0 or newer** (`engines.node` is `^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0`). Node.js 22.12 through 22.22.2, 23, and 24.0 through 24.7 are no longer supported, and the CLI refuses to start on them, naming the versions to upgrade to. Those releases fail when a CommonJS file a test imports requires TypeScript through the new loader's `module.registerHooks` (nodejs/node#59679 fixed it in 22.22.3 and 24.8.0).
  
  e2e now loads TypeScript with its own loader, built on oxc, instead of tsx. tsx brought in esbuild, whose postinstall script made every `pnpm install` on pnpm 11 and later fail with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` until the project approved the build; nothing e2e installs runs an install script now. Config and tests load as before: ESM whatever `package.json` says, `./x.js` and `./x` resolve to `x.ts` and `./x.jsx` to `x.tsx`, directory index imports, tsconfig `paths` and `baseUrl`, workspace packages exporting `.ts` source, JSX in `.tsx` and `.jsx`, enums, namespaces, `experimentalDecorators`, and source-mapped stack traces. JSON imported without `with { type: 'json' }` still loads. A test file whose name holds `%`, `#`, or a space now collects with its source location instead of failing with "URI malformed" or losing the location. Each file reads its nearest `tsconfig.json` rather than the one in the working directory. What changes: `import` statements in a `.cts` file are no longer compiled into `require` calls (write `import x = require()`); standard decorators without `experimentalDecorators`, auto-accessors, and ES module `import` and value `export` declarations in `.cts` are refused with their line (`import type`, `export type`, `import x = require()`, and `export =` work); the CLI refuses the Bun (`bun --bun`) and Deno runtimes (install with any package manager, run on Node.js); a type imported without `import type` that stays in the output (a decorated member's type under `emitDecoratorMetadata`) fails to load, with an error naming the import; a `.ts` file a CommonJS file requires runs as an ES module like every other `.ts`, so one written with `module.exports` needs the `.cts` extension; and an import written in a JavaScript file resolves as Node.js resolves it, without TypeScript's extension rules or tsconfig `paths`. TypeScript inside an installed package compiles without the project's `tsconfig.json`.

title: fix(mcp): redact secrets from what user code prints in the e2e mcp process
body:
Stacked on #815. Base is `oskar/fix-mcp-error-redaction`; retarget to `main` once #815 merges.

Project tools and the config's top-level code run inside the `e2e mcp` process. Whatever they wrote to stdout or stderr reached the operator's stderr verbatim, configured secrets included. `e2e run` already redacts the same output in its workers (`StreamRedactor` over `processSecrets` in `packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts`), but `src/cli/mcp.ts` only moved stdout writes over to stderr. The protocol stream itself was never corrupted, since stdout writes already went to stderr.

- `claimStdio` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/mcp.ts`) patches `process.stdout` and `process.stderr`, so every write goes through `McpOutput` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/output.ts`): one `StreamRedactor` over `processSecrets` (the ledger #815 fills), shared by both streams because they land on one stderr. The protocol keeps the saved stdout writer, and the server's own log lines, already redacted at the source, go out as written.
- Fails closed while a config loads. The config's top-level code can print a secret before the process knows it is one, so `SessionHost` wraps load plus `registerStaticSecrets` in `withholdOutput`. Output is held until the load finishes, then released redacted. If the load fails, the config's secrets are unknown, so the held output is dropped and a `withheld N bytes` warning is logged in its place.
- An unfinished line is released, redacted, once no tool call is in flight rather than at exit. A concurrent call may be partway through a value. Backpressure still reaches the writer: `write` returns stderr's answer, and a writer waiting on stdout gets `drain` when stderr drains.
- An uncaught error or unhandled rejection (a project tool's unawaited promise) used to go out raw on fd 2, and the crash left the session's app process running. It is now logged redacted and held like user output during a config load. The server then shuts down the same way it does on a signal: sessions close, apps stop, exit code 1.

Out of scope: a child process that inherits the server's stdio writes straight to the descriptors, which `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` now notes. A config's top-level output in the `e2e run` main process is also unredacted. That is a separate gap and its own change.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/mcp-user-output.test.ts` drives the built `e2e mcp` over a real stdio client. The project has a config that prints a secret at top level, a tool that prints it through `console.log`, `console.error`, split `process.stdout.write`s, and a write with no trailing newline, a tool that leaves a rejection unawaited, and a config that prints the secret and then throws. Both cases fail on #815's head and pass here. Mutation-checked: drop the load hold, the stderr patch, the failed-load withhold, live redaction, or the per-call release, and a case fails. `tests/unit/mcp-output.test.ts` covers concurrent loads where one fails, shutdown during a load, and a tail split across writes.
- Ran the built CLI on the testbed through an MCP stdio client (`open_session` on a broken config, then on a config with credential `admin` / `verify-pw-42` and project tools `seed_admin` and `stray`, on port 4391), comparing `main` to this branch. stderr:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `[broken config] admin:verify-pw-42` | `e2e mcp: [warning] withheld 35 bytes of output printed while a config failed to load: ...` |
| `[config] seeding admin with verify-pw-42` | `[config] seeding admin with <secret:admin.password>` |
| `[tool] POST /seed admin:verify-pw-42` | `[tool] POST /seed admin:<secret:admin.password>` |
| `[tool] stdout admin:verify-pw-42` | `[tool] stdout admin:<secret:admin.password>` |
| `[tool] stderr admin:verify-pw-42` | `[tool] stderr admin:<secret:admin.password>` |
| `Error: login failed for admin:verify-pw-42` (Node crash, testbed app left listening on 4391) | `e2e mcp: [error] uncaught: Error: login failed for admin:<secret:admin.password>` then `Session ... closed (server shutdown)`, port free |

title: fix(agent): fail tainted fallback-only steps with POLICY_DENIED
body:
After a secret fill the attempt is pixel-tainted, so the runner withholds `pixelFallback`. An agent step that could only read the screen from that fallback screenshot never got it: it failed with the engine's `operation timed out` (`ACTION_FAILED`), and `act` spent two operation budgets doing so (the cache's opening probe swallowed the first timeout and the executor's first look timed out again).

- `retryingObserve` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/phases.ts`) now owns the `pixelFallback` decision: callers say whether the step wants fallback (`act` and executor observations in `observation-feed.ts`, `vision: true` judgments in `invocation.ts`), and the taint is read per capture. A capture whose fallback a secret fill withheld and that times out becomes `POLICY_DENIED`, naming the fill. The step clock still wins: a capture cut short by the step deadline stays `STEP_TIMEOUT`.
- A `vision: false` judgment never asks for fallback and keeps its timeout. `vision: 'only'` was already denied before any capture.
- The step cache's opening probe (`step-cache.ts` `captureStart`) propagates that denial instead of treating it as a miss, so `act` fails after one operation budget. Later probes still hand off to the executor, and a denied start is not an eviction.
- Docs: `reference/errors.mdx`, `reference/agent.mdx`, `security.mdx`, and the skill's debugging table.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[semantic capture times out] --> B{step clock out?}
  B -- yes --> T[STEP_TIMEOUT]
  B -- no --> C{fallback wanted and secret filled?}
  C -- yes --> P[POLICY_DENIED: a secret was filled]
  C -- no --> E[engine error, as before]
```

Follow-up: #821 moves these tests to `agent-fallback-handoff.test.ts` and still asserts `'timed out'` for the two tainted cases. Once this lands, tighten that assertion to `POLICY_DENIED` (the cubic thread on its line 393).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `tests/integration/agent-semantic-fallback.test.ts` now asserts `POLICY_DENIED` for both tainted cases, one observation for the tainted `act`, and a timeout for a tree-only judgment after a fill. On main it fails with `expected 'ACTION_FAILED' to be 'POLICY_DENIED'`. Mutations checked: dropping the flag from the feed or from the judgment, setting it for tree-only judgments, or removing the opening-probe rethrow each fail it. Removing the guard-first order fails the new unit test in `agent-phases.test.ts`.
- Built CLI, scratch project in `/tmp` on `@e2e-dev/web`: a page whose main thread hangs after the password field's input event, `actionTimeout: 3000`, then `agent.act`, `agent.assert({ vision: true })`, and `agent.assert()` after `fill(credentials.user('admin').password)`. The secret appears nowhere under `.e2e/`.

| step | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.act` | `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out`, 6.06s | `POLICY_DENIED: agent.act could not read the semantic tree, and its screenshot fallback is denied: a secret was filled in this attempt, so no pixels leave the runner until it ends (PIXEL_TAINTED)`, 3.00s |
| `agent.assert` `vision: true` | `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out`, 3.00s | `POLICY_DENIED: agent.assert could not read ... (PIXEL_TAINTED)`, 3.01s |
| `agent.assert` tree-only | `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out`, 3.00s | `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out`, 3.00s |

A fresh-context review found three things, all fixed: the denial had overridden `STEP_TIMEOUT` at the deadline, the denying path had no unit test, and the JSDoc on `begin()` was stale.

`web agent` fails with `REPLAY_STALE` on main too (since `chore: version packages (#774)` moved the cache key); it is not from this change.

title: fix(web): fail operations on a hung page at their timeout, not the test timeout
body:
A web test on a page whose script never yields (a button that starts `while (true) {}`) waited for the whole test timeout instead of failing at `actionTimeout`.

- Root cause: `guard` and `AttemptSession.run` only raced the attempt signal, so the operation's `timeoutMs` was enforced by Playwright alone. On a renderer stuck in a script, Playwright never answers an evaluate (`locate` runs one, with no timeout) or a mouse or keyboard call, and while a trace records (the local default) even `click({ timeout })` and `goto({ timeout })` stay pending past their timeout.
- Fix: every guarded operation now runs under its budget's deadline (`withOperationDeadline`, `packages/web/src/operation-budget.ts`) and fails as `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` (`ACTION_FAILED` in the report). Playwright gets a timeout 250 ms shorter, so when it can answer, its classified error (`NOT_ACTIONABLE ... intercepts pointer events`, `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`) still arrives first.
- A tap, point action, or keystroke the deadline cut off is `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`, not a plain timeout: the input may have landed, so replay hands off as `action-uncertain` instead of repeating it.
- `waitForDownload` runs the test's trigger, so the deadline does not cut it: the waiter keeps its full timeout and the `no download started within <n>ms` message names it.
- `e2e`: with locate bounded, a read that starts with under 100 ms of a wait left can time out because the wait did. Such a cut-off read, after one that completed, now ends the wait on its last sample (`cutOffAtDeadline`, `packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts`): a missing locator stays `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, a missing frame keeps its reason, an assertion keeps `ASSERTION_FAILED`, each with the timeout as `cause`. A read that started with more budget and still timed out hung, and stays `ACTION_FAILED`; a negation never passes on it. `docs/reference/engine.mdx` says so.
- `expect(browser)` matchers (`toHaveURL`, `toHaveTitle`, `toHaveClass`) read within the assertion's remaining budget instead of the action timeout, and report their last sample, so on a frozen page they end at their own timeout. `hung-page.test.ts` covers it.
- `app.open()` to a server that never answers was already bounded by Playwright's `goto` timeout. Its documented budget is `config.timeout` (`docs/reference/app.mdx`), which by default equals the test timeout, so it still ends at the test timeout by design. It now reports the navigation's `ACTION_FAILED` rather than `TEST_TIMEOUT`, and 5 s sooner.

Tests: `packages/web/tests/integration/hung-page.test.ts` (locate, point tap, traced tap, traced navigation on a frozen page fail on main with "still pending"; each call must also take its whole budget; a covered button keeps `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, which fails if the 250 ms lead is removed), `time.test.ts` and `locator-engine.test.ts` cases for the cut-off rule (a hung read stays a failure and a negation does not pass on it; mutation-checked), and a `failure-evidence.test.ts` case.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI, a scratch test (not committed) that serves a never-answering URL and a page whose button runs `while (true) {}`, each test `{ timeout: 60_000 }`:

```ts
test('opens a server that never answers', { timeout: 60_000 }, async ({ app }) => {
  await app.open(`${origin}/never`);
});

test('taps a button that freezes the page', { timeout: 60_000 }, async ({ app, screen }) => {
  await app.open(`${origin}/`);
  await screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Freeze' }).tap();
});
```

| config | test | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| testbed default (`actionTimeout` 30 s, `timeout` 120 s) | tap on frozen page | 70.0 s, `TEST_TIMEOUT` | 35.1 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (tap step 30.0 s) |
| testbed default | open never-answering server | 70.1 s, `TEST_TIMEOUT` | 64.9 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (open step 59.8 s) |
| `actionTimeout: 5_000`, `timeout: 10_000` | tap on frozen page | 70.0 s, `TEST_TIMEOUT` | 10.1 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (tap step 5.0 s) |
| `actionTimeout: 5_000`, `timeout: 10_000` | open never-answering server | 20.1 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (open step 10.1 s) | 14.9 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (open step 9.8 s) |
| `actionTimeout: 5_000`, `timeout: 10_000` | `not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 3_000 })` after freezing | not run on main | 9.2 s, `ACTION_FAILED` (assertion step 3.0 s) |

The rest of each attempt after the failing step is the 5 s failure-evidence look.

main:

```text
   × opens a server that never answers (timed-out) 70.13s
     → test timed out after 60000 ms in phase body
   × taps a button that freezes the page (timed-out) 70.02s
     → test timed out after 60000 ms in phase body
```

this branch:

```text
   × opens a server that never answers 64.88s
     → operation timed out
   × taps a button that freezes the page 35.07s
     → tap timed out before the page answered; its input may have been dispatch…
```

title: fix(run): redact secrets from what the config, collected test files, and reporters print
body:
User code runs in the `e2e run` process too, and what it printed reached the terminal with secrets in the clear. Worker output was redacted, except the config's top-level output, which each worker printed before it registered the config's secrets. - `packages/e2e/src/run/process-output.ts`: `RunnerOutput` redacts every write to `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` in the runner process with the process-wide secret ledger. While the config loads, output is held until the load registers the secrets. If the load fails, the output is dropped and a warning printed in its place. Each worker's bootstrap uses the same hold, `ConfigLoadHold`. - `packages/e2e/src/cli/run-output.ts`: `e2e run` claims both streams for the run. Only the list reporter writes to the terminal past the redactor. - While the list reporter is up, runner output goes through `ListReporter.processOutput` and prints under `stdout | runner` / `stderr | runner`, the way worker output does, on stdout, in a pipe too. On main, the live window painted over it in a TTY. This includes Node warnings raised in the runner, such as the TypeScript loader's unreadable-tsconfig warning, which used to go to stderr (`typescript-loader.test.ts` updated). Without the `list` reporter, output stays on its own stream. - The runner registers the static secrets once the config has loaded (`runner.ts`, `loadConfig`). - Not stacked on #826. Its `McpOutput` puts both streams on one stderr with one redactor and flushes per tool call. Here the streams stay apart and route around the live window. The two share `StreamRedactor` and the hold-while-loading rule. Once both land, `McpOutput` can adopt `ConfigLoadHold`. ```mermaid flowchart LR U["user code in the runner
config, collection, reporters"] --> H{config loading?} H -- yes --> Q[held] Q -- loaded --> R Q -- failed --> X[dropped, warning] H -- no --> R[StreamRedactor per stream] R --> L{list reporter up?} L -- yes --> LR[printed above the live window] L -- no --> T[terminal] ``` Still unredacted, as on main: the config's top-level output in `e2e list`, `e2e cache`, and `e2e explore`, and an uncaught error in the runner, which Node writes straight to fd 2. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, scratch config with `secrets: { apiToken }`. The config logs the value at top level. A test file logs it at top level and in its body. A custom reporter logs it in `onEvent` and `onRunFinished`. Ran `e2e run` in a 120x40 tmux pane (TTY, live window) and captured the final screen. - `tests/integration/run-user-output.test.ts` runs the built CLI. It fails on main and passes here. Mutation check: dropping the worker hold, or the runner's `registerStaticSecrets`, fails it again. - The testbed suite passes, `test:stress` output matches main, and `--reporter json` still prints a parseable report. main: the secret is printed in clear. The runner's `test file top level` and `reporter onEvent` lines are missing from the screen: they were written, unredacted, then painted over by the live window. ```text config top level: leak-token-1234567 config top level stderr: leak-token-1234567 RUN e2e v0.17.0 apps/testbed run … · targets: web ✓ target "web" command ready 88ms stdout | web config top level: leak-token-1234567 stderr | web config top level stderr: leak-token-1234567 stdout | web test file top level: stdout | web tests-leak/leak.e2e.ts > prints test body: ✓ web tests-leak/leak.e2e.ts (1 test) 1.64s ✓ prints 1.64s Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) Start at 10:10:12 Duration 1.98s (startup 88ms) Report .e2e/report.json reporter onRunFinished: leak-token-1234567 ``` this branch: ```text config top level: config top level stderr: RUN e2e v0.17.0 apps/testbed run … · targets: web stdout | runner test file top level: ✓ target "web" command ready 89ms stdout | web config top level: stderr | web config top level stderr: stdout | web test file top level: stdout | runner reporter onEvent: stdout | web tests-leak/leak.e2e.ts > prints test body: ✓ web tests-leak/leak.e2e.ts (1 test) 1.67s ✓ prints 1.67s Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) Start at 10:10:19 Duration 2.02s (startup 89ms) Report .e2e/report.json reporter onRunFinished: ```

title: iOS: false "covered by another visible element" for controls above an expo-router tab bar (still on agent-device 0.21.20, after #3097)
Feature: duration option for screen.swipe({ from, to })
body:
### Problem

`screen.swipe({ from, to })` sends a path swipe with a fixed, very short duration (~100 ms — `durationMs: 100` in `video.gesture-telemetry.json`). On an Android emulator, a React Native `ScrollView` often does not scroll at all for that gesture (it reads as a tap / cancelled fling), while the same path sent with `adb shell input swipe 540 1560 540 840 300` scrolls reliably. `scrollUntilVisible` works, but there is no way to do a controlled custom drag (a specific distance, a slow drag for a carousel or a pull-to-refresh) from a test.

Seen with e2e 0.17.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.9.2 (agent-device 0.21.20), Android 15 emulator (API 35), React Native 0.81.5.

### Proposed API

```ts
await screen.swipe({ from: { x: 540, y: 1560 }, to: { x: 540, y: 840 }, durationMs: 300 });
```

`durationMs` optional; omitted = today's behaviour. (A `speed` in px/s would work as well.)

### Which surface

public types (SDK)

### Compatibility

Additive — no existing behaviour changes.

title: Feature: locator.or(other) (Playwright parity)
body:
### Problem

Waiting for "either of two elements" needs a hand-written poll today. Example: after a test that switches the app language, its cleanup has to wait for the tab bar in English OR in the other language:

```ts
await expect
  .poll(async () => (await tabs.discover.isVisible()) || (await tabs.odkrywaj.isVisible()), { timeout: 20_000 })
  .toBe(true);
```

`isVisible()` answers instantly, so it cannot be used for this without the poll, and the poll loses the locator in the report / failure message.

### Proposed API

Playwright parity:

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('tab', 'Discover').or(screen.getByRole('tab', 'Odkrywaj'))).toBeVisible();
```

`locator.or(other)` matching nodes matched by either locator; actions on it require exactly one match, as today.

### Which surface

public types (SDK)

### Compatibility

Additive — no existing behaviour changes.

title: test(web-benchmark): re-record agent recordings for @e2e-dev/web 0.12
body: The `web agent` job fails on main and on every open PR with 25 `REPLAY_STALE`. #774 (`chore: version packages`) bumped `@e2e-dev/web` from 0.11.2 to 0.12.0. The cache key carries the engine minor (`packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts:185`), so every committed entry sat under an old hash, and `--strict-cache` refused each step whose recording was stored under another key. No cache code changed. - Re-recorded `tests-agent/` live: 30 new entries. - Deleted the 30 entries under the old keys. - Cache JSON only. Steps not replayed are the same ones as before for the same reasons as #796: the cart totals and wishlist acts end in planted bugs (missed by design), shadow-dom-form and iframe-form miss at a gap, and lying-labels and async-states hand off at a gap. `pick Express delivery`, left out in #796, now records and replays. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Web benchmark, `e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` against the built packages, the same command CI runs. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Tests | 25 failed (`REPLAY_STALE`) | 33 passed | | Replayed | 0 | 26 | | Handed off | - | 2 | | Missed | - | 4 | | Model calls | - | 20 | | Cost | - | $0.0035 | Recording run: 33 passed, 32 missed, 142 model calls, $0.048. ## Follow-up Every minor release of an engine invalidates all committed recordings this way, and the release PR does not catch it. Separate change.

title: fix(cache): replay a recorded step that types an empty value
body: Fixes #789. - The recorder writes a `type` or `typeText` action with value `""` (clearing a field), and the reader rejected it. `readInputText` returns `undefined` for `""` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/trace.ts`), so the entry was `invalid-entry`: the step called the model on every run and failed with `REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`. - New `readTypedValue` allows `""` for the `type` and `typeText` value only. `select`, `text`, `url`, and upload paths still reject it, and a unit case pins `select`. - Replay already handles it: the dispatcher only checks `typeof value === 'string'`, and the `unique()` templating passes `""` through. - Adds a `/clear-field` fixture page and a `clears a field` flow in the trace cache replay suite: type a draft, then type `""`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built `dist`, round-trip of a `type` entry through JSON (`buildTraceEntry` then `readTraceEntry`). - `tests/integration/trace-cache-replay.test.ts` against a `dist` built from main's reader and from this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `value: "nonempty"` reads back: `true` | `true` | | `value: ""` reads back: `false` | `true` | | replay suite: `× replays every step on the second run with zero model calls` (`AssertionError: expected [ Array(2) ] to have a length of +0 but got 2`) | `Tests 20 passed (20)` | Also green locally: `pnpm check`, `e2e` unit suite (2521 passed), and the other trace cache integration files (42 passed). Not run: the web benchmark, and a live `agent.act` against a real model recording a field clear. `apps/testbed` `tests/speed.e2e.ts` (`forty taps each cost no more than a few locator reads`) failed 3 of 6 runs on this branch at about 102.7 ms against its 100 ms budget, and passed on the others. I ran it twice on main and both passed. That test taps and never reads the trace cache, but two runs is not enough to call it unrelated.

title: test(web): stop the mid-trace video only after a painted frame arrives
body: `lifecycle.test.ts` > "splits a running trace around a video started mid-attempt, so every recording fills the viewport" failed on main at f99e80eb, on Node 26 and 24.8.0 ([run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/37190112507)): ``` AssertionError: video/video.webm inked: expected 0 to be greater than 0.0005 ❯ tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts:1070:56 ``` f99e80eb only re-records web-benchmark entries, and the same test passed on the commit before it, so it is a race in the test. - The test stopped each segment right after `viewer.screenshot()`. The first segment navigates to `/form`, and a recording stopped then can end on the blank frame of the navigation, before the page painted into the screencast: `inked` 0. - The restart/reset video test next to it already guarded against this with a frame watcher and a `settle` that waits for a painted frame. That watcher moves into a shared `paintWatcher`, and both tests use it. - `settle` now waits for a painted frame delivered after it is called. The mid-trace test records the same page in both segments, so a painted frame from before the navigation must not count. Frames are numbered on arrival, since Playwright calls `onFrame` concurrently and a late decode must not overwrite a newer frame. A page that already painted gets a fresh frame from a screenshot inside the poll. - Test-only: no changeset. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, on macOS (M1), `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts`. - I could not reproduce the failure on main locally: 21 runs of the test passed, 15 of them with every core busy. It showed up on the Linux runners only. - With this change: the two video tests passed 8/8 with every core busy, `lifecycle.test.ts` passed 29/29 three times, and `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run test` passed (537 tests, 1 skipped). A fresh-context review also ran them 17 times, 12 of them in parallel batches, all passing.

title: fix(run): redact run-level errors with the run's secrets
body: ## What and why A run-level error could carry a secret into `report.json`, the GitHub reporter, and the terminal in the clear. `serializeError` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts`) takes an optional `redact` and falls back to identity when a call site gives none, and several run-level paths gave none: a suite hook failure (`packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts:222`), engine disposal and collection errors (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:339`, `:405`), a worker's fatal error (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts:123`), an in-memory run's fatal (`packages/e2e/src/run/in-process.ts:71`), model preflight (`packages/e2e/src/run/standalone.ts:204`), the runner's failure sink (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:368`), and the scheduler's own protocol errors (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:633`, `:694`, `:771`, `:792`). Sibling calls on the same objects already passed a redactor, so the omission was easy to miss. The gap matters because a hook or an engine can quote a value the app echoed back. A `beforeAll` that signs in and fails with the response body in its message is the common shape: by the time the message reaches the reporter it is a plain string, and the report renders `run.errors` verbatim (`packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:746`). `docs/security.mdx` already says the runner replaces every occurrence of a registered secret value with `` in reports, so these paths were breaking a promise the rest of the runner keeps. The fix installs the process's live secret ledger (`processSecrets` in `packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts`) as the default redactor, so `serializeError` uses it when a call site gives none: ```ts // packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts const redact = extras.redact ?? redactorSlot.get(globalThis) ?? ((text: string): string => text); ``` The slot is a `globalThis` value (`internal/realm-slot.ts`, the same mechanism `secrets.ts` uses for its registry). `internal/` cannot import `run/`, where the ledger lives, and a project can load a second copy of e2e, so a module-local variable would not be shared. An explicit per-call redactor still wins, and the slot clears to identity when no runner is active. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[error thrown] --> B["serializeError(error, options)"] B --> C{"options.redact?"} C -- yes --> D[use it] C -- no --> E{"process ledger installed?"} E -- yes --> F["redact with processSecrets"] E -- no --> G[identity] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes A scratch project with one secret (`secrets: { probe: 'plain-secret-value-1234' }`), a fake engine, and a `beforeAll` that throws the value in its message. Ran the built CLI (`packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`) from a `main` worktree and from this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `beforeAll failed: sign-in failed for plain-secret-value-1234` | `beforeAll failed: sign-in failed for ` | The same value in `run.errors` of `report.json`: ```diff "run": { "errors": [{ "code": "HOOK_FAILED", - "message": "beforeAll failed: sign-in failed for plain-secret-value-1234", + "message": "beforeAll failed: sign-in failed for ", ``` - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/errors.test.ts` covers the resolution order: the installed redactor is used when none is given, a per-call one wins, and no redactor means identity. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/session-secrecy.test.ts` covers the wiring, that importing the run layer installs the ledger so a serialized error carries no secret. Both fail on the pre-fix code and pass here. - `pnpm --filter e2e run build`, `pnpm --filter e2e run typecheck`, and `oxlint` on the changed files exit 0. `pnpm --filter e2e run test:unit` fails the same files as a clean tree (17, all Windows path and CRLF cases), so nothing here regresses. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`): `.changeset/error-default-redactor.md`, a patch bump for `e2e`. - [x] Breaking change: no. `serializeError` is internal, the default only adds redaction where there was none, and an explicit per-call redactor keeps winning. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/security.mdx` already documents this behavior for reports, so there is no prose to fix, and no `skills/e2e/` page covers the error-serialization path. - [x] Contract change: none. `serializeError` is not in `dist/index.d.ts` or `dist/engine/index.d.ts`, and no wire schema is touched. - [x] Engine contract (`e2e/engine`): not touched, so no engine changesets are needed.

title: fix(run): a worker crash during a retry keeps the attempts before it
body:
When a test with `retries: 1` failed its first attempt and its retry crashed the worker, the report showed a single fabricated attempt 0 (`WORKER_CRASH`), and attempt 0's real error was gone. Serial groups had the same problem. The worker sent a test's result only once all its attempts were done (`runOrdinaryPair` in `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`, `runSerialUnit` in `serial.ts`), so a crash took every finished attempt with it.

- The worker streams progress ahead of the result with four typed messages in `packages/e2e/src/run/worker/protocol.ts`: `attempt-start` and `attempt` for ordinary and setup pairs, `serial-member` and `serial-attempt` for serial groups.
- The scheduler keeps them per pair and per group until the result or group arrives (`SchedulerWorker.attempts`, `serialGroups`).
- Crash during an attempt (its re-import and `beforeAll` included): the kept attempts, then a `WORKER_CRASH` attempt with the index `attempt-start` named.
- Crash between attempts (an `afterAll` after the last one): recorded on the last attempt as a secondary error with `cleanup: 'forced'`. No retry attempt is invented.
- Serial crash: finished group attempts, then a failed one holding the members finished so far, with the running member failed with `WORKER_CRASH`. A crash after a member finished fails the group attempt without blaming that member. A retry that crashed before any member keeps attempt 0's member verdicts. `SerialGroupProgress` is in `serial.ts`.
- A serial crash after the last group attempt, with no retry to follow, goes on that attempt the same way.
- Setup tests send each attempt before `afterAll` and the session saves, with the `SESSION_CONTRACT` check already applied, so a crash in either goes on that attempt. Its sessions still count as failed for dependents.
- Interrupt that terminated or killed the worker: the finished attempts stand with the verdict they reach, `flaky` included. A serial attempt in flight is recorded `interrupted` and keeps the members it finished. That verdict comes from one pure helper, `retryVerdict` in `retry.ts`, which `runWithRetries` uses too.
- Worker `send` now hands each message to the IPC channel right away instead of chaining it on the previous message's ack. Before, a `pair-start` sent just before a body called `process.exit` never left the process.

Overlap with #824 (worker hang watchdog, open): its watchdog kill also goes through `synthesizeCrashResults`. It reports the blocked test `timed-out` with only the synthesized attempt, so it drops earlier attempts the same way. Whichever PR lands second reconciles them. The watchdog kill should append its `TEST_TIMEOUT` attempt after the kept ones. Test for it: `retries: 1`, attempt 0 fails, attempt 1 busy-loops, both attempts reported, the last one `TEST_TIMEOUT`. Both PRs make the same `send` change in `worker/entry.ts`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as worker
  participant S as scheduler
  W->>S: pair-start
  W->>S: attempt-start 0
  W->>S: attempt 0 (failed)
  W->>S: attempt-start 1
  W--xS: process exits
  S->>S: result = attempt 0 + WORKER_CRASH attempt 1
```

A worker that exits on its own during the interrupt grace now counts as a crash, not an interrupted skip.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Scratch project in `/tmp` with a no-op custom engine and `--workers 1`, using the built CLI from `origin/main` (f99e80eb) and from this branch.

| scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retries: 1`, attempt 0 throws, attempt 1 `process.exit(7)` | `[[0, failed, WORKER_CRASH]]` | `[[0, failed, ERROR "first attempt fails"], [1, failed, WORKER_CRASH]]` |

group failed

title: perf(cli): e2e init memoizes stats while planning and skips loading zod and the wordmark
body: ## What and why `e2e init` did the same filesystem work many times over. This removes the repeats. - `firstBlocker` ran one `lstat` per path segment for every bundled skill file, so the shared prefix got stat'd once per file. A per-plan memo (`statMemo`) now stats each path once, and the walk above the skill root runs once per file set. - `planSkillInstall` skips the per-file walk and content reads when the skill root does not exist. - `planSkillLink` and `describeBlocker` compare paths lexically when the `lstat` walk found no symlink. `realpathSync` only runs when a link is on the way. - `package.json`, `.gitignore`, and the MCP configs are read once through `readIfPresent`, which treats `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` as missing, instead of `existsSync` then `readFileSync`. `readDocument` returns the text with the parsed document, so `planMcpRegistration` reads each config once. - Parent directories get `mkdir`'d once per run instead of once per file. - `readSkillFiles` caches the bundle per process. - The wordmark is a dynamic `import()` loaded only on a TTY, and its layout is computed on first use. - A hand-written `parseManifest` replaces the zod schema, so init no longer loads zod. Errors still name the key: `dependencies.react: expected a string`. - `isLoopbackHost`, `isPlainObject`, and `compareCodePoints` move to `internal/hosts.ts`, `internal/objects.ts`, and `internal/compare.ts`. Init stops pulling in `urls.ts`, `options.ts`, and `globs.ts`. This is a move only, callers are updated, and nothing is re-exported. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI, `e2e init --yes` in a project with a tab-indented `package.json`. Indentation, sorted `devDependencies`, the skill copy and its symlink, and both MCP configs come out the same as on main. - `{"dependencies":{"react":1}}` exits 2 with `package.json could not be read: dependencies.react: expected a string`. Interleaved A/B against `main` (f99e80eb), 12 cores, load average about 10 during the run: | Scenario | main | this PR | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `vitest run tests/unit/cli-init.test.ts` (median of 12) | 1444 ms | 1126 ms | -22% | | `e2e init --yes`, fresh project (median of 40) | 393 ms | 375 ms | -5% | The unit file runs `init()` many times in one process, so the per-process skill cache and the shorter stat walks add up there. A single CLI run is mostly Node startup and module loading, which is why the gain there is small.

title: feat(locator): duration option for path screen.swipe (#831)
body: Fixes #831 ## What and why - Adds an optional `durationMs?: number` to `screen.swipe({ from, to, durationMs? })`. - On mobile (e.g., Android emulators with React Native `ScrollView`), path swipes at the default ~100 ms duration are often dropped or cancelled as taps/flings. Allowing tests to specify `durationMs` enables reliable scrolls, carousels, and pull-to-refresh gestures. - Routes path swipes with `durationMs` to `client.interactions.pan` on `agent-device` (since `agent-device`'s `interactions.swipe` disallows custom durations and delegates timed gestures to pan), while preserving `interactions.swipe` for swipes without duration. - On web, dispatches multi-step pointer dragging via `page.mouse.move(..., { steps })` matching `Math.round(durationMs / 16)`. - Directional swipes (`screen.swipe({ direction, momentum? })`) strictly reject `durationMs` at compile time (`durationMs?: never`) and at runtime via `rejectUnknownOptions`. - Duration bounds are validated from `16` to `10000` ms (matching hardware frame rate minimum and device limits). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Typecheck**: `pnpm --filter e2e run typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run typecheck` passed (0 errors, verified compile-time assertions in `sdk-types.ts`). - **Unit Tests**: - `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/fixture-runtime.test.ts` passed (47/47 tests, including Issue #831 parameters `{ from: { x: 540, y: 1560 }, to: { x: 540, y: 840 }, durationMs: 300 }`, bounds validation, and step recording). - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/unit/actions.test.ts` passed (39/39 tests, multi-step pointer drag). - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile exec vitest run tests/unit/engine.test.ts -t "maps every supported action"` passed (verifies `swipe` vs `pan` dispatch). - **Linter**: `npx oxlint` passed (0 warnings, 0 errors across 943 files). - **Error Codes**: `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-error-codes.ts` passed (all 84 error codes documented). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: mobile: reads on a continuously updating Android screen take ~20–40 s each (no way to skip the settle wait for snapshots)
body:
## Summary

On Android, every `expect(...)` / locator action on a screen whose content keeps changing (a list of rows whose values update about once a second) takes ~20–40 s, while the same calls on a static screen take ~1 s. A test that spends a few minutes on such a screen runs into its timeout, and occasionally a single read hits the 30 s adb timeout:

```
ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed: Android snapshot helper failed: adb timed out after 30000ms
```

iOS runs of the same test on the same screen are fast.

## Environment

- `e2e` 0.16.0, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.9.1, bundled `agent-device` 0.21.18
- Android emulator, API 35, arm64, animations disabled (`window/transition/animator` scales `0`)
- React Native 0.86 debug build
- macOS host

## What we measured

From `report.json` step durations on the changing screen (one run, first steps):

```
1916 913 32036 22475 19637 20699 19937 21127 19214 23416   (ms)
```

The steps are ordinary `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`, `locator.tap()` and `locator.fill()` calls. The same kinds of steps on static screens in the same run take a few hundred ms. A plain `agent-device snapshot` against a static screen of the same app returns in ~1 s.

Disabling system animations only shaved a few seconds off (≈25–30 s → ≈20 s), so the delay looks tied to the content updating rather than to animations.

## Expected

A way to read a screen that never becomes idle without paying a long wait per call — for example a per-engine (or per-call) option to skip or bound the wait for the UI to settle before a snapshot, similar to Maestro's `waitToSettleTimeoutMs: 0`. `mobile({ settle })` only covers the wait after taps, fills and scrolls, not reads.

## Repro shape

1. A React Native screen with a `FlatList` of ~30 rows, each row showing a number that changes every second (any timer-driven value works).
2. Android emulator, `mobile({ platform: 'android' })`.
3. A test that does a handful of `expect(screen.getByTestId(...)).toBeVisible()` and `tap()` calls on that screen.
4. Compare step durations with the timer stopped.

Related: #831 (a `duration` for path swipes) is the other thing we needed for this kind of screen — a fast fling did not register on a slide-to-confirm control.

title: Mobile replay misses on unstable iOS 27 screen identity
body:
`@e2e-dev/mobile@0.9.1`, `e2e@0.16.0`, `agent-device@0.21.20`, iOS 27.0 Simulator (24A434).

A successful native SwiftUI recording misses every `agent.act` on the next fresh-install run with `cache.reason: "wrong-context"`. Recording again does not resolve it. In two consecutive debug runs, the first step's startPath changed from `<bundle> / Today` to `<bundle> / Settings`; the next four changed from `<bundle> / Training` to `<bundle>`. The same visible screens and controls were present.

`screenTitle()` in mobile's `nodes.ts` picks the first navigation-bar and prefers its label over its identifier. On iOS 27 a custom principal toolbar item and a trailing Settings/New button can supply that label, while the bar's identifier still names the screen. A full-screen, untitled sheet can also include the presenting screen's navigation bar in one tree and omit it in the next. Thus the identity varies with the accessibility-tree representation, rather than a navigation change.

The opaque route comparison correctly refuses different strings, but the mobile identity is unstable before it reaches that comparison. Please keep the context safety check: prefer a reliable visible-screen identifier, and support an explicit screen-identity resolver for native surfaces whose app-defined accessibility identifiers identify the foreground screen. An untitled sheet should not inherit a background navigation bar. A regression fixture could compare two captures of the same SwiftUI custom-toolbar screen and the same presented untitled sheet.

Observed cost: a record run used 261,807 tokens in 227s; the immediate replay used 169,989 tokens in 218s, with all five act steps missing and zero actions replayed. These are successful tests, not failures of the app's workflow.

title: fix(decision): offer dismiss_keyboard while an on-screen keyboard is showing
body:
## What and why

- The decision executor offers `scroll_up`, `scroll_down` and `back` next to the element operations, but not the runner's `dismissKeyboard`. On a device the keyboard that typing raises can cover the next control, and the tree drops whatever it covers, so the model has nothing that reaches it.
- `packages/decision/src/elements.ts` now adds `dismiss_keyboard` to the controls when the target declares `dismissKeyboard` and the tree lists a `keyboard` or `key` node outside any hidden subtree. That is the probe `keyboardShowing` uses in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`. An iOS number pad lists only its keys. `perform` in `packages/decision/src/dispatch.ts` runs it through `ctx.actions.dismissKeyboard()`, so the runner authorizes, budgets and records it, and `CONTROL_LABELS` in `executor.ts` names it "dismiss the keyboard" in turns and history. Web declares no dismiss and is unchanged.
- The criterion in `packages/decision/src/questions.ts` states the fact: "The on-screen keyboard is up. Controls it covers are missing from the elements; hide it to reach them." With the built-in tool's wording ("when it covers what you need to reach") Jev never picked it in 23 decisions, p at most 0.20.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- The live runs below were on the layout before #965. The port onto the new layout is covered by unit tests: `elements.test.ts` (offered while keys show, not for a hidden keyboard, a hidden subtree, no keyboard, or no `dismissKeyboard` verb) and `executor.test.ts` (the operation question lists it and choosing it calls `dismissKeyboard`).
- Our React Native app on an iOS 26.5 simulator, not the mobile benchmark: `e2e run tests/client-workout.e2e.ts --no-cache` with Jev 1.13 through `@ai-sdk/typesafe-ai`. The step types reps and weight into number-pad fields, then taps "Log set", which the pad covers.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| "Log set" is gone from the tree. Jev taps "Finish" 8 times, each `APP_UNREACHABLE`, then claims `failed` and the check agrees (`ACTION_FAILED`) | 2/2 runs pick `dismiss_keyboard`, after 3 and after 7 failed taps, then tap "Log set". The logger moves to set 2 |

- Its probability climbs from about 0.2 to 0.3 with each failed tap and wins once it passes `tap`. It sits close to `tap`, so how many taps it takes varies between runs.
- Neither run passes. Run 1 ends `blocked` on the completion check. Run 2 types into set 2 as well, the pad comes back, and Jev taps "Finish" 9 more times before it claims `failed`. That loop is what #844's stall guard is for.
