title: fix(e2e): resolve ./x.jsx and ./x.js in TypeScript's order, like tsx did
body: Regression from #790 (unreleased, ships in #825): `import { C } from './Comp.jsx'` with only `Comp.tsx` on disk failed with `Cannot find module '.../Comp.jsx'`. TypeScript and e2e 0.17.0 (tsx) load it. - The loader derived its candidates from a per-extension `written` field, so `./x.jsx` had none, and `./x.js` tried `x.jsx` before `x.js`. - `packages/e2e/src/config/compiled-files.ts` now spells out TypeScript's table (`tryAddingExtensions` in TS 5.9, same as tsx's map): ```ts const WRITTEN: Readonly> = { '.js': ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx'], '.jsx': ['.tsx', '.ts', '.jsx', '.js'], '.mjs': ['.mts', '.mjs'], '.cjs': ['.cts', '.cjs'], }; ``` - This covers relative imports, extensionless and directory imports, tsconfig `paths`, and `#` imports and package exports, because they all resolve through it. - Amends #790's changeset rather than adding one, since the regression never shipped. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Packed `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` from main and from this branch into a scratch project in `/tmp`, then ran `npx e2e run` on a test that imports `./lib/Comp.jsx` (only `Comp.tsx`), `./lib/helper.jsx` (only `helper.ts`), `./lib/plain.jsx` (only `plain.js`), and `./lib/both.js` (both `both.js` and `both.jsx` exist). - `tsc` 5.9 `--traceResolution` on the same project resolves the four imports to `Comp.tsx`, `helper.ts`, `plain.js`, and `both.js`. The branch loads the same files. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `COLLECTION_ERROR: Cannot find module '.../tests/lib/Comp.jsx'` | `✓ jsx specifiers resolve like TypeScript` | | `./both.js` test: `expected "jsx" to be "js"` | `✓ ./both.js loads both.js, as TypeScript does` |

title: fix(decision): decide through experimental_decide and reject unsupported models at config load
body: Fixes for `@e2e-dev/decision` before its first publish in #825, from the pre-release stress test. - Calls `experimental_decide` now. `experimental_evaluate` is deprecated in ai 7.0.128, and `typeSafeAi.decisionModel()` (@ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.13) failed typecheck with TS2741 `doEvaluate` missing. `model` is typed `Exclude` from `ai`, so decision models and the deprecated evaluation models both typecheck and run. - Peer `ai` goes from `^7.0.0` to `^7.0.128`, the first release that exports `experimental_decide` (checked against the 7.0.127 and 7.0.128 tarballs). On main the floor was wrong anyway: `experimental_evaluate` first shipped in 7.0.103. pnpm only warns on an unmet peer, so the package reads `experimental_decide` off the `ai` namespace, and an older `ai` gets `INVALID_CONFIG: decisionExecutor() needs ai 7.0.128 or later` instead of a module link error. - Drops the `@ai-sdk/provider@4.0.21` pin, which installed next to the 4.0.22 that `ai` brings. Types come from the `ai` peer. - `decisionExecutor()` checks the model at config load and throws `ConfigurationError('INVALID_CONFIG')` naming the fix, the way `web()` and `easSimulators()` do. Main threw a raw `TypeError` (`packages/decision/src/executor.ts:29`). - `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` names the env var the provider reads (`Set TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY to the decision model API key.`). The name comes out of the SDK's `LoadAPIKeyError` text and nothing else in that text is kept. - README, docs page, docs example, and skill now use `decisionModel()`. `errors.mdx` lists `decisionExecutor()` under `INVALID_CONFIG`. The existing unreleased changeset is amended, not added to. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. Packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, `@e2e-dev/decision` into a scratch project (`/tmp/rc-decision`), `ai@7.0.128` (floor and npm latest are the same version today), testbed `/todos` app, mock choice model. No real model key on this box. | | main (7aafa007 tarball) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `model: openrouter('inception/mercury-2.5')` | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')` | `INVALID_CONFIG: decisionExecutor({ model }) got the language model openrouter/inception/mercury-2.5; pass an AI SDK decision model, e.g. decisionExecutor({ model: typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest') })` | | `model: 'openai/gpt-5'` | `TypeError: ... (reading 'includes')` | `INVALID_CONFIG: decisionExecutor({ model }) got the string "openai/gpt-5"; ...` | | no model | `TypeError: ... (reading 'supportedQuestionTypes')` | `INVALID_CONFIG: decisionExecutor({ model }) got undefined; ...` | | `tsc` on `decisionExecutor({ model: typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest') })` | `TS2741: Property 'doEvaluate' is missing` | passes, `evaluationModel()` too | | `typeSafeAi.decisionModel()` run with no key | `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: Set the evaluation model API key.` (from source, not run) | `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: Set TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY to the decision model API key.` | | `ai@7.0.127` | peer `^7.0.0` accepts 7.0.100-7.0.102, whose import fails with a link error (stress test, ai@7.0.100) | `npm install` fails with ERESOLVE on `peer ai@"^7.0.128"`; forced with `--legacy-peer-deps`: `INVALID_CONFIG: decisionExecutor() needs ai 7.0.128 or later; update the ai package` | Real CLI, both model kinds, checks a todo and asserts on `/todos`: ```text ✓ decision executor checks a todo and asserts > agent.act "mark the Pay the invoice todo done" 337ms · 3 model calls ✓ decision executor checks a todo and asserts > agent.assert "a todo is marked done" 129ms · 1 model call Tests 1 passed (1) AI 4 tokens · 4 model calls · mock/heuristic-1 (doDecide) AI 4 tokens · 4 model calls · mock/heuristic-legacy (doEvaluate) ``` Unsupported model, as a user sees it (exit 2): ```text ERROR configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config) decisionExecutor({ model }) got the language model openrouter/x; pass an AI SDK decision model, e.g. decisionExecutor({ model: typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest') }) ``` New tests: unit tests for each rejected shape and the key message, a test with `experimental_decide` mocked away, and type tests in `tests/types/options.ts` for `decisionModel()`, `evaluationModel()`, and both literal shapes.

title: fix(mobile): update agent-device to 0.21.22
body: ## What and why - Bumps `agent-device` 0.21.21 -> 0.21.22 in `@e2e-dev/mobile` and docs ([release](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/releases/tag/v0.21.22)), following #912. - The release has one Limrun fix: an iOS settings refusal on a Limrun instance reported `deviceId: 'booted'`, the simctl udid every Limrun instance uses. It now reports the session's device ([#3243](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3243)). The other change in the release is test-only. - No engine code change. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `@e2e-dev/mobile`: build, `typecheck`, and `vitest run` pass (12 files, 231 tests). - Live on Limrun iOS and Android instances attached by URL and token, with a cloud provider that allocates leases with `retainOnClose`: the lease suite (closeApp, next file, 75 s idle) and the worker-retire suite give 12 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are the suite's intentional ones. - Settings on a Limrun iOS instance through the 0.21.22 client: appearance, permissions, location, and clear-app-state succeed. The refused notifications permission now carries the session's device: ```text FAIL permission grant notifications: UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION iOS simulator does not support setting notifications permission via simctl privacy on this runtime. deviceId=limrun:ios:e717e70cf8fd47b400d7ed01c875a175 ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(config): reject a non-string credential username with INVALID_CONFIG
body: ## What and why - A function as a credential `username` passed validation, then crashed in the config digest with a raw "value of type function is not JSON-safe". No tests ran and the error named nothing. Only `password` may be a function. - `resolveSecrets` now checks credential shape: not an object, an unknown key (with a did-you-mean), or a non-string `username` is `INVALID_CONFIG`. A credential with no username in the config or `E2E_USER__USERNAME` is `INVALID_CONFIG` too. A username set only by the env var still works. - Stricter than before: an unknown credential key (typo, `otp: () => ...`) used to be silently ignored. Changeset says so. - Type already said `username: string`; added a type test so it stays that way. Docs: one sentence in authentication + skill, new `INVALID_CONFIG` entry in errors. Fixes ENG-923 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes | Config | main | branch | | --- | --- | --- | | function `username` (`e2e run`, `e2e list`) | `ERROR` "value of type function is not JSON-safe", exit 1 | `INVALID_CONFIG: credential "admin" username must be a string, got a function; only password may be a provider function`, exit 2 | | string username + function password | - | testbed `dashboard.e2e.ts` 7 passed | | username only from `E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME` | - | 7 passed | | no username anywhere | - | `INVALID_CONFIG: has no username; set username or E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME` | - `pnpm check` passes, e2e unit suite 2462 passed. New shape test fails on main. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(agent): send cache hints only to OpenAI Responses models
body: Fixes ENG-879 - `providerHints` added `providerOptions.openai.{ promptCacheKey, store: false }` to any provider whose name starts with `openai`. - `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` copies `providerOptions[]` into the request body as-is. Name the provider `openai` and the body gets a camelCase `promptCacheKey`, which a strict Chat Completions endpoint rejects: `Unknown parameter: 'promptCacheKey'`. - That provider reports `openai.chat`, the same string as `@ai-sdk/openai`'s own chat model, so the provider string can't tell them apart. - Hints now go only to Responses models (`*.responses` named `openai*`, or containing `azure`, the same rule the AI SDK uses to pick the options key) and to gateway `openai/*` models (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/provider-hints.ts`). - Trade-off: `openai.chat(...)` / `azure.chat(...)` lose the prompt cache routing key. Prefix caching still happens automatically. `store: false` makes no difference on chat because nothing is replayed by item id. The default `openai(...)` is Responses and keeps both hints. - A provider named e.g. `openai-proxy` was never affected, because its options key is `openai-proxy`. Its test is there to pin that. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web-benchmark, `e2e run --no-cache tests-agent/login-form.e2e.ts` with a scratch config. - Run 1: `createOpenAICompatible({ name: 'openai' })` through a local proxy that rejects unknown params the way api.openai.com does, then forwards to the AI Gateway (the gateway itself ignores unknown params). - Run 2: `gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast')` with a fetch that logs `providerOptions.openai`. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | openai-compatible named `openai` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: Unknown parameter: 'promptCacheKey'.` body keys `model,promptCacheKey,store,tool_choice` | passes, 3 model calls, 94% cached. Body keys `model,tool_choice` | | gateway `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` | passes, 97% cached. Every call sends `{"promptCacheKey":"e2e-ba0a…","store":false}` | passes, 97% cached. Every call sends `{"promptCacheKey":"e2e-ba0a…","store":false}` | - Unit tests in `provider-hints.test.ts` build the real request body through `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and `@ai-sdk/openai`. The `openai`-named compatible row and the `openai.chat` / `azure.chat` / `openai-proxy.chat` rows fail on main.

title: fix(web): poll checked state after check/uncheck click until the action deadline
body:
Fixes ENG-904

- `check()`/`uncheck()` and the agent's `check` verb read `isChecked()` once right after the click and threw a non-retryable `ACTION_FAILED` if it had not flipped yet. A controlled checkbox (React state set after an await) or a Headless UI style `role=switch` that commits `aria-checked` later failed, and the agent step was not recorded, so reruns called the model again.
- `setChecked` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`) now polls the state with `pollCondition` from `e2e/engine` against the operation's own deadline and signal (`dispatchLocatorAction` takes the `ConnectionBudget` instead of a bare timeout). There is no new timeout. A control that never changes fails with the same error when the action timeout runs out.
- Playwright's own `check()` reads once and fails these controls too (`Clicking the checkbox did not change its state`). That difference is documented in `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx`.
- A control that is detached on the first read after the click still counts as done (#788). If it is replaced later while still in its old state, it now fails instead of passing on a click the app rejected.
- Testbed `/controls` gains a controlled checkbox and a `role=switch`, each committing its state from a 400ms `setTimeout`.

- `pollCondition` no longer sleeps past its deadline: the last read starts at it, so a state that arrives late is not accepted. Applies to every caller (expect, locators, web expectations).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `packages/web/tests/integration/check-actions.test.ts`, real Chromium, locator and element targets: the 4 new async cases fail on main (`check clicked the control but its checked state did not change`) and pass here. A rejected click on a control that a re-render replaces later still fails.
- Testbed, `e2e run tests/controls.e2e.ts`: the new test checks then reads `isChecked()` immediately, so it cannot lean on assertion polling.
- Agent, `agent.act('subscribe to the newsletter and turn on Dark mode')` on the testbed with a live model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `--no-cache --ai-trace`), read with unbox-ai.
- Web benchmark: `pnpm test:web-benchmark` 91/91. `tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts --strict-cache` replays 7/7.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| testbed `controls.e2e.ts` new test | `ACTION_FAILED: check clicked the control but its checked state did not change: getByLabel("Subscribe to newsletter")` | passes, 16/16 in file |
| agent `check` tool results | `check #n47 failed: ACTION_FAILED ...`, same for `#n48`. The model then tapped `#n47`, which unchecked it once the late commit landed, and reported passed. `toBeChecked` failed | `Checked #n47.`, `Checked #n48.`, 2 model calls, test passes |
| agent rerun with cache | step not recorded | `Cache 1 replayed`, 0 model calls |

There is no committed agent test for this. On main its outcome depends on what the model does after the failed `check`, so a model that only re-observes would pass with the bug present. The deterministic testbed test and the integration tests are the regression guard.

title: fix(agent): retry the auto-only tool_choice refusal of Meta's Muse Spark with auto
body: Fixes ENG-922 - Meta's Muse Spark models accept only `tool_choice: "auto"`. A forced choice gets HTTP 400 ``only `"auto"` is supported for `tool_choice`. `"none"`, `"required"`, and named function choices are not currently supported``. AI Gateway and OpenCode Console (the report used `go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, served via `@ai-sdk/openai`) pass that message through unchanged. - None of the `FORCED_CHOICE_PATTERNS` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/tool-choice.ts`) matched, so `freeToolChoiceRetry` never fell back to `auto` and the first turn failed with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. - Added one pattern, `/only\W+auto\W+is supported for\W+tool_choice/i`. `\W+` also matches backticks, quotes, and the escaped quotes in a raw JSON body. The existing 4xx-only gate still applies. - I looked at matching on the provider error shape instead of the wording. There's no shared field: Anthropic's errors have no `param`, DeepSeek sends `param: null`, and this one comes through the gateway as a 400 with no structured reason. So the fix stays a message pattern and I didn't add a looser heuristic. - Docs: one line in `docs/models.mdx` beside the DeepSeek note. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, real model through AI Gateway: `E2E_MODEL=meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts tests-agent/act.e2e.ts --grep 'multi-action todo' --no-cache`. The step's deterministic checks are 1 remaining, both todos visible. - Also ran an openai-compatible fake server that sends 400 `only auto is supported for tool_choice` for any non-auto choice. On main the run fails after one `required` request. On this branch the server log shows `required`, then `auto`, and the step passes. - The new unit test in `tool-loop-tool-choice.test.ts` fails against main's `tool-choice.ts`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× act drives a multi-action todo flow` | `✓ act drives a multi-action todo flow 30.38s` | | ``MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: only `"auto"` is supported for `tool_choice`. `"none"`, `"required"`, and named function choices are not currently supported`` | `agent.act ... 29.93s · 6 model calls`, `$0.0040` | Not verified: a live OpenCode Console login (none available locally). The Console route for this model is `@ai-sdk/openai` according to models.dev, and the upstream wording is the same.

title: fix(agent): name the status and the body of a provider error the SDK could not parse
body: Fixes ENG-875 - When an error body doesn't match the provider's error schema, the AI SDK's JSON error handler (`createJsonErrorResponseHandler`) uses `response.statusText` as the message. `statusText` is empty over HTTP/2. The status and body stay on the `APICallError`, and `data` stays `undefined`. The ChatGPT backend's `400 {"detail":"Unsupported service_tier: fast"}` hits this path. - We only read `cause.message`, so the step failed `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with an empty message and the `--ai-trace` step error was `""`. - New `providerFailureMessage` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts`): for an `AI_APICallError` with status >= 400, a string body, and no parsed `data`, it returns `HTTP [ ]: `. - The body is redacted with the process secret redactor first, then cut at 1 KB with a `…` marker, so a secret that straddles the cut can't leak a prefix. - Errors the SDK parsed keep their message unchanged. Gateway errors are not `AI_APICallError`, so they are untouched too. - A spent `RetryError` is described by its last attempt, the same way judgments already unwrap it. Before this, a retryable HTTP/2 502 with an HTML body still read `Failed after 6 attempts. Last error: ` with nothing after it. - Used in `agent/model/sdk.ts` (judgments, including the `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW` message), `agent/tool-loop.ts` (act), and `internal/ai-trace.ts` (`onError`). - `docs/reference/errors.mdx` has one added sentence on the `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` row. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI against a local openai-compatible fake server that answers every request with `400 {"detail":"Unsupported service_tier: fast"}` and an empty status text. Command: `e2e run --config --ai-trace`, one `agent.act` step. The scratch config is not committed. - The new unit tests fail on main. The `ai-trace` one gets `''`, and the act and judgment ones get an empty provider message. They pass here and cover the act and judgment paths through a real `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` model with a stubbed `fetch`, redaction of a secret straddling the cut, and a 502 retry chain. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | step error | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: ` | `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: the model provider failed: HTTP 400: {"detail":"Unsupported service_tier: fast"}` | | `.e2e/ai-trace.json` step `error` | `""` | `"HTTP 400: {\"detail\":\"Unsupported service_tier: fast\"}"` | Not verified: the real ChatGPT backend (no stored login locally). The fake server reproduces the reported response shape.

title: fix(cache): --strict-cache replays on retries and never writes the cache
body: ## What and why - Under `--strict-cache` a retry skipped replay (`cache.reason: retry`), called the model, and re-staged its live recording over the committed entry. Attempt 1 could also evict the entry when it failed before anything verified the step. A strict run left `.e2e/cache` changed and spent model calls on recorded steps. - Retries skip replay on purpose: outside strict, a retry after a bad replay should not loop on the same trace, so it runs live and re-records. Strict means the opposite: committed recordings are reviewed test data, and a recording that does not hold should fail, not be absorbed by a model call. - `createAgentCacheContext` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts`) now builds a strict context as `read-only` whatever the configured mode, with `replayEligible` on every attempt. Nothing is recorded, written, or evicted, and a retry replays the same entry as attempt 1. - The `failedStale` guard in `StepTraceSession.conclude` is gone: it existed only to keep a stale entry from eviction in a strict read-write run, which can no longer happen. - Behavior change: a strict run no longer records a never-recorded step, even in `read-write` mode. It still runs live. Docs say to record new steps with a run without strict, and to prefer `--strict-cache` in CI over `cache.strict` in the config. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[attempt n] --> B{cache.strict} B -- off --> C{n = 0} C -- yes --> D[replay, read-write per mode] C -- no --> E[live, re-record] B -- on --> F[replay, read-only: no write, no evict] ``` Fixes ENG-876 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, a scratch test (not committed): `agent.act` on the wizard, then on the first attempt only it throws before the `expect` that verifies the step. Recorded once with a lenient run (gateway model), snapshotted `.e2e/cache`, then ran `e2e run --strict-cache --retries 1` on main and on this branch from the same snapshot. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `Cache 1 replayed · 1 missed`, retry `6 model calls`, 26.6k tokens | `Cache 2 replayed`, no model calls | | entry rewritten: `createdAt`, `summary`, `endWaitMs` changed (sha `acf1b63a` -> `1f52bb4f`) | `diff -r` clean, sha `acf1b63a` unchanged | ```text main ✓ ... > agent.act "create a workspace named "Atlas" on the Pro plan..." 540ms ✓ ... > agent.act "create a workspace named "Atlas" on the Pro plan..." 15.00s · 6 model calls Tests 0 passed | 1 flaky (1) Cache 1 replayed · 1 missed this branch ✓ ... > agent.act "create a workspace named "Atlas" on the Pro plan..." 528ms ✓ ... > agent.act "create a workspace named "Atlas" on the Pro plan..." 509ms Tests 0 passed | 1 flaky (1) Cache 2 replayed ``` - New integration tests in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-trace-cache.test.ts` (`--strict-cache never writes the cache`): a retry after a failed first attempt replays both attempts with zero executor calls and leaves the entry's bytes and mtime unchanged, and a never-recorded step runs live without creating the cache directory. Both fail on main. - Testbed suite passes on the branch. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(runner)!: a failed expect.soft before test.skip fails the attempt
body: - A failed `expect.soft` followed by `test.skip(...)` was reported SKIPPED with exit 0. The soft failure only showed up as a `secondaryErrors` entry and a "Skipped After Failure" warning, so a test that checks a value softly and then skips on a feature flag hid a real regression. - The soft failure now sticks. The attempt is `failed`, the soft failures are its error, the skip reason goes in the attempt's `skip`, and the attempt retries like any other failure. A skip no longer closes the soft collection inside the body. It is settled after the race, where the failure is recorded (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`). - Playwright 1.63.0 does the same (checked locally): `expect.soft` then `test.skip` gives a `failed` result, outcome `unexpected`, exit 1, with a `skip` annotation. One difference: for a failed attempt followed by a skipped retry, Playwright reports `flaky`. Here the test stays `skipped`, as before, listed under "Skipped After Failure", and `failOnSkippedFailure` still controls the exit code. - Wire: `report-v1` now allows `skip` on an attempt or serial member with any status except `passed` (it was only allowed on `skipped`). It is edited in place, as #713 and #724 did. A unit test pins the rule against the valid fixture. - CLI: under "Failed Tests", a line like `❯ skipped ` follows the error. The test's trace page (`trace.md`) gets `Also skipped: `. - Docs: `test`, `expect`, `config` (`failOnSkippedFailure` now covers only the skipped-retry case) and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. Breaking changeset (minor). Fixes ENG-833 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project in /tmp with a lifecycle-only engine (no browser, no model), `retries: 1`, three tests: soft failure then skip, hard failure then skip on retry, clean skip. Ran `npx e2e run` with the packed `e2e` from main (13da94b7) and then from this branch. - The new integration tests in `tests/integration/skip-after-failure.test.ts` fail 4/7 on main source and pass on this branch. title: test(web-benchmark): re-record agent recordings for @e2e-dev/web 0.13
body:
## What and why

- The `web agent` job fails on main and every open PR with 30 `REPLAY_STALE`. #825 (`chore: version packages`) bumped `@e2e-dev/web` from 0.12.0 to 0.13.0. The engine reports its own package version (`packages/web/src/engine.ts` `ownVersion()`), and the cache key keeps its major.minor (`engineCompatibilityVersion` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts`). So every committed entry sat under an old hash, and `--strict-cache` refused each step whose recording was stored under another key. No cache code changed.
- Re-recorded `tests-agent/` live: 30 new entries, one per old entry (same `recordedFor` step), and deleted the 30 old ones. Cache JSON only.
- Recorded on macOS, CI replays on Linux. The first rich-text-editor trace selected with `Control+Shift+ArrowLeft` then 8x `Shift+ArrowRight`. On macOS Chromium that chord selects to line start, so the presses leave "approved". On Linux it selects one word, so they collapse it and bold nothing. Re-recorded until the trace passes on Linux Chromium too: it now selects with `Shift+ArrowLeft` from the end. No other entry uses a modifier chord.
- Re-recorded playbook-cleanup: the first trace opened with two redundant taps on another playbook's menu.
- Steps not replayed are the same as #833: two planted-bug acts with no entry (missed by design), two gap misses, two gap handoffs.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Web benchmark, `e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` against the built packages, the same command CI runs.

| | main | this branch (run 1) | this branch (run 2) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tests | 30 failed (`REPLAY_STALE`) | 33 passed | 33 passed |
| Replayed | 0 | 26 | 26 |
| Handed off | - | 2 | 2 |
| Missed | 32 | 4 | 4 |
| Model calls | 8 | 20 | 20 |
| Cost | $0.0015 | $0.0035 | $0.0035 |

- rich-text-editor trace replayed key by key in Linux Chromium (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble`): old trace "Only the word approved must be bold", new trace "Document approved". Strict replay of that test 3x on macOS: 1 replayed each, plus a full strict suite: 33 passed, same counts as above.

Recording run: 33 passed, 32 missed, 124 model calls, $0.028.

## Follow-up

Same as #833: every minor release of an engine invalidates all committed recordings, and the release PR does not catch it. Separate change.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(web): read a sentence whole across its inline links and emphasis
body:
The tree the agent reads dropped every word inside an inline element from its sentence. `

Read our privacy policy for details.

` reached the model as `text="Read our for details."`, so explore reported missing copy that the page actually shows (13 of 17 findings on one marketing site). Every agent step had the same gap. Fixes ENG-919 ## What changed - Tree mode read an element's text with `directTextOf`, which counts only its own text nodes. It now uses `lineTextOf` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`): the element's text plus the text of each visible inline descendant (`inline*`, `ruby`, `display: contents`), in place. A block child, a line break, a form control, an image, or a frame splits words and contributes no text of its own. - The same rule applies to every inline element (`a`, `strong`, `em`, `code`, `span`). Only an element with text of its own reads through its children. A wrapper made only of elements lists them the same way it did before (`` does not change). - An inline element that is listed only for its text (`strong`, `em`, `code`, a plain `span`) is no longer listed separately once its parent's line includes that text (`isReadInLine`). A link, a button, or a node with a test id is still listed so the agent can act on it. The words of a link now appear twice (in the sentence and in the link's name), but the removed fragment lines save about as many tokens: a benchmark suite run used 76.4k tokens here vs 76.5k on main. - When a line is longer than the 512-char text bound, its inline descendants stay listed, so nothing after the cut is lost. - Node mode (locator reads, `getByText`) is unchanged. ```text main this branch #n29 text="We ship every week. Read the for what…" #n29 text="We ship every week. Read the release notes for what changed this week." #n30 link "release notes" href="/release-notes" #n30 link "release notes" href="/release-notes" #n31 text="Plans start at per seat, billed , and…" #n31 text="Plans start at $12 per seat, billed annually, and include the e2e CLI." #n32 text="$12" #n33 text="annually" #n34 text="e2e" ``` Cache keys do not change: tree text is not part of the key. Recorded anchors can change, though. One web-benchmark entry (`promo-storefront`) recorded `Jonas ★★★★★ Great bass…` as two text anchors, and the branch failed it with `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch). That entry is re-recorded here (same actions, the anchor is now one line). The re-recorded entry uses the `@e2e-dev/web` 0.13 key from #825. The other 29 entries in the suite are still under the 0.12 key, and the benchmark has been red on main since #825. Re-keying them belongs in its own re-record PR (like #833), so they are left alone here. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `packages/web/tests/integration/line-text.test.ts` is the new regression test. Against main's reader it fails 4 of 6 tests (the wrapper case passes there as intended), and all 6 pass on this branch. The web package suite passes (crosscheck and conformance included), and so does crosscheck against every web-benchmark scenario (`CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL`). - Testbed: a new `/plans` page with inline links, bold, italic, and code (not in the nav), plus `tests-agent/judgments.e2e.ts` "assert reads a sentence whole across its inline link and emphasis", paired with `getByText` checks. Run live with `gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` and `--no-cache`. - Web benchmark: the deterministic suite passes 91/91. `tests-agent` with `CI=1 --strict-cache` passed 33/33 against the 0.12 keys before the rebase and the review fixes, and the re-recorded `promo-storefront` entry replays with no model call under the 0.13 key. - Testbed deterministic suite: 71 passed, 1 skipped. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `e2e explore "Go to the /plans page and review its copy: report any sentence with missing or broken words"` | 2 findings: "Plans page sentence omits the release-notes link text" ("Read the for what changed this week."), "Plans pricing sentence omits price and billing interval" ("Plans start at per seat, billed , and include the CLI.") | Findings: none | | What `agent.assert` sees for `/plans` (`unbox-ai`) | `text="Plans start at per seat, billed , and include the CLI."` plus loose `"$12"`, `"annually"`, `"e2e"` lines | `text="Plans start at $12 per seat, billed annually, and include the e2e CLI."` | | `agent.assert` on the two full sentences, 5 runs | 5/5 pass (the judge fills in the gaps from the loose fragments) | 5/5 pass, 1.1k vs 1.2k input tokens | Before the PR, a fresh-context review found two problems, and both are fixed with tests. Zero-size and `font-size: 0` inline text had leaked into the line, and inline text after the 512-char cut was lost. Overlap with open reader PRs (#871, #895, #898, #900): this change touches none of their hunks in `read-semantics.ts`. It adds a new test file instead of editing `crosscheck/fixtures.ts`.

title: fix(core): match Unicode characters in test globs
body:
- A single `?` test glob skips a filename containing one emoji because the matcher consumes UTF-16 code units. Compile wildcard segments in Unicode mode so `?` consumes one code point. - Escape only regexp metacharacters, keeping literal Unicode and punctuation valid in Unicode mode. The shared redaction caller retains literal matching. - Includes a patch changeset and the test-glob reference note. AI-assisted work on behalf of rudycelekli; signed DCO commit. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Rebuilt the published `e2e` package, created real `tests/a.e2e.ts`, `tests/🐟.e2e.ts`, and `tests/ab.e2e.ts` files, and invoked `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js list 'tests/?.e2e.ts'` from that scratch project. | main (`89b783d`) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `tests/a.e2e.ts › collected [noop]` | `tests/a.e2e.ts › collected [noop]`
`tests/🐟.e2e.ts › collected [noop]` | - The `*` control lists all three files on both versions; `?` still excludes the two-character ASCII name. - The new unit assertions fail on main and pass here. Focused glob/regexp/redaction tests: 35 passed. Core unit suite: 2460 passed, one skipped. Direct core typecheck and lint pass. The rebuilt CLI native Chromium testbed suite: 14 files, 71 passed, one skipped. - Full `pnpm check` stops at the same filtered mobile-benchmark dependency on untouched main. The full Next benchmark is unavailable in the lean local dependency environment and was not rerun; hosted CI remains a required gate.

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- [#965](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/965) [`b92658b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b92658be6eb61a086c30b11fc36399872b863910) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Ask the operation first and its target second, with the goal and the recent actions in every question. Every target question carries a `none` option. Offer the whole action grammar: hover, right-click, double-tap, long-press, drag, scroll-to, and upload. Add `vision: true`, which sends the screenshot as a file part of the decision state (`ai` 7.0.134, `openai.decisionModel('gpt-6-luna')` with `@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.90) for screenshot verdicts and a `tap_at` that the text model names and score questions locate. Name a provider refusal.

- [#937](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/937) [`f1a1ac2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f1a1ac241042c089ae773213c4e4f0da34f2f3d8) Thanks [@outof-place](https://github.com/outof-place)! - `decisionExecutor({ providerOptions })` sends provider options with every decide call, the completion checks included, such as `{ gateway: { zeroDataRetention: true } }` for Vercel AI Gateway. They reach the decision model only: the text model keeps the agents entry's `providerOptions`. A value that does not map provider names to option objects fails config load with `INVALID_CONFIG`.
## e2e@0.19.0

### Minor Changes

- [#947](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/947) [`f3aa4c8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f3aa4c8c9ec6c04db0f76cc243573e3480370ef5) Thanks [@kblok](https://github.com/kblok)! - `locator.dblclick()` is an alias of `doubleTap()`, as `click()` is of `tap()`, so a test ported from Playwright or Cypress keeps its double clicks.

- [#869](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/869) [`1b92a6d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1b92a6ddfa8768c303953548e1b1e6cc5afbac8d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `trace` keeps its modes but now writes e2e's own trace instead of a Playwright zip: a markdown page per test, on every engine, and the terminal names it under each failed test (`❯ trace .e2e/results/<test>/trace.md`). The default is `retain-on-failure`, locally and in CI. Each step on the page shows what it did: the node an action landed on, the values an assertion or `waitFor` read while it waited, the replay cache's decision (where a replay stopped and why, what became of the recording, the entry file), what the app logged meanwhile (console output, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and 4xx and 5xx responses, also gathered in one App log section with each line's step), where the page went (a navigation, a new tab, a frame), and how the screen changed since the step before. The page also names the browser and user agent, or the device, the test ran on. The `markdown` reporter's `summary.md` names each failure's trace page when one was kept. `report.json` is still written for scripts, but the `list` summary no longer prints its path (`--debug` does), and prints `Report (not written)` only when it is missing. Everything a test left now sits in one directory, `<output>/results/<test>/` (`.e2e` by default): its `trace.md` (which shows the failure screenshot inline and links each file) and an `attempt-<n>/` per attempt, numbered from 1, with the screen at failure as `screen-at-failure.txt`. It replaces `.e2e/artifacts/<target>/<test id>/<agent>/attempt-<n>/`; a `--last-failed` rerun writes under each test's `rerun-<n>/`. Point CI uploads at `.e2e/results`, and add `.e2e/results/` to `.gitignore` (or rerun `e2e init`). A stale recording made from this version on names what changed in its key under `--strict-cache`, such as the agent's context. For engine authors: `startTrace` and `stopTrace` are no longer called, `trace` leaves `artifactCapabilities`, `EngineAttemptContext.appLog` takes what the app logs, `navigation` where it went on its own, `screen` takes a screen for the trace (one a `locate` matched against, or one read right after an action, bounded), and `environment` takes what the attempt runs on. report-1 drops the `trace` artifact kind and the `not-required` redaction (`StoredArtifact.kind` and `redaction` narrow the same way), drops `TRACE_WITHHELD`, and adds `attempt.appLog` (each line with its step), `navigation` events, `failure.viewport` and `failure.nodes`, `step.phase`, `step.screen`, `attempt.environment`, and `step.cache.entry`, `detail`, and `write` (report only; `result.cache` from `agent.act()` gains `entry` and `detail`). `FinishedRun.traces` maps results to their pages.

- [#965](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/965) [`b92658b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b92658be6eb61a086c30b11fc36399872b863910) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A custom `StepExecutor` that declares `vision: true` receives `agent.assert(..., { vision })` as `ctx.step.vision` instead of `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.

- [#978](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/978) [`2f60b54`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2f60b547f4f7f0f2a9931884a46d44ccbd2e0a84) Thanks [@mvanhorn](https://github.com/mvanhorn)! - `list` from `e2e/runner` reports the tests a config, file selection, and title grep would select, in process, without starting an app, an engine, or a worker. The result includes pairs a filter removed, positional arguments that matched no file, and the selected target names. `e2e list --reporter json` renames `skipReason` to `reason` and adds each pair's identity: `id`, `source`, `session`, `sessions`, `serialId`, and `agent`, beside the fields it already printed.

- [#924](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/924) [`d3d9081`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d3d9081eedd9f09d317c6443940dc9304a754e78) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Breaking: a failed `expect.soft` before `test.skip(...)` now fails the test, as in Playwright. Before, the test was reported `skipped` and the run exited 0 unless `failOnSkippedFailure` was set. The attempt is `failed` with the soft failures as its error, keeps the skip reason in its `skip` field, and retries like any failure. In `report.json`, an attempt or serial member may now carry `skip` with a failed status. The CLI prints the reason under the failure, and the trace page (`trace.md`) names it. `failOnSkippedFailure` now covers only a retry that skips after an earlier failed attempt.

- [#977](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/977) [`5137778`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5137778251928c42a736510fda002a984e924d17) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `toHaveScreenshot` for visual comparison on every engine that captures pixels: `await expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot('home.png')` compares the screen and `expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot()` one element against a PNG stored beside the test file, one per target and operating system. A missing one fails the test and is written beside it, or in CI attached to the results instead; `--update-snapshots` (`-u`) writes missing and different ones and passes. Options: `threshold`, `maxDiffPixels`, `maxDiffPixelRatio`, `mask`, `maskColor`, `timeout`. A mismatch attaches the expected, actual, and diff images to the step. On iOS and Android the status bar is held in a fixed state for these screenshots.

### Patch Changes

- [#893](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/893) [`7eb03ca`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7eb03cafdb869c23fadf07ff15facc3f2ccc0790) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Stop a fixture setup that finishes after its attempt was abandoned from starting later fixtures, hooks, or the test body. The late fixture still releases its own teardown.

- [#921](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/921) [`f2cf2ad`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f2cf2ad12aa1b6e5eeed4737d2d5b61e6be43531) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Agent steps on Meta's Muse Spark models, through AI Gateway or OpenCode Console, no longer fail with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: only auto is supported for tool_choice`. The refusal now reads as one, so the step retries with `auto` and the tool-calls-only rule, as it does for Anthropic and DeepSeek.

- [#929](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/929) [`e77c17a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e77c17ae0c1e0ac9a1abadd69b88e31e1cd54baf) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The replay cache key no longer carries the engine's version, so upgrading `@e2e-dev/web` or `@e2e-dev/mobile` keeps every committed recording. A recording re-finds its nodes at replay, which is where a node an engine release resolves differently is caught. Entries recorded before this release sit under the old keys: a `read-write` run records them again, and `--strict-cache` names them as `REPLAY_STALE` until it does.

- [#935](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/935) [`3c37d98`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3c37d981d98eb729edfa1b2d61f994fdfaf0db49) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Cancel the ChatGPT authorization-code token exchange when sign-in is interrupted.

- [#901](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/901) [`67b11b5`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/67b11b5af5f42e647b313b0634714344fc340c45) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Skip MCP tool execution when the client cancels a queued call or cancels during argument validation.

- [#936](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/936) [`5cdd3c6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5cdd3c60be848f709af1424a890c26755bbbf86a) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Cancel in-flight app and service readiness HTTP probes when the run is interrupted.

- [#899](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/899) [`d5a4eab`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d5a4eab34ea7b278cd61ef03f04f657c9b6405fb) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Cancel the initial OAuth device-code request promptly when login is interrupted, without showing or saving a cancelled login.

- [#918](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/918) [`9fb70b9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9fb70b9e99a379bda65b404d994a4f7aac9403c6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A credential whose `username` is not a string, or with a key other than `username` and `password`, fails the config load with `INVALID_CONFIG` naming the field, instead of a raw "value of type function is not JSON-safe" error. Only `password` may be a function. A credential with no username in the config or `E2E_USER_<NAME>_USERNAME` is `INVALID_CONFIG` too.

- [#907](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/907) [`fef1246`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/fef1246fb07fb35fb088d4489a2d7b16fc7a1187) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Keep direct locator reads within their original action timeout when a stale reference requires resolution again.

- [#887](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/887) [`4132715`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4132715cd55f840018402faafd07376af76a68d7) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - `e2e init` no longer writes an MCP config through a symlink: a `.mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json` reached through a link, or under a linked directory, is skipped with a warning naming the link and its target, the way a linked skill directory already was. Before, the merge read and overwrote the file the link pointed at, which could be a dotfiles repo or a shared config outside the project.

- [#919](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/919) [`b6efcf7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b6efcf71492192d1dc03b4b9ee9ccfe84b489e8e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `store: false` and a prompt cache key now go only to OpenAI and Azure OpenAI Responses models and to `openai/*` models on the gateway. An OpenAI-compatible provider named `openai` no longer fails with `Unknown parameter: promptCacheKey`.

- [#920](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/920) [`745b353`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/745b353b7a9e4686e7e996369725bd0f48a1b5d6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A polling assertion takes its last read at its timeout instead of up to 100 ms after it, so it no longer passes on a state that arrived after the timeout.

- [#922](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/922) [`c10dc00`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c10dc00992fb0207ef09e3d983822c53d076a39e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - When the provider package can't read a provider's error body, `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` no longer shows an empty message. One example is the ChatGPT backend's HTTP 400 `{"detail": "Unsupported service_tier: fast"}`. The message and the `--ai-trace` entry now show the HTTP status and the body, with secrets redacted and the body cut at 1 KB. An `agent.act` step that used up its transport retries now names the last attempt's failure, as judgments already did.

- [#905](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/905) [`ea0681a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ea0681ae8bded230f857ef25dac951d4917c5efb) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Reject read-only environment credentials before starting a provider login that cannot be saved.

- [#923](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/923) [`99d5ab5`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/99d5ab53367c5dc8df5a1c9959a08f2b37d3db47) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `--strict-cache` (and `cache.strict`) never writes or deletes a cache entry, even in `read-write` mode, and retries replay like the first attempt. Before, a retry skipped replay, called the model, and overwrote the committed entry, and a failed attempt could evict it.

- [#984](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/984) [`bc453bd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bc453bd52d5fe1b9a9fd59405db0c04676bfa188) Thanks [@ASVLCII](https://github.com/ASVLCII)! - Align `e2e cache ls` columns by displayed width for test file names containing wide characters, combining marks, or emoji.

Machines are named after the run and target, so `sweep` deletes what a dead worker left, and downloads are read off the machine's disk. `app: { source, setup, start, port, env }` runs the app under test inside each browser machine instead of on the runner's computer: `source` is copied in, `setup` and `start` run there, and the run waits for `port` to answer, so in `attempt` scope every attempt's branch holds its own copy of the running app and its data.

title: fix(cache): drop the engine version from the replay cache key
body: ## What and why - Every `chore: version packages` merge fails the strict `web agent` job on main with `REPLAY_STALE` on all 25 replayable steps (#825 now, #774 before it, re-recorded in #833). The cache key carried the engine's `major.minor`, and a 0.x engine bumps its minor on every release. - The key now keeps the engine's name and SPI version only. A release of the same engine is caught where it matters: each recorded action re-finds its node against a fresh observation at replay, so a node a new version resolves differently misses then (`relocate.ts`). Keying on the version only cold-started recordings for engines that had not changed how a node resolves. - The 30 web benchmark entries move to their new hashes. Each was re-keyed offline: the old key rebuilt from the entry's `recordedFor` and the agent config hashed to the committed file name for all 30, then the same parts hashed without the engine version. Entry contents are untouched (`git` shows 30 renames). - The mobile benchmark entries stay as they are. They were recorded on Sep 23-24 under `conservative/5` and the pre-#732 key shape, so they have been stale since #732 and need a real re-record on a Mac, not a re-key (mobile CI does not run strict, so it spends model calls instead of failing). - Docs: `cache.mdx` "What must match", `writing-an-engine.mdx`, the engine reference, and the AGENTS.md note on key changes. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web-benchmark run test:agent --strict-cache` against the built packages with a dummy gateway key, so a step that reaches the model fails and a replayed one cannot be mistaken for a live run: | | main (#825 CI) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `REPLAY_STALE` | 25 | 0 | | Replayed | 0 | 26 | | Handed off | - | 2 | | Missed | - | 4 | | Model calls | 8 | 1 (dummy key, rejected) | The 26/2/4 split is the one #833 recorded. The 7 failures are all `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` from the dummy key on the handed-off and never-recorded steps; the cache directory was left unchanged by the run. - `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run --project unit`: 2459 passed. `lint`, `typecheck`, `docs:check` pass. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(oauth): stop device polling at code expiry
body: - A device-code token request can stay pending after the advertised code lifetime, leaving `e2e login` stuck. Bound each poll by the remaining lifetime and abort its HTTP request when the code expires. - Stop before dispatch when the sleep interval exhausts the lifetime, and refuse a grant that arrives after expiry. Preserve the existing `TIMEOUT` message. - This addresses expiry; #899 addresses user interruption in the same file. A temporary combined branch passed all 92 OAuth tests plus the real CLI expiry, initial-request cancellation, and in-flight cancellation consumers. The combined poll retains #899's cancellation catch around the expiry-bounded request. - Includes the matching docs sentence and patch changeset. AI-assisted work on behalf of rudycelekli, with a signed DCO commit. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Rebuilt the published CLI and ran `e2e login github-copilot --client-id local-proof`. A local HTTP server supplies the ordinary device response (`expires_in: 2`, `interval: 1`) and holds the token response. A preload redirects the GitHub endpoints to loopback; no live account or credentials are used. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Remains alive beyond expiry and requires SIGKILL cleanup. | Exits with code 1 at expiry and prints `the device code expired before the login finished; run the login again`. | - Regression tests cover sleep-to-expiry, a stalled poll, and a grant arriving late. Standalone OAuth suite: 87 passed; core unit suite: 2463 passed, one skipped. Core build, direct package typecheck, and lint pass. - The monorepo check stops at the same filtered mobile-benchmark dependency on untouched main. The full Next benchmark was not rerun locally. Current hosted Node matrix runs on other branches also show a separate existing exact-500ms download-diagnostic assertion failure; hosted checks remain a required gate. ## Current verification - October 9, 2026 (New York) Signed merge onto main `163257bd6a7cce092695725b7d6a485c93586098`, current head `d7517678e02a27966dbc309014280fb1b61f7987`. Focused current source passes 97 OAuth tests; the actual built consumer/CLI controls were rerun before pushing. Every current hosted check has completed successfully and the repository babysit script returns READY with no outstanding comments, review threads or changes requested. The older CI authorization notes above describe earlier heads. Full local monorepo checks remain environment-limited; hosted acceptance is reported separately.

title: ci: gate merges through the merge queue with one required check per workflow
body: The `Main` ruleset enables a merge queue but requires no status checks, and no workflow listens to `merge_group`. So the queue merges right away and auto-merge waits on nothing: #929 merged while `spec` and `mobile` were still running. - Each of `spec`, `benchmark`, `mobile`, `docs` ends in a ` gate` job. It fails when any job it needs failed or was cancelled and passes over a skipped one. These four are the only checks the ruleset will require. - All four trigger on `merge_group`, so the queue runs every suite on the queued tree before it merges. - `mobile`: `changes` plans the suites as a matrix. A fork or Dependabot PR leaves out `agentic` at the job level. Before, those jobs built the Expo app and booted 2 simulators, then skipped only the run step and reported green. - `mobile` on push to main runs no suite (the queue already tested the same tree). It only rebuilds the Expo app on a cache miss (`lookup-only`), because main's cache scope is the one PRs and queue entries restore from. The per-platform build commands moved into `.github/actions/expo-app` so both paths share them. - `docs` drops its workflow-level `paths:` (a required gate would sit pending forever) for a `docs` entry in `.github/filters.yml`. It no longer runs on push to main. - `benchmark` `web agent` skips Dependabot PRs, as mobile already did. - `spec` and `benchmark` still run on push to main (cheap, they warm main's caches, and they keep a health signal). ```mermaid flowchart LR PR[pull_request] --> G1[4 gates] AM[auto-merge] --> Q[merge_group] Q --> G2[4 gates on queued tree] G2 -- all green --> M[merge to main] M --> S[spec + benchmark, mobile app cache warm] ``` **Trust change:** the queue runs a queued PR's code with repo secrets, fork or not. Enqueueing is now the trust decision (written into AGENTS.md security invariants). **Rejected review finding:** the agent-device runner cache will no longer be saved on main. Measured on #917, a cache miss costs nothing visible (suite 9:46 on a miss vs 10:53 on a hit), so it isn't worth warming. ## After merge Update the `Main` ruleset (doing it before this lands would block every open PR): - add `required_status_checks`: `spec gate`, `benchmark gate`, `mobile gate`, `docs gate` (GitHub Actions integration) - raise `check_response_timeout_minutes` from 60 to 120 (mobile jobs time out at 60, plus the macOS queue) ## Verified Ran it locally: no - CI-only. `actionlint` is clean (Blacksmith labels and one existing SC2016 ignored) and `pnpm check` passes. The `pull_request` path is verified by this PR's own runs. The `merge_group` path can only be exercised after the ruleset update.

title: fix(core): stop surviving app-command descendants
body:
## What and why

- Keep an owned process group in the forced-exit registry after its leader exits. Descendants can still serve requests; normal cleanup must send SIGTERM, preserve the declared shutdown grace, and escalate survivors to SIGKILL.
- Preserve current readiness-probe cancellation. Remove the fake-timer unit test, unrelated #934 download change, and configuration paragraph requested in review. Retain the patch changeset.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Leader exits] --> B[Keep owned group registered]
  B --> C[Stop sends SIGTERM]
  C --> D{Group survives grace?}
  D -- yes --> E[SIGKILL survivors]
  D -- no --> F[Release registry entry]
  E --> F
```

Wall medians are 3.36 s on main and 3.39 s here; the harness classifies timings as the same. No performance improvement is claimed.

Current hosted spec, benchmark, docs, and mobile workflows all pass at signed head `22a2b325`; maintainer re-review remains required.

title: fix(oauth): cancel model calls waiting for token refresh
body: - A canceled subscription model call can stay pending while an expired token is refreshing. The request's abort signal only reaches the later model HTTP request, so a held refresh delays cancellation indefinitely. - Race the request pipeline with its own signal, preserve the original abort reason, and check cancellation before sending. Leave a shared refresh available to another active model call. - Regressions cover an already-aborted call and two callers sharing one refresh: the canceled waiter returns before refresh completes, the active caller succeeds, and only its model request is sent. - Includes the matching subscriptions docs sentence and patch changeset. AI-assisted work on behalf of rudycelekli with a signed DCO commit. This is separate from device-login interruption #899 and device-code expiry #930; it changes `oauth/fetch.ts`, not their login flow. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Rebuilt the public `e2e/oauth/chatgpt` model and invoked `doGenerate` through the actual AI SDK. A local HTTP server holds the refresh response; native fetch is redirected to loopback and uses fake expired credentials. Abort the model call after that HTTP request arrives: ```text main: still pending 300ms after abort; returns only after refresh released this branch: AbortError: This operation was aborted, before refresh released ``` No live subscription account or model service was used. Fetch regressions: 12 passed; OAuth suite: 86 passed; core unit suite: 172 files, 2463 passed, one skipped. Core build, direct package typecheck and lint pass. Only `docs/subscriptions.mdx` conflicted. It retains main’s updated login help and the cancellation guarantee as a separate paragraph. title: test(core): assert the remaining download wait budget
body: - The native download diagnostic integration assertion assumes the configured `500ms` timeout is the exact wait budget. The engine correctly reports the remaining deadline after setup, so normal timing jitter makes the strict expression return no match and the trigger duration becomes `NaN`. - Keep the complete diagnostic format and `ACTION_FAILED` classification, capture both integer durations, require a positive wait capped by the configured 500ms, and retain the trigger's 190ms lower bound. - Test-only reliability correction; no runtime or public behavior changes. AI-assisted work on behalf of rudycelekli with a signed DCO commit. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Two actual hosted native spec failures show the old assertion rejecting the download timing: [Node26 run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/37471012930) and [Node22 run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/37471022321). Both reach the same assertion and produce `NaN` while the expected failure remains `ACTION_FAILED`. Rebuilt the core CLI and web engine at this signed head. The native Chromium `web-platform.test.ts` suite consumes the built CLI and passes all 40 cases, including the 200ms no-download trigger and schema validation of its failed report. Lint and diff checks pass. This patch does not weaken the message grammar or accept a wait beyond the requested budget. Hosted workflows remain required.

title: fix(core): cancel readiness HTTP probes when interrupted
body: A run interrupted while a readiness endpoint holds its HTTP response waits for the separate 2-second probe timeout before teardown. This affects both the preflight check and probes after the app command starts. Pass the run signal into both probes and combine it with the existing probe timeout. Cancellation remains a non-answer to readiness; the existing signal guards prevent spawning after an interrupted preflight and stop an already spawned command. ## Verified - Built public CLI `e2e run`, actual loopback HTTP server holding response headers, SIGINT after the request arrives: current main exited 130 after 2,006 ms; this branch exited 130 in 13 ms (29 ms on the signed-head rerun). The docs and mobile dependencies and Next.js benchmark dependencies are not installed locally; full check and web benchmark are not claimed green. - Current open PR files screened. #932 changes descendant shutdown ownership in the same source file; this fixes in-flight startup HTTP cancellation. #648 changes the services architecture but leaves these probes unchanged. title: feat(decision): send providerOptions with every decide call
body: `decisionExecutor()` has no way to set provider options on its decide calls, so a gateway-routed decision model cannot ask for zero data retention or any other provider setting. This adds a decide-only `providerOptions`, the same way `createToolLoopExecutor({ providerOptions })` takes them. - `decisionExecutor({ providerOptions })` sends them with every decide call: the operation and target questions, `typeSecret`, and the completion checks. - They reach the decision model only. The text model keeps the agents entry's `providerOptions` (`ctx.providerOptions`), as the spec in #775 asks, so a gateway setting meant for one model (a fallback list, for example) never reaches the other. - A value that does not map provider names to option objects fails config load with `INVALID_CONFIG`. ```ts import { gateway } from 'ai'; import { decisionExecutor } from '@e2e-dev/decision'; const executor = decisionExecutor({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev'), textModel: gateway('openai/gpt-4.1-nano'), providerOptions: { gateway: { zeroDataRetention: true } }, }); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web benchmark, `tests-agent/login-form.e2e.ts --no-cache` with `agents.default.executor` set to the snippet above (`gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev')`), and a `createGateway({ fetch })` that logs each `/decision-model` request's `providerOptions` and the response's `providerMetadata.gateway.routing.planningReasoning`. The test passes on both; only this branch sends the options, and only then does the gateway route with zero data retention: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | decide calls | 5 | 5 | | calls carrying `providerOptions` | 0 | 5 | | gateway routing says `ZDR requested` | 0 | 5 | | routing | `typesafe-ai(system) → digitalocean(system)` | `ZDR execution order: typesafe-ai(system)` |

title: feat(cache): replay-only runs that fail a step with no recording instead of calling the model
body:
We gate every push on a replay of our committed recordings. The gate must make zero model calls:
a step whose recording is missing or stale should fail, not quietly spend tokens. Today
`cache: { mode: 'read-only', strict: true }` gets close but not all the way:

- A step with no entry at all still runs live under strict (`docs/cache.mdx`, "a never-recorded
  step runs live"); `no-entry` is not in `STALE_REASONS` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`).
- `failIfRekeyed` only recognizes an entry that records its whole step (`paramsDigest`,
  `callIndex`, `agent`). Entries written before 0.17 carry only `testId`, `targetId` and
  `instructionDigest`, so after a key change (0.13's engine minor, or #929) strict treats them as
  never recorded and the step goes live. We hit this with 22 committed recordings on the 0.18
  upgrade.
- `agent.assert`, `waitFor` and `extract` always run live, and `maxModelCalls` cannot be 0.

So a replay-only gate today needs three workarounds, the same trick #929's Verified section used:
a model that throws in every agent slot, stripping `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`
(the gateway falls back to an OIDC token from `.vercel/project.json`), and an audit of
`report.json` that every `agent.act` is `self-finalized` with `metrics.modelCalls === 0`.

Proposal: `cache.replayOnly: true` (and `--replay-only`) that implies strict and read-only, fails
any agent step without a replayable entry with a typed code (e.g. `REPLAY_MISSING`), refuses
`assert` / `waitFor` / `extract` at collection or at the call with the same code, and never
resolves a model. Happy to send the PR once the shape is agreed (it touches the CLI, the config
schema and an error code, so it seems to want a maintainer's yes first). Related: #923.

title: feat(report): record each step's cache outcome (written, kept, evicted and why)
body:
`StepCacheInfo` (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`) says how a step read the cache (`mode`,
`reason`), but not what the attempt did to the recording at the end: written, kept as it was, or
evicted and why (repair after an end mismatch, unconfirmed write, failed after a replay). Those
decisions are deliberate (`step-cache.ts` `conclude`, `cache/context.ts`), so a self-healing CI
loop needs them to know which tests to run a second pass for. Today we reconstruct it by diffing
the cache directory against git before and after the run.

Proposal: an optional `outcome: 'written' | 'kept' | 'evicted'` plus `outcomeReason` on
`StepCacheInfo`, filled at attempt-end settlement. Additive, so no schema break.

title: feat(tools): inbox tools for flows that send email (OTP, magic links)
body:
Following #677 (`maildev()`, `new_email_address`, `wait_for_email`), which has stalled since
2026-09-30: we run three inbox backends behind one interface in our suite and would contribute the
generic core if it fits as a tool pack like `@e2e-dev/mobile/tools`:

- Mailpit (local stacks): search by exact recipient, since Mailpit's `to:` matches fragments;
- SES inbound to S3 (real delivery with SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdicts from the SES header block);
- Resend receiving (`GET /emails/receiving`, 10 req/s per team, no recipient filter server-side).

Common shape: unique plus-addresses per test, a poll with deadline, exact recipient match, and
code extraction that requires exactly one code of the expected length. Would you take this as
`@e2e-dev/<name>` or under `e2e/tools`, and should it wait for #677?

title: fix(web): serialize method functions for page evaluation
body: Passing an object method to `browser.evaluate` produces method shorthand such as `title() { ... }`, which is not a standalone function expression. Evaluation fails with `EVALUATE_FAILED`; the same source in an init script fails to execute in the page. Normalize ordinary and async identifier methods into function expressions before inlining them. Parsing checks the expression without executing it on the host. Existing arrow and function expressions retain their source. Both evaluation and configured/test init scripts use the same internal helper. ## Verification Historical native verification of the unchanged production implementation: the built public CLI with real Chromium failed both evaluation and init-script cases on main and passed them on this implementation. The full native web suite passed 506 tests with 1 skipped, and the public CLI testbed passed 73 with 1 skipped. The configured init-script lifecycle regression covers frames, tabs, and replaced contexts. Getter and bound-method refusal controls are retained. The maintainer-requested test/docs repair is e4fa77d: ordinary and async argument cases now live in the web evaluation unit suite, and the init-script integration regression remains. The added web reference prose and unrelated download-budget change were removed. Production files, the init-script regression, and the patch changeset are byte-identical to the prior head. All four required hosted gates (`spec gate`, `benchmark gate`, `mobile gate`, `docs gate`) succeeded on e4fa77d. All five Node test jobs and the actual web suites passed. The mobile suites were intentionally skipped by the workflow for this web-scoped change; a successful mobile gate does not claim a new device run. No public type or wire-format changes. This does not claim support for every computed/getter method source form. AI-assisted implementation and verification on behalf of rudycelekli; independently source reviewed before publication. Merge and Ready for Human Review remain maintainer actions.

title: fix(decision): give the completion check the step origin and page moves
body: ## Summary Fixes #885. Navigation steps usually end blocked even when the tap was correct. The completion check only saw the goal, the current page, and the step actions. It never saw where the step started, so after Click Back it could not tell came back from never moved. Named links held at 0.33 to 0.40 and Back held at 0.08 to 0.11 in the report. ## Change Forward what the executor already knows to the completion check: - packages/decision/src/executor.ts: record the first observed path as the step origin and pass it to completionRequest. - packages/decision/src/questions.ts: accept origin in CompletionInput, send origin.path when it differs from the current page, mark actions that changed the page with (page changed), and tell the check that a move from origin to a new page counts even for generic labels such as Back. - packages/decision/tests/executor.test.ts: cover origin sent on navigation and origin omitted when the page never changes. - .changeset/decision-completion-origin.md: patch changeset for @e2e-dev/decision. No operation logic changes. Steps that never leave their page send no origin, so existing checks read the same state as before. ## Test plan - pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/decision run test: 5 files, 90 passed. - pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/decision run typecheck: clean. - oxlint on changed files: clean.
