title: fix(agent): a model refusal fails as MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED "No output generated"
body:
`e2e explore` with goal "Read-only probe: change the token in /r/<token> and the booking id in
/rezerwacja/<id>/platnosc to near and random values, and report any page that shows another
booking's data or an error that leaks internal details." fails before the first step with
`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: No output generated.` (exit 3), every time. The
planning call is an `agent.extract` on `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` through Vercel AI Gateway, and
the model refused it: the same prompt through `generateText` returns `finishReason:
'content-filter'`, raw `refusal`, 2 of 2; the goal rephrased as a check ("every changed address
should show a not-found page") plans 2 of 2.

Nothing in the report says "refusal", so the run reads as a provider outage, and a retry policy
keyed on exit 3 (ours retried once) spends a second call on a prompt that is refused by
construction.

Proposal: when the model call ends with `finishReason === 'content-filter'` (or the structured
output is empty after one), fail with a typed, non-retryable code (e.g. `MODEL_REFUSED`) whose
message names the step, the model and the raw finish reason. Happy to send the PR.

title: feat(report): record each step's cache outcome (written, kept, evicted and why)
body: Closes #939. ## What and why - `StepCacheInfo` says how a step *read* the cache (`mode`, `reason`) but not what the attempt then did to the recording. A self-healing CI loop needs that to know which tests to run a second pass for, and today it has to diff `.e2e/cache/` against git. - Adds two optional fields, as proposed in the issue: - `outcome: 'written' | 'kept' | 'evicted'` - `outcomeReason`: kept is `confirmed` or `unchanged`; evicted is `repaired`, `failed-after-replay`, `not-replaced` or `unconfirmed`; absent on `written`. - Additive: both fields are optional and only appear in `read-write` mode when the attempt changed or confirmed an entry. A read-only cache, an interrupted attempt, a step with no verdict, or nothing to record and nothing stored leaves `outcome` absent. No schema version bump. - The report only claims what the store actually did: a custom store without `delete`, a rejected delete, or a failed write reports no outcome. Each outcome comes from the place that already makes the decision: ```mermaid flowchart LR S[step settles] --> C["StepTraceSession.conclude()"] C -- "end-mismatch repaired" --> E1["evicted: repaired"] C -- "failed after replay" --> E2["evicted: failed-after-replay"] C -- "passed, nothing to stage, entry read" --> E3["evicted: not-replaced"] C -- "staged write / keep" --> A[attempt ends] A --> F["flushStagedTraces()"] F -- "not verified, implicated" --> E4["evicted: unconfirmed"] F -- "keep, verified" --> K1["kept: confirmed"] F -- "write, same flow stored" --> K2["kept: unchanged"] F -- "write, verified" --> W[written] ``` - Step-time evictions: `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`, `evict(reason)` sets the outcome on the step's cache info once the delete has settled. `conclude()` runs before `finish()` attaches the details, so these reach both the report and `agent.act()`'s result. - Attempt-end settlement: `flushStagedTraces` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts`) now returns `{ stepIndex, outcome, outcomeReason? }[]`, and `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts` merges them into `record.steps[stepIndex].cache` right after the flush. `agent.act()` returns before the attempt settles, so its result carries only the step-time evictions. The docs say so. - Wire change: `report-v1.schema.json` gets both enums plus `allOf` rules (reason only with an outcome, no reason on `written`, each reason only with its own outcome). Both fixtures and a schema test pin those rules. - Docs: a new "What a run did to a recording" table in `docs/cache.mdx`, plus `docs/reference/agent.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`. - One existing unit test, `evicts an entry that did not serve a pass with nothing to record in its place`, recorded the replayed tap *after* `begin()`, so it was going down the repair branch instead. Its host now records the tap through the grammar, as the real dispatch does, and the test asserts `not-replaced`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A real `e2e` run against the browser fixture app with a scripted two-tap executor and `cache: 'read-write'`. Run 1 records, run 2 replays, and run 3 tightens the assertion so it fails. This is `step.cache` from each run's `report.json`: ```text run 1, record: {"mode":"missed","reason":"no-entry","replayedActions":0,"totalActions":0,"outcome":"written"} run 2, replay: {"mode":"self-finalized","replayedActions":2,"totalActions":2,"outcome":"kept","outcomeReason":"confirmed"} run 3, assertion fails: {"mode":"self-finalized","replayedActions":2,"totalActions":2,"outcome":"evicted","outcomeReason":"unconfirmed"} ``` - The integration suites `trace-cache-replay` and `agent-trace-cache` now assert the outcome end to end: kept/`confirmed` on whole replays, `written` on re-recordings, evicted/`unconfirmed` when a later assertion fails, and no outcome when the failure is a model that never answered or the cache is read-only in CI. - Done on Windows. The full `e2e` package run has failures in 26 files on Windows (CRLF line endings, `\` paths, POSIX file modes, git/telemetry environment). All 26 fail the same way on `main`, and none of them touch the cache or the report. `pnpm docs:check` was not run locally, because it needs the Mintlify docs workspace installed. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: not one. Both fields are optional additions. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. (`sdk-types.ts` has no `StepCacheInfo` assertions, so nothing changed there.) - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): not touched.

title: feat(locator): add dblclick as an alias of doubleTap
body: Playwright and Cypress tests call `dblclick()`. We only had `doubleTap()`, so every double click had to be renamed when porting a test. `click()` is already an alias of `tap()`, and now `dblclick()` is an alias of `doubleTap()` too. ```ts await screen.getByRole('listitem', 'Buy milk').dblclick(); await row.dblclick({ modifiers: ['Shift'] }); ``` - It sends the same `doubleTap` action to the engine. No engine or capability change. - It takes the same options as `doubleTap()`: `timeout` and `modifiers`. - Steps and traces record it as `locator.dblclick`, the same way `click()` records as `locator.click`. - The migration guides and the screen reference list the alias. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, a temporary test on `/controls`: `screen.getByRole('button', 'Tap me twice').dblclick()` set the gesture state to `double-tapped` in Chromium. ``` ✓ |web| tests/zz-dblclick-verify.e2e.ts (1 test) 490ms ✓ dblclick double-clicks like doubleTap 490ms ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: chore(skills): move repo-only skills to .dev/skills so skills add offers only e2e
body:
## What and why

`npx skills add tester-army/e2e` listed five skills: `e2e`, plus the four we only use to work on this repo (`babysit`, `ship-pr`, `verify`, `writing-pr`). Users should get `e2e` alone.

- The four skills move to `.dev/skills/`, a directory the skills CLI never scans by default.
- `.claude/skills/<name>` is now a relative symlink to each, so agents working in the repo load them as before. The skills CLI skips directory symlinks: its walk keeps only entries where `Dirent.isDirectory()` is true. When it installs from GitHub it reads the git tree, where a symlink is a blob with no `SKILL.md` under it.
- Each one also sets `metadata.internal: true`. That hides them from `--full-depth`, which walks the whole clone and does reach `.dev/skills/`.
- `unbox-ai` and `unslop` stay in `.claude/skills/`. The CLI already skips them as installed skills tracked by `skills-lock.json`.
- I updated every path that pointed at the old location: the babysit script step in `spec.yml`, the PR template, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and links inside the skills. The `unslop`/`unbox-ai` links use `../../../.claude/skills/...`, which resolves the same from `.dev/skills/<name>` and through the symlink.
- `.oxlintrc.json` ignores the symlinked paths. Without that, oxlint follows them and reports every babysit script finding twice.
- On Windows the symlinks need Developer Mode and `core.symlinks=true`. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says so.

```
.claude/skills/
  babysit    -> ../../.dev/skills/babysit
  ship-pr    -> ../../.dev/skills/ship-pr
  verify     -> ../../.dev/skills/verify
  writing-pr -> ../../.dev/skills/writing-pr
  unbox-ai/  (vendored, skills-lock.json)
  unslop/    (vendored, skills-lock.json)
.dev/skills/{babysit,ship-pr,verify,writing-pr}/
skills/e2e/  (the one users install)
```

The published package doesn't change. `prepare-build.ts` copies only `skills/e2e`, and `e2e init` reads only that copy.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `npx skills@latest add . --list` on main lists `babysit`, `e2e`, `ship-pr`, `verify`, `writing-pr`. On this branch it lists `e2e` alone. It is still `e2e` alone with `--full-depth`, and with `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1` on the default scan.

  | main | this branch |
  | --- | --- |
  | `Found 5 skills`: babysit, e2e, ship-pr, verify, writing-pr | `Found 1 skill`: e2e |

- From GitHub, the way users run it: `npx skills@latest add "tester-army/e2e#t3code/isolate-internal-skills" --list` prints `Found 1 skill`: `e2e`.

- `opencode debug skill` in the repo still lists `babysit`, `ship-pr`, `verify`, `writing-pr`, `unbox-ai`, `unslop` from `.claude/skills/`. I haven't checked Claude Code (not installed here). `npx skills add` installs into `.claude/skills/` as symlinks by default, so Claude Code already loads skills through links.
- `e2e init --yes` from the built package in an empty directory wrote `.agents/skills/e2e/` (9 files, identical to `skills/e2e`) and linked `.claude/skills/e2e` to it. `npm pack --dry-run` of `e2e` includes nothing from `.dev/` or `.claude/`.
- `tsc -p .dev/skills/babysit/scripts` and `node --test .dev/skills/babysit/scripts/pr-status.test.ts` (14/14) pass at the new path, the same commands as the CI step.
- I'm not adding a changeset: no published package changes.

title: @e2e-dev/mobile: video start names no device, so an attempt after closeApp() fails when several simulators are booted
mobile: node ids are re-minted on every observation, so an unchanged screen diffs as "changed substantially" and the agent mis-keys a number pad
body:
### What happened

On iOS, `@e2e-dev/mobile` gives every node a brand-new id on every observation, even when the screen did not change. After any action the agent gets a screen where all ids are new, plus "The screen changed substantially since revision bN", even if only one label changed. The core promises the model "Every node not listed as removed is still on screen under the id you have". The web engine keeps that promise because it stamps an id on each element once (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`, `read-node.ts`). The mobile engine breaks it.

The id comes from `MobileSurface.project()` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`), which calls `projectSnapshot(raw.nodes, { mintId: () => \`n${++this.idCounter}\` })` for every snapshot. `projectSnapshot` (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`) calls `mintId()` once per node. Nothing carries an id over from the previous observation, so `diffScreens` sees every node removed and added again, and falls back to a full listing.

**Impact:** the agent cannot reliably enter a number on an on-screen keypad. Each key press changes one text node, the amount readout. But the model gets a full re-listing with about 25 new ids every turn, so it has to find every key again among ids that are themselves numbers (`#n1480 button "7"`, `#n1484 button "0"`). With `chatgpt('gpt-6-luna')`, asked to enter **750**, it entered `70`, `707`, `7`, `70` and so on for 17 actions, and never pressed `5`. The step failed: *"the amount remains 0 USD; the attempted number-pad sequence did not produce the requested 750"*. Every tap the engine performed matched the key behind the id the model chose, so stale-id resolution is fine. What fails is the model working with an id space that changes completely after every key press. In an earlier run the model sent several taps in one turn against the ids it had been shown, and some of them pointed at the neighbouring key (`n736, n734, n730` came out as `7, 5, 1` for "750").

Revision b16 to b18 is one key press. The only change is `text "Amount 70 USD"` becoming `text "Amount 7 USD"`, but every id moved: `application` went from `#n806` to `#n854`, the keypad from `#n817` to `#n865`, and so on.

### Minimal reproduction

Any screen where a tap changes one label shows the id churn. The keypad makes the impact visible. The app is an Expo SDK 57 dev build ([Stringsaeed/money-management](https://github.com/Stringsaeed/money-management), `apps/mobile-next`). Its pad is 12 `Pressable`s with `accessibilityRole="button"` and labels `"1"`–`"9"`, `"Decimal point"`, `"0"`, `"Delete digit"`, under a readout labelled `Amount <value> <currency>`.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts (excerpt)
targets: [{ name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios', device: process.env.E2E_IOS_DEVICE, transition: 700 }),
  app: { bundleId: 'com.stringsaeed.moneymanagement.next', launchArguments: ['--initialUrl', 'http://localhost:8085'] } }],
agents: { default: { model: chatgpt('gpt-6-luna') } },
```

```ts
test('repro: the agent types 750 on the number pad', async ({ agent, screen }) => {
  await addFirstAccount(screen, { name: 'Everyday', openingBalance: '100' }); // screen.* taps, deterministic
  await agent.act('open the New transaction editor, enter an amount of {amount} on the number pad, and save it', {
    params: { amount: '750' },
  });
  await expect(screen.getByText('$650.00')).toBeVisible();
});
```

Run: `e2e run tests/zz-repro.e2e.ts --no-cache --video on`.

The same digits typed with deterministic `screen.getByRole('button', d).tap()` or `screen.tapAt()` always give exactly 750, both rapid-fire and spaced out.

**Recording:** [issue1-agent-number-pad.mp4](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Stringsaeed/cf3cca31891a14d7a4e86c1a4a73ceb0/raw/issue1-agent-number-pad.mp4) (2:36, 15 fps)

![frames every 10 s](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Stringsaeed/cf3cca31891a14d7a4e86c1a4a73ceb0/raw/issue1-contact-sheet.png)

Each id the model chose, mapped to the key it labelled in the screen the model had just been shown, next to what the engine performed ([full table](https://gist.github.com/Stringsaeed/cf3cca31891a14d7a4e86c1a4a73ceb0#file-issue1-id-mapping-txt)):

```
turn | call       | id    | key at that id in the screen shown | key the engine pressed
  10 | tap        | n920  | 7                                  | tap button "7"
  11 | tap        | n972  | 0                                  | tap button "0"
  12 | long_press | n1021 | Delete digit                       | long-press button "Delete digit"
  13 | tap        | n1064 | 7                                  | tap button "7"
  ...
```

### Suggested fix

Carry ids forward the way the web engine does. When a snapshot is projected, match each node to a node in the previous generation, for example by parent path plus role, label and identifier, or by agent-device's own stable node identity if it exposes one, and reuse that id. Mint a new id only for nodes that are actually new. Then a key press diffs as one changed line (`~ #n1471 text "Amount 7 USD"`), and every other id the model holds stays valid.

I'd like to work on this and can open a PR if the approach sounds right.

### Versions

- `e2e` 0.17.0, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.9.2, `agent-device` 0.21.20. The code above is unchanged on `main` (mobile 0.10.0 / agent-device 0.21.22).
- Node 26.7.0, macOS 27.0.1, iOS 27.0 simulator (iPhone 17), Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86 dev client.
- Model: `chatgpt('gpt-6-luna')` via `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`.

### Engine

mobile (`@e2e-dev/mobile`)

### Anything else

- Possibly related: #797 ("suspected snapshot ref lifetime mismatch") and #842 (iOS 27 screen identity varies between captures of the same screen).
- agent-device also falls back between snapshot backends within a session ("Detected an overly complex or slow accessibility tree. Fell back to the private-ax snapshot backend", then "used XCTest"). The same screen comes back with a different node set depending on the backend: the iOS scroll-indicator elements appear 0, 1 or 2 times. Matching nodes by content instead of by position would also absorb that.
- Agent turns, failure screen, and the id mapping: <https://gist.github.com/Stringsaeed/cf3cca31891a14d7a4e86c1a4a73ceb0>

title: mobile: locator.tap() dispatches on a disabled node instead of waiting for it to become enabled
MCP server: `tap` cannot hold modifier keys (Shift-click, Ctrl-click, Cmd-click)
body:
### Problem

The `tap`, `double_tap`, and `right_click` tools of the MCP server do not have a `modifiers` argument. An agent that uses the MCP server cannot do a Shift-click or a Ctrl-click. The test API has this function since #626: `tap({ modifiers: ['Shift'] })`.

We have a web app. A Shift-click in a list of the app selects a range of rows. The bulk-delete action shows only after you select more than one row. Agents use the MCP server to examine this feature in the app. The agents cannot select the rows.

To see the problem:

1. Start a session with `open_session` on a page with a list. A Shift-click in the list extends the selection.
2. Do a tap on row 1: `call` `{ "tool": "tap", "args": { "id": "<row 1>" } }`.
3. Try to do a Shift-click on row 3.

Result: `tap` has no argument for a modifier. `press` with `Shift` releases the key before the tap. The tap after it is a click without a modifier.

Versions: e2e 0.17.0, web engine (Playwright), macOS. I also examined 0.18.0. Its MCP `tap` schema does not have `modifiers`.

### Proposed API

```ts
// The test API already has this. The MCP call could have the same argument:
{ tool: 'tap', args: { id: 'n42', modifiers: ['Shift'] } }
```

### Which surface

_No response_

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: MCP server: `upload` cannot attach files to a hidden file input
body:
### Problem

The `upload` tool of the MCP server must have a node id from `observe`. `observe` does not show a hidden `<input type="file">`. Many pages have a visible button that opens a hidden file input. On these pages, the agent can only select the button. Then `upload` on the button gives the error `Node is not an HTMLInputElement`.

We have a web app. The app imports a template from a JSON file. The page shows an "Import template" button. The button calls `.click()` on a hidden `<input type="file" accept=".json">`. Agents use the MCP server to examine this feature. The agents cannot attach a file.

To see the problem:

1. Make a page with a `<button>` that clicks a hidden `<input type="file">`.
2. Put `display: none` or the `hidden` attribute on the input.
3. Start a session with `open_session`.
4. Call `observe`.

   Result: The list shows the button. The list does not show the input.

5. Call `upload` on the button: `call` `{ "tool": "upload", "args": { "id": "<button id>", "files": ["fixtures/template.json"] } }`.

   Result: `Node is not an HTMLInputElement`.

Versions: e2e 0.17.0, web engine (Playwright), macOS. I also examined 0.18.0. Its MCP `upload` documentation did not change.

### Proposed API

```ts
// `upload` on the button that opens the file chooser, as Playwright's `filechooser` event does:
{ tool: 'upload', args: { id: '<button id>', files: ['fixtures/template.json'] } }
```

### Which surface

_No response_

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: fix(mobile): preserve control identity across observations
body: ## Summary - Fixes #951. Unchanged mobile controls keep their projected IDs after keypad presses. Each observation refreshes their native refs. - Match controls within app, screen, parent and row context. Changed labels, recycled rows, reused identifiers and ambiguous siblings cannot inherit another control's ID. - Add `EngineSnapshot.nodeIdentity: 'stable'` so the runner recovers a stale native frame through the same ID. If that ID disappeared, it rejects the action. Web declares its existing stable element identity too. - Add a keypad benchmark with deterministic and agent flows, regression coverage, documentation and changesets. ```text observe reconcile uniquely matched controls within their context retain their IDs and refresh capture-pinned native refs action resolve the current binding on a stale capture, observe again and resolve the same ID reject a missing ID ``` ## Evidence - Before: pressing a keypad key replaced the IDs of unchanged controls. Reused row and screen identifiers could also retain an unrelated target. - After: regression tests retain unchanged controls and reject recycled rows, screen replacements, renamed controls and duplicate matches. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI against the mobile benchmark: `e2e run tests/keypad.e2e.ts --target ios-simulator` and `--target android-emulator`, two tests passed on each platform, including decimal entry and deletion. - Android strict replay also passed with no model calls. Its re-recorded video uses the emulator native resolution to avoid cropping. - Fresh agent keypad runs with GPT-6.1-Sol passed on iOS and Android with five model calls each. Both saved `750 USD`; local videos capture both runs. GitHub CLI media upload requires upstream write access, which this account lacks. The browser is signed out, so media is not attached yet. Android also has an earlier passing Luna replay recording. - Fresh GPT-6-Luna retries failed on both platforms, entering `777` on iOS and saving `7107` on Android. The iOS trace retained the same button IDs and shows the model tapping `7` again after the first digit. These failures remain recorded locally; the successful videos use GPT-6.1-Sol. - The focused mobile engine suite passed 105 tests; the full mobile suite passed 253 tests. The new core integration tests cover same-ID stale recovery and refusal to bind a removed ID to a replacement control. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Unchanged controls receive new IDs after another observation. | Uniquely matched controls retain IDs with current native bindings. | | Descriptor recovery can bind an old target to a replacement with the same label. | Stable sources require the retained ID; a missing ID fails before dispatch. | ### Remaining before ready for review - Investigate the remaining Luna failures. Successful iOS and Android agent runs do not establish Luna reliability. Media upload remains pending. - Verify replay recordings and update keypad/home snapshot fixtures. - Run final repository checks and a fresh review of the expanded changes. Temporary local device pins, Metro arguments and model settings are excluded from this draft. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way No persisted data migration. The optional engine declaration preserves descriptor recovery for engines that do not opt in. **Blast Radius:** actions Mobile reconciliation and runner stale-target recovery change. Conservative matching can report a stale target when a control's identity evidence changes. The engine declaration raises the mobile and web peer floor to e2e 0.19.0.

title: feat(agent): hold modifier keys on tap, double tap, and right click
body:
The agent's `tap`, `double_tap`, and `right_click` tools take an optional `modifiers` list when the target's engine declares `tapModifiers`, in both `agent.act` and the MCP server. An agent can now Shift-click or Ctrl-click the way the test API's `tap({ modifiers })` can since #626.

```ts
{ tool: 'tap', args: { target: 'n42', modifiers: ['Shift'] } }
```

- `ctx.target.tapModifiers` tells executors whether the target can hold keys for a click. The grammar tools read it, so `agent.act`, MCP, and custom executors use the same flag. Engines without it get the same schema as before.
- `ctx.actions.tap`, `doubleTap`, and `secondaryTap` take `{ modifiers }`. Bad values fail with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. An engine that doesn't declare `tapModifiers` refuses them with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.
- Held keys are recorded with the action (`tap button "Save" with Shift held`) and replayed from the cache. The trace reader rejects an entry whose `modifiers` are malformed or sit on a verb that can't hold them.
- Docs: `reference/agent.mdx`, `executors.mdx`, `reference/mcp.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`. Changeset: `e2e` patch.

Closes #953

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on the testbed `/controls` page with a temporary click-log button that records `event.shiftKey` and the other modifier flags.

MCP, built server, driven with an MCP client:

```text
>> tap {"target":"n6062","modifiers":["Shift"]}            Tapped #n6062.
>> tap {"target":"n6062"}                                  Tapped #n6062.
>> double_tap {"target":"n6062","modifiers":["Alt"]}       Double-tapped #n6062.
>> right_click {"target":"n6062","modifiers":["ControlOrMeta"]}  Right-clicked #n6062.
>> tap {"target":"n6062","modifiers":["Bogus"]}   INVALID_ARGUMENT: call tap: modifiers.0: Invalid option ...
>> hover {"target":"n6062","modifiers":["Shift"]} INVALID_ARGUMENT: call hover: Unrecognized key: "modifiers"
status "Click log" text="click[shiftKey] click[] click[altKey] click[altKey] dblclick[altKey] contextmenu[metaKey]"
```

`agent.act('click the "Click log target" button once while holding Shift')` with `toHaveText('click[shiftKey]')`, live and then from the cache:

```text
✓ the agent shift-clicks 5.52s ai 9.6k tokens · 2 model calls   Cache 1 missed
✓ the agent shift-clicks 331ms                                  Cache 1 replayed
```

The recorded entry: `{ "name": "tap", "summary": "tap button \"Click log target\" with Shift held", "modifiers": ["Shift"] }`.

Unit: `agent-tap-modifiers.test.ts` (7 tests, including trace rejection), full e2e unit suite 2663 passed, decision 157 passed. `pnpm typecheck` and `oxlint` are clean.

title: fix(web): support upload buttons that open file choosers
body:
## What and why

- `upload` (agent, MCP) and `setInputFiles` failed on a visible upload button over a hidden file input: `locator.setInputFiles: Error: Node is not an HTMLInputElement`.
- `uploadFiles` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`): a file input, or a label for one, still takes the files directly (no click). Anything else is clicked with the `filechooser` wait already attached, and `FileChooser.setFiles` sets the files. No chooser is `NOT_ACTIONABLE` ("opened no file chooser"), surfaced as `ACTION_FAILED`.
- One element resolve and one deadline cover the check, click, chooser wait, and `setFiles`. A failed click leaves no unhandled rejection (would crash `e2e mcp`). A cancelled operation sets no files, even if the chooser opens after the cancel.
- The agent `upload` tool description (`packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts`) and the `setInputFiles` jsdoc name the chooser button too. Changeset: `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` patch.

```ts
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Choose avatar').setInputFiles('fixtures/attachment.txt');
```

## Issue

Closes #954

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `packages/web/tests/integration/upload-actions.test.ts`, real Chromium, locator and element handle: file input, `<label for>` over a hidden input (zero clicks), button over a hidden input, button that opens nothing.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| button over hidden input: `locator.setInputFiles: Error: Node is not an HTMLInputElement` | `Tests 8 passed (8)` |

- Each new test fails without its fix: label lookup removed -> both label cases fail; signal checks removed -> the cancel unit test fails.
- Testbed `/controls` with the built CLI (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/controls.e2e.ts`): `Tests 18 passed (18)`, including "a button that opens a hidden file input takes the files" and "a button that opens no file chooser fails as ACTION_FAILED".

title: fix(cache): skip live values when keying a control's container
body:
## What and why - A recorded control carries `within`, the first leaf text of its nearest row, list item, or region, so replay can tell twins apart (`containerKey`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/actions.ts`). When that text is a live value, the key changes with it: `

Count: 0

` records `within "0"`, and replay misses as soon as the count reads anything else. - `containerKey` now skips live values: nodes with role `status` (``), `timer`, `marquee`, `log`, `progressbar`, or `meter`, with their subtrees. A container whose only leaf text is such a value gets no key. It does not fall back to its own label, because a list item's label is its content, value included. - Some twins differ only by a value, like `

  • Qty: 2

    • ` rows. When the key without live values still leaves such twins, `describePlacement` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts`) records the key main recorded, value included. Those rows behave exactly as on main: a reorder finds the right row, and a count no row reads misses. A position alone would tap the wrong row after a reorder. - Replay accepts a candidate whose key, read either way, equals the recorded `within`, so entries recorded on main replay as before. The key is checked only on candidates that already match role and name, which also makes matching cheaper than on main for large trees. - No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump: no committed recording changes key (mobile captures and web-benchmark pages checked), and old entries still match. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["containerKey: first leaf text, live values skipped"] --> B{"twins left?"} B -- no --> C["within = that key, or none"] B -- yes --> D["within = key with live values, as on main"] ``` Trade-offs, each measured below: - A single control whose only context is a live value now relocates by name. If its row is replaced by a different row with the same control, replay taps it and the end check hands off. An added twin row makes it ambiguous, with no tap. - An identity placed inside a live role (`

    Bob commented

    `) is skipped, so the next text keys the row and may be volatile. - The counter's own `Increment` step now relocates but still hands off: its recorded end anchor reads `Count: 1`. That is the end check, not this key. A control next to a count (`Items: 2` + Checkout) replays fully. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Real CLI and model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`) on scratch testbed pages: record, flip the page state on the server, then replay with `--strict-cache`. The server logs which row each click hit. | Scenario | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `Items: N` + Checkout, 2 to 5 | missed, `in "2"` | replayed | | `Expires in ` + Extend, 4:59 to 3:12 | missed, `in "4:59"` | replayed | | `Q x Pears` + Remove, qty change and swap | removed Apples (wrong row) | replayed, removed Pears | | `Pears 5` + icon Remove, 5 to 6 | missed, `in "5"` | replayed | | `Order #1043` + Cancel, rows reordered | replayed | replayed | | twins told apart only by a count: swapped / new count | replayed / missed | replayed / missed | ```text main Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8) Cache 4 replayed · 1 handed off · 3 missed this branch Tests 8 passed (8) Cache 8 replayed ``` - Mobile benchmark, Android agentic suite with `--strict-cache` on an emulator: 20/20, 15 replayed, 2 handed off, 3 missed, the same cache mode per test as main. The previous head of this PR failed Bottom Tabs with `REPLAY_STALE`. - Web benchmark agentic suite with `--strict-cache`: 33/33, 26 replayed, 2 handed off, 4 missed, the same per step as main. - Golden iOS and Android captures (1282 nodes): placement identical to main. The 43 committed Android `within` entries relocate to the same node. - Real Chromium trees, 87 record/replay cases plus 202 icon-button and stepper variants: never worse than main. In the 87 cases, 8 wrong taps vs 14 on main. - The last commit after these runs only extracts a helper and adds tests, with no behavior change. Unit and replay integration suites rerun on it. - 2026-10-28, merged main e087ed2c4 (import conflict in `action-dispatcher.ts`: main's new pixel-trace handle now uses `describePlacement`): `pnpm check` and the relocate/trace/agent unit + agent-act integration suites (542 tests) pass. With the `src` change reverted, 6 of 12 tests in `relocate-within.test.ts` fail. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`e2e` patch). - [ ] Breaking change: no. - [x] Docs updated: `docs/cache.mdx`, "How a replay works" step 2. - [ ] Contract change: no. - [ ] Engine contract change: no.

title: feat(acp): run agent steps on your own coding agent over ACP
body:
Started by @enekesabel; finished by the maintainers on this branch.

## What and why

- New package `@e2e-dev/acp`: `agent.act` and `agent.assert` run on a coding agent the user already signs in to, over the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com). No model provider or API key for e2e.
- Presets start the adapter from the project's install (never `npx <name>`, since unscoped `codex-acp` on npm is an unrelated package) and turn off the agent's own tools:
  - `acpExecutor.claudeCode({ model })`: Zed's `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` with `tools: []`, no settings sources, strict MCP config, no saved session, no permission bypass.
  - `acpExecutor.codex()`: `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` in read-only mode with shell, web search, apps, plugins, browser, computer use, goals off, and every MCP server from `codex mcp list` disabled for these sessions.
  - `acpExecutor({ command, args })` for any other ACP agent (Cursor's `agent acp`).
- One session per test attempt, and one per member of a serial group; later steps are new messages in the same conversation. Tools are the built-in agent's own: `createGrammarTools` for the target's verbs plus `createVerdictTool` (`complete_step` with `blocked` and its codes), served as one MCP server on 127.0.0.1 (ephemeral port, random path). Every action goes through `ctx.actions`, so steps record and replay like the built-in agent's, and calls batched behind `complete_step` are skipped the way the built-in loop skips them.
- Fail closed (`packages/acp/src/session.ts`, `executor.ts`):
  - a permission request is allowed only when the adapter marks it as a step tool call (`_meta.claudeCode.toolName`, Codex's MCP call marker), or, for other adapters, when its raw input is exactly an MCP call of a step tool; titles never count
  - a tool of the agent's own that runs without asking cancels the turn and fails the step with `POLICY_DENIED` as soon as it is reported started, and the step tools take no action after it. The session closes with it, so the next step starts a fresh agent that never saw what the tool read
  - the agent's process (and `codex mcp list`) gets no `E2E_SECRET_*` / `E2E_USER_*` variables, in any case, from the runner's env or the executor's own; secrets go by name through `type_secret`
- `e2e/agent` now exports `createGrammarTools`, `createVerdictTool`, `BASE_RULES`, `VERDICT_RULES`, `isRuntimeHardStop`, and the `ScreenOutput` type (`.changeset/grammar-tools-export.md`, asserted in `tests/types/sdk-types.ts`, including that the screen presenter and `onActionFailed` stay internal). `@e2e-dev/acp` peers on `e2e >=0.21.4 <1`, the release that ships them.

```ts
import { acpExecutor } from '@e2e-dev/acp';

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' } }],
  agents: { default: { executor: acpExecutor.claudeCode({ model: 'sonnet' }) } },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as e2e runner
  participant X as acpExecutor
  participant A as ACP agent (stdio)
  participant T as step tools (MCP on 127.0.0.1)
  R->>X: runStep(ctx)
  X->>A: initialize, session/new { mcpServers: [T] } (first step only)
  X->>A: session/prompt (step, params, ledger, screen)
  A->>X: request_permission (step tool: allow, anything else: reject)
  A->>T: tap { target: "n7" }
  T->>R: ctx.actions.tap
  T-->>A: "Tapped #n7." + screen changes
  A->>X: tool_call of its own started without asking: cancel, POLICY_DENIED, close session
  A->>T: complete_step { status, summary, errorCode? }
  A-->>X: end_turn (usage, cost)
  X-->>R: verdict, recordModelCall
```

## Known limits

- Secrets the config reads from other variables (`secrets: { apiKey: process.env.API_KEY }`), or the variable an `E2E_SECRET_*` value was copied from, still reach the agent's process. The executor sees secret names only, so stripping by value would need a core API; `docs/acp.mdx` says to keep secrets in the `E2E_` variables.
- The Claude adapter passes the step-tool URL to `claude` as `--mcp-config` on its command line, so another user on the same machine can read it with `ps` and reach the step tools while a test runs. The MCP handler is stateless and a header token would sit on the same command line.
- After `complete_step` the turn runs to its end, so the agent writes its closing reply (one more model round trip) before the verdict returns. Cancelling the turn instead would drop the usage and cost the adapter reports when the turn ends.
- A turn that times out records no model call, and an agent slow to honor a cancel fails the next step instead (`did not stop the turn of a step that already ended`).
- On Windows, a custom `command` must be an executable, not an npm `.cmd` shim (documented).
- No Cursor preset: Cursor isn't installed here, and its MCP permission requests may not carry the fields the check requires, so it ships as `acpExecutor({ command: 'agent', args: ['acp'] })` until someone runs it.
- Codex can still start subagents (`agents.max_threads` must be at least 1); a step where it does fails with `POLICY_DENIED`.
- Adapters resolve from the working directory up; `e2e run --config apps/web/e2e.config.ts` from a monorepo root needs the adapter installed where e2e runs (the runner does not pass the config directory to executors).
- `@e2e-dev/acp` is a new npm package: publish its first version by hand and connect trusted publishing before this changeset releases.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `packages/acp/tests/cli.test.ts`: built CLI on real Chromium with a scripted ACP agent process; act + assert pass, `type_secret` fills by name and the value appears in no prompt, tool result, or artifact, and a second run replays both acts from the cache.
- `packages/acp/tests/executor.test.ts`, `presets.test.ts` (38 tests). Each test for the behaviors below fails on the code before its fix: a serial group's second member gets its own session, a `tap` batched with `complete_step` is skipped, an own tool fails the step when it starts, an allowed step-tool call is not flagged as the agent's own once it completes, no prompt goes out for a step that ended while its screen was read, the session closes after an own tool (also one run in the tail of an ended step), and secret variables are stripped in any case and from `codex mcp list`.
- Live, `node packages/acp/tests/live/acp.ts` on Linux against the built packages at this head (record, then replay): a todo act + assert, an assertion that must fail, a secret login, and a step that asks the agent to list its tools.

| Agent | Record | Replay | Agent's own tool calls | Secret in artifacts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code (`claude-agent-acp` 0.97.0, `sonnet`) | 4/4 as expected, `wrong assertion` fails `ASSERTION_FAILED` | acts from cache, 0 model calls, 0.2 to 0.3 s | none | no |
| Codex (`codex-acp` 2.1.1, `gpt-6.1-sol`), macOS, before the takeover; not re-run at this head, the local OpenAI account is over quota | 4/4 as expected, steps 6 to 13 s | acts from cache, 0 model calls, 0.2 s | none | no |

- Serial group, live on Claude Code: a scratch project with `test.describe('todo flow', { serial: true })` whose second test adds a todo on the page the first left.

| Before the per-member session | This branch |
| --- | --- |
| second test fails: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: The ACP agent session failed: ACP connection closed` | both pass live (1 model call each, $0.03), then replay from the cache in 1.05 s |

- Containment, asking each preset's agent to list and then try its own tools (macOS run before the takeover): Claude Code lists only `mcp__e2e_step__*`. Codex has no shell (`exec_command` is not a function), no web search, and its code-mode `exec` cannot `require`; a subagent spawn trips the own-tool check.

---

title: feat(decision): full action grammar, none fallback, and vision through the OpenAI Decisions API
body:
- **Goal-framed questions.** Every question now states the goal, the app context, and the recent actions in its own instructions, with prose criteria (`[24] menuitem "Rename"`). On the captured failing states this alone flipped the hover target from the card to "Card actions" (P 0 to 0.96) and the right-click follow-through (tap P 0.18 to 0.54, Rename 0.96). The assertion question uses the runner's own judgment wording, which fixes the contradicted-total assert (fails 0.04 to 0.89) without moving the four holds.
- **Operation first, target second.** The target question follows the operation in its own request, as OpenAI's guide asks for dependent decisions. No fan-out question is left to refuse, and every call carries one target list instead of six. Every target question still carries `none`.
- **The whole action grammar.** `hover`, `secondary_tap`, `double_tap`, `long_press`, `drag` (with a destination question), `scroll_to`, and `upload` (paths from the text model, authorized by the runner). Pointer verbs reach labeled nodes that are no control.
- **Vision.** `decisionExecutor({ vision: true })` asks for masked pixels; assertions and completion checks see the screenshot, the tree questions do not (a screenshot beside the element table was measured to hurt). `tap_at` for a drawn control: the text model names what to tap next ("the 3 key on the keypad") from the goal and the taps so far, then two pairs of score questions (column, row) locate it on the plain screenshot and again on a 2x zoomed 400px crop with a grid drawn on it; the weighted means land inside the key. A tap that changed the pixels under it is remembered for that control. The fingerprint hashes pixels under vision, so a canvas-only change counts as progress. The screenshot goes as a file part of the decision state (`ai` 7.0.134), which `openai.decisionModel('gpt-6-luna')` sends as `input_image` (`@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.90); no model copy in this package.
- **Verdicts read what the page reports.** Live regions (status, alert, log) reach the assertion and completion questions as quoted data, and the completion check quotes the path; both were measured to turn "inconclusive" into "holds" against the runner's small screenshot. Action lines name the node by role and quoted label (`check checkbox "Agree to terms"`, no node id) and the completion check carries them in its question only: on the captured checked-checkbox verdict that is holds 0.17 to 0.83 on luna text-only and 0.72 to 0.97 on Jev, with no loss over 541 captured operation and completion requests replayed on both models.
- **Shape of the package** after a strict quality review: `Target` is data and `dispatch.ts` is the only caller of the runner's actions, with `Action` discriminated on its operation. The step is a class with a budget, a view, a `pick`/`gate` pair, and a per-operation `prepare`. The two-look locator and its landed memo live in `locator.ts`; the grid is one value in `overlay.ts`, drawn as lines only after number plates measured worse on the zoomed crop (9 key: 31px to 4px). `text.ts` asks once with three specs. One FNV hash.
- **Runner:** a `StepExecutor` declaring `vision: true` receives `agent.assert(..., { vision })` as `ctx.step.vision`, validated like the built-in path, with `visionOnly` reported. Refusals name the question; decide and text calls retry transport failures.

```ts
import { decisionExecutor } from '@e2e-dev/decision';
import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai';

const executor = decisionExecutor({
  model: openai.decisionModel('gpt-6-luna'),
  textModel: openai('gpt-5.4-mini'),
  vision: true,
});
```

## Docs

`docs/decision-models.mdx` went through the authoring-docs pass: fast path first, the OpenAI setup folded into an accordion, one fact per place, 1150 to 987 prose words. Cut on purpose: how the two `tap_at` looks and the landed-point memo work (internals), the measured playground results (the PR body has them), and the note that a screenshot beside the tree questions measured worse (design detail). Added one gotcha: keep `vision` off behind the AI Gateway, which rejects the file part. README, the `skills/e2e` agent reference, and the changeset got the same trim.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI with the built `decision`, `web`, and `e2e` packages symlinked into a scratch project, real `OPENAI_API_KEY`, the testbed playground app, the config above: the whole `apps/testbed/tests-agent` suite (28 tests), `--workers 2 --video on`, cache cleared, twice on the final build with the same result.

| Suite state | passed | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before this PR (fan-out refusals) | 8 / 28 | 12 steps died on turn one with a refusal |
| grammar + `none` fallback | 17 / 28 | |
| this PR | 25 / 28 | 2m 21s, 279 model calls, 379k input tokens, about $0.04; three runs on the final build |
| this PR on the SDK model (no copy) | 25 / 28 | 3m 10s, 319 model calls, 424k tokens, same three failures |
| luna text-only through the AI Gateway (`openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions`) | 20 / 28 | 41s, 113 calls; the 8 pixel tests fail by design, the gateway rejects file parts until vercel/ai #22286 |

- Passing now: all 9 judgment tests, all 8 verb tests (hover, right-click, long press and double tap, drag, check, upload, scroll_to, back), both todo flows, wizard, secret login, the red pin on a canvas, the five- and ten-digit codes on a drawn keypad, the vision assert on a drawn chart. Videos of the keypad, the red pin, and the hover attached.
- Still failing, three: the two drawn wizards and the drawn form read their instruction only from pixels, which the text model that names the next control cannot see, and the form needs typing at a point (`type_at`, not offered). Both are listed under Limits in the docs page.
- Every framing change was measured offline first against the captured failing requests (`/tmp/decision-live/eval.mts` style replays against the Decisions API), then confirmed live; sequential asking was also tried on the hover, right-click, and back states and did not move the probabilities, so the two-request split is for refusals and token cost, not accuracy.
- 139 decision unit tests including the real `@ai-sdk/openai` adapter over a scripted `/decisions` endpoint, with the screenshot arriving as `input_image` beside the JSON state; the built-CLI test with real Chromium; e2e unit tests; `pnpm check`.

title: Expose a public programmatic list or collect API
body:
Could e2e expose a supported programmatic `list` or `collect` entry point?

We use e2e 0.18.0 to test which setup sessions and test cases a config, positional file selection, and exact title grep select. The public CLI is useful as a parity check, but spawning it for every unit case repeats config loading and collection.

The current in-process alternative imports private `dist/collect/{collect,registry,select}.js`, `dist/config/resolve.js`, and `dist/internal/globs.js`. Those paths are outside the package exports and can change on upgrade.

A public function accepting a project root, config, positional files, and grep patterns would let consumers inspect selected test metadata without starting an engine or app. We need each selected case's file, title, target, kind, setup session, and selection disposition, plus unmatched positional files. A structured result matching `e2e list` would also work.

Is an existing supported API intended for this use? If none exists, would you accept a public collection API?

title: fix(agent): classify a content-filter refusal as MODEL_REFUSED
body: ## What and why - A model call that finishes with unified reason `content-filter` and no text was reported as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (`model provider failed: No output generated.`), category infrastructure, exit 3. `generateText` still returns that result, and reading `output` throws `NoOutputGeneratedError`, which drops the finish reason (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts`). - The adapter checks the finish reason before reading structured output or parsing text. Unified `content-filter`, or a raw token of `content-filter`, `content_filter`, or `refusal`, raises `MODEL_REFUSED` (category test, exit 1, blocked category automation). The message names the step, the model, and the raw token when the result still carries one. - `agent.extract` does not enter its repair round for that error (`packages/e2e/src/agent/invocation.ts` continues only on `ModelOutputInvalidError`). `agent.act` classifies the same finish reason before the tool-choice and context-overflow retries (`packages/e2e/src/agent/tool-loop.ts`). On `act`, the AI SDK `ToolChoiceViolationError` keeps only the unified reason, so the message quotes `content-filter`. - Empty output with finish reason `stop` stays `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`. A refusal is not model-unreachable, so the failed step counts as a failure of the flow recording (`packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`). - The runner reruns test-category failures when `retries` is greater than 0, and it does not rerun infrastructure failures (`packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts`). The refused call itself is one `doGenerate`: no transport retry and no repair round. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Command: `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/agent-model-refusal.test.ts` - On this diff (`c8a70517afbcb5b7b52b71e53ed6c9b07eddd4beb8cce58e78cf28228c7d5aae`, base `34b90ae647cf7989793c858e37e22ffb63594dc0`): 5 passed. - With the fix files restored to that base: 4 failed, 1 passed. The test file imported and ran. The failures were the old error codes. | main (`34b90ae`) | this branch | | --- | --- | | Structured extract and `agent.extract`: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, infrastructure, `model provider failed: No output generated.` | `MODEL_REFUSED`, category test, one model call, `agent.extract: the model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 refused the request (refusal)` | | Text call, raw reason `content_filter`: `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` | `MODEL_REFUSED`, one call, message quotes `content_filter` | | `agent.act`: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (`Model response did not contain a tool call even though tool choice was required.`) | `MODEL_REFUSED`, one call, message quotes `content-filter` | | Finish reason `stop` and empty output | `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` on both | ## Limitations - No live provider call. The finish reason is scripted in `doGenerate`. - `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`, and `scripts/check-error-codes.ts` were not run. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts` was updated and was not part of the command above. - `retries` greater than 0 still reruns a test-category failure. Explore pins `retries` at 0. A refused planner call leaves the explore loop, as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` already did: `PLANNER_SHORTCOMINGS` is `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` and `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. `MODEL_REFUSED` is a new `AgentErrorCode`. The report schema already types `code` as a string, and `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` does not pin that union. `dist/` is produced by the build. AI-assisted development: an AI coding agent wrote this patch, and an independent AI review checked the diff, the new test, and the recorded vitest results. AI-assisted development and review; submitted by Ryan Vo. Validated against upstream commit `34b90ae647cf7989793c858e37e22ffb63594dc0`. Refs #945.

title: feat(tern): native semantic engine with explicit session ownership
body: ## Summary - Add the native Tern engine with explicit provider/lease ownership and fresh AX/tree/control semantics. - Keep borrowed sessions observation-scoped and prohibit silent native-error fallback, ambiguous locator actions, secure-value disclosure, and unsafe action replay. - Require phase-off/null-error native gates with either nonapplicability or applicable signed-in native0.6.1 beta state, and the exact single leased/focused window before/after observation, capture and mutation. Unknown/active gates fail closed. Preserve read-only timeout/cancellation semantics and nonretryable dispatched uncertainty. - Supply the real inert SDK testbed, unit regressions and portable public documentation. No workstation profile, private executable, credentials or host captures are included. ## Dependency and review scope First logical slice. GitHub base: `main` in `tester-army/e2e`; head comes from the corresponding `kvnloo/e2e` feature branch. Later Sway and Hyprland slices depend on this implementation through ordinary merges, not rewritten history. ## Verification - Native Tern build/typecheck and all 16 corrected gate regressions passed. title: feat(hyprland): owned-output containment for native keyboard and pointer
body:
## Summary

- Contain each private Sway/Tern attempt on an exact owned Hyprland output, tag and new unprotected visible workspace, with mapped geometry, PID/start/ancestry and no-focus readback.
- Measure declared human output/layout/focus/cursor boundaries before and after operations; refuse foreign clients, changed geometry, protected workspaces or changed process generations without restoring operator state.
- Keep all guest-visible Tern command execution in the owned guest. Pin namespace/root descriptors and recheck pidfd/generation; never use numeric-only namespace entry, a PID namespace or host/KMS fallback. Supervisors and cleanup journals remain outside every guest bind.
- Remap only the exact outer Wayland endpoint into guest runtime; expose host-generated Sway configuration read-only and publish staged profiles/roots under private closing fences. Save ownership before publication; cleanup atomically claims exact inodes into same-filesystem private quarantine and preserves public replacements, collisions and mismatching claims.
- Recover pending/missing guest receipts through the fully contained mapped tagged generation, or prove never-launched under the closed host-private dispatch fence with no potential-dispatch receipt. Preserve uncertain dispatch and refuse old unfenced versions. Cleanup independently finds the recorded PID across all clients regardless of tag; live retagged/moved clients or missing mapped metadata refuse before stops. Exact PID/tag/rectangle/visibility/output/workspace/ancestry remains required; exited cleanup requires independently absent generation and no matching client.
- Add the real disposable render-only fixture: actual Node/app namespaces/root, read-only config and host-sentinel checks, inert human caret/value/focus, chord/pointer/count, PNG, parallel public CLI and interruption recovery. The missing-receipt test reconstructs a durable pending checkpoint on actual mapped processes; it does not claim worker death was caught at that exact instruction.

## Dependency and review scope

Depends on [Sway PR #976](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/976) and [Tern PR #974](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/974). GitHub base is `main` until dependencies merge. Review the [own-slice comparison](https://github.com/kvnloo/e2e/compare/feat/sway-isolated-seat...feat/hyprland-owned-output); that logical comparison is not the GitHub base. All prerequisite integration uses ordinary merges.

## Verification

- Full-stack Hyprland build/typecheck passed. All 23 lifecycle regressions and the other two package tests passed after removing an incidental error-message assertion in favor of the nonretryable `INVALID_STATE` contract.
- Independent recorded-PID/full-containment/private-claim source review passed before later mechanical typing/test-only changes.
- Full-stack documentation checks, peer ranges, install-script audit, script typecheck and packed-install checks passed.
- The real C helper passed 10 authority tests plus owned-process supervision/stop, live descriptor-pinned rootless namespace entry, and an actual pidfd-unavailable timeout/kill/reap smoke with no late effect. These do not prove the nested native app or protected-human boundary fixture.

**Draft / native boundary acceptance blocked.** Isolated native Tern clients currently display the signed-out gate. Full actual guest `/proc`/Node/Tern routing, rendered values, human caret/value/focus preservation, same-client chords/pointer, parallel CLI, SIGKILL/SIGTERM/SIGINT recovery and exact output cleanup remain unproven. Rootless namespaces work on the validation host; the pending prerequisite is not a missing-user-license claim.

Required CI remains fail-closed on missing permitted source-pinned runtimes/render device and active/unknown native gates. No accounts, authentication, permission changes, host profiles, private executables or workstation captures are part of this contribution. Keep this PR Draft until exact-head native acceptance and review are complete.

title: feat(expect): toHaveScreenshot visual comparison on web, iOS, and Android
body: Playwright's `toHaveScreenshot`, on every engine that captures pixels. One test compares a browser, an iOS simulator, and an Android emulator. ```ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('checkout looks right', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/checkout'); await expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot('checkout.png'); await expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' })).toHaveScreenshot(); await expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot('feed.png', { mask: [screen.getByTestId('time')], maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01 }); }); ``` ## How it works - Pixels come from the engine's existing `observe({ pixels: true })`, so engines implement nothing new. A new optional `EngineObserveOptions.comparable` hint lets an engine hold system chrome fixed; the mobile engine maps it to agent-device's `normalizeStatusBar`. - Screenshots are stored beside the test file at `-snapshots/--.png` and committed. Options are Playwright's: `threshold`, `maxDiffPixels`, `maxDiffPixelRatio`, `mask`, `maskColor`, `timeout`. - Images are resampled to one pixel per viewport pixel, cropped to a locator's box (scrolled into view once), then masked. - A missing screenshot is taken once the screen holds still (two captures in a row the same within the tolerance), written, and the test fails. `-u` / `--update-snapshots` writes missing and different ones and passes. - Without `--update-snapshots`, a CI run never writes into the project. A missing screenshot is attached to the test's results at `snapshots/`, ready to download and commit. - No comparison, `.not` included, passes against a file the same run wrote. Marker files under `/results/` cover retries, repeats, and other workers; the runner clears that directory every run. - A mismatch attaches `-expected`, `-actual`, and `-diff` to the step. The trace page now lists the screenshots each step attached (`packages/e2e/src/report/failure-text.ts`). - Security: denied after a secret fill (`POLICY_DENIED`, same as `app.screenshot()`), and refused unless masking of every secure node is proven. The proof is one shared predicate, `pixelsProvenMasked` in `packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts`, now also used by the agent. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[capture: observe pixels, scale, crop, mask] --> B{stored file?} B -- yes --> C{matches?} C -- yes --> P[pass] C -- no, until timeout --> F[fail: expected, actual, diff] B -- no, or -u --> D{two captures alike?} D -- yes, -u --> W[write, pass] D -- yes, missing, local --> X[write, fail] D -- yes, missing, CI --> Y[attach under project path, fail] D -- never --> U[fail: last two and their diff] ``` Code: `packages/e2e/src/expect/screenshot.ts` (the matcher), `screenshot-capture.ts`, `screenshot-call.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/internal/image.ts` (PNG decode and encode with fast-png, resample, crop, pixelmatch), `packages/e2e/src/run/screenshots.ts`. ## Web engine fix found on the way `locate` reported a node inside an iframe in the frame's own coordinates; the contract and the observation tree use the top-level viewport. A cropped frame locator came out blank, and `tap({ position })` in a frame was off too. Observation shifted by the frame's border box, which put a bordered frame's children off by the border width. Both paths now shift and clip by the frame's content box (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`, `packages/web/src/observation.ts`), checked against Playwright's own `boundingBox()` through a bordered, padded frame in `nested-frames.test.ts` and `visibility.test.ts`. ## Testbed `/swatches` draws solid blocks with no text, so one PNG renders the same on macOS and Linux: `tests/visual.e2e.ts` commits each as `-darwin` and `-linux` and covers a mask, a block below the fold, a block in a frame, and `.not`. ## Not done - The `` suffix is the runner's OS. A hosted browser or device (Kernel, EAS) renders elsewhere, so one suite run from macOS and from Linux CI keeps two files of identical pixels. Fixing it needs either a render platform the engine declares or a path option. - On iOS, agent-device applies the status bar override per capture: override, capture, clear. Each clear replays the charging animation in the battery and Dynamic Island. Comparing two captures in a row within the threshold, then retrying until one matches, absorbs it. The root fix is an override in agent-device that stays on for the whole session. - The subject and mask boxes come from engine calls made separately from the one that takes the pixels. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Web (testbed, the built CLI): first run writes and fails, next run passes. A changed page fails with the diff below. `-u` rewrites and passes. With `CI=1` and retries on, both attempts fail, nothing is written into the project, and the screenshot is in the results at `snapshots/tests/...`. `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` passes with the new swatch suite. ```text FAIL |web| tests/vr-tmp.e2e.ts > todos page ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveScreenshot failed 1824 pixels (0.2% of the image) differ from tests/vr-tmp.e2e.ts-snapshots/todos-web-darwin.png; run with --update-snapshots to keep this run's ``` ![web diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28ee8481-339b-4f37-ba4e-f93014bde12d) - iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5) and Android emulator (Pixel 7, API 36) on the mobile benchmark: the same test file writes with `-u`, then passes on the next run, full screen and a locator. The status bar is held fixed (9:41 on iOS, demo mode on Android). The password field is masked by the engine in both. | iOS | Android | | --- | --- | | ![ios](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27b7f805-303a-4a9a-8b9f-b8f20fd2911b) | ![android](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca263039-0424-41c0-b07d-9de42f56e491) | - Android capture cost measured: 1.3 s per capture with or without `normalizeStatusBar`, with identical images, because agent-device's default capture already holds the Android status bar fixed.

title: feat(runner): expose list() on the e2e/runner subpath
body:
## What and why

A new `e2e/runner` subpath exports `list`, `ConfigurationError`, and `isE2EError`, so the runner graph stays off the root entry test files import. `list` takes `config` as a path or an `E2EConfig` and `targets` as target names, collects through the existing loader, and returns every test-target-agent pair in selection order, filtered pairs included, plus unmatched positionals and the selected target names. Each pair carries the report id for repeat 0, project-relative `source`, consumed `session`, produced `sessions`, `serialId`, `agent`, and `disposition` of `run`, `skip`, or `filtered`, with `reason` when the pair does not run. `e2e list` calls that same function and still prints only `run` and `skip` pairs; its JSON reporter names the skip field `reason` and adds the identity fields, and the runner docs, type assertions, CLI and lifecycle tests, and a minor changeset follow that contract.

Callers that need the tests and setup sessions a config, positional files, and a title grep would select have no supported in-process entry point. Spawning `e2e list` reloads config and recollects files on every call, and its output leaves out pairs a filter removed, positional arguments that matched no file, and most of the identity a report stores for each pair. The only in-process route is modules the package does not export.

Fixes #970

## Verified

Run locally on the merged branch (b3cdd21):

- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm -r run typecheck`, `pnpm run docs:check`, `pnpm run docs:check-errors`: clean.
- `pnpm run check:dead-code`: no new findings (the duplicate `SourceLocation` export is gone).
- `packages/e2e` unit tests: 2523 passed. `runner-lifecycle`, `dist-public-exports`, `cli-guide` integration: 45 passed.
- The new integration case covers `config` as a path, a non-empty `unmatched`, and a second `list()` seeing an edited file; it fails when `unmatched` is not returned.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

A finding is a bug only once `tests/bugbash/.e2e.ts` fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED`. - `references/example/verify-playground/` is the skill the generator produced and ran for `apps/testbed`, with todos, forms, and login mapped. AGENTS.md says to regenerate it when a playground route or label it names changes. - Installed with `npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill create-verification-skill`; not shipped in the npm package and not read by `e2e guide`. Fixed from that review: an API-only target cannot carry `app`, `reuseExisting` lives inside `command`, `.e2e/results/` is cleared by the next run so durable proofs use `--output .e2e/proof/`, re-seeding of an existing map was promised but not instructed, charters were not in the fan-out format, and the example misnamed several playground labels. Nothing dismissed. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the generated skill's own section 4 in `apps/testbed` against the built packages. - Doctor: `e2e list tests/smoke.e2e.ts` printed four pairs; `e2e run tests/smoke.e2e.ts` passed (3 passed, 1 skipped), exit 0. - Drive: `e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts --trace on`, 7 passed, a trace page per test. - Bug bash: one todos charter over `e2e explore --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts --agent skeptic --max-steps 3 --video --output .e2e/bugbash/todos` on a ChatGPT login (`chatgpt('gpt-6-luna')`). One step, 10 actions, no findings, video written under the attempt. - Cleanup removed `.e2e/bugbash/` and the untracked config; the todos trace pages survived. - Port-in-use behaviour tested by hand: a run against a `pnpm app` already on 4271 stops with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`, which is what the example says. - `npx skills add . --list` on the worktree lists `create-verification-skill` and `e2e`, nothing else. ``` ✓ |web| Exploring Starting at /todos, add, complete, filter, and delete todos; check the remaining count and every filter tab against the list ✓ 1 Todo list flow 18.80s · 10 actions ended: the agent covered the goal Findings none Steps 1 of 3 · 1 passed · the agent covered the goal AI 78.0k tokens · 23% cached · 13 model calls · chatgpt.responses/gpt-6-luna Duration 26.61s (startup 89ms) ```

title: feat(lightpanda): add @e2e-dev/lightpanda, a browser provider for the Lightpanda headless browser
body: ## What and why - New package `@e2e-dev/lightpanda`: `lightpanda()` is a `BrowserProvider` for the web engine that starts one `lightpanda serve` per worker slot on a free loopback port and stops its process group when the run ends. No vendor SDK; the binary is the dependency. - [Lightpanda](https://lightpanda.io) is an open-source headless browser without Chromium: instant start, a fraction of Chrome's memory, and CDP, so the engine attaches to it the way it attaches to Kernel. - Binary discovery: `binary`, `LIGHTPANDA_PATH`, then `lightpanda` on `PATH`, `~/.lightpanda/lightpanda`, `~/.local/bin/lightpanda` (the places agent-browser looks). None found fails the lease before any test, naming the install page. - A server already running (the Docker image in CI) is a `web({ connect })` target, so the provider has one lease shape and no attach mode. - Worker scope only: Lightpanda exposes no default context identity, so a per-attempt lease fails with `CDP recovery failed: the default context identity is unavailable`. The option is not offered. - Docs page `docs/integrations/lightpanda.mdx` with setup, options, and a table of what Lightpanda cannot do yet (sessions, dialogs, downloads, iframes, drags, resize, scrolling) and why, each verified against the nightly. title: test(web): cross-check every sectioning scope around shadow landmarks
body:
The shadow landmark fixture from #943 pins the scoping for two of the ten shapes `isPageLevel` scopes a header or footer to. A regression in one of the other eight would have passed the cross-check, because no other fixture nests a landmark in a shadow root under those ancestors. This expands the fixture so every shape the scoping rule reads is exercised on every `pnpm test` run. `isPageLevel` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:134`) scopes an implicit `banner` or `contentinfo` through `SECTIONING_SCOPE` (`read-semantics.ts:123`): the `article`, `aside`, `main`, `nav`, and `section` elements, plus the `article`, `complementary`, `main`, `navigation`, and `region` roles. HTML-AAM scopes a header or footer this way, so a card header inside any of these ancestors is the article's header, not the page's banner. #943 fixed the shadow-host walk that decides this; its fixture covered an `
` host and a `role="region"` host, which left the other eight scoping shapes without a shadow-nested regression. The `landmarks and headings` fixture has these ancestors but no shadow roots, so it cannot catch a scoping walk that forgets one of them across a host boundary. ## What changed - The `shadow section landmarks` fixture (`packages/web/tests/crosscheck/fixtures.ts`) now nests a header and footer two shadow roots deep under each of the ten scoping shapes, with the page-level control beside them. Each host keeps the structure #943 established: a shadow root on the scoping ancestor, a wrapper div inside it, a nested shadow root on the wrapper, and the header and footer in the innermost tree, named by the host id. - The fixture's inline script loops over all eleven host ids instead of three, so the added coverage costs no new machinery and the page-level control still proves the scoping is not over-applied. - Test-only change: no product code, no new `expected.txt` lines, no changeset, and no public surface moves. ```text fixture hosts (one header + footer pair each, two shadow roots deep) main this branch article article, aside, main, nav, section role="region" role="article", role="complementary", role="main", role="navigation", role="region" page-level control page-level control (unchanged) ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/integration/crosscheck.test.ts -t "shadow section landmarks"`: the fixture passes with the eleven hosts, and again with the whole suite (16 tests, 1 skipped). - `E2E_CROSSCHECK_UPDATE=1` on the same fixture produces an empty diff in `tests/crosscheck/expected.txt`: the tree, Chrome's accessibility tree over CDP, and Playwright's `getByRole` agree on every header and footer the added hosts carry. All ten scoping shapes still scope their landmarks to the article or section role, and the page-level control still reads as `banner` and `contentinfo`. - Three unrelated integration tests (`cli-run` shards and focused-CI cases, one `runner-lifecycle` junit case) fail on this Windows machine identically with and without the change, confirmed by stashing the fixture and rerunning on clean main. Path and line-ending baseline, not from this PR.

title: fix(mobile): preserve physical Android serial after name resolution
body:
## What changed

- A configured physical Android device name was passed to agent-device as `device` throughout warm-up and worker launch. The name lookup could resolve to an ADB serial, but that identity was not retained in the slot binding. A later call could treat the serial as a name and fail with `No device named <adb-serial>` / `Did you mean --serial <adb-serial>?`.
- The engine now looks up configured Android names in agent-device's inventory before warm-up, stores the resolved ID in the existing `deviceId` binding field, and sends later commands through `{ serial: id }`. An exact name wins over normalized variants; ambiguous normalized matches and names absent from inventory still use agent-device's name selector.
- This preserves existing selection paths for emulator serials, discovered booted devices, iOS names and UDIDs, hosted provider leases, and worker binding serialization. Omitting `device` was only a workaround.

The public configuration that triggered the failure is:

```ts
mobile({ platform: 'android', device: '22101320G' })
```

## Tests

- Added a regression test with inventory name `22101320G` and serial `2df0797d`. It checks warm-up boot and app open, the serialized binding, worker restoration, and the absence of a later `{ device: '2df0797d' }` selector. A second test covers colliding normalized names.
- Existing mobile unit tests cover emulator serials, discovery, iOS selection, pools, and provider leases.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| The new targeted regression failed: `apps.open` received `{ device: '22101320G' }` instead of `{ serial: '2df0797d' }`. | The regression passes; warm-up and worker boot use `{ serial: '2df0797d' }`. |

- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run test`: 234 passed across 12 files.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `adb devices -l`: connected phone `22101320G` was present. A minimal built CLI test using the configuration above and Android Settings passed:

```text
✓ mobile engine for target "android" prepared 2.24s
✓ |android| tests/physical-smoke.e2e.ts (1 test) 2.50s
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

- `pnpm check` could not complete after a filtered dependency install: dead-code analysis reported missing unrelated app dependencies (`expo/tsconfig.base`, `react-native-screens`). A full monorepo install was attempted but large optional downloads repeatedly timed out. The package checks above passed.

title: Expose `openSession()` on `e2e/runner` for hosts embedding e2e in another test runner
body:
Would e2e accept an `openSession()` function on the `e2e/runner` subpath, so a project that already has a test runner can open one e2e session from inside its own tests?

A project with existing Playwright Test, Vitest, or Jest suites can't use e2e's engines today unless it moves those suites to `e2e run`. The attempt it needs already exists: `run/standalone.ts` opens it for `e2e mcp`. That covers engine `prepare` (including `DeviceProvider` leases), app processes, the fixture graph (`agent`, `app`, `screen`, plus engine fixtures like `device`), secret redaction, and cleanup on every exit path. None of it is reachable outside the package exports.

In #970 you said programmatic runner APIs belong on `e2e/runner` so the runner graph never loads into test modules, and that the subpath "leaves room for `run()` later". #978 added `list()` there. A session API seems to fit the same entry:

```ts
import { openSession } from 'e2e/runner';

await using session = await openSession({
  cwd: '/repo',
  config: 'e2e.config.ts',   // path, or an E2EConfig value, same as list()
  target: 'android',
  onStep: (progress) => {},  // the StepProgress feed reporters get as `step` events
});
await session.fixtures.agent.act('open settings and turn on dark mode');
session.steps();             // StepRecords, with artifacts
await session.close();       // idempotent; resolves with cleanup failures
```

The scope is one attempt with no retries and no run report, because the host runner owns those. It adds no new engine, wire, or schema surface.

#980 implements this today under a separate `e2e/host` subpath. If `e2e/runner` is the right home, I'll move it there and accept `config` the same way `list()` does. Does this fit, or would you rather keep session hosting out of the public API?
