title: iOS simulator: device.setNetwork('offline') and setAirplaneMode(true) only change the status bar. The app stays online
fix(cache): a row of a windowed list is not keyed by its list's first rendered row; mobile benchmark re-recorded, Android strict
body:
## What and why

- The 39 mobile recordings dated from Sep 23-24, before the Oct 3 replay policy bump (#732) and the key change in #929. Every mobile agentic CI run missed all of them (`20 missed` / `21 missed` on the last three merge queue runs) and called the model for every step.
- Both platforms are re-recorded on a Mac: iPhone 17 Pro on the pinned iOS 26.5 runtime, Pixel 7 API 36 headless, against release builds made the way `.github/actions/expo-app` makes them. 20 Android entries, 21 iOS.
- The Android agentic job runs with `--strict-cache` like the web one: a recording that no longer replays fails its step as `REPLAY_STALE` instead of spending model calls on every run.
- iOS stays lenient. Three iOS recordings hand off on every replay, each an engine gap the README now names: Debounced Search (replay looks before the debounced results render, and relocation settles on the search field's wrapper, which reads "Benchmark Target" too), Choice Controls (the notes field's keyboard covers the Mushrooms checkbox and iOS drops it from the tree), Stripe PaymentSheet (the card form's fields are not in the tree after the Card tab is tapped). The other 18 replay.
- The web benchmark cache kept 30 entries under the pre-#929 key next to their re-keyed twins; the orphans go. Every one of the 30 has a live twin recorded for the same step.
- One cache fix, found by the first strict Android run on this branch. The container key of a row inside an unnamed list was the list's first leaf text (`containerKey`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/actions.ts`). On Android a windowed list renders whichever rows are near the viewport, so that text is a scroll position: the Huge Virtualized List tap was recorded as `tap group "Row 0512" in "Row 0500"` and handed off whenever the window started at 0501, once locally and once in CI. A container whose first text sits in a twin of the row the node came up through is a list and keys nothing by that text; its own label still keys it. The four Android entries that carried such a key (Infinite Scroll List, Huge Virtualized List, Sticky Chrome Target, Product Catalog) are re-recorded. iOS entries carry no placement. Web entries are unaffected: strict web replays the same 26.

```ts
// packages/e2e/src/agent/actions.ts
const key = (namedAfterTwinOf(container, nodes.get(came)) ? undefined : firstLeafText(container)) ?? ownLabel(container);
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[mobile agentic job] --> B{platform}
  B -- android --> C[e2e run --strict-cache]
  C --> D{entry replays?}
  D -- yes --> E[replayed, no model call]
  D -- no --> F[REPLAY_STALE, job fails]
  B -- ios --> G[e2e run]
  G --> H{entry replays?}
  H -- yes --> E
  H -- no --> I[hand off to the model]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- mobile-benchmark, Android, `e2e run --target android-emulator --config e2e.agent.config.ts --strict-cache` on Pixel_7_API_36 with the committed entries: `20 passed`, `15 replayed · 2 handed off · 3 missed`. The hand-offs and misses are swipes and run-time values, which the grammar does not record.

title: Replay cache: model identity is outside the observation surface — a model swap replays silently and the report attributes the pass to a model that never ran
body:
First: this is a verified consequence of a documented design choice, not an implementation bug. `docs/cache.mdx` states that an entry belongs to test/target/instruction/params/agent and that "changing the model does not [cause a miss]". We think the consequence deserves a second look, and we have three independent reproductions.

## What happens

1. Record an `agent.act` step under agent `default` with model A. Entry saved under `.e2e/cache/`.
2. Change the config so `default` uses model B (same agent name).
3. `npx e2e run` → the step replays (`cache.mode: "self-finalized"`), **zero model calls** (`modelTokens: 0`, `maxModelCallsInStep: 0`), all green, no warning, no re-record request.

The run header prints `model .../B`, but B never executed. In fact `report.json` contains **no model identity at all** for replayed runs — we grepped. The pass is attributed, on the console only, to a model with zero footprint in the artifact.

`--strict-cache` cannot catch this: it fails on replay *failure* (e.g. `REPLAY_STALE`), and here replay *succeeds*. Two worlds — "ran model A" and "ran model B" — produce the same green, and the observation is blind to the difference. In CI, "upgrade the model" is precisely when you want the suite to actually exercise the model; today it can keep passing on yesterday's recording indefinitely.

## Byte-level anchor

Cache entry `payload.recordedFor`:

```json
{ "testId": "...", "targetId": "web", "instructionDigest": "...", "paramsDigest": "...", "callIndex": 0, "agent": "default" }
```

No model field. Two entries recorded under the same agent with different models are byte-identical except where the flow itself differed.

## Environment / reproduction

- e2e 0.18.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.13.0, Playwright chromium-headless-shell 153
- OpenAI-compatible endpoint, two distinct tool-capable models (verified with `k3-agent`/`k2d8-preview` on one setup, `k3`/`kimi-for-coding` on two others)
- **Repro package: https://github.com/BiBoyang/e2e-replay-cache-repro** — one command (`./run-experiments.sh`) runs the full matrix with expected results echoed; ~9 model calls / ~45k tokens
- 13-step matrix: baseline record, replay, model swap, `--agent` control, UI fault injection (`Add` → `Add task`) with `--strict-cache`, live repair, restore, negative control
- 3 independent reproductions (2026-10-09), every cell consistent

## Suggestions (any one would close the hole)

1. Include provider+modelId in the entry key (or in `recordedFor` with a loud mismatch warning), so a model swap forces a live re-run.
2. Record the resolved model identity in `report.json` for every run, replayed or not — today the artifact cannot answer "which model was this pass evidence about?".
3. Minor: in strict mode a `REPLAY_STALE` step is counted as `1 handed off` in the summary line, though no hand-off occurred. `report.json` distinguishes it; the terminal summary doesn't.

Everything else we touched behaved well and deserves the praise: verification whitelist for recordings ("the attempt passing" doesn't count), action-granular replay-failure attribution (`target-not-found` at action 2 of 2), zero-model-call strict detection, and a repair loop that converges.

title: docs(skills): require a shortening pass on every docs page in authoring-docs and ship-pr
body: - `authoring-docs` opens with a required section, "IMPORTANT: shorten every page". It applies to every page an agent writes, edits, or rewrites, new pages and small edits included. - The pass measures the page against its sidebar neighbors with `wc -l` and a rough prose word count. Then it works three kinds of cuts in order: - cut what the reader doesn't act on - merge what's said twice, so each fact has one place on the page and a fact another page owns is a link - fold what only some readers need - When a user asks how to shorten a page, the agent shows the plan before editing: cuts grouped by kind, rough line savings and a reason for each, the target outline, and a recommendation. - It lists the claims a shortening pass tends to break, each taken from a real rewrite of `docs/integrations/smol.mdx`: - a caveat cut away from its claim - a merged sentence that is wrong against `src/` - a leftover fact parked under the nearest heading - a fact cut without saying so in the PR body - On a PR that isn't about docs, the pass covers only the sections the change touches. Cuts for the rest of the page are listed as a follow-up, so a feature PR doesn't restructure whole pages. - In "Rewriting a legacy page", the shortening step now runs before the fact comparison. The agent-prompt rule also skips a setup that is one install and a config change. - `ship-pr` step 1 runs the pass on every touched guide page before `pnpm check`, so the checks catch an anchor the pass broke. It links to the section instead of restating it. ## Verified Ran it locally: no runtime surface. This changes only text in two repo-internal skills. - Parsed both skill files with `mdast-util-from-markdown`. The four-backtick fence around the `awk` line holds, and the headings come out as intended. - Ran both measuring commands from the repo root: `wc -l docs/integrations/*.mdx` and the `awk` prose count, which gives 1325 words for `smol.mdx` on main. - `pnpm check` passes. - A fresh-context review checked the new rules against the skeleton, the model pages (`docs/quickstart.mdx`, `docs/bug-bash.mdx`), `ship-pr`, and `AGENTS.md`. title: fix(scripts): derive error-code source roots from the published packages
body: ## What and why `scripts/check-error-codes.ts` keeps the error reference honest: it reads every code the published packages can raise and fails when `docs/reference/errors.mdx` misses one or names one no source raises. The set of packages it reads from was a hand-written array of five paths, and it had drifted from what actually ships. `packages/eas/src/provider.ts` and `packages/smol/src/provider.ts` both raise `ConfigurationError('INVALID_CONFIG', ...)`, but neither was ever scanned, so a code introduced only in one of them could go undocumented while the check stayed green. That is the exact failure the script exists to prevent. The array also contradicted the script's own header, which says the inventory is read from the source and not from a hand-kept list. And it was already demanding maintenance: the open `feat(acp)` pull request has to hand-add `packages/acp/src` to it. This derives the roots from `publicPackages()` instead, the same helper `scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` already uses to walk the publishable packages. A new engine or integration is covered the moment its manifest exists, with nothing to remember. ```ts // scripts/error-codes.ts import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'; import { dirname, join, relative } from 'node:path'; import { REPO_ROOT, publicPackages } from './public-packages.ts'; /** Every published package's `src`, project-relative with `/` separators. */ export function sourceRoots(): string[] { return publicPackages() .map(({ path }) => `${relative(REPO_ROOT, dirname(path)).split('\\').join('/')}/src`) .filter((dir) => existsSync(join(REPO_ROOT, dir))) .toSorted(); } ``` The scanned set grows from five packages to eight, and the three additions are all published: `@e2e-dev/eas`, `@e2e-dev/kernel`, and `@e2e-dev/smol`. Kernel raises no codes today, so it changes nothing in the output, but it belongs in the set for the same reason the others do. ``` main (literal) this branch (derived) packages/e2e/src packages/decision/src packages/web/src packages/e2e/src packages/mobile/src packages/eas/src packages/github/src packages/github/src packages/decision/src packages/kernel/src packages/mobile/src packages/smol/src packages/web/src ``` The check output is unchanged, `83 in source (26 agent, 63 runner, 10 engine), all documented`, which is what confirms the wider net finds no new undocumented code today and simply closes the door on a future one. Two small pieces come with it. `scripts/error-codes.ts` holds the new `sourceRoots()` on its own, so the test imports it without the checker's `main()` running as a side effect, matching the `install-scripts.ts` / `check-install-scripts.ts` split already in `scripts/`. `scripts/check-error-codes.test.ts` asserts the roots equal the `src` of every published package and names `packages/eas/src` and `packages/smol/src` as the regression that motivated the change. No changeset. The change is to a repo-side check under `scripts/`, not to a published package. Note for the reviewer: the open `feat(acp)` pull request touches the same array to add `packages/acp/src`. If that lands first, this derivation drops the need for that line rather than conflicting with it, since `@e2e-dev/acp` publishes and its `src` is picked up automatically. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts` prints `error codes: 83 in source (26 agent, 63 runner, 10 engine), all documented in docs/reference/errors.mdx and docs/reference/engine.mdx` and exits 0, same as main. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases

### Minor Changes

## @e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.0

### Minor Changes

- [#999](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/999) [`4bb3e42`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4bb3e42f501e69dce9377a40542993d3c808d3e8) Thanks [@reiidoda](https://github.com/reiidoda)! - Breaking: `device.setNetwork('offline')` and `device.setAirplaneMode(true)` now fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` on iOS. They previously changed only the simulator's status bar while the app stayed online. Restoring the network with `setNetwork('online')` or `setAirplaneMode(false)` does nothing on iOS, so shared cleanup hooks still work.
  
  Run offline tests on Android with `platforms: ['android']` and `setAirplaneMode(true)` (Android 11+). `setNetwork('offline')` turns off Wi-Fi only; cellular data can keep the app online.

- [#1059](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1059) [`e291f09`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e291f09c6a1c78069cd1a7af3b973a3bf8aca9e5) Thanks [@thiagobrez](https://github.com/thiagobrez)! - `device.fold` works on foldable Android emulators. agent-device 0.21.25 sets the emulator console posture and waits for the device state Android commits, so the engine no longer refuses Android before the command; a fold to the cover display also clears the lock screen the emulator raises. Before, `device.fold` on an Android target failed with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.

- [#1023](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1023) [`490a97e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/490a97e7ccdaae259a7808ed23c4cf124946a18a) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - `device.locator()` and the `selector` locator match with agent-device's own term rules (`listSelectorChainMatches`, 0.21.21) instead of the engine's copy of them, which had drifted. A selector can match different nodes than before:
  
  - `role` takes agent-device's kind, the role `agent-device snapshot` prints (`text-field`, `navigation-bar`, `scroll-area`), not the `getByRole` role. `role=textbox` becomes `role=text-field`, `role=navigation` becomes `role=navigation-bar`, `role=search-field` becomes `role=search`, `role=listitem` becomes `role=cell`. Platform type names (`StaticText`, `NavigationBar`) still match through agent-device's deprecated aliases; the docs now use the kind.
  - Text terms (`id`, `label`, `value`, `text`) compare case-insensitively.
  - `visible` means hittable or a non-empty frame, and `hidden` its opposite.
  - `editable` means a fillable type that is enabled; a disabled field is not editable.
  - `hittable` matches only a node that reports it; one that doesn't say is no longer counted as hittable.
  - `text` reads the first non-empty label, value, or identifier.

### Patch Changes

- [#1025](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1025) [`880ae70`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/880ae70c9c6ade9d6f69e7d7a17b7f4a6b4056b3) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - agent-device 0.21.25: `settings permission --app` resolves a display name to the installed app's id and refuses an app that isn't installed ([callstack/agent-device#3386](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3386)), and on iOS a canceled request keeps its session until the runner finishes the canceled command ([callstack/agent-device#3385](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3385)).

- [#988](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/988) [`c807f94`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c807f9480646a13f00d308cdd0a90034908b5543) Thanks [@enesonus](https://github.com/enesonus)! - Add the Limrun device provider with one hosted instance per worker, app
  installation, recording through agent-device, and cleanup on run exit.
  Renew retained driver leases while other targets run. Keep provider-owned
  local daemons isolated from ambient remote-daemon environment settings.

- [#1025](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1025) [`880ae70`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/880ae70c9c6ade9d6f69e7d7a17b7f4a6b4056b3) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - Permissions are set on the app by name, with agent-device's `settings permission --app` (0.21.21, with display names resolved since 0.21.25). `device.setPermission()` and the permissions a launch presets no longer open the app first to put agent-device's session on it, so a permission goes in before the app's first launch with no foreground open. `device.setPermission()` always acts on the pinned app, as documented, not on whichever app the session last opened. The warm-up in `prepare` still opens the pinned app, and a worker no longer lists agent-device's sessions at start.

- [#1026](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1026) [`62d5524`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/62d55249c1348446d5f536ad9474383016075bb1) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - The mobile engine measures an observation in the viewport agent-device publishes with each snapshot (0.21.21), and infers it from the tree's largest window or rect extent only for a snapshot that publishes none. On a snapshot that publishes one, a tree that doesn't reach the screen's edges no longer shrinks the viewport, so a system panel above the bottom of the screen is no longer taken for the navigation bar.

- [#1024](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1024) [`9065cf8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9065cf8d36ec5616b18c842b577e8bf0ffd6740d) Thanks [@thymikee](https://github.com/thymikee)! - A missing agent-device session is recognized by agent-device's `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` code and its `session_or_device_selector_required` reason (0.21.21) instead of a pattern over the message, so a reworded message can no longer change whether a failure reports as `APP_NOT_OPEN`.
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- [#843](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/843) [`ac657d1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ac657d1d0c063cd19ee458ee1d645783bf1ef8ce) Thanks [@pvedula7](https://github.com/pvedula7)! - The decision executor offers `dismiss_keyboard` while an on-screen keyboard is showing and the engine can dismiss it. Before, a control the keyboard covered after typing (an iOS number pad over a submit button) could not be reached, and the step failed.

- [#910](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/910) [`42ce272`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/42ce272c9ccc8e59571eaa14122e55ed85554b29) Thanks [@Ashfaqbs](https://github.com/Ashfaqbs)! - The decision executor now forwards an element's `selected` state to the model, the same way it already forwards `checked` and `expanded`. Without it, a tab bar's active tab looked identical to the rest, so the completion check for a tab switch landed near 50/50 and sometimes blocked a step that actually worked, or claimed a step done before anything was tapped.

- [#844](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/844) [`5e55d7c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/5e55d7c92d67f9b8741c7835ef23de5d62c637c2) Thanks [@pvedula7](https://github.com/pvedula7)! - The decision executor's stall guard now counts an action that errored as no progress, so three actions in a row that failed or changed nothing on screen block the step. It used to look only at whether the page changed, and a ticking timer on screen changes it every time: a tap that failed with `APP_UNREACHABLE` again and again never tripped the guard, and the model could repeat it until it gave up and claimed the step failed. A skipped pick and a rejected `done` or `failed` claim also carry an error in the step's history, so they count toward the three as well.

title: opencodeConsole(): five OpenCode Go ids silently cap output at 4096 tokens
cli: e2e models opencode-console cannot list ids from OPENCODE_API_KEY alone
body:
### Problem

`npx e2e models opencode-console` lists ids only from a stored Console login. With `OPENCODE_API_KEY` set and no login stored, it exits with

    no OpenCode Console login is stored; run `npx e2e login opencode-console`

even though `opencodeConsole('<id>')` runs fine with that same key — measured: 31 of 31 Go ids answer. `docs/reference/environment.mdx` states this ("`e2e models` still reads the stored login"), so this is a request rather than a defect. It does make the CI path the docs recommend unable to discover the ids the key serves, and the message does not mention the key, so it reads as "no credentials" while working credentials are present.

### Proposed API

`npx e2e models opencode-console` falls back to listing ids through `OPENCODE_API_KEY` when no login is stored. If that is not wanted, the message could name both credentials: "no OpenCode Console login and no `OPENCODE_API_KEY` stored; run `npx e2e login opencode-console` or set `OPENCODE_API_KEY`".

### Which surface

CLI flags

### Compatibility

- [x] nothing that exists today changes (the login path keeps working as it does now)

title: environment: OPENCODE_API_KEY is described as a Console service account key, but a Go subscription key works
body:
### Page

`docs/reference/environment.mdx` (line 25), the CI section of `docs/subscriptions.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` (line 83).

### What is wrong

All three describe `OPENCODE_API_KEY` as "an OpenCode Console service account key". Measured against the code: an OpenCode Go **subscription** API key works the same way — with `OPENCODE_API_KEY` set to it and no stored login, `opencodeConsole('go/<id>')` answers for all 31 Go ids my workspace lists, and logging out of `opencode-console` makes no difference.

The repo never mentions a Go key: `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` and `zen/go` have zero hits, and `opencode-go` appears only in the provider and its unit test. A Go subscriber reading the page will not learn that the key they already hold is accepted; they read "service account key" and go create a Console one.

CONTRIBUTING.md says where the docs and the code disagree the code wins and the docs are a bug, so here is the code: `opencodeConsole()` reads `OPENCODE_API_KEY` in place of the stored login (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/opencode-console.ts`).

### Suggested wording

Environment table: "An OpenCode Console service account key or an OpenCode Go subscription key; `opencodeConsole()` uses it in place of the stored `opencode-console` login. `e2e models` lists ids from the stored login only."

CI section of `subscriptions.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`: "OpenCode Console: a service account key from the Console (Service Accounts, then API Keys), or the API key of your OpenCode Go subscription. Set it as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`."

No public type, error code, CLI flag, or wire field moved, so no `.d.ts` review, `sdk-types.ts` assertion, schema, or fixture is involved. - [ ] Engine contract change: none. fix(opencode-console): ask for 8192 output tokens on the Anthropic route
body: Fixes #1013 ## What and why - `opencodeConsole('')` now asks for an explicit output cap on the models the workspace config serves over Anthropic. - The Anthropic SDK does not know those ids, so a call that sets no `maxOutputTokens` is limited to 4096 tokens with nothing but a `compatibility` warning: the answer comes back `finishReason: 'length'` at 4096 and no part of the result says why. - `packages/e2e/src/oauth/opencode-console.ts:122` fills in 8192, the cap `docs/reference/config.mdx` already documents for a judgment, and leaves a caller's own `maxOutputTokens` untouched. - Agent steps were never affected: the runner passes `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8192` on every call (`packages/e2e/src/agent/invocation.ts:147`). The issue carries that correction; the scope here is the direct call. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `generateText({ model: opencodeConsole('go/minimax-m3'), prompt })` with no cap: 4096 output tokens, `finishReason: 'length'`, the SDK's silent default | the same call: `max_tokens: 8192` on the wire (pinned by the new unit case), and the answer is no longer cut at 4096 | ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New case in `tests/unit/oauth/opencode-console.test.ts`: the request carries `max_tokens: 8192` when the call sets no cap and the caller's `1234` when it does. On `main` that case fails with `expected 128000 to be 8192`. - `pnpm --filter e2e test`: 248 files, 3152 passed, 2 skipped. - `pnpm check`: exit 0, including `mint validate` and the broken-link check over the docs page. - Every id the issue lists accepts 8192 against the real subscription with no error (`go/minimax-m3`, `go/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `go/qwen3.8-flash`, `go/qwen3.8-max`, `go/space-bunny`), so the value is safe to ask for. - It is still a cap: a prompt that never ends stops at 8192 with `finishReason: 'length'`, where it used to stop at 4096. What changes is that the number is the provider's own and documented, and a caller who needs more gets it: `maxOutputTokens: 12000` came back with 11001 tokens and `finishReason: 'stop'`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`e2e`: patch). - [ ] Breaking change: none. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/subscriptions.mdx`. `skills/e2e/` does not describe the cap. - [ ] Contract change: none; no emitted `.d.ts` and no wire schema moved. - [ ] Engine contract change: not applicable.

title: docs: rewrite and shorten the guide pages with the authoring-docs skill
body:
Rewrites the 40 guide pages under `docs/` (everything except `docs/reference/`) to the shape in `.dev/skills/authoring-docs`, then runs its shortening pass on each. Two commits per page (`rewrite`, then `shorten`), so each page can be read old against new.

- Every page opens with a sentence that defines its subject, uses task headings in reading order, and ends with `## Next` cards.
- Long examples, mapping tables, and edge cases are folded into `Accordion`s. Alternatives are in `Tabs`. The CI service pages get a copyable agent prompt.
- Facts said twice now have one place, and pages link to the page that owns a fact instead of copying it.
- Anchors that other pages link to are unchanged. Renamed or removed anchors had no links from `docs/`, `skills/`, `README.md`, or `packages/*/src`.

Across the 40 pages, prose words drop from 45,267 to 40,153 (-11%) and source lines from 8,997 to 8,503 (-5.5%). Most pages land 5-15% shorter in prose. The migration pages and the CI service pages moved least: they are mostly mapping tables and YAML where each row is its own fact, and the CI service pages gained an agent prompt. Eight pages are longer in lines than on main, mostly from `## Next` cards, accordion tags, and the prompts.

## Wrong or stale claims fixed

Each was checked against `packages/*/src`:

- `decision-models`: a point tap costs three decision calls and one text call, not four.
- `writing-an-engine`: removes the origin checks on `location`. #290 removed origin policy. The JSDoc at `packages/e2e/src/engine/index.ts:612-617` still says it; left for a code PR.
- `mobile`: the Android `installApp` troubleshooting named agent-device 0.21.18. The pinned 0.21.22 parses the manifest itself and searches `~/Library/Android/sdk` on macOS.
- `web`: in CI, e2e ignores `reuseExisting` and starts the command; only a server that already answers is `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`. Adds: `reuseExisting` with port `0` is `INVALID_CONFIG`, and plain HTTP passes only on loopback hosts.
- `authentication`: `INVALID_CONFIG` also fires for a password shorter than 6 characters (`MIN_SECRET_LENGTH`).
- `ci`: rerun folders are `rerun-<n>/`, not `rerun-1/`.
- `migrate/playwright`: `use` and `testMatch` are among the Playwright keys e2e rejects.
- `visual-testing`: only writing a screenshot waits for two identical captures; a comparison stops at the first match.

fix(oauth): read OPENCODE_API_KEY in e2e models opencode-console
body:
Fixes #1014.

- `e2e models opencode-console` reads `OPENCODE_API_KEY` when it is set, in place of the stored login, as `opencodeConsole()` already does. With both set, the listing now shows the workspace the tests actually run on.
- `e2e models` with no provider includes OpenCode Console when only the key is set.
- With no credential, both errors name the key along with `npx e2e login opencode-console`. A rejected key says `check OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
- The key lookup lives in one place: `apiKeyEnv` on the provider (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/types.ts`) and `credentialSource()` in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers.ts`, used by both `opencodeConsole()` and `listModels()`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI (`dist/cli/bin.js models`) on main and on this branch. A stub server stood in for `opencode.ai/console/api/config` (fetch redirected by a `--import` preload) and logged the bearer each run sent.

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| key only, `models opencode-console` | `no OpenCode Console login is stored; run npx e2e login opencode-console`, exit 1 | 2 models (Zen + `go/`), `Bearer <key>`, no `x-org-id`, exit 0 |
| key only, bare `models` | `no login is stored; sign in with e2e login <...>`, exit 1 | lists OpenCode Console, exit 0 |
| neither | `... run npx e2e login opencode-console`, exit 1 | `... run npx e2e login opencode-console or set OPENCODE_API_KEY`, exit 1 |
| key + stored login | lists via the login (`Bearer st_tok`, `x-org-id: org_1`) | lists via the key (`Bearer <key>`), same as `opencodeConsole()` |
| rejected key + stored login | lists via the login, ignoring the key the tests use | `OpenCode Console rejected the stored token (401: invalid key); check OPENCODE_API_KEY`, exit 1 |
| login only | lists via the login | unchanged |

- Not verified against the live service, since no OpenCode key was available. OpenCode's docs describe a single `oc_sk_` key kind bound to a workspace, and Go as a property of the workspace, so a Go subscription key is most likely the same key as a service account key. The listing reads the same config `opencodeConsole()` already reads with the key.

title: fix(web): observe responses before the first navigation
body: ## What and why - `browser.waitForResponse` can observe the response from the first `browser.goto` or `app.open`. Previously it rejected with `APP_NOT_OPEN` before navigation could begin. - The wait and navigation share one pending active page and resume in call order. Existing media emulation, recording, cleanup and active-tab scope are retained. - Includes Chromium, lifecycle and built-CLI regressions, documentation, the generated consumer skill and a web patch changeset. Addresses the pre-navigation response-wait gap in #1020. ```ts const [response] = await Promise.all([ browser.waitForResponse('**/network'), browser.goto('/network'), ]); expect(response.status).toBe(200); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR W["waitForResponse"] --> P["Shared first-page opening"] G["goto or app.open"] --> P P --> L["Register response listener"] L --> N["Navigate"] N --> R["Resolve response wait"] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Tested head `4bb44bfa` against base `c82a03a2`, including the media-emulation changes from #1030, on Linux Node 22.23.3. title: fix(mobile): match device selectors with agent-device's own term rules
body: ## What and why - `device.locator()` parsed selectors with agent-device's parser, then matched terms with the engine's own copy of agent-device's rules (`packages/mobile/src/selector.ts`). The copy had drifted on `hittable`, `visible`/`hidden`, `editable`, `text`, `role`, and case. So a selector that worked on the agent-device CLI could match different nodes here. - agent-device 0.21.21 exports `listSelectorChainMatches` from `agent-device/selectors` ([callstack/agent-device#3180](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3180), filed from this integration). The engine now calls it and maps the matched nodes back to its projected ones. The copied term rules are gone. ```ts const matched = listSelectorChainMatches(nodes, chain, { platform })?.matchedNodes ?? []; return matched.flatMap((node) => byNode.get(node) ?? []); ``` - `resolveExpression` takes the target's platform, since agent-device's `editable` depends on it. - Strictness stays the runner's. An agent-device action skips an ambiguous `||` alternative, but a locator action on several matches still fails. The reference page says so. - Selectors can now match different nodes than before. The changeset is a `minor` and lists each change. `role` takes agent-device's kind (`text-field`, `navigation-bar`, `scroll-area`), not the `getByRole` role (`textbox`). Text terms compare case-insensitively. The docs examples move from the platform type names (`role=NavigationBar`), which agent-device keeps only as deprecated aliases, to the kind (`role=navigation-bar`). - `normalizeKind` in `nodes.ts` loses its export: the selector was its only outside user. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - iOS 27.1 simulator (iPhone 17 Pro), iOS Settings, a scratch project on the built packages. One test logs `await device.locator(selector).count()` for each selector. The last column is `agent-device is exists ''` on the same screen, as ground truth: | selector | main | this branch | agent-device CLI | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `role=NavigationBar` | 1 | 1 | exists | | `role=navigation-bar` | 1 | 1 | exists | | `role=navigation` | 1 | 0 | no match | | `role=textbox` | 1 | 0 | no match | | `role=search-field` | 1 | 0 | no match | | `role=text` / `role=StaticText` | 13 | 13 | exists | | `editable` | 1 | 1 | exists | | `hittable=false` | 2 | 2 | exists | | `text=General` | 4 | 4 | exists | - The new `selector.test.ts` runs the term rules over a raw Android form and the captured benchmark trees for both platforms. Nine of its 14 tests fail against main's matcher. - Not run locally: the mobile benchmark. This PR's mobile jobs run it on iOS and Android. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. On the breaking-change box: `@e2e-dev/mobile` selectors are not on the stability policy's covered list, but `role=textbox` and case-sensitive text did work before. That's why the changeset is a `minor` and names every change. If you'd rather keep the old role spellings through a deprecation window, say so and I'll add the warning. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: refactor(mobile): recognize a missing session by agent-device's code and reason
body: ## What and why - `translateError` decided `INVALID_STATE` with a pattern over agent-device's message (`no active session|requires an active session|...`). agent-device 0.21.21 gives the one refusal that pattern needed beyond `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, ` requires an active session or an explicit device selector`, a typed `details.reason: 'session_or_device_selector_required'` ([callstack/agent-device#3181](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3181), filed from this integration). - The engine now reads the code and the reason: ```ts if (normalized.code === 'SESSION_NOT_FOUND' || details(cause).reason === NO_SESSION_REASON) { ``` - Every other alternative in the pattern is a `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` message in agent-device 0.21.22, or a message agent-device does not send (`open an app first`, `no app open`). - `staleOr` keeps keying on the reason alone. [callstack/agent-device#3183](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3183) made a drag's stale ref report `dispatched: 'no'`, but agent-device's golden table keeps `unknown` for a drag refused after Android blocking-dialog recovery. Requiring `no` would stop retrying that case. - The unsupported-capability pattern stays: a platform refusing a setting e2e itself names still arrives as `INVALID_ARGS` text. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - iOS 27.1 simulator, a scratch project on the built packages: `app.open()`, `device.closeApp()`, then `device.foregroundApp()`. agent-device refuses `appstate` with the typed reason, and both builds report it the same way: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `APP_NOT_OPEN`: `device.foregroundApp failed: appstate requires an active session or an explicit device selector (e.g. --platform ios).` | `APP_NOT_OPEN`, same message | - `errors.test.ts` adds the case the change is about: the same text without the reason stays `ENGINE_FAILURE`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: refactor(mobile): set permissions on the app by name, without an open first
body:
## What and why

- agent-device's `settings permission` acted only on the app its session was on. To set a permission before the first launch, the engine opened the app first just to put the session on it. That took:
  - a `sessionApp` field on the surface and on every slot binding;
  - a `sessions.list` at worker start, to check that the warm-up's session survived;
  - a foreground open before `setPermission` and before the permissions a launch presets;
  - a retry that matched the refusal text `requires an active app in session`.
- agent-device 0.21.21 takes an explicit `app` ([callstack/agent-device#3179](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3179), filed from this integration), and 0.21.25 resolves a display name there and refuses an app that isn't installed ([callstack/agent-device#3386](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3386)). This PR bumps `agent-device` to 0.21.25 for that: on 0.21.22 a target pinned by display name (`bundleId: 'Settings'`, as in the quickstart) would get its permission written for a client literally named `Settings`. `simctl privacy` and `pm` need only the id, not a running app. All of the above is gone:

  ```ts
  client.settings.update({ setting: 'permission', permission, state, ...this.selection(), ...(app === undefined ? {} : { app }) })
  ```

- The permission call carries the worker's device selection. Before, the open in front of it bound the session to the device; without that open, a worker with no session (after `closeApp`, or on a slot whose earlier worker retired) would send the change to the daemon's default device.
- `device.setPermission()` acts on the pinned app, as its docs say, not on whichever app the session last opened.
- The warm-up in `prepare` still opens the pinned app, so a test that starts without `app.open()` finds it on screen. Its other reason, that a timed-out open resets the daemon every slot shares, is gone since agent-device 0.21.21 ([callstack/agent-device#3177](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3177)), and the comments say so.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph main
    A1[open app, foreground] --> B1[settings permission] --> C1[open --relaunch]
  end
  subgraph this branch
    B2[settings permission --app] --> C2[open --relaunch]
  end
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- iOS 27.1 simulator (iPhone 17 Pro), a scratch project on the built packages, target `com.apple.Maps`. The test runs `device.closeApp()`, `device.setPermission('photos', 'grant')`, `app.open()`, `device.closeApp()`, `device.setPermission('photos', 'deny')`. Commands agent-device received for the session, from its `events.ndjson`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| boot, **session_list**, close, **open**, settings, open, close, **open**, settings | boot, close, settings, open, close, settings |

- The simulator's `TCC.db` has `kTCCServicePhotos | com.apple.Maps | 0` from the branch's final `deny`.
- On 0.21.25, the same simulator with the target pinned by display name (`app: { bundleId: 'Maps' }`): `device.setPermission('photos', 'grant')` before the first `app.open()` wrote `kTCCServicePhotos | com.apple.Maps | 2`.
- Not run locally: Android, and the mobile benchmark. This PR's mobile jobs run both.

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

`DeviceLease` loses the optional `sessionApp` it inherited from `SlotBinding`. It was never documented, and the lease-to-binding path already dropped it.

title: fix(mobile): measure observations in the viewport agent-device publishes
body: ## What and why - The engine inferred the screen size from the tree: the largest application or window rect, else the extent of every rect (`viewportOf` in `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`). Every observation's viewport, the screen root's box, and the Android system-bar filter depend on that guess. - agent-device 0.21.21 publishes the viewport a snapshot's rects are measured in ([callstack/agent-device#3182](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3182), filed from this integration). The engine now prefers it: ```ts const viewport = options.viewport ?? viewportOf(raw); ``` - The inference stays as the fallback, because not every producer publishes a viewport. Appium-sourced Android trees never do, and agent-device's Android helper leaves it out when its two display reads around a dump disagree. Android screenshots carry no logical size either, so without the inference those captures could not be observed at all. - The difference shows when the tree doesn't reach the screen's edges. A system panel at the bottom of a tree that ends at 1800 px of a 2400 px screen was dropped as the navigation bar. Measured against the published screen, it stays (`nodes.test.ts`). - The benchmark's snapshot capture (`tests-capture/snapshots.e2e.ts`) keeps `viewport` now, and the golden test projects with it, so the next recapture records it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Android emulator (API 35, 1080x2400), Settings, through `e2e mcp`: `open_session`, then `call {tool: "observe"}`, in landscape and portrait. The observation from this branch is byte-identical to main's (node ids normalized); the status-bar icons are filtered on both. - agent-device on the same screens publishes `1080x2400` in portrait and `2400x1080` in landscape. Both match what the inference reads there, so these screens show no change. - The new tests fail on main: the published viewport outranks the application node's 390x844, and the panel case above. - Not run locally: the mobile benchmark. This PR's mobile jobs run it on iOS and Android. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(report): retain serial duration with interrupted retry verdicts
body:
- A serial retry the run interrupts, or one that never reaches its members (collection or launch failure), no longer stands for the members' verdict. The report and every reporter now take the verdict and duration from the last attempt that ran them. Before, JUnit and Markdown timed a failed member by the cut retry (often 0 ms or a few ms).
- The runner decides once: `finishedSerialAttempt` (`packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts`) sets `cutRetry` on the attempt record before it is streamed, `memberResults` reads it from `group.attempts`, and report.json carries it on each serial attempt (`report-v1.schema.json`, optional, absent in older reports).
- `outcome()` (`packages/e2e/src/report/outcome.ts`) gains a `verdict` attempt; `durationMs` and the failure block come from it. Older reports without `cutRetry` fall back to `isCutSerialRetry` on the attempt status.
- Docs: `docs/reference/test.mdx` serial rules and the `docs/debugging.mdx` jq query skip cut attempts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Serial attempt finishes] --> B[Set cutRetry on the record]
  B --> C[Stream serialAttemptFinished]
  C --> D[Verdict = last attempt not cut]
  D --> E[report.json, JUnit, Markdown]
```

## Verified

title: --strict-cache: REPLAY_STALE (end-mismatch) on unchanged pages since 0.19 — Next.js route announcer recorded as an alert anchor
body:
### Environment
- e2e 0.19.0 + @e2e-dev/web 0.14.0 (fails) · e2e 0.16.0 + @e2e-dev/web 0.11.2 + playwright 1.63.0 (passes)
- ai 7.0.127, @ai-sdk/openai 4.0.83, model `chatgpt('gpt-6-luna')` via `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`
- Node 24.18.0, macOS 26.6.2, chromium headless shell 1243
- App: Next.js 16.4.0 (App Router), React 19.3.0, `next build && next start`, local
- Config: `cache: { mode: 'read-write', dir: '.e2e/cache' }`, `workers: 1`, `retries: 0`

### Steps
1. A minimal Next.js app with one site title (`metadata = { title: 'Acme Notes' }` in the root layout) and no per-page titles. A left nav with `<Link>`s to `/`, `/library` and `/settings`; the nav shows labels on every page except `/`. `/` is dynamic (`export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`) with `generateMetadata` that awaits a random 0-150 ms delay and returns `{}`. `/library` is static.
2. One test:
   ```ts
   test('open Library from the left navigation', async ({ app, agent, browser }) => {
     await app.open('/');
     await agent.act('Open the Library page from the left navigation');
     await expect(browser.locator('[data-testid="notes"]')).toContainText('Meeting notes');
   });
   ```
3. Record once (`e2e run`), then run `e2e run --strict-cache` 10 times.

### Expected
Every strict replay self-finalizes. The page and the flow are identical on every run, and 0.16.0 replays 10/10 on the same app.

### Actual
| | strict replays | REPLAY_STALE |
|---|---|---|
| 0.16.0 | 10 | 0 |
| 0.19.0 | 10 | 2 |

`steps[].cache` on each stale run:
```
reason: end-mismatch
detail: every recorded action ran, but the recorded end state did not show on /library: expected alert "Acme Notes", node "Acme Notes"
```
Same symptom on a larger hosted Next.js app: about half of strict replays stale on 0.19.0, 12/12 clean on 0.16.0.

### Cause (as far as I can read it)
- Next's App Router mounts a route announcer: a shadow-DOM `<div role="alert" aria-live="assertive">`.
- On navigation it writes `document.title` into that div, but only when the title differs from the last one it read.
- With streamed metadata, whether the title differs depends on whether the metadata arrived before or after hydration. In a Playwright probe of the app above, the announcer fired on 17 of 20 identical clicks and stayed empty on 3.
- In 0.19.0, `ANNOUNCEMENT_ROLES` in `cache/anchors.js` records `alert`/`status` nodes before every other anchor, and the cap never crowds them out. So the announcer's text becomes the recording's first end anchor (`endAnchors[0] = { role: 'alert', name: 'Acme Notes' }`). `deltaHolds` then requires it on replay, and also rejects an announcer alert the recording did not see.
- In 0.16.0 the same step records leaves in document order, capped at 8. The announcer at the end of `<body>` falls outside the cap and is never checked.

This is not a regression in matching. 0.19.0 now promotes a framework-owned live region that changes text on load timing, not on what the step did.

### Suggestions
- Exclude the Next.js route announcer (`next-route-announcer > #__next-route-announcer__`) from anchors, or more generally any live region that only echoes `document.title` / the route.
- Or treat an announcement whose text equals the document title (or the previous one) as navigation noise, not an outcome.
- The `end-mismatch` detail prints `endAnchors.slice(0, 2)` (`agent/step-cache.js`), i.e. the first recorded anchors, not the ones that failed. Here it names `node "Acme Notes"`, which was very likely present. Naming the anchors that did not hold would have made this a one-minute diagnosis.

title: fix(web): omit Next.js route announcer from observations
body:
Fixes [#1057](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/1057).

## What and why

- Next.js App Router's `<next-route-announcer>` echoes `document.title` into a shadow `<div id="__next-route-announcer__" role="alert">` on a hydration schedule of its own. The web engine recorded it as an outcome alert, so an identical navigation replayed stale (`REPLAY_STALE`, `end-mismatch`) depending on whether the echo had landed.
- Fix: `next-route-announcer` joins `SKIP_TAGS` in `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`. The skip runs before the walk descends into light children or a shadow root, so the whole announcer subtree is never observed. A direct locator still reads it.
- An app's own `role="alert"`, even with the title's text, is still observed and still stops a replay that raised it.
- No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump: older entries that recorded the echo re-record on the next read-write run.
- Tests: a web integration test (announcer empty and populated yield no alert node, app alert kept, locator still reads the text) and a three-row record/replay matrix in `packages/e2e` against a fixture page with the real announcer shape.
- Maintainer follow-up commit: collapsed the per-node check into SKIP_TAGS and trimmed the tests. The author's commit and credit stay as they were.

It goes in the image URL (`?v=`, which also busts social caches) and in a `tEXt` chunk of the PNG. `pnpm docs:check` compares both against the expected digest without rendering, and fails on a stale or orphaned card. - A page with no card (the home page, or one nobody ran the script for) falls back to the brand card `images/og.png`, still set site-wide in `docs.json` as on main. - The card is typed by `@types/react` 19.1.4, the copy `@vercel/og` resolves, so two React type copies do not clash. - A page that leaves the navigation loses its card and its `og:image` lines, so it falls back instead of pointing at a deleted file. - `docs/.mintignore` hides `/og/`: the generator, its fonts (OFL), the background, and the mascot cut-out. It is anchored so `images/og/` still ships. - `docs/package.json` engines move from `>=22.12.0` to the runner's `^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0`. The docs scripts run `.ts` files directly, which needs Node 22.18 or later, so the old floor was already wrong. - `@vercel/og` is pinned to 0.11.1. Versions 1.0.0 to 1.0.3 fail to import from a Node ESM script (`Dynamic require of "fs"`, a missing `hb.wasm`). ```mermaid flowchart LR A[docs.json nav + page frontmatter] --> B[og/generate.ts] B -->|stale digest| C[render with @vercel/og] C --> D[images/og/page.png + tEXt digest] B --> E[og:image frontmatter ?v=digest] F[page without og:image] --> G[Mintlify card on og-background.png] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Docs site, `mint dev` (pinned 4.2.909): `/reference/cli` serves ``. `/images/og/reference/cli.png` and `/images/og/agents.png` return 200, while `/og/generate.ts` and `/og/mascot.png` return 404. `/` still points at `images/og.png`. - Fallback: a throwaway `forgotten.mdx` added to the nav without running the script served `og:image` `images/og.png`, and `docs:check` failed on it with "Open Graph card is stale". After removing it from the nav, the script deleted its card and stripped its frontmatter lines. - `--check` failed when a card PNG was swapped for another page's and when a layout value changed. It passed after a comment-only edit to the script. A CRLF page kept its line endings through a rewrite. | --- | --- | ![smol](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/671bc0e9-84a1-4975-bbcd-943f11f53a48) Not done: the shortening pass from authoring-docs on the 41 guide pages. This change adds only two generated frontmatter lines to each and touches no prose.

title: feat(skills): split mcp and bug-bash into their own skills
body: skills.sh lists this repo with one useful skill, `e2e`, whose description has to cover everything from config to bug bashes. An agent picks skills by description, so "bug bash this app" or "check my change in the running app" triggers weakly, and nobody searching skills.sh for MCP or QA finds us. This splits the two task-shaped topics into skills of their own: | Skill | Job | | --- | --- | | `e2e` | Set up, write, run, and debug tests (unchanged topics minus the two below) | | `e2e-mcp` | Use the live app from a coding agent through `e2e mcp` (was `references/mcp.md`) | | `e2e-bug-bash` | Bug bash an app and prove each bug with a repro test (was `references/bug-bash.md`) | | `create-verification-skill` | Unchanged, still installed only through `skills add` | - The two files move with `git mv` and gain frontmatter plus an intro. Each refers to the others by topic (`npx e2e guide `), never by relative path, so `npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill ` works for any one of them alone. - `BUNDLED_SKILLS` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/skill.ts` lists what the package ships. A sibling `e2e-` is served as topic ``, so `e2e guide mcp`, `e2e guide bug-bash`, and `e2e://guide/mcp` keep working. - `e2e init` installs each bundled skill with the existing copy, link, and symlink-safety rules. A rerun in a project an earlier version set up adds the two new skills to the locations chosen before, and removes the old `references/mcp.md` and `references/bug-bash.md` (`RETIRED_FILES`). Without that removal, a pre-split `.claude/skills/e2e` copy would never become the link, since it held files the bundle no longer ships. - Docs: `coding-agents.mdx` lists the skills and folds the skills.sh install into an accordion; `bug-bash.mdx`, `quickstart.mdx`, `reference/cli.mdx`, `reference/mcp.mdx`, README, and AGENTS.md follow. Not in this PR: the skills.sh page still shows `verify`, `babysit`, `writing-pr`, `ship-pr`, `unbox-ai`, and `unslop`, from installs recorded before #948 hid them. That needs a removal request to Vercel. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes The packed `e2e` tarball installed into a scratch project, then `init` and `guide`: ```text $ npx e2e init --yes ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e/ (7 files) ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e-mcp/ (1 files) ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e-bug-bash/ (1 files) ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e-mcp -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e-mcp ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e-bug-bash -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e-bug-bash $ npx e2e guide mcp | head -1 # Driving the app over MCP $ npx e2e guide bug-bash | head -1 # Running a bug bash ``` Upgrade: a project whose `.agents/skills/e2e` and `.claude/skills/e2e` are copies of main's skill, then the branch's `init --yes`: ```text ◆ Updated .agents/skills/e2e/ (7 files, removed 2 no longer shipped) ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e-mcp/ (1 files) ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e-bug-bash/ (1 files) ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e (replaced the copy) ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e-mcp -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e-mcp ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e-bug-bash -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e-bug-bash $ ls .agents/skills/e2e/references agent.md debugging.md explore.md running.md setup.md writing-tests.md ``` What skills.sh users get, from this branch's checkout: ```text $ npx skills add --list ◇ Found 4 skills │ create-verification-skill │ e2e │ e2e-bug-bash │ e2e-mcp ``` Routing: `examples/with-vite` with the branch's skills, one `claude -p` per prompt, read-only tools. The first tool call of each run: | Prompt | Skill loaded | | --- | --- | | Open the app and tell me what the greeting screen shows | `e2e-mcp` | | Bug bash this app | `e2e-bug-bash` | | Add an e2e test for the greeting | `e2e` | | QA the greeting flow before we release it and tell me what's broken | `e2e-bug-bash` | | I changed the greeting copy; check in the running app that it looks right | `e2e-mcp` | One run per prompt, Claude Code only; Codex was not tried. --- Opened by Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Reviewed before opening by gpt-6-astra (three rounds) and a fresh-context Fable 5 reviewer.

title: feat(mobile): drive devices with argent through mobile({ driver: 'argent' })
body: PoC of Software Mansion's [argent](https://github.com/software-mansion/argent) as a second driver for `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ```ts const iphone = mobile({ platform: 'ios', driver: 'argent' }); ``` - `packages/mobile/src/options.ts` adds a `DeviceClient` interface: the agent-device client methods the engine calls, with each result narrowed to the fields it reads. agent-device's client already fits it. - `packages/mobile/src/argent.ts` implements `DeviceClient` on `@swmansion/argent/client`, a new optional peer loaded only by this module. The surface, the pool, the `device` fixture, and the agent tools are unchanged. - argent has no sessions or element refs. The driver gives each node of argent's `ui-tree` a ref, converts its normalized frames to points or pixels, and taps the node's centre. A fill taps the end of the field, waits for focus, sends one backspace per character, then types. - Before a tap, long press, or fill, the driver waits for the tree to stop changing (200 ms, 600 ms around the keyboard). XCTest waits for idle on its own; without this wait, WebKit dropped a tap sent while the keyboard was closing. `app.open()` waits for the first screen plus 500 ms of stillness, because a Flutter app lists its controls before it takes taps. - Device commands argent has no tool for throw `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before anything reaches the device: `clearState`, `closeApp`, `alert`, the clipboard, network, location, appearance, biometrics, the keychain, hover, and comparable screenshots. A device provider (EAS, Limrun) is `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load. - The argent driver refuses text containing `{{secret:NAME}}` with `POLICY_DENIED`. argent's tool server fills that placeholder from the host's environment and `.env` files, which would bypass `authorizeSecretFill` and the redaction ledger. A secret that isn't printable ASCII is refused rather than typed through the device clipboard. - The replay cache keys on `app.identity`, not the driver. The mobile benchmark's argent targets (`E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_DRIVER=argent`) record under a `-argent` identity, and the docs tell users to do the same. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[AgentDeviceSurface] --> C{DeviceClient} C -- "driver: 'agent-device'" --> A[agent-device client] C -- "driver: 'argent'" --> R[argent.ts] --> T[argent tool server] ``` Known limits, documented in `docs/reference/mobile.mdx#the-argent-driver`: - argent's Android tree has no role description, so `getByRole('tab')` finds nothing on a React Native tab. - Two argent installs driving one simulator read empty trees. - On one Android emulator, agent-device's snapshot helper and argent's devtools conflict. - On the emulator, Gboard treats argent's taps as a stylus; set `stylus_handwriting_enabled` to 0. - A call that times out is abandoned only on our side; argent's tool server keeps running it. The per-call budget grows with the length of the text, so a long fill doesn't hit it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) and an API 36 Android emulator, on the built packages packed into a scratch project. The example apps, `deterministic.e2e.ts` then `agentic.e2e.ts` (model `chatgpt('gpt-6-luna')`): | | iOS (argent) | Android (argent) | agent-device, deterministic | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | with-swiftui | 3/3, 2/2 | | iOS 3/3 | | with-expo | 3/3, 2/2 | 3/3, 2/2 | iOS 3/3, Android 3/3 | | with-compose | | 3/3, 2/2 | Android 3/3 | | with-kotlin-multiplatform | 3/3, 2/2 | 3/3, 2/2 | iOS 3/3, Android 3/3 | | with-flutter | 3/3, 2/2 | 3/3, 2/2 | iOS 3/3, Android 3/3 | That table is from before the self-review fixes. After them, every deterministic suite above passed again on argent. The agentic reruns then hit ChatGPT returning "Our servers are currently overloaded" on most `agent.assert` calls. In those runs every `agent.act` and its paired deterministic check passed, and swiftui, expo (iOS), and flutter passed in full. Mobile benchmark, deterministic suite, argent. Tests that use only the unsupported commands were excluded: | | passed | failed | | --- | --- | --- | | iOS | 44 | 2: `clearState` (unsupported), `setOrientation` (also fails on agent-device on this Mac) | | Android | 44 | 3: `getByRole('tab')`, plus two `refusals` tests that rely on the excluded `clearState` test leaving the app on its home list | agent-device on the same iOS simulator: 53 passed, 1 failed (`setOrientation`). Testbed: 77 passed, 1 skipped. Videos: the greeting test on argent, iOS SwiftUI then Android Compose. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25dd040c-668b-4bee-91a7-2e04697b8380 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd228616-4558-456c-b5a7-193eafab3b63

title: docs(skills): route each job to one reference from the e2e skill
body:
Agents reading the `e2e` skill on main often never reached the reference for the job. "Open the app" and "check my change in the running app" went to Claude Code's built-in `run` skill, because the description never mentioned driving the live app over `e2e mcp`. Following [Anthropic's skill best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices#progressive-disclosure-patterns), this keeps one skill and adds a decision tree at the top.

- `skills/e2e/SKILL.md` opens with a "Start here" table: one row per job, each sending the agent to one reference. The old `## Workflow` is now `## Workflow: writing a test`, since that is all it covers.
- The description is in third person and says what the skill does and when to use it. It adds checking a change in the running app, screenshots and video, and QA or bug bash requests (681 chars, under the 1024 limit).
- Every reference over 100 lines opens with a `## Contents` list of its sections, so an agent that reads only the head of a file still sees what the rest holds. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/skill.test.ts` checks the list against the headings.
- References stay one level deep: `agent.md` points to topic `setup` instead of linking `setup.md#...`. That link also pointed nowhere when `npx e2e guide` or `e2e://guide/<topic>` printed it.
- `mcp.md` gives the qualified tool name (`mcp__e2e__open_session`) and says to use the `e2e` server's tool when another server offers the same name. Its setup section says a session needs the project's config, so an agent in a project without one starts at topic `setup` instead of hitting `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI: `npx e2e guide` prints the new overview with the table, `npx e2e guide <topic>` prints each of the eight references with its `## Contents` list, and `guide agent` shows the `setup` pointer.
- Routing eval: a local script (not in this PR) copies `examples/with-vite` to a scratch directory with the skill installed and runs `claude -p --setting-sources project` or `codex exec --ignore-user-config` on eight typical requests. A case passes when the agent loads the skill and opens the expected `references/<topic>.md`. One run per request:

| Agent / model | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code, default model | 5/8 | 8/8 |
| Claude Code, Sonnet | 3/8 | 6/8 |
| Codex, default model | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| Codex, gpt-6.1-sol | 8/8 | 8/8 |

On main, Claude Code missed both live-app requests (sent to the built-in `run` skill) and "Bug bash this app". Codex routed correctly on both builds, but on main it opened 10 references across 16 runs that it did not need (for example `bug-bash`, `explore`, and `mcp` together for "Bug bash this app"); on this branch it opened 3. A rerun of the default Claude model on this branch scored 7/8: for the `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` request it answered from the rules in `SKILL.md` without opening `debugging.md`, so expect some variation from run to run.

---
Written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5); reviewed by Codex (gpt-6-astra).

title: fix(limrun): pin agent-device 0.21.25 to match mobile
body:
## Why

main is red since #1059. It bumped `packages/mobile` to agent-device 0.21.25 and rewrote the lockfile, dropping the 0.21.22 snapshot. `packages/limrun` (#988, merged after #1059 branched) still pinned 0.21.22, so pnpm never links it and every workspace build dies in limrun:

```
src/driver.ts(1,71): error TS2307: Cannot find module 'agent-device'
src/heartbeat.ts(1,41): error TS2307: Cannot find module 'agent-device'
```

## What

- limrun: agent-device 0.21.22 -> 0.21.25, lockfile importer updated
- limrun: agent-device moves from an exact-pinned peerDependency to a regular `dependency`. limrun imports it directly (lease allocation in `driver.ts`, renewal in `heartbeat.ts`), but users should not have to install and lockstep a third-party pin. Identical pins dedupe to one copy; the runtime version assert in `daemon.ts` stays as the safety net.
- README, docs and the with-limrun example drop the manual agent-device install step
- changeset: limrun patch

## Verified

- `pnpm run build` across the workspace: green
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/limrun test`: 14 passed
- `check:peer-ranges`, `check:install-scripts`, `docs:check`, `lint`: green

title: feat(eas): manage sessions through Expo's REST API and report the client
body:
- `@e2e-dev/eas` creates, polls, and stops EAS Simulators sessions through Expo's REST API (`/v2/device-run-sessions`) instead of GraphQL.
- `create` sends `client: "@e2e-dev/eas@<version>"`. EAS stores it as the session's `request_client`, so Expo can see which sessions this package starts ([expo/universe#31970](https://github.com/expo/universe/pull/31970)).
- `stop` is one request. EAS now cancels the job of a session that is still queued ([expo/universe#32217](https://github.com/expo/universe/pull/32217)), so the provider no longer calls `cancelJobRun` itself.
- `state` reads `status` and `remoteConfig` from `GET /:id`. The session status replaces the job status the GraphQL query read: `new` and `queued` mean queued, `starting` means a worker is booting it, and `stopped` and `errored` mean ended. EAS sets these from the session's job ([expo/universe#31475](https://github.com/expo/universe/pull/31475)).
- The `EasSessions` interface is unchanged, so `provider.ts` does not change.

| Call | Before (GraphQL) | After (REST) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create | `createDeviceRunSession` | `POST /v2/device-run-sessions` |
| state | `deviceRunSessions.byId` | `GET /v2/device-run-sessions/:id` |
| stop | `ensureDeviceRunSessionStopped`, then `cancelJobRun` when queued | `POST /v2/device-run-sessions/:id/stop` |

## Merge order

Draft until both server PRs are deployed to `api.expo.dev`:

- [expo/universe#31475](https://github.com/expo/universe/pull/31475) sets the session status to `queued` and `starting` from its job. Without it, the status stays `new` while the session boots, so this package reports every boot as queued and never starts the 15-minute boot limit.
- [expo/universe#32217](https://github.com/expo/universe/pull/32217) makes REST stop cancel a job that is still queued. Without it, a session stopped while queued still starts later and bills the account.

## Verified

Ran it locally: no - the session status sync and queued-job cancel need expo/universe#31475 and expo/universe#32217 on `api.expo.dev`, and a live run starts billed EAS Simulators sessions.
- `packages/eas/tests/unit/eas.test.ts` runs against a fake of the REST API (request paths, lowercase enum values, `{ errors: [{ code, message }] }` with HTTP 400, `NOT_FOUND_ERROR` on stop).
- A fresh-context review checked the request body, response fields, and error shape against the server's REST router.

title: feat(cli): add e2e run --watch
body:
`e2e run --watch` (`-w`): run, then run again on save or on a key, the way vitest does.

- A saved test file (matched by the config `tests` globs) reruns whole in place of the positionals. A saved source file beside the tests (`.ts`, `.js`, `.json` under the glob directories or next to the config) or a saved config reruns the current selection. Changes during a run queue and run next, merged.
- Keys on a TTY, vitest's table: `a`/enter all (filters cleared), `r` current pattern, `f` failed (via `--last-failed`, wherever the failure is), `u` update snapshots, `p` file prompt, `t` title regex prompt, `h`, `q`. Any key during a run cancels it, a second one forces it. Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D, escape interrupt and end the session; Ctrl-Z suspends the job.
- Every iteration is one complete `run()`, so each writes its report and tears the app down. Each iteration passes `freshGraph` so config and collection re-evaluate the project's own modules, and a saved helper is what the next run collects (`packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts`).
- Watch roots are the literal prefix of each glob, recursive, plus the config directory flat. A root-level glob watches the root flat plus each non-dot, non-`node_modules` directory, so Linux never registers an inotify watch per file under `node_modules`. A watcher `error` drops that root with a notice instead of crashing.
- What the run writes (`output`, `cache.dir`) is never a change, so a non-dot output inside a watched directory does not retrigger the run; a config that moves them rebuilds the watcher.
- The config file and its directory are watched before the first run, so a save during it is queued; the test directories come from the config and are watched once it has loaded.
- Refused in CI and with `--reporter json` (exit 2); a config-level `json` reporter ends the session after the first run. Without a TTY on stdin only file changes rerun. Exit code on quit is the last finished run's.
- Ctrl-C arrives as a keypress in raw mode, so `SignalLadder.escalate()` is now public and the keyboard feeds the same ladder.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> run
    run --> wait: run finished
    run --> run: pending change or key, merged
    run --> [*]: Ctrl-C (ladder), config json reporter
    wait --> run: file / source / config saved, a r f u enter
    wait --> prompt: p t
    prompt --> run: answer (r)
    prompt --> wait: escape
    wait --> [*]: q, Ctrl-C
    run --> wait: key cancels (interrupt, then force)
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run -w tests/todos.e2e.ts` in tmux. Keys `h`, enter, `r`, space mid-run (cancel), `t` + `adds`, `u`, `q`:

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
Waiting for file changes...
  press h to show help, press q to quit
  press a, enter to rerun all tests
  press r to rerun current pattern tests
  press f to rerun only failed tests
  press u to update snapshot
  press p to filter by a filename
  press t to filter by a test name regex pattern
  press q to quit
 RERUN  all tests x2
      Tests  7 passed (7)
 RERUN  current pattern x3
      Tests  7 passed (7)
 RERUN  all tests x4
interrupted: stopping the running test and tearing down (interrupt again to force)
      Tests  1 interrupted | 4 passed | 2 skipped (7)
run cancelled
◆  Filter by a test name regex pattern (empty clears the filter)
 RERUN  current pattern (title: adds) x5
      Tests  1 passed (1)
 RERUN  update snapshot (title: adds) x6
      Tests  1 passed (1)
EXIT=0
```

- Saved `tests/helpers.ts`, then `mkdir tests/new` with a new test file:

```text
 RERUN  tests/helpers.ts x2
      Tests  7 passed (7)
 RERUN  tests/new/x.e2e.ts x3
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- Ctrl-Z then `fg` then `r`; a new failing file, then `f`; `t` then Ctrl-C inside the prompt ends the session with no process left, port free:

```text
zsh: suspended  node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run -w tests/todos.e2e.ts
 RERUN  current pattern x2
 RERUN  tests/zzfail.e2e.ts x3
      Tests  1 failed | 0 passed (1)
 RERUN  failed tests x4
   × zz fails 75ms
◆  Filter by a test name regex pattern (empty clears the filter)
■  Filter by a test name regex pattern (empty clears the filter)
```

- `--output tests/results` (the run writing under the watched directory): one run, no rerun, `q` exits 0. Config touched 4s into the first run: `RERUN config changed x2` after it.
- Ctrl-C idle exits 0; Ctrl-C mid-run exits 130; non-TTY (`< /dev/null | cat`) reruns on touch, prints no key hint, SIGINT exits 0; `CI=1` and `--reporter list,json` exit 2 before anything runs; 13 reruns in one session leave no `MaxListenersExceededWarning`.
- Not covered: Linux `fs.watch` recursive is exercised only by the unit tests with a fake watcher; macOS here.

title: fix(bench): compare run exit statuses alongside test outcomes
body: The A/B benchmark records each run's exit code but omits it from its compared counters. A failed suite hook or reporter can therefore disappear from the comparison when test attempts match. This includes the run exit code in the existing counter comparison, exposing stable differences and unstable statuses without changing test identity or timing. Full `pnpm check` passes, including workspace build/typechecks and repository checks. The19class-member findings printed by fallow also occur on the unchanged baseline and do not fail that command. Separate agent review passed on this exact revision; ADR included. No browser/model calls were needed.

title: fix(bench): report instability independently on both builds
body: When both builds produce inconsistent step sequences, the A/B report currently reports only baseline instability and omits candidate instability. This evaluates each side independently so both unstable builds appear in the changed-behavior report. The new regression fails against the frozen baseline; all 13 benchmark tests pass with the fix. Script TypeScript checking and full `pnpm check` passed. A separate agent reviewed the exact revision and independently reproduced the baseline failure.
