title: fix(cache): report eviction only after store deletion succeeds
body:
A rejected custom cache-store deletion currently leaves the entry in place while the step report claims `write: evicted`. This reports eviction only after deletion resolves in both the direct eviction and settlement paths, preserving the existing best-effort behavior on a rejected store operation.

Regressions reproduce false eviction claims on the unchanged baseline, verify the retained cache bytes, and check that subsequent confirmed writes still proceed. All 79 cache tests passed without filtering, and full `pnpm check` passed on the final revision. Separate agent review passed for that exact revision. The ADR, changeset and cache guide update are included. Related cache-outcome reporting discussion: #939. No browser or model calls were needed.

The default FileCacheStore now suppresses only ENOENT on unlink: other failures remain observable to the best-effort eviction caller. A real non-root POSIX permission-denied regression failed on the previous revision and passes on this correction; retained bytes and absent eviction outcome are asserted, with a missing-entry control. Candidate: 80 cache tests and full pnpm check pass. Renewed separate review independently ran 124 impacted tests without failures or skips. The permission test skips Windows/root and restores permissions in finally. ADR updated in the same reviewed revision.

title: fix(mobile): bound each input by its budget
body:
## What and why

- The mobile engine bounded each agent-device call only by `operation.signal`. The harness aborts that signal with the attempt, never at `timeoutMs`, so an input that outlived `actionTimeout` held the step until the test timeout.
- The `OperationContext.signal` docs said it also aborts "when the operation budget is spent". It doesn't for locator operations. The web engine enforces `timeoutMs` itself (`packages/web/src/operation-budget.ts`). The doc comment now says so.
- `InputBudget.send` (`packages/mobile/src/support.ts`) wraps each device command that sends input. That covers node actions, the screen swipe, point actions, typing, keys, `back`, and the keyboard dismissal with its gesture fallbacks.
  - **No budget left:** nothing is sent, and the result is `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`.
  - **Sent but no answer in time:** `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`, which the runner never repeats. Web's `inputCutOff` does the same.
  - **Little budget left:** the input is still sent and gets 250 ms to answer.
  - **A hold longer than the budget left:** a long press, or a timed swipe, that holds at least as long as the budget left is refused before it is sent. It fails as `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, naming the hold and the time left.
  - **Several commands in one input:** a focus tap then a keystroke is sent one command at a time, so no keystroke follows a tap that used the budget up.
  - **Abandoned commands:** a timed-out command stays tracked as in flight until it settles, so the next attempt still waits for it.
- Reads stay unbounded, as on main. That covers observe, locate, and the relocation before a tap. Bounding them broke this PR's first CI run: a locator poll's last iOS snapshot was cut off at the deadline and read as `ACTION_FAILED` instead of `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`.
- `docs/mobile.mdx` › Troubleshooting says what an action that outlives its timeout does.
- Hung reads still hold the step until the test timeout, as on main: #1099.
- No runtime change to `e2e`, so mobile's peer floor stays.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **Setup:** iOS simulator (iPhone 18 Pro Max, iOS 27), a scratch project on the built packages, `com.apple.Preferences`, `actionTimeout: 4_000`.
- **Long press:** `getByTestId('com.apple.settings.general').longPress({ duration: 8_000 })`.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| step passes after 8.7 s (agent-device `longpress ok 8685ms`) | `73279167`: refused before sending (no `longpress` request): `ACTION_FAILED: longPress holds for 8000 ms, but only 616 ms of its timeout are left; raise the timeout or shorten the hold` |

  Before the hold refusal, `f1befc86` sent it and failed at 4.0 s: `ACTION_FAILED: longPress timed out before the device answered; its input may have been dispatched`.

- **Missing locator:** `getByText('No such row').tap({ timeout: 3_000 })` reports `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` on the branch, which is the CI regression fixed.
- **Unit tests:**
  - every input entry, hung, times out as `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`;
  - a slow relocation that spends the budget sends no press;
  - a focus tap that answers past the budget sends no keystroke;
  - a timed-out tap keeps the next attempt waiting until it settles;
  - a long press longer than its timeout is refused unsent;
  - each of these fails when its mechanism is removed.
- **CI:** `ios deterministic` and `android deterministic` (the mobile benchmark's deterministic suites) pass.
- **Not verified on a device:** the agent-origin path. No mobile agent suite runs on a fork PR. Near a step deadline it behaves like web: a tap left with a small budget gets 250 ms to answer.
- **Review:** five fresh-context review rounds, cubic, and okwasniewski. Every finding was fixed or answered.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

The `e2e/engine` change is the `OperationContext.signal` doc comment only. The behavior it describes is unchanged.

title: Hosted sessions: expose a versioned redacted debug report and artifact manifest
body:
## Context
Non-blocking follow-up to [hosted sessions PR 980](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980) and [session API discussion 992](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/992).

We are embedding e2e in an existing Appwright/Playwright fixture graph, borrowing its already-prepared device. The consumer owns reporting, publication and a hosted debug viewer; this request does not ask e2e to build or host that viewer.

The current [session API](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ba973a10ed9582335f9bea8dd5e018948262e150/packages/e2e/src/run/open-session.ts) exposes `steps()`, `artifactsDir` and `tracePath`. The [host trace writer](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ba973a10ed9582335f9bea8dd5e018948262e150/packages/e2e/src/run/host-trace.ts) already builds a report internally, but publishes Markdown. A viewer should not parse Markdown, guess artifact paths from IDs, scan arbitrary files or import private runner internals.

## Proposal
Expose a documented, versioned, immutable debug/report export for a closed session. Prefer reusing the existing report schema. API names such as `session.report()` or `session.exportDebugBundle()` are illustrative, not a prescribed new schema.

Include:
- Run/attempt/target identity, final SDK outcome, step timings/status/errors and recorded events.
- Available redacted reasoning excerpts and tool turns; do not promise unavailable provider reasoning.
- An artifact manifest with IDs, kind/media type, safe relative paths, and step/observation associations.
- Redacted semantic evidence where recorded. Missing/withheld evidence must be explicit.

The consumer can then serialize/upload an allowlisted bundle and render it independently. No automatic publication.

## Acceptance / boundaries
- Export agrees with the hosted trace and is available after close, including failed/timed-out sessions.
- Artifact references resolve without directory scans or filename-based provenance guesses.
- Existing secret redaction, pixel masking/taint restrictions and retention policies remain authoritative; no raw native XML, external error causes or arbitrary consumer files are exported.
- Export is deterministic/idempotent, versioned and documented; tests cover redaction, artifact association, missing evidence and failed close.
- No new device ownership, fixture graph or test-runner requirement.

Workflow: SDK redacted attempt → public report/manifest → consumer publisher → consumer debug viewer.

## Related follow-ups
- External outcomes: #1075 (correct final report status and retention).
- Debug checkpoints: #1077 (richer step/observation evidence).
- Always-on agent pixel policy: #1076 (separate from debug capture).

title: Hosted sessions: accept external runner outcomes and retry metadata
body:
## Context
Non-blocking follow-up to [PR 980](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980) and [discussion 992](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/992).

The external runner intentionally owns test execution, expected failures, retries and provider/device cleanup. However, an external Playwright assertion can fail while every e2e operation succeeds. The SDK's trace can then show a passing session, and SDK-owned retain-on-failure evidence can disagree with the authoritative test outcome.

The current [public session close API](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ba973a10ed9582335f9bea8dd5e018948262e150/packages/e2e/src/run/open-session.ts) accepts no external outcome.

## Proposal
Offer a documented way to supply a bounded external outcome before finalizing the session, e.g. a close option or separate finalization method. Exact API is open for discussion.

Useful metadata:
- Actual status (passed/failed/timed out/skipped/interrupted, with documented mapping).
- Expected status or expected-failure annotation.
- External retry index and a stable external test identity when supplied.

Do not accept or retain arbitrary raw Error objects/causes. Preserve SDK failures separately; an external passing status must never erase a soft assertion, abandoned operation, timeout or cleanup failure.

## Acceptance / boundaries
- An external-only failure is visible in the trace/export, with its source distinguished from SDK failures.
- Evidence retention uses a documented effective-outcome policy, including expected failures.
- Independent external retries remain separate sessions; this does not add an SDK retry loop or move ownership out of Playwright.
- Close remains idempotent and cleanup cannot be skipped by outcome reporting.
- Tests cover external-only failure, timeout, skip, expected failure, retry identity and SDK failure plus external pass.

## Related follow-ups
- Structured debug export: #1074 should carry the effective outcome and external retry identity.

title: Agents: opt-in safe pixel evidence on every agent step with per-call overrides
body:
## Context
Non-blocking capability request related to [PR 980](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980) and the consumer-hosted mobile integration.

At [the current API](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ba973a10ed9582335f9bea8dd5e018948262e150/docs/reference/agent.mdx), `act` is adaptive: it reads the tree and requests screenshots when needed; the `screenshot()` tool enables fresh images after later actions in that step. `act` explicitly does not accept `vision`. Judgments (`assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`) support per-call `vision` and default to tree evidence.

For selected mobile suites we want an explicit policy that starts each acting flow with permitted pixel evidence, rather than relying on the model to decide to request its first image.

## Proposal
Consider an opt-in named-agent and/or hosted-session policy for always including safe tree-plus-pixel evidence:
- Acting flows: a fresh permitted image for the first model turn and refreshed evidence after actions, consistent with the existing pixel-tool loop.
- Judgments: opt-in defaults for `assert`, `waitFor`, and `extract`.
- Explicit per-call overrides, so individual steps can remain tree-only.

Exact option names/scope are a design question. This is not a suggestion to pass today's unsupported `vision: true` to `act`.

## Acceptance / boundaries
- Defaults remain unchanged: adaptive acting and tree-only judgments.
- Apply to model-backed agent observations, not indiscriminate model calls for every deterministic locator operation.
- Never override engine pixel withholding, masking proof, secret-fill taint or provider image support. Record safe degradation; existing strict pixel-only judgment semantics remain intact.
- Custom executors must explicitly support the relevant capability; do not change their inputs silently.
- Report whether pixels were actually used, degradation reasons, image bytes and model/token usage.
- Document latency/cost/context budgets and cache/replay compatibility; do not introduce unsafe action retries.
- Artifact capture/publication is separately configurable. Debug checkpoints must not require this mode.

## Related follow-ups
- Debug checkpoints: #1077 separates saved evidence from model input.
- Structured debug export: #1074 carries usage/degradation evidence for a consumer viewer.

title: Debug evidence: opt-in observation checkpoints independent of model vision
body:
## Context
Non-blocking debugging follow-up to [PR 980](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980).

We want a reliable before/after timeline in a consumer-owned hosted viewer. Taking screenshots asynchronously from `onStep` can capture a later screen and associate it with the wrong action; [onStep is a nonblocking progress feed](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ba973a10ed9582335f9bea8dd5e018948262e150/packages/e2e/src/run/open-session.ts), not an awaited screenshot hook.

Saving debug evidence and sending pixels to a model are different decisions.

## Proposal
Provide an opt-in, SDK-owned checkpoint policy (or a documented read-only observation hook) that associates safely captured evidence with the actual step/agent observation. Reuse observations already captured where possible.

Useful evidence:
- Stable step/observation IDs and capture timestamps.
- Redacted semantic snapshot/diff and, when proven safe, a masked screenshot.
- Selected target node/geometry or performed point when available, for highlighting.
- Explicit reasons when image evidence is unsupported, withheld, tainted or unavailable.

Define whether checkpoints cover public steps, inner agent actions and cache replay; do not silently equate these.

## Acceptance / boundaries
- Before/after evidence cannot be attributed to a later action.
- Debug capture can be enabled without enabling model vision or additional model calls.
- No consumer hook starts a second device session or changes engine ownership.
- Keep masking, secret-fill taint, cancellation/deadline handling and retention authoritative. No raw XML or unvalidated screenshots.
- Bound capture frequency/storage and document overhead; default behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests cover consecutive actions, cache replay, cancellation and sensitive fills.

## Related follow-ups
- Structured debug export: #1074 provides the artifact/observation manifest for consumer viewers.
- Agent pixel policy: #1076 is independent; enabling debug checkpoints must not enable model vision.

body: ## What and why - Opt into awaited, bounded before/after capture attempts for selected hosted top-level public steps, independent of model vision and the nonblocking progress callback. Own and validate policy before asynchronous opening. - Mask formatter-owned scalar fields before clipping; omit historical selections only from checkpoints. Preserve default model/executor observations. - Bind pixels at capture start and JSON after final masking. Validate canonical unavailable records against original SDK boundaries before the first write and again before store handoff. Opaque providers withhold content before observation; fixed null-capture facts remain separate from content permission. ```ts const session = await host.openSession({ name: 'checkout', debugCheckpoints: { pixels: true, maxSteps: 10, maxBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024, captureTimeout: 500, retain: 'retain-on-failure', }, }); await session.close(); const checkpoints = session.checkpoints(); ``` The example overrides the unchanged defaults: 50 steps, 8 MiB, 1000 ms, pixels off, retain-on-failure. Addresses #1077. Follow-up to [merged hosted sessions PR](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980), rebased onto main at `4b4b29727dde17eb135b030c031c10607a2d6299`. This branch contains only this follow-up's scope. ## Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Opted-in before or after boundary] --> B{Prospective content proof?} B -->|Yes| C[Bounded capture with original ticket] B -->|No| D[Fixed unavailable facts without capture] C --> E[Operation and required closing lifecycle] D --> E E --> F[Retention and final source proof] F --> G[Validate bytes before first write] G --> H[Recheck after read before store] H --> I[Copied checkpoint view] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, at `05d0f8dc3ad9d48a474c29d71b316ee4e819f4e1`. One feature commit; pinned base unchanged. - `pnpm check` and builds passed, including emitted declarations, SDK assertions, schemas and docs. Units: 2,918 passed, 2 existing skips. Owning selected gate: 604 passed. - Parent gate: 510 passed. Independent 13-path correction review: 746 passed, plus 157 overlapping forced-UUID collision checks and a no-emit typecheck. Counts overlap, not additive coverage totals. - Public async-mutation/getter controls verify one owned, validated policy snapshot before engine opening, without freezing caller objects. Invalid policies reject before engine start. - Retention assertions now run outside swallowed callbacks; an independent mutant exposes the old oracle weakness. Windows separator normalization has positive/negative controls, not native Windows validation. - Viewport schema dependencies match capture identities. Fewer than 8 remaining bytes suppress pixels because even the PNG signature cannot fit; 1/7/8-byte controls verify the boundary. This is not a compressed-size or engine peak-memory estimate. Retained-content quota, 200-record ceiling and 2,048 private positions per capture remain distinct limits. - Built CLI Chromium: 15 files, 77 passed, 1 existing skip. Original custody, mask-before-caps, canonical unavailable facts, monotonic secrecy, retention and whole-JSON/first-byte privacy guards remain implemented. No ID filtering or weakened collision assertions. - All eight Cubic findings have published, attributed replies and resolved threads. Current independent review covered the correction delta and critical callers, not exhaustive historical approval. Private composition predates these corrections and is not current-head public interoperability proof. - Exact-head GitHub evidence: [docs](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38486473864), [spec](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38486473782), [web benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38486473736) and [deterministic mobile](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38486473815) gates all passed. Secret-dependent fork jobs are skipped, not passes. Cubic automatic re-review completed on this exact head with zero issues across all 13 correction files, and no threads remain open. No manual bot trigger was sent. Human approval and consumer/device validation remain separate. - Capture uses the existing deadline; unavailable facts may be recorded without observation. Not an inner-action/poll/fixture/CLI/MCP/replay timeline. Synthetic faults and Chromium are not native-device/cloud/live-model/physical-disk/backend/adoption proof. title: fix(verification-skill): interview can initialize projects with no supported user interface
body:
## Summary

Page: `skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md`.

What is wrong: the interview tells an agent with no existing e2e files to run `npx e2e init` without making a supported web, mobile, or HTTP target a prerequisite. Its only unsupported-project stop instruction names native desktop apps. A CLI-only project fits none of the listed targets, yet reaches the unconditional initialization instruction. That instruction adds browser-test configuration, dependencies, MCP registrations, and ignore entries before there is anything e2e can drive.

This is a problem with the generator's instructions, not a request for a CLI engine or a claim that `e2e init` should detect project types. The existing unsupported-native-desktop stop and the rule to generate only from observed behavior establish that an unsupported project should receive a stop result rather than an invented verification recipe.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read the generator skill at the source baseline below. In section 1, compare the Surface row with the e2e state row. The former gives a stop only for native desktop apps; the latter says, "Nothing there means `npx e2e init` first". There is no general unsupported-project branch before section 2.
2. Create a disposable directory with only a `README.md` documenting `python3 hello.py example` and this `hello.py`. It has no browser UI, mobile app, or HTTP listener.

```python
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("name")
args = parser.parse_args()
print(f"Hello, {args.name}!")
```

3. Run `python3 hello.py example`; it prints `Hello, example!`.
4. Execute the e2e-state instruction in that directory using the latest stable package. `--yes` selects the documented noninteractive defaults and skips dependency installation.

```sh
E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx -y e2e@latest init --yes
```

5. Inspect the added files and generated `app.url`. The command succeeds and creates a browser target even though the project has no HTTP service.

This reproduces the initialization instruction's consequences. I did not run an autonomous agent through the entire unmodified generator skill, so the report does not claim that every agent will initialize this project. The missing applicability guard is visible in the instructions themselves.

## Expected behavior

The generator should establish that e2e can exercise a real user path before running project-writing setup. For a CLI, library, or batch project with no web, mobile, or HTTP target, it should stop with the observed reason, say that no verification skill was generated, and leave the checkout unchanged. A desktop app whose browser build is only a static notice because its features require native IPC should receive the same unsupported result; the presence of frontend source alone does not supply a drivable user path.

This follows the skill's existing native-desktop stop rule and "Generate from what you observed" rule. API-only projects remain supported by the explicitly documented `app` and `fetch` approach.

## Actual behavior

The e2e-state instruction is unconditional for a project without e2e files. The interview has no general stop result for an unsupported project, and section 5 describes only a generated skill's handover.

In one local disposable CLI fixture, the initialization command exited 0 and reported:

```text
Created package.json
Created e2e.config.ts
Created tests/example.e2e.ts
Created .agents/skills/e2e/ (9 files)
Linked .claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e
Created .mcp.json (e2e mcp server)
Created .cursor/mcp.json (e2e mcp server)
Updated .gitignore (10 entries)
```

The generated package includes `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, `ai`, and `zod` dev dependencies and a `test:e2e` script. Its config uses `web()` with `process.env.APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'`. The fixture still only has its stdout CLI; initialization did not establish an app at that URL. No dependency installation, browser run, or generated verification-skill proof was performed.

## Evidence

- Expected source: the generator's section 1 Surface row explicitly stops for an unsupported native desktop app, and its Rules require generating from observed behavior. See the [source skill](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md#L24-L42).
- Failure source: section 1 e2e-state row directs initialization on absence of e2e files without a general unsupported-target prerequisite; sections 2 and 5 supply only generation and successful handover branches. The local command output above establishes the file-writing consequence of that instruction.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: incomplete
- Missing fact: the behavior of an autonomous agent executing the full unmodified generator skill on this fixture without an added stop hint was not observed.

The primary violation evidence is the missing applicability guard in the instructions. Local verification reproduced the quoted initialization instruction's writes; it did not execute a complete autonomous generator invocation.

## Restoration check

Invoke the generator on a CLI-only fixture with no e2e installation and no web, mobile, or HTTP target. It should give an evidence-based unsupported result before initialization or any other project write, state that it generated no skill, and leave every project file unchanged. Apply the same check to a desktop frontend whose only browser output is a native-runtime notice. As a control, a real HTTP-only service should still take the documented supported API path; rejecting every project without interactive browser controls would not restore this contract.

## Runtime or environment

Source baseline: current default branch `main`, commit `fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f`. Stable npm package tested: `e2e` 0.20.0, confirmed with npm's `latest` tag and `npx -y e2e@latest --version`. Runtime: Node.js v26.10.0 on macOS arm64. The generator is installed separately from the repository through `npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill create-verification-skill`; it is not bundled in the npm package.

## Additional context

Suggested wording: make supported-target selection a prerequisite for initialization and generation. For an unsupported project, define a stopped handover that reports the observed entry point, why the existing engines cannot drive it, and that no files were written. The exact organization of the instructions is up to maintainers.

The reference can be read without initializing the target project: `npx -y e2e@latest guide setup` succeeded from a scratch directory. This supplies a practical read-only route while investigating applicability.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: provisional
- Impact basis: Following the interview's initialization instruction on an unsupported CLI adds unrelated browser-test files and project configuration. The writes are reversible. The full unmodified agent workflow and how often agents follow this branch remain unobserved.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Inspect the real user entry point first and stop before init when no supported target exists. The standalone guide command was verified without initializing the target project.

title: fix(skill): bug-bash config template preserves exclusions that hide repro tests
body:
## Summary

The bug-bash config template says it includes the project's tests plus repro tests, but it cannot select a repro when the valid base config excludes that directory. The inherited negative glob wins over the appended positive glob. A developer following the template receives `NO_TESTS` instead of verifying the repro. This is a documentation bug in the template, not a request to change exclusion semantics.

Page: `skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md`, the config template in step 1. The `create-verification-skill` generator directs generated verification skills to this topic.

## Steps to reproduce

I ran the following with the published packages stated under Runtime or environment. No app, browser, or model is needed for `list`.

1. Install the runner and web engine in a disposable project.
2. Create this valid base config and the separate bug-bash config using the template's exact `tests` expression.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';

export default {
  tests: ['tests/**/*.e2e.ts', '!tests/bugbash/**'],
  targets: [{ name: 'web', engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000' } }],
} satisfies E2EConfig;

// e2e.bugbash.config.ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import base from './e2e.config.ts';

const shared: E2EConfig = base;
export default {
  ...shared,
  tests: [shared.tests ?? 'tests/**/*.e2e.ts', 'tests/bugbash/**/*.e2e.ts'].flat(),
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

3. Add these test files.

```ts
// tests/smoke.e2e.ts
import { test } from 'e2e';
test('smoke control', async () => {});

// tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from 'e2e';
test('cart total repro', { tags: ['bugbash'] }, async () => {
  expect(1).toBe(2);
});
```

4. Run these commands. I invoked the installed CLI directly with `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`; the commands below use the equivalent project CLI invocation.

```sh
npx e2e list --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts
npx e2e list tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts
```

5. As a control, use the same base target and tests with `tests: ['tests/**/*.e2e.ts']` in a separate config, then list that config. Both files are selected.

## Expected behavior

The documented bug-bash config selects the repro tests it adds and the project's tests needed for setup sessions. A base config may legitimately exclude intentionally failing repros from normal runs. The separate bug-bash recipe must account for that valid input, or state an explicit supported limitation and provide a working recipe for it.

## Actual behavior

The first command exits 0 and prints only the smoke control:

```text
tests/smoke.e2e.ts › smoke control [web]
```

The second command exits 2:

```text
NO_TESTS: no test file matched tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts (excluded by the tests entry "!tests/bugbash/**"); the config globs discovered tests/smoke.e2e.ts; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this
```

The control command exits 0 and prints both files:

```text
tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts › cart total repro [web] #bugbash
tests/smoke.e2e.ts › smoke control [web]
```

This verifies selection only. I did not run the deliberately failing test or start the app. The fixture uses the template's exact `tests` expression with a valid base config. I did not execute the template's model or credential settings.

## Evidence

- Expected source: The [bug-bash template](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md#L82-L83) says "The project's tests, so a repro can use its setup tests' sessions, plus the repro tests from step 6." The [setup config table](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/e2e/references/setup.md#L137) explicitly supports leading `!` exclusions.
- Failure source: The published CLI's `list` outputs and exit statuses above. The [glob implementation](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/e2e/src/internal/globs.ts#L81-L97) confirms exclusions apply regardless of order.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

## Runtime or environment

- Current default branch checked: `fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f`.
- Latest published stable packages checked and installed: e2e 0.20.0 and `@e2e-dev/web` 0.14.0.
- Probe runtime: macOS arm64, Node v26.10.0. No browser, app service, model, or saved login participated.
- The generator is installed from the repository rather than shipped in the runner package. Its current topic link and the published bug-bash topic lead to the same template expression.

## Restoration check

With the inline base config's repro exclusion, the documented bug-bash recipe must list the smoke control and the repro, and listing the repro by path must succeed. Normal selection through the base config must continue to omit the repro. Preserve the project's setup test selection when adapting the separate config; do not weaken the runner's documented exclusion semantics to make the example pass.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The supported base configuration makes the documentation's repro-verification path fail with `NO_TESTS`. The failure is limited to inherited exclusions matching the repro directory; the ordinary suite can still run.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Remove the matching inherited exclusion in the separate bug-bash config, as verified by the control. Alternatively, the topic already documents tagging repros and excluding that tag in gating commands, avoiding a base glob exclusion.

title: fix(skills): signed-in doctor selects only setup and exits NO_TESTS
fix(skills): bug-bash proof omits aborted-run and charter-coverage checks
body:
## Summary

Step 4.3 of `create-verification-skill` tells an agent to run one mapped explore charter, read Findings, and treat that as proof of the model, config, and output directory. It gives no acceptance check for an aborted run or for whether the recorded steps exercised the charter. A supplied run exited 0 with no findings after only a generic "Survey the app" step and `run.explore.ended: "aborted"`. The written proof criterion can therefore mark the bug-bash path as proven without charter-specific execution.

## Page

`skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md`, section 4, step 3.

## Steps to reproduce

The runtime observation below comes from a measured run in a private web project. This report does not provide a fresh executable reproduction of the abort. The exact sanitized charter, model/provider configuration, and complete report are unavailable here. The skill's current proof instructions and the public report contract were inspected directly.

1. Follow step 4.3 with a mapped charter, a configured model/persona, `--max-steps 3`, and a dedicated output directory.
2. In the supplied case, the command exited 0. Its saved report showed `run.explore.ended` as `aborted`, one passed generic survey step, and zero findings. The diagnostic projection appears under Actual behavior.
3. Apply the written proof instructions to that case. Reading the empty Findings list does not establish whether the charter ran, and the skill does not tell the agent to check the ending or recorded step instructions before calling the bug-bash path proven.

Steps 1 and 2 were executed by the originating investigator, not rerun by the reporter. Step 3 is a review of the written acceptance criterion against the supplied observation. No claim is made that every agent will accept the result.

## Expected behavior

The skill promises to "Prove the generated skill before handing it over" by running its instructions end to end. A bug-bash proof must establish that the configured explorer performed substantive work for the mapped charter, and must retain an aborted attempt as failed or unproven. The report already exposes the ending and each exploration step. Empty Findings or process exit 0 alone cannot establish that contract.

## Actual behavior

Step 4.3 says:

> Read its `Findings` and triage; do not verify every finding now. This proves the model, the config, and the output directory, not the app.

It only explicitly marks bug bash unproven when no model exists. It does not require inspecting `run.explore.ended` or whether the recorded steps followed the charter. The surrounding "Fix what fails" instruction does not identify the reported aborted-but-zero-exit result as a failed proof.

The originating investigator supplied this exact diagnostic projection of one saved report and process outcome:

```json
{"exit":0,"ended":"aborted","reason":null,"steps":[{"title":"Survey the app","status":"passed"}],"findings":0}
```

`reason` is part of that supplied diagnostic projection, not asserted to be a documented report field. Three other charter attempts in the same project also ended `aborted`, with process exit codes 0, 0, and 1. The underlying cause of those aborts is outside this issue. This report concerns the skill's proof criterion, which remains insufficient even when a different failure causes an abort.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [Generator proof instructions](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md#L103-L124) require end-to-end execution before handover.
- Failure source: The supplied diagnostic projection above and the current step 4.3 text, which declares proof after reading Findings without checking the ending or charter coverage.
- Evidence provenance: supplied
- Local verification: not-run
- Reproduction completeness: incomplete
- Missing fact: The exact sanitized charter, model/provider config, and full report needed to reproduce the original aborted exploration from a fresh project.

The aborted run is attributed to the originating investigator; the current skill and report documentation were inspected directly. No live model exploration was rerun for this report.

The [CLI explore report contract](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/docs/reference/cli.mdx#L651-L653) documents `run.explore` with `ended`, assessment, steps, and findings, including the ending value `aborted`. The [report schema](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/e2e/schema/report-v1.schema.json#L775-L793) requires `ended`, `steps`, and `findings`; [public report types](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts#L115-L137) give each step a title, instruction, and status. The [explore outcome table](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/docs/reference/cli.mdx#L676-L682) describes exit 0 for steps with no issue finding when not every step is blocked; it does not require an exploration to end `finished`. A productive charter can also exit 1 after discovering an issue, so exit 0 alone is not the right acceptance test.

## Restoration check

Apply the revised proof instructions to the supplied aborted survey-only result. They must leave the bug-bash path unproven and identify the missing charter execution. As a control, a run that records substantive work for the mapped charter can prove the explorer path even if it discovers an issue and exits 1. A `--max-steps 3` budget ending should state its actual coverage limit. This issue does not require every finding to be verified or the application itself to be declared correct.

## Suggested wording

After reading Findings, inspect `report.json` for the ending and the steps actually performed. An aborted run, or one that only ran a generic fallback survey without exercising the mapped charter, leaves bug bash unproven. Report budget-limited coverage accurately, and distinguish findings-driven exit 1 from a failure to execute the charter.

## Runtime or environment

Checked on 2026-10-12. Current remote `main` and the inspected skill source were at `fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f`. Latest npm stable remained e2e 0.20.0 and `@e2e-dev/web` 0.14.0. The originating investigator measured the supplied private-project runs with those package versions and Node 24.21.0 on macOS arm64. Current source/documentation inspection was performed for this report; live model exploration was not rerun. The generator skill is distributed from the repository, rather than bundled in the npm package.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The supplied result demonstrates an aborted survey-only run that satisfies the written Findings check while leaving the mapped charter unexecuted. Agents can hand over a verification skill with an unproven bug-bash path. The frequency of that acceptance is unknown.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The documented report exposes the ending and substantive step instructions, so an agent can inspect them and retain the aborted or uncovered charter as unproven without modifying e2e.

title: fix(verification-skill): require a supported surface before initializing a project
body: The interview sends an agent to `npx e2e init` whenever the project has no e2e files, and the only unsupported-project stop in the skill names a native desktop app. A CLI, a library, or a batch job reaches the initialization instruction with nothing an engine can drive, and `e2e init` writes a browser target, dependencies, MCP registrations, and ignore entries into it. - `skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md`, Surface row: stops on any project where no engine has a surface to drive, including a desktop frontend whose only browser output is a native-runtime notice. A service with no UI is not in that group: the same row drives it through `web()`. - Same file, e2e-state row: `npx e2e init` runs only after the Surface row found something an engine can drive. - Same file, section 5: a stopped project is handed over with its observed entry point and no generated skill. Fixes #1082 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - scratch CLI project: `hello.py` printing `Hello, example!` from `python3 hello.py example`, no browser UI, no HTTP listener - `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx -y e2e@latest init --yes`, the command the e2e-state row names What the project gained from that one command, with nothing an engine can drive in it: ```text ◆ Linked .claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e ◆ Created .mcp.json (e2e mcp server) ◆ Created .cursor/mcp.json (e2e mcp server) ◆ Updated .gitignore (10 entries) ● No tsconfig.json; add one for editor completions on e2e.config.ts and tests/ └ Next: npm install, then APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run test:e2e $ grep -n url e2e.config.ts 16: url: process.env.APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000', ``` The branch cannot be shown by running `e2e init`: the change is the stop in front of it. `, one `test.setup` saving the `member` session and two tests that consume it | main, the documented auth doctor | this branch, the documented auth doctor | | --- | --- | | the setup file alone | a test that consumes the session | ```text $ npx e2e run tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts --output .e2e/setup-only ERROR configuration error NO_TESTS (collection) 2 tests were collected but none is runnable: 1 setup tests, which run only for the sessions selected tests need, 1 file not selected by a positional argument Test Files no test files Tests no tests executed Errors 1 error EXIT=2 ``` ```text $ npx e2e run tests/signed-in.e2e.ts --output .e2e/signed-in # the fixture's signed-in test ✓ target "web" command ready 102ms ✓ |web| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test) 163ms ✓ |web| tests/signed-in.e2e.ts (1 test) 85ms Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) EXIT=0 ``` The control the issue asks for, a setup that fails before saving its session: the same doctor run reports the failure instead of a collection error. ```text $ npx e2e run tests/signed-in.e2e.ts --output .e2e/setup-fails # setup broken on purpose expected: visible observed: no node (match count 0) ❯ trace .e2e/setup-fails/results/auth-setup-save-member-session-d8d7fed509d4b575/trace.md Test Files 1 failed | 0 passed | 1 skipped (2) EXIT=1 ``` `gh pr create --attach` needs write access, so the evidence above is text rather than an uploaded image.

title: fix(verification-skill): keep an aborted bug bash unproven
body: Step 4.3 of the generator treats reading the `Findings` list as proof of the bug-bash path. A run can exit 0 with no findings after a single generic survey step and `run.explore.ended: "aborted"`, and the written criterion accepts it, so a generated skill is handed over with its bug-bash path never exercised. - `skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md`, step 4.3: reads `run.explore` in `report.json` for the ending and the steps the explorer actually ran. - An aborted ending, or steps that are not the mapped charter, stays unproven and the handover says so. - The steps prove the charter ran, not the exit code: `1` is also what a run that executed no step exits with. A `--max-steps` ending states the coverage the run reached. Fixes #1085 ## Verified Ran it locally: no - reproducing the abort needs a model-assisted `e2e explore` run, and this change only moves the acceptance criterion. The contract it now reads is in the tree: - `packages/e2e/schema/report-v1.schema.json:779,790` requires `ended`, `steps`, and `findings` on the block, and allows `ended: "aborted"`. - `packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts:132` types the same five endings, and each step carries `title`, `instruction`, and `status`. - `packages/e2e/src/explore/body.ts:216-241` is why the exit code cannot stand in for the steps: `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED` when no step ran and an `ASSERTION_FAILED` when issues were found are both failures, so the same `1` covers a run that executed the charter and a run that executed nothing. - `docs/reference/cli.mdx:676-682` gives exit 0 to a run where steps ran, no `issue` finding was reported, and not every step was blocked, so exit 0 alone does not establish that exploration finished. The step keeps the run the issue supplied (exit 0, one generic survey step, empty `Findings`, `ended: "aborted"`) unproven, which is the acceptance the old wording allowed.

title: fix(report): explore labels a selected target with the first configured target
body:
## Summary With multiple configured web targets, `e2e explore --target mixed` starts the selected target but the list reporter prints `|capacity| Exploring`, where `capacity` is the first configured target. The JSON result and Markdown summary correctly identify `mixed`. This is a display defect; the selected target executes. ## Steps to reproduce 1. In a fresh disposable directory, install the release baseline below with `npm install --save-dev e2e@0.20.0 @e2e-dev/web@0.14.0 ai@^7 @ai-sdk/openai@^4`. Have a working e2e `openai` login for the model used below. No test file is needed because `explore` generates its own exploration. 2. Create `index.html` containing the following static fixture. ```html Target label reproduction

Explore fixture

A static local page for testing reporter target labels.

``` 3. Create `e2e.config.ts` with two targets, in this order. ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { chatgpt } from 'e2e/oauth/chatgpt'; export default { targets: ['capacity', 'mixed'].map(name => ({ name, engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command: { executable: 'python3', args: ['-m', 'http.server', '{port}', '--bind', '127.0.0.1'] }, }, })), agents: { default: { model: chatgpt('gpt-6.1-sol'), providerOptions: { openai: { reasoningEffort: 'high' } }, }, }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` 4. Run `npx e2e explore "Explore the page" --target mixed --max-steps 1 --reporter list,markdown` with output redirected to a log so the reporter uses its non-TTY output. Compare its target-ready line, `Exploring` badge, and `.e2e/report.json` at `run.results[0].targetId`. 5. Run the same command with `--target capacity --output .e2e-control` as a control. The list badge and JSON target agree for the first target. The release command and control were executed. The same non-first-target case was also executed using the current default-branch CLI source, loaded with the release package's TypeScript loader, against the same fixture and installed web engine. Each explore was run separately with the one-step limit. ## Expected behavior The list reporter should label the exploration with the target selected by `--target`. For the second target, `Exploring` should show `|mixed|`, matching the target-ready line and JSON result. The CLI help describes `--target` as "the target to explore" and reserves the first configured target for the default. ## Actual behavior Both tested CLI baselines printed these meaningful lines for the second target. Timings and the generated run identifier are omitted. ```text RUN e2e v0.20.0 targets: capacity, mixed model chatgpt.responses/gpt-6.1-sol ✓ target "mixed" command ready ❯ |capacity| Exploring Explore the page ``` Both JSON reports had `run.results[0].targetId === "mixed"` and both configured target IDs in `run.targets`. Their Markdown summary footers named `mixed`. The release control printed `|capacity|` and its JSON result named `capacity`. All three runs exited 1 with `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED` because the planner concluded that the static page offered no interactive exploration step. That outcome is separate from the badge mismatch: the wrong `Exploring` badge had already appeared before planning. The non-first-target runs printed a `FAIL |mixed|` result line correctly; they did not print a final `Explored` header, so that header was not measured. This fixture exercises reporter attribution without relying on a successful agent exploration. No claim is made about all Markdown target labels or other engines. ## Evidence - Expected source: The executed CLI help and `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:724` define `--target` as the target to explore. `packages/e2e/src/explore/index.ts:117,147` selects the requested target and passes its name to the runner. - Failure source: Fresh isolated release and default-branch CLI logs, with matching JSON reports and the first-target control, summarized above. The default-branch reporter's [exploreBadge method](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts#L925) reads `this.targets[0]`; `runStarted` at line 494 stores the event's entire target list. `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:684-706` emits all configured targets before selecting the requested target. - Evidence provenance: observed - Local verification: reproduced - Reproduction completeness: complete ## Restoration check Run the same second-target case and first-target control. For `--target mixed`, the list reporter's `Exploring` badge must say `mixed`, and the target-ready line, JSON result, and Markdown footer must continue to name `mixed`. For `--target capacity`, all must name `capacity`. A fix must preserve the selected execution target and JSON attribution. The static fixture's separate no-step exit does not determine whether the target-label contract is restored. ## Runtime or environment - Release: `e2e 0.20.0`, confirmed as npm `latest`; `@e2e-dev/web 0.14.0`; `playwright-core 1.63.0`; `ai 7.0.138`; `@ai-sdk/openai 4.0.92`. - Default branch: `main` at `fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f`, freshly cloned. The source CLI was executed with `node --import ./node_modules/e2e/dist/config/register.js /packages/e2e/src/cli/bin.ts explore "Explore the page" --target mixed --max-steps 1 --reporter list,markdown --output .e2e-main`. This uses the release TypeScript loader and installed web engine; it is not a full monorepo build. - Node: `v26.10.0`; macOS `27.0.1` arm64; Python `3.14.7`; reporter `list,markdown`; model `chatgpt('gpt-6.1-sol')` through the e2e OpenAI login. - Engine: `@e2e-dev/web`. The observed defect is in the list reporter; other engines were not exercised. ## Triage assessment - Impact level: P3 - Assessment status: supported - Impact basis: The terminal exploration badge names the wrong configured target, while the selected target starts and the JSON result and Markdown footer retain the correct target. No execution or result-attribution change was observed. - Workaround status: available - Workaround basis: The target-ready line and JSON result provide the correct selected target in the tested non-first-target cases, and the Markdown footer also identifies it correctly.

title: fix(mcp): status content names mislead role-locator guidance
body:
## Summary For an unlabelled `

Saved.

`, MCP `observe` and role-only `locate` display `status "Saved."`, but the role locator's accessible name is empty. When `locate {role: "status", name: "Saved."}` correctly finds no node, its advice sends the user back to the "accessible name in the observation" or suggests `exact: false`; neither resolves this case. This makes the documented observe/locate workflow misleading when an agent chooses a role-query name from the displayed message. The web reader intentionally gives status messages a content-derived engine name. The report concerns how MCP presents and explains that name, not a request to make Playwright role locators match content that is not an accessible name. ## Steps to reproduce Use the published baseline under Runtime or environment. No model or credentials are required. All following steps were executed against an isolated static fixture. 1. In a new directory, install the runner and web engine with `npm install --save-dev e2e @e2e-dev/web`. 2. Save `index.html`: ```html

Saved.

``` 3. Save `e2e.config.ts`: ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; export default { tests: '*.e2e.ts', workers: 1, retries: 0, assertionTimeout: 500, targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command: { executable: 'python3', args: ['-m', 'http.server', '{port}', '--bind', '127.0.0.1'], }, }, }], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` 4. Start `npx e2e mcp` over stdio. Through an MCP client, run `open_session {}`, then the following session calls in order: ```json {"tool":"observe","args":{}} {"tool":"locate","args":{"role":"status"}} {"tool":"locate","args":{"role":"status","name":"Saved."}} {"tool":"locate","args":{"role":"status","name":"Saved.","exact":false}} {"tool":"locate","args":{"text":"Saved."}} ``` 5. Run `close_session {}` and stop the MCP client. Save `status.e2e.ts`, then run `npx e2e run status.e2e.ts --workers 1 --retries 0`: ```ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('displayed status name is not a locator accessible name', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status', 'Saved.')).toBeVisible(); }); test('text lookup and role plus text filter work', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/'); await expect(screen.getByText('Saved.')).toBeVisible(); await expect(screen.getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: 'Saved.' })).toBeVisible(); }); ``` 6. As a control, save `labelled.html` containing `

Saved.

`. Opening that page and using `locate {role: "status", name: "Save result"}` returns one match, and the corresponding `screen.getByRole('status', 'Save result')` visibility assertion passes. ## Expected behavior MCP should distinguish the reader's deliberate content-derived name from the accessible name used by `locate` and `screen.getByRole`, or explain the difference wherever it recommends using observation names for role queries. For this fixture, the zero-match guidance should accurately describe why the quoted message cannot be used as the accessible-name filter. It should leave the user with a usable text-based locator without implying that `exact: false` can turn status content into an accessible name. The intended content-name vocabulary and the existing browser accessible-name matching can both remain valid. An explicit accessible name must still match through the role locator. ## Actual behavior Both tested baselines produced the following MCP results. Node ids are omitted except for the fixture node; the observation showed that node in the quoted name position, without a separate text field. ```text observe: #n2 status "Saved." locate {role: "status"}: 1 node matches getByRole("status"). Use: screen.getByRole("status") - status "Saved." locate {role: "status", name: "Saved."}: 0 nodes match getByRole("status", name: "Saved."). A test using this locator would fail with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND. Check the accessible name in the observation (observe), or loosen the match with exact: false. locate {role: "status", name: "Saved.", exact: false}: 0 nodes match getByRole("status", name: "Saved."). A test using this locator would fail with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND. Check the accessible name in the observation (observe), or loosen the match with exact: false. locate {text: "Saved."}: 1 node matches getByText("Saved."). Use: screen.getByText("Saved.") - status "Saved." ``` The role-name test failed on both baselines with the expected locator rejection: ```text ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeVisible failed locator: getByRole("status", name: "Saved.") expected: visible observed: no node (match count 0) ``` Each test run exited 1 with that one failure. The text lookup, role plus text filter, and explicit accessible-name controls passed. The failure is the advice/display ambiguity, not the zero-match result itself. ## Runtime or environment - Published baseline: `e2e 0.20.0` and `@e2e-dev/web 0.14.0`, both npm `latest` when tested. - Current default-branch baseline: `main` at `fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f`; the same MCP calls and tests ran with both packages' current source transpiled to JavaScript using `oxc-transform 0.152.0` and the isolated published installation's dependencies. This was a focused execution check, not the repository's full build or test gate. - `playwright-core 1.63.0`; headless Chromium `153.0.8010.12` from the failing trace. - Node `v26.10.0`; macOS `27.0.1`, arm64. - MCP server over stdio; deterministic calls and tests only. ## Evidence - Expected source: The shipped MCP guide describes `observe` as `#id role "name" ...` and instructs users to check locators before writing them; the writing-tests guide defines the role query's name as an accessible name. The MCP locate argument schema also calls `name` an "Accessible name, with role". - Failure source: The isolated static-page MCP replies and deterministic test results quoted above; the zero-match reply explicitly calls the value in `observe` an accessible name. - Evidence provenance: observed - Local verification: reproduced - Reproduction completeness: complete The contract sources are [MCP guide, observation format and workflow](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/e2e/references/mcp.md#L59-L96) and [writing-tests guide, role query and exact name matching](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md#L142-L169). The deliberate reader policy is explicit in [read-semantics.ts](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts#L654-L681) and [the cross-check's engine-named-role policy](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/web/tests/crosscheck/crosscheck.ts#L53-L58). The role locator delegates to browser name matching in [locators.ts](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/web/src/locators.ts#L127-L139). The relevant MCP argument, zero-match advice, and node-name renderer are in [catalog.ts](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f/packages/e2e/src/mcp/catalog.ts#L107-L186). ## Restoration check Repeat the unlabelled status fixture's `observe` and `locate` calls. The output or guidance should make clear which value is display content and which name a role query can actually match, and should not direct the user to retry the same content as an accessible name. A text lookup or role plus text filter should continue to find the fixture. Keep the labelled status control: a real accessible name must continue to match. A change that merely makes the unsupported content-name role query pass does not establish restoration of this reporting contract. ## Additional context This report acknowledges the intentional content-name policy documented in [merged PR #583](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/583). It does not ask to undo it. [Issue #48](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/48) addressed the retired v1 observer/deterministic architecture and closed as not planned; its closing guidance directs resurfaced v2 requirements to fresh reports. Neither covers the specific MCP accessible-name advice shown here. Searches across open and closed issues and PRs found no report addressing that narrow guidance problem. ## Triage assessment - Impact level: P2 - Assessment status: supported - Impact basis: The deterministic MCP workflow offers an unusable role-query name and misleading recovery advice for an unlabelled status message. Following it produces a failing test; reach beyond the tested status fixture was not measured. - Workaround status: available - Workaround basis: MCP text lookup and the deterministic `getByText` and `getByRole('status').filter({ hasText })` controls were observed to find the same fixture. These preserve the relevant visibility check without changing the app's accessibility semantics.

title: fix(agent): dense screens are not cut to fit long judgment instructions, so e2e explore aborts while planning
body:
## Summary On a screen whose semantic tree is larger than the observation budget, a judgment call whose instruction is longer than a fixed size is refused by the adapter's pre-flight with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound N exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens M`, instead of having the screen cut further so the request fits. The `e2e explore` planner runs as such a call (`agent.extract`), and its instruction grows with every step's title and summary. On such a screen, a run with a short goal, `--max-steps 3`, and the default `maxInputTokens` plans and runs two steps, then the third planning call is refused: the run ends `aborted` with no closing assessment, `status: "blocked"`, exit 1. A goal near the 2,000-character limit, or a direct `agent.extract` with a long instruction, fails on the first call. Act steps on the same screen complete normally. ## Runtime or environment - Versions: e2e 0.20.0 (latest on npm), @e2e-dev/web 0.14.0, ai 7.0.138, @ai-sdk/openai 4.0.92, zod 4.6.7, Node v26.10.0, macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), Chromium 153.0.8010.12, viewport 1280x720. - Engine: `@e2e-dev/web`. - Source locators below are at `main` commit fc9064415d427060fad1d406c4c491dda248ad4f. `packages/e2e/src/agent`, `packages/e2e/src/explore`, `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`, `docs/reference/config.mdx`, and `docs/reference/errors.mdx` have no changes between the `e2e@0.20.0` tag and that commit. ## Steps to reproduce The failing request is refused before it is sent, so steps 1 to 5 need no API key and spend no tokens. Any AI SDK model instance works. 1. In an empty directory with `"type": "module"` in `package.json`, run `npm install e2e@0.20.0 @e2e-dev/web@0.14.0 ai@7.0.138 @ai-sdk/openai@4.0.92 zod@4.6.7`. 2. Save this as `make-page.mjs`, run `node make-page.mjs`, then serve the page with `python3 -m http.server 48232 --bind 127.0.0.1` from inside `site/`. The resulting page has 1,753 accessibility nodes. ```js import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'; const rows = Array.from({ length: 180 }, (_, i) => `Item ${i + 1}Warehouse ${'NSEW'[i % 4]}${(i * 37) % 500} units$${((i * 13.7) % 900).toFixed(2)}`).join(''); const orders = Array.from({ length: 120 }, (_, i) => `
  • Order ${i + 1} for customer ${(i * 7) % 311}
    • `).join(''); mkdirSync('site', { recursive: true }); writeFileSync('site/index.html', `Inventory

    Inventory

    180 items in 4 warehouses.

    ${rows}
    All items
    ItemWarehouseStockPriceAction
      ${orders}
    `); ``` 3. Save this as `e2e.config.ts`: ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai'; export default { tests: 'tests/**/*.e2e.ts', targets: [{ name: 'web', engine: web({ browser: 'chromium' }), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:48232' } }], // Any model: the failing request is refused before it is sent, so no API key is needed. agents: { default: { model: openai('gpt-6.1-sol') } }, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` 4. Run explore with a 1,903-character goal (the limit is 2,000): ```sh GOAL=$(node -e "console.log('Check that each row of the All items table shows its stock in units and its price in dollars with two decimals. '.repeat(17).trim())") npx e2e explore "$GOAL" --max-steps 3 --output out-explore ``` 5. Save this as `tests/extract.e2e.ts` (a 3,388-character instruction) and run `npx e2e run`: ```ts import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { z } from 'zod'; const instruction = 'the Stock cell of the row whose Item cell reads Item 42, exactly as shown, '.repeat(45) + 'as one string'; test('extract with a long instruction on a dense page', async ({ app, agent }) => { await app.open('/'); await agent.extract(instruction, { schema: z.string() }); }); ``` 6. Natural case, one model-dependent run that needs a working model and spends tokens. It used a different synthetic static page from steps 2 to 5, not reproduced here: a Summary section stating the item and warehouse counts, with a name filter input, a region select, and an Apply button that have no script behind them; a 180-row items table; and a 120-item orders list (1,775 accessibility nodes). The planning call that gets refused depends on how long the model's step summaries are. The agent used `chatgpt('gpt-6.1-sol')` from `e2e/oauth/chatgpt` with `providerOptions: { openai: { reasoningEffort: 'high' } }`, `maxSteps: 40`, `maxModelCalls: 40`, a one-sentence `context` and `system`, and the default `maxInputTokens`. The 168-character goal was `Starting at /, check that the Summary's item and warehouse counts agree with the All items table, and that the Region and name filters narrow the table to matching rows`, run with `--max-steps 3`. ## Expected behavior `AgentOptions.maxInputTokens` is documented as "Input tokens per model request, 1 through 1000000; default 64000. A dense screen is cut to fit under it." The `maxObservationBytes` option beside it is the observation ceiling "for act turns and judgments". The judgment tier's budget code states the same intent: "Deriving the budget from what the rest of the request actually costs makes a big screen truncate visibly rather than fail the adapter's pre-flight check." When the request includes a valid instruction (an explore goal within its 2,000-character limit, the planner's record of earlier steps, or an `extract` instruction), the screen should be cut far enough that the request fits under `maxInputTokens`. The error code's documented meaning, "The model-call or action-step budget ran out before a conclusion" (`docs/reference/errors.mdx:72`), also does not describe a request refused before any budget ran out. The planner should then keep planning, and `e2e explore` should end for one of its own reasons (`finished`, `step-limit`, `time`, `stuck`) with a closing assessment. A refusal would be consistent with the contract only when the system message and instruction alone leave no room for the 1,024-byte minimum observation. In every case here they leave more than 50,000 bytes. ## Actual behavior Step 4 ends after 1.33 seconds, before any step runs and without sending a request: ```text no step ran ended: the run was cut short ... STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound 64990 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000 ... AI 0 tokens · 1 model calls · openai.responses/gpt-6.1-sol ``` Its `report.json` has `run.explore.ended: "aborted"`, no `summary`, `run.status: "blocked"`, `run.exitCode: 1`, and `run.usage.maxObservationBytes: 56864`, so the observation was cut to the budget, but that budget left room for only a fixed amount of instruction. Step 5 fails the same way: `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound 64481 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000`, with 0 tokens spent. With `.repeat(105)` in place of `.repeat(45)` (a 7,888-character instruction, under the 8,192-byte limit `docs/reference/agent.mdx` sets for act instructions), it fails with `model input upper bound 68981 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000`. With `.repeat(1)` it passes the pre-flight. Both of those runs record `run.usage.maxObservationBytes: 58817`, so the screen is cut by the same amount whatever the instruction's length. In the natural case (step 6), steps 1 and 2 ran (16 and 8 actions; each reported a finding about the inert filters, so both are marked failed), and their summaries were 384 and 381 characters. The third planning call was then refused with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound 64190 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000`. The run reported `Steps 2 done of 3 · planning`, `ended: "aborted"`, no summary, `status: "blocked"`, and exit 1, after spending 805.7k tokens. Its two findings were kept in the report. Controls on the step 1 to 5 setup: with `maxInputTokens: 128_000` on the agent, the step 5 test passes the pre-flight and fails only with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: OpenAI API key is missing`. Step 4 behaves the same with the `128_000` config, and so does step 5 with the default `maxInputTokens` and a one-clause instruction. On the step 6 page, a 1,731-character goal of the same kind failed its first planning call at the default limit with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound 64813 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000`. With a working model and `maxInputTokens: 128_000`, the same goal passed both of its planning calls: the planner wrote a charter, and after the single step (`--max-steps 1`) it returned a closing assessment, so the run ended with `ended: "step-limit"`. That step itself ended blocked (`AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`), which made the run `status: "blocked"`, exit 1; I had set the agent's `maxModelCalls` to 3 for that run to limit cost. The step used 2 of those calls, so the cap did not cause the block, and the blocked step is unrelated to this report. The same `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` error (`64081 exceeds ... 64000`) first appeared on a private app page with the same versions, with the same `ended: "aborted"`, no summary, `status: "blocked"`, and exit 1. Setting `maxInputTokens: 128_000` let that goal finish with `ended: "step-limit"`. ## Evidence - Expected source: `docs/reference/config.mdx:697-700` (`maxObservationBytes` and `maxInputTokens` in `AgentOptions`, mirrored at `packages/e2e/src/types.ts:1333-1336`) and the `observationByteBudget` doc comment at `packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-budget.ts:49-56`. - Failure source: the step 4 to 6 runs quoted under Actual behavior. - Evidence provenance: observed - Local verification: reproduced - Reproduction completeness: complete Static breadcrumbs for retracing, not a prescribed fix: judgment calls size their observation from `fixedBytes: this.systemBytes` plus a fixed `INSTRUCTION_RESERVE = 4_096` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/invocation.ts:309-321`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-budget.ts:13` and `:61`). The prompt they send, built by `buildPrompt` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts`, holds the 1,041-byte `EXTRACT_REQUEST`, the instruction, and the observation, and `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts:69-78` refuses any request over `maxInputTokens`. `planInstruction` (`packages/e2e/src/explore/plan.ts:150`) appends each step's title and summary. Measured with the installed function, the instruction is 2,088 bytes with no steps and a 100-character goal, and grows by about 433 bytes per step with 400-character summaries. `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` is not in `PLANNER_SHORTCOMINGS` (`packages/e2e/src/explore/body.ts:32` and `:129`), so the refusal ends the run rather than falling back to the built-in charter. ## Restoration check With the step 1 to 5 files and the default `maxInputTokens`, step 4 and step 5 currently end with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` before any request is sent. So does the step 5 test with `.repeat(105)` (7,888 characters, `68981 exceeds ... 64000` today), which a slightly larger fixed reserve would not cover. When restored, all three requests pass the pre-flight with the screen cut so that their input upper bound stays at or under 64000; without a key they then fail with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (API key missing), as the `128_000` control does today. With a working model, an explore run whose planner record outgrows today's reserve, as in step 6, continues past that planning call and ends with a reason other than `aborted` and a non-null summary. As discriminating controls, `maxInputTokens` stays a hard ceiling (no request whose input upper bound exceeds it is sent), and the step 5 test with `.repeat(1)` on the step 2 page still gets an observation no smaller than today's `run.usage.maxObservationBytes: 58817`. ## Triage assessment - Impact level: P2 - Assessment status: supported - Impact basis: On a screen whose tree exceeds the observation budget (about 57,000 to 59,000 bytes at the default `maxInputTokens`, depending on the system message; 56,864 in step 4), `e2e explore` stops at the first planning call whose instruction outgrows the fixed reserve. In the observed natural run with a short goal, that was the third call. The remaining steps and the closing assessment are lost, while earlier findings are kept. Direct `extract` calls with instructions of roughly 3,000 bytes or more fail on such screens too. Screens whose tree plus the rest of the request fits under `maxInputTokens` are unaffected. - Workaround status: available - Workaround basis: Raising the agent's `maxInputTokens` above the tree size plus the instruction (`128_000` in both the private and local runs) let the same goals finish. It is a one-line config change, but it raises input tokens per model call and has to grow with the page.

title: fix(agent): cut a dense screen by the judgment's measured instruction
body: ## What and why - A judgment (`agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, `agent.extract`) sized its observation from the system message plus a fixed 4,096-byte reserve (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation-budget.ts`). The instruction itself was never measured. - An instruction past that reserve, a few thousand characters of `extract` or the explore planner's record of earlier steps, pushed the request over `maxInputTokens` and the adapter's pre-flight refused it with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` before anything was sent. `e2e explore` then ended `aborted` with no assessment. - The budget now subtracts the instruction's measured bytes; the reserve stays for the request text, markup and a repair section. The act loop passes 0: its instruction opens the history and is not resent with each observation. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[system bytes] --> O[observation budget] I[instruction bytes, measured] --> O R[reserve: request text, markup, repair] --> O O --> C[screen cut to fit maxInputTokens] ``` Closes #1091 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The issue's dense page (1,753 nodes) under `/tmp`, `e2e run` on its `agent.extract` test and `e2e explore` on its 1,903-character goal, no API key, default `maxInputTokens`. Same commands against a main build. | run | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | extract, 3,388-char instruction | `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: model input upper bound 64481 exceeds the agent's maxInputTokens 64000`, observation 58,817 bytes | pre-flight passes, fails only on `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: OpenAI API key is missing`, observation 55,429 bytes | | extract, 7,888-char instruction | not run (issue reports 68981 exceeds 64000) | pre-flight passes, key missing, observation 50,942 bytes | | extract, 1-clause instruction | observation 58,817 bytes | observation 58,722 bytes | | explore, 1,903-char goal, `--max-steps 3` | `no step ran`, `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED ... 64990 exceeds ... 64000`, `ended: aborted`, observation 56,864 bytes | pre-flight passes, fails only on the missing key, observation 52,956 bytes | ```text # this branch, explore no step ran ended: the run was cut short MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: OpenAI API key is missing. ... ``` The short-instruction control loses 95 bytes of observation: the instruction's own size, now measured instead of folded into the reserve. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. (`docs/reference/config.mdx` already promises "a dense screen is cut to fit under it"; no change.) - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.
