# Releases
## e2e@0.21.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1132](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1132) [`c82a03a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c82a03a25ff62b2f189965f7171efe83c960b19f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.command.inheritEnv` passes host variables to the app by name or trailing-`*` prefix (`['DATABASE_URL', 'STRIPE_*']`), copying each one only when it is set, so a host can hand the app per-run values without listing them in the config or spreading `process.env`. `command.env` wins over an inherited value, and inherited values are redacted from a quoted startup failure like `command.env`. A bare `*` and a `*` anywhere but the end are `INVALID_CONFIG`.

- [#1134](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1134) [`8497c06`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/8497c06967cdf18adf7b6c429d85bcecd11ba584) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `E2E_CACHE_DIR` and `e2e run --cache-dir <dir>` (also on `e2e cache`) replace `cache.dir`, so checkouts and worktrees of one project can share a replay cache without editing the config. The flag wins over the variable, both resolve from the project root with `~` or a leading `~/` as the home directory, and the cache mode stays as configured. With a custom `cache.store`, `--cache-dir` is an error and `E2E_CACHE_DIR` is ignored.

- [#1137](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1137) [`27a6ed0`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/27a6ed0d83fdd6ca0d97a6f1fed780f04d036991) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e feedback` now asks for reports the e2e team can act on. A `--type bug` report needs `--repro`, steps that reproduce it every time. Without it, the command sends nothing and prints a prefilled GitHub issue instead, so the team can ask you for a reproduction there. When the registry confirms the installed e2e is older than the latest release, the report exits 2 and sends nothing, since the problem may already be fixed; upgrade and check again, or pass `--allow-outdated`. The new `--error-code` flag takes the e2e error code involved, and `--task`, `--expected`, `--actual`, and `--approach` now take at most 1500 characters.

- [#1135](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1135) [`78655e1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/78655e1327777f23641898515f89b4cbe4192b8a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e init` takes a flag per wizard question: `--engine`, `--gateway`, `--endpoint`, `--skills`, `--mcp`, and `--install`/`--no-install`. A flag skips its prompt; with `--yes`, an omitted flag keeps its default. Without a terminal, pass `--yes`. `--endpoint` implies `--gateway openai-compatible`. `--skills` and `--mcp` take comma-separated locations or `none`. An unknown value exits 2 before any write and lists the valid ones.
  
  ```sh
  npx e2e init --yes --gateway openrouter --skills .agents/skills --mcp .mcp.json --install
  ```

- [#1097](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1097) [`a869c06`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a869c06304941a8e883dde267f9ca10ead856088) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `textContent()`, `inputValue()`, `getAttribute()`, `isEnabled()`, `isDisabled()`, `isChecked()`, and `boundingBox()` now wait for their one match until the action timeout, as actions and Playwright's reads do, instead of failing at once with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` when the node is still rendering. `isVisible()`, `isHidden()`, `count()`, `all()`, and `allTextContents()` still answer from the current screen. A read of a node that never appears fails after the action timeout.

- [#1131](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1131) [`babae32`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/babae32bdafac507f835e263f6a87ce6699fec1e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e run --max-duration <ms>` and the config key `maxDuration` stop a run once it has spent that long running tests: nothing more is dispatched, the running tests end as `interrupted`, the rest are skipped with the new cause `time-limit`, and the run records a `RUN_TIMEOUT` error and exits 1. `--last-failed` runs the interrupted and skipped tests next. The report schema's skip causes gain `time-limit`.

- [#980](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980) [`3a53fbd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3a53fbd8e5fb8ed345dd00331b3a5b5b90bac1d3) Thanks [@bheemreddy181](https://github.com/bheemreddy181)! - Add `openHost<Fixtures>()` to `e2e/runner` for other test runners. A worker-lifetime host prepares the target, starts app processes, and initializes its engine once. `host.openSession({ name, timeout, signal, agent, onStep })` opens a fresh test-lifetime attempt with typed fixtures, its own deadline, steps, and artifacts. Only one hosted attempt can be opening, live, or closing per process; a host can open sessions sequentially.
  
  A session's `timeout` is enforced: when it passes, every operation still running fails with `TEST_TIMEOUT`, the session is timed out, and `close()` reports it. A launch that fails or is cancelled leaves the host usable for the next session; only a session whose engine cleanup failed closes the host.
  
  Closing a session writes a redacted `trace.md` under a safe, unique `results/host/` directory, available through the absolute `tracePath` for attachments. `close()` returns soft expectation and cleanup failures; async disposal throws an `AggregateError` when failures exist. Closing the host cancels any pending or active session, then disposes and releases its worker resources once. Both close methods are idempotent. `config` accepts a path or an `E2EConfig` value. The one-shot MCP attempt stays internal.

Those ids are unknown to the Anthropic SDK, which limits a call that sets no `maxOutputTokens` to 4096 tokens and only warns: a long answer ended with `finishReason: 'length'` and nothing in the result said why. The provider now asks for 8192, the cap the runner already allows a judgment, and a caller's own `maxOutputTokens` is left untouched.

title: fix(locator): reads wait for their match until the action timeout
body: ## What and why - `textContent()`, `inputValue()`, `getAttribute()`, `isEnabled()`, `isDisabled()`, `isChecked()`, and `boundingBox()` now poll for their one match until the action timeout, through the same `resolveExactlyOne` loop actions use. They used to fail at once with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` when the node was still rendering, while actions and Playwright's reads wait. - Reads already waited for a missing frame and re-resolved a stale node within the action timeout; zero matches was the one case that did not. Item 7 of #1020 hit this on every menu close; #1078 proposed documenting it as by design instead, and was closed for this fix. - `isVisible()`, `isHidden()`, `count()`, `all()`, and `allTextContents()` still answer from the current screen, as in Playwright. - `resolveForRead` is gone; `LocatorEngine.read` is its only caller (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts`). - `expect(browser).toHaveClass` reads through `getAttribute` inside its own poll, bounded by the assertion deadline. A read that waits longer than that deadline turned a never-arriving node into `ACTION_FAILED operation timed out`. It now samples `count()` first, so absence stays `ASSERTION_FAILED` observing `no node` (`packages/web/src/browser.ts`). Found by the fresh-context review. - Docs: `reference/screen` prose and table, `migrate/playwright` row back to `the same`, `core-concepts`, `migrate/selenium`, `skills/e2e` text; changesets `e2e` minor and `@e2e-dev/web` patch. ```ts await app.open('/checkout'); await screen.getByRole('button', 'Apply').tap(); expect(await screen.getByLabel('Total').textContent()).toBe('$42.00'); // waits for the re-rendered field ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-reads-wait.e2e.ts`: a scratch test opens `/controls`, inserts `42` after 1.5 s, then reads `textContent()`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | fails in 0.5 s: `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND locator matched no nodes: getByLabel("Late total")` | passes in 1.76 s | - `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` (real Chromium through the built runner): `reads wait for a node that arrives late` and `a read of a node that never arrives fails with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` both fail with main's engine built into dist and pass here. The second one takes the full 5 s action timeout. - Same suite: `class assertions on a node that never arrives fail as assertions` fails with `ACTION_FAILED` when the `browser.ts` hunk is reverted, passes here as `ASSERTION_FAILED` with `observed: no node`. `hung-page.test.ts` still ends a class assertion on a frozen renderer at its own timeout. - Unit: `locator-engine.test.ts` polls zero matches then reads, and gives up at the action timeout without a read; `locator-basics.test.ts` keeps `isVisible()` immediate at zero matches and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` immediate on several. - Testbed suite: 77 passed, 1 skipped. Full `pnpm test` green. ## Checklist - [x] Changesets added (`e2e` minor, `@e2e-dev/web` patch). - [x] No breaking change: a read that used to throw at once now throws after the action timeout; no signature or error code changes. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/reference/screen.mdx`, `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx`, `skills/e2e/`. - [x] No public type, wire, or engine contract change (one JSDoc line on `textContent`).

title: Bound mobile reads by the operation budget without turning a slow last poll into a timeout
body:
## Problem

On `@e2e-dev/mobile`, a read that hangs holds the step until the test timeout. That covers observe, locate, and the relocation snapshot `settled()` takes before a tap. #1073 bounds inputs by their operation budget but leaves reads unbounded, as on main.

Bounding reads the same way broke the locator poll. On iOS a snapshot takes 1–2 s, so the poll's last read was cut off at the deadline. Core then classified it as a read that "hung with budget to spare" (`ACTION_FAILED`) instead of `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. That is the `controls.e2e.ts` failure in #1073's first CI run.

## What a fix needs

- Core's poll classification (`cutOffAtDeadline`, `pollCondition`'s 100 ms rule) has to tell a slow engine's last read from a hung one. One option: an engine declares a read latency, or the poll measures it, and the poll grants the last read that long past the deadline.
- Only then can the mobile engine bound reads by `timeoutMs`. A hung snapshot would then fail the step at the budget, and a slow one would still finish.

Raised in review of #1073.

title: Feature request: official Docker deployment for remote MCP sessions and runner integration
body:
## Summary

Could e2e provide an official Docker image (or maintained Dockerfile) and Docker Compose example for a self-hosted, long-running remote MCP service, with a documented way to invoke the test runner and retrieve results?

Our goal is to integrate e2e into existing online automation/chat platforms such as n8n, Dify, and Open WebUI. Testers should submit case documents through a web interface; installation and configuration should happen once on the server.

## Use case

Our case documents contain a test objective, ordered steps, and pass criteria, all written in natural language. We want an external AI agent to interpret these cases, operate the application, and produce per-case results with evidence. Where a criterion can be expressed exactly, we also want to use deterministic assertions.

One execution contains a group of cases. Browser state must remain available throughout that group and be closed explicitly when the flow finishes. Concurrent case groups must have separate browser state.

Our current cloud Playwright MCP integration has window contention between users/executions and large, frequently requested page snapshots. These are observations about our integration, not a claim that all Playwright MCP deployments have this problem. Clients can reconnect for individual tool calls while the browser remains open for the case group.

e2e's explicit session IDs and incremental action feedback look relevant to these needs.

## Current integration gap

The documented `e2e mcp` interface uses stdio and provides application interaction tools. The runner is available through `e2e run`, but the MCP interface does not expose test-suite execution.

We have not found an official Docker/Compose deployment that combines remote access, session lifecycle management, and runner integration. Currently, adopting this approach appears to require maintaining a transport bridge and a separate execution wrapper ourselves.

## Proposed scope

A staged implementation would be useful:

1. **Containerized remote MCP**
   - An official versioned image, or maintained Dockerfile, with e2e, the web engine, Chromium, and required system dependencies.
   - A Compose example exposing Streamable HTTP, with configuration for mounted project files, model credentials when needed, and artifact storage.
   - Existing session tools available remotely, including explicit open/call/close behavior.
   - A documented way to bind each case-group execution to its own session across client reconnects. Short-lived remote connections should not accidentally destroy the long-lived backend session or route another user's calls into it.
   - Documented cleanup on completion, cancellation, idle expiry, and service shutdown.

2. **Runner integration**
   - A supported way to start an existing configured test suite and obtain a run ID, progress, final outcome, and report/artifact references.
   - This could be MCP tools, a small HTTP API, or a documented programmatic integration built on the public runner API. Names such as `start_run`, `get_run_status`, and `get_run_report` are illustrative.
   - Per-run artifact directories and clearly documented concurrency/isolation behavior.

We are looking for a deployable execution service that existing platforms can call. A new chat UI or full agent platform is not necessary.

## Expected acceptance example

Two n8n executions connect to the same deployed endpoint. Each opens its own session, performs several steps while preserving its own browser state, and closes that session at the end. They do not contend over the same pages.

A runner request starts a configured suite and exposes its final result and evidence without requiring an end user to install e2e or use a terminal.

## Related work

- #994: programmatic test execution with runtime configuration.
- #992 and PR #980: public APIs for hosting e2e sessions.
- #1074 and #1075: structured hosted reports and external runner outcomes.

This request concerns a maintained deployment and remote-access layer around those capabilities. If such a self-hosted deployment is already supported, a documentation pointer would also resolve the request.

## Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes existing behavior; the proposal is intended to be opt-in and preserve the current CLI and stdio MCP workflows.

title: fix(decision): take a distribution-less answer as a committed choice
body: - AI Gateway reruns an uncertain decision on a fallback model when `providerOptions.gateway.models` carries a `when: { confidenceBelow }` entry (Vercel changelog, 2026-10-06). The executor already forwards `providerOptions` untouched, so a decision-model fallback worked by accident. - A language-model fallback returns `{ type: 'choice', choice }` with no `probabilities` and no confidence. `selected()` in `packages/decision/src/decide.ts` threw `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` on it, so the escalated step died. - A distribution-less answer now reads as a committed choice: probability 1, confidence 0. `minProbability` lets it through, `minConfidence` blocks it, matching the documented "0 when the provider reports none". Score answers get the same treatment. - Docs show the gateway fallback on the executor and name the gate interaction. ```ts providerOptions: { gateway: { models: [{ model: 'openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions', when: { confidenceBelow: 0.6 } }] }, }, ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Live AI Gateway, Jev primary, `confidenceBelow: 0.99` to force the fallback, one choice and one score question, through the package's own `decide()`. | fallback | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `openai/gpt-5-nano` (language model) | `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID The decision model returned an answer without a choice distribution.` | `intent {choice:"billing", probability:1, confidence:0}`, `quality {choice:"2", probability:1, score:2, confidence:0}` | | `openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions` (decision model) | `intent {choice:"billing", probability:0.89, confidence:0.83}` | unchanged | - With the threshold below Jev's confidence the gateway returns the primary result unchanged and nothing in the executor differs from main. - `tests/cli.test.ts` fails on this branch and on `HEAD` alike with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`, unrelated to this change.

title: fix(mcp): point a role name that matches nothing at the node's text
body:
## What and why - `observe` names a status, an alert, or a list item from its text, so an unlabelled `

Saved.

` reads `status "Saved."`. A role query's `name` matches only the accessible name, which is empty here, so `locate {role: "status", name: "Saved."}` correctly finds nothing. - The zero-match advice then sent the agent back to the observation for the accessible name, or to `exact: false`. Neither can work for this node, and the `exact: false` hint repeated even on a query that already had it. - Each locate query now carries its own zero-match advice (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/catalog.ts`). A role query with a name says that `observe` can show a node's text in place of its name and prints the `getByRole(role).filter({ hasText })` and `getByText` calls that match that text. The `exact: false` hint only shows while the query is still exact. - Docs: the `locate` row in `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` and workflow step 2 in `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`. A real accessible name still matches as before, and the content-name policy from #583 is unchanged. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - unit level, not the MCP server against a browser (no Chromium in my environment) - `vitest run tests/unit/mcp-session.test.ts`: the two new tests fail on main and pass here | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `0 nodes match getByRole("status", name: "Saved.").`
`A test using this locator would fail with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND. Check the accessible name in the observation (observe), or loosen the match with exact: false.` | `0 nodes match getByRole("status", name: "Saved.").`
`A test using this locator would fail with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND. A role query matches the accessible name only, and observe can show a node's text in its place (a status or alert message, a list item). If "Saved." is that text, use screen.getByRole("status").filter({ hasText: "Saved." }) or screen.getByText("Saved."). Otherwise loosen the match with exact: false.` | With `exact: false` the last sentence is left out. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. title: feat(mobile): name screens by an app-declared marker with screenIdPrefix
body:
## What and why

- `screenTitle()` reads the screen only from an iOS navigation bar or an Android toolbar. React Native apps commonly hide that header (`headerShown: false`, custom headers), so every screen's location collapses to `<bundle id>` and the replay cache's start-screen check (`wrong-context`) cannot tell screens apart.
- New opt-in `mobile({ screenIdPrefix })`: the value after the prefix in an on-screen element's accessibility identifier (iOS) or resource id (Android) names the screen. React Native sets both from `testID`; a native Android id's `<package>:id/` is dropped before matching.
- When several elements match, hidden nodes and nodes wholly outside the viewport are skipped. Of the rest, the last in document order wins. The layered fixture proves that order on real iOS and Android trees; it does not establish ordering between separate navigator screens. iOS has no `visibleToUser`, so viewport overlap matters for screens kept mounted underneath.
- `screenMarker` is private. `screenName` requires the resolved viewport from `surface.ts`.
- A marker outranks the title bar. The option is opt-in, so this changes nothing for existing users. With the option unset, locations stay as they are. A screen that gains a marker gets a new location, so its recorded steps miss once with `wrong-context` and record again. The cache key is unchanged.
- The iOS navigation-bar identifier fix is #1183, not this PR. Related to #842, which stays open: an untitled sheet still takes the bar of the screen behind it.

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
const iphone = mobile({ platform: 'ios', screenIdPrefix: 'e2e-screen:' });
```

```tsx
// a React Native screen with headerShown: false
<View testID="e2e-screen:Offers" style={{ flex: 1 }}>{/* ... */}</View>
// location: "<bundle id> / Offers" (was "<bundle id>")
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Separate ordinary artifact completeness, private hosted eligibility, checkpoint recordedness and retained-file availability. - Bind original evidence bytes at producer boundaries and recheck custody, live secrecy and canonical unavailable-record source/time joins before store handoff. Consumers still host/upload artifacts and recheck containment, size and hash at use time. ```ts await session.close(); const bundle = session.exportDebugBundle(); // bundle is undefined while live or closing. // Use session.artifactsDir as the artifact path root. ``` Addresses #1074. Follow-up to [merged hosted sessions PR](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980), rebased onto main at `4b4b29727dde17eb135b030c031c10607a2d6299`. This branch contains only this follow-up's scope. ## Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Original SDK capture ticket] --> B[Bind original bytes within existing budget] B -->|Settles| C[Authorize before writes and recheck after IO] B -->|Deadline or abort| D[Invalidate ticket and fence late bytes] C --> E[Final cleanup and redaction] D --> E E --> F[Validate joins and freeze at close] F --> G[Caller rechecks and hosts allowlisted artifacts] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, at `c085adf09c3105c4421e7258daf3a74e25fc805f`. These scopes overlap, not additive coverage totals. - Current built public consumer smoke passed for immutable passed/failed/timed-out bundles. Current real Chromium CLI: 15 files, 77 passed, 1 existing skip; not historical-head reuse. - The descriptor race retains 28 source/built FD-safety assertions and three unchanged original probes. A never-callback public-assert regression fails on the preceding head and passes now: binding abandons at the existing absolute capture deadline or caller cancellation, invalidates the ticket first, and cannot renew authority from late bytes. The issued stream remains the sole FD close owner until safe cleanup. - Test-owned projects are cleaned after host close, preserving preexisting directories. Changeset, runner and debugging wording now cover no-retained-path registrations as well as ENOENT; other filesystem failures remain withheld. - Seventeen Cubic findings have published, attributed replies and resolved threads. These include runtime, schema, fixture/oracle and documentation fixes plus an intentional privacy-policy disposition. Complete ellipsis prose may still be withheld when prior cuts lack trusted completeness; a marker-only filter would reopen secret-prefix disclosures. This is not an availability fix. - Independent re-review accepted the three latest corrections, preserved the FD fix and found no new scoped critical/important issue. All 21 prior accepted privacy/custody obligations remain implemented. Complementary source/delta reviews are not exhaustive historical certification; private composition predates these corrections, not current public-head interoperability proof. - The failure-trace change hardens an existing genuine SDK helper; the current public hosted path did not reproduce the alleged failure-screen leak. Hashing is bounded to 64 KiB chunks, not Store buffering or opaque-engine allocation. - Exact-head GitHub validation: [docs](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38508718198), [spec](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38508718178) and [web benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38508718174) gates passed; [deterministic mobile](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38508718229) is still running. Trusted engine/caller OS code is not sandboxed; already-issued IO may retain its FD indefinitely if it ignores cancellation, with no atomic physical-close SLA. title: feat: add claude and codex plugins
body:
The e2e skills install only through `npx skills add` or `e2e init`, so Codex and Claude Code have no plugin to install them from, and nothing to submit to either app's plugin directory.

- One plugin package, `plugins/e2e/`, holds both skills (`e2e`, `create-verification-skill`). It ships no MCP server; the server still comes from the project's `e2e` dependency.
- Both apps install it from this repo: `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` (Codex) and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude) point at `./plugins/e2e`. Install it as `e2e@e2e`.
- `skills/` is still where the skills are written. `scripts/sync-plugin.ts` copies them into the plugin, prunes copies whose source is gone, writes `LICENSE` and the Claude manifest from the Codex one, and sets both manifests' `version` to the runner's.
- `pnpm plugins:check` is part of `pnpm check` and `spec.yml`, so a skill edit that wasn't synced fails CI.
- `version-packages` runs the sync. Claude caches installs by version, so the plugin needs a new version with every release or installs never update.
- Written by hand in the plugin: the Codex manifest apart from `version`, `assets/`, and each skill's `agents/openai.yaml` (Codex UI metadata).
- The example skill under `create-verification-skill` now has `SKILL.example.md` as its entry point, so neither app picks it up as a third skill.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[skills/] -->|pnpm plugins:sync| P[plugins/e2e/skills/]
  C[.codex-plugin/plugin.json] -->|sync| CL[.claude-plugin/plugin.json]
  R[packages/e2e version] -->|sync| C
  P --> M1[.agents/plugins/marketplace.json]
  P --> M2[.claude-plugin/marketplace.json]
```

Skill and docs changes that come with it:

- The Claude Code MCP command is now `claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- npx e2e mcp` everywhere: docs, skill, `e2e mcp --help`, and `init`'s hint. A user-scope server runs `npx e2e mcp` in whatever directory Claude starts in.
- Codex MCP setup is documented as a project `.codex/config.toml` entry (`docs/reference/mcp.mdx`, `docs/coding-agents.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`). `init` does not register Codex.
- The skill points to `npx e2e guide <topic>` when the plugin's copy and the installed package differ, and runs `e2e feedback --dry-run`, then sends only once the user agrees.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `claude plugin validate ./plugins/e2e` and `claude plugin validate ./` pass.
- Claude Code with an empty config directory: `claude plugin marketplace add ./` and `claude plugin install e2e@e2e` succeed, and the installed skills match `plugins/e2e/skills/`. A `claude -p --plugin-dir ./plugins/e2e` session lists `/e2e:e2e` and `/e2e:create-verification-skill`, loads `e2e:e2e`, reads `references/mcp.md` from the plugin, and quotes the project-scope command.
- Codex 0.162.1 with an empty `CODEX_HOME`: `codex plugin marketplace add ./` and `codex plugin add e2e@e2e` succeed. `codex plugin list` shows `e2e@e2e installed, enabled 0.20.0`. The app-server's `skills/list` returns exactly `e2e:e2e` and `e2e:create-verification-skill` with their display names and icons. A model session was not run: the OpenAI account was out of quota.
- `npx skills add . --list`, with and without `--full-depth`, still offers only `skills/*`; the plugin copies do not show up as duplicates.
- `scripts/sync-plugin.ts` on a scratch copy: deleting a skill and a reference makes `--check` exit 1 and list the stale files; sync removes them with no empty directories left; a new skill without `agents/openai.yaml` fails the check.
- The built `e2e mcp --help` prints `claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- npx e2e mcp`.
- Docs pages render in `mint dev`: the plugin install accordion on `/coding-agents` and the Codex block on `/reference/mcp`.

---
Written by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code), reviewed by Claude Fable.

feat(skills): add migrate-to-e2e for moving a suite one slice at a time
body:
- New consumer skill `skills/migrate-to-e2e/SKILL.md`. It moves a Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Detox, or Maestro suite to e2e one slice per session. The old suite keeps running beside the new tests until the user retires each old test.
- Before the inventory or any code, the agent reads two docs from a table of links: the migration guide for the detected runner and the engine page (`web.md` or `mobile.md`). The skill points at the guides for the API mapping instead of restating it, so a mapping change edits only the guide.
- Progress lives in a `MIGRATION.md` progress file, which the next session resumes from:
  - one row per source file (per test when a file's tests differ in status), with its assertion count before and after and its pass count per target
  - statuses: `todo`, `ported`, `retired`, `blocked`, `stays`
  - the shared helpers ported, the gaps found, and the `Next` slice
- A port counts as done when it passes 3/3 with `--repeat-each 3` on every target and has at least the source's assertion count.
- The agent asks the user before it deletes a source test or helper, edits the old runner's config or CI, or changes app code.
- Installed with `npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill migrate-to-e2e`. Like `create-verification-skill`, it is not shipped in the package and `e2e guide` does not read it.
- Wiring:
  - a "Migrate an existing suite" section in `docs/coding-agents.mdx`
  - a one-line pointer under the prompt on each `docs/migrate/*.mdx`
  - entries in `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `docs/migrate/maestro.mdx` now says Maestro matches text case-insensitively. Both benchmark arms lost runs on `getByText('Mute Account')` against "Mute account".

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[session starts] --> L{MIGRATION.md?}
  L -- no --> D[read guide + engine page] --> I[inventory, all tests todo] --> H[harness + smoke test]
  L -- yes --> R[read progress file + guide, recheck, run ported tests]
  R --> HD{harness done?}
  HD -- no --> H
  HD -- yes --> P[pick slice, write Next]
  H --> P --> T[port helpers, then each test] --> V[3/3 per target, assertion count] --> O[update progress file, hand over, ask what to retire]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `npx skills add . --list` from this branch lists `migrate-to-e2e` beside `e2e` and `create-verification-skill`.
- I benchmarked the skill against the Maestro guide's existing copy-paste prompt on the Bluesky social-app Maestro suite (`bluesky-social/social-app@eac1e13`, 22 flows). Setup: e2e 0.20.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.0, an iPhone 17 simulator on iOS 26.5, and an Android API 36 emulator. Each arm ran as a fresh-context agent with the same model and the same session preamble, which allowed no questions and no deletes.

| Session | Arm | Flows ported (total) | Proof | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | skill | 4 (4) | 3/3 iOS + 3/3 Android each, 24/24 | 119 min (CI wiring included) |
| 1 | guide prompt | 4 (4) | 3/3 iOS + 3/3 Android each | 33 min |
| 2 | skill | 4 (8) | 24/24 new, slice 1 rerun first, 16/16 full suite | 57 min |

- The benchmark stopped after three sessions: the system cleared its temp directory, which held both clones and the builds. It is not a full 22-flow comparison.
- What it showed:
  - The skill's resume path worked: session 2 read the progress file, reran slice 1, and took the `Next` slice.
  - Both arms preserved every Maestro assertion.
  - The skill is slower per session. Session 1 spent time on CI wiring and inventorying all 22 flows.
- Skill changes from the benchmark, already in this PR:
  - CI wiring is now proposed to the user instead of done unasked.
  - With no `e2e` MCP tools, the agent reads the trace page instead of building a bridge (session 2 built one).
  - A command in the progress file that cannot run here says so.
  - An unclear source step (a tap on a disabled control, a coordinate tap that may miss) keeps its intent, and the agent asks the user.
- e2e gaps both arms hit, to file separately:
  - a tap on a 1x1 pt node rounds outside its box
  - `app.clearState()` doesn't select a device when two are booted
  - `e2e init` writes `e2e@^0.19` under pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge`
- A fresh-context review found eight issues, all fixed:
  - `init` without `--yes` fails in an agent's shell
  - a resumed session could skip an unfinished harness
  - a helper could be deleted without confirmation
  - WebdriverIO was claimed without a guide
  - the `tests/` rule conflicted with Playwright's default `testDir`
  - the status-label claims only fit two of the guides
  - two docs wording issues

- I also ran the skill on a Playwright suite: `calcom/cal.com@54343aa`, 314 tests in 60 files (425 test-project pairs across 7 Playwright projects), Postgres and Mailhog in Docker, the production build, e2e 0.20.0 and @e2e-dev/web 0.14.0. One session: inventory, harness, and one slice.

| Source file | e2e | Explicit assertions | e2e `--repeat-each 5` | Playwright, same build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login.e2e.ts` (smoke; 1 test skipped in both) | `tests/login.e2e.ts` | 5 → 5 | 10/10 | 2/2 |
| `change-password.e2e.ts` | `tests/change-password.e2e.ts` | 1 → 1 | 5/5 | 1/1 |
| `change-theme.e2e.ts` | `tests/change-theme.e2e.ts` | 20 → 20, plus 3 `expect.poll` for `waitForFunction` | 30/30 | 6/6 |

- `playwright test --list` still lists the same 425 entries after the e2e files went in, and `e2e list` lists only `tests/`, so neither runner collects the other's.
- The source skips its logout test as "extremely flaky". Unskipped, the e2e port passed 3/3.
- Skill changes from the cal.com run, in this PR:
  - The progress file has one row per source file. A row per test would have been 314 rows. Grep found 291 of the 314 tests, so the skill now counts with the runner's list mode and warns that `--list` repeats each test once per project.
  - cal.com's `users.create()` is a Prisma factory that imports the app's code. It doesn't load under e2e: every `.ts` file loads as an ES module, so the generated Prisma client fails on `__dirname` and `@calcom/features` fails on a named import from CommonJS `@sentry/nextjs`. The skill now says to run such a helper unchanged in a child process with the repo's TypeScript runner. Here that was ts-node, behind a JSON-lines fixture.
  - The assertion count is now "at least the source's", because a `waitForFunction` becomes an `expect.poll`.
  - A test the source skips is now ported in full and stays skipped.
  - Hidden test-id twins take `{ visible: true }`. A second toast stacked over the first only showed up in the repeat runs, and `.last()` fixed it.
  - `app.command` doesn't inherit the shell's environment, so the skill says to load the old config's `.env` in the e2e config. It also covers monorepo placement, Playwright files already named `*.e2e.ts`, init's `test:e2e` script, and keeping a source helper the e2e suite still uses.
- Playwright guide rows added from the same run:
  - `page.click(selector)` and the other `page` methods that take a selector act on the first match. Ported to a strict locator they fail with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`.
  - A fixed `storageState: { cookies }` becomes `browser.setCookies`.
  - `waitForResponse` takes a glob tested against the full URL, so Playwright's `'/api/x'` never matches. `docs/reference/web.mdx` now lists the `?` wildcard and the `\` escape.
  - `waitForURL` takes one exact URL, so `'**/x'` never matches.
- e2e gaps from cal.com, to file separately:
  - The loader resolves a workspace package's file subpath (`@calcom/lib/constants`) but not its directory subpath (`@calcom/prisma/enums`). It handles `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` but not `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` (`packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts:203`). The one-condition fix got past that error locally.
  - `waitForURL` reads a string as an exact URL and `waitForResponse` reads it as a glob.

title: fix(web): read accessibility defaults from ElementInternals
body:
## What and why

- After hydration, a custom element that sets `ElementInternals.role` and `ariaLabel` loses its role and accessible name in e2e. The browser accessibility tree still exposes them, but the engine and Playwright role selectors read content attributes.
- Capture live `role`, `ariaLabel`, and `ariaHidden` defaults before application scripts run. The shared semantic reader gives present attributes priority, including empty values, without changing the page's DOM. Other internals properties remain unsupported.
- Keep native role matching and closed-shadow scopes. Recompute names when supported defaults affect a control or its label, and retain hidden content explicitly referenced by `aria-labelledby`. Pages that never attach internals use the recorded native matches without another DOM walk.
- Addresses item 2 of #1020. Includes a web patch changeset and updates the screen reference and test-writing skill. No public API change.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[attachInternals] --> B[Live internals in WeakMap]
  B --> C[Shared semantic reader]
  C --> D[Observations and accessible names]
  C --> E[Affected role and name matches]
  F[Native Playwright role matches] --> G[Merge per search root]
  E --> G
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI against the same scratch hydration test on main and this branch, with `e2e run element-internals.e2e.ts --video=on`. Both start with a server-rendered image; the test replaces it with a custom element whose role and name come from internals.
- Both runs recorded videos. They remain local because `gh pr create --attach` rejected the upload with `attaching files requires write access to the repository` for this fork contribution. The terminal evidence appears below.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| Initial image matches, hydrated image fails with match count 0 | Both visibility assertions pass |

Main failure:

```text
ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByRole("image", name: "₹1,234.00")
expected: visible
observed: no node (match count 0)
```

Branch result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

- Five Chromium regressions cover hydration and live overrides, closed roots and composed locators, mixed content-attribute states, first-script initialization in frames and replacement contexts, and native names affected by hidden descendants or label references. The crosscheck fixture compares the custom image's role and name with Chrome's accessibility tree.
- `bench:ab` on testbed `tests/forms.e2e.ts`, six randomly ordered main/branch pairs with one worker. Every outcome, step, and counter matched. The suite and wall-time comparisons fall within the configured 5% threshold.

| Metric | main median | this branch median | Paired change, 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Forms suite | 2.20 s | 2.25 s | +0.5%, -4.0% to +4.1% |
| Process wall time | 3.31 s | 3.29 s | -1.8%, -4.1% to +4.1% |

- A synthetic page with 5,000 nodes nested at depth 20 and no attached internals gave median role-query times of 2.45 ms for the native locator control and 2.75 ms for this branch, over six alternating samples each. This checks the path that skips the fallback DOM walk.
- Verified on Node 26.9.0, pnpm 12.3.4, and Playwright 1.63.0 Chromium. Firefox and WebKit were not exercised for this change.

title: fix(e2e): load a directory's index.ts through a package subpath or # import
body: - Node.js throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` when an ES module `import` names a directory. e2e's loader moved only `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` onto the TypeScript file behind the target (`packages/e2e/src/config/esm-hooks.ts`, `resolveExport`), so these failed collection from a `.ts` test or helper: - a subpath of a workspace package without `exports` that is a directory: `@calcom/prisma/enums` → `packages/prisma/enums/index.ts` - an `exports` entry that names a directory - a `#` import mapped to a directory - Both codes now take the same fallback, so the directory loads its `main` or `index.ts`, the way TypeScript resolves it and the way a relative `./dir` import already did. - The unit test's stand-in resolver reported a directory as `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (it read the path and got `EISDIR`), so the existing `#dir` case passed while the real import failed. It now throws what Node.js throws. The integration fixture gains a package without `exports` imported as `@scope/legacy/enums` and as `#legacy/enums`. - Not covered: under Yarn PnP, a package subpath that names a directory still fails. PnP's resolver throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` without the target's `url`, so the loader can't tell which directory it found. The `#` case already worked under PnP. The docs and the changeset say so. - Found while migrating cal.com's Playwright suite with the `migrate-to-e2e` skill (#1109): its Prisma factory imports `@calcom/prisma/enums`. ```ts // tests/enums.e2e.ts in a monorepo whose workspace package has no `exports` import { MembershipRole } from '@calcom/prisma/enums'; ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `calcom/cal.com@54343aa`, a test importing `@calcom/prisma/enums`, run with `npx e2e run`. I swapped this branch's built `dist/config/esm-hooks.js` into its `node_modules/e2e`: | e2e 0.20.0 (main) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `COLLECTION_ERROR`: `Directory import '…/node_modules/@calcom/prisma/enums' is not supported resolving ES modules imported from …/tests/enums-probe.e2e.ts` | `✓ tests/enums-probe.e2e.ts (1 test)`, `1 passed` | - `tests/integration/typescript-loader.test.ts` with the fix reverted fails with the same `Directory import … @scope/legacy/enums` collection error; with it, 12/12 pass. The unit file's `#dir` case also fails with the fix reverted. - A fresh-context review checked that `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` carries `url` on Node 22.22.3, 22.23.2, 24.8.0, 24.21.0, and 26. It also checked that `require()` of a directory still fails as Node reports it, and that a JavaScript importer still gets Node's resolution. It found the Yarn PnP gap above and a stale header comment; both are addressed.

title: fix(mobile): bound reads by operation budget with last-read grace (#1099)
body:
## What and why

- On `@e2e-dev/mobile` a snapshot or screenshot that hung held the step until the test timeout (#1099). Every device read now runs under the operation's budget (`InputBudget.read`, `packages/mobile/src/support.ts`), so a hung read fails the step as `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` (or `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED` once an input of that operation went out).
- Bounding reads alone broke slow polls: on iOS a snapshot takes 1-2 s, so the last read of `waitFor`/`expect`/`toHaveScreenshot` got cut at the deadline and failed as a hang instead of `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`.
- Core fix: `ReadWindow` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts`). Each read of one wait gets the time left plus the slowest read that wait already finished, capped by the running phase's deadline. A read cut off within that tail ends the wait as a normal timeout; a read that hung with more time left is still the failure.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile` now needs `e2e >=0.21.4` (this PR's e2e patch changeset ships it): on 0.21.3 core, mobile reads would end at the deadline with no last-read grace.
- No public type change: `ReadWindow` is internal; `OperationContext.timeoutMs` docs note the last read can get more than the deadline leaves.

## Issue

Fixes #1099

## Verified

Ran it locally: no device run. Unit evidence on the head merged with main (`f4e8c8e1a` + nit `7f1d05ed8`):

- Reverting the read bound (`readWithin` -> direct call) fails 6 mobile tests, e.g. "bounds a snapshot by the operation budget" and "takes no second snapshot for a capture the budget abandoned".
- Reverting the slowest-read grace in `ReadWindow.timeoutMs()` fails 5 core tests (time, locator-engine, locator-wait-for), e.g. "lets a slow last resolve finish past the deadline: a late match resolves".
- Reverting the slowest-read term in `ReadWindow.cutOff()` fails "ends on a read cut off within the longest read time of the deadline, and fails on one that hung with more left".
- `pnpm check` passes; e2e (3171), mobile (420), web (290) unit suites pass.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| A hung snapshot holds the step until the test timeout | The step fails at its own timeout |
| (with bounded reads only) a slow last iOS read in `expect` fails as a hang | The last read finishes; a missing node is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` / `ASSERTION_FAILED` |

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: fix(cli): report a skipped test in one shard only
body: ## What and why - `--shard` cuts its slices from the runnable tests only, and `applyShard` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts:776`) left every skipped pair (`{ skip }`, `test.skip(...)` at declaration, a missing capability) untouched. So each shard kept every skipped test, and `e2e list --shard`, the `list` summary, `junit.xml`, `summary.md`, and `report.json` of every shard listed it again. A matrix of 3 shards over 3 tests and 1 skipped one reports 6 results instead of 4, and anything that adds the shards' JUnit files up counts the skip 3 times. - Now a skipped test is reported by the shard that runs the test before it in report order, the first shard when none comes before. The cut itself is unchanged: slices still differ by at most one runnable test, and a skipped test still never makes a shard non-empty. - In the other shards the pair becomes `filtered` and keeps its own `skip`, the way a `platforms` miss already does, so `NO_TESTS` still counts it as skipped with `test.skip` and the "split across N shards" count does not grow. - Playwright also reports each skipped test in one shard, but counts skipped tests as items of the cut; here the cut stays runnable tests only, so the documented slice sizes hold. ```ts // packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts, applyShard (this branch) let previousKept = shard.index === 1; return pairs.map((pair) => { if (pair.test.kind !== 'test') return pair; if (pair.disposition === 'skip') return previousKept ? pair : { ...pair, disposition: 'filtered' as const }; if (pair.disposition !== 'run') return pair; previousKept = kept.has(shardItem(pair)); ... ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project, built CLI, one file with `one`, `two`, `three`, and `later` (`{ skip: 'not ready yet' }`), `e2e run --shard i/3 --reporter list,junit`: | shard | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | 1/3 | `1 passed \| 1 skipped (2)`, junit `tests="2" skipped="1"` | `1 passed (1)`, junit `tests="1" skipped="0"` | | 2/3 | `1 passed \| 1 skipped (2)`, junit `tests="2" skipped="1"` | `1 passed (1)`, junit `tests="1" skipped="0"` | | 3/3 | `1 passed \| 1 skipped (2)`, junit `tests="2" skipped="1"` | `1 passed \| 1 skipped (2)`, junit `tests="2" skipped="1"` | - The shards' `report.json` files validate against `report-v1.schema.json`, and their `summary.selected` now add up to the unsharded run's. - New unit test in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/select.test.ts` (a skipped test first, in the middle, and last, over 2 shards) fails on main and passes here. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: cli: flags for every `e2e init` wizard choice, so a host can run it non-interactively
body:
### Problem

`init --yes` fixes every wizard answer: Web engine, Vercel AI Gateway, skill and MCP config in both locations, no dependency install. A tool that runs `init` for its users cannot pick anything else without a TTY.

We build [cezar](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar), a local orchestrator that runs coding-agent tasks in parallel git worktrees and gates each task on check steps. e2e is the browser check we recommend; cezar sets it up for users in one click (it runs `e2e init`, configures the project, and proves it with `e2e list` and `e2e run`).

Today our setup runs `init --yes`, then a coding agent rewires the model provider, deletes `.cursor/` when the repo never used Cursor, and installs dependencies. That costs an agent session for choices the wizard already knows how to make.

### Proposed API

```sh
npx e2e init --yes \
  --engine web \
  --provider openrouter \
  --skills agents,claude \
  --mcp claude \
  --install
```

- One flag per wizard question. The values are the wizard's options.
- An omitted flag keeps today's `--yes` default, so nothing changes for existing callers.

Happy to open a PR for this if you are interested. Let me know if this shape works or what you would prefer.

CLI flags

title: cli: `e2e doctor --json` as a preflight a host can run (follow-up to #536)
body:
### Problem

Follow-up to #536, which was moved to the internal tracker. Is it still planned? Here is a host use case for it.

We build [cezar](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar), a local orchestrator that runs coding-agent tasks in parallel git worktrees and gates each task on check steps. e2e is the browser check we recommend; cezar sets it up for users in one click (it runs `e2e init`, configures the project, and proves it with `e2e list` and `e2e run`).

cezar shows "e2e installed" in its settings based on files existing. A missing model key, an uninstalled browser or an old Node shows up only when a check step exits 2, after the coding agent has already spent its session on the task. The field we need most: which credential variable the configured model reads, and whether it is set.

### Proposed API

```sh
npx e2e doctor --json
```

```json
{
  "version": "0.20.0",
  "ok": false,
  "checks": [
    { "id": "node", "status": "pass" },
    { "id": "config", "status": "pass", "targets": ["web"] },
    { "id": "browser", "status": "pass" },
    { "id": "model-credential", "status": "fail", "code": "MODEL_UNAVAILABLE", "reads": ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"] }
  ]
}
```

- No app start and no model call, so it is cheap enough to run before every task.
- Exits 0 when every check passes and 2 otherwise.

config: `E2E_CACHE_DIR` to point the replay cache at a host-provided directory
body:
### Problem

We build [cezar](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar), a local orchestrator that runs coding-agent tasks in parallel git worktrees and gates each task on check steps. e2e is the browser check we recommend; cezar sets it up for users in one click (it runs `e2e init`, configures the project, and proves it with `e2e list` and `e2e run`).

Every cezar task starts in a fresh worktree. `.e2e/cache/` is gitignored, so every task re-records every `agent.act` with live model calls. cezar gives check steps a shared per-project directory, but using it means every user pastes this into their config:

```ts
cache: {
  mode: 'read-write',
  dir: process.env.CEZ_SHARED_CACHE_DIR ? join(process.env.CEZ_SHARED_CACHE_DIR, 'e2e') : '.e2e/cache',
},
```

We checked that cache writes go through a temp file and an atomic rename (`cache/store.js`), so sharing one directory across parallel worktrees is already safe. Thanks for that.

### Proposed API

```sh
E2E_CACHE_DIR=~/.cezar/cache/my-project/e2e npx e2e run
```

- `E2E_CACHE_DIR` overrides `cache.dir` and leaves `cache.mode` alone.
- `--no-cache` still wins.
- The same path rules as `cache.dir` apply.

title: cli: a wall-clock budget for `e2e run`, like `explore --timeout`
body:
### Problem

`e2e explore --timeout` bounds the whole run. `e2e run` has only the per-attempt `timeout` (120000 ms by default) and `startupTimeout`, so its worst case is tests × attempts × timeout.

We build [cezar](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar), a local orchestrator that runs coding-agent tasks in parallel git worktrees and gates each task on check steps. e2e is the browser check we recommend; cezar sets it up for users in one click (it runs `e2e init`, configures the project, and proves it with `e2e list` and `e2e run`).

The check runs unattended and holds one of the user's few parallel task slots. When a change breaks the app so every test times out, a 40-test suite holds that slot for about 80 minutes. `--max-failures` helps with failures but not with a suite that is slow and still passing.

### Proposed API

```sh
npx e2e run --max-duration 900000
```

```ts
export default { maxDuration: 900_000 } satisfies E2EConfig;
```

- Named to avoid clashing with the per-attempt `timeout`.
- When the budget is reached, it behaves like `--max-failures`: nothing more is dispatched, running tests end as `interrupted`, and the report says why (for example a `RUN_TIMEOUT` code).
- The exit code is your call.

Happy to open a PR for this if you are interested. Let me know if this shape works or what you would prefer.

title: config: pass host env vars through to `app.command` without listing them in the config
body:
### Problem

`app.command` inherits only `PATH`, `HOME`, the temp variables and `command.env`. That is a good default, because it keeps model keys out of the app. The only way to add a variable is to name it in the committed config, which works for the project's own variables but not for values a host supplies per run.

We build [cezar](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar), a local orchestrator that runs coding-agent tasks in parallel git worktrees and gates each task on check steps. e2e is the browser check we recommend; cezar sets it up for users in one click (it runs `e2e init`, configures the project, and proves it with `e2e list` and `e2e run`).

cezar can inject per-task values into a check step, such as a per-task database URL or secrets the user stored for checks. To reach the app, each one has to be named in `e2e.config.ts`. The shortcut `env: { ...process.env }` works, but it also passes the model keys to the app and undoes the isolation.

### Proposed API

```ts
app: {
  command: {
    executable: 'npm',
    args: ['run', 'dev', '--', '--port', '{port}'],
    inheritEnv: ['DATABASE_URL', 'STRIPE_*'],
  },
},
```

```sh
# The same list from a host, without editing the config
E2E_APP_INHERIT_ENV=DATABASE_URL,STRIPE_* npx e2e run
```

- Names and trailing-`*` patterns only. A listed variable is copied when it is set.
- `command.env` still wins over an inherited value.

Happy to open a PR for this if you are interested. Let me know if this shape works or what you would prefer.

### Which surface

config keys

title: feat(config): pass host env vars to app.command via inheritEnv and E2E_APP_INHERIT_ENV (#1119)
body: ## What and why Fixes #1119. Currently, `app.command` processes inherit only `PATH`, `HOME`, temp variables, and `command.env`. This provides good security defaults, but when an orchestrator or CI host wants to supply run-specific environment variables (e.g. dynamic database URLs, external test credentials) without modifying the committed `e2e.config.ts`, developers had to resort to `env: { ...process.env }`, which leaks model keys and breaks isolation. This change adds: 1. `inheritEnv?: readonly string[]` to `CommandConfig` (`app.command.inheritEnv`), accepting variable names or trailing `*` prefix patterns (e.g., `['DATABASE_URL', 'STRIPE_*']`). 2. Support for `E2E_APP_INHERIT_ENV` environment variable on the host (comma-separated list of variable names or patterns, e.g. `DATABASE_URL,STRIPE_*`). 3. Matching host environment variables are copied into the spawned process's environment. `command.env` values still take precedence over inherited variables. 4. Validation for `inheritEnv` in `normalizeCommand` ensuring an array of non-empty strings. 5. Documentation updates in `docs/reference/config.mdx` and `docs/reference/environment.mdx`. ## Verified Ran locally: yes - `pnpm --filter e2e run typecheck` passes (including `sdk-types.ts`). - `node packages/e2e/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/e2e/tests/unit/managed-process.test.ts -t "inherits environment variables"` passes. - `node packages/e2e/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/e2e/tests/unit/config.test.ts -t "validates inheritEnv"` passes. - `pnpm run lint` (`oxlint`), `pnpm run docs:check-errors`, `pnpm run check:peer-ranges`, and `pnpm run check:install-scripts` pass. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

Release notes

Sourced from playwright-core's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

  • 9184a35: Add ordered text, file, and JSON parts to experimental decision state. Support image input in OpenAI Decisions and language model adapters. Gateway retains its existing string and JSON request format and rejects files, as does TypeSafe AI.

    Arrays passed directly as state now contain decision state parts. Wrap JSON arrays in an object or a json part.

  • 268225c: feat(provider): add a portable max reasoning level with native provider mappings, compatibility coercions, and budget-based fallback support.

    Compatibility notes:

    • TypeScript source compatibility: Adding max widens LanguageModelV4CallOptions['reasoning'] and the derived ReasoningLevel type. Third-party providers and consumers with exhaustive switches or Record<ReasoningLevel, ...> mappings must handle max before upgrading. Ordinary calls using existing reasoning levels remain accepted.
    • Amazon Bedrock: Existing Nova 2 calls using portable reasoning: 'xhigh' now send maxReasoningEffort: 'high' instead of the unsupported 'max', and return a compatibility warning. Anthropic and OpenAI Bedrock effort mappings retain their existing xhigh behavior. Release notes

Sourced from @​modelcontextprotocol/server's releases.

@​modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy@​2.3.1

Patch Changes

  • #2952 5a18673 Thanks @​claude! - requireBearerAuth in @modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy takes the optional expectedResource that @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0 and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0 added: the resource the token must be issued for (its audience), usually the server's URL. When it is set, a token is accepted only if the verifier reports that value in AuthInfo.resource; the two are compared as strings, ignoring a fragment and one trailing slash. A token reported for another value, or for none, is answered 401 invalid_token with the usual WWW-Authenticate challenge. When it is not set, nothing changes. The package stays frozen otherwise; this option is added so that its requireBearerAuth matches the 1.x middleware it is a copy of.
