title: feat(cli): add e2e run --max-duration and maxDuration config
body:
Closes #1118.

`e2e run` had only the per-attempt `timeout`, so a suite where every test hangs holds its CI slot for tests x attempts x timeout. This adds a run-level budget that stops the way `--max-failures` does.

```sh
npx e2e run --max-duration 900000
```

```ts
export default { targets, maxDuration: 900_000 } satisfies E2EConfig;
```

- `--max-duration <ms>` overrides the config's `maxDuration`. Both take a positive integer of ms; `0` is `INVALID_CONFIG`.
- The clock starts with the scheduler (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts`), so app startup stays bounded by `startupTimeout` and is not counted.
- When it runs out, the scheduler goes through the `--max-failures` stop path (`stopEarly` with a `SkipInfo`): nothing more is dispatched, running tests end as `interrupted`, and tests that never started are skipped with the new cause `time-limit`.
- The runner records one `RUN_TIMEOUT` run error (class `test`) and exits 1, not 130. `--last-failed` picks up the interrupted and `time-limit` tests.
- A `maxDuration` past `setTimeout`'s cap (2^31-1 ms, now shared as `MAX_TIMER_MS` in `internal/time.ts`) sets no timer instead of firing at once.
- `e2e explore` ignores the config's `maxDuration` and keeps its own `--timeout`.
- Wire: the report schema's skip causes gain `time-limit` (additive). `maxDuration` stays out of the config digest, so turning it on leaves recordings valid.
- Docs: `reference/config#maxduration`, the `reference/cli` flag row, `reference/errors` `RUN_TIMEOUT`, the CI guide, and `skills/e2e/references/running.md`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI, scratch project on the testbed app (web engine, 1 worker), config `maxDuration: 600_000`. The suite has one passing test, one that sleeps 30 s, one after it, and a second file.
- `e2e run --max-duration 5000`: the flag wins over the config, the run stops at about 5 s, and it exits 1.

```
 ↓ |web| tests/b-quick.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 skipped)
 ❯ |web| tests/a-slow.e2e.ts (3 tests | 1 interrupted | 1 skipped) 4.78s
   ✓ loads the home page 150ms
   × waits on a slow backend (interrupted) 4.63s
   ↓ never starts [run stopped at its time limit of 5000 ms (maxDuration)]

 ERROR  test error RUN_TIMEOUT
run stopped at its time limit of 5000 ms (maxDuration): the running tests end as interrupted, the rest are skipped

      Tests  1 interrupted | 1 passed | 2 skipped (4)
     Errors  1 error
   Duration  5.13s (startup 91ms)
exit=1
```

- `report.json`: `status: failed`, `exitCode: 1`, `errors: [{ code: RUN_TIMEOUT, category: test }]`, skip cause `time-limit` on the two tests that never started.
- With the config set to `maxDuration: 3_000` and no flag, `e2e run --last-failed` selected exactly the 3 tests that had not passed and stopped at 3 s with the same output.

title: feat(config): pass listed host env vars to app.command with inheritEnv
body: ## What and why - `app.command.inheritEnv` copies host variables into the app process, by exact name or trailing-`*` prefix. A host that sets per-run values (a per-task `DATABASE_URL`, check secrets) no longer has to list each one in `e2e.config.ts` or spread `process.env`, which also hands the app the model keys. - A variable is copied only when it is set. `command.env` wins over an inherited value. Without `inheritEnv`, nothing changes. - Validation at config load (`INVALID_CONFIG`): a bare `*` (it would undo the isolation), a `*` anywhere but the end, an empty entry, `=`, or whitespace. - Inherited values are redacted from a quoted startup failure the same way `command.env` values are (`packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`). - `openHost` and the runner copy from the `env` they resolve against, not always `process.env`, so a programmatic host passing `env` gets its own values. - The `E2E_APP_INHERIT_ENV` env var form from the issue is left out on purpose: a host that controls the environment can already set the listed variables. ```ts app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000', command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'], inheritEnv: ['DATABASE_URL', 'STRIPE_*'], }, }, ``` Closes #1119 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project in `/tmp` with the built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` linked in, and an `app.command` (a node server) that prints the variables it sees and serves them as a page. Config: `inheritEnv: ['DATABASE_URL', 'STRIPE_*']`, `env: { STRIPE_HOOK: 'from-config' }`. `DATABASE_URL=postgres://host/db STRIPE_KEY=sk_test_host STRIPE_HOOK=from-host OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake-model-key AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=fake-gateway-key e2e run tests/env.e2e.ts` ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 95ms ✓ |web| tests/env.e2e.ts (1 test) 252ms ✓ app sees only the listed host env 252ms ``` App log: the listed variables arrive, `command.env` beats the host value, and the model keys stay out: ```text DATABASE_URL=postgres://host/db STRIPE_KEY=sk_test_host STRIPE_HOOK=from-config OPENAI_API_KEY=(unset) AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=(unset) ``` - The same config without `inheritEnv` behaves as before: `DATABASE_URL=(unset) STRIPE_KEY=(unset) ...`. - `openHost({ env: { ...process.env, DATABASE_URL: 'postgres://per-task/db' } })` with `DATABASE_URL=postgres://orchestrator/db` in the shell: the app logged `DATABASE_URL=postgres://per-task/db`. - Invalid entries: ```text ERROR configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config) target "web" app.command.inheritEnv[1] cannot be "*": it would pass every variable to the app, model keys included; list the names or prefixes it needs ``` ```text target "web" app.command.inheritEnv[0] must be a variable name or a prefix ending in * (such as "STRIPE_*"), got "STR*PE" ``` - Unit tests cover matching, precedence, the passed `env`, redaction, and validation. The precedence test fails when the merge order is swapped. Testbed suite not run (its fixed port could clash with other local runs); the change only applies when `inheritEnv` is set. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(mobile): read XCUIElementType class names as their XCTest types
body: ## What and why On iOS, agent-device's WebDriver runtime reports XCUITest class names such as `XCUIElementTypeButton` and `XCUIElementTypeStaticText`, where the native runner reports `Button` and `StaticText`. Every hosted Appium cloud goes through that runtime: TestMu AI, BrowserStack and AWS Device Farm. The mobile engine read those as unknown types, so `getByRole('button', …)` matched nothing, and `observe` listed nodes as `xcuielement-type-button`. `normalizeKind` now drops the `XCUIElementType` prefix before mapping the type. A button is then a `button`, a tab bar's buttons are `tab`s, and the navigation bar titles the screen. This was split out of #772 as requested in its review. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm check` passes. - `@e2e-dev/mobile` tests pass (251), including a new case in which a snapshot with every type `XCUIElementType`-prefixed projects the same roles and screen title as the native one. - Seen live on a TestMu AI iOS simulator and a real iPhone: `getByRole('button', …)` matched only with this change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change. n/a - [ ] Docs updated. n/a (no behaviour documented) - [ ] Contract change. n/a - [ ] Engine contract change. n/a 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(config): E2E_CACHE_DIR and --cache-dir override cache.dir
body: Closes #1117 - `E2E_CACHE_DIR` and `--cache-dir ` replace `cache.dir`, so worktrees and checkouts of one project can share a replay cache without editing the config. - Precedence: `--cache-dir` > `E2E_CACHE_DIR` > `cache.dir` > `.e2e/cache`. The mode is untouched and `--no-cache` still wins. - Both resolve from the project root, like `cache.dir` and `--output`, and go through the same output-overlap checks. Error messages name the source (`would hold --cache-dir .e2e/results/c under results/`). - Read once in `resolveConfig` (`packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts`, `cacheDirOverride`), so workers, watch mode, and `e2e cache` all get the same directory. A blank `E2E_CACHE_DIR` counts as unset, the same rule as other `E2E_*` variables. - The flag is on `run` and `cache ls|stats|clear`. `explore` and `mcp` don't use the cache, so they only get the variable through the output-overlap check. - `--cache-dir` together with a custom `cache.store` is `INVALID_CONFIG`, because the flag would name a directory nothing reads. The ambient variable is ignored there. - `REPLAY_STALE` advice no longer says "commit" for a cache directory outside the project. - Vitest blanks `E2E_CACHE_DIR` and `scripts/bench-ab.ts` drops it, so a developer's shared cache never leaks into fixture projects or A/B runs. - Docs: `cache.mdx` gets a "Share the cache across checkouts" section (with the note that checkouts need the same `projectId` or package `name`), plus `reference/cli`, `reference/config`, `reference/environment`, and `skills/e2e/references/running.md`. ```bash E2E_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/my-app/e2e npx e2e run npx e2e run --cache-dir ../shared-cache ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The built CLI on a scratch project in `/tmp`, copied into two separate checkouts (`checkout-a`, `checkout-b`). It has a web target, one `agent.act` step, and a scripted model that logs each call, so a replay is visible as zero model calls. `checkout-a`, `E2E_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/verify-1117/shared e2e run` records: ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 89ms [scripted model] call 1 [scripted model] call 2 ✓ increments the counter > agent.act "increment the counter once" 399ms · 2 model calls Test Files 1 passed (1) AI 4 tokens · 2 model calls · scripted/scripted-counter Cache 1 missed ``` `checkout-b`, same variable, replays from the shared directory with no model call. Its own `.e2e/` has no `cache/`: ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 94ms ✓ increments the counter > agent.act "increment the counter once" 172ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Cache 1 replayed ``` Other checks in `checkout-b`: ```text $ E2E_CACHE_DIR=../shared e2e cache ls TEST TARGET INSTRUCTION AGE ACTIONS tests/counter.e2e.ts::increments%20the%20counter web bc8b5c526994 <1m 1 $ e2e run --cache-dir ../shared -> Cache 1 replayed $ E2E_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/nowhere e2e run --cache-dir /tmp/.../shared -> Cache 1 replayed (flag wins) $ e2e run -> Cache 1 missed (default .e2e/cache) $ E2E_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/.../shared e2e run --no-cache -> 2 model calls, no Cache line $ E2E_CACHE_DIR=.e2e e2e run output ".e2e" (the default) is the cache directory .e2e or inside it; keep results and the replay cache apart $ e2e run --cache-dir .e2e/results/c output ".e2e" (the default) would hold --cache-dir .e2e/results/c under results/, which the run owns; move --cache-dir or the output ```

title: feat(cli): flag per e2e init wizard question
body: Closes #1114. `e2e init` takes a flag for every wizard question, so a host that sets up e2e for its users can pick each answer without a TTY. ```sh npx e2e init --yes \ --engine web \ --gateway openrouter \ --skills .agents/skills \ --mcp .mcp.json \ --install ``` | Flag | Values | Prompt it answers | | --- | --- | --- | | `--engine ` | `web`, `mobile`, `none` | Which engine? | | `--gateway ` | `vercel`, `openrouter`, `openai-compatible`, `chatgpt`, `copilot`, `opencode-console`, `grok`, `none` | Which model gateway? | | `--endpoint ` | HTTPS, or HTTP on loopback | Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API | | `--skills ` | `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, comma-separated or repeated, or `none` | Install the e2e skill? | | `--mcp ` | `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, comma-separated or repeated, or `none` | Register the MCP server? | | `--install` / `--no-install` | | Install dependencies? | - Values are the ids the wizard already uses (`GATEWAYS`, `getEnginePresets()`, `SKILL_LOCATIONS`, `MCP_LOCATIONS`), so a new preset gets a flag value for free. - The flag is `--gateway`, not the `--provider` the issue proposed. The code, the prompt, and telemetry all say gateway, and `e2e login [provider]` already uses provider ids (`openai`, `github-copilot`) that differ from these. - A flag skips its prompt with or without `--yes`. Without `--yes`, the prompts for omitted flags and the "Apply these changes?" confirmation still appear. An omitted flag under `--yes` keeps today's default, so `init --yes` output is byte-identical to main. - Bad values exit 2 through commander before `init` runs, so nothing is written. `--endpoint` without `--gateway openai-compatible` is also rejected. - `--skills`/`--mcp` override the locations found by an earlier run (`chooseLocations`, `packages/e2e/src/cli/init.ts`). `--engine`/`--gateway`/`--endpoint` with an existing config log a warning naming the flags that were ignored. - Telemetry: `usedFlags` still sends flag names only, never values. It used to report both `--install` and `--no-install` when either was given, because the pair shares one attribute; it now reports only the one that was passed. `--endpoint` never leaves the machine. - `--yes` help said "Playwright, AI on, no installation". It now lists the real defaults: web, vercel, every skill and MCP location, no installation. - `validateEndpoint` moved to `init/gateways.ts` so the CLI parser and the prompt share it. - Docs: `reference/cli.mdx` flag table, `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`, and `telemetry.mdx` (which was missing `opencode-console`). The Detox and Maestro migration prompts now use `init --yes --engine mobile` instead of swapping `@e2e-dev/web` by hand. Those prompts run `npx e2e init`, so the new flag needs a release to work. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built `packages/e2e` on main (`/tmp/e2e-main`) and on this branch, then ran `init --yes` from each in an empty `/tmp` dir. Stdout is identical. The only file that differs is the skill's `references/setup.md`, which this PR edits. ``` $ node dist/cli/bin.js init --yes --engine web --gateway openrouter --skills .agents/skills --mcp .mcp.json --install ● Add dev dependencies: e2e@^0.20.0, @e2e-dev/web@^0.14.0, ai@^7.0.0, zod@^4.1.8, @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider@^3.0.0 ● Add scripts: test:e2e (e2e run) ◆ Created package.json ◆ Created e2e.config.ts ◆ Created tests/example.e2e.ts ◆ Created .agents/skills/e2e/ (9 files) ◆ Created .mcp.json (e2e mcp server) ◆ Updated .gitignore (10 entries) added 55 packages, and audited 56 packages in 4s └ Next: APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run test:e2e $ ls -A .agents .gitignore .mcp.json e2e.config.ts node_modules package-lock.json package.json tests $ npx e2e list tests/example.e2e.ts › app opens [web] ``` No `.claude/` and no `.cursor/`. `npm install` ran, and the installed CLI lists the example test. ``` $ init --yes --engine none --gateway none --skills none --mcp none ● Skipped the agent skill; agents can still print it with npm exec -- e2e guide ● Skipped the MCP server; register it later with: claude mcp add e2e -- npx e2e mcp $ ls -A .gitignore e2e.config.ts package.json tests $ init --yes --engine playwright error: option '--engine ' argument 'playwright' is invalid. Allowed choices are web, mobile, none. (exit 2) $ init --yes --mcp claude error: option '--mcp ' argument 'claude' is invalid. unknown MCP config file "claude"; expected .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, none (exit 2) $ init --yes --endpoint https://llm.example/v1 error: --endpoint is the base URL for --gateway openai-compatible; pass that gateway with it (exit 2) ``` None of the rejected runs wrote anything (the directory stayed empty). I also ran `init --engine web --gateway none --skills none --mcp .mcp.json --no-install` interactively in a pty. The only prompt was "Apply these changes?", and it wrote `.mcp.json` with no skill directory.

title: fix(plugins): sync the plugin with skills that landed beside it
body:
`spec` and `release` fail on main since #1107. #1107 copies `skills/*` into `plugins/e2e/skills/`. It landed after #1104, #1108, and #1109 had changed those skills, so its copies were stale: - `pnpm plugins:check` (the `check` job) reports four stale `skills/e2e` copies, and `migrate-to-e2e` (new in #1109) has no hand-written `agents/openai.yaml`. - The release job's `version-packages` runs `scripts/sync-plugin.ts`, which exits on the missing `openai.yaml`. No release PR or publish can run until this lands. Fix: - Add `plugins/e2e/skills/migrate-to-e2e/agents/openai.yaml`, matching its siblings. It allows implicit invocation, since the skill's description asks to trigger on "migrate our tests to e2e". - Regenerate the copies with `pnpm plugins:sync`. - List `migrate-to-e2e` in the plugin README and on `docs/coding-agents.mdx`, which named only two skills. - `migrate-to-e2e` now offers gap feedback with a `--dry-run` preview and sends it only on consent, as the e2e skill's Feedback section requires. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes | main ([spec run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38546808041), [release run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38546808250)) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `plugins/e2e/skills/migrate-to-e2e/agents/openai.yaml is missing; write one by hand`
`Plugin files are out of date; run pnpm plugins:sync` (5 files) | `pnpm plugins:check`: `e2e plugin: checked 19 generated files` | | `version-packages`: sync step exits 1 | `node scripts/sync-plugin.ts`: `synced 19 generated files`, tree unchanged | `pnpm check` passes in full. --- Made by Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5.

title: feat(feedback): send bugs without a repro to GitHub, refuse outdated reports
body: ## What and why `e2e feedback` reports are mostly agent-written. Most of the low-quality ones were sent from old versions, were flakes that need a repro, or repeated bugs we already knew about. 61 of 90 recent reports came from an older version than the latest release. Reports that need a repro die in Linear, because PostHog feedback is anonymous and we can't ask the reporter. - A `--type bug` report needs `--repro`, steps that reproduce it every time. Without it, the command sends nothing and prints a prefilled GitHub bug-form link (`what` and `versions` filled in, redacted, under 8000 chars). The user adds a minimal repro and submits it themselves. The agent never files it. - Before sending, it asks the registry for `e2e@latest`. If the installed version is older, it exits 2 and sends nothing. `--allow-outdated` overrides. A failed or slow registry check (3s timeout) is skipped. Under `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`/`DO_NOT_TRACK` no request is made. - New `--error-code ` field (`error_code` on the event) so reports group by code. `--task/--expected/--actual/--approach/--repro` are capped at 1500 characters. - Skill Feedback section: - never report app behaviour, one-off flakes, or outdated versions; - search GitHub issues first and comment on a match; - a bug that needs the app goes to GitHub. - Docs: CLI reference, telemetry, security outbound connections (`registry.npmjs.org`). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Built CLI against the live registry (latest 0.20.0): ```text $ e2e feedback --type bug -m "tap lands on the wrong tab" --actual "TARGET_NOT_FOUND on second run" --error-code TARGET_NOT_FOUND --dry-run Not sent: a bug without --repro goes to GitHub, where the e2e team can ask for a reproduction. Open this prefilled issue, add a minimal reproduction, and submit it: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml&labels=bug&title=tap+lands+on+the+wrong+tab&what=tap+lands+on+the+wrong+tab%0A%0AActual%3A+TARGET_NOT_FOUND+on+second+run%0AError+code%3A+TARGET_NOT_FOUND&versions=e2e+0.20.0%2C+node+24.19.0%2C+darwin+27.0.0 exit=0 # package version set to 0.19.0 $ e2e feedback -m x --dry-run feedback not sent: e2e 0.19.0 is older than the latest release 0.20.0, which may already fix this. Upgrade e2e, check the problem still happens, and send it again; --allow-outdated sends it anyway. exit=2 $ e2e feedback -m x --error-code nope error: option '--error-code ' argument 'nope' is invalid. must be an e2e error code such as LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS, at most 64 characters exit=2 ``` - `packages/e2e` unit tests: 2609 passed. New cases cover GitHub routing and redaction, the URL length cap, the outdated refusal and `--allow-outdated`, a registry failure, `--error-code` validation, and `olderThan`. - lint, typecheck and docs:check pass. - check:dead-code fails on 20 unused class members, and plugins:check fails because `plugins/e2e/skills/migrate-to-e2e` is missing. Neither comes from this PR. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(plugins): fit the Codex listing within OpenAI's directory limits
body: The Codex manifest in `plugins/e2e` fails OpenAI's plugin directory checks for a skills-only upload ([submission errors](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission-errors)): - `interface.shortDescription` was 48 characters. The directory's limit is 30. - `interface.screenshots` must not appear in a skills-only ZIP at all, even as `[]` (`screenshot_configuration_excluded`). This change shortens the description to `Agentic tests for web & mobile` (30 characters) and drops `screenshots`. The Claude manifest is generated from this one without `interface`, so it doesn't change. Possible follow-up: each `skills/*/agents/openai.yaml` points its icons at `../../assets/icon.png`. Codex accepts that path at runtime, but the directory's asset-path rule forbids `..`, and the docs don't say whether that rule covers skill icons. title: fix(skill): select bug-bash repro tests when the base config excludes them
body: Fixes #1083 ## What and why The bug-bash config template in the bundled skill spreads the project's `tests` and appends the repro directory, so a repro can run beside the tests it needs for its setup sessions. That breaks when the project's own `tests` excludes the repro directory, which is a valid and common choice: it keeps intentionally failing repros out of the run that gates merges. The runner applies a `!` exclusion whatever its position in the list, so appending the repro directory after `!tests/bugbash/**` selects nothing. `e2e list --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts` printed only the project's tests, and listing the repro by path exited `NO_TESTS`, so a developer following the recipe could not verify a single finding. That verification step is the reason the bug bash exists. The template now removes a base exclusion that hides the repro directory before it appends the repro glob, and keeps every other exclusion. The runner's documented, order-independent exclusion semantics are untouched. This is a template fix, which is what #1083 asks for. - `skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md`: the template derives the bug-bash `tests` list from the base list with the repro directory's own exclusion removed, plus a sentence beside it that names the behavior. - `plugins/e2e/skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md`: the generated plugin copy, from `pnpm plugins:sync`. - `.changeset/bugbash-config-repro-exclusion.md`: an `e2e` patch, because the skill ships in the published package. The old and new `tests` line, side by side: ```ts // before tests: [shared.tests ?? 'tests/**/*.e2e.ts', 'tests/bugbash/**/*.e2e.ts'].flat(), // after const repro = 'tests/bugbash'; const baseTests = [shared.tests ?? 'tests/**/*.e2e.ts'].flat(); const hidesRepro = (glob: string): boolean => { if (!glob.startsWith('!')) return false; const path = glob.slice(1).replace(/^\.\//, ''); return path === repro || path.startsWith(`${repro}/`); }; tests: [...baseTests.filter((glob) => !hidesRepro(glob)), `${repro}/**/*.e2e.ts`], ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes A scratch project with a base config `tests: ['tests/**/*.e2e.ts', '!tests/bugbash/**']`, one test in `tests/`, and one repro in `tests/bugbash/`, listed with the built CLI: | command | main template | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `e2e list --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts` | `tests/smoke.e2e.ts` only | `tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts`, `tests/smoke.e2e.ts` | | `e2e list tests/bugbash/cart-total.e2e.ts` | `NO_TESTS` (exit 2) | the repro (exit 0) | The fix holds for `!tests/bugbash/**`, `!./tests/bugbash/**`, and `!tests/bugbash`, and an unrelated exclusion such as `!tests/slow.e2e.ts` stays in the list. - `node scripts/check-docs-examples.ts`, `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts`, and `oxlint` on the tracked tree pass. - `node scripts/sync-plugin.ts --check` reports the plugin copy in sync. - The updated snippet typechecks inside `apps/testbed` with no errors. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. The template lives only in the skill (`docs/bug-bash.mdx` defers the full procedure to `npx e2e guide bug-bash`), so the skill and its plugin copy are the change. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: cache: replay end wait is fixed at record time, so --strict-cache fails a step under load (end-mismatch) although the end state arrives
body:
### What happens

Under CPU load, a replayed `agent.act` step fails with `REPLAY_STALE (end-mismatch)` under `--strict-cache`, although the recorded end state does appear on the page. Without `--strict-cache`, the same step is handed off to the agent, which costs model calls for a step that would have replayed fine.

The end-state wait is fixed when the step is **recorded**. In `dist/agent/step-cache.js`, `StepTraceSession.stage()`:

```js
endWaitMs: Date.now() - this.endWaitBaselineMs(recorder) + END_WAIT_MARGIN_MS,
```

with `END_WAIT_MARGIN_MS = 10_000`. A step recorded on a quiet machine, where the app answered in about 1 s, gets an `endWaitMs` of about 11 s. When the same step replays while the machine is busy (for example a test run with several workers, where other tests drive the same local app server), the app can take longer than that to render the end state. The replay then gives up with `end-mismatch`, even though the expected nodes show up shortly after.

### Evidence (e2e 0.20.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.14.0, Node 24, macOS)

- A checkout flow whose last step is `agent.act('Confirm the order.')`, recorded in read-write mode and committed. The end check expects a confirmation heading and a document title.
- Run alone with `--strict-cache`: `Cache 3 replayed`, passes, every time.
- Run with `--workers=2`, next to about 470 other tests that use the same app server: the last step fails after 14.8 s with
  ```
  REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays (end-mismatch) ...
  every recorded action ran, but the recorded end state did not show on /checkout/confirmation?...:
  expected node "<document title>", heading "<confirmation heading>"
  ```
  This happened in 2 out of 2 full runs. (The step text, path and labels are anonymised.)
- The run's `screen-at-failure.txt` for that attempt contains **both** expected nodes (the title and the heading). So the end state arrived, just after the wait ended.
- Rerunning only that test with `--last-failed --workers=1 --strict-cache` passes (`Cache 3 replayed`, 0 model calls).

#850 and #1057 touched `endWaitMs` and end-mismatch too, but for different causes (a growing wait after a hand-off, and a route announcer recorded as an anchor). This one is only about load at replay time.

### Proposal

Any of these would fix it. In order of preference:

1. **Use the larger of the recorded wait and the assertion timeout:** `max(trace.endWaitMs, config.assertionTimeout)`. A test author already states how long they will wait for the app to show something, and a replay end check is that kind of wait. A replay that ends early still costs nothing extra, because the wait polls.
2. **A config option**, e.g. `cache: { endWaitMarginMs }` (or `endWaitMinMs`), to raise the margin for slow or shared environments.
3. **Scale the margin at replay time**, for example with the ratio between the replay's own action timings and the recorded ones.

For now we work around it by running the agent-driven test on its own after the parallel tests, and by giving a `REPLAY_STALE` one rerun alone. Happy to help test a fix.

title: ci(release): patch bumps by default while packages are 0.x
body:
Every feature changeset bumped `minor`, so `e2e` went 0.3 -> 0.21 in six weeks. On 0.x, minor is the breaking slot, so this makes `patch` the default.

- New `scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts` (in `pnpm check` and `spec.yml`) fails on a 0.x `minor` unless the summary opens with `**Breaking:**` or `**Release:**`, and on a 0.x `major` unless it opens with `**Release:**`, since `1.0.0` falls outside every `>=x <1` peer range. Parsing uses `@changesets/parse`.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the `ship-pr` skill tell agents to use `patch` for features and never to pick `minor` on their own.
- No pending changesets to convert: #1095 released them as 0.21.0. The next feature release is 0.21.1.
- Users benefit too: `e2e init` writes `^0.21.0` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/versions.ts:26`), which on 0.x takes patches only, so today a project never gets a feature release without editing `package.json`.

```md
---
"e2e": minor
---

**Breaking:** `cache.dir` is removed, use `E2E_CACHE_DIR` or `--cache-dir`.
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `pnpm check:changeset-bumps` on the 9 minors pending before #1095: exit 1, one line per file. Rewritten as patches: `changeset bumps: 27 pending, none an unannounced 0.x minor or major`.
- Scratch changesets: `major` + `**Breaking:**` and a plain `minor` both fail with the right message; an empty `---\n---` changeset passes.
- `pnpm test:scripts` passes, including the new `scripts/changeset-bumps.test.ts`.

title: fix(runner): time out a host session closed past its deadline
body: ## What and why - An `openHost()` session (#980) could hit its deadline and still close as passed. The timeout was recorded only when the expiry timer fired, at deadline + 1 ms, and `close()` cleared that timer first. So a session closed in that window, for example right after an `expect.poll` was cut at the deadline, returned `[]` from `close()` and wrote a passed trace. That contradicts `docs/reference/runner.mdx`: "Either way the session's outcome is timed out and close() returns the timeout." - `packages/e2e/src/run/standalone-attempt.ts`: the timer callback is now a run-once `expire()`, and `close()` calls it when `deadline.expired()`. The deadline decides the outcome, not the timer race. - `expect.poll` still records no step. That is true in normal runs too, so it is left for a separate change. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built testbed, real web engine: `openSession({ timeout: 1000 })`, then `expect.poll(() => 0, { timeout: 5000 }).toBe(1)`, then `close()`. - main: `close()` returns `[]`, trace says passed. - branch: `close()` returns `TEST_TIMEOUT`, trace says timed out. - `tests/integration/open-host-deadline.test.ts`: the poll case now asserts `['TEST_TIMEOUT']` and a timed-out trace, and a new busy-loop case was added. Both fail on main and pass here. - `pnpm check` and the e2e package tests pass. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(agent): keep the request prefix a Claude 5.x thinking block is bound to
body:
Closes ENG-984. Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1 sign every thinking block over the request prefix that produced it, the system prompt and the messages before the block, and answer a replay after any edit to that prefix with: ``` messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. ``` The act loop edited that prefix in two places: - On the switch to `auto` after the provider refused or downgraded a forced tool choice, it appended the tool-calls-only rule to the system prompt. Recent `@ai-sdk/anthropic` versions and the AI Gateway downgrade with a warning instead of a 400, so turn 1 succeeds with a thinking block and turn 2 replays it under a changed prompt. This fires on the first step of every worker and is what the reporter hit; the issue text names only the second cause. - Screen and screenshot elision (`transcript-compaction.ts`) rewrites earlier messages once superseded screens pass their budget. Every block signed before the edit is invalid from then on. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[turn n: history prepared] --> B{a message differs from
the last request's object?} B -- no --> C[send as is] B -- yes --> D[afterEdit: drop reasoning parts
from that message on
Anthropic only] D --> E[note it on the turn] --> C ``` - `packages/e2e/src/agent/tool-loop.ts`: the tool-calls-only rule is part of every step's instructions from turn 1, so the switch to `auto` changes only `tool_choice`, which the check ignores. `prepareTurn` compares a digest of what each message holds with the digests taken when the last request was sent (`message-shape.ts`: SHA-256 over the content with provider options left out and bytes hashed), so a replaced message and one a custom `prepareMessages` edits in place both show up while a moved cache breakpoint or a cloned history does not, and hands the first rewritten index to the provider hints. - `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/provider-hints.ts`: `afterEdit` removes the `reasoning` parts of assistant messages from the rewritten one on, and drops a reply that was only reasoning. Anthropic allows removing thinking from the end of a history; a block produced after the elision stays valid because the elided message does not change again. Other providers get the history untouched, since OpenAI Responses needs its reasoning items beside their function calls. The Anthropic detection now also recognizes Claude on Bedrock (`eu.anthropic.claude-…`) and Vertex AI (`vertex.anthropic.messages`), where the same check runs; before, only the direct provider and the gateway were matched. - `tests/unit/tool-loop-prefix.test.ts`: the real `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider over a fake `fetch`, asserting on the request bodies that the system prompt is byte-identical through the switch, that no thinking is replayed after an elided message while later thinking is, and that a non-Anthropic model keeps every reasoning part. - Not done: `prefix_mismatch_behavior: drop_block`. It needs a beta header, a provider version and a gateway that forward it, is rejected under Sonnet 5.5's `between_tools`, and hides the edit instead of removing it. title: feat(runner): execute suites through e2e/runner
body:
- Expose `run()` on `e2e/runner` with `cwd`, `config`, `files`, `interruptSignal`, and `onEvent`. Return the completed report without exiting the caller; execution settings belong in config.
- Reuse the suite executor and config/selection conversion. Report overlapping public calls with `RUNNER_BUSY` before changing credentials, while preserving supported hosted-session behavior.
- Redact suite logs while preserving caller logs and callback context. Recheck caller-installed stream writers before each run.
- Update public type assertions, docs, the shipped skill, and generated plugin. Include a patch changeset (0.x policy). The API and overlap policy still need maintainer agreement in #994.

Closes #994.

```ts
import { run } from 'e2e/runner';

const controller = new AbortController();
const result = await run({
  cwd: projectDirectory,
  config,
  files: ['tests/signup.e2e.ts'],
  interruptSignal: controller.signal,
  onEvent(event) {
    if (event.type === 'test-started') console.log(event.title);
  },
});
console.log(result.status, result.report.run.summary);
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR

  B --> C[Load and collect]
  C --> D[Execute suite]
  D --> E[Cleanup]

```

title: fix(agent): stop the run once when the provider does not serve the model
body:
Fixes ENG-985. A GitHub Copilot Free login lists `claude-haiku-4.5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-6-luna` and the rest as `enabled`, and Copilot answers every call by id with 400 `model_not_supported`: Free serves models through auto model selection only ([GitHub's plans page](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans)), and `GET /models` carries nothing that says so. The same body answers a model the settings turned off and an id Copilot does not list. The listing and the request path were both right. What was wrong is the failure mode: every test booted, called, and failed with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` and Copilot's bare sentence, the transport-error class, exit 3, and nothing named the cause. - `copilot()` (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/copilot.ts`) wraps its model: a 4xx whose body code is `model_not_supported` is marked with the explanation a user reads, through `src/internal/unserved-model.ts`. Copilot's other codes (`unsupported_api_for_model` for a model on the wrong endpoint) and every other provider answer stay `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` as before. - The agent reads only the mark: `unservedModelError` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts`) turns a marked failure into `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, from the judgment adapter and the act loop alike. No vendor code lives there; the next plan-gated provider marks its own answer. - The agent fixture reports that error through `WorkerModels.unservedModel`, the hook the preflight already uses for a missing model: one run error, the run stops, exit 2, from `e2e run` and `e2e explore` alike, and from a custom executor that calls `copilot()` itself. Two workers meeting it at once still produce one entry. - Docs: the `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` row and every page that defined the code as "no model configured" (Models, Debugging, Cache, the skill's agent and debugging references), the Subscriptions page (the listing shows GitHub's catalog, a plan refusal shows nowhere, Free serves models through auto selection only), the CLI reference, the skill's setup reference. No model names in any of it: which ids a plan serves is GitHub's to change. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[agent step calls copilot model] --> B{Copilot answer} B -- 4xx model_not_supported --> C[copilot marks the failure with the explanation] C --> D[agent: MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, fixture reports it once] D --> E[run error, run stops, exit 2] B -- any other failure --> F[MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED, as before] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, a Copilot Free login (`access_type_sku: free_limited_copilot`), two agent tests (`agent.assert`, then `agent.act`) with `copilot('claude-haiku-4.5')`, then an id Copilot does not list, then `e2e explore`, then `copilot('gpt-4.1')` as the control. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `e2e run`, `copilot('claude-haiku-4.5')` | each test boots, calls, and fails: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: The requested model is not supported.`; exit 3 | one run error, the run stops in 2.0 s; 1 interrupted, 1 skipped; exit 2 | | `e2e run`, `copilot('gpt-4.1-typo')` | the same per-test failure | the same run error naming `gpt-4.1-typo`, 1.4 s, exit 2 | | `e2e explore`, `copilot('claude-haiku-4.5')` | the same per-step failure | `no step ran`, the same run error, 1.7 s, exit 2 | | `e2e run`, `copilot('gpt-4.1')` | passes | passes, 2 tests, 3 model calls |
this branch, copilot('claude-haiku-4.5') ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 87ms × copilot plan probe: assert on the todos page > agent.assert "one todo is listed and it is not marked done" 1.04s · 1 model call failed ❯ |web| tests-scratch/copilot-probe.e2e.ts (2 tests | 1 interrupted | 1 skipped) 1.61s ai 0 tokens × copilot plan probe: assert on the todos page (interrupted) 1.61s ai 0 tokens ↓ copilot plan probe: act on the todos page [run interrupted before execution] ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Run Errors 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ ERROR configuration error MODEL_UNAVAILABLE GitHub Copilot does not serve claude-haiku-4.5 to this account: the plan does not include it, it is turned off in Copilot settings on GitHub, or Copilot lists no such id; npx e2e models github-copilot lists the ids, and the listing cannot see plan limits Test Files 1 interrupted | 0 passed (1) Tests 1 interrupted | 0 passed | 1 skipped (2) AI 0 tokens · 1 model calls · github-copilot.chat/claude-haiku-4.5 Errors 1 error Duration 1.98s (startup 87ms) ```
this branch, e2e explore ```text ✓ target "web" command ready 97ms ❯ |web| Exploring Open the todos page and look around no step ran ended: the run was cut short ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Run Errors 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ ERROR configuration error MODEL_UNAVAILABLE GitHub Copilot does not serve claude-haiku-4.5 to this account: the plan does not include it, it is turned off in Copilot settings on GitHub, or Copilot lists no such id; npx e2e models github-copilot lists the ids, and the listing cannot see plan limits Findings none Steps 0 done of 1 · planning AI 0 tokens · 1 model calls · github-copilot.chat/claude-haiku-4.5 Errors 1 error Duration 1.70s (startup 97ms) ```
main, copilot('claude-haiku-4.5') ```text FAIL |web| tests-scratch/copilot-probe.e2e.ts > copilot plan probe: assert on the todos page MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: The requested model is not supported. ❯ at http://127.0.0.1:4279/todos ❯ trace .e2e/results/copilot-probe-copilot-plan-probe-assert-on-the-79f031053e41dbdf/trace.md Test Files 1 failed | 0 passed (1) Tests 1 failed | 0 passed (1) AI 0 tokens · 1 model calls · github-copilot.chat/claude-haiku-4.5 ```

title: fix(cache): floor the replay end wait at the assertion timeout
body: Fixes #1144 ## What and why A replayed `agent.act` step waited for its recorded end state for exactly as long as the recording had measured, and that number was fixed into the entry when the step was recorded. `StepTraceSession.stage()` wrote `endWaitMs: Date.now() - endWaitBaselineMs(recorder) + END_WAIT_MARGIN_MS`, and the replay handed that value straight to `verifyEndState`. A step recorded on a quiet machine, where the app answered in about a second, carried a wait of about eleven seconds. Replayed on a busy machine, next to hundreds of other tests driving the same app server, the same step can need longer than that for the end state to render, so the replay gave up with `end-mismatch` although the state arrived, and the run's failure screen held both expected nodes. Under `--strict-cache` that same condition fails the step as `REPLAY_STALE`; without it, the step is handed to the agent and spends model calls on work the cache would have finished. The wait is now the larger of the recorded wait and `assertionTimeout`: ```ts // before ...(trace.endWaitMs === undefined ? {} : { waitMs: trace.endWaitMs }), // after const waitMs = Math.max(trace.endWaitMs ?? 0, this.options.assertionTimeout); ``` `assertionTimeout` is the deadline a test author already sets for how long the app may take to show something, since `expect` polls up to it, and a replay's end check is that same kind of wait, so the replay never waits less than it. Nothing else moves. A recorded wait longer than `assertionTimeout` is kept, an entry written before `endWaitMs` existed now waits `assertionTimeout` instead of returning at once, and the wait still polls, so it returns the moment the anchors hold and a step that settles early costs no extra time. The plumbing is one new field. `StepCacheOptions` gains `assertionTimeout`, and `ActDispatch` passes `runtime.config.assertionTimeout` where it builds the session. The config default is 5000 ms, so a run that never set it now waits that much rather than the recorded wait alone. - `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts`: add `StepCacheOptions.assertionTimeout`, and have `endStateMatches` pass `max(trace.endWaitMs ?? 0, assertionTimeout)` as the end wait. - `packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts`: pass `runtime.config.assertionTimeout` into the cache session. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts`: three fake-clock cases under a new `the replay end wait` block. - `docs/cache.mdx`: one bullet under "How the end check reads the screen". - `.changeset/cache-end-wait-assertion-timeout.md`: an `e2e` patch. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes The three new cases run under a fake clock with semantic screens, no browser and no model. One recording carries a short `endWaitMs` and its end state renders past that wait but inside `assertionTimeout`. One recording's wait is longer than `assertionTimeout` and must be kept. One entry has no `endWaitMs` at all and must still wait `assertionTimeout`. The first and third fail on main and pass here; the middle one passes on both, as a guard that the floor never shortens a recorded wait. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | a step recorded at about 1 s waits about 11 s; the end state arrives after that and the replay fails `end-mismatch` | the same step waits `assertionTimeout` (30 s in the case), returns the moment the anchors hold, and replays | - `pnpm --filter e2e run typecheck`: exit 0. - `pnpm --filter e2e run test:unit`: `step-cache.test.ts` 66 passed and `trace-replay.test.ts` 40 passed. The rest of the suite's failures are pre-existing on this machine and identical on `main` (Windows line endings and path separators): the branch and `main` both report 20 failed files and 48 failed tests over the same files. - `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts`, `node scripts/check-docs-examples.ts`, `node scripts/check-docs-package-managers.ts`, and `oxlint`: pass. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(cli): add e2e run --step and --inspect
body: ## What changed - `e2e run --step` runs the first step, which opens the app, then holds every later step until a key is pressed: `c` runs it, `t` finishes the current test, `r` runs the rest, `q` (or Esc, Ctrl-C) stops the run with exit 130. - `e2e run --inspect` steps the same way from a local page: the test file with the line about to run, the steps grouped by test with a `Test N of M` count, and Next, Finish test, Run the rest and Stop buttons. It implies `--step` and `--headed` and needs no terminal. - The web engine opens that page in a window on the left half of the screen and starts its browser on the right half. On a Wayland desktop it starts Chromium through XWayland, because Wayland ignores a program's window position. - A setup test and a retry run without stopping. The page has Hold setup steps and Hold retries toggles. - New optional contract: `EngineInitInfo.inspector`, the page's address, which an engine may show beside its window. `@e2e-dev/web` now needs `e2e >=0.22.0`, the release that carries it (same pattern as #913). `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` asserts its shape. Playwright's `--debug` was listed as "not yet" in `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx`; it now maps to `--inspect`. `e2e run --debug` keeps its meaning (timings and the agent step table). ## How it works Only the runner owns the terminal, so a worker cannot read keys. Before each step the worker asks the runner and waits for the answer. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as Worker (test body) participant R as Runner (step gate) participant P as Terminal or inspector page W->>R: step-gate (test, attempt, api, label, file:line) R->>P: prompt / state over SSE P-->>R: c, t, r, q or a button POST R-->>W: step-go (go or refuse) W->>W: run the step body ``` - `packages/e2e/src/run/step-gate.ts`: the gate. It queues prompts one at a time, ignores keys for 150 ms after a prompt appears, and keeps "finish this test" per target, test id, agent and repeat. - `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`: `StepRecorder` awaits a `beforeStep` hook before a step's body. The wait is not part of the step's duration or `startedAt`, so video offsets still line up. - `packages/e2e/src/run/worker/session.ts`: answers `step-go` at once, even while a test runs. A refusal interrupts the worker before the step fails, so the test ends as `interrupted`, not `failed`. - `packages/e2e/src/run/inspector.ts` and `inspector-page.ts`: the page server, built with Node only. - `packages/web/src/inspector-window.ts`: places the two windows. The inspector window is launched through Playwright (`launchPersistentContext` with `--app=`), which talks to Chromium over a pipe: no TCP debugging port is opened, and the window ends with the worker even when the worker is killed. - A stepped run uses one worker and a 24 hour test timeout, since the person sets the pace. `--max-duration` and `maxDuration` are ignored (the run says so), because they would cut a session short. - Ctrl-C stops the run even while a step is running. Raw mode delivers no signal, so the gate handles it itself and then hands the terminal back, which makes a second Ctrl-C a real SIGINT that escalates as usual. - Without a list reporter (`--reporter markdown`, `junit`, or a config with no `list`) nothing would draw the prompt, so the gate prints it to stderr. ```ts // e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts --inspect export interface EngineInitInfo { /** The inspector of a run stepped through with `--inspect`; an engine may show it beside its window. */ readonly inspector?: { readonly url: string } | undefined; } ``` ### Security of the page - Bound to `127.0.0.1`, random port, random token in the path. - Host and Origin of every request are checked, so a page the person visits cannot reach it. - `POST` takes `application/json` only, bodies are capped at 1 KiB, and the only actions are the three keys plus the two holds. - `/source` serves only files a step names, and only inside the project root. - Step labels reach the page after the runner's redaction. The page shows test source as written. - The inspector window has no DevTools port open (checked: no Chromium TCP listener while it runs). ### Refusals `--step` and `--inspect` exit 2 in CI, with `--watch`, with `--reporter json`, and with `--workers` above 1. `--step` also needs stdin and stdout to be a terminal. ### Docs The two new sections of `docs/debugging.mdx` went through the shortening pass: 108 to 77 lines, 722 to 518 prose words. Cut on purpose: - the second three-tab command block for `--inspect` (the page says to run the same command with the flag); - "it goes on like this to the end of the file" (the intro already says every later step); - "like `--step`, the first step runs on its own" under `--inspect` (it implies `--step`); - the reasons behind the 150 ms key guard, the setup and retry rule (kept once, in the `--step` list) and the XWayland explanation (kept as one clause); - "Finish test applies to one test on one target" (the key table says "this test" and the groups name the target). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Surface: `apps/testbed` on the built CLI. - `e2e run tests/smoke.e2e.ts tests/todos.e2e.ts --step --headed` in a pseudo-terminal: step 1 ran alone, every later step waited for `c`, and `t` at step 3 let the rest of that test through and held at the next test's first step. - `e2e run tests/smoke.e2e.ts tests/todos.e2e.ts --inspect`: the page was driven over its own HTTP interface. 78 steps were held, each released by one press, the source pane switched file at step 14, and the tests passed. Window positions, read from the X server while paused: inspector at x=0 (960 wide), browser at x=960 (960 wide). - Two web targets on the same app: they run one after the other, one inspector window and one browser at a time. This found and fixed a bug where both targets shared test ids and their steps merged into one group. - Real sign-in setup (`tests/dashboard.e2e.ts`): 13 of the setup test's 14 steps went through without stopping, and all 19 steps of the five dashboard tests were held. - Refusals: `--inspect` in CI, `--step` without a terminal, `--inspect --workers 2` and the removed name `--ui` each print their error. - Cleanup: SIGKILL of the worker while paused closed both the inspector window and the browser within 5 seconds. Only a small `/tmp/e2e-inspector-*` profile directory stays, which a killed process cannot remove. Paused in one file: Two files, finished tests collapsed: Two targets: Not verified: macOS, Windows and plain X11 window placement (checked on GNOME under Wayland, through XWayland only), and a web target next to a mobile target. ## Review A reviewer with no memory of the change read the diff against `AGENTS.md` and the repo's review patterns. It found the server sound and raised six points. Fixed here, each with a test that fails without the fix: - Ctrl-C was ignored while a step ran (raw mode stayed on after `c`). - The prompt was invisible without a list reporter. - `maxDuration` could end a stepped session. - The inspector window was orphaned when the worker was killed, and left a loopback DevTools port open (both fixed by launching it through Playwright). - `EngineInitInfo.inspector` had no assertion in `sdk-types.ts`. Left as is: if a worker dies while its step is held, the prompt stays on screen until the next key. The run already reports the crashed worker and ends, and the answer to a dead worker is dropped.

title: feat(runner): expose the closed hosted session report
body: ## What and why - Expose the session's existing public `Report` through `session.report()` once its trace has been written. It returns `undefined` before that or after a failed write. - Retain the report already built by `writeHostTrace` and clone it for callers. Existing trace rendering/redaction is unchanged. - Artifact paths are relative to `/results`. Caller lifecycle, retries, hosting, and outer test verdicts remain caller-owned. Refs #1074. Per the [maintainer's follow-up](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1156#pullrequestreview-5528435506), the shared late-secret gap is deferred to #1157, not remediated here. No report-rewriting or cut-tracking machinery is added. ## Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[session.close] --> B[Build existing Report] B --> C[Write existing trace.md] C --> D[Retain Report after successful write] D --> E[session.report clones Report] ``` ## Verified On `77e3d49e`, locally on a Linux Devbox: - `pnpm check` passed, including the new patch-changeset policy and public `Report` type assertion. - Five owning host test files: **50 passed**, no skips. SDK ownership subset: **6 passed**, 5 intentionally unselected. - Independent review of the combined tree found no new important issues. The `main` sync preserves its hosted-run ownership/release handling. - CI on `77e3d49e`: [docs](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38745500557), [spec](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38745500335), [web benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38745500641), and [mobile deterministic tests](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/38745500346) passed. Web-agent and mobile app-cache jobs were skipped. - Cubic completed its check **without an AI review because this head is a merge commit**. That success status is not current-head AI-review clearance. Maintainer follow-up remains pending. Prior-head green checks are not current-head validation. No fresh full default/stress suite, testbed/web benchmark, live-provider, or native-device run was performed locally.

title: secrets: handle late-resolved values and prefixes consistently across steps and reports
body:
## What happened

As described in the [review of PR 1156](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1156#pullrequestreview-5527238707), text truncated by the SDK before a secret provider resolves can retain a secret prefix after final redaction. The review identifies this existing problem in app-log output and notes that the shared problem also affects `steps()` and `report.json`, not just `trace.md`.

The [subsequent automated review](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1156#discussion_r4278478026) also identifies complete late-resolved values in the returned `Report`, not only truncated prefixes. The shared final-redaction gap should cover both cases.

## Expected behavior

Handle late-resolved secrets and SDK truncation consistently in the shared recording/redaction path, with regression coverage for the affected outputs. Avoid a hosted-report-only rewrite or a second copy of the report schema.

## Context

Opened at the maintainer's request so this can be addressed separately from the small [`session.report()` accessor PR](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1156). This issue tracks the behavior already discussed publicly; it does not add reproduction payloads or private values.

title: test(web): stop asserting popup load-time media, a race
body: ## What and why - `media.test.ts` asserted that a tab the app opens itself reads the context's configured media (`dark`) at load. The engine applies a test's `emulateMedia` to such a tab on the `page` event without blocking it, so its head script can run before or after that lands. On Linux CI it often lands first, and `atLoad` reads `light`. - This has failed `test (*)` on #1148, #1149, a main push (edf3423), and other PRs, all with `expected { dark: false } to deeply equal { dark: true }`. - Dropped that assertion. The test still checks what the engine does guarantee: the popup reports the test's change once it exists, and a later change too. - The `web.mdx` media section and the `watchPages` JSDoc claimed the popup "paints with the configured values" first. They now say its load-time scripts may still read those values. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `vitest run tests/integration/media.test.ts` 15x: 5/5 every run. - `pnpm run check` passes. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(decision): Jev vision and a third tap_at look
body:
TypeSafe Jev now takes images (`jev-latest` / 1.13+). This makes `vision: true` work on Jev, tightens `tap_at`, and adds `type_at` for drawn fields.

- Bump `@ai-sdk/typesafe-ai` 3.0.16 -> 3.0.19 (decision devDep, docs). 3.0.19 sends the screenshot file part; 3.0.16 rejects it.
- `PointLocator` takes a third look: full screenshot, 400px zoom, then a 200px zoom, all at 2x with the grid on the zooms (`packages/decision/src/locator.ts`). A point tap now costs 4 decide calls + 1 text call.
- New `type_at` operation, offered with vision when the engine has `typeText`: one text call names the drawn field and its value, the locator finds the field on the full screenshot (no zooms: a crop holds the stacked neighbor fields and the mean lands between them), then `tapAt` + `typeText` at the caret (no replace: mobile cannot clear a focused field without a node). 2 decide calls + 1 text call.
- Action space fixes found on the web benchmark (none vision-specific): `tap` is offered on text fields (opens date pickers and custom comboboxes), `drag` drops onto any pointable node, not only drop-zone roles (boards whose columns are bare text), and a lone target is asked instead of dispatched, so `none` stops an operation that fits only the wrong element (a `long_press` that pressed the back link).
- Docs: Vision section shows Jev setup (`TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY`, provider 3.0.19+); JSDoc and README name Jev as a vision model.
- AI Gateway still rejects images for decision models, docs say so.

```ts
const executor = decisionExecutor({
  model: typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest'),
  textModel: openrouter('inception/mercury-2.5'),
  vision: true,
});
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

**Locator, offline:** real `PointLocator` on Jev over 54 drawn targets (map pins, 12-key keypad, 8 wizard screens x 5 targets) at the runner's 768px capture.

| Looks | Hits (runs) |
| --- | --- |
| full + 400px zoom (main) | 47, 49, 49 / 54 |
| full + 400px + 200px zoom (this PR) | 54, 53, 54, 53 / 54 |
| full + 400px + 160px zoom | 53, 53 / 54 |
| 400px zoom without grid | 43, 44 / 54 |
| 400px zoom, 10 cells | 49, 50 / 54 |

Main misses both map pins (~21px and 86px off, pin radius 20).

**`type_at` locator, offline:** drawn form (Name, City), full screenshot only: 72/72. With the 400px zoom: ~4 in 5 (zoom mass split 0.31 Name / 0.25 City).

**Live, no cache:** built dist, `typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-preview')` (jev-1.14.0) direct, text model `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, `vision: true`.

| Suite | Setup | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| testbed canvas form, x3 | before `type_at` | 0/3 |
| testbed canvas form, x3 | this PR | 3/3 |
| testbed `tests-agent` (29) | Jev, no vision | 23/29 |
| testbed `tests-agent` (29) | Jev vision, main locator | 23-24/29 |
| testbed `tests-agent` (29) | Jev vision, this PR | 25/29 |
| web benchmark `tests-agent` (33) | default agent, `gpt-6-luna-fast` | 33/33, 5m54s |
| web benchmark `tests-agent` (33) | Jev vision, this PR | 21/33, 1m16s |

```text
 ✓ fills a form drawn on a canvas through type_at and the keyboard (x3)
    Repeats  1 of 1 test passed all 3 runs
```

Testbed failures: two drawn wizards (the text model never sees the drawn instruction), the 10-digit keypad (misses the 9 key), and the workspace wizard ("chose tap but no target"). The last two fail 0/3 on the previous commit too, so not from `type_at`.

Benchmark, 3 runs each, no cache, Jev vision:

| Code | Pass |
| --- | --- |
| before the action space fixes | 63/99 |
| this PR, three separate x3 runs | 67/99, 60/99, 59/99 (one with a tap wording later reverted) |

Totals are within run-to-run noise (about ±4 of 99); the per-test effect is not: date-picker 0/3 -> 3/3, kanban 0/3 -> 2/3. Still failing everywhere: hover-menu, drag-and-drop (after the first drop the zone's only label is its contents), context-menu-trap, lying-labels, infinite-scroll, virtualized-table, otp-auto-advance, rich-text-editor, wishlist judgment. Jev is far behind the default agent on this suite.

Earlier "26/29" testbed numbers replayed 17 steps from cache; the table above is no cache.

Docs use `jev-latest`, which resolves to jev-1.13.0; the numbers above are on `jev-preview`.

Not re-measured on `gpt-6-luna` (no OpenAI key at hand); the old code noted a tighter third look drifted there.

A close with no session open (a second close in a row, or one before `app.open()`) left the daemon to pick a device from every booted one, so it failed when several were booted. - I folded the changelog line into #962's unreleased `pinned-mobile-recording` changeset rather than adding a second entry. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Mobile benchmark app on a pinned iPhone 17 Pro sim (UDID), with 4 iOS devices booted, running a scratch test with `await device.closeApp(); await device.closeApp();`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `ENGINE_FAILURE: device.closeApp failed: 4 devices match this request equally; select one explicitly.` | `✓ closeApp with no session open on a pinned device 1.09s` | - In the unit test from #962 that covers several booted devices, each `closeApp` with no session open now asserts the selection. title: feat(lightpanda): add @e2e-dev/lightpanda, a browser provider for the Lightpanda headless browser
body: ## What and why - New package `@e2e-dev/lightpanda`: `lightpanda()` is a `BrowserProvider` for the web engine that starts one `lightpanda serve` per worker slot on a free loopback port and stops its process group when the run ends. No vendor SDK; the binary is the dependency. - [Lightpanda](https://lightpanda.io) is an open-source headless browser without Chromium: instant start, a fraction of Chrome's memory, and CDP, so the engine attaches to it the way it attaches to Kernel. - Binary discovery: `binary`, `LIGHTPANDA_PATH`, then `lightpanda` on `PATH`, `~/.lightpanda/lightpanda`, `~/.local/bin/lightpanda` (the places agent-browser looks). None found fails the lease before any test, naming the install page. - A server already running (the Docker image in CI) is a `web({ connect })` target, so the provider has one lease shape and no attach mode. - Worker scope only: Lightpanda exposes no default context identity, so a per-attempt lease fails with `CDP recovery failed: the default context identity is unavailable`. The option is not offered. - Docs page `docs/integrations/lightpanda.mdx` with setup, options, and a table of what Lightpanda cannot do yet (sessions, dialogs, downloads, iframes, drags, resize, scrolling, media emulation) and why, each verified against the nightly. Testbed gets `e2e.lightpanda.config.ts` and `pnpm test:lightpanda` to re-check that table as Lightpanda ships fixes. ```ts import { lightpanda } from '@e2e-dev/lightpanda'; export default { targets: [{ name: 'lightpanda', engine: web({ browser: lightpanda({ loadResources: ['iframe'] }) }), app: { url } }], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant R as runner (prepare) participant P as lightpanda() participant S as lightpanda serve participant W as worker R->>P: acquire(slot n) P->>S: spawn --host 127.0.0.1 --port free, detached P->>S: poll /json/version (10 s cap) S-->>P: Lightpanda-Version P-->>R: lease { id: ws://127.0.0.1:port/ } W->>S: connectOverCDP, one context per attempt R->>P: release(lease) P->>S: SIGTERM group, SIGKILL after 5 s ``` ### Benchmark Testbed, the six files that pass on both engines copied four times (96 tests), M4 Pro, mean of two runs. Baseline is `web()` Chromium on this branch; the candidate is `lightpanda()`. | Workers | Chromium wall | Lightpanda wall | Chromium peak RSS | Lightpanda peak RSS | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 31.6 s | 21.8 s | 358 MB | 124 MB | | 4 | 9.8 s | 6.6 s | 1.30 GB | 364 MB | | 8 | 6.7 s | 5.0 s | 2.52 GB | 587 MB | | 14 | 6.1 s | 4.1 s | 4.12 GB | 954 MB | Per-test time grows 33 percent from 1 to 14 workers on Lightpanda and 77 percent on Chromium; Chromium stops gaining past 8 workers on 14 cores. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, `LIGHTPANDA_PATH=... pnpm test:lightpanda --workers 4`: four servers leased on distinct ports, logged as `lightpanda 1.1.0-nightly.10619 at ws://127.0.0.1:51165/`, released at the end, `pgrep lightpanda` empty after. - Full testbed suite on the provider: 57 passed, 21 failed, 1 skipped (nightly 10619, rebased on main at ce4dac37); every failure is in the docs table and reproduced with a bare Playwright `connectOverCDP` probe, so none is engine-side. - `scope: 'attempt'` tried live and fails as described, which is why it is absent. - Empty `PATH` and `HOME`: the run fails before any test with `lightpanda is not on PATH, in ~/.lightpanda, or in ~/.local/bin; install it (https://lightpanda.io/docs/open-source/installation) or set LIGHTPANDA_PATH`. - Docs page rendered in `mint dev`, sidebar icon and tables in place. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. Supersedes #983, which GitHub would not reopen after the rebase force-push.

title: fix(web): reject connect without a cdpEndpoint resolver at config load
body:
A `web({ connect })` with `reconnectEndpoint` but no `cdpEndpoint` passed config load and failed every attempt with `ENGINE_FAILURE: connection failed: resolve is not a function`: the persistent attach called the undefined resolver (`packages/web/src/surface.ts:449` hands it to `packages/web/src/cdp-recovery.ts:52`). A `cdpEndpoint` given as a string did the same at init, as `browser connect failed: source.resolve is not a function`.

- `web()` validates `connect` in one place now, `validateConnect` in `packages/web/src/engine.ts`: not a plain object, no `cdpEndpoint`, or a `cdpEndpoint` or `reconnectEndpoint` that is not a function is `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load. The missing-key message says `reconnectEndpoint` only reconnects to the browser `cdpEndpoint` provisioned.
- Messages name the value's kind (`got a string`) and never echo it: a CDP URL can carry a session token.
- `docs/reference/web.mdx`: the `connect` paragraph says `cdpEndpoint` is required and both keys are resolvers, and drops the resolver call timing that read as if one browser served the worker. The recovery section opens with the fresh-browser-per-attempt rule and points to the setup-test session for reusing a sign-in across files (ENG-945); the engine mechanics it described are gone, nine lines shorter than main. `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` carries the same contract.

Closes ENG-986, ENG-945.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, a scratch config selecting each `connect` shape with `ENG986_CASE=missing|string|reused`, `e2e run --config e2e.scratch-eng986.config.ts`, built packages on both sides:

| shape | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ reconnectEndpoint }` only | every test `ENGINE_FAILURE: connection failed: resolve is not a function` | `INVALID_CONFIG` at load, no test runs |
| `{ cdpEndpoint: 'ws://…' }` (a string) | every test `ENGINE_FAILURE: browser connect failed: source.resolve is not a function` | `INVALID_CONFIG` at load, no test runs |
| both resolvers returning one headless Chromium | second test `CDP recovery failed: cdpEndpoint reused a browser from a previous attempt` | same, by design, now stated up front in the docs |

```
 ERROR  configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config)
web({ connect }) requires cdpEndpoint, the resolver that provisions the browser: (signal) => url; reconnectEndpoint only reconnects to the browser cdpEndpoint provisioned
```

```
 ERROR  configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config)
web({ connect: { cdpEndpoint } }) must be a resolver function (signal) => url, got a string
```
