title: fix(mobile): keep locator polling through unreadable android snapshots
body: ## What and why - agent-device throws a retriable `COMMAND_FAILED` with `details.androidSnapshotHelperFailureReason` (`empty-helper-output`, `content-poor-app-window`, `system-window-only`) when an Android snapshot has no usable app content, e.g. while the app is still loading. - `translateError` mapped it to non-retryable `ENGINE_FAILURE`, so `resolveOnce` stopped polling and `toBeVisible` failed immediately instead of waiting out its timeout. - `locate()` now treats an unreadable capture as zero matches and keeps polling. If the capture overruns the time budget, the original error is rethrown. - Tradeoff: while the screen is unreadable, `not.toBeVisible()`, `count()` and `isVisible()` see 0 matches. Alternative is a retryable `NODE_STALE`; open to switching. - Seen as flakes in react-navigation Android CI: https://github.com/react-navigation/react-navigation/pull/13299 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - unit tests and `pnpm check` only, not on a real emulator. - 4 new unit tests in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(skills): add an optional defect check to migrate-to-e2e
body:
Adds an opt-in defect check to the `migrate-to-e2e` skill. The goal is to give reviewers evidence that a ported test catches what the original caught before the original is deleted.

- The first session asks once and records `Defect check: on|off` in `MIGRATION.md`. A resumed session whose file has no such line asks then.
- With it on, step 6 gains five steps:
  1. With the user's agreement, plant a small bug in an end state the source test asserts, such as a wrong checkout total.
  2. Rebuild and confirm the app shows the bug.
  3. Run both suites. The old one runs only when it can run here; otherwise the row says `old not run`.
  4. Revert only the planted file.
  5. Record the outcome in a new `Defect check` column.
- Reading the outcome:
  - Only the old suite passes: the agent records that the source was weaker.
  - Only e2e passes: the port lost an assertion and is not done.
  - Neither fails: the agent picks another bug.
  - A failure before the step that checks the planted state does not count as a catch.
- Leftover bugs: the planted file is noted under `Next` until it is reverted, so a session that stops mid-check leaves a trail, and the next session reverts it first.
- The planted bug is the one exception to the skill's "do not change app code" rule.
- `docs/coding-agents.mdx` mentions the option in its `migrate-to-e2e` summary. `plugins/e2e` is resynced.

No changeset: the skill is not shipped in the npm package (same as #1109 and #1136).

## Verified

Ran it locally: no. The change is skill text only. I have not run the skill on a real migration with a planted bug. `pnpm check` passes, including `plugins:check` and `docs:check`. A fresh-context review found five issues, and all five are fixed here:

- A repo-wide revert could wipe the session's uncommitted port.
- "Timeout is not a catch" would have misread real assertion failures in Playwright, Cypress, Detox, and Maestro, which report failed assertions as timeouts.
- An interrupted check left no record of the planted bug.
- Migrations already in progress were never asked whether to turn the check on.
- There was no instruction for a project where the old suite cannot run.

cubic's three findings (conditional `Run old`, the stricter-port outcome, and the docs claim) are fixed in e26397e3.

title: docs: fix packaged docs against source, ship snippets, check anchors
body: Every `docs/**/*.mdx` page ships in the `e2e` package so coding agents can read the docs offline. An audit of those 57 pages against `packages/*/src` turned up about 45 wrong or stale claims. This PR fixes them, ships the snippets the pages import, and adds a check for `#anchor` links, which `mint broken-links` does not cover. **Packaging** - `packages/e2e/scripts/prepare-build.ts` now copies `docs/snippets/*.jsx`. `quickstart` and `models` keep the provider list (packages, env vars, model setup) only in `model-provider.jsx`, so offline those sections were empty. Every page-level `import` now resolves inside the package. - New `scripts/check-docs-anchors.ts`, run by `docs:check`. It slugs headings, tabs, and accordions the way Mintlify does (`@sindresorhus/slugify` 2.2.0, the version `@mintlify/common` pins). It found `/reference/config#tests` in `reference/cli.mdx`, which matches no heading. **Wrong claims fixed** - `security.mdx` said there is no update check, but `e2e feedback` fetches `registry.npmjs.org/e2e/latest`. - `reference/security.mdx`: - A tool without `execute` fails with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`, not `INVALID_CONFIG`. - The saved-session envelope keeps the secret-filled flag unencrypted (authenticated only). - Redaction covers only `.txt`/`.csv`/`.json`/`.html`/`.htm` downloads. - Limrun is now listed under outbound connections. - `reference/engine.mdx`: a failing `startVideo` fails the launch only when the video mode was set explicitly. Also adds the missing `EnginePrepareInfo.headed`, and maps `select_at`/`type_at`/`press_at` to their action kinds. - `reference/mobile.mdx`: `mobile({ app })` gets the generic unknown-key error. Also covers the `prepare` failures that end the run, `press('Space')`, and the `FoldPose` export. - `migrate/playwright.mdx`: `web({ connect })` is CDP-only, so `use.connectOptions` is now a "missing" row. There is no `-g`. - `migrate/maestro.mdx`, `migrate/detox.mdx`, `skills/migrate-to-e2e`: use `init --engine mobile` instead of initializing for web and swapping the engine by hand. - `ci/bitrise`, `ci/codemagic`, `ci/eas-workflows`: Node 24. A preinstalled 22.x can be older than 22.22.3, which fails with `NODE_UNSUPPORTED`. - `reference/errors.mdx`: - `AgentError` now shows `category`/`retryable`/`details`. - The two conflicting `POLICY_DENIED` rows are merged into one that links the security rules. - Adds how `e2e login`/`logout`/`models` print failures. - Smaller fixes: - `environment.mdx`: 4 CI markers, `LIMRUN_*`, `E2E_WEB_BROWSERS_*`, and `inheritEnv`. - `agent.mdx`: `vision` with a custom executor, `StepCacheInfo.entry`/`detail`, and mobile's missing `selectOption`. - `config.mdx`: `undefined` handling. - `mcp.mdx`: exit codes. - `debugging.mdx`: a jq recipe for serial groups, and `unbox-ai runs`/`--run 0`. - `telemetry.mdx`: `--watch` and `run()`. - `expect.mdx`: two sample messages the code shown could not produce. - `screen.mdx`: null guard on `boundingBox()` and the swipe duration range. - `web.mdx`: `WebBasicAuth` and `WebInitScript`. - `authentication.mdx`: missing imports. - Source, with an `e2e` patch changeset: - `engine/manifest.ts`: the `version` error no longer says the version keys the replay cache (it keys sessions and reports). - `types.ts`: the `E2EConfig.output` JSDoc names `results/` instead of `artifacts/`. Pages are not shortened here, to keep the diff reviewable. Per-page shortening PRs stack on this one. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm run check`, including the new anchor check: `docs anchors: 320 anchor links across 57 pages resolve`. On `origin/main` it reports `docs/reference/cli.mdx:565: no #tests in docs/reference/config.mdx`. - The anchor check was run on a scratch page with a 4-backtick fence around a 3-backtick one, duplicate accordion titles, ``, ``, an explicit tab `id`, and a `{#custom}` heading. Each case resolves or fails the way Mintlify renders it. - `node scripts/prepare-build.ts && npm pack --dry-run`: 57 pages plus 5 `docs/snippets/*.jsx` ship, and every page `import` resolves inside the package. - Every changed claim was checked against `packages/*/src` by a separate fresh-context verification pass. - `mint dev` renders the changed pages: | `errors.mdx` POLICY_DENIED | `debugging.mdx` serial groups | `web.mdx` WebBasicAuth | | --- | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5678c36-e46d-4586-901d-7e4a1abf1b1b) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af08c065-63e3-4929-a9c5-2f0fa5c607c4) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/851f673d-eeb7-4d80-9be3-1b5d4dab1c4d) |

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.2.4

### Patch Changes

- [#1035](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1035) [`7e568f2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7e568f2826aeb08ffa3fd0a263c579df578d8d26) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Count the tokens and served model of a model call that returns while its step is being cancelled.
## e2e@0.21.2

### Patch Changes

- [#957](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/957) [`b1646e2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b1646e25ba12be7146238fcbc6972ad9d101358b) Thanks [@zichen0116](https://github.com/zichen0116)! - The agent's `tap`, `double_tap`, and `right_click` tools, in `agent.act` and the MCP server, take an optional `modifiers` list (`Shift`, `Control`, `Alt`, `Meta`, `ControlOrMeta`) on an engine that declares `tapModifiers`, like the test API's `tap({ modifiers })`. The held keys are recorded and replayed from the cache. Custom executors see the capability as `ctx.target.tapModifiers` and pass `{ modifiers }` to `ctx.actions.tap`, `doubleTap`, and `secondaryTap`.

- [#1192](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1192) [`40bea9e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/40bea9e60948c4a9be25010870112ec1b0383f17) Thanks [@adc77](https://github.com/adc77)! - Report the model behind cached actions and identify replays made with a different model.

- [#1029](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1029) [`7d067af`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7d067afef236ef802fde9be142b9d2da22bd3ede) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Align failure code-frame carets and clip source lines by terminal display width.

- [#1190](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1190) [`e4d16ec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/e4d16eceebc18911ca04542393c1581dc451208c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A TypeScript file that another loader (such as `tsx`) left with an inline source map that is not JSON or not shaped like a source map now loads, with stack traces pointing at that loader's output, instead of failing with a `TypeError`.

- [#1153](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1153) [`bf3c8e8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bf3c8e8ac1e9d62e4c4f4ceed05fcd30325ccc4f) Thanks [@TheTuso](https://github.com/TheTuso)! - `copilot()`: a model GitHub Copilot does not serve to the account (`model_not_supported`) now stops the run once with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` naming the model and the cause, instead of failing every test with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`.

- [#1178](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1178) [`2791786`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/2791786ced4122968411c509f64cf969b9f1d31f) Thanks [@michalpobuta](https://github.com/michalpobuta)! - The `getByTestId` and `SemanticNode.testId` docs now say an engine may also match an id without its platform's namespacing. No type changes.

- [#1168](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1168) [`236611f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/236611fafbf70be803c0c8725a8824d6bb008096) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Correct two messages: a missing engine `version` no longer claims it keys the replay cache, and the `output` option's description names `results/` instead of `artifacts/`.

- [#1187](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1187) [`82d1f3f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/82d1f3fa856cd0af2a87b7eaf9838618b251d66f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - With more than one worker, `e2e run` starts the files that took longest in the previous run first, so a slow file no longer starts last and holds the run open after the other workers finish.

title: feat: retain configurable run result history
body:
- Full reruns clear `results/`, which can erase the trace and screenshot needed to investigate a flaky test. Add opt-in run history for item 8 of #1020.
- The proposed `keepResults` setting saves the canonical report, result artifacts and enabled AI trace under `<output>/history/<run-id>/`. Its limit includes the latest run; `0` leaves existing history untouched.
- Publish each copied snapshot before pruning owned history. Cache files, encrypted sessions and MCP recordings are excluded. Reserve `history/` consistently in output validation, including when retention is disabled.
- API name, placement and counting rules await maintainer confirmation. The proposed redesign to move the previous run into history at startup remains deferred until that decision, including the reporter-path and snapshot-rendering concerns in the review.

```ts
export default {
  keepResults: 3,
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Write current report and traces] --> B[Copy into staging]
  B --> C[Publish history/run-id]
  C --> D[Prune older owned snapshots]
```

Refs #1020, item 8.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI with real Chromium on `apps/testbed`: intentional failure followed by two successful full reruns with `keepResults: 2`, using `node ../../packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.history-probe.config.ts`.

| Check | main | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Failure evidence after a full rerun | Old screenshot and trace removed | Archived report and screenshot bytes unchanged; trace points to saved artifacts |
| Third run with a limit of two | No history | Exactly the second and third snapshots remain |

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
    Traces  .e2e/history-probe-1020/results/ (1 page, trace.md in each test's directory)
   History  .e2e/history-probe-1020/history/01a14495-b01f-79a5-938f-1a9ee3893247/report.json
```

- The CLI rejected cache paths under history with omitted, zero and positive retention settings, plus flag, environment-variable and symlink paths. Each rejection preserved existing output unchanged.
- Full testbed: 78 passed, one skip. Deterministic browser benchmark with history enabled: 91 passed; the archived report matched the canonical report byte for byte.
- Six randomized pairs of `tests/todos.e2e.ts` against main `40bea9e6`, with history disabled, matched every outcome, step and counter.

| Default-history benchmark | main median | Branch median | Paired change, 95% interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Process wall time | 4.00 s | 4.31 s | +0.1%, -10.8% to +13.6% |
| Sum of test attempts | 2.93 s | 3.20 s | -1.4%, -9.3% to +15.3% |

- Timing was noisy and the comparison remained unresolved. No performance claim.
- Rendered the configuration reference in Chromium. Its screenshot remains local because GitHub attachment uploads require upstream write access.

title: feat(mobile): match Android test ids without their package prefix
body:
## What and why

I was adding a .NET MAUI example (it comes in a follow-up PR) and the Flutter tests, copied over unchanged, passed on iOS and found nothing on Android. MAUI writes `AutomationId` into the resource id as `<package>:id/<AutomationId>` ([SemanticExtensions.cs#L98](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/blob/51cf98f249bbb18aacfa0d35e5add1f50bf5fc38/src/Core/src/Platform/Android/SemanticExtensions.cs#L98)), the shape of a classic `android:id` from an XML layout, which Android reports with the package of the resource table. Compose (with `testTagsAsResourceId`), React Native and Flutter write the bare string, and those are the only Android stacks in the examples and benchmarks, so `getByTestId` never had to deal with a prefix.

- On Android, `getByTestId('greet')` now also matches `<package>:id/greet` for any package but the framework's `android` (`ANDROID_RESOURCE_ID` in `packages/mobile/src/locate.ts`), the way Maestro's `idMatches` does. That covers builds whose resource package differs from the application id (`applicationIdSuffix`, flavors).
- The full id still matches, and a RegExp is tested against both forms. iOS, the projected tree and the cache's `id=` selectors don't change.
- `SemanticNode.testId` and the `getByTestId` JSDoc, with their copies in `docs/reference/engine.mdx` and `docs/reference/screen.mdx`, now say an engine may also match an id without its platform's namespacing. The Android rule is in `docs/reference/mobile.mdx`. No type changes; `e2e` gets a patch changeset for the doc comments.

Two things change for existing Android suites, and the `@e2e-dev/mobile` changeset says so. A negative check on a bare id like `toHaveCount(0)` used to pass because nothing matched, and now it sees the node. And if one screen has both `greet` and `<package>:id/greet`, the string `greet` is ambiguous, so the runner's strictness check refuses it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The MAUI example from the follow-up PR on an Android 15 emulator and an iOS 26.4 simulator, with `@e2e-dev/mobile` packed from main and from this branch and installed into it with `npm install --no-save`.

| Example locator tests | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android | 0/3, `locator matched no nodes within getByTestId("greet")` | 3/3 |
| iOS | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Unit tests cover an `applicationIdSuffix` build (app `com.foo.debug`, view `com.foo:id/greet`), framework ids staying full-only, and a bare id next to a prefixed one returning both nodes.

I didn't run `bench:ab`, since it only covers the web suites and this is one string comparison in the mobile `locate`. The mobile benchmark shouldn't move either. The prefixed ids in its Android snapshots are `dev.e2e.benchmark:id/action_bar_root` and the status bar's `com.android.systemui:id/*`, and no test queries any of their short names.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. (Doc comments only, no type or wire change.)
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. (Only the `SemanticNode.testId` comment changed; `@e2e-dev/web` behaves the same, so it has no changeset.)

title: fix(report): name the step whose error ended the test
fix(mobile): read an iOS screen title from the navigation bar identifier
body: ## What and why Split out of #1105, for #842. This does not close #842: an untitled sheet still takes the navigation bar of the screen behind it. - `screenTitle` returns an iOS navigation bar's identifier only when a text inside the bar shows that same string. UIKit and SwiftUI put the title in both. The bar's label is the back button on a pushed screen, and an untitled screen's identifier is a class name (`_Tt…`, `Module.ClassName`, or a bare ObjC name) with no matching text, so neither is a title. - An Android toolbar's resource id is not a title. The title is the toolbar's label, else the first text inside it. - iOS recordings that start on a pushed screen were re-recorded on an iPhone 17 Pro running the iOS 26.5 runtime. `--strict-cache` fails with `REPLAY_STALE` until that re-record. ## Verified iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5 (23F73), the benchmark Release build. - `pnpm run typecheck` and `packages/mobile` unit tests (308). - Committed iOS captures assert `screenTitle` (`modal-flow` → `Modal Flow`, `home` → `Benchmark Examples`, `bottom-tabs`, `stripe-paymentsheet`, and the untitled SwiftUI screen → none). - SwiftUI fixture app (`tests-capture/swiftui-bar`, `NavigationStack` plus a custom toolbar), raw snapshots committed: Inbox / Message / Compose take the `navigationTitle`; the untitled screen's identifier is `_TtGC7SwiftUI32NavigationStackHosting` and `screenTitle` is undefined. - Agent cache re-recorded on that simulator. Login Form, Modal Flow, Apple Pay, and Permission Prompt replay under `--strict-cache` at `dev.e2e.benchmark / `. Bottom Tabs (no bar) replays at `dev.e2e.benchmark`. - WebView Accessibility, Debounced Search, and Choice Controls are main's recordings with only `startPath` and `endPath` changed to the screen title. WebView replays under `--strict-cache` with `Coupon applied` in its end check. - Permission Prompt resets the microphone on the device under test (`device.setPermission('microphone', 'reset')`, iOS only) before the step, so the recorded Allow tap replays on a reused simulator. Replayed under `--strict-cache`. - Deleted: Apple Pay Billing Address (the sheet keyboard covers the remaining fields, `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`; CI already skips it) and Stripe PaymentSheet (the recording taps New card, dismisses the keyboard, and taps Pay without entering a card, so it cannot replay to the end). - Main's Debounced Search and Choice Controls do not finish under `--strict-cache` on iOS 26.5 either, with or without this change: the recorded tap on the `Benchmark Target` row has no touch point of its own (`action-failed`), and the `✓, Mushrooms` checkbox is not on screen (`target-not-found`). iOS CI does not run `--strict-cache`, so both hand off to the model there as they do on main. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: ci(mcp): list e2e mcp in the MCP Registry
body: Lists `e2e mcp` in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.tester-army/e2e`, published from CI after each release. Nothing is published by hand: registry versions are immutable. - `packages/e2e/package.json`: `mcpName`, which the registry checks on npm to prove ownership. - `packages/e2e/server.json`: npm package entry, `npx e2e@ mcp` over stdio. - `scripts/sync-mcp-server.ts`: `version-packages` keeps `server.json` on the runner's version, so the release commit carries the entry. `spec.yml` and `pnpm check` run `mcp-server:check`. - `.github/workflows/mcp-registry.yml`: checks out the `e2e@` tag, skips a version already listed, waits for npm to serve that version with `mcpName`, then publishes with a pinned, sha256-checked `mcp-publisher` v1.8.1 over GitHub OIDC. Dispatch it by hand with a version to retry a failed publish. - `release.yml` calls it only when changesets published `e2e`. Nightlies are never listed. - `docs/reference/mcp.mdx`: a short note on the registry listing. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[release job: changeset publish] -->|e2e in publishedPackages| B[mcp-registry.yml] D[workflow_dispatch version] --> B B --> C{already listed?} C -- yes --> E[skip] C -- no --> F[wait for npm mcpName] --> G[mcp-publisher login github-oidc + publish] ``` First listing is the next e2e release (0.21.1 on npm has no `mcpName`). Older versions can't be backfilled. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Version skew, since a registry client runs `npx e2e@ mcp` while the project has its own e2e installed. Scratch project with a web target, a local app, and a project tool built with the project's `defineTool`. I drove it with an MCP stdio client: `open_session`, `call observe`, `call ping` (project tool), `call locate`, `close_session`. | server (npx) | project install | result | | --- | --- | --- | | 0.20.0 (own) | 0.20.0 | all ok (baseline) | | 0.21.1 | 0.20.0 | all ok | | 0.19.0 | 0.21.1 | all ok | | this branch, packed tgz | 0.20.0 | all ok, `locate` returns `screen.getByRole("button", "Go")` | Shared state already goes through `Symbol.for` slots (`packages/e2e/src/internal/realm-slot.ts`), so two copies work. That's why this is an npm package listing, not discovery only. ``` e2e mcp: [info] e2e mcp 0.21.1 serving /private/tmp/mcp-skew open_session ok Session ... open on target "web" (platform web, engine web 0.15.1) call observe ok #n2 heading "Hello skew" / #n3 button "Go" call ping ok pong call locate ok 1 node matches getByRole("button", name: "Go"). ``` Release plumbing, all without publishing: - The packed tarball's `package.json` has `mcpName: io.github.tester-army/e2e`. `server.json` is not in the tarball. - `pnpm run version-packages` in a throwaway worktree bumped `server.json` to 0.21.2 along with the package. `mcp-publisher validate` passes on that output and on the committed file. - The registry API returns 404 for this server today and 200 for a listed one, so the "already listed" check works. - The workflow's jq and bash snippets run locally against sample `publishedPackages` JSON. actionlint is clean. title: chore(lint): reject chained type assertions in package source
body: ## What and why - New repo-local oxlint plugin in `scripts/oxlint-plugin/`, loaded through `jsPlugins`. Its one rule, `e2e/no-chained-type-assertions`, is on for `packages/*/src/**`. - Adapted from [dmmulroy/anti-slop](https://github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop) (MIT). The license sits next to the rule. - The rest of that rule set misfires here: blank-line spacing, the conditional spread that `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` needs, and blanket `typeof`/`unknown` bans. - `x as unknown as T` turns off TypeScript's overlap check. 14 of the 16 hits in `src` are fixed: - `internal/ai-trace.ts:225`: six casts dropped. The structural event views are now checked against the AI SDK types, as the comment above them claims. - `agent/error.ts`, `internal/errors.ts`: the cross-realm error guards narrow with `in` instead of casting. - `internal/source.ts`: stack frame groups are checked instead of cast. - `oauth/device-code.ts:145`: the RFC 8628 poll cast raw JSON to `TokenResponse`. Both token paths now go through one zod `parseTokens` in `oauth/token-endpoint.ts`. - Two hits keep the double cast, each with a reasoned disable comment: the phantom `RedactedNode` brand mint and the `EngineHandle` built key by key. - `@oxlint/plugins` is a root devDependency pinned to oxlint's version (1.83.0). Dependabot's `dev-tooling` group moves the two together. - Tests are out of scope (195 hits, mostly fakes). ```jsonc "jsPlugins": [{ "name": "e2e", "specifier": "./scripts/oxlint-plugin/index.ts" }], "overrides": [{ "files": ["packages/*/src/**"], "rules": { "e2e/no-chained-type-assertions": "error" } }] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `oxlint` on a planted `(process.env as unknown as { n: number }).n`: it fires in `packages/e2e/src` and stays quiet in `packages/e2e/tests`. ``` packages/e2e/src/planted-lint-probe.ts:1:25: error e2e(no-chained-type-assertions): Chained assertions skip the compiler check. ... ``` - After type stripping, `observation.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `read-semantics.ts`, `ai-trace.ts` and `openai.ts` emit the same JS as main. - `requestTokens` against a local server answering `null`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` | `OAuthError FLOW_FAILED` | - Testbed suite on the built packages: 78 passed. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

Files new since that run go first; ties keep collection order. - Before, a long file collected late could start last and hold the run open after every other worker went idle. - Report order is unchanged; it is sorted separately. title: perf(runner): scrollUntilVisible strides back to back
body: ## What and why - `scrollUntilVisible` slept `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (100ms) after every swipe. A long scroll spent most of its time there (~435 strides in `virtualized-table`). - The sleep was hiding a race: Playwright's `mouse.wheel` resolves before the scroll reaches script, so an immediate read can see the pre-scroll DOM. - Fix at the source: the web engine's swipe now resolves after a rendered frame (`wheelRendered`, rAF then a task), and the runner reads again right away. - The fixture's raw `mouse.wheel` is unchanged. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `apps/web-benchmark`, `e2e run --workers 1`, 2 runs each. All 91 tests pass. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | serial | 117.0s / 117.9s | 89.0s / 89.3s | - Mobile shares the loop: `apps/mobile-benchmark` `tests/flows-lists.e2e.ts` on an iOS 26.5 sim passes 7/7 on both, 244s on main vs 232s here (row 512 list: 155s vs 146s).

title: chore(lint): require a check on JSON parsed in package source
body:
## What and why

- `JSON.parse` and `.json()` return `any`. Typing that result (`as T`, `const x: T =`, `return` from a function typed `T`) skips every check, so a bad body surfaces later as a `TypeError` or a wrong value.
- New rule `e2e/no-unchecked-json` in the local plugin, on for `packages/*/src/**`. Parsed JSON must be typed `unknown` (or `Promise<unknown>`) wherever it lands, until a schema or a check narrows it.
  - It covers assertions, declarations (an untyped one too), assignment to a typed `let`, and returns, including from an untyped function. An inline callback such as `.then((r) => r.json())` is exempt, because the call it feeds is checked where it lands.
  - It looks through `await`, `?.`, `!`, `.catch(...)` and `.then((r) => r.json())`.
  - It is AST-only, so passing parsed JSON straight to a typed parameter still gets through.
- 26 hits fixed, most with a real check:
  - **oauth:** zod schemas plus one `readJsonBody(response, schema, subject)` in `oauth/errors.ts`. A body that is not JSON, or has the wrong shape, becomes `FLOW_FAILED` naming the vendor.
  - **config:** typed readers. A malformed inline source map from an earlier loader (`tsx`) is dropped instead of failing the import.
  - **eas, limrun:** typed readers (no zod there). `isRecord` moves to `packages/eas/src/json.ts`.
  - **lightpanda:** `/json/version` read as `unknown`. A body without a version now reports `unknown` instead of polling until the startup timeout.
- 3 reasoned disables:
  - `agent/act-validation.ts:117`: our own `JSON.stringify` output.
  - `web/src/observation.ts:163`: page-reported metadata, as unchecked as the structured branch next to it.
  - `web/src/browser.ts:521`: the public `json<T = unknown>()`, where the caller names `T`.

```ts
// packages/e2e/src/oauth/token-endpoint.ts
return readJsonBody(response, TokenResponseSchema, `the ${vendor} token response`, 'is missing access_token');
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Rule tests: 18 unchecked shapes reported, 13 `unknown`-typed or non-JSON ones pass. `src` is clean.
- Each behavior change has a unit test that fails on the base and passes here. For example:

  | input | base | this branch |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | token endpoint answers HTML | `SyntaxError` | `FLOW_FAILED: the Acme token response is not JSON` |
  | device-flow poll answers `null` | `TypeError` | `FLOW_FAILED` |
  | EAS `createDeviceRunSession` without its fields | `TypeError` | `EAS: unexpected response to createDeviceRunSession` |
  | ChatGPT device grant without `code_verifier` | posts the string `"undefined"` | `FLOW_FAILED` before the exchange |

- Real loader (`node --enable-source-maps --import packages/e2e/src/config/register.ts`), a `.ts` file carrying an inline map of `{"version":3}`:

  | base | this branch |
  | --- | --- |
  | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map') at new TraceMap` | `Error: boom on line 3`, mapped to the file |

- Testbed suite on the built packages: 78 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(cache): replay same-app navigations where the app runs now
body: Fixes ENG-999. - The agent's `navigate` recorded its argument verbatim (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts`), so an absolute URL on the app's origin kept the recording run's port. `startPath` and `endPath` were already app-relative (`appLocation`), so a replay on a fresh port with a stable `app.identity` passed the start check, then opened the dead origin and stopped with `action-failed`: the agent redid the step, or `--strict-cache` failed it with `REPLAY_STALE`. - `appNavigation` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/route.ts`) cuts the app's origin off such a URL and keeps the rest as typed, so redaction and `unique()` slots read the same text as before. - Kept as given: another origin, a relative reference, a URL with credentials, and any rest that would not open the same URL on the recorded origin (`//host/x`, a backslash). - Replay is unchanged: it already resolves a path against the current `app.url`. Entries recorded before this still replay on their own origin and keep the old address until re-recorded. A deployment under another base path still misses, as `startPath` does. - Step text for such a navigation reads `navigate to "/todos"` instead of the full URL. - The links the agent reads use the same rule (`renderHref` and `treeHref` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts`): an app link `http://127.0.0.1:3000//settings` showed as `href="//settings"`, which a navigate resolves to the host `settings`; it now shows whole. In Chromium on a page with that link, the agent's line read `href="//settings"` before and the full URL now. ```diff "actions": [{ "name": "navigate", - "summary": "navigate to \"http://127.0.0.1:4291/todos\"", - "url": "http://127.0.0.1:4291/todos" + "summary": "navigate to \"/todos\"", + "url": "/todos" }], "startPath": "/", "endPath": "/todos" ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built-in agent, live (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`): a scratch app on port `0` with no `app.identity` shows an invite link as text, and the step is "Open the invite link shown on the page". The model called `navigate` with `{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:50034/invite/team-blue"}` (`--ai-trace`). Then a strict replay on a new port: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | recorded `navigate.url` | `http://127.0.0.1:49979/invite/team-blue` | `/invite/team-blue` | | replay on a new port, `--strict-cache` | ✗ `REPLAY_STALE`, `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` | ✓ `Cache 1 replayed`, no model call | - testbed, a scratch config with a stable `app.identity`, the port from `PORT`, and a deterministic executor that navigates to the Todos link's `href` from `observe({ tree: true })`, an absolute URL on the app. Recorded on port 4291, then replayed on 4292 with `--strict-cache` while 4291 was down. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | recorded `navigate.url` | `http://127.0.0.1:4291/todos` | `/todos` | | replay on 4292, `--strict-cache` | ✗ `REPLAY_STALE` | ✓ `Cache 1 replayed` | main: ```text × opens todos through the main nav > agent.act "Open the "Todos" page from the main nav" 115ms failed REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays (action-failed), and cache.strict hands no step to the agent; ... - cache: no replay: a recorded action failed; at action 1 of 1, navigate to "http://127.0.0.1:4291/todos": navigation failed: page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED ``` - An entry holding the absolute URL, replayed on its own port with `--strict-cache`: `Cache 1 replayed`, and the file is unchanged. - The new integration test in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-trace-cache.test.ts` (two fixture apps sharing one `app.identity`) fails on the main build with `url: "http://127.0.0.1:61091/about"`, and without that check with the reported `REPLAY_STALE` (`action-failed`, `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`). It passes here.

title: fix(cache): report the models behind replayed recordings
body:
- Save one optional `recordedBy: { provider, model }` from the resolved configured model, redacted once by the recorder. Cached steps expose it in `step.cache.recordedBy` and the trace page.
- Show `replayed · recorded with provider/model` only for a known mismatch, once per test and recording inside its file block. Compare only the agent named in the header, including when a step pins another agent.
- Preserve replay keys, per-member saves, the existing header and AI summary. Ignore malformed, blank or oversized attribution without losing a cache hit. Older recordings stay compatible.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Record with A] --> B[Replay with B]
  B --> C[Report A and show the mismatch]
```

Addresses #1000. Maintainer confirmation of this approach remains pending, including whether a repaired step should report the consulted recording's A while its replacement entry names configured model B.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Built CLI on a real Chromium counter app: `node ../../packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.model-probe.config.ts` from `apps/testbed`, using controlled AI SDK responses.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| Replay under B has no record of configured model A | JSON and trace page identify A; console names A inside the file block |

```text

✓ |web| model-probe.e2e.ts (1 test)
  ✓ model provenance
    agent.act "increment the counter twice" replayed · recorded with fake-loop/model-A
```

- The actual decision executor recorded configured text model A, replayed without a notice under A, and showed one under B. With no configured text model, recording and replay omitted attribution. Replays made zero decision calls.
- Regression tests cover mixed-model executors, unreported model identities, retry and serial deduplication, per-call pinned agents, and the 300-character boundary. Oversized attribution still replays with zero model calls.
- `--no-cache --ai-trace` matched main's 4,438-character prompt, 23 tools and action sequence. Testbed: 78 passed. Browser benchmarks: 91 deterministic tests and 26 replay tests, zero replay calls and all 30 committed entries unchanged. The stress suite produced its expected failures.
- The repeated-label CLI case replayed two distinct recordings across two attempts with zero executor calls, two notices and unchanged recording bytes.
- Previewed all three updated docs pages. The cache guide only reorders the reuse rule before the evaluation advice, with no prose added or removed.

At `0710b120`, `pnpm check` and all 4,556 tests passed. A fresh-context review found no critical or important issues.

Six randomized paired control-inventory benchmarks against main `e6260535` matched all outcomes and counters, including zero model calls:

| Seven control-inventory tests | 7.43 s | 7.39 s | Same within 5% |

title: feat(config): add firstAvailable to pick a model by credential
body: Closes #1116. ## What and why - `firstAvailable([{ env, model }])` returns the first model whose environment variable is set, once, at config load. ```ts import { firstAvailable } from 'e2e'; import { gateway } from 'ai'; import { anthropic } from '@ai-sdk/anthropic'; const agent = { model: firstAvailable([ { env: 'AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY', model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast') }, { env: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', model: anthropic('claude-sonnet-5') }, ]), }; ``` - With none set, config load fails with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` and names every variable checked. title: Expose programmatic exploration with runtime configuration through e2e/runner
docs(reference): rewrite the API reference in the Next.js shape
body:
Rewrites all 16 `docs/reference/` pages in the shape of the Next.js API reference (for example [`next/image`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image)): a reader finds a member in a short table at the top and its details one click down.

## The shape

- A lede and one minimal example with a file title.
- `## Reference` is the first section on every page and holds the API.
  - One group (app, agent): a summary table, then each entry as `###`.
  - Several groups (screen, config, test, web, ...): each group is a `###` with its summary table, and entries are `####`.
- Summary tables stay minimal: the linked name plus `Returns`, `Type | Default`, or a description of at most six words. No Example column; details live in the entry.
- Each entry: what it is, a short example with the default as a code comment, accepted values, a `Throws | When` table, at most one `<Note>`.
- Explanatory sections (behavior rules, budgets, setup) follow `## Reference`, then `## Types`, `## Examples`, `## Related`.
- No Version History tables: nothing reliable feeds them yet.

Mintlify gives `##` to `####` an anchor and a line in "On this page", and `#####` neither. Linked sub-parts that landed at `#####` (`cli#flags`, `cli#output`, `web#recovering-a-cdp-transport`, ...) keep their anchors through an explicit `<a id>`.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa18f95a-1ee1-49cf-a913-9b5d905a923a) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07140f02-376d-4e05-bce9-803e2fcfc4ca) |

![a page with several groups](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3baa4d1a-643d-4475-90e5-4dfe5bef92a3)

## Shorter and corrected

- A shortening pass, per `authoring-docs`, merged facts said twice, gave each declaration's JSDoc one home, linked defaults to the page that owns them (timeouts to config, key names to engine, secure fields to expect), and split long sentences. It cut no fact.
- Reviews (a fresh-context self-review and Cubic) checked the pages against the source. Where the old pages disagreed with the source, they now follow it. Examples: `mcp --target` is a default that `open_session` overrides; a locator assertion times out as `ASSERTION_FAILED`; `agent.assert` keeps its evidence screenshot after a pass too; `stop_recording` can return a provider URL; a fork's `pull_request` token cannot post the GitHub comment; `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` and `APP_UNREACHABLE` say when and how they report.
- The pages are longer than on main (8,643 to 13,272 lines), mostly summary tables and per-entry examples.

## Skills

`.dev/skills/authoring-docs/SKILL.md` now describes the reference shape (headings, summary tables, entries, keep every fact), and `ship-pr` points reference edits at it, so later changes keep pages in this shape.

No changeset: the pages ship inside `e2e`, but this is a docs restructure, as in #1171 and #1185.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm check` and `docs:check`: OG cards, verbatim examples, package-manager blocks, 858 anchors, `mint validate`, broken links, and the error-code check (85 codes).
- `mint dev`: the pages render with Reference, groups, and entries in "On this page", and the summary tables link to their entries. Screenshots above: main from the live site, this branch from `mint dev`.
- A token-by-token comparison of each page before and after the shortening pass found no code name or number lost, other than ones moved to the page a new link points at.

title: feat(testmu): hosted Chrome and Edge for the web engine with testmuBrowsers()
body:
## What and why

- `testmuBrowsers()` from `@e2e-dev/testmu/web`: a `BrowserProvider` that runs web targets in TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Chrome and Edge over CDP (`wss://cdp.lambdatest.com/puppeteer`). Each worker slot gets one session.
- One package per service: it ships in `@e2e-dev/testmu` next to `testmu()`. `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/web` are optional peers. The root entry never imports `@e2e-dev/web`, and `./web` never imports `@e2e-dev/mobile` or agent-device, so a project with one engine loads and type-checks the entry it uses, with `skipLibCheck: false` too. `packages/testmu/tests/unit/entries.test.ts` pins it.
- Session names (`e2e-<run id>-<target>-<slot>`) and the `e2e` project default come from `packages/testmu/src/dashboard.ts`, shared with `testmu()`, so a run's device and browser sessions sit in one build and can't drift.
- Options are `browserName` (`Chrome` by default, or `MicrosoftEdge`) and `capabilities`. `browserVersion` is sent next to `browserName`; every other key goes into `LT:Options`. `user`, `accessKey` and `name` are reserved. A nested `LT:Options`, a `browserName` inside `capabilities`, a non-array `browserOptions`, or a value JSON can't carry fails at config load.
- Defaults: `platform: 'Windows 11'` (the hub refuses a session without one), `project: 'e2e'`, `build: <run id>`, `idleTimeout: 600`, and for Edge `--user-data-dir=remote-debug-profile-edge` in `browserOptions` (without it the Edge CDP connect never completes). A user-set value wins.
- `LT_USERNAME` and `LT_ACCESS_KEY` go only into the CDP URL. Without them the lease fails before any session starts.
- Docs: `integrations/testmu-browsers` next to `integrations/testmu`, plus the browser, integrations, environment, security and skill references.
- First written by @SahilSawLT in LambdaTest/e2e#4, and split out of #772 on review.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { testmuBrowsers } from '@e2e-dev/testmu/web';

export default {
  targets: [
    {
      name: 'testmu-web',
      engine: web({ browser: testmuBrowsers({ browserName: 'MicrosoftEdge', capabilities: { platform: 'Windows 10' } }), viewport: null }),
      app: { url: 'https://staging.example.com' },
    },
  ],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

title: fix(docs): keep the TesterArmy card on screen beside a long table of contents
body: The TesterArmy card under "On this page" is pinned below the table of contents with CSS anchor positioning. The table of contents kept the whole column height, so on any window shorter than the two together the card's "Start testing" button sat below the screen, and since the card is `position: fixed`, no scroll could reach it. On `/browser` that is every window under about 965px. This makes the right column work like the AI SDK docs: the list scrolls, the card stays on screen. - `docs/style.css`: the table of contents leaves 13rem for the card and scrolls in the rest. That rule sits in the same `@supports` as the anchor, the only case where the card is pinned under the list. 13rem is the card's current height plus its gap and a margin, and the comment says to change it with the card. - Below a 40rem window height the card is hidden and the list keeps the whole column, so a short window (devtools docked at the bottom) loses the card, not the page navigation. AI SDK's list shrinks to its heading there. - The list fades at the bottom while more entries are below it (Base UI's `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end`), and "On this page" stays put while entries scroll under it. `scroll-padding-block` keeps a keyboard-focused entry clear of both, and the list's own focus ring is drawn on top so neither hides it. - `docs/table-of-contents.js`: Mintlify highlights the entry for the section on screen but never scrolls the list, so once the list scrolls, that entry can sit under the cut. The script scrolls the list into the same scroll padding when `data-active-deepest` moves. It is the docs site's first script; Mintlify loads any `.js` file in `docs/` on every page. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `mint dev` for main and for this branch, headless Chromium. title: docs(models): pick a model by the key that is set
body:
Answers #1116 with docs instead of a `firstAvailable` export. A ternary in `e2e.config.ts` already picks the model per machine, and every worker picks the same branch (a mismatch fails with `CONFIG_NOT_DETERMINISTIC`).

- `docs/models.mdx`: new "Pick a model by the key that is set" under "Several models in one config".
  - One agent name, so teammates share recordings. The cache key holds the agent name, not the model (`packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts`).
  - `gateway()` goes last: Vercel OIDC signs it in with no variable to test.
  - A key in `.env` counts only when `process.loadEnvFile()` runs before the ternary.
- `docs/reference/config.mdx`: `process.loadEnvFile('.env')` resolves against the directory e2e runs from, but workers start in the config's directory (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/handle.ts:62`). From a subdirectory, the `existsSync` guard makes the main process and the workers disagree, and the run fails with `CONFIG_NOT_DETERMINISTIC`. Adds one sentence with `new URL('.env', import.meta.url)`. `'.env'` stays the main example because `import.meta` fails `tsc` in a CommonJS package.
- `models.mdx`: 270 -> 290 lines, 1123 -> 1200 prose words. Nothing cut.

```ts
import { anthropic } from '@ai-sdk/anthropic';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

const agent = {
  model: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    ? anthropic('claude-sonnet-5-5')
    : gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast'),
};
```

body:

title: feat(runner): run only the tests a pull request can affect
body:
## What and why

- Adds `filters` to the config: test filters that run before the tests and leave out the ones a pull request can't affect. Most pull requests touch one area, and running the whole suite on each one is slow and costs money.
- `decisionFilter({ model })` in `@e2e-dev/decision` asks a decision model, such as Jev, whether the diff can change what each test checks, and whether it can break the setup that saves the test's session. It leaves out a test only when both are rated under 20% likely affected.
- Filters run only with `--changed-since <ref>`, the same flag name as Jest's `--changedSince`. Unlike Playwright's `--only-changed`, which runs changed test files and the test files that import a changed file, the change here includes app source, and a filter decides what it can affect. CI passes it on pull requests: `npx e2e run ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('--changed-since origin/{0}', github.base_ref) || '' }}` with `fetch-depth: 0`. `main`, the merge queue, and local runs without it run every test. Core reads nothing from the CI environment: the flag alone decides.
- Core rules, which no filter can change:
  - a `--last-failed` rerun is never filtered, so `e2e run || e2e run --last-failed` can't go green on a failure a filter left out;
  - with no file changed since the merge base, no filter runs;
  - an empty or `-`-led ref fails with `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE` before anything runs, and so does a ref git can't measure from (unknown, or no merge base in a shallow checkout) when a filter would run, exit 2;
  - `--changed-since` with no filters configured warns that every test runs;
  - a filter that throws, returns something invalid, or runs past 5 minutes leaves nothing out, with a warning.
- The decision filter's own rules (a custom filter gets every test and decides for itself):
  - a changed test file or setup file, or either's stored screenshots (`<file>-snapshots/`), runs its tests without a question, and the note counts them;
  - a change to a file named `e2e.config.{ts,mts,js,mjs}` or to a lockfile of any package manager (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, deno, CocoaPods, SwiftPM, Gradle, Bundler, Poetry, uv, Go, Cargo, Composer, pub, Mix, NuGet, Nix, Bazel) leaves nothing out when it is in the project's directory, inside it, or above it (the workspace root). A sibling project's or a docs folder's goes to the model.
- `e2e list` claims and redacts the process output as `run` does, since filters and model SDKs run in it, and `--reporter json` keeps stdout for the document.
- `pull_request_target`: the docs recipe passes the flag on `pull_request` only, and the docs say never to pass it on `pull_request_target`, where a fork's diff would reach the model in a run that holds the repository's secrets.
- The change is every file that differs from the merge base of the ref and HEAD, uncommitted and untracked files included. The decision filter reads only what the commits change; an uncommitted or untracked file goes to the model by name only, so a token a CI step writes into the checkout never reaches it.
- This repo's CI uses it on the testbed step: `spec.yml` gets `fetch-depth: 0`, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, and `--changed-since origin/<base>` on pull requests.
- The tradeoff: a PR's testbed check now runs only what Jev keeps. The merge queue and `main` still run every test, so the merge gate stays deterministic. This is noted in `AGENTS.md`.

```ts
filters: [decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev'), providerOptions: { gateway: { zeroDataRetention: true } } })],
```

A custom filter is `{ name, filter }`. The contract is `TestFilter` in `packages/e2e/src/types.ts:1501`; each candidate carries `setupFile` when a setup test saves its session:

```ts
export const areas = {
  name: 'areas',
  filter(tests, { changes, signal, redact }) {
    return { exclude: { [testId]: 'the change reaches none of its areas' }, note: 'optional one-liner' };
  },
} satisfies TestFilter;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[select: flags, then --shard] --> B{--changed-since, not --last-failed, a file changed?}
  B -- no --> R[run every selected test]
  B -- yes --> E[filters in config order, each judges what the last kept]
  E --> F[run what is left; left-out tests report as skipped]
```

### The decision filter

- What it sends:
  - the diff of `changes.files` only, base to HEAD (`git diff -M --irreversible-delete`, so renames and deletions cost a header), then each file no commit changes by name, never its contents;
  - the test files and the setup files, keyed by their path from the repository root as the diff names them.
  - Secrets are redacted from the diff, the file contents, the file paths, and the questions with `context.redact`, which masks every fixed secret and credential password and any run of 8 or more of their characters, so a multi-line key split across diff lines is masked too.
- Questions: one per test, and one per setup file ("can the diff break this setup or the session it saves?"). A test is left out only when both answers are under 20%.
- Batching: files are packed into calls that fit Jev's 32k-token state limit, counted in UTF-8 bytes, at most 200 questions per call (a larger file is split across calls), 8 calls at once.
- When it leaves tests unjudged, they run:
  - a failed call leaves its own tests in, and after 3 failures no more calls start;
  - a diff over 60 kB leaves nothing out, with a note.
- When no call answers (no key, as on a fork's pull request), or git or a file read fails, the filter throws. Core fails it open: `warning: decision failed, so it leaves nothing out: <reason>`, `outcome: "failed"`, every test runs.
- `providerOptions` goes with every call, as on `decisionExecutor`.
- Spend: the note reports it, `(11 calls, 358.8k tokens, $0.0139)`. Cost comes from the AI Gateway, using the list price on your own provider key.
- Narrowing the change, always running smoke tests, or running everything on an `infra/` change is a few-line wrapper around `decision.filter`, shown in `docs/filters.mdx`, not an option.

### Where it shows

| Output | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal | `decision kept 7 of 77 tests, left out 70 (1 call, 17.6k tokens, $0.0007)`, then a `Left out` row in the summary |
| PR comment, `summary.md` | `e2e: 7 passed, 70 left out by filters`, the change line, one line per filter, a folded table of left-out tests with reasons |
| `report.json` | `run.filters` (`outcome` when a filter failed or timed out), `run.changes` (`base` and `files` once git measured the change, else `skipped` alone), `skip.filter` (schema and both fixtures updated) |
| `junit.xml` | left-out tests as skipped cases |
| `e2e list --changed-since origin/main` | the same decision, without starting an app |

### Releases

- `e2e`: patch.
- `@e2e-dev/github`: patch.
- `@e2e-dev/decision`: minor with a **Release:** line, and its `e2e` peer becomes `>=0.21.3`.
- New error code: `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE`.
- New flag: `--changed-since`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed: built CLI, real Jev through the AI Gateway, a branch that breaks the todo counter (`basics.mjs`, one line), `e2e run --changed-since main --reporter list`:

```text
ℹ judging 1 file changed since 3f2c3da
ℹ decision: asking typesafe-ai/jev about 78 tests in 14 files
 ✓ filter "decision" done 874ms
ℹ decision kept 6 of 78 tests, left out 72 (1 call, 18.8k tokens, $0.0007)
...
      Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)
   Left out  72 tests by decision
```

  A run of the same branch without the flag fails the same 4 tests.

- Large suite: the testbed's tests copied 20 times (280 files, 1540 tests), `e2e list --changed-since big-main`. It took 2s, and all 80 copies of the 4 failing tests were kept:

```text
decision: asking typesafe-ai/jev about 1540 tests in 280 files
decision kept 132 of 1540 tests, left out 1408 (11 calls, 358.8k tokens, $0.0139)
```

- A login form label change (`Password` to `Passphrase`), which only the `admin` setup test touches. `e2e list --changed-since main`, 3 runs each. With the setup question, the dashboard `admin` tests are kept; with `setupFile` stripped (the old behavior), Jev left them out at 8-13%, so the broken setup never runs. | --- | --- | --- |
| with the setup question | kept (3/3) | kept (3/3) |

- The other paths, with the built CLI:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |


- This PR's own `check` job passes `--changed-since origin/main` from `spec.yml`. The PR edits the testbed config, so the decision filter leaves nothing out, as designed (`apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts changed, so the decision filter left nothing out`).

- After moving the lockfile and pin rules into the decision filter, on the label branch:

Docs cuts from the shortening pass: on `docs/filters.mdx`, "many test files per call and up to 8 calls at once" is cut as an internal detail; it stays in `AGENTS.md` for contributors.

- Round 8 review (5 subagents: core and decision code-quality reviews, an adversarial bug hunt, git and environment edge cases, live Jev CLI runs). Fixed: the docs `areas` example left out a test whose own file changed (a false green); lockfile and config names matched anywhere in the repo, so a docs example's `e2e.config.ts` ran every test; `e2e list` printed a secret a filter or the config logged and broke `--reporter json`; `:/message` refs were rejected; the docs said a git failure warns when it is `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE`; a partial cost sum was shown as the total; the gate module folded into `filterSelection`. Held up:

  - Linux in Docker (`node:24`, `node:22-bookworm`) and Node 22.23.2 and 24.19.0 on macOS;
  - 12 live Jev scenarios on the testbed: the counter break (7 of 78 kept, 4 failed, `|| --last-failed` stays red), shards 1/2 and 2/2, junit, report.json schema-valid, summary.md and the GitHub reporter, list vs run, no key and invalid key (warning, all run), everything left out (exit 0, no app), Ctrl-C (130 in 0.03 s), timeout via the harness option, both docs examples, the SDK, `--watch` through a pty, lockfile and test edits, uncommitted secrets never sent;

Not in this PR:

- The terminal's `Duration` and `startedAt` start after the filters, as they do after engine prepare.
- The filter's spend is not added to `run.usage` or to the run's overall spend line. That needs a `usage` field on `TestFilterResult`.
- A diff over 60 kB still runs every test. Splitting it across calls, and a sharper question, wait for an eval on PRs from other repos.

title: fix(web): include aria-owned text in accessible names
body: ## What and why - A button can be found by its `aria-owns` text while observations and `toHaveAccessibleName` report an empty name. Include owned text after DOM children in the shared name reader. - Share flat-tree parent traversal for naming and visibility. Append owned targets in the child helper, deduplicate direct references and preserve explicit labels, plain label text and secure-field handling. - Names follow Playwright's role-query behavior where it differs from Chromium: text assigned to an external open slot is skipped, while a directly owned target with `content-visibility: hidden` contributes text. Regression tests pin both cases so name assertions agree with exact role queries. ```html Save changes ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the built CLI against a temporary testbed fixture with the HTML above. `getByRole('button', 'Save changes')` finds one button in both builds; the name assertion fails on main and passes here. Ordinary text and explicit-label controls pass in both. No model calls. | main (`ea7cdb51`) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `toHaveAccessibleName('Save changes')` fails, observed name `""` | Assertion passes, name `"Save changes"` | | Original cases: 1 failed, 2 passed | Original cases: 3 passed | ```text main: ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveAccessibleName failed locator: getByRole("button", name: "Save changes") expected: accessible name "Save changes" observed: name "" (match count 1) this branch: Tests 6 passed (6) ``` - Regression tests cover ID order, duplicates, missing references, cycles, hidden ancestors, generated text, explicit labels, secure fields and open/closed shadow roots. The fixture also runs against Chromium's accessibility tree and Playwright's role selector.
