title: fix(cache): replay steps on nodes known only by a generated test id
body:
Part of ENG-845.

A flow editor names each node `rf__node-<uuid>` and mints a new id on every run. When that test id was all a node had, the replay cache recorded it verbatim, so the next run could never find it. A step whose effect included such a node ended in `end-mismatch`, and a click on one in `target-not-found`, on every run (`REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`).

- `testIdShapeTier` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts`) reads a test id that is a node's only identity as a shape: each uuid, hex id, cuid, or recent epoch time in it becomes `#` (`rf__node-#`, `row-#-delete`). Indexed ids such as `todo-item-12` or `rf__node-dndnode_0` stay exact.
- End check (`packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`): such a node is skipped while a stable anchor exists, like volatile text. When it is the only change, any node of its shape that was not on screen before the replay counts. A vanished one is still checked exactly.
- Click targets: the recording counts the nodes of that shape (`position`). After an exact miss, replay matches by shape only where a place means something, the same rule as an unnamed control: the node was alone, or it sits in a named row or group.
- No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump. Exact matching runs first and is unchanged, the shape paths only run where main always missed, and none of the 389 test id descriptors in the committed benchmark recordings has a minted part.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[recorded target] --> E{exact match}
  E -- found --> A[act]
  E -- none --> M{only a minted test id?}
  M -- no --> H[hand off]
  M -- yes --> P{alone when recorded, or in a named container?}
  P -- no --> H
  P -- yes --> C{same count of that shape?}
  C -- yes --> A
  C -- no --> H
```

What the "add a node" step records:

```jsonc
// main
"endAnchors": [{ "role": "status", "name": "Node added" }, { "role": "box", "testId": "rf__node-712f7aa3-f7cc-4bbf-bf52-1ddf74…" }]
// this branch
"endAnchors": [{ "role": "status", "name": "Node added" }]
```

Known limits:

- nanoid's alphabet includes `-` and `_`, so its pieces often look like words. 79% of nanoids are recognized and skipped as end anchors, but two nanoids share a shape only about 20% of the time; the rest hand off as on main.
- Two nodes of one shape with no named container still hand off: their order is not an identity.
- A click recorded before this release has no count, so it hands off once and re-records.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch testbed project: "Add node" appends `<div data-testid="rf__node-${crypto.randomUUID()}">` and sets a status; clicking a node sets `Node <n> selected`. Built-in agent (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`), one recording run, then `e2e run --strict-cache`, the same commands on main (ea7cdb51) and this branch:

| Step | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| add a node | `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch): missing box `rf__node-712f7aa3-…` | replayed in 172 ms, no model call |
| click the only node | `REPLAY_STALE` (target-not-found) | replayed in 152 ms, no model call |
| click the second of two nodes, no container | `REPLAY_STALE` (target-not-found) | `REPLAY_STALE` (target-not-found), on purpose |

- The same recordings replayed against a broken app on this branch: an "Add node" that does nothing fails with `end-mismatch`, and an extra node on the canvas with `target-ambiguous`.
- Web benchmark `tests-agent` with `CI=1 --strict-cache`: `26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed` on main and on this branch, the same six steps (two never recorded, four with a run-time value).

title: fix(mobile): retain leased device sessions during worker replacement
body:
## Why

- After a failed test, worker cleanup closed the leased device session. Another session could claim the device before the replacement started, causing later tests to fail with "Device is already in use". Addresses #792.

## What changed

- Keep a healthy session during worker replacement. A revocable `EngineDisposeContext.reuseSignal` distinguishes replacement from final cleanup without calling the disposal hook twice.
- Close the session on forced shutdown, IPC disconnect, or an unconfirmed native recording stop. Retry a retained provider recording stop before another attempt on the same worker.
- Validate retention grants in the cloud-provider example, releasing declined grants before acquisition fails. Update lifecycle docs, TestMu wording, and release notes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Mobile worker retires] --> B{Leased, reuse permitted, no unconfirmed native recording?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Replacement resumes session]
  B -- No --> D[Close session]
  C --> E[Run closes session and releases lease]
```

## Scope

- Covers worker replacement and cleanup. Explicit `device.closeApp()` still ends the session and drops its claim.
- Cleanup remains bounded. A worker killed with SIGKILL or one that already exited cannot release daemon resources. Revocation only applies while disposal is pending.
- Failed external recording stops keep the device claim. The worker retries while it owns the handle; providers must clean up remaining external recordings at lease release/run end. Session close cannot guarantee that a cloud recording stops.

## Blast radius

- Mobile keeps its existing `e2e >=0.15.0 <1` peer range. Older cores omit reuse permission, so mobile closes the session during disposal. The engine owns the session; the provider owns the lease.

- Open finding from Cubic: a provider video recovered after its original attempt report closes is cleaned up but may be absent from that report. The built CLI reproduces this loss. Reporting late artifacts across worker IPC and hosted sessions needs a scope decision; this finding remains open.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI, real subprocess workers, actual mobile engine, simulated backend. Checkers reproduce parent loss, third Ctrl-C, native recording-stop failure, and provider recording retry failure before their fixes, then pass here. Healthy replacement also passes. The executable cloud example's declined-grant test fails before its fix and passes after it.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| A competitor claims the device during worker replacement. | The competitor is refused; the replacement uses the original lease; run cleanup releases it once. |

```text
BUG REPRODUCED parent-crash
BUG REPRODUCED third-sigint
BUG REPRODUCED recording-stop
BUG REPRODUCED provider-retry
PASS parent-crash
PASS third-sigint
PASS recording-stop
PASS provider-retry
```

- Native simulator and hosted-provider behavior were not exercised locally. The simulated backend proves runner and engine cleanup behavior, not native daemon locking.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` passes, 78 tests and one skipped. Two measured forms pairs against the merge base each execute five tests per build with matching outcomes, steps, and counters. Timing is unresolved under high host load; no performance claim is made.

- Maintainer follow-up restores the lifecycle comments, separates reuse revocation from worker retirement, names the keep-session decision, and documents native recording reset claim loss. The Cubic stop-confirmation wording is corrected.
- The packed mobile package typechecks with `skipLibCheck: false` and closes its session without reuse permission on exact `e2e@0.15.0` and `e2e@0.21.2`. This does not claim current mobile source can compile against the old core declarations.

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1206](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1206) [`da13624`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/da13624d31fa6cf2204c7b99f1474d718ca1a02a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Release:** Add `decisionFilter({ model })`, a test filter that asks a decision model which tests a pull request can affect and leaves out the rest, such as `filters: [decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev') })]`. The model must answer `boolean` questions; `providerOptions` passes options such as zero data retention to every call. Needs `e2e` 0.21.3 or later.

### Patch Changes

- [#1345](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1345) [`47127f7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/47127f734f34927b040f85aa7db9f9f6a02a2a7d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `decisionFilter` leaves nothing out when the config file the run loaded changed, whatever its name, such as `e2e list --config e2e.ci.config.ts --changed-since origin/main` after an edit to `e2e.ci.config.ts`. A test filter reads that file as `context.configFile`.
## e2e@0.21.3

### Patch Changes

- [#1219](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1219) [`f589a32`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f589a32195bd9c2501f1ce98a118d18afa6da5ec) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `onAction` to `agent.act`: a hook that runs after each action once the screen settles, for replayed actions too. Use it to take a screenshot per action.

- [#1326](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1326) [`04acca1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/04acca1ef06cb660a1bcd467275aa6b661b4cd29) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.screenshot()` returns the absolute path of the file it wrote, not a path relative to the attempt directory.

- [#1218](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1218) [`58a5cec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/58a5cec116ca79b1589cb78b6baae40abf3e735a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Keep screenshots after a secret fill. `app.screenshot()`, `toHaveScreenshot()`, and assertion and failure screenshots no longer stop once a test fills a secret. They mask secure fields only, and `toHaveScreenshot()` still fails when the engine can't prove they are masked. The model still gets no pixels after a fill.

- [#1072](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1072) [`689620d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/689620d728d04202757ffd11ed001b512b68044a) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Do not report a cache entry as evicted when a custom store rejects its deletion.

- [#1310](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1310) [`329e03f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/329e03f7a81e3bb3a8ca5d6e7c96a9a6f21218a2) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Add `--action-timeout <ms>` and `--assertion-timeout <ms>` to `e2e run`. They replace the config's `actionTimeout` and `assertionTimeout` for one run, so a wrong locator can fail in 5 s instead of 30 s while you write a test. A call's own `timeout` still wins, and a value that is not an integer from 1 through 2147483647 is a usage error, exit 2. Watch mode keeps them for every rerun.

- [#1240](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1240) [`332b934`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/332b934684b75227ad60dbc0cc8c59b818ac48e0) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Add `e2e upgrade` (alias `e2e update`): upgrades `e2e` to the latest release, a dist-tag such as `nightly`, or one version, and moves each `@e2e-dev/*` package the project lists from the registry to the newest release whose peer ranges accept it. Linked packages and ones the registry doesn't have stay as they are. The project's package manager installs them; `--dry-run` prints the plan. Each upgrade sends an `e2e_upgrade_completed` telemetry event with the result and the `e2e` versions before and after. The update notice now suggests `e2e upgrade` instead of an install command for `e2e` alone.

- [#1321](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1321) [`72abddd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/72abdddd961e2e3a7d24c973eeb2783bea43ee47) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The e2e plugin now installs in Cursor, from a copy in `~/.cursor/plugins/local/`, with the same three skills as the Claude Code and Codex plugin. Grok Build reads the Claude Code files, so the repository works there as a marketplace too.

- [#1345](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1345) [`47127f7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/47127f734f34927b040f85aa7db9f9f6a02a2a7d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `decisionFilter` leaves nothing out when the config file the run loaded changed, whatever its name, such as `e2e list --config e2e.ci.config.ts --changed-since origin/main` after an edit to `e2e.ci.config.ts`. A test filter reads that file as `context.configFile`.

- [#1275](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1275) [`6a59d1a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6a59d1acfba13745ce126817e3226cee71d033e5) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Update dependencies: the web engine drives Playwright 1.64.1 (and the Chromium it installs), and smol machines boot the matching `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble` image. The runner moves to `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform`, and `@oxc-project/runtime` 0.154.0, `@vitest/expect` 5.0.5, and `@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.28.

- [#1286](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1286) [`a39c1c3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a39c1c30a4de5b62e14ea86f85613f7ecf331c24) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `expect(await response.json()).toMatchSchema(schema)` type-checks: `expect` no longer hands the engine's `json<T>()` a locator type to infer, so the value matchers apply.

- [#1252](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1252) [`3bd32ef`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3bd32ef8ef847368d3a9ad994520309fa39c53a7) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `e2e explore` and the MCP `open_session` now launch a device target's pinned app before their first observation, as a test's `app.open()` does. They no longer depend on the engine's warm-up having opened it, which it skips for a target with an `app.appPath`, and used to fail with `APP_NOT_OPEN`.

- [#1306](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1306) [`3df649c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3df649c0c651cc94b1c079f65c896414596a56b7) Thanks [@knowbody](https://github.com/knowbody)! - Let retiring workers use the configured cleanup timeout for engine disposal so cleanup can finish and report errors before the worker exits.

- [#1318](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1318) [`bbb13bf`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bbb13bf7ffa54734711d9b01930f8fc378cc93be) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - `e2e init --example <name>` starts a new project from one of the repository's example apps (`with-vite`, `with-next`, `with-astro`, `with-expo`, `with-swiftui`, `with-compose`, `with-kotlin-multiplatform`, `with-flutter`, `with-maui`). It downloads the example from the GitHub tag of the running CLI into an empty directory, points its `e2e` and engine ranges at this release, and then runs the usual skill, MCP, and install steps in the example's e2e project.

- [#1280](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1280) [`1071933`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/10719338135a1b1123d8fca78fa6c6f08eb8f68f) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Find `e2e.config.js` and `e2e.config.mjs` as well as `e2e.config.ts` and `e2e.config.mts`, so a project written in plain JavaScript needs no `--config` flag. A TypeScript config still wins in its directory, so the `e2e.config.js` that `tsc` emits beside it is ignored. `e2e init` leaves an existing JavaScript config alone and writes its example test as `tests/example.e2e.js`, and a run that finds only `*.e2e.js` files names the `tests` glob to set. The quickstart shows the JavaScript setup, and the [config reference](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/config#javascript) the details.

- [#1317](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1317) [`9ceb071`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9ceb0710c371ee3acf1a67c1db81dabbf7ef30cc) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Every action in an `e2e mcp` session now answers with the test line that repeats it, such as `Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Save").tap();`, so a coding agent can write the test while it walks the flow. The locator comes from the node as the agent saw it and is checked against the live screen first: it must match that node and nothing else, and twins are narrowed with `{ visible: true }`, a container, or `.nth()`. When no locator works, the result says why and prints no line. Fills name `credentials.user(name)` or `secrets.get(name)`, never a value. The new read-only `test_lines` catalog tool returns the session's lines in order as a draft test body. A project tool can no longer be named `test_lines`, and the `e2e_mcp_session` telemetry event counts its calls under its own name.

- [#973](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/973) [`93f77d8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/93f77d81e2e781b79be242ca1743b705074bb665) Thanks [@A220man](https://github.com/A220man)! - A model that refuses a request (finish reason `content-filter`) now fails the step as `MODEL_REFUSED` instead of `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with "No output generated". Rephrase the instruction or use another model.

- [#1284](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1284) [`90e6fb8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/90e6fb8bef87844957c31fb4b31bd7d2e85d2e75) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `tap_at` and `hover_at`, in `agent.act` and `e2e mcp`, now act on the bare point the model aimed at whenever the engine takes one, instead of snapping to the listed control under it and acting on that control's center. Before, a point outside an iOS popover snapped to the full-screen dismiss region and tapped its center, inside the popover, so the popover never closed. An engine that taps listed nodes only still gets the control by id.

- [#1049](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1049) [`137b50f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/137b50f0c8505a01ca53e4eb4c38df95e12bd395) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Add `locator.or(other)`, which matches either locator in document order and stays strict when both match. Third-party engines must handle the new `union` kind of `LocatorExpression`.

- [#1151](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1151) [`84bd64a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/84bd64ae7554fa8d0d5799d4be7ccedbf26abf41) Thanks [@TheTuso](https://github.com/TheTuso)! - Agent steps on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1 no longer fail with `Invalid signature in thinking block. The block is bound to a different conversation` on a worker's first step or after an earlier screen or screenshot was elided.

- [#1301](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1301) [`82039ad`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/82039ad6d640080f000c159083216c0faad53202) Thanks [@nguyenvanhieu1710](https://github.com/nguyenvanhieu1710)! - Record `observationTruncated: true` on an agent step when any semantic observation in the step was incomplete.

- [#1239](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1239) [`d7ec0ec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d7ec0ecf4458d8818087bd7c9cb31bd1dc241eed) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `screen.tree()` and `screen.debug()`. `tree()` returns the whole screen as the agent reads it, one node per line with secrets redacted. `debug()` prints the same text to the test's output.

- [#1314](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1314) [`b8cb0b3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b8cb0b34a4dfeb3919468f189442ae3df662dd0f) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now gives a coding agent a fast loop for fixing a test: rerun only that test by `file:line` with `--action-timeout 5000`, keep the replay cache on so goals that passed replay without model calls, add `--retries 0` when the config sets retries, don't rename the test or reword a passing goal mid-loop, and, when the test passes, run it one time with `--no-cache`. The coding agents guide no longer tells agents to add `--no-cache` after every change, and the caching guide has a section on rerunning a test while you fix it.

- [#1309](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1309) [`c5e3248`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c5e324854fd523d264eca8e70d69ead6b219d0fa) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The e2e skill now tells a coding agent how to fix a failed test. It fixes from the terminal's failure block and the trace page, every line that evidence covers at once, and checks the lines after the failure before the next run. To see a screen the evidence leaves out, it goes straight there in an MCP session instead of walking the flow again from the start.

- [#1313](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1313) [`f7a34c1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7a34c1b1250ca71e2418d81a5b0bdae85395221) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now keeps an `e2e mcp` session open between test runs while the agent writes or fixes a test on the web, so a live look after a failed run goes straight to the screen in that session instead of opening a new one. It says when a run can go beside the session: with no `app.command`, with a port-0 URL (unless the dev server allows one copy per directory, as `next dev` does), or with `reuseExisting: true` on a fixed port. A fixed port without `reuseExisting` makes the run fail with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`, so the agent offers `reuseExisting: true` to the user instead of adding it, and closes the session before each run until then. With `reuseExisting` and `CI` set, it unsets `CI` for the run or closes the session. On mobile it closes the session before each run. The MCP server page shows the same cases as a table.

- [#1333](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1333) [`4982d8d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4982d8df256180f0a6d68dd49fba0384794924fb) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The e2e skill now explains what a frame from another site, such as a hosted card field, means for agent steps. The browser engine's semantic tree leaves out that frame's content, so the skill scripts steps there with `browser.frameLocator` and judges the frame with `vision`. An `agent.act` whose only change is inside that frame records no replay and runs live every run.

- [#1311](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1311) [`74c2b73`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/74c2b737401c3927084eaf568b55b4854375c699) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now tells a coding agent to start each test near the screen it checks, so every rerun skips the steps that lead there: in a browser a saved session instead of the sign-in form and `app.open` on the screen's path, on a device `device.openLink`, and data created through the app's API in a `test.extend` fixture. A test across several screens grows one screen at a time, with the goals already verified replaying from the cache. Core concepts says the same in one bullet.

- [#1343](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1343) [`1ed4de1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1ed4de1158b0490e5f09fcf14ed24ec55bb0e2a3) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now tells a coding agent to replace a fixed-time sleep with `agent.waitFor` on the state it was waiting for, or a matcher with a longer `timeout` when a locator names that state.

- [#1216](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1216) [`19f3ca2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/19f3ca2916cbfdd76589e3c68266a2d16887a041) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The run telemetry event now sorts executed tests by how the replay cache carried them (`tests_code_only`, `tests_replayed`, `tests_assisted`, `tests_live`), counts `agent.act` steps that ran with the cache off (`agent_steps_uncached`), why steps missed the cache or handed off (`agent_miss_reasons`, `agent_handoff_reasons`), and the model calls by agent entry point (`model_calls_act`, `model_calls_assert`, `model_calls_extract`, `model_calls_waitfor`).

- [#1206](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1206) [`da13624`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/da13624d31fa6cf2204c7b99f1474d718ca1a02a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add test filters: `filters: [decisionFilter({ model })]` from `@e2e-dev/decision` leaves out the tests a change can't affect. They run with `--changed-since <ref>`, such as `origin/main` on a pull request; without the flag every test runs. `e2e list --changed-since origin/main` previews the decision, and left-out tests show in the pull request comment, `junit.xml`, and the report. A run with nothing to run starts no engine or app, and after Ctrl-C, or a reporter that runs past its deadline, the CLI exits as soon as the output is written.

- [#1239](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1239) [`d7ec0ec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d7ec0ecf4458d8818087bd7c9cb31bd1dc241eed) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Print `console.log` and other test output when the `list` reporter is off. With `--reporter json`, all user output goes to stderr, so stdout holds only the report.

- [#1323](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1323) [`0f6c3ef`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0f6c3ef31840f40fe9a987523abb98eec914f17a) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Put the test's title path in agent prompts. Under `e2e run`, every step of the built-in agent and every judgment behind `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` now opens with a `Test: <describe> > <test>` line, and a custom executor reads the title path as `ctx.attempt.titlePath`. The line goes in the step's prompt, not the system prompt, so provider prompt caching still serves every test of a run, and existing recordings keep replaying.

- [#1238](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1238) [`7b6ac53`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7b6ac5327eb6f98fb51f7e22184fdd5274905e75) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Print a notice after a command when a newer `e2e` is on npm, with the install command for the project's package manager. The registry is checked once a day. Nothing prints in CI or when piped. Set `E2E_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=1` or `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` to turn it off. `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turn it off too.

- [#996](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/996) [`7e72ea2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7e72ea2d8d2cd05ef04b34c6f084d9908b348806) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Reject an invalid `shard` passed to `run()` or `list()` with `INVALID_CONFIG`, enforcing the same numeric bounds as the `--shard` flag. - [#1209](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1209) [`ef977f4`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ef977f4856da009cac26d78d2e9bb14e5991ee41) Thanks [@knowbody](https://github.com/knowbody)! - Engine disposal receives optional revocable permission to preserve run-owned resources for a replacement worker. title: fix(cache): bound replay end wait by assertion timeout under load (#1144)
body:
## What and why

Fixes #1144.

When an \^Ggent.act\ step replays under load, the recorded end state may take longer to appear than it did on the quiet recording machine. Previously, \endWaitMs\ was strictly fixed at record time:
\\\	s
endWaitMs: Date.now() - this.endWaitBaselineMs(recorder) + END_WAIT_MARGIN_MS
\\\
On busy machines (e.g., parallel worker test runs against a shared app server), this caused steps to prematurely fail with \REPLAY_STALE (end-mismatch)\ even when the expected end state showed up moments later.

This change uses \max(trace.endWaitMs ?? 0, assertionTimeout ?? 0)\ as the budget when verifying end state on replay. Since end state verification polls, this costs nothing extra when the app renders quickly, while granting slow end states under load up to the test author's configured assertion timeout before reporting an end-mismatch.

## Verified

Ran locally: yes

- \pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts\ passes (including new unit test \waits out the larger of recorded endWaitMs and assertionTimeout for the end state\).

title: fix(cache): replay steps that show a date in another language or in numbers
body:
Part of ENG-845.

The replay cache records what a step changed on screen and checks it again on replay. Text that reads differently on every run is skipped (`VOLATILE_TEXT`, `packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`), but its dates were English month names and ISO only. `٨ سبتمبر ٢٠٢٦`, `8 września 2026` and even `9/8/26` were recorded as end anchors, so the next day's replay ended in `end-mismatch` and re-recorded that day's date (`REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`).

- `packages/e2e/src/cache/dates.ts` adds dates and clock times in any script and digits: numeric (`9/8/26`, `٨‏/٩‏/٢٠٢٦` from `toLocaleDateString('ar-EG')`, `08.09.2026`), with year, month, and day signs (`2026年9月8日`), and a day, a month name, and a year in either order (`8 de septiembre de 2026`, `2026. szeptember 8.`).
- Month names and the words around them (`de`, `gada`, `พ.ศ.`) come from `Intl`: the parts of a full date in about 80 languages. A 4-digit year in ASCII digits must read as one (19xx, 20xx, Buddhist 25xx). So counts and codes stay anchors: `Imported 12 of 1500 records`, `Affichage de 1 à 25 des 1500 résultats`, `Error 1001 at line 12`, `Ticket 12-34-5678`.
- The patterns are built on the first recorded step (about 60 ms), not at startup.
- English month-name dates are untouched. Over 3,066 strings (every English `Intl` format and ~120 UI strings), nothing main treats as volatile turned stable.
- No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump: the change decides what a new recording keeps, and masks dates in alert text on both sides of the check.

| `Intl` format, 66 locales | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dateStyle: 'short'` | 4 | 63 |
| `dateStyle: 'medium'` | 13 | 65 |
| `dateStyle: 'long'` | 11 | 65 |
| `dateStyle: 'full'` | 11 | 65 |
| `timeStyle: 'short'` | 52 | 62 |

Known limits:

- A month name without a year outside English (`8 września`) still reads as stable: it has the shape of `3 records`.
- Missed: a dotted time (`17.42`), Filipino month-first dates, Nepali and Bulgarian short dates, countdowns and ages outside English (`3 дня назад`).
- Read as dates: `Size 10/12/14`, `Section 12.3.2026`, `Version 12.10.11`, and a total that reads as a year beside a month abbreviation (`25 des 2000 résultats`). Each is skipped only while another stable anchor exists.
- A recording made before this release that kept a date hands off once and re-records; under `--strict-cache`, re-record it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch testbed project: "Place order" sets a status and shows the order date, `Intl.DateTimeFormat(LOCALE, { dateStyle })` of a server-side day. Built-in agent (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`): a run on 2026-09-08 records the step, then `e2e run --strict-cache` on 2026-09-09. Same commands on main (ff3bf391) and this branch:

| Date on screen | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `٨ سبتمبر ٢٠٢٦` (ar-EG, long) | `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch): missing node "٨ سبتمبر ٢٠٢٦" | replayed in 178 ms, no model call |
| `9/8/26` (en-US, short) | `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch): missing node "9/8/26" | replayed in 173 ms, no model call |
| `September 8, 2026` (en-US, long) | replayed in 175 ms | replayed in 176 ms |

```text
main
   × places an order > agent.act "place an order" 14.29s failed
REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays (end-mismatch), and cache.strict hands no step to the agent; re-record it with a read-write run without --strict-cache and commit the changed entry under .e2e/cache
  detail: every recorded action ran, but the recorded end state did not show on /: missing node "٨ سبتمبر ٢٠٢٦"

this branch
   ✓ places an order > agent.act "place an order" 178ms
      Cache  1 replayed
```

- `tests/integration/volatile-date-cache.test.ts` records the same flow and replays it the next day with `--strict-cache`: it fails on main (exit 2) and passes here, for an Arabic long, an Arabic numeric, and an English numeric date.
- Web benchmark `tests-agent` with `CI=1 --strict-cache`: `26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed` on main and on this branch, the same outcome for all 32 agent steps, no recording rewritten.

title: Hosted sessions: honor action replay cache with stable logical identity
body:
## Problem

In public **`e2e@0.21.2`**, an external runner using `openHost()` / `host.openSession()` can supply the public `cache` configuration, but hosted agent acts do not participate in action replay caching. A file cache directory or custom `CacheStore` cannot enable it on this execution path.

We need persistent replay for the same logical test across fresh hosted sessions, while retaining the existing external runner, borrowed engine, and SDK built-in agent. This is separate from provider prompt caching.

## Source evidence

Checked the published package and the [0.21.2 release commit](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f):

- [`standalone-attempt.ts:171–175`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f/packages/e2e/src/run/standalone-attempt.ts#L171-L175) calls `createFixtures` without a cache context. Hosted close also does not settle staged action recordings.
- [`fixtures.ts:207`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f/packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts#L207) only forwards cache when `environment.cache` was supplied.
- [`act.ts:246–250`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f/packages/e2e/src/agent/act.ts#L246-L250) creates `StepTraceSession` only when `runtime.cache` exists. Resolving cache configuration is not sufficient.
- The ordinary suite executor does create/pass `AgentCacheContext` and call `settleStagedTraces`; its engine launch/settle methods reused by hosted sessions do not execute that suite-body cache plumbing.

There is a second requirement once cache is connected: hosted [`testId` is `host:<attemptId>`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f/packages/e2e/src/run/standalone-attempt.ts#L269-L275), with a fresh attempt UUID. [`buildTraceCacheKey` includes `testId`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f/packages/e2e/src/cache/identity.ts#L176-L180). Public `OpenSessionOptions` has no stable logical test/cache identity input; reusing `name` or `projectId` does not replace this field.

**Verification limit:** this is a source-path audit, not a measured cold/warm device reproduction. The current hosted path constructs no trace-cache lookup at all; the UUID is an additional cross-session identity gap, not an observed sequence of cache misses.

## Was this removed?

It appears to be missing hosted integration rather than a recent removal. In the [original hosted-session introduction](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/980), merged as `3a53fbd8e5fb8ed345dd00331b3a5b5b90bac1d3`, [`createFixtures` already omitted cache](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/3a53fbd8e5fb8ed345dd00331b3a5b5b90bac1d3/packages/e2e/src/run/standalone-attempt.ts#L171-L177), and hosted identity was already per attempt. Suite-runner replay caching remains present in 0.21.2. I did not find evidence establishing an intentional removal decision for hosted caching.

Related: #1075 discusses stable external test identity, but does not currently provide hosted replay-cache wiring or an agreed identity API.

## Requested supported behavior

Could the public hosted API:

1. Honor the existing cache configuration by creating/forwarding the SDK-owned action-cache context and awaiting confirmed-recording settlement at close.
2. Provide a documented stable logical cache identity scoped with project/target, distinct from unique attempt IDs and artifact directories. The precise public API is for maintainers to choose.

Acceptance: two separate hosts/sessions for the same logical test can record an act confirmed by a subsequent SDK assertion, then actually replay that act on the second session; assertions remain live. Different logical tests must not collide, attempt/artifact identities remain unique, and cache-off/cleanup/interruption behavior remains correct.

The external runner would still own final pass/fail and any success-only remote publication. This does **not** request an external-outcome/retry framework, new executor, private cache API, custom key format, or migration to `e2e run`. If another supported public hosted integration is intended, please point us to it.

title: fix(agent): report model refusals as typed MODEL_REFUSED instead of MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED
body: Fixes #945. ## What A model refusal (finish reason `content-filter`) on any adapter model call — `agent.extract` included — is now reported as the typed, non-retryable `MODEL_REFUSED` code (category `configuration`, exit 2) instead of `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: No output generated.` (exit 3). The message names the step, the model, and the raw finish reason, so the report reads as a refusal instead of a provider outage, and retry policies no longer burn a second call on a prompt that is refused by construction. Also fixed on the text path (no schema), where a refusal previously surfaced as `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` — which `invocation.ask` would spend a repair round retrying. Drive-by fix in the same seam: the SDK's no-output error was renamed in AI SDK v7 (`NoOutputGeneratedError`), so the old `NoObjectGeneratedError.isInstance` check in `translateModelError` never matched and empty non-refusal output fell through to `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. It now recognizes both names and maps back to `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` as originally intended. ## Changes - `packages/e2e/src/types.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/error.ts`: new `MODEL_REFUSED` code, `configuration` category — deliberately not `test`, so the runner's retry policy (which only retries `test`) never retries a refusal. - `packages/e2e/src/agent/model/sdk.ts`: `throwIfModelRefused` checks `result.finishReason` right after `generateText`, before parsing / touching `result.output` (whose getter throws the SDK's no-output error); both the structured and text branches covered. - `docs/reference/errors.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md`: documented (`node scripts/check-error-codes.ts` green). - `.changeset/model-refused-typed-error.md`: patch changeset. ## Verified - New `packages/e2e/tests/unit/model-refusal.test.ts` (3 tests) against a local stub provider returning `finish_reason: content_filter`: - pre-fix: structured path → `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` (`model provider failed: No output generated.` — the exact report from #945); text path → `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`. Both fail as expected. - post-fix: both → `MODEL_REFUSED` with step/model/reason in the message; `serializeError(...).retryable === false` and `isRetryEligible(...) === false`. - Full unit suite: 185 files / 2737 tests pass. `oxlint` clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from pre-existing `@e2e-dev/web` resolution errors in integration tests (package not installed in this env), `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts` green.

title: fix(agent): map the SDK's NoOutputGeneratedError to MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID
body: Split out of #1214 per review feedback: the no-output-error remap is its own change with its own test. When the model produces nothing to parse (an empty `length` finish, say), the AI SDK throws `NoOutputGeneratedError` from the `result.output` getter. The adapter's error translation did not recognize it, so it fell through to `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` — an infrastructure verdict for what is really a response that failed the closed grammar. This maps it to `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` instead: test category, run-retry eligible, and the invocation spends a repair round on it like any other malformed response. Notes: - `NoObjectGeneratedError` and `NoOutputGeneratedError` are distinct classes in AI SDK 7.0.107 (both exported); the former is thrown parsing text, the latter by the `result.output` getter. No rename involved. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/no-output-error.test.ts` scripts a `length` finish with empty text through the real adapter: it fails as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` without the fix and `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` with it.

title: feat(telemetry): sort executed tests by cache tier and count miss reasons
body:
The run event had no per-test cache view, so "what % of tests run without the model" could not be read off PostHog, and a cache miss could not be told apart (first recording vs retry vs stale replay).

- `tests_code_only`, `tests_replayed`, `tests_assisted`, `tests_live`: every executed test in exactly one tier, across its attempts. The four sum to `tests_executed`.
  - code-only: no agent step
  - replayed: every agent step self-finalized from the cache, no executor ran
  - assisted: the agent ran, cache carried at least part of a step
  - live: the agent ran every agent step, no cache help
- `agent_steps_uncached`: `agent.act` steps with no cache record (cache off, executor `cache: 'off'`), so replayed + partial + missed + uncached = act steps.
- `agent_miss_reasons`, `agent_handoff_reasons`: counts keyed by the runner's closed reason tokens (`no-entry`, `retry`, `wrong-context`, `gap`, `target-not-found`, ...), through `plainToken`.
- `model_calls_act|assert|extract|waitfor`: where the model spend goes. Only act can replay, so assert-heavy suites never become deterministic.
- `testSteps` (`packages/e2e/src/telemetry/events.ts`) now skips results with no attempt (unselected, never run, serial members whose attempts live on the group) and skipped serial members, matching `summary.executed`. Before, those would have landed in `tests_code_only`.

Dashboard [e2e CLI Analytics](https://eu.posthog.com/project/269593/dashboard/942107) already has tiles reading these: tests by cache tier, fully deterministic %, misses by reason, model calls by API.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Packed `e2e` + `@e2e-dev/web` into a scratch project with the web-benchmark agent suite and its committed cache, `E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1 e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts` (bad gateway key, so misses fail live):

```
Tests  7 failed | 27 passed (34)
Cache  26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed

{"tests_executed":34,"tests_code_only":1,"tests_replayed":26,"tests_assisted":2,"tests_live":5,
 "agent_steps_replayed":26,"agent_steps_partial":2,"agent_steps_missed":4,"agent_steps_uncached":0,
 "agent_miss_reasons":{"gap":2,"no-entry":2},"agent_handoff_reasons":{"gap":2},"model_calls_assert":1}
```

- Same project with two file positionals, so 26 tests unselected:

```
{"tests_discovered":34,"tests_selected":8,"tests_executed":8,"tests_code_only":1,"tests_replayed":7,"tests_assisted":0,"tests_live":0}
```

- The new unit test (unselected result, serial member, skipped member) fails on the pre-fix `testSteps` with `expected 10 to be 7`.

body: ## What and why The MAUI example split out of #1178, now that `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.3 is out with the Android test id match it needs. - `examples/with-maui`: the greeter demo in .NET MAUI 10, tested on Android and iOS. They live in `e2e/` next to the .NET project and pin `e2e` `^0.21.2` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` `^0.12.3`. - The csproj leaves `e2e/` out of its default globs, so `node_modules` doesn't show up as 7,000 project items in Rider or Visual Studio. It adds the iOS target only off Linux, the way the MAUI template does, and the README says to install `maui-android` there. I haven't tried a Linux build. - The README lists three things I hit while building it. `AutomationId` reads as `:id/` on Android. `SemanticProperties.Description` on an `Entry` makes Android report a filled field as `Name, Ada`, so the example sets it on iOS only. title: feat(e2e): keep artifact screenshots after a secret fill
body: After a test fills a secret, the runner used to stop taking any screenshot for the rest of the attempt. Screenshots are the project's own artifacts, on disk and in CI, so this PR keeps them. Pixels sent to a model stay withheld. - `app.screenshot()`, `toHaveScreenshot()`, `agent.assert` evidence, and failure screenshots now work after a fill. Before, they failed with `POLICY_DENIED` or were dropped. - Model-facing pixels don't change: vision, the pixel tools, `ctx.pixelsTainted`, and MCP `screenshot` still answer `PIXEL_TAINTED` after a fill, because model input leaves the machine. - `SecretExposure.withholdsPixels` is renamed to `withholdsModelPixels` (`packages/e2e/src/run/secrecy.ts`), so every remaining consumer reads as model-facing. - `toHaveScreenshot()` keeps its other guard: it still refuses when the engine can't prove every secure field on screen is masked. - Trade-off: an artifact screenshot masks secure fields only. A secret the app shows anywhere else is in the image, the same as with video, which was never gated. `docs/reference/security.mdx` says so in a `Warning`. ```mermaid flowchart LR F[secret fill] --> T{pixel consumer} T -- model: vision, pixel tools, MCP --> W[withheld, PIXEL_TAINTED] T -- artifact: app.screenshot, toHaveScreenshot, evidence --> K[kept, secure fields masked] ``` The stacked PR adds `agent.act({ onAction })`. A per-action screenshot hook is useless if it stops working at sign-in. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, live model (`e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts`): an `agent.act` sign-in that fills `admin.password` through `typeSecret`, `app.screenshot()` after each action, then `agent.assert`. Every screenshot was taken. The password field is masked, and `grep -r admin-pass .e2e/` finds nothing. | after the secret fill | after Sign in | | --- | --- | | ![after fill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9f9f8c9-5f52-4f51-8d46-c166224b1d5c) | ![after sign in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b4ef306-154d-45e3-9058-4ce2b9c3ad15) |

title: feat(e2e): add onAction hook to agent.act
body: Adds `onAction` to `agent.act`: a hook that runs after each action the step completes, once the screen settles. Users asked for a screenshot after every agent action. Instead of a `screenshot: true` flag, this ships one general primitive: the screenshot is one line of user code, and the next request (logging, a live UI, metrics) needs no new API. ```ts await agent.act('open settings and turn on dark mode', { onAction: ({ index, action, source, summary }) => app.screenshot(`${index} ${action}`), }); ``` - It fires from the one point where every action commits, `ActionDispatcher.runActionNow` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts`), so model and cache-replayed actions both reach it (`source: 'model' | 'replay'`). Mutating project tools reach it as `tool:`. - Before the hook runs, the screen settles the way the action's policy asks (`SETTLE_AFTER[kind].look`), so a frame shows the effect and not the screen mid-transition. That capture is skipped when no hook is set. - A throw from the hook, or from that settle, hard-stops the step as an `ActionHookError`. It never reaches the executor as a failed action to retry (which would double-tap a committed action) or the replay as a divergence. - An `ActionHookError` concludes the cache step as `no-verdict`, so a broken hook neither saves nor evicts a recording. - A verifying step that runs inside another step (an `expect` in the hook) now proves only the steps before that one (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`). Before, it would have confirmed the act's half-checked recording. - `StepAccounting.checkpoint` now throws once the step has hard-stopped, so a batched action queued behind a failed hook doesn't run. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[executor or replay] --> D[runActionNow] D --> E[engine action] E --> R[record trace] R --> H{onAction set?} H -- no --> N[next action] H -- yes --> S[settle] --> U[hook] --> N U -- throws --> X[ActionHookError: step fails, recording untouched] ``` Stacked on #1218, which keeps artifact screenshots after a secret fill. Without it, the example above fails on every sign-in act. Not in this PR: `ActionEvent.action` is a `string`, not a typed union, so the grammar stays out of the public API for now. `index` is the action-budget slot, so a failed attempt skips a number. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, live model, the real CLI (`e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts`): `agent.act('sign in ...', { onAction })` with `app.screenshot()` in the hook. The first run gave 3 model calls and 3 frames tagged `model`. The cached rerun gave 0 model calls and the same 3 frames tagged `replay`. ```text ✓ ... > agent.act "sign in with the given username and password" 8.97s · 4 model calls ✓ ... > agent.act "sign in with the given username and password" 606ms 001-1-replay-type__type__admin__into_textbox__Username_.png 002-2-replay-typeSecret__fill_secret__admin.password__into_textbox__.png 003-3-replay-tap__tap_button__Sign_in_.png ``` | after the secret fill | after Sign in (settled) | | --- | --- | | ![after fill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85bab44e-2771-4c8b-997d-c0da416afa73) | ![after sign in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4f82e8c-3352-498b-8d1b-4aac9945efbd) |

title: feat(hosted): honor action replay cache in standalone attempts
body: `openStandaloneAttempt` now participates in action replay caching: - Builds `createAgentCacheContext` with `testId: session:`, `projectId`, and `targetIdentity(target)`, mirroring the suite executor in `run/execute.ts`. - Passes the context into `createFixtures`, which already forwards it to `agentRuntime.cache`. - Calls `flushStagedTraces` at close with `lastVerifiedStepIndex: steps.lastVerifiedStepIndex` and `implicatesUnconfirmed: true` — a standalone attempt always closes as passed, so anything a later assertion verified is confirmed. The stable logical identity API discussed in the issue (attempt UUID vs. logical test id) is intentionally **not** changed here — that's stage 2 and is for maintainers to choose. ## Verified - `pnpm build` — green across all 7 packages. - `tests/unit/standalone-cache.test.ts` — new, 5/5 passing. Asserts: context is built when cache is on, `undefined` when off; two sessions sharing `testId` claim identical keys; different targets never collide; `flushStagedTraces` writes confirmed traces and evicts unconfirmed ones. - `tests/unit/trace-cache-config.test.ts` — 18/18 still passing, no regression in the cache system. Pre-existing Windows-only failures in `oauth/store`, `source-location`, `managed-process`, `cli-init`, and the engine integration suites are unchanged by this diff (verified against clean `main`).

title: docs(mobile): clarify recording recovery limits
body:

## Scope

title: test(authoring): evaluate lower-test context in E2E authoring
body:
## Why

- Measure whether inspecting lower-level tests improves E2E authoring before changing production guidance.
- The forty-run pilot reached its provisional detection ceiling. Six connected product tickets check whether a harder baseline leaves useful headroom.

## What changed

- Add two regressions per ticket, correct-only budget calibration, immutable first attempts, and separate human attribution.
- Publish the complete twelve-session baseline capture, including every unusable execution. The result remains `unresolved-operational-feasibility`.
- Fix worker retirement to use the configured disposal grace. Isolate the failed-write and synthetic timeout controls from unrelated setup operations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Freeze and verify the bank] --> B[Six correct-only calibration authors]
  B --> C{All six usable?}
  C -->|No| D[Retain failures and stop admission]
  C -->|Yes| E[Seal common budget]
  E --> F[Twelve baseline authors and 72 fixed cells]
  F --> G[Validate executions and human attribution]
```

## Scope

- Keep this PR draft and production authoring guidance unchanged. No sixty-run comparison ran or is authorized by these results.
- All twelve authors finished. Two correct-app repeats are unusable, and twenty member attributions await human judgment. All forty-eight changed-app repeats failed, which supplies no passing candidate for qualifying headroom but does not establish intended detection.
- Raw captures and the external operator remain private. Public aggregates do not independently reproduce the live capture.
- Maintainer review of the study scope and corpus is the next decision before another cohort. Human labels cannot repair an unusable execution.

## Blast radius

- The study is a private repository app. The scheduler correction also affects ordinary worker retirement and final disposal. It reuses the configured grace and changes no public signature.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Copied built CLI and real Chromium. `node apps/test-authoring/connected-cli.ts verify-bank --experiment BANK` verified 36 lower launches and 108 browser controls. Fresh independent review accepted the exact bank and native MCP admission before calibration.
- Six `validate-calibration` calls passed both correct-app repeats for all six exact exports. `seal-baseline` froze 46 completed responses, 2,100,000 full reported tokens, and 720 authoring seconds. All twelve baseline first attempts completed within those limits.
- Twelve `grade` calls retained all 72 predefined execution cells. `node apps/test-authoring/connected-cli.ts summarize --experiment BANK` retained ordered gate 2, `unresolved-operational-feasibility`. The final summary retains two unusable slots and ten pending-human slots. No failed cell was retried or repaired.
- The [complete baseline result](https://github.com/knowbody/e2e/blob/eval/test-authoring-context/apps/test-authoring/results/connected-baseline-2026-10-19.md) records raw outcomes, validity failures, calibration sources, and limits. Earlier pilots remain separate. No inspection-benefit conclusion follows.
- Earlier built-CLI disposal verification remains recorded in the [first connected report](https://github.com/knowbody/e2e/blob/eval/test-authoring-context/apps/test-authoring/results/connected-calibration-2026-10-18.md).

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| A fixed ten-second retirement timer kills the worker before its configured thirty-second engine cleanup budget ends. | A 12.34-second disposal pause completes without cleanup error or remaining process. A pause beyond the engine budget produces `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT`, cleanup phase, and CLI exit 3. |

title: fix(cache): find a test-id control after the text of its row changes
body: ## What and why - A recorded target's `within` is the first text of its row. On a feed that text is a post title, so a control with a stable test id fails `target-not-found` once the row's content changes. - When the row-scoped lookup finds nothing, `relocateDescriptor` now matches the strict fields (test id, role, name) across the whole screen and accepts exactly one match (`identifiedOutsideContainer` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/relocate.ts`). - The semantic tier stays scoped to the row, so a churned test id never lands on another row's control of the same name. - The new path runs only where replay used to fail, so replays that pass on main pick the same node. Recording is unchanged and `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` stays `conservative/6`. - #805 replaces this lookup with a fallback ladder that keeps `within` on every rung. If that lands first, this belongs as a rung there instead; happy to rebase onto it or close this in its favour. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/relocate-within.test.ts` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `expected { kind: 'failed', … } to deeply equal { kind: 'found', id: 'b0' }` | 7/7 pass | - Hit on an Android Compose app (`testTagsAsResourceId`) replaying against live content, where taps inside feed rows were keyed by the row's post title.

title: Replay "the first row" of a list whose length changes between runs
body:
### Problem

An agent step like `agent.act('open the first post in the "Your inbox" list')` taps a row that shares its test id with every other row. Recorded on Android with `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.2 and e2e 0.21.1, the target is:

```json
{ "role": "group", "testId": "inbox-item", "selector": "id=inbox-item", "within": "<title of the first post>" }
```

Each row sits in its own wrapper, so `containerKey` keys it by the row's own title and `describePosition` counts one match inside it, so no `position` is recorded. The recording means "the row titled X", while the instruction meant "the first row". Once a new post tops the inbox, the step hands off as `target-not-found`. Without `within` it would fare no better: the test id matches every row, and a recorded `position` holds only while the row count stays the same. Against a live backend the top of the inbox changes often, so the step keeps going back to the model. "Reply to the last message" in a thread has the same shape.

That fail-closed behaviour is deliberate, and I agree with it as the default. A recording can't tell "the first row" from "the row that happened to be first", and #637 explains why a lone survivor of a recorded set is ambiguous. What's missing is a way for the test author to say the step means a position.

For comparison, Maestro makes position part of the selector: `index: 0` takes the first match in y-then-x order, a negative index counts from the end, and the match count is never checked. Trailblaze's index selector is also a plain position at replay.

### Proposed API

```ts
await agent.act('open the first post in the feed', { position: 'first' });
await agent.act('reply to the last message', { position: 'last' });
```

The option is recorded with the entry, and the target is recorded without `within`. On replay it resolves to the first (or last) node carrying that test id, in document order, whatever their count. Without the option, nothing changes. A config key for the whole suite would also work, if you'd rather not widen `act`.

If this would fit better as a rung in #805, that works for us too.

### Which surface

public types (SDK), report or cache format

title: fix(agent): fill params into agent step labels
body: `agent.act('add a todo named {title}', { params: { title: 'Buy milk' } })` showed `add a todo named {title}` in the terminal, the report, and trace pages. It now shows `add a todo named Buy milk`. - `actLabel` fills each `{name}` that names a top-level param: a string as itself, other JSON as JSON (`packages/e2e/src/agent/act-label.ts`). `{{name}}`, names no param has, and braces inside a `` marker stay as written. - A param that is or holds a `Secret` keeps `{name}`. A plain-string param equal to a secret's value still redacts to ``. - Later steps' models read the step label as their list of prior steps. So the label is display only. The step keeps the instruction as written in a new optional `StepRecord.instruction`, and the ledger reads `instruction ?? label` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/ledger.ts:43`). Model prompts, custom executors, and the replay cache key are unchanged, and `unique()` values stay out of later prompts. - Wire: report-v1 gets an optional `step.instruction` (max 8192), set only when it differs from the label. The schema, both fixtures, and `report/build.ts` change together. - `SecretLedger.redactBound` caps the label and the instruction at 8192 chars without cutting a `` marker in half. - `scripts/bench-ab` signs a step by `instruction ?? label`. Otherwise every test with a `unique()` param would read as unstable. ```mermaid flowchart LR I["instruction + params"] --> L["actLabel: fill, redact, bound"] L --> D["label: terminal, report, trace"] I --> R["redactSpec"] R --> M["executor / model prompt"] R --> C["cache key"] R --> S["step.instruction"] S --> P["prior-step ledger"] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI. A custom executor logs `ctx.step.instruction`, and the test runs: ```ts await agent.act('add a todo named {title}', { params: { title: 'Buy milk' } }); await agent.act('sign in as {user} with {password}', { params: { user: 'admin', password: credentials.user('admin').password }, }); ``` | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | terminal | `agent.act "add a todo named {title}"` | `agent.act "add a todo named Buy milk"` | | terminal | `agent.act "sign in as {user} with {password}"` | `agent.act "sign in as admin with {password}"` | | executor got | `"add a todo named {title}"` | `"add a todo named {title}"` | | report.json `instruction` | absent | `"add a todo named {title}"` | ```text executor got "add a todo named {title}" ✓ fills params into step labels > agent.act "add a todo named Buy milk" 1ms executor got "sign in as {user} with {password}" ✓ fills params into step labels > agent.act "sign in as admin with {password}" 0ms ``` - No file under `.e2e/` contains the `admin` password. - web-benchmark `tests-agent/` replaying its committed recordings: 33 passed, 26 replayed. The `unique()` scenario reads `agent.act "add a new address labelled Cabin mve0d9t1 at 7 Pine Way, Bend"` (main prints `{label} at {line}`) and still replays from cache.

title: feat(mobile): configure iOS simulator screenshot density
