These are scripted-client tests, not native device evidence. ## Checklist - [x] Patch changeset added for `@e2e-dev/mobile`. - [x] Docs and consumer skill updated; plugin copies regenerated. - [x] Public declaration reviewed and compile-time option assertions added. - [x] No breaking change, wire-format change or shared engine-contract change.

title: Project tools: read a node's computed style through ToolContext
body:
A read-only project tool can observe the redacted tree through `ToolContext` (rect, text, value, states, a few attributes), but it cannot read a rendered property of a listed node such as `color`, `font-weight`, `visibility` or `opacity`. A check like "the error text is red" therefore needs a screenshot judgement instead of a measured value.

**Proposal:** `ToolContext.read(node, { style: ['color', ...] })`, returning `getComputedStyle` values for an allow-listed set of properties, redacted like the tree, read-only and available to tools with `mutates: false` only.

Versions: e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2.

title: Feature request: a clock option for web targets (web({ clock }))
body:
Playwright's `page.clock.install({ time })` has no e2e equivalent yet (`docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` lists `clock` as "none yet"). Verifying date-dependent behaviour (a default date, "today", relative times) needs the browser on a fixed instant that then runs at real speed, in every document and frame of a session, before the page's scripts run, including `Intl` "now" and `Temporal.Now`.

Today we use `web({ initScripts })` with our own shim. It works, but it duplicates what Playwright's clock already does.

**Proposal:** `web({ clock: { time: string | number, mode?: 'running' | 'paused' } })`, mapped to `context.clock.install` on every context e2e creates.

Versions: e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2.

title: ci(docs): run the docs gate when the example checker's helpers change
body: ## What and why `.github/filters.yml` decides which suites a pull request runs. The `docs` block lists the four checker scripts as `scripts/check-docs-*.ts`, and two modules those checkers import fall outside that pattern, so a change to either one leaves the filter output false and the `build` job in `.github/workflows/docs.yml:38` is skipped. `scripts/check-docs-examples.ts:23` imports `./docs-examples.ts` for the example list, and `scripts/docs-examples.ts:17` takes `REPO_ROOT` from `./public-packages.ts`. Neither path matches `scripts/check-docs-*.ts`, `docs/**`, `skills/e2e/**`, or any other entry in the block, and the `check` script in `docs/package.json` is what runs them. Nothing reports the skip. A skipped job passes the required `docs gate` on purpose (`.github/workflows/docs.yml:58`, `needs: [changes, build]`, `if: always()`), `docs.yml` runs on pull requests, merge queue entries, and manual dispatch only, with no `push` trigger, and `spec.yml` runs its own steps one by one instead of the root `pnpm check` that does include `docs:check`. So the check that consumes those modules never runs, neither on the pull request nor on `main` afterwards. The pattern was correct when it was written. PR #931 wrote the docs block for the four `check-docs-*.ts` checkers. PR #1017 later moved the example list into `docs-examples.ts`, which reads the repository root from the older `public-packages.ts`, and the block was never extended. `AGENTS.md` asks for the opposite ("A new build input or benchmark dependency goes into `filters.yml` in the same change"), and PR #886 is this same fix for the `mobile` block, where `packages/github/**` was missing. What the two modules do, so the stakes are concrete. `docs-examples.ts` is what turns an example file that no docs page shows into a failure instead of an unchecked file, and `public-packages.ts` is where that walk gets the repository root. A regression in either one reads as a green docs gate. ## What changed Two entries and a comment in the `docs` block: ```yaml docs: - 'docs/**' - 'skills/e2e/**' # The docs check and the modules it imports: `check-docs-examples.ts` reads # the example list from `docs-examples.ts`, which takes the repository root # from `public-packages.ts`. - 'scripts/check-docs-*.ts' - 'scripts/docs-examples.ts' - 'scripts/public-packages.ts' ``` What each path does to the docs suite: | change | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `scripts/docs-examples.ts` | skipped | runs | | `scripts/public-packages.ts` | skipped | runs | | `scripts/check-docs-examples.ts` | runs, through `check-docs-*.ts` | runs | | `docs/**` and `skills/e2e/**` | runs | runs | | `packages/e2e/src/**` | skipped | skipped | `public-packages.ts` is in the block because the docs check reaches it through `docs-examples.ts`. Four other gates read it too (`check-error-codes`, `check-peer-ranges`, `check-install-scripts`, `check-changeset-bumps`), and all of them run in the unfiltered `spec.yml`, so their coverage does not depend on this block. CI only. No changeset, and nothing changes for anyone consuming the published packages. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Matched both versions of the block against the four script paths with Node 24's glob matcher (`node:path.matchesGlob`). On `main` both helper modules report no match, which is the skip; here both match, and the four checkers keep matching through the existing `check-docs-*.ts` pattern. `picomatch`, the matcher `dorny/paths-filter` itself uses, is not installed in this checkout, and the change only adds positives to a block that carries no negatives. - Re-parsed the file after the edit with a YAML parser. The top-level keys `runner`, `web`, `mobile`, and `docs` are intact, and the `*runner` anchor still merges into the `web` and `mobile` blocks. - Ran the checkers the docs suite runs, at this revision: ```text check-docs-examples exit 0 docs examples: 19 files shown verbatim in docs/reference/runner.mdx, docs/integrations/limrun.mdx, ... check-docs-package-managers exit 0 docs package managers: every command block in 60 pages offers npm, pnpm, bun check-docs-logos exit 0 docs logos: 15 vendor pages have a sidebar icon and card logos check-docs-anchors did not run: @sindresorhus/slugify (root package.json:51) is missing from this checkout ``` - This PR edits `filters.yml`, which every list includes on purpose so a change to the gate runs what it gates, so its own CI run exercises the docs workflow. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: Run exits 0 with passed tests when requested video fails cleanup
body:
The CLI returned exit code 0 and reported all tests passed while both recorded Chromium attempts had failed video cleanup and no retained video artifacts.

Expected: clearly flag incomplete requested recordings or failed cleanup in the run result or exit status.

Observed attempt fields:

```json
{
  "status": "passed",
  "cleanup": "failed",
  "secondaryErrors": [{
    "category": "infrastructure",
    "code": "CLEANUP_TIMEOUT",
    "message": "stopping the video timed out",
    "phase": "cleanup"
  }]
}
```

Both artifact lists contained screenshots but no video. Command shape: `npx e2e run --video on --no-cache`.

Versions: e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2, Node 22.23.2, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, macOS.

Tried: inspected report secondary errors and artifact lists; reduced screencast size from 1440x1100 to 960x720, set quality 60, and increased cleanupTimeout from 30000 to 90000. A separate short recording then completed and retained video. Full-length recordings with those settings have not been rechecked.

Workaround: the local wrapper checks selected test results, cleanup status, secondary errors, and requested video artifacts instead of trusting exit code 0 alone.

An independent minimal reproduction is not available yet. This report includes framework behavior only, with no target application content, private URLs, or credentials.

title: feat(engine): engine protocol for out-of-process engines
body:
The engine contract now crosses a process boundary, and the harness drives every engine over it. An engine runs in a child process, on another machine, or on a device, written in any language, and the harness drives it exactly as it drives one built with `defineEngine`. `defineEngine` stays as the TypeScript way to write an engine: the harness serves it in process over `loopbackTransport`, so every suite crosses the wire and a contract change that cannot fails everywhere. ## The protocol The Language Server Protocol, applied to engines: - Same base layer: JSON-RPC 2.0 over `Content-Length` framing, requests and notifications both ways. - Same lifecycle: `initialize` / `initialized` / `shutdown` / `exit`. - A server announces a manifest the way a language server announces capabilities. Each engine member is one request (`engine/observe`, `keyboard/type`, `lifecycle/init`, ...) whose params are its arguments by name. Callbacks into the harness (`appLog`, `screen`, `resolveSecret`, `log`) are server-to-client messages. An `AbortSignal` crosses as an id plus `$/abort` with its reason, so a `TestTimeoutError` reaches the engine as it would in process. Errors keep their code, retryability, and category. ```mermaid flowchart LR H[harness: ResolvedTarget.engine
EngineClientHandle] -- JSON-RPC --> T{transport} T -- loopback --> S1[serveEngine: web, mobile, any defineEngine] T -- spawn stdio --> S2[server in a child process] T -- socket --> S3[server on another machine] T -- adb forward / xcodebuild --> S4[Java or Swift server on a device] ``` ```ts import { connectEngine, spawnTransport } from 'e2e/engine'; engine: connectEngine({ manifest: { name: 'kiosk', version: '1.0.0', spiVersion: 1, platform: 'kiosk', methods: ['engine/observe', 'engine/perform'], actions: ['tap'] }, transport: spawnTransport({ command: './kiosk-engine' }), resolveLocators: true, // the server only produces a tree session: { restart: (operation) => relaunchFromHost(operation) }, // answered on the client }); ``` - One table, `METHODS` in `packages/e2e/src/engine/protocol/protocol.ts`, maps each method to its member and arguments. `describeEngine`, the server, and the client are all read off it. - `connectEngine` builds an engine from the manifest and hands it to `defineEngine`, so a manifest is held to every rule an in-process engine is (`engine/perform` needs `actions`, `keyboard/type` needs `keyboard/press`, ...). The manifest is declared at config load; the server's own must match at `initialize`. Its JSON Schema ships as `schema/engine-manifest-v1.schema.json`. - The harness holds only protocol clients: `ResolvedTarget.engine` is an `EngineClientHandle`, produced by `protocolEngine` in `resolveTargets`. One engine always gets the same client, so handle identity checks (MCP `ENGINE_IN_USE`, hosted workers) still hold. - `fixtures`, `validateApp`, declared secrets, and `session` hooks run on the client. A `session` hook replaces the server's method, for what only the host can do (relaunching an app with `simctl`). - A server that cannot write the host's artifact directory returns a screenshot's bytes; the client writes the file. Transports receive the target's app, so a device transport can install `appPath`. - A server forgets a signal id once it aborts, or once the attempt it was first seen in ends. - Cleanup is bounded: a server that ignores the `finish`/`dispose` budget is closed by its transport anyway, and a late `endAttempt` retires only its own attempt. - A secret resolves once: the server derives redacted forms (basic-auth header) through `attempt/deriveSecret` while the value resolves. `ResolveSecretOptions.derived` may return a promise. - Errors keep their stack, Node error code, and causes across the wire. `serveEngine` always answers `lifecycle/startAttempt`/`endAttempt` (and `describeEngine` lists them), so signals are freed for engines without attempt hooks. - Worker connections queue: an MCP session closing while the next one opens calls `init` again before `dispose`, so calls go to the newest connection and `dispose` ends the oldest. - **Contract change:** `Engine.dispose` runs once `init` was called, even when it failed. A worker that never initialized opened no connection, so its engine gets no `dispose`. In the changeset. - Docs: one Engines section. Guides: `engines` (overview), `writing-an-engine`, `engine-servers` (new). Reference: `reference/engine` and `reference/engine-protocol` (new). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. Built packages, this branch: | Suite | Result | | --- | --- | | `e2e` package (unit + integration) | 4033 passed | | `@e2e-dev/web` / `@e2e-dev/mobile` | 635 / 447 passed | | testbed / testbed agent | 81 / 29 passed | | web-benchmark / web-benchmark agent | 91 / 33 passed | | mobile benchmark, both platforms | 112 passed; the 2 failures (iOS `setOrientation`, Android `setNetwork`) fail the same way on main on this machine | CI: all checks green, including e2e ios 55 passed, android 57 passed, ios agent 20 passed (1 flaky: the Gestures double-tap XCTest cannot always deliver, flaky on main too), android agent 20 passed. **Engines in other languages.** The experimental Java Android engine and Swift iOS engine (from the closed #1234 and #1236) were ported onto this protocol; the protocol needed one addition for them, client-side `session` hooks. Mobile benchmark selection, same device, agent-device 0.21.35, two runs each: | Engine | Android (emulator) | iOS (simulator) | | --- | --- | --- | | native over this protocol | 42/42, 140s / 136s | 41/41, 383s / 383s | | `mobile()` on agent-device | 42/42, 288s / 291s | 41/41, 420s | - iOS on one simulator with no other run on it. One more native run hit a web-view tap flake that also fails 2 in 8 runs without this PR; one more agent-device run took 444s with 2 of its own failures. - The iOS gap was swipes: XCTest waited for the list to stop coasting after each one (3.1s against agent-device's 0.9s). The native server now skips that wait around scroll swipes only; reads were already 6x faster (92ms against 575ms per `locate`). - The engines themselves stay on local branches; this PR ships only the protocol. - **Errors:** an engine throwing `EngineError`, `TestError`, a plain `Error`, a `TypeError`, a string, and a retryable `NODE_STALE` reports the same code, category, and message over the protocol as in process. - **Overhead:** `observe` costs its JSON round trip: 0.14 ms for 200 nodes, 1.6 ms for 2000, 10-28 ms for a 10000-node tree. Testbed wall time shows no consistent gap against main. - **A real child process:** unit tests cover a server in its own process, a crash mid-call that surfaces the server's stderr, and a hand-written JSON-RPC server with no `serveEngine`.

title: fix(run): exit 3 when a passed test's cleanup failed
body: #1231: a run whose tests all pass but whose required video cannot be finalized exits 0, with the loss visible only as an attempt-level `cleanup: "failed"` and a secondary error. The exit-code fold never looked at cleanup state. - `verdictExitCodes` (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`) now folds an attempt's failed cleanup into the exit code, for ordinary and serial-group attempts alike: the cleanup-phase secondary error's category, defaulting to `infrastructure` (exit 3) when the record carries none. - A forced cleanup (`cleanup: "forced"`) is untouched: the interrupt already sets 130. - Docs (`docs/reference/errors.mdx`) note the new rule under exit codes; changeset added. This covers both producers of `cleanup: "failed"`: `stopVideo` for a required recording (`packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`) and the session-close path, plus the standalone attempt's close. Best-effort recordings still fail quietly by design. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, at the unit level (a real video-finalization failure needs a browser; the regression test drives the exact record shape from the issue: `status: "passed"`, `cleanup: "failed"`, a `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT` cleanup-phase secondary error). - New `packages/e2e/tests/unit/runner-exit-codes.test.ts` (8 tests): all fail on main, all pass here. - Full unit suite: 185 files, 2750 tests, 0 failures. - `tsc --noEmit`: no new errors (only the pre-existing `@e2e-dev/web` resolution errors this env has on main); `oxlint`: clean. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | passed attempt + failed required-video cleanup folds to `0` | folds to `3` (infrastructure), run status `error` | Closes #1231

title: feat(android): experimental direct Android engine over the engine protocol
body: Stacked on #1232. An Android engine that is an engine protocol server written in Java, running on the device: the proof that an engine can live outside the runner's process and language, and a measure of what driving the device directly buys over agent-device. ## `@e2e-dev/android` (private, experimental) A Java engine server (`packages/android/server/java/`) that runs on the device as an instrumentation. It listens on an abstract socket and drives the device in process through `UiAutomation`: the tree comes from accessibility nodes, and touches and keys are injected events. There is no adb process, no daemon hop, and no XML dump per call. The host half (`src/transport.ts`) installs the APK, starts the instrumentation, and forwards a port. The APK builds in seconds with `javac`, `d8`, `aapt2`, and `apksigner`, no Gradle. Mobile benchmark, deterministic Android suite (`apps/mobile-benchmark/e2e.android.config.ts`, 42 tests, Pixel 7 API 36 emulator, one worker): | Suite | agent-device | direct | Speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | controls | 130.9s | 37.1s | 3.5x | | flows | 47.7s | 11.9s | 4.0x | | flows-lists | 110.1s | 72.8s | 1.5x | | login-form | 28.7s | 8.6s | 3.3x | | smoke | 3.8s | 1.4s | 2.6x | | **total** | **321s** | **131s** | **2.4x** | Engine calls on the same screens (`packages/android/bench/bench.ts`, nearest-rank p50, 5-20 samples per row, init one cold sample): | Operation | agent-device | direct | Speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | init (cold) | 1593 ms | 168 ms | 9.5x | | restart app | 887 ms | 156 ms | 5.7x | | observe | 15.3 ms | 2.0 ms | 7.6x | | tap | 132 ms | 30.4 ms | 4.3x | | fill (19 chars) | 1028 ms | 4.4 ms | 231x | | screenshot | 1459 ms | 65.7 ms | 22x | | swipe | 402 ms | 465 ms | 0.9x | | back, list up | 320 ms | 416 ms | 0.8x | | keyboard.type (10 chars) | 67 ms | 333 ms | 0.2x | It wins wherever agent-device spends an adb process or a daemon hop per call. It loses where the app sets the pace: - `swipe` waits for the list to come to rest. - `back` is held up by the pop animation, which blocks accessibility queries for about 450 ms. - `keyboard.type` sends one key event per character, and React Native re-renders on each. agent-device commits the whole string through its IME. `fill` sets text with `ACTION_SET_TEXT`; agent-device types it and reads it back. Both engines pass all 42, twice in a row. The direct engine declares the same device surface as the mobile engine: `press` takes Enter, Space, or one character, the keys a soft keyboard has, and refuses modifiers and other named keys with the mobile engine's reasons. Not there yet (in its README): one device per run, a `device` fixture with `back()` only, no video or state capture, no `selector` locators, no `launchArguments` or `permissions` (refused at config load). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Android:** the mobile benchmark selection above on both engines (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.android.config.ts`, with `BENCH_ENGINE=agent-device` for the baseline) and `node bench/bench.ts --rounds 20`. - **Review rounds:** after the cubic pass, the Android suite still runs 40/42 in 134s, and no server process is left on the device after the run. - Reviewed together with #1232: the fresh-context review and four cubic rounds covered both layers, and the Android findings (cancellation, masking, one session at a time, safe package names, device cleanup) are fixed here.

title: feat(ios): experimental Swift iOS engine over the engine protocol
body:
Stacked on #1234. A second language behind the engine protocol: an iOS engine written in Swift and hosted by an XCUITest bundle on the simulator. It measures what driving the app straight from XCUITest buys over `mobile()` on agent-device. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR H[harness: connectEngine] -- JSON-RPC over TCP 127.0.0.1 --> S[EngineServer.testServe
Swift, in the XCUITest runner] T[transport.ts] -- xcodebuild test-without-building --> S S -- XCUIApplication.snapshot, XCUICoordinate --> A[app under test] ``` - `packages/ios/server/E2EServer.xcodeproj` is a host app plus the `E2EServer` UI test bundle. It's hand-written, so there's no generator dependency, and it builds with `build:server`. - `EngineServer.testServe` listens on a localhost port, which the simulator shares with its Mac. It answers the protocol on the main thread, one connection at a time, and honors `$/abort` and abandonment as the Android server does. - `Device.swift` builds the tree from one XCUITest snapshot. It masks secure fields in pixels and screenshots, and acts with XCUITest gestures at the observed frames. - `transport.ts` installs `appPath` and starts the test with `xcodebuild test-without-building` on a free port. It waits for `E2E_SERVER_READY`, then connects with a plain socket. - `ios({ waitForIdle: false })` replaces XCUITest's private idle wait with a no-op, as WebDriverAgent can. It's opt-in and exists to measure what that wait costs. - `apps/mobile-benchmark/e2e.ios.config.ts` runs the deterministic selection on it. `BENCH_ENGINE=agent-device` runs the same selection on the default engine. ## Results iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5, mobile benchmark app, agent-device and the Swift engine both with the benchmark's `transition: 1500`, one worker. **Both pass all 41 suite tests, twice in a row.** | Suite | agent-device | Swift | Speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | controls | 164.5s | 138.5s | 1.2x | | flows | 69.5s | 57.3s | 1.2x | | flows-lists | 233.3s | 231.2s | 1.0x | | login-form | 47.1s | 28.1s | 1.7x | | smoke | 8.9s | 6.4s | 1.4x | | **total** | **523s** | **461s** | **1.13x** | Engine calls (p50): | Operation | agent-device | Swift | Swift, no idle wait | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | observe | 94.4 ms | 18.0 ms | 17.6 ms | | locate | 76.2 ms | 14.6 ms | 14.4 ms | | screenshot | 671 ms | 105 ms | 104 ms | | fill (19 chars) | 4852 ms | 1989 ms | 1538 ms | | keyboard.type (10 chars) | 1213 ms | 429 ms | 428 ms | | tap | 484 ms | 422 ms | 390 ms | | back, list up | 1055 ms | 1710 ms | 1034 ms | | swipe | 558 ms | 1433 ms | 1423 ms | | restart app | 710 ms | 1705 ms | 1714 ms | To match the mobile engine where the platform gives no signal, the Swift engine: - Reads React Native's checkbox and radio roles out of the accessibility value. - Taps a uniquely addressed node as an XCUITest element. That scrolls a covered one clear (the sticky footer) and reaches another process's sheet (Save Password). - Makes a control that arrived with the last action wait out the transition budget, because a presenting view drops touches while it reports its final frame. - Relaunches from the Mac with `simctl` for restart and `clearState`, and returns once the app answers. The gain is much smaller than on Android (2.4x there). agent-device already drives iOS through an XCTest runner, so going direct removes only the daemon and HTTP hop: - **Reads are 5-6x faster** (snapshot, locate, screenshot). - **Gestures are paced by XCUITest itself:** its idle wait, and over a second per `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:)` swipe. The next lever is XCTest's private event synthesis for gestures (what WebDriverAgent uses). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Suite:** `apps/mobile-benchmark`, `e2e.ios.config.ts` on simulator stab-1, 41/41 on two consecutive runs (461s, 462s), against `BENCH_ENGINE=agent-device` (41/41, 526s). - **Micro-bench:** `E2E_IOS_UDID= node bench/bench.ts --rounds 10`, run twice with matching numbers. - **Clean exit:** the runner's `xcodebuild` process ends on dispose, with no orphan left after a run.

title: report: note when an agent step's observation was truncated
body:
**Context**

While doing a fault-injection pass over the trace cache (the replay safety held up nicely — damaged entries always degraded to a miss or a hand-off, never to a false pass), I kept running into one dead end when trying to explain a blocked step on a large page: the report does not say whether the agent's semantic observation was truncated.

**What I observed** (snapshot `c994aa6f`)

- `MAX_OBSERVED_NODES = 3000` in `packages/web/src/observation-capture.ts`; when the walk is cut, `EngineSnapshot.truncated` is set and the model *is* told — `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:79` appends "The observation above is incomplete: nodes past its cut are on screen but not listed."
- `StepRecord` (`packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts:185`) already carries `visionDegraded` / `visionOnly` for vision-quality degradation, but nothing equivalent for a truncated semantic tree.
- The only trace of it afterwards is the step's transcript artifact, which is best-effort and absent when artifacts are off.

**Why it seems worth a field**

On a `blocked` step over a big page, `report.json` cannot distinguish "the control isn't there" from "the tree was cut before it". That is a debugging papercut rather than a correctness issue — the model itself is told, so nothing silently passes.

**Possible shape, if you think it's worth it**

An optional boolean threaded from the observation feed onto the step record (no observation content, no report-size change), e.g. `observationTruncated?: boolean`, possibly alongside the existing vision fields.

**If this was a deliberate omission, feel free to close it.** I can see the argument that the report is a receipt and debug evidence is opt-in (#1077) — I just couldn't find that decision written down anywhere, so I thought I'd ask rather than assume. Happy to be told it's by design.

Thanks — and the cache work is genuinely impressive; this is the only thing the pass turned up.

title: feat(cli): print an update notice when a newer e2e is on npm
body: After a command on a terminal, e2e now prints a notice when npm has a newer release, so people get reminded to upgrade. ``` Update available 0.20.0 → 0.21.2 Run pnpm add -D e2e@latest to update. Changelog: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/packages/e2e/CHANGELOG.md ``` - `packages/e2e/src/cli/update-check.ts`: at most one registry request a day, started in `preAction` while the command runs and awaited in `main`'s `finally` next to the telemetry flush (1.5s timeout). The answer is cached in `~/.config/e2e/update-check.json`, so every command between checks reminds with no request. A failed request still counts as a check, so offline machines don't pay for it on every run. - Install command: the nearest `packageManager` field or lockfile at or above the cwd decides the package manager, so `apps/web` in a pnpm monorepo gets `pnpm add`. At a pnpm workspace root it adds `-w`. - Silent in CI, when stderr isn't a TTY, from a source checkout, for `e2e mcp`, and under `E2E_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED`, `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, or `DO_NOT_TRACK`. A saved `e2e telemetry disable` does not stop it, same as `e2e feedback`. - `latestRelease`/`olderThan` moved from `cli/feedback.ts` to `internal/release.ts` so both share them. `package-manager.ts` gets `fieldManager`/`lockfileManager`, both extracted from `detectPackageManager`. - Docs: CLI reference, environment reference, and both security pages, which used to say only `e2e feedback` contacts npm. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: packed CLI (`pnpm pack`) installed into scratch projects in `/tmp`, with the installed version set to 0.20.0, run inside a pseudo-terminal (`script`) so stderr is a TTY. | Scenario | Result | | --- | --- | | First run, npm project | Real registry request, notice with `npm install --save-dev e2e@latest`, 0.5s total | | Second run | Read from cache with no request (0.15s) | | `apps/web` in a pnpm workspace (lockfile at root) | `pnpm add -D e2e@latest` | | pnpm workspace root | `pnpm add -D e2e@latest -w` | | Piped stderr, `CI=1`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `--version` | No notice |

title: feat(e2e): add screen.tree and screen.debug, print test output without list reporter
body: ## What and why - New `screen.tree()` reads the screen once and returns it as text. It uses the same lines and secret redaction as the trace's "Screen at failure". `screen.debug()` prints that text to the test output. Both work on every engine and are recorded as steps. - On a frame they throw `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and they are left off `Locator`. No engine can return a subtree yet: web located nodes have no children, and mobile ids change on every capture. - Fix: test `console.log` output only printed with the `list` reporter, so `--reporter json/junit/markdown/...` dropped it. Now it prints to its own stream. - Fix: with `--reporter json`, user output (config top level included) landed on stdout ahead of the report, which broke `| jq`. User output now goes to stderr, and the json reporter writes to the terminal directly (`packages/e2e/src/run/process-output.ts`). ```ts test('checkout', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/checkout'); await screen.debug(); const tree = await screen.tree(); }); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed web, scratch test with `console.log` + `screen.debug()`, config logging at top level: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `--reporter junit`: test output missing | `hello from the test` + tree printed | | `--reporter json \| jq`: parse error, `config top level` on stdout | stdout parses as the report, user output on stderr | ``` stdout | |web| tests-scratch/pr/debug.e2e.ts > debug hello from the test #root document "Playground" #n2 navigation "Main" #n3 link "Home" href="/" #n4 link "Todos" href="/todos" ``` - testbed login: the filled password renders as ``, plaintext absent; the trace lists `screen.debug` and `screen.tree` steps. - iOS simulator, mobile-benchmark: `screen.debug()` prints the app tree. Android not run.

title: feat(cli): add `npx e2e upgrade`
body:
Adds `e2e upgrade`, with `e2e update` as an alias. It moves a project's `e2e` to the latest release, a dist-tag, or one version, and every `@e2e-dev/*` package the project lists along with it. ```console $ npx e2e upgrade # latest $ npx e2e upgrade 0.21.0 # one version $ npx e2e upgrade nightly # a dist-tag $ npx e2e update --dry-run # the plan, nothing written ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[nearest package.json
that lists e2e] --> B[registry metadata
e2e + @e2e-dev/*] B --> C[e2e target
tag or version] C --> D[each sibling: same tag if its
peer ranges accept, else newest that does] D --> E[write specs into
package.json] E --> F[one manager install] F -- fails or Ctrl-C --> G[put back package.json
and changed lockfiles] ``` - **Siblings follow `e2e`.** A deprecated release is never picked, and a prerelease only when `e2e` gets one. An integration resolves after the engine it peers on, so `@e2e-dev/kernel` follows `@e2e-dev/web` down on a downgrade. Peer ranges are read by the new `packages/e2e/src/internal/semver.ts`, which covers the shapes the packages publish (`>=0.15.0 <1`, an exact prerelease pin) and node-semver's prerelease rule. - **One install.** The new specs go into `package.json`, each in its section, then one ` install` resolves them together. An add command per package meets the old `e2e` spec in npm's peer check (`ERESOLVE`) when packages sit in different sections. A named version or a prerelease is pinned exactly; a dist-tag keeps the old spec's `^` or `~`. pnpm gets `--no-frozen-lockfile` and Yarn `YARN_ENABLE_IMMUTABLE_INSTALLS=false`, so CI works. - **A failed or interrupted install** puts back `package.json` and every lockfile it changed, byte for byte (`bun.lockb` is binary). SIGINT and SIGTERM are held off `e2e` while the package manager runs, so Ctrl-C stops the install and the restore still runs. - **Edge cases:** a package listed in two sections is rewritten in both; the whole sibling plan's peer ranges are checked before anything is written; a Windows path spec (`..\\web`) counts as linked. - **Linked packages are left alone** (`workspace:`, `file:`, `catalog:`, a path, git). A linked `e2e` exits 2. - **Package manager detection** (`detectWorkspacePackageManager` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/package-manager.ts`): the package's own `packageManager` field or lockfile (or pnpm at a pnpm workspace root), else those of a workspace root above whose globs include it (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` in block or flow form, or `workspaces`). A lockfile above a project no workspace lists does not count; `examples/with-vite` otherwise resolved to this repository's pnpm. - **The update notice from #1238 now suggests `e2e upgrade`** for the package that lists `e2e`, through the same detection, instead of `e2e@latest` alone, which left the engine behind. It stays quiet after `e2e upgrade` itself. The skill says `npx e2e@latest upgrade`, since a skill from `npx skills add` can be newer than the project's e2e. `olderThan` orders versions through the new semver module. - **Telemetry:** one `e2e_upgrade_completed` event per run: the result, the target kind or a dist-tag e2e publishes, the `e2e` versions before and after, the package manager, the sibling names inside the `@e2e-dev` scope, and package counts (`docs/telemetry.mdx`). The security pages list the registry requests. - `e2e --help` lists commands without their aliases; `upgrade|update` widened the column and wrapped every summary. The summary says `(alias: update)`. Exit codes: 0 installed, already up to date, or `--dry-run`; 2 for a range, an unknown version or tag, no project, a linked `e2e`, no fitting sibling release, or a failed install; 3 when the registry does not answer; 130 on Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during the install. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. The built CLI against the live npm registry, in scratch projects and `examples/with-vite`. npm, packages split across sections with an exact pin beside `^`, the case where per-section add commands hit `ERESOLVE`: ```text $ e2e upgrade Upgrading with npm: e2e 0.15.0 → 0.21.2 @e2e-dev/web 0.12.0 → 0.15.2 @e2e-dev/github 0.3.3 → 0.4.2 package.json: "e2e": "0.21.2", "@e2e-dev/web": "~0.15.2", "@e2e-dev/github": "^0.4.2" $ npm install ... Upgraded: e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2, @e2e-dev/github 0.4.2 Release notes: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/releases/tag/e2e%400.21.2 ``` `package.json` kept its order and indentation; `npm ls` showed the new versions. Other runs: | Case | Result | | --- | --- | | `upgrade 0.15.0 --dry-run` on 0.21.2 | `e2e 0.21.2 → 0.15.0 (downgrade)`, `@e2e-dev/web → 0.12.0`, exact pins | | `upgrade nightly --dry-run` | every package to its `0.x.y-nightly-20261019081103` build | | pnpm workspace member, unindented `packages:` list, run under `npm_config_user_agent=npm` | `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile`, no stray `package-lock.json` in the member | | Yarn 4 (Plug'n'Play) with `CI=true` | lockfile updated to `e2e@npm:^0.21.2`; a second run printed `Already up to date` | | npm project whose `postinstall` exits 1 | `package.json and package-lock.json are back as before`, both byte-identical, `npm ci` passes | | fake `npm` that sleeps, SIGINT sent to the process group | exit 130, `package.json` byte-identical | | an unresolvable dependency beside `e2e` | exit 2, `package.json` back | | `upgrade ^0.20`, `upgrade 9.9.9`, `upgrade beta2`, `apps/testbed` (`workspace:*`), no project | exit 2, nothing written | | yarn 1 with `.agents/skills/e2e` | upgraded, then `refresh it with yarn e2e init` | Telemetry, from a copy of the build outside the checkout with `E2E_TELEMETRY_DEBUG=1`: ```text [telemetry] {"event":"e2e_upgrade_completed", ... "result":"dry-run","target":"version","from_version":"0.21.2","to_version":"0.20.0","prerelease":false,"manager":"npm","siblings":["kernel","web"],"packages_moved":0,"packages_linked":0, ...} [telemetry] {"event":"e2e_upgrade_completed", ... "result":"unknown-target","target":"other","from_version":"0.21.2","to_version":null, ...} ``` Two fresh-context review rounds ran before this PR, and cubic's 22 findings after it (21 fixed, 1 disproved in its thread); the pre-PR findings (the `ERESOLVE` above, exact pins turned into `^`, the notice after an upgrade, `^` eaten by cmd.exe, YAML list forms, Ctrl-C, lockfiles after a failed script, Yarn Berry in CI, Plug'n'Play) are fixed and covered by tests that fail without the fix. Not verified: bun (not installed here), Windows, and the update notice on a real terminal; its unit tests cover the command it prints. Found while verifying, not fixed here: `@e2e-dev/web` 0.11.2 declares `e2e >=0.15.0 <1` but imports `rejectUnknownOptions`, which `e2e` first exports in 0.16.0, so a fresh install of `examples/with-vite` on main fails with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`. `e2e upgrade` trusts published peer ranges; deprecating the affected `@e2e-dev/web` releases on npm would keep it from picking them.

title: fix(lint): report parsed JSON behind a satisfies expression
body: ## What and why `e2e/no-unchecked-json` exists because `JSON.parse` and `.json()` return `any`, so typing that result skips every check and a bad body surfaces later as a `TypeError` or a wrong value. The rule requires the result to land as `unknown` (or `Promise`) until a schema or a check narrows it, and it is enabled for `packages/*/src/**` at `.oxlintrc.json:39-43`. The rule already looks through the wrappers that do not change the value: `await`, `!`, optional chaining, and parentheses (`scripts/oxlint-plugin/no-unchecked-json.ts:3-13`). `satisfies` belongs in that list. It checks that the expression is assignable to a type, then returns the expression with its original type, so `const value = JSON.parse(text) satisfies User` still binds `any`. Assignability is not a runtime check, and `any` is assignable to everything, so the pattern reads like validation while doing none. There was no `TSSatisfiesExpression` listener and `unwrap()` did not step through the node, which left it as the one wrapper the rule could not see. `satisfies unknown` is not a way out either. It also leaves the binding as `any`, so the rule reports it too. What stays valid is a binding that is actually declared `unknown`, because downstream use is checked from there: ```ts const value: unknown = JSON.parse(text) satisfies User; // value is unknown, fine const other = JSON.parse(text) satisfies User; // value is any, reported ``` No file under `packages/*/src` uses the pattern today, so the change adds no cleanup. It closes the next shape that would otherwise pass the rule silently. ## What changed - `scripts/oxlint-plugin/no-unchecked-json.ts:3-12`: `unwrap()` steps through `TSSatisfiesExpression`, next to `AwaitExpression` and the parenthesized, non-null, and chain group. - Every listener funnels through `isJson()`, which calls `unwrap()`, so the declarator, assignment, return, arrow-body, and assertion paths all pick up the change without a new visitor. - `scripts/oxlint-plugin/no-unchecked-json.test.ts:14-15` adds the two valid `: unknown` shapes, and `:32-36` adds five invalid ones: a declarator, `satisfies unknown`, `(await response.json()) satisfies User`, an assignment to a typed `let`, and a return from a typed function. | shape | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `JSON.parse(t) as User` | reported | reported | | `const v: User = JSON.parse(t)` | reported | reported | | `JSON.parse(t) satisfies User` | no report | reported | | `JSON.parse(t) satisfies unknown` | no report | reported | | `(await r.json()) satisfies User` | no report | reported | | `let v: User; v = JSON.parse(t) satisfies User` | no report | reported | | `function f(): User { return JSON.parse(t) satisfies User }` | no report | reported | | `const v: unknown = JSON.parse(t) satisfies User` | no report | no report | | `function f(): unknown { return JSON.parse(t) satisfies User }` | no report | no report | Tooling only. No changeset, and nothing changes for anyone consuming the published packages. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Ran the rule through the real plugin host, the `oxlint` 1.83.0 binary with `@oxlint/plugins` 1.83.0, on a scratch file under `packages/e2e/src`, which is the scope `.oxlintrc.json:39` configures. Before the change it reported 2 errors, the `as` and `: User =` controls. After it reported 7, covering the five new shapes, while the two `: unknown` forms stayed clean. The scratch file is removed. ```text before: 2 no-unchecked-json reports (as User, const v: User =) after: 7 no-unchecked-json reports (the same 2 plus 5 satisfies shapes) ``` - The rule's own `RuleTester` suite did not run on this machine. oxlint's `RuleTester` allocates one 6 GiB buffer for raw transfer, and this machine has about 5 GB free, so every case fails with `Array buffer allocation failed`, including cases this change does not touch. CI runs the file through `pnpm test:scripts` (`node --test "scripts/**/*.test.ts"`). `@oxlint/plugins` is declared at `package.json:50` but was missing from this checkout; unpacking that exact version is what let the local binary load the plugin. - `oxlint packages apps scripts docs`: `0 warnings and 0 errors` on 1091 files. - `tsc -p scripts` reports no error in either changed file. It exits 1 in this checkout on two missing dev dependencies, `@changesets/parse` and `@sindresorhus/slugify`, neither of which this change touches. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: e2e run --step: hold each step until a key is pressed
body:
### Problem

When a test fails midway, the only ways to watch it are `--headed`, which runs at full speed, and sprinkling sleeps through the test. There is no way to run one step, look at the app, then run the next. Playwright's `--debug` covers this; e2e has no equivalent, and `e2e run --debug` here means phase timings.

Proposal: `e2e run --step` runs the first step, which opens the app, then holds every later step until a key is pressed in the terminal. The keys and prompt are under Proposed API. Setup tests and retries run without stopping, and a key pressed within 150 ms of a prompt appearing is ignored.

A first attempt (#1155 ) also added a browser-side inspector. It was closed; this issue keeps only `--step`.

**Shape**
- One seam in core: `RunOptions.beforeStep`. No public API change, no engine contract change, no peer-range bump.
- The CLI owns the prompt in `src/cli/step/`, reading raw-mode keys the way `watch` does. Core never touches stdin. Ctrl-C goes through `SignalLadder.escalate()`.
- A worker holds the step and asks the runner over the existing worker channel (`step-gate`, answered by `step-go`), since only the runner owns the terminal.
- `--step` forces one worker, and holds are serialized in call order, so steps started together in one test still give one prompt at a time.
- A held call is recorded only once it is let go, so `startedAt` and `durationMs` never include the wait.

**Timeouts.** Only held time is excluded. The test deadline, the worker watchdog and `maxDuration` pause while a step is held and resume with what they had left. A test that hangs after a hold still times out, and the run still ends at `maxDuration`. Steps in `afterEach` hooks and fixture teardowns run without a prompt, since their cleanup budget is fixed.

**Refused with exit 2:** CI, no TTY, `--watch`, the `json` reporter (flag or config), `--workers` above 1.

**Failures.** If the hook throws, the run aborts with that error, not "interrupted". Any interrupt resolves a held step as false.

**Questions**
1. Is `beforeStep` on `RunOptions` the right seam?
2. Is exit 130 for `q` acceptable? It would be documented as "interrupted by a user or CI signal, or `q` at the `--step` prompt".
3. Is skipping the prompt for `afterEach` and teardown steps fine, or should they be held with their own paused budget?

A working branch exists, with unit tests for the prompt, recorder and deadline pause, and integration tests through a worker process for timeouts, stop, interrupt and hook failure. I'll open the PR once the shape is agreed.


### Proposed API

```ts
npx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts --step --headed

step 1: app.open /todos  (tests/todos.e2e.ts:5)  · runs now; later steps wait for a key
step 2: locator.fill getByLabel("New todo")  (tests/todos.e2e.ts:9)
  c runs it · t finishes this test · r runs the rest · q stops the run

c       run the held step, hold the next
t       run the rest of this test (retries included), hold at the next test
r       run the rest of the run without stopping
q, Esc  stop as an interrupt: exit 130, current test interrupted, the rest skipped
Ctrl-C  same, and each further press climbs the existing signal ladder

Core seam (RunOptions is internal, not exported from e2e/runner):
  beforeStep?: (step: StepToHold, context: { notice(line: string): void }) => Promise<boolean>
  true lets the step run; false stops the run as an interrupt.
```

### Which surface

CLI flags

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: fix(e2e): launch a device's pinned app before explore and MCP look at it
body: On a device target, `e2e explore` and MCP `open_session` took their first look at the screen without ever opening the app. They depended on the mobile engine's warm-up to have opened it, and the warm-up skips the open when the target names an `app.appPath`. The result was `APP_NOT_OPEN: iOS snapshot requires an active app session`, and MCP returned no session id (ENG-865, two `e2e feedback` reports). - `launchesPinnedApp(target)` (`packages/e2e/src/config/targets.ts`) says when `app.open()` launches a pinned app rather than opening a URL: no app URL, and an engine with no `open` that relaunches the app in `restart`. - Explore now opens the app on such a target too (`packages/e2e/src/explore/index.ts`), so its first step is `app.open`, as on the web. - MCP calls `attempt.fixtures.app.open()` for such a target before the session's first observation (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts`). It is recorded as an ordinary `app.open` step, and the opening text names the app (`App: com.example.app, launched fresh.`), as it names the URL on the web. - The app now launches fresh, the way a test's `app.open()` launches it, instead of opening on whatever screen the warm-up left. - On a local device, a target with only `app.appPath` still has nothing to launch in explore or MCP, since only a test's `device.installApp()` installs the build. It now fails naming the missing install instead of `APP_NOT_OPEN`. - The fake engine gets a `device` mode (no `open`, `restart` opens the app), used by one new explore test and one new MCP test. Both fail on main. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - iOS simulator (iPhone 17 Pro) on a Mac, the built CLI from main and from this branch. The pinned app is Settings: `app: { bundleId: 'com.apple.Preferences', appPath: './missing.app' }`, so the warm-up skips the open, as for an Expo project that names its build. - MCP: a stdio client calls `open_session`. Explore: `e2e explore "Look around Settings" --max-steps 1` with a deliberately invalid AI Gateway key. Explore looks at the screen before its first model call, so an unauthorized model call means the screen was readable. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | MCP `open_session` | `APP_NOT_OPEN: snapshot failed: iOS snapshot requires an active app session on the target device.`, no session | `Session … open on target "ios"`, first observation returned | | explore | step 1 `agent.extract` fails with `APP_NOT_OPEN` | step 1 `app.open` (2.4s), then `agent.extract` reaches the model at `com.apple.Preferences / Settings` | With `bundleId` alone both builds open the session, since the warm-up opens the app. This branch adds the `app.open` step there as well. Not run: Android, and an exploration with a working model. --- Made with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

title: ci(examples): run every example nightly against main and report to Slack
body:
Runs every example in `examples/` (except `with-limrun`) every night at 23:00 Europe/Warsaw, against the packages built from main, and posts one Slack message for the whole run.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[pack: build main, pnpm pack e2e, web, mobile] --> W[web x4: Vite, Next, Astro, Expo web]
  P --> A[android x5: Compose, KMP, Flutter, MAUI, Expo]
  P --> I[ios x5: SwiftUI, KMP, Flutter, MAUI, Expo]
  W & A & I --> S[summary: one Slack message]
```

- `.github/workflows/examples.yml`: `schedule` with `timezone: Europe/Warsaw` plus `workflow_dispatch`. No `pull_request` or `merge_group` trigger and no gate job, so it never blocks a merge. The `pack` and `summary` jobs run only when `github.repository` is `tester-army/e2e`, and every example job needs `pack`, so a fork that dispatches it runs nothing.
- `.github/actions/example-packages`: points the example's `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile` at the tarballs the `pack` job made, then runs `npm install`. Everything else resolves fresh, since the examples commit no lockfile.
- Android jobs build the app, then install and test on an API 36 emulator (the same runner action and flags as `mobile.yml`). iOS jobs boot the newest iPhone simulator while the app builds, building for `arm64` only.
- Deterministic and agent tests both run, with `--retries 1`, so a test that only passed on the retry shows as flaky. The `pack` job fails right away when `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is missing, since otherwise the agent tests skip and the night looks green.
- `scripts/examples-nightly/`: each job uploads an `outcome.json` (setup, build, and test step outcomes) and its `report.json`. The summary job turns them into one message and posts it to the `SLACK_EXAMPLES_NIGHTLY_WEBHOOK_URL` incoming webhook (already set on the repo):

```
❌ *Nightly examples*: 1 of 14 failed on `main@96819fd`. <run>

✅ *Vite* · web: 5 passed (1m 05s)
🟡 *Next.js* · web: 1 flaky, 4 passed (58s)
❌ *.NET MAUI* · iOS: app build failed <log>
```

  A line that is not green links to its job's log. A run where every test skipped counts as failed, and so does a night where no job reported a result. If the jobs API cannot be read, the message says a job that wrote no result may be missing. When the key is missing or main fails to pack, the message says which and that no example ran.
- `AGENTS.md` and `examples/README.md` no longer say the examples run in no CI.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode 27.1, as far as a Mac can go. CI-only parts are listed at the end.

- The `pack` step's three `pnpm pack --out` calls, then the action's swap and `npm install` on copies of the examples: `npm ls` shows `e2e@0.21.2` and `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.2` from the tarballs.
- `with-vite`, `CI=1 npx e2e run --retries 1`: 3 passed, 2 agent tests skipped (no key here).
- `with-swiftui`: the matrix `xcodebuild` line, the job's simulator pick (iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0), `simctl install`, then `npx e2e run --target ios --retries 1`: 3 passed, 2 skipped.
- `with-flutter`: `flutter build ios --simulator`, install, same run: 3 passed, 2 skipped.
- `with-expo`: `expo prebuild` for both platforms produces `ios/withexpo.xcworkspace` and an Android release build signed with the debug keystore, and the iOS Release `xcodebuild` line produces `build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/withexpo.app`.
- `with-kotlin-multiplatform`: the iOS `xcodebuild` line with `ARCHS=arm64` produces `iosApp.app`, with `ANDROID_HOME` unset.
- `scripts/examples-nightly/post.ts --dry-run` against a real Vite report plus a made-up failed MAUI build, and with the pack job failing for each of its two reasons, printed the messages above.

Not run locally: the Android jobs, MAUI on either platform (no .NET here), Linux Chromium, and the Slack post itself. The first manual dispatch after merge covers them.

title: feat(runner): expose explore() through e2e/runner
body: Closes #1196. `e2e/runner` gets `explore()`, the counterpart of `e2e explore` that `run()` is to `e2e run`. ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { explore } from 'e2e/runner'; const result = await explore({ cwd: projectDirectory, config, // an E2EConfig value, or a config file path goal: 'Explore the login flow and report any bugs', target: 'web', maxSteps: 8, timeoutMs: 600_000, interruptSignal: signal, onEvent(event) { if (event.type === 'explore' && event.progress.phase === 'finding') console.log(event.progress.finding.title); }, }); result.status; // passed | failed | blocked | error | interrupted result.explore.ended; // finished | step-limit | time | stuck | aborted result.explore.findings; // kind, severity, title, expected, actual, reproduction result.reportPath; ``` - **Public wrapper:** `packages/e2e/src/explore/public-explore.ts` wraps the internal `explore()`. - Options are an explicit interface, passed through one by one, so CLI-only settings (`reporters`, `output`, `headed`, `forceSignal`) never reach the explorer. - The result is `RunResult` plus the `explore` record, with no live `config` or `results`. - **Shared with `run()`:** `run()` and `explore()` now share one `ownedRun()` (`packages/e2e/src/run/public-run.ts`). It handles the process reservation (`RUNNER_BUSY` across both), the owned and redacted output, cancellation and `onEvent` bound into the run's async context, and telemetry (`command: 'runner.explore'`). `run()` behaves as before. - **Config-load output:** the internal `explore()` takes `quiet` and `processOutput`. It holds what a config's top-level code prints while the config loads, until the config's secrets are registered, the way `run` loads its config. - **Notices:** with no `notice` callback, the notices `e2e explore` prints before the run starts (the target chosen, a custom executor replaced, a non-default agent) go to the run through `tests.notices`. The run emits them as `run` notices during setup, before the `plan` event, so `explore()` callers see them in `onEvent`. The CLI passes its own `notice` and is unchanged. - **Errors:** options or a config that cannot start an exploration reject before anything starts, as the CLI flags do (`INVALID_CONFIG`, `UNKNOWN_TARGET`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, and the config load codes). After that, everything resolves with its status in the report. - **Docs:** `reference/runner.mdx#explore` (with a typechecked example in `docs/examples/runner/explore.ts`), a pointer from `explore.mdx`, and the telemetry and security pages. The skill reference (`skills/e2e/references/running.md`) is synced to the plugin. - **Type checks:** `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` pins the option and result shapes, and `explore` is not exported from `e2e`. Not in this PR: the CLI's `e2e explore` still never claims process output, so a config that prints a secret at its top level reaches the terminal unredacted there. `e2e run` and `explore()` both redact it. The plumbing now exists, so it's a small follow-up; happy to open it separately. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, through the built package. There was no live model run, because I don't have a gateway key; the explorations use the repo's scripted model. - `tests/integration/explore.test.ts`, the "explore from e2e/runner" tests, import `dist/runner.js` and explore the fixture app in Chromium: - **Finding:** a scripted finding fails the run (exit 1). `result.explore` equals `report.run.explore`, `report.json` is written, and `onEvent` sees `started`, `step-started`, `finding`, `step-finished` and `finished`. - **Cancel:** aborting at `step-started` resolves `interrupted` (130) with attempt cleanup `complete`, and the next exploration passes. - **Rejections and overlap:** `maxSteps: 0` and an unknown target reject before anything starts. A `run()` started during an exploration rejects with `RUNNER_BUSY`. - **Notices and extra keys:** with two targets, the "exploring target" notice arrives as a `run` notice before `plan`. `output` and `reporters` passed past the type are ignored. - **Config output in a separate process:** a Node script imports `e2e/runner` and explores with a file config whose top level prints a configured secret. The terminal shows `config console.log: `. A config that prints and then throws has its output withheld. - With the `withholdDuring` change reverted, both tests fail and the raw token prints: | without the hold | this branch | | --- | --- | | `config console.log: explore-output-token-42` | `config console.log: ` | - **Docs example:** `docs/examples/runner/explore.ts` typechecks against the built packages. ### Live run (maintainer, rebased on main) Script imports `explore` from built `dist/runner.js`, runtime `E2EConfig` with two targets against the testbed bug garden, `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`: ```text 0.0 run-started 0.0 notice run exploring target "web"; pass --target to explore another 0.0 plan 3.5 explore step-started Cart and checkout 8.9 explore finding Home greeting exposes an unrendered userName template token 14.3 explore finding Neuromancer catalog listing shows negative stock 22.0 explore finding Checkout newsletter checkbox label misspells "Receive" 30.4 explore finding Order confirmation uses epoch dates and delivery precedes order 36.7 explore finished 37.5 run-finished RESULT exitCode 1, status failed, ended finished, 4 findings, keys exitCode,status,report,reportPath,aiTracePath,explore ``` - Abort 5s into a step: `run-interrupted`, resolves 130 / `interrupted`, `ended: aborted`, partial finding kept, app port released, caller keeps running. - Rejections: `maxSteps: 99` -> `INVALID_CONFIG`, `target: 'nope'` -> `UNKNOWN_TARGET`, `agent: 'ghost'` -> `INVALID_CONFIG`, all `isE2EError`. - Credential password absent from every file under the output dir; `video.webm` written.

title: docs(agents): correct the check chain, the core invariant, and the CI gate claim
body: ## What and why `AGENTS.md` is the file a coding agent reads before touching this repository, so a claim in it that no longer holds costs time twice: the agent follows the instruction, finds the opposite, and then has to work out which of the two to trust. Three claims in it are in that state. The first is the `pnpm check` chain at `AGENTS.md:256`. The line is labelled "(full gate)" and lists ten steps, skipping `check:changeset-bumps`, which `scripts.check` in `package.json` runs between `check:peer-ranges` and `check:install-scripts`. A contributor reading the file to find out whether their changeset bump is validated gets no answer there. The second is the core invariant at `AGENTS.md:38`. It reads "no `Web`, `browser`, `page`, `route`, or `playwright` noun lives in `src/` (grep for them; zero hits is the invariant)". Following that instruction returns 355 lines across 87 files under `packages/e2e/src`. Almost all of them are the words doing legitimate work: `web`, `ios`, and `android` as platform labels, `browser` as a capability name on the engine surface, `route` as the name of a module that describes where a screen is rather than a URL (`cache/route.ts`), and error text that names a factory (`config/targets.ts:66` tells the reader to call `web()` from `@e2e-dev/web`). The invariant the sentence reaches for does hold, and it is about imports: nothing under `src/` imports an engine package, and the only `@e2e-dev/` mentions are four lines of preset text in `cli/init/engines.ts`, which the next sentence already names as the exception. The third is the CI gate claim at `AGENTS.md:577`. It says "Each workflow ends in a ` gate` job, the only checks the `Main` ruleset requires (`spec gate`, `benchmark gate`, `mobile gate`, `docs gate`)". The parenthetical holds and those four gates are the required checks, but "each workflow" does not: five of the nine workflows under `.github/workflows/` have no gate job, and one of them says so in its own header (`.github/workflows/examples.yml:19-20`, "Nothing here gates a pull request: no pull_request or merge_group trigger, and no gate job"). The sentence follows "All four run on pull requests and in the merge queue", so the intent is readable from context, but a reader who takes the sentence literally goes looking for gates that do not exist. ## What changed Three edits, all in `AGENTS.md`. No behavior, no user-facing page, and nothing that ships: `AGENTS.md` is not part of the published package (`packages/e2e/package.json` and `packages/e2e/scripts/prepare-build.ts` do not mention it), so no changeset. The invariant becomes the check that holds, and names what a leftover word means so the next reader does not "fix" it: ```diff - internals: no `Web`, `browser`, `page`, `route`, or `playwright` noun lives in - `src/` (grep for them; zero hits is the invariant). The one exception is the + internals: no engine package is imported from `src/` (grep for + `from '@e2e-dev/` and `import('@e2e-dev/`; the presets below are the only + hits). Engine words still appear as platform labels, capability names, and in + error text that names a factory, such as `config/targets.ts` telling you to + call `web()`; no path through them reaches engine code. The one exception is the ``` The chain gains the missing step, in the position `scripts.check` runs it: ```diff -pnpm check # lint -> check:dead-code -> typecheck -> docs:check-errors -> check:peer-ranges -> check:install-scripts -> plugins:check -> mcp-server:check -> docs:check (full gate) +pnpm check # lint -> check:dead-code -> typecheck -> docs:check-errors -> check:peer-ranges -> check:changeset-bumps -> check:install-scripts -> plugins:check -> mcp-server:check -> docs:check (full gate) ``` The gate sentence now says "Each of the four ends in a ` gate` job", which is what its own paragraph introduces. For reference, the nine workflows and what they carry: | workflow | triggers | gate job | | --- | --- | --- | | `spec.yml` | `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `push`, dispatch | `spec gate` | | `benchmark.yml` | `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `push`, dispatch | `benchmark gate` | | `mobile.yml` | `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `push`, dispatch | `mobile gate` | | `docs.yml` | `pull_request`, `merge_group`, dispatch | `docs gate` | | `agent.yml` | schedule, dispatch | none | | `examples.yml` | schedule, dispatch | none | | `mcp-registry.yml` | `workflow_call`, dispatch | none | | `release.yml` | `push` to `main`, schedule, dispatch | none, and it requires a green `spec gate` on the commit it releases | | `review-label.yml` | `pull_request_target` | none | ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Compared the documented chain with `scripts.check` by extracting both step lists and diffing them: ten steps, same order, so the line now mirrors `package.json` exactly. - Re-ran the greps the corrected sentence prescribes. `from '@e2e-dev/` and `import('@e2e-dev/` return four lines, all in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/engines.ts`. A word grep for `browser`, `playwright`, `page`, `route`, and `web` returns 355 lines across 87 files, which is the number the old sentence called zero. - Read the gate jobs straight from the nine workflow files: `spec`, `benchmark`, `mobile`, and `docs` each end in one, the other five have none. - Nothing in CI reads `AGENTS.md` (`rg AGENTS.md .github scripts` finds no checker), so no test can fail on a stale claim here. The greps above are the check, and they are also what a reviewer can rerun. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: Web trace screenshots can cause React hydration warnings by hiding carets with inline styles
body:
`@e2e-dev/web` 0.15.2 automatically captures a trace screen after `app.open()` finishes navigation. On a server-rendered React page, this can precede hydration. `capturePixels()` passes `caret: 'hide'` to Playwright, which temporarily changes input and textarea inline styles. React then reports a hydration mismatch even though the application rendered matching HTML.

Reproduction:

1. Enable `trace: 'on'` with the web engine and navigate from a loaded page to an SSR React form using `app.open()`.
2. Attach console/page-error listeners before navigation. Hydration must still be pending when the automatic trace screenshot starts; a scenario's subsequent hydration wait cannot prevent that capture.
3. Observe the warning below. The same navigation without the automatic capture does not warn.

Sanitized trace:

```text
PlaywrightSurface.open -> acted -> TraceFeed.screenAfterAction
  -> captureObservation -> capturePixels
  -> page.screenshot({ animations: 'disabled', caret: 'hide', ... })

A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties.
  <Input>
    <input id="instrument-wizard-basics-name" ...>
-     style={{caret-color:"transparent"}}
  <Textarea>
    <textarea id="instrument-wizard-basics-description" ...>
-     style={{caret-color:"transparent"}}
```

Suggested fix: use `caret: 'initial'` with Playwright's temporary screenshot stylesheet (`style: '* { caret-color: transparent !important; }'`). This keeps carets out of captured pixels without editing React-owned form attributes. Secure-field masks and trace capture remain enabled. Alternatively, expose a supported pre-capture readiness hook.

Our browser fixture asserts that the navigation emits no console or page errors; the original package fails that assertion. With the stylesheet change, the same fixture and its session setup passed (2 tests, 19 seconds, zero console/page errors), with tracing and secure-field masks still enabled.

title: feat(web): set the browser clock before page scripts
body:
- Add `web({ clock })` using Playwright's context clock before init scripts and page scripts. Apply it again after context reset and saved-session restore.
- Validate dates and modes at config load. Reject persistent contexts, where reconnecting could reset time.
- Let scrolling settle while page timers are paused, without advancing the emulated clock.

```ts
web({ clock: { time: '2032-01-02T03:04:05Z' } });
web({ clock: { time: 0, mode: 'paused' } });
```

Paused mode stops page timers and animation frames. No per-test clock controls are added.

Closes #1229.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Built CLI: `e2e run --config e2e.config.ts --reporter list,markdown` against a local fixture.

```text
running                 10 passed
paused                  10 passed
running, epoch zero     10 passed
paused, negative epoch  10 passed
default mode            10 passed
```

- Built CLI in Chromium, 50 checks across five configurations: startup, navigation/reload, same-origin and cross-origin frames, popups, context reset, session restore, running/paused timers, and screen swipes. Covered ISO strings, numeric timestamps, epoch zero, and negative time.
- The paused-swipe regression fails with the previous rendering wait and passes here, with the scroll event delivered and the emulated clock still paused. Stalled-timeline tests cover point, viewport and node swipes, including bounded polling and non-retryable post-dispatch errors. Cancellation and deadline-expiry tests verify that no wheel is sent after preparation consumes the budget on point, viewport and node paths. Removing clock installation fails two running-mode startup/navigation tests; removing the shared wheel checkpoint fails six tests. Both restored suites pass.
- Follow-up checks in an isolated Chromium container: running and paused built-CLI startup/navigation/swipes pass, with 610 web tests, 79 testbed tests and 91 deterministic web benchmark tests passing. Rendered the clock reference section locally.

| Surface | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web({ clock })` | `INVALID_CONFIG`, unknown key `clock` | 50 CLI checks passed |
| Clockless scrolling, six paired runs | Same steps, outcomes and counters | Same steps, outcomes and counters |

| Scroll suite | main median | branch median | Paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sum of attempts | 6.88 s | 6.74 s | -2.3%, 95% CI -3.8% to -1.2%; same within ±5% |

Suite timing stayed within the ±5% threshold; this makes no performance claim. Firefox, WebKit and hosted providers were not tested with clock enabled. The option names and persistent-context restriction remain for maintainer review.

The docs screenshot remains local because the installed GitHub CLI 2.92 does not support attachments.
