title: feat(cache): scope first and last replay to a test id
body:
- Let a changing list replay by an explicitly requested first/last match instead of the recorded row's content or count.
- Scope the option to one test id, retaining its edge across re-rendered handles. Validate matching node and point targets, including drag endpoints, before input; refuse incomplete observations.
- Separate positional cache keys, occurrence counts and provenance. Ordinary keys, numeric positions and end-state verification keep their existing behavior.

```ts
await agent.act('open the first inbox item', {
  position: { testId: 'inbox-item', at: 'first' },
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  K[Position-scoped cache key] --> R{Recording?}
  R -- yes --> T[Resolve test id, role and edge]
  T --> V[Existing end-state verification]
  R -- no --> E[Live executor]
```

Closes #1225.

Maintainer decision: keep the scoped `act` option, including its public name, or prefer the existing locator pattern suggested in review? The issue example can already use `screen.getByTestId(...).first()/last()` with a separate agent step. This PR keeps the API as a proposal.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Documentation follow-up at cedae53c restores the counted-position JSDoc and removes cache-identity internals from the guide. `pnpm check` passes.

After merging main in bf35e1ed, `pnpm check`, the full `pnpm test` suite, 79 testbed tests, 91 web benchmark tests and 7 strict-cache replays passed. The first/last integration tests also verify before/after hook timing during live execution and replay.

Built CLI against a local Chromium inbox fixture:
`e2e run --config e2e.config.ts --reporter list,markdown`

```text
first/last cold recordings                       2 passed
changed, single, reordered, retained-old-row      8 replayed
ordinary/first/last, cold and warm in one cache   6 passed
first/last re-rendered immediately before click  2 passed
```

The eight changing-list replays opened the expected row with zero executor invocations. These recordings were produced through the public API, without editing cache files. Cold runs use a scripted executor to count fallbacks.

| Case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changing rows, ordinary call | `target-not-found`, executor runs | Same conservative handoff |
| Explicit positional option | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, unsupported option | 16 CLI checks passed |
| Unchanged ordinary recording | Replays | Replays with the same key |

Chromium integration tests also cover mixed-action steps, key isolation under strict cache, empty lists, contradictory choices, truncated observations, both drag endpoints, re-renders during input and between batched actions, and content-dependent end-state handoff. Testbed and deterministic web benchmark pass. Reference documentation passes site validation.

Point-input regressions fail before the fix because a rejected tap selects Beta and a rejected hover enters Beta. After the fix, both point verbs refuse contradictory and incomplete edge evidence before input, without saving a recording. The full core suite and all 16 public-API CLI checks pass in an isolated Chromium container.

Earlier measurements at cd84be07 against d8c597b6: committed control-inventory recordings, `--strict-cache`, six paired runs:

| Metric | main | this branch | Paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Suite attempts | 9.40 s | 9.39 s | +0.1%, 95% CI -9.4% to +2.7%; under the 10 ms floor |

Every run used the same steps and outcomes. Navigation event counts varied on both builds, 8 to 10 on main and 9 to 10 here. Timings were noisy on the shared VM; no performance claim.

The original Android flow was not run locally. An uncached model run stopped at AI Gateway authentication before any tool call because credentials are unavailable. The existing docs screenshot remains local because the installed GitHub CLI 2.92 cannot attach it.

title: fix(docs): explain off-site iframe limits beside iframe and vision guidance
body:
## Summary

The iframe and agent authoring guidance does not connect the browser engine's intentional off-site frame boundary to the ways a test can inspect that content. A visible payment form can be absent from the semantic tree used by an agent judgment. The boundary is documented in the security reference and SECURITY.md, but readers of the iframe, Vision, and bundled skill guidance have to discover that connection themselves.

### Page

- `docs/browser.mdx`, "Reach into an iframe".
- `docs/reference/agent.mdx`, "Vision".
- `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`, iframe guidance; `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`, Vision guidance; `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md`, iframe and inconclusive-judgment troubleshooting.

### What is wrong

The browser guide introduces the feature with "browser.frameLocator scopes queries to a frame" and examples for nested frames. It does not explain that these exact queries have different coverage from the semantic observation supplied to `agent.act`, `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract`. The Vision reference lists the default evidence as "Semantic tree", but does not identify off-site frame contents as a case where visible UI is missing from that tree. The debugging reference mentions iframes for `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and pixels for `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`, without explaining the shared authoring scenario.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Inspect the listed pages in either source baseline below. Compare them with the security reference's "Site check" section, which states that observations omit child frames from other sites and `data:` frames.
2. For a model-free demonstration, install the example repository's locked dependencies with `npm ci` and start its app as documented in its README. Its default host is `http://localhost:3000`; its card and nested field frames use `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
3. Configure an e2e web target with `app.url` set to the host URL. Run `e2e mcp`, open a session, and call its `observe` tool. No model is required.
4. Close the session. Configure `app.url` as the frame hostname instead, open another session, and observe again.
5. Independently check exact access from the original off-site host with the following test. Import `test` from `@e2e-dev/web` and `expect` from `e2e`:

```ts
test("reads the off-site pay button", async ({ app, browser }) => {
  await app.open("/");
  await expect(
    browser.frameLocator('[data-testid="checkout-iframe"]')
      .getByRole("button", { name: "Pay $165.00" })
  ).toBeVisible();
});
```

The executed probes used an unused port instead of the default, with both public origin variables updated as the example README instructs. They used a config with no model. The example's model-backed suite was not rerun.

## Expected behavior

The iframe authoring path should explain the existing distinction between exact frame queries and the agent's semantic tree, and direct readers to the applicable judgment evidence mode. The Vision and bundled guidance should make the same limitation discoverable. This asks for documentation of the existing behavior, without changing the observation boundary.

## Actual behavior

The off-site observation contained three nodes:

```text
#root document "e2e iframe checkout"
 #n2 main
  #n3 iframe "Card payment" testid="checkout-iframe"
```

There were no child contents or truncation warning. With the host opened on the frame hostname, the observation contained 23 nodes, including the card document, nested field documents, textboxes, and a Pay button. The exact off-site `frameLocator` assertion passed, 1/1 test with retries disabled.

The current main authoring pages still omit the boundary/remedy connection. This is a documentation omission; the observed filtering agrees with the security contract.

## Runtime or environment

- Published packages in the isolated install: `e2e` 0.21.2 and `@e2e-dev/web` 0.15.2, both npm `latest` at verification.
- Documentation inspected at release tag `e2e@0.21.2`, commit `393005aa6952eaef62886cd03c8d8060f8f05a4f`, and default-branch main commit `ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d`.
- Example: [tester-army/e2e-iframes](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e-iframes), commit `0e2cbe8b6ca32ba7205216955edfd463b6ec99ce`.
- Node 26.12.0, macOS arm64, Darwin 27.0.0; default headless web engine.
- Runtime observations concern the published packages; main was inspected as source, not built or run.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [CONTRIBUTING.md, "The contract"](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-contract) says code is authoritative when documentation and code differ. The [security reference's "Site check"](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/docs/reference/security.mdx#site-check) establishes the actual frame boundary.
- Failure source: The inspected [iframe guide](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/docs/browser.mdx#reach-into-an-iframe), [Vision reference](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/docs/reference/agent.mdx#vision), and bundled paths listed above omit that connection; the model-free comparison demonstrates why it affects authoring.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Documentation inspection, both semantic observations, and the exact frame assertion were performed for this report.

The implementation in `packages/web/src/observation.ts` enters a child frame only when `isOnSiteFrame(frame.url(), deps.site)` holds, and explicitly says omitted off-site frames are boundary nodes rather than truncation. The site's comparison is an approximation of the registrable domain, not a blanket same-origin rule; `localhost` and an IP literal count as separate sites.

## Restoration check

From "Reach into an iframe", a reader should be able to determine why an off-site frame's visible contents are missing from an agent's tree, choose exact `frameLocator` queries or an appropriate Vision judgment, and find the same explanation in the bundled agent skill and debugging guidance. Keep the runtime control intact: off-site content stays outside the tree while exact frame access still works.

### Suggested wording

"Agent semantic observations omit child-frame contents from other sites, leaving an iframe boundary node. This intentional omission is not truncation. Exact `browser.frameLocator(...)` queries can inspect the frame directly. For a judgment about visible frame content, use `vision: true` when screenshots are available, or the documented visual-only mode when appropriate. Screenshots cover the current viewport and remain subject to the Vision withholding rules."

A short explanation or cross-reference beside the existing iframe and Vision sections, mirrored into the bundled guidance, would make the existing behavior discoverable without adding a separate guide.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Test authors can ask a tree-only judgment about visible embedded content that the engine deliberately omits; the authoring and troubleshooting pages do not explain this bounded evidence gap.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The exact frame assertion passed against off-site content. The existing Vision reference documents screenshot evidence modes and their availability limits; no Vision model run is claimed here.

title: fix(docs): explain why off-site iframe-only acts never record a replay
body:
## Summary

The replay-cache guidance omits a limitation that matters for hosted payment fields and other off-site embeds: an `agent.act` can successfully change the visible iframe and pass a subsequent locator assertion, yet save no replay because its outcome changes neither the observed controls nor the host route. The same act runs the model again on the next run. This report asks for documentation of the current recording behavior, not a change to the site boundary or a new ability to record iframe-only effects.

## Page

`docs/cache.mdx` (When a recording is written; Why a step was not replayed), `skills/e2e/references/agent.md` (The replay cache), and `docs/browser.mdx` (Reach into an iframe).

## What is wrong

The recording guidance uses visible screen changes and later verification to explain eligibility, without identifying that an off-site iframe can visibly change while the recorder sees no eligible change. The reduced case below demonstrates the difference.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the public [iframe checkout example](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e-iframes) at the fixture revision below and run `npm ci`. Add `@ai-sdk/openai@^4` for the tested model route and use an existing e2e OpenAI login; other tool-capable models should be usable but were not tested here.
2. Save the following config as `e2e.repro.config.ts`. The host and card origins deliberately use different sites; port 3200 avoids assuming the default dev port is free.

```ts
import type { E2EConfig } from "e2e";
import { web } from "@e2e-dev/web";
import { chatgpt } from "e2e/oauth/chatgpt";

export default {
  cache: "read-write",
  agents: { default: {
    model: chatgpt("gpt-6.1-sol"),
    providerOptions: { openai: { reasoningEffort: "high" } },
    system: "You are a thorough QA agent. Verify every outcome.",
  } },
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: {
    url: "http://localhost:3200",
    command: {
      executable: "node",
      args: ["node_modules/next/dist/bin/next", "dev", "-p", "3200"],
      env: {
        NEXT_PUBLIC_HOST_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:3200",
        NEXT_PUBLIC_CARD_ORIGIN: "http://127.0.0.1:3200",
      },
      log: ".e2e/logs/app.log",
    },
  } }],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

3. Save this reduced test as `tests/cache-repro.e2e.ts`:

```ts
import { test } from "@e2e-dev/web";
import { expect } from "e2e";

test("off-site-only validation has a verified outcome", async ({ app, agent, browser }) => {
  await app.open("/");
  await agent.act("click the Pay button without filling in the card form");
  await expect(browser.frameLocator('[data-testid="checkout-iframe"]').getByText("Enter the name on the card.")).toBeVisible();
});
```

4. With an initially empty replay cache, run the command below twice without changing the test, config, or cache. Preserve each `.e2e/report.json` before the next run. Do not use `--no-cache`, which disables writes too.

```bash
npx e2e run tests/cache-repro.e2e.ts --config e2e.repro.config.ts --workers 1 --retries 0 --debug
```

5. Read the agent step's `cache` and `metrics.modelCalls` fields in both reports.

## Expected behavior

The cache and agent guides should explain this exception to the statement that a passing act is saved after a later verification. In particular, they should connect `no-change` to effects confined to off-site frames, explain the repeated model calls, and point to exact `frameLocator` actions when predictable model usage is required. The iframe guide is a useful place to link this cache limitation.

## Actual behavior

Both executions passed the iframe locator assertion, exited 0, used two model calls, and reported one cache miss. Each act used `tapAt`; its trace said the listed nodes were unchanged while the screenshot changed. Both reports contained the same cache entry key and these values:

```json
{
  "mode": "missed",
  "reason": "no-entry",
  "replayedActions": 0,
  "totalActions": 0,
  "write": "no-change"
}
```

The cache guide defines `no-change` without mentioning iframe observation boundaries. Its reason table says a next verified pass records a `no-entry` step, without this qualification. The bundled agent guide similarly says a passing act saves its actions once a later check verifies the outcome. Neither page connects iframe-only visible effects to never recording an entry. The iframe section only describes exact locator access.

Strict mode does not make this case model-free: the existing strict-mode contract explicitly leaves never-recorded steps live. That consequence is supported by the docs and source; a strict-mode runtime run was not performed here.

## Runtime or environment

- Executed packages: `e2e` 0.21.2 and `@e2e-dev/web` 0.15.2, both npm `latest` when checked; `@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.97 and `ai` 7.0.145.
- Runtime: Node 26.12.0, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, default Chromium web engine.
- Model: `chatgpt("gpt-6.1-sol")` from `e2e/oauth/chatgpt`, reasoning effort `high`.
- Fixture revision: `0e2cbe8b6ca32ba7205216955edfd463b6ec99ce`.
- Release source tag: `e2e@0.21.2`.
- Current default branch inspected: `main` at `ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d`. Its cache page and bundled agent guide are unchanged from the release tag; the relevant frame-filter and no-change recording conditions are unchanged too. The branch was inspected, not built or executed.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [Caching, When a recording is written](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/docs/cache.mdx#L22-L56), including “the runner saves the recording at the end of the attempt when a later verification step passed.” The repository's contribution contract treats disagreement between code and docs as a documentation bug.
- Failure source: The two executed reduced tests and report excerpts above; direct inspection of the cache page, [bundled agent cache guide](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/skills/e2e/references/agent.md#L284-L329), and [iframe guide](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/docs/browser.mdx#L94-L114) found no explanation of this recording limitation.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime observations above come from the published packages; current-branch documentation and implementation observations come from source inspection.

The [frame observation filter](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/packages/web/src/observation.ts#L182-L224) intentionally omits off-site child-frame contents. The [cache staging condition](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/ee901b333ed12352418dfb07bda5eafe32e71c8d/packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts#L600-L610) returns `no-change` when the observation delta has no appeared/gone controls and the route did not move. The site rule itself is already documented in the security reference; this report concerns explaining its replay-cache consequence.

## Restoration check

A reader of the cache and bundled agent guidance should be able to predict the two-run result above: an off-site iframe-only visible change can remain `missed / no-entry / no-change` despite a passing locator check. The guidance should also explain that never-recorded steps still run live under strict replay. No runtime change is required to close this documentation report.

A model-free workaround was verified separately against the same validation check: replace the act with `await card.getByRole("button", { name: "Pay $165.00" }).tap()`, where `card` is the same `browser.frameLocator` scope. That test passed with zero model calls. This keeps the validation coverage without depending on a recording of iframe-only effects.

## Suggested wording

An act whose only visible effect is inside an off-site iframe may finish successfully but record no replay. Those frames' contents are absent from the observation used to check the recording's end state, so a step with no observed control or route change reports `write: "no-change"` even when a later iframe locator assertion passes. It runs live again on subsequent runs, including strict mode when no entry has ever been recorded. Use exact `browser.frameLocator(...)` actions for iframe input or clicks that must avoid model calls.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The unqualified recording guidance can lead users of hosted fields and off-site embeds to expect replay after verification while the same successful step uses model calls on each run; both runs of the reduced case did so. Reach beyond the observed case was not measured.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: An exact frameLocator button action passed the same validation assertion with zero model calls; it preserves this test's outcome without changing the observation boundary.

title: feat(cige): run, classify, replay, and safely repair CIGE test cases
body:
## The problem

An e2e test written today mixes four things in one TypeScript body:

- where it runs
- why it exists
- what the agent must never do
- the path it takes

When the test goes red, nothing in it says which of these broke. A failed `agent.act` can mean the staging API is down, the flow moved, the product has a bug, or the agent found a shortcut that should never have counted as a pass. An agent asked to fix the test can't tell whether it may edit the steps, the setup, or the assertion. A fix that edits the assertion so the test goes green hides a product bug.

[CIGE](https://www.amazon.science/publications/cige-an-agentic-ai-test-case-standard) is a test case standard for agentic runners that separates those concerns. The paper reports the authors' experience on an industry codeless agentic testing platform: about 90% less maintenance effort, 38% fewer false positives, and 62% less execution time.

| Field | Says | Who may change it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context | Where the test runs, and pointers to its spec, release notes, and expected output | A repair for environment drift, approved by a human |
| Intent | Why it exists and what a pass needs | A human. A repair may only add criteria or evidence |
| Guardrails | What the agent must never do | A repair may make them stricter, never looser |
| Execution | The first path to try | A repair for a changed flow |

e2e already has the pieces: atomic `act` goals, judges that never see `system` or the ledger, `agentContext`, `onAction`, `blocked` versus `failed` verdicts with a closed code table, tags, sessions, platforms, and per-test traces. This PR maps CIGE onto them in a new package and a consumer skill. It changes nothing in `packages/e2e`.

## What CIGE adds

- Test cases structured for developers and agents: schema-validated JSON for people, run summaries and a skill for agents, for authoring and maintenance.
- A field-scoped self-healing workflow: a first failure classification in every run summary, and role-scoped guides (classify, recover, repair, escalate) that one agent or several can follow, gated by replay and a mechanical Intent check (`e2e-cige diff`).
- Pluggable ground truth for classification: spec, release notes, and expected output per build, fetched on request, with readiness checks before anything fails.
- An extensible implementation of the CIGE standard: `x-` fields, plugins, and custom step kinds, with validation intact.
- Per-test runtime guardrails: in every agent instruction, enforced after every action (replays included), extensible with plugin checks; the judges stay independent of them.
- Intent as identity: unique per case and the test title, so runs filter by it (`--grep`), and by case id (`--tag cige:<id>`).
- Evidence beyond the screen that fails closed, plus a `screen-only-evidence` signal for a pass that may be false.
- Variants across data, platforms, personas, and sessions, under one Intent.
- No change to e2e core.

What this PR does not claim: the paper's measured gains (they come from another platform), or guardrails the runner blocks before an action (`deny` stops the step after it).

## What a customer does

1. Writes a case as JSON (`tests/cige/checkout.cige.json`), with editor validation from the shipped `cige-1` schema.
2. Declares the project's ground truth one time, in `cige.config.ts`: hooks, environments and how each resets, the build id from CI, and resolvers for the spec, release notes, and expected output. The `cige` skill asks for these before it writes the first case.
3. Runs `npx e2e run`. Each case is one test per variant, tagged `cige:<id>`. Each result gets a run summary.
4. On a failure, the `cige` skill reads the summary, classifies it, makes only the repair that kind allows, replays the case, and proves with `e2e-cige diff` that the Intent held.

```json
{
  "id": "checkout-discount",
  "Context": { "system": "Shop web app", "environment": "staging", "open": "/cart", "specRef": "docs/specs/checkout.md", "buildRef": "releases/{build}.md" },
  "Intent": {
    "statement": "A shopper can check out with the discount code {code}",
    "evidence": [{ "id": "order-record", "hook": "orderPersisted" }]
  },
  "Guardrails": ["Use only the test card", { "id": "no-refund", "rule": "Never refund an order", "deny": { "actions": ["tool:refund"] } }],
  "Execution": [{ "id": "e1", "step": "apply the discount code {code}" }, { "id": "e2", "step": "pay with the test card" }],
  "Variants": [{ "id": "save10", "params": { "code": "SAVE10" } }, { "id": "save20-mobile", "params": { "code": "SAVE20" }, "platforms": ["ios", "android"] }]
}
```

```ts
// cige.config.ts: read by cigeSuite(), the cige() reporter, and the e2e-cige command
export default defineCige({
  cases: 'tests/cige/*.cige.json',
  build: process.env.GITHUB_SHA,
  hooks: { orderPersisted: async ({ screen }) => (await fetch(`/test-api/orders/${await screen.getByTestId('order-id').textContent()}`)).ok },
  environments: { staging: { config: 'e2e.staging.config.ts', reset: resetStaging } },
  refs: { build: ({ build }) => ({ url: `https://github.com/acme/shop/commit/${build}` }) },
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[.cige.json + cige.config.ts] --> S[cigeSuite: one test per variant]
  S --> E["Execution: agent.act + guardrails, deny via onAction"]
  E --> V["Intent.evidence (hook must return true), then Intent judged"]
  V --> R["cige(): .e2e/cige/id.run-summary.json"]
  R --> K["cige skill: classify"]
  K -->|infrastructure| ENV["e2e-cige env reset"]
  K -->|stale path| EX["rewrite Execution"]
  K -->|false pass| G["add guardrail / evidence"]
  K -->|defect| D["e2e-cige refs: file bug or propose Intent"]
  ENV --> RP["e2e-cige replay id"]
  EX --> RP
  G --> RP
  RP --> DF["e2e-cige diff: blocks a weakened case"]
```

## How CIGE maps onto e2e

| CIGE | e2e |
| --- | --- |
| Intent | The test title and the `cige:<id>` tag, then a final `agent.assert`. The judge never reads the guardrails or the acting agent's summaries, so a lenient prompt can't lower the bar |
| Evidence | A pass needs every `Intent.evidence` item: a screen judgment, or a hook in your code. A hook holds only when it returns `true`; a forgotten `return` fails. A hook that throws is `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` (a backend that's down is not a product defect), unless it threw an e2e error, which keeps its code |
| Context | `agentContext`, facts only. `platforms`, `requires`, `session`, and `agent` become the test's options. `specRef`, `buildRef`, and `expectedRef` never reach the model |
| Variants | One test per variant (`cige:<id>/<variant>`): its values fill `{name}` placeholders, as params for `act` steps and as text for judgments |
| Guardrails | Appended to each `act` instruction. A `deny` rule is checked in `onAction` after every action, replayed ones included, and stops the step with `POLICY_DENIED` |
| Execution | One `agent.act` per step, or `agent.assert` for a `verify` step. Ids give a failure a stable name such as `e2` |

The reporter's first guess at a failure type (`packages/cige/src/classify.ts`) reads the error class and step status e2e already writes to `report.json` (`error.category`, a `blocked` step), so a new code in core needs no change here. Only the test-class path codes are named, typed as `AgentError['code']`:

| Where and what | `failureType` |
| --- | --- |
| A precondition failed, or an error of class `infrastructure` or `configuration` (not `POLICY_DENIED` or `REPLAY_STALE`) | `infrastructure` |
| An Execution step failed: `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `ACTION_FAILED`, `REPLAY_STALE` | `outdated-test-logic` |
| A `verify`, a piece of evidence, the Intent, or a plugin's check step was judged false | `product-defect` |
| An act step whose goal the agent could not reach (`ASSERTION_FAILED`) | Absent, signal `goal-unreachable`: a changed flow or a defect |
| A blocked test-class step (not `APP_NOT_OPEN`), a spent budget, the clock, no conclusion | Absent, signal `automation-limit` |
| A guardrail violation, an agent's refusal citing one (`guardrail-refused:<id>`), an inconclusive judgment, anything else | Absent; `signals` names what it saw |

A false positive is never set by the reporter: the skill decides it from the `screen-only-evidence` signal and the trace.

## The `e2e-cige` command

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `replay <id> [--variant v]` | Runs the environment's `reset` (refuses an environment without one), then `e2e run --config <env config> --tag cige:<id> --no-cache`, and exits with e2e's code. Other cases' summaries and all refs stay |
| `env provision\|reset\|teardown <name>` | Restores an environment without touching any case |
| `refs <id>` | Runs the config's resolvers on request and writes the spec, release notes, and expected output to `.e2e/cige/<id>.refs/`. Never runs during a run |
| `check [--resolve]` | Lists each case that lacks a spec or build ref, a build for `{build}`, or an environment with a reset, before anything fails. The reporter adds a `CIGE gaps` row under the run summary |
| `diff --base origin/main` | From the merge base, exits 1 when a change weakens or redirects a case: Intent changed, a variant's data changed, a criterion, evidence item, guardrail, deny pattern, variant, or case removed, any Context change, or a change to the CIGE config or any module it imports. It finds those by loading the config in a child Node process, then parsing each module (Node's type stripping, then acorn) for lazy imports, so `#` aliases, workspace packages (one built to an ignored `dist` counts by its sources), symlinks, lazily imported hooks, and the resolution fields of the package.json that maps them count. A config it can't load or follow (a computed `import()`/`require()`, `createRequire`, `eval`) blocks as `config-unverified`. Loading runs the config's top-level code, so `diff` needs the run's env. App code the config doesn't import, data files a hook reads, and installed packages are out of its reach. Rewriting Execution and additions pass, so tightening after a false pass needs no human. `--allow-intent` is the human's override and records nothing |

It spawns the installed `e2e` bin; it uses no internal API.

## Extending CIGE

The schema stays closed, so a misspelled key still fails to load. Three layers open it on purpose:

| Layer | How | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your own fields | `x-` keys on any object (`"x-owner"`, `"x-deny-host"` on a guardrail), kept as `extensions` | Hooks and plugins read them. The model never sees them unless a plugin adds them. Top-level ones are copied into summaries. `diff` blocks an `x-` change under Intent or on a guardrail |
| Your own behavior | `plugins` in `cige.config.ts`: `context`, `onAction`, `classify`, `summarize`, `readiness`, `steps` | Context lines, guardrail checks driven by `x-` data, classification changes (`classification.adjustedBy`), summary fields under `extensions.<plugin>`, `check` gaps |
| Your own steps | `{ "id": "e4", "use": "order-api", "with": {...} }` | Runs a plugin's step kind in Execution order; variants fill `with`; a failure names the step |

```ts
export const shop: CigePlugin = {
  name: 'shop',
  context: (testCase) => {
    const flags = testCase.context.extensions?.['x-feature-flags'];
    return Array.isArray(flags) ? `Feature flags on: ${flags.join(', ')}` : undefined;
  },
  steps: {
    'order-api': async ({ step }) => {
      const response = await fetch(new URL(String(step.with.path), 'http://localhost:3000'));
      if (response.status >= 500) throw new AgentError('ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE', `GET ${String(step.with.path)} answered ${response.status}`);
      if (response.status !== step.with.expect) throw new AgentError('ASSERTION_FAILED', `GET ${String(step.with.path)} answered ${response.status}`);
    },
  },
};
```

A new extension point is a plugin hook, never an open key (AGENTS.md says so).

## The `cige` skill, in this repo

`skills/cige/` (installed with `npx skills add tester-army/e2e --skill cige`, and in the e2e plugin) routes each job to one reference: authoring, classify, recover, repair, escalate. Each may write only its own field, replays with `e2e-cige replay`, and ends with `e2e-cige diff --json` in the hand-off. Authoring asks the user, one time per project, where specs, release notes, and expected output live and how each environment resets.

## Cost to the repo

- No change to `packages/e2e`. The package imports from `e2e` only. Peer `e2e >=0.21.0 <1`; `zod`, `acorn`, and `oxc-parser` (the version `e2e` ships) as its dependencies; a patch changeset.
- `cige-1` is pinned by `packages/cige/schema/cige-1.schema.json`, generated from the loader's zod schema at build (a test fails on a stale copy), with a valid and an invalid fixture.
- `docs/cige.mdx` under Features, three typechecked examples in `docs/examples/cige/`, and links from the README, `docs/coding-agents.mdx`, `docs/agents.mdx`, and `docs/reference/agent.mdx`. The shipped e2e skill doesn't mention it. The field reference lives in `packages/cige/README.md`.
- The testbed's weekly agent suite gains two CIGE cases (`apps/testbed/tests-agent/cige/`): the wizard with two variants, and the todo list with a `deny` guardrail. Each pass is backed by a code check of the page.
- 125 package tests, no model and no browser.
- The repo's `verify` skill gains a `@e2e-dev/cige` row, so a later change to the package or the skill is proven on the testbed, not only by unit tests.
- First release needs a maintainer: per CONTRIBUTING.md, a new public package is published by hand once and connected to its npm trusted publisher before `release.yml` can publish it. The changeset queues `@e2e-dev/cige`, so that step has to happen first, or the changeset waits.
- I'll maintain it and answer its issues.

## Not in this PR

- Blocking an action before it runs. `onAction` fires after the action, which the docs page says. Blocking needs the built-in agent exported as a wrappable executor, a core API question for an issue first.
- Writing report `extensions` from a reporter. The summaries are a sidecar file.
- YAML, and importers from Gherkin and existing `*.e2e.ts` files.

  - With `--ai-trace`, the plugin's `Feature flags on: wizard-v1` context line reached the model 6 times; `x-owner` and `x-ticket` reached it 0 times; every act instruction carried the guardrail block.
  - The first live run caught two misclassifications, fixed here: an unreachable act goal was typed `product-defect`, and an agent's own guardrail refusal named no guardrail.
  - `e2e-cige replay orders-infra` printed `resetting local-openai`, ran `e2e run --config e2e.cige-local.config.ts --tag cige:orders-infra --no-cache`, and exited with e2e's code. `e2e-cige refs wizard-workspace --variant atlas-pro` wrote `index.json` and `build.md` (the last five commits under `app/`). `e2e-cige check --resolve` on the testbed: `All 2 CIGE cases are ready to classify and replay.`
- `e2e-cige diff --base upstream/main` on the testbed reports the new cases as `case-added` and the new `cige.config.ts` as `config-changed`, which needs approval: adding hooks is a human's call.
- **Live repair loop, driven by `skills/cige`** (`gpt-6-luna`, on a throwaway local branch, deleted afterwards):

| Step | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | The testbed wizard gained a Billing choice and a case "A visitor can create the workspace Lyra on the Pro plan" whose `e2` was "choose the Pro plan with Monthly billing". It passed live |
| Product drift | Commit `feat(wizard): drop the billing choice; every plan bills annually` |
| Failure | `e2` failed: "no Monthly billing option was available". Summary: `ASSERTION_FAILED`, `goal-unreachable`, no type |
| Classify (`classify.md`) | It reached the system. `goal-unreachable` routes to step 2. `e2e-cige refs`: the release notes hold the drop-billing commit; the spec still has name, Pro plan, and Create. So `outdated-test-logic` |
| Repair (`repair.md`, Mode A) | Read the failure screen (no billing step) and changed only `e2`, to "choose the Pro plan", keeping its id |
| Replay | `e2e-cige replay workspace-pro`: reset, then the case alone with no cache. Passed; the evidence hook read `Created "Lyra" on the Pro plan` |
| Prove | `e2e-cige diff --json`: `execution-changed: steps e2`, `intentUnchanged: true`, `blocking: 0` |
| Shortcut check | Weakening the Intent and dropping its evidence instead: `diff` lists 3 changes that need approval and exits 1 |

  - The loop caught one bug, fixed here: on a CIGE config other than `cige.config.ts`, the summary's `refs` and `replay` commands found no case. The new `configFile` option passes `--config`.
  - The `e2e` MCP server didn't connect in that session, so the repair read the failure screen the run captured instead of a live MCP session.
- The weekly agent workflow runs the committed cases with the Gateway key.

title: ci(examples): install the Android MAUI workload for the iOS build
body:
The `ios maui` job in the nightly examples run has failed at "Build the app" in both runs so far ([39281408611](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/39281408611), [39345923541](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/39345923541)):

```text
error NETSDK1147: To build this project, the following workloads must be installed: android
  [examples/with-maui/WithMaui.csproj::TargetFramework=net10.0-android]
```

- On macOS, `WithMaui.csproj` targets both `net10.0-android` and `net10.0-ios`. `dotnet build -f net10.0-ios` restores the project first, and restore reads every target framework, so it needs the Android workload as well.
- The iOS job installed only `maui-ios`. It now installs `maui-ios maui-android`, the two workloads the project targets. The README's `dotnet workload install maui` already covers both, so users never hit this.
- The build command stays the one the README documents.

The same night had two other failures that this PR does not touch:

- `android kmp`: `sdkmanager` failed to unpack the API 36 system image (`Error on ZipFile unknown archive`) before the emulator started. This is a runner download problem. Every other Android job that night downloaded the same image without trouble.
- `ios expo`: the agent test `the agent finds the empty-name error` failed on both attempts. The engine read the empty, focused name field as `value="Ada Lovelace"`, which is the field's placeholder, and agent-device sent no `placeholder`. The agent took the placeholder for typed text and spent its turns trying to clear it. The previous run read the field the same way and passed by luck. Fixed in #1274.

## Verified

Ran it locally: no - CI-only. The fix only shows up on a macOS runner with the MAUI workloads, and the nightly run is the one place that builds it. The next scheduled run will show it, or a `workflow_dispatch` of `examples.yml` on this branch (that run also posts to the nightly Slack channel).

title: fix(mobile): read an empty iOS text field as empty, not as its placeholder
body:
On iOS, an empty text field read as if it held its placeholder text. That broke the `ios expo` agent test in the [nightly examples run](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/39345923541) on both attempts.

- agent-device reports an empty React Native `TextInput` on iOS with `value` equal to `placeholder` and no `hintShowing` flag. Only UIAutomator sets that flag; the iOS runner has no such field:

  ```json
  {"type":"TextField","label":"Name","value":"Ada Lovelace","placeholder":"Ada Lovelace","identifier":"name","editable":true}
  ```

- `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts` blanked the value only on `hintShowing`, so the field became `textbox "Name" value="Ada Lovelace"`. The agent's view hides `placeholder` when a field has a name (`packages/e2e/src/agent/observation.ts:448`), so the model saw only a field it thought was already filled.
- Asked to "press Greet without typing a name", the agent spent its 11 turns trying to delete "Ada Lovelace" and never pressed Greet. The run before it read the field the same way and passed by luck.
- The reader now treats an editable iOS field whose value equals its placeholder (trimmed) as empty. agent-device's runner uses the same check during text entry (`textMatchesPlaceholder`). Android still relies on `hintShowing`.
- History: #499 hit this on the CI Mac and added the `hintShowing` check, believing the iOS bridge set the flag. No agent-device version does that on iOS: 0.21.13, the version #499 used, and 0.21.28 both read it from Android sources only. The test that check came with fed iOS a flag that never comes. agent-device later added `placeholder` to iOS nodes so consumers could tell an empty field from a filled one ([callstack/agent-device#2961](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/2961)). The reader never used it for that until now.
- Trade-off: on iOS, text typed to exactly match the placeholder also reads as empty. The snapshot cannot tell the two apart. `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` now says so.
- The iOS goldens in `packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/snapshots/ios/` do not change. In those captures of the mobile benchmark, empty fields come with no `value` at all. The unit test pins the shape captured from `examples/with-expo`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `examples/with-expo` built for the iOS simulator as the nightly builds it (`expo prebuild`, Release `xcodebuild`), on an iPhone 17 Pro with iOS 26.5, Xcode 27.1, and agent-device 0.21.28, the same agent-device version the nightly used.
- A probe test dumped the screen the agent reads in three states. main used the npm packages; this branch used `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile` packed from the branch, the way the nightly swaps them in:

| state | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| empty, after `app.open()` | `textbox "Name" testid="name" value="Ada Lovelace"` | `textbox "Name" testid="name"` |
| empty, focused | `textbox "Name" testid="name" value="Ada Lovelace" [focused]` | `textbox "Name" testid="name" [focused]` |
| after `fill('Ada')` | `value="Ada"` | `value="Ada"` |
| after Greet clears it | `textbox "Name" testid="name" value="Ada Lovelace"` | `textbox "Name" testid="name"` |

- The example's `tests/deterministic.e2e.ts` passes on the branch build.
- Not run: the example's agent test. No model key was set locally.

title: web: let an app expose drawn objects (canvas, WebGL) as semantic nodes
body:
## Problem

Apps that draw their content on a `<canvas>` are hard to test with e2e today. Whiteboards, diagram editors, maps, charts, and React Three Fiber scenes all fall in this group. The in-page reader lists `canvas` among its opaque tags, so the whole board is one node in the observation. In my 2D fixture it shows up as `box "Tablero"` with no children.

That leaves three gaps:

- `screen` locators can't target a drawn object. There is no `getByRole('note', 'Alfa')` for a sticky note drawn on the canvas.
- The agent falls back to the pixel tools. `tap_at` works, but a bare-point action replays only on a viewport of the recorded size. There is no `drag_at`, so `agent.act` can't move an object to a free spot.
- A judgment sees nothing of the drawn content unless `vision` is on.

A canvas app usually keeps a scene model in memory with each object's type, label, and box. If the engine could read that model, drawn objects could be ordinary nodes.

## What I tried

I wrapped `web()` in an engine of my own with `defineEngine`, on e2e 0.21.2 and @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2. The wrapper keeps every member of the `web()` handle and overrides three of them:

- `observe` calls the inner `observe`, then runs a page function, `readScene()`. It returns the drawn objects with a role, a name, a box in viewport CSS pixels, and an optional parent. The wrapper adds them as children of the DOM node whose box matches the canvas. An object whose center is outside the canvas box gets `states.hidden: true`.
- `locate` returns the inner matches plus `resolveExpression(expression, drawnNodes)`.
- `perform` sends pointer input to the center of a drawn node for `tap`, `doubleTap`, `hover`, and `dragTo`. `scrollIntoView` calls a second page function, `reveal(id)`, that pans the app's camera. A hidden node throws `NOT_ACTIONABLE`.

I tested it on a 2D canvas fixture with two frames, two notes, and pan and zoom buttons. I also tested it on a production React Three Fiber app, where `readScene()` uses the app's own test probes. The results:

- `await expect(screen.getByRole('note', 'Alfa')).toBeVisible()` passes, and `dragTo` between two drawn nodes moves the object in the app.
- `agent.act('Drag the "Alfa" note onto the "Beta" note')` works with a real model, Claude Haiku 5.5 behind a custom `StepExecutor`. The model picked `drag` with the two drawn node ids in one move.
- The replay cache works across runs. In the fixture, the recorded trace stores targets such as `{ role: 'note', name: 'Gasolina' }`. After a zoom, the replay finds the same objects at new positions and finishes without calling the executor. In the React Three Fiber app, the second run replayed the drag without calling the model, on a new case with new element ids.
- With the object off screen, the replay gets `NOT_ACTIONABLE` and hands off to the executor. The executor's `scroll_to` calls `reveal`, then the drag succeeds.

The wrapper works, but it depends on things the contract doesn't promise:

- It spreads the frozen handle that `web()` returns, minus `capabilities`, into a new `defineEngine` call.
- It reaches the page with `surfaceOf(inner)`, which the docs describe for executors, not for engines.
- Its pointer input skips the guard, settle, staleness, and error classification that the built-in actions get.

## Proposed API

A `web()` option names the element that holds the drawing and two page functions. The engine does the rest.

```ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';

export default {
	targets: [
		{
			engine: web({
				drawn: [
					{
						// Drawn nodes become children of the first match.
						selector: 'canvas[data-engine]',
						// Runs in the page on every observation and locate.
						// Boxes use viewport CSS pixels, like SemanticNode.rect.
						read: () =>
							window.__board.objects().map((o) => ({
								id: o.id,
								role: 'note',
								name: o.title,
								rect: o.screenRect,
								parent: o.frameId,
							})),
						// Optional. Runs in the page to bring one object into view.
						reveal: (id) => window.__board.panTo(id),
					},
				],
			}),
			app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' },
		},
	],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

A test file then reads like any other:

```ts
await expect(screen.getByRole('note', 'Alfa')).toBeVisible();
await screen.getByRole('note', 'Alfa').dragTo(screen.getByRole('group', 'Done'));
await agent.act('Move the "Alfa" note into the "Done" frame');
```

I'd expect the engine to:

- Read the drawn nodes inside the same observation, so revisions and staleness cover them like any other node.
- Send `tap`, `doubleTap`, `secondaryTap`, `longPress`, `hover`, and `dragTo` on a drawn node through the existing pointer path at the node's center, with the same settle and error rules as `performAt`.
- Map `scrollIntoView` to `reveal`, and report `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` for the other action kinds.

## Open questions

- Is a `web()` option the right place? A supported way to extend any engine's observation would also serve a Flutter web or Unity engine.
- Should the agent's observation text carry coarse geometry for drawn nodes? Without it, a judgment such as "Alfa is on top of Beta" stays inconclusive from the tree, and the test has to check positions itself.
- How should secure-field masking treat a drawn region? My prototype ignores it.

## A smaller gap: `drag_at`

The agent has `tap_at`, `hover_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at`, but no `drag_at`. Engines already declare `dragTo` in `pointerActions` with a `ViewportPoint` target, so only the agent's tool set is missing it. I can send that as a separate PR first if you want it.

## Environment

Windows 11, Node 26.3.0, e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2, and Chromium headless shell 153.0.8010.12.

## Which surface

Config keys (`web()` options). Also the engine contract (`e2e/engine`) if you prefer a general extension point.

## Compatibility

The change only adds an option. Nothing that exists today changes.

title: feat(config): discover e2e.config.js and document a JavaScript setup
body:
A project written in plain JavaScript can now use e2e without `--config` on every command, and the docs show how to set it up.

- Discovery reads `e2e.config.js` and `e2e.config.mjs` as well as `.ts` and `.mts` (`packages/e2e/src/config/names.ts`).
- A TypeScript config wins in its directory, so the `e2e.config.js` that `tsc` emits beside `e2e.config.ts` doesn't start failing existing projects with `CONFIG_AMBIGUOUS`. Both TypeScript names, or both JavaScript names, together are still ambiguous.
- `e2e init` treats an existing JavaScript config as existing, writes its example as `tests/example.e2e.js`, and skips the "No tsconfig.json" hint.
- `NO_TESTS` names the glob to set when every near miss is `*.e2e.js` (or every one is `*.e2e.mjs`), instead of saying "rename to *.e2e.ts".
- The `INVALID_CONFIG` hint for a missing default export drops `satisfies E2EConfig` in a JavaScript config.
- The default `tests` glob stays `tests/**/*.e2e.ts`. A JavaScript project sets `tests` itself, which the docs say.

Docs:

- Quickstart: a folded "Use JavaScript instead of TypeScript" section in "Create the test project". It shows only the lines that change, so it works for the web and mobile configs.
- `reference/config`: a new `JavaScript` section under Loading (JSDoc `@type`, ES modules, the `tests` glob, `// @ts-check` and `jsconfig.json`, importing a `.ts` helper), plus discovery rules under "Finding the config file".
- The section's example is `docs/examples/javascript/e2e.config.js`. `docs/examples` now typechecks `.js` with `checkJs`, so the JSDoc type is checked (a misspelled key fails `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/docs typecheck`).
- The config names are updated wherever docs, skills, the `--config` help, and the MCP `open_session` description listed only `.ts`/`.mts`: errors, CLI, runner, the migration guides, and `skills/e2e`.

```js
/** @type {import('e2e').E2EConfig} */
export default {
  tests: 'tests/**/*.e2e.js',
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' } }],
};
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch project with the built CLI and `@e2e-dev/web`, a static page, `e2e.config.js` and `tests/hello.e2e.js`, no `tsconfig.json`:

```
### 1. JS config, tests glob not set
 ERROR  configuration error NO_TESTS (collection)
no test file matched "tests/**/*.e2e.ts" under …/jsproj; found tests/hello.e2e.js, which the pattern does not match: set tests in the config to a glob such as "tests/**/*.e2e.js"; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this
### 2. tests set
 ✓ target "web" command ready 192ms
 ✓ |web| tests/hello.e2e.js (1 test) 433ms
   ✓ greets 433ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
### 3. e2e init with JS config
▲  Exists, not touching: e2e.config.js
◆  Created tests/example.e2e.js
### 4. TS config beside emitted JS
NO_TESTS: no test file matched "tests/**/*.e2e.ts" …   (the .ts config was picked, with its default glob)
```

- Also passed with `e2e.config.mjs` + `*.e2e.mjs` tests, and without `"type": "module"` (Node.js warns that it reparsed the file as ESM, which the docs mention).
- A `.js` test importing a `.ts` helper ran. `tsc -p jsconfig.json` with the documented options caught a misspelled config key.
- Docs previewed with `mint dev`:

| Quickstart | Config reference |
| --- | --- |
| ![quickstart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42b20a6f-c020-462a-bbf5-be5d0af313e0) | ![config reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17fd1c72-e59a-445e-94b6-59fbcb102888) |

title: fix(mobile): wait through an iOS app not running yet after a launch
body:
On a physical iPhone, an assertion right after `app.restart()` failed at once with `ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed: app '…' is not running`, while the splash was still up. Reported through `e2e feedback` (ENG-939); the workaround was `expect.poll` swallowing the error.

- agent-device relaunches on a physical device with `devicectl device process launch`, which returns before XCTest reports the app as running. The iOS runner refuses every read in that window with `APP_NOT_RUNNING`, and our error translation made it a non-retryable `ENGINE_FAILURE`.
- A locate now reads that refusal as a screen still arriving, the same way #1166 treats an unreadable Android capture: zero matches, and the poll keeps waiting until the deadline.
- The tolerance only holds between a launch (`open`, `restart`, `openLink`) and the first successful snapshot. The runner also raises `APP_NOT_RUNNING` for an app that crashed or was closed, and that must not read as an empty screen, or `not.toBeVisible()` would pass on a dead app (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`, `launching`).
- A wait that runs out while the app is still down fails with agent-device's message and hint, not with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`.
- An app that crashes before its first readable screen gives the same refusal as one still starting, so an immediate negative read (`not.toBeVisible()`, `count()`) sees no matches there, as on Android since #1166. Positive waits and actions still fail with the reason. `docs/mobile.mdx` says so.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on an iOS 26.5 simulator on the Mac, using the SwiftUI example app (`examples/with-swiftui`) and the built packages. The simulator's `simctl launch` doesn't leave the physical-device gap, so a plain restart loop passed on main too (10/10). The repro recreates the gap: it stops the app right after `app.restart()` and relaunches it 2 s later in the background, then asserts.

```ts
await app.restart();
execFileSync('xcrun', ['simctl', 'terminate', UDID, BUNDLE]);
spawn('sh', ['-c', `sleep 2 && xcrun simctl launch ${UDID} ${BUNDLE}`], { stdio: 'ignore', detached: true }).unref();
await expect(screen.getByText('Say hello')).toBeVisible();
```

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App comes up about 2 s after the restart | fails at once: `ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed: app 'dev.e2e.examples.swiftui' is not running` | passes 3/3, visible after 3.5 to 4.4 s |
| App never comes back after the restart | fails at once with that message | waits the `expect` timeout, then fails with the same message and hint |
| App terminated mid-test, then `not.toBeVisible()` | fails at once with that message | fails at once with that message |

Also run on a physical iPhone 16 Pro (iOS 27.0.1) with three `app.restart()`s each followed at once by an assertion. The phone's free developer profile leaves room only for agent-device's runner, so the app under test was the built-in Settings app. It did not reproduce the bug on main: agent-device's relaunch took about 60 s on the phone and Settings was up by the time it returned. Main and this branch both passed with the element visible about 6 s after each restart, so the branch does not regress on a device. The user's case, an installed app still on its splash when the assertion runs, is covered by the simulator repro above, not observed on a device.

## Not in this PR

- An observation in the same window (the agent's next turn right after `app.restart()`) still fails at once, as the docs already say for Android. The fix there would be a readiness wait in `open()`, which costs an extra read on every launch; left for a follow-up if anyone hits it.

---

Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code), reviewed in a fresh context by Fable 5.

title: feat(agent): add drag_at to the pixel tools
body:
## What and why - The agent has `tap_at`, `hover_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at`, but no drag, so `agent.act` cannot move a shape on a canvas or a pin on a map that the tree does not list. Engines already declare `dragTo` in `pointerActions` with a viewport point target; only the agent side was missing. Split out of #1277. - New agent tool `drag_at {x, y, to_x, to_y}`, in screenshot pixels like the other point tools. New executor action `ctx.actions.dragAt(from, to)`, which returns a `PointDragResult`. - Same rule as `tap_at` after #1284: the bare points go to the engine's `dragTo` pointer kind, where the model aimed. An engine without that kind drags by id when the points land on two different listed controls, as an ordinary `drag`, and fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` otherwise (a node dragged onto itself does nothing). - The trace records a `dragAt` entry as `from: { point, within? }` and `to: { point, within? }` plus the viewport. Each `within` is the point's place inside the listed node that contained it, with that node's container and place among twins, so each end follows a layout shift on replay the way a `tap_at` point does. One reader and one text mapper serve `tapAt`/`hoverAt` and both drag ends. In `replay.ts` the planned `point` and `within` kinds are now one `point` kind with a `PointEnd`, which the drag reuses for both ends. - Additive only: `ExecutorActions` gains a member and no existing signature changes. `GrammarVerb` is internal, so the engine contract (`e2e/engine`) is unchanged. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["drag_at(x, y, to_x, to_y)"] --> B{"engine declares
pointerActions dragTo?"} B -- yes --> C["performAt(from, { kind: 'dragTo', target: to })"] B -- no --> D{"ends on two different
listed controls?"} D -- yes --> E["drag by id"] D -- no --> F["UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY"] ``` From a custom `StepExecutor`: ```ts const result = await ctx.actions.dragAt({ x: 180, y: 36 }, { x: 120, y: 60 }); // result.source and result.destination name the listed controls at each end, when there are any. ``` Code: `packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts` (`pointDrag`), `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts` (`drag_at`), `packages/e2e/src/cache/trace.ts` (`PointDragAction`), `packages/e2e/src/agent/replay.ts` (`pointDrag` plan). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-act-pixel-tools.test.ts` with real Chromium on the canvas fixture. A scripted agent calls `drag_at {x: 180, y: 36, to_x: 120, to_y: 60}` on a pin the tree does not list, and the page logs `moved red to 200,100`. A second case drags between two listed controls on the web engine, which gets the bare points (`drag from the point (50, 275) on button "Reset" to the point (100, 315) on textbox "Note"`). A fixture engine with node drags only joins the same kind of two controls by id and refuses two points inside one control with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - 2026-10-28, merged main d2ffb319c: resolved the `mcp/catalog.ts` doc comment (main added `run_code`), the web MCP catalog count is now 29, and the `performAt` JSDoc names `drag_at`. `pnpm check` and the full `e2e` suite (3993 tests) pass. Dropping the `to` end's placement in the recorder fails 2 recorder tests; routing by id first fails the bare-points web case. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Not breaking. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. No wire change. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. Not an engine contract change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(agent): tap_at and hover_at tap where the model aimed
body: `tap_at` outside a native iOS popover never dismissed it. iOS lists a full-screen `dismiss popup` button behind the popover, so the point snapped to that button and the tap went by id to its center, which is inside the popover. The tap hit the calendar instead of the backdrop. - `tap_at` and `hover_at` still snap a point to the listed control under it, but only when the control's own center is reachable. When the innermost node at the center belongs to another node (an overlay, or an enabled control nested inside it, like a card link around its "Add to cart" button), the runner sends the bare point through the engine's `performAt` instead (`packages/e2e/src/agent/point-tap.ts`, `centerReaches`). - An engine without a bare-point tap keeps tapping by id, as before. - The step summary says which happened: `Tapped the point (187, 150) inside #n738 button "dismiss popup"` instead of `Tapped #n738 …, the control at (187, 150)`. - "Innermost" is the tree's stand-in for what is on top, the same rule `hitTest` already uses, not paint order. An overlay listed shallower than the control is not seen. - `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at` are unchanged: they act on a field, so the field's center is the right place. - Replay stays as durable as before: the recorder stores a bare point as `within` the node under it. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `e2e mcp` against Apple's UIKitCatalog on an iPhone SE (3rd gen) simulator, iOS 26.5: open the Date Picker popover, then `tap_at` at (187, 150), above it. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `Tapped #n738 button "dismiss popup" testid="PopoverDismissRegion", the control at (187, 150).` The popover stays open. | `Tapped the point (187, 150) inside #n738 button "dismiss popup" testid="PopoverDismissRegion".` The popover closes. | | ![main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d839299b-c364-4bfe-b8c7-66406b0bb837) | ![branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/677e0021-f62a-4d04-a1e1-bfb03c58e824) | - Mobile benchmark on two iPhone 17 Pro simulators (iOS 26.5), branch build: deterministic suite 55 passed, 1 skipped; agentic suite with a model key 21 of 22. The failure, Apple Pay Billing Address, is the simulator timing out while typing into the Apple Pay sheet, which uses no point tool. - The new unit and integration tests fail with the nested-control check or the engine-capability check removed. --- Changes made by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code.

title: fix(e2e): let expect(await response.json()) reach the value matchers
body: `expect(await response.json()).toMatchSchema(schema)` failed to type-check on the web engine's `WebResponse`: ``` TS2339: Property 'toMatchSchema' does not exist on type 'AsyncExpectation'. ``` - `json(): Promise` infers `T` from its contextual type. `expect`'s first overload was `(actual: Locator)`, so `T` became `Locator` and the call routed to the locator matchers. `expect.soft` did the same. - The locator and screen overloads are now generic (`(actual: NotAny)`). TypeScript infers nothing from a bare type parameter, so `json()` keeps `unknown` and lands on the value overload. `packages/e2e/src/types.ts:1011` - `NotAny` keeps `any` off the locator overload. A generic `L` would otherwise match `any`, and the DOM `fetch(...).json()` from the API testing guide would have regressed. - `json()` is unchanged, so `const users: User[] = await response.json()` still infers `T`. Closes ENG-974. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Typechecked a scratch test in `apps/testbed` (DOM lib) against the built packages, on main and on this branch: | `expect(...)` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `await response.json()` (web engine) `.toMatchSchema` | TS2339 | ok | | `expect.soft(await response.json())` `.toMatchSchema` | TS2339 | ok | | `await (await fetch(url)).json()` (DOM `any`) `.toMatchSchema` | ok | ok | | `JSON.parse('[]')` `.toEqual` | ok | ok | | `const users: User[] = await response.json()` | ok | ok | | locator, `screen`, `browser`, `Locator \| undefined` routing | unchanged | unchanged | - `sdk-types.ts` gains the engine-response and `any` cases for `expect` and `expect.soft`. Both fail against the old overloads. - All 9 nightly examples (vite, next, astro, expo, swiftui, compose, kotlin-multiplatform, flutter, maui) pass `tsc --noEmit` with this branch's packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile` swapped in. --- Changes by Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, via T3 Code.

title: fix(cli): exit when a timer or socket keeps the process alive after the command
body:
Fixes [ENG-958](https://linear.app/tester-army/issue/ENG-958/cli-e2e-run-stays-alive-after-reports-are-written-when-handles-stay).

## What and why

- The CLI process imports `e2e.config.ts` and, to collect tests, every test file (`packages/e2e/src/collect/collect.ts`, `importModule`). A timer or socket either one opens at import, such as a database pool, a keep-alive agent, or a `setInterval`, keeps `e2e run` and `e2e list` alive after the report is written and the exit code is set. `e2e mcp` stays alive the same way after its client disconnects.
- `bin.ts` calls `exitIfStopped()` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/run-output.ts`, added in #1206), which exits only after Ctrl-C or when the run stopped waiting for a test filter or a reporter. Any other run ends only once nothing is left open. This change builds on it and on `drainRunnerOutput()` from the same file.
- New `exitAfterGrace()` in `run-output.ts`, called from `bin.ts` after `exitIfStopped()`, starts an unref'd 2 s timer:
  - A process with nothing left open ends on its own first, as today. `beforeExit` hooks and short timers left by user code still print (`tests/integration/run-user-output.test.ts`).
  - A process still alive when the timer fires waits for app stops already in flight (new `stopsSettled()` in `packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`), so an app or service command keeps its full `shutdownTimeout`. Then it kills any app process group e2e started and nothing is stopping (`killManagedProcessGroups`), drains its output, and exits with the exit code the command set.
- `exitIfStopped()` and its work-left-behind flag are unchanged.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed, the built CLI, a scratch target whose test file or config calls `setInterval(() => {}, 60_000)` at import. A command still running after 25 s was killed.

| | main (`69e123b1`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No open timer, `e2e run` | exit 0, 0.9 s | exit 0, 0.9 s |
| Timer in a test file, `e2e run` | still running, killed | exit 0, 2.9 s |
| Timer in the config, `e2e run` | still running, killed | exit 0, 2.9 s |
| Timer in a test file, `e2e list` | still running, killed | exit 0, 2.4 s |
| Timer in the config, `e2e mcp`: `open_session`, then the client closes stdin | still running after 20 s | exit 0, 2.0 s after the disconnect |

```text
# tests-eng958/page.e2e.ts calls setInterval(() => {}, 60_000) at import; this branch
$ e2e run --config e2e.eng958.config.ts
 ✓ target "web" command ready 89ms
 ✓ |web| tests-eng958/page.e2e.ts (1 test) 144ms
   ✓ page renders 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
   Duration  461ms (startup 89ms)
exit 0 after 2.8s
```

- `e2e run --watch` with the timer keeps watching after the first run and exits on Ctrl-C.
- The new integration tests hang on main and pass here: `run` and `list` exit codes with an open timer, and a 400-test `--reporter json` report through a pipe with an open timer (`cli-run.test.ts`, 60 s spawn limit); `e2e mcp` after a disconnect with a timer in the config (`mcp-disconnect.test.ts`, 20 s).
- Exit codes the command sets survive the grace exit: a passed test whose cleanup failed (#1233) with a timer in the config exits 3 (`cli-run.test.ts`, hangs on main).
- On `ee901b33` (main before #1206), an iOS simulator run and a web plus iOS run with no open timer exited as soon as the command was done.

title: fix(web): hide the screenshot caret with a stylesheet
body: ## What and why The web engine captures the observation screenshot that follows an action, including the automatic trace screen after `app.open()`, in `capturePixels` (`packages/web/src/observe.ts:62`). It passed `caret: 'hide'` to `page.screenshot()`. Playwright implements that option by walking every `input`, `textarea`, and `[contenteditable]` in each root, storing the current inline `caret-color`, setting it to `transparent` with importance, and restoring it after the frame (`playwright-core` 1.64, `inPagePrepareForScreenshots`). A server-rendered React page that is still hydrating during that window sees a style React did not render, compares it with the server HTML, and logs "A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties" against its own `` and `

title: fix(web): hide screenshot carets with temporary stylesheet (#1259)
body: ## Summary Fixes #1259. When capturing observation pixels (`capturePixels`), `@e2e-dev/web` previously passed `caret: 'hide'` to Playwright's `page.screenshot()`. Internally, Playwright hides carets by injecting an inline `style="caret-color: transparent !important;"` attribute directly onto active `input` and `textarea` elements. On server-side rendered React pages navigated via `app.open()`, this mutation can happen before client-side hydration completes, triggering React hydration warnings. This change switches `caret: 'initial'` and uses Playwright's `style` parameter (`* { caret-color: transparent !important; }`) to hide carets via a temporary stylesheet during capture without mutating any element's inline attributes. ## Verified - Verified that Playwright's default `caret: 'hide'` triggers a DOM attribute mutation on `#test-input` while `caret: 'initial'` with `style: '* { caret-color: transparent !important; }'` triggers no mutations. - Added an integration test in `packages/web/tests/integration/lifecycle.test.ts` verifying that `engine.observe({ pixels: true })` captures screenshot pixels with zero `style` attribute mutations detected via `MutationObserver`. - Ran `packages/web` vitest integration test suite covering `lifecycle.test.ts` and `semantic-fallback.test.ts`: all passed.

title: fix(mobile): keep the known viewport when the app reads smaller than the screen
body: On iOS, a swipe that starts at a sheet's grabber (y≈52) can land in the system's top-edge zone and pull down Notification Center instead of dismissing the sheet. With Notification Center up, agent-device's XCTest snapshot backend reads the app behind it at a third of the screen: 130x281.33 on a 390x844 iPhone, marked `healthy`. `project()` stored that as the known viewport, so every rect and tap after it was measured against the wrong screen (ENG-914). The triage blamed a sparse mid-transition frame. On an iOS 26 simulator the shrunk tree was `healthy` and lasted as long as Notification Center stayed down, so a sparse-only guard would never fire. - A snapshot replaces the known viewport only when it is the same size or that size rotated (`sameScreen`, `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`). - Any other size is checked once against the simulator screenshot's logical size. If they disagree, the known viewport stays. The screenshot reports portrait even in landscape, so it confirms a size but not an orientation; rotations are taken from the tree. - A real device's screenshot carries no logical size, so there the tree's size still wins, as on main. Android reports a constant screen size and never produced this. - `viewportFor` accepts a rotated size itself, so the keyboard dismissal, which projects its own snapshot, still follows a rotation since the last observation. ```mermaid flowchart LR S[snapshot size] --> K{known?} K -- no --> A[adopt] K -- yes --> R{same or rotated?} R -- yes --> A R -- no --> P{screenshot logical size} P -- agrees --> A P -- none --> A P -- disagrees --> KEEP[keep known] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - iPhone 16e simulator (iOS 26), Calendar. Through agent-device directly, a swipe from the Calendars sheet's grabber pulled Notification Center and the snapshot came back as `Application "Calendar" 130x281.33`, `healthy`, with the screenshot at 390x844. - A scratch e2e test against the built branch packages: portrait, landscape, back to portrait, open the Calendars sheet, swipe from its grabber. Passed. The engine's viewport (logged from `dist`) was 390x844, then 844x390 in landscape with no screenshot probe, then 390x844 through the swipe. - On this simulator the engine read through agent-device's AX backend, which reported 390x844 even with Notification Center down, so main did not misbehave end to end. The live 130x281.33 tree is replayed in a unit test instead. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | viewport after the 130x281.33 tree (`keeps the known viewport for an app drawn smaller than the screen`) | 130x281.33 | 390x844 | Fixes ENG-914 Made with Claude Code (Opus 5.5); reviewed by Claude Fable 5.1. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8760d40e-71ee-4091-bad7-59d76cdf3aae

title: Locator filter({ hasNot }): exclude candidates that contain a locator
body:
### Problem

`filter` keeps candidates that contain some text (`hasText`) or some locator (`has`). Open PR #1037 adds `hasNotText`. What remains is the structural counterpart, `hasNot`: drop candidates that contain a given locator.

Text exclusion is a substring test ([screen.mdx L297-L299](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/docs/reference/screen.mdx#L297-L299)), so it can't tell a status apart from text that merely contains it. `hasNotText: 'Archived'` also drops a row whose description says "Unarchived on Monday". A locator can say exactly which element must be absent:

```ts
// the order rows that carry no "Archived" badge
const active = screen.getByRole('listitem')
  .filter({ hasText: 'Order 1042' })
  .filter({ hasNot: screen.getByRole('status', 'Archived') });   // INVALID_LOCATOR today
await active.getByRole('button', 'Cancel order').tap();
```

At 93f77d8, `filter` rejects any key except `hasText` and `has` with `INVALID_LOCATOR` ([screen.ts L649-L658](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts#L649-L658)). The migration guide lists `hasNot` as missing ([playwright.mdx L145](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/docs/migrate/playwright.mdx#L145)). Our current workaround is a negative-lookahead `RegExp` in `hasText`. That only works when the excluded thing has unique text, and it is hard to review.

### Proposed API

```ts
rows.filter({ hasNot: screen.getByRole('status', 'Archived') });
rows.filter({ hasText: 'Order 1042', hasNot: screen.getByRole('button', 'Restore') });
```

- The same ownership and scoping rules as `has`: the inner locator is evaluated relative to each candidate, and a locator made by another target's screen is `INVALID_LOCATOR`.
- On every engine, as `has` is today ([mobile locate.ts L19-L39](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/mobile/src/locate.ts#L19-L39)).
- Composes with `hasText`, `has`, and #1037's `hasNotText`.

### Which surface

public types (SDK), engine contract (`e2e/engine`)

The filter fields are part of `LocatorExpression` ([contract.ts L87-L98](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts#L87-L98)).

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: Locator failures: show how many candidates each filter step left
body:
### Problem

When a filtered locator fails, the error names the whole expression, and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` gives the final match count ([engine.ts L594-L615](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts#L594-L615)). It doesn't say *which* step narrowed too much or too little. With a chain such as:

```ts
screen.getByRole('listitem')
  .filter({ hasText: 'Order 1042' })
  .filter({ has: screen.getByRole('button', 'Cancel order') });
```

a `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` could mean there are no list items yet, the text differs ("Order #1042"), or the button is named differently. The trace already helps: `trace.md` ends with the screen at failure, its node count, the nodes closest to what the locator asked for, and the full tree ([failure-text.ts L555-L575](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/e2e/src/report/failure-text.ts#L555-L575)), and `screen.tree()` prints the same listing from a test (#1239). What none of them say is how many candidates survived each filter step, so working that out still means reading the tree by hand or rewriting the locator one step at a time and rerunning.

This is independent of any new filter: it helps the `hasText` and `has` filters that exist now, and any added later (#1037).

### Proposed API

No new API; a diagnostic. On `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` for a filtered locator, include the candidate count after each step, in the error message and in `trace.md`:

```text
LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND
  getByRole("listitem")                                               6
  ….filter({ hasText: "Order 1042" })                                 1
  ….filter({ has: getByRole("button", name: "Cancel order") })        0
```

- Ideally the counts come from the same resolution attempt as the failure (the last one before the deadline). On web a filter chain is composed into one Playwright locator ([locators.ts L298-L315](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/web/src/locators.ts#L298-L315)), so per-step counts may need one `count()` per prefix taken after the failure; where that is how they were read, the lines should say so, because a page that changes between reads can make them disagree.
- The step labels reuse the existing expression rendering ([expression.ts L151-L184](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/e2e/src/locator/expression.ts#L151-L184)), and text passes through the usual redaction.

### Which surface

report or cache format

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

Error messages gain lines; codes and exit codes are unchanged. CONTRIBUTING.md's stability policy leaves the exact text of error messages uncovered.
