title: web: evaluate a function against one locator match, the primitive for toHaveCSS and toHaveJSProperty
body:
### Problem

Closing #1045, the automated review posted on behalf of @okwasniewski asked for "one generic 'read a value from a locator' primitive, which would also cover `locator.evaluate`, `toHaveJSProperty` and `toBeInViewport`, and build `toHaveCSS` on top of it", rather than a hook that serves one matcher ([comment](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1045#issuecomment-6215907255)). It said this would be tracked on #1020, which is now closed. This issue tracks the primitive and the two matchers; `toBeInViewport` is in #1295, because the engine already reports each node's box and the viewport size on every platform, so it may not need a page script.

Today, reading a computed style or DOM property means `browser.evaluate` with a CSS selector that finds the element a second time:

```ts
await expect.poll(() => browser.evaluate(() =>
  getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('nav')!).position)).toBe('sticky');
```

The selector doesn't share the locator's scope, strict single match, or frame, so it can quietly read a different element from the one the test meant. The migration guide lists `locator.evaluate`, `toHaveCSS` and `toHaveJSProperty` as missing ([L182](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/docs/migrate/playwright.mdx#L182), [L211](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/docs/migrate/playwright.mdx#L211)).

### Proposed API

A browser-only method, separate from `browser.evaluate(fn, arg)`, whose second argument is already arbitrary JSON ([browser.ts L217-L223](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/web/src/browser.ts#L217-L223)), so its behaviour stays unchanged. The name is open:

```ts
const position = await browser.evaluateOn(nav, (el) => getComputedStyle(el).position);
const width = await browser.evaluateOn(sidebar, (el, extra) => (el as HTMLElement).offsetWidth + extra, 0);
```

- Resolves the locator with its usual scope, ownership, strict single match and frame, and waits for the match like other reads (#1097).
- The element is supplied inside the page only; test code never holds a handle. The explicit argument and the return value stay JSON, as with `browser.evaluate`.
- Documented as a read: the callback can change the page, but tests shouldn't use it to.

The matchers then follow the `expect(browser).toHaveClass(locator, …)` precedent ([browser.ts L158-L166](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/93f77d8/packages/web/src/browser.ts#L158-L166)), and poll like the rest of `expect`:

```ts
await expect(browser).toHaveCSS(nav, 'position', 'sticky');
await expect(browser).toHaveJSProperty(sidebar, 'offsetWidth', 240);
```

Related: #1228 asks for computed-style reads in project tools (`ToolContext`), a different surface.

### Which surface

public types (SDK)

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

New method and matchers; `browser.evaluate` is unchanged.

title: Mobile: delayed keyboard movement can send the next tap to stale bounds
fix(mobile): reobserve targets after keyboard transitions
body:
## What and why

- Retain keyboard state with each captured index. An unchanged rectangle skips the transition wait only when keyboard state also stayed unchanged. Tap, focus, fill, typing, character presses, Enter and dismissal share this rule; the action-kind exceptions are removed.
- Map `target_still_moving` to retryable `NODE_STALE` only with `dispatched: 'no'`. Missing/unknown dispatch stays nonretryable.
- Update regression coverage, comments, reference/skill documentation and the patch changeset.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Target captured] --> B{New or moved target, or keyboard changed?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Wait remaining budget and refresh]
  B -->|No| D[Act immediately]
```

#1253 keeps native readiness ownership for eligible opt-in Android presses; this change belongs to the adapter transition policy. #1300 handles losing the target after refresh. Merge #1300 first, then retain its stale check when rebasing this PR. A disposable combined checkout passed 367 mobile tests after resolving the binding-argument overlap.

## Issue

Fixes #1296.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. Head `530e53046a9d790f8891629443b9c383568e873f`.

[Public controlled fixture and capture evidence](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/530e53046a9d790f8891629443b9c383568e873f/packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/keyboard-signal/README.md): visible software-keyboard nodes precede the button moving from y418.67 to y258.67. The original consumer raw capture was not retained; this verifies the signal in a fresh controlled reproduction.

| Check | Current main `d8c597b` | This PR |

| Same focused regressions | 17 fail / 4 pass | 21 pass |
| Pre-rebase built CLI, same diagnostic binary, one worker, zero retries | `93f77d8`: 1/1 pass, 3.71s body | `828b1e8`: 1/1 pass, 4.24s body |

Both live runs pass, so they establish compatibility, not a deterministic native failure or performance claim. The video run also passed; media remains local because upstream attachment upload requires repository write access. The diagnostic host used a local generated UIScene adaptation for iOS 27; no full unmodified benchmark or Android device pass is claimed.

Rebased onto current main `d8c597b`, preserving its viewport fix: all 374 mobile tests and `pnpm check` pass. A fresh built-CLI run with agent-device 0.21.29 also passes, one worker and zero retries. Unchanged-state fast-path tests assert no pending timer. Independent review found no remaining issues.

The reviewed runtime head `4a092a550` passed the spec, docs and mobile gates, including iOS and Android deterministic suites. The documentation-only follow-up `17b7d310` removes the one-off diagnostic README and rewrites the changeset for users; the evidence permalink above remains available at its original commit. `pnpm check`, all 374 mobile unit tests and an independent review pass for this follow-up. title: chore(deps-dev): bump @modelcontextprotocol/client from 2.2.0 to 2.3.0 in /packages/e2e
body:
Bumps [@modelcontextprotocol/client](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) from 2.2.0 to 2.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​modelcontextprotocol/client's releases.

@​modelcontextprotocol/client@​2.3.0

Minor Changes

  • #2901 433eb41 Thanks @​claude! - The HTTP client transports and the OAuth client helpers now follow a redirect only when it stays within the origin of the request (same scheme, host and port, or http to https on the same host with default ports) and keeps the method (a 307 or 308, or any redirect of a GET). Any other redirect is not followed. A transport then fails the request with an error that names the target; the session is kept and later messages still send. OAuth metadata discovery moves on to the next well-known URL, and any other OAuth request fails with an error that gives the status. Same-origin redirects that keep the method keep working on Node, up to five in a row, and no code changes are needed there. If your endpoint redirects to another origin, configure the transport with the URL it redirects to. A requestInit.redirect of 'error' or 'manual' is passed to fetch as it is for the requests a transport sends to the server (POST, GET and DELETE of the Streamable HTTP transport, POST of the SSE transport); for its OAuth requests, and for any other value, requestInit.redirect is not consulted by default. Browsers do not expose the target of a redirect to a page, so there a redirected request fails instead of being followed. Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport leaves its redirects to the fetch implementation, as before this change.

Patch Changes

  • #2599 5238fba Thanks @​freya0926! - A server can now serve, and a client can now call, tasks/get and tasks/cancel of the Tasks extension (SEP-2663) on a 2026-07-28 connection, when the handler is registered and the request is sent with an explicit schema. Every other method that a protocol revision removed is still refused. If one server factory serves both eras and such a handler is meant for 2025-era clients only, register it only when ctx.era === 'legacy'.

  • #2846 63c0fca Thanks @​Sthreal! - Receiving a large message as a single SSE event over Streamable HTTP, such as a tool result of tens of megabytes, is now fast: a 50 MB result that took about 13 seconds arrives in under a second. The client now requires eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later. SSEClientTransport reads through the eventsource package and gets the same speed-up once that also resolves eventsource-parser 3.0.8 or later.

  • #2908 633dd3e Thanks @​claude! - The license field of the package manifests is now Apache-2.0; the LICENSE file shipped in each package carries the full terms, including the MIT text for earlier contributions. No code change.

  • #2903 e765b3b Thanks @​claude! - With versionNegotiation in 'auto' or pin mode, a server/discover probe answered with a 2xx that carries no usable reply (a body that is not JSON under application/json, a bare 204, a missing or unaccepted content type) still rejects connect() with EraNegotiationFailed; an empty SSE stream or a 202 surfaces as the probe timeout instead. The message now says the server answered with an unusable reply (...) instead of reading like a network failure. To connect to a 2025 server behind a front that answers the probe this way, pass connect(transport, { prior: { kind: 'legacy' } }) or use mode: 'legacy'.

  • #2905 c0cd01a Thanks @​claude! - SSEClientTransport now retries the SSE connection once after onUnauthorized() resolves, as documented. If the retry is also answered with 401, start() rejects with SdkHttpError (ClientHttpAuthentication) instead of calling onUnauthorized() again. A 401 on a later reconnect of a stream that had opened still gets one refresh.

title: Mobile transition refresh can tap another control through a recycled native ref
body:
### What happened

After restarting an iOS app, screen.getByLabel("NameOfBottomTab").tap() resolved the intended button, but the driver tapped ("DifferentBottomTab") at x=265, y=800. The tap step passed; the next chat-control lookup failed with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND.

The unsafe path is AgentDeviceSurface.relocated(): it takes a new snapshot, refind() requires the same role/name/text/testId, and a failed match returns the old binding. Native references are snapshot-local: the old reference can now identify a different control. A native button becoming a tab after its parent hierarchy changes is enough to lose the match.

Expected: report retryable NODE_STALE before dispatching input, so the existing locator loop resolves the original selector again within its action timeout. Never send a stale ref after a failed relocation.

This is independent of selector choice. A test ID does not bypass refind()'s role comparison or the stale-binding fallback.

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
Deterministic engine reproduction, using the existing packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts fake-client harness:

1. Mark an action so the next new control requires a transition refresh.
2. Observe Chat as a button with native ref @e11.
3. Make the next capture return a tab-bar containing Chat at @e12 and Orders at @e11.
4. Perform a deterministic tap on the previously observed Chat node.

Current main sends interactions.press({ref: "@e11"}), which now targets Orders. Expected: retryable NODE_STALE, zero dispatched input. Resolve Chat again and the only tap should use @e12.

The proposed PR includes this regression and covers a target disappearing entirely. Both fail on main.
```

### Versions

e2e 0.21.2; @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.3; agent-device 0.21.28; Node 24.22.0; iOS 27.0 simulator. Also reproduced with deterministic tests against upstream main d7c6b5e.

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

### Anything else

Fix branch: https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/codex/mobile-stale-transition-ref

Verification: both deterministic regressions fail on main d7c6b5e and pass with the fix. All 344 mobile unit tests and pnpm check pass. Three independent, concurrent iOS consumer chat runs passed 15/15 checkpoints with zero test retries using an equivalent patch to published mobile 0.12.3.

The live timing remains intermittent: an unpatched follow-up run and a ten-restart probe also passed. We did not capture the fallback firing during those follow-ups; the engine regression reproduces the unsafe reference reuse deterministically.

title: fix(mobile): reject stale refs after transition refresh
body:
## What and why

- After a transition wait, a test action re-finds its control in a fresh snapshot. When that snapshot no longer lists the control, main sent the old binding anyway, so a recycled native ref could tap another control.
- Now `relocated()` throws retryable `NODE_STALE` before any input (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`, `relocated()`), and the locator resolves the selector again within its timeout (`performUntil` re-resolves on retryable `NODE_STALE`).
- Merged with main after #1297 (keyboard transitions) and #1410 (input revalidation): the input path keeps #1410's stricter checks and message; the new throw covers every other action.
- Related: #1413 pins refs to their snapshot generation; it overlaps in `relocated()` and should keep this throw when it merges after this PR.

## Issue

Closes #1299.

## Verified

Ran it locally: no device run. Unit evidence on the head merged with main:

- Restoring main's `found === undefined ? entry : ...` fallback fails both regressions: "acts on a control that came with the last action where a fresh snapshot lists it once the budget has passed" and "does not tap a recycled ref when a native button becomes a tab during relocation".
- `pnpm check` and all 413 mobile unit tests pass.

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target absent after refresh | Dispatches stale binding | `NODE_STALE`, no input |
| Old ref reused by another control | Taps the wrong control | Locator resolves the intended control again |

title: Question: Should new black-box UI tests use one persistent e2e MCP session before running the final test?
body:
### Problem

Hi, I would like to clarify the intended authoring workflow for a new black-box mobile UI test.

The bundled `e2e` skill currently says to learn the screens before writing a test by reading the source, running headed, or using an `e2e mcp` live session. It then says to write the test, run it, inspect the trace, fix it, and repeat.

In my case:

- The target was an Android app whose UI source was not available.
- The project already had the `e2e` MCP server registered.
- The requested flow crossed several previously unknown screens.
- The coding agent wrote part of the final test, ran the full test from `app.open()`, inspected the trace, added the next screen, and repeated.
- This resulted in many complete device runs. Each run correctly started from a fresh app state, so the authoring process became very slow.
- Replay cache hits avoided model calls, but they did not restore the app to an intermediate screen.

The MCP documentation appears to support a more efficient workflow:

1. Open one persistent live session.
2. Walk through the complete requested flow.
3. Use `observe` and `locate` to validate all intended locators.
4. Write the final test after the requested path is understood.
5. Run the final test from a fresh state for verification.

I am not suggesting that normal test runs should resume from an intermediate app state. Fresh state and test isolation are desirable for final verification.

My questions are:

1. For a new black-box UI flow, is the intended design to prefer one persistent `e2e mcp` discovery session before writing and running the final test?
2. Is repeatedly modifying and rerunning the full test considered an expected authoring workflow?
3. Was the choice between source inspection, headed runs, and MCP intentionally left entirely to the coding agent?
4. Should the bundled skill include a conditional rule such as:

   > When the requested black-box UI path is not already known and an e2e MCP server is available, first map the complete requested path in one live session and validate the locators before editing the final test.

5. If this is not the intended workflow, what is the recommended way to author this kind of mobile test efficiently?

This question is specifically about the bundled skill and authoring workflow, not about adding checkpoint/resume behavior to the runner.

title: fix(mobile): start the iOS keyboard-dismissing drag clear of controls
body: On an iPhone, the keyboard has no dismiss key, so `device.dismissKeyboard()` sends it away with a short drag. That drag started at the exact centre of the screen and travelled 3% of the screen width, which is still within touch slop. If a control sat at the centre, the drag pressed it. In the user report it selected a different filter button; in the benchmark repro below it checks a checkbox. When a control took the touch, the keyboard also stayed up, because the scroll view never got the tap. Fixes ENG-910. - Each drag now starts at the point nearest the centre that no control covers, with 8 pt of clearance (`packages/mobile/src/keyboard.ts`). - When the screen has a scroll view, the start must be inside one: a scroll view is what turns the drag into a dismissal, and a drag anywhere else does nothing. - A control is a node with a control role (bars included), or a leaf that isn't plain content. A React Native `Pressable` with no role shows up as an unnamed leaf, while text and images don't count. - A leaf over half the screen counts as a flattened tree's merged content, not a control. Those screens drag at the centre as before, and the committed iOS recording for Flattened Registration Form depends on that. - The start point is picked again from the latest capture before each drag (horizontal, then vertical). - A screen with no clear point fails with the existing `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` instead of touching a control. - New benchmark test on Choice Controls (`apps/mobile-benchmark/tests/device.e2e.ts`): it sets a valid order, fills the notes field, dismisses the keyboard, and places the order. A toggled control would leave Place order disabled. Known gaps, written up in the JSDoc: a `Text` with its own `onPress` reads as plain text, and a control inside a flattened tree can't be seen. Both get the same drag main makes today. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - mobile benchmark on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5), `e2e run tests/device.e2e.ts --target ios-simulator --grep "choice controls" --video` - main: both drags start at (201, 437), on the Mushrooms checkbox. It gets checked, the keyboard stays up, and the test fails: ```text × dismissing the keyboard over choice controls leaves them as they were 25.91s UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: keyboard dismissal failed: the keyboard has no dismiss key and stayed up through a horizontal and a vertical drag at the centre of the screen. ``` - this branch: one horizontal drag from (201, 517), in the gap between "Rush delivery" and its switch, dismisses the keyboard and changes no control: ```text ✓ dismissing the keyboard over choice controls leaves them as they were 16.88s ``` - whole iOS deterministic suite on this branch: `Tests 56 passed | 1 skipped (57)`, including Sequential Onboarding's dismissals - iOS agent replay, `--config e2e.agent.config.ts --grep "Flattened Registration Form"`: `replayed all 11 recorded actions, no model call`, `dismissKeyboard` included. The run had no model key, so only the judgment afterwards couldn't run. - the start point on every committed golden snapshot (iOS and Android): flattened screens and text-heavy scroll views start at the centre as before, Choice Controls steers clear of its checkbox, and the benchmark home list (all rows) is refused - Android not run: it presses the keyboard's own dismiss key and never reaches this path | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | ![main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05c24445-9c05-4b1a-8165-0afc058f9de1) | ![fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5643665-1b7e-4b12-941d-5df178021a03) | The videos below show main first, then this branch. --- Changes made by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fcc3f62-05f9-424d-bdb8-584be75b1ef3 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c243f156-3493-4e5c-881c-fd9c1802d759

title: fix(e2e): honor cleanup grace when retiring workers
body: - Workers retiring after a run unit or draining at run end were killed after 10 seconds, even when `cleanupTimeout` allowed longer. A late disposal error could disappear and leave the run successful. - Use the existing `forceGraceMs` (`cleanupTimeout` plus the runner's 1-second margin) for both shutdown paths. Keep forced termination bounded. - Add scheduler regressions for retirement, final drain, late cleanup errors, and a shorter shutdown grace, plus an `e2e` patch changeset. This restores the cleanup budget already documented in the config and engine references. - Split from #1223 as requested in https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1223#issuecomment-6295762226. No eval code or authoring guidance changes. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Retire or drain worker] --> B[Dispose within cleanupTimeout] B --> C{Worker exits within forceGraceMs?} C -- yes --> D[Preserve cleanup errors] C -- no --> E[Kill worker] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built the packages on main `d7c6b5e5` and this branch, then ran the same standalone `e2e run` probe with a custom engine whose `dispose` waits 12 seconds. No model calls. The table compares final-drain behavior; scheduler unit tests separately cover retirement. | Probe | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | 12-second disposal, 30-second cleanup budget | Hook killed before completion; exit 0 | Hook completes; exit 0 | | Same disposal, then throw `controlled disposal failure` | Error lost; exit 0 | `ENGINE_FAILURE` in cleanup; exit 3 | | 12-second disposal, 7-second cleanup budget | `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT`; exit 3 | `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT`; exit 3 | | Four scheduler disposal regressions | 4 fail | 4 pass | The fixed CLI reports the late error: ```text ERROR infrastructure error ENGINE_FAILURE (cleanup) controlled disposal failure Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) Errors 1 error ``` - Deterministic Chromium validation used the built CLI through the testbed (79 passed, 1 skipped) and web benchmark (91 passed). Full repository checks and a fresh-context independent code review also passed. Native device behavior was not exercised locally.

title: feat(browserstack): add @e2e-dev/browserstack device provider
body: Refs #1404 ## What and why - New `@e2e-dev/browserstack`: `browserstack({ device, osVersion, app })` leases BrowserStack App Automate real Android and iOS devices for `@e2e-dev/mobile`, one isolated agent-device daemon per worker slot, the same shape as `@e2e-dev/testmu`. - agent-device ships BrowserStack in core (`leaseProvider: 'browserstack'`), so there is no plugin to install. - The lease plumbing testmu and browserstack shared (daemon per slot, heartbeat, `daemon stop`, acquire/release) now lives in `@e2e-dev/mobile/lease` as `agentDeviceLeases()`, run on mobile's own agent-device. Both providers use it and peer `@e2e-dev/mobile >=0.12.5`. The device-cloud example in `docs/mobile.mdx` uses it too. - BrowserStack's `app` capability takes only an uploaded app (`bs://`, `custom_id`, `shareable_id`); a public URL fails session creation with `BROWSERSTACK_INVALID_APP_URL`, which agent-device surfaces as `WebDriver create-session response missed sessionId`. An `https` `app` is therefore uploaded once per run through `POST /app-automate/upload` (`url=`) and its `bs://` id shared by every slot (`packages/browserstack/src/provider.ts`, `uploadAppFromUrl` in `src/sessions.ts`). - Release is strict: `daemon stop` must report `providerReleases.status: 'completed'` with nothing pending. A forced stop or a lost shutdown report (`status: 'unknown'`, `pending: null`) fails the release and keeps the lease and its state for diagnosis instead of treating a possibly billed session as ended, and a granted lease needs its id listed under `released`, so a retry that finds no daemon still fails (`assertSessionsEnded` in `packages/mobile/src/lease/daemon.ts`). `@e2e-dev/testmu` now gets the same strict release. - An `https` app URL never reaches logs or errors: the upload notice names only the `bs://` id, API errors redact the URL and its query before truncation, and a transport error keeps only a redacted cause. - `record` links BrowserStack's session video, found by build name (every build of that name, since projects can share one), then session name, with `video_url` read again at `stop`. - Options mirror the agent-device BrowserStack flags: orientation, geoLocation, timezone, language, locale, appiumVersion, networkProfile / customNetwork (mutually exclusive), and iOS-only `noResignApp`. ```ts mobile({ platform: 'android', device: browserstack({ device: 'Google Pixel 7', osVersion: '13.0', app: apk, appiumVersion: '3.2.0' }), }) ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Docs example, live on BrowserStack App Automate: `e2e run` with `docs/examples/mobile/browserstack.config.ts` and `browserstack.e2e.ts` (WikipediaSample.apk by URL, Google Pixel 7 / Android 13.0): ``` ℹ browserstack (1 of 1): uploaded the app URL as bs://… ℹ browserstack (1 of 1): lease …: Google Pixel 7, android 13.0; session e2e-…-pixel-7-1 reserved ✓ mobile engine for target "pixel-7" prepared 19.98s ✓ |pixel-7| tests/home.e2e.ts (1 test) 2.23s ℹ browserstack: released 1 device(s) ``` - A production app (`bs://` id, Google Pixel 9 / Android 16.0): open, assert a banner, tap, assert it is gone; passed in 10.4 s, device released. - `findSession` against the live API found that session by build and name and returned its video URL. - The WikipediaSample shows an old-target-SDK dialog on Android 16, so the example pins Android 13.0. Maintainer takeover (squashed and rebased on main): the shared lease helper, strict release for testmu, and fixes from review (a throwing log no longer leaks a granted lease, the service env can't override `AGENT_DEVICE_*`, signed URL out of error causes, same-named builds across projects). `pnpm check` passes; unit tests: mobile 476, testmu 87, browserstack 53. No live BrowserStack or TestMu run after the refactor. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: n/a. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/integrations/browserstack.mdx`, `docs/integrations/testmu.mdx`, index card, `mobile.mdx`, `reference/environment.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. - [ ] Contract change: n/a. - [ ] Engine contract change: n/a. Logos: Devicon 2.16.0 (MIT) `browserstack-plain.svg` for the sidebar and `browserstack-original.svg` for the card; Simple Icons has no BrowserStack mark. Happy to swap in BrowserStack's official files.

title: docs(skills): fix a failed test from its trace page instead of walking the flow again
body: After a red run, a coding agent tends to open an MCP session and click through the whole flow again to look at the screen that failed, then fix one line and rerun. The run already recorded that screen. The skill now tells the agent to fix from what the run printed and wrote, and to check the lines after the failing step before it reruns. ## What changed - `skills/e2e/SKILL.md`: a new "Workflow: fixing a failed test" section after "Workflow: writing a test", whose step 5 now points to it. 1. Read the terminal's failure block (code frame, `expected`/`observed`, `❯ at`, `❯ on screen`) and the trace page it names (`❯ trace`, `## Screen at failure`). 2. Fix every line that evidence covers, not only the failing one. 3. A test stops at its first failed step, so check the lines after it before rerunning: against the screen at failure, the app source, or a live session. 4. For a screen the evidence and the source leave out, go straight to it in a session: on the web, `navigate` to the path of the `❯ at` URL or the screen's route. On a device, take the shortest path from launch. Never walk the flow from the start. 5. Rerun. - `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md`, "Read the failure": item 1 names the terminal markers. A new item 2 holds the same rule and says what each field means for the fix. Items 3 to 5 are renumbered. - `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`, workflow step 4: fix from the evidence, and go straight to a screen it leaves out. - `docs/coding-agents.mdx`, "How an agent reads a failure": two short paragraphs that say the same for readers (242 to 250 lines, 917 to 994 prose words). - A `.changeset` entry, `e2e: patch`, because the skill ships in the package. The field names come from what the CLI prints today: `❯ at`, `❯ on screen`, and `❯ trace` (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts:1035-1040`), plus `## Screen at failure` and `Closest to what the locator asked for:` (`packages/e2e/src/report/failure-text.ts:555-569`). ## Decisions - The rule lives in `SKILL.md`, not only in `debugging.md`. In the main baselines, the agent fixing the seeded test opened `writing-tests.md` (the routing table sends "Writing or fixing a test" there) and never opened `debugging.md`. `SKILL.md` is the one file every agent reads. `debugging.md` repeats the rule because `npx e2e guide debugging` has to stand on its own. - The skill says to navigate to the path of the `❯ at` URL. With a port-0 app URL, the run's port is gone by the time a session opens. - I didn't touch the cache, timeout, or session-closing guidance; other PRs own it. Step 5 says "topic `mcp` says when a session must close first" and doesn't restate the rule, so a change to that rule won't conflict with this PR. - `docs/debugging.mdx` is unchanged. It has no section for coding agents. - I left the routing table alone to keep merges with the other skill PRs small. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js guide` and `guide debugging` print the new text. `pnpm pack` of `packages/e2e` ships it in `skills/e2e/` and `docs/coding-agents.mdx`. - The docs page renders in `mint dev`: ![coding-agents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2484efe-a294-4b32-9b07-1b6208743403) ### A/B harness I used the skill A/B harness: a fresh OpenCode agent (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`) with the e2e skill and MCP server, in a scratch testbed project. - `fix-journey` seeds a test with three mistakes: a wrong label on `/forms`, a wrong button on step 1 of `/wizard`, and a wrong summary text. Each run surfaces only the next one. - `fix-journey-no-source` is the same task plus "don't read files outside this project". The agent then can't grep the app's HTML, which a large app's source wouldn't allow either. - `main-fix-*` are the shared baselines. `b-main-fixnosrc-*` ran the base commit's skill. `b-*-1,2` ran this PR's first wording, `3,4` the second, and `5,6` the final one. - "e2e cmds" is the harness count of commands that contain `e2e run`. In four arms, one of those was a BSD `sed -i` that failed before `&&`, so the run never started. "runs" counts the ones that executed. | Run | Wall min | e2e cmds | runs | Sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | main-fix-1 | 1.7 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 12 | 0.10 | 0 | | main-fix-2 | 1.1 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 11 | 0.06 | 0 | | b-fix-1 | 1.0 | 3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 11 | 0.10 | 0 | | b-fix-2 | 0.9 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 12 | 9 | 0.09 | 0 | | b-fix-3 | 1.2 | 3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 15 | 11 | 0.11 | 0 | | b-fix-4 | 1.0 | 3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 11 | 0.10 | 0 | | b-fix-5 | 1.0 | 3 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 10 | 0.09 | 0 | | b-fix-6 | 1.1 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 11 | 0.11 | 0 | | b-main-fixnosrc-1 | 1.6 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 7 | 0.08 | 0 | | b-main-fixnosrc-2 | 1.5 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 6 | 0.08 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-1 | 1.6 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 10 | 0.09 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-2 | 1.6 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 7 | 0.09 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-3 | 1.7 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 8 | 18 | 15 | 0.13 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-4 | 1.5 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 7 | 0.08 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-5 | 1.6 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 8 | 18 | 14 | 0.12 | 0 | | b-fixnosrc-6 | 1.5 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 10 | 0.09 | 0 | What the agents did, from `events.jsonl`: - On `fix-journey`, all six branch arms read `## Screen at failure` after the first red run. Then they read the app source for the screens past it and fixed all three lines before the second run, which passed. They said why, in their own words: "Let me check the app source for the remaining screens, so I can fix everything in one pass" (b-fix-1), "check the wizard page, which the failure screen doesn't cover" (b-fix-4). On main, one of two arms did that (main-fix-2). The other fixed one line per run and needed 4 runs. - On `fix-journey-no-source`, both main arms and both first-wording arms fixed one line per run, from each run's screen at failure, and opened no session. The first wording said to look live "only when none of that shows what a line needs", and the agents read that as only the failing line. With the later wording, 2 of 4 arms (b-fixnosrc-3 and -5) opened a session after the second run failed on `/wizard`. They called `navigate {url: "/wizard"}` directly, with no sign-in and no `/forms`. Then they tapped through the wizard's two inner steps, which have no URL, and fixed the button and the summary text before the next run, which passed. - No arm walked the flow from the start. Every arm passed in the end. - Wall time didn't move. On this app, a failing run costs 30 s on a wrong locator or 6 s on a wrong assertion, about what the session walk costs. Fewer runs, and fixes per run, are the behavior change. This doesn't show a speedup on a large app, where a rerun costs more and the agent can't read the source.

title: feat(cli): add --action-timeout and --assertion-timeout to e2e run
body: Adds `--action-timeout ` and `--assertion-timeout ` to `e2e run`, so a test you're still writing fails in a few seconds instead of waiting out the 30 s action timeout. ```bash npx e2e run tests/signup.e2e.ts --action-timeout 5000 ``` - Each flag replaces the config's `actionTimeout` or `assertionTimeout` for one run. They go into the same `CliOverrides` as `--retries` (`packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts`), so a child-process worker that resolves the config again gets them through its bootstrap (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts:159`). - A call's own `{ timeout }` still wins, as in Playwright. The code already does this: `timeoutMs ?? this.options.actionTimeout` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts:119`), `timeout ?? engine.assertionTimeout` (`packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts:172`, `expect/poll.ts:92`), `timeout ?? environment.config.actionTimeout` (`run/fixture-recording.ts:80`). The integration test covers it, and the docs now say it. - Validation: the parser takes an integer 1-2147483647, the `--max-duration` bounds. Anything else is a usage error, exit 2. `resolveConfig` checks again for the `run()` path with `timerMs`, which returns `INVALID_CONFIG`, also exit 2. - Watch mode keeps the flags on every rerun, since `planRun` spreads the base options (`packages/e2e/src/cli/watch.ts:57`). - Docs: rows in `docs/reference/cli.mdx`, override and precedence bullets under `actionTimeout` and `assertionTimeout` in `docs/reference/config.mdx`, the flag row in `skills/e2e/references/running.md`, and an authoring tip in the Tools table of `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md`. ## Decisions - **Not on `e2e explore` or `e2e mcp`.** `e2e explore --timeout` is the exploration's wall clock (180000-900000, `explore/index.ts:33`), not the config's `timeout`, and an exploration has no test lines to fail fast on. An MCP session's actions target node ids from the last `observe`, so they don't wait out the action timeout the way a wrong locator does. `e2e run` still has no `--timeout`. The new names follow `--max-duration` -> `maxDuration`: config key in kebab case. - **The config value is still checked when a flag replaces it.** `--retries` short-circuits (`boundedInt(cli) ?? boundedInt(raw)`), so `retries: 99` passes while `--retries 1` is given. Here `actionTimeout: '30s'` fails with or without the flag. - **Upper bound.** A fresh-context review caught that `setTimeout` fires after 1 ms for anything above 2147483647. Without the bound, a fixture call such as `browser.evaluate` or `session.save()` would fail almost at once under `--action-timeout 999999999999`. The flags now stop at the timer maximum. The config keys (`actionTimeout`, `assertionTimeout`, and `timeout`, `launchTimeout`, `cleanupTimeout`) already had this gap. I left them alone so this PR doesn't change what configs are accepted. - **No wire change.** `report.json` records no timeouts. The config digest covers the config file only, so a flag can't trip the worker's digest check. The replay cache key doesn't include the digest, so recordings stay valid under the flags. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Built CLI on the A/B harness scratch project (`run-arm.mjs --setup-only --seed seeds/fix-journey`). The seeded test has a wrong label on `/forms`. Main is the base commit's build (`t3-6e7ffaee`, `d7c6b5e5`). | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `e2e run` (wrong label) | fails at `getByLabel("Name")` after **30.46 s**, process 31.2 s | same, 30.48 s | | `e2e run --action-timeout 3000` | `error: unknown option '--action-timeout'`, exit 2 | fails at the same line after **3.37 s**, process 4.2 s, same nearest nodes and trace page | | fixed test, `--action-timeout 3000 --assertion-timeout 2000` | - | passes, 681 ms | | wrong summary text, `e2e run` | 5.73 s | 5.73 s | | wrong summary text, `--assertion-timeout 1000` | unknown option | `ASSERTION_FAILED` after 1.76 s | ```console $ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --action-timeout 3000 ✓ target "web" command ready 87ms ❯ |web| tests/journey.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 failed) 3.37s × an admin signs in, saves a profile, and creates a workspace 3.37s → locator matched no nodes within getByLabel("Name") ... ❯ tests/journey.e2e.ts:14:3 ❯ on screen #n12032 textbox "Full name" purpose=username ❯ trace .e2e/results/journey-an-admin-signs-in-saves-a-d41c531a416735aa/trace.md $ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --action-timeout 0 error: option '--action-timeout ' argument '0' is invalid. must be an integer from 1 through 2147483647 $ echo $? 2 ``` - Testbed default suite on a port-0 copy of its config (another run held port 4271), `--action-timeout 5000 --assertion-timeout 5000`: 15 files, 79 passed, 1 skipped, 18.0 s. Without the flags: the same results, 17.1 s. - The new integration test (`tests/integration/cli-run.test.ts`) runs the built CLI on the fake engine with 30 s timeouts in the config. With the runner line that forwards `--action-timeout` deleted, the wrong-locator step takes 30,023 ms and the test fails. With it, the step takes about 400 ms. ### A/B, fix task (n=2, sanity check) `run-arm.mjs --task tasks/fix-journey.md --seed seeds/fix-journey`, Sonnet 5.5, main's skill against this branch's. | Run | Wall min | e2e runs | Sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | main-fix-1 | 1.7 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 12 | 0.10 | 0 | | main-fix-2 | 1.1 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 11 | 0.06 | 0 | | f3-fix-1 | 1.6 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 8 | 0.12 | 0 | | f3-fix-2 | 1.0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 11 | 9 | 0.12 | 0 | - Both branch agents read `references/debugging.md` before their first run. Neither used the flag on that run, so both paid the 30 s timeout once. - f3-fix-1 had two 30 s runs, then ran `npx e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts --action-timeout 5000` for the third. That run hit the assertion mistake, so it took 5.7 s whatever the flag. - f3-fix-2 read the app's source through the server path in `e2e.config.ts` and fixed all three mistakes after one run. - Nothing here shows a speedup. It shows the tip gets read and picked up, late. Putting it in `SKILL.md`'s run step might get it onto the first run, but that line belongs to the rerun-loop PR in this batch, so I kept to `debugging.md`.

title: docs(skills): start each test near the screen it covers
body:
Every run of a test, and every rerun while a coding agent fixes one line, walks through everything before the screen under test. This tells the agent to keep that part short.

- `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`: a new section, "Start near the screen under test", added to `## Contents`:
  - sign in once in a `test.setup` and declare `session`. Sessions last one run, so the setup still runs every run, once per target for the selected tests that need it
  - `app.open('/path')` straight to the screen. `observe` over MCP prints the path
  - seed data through the app's API in a `test.extend` fixture that sends `browser.cookies()` (when the app signs in with a cookie) and parses the response with `toMatchSchema`, so a failed seed fails in the fixture, not 30 s later on a locator. Over MCP, a project tool does the same
  - on a device there are no sessions. `device.openLink` opens a deep link
  - grow a long test one screen at a time when its steps were not checked live. Verified `agent.act` steps replay from the cache, which keeps them across a later failure. That holds for a first attempt with a read-write cache, so grow outside `CI` and with `--retries 0`. Keep the title, goals, and params (`unique()` for run-unique data) unchanged so the keys still match
- `skills/e2e/SKILL.md` workflow step 3: one sentence that points there.
- `docs/core-concepts.mdx`, "Organize tests": the first bullet says the same briefly and replaces "Prepare its data in fixtures or hooks."
- Changeset: `e2e` patch, since the skill ships in the package.

The claims rest on:

- one setup unit per target and setup test: `packages/e2e/src/run/units.ts:60`. Setups run only for sessions a selected test needs: `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts:499`
- the session is restored at launch, before fixtures exist: `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:630` and `:1014`
- the cache keeps entries a check confirmed before a failure: `settleStagedTraces`, `packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts:188`

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js guide writing-tests` prints the new section.
- The skill's fixture example, run in a scratch project against the testbed app with a small `/api/projects` endpoint added that requires the session cookie and JSON. The setup signed in, the fixture seeded, the test opened the deep link, and the teardown deleted the project:

  ```text
   ✓ |web| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test) 581ms
   ✓ |web| tests/example.e2e.ts (1 test) 203ms
  .e2e/logs/app.log: seeded project 411, deleted project 411
  ```

  Without `session`, the same test fails at the fixture line in 134 ms:

  ```text
     × renames a project 134ms
  ASSERTION_FAILED: expected {"error":"signed out"} to match the schema:
  - id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined
  ```

  The example also typechecks with and without the DOM lib.
- One setup for three dependent tests, and selecting one dependent by `file:line` still runs its setup:

  ```text
   ✓ |web| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test) 304ms
   ✓ |web| tests/near.e2e.ts (4 tests) 320ms

  $ e2e run tests/near.e2e.ts:19
   ✓ |web| tests/auth.setup.e2e.ts (1 test) 328ms
   ✓ |web| tests/near.e2e.ts (1 test) 275ms
  ```

- Not verified live: the cache claim behind "grow one screen at a time". No model key on this machine, so it rests on `settleStagedTraces` and `tests/integration/agent-trace-cache.test.ts`.
- The docs bullet, rendered with `mint dev` (`pnpm docs:check` and `scripts/check-docs-anchors.ts` pass):

  ![Organize tests bullet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc36c3ea-485e-4aa5-ae91-5f3202751e57)

### Skill A/B

A fresh OpenCode agent (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`) with the e2e MCP server authors tests in a scratch copy of the testbed app, once with main's skill and once with this branch's. n=2 per arm, so this is a sanity check, not a benchmark.

`author-journey` asks for one test covering sign-in, the profile form, and the workspace wizard. `author-signed-in` is a task I added: the same three flows, framed as things a signed-in admin does, with no "one test" constraint.

| Run | Skill | Task | Wall min | e2e runs | MCP sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit | What it wrote |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| main-author-1 | main | journey | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 19 | 26 | 17 | 0.16 | 0 | one test: sign-in form, then `app.open('/forms')`, `app.open('/wizard')` |
| main-author-2 | main | journey | 0.9 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 23 | 14 | 0.14 | 0 | same |
| e-author-journey-1 | branch | journey | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 24 | 16 | 0.20 | 0 | same |
| e-author-journey-2 | branch | journey | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 23 | 16 | 0.19 | 0 | same |
| e-main-author-signed-in-1 | main | signed-in | 1.0 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 26 | 14 | 0.20 | 0 | `test.setup` + `session: 'admin'`, three tests opened by path |
| e-main-author-signed-in-2 | main | signed-in | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 23 | 16 | 0.18 | 0 | same |
| e-author-signed-in-1 | branch | signed-in | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 24 | 15 | 0.21 | 0 | same |
| e-author-signed-in-2 | branch | signed-in | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 26 | 14 | 0.20 | 0 | same |

- No behavior change on this app, and no regression. Every agent on either skill already opened `/forms` and `/wizard` by path and passed on its first run.
- On `author-journey` both branch agents read the new section (`read references/writing-tests.md` in both event streams) and still kept the sign-in form inside the one test, since the task asks for one test that includes the sign-in.
- On `author-signed-in`, main's skill already leads to a setup test and a session, from the existing "Sign-in sessions" section. The branch writes the same files.
- The branch journey arms cost $0.19-0.20 against $0.14-0.16 for the older main baselines. The main arms run next to the branch on the second task cost $0.18-0.20, so I read that as run-to-run variance, not the skill.
- The testbed has no API to seed and the harness config has no model for `agent.act`, so the seeding and growing advice is not exercised. It pays off on a large app where the screen under test sits deep in a flow, which this harness cannot show.

## Decisions

- The docs bullet goes in `core-concepts.mdx` "Organize tests", not `coding-agents.mdx`: the advice holds for anyone who structures tests, and that section's example already starts with `app.open('/billing')`. The example in `coding-agents.mdx` ("How an agent writes and runs a test") still signs in inside the test. I left it alone.
- "Keep the title and goals unchanged while the test grows" is close to what the fast-rerun-loop PR in this batch says. It stays here because growing a test pays off only while the earlier keys hold.
- A fresh-context review ran twice. Fixed from it: the cache key sentence now names params and `unique()`; the fixture example sends a JSON content type and the session's cookies and checks the response; the web-only advice in `SKILL.md`, `core-concepts.mdx`, and the changeset now names the device path; the cookie line is limited to apps that sign in with a cookie; the "pays only for its new part" claim names the retry and `CI` exceptions.
- Shortening pass on `core-concepts.mdx`: the edited bullet replaces one sentence, and nothing else on the page says it. 230 to 234 lines, 719 to 756 prose words. No other cuts in "Organize tests".

title: docs(skills): write each test line while walking the flow over MCP
body:
The skill told the coding agent to learn the screens over `e2e mcp` first and write the test afterwards. Agents did exactly that: walk the whole flow, close the session, then write the file in one go from what they remember. Now the agent writes the test while it walks.

- `skills/e2e/SKILL.md`, "Workflow: writing a test", step 2: with a connected `e2e mcp` server, create the test file before `open_session`, opening on the screen it covers, then add each step to the file as you take it. An `act` goal goes in before you walk its path. A `screen` line is the `Test line:` its action printed (#1317), copied as is. When the outcome shows, `locate` it and add the `expect`. Without a server, the old fallback stays (read the components, a `--headed` run). Step 3 now opens with "A step is an `agent.act` goal or `screen` lines" and keeps #1311's "start the test on the screen it covers" sentence.
- `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`, "Workflow", steps 1 to 3:
  1. Create the file, `open_session`, go to the screen the test opens on (`navigate` on the web, the shortest path on a device). Actions that only got you there, such as a sign-in a saved session replaces, stay out of the test when the test's opening reaches that screen directly.
  2. Walk one screen at a time and write each screen's steps before you leave it. An `agent.act` goal is written before its path, and the path's actions and their test lines stay out. A `screen` line is the action's `Test line:`. `locate` comes in only when the action printed `No test line:`.
  3. Each outcome gets its check before the next step: an `expect` on a locator tried with `locate`, or an `agent.assert`. `test_lines` is the catch-up for a line you missed. The step ends with an example walk.
- Steps 4 and 5 are main's: #1309's "fix from the failure block and the trace page, go straight to a missing screen" and `close_session`. The "Workflow: fixing a failed test" section in `SKILL.md` is untouched.
- Which kind of line a step becomes (my call, kept within the skill's existing rules):
  - `agent.act` is the default, for a path that varies. Write the goal in the words on screen, with its values in `params`, before you walk its path.
  - A `screen` line is for an exact value or interaction: a sign-in form in a setup test, a field that must receive one specific string (SKILL.md's list), or an interaction that is the point of the test (`writing-tests`' empty submit).
- Take a screen's actions, then add the lines they printed in one edit, so writing as you walk costs a turn per screen, not a turn per line.
- The `e2e mcp` server instructions (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/server.ts:55`) said "Write deterministic tests (tests/*.e2e.ts) from what you saw", the opposite of the new skill, and every MCP client reads them. They now say "Write the test (tests/*.e2e.ts) while you walk the flow, adding each step to the file as you take it". #1317's sentence before it already says each action answers with its test line. `e2e mcp --help` lists `test_lines` and says "Each action prints the test line that repeats it, so the agent writes a test while it walks the real app." The opening sentence of `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` changed to "while they write tests".
- Docs: `docs/coding-agents.mdx` ("Let the agent use the app", "How an agent writes and runs a test") and `docs/mcp-server.mdx` (the "Write a test" row, the example prompt, #1317's "How it writes a test line", and the lede of "How it checks a locator", which is now about lines no action printed).
- `type_secret`'s row in mcp.md's catalog now says it prints a test line too, since a sign-in form is one of the `screen` cases.
- Not touched: failure reading, reruns, the cache, and session closing. One clause in an mcp.md Rules bullet changed, "the test is what you write afterwards" -> "the test is the file you write as you walk", because it contradicted the new workflow.

The walk from `mcp.md`:

```text
write   tests/members.e2e.ts: imports, test(...), app.open('/settings/members')
call    open_session, then navigate {url: "/settings/members"}   its line is the app.open already written
edit    + await agent.act('invite {email} as an editor', { params: { email: 'ada@example.test' } });
call    tap, type, select, tap                   the goal's path; its test lines stay out
call    locate {role: "status"}                  1 node matches, text "Invite sent"
edit    + await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Invite sent');
call    type {target: "n40", value: "ada"}       prints the test line below
        Test line: await screen.getByRole("searchbox", "Search members").fill("ada");
edit    + that line, as printed
call    locate {role: "listitem"}                1 node matches
edit    + await expect(screen.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(1);
```

## A/B: does a fresh agent follow it?

These runs predate the rebase onto #1317. The branch wording then had the agent `locate` every control before writing its line; it now copies the printed `Test line:` and calls `locate` only for assertions and controls with no line. The order of events (file first, write per screen) is what the A/B measured, and that part of the wording is unchanged. The `locate` counts below would drop with the current wording. I haven't rerun the harness.

The harness ran a fresh OpenCode agent (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`) on the "author one journey" task: sign in, a profile form, the workspace wizard on the testbed playground, with the e2e MCP server and the skill under test. The scratch config has no model, so every arm wrote `screen` lines only.

"Writes" means file writes before `open_session` / during the walk / after the last action.

| Run | Skill | Wall min | e2e runs | Sessions | MCP calls | `locate` | Writes | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main-author-1 | main | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 19 | 1 | 0/0/1 | 26 | 17 | 0.16 | 0 |
| main-author-2 | main | 0.9 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 0 | 0/0/1 | 23 | 14 | 0.14 | 0 |
| a-main-author-1 | main, rerun today | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 0 | 0/0/1 | 22 | 15 | 0.18 | 0 |
| a-main-author-2 | main, rerun today | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 0 | 0/0/1 | 25 | 13 | 0.19 | 0 |
| a-author-7 | this branch | 1.4 | 1 | 1 | 30 | 13 | 1/6/1 | 44 | 20 | 0.25 | 0 |
| a-author-8 | this branch | 1.3 | 1 | 1 | 31 | 14 | 1/6/1 | 46 | 23 | 0.27 | 0 |

- Order of events. All four main arms walk the whole flow, then write the file once at the end (`events.jsonl`: 15 to 17 `e2e_call`s, then one `write` just before or after `e2e_close_session`). Both branch arms write the skeleton before `open_session`. Then, on each screen, they `locate` its controls in one turn and add the lines in the same turn as the actions. They write 8 times in all, and the last edit adds the wizard's `expect` before `close_session`.
- Locators. The branch arms tried 13 to 14 locators with `locate` before writing them. Main tried 0 or 1 and wrote names from `observe`.
- Cost. On this small app, main's tests also pass on the first run, so the A/B shows no gain in correctness. It shows the price: 3 to 10 more model steps, $0.06 to $0.09 more, and 0.5 to 0.8 more minutes than today's main reruns. Most of the extra MCP calls were those `locate`s, which the printed test lines now replace. The benefit is meant for long flows and apps whose rendered names differ from what an agent would guess, and this harness can't show it. n=2 per arm, so read the numbers as a sanity check.
- Not exercised: the `agent.act` half of the walk (goal first, then walk its path), since the harness config has no model.

<details><summary>Earlier wordings of this PR, same task</summary>

| Run | Wording | Wall min | MCP calls | `locate` | Writes | Model steps | Cost $ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| a-author-1 | first draft, "write the step, then do it" | 0.9 | 19 | 2 | 0/0/1 | 17 | 0.25 |
| a-author-2 | first draft | 0.7 | 28 | 11 | 0/0/1 | 17 | 0.26 |
| a-author-3 | + "do not walk first", file before `open_session`, example | 0.9 | 31 | 14 | 1/3/1 | 18 | 0.24 |
| a-author-4 | same | 1.0 | 30 | 13 | 1/5/1 | 18 | 0.24 |
| a-author-5 | + server instructions | 1.0 | 33 | 15 | 1/7/1 | 23 | 0.28 |
| a-author-6 | same | 1.1 | 33 | 15 | 1/6/1 | 23 | 0.30 |

The first draft didn't change the order: both arms still walked first and wrote at the end. What changed the order was the explicit "do not walk the whole flow first", creating the file before `open_session`, and the example walk.
</details>

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, after rebasing onto main at `72abdddd` (with #1309, #1310, #1311, #1317). Web only.

After merging main again at `cfe76ba3` (with #1313 and #1314): `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` conflicted twice. The walk (steps 1 to 3 and the example) is this PR's; step 4 is #1314's "run only that test" by `file:line`; step 5 is #1313's "leave the session open". In Rules, "the test is the file you write as you walk" leads into #1313's rules for running beside a session, which replace the old `reuseExisting` line. `SKILL.md` merged without conflicts and reads as one workflow. Re-ran `pnpm check`, `pnpm plugins:check`, and `skill.test.ts` on the merge.

- Built package: `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js guide` and `guide mcp` print the merged steps, with #1309's fixing workflow and mcp.md step 4 intact. `e2e mcp --help`:

  ```text
  call runs the session's tools (observe, tap, type, press, select, scroll,
  navigate, type_secret, locate, test_lines, screenshot, and the project's own),
  tools describes them, close_session ends it. Each action prints the test line
  that repeats it, so the agent writes a test while it walks the real app.
  ```

- MCP server, the walk the skill describes, on the testbed's `/todos` (a port-0 copy of `apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts`, not committed). A real MCP client against the built `e2e mcp`. The instructions it gets end with "Write the test (tests/*.e2e.ts) while you walk the flow, adding each step to the file as you take it, and run it with the CLI". The actions print:

  ```text
  Navigated to /todos.
  Test line: await app.open("/todos");
  Typed into #n6028.
  Test line: await screen.getByRole("textbox", "New todo").fill("Buy milk");
  Tapped #n6029.
  Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Add").tap();
  1 node matches getByRole("listitem").
  Use: screen.getByRole("listitem")
  ```

  Those three lines copied as printed, plus an `expect` on the located `listitem`, pass `e2e run` on the first try:

  ```text
   ✓ |web| tests/pr1312-walk.e2e.ts (1 test) 224ms
     ✓ adds a todo 224ms
  ```

- Mobile: the device half of step 1 ("the shortest path from the launch screen") follows #1309's wording and the absence of `navigate` in `@e2e-dev/mobile`. Not run on a simulator or emulator.
- The A/B above ran before the rebase (see its note).
- Docs: rendered with `mint dev` after the rebase. Before -> after against main: `mcp-server.mdx` 137 -> 138 lines, 587 -> 607 prose words; `coding-agents.mdx` 264 -> 266 lines, 1055 -> 1076 words. Shortening pass on the touched sections: "and adds the assertions" left #1317's "How it writes a test line", since the next section covers assertions.

| `docs/mcp-server.mdx` table | `docs/mcp-server.mdx` lines and locators | `docs/coding-agents.mdx` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![mcp server table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1825619b-2412-4ee0-81a9-db69c3780ca7) | ![mcp server lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a035e9a-2cc2-406c-a808-3659b709e619) | ![coding agents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91a86046-826f-4013-999d-f599afdf6b85) |

## Review

Fresh-context review before the rebase, findings fixed:

- `open_session` opens the app's base URL, not the path `app.open` names, so the walk could start on another screen than the test. Step 1 and the example now `navigate` to the path first.
- mcp.md's `screen` list was wider than SKILL.md's, and the first example filled an invite form with `screen`, which `agent.md` writes as `agent.act` with params. The lists now match. The example's invite is an `act` goal with `params`, and a `screen` line comes from the exact string the count depends on.
- SKILL.md step 3 told agents without an MCP server to `locate`. The walk and `locate` now live only under step 2's MCP branch.
- The mcp.md opening line said the testing agent writes tests. Reworded.
- "Every locator has matched once" over-claimed, since `locate` can't try a `.filter()` chain. It now reads "every locator you copied from a `Test line:` or a `locate` result", and says the first run checks the rest.
- Each docs page said "writes while it walks" twice. Now it's once per page, and `coding-agents.mdx` says "with `e2e mcp`".

Fresh-context review after the rebase, fixed:

- The "Write a test" row said the agent copies a line from each action, but an `act` goal's path stays out. It now reads "Writes the test as it walks the flow, from checked test lines".
- `locate` was explained in both step 2 and step 3; it now lives in step 3, with the outcome it checks. Step 3 no longer says to `locate` an `agent.assert`.
- "Add each step as you take it" against "add a screen's lines in one edit": step 2 now says to write each screen's steps before you leave it.
- On a device, or a screen the test can't open directly, the steps that reach it are the test's first steps, not left out.
- The example's edits now carry `await`, like the copied line, and say that `navigate`'s line is the `app.open` already written.
- "checks each locator" (mcp.md opening, `coding-agents.mdx`) became "checks its locators", for the same `.filter()` reason.

Left for a follow-up (outside this PR's files, or #1317's code):

- `test_lines`' own description and footer (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/test-lines.ts:191`, `:209`) say "Paste it into a test", which reads as pasting the whole draft, act goals' paths included.
- `skills/e2e/references/bug-bash.md` (regression tests), `skills/migrate-to-e2e/SKILL.md:167`, and the generated verification-skill example still say to `locate` each locator before writing it. They could point at the printed test lines instead.

title: docs(skills): keep the MCP session open between test runs
body: Today `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` tells the agent to close the MCP session before every `e2e run` unless the app command sets `reuseExisting`. So after a red run, the agent opens a new session to see the failing screen. Since #1309 it goes straight to that screen instead of walking the flow, but still in a new session. This change keeps the session open between runs on the web, parked on the screen under test, so the live look happens in the session the agent already has. - `references/mcp.md` Rules: what a run beside an open session does, case by case, from the target's `app`. Each case was checked on the built CLI (see Verified): - no `command`: both use that app - port 0: each starts its own copy, except a dev server that allows one copy per directory (`next dev` in Next.js 16 fails the run with `APP_UNREACHABLE`) - fixed port with `reuseExisting: true`: the run reuses the session's app, and whichever started the app stops it. The session closing during a run (`close_session`, 30 idle minutes, the 4-hour limit; a run is not session activity) stops the app under the run, so the skill says to `observe` once before a long run - fixed port without it: `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` - Config edits: the agent offers `reuseExisting: true` to the user and never adds it unasked (CI ignores it, and it is not part of the replay cache key). Until the user agrees, it closes the session before each run. I did not suggest switching a fixed port to port 0: it changes `app.identity`, which keys every recording, and it needs `{port}` support in the app's command. - `CI` set (many agent sandboxes): `reuseExisting` is ignored, so the agent prefixes the run with `CI=` or closes the session. Unsetting `CI` also drops the other CI defaults; the skill says so. `bug-bash.md` already gives the same advice. - Mobile: close the session before each run. A session stays open only on a target whose `device` no run uses, with `--target` on each run; adding a target is a config edit, so the agent asks. - `references/mcp.md` Workflow step 5, right after #1309's step 4 (fix from the failure block and trace page, go straight to a missing screen): leave the session open through those runs, so step 4's live look needs no new session, and `close_session` once the test passes. `observe` does not reload, so the agent `navigate`s even to the screen the session is on when the run or a fix may have changed it. A live look's actions print #1317's `Test line:` too, and `test_lines` lists them after the first walk, so the step says to copy a fixed line from its action. - `SKILL.md` Rules: one line pointing at the above. In the A/B below, 14 of 18 agents never opened `references/mcp.md`, but every one loaded `SKILL.md`. - `references/debugging.md`: the `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` row names an open session's app as a cause and says to `close_session` first. Otherwise the agent stops the process only if it started it, and offers `reuseExisting` instead of setting it. - `docs/mcp-server.mdx` "Run tests next to a session": the same cases as a table. After a failed run, the agent goes to the failing screen in that session instead of opening a new one. `docs/web.mdx`: the `reuseExisting` row links there. Workflow steps 1 to 4 come from #1317 (test lines while walking) and #1309 (fixing from the trace page), unchanged here. `SKILL.md`'s "Workflow: fixing a failed test" (#1309) already says "open or reuse a session" and sends the agent to topic `mcp` for when a session must close before a rerun; this PR's Rules are that answer. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes **After the rebase onto main (#1309, #1317, #1310, #1311).** Only Markdown conflicted, so I did not rerun the side-by-side matrix below. I re-checked the one new claim, about test lines, on the built MCP server: the same harness project with a port-0 app, a session parked on `/forms`, `e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts` beside it, then a live look in the same session: ```text walk: navigate /forms -> Test line: await app.open("/forms"); walk: type Full name -> Test line: await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Full name").fill("Grace Hopper"); e2e run beside the session: exit 0 | ✓ target "web" command ready 87ms | Tests 1 passed (1) live look: navigate /forms -> Test line: await app.open("/forms"); live look: tap Save profile -> Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Save profile").tap(); test_lines: await app.open(); await app.open("/forms"); await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Full name").fill("Grace Hopper"); await app.open("/forms"); await screen.getByRole("button", "Save profile").tap(); ``` `npx e2e guide mcp` from the built package prints the merged steps 4 and 5. **The built CLI, a session and a run side by side** (before the rebase). I used a harness project (the testbed playground app, `node server.mjs`) and drove `e2e mcp` with the MCP SDK client. The script opens a session, parks it on `/forms`, runs `e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts --retries 0`, then calls `observe` in the session again: | Target's `app` | `e2e run` beside the session | Session after the run | | --- | --- | --- | | fixed port, no `reuseExisting` | exit 3, `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING ... stop that process or set reuseExisting: true` | still on `/forms` | | fixed port, `reuseExisting: true` | exit 0, `target "web" command reused 5ms` | still on `/forms`; `close_session` then stops the app | | port 0 (`{port}` in `env`) | exit 0, `target "web" command ready 86ms` (its own app; the session's is on :63134) | still on `/forms`; `screenshot` and `start_recording` still work after the run cleared `.e2e/results` | | `reuseExisting`, run with `CI=1` | exit 3, `reuseExisting is ignored in CI, starting the command` then `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` | still on `/forms` | | `reuseExisting`, run with `CI=` | exit 0, `command reused 7ms`, no `CI` in the run header | still on `/forms` | | port 0, run with `CI=1` | exit 0, `command ready 88ms` | still on `/forms` | | port 0, Next.js 16.4 `next dev --port {port}` | exit 3, `APP_UNREACHABLE ... exited with code 1`, log: `Another next dev server is already running` | still on `/` | Who owns a reused app (`reuseExisting: true`, a test that sleeps 8 s between two pages): ```text # session first, closed 3 s into the run close_session during the run -> app at :47391 does not answer e2e run exit 3: APP_UNREACHABLE: nothing answered at http://127.0.0.1:47391/wizard (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED) # run first, session opened 3 s into it e2e mcp: [info] app: target "web" command: reusing the process already serving http://127.0.0.1:47391/ e2e run exit 0 navigate /wizard after the run failed: APP_UNREACHABLE: ... net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED ``` Not verified: mobile. I had no free simulator for a session and a run at once. The mobile text keeps what `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` and `setup.md` already say about one device per session. **A fresh agent (OpenCode, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`) with main's skill and with this branch's** (before the rebase, so neither arm had #1309's or #1317's text), n=2 to 4 per arm, in a scratch testbed project with the app on port 0. The `fix-mcp` task is the seeded three-mistake `fix-journey` test plus "Use the e2e MCP server to look at the app", added so that sessions come into play. In the plain `fix-journey` task no agent opens a session on either skill. With main, 0 of 4 did. - 3 of the 4 `author` arms on this branch read `references/mcp.md`, and `c-author-3` closed the session before its run even after reading it. `c-author-1` kept it open without reading it. Model variance is large at this n. - No speedup shows, and none should be claimed. On this small app every agent opened exactly one session and fixed all three mistakes from one walk, so there was never a second walk to save. Neither edited `e2e.config.ts`. The branch agent never opened `references/mcp.md`, so it did not offer `reuseExisting` either. **Docs page**, rendered with `mint dev` before the rebase. (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:442`). Agents read that text on every session; most never open `references/mcp.md`. #1317 rewrote both strings for test lines and kept the close advice. Aligning them is a code change outside this docs PR, so I left it out. - `bug-bash.md` step 1 recommends port 0 for parallel explorers. That has the same `next dev` gap and is out of this PR's scope. - `docs/debugging.mdx` has the same `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` row for people and does not name an open session; I left that page alone. - The shared A/B harness's `--reuse-existing` flag sets `reuseExisting` on a port-0 URL, which the config rejects with `INVALID_CONFIG`.

title: docs(skills): rerun one test with the replay cache on while iterating
body: A coding agent fixing a red e2e test reruns the whole file over and over, and the docs told it to add `--no-cache` after every change. That makes every `agent.act` before the broken line call the model again on each iteration, even though the replay cache already keeps the goals a passing check confirmed before the failure. This gives the agent a fast inner loop instead. - `skills/e2e/SKILL.md`: writing step 4 runs one test by `file:line`, and step 5 of "Workflow: fixing a failed test" (#1309) reruns it the same way instead of rerunning the file. A new section after that workflow, "Rerunning a test while you fix it", covers the loop: - `--action-timeout 5000` (#1310), so a wrong locator fails in 5 s instead of 30 s; dropped for the final `--no-cache` run - keep the cache on; what replays and what runs live - which edits re-record a goal: renaming the test, its `describe`, or its file; rewording a goal or its params; changing the agent's `context` or the test's `agentContext` - `--retries 0` when retries are on, since a retry never replays outside strict mode - a stopped run saves nothing - `--no-cache` one time once the test passes - `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`, "The replay cache": what a failing run keeps and evicts, the full list of key parts, and when `--no-cache` is the right call. - `skills/e2e/references/debugging.md`: the `--no-cache` row now says when to use it. Rerun with the cache on first, because the failed run already deleted the replay it implicates. If the failure repeats after a kept replay and `--no-cache` passes, tighten the check after that goal (`--no-cache` writes nothing, so the stale entry would otherwise replay forever). The "Read the failure" bullet from #1309 reruns by `file:line`. - `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md`: workflow step 4 runs and reruns that one test by `file:line`. - `skills/e2e/references/running.md`: the `--retries` row says a retry runs agent steps live. - `docs/coding-agents.mdx`: fixes the "adds `--no-cache` after it changes a test" line and shows `npx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts:3 --action-timeout 5000`. - `docs/cache.mdx`: a new "Rerun a test while you fix it" section. "What must match" now names moving the file and renaming a `describe`. - A changeset (`e2e`: patch), since the skill ships in the package. Decisions: - The loop is its own section in `SKILL.md`, right after #1309's fixing workflow. That workflow says how to fix from the run's evidence; this section says how to rerun. The workflow's step 5 points here instead of repeating the flags. - `--action-timeout` goes in the loop itself. In #1310's A/B runs, both agents read its tip in debugging.md's Tools table before their first run, and neither used the flag on it. The timeout isn't part of a recording's key (`packages/e2e/src/cache/context.ts`), so changing it keeps the recordings. - For a stale replay, the skill tells the agent to tighten the check, not to delete the entry under `.e2e/cache/`. The skill's rule is that `.e2e/` is read-only, and `e2e cache clear` would wipe every other test's recordings, committed ones included. Docs shortening pass (`authoring-docs`): I cut no facts. The coding-agents paragraph replaces the wrong `--no-cache` sentence with the loop. Measured against current main: | Page | Lines before → after | Prose words before → after | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `docs/cache.mdx` | 400 → 422 | 2646 → 2830 | | `docs/coding-agents.mdx` | 264 → 272 | 1055 → 1120 | Follow-up cuts for `cache.mdx`, not done here: the `--no-cache` `CodeGroup` under "Why a step was not replayed" could become a link to the new section, and "Commit the replay cache" repeats the `.gitignore` fact from "Modes". ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, with a scripted model. No live model was reachable on this machine: the stored ChatGPT login returns 401 ("session has ended"), there are no other `e2e login` entries, and there is no API key. So the scratch project's `agents.default.model` is a scripted AI SDK v4 model. It reads node ids off the act-loop prompt and calls `type`, `tap`, and `complete_step`, and it logs every call. Everything else is the built CLI from this branch: runner, cache, `@e2e-dev/web`, Chromium, and the testbed playground app. The model's identity isn't part of the cache key, so the cache decisions below don't depend on which model answers. A real model only makes each live call slower. Scratch test (testbed `/forms` and `/wizard`), run each time as `npx e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts:4 --debug`: ```ts test('a member saves a profile and creates a workspace', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/forms'); await agent.act('save the profile with the full name "Grace Hopper"'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status', 'Save result')).toHaveText('Saved profile for Grace Hopper'); await app.open('/wizard'); await agent.act('name the workspace "Atlas" and go to the next step'); await expect(screen.getByLabel('Plan')).toBeVisible(); await screen.getByLabel('Plan').selectOption('Pro'); await screen.getByRole('button', 'Next').tap(); await screen.getByRole('button', 'Create workspace').tap(); await expect(screen.getByRole('status', 'Summary')).toHaveText('Created "Atlas" on the Pro plan'); }); ``` `step.cache` of the two `agent.act` steps, from `.e2e/report.json`, as `mode · write`: | Run | Change | Result | Goal 1 | Goal 2 | that check fixed | pass | self-finalized · kept | missed · saved | 3 | 1.5 s | | 8 | `--no-cache` | pass | no `step.cache` | no `step.cache` | 6 | 1.6 s | | 9 | cache cleared, new test with a wrong trace page: ```text 2. ✓ `agent.act` "save the profile with the full name "Grace Hopper"" (214ms) — `tests/journey.e2e.ts:6` - cache: replayed all 2 recorded actions, no model call; recorded with `scripted/scripted-testbed`; recording kept (`.e2e/cache/760ca33a....json`) ``` Run 2b, the same failure with the config's retry: the retry runs both goals live and waits out the locator again. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-cache-config.test.ts` (`settleStagedTraces`), `packages/e2e/tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts`, and `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-trace-cache.test.ts` ("evicts a previously good entry once its flow is implicated in a failure", "--no-cache overrides the config", "replays on a retry ... when the first attempt fails" under strict). ### After the rebase onto main The same scratch project and scripted model, against this head's build. Line 15 is broken (`'Create the workspace'`) from the first run. Each run is `npx e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts:4 --debug`: | Run | Change | Flags | Result | Goal 1 | Goal 2 | Model calls | Duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 | new test, line 15 broken | `--action-timeout 5000` | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` | missed · saved | missed · saved | 6 | 6.7 s | | 2 | none | `--action-timeout 5000` | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` | self-finalized · kept | self-finalized · kept | 0 | 6.1 s | | 3 | line fixed | `--action-timeout 5000` | pass | self-finalized · kept | self-finalized · kept | 0 | 1.0 s | | 4 | none | none | pass | self-finalized · kept | self-finalized · kept | 0 | 1.1 s | | 5 | none | `--no-cache` | pass | no `step.cache` | no `step.cache` | 6 | 1.4 s | - With the flag, the broken locator fails the test in 6.1 s. Run 2 above, the same failure at the default 30 s, took 31.2 s. - Run 4 replays the recordings run 1 made with the flag, so dropping the flag keeps them. ### A/B: a fresh agent with main's skill and with this branch's This ran before the rebase, so the branch skill had neither #1309's fixing workflow nor the `--action-timeout` bullet. I didn't rerun it. The harness's own tasks have no `agent.act` steps, so the cache can't show there. I added a seed, `seeds/d-fix-agent-journey`: - the journey above, with the same scripted model - `retries: 1` in the config - three broken deterministic lines after the two goals: a wrong label, a wrong button name, a wrong summary text Task: "tests/journey.e2e.ts fails.
