The "then stop" branch arms ran on this PR's first commit; the open-prompt branch arms ran on its second. Both have the same loop instructions. | Run | Skill | Prompt | Wall min | e2e run commands | Sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Scripted model calls | Final exit | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | d-main-fix-agent-journey-1 | main | then stop | 2.8 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 6 | 0.09 | 24 | 0 | | d-main-fix-agent-journey-2 | main | then stop | 2.7 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 5 | 0.09 | 24 | 0 | | d-fix-agent-journey-1 | branch | then stop | 1.6 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 6 | 0.09 | 6 | 0 | | d-fix-agent-journey-2 | branch | then stop | 1.5 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 9 | 5 | 0.07 | 6 | 0 | | d-main-fix-agent-journey-open-1 | main | open | 2.7 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 9 | 5 | 0.08 | 24 | 0 | | d-main-fix-agent-journey-open-2 | main | open | 2.7 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 9 | 8 | 0.09 | 24 | 0 | | d-fix-agent-journey-open-1 | branch | open | 1.6 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 6 | 0.09 | 12 | 0 | | d-fix-agent-journey-open-2 | branch | open | 1.7 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 9 | 0.09 | 12 | 0 | What the agents did (from `events.jsonl`): - Every branch arm ran every command as `npx e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts:4 --retries 0`. The three failing runs took 31.8 s, 31.2 s, and 6.1 s; goals replayed after the first run. Main arms ran `npx e2e run tests/journey.e2e.ts`, so each failing run also ran the config's retry: 63 s, 62 s, and 12 s, with the retry running both goals live (6 calls per failing run). - No arm on either skill added `--no-cache` mid-loop. Main's skill never told them to; only the docs line this PR fixes did. - With the open prompt, both branch arms ran `--no-cache` one time after the pass (the 6 extra calls). With "then stop", both skipped it and said why: "I did not do the extra `--no-cache` run that the e2e skill suggests once a test passes, because you asked me to stop." - The wall-time gap comes from `retries: 1`, which the seed sets on purpose. With the local default of 0, the two skills would differ only in the final `--no-cache` run. This is n=2 on a small app with a scripted model, so it's a behavior check, not a benchmark. Rendered docs (`mint dev`). The `coding-agents.mdx` shot is from after the rebase; `cache.mdx` didn't change in it: | `docs/cache.mdx` | `docs/coding-agents.mdx` | | --- | --- | | ![cache section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d3e09a5-4fa4-49e0-9571-c366728e848d) | ![coding agents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/595733b9-6c16-418a-a9fa-acf7da0e0325) | Self-review: three fresh-context review rounds before the rebase, and one more on the merge after it. Before the rebase, I fixed every finding: - the full list of key parts, including `context` and `agentContext` - no absolute "only these run live" claims - strict mode exceptions for both `--strict-cache` and `cache.strict` - the read-write requirement in CI - `retries` on a test or `describe` wins over `--retries` - 30 s is the action timeout, 5 s the assertion timeout - a stale `file:line` can run another test - `--no-cache` doesn't fix a kept stale replay - a stopped run saves nothing After the rebase, I fixed: the flag also bounds each action in an agent step; the retries bullet names `CI`; the sentence on what runs live no longer reads as if the trace page showed `agent.assert`; `mcp.md` step 4 reran the file. I declined making the final `--no-cache` run conditional on a goal having replayed. That would change three pages, and one unconditional run keeps the loop simple.

title: feat(mcp): run a test in a session and stop on the failure screen
body:
`open_session` takes a `test`, named the way `e2e run` takes a positional. The session runs that one test and then hands itself over on the screen where the test passed or failed. A coding agent fixing a test gets the failure and the live screen in one call. It doesn't have to click through the flow again from the start, and it can act out the test's next lines from the failure screen before it reruns. ```txt open_session {test: "tests/journey.e2e.ts:4"} ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A["open_session {test}"] --> B["collect + select
(e2e run's path)"] B -- "none / several / unsupported" --> X["NO_TESTS, TEST_AMBIGUOUS,
SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED
(nothing booted)"] B --> C["boot engine, open attempt"] C --> D["beforeAll, test.extend fixtures,
beforeEach, body
(test timeout)"] D --> E["stop: failure evidence,
settle replay cache"] E --> F["session: observe, locate, act"] F --> G["close_session: afterEach,
fixture teardown, afterAll"] ``` ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/run/standalone-test.ts` (new) selects the test through `collect` and `select`, and refuses what a session can't run alone. It runs the hooks, fixtures, and body on the session's attempt under the test's timeout. It publishes the attempt for `expect.poll`, `expect.soft`, and `test.skip` only while test code runs, captures `captureFailureEvidence`, and settles the replay cache. Teardown waits for close. - `run/standalone-attempt.ts`: a one-shot attempt with a `test` builds a second fixture set for it on the same session, with its own budget, the test's id and agent context, a cache context as on a run's first attempt, and screenshot markers of its own. After the body the test's budget stays aborted until teardown, so a body its timeout cut short can't drive the session the agent now uses. `run/standalone.ts`: the attempt's close runs the test's teardown before the host's close cancels its operations. - `mcp/session.ts`: the `test` input. With a test, the session neither opens the app URL nor launches the pinned app, and the opening text leads with `mcp/test-outcome.ts`: the outcome, the code and message, the failing line with a code frame, the URL, the nearest nodes, the last 15 steps, and how to rerun. Each session loads the config and the test files in its own module graph (`mcp-`), so a rerun sees edited helper files. - Test lines (#1317) in a session that ran a test: the test's own steps and opening print none, since they are already in the test file. The first screen after the test is observed through the catalog's context, so the agent's first action on it gets its `Test line:`, and `test_lines` (`mcp/test-lines.ts`) drafts the lines as the ones that continue the test, with no `app.open()` of the session's own. - `cli/mcp.ts`: an `unhandledRejection` listener. A rejection while a session's test code runs fails that test, as in a run's worker. One after its body ended is an `UNHANDLED_REJECTION` line at the newest open test session's `close_session`, or a warning on stderr once every such session closed. Before any session has run a test, a rejection still shuts the server down, as today. - New codes `TEST_AMBIGUOUS` and `SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED`. `select()` takes a `noTestsHint`, so the MCP `NO_TESTS` message doesn't name `--pass-with-no-tests`. `codeFrame` takes a width. - Skill: steps 4 and 5 of `SKILL.md`'s "Workflow: fixing a failed test" (from #1309) name `open_session {test}` as the way to look live at the failure screen and to rerun, and `references/mcp.md` gains "Fixing a failing test". Both tell the agent to put the `Test line:` an action prints in place of a wrong line. Docs: `reference/mcp.mdx` "Running a test", `mcp-server.mdx` "Fix a failing test", `reference/errors.mdx`. Against main, `mcp-server.mdx` grows from 137 to 161 lines (587 to 712 prose words), `reference/mcp.mdx` from 499 to 565. No fact was cut. The guide's "Run tests next to a session" lost the sentence the feature made false. ## Decisions - **Replay cache.** The test reads and writes it as a run's first attempt: recorded steps replay, a new recording is saved once a later check passes, and a failure evicts what no check confirmed. It settles when the body ends, so nothing the agent does in the session afterwards can confirm or evict an entry. In a session, an `afterEach` check confirms nothing. - **Rerun.** `close_session`, then `open_session {test}` again, not a catalog tool. A rerun needs a fresh attempt, step, catalog, and module graph, which is what an open builds. - **Refused in v1** with `SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED`: a serial group member, a test that starts from a setup test's `session`, a test that runs as several agents. Setup sessions are the biggest gap. Supporting them means running the setup pair through `TargetExecutor.runSetupUnit` on the session's worker first. - **One at a time.** Test code in different sessions takes turns: `publishAttempt` has one slot per process. Collection takes turns too: `collectModule` has one slot, and a file's top-level `await` can yield it mid-file. An open cancelled while its test waits for its turn runs none of the test's code. - **A body cut short** by its timeout or a stray rejection gets up to `cleanupTimeout` to reach a harness call, which fails on its aborted budget, before the turn ends. - No test result, report, or `trace.md` for a session's run. Retries and the test's `trace` and `video` modes don't apply. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes After merging main at `6b418575` (with #1316, `run_code`): `test-lines.ts` keeps both: `run_code` statements join `test_lines`, and after `open_session {test}` the lines continue that test. The unit tests for both drafts stay. `docs/mcp-server.mdx` keeps #1316's "How it runs a test line" and this PR's "Fix a failing test", which now says `run_code` runs a fixed line on the failure screen. The skill keeps `open_session {test}` and adds #1316's "or `run_code` for the fixed line" in the fixing workflow and `mcp.md` step 4, and the `test_lines` row names both. A new case in `mcp-test-run.test.ts` runs `run_code` in a session opened with `test` and checks the statement continues the test in `test_lines`. Re-ran `pnpm check`, 183 unit and 62 integration tests (`mcp-test-run`, `mcp-run-code`, `mcp-test-lines`, `mcp-server`, `mcp-session-host`). After merging main at `ec941749` (with #1312 and the agent's test title, #1323/#1344): - `mcp/server.ts`: the instructions keep #1312's "write the test while you walk the flow" and add this PR's pointer to `open_session {test}`. - `run/standalone-attempt.ts`: the session's attempt takes main's `titlePath: []`. A follow-up commit gives the test that `open_session {test}` runs its own title in agent steps, as `e2e run` does; `mcp-test-run.test.ts` now checks the first model call's prompt carries `Test: increments the counter`, and fails with the override removed. - `references/mcp.md`: #1312's intro and "the test is the file you write as you walk", with this PR's clauses on running a test and on the replay cache. `errors.mdx`: main's `NO_TESTS` row plus this PR's `open_session` case. - Re-ran `pnpm check`, `skill.test.ts`, and the `mcp-test-run`, `mcp-test-lines`, `mcp-server`, `mcp-session-host`, and `open-host-lifecycle` tests: all pass. After merging main at `cfe76ba3` (with #1313 and #1314): the skill and `docs/mcp-server.mdx` conflicted. `SKILL.md` keeps this PR's step 4 (`open_session {test}`) before #1314's "Rerunning a test while you fix it", and step 5 reruns that test by `file:line` or in a new session with `open_session {test}`. `mcp.md` step 4 is #1314's one-test rerun with `open_session {test}` as the first way to reach the failure screen; step 5 is #1313's "leave the session open"; Rules keep this PR's cache sentence and take #1313's rules for running beside a session. "Fixing a failing test" now confirms with `npx e2e run tests/.e2e.ts:`. `docs/mcp-server.mdx` takes #1313's section and says a session can run a test, which uses the replay cache. title: feat(mcp): run test code in a live session with run_code
body:
A coding agent writing a test over `e2e mcp` used to walk the flow by node id, write the test from memory, and learn what it got wrong on the first `e2e run`, where a wrong label waits out the 30 s action timeout. #1317 now prints a checked `Test line:` for every action. The lines no action prints, an assertion or a step the agent writes without walking it, still meet the app for the first time in `e2e run`. This adds a `run_code` catalog tool: the agent sends the statements it's about to write, the session runs them on the live app, and the ones that pass join the `test_lines` draft.

The tool was first named `try_lines`; review renamed it `run_code`, so it no longer reads one letter away from `test_lines` and says plainly that it runs code against the app. The grammar modules follow it (`code-parse.ts`, `code-surface.ts`).

```txt
call {tool: "run_code", args: {code: "await screen.getByLabel('Full Name').fill('Ada Lovelace');\nawait screen.getByRole('button', 'Save profile').tap();"}}
```
```text
Statement 1 of 2 failed, and the one after it did not run. Each statement waited at most 5000 ms.
1. failed: await screen.getByLabel('Full Name').fill('Ada Lovelace');
   LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator matched no nodes within getByLabel("Full Name")
2. not run: await screen.getByRole('button', 'Save profile').tap();

Screen unchanged since revision b6 (re-observed as revision b8, path /forms); the ids you have stay valid.
```

## What changed

- `run_code {code, timeout?}` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/run-code.ts`) runs statements in order on the session's `app` and a `screen` over the session's engine, with matchers from `createAsyncExpectation`, which is what `expect` runs for a locator. Waits, the exactly-one rule, and failure messages are a test's. The first failure stops the call and the rest are reported `not run`. A read (`textContent()`, `count()`, ...) shows its value. The result ends with the presenter's screen diff, and a failed statement makes it an MCP error result.
- No evaluation. `code-parse.ts` parses the code with oxc-parser, already a runtime dependency (`oxcParser()` in `src/config/typescript.ts`), and walks the ESTree nodes into plain data. A statement's source is the code it spans. Every member name is checked against a closed table typed against `Screen`, `Locator`, `App`, and `AsyncExpectation` (`code-surface.ts`), in both directions: a name the interface lacks fails to compile, and so does a public member the table neither lists nor leaves out with a reason (`Covers<T>`), so a member the API gains, like main's `Locator.or` from #1049, can't drop out of `run_code` unnoticed. The runner only calls names from that table. Anything else, and code that doesn't parse, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` quoting the code with `line:column` from node offsets, and no statement runs.
- Limits: 10,000 characters, 50 statements, and 1,000 opening brackets. oxc's parser recurses once per nesting level on the server's own thread, and about 5,300 nested brackets overflow the stack and kill the process (SIGSEGV), every session with it. The deepest code these limits let through, brackets and then arrow functions, parses on a 4 MB stack, half of Node's main-thread default.
- Timeout: each statement runs under the new `AttemptBudget.capped(timeout)`, which brings the phase deadline forward for the body and puts it back after (default 5000 ms, max 120000). Every locator, matcher, and navigation is already capped by that deadline, so a wrong locator fails at 5 s with the `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` a test gets. The config's own timeouts still apply when shorter.
- Secrets. Of the two options the brief allowed, this routes through authorization instead of refusing. `fill(credentials.user('admin').password)` and `fill(secrets.get('apiKey'))` go through the new `LocatorEngine.fillSecret`, which reads the node each resolve lands on and runs `authorizeSecretFill` on it before the value is handed over, again after a stale re-resolve. Same checks and `secret.*` policy events as `type_secret`; `authorizeSecretFill` resolves the value through the attempt's `SecretResolver`, which raises the pixel taint before the engine types it. The login line is the one an agent most needs to run before writing it, so a refusal would have cost the most there. A Secret anywhere but `fill`'s first argument is a parse error.
- Guessing a secret through match results is closed two ways.
  - The `screen` run_code runs on comes from `createScreenContext` in `run/fixtures.ts`, the factory the test fixtures use, over a session whose `read` passes every node through `redactNode`. A read returns, and a matcher compares, `<secret:name>` where a value was, so no `toContainText`, `toHaveValue(/…/)`, or other matcher outcome depends on a secret's characters. A matcher that expects `<secret:name>` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, since it would pass here and fail in a test.
  - A locator is matched inside the engine against the raw page, attributes and hidden nodes included. So when the config declares any secret, a locator found by part of a text (a regex, an `exact` other than literal `true`, `hasText`) is `POLICY_DENIED` before anything runs. Exact locators still run.
- No regex guard. A matcher tests a regex in the server's thread, where `timeout` can't stop it mid-match. The docs say so, and the skill tells the agent to avoid nested quantifiers.
- Left out on purpose:
  - Engine fixtures (`browser`, `device`). An allowlist of `browser.goto` and `expect(browser).toHaveURL` in core would name the web engine's members there (review-triage pattern 13). A statement on one gets a message naming it as an engine fixture, built from the `engine.fixtures` keys.
  - `app.screenshot`, which writes an unmasked file after a fill.
  - `toHaveScreenshot` and `expect(screen)`, which need a test file.
  - `setInputFiles`, which reads arbitrary paths. `upload` has the path policy.
  - `screen.debug`, which prints to the server process.
  - `all()`, which returns locators.
- Beside #1317's test lines:
  - The statements that pass, reads aside, join the `test_lines` draft as written, in the order they ran, each with `await` and `;` (`SessionTestLines.ran` in `packages/e2e/src/mcp/test-lines.ts`). Failed and unrun statements add nothing, as a failed action prints no line. Without this, a session that opened a page or filled a form through `run_code` drafted a body that skipped those steps and started on the wrong screen.
  - `run_code` observes through the catalog's watched context, so the next action's `Test line:` is read from the screen `run_code` returned. Through the unwatched context, an id from a `run_code` screen on a new page would get `No test line: #n.. is not on the newest screen`.
  - `run_code` statements are not rewritten: an `app.open` with an absolute URL keeps its port, where a `navigate` line uses the path. Agents write paths here, so I left it.
- `run_code` is reserved for project tools beside `test_lines` (`HARNESS_TOOL_NAMES`), so MCP telemetry counts it by name through the list #1317 derives from those names. It's named in the server's instructions and the `tools` description.
- Docs:
  - `reference/mcp.mdx`: a `run_code` entry (inputs, behavior, the grammar table, and one Throws row per refusal), a catalog row, the sessions rule, and `test_lines` naming the statements `run_code` passed.
  - `mcp-server.mdx`: a short "How it tries a test line" section after #1317's "How it writes a test line".
  - `reference/security.mdx`: two policy-denial rows, and a "where redaction stops" line for `locate`, see below.
  - `tools.mdx` and `reference/errors.mdx`: the reserved name.
- Skill:
  - `mcp.md`: a tools row, and workflow step 3: run each line no action printed (an assertion, a step you didn't walk); after a failure, run the fixed statement and the rest from where the passing ones left the app, not from the start.
  - `SKILL.md` "Workflow: fixing a failed test" step 4 (from #1309) and `debugging.md`: look live with `observe` and `locate`, or `run_code` for the fixed line and the ones after it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on the web only (no simulator or emulator).

At `ed6297d6`, after the second review: `pnpm check`, then the unit tests `mcp-code-parse`, `mcp-test-lines`, `agent-config`, `telemetry-events`, `locator-engine`, `skill`, and the 9 files that use `createFixtures` (354 tests), and the integration tests `mcp-run-code`, `mcp-test-lines`, `mcp-server`, `agent-policy`, `mcp-session-host`, `open-session`, `extended-fixtures`, `screenshot-assertions`, `engine-secrets`, `filled-secrets`, `screen-tree-secrets`, and `truncated-secrets` (106 tests).

The built server over stdio (`packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js mcp`) on a scratch project: the testbed playground started on port 0, the web engine, and an `admin` credential. An MCP SDK client script drove it. Node lines are trimmed. The blocks show oxc's syntax error, the bracket bound and the deepest nesting the limits allow refused with the server still answering after them, a statement over several lines with a comment echoed as written, a regex the dropped guard used to refuse now running, and an option `fill` lacks refused on a secret fill. The last two blocks are a grammar action on an id a `run_code` screen listed, then the `test_lines` draft. No output held the credential's value.

```text
===== secret check =====
21 outputs, 0 contain the credential's password
```

To check the second redaction pass was redundant, I ran `mcp-run-code.test.ts` with `renderValue`'s redaction and the server's `redacting` wrapper both removed: all 11 tests passed, `never returns a secret value` included. The node-level ledger redacts every read, and the `call` handler redacts the result with the session's ledger after that.

- `tests/integration/mcp-run-code.test.ts`, the built CLI over stdio on the fixture app, covers:
  - a passing block with reads
  - a stop at the first failure inside the timeout
  - ambiguity and assertion messages
  - a refused block running nothing
  - the passing statements in `test_lines`, reads and failures left out, and the next action's test line read from the screen `run_code` returned (with `run_code` observing through the unwatched context, this test fails with `No test line: #n42019 is not on the newest screen`)
  - secret fills refused for the email field, a button, an unknown credential or secret, an unknown `fill` option, and a timeout that isn't a number
  - a password field read and `toHaveValue`, both refused
  - pixels clean after a refused fill and tainted after a real one
  - generic-secret reads redacted
  - matchers comparing redacted text: `toContainText('sk-live')` fails, `toHaveText('<secret:apiKey>')` is refused
  - partial locators refused, `exact: 0` included
  - the drafted secret fills naming `credentials.user('admin').password` and `secrets.get('apiKey')`
  - no returned text containing either secret value
- `tests/unit/mcp-code-parse.test.ts`: the grammar, about 75 exact refusal messages (`process`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `import(...)`, `{ toString }`, assignments, arrow functions, `${}` in templates, computed keys, spread, optional chaining, oxc syntax errors), the size and nesting limits with the deepest code they allow, and parsing with `eval` and `Function` replaced by throwing stubs.
- `tests/unit/mcp-test-lines.test.ts`: `run_code` statements drafted among the action lines, `await` and `;` added where missing, the `credentials` import named.
- `tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts`: `fillSecret` authorizes on every resolve, and `capped` ends a missing node's wait at the cap and gives the deadline back.

A/B on `tasks/author-journey.md` (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`), run before the rebase and the rename, so the arms called the tool by its old name, `try_lines`: main's arms had no #1317 test lines, and I didn't re-run it. Arms 1-2 ran on the first commit, which still allowed `browser`. Arms 3-4 ran on the second, with an observation-based guard since replaced. Arms 5-6 ran on the third commit; the commits after it add a skill line and a refusal (matchers expecting `<secret:name>`) that none of those arms hit.

| Run | Wall min | e2e runs | Sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main-author-1 | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 19 | 26 | 17 | 0.16 | 0 |
| main-author-2 | 0.9 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 23 | 14 | 0.14 | 0 |
| f4-author-1 (commit 1) | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 0.17 | 0 |
| f4-author-2 (commit 1) | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 12 | 17 | 15 | 0.18 | 0 |
| f4-author-3 (commit 2) | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 18 | 14 | 0.21 | 0 |
| f4-author-4 (commit 2) | 0.5 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 18 | 13 | 0.20 | 0 |
| f4-author-5 (commit 3) | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 18 | 13 | 0.20 | 0 |
| f4-author-6 (commit 3) | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 18 | 13 | 0.20 | 0 |

- Behavior from `events.jsonl`: main arms walk the journey one grammar click at a time (`navigate` 3-4, `type` 3, `type_secret` 1, `tap` 5, `select` 2, `check` 1), then write the test. Branch arms replace the clicks with 5-7 `run_code` calls (then `try_lines`) of 1-4 statements each, the same `screen.*` lines they then paste into the test. Every branch arm passed its first `e2e run`, as both main arms did.
- No arm hit a refusal. Arms 5-6 used only exact locators, `toContainText`, and `toHaveText`.
- Numbers: MCP calls about halved (17-19 to 10-12). Wall time is within noise here. Cost went up about 30% (0.14-0.16 to 0.20), I think from the longer `mcp.md` and tool description the agents read. On this small app main's agent doesn't show the slow loop, so this is a behavior check, not a speedup claim. The case `run_code` is for, a first try that is wrong, doesn't come up in this task.
- One `fix-journey` arm on commit 2 (`f4-fix-1`): 1.5 min, 4 runs, no session, exit 0, the same shape as `main-fix-1/2`. The agent fixed from terminal output and never opened a session.

## Review

Three fresh-context review rounds. Fixed:
- the regex and substring secret oracle (twice; the observation-based guard of round 1 missed attributes, hidden nodes, and `exact: 0`)
- `app.screenshot` getting past the pixel taint
- the echoed source rewriting comments and templates
- `toHaveScreenshot` that could never run
- core naming `browser` members
- regex catastrophic backtracking (a partial guard, dropped after the second review)
- `run_code` missing from the server instructions and the changeset
- a matcher on `<secret:name>` passing here and failing in a test
- the partial-locator check's own query list, now derived from the grammar table so it fails closed


After the rebase, one more fresh-context review of the rebase delta. Fixed: the `run_code` entry still said to paste passing lines into the test while they also join the draft; the skill's "or a line you changed" would rerun an action #1317 had already printed and leave both lines in the draft; the skill's exact-text advice had no answer for a row, now `filter({ has: screen.getByText('Offer B') })`.


After the rename and the merge of main, one more fresh-context review. Fixed: `run_code` refused `Locator.or`, which the merge brought in from #1049 and `writing-tests.md` tells agents to use; the tables are now exhaustive against the public interfaces so the next member fails `tsc` instead. Also renamed the last `try`-named leftovers (`RunCodeResult`, the fixture's API key).

After okwasniewski's second review, one more fresh-context review of that delta. Fixed: the bracket bound alone left nesting without brackets (arrow functions, assignments) to the length limit, and at 20,000 characters the deepest code left under a quarter of the stack spare; the limit is now 10,000. And the docs promised every statement stops at `timeout`, which a backtracking regex doesn't; they say so now.

## For the maintainer

- `browser` and `device`: an engine-declared allowlist would let `expect(browser).toHaveURL` and `browser.goto` in without core naming them. One shape is a `tryable` flag on `FixtureOperation`, read through the `FixtureRecorder`. It's an engine SPI change, so I left it for a follow-up.
- Pick one secret policy for partial locators. `run_code` refuses a regex, an `exact` other than `true`, or `hasText` whenever the config declares a secret, which most projects do (a login credential). The fail-closed reason is that a password shows in plain text behind a "show password" toggle. But `locate {text, exact: false}` in the same session still answers the substring question; I documented that under "Where redaction stops" and left `locate` alone. Option (A) applies the same rule to `locate`, which means changing its zero-match hint and skill step 2, which recommend `filter({ hasText })`. Option (B) drops the `run_code` refusal and lists both tools there. I kept the new tool closed and left the existing one to you. Meanwhile the skill tells the agent to try exact text in projects with secrets. #1317 adds a third case: its test lines scope a row with `filter({ hasText })`, and `run_code` refuses that line in a project with secrets. The action already ran, so the printed line needs no trying, and the skill points at `filter({ has: screen.getByText(...) })` for a row the agent writes itself.
- Default timeout 5000 ms, which also caps `app.open`, `restart`, and `clearState` (a test gives them `config.timeout`). A slow first compile can make `app.open` fail at 5 s. The docs and skill say to raise `timeout`.

title: feat(mcp): show the test line for each action in a session
body: Every grammar action in an `e2e mcp` session now answers with the test line that repeats it, so a coding agent can write the test while it walks the flow, without a `locate` call per control. ```txt Tapped #n6031. Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Sign in").tap(); Screen changes since revision b4 ... ``` - **Where the locator comes from.** The target node as the newest observation listed it, read before the action runs, since the action may remove it. The session's context asks every observation for its tree and drops it again unless the caller asked (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/test-lines.ts`, `watch`). - **Which locator.** Role and name, label, placeholder, text, then the test id read off the live node (the observation tree carries none), in the skill's order. Each is built with `locateQuery` and tried with `LocatorEngine.resolveNow`, as `locate` does. The first that matches the target and nothing else wins. - **Twins.** A locator that also matches twins is narrowed to `{ visible: true }`, then scoped under a container (`getByRole("listitem").filter({ hasText: "Offer B" })`), then pinned with `.nth(i)` plus a `//` comment. A position is printed only when the live twins are the ones the observation listed, each in place or all shifted by one offset, or in their boxes in another order (light DOM before shadow roots). Otherwise the result says `No test line:` and why. - **Never a line that fails.** No locator reaches the target alone, a failed action, typing into the focused field, `press` with `times`, `scroll`, `scroll_to` a text, `dismiss_keyboard`, and a `type` the keyboard took all print a reason instead. Point tools print nothing. At most 10 locators are tried per target, since each one is a full snapshot on a device. - **Verbs.** `tap()`, `doubleTap()`, `longPress()`, `secondaryTap()`, `hover()` (with `modifiers`), `fill(value)` (grammar `type` with a target replaces the value, so `fill`, not `pressSequentially`), `press(key)`, `selectOption(label)`, `check()`/`uncheck()`, `dragTo(locator)`, `setInputFiles(...)`, `scrollIntoView()`, `app.open(path)` (a URL on the app's origin becomes its path, so the line survives the next run's port), `app.back()`, and `app.open()` for the session's own opening. - **Secrets.** `type_secret` writes `credentials.user(name).password` or `secrets.get(name)`. A typed value equal to a credential's username becomes `credentials.user(name).username`. Results and `test_lines` pass the attempt's secret ledger like every session result. - **`test_lines`.** A read-only catalog tool that returns every line so far, in order, as a draft test body, with a `//` comment where an action had none and a note on which of `credentials`/`secrets` to import. - **MCP only.** `createSessionCatalog` wraps the grammar tools; the testing agent's loop never sees a line. `test_lines` joins the reserved tool names (a project tool can no longer take it) and telemetry now derives its session tool set from that list, so `test_lines` calls aren't folded into `other`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["call tap #n42"] --> B["node #n42 from the newest observation tree"] B --> C{"role+name, label, placeholder, text, test id: resolveNow matches only the target?"} C -- yes --> E["run the action"] C -- twins --> D{"visible: true, container scope, certain position?"} D -- yes --> E D -- no --> F["reason"] F --> E E --> G{"action failed?"} G -- no --> H["Test line / No test line after the lead; recorded for test_lines"] G -- yes --> I["result as before, nothing recorded"] ``` Docs: `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` (catalog row, `test_lines` entry with the verb table), `docs/mcp-server.mdx` ("How it writes a test line"), `docs/tools.mdx` and `docs/reference/errors.mdx` (reserved name). Skill: `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` (tools table, workflow step 1 says to copy each line, step 2 keeps `locate` for what no action printed) and one clause in `SKILL.md`. Decisions I made that the maintainer may want to revisit: - Point tools print no line, not `screen.tapAt(...)`: screenshot coordinates break on the next viewport, and a listed control should be written as a locator. - `.nth(i)` is printed (with a comment) rather than no line when only a certain position tells twins apart. - `scroll` and `scroll_to` a text print a reason, not `screen.scrollUntilVisible(...)`, since the session can't check that line before the scroll. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes **The built MCP server on the testbed app** (an A/B harness `--setup-only` project, driven by a small MCP SDK client). The author-journey flow, one action per call: ```txt >>> type {"target":"n6028","value":"admin"} Typed into #n6028. Test line: await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Username").fill(credentials.user("admin").username); >>> type_secret {"target":"n6030","name":"admin.password"} Filled secret "admin.password" into #n6030; its value is masked in every observation. Test line: await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Password").fill(credentials.user("admin").password); >>> select {"target":"n36037","value":"Mobile"} Selected "Mobile" in #n36037. Test line: await screen.getByRole("combobox", "Team").selectOption("Mobile"); >>> check {"target":"n36044"} Checked #n36044. Test line: await screen.getByRole("checkbox", "Email notifications").check(); ``` `test_lines` at the end: ```txt Draft test body from this session's actions, in order (16 lines): await app.open(); await app.open("/login"); await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Username").fill(credentials.user("admin").username); await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Password").fill(credentials.user("admin").password); await screen.getByRole("button", "Sign in").tap(); await app.open("/forms"); await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Full name").fill("Grace Hopper"); await screen.getByRole("combobox", "Team").selectOption("Mobile"); await screen.getByRole("checkbox", "Email notifications").check(); await screen.getByRole("button", "Save profile").tap(); await app.open("/wizard"); await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Workspace name").fill("Atlas"); await screen.getByRole("button", "Next").tap(); await screen.getByRole("combobox", "Plan").selectOption("Pro"); await screen.getByRole("button", "Next").tap(); await screen.getByRole("button", "Create workspace").tap(); Paste it into a test body, async ({ app, screen }) => { ... }, and add an expect after each step that should change the screen. Import credentials from 'e2e'. ``` A second walk over `/todos`, `/controls`, and `/board` covered `press`, `long_press`, `double_tap`, `hover`, a radio, a switch, a listbox, `scroll_to`, `scroll` (reason), `drag`, and `back`. The testbed's `Sale` banner has a hidden twin with the same text and test id, and printed `await screen.getByText("Sale", { visible: true }).tap();`. **The real proof: both drafts pasted into test files as is, plus one hand-written `expect` each, run green** with the built CLI: ```txt ✓ target "web" command ready 88ms ✓ |web| tests/draft.e2e.ts (1 test) 858ms ✓ |web| tests/verbs.e2e.ts (1 test) 2.16s Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` `packages/e2e/tests/integration/mcp-test-lines.test.ts` does the same in CI on a fixture page: it drives the built server, checks every line (a container scope, an `.nth(1)` between plain-div twins, a shadow-root twin the locator engine lists second, a test-id-only icon button, and the password by credential), then writes the draft into a test and runs it to `passed`. **iOS simulator** (Settings app, a simulator I booted and shut down): lines print and replay. ```txt >>> tap {"target":"n74"} 4974ms Tapped #n74. Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "General").tap(); >>> tap {"target":"n756"} 3221ms Tapped #n756. Test line: await screen.getByRole("listitem", "Keyboard").tap(); ``` ```txt ✓ mobile engine for target "ios" prepared 706ms ✓ |ios| tests/settings.e2e.ts (1 test) 5.69s ✓ the drafted settings walk replays 5.69s ``` One `locate` there took 110 to 341 ms (5 samples), which is what each try adds per action; a control with a unique role and name costs one. Not run on an Android emulator. **A/B harness, `author-journey`** (Sonnet, n=2 per arm; main rows are the shared baselines): | Run | Wall min | e2e runs | Sessions | MCP calls | Tool calls | Model steps | Cost $ | Final exit | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | main-author-1 | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 19 | 26 | 17 | 0.16 | 0 | | main-author-2 | 0.9 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 23 | 14 | 0.14 | 0 | | branch-1 (first commit) | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 25 | 15 | 0.19 | 0 | | branch-2 (first commit) | 0.6 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 21 | 15 | 0.18 | 0 | | branch-3 (head) | 0.7 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 25 | 15 | 0.21 | 0 | | branch-4 (head) | 0.8 | 1 | 1 | 17 | 25 | 15 | 0.19 | 0 | - Every branch arm wrote the locators the actions printed, word for word: `getByRole('textbox', 'Username')`, `getByRole('combobox', 'Team')`, and so on. Both main arms wrote `getByLabel(...)` for the fields instead. main-author-1 also spent one `locate` call and one extra `navigate`; no branch arm called `locate`. - The walk itself didn't change: all six arms walk the flow once over MCP, write the test after the walk, and pass on the first run. None called `test_lines`; on a three-screen flow the agent copied the lines from the results. - The cost gap is in the first two model steps: the branch arms wrote about 17k more tokens to the prompt cache, because the MCP server's instructions and tool descriptions changed, so the cached prefix main runs had warmed didn't match. By the end of the walk the branch arms also carried about 2k more cached input, the printed lines. Wall time is within noise at n=2. - The testbed is small enough that main's Sonnet authors this flow in one run, so this shows behavior (the lines get used) and no regression, not a speedup on a large app. Testbed default suite: 79 passed, 1 skipped (on a port-0 copy of the config, since another agent held 4271). ## Review A fresh-context reviewer ran two rounds. Fixed: - A twin was placed by its box from the observation alone, so a page that shifted could make `.nth()` pin the wrong one. Now placement by position needs the twins where the observation saw them (each in place, or all moved by one offset). - Round two found the locator engine lists shadow-root matches after light-DOM ones while observe lists them in place, so "same count" didn't mean "same order". Twins in their old boxes in another order are now matched by box, and only a match placed for certain lends its test id. The fixture page covers it. - `test_lines` calls were folded into `other` in telemetry; the set now comes from the reserved names. - The `tools` and `call` descriptions didn't mention lines; ids are looked up on the newest screen only; the probe count per target is capped at 10. - A test ties the wrapped tools to `GRAMMAR_TOOL_NAMES`, so a new verb must get a line or a reason. Dismissed: the claim that `TargetSession.read` accepts observation refs (the session adapter answers only located refs, `packages/e2e/src/engine/session.ts`), so the target's live box can't be read directly before the action.

title: feat(e2e): start a project from an example app with e2e init --example
body: `e2e init my-app --example with-expo` copies one of the apps under `examples/` into a new or empty directory. It then runs the usual skill, MCP, and install steps in the example's e2e project. ```bash npx e2e init my-app --example with-flutter # "flutter" works too ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A[--example] --> B{dir empty?} B -- no --> X[exit 2, nothing downloaded] B -- yes --> C[codeload tarball at e2e@version] C -- 404 --> D[fall back to main, warn] C --> E[stream, extract examples/name, stop past it] D --> E E --> F[package.json: dir name + this CLI's e2e/@e2e-dev ranges] F --> G[wizard in root or e2e/: skill, MCP, .gitignore, install] G -- cancel / Ctrl-C --> R[remove the copy] ``` - `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/examples.ts`: the example list, a streaming download from `codeload.github.com/tester-army/e2e`, and a small tar reader. The tar reader handles ustar prefixes, pax `path`, and GNU long names. It refuses `..` paths, never writes links, and keeps the executable bit, so `gradlew` still runs. - The tag matches the running CLI, so the example code matches the runner. Example pins are bumped by hand and trail releases: `with-vite` at `e2e@0.21.2` pins `e2e ^0.15.2`. The copy rewrites `e2e` and the recorded `@e2e-dev/*` ranges to what `init` writes for a new project. - The example's config, tests, and scripts stay as they are. No `tests/example.e2e.ts` and no `test:e2e` script get added. For native apps (SwiftUI, Compose, KMP, Flutter, MAUI) the wizard runs in `e2e/`, so the skill and MCP files land there. The docs say to open the agent in that folder. - The download has a 30 s idle limit, not a total one, because the tarball is the whole repo (about 28 MB gzipped before `examples/`). Ctrl-C during the download goes through the clack spinner's `onCancel`, removes the partial copy, and exits 130. - `--example` with `--engine`, `--gateway`, or `--endpoint` is a usage error (exit 2). `with-limrun` isn't offered, since it reuses the SwiftUI and Compose apps. `tests/unit/init-examples.test.ts` fails if the list and `examples/` drift apart, or if a listed script is missing. - Telemetry: `e2e_init_completed` gets `example` (the folder name or `null`) and a new `example-failed` result. Both are documented in `docs/telemetry.mdx`. - Docs: a "Starting from an example" section and flag row in `docs/reference/cli.mdx`, plus `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` and `examples/README.md`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. Scratch directory, built CLI (`packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`), real GitHub. - `init vite-app --example vite --yes --install`, then `npm run test:e2e` in the copy: ``` ✓ target "web" command ready 659ms ↓ |web| tests/agentic.e2e.ts (2 tests | 2 skipped) ✓ |web| tests/deterministic.e2e.ts (3 tests) 940ms ``` The agent tests skip without `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`. Before the range rewrite, the same run installed `e2e@0.15.2` and failed with `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED`. - `init flutter-app --example flutter --yes`: about 2.4 s end to end. The skill and MCP files land in `flutter-app/e2e/`, and the run ends with `Next: cd flutter-app/e2e, then npm install, then build and install the app as ../README.md describes, then npm run test:e2e:android`. - `init compose --example with-compose`, diffed against `git archive e2e@0.21.2 examples/with-compose`: identical except `e2e/package.json` `name`. `gradlew` is `-rwxr-xr-x`. - `init expo-app --example expo`: `package.json` diff against the tag is the name plus `e2e ^0.16.0 → ^0.21.2`, `@e2e-dev/web ^0.11.1 → ^0.15.2`, `@e2e-dev/mobile ^0.9.0 → ^0.12.3`. - `kill -INT` 0.6 s into a download: `■ Canceled`, `Cancelled; no changes were made`, exit 130, and no directory left. - Each of these exits 2 before downloading anything: - `--example svelte`: the error lists the valid names. - `--example expo --engine web`: `drop --engine`. - A non-empty directory: `is not empty; --example needs a new or empty directory`. Not verified: building and running a native example (Flutter, SwiftUI, and the others) on a device after copying. The copy is byte-identical to the tag apart from `package.json`, and the nightly examples workflow already covers those apps.

title: fix(cache): hand off a replay whose end state never shows once its recorded wait runs out
body:
Fixes ENG-927. Refs #1144.

When a replayed `agent.act` step's recorded end state never showed, the agent got the step 14 to 31 s later. Two causes:

- `stage()` stamped `endWaitMs` after the executor's verdict, so the model's last turn counted as app time. A step whose app answered in 0.6 s stored 16.7 s after 6 s of model thinking.
- `verifyEndState` polled for about 14 s before it applied the recorded wait, from the same start, so a typical 11 s wait never mattered.

Changes:

- The observation feed timestamps its recent looks (`observation-feed.ts`). `stage()` measures the wait to the first look since the last action that already showed the end state, with the replay's own check (`measuredEndWaitMs` in `step-cache.ts`). The #881 baseline is unchanged.
- `verifyEndState` (`replay.ts`) waits on one deadline: the recorded wait from the replay's last action, cut so the step clock keeps 20 s for a hand-off. It looks at 0.1, 0.4 and 1 s, then every second. The first second of looks is always taken, also after a slow route, and no look starts that the step clock cannot finish.
- `--strict-cache` still waits at least 15 s, counted from the first look, and keeps 2 s so a miss fails as `REPLAY_STALE`, not `STEP_TIMEOUT`. A longer strict wait for loaded machines (#1144, #1154) can go on top of this: it is one number in `endWait()`.

Trade-offs:

- Without `--strict-cache`, an end state that shows more than 10 s later than it did when recorded now hands off instead of replaying.
- Entries recorded before this keep their stored wait: re-recording the same flow does not rewrite the file.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch app on the testbed: a "Place order" button whose confirmation shows 0.5 s after the click (or never), and a deterministic executor that waits `ENG927_THINK_MS` before its verdict. Recorded once, then `e2e run --cache-dir <copy>` per scenario, main and this branch on the same entries.

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded `endWaitMs`, 0 s final turn | 10,718 ms | 10,613 ms |
| Recorded `endWaitMs`, 6 s final turn | 16,729 ms | 10,607 ms |
| End state never shows (10.7 s entry): hand-off after the replayed click | 14.1 s | 10.7 s |
| `--strict-cache`, end state at +12 s | replays at 14.3 s | replays at 12.4 s |
| `--strict-cache`, end state at +16 s | `REPLAY_STALE` at 14.3 s | `REPLAY_STALE` at 15.2 s |
| No strict, end state at +12 s | replays at 14.3 s | hands off at 10.7 s |

```text
# main, end state never shows
   × places an order > agent.act "Place the order" 14.36s failed
# this branch
   × places an order > agent.act "Place the order" 10.97s failed
```

- Web benchmark agent suite with `--strict-cache` on this branch: 33 passed, `26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed`, the same as main.

title: fix(web): keep a timeout a timeout in staleOr and navigationStaleOr
body: `staleOr` and `navigationStaleOr` are meant to keep a Playwright timeout a timeout, but both matched their stale patterns first. A `TimeoutError` whose call log quoted `resolved to hidden`, `not attached`, or `frame was detached` became a retryable `NODE_STALE`, so the runner retried or re-read after a budget that had already run out. The timeout check now runs first in both. Added tests with real call-log text. ## Verified Ran locally: the new tests fail on main with `NODE_STALE` and pass with the fix. The web unit suite passes and `pnpm check` is green. Three browser-launch integration tests time out on my machine, and one of them does the same on main. | | main | branch | |---|---|---| | `staleOr`, timeout with `resolved to hidden` or `not attached` in its call log | `NODE_STALE`, retryable | `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`, not retryable | | `navigationStaleOr`, timeout with `frame was detached` in its call log | `NODE_STALE`, retryable | `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`, not retryable |

title: Problems identifying visibility causing flakiness
body:
### What happened

Hello,

I am using the harness with getByRole, getByText, scrollUntilVisible, etc. I am noticing frequent issues with flakiness stemming from weaknesses in the harness's ability to determine visibility. For example look at the following flake:

1. Opening the keyboard raises the Back/Next footer over top of the Brand input.
2. **scrollUntilVisible incorrectly considers the Brand input visible, so it never scrolls.**
3. e2e taps Brand’s covered position, which cannot work because the Brand form field is not visible. Product name keeps focus.
4. Typing then appends the intended text to the Product name form field, leaving Brand empty.

My previous experience was with Detox, and while Detox had its own flakiness for sure it was rarely this kind of severe flaw in the underlying ability of the test harness to know the visibility of objects on the screen. I am curious if developers are aware of the issue or if there's something I'm doing wrong. Is there an opportunity to use OpenCV or some other vision framework to solve some of this?

Thanks for reading!

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
1. Have a covered TextInput in an application
2. e2e considers that input visible
```

### Versions

e2e: 0.21.2, node: 24.22.0, "@e2e-dev/mobile": "^0.12.3",

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

### Anything else

_No response_

title: feat(ocr): add local screenshot recognition and guarded workflows
body: ## What and why Draft: browser/device verification and the full repository gates remain incomplete, as detailed below. This is not ready for merge. - Add the opt-in `e2e/ocr` entrypoint for drawn text that is missing from the semantic tree, without changing the default agent or adding dependencies. - `tesseractOcr()` runs a separately installed local Tesseract process. `ocrTools()` provides read-only OCR evidence to an agent; `ocrExecutor()` runs explicit callback workflows without a model. - Text taps require a unique, sufficiently confident match, unchanged fresh pixels and valid geometry, then use the harness action dispatcher. Assertions cannot tap; known disabled and secure controls remain protected. OCR executor steps do not replay cached coordinates. - Include Web/mobile configuration examples, compile-time API assertions, and deterministic plus opt-in real-Tesseract tests. ```ts import { ocrExecutor, tesseractOcr } from 'e2e/ocr'; const executor = ocrExecutor({ provider: tesseractOcr(), async runStep(context, ocr) { if (context.step.kind === 'act') await ocr.tapText({ text: 'Continue' }); else await ocr.assertText({ text: 'Complete' }); return { status: 'passed', summary: context.step.instruction }; }, }); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, with real Tesseract on synthetic screenshots and a scripted engine, not a real browser or mobile device. Built CLI, using a temporary fixture project and `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 node ../../../dist/cli/bin.js run --reporter list,markdown`: ```text ✓ real local OCR on synthetic captures > agent.act "tap Continue" ✓ real local OCR on synthetic captures > agent.assert "Complete is visible" Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) ``` The fixture dispatches the recognized point through the harness and switches to a new PNG only after a valid tap. The report has zero model calls and one action. The committed integration test also reruns the same workflow and verifies the tap is executed again rather than replaying OCR coordinates. Current-upstream validation: all packages build and typecheck; 88 OCR tests pass (including real Tesseract smoke), core unit tests 3,007 pass / 4 skip, mobile tests 347 pass, and script tests 84 pass. Lint, dead-code checks (existing advisory warnings), docs examples/anchors/logos/package-manager checks, error codes, peer ranges, changeset checks, generated plugin/MCP checks and generated docs social cards pass. Importing the built OCR entrypoint with runtime `ai` and `@ai-sdk/*` resolution forbidden succeeds. ## Limits still requiring validation - Real Android/iOS and browser OCR flows are not verified. The pinned Playwright Chromium download returned an invalid/truncated archive in this environment. Web unit tests therefore have 284 passes and one browser-dependent failure; additional browser executor/policy integration runs stop at `BROWSER_INSTALL_FAILED`. Full testbed, web benchmark and full `pnpm test` are not claimed passing. - Full Mintlify validation/rendering was not run. Local static docs checks passed; no docs were submitted to Mintlify services for this check. - Existing executor screenshots cap the longest side at 768 pixels. Small text can be lost before OCR; Chinese trained data was not tested. - Pixel comparison is not an atomic UI transaction. Verify outcomes after taps, and do not blindly retry consequential actions. - Screenshot masking is not general PII removal. Custom providers are trusted code; the normal agent receives OCR text as model evidence. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. Added a patch changeset for the additive `e2e/ocr` entrypoint, following the current 0.x policy. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). Not applicable: this is opt-in and does not replace an existing API. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. Reviewed the built OCR declarations and added compile-time callback-boundary assertions; no wire format changes. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. Not applicable: the existing engine contract is unchanged. - [ ] Full repository gates, browser/testbed benchmarks, and real-device OCR validation complete. These remain blocked or unrun as listed above. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to implement, rebase, review, test, and document this contribution. The reported results are from executed local checks, with unverified surfaces listed explicitly. No live model calls were used to validate the OCR workflow.

title: web: SVG-intercepted diagram labels cannot be double-clicked through agent point tools or browser.mouse
body:
## Runnable public reproduction [Standalone public repository](https://github.com/fghpdf/e2e-svg-double-click-repro), verified from a fresh clone at commit `1b73765`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/fghpdf/e2e-svg-double-click-repro.git cd e2e-svg-double-click-repro npm ci npm run browsers npm run repro ``` Requires Node.js 24.8+. `npm run repro` intentionally exits 1 with two failed tests: agent `doubleTap` and agent `tapAt` both encounter SVG pointer interception. `npm test` runs three passing controls, including successful label editing on the original page when directly targeting the event-handling container, and the accessible-container workaround. The repository contains the minimal HTML/SVG app, local server, `e2e.config.ts`, tests, lockfile, and README. It pins the published `e2e@0.21.2` and `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.2` packages. A model-free `StepExecutor` repeats the reported action choices through the actual agent dispatcher; no API key or company code is needed. This reproduces action execution, not the model's reasoning. --- ## Problem In a DOM/SVG diagram editor, a real double-click on a node starts inline label editing, but `agent.act` cannot complete the same interaction. The semantic target is a readonly textarea with `pointer-events: none`; a sibling SVG receives pointer input and the event bubbles to the node container. Reported environment: e2e 0.21.2, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.2, bundled playwright-core 1.64.0; Chromium, macOS, Node 26; Claude Sonnet via an AI SDK provider. ## Minimal reproduction Serve the following as /repro.html: ```html
``` In a configured web test: ```ts test('rename the node', async ({ app, agent, browser }) => { await app.open('/repro.html'); await agent.act('double-click the node label and rename it to "Renamed"'); await expect(browser.locator('textarea')).toHaveValue('Renamed'); }); ``` The fixture above is transcribed from a user report; it has not yet been independently executed against current main. ## Observed in the reported project - `doubleTap` on the textbox times out with ` ... intercepts pointer events: NOT_ACTIONABLE`. - `tap_at` at the label coordinates also encounters actionability failure, while tapping empty page space works. - The agent reports `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED` because no coordinate double-click tool is available. - Test code has only `browser.mouse.move/down/up/wheel`. Repeating down/up without click-count support did not trigger the expected double-click in this project. A synthetic `dblclick` through `browser.evaluate` was used as a workaround. - Giving the event-handling container `role="group"` and an accessible name allowed the agent's double-click to work. That requires application changes and may be impractical for third-party components. ## Current-source findings Current main already implements raw coordinate double-tap in `dispatchPointerAction` using Playwright's `mouse.dblclick` (packages/web/src/actions.ts). The gap appears to be exposing/routing that capability to the agent and to deterministic test code: - POINT_VERBS in packages/e2e/src/agent/point-tap.ts contains only tapAt and hoverAt. - `hitTest` chooses a listed interactive control by semantic geometry, which can be the pointer-inert textarea instead of the actual DOM hit target. - Browser.mouse in packages/web/src/browser.ts still exposes move/wheel/down/up, without click/dblclick or button/clickCount options. ## Expected / proposed scope Provide a supported way to send a real coordinate double-click when the semantic control differs from the pointer target, while retaining the existing policy, recording, and error handling. A small first change could expose `browser.mouse.dblclick(x, y)` (and/or validated button/clickCount options), with a regression proving that the browser emits a real dblclick and enables editing in the fixture. A separate agent change could expose coordinate double-tap with explicit raw-point semantics. Two independent single-click tool calls are not an equivalent gesture. ## Related work - #1276: a styled radio's semantic input is intercepted by its visible sibling. Related target mismatch, but a different gesture and component structure. - #1284 (currently open): allows tap_at/hover_at to use a bare point when another *listed* node covers the control's center. Its semantic-tree check may not detect an SVG omitted from that tree, and it does not add coordinate double-tap. - #1277: semantic nodes for drawn canvas/WebGL objects and a drag_at request. This report concerns existing DOM/SVG nodes rather than opaque drawn objects. - #486 / #501: general agent action coverage; this is specifically the coordinate and interception path. Would a focused deterministic mouse double-click PR be a suitable first contribution, followed by the agent point-action gap? This issue was prepared with an AI assistant from the user's report and checked against current source; no company source code or screenshots are included.

title: fix(oauth): open the sign-in URL without a command interpreter on Windows
body: ## What and why `e2e login` opens the sign-in URL in the user's browser. On Windows it did that with `cmd /c start "" `, and the only character it escaped was `&`. That is fine for a URL the runner built, but the URL is not always one the runner built. In the device flow it is the `verification_uri` that the provider's own HTTP response carries (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/device-code.ts:111`), and the schema accepts it as a plain string, with no check on its shape. The provider's response is external input, and `cmd` reads `|`, `&`, `^`, `<`, `>`, and `%` inside a URL as command syntax. A URL that carries a pipe makes `cmd` run whatever follows it, and a single `^` cancels the `&` escape the code applied, so a URL carrying `^&` was enough to run a command of the sender's choosing on the machine that ran `e2e login`. Three providers use the device flow, so their sign-in URLs took that path: GitHub Copilot, SuperGrok, and OpenCode Console. The ChatGPT flow builds its own authorize URL with `URLSearchParams` inside the runner (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/providers/openai.ts:181`), so it was never exposed. The fix keeps the URL out of any command interpreter and narrows what the runner opens at all. The URL now goes to the default handler for its scheme as one plain argument, and only `http:` and `https:` are opened. A URL with any other scheme is left to the user, who reads the link the CLI prints and opens it themselves, which is what the CLI already did whenever the browser did not come up. Per `CONTRIBUTING.md` this belongs through `SECURITY.md` rather than the issue tracker, so I have not opened an issue. If a coordinated advisory is wanted, I can send the details to security@tester.army. ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/oauth/browser.ts` is new and holds `browserCommand(platform, url)`. On Windows it returns `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` with the URL as its second argument, so nothing reads the URL as a command line. macOS keeps `open` and Linux keeps `xdg-open`, both of which already took the URL as a plain argument. The platform is a parameter, so the argv is testable on any machine. - The builder opens only `http:` and `https:` URLs (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/browser.ts:23`, `:40-47`). Anything else returns undefined, and the CLI does not open it. - `packages/e2e/src/oauth/cli.ts:266` calls the builder and spawns what it returns. The `cmd /c start` call and the `^&` escape are gone. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/oauth/browser.test.ts` is new, with six tests over the argv, the URL arriving unchanged, and the scheme rule. - `docs/reference/security.mdx:93` records the rule in the navigation table, next to the schemes the runner's own navigation accepts. - The changeset is a patch for `e2e`, since `e2e login` ships in the published package. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Windows opener: `cmd /c start "" `, with `&` written as `^&` | Windows opener: `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler `, the URL as one argument | | A URL carrying `\|` makes `cmd` run what follows the pipe | the URL reaches the handler unchanged | | A URL carrying `^&` cancels the escape, and `cmd` runs the rest | the URL reaches the handler unchanged | | A `file:`, `data:`, or `javascript:` URL is opened by the shell | the CLI prints the URL and does not open it | ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The new unit test was written first and run against the old behavior, extracted verbatim into the new module. It failed 4 of 6 on exactly the three things this fixes, and passed 6 of 6 after the change. ```text before: 4 failed | 2 passed (6) expected 'cmd' not to be 'cmd' expected 'https://example.com/login/device?code…' to be 'https://example.com/login/device?code…' (the ^& escape had changed the URL) expected { Object (command, args) } to be undefined (a file: URL was opened) after: 6 passed (6) ``` - The injection was reproduced on Windows in the exact shape the old code used, and then shown to be gone with the new one. The payload is a URL that carries a pipe and writes a file: ```text old: cmd /c start "" x|set>p1.txt -> p1.txt written, the injected command ran old: cmd /c start "" x^&set>p2.txt -> p2.txt written, the caret cancelled the escape new: rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler https://example.com/login/device?code=x|set>pwned.txt the program receives one argument, "https://example.com/login/device?code=x|set>pwned.txt", and no file is written ``` - The browser still opens. `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler https://example.com/` exits 0 with no output and no error, so the sign-in page comes up as before. - The unit suite of `packages/e2e` on the branch, and on the same tree with the change stashed: ```text main: Test Files 20 failed | 173 passed (193) Tests 47 failed | 2851 passed | 25 skipped (2923) branch: Test Files 20 failed | 174 passed (194) Tests 46 failed | 2858 passed | 25 skipped (2929) ``` The set of failing files is the same 20 in both runs. The three tests that differ flake in both directions, two telemetry tests that passed on the branch and one managed process test that failed on it, so they are the timing flakes this suite has on Windows rather than a change in behavior. The branch adds the new file and its 6 passing tests. - `oxlint` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the three touched files, and `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/e2e` is clean. `fallow dead-code` reports the same 2 files and the same 22 class members before and after the change, so the new module is not dead code. - `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts` reports 86 error codes in source, all documented. `node scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` passes, and `node scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts` reports "34 pending, none an unannounced 0.x minor or major" with this changeset in the set. - `check-install-scripts` did not run here, because this machine's install is partial. It runs in `spec.yml` on every pull request. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: ci: check community PRs against the contributing policy
body:
## What and why

- Community PR rules modeled on opencode's `pr-standards` / `compliance-close` / `close-prs`. Too many unsolicited PRs (221 fork PRs in the last 30 days, 69 `feat`).
- `pr-policy.yml` (`pull_request_target`, base-branch script only, never PR code) runs `scripts/pr-policy/check.ts` on community PRs (fork, non-member, non-bot). It checks:
  - a conventional title;
  - a linked issue for `fix|chore|test|perf|ci|build|revert` (`feat|docs|refactor` exempt, same as opencode);
  - a description;
  - a filled `## Verified`.
- A failing PR gets `needs:compliance` and one bot comment, kept up to date.
- `pr-policy-sweep.yml` runs daily at 06:00 UTC. It closes a flagged PR that still fails 72h after the comment, re-checking the live title and body (so linking the issue from the sidebar counts). It also closes community PRs open more than a month with fewer than 2 positive reactions and no maintainer approval (label `stale-cleanup`, never re-closed). Manual runs default to dry-run.
- The check skips PRs opened before `POLICY_START` (2026-10-23). The stale sweep has no cutoff, same as opencode.
- CONTRIBUTING.md gets a `## Pull requests` section: what we accept, features need agreement on an issue first.
- The PR template gets `## Issue`, the feature request template a "wait for agreement" note, and writing-pr mentions `## Issue`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[PR opened/edited/pushed] --> B{community?}
  B -- no --> Z[skip]
  B -- yes --> C{problems on live PR?}
  C -- no --> D[clear label + comment]
  C -- yes --> E[needs:compliance + comment]
  E --> F[daily sweep: still failing 72h later?]
  F -- yes --> G[close]
  F -- fixed --> D
```

## Issue

None. Maintainer-requested.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `node --test scripts/pr-policy/rules.test.ts`: 12 pass. `tsc -p scripts`, oxlint, and fallow are clean.
- Ran the rules on the 21 fork PRs from 2026-10-10 onward (real bodies and `closingIssuesReferences`): 16 pass. The other 5 are `fix`/`ci` PRs with no linked issue.
  - The first version wanted a `## What and why` heading and flagged 12 PRs that open with bullets the way writing-pr says to. It now accepts any description outside the template sections.
- `check.ts --dry-run` on real payloads (`created_at` moved past the cutoff):
  - #1306: `needs an existing issue`
  - #1269: compliant

title: feat(e2e): add screen.doubleTapAt for viewport gestures
body:
## What and why

Add `screen.doubleTapAt(point, options?)` alongside `screen.tapAt`. It sends a bare viewport double-tap through the existing `performAt` path on engines that declare the `doubleTap` pointer action. This lets test code edit a diagram label when a sibling SVG receives pointer input.

```ts
await screen.doubleTapAt({ x: 120, y: 240 }, { timeout: 1_000 });
```

The web-only `browser.mouse.dblclick` candidate is removed. The Playwright migration guide maps `page.mouse.dblclick(x, y)` to the shared API, and the changeset targets `e2e`.

Related to #1327 ([runnable repro](https://github.com/fghpdf/e2e-svg-double-click-repro)). Locator-relative double-tap and a coordinate double-tap tool for `agent.act` remain separate; this PR does not close the issue.

## Separate test path fix

Use `fileURLToPath` in two hosted-session test helpers so temporary paths work in checkouts with non-ASCII characters or spaces.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The fixture regression failed before implementation because `screen.doubleTapAt` was missing. All 44 fixture tests now pass, including bare dispatch, timeout forwarding, validation, and step recording. The built CLI passes all 7 pointer tests in Chromium. The SVG regression verifies the trusted primary-button event sequence and confirms the label becomes `Renamed`.

```text
e2e run tests/pointer.e2e.ts --video
✓ screen.doubleTapAt edits a label beneath a sibling SVG
Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The recording is local because GitHub CLI requires upstream write access to upload attachments.

title: docs: explain what the agent misses inside an off-site iframe
body: An iframe from another site, such as a hosted card field, shows in the agent's semantic tree as an empty `iframe` node. The docs never told test authors what that means for them: - A tree-only judgment (`agent.assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`) about the frame's content works without that content (#1270). - An `agent.act` whose only change is inside the frame never records a replay. The cache sees no change, writes `no-change`, and the step calls the model on every run, strict cache included (#1271). Both come from the same deliberate boundary: `isOnSiteFrame` in `packages/web/src/observation.ts:189-193`, with the replay result coming from the `no-change` check in `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts:610`. The boundary itself was documented only in the security reference's [site check](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/security#site-check). What changed: - `docs/browser.mdx`, "Reach into an iframe": one paragraph. It states the boundary and says the agent reaches that content only through screenshots. It points to `frameLocator` for steps, `vision` for judgments, and the cache consequence. - `docs/cache.mdx`: the `no-change` row covers the frame case and says the step runs live on every run. The `no-entry` row gets that exception. The old "a step that took no action records nothing" sentence moves out of the `no-change` row: such a step stages as `skipped` (`step-cache.ts:601`) and reports no `write` at all. - `docs/reference/agent.mdx`, "Vision": one sentence linking to the iframe section. - `skills/e2e/` (plus the synced plugin copy): the same facts in `agent.md`, `writing-tests.md`, and `debugging.md` (`ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`), and a patch changeset since the skill ships in `e2e`. No runtime change. Fixes #1270 Fixes #1271 Linear: ENG-1054 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Docs site, `mint dev` on the branch: the three edited sections render, and both links resolve. | Reach into an iframe | `step.cache.write` table | Vision | | --- | --- | --- | | ![browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d54ee98-662b-4fa4-be04-b730e710187c) | ![cache](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e65e9bfb-aeff-4528-b698-5a0764e54e28) | ![vision](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4607c978-01b0-4a1d-bd4c-8d686df122c4) | - I checked every claim against the source. I didn't rerun the reporter's model-backed repro; the issues include its report output. --- Made by Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

title: feat(cli): select web and mobile together in e2e init
body: `e2e init` asked for one engine, so a project testing a web app and a mobile app had to hand-edit the config. The engine question is now a multiselect. - The prompt lists Web (preselected) and Mobile (iOS/Android). Submitting with nothing selected replaces the old **None** option: clack's multiselect can't keep None exclusive. - `--engine` takes a comma-separated or repeated list, like `--skills`: `--engine web,mobile`. `--engine mobile` and `--engine none` work as before; `none` with an engine is a usage error (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/flags.ts`). - One engine writes exactly what it wrote before. Both write a target each and `workers: 1` (the mobile setting, which now also covers the web target). - With both, the examples go in `tests/web.e2e.ts` and `tests/mobile.e2e.ts`, each test with `requires: ['browser']` or `requires: ['device']`. Without it, each test would also run on the other target and fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` already recommends `requires: ['device']` for mixed suites. - Presets now hold a target entry and settings instead of a finished `targets` block, and `createScaffold` composes them (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/scaffold.ts`). The engine-less config moved there from the preset list, since it's no longer a prompt choice. - A re-run on a project with an existing config adds no `tests/example.e2e.ts` when the per-engine examples are there, so `init` stays idempotent. - Telemetry's `engine` reports `web,mobile`, in preset order whatever the toggle order. ```ts // e2e.config.ts from --engine web,mobile on macOS export default { targets: [ { engine: web(), app: { url: process.env.APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000', // Or let the runner start the dev server: // command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'] }, }, }, // Replace Settings with your app's bundle id. { name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios' }), app: { bundleId: 'Settings' } }, ], workers: 1, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, with the built CLI on scratch projects (`verify` surface: a scratch project for `init`). The prompt in a real pseudo-terminal, after toggling Mobile with Space and pressing Enter: ``` ◆ Which engines? Select none for HTTP tests or your own engine. │ ◼ Web (Playwright) │ ◼ Mobile (iOS/Android) (agent-device) ... ◇ Which engines? Select none for HTTP tests or your own engine. │ Web, Mobile (iOS/Android) │ ◆ Which model gateway for agent steps? Adds AI SDK v7. ``` `e2e init --yes --engine web,mobile`, then `e2e list` with the workspace packages linked: each example runs on its own target only. ``` tests/mobile.e2e.ts › Settings opens [web] (skipped: engine lacks required capabilities: device) tests/web.e2e.ts › app opens [web] tests/mobile.e2e.ts › Settings opens [ios] tests/web.e2e.ts › app opens [ios] (skipped: engine lacks required capabilities: browser) ``` A second `e2e init --yes` on that project prints `Nothing to create; project already initialized` and leaves `tests/` with the two files. The new integration test in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/cli-init.test.ts` runs `e2e run --target web` on the generated project against a local page: the web example passes. Not run: the mobile example on a simulator or emulator. The single-engine mobile scaffold is unchanged, and the combined one is the same target entry inside a list.

title: docs: add a page objects page
body:
The skills said "never add a sleep" but gave a coding agent nothing to put in its place, so a sleep was what it kept reaching for. They now name the replacement: `agent.waitFor` on the state the test was waiting for.

- `skills/e2e/SKILL.md`: the step for fixing a failed test rules out sleeps and fixed delays and points to `agent.waitFor('<that state>')`.
- `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`: a bad/good example under `waitFor`, plus its limits: it needs a model even under a custom executor, it is never cached, and it judges on every screen change up to `maxModelCalls`, so for a long wait on a screen that keeps changing, raise `interval`.
- `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`: the Habits line waits for a state, not a duration. A matcher with a longer `timeout` is still the choice when a locator names the state exactly.
- `skills/migrate-to-e2e/SKILL.md`: an old suite's sleep is ported as `agent.waitFor`, or as an assertion when a locator names the state or the config has no model.

```ts
// BAD: guesses how long the export takes.
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10_000));

// GOOD: waits for the state, up to the timeout.
await agent.waitFor('the export finished and a download link appeared', { timeout: 60_000 });
```

The `docs/migrate/*.mdx` tables still map `waitForTimeout` and fixed waits to a locator assertion. That is still right when a locator names the state, so this PR leaves them alone.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built `e2e` and ran `npx e2e guide agent` in `apps/testbed`: the new rule, example, and limits appear in the `waitFor` section the CLI serves.
- `pnpm plugins:check` confirms the plugin copies match `skills/`.
