title: docs: add a Writing fixtures guide
body:
The only place that explained `test.extend` was the reference entry on `reference/test.mdx`. That entry lists the contract, but it never shows a suite built around fixtures. This PR adds `docs/fixtures.mdx` ("Writing fixtures") to the Extend group, below Project tools.

- **Lede:** fixtures create test data. To sign in, use a saved session instead.
- **Define fixtures in one file:** a `tests/fixtures.ts` (expandable) whose fixtures create a `project`, then a `task` in it, with `agent.act`, and delete the project at teardown. The test file restores the `admin` session. A note says a `fetch` to a test API is faster where the app has one.
- **Build one fixture on another**, **Give each setup its own test**, **Read fixtures in hooks**, **When a fixture fails:** two sentences or a snippet each, linking to the reference for the full contract.

The two example files live in `docs/examples/fixtures/tests/`, so they typecheck against the built packages. They're registered in `scripts/check-docs-examples.ts`, which keeps the page's code blocks identical to them. `core-concepts.mdx` and the reference entry now link to the new page.

```ts
export const test = base.extend<{ project: string }>({
  project: async ({ app, agent, screen }, use) => {
    const name = `Launch plan ${Date.now()}`;
    await app.open('/projects');
    await agent.act('create a project named {name}', { params: { name: unique(name) } });
    await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', name)).toBeVisible();
    await use(name);
    // teardown deletes it the same way
  },
});
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Docs site, `mint dev`: the page renders with its sidebar entry and table of contents. The long example collapses behind "Show more", and the accordion and cards display correctly in light and dark mode.
- Testbed, a scratch config with a scripted executor (no model key) and the todos page: `agent.act` in a fixture's setup and in its teardown both ran and passed. The report recorded those steps in phases `beforeEach` and `afterEach`. A second scratch test with `{ session: 'admin' }` read the signed-in dashboard greeting from inside a fixture, so the session is restored before fixtures run. The scratch files are not committed.

  ```
  [executor] act "add a todo {title}" title=Write the announcement
     ✓ completes a todo > agent.act "add a todo {title}" 171ms
  [executor] act "delete the todo {title}" title=Write the announcement
     ✓ completes a todo > agent.act "delete the todo {title}" 152ms
  [teardown] todo deleted
   ✓ |web| tests-fixture-agent/todo.e2e.ts (1 test) 791ms
  [fixture] greeting: Welcome back, admin!
   ✓ |web| tests-fixture-agent/session.e2e.ts (1 test) 62ms
  ```
- I checked every behavior claim against `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`, `run/extended-fixtures.ts`, and `run/execute.ts`.
- A fresh-context review found four issues in the first draft, all fixed before opening:
  - Not every name clash fails at import: an engine name fails during the attempt. The page now links to the reference list of mistakes instead.
  - Top-level hooks only lack the types for your fixtures, not the fixtures themselves. The hooks section now says so.
  - The worker cache kept a failed install. (That section was later cut to keep the page short.)
  - The example built its URL from a separate env var, so a target using port `0` would call the wrong address. (That example has since been replaced by the agent-based one.)

title: ci(site): redeploy e2e.tester.army on every docs change on main
body: Rebuilds e2e.tester.army on every push to `main` that touches `docs/`, instead of only after an e2e release. - New `.github/workflows/site.yml`: on `push` to `main` with `paths: docs/**` (plus the workflow itself), or by `workflow_dispatch`, it POSTs the existing `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK` secret. It has no permissions and queues instead of cancelling. No ruleset requires it, so a workflow-level `paths:` filter is fine here. That isn't true for the `filters.yml` gates. - Removes the `site` job from `release.yml`. The site now reads `docs/` from `main`, not from the newest release tag, so a release no longer changes what it builds. A release that edits docs is a push to `main` touching `docs/`, so it still triggers a rebuild. - `CONTRIBUTING.md` drops the line saying a release calls the hook. This doesn't touch Mintlify, which still hosts `/docs` on the domain until the cutover and builds from `main` through its GitHub app. ## Verified Ran the app locally: no. This is CI only. - `actionlint` on `site.yml` and `release.yml` reports only the Blacksmith runner label it reports on every workflow here. - The `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK` secret exists on this repository. The hook call is the same step the removed `site` job ran. - After merge, run `site` once with `workflow_dispatch` to confirm the hook answers.

title: docs(skills): replace fixed sleeps with agent.waitFor
body: The skills said "never add a sleep" but gave a coding agent nothing to put in its place, so a sleep was what it kept reaching for. They now name the replacement: `agent.waitFor` on the state the test was waiting for. - `skills/e2e/SKILL.md`: the step for fixing a failed test rules out sleeps and fixed delays and points to `agent.waitFor('')`. - `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`: a bad/good example under `waitFor`, plus its limits: it needs a model even under a custom executor, it is never cached, and it judges on every screen change up to `maxModelCalls`, so for a long wait on a screen that keeps changing, raise `interval`. - `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`: the Habits line waits for a state, not a duration. A matcher with a longer `timeout` is still the choice when a locator names the state exactly. - `skills/migrate-to-e2e/SKILL.md`: an old suite's sleep is ported as `agent.waitFor`, or as an assertion when a locator names the state or the config has no model. ```ts // BAD: guesses how long the export takes. await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10_000)); // GOOD: waits for the state, up to the timeout. await agent.waitFor('the export finished and a download link appeared', { timeout: 60_000 }); ``` The `docs/migrate/*.mdx` tables still map `waitForTimeout` and fixed waits to a locator assertion. That is still right when a locator names the state, so this PR leaves them alone. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built `e2e` and ran `npx e2e guide agent` in `apps/testbed`: the new rule, example, and limits appear in the `waitFor` section the CLI serves. - `pnpm plugins:check` confirms the plugin copies match `skills/`.

title: fix(agent): keep the test title out of the system prompt so prompt caching spans tests
body: #1323 put `Test: ` into the agent's trusted context, and that context is part of the system prompt. The system prompt now changes from test to test, so the provider prompt cache stops matching across tests. On a live Sonnet 5.5 run, the cost of the same 8 tests went from $0.13 on 0.21.2 to $0.22 on main. OpenAI's `promptCacheKey` hashes the system prompt, so it now varies per test too. #1323 is unreleased, so this fixes it before #1210 publishes. - The title moves into the step's user prompt. The built-in agent's act prompt (`packages/e2e/src/agent/default-agent.ts`) and every judgment prompt (`buildPrompt` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts`) now open with `Test: billing > upgrades the tier`. The system prompt is the same for every test, as it was in 0.21.2. - `ctx.agentContext` goes back to the agent's `context` plus the test's `agentContext`. Custom executors read the title from the new `ctx.attempt.titlePath`, which is redacted per step like the context. - The `keyedContext` split from #1323 is gone. The cache key digests `agentContext` again, which is the same value it digested before, so committed recordings keep replaying. - The explore prompts now point at the `Test:` line for the goal. #1323 put the goal there, and the prompts still said it was in "project context". - The #1323 changeset is reworded to describe the final behavior. Not covered: `@e2e-dev/decision`'s executor reads `ctx.agentContext` and never had the title. The changeset scopes the line to the built-in agent. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - web benchmark, `tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts` + `login-form.e2e.ts` (8 tests), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` with adaptive thinking, `--no-cache --workers 1`, the same config and port on both builds: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | tests | 8/8 | 8/8 | | tokens | 197.9k | 197.9k | | cached | 61% | 84% | | cost | $0.22 | $0.11 | ```text main: AI 197.9k tokens · 61% cached · $0.22 · 21 model calls · gateway/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 branch: AI 197.9k tokens · 84% cached · $0.11 · 21 model calls · gateway/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 ``` - Strict replay of the committed web-benchmark recordings on this branch (`--strict-cache`, the default model) gave `Cache 26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed` and 33/33 passed. That matches main, with no `REPLAY_STALE`. - New unit tests show that the act and judgment prompts open with the title, that two tests with different titles send an identical system prompt, and that a secret value in a title is redacted in the act prompt (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/agent-entry-prompt.test.ts`). <!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. --> <a href="https://cubic.dev/pr/tester-army/e2e/pull/1344?utm_source=github" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-no-image-dialog="true"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-light.svg"><img alt="View guided diff" src="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/review-in-cubic-light.svg"></picture></a> <a href="https://www.cubic.dev/action/auto-fix/pr/tester-army/e2e/1344?returnTo=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Ftester-army%2Fe2e%2Fpull%2F1344&source=description" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-no-image-dialog="true"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/turn-on-auto-fix-dark.svg"><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/turn-on-auto-fix-light.svg"><img alt="Turn on auto-fix" src="https://www.cubic.dev/buttons/turn-on-auto-fix-light.svg"></picture></a> <!-- End of auto-generated description by cubic. -->

title: fix(decision): leave nothing out when the loaded config changes
body: `decisionFilter` (#1206, new in #1210) runs every test when a run-all file changes, but it recognized the config only by the names `e2e.config.*`. A run with `--config e2e.ci.config.ts` sent a change to that file to the decision model like any other file. In the pre-release bug bash, 3 of 4 decision models left out all 78 testbed tests for a config-only change. - e2e hands filters `context.configFile`, the config the run loaded, relative to `changes.root` as `changes.files` spells it (`packages/e2e/src/run/test-filters.ts`). The directory is resolved on disk and the file keeps its own name, so a symlinked config matches the path git lists. It is `undefined` for a config object or a config outside the repository. - `decisionFilter` leaves nothing out when that file changes, whatever its name, compared in NFC (`packages/decision/src/filter.ts`). With an older e2e that does not set the field, it falls back to the name list. - `configFile` is optional on the public `TestFilterContext`, so a hand-built context in a user's filter tests still compiles. Not covered: files the config imports still go to the model. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A scratch git repo with three tests and a custom `e2e.ci.config.ts` using `decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev') })`, with only that config changed. Built CLI, `e2e list --config e2e.ci.config.ts --changed-since HEAD~1`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | model call, 2 of 3 tests left out | no model call, all 3 kept | ```text # main judging 1 file changed since 42794d4 decision: asking typesafe-ai/jev about 3 tests in 3 files decision kept 1 of 3 tests, left out 2 (1 call, 867 tokens, <$0.0001) tests/cart.e2e.ts › cart page shows its heading [web] (left out by decision: 15% likely affected) tests/login.e2e.ts › login page shows its heading [web] tests/search.e2e.ts › search page shows its heading [web] (left out by decision: 15% likely affected) # this branch judging 1 file changed since 42794d4 decision kept all 3 tests (e2e.ci.config.ts changed, so the decision filter left nothing out) tests/cart.e2e.ts › cart page shows its heading [web] tests/login.e2e.ts › login page shows its heading [web] tests/search.e2e.ts › search page shows its heading [web] ``` - The integration test covers `configFile` for a discovered config, a custom `--config` name, a project nested in a monorepo, a symlinked config, and a config object (`packages/e2e/tests/integration/test-filters.test.ts`).

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/decision@0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1206](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1206) [`da13624`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/da13624d31fa6cf2204c7b99f1474d718ca1a02a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Release:** Add `decisionFilter({ model })`, a test filter that asks a decision model which tests a pull request can affect and leaves out the rest, such as `filters: [decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev') })]`. The model must answer `boolean` questions; `providerOptions` passes options such as zero data retention to every call. Needs `e2e` 0.21.3 or later.

### Patch Changes

- [#1345](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1345) [`47127f7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/47127f734f34927b040f85aa7db9f9f6a02a2a7d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `decisionFilter` leaves nothing out when the config file the run loaded changed, whatever its name, such as `e2e list --config e2e.ci.config.ts --changed-since origin/main` after an edit to `e2e.ci.config.ts`. A test filter reads that file as `context.configFile`.
## e2e@0.21.3

### Patch Changes

- [#1219](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1219) [`f589a32`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f589a32195bd9c2501f1ce98a118d18afa6da5ec) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `onAction` to `agent.act`: a hook that runs after each action once the screen settles, for replayed actions too. Use it to take a screenshot per action.

- [#1326](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1326) [`04acca1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/04acca1ef06cb660a1bcd467275aa6b661b4cd29) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.screenshot()` returns the absolute path of the file it wrote, not a path relative to the attempt directory.

- [#1218](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1218) [`58a5cec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/58a5cec116ca79b1589cb78b6baae40abf3e735a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Keep screenshots after a secret fill. `app.screenshot()`, `toHaveScreenshot()`, and assertion and failure screenshots no longer stop once a test fills a secret. They mask secure fields only, and `toHaveScreenshot()` still fails when the engine can't prove they are masked. The model still gets no pixels after a fill.

- [#1072](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1072) [`689620d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/689620d728d04202757ffd11ed001b512b68044a) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Do not report a cache entry as evicted when a custom store rejects its deletion.

- [#1310](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1310) [`329e03f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/329e03f7a81e3bb3a8ca5d6e7c96a9a6f21218a2) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Add `--action-timeout <ms>` and `--assertion-timeout <ms>` to `e2e run`. They replace the config's `actionTimeout` and `assertionTimeout` for one run, so a wrong locator can fail in 5 s instead of 30 s while you write a test. A call's own `timeout` still wins, and a value that is not an integer from 1 through 2147483647 is a usage error, exit 2. Watch mode keeps them for every rerun.

- [#1240](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1240) [`332b934`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/332b934684b75227ad60dbc0cc8c59b818ac48e0) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Add `e2e upgrade` (alias `e2e update`): upgrades `e2e` to the latest release, a dist-tag such as `nightly`, or one version, and moves each `@e2e-dev/*` package the project lists from the registry to the newest release whose peer ranges accept it. Linked packages and ones the registry doesn't have stay as they are. The project's package manager installs them; `--dry-run` prints the plan. Each upgrade sends an `e2e_upgrade_completed` telemetry event with the result and the `e2e` versions before and after. The update notice now suggests `e2e upgrade` instead of an install command for `e2e` alone.

- [#1321](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1321) [`72abddd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/72abdddd961e2e3a7d24c973eeb2783bea43ee47) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The e2e plugin now installs in Cursor, from a copy in `~/.cursor/plugins/local/`, with the same three skills as the Claude Code and Codex plugin. Grok Build reads the Claude Code files, so the repository works there as a marketplace too.

- [#1345](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1345) [`47127f7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/47127f734f34927b040f85aa7db9f9f6a02a2a7d) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `decisionFilter` leaves nothing out when the config file the run loaded changed, whatever its name, such as `e2e list --config e2e.ci.config.ts --changed-since origin/main` after an edit to `e2e.ci.config.ts`. A test filter reads that file as `context.configFile`.

- [#1275](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1275) [`6a59d1a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/6a59d1acfba13745ce126817e3226cee71d033e5) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Update dependencies: the web engine drives Playwright 1.64.1 (and the Chromium it installs), and smol machines boot the matching `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble` image. The runner moves to `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform`, and `@oxc-project/runtime` 0.154.0, `@vitest/expect` 5.0.5, and `@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.28.

- [#1286](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1286) [`a39c1c3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a39c1c30a4de5b62e14ea86f85613f7ecf331c24) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `expect(await response.json()).toMatchSchema(schema)` type-checks: `expect` no longer hands the engine's `json<T>()` a locator type to infer, so the value matchers apply.

- [#1252](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1252) [`3bd32ef`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3bd32ef8ef847368d3a9ad994520309fa39c53a7) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `e2e explore` and the MCP `open_session` now launch a device target's pinned app before their first observation, as a test's `app.open()` does. They no longer depend on the engine's warm-up having opened it, which it skips for a target with an `app.appPath`, and used to fail with `APP_NOT_OPEN`.

- [#1306](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1306) [`3df649c`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3df649c0c651cc94b1c079f65c896414596a56b7) Thanks [@knowbody](https://github.com/knowbody)! - Let retiring workers use the configured cleanup timeout for engine disposal so cleanup can finish and report errors before the worker exits.

- [#1318](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1318) [`bbb13bf`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/bbb13bf7ffa54734711d9b01930f8fc378cc93be) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - `e2e init --example <name>` starts a new project from one of the repository's example apps (`with-vite`, `with-next`, `with-astro`, `with-expo`, `with-swiftui`, `with-compose`, `with-kotlin-multiplatform`, `with-flutter`, `with-maui`). It downloads the example from the GitHub tag of the running CLI into an empty directory, points its `e2e` and engine ranges at this release, and then runs the usual skill, MCP, and install steps in the example's e2e project.

- [#1280](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1280) [`1071933`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/10719338135a1b1123d8fca78fa6c6f08eb8f68f) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Find `e2e.config.js` and `e2e.config.mjs` as well as `e2e.config.ts` and `e2e.config.mts`, so a project written in plain JavaScript needs no `--config` flag. A TypeScript config still wins in its directory, so the `e2e.config.js` that `tsc` emits beside it is ignored. `e2e init` leaves an existing JavaScript config alone and writes its example test as `tests/example.e2e.js`, and a run that finds only `*.e2e.js` files names the `tests` glob to set. The quickstart shows the JavaScript setup, and the [config reference](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/config#javascript) the details.

- [#1317](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1317) [`9ceb071`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9ceb0710c371ee3acf1a67c1db81dabbf7ef30cc) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Every action in an `e2e mcp` session now answers with the test line that repeats it, such as `Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Save").tap();`, so a coding agent can write the test while it walks the flow. The locator comes from the node as the agent saw it and is checked against the live screen first: it must match that node and nothing else, and twins are narrowed with `{ visible: true }`, a container, or `.nth()`. When no locator works, the result says why and prints no line. Fills name `credentials.user(name)` or `secrets.get(name)`, never a value. The new read-only `test_lines` catalog tool returns the session's lines in order as a draft test body. A project tool can no longer be named `test_lines`, and the `e2e_mcp_session` telemetry event counts its calls under its own name.

- [#973](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/973) [`93f77d8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/93f77d81e2e781b79be242ca1743b705074bb665) Thanks [@A220man](https://github.com/A220man)! - A model that refuses a request (finish reason `content-filter`) now fails the step as `MODEL_REFUSED` instead of `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with "No output generated". Rephrase the instruction or use another model.

- [#1284](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1284) [`90e6fb8`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/90e6fb8bef87844957c31fb4b31bd7d2e85d2e75) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `tap_at` and `hover_at`, in `agent.act` and `e2e mcp`, now act on the bare point the model aimed at whenever the engine takes one, instead of snapping to the listed control under it and acting on that control's center. Before, a point outside an iOS popover snapped to the full-screen dismiss region and tapped its center, inside the popover, so the popover never closed. An engine that taps listed nodes only still gets the control by id.

- [#1049](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1049) [`137b50f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/137b50f0c8505a01ca53e4eb4c38df95e12bd395) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Add `locator.or(other)`, which matches either locator in document order and stays strict when both match. Third-party engines must handle the new `union` kind of `LocatorExpression`.

- [#1151](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1151) [`84bd64a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/84bd64ae7554fa8d0d5799d4be7ccedbf26abf41) Thanks [@TheTuso](https://github.com/TheTuso)! - Agent steps on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1 no longer fail with `Invalid signature in thinking block. The block is bound to a different conversation` on a worker's first step or after an earlier screen or screenshot was elided.

- [#1301](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1301) [`82039ad`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/82039ad6d640080f000c159083216c0faad53202) Thanks [@nguyenvanhieu1710](https://github.com/nguyenvanhieu1710)! - Record `observationTruncated: true` on an agent step when any semantic observation in the step was incomplete.

- [#1239](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1239) [`d7ec0ec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d7ec0ecf4458d8818087bd7c9cb31bd1dc241eed) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `screen.tree()` and `screen.debug()`. `tree()` returns the whole screen as the agent reads it, one node per line with secrets redacted. `debug()` prints the same text to the test's output.

- [#1314](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1314) [`b8cb0b3`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b8cb0b34a4dfeb3919468f189442ae3df662dd0f) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now gives a coding agent a fast loop for fixing a test: rerun only that test by `file:line` with `--action-timeout 5000`, keep the replay cache on so goals that passed replay without model calls, add `--retries 0` when the config sets retries, don't rename the test or reword a passing goal mid-loop, and, when the test passes, run it one time with `--no-cache`. The coding agents guide no longer tells agents to add `--no-cache` after every change, and the caching guide has a section on rerunning a test while you fix it.

- [#1309](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1309) [`c5e3248`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c5e324854fd523d264eca8e70d69ead6b219d0fa) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The e2e skill now tells a coding agent how to fix a failed test. It fixes from the terminal's failure block and the trace page, every line that evidence covers at once, and checks the lines after the failure before the next run. To see a screen the evidence leaves out, it goes straight there in an MCP session instead of walking the flow again from the start.

- [#1313](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1313) [`f7a34c1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f7a34c1b1250ca71e2418d81a5b0bdae85395221) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now keeps an `e2e mcp` session open between test runs while the agent writes or fixes a test on the web, so a live look after a failed run goes straight to the screen in that session instead of opening a new one. It says when a run can go beside the session: with no `app.command`, with a port-0 URL (unless the dev server allows one copy per directory, as `next dev` does), or with `reuseExisting: true` on a fixed port. A fixed port without `reuseExisting` makes the run fail with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`, so the agent offers `reuseExisting: true` to the user instead of adding it, and closes the session before each run until then. With `reuseExisting` and `CI` set, it unsets `CI` for the run or closes the session. On mobile it closes the session before each run. The MCP server page shows the same cases as a table.

- [#1333](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1333) [`4982d8d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4982d8df256180f0a6d68dd49fba0384794924fb) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - The e2e skill now explains what a frame from another site, such as a hosted card field, means for agent steps. The browser engine's semantic tree leaves out that frame's content, so the skill scripts steps there with `browser.frameLocator` and judges the frame with `vision`. An `agent.act` whose only change is inside that frame records no replay and runs live every run.

- [#1311](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1311) [`74c2b73`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/74c2b737401c3927084eaf568b55b4854375c699) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now tells a coding agent to start each test near the screen it checks, so every rerun skips the steps that lead there: in a browser a saved session instead of the sign-in form and `app.open` on the screen's path, on a device `device.openLink`, and data created through the app's API in a `test.extend` fixture. A test across several screens grows one screen at a time, with the goals already verified replaying from the cache. Core concepts says the same in one bullet.

- [#1343](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1343) [`1ed4de1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1ed4de1158b0490e5f09fcf14ed24ec55bb0e2a3) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled agent skill now tells a coding agent to replace a fixed-time sleep with `agent.waitFor` on the state it was waiting for, or a matcher with a longer `timeout` when a locator names that state.

- [#1216](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1216) [`19f3ca2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/19f3ca2916cbfdd76589e3c68266a2d16887a041) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The run telemetry event now sorts executed tests by how the replay cache carried them (`tests_code_only`, `tests_replayed`, `tests_assisted`, `tests_live`), counts `agent.act` steps that ran with the cache off (`agent_steps_uncached`), why steps missed the cache or handed off (`agent_miss_reasons`, `agent_handoff_reasons`), and the model calls by agent entry point (`model_calls_act`, `model_calls_assert`, `model_calls_extract`, `model_calls_waitfor`).

- [#1206](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1206) [`da13624`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/da13624d31fa6cf2204c7b99f1474d718ca1a02a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add test filters: `filters: [decisionFilter({ model })]` from `@e2e-dev/decision` leaves out the tests a change can't affect. They run with `--changed-since <ref>`, such as `origin/main` on a pull request; without the flag every test runs. `e2e list --changed-since origin/main` previews the decision, and left-out tests show in the pull request comment, `junit.xml`, and the report. A run with nothing to run starts no engine or app, and after Ctrl-C, or a reporter that runs past its deadline, the CLI exits as soon as the output is written.

- [#1239](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1239) [`d7ec0ec`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d7ec0ecf4458d8818087bd7c9cb31bd1dc241eed) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Print `console.log` and other test output when the `list` reporter is off. With `--reporter json`, all user output goes to stderr, so stdout holds only the report.

- [#1323](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1323) [`0f6c3ef`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0f6c3ef31840f40fe9a987523abb98eec914f17a) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - Put the test's title path in agent prompts. Under `e2e run`, every step of the built-in agent and every judgment behind `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` now opens with a `Test: <describe> > <test>` line, and a custom executor reads the title path as `ctx.attempt.titlePath`. The line goes in the step's prompt, not the system prompt, so provider prompt caching still serves every test of a run, and existing recordings keep replaying.

- [#1238](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1238) [`7b6ac53`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7b6ac5327eb6f98fb51f7e22184fdd5274905e75) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Print a notice after a command when a newer `e2e` is on npm, with the install command for the project's package manager. The registry is checked once a day. Nothing prints in CI or when piped. Set `E2E_UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=1` or `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` to turn it off. `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turn it off too.

- [#996](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/996) [`7e72ea2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7e72ea2d8d2cd05ef04b34c6f084d9908b348806) Thanks [@rudycelekli](https://github.com/rudycelekli)! - Reject an invalid `shard` passed to `run()` or `list()` with `INVALID_CONFIG`, enforcing the same numeric bounds as the `--shard` flag. Both shard fields are required.

- [#1209](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1209) [`ef977f4`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/ef977f4856da009cac26d78d2e9bb14e5991ee41) Thanks [@knowbody](https://github.com/knowbody)! - Engine disposal receives optional revocable permission to preserve run-owned resources for a replacement worker. Final shutdown, forced termination, and parent disconnect revoke that permission while disposal is pending. Each worker still invokes an engine's disposal hook one time. Missing permission requests final cleanup, including direct and standalone calls.

title: fix(urls): keep a trailing DNS dot from merging sites
body: An absolute hostname such as `bank.example.com.` is the same site as `bank.example.com`. `siteOf` kept the trailing dot as an empty label, so every such host collapsed to `com.` or `uk.` and `sameSite` treated them as one site. Secrets, headers, and frame reads for one app then applied to another. The new unit case fails on main (`www.bank.example.com.` reads as `com.`, and `https://evil.com./steal` matches that site) and passes after the dot is dropped before the labels are split. Existing registrable-domain cases are unchanged. Test: `packages/e2e/tests/unit/urls.test.ts` (trailing DNS dot).

title: fix(urls): allow plain HTTP for an absolute loopback name
body: localhost. is the same loopback host as localhost. isLoopbackHost kept the trailing dot, so plain HTTP to that name was rejected and a schemeless localhost.:3000 was given https. The new unit case fails on main (isLoopbackHost('localhost.') is false, and normalizeBaseUrl('http://localhost.:3000') throws) and passes after the absolute-DNS dot is dropped. Other loopback names are unchanged. Test: packages/e2e/tests/unit/urls.test.ts (absolute-DNS loopback name).

title: feat(locator): add locator.or(other) unions (Playwright parity)
body: Closes #832. `locator.or(other)` unions two locators: the result matches the nodes either one matches, each node once, in document order. ```ts await expect(screen.getByRole('tab', 'Discover').or(screen.getByRole('tab', 'Odkrywaj'))).toBeVisible(); ``` ## Why an expression kind The union is resolved inside one engine `locate` call, not by calling `locate` twice from core. One call is forced: `session.locate` mints one revision per call (`packages/e2e/src/engine/session.ts:272-295`) and web ref ids are sequential per read (`packages/web/src/refs.ts:31-34`), so two calls cannot dedupe a node both branches match, cannot restore document order, and would churn `NODE_STALE` on every later read against the other subset. As a `LocatorExpression` kind the union rides the runner's existing polling, strictness, and staleness paths untouched, and every label an assertion failure or report prints comes from `describeExpression`, which is what fixes the issue's real complaint: `expect.poll` timeout messages carry no locator at all. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[LocatorImpl.or] --> B[or expression kind] B --> C[core reference interpreter] B --> D[web: project to Playwright locator.or] B --> E[mobile: union over projected tree] ``` ## What lands - Core: `or` kind in the contract (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`), interpreter case unioning by node identity in `tree.all` order (`packages/e2e/src/engine/resolve.ts`), `orExpression`, `describeExpression` rendering `a.or(b)`, and `expressionHints` answering `{}` (no single arm's role or name is truthful for a union) in `packages/e2e/src/locator/expression.ts`; `LocatorImpl.or` behind the `ownLocator` same-screen guard, so a foreign-screen locator or a non-locator fails `INVALID_LOCATOR` before any step (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts`); public `Locator.or` (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts`) plus `sdk-types.ts` compile-time assertions, including that `screen.or` must not exist. - Actions, reads, and single-node matchers on a union still require exactly one match: two matches throw `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` at once (zero polling), absence still polls to `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. Set matchers count the deduped union. - Web: projects onto Playwright's own `locator.or` (`packages/web/src/locators.ts`), so scopes, `has` targets, positions, and filters compose after a union. A union branch that is a `getByDisplayValue` query, an exact-string `getByLabel`, or reaches a nested frame fails `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Framed unions are refused by the synchronous `rejectFramedUnion` pre-pass in `WebSurface.locate` before frame validation, because `validateFrames` walks a flat `frameSelectors` list as a nested chain and would otherwise turn the documented instant rejection into a retried `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` that burns the action timeout. `frame(f) >> or(a, b)` stays supported: the union projects inside the one frame scope. - Mobile: unions over the projected accessibility tree in document order (`packages/mobile/src/locate.ts`); a framed branch keeps the existing per-branch `FRAME_NOT_FOUND`. - Docs (`screen.mdx`, `engine.mdx`, `migrate/playwright.mdx`, `writing-an-engine.mdx`), the `skills/e2e` writing-tests bullet, three minor changesets, and the mobile peer floor raise to `>=0.18.0 <1` (an engine without the `or` case cannot serve a core that emits it). No new error codes. `ENGINE_SPI_VERSION` stays 1; the kind is additive and old engines never receive it from old cores. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI on the testbed against real Chromium, temp suite deleted after: - a union whose second branch alone matches passes `toBeVisible()` with no hand-written poll, including the language-switch shape where the target appears mid-assertion; - a two-match tap fails `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` after 95 ms against a 5 s timeout, proving the at-once (non-polling) path; - a no-match union polls and fails `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` after 2.1 s of a 2 s timeout; - both branches render in the error and in the `summary.md` step label: `getByRole("tab", name: "Open").or(getByRole("tab", name: "Done"))`. - Full gates on this branch, each exit 0: `pnpm check` (lint, fallow, typecheck incl. `sdk-types.ts`, error codes, peer ranges, docs), `pnpm test` (workspace unit + integration), `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` (71 passed), the web crosscheck in fixture mode, the mobile golden trees (53 passed), and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` (91/91). - Committed-recording agent replay with `CI=1`, and once with `--strict-cache`: identical results on main and this branch (26 replayed steps pass; the same 7 failures are the key-less `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: Unauthenticated` of a fork), no `REPLAY_STALE`. - `playwright-core@1.63.0` carries chainable `Locator.or` (`types/types.d.ts:16449`), which the web projection relies on for scope and `has` composition; unit and integration tests cover those shapes. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `locator.or` does not exist; the workaround is `expect.poll(async () => (await a.isVisible()) \|\| (await b.isVisible()))` and its timeout message names no locator | `expect(a.or(b)).toBeVisible()` waits for one node under either name; `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, and the report step label all render `getByRole("tab", name: "Open").or(getByRole("tab", name: "Done"))` | | a framed union, once expressible, would fail as a polled `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` | rejected as `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, non-retryable, before any frame round trip (verified under 5 ms against a 5 s budget) | Cannot verify locally: testbed `test:agent`/`test:dogfood` and the 8 unrecorded benchmark agent steps (a fork PR has no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, they call the model for exactly those steps), the mobile benchmark suites (need a simulator/emulator), and the Node 24/26 CI matrices.

title: fix(cli): reject an empty --reporter instead of running with no reporters
body:
## What and why

- `--reporter ''`, `--reporter ','`, or `--reporter "$REPORTERS"` with the variable unset parsed to `[]`, and that list replaced every configured reporter. A failing run printed nothing to the terminal and exited 1.
- `parseReporters` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts:145`) now throws `InvalidArgumentError('must name at least one reporter')` on an empty list. That makes it a usage error with exit 2, matching `parseNames` for `--tag`, `--target`, `--agent`, and `--exclude-tag`. `run` and `explore` share the parser, so both are covered.
- `docs/reference/cli.mdx` and the `running.md` skill reference say an empty `--reporter` is a usage error. Patch changeset for `e2e`.
- Left alone: `reporters: []` in the config still runs with no built-in reporters. Before this change, `--reporter ''` was an undocumented way to keep only the config's reporter objects; that use now needs the config.

## Issue

Fixes #1352

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`), with a scratch test that fails on purpose (`expect(1).toBe(2)`), run on main's build and then on this branch's build.

| command | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run --reporter ''` | no output, exit 1 | `error: option '--reporter <ids>' argument '' is invalid. must name at least one reporter`, exit 2, no run |
| `run --reporter ','` | no output, exit 1 | `error: option '--reporter <ids>' argument ',' is invalid. must name at least one reporter`, exit 2, no run |
| `explore --reporter ''` | not run on main (same parser as `run`) | same usage error, exit 2 |
| `run --reporter list` | list output, `1 failed`, exit 1 | unchanged |
| `run` (config reporters) | list output, `1 failed`, exit 1 | unchanged |

- A normal run on this branch, `e2e run tests/forms.e2e.ts`, gives `Tests 5 passed (5)` and exit 0.
- New unit test: `rejects an empty --reporter on run and explore with exit code 2 instead of running with no reporters` (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/cli.test.ts`). It fails on main because the exit code is 0, and passes here.

body:
### What happened

`e2e run --reporter ''` runs with no reporters at all. So does `--reporter ','`, or `--reporter "$REPORTERS"` when the variable is unset in CI. The empty list replaces every built-in reporter in the config. A failing run prints nothing to the terminal and exits 1, so there is no sign of which test failed.

Every other list flag rejects an empty value. `docs/reference/cli.mdx` says `--tag ''`, `--target ''`, `--agent ''`, and `--exclude-tag ''` are a usage error, exit 2.

```sh
# a project with one failing test
npx e2e run --reporter ''
echo $?   # 1, and nothing printed
```

title: expect: toHaveCount(0) fails on a frame that has closed
body:
### What happened

After an iframe closes, `toHaveCount(0)` on a locator inside it fails instead of passing. It polls until the timeout and fails with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` "no frame matches #checkout". `not.toHaveCount(2)` and the list form `toHaveText([])` fail the same way.

On the same locator, `count()` returns 0 and `toBeHidden()` passes. The Cypress migration guide maps `.should('not.exist')` to `toHaveCount(0)`, so a ported test that checks a closed checkout or modal iframe fails.

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
test('the checkout frame closes', async ({ browser, screen }) => {
  await screen.getByRole('button', 'Close checkout').tap(); // removes <iframe id="checkout">
  const buttons = browser.frameLocator('#checkout').getByRole('button');
  expect(await buttons.count()).toBe(0); // passes
  await expect(buttons).toBeHidden();    // passes
  await expect(buttons).toHaveCount(0);  // LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: no frame matches #checkout
});
```

### Versions

e2e 0.21.x (main at 69e123b1), @e2e-dev/web 0.15.x, node 24

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

title: fix(expect): read a missing frame as zero matches in toHaveCount
body:
## What and why

- After an iframe closes, `expect(browser.frameLocator('#checkout').getByRole('button')).toHaveCount(0)` polled until the timeout and failed `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: no frame matches #checkout`. `not.toHaveCount(2)` and `toHaveText([])` failed the same way. On the same locator, `count()` returned 0 and `toBeHidden()` passed.
- Cause: the whole-set poll samples (`sample()` in `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts`) went through `resolveAll` and `readAll`, the only reads that still passed `missingFrame: 'wait'`. `count()`, `all()`, `allTextContents()`, and the visibility matchers already read a missing frame as zero matches.
- Those samples now call `resolveNow` and `readAllNow` with the poll's deadline. `resolveAll` and `readAll` duplicated them after the change, so they are gone.
- A positive expectation still waits for the frame. `toHaveCount(1)` keeps polling and then fails `ASSERTION_FAILED` with `observed: count 0`, not `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. The list form of `toHaveText` fails with `observed: text []`.
- This matters for Cypress users: the migration guide maps `.should('not.exist')` to `.toHaveCount(0)`.
- `docs/reference/expect.mdx` (Strictness) now lists these matchers among those that read a missing frame as zero matches.

## Issue

Fixes #1353

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Unit: `tests/unit/expect-missing-frame.test.ts` fails on main with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` (3 of 4 tests) and passes here.

title: fix(web): check a radio or checkbox through its own label when the label covers it
body:
## What and why - Element Plus draws `el-radio-button`, `el-radio`, and `el-checkbox` with the native input under the label's styled spans (`opacity: 0; z-index: -1`), or with no box at all (`width: 0; height: 0`). Playwright's hit-target check accepts only the target or its descendants, so `check`, `uncheck`, and `tap` on the input failed `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (` intercepts pointer events`, `element is not visible`), and an agent step on such a radio ended `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`. Plain Playwright `.check()` fails the same way. - `clickControl` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`) now clicks a native checkbox or radio through its own label when, at the input's centre, the topmost element that is the input or inside one of its labels is label content (`elementsFromPoint`, so a loading mask or modal on top does not change the choice), or when the input has no box (then its first rendered label). The click lands at the input's point relative to the label, so a link elsewhere in the label is not what gets pressed. Playwright's actionability checks run on the label: they wait out a mask that goes away, and anything that stays on top still fails `NOT_ACTIONABLE`. The input is clicked as before when it is disabled (a disabled `
`'s included, `:disabled`), is the topmost itself, has a link, button, or other interactive element of its label at the click point (so `tap` never follows a link), or has its centre outside the label's box. - One `evaluateHandle` (`pickStandIn`) returns the label itself, under the action's deadline. While neither the control nor any of its labels is rendered (a `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` dialog not open yet), the page throws and `clickControl` reads again through `pollCondition` until the deadline, then fails `NOT_ACTIONABLE: ... the control and its labels are not visible`. A tap on anything else pays that one read and keeps `locator.click`, re-resolving, under the same deadline. The operation's signal is checked right before either click, so a read still in flight when the operation is cancelled clicks nothing. A locator that never appears still fails `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`tap did not become actionable in time: ... waiting for locator(...)`) within one timeout. - `setChecked` keeps polling the input's checked state after the label click. - Holds in a shadow root (`getRootNode().elementFromPoint`) and inside a frame (the frame's own viewport coordinates). ```ts await screen.getByRole('radio', '安装').check(); // was ACTION_FAILED: intercepts pointer events await screen.getByRole('checkbox', 'Agree').check(); // was ACTION_FAILED: element is not visible ``` ## Issue Fixes #1276 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `packages/web/tests/integration/check-actions.test.ts`, the `a control its own label covers` cases, through a locator and an element handle: check and tap on each of the three Element Plus shapes; each shape behind a mask removed after 300ms and inside a `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` container shown after 300ms (the review's repros, all 14 red on f74e0e31); a modal-covered and a disabled control that must stay `NOT_ACTIONABLE` and unchecked; a radio whose label covers it from outside the label's box; a boxless checkbox whose first label is hidden by `display` or by `visibility` and whose second is not, and one whose every label is hidden; a radio under a link in its own label and a boxless checkbox whose label has a link at its centre, both of which must stay `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, unchecked, and on the same URL; a radio-button inside `
`; a shadow root; a frame; a tap on a locator that never appears; an action cancelled while its stand-in read is in flight, which must click nothing. On this branch: `Tests 75 passed (75)`; the full web suite `Tests 642 passed | 1 skipped (643)`, `pnpm check` green. - Built CLI on a scratch project whose page carries the real theme-chalk CSS for the three controls (`el-radio-button.css`, `el-radio.css`, `el-checkbox.css`): three tests on the settled page, and each again behind a `v-loading`-style mask removed after 800ms and in a `display:none` container shown after 800ms. `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`, `@e2e-dev/web` built from main, from the previous head, and from this branch: | main | f74e0e31 (previous head) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `Tests 9 failed \| 0 passed (9)`, 180.67s | `Tests 2 failed \| 7 passed (9)`, 65.21s | `Tests 9 passed (9)`, 7.51s | | `ACTION_FAILED: check did not become actionable in time: elementHandle.click: Timeout 29616ms exceeded. 安装 intercepts pointer events: getByRole("radio", name: "安装")` | the two mask cases on radios: `安装 intercepts pointer events`, ` intercepts pointer events` | `✓ \|web\| tests/element-plus.e2e.ts (3 tests) 1.08s` | | `ACTION_FAILED: check did not become actionable in time: elementHandle.click: Timeout 29626ms exceeded. element is not visible: getByRole("checkbox", name: "Agree")` | | `✓ \|web\| tests/late.e2e.ts (6 tests) 6.54s` | Through the CLI the dialog case already passed on f74e0e31, because the role locator resolves only once the dialog is shown; the engine tests above reproduce it with raw locators and element handles. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; title: cache: a replay gives up on the recorded destination path after ~5 s, not END_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS (15 s)
fix(cache): keep polling for a replay's destination path until its timeout
body:
## What and why

- `endScreen` in `step-cache.ts` stopped polling when `END_PATH_DELAYS_MS` ran out (~5 s), so `END_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) never applied and a navigation that commits after 5 s handed off as `end-mismatch`.
- It now repeats the last delay until the timeout, the same line `pollSettled` uses.
- Trade-off: a replay whose route never matches hands off after up to 15 s instead of 5 s, and that wait counts against the step's `timeout`. 15 s is the bound the constant already documents.

## Issue

Fixes #1356

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch project, scripted executor (no model): a button whose navigation commits 8 s after the tap. Recorded once, then `e2e run --strict-cache` on the same entry with each build:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--strict-cache` replay | `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch) at 5.69 s | `Cache 1 replayed`, 8.37 s |

- New unit test in `step-cache.test.ts` ("keeps looking past the backoff…"): fails on main (`expected undefined to be 'passed'`), passes here.
- `pnpm bench:ab -- tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts --config e2e.agent.config.ts` (Linux, Node 26, committed recordings replayed, no model calls, 12 pairs, then 10 with a second seed): every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on both builds; suite time `same` (-0.8%, 95% CI -2.6% to +1.5%; a second seed -1.2%, -4.4% to +1.7%). The `events navigation` counter read 8-10 on this branch in one run and 10 in the other; it read 9-10 on main in another bench, so it varies on main too (most likely the initial page load event racing `app.open`).

unit tests fail on a Windows checkout because Git checks out CRLF
body:
### What happened

On Windows, Git for Windows checks text files out with CRLF by default (`core.autocrlf=true`), and the repo has no `.gitattributes`. 13 unit tests that read skill Markdown or compare list-reporter goldens then fail only because of line endings: the skill frontmatter and Contents checks, the `e2e init` skill-copy tests, and three `ListReporter goldens` cases.

### Minimal reproduction

With a checkout made by Git for Windows with its defaults, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```bash
cd packages/e2e && npx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/cli-init.test.ts tests/unit/report-list.test.ts tests/unit/skill.test.ts
```

| Checkout | Failed |
| --- | --- |
| main 69e123b1, CRLF (`skills/e2e/SKILL.md: ... with CRLF line terminators`) | 24 |
| same commit plus `.gitattributes` below, fresh worktree (LF) | 11 |

The 13 pass only with LF; none fails only with it. The other 11 fail either way (path quoting, symlinks, file URLs) and are not part of this.

### Versions

e2e 0.21.3 (main 69e123b1), Windows 11, Git for Windows, node 22.23.3

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

I have a branch ready with this `.gitattributes`:

```gitattributes
* text=auto eol=lf
*.bat -text
OFL.txt -text
```

`git add --renormalize .` with it changes no other file: the two `gradlew.bat` and the font licences, committed with CRLF or mixed endings, stay byte for byte. If you'd rather not add the file, a line in CONTRIBUTING (`git clone -c core.autocrlf=false` on Windows) would do; CI doesn't run Windows, so this only affects contributors.

Investigated and drafted with AI help (Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI Sol 6.1, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash); the output above is from real runs.

title: agent.assert right after a replayed act fails inconclusive on a page still loading
body:
### Problem

A recorded `agent.act` replays in milliseconds and finishes as soon as its recorded changes show. Those can be the page shell (a heading, the nav) while the content below still loads. The `agent.assert` right after it judges the shell once and fails with `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`. When the step ran live, the model's own latency hid this, so the test passes live and fails from the cache.

```ts
await agent.act('open the orders page');           // replayed: ends on the shell
await agent.assert('order 1042 is listed as paid'); // judged once on "Loading…": ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE
```

Unit repro on main 69e123b1 (in-memory engine, a screen that shows `Loading…` for 2 s, a scripted judge): `assert` fails `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` after 1 judgment; `waitFor` on the same screen passes after 2.

Same root cause as #490 (a loading screen counts as settled); its PR #398 was closed unmerged. If that direction is coming back, this is a duplicate.

### Proposed API

Which would you prefer, if any?

- **A. One more look.** On `inconclusive`, wait for the screen to change (as `waitFor` does, at its default 3 s interval) and judge once more, inside the existing budget of 2 model calls and the step's `timeout`. `holds` and `fails` stay final at once. As a default this changes `assert`'s runtime behavior, which the stability policy counts as breaking, so it would need to be opt-in or go through a deprecation window. Cost I measured with a local prototype of the default version: an assert that stays inconclusive on a screen that never changes fails at its timeout (30 s by default) instead of at once, and `tests/integration/agent.test.ts` goes from 11.9 s to 51.6 s. Bounding the wait to one interval (3 s) instead of the timeout should cost less; I have not measured that.
- **B. Docs only** (instead of A, not with it). A paragraph in `docs/cache.mdx` under "How a replay works": a replay finishes as soon as the recorded changes show, so check content that loads after it with `agent.waitFor`, not `agent.assert`.
- **C. `maxModelCalls` on `assert`**, as `waitFor` takes, so a test can opt into more judgments.

B is ready as a branch and I can open that PR. A and C would need your call on the API first; I haven't built an opt-in version.

### Which surface

public types (SDK)

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). B and C do not; A as a default would.

Investigated and drafted with AI help (Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI Sol 6.1, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash); the output above is from real runs.

title: report: count the steps whose recording was not saved in the Cache summary
body:
### Problem

A passing `agent.act` with no check after it is not recorded (`step.cache.write: unconfirmed`), and nothing in the console says so: the summary counts only replayed, handed off, and missed. A passing test writes no trace page by default, so the reason is only in `.e2e/report.json`. We hit this as green tests that never replayed under `--strict-cache`, and only found why by reading the cache's settlement code: the `act` had no verifying check after it.

Two tests on the same page (scripted executor, no model), the first with no check after its `act`, on main 69e123b1:

```text
      Tests  2 passed (2)
      Cache  2 missed
```

`report.json`: the first step has `write: unconfirmed`, the second `write: saved`.

Code: [`stepsCacheTally` and `cacheText`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/69e123b17e04ed624df16d32f3b1ef95ce22c083/packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts#L266-L299).

### Proposed API

No API change. The list reporter's `Cache` row adds a count of steps whose `write` is `unconfirmed`, `no-change`, or `not-written`, the outcomes where the attempt saved nothing for the step:

```text
      Cache  2 missed · 1 not saved
```

I have this ready as a branch: the tally in `report/format.ts`, a unit test, and a line in `docs/cache.mdx`. Happy to open the PR if the wording and the three outcomes are what you want.

### Which surface

(none of the options: the console summary of the list reporter)

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
