title: chore(deps): bump fallow from 3.33.1 to 3.34.0
body:
Bumps [fallow](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow) from 3.33.1 to 3.34.0.
Release notes

Sourced from fallow's releases.

v3.34.0: fallow mutation, segment-safe config globs, audit sub-analysis selection

Changed

  • A single * in a config path glob now stays within one path segment. Only ** crosses directories. Before, src/plugins/*/index.js in entry also matched src/plugins/alpha/components/button/index.js. Each nested match became an entry point, so fallow did not report it as an unused file. The rule first applied to entry and dynamicallyLoaded (#3513, closes #3490). It now applies to every config path glob (#3541):

    • ignorePatterns, ignoreFindings, overrides[].files, ignoreExports[].file and ignoreCatalogReferences[].consumer,
    • duplicates.ignore, similarCode.ignore, health.ignore and health.thresholdOverrides[].files,
    • the boundaries zone and coverage globs, and the rule-pack file globs,
    • the framework[] fields usedExports[].pattern, manifestEntries[].manifests and detection.pattern.

    To keep the old match, change the single * to **. For example, change src/generated/* to src/generated/**, and *.test.ts to **/*.test.ts. For each pattern that now matches fewer files, fallow prints a warning on stderr. The warning names the config field, the pattern, the count of files that only the old rule matched, and the rewrite. --quiet hides the warning, and the JSON output does not change. A narrower glob can show new findings. Fallow matches a glob against each file path, not against each directory. Thus a line that you copy from .gitignore can match fewer files in ignorePatterns. Globs that match package names or import specifiers, such as ignoreDependencies and ignoreUnresolvedImports, do not change. Thanks @​jleifeld for the report.

  • An existing prop-drilling: "error" setting now enforces CI. To report chains without an error, change the rule to warn. Archived JSON reports with effective_severity: "error" also render as errors. A config change does not rewrite those reports.

  • Storybook, Vitest, Rstest, Jasmine and Playwright globs now accept every extglob group. One shared rewrite reads @(..), ?(..), +(..), *(..) and !(..) for these plugins and for import.meta.glob.

    • Storybook: before, only @(..) matched. Now ../src/**/!(*.dev).stories.@(js|ts) matches, and !(*.dev) excludes the files that match *.dev.
    • Playwright: before, a testMatch glob with a group made every script below testDir an entry point. Now only the matched files are entry points.
    • Vitest: before, a test.include glob with any group made no file an entry point. So fallow reported every test file as unused. A plain (a|b) group still matches one alternative.
    • Vitest, Rstest and Jasmine: !(..) and *(..) now match.
    • A +(..) group in an include glob now matches one or more repetitions. Before, Vitest, Rstest and Jasmine matched the group once only. The rewrite can also make a few more files entry points, for example a.test.jsx and a.test.tsx for *.test.+(ts|js). An exclude glob still matches the group once only.

  • Complexity findings name more callback bodies. A function that got <anonymous> or <arrow> now takes a name from the code around it. Effect.fn("Users.create")(function* ...) gives Users.create, and it("renders", () => ...) gives it("renders"). A generator that a named function returns gives that name, for example load for const load = () => Effect.gen(function* ...). Scores and existing names do not change. A renamed finding gets a new CodeClimate fingerprint one time. An identity baseline gives the allowance of an <anonymous> or <arrow> bucket to the new names in the same file. A file move no longer moves an <arrow> bucket.

  • Runs are faster in five places.

    • Plugin detection no longer walks node_modules for a Vitest, Jest or Rstest project glob. Since 3.33.1, a test.projects glob such as apps/**/vitest.config.ts read the full dependency store of a pnpm monorepo once per workspace. Plugin detection then took minutes. The walk now skips node_modules, .git, gitignored paths and symlinks that point out of the project root. Thanks @​wouterkroes for the report (closes #3532).
    • Import resolution is fast again in monorepos whose packages extend a root tsconfig that references them. Since 3.20.0, each source file checked about 760 configs in place of about 30. On a monorepo with 28 references and 4,200 modules, resolve imports takes 0.5 s in place of 10.1 s, with the same findings. Thanks @​thymikee for the report and for the patch in #3504 (closes #3503).
    • A run with a restored CI cache no longer rewrites every cache entry. An entry whose content did not change gets only its new timestamps. On a large monorepo, such a run is about a fifth faster. The dead-code run also frees its parsed modules on a helper thread.
    • An import through a barrel that does export * of many packages is now checked only against the packages that export its name. Findings do not change.
    • Each glob compile is about three times cheaper. A dead-code run takes about 5 to 7 percent fewer instructions on a mid-size project, and the binary is smaller.

  • The build uses one oxc version. oxc_coverage_instrument moves to 0.14, which uses oxc 0.152 like the rest of fallow. cargo deny now fails when two versions of the core oxc crates enter the dependency graph.

  • The MCP audit tool has a fallow://tools/audit guide. The guide names the five diff-risk rules and holds the styling, coverage, baseline, grouping, runtime-coverage and FALLOW_DIFF_FILE detail. The tool description is now a short summary that points to the guide (#3369).

  • The guidance for workspace dependency declarations is clearer. Root imports of npm workspace packages need a dependency declaration, although npm links resolve them. The guidance covers private and tooling ancestor exceptions, self-references and explicit opt-outs. The policy does not change. Thanks @​VariableVince for the question (closes #3325).

Features

  • fallow mutation measures how well the tests detect code changes. The command makes small changes (mutants) in the changed code and runs the project tests against each one. A mutant that no test fails on survives. The report gives the mutation score over the tested mutants and the survivors by file with their covering tests. It also gives the share of mutants that a test reaches.
    • The default scope is the changed code against the base ref, as for audit. --all and file paths widen or narrow it.
    • --plan selects and ranks the mutants and runs no code. fallow mutation inspect <mutant_id> shows one mutant against the current file. It reads the report of the last run, or the file that --report names. A changed file gives a stale status.
    • The runner is Vitest (>=4.1.0 <6.0.0), node:test of Node.js 22.18 or later, or bun test (>=1.4.0 <2.0.0). The default mutation.runner: auto detects it. An unsupported version exits with code 2 and FALLOW_MUTATION_RUNNER_UNSUPPORTED (#3407).
    • The node:test runner takes the module loading flags of the node --test command in the project scripts, such as --experimental-transform-types and --import (#3487). A borp script is a node:test run, and its globs give the test entry points (#3482).
    • Vue, Svelte and Astro components get mutants in their script blocks. Code that the framework compiler moves out of its block gives no mutant, for example the arguments of defineProps. An expression that holds a Svelte rune call gets no mutant, but the arguments of a rune still get mutants. With node:test and bun test, the plan leaves component files out with the skip reason runner-cannot-load (#3470).
    • The plan prunes the mutants in the default export of a tool config file, such as vite.config.ts, with the reason framework-config (#3483). A mutant inside a function of the config stays.
    • The regex-literal operator removes a ^ or $ anchor, negates a character class, or swaps the case of \d, \w or \s.
    • A run refuses a dirty git worktree unless --allow-dirty is set. The plan prunes mutants near file system, process, network or database calls unless --allow-side-effects is set. Fallow does not write to project files, and the report lists any path that the tests changed. -o <file> writes the report after the run, and the worktree check leaves that file out.
    • With --max-mutants, the coverage counts the planned mutants that did not run. The dry run decides their coverage. A capped run therefore reports the coverage of the full run.
    • The exit code is 0 by default. --min-score or mutation.minScore makes a lower score exit with 1. --verdicts <file> marks equivalent mutants, which leave the score.
    • A survived or timed-out mutant runs once more, so host load alone does not count as detection. A changed result is flaky and leaves the score. retried: true marks a status from both runs.
    • A type test (*.test-d.ts, *.spec-d.ts, or a TypeScript file below test-d/) is not a test file of the plan.
    • --typecheck or mutation.typecheck type-checks each survivor through the --type-aware companion. A survivor that adds a type error gets compile_error and leaves the score. Without a companion, the run exits with 2 before the tests start. A Vue, Svelte or Astro survivor stays survived with the skip reason unsupported-file (#3471).
    • Each no_coverage mutant has a test_reach object with the class mocked-only, none, none-file, transitive or direct.
    • A run reuses the killed and survived results of an earlier run from the fallow cache. The key covers the mutant, its covering tests and their imports, the runner setup and config, the lockfile, and the tsconfig.json extends chain. Dynamic imports that the module graph does not resolve, and files that a test reads, are not in the key. --no-cache runs each mutant.
    • fallow health --mutation-report <file> adds the mutation score of each complexity finding next to its CRAP score. The score never changes CRAP or the health score.
    • The new mutation config section sets the runner, the operators, the minimum score and the concurrency. --setup-timeout sets how long each runner process can take to start, finish its dry run or reload (default 2m).
  • fallow audit takes --only and --skip. The values are the same as for bare fallow: dead-code, architecture, dupes and health. The config keys audit.deadCode, audit.health and audit.dupes set the default selection. A skipped sub-analysis is skipped on the head and on the base, so it leaves the verdict, summary and attribution. A warn-only gate for complexity and duplication is now fallow audit --skip dead-code with the complexity rules at warn.
    • The JSON report omits the block of a skipped sub-analysis and sets summary.dead_code_skipped, complexity_skipped or duplication_skipped.

... (truncated)

title: ci(examples): keep the agent-device daemon state out of the cache and give an infrastructure failure a second pass
body:
The four failed nightly examples runs since Oct 22 failed for four different reasons, none in an example. This fixes the three that came from CI itself. The fourth (Oct 22, `pack`) was a real break on main: #1335 bumped `next` without the lockfile and #1336 fixed it.

| Night | Job | Cause | Fix here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 25 | ios kmp | `devices failed: Failed to communicate with daemon` at prepare, no test ran | cache only the runner build |
| Oct 24 | ios swiftui | `ENGINE_FAILURE`: the iOS runner session was invalidated during a tap, which `--retries 1` doesn't retry | second pass on exit 3 |
| Oct 23 | android maui | system image download arrived corrupt (`Error on ZipFile unknown archive`) | cache the image, install with retries |

## Changes

- **Cache only `~/.agent-device/apple-runner/derived`** in `examples.yml` and `mobile.yml`. The cache held all of `~/.agent-device`, saved once from a job whose daemon was still running. So every iOS job, in both workflows (they share the key), started against that daemon's pid, lock, and sessions: `Replacing daemon (pid 1599, v0.21.29) in /Users/runner/.agent-device: unreachable` shows up in every iOS job. The one Kotlin Multiplatform job on Oct 25 printed no such line and failed on the daemon. The key changes so no job restores the old cache.
- **`scripts/examples-nightly/run-tests.sh`** gives the suite one second pass on exit 3 only, because `isRetryEligible` (`packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts:13`) spends retries on test failures and timeouts alone. It reruns `--last-failed` when the first pass wrote a report, else the whole suite. A first pass whose tests all passed (a teardown that failed) leaves nothing to rerun, so the exit 3 stands and a teardown that breaks every night stays red. A test failure (exit 1) gets no second pass.
- **The Slack summary** marks a line the second pass recovered as 🟡 flaky and says which pass it was, since the rerun's report counts only what it ran.
- **Android**: the emulator system image is cached and installed with three attempts before `android-emulator-runner`, whose own install then has nothing to download.
- **Evidence on failure**: agent-device's `daemon.log`, `logs/`, and each session's `runner.log` are uploaded with the results. Both uploads also run after a second pass that recovered the suite, so the first failure stays readable while the job is green.
- **Docs**: `docs/ci.mdx` and `docs/ci/github-actions.mdx` told users to cache all of `~/.agent-device`. They now name the `derived` directory and say why.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `run-tests.sh` against the built CLI in `apps/testbed`. Another worktree's server held port 4271, so the first pass exited 3 with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` and no report. The script ran the suite again (`full`). On a free port: exit 0 and no second pass. `--last-failed` after a run where every test passed gives `NO_TESTS`, exit 2, `Report (not written)`, which is the case the script checks.
- Every branch of the script with a stubbed `npx`:

  | First pass | Second pass | Script exit | Marker |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 0 or 1 | none | 0 or 1 | none |
  | 3, report | `--last-failed` passes | 0 | `last-failed` |
  | 3, report | `--last-failed` fails | 1 | `last-failed` |
  | 3, report | `NO_TESTS`, report untouched | 3 | none |
  | 3, no report | full suite passes | 0 | `full` |

- `post.ts --dry-run` on built outcome directories:

  ```
  🟡 *Nightly examples*: all 3 passed, 2 flaky on `main@abc1234`.
  ✅ *Vite* · web: 5 passed (40s)
  🟡 *Kotlin Multiplatform* · iOS: infrastructure failure before any report, then the suite once more: 5 passed (1m 09s)
  🟡 *SwiftUI* · iOS: infrastructure failure, then the tests it stopped once more: 1 passed (16s)
  ```

- `examples.yml` dispatched on this branch, cold caches: [run 40298098894](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40298098894), all 16 jobs green. No job printed `Replacing daemon`, where every iOS job did before. The iOS runner and the system image were built and saved under the new keys. Its Slack message says `main@b154949` because the summary names the commit as main whatever the ref.
- Dispatched again with warm caches: [run 40299449250](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40299449250), green. All five iOS jobs restored `agent-device-runner-*` and all five Android jobs the system image. Again no `Replacing daemon`.
  - The SwiftUI flake from Oct 24 happened again, in the same test (`asks for a name when the field is empty`), with the same `ENGINE_FAILURE` on the tap. The script ran that one test again, it passed in 5s, and Slack showed: `🟡 *SwiftUI* · iOS: infrastructure failure, then the tests it stopped once more: 1 passed (5s)`.
  - The new `agent-device-ios-swiftui` artifact had the runner log, which shows the cause: right after `app.open` relaunched the app, XCTest ran the tap against the old process, `Failed to resolve query: Lost connection to the application (pid 5516)`. That race is in agent-device, not in CI, and is out of scope here.

title: fix(web)!: scope headers and basicAuth to the app's origin
body:
`web({ basicAuth })` answered a `401` from any origin, and `web({ headers })` went to every host on the app's site: another port on the same host, sibling subdomains, every host under a shared domain such as `vercel.app`. A third-party origin the app embeds could collect a preview password or a `x-vercel-protection-bypass` token. Fixes ENG-846.

## What changed

- Both now go to the app's origin only: the scheme, host, and port of `app.url`.
- One new option, `credentialOrigins`, lists extra origins for both. Each entry must be an exact `http:`/`https:` origin, else `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load. That includes a `*` in the host and port `0`, which would match nothing.
- `basicAuth` becomes Playwright's per-origin `httpCredentials` array, one entry per allowed origin (`packages/web/src/protected-app.ts`).
- WebKit is the exception. It never matches a scoped credential to an origin on a default port (443/80) or with an IPv6 host. When an allowed origin is one of those, WebKit gets one unscoped credential, as on main, and the docs say so.
- The engine only knew the app's site, so the runner now passes `EngineAppInfo.origin` to `prepare` and `init` (`packages/e2e/src/config/app.ts`). It carries the run's real port when `app.url` uses port `0`, and is left out until that port is assigned (`e2e doctor`).
- `@e2e-dev/web` raises its `e2e` peer floor to `>=0.23.1`. On an older runner, `init` fails with `INVALID_CONFIG` instead of sending credentials nowhere. If #1590 releases 0.23.1 first, the floor moves to 0.23.2 when I rebase.
- `browser.route`'s `route.continue()` and `route.fetch()` add the configured headers under the same origin rule.
- Breaking for `@e2e-dev/web` (`minor`, `**Breaking:**`). The changeset carries the migration note.

```ts
engine: web({
  headers: { 'x-vercel-protection-bypass': process.env.VERCEL_BYPASS! },
  basicAuth: { username: 'preview', password: secrets.get('previewPassword') },
  credentialOrigins: ['https://api.example.com'],
}),
```

Not changed: a header Playwright injects into a request stays on that request's redirects, to any origin. Playwright reapplies a routed request's headers to every redirect hop without routing the hop (`crNetworkManager`, `_alreadyContinuedParams`). This was already true on main. The docs now say so, and a test pins it. Closing it means fetching outside the browser with `route.fetch({ maxRedirects: 0 })`, which costs the HTTP cache and streaming, so it's out of scope here.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- I built the CLI and ran a scratch project against a gate server. The app runs on one port and the same gate listens on a second port of the same host. Each page reports the header it received and whether basic auth passed.

| Case | main | this branch | branch, other port in `credentialOrigins` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| App origin: header / basic auth | `on` / Protected | `on` / Protected | `on` / Protected |
| Other port: header | `on` (the bug) | `none` | `on` |
| Other port: basic auth | Protected (the bug) | Unauthorized | Protected |

- The CLI refuses `credentialOrigins: ['https://*.vercel.app']` and `['http://127.0.0.1:0']` at load with `INVALID_CONFIG`, naming the entry.
- WebKit on macOS with Playwright 1.64.1, headless, against a basic-auth server. Chromium answers in every case.

| WebKit | scoped credential | unscoped (this branch's fallback) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| port 80 | Unauthorized | Protected |
| a free port | Protected | - |
| `[::1]` | Unauthorized | Protected |

- New integration tests cover the bug cases. `protected-app.test.ts` sends a request to another port on the same host and to a third-party site, for both `headers` and `basicAuth`, with and without the extra origin, plus redirects in both directions. `routes.test.ts` covers `continue({ url })` and `route.fetch()` to another port on the same host and to a listed one. Both new route tests fail against main's engine source.
- Earlier, the same tests ran headed on macOS (Chromium). Headed Chromium fails a navigation to an unanswered `401` with `ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` rather than rendering the page. Main does the same for any unanswered `401`, but now more origins go unanswered.
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` pass.

---
Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code). Reviewed by Fable 5.1.

title: feat(cli): e2e upgrade updates the agent skill copies
body:
`e2e upgrade` used to finish with "The agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e is the old version's; refresh it with e2e init". Now it updates the copies itself.

- After the install, it reads the skill from `node_modules/e2e/skills/e2e`, the new version's. The process running the upgrade is still the old e2e, so its own bundled skill would be the wrong source (`refreshSkills` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/upgrade.ts`).
- Writes go through `init`'s `planSkillInstall`: a copy that already matches is left alone, files the new skill no longer ships stay, a symlink out of the project and an entry a write cannot pass are named and never written through.
- `.claude/skills/e2e` as the symlink `init` writes is covered by updating `.agents/skills/e2e`, so it isn't reported (`skillCopies`).
- "Already up to date" also refreshes a stale copy, for someone who upgraded with their package manager.
- `--dry-run` names the copies: on a version change the ones a write would reach, on the up-to-date path the ones that actually differ from the installed skill.
- A copy that can't be written prints a warning naming `e2e init`; the upgrade still exits 0, since the packages are installed by then.
- Yarn Plug'n'Play has no `node_modules` to read, so it falls back to the old hint.
- `readSkillFiles()` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/skill.ts` takes an optional directory.

```console
$ npx e2e upgrade
Upgrading with npm:
  e2e  0.20.0 → 0.21.3
package.json: "e2e": "0.21.3"
$ npm install
...
Upgraded: e2e 0.21.3
Release notes: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/releases/tag/e2e%400.21.3
Updated the agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e/ (9 files)
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Scratch npm project with `e2e@0.20.0` from npm, a stale `.agents/skills/e2e/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/skills/e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e`, driven by the built `packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js` against the real registry:

```console
$ e2e upgrade --dry-run
Would upgrade with npm:
  e2e  0.20.0 → 0.21.3
package.json: "e2e": "0.21.3"
$ npm install
then the agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e from the new e2e

$ e2e upgrade
...
Upgraded: e2e 0.21.3
Release notes: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/releases/tag/e2e%400.21.3
Updated the agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e/ (9 files)

$ diff -r .agents/skills/e2e node_modules/e2e/skills/e2e && echo identical
identical
$ ls -l .claude/skills
e2e -> ../../.agents/skills/e2e

# made SKILL.md stale again, packages current
$ e2e upgrade --dry-run
Already up to date: e2e 0.21.3
Would update the agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e/
$ e2e upgrade
Already up to date: e2e 0.21.3
Updated the agent skill in .agents/skills/e2e/ (9 files)
$ e2e upgrade
Already up to date: e2e 0.21.3
```

- Not run locally: the testbed suite. Port 4271 was held by a testbed server from another worktree that I didn't start, so I left it running. This change doesn't reach the runner; CI's testbed job covers it.

title: fix(agent): say tap_at and hover_at act on the bare point where the engine can
body:
## What and why

- The built-in agent's rules told the model that every point tool acts on a listed control under the point by its id.
- `tap_at`, `hover_at`, and `drag_at` (added in #1282) act on the bare points when the engine supports it, and fall back to the listed controls by id only when it does not (`packages/e2e/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts`, `executor.ts` `dragAt`). `type_at`, `press_at`, and `select_at` do act on a listed control by id.
- The rule in `packages/e2e/src/agent/default-agent.ts` now says both, matching `docs/reference/agent.mdx` and the tool descriptions.

title: feat(cli): run the init wizard when e2e explore finds no config
body:
`e2e explore` in a project without a config used to stop with `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`. In a terminal it now runs the `e2e init` wizard first, then explores if the new project can run an exploration straight away.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[e2e explore] --> B{config found, or --config given?}
  B -- yes --> X[explore]
  B -- no --> C{stdin and stdout a TTY?}
  C -- no --> E[CONFIG_NOT_FOUND, nothing written]
  C -- yes --> D[init wizard]
  D --> F{anything left to do by hand?}
  F -- no --> G["Starting e2e explore ... on http://localhost:3000"] --> X
  F -- yes --> H["Next: steps left, then e2e explore as typed"]
```

- `init` takes a `continueWith` command as words (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init.ts`). The closing line ends with that command, shell-quoted, instead of `e2e run`. `ready` is true only if nothing is left: dependencies installed, a model whose key is set or whose sign-in is done, and an engine target that isn't the mobile placeholder (`continueSteps`).
- Gateway presets now list the environment variables they authenticate with (`keys` in `init/gateways.ts`), so a missing `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` shows up as a step left instead of a failed model call.
- `initBeforeExplore` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts` runs before the explore action. It skips the wizard when there is no terminal, when `--config` is given, and when discovery finds a config or refuses one (`CONFIG_AMBIGUOUS` falls through to explore's own error). It records the usual `e2e_init_completed` event; `docs/telemetry.mdx` now says so.
- Docs: `docs/explore.mdx`, the `--config` row in `docs/reference/cli.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/explore.md`.

Fresh-context review findings, all fixed: gateway `None` claimed to be ready, as did a missing API key and the Settings placeholder on mobile. The ready path also hid the URL it explores, and the Next line dropped the goal and flags. The telemetry docs were missing the new init event.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. I ran the built CLI in a scratch git repo under a pseudo-terminal, using `expect` to answer the wizard with its defaults (web, Vercel AI Gateway, every skill and MCP location).

`e2e explore "Check the cart's totals" --max-steps 2`, no key set, install declined:

```text
└  Next: npm install, then set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, then APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm exec -- e2e explore 'Check the cart'\''s totals' --max-steps 2
EXIT 0
```

Same command, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=fake-key`, install accepted: npm installed the published packages and the exploration started in the same process. It ran with the typed goal and 2 steps, then failed at the gateway because the key is fake:

```text
└  Starting e2e explore 'Check the cart'\''s totals' --max-steps 2 on http://localhost:3000 (set APP_URL for another URL)

MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED: model provider failed: Unauthenticated request to AI Gateway.
      Steps  0 done of 2
EXIT 3
```

No terminal (`e2e explore < /dev/null | cat`): `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: no e2e.config.ts ... run e2e init to create one, or pass --config <path>`, exit 2, and the directory still held only `.git`.

title: Retry tests that fail with an infrastructure error
body:
### Problem

`isRetryEligible` (`dist/run/retry.js`) only spends retry budget on timeouts and `category: 'test'` failures. A test that hits an infrastructure error fails on its first attempt even with `retries: 1`.

On a nightly Android suite (@e2e-dev/mobile), most of our false failures are one-off device errors: `open <app> failed: Daemon request timed out`, or `snapshot failed: Android snapshot helper failed: java.lang.NullPointerException`. They pass on a second attempt, but never get one.

### Proposed API

Let infrastructure errors use the same retry budget, so a test that passes on the second attempt is reported as flaky. Opt-in is fine:

```ts
export default {
  retries: 1,
  retryOn: ['test', 'infrastructure'],
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

We patch `isRetryEligible` to add `|| attempt.error.category === 'infrastructure'` today.

### Which surface

config keys

title: Identify replay cache targets by test ID only
body:
### Problem

We require a test ID for every outcome and every tapped element, and replay strictly against production. Three parts of the replay cache still depend on visible content, so recordings break when production content changes even though the test ID still picks the right node:

1. A recorded target that has a `testId` still stores its `name`, `text` and `value` (`dist/cache/recorder.js`). When a post title or count changes, the step replays as stale.
2. End-state anchors (`dist/cache/anchors.js`) compare names and text, even when every anchor on the screen has a test ID.
3. The agent sometimes records a tap on an unidentified wrapper around (or inside) the element that has the test ID (`dist/agent/action-dispatcher.js`), so the recording has no test ID to replay against.

#1225 and #1269 cover the related case of a list whose length changes.

### Proposed API

One opt-in that makes the cache identify targets by test ID only:

```ts
export default {
  cache: { targets: 'test-id' },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

With it set: record only identifying fields for a target with a `testId`, compare only test IDs when a step's anchors are all test IDs, prefer the identified node when the agent's target is an unidentified wrapper, and refuse to record a step whose target has no test ID. We run a patch that does this today and can share it.

### Which surface

config keys, report or cache format

title: Mobile BrowserStack acquisition failures and an official provider integration
body:
## Problem

I am running native iOS and Android tests on BrowserStack through `@e2e-dev/mobile` and an application-owned `DeviceProvider` backed by agent-device. iOS session acquisition sometimes fails before the selected test starts.

One observed failure reported:

```text
browserstack did not create the WebDriver session within 180000ms
```

Another acquisition failed as `ENGINE_FAILURE` during launch while the account capacity API reported free sessions. Its underlying provider cause is not confirmed. Our adapter wrapped that exception, so the generic top-level error alone is not evidence of a specific BrowserStack or e2e bug.

Application actions, the UI planner and assertions had not started. Raising the test timeout or changing prompts cannot repair that stage. A free account slot also does not prove that the requested device or Appium runner is ready.

Reproduced with `e2e@0.21.3`, `@e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.4` and `agent-device@0.21.29`, using hosted physical iOS devices. I do not have a deterministic public app reproducer yet. This issue tracks the integration and lifecycle questions rather than claiming a proven vendor root cause.

A subsequent read-only provider-history lookup confirmed that the failed session ended with status `timeout`, reason `TIMEOUT`, and duration 272 seconds. The preceding sessions ended normally. This establishes that the failed remote session is terminal. It does not identify which Appium startup component timed out, so the low-level cause remains open.

## Current behavior in the SDK

I checked main at `e9e8c5005aaf94f22551f4cc7c5a85f6d4a6d17f`:

- [`DeviceProvider`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e9e8c5005aaf94f22551f4cc7c5a85f6d4a6d17f/packages/mobile/src/provider.ts) already defines `acquire`, `release` and optional provider recording. Requests identify a run, target and worker slot, but not a test attempt. Its acquisition signal aborts on interruption and has no acquisition budget of its own.
- [`DevicePool.prepare`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e9e8c5005aaf94f22551f4cc7c5a85f6d4a6d17f/packages/mobile/src/pool.ts) acquires and warms devices before workers run. A failed acquisition ends the run before normal test retries can help. Leases that were returned are retained for final release. A remote session created after a lost response needs a separate reconciliation path because no usable lease may have reached the caller.
- The [device-cloud example](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e9e8c5005aaf94f22551f4cc7c5a85f6d4a6d17f/docs/examples/mobile/device-cloud-provider.ts) demonstrates the generic integration. There is no BrowserStack integration package in that revision.

The [earlier worker-replacement issue](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/792) concerns keeping an already leased session alive. This report concerns initial acquisition and fresh state between test attempts.

## Proposed direction

Would an official `@e2e-dev/browserstack` package implementing the existing `DeviceProvider` contract be the right approach? I do not think core needs BrowserStack-specific execution or a second test runner.

An adapter could centralize:

- Device/OS/Appium capabilities, app upload or app references, credentials read from `request.env`, and session/build correlation.
- Capacity and provider queue diagnostics, distinct from device readiness.
- Original provider error codes, timeout and dispatch outcome in redacted diagnostics.
- Provider session IDs, recording links and verifiable remote release.
- Safe recovery after failed creation. Retry automatically only when non-dispatch is proven. A timeout or lost response must stop for reconciliation, not blindly repeat `POST /session` and risk duplicate billable sessions.

The mobile engine also needs a separate discussion about optional attempt-scoped leases. Frameworks with per-test device fixtures can give each attempt fresh hosted state. The current worker/run lease is reusable but is not equivalent, especially where hosted `clearState` is unsupported. An opt-in attempt policy could provide test/retry identity and acquire/release around each attempt while preserving the existing worker-scoped default and native replay.

agent-device should continue owning WebDriver transport, session-creation deadlines and ambiguous-creation recovery. The e2e mobile engine should own when an attempt receives and releases a device. A vendor adapter should connect those responsibilities rather than duplicate either implementation.

## Verification needed

A provider integration should cover non-dispatched failures, provider rejection, an ambiguous creation timeout, late-created sessions, cancellation, partial multi-slot acquisition, release failures and worker replacement. Device evidence should prove fresh attempts and native warm replay on both platforms. Application assertions must remain live.

No credentials, private application artifacts, internal CI links or screenshots are included here.

feat(web): add bounded buffered file uploads
body:
- Add `web({ fileUploads: 'buffered' })` for tests that inspect multipart request bytes before forwarding. Chromium can omit disk-backed file bytes from intercepted request bodies; replaying that body can truncate the upload.
- Read the selected files through bounded regular-file handles, then hand their actual bytes to Playwright's native file-payload API. No HTTP body or destination is rewritten. Path-based uploads remain the default, including their existing large-file behavior.
- Buffered mode limits the selection to 32 files and 2,000,000 bytes. It refuses symlinks, files changed during reading, oversized selections and PDF extensions without a PDF header. It uses basenames and normal MIME lookup. Payload `lastModified` follows Playwright's current-time behavior, documented as opt-in.

```ts
engine: web({ fileUploads: 'buffered' })
```

The common preparation helper can also serve the preferred button-upload path in #958. This PR contains none of the closed #1386 chooser-node workflow. It grants no upload destination or mutation permission and changes no redirect policy.

## Issue

Related to the native upload work in #954 and #958. This addresses the separate file-byte omission seen when a guarded caller inspects and replays multipart bodies.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, deterministic Chromium and owned loopback HTTP, Playwright1.64.1 and Node24.19.0.

- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/unit/upload-files.test.ts tests/unit/actions.test.ts tests/unit/protected-app-options.test.ts tests/integration/buffered-upload.test.ts`: 72 checks passed in independent review. The server verifies the selected binary file's exact bytes, name, size and SHA. The page receives200, and a307 response is not followed.
- Core/web builds and package typecheck passed, including public negative type checks. File-change, pathname replacement, cancellation after reads/cleanup, aggregate byte/count bounds and the default no-read path have regression coverage. A real file-close preparation delay times out before any native call as NOT_ACTIONABLE; a started native call that hangs remains ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED. The old classifier fails this causal control,12pass/1fail. Non-upload classification and cancellation remain unchanged.

| Native multipart control | Path/default | Buffered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intercepted selected file | File content omitted | Exact selected bytes present |
| Strict byte guard | Refuses before forwarding | Accepts exact name/size/SHA |
| Owned server | No upload forwarded | Exact bytes received once |
| Redirect follow | No change |307 target never reached |

These are native protocol and source checks, not a real-agent or production-application pass. Full CLI/testbed/benchmark and model verification have not run for this change; no model or production call was made. A separate real-agent loopback allocation is planned before any application opts in. The complete application upload failures remain retained.

title: Mobile fill can use stale input geometry after the transition budget expires
body:
## What happened

A mobile replay resolved the intended input identifier but filled using geometry from an earlier accessibility snapshot after the form moved. The old field rect was `(40,237,322,49)`, with rounded center `(201,262)`. A later pre-tap read placed the intended field at `(40,126,322,49)`, while the old point intersected a neighboring input. Identifier selection and center arithmetic were correct.

Startup form movement was confirmed, but the relative contribution of capture timing and accessibility-tree lag is not established. This is not a confirmed app or Appium defect.

## Reproduction at the engine boundary

1. Launch a generic two-input form.
2. Return the intended input at y=237 from an accessibility capture that takes more than 500 ms.
3. Before fill, return the same unique input identity at y=126 and a neighboring input under the old point.
4. Perform fill using the reference from the earlier capture.

On current main, the elapsed transition budget can skip refresh. Replay's held-still start compares semantic descriptions without rects, so geometry-only movement can also appear unchanged. The expected result is fresh target validation before fill or clear, with `NODE_STALE` before mutation when the target changes. Existing targeted retry should re-observe and rerun secret authorization.

## Scope and limits

- Observed with `e2e 0.21.3`, `@e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.4`, `agent-device 0.21.29`. The relevant e2e paths remain on main `1a7a331b`, which pins agent-device `0.21.31`.
- Keep the fix in the mobile engine and its deterministic regressions. No dependency bump or global observation/cache rewrite is proposed.
- A semantic preflight reduces stale-snapshot dispatch but cannot make a coordinate-only backend atomic or prove that its accessibility tree matches rendered pixels.
- Replacement and empty-clear semantics are a separate agent-device defect. Fixing them does not address the initial stale target.
- No new hosted-device allocation or run is authorized. Public evidence will use generic scripted inputs, not private logs, sessions, recordings, or credentials.

## Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Resolve intended input] --> B[Fresh semantic preflight]
  B --> C{Identity geometry and security facts unchanged?}
  C -- yes --> D[Fill or clear using fresh binding]
  C -- no --> E[NODE_STALE before mutation]
  E --> F[Existing re-observation and authorization retry]
```

title: fix(mobile): revalidate input bindings before fill and clear
body:
## What and why

- `fill` and `clear` always dispatch through one fresh mobile snapshot and `refind()`, even when capture latency consumed the transition budget. Existing transition waits and nearest-node matching remain in use.
- Follow moved fields and identical inputs using the fresh binding. Missing fields, changed security facts, or incomplete captures return `NODE_STALE` before mutation so existing retries re-observe and rerun secret authorization.
- Reuse `TEXT_INPUT_ROLES`; keep the non-input refusal and shorten the docs, skill, and changeset. No dependency or agent-device changes. Replacement/empty-clear behavior is separate.

## Issue

Fixes #1409

## Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Resolved target] --> R{Input role?}
  R -- no --> U[UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY]
  R -- yes --> B[Existing transition wait when needed]
  B --> C[One fresh snapshot and refind]
  C --> D{Target present and security facts unchanged?}
  D -- yes --> E[Fill or clear with fresh binding]
  D -- no --> F[NODE_STALE before mutation]
  F --> G[Existing re-observation and authorization retry]
  G --> C
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, scripted mobile command stream and built packages, not a device.

Validation head: `7d710946a1d7175e5742b4167a97dec59aa97f6c`.

| main `1a7a331b` | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| Four slow-capture freshness cases fail | All four dispatch the fresh ref with one capture |
| Six duplicate/sliding compatibility cases pass | All six still pass; no uniqueness or rect-equality refusal |

- Owning-boundary tests reproduced 13 failures on the previous PR implementation. The revised engine test file and full mobile unit suite pass, 383 tests total, including cancelled fill/clear transition waits.
- Built mobile smoke:
  ```text
  Built mobile smoke: moved input -> fresh @e42, 1 capture, 1 fill.
  ```
- The four core fake-engine retry cases are supplemental guards, not regression proof for this fix. They pass, as do 3,060 core unit tests, with one skipped.
- Local workspace typecheck, lint, docs, mobile dead-code analysis, and package-policy checks pass.
- Exact-head [spec](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40542676090), [docs](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40542675865), and [benchmark gate](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40542675949) passed; benchmark suites were skipped. [iOS and Android deterministic suites](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/40542676045) remain pending.
- Cubic completed its exact-head incremental review with zero issues across the five cleanup files; all review threads remain resolved.
- The earlier duplicate-identity finding was resolved after the [maintainer's policy clarification](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1410#issuecomment-6447108251). The latest cleanup keeps the original `settled()` signature and separates waiting from the single input relocation.

## Active blockers and limits

- Merged main (`11cffff2d`) after #1297 landed: fill/clear keep one input relocation, `waitForTransition()` keeps #1297's keyboard-visibility check, and `bind()` takes the projected screen. Mobile typecheck, 408 mobile unit tests, the stale-input integration test, lint, and dead-code pass locally; CI is green on that head. #1300 and #1413 are still open and do not block this merge.
- The maintainer's helper/doc-wording cleanup nits are addressed. Human approval is still outstanding.
- No local simulator/emulator or hosted-device verification. No performance claim. A fresh semantic read does not make coordinate dispatch atomic or rule out platform accessibility lag.
- The fork's Mintlify preview awaits maintainer approval. Readiness has not been changed.

title: docs(migrate): add a TesterArmy migration guide
body:
TesterArmy saved tests live in TesterArmy's cloud, and there was no guide for moving them into e2e. Every other runner we support (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Detox, Maestro) has one.

- New page `docs/migrate/testerarmy.mdx`, under Migrate after From Maestro. It has a copyable agent prompt: connect the `testerarmy` MCP server, run `npx e2e init`, port the project settings, then rewrite one group at a time with `get_test`.
- Two tables cover the mapping. One maps project settings (environments, credentials, TOTP, `agentInstructions`, memories, viewport, schedule) to e2e config. The other maps step types and groups (`act`, `assert`, `login`, `files`, `screenshot`, `javascript`, `prepTestId`, `runMode`) to e2e calls: an agent call, or a locator call when the step needs no judgment. Features e2e lacks are marked "Not yet" (accessibility audit, inbox credentials, `temporaryEmail`, microphone, mobile photo-library files) or "No equivalent" (browser region, web search).
- The guide only reads from TesterArmy. The agent never creates, edits, deletes, or runs anything there. TesterArmy never returns passwords, so each credential reads its password from an environment variable.
- `migrate-to-e2e` skill: TesterArmy is now in the detection table, and a new `### TesterArmy` section treats each saved test as a source file and each group as a slice. It allows `run_test` and `run_group` only when the user agrees. For when to use a locator instead of the agent, it points to the guide.
- The sidebar icon is TesterArmy's official black mark (`testerarmy-mark-black.svg` from the brand kit), redrawn as one path on its pixel grid (8 KB) and cropped to the mark.
- `coding-agents.mdx`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the plugin README now list TesterArmy among the runners.

## Verified

- Docs site (`tester-army/e2e-site` with `E2E_DOCS_DIR` set to this branch): the page renders, the prompt copies, both tables and tabs render, and the icon matches its Migrate neighbors in light and dark mode.

title: fix(mobile): pin each action's ref to the snapshot it came from
body:
## What and why

- agent-device tells us which capture a snapshot's refs came from (`refsGeneration`). The mobile engine dropped that number and sent plain `@e4`. The daemon resolves a plain ref against its newest snapshot. So a ref from an older capture could tap a different element.
- Each node binding now keeps its capture's generation, and every ref action sends `@e4~s7`. When a newer snapshot has replaced that capture, the daemon refuses the ref with `ref_generation_mismatch`. The engine already maps that to retryable `NODE_STALE`, so the action finds its node again.
- One case needed more than that. A test's `dragTo` locates the drop target in a second snapshot after the source's. With both ends pinned, the source would be one generation old on every retry until the timeout. So the drag finds both nodes again in the newest capture first (`current()` in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`). It only accepts a node that is still in the same place. If the node moved or disappeared, the drag fails as stale before anything is sent, and the action locates both ends again. An identical sibling can't stand in for the source.
- An agent-device that reports no generation still gets plain refs, so older daemons behave as before.
- Merged with main after #1297/#1410: bindings carry both `keyboardVisible` and `refsGeneration`, and `current()` reads main's `latestScreen`. Overlaps #1300 only in `relocated()`: if #1300 lands first, keep its `NODE_STALE` throw and `this.bind(found, projected)`.

## Issue

Fixes #1406

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. I used the built packages with a fake agent-device HTTP daemon, not a simulator.

- The issue's own repro (`generation.e2e.ts`, run with the built `e2e run` CLI). The fake daemon flips the button to Reopen only when the tap carries `~s7`.
- A drag check over the same fake daemon. It locates the source and the target in two separate snapshots and refuses any ref from an older one. The real client sent `{"kind":"drag","source":"@e1~s2","destination":"@e2~s2"}`, both from the newest snapshot, and the daemon refused none.
- New unit tests in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts`. They fail on main. The drag test also fails if the change only pins refs, without `current()`: it gets `ref_generation_mismatch`. Another test drags a source that disappears between the two locates while an identical twin stays on screen. The drag fails as `NODE_STALE` and no drag is sent. A third test pins a tap on a control found again after a transition.

| main `1a7a331b` | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `ERROR: Expected values to be strictly equal: + 'Complete' - 'Reopen'` | `✓ taps include the snapshot version` |
| Taps send `@e4` | Taps send `@e4~s7` |
| A tap with a ref from an older capture goes through | A tap with a ref from an older capture is refused as `NODE_STALE` |

I didn't run this on a real simulator or emulator.

I wrote this with help from an AI agent (Claude Code), and I reviewed the change myself.

title: Official E2B integration: Android devices and web browsers in E2B sandboxes
body:
Hello! I work on integrations at E2B. We would like to add an official E2B integration and maintain it.

## Problem

We want to run e2e suites on E2B sandboxes, for web and Android targets, without a local emulator or browser. Today a user must write a `DeviceProvider` and a `BrowserProvider` by hand to do this. There is no E2B package.

E2B has an `android-16` template. The sandbox boots Android 16 (x86_64, redroid) and `adb` is ready at `127.0.0.1:5555` when the sandbox starts. E2B sandboxes also run Chromium.

## Proposed API

One package, `@e2e-dev/e2b`, with the same layout as `@e2e-dev/testmu`. Each engine is an optional peer, and each provider has its own entry:

```ts
import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { e2b } from '@e2e-dev/e2b';
import { e2bBrowsers } from '@e2e-dev/e2b/web';

export default {
  targets: [
    { name: 'android', engine: mobile({ platform: 'android', device: e2b() }), app: { bundleId: 'com.example', appPath: 'app.apk' } },
    { name: 'web', engine: web({ browser: e2bBrowsers() }), app: { url: 'https://example.com' } },
  ],
  workers: 4,
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

`E2B_API_KEY` (and `E2B_DOMAIN` for a dedicated cluster) come from the run's environment.

**Android, `e2b()`: `DeviceProvider`.** One sandbox per worker slot. The provider installs the engine's `agent-device` version in the sandbox and starts `agent-device proxy` with a bearer token for each lease. The lease returns `daemon: { baseUrl, authToken }` (the sandbox's public port) and `deviceId: '127.0.0.1:5555'`. The runner needs no local `adb` and no tunnel. The engine installs the APK through the daemon. `release` kills the sandbox. A sandbox lifetime (`timeoutMs`, 1h by default) kills it if the runner dies.

**Web, `e2bBrowsers()`: `BrowserProvider`.** Chromium headless shell in a sandbox template built from the Playwright image that `@e2e-dev/web` pins (`v1.64.1-noble`). Chrome refuses DevTools requests whose `Host` is not localhost, so a small relay in the sandbox forwards CDP from the public port and accepts only paths under a token for each lease. The lease returns that `wss://` endpoint. `worker` and `attempt` scope like `kernel()`. Sandboxes are tagged with run, target, and slot, so `sweep` can kill what a dead worker left.

No change to `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, or `@e2e-dev/mobile`. iOS is not possible on E2B (it needs macOS hardware).

## Status

Both paths work on our side:

- Android: on a branch, with the built CLI and 2 workers, the provider leased 2 sandboxes in parallel, ran locator tests against Settings, returned screenshots, and released both sandboxes (about 20s to prepare).
- Web: a probe connected Playwright over CDP through the relay and loaded a page. A request without the token, or with a wrong one, gets 404.

If you agree with this approach, I will open one PR with the package, unit tests, `docs/integrations/e2b.mdx`, an example, and a changeset.

## Which surface

docs only (new integration package; no change to existing packages)

title: scripts: the shared peer-range core and the pr-policy GitHub layer have no unit tests
body:
### Problem

Two modules under `scripts/` carry logic whose failure is quiet and expensive, and neither has a unit test today.

`scripts/public-packages.ts` is the peer-range core that `check-peer-ranges.ts`, `restore-peer-ranges.ts`, and `canary-changeset.ts` share. It decides which packages under `packages/` publish, builds the `>=<version> <next major>` range every public package keeps on another (`@e2e-dev/web` on `e2e` reads `>=0.18.0 <1` today), and recognizes that shape again, which is what notices when a canary snapshot's exact pin survived a publish and landed on main. `restore-peer-ranges.ts` rewrites pins through `widePeerRange()`, and `check-peer-ranges.ts` accepts nothing else through `isWidePeerRange()`, so the ceiling-must-be-next-major comparison is what stands between a wrong pin and changesets patch-bumping every dependent on every release of the sibling.

`scripts/pr-policy/github.ts` is the API layer `check.ts` and `sweep.ts` call to label, comment, and close community pull requests. The sweep closes up to 20 PRs per run at its cap, and its decisions hang on matches this file makes: only the bot's own marker comment counts as the check's comment (`policyComment`), and `flag` decides between rewriting a comment in place and deleting and reposting one. #1329's fresh-context review fixed an "anyone could plant the marker comment" bug in exactly this layer; with no test over it, the same class of regression would land silently.

### How to see it today

```text
$ ls scripts/*.test.ts scripts/*/*.test.ts
scripts/bench-ab/compare.test.ts
scripts/bench-ab/stats.test.ts
scripts/changeset-bumps.test.ts
scripts/check-error-codes.test.ts
scripts/docs-examples.test.ts
scripts/examples-nightly/format.test.ts
scripts/install-scripts.test.ts
scripts/oxlint-plugin/no-chained-type-assertions.test.ts
scripts/oxlint-plugin/no-unchecked-json.test.ts
scripts/pr-policy/rules.test.ts
```

`scripts/public-packages.ts` and `scripts/pr-policy/github.ts` are not in the list. The policy rules beside them are tested (`rules.test.ts`, 12 tests), and every gate the scripts run in passes today, so nothing current fails: the gap only opens when one of these two modules regresses, and then all gates stay green while the behavior changes. An example of how far a silent break reaches: if `isWidePeerRange` stopped comparing the ceiling to the next major, `check-peer-ranges.ts` would accept `>=0.15.0 <2` from a committed canary output, `pnpm check` would pass, and the first consumer updating `e2e` alone would hit an exact peer npm refuses.

### Proposed fix

Two test files, following the existing `node --test` pattern:

- `scripts/public-packages.test.ts` over `widePeerRange` (the floor with the prerelease suffix dropped, a non-semver version refused), `isWidePeerRange` (the produced shape at any floor, and the refusals: a caret, a bare floor, an exact pin, a dotted ceiling, a ceiling that is not the next major, a prerelease floor), `siblingPeers`, and `publicPackages` against the repository's real manifests.
- `scripts/pr-policy/github.test.ts` with `fetch` stubbed through `node:test`'s `mock.method`: the GraphQL binding from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and its error joining, `policyComment`'s pagination and bot-marker matching, and the `flag`, `clear`, and `closeWithComment` request shapes and order.

The top-level programs (`check-dist.ts`, `stamp-dist.ts`, `canary-changeset.ts`, `sync-plugin.ts`, `examples-nightly/post.ts`) stay out of scope: they run at import and keep their logic inline, so covering them means extracting that logic first.

I have both test files ready and will open the pull request linked to this issue.

### Which surface

scripts (CI and release tooling; no published package ships them)

title: feat(locator): show how many candidates each filter step left
body: ## What and why A filtered locator fails with one line that names the whole expression, and that is all it says. With a chain like the one below, `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` can mean any of three things: there are no list items yet, the text is spelled differently, or the button is named differently. Working out which step emptied the candidate set means reading the tree by hand, or rewriting the locator one step at a time and rerunning. `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` only says how many nodes the whole chain matched, so the step that failed to narrow stays anonymous there too. ```ts screen.getByRole('listitem') .filter({ hasText: 'Order 1042' }) .filter({ has: screen.getByRole('button', 'Cancel order') }); ``` For a filtered locator, the two failures now carry the count each step left, in the error message itself: ```text locator matched no nodes within getByRole("listitem").filter({ hasText: "Order 1042" }).filter({ has: getByRole("button", name: "Cancel order") }); candidates left after each filter step, counted after the failure: getByRole("listitem"): 6 getByRole("listitem").filter({ hasText: "Order 1042" }): 1 getByRole("listitem").filter({ hasText: "Order 1042" }).filter({ has: getByRole("button", name: "Cancel order") }): 0 ``` The counts are read after the failure, one immediate resolve per prefix on a short fresh deadline, and the message says so, because a page that changes between the failing attempt and the diagnostic pass can disagree with it. The step labels reuse the existing expression rendering, so nothing new learns to describe a locator, and the text goes through the run's redaction at record time like any error message. A few boundaries keep the message quiet when the lines would say nothing. A locator with no filter step, an index-only chain, and a union root keep today's message. If the diagnostic pass cannot read, the failure stands without the lines, since a diagnostic must not fail the failure. `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` keeps its `matches` detail and gains the same lines. No new API and no wire change. The counts live in the message text, `report-v1` bounds the message through `serializeError` as before, and error codes, exit codes, and the public type surface are unchanged. CONTRIBUTING.md's stability policy does not cover the exact text of error messages. ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/locator/expression.ts` gains `filterSpine(expression)`: the prefixes of a filtered chain, innermost first, following `filter` and `index` steps down their `source`. It returns undefined when no filter sits on the spine, which is what keeps plain queries and `or()` roots out of the message. - `packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts` builds the lines where the two failures are raised. The not-found path in `resolveCounted` and the ambiguity path both call `candidateCounts`, which resolves each prefix once through `resolveNow` on a fresh 500 ms deadline capped by the attempt budget, and returns undefined when any resolve throws, so the message stays as it is today. The old module-level `assertSingle` became the async `singleOf` method, so both sites share one ambiguity error. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/expression.test.ts` covers the spine: the prefixes in order, an index step between filters, the no-filter cases, and a union root. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts` adds a fake session that answers per expression, keyed by the rendered locator, so the tests pin exactly which expressions a failure path resolves and in which order. They cover the per-step lines on `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, a locator with no filter step left alone, the plain failure kept when the walk cannot read, and an index step between filters counted under its own label. - `docs/reference/errors.mdx`: the `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` entries name the per-step listing. - A patch changeset for `e2e`, since the locator engine ships in the published package. ## Issue Fixes #1293 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The tests were written first and run against the unmodified engine. The 9 new tests failed on exactly the missing feature, and after the change the two touched files pass in full. ```text before: 9 failed | 79 passed (88) after: 88 passed (88) tests/unit/expression.test.ts + tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts ``` - The unit suite of `packages/e2e` fails the same 22 files on this branch as on the commit the branch was cut from, checked by diffing the failing-file sets of two `tests/unit` runs: ```text branch: Tests 61 failed | 2973 passed | 34 skipped (3068) main: the same 22 failing files, none added, none gone ``` Those failures are this machine's Windows baseline, CRLF checkouts, symlink privilege, and path separators, and they are identical on both sides. The locator-adjacent files all pass: expression, locator-engine, resolve-expression, locate, locator-action-options, locator-basics, locator-union, and locator-wait-for, 296 tests together. - `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/e2e` is clean, which includes the `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` assertions. `oxlint` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the four touched files. - `node scripts/check-error-codes.ts` reports 87 codes in source, all documented, with the two updated entries in the set. `node scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` passes, and `node scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts` reports the new changeset in the pending set with no unannounced 0.x minor or major. - Integration tests did not run on this machine: their fixtures import the runner from `dist`, which needs a full rebuild this box has not done. They run in `spec.yml` on every pull request. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: test(scripts): cover the release package helpers and the pr-policy GitHub layer
body: ## What and why The scripts that guard this repository's releases and its community pull request policy run with no unit tests today. Two of the modules under `scripts/` carry logic whose failure is quiet and expensive. `scripts/public-packages.ts` is the peer-range core that `check-peer-ranges.ts`, `restore-peer-ranges.ts`, and `canary-changeset.ts` share: it decides which packages under `packages/` publish, builds the `>= ` range every public package keeps on another, and recognizes that shape again, which is what notices when a canary pin survived a publish and landed on main. `scripts/pr-policy/github.ts` is the API layer `check.ts` and `sweep.ts` call to label, comment, and close pull requests, and the sweep closes up to 20 community PRs per day at its cap, so a regression in its request shapes or its comment matching lands on someone else's repository before anyone sees a red build. The test suite under `scripts/` covers ten files already, and the policy's own rules are tested in `scripts/pr-policy/rules.test.ts`, but nothing covers the range shape or the GitHub layer underneath it. This PR adds the two missing test files and changes no production code, so the checks the scripts already run in CI are also what exercises the new tests. ## What changed - `scripts/public-packages.test.ts` covers `widePeerRange`, the floor with the prerelease suffix dropped and a non-semver version refused; `isWidePeerRange`, the produced shape at any floor and the refusals, a caret, a bare floor, an exact pin, a dotted ceiling, a ceiling that is not the next major, and a prerelease floor; `siblingPeers`, only peers that name another public package, with their ranges; and `publicPackages` against the repository's real manifests. - `scripts/pr-policy/github.test.ts` stubs `fetch` through `node:test`'s `mock.method` and covers what `check.ts` and `sweep.ts` actually do to a pull request. `graphql` posts to `/graphql` with `owner` and `name` bound from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, joins GraphQL error messages, and refuses a response without data. `policyComment` pages 100 at a time until a short page and finds only the bot's marker comment. `flag` rewrites the comment in place on a labeled PR, sends nothing when the comment already matches, and deletes a stale comment, posts a new one, and labels an unlabeled PR. `clear` deletes the comment and the label, tolerates a 404 on the label, and still fails on a real API error. `closeWithComment` comments before it closes. - No production file changed, and `scripts/` ships in no package, so the PR carries no changeset. ## Issue Fixes #1415 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The two new files pass under the scripts runner: ```text node --test scripts/public-packages.test.ts scripts/pr-policy/github.test.ts tests 17 pass 17 fail 0 ``` - The full scripts suite splits on this machine. title: fix(mobile): recover iOS act from Enter without keyboard and lost app
body: Fixes the iOS agentic flake in `act completes Login Form` (APP_NOT_OPEN after Safari took the screen). ## Root cause (CI run 40408011065 report) - Replay of the cached Login trace: first `Log in` tap closed the keyboard. - Next recorded step, `press('Enter')` on Password, ran with no keyboard up. agent-device's XCTest `keyboardReturn` failed and reset the runner session. - Next observation took 25.6s and saw only `application "Safari"` (Save Password sheet host). Model then guessed app names: `e2eBenchmark`, `Mobile Benchmark`, `Benchmark`, all APP_NOT_INSTALLED. ## Changes - `press('Enter')` on an unfocused field taps it first, as a character key already did (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`, `pressKey`). - `open_app` with no `app` reopens the app under test. A wrong name gets an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` that tells the model to omit `app`, instead of agent-device's "Run apps..." CLI hint. - `withHint` drops agent-device's per-code default hints (CLI advice), for every translated device error. ```ts // agent tool call after another app takes the screen open_app({}) // -> "Opened the app under test (dev.e2e.benchmark)." ``` Not fixed here: `act completes Gestures` double tap. XCTest can't deliver two taps under RN's 300ms window (`count: 2` lands 300-301ms apart; `doubleTap()` and single-record variants reach RN as one press). Needs a HID touch path in agent-device, separate change. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes (iPhone sim, mobile-benchmark, agent-device 0.21.31) - Scratch test: fill, `press('Enter')`, `press('Enter')`, tap `Log in`. Keyboard down for the second Enter. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | fails with the CI `keyboardReturn` error | passes 3/3 | - Scratch agentic test: open Safari, then `agent.act` back to Login Form. Agent called `open_app({})`, passed 2/2. - Deterministic `login-form` + `controls` on iOS and Android: 53 passed, 2 skipped. Agentic Login Form, Text Input, Choice Controls: 6/6. - Original flake didn't reproduce locally (5/5 under CPU stress on a fresh sim). - Self-review: limrun iOS refuses Enter, so the new focus tap lands before that refusal; dismissed, the test fails either way.

title: feat(web): grant browser permissions from a web target's app.permissions
body:
Headless Chromium refuses `navigator.clipboard.writeText` unless the browser context grants the permission, even after a real click, so an app's "Copy" button can't be tested. `web()` rejected `app.permissions` as a device-only key, and the reporter had to write a custom executor calling `grantPermissions` themselves.

- A `web()` target now takes `app.permissions`. Each `grant` is applied with `context.grantPermissions` on every context the attempt opens (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`), so it holds after `app.restart()`, `app.clearState()`, and on CDP or provider-leased browsers.
- The grant covers every page, on any origin, the same way navigation has no origin allowlist (#290).
- Names are checked at config load against what Playwright 1.64 grants on the target's browser (`packages/web/src/permissions.ts`), with a did-you-mean. A provider or `connect` (Lightpanda included) takes Chromium's names, since the engine drives it over CDP.
- `deny` and `reset` are `INVALID_CONFIG` on web: Playwright only grants, and Chromium denies every permission a grant leaves out, so neither can mean what it does on a device. Changing permissions mid-test is ENG-1066.

```ts
{
  engine: web(),
  app: {
    url: 'http://localhost:3000',
    permissions: { 'clipboard-read': 'grant', 'clipboard-write': 'grant' },
  },
}
```

Docs: a "Granting browser permissions" section in `docs/web.mdx`, the per-browser names under `permissions` in `docs/reference/config.mdx`, and the skill's setup table.

## Issue

Fixes ENG-1038

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI on a scratch project in `apps/testbed`: an app whose "Copy link" button calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, and a test that clicks it, expects "Copied", and reads the clipboard back. Same config, with `permissions: { 'clipboard-read': 'grant', 'clipboard-write': 'grant' }`, run on main and on this branch.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_CONFIG`: target "web" declares app.permissions, which describes an installed device app; a web() target opens app.url | ✓ copies the link (200ms) |

Without `permissions` on this branch, the same test fails as the bug report describes:

```text
 FAIL  |web| copy.e2e.ts > copies the link
ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByText("Copied")
observed: no node (match count 0)
```

And a `deny` is refused at load:

```text
 ERROR  configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config)
target "web" app.permissions.clipboard-write is deny, but a web() target only grants; leave the permission out instead
```

- `packages/web/tests/integration/permissions.test.ts` covers the grant across restart and context reset, and the refusal without it, in a real browser.
- Lightpanda implements `Browser.grantPermissions` (`src/server/cdp/domains/browser.zig` upstream), so a Lightpanda target with `app.permissions` does not fail at attempt start. Not run live: no Lightpanda binary on this machine.

title: fix(mobile): boot one simulator when nothing is booted and no device is named
body:
An iOS target with no `device`, on a machine where no simulator is booted, fails `e2e run` in `prepare`:

```
ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) boot failed: 43 devices match this request equally; select one explicitly
```

The `e2e init` iOS preset writes `mobile({ platform: 'ios' })`, so the first run of a fresh project hits this on most Macs. Android hits it too once two AVDs exist and none is running.

## Issue

Fixes ENG-1037

## Cause

With nothing booted, the pool bound one empty slot (`{}`), so `warm` and the worker's `init` called `devices.boot({ platform: 'ios' })`. agent-device 0.21.33 ranks every shut-down iPhone simulator the same and throws `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`.

## Fix

- `BootedDevices` in `packages/mobile/src/pool.ts` now reads the whole inventory. When nothing is booted, `coldPick` chooses one shut-down simulator or emulator no other agent-device session holds, ranked by:
  - phone before tablet (`formFactor: 'phone' | 'tablet'`)
  - newest OS
  - name in numeric order
  - id
- Only agent-device's own fields (`kind`, `target`, `appleOs`, `osVersion`) decide: TV and visionOS simulators, AVDs it reports as `tv`, and physical devices are never picked. It lists a shut-down AVD with no form factor or OS version, so on Android the pick is the first AVD by name.
- On a stock Xcode 26 set the pick is iPhone 16e: numeric name order puts it before iPhone 17.
- A simulator binds by UDID and an AVD by name, since an AVD has no serial until it runs. If nothing bootable is listed, the old daemon-picks path remains.
- `deviceLabel` reads `name (id)` when a binding has both, and booted devices now carry their name. Progress lines, error text, and the report's device show `iPhone 17 (948FF738-…)` instead of a bare UDID.

```ts
const coldPreference: readonly DeviceOrder[] = [
  (a, b) => formFactorRank[a.formFactor] - formFactorRank[b.formFactor],
  // Newest OS first; an empty string sorts lowest, so an unknown OS comes last.
  (a, b) => numeric.compare(b.osVersion ?? '', a.osVersion ?? ''),
  (a, b) => numeric.compare(a.name, b.name),
  (a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id),
];
```

A device name alone is still not unique across iOS runtimes: agent-device takes the first match. A UDID remains the way to pin one.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- MacBook, Xcode 26.6. agent-device was scoped to a private simulator set (`AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_SIMULATOR_DEVICE_SET`) holding iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17, and iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) on iOS 26.5, all shut down. Nothing else on the machine was touched.
- `apps/mobile-benchmark`, `E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_IOS_DEVICE` unset (no `device`), Release build from `.github/actions/expo-app`, `e2e run tests/smoke.e2e.ts --target ios-simulator`.
- main is this branch with main's `pool.ts` rebuilt in.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `no booted ios device; agent-device boots one` | `no booted ios device; picked iPhone 17 (26.5). Name another in the target's `device` option, or boot one first` |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) boot failed: 2 devices match this request equally; select one explicitly.` | `booting iPhone 17 (1F5AAED4-5302-4A25-AFEF-C49DA590E829) (1 of 1)` |
| no test ran, exit 3, nothing booted | engine prepared 29.4s, `home lists the scenarios and opens one` passed, exit 0; only iPhone 17 booted |

On main the error says 2, not 3: agent-device already ranks the iPad below the two tied iPhones.

Not run on a real Android emulator; the Android pick (bind by AVD name, skip an AVD reported as a TV) is covered by `tests/unit/engine.test.ts`. Skipping a shut-down simulator another session holds is covered there too, not on a device.

title: fix(agent): label replayed steps as recorded in an earlier run
body: ## What and why A fully replayed agent.act step still carried the `observed:` label in the prior-step ledger, so the next step could not tell a recording run's verdict from the current run's own result. Replaying "delete Record A" and then running against "Record B" left the model seeing `observed: Deleted Record A.` — a name from an earlier run with no marker that it came from another run — which made the agent fail a step on conflicting input. The cause is in `packages/e2e/src/agent/ledger.ts`. `handoffOf` strips the replay notice from a self-finalized step's explanation, and `formatEntry` then hard-coded `observed:` in front of whatever remained, so the ledger presented a recording run's summary as if the current step produced it. Per the review comment on #1425, the fix leaves the recorded verdict text untouched and only changes the label: a fully replayed step now reads `recorded in an earlier run: ` while an executor-run step keeps `observed: `. ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/agent/ledger.ts` — `PriorStep` gains an optional `handoffLabel`; `projectPriorSteps` sets it to `recorded in an earlier run` when `cache.mode === 'self-finalized'` and `observed` otherwise; `formatEntry` prints `${handoffLabel ?? 'observed'}: ${handoff}` instead of always writing `observed:`. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/agent-ledger.test.ts` — new test asserting a replayed step is labeled `recorded in an earlier run:` and contains no `observed:`. - `.changeset/ledger-recorded-in-earlier-run.md` — `e2e` patch. ## Issue Fixes #1425 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: the prior-step ledger, which is the context later model steps read. ```text node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/unit/agent-ledger.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 6 passed | 6 passed ``` The new test was written first and failed on main (`expected ... to contain 'recorded in an earlier run: opened the customers page'`, received `observed: opened the customers page`), then passed after the change. Related suite `step-cache.test.ts`: 65 passed. `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/e2e`: exit 0. `oxlint` on both changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | ` observed: opened the customers page` | ` recorded in an earlier run: opened the customers page` | Not verified: browser-backed integration suites (need Chromium; no impact — the change is unit-level in the ledger, touches no engine code or wire format, and exports no new API). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(config): retryOn lets infrastructure failures spend retry budget
body: ## What and why A test that fails because of a one-off infrastructure error — a device daemon timeout, a crashed snapshot helper — never spent retry budget, so it failed on the first attempt even with `retries: 1`, and a suite whose failures are transient reported them as failed instead of flaky. The retry policy in `packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts` only accepted timeouts and `category: 'test'` failures, so infrastructure errors were excluded entirely. New config key `retryOn` names whose failures spend the retry budget. Default is `['test']`, which is exactly the old behavior, so existing configs keep working unchanged. `retryOn: ['test', 'infrastructure']` also retries infrastructure failures, so a test that passes on a second attempt lands as flaky. Timeouts always consume the budget whatever `retryOn` says, and validation rejects unknown categories, empty arrays, and duplicates. ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/types.ts` — public type `RetryOnCategory` is `'test' | 'infrastructure'`, and `E2EConfig` gains `retryOn?: readonly RetryOnCategory[]`. - `packages/e2e/src/run/retry.ts` — `RETRY_ON_CATEGORIES` and `DEFAULT_RETRY_ON = ['test']`; `isRetryEligible(attempt, retryOn)` accepts a failure when its category is named (defaults to `['test']`); `runWithRetries(..., retryOn?)` threads the value to every budget check. - `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts` — `runOrdinaryPair` passes `pair.options.retryOn` to `runWithRetries`. - `packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts` — `runSerialUnit` passes `members[0]!.options.retryOn`; `retryFollows` reads it from the same options. - `packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts` — `ResolvedTestOptions` gains `retryOn`, resolved from `config.retryOn` in `resolveOptions`. - `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts` — `retryOn` is read from `raw.retryOn`, validated as a non-empty array with each of `test` / `infrastructure` at most once, and defaulted to `['test']`. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/retry.test.ts` — four new tests: eligible categories include infrastructure;
