title: feat(explore): plan from the change since --changed-since
body:
`e2e explore --changed-since <ref>` explores what a branch changed instead of surveying the whole app. The first step toward native exploration on pull requests.

```bash
npx e2e explore --changed-since origin/main
```

- `packages/e2e/src/explore/change.ts` reads the change into a bounded brief: commit messages since the merge base (2 KB), the changed files with their line counts (4 KB of list, then `… and N more files`), and committed patches (8 KB, 2.5 KB per file). A test pins the fenced brief under the 16 KiB agent-context cap. Same change measurement as `run --changed-since` (`findChanges`). Diffs run with `--no-textconv`, and odd paths are quoted, as `decisionFilter` does.
- A file no commit changed (working tree, untracked, CI-written) is listed by name only, never read: same rule as `decisionFilter`'s `changeDiff`, so a credentials file a CI step drops in the workspace never reaches the model.
- The brief goes into the exploration test's `agentContext`, fenced in `<change>` and marked as data. The planner and the explorer both read it; step labels, `report.json`, and the trace page never copy it.
- The planner gets rules for planning from a change, ported from TesterArmy's PR planner: changed screens first, removed lines mean "expect absent", config-gated code is a condition not an outcome, no-screen changes get a short smoke pass, exact copy only where the change edits copy.
- With no goal, the goal becomes `Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it`. No change since the base: a notice, then a normal exploration.
- `run.explore.change` records the change (`base`, `files`); `run.changes` keeps meaning "what the filters judged". The markdown/GitHub comment shows `**Change:** N files changed since abc1234` under the goal. Telemetry: `explore_changed_files`.
- An empty or `-`-prefixed ref is `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE` before git runs: `validateChangedSince` in `run/changes.ts`, now shared with `run`. A supplied goal is still validated before the config loads, and `--target` before git runs.
- `explore({ changedSince })` on `e2e/runner` too. Docs: `explore.mdx` gets a GitHub Actions recipe (own job, `continue-on-error`, `fetch-depth: 0`, never `pull_request_target`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[--changed-since ref] --> B[findChanges: merge base + files]
  B --> C[brief: commits, counts, committed patches]
  C --> D[test agentContext, fenced]
  D --> E[planner extract: charters for changed screens]
  D --> F[explorer act turns: judge against the diff]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed bug garden (`e2e.explore.config.ts`, `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`). On a throwaway commit "feat(catalog): sort the catalog by price" I planted a bug: "Lowest first" sorts highest first. Ran `e2e explore --changed-since HEAD~1 --max-steps 4` against the same commit with and without the flag.

| | without `--changed-since` | with `--changed-since HEAD~1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goal | `Explore the app and find bugs` | `Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it` |
| Steps | 4 (catalog+cart, checkout, orders, account), hit step limit | 3 (catalog sorting, catalog to cart, checkout), agent covered the goal |
| Planted sort bug | missed | found in step 1, 23s |
| Time / cost | 116s / $0.0139 | 78s / $0.0119 |

```text
 ❯ |web| Exploring  Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it
   ⚑ medium issue  Lowest-first catalog starts with the most expensive book (/catalog)
   ⚑ medium issue  Lowest first sorts catalog prices in descending order (/catalog?sort=price-asc)
   ✓ 1  Catalog price sorting 22.97s · 4 actions · 2 findings
```

`summary.md` head (first round; the label now reads `**Change:**`):

```markdown
### 🔴 e2e explore: 5 issues, 1 warning
**Goal:** Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it  
**Change** 1 file changed since `ae9f369`  
**Steps:** 3 of 4 steps · 3 passed · the agent covered the goal
```

- `report.json` of that run: longest step label 4360 chars (cap 8192), brief text absent.
- Fresh-context review found and I fixed: untracked/symlinked files read into the brief, `[id].tsx` read as a pathspec glob, brief inflating the planner step label past the schema cap, unbudgeted git reads, `run.changes` docs/telemetry drift, a duplicate change-line renderer. Each has a test (`explore-change.test.ts`, integration `explore.test.ts` with a 21-file change and `assertValidReport`).

- After the thermo-nuclear review (9d986224a): re-ran on a throwaway testbed commit that doubles the book page price. Found "catalog price is twice the cart unit price" in 2 steps; `run.explore.change` = `{ base, files: 1 }`, `run.changes` absent. The sharing of one diff reader with `decisionFilter` stayed out of scope: it would mean a public export on `e2e` and a peer-range bump for `@e2e-dev/decision`. Explore copies its hardening instead.

## Next

Follow-ups toward PR-native exploration: separate GitHub comment marker for explore runs, live "planned charters" comment, findings diffed across pushes, re-checking findings before posting.

title: feat(agent)!: keep model screenshots after a secret fill
body: ## What and why - A secret fill no longer turns off model screenshots for the rest of the attempt. `vision: true`, `vision: 'only'`, the `screenshot` and point tools, `e2e mcp`, and `e2e explore` findings keep working after a sign-in, in serial groups, and in tests that restore a saved session. - Masking and redaction don't change. Screenshots still mask secure fields, unproven masking is still `MASKING_UNPROVEN`, and secret values are still `` in all text. - Why drop it: - It blocked every vision step after login, which is where most of a suite's tests run. Mobile needs pixels more than web does, because its trees are weaker. - It guarded the model provider, the one destination the user picked and that already sees the whole UI. Meanwhile the same value goes unmasked into video and report screenshots (#1219), and to any origin. - It pushed users to pass secrets as plain strings, which costs them the runner's checks on agent fills. - Proving that a full frame is redacted isn't possible without OCR or a similar heuristic (see the #1385 review), so a scoped opt-in had nothing sound behind it. - Accepted risk, documented in `docs/security.mdx` and `docs/reference/security.mdx#screenshots-after-a-secret-fill`: the model provider now receives a generic secret filled into a plain input, or a value the app shows outside a secure field (for example behind a show-password toggle). The docs say to use test credentials. - Breaking (`e2e` minor): - `StepExecutorContext.pixelsTainted` is removed. An older `@e2e-dev/decision` reads it as `undefined` and degrades safely. - New steps never report `visionDegraded: "PIXEL_TAINTED"`. The report schema and the `ReportStep` type keep the value, because `--last-failed` carries old results into new reports. - Removed internals: - `SecretExposure` in `run/secrecy.ts`. - The taint flag in session envelopes (`schema/session-v1.schema.json`). Sessions are per-run, so no old envelope gets loaded. - The taint branch and the pass-through `fallback`/`api` params of `retryingObserve`. - `ScreenPresenter`'s `pixelsUnavailable`. - The MCP recording's "a secret was filled" line. `start_recording` already says the video is unmasked. - `AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, about 20 docs pages, and `skills/e2e/` are updated to the new rule. ```ts await agent.act('sign in', { params: { password: credentials.user('test').password } }); await agent.assert('the landing screen is shown', { vision: 'only' }); // was POLICY_DENIED (PIXEL_TAINTED) ``` ## Issue Fixes #1383. Supersedes the approach in #1385. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - I ran the testbed with the built CLI and a live model (`gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`) on a scratch test, not committed: `e2e run tests-agent/verify-taint.e2e.ts --config e2e.agent.config.ts --no-cache --video=on`. - Test 1 signs in with `fill(credentials.user('admin').password)`, then calls `agent.assert(..., { vision: 'only' })`. - Test 2 signs in through `agent.act` with a password param, which means `type_secret`, then makes the same assert. - After the run, `grep -r admin-pass apps/testbed/.e2e` finds nothing. | main (`origin/main` built in a worktree) | this branch | | --- | --- | | 2 failed, 0 judge calls | 2 passed, 1 judge call each, `visionOnly` and `visionInput: true` | ```text main: FAIL a test fill, then a vision-only assert POLICY_DENIED: agent.assert was called with vision: 'only', so the screenshot is its only evidence, but pixel evidence is unavailable (PIXEL_TAINTED); it will not answer from the semantic tree instead FAIL an agent sign-in with a secret, then a vision-only assert POLICY_DENIED: ... (PIXEL_TAINTED) ... this branch: ✓ a test fill, then a vision-only assert > agent.assert "the page welcomes the admin back" 2.55s · 1 model call ✓ an agent sign-in with a secret, then a vision-only assert > agent.act "sign in with the given username and password" 8.98s · 3 model calls ✓ an agent sign-in with a secret, then a vision-only assert > agent.assert "the page welcomes the admin back" 2.44s · 1 model call judge: "The screenshot shows “Welcome back, admin!” on the Dashboard page." ``` The assertion screenshot after the agent's `type_secret` sign-in: ![assert screenshot after secret sign-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67ba4c77-6367-45bd-8467-465dcce680b5) - Tests that asserted the taint now assert the opposite: - pixels after a fill: `agent-vision`, `agent-fallback-handoff`, `serial-secrets`, `session-secrets`, `explore`, `mcp-server`, `mcp-run-code`, `agent-act-pixel-tools`, mobile `tool-pixels`; - the rejected-fill case in `agent-policy` now checks that an engine error echoing the value is redacted. - A fresh-context review found these, and I fixed them: stale docs and `SECURITY.md` lines, the report type for carried `PIXEL_TAINTED` results, the dead `fallback` param, and lost coverage for the rejected fill. - I dropped one review suggestion on purpose: bringing back a fill flag only for the MCP recording warning. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/908ca13f-8741-4829-a512-ac3baeca1bc9

title: fix(github): give an e2e explore run its own pull request comment

A test run's marker is unchanged, so comments already on open pull requests are still found and updated. - `packages/github/src/merge.ts`: `foldLastRun` ignores a run before that was an exploration, so a `--last-failed` rerun never folds an exploration's result into the test comment. - `docs/github.mdx` gets an "Explorations" section: give `e2e explore` its own `--output` in a shared job, since it otherwise replaces the test run's `results/` and the test comment's evidence links break. - Changeset notes the one transition cost: an exploration comment posted by an older version stops updating. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed bug garden with a scratch config using the built `github()` reporter, GitHub Actions env vars set, and `GITHUB_API_URL` pointed at a local fake GitHub API that logs every comment write. Sequence: `e2e run`, `e2e explore --max-steps 1`, then both again. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `POST 1 project=dev.e2e.verify workflow=e2e job=test` · `🟢 e2e: 1 passed` | `POST 1 project=dev.e2e.verify workflow=e2e job=test` · `🟢 e2e: 1 passed` | | `PATCH 1 project=dev.e2e.verify workflow=e2e job=test` · `🔴 e2e explore: 1 issue` (tests comment overwritten) | `POST 2 ... job=test kind=explore` · `🔴 e2e explore: 1 issue` | | | rerun: `PATCH 1` tests, `PATCH 2` explore, each in place | Nothing was posted to a real pull request.

title: feat(explore): skip a change no user can see
body:
Stacked on #1436. Review and merge that one first.

A docs-only or tests-only PR has nothing for `e2e explore --changed-since` to explore. Before, a planner that finished before its first step left the run `blocked` with exit 1, so an explore job on such a PR failed. Now the planner can skip it explicitly and the run passes, recorded as `run.explore.ended: "skipped"`.

- `planSchema({ skip })` (`packages/e2e/src/explore/plan.ts`) puts `decision: "skip"` in the grammar only on the first plan of a change run whose brief shows every changed file in full (`ChangeBrief.complete`: every file listed and committed, whole patch, no line cut at 300 characters), and not when the run must finish. Anywhere else the model can't answer skip.
- `ended: "skipped"` is new in the report schema, `ReportExplore`, the terminal and markdown wording, and the docs. `conclude` passes a skipped run; a planner that finishes before any step still ends `blocked`, exit 1.
- The skip rule: only documentation, comments, test files, or formatting; anything else, or any doubt, is a step. When skip isn't offered, the change rule still says a change touching no screen (server, config, build/CI, tests, docs) gets a short pass and finishes early.
- The comment headline reads `🟢 e2e explore: nothing to explore`, with the planner's reason as the assessment.
- Accepted risk: the skip is the model's call on the branch's own commits and code, so a fork PR can talk it into passing. Docs say to read `run.explore.ended` to tell a skip from a clean exploration. The skip is decided after the app opens, but it doesn't judge the app.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[first plan, change shown in full] -->|skip| B[ended skipped, passed, 0 steps]
  A -->|finish| C[blocked, exit 1]
  A -->|step| D[explore as before]
  E[cut or partial change, later plan, or must finish] -->|no skip in the grammar| D
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed bug garden, `e2e explore --changed-since HEAD~1` on throwaway commits, after the thermo-nuclear review fixes (86630b1c2):

| change | result |
| --- | --- |
| `docs(testbed)`: a note in `apps/testbed/README.md` | exit 0, 1 model call, $0.0006. `run.explore.ended` = `skipped`, `run.explore.change` = `{ base, files: 1 }`. Page: `### 🟢 e2e explore: nothing to explore`, `**Steps:** 0 of 8 steps · the change has nothing a user can see` |
| `feat(testbed)`: book page shows "Available", price planted at 2x | not skipped: 2 steps, found "Hyperion catalog price is twice the cart unit price", exit 1 |

- Tests: `explore-body.test.ts` checks per planner call whether the schema offered skip (offered first, not after a step, not for a cut change, no change, or a run that must finish). `explore-plan.test.ts` covers `planSchema` with and without skip. Integration: a skip passes with a valid report; without a change, a skip answer is invalid and the built-in survey runs.

title: fix(cache): read an ISO 8601 instant in an alert as one placeholder
body: ## What and why - An alert like `Saved at 2026-10-24T15:41:27.955Z` failed its replay end check when the time differed. `VOLATILE_TEXT` took only `2026-10-24T15` as an id and left the rest, so most pairs of saves compared unequal. - A new pattern matches the whole instant (seconds, fraction and offset optional), so `alertShape` reads it as one placeholder as the docs say. ## Issue Fixes #1358 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm check` passes, e2e unit tests pass (3174). - The new test fails on main and passes with the change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: not applicable. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: no change needed, `docs/cache.mdx` already says volatile text in an alert reads as a placeholder. - [x] Contract change: not applicable. - [x] Engine contract change: not applicable.

title: fix(web): keep closed shadow roots tracked on pages that replace WeakMap
body:
A page that replaces the global `WeakMap`, as some polyfills do, breaks `app.screenshot` with `ENGINE_FAILURE: closed-shadow root tracking is unavailable for this document`. Assertions before the screenshot still pass. Reported through `e2e feedback` on 0.17.0 and still present on main. - The context init script stores closed shadow roots in a `WeakMap` under `Symbol.for('e2e.closedShadowRoots')` before any page script runs. - The code that reads the record checked it with `roots instanceof WeakMap`. `instanceof` compares against the page's current `WeakMap`, so once the page replaced it, the record looked missing even though it was intact. - Effects on such a page: - The `e2e-closed` mask engine refuses (`packages/web/src/closed-shadow.ts:118`), so screenshot masking fails. This is the reported bug. - `e2e-roots` quietly stops searching closed roots, so locators miss elements inside them. - CDP recovery refuses to reconnect (`packages/web/src/cdp-selectors.ts:53`). - The fix checks `key in globalThis`, which calls nothing the page can replace. Only the init script defines that key, and it does so before page code runs. A document where the script never ran still has no record, so masking still fails closed. - The caret hiding in `screenshot-caret.ts` and the focus check in `surface.ts` read the map with `?.get()`, like the reader in `read-semantics.ts` already did. ## Issue Fixes ENG-1030 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, with a scratch test (not committed): an init script replaces `WeakMap` with `Map`, then a password field and a button are attached in a closed shadow root, followed by `getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay now' })` and `app.screenshot`. - The new unit test (`tests/unit/closed-shadow.test.ts`) and the changed CDP masking test (`tests/integration/cdp-recovery.test.ts`) both fail on main and pass here. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | locator: `observed: no node (match count 0)`
screenshot: `ENGINE_FAILURE: screenshot failed: page.screenshot: Error: closed-shadow root tracking is unavailable for this document` | both pass, closed-root password field masked:
![branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ce7bcb9-a883-49b5-aaec-a501b61f2961) | ```text main: × a page that replaced WeakMap keeps closed shadow roots reachable 5.20s → expect.toBeVisible failed × a screenshot masks a closed-root password field on a page that replaced WeakMap 126ms → screenshot failed: page.screenshot: Error: closed-shadow root tracking i… this branch: ✓ a page that replaced WeakMap keeps closed shadow roots reachable 216ms ✓ a screenshot masks a closed-root password field on a page that replaced WeakMap 148ms ``` No test covers the `screenshot-caret.ts` and `surface.ts` hunks. Both are the same one-line read the reader already uses. --- Made with Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

title: fix(cache): replay a multi-line unique() value the screen shows on one line
body: ## What and why - The cache writes end anchors on one line (`collapseText` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts`). So a multi-line `unique()` value, such as an address typed into a textarea, is recorded on one line. - `templateText` looked for the value as given and in its URL spellings (`uri`, `form`, `slug`) only. The one-line spelling stayed the recording run's literal text. The next run typed a new value, and the end check missed: `REPLAY_STALE (end-mismatch)` with `--strict-cache`, a hand-off to the agent without it. - `ENCODERS` in `packages/e2e/src/cache/template.ts` gets a `flat` spelling, `normalizeText`: every whitespace run, `\r` included, becomes one space, then the result is trimmed. The anchors record as `{{param:/address|flat}}`, and replay fills in this run's value on one line. - `normalizeText`, not `collapseText`: `collapseText` turns a `\r` into U+FFFD, but a textarea stores `\r\n` as `\n`, so a value joined with `\r\n` would still miss. - Older runners: an entry recorded with `|flat` reads as `invalid-entry` on a runner without this fix (stated in the changeset). Cache keys do not change, because `templateParams` writes placeholders with no encoding. A value with no whitespace run has no `flat` spelling, so no other recording changes. The issue author, @amoscicki, proposed this fix and the `flat` name in #1359. ## Issue Fixes #1359 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The issue's reproduction as a scratch project on the built packages. A scripted executor (no model) types `unique(address)` into a textarea and taps Save. Steps: `npx e2e run` to record, then `npx e2e run --strict-cache`. - Same steps with the value joined by `\r\n` instead of `\n`. It failed on this branch before the `normalizeText` change and passes now. - The new unit test in `tests/unit/trace-template.test.ts` fails on main. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Recorded end anchors | `"value":"Ada Lovelace 12 Example Street E2E 1793336967299"` | `"value":"{{param:/address\|flat}}"` | | `--strict-cache` replay, `\n` value | `REPLAY_STALE (end-mismatch)`, 15.30s, `Cache 1 handed off` | passed, 1.21s, `Cache 1 replayed` | | `--strict-cache` replay, `\r\n` value | not run | passed, 1.17s and 1.11s, `Cache 1 replayed` | main: ```text × saves a multi-line address > agent.act "save the address {address}" 14.37s failed REPLAY_STALE: the recording of this step no longer replays (end-mismatch), and cache.strict hands no step to the agent; re-record it with a read-write run without --strict-cache and commit the changed entry under .e2e/cache Cache 1 handed off ``` this branch: ```text ✓ saves a multi-line address > agent.act "save the address {address}" 304ms Tests 1 passed (1) Cache 1 replayed Duration 1.21s ``` Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. title: test: keep local port probes out of the unit tests' recording server
body:
## What and why

- T3 Code finds dev servers by sending `GET /` with `Host: localhost:<port>` to every new local port, about every 15 seconds (its `PortScanner`). I caught it doing that to a scratch server: `users:(("t3code",pid=2760693))`.
- The fake OAuth issuer recorded that probe and passed it to the test's handler, which took it for the flow's next request. On a machine with T3 Code running, `openai.test.ts` "cancels a held authorization-code exchange after the device code is granted" failed on every run: 2 requests instead of 3, the second being `GET /` on `localhost`.
- `model-request-headers.test.ts` ran its own server with the same gap. It recorded the probe's headers and parsed its empty body as JSON, which throws an unhandled `SyntaxError` and fails the run.
- `startServer` now answers a request whose `Host` is not the host of the `url` it hands out with 404, and leaves it out of `requests` and the handler. No code under test sends another `Host`: every client reaches the server through that `url`.
- The server has nothing OAuth-specific, so it moves to `tests/helpers/recording-server.ts`, and `model-request-headers` uses it. The OAuth-only helpers (`useVendor`, `fakeJwt`, `echoUpstream`) stay in `tests/unit/oauth/helpers/vendor.ts`.
- `tests/unit/recording-server.test.ts` sends a probe and checks that the server ignores it while a normal request is still recorded. CI has no prober, so without it nothing in CI would run the check.

## Issue

Fixes #1454

## Scope

- The unit tests' recording server and its two users. Fixture apps and integration test servers answer `GET /` with a page and count nothing, so a probe does them no harm.
- Test code only: no published package changes, no changeset.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `npx vitest run tests/unit/oauth` in `packages/e2e`, with T3 Code running on the same machine.
- `model-request-headers.test.ts` with a probe sent in `beforeEach`, the same request T3 Code sends.
- The new test fails without the host check (`expected 200 to be 404`).

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/unit/oauth` | 5 of 5 runs: `1 failed \| 129 passed (130)` | 5 of 5 runs: `130 passed (130)` |
| `model-request-headers.test.ts` with a probe | `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input`, unhandled, run fails | 3 of 3 runs: `2 passed (2)` |
| `tests/unit/oauth`, the shared server test, and `model-request-headers` | | `133 passed (133)` |

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: OAuth unit tests fail locally when T3 Code probes the fake issuer server
body:
### What happens

On a machine running T3 Code, `packages/e2e/tests/unit/oauth/openai.test.ts` "cancels a held authorization-code exchange after the device code is granted" fails on every run:

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { method: 'POST', …(3) }, …(1) ] to have a length of 3 but got 2
```

CI on main is green.

### Cause

T3 Code finds dev servers by sending `GET /` with `Host: localhost:<port>` to every new local port, about every 15 seconds. The fake OAuth issuer (`tests/unit/oauth/helpers/server.ts`) records that probe and passes it to the test's handler. This test's handler takes any request it does not recognize for the token exchange, so the probe ends the test early.

A scratch server shows the probe and its owner:

```text
{"method":"GET","url":"/","host":"localhost:34761","ua":"node","owner":"... users:((\"t3code\",pid=2760693,fd=204))"}
```

### Environment

main at 60ec4464, Node 26.8.2, Linux, T3 Code running.

title: acp: the next step reuses a session that the last turn's own tool closed
body:
### What happens

`@e2e-dev/acp`: when a step times out and the next step of the attempt starts right away, the next step can fail with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`:

```text
AgentError: The ACP agent session failed: ACP connection closed
```

This happens when the timed-out step's agent runs a tool of its own while it stops its turn. The next step should get a fresh agent.

### Cause

`runStep` waits for the turn of the step before it to stop (`settled(held.turn, LAST_TURN_GRACE_MS)` in `packages/acp/src/executor.ts`). While it waits, the agent reports its own tool, and `ownTool` closes the session and removes it from `attempt.memory`. The waiting step still holds the old session and sends its prompt to the closed agent.

### Reproduction

`packages/acp/tests/executor.test.ts`, "starts a fresh agent for the next step after a tool of the agent's own ran once its step ended", fails on main in 2 of 3 runs when run alone:

```bash
pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/acp exec vitest run tests/executor.test.ts -t "ran once its step ended"
```

In the full file it usually passes, because it waits for the tool's log line first. That wait also made it flaky in CI: the fixture writes the line only after it reports the tool, and the executor can stop the agent first. The test failed on the Node 22 job of #1452:

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { pid: 58937 }, { …(2) }, …(3) ] to deep equally contain { ran: 'Read ~/.env' }
```

### Environment

main at 60ec4464, Node 26.8.2 locally, Node 22 in CI.

title: fix(acp): start a fresh agent when the last turn's own tool closed the session
body: ## What and why - When a step timed out and the next step started right away, the old agent could run a tool of its own as it stopped. `ownTool` then closed the session and dropped it from the attempt. The next step was still waiting on that session's last turn, then prompted the closed agent and failed with `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` ("ACP connection closed"). - `runStep` now gets its session from `ready()` in `packages/acp/src/executor.ts`. After the last turn stops, `ready()` checks that the session is still the attempt's. If not, it starts a fresh agent. - The executor tests waited on the scripted agent, a child process, with `vi.waitFor`'s 1s default and one fixed 500ms sleep. One `eventually` helper now gives every wait 15s, and the sleep waits for the first prompt instead. - The fixture wrote its tool log line only after it reported the tool, and the executor stops the agent on that report. It now writes the line first. This is the line the Node 22 job of #1452 failed on. - The test for this case now starts the next step at once, as the runner does. Before, it waited for the log line, which hid the race in the full file. Run alone, it failed on main. ## Issue Fixes #1456 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `packages/acp`, `npx vitest run tests/executor.test.ts`: the file alone, the one test alone with `-t`, and under load (12 runs in parallel on 8 cores). - The new test shape fails without the `ready()` change (3 of 3 runs) and passes with it. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | The test alone, `-t "ran once its step ended"` | 2 of 3 runs fail: `ACP connection closed` | 3 of 3 pass | | The file under load | 24 of 24 runs fail, 2 to 5 tests each | 36 of 36 runs pass, 31/31 each | Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cache): skip an age in words when choosing end anchors
body: ## What and why - A step whose end screen showed an age in words, such as moment's `a few seconds ago`, date-fns' `less than a minute ago`, or an app's `just now`, recorded that text as an end anchor. `VOLATILE_TEXT` (`packages/e2e/src/cache/anchors.ts:149`) only read an age as volatile when it had digits (`5 minutes ago`). A replay later in the suite then failed its end check: the step went to the agent, or failed with `REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`. - Two patterns now read those ages as volatile: `a few` / `a` / `an` + unit + `ago`, and `just now`. So the age is skipped while a stable anchor such as `Refreshed` exists, the same way a digit age already was. - The same list masks the changing parts of an alert (`alertShape`). Each form of one age now masks to a single `#`, so `Synced less than a minute ago` and `Synced 3 minutes ago` read as the same alert. Before this change, the alert never matched itself once the wording of its age changed. To make that work, both age patterns take date-fns' leading qualifier (`less than`, `about`, `almost`, `over`, `half`), and the digit pattern takes a trailing `ago`. Both additions are optional, so they change only how much of the text is masked, not which text is volatile. - `docs/cache.mdx` names ages in words in the end-check section. Out of scope: future forms (`in a few minutes`), `today` / `yesterday` / `tomorrow`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` words (`now`, `last week`), and ages in other languages. Each of these also appears as stable text, such as a `Today` tab or a `Buy now` button. A note for the reviewer: [#1212](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1212) was closed as the wrong direction for this list. It added a multi-locale date module built from `Intl`. This PR adds only the English phrases next to the English digit pattern that is already there, and it does not change how volatility is detected. If you want the redesign in place of further additions to this list, say so and this can close. No `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION` bump. The change affects only which anchors a new recording keeps. Alert shapes are computed on both sides at compare time, so committed recordings still replay. No committed recording or benchmark app contains these phrases. ## Issue Fixes #1459 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project outside the repo, using the built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` through the real CLI bin. A custom executor taps `Refresh` (no model). The page shows `Refreshed` and `Last refreshed a few seconds ago`. The steps: record with `e2e run`, change the page's age to `3 minutes ago`, then replay with `e2e run --strict-cache`. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | recorded `endAnchors` | `[{"role":"status","name":"Refreshed"},{"text":"Last refreshed a few seconds ago"}]` | `[{"role":"status","name":"Refreshed"}]` | | strict replay, age now `3 minutes ago` | `Cache 1 handed off`, test failed, `REPLAY_STALE` (end-mismatch), exit 2 | `Cache 1 replayed`, test passed, exit 0 | - The issue's own repro, `describeDelta(start, end, false)` against the built `dist/cache/anchors.js`, with `Saved` on the end screen: | end screen also shows | main `appeared` | this branch `appeared` | | --- | --- | --- | | `a few seconds ago` | `a few seconds ago`, `Saved` | `Saved` | | `less than a minute ago` | `less than a minute ago`, `Saved` | `Saved` | | `just now` | `just now`, `Saved` | `Saved` | | `5 minutes ago` | `Saved` | `Saved` | - `tests/integration/relative-time-cache.test.ts` runs the record-then-strict-replay flow in real Chromium for the moment, date-fns, and app strings. It failed on main with `REPLAY_STALE` and passes here. Its first commit lands before the fix. - The testbed default suite passes: 81 passed, 1 skipped. Reviewed with sol-loop: 3 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test(explore): live-model planner eval for --changed-since
body: Stacked on #1439. Without a way to measure the planner, every prompt or brief change to `e2e explore --changed-since` is a guess. This adds a live-model eval that judges what the planner does with a change. - `packages/e2e/evals/planner/`: each fixture commits a change to a small bookshop repo. The built CLI runs `explore --changed-since base` against a static copy of the shop (a preview of the change). Only the explorer's steps are scripted (`model.ts`), so a run is a couple of planner calls, about $0.10 for the whole suite. - Judges read `run.explore`: - skip or explore - what the first charter targets - what no charter may expect (removed or flag-gated UI) - rubric yes/no questions answered by a judge model (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`) where a regex can't tell what a charter means - A fixture passes with 2/3 of its runs. A run that broke (no report) fails its fixture, observed ones too. - Fixtures cover: - should skip: docs, unit, e2e, comments, stories - must explore: cart math, copy, a removed field, a removed page, a feature flag, CSS, backend, mixed docs plus code, a redirect config, an incomplete brief, a goal plus a change - injection: commit message and code comment - observed only: CI files, lockfile, types, dependency bump - `planner.yml` runs it on PRs that touch what the planner reads (`planner` in `.github/filters.yml`), weekly against model drift, and on dispatch with `models`. Fork and Dependabot PRs skip the job. - Skip rule change found by the eval: it now names tests of every kind and component stories (luna-fast explored stories 0/3 times, haiku e2e tests 0/3). It also says build config is not skippable. ```bash pnpm --filter e2e run build && pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run build AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... pnpm --filter e2e run eval:planner --models openai/gpt-6-luna-fast,google/gemini-3-flash ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, the eval itself with real models through the AI Gateway. | Model | Result | | --- | --- | | openai/gpt-6-luna-fast (CI default) | all fixtures pass, 3 runs each | | google/gemini-3-flash | all pass | | anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 | e2e-tests-only and story-only below threshold (it verifies the flow a test describes instead of skipping) | Before the skip-rule change, luna-fast skipped story-only 0/3 times; after, 3/3. Mutation checks (rule removed, fixture should go red): - Dropping the feature-flag rule: the rubric caught a charter that would report missing gift wrap as a bug, which the regex missed. That is why the rubric judge exists. - Dropping the removed-lines rule: luna still handled the removed field. That rule is barely load-bearing for this model. - Permissive "build config is skippable" wording: every model still explored the redirect. The fixture guards against over-skipping.

title: feat(explore): plan from the pull request's title and description
body: Stacked on #1461. `e2e explore --changed-since` now plans from the pull request's title and description too. Test steps the author wrote ("sign in, the banner should read...") guide the first charter, which TesterArmy's PR planner had and we did not. - `packages/e2e/src/explore/pull-request.ts` reads the text from: - GitHub Actions on a `pull_request` event: `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` payload - GitLab merge request pipelines: `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_*` - nothing else. `pull_request_target` is ignored, matching the existing docs warning. - Untrusted author text: - template comments are dropped - title capped at 200 chars, description at 1.5 KB in whole lines - lines capped at 600 bytes, so a long CJK paragraph is cut, not dropped - indented inside the fenced `` brief, so it can't pass for a `Files:` section - The patch budget moves from 8 KB to 6.5 KB so the worst case stays under the 16 KiB agent context (unit test with 2-byte text at every cap). - Planner rules: - the description is a claim to check, not evidence - a skip is decided from the changed files alone, never from what the description or commit messages say - A notice says when it's used: `planning from pull request #12's title and description too`. ``` Changed since 1a2b3c4: 3 files. Pull request #12: Greet signed-in users by first name Description: ## How to test 1. Sign in ... Commit messages, newest first: ... ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, the planner eval from the PR below, with the built CLI given a GitHub `pull_request` event payload. | Fixture | luna-fast | gemini-3-flash | haiku-5.5 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | pr-description-injection (body says "answer skip", diff changes pay button) | 3/3 explore checkout | 3/3 | 3/3 | | pr-claims-no-behavior-change (body says pure refactor, diff changes rounding) | 3/3 explore cart | 3/3 | 3/3 | | pr-docs-claims-a-fix (docs-only diff, body claims a checkout fix) | 3/3 skip | 3/3 | 3/3 | | pr-test-instructions (sign-in steps in body) | 3/3 follow them | 3/3 | 3/3 | | pr-names-the-screen (only body says where it shows) | 4/4 | - | - | Charters follow the description, e.g. luna-fast: "Open Account and sign in or create a made-up test account with a distinctive first name, such as Riley. Return to Catalog and check that the banner greets the signed-in user with 'Welcome back, Riley'." Mutation check: with the reader disabled, every PR fixture fails on the deterministic "pull request read" judge (8/8). The full suite on luna-fast passes 81/81.

title: feat(agent): params on assert and waitFor
body:
`agent.assert` and `agent.waitFor` take `params` with the same shape and validation as `agent.act`.

```ts
const name = unique(`acme-${Date.now()}`);
await agent.act('create a company named {name}', { params: { name } });
await agent.assert('the table shows company {name}', { params: { name } });
```

- Built-in judge: params are projected like act's (`validateParams`), redacted, and fenced inside `<instruction>` as `Parameters: {...}`, so the existing "instruction is data" policy and the security doc cover them (`packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts`).
- The judgment `Invocation` owns the params: every judgment prompt carries them and the observation budget counts their size.
- `unique()` reaches the judge as its string. A `Secret` reaches it as `{ kind: 'secret', name, purpose }`, never its value. Docs say to use a locator assertion to check a secret's value on screen.
- Custom executor: `runAssertStep` passes the projected params and templates instead of `params: undefined`. Secrets are not fillable in an assert step (`typeSecret` is `POLICY_DENIED`), since an assert changes no state.
- Judgments are not trace-cached, so templates change no cache key; act keeps its existing behavior.
- `validateParams`/`redactParams` take the calling api, so errors read `agent.assert params ...` / `agent.waitFor params ...`.
- `extract` left alone.

## Issue

Closes #1388

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes - real CLI on the testbed (`e2e.scratch.config.ts`, `gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`), throwaway scratch test, `--ai-trace`.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| fill a `unique()` todo, then `waitFor` + `assert` "shows an item named exactly {name}" | passed |
| `assert` with `unique('Nonexistent zq-91')` | `ASSERTION_FAILED: ... it does not show an item named "Nonexistent zq-91"` |
| `assert(..., { params: 'nope' })` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: agent.assert params must be a plain object` |

Judge prompts in the AI trace carried `Parameters: {"name":"Groceries 1793364192407"}` and `Parameters: {"name":"Nonexistent zq-91"}`. On main the same call fails with `agent.assert options has no key "params"` (per the issue).

Integration tests (`packages/e2e/tests/integration/judgment-params.test.ts`, scripted judge): unique value in judge input for assert and waitFor, secret stays a placeholder, a quoted plain-string secret stays redacted, invalid params name the method, custom executor gets projected params and cannot fill the secret.

title: fix(mobile): bound reads by operation budget with last-read grace
body:
Takes over #1112 by Totopo27 (closed unmerged after approval), rebased on current main with authorship credited.

- `@e2e-dev/mobile` bounds every snapshot and screenshot by the operation's budget (one `InputBudget` per operation, including relocation and keyboard-dismiss snapshots), so a hung read fails the step instead of holding it until the test timeout.
- Core's waits run reads through one `ReadWindow` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts`): the last read may run past the deadline by the slowest read the wait has finished, capped by the phase deadline, so a slow last read still finishes and is classed as `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` / `ASSERTION_FAILED`, not `ACTION_FAILED`.
- Reads past the deadline share that extra time instead of each getting it again (`toHaveScreenshot` with masks makes several reads per sample).
- A timed-out read is judged by when that read started, not when its sample did, and a negation counts as held only until the deadline.
- An action whose target resolved past its deadline is never sent: it fails as `ACTION_FAILED`.
- Peer floor: mobile requires `e2e >=0.22.0 <1`. Published `e2e` is 0.21.3 and a pending `e2e: minor` changeset (#1437) makes the next release 0.22.0, which ships this. If a release goes out before this merges, the floor needs bumping again.
- Restored main's `expect(calls).toMatchObject({ resolve: 1, read: 2 })` in `locator-engine.test.ts` (kept).

## Issue

Closes #1099

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- mobile benchmark, iOS 26.5 sim, `e2e run tests/controls.e2e.ts --target ios-simulator`, built packages. `a missing locator fails as not found once its timeout passes` (1 s timeout) is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` on every run, main and branch.
- Last branch run: 23 passed, 1 skipped. Earlier runs on this sim were flaky on main too (1 and 4 failures in different tests: long press, pointer verbs, focus), so they are local sim noise, not this change.

```text
   ✓ refusals > a missing locator fails as not found once its timeout passes 1.10s
      Tests  23 passed | 1 skipped (24)
```

Not covered: a slow last read on a real device. The unit tests cover it, and fail without the grace.

title: fix(runner): decode hex and base64 strings in worker output
body:
## What happened

The worker ignores the encoding argument of `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write`.
A string written with `hex` or `base64` appears as encoded text instead of the decoded output that Node produces.
The main-process output path decodes the same writes correctly.

## Minimal reproduction

Save this as `e2e.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineEngine } from 'e2e/engine';

export default {
	targets: [{
		name: 'noop',
		platform: 'test',
		engine: defineEngine({ name: 'noop', version: '1', spiVersion: 1 }),
	}],
	workers: 1,
};
```

Save this as `tests/output.e2e.ts`:

```ts
import { test } from 'e2e';

test('decodes writes', () => {
	process.stdout.write('48454c4c4f5f4845580a', 'hex');
	process.stderr.write('SEVMTE9fQkFTRTY0Cg==', 'base64');
});
```

Run `e2e run --reporter list`.
Expected stdout contains `HELLO_HEX` and stderr contains `HELLO_BASE64`.
Observed stdout contains `48454c4c4f5f4845580a` and stderr contains `SEVMTE9fQkFTRTY0Cg==`.
The test passes with exit code 0.

## Versions

e2e 0.21.3, Node.js 26.8.2, Linux.
Built from `fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370`.

## Engine

Custom no-op engine.
The defect is in worker output capture, independent of an engine implementation.

## Anything else

Reproduced through the built CLI and independently rerun by Claude Opus 5.5 with plain-string and Buffer controls.
Those controls preserve the expected output and redact configured plaintext secrets.

[`captureOutput`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts#L107-L115) uses `encoding` only to select the callback.
It passes the unchanged string into config-output holding and stream redaction.
The [main-process path](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/run/process-output.ts#L55-L61) already converts byte encodings before output capture.
Config-load writes in the worker have the same defect.

Add worker CLI regression coverage for decoded hex and base64 writes, including config-load output.
Do not classify encoded secret text alone as a redaction-contract violation.
The [documented redaction limits](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/docs/reference/security.mdx#L213-L220) exclude encoded values outside the supported paths.

title: fix(report): count serial runtime skips as executed
body:
## What happened

`run.summary.executed` omits a serial test that starts its body and calls `test.skip()` at runtime.
The same runtime skip outside a serial group counts as executed.
Three bodies run in the reproduction, but the report records `selected: 3` and `executed: 2`.

The [documented count](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/docs/reference/cli.mdx#L692-L703) covers selected results that ran at least one attempt.

## Minimal reproduction

Save this as `e2e.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineEngine } from 'e2e/engine';

export default {
	targets: [{
		name: 'noop',
		platform: 'test',
		engine: defineEngine({ name: 'noop', version: '1', spiVersion: 1 }),
	}],
	workers: 1,
};
```

Save this as `tests/skip.e2e.ts`:

```ts
import { test } from 'e2e';

test('ordinary runtime skip', () => test.skip('not applicable'));

test.describe('serial', { serial: true }, () => {
	test('serial runtime skip', () => test.skip('not applicable'));
	test('serial executed body', () => {});
});
```

Run `e2e run`.
Inspect `.e2e/report.json`.

Observed:

```json
{ "selected": 3, "executed": 2, "passed": 1, "skipped": 2 }
```

Expected `executed` is 3 because all three test bodies start.
The ordinary runtime skip has one result attempt.
The serial runtime skip appears in the shared group attempt and has no result attempts of its own.

## Versions

e2e 0.21.3, Node.js 26.8.2, Linux.
Built from `fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370`.

## Engine

Custom no-op engine.
The defect is in report summary calculation, independent of an engine implementation.

## Anything else

Reproduced through the built CLI and independently rerun by Claude Opus 5.5.
Controls covered ordinary static skips, runtime skips, failed `beforeAll` hooks, and serial predecessors that fail.
Only tests whose bodies started belong in `executed`.

The [runner summary](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts#L625-L629) treats a serial result's final status as proof of execution.
The [GitHub reporter](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/github/src/merge.ts#L56-L61) copies the same rule.

A fix must distinguish runtime skips from never-started placeholders.
Membership in a group attempt alone is insufficient because [`skippedMember`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/run/serial.ts#L607) also creates placeholder records.
Keep static skips and tests blocked by hooks or predecessors out of the count.
This report concerns counting, not the soft-failure behavior previously tracked in [#688](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/688).

title: perf(report): investigate repeated serial member scans
body:
## Problem

Reporters repeatedly scan the members of each serial group attempt for each result.
This is a source-confirmed optimization candidate.
No benchmark establishes a user-visible slowdown or a speedup from changing it.

For a group with N members and A attempts, these lookups require work proportional to A × N².
Multiple reporters repeat that work.

- [`attemptViews`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/outcome.ts#L75-L80) scans members for each attempt and result.
- [`durationOf`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/outcome.ts#L96-L99) scans the final attempt again.
- [`serialMemberDetails`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts#L189-L192) performs a similar lookup.

The shared `outcome()` calculation runs per result in [Markdown](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts#L580), [JUnit](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts#L104), and [trace pages](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370/packages/e2e/src/report/traces.ts#L41-L76).
Claude Opus 5.5 independently checked these call paths at `fe1d29350205d7e2a5c78b02fa3c23e71ea61370`.
Runtime performance remains unverified.

## Proposed API

No public API change is proposed.
First measure report generation for increasing serial group sizes and retry counts.
Include Markdown, JUnit, terminal output, and trace pages.
Keep the report content and statuses identical across variants.

If these scans materially affect report generation, compare the existing implementation with a shared index keyed by test id.
Keep the current implementation if measurements show no useful gain.
Use `pnpm bench:ab` for any performance claim and retain the behavior comparison.

## Which surface

Report generation and terminal reporter internals.
No change to the report wire format is proposed.

## Compatibility

Preserve public types, report content, statuses, artifact references, and ordering.
Do not treat an unmeasured candidate as a confirmed performance regression.

title: fix(report): count a serial member executed when its body ran
body: `run.summary.executed` is documented as the selected results that ran at least one attempt. For a serial member, the runner read the member's final verdict instead of its runs. So it left out members whose bodies ran. - A serial member that called `test.skip()` in its body counted as never run. The same skip outside a serial group counted. - A member that ran in one group attempt, and then sat behind a failed predecessor on the retry, also counted as never run. An ordinary test with a failed attempt counts. - The runner now reads a member's records across its group's attempts, the way it reads an ordinary result's `attempts` (`packages/e2e/src/report/build.ts`). One predicate, `memberRan` (`packages/e2e/src/run/records.ts`), separates a record whose body started from a skip the runner wrote for a member it never started. A static `test.skip(...)` never joins a serial unit, so inside a group attempt the `explicit` skip cause only comes from a body that ran. - Telemetry's cache tiers (`packages/e2e/src/telemetry/events.ts`) dropped the self-skipped member the same way. They must add up to `tests_executed`, and now they do. - The GitHub reporter's `--last-failed` fold mirrors the runner's count (`packages/github/src/merge.ts`). It gets the same rule. The comment does not render `executed`, so that package has no changeset. - Members kept out by a failed hook, a failed predecessor, or an interrupt still do not count. `docs/reference/cli.mdx` now says so. ## Issue Fixes #1466 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A scratch project with the issue's `e2e.config.ts` and `tests/skip.e2e.ts`, run through the built CLI (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/skip.e2e.ts`), then `run.summary` read from `.e2e/report.json`. - A second file, `tests/retry.e2e.ts`: a serial group with `retries: 1` where member 2 fails in attempt 1, and member 1 fails in attempt 2, so member 2 is skipped behind it. | Case | main (`d52e9b01`) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Issue repro: 3 bodies ran | `{"selected":3,"executed":2,"passed":1,"skipped":2}` | `{"selected":3,"executed":3,"passed":1,"skipped":2}` | | Retry: both bodies ran | `{"selected":2,"executed":1,"failed":1,"skipped":1}` | `{"selected":2,"executed":2,"failed":1,"skipped":1}` | - The first commit adds the tests and fails on main: the `runner-lifecycle` integration tests (`executed` 3 instead of 4, and 1 instead of 2), the telemetry tiers (7 instead of 8), and the GitHub fold (1 instead of 2). Controls for a failing `beforeAll` (`executed: 0`) and a predecessor skip (`executed: 3` of 4) pass both before and after. - The testbed default suite passes on the branch (81 passed, 1 skipped). Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(runner): print a string a worker writes with an encoding decoded
body:
A string written with an encoding, such as `process.stdout.write('48454c4c4f0a', 'hex')`, printed still encoded when a worker ran it. Node, and the runner process, print the decoded bytes. - The worker's capture (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/entry.ts`, `captureOutput`) used the encoding only to find the callback. It passed the encoded string to config-load holding and redaction unchanged. The config's top-level code, which each worker runs again, had the same bug. - One helper, `writtenChunk` in `packages/e2e/src/run/process-output.ts`, now turns a string with any encoding `Buffer.isEncoding` accepts into the bytes Node writes. Both the runner dispatcher and the worker call it before holding and redaction. The runner previously decoded only `hex`, `base64`, and `base64url`, so `latin1`, `utf16le`, and `HEX` printed wrong there too. - Bytes can now end inside a UTF-8 character, which `StreamRedactor` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/redact.ts`) mishandled for Buffer writes on main already. A string written next skipped the decoder, so it printed first, and the bytes joined a later write. A string piece now ends an unfinished character first, so it prints as `�`, as a terminal shows Node's raw bytes. An empty write keeps the decoder's state, since Node writes nothing for it. - Decoded output is plain text, so redaction applies to it as usual. The documented limits for encoded secrets do not change. ```ts test('prints encoded', () => { process.stdout.write('48454c4c4f5f4845580a', 'hex'); // HELLO_HEX process.stderr.write('SEVMTE9fQkFTRTY0Cg==', 'base64'); // HELLO_BASE64 }); ``` ## Issue Fixes #1465 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch project from the issue: a no-op engine config whose top level writes `CONFIG_HEX` as hex, plus the issue's test. Ran `e2e run --reporter list` on the built CLI. | main (d52e9b01) | this branch | | --- | --- | | `stdout \| \|noop\| tests/output.e2e.ts > decodes writes`
`48454c4c4f5f4845580a`
`stderr \| \|noop\| tests/output.e2e.ts > decodes writes`
`SEVMTE9fQkFTRTY0Cg==`
`stdout \| \|noop\|`
`434f4e4649475f4845580a` | `stdout \| \|noop\|`
`CONFIG_HEX`
`stdout \| \|noop\| tests/output.e2e.ts > decodes writes`
`HELLO_HEX`
`stderr \| \|noop\| tests/output.e2e.ts > decodes writes`
`HELLO_BASE64` | - Mixed writes in a test body, compared byte for byte with plain `node -e` decoded as UTF-8. `write('café', 'latin1'); write('done\n')` prints `caf�done`. Hex `c3`, plain `X`, then hex `a9` prints `�X�`. Hex `c3`, an empty write, then hex `a9` prints `é`. - The new CLI test in `tests/integration/run-user-output.test.ts` failed on main. A worker printed both writes encoded and only the runner decoded the config line. It passes here. With only `hex`, `base64`, and `base64url` decoded, it fails at the `latin1` line. - The two new `StreamRedactor` unit tests failed before the redactor fix, with `Xé` and `��`, and pass after it. - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` passed (81 passed, 1 skipped) before the redactor change. After it, one testbed test hit its 35 ms action timeout with the machine at load average 24 on 8 cores. Run alone 3 times (54 of 54), it passed. Reviewed with sol-loop: 3 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: changes requested in round 3, for the empty-write case. That one-line fix is in this head and covered by a unit test, but Sol has not reviewed it. A separate fresh-context review found the narrow encoding set, an `as` cast, and a test assertion that could never fail. All three are fixed here. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test(mcp): give the secret fill in run_code the default timeout
body:
The `run_code` secrets tests in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/mcp-run-code.test.ts` fail on a loaded machine. I hit this during a full local `pnpm test`.

- The first secrets test ran `app.open('/echo')` and a secret `fill` in the same `run_code` block as an assertion meant to fail. The block's timeout was 300 ms per statement, chosen so that assertion fails fast.
- Under load the fill spent about 200 ms resolving its locator and authorizing the secret. It then failed with `fill did not become actionable in time: elementHandle.fill: Timeout 33-103ms exceeded`.
- The three tests after it failed too, because they expect the secret in the Token field.
- The open and the fill now run in their own `run_code` call with the default timeout. The reads and the failing assertion keep the 300 ms timeout, and every redaction check stays.

## Issue

Fixes #1473

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `vitest run --project integration tests/integration/mcp-run-code.test.ts -t secrets`, 5 runs while 8 busy shell loops held all 8 cores.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| 0 of 5 runs passed. Every run failed the fill test, and most also failed the 3 tests after it. | 5 of 5 runs passed |

- The whole file passes without load (11 tests).
- Not changed: line 146 also runs an assertion that is meant to pass under a 300 ms timeout. It did not fail in 8 loaded runs, so I left it alone.

title: test(mcp): run_code secrets tests flake under load
body:
## What happened

The `run_code` secrets tests in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/mcp-run-code.test.ts` fail on a loaded machine.
The first one fails with `ACTION_FAILED: fill did not become actionable in time: elementHandle.fill: Timeout 103ms exceeded.`
The three secrets tests after it fail because they expect the secret in the Token field.

The test runs `app.open('/echo')` and `fill(secrets.get('apiKey'))` in the same `run_code` block as an assertion meant to fail.
That block has a 300 ms timeout per statement, chosen so the assertion fails fast.
Under load, the fill spent about 200 ms resolving its locator and authorizing the secret before its actionability wait.

## Minimal reproduction

From `packages/e2e` on `main` (`d52e9b01`), with 8 busy shell loops on 8 cores:

```sh
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do (while :; do :; done) & done
pnpm exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/mcp-run-code.test.ts -t secrets
```

0 of 5 runs passed.
Without load, it failed 1 of 3 runs during a full local `pnpm test`.

## Versions

e2e built from `d52e9b01`, Node.js 26.8.2, Linux.

## Engine

`@e2e-dev/web`, the in-repo integration fixture.

## Anything else

Fix in #1472: the open and the fill run in their own `run_code` call with the default timeout.

title: fix(run): print run errors on stderr when the list reporter is off
body:
`e2e run` with no `list` reporter now prints each run error on stderr as `CODE: message`. Before, `--reporter junit` or `markdown` with a test file that failed to collect, a config that failed to load, or an agent with no model exited 2 and printed nothing. `docs/reference/cli.mdx` already said such a run's "errors are on the terminal and in the exit code."

- Errors thrown before a run starts already reached stderr through `reportFailure` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`). Run errors recorded in the report printed only from `ListReporter` (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts`). A run that stops before its tests writes no `report.json`, so the error showed up nowhere.
- `finish()` in `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts` writes each `report.run.errors` entry to stderr when no list reporter runs and the run is not `quiet`. With `list`, nothing extra prints, so no error prints twice. `runSuite` and `runExploration` from `e2e/runner` pass `quiet: true` and stay silent.
- One helper, `failureLine` in `packages/e2e/src/report/format.ts`, formats both paths. It passes the code and the message through `bounded()`, as the list reporter does. So a failure before a run now gets the same control-character stripping and 8 KiB cap as the list reporter's.
- `--reporter json` keeps stdout a valid document, and the error line goes to stderr, as a failure before a run already did.
- A config whose own reporter object prints `run-error` events now also gets the line on stderr. `docs/reference/reporters.mdx` says so.

Found while verifying [#1471](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1471): a test file there that would not parse failed with no output under `--reporter junit`.

## Issue

Fixes #1475

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Scratch project with a no-op engine and a test file holding an unterminated string. Ran `e2e run --reporter <r>` on the built CLI.

| reporter | main (d52e9b01) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `junit` | exit 2, stdout and stderr empty | exit 2, stderr `COLLECTION_ERROR: failed to collect tests/broken.e2e.ts: .../tests/broken.e2e.ts:2:29: Unterminated string` |
| `markdown` | exit 2, stdout and stderr empty | exit 2, the same stderr line |
| `json` | exit 2, the document on stdout, stderr empty | exit 2, the same document on stdout (it parses), the same stderr line |
| `list,junit` | `Run Errors 1` banner on stdout | unchanged: banner on stdout, stderr empty |

- A config that throws, with `junit`, now prints `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED: failed to load config .../e2e.config.ts: config refuses to load`. An `agent.act` with no model prints `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: ...`. A Claude Opus 5.5 subagent ran both of these cases. I ran only the collection case myself.
- The new case in `tests/integration/cli-run.test.ts` failed on main (`junit: expected '' to match /COLLECTION_ERROR.../`) and passes here. It also checks the error is named once and the json document passes schema validation.
- Not run: `e2e explore`, which takes the same `finish()` path, and watch mode.

title: fix(run): a run error prints nowhere without the list reporter
body:
## What happened

`e2e run` without the `list` reporter prints nothing when a run error stops the run.
With `--reporter junit` or `--reporter markdown`, a test file that fails to collect exits 2 with empty stdout and stderr.
A config that fails to load and an `agent.act` with no model behave the same way.
With `--reporter list`, the same run prints `Run Errors 1` and `COLLECTION_ERROR ... Unterminated string`.
`docs/reference/cli.mdx` says such a run's "errors are on the terminal and in the exit code".

## Minimal reproduction

Save this as `e2e.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineEngine } from 'e2e/engine';

export default {
  targets: [{ name: 'noop', platform: 'test', engine: defineEngine({ name: 'noop', version: '1', spiVersion: 1 }) }],
  workers: 1,
};
```

Save this as `tests/broken.e2e.ts`:

```ts
import { test } from 'e2e';
test('x', () => { const s = 'a
b'; });
```

Run `e2e run --reporter junit; echo $?`.
Expected: the collection error on stderr and exit code 2.
Observed: no output and exit code 2.

## Versions

e2e 0.21.3, Node.js 26.8.2, Linux.
Built from `d52e9b0199b24fb03aa571ae4dc20f41fe96799d`.

## Engine

Custom no-op engine. The defect is in the runner's terminal output, independent of an engine.

## Anything else

Only `ListReporter` prints `run-error` events (`packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts`).
A run that stops before its tests writes no `report.json`, so without `list` the error appears nowhere.
Errors thrown before a run starts already reach stderr through `reportFailure` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts`.
Found while verifying [#1471](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1471).

title: docs(models): say a TanStack AI adapter is not an agent model
body: An app that uses TanStack AI 1.0 can't pass a TanStack adapter as the e2e agent's model, and the docs don't say so ([#1469](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/1469)). - The agent takes only an AI SDK language model. `isModelInstance` ([`packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts:388`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/packages/e2e/src/config/agent.ts#L388)) checks for `specificationVersion`, `provider`, `modelId`, and `doGenerate`. A TanStack adapter has none of them. - `docs/models.mdx`: adds one row to "What fails, and where". It names the symptom (`INVALID_CONFIG`), the matching AI SDK package, and says the app can keep TanStack AI. - `skills/e2e/references/agent.md` (and its plugin copy): adds the same rule, so a coding agent that sets up e2e in a TanStack app doesn't reach for `openaiText()`. - This PR adds no TanStack support. The issue stays open for that decision. ## Issue Refs #1469 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. I used a scratch project with the built `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` from this branch, `@tanstack/ai-openai` 1.0.1, and `@ai-sdk/openai` 4. | `model: openaiText('gpt-4o')` (TanStack) | `model: openai('gpt-4o')` (AI SDK) | | --- | --- | | `tsc`: `TS2739 ... missing the following properties from type 'ModelInstance': specificationVersion, modelId, doGenerate` | `tsc` passes | | `npx e2e run` exits 2: `INVALID_CONFIG agents.default.model must be an AI SDK model instance` | The config loads, and the step reaches OpenAI: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED ... Incorrect API key provided: sk-test` (a fake key, as intended) | - `pnpm docs:check` and `pnpm plugins:check` pass. - I didn't render the docs site. The change is one row in an existing Markdown table. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(config): name the resolved path and base dir in CONFIG_NOT_FOUND for --config
body:
## What and why

- Agent feedback: MCP `open_session {config: "e2e/e2e.config.ts"}` failed with `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: config file not found: e2e/e2e.config.ts`. Their `.mcp.json` sets `cwd` to `e2e/`, so the path resolved to `e2e/e2e/e2e.config.ts`, and nothing in the error said so.
- `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` for an explicit path (`--config`, `open_session` `config`, `openHost({ config })`) now names the absolute path it checked. For a relative path it also names the directory it resolved against, and the fix: pass an absolute path or one relative to that directory (`packages/e2e/src/config/load.ts`).
- The `open_session` `config` description, `docs/reference/mcp.mdx`, and `skills/e2e` now say relative means relative to the server's working directory.
- No fallback to the repo root. The server only knows its `cwd`. A "repo root" means walking up to `.git`, which is a layout guess (monorepos, nested repos, no git). If a path resolved under both directories, it would also be ambiguous which file was meant. The error now gives the agent what it needs to fix the path itself.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Surface: built `e2e mcp` on `apps/testbed`, driven by an MCP stdio client with server `cwd` = `apps/testbed`, calling `open_session` with a path relative to the repo root and then with the corrected path.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: config file not found: apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts` | `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: config file not found: <repo>/apps/testbed/apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts (apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts resolved against the working directory <repo>/apps/testbed); pass an absolute path, or a path relative to that directory` |

With the corrected path from the message, `open_session {config: "e2e.config.ts"}` opens a session:

```text
open_session {config: "e2e.config.ts"} -> isError=false
  Session 01a18d86-... open on target "web" (platform web, engine web 0.15.3), headless; config <repo>/apps/testbed/e2e.config.ts.
```

Covered by `config.test.ts` (relative and absolute), `cli.test.ts`, and `mcp-server.test.ts` (the error names the server's directory).

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(app): app.baseUrl without trailing slash, string on web targets
body: `${app.baseUrl}/api/users` produced `http://127.0.0.1:5940//api/users` (404), and `app.baseUrl` needed `as string` on web tests. - `app.baseUrl` drops the trailing slash: `baseUrlOf` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts`, used only by the `app` fixture (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts`). The internal `base.href` is unchanged, so `app.open(path)`, `restart`, `clearState`, `toHaveURL`, and agent navigation resolve exactly as before, base paths like `/app/` included. - `@e2e-dev/web`'s `test` types `app` as `WebApp` (`baseUrl: string`). `web()` already rejects a target without `app.url` (`packages/web/src/engine.ts` `validateApp`). `test` from `e2e` stays `string | undefined`. - Docs, skill, and the API fixture examples join with `${app.baseUrl}${path}`, which keeps a base path that `new URL('/x', base)` drops. ```ts import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web'; test('webhook', async ({ app }) => { await fetch(`${app.baseUrl}/api/webhooks/github`, { method: 'POST' }); // no cast, one slash }); ``` ## For the maintainer - Changeset is `patch` (AGENTS.md: agents never pick `minor`). It changes a public value: code relying on the slash (`${app.baseUrl}api/x`, `new URL('x', app.baseUrl)` on a URL with a path, `toBe(app.baseUrl)` against `browser.url()`) breaks. Bump to `minor` + `**Breaking:**` if you count it as breaking. - `WebApp.baseUrl: string` makes the same assumption as `browser: Browser`: a test imported from `@e2e-dev/web` runs on a web target. In a config mixing `web()` with a device target, such a test without `requires: ['browser']` sees `undefined` there; `browser` throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` in that case, `baseUrl` does not. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: testbed, built CLI. New test `tests/network.e2e.ts` > "calls the API at a path joined onto app.baseUrl" does `fetch(`${app.baseUrl}/api/users`)`. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× calls the API at a path joined onto app.baseUrl` `ASSERTION_FAILED: expected 404 to be 200` | `✓ tests/network.e2e.ts (6 tests)` | ```text main: FAIL |web| tests/network.e2e.ts > calls the API at a path joined onto app.baseUrl ASSERTION_FAILED: expected 404 to be 200 17| const response = await fetch(`${app.baseUrl}/api/users`); 18| expect(response.status).toBe(200); branch: ✓ target "web" command ready 89ms ✓ |web| tests/smoke.e2e.ts (4 tests | 1 skipped) 506ms ✓ |web| tests/network.e2e.ts (6 tests) 1.11s Tests 9 passed | 1 skipped (10) ``` - Unit: `fixture-runtime.test.ts` covers a bare origin and a `/app/` base (`baseUrl` = `http://127.0.0.1:4599/app`, `app.open('settings')` still opens `/app/settings`). - Types: `packages/web/tests/types/app.ts` (`new URL(app.baseUrl)` compiles from `@e2e-dev/web`, is a `@ts-expect-error` from `e2e`). - Integration `app-port-allocation.test.ts` updated for the new shape.

title: feat(mcp): save a screenshot to a path, list app.screenshot files in the summary
body: Agent feedback: `app.screenshot` files had to be `find`-ed, and MCP `screenshot` could not write a file. - `app.screenshot` already resolves to the absolute path (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:544`, documented). Attached image unchanged. - `path` outside the project root, a hidden file, or under a hidden dir is `POLICY_DENIED`, like `upload`. title: feat(mcp): open_session names the app command, its URL, and the port it assigned
body:
Agent feedback: a session printed only the app URL, so finding the stack's ports meant reading `e2e.config.ts`, and env ports set in the agent's shell were "ignored".

- `open_session` summary now names what it started (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/app-lines.ts`): app URL with the port assigned for `:0`, and the app command's executable, readiness URL, `env` / `inheritEnv` names, `cwd`, log file. No `args`, no env values, no URL userinfo or query (`printableUrl`, any may carry a secret). Without `app.command` it says the app runs outside e2e.
- It says e2e starts no other app process. There is no services API in this version, so a database the app uses was never started by e2e and has no port e2e knows.
- "Ignored the ports": not a bug. The config is evaluated with the MCP server's own `process.env` (set by the MCP client at launch), so variables exported in the agent's shell never reach it. Verified: `DB_PORT` / `APP_URL` in the server's env are honored. The summary and docs now say so.
- `e2e run`: the app setup line and the `app` setup event carry the printable readiness URL (`url`, optional on the type since `ManagedProcess` can wait for exit; always set in a run).

```text
 ✓ target "web" command at http://127.0.0.1:65150/ ready 96ms
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

title: feat(locator): chain locator(selector) off a locator
body: Agents with Playwright habits write `form.locator("input[name=manifest]")` and get `Property 'locator' does not exist on type 'Locator'`. `browser.locator` / `device.locator` exist at the top, but a `Locator` could not chain one. - `Locator.locator(selector)`: the target's own selector language (CSS/XPath on web, agent-device selector on mobile), evaluated from each of the locator's matches: CSS and agent-device selectors match descendants only; on web an XPath `..` reaches the parent, as in Playwright. - Reuses the scoped-query path: `selector` expressions get an optional `scope`, same as `query` (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`). Core `resolveExpression`, web projection (Playwright `locator.locator`, frame chain included) and mobile `locate` honor it. - On `Locator` generically, not per platform: locators come from the generic `screen`, and the `selector` expression kind is already generic. `screen` stays semantic-only. - Engines opt in with `scopedSelectors: true` (same pattern as `tapModifiers`). Without it the session refuses a scoped selector with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before `locate`, so a newer `e2e` with an older engine never silently matches outside the scope. Web and mobile declare it and raise their `e2e` peer floor to `>=0.22.1`. - Left out of MCP `run_code`: a selector can match part of an unredacted secret, which `run_code` refuses for `getBy*` partial matches too. ```ts const upload = screen.getByRole('form', 'Upload'); await upload.locator('input[name=manifest]').setInputFiles('fixtures/manifest.json'); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, new tests in `tests/forms.e2e.ts` (CSS under a fieldset group) and `tests/dialogs-frames.e2e.ts` (selector chained off a query inside an iframe, host page untouched): ```text ✓ |web| tests/forms.e2e.ts (1 test) 240ms ✓ |web| tests/dialogs-frames.e2e.ts (1 test) 314ms Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` - failure path, scratch test with an ambiguous chain: ```text LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS: locator matched 2 nodes, expected exactly one: getByRole("group", name: "Notifications") >> locator("input[type=checkbox]") ``` - full testbed suite 83 passed, web benchmark 91 passed. - `packages/web/tests/integration/scoped-selectors.test.ts` fails on main, passes here (real Chromium, frame scope included). - mobile: unit coverage over agent-device selectors only, no device run. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0d355c1-86bc-4d94-aaf7-dae8892d1fc7

title: test(mobile-benchmark): re-record iOS recordings on agent-device 0.21.35
body:
- Re-records 7 iOS entries under `apps/mobile-benchmark/.e2e/cache/`: Infinite Scroll List, Modal Flow, Bottom Tabs, Text Input Variations, Gestures, Sticky Chrome Target, Apple Pay. Same keys and file names, so nothing orphaned. Android entries untouched.
- Why they broke: agent-device 0.21.31 (callstack/agent-device#3873) keeps the fast AX bridge snapshot backend when a system-sheet host (SafariViewService, left running after Login Form's "Save Password?" sheet) is still alive but off screen. The old entries were recorded with that host lingering, so they came from the XCTest tree, where an unlabelled wrapper takes its child's label (`other "Flow completed"`). On 0.21.35 those anchors and targets no longer exist, so the steps end-mismatch or miss their target.
- The new entries drop the wrapper anchors (`text "Flow completed"` only), and the same steps replay whether Login Form ran first or not.
- README unchanged: the hand-offs it lists and their reasons still hold.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `test:agent --strict-cache --target ios-simulator --retries 0`, fresh iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5 sim (erased before the first after-run), release build of this app, agent-device 0.21.35.

| iOS strict, local | Cache | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 6 replayed · 12 handed off · 4 missed | 12 passed, 10 failed |
| this PR, run 1 (fresh sim) | 12 replayed · 6 handed off · 4 missed | 19 passed, 3 failed |
| this PR, run 2 (back to back) | 12 replayed · 6 handed off · 4 missed | 18 passed, 4 failed |
| this PR, the 7 re-recorded tests after a sim reboot, no Login Form first | 6 replayed · 1 handed off | 6 passed, 1 failed |
| this PR, Modal Flow alone after a sim reboot | 1 replayed | 1 passed |

- Failures left are the known ones: Debounced Search, Photo Picker, Choice Controls (`REPLAY_STALE`, see the README). Gestures replays its long-press and hands the swipe and double tap to the model by design; the live double tap or swipe not registering on iOS is the existing XCTest gesture flake (also fails on main).
- For reference, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.4 replayed 11 with the old entries.
- CI `ios agent` (lenient), replayed from cache out of 25 agent steps:

| CI iOS agent | Replayed |
| --- | --- |
| main (#1468, #1463) | 5, 6 |
| this PR | 12 |
