title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## e2e@0.23.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1552](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1552) [`d2556bc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d2556bc23fd01afe8f72a2e94e5fc18b4787b433) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Breaking:** `inputValue()` on a node with no value, such as a heading or a button, and `isChecked()` on a node with no checked state throw `ACTION_FAILED`, as in Playwright, instead of returning `""` and `false`. A field with no value still reads `""`, and a checkable role with no state reported still reads `false`. `uncheck()` on an ARIA `role="radio"` now clicks it, as in Playwright; a native radio still refuses.

### Patch Changes

- [#1524](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1524) [`cba5e0e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/cba5e0ecfbb7a1b0c61d0328dad9485cc87c2ab6) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The built-in agent can resize the viewport with the new `resize_viewport` tool, so `agent.act` and `e2e explore` can check layouts at desktop, tablet, and phone widths. The tool is offered when the target's engine implements the new optional `session.resize` hook. Custom executors call `ctx.actions.resize({ width, height })`, and the replay cache records and replays it.

- [#1479](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1479) [`d15a98e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d15a98e0711a185873a7a57a108dd254673e327c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.baseUrl` no longer ends in a slash, so `${app.baseUrl}/api/users` requests `/api/users` instead of `//api/users`. With `test` from `@e2e-dev/web`, `app.baseUrl` is typed `string`, since a `web()` target always declares `app.url`. A test that relied on the trailing slash, such as `${app.baseUrl}api/users` or `new URL('users', app.baseUrl)` on a URL with a path, adds the slash itself.

- [#1491](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1491) [`108bc60`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/108bc604cdcfcfacc8ab66bd179c408bf6887ccf) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Bump @agentclientprotocol/sdk to 2.2.0, @ai-sdk/provider to 4.0.35, and oxc to 0.156.0.

- [#1516](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1516) [`0410fc9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0410fc9c74ffac45d5174b7a3a5b3e6f15fdf32f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Bump agent-device to 0.21.36, @agentclientprotocol/sdk to 2.4.0, @vitest/expect to 5.1.0, and oxc to 0.157.0.

- [#1573](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1573) [`3d5f4ea`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3d5f4ea6217ccc26957bf67869b333e0aff49e23) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Bump @ai-sdk/provider to 4.0.36.

- [#1451](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1451) [`b4dd4bd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b4dd4bd20db47f2a13a89f6dc8c2242cf0fc17a1) Thanks [@amoscicki](https://github.com/amoscicki)! - The run summary's `Cache` line counts the steps of passing and flaky tests whose recording was not saved (`step.cache.write` of `unconfirmed`, `no-change`, or `not-written` in the attempt that passed), such as `4 missed · 1 not saved`.

- [#1493](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1493) [`91bd614`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/91bd61490d20c7536a77ed5ed74e556a856da738) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `e2e doctor`: checks that `e2e run` can start without starting anything. It covers the Node.js runtime, the config and its targets, each engine's own checks, and the model each agent resolved to. `--json` prints the `doctor-1` report for a host, `--check-model` calls each model once, and the command exits 2 when a check failed. Engines can report their checks through the new optional `doctor` hook.

- [#1575](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1575) [`7d7d0e1`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7d7d0e16159c2242506222489f34b7dfd3cec7b4) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - `e2e init` and `e2e --help` show the new e2e logo, its six rows of bars drawn in full blocks, one row per bar. In `e2e init` the logo shades in from ░ to █, top rows first, in about half a second. The logo needs a terminal at least 52 columns wide, and prints without motion on one shorter than 7 rows.

- [#1478](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1478) [`2208056`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/22080566738afd2a987ce86d156b27112ba571b0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` for an explicit config path (`--config <path>`, the MCP `open_session` `config` input, or `openHost({ config: '<path>' })`) now names the absolute path it checked and, for a relative path, the working directory it resolved against.

- [#1572](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1572) [`0c04696`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0c0469605aeb4955f161fb16dd7fa20b2d7037cb) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Documentation links in CLI help, `e2e init` output, and the MCP server listing now point to https://e2e.com/docs.

- [#1232](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1232) [`3f43edd`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/3f43edd166c6ebbe491b1610abd38d4f8e655459) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add the engine protocol: `connectEngine`, `serveEngine`, and transports in `e2e/engine` run an engine in another process, on another machine, or in another language over LSP-style JSON-RPC. Every engine built with `defineEngine` now runs through the protocol in process, so the harness drives every engine the same way.
  
  `Engine.dispose` now runs only once `init` was called, even when `init` failed. A worker that never initialized no longer disposes its engine.

- [#1522](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1522) [`73734c6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/73734c644f01b9169c8898202fae4862bba8c98c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e explore` digs deeper once the main flows are covered: it returns to them with edge-case inputs, combined filters and sorting, reloads, and other accounts, finishes early only when nothing new is reachable, and checks other screens that offer a control it found broken.

- [#1523](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1523) [`f4be1c4`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f4be1c456858b6c8bd4839053f5e267f75c937d8) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e explore` runs longer: `--max-steps` goes up to 100 and `--timeout` up to 7200000 (2 hours).

- [#1480](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1480) [`723c1af`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/723c1af84ebe70e7c702d5790ae4821c7a8b54b0) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A failed test's block in the terminal and in `summary.md` quotes the first 3 errors the app logged (console errors, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, 5xx responses), so an app error behind a locator failure shows without opening `trace.md`.

- [#1499](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1499) [`1d671f6`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/1d671f6786b1eff4b43718ddc413b0bfa21abbcb) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The markdown report footer (`summary.md`, the `@e2e-dev/github` pull request comment and job summary) now reads `Tested by e2e <version> · ...`, with `e2e` linking to https://e2e.com.

- [#1464](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1464) [`57f9ed9`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/57f9ed9eda7469535fba72bd24f9ff2ce7ad023e) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `locator.waitFor`, `expect` on a locator, and `toHaveScreenshot` give their last read extra time past the timeout, up to their slowest read so far and within the test timeout, so a screen that shows up during a slow last read still passes.

- [#1576](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1576) [`33a1541`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/33a154157975bb38a421a912052e4d0e436067c8) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - Start faster by loading heavy dependencies when a command or session needs them. The CLI no longer loads the MCP server, the prompt library, or the schema library until `mcp`, `init`, `login`, `logout`, `models`, `explore`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, or `--watch` runs, so `e2e --version` and `--help` take about 25% less time. `@e2e-dev/web` imports Playwright when a browser is first launched or looked up, so a process that only reads the config skips it: `e2e list` on a web project takes about 44% less time, and importing the package half as long. A worker loads Playwright for its first browser instead of before its first test, so that test's reported duration grows by about 0.14 s while the run takes no longer. `e2e/runner` no longer loads the explorer when imported. `@e2e-dev/acp` loads the ACP and MCP SDKs when its first session starts, and `@e2e-dev/limrun` loads `@limrun/api` when its first device is leased.

- [#1434](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1434) [`50d8063`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/50d80633556cd3a612ec1f30f490ab4cd8dd361c) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - Later agent steps now see a fully replayed step's summary labeled `recorded in an earlier run` instead of `observed`.

- [#1482](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1482) [`d94593b`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d94593b0c1c783f887ae130e64b2c25c3ec94b30) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The `list` reporter prints each test as it finishes when stdout is not a terminal (piped, redirected, most CI), instead of only once its whole file finishes, and ends every run with a `Failed` row per failed test (`file:line`, the error's first line, the trace page when one was written), so `e2e run | tail` still names what broke.

- [#1416](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1416) [`79e2e13`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/79e2e13d3365da30b8f85ff08670f888bfc12b57) Thanks [@DeryFerd](https://github.com/DeryFerd)! - Filtered-locator failures can list how many candidates each filter step left, when the post-failure diagnostic pass can read the chain, so a step that narrowed too much or too little names itself. The message says the counts were read then.

- [#1520](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1520) [`50fa7af`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/50fa7afc1a6fcf84e73adb908e7f55693dc1bf2a) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `e2e mcp` has a `run_tests` tool: it runs a test file, one test (`tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12`), or the whole suite as `e2e run` does and returns what the run printed, so a coding agent can run tests without a shell.
  
  ```txt
  run_tests {files: ["tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12"]}
  ```

- [#1498](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1498) [`4b56473`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4b56473e59645ed7234347c5080aa2ed3b2f0ae5) Thanks [@21prnv](https://github.com/21prnv)! - A replay no longer fails its end check on a date written with an ordinal suffix, such as `October 26th` or `3rd October`, when the day differs from the recording.

- [#1571](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1571) [`4c44e44`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/4c44e44957076350798c54bdcca7442fbf935327) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - The agent compares screenshots with a native SHA-256 instead of a byte-by-byte loop in script, so a settle poll or screen update that carries pixels no longer spends about 8 ms of the event loop per megabyte of image.

- [#1493](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1493) [`91bd614`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/91bd61490d20c7536a77ed5ed74e556a856da738) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A model call without a response schema that the provider ends on an `error` finish now fails as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` instead of `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`.

- [#1500](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1500) [`7b1b8b2`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/7b1b8b27d8212212923934fdd99b4a7050746823) Thanks [@bheemreddy-samsara](https://github.com/bheemreddy-samsara)! - Add coordinates to `agent.act`'s `onAction` event: narrow on `event.action` to read `point` for `tapAt` and `hoverAt`, or `from` and `to` for `dragAt`, replay included. Points are in the same space as `screen.tapAt` and `boundingBox()`, rounded and clamped to the viewport.
  
  `ActionEvent` is now a union keyed by `action`, typed `ActionName` or `tool:<name>` instead of `string`. New `ActionName` and `ActionDetails` types.

- [#1474](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1474) [`d10655f`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d10655f3430f867172fdedba2ad8cdceeb4ceaeb) Thanks [@samanyudas](https://github.com/samanyudas)! - `e2e run` without the `list` reporter prints each run error on stderr as `CODE: message`. Before, `--reporter junit` or `markdown` with a test file that failed to collect, a config that failed to load, or no model for the agent exited 2 and printed nothing.

- [#1481](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1481) [`f078364`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f0783641ef4250b62b8b7600be7384dffc4be2ea) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The `list` summary names the first 10 `app.screenshot` files in a `Screenshots` row, then counts the rest. The MCP `screenshot` tool takes an optional `path` (a `.png`, relative to the project root): it saves the masked full-resolution screenshot there and returns the absolute path.

- [#1470](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1470) [`b8485ba`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/b8485ba2e76d3e37e304f4ec7d863ef6f3ba251c) Thanks [@samanyudas](https://github.com/samanyudas)! - `run.summary.executed` now counts a serial member whose body ran, the same way it counts an ordinary test. Before, it left out a member that called `test.skip()` in its body, and a member that ran in one group attempt before a retry skipped it behind a failed predecessor. The run's telemetry cache tiers count them the same way.

- [#1483](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1483) [`0b84d35`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/0b84d35f8cbcbc1a217850ce7aaafde30caa27ea) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `open_session` now names the app command it started: its executable, the URL it answers on, the port a free-port `url` was assigned, and the `env` and `inheritEnv` names it got. It prints no `args` and no `env` values. It also says the config reads the MCP server's environment, not the agent's shell. `e2e run` prints the URL on the app command's setup line, and the `app` setup event carries it as `url`.

- [#1546](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1546) [`a8ed7f7`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/a8ed7f76c621495ce746919bad2d46c32418bc37) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `locator.setInputFiles([])` clears a file input and fires `input` and `change`, as in Playwright. It used to throw `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A blank path is still refused.

- [#1567](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1567) [`65ebc7d`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/65ebc7d47b17f289c29cf285995276b50095b781) Thanks [@NathanWalker](https://github.com/NathanWalker)! - The bundled e2e skill now names NativeScript's `testID` among the ids `getByTestId` reads on a device.

- [#1538](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1538) [`c7cbcef`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/c7cbcef8a29d1e3cd4e72284dbc47a1dd9e69b70) Thanks [@kacperkapusciak](https://github.com/kacperkapusciak)! - The bundled skills declare what they need to run (`node` and `npx`, and the optional `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` for the e2e skill) in `metadata.openclaw`, the frontmatter ClawHub reads. All three are now on ClawHub under `@e2e`.

Before, a bordered element shifted the tap by its border width. Engines can report that point as the new optional `SemanticNode.origin`.

- [#1539](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1539) [`732ea8a`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/732ea8af9ab5924ca6bd7b32aecf615ea9e61188) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Add `test.fail` to mark a test that is expected to fail: `test.fail(title, fn)`, `test.fail(condition, reason)` inside a body, or the `fail` test option. A marked test that fails with a test failure passes, and the report keeps the reason and the original error under `expectedFailure`. The runner process decoded only `hex`, `base64`, and `base64url`, and now decodes every encoding Node accepts too. title: docs(acp): move coding agent docs under subscriptions
body: ## What and why - Coding agent (Claude Code, Codex over the Agent Client Protocol) docs now live in `docs/subscriptions.mdx` under `## Use your coding agent`, next to the other "use what you already pay for" options. Plans table gets a row linking there. - Removed `docs/acp.mdx` and its og image. Dropped the "Use another ACP agent" section (generic `acp()`, Cursor, Windows `command` note, non-preset tool-allow rule). `acp()` stays exported, just undocumented. - `/acp` redirects to `/subscriptions#use-your-coding-agent`. - "How a test runs" and "Limits" folded into accordions; containment and secrets stay visible. - Links updated in `README.md`, `packages/acp/README.md`, `skills/e2e/references/agent.md` (+ plugin mirror). - Docs say "Agent Client Protocol", never the "ACP" abbreviation. ## Verified Ran it locally: no - docs move only; `mint dev` rejects `docs/docs.json` locally (missing `theme`/`colors`, also on main), so no render. `pnpm docs:check` (982 anchors resolve) and `pnpm plugins:check` pass; no `/acp` links left in the repo.

title: fix(docs): close the subscriptions Limits accordion and check every page compiles as MDX
body: #1488 moved the ACP docs into `docs/subscriptions.mdx`. Its new "Limits" accordion holds a bullet list at column 0 inside an `` indented by two spaces. In MDX the indented `` then joins the last list item, because two spaces reach the item's content column, and the component never closes. A standard MDX compiler (`@mdx-js/mdx` 3) rejects the page, so any build that compiles these docs with it fails: ```text docs/subscriptions.mdx:387:3: Expected the closing tag `` either after the end of `listItem` (387:15) or another opening tag after the start of `listItem` (385:1) ``` - `docs/subscriptions.mdx`: indent the list two spaces, like the `` lists in `docs/mobile.mdx`. A blank line before the closing tag isn't enough; the tag still belongs to the list item. - `scripts/check-docs-mdx.ts`, part of `pnpm docs:check`: compiles every docs page with `@mdx-js/mdx` and `remark-gfm` (new root dev dependencies, like `@sindresorhus/slugify` for the anchor check) and reports `file:line:column` with the compiler's reason. About 1.3s for 67 pages. The `docs` filter already matches `scripts/check-docs-*.ts`. - `authoring-docs`: a rule under "Showing less at one time" for bullet lists inside indented components, plus a "Before you commit" item saying `pnpm docs:check` compiles every page as MDX. The page edit only re-indents the list, so I skipped the shortening pass on `subscriptions.mdx`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.ts` on `main`'s `subscriptions.mdx` against this branch's: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `docs/subscriptions.mdx:387:3: Expected the closing tag either after the end of listItem ...`, exit 1 | `docs mdx: 67 pages compile as standard MDX`, exit 0 | - Parsed the fixed page with `@mdx-js/mdx`: the "Limits" accordion holds one unordered list with the same three items, and nothing after it. - `pnpm check` passes (including `docs:check`). - `npx mint dev` could not run: the current CLI rejects `docs.json`'s `theme` before it builds anything, on `main` too. So no Mintlify render was checked; the indented list follows the existing `` pattern in `docs/mobile.mdx`.

title: chore(deps): bump workspace deps to latest, @agentclientprotocol/sdk to 2.2.0
body: Every workspace dependency on latest, except the Expo SDK 58 upgrade of `apps/mobile-benchmark`. agent-device 0.21.35 and playwright-core 1.64.1 were already latest. - `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` 1.7.0 -> 2.2.0 (major). 2.0 removed `ClientSideConnection` / `AgentSideConnection`, so `packages/acp/src/session.ts` and `tests/fixtures/scripted-agent.ts` now use the `client()` / `agent()` app API with `request(methods.agent.session.*)`. Imports come from `@agentclientprotocol/sdk/unstable`, because prompt `usage` and `usage_update` are unstable in 2.x. - Live ACP adapter pins: claude-agent-acp 0.99.1, codex-acp 2.5.0. - ai 7.0.159 and all `@ai-sdk/*`, oxc 0.156, oxlint 1.90, fallow 3.38, `@onkernel/sdk` 0.139, `@limrun/api` 0.68.1, smolmachines 1.32.4, `@types/node` 26.6.6. - Mobile benchmark: latest Expo SDK 57 patches (expo 57.0.31, react-native 0.86.3), matching `expo install --check`. The native fingerprint changes, so CI rebuilds the app. - `@ai-sdk/openai` 4.0.106 sends JSON decision state as `input_json` (`data`) instead of `input_text`. Updated `packages/decision/tests/openai.test.ts` to the new wire shape. - fallow 3.34+ treats the `StandardSchemaV1` interface and its merged namespace as a duplicate export. `.fallowrc.json` ignores that one export. ```ts const connection = client({ name: 'e2e' }) .onRequest(methods.client.session.requestPermission, ({ params }) => answerPermission(params, ours, calls, turn.own)) .onNotification(methods.client.session.update, ({ params }) => observe(params, ours, calls, turn, onOwnTool)) .connect(ndJsonStream(stdin, stdout)); await connection.agent.request(methods.agent.session.prompt, { sessionId, prompt }); ``` Left out: Expo SDK 58 (react-native 0.88, react 19.3, Stripe RN 0.84). It's a native upgrade with re-recording, so it gets its own PR. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node packages/acp/tests/live/acp.ts` against real Claude Code (claude-agent-acp 0.99.1, sonnet) and Codex (codex-acp 2.5.0). Both record, then replay. The todo flow, secret login and tool inventory pass. The wrong assertion fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` as expected. Usage and cost come through, no secret in artifacts, and none of the agent's own tools ran. - `pnpm check` green. `pnpm test` green apart from `acp > skips actions batched behind the verdict`, a flake that is already on main (2/15 full acp runs fail on origin/main). - Not run: OpenAI Decisions API live with `input_json` (no key locally), and a native benchmark build (CI builds it per fingerprint).

title: feat(android): experimental @e2e-dev/android engine
body: `@e2e-dev/android` is an experimental Android engine. It is an [engine protocol](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/engine-protocol) server written in Java that runs on the device as an instrumentation and drives it in process through `UiAutomation`. There is no agent-device, and no adb call, shell process, or XML dump per action. adb only installs the server, starts it, and forwards one TCP port. On the same emulator, it runs the 42 deterministic Android tests of the mobile benchmark in **~123s, against ~292s on `@e2e-dev/mobile`** (2.4x), and both engines pass all 42. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[e2e runner] -- engine protocol over adb forward --> S[EngineInstrumentation on device] S -- UiAutomation --> A[app windows: a11y tree, touches, keys] ``` ## Use it ```ts title="e2e.config.ts" import { android } from '@e2e-dev/android'; export default { targets: [{ name: 'android', engine: android(), app: { bundleId: 'com.example.app', appPath: './app-release.apk' } }], workers: 1, }; ``` ```ts import { expect } from 'e2e'; import { test } from '@e2e-dev/android'; // typed `device` fixture: back() ``` - `android({ serial?, adb?, serverApk? })`. The device is `ANDROID_SERIAL`, else the one device attached. - The server APK ships inside the npm package. `prepack` builds it with the SDK's javac/d8/aapt2/apksigner (no Gradle), so users need no JDK. `spec.yml` compiles it on every PR, and both release jobs set up JDK 17. - Docs: new page `docs/android.mdx` (marked experimental), linked next to Mobile under Platforms. - Peer `e2e >=0.22.1 <1`. 0.22.0 shipped before #1232, so 0.22.1 is the first release with the protocol. ## Benchmark Pixel 7 API 36 emulator (`emulator-5554`), Mac mini. Selection: `apps/mobile-benchmark/e2e.android.config.ts` (smoke, login-form, flows, flows-lists, controls: 42 tests, 1 skipped), one worker, `--retries 0`. `@e2e-dev/mobile` uses the pinned agent-device 0.21.35. Runs were interleaved; load is `uptime` 1-min average at start/end. | Run | Engine | Wall | Passed | Load (start / end) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | android (native) | 123.7s | 42/42 | 6.85 / 9.38 | | 2 | mobile (agent-device) | 292.2s | 42/42 | 9.11 / 6.62 | | 3 | android (native) | 122.8s | 42/42 | 6.62 / 8.48 | | 4 | mobile (agent-device) | 291.5s | 42/42 | 8.48 / 8.23 | Per-step medians from `report.json` (ms, runs 1-4 in order): | Step | n | native | agent-device | native | agent-device | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `locator.tap` | 90 | 41 | 1544 | 40 | 1550 | | `locator.fill` | 14 | 100 | 1416 | 84 | 1476 | | `locator.press` | 10 | 104 | 1514 | 92 | 1504 | | `app.open` | 40 | 166 | 707 | 166 | 752 | | `locator.longPress` | 3 | 1264 | 2535 | 1261 | 2535 | | `locator.swipe` | 7 | 162 | 284 | 149 | 232 | | `screen.scrollUntilVisible` | 3 | 8336 | 10151 | 8459 | 9675 | | `expect.toBeVisible` | 64 | 174 | 98 | 178 | 98 | | `expect.toHaveText` | 44 | 111 | 82 | 110 | 84 | Native `expect` steps take longer because native actions return before the app reacts, so the wait moves from the action into the assertion's polling. ## Speed work The server logs each request's time (`adb logcat -s e2e-android`), which is how these were found. | Change | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Port onto the current protocol | - | 136.3s, 42/42 | | `slow` swipes ease out, so the finger slows before lifting (a short fling: ~80ms coast instead of ~700ms); rest is read from the scrolled container's layout each frame instead of a 150ms idle window; moves inject without waiting | 136.3s (swipe p50 1274ms) | 121-124s (swipe p50 536ms) | What didn't help, and where the rest goes: - A faster `slow` gesture (300ms) or a longer stride: same rows per second, because the shorter gesture coasts more. A longer stride could also carry a target past a short list without it ever being seen. - `restart`: 140 of its ~165ms is `am start -W`, the app's cold start to first frame. - The slowest observes (350-530ms) happen right after the tap that pushes a screen: the accessibility query waits while the app mounts it. - ~40s of a run is the harness's 100ms poll interval between observes while the app catches up. A push-style "screen changed" signal would need a protocol change, so it's out of scope here. ## Known gaps - One device per run (`workers: 1`). No device pool, emulator boot, or video. - `device` has only `back()`. The `device.e2e.ts` and `device-fixture.e2e.ts` suites stay on `mobile()`. - No `selector` locators, `app.launchArguments`, or `app.permissions`. Text the virtual key map can't spell is set on the field, not typed. - Typing goes key by key (no IME commit). - No CI job runs the suite on an emulator yet. - First publish: npm Trusted Publishing needs the package to exist, so `@e2e-dev/android` has to be published once by hand and its trusted publisher connected **before** this merges. Otherwise the nightly and release `changeset publish` fail on it. - Each release machine signs the server with its own debug key, so an upgrade reinstalls it once (`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` is handled by uninstall + install). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.android.config.ts --retries 0` in `apps/mobile-benchmark`: 42 passed on 5 consecutive native runs of the final server (table above, plus two earlier). - Packed tarballs: `pnpm pack` of `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/android` (tarball contains `build/e2e-android-server.apk`), installed in a scratch project under `/tmp`, ran a login-form test from the benchmark (fill, press Enter, tap, assert error, `device.back()`): passed in 2.2s. The device's server hash matched the tarball's APK. - Fresh-context review: fixed the default momentum (`none`, not `slow`), cached reads in rest detection, the server teardown when one connection opens while another closes, the hand-rolled socket connect, `adb.exe` on Windows, and the peer floor. Not changed: the reviewer said ease-out on a small node may not fling at all. That's acceptable for `slow` ("the engine decides how far each carries"): it becomes a drag with an exact stride.

title: feat(cli): e2e doctor preflight with engine doctor hook
body:
Adds `e2e doctor`, a preflight a host can run before a task to learn whether `e2e run` can start. It starts nothing and calls no model unless asked. - Checks four things: - `node`: the runtime. - `config`: the config loads and resolves, with its path and targets. - Per-target engine checks. - `model`: one check per agent. - Never claims which credential a model reads, because the instance owns it. A model check reports the `provider` and `modelId` the AI SDK instance names, so the host can match them to the key it stored. Its status is `unknown` unless e2e can know: - A model from `e2e/oauth/*` reads its provider's API key variable when set, else a login e2e stores, so doctor checks that credential (`pass` or `fail`, with `login` set). The constructors tag the instance through a realm slot (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/login-model.ts`). - `--check-model` makes one short call per model and set of provider options, then reports `pass`, or `fail` with the error code the run would raise. - Engines report their own checks through a new optional hook, `doctor(info) => EngineDoctorCheck[]`, sent over the engine protocol as `lifecycle/doctor` on a connection of its own. A finding that isn't well formed fails as `engine`, a 30 s bound applies, and the hook's progress lines go to stderr. - `@e2e-dev/web` implements it with two checks: - `browser`: `pass` when installed, `warn` when the first run will download it, `skip` for a provider or `connect`. - `init-scripts`: a script file that `prepare` would fail to read. Its peer becomes `e2e >=0.22.1`, since an older e2e rejects the unknown `doctor` key. - `@e2e-dev/mobile` implements it by running agent-device's doctor once for each configured device: - `agent-device`, `toolchain`, and `ios-runner-cache` are reported once. `device` is reported per device, and `target-app` checks the `bundleId` when there is one booted device and no `appPath`. - `app-path` checks that the `appPath` build exists. With a device provider, `device` is `skip`. - The `metro` check is dropped (e2e can't tell whether the build loads from a dev server), and so are `info` findings. Same peer bump. - The docs now point at `e2e doctor` instead of `agent-device doctor`. - Output: - `--json` prints the `doctor-1` report. The schema and fixtures are in `packages/e2e/schema/doctor-v1.schema.json`, and messages are redacted of the config's secrets. - Exit 0 when no check failed, 2 otherwise. `warn`, `skip`, and `unknown` never fail. - On a runtime the CLI refuses, `doctor --json` still prints a report with `node: fail`. ```mermaid flowchart LR N[node] --> C{config loads?} C -- no --> F[config: fail + CONFIG_* code] C -- yes --> E[each target: engine.doctor over the protocol] E --> M[each agent: provider/modelId
login check or --check-model call] ``` ```jsonc // e2e doctor --json { "schemaVersion": "doctor-1", "version": "0.22.1", "ok": true, "checks": [ { "id": "node", "status": "pass", "message": "Node.js 24.19.0 (^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0)" }, { "id": "config", "status": "pass", "path": "/app/e2e.config.ts", "targets": [{ "name": "web", "platform": "web", "engine": "web" }] }, { "id": "browser", "status": "warn", "target": "web", "message": "chromium is not installed; the first run downloads it, ..." }, { "id": "model", "status": "unknown", "agent": "default", "model": { "provider": "gateway", "modelId": "openai/gpt-6-luna-fast" } } ] } ``` Not in this PR: doctor checks for `@e2e-dev/mobile` and the hosted providers. Those targets report `engine: skip` until their engines implement the hook. ## Issue Closes #1115 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. The built CLI on `apps/testbed`, plus a scratch config there with a second `connect` target, a gateway agent, and a `chatgpt()` agent. No login was stored and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` pointed at an empty directory. The `--check-model` run used a real AI Gateway key. ``` $ e2e doctor # apps/testbed ✓ node Node.js 24.19.0 (^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0) ✓ config /e2e.config.ts · targets: web (web) ✓ browser [web] chromium is installed - model [default] no model configured: tests without agent steps run, agent steps fail e2e run can start here exit 0 $ PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH= e2e doctor --config scratch.config.ts ✓ node Node.js 24.19.0 (^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0) ✓ config /doctor-scratch.config.ts · targets: web (web), cdp (web) ! browser [web] chromium is not installed; the first run downloads it, or run "npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium" now - browser [cdp] the browser is attached over CDP ? model [default] gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast · the model reads its own credential; --check-model calls it ✗ model [sub] chatgpt.responses/gpt-6-luna · MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: no stored openai login: run `npx e2e login openai` 1 check failed exit 2 $ e2e doctor --config scratch.config.ts --check-model --target web # real AI Gateway key ✓ model [default] gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast · answered ✗ model [sub] chatgpt.responses/gpt-6-luna · MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: no stored openai login: run `npx e2e login openai` exit 2 ``` - The same `--check-model` run with a bogus key failed as `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` with the gateway's "Unauthenticated request" message. - With `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` holding an openai login, the `sub` agent passed with `"login": "openai"`. That case is also in `tests/integration/cli-doctor.test.ts`. - Under `bun --bun`, which the CLI refuses, `e2e doctor --json` printed a doctor-1 report with `node: fail` and exited 2. - Mobile benchmark on this Mac, with `E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_IOS_DEVICE="Bogus,bsky-e2e"`: ```text ✗ device [ios-simulator] "Bogus": No iOS devices found. Start or create a simulator/emulator, ... ✓ agent-device [ios-simulator] agent-device 0.21.35 using ~/.agent-device ✓ toolchain [ios-simulator] Apple toolchain: Xcode 27.0; xcode-select /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer. ✓ device [ios-simulator] "bsky-e2e": 1 iOS device available; 1 booted. ✓ target-app [ios-simulator] "bsky-e2e": Target app is launchable: dev.e2e.benchmark ✓ ios-runner-cache [ios-simulator] iOS runner artifact cached; first open skips the runner build 1 check failed exit 2 ``` Without the env overrides, both targets pass (exit 0). The Android target with `E2E_MOBILE_BENCHMARK_ANDROID_APP=/tmp/nope.apk` fails `app-path`. - Testbed suite green on the branch. The web benchmark wasn't run: the web engine's run path is unchanged and only gains the new hook.

title: feat(ios): experimental @e2e-dev/ios engine
body: Experimental `@e2e-dev/ios`: an iOS simulator engine that is an [engine protocol](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/engine-protocol) server in Swift, hosted by an XCUITest bundle on the simulator. No agent-device, no daemon, no HTTP hop: observe, locate, and gestures run in process. Built on the engine protocol from #1232. ```ts import { ios } from '@e2e-dev/ios'; export default { targets: [{ name: 'ios', engine: ios(), app: { bundleId: 'com.example.app', appPath: './build/MyApp.app' } }], workers: 1, } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` - The package ships the server's Xcode project. The transport builds it on first use with `xcodebuild build-for-testing` into `~/Library/Caches/e2e/ios-server/` (key: sources, Xcode, arch; `E2E_IOS_BUILD_DIR` overrides), about 7s cold here. `npx e2e-ios-build` builds ahead for CI. A first build that outlives `launchTimeout` keeps going for the next run. - `ios()` is the `connectEngine` client; restart and `clearState` relaunch through `simctl`. - Docs: `docs/ios-engine.mdx` (experimental, under Platforms next to Mobile). CI compiles the server in the iOS deterministic mobile job. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[e2e runner] -- engine protocol over TCP --> S[Swift server in XCUITest runner] S -- XCUITest snapshot --> A[app] S -- XCTest event synthesis --> A H[transport on the Mac] -- xcodebuild test-without-building --> S H -- simctl relaunch / clear --> A ``` ## Benchmark Mobile benchmark iOS selection (`apps/mobile-benchmark/e2e.ios.config.ts`, 41 tests: smoke, login-form, flows, flows-lists, controls), `--retries 0`, iPhone 17 Pro simulator iOS 26.5, Xcode 27, Mac mini shared with other sessions. Runs interleaved native, agent-device, native, agent-device. `@e2e-dev/mobile` on agent-device 0.21.35 (the repo pin), with the benchmark's `transition: 1500`. | Run (in order) | Engine | Wall | Passed | Load avg at start (1/5/15 min) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | native `@e2e-dev/ios` | 251s | 41/41 | 9.29, 11.07, 12.16 | | 2 | `@e2e-dev/mobile` (agent-device) | 434s | 39/41 | 4.82, 7.36, 10.21 | | 3 | native `@e2e-dev/ios` | 253s | 41/41 | 4.32, 6.10, 8.48 | | 4 | `@e2e-dev/mobile` (agent-device) | 427s | 41/41 | 6.55, 5.97, 7.78 | Native is 1.7x faster (252s vs 431s mean). agent-device's run 2 failed `infinite scroll reaches the target item` and `huge virtualized list reaches row 512` (`toHaveText` after a scroll). An earlier round on the pre-review code measured the same split: native 257s / 259s, agent-device 433s / 449s, all 41/41, load 9 to 21. The agent-device runner from the agent-device runs stays alive idle on the simulator during the native runs. Per-operation medians (ms), from the same runs: | operation | native median (n/run) | agent-device median (n/run) | native s/run | agent-device s/run | |---|---|---|---|---| | perform:tap | 351 (89) | 1379 (89) | 42 | 111 | | locate:query | 26 (777) | 50 (860.5) | 26 | 102 | | perform:swipe | 606 (71.5) | 845 (83.5) | 46 | 68 | | perform:fill | 1402 (15) | 2636 (15) | 20 | 45 | | session.restart | 1632 (40) | 798 (40) | 66 | 32 | | perform:press | 657 (10) | 924 (10) | 7 | 12 | | artifacts.screenshot | 142 (1) | 640 (2) | 0 | 1 | | session.back | 1380 (1) | 999 (1) | 1 | 1 | | init | 1781 (1) | 173 (1.5) | 2 | 0 | | observe | 34 (3) | 73 (4) | 0 | 0 | `session.restart` is slower natively because it returns once the relaunched app answers an observation; agent-device returns at launch and its next locate waits instead. `init` is the runner start (`xcodebuild test-without-building`) with the server already built. ## How it got fast Profiled every engine call (wrapper around the engine handle) and the server's phases, then fixed the largest hotspot each round. Full suite wall time, 41/41 every round: | Round | Change | Wall | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | ported engine (1.5s transition budget, XCUITest swipes) | 396s | | | 1 | idle signals and the sheet's host process instead of the transition budget | 323s | -18% | | 2 | synthesized step swipes (1.64s to 0.61s each) | 277s | -14% | | 3 | the engine's own bounded idle wait, XCUITest's waits off | 259s | -6.5% | | final | after review fixes, the runs above | 251s / 253s | | Machine load varied from about 4 to 21 across rounds. - **Idle signals instead of a time budget.** The engine mirrored agent-device's `transition` (wait up to 1.5s after an action for anything that moved). XCTest already knows when the app is idle: before each event the server waits for the app's run loop to idle, then its animations (`Idle.swift`). A system sheet (Save Password) animates in another process, so a node hosted by another foreground process waits for that process too. - **Step swipes synthesized.** XCUITest's `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:withVelocity:)` took 1.6s per swipe. `Gesture.swift` sends one `XCSynthesizedEventRecord`: most of the travel in 150ms, the last 15% at XCUITest's default drag speed, so the fling (and the rows covered per step) matches in 0.6s. A swipe does not wait for the list to stop coasting; a tap waits for idle, throws `NODE_STALE` when its element is gone, and a tap at a point checks the node is still at the observed frame. - **XCUITest's own waits off.** Every XCUITest gesture runs with `XCUIApplicationInteractionOptionSkipPre/PostEventQuiescence`; the engine's wait replaces them. Tried, no gain (under 3%, reverted or kept for simplicity only): - Skipping the post-event idle wait on taps: 277s to 272s; the time moved into locate polling. - Restart: 1.7s, of which the RN app's cold start is about 1.2s (first frame at 1.0-1.3s after `simctl launch`); one `simctl launch --terminate-running-process` instead of terminate + launch saves one process spawn. Remaining time is the app and XCTest: about 210ms per synthesized event is testmanagerd's round trip (a raw `XCSynthesizedEventRecord` tap with a 10ms hold takes 216ms; `tap()` 320ms), app cold start per test, and swipe travel. ## Web view coupon flake `web view coupon form` hung about 1 run in 50: after the tap on the web form's switch, XCUITest's post-event idle wait never got "animations complete" and gave up after 60s, then the next event waited another 60s, and the test timed out. XCTest log: ```text t = 4.36s Tap Switch (First Match) t = 4.42s Synthesize event t = 4.70s Wait for dev.e2e.benchmark to idle t = 64.73s App animations complete notification not received, will attempt to continue. ``` An app with an animation that never ends (reproduced with a repeating `UIView.animate` in the host app) never reports animations idle, and this Xcode has no `waitForIdleTimeout` to bound it. The engine now asks for XCTest's two signals separately (`_notifyWhenMainRunLoopIsIdle:`, `_notifyWhenAnimationsAreIdle:`): run loop idle within the operation's budget, animations idle within 3s. Across the suite the animation waits had p50 6ms, p99 384ms, longest finite 1.2s; the bound fired once, on pull-to-refresh's spinner. 40/40 coupon runs after the change. ## Known gaps - Peer `e2e >=0.22.1 <1` assumes #1232 ships in the next patch; set it to the release that contains the protocol when that lands. - Private XCTest API: `_performWithInteractionOptions:block:`, `_notifyWhen...Idle:`, `XCSynthesizedEventRecord`, `XCTRunnerDaemonSession`, `monitoredApplicationWithProcessIdentifier:`. Any Xcode release can break them. - Simulators only, iOS 18+, one worker; no `app.url`, `launchArguments`, `permissions`, video, device controls beyond `back()`, locator `dragTo`/`hover`, or key modifiers. Double tap is XCUITest's and can land as two taps. - The build cache keeps one directory per key and is never pruned. - `clearState` deletes the data container from the Mac; not checked against `UserDefaults` cached by cfprefsd. - npm trusted publishing has to be set up for the new package name before the first release. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Full selection twice per engine above with `--retries 0`; native 41/41 every run. After rebasing onto main: native 41/41 twice more (254s, 259s). - `pnpm pack`, installed the tarball (with a packed `e2e` from this branch) in a scratch project under `/tmp`, `E2E_IOS_BUILD_DIR= npx e2e run`: the server built from `node_modules` in about 7s and both tests passed (login, and a focused secure field filled wrong, then right, cleared, then right again, then signed in). - `e2e-ios-build` from the tarball builds into the same content-hashed key as the repo.

title: feat(agent): expose point coordinates in onAction
body: ## Issue Fixes #1501 ## Summary - `ActionEvent` is a union narrowed by `action`: `point` for `tapAt`/`hoverAt`, `from`/`to` for `dragAt`, replay included. New `ActionName` and `ActionDetails` types. - Coordinates use the same space as `screen.tapAt` and `boundingBox()`, rounded and clamped to the viewport. Mobile engines have no `hoverAt` or `dragAt`. No engine protocol or cache format changes. - `ActionName` derives from the trace format and `ActionDetails` is the one map of per-action fields; a missing or stale key is a compile error. Points are copied, so hook mutations cannot alter what replay records. ```ts await agent.act('move the pin', { onAction: (event) => { if (event.action === 'dragAt') console.log(event.from, event.to); }, }); ``` ## Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Executor or replay] --> B[Dispatch coordinate action] B --> C[Commit action and settle] C --> D[Copy point or drag endpoints] D --> E[Await onAction] ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Documentation head `1a28d00ded3d52822d0344a0ecea79e93c522390`: `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm plugins:check`, and `pnpm check:changeset-bumps` pass. Runtime sources are unchanged from `ed7d121b89f543fc3dbcfd7e71457cdb288f953d`, where a clean checkout passed `pnpm check`, all 3,247 unit tests, and the 33 focused integration tests. - Built CLI against the canvas fixture, `e2e run --debug`, first recording and then replaying. The hook mutates `point`, `from`, and `to` to `{ x: 50, y: 50 }` after capturing each event. Both runs still report the original dispatched coordinates and verify the pin's final position. Replay self-finalizes with three actions; the integration test also checks the persisted coordinates and that replay never invokes the executor. Fixture project and HTTP server were cleaned up. ```text model hoverAt point={"x":0,"y":0} model tapAt point={"x":300,"y":60} model dragAt from={"x":300,"y":60} to={"x":200,"y":100} replay hoverAt point={"x":0,"y":0} replay tapAt point={"x":300,"y":60} replay dragAt from={"x":300,"y":60} to={"x":200,"y":100} Tests 1 passed (1), on each run ``` - Mutation check: removing the defensive copies fails the regression test because the persisted coordinates change to `{ x: 50, y: 50 }`. Restoring the copies passes recording and replay. - No live model validation. Engine behavior, model inputs, and replay wire format are unchanged. ## CI and review - Head `1a28d00ded3d52822d0344a0ecea79e93c522390`: all four required gates pass: [spec](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/41322640655), [benchmark](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/41322640611), [mobile](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/41322640666), and [docs](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/41322640763). Spec's Node matrix and both install jobs pass; the testbed executes 82 passing tests and one skip. Mobile deterministic runs execute 55 passing tests and one skip on iPhone 17 Pro/iOS 26.5, and 57 passing tests and one skip on Pixel 7/API 36. These are deterministic-suite results, not dedicated native hook regression coverage. The web agent CI job is skipped on the fork. - Cubic completed on this exact head with zero findings. The follow-up automated review confirms the code and documentation fixes; the prior changes-requested review is dismissed. There are zero unresolved review threads, including outdated threads. The branch has no merge conflicts. - Feature-policy agreement on #1501 remains a maintainer decision.

title: Expose coordinate-based action geometry in the onAction hook
agent.assert: portable visibility across device sizes — let the judge explore (scroll/swipe), or add an explicit scroll-to-assert primitive
body:
### Problem

On mobile, whether a set of options is visible in a single viewport depends on device size. The same `agent.assert(..., { vision: 'only' })` that passes on a tablet can fail on a compact phone purely because the content needs scrolling to be fully seen — not because the feature is missing.

Concrete case we hit: a Driver Settings screen lists several rows (HOS Settings, Account, Language, Theme, …). On a tablet-class device the whole list fits; on a compact phone it does not. Our `agent.act` prompt said "scroll to confirm all options are visible", the actor scrolled to the bottom, and the final `vision: 'only'` assertion then judged a frame where the top rows (HOS Settings, Account) had scrolled out of view — so it reported "not all options visible" even though every option exists. The content was present (an earlier frame showed it); the single judged frame just could not contain it all at that scroll position.

Today the judge is a pure, read-only verdict on one captured observation. That is great for determinism, but it means a "are all of X present?" assertion is implicitly a "are all of X present *in one viewport at the current scroll position*?" assertion, which is device-size dependent and pushes authors toward brittle scroll-then-assert prompts.

### Proposal / feedback

Consider giving the judge a bounded way to **explore by scrolling/swiping** when evaluating an assertion — i.e. let `agent.assert` pan a scrollable region to look for the asserted content before returning a verdict, rather than judging only the frame it is handed. The motivating property: an assertion like "the Settings screen shows HOS Settings and Account" should give the same result on a compact phone and a tablet, without the author scripting device-specific scrolls.

This is explicitly feedback, not a fixed design — we see real tension to resolve:

- **Determinism / replay cache.** The judge is currently side-effect-free; letting it scroll makes it mutate the device and makes the verdict depend on an exploration path, which complicates reproducibility and what the replay cache records. Any exploration would need to be bounded and deterministic (e.g. fixed direction/step count, stop on first match, capped), and the cache would need to represent it.
- **Actor vs judge separation.** Scrolling is an action; moving it into the verdict blurs the actor/judge boundary the framework guards. An alternative is keeping exploration in the actor but giving authors a first-class "assert this item is reachable by scrolling this region" primitive, so the scroll is explicit and recorded rather than implicit in the judge.
- **Overlap with existing work.** This is related to but distinct from #1295 (`toBeInViewport`: assert a match intersects the viewport *without* scrolling) and #1324 (visibility flakiness). #1295 is the opposite angle (does it intersect the current viewport); this is "find it even if it needs scrolling, portably across device sizes."

### Why it matters

Mobile suites run the same specs across phone and tablet form factors. A viewport-dependent assertion result is a common source of device-specific flakiness and forces authors into scroll-then-assert prompts that are themselves fragile (the scroll can move the asserted content out of the judged frame, as above). A portable "is this content reachable/visible on this screen" capability — whether in the judge or as an explicit actor-side assertion primitive — would remove a whole class of device-size test bugs.

Happy to provide the recorded session and frames from our case if useful.

title: feat(web)!: WebDriver BiDi driver replaces Playwright
body:
## Summary

- `@e2e-dev/web` drives Chromium and Firefox over WebDriver BiDi. Playwright is removed: no `playwright-core` dependency, no WebKit, no `surfaceOf`.
- Own BiDi client. Firefox speaks BiDi natively; Chromium runs the `chromium-bidi` mapper in a child process. No chromedriver or geckodriver.
- Both browser sockets use `ws` with compression off. Node 22's built-in WebSocket drops the Chromium connection on a CDP message over 4 MB, and Firefox closes a connection after that client's 4096th frame.
- `connect: { cdpEndpoint, context: 'existing' }` drives the page a host already shows, for one that can create no browser context (an Electron app). It replaces what `reconnectEndpoint` was used for there.
- Browsers are pinned builds (Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.38, Firefox 159.0.1), installed with `npx @e2e-dev/web install`, each checked against a pinned SHA-256.
- Ports from main: `credentialOrigins` (#1393), CDP handshake headers (#1634), `readStyle` (#1633), tabs (#1710), core `launch` (#1737), check through a covering label (#1595), screenshot retry after navigation (#1614), `toHaveRole` (#1857), a download's suggested file name for provider reads (#1726), and the Japanese and Chinese docs (#1875, #1886): the 31 pages whose English this PR changes are updated in both.
- Two CDP-only browsers do not work on this driver yet, and their pages say so: Lightpanda opens no page, and Moli (#1843) reads a page but no action reaches an element (18 of 79 testbed tests pass, 35 of 78 on main's driver). Both gaps are on the browser's side.
- Review findings and the commit that fixed each: https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1503#issuecomment-6949569123
- Tests never skip a browser: each Firefox or Chromium limit is a test of what the browser does. Two bugs those skips hid are fixed: Firefox element screenshots were a pixel off after a scroll, and Firefox `dragTo` on an HTML5 `draggable` dropped nothing silently (now `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, [bug 1515879](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1515879)).
- New `web (windows)` CI job: launch, keyboard, and tabs on both browsers.

What breaks is in `.changeset/web-bidi-only.md`. Limits are in `docs/reference/web.mdx`.

## Benchmark totals (before the rebase; 20 warm / 10 cold iterations, M5 Pro, headless)

| Total | PW chromium | BiDi chromium | PW firefox | BiDi firefox |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sum of p50s, every scenario (ms) | 1534 | 981 (-36%) | 2623 | 2116 (-19%) |
| cold launch + new page + 6 agent steps (ms) | 334 | 274 (-18%) | 768 | 1279 (+66%) |
| testbed wall clock, median of 3 (ms) | 17525 | 16895 (-4%) | 21102 | 20980 (-1%) |
| node + browser CPU, warm loop (s) | 51.7 | 20.3 (-61%) | 77.7 | 33.7 (-57%) |
| peak RSS, node + browser (MB) | 1405 | 1542 (+10%) | 2351 | 2644 (+12%) |

Firefox cold launch is slower: the Remote Agent holds `session.new` until startup finishes (925 ms vs 314 ms), once per worker.

## Issue

Spike, no issue.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `@e2e-dev/web`: 2735 tests on Chromium and Firefox, 0 failures, on Node 24 and on Node 22.22.3. One env-gated skip: the crosscheck benchmark scenarios, which run in `benchmark.yml`.
- Testbed through the built CLI on Chromium (589 tests), and on Firefox without the Playwright-tagged tests: all pass.
- Reviewer repros rerun on the head (web font under a route, HTTP cache, tracked inputs, binary bodies in `route.fetch()`, attach on a loaded tab, Electron 45.3.3, a consumer project with `skipLibCheck: false`): all pass.
- `e2e` 4899 and core tests pass, and the 13 other packages' tests. Build, typecheck, oxlint, fallow, docs, plugin, MCP, peer-range, consumer-types, and changeset checks are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [x] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it.
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: test(testbed): Playwright's page tests in the testbed suite
body:
## What and why

- Playwright's own page tests (microsoft/playwright `tests/page` + `tests/library/download.spec.ts` at `v1.64.1`, our `playwright-core` pin), rewritten against the e2e public API, as ordinary testbed tests in `apps/testbed/tests/`. 32 files, ~500 tests: click, fill, check, select, keyboard, locators, actionability and scroll into view, frames, dialogs, route/fulfill/continue/fallback, waitForURL/Response, network idle, screenshots + masks, downloads, file chooser.
- Each describe is tagged `playwright` (`--tag playwright` runs only them). Each file header names its source and lists the tests left out, with the reason.
- Known differences are `fail: 'reason'` (#1539), so a closed gap fails the run until its mark goes: 16 tests. 6 fail with an error `fail` does not cover (an engine failure, or a refused argument), so they are `skip: 'reason'`.
- The playground serves Playwright's assets and its test server's dynamic routes for any path it has no page for (`apps/testbed/app/playwright/`, with `LICENSE` + `NOTICE`; assets unchanged, ignored by lint and fallow). One app, one config, chromium only.
- CI: on a pull request the Testbed step leaves the `playwright` tests out of the model-filtered run and a second step runs all of them (23s locally); a push to main runs everything once.
- 6 testbed tests the ported ones cover are removed (custom dialog handler, route stub/abort, raw keyboard, scrollIntoView, waitForURL).
- One engine fix the tests found: a fixture call that times out names what it waited for (`operation timed out in browser.waitForResponse "foo.css"`), and url-pattern steps quote string patterns.

Marked `fail` (open gaps unless noted):

- elements inside a `visibility: hidden` iframe read as visible (3 tests)
- `uncheck` refuses `role=radio`; `inputValue` on a non-input reads `""` instead of throwing
- `route.fulfill` body string-only; header overrides can't delete a header
- `?` in route globs matches one character (Playwright: literal)
- a page deleting `Map`/`Array` breaks evaluate (main world)
- two screenshot steps at once interfere
- by design per the migrate guide: bare-string `selectOption` matches label only, `textContent()` is rendered text, `isChecked()` on a non-checkable reads false

Marked `skip`: multiple `set-cookie` in a fulfill (2), screenshot while navigating, screenshot with a stalled subframe, `setInputFiles([])`, `timeout: 0`.

CodeQL on the routes (`apps/testbed/app/playwright/routes.mjs`, test-only): the app listens on `127.0.0.1` only; delays and sizes are clamped, redirects stay on the app's two origins, credentialed CORS goes only to those origins, the multipart parse is linear.

## Issue

None. #1503 stacks on this.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

```text

e2e run --tag playwright            503 passed | 6 skipped      23s
pnpm test --exclude-tag playwright   76 passed | 1 skipped
pnpm test (all)                     579 passed | 7 skipped      29s
e2e + web unit, lint, fallow, typecheck, build clean
```

- [x] Changeset added for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change.
- [ ] Docs updated in the same PR (error text only; no page describes it).

title: junit reporter: link a failed test's failure screenshot so GitLab displays it in the test report
body:
### Problem

When a test fails in GitLab CI, the pipeline's test report shows the failure message but not the screenshot e2e took at the failure. The file is in the job's artifacts, since [`docs/ci.mdx`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/8857d24ec36fa28d6ea129904b4f7ee51c593ba6/docs/ci.mdx#L37) says to upload `.e2e/` (`results/` included), and the attempt names it (`failure.screenshot` is the id of a `screenshot` artifact). But `junit.xml` doesn't reference it, so you download the artifacts and look for the test's folder.

The markdown page and the GitHub comment already list this evidence (`evidence` [in](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/8857d24ec36fa28d6ea129904b4f7ee51c593ba6/packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts#L252) `report/markdown.ts`). `junit.xml` is the only output without it.

GitLab links a file from a failed test's details when the testcase's `<system-out>` has `[[ATTACHMENT|path]]`, with the path relative to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR`: https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/testing/unit_test_reports/ ("Add screenshots to test reports")

A locator-only test that fails (`@e2e-dev/web`, no model), on main 8857d24e (e2e 0.22.0). `junit.xml`:

```xml
<testcase name="checkout > places an order [web]" classname="tests/checkout.e2e.ts" time="3.564">
  <failure message="expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByRole("heading", name: "Order confirmed")
expected: visible
observed: no node (match count 0)" type="ASSERTION_FAILED">ASSERTION_FAILED (body): expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByRole("heading", name: "Order confirmed")
expected: visible
observed: no node (match count 0)</failure>
</testcase>
```

The same attempt in `report.json` has `failure.screenshot` pointing at `checkout-places-an-order-011faed9e9076da8/attempt-1/screenshots/001-failure.png` (`redaction: "complete"`), and the file is on disk under `.e2e/results/`.

### Proposed API

No API or config change. A failed or errored case whose told attempt has `failure.screenshot` gets one line; every other case stays as it is:

```xml
<testcase name="checkout > places an order [web]" classname="tests/checkout.e2e.ts" time="3.564">
  <failure message="..." type="ASSERTION_FAILED">...</failure>
  <system-out>[[ATTACHMENT|.e2e/results/checkout-places-an-order-011faed9e9076da8/attempt-1/screenshots/001-failure.png]]</system-out>
</testcase>
```

The reporter already gets `projectRoot` and `artifactsRoot` in `FinishedRun` ([`types.ts`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/8857d24ec36fa28d6ea129904b4f7ee51c593ba6/packages/e2e/src/types.ts#L1514-L1518)), so the path can be built without reading anything outside the run. It is the same file the upload already holds, so nothing new leaves the job. Reporter output is outside the stability policy, and a CI service that doesn't read the tag treats the line as ordinary test output.

One question before a PR: which base should the path use? GitLab resolves it from the repository root, so a path from the project root breaks when the e2e project is in a subdirectory. Either the project root (right when the project is the repository root), or the path from `CI_PROJECT_DIR` when it is set, the way `@e2e-dev/github` uses `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.

If leaving evidence out of `junit.xml` was intentional, to keep it the smallest reporter example, that's fine too. Otherwise I'm happy to open the PR: the change in `report/junit.ts`, cases in `tests/unit/report-junit.test.ts`, a line in `docs/ci.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/running.md`, and a patch changeset.

### Which surface

(none of the options: the output of the `junit` reporter)

### Compatibility

Additive. Only a failed or errored case with a failure screenshot gains a `<system-out>` (today such a case has none). Every other case is unchanged, and the report schema, config, CLI and exit codes are untouched.

title: web: configurable observation node budget for dense pages
body:
### Problem

The web engine has a fixed 3,000-node observation budget in `packages/web/src/observation-capture.ts`. On a storefront page with about 4,900 nodes, fixed navigation controls appear late in traversal and are omitted. The page looks ready, but the agent cannot address those controls. Our downstream `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.4` patch raises the constant to 8,000 and made those controls available. That is a local workaround; raising the default for every target would spend more tokens everywhere.

I checked current upstream source: `MAX_OBSERVED_NODES` is still 3,000. #1237 covers reporting truncation; this request is about choosing the limit for a known dense target.

### Proposed API

```ts
web({ observationNodeBudget: 8_000 })
```

Keep 3,000 as the default. Validate the override as a positive safe integer at target creation, and pass one shared budget through the main document and its frames. Preserve the existing truncation flag and observation timeout. Tests would cover the default, an override reaching a control after the old cutoff, invalid values, and a shared cross-frame limit. Documentation would explain the extra token and capture cost.

title: fix(cache): extract shared date patterns to internal/dates and drop false positives
body:
## What and why

Follow-up to #1496 and #1498 addressing maintainer review feedback:
- Extracted shared date and time regex patterns (`ISO_DATE`, `CLOCK_TIME`, `MONTH_DAY_DATE`, `DAY_MONTH_DATE`) into neutral `src/internal/dates.ts`, shared by both `agent/derived.ts` and `cache/anchors.ts`. Kept `MONTH` and `DAY` unexported to avoid unused exports.
- Rebased on `main` (now containing #1498) and dropped duplicated `deltaMismatch` tests.
- Reverted unrelated import churn in `anchors.ts` and collapsed blank lines in `derived.ts`.
- Eliminated false-positive volatile anchor matches on non-date terms (e.g. `Marketing 12`, `Mayor 3`, `Augusta 3`, `12 Marketing`) which previously matched due to loose `[a-z]*` month prefixes.
- Updated unit test in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-anchors.test.ts` with inputs that main actually matched to prove the fix.
- User-facing changeset in `.changeset/unify-date-anchor-patterns.md`.
- *Note on non-English months*: Main's `[a-z]*` pattern previously matched some non-English month words by accident (e.g. `3 septembre`, `Octobre 3`, `Juni 3`, `Marzo 3`). With this change they are no longer treated as volatile text anchors (leading safely to a cache handoff rather than a false pass).
- *Note on `derived.ts` spacing*: The shared pattern uses `\s+` instead of the previous single space between month, day, and year, so inputs with multiple spaces or whitespace tabs (e.g. `Oct  26`, `Oct\t26`, `26\nOct`) now also count as dates in `derivedReason`.

## Issue

Follow-up refactor to #1496 / #1498

## Verified

Ran regression checks covering:
- Dates with ordinal suffixes in both month-first and day-first formats.
- False positive checks against `Marketing 12`, `Mayor 3`, `Augusta 3`, and `12 Marketing`.
- Unit tests in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-anchors.test.ts` and `agent/derived.ts` integration.

title: fix(mobile): name the agent-device session for device-cloud leases

title: agent: assert and waitFor cannot judge the current URL
body:
### What happened

An instruction about the current URL fails even when the URL matches.

```ts
await app.open('/page');
await agent.assert('The URL path is /page'); // ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE
await agent.waitFor('The URL path is /page'); // STEP_TIMEOUT
```

A wrong path gives the same `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` instead of `ASSERTION_FAILED`. The judge says it cannot see the URL:

```text
ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE: The observation does not show the current URL or its path, so I cannot determine whether it is /page.; the judge saw the semantic tree only; if the engine captures pixels, pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels
```

`expect(browser).toHaveURL('/page')` passes on the same page.

I expected the judge to compare the current URL with the instruction.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/two-pack/e2e-judge-url-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set a model in `.env`. The README lists the options.
2. `npm install`
3. `npm test`

With `gpt-6-luna` through the OpenAI API, 4 of the 5 tests fail:

| Test | Instruction | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| control | `toHaveURL('/page')` on `/page` | passes | passes |
| assert A | `The URL path is /page` on `/page` | passes | `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` |
| assert B | `The URL path is /other` on `/page` | `ASSERTION_FAILED` | `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` |
| waitFor A | `The URL path is /page` on `/page` | passes | `STEP_TIMEOUT` |
| waitFor B | `The URL path is /moved` on `/moving`, which moves to `/moved` after 3 s with the same content | passes | `STEP_TIMEOUT` |

Without a key, `npm run test:stub` runs the same tests on a stub model and writes every prompt to `.e2e/stub-prompts.log`. The URL is in none of them.

### Versions

e2e 0.22.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.4, node 24.22.1, model gpt-6-luna

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

There are two causes, both in core:

- `buildPrompt` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts` leaves the location out of `<observation>`. `agent.act` gets it, and `docs/reference/security.mdx` lists the current URL as part of the prompt.
- `waitForNextJudgment` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/index.ts` judges again only when `observationShape` changes, and that shape ignores the location. In `waitFor B` only the URL changes, so the judge is asked once.

title: fix(agent): show the judge the current location
body: ## What and why - The built-in judge never saw the current URL, so `agent.assert` and `agent.waitFor` about the address ended `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` or `STEP_TIMEOUT`, whether or not it matched. `agent.act` already reads the location. - `buildPrompt` now puts it on `` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/prompts.ts:101`). It is the same redacted value `act` reads, a path on the app's origin and the whole address off it, without userinfo, cut at 256 characters like a link target (`judgedLocation` in `observation.ts`). - `JUDGMENT_REQUEST` gets one line: the location is evidence only for an instruction about the address, never for what the screen shows. - `waitFor` judges again when only the location changes, as after `history.replaceState` (`index.ts:390`). It skips that under `vision: 'only'`, which is not shown the location. ```text ``` ## Issue Fixes #1514 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The issue's reproduction, https://github.com/two-pack/e2e-judge-url-repro, run with `npm test` and `gpt-6-luna`: | Test | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | control, `toHaveURL('/page')` | passes | passes | | assert A, `The URL path is /page` | `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` | passes | | assert B, `The URL path is /other` | `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` | `ASSERTION_FAILED` as expected | | waitFor A, `The URL path is /page` | `STEP_TIMEOUT` | passes | | waitFor B, only the URL changes | `STEP_TIMEOUT` | passes | - Web benchmark `tests-agent`, `--strict-cache` with `gpt-6-luna` in place of the gateway model: 33 passed, no `REPLAY_STALE`. - `pnpm bench:ab` on the web benchmark: every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on both builds, and suite time was `same`. - Not run: `--no-cache --ai-trace` on the agent suites. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(mcp): run_tests tool runs e2e run from the MCP server
body: ## What and why - `e2e mcp` gets a fifth tool, `run_tests`: runs one test, a file, or the whole suite as `e2e run` does, so an agent with only the MCP server can write, run, and fix tests without a shell. - The run is the CLI's own `e2e run`, spawned from the same e2e install (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/run-tests.ts`). Workers, retries, cache, `report.json`, and exit codes match the CLI exactly. In-process `runSuite` was ruled out: it conflicts with live sessions' registries, process ownership (`RUNNER_BUSY`), and the server's stdio claim. - Result = command line, exit code + meaning, then the list reporter text (what agents already read from `npx e2e run`). Exit 0/1 are results; 2+ is `isError`. Output past 60k chars keeps its end. - Typed fields map to CLI flags (`files`, `config`, `target`, `grep`, `tag`, `lastFailed`, `retries`, `actionTimeout`, `repeatEach`, `noCache`, ...). Values go in `--flag=value` form and files after `--`, so neither can be read as a flag (`--watch` included). - Lifetime: one run at a time (`RUNNER_BUSY`). A cancelled call climbs the CLI's Ctrl-C ladder every 15s, then SIGKILLs the child's process group. Server shutdown refuses new runs and stops the one in flight. If the server dies, the CLI sees its IPC channel close and interrupts itself (`packages/e2e/src/cli/signals.ts`). - Each stdout line is an MCP progress notification (bounded to 1000 chars) when the client sends a progress token. ```txt run_tests {files: ["tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12"], retries: 0, actionTimeout: 5000} ``` ```text e2e run --retries=0 --action-timeout=5000 -- tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12 exit 1: a test failed or timed out RUN e2e v0.22.0 /work/shop ... ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Verified with the built server on `apps/testbed` and a real MCP client (`@modelcontextprotocol/client` over stdio): | Call | Result | | --- | --- | | `{files: ["tests/todos.e2e.ts:20"], retries: 0, actionTimeout: 5000}` | exit 0, 1 passed, 9 progress events | | `{}` (whole suite) | exit 0, 82 passed, 1 skipped, 18s, 106 progress events | | failing scratch test | exit 1, the CLI's failure block with code frame and trace path | | cancel a whole-suite run after 3s, then run one test | next run started about 1s later and passed; no stray processes | | client disconnects mid-run | server, CLI, and app process all gone; port 4271 free | | `run_tests` while a session is open (testbed app on a fixed port) | `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`, as documented in mcp-server.mdx; the session keeps working | `tests/integration/mcp-run-tests.test.ts` covers the same cases, plus: a run queued behind a cancelled one is refused at shutdown, and a SIGKILLed server's run exits on its own. A thermo-nuclear review (GPT 6 Astra) found 8 issues; all are fixed in this PR: shutdown admission, no kill deadline, orphan on server death, a kill `error` treated as an exit, watch bypass via `files`, unbounded pending progress line, a truncation edge case, and a test with no readiness barrier. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(explore): return to covered flows with edge-case lenses
body:
Explore runs planned one pass over the flows the goal names and finished early, missing edge-case input bugs, filter and sort combination bugs, and the same defect on other screens.

- Planner (`packages/e2e/src/explore/plan.ts`): after breadth, return to each flow with a new lens per step: edge-case inputs; filters, sorting, and search combined; state after reload or across screens showing the same data; another account or role (only with more than one account and no restored `--session`). Plan a step checking sibling screens for a control a finding named. Step titles name the lens, so the planner sees which lens each step used. Finish only when nothing new is reachable or every applicable lens ran, not while time is left.
- Explorer (`packages/e2e/src/explore/executor.ts`): an edge-case input rule (deletes or renames only records it created this run; an edge input is a defect when the app mangles, loses, or contradicts it, or a required field accepts blank input), and "the same defect on another kind of screen is a new finding, on another record of the same screen it is not".
- Tradeoff: runs now usually use the whole step budget, about 2x time and cost.
- `docs/explore.mdx` sentence, unit test for the account lens, patch changeset.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Built CLI, `e2e explore` on the testbed bug garden (`apps/testbed/app/bug-garden.mjs`, 11 planted defects), same goal, `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `--max-steps 12 --timeout 900000`, 3 runs each:
