title: feat(explore): allow runs up to 100 steps and 2 hours
body: On a larger app, 12 steps / 15 minutes ends before the main flows are explored in depth, and longer runs keep finding new defects. - `e2e explore --max-steps` max 12 -> 100, `--timeout` max 900000 -> 7200000 (2 hours), `packages/e2e/src/explore/index.ts`. Defaults unchanged: 8 steps, 600000. - Planner prompt stays bounded: only the latest 8 steps carry their summary, older ones list title and outcome (`packages/e2e/src/explore/plan.ts`). Without this, 100 steps of summaries overflow the 64k `maxInputTokens` default and the run aborts with `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. - Docs (`explore.mdx`, `reference/cli.mdx`, `reference/runner.mdx`), skill references, JSDoc, patch changeset. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI on the testbed, bounds: ```text $ e2e explore --max-steps=101 error: option '--max-steps ' argument '101' is invalid. must be an integer from 1 through 100 (exit 2) $ e2e explore --timeout=7200001 error: option '--timeout ' argument '7200001' is invalid. must be an integer from 180000 through 7200000 (exit 2) ``` - Live runs on the bookshop (`e2e.explore.config.ts`), all reach the assessment: ```text --max-steps=100 --timeout=180000 budgets {"maxSteps":100,"timeoutMs":180000} finished, 1 of 100 steps, 2 issues --max-steps=1 --timeout=7200000 budgets {"maxSteps":1,"timeoutMs":7200000} step-limit, 1 of 1 steps, 2 issues --max-steps=100 --timeout=1200000 finished, 7 of 100 steps, 9 issues | 1 warning, 4m 56s ``` - Unit test builds 100 max-size steps and checks the planner prompt stays under 40k chars (about 420k before the fix).

title: feat(agent): resize_viewport verb for responsive layouts
body: ## What and why - Agents could not check responsive layouts or bugs that only show at narrow widths: the viewport was fixed for the whole attempt. - New optional engine hook `EngineSession.resize?(size, context)` (protocol method `session/resize`). `@e2e-dev/web` implements it via `setViewport`. - The built-in agent gets a `resize_viewport` grammar tool only when the target's engine has the hook. Sides are whole CSS pixels, 200 to 4096. - Custom executors call `ctx.actions.resize({ width, height })`. - Cache: recorded in `trace-1` as a `resize` action and replayed as given. A resize before the opening `navigate` keeps the trace's replay-from-anywhere exemption. - The step's report entry carries the new `viewport`, as `browser.setViewport` does. - MCP: `resize_viewport` prints no test line (core stays engine-neutral), the note names the size to set with the engine fixture. ```ts test('the header collapses into a menu button at phone width', async ({ browser, agent, screen }) => { await browser.goto('/'); await agent.act('resize the viewport to a phone, 390 wide and 844 tall'); await expect(screen.getByRole('link', 'Pricing')).toBeHidden(); await expect(screen.getByRole('button', 'Open menu')).toBeVisible(); }); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI on the testbed with a scratch config pointing at a small page whose header collapses to a menu button and whose grid goes to one column below 600px. Test above plus `app.screenshot` before and after. - Live run (`--no-cache --ai-trace`): the agent's first call is `resize_viewport`, 2 model calls, test passes. The cache entry holds `{ "name": "resize", "size": { "width": 390, "height": 844 } }`. - Replay with `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` unset; the `agent.act` step in `report.json` has `"viewport":{"width":390,"height":844,"scale":1}`: ```text ✓ |web| tests-rv/responsive.e2e.ts > the header collapses into a menu button at phone width Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) Cache 1 replayed ``` | Before resize | After `resize_viewport` (replay) | | --- | --- | | ![desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9b868e1-0805-4cdb-8c83-eb6ec431fe0e) | ![phone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0dba549-9e9c-4106-b313-b1f72bd7dda0) |

title: feat(report): link failure screenshots as GitLab attachments in JUnit XML
body:
## What and why

- The `junit` reporter links a test's failure screenshot as `<system-out>[[ATTACHMENT|<path>]]</system-out>`, which GitLab CI shows in the pipeline test report.
- It applies to a test that failed, timed out, passed only on a retry, or failed as `test.fail` expected.
- The path is relative to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR`, else the project root. A screenshot outside that base gets no link.
- One `systemOut(lines)` renders every `<system-out>`: the flaky note, the `test.fail` note, then the attachment.
- `posixRelative(from, to)` in `report/write.ts` replaces three copies in `junit.ts`, `markdown.ts`, and `traces.ts`.

## Issue

Fixes #1507

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- 45 tests in `report-junit.test.ts`, including `CI_PROJECT_DIR` unset, blank, a parent of the project, equal to the artifacts root, symlinked to either, and an artifacts root that is itself a symlink.
- Testbed, `CI_PROJECT_DIR=<repo root> e2e run --reporter junit` with one failing test and one `{ fail: 'known bug' }` test:

~~~xml
<system-out>[[ATTACHMENT|apps/testbed/.e2e/results/zz-junit-verify-deliberately-fails-for-junit-…/attempt-1/screenshots/001-failure.png]]</system-out>
<system-out>failed as expected: known bug
~~~

Both PNGs exist at those paths. With `CI_PROJECT_DIR` unset the paths start at `.e2e/results/`.

title: APP_UNREACHABLE drops the first startup lines when an app keeps logging
body:
`ManagedProcess.outputSince` (`packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`) returns only the last `OUTPUT_TAIL_LINES` (20) lines that the process wrote after it started. Some dev stacks fail early and then keep printing, for example a file watcher. The real error then falls out of the `APP_UNREACHABLE` message.

**Proposed change:** when the read starts at the process's own log offset, return the first 20 and the last 20 lines with a `[startup output omitted]` marker between them. Keep both reads bounded by `OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES` and pass them through the existing redactor.

The code is unchanged in 0.22.0 and in the 2026-11-02 nightly. We carry this as a local patch against 0.21.3 and can open a PR with a test.

title: mobile: the auto-selected iOS pool includes a paired iPhone that is not connected
body:
### What happened

Without `device`, `mobile({ platform: 'ios' })` gave a worker slot to a paired iPhone that is not connected. The phone is unplugged and off Wi-Fi, and `xcrun devicectl list devices` shows it as `unavailable`. Every test scheduled on that slot fails at `app.open()`:

```text
ENGINE_FAILURE: open com.apple.Preferences failed: Failed to list iOS apps: The device is not able to fulfill the requested usage assertion requirements. (com.apple.dt.CoreDeviceError error 4016 (0xFB0)) Hint: Ensure the iOS device is unlocked, trusted, and available in Xcode > Devices, then retry.
```

The tests on the booted simulators pass. Which test fails depends on which one the phone's worker picks up. With fewer workers than booted devices, the phone may get no slot, so the failure comes and goes between runs.

I expected the automatic pool to hold only devices the run can reach, with a connected phone still in it. A device named in `device` should still be driven as named and fail clearly when it is unreachable, without a fallback to another device.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/gronxb/e2e-repro-disconnected-ios-device

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a Mac, pair an iPhone with Xcode, then unplug it so `xcrun devicectl list devices` shows it as `unavailable`.
2. Boot at least one iOS simulator.
3. `npm install`
4. `./repro.sh`, which prints both device inventories, then runs `npx e2e run` (six launch-only tests on six workers).

```text
== devicectl: physical devices and their tunnel state
My iPhone  00008160-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX  tunnelState=unavailable
== agent-device: booted iOS devices
iPhone 16  0368C5D9-63CF-447E-B6BB-0E3184B1CD0A  kind=simulator  booted=true
iPhone 17  85F41C8A-12A5-43D0-880C-04900468F2DD  kind=simulator  booted=true
iPhone 17  5D1B8C0C-2FD6-4B03-AC8F-7A93CAB2EA5B  kind=simulator  booted=true
My iPhone  00008160-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX  kind=device  booted=true
== e2e run
ℹ 4 booted ios device(s); driving 4: iPhone 16, iPhone 17, iPhone 17, My iPhone
   × |ios| tests/open-4.e2e.ts > Settings launches
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

Expected: the phone is left out of the pool, and all six tests run on the simulators.

### Versions

e2e 0.22.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.5 (agent-device 0.21.35), node 24.22.1, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

### Anything else

- `BootedDevices` in `packages/mobile/src/pool.ts` keeps every inventory entry with `booted: true`. agent-device's `devicectl` inventory sets `booted: true` on every physical Apple device it lists and never reads `connectionProperties.tunnelState`. This is still the case in agent-device 0.21.36 and 0.21.37-nightly.20261103.128. `agent-device boot` and `capabilities` both succeed on the disconnected phone, so the app launch is the first thing that fails.
- In `prepare`, the phone's slot also logs `prepare ios-runner failed: The iOS device reports that Developer Mode is turned off`. The 4016 error lists no assertable states (`CurrentlyAssertableStates = ()`), and devicectl reports the tunnel as `unavailable`, so I read the failure as a connection problem.
- Found while reproducing, separate from this bug: passing a physical iPhone's UDID (`00008160-…`, 8+16 hex) as `device` makes the engine read it as a name, because `deviceSelection` only matches the simulator UDID shape. agent-device then refuses it with "is the id of …, not its name. Did you mean --udid". Naming the phone by its name works.
- I have a fix ready. With no `device`, the engine asks `devicectl` once and leaves out physical devices whose tunnel is `unavailable`. It skips that check for a remote daemon, and it keeps every device if `devicectl` cannot answer. I can open a PR.

title: perf(web): capture trace screens without element handles
body:
## What and why

- The trace's screen after each action is a diagnostic capture. The engine contract says a post-action read is on the action path, so it must be bounded and may skip expensive work, and refs in it are not valid for `perform` (`docs/reference/engine.mdx`).
- The web engine still read, staged, and disposed one `ElementHandle` per observed node for that capture. With the default `retain-on-failure` trace, this ran for every attempt.
- `captureObservation` now takes `retainRefs` (default `true`); the trace passes `false`. The capture reserves ids as before, skips the per-node handle readback, and fetches only iframe boundary elements so `contentFrame()` still stitches nested documents. The snapshot is byte-identical.
- Direction checked against history: #869 introduced trace pages and measured the cost (about 14 ms per step); its mobile engine already reuses the locate snapshot for the trace. #562 is the same-file metadata-transfer precedent, and the contract explicitly allows skipping expensive trace reads.

## Issue

No issue. This is a maintainer performance fix inside the existing trace contract; the public API and trace output do not change.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes (macOS, Chromium 156, Node 24; branch build)

- `pnpm check` exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run test`: 67 files, 642 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/integration/traces.test.ts`: 6 passed.
- Trace parity: the built CLI ran `--trace on` on `iframe-form`, `hover-menu`, and `rich-text-editor` (6 tests) on main and on this branch. After masking timings and run ids, all six `trace.md` files are identical, including the `screen:` lines.
- New `packages/web/tests/integration/trace-capture.test.ts`: the normal and trace-only captures produce byte-identical trees with nested iframes; the trace path makes 0 `getProperties()` calls and only indexed iframe reads; the trace path stages no refs.
- Full root `pnpm test` was not run.
- The final commit only wraps one comment line in `trace-feed.ts`; the results above ran on the previous revision `23a7dc28`.

Bench: `pnpm bench:ab --suite web-benchmark --no-build`, 6 pairs in random order, trace on by default, threshold ±5%, load average 1.6.

| Pair | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 72.36 s | 66.30 s |
| 2 | 72.46 s | 66.30 s |
| 3 | 71.83 s | 65.39 s |
| 4 | 72.00 s | 66.93 s |
| 5 | 72.28 s | 65.94 s |
| 6 | 72.12 s | 65.99 s |

| Metric | Base | Head | Change (95% CI) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wall (process) | 73.64 s | 67.56 s | -8.4% (-8.7% to -7.6%) | faster |
| suite (sum of attempts) | 72.20 s | 66.14 s | -8.5% (-8.9% to -7.7%) | faster |
| action (events) | 39.57 s | 35.02 s | -11.5% (-12.4% to -10.3%) | faster |
| step `screen.scrollUntilVisible` | 24.41 s | 19.86 s | -18.5% | faster |
| step `locator.tap` | 11.59 s | 10.72 s | -7.3% | faster |
| step `app.open` | 8.59 s | 8.21 s | -4.3% | same |

Every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on every run of both builds. 16 of 91 tests moved outside the threshold, all faster.

### Counter note

`bench-ab` reports one counter movement: `engine` events 809-810 -> 826-829. It comes from `infinite-scroll › scrolls the feed until the Golden Ticket loads`, where `scrollUntilVisible` runs 46 -> 63-65 engine events. The feed loads on a `setTimeout`, so faster captures fit more scroll strides into the same load. The step sequence and outcome are unchanged, and base repeats at 46.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. (`.changeset/web-trace-screen-no-handles.md`, patch for `@e2e-dev/web`.)
- [x] Breaking change: not applicable.
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: no change needed; the public API and trace output are unchanged.
- [x] Contract change: none; `captureObservation` remains internal.
- [x] Engine contract change: none.

## AI assistance and human review

AI was used to prepare these changes. Human-reviewed by @kdy1.
- Harness: Claude Code (T3 Code delegate, macOS)
- Model: claude-sonnet-5-5
- Reasoning Effort: high

title: chore(deps): bump node-forge from 1.4.0 to 1.4.3
body:
Bumps [node-forge](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge) from 1.4.0 to 1.4.3.
Changelog

Sourced from node-forge's changelog.

1.4.3 - 2026-11-03

Security

  • HIGH: X.509 certificate chain verification ignores name constraints.
    • pki.verifyCertificateChain() does not check the nameConstraints extension (RFC 5280 4.2.1.10). A non-critical nameConstraints extension in a CA certificate is ignored, so a name-constrained intermediate CA can issue certificates for names outside its permitted subtrees, or inside its excluded subtrees, and the chain verifies. Exploitation requires the private key of a name-constrained CA that chains to a trusted root. A critical nameConstraints extension is rejected as an unsupported critical extension.
    • Reported by @​bhaswanthc.
    • CVE ID: CVE-TBD
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-3cc4-3294-vgjf
  • MODERATE: TLS client crash on a handshake record without a session.
    • A TLS client throws an uncaught TypeError from process() when it receives a ServerHello while it has no session: after a close_notify alert or a call to close(), or before handshake() is called. A malicious server, or an on-path attacker, can terminate a Node.js process that passes socket data to process() without catching exceptions. Servers are not affected.
    • Reported by @​manus-use.
    • CVE ID: CVE-TBD
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-j8rw-jp99-435v
  • MODERATE: ReDoS in forge.http response header parsing.
    • forge.http trims response header and Set-Cookie values with a regular expression that takes quadratic time on a long run of whitespace followed by another character. A server, or an on-path attacker, can block a forge.http client for minutes with one large header.
    • Reported by @​manus-pi.
    • CVE ID: CVE-TBD
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-6cv4-p8m7-4r25
  • MODERATE: TLS client crash on an unsupported ServerHello compression method.
    • A TLS client accepts any compression method in the ServerHello, although it only offers no compression. An unknown method makes process() throw an uncaught Error at ServerHelloDone, before the server is authenticated. A malicious server, or an on-path attacker, can terminate a Node.js process that passes socket data to process() without catching exceptions, including through forge.tls.wrapSocket. Servers are not affected.
    • Reported by @​alienkeric.
    • CVE ID: CVE-TBD
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-w4xr-hqv8-ch44
  • LOW: Ed25519 signature verification accepts small-order public keys.
    • ed25519.verify() does not reject public keys of small order, such as the identity point. Under such a key, a signature with S = 0 and a small-order R verifies for many or, with the identity key, all messages, without any private key. Applications are affected only if

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 936b24d Release 1.4.3.
  • 4d8f79a Update changelog.
  • 1d9816d Check the ServerHello compression method.
  • 326a4d0 Trim forge.http header values in linear time.
  • 2cfaeb5 Ignore handshake messages on a TLS client without a session.
  • 6b23eae Complete nameConstraints enforcement.
  • 862aa5f Enforce nameConstraints in verifyCertificateChain().
  • 956f2b5 Document ed25519.verify() small-order key behavior.

chore(examples): restyle the examples to the e2e design system
body: All ten examples now follow the e2e design system: the brand palette, the 8px spacing grid, square controls, lowercase headings and UI, and the official e2e logo. The tests and READMEs follow the new copy. - Palette: black canvas, off-white text, `#1C1C1C` surfaces, e2e blue (`#1A5FFF`) for the greet button, green for the caption and focus, mint for the error. The button changes no colour on hover or press; a press scales it slightly, except in Flutter, which keeps its stock `TextButton` for keyboard focus. - Fonts: Inter and JetBrains Mono (both SIL OFL) replace Stack Sans Notch and DM Mono. The brand's own typefaces are commercially licensed and can't ship in a repository that `e2e init` copies, so these stand in for them. The `OFL.txt` notices list the new fonts. - Text field: the design system's field, with the `name` label inside it above the value. Focus and the error change the outline colour only, so nothing moves. The `Ada Lovelace` placeholder is gone. On the web examples from 768px up, the greet button sits beside the field (both 56px tall) and the error and greeting span the row below; phones keep the stacked, full-width button. - Logo: the logotype is drawn from the official logo's bar geometry. Web uses the SVG, Expo the PNG, and SwiftUI, Compose, KMP, Flutter and MAUI draw it natively, so no image is needed. The app icons are the blue e2e sign, replacing the helmet. - Copy and tests: `say hello`, `name`, `greet`, `enter a name first.`, `hello, Ada!` and the `[ with-vite ]` caption are written lowercase in the source, never through `text-transform`, because locators match case. title: feat(explore): run parallel explorers with focuses and merge their findings
body:
One explorer walks the main flows once and finds the easy bugs. Several explorers working on the same goal, each with a different focus, find more. A merge step afterwards keeps the report free of duplicates.

## What changed

- `e2e explore --parallel <n>` runs 1-5 explorers, default 1. It is also available as `parallel` on `explore` from `e2e/runner`. With `--parallel 1` the behavior and the report are the same as before.
- Each explorer gets the whole goal plus one focus, a kind of defect, worded for any app (`explore/focus.ts`):
  1. wrong results
  2. input and validation
  3. state and navigation
  4. layout and environment, worded per target platform: widths and `resize_viewport` on web; rotation, background and resume, the keyboard, permission prompts and deep links on iOS and Android; a generic wording elsewhere. With more than one account and no `--session`, it also checks other roles.
  5. errors and recovery

  The planner reads the focus on a `Focus:` line next to the goal. The explorer reads it through the test's `agentContext`. Explorers are told that they share the app with the other explorers.
- `--focus "<text>"` (repeatable, up to 5), and `focuses` on `explore` from `e2e/runner`, replace the built-in list with the user's own, one explorer each. Without `--parallel`, the explorer count is the number of focuses. A `--parallel` that does not match it exits 2. Labels come from each text's first clause.
- One run holds N explorers. Each explorer is a test in its own virtual file (`explore/1`..`explore/n`), so each one is its own work unit. The app command and a `--session` setup run once. Reporters, artifacts, video, the AI trace, usage and the exit code all stay the runner's own.
- `--timeout` and `--max-steps` are each explorer's own budget, not a budget for the whole run.

### Units built in memory (`packages/e2e/src/run/unit-source.ts`)

- A generic `UnitSource` builds a virtual file's registration plus its `UnitAttemptPolicy` (agents to use, cache off).
- `TargetWorker` calls it the same way in both transports. The policy travels with the realm, so the transports no longer pass state through a shared map.
- The tests' events cross back as a generic `unit-event` message carrying the unit's file.
- In the runner's process the source also has generic hooks: `start` (put events on the run's spine), `receive` (a unit's events), `finish` (after the engines and the app are gone), and `report` (fields for `run`). The explore adapter uses them to emit `explore` events, merge, and add `run.explore`.
- A worker process loads the source from a module descriptor (`UnitSourceModule`). The explorer adapter (`explore/explorer.ts`: `explorerSource`, `createUnitSource`) is the only code that knows about explorers.
- `scheduler.ts`, `worker/entry.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `runner.ts` and `execute.ts` do not mention exploration.
- With a config file, each explorer gets its own worker process. With a config value, the explorers run one after another in-process, and a notice says so. When the engine provides fewer workers than explorers, a notice says so and the rest wait.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E[explore] -- UnitSource / UnitSourceModule --> R[runner]
  R --> W1[worker 1] & W2[worker 2] & W3[worker 3]
  W1 & W2 & W3 -- "TargetWorker: source.build(file) -> registration + policy" --> T[explorer tests]
  T -- "unit-event (file, progress)" --> REC[ExploreRecord]
  REC -- after teardown --> M[merge call] --> REP[run.explore]
```

### Merge (`explore/merge.ts`, `explore/record.ts`)

- After all explorers finish, one structured call groups the findings that describe the same failure. Each finding is sent with its title, expected and actual results, path, and reproduction steps.
- The grouping is validated when the answer comes back. A repeated index, an index out of range, or an empty group is rejected, and every finding is kept, with a notice. Indices the model left out become groups of one.
- The call's usage is recorded before the result is applied. The model adapter attaches the answer's usage to the error a failed call throws, so an answer outside the schema is counted too. The usage survives an invalid grouping and an interrupt that lands during the call (`status: interrupted`). A provider that honors the abort and rejects reports no usage, and none is invented.
- One `merge` progress event carries the outcome and the usage. The list reporter adds that usage to its AI totals, so the terminal agrees with `report.json`.

### Report and reporters

- The report changes are additive:
  - `run.explore.explorers[]`
  - `merge`: `status` (`merged`, `failed` or `interrupted`), `reported`, and `model`, which holds the call's usage once it answered
  - `explorer` on every step and finding
  - `merged[]` on a kept finding, listing the absorbed findings with their evidence
- The schema requires explorer identity whenever `explorers` is present, bounds that identity by the explorer count, rejects `merge` without `explorers`, and requires `model` when the merge succeeded.
- List reporter:
  - Every explorer gets its slot from the first explorer's start, so one that never started is still shown.
  - When the run ends, every slot is finalized: an interrupt shows each unfinished explorer as cut short, never as "waiting".
  - Rows are tagged `[i]`, and the record and the findings name the explorer they came from.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The built CLI ran on the testbed bug garden (11 planted defects) with model `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `--max-steps 6 --timeout 480000` per explorer, and the same goal in every run. I classified the findings by hand.

| Run | Real defects | Reported -> after merge | False positives | Cost | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--parallel 1` | 9 | 10 | 0 | $0.026 | 145s |
| `--parallel 3`, earlier focus wording | 9 (8 planted + 1) | 28 -> 14 | 3 | $0.108 | 284s |
| `--parallel 3`, focuses by kind of defect | 11 (9 planted + 2) | 34 -> 22 | 4 | $0.124 | 383s |
| `--parallel 3`, Ctrl-C at 75s | - | 19 kept, no merge | - | $0.038 | 75s |

In the defect-kind run:
- The 2 unplanted defects: an account save accepts an empty email, and the sign-in form drops the username when the password is blank.
- False positives: 2 from explorers sharing one cart, and 2 wishes (no search or sort controls; order entries that do not open).

Mobile, on the iOS mobile benchmark app with two simulators:

| Run | Explorers | Reported -> after merge | Cost | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--parallel 2 --max-steps 4` | wrong results, input and validation | 7 -> 6 | $0.082 | 401s |
| `--parallel 4 --max-steps 2` | the first four, two at a time | 5 -> 4 | $0.098 | 416s |

- The run printed `runs 2 of its 4 tests at a time` and queued explorers 3 and 4.
- The mobile environment explorer (4) planned keyboard-coverage and accessible-name checks. It reported text inputs without accessible names.
- It also reported a password field drawn as a black box, which is the runner's own secure-field masking (a false positive).
- With two steps, it did not reach rotation or backgrounding.

- The terminal AI row matches the report exactly. In the `--parallel 3` run, step tokens (1,518,154) plus the merge call's tokens (4,069) equal `run.usage.modelTokens` (1,522,223). The cost is $0.1083.
- After Ctrl-C:
  - All 3 explorers show as `ended: the run was cut short`.
  - The summary reads `Steps  7 of 18 · 4 passed · 3 failed · 3 explorers`.
  - The report has 3 results marked `interrupted`, `explorers[].ended` set to `aborted`, and no `merge`.
- The app command started once in every run.
- The false positives come from the garden's single cart and single sign-in shared by every visitor: explorers changed each other's carts and display names.

New integration tests (`tests/integration/explore-parallel-workers.test.ts`) run on real child-process workers, with the scripted model built inside the config file:
- Both explorers wait at a barrier before either finishes. The test asserts two distinct worker PIDs; explorers that run one after another fail it.
- An interrupt while both workers are mid-step: both results are interrupted and cleaned up, both explorers end as aborted, and nothing is merged.
- A SIGKILL in explorer 2's worker: that explorer fails with `WORKER_CRASH` and keeps the progress it had already relayed, and explorer 1's record is unaffected.

Other tests:
- In-process: the run's usage equals the steps' usage plus the merge call's usage.
- An interrupt during a pending merge call keeps every finding and reports `interrupted`. When the answer races the interrupt, the call's exact usage is counted; when the provider rejects on abort, the run's usage is the steps' alone.
- A malformed merge answer (`{"groups":"all"}`) keeps its usage on the error through the real adapter.
- An invalid grouping falls back to keeping every finding, and the call is still counted.
- Unit tests cover validating the grouping, the merge accounting, the unit source, the schema negatives, and the list reporter after an interrupt.

title: feat(skills): publish the consumer skills on ClawHub
body:
The three consumer skills (`e2e`, `create-verification-skill`, `migrate-to-e2e`) are published on [ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/), the OpenClaw skill registry, under a new `@e2e` publisher. This PR adds the frontmatter ClawHub reads to the files in this repo, so later publishes come from `main`.

- `metadata.openclaw` in each `skills/*/SKILL.md`: `requires.bins` (`node`, `npx`), `homepage`, and for `e2e` an optional `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in `envVars`. ClawHub's scanner compares what a skill declares with what it uses.
- Lists are block style. `skills-ref`, the Agent Skills validator, parses frontmatter with strictyaml and rejects `[node, npx]`. A new test in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/skill.test.ts` fails on flow collections in any consumer skill's frontmatter. The old test pinned the `e2e` frontmatter to just `name` + `description`, so it is loosened.
- `docs/coding-agents.mdx` gets an "Install in OpenClaw or Hermes Agent" accordion. Hermes Agent reads the repository as a tap (`skills/` is already the layout it expects), and it also searches ClawHub.
- `create-verification-skill` linked its example as a directory. Hermes installs a GitHub skill as `SKILL.md` plus the files it links, so the install failed as a "stale index entry". It now links all five example files, and a second test fails when any file in a consumer skill is not linked from its `SKILL.md`.
- Plugin copies regenerated with `pnpm plugins:sync`.

```yaml
metadata:
  openclaw:
    homepage: https://e2e.com
    requires:
      bins:
        - node
        - npx
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `clawhub skill publish ./skills/<name> --owner e2e`: 1.0.0 for all three, then 1.0.1 from this branch's files. ClawHub moderation marked each `CLEAN`.
- `clawhub --workdir <tmp> install @e2e/migrate-to-e2e` and `@e2e/create-verification-skill` installed the skills, and `clawhub inspect @e2e/e2e` shows `@e2e/e2e` public at 1.0.0.
- `agentskills validate skills/<name>` (skills-ref): `e2e` and `migrate-to-e2e` are valid. `create-verification-skill` fails on `disable-model-invocation` on main too.
- Hermes Agent from source: `hermes skills install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tester-army/e2e/feat/skills-clawhub/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md` installs `SKILL.md` and all five example files. On main the same skill fails to install.
- `e2e guide` on the built package still strips the longer frontmatter.

title: feat(e2e): test.fail for tests expected to fail
body: Adds `test.fail`, so known gaps can be marked inline and the run fails once a gap closes. ```ts test.fail('shows the cart badge', async ({ app }) => {}); // register test('gap on web', async ({ platform }) => { test.fail(platform === 'web', 'tap on a display: contents element'); // runtime, does not throw }); test('exports a PDF', { fail: 'PDF export is broken' }, async () => {}); // option ``` - Marked test that fails with a product failure (assertion, action, thrown error, timeout): `passed`. The attempt keeps `expectedFailure: { reason, error }`; the result gets `expectedFailure: { reason }`. - Marked test that passes: `failed` with new code `UNEXPECTED_PASS`, which names the reason. Not retried. An expected failure is not retried either. - Not covered: infrastructure, configuration, and internal errors (`ENGINE_FAILURE` included, also when one lands beside the test failure outside cleanup), interrupts, and blocked agent verdicts (`STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` and similar). A Firefox `ENGINE_FAILURE` tap stays a failure. Covering it would hide browser crashes; the right fix is for the engine to report that tap as `NOT_ACTIONABLE`. - A skip wins, also after a failure. Setup tests and serial members cannot be marked (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`); `fail` on a serial member or a `describe` is a `COLLECTION_ERROR`. - Report: additive optional fields in `report-v1.schema.json`. List, markdown, JUnit, trace page, MCP `open_session` text, and telemetry (`tests_failed_as_expected`) show expected failures. - Differs from Playwright: timeouts count as expected failures, and an unexpected pass is not retried. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, scratch file using every form (not committed), `e2e run tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts`: exit 1, and `retries: 2` on the unexpected pass ran only one attempt. ```text ✓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > register form: heading is wrong (failed as expected) 715ms → expected to fail: ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeVisible failed ✓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > option form: known gap (failed as expected) 633ms → todos page has no Archive button: LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: locator matched no … ✓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > runtime form: web only gap (failed as expected) 597ms → title differs on web: ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed ✓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > runtime condition false: normal test 63ms × |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > gap closed: passes unexpectedly 66ms → test is marked test.fail ("playground heading was missing") but passed; … ↓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-fail.e2e.ts > skip wins [not today] ``` `report.json`, trimmed: ```json {"t":"option form: known gap","status":"passed","expectedFailure":{"reason":"todos page has no Archive button"},"attempts":[{"status":"passed","ef":{"reason":"todos page has no Archive button","error":"LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND"}}]} {"t":"gap closed: passes unexpectedly","status":"failed","expectedFailure":{"reason":"playground heading was missing"},"attempts":[{"status":"failed","error":"UNEXPECTED_PASS","ef":{"reason":"playground heading was missing"}}]} ``` - Fresh-context review: fixed skip beside a failure (schema-invalid report), blocked agent verdicts, and infra errors in `secondaryErrors` being covered, plus trace-vs-video retention on an unexpected pass. Not changed: `test.fail()` called in `afterEach` applies under `e2e run`, but is refused in an MCP session's teardown.

title: feat(cli): e2e run --step holds each step until a key
body: `e2e run` had no way to stop between steps. `--headed` shows the app, but the test runs straight through. Playwright users reach for `page.pause()` or `--debug` and find nothing. `e2e run --step` runs the first step, then holds each later top-level step until a key is pressed. The keys follow `--watch`. | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | Enter | runs the held step | | `n` | runs the rest of this test, holds at the next test | | `a` | runs the rest of the run without stopping | | `h` | shows or hides every key | | `q`, Esc | stops the run like Ctrl-C (exit 130) | ```text ❯ web tests/coffee.e2e.ts 0/2 └── orders two drinks paused ✓ app.open "/" 50ms ▶ step 2 locator.click "getByRole("radio", name: "Latte")" tests/coffee.e2e.ts:7 press enter to run this step, press h to show help, press q to quit ``` ## How it works ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as worker (StepRecorder) participant S as scheduler participant G as StepGate (CLI) W->>W: AttemptHolds stops the test clock W->>S: step-hold S->>G: beforeStep(step, { signal, show }) G-->>S: resolves on Enter / n / a S->>W: step-release W->>W: clock runs again with the time it had left ``` - `RunOptions.beforeStep` (`packages/e2e/src/run/step-hold.ts`) is an internal seam. It is not public API, so there are no `.d.ts` or wire schema changes. A worker holds each top-level step over IPC (`step-hold`, `step-release`, `step-cancel`). - Held time counts toward no timeout. `AttemptHolds` stops the test clock and rearms the deadline with what was left. The scheduler pushes `maxDuration` back by the held time. - Setup tests, retries, teardown steps, and steps inside an `expect.poll` read run without stopping. - Steps held together in one `Promise.all` share one prompt and run on one Enter. A `waitForResponse` placed beside the click that triggers it (the pattern in `docs/browser.mdx`) would otherwise run alone and time out while the click waits for its key. - The prompt is drawn in the list reporter's live window under its test. Without a live window, it is one plain line. - `--step` is refused, with exit 2: - in CI; - without a TTY; - with `--watch`; - with `--workers` above 1; - with the json reporter. It forces one worker. - Docs: - `docs/debugging.mdx` gets a "Step through a test" section. - The CLI reference, the errors reference, the Playwright migration rows (`page.pause()`, `--debug`), and the skill references are updated. - Patch changeset. ## Issue Closes #1251 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Surface:** the packed `e2e` build in a scratch project. It has a one-page app and two test files. Each run was driven in tmux on LBox with `e2e run --step`. - **Coffee test, keys:** Enter runs one step and moves to the next prompt. `h` shows the full key list and `h` again hides it. `n` finishes the test and holds at step 1 of the next test. `a` runs to the end. Result: 2 passed, exit 0. - **`Promise.all` test, 7 s pause:** both steps show in one prompt. I waited 7 s before pressing Enter, longer than the 5 s `waitForURL` gets. The test passed with exit 0. ```text └── waits for the page a navigation opens paused ✓ app.open "/" 50ms ▶ step 2 browser.waitForURL "/\/menu$/" tests/together.e2e.ts:6 ▶ step 3 app.open "/menu" tests/together.e2e.ts:6 press enter to run these 2 steps, press h to show help, press q to quit ... ✓ web tests/together.e2e.ts (1 test) 8.61s ``` - **Integration tests:** `tests/integration/step-hold.test.ts` checks against real workers that: - a hold stops the test clock and the time limit; - a test that hangs after a release still times out on the time it had left; - an interrupt ends a held step as `interrupted`; - setup tests, teardown, retries, and poll reads are never held. - **Unit tests:** `tests/unit/cli-step.test.ts` checks the keys, the 150 ms guard, and the shared `Promise.all` prompt. - **Headed run on macOS:** Krzysztof ran an earlier build of the same demo with `--step --headed` on a Mac. That was before the `Promise.all` grouping change. Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved. That approval was before the `Promise.all` grouping, which a later fresh-context review asked for. --- Written by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: fix(core): fail runs when app commands exit after readiness
body:
## Why

- A run must fail when its managed app exits after readiness.
- The startup listener kept later exit status locally, so tests could pass against a dead app.

## What changed

- Interrupt active tests and skip queued tests only for dependent targets with unfinished work.
- Notify every owner of a shared command and ignore exits after owners finish, including teardown.
- Report the exit code or signal with a bounded, redacted log excerpt when available.
- Give navigation recovery advice that accounts for an existing command.

Applies to `e2e run`, including MCP `run_tests`.
Hosted `openHost` sessions and interactive MCP `open_session` sessions do not yet forward managed command exits into session cancellation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  App[Managed app exits] --> Owners[Declaring targets]
  Owners --> Pending{Unfinished work?}
  Pending -->|Yes| Stop[Interrupt active work and skip queue]
  Pending -->|No| Ignore[Ignore exit]
```

## Issue

Fixes #1532

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Ran the built CLI with real HTTP apps and Chromium using `e2e run --reporter list`.
Fourteen fresh CLI reports covered shared commands, healthy targets, startup buffering, teardown, Ctrl-C, forced worker termination, log redaction, and navigation hints.
Each report passed schema, unique-result and process-cleanup checks.
Two further CLI scenarios forced the watchdog to kill ordinary and serial workers before the app-exit grace timer, with `--max-failures 1`.
Both preserved healthy active and queued tests.

| Scenario | main `732ea8af` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App exits 1 or 0, or receives SIGTERM | Exit 0, queued work runs | Exit 3, active test interrupted, queued work skipped |
| App exits while a separate target remains healthy | App death goes unreported | Only dependent target stops. Healthy target finishes both tests |
| App exits during final disposal | Exit 0 | Exit 0 |

Built CLI output from the watchdog-first scenario:

```text
× |a| tests/repro.e2e.ts > blocked a (interrupted)
↓ |a| tests/repro.e2e.ts > a queued [target "a" command exited with code 1 after becoming ready]
✓ |b| tests/repro.e2e.ts > healthy active
✓ |b| tests/repro.e2e.ts > healthy queued
ERROR infrastructure error APP_UNREACHABLE
target "a" command exited with code 1 after becoming ready
output in .e2e/logs/a.log since target "a" command started:
  app a exits
```

The command returned 3 without `TEST_TIMEOUT` or a failure-limit event.
The scheduler returns the affected target set directly.
Twelve built-CLI scenarios matched before and after the reduction, including exit codes, skip reasons, interrupted attempts, and diagnostics.

The buffered-exit regression waits for runner-confirmed readiness, then confirms the first app is dead before letting a second app finish startup.
Four further mutations fail their regressions: dropping buffered delivery, removing serial exit-code handling, replacing the returned-unit skip reason, and iterating the live worker array.
A real Ctrl-C after a separate app failure still returns 130.
Three further built-CLI Chromium checks covered refused navigation with a log, without a log, and without a managed command.
The managed hint explains how to enable output capture.

Six paired testbed forms runs matched outcomes, step sequences, and every counter.
Every measured CLI run exited 0.
The suite interval stayed within the configured 5% threshold.
The host had background CPU load, so no speedup is claimed.

| Metric | main median | this branch median | Paired change, 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Suite attempts | 3.02 s | 3.01 s | -0.1%, -2.5% to +4.5% |

Reviewed with sol-loop: 5 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on xhigh. Sol verdict: approved

Created with GPT-6.1 Sol in T3 Code.

The refactored code preserves this behavior with clearer comments and explicit intent. - `about:blank` is still permitted as the sole exception to the http(s) allowlist, per the browser-nesting-schemes rationale. ## Verified - Ran vitest: 43/43 passed ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (not needed: pure internal logic change) - [x] Docs updated (no user-facing API change) - [x] Contract change (no public type or wire format change)

title: ci: publish the skills to ClawHub after each e2e release
body: After each release that publishes `e2e`, `release.yml` now calls a new `clawhub.yml` that publishes `skills/*` to ClawHub as `@e2e/` from the release tag. Until now that was a hand-run `clawhub skill publish` (#1538). ```mermaid flowchart LR R[release job] -->|e2e published| M[mcp-registry.yml] R -->|e2e published| C[clawhub.yml] C --> P["clawhub skill publish skills/<name> --owner e2e"] ``` - Modeled on `mcp-registry.yml`: `workflow_call` from `release.yml` with the version, plus `workflow_dispatch` to retry. A dispatch defaults to `dry-run: true`. - It checks out `e2e@`, so ClawHub gets the skills that shipped in the npm package. A skill whose files match a version already on ClawHub is skipped; a changed one gets the next patch version. - The CLI comes from a lockfile in `.github/actions/clawhub` (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`), not `npx clawhub@x`, because it runs with the token. The action is checked out from the default branch, since a release tag can predate it. - An empty `CLAWHUB_TOKEN` fails the job. Without the check, `clawhub login --token ""` falls through to the device login and prints its code in the public log. - One skill that fails doesn't stop the others; the job fails at the end and lists them. - It runs on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404` like the other jobs. ClawHub's reusable `skill-publish.yml` was the alternative, but it pins `ubuntu-latest` and its own actions by tag. - `CLAWHUB_TOKEN` is a repository secret now. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, without GitHub Actions - Ran the action's install script, then the Publish step's script under `bash -e -o pipefail` with `DRY_RUN=true` against `main`'s skills: all three report `already published`, exit 0. - `clawhub login --token` in a fresh `HOME`, then a real publish of unchanged `migrate-to-e2e`: `OK. migrate-to-e2e@1.0.1 is already published`, exit 0, so a release that doesn't touch the skills publishes nothing. - `actionlint` is clean apart from the Blacksmith runner label it doesn't know. - Not run on Actions: `workflow_dispatch` needs the workflow on `main`. After merge, a dispatch with `version: 0.22.0` and `dry-run: true` checks it end to end. Don't dispatch a real publish for 0.22.0: that tag predates #1538 and would publish skills without its changes. The first real publish is the next e2e release.

title: fix(web): take concurrent observations in turn
body: - Two screen reads at once on one page (e.g. two `expect(screen).toHaveScreenshot(...)` under `Promise.allSettled`) failed one of them with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: node became stale`. - Root cause: each web `observe` called `refs.beginCapture()`, so a second observation started while the first was in flight made the first throw `NODE_STALE: observation capture was superseded` at publish (`packages/web/src/refs.ts`). - Fix: `AttemptSession.observeInTurn` queues observations per attempt. Each runs after the one before it, publishes its ref generation in call order, and spends its wait from its own deadline. Supersession on session invalidation (`refs.clear()`) is unchanged. - Removed the `fail` mark on testbed `screenshot.e2e.ts` "mask option > should mask in parallel". - Tests: new integration test `concurrent-observe.test.ts` (fails on main with `observation capture was superseded`), and the unit test that asserted the old supersede now asserts in-order publishing. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: built CLI on the testbed (`cd apps/testbed && node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run ...`). | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× should mask in parallel` -> `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: node became stale` | `✓` 3 of 3 runs | ```text # main, mark removed × |web| tests/screenshot.e2e.ts > page screenshot > mask option > should mask in parallel 796ms → node became stale # this branch run --tag playwright: Tests 503 passed | 6 skipped (509) pnpm test (testbed): Tests 579 passed | 7 skipped (586) @e2e-dev/web: Tests 641 passed | 1 skipped (642) ```

title: docs(migrate): match the Playwright mapping to what e2e does
body:
## What and why

`docs/migrate/playwright.mdx` claimed parity in rows that the ported Playwright tests in `apps/testbed/tests` (#1505) disprove or leave out. Each row below now matches main, checked against the source and the tests' `fail`/`skip` marks and "Not ported" headers.

- Runner and CLI rows (`workers`, `retries`, `trace`, `video`, hooks, `test.skip`, `test.setTimeout`, `test.use`, CLI flags, `-u`) go from `same` to `renamed`/`missing` and name their limits.
- `test.fail()` is now `same`. The row notes that members of a serial group and setup tests can't be marked (keeps main's #1539 row).
- `inputValue()` on an element that isn't an input reads `""`, where Playwright throws (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:562`).
- `uncheck()` on a checked radio, `role=radio` included, is `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts:59`).
- The 1 s hold of a negated matcher is capped by its timeout.
- `?` in a `browser.route` glob matches one character, where Playwright reads it literally.
- `route.fulfill` bodies are strings only, and each header takes one value, so one `set-cookie`. A `route.continue` header can't be deleted (`packages/web/src/route-options.ts`).
- `{ timeout: 0 }`: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on `waitForResponse`, `waitForDownload`, and `toHaveScreenshot`. Any other call times out at once.

- `browser.evaluate` and locator reads run in the page's main world.

title: fix(web): tap position from inside the border, port the remaining click tests
body:
Ports the 11 tests from Playwright v1.64.1 `tests/page/page-click.spec.ts` that the `click.e2e.ts` header listed as "could be ported with the current API; not done yet". Fixes the one gap they exposed.

- All 11 pass, with no marks: waitFor visible when already visible, px and em border with offset, LABEL with pointer-events:none, retry when element detaches after animation, retry when animating from outside the viewport, microtasks in order, iframe with border 2, button overlaid by a permission popup, PointerEvent.pressure on pointerdown and pointermove.
- Fix: `tap({ position })` now measures from inside the node's border, as Playwright's `click({ position })` does. Before, a bordered button shifted the tap by its border width (`offsetX` 12 with an 8px border, -4 with a 24px border, instead of 20).
- Engine contract: new optional `SemanticNode.origin`, the point an offset into the node is measured from when it is not `rect`'s corner (`packages/e2e/src/engine/contract.ts`). `performWithin` uses `origin ?? rect` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts`). Additive: an older engine falls back to `rect`, an older runner ignores the field. Mobile never sets it.
- Web engine sets `origin` from the computed border widths (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`). Inside a frame, `rect` is clipped but `origin` is only shifted, and a clip that moves the corner keeps the unclipped corner as `origin` (`placeBoxInFrame` in `packages/web/src/observation.ts`), so a position tap inside a frame lands where it would at the top level.
- The model never sees `origin`: the observation projection does not copy it, and redaction keeps it as-is.

fix(web): elements inside a hidden iframe read as hidden
body: - The web engine now reads each `frameLocator` hop's iframe element in the document around it, in `frameOf` (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`), using the `e2e-shown` engine that is already registered. If the iframe is hidden, every node inside it is hidden too, and so is every frame nested under it. This is how Playwright's `_queryFrames` carries `frameVisible`. - The read happens in the parent document, so cross-origin frames work. It costs one `count` per hop, skipped once an outer frame is already hidden. - In a hidden frame, `isVisible()`, `toBeVisible`/`toBeHidden`, `waitFor` and actionability waits all see `states.hidden: true`. Observation already left hidden iframes out (`read-semantics.ts`), so it agrees. - A `{ visible: true }` or role query inside a hidden frame matches nothing, under an index or scope too, as the engine contract requires ("a role query never matches a node whose `states.hidden` is true"). This differs from Playwright: its `getByRole` and `visible=true` filter are per document and still match there. - Removed 3 `fail` marks in `apps/testbed/tests/locator-frame.e2e.ts`: - should treat elements inside hidden iframe as hidden - should treat elements inside hidden cross-origin iframe as hidden - should wait for hidden iframe to become visible ```ts await expect(browser.frameLocator('[name=hidden]').locator('button')).toBeHidden(); expect(await browser.frameLocator('iframe').locator('div').isVisible()).toBe(false); // cross-origin ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Testbed, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --tag playwright`, on another port because a parallel checkout held 4271: 503 passed, 6 skipped. On main the 3 tests carried `fail` marks and failed. - Full testbed suite: 579 passed, 7 skipped. - Web benchmark: 91/91. - New integration test `packages/web/tests/integration/hidden-frames.test.ts` covers: - a hidden frame - a frame under a hidden ancestor - a nested chain - an iframe with `visibility: visible` under a hidden ancestor - visible and role queries - a frame that shows again - Known flake, not from this PR: `should wait for frame to go` failed 2 of 15 runs on main as well (a `boundingBox` wait race when the frame is removed mid-locate).

title: fix(web): classify aborted navigations and capture screenshots across navigations
body:
Part of the Playwright parity follow-ups. The web engine reported two failures caused by the test or the page as `ENGINE_FAILURE` (infrastructure, exit 3), which `test.fail` rightly refuses to absorb.

- **Route-aborted navigation.** A test route that aborts the attempt page's document request is noted (`PlaywrightSurface.noteRouteAbort`), and the `goto` it fails throws `ACTION_FAILED` (`navigation failed: a route aborted the request for <url>`), the code `browser.goto` already documents for a failed navigation, instead of `net::ERR_FAILED` as `ENGINE_FAILURE`. Subresource, subframe, and popup aborts never count.
- **Latched handler error during a failing step.** `guard` now rethrows an error a route or dialog handler latched while the operation ran. Before, the step failed with the consequence (`net::ERR_FAILED`), and failure-evidence capture then consumed the latched real cause (such as `route.fulfill has an invalid header name`), so it never reached the report. This is how the multiple `set-cookie` tests hid their real cause before #1548.
- **Screenshot while navigating.** `app.screenshot()` failed with "Execution context was destroyed" because Playwright resolves the secure-field `mask` locators in one document and throws when navigation replaces it (20/30 captures failed with masks, 0 without, on the redirect loop). The capture now watches the page's own `framenavigated` / `framedetached` events: a capture that fails while a frame replaced its document is taken of the replacing document, masked by the same rule. Only that event triggers it, with no message matching and no sleep, bounded by the step's own deadline; a page that replaces its document during every capture until then fails with `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` -> `ACTION_FAILED`. A failure with no replacement is thrown as before. I found no single-shot alternative: Playwright resolves masks and takes the frame in separate calls, so a document replaced between them has to be captured again.
- A closed page, context, or browser stays `ENGINE_FAILURE`.

Testbed marks:

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| screenshot: should work while navigating | `skip` | passes, mark removed |

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, `e2e run --tag playwright --grep "while navigating|multiple set-cookie|aborting main resource"` with the skips removed:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE: screenshot failed: page.screenshot: Execution context was destroyed` | passes (10 captures during the redirect loop) |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE: navigation failed: page.goto: net::ERR_FAILED` (route handler refused its header) | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: route.fulfill header "Set-Cookie" must not contain a control character` (before #1548 made that header valid) |

- Rebased on main with #1548 and #1551: `e2e run --tag playwright` 509 passed, 1 skipped. Full testbed suite: 585 passed, 2 skipped.
- New tests in `packages/web` (`routes.test.ts`, `screenshot-navigation.test.ts`, `surface-guard.test.ts`) fail against the old engine code (verified by reverting `src/`). `screenshot-navigation.test.ts` decodes each PNG and checks the password field is covered by the opaque mask.
- Firefox `tap({ position })` on a `display: contents` element (from the plan): on main it already fails as `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, not `ENGINE_FAILURE`, so no change here.

title: fix(web): screenshot past a frame whose navigation is held
body: In Chromium, a screenshot taken while an iframe's first request is held now captures, as Playwright's does. - Chromium gives an iframe's initial empty document no script context until script in the parent touches it. Until then Playwright waits for the navigation to commit, so any evaluate in that frame hangs. - The secure-field sweep (`secureFieldMasks`) probed and masked every frame, so `count()` and the masked `page.screenshot` hung until the capture deadline. The engine returned no pixels and `toHaveScreenshot` failed with "the engine returned no screenshot". - New `hasReadableDocument` (`packages/web/src/frame-document.ts`): a frame with an empty URL (no commit yet) is read from its parent through `contentDocument`, which gives it a context. A parent that cannot read it (sandboxed) means no script could have filled it, so it shows nothing and is left out. If the check itself fails, the frame stays in, so it fails closed. - Used by the observation pixels, the artifact screenshot, and the observation tree walk. Before, the tree walk spent 3s on the frame and reported the tree truncated. - Removes the `skip` from "mask option > should work when subframe has stalled navigation" in `apps/testbed/tests/screenshot.e2e.ts`. The `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT` the test also hit came from the route handler still holding its request after the failed assertion. Settle waits for running route handlers by design (documented in `docs/reference/web.mdx`, `route`), so this PR leaves that alone. Once the screenshot works, the test releases the route and nothing hangs. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, `e2e run tests/screenshot.e2e.ts --grep "stalled navigation"` with the skip removed: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× should work when subframe has stalled navigation 44.70s`, `ASSERTION_FAILED: the engine returned no screenshot`, plus `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT: settling the attempt timed out` | `✓ should work when subframe has stalled navigation 753ms` | - `e2e run --tag playwright`: 504 passed, 5 skipped (6 skipped before). - New integration test `packages/web/tests/integration/stalled-frame.test.ts` covers a held frame, a secure field the parent writes into the held frame's initial document (still masked), and a sandboxed held frame. With the URL check reverted, the held and sandboxed cases fail with a capture timeout. - Firefox never hung. WebKit hangs on a plain screenshot with no masks, a separate gap this PR does not touch.

title: feat(e2e)!: inputValue and isChecked throw on the wrong element, uncheck clicks ARIA radios
body:
Follows the Playwright gaps plan: two items, both decided "match Playwright".

- `inputValue()` on a node with no value (a heading, a button) throws `ACTION_FAILED` with Playwright's message, instead of `""`. Same rule `toHaveValue` already uses (`isValueControl` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/roles.ts`): a value role with no value reported still reads `""`, since a device engine omits an empty value.
- `isChecked()` on a node with no checked state throws `ACTION_FAILED` ("Not a checkbox or radio button"), instead of `false`. Checkable means a reported state or one of Playwright's `kAriaCheckedRoles` (`checkbox`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `option`, `radio`, `switch`, `menuitemradio`, `treeitem`), so an ARIA switch without `aria-checked` still reads `false`.
- `uncheck()` on an ARIA `role=radio` clicks it, like Playwright. Only a native `<input type=radio>` refuses, with the same message as before. An ARIA radio whose click leaves it checked fails at the deadline with a hint about the radio group.
- `ACTION_FAILED` because that is what `check()` on a wrong element already gives.
- Breaking, so the changeset is `minor` with `**Breaking:**`. Docs updated: `reference/screen.mdx`, `reference/errors.mdx`, `skills/e2e` reads paragraph, and in `migrate/playwright.mdx` (on top of #1545) the `check()`/`uncheck()`, `inputValue()`, `isChecked()` rows and the `toBeChecked` note.

```ts
await screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).inputValue(); // ACTION_FAILED: Node is not an <input>, <textarea> or <select> element
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Save').isChecked();          // ACTION_FAILED: Not a checkbox or radio button
```

Marks removed (4 `fail`): `check.e2e.ts` "should uncheck radio by aria role", "should uncheck the box by aria role"; `locator-convenience.e2e.ts` "inputValue should work", "isChecked should work".

Callers checked: no agent, MCP, or engine code calls these reads; benchmarks read `textbox`/`switch`/`checkbox` nodes; two integration/unit tests that pinned `""`/`false` on a heading/listitem now assert the throw.

Left as is, on purpose:
- `toBeChecked` stays lenient (`.not.toBeChecked()` passes on a button). Not in scope; the migrate guide says so.
- On a `<label>`, both reads now throw where Playwright reads the labeled control (before: a wrong `false`/`""`). Listed as `missing` in the migrate guide.
- A custom-drawn iOS field reported as `other` with no value throws on `inputValue()`, as `toHaveValue` already does there.

title: fix(web): browser.evaluate survives clobbered page globals
body:
## Summary

`browser.evaluate` broke when the evaluated code deleted or replaced a page global. Its result went through Playwright's in-page serializer, which calls the page's `Map` and `Array.isArray`. When those were clobbered it returned `undefined`, and e2e crashed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ok')`.

- The page-side boundary now encodes the result as JSON text and returns it through `evaluateHandle`. Playwright hands back a primitive handle's value without running anything in the page.
- The encoder (`pageValueEncoder`) is built before user code runs and takes its intrinsics from literals (`({}).constructor`, `[].constructor`), so it never reads `Array`, `Object`, or `JSON` from the page. The keepNames `__name` helper takes `defineProperty` the same way.
- Results are strict JSON: `null`, booleans, finite numbers, strings, arrays, and plain objects, with the same `INVALID_ARGUMENT` reasons `validateJsonValue` gives. **Behavior change:** a class instance (a `DOMRect`, an element, an `Event`) used to arrive as a partial object through Playwright's serializer, and now fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Return `rect.toJSON()` or the fields you need. The docs already promised a `JsonValue` return. One ported test resolved with an iframe's `load` Event and now resolves with nothing.
- User code still runs in the main world and sees page globals of any name.

### Locators on a page that replaced `Map`: classified, not fixed

Call path: `locator.count()` → `engine.resolveNow` → `surface.locate` → `locator.evaluateAll(takeReadsFunction)` → Playwright `frame.evalOnSelectorAll` → `queryArrayInMainWorld` → main-world `InjectedScript`, whose constructor calls `new Map()`.

Moving locates to the utility world is a redesign, not a fix, for three reasons:
- Every e2e selector engine is registered with `contentScript: false`, which forces even Playwright's own `count()` into the main world.
- `evaluateAll` always resolves in the main world, and Playwright's protocol has no world option.
- The engines must stay in the main world: closed-shadow reach reads a registry that the main-world `attachShadow` hook writes, which is invisible from an isolated world. The `e2e-read` results live as main-world expandos on the matched elements.

Instead, a failure from a page that broke its main world is now classified as `EVALUATE_FAILED` (test category) instead of `ENGINE_FAILURE`. `pageScriptFailure` proves the cause from both worlds without matching any error text: Playwright's utility world reads the frame (`:root` count) both before and after a main-world query that runs no e2e code fails. A crashed or closed page fails one of the utility-world reads, and a bug in e2e's own code passes the main-world query, so both stay unclassified (unit-tested in `tests/unit/errors.test.ts`). This covers locate and a later `browser.evaluate` (Playwright's main-world argument parser also calls `new Map()`).

Testbed marks:
- `screenshot.e2e.ts` "should work with Array deleted": `fail` mark removed, and the test passes.
- `locator-misc-2.e2e.ts` "locator.count should work with deleted Map in main world": stays `fail`, with an accurate reason. It is now absorbed, with error code `EVALUATE_FAILED`.

`docs/reference/errors.mdx` widens the `EVALUATE_FAILED` row.

## Verified

Built packages, real CLI on the testbed:

```text
$ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --tag playwright --grep "deleted Map|Array deleted"
   ✓ locator misc 2 > locator.count should work with deleted Map in main world (failed as expected)
   ✓ page screenshot > should work with Array deleted
   report.json: "code":"EVALUATE_FAILED","message":"locate failed: the page deleted or replaced a JavaScript built-in that in-page automation code needs: locator.evaluateAll: TypeError: Map is not a constructor ..."

$ node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --tag playwright
 Test Files  32 passed (32)
      Tests  503 passed | 6 skipped (509)

$ pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test
 Test Files  47 passed (47)
      Tests  579 passed | 7 skipped (586)
```

- Before the fix, both target tests failed at `browser.evaluate` with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ok')`.
- `pnpm test` (root) and `pnpm check` both pass.
- New integration tests in `packages/web/tests/integration/evaluate.test.ts` run in real Chromium. They cover:
  - globals clobbered in the same call;
  - a page that deleted `Array`, `JSON`, and `Object.prototype.__proto__` before the call;
  - a later evaluate and a `surface.locate` after `Map` is replaced (`EVALUATE_FAILED`, test category);
  - keepNames output after deleting `Object`;
  - strict JSON (DOMRect, nodes, and DOMException rejected; shared objects, escapes, and lone surrogates kept).

title: feat(e2e): timeout 0 means no step deadline; settle by-design Playwright gaps
body: Two parts of the Playwright gaps plan, both decided: **1. `timeout: 0` means no deadline of its own**, as in Playwright. The test timeout (`cleanupTimeout` in `afterEach`) still bounds it, so a run cannot hang. - `stepTimeout(timeout, api)` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts` is the one place a call's own `timeout` is checked: finite and `>= 0`, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `0` becomes an infinite budget that `Deadline.min` caps at the phase deadline. `withTimeout` sets no timer for it. - `LocatorEngine.deadline()` runs every user timeout through it: locator actions, `waitFor`, `scrollUntilVisible`, locator matchers, `toHaveScreenshot`. Locator actions used to accept negative values and time out at once. Now they refuse them. - `LocatorEngine.operation()` (behind `context.operation`) keeps plain numeric semantics. Engines pass `deadline.remaining()` to it, as `docs/reference/engine.mdx` recommends, so `0` there still means expired. - Fixture calls (`fixture-recording.ts`) and `@e2e-dev/web` (`goto`/`reload`/`back`/`forward`, `waitForResponse`, `waitForDownload(s)`, `waitForURL`, browser matchers) convert at the boundary. `stepTimeout` is exported from `e2e/engine` so contributed engines can do the same. - `expect.poll({ timeout: 0 })` polls until the attempt deadline. Outside a test nothing bounds it, so it is `INVALID_CONFIG`. - Agent calls (`act`/`check`) still refuse `0`. Playwright has nothing like them. **2. By-design gaps settled.** Deleted three ported tests that pinned Playwright behavior e2e keeps on purpose. Each is now listed in its file's "Not ported" header and stated in `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx`: - `route.e2e.ts` "should not support ? in glob pattern": `?` matches one character - `locator-convenience.e2e.ts` "textContent should work": rendered text, whitespace normalized - `select-option.e2e.ts` "should select single option": a bare string selects by label only Marks: removed the `skip` on `wait-for-response.e2e.ts` "should work with no timeout" and 3 `fail`s (with their tests). Three `click.e2e.ts` waits are back to Playwright's original `timeout: 0` (they used `10_000`). `filechooser.e2e.ts` "should work with no timeout" stays out because it still needs `page.waitForEvent`. The testbed README now says `fail` marks a gap to close, and by-design differences go in the header. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed `e2e run --tag playwright`: 506 passed, 1 skipped after rebasing on main (this PR removes one skip and three `fail`s) - full `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`, plus a scratch spec on main and on this branch: ```ts test('waitForResponse with timeout 0', ...) // fetch fires after 50 ms test('tap with timeout 0 waits for the button', ...) // button shown after 300 ms test('tap with timeout 0 is cut at the test deadline', { timeout: 3000 }, ...) test('negative timeout', ...) // tap({ timeout: -1 }) ``` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `× waitForResponse ... → browser.waitForResponse timeout must be positive and finite` | `✓ waitForResponse with timeout 0 183ms` | | `× tap ... waits for the button → operation timed out: locator("button")` (93 ms) | `✓ tap with timeout 0 waits for the button 418ms` | | `× tap ... cut at the test deadline → operation timed out: locator("#missing")` (94 ms) | `× ... (timed-out) 3.05s → test timed out after 3000 ms in phase body` | | `× negative timeout → no app page is open` (not refused) | `× negative timeout → the step timeout must be a finite number of milliseconds, 0 or more; got -1` |

title: test(web): read crosscheck pages with the clock paused
body: The web crosscheck sometimes failed on `benchmark: stale-dom` with `getByRole button "Decoy" / "Tap me": ours match, theirs no match` (seen on #1552, gone on rerun). It was a race in the harness, not a regression in the engine. - `stale-dom` remounts every row on a 1s `setInterval`. The crosscheck tags the engine's elements, reads Chrome's AX tree, and then asks Playwright, all on the live page. When a tick landed between those reads, Playwright was asked about tagged buttons that had already been detached. - Reproduced at random tick phase under 8x CPU throttle: 8/40 runs on main, the same at `HEAD~4` (before #1546-#1551). None of those merges caused it. - Fix: `openCheckPage` (`packages/web/tests/crosscheck/crosscheck.ts`) installs Playwright's clock paused before any document loads. Timers never fire, so the engine and both oracles read the same document. React and Next.js still hydrate (their scheduler uses `MessageChannel`), and `expected.txt` is unchanged. - No retries or margins. Pausing the clock mid-page can't target "now" (`pauseAt` throws on a past time), and CDP virtual time stalled Playwright calls, so the clock is paused from the start. - Coverage cost: the reviewer diffed all 42 scenarios. Only `overlay-trap` changed, losing a close button that a 500ms timeout reveals and that was only checked when the timeout beat `networkidle`. - New fixture `list rebuilt every millisecond` guards the race. AGENTS.md notes that content revealed by a timer is never read. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `stale-dom` through `crossCheck` 40 times, random phase, 8x CPU throttle: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | 8/40 runs report the two `getByRole` misses | 0/40, same 9 nodes compared | - New fixture with the clock install removed: fails with `chrome unknown` / `missing` on the rebuilt buttons. With it: passes. - Full crosscheck against a local benchmark (`CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL`): 19/19 passed, `expected.txt` untouched.

title: Mobile root scroll gestures can start on the software keyboard
body:
## Outcome

Withdrawn as unsupported on the current SDK. The original command-stream reproduction modeled `interactions.scroll` as an unbounded gesture and omitted agent-device's existing keyboard avoidance.

With pristine agent-device **0.21.36** and upstream main **1bbda5a84987257184457f1374729ed31ece594e**, a [public UIKit/Android fixture](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/4babb9ae37d64edcd0d6f457ad799a2a1b0c8aaa/reproductions/root-scroll-native) passes all six native slow/normal/fast cases: three on iOS 27.0 and three on Android 37.1 with Gboard. Each reaches terminal Row 39, preserves Notes and leaves composer touches at zero.

The [SDK's matching-release policy](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/v0.21.36/packages/contracts/src/scroll-gesture.ts#L423-L522) measures live geometry, clips above the keyboard with accessory clearance, and handles occlusion. The adapter point-swipe override proposed in #1557 was unnecessary and introduced its own Android fast-swipe composer regression. That PR is withdrawn, with [public recordings](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/3952f8e1eaa107b42bebf4b792dcec52ca124fd8/reproductions/root-scroll-native/evidence) and a response to every review point in its conversation. A generic SDK main bug was not reproduced.

Closing as not planned because no missing adapter fix is established.

title: Mobile: cancelled recording-stop wait can repeat finalization during cleanup
body:
### What happened

When a caller stops a screen recording and cancels its wait before the device answers, the SDK command continues but the adapter loses its success continuation. The recording stays marked active. Another caller or `endAttempt` then sends another stop for the same recording.

Expected: share one finalization command, clear the recording when it actually stops, and preserve each caller's cancellation result. A genuinely failed SDK stop should remain retryable during cleanup.

### Reproduction

[Public regression and fix](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/bbb8852cac2f5606cb4252eeab0b567ee165ef21/packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts#L2652). This scripts only the SDK boundary; it needs no simulator, app, model, or credentials.

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse --branch codex/mobile-share-recording-stop https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e.git recording-stop-repro
cd recording-stop-repro
git sparse-checkout set packages scripts docs skills plugins
pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile... install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm --filter e2e run build
git fetch --depth 1 origin e99a6fa83dd35af4b13cde7c2b31475cadb8787f
git restore --source=e99a6fa83dd35af4b13cde7c2b31475cadb8787f -- packages/mobile/src/surface.ts
pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile exec vitest run tests/unit/engine.test.ts --maxWorkers 1 -t 'pending recording stop'
```

On the pinned main source the assertion receives four recording calls: one start and three stops, instead of one start and one stop. Restore the fixed source with `git restore --source=HEAD -- packages/mobile/src/surface.ts` and repeat the last command; it passes.

A separate built-CLI check, with the actual compiled mobile adapter and a simulated SDK, uses a 500 ms cleanup budget and a 750 ms stop response. Main sends two stops and also times out ending the attempt. The fixed adapter sends one stop and completes attempt cleanup. Both correctly keep the original video-stop wait timeout and exit 3. This is lifecycle evidence, not native recording or media validation.

### Versions

Reproduced at main `e99a6fa83dd35af4b13cde7c2b31475cadb8787f`, Node 24.22.0, `e2e` 0.22.0, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.5, `agent-device` 0.21.36. The deterministic case does not call a device daemon.

### Engine

`@e2e-dev/mobile`

title: fix(mobile): share pending screen recording stops with cleanup
body:
- Keep one screen-recording stop in flight across cancelled callers and attempt cleanup. A confirmed completion clears the recording; an actual SDK failure permits a later retry.
- Preserve cancellation before dispatch, document cleanup behavior, and add the patch changeset.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Stop requested] --> B[Shared device stop]
  A --> C[Caller cancels its wait]
  C --> D[Attempt cleanup]
  D --> B
  B --> E[Clear recording on success]
```

## Issue

Fixes #1558.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, the built CLI and compiled mobile engine over a simulated SDK, with real subprocess workers. A 750 ms finalization response exceeds the caller's 500 ms cleanup budget.

| Case | main `e99a6fa` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK stop commands in the built CLI | 2 | 1 |
| Ending the attempt | `CLEANUP_TIMEOUT` | completes |
| Original stop-wait timeout and exit 3 | retained | retained |
| Deterministic cancelled waiter + concurrent caller + cleanup | 3 SDK stops, fails | 1 SDK stop, passes |

```text
main:        stopping the video timed out; ending the attempt timed out
this branch: stopping the video timed out
```

- Cancellation and actual-stop-failure retry cases pass, including cleanup entering between SDK rejection and adapter state updates. Mobile build/typecheck, repository lint, and all 494 mobile unit tests pass. The public reproduction commands are in #1558.
- The full local workspace gate has not completed. Dead-code checking on the partial workspace install reports identical findings on main and this branch.
- Simulator benchmarks, native daemon behavior, and actual media were not exercised. The simulated SDK establishes adapter lifecycle behavior.
