title: Mobile screen swipes bypass the transition budget after alert dismissal
body:
### What happened

A deterministic screen swipe bypasses the mobile engine's transition budget. Immediately after `device.alert('accept')`, the engine records the dismissal as an action but sends `interactions.scroll` without waiting for that action's remaining transition budget. A readable accessibility tree does not establish that the overlay has finished dismissing.

### Public reproduction

[Runnable controlled reproduction](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/afb089e/packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/root-transition), based on upstream `e99a6fa83dd35af4b13cde7c2b31475cadb8787f`. Its README contains install, build, and CLI commands. It uses the built CLI and mobile adapter over a scripted agent-device client. No simulator, native app, credentials, or model is required.

The client exposes readable content throughout and ignores screen scrolls during its modeled 1000 ms alert-dismissal transition. The test is:

```ts
await app.open();
await device.alert('accept');
await screen.swipe({ direction: 'down' });
await expect(screen.getByText('Scrolled after alert')).toBeVisible();
```

On unmodified main, the gesture is sent during dismissal and the test fails. Waiting the remaining budget before the root gesture makes it pass. This proves adapter timing, not that every native overlay behaves this way.

### Expected

A deterministic screen swipe should honor the remaining transition budget, including after fixture actions and launch. Cancelling that wait should send no gesture. Unchanged-control shortcuts and agent-origin settling can remain as they are.

Related #1296/#1297 concern controls and keyboard transitions. This report concerns the root-swipe branch, which has no target control and bypasses `waitForTransition` entirely.

### Versions

Upstream `e99a6fa`, mobile package 0.12.5 with agent-device 0.21.36, Node 24.22.0. Controlled CLI reproduction only; no fresh native benchmark run.

title: Mobile: explicit wait for the remaining transition budget after overlay dismissal
body:
## Problem

After dismissing an overlay, a control beneath it can have the same accessibility identity, bounds, and keyboard state as before the dismissal while the overlay is still fading. The mobile adapter deliberately acts immediately on that unchanged control, so raising `transition` does not add a synchronization point for this case.

I am requesting an opt-in API, preserving that default fast path. This is separate from the keyboard-state refresh in #1296/#1297 and from root-screen scroll timing.

## Proposed API

```ts
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Close overlay').tap();
await device.waitForTransition();
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Underlying action').tap();
```

`device.waitForTransition(): Promise<void>` would wait only for the remainder of the configured `mobile({ transition })` budget since the last completed screen-changing action. It would send no input, would not start a new transition budget, and would obey the fixture action timeout/cancellation. If the budget has elapsed, it would return immediately. The wait would appear as a fixture step in the report.

This is a bounded timing choice, not a guarantee that a native animation has finished.

## Tradeoffs

- Tests could opt in at a known dismissal without delaying every capture or changing unchanged-control behavior elsewhere.
- The existing transition duration supplies the budget; repeated calls would not add another full delay.
- Test authors must identify the affected boundary and choose a suitable duration. This remains time-based synchronization rather than native animation/readiness detection.

## Native reproduction on main

Verified 2026-11-10 with a real UIKit fixture and unmodified main `d8b694ffa48b04c94d70a11cc280267f1ea9a100`, after merged #1564. Framework source builds identify as `e2e` 0.23.0 / `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.6, with `agent-device` 0.21.36, on iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27.0.

[Public native app, commands, reports and all recordings](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/b2126a9bba45a91e016284b622cf297dc60ac033/reproductions/overlay-transition-native-1563/README.md). The 750 ms custom composite fade reproduces with transition budgets of 1,000 ms and 2,000 ms. [Trace step 4](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/b2126a9bba45a91e016284b622cf297dc60ac033/reproductions/overlay-transition-native-1563/evidence/main-1000/results/overlay-uikit-fade-750ms-96e13e53b3b43ced/trace.md#steps) reports a successful tap, but the native counters show underlying taps 0 / overlay touches 1. Native events place that touch before animation completion. The stock UIKit page-sheet control passes.

This is a constructed native reproduction with a touch-owning parent retained while its children fade, not a claim that all native modals behave this way. The public API proposal still needs maintainer agreement.

## Earlier scripted policy model

[Public fixture and commands](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/95add100591381b3759cb22d9e6d4fa506e686b6/packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/overlay-transition).

The real built CLI and mobile adapter run against a scripted SDK client. Both controls remain unchanged; the client models a 750 ms overlay dismissal with a 1,000 ms transition budget. The normal run fails (1/1, 1.65 s) because the underlying input is intercepted. A comparison run with an explicit wait passes (1/1, 2.13 s). The comparison sleep illustrates the requested synchronization point; it is not an implementation of this API or a recommendation to add fixed sleeps to tests.

No simulator, native app, model, or credentials are used. This proves the adapter's current policy and the modeled interaction, not that a current native producer repeats this condition.

Per [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests), I am seeking maintainer agreement before implementing the public API or opening a feature PR.

title: fix(mobile): wait for transitions before screen swipes
body:
- Screen swipes in tests now honor the transition budget after the preceding action, including native alert dismissal.
- Share `waitOutTransition(operation, budget)` with control transitions. Unchanged-control shortcuts and agent settling remain. A budget too short for the transition fails unsent, including an early timer wake.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Last action returns] --> B[Wait within transition and action budgets]
  B --> C{Cancelled or budget too short?}
  C -->|Yes| D[No input]
  C -->|No| E[Send screen swipe]
```

## Issue

Fixes #1562.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes.

[Public controlled CLI reproduction](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/afb089e/packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/root-transition): main `1bbda5a` fails, this branch `f52bdc7` passes. All 505 mobile tests and `pnpm check` pass. The agent-origin regression fails if its wait is made unconditional; integer/fractional early-wake, cancellation, and sufficient-budget cases pass.

Native pacing cost is measurable. [Fixture source/build](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/4babb9ae37d64edcd0d6f457ad799a2a1b0c8aaa/reproductions/root-scroll-native) and [timing suite, reports, and clips](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/39fce0d/reproductions/root-swipe-timing-1564) are public. These are median test-body seconds from the official `bench:ab` harness on the same UIKit 40-row list binary, iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27.0 Simulator, agent-device 0.21.36. Each budget has three measured pairs and one excluded warmup, one worker, zero retries. Both builds pass both cases with matching reported behavior/counters.

| Transition | Native case | Main `1bbda5a` | PR `f52bdc7` | Action API time, main → PR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 500 ms | Four consecutive swipes | 4.48 s | 6.35 s | 2.21 → 4.11 s |
| 500 ms | `scrollUntilVisible`, row 25 | 5.44 s | 6.53 s | 3.63 → 4.60 s |
| 1500 ms | Four consecutive swipes | 4.44 s | 10.32 s | 2.21 → 8.11 s |
| 1500 ms | `scrollUntilVisible`, row 25 | 5.69 s | 10.46 s | 3.70 → 8.56 s |

API time sums the four `screen.swipe` steps or the one `scrollUntilVisible` step. Test bodies also include app launch and assertions. Identical temporary fixture files were untracked in both prepared checkouts; production files matched the listed commits.

Waiting between consecutive test swipes is intentional: a swipe can itself start a scroll or pager animation, and a screen-root gesture has no target binding whose unchanged position proves readiness. Captures and assertions consume the budget before the next swipe. The configured budget is a heuristic, not proof that a native animation has completed.

These fixture runs measure pacing cost, not a failure-rate improvement or the entire Expo benchmark suite. One measured pair per budget is linked below. GitHub disallows uploading attachments to this upstream repository with this account's read access, so the clips are published on the public evidence branch.

| Transition | Main clip | PR clip |

title: test: the video first-frame and shared-app hung-start tests flake under load
body:
### What happened

Two tests on `main` fail under load even though the recorder and process pool follow their contracts.

- `packages/web/tests/unit/video.test.ts`, "waits for a segment's first frame…": `expected 110 to be greater than or equal to 140`. The fake page starts its 150 ms frame timer inside `video.arm()`, but the test starts measuring after `arm()` returns. A pause between those events reduces the measured wait.
- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/shared-app-processes.test.ts`, "aborts a hung start…": four `expect.poll(serving)` calls use the 1 s default. A slow process start or exit can exceed that limit.

The hung-start test also leaves an unfinished start behind when a poll fails. Its teardown deletes the project without cancelling and waiting for that start. A later `APP_UNREACHABLE` with exit code 1 may come from the deleted script; the child's output was discarded, so a port collision has not been ruled out.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/tree/a9c3de9f0ca5eca2e112ff596271c5fabad0f0e7

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install dependencies and build with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`.
2. In the video test's fake `screencast.start`, add a 40 ms busy wait after scheduling the first frame:
   ```ts
   const pausedUntil = performance.now() + 40;
   while (performance.now() < pausedUntil) {}
   ```
   Run `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/unit/video.test.ts`. The test fails with a measured wait of about 110 ms.
3. In the shared-app fixture, wrap the body of `server.cjs` in `setTimeout(() => { /* existing body */ }, 1500)`. Run `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/integration/shared-app-processes.test.ts -t 'aborts a hung start'`. Its first poll times out before the server listens.

Expected: check first-frame ordering directly, allow a reasonable process polling budget, and finish cancelling/stopping app processes before deleting their project.

### Versions

Reproduced at `a9c3de9f`: e2e 0.22.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.4, Node.js 24.14.1, macOS with 10 cores.

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

The hung-start test failed in CI on 2026-10-30 in [spec, test (22)](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/actions/runs/41087289059), at line 131, the poll waiting for the abandoned process to stop.

Related: #1473.

title: ci: cache the apt packages Playwright installs for Chromium
body:
## What and why

- `playwright-core install chromium --with-deps` downloads the same 38.2 MB of `.deb` files (17 upgrades, 9 new font packages) from the Ubuntu mirror in every job.
- In 38 of 84 recent `spec` jobs, the mirror served them at about 200 kB/s. The step took 118-302 s instead of 14-45 s. Example from one job log: `Fetched 38.2 MB in 3min 13s (198 kB/s)`, against `Fetched 38.2 MB in 5s (8481 kB/s)` in a fast job.
- The `spec` gate waits for its slowest job. 13 of 14 recent `spec` runs had at least one slow install job.
- The new `.github/actions/chromium` composite action does these steps:
  1. It points apt's archive directory at `/var/cache/chromium-apt` (`Dir::Cache::Archives`). The runner owns the directory, so the cache can restore into it. `partial` belongs to `_apt:root` with mode `0700`, like `/var/cache/apt/archives/partial`. The runner's temp directory did not work: `_apt` cannot traverse `/home/runner`, so apt downloaded as root (`W: Download is performed unsandboxed as root`).
  2. It restores the newest cache entry for the Ubuntu release, architecture, and Playwright version.
  3. It runs the same `install --with-deps` command, so apt downloads only the packages whose version changed.
  4. It runs `apt-get autoclean` to remove versions that the mirror no longer serves.
  5. It saves the archives under a digest of their file names, but only when the set changed.
- The installed packages do not change, so rendering and screenshot baselines do not change.
- All five install steps use the action: `spec` check and test, both benchmark jobs, and the weekly agent job. The `web` path filter in `.github/filters.yml` lists the action.

## Issue

No matching issue. This is a CI time optimization.

## Verified

title: perf(agent): read each scroll_to page once when it landed
body:
## What and why

- `scroll_to({ text })` took two captures per page: one, then a second 75 ms later to prove the page held still. The first was thrown away.
- A page now takes one capture when it landed: at least a third of its lines (two at least) are new, and it has at least as many nodes with a name or text as the page before (`pageLanded` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/reading.ts`). A page that reads the same (not rendered yet, or the list ended), differs by a line or two (a counter ticking beside a stale list), or is thinner (a windowed list still drawing rows) gets the old settle. The end of a list is still `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`.
- Lines are keyed by position, so the one-third share only does work on a windowed list. On a list whose rows move (a native list, an unwindowed web list) any movement makes nearly every line new and the page counts as landed. The mobile numbers below are that case.
- Clock-like values (`12:05`) no longer count as a moved page. On main, a ticking clock beside a list delayed the end-of-list report to 800 screens. It now ends after 3 swipes. Rows that differ only by a clock-like value keep paging, and so does a page of one line whose value changes (a pager that goes `10:30` to `11:00`), since a clock needs a line beside it to tick beside. The page is the whole screen, so a carousel with any other named node beside it (a title, a button) still reads as a ticking clock and can end in a false `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`. Main would keep paging there. The screen alone cannot tell the two apart, so this is documented in the `pageMoved` comment, not fixed.
- Precedent: #563 (second change wait after `scroll_to` text) and #1189 (the web swipe resolves after a rendered frame, so a stale first read is not expected on web).

## Scripted scroll suite

- `apps/testbed/e2e.scroll.config.ts`, `tests-scroll/`, and `test:scroll` run `scroll_to` by text with a scripted executor over the windowed `/scroll` page. The testbed numbers below come from it.
- It has its own config because the `agent` fixture needs the default agent to hold a model or an executor, and the default testbed suite's default agent holds neither on purpose. A named `agents` entry fails with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`.
- It is a CI step of its own (`Testbed, scroll_to` in `spec.yml`), not part of `test`: `test` forwards `--changed-since` to its last `run` only, so a chained suite would run unfiltered and its failure would skip the default suite.
- If you prefer a smaller PR, I will drop this suite. The integration tests in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/` cover the loop.

## Issue

No issue. Performance change inside the existing `scroll_to` contract.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes (macOS, Chromium, iOS simulator, Android emulator). `pnpm check` and the unit suite exit 0, and the scroll integration tests and `test:scroll` pass at `c24650dd`. The web tables were measured on `201b7758`, before the rebase onto `e99a6fa8` and the review fixes since. Steps and outcomes are identical on every `pnpm bench:ab` run. The full testbed script and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` exit 0 at `9f3c9cc0`.

### Web

| 8 pairs | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| testbed scripted suite (load 2.1) | 8.37 s | 5.48 s | -34% |
| Row 118 test | 4.34 s | 2.50 s | -43% |
| web benchmark replay, `--strict-cache` (load 2.7) | 66.07 s | 27.97 s | -58% |
| `virtualized-table` | 58.92 s | 22.58 s | -62% |
| `infinite-scroll` | 5.66 s | 3.96 s | -31% |

- Testbed command: `pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed --config e2e.scroll.config.ts --threshold 3 --min-pairs 8 --no-build`. The base worktree needed the config and `tests-scroll/` copied in by hand.
- Observation events in the web run moved from 464 to 466-469. `infinite-scroll` loads its feed on a timer, so a faster loop looks a few more times. This is my explanation; I did not trace it.
- Smooth scrolling in a real browser passes on both builds. Long animations cost extra swipes (13 to 21 screens at 4 s), and the run is still faster end to end.
- Two earlier review fixes (`9423bc7b`, `6e436ba5`) were each measured against the head before them (Apple M5 Max, load 4.3): same steps and outcomes, web replay 27.32 s to 27.48 s and 27.69 s to 27.58 s (both same).

### Mobile

The benchmark app's Release build, driven through `@e2e-dev/mobile` with a scripted executor (no model): `scroll_to` by text, then a tap on the row it reached, then the scenario's `success-message`. The executor and test were scratch files and are not in this PR. Merge base `e99a6fa8` against this branch, three runs each in the order main, branch, branch, main, main, branch, one run at a time after a discarded warmup, medians. The per-test step time includes the swipe and its fling wait, which is most of it.

iOS: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, agent-device 0.21.36.

| Case | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Row 0512, Huge Virtualized List (600 rows) | 182.6 s | 164.4 s | -10% |
| Item 137, Infinite Scroll List | 31.2 s | 28.1 s | -10% |
| Row 0100, Huge Virtualized List | 31.2 s | 31.0 s | same (one branch run took 27.5 s) |

- The number of observations per case is the same on both builds (Android exactly; iOS 67 to 73 in Row 0512 on both), so no extra page was needed and a mid-fling capture did not skip a row.

- The landing rule compares a page only with the page before. A page that was itself still drawing is not caught, and a page with a single new line takes the confirming read.

title: perf(web): make element handles for observed nodes when an action needs one
body:
## What and why

- An observation made one `ElementHandle` per listed node and released each one when the next observation replaced it. On a 3000-node page that is 3000 handle round trips per observe and about 100 ms of event-loop time disposing the previous generation. An action touches a few nodes at most.
- The reader already returns its elements as one in-page array. `ElementList` (`packages/web/src/element-list.ts`) keeps that array behind a single handle. A node's handle is made the first time an action reaches for it (`RefRegistry.lookup`, now async) and goes away with the list.
- A ref still names the element the walk read, not whatever sits at that position later (#239). Only iframe boundary elements are fetched during capture, for `contentFrame()`. A missing element, a list that was replaced, or a document navigated away since the walk is still a retryable `NODE_STALE`.
- This is the "lazy element handles per observation" follow-on #107 left out.
- The second commit replaces the byte loop in `pixelDigest` with the native SHA-256 the package already has. The digest is only compared in memory (`screen-update.ts`, `observationShape`), so no recording or cache key changes.

Overlap: #1529 skips the handle readback for the trace's post-action capture. It edits the same functions in `observation.ts` and `observation-capture.ts`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase. With this change the trace capture no longer reads back handles at all, so I expect `retainRefs` to become unnecessary. I have not rebased onto #1529 or measured the two together.

## Measured

Observe on a 3000-node page, built merge base against this branch, median of repeated runs:

| Page | main | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 3000 nodes | 360 ms | 78 ms |
| 400 nodes | 57 ms | 14 ms |

A tap after a fresh observe is unchanged within noise.

`pnpm bench:ab` on `apps/web-benchmark` (6 pairs, merge base `e99a6fa8` against this branch before the review fixes below; the fixes only touch the error path and a dispose count):

| Metric | main | this branch | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| wall (process) | 74.05 s | 68.19 s | -7.9% (-8.4% to -7.5%) |
| action (events) | 39.65 s | 35.11 s | -11.3% |
| step `screen.scrollUntilVisible` | 24.42 s | 20.12 s | -17.7% |
| step `locator.tap` | 11.55 s | 10.58 s | -8.5% |

Behavior matched on every test in every run of both builds.

Two things in that output need a reason:

- `events engine` rose from 809-810 to 825-830. Only `swipe` events differ, and only in `tests/infinite-scroll.e2e.ts` (46 to 62). `scrollUntilVisible` loops read, swipe, read until the target shows, and the app loads more items on a 400 ms timer, so a faster iteration (about 66 ms to about 43 ms) fits more swipes into the same wait. Time spent in swipes stayed about 2.6 s on both builds. I derived this from the numbers; I did not run a slowed-down loop to confirm it.
- `tests/control-inventory.e2e.ts › scrollIntoView brings the footnote into view` is 177 ms to 265 ms. The `scrollIntoView` step itself got faster (41-56 ms to 36-41 ms). The final `expect.toHaveText` went from 5 ms to 107 ms: the first check now lands before the page's `IntersectionObserver` callback sets "in view", and the next poll is 100 ms later (`POLL_INTERVAL_MS`). That race exists on main too; the slower post-action work happened to hide it. Inferred from the step timings and the poll interval, not isolated.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes (macOS arm64, Node 26, Chromium via Playwright; built packages)

- `pnpm check`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test`: exit 0.
- `pnpm test:testbed`: 47 files, 584 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: 41 files, 91 passed.
- A fresh-context review found two things, both fixed: an action on an observed ref after a navigation failed as non-retryable `ENGINE_FAILURE` instead of `NODE_STALE`, and the shared array handle was owned once per node instead of once per list. The new tests in `element-list.test.ts` fail without the first fix.
- cubic found that a ref resolving after the operation's deadline could still start the action, and that the lookup test ignored the index. Fixed in `0faf561d`: the signal is checked after each lookup (the drag test fails without it), and the scripted handles are keyed by index. The check in `surface.perform` has no test of its own; the drag test covers the same pattern.
- Web package tests after those fixes: 72 files, 676 passed, 1 skipped.
- CI on `0faf561d`: all 30 checks passed, including the web benchmark's agent suite (33 passed, replayed with the committed recordings) and the iOS and Android agent suites. The iOS agent job lost its worker once on the first push (`WORKER_EXIT`, SIGKILL, in `Debounced Search`, which passed on the next push) and one model-driven `Gestures` attempt failed and passed on retry. Neither touches the web engine, and I did not look at the runner logs for either.
- Not verified: the live agent path with `--no-cache --ai-trace` (no `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` here). The change does not touch the prompt, the tree text, or the cache key.

title: fix(decision): reserve a slot for the none target in the choice limit
body: - `MAX_CHOICES = 255` capped the element table, and every target question then appended `none` on top (`packages/decision/src/questions.ts:155`). On a page with 255+ rows that sent 256 choices, one over TypeSafe's per-question limit. - New `MAX_TARGETS = MAX_CHOICES - 1` caps the element table and the shared `select` option group. Drag destinations come from the kept rows, so they follow. - Same ordering as before: controls before passive rows, viewport first, then tree order. Only the 255th row moves into `omitted`, and the model can still scroll to it. - Reported by a user who patched `dist/elements.js` in 0.3.0 to `254` after dense pages failed in CI. ## Verified Ran it locally: no - a live run needs a 255+ element page and a TypeSafe-routed model. title: perf: skip the MCP server, prompt library, and Playwright until a command needs them
body:
- `e2e --version`, `--help`, `run`, and `list` no longer load the MCP server, `@clack/prompts`, or `zod` at startup. `mcp`, `init`, `login`, `logout`, `models`, `explore`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, and `--watch` import their module when they run. `--version` reads 260 files, 2.2 MB, instead of 438 files, 4.6 MB. `list` on a web project reads 336 files, 3.1 MB, instead of 517 files, 11.9 MB.
- The bounds and choice lists a flag needs moved into modules that import nothing heavy, so defining a flag loads nothing. These are `SESSION_BOUNDS`, `STEP_BOUNDS`, `TIMEOUT_BOUNDS`, `PROVIDER_IDS`, and the `upgrade` target parser.
- `@e2e-dev/web` imports `playwright-core` at the first browser lookup, launch, or attach. `e2e list` never loads it, and neither does the main process of a run on a CDP-attached or provider-hosted browser. `browserCheck` and `ensureBrowsersInstalled` are async now.
- `BrowserConnection.acquire` sets `pending` before it awaits, because the first call now loads Playwright. A `dispose` that arrived during that load would miss the browser the launch then produced, and two callers could each launch one.
- `e2e/runner` loads the explorer when `explore` is called. `@e2e-dev/acp` loads the ACP SDK and the MCP server at its first session, and `@e2e-dev/limrun` loads `@limrun/api` at its first lease. A missing `@limrun/api` now fails at that lease instead of at config import.
- A `STARTUP` table in `package-imports.test.ts` fails with the import chain when the CLI, runner, worker, acp, limrun, or web entry reaches one of these packages through static imports again. The scan also counts `import { type X } from 'x'` as a runtime import, because `verbatimModuleSyntax` leaves `import {} from 'x'` in the output.

## Measured

`main` at `76a5280b` against this change, on one Apple M1 Max with Node 26.12.1, measured before the last rebase onto `4dce5a76`, a tap-position fix that does not touch loading. The runs alternate between the two builds in random order. Each row is the median of the paired runs with the 95% bootstrap interval of the paired change, computed by `scripts/bench-ab/stats.ts`. All 14 rows are `faster` against a threshold of 3% and 10 ms.

| Scenario | main | this PR | change (95% CI) | pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `e2e --version` | 272 ms | 198 ms | -27.4% (-27.8% to -27.0%) | 30 |
| `e2e --help` | 272 ms | 198 ms | -27.2% (-27.6% to -26.7%) | 30 |
| `e2e list`, web project, 4 tests | 452 ms | 238 ms | -47.4% (-47.6% to -47.0%) | 30 |
| `e2e list`, testbed, 51 files | 567 ms | 379 ms | -33.3% (-33.9% to -32.9%) | 20 |
| `e2e init --yes`, new directory | 295 ms | 245 ms | -16.7% (-17.3% to -16.1%) | 15 |
| `e2e doctor --target web` | 450 ms | 415 ms | -8.1% (-8.4% to -7.5%) | 20 |
| `e2e mcp`, until `tools/list` answers | 386 ms | 363 ms | -5.8% (-6.2% to -4.7%) | 20 |
| `e2e run`, local browser, 1 worker, 4 tests | 1.75 s | 1.69 s | -3.7% (-4.1% to -3.3%) | 20 |
| `e2e run`, CDP attach, 1 worker, 4 tests | 1.83 s | 1.63 s | -10.8% (-11.4% to -9.9%) | 20 |
| `e2e run`, CDP attach, 3 workers, 4 tests | 1.56 s | 1.36 s | -13.2% (-13.4% to -12.8%) | 20 |
| import `@e2e-dev/web` | 316 ms | 166 ms | -47.5% (-47.8% to -47.1%) | 20 |
| import `@e2e-dev/limrun` | 203 ms | 141 ms | -30.6% (-31.4% to -30.2%) | 20 |
| import `@e2e-dev/acp` | 223 ms | 194 ms | -13.3% (-13.7% to -12.9%) | 20 |
| import `e2e/runner` | 207 ms | 183 ms | -12.2% (-12.5% to -11.6%) | 20 |

The imports include about 100 ms of Node starting. Peak memory of the largest process drops from 104 MB to 85 MB for `--version`, from 181 MB to 91 MB for `list` on the web project, and from 228 MB to 142 MB for `list` on the testbed. `run` stays at about 200 MB.

A local launch still loads Playwright in the main process, in `prepare`, and in every worker, so `run` saves only the CLI's startup, 40 to 70 ms. A run whose browser is attached over CDP skips Playwright in the main process too.

`pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed --threshold 3 --min-pairs 30 --max-pairs 30 -- tests/forms.e2e.ts` ran every test through the same steps with the same outcome on both builds, and every counter matched.

| Metric | main | this PR | change (95% CI) | verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| wall (process) | 3.21 s | 3.17 s | -1.3% (-1.6% to -1.0%) | same |
| suite (sum of attempts) | 1.97 s | 2.11 s | +7.2% (+6.7% to +7.6%) | slower |

The `slower` row comes from one test, the first one a worker runs. `fills, clears, and submits a profile` takes 1.51 s on main and 1.66 s here. title: fix(run): quote a long app log's first lines in APP_UNREACHABLE
body: ## What and why - When an `app.command` dies during startup, the `APP_UNREACHABLE` message is often the only diagnostic a run leaves. With a `command.log`, it quotes what the process appended since it started, `command.env` and `inheritEnv` values redacted. - That quote was a tail: the last 20 lines of the last 4 KiB. A process that prints its fatal error early and keeps logging (file watchers, bundlers, half-started dev servers) buried the one line that explains the failure. #1527 hit this: the cause was in the first lines, the message showed only the end. - `outputSince(offset)` read a single window at the end of the file, so nothing before it could be recovered downstream. It now reads the other end too. ## What changed - `packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`: `outputSince` reads two windows of `OUTPUT_WINDOW_BYTES` (4 KiB), one from the command's own log offset and one ending at the end of the file. - Windows that meet (the log since the command started fits in 8 KiB): quoted whole up to 40 lines, otherwise the first 20, `[startup output omitted]`, the last 20. - Windows that do not meet: always the first 20, the marker, the last 20. The marker stays even when one huge first line leaves nothing above it. - The head starts at the command's own offset without clipping, so a first line written after a previous run's unfinished line survives. - A clipped edge drops its fragment before empty lines are filtered, so a whitespace-only fragment cannot take the complete line above it. - Every quoted line goes through the same `this.redact` pass as before. - `packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts`: the inline read became a module-level `readLines(fd, from, to, { start, end })` helper that both windows share. - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/managed-process.test.ts`: `keeps the last 20 lines only` became a whole-log test, since a 25-line log has nothing omitted now. New exact-equality tests cover the line cap on both branches, both byte thresholds of the overlap check, cuts inside a line and exactly between lines, the whitespace fragment, an `offset > 0` log with and without a final newline, and the marker after a huge first line. - `docs/web.mdx`, `docs/reference/config.mdx`, `docs/reference/errors.mdx`: the quote is described as whole for a short log, otherwise the first and last lines with the marker between them. The config page names the byte bound. - `.changeset/app-unreachable-first-lines.md`: `e2e` patch. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[app.command fails at startup] --> B[read the log since the command started] B --> C{do the head and tail windows meet?} C -- yes --> L{more than 40 lines?} L -- no --> D[quote every line] L -- yes --> E C -- no --> E[first 20 lines] E --> F[startup output omitted] F --> G[last 20 lines] D --> H[redact command.env and inheritEnv values] G --> H H --> I[APP_UNREACHABLE message] ``` ## Issue Fixes #1527 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: the `APP_UNREACHABLE` message the built CLI prints when `app.command` exits before the app is ready, on a scratch project whose command writes one fatal line, one line naming `DATABASE_URL`, then 40 watcher lines, and exits 1. The main side below is the `dist` built before this change, the branch side is the same command after rebuilding `packages/e2e`. ```text main: output in .e2e\app.log since target "web" command started: watcher: rebuilt module 21 ... watcher: rebuilt module 40 this branch: output in .e2e\app.log since target "web" command started: fatal: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open .env.local hint: DATABASE_URL= watcher: rebuilt module 1 ... watcher: rebuilt module 19 [startup output omitted] watcher: rebuilt module 21 ... watcher: rebuilt module 40 ``` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | the fatal line and modules 1 to 20 are missing from the message | the fatal line comes first, the gap is marked | | the line naming `DATABASE_URL` is missing, so no value could leak | the same line is quoted with the value masked as `` | | the log file keeps the raw value | the log file keeps the raw value, the message does not | - The first two new tests were written first and watched failing on the old code (`expected [ ' line 41', ... ] to equal [ ' line 1', ... ]`), then passing after the change. The whole file on the latest head: 34 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped. - The one failure is `fails with APP_UNREACHABLE when the log path cannot be opened`, and it fails on this machine on `main` too, with the change stashed: opening a directory as an append log resolves here instead of throwing, so no `InfrastructureError` is raised. Windows-only, unrelated to this change. - `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/e2e`: exit 0. `oxlint` on both changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `check-changeset-bumps.ts` and `check-error-codes.ts`: exit 0. - Not run locally: the full `pnpm check` chain and the browser-backed integration suites, which need a full build of every package (about twelve minutes here) and Chromium. CI ran them on the latest head and the `spec`, `benchmark`, `mobile`, and `docs` gates passed. The change touches no engine code, no wire format, and no exported type. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: perf: decode and encode PNGs with @napi-rs/image
body:
- `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, and `@e2e-dev/decision` read and write PNGs with `@napi-rs/image` instead of `fast-png` and `pngjs` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/image.ts`, `packages/mobile/src/png.ts`, `packages/decision/src/png.ts`). `pixelmatch` stays: the addon has no diff API.
- Chromium's captures are 8-bit RGB. The addon widens them to RGBA itself (`opacity(1)` keeps every sample), which was most of the decode once the codec was native. Other color types go through a short layout step in JS.
- Decoded pixels match the old libraries on the 76 PNGs the repo tracks and on a synthetic matrix of color types, depths, interlacing, palettes, and transparent colors. Two behaviors change on purpose and are in the changeset: gray PNGs with 1, 2, or 4 bits now decode, and a 16-bit gray or RGB PNG with a transparent color compares at 16 bits.
- `e2e` loads the addon when the first PNG is read or written (`createRequire`, as `oxc()` does), so `--version`, `--help`, and a run that takes no screenshot never need the binding. A missing binding fails the call with the new `IMAGE_CODEC_UNAVAILABLE` (`docs/reference/errors.mdx`). The `STARTUP` table in `package-imports.test.ts` pins the lazy load.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/decision` import the addon with the package. They are opt-in, and a lazy load there would turn a missing binding into a secure screenshot silently withheld (`redactSecure`) or a zoom silently skipped (`decode` in `overlay.ts`). Stopping at import is the louder failure.

## Speed

Main (`0c1b3572`) against this branch: both `dist` builds in one process, A/B then B/A, 11 rounds per cell, medians over three real screenshots per profile. Each case first checks that both sides produce the same pixels.

| | web 1280×720 | web 2560×1440 (DPR 2) | phone 1170×2532 (DPR 3) | device 804×1786 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decode | 30.8 → 2.06 ms | 117 → 9.98 ms | 97.5 → 7.78 ms | 20.4 → 2.64 ms |
| encode | 32.9 → 5.32 ms | 134 → 16.4 ms | 106 → 19.9 ms | 50.8 → 6.66 ms |
| model-bound downscale, `downscalePixels(768)` | 50.4 → 9.87 ms | 147 → 28.0 ms | 120 → 23.4 ms | 38.8 → 11.2 ms |
| `toHaveScreenshot` capture, whole screen | 31.1 → 2.51 ms | 136 → 29.4 ms | | |
| mobile `maskPng`, 2 rects | | | 197 → 28.5 ms | 90.5 → 8.84 ms |
| decision `zoomAround(400, 2x)` | 39.3 → 5.36 ms | 39.4 → 5.38 ms | 39.1 → 7.68 ms | 37.6 → 5.55 ms |

What is left at 2560×1440 is the JS box resample, unchanged here: 14.6 of the 28 ms.

`pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed -- tests/visual.e2e.ts`, 30 pairs. Every test ran the same steps with the same outcome, and every counter matched. The harness notes that the suite's tests differ between the builds because `screenshot.e2e.ts` was ported; `visual.e2e.ts` itself is unchanged.

| | main | this PR | change (95% CI) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| step `expect.toHaveScreenshot` | 454 ms | 340 ms | -24.6% (-27.8% to -23.2%) |
| suite, sum of attempts | 2.24 s | 2.09 s | -6.8% (-7.5% to -5.9%) |
| wall, process | 3.32 s | 3.14 s | -5.1% (-5.6% to -4.5%) |
| `e2e --version`, 30 interleaved pairs | 194.7 ms | 188.7 ms | -3.4% |

## Decisions for the reviewer

- Platforms. The addon publishes 12 bindings and oxc, already in `e2e`, publishes 19. Linux on ppc64, s390x, and riscv64 (gnu and musl), armv7 musl, android arm32, and OpenHarmony have none. There `toHaveScreenshot` and any agent screenshot the runner has to resize (a side over 768 px) fail with `IMAGE_CODEC_UNAVAILABLE`, and `mobile` and `decision` fail at import. The changeset is a `patch`; whether this is a `**Breaking:**` minor is your call.
- Encoded size. `FilterType.Adaptive` makes a Chromium capture about 15% larger than `fast-png` wrote it (55 to 63 KB at 1280×720) and a device screenshot about 20% smaller. "The smaller of no filter and adaptive" would never be larger than `fast-png` on a Chromium capture, costs about twice the encode time (5.3 to 9.7 ms at 1280×720), and touches the same three files. Not done here.
- Shared layout code. The step from the addon's pixel layouts to 8-bit RGBA (`LAYOUTS`, `narrow`, `spread`) exists in `e2e`, `mobile`, and `decision`. `mobile` and `decision` reach `e2e` only through its public entries, so sharing it means a new export on `e2e` or `e2e/engine`, or a new package. `readPngSize` is copied in web and mobile for the same reason.
- Install size. The binary is 15.5 MB on macOS arm64 and 21.1 MB on Linux x64 (8.3 MB download), against 1.25 MB for `fast-png`, `fflate`, and `iobuffer`. `pngjs` stays through `pixelmatch`.
- Memory. The addon frees what a `Transformer` holds in a finalizer that Node runs a loop turn after V8 collects the owner, and it does not tell V8 about that memory. A loop that calls these functions back to back without yielding keeps about 70 MB per 2560×1440 capture: 120 calls peak at 8.4 GB where main stayed at 253 MB. Real runs yield between calls: worker peaks are 240 MB for `visual.e2e.ts` (main 315 MB) and 490 MB for `screenshot.e2e.ts` (main 427 MB).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- The built CLI on the testbed, `tests/visual.e2e.ts` against the stored screenshots `fast-png` wrote: 4 passed, and no tracked file changed.
- The failure path, with the platform binding left out (`@napi-rs/image-darwin-arm64` unresolvable, which is what `--omit=optional` does), on a testbed config without `decisionFilter`:
  - `tests/todos.e2e.ts` passes: 7 passed, exit 0.
  - `tests/visual.e2e.ts` fails every test with exit 3:

```text
 × |web| tests/visual.e2e.ts > screenshots > compares a block with a changing part masked
IMAGE_CODEC_UNAVAILABLE: e2e reads and writes screenshots with @napi-rs/image, and its native binding for darwin-arm64 (@napi-rs/image-darwin-arm64*) is not installed. npm skips it with --omit=optional, or when package-lock.json was written on another platform (npm/cli#4828): install again without --omit=optional, or delete package-lock.json and node_modules and run npm install. The package has no binding for Linux on ppc64, s390x, or riscv64
```

  - The testbed's own config imports `@e2e-dev/decision`, so there the same missing binding stops at config load, exit 2: `failed to load config .../e2e.config.ts: Cannot find native binding. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies (https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828). ...`
- The mobile benchmark I could not run here (no device). CI ran it on this head: the iOS simulator passed 55 deterministic tests and 21 agentic ones, the Android emulator 57 and 20, with one retry on Android's `Gestures`, which flaked the same way on #1576.
- Not run: the agentic suites live against a model (CI replays their recordings), Windows, and Linux outside CI.

title: Let a test file choose its target or app environment
body:
> I am an AI agent commenting on behalf of John Carlo Austria.

We use `e2e` 0.22.0. Two test files in our suite need different builds of the same app, and the runner does not let a file choose its build.

**What we need**

One file tests our developer tools panels, so its build must set `ENABLE_DEVTOOLS=true`. The other file taps a button at the bottom right of the page. At 390 × 844, the developer tools trigger covers that button, so the tap does not land. This file needs a build with `ENABLE_DEVTOOLS=false`.

**What we tried**

We added two targets with different app environments:

```ts
targets: [
  { name: "devtools", engine: web(), app: { url, command: { executable, args, env: { ENABLE_DEVTOOLS: "true" } } } },
  { name: "clean", engine: web(), app: { url, command: { executable, args, env: { ENABLE_DEVTOOLS: "false" } } } },
]
```

This does not work, because every test runs on every target. The docs say this in `docs/web.mdx`: "Every test runs on every target, with a separate result per target name." Each file then fails on the build that it cannot use. `TestOptions` has no target or environment field. The `--target` flag selects a target for the whole run, not for one file.

**What we do now**

We moved the tap check to a separate Playwright package that builds the app without the developer tools. We want to move it back into `e2e`.

**Request**

Can a test file name the targets that it runs on? An option in `TestOptions` would let both checks stay in one `e2e` suite.

title: feat(runner): start the tests a change is likeliest to break first
body:
- A test filter can score the tests it keeps: `TestFilterResult.relevance` maps test ids to a number from 0 to 1. With `--changed-since`, each target starts the files of the likeliest tests first, in bands at 75%, 50%, and 25%. Targets go by the band of their best file, ties in config order.
- Inside a band the existing longest-first order still decides: with more than one worker, the file the timings history (#1639) holds longest starts first, and a file with no time starts before the timed ones. `docs/filters.mdx`, `docs/reference/config.mdx`, and `docs/ci.mdx` say how it combines with the bands.
- `decisionFilter()` scores every test it hands back: 1 for a test whose file, setup file, or stored screenshots changed, the model's answer for one it judged: the higher of the test's rating and its setup's, where a rating the model did not give counts as 0.5. It asks the model nothing new.
- A filter that fails can still score. The error it throws may carry `relevance`, which the run checks like a result's, and the failure still warns, leaves nothing out, and records `outcome: failed`. `decisionFilter()` puts the scores the change alone gives (1 for a test the change touches, 0.5 for the rest) on the error it throws when every call fails, so a run with no key, or with the model down, still starts the touched tests first.
- The run prints `ranked 7 of 12 tests by relevance, likeliest first` when the scores put tests in more than one band. `e2e list` says nothing, since it starts nothing.
- `@e2e-dev/decision` now needs `e2e >=0.23.1`. An older runner rejects the unknown `relevance` key and drops the whole filter, as the main column below shows.

This shortens the time to the first failure: `--max-failures`, `maxDuration`, Ctrl-C, and CI with its default single worker, where longest-first never applied. It does not shorten a run that finishes whole. With several workers it can lengthen one, since a likely short file now starts before an unlikely long one.

The sort key is the file's band (its likeliest test), then its time in the timings history (untimed first), then collection order. A target ranks by its best file, ties in config order. `scheduler.ts` is unchanged: it already drains targets and files in plan order, and `scheduler.test.ts` pins that. The report lists tests in the same order whatever starts first, and the report format is unchanged.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Surface: the built CLI on a scratch project with `@e2e-dev/web` (real Chromium) and a file-backed config whose local filter scores tests, main (`0c1b3572`) against this branch. The filter needs no model.
- `pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed -- tests/forms.e2e.ts`, a run with no scores (4 pairs): every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on both builds, every counter matched, and the timings were the same (wall +1.3%, interval -2.0% to +1.7%). It ran before the last commit, which changes only what a failed filter leaves.
- Not verified: the real Jev model, since there is no AI Gateway key here. The scripted-model tests cover the scores, and `filter-runner.test.ts` runs the real `list` on the decision filter's result. The band edges (75%, 50%, 25%) are my estimate until real scores are seen. The peer floor assumes the next release is 0.23.1.

`e2e run --changed-since main --workers 1 --max-failures 1` on three tests: `alpha` and `beta` sleep 3 s, `gamma` fails at once and is collected last. The filter scores `gamma` 1.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filter line | `warning: likeliest returned an invalid result ... unknown key "relevance"` | `ranked 1 of 3 tests by relevance, likeliest first` |
| start order | alpha, beta, gamma | gamma |
| first failure at | +6.5 s | +0.3 s |
| `alpha`, `beta` | passed, 3.3 s and 3.1 s | skipped, `failure-limit` |
| wall time | 7.8 s | 1.2 s |

```text
main
ℹ judging 2 files changed since 60ed46c
ℹ warning: likeliest returned an invalid result, so it leaves nothing out: unknown key "relevance": a filter returns { exclude: { [test.id]: reason }, note? }, and every test it doesn't name runs
   ✓ |web| tests/alpha.e2e.ts > alpha 3.32s
   ✓ |web| tests/beta.e2e.ts > beta 3.06s
   × |web| tests/gamma.e2e.ts > gamma 131ms
stopped after 1 failure (--max-failures 1): the running tests end as interrupted, the rest are skipped

this branch
ℹ judging 2 files changed since 60ed46c
ℹ likeliest kept all 3 tests
ℹ ranked 1 of 3 tests by relevance, likeliest first
   × |web| tests/gamma.e2e.ts > gamma 343ms
   ↓ |web| tests/alpha.e2e.ts > alpha [run stopped after 1 failure (--max-failures 1)]
   ↓ |web| tests/beta.e2e.ts > beta [run stopped after 1 failure (--max-failures 1)]
```

`e2e run --changed-since main --workers 1 --max-failures 1` with the real `decisionFilter()` on `typesafe-ai/jev` and no AI Gateway key, so every model call fails. The tests are the same three, and the change edits `gamma`'s test file, so the change touches it. "Before" is this PR's previous head (`d2c2217e`), which dropped the scores of a failed filter.

| | before | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filter lines | `warning: decision failed, so it leaves nothing out: AI Gateway authentication failed: No authentication provided.` | the same warning, then `ranked 3 of 3 tests by relevance, likeliest first` |
| `run.filters` | `outcome: failed` | `outcome: failed`, same note |
| start order | alpha, beta, gamma | gamma |
| first failure at | +6.5 s | +0.3 s |
| `alpha`, `beta` | passed, 3.3 s and 3.1 s | skipped, `failure-limit` |
| wall time | 6.8 s | 0.6 s |

`e2e list` with the same filter prints the warning and the three tests, and no ranking line, as before.

The same failure on the testbed's own config, which runs `decisionFilter()` on Jev: `e2e run --changed-since HEAD --workers 1 tests/forms.e2e.ts tests/todos.e2e.ts` with no key and an uncommitted comment added to `todos.e2e.ts` (reverted after), so the change touches that file. `forms` is collected first.

| | before (`d2c2217e`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filter lines | the `decision failed` warning | the same warning, then `ranked 11 of 11 tests by relevance, likeliest first` |
| first test started | `fills, clears, and submits a profile` (`forms`) | `adds todos with the button and the keyboard` (`todos`) |
| the 7 `todos` tests started | 5th to 11th | 1st to 7th |
| result | 11 passed | 11 passed |

`e2e run --changed-since main --workers 2` right after a run that recorded the timings, on four tests: `a` 1 s, `b` 3 s, `c` 4 s, `d` 1 s. The filter scores `d` 0.9 and `c` 0.3. Both builds read the same recorded times. This table was taken before the timings history (#1639) landed on main.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| start order | b, c (together), a, d | c, d (together), b, a |
| why | longest first, since main drops the scores | `d` is in the top band and `c` in a lower one, then `b` goes before `a` by time |
| wall time | 6.2 s | 6.2 s |

After rebasing onto the timings history, the same four tests on this branch (a first run wrote `timings.json`, then `--changed-since main --workers 2`) start c, d, b, a again, in 5.7 s.

Two integration tests pin the wiring. In `test-filters.test.ts`, a filter that throws with scores still starts the failing test first under `--max-failures 1`, and its warning and `outcome: failed` stay. In `parallel-workers.test.ts`, a run with one worker ignores the timings history and a run with two workers uses it; that test fails when the `runWorkers > 1` gate is removed or always on.

title: chore: version packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @e2e-dev/browser-run@0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1634](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1634) [`352b774`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/352b774b33d1b12c6493876ca73532ea0e3506ae) Thanks [@irvinebroque](https://github.com/irvinebroque)! - **Release:** New package: `@e2e-dev/browser-run`. A Cloudflare Browser Run browser provider for hosted Chromium leases.
## @e2e-dev/web@0.16.0

### Minor Changes

- [#1393](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1393) [`046bd08`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/046bd08f4a5ea4693239c825539812f6b0d05060) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - **Breaking:** `web({ headers })` and `web({ basicAuth })` go only to the app's origin, the scheme, host, and port of `app.url`. Before, `headers` went to every host on the app's site (another port on the same host, sibling subdomains, every host under a shared domain such as `vercel.app`), and `basicAuth` answered a `401` from any origin, so a third-party origin the app embeds could collect the credential.
  
  To migrate, list each other origin that needs the credentials in `credentialOrigins: ['https://api.example.com']`; it covers both. An app whose `app.url` redirects to another origin (`http:` to `https:`, the apex to `www`) needs the origin it lands on listed, or set `app.url` to it. `headers` still ride a request's own redirects to any origin, as before. WebKit can't scope basic auth to an origin on a default port or an IPv6 host, so there it still answers any origin. Update `e2e` with this release: the engine needs the app's origin from the runner.

### Patch Changes

- [#1609](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1609) [`34a260c`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/34a260cc59d7ebd1d414fd2716f955bd2a51795f) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Bump playwright-core to 1.65.0 and commander to 15.1.0. `fill` no longer rejects malformed date, time, color, and range values, and actions wait for an element to leave an `inert` subtree. Smol sandboxes use the Playwright 1.65.0 image.

- [#1595](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1595) [`12c6c01`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/12c6c01929883782062fd9e308cd4be71977bf7c) Thanks [@samanyudas](https://github.com/samanyudas)! - `check`, `uncheck`, and `tap` click a checkbox or radio hidden under its own label (as in Element Plus) through that label. `uncheck` still refuses a native radio without clicking it. Anything else on top of the point the click lands on still fails `ACTION_FAILED`.

- [#1672](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1672) [`3735887`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/373588756937562aa89c7dd7f7995ac6b16db972) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Move GitHub repository metadata and CLI links to e2e-inc/e2e after the organization rename. Register the MCP server as io.github.e2e-inc/e2e.

- [#1595](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1595) [`12c6c01`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/12c6c01929883782062fd9e308cd4be71977bf7c) Thanks [@samanyudas](https://github.com/samanyudas)! - The agent now sees a checkbox or radio that a component library shrinks to no size under its own label (as in Element Plus), with its checked state. Before, it saw only the label text, and a tap that ticked the box reported no change.

- [#1665](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1665) [`3c9de80`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/3c9de80d9e6017c8ce66e310742b92580a029cba) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - Open an MCP session in a directory with no config: `open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url}}` names the engine to drive and `app` the app under test. `engine` is a package name, or the factory call a config would write as `{package, export, options}`, where an option can be another such call: `{package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: {platform: "ios", device: {package: "@e2e-dev/limrun", export: "limrun"}}}`. Each package is found in the project, beside e2e, or in `~/.e2e/engines`; when it is in none, `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED` names the install command. `@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` export their factory as the default export for this, and `mobile()` called without a platform now says which platforms it takes.

- [#1614](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1614) [`f6aba97`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/f6aba97257700339b60fb67722178d23ee2c5f93) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - A screenshot taken while the page navigates still captures the document showing when Playwright reports the destroyed context before the navigation event.

- [#1592](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1592) [`b43e846`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/b43e8469ce55c96e54d979d08ccf0034ad93e546) Thanks [@KrzysztofMoch](https://github.com/KrzysztofMoch)! - `expect(browser).toHaveURL` failures print a relative expected URL resolved against the app URL, the same way it is compared, so it reads beside the absolute observed URL.

- [#1747](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1747) [`a94c765`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/a94c76534498c867f4dc74d061b5a4ac0804b1b4) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Send CDP handshake headers for hosted browser leases.

- [#1710](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1710) [`0920ef5`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/0920ef5f941a428545c9e16a36d5ba361ac1ba54) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - The `browser` fixture drives tabs. A tab the app opens (a `target="_blank"` link, `window.open`, an OAuth popup) joins `browser.tabs()` in the background, and the active tab stays where it was. `browser.waitForPopup(trigger)` runs the trigger and makes the tab it opens active, `browser.newTab()` opens a tab in the same context, and each `BrowserTab` has `url`, `title`, `isActive`, `isClosed`, `activate`, and `close`. When the active tab closes, the tab that opened it is active again, or the tab active most recently when that one is closed too. The agent's `switch_tab` and `close_tab` verbs move between tabs and close them. The web engine needs `e2e` 0.23.1 or newer. [Tabs](https://e2e.com/docs/reference/web#tabs)

## @e2e-dev/decision@0.3.3

### Patch Changes

- [#1672](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1672) [`3735887`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/373588756937562aa89c7dd7f7995ac6b16db972) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - Move GitHub repository metadata and CLI links to e2e-inc/e2e after the organization rename. Register the MCP server as io.github.e2e-inc/e2e.

- [#1587](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1587) [`34ccc5f`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/34ccc5f38820befd2cc77795dd463507aaccd8ea) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - PNG decoding and encoding now run on `@napi-rs/image`, a native addon with a prebuilt binary per platform, in place of `fast-png` and `pngjs`: decoding is 8 to 15 times faster, encoding 5 to 8 times, and a `toHaveScreenshot` capture 4 to 12 times. Stored screenshots decode to the same pixels as before. A screenshot the runner writes (a new baseline, or one rewritten because the screen changed) has the same pixels in different bytes: a Chromium capture comes out about 15% larger and a device screenshot about 20% smaller. The binary adds about 15 to 21 MB to an install, depending on the platform, and the package publishes none for Linux on ppc64, s390x, or riscv64. `e2e` loads it when the first screenshot is read or written, so `--version` and a run that takes none never need it, and a missing binding fails that call with `IMAGE_CODEC_UNAVAILABLE`; `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/decision` load it when they are imported. Gray PNGs with 1, 2, or 4 bits per sample now decode, and a 16-bit gray or RGB PNG with a transparent color now compares pixels to it at 16 bits, so a pixel that only rounds to it at 8 bits stays opaque.

- [#1589](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1589) [`b5e4703`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/b5e47036ba0f8657478be967eb9e1a3a120dec51) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - A test filter can score the tests it keeps. `relevance` in its result gives each test a number from 0 to 1, and a run with `--changed-since` starts the files of the likeliest first in each target, in bands at 75%, 50%, and 25%, so a failure shows sooner and `--max-failures` stops earlier. Targets go by the band of their best file, ties in config order. Inside a band, a run with more than one worker still starts the file the previous run spent longest in first.
  
  `decisionFilter()` now scores every test it keeps: 100% for a test whose file, setup file, or stored screenshots changed, the model's answer for one it judged, and 50% for one it did not judge. When it fails, as without a key, it puts the scores the change alone gives on the error it throws, so the run still warns and runs every test, with the touched ones first. A filter of your own can do the same: an error it throws may carry `relevance`. `decisionFilter()` requires e2e 0.23.1 or newer, since an older runner refuses the new `relevance` key and drops the whole filter.
## @e2e-dev/e2b@0.0.1

## e2e@0.23.1

### Patch Changes

- [#1710](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1710) [`0920ef5`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/0920ef5f941a428545c9e16a36d5ba361ac1ba54) Thanks [@kdy1](https://github.com/kdy1)! - The agent tells the model when an action opened a tab in the background (`The app opened a new tab (tab 2 of 2). The screen still shows tab 1; use switch_tab to see it.`), names the tab in every screen header while more than one is open (`tab 1 of 2`), and gets `switch_tab` and `close_tab` verbs on engines that declare the new `session.switchTab` and `session.closeTab` hooks. `EngineSnapshot.tabs` reports the open tabs. [Action tools](https://e2e.com/docs/reference/agent#action-tools)

- [#1600](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1600) [`f5c9099`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/f5c9099615ad608e46a387435fac6e4770302f68) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - The built-in agent can try an upload when the step names no file. `upload` takes `sample:photo.png`, `sample:photo.jpg`, `sample:document.pdf`, `sample:notes.txt`, `sample:table.csv`, and `sample:empty.txt`, small files e2e ships, and the tool lists them. An `e2e mcp` upload of a sample prints no test line, since a test needs a project file.

- [#1541](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1541) [`11dea90`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/11dea90ddc27a007e81aec582d92d3e491a71dda) Thanks [@samanyudas](https://github.com/samanyudas)! - Fail `e2e run` when an app command exits unexpectedly after readiness.
  Report its exit code or signal and redacted log tail.
  Interrupt active tests and skip queued tests only for targets that depend on that command.

title: docs(ci): cache Playwright browsers in the GitHub Actions web workflow
body: ## What and why - The GitHub Actions web workflow in `docs/ci/github-actions.mdx` and its copy in `skills/e2e/references/running.md` now cache `~/.cache/ms-playwright`, keyed on the runner OS, CPU architecture, and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. - On a cache hit, `pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps` finds the browsers and downloads nothing; `--with-deps` still installs the system libraries. The lockfile pins `@e2e-dev/web` and its Playwright, so a version bump changes the key and downloads fresh browsers. `runner.arch` is in the key because Playwright's browser folders don't name the CPU, so an x64 and an arm64 job would otherwise restore each other's Chromium. - An `e2e` patch changeset ships the skill change, since the package bundles `skills/e2e/`. - This follows @kdy1's CI speedups for this repo (#1530, #1569) in a form a user can copy. `--only-shell` is left out because `e2e-web install` accepts only `--with-deps`. The apt cache is left out because it needs a 77-line composite action. ```yaml - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0 with: path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml') }} ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, the install command, not the workflow on Actions. - Built `@e2e-dev/web`, then ran `pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium` from `apps/testbed` twice against an empty `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, the second time standing in for a restored cache: | Run | Downloads | Time | | --- | --- | --- | | empty cache | ffmpeg, Chromium, headless shell | 20.3 s | | cache present | none | 0.2 s | - `pnpm docs:check` and `pnpm plugins:check` pass. - Not run on GitHub Actions; the step is the stock `actions/cache` usage at the SHA the mobile workflow on this page already pins.

title: fix(web): print toHaveURL's expected URL resolved against the app URL
body: A failed `expect(browser).toHaveURL('/e/control-inventory/summary')` printed the expected URL as written and the observed URL in full: ``` expected: URL /e/control-inventory/summary observed: URL http://127.0.0.1:4280/e/control-inventory?view=details ``` The comparison was right: `urlMatches` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/urls.ts:201`) resolves a string against the app URL and compares full hrefs. Only the label was built from the raw argument, so anything that diffs the two lines (the HTML reporter does) marked the origin as a difference when it never was one. - `describeExpectedUrl` in `packages/web/src/browser.ts` prints a string resolved against the same `baseHref()` the comparison uses. A string that does not parse, or a RegExp, prints as written. Negation and `(ignoring case)` are unchanged. - `browser.waitForURL` runs the same poll, so its timeout message gets the fix too. - The mobile engine and core have no `toHaveURL`; nothing else builds this label. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, a throwaway test that opens `/about?view=details` and expects `toHaveURL('/about/summary')`, run with the built CLI against main's engine and this branch's: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `expected: URL /about/summary` | `expected: URL http://127.0.0.1:4271/about/summary` | | `observed: URL http://127.0.0.1:4271/about?view=details` | `observed: URL http://127.0.0.1:4271/about?view=details` | - The new case in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` fails against main's engine and passes here. title: fix(mobile): refuse launch options installApp drops, deprecate foreground openApp launch arguments
body:
## What and why

A user wanted e2e to launch their iOS app with custom process arguments and tried passing them to `device.installApp`. The launch path already works end to end: `app.launchArguments` reaches the process on `app.open()`, `app.restart()`, `app.clearState()`, and `device.openApp(app, { relaunch: true, launchArguments })` (simulator: `simctl launch <udid> <bundle> args...`, CoreDevice phone: `devicectl ... -- args`). The gap was silent drops:

- `device.installApp(path, { launchArguments })` ignored the option. It now fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and names where the option goes. `launchArguments`/`launchArgs` point to `app.launchArguments`, `permissions` to `app.permissions`, `relaunch` to `app.open()`. A non-string first argument and any other unknown option fail too.
- `device.openApp(app, { launchArguments })` without `relaunch` left a running app with its old arguments. This form is now **deprecated**. It still sends the arguments and prints a `DeprecationWarning` (`E2E_MOBILE_OPEN_APP_ARGUMENTS`) once per worker, following the CONTRIBUTING stability policy. An empty list doesn't warn.
- `device.openApp` rejects unknown options (Detox's `launchArgs` names `launchArguments`) and non-array `launchArguments` (a string used to be spread into characters).

The checks live in `packages/mobile/src/device-options.ts` and only the `device` fixture runs them. The agent's `open_app` tool and `restart`/`reset` build their own options and skip them. Each API has one hints map in front of `rejectUnknownOptions`. I didn't extend core's `rejectUnknownOptions` with hints: using a new `e2e/engine` parameter would raise `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s `e2e` peer floor. The `launchArguments` array check stays separate from core's config check (`config/app.ts`) for the same reason: that helper isn't exported.

No install-time arguments were added. e2e and agent-device set no process environment variables. The docs say so and link to `app.environment`'s config entry.

Also fixed: the `installApp` step label printed `[object Object]` when a test passed an object first.

Docs: `docs/mobile.mdx` shows the install-then-`app.open()` flow with `appPath` + `launchArguments`. `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` documents the deprecation and the new `INVALID_ARGUMENT` cases and keeps the JSDoc copies in sync. `docs/reference/config.mdx#environment` gets the process-env note, and the skill reference gets one line.

## Issue

No public issue. User report.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. iOS 26.5 simulator, Settings app, built packages, launch args read from `ps` via the `simctl spawn launchctl list` pid.

- Before the change: `-E2EProbe from-config` was in the process args after `app.open()`, `app.restart()`, and a no-args `openApp({ relaunch: true })`. `-E2EProbe per-launch` was there after `openApp({ relaunch: true, launchArguments })`. A foreground-only `openApp({ launchArguments: ['-E2EProbe', 'fg'] })` kept `from-config` with no error.
- After the change:
  - The happy path is unchanged.
  - Foreground `launchArguments` passes and prints `[E2E_MOBILE_OPEN_APP_ARGUMENTS] DeprecationWarning: device.openApp({ launchArguments }) without relaunch: true is deprecated ...`.
  - `installApp('./x.app', { permissions })` fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT: device.installApp options has no key "permissions"; an install launches nothing: set the target's app.permissions, or call device.openApp(app, { relaunch: true, permissions })`.
  - `installApp({ launchArguments })` fails with `device.installApp takes the build's path first, then { app, reinstall }`, and its trace step reads `device.installApp appPath`.
- `pnpm check` passes. `@e2e-dev/mobile` unit tests pass (504).
- Not run on a physical iPhone. agent-device refuses launch arguments on XCTest-only (non-CoreDevice) iPhones, as `docs/mobile.mdx` already says.

## Checklist

- [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.
- [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
- [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures.
- [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: docs(migrate): add an Appium migration guide
body:
## What and why

- New guide `docs/migrate/appium.mdx` ("From Appium"). Before this, the migrate overview and the `migrate-to-e2e` skill said Appium had no guide and pointed to Detox and Maestro for a partial mapping.
- The guide maps each part of Appium (server, drivers, capabilities, sessions, selectors, element and `mobile:` commands, expect-webdriverio, runner) to e2e targets, `app`, `device`, `screen`, `expect`, and agent steps. It has before/after examples for login (find, tap, type, assert), permissions plus a deep link, and CI, then a migration checklist and a list of what has no direct equivalent.
- Uses the same gap markers as the Detox and Maestro guides: "Not yet" means e2e doesn't have it today, "No equivalent" means it's left out on purpose (XPath, image selectors, session reuse). The `migrate-to-e2e` skill reads both as gaps.
- I checked every e2e call against `packages/mobile/src` and the reference pages. The full e2e files live in `docs/examples/appium/`, so `check-docs-examples` and the docs typecheck cover them. A second fresh-context pass checked each claim against source and the Appium/WebdriverIO docs. It found a removed command (`driver.reset()`), the clipboard base64 difference, driver-specific `mobile:` names, `~` meaning a content description on Android, and several overclaims (`press` keys, `pressSequentially` appending, `closeApp` ending the session, `foregroundApp` on iOS). All of these are fixed.
