title: feat(e2b): run Android and web targets in E2B sandboxes
body:
## What and why - New package `@e2e-dev/e2b`: run targets in [E2B](https://e2b.dev) sandboxes, as agreed in #1414. - `e2b()`: a device provider for the mobile engine. Android 16 on E2B's public `android-16` template, one sandbox per worker slot. The `.apk` is installed through agent-device, like `device.installApp()`. - `e2bBrowsers()` from `@e2e-dev/e2b/web`: a browser provider for the web engine. Chromium in a sandbox per worker slot, or per attempt. - Sandboxes refuse public traffic. A loopback tunnel on the runner (`packages/e2b/src/tunnel.ts`) adds E2B's traffic token, because the web engine connects with a CDP URL alone and agent-device's client sends no custom header. A lease holds only `127.0.0.1:`, so the token never reaches a lease, log, or report. - The browser template is built once per E2B team from the Playwright image `@e2e-dev/web` pins. The docs page has the 8-line script. ```mermaid flowchart LR R[e2e runner] -->|127.0.0.1| T[loopback tunnel] T -->|HTTPS + traffic token| E[E2B edge] E --> A[agent-device proxy
Android sandbox] E --> C[Chromium DevTools
browser sandbox] ``` ```ts engine: mobile({ platform: 'android', device: e2b() }) engine: web({ browser: e2bBrowsers() }) ``` ## Issue Fixes #1414 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Live E2B sandboxes, `e2e run` against the built packages: Android 16 installs Privacy Friendly 2048 from an `.apk`, launches it, and swipes; Chromium browses Wikipedia in worker and attempt scope, and reads a download back. No sandbox is left running after a run. - The video is the live demo: a chat page where each message is an `agent.act` step on the same sandbox, Android first, then Chromium. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc294a02-f8f9-4bc2-a9b7-b94fba571f00 ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(web): answer native dialogs an agent step's action opens
body:
An agent never sees a native `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt`, or leave-page dialog: they sit outside the page. With no `browser.onDialog` handler, the web engine dismissed each one and failed the next operation with `INVALID_STATE`. So an agent step could not leave a form with unsaved changes or confirm a delete, live or from the replay cache.

- `DialogRouter` asks its surface whether an agent step made the newest action (`packages/web/src/dialogs.ts`). If so, a dialog no handler takes is answered: alerts, confirms, and leave-page dialogs are accepted, and a prompt is dismissed, since the agent never sees its text. The app log gets one `system` line, such as `confirm dialog "Delete this label?" accepted for the agent`.
- Ownership moves only on actions. `PlaywrightSurface.guardAction()` (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`) wraps every operation that acts: navigation, input, `browser.evaluate`, keyboard, mouse, `browser.setViewport`, `browser.emulateMedia`. It claims the dialog once the operation runs, so one refused by a pending error claims nothing. Reads (`observe`, `locate`, screenshots) and a route handler's `route.fetch` never take a dialog. So a test's own late dialog still fails its next step while an agent judgment polls, and a test route handler fetching mid-action can't steal the agent's dialog.
- `OperationContext.agentStep` (new, optional) marks an agent step's operations, replays included (`packages/e2e/src/agent/phases.ts`). Replayed actions keep `origin: 'test'` for settling, so without it a recorded dialog step failed under `--strict-cache`. It crosses the engine protocol. An older core omits it and the engine falls back to `origin`.
- A dialog a test's own step opens behaves as before: dismissed, and the next step fails with `INVALID_STATE`. A registered handler always wins.
- `docs/reference/web.mdx` said an unhandled dialog throws `APP_NOT_OPEN`. The code throws `INVALID_STATE`, so the table now says that.
- The web benchmark gets an agent scenario on `/e/deferred-dialog`, whose confirm opens 900 ms after the click, with its committed recording.

## Why

In 201 `e2e explore` runs on 0.22.0 against a self-hosted Gitea (their `report.json` and AI traces):

- 226 agent observations and actions failed with `unhandled beforeunload dialog`.
- 114 `navigate` calls failed with `net::ERR_ABORTED`. 113 of them were the dismissed leave-page dialog.
- 59 steps ended blocked. The model saw only `Action failed: unhandled beforeunload dialog:` and retried `back` until the step timed out.

## For review

- **Confirms are accepted.** The agent's action asked for the destructive step and the agent can't see the dialog to decline it. That also removes the app's last guard if an explorer clicks "Delete workspace" against its instructions. The alternative is to dismiss confirms, tell the model the text, and give it an explicit way to accept, which needs a model-visible notice channel first.
- **The model and MCP callers don't see the app log line.** An MCP action's test line registers no handler, so the docs and the MCP skill now say a scripted test of that flow needs `browser.onDialog`. `run_code` is test code, so its dialogs still fail the next call. Surfacing answered dialogs in action results is a follow-up.
- **Porting to #1503:** a trial cherry-pick onto its head conflicts only in `driver/dialogs.ts` imports. `BidiSession` builds the router there and would pass the same two callbacks, and its action entry points would take `guardAction`'s ownership line.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `packages/web/tests/integration/agent-dialogs.test.ts`, real Chromium, 8 cases: an agent leaves a dirty form; agent confirm, alert, and prompt; a replayed agent action (`origin: 'test'`, `agentStep: true`); a test route handler's `route.fetch` before the agent's alert; a test's `setViewport` whose resize handler confirms after an agent tap, which must fail the test's next step; a test action refused by a pending route error, which must leave the agent's alert with the agent; a test's 300 ms delayed confirm while agent reads poll, which must still fail with `INVALID_STATE`; and a test's own confirm. On main, both live agent cases fail with `unhandled ... dialog`. The viewport and refused-action cases fail without their fixes.
- Web benchmark, `tests-agent` `deferred-dialog`: recorded live once, then replayed twice with `CI=1 --strict-cache`: `Cache 1 replayed`, no model call, and the app log shows `confirm dialog "Really submit the report?" accepted for the agent`.
- The whole web benchmark agent suite under `--strict-cache`, with the same counts on main for the existing recordings:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tests | 33 passed | 34 passed (+ `deferred-dialog`) |
| Cache | 26 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed | 27 replayed · 2 handed off · 4 missed |

- Testbed `tests/dialog.e2e.ts` and `tests/dialogs-frames.e2e.ts` (15 tests) and web benchmark `tests/native-dialogs.e2e.ts` and `tests/deferred-dialog.e2e.ts` (4 tests) pass, so scripted handlers behave as before.
- `e2e explore` (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `--max-steps 4`) on a scratch notes app with a leave-page guard on its editor and a `confirm()` before each delete. Its delete removes the wrong note, a planted bug:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steps | 3 of 4, all blocked, ended "steps kept failing" | 4 of 4, the step limit was reached |
| Failed agent actions | 7 (`unhandled beforeunload dialog`) | 0 |
| Planted delete bug | not reached | found: "Deleting Trip plan removes Groceries instead" |
| Cost | $0.0107 | $0.0106 |

- Agentic repro tests against the same app (`e2e run --tag bugbash`):

| Repro | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delete removes the chosen note (real bug) | `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`: blocked by the confirm | `ASSERTION_FAILED`: confirmed |
| Leaving the editor unsaved keeps the list (not a bug) | `ACTION_FAILED`: blocked by the leave-page dialog | passes |

title: feat(agent): sample files the agent can upload
body: The `upload` tool told the model to use project-relative paths, "e.g. fixtures/photo.png". Few projects keep such a file, so `agent.act` and `e2e explore` guessed that example, got `no file at ...`, and skipped every upload flow: avatars, attachments, imports. - `upload` takes six small files e2e ships: `sample:photo.png`, `sample:photo.jpg`, `sample:document.pdf`, `sample:notes.txt`, `sample:table.csv`, and `sample:empty.txt` (`packages/e2e/src/agent/sample-files.ts`). The tool description lists them instead of the made-up example, for when the step names no file. - They're e2e's own bytes, written once per process to a temporary directory and removed at exit. A `sample:` path never resolves against the project root and only an exact name is accepted, so it reads no project or user file. Project paths keep every existing check. - A missing project file is still `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and doesn't offer a sample, so a step whose fixture is missing fails instead of passing on the wrong file. An unknown sample name lists the samples. - An `e2e mcp` upload of a sample prints `No test line:`, since `setInputFiles` in a test takes a project file. - The trace cache keeps the path as given, so a replay attaches the same sample. ```ts await agent.act('upload a profile picture and check that it shows'); // the model attaches sample:photo.png when the step names no file ``` ## Why In 201 `e2e explore` runs on 0.22.0 against a self-hosted Gitea, 55 blocked or failed steps and 23 more passed steps ended without testing an upload because no file was available. The explorers' own summaries said, for example, "No test image was supplied and fixtures/photo.png was unavailable". ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `e2e explore` (`openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, `--max-steps 3`) on a scratch profile page whose avatar upload stores every file as 0 bytes, a planted bug. One run on main, two on this branch: | | main | this branch, run 1 | this branch, run 2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Uploads | none: "no image fixture was available" | 3 (`sample:photo.png`, `sample:photo.jpg`) | 4 | | Steps | 1 passed, 2 blocked | 3 passed | 2 passed, 1 blocked | | Planted 0-byte bug | not reached | not reported (reported a missing preview instead) | found: "Profile accepts a zero-byte file as the current avatar" | | Cost | $0.0098 | $0.0121 | $0.0121 | ```text upload "sample:photo.png" to button "Avatar image" upload "sample:photo.jpg" to button "Avatar image" policy upload.path allowed ``` - The PDF sample is byte-identical to a reference that `file` reads as a one-page PDF 1.4. The PNG and JPEG decode as valid 32 by 32 images, and the JPEG has no metadata.

title: mobile: device.setPermission sends an unknown permission name or state to the device instead of failing with INVALID_ARGUMENT
test: cli-doctor's "config still loading at Ctrl-C" case flakes with exit code null under load
body:
`packages/e2e/tests/integration/cli-doctor.test.ts`, "reports a config still loading at Ctrl-C as cancelled", sends SIGINT on a fixed `setTimeout(..., 2000)`.
On a busy machine the CLI has not armed its Ctrl-C handler (`SignalLadder.arm()` in `src/cli/index.ts`) after 2 seconds, so the default SIGINT action kills it and the test sees exit code `null` instead of `130`.
The fixture's `process.stderr.write('loading')` can't serve as a ready signal: the CLI holds what a config prints while it loads (`ConfigLoadHold`), so that line never reaches the test.
Repro: `pnpm build`, start 40 `yes > /dev/null` loops, then run `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/integration/cli-doctor.test.ts -t 'config still loading'` 20 times. On a 10-core Mac, 1 of 20 runs failed with `AssertionError: expected null to be 130`. PR #1519's body reports the same failure on Ubuntu.

title: fix(mobile): validate device.setPermission's name and state before the device call
body: ## What and why - `device.openApp({ permissions })` checks permission names and states, but `device.setPermission` sent them straight to agent-device, so `'camra'` failed as `ENGINE_FAILURE` ("settings permission requires a target: ..."). - `setPermission` now runs the same check first: a bad name (naming the nearest one), a bad state, or a missing state is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, and no device command is sent. - The reference gets a Throws table for `setPermission`. ## Issue Fixes #1603 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - built CLI on an iPhone 16 simulator (iOS 18.5), scratch target on `com.apple.Preferences`, plus `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile run test` and `pnpm check`. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `setPermission('camra', 'grant')` | `ENGINE_FAILURE: permission camra grant failed: settings permission requires a target: all\|camera\|...` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: device.setPermission has unknown key "camra"; did you mean "camera"?` | | `setPermission('camera', 'allow')` | `ENGINE_FAILURE: ... Invalid permission state: allow. Use ...` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: device.setPermission.camera must be one of grant, deny, reset, got "allow"` | | `setPermission('camera', 'reset')` | passes | passes | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(mobile): skip keyboard dismissal the capture measured away
body: ## Issue Fixes #1560 ## What changed - `dismissKeyboard` now takes a fresh capture before sending input and does nothing when the producer measured no keyboard on screen: an explicit `absent` fact, or a `visible`/`derived` frame lying entirely outside the viewport (`keyboardMeasuredAway` in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`). The viewport falls back to `viewportOf(nodes)` when the capture omits it, the same inference `projectSnapshot` uses. - Keyboard states the producer cannot measure (`unmeasurable`, `visibility-only`, `tree-rejected`, missing fact) keep the native `command.keyboard({ action: 'dismiss' })`, and the gesture fallback still takes its own fresh look, so an unknown first capture cannot short-circuit it. - When nothing is open yet (`INVALID_STATE` on an unmanaged session), the capture reads as empty and the call falls through to the native dismissal instead of failing or silently skipping. - Docs (`docs/reference/mobile.mdx`, `Device.dismissKeyboard`) and a patch changeset for `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The issue's controlled reproduction (scripted agent-device client through the built CLI, no simulator), run against this branch's `dist`: ```text RUN e2e v0.22.0 packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/keyboard-dismiss run 01a1ac6c-6e8a-735e-80e4-75c2a52a21c3 · targets: absent, offscreen ✓ |absent| dismiss.e2e.ts > dismissing an absent or off-screen keyboard sends no input to the form 30ms ✓ |offscreen| dismiss.e2e.ts > dismissing an absent or off-screen keyboard sends no input to the form 29ms Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Same fixture, `surface.ts` from `origin/main`: both targets fail — `command.keyboard` flips the scripted form to `Changed`, then `ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeVisible` on `Unchanged` | Both targets pass; no keyboard command or swipe is sent | - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile test:unit`: 501 tests pass, including 7 new cases in `dismissing a keyboard the capture measured away` (absent, below-viewport `visible`, above-viewport `derived`, intersecting frame keeps dismissal, `unmeasurable` keeps dismissal, node-inferred viewport, gesture fallback after an unknown state). - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm docs:check`: clean.

title: web: launch Chromium with the sandbox on (agent can navigate off-origin)
body:
## Summary

`@e2e-dev/web` launches Chromium without `chromiumSandbox`. Playwright's default for that option is `false`, so every browser process gets `--no-sandbox`. There is no config option to turn it on.

- `packages/web/src/browser-connection.ts:71`: `type.launch({ headless: !headed, timeout: timeoutMs, ...RUNNER_OWNS_SIGNALS })`
- `playwright-core` (1.64.1 and 1.65.0) adds `--no-sandbox` whenever `options.chromiumSandbox !== true`.

For plain Playwright tests against a trusted localhost app, that default is a reasonable trade-off. e2e is different, because the docs say: "There is no origin allowlist: the agent can follow the app to another site" (`docs/security.mdx`, `SECURITY.md`). A page the agent reaches can be off-origin or user content rendered by the app under test. If that page exploits a renderer bug, the OS sandbox doesn't contain it. It then runs as the user running `e2e run`, with the checkout, `.env`, model keys and so on.

This is timely: Playwright 1.64.1 (pinned by `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.5`, the current latest on npm) bundles Chromium 156.0.8078.4, which predates the late-October 2026 Chrome security fixes (e.g. CVE-2026-118306). Thanks for #1609, which bumps to 1.65.0 / Chromium 158. Once 0.15.6 is published, that covers the known CVEs. The sandbox default stays the same, though, and it's the layer that protects against the next renderer bug.

## Suggestion

1. Launch with `chromiumSandbox: true` by default.
2. Add an explicit opt-out for hosts where the sandbox can't start: root, containers, or Ubuntu 23.10+ with `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`. For example, a `web({ ... })` option or an env var. Playwright's error there is "Chromium sandboxing failed!", which the docs could point to the opt-out from.
3. Mention it in the security docs next to the "no origin allowlist" note.
4. Minor: `packages/smol/src/provider.ts:194` starts Chrome with `--no-sandbox` inside the smol VM. That's presumably intended, since the VM is the boundary. Worth confirming, given the docs note that smol VMs "reach every loopback port on the machine".

## What we checked

We made this change in our plain-Playwright suite: `launchOptions: { chromiumSandbox: true }`. During a run, no Chromium process carried `--no-sandbox` (without the option, all of them did). All tests pass, with no other changes on a normal Linux desktop.

title: fix: page a list that appends at the end, and retry a screenshot after navigation
body: Two failures on main, both a timer that returned before the page had caught up. - `scroll_to({ text })` treated two polls of an unchanged screen as the end of the list. On the Playwright 1.65 runner, the web agent recording for infinite-scroll died there: 13 screens, stopped at item 60 while "Loading more" was still up, `REPLAY_STALE` (`action-failed`, `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`). An unchanged page is re-read for a second after the first held-still look, so an append that lands in that second keeps the paging going. `docs/reference/agent.mdx`. - `app.screenshot` already retries when the document is replaced, but only after `framenavigated` has been delivered. Node 24's spec job rejected `page.screenshot` with "Execution context was destroyed" before that event, so the shot failed instead of capturing the new document. The capture waits up to 250ms for the event, then takes the new document. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes The new tests failed on the old code and pass on this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `scroll_to` of a page that turns 400ms after the swipe: `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` in 378ms | passes, 2 swipes, finds Row 7 | | screenshot whose `framenavigated` arrives on the next macrotask: `ENGINE_FAILURE` | masked capture, `page.screenshot` called twice | ```text $ pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/agent-scroll-pages.test.ts tests/integration/agent-scroll-settle.test.ts tests/integration/agent-scroll-smooth.test.ts Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 20 passed (20) $ pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/screenshot-navigation.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 6 passed (6) ``` Also green: e2e and web unit tests, the web integration suite (383 passed, 1 skipped), lint, typecheck for both packages, dead-code, changeset bumps, docs anchors and mdx. title: feat(e2e): run the CLI on Bun 1.4.3 and newer, without Node.js
body:
The e2e CLI runs on Bun 1.4.3 or newer with no Node.js installed: `bunx --bun e2e run`. Node.js behavior does not change. ## What changed - **Loader.** e2e's Node.js loader runs on `module.registerHooks`, which Bun lacks ([oven-sh/bun#35690](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/35690) is a draft). On Bun, e2e registers no hooks. Bun compiles TypeScript and resolves tsconfig `paths` and `#` imports itself ([`config/bun-loader.ts`](packages/e2e/src/config/bun-loader.ts)). - **Fresh instances.** Bun ignores the query e2e uses on Node.js to key module instances. So the loader deletes the module from `require.cache`, which holds ES modules too, and imports it again. A fresh graph also reloads every project file the entry imports by path, `#` import, or tsconfig alias. `Bun.Transpiler.scanImports` and `Bun.resolveSync` find those files. - **Redaction.** Bun's `console` writes past the `process.stdout.write` that e2e patches to redact secrets and route output. The loader points `console` at the streams before any project code runs. - **One run per process.** Bun runs an imported module's top level outside its importer's AsyncLocalStorage context, and holds one instance of each module per process. Two runs in one process can't be kept apart, so on Bun: - `e2e/runner` throws `NODE_UNSUPPORTED`. It already did, because of the missing hooks. - `e2e mcp` opens one session at a time. - **Version guard.** A Bun older than 1.4.3 gets the version to upgrade to: Bun 1.4.2 races a `require()` of an ES module whose graph waits on top-level await. Deno is still refused. - **Fixes Bun exposed:** - The signal ladder trusts `process.connected` only when there is an IPC channel (`cli/signals.ts`). - Stack frames may have no column (`collect/registry.ts`). - Config errors read Bun's syntax and resolve error shapes (`config/diagnose.ts`). - **Init.** In a Bun project, `e2e init` registers the MCP server with `bunx`. - **CI.** A `bun` job runs `tests/integration/bun-runtime.test.ts` on Bun 1.4.3 and on the latest Bun. The CLI, and everything it spawns, gets a PATH with no `node` on it. ```mermaid flowchart LR L[load a config or test file] --> R{runtime} R -- Node.js --> N["registerHooks + oxc
an instance per ?e2e-graph= query"] R -- Bun --> B["Bun compiles it
delete from require.cache, import again"] ``` [CLI reference, Bun](https://e2e.com/docs/reference/cli#bun) lists what still differs on Bun: - `#` imports that map to a directory. - Legacy decorators in `.cts` files. - Watch mode and MCP read `tsconfig.json` and computed-path imports one time. - `executable: 'node'` under `bun `. - The line reported for a test that a helper declares after an `await`. The mobile engine and the integrations are not verified on Bun yet. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - **Released e2e vs this branch:** `e2e --version` on Bun 1.4.4, with only Bun and git on PATH. | e2e 0.23.0 from npm | this branch | | --- | --- | | `e2e runs on Node.js: Bun 1.4.4 reports Node.js 26.3.0 but has no module.registerHooks, which e2e's TypeScript loader needs.` (exit 2) | `0.23.0`. Then `e2e doctor` on the testbed prints `✓ node Bun 1.4.4 (>=1.4.3)` and `e2e run can start here` | - **Testbed on Bun:** the built CLI on Bun 1.4.4, run with `env -i PATH=:/usr/bin:/bin bun run e2e run`. Same totals as on Node.js 24.19: ```text Test Files 47 passed (47) Tests 587 passed | 1 skipped (588) Duration 23.41s ``` - **`e2e mcp --max-sessions 3` on Bun:** it logs that the flag is ignored. A second `open_session` gets `no session slot is free (e2e mcp --max-sessions 1)`. - **Reverting fixes:** each Bun test added for a loader or MCP fix fails with its fix reverted. That covers reloading a JSX `.js` file and a data file in a fresh graph, query imports, dotted aliases, console redaction, and the one-session cap.

title: Support running the e2e CLI and test workers on Bun
body:
### Problem

We want to run our browser tests with Bun as the JavaScript runtime, alongside our Bun-based application and source tests. Installing e2e with Bun works, but executing the CLI with Bun currently requires switching back to Node.js.

Reproduced in a fresh directory with only `e2e@0.23.0` as a dev dependency (the current npm latest), on Linux x64:

```sh
mkdir e2e-bun-repro
cd e2e-bun-repro
bun add --dev e2e@0.23.0

bun node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js --version
# exit 2

node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js --version
# 0.23.0
# exit 0
```

Bun output:

```text
e2e runs on Node.js: Bun 1.4.4 reports Node.js 26.3.0 but has no module.registerHooks, which e2e's TypeScript loader needs. Run the CLI with Node.js: npx e2e, or bunx e2e (without --bun).
```

Environment:

- Bun: 1.4.4; `typeof require("node:module").registerHooks === "undefined"`
- Node.js control: 26.13.0; the same property is a function
- e2e: 0.23.0
- No project config, test file, browser, or model credentials are needed to reproduce this startup rejection.

The runtime check intentionally rejects this environment, so this is a request for Bun runtime support.

### Proposed API

Support the existing CLI and configuration when explicitly launched with Bun:

```sh
bun node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.config.ts
# equivalently, through the package binary:
bun run --bun e2e run --config e2e.config.ts
```

No new test/config syntax would be needed. Select a Bun-compatible loading path when running under Bun, while preserving the existing Node loading path. The Bun path would need to cover config/test/helper TypeScript loading and resolution without relying on Node's `module.registerHooks`, and spawned test workers would use the same selected runtime.

The runtime guard should admit Bun only after that path works; retaining correct discovery, worker cleanup, and reporting is part of the requested support.

### Upsides

- Projects using Bun can run their ordinary browser suite without provisioning a second JavaScript runtime specifically for e2e.
- Existing tests, engine integrations, and config can remain reusable.
- Runtime selection is explicit through the executable used to launch the CLI.

### Downsides

- A second loader/runtime path adds maintenance and CI coverage.
- Bun and Node differ in module resolution, CommonJS/ESM interoperability, native addon loading, and subprocess behavior.
- Bun's built-in TypeScript support alone does not establish compatibility with e2e's loading and worker contracts.

### Alternatives

We currently run e2e with Node.js. That works, but retains the extra runtime in local development and CI. Waiting for Bun to implement the required Node loading APIs is another option; even then, the full runner would need compatibility validation.

### Which surface

CLI runtime support, internal config/test loading, worker startup, and documentation. Existing SDK/config/engine/report formats should stay compatible.

### Compatibility and validation

- Existing Node execution should continue to work unchanged.
- Validate config and helper imports, discovery/filtering, a deterministic Web engine test, worker shutdown on success/failure/cancellation, and report generation under Bun.
- The minimal reproduction above only establishes the startup blocker; it does not establish that all later runner behavior is already compatible.

title: fix(web): launch Chromium with its sandbox on where it can start
body:
## Issue

Fixes #1613.

- `@e2e-dev/web` launched Chromium without `chromiumSandbox`, so Playwright added `--no-sandbox` to every browser process.
- The agent can follow the app to another origin, so a renderer exploit on a page it reaches ran unsandboxed as the user running `e2e run`.

## What changed

- A locally launched Chromium runs with its OS sandbox on by default on macOS and Windows.
- On Linux the default stays off. The sandbox needs unprivileged user namespaces there, which root, most containers, and Ubuntu 23.10+ block, so on would fail the launch on most CI hosts.
- `web({ chromiumSandbox })` sets it either way: `true` on a Linux host that can sandbox, `false` elsewhere.
- A sandbox that is on and cannot start fails with an `ENGINE_FAILURE` that names the option, in place of Playwright's launch call log.
- `connect`, browser providers, Firefox and WebKit are untouched.

```ts
web({ chromiumSandbox: true }); // default: true on macOS and Windows, false on Linux
```

- `packages/web/src/browser-connection.ts`: `defaultChromiumSandbox()`, and `acquire` takes an options object.
- Docs: `docs/reference/web.mdx`, `docs/security.mdx` (plus `ja` and `zh`), `SECURITY.md`, the skill's `setup.md`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed, `e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts` on macOS, watching the Chromium the CLI spawned:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| browser process carries `--no-sandbox` | default: no `--no-sandbox`, renderers start with `--seatbelt-client`; 7 passed |
| no option to change it | `web({ chromiumSandbox: false })`: `--no-sandbox` is back; 7 passed |

- Web integration suite on macOS, now sandboxed by default: 484 passed, 1 skipped.
- Not run: `chromiumSandbox: true` on a Linux host that allows user namespaces. Linux CI runs the default, which is the same launch as main.

title: fix(acp): retry a failed session directory removal after the agent exits
body: Fixes #1623. On Windows, teardown() sent SIGTERM to the agent and then removed its session directory at once. Windows refuses to remove a directory while a process still has it as its working directory, so rmSync threw EPERM synchronously and took the worker down with WORKER_CRASH. Because the test never passed, no recording was saved, so every rerun burned another model call. The directory is now removed at once, and retried after the agent exits when the first removal fails. On POSIX the first removal usually succeeds while the agent is still stopping, so a worker exiting right after the attempt leaves nothing behind; on Windows a process the agent started in the directory still holds it, so the removal fails there and waits for the exit. A failed removal never throws: a leftover temp directory is harmless. ## Verified - 2 regression tests in packages/acp/tests/executor.test.ts: the removal is retried after the agent exits when the first try fails (forced by a file in a read-only directory), and on POSIX the directory is gone at once while the agent is still alive. The new immediate-path test fails on the remove-only-after-exit code (red verified) and passes with the fix. Both are skipped on Windows, where Node terminates the child immediately for SIGTERM and the delay handler cannot run, so they check the ordering on POSIX only. The fallback test also skips as root, where a read-only directory does not block removal. - packages/acp executor tests 33/33 pass; full acp suite 36/39. The 3 cli.test.ts failures are pre-existing and unrelated: identical on clean origin/main, caused by Chromium refusing to launch as root without --no-sandbox in this sandbox; they should pass in CI. - typecheck clean, oxlint clean. - The Windows EPERM itself cannot reproduce on Linux (POSIX allows removing a live process's cwd), and no CI workflow runs on Windows, so the EPERM path itself is unverified.

title: perf(agent): wait 1 s, not 2 s, after a caret key in a focused text field
body:
- After `press` or `pressKey`, a settled look waits up to 2 s (`FULL_CHANGE_WAIT_MS`) for the tree to change shape. A caret key (ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End, Control/Meta+a, with Shift or Control) in a `textbox` or `searchbox` that already holds the focus usually changes nothing the tree records, so the whole window was spent.
- That wait is now 1 s (`HELD_STILL_MS`) for those keys: `changeWaitAfter` in `packages/core/src/agent/settle-policy.ts`. The first version used 150 ms; review showed a `selectionchange` handler that reveals a toolbar 700 ms later was missed, so the window now covers it.
- Kept at 2 s: taps, the first key or tap that gives a field the focus, `combobox`, Alt chords, Tab and the vertical keys, and every other action.
- `armChange` (`packages/core/src/agent/observation-feed.ts`) keeps the later deadline when a window is still pending. Without it, `tap(Save)` then `pressKey('End')` in one turn would cut the tap's 2 s window. `focusedNode()` returns a node only when exactly one node has the focus.
- Known limit: a handler that updates the tree more than 1 s after the key is read on the next look, as after any action with a window shorter than its delay.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Surface: the web benchmark's `tests-agent/` replay with `--strict-cache`, through `pnpm bench:ab --config e2e.agent.config.ts` against the merge base (`e27f492c`), 6 pairs in random order.
- The 7 tests that call the model on a replay (3 planted-bug judgments, 4 `act completes …` scenarios) are left out of `bench:ab` with `--grep-invert`, since their model calls differ between runs. They ran once on the 150 ms version of this branch with a key (`CI=1 e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --ai-trace`, recordings read-only): 33 tests passed, no `REPLAY_STALE`. On this head CI's `web agent` job ran them with a key: 33 passed, 20 model calls. The `--no-cache` path was not run.
- Behavior: every test ran the same steps with the same outcome (status, cache mode, replayed actions) on every run of both builds.

| Metric | main | this branch | change (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| wall (process) | 68.71 s | 62.86 s | -9.0% (-11.4% to -5.8%) |
| suite (sum of attempts) | 67.52 s | 61.67 s | -9.2% (-11.6% to -5.9%) |
| observe (events) | 38.70 s | 32.78 s | -15.3% (-15.6% to -15.0%) |
| action (events) | 25.89 s | 25.64 s | same (-7.8% to +6.4%) |
| `act completes rich-text-editor` | 20.49 s | 14.58 s | -28.9% (-29.3% to -28.4%) |

- Review regression test: `tests/integration/agent-caret-settle.test.ts` has a fake-engine popup that opens 700 ms after `press` and after `pressKey` on a focused field. Both cases fail at the 150 ms window and pass at 1 s. The same file keeps a first tap, a tap on the focused field, a caret key before the field held the focus, and a batched tap then key at the full window.
- After merging main (the agent moved into `@e2e-dev/core`, #1737): e2e unit 3707 pass, agent integration 228 pass, `pnpm check` exit 0. title: iOS: `fill()` on a React Native `secureTextEntry` field next to a show/hide toggle fails with "No focused text input" and presses the toggle (follow-up to #872)
body:
## Summary

On an iOS simulator, `fill()` into a React Native `secureTextEntry` field fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE: perform fill failed: No focused text input was available for typing.` It fails the same way with a credential password and with a plain string. After the failure, the field's show/hide toggle has been pressed, so the field now shows plain text.

This is the second half of #872. The bullet-only verification error that #872 reported is gone for us, but the toggle press that #872 also noted still happens, and `fill` now fails before verification. `type_secret` in `agent.act` goes through the same `fill`, so a password sign-in on iOS can't succeed. A model-driven step then makes it worse: it falls back to tapping "Show password", after which `type_secret` is refused with `POLICY_DENIED` because the field is no longer a password field.

`pressSequentially()` on the same field works, and the field stays secure.

## Environment

- e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.6, agent-device 0.21.36 (also reproduced with plain agent-device `0.21.37-nightly.20261108.152`)
- iOS 27.0 and iOS 26.3 simulators (iPhone 17 Pro), Xcode 27.1, macOS
- React Native 0.86.3, Expo SDK 57, Release build for the simulator

## Reproduction

The password field is a standard `TextInput` in a row, with the toggle as a sibling to its right:

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center' }}>
  <TextInput style={{ flex: 1 }} placeholder="••••••••" secureTextEntry={!visible} />
  <View style={{ paddingRight: 16 }}>
    <TouchableOpacity
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={visible ? 'Ukryj hasło' : 'Pokaż hasło'} // Hide / Show password
      onPress={() => setVisible(v => !v)}
      hitSlop={8}
    >
      <Ionicons name={visible ? 'eye-off' : 'eye'} size={20} />
    </TouchableOpacity>
  </View>
</View>
```

The tree reports the field correctly as secure. From agent-device's snapshot:

```
TextField        "you@example.com"  rect x21 y365 w360 h19   editable, password:false
SecureTextField  "••••••••"         rect x21 y449 w324 h19   editable, password:true
Button "Pokaż hasło"                rect x345 y448 w20 h21
```

Test, from a signed-out start (`app.clearState()` + `device.clearKeychain()`), with no agent steps:

```ts
test('A: fill', async ({ screen }) => {
  const user = credentials.user('athlete');
  await screen.getByPlaceholder('you@example.com').fill(user.username);   // ok
  await screen.getByPlaceholder('••••••••').fill(user.password);          // fails
});

test('B: pressSequentially', async ({ screen }) => {
  const user = credentials.user('athlete');
  await screen.getByPlaceholder('you@example.com').fill(user.username);
  await screen.getByPlaceholder('••••••••').pressSequentially(process.env.E2E_USER_ATHLETE_PASSWORD ?? '');
  await expect(screen.getByLabel('Pokaż hasło')).toBeVisible();           // still secure
  await screen.getByText(/^Zaloguj się$/).last().tap();
  await expect(screen.getByText('Dziś i jutro')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 }); // signed in
});
```

```
× A: fill  16.98s
  → ENGINE_FAILURE: perform fill failed: No focused text input was available for typing.
✓ B: pressSequentially  16.28s
```

A's sign-in tap and Home check are left out here, since it never gets that far. A plain string also fails when passed to agent-device's own `fill` (below), so it isn't specific to secrets.

The same thing happens with plain agent-device, outside e2e:

```sh
agent-device fill @e6 "probe@example.com"   # email: "Filled 17 chars"
agent-device fill @e8 "dummy-pass-123"      # secure field: TEXT_INPUT_NOT_FOCUSED
agent-device snapshot -i
# @e8 [text-field] "••••••••" [focused] [editable]   <- was [securetextfield]
# @e9 [button] "Ukryj hasło"                          <- toggle got pressed

# fresh launch:
agent-device press @e8
agent-device type "dummy-pass-123"          # "Typed 14 chars", field stays [securetextfield]
```

Runner log for the failing `fill`:

```
AGENT_DEVICE_RUNNER_TEXT_ENTRY_FOCUS evidence=input-reports-keyboard-focus polls=1
... phase=focus durationMs=845.3 chars=14 mode=replacement
... phase=initial-resolve durationMs=0.0 chars=14 mode=replacement
... phase=clear durationMs=2972.5 chars=14 mode=replacement
(then TEXT_INPUT_NOT_FOCUSED)
```

## What we think happens

This is inferred from the log and the screen, not checked in the runner source.

Focus succeeds, and the failure follows the ~3 s `clear` phase of replacement mode. iOS blocks select-all on secure fields, so the clear probably falls back to a caret tap near the field's trailing edge (x ≈ 345). The toggle starts at x = 345, and with `hitSlop={8}` it reaches into the field, so the tap lands on the toggle. The app flips `secureTextEntry`, React Native swaps the native input, and the input the runner was holding focus on is gone, hence `TEXT_INPUT_NOT_FOCUSED`. `pressSequentially` (focus + `keyboard.type`) never clears, which is why it works.

## Expected

`fill()` with a credential password or a plain string enters the text into a secure field, the field stays secure, and no control next to the field is pressed.

Possible directions:
- Skip the clear phase when the field is empty (it shows only its placeholder, or the tree reports no value).
- For a `password: true` field, clear with a bounded run of deletes instead of select-all plus a caret tap.
- Keep any fallback caret tap inside the field's rect, inset from the edges, so it can't hit a neighbouring control.

## Workaround

`pressSequentially()` with the password as a plain string works. But it refuses a `Secret`, so the password loses redaction and can't be used through `credentials` or in `agent.act`. If `pressSequentially` could accept a `Secret` for a `password` field, that would also unblock this.

title: ResultStatus conflates "observed failure" with "missing observation" (timed-out / interrupted)
body:
Hi — while studying how different frameworks model verdicts, I noticed something in `packages/e2e/src/run/records.ts` that I think has a semantic cost in write-heavy flows:

```ts
export type ResultStatus = 'passed' | 'flaky' | 'failed' | 'timed-out' | 'interrupted' | 'skipped';
```

## The issue

`timed-out` and `interrupted` are grouped on the failure side (`FailedStatus`), but their epistemic state is different from `failed`:

- **failed** = "I observed the outcome, and it did not match the expectation."
- **timed-out / interrupted** = "I did **not** observe the outcome at all." The system under test may have already completed the action (side effects included).

Folding the second kind into the same bucket means a report's `failed` count mixes two things: observed mismatches and missing observations. The denominator is no longer clean — you can't tell "how many tests found real problems" from "how many tests never got to finish observing".

## Why this matters more for agent-driven flows

For read-only UI assertions, a timeout is usually safe to retry. But agents increasingly drive **write** operations (place an order, send a message, approve a request). There, a timeout followed by an automatic retry can duplicate the side effect — the second run is a real second order.

So the retry heuristic "failed → try again" is only safe when you know the attempt had no effect, and a timeout is precisely the case where you **can't** know.

## What we do in our project (agent-web)

We use a three-valued verdict instead:

- `pass` — every machine-checkable assertion held.
- `fail` — an assertion observed a mismatch.
- `unknown` — observation was missing: timeout, interruption, environment fault. **It stays in the denominator** (decidability = (pass+fail)/N), and unknown verdicts from write steps carry a "do not replay" flag, because replaying assumes the absent attempt had no side effect — which is exactly what a timeout refuses to guarantee.

We also surface a step-level distinction similar to your `blocked` (`StepVerdictStatus = 'passed' | 'failed' | 'blocked'`), but at the run/result level there's no counterpart today.

## Suggestion

Not asking for a design change to your retry model — just considering whether an explicit outcome like `unknown` / `no-observation` (distinct from `failed`) would be worth modeling, so downstream reports can separate "found a bug" from "never finished observing", and write-flow users can make replay-safety decisions from the verdict itself.

Happy to share more about our model if useful. Thanks for reading.

title: feat(agent): read computed styles in project tools
body:
## What and why

- A read-only project tool can measure computed CSS on a listed node, such as whether an error is red, through `getToolContext(options).read({ id }, { style })`.
- Only allow-listed properties of a node in the newest observation are read. Reads share the operation queue and step deadline, return secret-redacted values, and are denied to `mutates: true` tools.
- `ctx.read` throws the same agent codes as `ctx.observe` and `ctx.actions`: a detached or unlisted node is `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`, an engine without `readStyle` is `POLICY_DENIED`.
- Engines get an optional `readStyle(ref, properties, context)` member, `engine/readStyle` over JSON-RPC, and the `computed-style` capability. Web implements it; mobile does not. SPI and protocol versions stay 1.
- `e2e/engine` exports `COMPUTED_STYLE_PROPERTIES` and `validateComputedStyleProperties(properties)`. `@e2e-dev/web` calls the validator, so its `e2e` peer floor is `0.23.2`.

```ts
const context = getToolContext(executionOptions);
await context.observe();
const { style } = await context.read({ id: nodeId }, {
  style: ['color', 'font-weight', 'visibility', 'opacity'],
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Tool[Read-only project tool] --> ID[Node in newest observation]
  ID --> RPC[engine/readStyle]
  RPC --> CSS[getComputedStyle]
  CSS --> Redact[Redact values]
  Redact --> Tool
```

## Issue

Fixes #1228

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed, built CLI, scratch config with a scripted model and two project tools: `e2e run --config e2e.style-scratch.config.ts --video --reporter list,markdown`. The test signs in with bad credentials on `/login`, styles the alert, and the read-only tool measures it.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `context.read is not a function` | `rgb(255, 0, 0)`, `700`, and `<secret:tone>` for the opacity that matches a configured secret |

```text
 ✓ reads computed style through a project tool > agent.act "measure the error style and prove mutating reads are denied" 223ms · 3 model calls
 ✓ |web| tests-style-scratch/style.e2e.ts (1 test) 678ms ai 6 tokens
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

What the tools saw in that run:

```json
{
  "measured": { "style": { "color": "rgb(255, 0, 0)", "font-weight": "700", "opacity": "<secret:tone>" } },
  "unknownNode": "LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND",
  "badProperty": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
  "mutatingRead": "POLICY_DENIED"
}
```

- `grep -r` for the secret value under `.e2e/` finds nothing.
- Testbed suite on the built CLI: 588 passed, 1 skipped.

title: feat(browser-run): add Cloudflare hosted browsers
body:
[Cloudflare Browser Run](https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/) runs headless Chromium on Cloudflare's network. `@e2e-dev/browser-run` connects existing web tests to it.

```ts
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { browserRun } from '@e2e-dev/browser-run';

web({ browser: browserRun() });
web({ browser: browserRun({ scope: 'attempt' }) });
```

- Set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` with Browser Rendering - Edit permission. The app URL must be reachable from Cloudflare.
- Worker scope reuses a browser with an isolated context per attempt. Attempt scope leases a fresh browser per attempt and retry. The default inactivity timeout is ten minutes.
- CDP endpoints and handshake headers resolve together. Providers derive headers inside workers; credentials stay outside lease handoffs and page requests. `connect` also accepts `{ endpoint, headers }`.
- Screenshots, traces, and WebM screencasts work when enabled. Remote downloads and Cloudflare-native recording attachments are unsupported. History navigation can fail waiting for `load`; the separate navigation fix remains outside this PR.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[e2e runner] --> P[browserRun provider]
  P -->|create and delete sessions| C[Cloudflare Browser Run]
  R <-->|authenticated CDP| C
  C --> A[Public HTTPS app]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI against an HTTPS deployment of the actual testbed pages, with real Browser Run sessions, two workers, traces, and video. Ran both provider scopes with `node ../../packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --config e2e.browser-run.config.ts`; set `BROWSER_RUN_SCOPE=attempt` for the second run.
- Unfiltered runs: worker **21 passed, 1 failed**; attempt **14 passed, 1 failed**. Both failures are `browser.back()` waiting for `load`, followed by video cleanup on the closed page. This limitation is documented. Rerunning with `--grep-invert 'navigation verbs'` passed every selected test:

```text
worker:  Test Files  4 passed (4)   Tests  21 passed (21)
attempt: Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  14 passed (14)
```

- Observed forms, cookies/storage isolation, network routes, dialogs, frames, viewport/media settings, reload/init scripts, and worker-scope session persistence. The Cloudflare session list was empty after teardown. Scanned generated artifacts for the actual API token: no matches. Remote WebM videos were generated in both scopes; GitHub attachment upload requires repository write access and was denied for this account.
- Built CLI local testbed: **588 passed, 1 skipped**. Web benchmark: **91 passed**. The main/branch A/B run matched every step outcome and counter across two pairs; timing was unresolved on the busy host, so no performance claim.

| Regression | Before review fixes | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Errored 429 response body | Stream cancellation masks the retry | Regression passes; the rejected request retries |
| Journal write and DELETE both fail | Cleanup error replaces the journal error | Both errors and session ID retained |
| Attempt-scope reconnect | No regression covered reconnect credentials | Reconnect tests require headers for explicit and fallback endpoints |

Maintainer verification on 2026-11-12 after rebasing onto main:

- `pnpm check` passed, including the build, public type checks, and docs checks.
- Built CLI: `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` passed **588 tests, 1 skipped**; `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web-benchmark test` passed **93 tests**.
- Browser Run provider: **35 tests passed**. Full web suite: **825 tests passed, 1 skipped**. Fresh-context review found no critical or important findings.

title: feat(run): keep a timings history that CI can cache
body:
`e2e run` already starts the longest files first, but it read the previous run's durations from `report.json`, which a fresh CI checkout never has. This writes a small versioned history a CI cache can restore and save.

- Every run that reaches its tests writes `<output>/timings.json` (`timings-1`): `target::file` to milliseconds. It merges into the existing file with a moving average (a run moves an entry a third of the way), and drops files that are gone and targets the config no longer has.
- A file is timed only when the run carried out all of it, once. A `--grep`, `--last-failed`, interrupted (including a retry cut short after a failure), or limit-cut run leaves that file's entry alone, and repeats past the first do not count.
- A key is a target name, then a project-relative POSIX file with no `..` segment. The schema and the reader use the same pattern, and a table test keeps them in step.
- With one worker the file is still written, but files are ordered only with more than one. Files with no recorded time start first, then the rest longest first.
- Advisory: a missing, corrupt, or schema-invalid file is no history, never an error. An absent file falls back to `report.json`, so nothing regresses. A restored cache can reorder files, never change a result.
- `--timings <file>` moves it. `--last-failed` still reads `report.json` only.
- Docs: `actions/cache` recipe in `docs/ci/github-actions.mdx` (the key ends in `github.run_attempt`, since a rerun shares `run_id` and `actions/cache` never overwrites a key), the provider-neutral rule in `docs/ci.mdx`. `timings.json` joins the `e2e init` and repo `.gitignore` entries.
- Wire format: `schema/timings-v1.schema.json` with a valid and an invalid fixture, in the same change as the producer.

Not here: duration-balanced `--shard`, a `timings.file` config key, and dogfooding the recipe in `benchmark.yml`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[restore .e2e/timings.json] --> B[e2e run: longest files first]
  B --> C[merge measured files into history]
  C --> D[save .e2e/timings.json]
```

Refs ENG-1111

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI, `e2e run tests/check.e2e.ts tests/click.e2e.ts tests/controls.e2e.ts tests/browser.e2e.ts --workers 2`, once with no history and once seeded with the `timings.json` the first run wrote:

| | no history | with `timings.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `controls` (16 s file) starts | 2.5 s | 0 s |
| `click` (14 s file) starts | 1.3 s | 0 s |
| `check`, `browser` (short) start | 0 s | 14 s, 16 s |
| run | 19.4 s | 17.5 s |

One run per cell on one machine, so the size of the gain is indicative. The order is the point.

- Same CLI, edge cases: a valid-JSON file with another schema version, a string value, an array, or a `__proto__` key is ignored and rewritten, tests still pass. A `NO_TESTS` run writes nothing. `--last-failed` reads `report.json`, not `timings.json` (`NO_LAST_RUN` with only a timings file). An unwritable `--timings` path is one stderr line and exit 0. `--grep` on one test leaves the file byte for byte unchanged.
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, the testbed suite (587 passed), and the web benchmark (91 passed) are green locally. `pnpm test` ran before the review fixes; after them I reran `pnpm check`, the unit suite (3447 passed), the new integration file, and the testbed ordering check. CI is green on the final head.
- Not verified: the GitHub Actions recipe against a real workflow, and that a PR can read the base branch's cache but not write it. The page states GitHub's documented rule; I did not run it.

## Review

A fresh-context review found two things, both fixed in the second commit (cubic-dev-ai then raised nine smaller points, all fixed in the third and fourth): partial runs wrote non-comparable durations (a `--last-failed` rerun of one 2 s test cut a 60 s entry to about 40 s), and nothing tested the runner wiring. The new integration test fails with the partial guard removed. The review also noted `--timings` is not confined to the project root like `--output`; left as is, since the path is one the user names on their own command line and test code already runs with full authority.

## CI notes

- `packages/acp` `executor.test.ts` "retries the session directory removal after the agent exits" failed on `test (22)`, `(24)`, and `(22.22.3)` in earlier runs of this PR (`kill ESRCH` after a 500 ms wait), and on `oskar/fix-main-failing-tests` before it. It does not reproduce locally and this PR does not touch `packages/acp`; reruns passed. It needs its own fix.
- The Android agentic `Huge Virtualized List` step failed once with `REPLAY_STALE` and passed on rerun, with nothing in this diff that reaches it.

title: refactor(mobile): read for rest after a scroll or swipe, and set the transition wait by kind of action
body:
- This is a refactor of the rest wait #1668 added, plus one option. It gives the same protection as main (no tap lost on a moving list in the reviewer's re-run of 420 idle and 252 loaded scroll-then-tap pairs) with one read and about 100 ms less per scroll-then-tap, and it sets the wait by the kind of the last action. It does not fix a lost tap that main still has.
- After a scroll or swipe, a test acts on a control only once it stops moving. The `gesture` budget is the least wait, then the engine reads until two sightings of the control and its look-alikes agree, at most 4 s after the gesture. That read is also the relocation read, so a list that already sits still costs no extra read. A look-alike with no bounds is left out of the sighting.
- It replaces the re-read #1668 added (`steadied`), which compared the control's own bounds, 100 ms apart, for up to 2 s after the gesture and failed the action with `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` when its budget ran out first. This one compares the control with its look-alikes, 50 ms apart, runs up to 4 s, and goes ahead on the latest read when the budget runs out. #1668's opt-out of agent-device's own post-gesture settle (`postGestureStabilization: false`) stays as it is.
- `mobile({ transition })` also takes `{ default, gesture, launch }` (new `TransitionBudgets` type), so the least wait after a gesture can differ from the wait after a tap. The wait #1564 puts before a screen swipe follows the same kinds. A number still sets one wait for every action. A budget of 0 is no wait at all after any other action; after a scroll or swipe it sleeps for nothing and the rest check still runs.
- An action whose own timeout cannot fit another read goes ahead on the latest read instead of failing with `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`. Agent actions and the default and launch paths are unchanged. This is a behavior change from main and is open for the owner to decide.
- Left out on purpose: new benchmark budgets, which need CI runs of their own.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[scroll or swipe returns] --> B[sleep the gesture budget]
  B --> C[read the screen]
  C --> D{two sightings agree?}
  D -- no --> E{cap or timeout reached?}
  E -- no --> C
  D -- yes --> F[act on the control as read]
  E -- yes --> F
```

```ts
mobile({ platform: 'ios', transition: { gesture: 1_500 } }); // 500 ms after everything else
```

## Verified

Latest head (rest check kept at a budget of 0, look-alikes with no bounds left out): the 632 mobile unit tests pass and the three new or changed tests fail on the previous head; `tsc`, `oxlint`, `plugins:check`, and `docs:check` pass. The device suites below were not rerun on this head.

Ran it locally: yes
- `apps/mobile-benchmark` through the built CLI on an iOS simulator and an Android emulator, `@e2e-dev/mobile` built from main and from this branch, both on the pinned agent-device 0.21.36 (`--workers 1 --retries 0`, one run at a time). Both builds carried a wrapper around the agent-device client that records every call (not in this PR).
- iOS, a scratch test (below, not in this PR): 21 × `scrollUntilVisible` then tap on the huge virtualized list, `--repeat-each 10`, two runs per build in the order main, branch, branch, main (main was f6aba972, before #1564 and #1668 landed). That is 840 scroll-then-tap pairs, and all 40 repeats pass. A tap counts as sent on a moving list when the last two snapshots before it disagree about where the rows sit (more than 1 px).

| | main | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| scroll-then-tap pairs | 420 | 420 |
| taps sent after a last read that still saw the list moving | 6 | 0 |
| slow flings (the first two reads disagree) | 6 | 10 |
| scroll return to tap, median | 1,727 ms | 1,724 ms |
| scroll return to tap, slow flings (median, range) | 1,881 ms, 1,757 to 1,886 | 2,154 ms, 2,020 to 2,482 |

Fisher exact, one-sided: p = 0.015. Five of main's six were in one run (the other main run had one), so without that run the contrast alone is 1/210 against 0/420. Slow flings are 16 of 840 scrolls (1.9%). On the branch each waited 2.0 to 2.5 s for two reads to agree, with 3 to 5 reads, and none reached the 4 s cap. The baseline is main before #1668, with agent-device's own settle in place. The table was not repeated against main with #1668's re-read, so it shows what the rest wait adds over that settle, not over `steadied`.
- Full deterministic suite with this branch on agent-device 0.21.36: iOS 57 passed, 1 skipped (611 s); Android 57 passed, 1 skipped (379 s). The 1-minute load at start was 2.4 and 2.5 after waiting for it to drop below 3, with peaks of 6.3 and 7.3. The first scroll-then-tap run (main) had a load spike to 26.9 in its first two minutes from the cold simulator boot; only one of its five events fell in that window.
- After the review fixes (a fill or clear takes the read that found the field at rest, so it costs no read of its own), the full suites again on agent-device 0.21.36 with the new head: iOS 57 passed, 1 skipped (611 s) and Android 57 passed, 1 skipped (384 s), 1-minute load at start 2.5 after waiting.
- Rebased onto c74de8d0 and with the long-press fix: the full suites again on agent-device 0.21.36, iOS 57 passed, 1 skipped (690 s) and Android 57 passed, 1 skipped (466 s). Both run about 80 s longer than before, because #1564 now waits the remaining budget before every screen swipe and the benchmark's budget is 1.5 s. The 1-minute load at start was 3.0 and 2.4 after the wait cap, with peaks of 9.1 and 6.3.
- On the current head, with main (3ce6b589) merged in and agent-device 0.21.37 pinned since #1735: the 618 mobile unit tests and `pnpm check` pass. The previous head (33388e39, the PR's four commits on f64e7dba) passed CI with all four device jobs (iOS and Android, deterministic and agentic) green. Locally, the iOS deterministic suite on a simulator with 0.21.37 gave 57 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed (672 s, 1-minute load 3.5 at start after the 4-minute wait cap). The failure is `openLink opens the scenario a deep link names`, new from #1805: the app installed on that simulator is the 11-03 build, whose bundle has no `e2e-benchmark://` routing, so the link opens and the app ignores it. CI builds or repacks the app from each head's own source. Android was not run locally.

Not covered: this branch against main with #1668's re-read on 0.21.37, a swipe that starts a UIKit transition (the tree reports that screen's final frame at once, so only the `gesture` budget protects the tap, as before), and real devices.

<details>
<summary>The scratch test</summary>

```ts
test('fling taps: scroll to a row and tap it, twenty-one times', { timeout: 280_000 }, async ({ app, device, screen }) => {
  await openScenario({ app, device, screen }, 'Huge Virtualized List');
  for (let row = 24; row <= 504; row += 24) {
    const target = screen.getByTestId(`row-${row}`);
    await screen.scrollUntilVisible(target, { direction: 'down', timeout: 120_000 });
    await target.tap();
  }
});
```

</details>

title: feat(html-reporter): write the run as one HTML page
body: e2e reports a run as terminal output, JSON, JUnit, markdown, or a pull request comment. None of them shows a test's steps next to its screenshots and video, and the Playwright and Maestro migration guides list `reporter: 'html'` as missing. ## What changed - New package `@e2e-dev/html-reporter`. `htmlReporter()` writes `/report.html`, one page that opens from disk with no server: ```ts import { htmlReporter } from '@e2e-dev/html-reporter'; export default { targets, reporters: ['list', htmlReporter()] } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` - The page is a React app in `packages/html-reporter/app/`. Vite and `vite-plugin-singlefile` build it into one HTML file with the fonts and icons inlined. The reporter (`packages/html-reporter/src/reporter.ts`) fills that template with the report-1 document, the media, and the test-file lines around each step. - `media` picks how screenshots and videos reach the page: `'link'` (default, relative paths into `results/`), `'embed'` (one file to send), or `'none'`. - The page shows the tests as a tree (file, describe blocks, tests, failures first) with status tabs and search. Each test shows its attempts, the error with expected and received values diffed, the code frame, its steps synced to the video, agent step details, and a **copy prompt** button that puts the failure on the clipboard for a coding agent. - Core: `FinishedRun.redact(text)` (`packages/e2e/src/types.ts`). It masks configured secret values in text a reporter brings from outside the report, built from the same ledger as `TestFilterContext.redact`. The page uses it on the test-file lines it embeds. This needs the next `e2e` release, so the reporter's `e2e` peer floor is `>=0.23.1`. - `media: 'embed'` leaves out downloads the runner could not scan for secrets (`redaction: 'incomplete'`), and download links save the file instead of opening it. - Fonts are Geist and JetBrains Mono (OFL 1.1) and the icons are Lucide (ISC). The licence texts ship in the package and are listed in `NOTICE`. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[run finished] --> B["writeReport(run)"] B --> C[report-1 document] B --> D["media: link / embed / none"] B --> E["source lines, run.redact"] C & D & E --> F["dist/app/index.html template"] F --> G[".e2e/report.html"] ``` Not covered yet (documented in `docs/reference/reporters.mdx`): after `--last-failed` the page shows only the rerun's tests, and under `e2e explore` it shows no findings. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Testbed, built CLI, with `htmlReporter()` on the todos and forms suites plus one deliberately failing test, run with `--repeat-each 2`: ```text HTML report .e2e-html/report-link.html Failed × |web| tests-html-scratch/broken.e2e.ts:10 > scratch > fails on a wrong remaining count ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed × |web| tests-html-scratch/broken.e2e.ts:5 > scratch > fails on a wrong remaining count (repeat #1) ``` - The testbed's reporter stress suite (hostile titles, a 20 KiB message, timeouts, flakes, skips), plus a test that fills the configured `admin` password and then fails, with `media: 'embed'`. Every one of the 16 test pages opened in Chromium with no page errors and no dialogs. The password value is nowhere in `report.html`, and the frame shows `fill('')`. - Pages from the web benchmark agent suite and the mobile benchmark on an iOS simulator, in both themes and at phone width. | Run list | Failed test | | --- | --- | | ![run list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2e703a5-310a-42c1-82db-5344cd62553f) | ![failed test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2772d0ba-7e87-46db-9569-d3e805a8f0f9) | | Light theme | Reporter stress suite | Phone recording | | --- | --- | --- | | ![light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fd9a1da-84aa-4c19-b3e3-611606731cc8) | ![stress](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a9dcdc4-e491-4bcc-b34a-e0c205f96a8e) | ![mobile player](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11d38cbd-2ce6-4f92-a206-6bfa4f3fc959) | ## Review - A fresh-context review found 9 issues. Fixed: unscanned downloads embedded in a page meant for sending, `--repeat-each` rows that looked identical, download links that opened in the report's origin, emoji splitting in the expected/received diff, and no runner-level test for `run.redact` (`packages/e2e/tests/integration/reporters.test.ts`, which fails when `redact` passes text through). - Declined: - Folding `--last-failed` and explore findings into the page: documented above as a follow-up. - Streaming `'embed'` past V8's string limit (about 400 MB of media): the docs already warn that device video makes an embedded page large. - A test against the built template: the root `test` script builds first, and `embedPayload` already throws when the placeholder is not there exactly once. - Cubic: fixed 15 threads (copied-prompt fence, cache-only step details, headline counted from the listed tests, the reporter abort signal, video part clock, serial member error fallback, a doubled screen-reader status, and docs wording). Two threads about the secrets invariant are left open for a human: symlinked artifacts, and multiline secrets in code frames. Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved (before the fresh-context fixes above). Closes [ENG-1079](https://linear.app/e2e-inc/issue/ENG-1079/html-reporter). Written with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5).

title: docs(ci): add a GitLab CI/CD page
body: The docs had no GitLab page. `docs/ci.mdx` told GitLab users to copy the GitHub Actions workflow, and the only GitLab-specific instruction sat in one sentence of `docs/filters.mdx`. - New `docs/ci/gitlab.mdx`: - a web job that runs for merge requests and the default branch, with the browsers cached inside the project (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`) and `reports: junit` for the merge request widget. The rules sit on the job, not in `workflow:`, so the same job works as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or as a file a pipeline includes - adding the job to an existing pipeline with `include: - local:` - the model key as a masked and hidden CI/CD variable, set in the UI or with `glab variable set --masked --hidden --raw`, with GitLab's rules on masking, protected variables, and pipelines from forks - the identity verification GitLab.com asks of a new account before hosted runners take its jobs - `--changed-since` in merge request pipelines, skipped in merge trains, with `GIT_DEPTH: 0` - sharding with `parallel` and `CI_NODE_INDEX/CI_NODE_TOTAL` - iOS and Android jobs on self-managed runners. GitLab's hosted macOS runners don't support `testmanagerd`, which XCUITest needs, and its hosted Linux runners don't list KVM. Each job names its device through `E2E_DEVICE`, so a device left over from a timed-out job on the same machine is never driven. - GitLab logo (`docs/images/integrations/gitlab.svg`, the full-color tanuki from GitLab's source, so no dark-mode invert), a card on `docs/ci.mdx`, and the nav entry in `docs/docs.json`. - `docs/filters.mdx` links to the new section instead of carrying the GitLab command. ## Issue ENG-1135 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, and on GitLab.com hosted runners for the web job. - The web job ran in the [e2e-gitlab-ci playground](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci) (Next.js, npm, `node:24`). In each pipeline GitLab's test report showed 5 of 5 passed, 0 skipped, so the two agent tests ran with the masked, hidden `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` variable. | MR | Setup | Pipeline | | --- | --- | --- | | [!1](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/1) | the job as `.gitlab-ci.yml` | passed, 2m02s; passed again on `main` after merge | | [!2](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/2) | an existing `.gitlab-ci.yml` with a `build` job, the e2e job in `.gitlab/e2e.gitlab-ci.yml` through `include: - local:` | passed, 1m53s | | [!3](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/3) | committed replay cache | both `agent.act` steps replayed: 2 model calls instead of 7, the two `agent.assert` checks | The first pipelines failed before any job started, until the account's identity was verified. - The web job's `script` in a `node:26` container (Debian 13), against a copy of `examples/with-vite`, with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` under the project: ```text Chrome Headless Shell 156.0.8078.4 (playwright chromium-headless-shell v1248) downloaded to /builds/proj/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1248 ✓ web tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > shows the greeting form 643ms ✓ web tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > asks for a name when the field is empty 160ms ✓ web tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > greets the name you type 200ms Test Files 1 passed (1) JUnit .e2e/junit.xml ``` The first try failed with `APP_UNREACHABLE`: in the container Vite bound `localhost` to `::1` only. The page now says to make the app's command listen on `127.0.0.1`. - The `--changed-since` script picks `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_SHA`, then `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA`, and leaves the flag out off merge requests and in merge trains, under `sh` and `bash`. `e2e list --changed-since ` accepts a commit hash. - Every YAML block on the page parses. - The iOS and Android jobs did not run: they need a self-managed Mac and a Linux runner with KVM.

title: fix(mobile): read agent-device's covered mark as hidden
body:
## What and why

- agent-device marks a node `interactionBlocked: 'covered'` when something drawn over it holds its centre. e2e ignored the mark, so `toBeVisible` passed and `scrollUntilVisible` stopped on a field a footer covers (#1324).
- Outside the soft keyboard, a covered node now reads as hidden, so `toBeVisible` waits and `scrollUntilVisible` keeps scrolling. agent-device's refusal of an action on it already fails as `ACTION_FAILED` through the `staleOr` branch from #1686.
- Under the keyboard, #1686's keyboard rules decide, since agent-device counts the Android IME as a cover. So a focused field, the keyboard's own nodes, and a container with a child above the keyboard stay visible on Android as on main. "Under the keyboard" uses agent-device's own cover point, `centerOfRect`.
- On Android, while agent-device reports a keyboard it could not measure (no band), the mark hides nothing, as on main (`keyboardUnplaced` in `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`). iOS is unaffected: agent-device never counts the iOS keyboard as a cover.
- Role queries still find a covered node, so `getByRole(...).tap()` fails with agent-device's refusal rather than finding nothing. A node the keyboard hides stays out of role queries, as #1686 documents. Role queries and a fill's pre-check read the projected node's `platformHidden` fact (what the platform and the keyboard hide), so a field that turns covered before a fill goes to agent-device's refusal with no retry, as on main.
- The keyboard dismissal drag reads the projected node's `covered` fact, from a projection with the same keyboard band an observation gets. A covered leaf no larger than half the screen is an obstacle. Being covered makes no container one, since agent-device tests only a node's centre. The drag starts in a clear scroll view away from covered ones when it can, and else anywhere in a scroll view, covered or not. A button the keyboard half covers still keeps the drag off its visible top, as on main.
- The role-query note in `packages/core/src/engine/contract.ts` and `engine.mdx` lets an engine keep a node its driver marks covered; platform- and keyboard-hidden nodes stay out.
- The footer case needs two agent-device changes, proposed in callstack/agent-device#4347. Until e2e bumps to them, the Covered Field test and its agentic scenario are declared and skipped with that reason.

On main `c30354ff` (agent-device 0.21.41).

## Issue

Refs #1324

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. Unit tests on main `c30354ff` plus this branch, with agent-device 0.21.41. Before the rebase, on agent-device 0.21.36: the iOS 26.5 benchmark suite (57 passed) and an iOS 27.2 simulator.

| Run | Keyboard dismissal and fill tests (89: `keyboard.test.ts`, and the engine's keyboard dismissal and input freshness groups) |
|---|---|
| main `c30354ff` | 6 fail: the new behaviors (a covered leaf blocks the drag, also beside a keyboard narrower than the screen, in `keyboardDragStart` and through `device.dismissKeyboard()`; a clear scroll view is preferred; a covered one nested in it is avoided) and the new `covered` field. The other 83 pass, so in those cases this branch does what main does |
| `c011913c`, the rebase kdy1 reviewed | 10 fail: kdy1's repro through `device.dismissKeyboard()`, covered scroll views with and without children, the only scroll view covered, a covered card, a clear carousel with no point, a mark under the keyboard, a covered leaf beside a keyboard narrower than the screen, and a fill on a field that turned covered |
| `ceeafaee` | 3 fail: a covered leaf beside a keyboard narrower than the screen, in `keyboardDragStart` and through `device.dismissKeyboard()` (the drag started at {195,383}, inside its margin), and the new `covered` field |
| this branch | all 89 pass, and all 620 in the mobile package |

- 36 bugs planted in the changed lines, this round's and the earlier ones re-run on the new code; all 36 fail a test. That includes the one that survived okwasniewski's run: the keyboard band widened to the full screen width in `keyboardPlacement`, for the drag and the observation together, and for each alone.
- `pnpm check` passes.
