title: feat(cli): write a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD pipeline in e2e init
body:
`e2e init` gets a CI step. In a project with the web or mobile engine it asks which CI service to set up, then writes one job for each platform the config's targets run on: web, iOS, and Android.

```
◆  Add a CI pipeline that runs the tests?
│  ○ GitHub Actions
│  ● GitLab CI/CD (in every merge request and on the default branch)
│  ○ None
```

| Targets in the config | Jobs |
| --- | --- |
| web only | `web`, running every target |
| iOS and/or Android only | `ios` and/or `android` |
| web and mobile | all of them, each with `--target <its targets>` |

- `--ci github-actions|gitlab|none` answers the question. `--yes` alone writes none, since a pipeline runs on the next push. The wizard preselects the service the repository points to: its remote, a `.github/` folder, or a `.gitlab-ci.yml`.
- Targets come from the new config `init` writes, or from loading an existing one the way `e2e run` does (`loadConfigModule`, and `resolvePlatform`/`targetName` from `config/targets.ts`). The load happens after the user confirms and after the install, so the config never runs on a cancelled wizard and an example's engine is installed first. A config that still doesn't load falls back to `package.json`: web engine only, one web job runs every target; mobile engine, no pipeline.
- Web job: the project's package manager (npm, pnpm, Yarn 1, Yarn 2+, Bun), Chromium with a cache, `e2e run --reporter list,junit`. It runs every target that isn't iOS or Android, HTTP tests included.
- Mobile jobs on GitHub follow e2e-inc/e2e-react-native's workflow: `macos-26` with a Release simulator build, the image's own iPhone 17 Pro on a pinned iOS runtime, and `E2E_DEVICE` set to its UDID; `ubuntu-latest` with KVM, an `x86_64` release APK, and an API 36 emulator, with a system-image install that retries a download that drops or comes back empty.
- The app build: Expo (`expo run:ios`, `expo prebuild` + Gradle, no prebuild when `android/` is committed), bare React Native (`xcodebuild` on `ios/*.xcworkspace`, through Bundler with a `Gemfile`; `android/gradlew`), or a step that fails until replaced, which `init` names.
- GitLab's hosted runners can't run a simulator or an emulator, so its mobile jobs target self-managed shell runners with `tags` to replace, as on `docs/ci/gitlab.mdx`; `init` says so, and asks for `device: process.env.E2E_DEVICE` when the config lacks it.
- Node comes from `.nvmrc` or `.node-version`, else 24. A project in a subfolder or a workspace member gets the file at the repository root, the install at the workspace root, and the jobs in the project folder.
- Model key: GitHub passes the repository secret in the run step's `env`; GitLab gets CI/CD variables on its own. `init` reads the gateway from the config's import and prints the `gh secret set` or `glab variable set` command.
- `init` never overwrites a pipeline file. Beside an existing `.gitlab-ci.yml` it writes `.gitlab/e2e.gitlab-ci.yml` and prints the `include:` to add, renaming the jobs with `-run` when the pipeline has one of their names and saying when its `stages:` leave out `test`. A workflow or pipeline that already runs `e2e run` in one of its commands gets nothing; the words in a comment or a step name don't count. Nothing is written through a symlinked `.github` or `.gitlab`.
- Warnings for what would fail on the first push: no `app.command` (web job only), a subscription gateway or a loopback model endpoint, a build step to replace, GitLab mobile runners.
- The pipelines are YAML templates in `packages/e2e/templates/ci/`, each a complete pipeline for npm at the repository root and an Expo app, which `actionlint` and `glab ci lint` accept as is. `init` edits a copy with the `yaml` package's Document API (new runtime dependency, pure JS), keeping comments and formatting; a platform with no targets loses its job. For the template's own case the output equals the template byte for byte.
- GitHub action pins live only in the templates and match the docs and the e2e skill; `tests/unit/init-ci.test.ts` fails when they drift.
- Telemetry: `e2e_init_completed` gets a `ci` property.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[web or mobile engine in package.json?] -- no --> N[no question]
  A -- yes --> B{e2e run already in a workflow or .gitlab-ci.yml?}
  B -- yes --> N
  B -- no --> C[ask, preselect from remote / .github / .gitlab-ci.yml]
  C --> D[confirm changes, install]
  D --> E[targets: new config, or load the existing one]
  E --> F[web job for non-phone targets, ios and android jobs for phone targets]
  F --> G[.github/workflows/e2e.yml, .gitlab-ci.yml, or .gitlab/e2e.gitlab-ci.yml to include]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. The built CLI wrote the pipelines into real repos, and each ran unedited on hosted runners:

| Case | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub, web + iOS + Android, Expo, existing config with three targets | [e2e-react-native#5](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-react-native/pull/5), its own workflow replaced by the generated one | web passed; iOS passed (35/35, 51 min) on the first run; Android passed (23 min) on the final template. On that last run iOS lost 1 of 35 to a simulator `xcrun` timeout, with its job unchanged since the green run |
| GitHub Actions, npm, repo root | [e2e-github-actions#2](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-github-actions/pull/2), merged | 5/5, agent tests included |
| GitHub Actions, pnpm in `site/`, `.nvmrc` at the root | [e2e-github-actions#3](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-github-actions/pull/3) | 5/5 |
| GitHub Actions, pnpm version from `site/package.json` | [e2e-github-actions#5](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-github-actions/pull/5) | passed |
| GitHub, web job from the YAML template | [e2e-github-actions#6](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-github-actions/pull/6) | 5/5, cache replayed |
| GitLab, npm, new `.gitlab-ci.yml` | [e2e-gitlab-ci!1](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/1), merged | 5/5 in the MR test report |
| GitLab, beside an existing `.gitlab-ci.yml` via `include:` | [e2e-gitlab-ci!2](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/2) | 5/5 |
| GitLab, pnpm via corepack on `node:26` | [e2e-gitlab-ci!5](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/5) | 5/5 |
| GitLab, web job from the YAML template | [e2e-gitlab-ci!6](https://gitlab.com/e2e_inc/e2e-gitlab-ci/-/merge_requests/6) | 5/5 |

- `actionlint` and `glab ci lint` pass on every combination rendered: web only, mobile only, both, each build kind, npm/pnpm/Yarn/Bun, a subfolder, and a workspace member. The GitLab file for e2e-react-native passes `glab ci lint` too.
- Packed tarball in a scratch project, and the interactive wizard in a pseudo-terminal: the question above, with the service preselected from the remote.
- The Android job on GitHub needed two fixes found on that repo: `sdkmanager` can report success for an empty image, and the runner image's command-line tools (since image `20261103`) are older than the API 36 system image's package format, so `android-emulator-runner` failed to create the device ("contains no system images"). The job now installs command-line tools 23.0 (SHA-256 checked) and checks the image before the action runs.
- Built CLI and packed tarball in scratch repos: beside a Cypress workflow whose step is named `Cypress e2e run` and commented `# our old e2e runner`, `--ci github-actions` wrote `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (before: `Exists, not touching: .github/workflows/cypress.yml`); beside a workflow whose multi-line step runs `xvfb-run -a npx e2e run`, it wrote nothing.
- Not run on a runner: the bare React Native build, and GitLab's mobile jobs (gitlab.com's hosted runners can't run them).

Two fresh-context reviews found issues, all fixed: the first nine in the web-only version, then eight in the mobile one (the config loaded before the install, so an example got no pipeline; the GitLab header lost with the web job; and smaller ones). cubic's findings are fixed or answered in their threads, and kdy1's suggestion to keep the pipelines as YAML templates is in.

Tracked in ENG-1084.

title: test(acp): keep the delayed fake agent alive until its exit delay is up
body:
The acp test "retries the session directory removal after the agent exits when the first try fails" has failed 12 Linux CI jobs since #1626 (Node 22, 22.22.3, and 24): `kill ESRCH` at `tests/executor.test.ts:522`, because the fake agent, which should take 1.5 s to stop after SIGTERM, was gone within 500 ms. It blocks unrelated PRs such as #1647.

- Teardown (`packages/acp/src/session.ts`) closes the agent's stdin and stdout pipe right before the SIGTERM. A process whose only other hold is a signal listener can exit on stdin's EOF before the signal handler runs, and a late write can hit EPIPE.
- The fixture's delayed agent (`ACP_EXIT_DELAY_MS`) now holds the event loop until its delay is up. Once it is stopping, it logs a stdout error, an uncaught error, or a rejection instead of dying on it; before that, an error still ends it at once with code 1, so a real failure fails the test fast.
- The delay starts at SIGTERM or stdin's end, whichever comes first, so an agent whose test worker died without a teardown still exits.
- Both tests that use the delay print the agent's last log lines when it is gone early, so a future failure says why.
- Test code only; no changeset.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- The failure never reproduced: 6 runs on macOS and 37 in Linux containers (`node:22.22.3`, `node:24`, non-root, 1 and 2 CPUs), so the CI logs above are the evidence for the race.
- With the change: `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/acp` executor tests pass on macOS, and the full acp suite passed 15 times in a `node:22.22.3` container as a non-root user (the test skips as root).
- CI on this PR: the test jobs on all five Node versions passed, 22.22.3 included, where this test failed most. One `check` run hit an unrelated web-engine timeout (`locator-frame.e2e.ts`) and passed on rerun.
- A fresh-context review found the orphan case (a held agent whose worker died would never exit); fixed by also starting the delay at stdin's end.

Tracked in ENG-1185.

title: Feedback from a first real-world deterministic run (booking flow): mostly smooth, a few friction points
body:
## Feedback from a first real-world deterministic run

**Context:** e2e v0.23.0, `@e2e-dev/web`, deterministic locators only (no model configured). Target: a production backoffice booking flow (agenda → new appointment → pick existing contact → create animal record → submit), exercised through a local proxy. Single test, run with `npx e2e run`.

### What went smoothly

- The deterministic surface (`screen.getByRole/getByLabel/getByPlaceholder/getByText`, `.tap/.fill/.selectOption`) covered the whole flow — no `agent.*` step needed.
- `expect(...).toBeVisible/.toBeEnabled/.not.toHaveAttribute` polling handled async readiness well (waiting for form fields to leave `readonly` state).
- Failure artifacts were genuinely useful: `trace.md`, the failure screenshot, and `video.webm` made each misstep self-explanatory without reruns.
- Error codes are actionable — `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` and `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` each pointed at the exact locator and, in the trace, listed the actual candidate nodes.

### Friction

1. **Combobox option naming.** `getByRole('option', 'Smooth Collie')` failed with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` because the option's accessible name was `Ajouter « Smooth Collie »` ("Add …" prefix baked into the name). Fixed with a regex locator. The trace did list the real option names, so diagnosis was quick — but a "did you mean X?" hint in the error would save a cycle.
2. **`LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` on `getByText(/10:00/)`** — matched both the `Heure` input's value and the confirmation text. Expected behavior per the docs; fixed by anchoring the regex to the longer confirmation string. Worth noting mainly as a "write tight locators" reminder for new users.
3. **`tap()` fires while the app is not ready.** The submit button was clickable while async form state was still loading, so the app's own submit guard rejected the first click. Working as designed on e2e's side, but the fix (explicit `toBeEnabled` + `not.toHaveAttribute('readonly')` waits) had to be discovered by reading the app's validation code — a docs example for "wait for dependent state before submit" would help.

### Overall

Solid first experience — the deterministic tier is productive without any model subscription, and artifacts carry enough context to fix locators without re-running.

[Written by Devin](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7c85e2b77dc9436c9186dba9b53d17f8)

### Page

[skills/e2e/references/running.md, lines 17–18](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/skills/e2e/references/running.md#L17-L18), also printed by `e2e guide running`.

```

`doctor` has no `--reporter` option. Its JSON-output flag is `--json`, as shown in its help, the [CLI registration](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/packages/e2e/src/cli/index.ts#L980-L995), and the [CLI reference](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/docs/reference/cli.mdx#L998-L1018).

Verified with a fresh npm install of `e2e@latest`, resolving to `e2e@0.23.0`, on Node.js 26.12.1, npm 12.2.1, macOS arm64. Current `main` at the commit linked above still contains the same text; only the installed release was executed.

Reproduction in an empty directory (no config, engine, app, or model needed):

```sh
npm install --no-audit --no-fund e2e@latest
E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e guide running
E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e doctor --help
E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e doctor --reporter json
```

The final command exits 2, emits no stdout, and prints:

```text
error: unknown option '--reporter'
(add --help for usage)
```

As a control, `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e doctor --json` emits valid `doctor-1` JSON. In the empty directory it exits 2 for `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, rather than failing option parsing. The workaround is to use that flag.

### Suggested wording

Change the doctor comment to `# --json for a host, exit 2 on a failed check`, so the bundled guide agrees with the command. Verification is to run the JSON-output spelling printed by `e2e guide running` and receive a doctor report rather than an unknown-option error.

title: fix(docs): Expo Simulators example reads the workflow job ID as the app build ID
body:
## Summary

The Expo Simulators setup example reads `process.env.EAS_BUILD_ID` for `expoSimulators({ buildId })`. In an Expo Workflows custom job, Expo already sets that variable to the current job-run ID, so copying the config there selects the test job instead of the upstream simulator build. This affects the hosted-provider example in the integration guide and package README; the separate workflow guide correctly downloads the upstream build explicitly.

### Page

- [Expo Simulators setup](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/docs/integrations/eas.mdx#L42-L63).
- [Package README usage](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/packages/eas/README.md#L13-L33).

### What is wrong

```ts
device: expoSimulators({ buildId: process.env.EAS_BUILD_ID }),
```

The integration page distinguishes hosted simulators from the workflow guide, but does not restrict the provider to local execution or explain that this example variable collides with a worker-provided variable.

## Steps to reproduce

This is source-only verification; no Expo build, workflow, or simulator session was started.

1. Use the documented hosted-provider config in a custom workflow test job after an iOS simulator build job, with a linked Expo project, provider access, and credentials configured. Leave `app.appPath` unset, as the example does.
2. Make the test job depend on the build job. Do not override `EAS_BUILD_ID`; it is supplied by Expo. The desired app build is `needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id`.
3. Follow the worker and provider source paths below: the config reads the current test job-run ID and passes it as the simulator session's `buildId`, rather than the upstream build output.

The workflow premise is supported by Expo's public [with-e2e workflow example](https://github.com/expo/examples/blob/2cc7a440b01eb30e326b91cf1f3aae41e749d128/with-e2e/.eas/workflows/e2e.yml#L43-L67), which runs this provider from a custom job and deliberately passes the upstream output through `E2E_IOS_BUILD_ID`.

## Expected behavior

A copyable provider example should identify the simulator app build selected by the user, including when the runner is a custom workflow job. Its environment variable should not implicitly read Expo's built-in ID for the current job.

## Actual behavior

The worker-provided ID is selected before the provider acquires a session. The provider retains the supplied `buildId`, rejects a conflicting `appPath`, and forwards that ID unchanged to session creation. The source establishes the wrong request value; the exact server response to a job-run ID was not observed and is not asserted here. The snippet can work locally when the user explicitly supplies a valid app build ID under that name.

## Runtime or environment

- Documentation checked in a fresh clone of default branch `main` at `e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24`, and latest stable `e2e@0.23.0` at `5f256928ebe08a8c7126fbc2a83c64a02fb24491`. The affected examples and provider behavior are the same in both.
- Expo documentation source checked at `62faa9f7003d860e00e59dee0ec899e38f4e6daf`.
- Expo worker source checked at current `main` (`d57eadf88772a21e316a85a4d5f6759ddfd8576b`) and latest published EAS CLI release `v27.5.0` (`0e811ed8d055448eb88b1ebfd5fb2bfdc2b783ba`). The ID assignment path is present in both; this does not assert the exact revision deployed on Expo's servers.

## Evidence

- Expected source: Expo's [workflow environment reference](https://docs.expo.dev/eas/workflows/environment/#additional-environment-variables) documents `EAS_BUILD_ID` on every VM-backed job; its [source](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/62faa9f7003d860e00e59dee0ec899e38f4e6daf/docs/pages/eas/workflows/environment.mdx#L260-L264) confirms that scope. The [build environment reference](https://docs.expo.dev/eas/environment-variables/usage/#built-in-environment-variables) separately documents its build-job meaning. The workflow reference also advises against custom variables with the `EAS_` prefix.
- Failure source: The two setup examples above, combined with Expo's worker path: [service dispatch guard](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/blob/v27.5.0/packages/worker/src/service.ts#L90-L112) selects `rest.jobRunId` for `jobType === 'jobRun'`; [context creation](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/blob/v27.5.0/packages/worker/src/service.ts#L319-L329) passes that ID to [environment creation](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/blob/v27.5.0/packages/worker/src/context.ts#L43-L51); [getBuildEnv](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/blob/v27.5.0/packages/worker/src/env.ts#L47-L54) assigns it to `EAS_BUILD_ID`. The e2e [provider](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/packages/eas/src/provider.ts#L153-L176) passes `buildId` to the [session client](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/packages/eas/src/client.ts#L113-L120) without substituting an upstream build output.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction was not run. A custom job using the hosted provider is demonstrated by Expo's example, the built-in job ID is documented and assigned by the worker, and a defined ID with no `appPath` reaches session creation unchanged.

The e2e [workflow guide](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24/docs/ci/eas-workflows.mdx#L83-L106) uses `needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id` with `eas/download_build` and a local simulator on the worker. That path is distinct and is not reported as broken.

## Restoration check

For a custom test job whose own job-run ID differs from the upstream app build ID, following the revised hosted-provider example should select the upstream app build. Preserve local use with an explicitly supplied valid build ID. The separate workflow guide's download-and-local-device path should remain valid.

### Suggested wording

Use a dedicated variable, for example `E2E_IOS_BUILD_ID`, for the app build and explain that a custom workflow job can populate it from `needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id`. Note that `EAS_BUILD_ID` belongs to the executing job. The exact wording and variable name can follow project conventions.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The example selects the wrong object ID when copied into a supported custom workflow job using the hosted provider. Local callers that explicitly supply an app build ID are unaffected; no live failure or server error was measured.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Expo's public workflow example passes the upstream build output through a dedicated variable and reads that variable in config; this preserves hosted-provider use without overriding Expo's built-in variable.

title: fix(release): engine patch updates make unchanged runner ranges uninstallable
body:
## Summary

A fresh npm install of an unchanged project on an older runner minor now fails because engine releases within its existing patch ranges require a newer runner minor. Both engines show the same failure. This conflicts with the documented 0.x release policy that breaking changes use a minor bump and that patch ranges receive updates without a `package.json` edit.

## Steps to reproduce

Public reproduction input: the dependency ranges in [Expo's with-e2e example](https://github.com/expo/examples/blob/2cc7a440b01eb30e326b91cf1f3aae41e749d128/with-e2e/package.json). The following reduced fixture was executed without Expo, an app, a device, a model, or credentials.

1. In an empty directory, write this `package.json`:

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "e2e": "~0.21.3",
    "@e2e-dev/mobile": "~0.12.4"
  }
}
```

2. With no lockfile or `node_modules`, run `npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`. It exits 1 during dependency resolution.
3. In another empty directory, use the same fixture with `"@e2e-dev/web": "~0.15.3"` instead of the mobile engine. The same command exits 1 for the web peer.
4. Controls: repeat in empty directories with the mobile engine pinned exactly to `0.12.5`, or the web engine pinned exactly to `0.15.4`. Both installs exit 0. Dependency lifecycle scripts were deliberately disabled; the failure is in resolution before those scripts.

## Expected behavior

A patch release selected by an existing engine range should preserve the project's installability with its previously accepted runner range. A release that stops accepting that runner range should use the project's documented breaking-change version boundary. This does not require an engine to claim compatibility with a runner whose exports or contract it cannot use.

## Actual behavior

The mobile fixture selects the latest engine patch and exits 1:

```text
npm error code ERESOLVE
npm error ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
npm error Found: e2e@0.21.3
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer e2e@">=0.22.1 <1" from @e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.6
```

The web-only fixture also exits 1:

```text
npm error peer e2e@">=0.22.1 <1" from @e2e-dev/web@0.15.5
```

Published npm metadata shows:

| Engine release | `peerDependencies.e2e` |
| --- | --- |
| `@e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.5` | `>=0.15.0 <1` |
| `@e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.6` | `>=0.22.1 <1` |
| `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.4` | `>=0.18.0 <1` |
| `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.5` | `>=0.22.1 <1` |

`npm view e2e versions --json` contains no stable `0.22.1`; the first published stable runner satisfying the new floor is the tested latest runner. Nightlies named `0.22.1-nightly-*` exist, but do not satisfy this stable peer range. This is a patch-release compatibility report, not a claim that the peer floor should accept those prereleases or be lowered without checking runtime compatibility.

## Runtime or environment

- Platform: macOS, Apple silicon; Node.js 26.12.1.
- npm: 12.2.1 and latest 12.2.2; both floating-range fixtures fail on both versions. The exact-engine controls resolve on both, and their package installs pass on the latest npm.
- Latest stable npm packages checked: `e2e` 0.23.0, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.6, `@e2e-dev/web` 0.15.5.
- Source baselines: default branch `main` at `e83fdf9144faf9d8dac810b7a309499d2979fa24`; release tags `e2e@0.22.0` at `cad17c3200ceb5439a261f9c24e6e7ebbf85ddff` and `e2e@0.23.0` at `5f256928ebe08a8c7126fbc2a83c64a02fb24491`. Current `main` retains the raised engine peer floors.
- Engine: both `@e2e-dev/mobile` and `@e2e-dev/web`; no engine was launched.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [CONTRIBUTING.md, Changesets](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e2e%400.23.0/CONTRIBUTING.md#changesets) reserves 0.x minor bumps for breaking changes, uses patches for features and fixes, and explicitly explains patch-range updates without a manifest edit. The same policy remains on current `main`.
- Failure source: the reduced npm fixtures and output above; the published peer metadata can be checked with `npm view @e2e-dev/mobile@0.12.5 peerDependencies`, the following mobile patch, and the two web patches in the table.
- Evidence provenance: observed
- Local verification: reproduced
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The floor change is deliberate: [the initial locator commit](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/be655df8cf15710bc0c83718660835582aab4677) raised both floors and declared patch changesets; [the follow-up commit](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/f9a5e20d53a7da2d1d9bd33174f0fbd0463b7ea4) set the current floor. The associated [locator PR](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1484) describes the floor increase, although that PR is closed without a merge; the commits are present in the release history. The [mobile changelog](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e2e%400.23.0/packages/mobile/CHANGELOG.md) and [web changelog](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e2e%400.23.0/packages/web/CHANGELOG.md) document the new minimum under Patch Changes.

The [engine release guidance](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e2e%400.23.0/AGENTS.md) says to raise a peer floor when an engine relies on a newer export or contract field. The [upgrade command](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/e2e%400.23.0/docs/reference/cli.mdx#e2e-upgrade) intentionally selects compatible runner/engine sets. Those rules explain the floor and provide an upgrade path, but do not state an exception to the patch-versus-breaking version policy. Exact pins to the preceding engines were verified here as an installation workaround; no test suite was run with them.

## Restoration check

The unchanged floating-range fixtures should resolve and install without bypassing peer validation or moving their runner ranges to another minor. The exact-engine controls should remain installable. Any release-policy correction should also ensure that an engine update which drops an accepted runner minor does not enter an existing patch range. Preserve truthful runtime peer requirements; accepting an incompatible graph with `--force` or `--legacy-peer-deps` does not restore the contract.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P2
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: Fresh installs fail for projects that retain an older runner minor while allowing the affected engine patch updates. The two reduced cases fail deterministically at npm resolution; this is bounded to those version combinations.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Pinning the mobile or web engine to its preceding exact release passes installation with the unchanged runner range and peer validation enabled. This establishes installation only; runtime tests were not run.

title: fix(report): run header lists targets excluded by --target
body:
### What happened With several targets configured, `e2e run --target web` prints every configured target in its run header, even though only the selected target executes. The project's public Expo example reproduces this with no device, model key, or account. Execution and result attribution remain correct; the defect is the misleading header. **Expected behavior** The run header should accurately identify the current target selection: `web` for this command. The CLI reference documents `--target` as selecting targets by name and says only selected targets' app commands start. The list reporter renders terminal progress and the run summary. A header presented as the run's `targets:` should communicate that selection. **Actual behavior** The release command exited 0 but printed this header and these completed-test lines: ```text run 01a1c267-88bb-72cb-838a-5d623319f22f · targets: ios, android, web · CI ✓ target "web" command at http://localhost:8081/ ready 655ms ↓ |web| tests/agentic.e2e.ts > the agent gets a greeting [set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to run agent tests] ↓ |web| tests/agentic.e2e.ts > the agent finds the empty-name error [set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to run agent tests] ✓ |web| tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > shows the greeting form 397ms ✓ |web| tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > asks for a name when the field is empty 151ms ✓ |web| tests/deterministic.e2e.ts > greets the name you type 179ms Tests 3 passed | 2 skipped (5) ``` The only target-ready line was for `web`. Its configured app command is `npm run web`, which runs `expo start --web --port 8081`; the run explicitly logged that it was starting this command rather than reusing an app. No iOS or Android preparation or tests appeared. In the report, `run.targets.map(t => t.id)` was `["ios","android","web"]`, while all five `run.results` entries had `targetId: "web"`: three passed and two skipped. `run.summary.selected` was 5, `executed` was 3, and `run.usage.modelTokens` was 0. The configured-target inventory in `run.targets` is context, not a separate reported defect. The current `main` source CLI also exited 0 with the same example, all three names in its header, three passing web tests, two skipped web agent tests, and the same target IDs and zero model tokens in its report. This execution used the release TypeScript loader and npm-installed dependencies, not a full monorepo build. ### Reproduction https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/tree/e2e%400.23.0/examples/with-expo ### Steps to reproduce It already contains the app, three-target config, and tests. The initializer downloads that release's example and aligns its runner and engine dependency ranges. From a fresh directory, with port 8081 free: ```sh export E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 EXPO_NO_TELEMETRY=1 CI=1 unset AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY npx -y e2e@0.23.0 init expo-repro --example expo --yes cd expo-repro npm install npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium npx e2e run --target web --retries 0 node -e 'const {run}=require("./.e2e/report.json"); console.log(JSON.stringify({targets:run.targets.map(t=>t.id),resultTargets:[...new Set(run.results.map(r=>r.targetId))],summary:run.summary,modelTokens:run.usage.modelTokens},null,2))' ``` These steps were executed on the release baseline below, with output redirected to logs for the non-TTY list reporter. The browser download was placed in an isolated directory via `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Only the web test command was run; no native build, simulator, Expo login, or model was used. The example skips its two agent tests when the key is unset. ### Versions - Release: npm `latest` resolved to `e2e 0.23.0`; `@e2e-dev/web 0.15.5` and `@e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.6`. The initializer reported that it copied the release-tagged example. Its app installed `expo 57.0.32`. - Default branch: freshly cloned `main` at `c74de8d0436086e7a37b8f41130ed460e06513ed`. The source CLI was run from the example with `node --import ./node_modules/e2e/dist/config/register.js /packages/e2e/src/cli/bin.ts run --target web --retries 0 --output .e2e-main`. The clone resolved the example's npm dependencies plus the source manifest's `toml-eslint-parser 1.0.3` pin. - Node `v26.12.1`; npm `12.2.1`; macOS `27.2.0`, arm64; headless Chromium `156.0.8078.4`; default `list` reporter with `CI=1` and redirected output. ### Engine @e2e-dev/web ### Anything else #### Evidence - Expected source: The [CLI run flag reference](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/c74de8d0436086e7a37b8f41130ed460e06513ed/docs/reference/cli.mdx#L541) and `docs/reference/reporters.mdx`, `list` section; the installed release documentation retains the same target-selection contract. - Failure source: The executed public-example command, console excerpt, and report fields above. The current [run-started producer](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/c74de8d0436086e7a37b8f41130ed460e06513ed/packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts#L801-L825) emits all configured names before selection; the [list header renderer](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/c74de8d0436086e7a37b8f41130ed460e06513ed/packages/e2e/src/report/list.ts#L586-L603) prints that array under `targets:`. - Evidence provenance: observed - Local verification: reproduced - Reproduction completeness: complete #### Restoration check Run the public example's web command with the model key unset. The header should communicate `web`, while the existing correct behavior remains: only the web app starts, all three deterministic tests pass, and both agent tests skip. The configured-target inventory in the JSON report need not change. The supporting fixture below offers a model-free, all-web control: without `--target`, its header should communicate all three targets, and all three tests should run. That unfiltered control is a proposed restoration check, not a run performed in this continuation. #### Additional context The earlier inline fixture is retained as a smaller supporting case, separate from the public reproduction link. I also ran its `--target web --retries 0` command against the release: exit 0, one passing web test, only the web app ready, all three names in the header and `run.targets`, and zero model tokens. All three targets here use the web engine; `ios` and `android` are only names. It needs Python 3 to serve the static page. Install the release runner and web engine in a fresh directory, create these three files, install Chromium with the web engine's install command, and run `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx e2e run --target web --retries 0`. `site/index.html`: ```html Target header reproduction

Hello

``` `e2e.config.ts`: ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; export default { targets: ['ios', 'android', 'web'].map(name => ({ name, engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0', command: { executable: 'python3', args: ['-m', 'http.server', '{port}', '--bind', '127.0.0.1', '--directory', 'site'] }, }, })), } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` `tests/header.e2e.ts`: ```ts import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { expect } from 'e2e'; test('opens the static page', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/'); await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Hello')).toBeVisible(); }); ``` #### References The closed [exploration badge issue](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/issues/1089) concerns `e2e explore`'s target badge, not the `e2e run` header. The current reproduction confirms correct selected-target execution and reports only the header. #### Triage assessment - Impact level: P3 - Assessment status: supported - Impact basis: The run header lists unselected targets, while the selected app command, completed test lines, exit code, and result target IDs retain correct execution. No consequential execution change was observed. - Workaround status: available - Workaround basis: The target-ready line, completed-test badges, and `run.results[].targetId` identify the target that actually executed in both tested CLI builds.

title: fix(release): enforce the #1657 peer-floor rules in the release checks
body: ## Issue Fixes #1657 ## What changed - The 0.12.6 mobile and 0.15.5 web patch releases raised their `e2e` peer floor to `>=0.22.1`, but no stable `e2e@0.22.1` ever shipped, so a fresh install of an unchanged project on `e2e ~0.21.3` fails with ERESOLVE. The published 0.12.6/0.15.5 metadata cannot be changed, so this change does not touch it: it makes the release checks catch the next one, and corrects the floors the next releases will publish. - Rule (b), `scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts`: a peer floor must name a version the sibling released (`## x.y.z` in its CHANGELOG.md), or the runner version in the same release (the version the sibling's pending changesets will release). - Rule (a), `scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts`: a changeset that raises a peer floor past a runner minor the previous range accepted must be a `**Breaking:**` minor. The previous floor is read off the package's release tag; a raise counts only when it cuts off a released version on an older minor. - Rule (c), `scripts/engine-exports.ts` (new): every named import from `e2e` or an `e2e/*` entry, and from `@e2e-dev/core/engine`, must be exported by `e2e` at the floor version, read off the `e2e@` tag. A new `e2e/engine` import counts as raising the floor. - The floors move to the released versions they already meant in practice: acp to `e2e >=0.22.0` (first version exporting the `e2e/agent` rules and tools it imports), limrun to mobile `>=0.12.9 <1` (inside the 0.12 minor, so a patch is right), browser-run to `@e2e-dev/web >=0.16.0` (first web release with the `cdpHeaders` provider seam it implements). Web moves too: its `e2e` floor rises to `>=0.25.0` as a `**Breaking:**` minor (published `@e2e-dev/web@0.16.1` accepts e2e 0.24.0), and the html-reporter changeset is a one-line `**Breaking:**` note at 0.25.0. Mobile stays at `e2e >=0.24.0`, verified against the `@e2e-dev/core@0.24.0` and `e2e@0.24.0` tags. Against the pending release (#1974: core/e2e 0.25.0, web 0.17.0, mobile 0.12.9), `changeset status` gives core/e2e/web/html-reporter minor and mobile/limrun patch. - `AGENTS.md` release paragraph now names the three rules and the scripts that enforce them. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm run test:scripts` (`node --test "scripts/**/*.test.ts"`): 358 pass, 0 fail - `tsc -p scripts`: exit 0 - `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors - `node scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts`: exit 0, stderr empty - `node scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts`: exit 0 | Check | old tree (c74de8d0, new checks) | this branch (13b3a7c98) | | --- | --- | --- | | `node scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` | exit 1, four phantom floors: web/mobile `>=0.22.1`, acp `>=0.21.4`, limrun mobile `>=0.11.1` | exit 0, 5 packages' `e2e` imports verified against their floors (web now `e2e >=0.25.0`, mobile `e2e >=0.24.0`, `@e2e-dev/core >=0.24.0`) | | `node scripts/check-changeset-bumps.ts` | exit 0, 0 floor changes | exit 0, 5 floor changes, none a crossing raise | | Synthetic: web floor `0.18.0` to `0.23.0` with a patch changeset | not run on main | exit 1, rule (a) fires; with a `**Breaking:**` minor it passes | | Synthetic: web floor `0.22.0` | not run on main | exit 1, rule (c) names `stepTimeout`, `EngineDoctorCheck`, `EngineDoctorInfo` | Two notes, not failures: the eight packages peering on `e2e >=0.15.0` are now verified from the committed fixture `scripts/fixtures/e2e@0.15.0.json`, re-derived from the npm tarball (integrity matches the registry) with `resolveEntryExports` reading the shipped `.d.ts`: identical across all 6 subpaths. Rule (c) covers both siblings (`e2e` and `@e2e-dev/core/engine`); an integration's imports from `@e2e-dev/web` or `@e2e-dev/mobile` are the same shape but a different sibling, and are a follow-up, not part of this change.

title: fix(limrun): let tests run on Limrun devices again
body: ## What and why - Every `limrun()` lease failed seconds after Limrun created the device, so no test or `e2e mcp` session could run on one (`@e2e-dev/limrun` 0.2.4 with `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.6): ```text ENGINE_FAILURE: device provider "Limrun" could not lease a device: returned a lease without an id and a daemon baseUrl or JSON client configuration (no `session` or daemon keys) while preparing engine mobile for target "ios" ``` - #1513 put the agent-device `session` on the lease's `client`, so the install and heartbeat clients that reuse that object would name one. The mobile engine reserves that key (`RESERVED_CLIENT_KEYS` in `packages/mobile/src/bindings.ts`) and rejects a lease that sets it. - The driver now leaves `session` off the `client` it returns. Its allocate and install clients and the heartbeat add it themselves from `leaseSession(stateDir)`, the way `packages/mobile/src/lease/` does. - `DriverBinding.client` is typed as `DeviceClientConfig`, so a `session` in that literal no longer compiles. - `leaseSession` is a local copy of mobile's five lines. `@e2e-dev/mobile/lease` does not export it, and exporting it would raise Limrun's peer floor on mobile. - The driver unit test asserted that `session` was on the binding. It now asserts the exact client the engine receives, and fails on main. ## Issue No e2e issue. This is a regression from #1513, found on 2026-11-10 with the published packages. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - A scratch project on the built packages, against a real Limrun iOS simulator. The target is `mobile({ platform: 'ios', device: limrun({ hardTimeout: '15m' }) })` with `app: { bundleId: 'com.apple.mobilesafari' }`, run with `e2e run tests/safari.e2e.ts --video`. The test opens Safari, opens `https://example.com`, closes Safari's first-launch tip, and expects the page text. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | Lease rejected, no test executed, exit 3 | Lease accepted, 1 test passed, exit 0 | | no device to show | ![Safari on the Limrun simulator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f221b1d2-8570-484b-82f1-89b18c43477f) | main: ```text ℹ leasing 1 ios device(s) from Limrun ℹ Limrun (1 of 1): created ios_euna_01m723ptnafjqaby9advh0rnmp ℹ Limrun: released 1 device(s) ERROR infrastructure error ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) device provider "Limrun" could not lease a device: returned a lease without an id and a daemon baseUrl or JSON client configuration (no `session` or daemon keys) while preparing engine mobile for target "ios" Test Files no test files Tests no tests executed Errors 1 error ``` this branch: ```text ℹ leasing 1 ios device(s) from Limrun ℹ Limrun (1 of 1): created ios_euna_01m724he11fya8hmab1bjqgwm3 ℹ Limrun: leased ios_euna_01m724he11fya8hmab1bjqgwm3 ℹ booting limrun:ios:1e6bf23c551b5a69ed8fbb04f9baeb0f (1 of 1) ✓ mobile engine for target "ios" prepared 1.42s ✓ |ios| tests/safari.e2e.ts > Safari opens a page on a Limrun device 7.10s ℹ Limrun: released 1 device(s) Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) ``` - A second test idles 90s before driving Safari, past the lease's 60s TTL. It passed and logged no `driver lease renewal failed` line. I ran no control without the heartbeat. - After the runs the account has no instance in `creating`, `assigned`, or `ready`. - Not run: Android on Limrun, the `appPath` install on a live device (Safari is preinstalled, so that client is unit-tested only), and `e2e mcp` (it reaches the same engine `prepare`). - A fresh-context review of the diff found nothing to fix. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Breaking change: not applicable. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: no change needed, the docs do not describe the lease client's session. - [x] Contract change: not applicable. - [x] Engine contract change: not applicable. title: feat(mcp): open a session without a config by naming the engine
body:
`e2e mcp` only worked next to an `e2e.config.ts`. A coding agent in a fresh directory got `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` and had to set a project up before it could look at an app. Now `open_session` can name the engine instead. Fixes [ENG-1191](https://linear.app/e2e-inc/issue/ENG-1191/e2e-mcp-without-config-file). ```txt open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: "http://localhost:3000"}} open_session { engine: {package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: { platform: "ios", device: {package: "@e2e-dev/limrun", export: "limrun", options: {region: "eu"}} }}, app: {bundleId: "com.example.app"} } ``` - `engine` is a package name, or the factory call a config would write as `{package, export?, options?}`. The second call above is `mobile({ platform: 'ios', device: limrun({ region: 'eu' }) })`. - An option value with only those keys is called first and replaced by its result. That is how an engine gets a device or browser provider, which JSON can't carry. `export` names any export, so providers already on npm work without a release. - `app` takes `url`, `bundleId`, and `appPath` only. - Plain `open_session` with no config still fails. The error now shows both shapes, which is how an agent finds the option. - `engine` is refused where a config exists, and together with `target`, `config`, or `test`. - `@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` default-export their factory. `mobile()` without a platform now says which platforms it takes. ## Where a package comes from ```mermaid flowchart LR A[package name] --> B{in the project?} B -- yes --> L[load it] B -- no --> C{beside e2e?} C -- yes --> L C -- no --> D{in ~/.e2e/engines?} D -- yes --> L D -- no --> E[ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED
names the npm command] ``` - The server installs nothing. The agent runs the command the error prints, in its own shell. - An engine that brings its own copy of `e2e` works. Only the handle's brand and contract version cross. - Core still names no engine: `packages/e2e/src/mcp/default-engine.ts` imports a resolved file, never a specifier. ## Security - This is the first MCP argument that makes the server load code the agent named. `docs/reference/security.mdx` says so. - Only installed packages load. A path, a URL, a `..` segment, and a Node builtin name are refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. - A `__proto__` key in `options` stays an own property. ## Open for a decision - A nested factory call is recognized by shape: `package` plus nothing but `export` and `options`. A third-party engine option that looks like that would be read as a call. No shipped engine or provider has one. The fresh-context reviewer suggested a reserved key such as `{$call: {...}}`. I kept the plain shape, made the options object itself never a call, and made the not-installed error say how the value was read. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: the built `e2e mcp` server in directories with no config. Final build, driven over stdio (`limrun` here is the repo's, with #1663): ```text >>> open_session {} CONFIG_NOT_FOUND: no e2e.config.ts, e2e.config.mts, e2e.config.js, or e2e.config.mjs found in or its parent directories; run e2e init to create one, or pass engine to open_session to open a session without one: {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: ""}}, or {engine: {package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: {platform: "ios"}}, app: {bundleId: ""}} >>> open_session {"engine":"util"} INVALID_ARGUMENT: open_session: engine names an installed package such as "@e2e-dev/web", got "util" >>> open_session {"engine":"@e2e-dev/mobile","app":{"bundleId":"com.apple.mobilesafari"}} INVALID_CONFIG: mobile() needs platform: 'ios' or 'android', got no platform >>> open_session {"engine":{"package":"@e2e-dev/mobile","options":{"platform":"ios","device":{"package":"@e2e-dev/absent-cloud"}}},"app":{"bundleId":"com.apple.mobilesafari"}} ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED: an option value with only package, export, and options keys is read as a factory call, and package @e2e-dev/absent-cloud is not installed in , beside e2e, or in ~/.e2e/engines. Install it once for every project with: npm install --prefix "~/.e2e/engines" @e2e-dev/absent-cloud; then call open_session again >>> open_session {"engine":{"package":"@e2e-dev/mobile","options":{"platform":"ios","device":{"package":"@e2e-dev/limrun","export":"limrun","options":{"hardTimeout":"15m"}}}},"app":{"bundleId":"com.apple.mobilesafari"}} Session 01a1c478-7df0-770e-ab87-b38dcb0a1590 open on target "ios" (platform ios, engine mobile 0.12.6), headless; no config file: one target on @e2e-dev/mobile, every other setting at its default. run_tests and open_session {test} need an e2e.config.ts (npx e2e init writes one). App: com.apple.mobilesafari, launched fresh. >>> close_session {} Session 01a1c478-7df0-770e-ab87-b38dcb0a1590 closed (closed by the agent); 1 tool calls ran. ``` Real clients calling the tools, on earlier builds of this branch: - **Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol** (before the last review-fix commit). The server was added with `codex mcp add`. Codex showed the model `engine?: string | { package, export?, options? }`. Sol opened e2e.com with the string form, tapped `[ docs ]`, read `test_lines`, then opened `/docs/quickstart` with the object form. Every step passed. - **Claude Code** (string form). A fresh session with the server registered by `claude mcp add` opened e2e.com, went to the docs, and returned a four-line draft test. - **Two copies of `e2e`.** The runner alone in one tree, `@e2e-dev/web` installed with the printed command into a separate `~/.e2e/engines`: a session opened, `run_code` passed a tap and an assertion. - **iOS simulator** (string form). `@e2e-dev/mobile` drove Safari on a local simulator to e2e.com and the docs. | Web session, docs page | Limrun device, nested provider | | --- | --- | | ![web](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3c28f9d-6e04-4731-ab5e-02b96b5b16a1) | ![limrun](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92784376-4830-4461-9d66-7b5cdcea9aa2) | Not verified: Android, and an engine installed with pnpm or Bun into `~/.e2e/engines`. ## Review - Fresh-context review, seven findings. Fixed: `import`-only packages failed to load, an installed package with no built entry was reported as not installed, `engine: "@e2e-dev/mobile"` failed with a raw `TypeError`, a Node builtin name became a file import, two untested hunks, a stale comment. Kept with changes: the shape rule above. - Bot review on the PR, eight findings. Fixed six: a skill example with no `app.url` value, a `__proto__` test that would pass if the key were dropped, "no e2e.config.ts" where any config name counts, one debugging-table row covering two error codes, the string shorthand missing from AGENTS.md, and a security sentence that read as covering more than `engine`. Declined two: offering `engine` when a lookalike config file exists (that branch predates this PR and names the rename as the fix), and wildcard subpaths of `import`-only packages (the import fallback is deliberately narrow and fails with an explicit error). - Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved. That was before the review-fix commits. Docs pass: `docs/mcp-server.mdx` 199 to 212 lines, 1065 to 1105 prose words. `docs/writing-an-engine.mdx` 306 to 326 lines, 1606 to 1665 words. Both gain one short section; nothing was cut. Written by Claude Fable 5.2 in T3 Code, on the Claude Code harness.

title: perf(mobile): skip the post-gesture stabilization wait for a test's swipe and scroll
body:
- A test's swipe and scroll now send `postGestureStabilization: false`, so agent-device stops holding the next read for up to 3.5 s (1.5 s poll budget plus a 2 s distrust extension) after a gesture the test checks with `expect`. The agent's gestures keep the wait.
- Skipping the wait alone breaks taps: `scrollUntilVisible` finds the control while the list still coasts, and the tap lands on a moving list, which swallows it to stop the scroll. The step passes and nothing navigates. So the first action on a control within 2 s of a skipped wait re-reads the control every 100 ms until two reads agree on its bounds (`steadied` in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`). A list that already rests costs one extra snapshot.
- `fill` and `clear` keep `relocated`'s input checks on every re-read, and the poll stops with `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` when the action budget cannot fit another poll. Both came from the fresh-context review.
- agent-device 0.21.36 ignores the option, so nothing speeds up until the dependency moves to a release that has it. The nightly `0.21.37-nightly.20261109.153` accepts it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Surface: the built CLI on callstack/react-native-pager-view (40 tests in 16 files) on an iOS simulator (iPhone 17), cold boot per run, one build at a time, load below 2 before each run. Command: `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --target ios`, with `node_modules/e2e` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` pointing at the built worktrees.
- Time is the sum of attempt durations over the 38 tests that passed in every run below. Run-to-run noise on this suite is 1 to 2%.

| | main | this branch, nightly agent-device | this branch, agent-device 0.21.36 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Passed | 38/40, 39/40 (two runs) | 39/40 | 39/40 |
| 38 common tests | 427.1 s, 433.0 s | 409.0 s (-4.7%) | 438.1 s (+1.9%, inside noise) |
| `locator.tap` median | 573 ms, 556 ms | 767 ms | 613 ms |

- The one failure in every run, `issue-1096-keyboard-shrink`, fails on main too (`ENGINE_FAILURE`, "behind the visible keyboard"). It is not this change.
- Without the steady read, the same flag failed `issue-1154-page-change-focus` in 3 of 3 runs and `issue-1050-back-gesture` in 3 of 3 (1 of 4 on main). The first tap after a scroll got slower in exchange (714 to 767 ms against 556 to 573 ms), since the wait moved from the scroll to that tap. Lowering `transition` to 200 ms cut that cost but added 3 more failures, so it is not in this change.
- The main rows ran at `f4bf5299`; this branch is on `e27f492c`, which has unrelated commits in between.
- Tests: `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts` covers the flag per origin, the re-read until bounds agree, no re-read for the agent, a field that turns disabled after a gesture, and the budget stop.

## Review

A fresh-context review (gpt-6.1-sol) found two issues, both fixed and covered by tests: the re-read dropped `fill`'s input checks, and its 100 ms sleep ignored the operation's remaining budget.

title: feat(cli): e2e compile turns recorded agent.act steps into test code
body:
> **RFC, draft.** It works end to end and is tested, but I'm opening it to agree on the shape first: the command, the block format, and what counts as safe to compile. Names, codes, and defaults are all open to change. Open questions are at the end. `e2e compile` replaces a recorded `agent.act()` call with the `screen.*` and `app.*` lines its replay cache recording repeats, in place in the test, between two JSDoc comments. - **Compared with the replay cache**, a compiled step trades self-healing for review. A replay that doesn't match hands off to the agent. A compiled line fails like any hand-written locator, and `e2e compile revert` brings the agent back. - **Compared with `e2e mcp`'s `test_lines`**, which checks each line against the live screen while the agent walks the flow, compile writes from the recording alone. So it checks its own work: after writing, it runs each compiled test once and keeps only the blocks that pass. ## Why An `agent.act()` with no recording costs a model round trip, and a reviewer only ever sees the instruction, never what ran. The replay cache removes the model call, but a recorded step lives in `.e2e/cache/` as a JSON file named by its key hash, which never shows up in the test's diff. It also misses when its key changes (another engine or engine contract, the replay policy, the app's identity, a renamed test), and then the step calls the model again. This proposes a third state between "the agent does it" and "a person wrote it". The agent finds the path once, and `compile` writes that path into the test as code a reviewer reads and that runs with no model and no cache. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["agent.act('...')"] -->|e2e run records| B[(replay cache
trace-1)] B -->|e2e compile| C["/** @compiled */
screen.* lines
/** @end compiled */"] C -->|app changed, test breaks| D[e2e compile revert] D --> A ``` ## What it looks like ```bash npx e2e compile tests/checkout.e2e.ts # record, write, run once, keep what passes npx e2e compile tests/checkout.e2e.ts --dry-run # print the change; run and edit nothing npx e2e compile status [--json] # every step: compiles, compiled, stale, or why it stays npx e2e compile revert tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12 # put the agent.act() back (--dry-run to preview) ``` `--dry-run` is the only mode flag, and means the same on `compile` and `revert`, as on `e2e upgrade`. With several targets, `--target ` picks whose recordings compile. `examples/with-vite/tests/agentic.e2e.ts` before: ```ts test('the agent gets a greeting', { skip }, async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/'); await agent.act('get the app to greet {name}', { params: { name: 'Grace' } }); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('hello, Grace!'); await agent.assert('the app greets Grace by name'); }); ``` After `e2e compile` (recorded with Claude Code over `@e2e-dev/acp`; comments trimmed): ```ts test('the agent gets a greeting', { skip }, async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/'); /** * @compiled agent.act("get the app to greet {name}") * @from "await agent.act('get the app to greet {name}', { params: { name: 'Grace' } });" * @recording fd36642b39fe * @step 9dadd2295d82.71e0d496a8c9 * @recordedAt 2026-11-10 * @compiledAt 2026-11-10 * @verifiedAt 2026-11-10 */ await screen.getByRole("textbox", "name").fill("Grace"); await screen.getByRole("button", "greet").tap(); await expect(screen.getByText("hello, Grace!")).toBeVisible(); /** @end compiled */ await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('hello, Grace!'); await agent.assert('the app greets Grace by name'); }); ``` - A step with no recording is recorded first. `compile` runs its test (`e2e run `), and a step whose run does not pass stays an `agent.act()`. - The block is a pair of JSDoc comments found through oxc's comment list, so a trailing comment or CRLF line endings don't lose it. `@from` keeps the original statement byte for byte, and `revert` puts exactly that back (fixtures and imports compile added stay). The reverted call has the same cache key, so its recording replays again. - `@recording` and `@step` let `status` mark a block `stale` once its step is recorded again. - Credentials and secrets are written by name (`credentials.user('admin').password`, `secrets.get('pin')`), and `unique()` params as the expression the test passed. No value the ledger redacted can reach the file. ## When a recording is pinned to a call `compile` touches only a call a recording is pinned to. Everything else stays an `agent.act()`, and `e2e compile status` gives the reason as a code. - The call is a literal instruction in a bare `await agent.act(...)` statement of the test's own callback. A call inside a loop or a branch (`nested-call`) or in a helper (`not-in-body`) stays, because the source doesn't say how many times it runs. So does every call of a test declared in a loop (`loop-declared`), because one source serves several tests. - Params the source spells out are projected and digested the way the cache key is (`validateParams` + `templateParams`; `tests/unit/compile-params.test.ts` pins this against the runtime). A recording made with other params, under another replay policy (when the recording names its policy; older ones don't), or counted together with a helper's call is not taken (`tests/integration/cli-compile-pinning.test.ts`). - There must be one agent, one recording per call by `callIndex`, and a step's repeats compile together or not at all. A call with hooks (`onAction`, `onBeforeAction`) or a `timeout` stays (`step-options`). A target with no test id is located by its role and name, text, or placeholder, and its line ends in `// unverified locator`. A call whose params the source doesn't spell out takes its test's only recording of that instruction. Then the check: `compile` runs each compiled test once on every target, with no retries, and puts back the blocks of any test that doesn't pass (`verify-failed`). The blocks that pass get `@verifiedAt` and lose their `// unverified locator` comments. Some steps never compile, by design: a value read off the screen during that run (`runtime-value`), a project tool (`project-tool`), a hover or drag at a bare viewport point (`point`), and keyboard input to whatever had focus (`focus-keyboard`). Those stay with the agent. A tap at a bare viewport point, as on a canvas, compiles to `screen.tapAt({ x, y })`; it holds only on a viewport of the recorded size, which the checking run confirms. ## Coverage on this repo's examples and demos I ran every `agent.act()` in `examples/` and `apps/` on current `main` through `compile`, in a separate worktree. The examples ship an AI Gateway config, so for the run I swapped in my own subscriptions: Claude Code over `@e2e-dev/acp`, and ChatGPT through `e2e/oauth/chatgpt` for the dogfood suite that needs the built-in agent's project tools. The two benchmarks used their committed recordings. The output is a demo branch, not for merge: **[the compiled tests](https://github.com/gronxb/e2e/compare/feat/e2e-compile...feat/e2e-compile-demo)**. | Suite | `agent.act` steps | Compiled and passed | Left, and why | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `examples/with-{vite,next,astro,angular}` (web) | 8 | 8 | | | `examples/with-swiftui` (iOS), `with-compose` (Android) | 4 | 4 | | | `examples/with-{kotlin-multiplatform,flutter,maui}` (Android + iOS, verified on both), `with-expo` (iOS + Android + web, verified on all three) | 8 | 8 | | | `apps/testbed` `tests-agent` | 21 | 18 | 1 `focus-keyboard` (a canvas form typed through the keyboard); 1 `nested-call` (the test reads the step's summary); 1 `not-recorded` (the step ends where it began, so the cache keeps nothing) | | `apps/testbed` dogfood suites | 9 | 0 | 4 `project-tool`; 5 `not-recorded` (4 tests written to fail, 1 tool-only step with no action to replay) | | `apps/web-benchmark` `tests-agent` | 32 | 10 as written, **24** with one test per scenario | 4 `runtime-value`; 2 `nested-call` (expected failures inside a helper); 1 `focus-keyboard`; 1 `verify-failed` (a 431-screen scroll) | | `apps/mobile-benchmark` `tests-agent` (iOS) | 24 | 0 as written, **9** with one test per scenario | 2 `runtime-value`; 1 `focus-keyboard`; 2 `project-tool`; 4 `not-recorded` (the recording run did not pass); 6 `verify-failed` (below) | | **Total** | **106** | **48** as written, **71** with one test per scenario | | - Every example step compiles and passes on every target the example runs. Every step left in `apps/` has a code, and none is `ambiguous-recording`. - **One test per scenario.** Both benchmarks declare one test per scenario in a loop, so every scenario is `loop-declared` as written. The demo branch also declares each scenario as its own test, with the same titles and instructions, so the committed recordings still match; that is what the bold numbers count. It is a demo of what the loop costs, not a change I'm proposing to the benchmarks. - **What the checking run caught.** A SwiftUI greeting recording that tapped "열기" ("Open"), a transient iOS prompt, went back to `agent.act()`; a fresh recording compiled. On the mobile benchmark it put back six: two recordings that tapped iOS's "Not Now" and "Allow" dialogs, which a later run doesn't show; a scroll that stopped short of its row; two test ids that match several nodes on a later run (`PXGGridLayout-Info` in the photo picker, `Card` in Stripe's sheet); and a tap the keyboard covered. Fresh recordings of these fail the same way, so they are gaps in compile or the recorder, listed below. - **Simulator state.** The benchmark app asks for the microphone on launch while the permission is undetermined, and the system prompt covers the home list the scenarios open from. Mobile numbers are from a simulator with the prompt answered. - **Cross-platform ids.** Android reports an `AutomationId` or resource id as `:id/`; compiled lines write the short form, which the mobile engine matches on Android and iOS alike, so the .NET MAUI blocks recorded on Android pass on iOS. - **Imported names.** Compiled lines use a name the file already imports, such as the mobile benchmark's `expect` from its own fixtures module. ## Open questions - **Name.** `compile` can read as TypeScript compilation. Is it the right word next to `e2e cache` and `e2e run`? - **Block format.** JSDoc comments leave the public API unchanged. The alternative is a construct the runtime knows about (`agent.act(instruction, { compiled: { run } })`), which would let a failing compiled step hand off to the agent instead of failing. - **A mode with no run.** `compile` always runs the compiled tests, so it needs the app, its devices, and a model for any judgment left in the test. Restricted to test-id targets, a write with no run would have compiled 15 of the 106 steps above, and no canvas tap. Is that mode worth a flag, or is `--dry-run` enough? - **The checking run.** Is one passing run on every target, with no retries, enough? - **CI.** `compile` exits 0 even after `verify-failed`. Should `status` exit non-zero on `stale` blocks or below a coverage floor? A run with `CI` set records nothing unless `cache.mode` is `read-write`, so compile mostly belongs on a laptop today. - **Recordings after compile.** A compiled step never replays its recording again, except after `revert`. Should compile leave the committed recordings alone, or delete them in the same change? - **Date tags.** `@recordedAt`, `@compiledAt`, and `@verifiedAt` change on every recompile, which is diff noise. Are they worth it next to `@recording`? - **`status --json`.** Not a schema'd wire format yet. Should it be `compile-status-1` with fixtures? - **Recording verified lines.** If the recorder kept the verified test line for each action (what the MCP session does in `mcp/test-lines.ts`), most `// unverified locator` lines would be certain before the checking run. - **Engine verbs.** The agent's keyboard dismissal on mobile has a test line, `device.dismissKeyboard()`, but it belongs to `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s fixture, and core never names an engine's fixtures. Compile drops it, and a later tap behind the keyboard fails. Should an engine contribute compile lines for its own verbs? - **Twins by test id.** A recording names a target by test id without its position when the id repeats (seven photo grid cells share one), so the line is ambiguous on replay. Should the recorder keep a position whenever an id is not unique? - **Loops and helpers.** Should `compile` emit a separate compiled test per recording for a loop-declared test, or leave those alone? ## Verified Ran it locally: yes The worktree run above, on current `main`. For example, `examples/with-vite` with this branch built and packed: ```text $ npx e2e compile tests/agentic.e2e.ts --dry-run ✓ L11 "get the app to greet {name}" → 2 action(s), 1 assertion(s) (2 unverified locator(s)) ✓ L21 "press greet without typing a name" → 1 action(s), 1 assertion(s) (1 unverified locator(s)) 2 step(s) would compile, 0 left to the agent; without --dry-run, the files change and a run checks the lines $ npx e2e compile tests/agentic.e2e.ts ... ✓ L11 "get the app to greet {name}" → 2 action(s), 1 assertion(s) (2 unverified locator(s)) ✓ L21 "press greet without typing a name" → 1 action(s), 1 assertion(s) (1 unverified locator(s)) Verifying 2 compiled test(s): e2e run tests/agentic.e2e.ts:7 tests/agentic.e2e.ts:18 ... ✓ the agent gets a greeting passed with its compiled lines ✓ the agent finds the empty-name error passed with its compiled lines 2 step(s) compiled, 0 left to the agent $ npx e2e run tests/agentic.e2e.ts --video on ✓ the agent gets a greeting > agent.assert "the app greets Grace by name" · 1 model call ✓ the agent finds the empty-name error > agent.assert "the app asks for a name" · 1 model call ... Tests 2 passed (2) ``` No `agent.act` step is left in the run; only the judgments call a model. The compiled greeting test, 1.5 s into its run ([video](https://github.com/gronxb/e2e/blob/feat/e2e-compile-demo/compile-demo/compiled-greeting.webm)): ![The with-vite example after the compiled greeting step: the app reads hello, Grace!](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gronxb/e2e/feat/e2e-compile-demo/compile-demo/compiled-greeting.png) The file it writes matches the demo branch's, dates aside. `pnpm check`, the unit suite (3600 tests), and the two compile integration files (13 tests: record, write, check, revert, the `verify-failed` path, and pinning) pass. Secrets: on the demo branch, `git grep` for the testbed's and the web benchmark's credential passwords finds nothing, and the fills read the credential by name: ```text apps/web-benchmark/tests-agent/login-form.e2e.ts: await screen.getByTestId("password-input").fill(credentials.user("benchmark").password); apps/testbed/tests-agent/act.e2e.ts: await screen.getByRole("textbox", "Password").fill(credentials.user("admin").password); ```

title: fix(mobile): boot a shut-down device when none is booted and no device is named
body:
An iOS target with no `device`, on a Mac where no simulator is booted, fails `e2e run` in `prepare`:

```
ENGINE_FAILURE (launch) boot failed: 43 devices match this request equally; select one explicitly
```

The `e2e init` iOS preset writes `mobile({ platform: 'ios' })`, so the first run of a fresh project hits this on most Macs.

## Issue

Refs ENG-1037

## Cause

With nothing booted, the pool binds one empty slot, and both `warm` and the worker's `init` call `devices.boot({ platform: 'ios' })`. agent-device ranks every shut-down iPhone simulator equally and throws `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`.

## Fix

- agent-device 0.21.35 added an opt-in tie-break for exactly this (callstack/agent-device#4042, which replaced the e2e-side pick in #1433). e2e already pins 0.21.36, but never opted in.
- `bootRequest` (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`) adds `pick: 'newest'` when the selection names no device. Both boot calls go through it. A named device, UDID, or serial is sent unchanged.
- agent-device's `newest` prefers a phone or tablet over a TV, then the newest OS, then name order (not device age: `iPhone 16e` sorts before `iPhone 17`). Several booted matches still fail. Shut-down Android AVDs report no OS version, so on Android the name decides.
- Docs (`mobile.mdx`, the `device` option JSDoc and its reference copy, the skill's setup reference) say how the device is picked.

```ts
export function bootRequest(selection: DeviceSelection): DeviceSelection & Pick<DeviceBootOptions, 'pick'> {
  const named = selection.device ?? selection.udid ?? selection.serial;
  return named === undefined ? { ...selection, pick: 'newest' } : selection;
}
```

## Known gaps, all in agent-device

**A Vision Pro simulator can win the pick.** agent-device reports visionOS simulators as `target: 'mobile'` and ranks them level with iPhones under `--platform ios`, and no selector field excludes them. On equal OS versions the name decides, so `Apple Vision Pro` beats `iPhone 17`. Checked with agent-device's own `resolveInventoryDeviceSelection` on 0.21.36 and on `0.21.37-nightly.20261110.154`: shut-down Apple Vision Pro, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17, and iPad Pro, all on 26.1, give `Apple Vision Pro`; without the Vision Pro, `iPhone 17`. So on a Mac with the visionOS runtime installed, the run goes from a clear `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH` to booting the Vision Pro and failing later. Macs without that runtime get the fix. Naming a `device` avoids both. The real fix is ranking visionOS below iOS in agent-device's pick, not a second picker in e2e (the approach #1433 dropped).

**The pick ignores session claims.** agent-device's tie-break never reads `claimedBy`, so two runs starting at once on a cold Mac can both pick the device the first is still booting. Before this PR both failed with `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`. Left open for the maintainer in the review thread.

**A paired iPhone that isn't connected counts as booted.**

Verifying this on a Mac with a paired iPhone turned up callstack/agent-device#4209 (reported from #1528): agent-device lists a paired iPhone that CoreDevice cannot reach as `booted: true`. With nothing booted, e2e then drives that phone instead of reaching the no-booted path, and the run fails at app launch. The fix, callstack/agent-device#4210, merged on 2026-11-04, after 0.21.36, so it is only in nightlies. No e2e change is needed for it: the pool already reads `booted`. Once agent-device 0.21.37 ships, a bump picks it up, and ENG-1037 can be closed after a live run on a Mac with a paired phone.

## Verified

Ran it locally: no - the live simulator run was blocked by callstack/agent-device#4209 (above); unit tests only.
- Unit: `tests/unit/engine.test.ts` and `provider.test.ts` now expect `{ platform: 'ios', pick: 'newest' }` for an unscoped boot, and the existing UDID tests still expect no `pick`. Reverting `bootRequest` fails all four.
- Live: MacBook, no simulator booted, a scratch project matching the `e2e init` iOS preset (Settings app, no `device`), built packages, main and this branch. On both, agent-device listed the unavailable paired iPhone as booted (callstack/agent-device#4209 above), so e2e logged `1 booted ios device(s); driving 1: <the paired iPhone>` and never reached the changed code. No simulator was booted.
- Upstream: callstack/agent-device#4042 checked the same scenario live on agent-device (plain `boot` refuses, `--pick newest` boots iPhone 17, two booted devices still refuse).

---

Made with Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, running inside T3 Code.

title: chore: add context7.json to claim the Context7 library
body: Context7 indexes this repo so coding agents can pull e2e docs through its MCP server. To claim the library, the repo root needs a `context7.json` with the library URL and our team public key, and that file can also hold the parsing config. - `url` and `public_key` claim `context7.com/tester-army/e2e`. The key is public and meant to be committed. - `folders`: `docs` (the docs pages) and `skills/e2e` (the consumer skill). Source code, tests, `apps/`, and `examples/` stay out. - `excludeFolders`: `docs/images`, and `plugins`, which holds a generated copy of `skills/e2e`. - `excludeFiles`: the contributor files at the root (`AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`). Context7 always reads root markdown files, so `README.md` is still indexed. After merge, click "Claim Library" in Context7 and pick "context7.json" as the config source. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Validated `context7.json` with ajv against Context7's published schema (`https://context7.com/schema/context7.json`): valid. - The claim itself can only run after this lands on `main`. --- Changes made by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).
