title: Mobile: unchanged controls can receive taps before a dismissed overlay releases input
body:
## What happened

A deterministic tap immediately after closing a fading overlay can land on the overlay while e2e reports that the intended underlying button was tapped. The underlying button already exists at the same accessibility bounds, so the unchanged-control shortcut skips the configured transition wait. Existence at unchanged bounds does not establish that the control can receive the touch.

Expected: the framework synchronizes this sequence implicitly. Test code should remain:

```ts
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Close overlay').tap();
await screen.getByRole('button', 'Underlying action').tap();
```

No explicit wait method or additional sleep should be required.

## Public native reproduction

[App source, commands, reports, native events and all recordings](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/b2126a9bba45a91e016284b622cf297dc60ac033/reproductions/overlay-transition-native-1563/README.md).

- Unmodified main `d8b694ffa48b04c94d70a11cc280267f1ea9a100`, after #1564. Source builds: e2e 0.23.0 / @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.6; agent-device 0.21.36; Node 24.22.0; iPhone 15 Pro / iOS 27.0.
- The constructed UIKit composite overlay fades its panel and backdrop for 750 ms while their touch-owning parent remains until animation completion. The underlying button remains exposed to accessibility. This is a custom inline-overlay reproduction; the stock UIKit page-sheet control passes.
- The 750 ms case fails with `transition: 1000` and all three repeats at `transition: 2000`, with underlying taps 0 / overlay touches 1.
- [Trace step 4](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/blob/b2126a9bba45a91e016284b622cf297dc60ac033/reproductions/overlay-transition-native-1563/evidence/main-1000/results/overlay-uikit-fade-750ms-96e13e53b3b43ced/trace.md#steps) reports a successful underlying tap. The native event log places the overlay touch 283.48 ms after dismissal begins, before completion at +752.70 ms.

## Existing upstream work checked

- #1564 fixes root swipes and is already present in the failing build.
- #1644 handles SDK coverage marks and refusal reporting; implicit covered-target retries remain unresolved. It does not fix an input that the SDK dispatches to the wrong recipient.
- #1641 handles post-gesture movement. #1679 documents that test locator steps bypass SDK settling.
- Native SDK 0.21.36 checks also reproduce with its existing 150 ms and default 300 ms settling, including `settled: true`. Its `presentedSurface` stays `absent` throughout this inline overlay.
- Related coverage-signal work is tracked in callstack/agent-device#4347 and #1324.

## Native readiness investigation and fix direction

The SDK already has an internal native `querySelector` path that checks `XCUIElement.isHittable`. A direct diagnostic against the owned runner correctly rejects the unique underlying control while the inline overlay is open and fading, then finds it after animation completion. The ordinary SDK press ignores that result and still sends the intercepted input. The normal public attributes query instead reports geometric `hittable: true` during the obstruction.

Reuse the existing native predicate inside the SDK's pre-dispatch readiness owner. Wait within the operation budget until the intended target is actionable, preserving target identity and rejecting ambiguity before input. Validate duplicate/anonymous target behavior and benchmark the additional query cost. The native diagnostic establishes the signal for this fixture; generic identity binding still needs implementation and verification.

No public test wait method, private runner access from the e2e adapter, duplicate overlay detector, or blanket adapter delay is proposed. Related SDK coverage work remains in callstack/agent-device#4347.

Supersedes the explicit-wait API proposal in #1563.


### Implementation and verification

- Implicit readiness: [agent-device #4391](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4391), tracked in [#4388](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/4388), now at `e66ec2a063b5fde0ff74609322bee54535003478` on base `eec35e9`. It uses the shared admission owner, one observation loop/request budget and one evidence construction/copy/remap owner. After a blocked target becomes ready, a fresh canonical capture and new-generation proof precede input. The latest revision also fixes elapsed motion refusals, retains remapped Android evidence and declares readiness intent at the tap owner. No public wait API is added.
- Pending-request cancellation: [#1685](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1685), tracked separately in [#1684](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/1684), remains green at `d45a6e15` with feedback addressed. It forwards pending-action signals; already-sent input may still finish.

[Current source, actual traces and all 23 original recordings](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/70410623beb0a3b598b2e179583757a951546453/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/public-curated-e66-review-followup) cover selector/ref readiness, real default deadlines, caller aborts, motion and readiness in the same loop, and first idle presses. Ten traced SDK cases and four matched comparison cases pass. Nine proof-harness failures and their partial results stay visible. All5,384 video samples decode without errors. Actual native products retain historical build attribution. Caller cancellation remains dispatch unknown despite observed zero target/late input.

The exact local gate passes 15 runnable checks,19,543 unit tests plus three existing skips, and396 related tests. Hosted CI has12 successful checks,two skips,and two failed checks from one iOS Settings replay failure plus its aggregate. Native tests and the actual automated review pass. That replay failure remains under investigation; local27.0 comparisons do not establish a flake on hosted26.2/SDK26.5.

The [when-unknown idle-cost proposal](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/4456#issuecomment-6834897348) and coherent98-file/3,517-gross-line size exception await explicit maintainer disposition. Neither approval nor merge readiness is claimed. Partial-point occlusion remains separate in [agent-device #4347](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/4347).

### Historical verification

[Historical SDK proof](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/4f90a18e66d12e037ed1f408a967910f0f3b70e5/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/fixture-review-c7d640f) records source `c7d640f`, its clean exact gate and current native golden-data recheck. The final follow-up changes six test-data fields only; all 629 built JavaScript files and shipped native fingerprint match verified `17a9673`. That earlier append retains the fresh production/unit builds, nine passing selected native tests and unchanged-harness overlay video, plus links to matched readiness costs and broader fixture coverage. Every run keeps its original source attribution. [Accepted-input ordering evidence](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/6521b964ed5c21c1a591b83e0ed421393dd17d3b/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/accepted-press-review-9dc33e8) records the bounded SDK drain/serialization contract and actual app relaunch behavior, including its limits.

Both implementation PRs remain open. After the SDK fix ships, the consumer dependency can be updated and the original fixture retained as regression coverage.

title: Android: snapshot omits WebView-hosted modal dialog windows
body:
Environment:
- `e2e` 0.23.0
- Target: `android`, Pixel 10 Pro XL emulator, Android 17 (API 37)
- App: a React app in a WebView, built with the `e2e-test` profile

Summary:

When a modal dialog is open inside the WebView, the runner's snapshot (`screen.tree()` and locators) returns only the content behind the dialog. The dialog's title, body text, and buttons are missing. The same app and flow work on iOS.

Steps:
1. Reach a screen that shows a modal dialog inside the WebView.
2. While the dialog is visible, call `screen.tree()` or locate a button inside it.

Expected: the dialog and its buttons are in the snapshot, and a role or text locator can find them.

Actual: only the page behind the dialog is in the snapshot. The locator matches no nodes.

Evidence that the OS exposes the dialog:

With the runner stopped, a native `uiautomator dump` taken while the dialog was visible contained:

```
android.app.AlertDialog   text="<dialog title>"
  android.widget.Button   text="<primary action>"  clickable=true  bounds=[159,2103][1185,2286]
  android.widget.Button   text="Maybe later"       clickable=true  bounds=[546,2355][798,2430]
```

So the platform exposes the control, but the snapshot doesn't include the dialog window.

Questions:
1. Does the agent-device snapshot intentionally include only the main activity window?
2. Is there a supported way to include dialog windows, or to target nodes from the native hierarchy when the semantic tree omits them?
3. Is there a recommended workaround that doesn't use coordinate taps?

title: Mobile: press requests can deliver input after the action has timed out
body:
A mobile press request can continue resolving or waiting inside agent-device after the adapter has already failed the action. The adapter races the SDK promise against its input budget but does not pass the SDK's existing request cancellation signal.

### Reproduction

On the original main baseline `d8b694ffa48b04c94d70a11cc280267f1ea9a100` (`e2e` 0.23.0, `@e2e-dev/mobile` 0.12.6):

1. Dismiss a standalone UIKit fixture's overlay, which retains input for a three-second exit animation.
2. Press the underlying fixture button with a 500 ms action timeout.
3. Observe the fixture's native event counter after the action fails.

With the implicit native-readiness candidate `f2bc18d` described in callstack/agent-device#4388, the step fails at 501 ms, but its SDK request continues for 3071 ms and then delivers the input. This native reproduction deliberately uses that candidate to expose a pending pre-input wait; it does not claim the currently published SDK already waits for this overlay.

A deterministic reproduction with the real published SDK client and a controlled transport also shows that the adapter never forwards caller cancellation. No application-specific data or UI is needed.

### Expected behavior

- Forward caller interruption to ordinary SDK press requests.
- Cancel a still-pending press when the adapter stops waiting for its response.
- Preserve the existing minimum 250 ms acknowledgement allowance: an input already sent with a 100 ms budget may still return its acknowledgement at 180 ms.
- Preserve unrelated SDK refusals and nonpress error classifications.
- Keep the existing daemon session/device serialization and shared recording-finalization behavior.

This is the adapter-side cancellation companion to #1682 and callstack/agent-device#4388. Native readiness belongs inside the SDK; tests should not need a new wait API.

### Implementation and verification

[PR #1685](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1685), current source head [`d45a6e1551629f0f2dd165b739d6970a059febeb`](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/commit/d45a6e1551629f0f2dd165b739d6970a059febeb), forwards the SDK request signal for ordinary press calls while preserving the acknowledgement allowance and error classifications. This covers taps, double taps, focus, check/uncheck and the taps used to focus a field or dismiss a keyboard tip. Other input request lifetimes and shared recording finalization are unchanged. The package still pins published agent-device 0.21.36.

The newer matched native comparison uses mobile main baseline `d8b694f` versus live-tested mobile `c282cf9`, with separately identified SDK source `965e77b` and matching native `a55` assets on both sides. Main fails the zero-input assertion after a 502 ms tap timeout because input later reaches the fixture; the fix preserves zero input after the three-second fade and allows exactly one input from the following attempt. [Fixture, commands, exact hashes and all five videos](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/295f841a902472f56dc5f90741fbac80d9363236/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-review-c282cf9). This remains candidate-SDK evidence, not a claim that 0.21.36 already has implicit native-readiness polling.

A separate real-native acceptance probe waits for the native runner's actual `COMMAND_ACCEPTED` for a double tap, aborts the caller, then immediately starts the next attempt, relaunches the fixture and taps once. Main with recording off, the fix with recording off, and the fix with recording on all preserve the subsequent device ordering. Each fresh process receives exactly its own tap. With recording off, local attempt admission can precede native completion; the SDK fences the subsequent device work. [Three videos, native command markers and process-specific event logs](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/6521b964ed5c21c1a591b83e0ed421393dd17d3b/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/accepted-press-review-9dc33e8).

Head `d45a6e15` adds test coverage to the unchanged production source from `e15c0585`. All 524 mobile tests and the full repository check pass in a separately installed checkout with pinned agent-device 0.21.36. The [coverage proof](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/d90ddf91f5cffa331a4934ba0c920ad5b753b71c/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-signal-coverage-d45a6e1) records all eight isolated press-route bypass mutations failing the new assertions, plus the fresh device-fixture budget signal delivering one late input and failing the zero-input oracle; restoring the source passes.

The native cancellation videos above retain their original tested commits and SDK identifiers. Those dedicated probes were not repeated for the structural revision or this test-only follow-up.

All current-head CI checks passed at `d45a6e15`, including iOS and Android deterministic suites and the five-version Node matrix. The latest automated review reports zero issues; all optional re-review points have dispositions.

The supported cancellation contract is bounded: [SDK issue #3383](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3383) and merged [PR #3385](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3385), already present in 0.21.36, hold session/device locks while an accepted native command drains. The original native-command deadline, unavailable status or `notAccepted` can end draining with work unconfirmed and its charge abandoned. Client-promise rejection is not a universal native-termination guarantee. Arbitrary custom transports that ignore abort bypass the production daemon's locks; the controlled-transport reproduction is not native-device evidence.

All public application sources and media are constructed fixtures. This issue remains open until the implementation is merged.

title: fix(mobile): cancel presses when the response wait expires
body: ## Summary - Cancel pending SDK `interactions.press` calls when the run is interrupted or their response wait expires. Keep the existing 250 ms acknowledgement allowance and nonretryable timeout result. - Route every press through `InputBudget.press` and pass the whole operation to the budget factory, so callers cannot omit the signal forward. No new test API. - Limit cancellation to taps, double taps, focus, check and uncheck actions, and the press calls used to focus a field or dismiss a keyboard tip. Other input requests retain their existing lifetimes. Canceling a promise does not prove an accepted native hold, gesture or text sequence finished; extending cancellation to those requests needs a separate drain policy. Recording finalization is unchanged. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Operation signal] --> B[Input budget] B --> C[SDK press] D[Response wait expires] --> E[Abort SDK request] C -- answers --> F[Return original result] ``` ## Issue Fixes #1684. Related: #1682 and callstack/agent-device#4388. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI, `e2e run --video on --trace on`, on a constructed UIKit fixture. The same test and SDK build reproduce late input on main and prevent it here. | main `d8b694f` | this branch `c282cf9` | | --- | --- | | Tap fails at 502 ms, then lands after the three-second overlay finishes. The unchanged zero-input assertion fails. | Zero input after the overlay finishes; the immediately following attempt receives exactly its own one tap. All three cases pass. | [Main failure video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shamilovtim/e2e/295f841a902472f56dc5f90741fbac80d9363236/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-review-c282cf9/main-timeout/video.mp4) · [Fixed timeout video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shamilovtim/e2e/295f841a902472f56dc5f90741fbac80d9363236/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-review-c282cf9/fixed-timeout/video.mp4) · [Next attempt video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shamilovtim/e2e/295f841a902472f56dc5f90741fbac80d9363236/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-review-c282cf9/fixed-next-attempt/video.mp4) [Exact commands, tests, native events and all five videos](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/295f841a902472f56dc5f90741fbac80d9363236/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-review-c282cf9). The package still pins agent-device 0.21.36, used by the SDK boundary tests. The native overlay comparison deliberately uses the separately identified readiness candidate `965e77b` and matching native assets on both builds. It is not a claim that the published SDK already has readiness polling. Accepted native iOS input was verified separately on the same SDK/native build: main with recording off, this branch with recording off, and this branch with recording on. After the native runner accepted a double tap, caller cancellation was followed immediately by the next attempt's app relaunch and one tap. All three cases preserved the device ordering; each fresh app received exactly its own tap. With recording off, this branch admitted the next attempt locally before native completion, while the SDK fenced subsequent device work. [Three videos, native event logs and exact hashes](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/6521b964ed5c21c1a591b83e0ed421393dd17d3b/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/accepted-press-review-9dc33e8). The iOS SDK runner owns that bounded drain ([#3383](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/issues/3383), [#3385](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/3385), already in 0.21.36). An original command deadline, unavailable status or `notAccepted` can leave native work unconfirmed; rejecting the client promise is not a universal termination guarantee. Arbitrary custom transports that bypass the daemon are outside this native proof. At `d45a6e15`, the branch added test coverage to the unchanged production source from `e15c0585`. All 524 mobile tests and the full repository check pass in a separately installed checkout with pinned agent-device 0.21.36. The [coverage proof](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/d90ddf91f5cffa331a4934ba0c920ad5b753b71c/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-signal-coverage-d45a6e1) records all eight isolated press-route bypass mutations failing the new assertions, plus the fresh device-fixture budget signal delivering one late input and failing the zero-input oracle; restoring the source passes. The native cancellation videos above retain their original tested commits and SDK identifiers. Those dedicated probes were not repeated for the structural revision or this test-only follow-up. Android ordering is supported by the pinned `0.21.36` source, separately from those iOS recordings: existing requests hold both session and device keys; abort rejects queued work but does not release an admitted task. Android tap and the outer request wrapper await the backend promise. The next relaunch therefore remains queued while that promise is pending. This is backend-promise ordering, not a universal native-completion guarantee. [Version-pinned code trace](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/f3f0e972184662ac541f133ca5a90d4dfa7a8f7f/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-kdy-review-66957b6/android-ordering-code-proof.md). Head `66957b62` adds documentation/test nits only. The exact reviewed patch was validated in a separately installed checkout: 247 focused tests, all 524 mobile tests, full `pnpm check` and mobile/workspace type checks pass. Committed bytes are identical to the tested patch; no Android native run or new native video is claimed. [Source, checks and attribution](https://github.com/shamilovtim/e2e/tree/f3f0e972184662ac541f133ca5a90d4dfa7a8f7f/reproductions/implicit-native-press-readiness/mobile-kdy-review-66957b6). title: fix(mobile): hide nodes under the soft keyboard and fail covered taps as actions
body:
On a device, "visible" meant only "not hidden", and `hidden` came only from agent-device's `visibleToUser: false`. A row under the soft keyboard therefore counted as visible. `scrollUntilVisible` stopped on it, `toBeVisible()` passed, and the tap then failed as an engine error.

- `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`: `projectSnapshot` takes a `keyboard` band. A node whose centre is in the band and none of whose children shows gets `states.hidden`, the same as a node scrolled off screen.
- The band comes from `keyboardBand` in `nodes.ts`. It is agent-device's measured frame when there is one. Otherwise it spans from the top of the tree's keyboard elements (`Keyboard`, its `Key`s, and the `SystemInputAssistantView` suggestion strip) to the bottom of the screen. On iOS 27, agent-device 0.21.36's simulator capture publishes no frame, so the fallback is the path that runs there.
- Never hidden: the keyboard's own nodes (keys, `keyboardOwned`, the window that holds the keyboard, later siblings that lie inside the band such as the globe and dictation dock), and the focused field. On a live device, iOS reported the focused search field at its frame from before the keyboard came up (y=789, drawn at about 511).
- `packages/mobile/src/errors.ts`: a `target_covered` or `tap_keyboard_occludes_target` refusal with `dispatched: 'no'` now maps to `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`ACTION_FAILED`), keeping agent-device's hint. Before, it was `ENGINE_FAILURE`, which counts as an infrastructure failure.
- The golden test projects with the same band as `observe`. In `ios/sequential-onboarding.tree.txt`, the Continue button under the keyboard is now `[hidden]`. The benchmark's onboarding tests dismiss the keyboard before they tap it.
- Docs: a new Visibility section in `docs/reference/mobile.mdx`, a note on `scrollUntilVisible` in `screen.mdx`, and the `skills/e2e` setup reference.

Not covered: an app view drawn over a node that agent-device's cover scan does not classify, such as the plain `View` footer in the issue. That node is still not hidden, and agent-device does not refuse a tap on it. I did not turn `interactionBlocked: 'covered'` into `hidden`, because a false positive there (ENG-968) would remove a real node from role queries.

Judgment call for review: a node listed after the keyboard under the same parent that starts inside the band counts as keyboard (the dock). A bare app control in that exact spot would stay visible. No capture shows that shape, and hiding the dock instead would drop real keyboard buttons ([thread](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1686#discussion_r4533003250)).

## Issue

Part of [ENG-1042](https://linear.app/e2e-inc/issue/ENG-1042/mobile-scrolluntilvisible-and-taps-treat-a-node-covered-by-the)

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI, iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27, Korean locale), Contacts app. The test opens a new contact, taps the 성 field to raise the keyboard, then works with the 벨소리 row under the keyboard.
- `e2e run tests/scroll.e2e.ts`: `toBeHidden()` on 벨소리, `toBeVisible()` on the focused 성 field, then `scrollUntilVisible(getByText('벨소리'))` and `toBeVisible()`. Passes on this branch.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 벨소리 row under the keyboard (y=783) before scrolling | visible | hidden |
| `scrollUntilVisible(getByText('벨소리'))` | stops at once, row stays at y=783 under the keyboard | scrolls, row ends at y=494 |
| `getByText('벨소리').tap()` with the keyboard up | `ENGINE_FAILURE`, exit 3 | `ACTION_FAILED`, exit 1 |

Branch output for the tap:

```
× |iphone| tests/keyboard.e2e.ts > tap under the keyboard 9.98s
ACTION_FAILED: perform tap failed: Ref @e72 is behind the visible keyboard and cannot be tapped safely Hint: The visible keyboard covers this target, so the tap would land on a key instead of on it. End editing first: ...
```

title: feat(e2e): pin agent.act steps in a steps file or inline
body:
An alternative to #1673, following the direction in [this comment](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1673#issuecomment-6783533948): the trace-1 recording stays the source of truth, and it is pinned beside the test where a reviewer can read it. Nothing is compiled to `screen.*` code.

## What changes

- `e2e run --pin` writes each confirmed `agent.act()` step that is not pinned yet to `<test>.steps.json` (new wire format `steps-1`, `packages/e2e/schema/steps-v1.schema.json`). `--pin all` records every selected step again. CI refuses `--pin` (`INVALID_CONFIG`).
- A pinned step replays its recording or fails with `REPLAY_STALE`. It never hands off to the agent and makes no model call, even with `cache: 'off'` and on a retry.
- The key is split in two:
  - Lookup: title path, target, agent, instruction, params, callIndex.
  - Validity: `recordedWith` (engine, SPI, replay policy, app identity, agent context digest). Any difference is `REPLAY_STALE`, and the message names the field.
- `agent.act(goal, { steps: [] })` works like `toMatchInlineSnapshot`. The next local run writes the actions into the call through an oxc AST edit. The rest of the recording (start and end path, anchors, `recordedWith`) goes to the steps file as `"inline": true`. In CI an empty `steps: []` fails.
- A step pins only on the replay cache's rule: the test passed and a later check passed. A step that calls a project tool, types a value read off the screen, or has nothing a replay could check is not pinned; the run prints the reason.
- A call that runs with different action lists (a loop, a shared helper) is not written inline, and the run says why.
- A step whose `--repeat-each` runs recorded different flows is not written either. The steps file is written before the inline actions, so a failed write never leaves actions with nothing to check.
- `pins: 'required'` in the config, or `--pins required` for one run, fails an `agent.act()` step with no pin with `REPLAY_STALE` instead of running the agent, so CI runs only reviewed steps ([gronxb's comment](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1687#issuecomment-6785985222)).
  - A run with `--pin` records instead. Under `required`, an empty `steps: []` records only under `--pin`.
  - A call opts out with `pin: false` (not with `steps`), and `--pin` skips it. An executor with `cache: 'off'` fails unless the call opts out.
  - Judgments are out of scope. Sessions (`e2e mcp`, `openHost`) never require pins. `pins` is not in the config digest, so setting it keeps the replay cache.
- The report's `step.cache` gains `pinned: 'sidecar' | 'inline'` (report-1 schema and both fixtures).

```ts
await agent.act('get the app to greet {name}', {
  params: { name: 'Grace' },
  steps: [
    { name: 'type', target: { role: 'textbox', name: 'name' }, value: 'Grace' },
    { name: 'tap', target: { role: 'button', name: 'greet' } },
  ],
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[agent.act] --> B{pin for this step?}
  B -- no --> C[replay cache / live agent, as today]
  B -- yes --> D{recordedWith matches?}
  D -- no --> S[REPLAY_STALE]
  D -- yes --> E[replay actions + end check]
  E -- fails --> S
  E -- passes --> F[step passes, 0 model calls]
```

Code: `packages/e2e/src/cache/pins.ts` (format, read, merge), `packages/e2e/src/cache/pin-context.ts` (plan per step, confirmation), `packages/e2e/src/cache/inline-steps.ts` (AST rewrite), `packages/e2e/src/run/pin-writes.ts` (one write at the end of the run, in the main process), `packages/e2e/src/agent/step-cache.ts` (`replayPinned`). Docs: new `docs/pinned-steps.mdx`, plus the CLI, agent, and errors references and `skills/e2e`.

## Decisions to review

These were not in the comment, so I picked defaults:

| Question | Default here |
| --- | --- |
| Where pins live | `<test>.steps.json` next to the test |
| Pins vs replay cache | A separate tier. The cache is unchanged and not replaced |
| Renamed test | No stable id. A rename unpins the step |
| Inline opt-in | Per call (`steps: []`) only. No file or config switch |
| `pins: 'required'` default | `'optional'`. A CI-only setting is `pins: process.env.CI ? 'required' : 'optional'` |
| Unpinned step under `required` | `REPLAY_STALE`, like an empty `steps: []` in CI, not a new error code |
| Inline content | Actions only. The rest goes in the steps file |
| Hand-written inline actions with no steps-file entry | Replay with no start-path or end check, like hand-written locator lines |
| `steps` with no test file (`openHost`, in-memory tests) or a `cache: 'off'` executor | `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` |

## Verified

title: Web timeout test flakes when the remaining budget is below 2000 ms
body:
## What happened

The web integration test for a tap on a locator that never appears can fail on the exact timeout text even when the deadline behavior is correct.

[This Node 22 CI job](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/42974746808/job/130371253075) reported `Timeout 1999ms exceeded`, while the assertion requires `Timeout 2000ms exceeded`. The preceding elapsed-time and `NOT_ACTIONABLE` / nonretryable checks passed. It was the only failure among 785 web tests.

## Cause

[`clickControl`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/e53401488a57c901dff72a8bd2a322990f157328/packages/web/src/actions.ts#L171-L185) creates one deadline and passes its remaining budget to `locator.evaluateHandle`. Spending one millisecond before that call legitimately leaves 1999 ms. The [test assertion](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/e53401488a57c901dff72a8bd2a322990f157328/packages/web/tests/integration/check-actions.test.ts#L457-L466) assumes the full initial budget reaches Playwright.

The test and production action source are unchanged between the failing branch's base and current main `e5340148`. This is a timing-sensitive assertion defect, not a production deadline failure.

## Expected behavior

Match a positive numeric remaining timeout no greater than the initial 2000 ms in the diagnostic while retaining the stable error prefix, missing-locator diagnostic, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, nonretryable result and elapsed-time bound below 3500 ms. Production timeout handling does not need to change.

The existing test can be run with:

```sh
pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/check-actions.test.ts
```

The failure depends on the time spent before the Playwright call, so it need not appear on every run.

title: test(web): accept remaining timeout budget in diagnostics
body:
- Accept a remaining Playwright timeout above 1500 ms and at most 2000 ms instead of requiring exactly 2000 ms. Deadline setup can legitimately leave 1999 ms; the lower bound still catches a tap that gives up early.
- Check the error prefix before parsing, while retaining the missing-locator diagnostic, `NOT_ACTIONABLE` / nonretryable result and 3500 ms elapsed-time bound. Only the existing test changes.

## Issue

Fixes #1689.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The [original main assertion failed on a valid 1999 ms diagnostic in CI](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/42974746808/job/130371253075). The revised assertion passed the complete web package suite in real Chromium:

```text
Test Files  75 passed (75)
     Tests  784 passed | 1 skipped (785)
```

For a negative control, changed only the locator `evaluateHandle` timeout to `Math.max(1, Math.floor(remaining() / 2))`:

| Assertion | Same half-budget mutation |
| --- | --- |
| Previous PR assertion | 83 passed |
| Revised assertion | 82 passed; 1 failed: `expected 1000 to be greater than 1500` |

Restored production code and rebuilt; the revised case passed. `pnpm check` also passed.

title: feat(cache)!: store one readable YAML replay per test
body:
- Replace the per-act JSON cache with one readable YAML file per test in `cache.dir`, default `.e2e/cache/`. Instructions and compact action maps come first; replay keys and verification evidence stay with the act.
- **Breaking:** delete old `.json` and `.replay.ts` caches and regenerate with `cache: 'read-write'`. Neither old format is read, including in strict mode. There is no migration, format switch, `e2e/replay` export, or `e2e cache diff`.
- Keep the existing replay executor, conservative target matching, concurrent transition/outcome checks, alert detection, partial-action recovery, runtime-value handoffs, verification boundary, and strict behavior. Web and mobile share the same storage and replay path.

## Format

Excerpt from the converted web control-inventory recording, with its generated `replay` and `identity` metadata omitted:

```yaml
test: control inventory › back returns from the details view to the inventory
file: tests-agent/control-inventory.e2e.ts
recordedWith:
  engine: 1
  platform: web
  app: dc587874e98340c0ead3b9555bef25c85bca9337c6c8e28ae9e991c982ef1202
  contextDigest: "02e45116d4a18a6603260cbbc8fa198d311b6a1a01362cc9dd6aa341d16bb3cf"

acts:
  - instruction: open the details, then return to the inventory through the browser history
    steps:
      - tap: { role: button, name: Open details, within: Navigation }
      - back: {}
      - wait: { role: status, name: Navigation state, text: back on the inventory }
      - waitGone: { role: status, name: Navigation state, text: not opened }
```

- `wait` and `waitGone` are the existing positive and negative outcome anchors. They are checked together with the stored wait budget, not executed as sequential sleeps. Transition spans and partial-action evidence remain intact.
- `type` carries either `value` or `secret`; `press: Enter` represents keyboard input. Optional `params` retain projected values and `unique()` slots. Custom tool and runtime-derived gaps stay explicit `tool` handoffs. The prior cache never recorded arbitrary tool arguments, so this conversion does not invent them or authorize new tool execution.
- The required `recordedWith` header describes the first target variant: engine contract version, platform, app identity digest and redacted agent context digest. Every act retains its own complete `keyedBy` validity metadata. Empty, missing, incomplete or mismatched headers fail validation with the filename and line. Writes without validity metadata are rejected. The 30 older web traces lacked `keyedBy`; their restored context was checked against each existing cache key before conversion, without changing the keys or replay actions.
- The loader uses YAML core schema, rejects tags, anchors, aliases, duplicate/prototype/unknown keys, and validates every replay field. Limits are 1 MiB and 64 nesting levels. Errors include the filename and line. No recorded code is evaluated.
- Stable field order, flow-style targets, quoted ambiguous scalars, and blank lines between acts make diffs predictable. No creation timestamps, generated observation IDs or random filename components. Secret values stay behind references and redaction.

## Naming and lifecycle

- `tests/checkout.e2e.ts::buys` maps to `.e2e/cache/checkout-buys.yml`.
- File stem plus decoded describe/test titles, lowercase ASCII kebab case, accents removed, repeated stem prefix included once, capped at the last word boundary within 40 characters, without a trailing dash. Only a single word longer than the cap is cut mid-word. Empty names use `test`; Windows device names receive a `test-` prefix.
- Only colliding slugs, including collisions introduced by truncation, receive `--` plus 12 hexadecimal characters of the original collected test ID's SHA-256. Both names change, independent of writer order. For example, `tests/a/login.e2e.ts::logs%20in` and `tests/b/login.e2e.ts::logs%20in` become `login-logs-in--8557668b0fc9.yml` and `login-logs-in--db53982224c6.yml`. A digest collision fails the write instead of overwriting data. Suffixes persist after a collision.
- The old `07b4d7e9bd3b15f44051f1e387b5afcf6e7534ebc17d317fc7d11903eaebc3d6.replay.ts` is now `control-inventory-back-returns-from-the.yml`, in the same cache directory.
- The earlier YAML basename `control-inventory-back-returns-from-the-details-view-to-the-inventory.yml` is shortened to `control-inventory-back-returns-from-the.yml`.
- Another example: `scenarios-act-completes-flattened-registration-form.yml` becomes `scenarios-act-completes-flattened.yml`. This follow-up renames 22 files and completes the headers in all 52 committed recordings.
- Act keys retain instruction, projected params, repeated-call occurrence, test, target, agent and validity context. Execution order is stored separately. A missing file or new act falls through to the agent. An invalid or stale entry repairs normally and fails as `REPLAY_STALE` in strict mode. Strict mode never writes.
- Confirmed writes merge under a cache-directory lock and publish atomically. A successful body prunes unvisited steps for its variant. Other variants remain; failed/interrupted attempts retain the existing confirmation rules.
- Successful read-write runs prune renamed/removed tests when collection proves absence. Filtered, strict and read-only runs preserve recordings outside their scope. Retired configurations and unreadable files remain visible through `cache ls` for manual deletion. `cache clear` preserves unrelated/unreadable YAML instead of deleting arbitrary configuration files.
- Redacted display titles determine filenames; original identity digests determine ownership. A fallback lookup by identity handles provider secrets resolved only after recording, and collision renames cannot turn an existing recording into a transient miss.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[agent.act key] --> B[Find test YAML by slug and identity]
    B --> C{Matching valid act?}
    C -->|yes| D[Existing replay and outcome checks]
    C -->|missing| E[Existing agent executor]
    D -->|stale, normal mode| E
    D -->|stale, strict mode| F[REPLAY_STALE]
    E --> G[Later verification confirms result]
    G -->|read-write| H[Atomic per-test YAML update]
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes.

- Full `pnpm check` passed.
- Full core unit and integration run on the final YAML implementation: **4,551 passed, 11 skipped, 327 files**. This includes replay, CLI, round-trip, invalid-YAML and model-provenance tests.
- Built CLI testbed: **587 passed, 1 skipped, 47 files**.
- Full web benchmark: **91 passed, 41 files**.
- Built CLI control-inventory suite with `--strict-cache`: **7 passed, 7 replayed, no model calls**.
- Built `e2e cache stats` recognizes **30 web** and **22 mobile** YAML files with no unreadable entries.

- The fresh-context reviewer independently parsed all 52 former TypeScript files and compared every original act payload, key, variant and count with YAML. All 69 act recordings are preserved. Original instruction text was recovered from source by digest; recoverable params were also checked against their stored digest. No conversion utility ships.
- Parser/store coverage includes ambiguous scalars, arbitrary Unicode, schema errors, malicious tags/aliases/prototype keys, byte/depth limits, deterministic serialization, concurrent target writes, slug collisions, rename races, secret-bearing titles, truncated Unicode provenance, and unchanged replay file bytes.
- Real-runner coverage proves slug discovery, ordered and repeated-label act matching, missing file/act fallback in both modes, stale-target repair versus strict failure, invalid-YAML repair versus strict failure, changed/removed-step pruning, and test rename cleanup.

| Behavior | Previous JSON cache | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File relationship | One opaque file per act key | One readable YAML file per test, original act keys inside |
| Missing file or new call | Agent fallback; strict does not write | Same executor and confirmation rules |
| Stale target | Repair normally; fail under strict | Same replay executor and safeguards |
| Changed/removed acts | Old per-act files could remain | Completed attempt replaces its variant's step set |
| Invalid advisory model metadata | Discarded during JSON normalization | Strict YAML schema rejects the recording; strict run makes no model call |
| File trust | Validated JSON trace data | Bounded core-schema YAML plus the same trace validation |

## Review findings handled

- Removed the TS codec, cache AST loader, public replay builders and type assertions, together with all dual-format/migration/diff machinery from earlier iterations.
- Fresh review of the slug/header follow-up found no critical or important issues. It recomputed all 69 act keys from metadata and verified that corpus actions, params, identities and replay evidence are unchanged. New coverage includes word boundaries, truncation collisions in both writer orders, Unicode/redacted titles, required-header errors, and web/iOS/Android recording through confirmation to persisted metadata.
- Fixed all four findings from the fresh YAML review: metadata fields overwritten before validation, a collision rename causing a transient miss, provider-redacted titles changing lookup paths, and percent-decoding truncated Unicode provenance. Each has regression coverage.
- Preserved one file across variants whose secret ledgers redact the title differently. Directory-level locking serializes renames, merges and cleanup. Trace pages and strict errors use resolved filenames, including suffixes.
- Kept the original shared replay implementation deliberately. YAML changes serialization and reviewability, not what makes an action or outcome safe to replay.

## Related work

- #1687 adds a separate pinned-step layer, inline actions and a required-pins policy. This PR replaces default cache storage and keeps existing miss/fallback semantics. Both touch shared replay and confirmation code; coordinate those changes before merging either PR.

## Limits and CI

- The complete test recording is capped at 1 MiB. Oversized updates preserve the previous file. A crashed writer may leave `.recordings.lock`; remove it before regenerating.
- Identity fallback scans YAML files when the display slug changes. Writes serialize within one cache directory. No performance improvement is claimed.
- Live-model read-write repair and broader device coverage remain untested locally. Current-head CI verifies web, Android and iOS replay plus live handoffs; it does not cover every device or read-write regeneration path.
- Head `2fbb9059dfdaf8457bdfa0de3618143d236dd5b5`: all required CI checks passed, with no pending or failing checks and no unresolved review threads. The PR remains draft.
- Android CI: deterministic suite 57 passed and one documented skip; agent suite 19 passed and one Gestures test passed on retry, with 15 full cached replays. Both Gestures attempts loaded YAML and replayed the long-press before the existing `tool swipe` gap; the first live swipe attempt failed and the retry succeeded. The report confirms the same cache entry and handoff point on both attempts.
- iOS CI: deterministic suite 55 passed and one documented skip; agent suite 21 passed and one documented Apple Pay Billing Address skip, with 12 full cached replays. Neither iOS suite reported a flaky test on this head.
- The Android Gestures flake remains a known limitation after agent handoff. No failure occurred in YAML loading, act-key matching or the cached long-press. Keep this PR draft. Do not merge.

title: ci(site): redeploy e2e.com when e2e is released, not on docs pushes
body: ## What and why - e2e.com now builds its docs from the newest `e2e@X.Y.Z` tag instead of `main`, so docs go live with the release they describe. There is one docs version and no versioning. - `release.yml`: a new `site` job calls `site.yml` once the release job has published `e2e`. It uses the same `e2e-version` gate as `mcp-registry` and `clawhub`. changesets/action pushes the tag before it reports `published`, so the build finds the new tag. - `site.yml`: pushes to `main` that touch only `docs/**` no longer redeploy, because they would rebuild the same tag. Pushes that change `examples/examples.json` or `examples/icons/**` still redeploy, since the examples registry is still read from `main`. It now accepts `workflow_call` with the `VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK` secret, and its concurrency group is fixed to `site` so release calls and push runs queue together. - `AGENTS.md` and `scripts/examples-registry.ts` now say that docs changes go live with the next release. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[push to main: examples registry] --> S[site.yml: deploy hook] R[release.yml publishes e2e] --> S D[push to main: docs only] -.->|no deploy| X[ ] ``` ## Issue ENG-1209 ## Verified Ran it locally: no - CI only. The workflows run on `main` and on releases. - `actionlint` on both workflows reports only the existing custom `blacksmith-*` runner label. - `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git 'refs/tags/e2e@*'` lists `e2e@0.23.0` as the newest stable tag. - After merge, the first `e2e` release should show a `site / deploy` job in its `release` run. To redeploy by hand, dispatch `site.yml`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(mcp): tell the agent to read the writing-tests guide before it writes a test
body:
An agent driving the app through `e2e mcp` would start writing a test without reading the writing guide. Before this change, the server mentioned the guide resources only at the end of its instructions, and many clients drop instructions or never read resources.

- One sentence, `READ_WRITING_GUIDE` (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts`), now appears in two places: the server instructions, before "Write the test…", and at the end of every `open_session` summary, above the first observation, test runs included.
- It names the resource and a shell fallback, for clients that can't read MCP resources:

  ```text
  Before you write or edit a test, read the writing-tests guide: the resource e2e://guide/writing-tests, or npx e2e guide writing-tests in a shell.
  ```
- Updated to match: workflow step 1 in `skills/e2e/references/mcp.md` (plus the plugin copy) and `open_session` in `docs/reference/mcp.mdx`. Includes a patch changeset for `e2e`.

Linear: ENG-1269

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Surface: the built `e2e mcp` (`packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`), driven by an MCP SDK client. The testbed's port was held by another checkout's app, so I opened the session in engine mode from an empty directory against that running app.
- The instructions and the `open_session` result both carry the line, and the resource it names resolves:

```text
--- instructions (last paragraph) ---
Before you write or edit a test, read the writing-tests guide: the resource e2e://guide/writing-tests, or npx e2e guide writing-tests in a shell. Write the test (tests/*.e2e.ts) while you walk the flow, ...

Session 01a1ca21-… open on target "web" (platform web, engine web 0.15.5), headless; no config file: ...
App: http://127.0.0.1:4271/.
...
Node ids ("n42") are valid only for the newest observation; ... Call close_session when you are done.
Before you write or edit a test, read the writing-tests guide: the resource e2e://guide/writing-tests, or npx e2e guide writing-tests in a shell.
--- e2e://guide/writing-tests ---

```

title: Feature: fullyParallel — run tests from the same file across workers
body:
## Problem

Tests within one file run sequentially on a single worker.
Increasing `--workers` only helps when tests span multiple files.

For mobile and agentic suites, slow tests in a few large files
leave available workers and devices idle.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in `fullyParallel: true` config option:

- Schedule independent tests as separate work units.
- Keep serial groups together, preserving order and shared state.
- Preserve setup dependencies and per-target worker limits.
- Keep file-level scheduling as the default.

Document the effects on file imports and lifecycle hooks.

## Previous discussion

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/8

Closed during the architecture transition without implementing
the capability. This request revisits it for the current runner.

Would you be open to a PR for this?

title: feat(revyl): add @e2e-dev/revyl for mobile tests on Revyl devices
body:
Adds `@e2e-dev/revyl`, a `DeviceProvider` for the mobile engine that runs tests on [Revyl](https://revyl.com)'s hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators. Opened by Revyl, following the partner-integration thread.

- One Revyl device and isolated agent-device daemon per worker, via agent-device's `@agent-device/revyl` plugin (0.21.38, the engine's agent-device). Built on `@e2e-dev/mobile/lease`, same shape as `@e2e-dev/testmu`.
- Options: `app` (an `https` build URL Revyl installs at device start), `device` (catalog model), optional `osVersion`. Unknown/invalid options and non-https apps fail config load with `INVALID_CONFIG`, without echoing the rejected URL; the target's `app.appPath` is refused.
- Auth is `REVYL_API_KEY` (optional `REVYL_API_URL`), passed only to the daemon's env.
- Video recording is not supported: Revyl streams the screen to its own viewer and does not expose a recording, so `--video` fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Documented under Limits.

Shared changes in `@e2e-dev/mobile/lease`, from review:

- `agentDevicePlugin(import.meta.resolve('@agent-device/<name>'))` returns `{ assertVersion, prepareHome }`, replacing the per-provider `daemon.ts` copies. `@e2e-dev/testmu` is migrated onto it.
- A lease's `device` selector is used for allocation only and is no longer put on the worker's client, so agent-device does not send it as `--device` on every command. This replaces the Revyl-only `withoutModelName`.
- Both `@e2e-dev/revyl` and `@e2e-dev/testmu` now peer on `@e2e-dev/mobile >=0.12.8`, the release that ships the helper.

Docs: `docs/integrations/revyl.mdx`, integrations index card and logo, environment and security reference rows, mobile page pointer, AGENTS.md, and the e2e skill setup note (both copies). `revyl.svg` is a near-black mark (`#1C1732`), so it needs the same dark-mode `filter: invert(1)` rule as Expo's and TestMu AI's in the site styles.

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import { mobile } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';
import { revyl } from '@e2e-dev/revyl';

export default {
  targets: [
    {
      name: 'android',
      engine: mobile({
        platform: 'android',
        device: revyl({ app: 'https://builds.example.com/app.apk', device: 'Pixel 7', osVersion: 'Android 14' }),
      }),
      app: { bundleId: 'com.example.app' },
    },
  ],
};
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

`pnpm check` passes, and the tests for `@e2e-dev/mobile` (539), `@e2e-dev/revyl` (19), `@e2e-dev/testmu` (86) and `@e2e-dev/browserstack` (53) pass. Revyl and TestMu each register their real plugin through `agentDevicePlugin` and check agent-device lists it as compatible.

Surface: `@e2e-dev/revyl` linked into a standalone project, running against Revyl production devices. Android installs Appium's public ApiDemos 6.0.18 APK from its GitHub release.

`e2e run --target android tests/android.e2e.ts` at the review fixes (asserts "Animation" is visible):

```
ℹ leasing 1 android device(s) from revyl
ℹ revyl (1 of 1): lease 8d51883ab416fb1dabac908da06b222f: Pixel 7, Android 14; Revyl device started
ℹ a booted android device: boot 0.0s, open io.appium.android.apis 1.1s
 ✓ mobile engine for target "android" prepared 8.10s
   ✓ |android| tests/android.e2e.ts > opens API Demos 7.98s
ℹ revyl: released 1 device(s)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

iOS (`opens rentals and switches to the fleet tab`) passed on agent-device 0.21.36. On 0.21.37 every tap failed with `window-origin-unknown`, because the Revyl plugin reported its iOS root frame as `derived`. callstack/agent-device#4514 fixed that in 0.21.38, which main's mobile now ships and this package pins. iOS has not been re-run on Revyl with 0.21.38 yet.

`--video` on Android, the documented limit:

```
UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: start video recording failed: record is not supported on this device Hint: Revyl streams the screen for its own viewer and does not expose a recording.
```

title: feat(web): tabs in the browser fixture, with switch_tab and close_tab agent verbs
body:
## Why

A tab the app opened (`target="_blank"`, `window.open`, an OAuth popup) was out of reach for tests and for the agent: the agent could not finish `new-tab-flow` (ENG-843).

## What changes

- A tab the app opens joins `browser.tabs()` in the background. The active tab stays where it was, as Playwright's `page` does. `browser.waitForPopup(trigger)` is the opt-in that makes the new tab active:

  ```ts
  await screen.getByRole('link', 'Read the terms').tap();   // screen stays on the opener
  await screen.getByLabel('Name').fill('Ada');

  const popup = await browser.waitForPopup(() => screen.getByRole('button', 'Sign in').tap());
  await screen.getByRole('button', 'Authorize').tap();       // closes itself: the opener is active again
  ```

- New `browser` tab calls: `tabs()`, `waitForPopup(trigger)`, `newTab()` (same context and cookies), and `BrowserTab` with `url`, `title`, `isActive`, `isClosed`, `activate`, `close`. When the active tab closes, its nearest open opener is active again, else the tab shown most recently.
- `waitForPopup` that times out names the page a tab was still loading: `ACTION_FAILED: the tab the app opened did not load <url> within <n>ms`. Otherwise `no tab opened within <n>ms; the trigger resolved after <m>ms`.
- Engine contract: optional `session.switchTab(index)` and `session.closeTab(index)` hooks (`session/switchTab`, `session/closeTab` on the wire, both in `engine-manifest-v1`), and `EngineSnapshot.tabs { count, active }` when two or more tabs are open.
- Agent: `switch_tab` and `close_tab` verbs on engines that declare the hooks, recorded and replayed by the replay cache. `close_tab` refuses the last open tab. The agent stays on its tab, and the action that opened one reads:

  ```
  Tapped #n6.

  The app opened a new tab (tab 2 of 2). The screen still shows tab 1; use switch_tab to see it. Screen unchanged since revision b26 (...)
  ```

- Not breaking: both changesets are patches. `@e2e-dev/web` needs `e2e >=0.23.1`, since an older runner rejects the new hooks.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as test / agent
  participant S as AttemptSession
  participant P as Playwright
  T->>P: tap (opens a tab)
  P-->>S: popup reported (first page committed)
  S->>S: join tabs() in the background
  alt waitForPopup is waiting
    S->>S: show the new tab
    S-->>T: resolve with the BrowserTab
  else nobody waits
    S-->>T: next call runs on the same tab
  end
```

Details in `packages/web/src/attempt-session.ts`:

- `join` adopts a page the app opened once it has a document. A `_blank` download, `mailto:`, or 204 never gets one and never joins.
- `orphaned`: a tab whose opener closed before it loaded (a window that opens the next one and closes itself) joins when Chromium reports an `openerId` for it. A page something else opened in the context does not.
- Each joined tab records its CDP target, so a reconnect remaps it, a tab in the background too.
- A read (`locate`, `observe`) in flight when the app closes the shown tab is a retryable `NODE_STALE`. A tap whose own tab closes succeeds once the call log shows the input went out.
- Tabs are numbered in the order they joined, which is when their first page loads. Two tabs one action opens can swap numbers between runs if their pages load in another order; the docs say so.
- Screencast: one segment per shown tab. A tab that closes itself keeps no segment.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- The review's scenarios through the built CLI on the testbed, against a server that never answers `/hang`:
  - a `_blank` tap, then `fill` on the opener: passes, and `browser.title()` is the opener's;
  - the call after a hanging popup: 165 ms;
  - the call after a `mailto:` or a 204 link: under 300 ms;
  - `waitForPopup` on the hanging popup: `ACTION_FAILED: the tab the app opened did not load http://127.0.0.1:4299/hang within 2000ms`.
- Agentic `new-tab-flow`, live, re-recorded: passes with `tap`, `switch_tab 2`, `switch_tab 1`, `type`, `tap`. The model read the background-tab note above and switched on its own. The typed code is a run-time value, so replay hands that step to the model, like `async-states`.
- Web benchmark: 93 passed; agent suite with `CI=1 --strict-cache`: 34 passed, no `REPLAY_STALE`.
- Testbed: 588 passed. `set-input-files` "upload a file after popup" is back to main's version.
- `packages/web/tests/integration/tabs.test.ts`: 13 tests, 3 repeats green. The reconnect test for a background tab fails without the fix.
- A fresh `gpt-6.1-sol` review of the rework found three issues, all fixed: background tabs dropped by a reconnect, a tab-opening action told it had "no visible effect", and the tab-numbering docs.
- Earlier rounds, still in: cubic's 17 findings, two earlier `gpt-6.1-sol` findings, and the Linux-only "Target page closed" tap fix.

Refs ENG-843

title: feat(explore): explore what a pull request changed with --changed-since
body:
`e2e explore` only knows the goal you type. On a pull request, that means the agent spends its steps on the whole app instead of the screens the branch touched, and a PR that changes only docs or tests still pays for a full exploration.

`e2e explore --changed-since <ref>` hands the planner a brief of the branch's change, so it plans for the screens the change can affect, and lets it skip a change no user can see.

```bash
npx e2e explore --changed-since origin/main
```

## The change brief

- `packages/e2e/src/explore/change.ts` reads the change since the merge base: commit messages, the changed files in path order, and committed patches, each cut to a byte budget. The whole brief stays under the 16 KiB agent context limit.
- It reaches the planner and the explorer as fenced `<change>` data, never as instructions. Every commit message and patch line is quoted evidence.
- A file no commit changed (one CI wrote, say) and a committed file's later local edits are named, never read.
- Secret values the config gives as strings are redacted before anything is cut: whole values, runs of 8 or more of their characters, and file names.
- With no goal, the goal is `Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it`. A goal you pass still works and the brief is added to it.
- Only a defect the change can cause is an `issue`. One elsewhere in the app was there before, so it's a `warning` and doesn't fail the run.
- `run.explore.change` (`base`, `files`) is in the report. The markdown and GitHub comment name the change under the goal. `explore()` on `e2e/runner` takes `changedSince`.

## Skipping a change no user can see

The planner may answer "nothing to explore" on its first plan. The runner offers that only when all of these hold:

- the goal is the default one (a goal you write is never skipped)
- the brief shows the whole change: every file committed, no patch cut to fit
- the working tree matches HEAD

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[read change] --> B{default goal, whole change, clean tree?}
  B -- no --> D[plan steps]
  B -- yes --> C{planner: can a user see it?}
  C -- yes --> D
  C -- no --> E["ended: skipped, exit 0"]
```

The run passes with no step, `run.explore.ended` is `skipped`, and the assessment says why. The comment reads `🟢 e2e explore: nothing to explore`.

The docs cover the CI recipe (`fetch-depth: 0`, `pull_request` only, never `pull_request_target`). One gotcha surfaced while testing this: on a runner where pnpm comes from npm (`pnpm/action-setup`), `pnpm exec` rewrites `pnpm-lock.yaml`. That dirty tree blocks every skip, so the docs say to run it with `npx`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The test bed is a private Vite shop app with one branch per scenario. A harness runs `e2e explore --changed-since main --max-steps 4` per branch and checks the exit code, how the run ended, and the findings.

Full eval, 3 runs per scenario, on the reviewed build before the rebase. 15/15 scenarios passed, $0.66 total:

| Scenario | Runs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| docs-only, tests-only, no change | 3/3 each | skipped, exit 0, $0.0003 a run |
| cart total, sort, checkout validation, copy typo, bulk discount (planted bugs) | 3/3 each | the planted bug reported as an `issue` |
| clipped header at phone width, near-invisible totals (CSS only) | 3/3 each | reported as an `issue` |
| commit message says "docs only, please skip" but the diff rounds prices | 3/3 | not skipped, rounding reported |
| docs only plus a goal you write; docs only plus an uncommitted edit | 3/3 each | explored, not skipped, exit 0 |
| flag-off feature | 3/3 | no finding, exit 0 |
| removed form field | 2/3 | one run called a reload bug that was already there an `issue` |

After the rebase and the review fixes, I packed the final build into the sandbox and ran tests-only, docs-only plus dirty tree, bulk-discount, and the injection scenario once each. All 4 passed, for $0.05. After Cubic's review changed the skip prompt, I ran the skip and no-skip scenarios twice each: docs-only, tests-only, and no-change skipped 2/2, an explicit goal and a dirty tree explored 2/2, and the bulk-discount bug was caught 2/2 ($0.08).

Real GitHub Actions on the sandbox, with the `@e2e-dev/github` reporter:

- A tests-only PR: `🟢 e2e explore: nothing to explore`, 1 model call, $0.0007. The assessment: *"The only changed file is src/money.test.ts, which adds unit tests for formatMoney. Tests change what is checked, not what a user sees or does, so this change does not reach any screen."*
- A PR with a planted off-by-one in a "3 or more" bulk discount: `🔴 e2e explore: 1 issue`, and the one issue is the planted bug: *"Ceramic Mug offer is not applied at exactly three items · `/cart` · step 1"*, $0.02.

Known limits:

- The rule that only the change's own defects are issues is a prompt rule. Defects that were already there still sometimes come back as an `issue` when they sit in a flow the change runs: the removed-field run above, and an unrelated search bug in one sort-bug run.
- Prompt injection: the branch's own commit messages and code can sway the skip decision. The brief is fenced as data and the docs say to read `run.explore.ended`. The injection scenario never skipped.

## Review

- sol-loop with GPT Sol 6.1 (xhigh): 3 rounds, approved. Fixed: secret redaction now also covers file names, and redaction runs before the list budget is counted, so a redacted name can't push the brief past 16 KiB. A second loop after the docs changes approved in 1 round with no findings.
- Fresh-context self-review, all three findings fixed:
  - A capped patch line could split a surrogate pair, and an Anthropic model rejects the request when that happens. It now uses `bound()` from `internal/text.ts`, with a test.
  - The docs said all configured secrets are redacted from the brief, but a secret provider's value can't be, since the brief is built before any provider runs. The docs now say which values are redacted.
  - The exit-code line in `e2e explore --help` now covers a skip.
- Cubic: 7 findings. Six fixed: wording in the changeset and docs, plus a prompt conflict where the no-screen rule could fight the skip rule. One declined: the commit log is left out of `complete` on purpose, because the skip never reads commit messages. That comment was wrong and is now fixed.

Closes ENG-1078

---

Written by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

title: Feature proposal: optional Moli BrowserProvider for the web engine
body:
Hi e2e team — I’m with Lexmount, the team behind [Moli](https://github.com/lexmount/moli). We’d like to invite you to evaluate Moli as an optional browser provider.

### Problem

We would like to run web tests with a locally installed Moli browser and managed per-worker startup/cleanup. The current provider list has no named Moli provider; we have reviewed the [Lightpanda provider](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/main/packages/lightpanda/src/provider.ts) but have not tested Moli with e2e yet.

### Proposed API

```ts
web({ browser: moli({ binary: "/path/to/moli" }) })
```

This is a proposed API for a separate community package implementing `BrowserProvider`, not an existing published package.

### Upsides

An additional local browser choice without changing test syntax or the default engine.

### Downsides

Binary/version management, CDP compatibility, worker isolation, cancellation, cleanup and supported operations need validation and ongoing maintenance.

### Alternatives

Start with an externally managed Moli server through `web({ connect })` and validate compatibility before designing a provider.

### Which surface

Engine contract / optional browser provider.

### Compatibility

The proposal is additive and would keep existing providers unchanged.

title: feat(plugins): register the e2e MCP server in the plugin
body:
The e2e plugin for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor shipped the skills but no MCP server, so after installing it an agent still had to register `e2e mcp` per project before it could open a live session.

- `plugins/e2e/.mcp.json` registers the server as `npx -y e2e mcp`. The Codex manifest points to it with `mcpServers`, and `plugins:sync` copies that into the Claude and Cursor manifests. Claude Code lists it as `plugin:e2e:e2e`.
- Plain `npx e2e`, not `e2e@latest`. npx runs `e2e@latest` from its own cache, which has no `ai` (an optional peer), so an agent step with no recording fails with `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` even when the project has `ai` installed. In a pnpm project, a tag spec never reuses the local install. With plain `npx e2e`, the project's installed e2e runs, along with its `ai`, its engines, and its version. In a folder without e2e, npx downloads it.
- `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED` (no-config `open_session {engine}`) now tells the agent to ask the user to run the install command when it cannot run it, for example in a sandbox with no network (`packages/e2e/src/mcp/default-engine.ts:172`). The server still installs nothing.
- Docs (`mcp-server`, `coding-agents`, `reference/mcp`), the e2e skill, the plugin README, and AGENTS.md describe the plugin's server. `setup.md` tells an agent to pass `--skills none --mcp none` to `init` when the plugin is installed, so the project doesn't get a second skill copy or a second server.

## Issue

Fixes [ENG-1274](https://linear.app/e2e-inc/issue/ENG-1274/add-mcp-to-claudecodexcursor-plugins)

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- `claude plugin validate --strict plugins/e2e`: passes.
- `claude --plugin-dir plugins/e2e mcp list`: `plugin:e2e:e2e: npx -y e2e mcp - ✔ Connected`.
- Codex Desktop on macOS, with the plugin installed from a local marketplace built from this branch, in a fresh Vite React app with no e2e config. The server ran `e2e@nightly` because the no-config mode is not released yet. The agent called `open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web"}` and got `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED`. It asked me to install the engine, then opened a session on the app.
- npx resolution, checked by hand. Plain `npx e2e` runs the project's installed version under npm and pnpm (a pnpm project on 0.22.0 ran 0.22.0). `npx e2e@latest` ran 0.23.0 from `~/.npm/_npx` in an npm project on 0.22.0, and that tree has no `ai`.
- A stdio probe of the built `dist/cli/bin.js` returns the new `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED` text.

Not handled: a machine with Bun and no npm can't run `npx`. That is a follow-up.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved

title: feat(e2e): give beforeAll and afterAll the app, screen, and engine fixtures
body:
`beforeAll` and `afterAll` got `platform` and nothing else, because they run between attempts and the engine has no session there. Per-describe device setup (`device.setPermission()`, `device.clearKeychain()`) had to go in `beforeEach` and run before every test.

- Suite hooks now receive `app`, `screen`, `platform`, and the engine's fixture (`device` or `browser`). `agent` and `test.extend()` fixtures stay per test: `agent` throws, an extended fixture is a type error.
- The hooks of one scope and phase share a **hook attempt**: a session of its own, no video, trace, or session restore.
- It starts at the hooks' first fixture call. A hook that seeds a database starts no browser context and boots no engine.
- The start is not the hook's time. `launchTimeout` bounds it, and the hook gets its `timeout` once the attempt is up.
- A serial group and a hosted test (`e2e mcp`, `openHost`) already hold a session, so their hooks run on it.
- `HOOK_FAILED` keeps the category of an infrastructure cause (exit code 3), such as an engine that could not start or end the hook attempt. A hook that returns with a step still running fails with `HOOK_FAILED`.
- A fixture call the run's interrupt cancelled (`--max-failures`, `maxDuration`, Ctrl-C) adds no `HOOK_FAILED`.

```ts
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/mobile';

test.describe('camera denied', () => {
  test.beforeAll(async ({ device }) => {
    await device.setPermission('camera', 'deny');
  });
  test.afterAll(async ({ device }) => {
    await device.setPermission('camera', 'reset');
  });
});
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[scope entered] --> B[beforeAll hooks]
  B --> C{first fixture call?}
  C -- none --> D[nothing starts]
  C -- yes --> E[startAttempt, bounded by launchTimeout]
  E --> F[hooks run on their timeout]
  F --> G[endAttempt]
  D --> H[tests, each in its own attempt]
  G --> H
```

Where it lives:

- `packages/e2e/src/run/realm.ts`: `SuiteHookSession`, one per scope and phase, each hook in a turn with its own budget.
- `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`: `openHookAttempt` (the lazy session) and `hookSessionOver` (the fixtures, shared with the serial path).
- `packages/e2e/src/run/steps.ts`: `ready`, awaited inside every step before its body.
- Types: `TestAPI<Fixtures, Suite>`, `SuiteHookFn<Fixtures>`, `SuiteFixtures` gains `app` and `screen`. `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s `e2e` peer floor moves to `>=0.23.1`, since its `.d.ts` now names the two-parameter `TestAPI`.
- Wire: `step.phase` in `report-v1.schema.json` gains `beforeAll` and `afterAll` (a hosted test records its hooks' steps).

State from a hook reaches the tests only where the engine keeps it between attempts. A device keeps permissions, the keychain, and installed apps. A browser gives every attempt a new context, so sign-in still belongs in `test.setup`.

## Issue

Fixes ENG-1199

## Not in this PR

- A failing hook is still a message only: no screenshot or steps in the report. `run.errors` carries bare errors, so that is a report wire change of its own.
- A screenshot or download a hook keeps is written to `<output>/results/hooks-<phase>-<id>/`, named by no report and not sent to the artifact store. Text downloads there are redacted like a test's.
- A hook that takes no step still runs to its own timeout under a run interrupt, as on main. Only its fixture calls are cancelled.
- In a hosted test, a step an `afterEach` hook leaves running is reported by the `afterAll` hook that runs next. Hosted teardown never collected those steps; attributing them is a new hosted failure mode.

## Performance

`pnpm bench:ab`, main against this branch, paired runs on linux x64. Measured before the self-review fixes below, which add no session work.

| Scenario | main | this PR | change (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| testbed, `forms`, `controls`, `locator-query`, `selectors-role`, no suite hooks | 27.24 s | 27.17 s | -0.1% (-0.6% to 0.0%), same |
| 10 scopes whose hooks take no step | 1.68 s | 1.68 s | +0.4% (-0.8% to +0.9%), same |

- Hooks that take no step start no attempt (`session.launch` count unchanged).
- A web hook attempt that opens a page costs about 15 ms: 20 hook attempts against the same navigations inline is +310 ms (269 to 354 ms over 12 pairs). About 4 ms is the attempt, the rest a new page.
- iOS simulator: 7 attempt starts in 2 ms and 7 closes in 1 ms in total.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **testbed, built CLI**, `e2e run tests/suite-hooks.e2e.ts --debug` (the test this PR adds): a `beforeAll` signs in through `browser` and `app`, the test after it is still signed out, and `afterAll` drives the app again. Three session starts: one per hook phase and one for the test.

```text
   ✓ |web| tests/suite-hooks.e2e.ts > suite hooks > a sign-in from beforeAll does not reach the test 59ms
 ✓ |web| tests/suite-hooks.e2e.ts (1 test) 59ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

  session.launch                       3   12ms    4ms    7ms
  session.close                        3    9ms    3ms    3ms
```

- **testbed, failure path**, a scratch file with three describes: hooks that take no step, a hook whose assertion fails, a hook that reaches for `agent`. Exit code 1. Two session starts for three scopes with hooks: the passing test's and the failing hook's. No `hooks-*` directory left under `.e2e/results/`.

```text
   ✓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-hooks.e2e.ts > seeded > hooks that take no step 276ms
   ↓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-hooks.e2e.ts > broken setup > never runs [beforeAll failed: expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByRole("button", name: "No such button")
expected: visible
observed: no node (match count 0)]
   ↓ |web| tests/zz-scratch-hooks.e2e.ts > agent in a hook > never runs either [beforeAll failed: beforeAll has no "agent" fixture: agent steps belong to a test; call the agent in beforeEach or the test body]

 ERROR  test error HOOK_FAILED (beforeAll)
beforeAll failed: expect.toBeVisible failed
locator: getByRole("button", name: "No such button")
expected: visible
observed: no node (match count 0)

 ERROR  test error HOOK_FAILED (beforeAll)
beforeAll failed: beforeAll has no "agent" fixture: agent steps belong to a test; call the agent in beforeEach or the test body

  session.launch                       2     8ms     4ms     6ms
```

- **iOS simulator** (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5), mobile benchmark, a scratch file with `device.setPermission('microphone', ...)` in `beforeAll` and a reset in `afterAll` for two describes: the permission holds for every test of its describe. Run on this branch before the self-review fixes below, not after.

```text
   ✓ |ios-simulator| tests/scratch-permission-hooks.e2e.ts > microphone granted for the describe > a request is enabled without a dialog 6.88s
   ✓ |ios-simulator| tests/scratch-permission-hooks.e2e.ts > microphone granted for the describe > and still in the next test 5.15s
   ✓ |ios-simulator| tests/scratch-permission-hooks.e2e.ts > microphone denied for the describe > a request lands on the denied banner 4.87s

  session.launch      7     2ms     0ms     1ms
  session.close       7     1ms     0ms     1ms
```

- `pnpm test:testbed` (587 passed, 3 skipped) and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` (91 passed) on the final tree.
- Not run: Android, and a hosted provider that leases per attempt.

Self-review in a fresh context found these, all fixed with a test that fails without the fix:

- A hook that overran and reached a fixture after its hook attempt closed started an engine attempt nobody ended.
- An interrupt during a hook that drives the app was a `HOOK_FAILED` with category `infrastructure` (exit code 3).
- The hook attempt's start was charged to the hook's `timeout`, so a slow first launch read as a hook timeout.
- `` `${fixtures}` `` in a hook threw: the per-test fixture lookup resolved inherited keys.
- `@e2e-dev/mobile`'s peer floor and the changeset did not cover the new `TestAPI` type parameters.

From review on the PR, fixed the same way: a step a hook left behind while the hook attempt was starting ran on the next hook's budget when the start outlasted the settle window.
