title: feat(notte): add @e2e-dev/notte, a browser provider for Notte cloud browsers
body:
Adds `@e2e-dev/notte`, an official integration for [Notte](https://notte.cc) cloud browsers, as discussed with the e2e team. Notte maintains it.

```ts
web({ browser: notte({ solve_captchas: true }) })
```

- `notte()` is a `BrowserProvider` for `@e2e-dev/web`. Its options are Notte's start-session body, and `notte-sdk` is a peer (`>=1.10.0`, checked against 1.10.0 and 1.10.9).
- **Scope is always `attempt`.** A Notte session refuses `Target.createBrowserContext`, so `worker` scope fails on its first test.
- **Downloads.** Notte saves every download to the session's file storage, under the site's suggested filename rather than the download id. `downloads.read` finds the file by that name.
- **One small engine change in `@e2e-dev/web`, additive:** `BrowserDownloadContext` gets an optional `suggestedFilename`, passed from `download.suggestedFilename()`. The change has its own changeset, a docs line in `browser.mdx`, and an assertion in `provider-downloads.test.ts`. With an older engine, the provider falls back to the oldest file it hasn't read yet.
- A start response without `cdp_url` falls back to the session's `debugInfo`, as the SDK's own `Session` does.
- **Sweep.** Notte sessions have no tags to find a run's sessions by. Instead, each worker writes a marker file per session under the system temp directory (`src/ledger.ts`) and removes it on release. `sweep` stops whatever markers remain, so a session left by a crashed worker is stopped when the run ends rather than after Notte's 3-minute idle timeout.
- **Progress line:** `session <id>, watch at https://console.notte.cc/sessions/<id>`. The console link needs a sign-in. The token-bearing `viewer_url` is never logged.
- **`apps/testbed/e2e.notte.config.ts` and `test:notte`** run the testbed on Notte through a tunnel to the playground, like the Lightpanda config.
- The logo (`docs/images/integrations/notte.svg`) is near-black, so the site needs a dark-mode `filter: invert(1)` rule for it, like Expo's.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, with the built CLI and a real `NOTTE_API_KEY`.

**Testbed on Notte**: 45 files and 582 tests, through a Cloudflare tunnel to the playground. 435 passed on Notte. For comparison, the same suite on a local Chrome leased per attempt through the same tunnel passed 523, and its 58 failures come from the tunnel and attempt scope. 102 tests fail only on Notte:

| Cause | Tests | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The test opens `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` directly | 79 | A cloud browser can't reach the runner's loopback, which is the same for any hosted provider. This includes the 7 download tests that fetch from `127.0.0.1`. Every download served from the tunnel passes. |
| Notte answers JS dialogs server-side | 7 | `confirm` → `false`, `prompt` → `null` before `page.on('dialog')` can act. Documented. |
| Keyboard shortcuts from a macOS runner | 7 | The browser takes Windows combos. `ControlOrMeta` resolves to `Meta` on a Mac runner. Documented. |
| Subpixel scroll offsets (~0.001px) | 3 | |
| Folder upload, and the error text for a missing file chooser | 2 | Notte blocks `DOM.setFileInputFiles`. Files up to 50 MB upload fine. |
| Remote-latency timing | 4 | `waitForResponse`, `selectOption` actionability, frame detach, 307 redirect |

**Scenarios**, each followed by a check that Notte had no active sessions left:
- **Retries:** each attempt gets its own session.
- **Test timeout:** the session is released.
- **Ctrl-C mid-run:** exit 130, and the session is stopped.
- **Video** (`--video=on`): the engine screencast works.
- **Ten parallel workers:** all pass.
- **`viewport_width: 1920` with `viewport: null`:** the page is 1920×1080.
- **`kill -9` on a worker:** without `sweep`, Notte reported the session `closed`/`idle_timeout` 3 minutes later. With `sweep`, the run printed `released 1 browser(s) a worker left open` and stopped it at once.
- **Fresh npm install** of the packed tarball with published `e2e@0.23.0`, `@e2e-dev/web@0.15.5`, and `notte-sdk`: the tests run.

**Not verified:** agent steps (`agent.act` / `assert`). There was no model key on the machine I ran this from. They drive the same CDP page as the deterministic tests.

`pnpm check` passes.

title: Feature request: verify the app before reuseExisting attaches (app.readyCheck)
body:
### Problem

`app.command.reuseExisting: true` attaches to whatever HTTP server already answers `app.url`/`readyUrl`. Nothing checks that the server is the app under test, so a suite can silently run against a different app that happens to own the port.

Reproduction: a Vite app configured on port 5173, with another Vite app already listening there. The run printed the reuse notice, attached, and failed later with `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` against the wrong app.

Status-only readiness cannot tell which process answered. PR #147 documents this as a deliberate limitation, and `apps/web-benchmark/README.md` says: "`reuseExisting` trusts whatever answers on the port."


### Proposed API

```ts
app: {
  url: 'http://localhost:5173',
  command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'], reuseExisting: true },
  readyCheck: {
    status: [200],
    bodyContains: 'say hello',
    header: { name: 'x-app', contains: 'checkout' },
  },
},

- The probe follows redirects and must match every declared field.
- `reuseExisting`: a mismatch is `APP_MISMATCH` before attaching.
- A command the runner started: poll until it matches; at `startupTimeout`, `APP_MISMATCH` with the last observation.
- Observations name the status, final URL, and `<title>`.
```

### Upsides

Makes `reuseExisting` safe for local dev servers and MCP sessions.
Portable: HTTP-level, works through containers and tunnels, unlike PID/port detection.
Also catches a dev server serving an error page.
Examples can keep `reuseExisting` without the wrong-app failure.

### Downsides

- New public config surface and a new `APP_MISMATCH` error code.
- Reads up to 1 MiB of the body and follows redirects once a check is declared.
- A stale or too-loose check can still match the wrong app. This is a guard, not a security boundary.
- Added startup config that buys nothing when the app runs on a free port.


### Alternatives

- Maybe show a warning message to the user about the issue
- We might ask the agent to verify the app

### Which surface

public types (SDK), config keys

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: Official boxd integration: web targets in boxd machines
body:
### Problem

I work on boxd (https://boxd.sh?ref=e2e). boxd runs microVMs: full Ubuntu machines that start in about a second and can fork. I'd like to add an official boxd integration and maintain it.

Today a team that wants to run web suites in boxd machines writes a `BrowserProvider` by hand. There is no boxd package.

### Proposed API

One package, `@e2e-dev/boxd`, shaped like `@e2e-dev/e2b/web` and `@e2e-dev/smol`. `@boxd-sh/sdk` and `@e2e-dev/web` are peers.

```ts
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { boxdBrowsers } from '@e2e-dev/boxd';

export default {
  targets: [
    { name: 'web', engine: web({ browser: boxdBrowsers({ scope: 'worker' }) }), app: { url: 'https://example.com' } },
  ],
  workers: 4,
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

- `BOXD_API_KEY` comes from the run's environment.
- One machine per worker slot, with the Chromium build `@e2e-dev/web` pins. `scope: 'attempt'` forks the warm machine for each attempt.
- Chromium listens on the machine's loopback. A loopback tunnel on the runner carries the access token, so a lease holds only `127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- Machines are tagged with the run and target, deleted at release, and swept at the end of the run. `downloads` reads files back from the machine.
- Options: `scope`, `region`, `snapshot` (a prepared machine to start from), `timeoutMs`.

### Upsides

- Web suites run in full Linux machines without a local browser, in CI or from a laptop.
- `attempt` scope gets a clean browser per attempt from a fork, without a cold start.
- Same seam and layout as the E2B and smol packages, so nothing in core or the engines changes.

### Downsides

- One more package to keep in step with the Playwright version `@e2e-dev/web` pins.
- Web only for now. Android needs an emulator inside the machine, which I want to prove first before proposing it.
- Live tests need a boxd account. I'd run them before each release and keep the unit tests on a fake client, like the other providers.

### Alternatives

A `BrowserProvider` in each user's config. That works, but every team repeats the tunnel, cleanup, and sweep logic.

### Which surface

None of the listed ones: a new package, with no change to `e2e` exports, config keys, the CLI, or the engine contract.

title: feat(core): add launch, SessionState, and createAgent to @e2e-dev/core
body:
**Stack 3/3:** [session-half split](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1736) → [move into `@e2e-dev/core`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1737) → this PR.

> **2026-11-15:** rebased onto main `235986078` and the package renamed from `e2e-core` to `@e2e-dev/core`. Command output quoted below predates the rename.

`@e2e-dev/core` drives a browser or a native app from plain code. It is the engines, locators, agent, and replay cache, with no test runner, config file, or report. `e2e` is now built on it.

```ts
import { launch } from '@e2e-dev/core';
import { createAgent } from '@e2e-dev/core/agent';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web/engine';

await using shop = await launch(web(), { app: { url: 'https://shop.example.com' }, secrets: { PASSWORD: process.env.PASSWORD! } });
await using session = await shop.newSession();
await session.app.open('/login');
await session.screen.getByLabel('Password').fill(shop.secret('PASSWORD'));

const agent = createAgent(session, { model, cache: { dir: '.bot/cache' } });
await agent.act('add the item and apply the best coupon', { cacheKey: 'cart' });
```

## Engines without `e2e`

- `@e2e-dev/web/engine` and `@e2e-dev/mobile/engine` export the factories and their types without `test`, so a program never loads `e2e`.
- The engines' `e2e` peer becomes optional, needed only by the main entry that extends `test`.
- `@e2e-dev/core` gains its `@e2e-dev/core` and `@e2e-dev/core/agent` entries. `@e2e-dev/core/agent` also exports what `e2e/agent` does.

## What `@e2e-dev/core` adds

- **Hosts and sessions:** `launch(engine, options)` returns a host, and `host.newSession()` returns an isolated session with `screen`, `app`, `platform`, and the engine's fixture.
  - `EngineHandle<Fixtures>` makes `launch(web())` type `session.browser`. `defineEngine<Fixtures>()` requires a factory in `fixtures` for each fixture it names (besides `screen`, `app`, `platform`), returning that fixture, and a union of fixture sets needs one member's factories.
  - A session publishes nothing to `globalThis` and has no session deadline.
  - Each operation has a default timeout, set with `setDefaultTimeout`.
  - `launch` and `newSession` take a `signal`, and the host closes on Ctrl-C.
- **Saved state:** `session.saveState()` returns an in-memory `SessionState`.
  - It leaves the process only through `state.export({ key })`, encrypted with AES-256-GCM as a new `session-state-1` document (schema and fixtures in `packages/e2e/schema`).
  - The state carries the secret values the session knew.
- **Secrets:** pass values to `launch({ secrets })` and get handles from `host.secret(name)`. There is no process-wide registry.
- **Agent:** `createAgent(session, options)` in `@e2e-dev/core/agent`.
  - With `cache`, every `act` names its recording with `cacheKey`, enforced in types and at runtime.
- **Device links:** `app.linkBase` plus a new optional engine hook `session.openLink` (protocol method `session/openLink`) make `app.open(path)` open a link in a device app. `@e2e-dev/mobile` implements the hook.

Docs: a new `docs/core.mdx`, plus updates to the engine, config, errors, security, and agent reference pages.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **`@e2e-dev/core` without `e2e`:** a scratch project installed only the packed `@e2e-dev/core` and `@e2e-dev/web`, and `node_modules` held no `e2e`. It ran a script on real Chromium: a login page with a `host.secret()` fill, `saveState()`, `export({ key })` and `SessionState.import`, then a new session restored from that state.
  ```
  e2e installed? 0
  e2e-core copies: 1
  price: 39,000
  browser fixture: object
  restored session signed in
  ```
- **Install smoke:** `scripts/install-smoke.ts` now packs `@e2e-dev/core` too and fails on a second copy of it. It passes with pnpm 11 and pnpm 12, a single `@e2e-dev/core` copy after both the fresh and the frozen-lockfile install.
- **Built CLI:** testbed default suite 588 passed. Web benchmark `tests/` 93 passed.
- **Agentic benchmark** (`CI=1 test:agent --strict-cache`, no model key): the branch matches main, so no cache key moved. The 8 failures on both are steps that need a model call.

  | | main | this branch |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | cache | 26 replayed · 3 handed off · 6 missed | 26 replayed · 3 handed off · 6 missed |
  | failed tests (need a model) | 8 | 8, the same tests |
- **Review:** a fresh-context review (GPT-6.1 Sol) found three secret-handling gaps in session state, all fixed with regression tests that fail without the fix:
  - a restored state lost redaction of the launch's own secrets;
  - `saveState()` errors bypassed the sanitized error boundary;
  - a malformed IV or tag threw a raw crypto error instead of `SESSION_INVALID`.
- **Fixes from cubic, each with a test that fails without it:**
  - mobile `openLink` uses the input budget, so a timed-out open is `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`;
  - `linkBase` refuses an empty `?` or `#` and surrounding whitespace;
  - a recorded space press reads back (already broken on main for `press` keys);
  - agent operations follow `setDefaultTimeout`;
  - a failed close on Ctrl-C is reported on stderr (new SIGINT test on a child process);
  - `isRefusedLinkScheme` is shared from `@e2e-dev/core/engine` with the mobile engine.
- **`defineEngine<Fixtures>` typing** (added after the split, maintainer's choice on the cubic thread): `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` asserts that a missing factory, a factory returning the wrong type, and a union with no member's factories fail to compile, and that narrowing `app` needs none. Each assertion fails without the change. `web()` and `mobile()` compile unchanged.
- **Since the split:** this PR's code is the head reviewed and verified above, plus that typing change and the changesets split across the stack. A second fresh-context review (GPT-6.1 Sol) of the whole stack found the union bypass, fixed here.

## Left for later

- The agent `guard` (`stop`, `deny`, `check`) and `ActResult.status` were removed from this PR in `85af095ab`. They can come back as their own PR.
- `@e2e-dev/core`'s tests still live in `packages/e2e/tests` and import it through `@e2e-dev/core/lib/*`.
- Integrations (`@e2e-dev/kernel`, `eas`, `testmu`, and others) still peer on `e2e`, so they don't yet work with `@e2e-dev/core` alone.
- `@e2e-dev/core`'s `types.ts` still declares the test API types. They are type-only and add nothing at runtime.
- `session-state-1` copies session-1's 64 MiB cap without enforcing it on export, as session-1 does not; one rule for both formats would be its own change.

title: refactor(e2e): split the session half of a worker from the runner
body:
**Stack 1/3:** this PR → [move into `@e2e-dev/core`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1737) → [`@e2e-dev/core` API](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1734). > **2026-11-15:** rebased onto main `235986078` and the package renamed from `e2e-core` to `@e2e-dev/core`. Command output quoted below predates the rename. A refactor inside `packages/e2e` with no behavior change. It separates the half of a worker that drives an engine from the half that runs tests, so the next PR can move the first half into its own package. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph engine["session half (moves to @e2e-dev/core in 2/3)"] ES["EngineSessions
engine init and dispose,
attempt launch and close"] W["openWorker + WorkerPolicy"] A["launchAttempt + AttemptPolicy"] P["resolveProjectConfig"] end subgraph runner["runner half (stays in e2e)"] TE["TargetExecutor"] K["standalone-kinds.ts
hosted, one-shot"] R["resolveConfig
reporters, filters"] end TE -- extends --> ES K -- policy --> W K -- policy --> A R -- over --> P ``` - **`run/engine-sessions.ts`:** `EngineSessions` takes engine init and dispose, and each attempt's session from launch to close, out of `TargetExecutor`, which now extends it. - **`run/standalone.ts` and `run/standalone-attempt.ts`:** the standalone worker takes a `WorkerPolicy` (who claims the engine, what runs its sessions) and an `AttemptPolicy` (`identity`, `reserve`, `launched`, `closed` hooks). The hosted (`openHost`) and one-shot (MCP) kinds move to `run/standalone-kinds.ts`, with the publication, soft failures, and host trace they own. - **Config:** `resolveProjectConfig` (`config/resolve.ts`) resolves everything but reporters and test filters. `resolveConfig` in the new `config/resolve-run.ts` adds those on top. - **Types:** `ProjectConfig` (`types.ts`) is `E2EConfig` without `reporters` and `filters`. `E2EConfig`, `Report`, `Reporter`, and the filter types move to `src/run-types.ts`. `e2e` exports `ProjectConfig` (changeset). - **Smaller moves:** `describeTarget` → `run/provision.ts`, `TestIdentity`/`SkipInfo` → `run/records.ts`, and `pairRecording` → `internal/recording-modes.ts`, so the session side never imports `collect/`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. A refactor shows no behavior on screen, so the evidence is the existing suites, unchanged, against the built packages: - `pnpm test`: e2e 4624 passed (unit and integration), web 810, mobile 531, every other package green. - Testbed through the built CLI (`pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test`): 588 passed, 1 skipped. - `pnpm check` passes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: refactor: move e2e's core into @e2e-dev/core, and engines peer on it
body:
**Stack 2/3:** [session-half split](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1736) → this PR → [`@e2e-dev/core` API](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1734). > **2026-11-15:** rebased onto main `235986078` and the package renamed from `e2e-core` to `@e2e-dev/core`. Command output quoted below predates the rename. Moves the engine contract, locators, agent, replay cache, secrets, and the session half of a worker from `packages/e2e` to `packages/core`, published as the new `@e2e-dev/core` package. `e2e` is built on it. Nothing changes in behavior. ```mermaid flowchart BT core["@e2e-dev/core
engine contract, locators, agent, cache,
secrets, engine sessions, standalone worker"] e2e["e2e
CLI, collector, scheduler, reporters, expect, MCP"] web["@e2e-dev/web, @e2e-dev/mobile"] e2e -- "dependency, exact version (fixed group)" --> core web -- "peer" --> core web -- "peer" --> e2e ``` - **`@e2e-dev/core`:** 145 modules moved with `git mv` to the same paths under `packages/core/src`. Its one public entry is `@e2e-dev/core/engine`. `e2e` reaches the rest as `@e2e-dev/core/lib/` (`./lib/*` in its exports), which is not public API. The next PR adds the `@e2e-dev/core` and `@e2e-dev/core/agent` entries. - **`e2e`:** depends on `@e2e-dev/core` at its exact version (`workspace:*`), and the changesets `fixed` group keeps the two versions equal. `e2e/engine` and `e2e/agent` re-export it unchanged, so engines, integrations, and executors work as before. - **Engines:** `@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` import `@e2e-dev/core/engine` and peer on `@e2e-dev/core` beside `e2e` (`>=0.23.1 <1`). - **Yarn:** Yarn installs no peer the project does not list, and under Plug'n'Play the engine then fails to load. `e2e init` adds `@e2e-dev/core` beside an engine, and `e2e upgrade` adds a required `@e2e-dev/*` peer the project lacks, at the version `e2e` depends on. Checked on Yarn 4.18.1 PnP with packed builds: without core listed the config fails to load, with it the scaffolded test passes. - **CI:** - The root `build` and `test` scripts run `@e2e-dev/core` first, and so does the Bun job in `spec.yml`. - `.github/filters.yml` adds `packages/core/**` to the runner filter. - The nightly examples workflow packs `@e2e-dev/core` and overrides it in each example's npm install. - `scripts/install-smoke.ts` packs it too and fails on a second installed copy. **Most of the diff is mechanical:** of 639 files, 145 are pure renames and most of the rest only rewrite import specifiers to `@e2e-dev/core/lib/`. The parts to read: | What | Where | | --- | --- | | package manifests | `packages/core/package.json`, `packages/e2e/package.json`, `packages/{web,mobile}/package.json`, root `package.json`, `.changeset/config.json` | | the moved entries and their stubs | `packages/core/src/engine/index.ts` and `agent/public.ts` (verbatim), `packages/e2e/src/engine/index.ts` and `agent/public.ts` (re-exports) | | build and test config | `packages/core/tsconfig*.json`, `packages/core/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/e2e/vitest.config.ts` (the integration project externalizes core's `dist`, so tests and the built runner share one module state) | | guards | `packages/e2e/tests/unit/package-imports.test.ts` (follows imports into `@e2e-dev/core`; `ai` stays lazy there), `scripts/install-smoke.ts`, `scripts/check-error-codes.ts` | | CI | `.github/workflows/spec.yml`, `examples.yml`, `.github/actions/example-packages/action.yml`, `.github/filters.yml`, `CODEOWNERS` | | prose | `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` (stability, engine contract), `docs/writing-an-engine.mdx`, `docs/reference/engine.mdx`, READMEs | To confirm the rest is only import lines: `git diff -M --unified=0 -- 'packages/*/src' 'packages/*/tests' | grep '^[-+][^-+]' | grep -v "from '\|import('"`. **Before merging:** `@e2e-dev/core` does not exist on npm yet, and npm Trusted Publishing can only be added to a package that exists. Publish a placeholder `@e2e-dev/core@0.0.0` by hand and connect `release.yml` as its trusted publisher (CONTRIBUTING.md, "npm Trusted Publishing") before this merges. Otherwise the next release publishes `e2e` with an exact dependency on an `@e2e-dev/core` version that failed to publish. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. No behavior changes, so the evidence is the existing suites against the built packages, plus a fresh install: - `pnpm test`: e2e 4626 passed (unit and integration), web 810, mobile 531, every other package green, and `@e2e-dev/core`'s entries check. - Testbed through the built CLI: 588 passed, 1 skipped. - `scripts/install-smoke.ts` with pnpm 11 and pnpm 12: installs the packed `@e2e-dev/core`, `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile` with no build scripts, finds one `@e2e-dev/core` copy, typechecks a mobile tool, and runs a TypeScript test. - `pnpm check` passes. - Not run locally: the nightly examples workflow's npm override of `@e2e-dev/core`. It only runs on the nightly or on a manual dispatch, which posts to Slack. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Config timeouts above 2147483647 ms make every test time out at once
body:
### What happened

A config `timeout` above 2147483647 ms (2^31 - 1) is accepted, but every test then fails at once with `TEST_TIMEOUT`. Node's `setTimeout` clamps a delay past that limit to 1 ms (`TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2999999989 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.`).

```
 FAIL  |web| tests/timeout.e2e.ts > waits 200 ms, then sees the heading
TEST_TIMEOUT: test timed out after 3000000000 ms in phase body
```

Expected: `INVALID_CONFIG` naming the limit, exit 2, the way the CLI flags already behave:

```
$ npx e2e run --action-timeout 3000000000
error: option '--action-timeout <ms>' argument '3000000000' is invalid. must be an integer from 1 through 2147483647
```

With `timeout: 2_147_483_647` the same test passes.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/timeout-overflow

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd timeout-overflow && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`
3. Expected `INVALID_CONFIG` (or the test to pass). Got `TEST_TIMEOUT ... after 3000000000 ms`, exit 1.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.5, node 24.17.0, macOS

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

The config keys go through `positiveInt` (`packages/e2e/src/config/validate.ts:11`), which has no upper bound: `timeout`, `launchTimeout`, `actionTimeout`, `assertionTimeout`, `cleanupTimeout` (`config/resolve.ts:273-277`), `app.command.startupTimeout`/`shutdownTimeout` (`config/command.ts:114-115`), and an agent's `judgmentTimeout` (`config/agent.ts:198`). A test's own `{ timeout }` has the same gap (`collect/registry.ts:319-321`). The flags use `timerMs` and `MAX_TIMER_MS` (`internal/time.ts:85`); #1310 left the config keys alone on purpose.

A possible fix is to cap the `'milliseconds'` case of `positiveInt` at `MAX_TIMER_MS` and the test option the same way. I'm happy to open the PR.

title: markdown reporter does not escape &, so entity text in a title renders as a character
body:
### What happened

The `markdown` reporter escapes `<` and `>` but not `&`, so entity text in a test title (or message) changes meaning in `summary.md`. A test titled `renders © and <b> literally` is written unescaped:

```
**🔴 renders © and <b> literally**
| 🟢 | renders © and <b> literally | 1.8s |
```

GitHub renders that as **renders © and <b> literally** (checked with the GitHub markdown API). The same text reaches the job summary and the `@e2e-dev/github` comment, since both use `renderMarkdownReport`.

Expected: `&copy;`, so the title shows as written.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/markdown-ampersand

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd markdown-ampersand && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`
3. `grep copy .e2e/summary.md`: expected `&copy;`, got `©`.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.5, node 24.17.0, macOS

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

`escapeInline` in `packages/e2e/src/report/markdown-text.ts:55-60` replaces `<` and `>` but not `&`. Adding `.replaceAll('&', '&')` before them would fix it. Code spans are unaffected because entities are literal there. I'm happy to open the PR.

title: junit reporter turns \r into U+FFFD; the  encoding never applies
body:
### What happened

The `junit` reporter turns a carriage return into U+FFFD. A test that throws `new Error('line one\r\nline two')` produces:

```xml
<failure message="line one�
line two" type="ERROR">ERROR (body): line one�
```

Expected `message="line one
line two"`, which is what `attribute()` in `packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts:46` sets out to write. `\r` is a legal XML 1.0 character.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/junit-crlf

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd junit-crlf && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`
3. `grep -n "line one" .e2e/junit.xml`: expected `
`, got `�
`.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.5, node 24.17.0, macOS

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

`text()` (`report/junit.ts:36`) calls `sanitizeText` first. Its `CONTROL_PATTERN` (`internal/errors.ts:490`, `[\^@-\^H\u000b-\^_\u007f-\^_]`) covers U+000D, so the `\r` is already U+FFFD by the time `attribute()` runs `.replaceAll('\r', '')`, and that replacement never matches. Keeping `\r` on the junit path (or normalizing CRLF to LF before sanitizing) would fix it. I'm happy to open the PR.

title: fix(config): reject timeouts above the timer limit
body: ## What and why - `timeout`, `launchTimeout`, `actionTimeout`, `assertionTimeout`, `cleanupTimeout`, `app.command.startupTimeout` / `shutdownTimeout` and `agents..judgmentTimeout` now go through `timerMs` (`packages/e2e/src/config/validate.ts`) instead of `positiveInt`. A value above 2147483647 ms is `INVALID_CONFIG`, like the CLI flags and `maxDuration` already are. - A test's or group's own `{ timeout }` gets the same bound in `collect/registry.ts`, so it fails collection instead of timing out at once. - `positiveInt` is unchanged, since it also guards non-timer integers. - Docs: the limit is noted in `docs/reference/config.mdx` (top-level rules) and `docs/reference/test.mdx` (`timeout`). Patch changeset for `e2e`. ## Issue Fixes #1739 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New unit tests per key family (config top-level, `app.command`, `judgmentTimeout`, test/describe `timeout`) fail on `main` and pass here. - `e2e run` in `apps/testbed` with a config that sets `timeout: 3_000_000_000`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | config accepted; every test fails at once with `TEST_TIMEOUT` (the issue repro) | `INVALID_CONFIG (config)` `timeout must be at most 2147483647 milliseconds, got 3000000000`, exit 2 | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(report): escape & in markdown text, so entity text shows as written
body:
## What and why

- `escapeInline` (`packages/e2e/src/report/markdown-text.ts`) turned `<` and `>` into entities but left `&` alone, so entity text a test wrote was decoded on GitHub: a title `renders © and <b> literally` showed as `renders © and <b> literally`.
- It now replaces `&` first, then `<` and `>`, so the entities it writes are not escaped twice.
- It also stops an entity from becoming a mention or an issue link: GitHub's filters run on the rendered text, so a title `@alice` or `#12` rendered as `@alice` or `#12` before.
- `cell()` is shared by `summary.md` (and so the `@e2e-dev/github` comment and job summary) and the trace pages, so both get the fix. Code spans are untouched: entities are literal there already.

## Issue

Fixes #1740

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Unit: a new `report-markdown.test.ts` case covers a title and a failure message with `©`, `<b>`, and a bare `&`. It fails on main and passes here.
- Built CLI: `main` and this branch packed with `pnpm pack`, installed into the [`markdown-ampersand` repro](https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/markdown-ampersand) (`@e2e-dev/web` 0.15.5), `npx e2e run`, then the `summary.md` row rendered through the GitHub markdown API:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `summary.md` | `renders © and <b> literally` | `renders &copy; and &lt;b&gt; literally` |
| GitHub shows | renders © and <b> literally | renders &copy; and &lt;b&gt; literally |

title: web: check() and tap() fail on a Tailwind sr-only checkbox inside its own label
body:
### What happened `check()` and `tap()` can't operate a checkbox styled with Tailwind's `sr-only` inside its own label, which is the usual toggle-switch markup (Flowbite and most Tailwind kits; Bootstrap's `visually-hidden` is the same CSS): ```html ``` ```ts await screen.getByRole('checkbox', 'Email notifications').check(); ``` ``` ACTION_FAILED: check did not become actionable in time: elementHandle.click: Timeout 29684ms exceeded.
intercepts pointer events: getByRole("checkbox", name: "Email notifications") ``` `tap()` fails the same way, and so does an `sr-only` checkbox in a label that holds only text (`` intercepts). `check({ force: true })` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, so there is no workaround in the test. Expected: the checkbox is checked through its label, as `docs/reference/screen.mdx` says under `check`: "a checkbox or radio hidden under its own label ... is clicked through that label." ### Reproduction https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/sr-only-toggle ### Steps to reproduce 1. `cd sr-only-toggle && npm install` 2. `npx e2e run` 3. All three tests fail with `ACTION_FAILED ... intercepts pointer events`. Expected them to check the box. ### Versions e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.5, node 24.17.0, macOS. Also fails on the 2026-11-13 nightly (e2e 0.23.1-nightly, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0-nightly). ### Engine @e2e-dev/web ### Anything else A follow-up to #1276. On the nightly, removing only `margin: -1px` from `.sr-only` makes all three pass, so the stand-in from #1595 works but misses this case. In `pickStandIn` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts:143`), the label is used only when the control's centre lies inside the label's rect. `sr-only`'s `margin: -1px` puts the 1×1 input's centre just outside the label's left edge, so it returns `null` and the click goes to the hidden input. I'd like to work on the fix.

title: --max-failures with several workers reports unstarted tests as interrupted instead of skipped
body:
### What happened

With more than one worker, `--max-failures` lets a worker start its next test after the run has reached the limit. That test is then cancelled a few ms later and reported `interrupted`, instead of skipped with `failure-limit`.

Two files, each starting with a failing test, `npx e2e run --workers 2 --max-failures 2`:

```
   × |web| tests/b.e2e.ts > b next (interrupted) 4ms
   ↓ |web| tests/b.e2e.ts > b last [run stopped after 2 failures (--max-failures 2)]
   × |web| tests/a.e2e.ts > a next (interrupted) 5ms
   ↓ |web| tests/a.e2e.ts > a last [run stopped after 2 failures (--max-failures 2)]
      Tests  2 failed | 2 interrupted | 0 passed | 2 skipped (6)
```

`report.json`: `a next` and `b next` have status `interrupted` with one attempt `interrupted:CANCELLED`. 3 of 3 runs gave the same result. With `--workers 1` the run behaves as documented.

Expected, per `docs/reference/cli.mdx` (`--max-failures`): "Tests not started, including the rest of the file whose test reached the limit, are skipped with cause `failure-limit`." So `a next` and `b next` should be skipped, and the summary should read `2 failed | 4 skipped`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/max-failures-workers

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd max-failures-workers && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run --workers 2 --max-failures 2`
3. Expected `2 failed | 4 skipped`. Got `2 failed | 2 interrupted | 2 skipped`.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.15.5, node 24.17.0, macOS

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

Each worker only counts its own failures against the snapshot of the run's count it received when the unit was dispatched (`packages/e2e/src/run/worker/session.ts:256`, `countFailure`; the snapshot is passed in `scheduler.ts:670` and `:866`). When another worker's failure completes the limit, this worker still sees itself below it, starts the next test, and only stops when the scheduler's interrupt (`stopEarly`, `scheduler.ts:408`) arrives. #664 mentions that a failure on another worker cannot stop a worker early, but the docs promise a skip.

The status matters because the summary reports tests as stopped mid-run that never did any work.

I'd like to work on the fix.

title: chore(deps): bump hono from 4.13.14 to 4.13.18
body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.14 to 4.13.18.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.18

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

validator() skips validation for requests whose Content-Type parameters are formatted differently

Affects: validator('json') and validator('form') in hono/validator. A Content-Type with whitespace before ;, a trailing ;, or an unusual parameter name was not recognized, so the validator saw an empty object while the handler could read all fields. This completes the fix for GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v. The validator now decides by the media type alone, as c.req.parseBody() does. GHSA-92p4-j3wq-jmqx

bodyLimit() keeps every transfer chunk of a request body in memory

Affects: bodyLimit() in hono/body-limit. A body sent in very small transfer chunks was retained as one object per chunk, so a request within the configured limit could exhaust memory. The body is now buffered in one array bounded by maxSize. GHSA-39q9-qp46-w8xg

mount() and app.mount() forward a wrong path when a custom getPath adds a prefix

Affects: mount() in hono/mount and app.mount() on 4.13.16 and 4.13.17. With a getPath that prepends a prefix such as the host name, one segment too many was removed from the forwarded path, so middleware scoped inside the mount prefix could be skipped. The prefix is removed from the routed path again. Paths that would change meaning when forwarded now get 400, and an optional regular expression parameter in a mount path throws. GHSA-h25j-2p75-qj33

serveStatic() serves a path that was decoded twice when allowPercentInPath is enabled

Affects: serveStatic() in hono/serve-static and the runtime adapters, only with allowPercentInPath: true. A malformed percent escape in the request path was decoded a second time, so a path that middleware registered on the encoded form did not see could still reach a static file. The file path must now be the same as the routed path, and otherwise the response is 404. GHSA-74fm-fwc7-3fwp

Users who rely on validator(), bodyLimit(), mount() with a custom getPath, or serveStatic() with allowPercentInPath are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.17...v4.13.18

v4.13.17

What's Changed

title: chore(changeset): launch @e2e-dev/browser-run on a release minor

title: fix(web): check an sr-only checkbox or radio through its own label
body:
## What and why - Tailwind's `sr-only` (and Bootstrap's `visually-hidden`) shrinks a checkbox to one clipped pixel with `margin: -1px`. In a label with no left padding, the usual toggle switch, that pixel's centre sits half a pixel outside the label, so `pickStandIn` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`) rejected the label stand-in and Playwright clicked the hidden input: `
intercepts pointer events`. - A pixel-sized control whose centre lands outside its label, or hits nothing, now takes a label the way a boxless control does: the first visible label whose centre is not a link or another control. `controlPoint` clicks the label's centre for a control centred outside it, so the point read and the point clicked are the same. - On that path a label whose centre nothing hits yet (a dialog with `pointer-events: none` while it opens) is read again rather than taken, so a click never lands on a link there that was not checked. The boxless path keeps its current behaviour, so a wrapping or very tall label still works there. - Everything else reads as before: a pixel inside a padded label is still clicked at its own point, a visible pixel-sized input with no visible label is still clicked as itself, and a full-size radio covered from outside its label box is still refused. I kept the label-box check instead of widening it by a pixel, since `still refuses a radio whose label covers it from outside the label box` depends on it. Not covered, and failing on main too: an `sr-only` control under `zoom` or `transform: scale()` (it measures more than a pixel), and one whose label starts with a button, which the half-pixel point hits first. ## Issue Fixes #1744 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `check-actions.test.ts`: the 8 new `sr-only`/`visually-hidden` cases (check, tap, uncheck, both target kinds) fail on main and pass here. The padded-label-with-a-link, visible one-pixel, link-behind-an-opening-dialog, and wrapping-label cases pass on both, as guards. - Built CLI: `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web` packed from main and from this branch, installed into the [`sr-only-toggle` repro](https://github.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/tree/main/sr-only-toggle), `npx e2e run`: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `3 failed`: `ACTION_FAILED: check did not become actionable in time ...
intercepts pointer events` | `3 passed` (`check` 972ms, `tap` 142ms, text-only label 141ms) | | ![main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/main/sr-only-toggle/media/main-after.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/main/sr-only-toggle/media/branch-after.png) | This branch running `check()` on the toggle: ![check on this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhinavapasok/e2e-repros/main/sr-only-toggle/media/branch-check-sr-only-toggle.gif)

title: fix(run): wait for the runner's count before the next test under --max-failures
body: ## What and why - The scheduler is now the only owner of the failure count. `RunUnitMessage.answersFailures` is just a flag that the run has a limit; the snapshot (`{ limit, failures }`) and the worker's own `countFailure` arithmetic are gone. - While the run has a limit, a worker that reports a counted failure waits before its next test (`TargetExecutorOptions.beforePair`) until the runner answers. A setup unit holds one pair, so it needs no gate. The answer is a new `continue` message when the run is still below the limit, or the existing `interrupt` with the `failure-limit` skip once it is reached. One round-trip per failure, no timing. - The worker counts the failure before it emits the result, because an in-process runner answers inside `emit`. - Patch changeset for `e2e`. No docs change: `docs/reference/cli.mdx` already describes the fixed behavior. ## Issue Fixes #1745 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New 2-worker, `maxFailures: 2` test in `parallel-workers.test.ts`: file `a` fails at once, file `b` fails 500 ms later, so `b`'s worker trips the limit. It asserts the rest of the tripping file is skipped with `failure-limit` (no `interrupted`), and at most one `interrupted` overall. It fails 3 of 3 runs against a `main` build and passes 5 of 5 here. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `b next` `interrupted` (started after the limit, then cancelled) | `b next` and `b last` skipped, `failure-limit` | - New 2-worker, `maxFailures: 3` test: each file fails once, and both `next` tests must pass, so a lost `continue` hangs it. A `scheduler.test.ts` unit checks the answers: `continue, continue` below the limit, `continue, interrupt` at it, nothing without a limit. - `vitest run tests/unit`: 3653 pass. `vitest run tests/integration`: 972 pass, 3 fail in `cli-init.test.ts` only because `@e2e-dev/mobile` was not built locally (same on `main`). - `pnpm check` green. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(cli): step through a test without a terminal
body:
## Problem

`e2e run --step` holds each step until a key, so it needs a terminal. A coding agent's shell has none, so an agent could not step through a test.

## Change

Without a terminal, `--step` runs the test in a background process. Later commands from the same directory drive it:

```bash
npx e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts --step   # returns at the first held step, with its screen
npx e2e run --step next                 # runs it, returns at the next one
npx e2e run --step rest                 # or runs the rest
npx e2e run --step stop                 # or ends the run (exit 130)
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as agent shell
  participant S as e2e run --step-serve (detached)
  A->>S: e2e run tests/x.e2e.ts --step (spawns it)
  S-->>A: ✓ step 1, Paused before step 2, Screen
  A->>S: e2e run --step next (Unix socket)
  S-->>A: ✓ step 2, Paused before step 3, Screen
  A->>S: e2e run --step next
  S-->>A: × step 3 + error, summary, "The stepped run has ended." (exit 1)
```

- The run listens on a Unix socket (a named pipe on Windows) in a per-user `0700` temp directory keyed by the working directory, so one directory has one stepped run (`packages/e2e/src/cli/step-control.ts`).
- Each answer starts with the run's output since the last answer, including one line per finished step (`✓` / `×` with its error). The last answer ends with the summary and `The stepped run has ended.`, and the command exits with the run's code.
- The held step carries the screen it waits on, read in the worker and redacted the way the trace page is (`heldScreens` in `packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts`).
- `next` and `rest` act only on a step a command has printed. A command killed by its shell's timeout loses nothing: the next one gets the step or the end it missed, with a line saying its action was not applied.
- A held step with no command for 30 minutes stops the run, so an abandoned run does not keep its app and browser.
- With a terminal, `--step` is unchanged. Both paths drive the same `StepGate` (`packages/e2e/src/cli/step.ts`); the terminal path feeds it keys, the background run feeds it commands.
- A second start in the same directory exits 2 with `RUNNER_BUSY` (documented in `docs/reference/errors.mdx`).
- Docs: a new section in `docs/debugging.mdx`, `docs/reference/cli.mdx`, the skill references, and a changeset.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **Agent runs.** A scratch Vite + React todo app had a planted counter bug. A fresh agent with no context got only "use step mode to find why the test fails", three times on Linux and once on macOS with `--headed`. It learned the usage from `npx e2e run --help`, saw the bug one step before the assertion failed, and fixed it each time. Each round's friction drove changes here: per-step result lines, the ended line, the error indent under a failed step, the "not applied" note, and the busy message.
- **Headed on macOS.** The browser window stayed open across the separate `next` commands and closed when the run ended.
- **CLI output from the rebased build on the same app.** No terminal on stdin.

Start:

```text
$ npx e2e run tests/todos.e2e.ts --step < /dev/null
No terminal, so the run goes on in the background. Drive it from this directory with e2e run --step next, rest, or stop.
 ✓ target "web" command at http://localhost:5191/ ready 210ms
✓ app.open "/" 122ms
Paused before step 2 of completing a todo updates the counter [web]:
  locator.fill "getByLabel("New todo")" (tests/todos.e2e.ts:7)
Screen:
  http://localhost:5191/
  ...
  status "0 items left"
  button "Clear completed" [disabled]
Next: e2e run --step next runs it, e2e run --step rest runs the rest, e2e run --step stop ends the run.
```

The 6th `next` (exit 0):

```text
✓ locator.check "getByLabel("Buy milk")" 29ms
Paused before step 8 of completing a todo updates the counter [web]:
  expect.toHaveText "getByRole("status")" (tests/todos.e2e.ts:14)
Screen:
  ...
  checkbox "Buy milk" [checked]
  ...
  status "2 items left"
  button "Clear completed"
```

The 7th `next` (exit 1):

```text
× expect.toHaveText "getByRole("status")" 5.01s failed
  ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed
  locator: getByRole("status")
  expected: text "1 item left"
  observed: text "2 items left" (match count 1)
...
The stepped run has ended.
```

`tests/integration/cli-step.test.ts` drives the built CLI on the fake engine. It covers:
- the start, `next`, and `rest`;
- a run that cannot start;
- a stale claim lock;
- a second start;
- a killed command whose missed step is printed without being run;
- a run that ended while no command waited;
- a 500 KB answer to `stop`, which fails without the flush;
- an agent step printed once;
- a secret on a held screen printed as `<secret:apiToken>`.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Show an assertion's expected value in the pause line (`toHaveText "1 item left"`).
- A screen diff against the previous step.
- Hold on a failed step instead of ending the run.
- Read the screen only for steps that will be held: today every top-level step reads it, which costs more on mobile.
- Agent step lines and the summary are missing when the list reporter is turned off.

## Review

Council review (the design of `step-control.ts`):

| Delegate | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 5.5 (high) | 5/10 | 7/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 | 9/10 | 9/10 |
| Claude Fable 5.1 (high) | 5/10 | 7/10 | 8/10 | 7/10 | 6/10 | 9/10 |
| GPT Sol 6.1 (xhigh) | 6/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 | 7/10 | 10/10 |
| GPT Astra (xhigh) | 6/10 | 7/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 | 8/10 | 10/10 |

- **Claude Fable 5.2 (high), fresh review.** 7/10. It found:
  - a lost `stop` answer on exit, fixed with the flush;
  - agent steps printed twice;
  - a missing ended line on a fast failure.

  All three are fixed, with tests.
- **Fresh-context self-review.** It found that a run ending with no command waiting lost its result, and that the idle timer ignored commands. Both are fixed, with tests.

- **cubic.** It found five issues, all fixed:
  - a second start now prints `RUNNER_BUSY`;
  - the starting command no longer gets a stray "not applied" line when its run already ended;
  - three docs fixes: the terminal condition, Windows `< NUL`, and the `RUNNER_BUSY` remedy.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT 6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved

Made with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: fix(junit): encode a carriage return before the value is sanitised
body: ## What changed - `attribute()` escaped `\r` to ` ` **after** `text()`, and `text()` sanitises first: `sanitizeText` replaces `\r` with U+FFFD, so by the time the escape ran the carriage return was gone and the reference was never written. A CRLF failure message reached a report viewer with a replacement character where its line break was (`packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts:37`). - The escape now runs on the raw value, and the sanitiser runs afterwards, where neither the reference nor its `&` is touched. `text()` keeps its order, since element content may hold a raw newline. - Two helpers so each order is stated once: `escapeMarkup()` and `sanitize()`. - `.changeset/junit-attribute-carriage-return.md`, `patch` on `e2e`. ## Issue Fixes #1741 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, on Windows (Node 26). Reproduced first: with `packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts` taken from `origin/main` and the new test in place, the assertion fails and the report shows where the line break went: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `expected ' line two" ...>` | output: `` | ``` pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/report-junit.test.ts -p unit this branch: 43 passed, 3 failed main: 42 passed, 3 failed (same 3) ``` The 3 failures are the `CI_PROJECT_DIR` symlink tests, which need symlink support (Developer Mode on Windows, `CONTRIBUTING.md`); they fail identically on `main` and are unrelated to this change. No network, no device.

body:
### What happened

When opening an MCP session with an engine package that provides separate `import` and `require` exports, e2e selects the `require` entry instead of the `import` entry. However, I expected the `import` entry to be selected because the engine is loaded using a dynamic `import()`.

title: fix(mcp): load the import entry of an engine with separate import and require exports
body: ## What and why - `resolveEntry` in `packages/e2e/src/mcp/default-engine.ts` found the entry with `createRequire().resolve()`, so it used the `require` conditions. It only read the `import` entry when that threw `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. The entry is then loaded with `import()`, so a package that exports both picked the `require` file. - Now it reads the `import` target from `exports` first (the existing `importEntry` helper: `import`, `node`, or `default`, in the order written). `require` resolution stays for packages whose `exports` give no import target, or that have no `exports`. - An `import` target that is missing on disk is reported as "installed ... but its entry cannot be resolved", like the other unloadable entries, instead of falling back to the `require` file. - Patch changeset for `e2e`. No docs change: the docs do not describe how the entry is picked. ## Issue Fixes #1758 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New unit test in `mcp-default-engine.test.ts`: a package with `{ import: './index.js', require: './index.cjs' }` on `.` and on a subpath (written `require` first), each file returning an engine with a different name. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `from-require` (test fails) | `from-import` for `dual` and `dual/web` | - `vitest run tests/unit`: 3654 pass, 1 skipped. - `pnpm check` green. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: ACP executor ignores cancellation while waiting for the previous turn to stop
body:
## Summary

In `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2`, cancelling a step while it waits for a previous
ACP turn to stop leaves its `runStep` promise waiting. If the previous turn
ignores cancellation, the waiting promise eventually rejects with
`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` instead of its original `STEP_TIMEOUT`.

## Reproduction

Public reproduction: https://github.com/jxnxts/e2e-acp-cancellation-repro/tree/1f5dc21168dd4db1400301e0e28f0f99356a0548

From the standalone `public-reproducer` directory, using Node 24.22.2:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm test
```

The lockfile pins `e2e@0.23.0` and `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2`. A scripted ACP
agent connects to the real MCP tool server, starts one prompt, and ignores
cancellation. The probe cancels a second step while it waits for that turn.
No browser or model account is required.

Exit 1 is the expected bug reproduction, with:

```json
{"expected":"STEP_TIMEOUT","received":"MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED","sameReason":false,"prompts":1,"secondObservations":0}
```

Expected: reject with the second step's original cancellation reason.
The same probe passes with the proposed corrected build, exit 0 and
`received: STEP_TIMEOUT`, `sameReason: true`.

The runner already enforces the outer `agent.act` deadline. This concerns
the underlying executor promise that keeps running after cancellation.
Verified on macOS arm64, Node 24.22.2, npm 11.19.1.

title: fix(acp): cancel the wait for the previous agent turn when the step ends
body: - Cancel the previous-turn wait when the waiting ACP step ends, preserving its original cancellation reason and clearing the grace timer. - Reuse the existing abort helper in `packages/acp/src/executor.ts`. Add a scripted-agent regression and an ACP patch changeset. ## Issue Fixes #1760 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Built CLI with Chromium and a scripted ACP agent: the same probe fails on main and passes with this change. - [Standalone reproduction](https://github.com/jxnxts/e2e-acp-cancellation-repro/tree/1f5dc21168dd4db1400301e0e28f0f99356a0548), installed with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` then `npm test`, using published `e2e@0.23.0` and `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2`, then replacing only ACP with the corrected local tarball. | main / affected release | this branch | | --- | --- | | Exit 1: `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` replaces `STEP_TIMEOUT` | Exit 0: the same `STEP_TIMEOUT` object is preserved | ```text Affected: received=MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED sameReason=false Corrected: received=STEP_TIMEOUT sameReason=true ``` The runner already enforces the outer `agent.act` deadline. This fixes the executor promise that continues waiting after cancellation. Verified on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.2; no model account is needed.

title: ACP executor waits for its opening screen after the step is cancelled
body:
## Reproduction

Standalone reproduction: [jxnxts/e2e-acp-opening-screen-repro at 34868b65](https://github.com/jxnxts/e2e-acp-opening-screen-repro/tree/34868b65f8a429de4e41976e1a0254028c43e82b). It uses the public `acp().runStep` API and a scripted local ACP agent.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jxnxts/e2e-acp-opening-screen-repro.git
cd e2e-acp-opening-screen-repro
git checkout 34868b65f8a429de4e41976e1a0254028c43e82b
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm test
```

Verified on macOS arm64 with Node v24.22.2, `e2e@0.23.1` and `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2`. No browser, model login, paid inference or application service is used. `npm test` is expected to exit 1 with the published affected package.

The probe warms one ACP session, holds the next step's `ctx.observe` promise, and aborts that step with an `AgentError('STEP_TIMEOUT', ...)`. The observation is released in `finally` so the red run also cleans up.

## Expected

`runStep` rejects promptly with the original cancellation reason before the observation resolves. The `StepExecutorContext.signal` contract requires an executor to stop promptly on abort. No prompt should be sent for the cancelled step, and a following step can reuse the open session.

## Actual

With `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2`, the returned promise remains pending until the observation resolves:

```text
stoppedBeforeScreenRelease=false sameReason=false
AssertionError: runStep must reject with its abort reason before the opening screen is released
```

This concerns the executor promise. The runner already enforces the outer `agent.act` deadline, so this is not a claim that the whole test ignores its deadline.

## Scope

The uninterruptible await is `stepMessage(...)`, which includes the opening-screen observation, in `packages/acp/src/executor.ts`. It is separate from #1760 / #1761, whose cancellation bug occurs while waiting for the previous ACP prompt turn to settle; this probe completes its first turn normally and holds only the next observation.

title: fix(acp): stop cancelled steps while reading the opening screen
body:
## What and why

- A cancelled ACP step no longer waits for its opening screen. `runStep` races the screen read against the step signal with the existing `untilAborted` helper, so it rejects with the step's original reason while `ctx.observe` is still pending (`packages/acp/src/executor.ts:77`).
- `runStep` checks the signal before it starts the screen read (`packages/acp/src/executor.ts:75`), so a step aborted after the previous turn settles never calls `observe`.
- The cancelled step sends no prompt, and the session stays held for the next step.
- The previous-turn wait from #1761 is unchanged. The runner's outer deadline is unchanged too; this changes when the executor promise settles, and does not stop an engine operation that ignores its own cancellation.

## Issue

Fixes #1765

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/acp exec vitest run tests/executor.test.ts`, with `packages/acp/src/executor.ts` from main and then from this branch, on Node v24.22.2 and main `0a5ee163`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `× ends a cancelled step without waiting for its opening screen`: `runStep` has not rejected 1 s after the abort (`Number of calls: 0`) | passes: rejects with the same `STEP_TIMEOUT` object, one session, one prompt for the cancelled pair, then the next step passes on the same session |
| 1 failed, 38 passed | 39 passed |

- `does not read the screen for an already-aborted step` passes on main as well: since #1761, `ready()` rejects first for a step aborted before `runStep`. It pins the contract that `observe` is never called; it does not isolate the pre-check, which guards an abort that lands after the previous turn settles.
- Earlier [standalone reproduction](https://github.com/jxnxts/e2e-acp-opening-screen-repro/tree/34868b65f8a429de4e41976e1a0254028c43e82b) against the published `@e2e-dev/acp@0.1.2` (scripted ACP agent, held observation, no model account): main stays pending until the screen is released; the fix rejects with the identical reason (`stoppedBeforeScreenRelease=true sameReason=true`, `sessions=1 prompts=2`).
- Not run: a live ACP agent (Claude Code or Codex) on the testbed, which needs a model account.

- Local validation of the reviewed content: `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` and ACP typecheck passed; all 50 ACP tests passed. CI on the updated PR head must be checked separately.

title: test: use a Git-compatible null device on Windows
body:
### Problem

The Git test helper sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to `os.devNull`. On Windows, Node returns `\\.\nul`, but Git for Windows rejects that spelling:

```text
fatal: unable to access '\\.\nul': Invalid argument
```

Every test that initializes a throwaway Git repository then fails before it reaches the behavior under test.

### Reproduction

On Windows, run:

```console
pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/vcs.test.ts
```

### Proposed fix

Use the Win32 device name `NUL` for `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` on Windows and keep `os.devNull` on other platforms.

title: test(git): make repository fixtures portable on Windows
body:
- Git for Windows rejects Node's `\\.\nul` path. Use `NUL` for the test repositories' global config.
- Stage the executable bit explicitly in the mode-change fixture, so it works when `chmod` cannot change Git's file mode.

## Issue

Fixes #1768

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Windows: `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/vcs.test.ts tests/unit/changes.test.ts`: 12 passed, 1 skipped.
- Windows: `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/explore-change.test.ts -t 'shows a mode change'`: 1 passed, 20 skipped.
- Lint and `e2e` typecheck passed after building `e2e` and `@e2e-dev/web`.
- The full explore-change file still has two unrelated Windows failures in fixtures with newline filenames and long paths.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| Git exits with `fatal: unable to access '\\.\nul': Invalid argument` | Git accepts `NUL`; Git-backed assertions run |
| With the null device fixed, the mode-change fixture reports `nothing to commit, working tree clean` on Windows | The fixture commits `100644 -> 100755` and its existing assertions pass |

### CI

Four Node versions passed. Node 24.8.0 passed `e2e`, including the changed fixtures, then failed in ACP cleanup with `ENOTEMPTY` at `packages/acp/tests/executor.test.ts:25`: [failed job](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43560773386/job/132343722912).

The ACP helper registers log-directory deletion before step teardown, and `afterEach` runs them FIFO. The still-running child's cancellation handler can append to that directory while deletion runs. Reversing callbacks alone would not guarantee child exit. This needs a separate cleanup regression and fix, not a change to Git fixtures.

A maintainer needs to rerun that job: GitHub rejected the PR author's rerun request because it requires repository admin rights.

The cleanup fix and regression are proposed separately in #1774.

title: Windows: failures and steps lose source locations
fix(report): keep source locations on Windows
body:
Windows stack frames with a drive letter were discarded, leaving failure locations absent and step files as `unknown`. Recognize native paths and file URLs, and keep dependency frames excluded with either path separator.

## Issue

Fixes #1770

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Windows 11, Node 24, real Chromium on the testbed with built packages: exercised `tests-stress/a-fail.e2e.ts`, smoke tests and the full reporter stress suite. Intentional failures retained their outcomes; smoke tests passed.

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| Assertion failure has no `error.source` or code frame | `error.source` is `tests-stress/a-fail.e2e.ts:6:3`, with its code frame |
| Recorded steps have `source.file: "unknown"` | Steps name the test file and lines 5 and 6 |

```text
ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed
 ❯ tests-stress\a-fail.e2e.ts:6:3
      5|   await app.open();
      6|   await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Playground')).toHaveText(…
       |   ^
```

- Source/error/failure-text tests and all three list location tests pass. Regression cases cover drive paths, UNC, file URLs, spaces, parentheses, queries and dependency exclusion. Other list-reporter Windows path/golden cases still fail.

### CI

All five Node test jobs, web/mobile benchmarks, docs, Bun and fresh installs passed. The spec `check` job had 508 passed, 2 skipped and one iframe timeout: [failed job](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43561641148/job/132346542854). That job passed on the preceding commit; the later commit only qualifies the docs.

Inspection found an existing removal race in `packages/web/src/surface.ts`: `frameOf()` counts an iframe before reading it through a live locator. Removing it between those calls makes Playwright wait for it to reappear. A direct Chromium reproduction confirmed that behavior. No frame/locator code changed here; that needs a separate regression and fix. Local repeats also showed the intermittent timeout. A maintainer rerun is needed because the author cannot rerun upstream workflows.

title: scripts: the release-safety scripts ship with no tests
body:
`scripts/restore-peer-ranges.ts`, `scripts/canary-changeset.ts`, and `scripts/check-peer-ranges.ts` run in `pnpm check` and the release flow with no unit test beside them:

```
$ ls scripts/*.test.ts | rg "peer|canary|restore"
(no output)
```

PR #1417 started covering this family (`public-packages.test.ts`, `pr-policy/github.test.ts`) and stopped before these three. What each one guards:

- `restore-peer-ranges.ts` runs after `changeset publish` / `version-packages` to widen the canary's exact peer pins back to `>=<major.minor.patch> <major+1>`. A bug there leaves exact pins on main, and a consumer who updates `e2e` alone then hits the npm ERESOLVE AGENTS.md documents.
- `canary-changeset.ts` writes the all-public-packages bump that `pnpm run canary` and the nightly `release.yml` job consume. A wrong package list ships a snapshot whose peers name a different runner build.
- `check-peer-ranges.ts` is the `pnpm check` gate for peer-range shape on every peer one `packages/*` package declares on another.

Plan: a `test(scripts)` PR adding `node --test` coverage for the three (same harness as `scripts/changeset-bumps.test.ts`), no product-code change.

title: testbed: one serial group cannot catch cross-group scheduling regressions
body:
The testbed is the contract that every runner feature has a deterministic test (AGENTS.md layout), but the serial-group feature has exactly one group:

```
$ rg -n "serial: true" apps/testbed
apps/testbed/tests/wizard.e2e.ts:3:test.describe('workspace wizard', { serial: true, tags: ['wizard'] }, () => {
```

One group exercises serial ordering inside itself, but nothing covers how two serial groups queue relative to each other or to parallel work — a scheduler regression in `applySerialClosure` / cross-group dispatch would pass the default suite that gates every PR.

Plan: a `test(testbed)` PR adding a second, independent `test.describe({ serial: true })` stateful flow so the default suite covers cross-group serial isolation.

title: benchmark: a scenario can ship without any test
body:
`apps/web-benchmark/README.md` promises "Every scenario has a deterministic twin, `tests/<slug>.e2e.ts`", but nothing checks it, and the contract is already broken on `main` — the catalog entry `file-round-trip` has no test file and no reference anywhere in `tests/` or `tests-agent/`:

```
$ rg -n "file-round-trip|FileRoundTrip" apps/web-benchmark/tests apps/web-benchmark/tests-agent
(no output)
$ ls apps/web-benchmark/tests | rg -i "file|round"
(no output)
```

`apps/mobile-benchmark` has the same shape on the agentic side: every catalog entry has an entry in `tests-agent/scenarios.e2e.ts` today except the documented Control Inventory exclusion, and nothing keeps it that way — a scenario added to `src/examples.ts` can ship with no agentic coverage and both suites stay green.

Plan: a `test(scripts)` PR adding a `scripts/check-benchmark-coverage.ts` check (wired like the other `check-*` scripts) that fails when a web catalog slug has no `tests/<slug>.e2e.ts` (an explicitly skipped scenario keeps its file, per the README) or a mobile/web scenario has no agentic entry, with the documented exclusions encoded — plus the missing `tests/file-round-trip.e2e.ts` twin so the check starts green.

title: explore: the clipping ceilings mirror the report schema with no test
body:
`packages/e2e/src/explore/state.ts` hardcodes the clip ceilings with only a comment tying them to the wire schema:

```
packages/e2e/src/explore/state.ts:21:/** Ceilings mirroring `schema/report-v1.schema.json` `explore`. */
packages/e2e/src/explore/state.ts:22:export const MAX_TITLE_CHARS = 200;
packages/e2e/src/explore/state.ts:23:const MAX_INSTRUCTION_CHARS = 2_000;
```

Nothing asserts the mirror. `report-v1.schema.json` carries the same numbers as `maxLength`/`maxItems` (`exploreFinding.title` 200, `exploreStep.instruction` 2000, `exploreStep.summary` 4000, `reproduction` 20 items of 500, `path` 2048), so a one-sided edit either truncates text the schema would have accepted or lets `ExploreState` emit a report the schema rejects at report time instead of at the edit.

Plan: a `test(explore)` PR adding a unit test that reads `schema/report-v1.schema.json` and asserts each `ExploreState` ceiling matches its schema counterpart, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

title: agent: relocate re-captures the screen even when a recent observation matches
web: the tree lists controls behind a showModal() dialog, which no tap reaches
body:
### What happened

When a page opens a `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, everything outside the dialog is inert: Chrome's accessibility tree drops it, and no click reaches it. The web engine's tree still lists it, so an agent is offered controls it can't use:

```text
#root document "Store"
 #n2 main
  #n3 heading "Store"
  #n4 button "Add to cart"
  #n5 status "idle"
 #n6 dialog "Cookie consent"
  #n7 text="We use cookies."
  #n8 button "Accept" [focused]
```

A tap on `#n4` waits out its action timeout, then fails with `<dialog …> intercepts pointer events` (14.9s in the repro). A section with the `inert` attribute on the same page is left out of the tree (#585), so the agent is never offered that one.

Expected: while a modal dialog is open, the tree leaves out what is outside it, the way it does for an `inert` subtree.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/modal-inert

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd modal-inert && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`
3. `cat .e2e/results/*a-control-behind*/attempt-1/screen-at-failure.txt`: `button "Add to cart"` is listed beside the open dialog. The second test shows the `inert` section's button is not in the tree.

The repro's executor stands in for a model: it taps the node the tree names, so no API key is needed.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0, node 22.23.4, Linux

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

### Anything else

- `isInert` in `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:1148-1157` notes this already: "A modal dialog's inertness of the rest of the page is not in the style and stays listed."
- I checked it against Chrome's tree with the crosscheck harness. Chrome has no node for the page behind a modal, or for a lower dialog under a second `showModal()`. `aria-modal="true"` on a div leaves Chrome's tree unchanged, so only native modal dialogs are affected.
- Playwright's `getByRole` matches both the modal-blocked button and the `inert` one, and both clicks time out. So deterministic locators behave the same either way; this is about the tree the agent reads.
- One way to fix it: when `dialog:modal` matches, treat nodes outside the topmost modal dialog as inert in `hidesSubtree`. Happy to open the PR.

title: mobile(): a typo'd snapshot or videoTouches value loads and quietly uses the default
body:
### What happened

`mobile()` checks `platform`, `settle` and `transition` at config load, but not `snapshot` or `videoTouches`. A typo loads fine and the engine quietly uses the default:

- `snapshot: 'Interactive'` captures the full tree, because the engine compares against `'interactive'` exactly.
- `videoTouches: 'false'` (a string, e.g. from an env var) still draws the touch indicator, because it compares against `false`.

Expected: `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load naming the accepted values, the way `settle` and `transition` are rejected.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/f64e7dba8d617a8804cba96cd8c885658db8aca5/packages/mobile/src/surface.ts#L1151 and https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/f64e7dba8d617a8804cba96cd8c885658db8aca5/packages/mobile/src/surface.ts#L712

### Steps to reproduce

1. In any mobile project: `targets: [{ name: 'ios', engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios', snapshot: 'Interactive' as never, videoTouches: 'false' as never }) }]`
2. `npx e2e run`: the config loads, snapshots are full trees and the touches are drawn. Expected an `INVALID_CONFIG` error.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.7, node 22.22.0

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

Happy to send a small PR for this.

title: fix(mobile): refuse an unknown snapshot or videoTouches value in mobile()
