title: [web]: MCP full-screen fallback repeats unchanged navigation subtrees
body:
### What happened

I use `e2e mcp` to explore and verify UI flows before deciding whether to save them as regression tests. For example, when checking an order details page for the first time, the agent needs to inspect the new content and find the right locators.

When an action changes enough of the screen to trigger the full-tree fallback, MCP sends the entire tree again. On an app with persistent navigation, that response can repeat hundreds of sidebar nodes whose IDs and contents are unchanged.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an `e2e mcp` session on a web app with a persistent sidebar and a main panel that changes substantially between views. For example, use an order list that opens an order details view while keeping the sidebar mounted.
2. Call `observe` on the order list and note the sidebar node IDs and contents.
3. Open an order through MCP. Find an action result that starts with `The screen changed substantially` and compare its sidebar with the previous observation.

**Actual behavior.** The response contains the new order details and repeats the full sidebar, even though the sidebar's nodes are unchanged.

**Proposed behavior.** Include the new content in the response and summarize each large unchanged subtree on its root line. For example:

```text
#n54012 list (213 nodes inside, unchanged since revision b21)
```

Keep `observe` returning the complete tree so a client can retrieve the sidebar details if the earlier result is no longer in context.

### Why this matters

Each repeated subtree adds text to the tool result during the initial exploration, while the agent is still discovering the flow and identifying what to assert. Persistent navigation can repeat on several page transitions in a single session.

In one captured response using a local prototype, the folded output was **5,158 bytes**. Restoring the sidebar from the previous revision brought it to **15,448 bytes**, a **66.6% reduction in tool-result text** with folding enabled. This measurement covers one response. Session-wide token savings remain unverified.

title: fix(web): leave the page behind a modal dialog out of the agent's tree
body: ## What and why - A `` opened with `showModal()` makes everything outside it inert, and Chrome's accessibility tree drops it. The agent's tree kept it, so the agent was offered controls no tap reaches: each pick waited out its action timeout (14.9s in the repro) before failing with ` intercepts pointer events`. An `inert` subtree already leaves the tree (#585). - Before the walk, the reader finds the open `dialog:modal` elements (not `:modal`, which a fullscreen element matches) in the document and every open and closed shadow root. It keeps the one on top: the innermost one holding focus (a modal nested in another leaves the outer one's controls inert), else the one shown last. When the show order never saw one of them (a `show-modal` command) and focus doesn't decide, it picks none, so the tree stays as it is on main rather than drop the live dialog. - The walk skips everything outside that dialog's flat tree: the page, a lower modal, a popover opened outside it, an iframe (whose document is then never entered). The dialog's ancestors are walked but not listed, so light children slotted into a shadow-root dialog stay (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`). - A context init script numbers each opening of a dialog `showModal()` has shown, a `show-modal` command reopening it included (`packages/web/src/modal-dialogs.ts`, through the dialog's `beforetoggle`), since tree order picks the wrong dialog when a later one was shown first. Focus is checked before it, which also covers a dialog opened without calling `showModal()`, such as by an invoker command. - Locators and `toBeVisible` don't change: they follow Playwright, which matches inert content too. ## Issue Fixes #1782 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The repro from the issue ([`modal-inert`](https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/modal-inert): a scripted executor taps the node the tree names, no model), with the built CLI on main `b56e8ed5` and on this branch: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | tree with the modal open | `main`, `heading "Store"`, `button "Add to cart"`, `status "idle"`, then `dialog "Cookie consent"` | `dialog "Cookie consent"`, its text, `button "Accept"` | | agent taps "Add to cart" | offered; fails after 14.87s, ` intercepts pointer events` | not offered (0.1s), like the `inert` section's button | | agent taps "Accept", then "Add to cart" | passes | passes | - Crosscheck: seven new fixture pages (a modal over the page with an iframe and a later popover; two modals shown in reverse tree order, then the lower one shown again, focus blurred; a modal nested in a modal; a modal in a closed shadow root with a slotted button; a modal slotted into a shadow root; two modals where a `show-modal` command opened one, focus blurred; a modal a command reopens after another was shown, focus blurred). With main's reader the five pages without a command give 17 disagreements with Chrome; with this branch, none, and the page a command reopens matches Chrome too. The page whose dialog only a command opened keeps the page, as main does: its 4 lines are in `expected.txt` with the reason. Without the init script, the reverse-order page fails again. The crosscheck over every web-benchmark scenario passes too. - Tree capture on a page of 2,100 elements and 100 shadow roots, median of 25 alternating runs: with no modal, 84.7ms on main and 85.3ms here; with a modal open, 85.8ms and 477 KB of tree on main, 10.2ms and 640 B here. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: test(run): run two serial groups through the scheduler at once
test(benchmark): check every scenario has its test
body:
## What and why

Both benchmark READMEs promise their scenarios are tested: `apps/web-benchmark/README.md` says every catalog scenario gets a deterministic twin at `tests/<slug>.e2e.ts`, and `apps/mobile-benchmark/README.md` says every scenario gets one `agent.act` entry. Nothing checked either promise, so a scenario added to a catalog could ship untested with both suites green. `file-round-trip` did exactly that: the only web slug without a twin, and it never had one.

- New `scripts/check-benchmark-coverage.ts`, wired into `pnpm check` beside the other `check-*` scripts and given its own step in `spec.yml`'s check job, fails listing every gap: a web catalog slug with no `tests/<slug>.e2e.ts`, and a mobile catalog name with no entry in `tests-agent/scenarios.e2e.ts` outside the documented `Control Inventory` exclusion.
- The parsing and comparison live in `scripts/benchmark-coverage.ts` as functions (`webSlugs`, `mobileNames`, `unreadableWebSlugs`, `webProblems`, `mobileProblems`), with `node --test` coverage in `scripts/benchmark-coverage.test.ts`, so the rules sit beside the other check helpers rather than inside the program.
- Both catalogs parse in either quote style. A catalog that parses to no scenarios fails the check, as does a `slug:` the parser cannot read (a template literal, a bare identifier), so a reformatted entry can no longer hide a scenario. `declaresName` reads uncommented `name:` properties, so a commented-out entry is a gap rather than an entry.
- `apps/web-benchmark/tests/file-round-trip.e2e.ts` is the missing twin: it opens the page in `test.beforeEach`, downloads the issued voucher, checks the suggested filename and the `VOUCHER:WEB-5521` content, uploads the same file back through `setInputFiles`, and separately proves a file that is not the voucher is rejected, that the input resets, and that the issued voucher then verifies.
- The web agentic side is not checked here. That suite is intentionally partial, and covering it (a declared `gap` per scenario, plus an exclusion list the check reads) is the remaining part of #1777, so this PR references the issue instead of closing it.

The check's output on a green tree:

```text
benchmark coverage: 42 web scenarios and 25 mobile scenarios have their tests
```

Remove the twin and it fails with the gap it exists to catch:

```text
web: file-round-trip has no tests/file-round-trip.e2e.ts; the README promises every scenario a deterministic twin
```

## Issue

Refs #1777

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Red and green proven both ways: without `tests/file-round-trip.e2e.ts` the check exits 1 with the message above; with it, exit 0.
- Each stricter guard was proven by mutation, then restored: a `slug:` turned into a template literal exits 1 with `web: the catalog declares a slug this check cannot read: `login-form`; write it as a quoted slug, such as slug: "name"`; commenting out a real `name: 'Login Form',` in the mobile suite exits 1 with `mobile: Login Form has no entry in tests-agent/scenarios.e2e.ts`; both restored, exit 0 with `42 web scenarios and 25 mobile scenarios have their tests`.
- The twin's reset assertion was proven by mutation in both directions against the built app: with `uploadInputRef.current.value = ""` removed from `FileRoundTrip.tsx`, the rejecting test fails `ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveValue failed` while the download test passes; with the reset in place, `e2e run tests/file-round-trip.e2e.ts` passes 2/2.
- `node --test scripts/benchmark-coverage.test.ts`: 12 passed, 0 failed. `tsc -p scripts`: exit 0. `oxlint` on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web-benchmark run typecheck`: exit 0.
- Rebased onto `3761bb9b` (`build` keeps upstream's `@e2e-dev/notte` step, `check` keeps `check:benchmark-coverage`; `AGENTS.md`'s chain matches `package.json` step for step).

title: test(explore): pin the finding fields the schema test left unbounded
body: ## What and why `ExploreState` clips every free text it stores so the report the runner writes always validates against `schema/report-v1.schema.json`, and the unit test `snapshots a schema-valid explore block with bounded text` (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/explore-state.test.ts:102`) holds that line: it overflows the inputs, validates the snapshot with ajv, and pins the exact lengths the clip produces. Four of the finding's fields slipped past it, as noted on the issue: `expected` and `actual` were never overflowed, `path` was never overflowed, and the reproduction entries were checked for count (20) but never for their 500-character length, so a clip that stopped bounding any of them would still leave the test green while ajv only catches it if the value also exceeds the schema. - The existing test now feeds `expected`, `actual`, and `path` values longer than their ceilings (2,000, 2,000, and 2,048 characters) and pins each clipped length. - The reproduction assertion now pins the per-entry ceiling too: 30 entries of 900 characters come back as 20 entries of exactly 500. - The test stays a single snapshot case with hardcoded pins beside the ajv validation, the shape the issue asked to keep, so the schema and the clip are checked from two directions: ajv catches a value that exceeds the schema, the pins catch a clip that no longer matches it. The additions in place: ```ts finding(state, { title: 't'.repeat(300), expected: 'e'.repeat(2_500), actual: 'a'.repeat(2_500), path: 'p'.repeat(2_500), reproduction: Array.from({ length: 30 }, () => 'r'.repeat(900)), }); // ... expect(snapshot.findings[0]!.expected).toHaveLength(2_000); expect(snapshot.findings[0]!.actual).toHaveLength(2_000); expect(snapshot.findings[0]!.path).toHaveLength(2_048); expect(snapshot.findings[0]!.reproduction).toHaveLength(20); expect(snapshot.findings[0]!.reproduction.every((entry) => entry.length === 500)).toBe(true); ``` The numbers match the schema today (`exploreFinding.expected` 2000, `actual` 2000, `path` 2048, `reproduction` 20 items of 500), so a one-sided edit to either side now fails this test instead of surfacing as a rejected report at run time. ## Issue Fixes #1778 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/explore-state.test.ts`: 10 passed, 0 failed, the extended case among them. - `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/e2e`: exit 0. `oxlint` on the file: 0 warnings, 0 errors. - The pins were checked against `schema/report-v1.schema.json` directly while writing them (each `expect(...).toHaveLength` value is the schema's `maxLength` or `items.maxLength` for that field), and the ajv validation inside the test still runs on the same snapshot.

title: feat(html-reporter): filter a run's results by target
body:
## What and why

The HTML report already tags every result with its `targetId` and hides the tag unless a run selected more than one target, but there was no way to look at one target alone. On a multi-target run the list interleaves web and mobile results (and the status counts mix them), so reading "the mobile side of this run" meant eyeballing tags row by row.

- `app/data.ts` gains `onTarget(results, target)`, the same shape as the existing `byStatus` and `matchesSearch` helpers: it passes the list through untouched when no target is chosen and otherwise keeps only the results of the chosen target. Everything downstream (status counts, the file tree, the search) runs through it, so the tabs, the counts, and the list always agree.
- When a run selected more than one target, `app/list.tsx` renders a target nav above the status tabs: `all targets`, then each target with its own count. Selecting one writes `target` into the hash route (`#?target=mobile`), so the filtered view survives a reload and works as a link; `all targets` clears it.
- The header follows it (`RunHeader`): with a target picked the headline reads `tests on <target>` instead of the run's verdict, the counts narrow to that target, and the run-wide facts (started, duration, tokens, cost, version) follow a `run totals:` label so none of them reads as the target's own. Without a target the headline and facts are unchanged.
- `docs/reference/reporters.mdx` now describes the tabs where the page's list behavior is documented.

The helper:

```ts
export function onTarget(results: readonly Result[], target: string | undefined): readonly Result[] {
  return target === undefined ? results : results.filter((result) => result.targetId === target);
}
```

The nav is conditional markup, not a new route:

```tsx
{targets.length > 1 ? (
  <nav aria-label="Target" className="flex flex-wrap gap-x-e2e-4 gap-y-e2e-2">
    {/* "all targets" plus each target with its count, each an href through routeHref */}
  </nav>
) : null}
```

Before and after on the same two-target payload (a synthetic `web` + `mobile` run built from the report fixture):

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target nav | none | `all targets 7`, `web 4`, `mobile 3` |
| pick `mobile` | not possible | hash `#?target=mobile`, status counts `all 3`, one file section left |
| headline on `mobile` | not possible | `tests on mobile` instead of the run's verdict |
| facts on `mobile` | both targets always | the target first, then `run totals:` before the run-wide ones |
| `#?target=web` on a one-target run | unfiltered | unfiltered: `selectedTarget` ignores a choice no tab could clear |

## Issue

None (feat change, exempt per CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/html-reporter run test:unit`: 18 passed, including the `onTarget` cases (passthrough on `undefined`, filter by `targetId`, unknown target to empty list), the `selectedTarget` cases (a carried target on a multi-target run; none for an unknown target, no value, or any target on a single-target run), and the `statusTabs` cases (statuses with results in tab order; the active tab kept at 0).
- The package builds on this branch: `vite build`, `tsc --project tsconfig.build.json`, and `stamp-dist` all exit 0; `tsc --noEmit` passes for both configs.
- The built page was opened in headless Chromium against a two-target payload derived from `schema/fixtures/report-v1.valid.json` (a `mobile` target and a duplicate of each selected result, with the one mobile failure forced to passed so a target with no failures exists). On main's build the page renders no target nav; on this branch it renders `all targets 7 | web 4 | mobile 3`, and `#?status=failed&target=mobile` keeps the `failed 0` tab active instead of hiding it. On `#?target=mobile` the headline reads `tests on mobile` and the facts line reads `mobile (mobile) · run totals: · 7/24/2026, 7:00:00 PM · 1.0s · e2e 0.1.0`, with no target tag left on the rows; on `#?target=tablet` the headline and facts stay the unfiltered ones. Against a single-target payload, `#?target=web` renders exactly the unfiltered view: `tests failed`, no `run totals:`, no nav, all rows. The screenshots stayed local (this machine's `gh` is 2.91 and `--attach` needs 2.99), so the DOM numbers above are the record.
- `oxlint` on the changed files and the docs checks (`check-docs-mdx`, `check-docs-anchors`, `check-docs-package-managers`, `check-docs-logos`): exit 0.
- Rebased onto `3761bb9b` with no conflicts; upstream touched only `packages/html-reporter/package.json` in the meantime, so the DOM evidence above stands.

title: feat(decision): score unjudged tests with a configurable unjudgedRelevance
body: ## What and why `decisionFilter()` scores every test it is handed so the run starts the likeliest files first: 1 when the change touches the test, the model's probability when it judged, and 0.5 when it did not. That 0.5 was a hardcoded constant (`UNJUDGED_RELEVANCE` in `packages/decision/src/filter.ts:16`), which forces a fixed policy on every project. A repo whose unjudged tests are known-expensive wants them started early; a repo that trusts the model's answers wants the unjudged parked behind everything it did judge. The middle belongs to neither camp by default. - `DecisionFilterOptions` gains `unjudgedRelevance?: number`, from 0 to 1, defaulting to the current 0.5, so behavior is unchanged for everyone who does not set it. - `decisionFilter()` validates it at config load: outside 0 to 1, or not a number, fails as `INVALID_CONFIG` naming the option, the same failure mode the factory already uses for a bad `model` or `providerOptions`. - The resolved value threads through both scoring paths: `unaskedRelevance` (the scores handed out before or without asking, touched 1, everything else the option) and `verdicts` (where a missing answer for a test or its setup counts as the option before the two sides are maxed). A throw from git or a file read carries the same scores through the catch path. ```ts const unjudged = options.unjudgedRelevance ?? UNJUDGED_RELEVANCE; // ... function checkUnjudgedRelevance(value: number | undefined): void { if (value === undefined) return; if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0 || value > 1) { throw new ConfigurationError( 'INVALID_CONFIG', `decisionFilter({ unjudgedRelevance }) must be a number from 0 to 1; got ${String(value)}`, ); } } ``` Usage: ```ts filters: [decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev'), unjudgedRelevance: 0.1 })], ``` `docs/filters.mdx` documents the option where the score table explains what a missing rating counts as, and the changeset carries the `@e2e-dev/decision` patch. ## Issue None (feat change, exempt per CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/decision exec vitest run tests/filter.test.ts` with the local git-fixture environment workaround this box needs (`os.devNull` points git at an unreadable device path here): 55 passed, 1 failed, the failure the pre-existing one whose fixture filename contains a newline (NTFS refuses such a name; it fails on clean main the same way). - The whole package suite was compared against clean main rather than trusted as absolute counts: main 215 passed / 3 failed, this branch 219 passed / 3 failed, the failing set identical test for test (the two extra local failures are the same Windows-only Ctrl-C and newline-filename cases both ways), and the 4 new tests are the delta. - Two new scoring tests cover both paths: the model-did-not-judge test scores its missed test with the option instead of 0.5, and the lockfile test (no call at all) scores the unasked tests with it while the touched one stays 1. Two new config-refusal cases pin `1.5` and `NaN` to `INVALID_CONFIG` with the option's message. - `tsc --noEmit` (covers `tests/**`): exit 0. `oxlint` on the three changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Docs checks (`check-docs-mdx`, `check-docs-anchors`, `check-docs-package-managers`, `check-docs-logos`): exit 0, and `check-error-codes` reports all 92 codes documented. `check-changeset-bumps`: 3 pending changesets, none an unannounced 0.x minor or major. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. title: Ctrl-C skips afterEach when timeout + cleanupTimeout overflows
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of samanyudas**

Ctrl-C kills a busy worker about 1 ms after the signal when `timeout + cleanupTimeout` is more than 2^31-1 ms.
`afterEach` does not run, the engine is not disposed, and the report says the test was skipped before it ran.

## Reproduce

Config: `timeout: 2_147_483_647` (the largest value `timerMs` accepts), `cleanupTimeout: 30_000`, `workers: 1`, a fake engine that logs `init` and `dispose`, and one test that sleeps behind an `afterEach` that logs `afterEach.start` and `afterEach.end`.
Send SIGINT to the process group of `e2e run` after the body starts.

| Budgets | Logged events | Report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timeout: 60_000`, `cleanupTimeout: 5_000` | `init`, `test.start`, `afterEach.start`, `afterEach.end`, `dispose` | 1 interrupted |
| `timeout: 2_147_483_647`, `cleanupTimeout: 30_000` | `init`, `test.start` | 1 skipped, "run interrupted before execution" |

The second run also prints:

```
TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2147513647 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer.
```

Observed on `main` at b56e8ed5 with the built CLI on Linux.

## Cause

`config/resolve.ts` checks `timeout` and `cleanupTimeout` against `MAX_TIMER_MS` separately.
`run/runner.ts` passes their sum as `interruptGraceMs`, and `SchedulerWorker.killAfter` in `run/scheduler.ts` gives it straight to `setTimeout`.
Node runs a delay above 2^31-1 after 1 ms, so the kill timer fires right after the interrupt.
`forceGraceMs` (`cleanupTimeout + 1_000`) reaches the same timer and overflows when `cleanupTimeout` is within 1 s of the limit.

## Fix direction

Clamp the delay to `MAX_TIMER_MS` in `killAfter`, the one place both grace values reach `setTimeout`.

title: fix(core): cap the worker kill delay at the timer limit
body:
- `timeout` and `cleanupTimeout` are each checked against `MAX_TIMER_MS` (2^31-1 ms), but the scheduler's kill timer gets sums of them: `interruptGraceMs: config.timeout + config.cleanupTimeout` and `forceGraceMs: config.cleanupTimeout + FORCE_KILL_MARGIN_MS` in `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`.
- Node runs a `setTimeout` delay above 2^31-1 after 1 ms. Two cases broke:
  - `timeout` near the limit: Ctrl-C killed the busy worker right away. `afterEach` and engine disposal did not run, and the report called the test "run interrupted before execution".
  - `cleanupTimeout` near the limit: the end of every run killed each worker before engine disposal finished. The run still exited 0, so nothing showed it. A second Ctrl-C did the same.
- `SchedulerWorker.killAfter` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts`) is the one place both grace values reach `setTimeout`. It now caps the delay at `MAX_TIMER_MS`:

```ts
this.killTimer = setTimeout(() => {
  this.killed = true;
  this.runner.kill();
}, Math.min(graceMs, MAX_TIMER_MS));
```

- Tests, committed before the fix and failing on main:
  - `packages/e2e/tests/integration/interrupt-signals.test.ts`: one Ctrl-C with `timeout: 2_147_483_647` runs `afterEach`, disposes the engine, exits 130, and prints no `TimeoutOverflowWarning`.
  - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/scheduler.test.ts`: with `forceGraceMs: 2 ** 31`, a retired worker finishes a 12 s disposal without being killed. Vitest's fake timers copy Node's overflow rule, so this fails on main with `fleet.killed` equal to `[0]`.

## Issue

Fixes #1798

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Built CLI on a scratch project with a file-logging fake engine. For the Ctrl-C cases, a test sleeps behind an `afterEach` and SIGINT goes to the `e2e run` process group once the body starts. For the end-of-run case, one test passes and the engine's `dispose` takes 300 ms.
- The new integration test failed on main (events stopped at `test.start`) and passes here, along with the rest of `interrupt-signals.test.ts`.

One Ctrl-C, `timeout: 2147483647`, `cleanupTimeout: 30000`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `init`, `test.start` | `init`, `test.start`, `afterEach.start`, `afterEach.end`, `dispose` |
| `TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2147513647 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer.` | no warning |
| `1 skipped` ("run interrupted before execution") | `1 interrupted` |

A passing run with no signal, `timeout: 60000`, `cleanupTimeout: 2147483647`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `init`, `dispose` (no `dispose.end`), exit 0 | `init`, `dispose`, `dispose.end`, exit 0 |
| `TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2147484647 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer.` | no warning |

Two Ctrl-Cs with a hanging `afterEach`, `timeout: 60000`, `cleanupTimeout: 2147483647`:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `init`, `test.start`. The first Ctrl-C already killed the worker. | `init`, `test.start`, `afterEach.start`, `dispose` |

```text
=== fixed: timeout=2147483647 cleanup=30000
exit=130
--- signal.log
init
test.start
afterEach.start
afterEach.end
dispose
--- run.out (tail)
 ❯ |fake| tests/sleep.e2e.ts (1 test | 1 interrupted) 597ms

```

title: Performance: avoid repeatedly copying Markdown result groups
body:
_[gpt-6] responding on behalf of jxnxts_

## Problem

At main `b56e8ed52539eab09a08af7b76ef34d0328936ea`, [`fileGroups`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/b56e8ed52539eab09a08af7b76ef34d0328936ea/packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts#L414-L423) spreads the prior bucket array for each result. A file bucket of K results recopies K(K−1)/2 prior references, before the displayed-test cap applies.

Extracted-function measurement on Node 24.22.2 / M3 Pro: 10,000 entries in one file take median 32.7984 ms baseline versus 0.1554 ms with a fresh local array and push; 1,000 entries across 100 files take 0.3097 versus 0.2184 ms. These are local grouping CPU measurements, not full-renderer or suite improvements.

## Proposed API

None. Initialize an array once per local target/file bucket and append entries; preserve the existing comparator and all rendering behavior.

## Which surface

Markdown reporter internals, used by summary.md and the GitHub reporter. Distinct from closed #1467, which concerned serial-member lookup.

## Compatibility and verification

Preserve original entry objects, input immutability, target/file grouping and exact output order. Extracted equality passes on measured inputs and 100 generated frozen-input cases; implementation must additionally compare full built-renderer output and existing goldens and satisfy the repository verification/performance workflow. No public contract or report schema change.

I plan to work on the narrow internal change above, with repository tests and built-module verification before opening a PR. No public API change is proposed. Measurements above are extracted-function experiments, not an implemented or end-to-end improvement.

title: Mobile benchmark: device.openLink has no test on a real device
body:
### Problem

`device.openLink` is only covered by fake-client unit tests (`packages/mobile/tests/unit/links.test.ts`). No benchmark test opens a link on a simulator or emulator. The mobile benchmark declares the `e2e-benchmark` scheme in `app.json`, but the app doesn't handle it, so a link opens the app and stays on whatever screen it was on.

### Proposed API

No API change. In `apps/mobile-benchmark`:

```ts
await device.openLink('e2e-benchmark://login-form');
await expect(screen.getByTestId('email-input')).toBeVisible();
```

### Upsides

`openLink` gets a real run on iOS and Android in the existing `mobile` CI jobs, so a regression in agent-device's `open <url>` path or in the engine's foreground-app tracking after a link shows up.

### Downsides

`App.tsx` drifts a little from the upstream benchmark app. The iOS 26 simulator sometimes shows an "Open in “e2e Benchmark”?" prompt before handing a custom-scheme link to the app (I saw it on a freshly booted simulator), so the test has to tap Open when it shows.

### Alternatives

Keep only the unit tests, which never reach a device.

### Which surface

Mobile benchmark (tests only).

Happy to send the PR; I have it working locally on an iOS 26.3 simulator and an Android 16 emulator.

title: Workers race on the OAuth refresh
body:
### What happened

Parallel workers each refresh the same expired subscription login (`e2e/oauth/chatgpt`, `copilot`, `grok`, `opencode-console`).
They all send the same refresh token to the vendor at the same moment.
Vendors that rotate refresh tokens accept the first request and reject the others.

`createOAuthFetch` (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/fetch.ts`) lets only one refresh run at a time, but it does that only inside one process.
`e2e run` starts each worker as its own child process, so that check never sees the other workers.
`FileCredentialStore` locks `oauth.json` only for the write, not for the read, refresh, and write together.

A worker whose refresh is rejected polls the file for 2 s (`ROTATION_ATTEMPTS` × `ROTATION_WAIT_MS`) and then fails.
That recovers only when the winning refresh finishes inside that window, and only when the vendor does not revoke the token family on reuse.

### Reproduction

The repro runs the real `chatgpt()` model from 4 workers against a fake `auth.openai.com` and `chatgpt.com`.
The fake rotates refresh tokens and answers a reused one with `400 refresh_token_reused`.
The stored login is expired when the run starts.
Each test file does `generateText({ model: chatgpt('gpt-test'), prompt: 'hi' })`.

Observed on `main` at 2030b175, `npx e2e run --workers 4`:

| Vendor behavior | Refresh requests for `rt-0` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refresh answers in 400 ms | 4 (3 rejected) | 4 passed, after the 2 s poll |
| Refresh answers in 2.5 s | 4 (3 rejected) | 3 of 4 failed: `ChatGPT token request failed (400: refresh_token_reused); run \`npx e2e login openai\`` |
| Reuse revokes the token family | 4 (3 rejected) | 4 of 4 failed, and the stored login can no longer refresh |

Vendor log for the 2.5 s case:

```
07.919 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
07.943 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
07.950 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
10.361 refresh rt-0 -> 200 at-1 rt-1
10.373 responses at-1 -> 200
```

I did not confirm whether OpenAI or xAI revoke the token family on reuse.
The third row models the reuse detection that the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP recommends.

### Expected

One refresh per login per run, however many workers there are.
Every other worker uses the tokens that refresh stored.

### Which surface

`e2e/oauth/*` model constructors, under `e2e run --workers N`.

title: fix(oauth): refresh a login once across worker processes
body:
## Issue

Fixes #1807

## What changed

- `e2e run` starts each worker as its own process, but `createOAuthFetch` shared a refresh only inside one process. With `--workers 4` and an expired subscription login, four workers sent the same refresh token. ChatGPT, SuperGrok, and OpenCode Console rotate refresh tokens, so they rejected all but one.
- `FileCredentialStore.exclusive(providerId, refresh)` holds a lock file per login, `oauth.json.<provider>.refresh.lock`, across the refresh's re-read of the store, its token request, and its write (`packages/e2e/src/oauth/store.ts`). A worker that waited for the lock re-reads the store, finds the fresh tokens, and sends no refresh.
- The lock is `withFileLock()` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/file-lock.ts`. The store's existing write lock uses it too.
- The lock file names its holder: host and pid namespace, pid, and a random token. The holder touches the file every 2.5 s while it holds the lock, and touches and removes only a lock that holds its own token.
- A waiter takes the lock over in two cases:
  - at once, when the holder's pid on this host and pid namespace has exited
  - once the lock has gone untouched for 10 s, whoever it names
- The 10 s bound covers locks the pid cannot vouch for: another host's or sandbox's, an empty lock from an older e2e, and a pid another program now has. Waiters take turns through a `.break` file to remove a lock and check the holder again on their turn, so a lock created after the first check is never removed.
- A waiter gives the lock 30 s, then fails with `OAuthError('TIMEOUT')`. The holder's token request has no deadline: the vendor may rotate the token before a late answer, and dropping that answer would leave the stored token revoked.
- The 2 s poll for a token another process rotated (`rotatedElsewhere` in `packages/e2e/src/oauth/fetch.ts`) stays, and now runs after the lock is released. An e2e released before this change refreshes without the lock, so a run of it beside a run of this one still needs the poll.
- `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` is unchanged. That store cannot save anything, so each process still refreshes on its own, as `docs/subscriptions.mdx` already says.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W1 as worker 1
  participant W2 as worker 2..4
  participant L as oauth.json.openai.refresh.lock
  participant V as vendor
  W1->>L: create, holder named
  W2->>L: wait (holder runs, lock touched)
  W1->>V: refresh rt-0
  V-->>W1: at-1, rt-1
  W1->>L: write oauth.json, release
  W2->>L: take, re-read oauth.json
  Note over W2: at-1 is fresh, no refresh sent
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Scratch project with test files that each call `generateText({ model: chatgpt('gpt-test') })` through the real `e2e/oauth/chatgpt` constructor, run with `npx e2e run --workers 4 --no-cache`. A fake `auth.openai.com` and `chatgpt.com` rotates refresh tokens and answers a reused one with `400 refresh_token_reused`. The stored login starts expired.
- The main column ran at `2030b175`, the merge base before main was merged in, built in its own worktree. Branch rows ran at `6e07fa71` or later. The rows marked `4b1bf6d3` ran again at the head, after merging main, and the row marked `4747e779` just before it.

| Vendor behavior | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refresh answers in 400 ms | 4 passed, 4 refreshes of `rt-0` (3 rejected) | 4 passed, 1 refresh |
| Refresh answers in 2.5 s (`4b1bf6d3`) | 3 of 4 failed: `ChatGPT token request failed (400: refresh_token_reused); run \`npx e2e login openai\`` | 4 passed, 1 refresh |
| Reuse revokes the token family (`4b1bf6d3`) | 4 of 4 failed, stored login dead | 4 passed, 1 refresh |
| Refresh answers in 12 s | same failure as the 2.5 s row | 4 passed, 1 refresh |
| Refresh answers in 25 s (`5d95a6ed`) | same failure as the 2.5 s row | 4 passed, 1 refresh, the new token stored |
| First token request never answers (`5d95a6ed`) | 3 passed, 1 `TEST_TIMEOUT` after 120 s | 0 passed: the holder hit `TEST_TIMEOUT`, and 3 waiters failed after 30 s with `another e2e process is still refreshing the openai login after 30 s; run again once it finishes` |
| Revoked login, 8 workers | 8 `LOGIN_REQUIRED`, 6.0 s | 8 `LOGIN_REQUIRED`, 5.8 s |
| Lock left by an exited worker (`4747e779`) | not applicable | 4 passed, 1 refresh |
| Empty lock 60 s old, as an older e2e leaves it | not applicable | 4 passed, 1 refresh, about 10 s |
| Lock naming live pid 1, untouched for 1 hour | not applicable | 4 passed, 1 refresh, 4 s |
| A main run and a branch run at once, 2 workers each, the branch run starting 0.2 s later | 4 passed (main beside main) | 4 passed. Without the kept poll, the branch run failed in 5 of 6 trials |

Vendor log, 2.5 s case, main:

```text
07.919 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
07.943 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
07.950 refresh rt-0 -> 400 refresh_token_reused
10.361 refresh rt-0 -> 200 at-1 rt-1
10.373 responses at-1 -> 200
```

Same case, this branch:

```text
04.184 refresh rt-0 -> 200 at-1 rt-1
04.197 responses at-1 -> 200
04.232 responses at-1 -> 200
04.234 responses at-1 -> 200
04.242 responses at-1 -> 200
```

Process-level checks of the lock at `0be69e58`, outside the CLI. The lock's logic has not changed since, only its module and how it writes the holder token:

- 16 processes started in the same millisecond on an orphaned lock: one holder at a time in 10 of 10 trials.
- A caller inside a `bwrap --unshare-pid` sandbox waited for a holder outside it: the log reads `+holder -holder +caller -caller`. Before the pid namespace was part of the holder's name, the caller entered while the holder held the lock.
- A holder stopped with `kill -STOP` for 11 s mid-refresh lost its lock to the next waiter: `+A +B -B -A`. That is the accepted cost of the 10 s bound, below.

Tests: `file-lock.test.ts` covers the lock, and `store.test.ts` and `fetch.test.ts` cover the store and the refresh. `passes on any other refresh failure as it is` passes on the merge base too: it pins main's behavior through the restructured refresh.

Each race mutation below was checked against the test meant to catch it. Every cell is 10 runs, on this 8-CPU Linux machine:

| Mutation | Test | All CPUs | Pinned to 1 CPU | 2 CPUs under load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Takeover turn removed (no `.break` file) | `lets one waiter through a crashed holder's lock when another takes it over during the check in its takeover turn` | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Re-check in the turn removed | both `lets one waiter through a crashed holder's lock` cases | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Re-read inside the refresh lock removed | `uses the token another process stored while this one waited for the lock, sending no refresh` | 10/10 | 10/10 | not run |

The two-waiter tests start a second real waiter inside the first one's pid check, so the race happens on every run. With the pid namespace dropped from the holder's name, `names its host, pid namespace, and pid in the lock` fails. The crash-loop test (12 processes, half the holds ending like a crash, until 300 crashes) is a soak check on real processes. With the turn removed it failed 15 of 15 runs on all CPUs, 8 of 8 on 1 CPU, and 6 of 8 on 2 CPUs under load. Unmutated, it passed 31 of 31.

The testbed and benchmarks were not run: none of their configs uses a subscription login, so this change does not reach them.

## For maintainers

- The lock is hand-written, about 170 lines in `src/internal/file-lock.ts`: holder token, pid and pid-namespace check, heartbeat, and the `.break` turn. No lock helper exists in the repo. `proper-lockfile` uses the same heartbeat-and-stale design and would replace most of it, at the cost of a dependency.
- A holder paused for more than 10 s mid-refresh (a debugger, laptop sleep) loses its lock, and a second refresh can go out. Judging only by pid would keep its lock, but then a pid another program has since been given would block every run until someone removes the file. I chose the heartbeat bound.
- A token request that never answers now fails the other workers of that run after 30 s, where on main they each refreshed on their own. A deadline on the request would let the next worker refresh, but it also drops an answer that arrives late after the vendor rotated the token, and that revokes the stored login. I chose to lose a run rather than the login.
  - With retries on, a retried holder joins the same hung request, so its test times out twice.
  - The run leaves the lock file behind. The next run takes it over at once, because the pid it names has exited.
- The stale bound is 10 s. A loaded CI machine that pauses a holder longer loses its lock. 20 to 25 s would still sit under the 30 s wait.
- On Windows, `claim()` may get `EPERM` from a lock file that another process is deleting, and that fails the refresh. I have not run this on Windows. A retry on `EPERM` would cover it.
- A judgment step (`assert`, `waitFor`, `extract`) has a 30 s default budget, the same as the lock wait. Such a step waiting on another worker's refresh ends with `STEP_TIMEOUT` rather than the lock's `TIMEOUT`. The docs say so.

title: fix(cache): --strict-cache gives a false REPLAY_STALE for test ids over 300 characters
fix(cache): tell long-id steps apart under --strict-cache with an identity digest
body:
- Under `--strict-cache`, a step whose key misses is checked for a recording of the same step under another key (`packages/core/src/cache/rekeyed.ts`). - That check compares provenance as an entry stores it, and `recordedProvenance` cuts `testId`, `targetId`, and `agent` to 300 characters (`packages/core/src/cache/recorder.ts`). - Two ids that differ only after character 299 cut to the same string, so a never-recorded test matched another test's recording and failed with a false `REPLAY_STALE`. - Now `recordedProvenance` also writes an optional `identityDigest` (SHA-256 of the whole redacted test id, target id, and agent name) when `bound` would make one of them ambiguous. That is when it cuts the name, or when the whole name already ends like a cut (`…` at 299 or 300 characters, which a `createAgent` cache key can). ''].some((text) => boundIsAmbiguous(text, MAX_TRACE_DESCRIPTOR_CHARS)); // ... ...(ambiguous ? { identityDigest: sha256Hex(JSON.stringify([testId, targetId, agent ?? null])) } : {}), ``` ## Issue Fixes #1809 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Built CLI at `e6a69cfa` against a scratch web project (later commits change only comments, docs, and tests): two tests under a 342-character describe title, each running `agent.act('increment the counter')` with a scripted model. `Cache 1 replayed · 1 missed`

Main and this branch write the same key file in the same project (`3b488c9e….json`). - After changing the agent's `context`, `--strict-cache` on the first test fails with `REPLAY_STALE ... since the agent's context (its context, or the test's agentContext) changed after it was recorded`. A long-id step whose key really changed is still caught. - A short-id entry carries no `identityDigest`. - The same project with the describe title `checkout flow` passes 2 of 2 on main, so the id length is the trigger. - Mutations each fail the new tests: - the digest left out of `stepKey`, `>` changed to `>=`, only `testId` checked, the `…` case dropped, `>= maxChars - 1` changed to `>= maxChars` - the digest over unredacted names, the length measured on unredacted names, the target or agent name not redacted - the digest dropped on read, the `typeof` check on a read digest dropped, the `paramsDigest` check dropped - no backfill, a backfill on every replay (`recordedFor.identityDigest === undefined`, which kdy1 tried), a backfill that never replaces or drops a stored digest - The no-rewrite test counts the store's writes, since a rewrite in the same millisecond keeps the same bytes. - `pnpm check` passes. `e2e` unit tests: 3974 passed, 2 skipped, on the branch with main merged in. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Adds MyTimetable to e2e.com/examples as a community example.
MyTimetable is the Adelaide University CS Club's drag-and-drop timetable planner (Vite, React, HeroUI).

title: Agent: no-input tools reject extra fields, and some models loop on the error
body:
### Problem

`schemaTool` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/primitives.ts` closes every agent tool schema, so a field the tool doesn't declare fails validation and the error goes back to the model as the call's result. For tools with parameters that's the right call. For tools whose input is `z.object({})` (`observe`, `back`, `dismiss_keyboard`, and `screenshot` without `saveScreenshot`) it backfires with some open-weight models.

Running `agent.act` steps on `@e2e-dev/mobile` (Android emulator) with Qwen served by vLLM through `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, the model regularly adds arguments to these tools, e.g. `screenshot({"description": "check the home screen"})`. The call fails validation, the model reads the error, sends the same call again, and the step loops until it runs out of steps.

Today we work around it with a `wrapLanguageModel` middleware in our config that rewrites the input to `{}` for any tool whose schema declares no properties. With it, the same tests pass.

Versions: e2e 0.23.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.6, ai 7.0.168, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible 3.0.89. The same `schemaTool` is on `main` (cfa2aa0).

### Proposed API

```ts
// No new API. Only tools that declare no fields stop being strict.
function schemaTool<Schema extends z.ZodObject, Output = string>(definition: { /* unchanged */ }): Tool {
  // A tool that reads no fields has nothing a stray key could have meant,
  // so drop unknown keys there (zod's default) instead of failing the call.
  const noInput = Object.keys(definition.inputSchema.shape).length === 0;
  return { ...definition, inputSchema: noInput ? definition.inputSchema : definition.inputSchema.strict() } as Tool;
}
```

### Upsides

- Models that pad tool calls with extra fields (Qwen on vLLM here) can run agent steps without a custom middleware in every user's config.
- Nothing is lost: a no-input tool ignores its input, so the stray keys never changed what the call did.
- Tools with parameters stay strict, so a stray field that may signal a misunderstood intent still goes back to the model.

### Downsides

- Two behaviours depending on schema shape, which is a little surprising and needs a line in the docs.
- A model sending junk to a no-input tool is no longer corrected, so that confusion goes unnoticed unless it's logged (could show in `--debug` or `--ai-trace`).
- A tool that gains its first field later (as `screenshot` does with `saveScreenshot`) becomes strict again, so a model that pads calls fails there.

### Alternatives

- A middleware in the user's config (what we do today): works, but every user of such a model has to find the cause and write it.
- A config switch to turn strict tool input off everywhere: broader than needed, and loosens tools where strictness is useful.

Happy to send the PR, with tests, if the approach works for you.

### Which surface

_No response_

### Compatibility

- [ ] This changes or removes something that exists today (see the stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: Feature request: fail a test when the app throws (appLog.failOn)
body:
### Problem

A test can pass while the app throws. The web engine already records each attempt's uncaught exceptions, console output, failed requests, and 4xx/5xx responses (`AppLogEntry`, sources `error`, `console`, `network`), and the trace page lists them under "App log" with their step. Nothing in a test can act on them, though, so a click handler that throws `TypeError` passes as long as the screen looks right.

The migration guides list this as Planned for three runners: Playwright's `page.on('pageerror')` and `page.on('console')`, Cypress's `uncaught:exception` ("An app error doesn't fail a test"), and Selenium's `manage().logs()`. Today's workaround is a `browser.addInitScript` that collects `window.onerror`, plus a `browser.evaluate` assertion in `afterEach`: web-only boilerplate in every project.

### Proposed API

```ts
// e2e.config.ts: fail an attempt in which the app threw an uncaught error.
export default {
  targets,
  appLog: {
    failOn: 'error', // default off; also a list, such as ['error', 'network']
    ignore: [/analytics\.example\.com/], // a RegExp or a substring, matched on the entry's text
  },
} satisfies E2EConfig;

// The same option on a test or a group, for example to opt one page out:
test('legacy dashboard', { appLog: { failOn: false } }, async ({ app }) => {});
```

- `failOn` names app-log sources: `'error'` (an uncaught exception or an unhandled rejection), `'network'` (a failed request or a 5xx), `'console'` (`console.error`). Only `error`-level entries count.
- The body runs to the end, like `expect.soft`. The attempt then fails with a new `APP_ERROR` code that names the first matching entry, its step, and how many more there were. If the attempt already failed for another reason, the app error becomes a secondary error.
- Retries and `test.fail()` treat it like any other failure.
- `appLog` is the key #1455 proposes for `appLog.file`, so the two features share one option.

### Upsides

- Catches bugs a passing assertion hides, such as an exception in a handler or a 500 behind an optimistic UI.
- No engine change: the entries are already collected, and the check reads them where core builds `EngineAttemptContext.appLog`, the seam #1455 tees.
- No wire change: report-1 error codes are free strings, so this adds a documented code, not a schema field.
- Agent steps get the same check: an `agent.act` that completes while the app throws fails the test.

### Downsides

- Noise: third-party scripts throw too, hence `ignore` and off by default. An entry carries no origin, so `ignore` matches the text. An uncaught error's text includes its top stack frame, and a network line includes its URL.
- The mobile engine reports no app-log entries today, so on a device target `failOn` does nothing until that engine reports crashes. The option is engine-neutral; the effect is web-only for now.
- A new config and test option, and a new error code to document.

### Alternatives

- A matcher, `await expect(app).toHaveNoErrors()`, called where the test wants it. It's more explicit, but it has to be in every test, and a check at the end of the body misses errors raised in `afterEach`.
- An accessor, `app.errors()`, for custom assertions. It could ship with either.
- The `addInitScript` workaround above.

### Which surface

config keys, public types (SDK)

### Compatibility

Adds an option that is off by default; nothing that exists changes.

I'd like to build this if the direction sounds right.

title: mcp: allow integrations to append instructions (e.g. --instructions-file)
body:
`e2e mcp` passes a fixed instructions string to the MCP client. Its first sentence says the server drives "an e2e project's app (its e2e.config.ts)". Integrations that prepare an ephemeral config outside the repository have no way to tell the agent so: with no `e2e.config.ts` in the repo, agents conclude e2e cannot run and fall back to hand-written Playwright scripts.

Reproduce (e2e 0.23.0): register `e2e mcp` in a repo without `e2e.config.ts`, read the initialize instructions — only the project-config route is described; `e2e mcp --help` offers `--config`, `--target`, `--headed`, `--max-sessions`, nothing for instructions.

Proposal: an optional `--instructions-file <path>` whose bounded content is appended to the existing instructions. Defaults stay unchanged; no integration-specific text upstream.

Acceptance:
- Without the option, initialize returns today's instructions unchanged.
- With a readable local file, initialize returns the existing guidance plus the suffix.
- An unreadable or oversized file fails at startup with a clear error.

Our integration would append: "No e2e.config.ts in the repository? Run `devkit e2e-prep --url <url>` and pass the printed CONFIG path as `config` to `open_session`."

title: VOLATILE_TEXT misses Japanese (CJK) dates, so recordings break the next day
body:
Thanks for developing this awesome library!

In e2e 0.23.1 (latest; also unchanged in `0.23.2-nightly-20261114030211`), `VOLATILE_TEXT` in `dist/cache/anchors.js` prevents text that changes with each run from being included in anchors. This covers English month names, ISO-formatted dates, and `H:MM`-formatted times (the shared patterns in `dist/internal/dates.js`), but Japanese dates and times such as `2026年11月15日` or `12時30分` are not covered. Therefore, in Japanese apps displaying fields like "作成日" (Creation Date), the execution date gets recorded in `endAnchors` or `goneAnchors`. When running a replay on the following day or later, `deltaMismatch` reports that the "anchor does not exist," which either hands the process over to the model or causes it to fail under the `--strict-cache` option.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a page that displays today's date using `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('ja-JP', { year: 'numeric', month: 'long', day: 'numeric' })`.
2. Record an `agent.act` step that includes an end screen displaying that date. `{ "text": "2026年11月15日" }` will be included in `endAnchors` of the trace.
3. Change the system date by one day (or run it the next day) and execute the replay with `--strict-cache` specified. The step will fail with `REPLAY_STALE` because the date anchor no longer matches.

Suggested patterns (e.g. added to `dist/internal/dates.js`)
```js
/\d{1,2}月\d{1,2}日/,   // also matches 2026年11月15日
/\d{1,2}時\d{1,2}分/,
```

Since Chinese also uses the same `年月日` format, these patterns should be able to cover it too.

title: fix(cache): treat CJK and numeric dates as volatile anchor text
body: ## What and why - `VOLATILE_TEXT` only knew English month names, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` and `H:MM`, so a date like `2026年11月15日` or `2026/11/15` was recorded as an anchor and the replay went stale the next day. - New patterns in `packages/core/src/internal/dates.ts`, added to `VOLATILE_TEXT` in `packages/core/src/cache/anchors.ts`: - `CJK_DATE`: month and day with `月/日` or `월/일`, year optional (`11月15日`, `2026年11月15日`, `2026년 11월 15일`). - `CJK_TIME`: `時/时/시` with `分/분` (`12時30分`, `12시 30분`). - `NUMERIC_DATE`: slash or dot dates with a four-digit year, either end (`2026/11/15`, `2026. 11. 15.`, `15.11.2026`, `11/15/2026`). - The CJK patterns anchor on the digits instead of `\b`. A bare `3月` and a version like `v1.2.2026` stay stable. - Since `alertShape` masks the same patterns, an alert carrying one of these dates now compares with the date as a placeholder, like the English forms already do. ## Issue Fixes #1817 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New test in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-anchors.test.ts` formats 2026-11-15 through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for `ja-JP`, `zh-CN`, `ko-KR`, `de-DE` and `en-US` (numeric), and `ja-JP`, `zh-CN`, `ko-KR` (long month), plus the CJK time forms, and checks each is skipped next to a stable result. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `作成日 2026/11/15` is kept in `appeared` (test fails) | skipped as volatile, only `Task created` is recorded | ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(agent): judge a waitFor screen change without waiting out the interval
body:
After a false judgment, `agent.waitFor` waited out `interval` (3 s by default), counted from when the judgment returned, before it looked at the screen again. A condition that came true just after a judgment therefore resolved up to 3 s late.

## Change

- After a false or inconclusive judgment, `waitFor` now observes every 500 ms from the start ([`waitForNextJudgment`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/kdy1/eng-931-agent-waitfor-resolves-3s-after-the-condition/packages/core/src/agent/index.ts)). Before, it waited out `interval` first.
- A change is judged at once when either:
  - observations saw the screen hold still for `interval` before the change, or
  - this is the first change since the wait began.
- A screen that keeps changing (a progress counter, a clock) is still judged at most once per `interval` after the previous judgment. `maxModelCalls` budgets that passed before do not run out sooner.
- Only stillness that an observation saw counts. Nothing is observed while a judgment runs, so a slow model call does not prove the screen held still. Without this rule, a 3 s model call on a clock gave one judgment per tick (found in self-review).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  J[judgment: false] --> P[observe every 500 ms]
  P -->|same as judged| P
  P -->|changed after interval of seen stillness, or first change| N[judge now]
  P -->|changed inside a run of changes| W{interval since the last judgment?}
  W -- no --> P
  W -- yes --> N
```

- `interval` now means "least time between two judgments of a screen that keeps changing". This PR updates `docs/reference/agent.mdx`, the `WaitForOptions` JSDoc, and `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`. The skill had described `interval` as the observation cadence, which was already wrong.
- Cost: on a static screen, `waitFor` now also observes during the first `interval`. Observations call only the engine, with no model call.

Not covered: a change that comes less than `interval` after an earlier change still waits out `interval`, for example "Uploading 50%" and then "Done" 1.5 s later. Judging that second change at once is not possible without also judging every tick of a 1 s counter. That would roughly double the model calls on such screens, and long waits on them could hit `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`.

## Issue

Fixes ENG-931

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- **Setup:** a scratch project beside the testbed with the built CLI and the real judge `gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`. I ran each build 3 times. "main" is this branch with main's `packages/core/src/agent/index.ts`, rebuilt.
- **Pages:**
  - `/late` shows "Working" and switches to "Done" 2.5 s after load. The test calls `agent.waitFor('the export finished')` with the default `interval`.
  - `/clock` ticks every 200 ms. The test calls `agent.waitFor('the clock reads stop', { timeout: 10_000 })`, which must time out.

| `waitFor` step | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/late`, step time | 6.40 s, 6.63 s, 6.76 s | 4.78 s, 4.41 s, 4.56 s |
| `/late`, time outside model calls | 3.03 s, 3.02 s, 3.03 s | 1.05 s, 1.05 s, 0.53 s |
| `/clock`, model calls in 10 s | 3, 2, 3 (each third call was cut at the deadline) | 3, 3, 3 |

- In every `/late` run the first judgment returned after "Done" was already on screen (model calls took 1.4–2.3 s). Main then waited the full 3 s; this branch judged on its next 500 ms observation.
- **New integration tests** in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent.test.ts`, all with the scripted model:
  - A wait with `interval: 60_000` and `timeout: 5000` judges a URL change. It fails on main (`expected 'failed' to be 'passed'`) and passes here.
  - A 200 ms ticking page gets exactly 3 judgments in 2.5 s.
  - With a judge that takes 1.2 s per call, the ticking page still gets 3 judgments. Counting the judgment's own latency as stillness gives 4 (`expected 4 to be 3`).

title: fix(mobile): fail an action agent-device refuses for an unknown screen origin as an action failure
body:
- agent-device 0.21.37 (callstack/agent-device#4439) refuses an iOS ref action with `COMMAND_FAILED`, `details.reason: window-origin-unknown`, `dispatched: no` when its capture can't place the window on screen. It happens on a full-screen iPhone app right after a large web view loads. While that screen stays up the runner reads the tree through its private AX fallback, which never gets the viewport back (measured over 150 s).
- The engine reported the refusal as `ENGINE_FAILURE`, an infrastructure error (exit 3), although nothing was sent and the device is fine. It now maps to `NOT_ACTIONABLE` (`ACTION_FAILED`, exit 1) in `staleOr`, next to the covered-target refusals from #1686. A refusal with `dispatched: unknown` stays `ENGINE_FAILURE`.
- agent-device's hint names its CLI (`Take a fresh snapshot … or use screenshot …`). The message carries the test's move instead: `Nothing was sent. The app's window has no known position on the screen, so node bounds, boundingBox() included, may be offset from screen coordinates. For a tap, tap a screen point with screen.tapAt(), not one taken from those bounds.` A point tap isn't aimed from the capture, so agent-device takes it; other actions have no point form. After agent-device 0.21.38 (#1859) the refusal is left only for a placed iPad window, an offset root, or iPhone landscape, where a point read from `boundingBox()` carries the window's offset.
- No retry: re-observing returns the same capture state for as long as the screen stays heavy, so a retry only moves the failure to the deadline.
- The refused reasons and their hints are one map, `NOT_ACTIONABLE_REASONS`. `undefined` keeps agent-device's hint, and a string replaces its CLI advice.
- No docs change: callstack/agent-device#4573 (merged) makes agent-device accept a full-screen root, so the web view case goes away at the next agent-device bump, and the error hint names the move.

## Issue

Fixes #1821

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

title: iOS: locator.tap right after a large web view loads fails as ENGINE_FAILURE (window-origin-unknown)
body:
### What happened

On an iPhone simulator, `locator.tap()` right after a large `WKWebView` loads fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE` (exit 3, an infrastructure error):

```
perform tap failed: Ref @e2 has no established screen-coordinate origin Hint: Take a fresh snapshot after the accessibility channel recovers, or use screenshot to choose screen coordinates.
```

agent-device 0.21.37 (callstack/agent-device#4439) refuses the ref action with `details.reason: window-origin-unknown` and `dispatched: no`: nothing was sent and the device is fine, so `ENGINE_FAILURE` is the wrong class, and the hint names agent-device's CLI, which a test can't use. `screen.tapAt()` at the same point works.

The refusal itself (a full-screen iPhone root treated as unanchored) is agent-device's: callstack/agent-device#4573. It lasts for as long as the heavy screen stays up (over 150 s measured), so re-observing doesn't help.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/gronxb/e2e-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. Boot an iPhone simulator.
2. `npm install && ./repro.sh`
3. Expected the three reload-and-tap rounds to pass. The second round fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE` as above (2/2 runs).

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.7 (agent-device 0.21.37), node 24.22.1, iOS 26.5 simulator

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

title: perf(agent): keep the act tool set the same across steps for the prompt cache
body:
Two gaps in the provider prompt cache, both measured in ENG-1307 on the testbed agentic suite.

- **`type_secret` broke the shared `act` prefix.** The tool was offered only to a step that declared secrets, and its description listed their names. The tools come first in the prompt, so the first call of that step read 0 cached tokens while every other `act` step read about 4,400.
  - The built-in act loop now offers `type_secret` on every step where the engine can fill a secret. Its description is the same on every step (`packages/core/src/agent/primitives.ts`, `secretsListedByCaller`).
  - The step's opening message lists the declared secrets: `Secrets to fill with type_secret, by name: "admin.password" (password).` (`packages/core/src/agent/default-agent.ts`).
  - On a step that declares no secret, a call goes to the dispatcher, which already refuses an undeclared name with `POLICY_DENIED`. The model reads that as a failed action, and the failure-streak guard counts it.
  - `createGrammarTools` (ACP, MCP) does not change. ACP already does the same thing on its own.
- **Judgments never read the cache. This gap is accepted, not fixed.** A judgment prompt is about 1,100 tokens. Its fixed prefix is shorter than the 1,024 tokens that OpenAI needs before it caches.
  - `buildPrompt` now puts the `Test:` line after the fixed request text, so the prefix that tests share grows from about 350 to about 750 tokens (`packages/core/src/agent/prompts.ts`). A project with roughly 300 tokens of agent context gets past the minimum.
  - Not done: padding the judgment prompt past 1,024 tokens. Judgments were 2% of input tokens in the measured run.
- The replay cache key does not include the tools or the prompt text, so the committed recordings still replay.

## Issue

Fixes ENG-1307

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- I ran the testbed agentic suite with a live model, the same run as the issue: `e2e run --config e2e.agent.config.ts --no-cache --ai-trace`, on `gateway/openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`. I summed the `usage.inputTokenDetails` of each step in `.e2e/ai-trace.json` with the script from the issue.

| | main (5c7e18f9, from the issue) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all calls, cache read rate | 83.5% | 83.7% |
| `agent.act` | 85.1% | 85.3% |
| first `act` calls with a cache read | 19 of 21 | 19 of 21 |
| **first call of `act signs in with a secret credential`** | read 0, wrote 4,889 | **read 4,456**, wrote 450 |
| tools on that call | 28 (others 27) | 28 (all 28) |
| `assert` / `waitFor` / `extract` | 0% | 0% (accepted) |

- The 2 first `act` calls that did not read the cache started within the first 10 ms of the run, before any cache was written.
- 28 of 29 tests passed. `enters a code on the drawn keypad through points` failed once because the model tapped `31451` instead of `31415` on the drawn keypad. It did not call `type_secret`. With `--repeat-each 3`, it passed 3 of 3.
- I ran the live measurement before a review change: a call on a step without secrets now goes to the dispatcher, where before it returned a fixed text. That change does not touch the tool set or the descriptions.
- In the secret sign-in step, the model read the listed name from the opening message and called `type_secret {"name":"admin.password"}`. The password value appears in no file under `apps/testbed/.e2e/`, and not in the AI trace.
- The web benchmark agentic suite passed 34 of 34 with `CI=1 ... test:agent --strict-cache`, and no recording went stale (26 replayed, 3 handed off, 4 missed). The misses and hand-offs are entries that stop at a recorded gap (`minted-token`, `whole-node`). Neither the cache key nor the gap logic reads the tool set.

title: [web]: Improve MCP test-line generation for unnamed controls
body:
### Use case

I used `e2e mcp` on a standalone web form with an unlabeled numeric input and an **Add** button. Codex entered `10` and clicked **Add**. The page showed `Added 10 boxes`. The interaction worked, but `test_lines` recorded only the click as executable code:

```ts
// type: no test line: the node has no name, text, placeholder, or test id to find it by
await screen.getByRole("button", "Add").tap();
```

On this form, `locate` confirmed that `getByRole("spinbutton")` matched exactly one element. The following statement also passed through `run_code`:

```ts
await screen.getByRole("spinbutton").fill("10");
```

### Proposed enhancement

When the usual locator candidates cannot identify an unnamed control, try its role alone. If several controls share that role, try scoping the locator to an identifiable row, group, or dialog. Generate a line only when the resulting locator matches exactly one element and MCP can verify it is the element used in the original action. Keep the existing `No test line` comment when the target is ambiguous.

This would capture more of the steps needed to replay a successful interaction. In this example, replaying the flow on a fresh form requires entering the quantity before clicking **Add**.

title: test(acp): wait for the cancel log before teardown removes it
body:
`spec` on main has failed since 3ce6b589 (runs [43768414124](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43768414124), [43794693850](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43794693850), [43802621814](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43802621814)), and the nightly release refuses to publish because of it. In every failing job, one test fails: `acp > preserves cancellation while waiting for the previous turn to stop` in `packages/acp/tests/executor.test.ts`, with `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '/tmp/e2e-acp-test-…'`.

- The first step's abort sends `session/cancel` as a notification and rejects at once (`packages/acp/src/session.ts:244`). The scripted agent ignores the cancel, but it still logs `{ cancelled: true }` to `agent.jsonl` whenever it reads the notification.
- The rest of the test takes a few milliseconds. On a busy Linux runner, the agent appends that line while `afterEach` removes the log directory. `rmSync` deletes `agent.jsonl`, the append creates it again, and the `rmdir` fails.
- The test now waits for the cancel line before it starts the second step. The run no longer writes anything into the directory during teardown. The test also now checks that the abort sent the cancel.
- The second step sends the agent nothing. The `closed` write from `first.end` comes after the directory is gone, because cleanups run in registration order, and the agent catches that `ENOENT`.

Refs #1773. #1774 hardens teardown for the whole file, with LIFO cleanup and `rm` retries. The two changes are independent. Note that LIFO alone would let the `closed` write race the removal, so #1774 depends on its retries.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes (macOS). The failure is Linux-only, and it did not reproduce here, even with 16 concurrent runs under CPU load. To show the race, I delayed the scripted agent's cancel log by 200 ms (a slow child) and recorded, at teardown, whether the cancel line was already in the log:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `cancel logged at teardown: false`: the write is still pending when the directory is removed | `cancel logged at teardown: true`: nothing is left to write |

`pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/acp run test` passes 50/50 three times in a row, and `pnpm check` passes. CI on this PR is the Linux check.

title: fix(web,mobile): load the main entry without e2e installed
body:
`@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/mobile` declare `e2e` an optional peer, but their main entry imported it statically to build `test`. A program on `@e2e-dev/core` alone that imports the engine from the main entry fails before any of its code runs:

```ts
import { launch } from '@e2e-dev/core';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; // not '@e2e-dev/web/engine'

await using shop = await launch(web(), { app: { url: 'https://shop.example.com' } });
// Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'e2e' imported from …/@e2e-dev/web/dist/index.js
```

- The main entry now gets `test` from `runnerTest()` (`packages/web/src/runner-test.ts`, mobile's copy is the same). It requires `e2e` only when `require.resolve('e2e')` finds it.
- Without `e2e`, `web()` and `mobile()` work, and `test`, `describe`, and the hooks throw the new `RUNNER_NOT_INSTALLED` when called. The stand-in's `extend` returns itself, so the entry can still extend it while it loads.
- Only "`e2e` itself not found" counts as not installed. An installed `e2e` whose `dist` is missing also throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, but that error names the file and is rethrown.
- `createRequire`, not `await import()`: a top-level await would make `require('@e2e-dev/web')` from a CommonJS file (a `.cts` helper, for example) fail with `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`, and that works on main today. `require(esm)` shares the module instance with `import`, so a test file that imports `@e2e-dev/web` before `e2e` still registers on the same `test`.
- The main entry's `.d.ts` still names `e2e`. A TypeScript program without it imports from `/engine` or sets `skipLibCheck`; `docs/core.mdx` and the changeset say so.
- `scripts/install-smoke.ts` gains a second project: core, web, and mobile without `e2e`, importing both main entries. It fails on main and passes here.
- The changeset edits `.changeset/e2e-core.md`, which has not been released yet, since its line "need `e2e` only for their main entry" stopped being true.
- `package-imports.test.ts`: web's main entry no longer reaches any package statically, so the scanner's sanity check now asks for any module or package. `e2e`'s optional-peer home moves to `runner-test.ts`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- Packed `@e2e-dev/core`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `e2e` from main and from this branch, then installed them with npm into scratch projects: one with core and web only, one with `e2e` too.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| core only: `launch(web())` from `@e2e-dev/web`, read a price | `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'e2e'` | `price: $19` |
| core only: call `test`, `describe`, `beforeEach`, `test.skip` | `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at import | each throws `ConfigurationError RUNNER_NOT_INSTALLED` |
| core only: `require('@e2e-dev/web')` from a `.cjs` file | `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | `require ok: function function` |
| with `e2e`: `npx e2e run`, one file imports `@e2e-dev/web` before `e2e`, one after | 2 passed | 2 passed (also with `--workers 1`) |
| `node scripts/install-smoke.ts 12` with the new core-only step | `core-only main entries: exit 1` (`Cannot find package 'e2e'`) | exit 0 |

The message without `e2e`:

```
`test` from '@e2e-dev/web' needs e2e, the test runner, which is not installed. Install e2e to write tests, or import web() from '@e2e-dev/web/engine' to drive a browser with @e2e-dev/core.
```

- Not run locally: Bun and a mobile device. CI covers both on this head: the `bun (1.4.3)` and `bun (latest)` jobs, and the mobile benchmark on an iOS simulator and an Android emulator, all green.

title: test(acp): wait for the cancel ack before tearing down the step directory
body: - The `spec` gate fails on every main push since #1761: `preserves cancellation while waiting for the previous turn to stop` dies in `afterEach` with `ENOTEMPTY` on the test's temp dir (3 of the last 10 matrix jobs: [node 22](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43802621814/job/133086157900), [node 24.8.0](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43802621814/job/133086157918), [node 24](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43832837073/job/133182062431)). - Cause: the first step's abort rejects `runStep` at once, but the scripted agent is another process and appends `{ cancelled: true }` to `agent.jsonl` only when it reads the cancel notification. The rest of the test takes ~1 ms, so on a loaded runner that append lands between `rmSync`'s readdir and rmdir. - Fix: wait for the `cancelled` entry before moving on (which also asserts the executor sent the cancel), and run `cleanups` in LIFO order so the attempt ends before its directory is removed. ```ts first.abortStep(new AgentError('STEP_TIMEOUT', 'the first step timed out')); await expect(run).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'STEP_TIMEOUT' }); await eventually(() => expect(log()).toContainEqual({ cancelled: true })); ``` ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/acp test` against the built dist: 4 files, 50 tests green. - The fixed test 10 times in a loop: 0 failures. On main a probe at the end of the test showed the `cancelled` entry already present in all 15 local runs, so the race never reproduces on a fast Mac; the CI logs above are the reproduction. - `pnpm check` green.

title: [web]: Show live step captions in the browser and capture them in MCP recordings
body:
### Feature request

When I ask `e2e mcp` to test a web flow and record it, I’d like the agent to show short captions directly in the headed Playwright browser as it works.

For example, during a CSV import, the caption could change from **“Select the CSV file”** to **“Click Import”**, then to **“Verified: 2 orders imported”** once the agent has checked the result.

### How it would work

The agent sets or updates the caption at each major step. Anyone watching the browser sees it immediately, even when recording is off. When recording is on, the existing recorder captures the caption as part of the video frame, so the exported WebM can be shared as a single file.

Captions would be optional and should leave page layout, clicks, and the `observe` tree unchanged.

### Why I’d use it

I’d use this to share short test walkthroughs with teammates. They could see what the agent was trying to do and what it verified directly in the video.

### Demo

The video shows three live captions as the agent runs the import: **“Select the CSV file”**, **“Click Import”**, and **“Verified: 2 orders imported”**. The captions are visible in Playwright and appear in the original recording.
