title: perf(core): read a wait again at 20 and 50 ms, then every 100 ms from its start
body:
## What and why

- An action, `waitFor`, or assertion that misses on its first read slept a fixed 100 ms before reading again. Profiling the e2e suite of [webiny-js](https://github.com/webiny/webiny-js) (`e2e` 0.22, `@e2e-dev/web`) put those sleeps at 36% of step time: most waits end within a frame or two of the first read, then sit out the rest of the tick.
- `pollDelay` (`packages/core/src/internal/time.ts`) now reads at 0, 20, and 50 ms, then at every multiple of 100 ms from the start of the wait. Each pause is at least 10 ms and at most 100 ms.
- Every read time of the old schedule is still on the timeline, so a state is never seen later than on main. A read that outlasts the early marks lands on the next 100 ms mark, which keeps slow engines (a mobile snapshot takes about 190 ms) on the cadence they had.
- `pollReads` (so `pollCondition` from `e2e/engine`, which `@e2e-dev/web`'s `waitForURL`, `toHaveURL`, and `check` use), `resolveCounted`, `resolveOnce`, and `performWithin` in `packages/core/src/locator/engine.ts` share it. `expect.poll` keeps its `interval`; the stale-node retry in `readAllNow` keeps 100 ms.
- The deadline rule (`ReadWindow.cutOff`) is unchanged: it relies on no pause being longer than `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, which still holds.

```text
main:    0 ─────────── 100 ─────────── 200 ─────────── 300
branch:  0 ── 20 ── 50 ── 100 ─────────── 200 ─────────── 300
```

Faster detection can surface a race that was already in a test. In webiny's `uploadAndDeliver`, the test reads `document.images` right after waiting for the file name, and the card mounts its image a moment later: it failed 2 of 30 runs on this branch and 0 of 90 on main. Plain Playwright, which notices the file name sooner still, hits the same race. The test needs to wait for the image; nothing in e2e changes that.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

webiny-js e2e suite (standalone SQLite project, the five tests that need no license), built CLI, one worker, 3 interleaved runs per variant, the thumbnail wait added to both suites. Baseline is main at `5c7e18f9`; the poll code is identical on the rebased head.

| | main | this PR | delta | plain Playwright |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| suite wall | 21.74 s | 18.62 s | -14.4% | 16.79 s |
| login (median, n=30) | 690 ms | 558 ms | -19% | 555 ms |
| upload, file listed | 876 ms | 742 ms | -15% | 676 ms |
| install wizard | 1892 ms | 1646 ms | -13% | 1454 ms |
| auth setup | 931 ms | 788 ms | -15% | 541 ms |

`pnpm bench:ab` on `apps/web-benchmark` (`9d4aaf0c` against this head, 6 pairs, load 3.0): every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on every run of both builds, and no test or step got slower.

| Metric | main | this PR | change (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| suite (sum of attempts) | 61.49 s | 60.79 s | -1.1% (-1.8% to -0.2%) |
| `expect.toHaveText` | 2.65 s | 2.45 s | -8.0% (-10.1% to -5.7%) |
| `expect.toBeHidden` | 6.70 s | 6.53 s | -2.5% (-2.9% to -2.2%) |
| `expect.toHaveURL` | 201 ms | 44 ms | -78.4% (-84.8% to -68.7%) |
| shadow DOM form, wrong code | 263 ms | 171 ms | -33.0% (-36.2% to -22.5%) |
| scrollIntoView footnote | 241 ms | 157 ms | -33.8% (-36.3% to -31.7%) |

title: fix(agent): strip unknown fields on no-input agent tools
body: ## What and why Some models add arguments to agent tools that take no input. The call is rejected as invalid, the model sends the same call again, and the step repeats until the step budget runs out, so the tool never runs. Every built-in agent tool validates its input with a strict object schema, including tools whose shape declares no fields. A key the schema does not declare fails that check, and the failure is returned to the model as the tool result. Those tools ignore their input, so the extra keys never had an effect on the action. A tool with an empty schema shape still uses the strict schema, which keeps the provider-facing input closed, but a plain object is reduced to an empty object before that check, so extra keys are dropped and the call runs. Values that are not plain objects still fail validation. Tools that declare fields still reject unknown keys, and screenshot does too once a path field is present. The security and reference docs and a patch changeset describe that split. ## Issue Fixes #1812 ## Verified Ran `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/core run typecheck` locally; both passed. `packages/e2e/tests/unit/agent-grammar-tools.test.ts`: all 17 tests pass at 78c42b8, and 1 fails with the `primitives.ts` change reverted and `@e2e-dev/core` rebuilt. `pnpm run docs:check`, `pnpm run plugins:check` and `pnpm run mcp-server:check` pass at 78c42b8. title: Replay cache keeps CJK counts (42件) as anchors, so a growing tally makes the next replay stale
body:
### What happened

The replay cache drops a count that only moved (`41 items` -> `42 items`), but it does not recognize counts written with a CJK counter, such as `42件`.

`COUNT_TEXT` in `cache/anchors` only has English patterns (`\b\d+\s+(?:results?|items?|...)`). In Japanese, Chinese, and Korean the counter word follows the digits with no space (`42件`, `42个`, `42개`), so none of them match.

Effect on a Japanese app:

- A tally that grows with every run (`41件` -> `42件`) is recorded as an end anchor. On the next run it reads `43件`, so `deltaMismatch` reports it missing. The replay hands off to the model, or fails with `REPLAY_STALE` under `--strict-cache`. The English equivalent passes.
- A list screen opened by navigation keeps `全9件中 1〜9件を表示` as an anchor, while `Showing 1 to 9 of 9 results` is dropped.

Expected: `42件` is treated the same way as `42 items`.

This is separate from #1817, which covers Japanese dates in `VOLATILE_TEXT`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Toraastrta/e2e-cjk-count-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run repro`
3. Expected the `41件 -> 42件` case to record only `追加しました`, like the `41 items -> 42 items` case records only `Item added`. Instead `42件` is recorded too, and the next run (`43件`) reports it missing.

The script calls `describeDelta` and `deltaMismatch` from the installed `e2e@0.23.1` dist directly (they are not exported), so no model or browser is needed. The README shows the full output.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, node 22.22.3

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

I have a fix with a unit test ready (one pattern added to `COUNT_TEXT`) and can open a PR if this sounds right.

title: fix(cache): read CJK counts like 42件 as count text
body: ## What and why - `COUNT_TEXT` only matched English counts. CJK counters follow the digits with no space (`42件`), so a growing Japanese tally was kept as an anchor and the next replay went stale. - Adds one pattern for CJK counters that match the English set of generic tallies: 件, 個/个/개, 건, 項/项 (also 項目/项目), 条, 筆/笔, and 行/행 for rows. People counters and other units are left out, as in the English pattern. - Like the English pattern, the digits need a word boundary before them, so `X1笔` does not match. Words that only start with a counter (`3个月`, `3개월`, `个人版`, `笔记本`) and `第3条` are not counts, and neither are `3行目` or a spaced Korean word such as `2024 개발자`. - Tests next to the existing English one, and a `42件` example in `docs/cache.mdx`. ## Issue Fixes #1836 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The CJK count tests in `trace-anchors.test.ts` fail on `main` (`42件` is kept as an anchor) and pass with the fix. title: web: a name from content includes descendants with their own role (a tree item, a tab badge)
body:
### What happened

When the web engine names an element from its content, it adds the text of every descendant, including descendants whose own role is not named from content. Chrome and Playwright leave those out. So a parent tree item is named by its whole subtree, and a tab by its `status` badge:

| | e2e tree | Chrome and Playwright |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parent tree item | `treeitem "src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts"` | `treeitem "src"` |
| nested tree item | `treeitem "lib a.ts b.ts"` | `treeitem "lib"` |
| tab with a badge | `tab "Inbox 3"` | `tab "Inbox"` |

`getByRole('treeitem', 'src')` finds the node, then `toHaveAccessibleName('src')` on the same locator fails with `observed: name "src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts"`. A name read off the tree also matches nothing in Playwright's `getByRole`. On the agent's side, every expanded parent in an APG-style tree is named by every label under it, which gets longer the deeper the tree.

Expected: the names Chrome and Playwright give.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/name-from-content

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cd name-from-content && npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`: both tests fail on `toHaveAccessibleName`, with `observed: name "src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts"` and `observed: name "Inbox 3"`.
3. `cat .e2e/results/*parent-tree-item*/attempt-1/screen-at-failure.txt` shows the long names in the tree.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0, node 22.23.4, Linux

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

### Anything else

- `contentNameOf` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:647`) calls `childrenNameOf` for every descendant, whatever its role (line 660). Playwright's `allowsNameFromContent(role, targetDescendant)` lets a descendant add its content only when its role is named from content or is one of the text and structural roles. Other descendants add only their title, and a fieldset or figure its legend or figcaption. The engine follows Playwright for which roles are named from content (`NAME_FROM_CONTENT_ROLES`, line 739, extended in #553), but has no check for descendants.
- Other markup it hits: a button holding an unlabeled `role="img"` emoji, a link wrapping an `<article>` or `<figure>`, a heading holding `role="note"`.
- The engine's own `listitem`/`status`/`alert` naming policy doesn't need to change: the check applies only to roles accname names from content.
- `tests/conformance/expected.txt` lists the axe-core case for this (#13, a heading's `role="alert"` child) under the alert-naming policy. A fix resolves that line.
- I have a fix with a crosscheck fixture page and a `read-node-names` test that both fail on main. The tree on the web-benchmark home page and all 42 scenarios' first screens comes out the same, so committed recordings don't change. Happy to open the PR.

title: ci(site): redeploy e2e.com on every docs push to main again

flowchart LR
  D[push to main: docs/**] --> S[site.yml: deploy hook]
  E[push to main: examples registry] --> S
  S --> B[e2e.com builds docs and examples from main]

title: fix(web): leave descendants with their own role out of a name from content
body:
## Summary - `contentNameOf` read every descendant's content into a name from content, whatever the descendant's role. Chrome and Playwright skip descendants whose own role is not named from content, so the tree said `treeitem "src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts"` and `tab "Inbox 3"` where they say `treeitem "src"` and `tab "Inbox"`. - A descendant now adds its content only when it has no role, a role named from content, or a text or structure role, as Playwright's `allowsNameFromContent` reads it. Any other descendant adds only its title, and a fieldset or figure its legend or figcaption (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`, `addsContentToName`). - Which role a descendant has is read as Playwright reads it where the two differ in a way that matters: `
` has none (its text counts), `
`, ``, and `` have one that is not named from content. - The check runs only for the roles accname names from content. The tree's own `listitem`/`status`/`alert` naming stays as it was, and so do `aria-labelledby` targets and `
` or an `
`, structure kept, a reference kept whole), each also checked against Playwright's `getByRole`, and a cross-check fixture page against Chrome and Playwright. Both fail on main. Analysis and repro by the reporter, @Asheesh7298: https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/name-from-content ## Issue Fixes #1839 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Reporter's repro (`npx e2e run`) against packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/core` tarballs built from main (0cd14a0df) and from this branch. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | 2 failed | 2 passed | | `treeitem "src"`: observed name `"src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts"` | `toHaveAccessibleName('src')` passes | | `tab "Inbox"`: observed name `"Inbox 3"` | `toHaveAccessibleName('Inbox')` passes | main: ```text FAIL |web| tests/names.e2e.ts > a parent tree item is named by its own label ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveAccessibleName failed locator: getByRole("treeitem", name: "src") expected: accessible name "src" observed: name "src lib a.ts b.ts index.ts" (match count 1) FAIL |web| tests/names.e2e.ts > a tab is named without its status badge ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveAccessibleName failed locator: getByRole("tab", name: "Inbox") expected: accessible name "Inbox" observed: name "Inbox 3" (match count 1) ``` this branch: ```text ✓ |web| tests/names.e2e.ts > a parent tree item is named by its own label 244ms ✓ |web| tests/names.e2e.ts > a tab is named without its status badge 59ms Tests 2 passed (2) ``` - New `read-node-names` test and the cross-check fixture page fail on main (`treeitem "src lib a.ts"`, `tab "Inbox 3"`, `button "* Party"`, `heading "Title Note text"` against Chrome and Playwright) and pass here. - Web benchmark: dumped the engine tree (role and name of every node) of the home page and all 42 scenarios on main and on this branch: identical, so committed recordings keep their keys. Cross-check over the benchmark (`CROSSCHECK_BENCHMARK_URL`) and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` pass.

title: fix(report): round token counts before choosing the unit
body: ## What and why - Token counts from 999,950 up to a million showed as `1000.0k`, because `formatTokens` picked k before rounding. It now rounds first, so they show as `1.0M`. title: feat(expect): add toHaveRole locator matcher
body: ## What and why - Adds `expect(locator).toHaveRole(role)`, the Assertions item `expect(locator).toHaveRole('button')` from #1855. - It compares the role the engine reports for the one match (`SemanticNode.role`) as a string, so a `switch` is not a `checkbox`. It takes the `getByRole` vocabulary and reads `img` as `image`, through `canonicalRole` (now exported from `packages/core/src/locator/expression.ts`). - Like the other locator matchers, it polls, negates, needs one match, and takes only `timeout`. It answers on a password field, since a role is never withheld. Every engine already reports `role`, so there's no engine-contract change. - Docs: a `toHaveRole` entry in `reference/expect.mdx`; `migrate/playwright.mdx` moves `toHaveRole()` from "What e2e doesn't have yet" into the mapping and notes how it differs; the e2e skill lists it, and MCP `run_code` accepts it. ```ts await expect(screen.getByTestId('wifi')).toHaveRole('switch'); await expect(screen.getByTestId('wifi')).not.toHaveRole('checkbox'); ``` ## Issue Part of #1855 (Assertions: `expect(locator).toHaveRole('button')`). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - New unit tests (`tests/unit/expect-async-role.test.ts`), web integration tests on a `/role-matcher` page in Chromium (`tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts`), and a scripted-engine case (`tests/integration/scripted-matchers.test.ts`). With `main`'s sources, 10 of 95 unit and 4 of 51 integration tests fail (`toHaveRole is not a function`) and typecheck reports 19 errors. On this branch all pass and typecheck is clean. - The web tests cover a `contenteditable` heading (found by `getByRole('heading')`, read as `textbox`) and a failing `toHaveRole` on a password field whose value stays out of the result. - `pnpm check` passes, and so do the full `e2e` unit suite (3827 passed) and the testbed suite on the built CLI (586 passed). ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. @okwasniewski

title: fix(report): keep \r\n line breaks in serialized errors and the JUnit report
body:
## Issue

Fixes #1741

## What changed

`junit.xml` wrote U+FFFD where a failure message had `\r\n`. The JUnit reporter was not the cause: `serializeError` (`packages/core/src/internal/errors.ts`) ran `sanitizeText` when the error was recorded, so the `\r` was U+FFFD in `report.json` before `junit.ts` saw it, and its `` encoding never matched.

- New `sanitizeRecordedText` beside `sanitizeText` in `packages/core/src/internal/errors.ts`. It keeps the `\r` of a `\r\n` and replaces a lone `\r` with U+FFFD, like any other control character. `sanitizeText` and `CONTROL_PATTERN` are unchanged.
- `serializeError` uses it for the message, stack, and details. Skip reasons and `test.fail` reasons use it too (`run/execute.ts`, `run/expected-failure.ts`, `collect/select.ts`), so `<skipped>` and `<failure>` treat CRLF the same way.
- `junit.ts` keeps the order sanitize, then escape, then encode. `text()` now writes `\r` as `` as well, since a parser reads a raw `\r` in element text as a newline. Attributes get `
`.
- `e2e run --step` without a terminal printed a failed step's message as it was. It now goes through `bounded()` like every other terminal printer, so a recorded `\r` never reaches the terminal.
- Docs: the custom-reporter note in `docs/reference/reporters.mdx` now says what is kept.

A lone `\r` stays U+FFFD on purpose. Recorded messages also reach reporter events and `openHost` callers, and a bare `\r` printed there rewinds the line, so `failed\rpassed` would read as `passed`. A `\r\n` is safe there.

```text
input                     report.json            junit.xml
"line one\r\nline two"    "line one\r\nline two"  line one
line two
"failed\rpassed"          "failed�passed"     failed�passed
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, the built CLI: `e2e run tests/zz-crlf-repro.e2e.ts --reporter list,junit` with three tests, which throw `'line one\r\nline two'`, throw `'failed\rpassed'`, and call `test.skip('waiting on\r\nthe API')`. Same command on an `origin/main` build and on this branch.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CRLF failure, `junit.xml` | `message="line one�
line two"`, body `line one�` | `message="line one
line two"`, body `line one` |
| lone `\r` failure, `junit.xml` | `message="failed�passed"` | `message="failed�passed"` |
| CRLF skip, `junit.xml` | `<skipped message="waiting on�
the API"/>` | `<skipped message="waiting on
the API"/>` |
| `report.json` message | `"line one�\nline two"` | `"line one\r\nline two"` |
| terminal | `ERROR: line one�` | `ERROR: line one�` (no raw `\r` in the output) |

- `e2e run --step` on the fake engine with a `tap` that throws `'line one\r\nline two'`: the step line prints `ENGINE_FAILURE: actions failed: line one�` with no raw `\r`. The new `cli-step.test.ts` case fails when the `bounded()` call is removed.

title: perf(cli): load the YAML and TOML parsers only when e2e init needs them
body:
## What and why

- `cli/index.ts` statically imported `cli/init/flags.ts` for the `e2e init` options. Through it, every CLI start (`e2e run`, `e2e mcp`, `e2e --version`) loaded two parsers only `e2e init` uses:
  - `flags.ts > ci.ts > yaml` (since #1647)
  - `flags.ts > mcp-config.ts > codex-config.ts > toml-eslint-parser`
- The choice lists the flags need (`CI_IDS`, `MCP_LOCATIONS`, and their types) move to `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/choices.ts`, which imports nothing. `ci.ts` keeps `CI_SERVICES`, whose entries hold the YAML render functions. Both parsers now load only when `e2e init` runs.
- `e2e init --help` lists the same `--ci` and `--mcp` choices as before.
- `tests/unit/package-imports.test.ts` adds `yaml` and `toml-eslint-parser` to the modules `cli/index.ts` must reach only lazily; on main it fails and prints both chains. `init-ci.test.ts` checks that `CI_SERVICES` has one service per `--ci` choice, in order, now that the two lists live in separate files.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Built CLI, `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js --version`, 40 runs per build in random order, load 2.9 (Apple M3 Max, Node 24.20.0):

| | main | this PR | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CLI start to exit, median (IQR) | 114.5 ms (113.8-117.6) | 104.7 ms (104.0-106.7) | -9.8 ms (-8.6%) |

`e2e init` with `--ci github-actions` and `--ci gitlab` still writes the same pipelines (the `cli-init` unit and integration tests), and the testbed suite passes on the built packages.

title: perf(web): check the installed browser without loading playwright-core
body:
## What and why

- Before every run, the runner calls the web engine's `prepare`, which checks that the browser the run launches is installed. The check called `executablePath()`, which imports all of `playwright-core`: about 115 ms in the runner process, which never launches a browser (each worker imports Playwright again to launch). That was the whole `engine.prepare` phase.
- `isBrowserInstalled` (`packages/web/src/install.ts`) now answers a headless Chromium run from disk first: the `chromium-headless-shell` revision in `playwright-core/browsers.json`, the browser cache by Playwright's own rules (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` and its npm config spellings, `0` for the package's `.local-browsers`, else `ms-playwright` in the per-OS cache directory, relative paths against `INIT_CWD` or its npm config spellings, else the working directory), and the existing `headlessShellInstalled` check for the shell and its `INSTALLATION_COMPLETE` marker.
- The fast path can only answer "installed". Everything else asks Playwright as before: a headed run, Firefox and WebKit, an entry with `revisionOverrides`, an unknown platform, any read error, and a shell it does not find. A wrong guess costs the import; it never skips an install.
- Tests run the check in a child process that records whether `playwright-core` was resolved: an installed shell answers without loading Playwright, a missing shell or a headed run asks Playwright with the same verdicts as before, a relative path resolves against `INIT_CWD` and `npm_config_init_cwd`, the per-user default cache is found, and on the machine's real cache the verdict matches `registry.findExecutable('chromium-headless-shell').executablePath()`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

webiny-js e2e suite (standalone project, the five tests that need no license), built CLI, two invocations per run as its CI does (the installation test, then the rest with `--repeat-each 10`), 3 interleaved runs per build, `--debug` phase timings:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `engine.prepare` per invocation | 111-120 ms | 1-2 ms |
| suite wall, median | 18.49 s | 18.15 s (-0.34 s, -1.8%) |

Missing browser still installs: built CLI on `apps/testbed`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` set to an empty temp directory, `tests/check.e2e.ts`:

```text
ℹ Browser download complete.
 ✓ web engine for target "web" prepared 20.07s
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
cache afterwards: chromium_headless_shell-1255  ffmpeg-1013
```

A second run on that cache downloaded nothing and passed. The testbed suite (588) and the web benchmark suite (93) pass on the built packages.

title: fix(engine): wait for a crashed engine server's exit before its connection closes
body: - `spawnTransport` handed the child's stdout straight to the connection (`packages/core/src/engine/protocol/transport.ts`). - When a server exits during a request, its stdout can end before Node delivers the exit and the rest of its stderr. The connection reads both for its message the moment it closes, so the request failed with only `the peer closed the connection`. - That made `engine protocol over a child process > fails a request with the server stderr when the process dies mid-call` flaky. It failed on Node 22 in CI on #1810 ([job](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/43992576748/job/133736626540)) with exactly that message. - Now the connection reads stdout through `untilClosed`, an async generator that ends once the child has closed, or 2 s after stdout ended. The cap covers a server that closes stdout and keeps running, or one whose own child holds its stderr. - A stdout error still reaches the connection: the generator rethrows it as the stream's `error`. - `close()` is unchanged: it still waits for `exit`, not `close`. ```ts yield* stdout; await Promise.race([closed, delay(EXIT_AFTER_STDOUT_MS, undefined, { ref: false })]); ``` ## Issue None filed. Found as a CI flake on #1810. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Built CLI against a scratch project whose target is `connectEngine` with `spawnTransport` on the protocol tests' toy server, made to crash during the test: | Crash | main (25bde7a7) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Closes stdout, then 300 ms later writes stderr and exits 7 | `closed the connection: the peer closed the connection` | `closed the connection: the peer closed the connection; exited with code 7; stderr:` | | Writes stderr, then SIGKILLs itself | `...the peer closed the connection; stderr:` | `...the peer closed the connection; killed by SIGKILL; stderr:` | - Cells are the CLI's `Cleanup` summary line, which ends at `stderr:` on both builds and hides the stderr text that follows. That is a separate display issue, not changed here. The unit tests check that the stderr text is in the message. - New tests in `tests/unit/engine-protocol.test.ts`, each failing on main's transport: - stdout closes before the exit - the server's child writes stderr after the server exited - the server closes stdout and stays up (fails between 1.9 s and 3 s) - the server is stopped by a signal - Mutations each fail a test: waiting for `exit` instead of `close`, the cap alone, no cap, a 7 s cap, ending at once, a 1 s or 3.5 s cap, and the signal status dropped. - The child-process tests pass 10 of 10 runs under 32 busy loops pinned to one CPU. - `pnpm check` passes. `e2e` unit tests: 3822 passed, 2 skipped. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: iOS: a node swipe sends points from window-local bounds when agent-device cannot place the window on screen
body:
### What happened

On iOS, a node swipe (`locator.swipe()`, and a locator-scoped `scrollUntilVisible`) can start and end at the wrong screen points when agent-device cannot place the app's window on the screen. e2e sends the swipe anyway, so the finger lands offset by the window's position and the test fails somewhere later, or passes against the wrong control.

agent-device 0.21.37 (callstack/agent-device#4439) refuses its own ref actions in this state with `window-origin-unknown`, and #1820 maps that refusal to `NOT_ACTIONABLE`. A node swipe never reaches that check, because e2e computes the points from the node's rect and sends them as plain coordinates.

Expected: a node swipe aimed from such a capture fails as `NOT_ACTIONABLE` with nothing sent, the same as a ref tap on it does now.

This was found in review of #1820 ([item 2](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1820#issuecomment-6937444647)).

### Reproduction

No public app repository: this needs an iPad with a placed (Stage Manager) window, iPhone landscape, or an offset root, which no CI device here has. The unit-level reproduction under "Test scenarios" shows the defect with the engine's fake client.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an iOS app in a window that does not start at the screen's (0, 0), for example a placed iPad window. agent-device's capture of such a window was measured at (230, 260) in callstack/agent-device#4573.
2. Call `swipe()` on a locator that resolves to a scrollable node.
3. Expected `NOT_ACTIONABLE` with nothing sent. The swipe is sent at points offset by the window's origin.

### Versions

Code at e2e `613642198b8c6a43abd2bb3152ecedfebb7c8ea5` (main, 2026-11-17). `main` at `a7d79bd0` has no change to the files named here. `@e2e-dev/mobile` pins agent-device 0.21.37. agent-device 0.21.38 (bump: #1859) does not change any of this (see below).

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

### Root cause

1. When agent-device's capture has no reported screen origin (its private viewport evidence is not `reported`), the SDK `capture.snapshot` result leaves out `viewport`. It adds this string to `warnings` (`PublicSnapshotCaptureAnnotations`, `client-port.d.ts`; produced by `runnerSnapshotWarnings` in agent-device's Apple interactor):

   ```
   This snapshot cannot establish the window origin on screen. Coordinate-derived element interactions are unavailable until a capture measures the viewport.
   ```

   The node rects in that capture can be window-local, offset from screen coordinates by the window's position (callstack/agent-device#4439 body; callstack/agent-device#4573). agent-device's CLI help says: "When a fallback cannot establish the screen origin, viewport is omitted and coordinate-derived element actions refuse with window-origin-unknown before input; the snapshot may warn about the unavailable origin."

2. agent-device applies that refusal only to geometry it takes from its own snapshot: refs, selectors, `find`, and the gesture viewport fallback. Points a caller writes go through with no origin check and no warning. `swipe({ from, to })` builds its plan from the runner's native gesture viewport. ADR 0004 in callstack/agent-device#4439: "Independent native queries and authored screen coordinates retain their own authorities." No SDK swipe or scroll takes a ref: `SwipeOptions` is `from`/`to` only.

3. `@e2e-dev/mobile` never reads the `warnings` field of a snapshot. `RawSnapshot` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:142`) picks `nodes`, `viewport`, `truncated`, `appName`, `appBundleId`, `snapshotQuality`, `keyboard`, and `refsGeneration` only. The only `warnings` read in `packages/mobile/src` is `lease/daemon.ts:91`, which is unrelated.

4. The node swipe case in `perform` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1530-1534`) re-reads the control, then sends `client.interactions.swipe({ ...swipeWithin(rect, action.direction, action.momentum), ... })`. `swipeWithin` (`packages/mobile/src/support.ts:165-184`) returns points from the node rect alone. Nothing checks whether the snapshot that supplied the rect established a screen origin.

The missing `viewport` is not the cause. `projectSnapshot` falls back to `viewportOf(raw)` (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts:524`, `678-698`), but the node swipe does not read the viewport.

### Proposed scope

- Keep agent-device's origin warning on the projected snapshot. Add `warnings` to the `RawSnapshot` pick in `surface.ts`. Mark a projected screen as having no screen origin when its `warnings` contain the exact agent-device string above. Keep that string in one exported constant, with a comment that names agent-device 0.21.37 as its source. Match the whole string, not a fragment.
- Use the warning, not a missing `viewport`, as the signal. Snapshots without `viewport` also come from older agent-device builds and from tests: 50 of the 54 golden snapshots under `packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/snapshots/` and the default fake snapshot (`tests/helpers/fake-client.ts:85`, `SETTINGS_SNAPSHOT`) have none. The warning is specific to this state.
- In the `swipe` case of `perform`, after the control is re-read, check the snapshot that supplied the rect passed to `swipeWithin`. If it has no screen origin, throw `EngineError('NOT_ACTIONABLE', …, { retryable: false })` and send nothing. Use `notActionable` if it fits. A retry does not help: the state lasts as long as the window stays where it is.
- Message, in the style of the `window-origin-unknown` hint #1820 added to `NOT_ACTIONABLE_REASONS` in `errors.ts`: `perform swipe failed: the app's window has no known position on the screen, so node bounds, boundingBox() included, may be offset from screen coordinates. Nothing was sent. Swipe the screen with screen.swipe({ direction }), or between screen points with screen.swipe({ from, to }) not taken from those bounds.` Core's `screen.swipe` takes both forms (`packages/core/src/locator/screen.ts:232`).
- The check applies per snapshot, not per session. A later capture without the warning swipes normally.
- Unchanged: ref actions (tap, fill, long press, `dragTo`, and the rest), which agent-device already refuses itself. Root and screen swipes by direction (`interactions.scroll`), which the runner aims itself. Point actions (`performAt`, `screen.tapAt`, `screen.swipe({ from, to })`), where the caller owns the coordinates. Android, where agent-device sends no such warning.
- Add a `.changeset` entry for `@e2e-dev/mobile` (patch) that describes the new failure. No docs page describes the swipe's error classes today, so no docs change is needed.

### Acceptance criteria

- A node swipe whose rect comes from a snapshot with agent-device's origin warning fails with `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `retryable: false`, and the message above. agent-device receives no `interactions.swipe` call.
- The same node swipe on a snapshot without the warning sends the same `from`/`to` points as today.
- A locator-scoped `scrollUntilVisible` on such a snapshot fails the same way, because it goes through the node swipe.
- Ref actions, root swipes, and point actions on the warned snapshot behave as before.
- The warning text lives in one constant, and a unit test uses that constant.

### Test scenarios

All in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts`, beside `re-reads a control before a node swipe too, so the swipe starts from where the control rests` (line 3621). They reuse `harness`, `openAttempt`, `observed(h, 'Scroller')`, `test()`, `SETTINGS_SNAPSHOT`, and `SETTINGS_NODES`.

1. **Refused.** `h.fake.respond('capture.snapshot', () => ({ ...SETTINGS_SNAPSHOT, warnings: [ORIGIN_WARNING] }))`, with no `viewport`. Then `perform(scroller.ref, { kind: 'swipe', direction: 'down' }, test())` rejects with `{ code: 'NOT_ACTIONABLE', retryable: false }` and the message above. `h.fake.methods()` does not contain `interactions.swipe`.
2. **Warning only on the re-read.** The first snapshot has no warning and the re-read before the swipe has it. The swipe is refused, which shows that the snapshot that supplied the rect decides.
3. **Not sticky.** The first re-read carries the warning (refused), and the next capture has none. A second swipe sends `interactions.swipe` with `from`/`to` equal to `swipeWithin(rect, 'down', undefined)` for the Scroller's rect.
4. **Unaffected paths.** On the warned snapshot, `perform(root.ref, { kind: 'swipe', direction: 'down' })` still calls `interactions.scroll`. A ref tap still calls `interactions.press` with the ref; agent-device's own refusal of it is covered in `errors.test.ts`.
5. **Counterfactual.** Scenario 1 without the `warnings` entry sends the swipe. On the current code, scenario 1 sends it too, which is the defect.

### Out of scope

These paths also turn node geometry into screen points. Each needs its own decision, so they are not part of this issue:

- `locator.tap({ position })`: core computes the point from the node's `origin ?? rect` (`locator/engine.ts:540-542`) and calls `performAt`, which cannot tell it from `screen.tapAt`.
- The keyboard dismiss drag (`surface.ts:1695-1708`, `keyboardDragStart` in `keyboard.ts:73-91`) and the simulator typing tip's Continue button (`surface.ts:1732`).
- The agent's point verbs, which clamp to `observation.viewport`. With no `viewport`, that is the size derived by `viewportOf` (core `agent/action-dispatcher.ts`).
- `project()` learning `knownViewport` from a derived size (`surface.ts:1136-1137`).
- Asking agent-device for a structured code instead of the warning string.

title: e2e init says to add `test` to GitLab stages that already list it
body:
### What happened

`e2e init --ci gitlab` warns that the `test` stage is missing from a `.gitlab-ci.yml` that lists it:

```
The e2e jobs run in the test stage; add test to the stages in .gitlab-ci.yml
```

It happens when the `stages:` items are not indented under the key (valid YAML, and what some formatters write), when a comment or blank line sits between the items, or when the list is a flow list over several lines. I expected no warning.

`--ci` is on main and documented but not in a release yet (0.23.1 does not have it), so this needs a build of main.

### Reproduction

No public repository: the bug needs no app, config or test, only the two files the steps below create in an empty directory. I can push them to a repository if you prefer a link.

### Steps to reproduce

In a checkout of main (a7d79bd), after `pnpm install && pnpm build`:

```sh
E2E=$PWD
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q
echo '{"name":"repro","private":true,"type":"module"}' > package.json
printf 'stages:\n- build\n- test\n\nbuild:\n  stage: build\n  script: [make]\n' > .gitlab-ci.yml
node "$E2E/packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js" init --yes --engine web --gateway none --skills none --mcp none --ci gitlab --no-install
```

Actual: the output includes the warning above. Expected: it does not. With `- deploy` in place of `- test` the warning is correct.

### Versions

e2e main at a7d79bd (0.23.1 plus unreleased changes), node 22.23

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

`gitlabStages` in `packages/e2e/src/cli/init/ci.ts` reads the list with a regular expression that needs each item indented and on consecutive lines. I have a small fix that reads it from the parsed YAML instead and can open a PR.

title: fix(cli): read GitLab stages in any YAML layout in e2e init
body: ## What and why - `e2e init --ci gitlab` warned "add test to the stages" for a `.gitlab-ci.yml` that already lists `test`, when the items are not indented under `stages:`, have a comment or blank line between them, or are a flow list over several lines. - `gitlabStages` read the list with a regular expression that only knew two layouts. It now reads the `stages` sequence from the parsed YAML, with the `yaml` package the file already uses (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/ci.ts:149`). - It reads every document in the file, so a pipeline with a `spec:` header above `---` is still checked, as before. - A pipeline without `test` in its stages still gets the warning. ## Issue Fixes #1867 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - CLI, built from each side, in an empty git directory with a `package.json` and this `.gitlab-ci.yml`: ```yaml stages: - build - test build: stage: build script: [make] ``` `node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js init --yes --engine web --gateway none --skills none --mcp none --ci gitlab --no-install` | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `! title: feat(test): add test.skipIf and test.runIf
body:
Adds `test.skipIf(condition)` and `test.runIf(condition)`, the Vitest shape, so a test can skip on a boolean without an `if` around `test()`.

```ts
test.skipIf(process.env.CI)('file watcher', async ({ app }) => { ... });
test.runIf(process.platform === 'linux')('inotify', async ({ app }) => { ... });
```

- An `if` around `test()` hides the test: it is missing from `e2e list` and the report. These register it as skipped instead, so it shows up as `↓ skipped`.
- Both return a function with `test()`'s two call signatures (`TestRegistrar` in `packages/core/src/types.ts`). `runIf(c)` is `skipIf(!c)`.
- `test()`, `skipIf`, and `runIf` share one `registrar` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`, so they parse arguments and register the same way. The condition only sets the existing `skip` option.
- An explicit `skip` option wins. `test.skipIf(false)('x', { skip: 'tracked in #42' }, fn)` still skips, with that reason.
- Inside a serial group both throw `COLLECTION_ERROR` for any condition, like `{ skip }` already does there. A condition-dependent throw would pass on one machine and fail on another, so the fix is `skip` on the serial `describe`.
- A Promise condition is a type error (`SynchronousCondition`, the same guard `SynchronousBody` gives a `describe` body) and a `COLLECTION_ERROR` at runtime. It is always truthy, so `test.runIf(isFeatureOn())` with an async helper would never decide anything. The runtime check reuses `isPromiseLike`, which `describe` already uses.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["test.skipIf(c) / test.runIf(c)"] --> B[shared registrar]
  B --> C{inside a serial group?}
  C -- yes --> D[COLLECTION_ERROR]
  C -- no --> E["set skip, register"]
  E --> F["list and report show it as skipped"]
```

Docs: `docs/reference/test.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. Types are pinned in `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts`, including rejected forms such as `test.skipIf(true, 'reason')` and `test.skipIf(true).skip(...)`.

## Open questions

- Vitest has neither the serial-group rule nor the Promise check. I added both because each one turns a silent wrong result into a collection error. Say if you'd rather match Vitest exactly.
- A function condition, such as `test.skipIf(hasFeature)` with the call forgotten, is also always truthy and still skips silently. I can reject it the same way as a Promise if you want both rules.
- `describe.skipIf` / `describe.runIf` and `.each` chained after `skipIf` are out of scope here.

## Issue

Part of #1855 (Test runner row).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI, a scratch file with `skipIf(isCI)`, `runIf(linux)`, `runIf(win32)`, and `skipIf(false)` plus `{ skip: 'tracked in #42' }`:

```text
$ npx e2e run tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts --config e2e.scratch.config.ts
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > runs on windows only
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > kept reason [tracked in #42]
   ✓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > opens todos locally 547ms
   ✓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > runs on linux only 127ms
      Tests  2 passed | 2 skipped (4)

$ CI=1 npx e2e run tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts --config e2e.scratch.config.ts
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > opens todos locally
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > runs on windows only
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > kept reason [tracked in #42]
   ✓ |web| tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts > runs on linux only 567ms
      Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)

$ npx e2e list tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts --config e2e.scratch.config.ts
tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts › opens todos locally [web]
tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts › runs on linux only [web]
tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts › runs on windows only [web] (skipped: skipped)
tests-scratch/skipif.e2e.ts › kept reason [web] (skipped: tracked in #42)
```

- `test.skipIf(process.env.CI)` inside `describe('checkout', { serial: true }, ...)` fails collection the same way with and without `CI` set (exit 2 both times):

```text
 ERROR  configuration error COLLECTION_ERROR (collection)
tests-scratch/serialskip.e2e.ts: test.skipIf() cannot be used inside a serial group, which skips as one unit; set skip on the serial describe instead
```
- The default testbed suite passes (586 passed, 3 skipped).

title: docs(readme): describe the e2e MCP server
body:
Glama rejected the `e2e` MCP server listing because the README "contains no mention of MCP, Model Context Protocol, MCP tools/resources/prompts". The server ships as `e2e mcp`, but nothing in the README said so.

title: ci(docs): check the japanese docs against deepl
body: ## What and why Gives every translated docs section a second opinion from DeepL, so a mistranslated or stale section gets flagged in review. - `scripts/check-docs-translations-deepl.ts` splits `docs/ja/.mdx` and `docs/.mdx` at their headings, which pair up by position because `check-docs-translations.ts` keeps the outlines equal. For each section a pull request changes, in either language, DeepL translates our Japanese back into English and the English into Japanese. - `scripts/deepl-review.ts` scores both with chrF (character n-grams, so no Japanese tokenizer). A section is flagged when it is far from DeepL in **both** directions, left in English, or missing a glossary term that DeepL's version uses. A correct translation that only words things differently usually stays close in one direction. - The table in `docs/ja/README.md` is uploaded as a DeepL glossary (EN→JA and JA→EN), so DeepL uses our terms (ホスト型ブラウザ, サーバー). It is reused by a content hash, so an unchanged glossary costs nothing. - A section is flagged when both scores are below 0.25. That cut-off comes from the first real run on the site's UI copy: the one real mistranslation scored 0.11 at best, while rewordings scored up to 0.44. - A flag is a warning on the section's heading plus a side-by-side row in the job summary (English, DeepL's English, ours, DeepL's Japanese, scores). Every reviewed section, with its scores, is also uploaded as the `deepl-report` artifact, since GitHub shows only 10 warnings per step. The summary ends with the month's DeepL usage. - It never fails the job on a flag: DeepL is a second opinion, not the source of truth. A used-up monthly quota skips the review with a warning. The job fails only when DeepL can't be reached. - `.github/workflows/docs-translations.yml` runs it on pull requests that touch the docs. It is advisory and not a required check. It needs a `DEEPL_API_KEY` secret (Free plan, `:fx` key); without one, as on a fork, it skips. - Only changed sections are sent. The whole Japanese docs are about 1M characters, which is the Free plan's whole month. A full quickstart is about 8k. - **Fallback.** When DeepL's monthly quota runs out, the same review continues with `openai/gpt-6-luna` on the Vercel AI Gateway (`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, already a repo secret). The model gets the glossary and the です・ます style in its prompt and answers a JSON list, one translation per section. The report and warnings name whoever translated. Without a gateway key, a used-up quota still skips the review with a warning. Stacked on #1875. e2e-inc/e2e-site checks its UI copy the same way. ## Issue ENG-1360 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Fallback, live: with DeepL stubbed to answer 456, `gpt-6-luna` reviewed the 9 quickstart sections in 23 s. Scores ranged from 0.65 to 1.00, and the only flags were 2 glossary ones. - `node --test scripts/deepl-review.test.ts`: chrF, glossary parsing (including the real README's 35 terms), the review rules, MDX section splitting, the real quickstart pairing up section by section, and the DeepL client (glossary created once and then reused, request shape, a 456 error surfaced). - Ran the script against a stubbed DeepL: warnings land on `docs/ja/quickstart.mdx` at each section's heading line, and `--base HEAD` sends nothing. - Ran against the real DeepL API with the repo's key, over every translated section (1,191, before it was limited to changed sections). It worked end to end, and used up the month's quota. - A used-up quota, stubbed with a 456, ends the job with a warning and exit 0. - `pnpm docs:check`, `oxlint scripts/`, and `tsc -p scripts` pass.

title: fix(core): cancel running calls by name when a session closes
body: - Closing an `@e2e-dev/core` session or host while calls still run on it is how a program cancels. Core treated it as a missing `await`, because `launchAttempt` ran the runner's `abandonRunning()` for core sessions too. - Each running step now fails with `CANCELLED` and a message that names it, with the stack of the call. `close()` does not fail for them. - Only a session opened with `cancelsOnClose` takes the new path, which is core's `launch` (`packages/core/src/run/standalone-attempt.ts`). Runner attempts and MCP sessions keep `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`. - `StepRecorder.nameRunning(reason, error)` registers each running step's error right before the abort. A step that failed on its own, or that another abort reached first, keeps that failure. ```ts const open = session.app.open('/slow'); await session.close(); // resolves await open; // CANCELLED: the session closed while app.open "/slow" was running ``` ## Why A nightly report showed a program dying with a bare `E2EError: the session is closed` and blamed a concurrent `launch()` of two engines. Hosts turned out to be independent: the report's script passed 8 of 8 runs here, and a failing mobile launch left a concurrent web session untouched. The trace is what a call left running at session disposal produces, and it named neither the call nor its line. ## For the reviewer to decide A call that nothing awaits rejects unhandled when its session closes, so Node.js ends the program during the close and the host is never disposed. - On main that already happened for calls an `async` method wraps (`waitFor`, `scrollUntilVisible`). - For calls that return the step's own promise (`tap`, `app.open`), main observed the rejection, finished the close, and threw `the test body returned before ... finished` from `close()`. This PR makes them end the program too, with the named error. - Keeping the old behavior for those calls means `close()` fails on every deliberate cancel, Ctrl-C included. - The alternative that keeps teardown is what the runner does: an `unhandledRejection` listener while a host is open. It is a process-wide hook in a library, so it is not in this PR. ## Not in this PR - Reads (`textContent()`, `count()`) and `saveState()` are not steps. One cut mid-flight still fails with `operation cancelled`. - A program with no `finally` and no `await using` around a running call still exits 1 on Ctrl-C without disposing its host, as on main. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Scratch programs on the built packages, `@e2e-dev/web` on Chromium against `https://books.toscrape.com`, each run on main and on this branch. - The new tests in `core.test.ts`, `core-signals.test.ts`, and `step-name-running.test.ts` fail on main and pass here. | Program | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `await using` session, `locator.waitFor()` not awaited | `E2EError: the session is closed` at `Object.closed (launch.js:141)`, exit 1 | `E2EError: the session closed while locator.waitFor "getByText("this text is not on the page") → visible" was running` at `runWeb (signature3.ts:20)`, exit 1 | | `app.open("/")` awaited, `session.close()` called 300 ms in | open: `CANCELLED the session is closed`; close throws `the test body returned before app.open "/" finished; put await in front of every step call` | open: `CANCELLED the session closed while app.open "/" was running`; close resolves | | SIGINT during an awaited `app.open("/")` | stderr `@e2e-dev/core: closing a host on SIGINT failed: closing the host failed: the test body returned before app.open "/" finished; ...`, exit 130 | empty stderr, exit 130 |

title: feat(test): add test.each and test.for
body: Adds `test.each(rows)` and `test.for(rows)`, the Vitest shape: one test per row, titled from the row. ```ts test.each([{ user: 'Ada' }, { user: 'Grace' }])('signs in as $user', async ({ user }, { app }) => { ... }); test.each([[1, 2, 3]])('%i + %i = %i', async (a, b, sum, { app }) => { ... }); test.for([[1, 2]])('pair %i and %i', async ([a, b], { app }) => { ... }); ``` - Titles: `$name` / `$name.path` read an object row; `%s %d %i %f %j %o` take an array row's items in order; `%#` is the index, `%$` the row number, `%%` a percent sign. Formatting is one pass, so a value is never read as a token (`packages/e2e/src/collect/each.ts`). A title is always one line: an `Error` shows as its name and message, not its stack. - `test.each` spreads the rows into the body's args when every row is an array (decided once per table, as Vitest does); `test.for` passes the row whole. The fixtures come last in both. - Fixtures are set up on demand since #1891, from the names a body destructures. A row body takes its row first, so its names are read from the parameter after the row (`fixtureNames(fn, what, source, position)` in `packages/e2e/src/collect/fixture-names.ts`). `(row, fixtures) => {}` and `(...args) => {}` are a `COLLECTION_ERROR`, as `(fixtures) => {}` is for a plain test. - Each row goes through the same registration as `test()` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`), so options (`skip`, tags, timeout), serial groups, and duplicate-title checks work as for a plain test. Every row is located at its `test.each` call, through a helper too: the source location now reads the whole stack, not the default 10 frames. - Empty or non-array rows, and a tagged template table, throw `COLLECTION_ERROR`. - Types: `TestAPI.each` / `TestAPI.for` in `packages/core/src/types.ts`; pinned in `tests/types/sdk-types.ts`, incl. tuple rows typed per position. Out of scope: `describe.each`, and `.each` chained after `skip`/`only`/`skipIf`. ## Issue Part of #1855 (Test runner row). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, scratch file `tests/zz-each.e2e.ts`: object rows and spread rows that fill the real todos page under a `beforeEach`, `test.for`, rows that name no fixture, an `Error` row, and skipped rows. ```text node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-each.e2e.ts ↓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > skipped left [not this one] ↓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > skipped right [not this one] ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > each > adds todo Buy milk 347ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > each > adds todo Walk dog 117ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > each > adds One and Two, 2 todos 127ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > each > adds Three and Four, 2 todos 114ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > each > adds Ship runner (row 1) 102ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > 1 + 2 = 3 3ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > 2 + 3 = 5 4ms ✓ |web| tests/zz-each.e2e.ts > rejects with RangeError: too far 9ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 8 passed | 2 skipped (10) ``` - `e2e list` shows one entry per row with the formatted title. - Failure path: a body that takes the fixtures whole, a rest parameter, and a template table each exit 2 before anything runs. ```text tests/zz-each-bad.e2e.ts:3: test "signs in as Ada" must destructure parameter 2, where it takes the fixtures, as in ({ app, screen }) => {}; it takes "fixtures". e2e sets up only the fixtures a function names there tests/zz-each-bad.e2e.ts:3: test "adds 1 and 2" must destructure parameter 3, where it takes the fixtures, as in ({ app, screen }) => {}; it takes "...numbers". e2e sets up only the fixtures a function names there tests/zz-each-bad.e2e.ts: test.each() takes an array of rows, not a template literal table; write each row as an object or an array ``` ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat: support in-memory file uploads
body:
## What and why

- Accept an in-memory file payload or payload array in `locator.setInputFiles`, preserving paths and empty-array clearing.
- Reject combined payloads of 50 MiB or more as `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; larger files can use paths.
- Keep the original engine action intact. The web engine declares the payload action explicitly and requires `@e2e-dev/core` 0.25.0 or later below 1.0, with the same minimum for its optional `e2e` peer. The SPI v1 action list stays frozen so older engines do not advertise payload support. Include types, migration docs, consumer skill, and changeset.

```ts
await screen.getByLabel('Receipt').setInputFiles({
  name: 'receipt.txt',
  mimeType: 'text/plain',
  buffer: Buffer.from('Receipt total: 12.00'),
});
```

## Issue

Part of #1855, Locators and actions: `locator.setInputFiles({ name, mimeType, buffer })`. Assigned in https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/1855#issuecomment-6951485642.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, macOS arm64, Node 25.8.1.

- Built CLI against the testbed: `e2e run tests/set-input-files.e2e.ts --grep in-memory --video`. Checks filename, MIME type, binary contents, empty files, chooser buttons, and clearing. Recording retained locally: GitHub CLI attachment upload requires upstream write access, unavailable for this fork contribution.
- On `a0974fe4`: `pnpm check`, 194 core/schema tests, 19 web compatibility/upload tests, and all 24 built-CLI upload tests pass. This includes the upstream shadow-DOM event case and oversized-upload recovery.
- Full `pnpm test` and the deterministic web benchmark (93 tests) passed on `a0974fe4`.
- On `313b9f89`: `pnpm check`, 280 core/MCP tests, 60 web unit/integration tests, and 242 mobile tests pass.
- On `a3b65c43`: `pnpm check`, 76 locator tests, and all 24 built-CLI upload tests pass. Fresh-context review found no actionable issues.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  24 passed (24)
```

- On `d2f621ca` with current main: `pnpm check`, 280 focused tests, and all 24 upload tests on the built CLI pass.

Existing path-upload scenarios preserve behavior in the main-versus-branch comparison. Two pairs were measured; timing remains unresolved, with no performance claim.

| Existing path uploads | main | this branch |

| Multiple file input and chooser button | pass | pass |

feat(plugin): ship the Devin plugin manifest
body: Devin's plugin marketplace ([CognitionAI/devin-marketplace](https://github.com/CognitionAI/devin-marketplace)) lists a third-party plugin as a pinned subdirectory of its repo and reads that plugin's `.devin-plugin/plugin.json` for the card and MCP server. `plugins/e2e` had no such manifest, so Devin would fall back to the Claude files and show no short description or logo. - `scripts/sync-plugin.ts` now generates `plugins/e2e/.devin-plugin/plugin.json` from the Codex manifest, like the Claude, Cursor, and Copilot ones, so `pnpm plugins:check` catches drift and `version-packages` keeps the version and the `npx` pin current. - The manifest follows Devin's rules: description without a trailing period (108 chars, they ask for 60–130), `shortDescription` of 40 chars or fewer, `logo` as a path inside the plugin, a category keyword (`Development Tools`), and the MCP server inline. - The plugin README and CONTRIBUTING say how to add it in Devin today (Customize → Plugins → Add plugin → From repository, subdirectory `plugins/e2e`). AGENTS.md notes that the marketplace pins a commit, so a plugin change reaches Devin users only after a PR there bumps the `sha`. - `docs/coding-agents.mdx` waits for the marketplace listing, so the page can give the real install path. ```json { "name": "e2e", "version": "0.23.1", "displayName": "e2e", "description": "Write, run, and debug end-to-end tests for web and mobile apps with e2e, the open source agentic test runner", "shortDescription": "Agentic tests for web & mobile", "homepage": "https://e2e.com", "repository": "https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e", "logo": "assets/logo.png", "keywords": ["Development Tools"], "mcpServers": { "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "e2e@0.23.1", "mcp"] } } } ``` The marketplace entry (`{source: "git-subdir", url: "https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git", path: "plugins/e2e", sha}`) is a follow-up PR to their repo once this merges. ## Issue ENG-1322 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, except installing it in Devin (no `devin` CLI here). - Launched the server exactly as the manifest declares it (`npx -y e2e@0.23.1 mcp`) and did an MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` over stdio. The logo path and all three `skills/*/SKILL.md` resolve inside the plugin. ``` server: { name: 'e2e', title: 'e2e', version: '0.23.1' } tools: open_session, tools, call, close_session, run_tests ``` - Ran Devin's `scripts/validate.py` on a scratch copy of the marketplace: - as the upstream `git-subdir` entry pinned to current main: `ok: 236 entries (227 authored, 9 upstream)`, `--fetch` included. For upstream entries it checks only the entry, not our manifest. - with `plugins/e2e` copied in as an authored plugin, the manifest fields pass. It flags `version` and the `plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, and `mcp.json` files, which are rules for plugins hosted in their repo. Those files serve Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex, and SonarQube's upstream manifest carries `version` too. --- Opened by Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

title: feat(test): add test.fixme
body:
Adds `test.fixme`, Playwright's marker for a test that is known broken, so a ported suite keeps those tests visible as skipped instead of deleting them or rewriting each one as `test.skip`.
Reports carry it as its own skip cause, `fixme`, so a consumer can count known-broken tests apart from tests skipped on purpose.

```ts
test.fixme('exports a PDF', async ({ app }) => {});            // registered skipped, body never runs
test('switches orgs', async ({ platform }) => {
  test.fixme(platform === 'android', 'crashes on Android');   // skips the running test
});
```

## What and why

- `test.fixme` takes exactly the shapes `test.skip` takes: `(title, fn)` at registration, and `()`, `(reason)`, `(condition, reason)` inside a body or `beforeEach`. `test.fixme(false)` does nothing.
- report-v1 gets a new skip cause, `fixme`, beside `explicit` (`packages/e2e/schema/report-v1.schema.json`, `SkipInfo` in `packages/core/src/run/records.ts`). The reason text is `fixme`, or `fixme: <reason>` for a reason that is not blank, so the list, junit, markdown, and HTML output read `[fixme: crashes on Android]` with no reporter change.
- Both producers set the cause: a registered fixme test gets the registration mode `fixme`, which selection turns into the cause (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`), and the runtime forms throw a `RuntimeSkip` carrying the cause from `RUNTIME_SKIP_APIS` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/skip.ts`). A `RuntimeSkip` from an older copy of e2e, which has no cause, reports `explicit`.
- Every consumer that treated `explicit` as a skip the test gave itself now treats `fixme` the same way, through a `SelfSkipCause` type: serial member accounting and Skipped After Failure in core, and the merged report's `executed` count in `@e2e-dev/github` (the pull request comment does not show it). `--last-failed` leaves fixme tests out, as it does explicit ones. `NO_TESTS` counts them as `marked fixme`.
- A `{ skip: 'fixme' }` option, on a test or a group, stays cause `explicit`. Only `test.fixme` sets the cause. The Playwright guide says so in the `test.describe.fixme()` row, and its `test.fixme(title, fn)` row says a serial group takes `skip` on the group instead, where Playwright accepts the registration.
- The runtime forms reuse `skipRunningTest`, which now takes the API name, so a call outside a body or in a setup test names `test.fixme()`, not `test.skip()`. The `test.skip` messages are unchanged and now pinned in `runner-lifecycle.test.ts`.
- The registration form goes through the shared `registrar` and `registerOne` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`), and so does `test.skip(title, fn)` now. In a serial group, each fails with `test.fixme() cannot be used inside a serial group, ...` or `test.skip() cannot be used inside a serial group, ...`, as `skipIf` and `runIf` do. Before, `test.skip` gave the generic `test option "skip" cannot be overridden inside a serial group`.
- `NO_TESTS` used to say `skipped with test.skip` for any explicit skip, including `skipIf` and the `skip` option. It now says `skipped explicitly` (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts`).
- Docs: `docs/reference/test.mdx`, the Playwright guide (moved from "doesn't have yet" to "Map each API"), the `docs/ja` and `docs/zh` copies of both, and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md` with its plugin copy. The docs have no table of skip causes, so the `fixme` cause is documented in the `test.fixme` section. Types are pinned in `packages/e2e/tests/types/sdk-types.ts`, including rejected forms such as `test.fixme(title, options, fn)`.

## Open questions

- An older `@e2e-dev/github` installed beside this `e2e` counts a serial member that marks itself fixme as not executed, as it would for any new cause. I left the peer range alone.
- A test's own reason wins over its group's: `describe('g', { skip: 'tracked in #42' }, () => test.fixme('x', fn))` reports cause `fixme` and reason `fixme`. This is the existing layering in `select.ts`.
- Out of scope, and listed in the Playwright guide's "doesn't have yet" row: `test.describe.fixme` (use `{ skip: 'fixme' }` on the group) and Playwright's `test.fixme(title, details, body)` form, which stops collection with a `COLLECTION_ERROR` here. The `parseModifierCall` falsy-condition fix goes in a separate PR, as agreed.

## Issue

Part of #1855 (Test runner row, `test.fixme('not yet', fn)`).

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI, a scratch file with a registered fixme, a runtime fixme with a reason, a plain `test.skip`, a `{ skip: 'fixme' }` option, and a passing test:

```text
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/fixme-cause.e2e.ts > registered fixme [fixme]
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/fixme-cause.e2e.ts > option fixme [fixme]
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/fixme-cause.e2e.ts > runtime fixme with a reason [fixme: flaky on webkit]
   ↓ |web| tests-scratch/fixme-cause.e2e.ts > plain skip [not here]
   ✓ |web| tests-scratch/fixme-cause.e2e.ts > runs 8ms
      Tests  1 passed | 4 skipped (5)
```

  `report.json` for that run:

```text
["registered fixme"] {"cause":"fixme","reason":"fixme"}
["runtime fixme with a reason"] {"cause":"fixme","reason":"fixme: flaky on webkit"}
["plain skip"] {"cause":"explicit","reason":"not here"}
["option fixme"] {"cause":"explicit","reason":"fixme"}
["runs"] undefined
```
