title: feat(mobile): add device.isKeyboardShown()
body: ## What and why - Adds `device.isKeyboardShown(): Promise` to `@e2e-dev/mobile`, the Appium `isKeyboardShown()` row from the umbrella issue. - It reads one capture (a sparse tree is captured again first) and answers from what agent-device reports for the keyboard, else from visible keyboard elements in the tree: the same band observations hide covered nodes under (`keyboardBand`, `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`). | agent-device keyboard fact | answer | | --- | --- | | `visible`, `derived` | `true` | | `absent` | `false` | | `visibility-only`, `tree-rejected` with `visible` | that `visible` | | `tree-rejected` without `visible` | `true` for a keyboard element drawn on screen. With none, the keyboard is moving: it is captured again briefly, then `ENGINE_FAILURE` (which `expect.poll` retries) | | `unmeasurable`, or no reading | `true` for a keyboard element drawn on screen. With none: `ENGINE_FAILURE` for a sparse or cut tree, else `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Only `absent` (or a hidden probe) answers `false` | - It is a recorded step (`device.isKeyboardShown`), bounded by `actionTimeout`, and changes nothing on the device. It reads the screen as it is now, so after an action that closes the keyboard the docs say to poll it: ```ts await screen.getByTestId('email-input').fill('jane@example.com'); await device.dismissKeyboard(); await expect.poll(() => device.isKeyboardShown()).toBe(false); ``` - `dismissKeyboard()`, and the wait before acting on a control after the keyboard opened or closed, decide whether the keyboard is up by the same rule (`keyboardShownIn` in `packages/mobile/src/keyboard.ts`): a reading that cannot answer means no drag. The dismissing drag starts above the highest keyboard element drawn on screen, suggestion strip included (`keyboardElementsTop`), so a capture that lists only the strip (a hardware keyboard) drags from above it. A keyboard reported up with no frame and no keyboard element on screen gets no drag: `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, since no point is known to be above it. - Docs: `docs/reference/mobile.mdx` (summary row, entry, Throws), the Appium guide row moves from "What e2e doesn't have yet" to "Map each command", and the `ja` and `zh` pages get the new heading and code so their outline still matches. The mobile README lists the method. ## Issue Part of #1855, checklist item `device.isKeyboardShown()` (Device and app). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - iOS 27.2 simulator (iPhone 18 Pro), Xcode 27.2, the built CLI from this branch in a scratch project on Contacts: open a new contact, type a first name, close and discard it, so nothing is saved. ```text on the contact list: false after typing a first name: true after discarding the form: true after discarding the form: true after discarding the form: true after discarding the form: true after discarding the form: true after discarding the form: false ✓ |ios| keyboard.e2e.ts > isKeyboardShown follows the soft keyboard on a new contact form 27.18s Tests 1 passed (1) ``` The `true` reads after the discard are real: the sheet and the keyboard animate out for about 2.5 s on that machine. - A second run passed the same way. On this simulator agent-device reports `tree-rejected` without `visible` right after `fill`, while the keyboard slides in. Such a reading is now captured again until the keyboard lands. - The same check in Safari (address bar, then `dismissKeyboard()`) read `false`, `true`, `false` on an earlier build. - `apps/mobile-benchmark/tests/device.e2e.ts` on the iOS 27.2 simulator, with the benchmark app built after #1898: the new keyboard test and both onboarding tests pass, twice. `isKeyboardShown` polling read 4 settling captures before `true`, and the phone step dismisses. That run also carried the separate iOS 27 toolbar fix for `dismissKeyboard`, which comes as its own PR; without it, iOS 27 refuses the first drag. Some runs failed earlier, reading the home list, while the Mac's load average was 30 to 200. Android was not run locally. The Android emulator in CI draws no soft keyboard, even for a tapped field, so the keyboard reads are their own iOS-only test (`isKeyboardShown follows the keyboard up and through a dismissal`), and the onboarding test is unchanged from main. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed (`packages/mobile/dist/device.d.ts`). `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` covers `e2e`, not the mobile `Device` interface, so it is unchanged; no wire change. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: mobile-benchmark (Expo SDK 57) crashes at launch on iOS 27: no scene lifecycle
body:
### What happened

On iOS 27 the mobile benchmark app (`apps/mobile-benchmark`, Expo SDK 57) crashes at launch with `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP` when built with Xcode 27.2. Every iOS test then fails before it reaches its scenario, with `ENGINE_FAILURE: snapshot failed: app 'dev.e2e.benchmark' is not running` or a timeout on the home list.

Crashing thread:

```text
0 UIKitCore           ___UIApplicationEvaluateRuntimeIssueForNoSceneLifecycleAdoption_block_invoke
1 libdispatch.dylib   _dispatch_client_callout
2 libdispatch.dylib   _dispatch_once_callout
3 UIKitCore           -[UIApplication workspace:didCreateScene:withTransitionContext:completion:]
4 UIKitCore           -[UIApplicationSceneClientAgent scene:didInitializeWithEvent:completion:]
```

iOS 27 asserts at launch unless the app adopts the scene-based life cycle. The SDK 57 prebuild template (`expo-template-bare-minimum@57.0.35`) still starts React Native into a `UIWindow` from `AppDelegate`, and the built `Info.plist` has no `UIApplicationSceneManifest`. The SDK 58 template (`58.0.35`) adds:

- `SceneDelegate.swift`: `class SceneDelegate: ExpoAppSceneDelegate {}`
- `UIApplicationSceneManifest` in `Info.plist`, pointing at `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).SceneDelegate`
- `AppDelegate: ExpoAppDelegate, ExpoReactNativeFactoryProvider`, with no window of its own

`ExpoAppSceneDelegate` already ships in `expo@57.0.33`; only the SDK 57 template does not use it.

Also affected: `examples/with-expo` (`expo` ~57.0.26), which the nightly examples job runs.

CI is not affected yet: `mobile.yml` runs on `macos-26` with the default Xcode and pins the iOS 26.5 runtime. It breaks once the runner's default Xcode or the pinned runtime moves to 27. I could not check whether an app built with the iOS 26 SDK also crashes on the iOS 27 runtime, since this Mac only has Xcode 27.2.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/tree/main/apps/mobile-benchmark

### Steps to reproduce

In this repository, with Xcode 27.2 and an iOS 27.2 simulator booted:

1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
2. `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/mobile-benchmark ios`
3. The app exits at launch; the crash report is `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/e2eBenchmark-*.ips`.

The same crash in a blank Expo app, with SDK 58 as the control (`./repro.sh <simulator-udid>`):

```zsh
#!/bin/zsh
# A blank Expo app on SDK 57 crashes at launch on iOS 27; the same app on SDK 58 runs.
set -u
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8 LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 CI=1   # CocoaPods 1.17 on Ruby 4 fails without a UTF-8 locale
UDID="$1"
for v in 57 58; do
  npx --yes create-expo-app@latest sdk$v --template blank-typescript@sdk-$v >/dev/null
  (cd sdk$v && npx expo prebuild -p ios --clean >/dev/null && npx expo run:ios --device "$UDID" --configuration Release --no-bundler >/dev/null)
  xcrun simctl terminate "$UDID" com.anonymous.sdk$v >/dev/null 2>&1
  xcrun simctl launch "$UDID" com.anonymous.sdk$v >/dev/null; sleep 8
  if xcrun simctl spawn "$UDID" launchctl list | grep -q "UIKitApplication:com.anonymous.sdk$v"; then echo "sdk-$v: running"; else echo "sdk-$v: not running"; fi
done
```

| | expo | `DTSDKName` | `UIApplicationSceneManifest` | launch on iOS 27.2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sdk-57 | 57.0.33 | `iphonesimulator27.2` | absent | `SIGTRAP`, the stack above |
| sdk-58 | 58.0.26 | `iphonesimulator27.2` | present | runs |

A native SwiftUI app (`@main App`) built with the same SDK runs on the same simulator, as expected.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.7 (main at 4bff6fc6), Node 24.14.1, Xcode 27.2 (27B52), iOS 27.2 simulator runtime, CocoaPods 1.17.0

### Engine

@e2e-dev/mobile

### Anything else

Possible fix: move `apps/mobile-benchmark` and `examples/with-expo` to Expo SDK 58, whose prebuild adopts scenes. Or, on SDK 57, a config plugin that writes the SDK 58 `SceneDelegate`, the `Info.plist` entry, and the `AppDelegate` change. Moving the benchmark means rebuilding the cached Expo app and re-recording its iOS entries under `apps/mobile-benchmark/.e2e/cache/`.

Found while working on #1893.

title: `test.skip()` in an `afterEach` hook or fixture teardown fails the test with `ERROR: [object Object]`
body:
### What happened

Calling `test.skip(true, reason)` from an `afterEach` hook fails a test that passed, with code `ERROR` and the message `[object Object]`:

```text
   × |web| tests/late-skip.e2e.ts > passes 504ms
     → [object Object]
 FAIL  |web| tests/late-skip.e2e.ts > passes
ERROR: [object Object]
```

The same skip in a `test.extend()` fixture's teardown does the same. If the body had already failed, the skip adds a second `ERROR: [object Object]` to the attempt's secondary errors. Through `e2e mcp`, `close_session` prints `Cleanup (afterEach): ERROR: [object Object]`.

A skip there isn't supported (the Playwright guide says the conditional skip works in a test body or a `beforeEach` hook), so I expected a refusal like the one `test.fail()` gets in the same place: `INVALID_ARGUMENT: test.fail() cannot mark a test from an afterEach hook or a fixture teardown: its verdict is already reached`.

The teardown loops in `run/execute.ts` and `run/standalone-test.ts` hand the skip signal to `recordFailure` without the `isRuntimeSkip` check the body path has, so the signal object is stringified.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/skip-in-after-each

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`
3. Expected an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the cause, like a late `test.fail()`. Got `ERROR: [object Object]` and exit code 1.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0, node 22.23.4 (also on main)

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

Happy to send a PR: turn the skip signal into an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` in both teardown catches, with an integration test and a row under `test.skip`'s Throws table in `docs/reference/test.mdx`.

title: `@e2e-dev/html-reporter` overwrites `report.html` when a run stops before its tests
body:
### What happened

When a run stops before its tests start, e2e leaves the previous run's files in place, but `htmlReporter()` still writes `report.html`. The page is replaced with one that shows no tests and the run error, while `report.json`, `junit.xml`, and `summary.md` beside it still belong to the previous run. The terminal says the report was not written, then names the HTML report on the next line:

```text
 ERROR  configuration error NO_TESTS (collection)
1 tests were collected but none is runnable: 1 have titles matching none of /nomatch/; pass --pass-with-no-tests to allow this
 Test Files  no test files
      Tests  no tests executed
     Errors  1 error
     Report  (not written)
HTML report  .e2e/report.html
```

Checksums across that run: `report.html` changed, and `report.json`, `junit.xml`, and `summary.md` did not. `--last-failed` after a green run does the same. The page for the last run that actually ran is lost, and nothing rebuilds it from `report.json`.

`docs/reference/cli.mdx` (run, Output) says: "A run that stops before its tests writes none of them and leaves the previous run's files in place. That covers a config or collection error, `NO_TESTS`, `NO_LAST_RUN`, `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT`, an app command that fails to start, and an interrupt."

`writeReport` in `packages/html-reporter/src/reporter.ts` doesn't check `run.reportPath`, while the built-in `junit` and `markdown` reporters return early when it is undefined (`report/write.ts`, `report/markdown.ts`). The `FinishedRun` docs say `reportPath` is absent "when the write failed", but it is also absent whenever the run stops before its tests.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Asheesh7298/e2e-repros/tree/main/html-report-overwrite

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npx e2e run`. `.e2e/report.html` shows the test.
3. `npx e2e run --grep nomatch`. Exit code 2, `NO_TESTS`, `Report  (not written)`.
4. `.e2e/report.html` now shows no tests. Expected the page from step 2 to stay, as `junit.xml` and `summary.md` do, with no `HTML report` row printed.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0, @e2e-dev/html-reporter 0.0.1, node 22.23.4 (also on main)

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

Happy to send a PR: return early from `writeReport` when `run.reportPath` is undefined, with a unit test and a fix to the `reportPath` comment in `docs/reference/reporters.mdx`.

title: fix(mobile-benchmark): adopt UIKit scenes so the app launches on iOS 27
body: ## Issue Fixes #1894 ## What changed - `apps/mobile-benchmark/app.json` turns on `expo-build-properties`' `ios.enableSceneSupport`, Expo's own SDK 57 switch for the UIKit scene lifecycle. `expo-build-properties` is pinned at `57.0.23`, the version `expo@57.0.33`'s `bundledNativeModules.json` names. - On prebuild it rewrites the template `AppDelegate` to `ExpoAppDelegate, ExpoReactNativeFactoryProvider` with no window of its own, and adds a `UIApplicationSceneManifest` that names `EXExpoAppSceneDelegate` (shipped in `expo@57.0.33`). The SDK 58 template has the same shape. - No custom config plugin: Expo maintains this one, and on SDK 58 it only warns that the option is no longer needed. - The README says why the option is there, how to regenerate an `ios/` prebuilt before this change (`expo run:ios` does not re-prebuild an existing one), and to remove the plugin entry and dependency on SDK 58. - `examples/with-expo` needs no change: its `app.json` has had the same option since #856. A scratch prebuild of it (expo 57.0.33, expo-build-properties 57.0.23) produces the same AppDelegate and scene manifest. I did not build or run it, so its README "Last checked" line is unchanged. - No changeset: `@e2e-dev/mobile-benchmark` is private. - CI: the native fingerprint changes (`expoConfig`), so `mobile.yml` misses the Expo cache once and rebuilds the app on both platforms. The Android mods in `expo-build-properties` are no-ops without `android` props. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, the built CLI on the mobile benchmark, Xcode 27.2 (27B52), an iPhone 18 Pro simulator on iOS 27.2. This Mac has no iOS 26 runtime, so CI's iOS 26.5 job is the check there. Android was not run locally. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `Info.plist` `UIApplicationSceneManifest` | absent | `EXExpoAppSceneDelegate` | | launch on iOS 27.2 | `exited due to SIGTRAP ... ran for 5047ms` (`_UIApplicationEvaluateRuntimeIssueForNoSceneLifecycleAdoption`) | runs, home list shown | | `e2e run --target ios-simulator` (59 tests) | every test fails: the app is not running | 44 passed, 14 failed, 1 skipped | Deep links, which now reach JS through the scene delegate: - Warm: from Control Inventory, `simctl openurl e2e-benchmark://login-form` pushes Login Form. - Cold: with the app terminated, `simctl openurl e2e-benchmark://gestures` launches straight into Gestures, over Benchmark Examples. - `tests/device-fixture.e2e.ts` "openLink opens the scenario a deep link names" passed in the last full run. What the 14 failures are, and why I read them as not caused by this change: - 11 are `ACTION_FAILED: operation timed out` on a screen read, mostly the first read after opening a scenario ("expect gave up after 0 reads in 5.0s"). The screen at failure shows the expected node. The Mac was running an Android emulator and Gradle builds (load average 8 to 27), and a different set of tests failed in each of three runs: 18, then 14, with `openLink` failing in one and passing in the other. - `refusals › a missing locator fails as not found` got `ACTION_FAILED` where it expects `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`: the same read timeout. - `sequential onboarding echoes the exact values` and `onboarding rejects a malformed email` fail every run with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: keyboard dismissal failed: the keyboard has no dismiss key`. That is the engine against iOS 27's keyboard, not the app, and it is out of scope here. `dismissing the keyboard over choice controls` failed the same way in the previous run, and on a read timeout in this one. There is no main baseline on iOS 27 to compare the failures against, since main does not launch there. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: refactor(run): refactor the --step hold logic
body:
## What and why

This reworks `--step` holds to add `screen.pause()` in the next branch. Existing `e2e run --step` behavior stays the same.

1. The `beforeStep` run option is now `hold.ask`, and `hold.steps` says whether we hold steps.
   **Why:** On `main`, passing the hook also held every step. To handle `screen.pause()` later, we'll need the hook without holding steps.
2. `heldScreens` and `HeldStep.screen` are gone. The hold handler calls `context.readScreen()` when it needs the screen, and the runner asks the worker for it.
   **Why:** We used to decide up front whether to read the screen at every hold. Now we read it only when the code answering the hold needs it.
3. The worker option changed from `'hold' | 'screen' | undefined` to `holdSteps: boolean`.
   **Why:** After item 2, the worker only needs to know whether to hold steps.
4. `HeldStep` and `StepHoldRequest` now have a `kind` field. It's always `'step'` in this branch.
   **Why:** The next branch adds `'pause'`.
5. We still ignore a key pressed within 150 ms of a prompt. We now skip that guard per socket command, rather than when we create the gate.
   **Why:** In the next branch, one gate will handle both keys and commands. Keys need the guard, but commands don't.
6. We extracted socket request handling and replies from `serveSteps` into `commandServer` and `answerWaiting`.
   **Why:** The server for pauses needs both in the next branch, so we can reuse them.
7. We moved `stepAddress` and `parseLine` from `cli/step-control.ts` to `run/step-socket.ts` without changing them.
   **Why:** The MCP code will need the socket path later. It won't need to import a CLI module.
8. We moved `fakeStdin()` from the watch unit test to `tests/helpers/fake-stdin.ts`.
   **Why:** The pause tests use it in the next branch.

title: feat(cli): pause at screen.pause() under --watch
body:
<!--
Title: Conventional Commits, `!` for a breaking change. It becomes the squash commit.
Body: a few bullets on what and why, then evidence (code, diagram, before/after).
See .dev/skills/writing-pr/SKILL.md. No history; run output only as `## Verified` evidence.
-->

## What and why

This adds `--watch` support for `screen.pause`.

Under `e2e run --watch`, a test is now paused at each `screen.pause()` on every run, as in `e2e run`.

While a pause is shown, the keys are read by the pause prompt and not by watch mode:

title: docs: say that --no-cache calls the model instead of replaying cached actions
body:
The quickstart said "Add `--no-cache` to skip cached actions". That reads as if the agent steps don't run. They do run: with the replay cache off, each `agent.act` step calls the model instead of replaying its recording.

- `docs/quickstart.mdx`: "Add `--no-cache` to call the model instead of replaying cached actions."
- `docs/ja/quickstart.mdx` and `docs/zh/quickstart.mdx`: the same sentence, translated. The old Japanese 「キャッシュを使わずに操作させる」 and Chinese 「跳过缓存的操作」 carried the same ambiguity.
- `context7.json`: the rule agents read had the same "skip cached actions" wording.
- `docs/ja/quickstart.mdx` also ends three sentences in the polite request form (〜してください), as a Japanese-speaking reader asked:
  - the `--headed` sentence next to the `--no-cache` one, so the two parallel "Add ..." sentences read the same
  - the example prompt 「購入手続きのテストを追加してください」

The behavior is in `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:474` (`noCache` sets the mode to `'off'`), `packages/core/src/cache/context.ts:261` (no cache context when off), and `packages/core/src/agent/act.ts:269` (no cache means the step goes to the executor live).

title: Replay cache keeps CJK counts followed by a particle (42件を表示) as anchors
body:
### What happened

Since #1837, the replay cache reads `42件` and `42개의 결과` as counts. A count followed by a subject or object particle is still kept as an anchor: `42件を表示`, `42件が見つかりました`, `42건이 검색되었습니다`, `42개를 선택`.

The word-end lookahead in `COUNT_TEXT` (`cache/anchors`) allows `の`, `中` and `의` after the counter, but not `を`, `が`, `は`, `も`, `이`, `가`, `을` or `를`. A tally like `42件を表示` that grows with every run is recorded as an end anchor. The next run reads `43件を表示`, so `deltaMismatch` reports it missing, the same way `42件` did before #1837.

okwasniewski raised this as a follow-up in the last review on #1837.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Toraastrta/e2e-cjk-particle-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run repro`
3. Expected `42件を表示` to be dropped like `42件`, recording only `追加しました`. Instead it is recorded too, and the next run (`43件を表示`) reports it missing. The README shows the full output.

The script calls `describeDelta` and `deltaMismatch` from `@e2e-dev/core` in `e2e@0.23.2-nightly-20261118030221`, which includes #1837.

### Versions

e2e 0.23.2-nightly-20261118030221, node 22.22.3

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

I have a fix ready that adds these particles to the lookahead (leaving out `で`, since `3行で書く` is not a count) and can open a PR.

title: fix(cache): read CJK counts followed by を, が, 이 or 를 as counts
body:
## What and why

- A CJK count followed by a particle (`42件を表示`, `42건이 검색되었습니다`) was kept as an anchor, so a growing tally made the next replay stale.
- Adds `を`, `が`, `は`, `も`, `이`, `가`, `을`, `를`, `은`, `는` and `도` to the word-end lookahead in `COUNT_TEXT`, as okwasniewski suggested on #1837. `で` stays out, since `3行で書く` is not a count.
- A Korean particle only counts when no Hangul follows it, so `2024 개도국 지원` stays an anchor.
- Adds count cases for the parts of the lookahead that no test needed: the non-letter branch, `記錄`, `記録`, `结果` and `結果`. `中` gets its own case (`全41件中`), since `全9件中 1〜9件を表示` now also matches through `を`.

title: feat(test): change the running test's timeout with test.setTimeout
body: ## What and why - `test.setTimeout(timeout)` changes the running test's timeout from its body or a `beforeEach` hook, as Playwright's does. The new timeout counts from the start of the attempt, like the `{ timeout }` option it replaces for that attempt. A retry starts from the option again. - A timeout shorter than the time already spent times the test out at once. - In a `beforeAll` hook, it changes that hook's own timeout (the config `timeout`), counted from the hook's start. The tests keep their own. The worker fixtures the hook sets up and the device calls it makes run on the changed timeout too. - `afterEach` and `afterAll` hooks, test fixture teardowns, and worker fixture teardowns run on `cleanupTimeout`, so a call there is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. So is a value that isn't a positive safe integer up to `MAX_TIMER_MS` (the option's own rule), a call from a hosted session (`host.openSession`), and a call from code that a test or hook left running after it ended. A call outside a running test or hook is `COLLECTION_ERROR`, pointing at the option. ```ts test('imports a large file', async ({ app }) => { test.setTimeout(180_000); await app.open('/import'); }); ``` How it works: - `AttemptTimeout` (`packages/core/src/run/budget.ts`) owns the timeout one attempt or one `beforeAll` hook runs on. Both executors (`execute.ts`, `standalone-test.ts`) and `SuiteAttempt.within` build one. - `set(ms)` moves the `AttemptBudget` deadline by the difference (`shiftDeadline`). Operations, `--step` holds, `screen.pause()`, and the body race all read that deadline. - `race(work, onTimeout)` replaces the fixed `withTimeout` and reads the deadline again when it moves or the clock starts. - `stop()`, `refill()`, and `start()` stop the clock while a step is held or paused. `AttemptHolds` only calls them. - Once the race settles, `set` returns `false`, so code left running cannot move the timeout or the watchdog. - The published attempt gets a `setTimeout` hook beside `expectFailure`. A `beforeAll` hook is named through a `globalThis` slot (`inSuiteHook`, `packages/core/src/internal/test-timeout.ts`). - The worker announces the new timeout and what is left, so the scheduler's watchdog follows it and names it if it kills a blocked worker. - `e2e mcp` test runs take it too. ## Issue Part of #1855, item `test.setTimeout(60_000)` under Test runner. @okwasniewski ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, through the real runner (in-process, worker processes, and `e2e mcp`). - `tests/integration/test-set-timeout.test.ts`: raised and lowered from a body and a `beforeEach`; lowered below the time spent; a raised and a lowered `beforeAll`; a `beforeAll` on a `worker`-isolation engine whose device calls get the raised budget; refusals from `afterEach`, `afterAll`, a worker fixture teardown, bad values, and a call at collection; and a worker that blocks its event loop after a raise, which the watchdog kills past the new timeout. - `tests/integration/mcp-test-run.test.ts`: a lowered and a raised timeout in an `e2e mcp` test run. - `tests/integration/open-host-deadline.test.ts`: the hosted-session message. - `tests/unit/step-hold.test.ts`: `AttemptTimeout` lowered below the time spent, raised, moved while a step is held or `screen.pause()` waits, the release that announces it, and the refusal once the race settled. - Mutation checks, each on rebuilt `dist`: removing the deadline re-check in `set`, the watchdog announcement, the `e2e mcp` hook, the `ended` guard, the `beforeAll` timeout on the attempt's budget, or the `inSuiteHook` wrapper on worker fixture teardowns fails a test above. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. Japanese and Chinese pages carry the new section and migration rows. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(web): match route and waitForResponse by method
body:
## Issue

Part of #1855, the `browser.route({ method: 'POST', url: '**/api/orders' }, handler)` row under "Network and navigation".

## What changed

`browser.route`, `browser.unroute`, and `browser.waitForResponse` accept a `{ method, url }` pattern. A string or `RegExp` pattern keeps its current behavior.

```ts
await browser.route({ method: 'POST', url: '**/api/orders' }, (route) =>
  route.fulfill({ status: 201, json: { id: 42 } }));

const created = await browser.waitForResponse({ method: 'POST', url: '**/api/orders' });
```

- `method` is one HTTP method, case-insensitive, validated as an HTTP token.
- `url` keeps the existing glob or `RegExp` grammar.
- A route whose method does not match calls `route.fallback()`, so older routes, the configured headers, and the network still see the request.
- `unroute` removes routes registered with the same pattern, method included.
- Exports `RouteMatcher` from `@e2e-dev/web` and `@e2e-dev/web/engine`.
- Updates the web reference in English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese, the Cypress and Playwright migration pages, and the packaged skill and plugin copy. Adds a patch changeset for `@e2e-dev/web`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `pnpm test:testbed` through the built CLI: 586 passed, 3 skipped.
- A temporary testbed test of the new API through the built CLI: `POST` was fulfilled, `GET` reached the real server, and `waitForResponse({ method: 'GET' })` resolved. A second temporary test confirmed the step labels `browser.route POST "**/api/users"` and `browser.unroute POST "**/api/users"` in the report. Both were removed.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web run test`: 880 passed, 1 skipped across 82 files.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/integration/routes.test.ts tests/unit/route-pattern.test.ts`: 86 passed.
- `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: 93 passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed.

title: feat(test): add test.describe.fail and the fail option on describe
body: ## What and why - Closes the `test.describe.fail('legacy', fn)` row of #1855: mark every test in a group expected to fail. - `describe` now takes the `fail` option, the way it already takes `skip`. `describe.fail(title, fn)` is shorthand for `fail: true`, as `test.fail(title, fn)` is for a test. A reason goes in the option. - A test reads `fail` from its groups as well as itself (`packages/e2e/src/collect/select.ts:165`). Any truthy layer marks it and the innermost reason wins. `fail: false` does not unmark, same as `skip`. - Each test is still judged on its own: a failure passes it, a pass fails it with `UNEXPECTED_PASS`. - Refused on, inside, or around a serial group, since a serial member cannot be marked. ```ts describe.fail('legacy checkout', () => { test('pays by card', async ({ app, browser }) => {}); // expected to fail }); describe('legacy refunds', { fail: 'refund API not ported yet' }, () => {}); ``` ## Issue Part of #1855 (Test runner: `test.describe.fail('legacy', fn)`). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes A small page in Chromium through the built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`): the legacy card payment is broken, the coupon was fixed, refunds were never ported. ``` ✓ |web| tests/checkout.e2e.ts > legacy checkout > pays by card (failed as expected) 2.45s → expected to fail: ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed × |web| tests/checkout.e2e.ts > legacy checkout > applies a coupon 131ms → test is marked test.fail ("expected to fail") but passed; remove the mar… ✓ |web| tests/checkout.e2e.ts > legacy refunds > refunds an order (failed as expected) 2.16s → refund API not ported yet: ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveText failed ✓ |web| tests/checkout.e2e.ts > modern checkout pays 123ms ``` - Exit code 1 from the unexpected pass. `report.json` carries each result's `expectedFailure` reason, and none on the test outside the groups. - A serial group inside `describe.fail` stops the run before anything executes (exit 2): `a serial group cannot sit inside a group marked fail; its members cannot be expected to fail`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; title: docs: show how to connect e2e mcp to OpenCode
body: Our setup docs cover Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, but not OpenCode. OpenCode can't install the e2e plugin, and its MCP config uses a different shape from `mcpServers`, so an OpenCode user had no entry they could copy. The skill also sent agents to formats OpenCode ignores. - `docs/mcp-server.mdx`: an OpenCode tab in "Set it up" with the project `opencode.json` entry, and `opencode mcp list` as the check. OpenCode's unreleased `dev` branch moves servers to `mcp.servers.` and makes `mcp add` write the project config, so both lines need another look when that ships. Refs ENG-1317 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, with OpenCode 1.19.6 and `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, in a project from `e2e init --example with-vite` on e2e 0.23.1. - Skills: `opencode debug skill` lists `e2e`, `create-verification-skill`, and `migrate-to-e2e` from `.agents/skills/` (after `init` or `npx skills add e2e-inc/e2e`), and from the plugin's `skills/` folder. - MCP: with the entry above, `opencode mcp list` shows `✓ e2e connected`. - Full flow: `opencode run` loaded the skill, opened a session through the MCP server, typed a name, tapped the button, and checked the greeting with `run_code`. It then wrote `tests/grace.e2e.ts` from the returned test lines, ran it with `run_tests` (passed), and closed the session. `npx e2e run tests/grace.e2e.ts` passed on its own afterwards. - Skill change: in a fresh project with this branch's skill and no server registered, an OpenCode agent asked to set up the server wrote the project `opencode.json` and got `✓ e2e connected`. The global config held only OpenCode's empty default. The agent also read the first scratch project's `opencode.json` along the way, so this run doesn't isolate the skill text alone. - Docs: `pnpm docs:check` and `pnpm check` pass. title: chore(skills): add translation viewer, review, and terms skills
body:
## What and why

- Four repo-only skills for working on docs translations, plus `docs/es/Terms.md`, the first per-language glossary they use.
- The docs checks warn when a registered locale's outline, code blocks, or labels drift from English. They cannot see a dropped list item, a cut-short section, or a term translated three ways, and they only know the locales listed in the check scripts. These skills cover that, for any locale folder.

### Terms.md

`docs/<locale>/Terms.md` is the one place where the "special" words of a language are decided: how `agent`, `fixture`, `flag`, or `test suite` are written, or that a word stays in English.

- Whichever agent or person translates, they follow the same table, so a page written today and one written in six months use the same word.
- Maintainers get a single source of truth for a locale. A wording argument is settled once, in one row, instead of page by page in review.
- It stops over-translating technical terms. `fixture`, `worker`, `prompt`, and `end-to-end` stay in English because that is what developers read and type. A row can say so, with a note.
- A row lists accepted forms (`agente / agentes`), so plurals and verb forms are not flagged. The first form is preferred.
- It is checked, not just documented: `translation-review` warns when a section uses a term the table says is written another way, and the viewer hands the section's rows to the model and to the fix prompt.

`docs/es/Terms.md` has 73 rows.

### The skills

- `translation-review`: no model, same result each run. Per section it reports missing links, list items, table rows, components, prose left in English or cut short, and terms that drifted from `Terms.md`. Errors exit 1.
- `translation-viewer`: a local page with a file tree and English beside the translation. It also runs an external review with Chrome's built-in AI (Gemini Nano). The model is small and not perfect, but it is one most maintainers already have in their browser: no API key, no cost, nothing leaves the machine. It gives a second read from a model that did not write the translation, and findings whose quote is not on the page are dropped. Each finding has a Get prompt button that copies a fix prompt for a coding session, with the section's terms in it.
- `terms-add`: turns "X is Y in <language>" into a sorted row of `Terms.md`, and lists the pages that now disagree.
- `terms-find`: Microsoft has translated its documentation and products into dozens of languages for decades, long before AI translation, with professional translators and a maintained terminology. We rely on that work to check common terms. It looks the term up in Microsoft's Terminology Search in the browser, with a script over Microsoft Learn and MDN as a fallback. Microsoft's usage is a reference, not a rule: `Terms.md` decides.
- A folder under `docs/` counts as a locale when it has `navigation.json` or `Terms.md`, so these work before a language's first translation PR merges.

## Issue

Part of #1890.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `review.mjs es` on the nine Spanish pages (separate PR): 0 errors, 18 warnings. Deleting a list item from `web.mdx` produced the list-item error. On this branch alone, with only `Terms.md`, it reports the nine pages as not translated.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `oxlint .dev/skills`, and `pnpm plugins:check` pass on this branch.
- Review round: fixed the quote filter's whitespace bug, the viewer's stale-state and local-access checks, `terms.mjs` argument and row-loss handling (plus `init`), CJK, multiline-tag, `href`, and hyphenated-term handling in the review, and `terms-find`'s term escaping and rate-limit reporting. The review script then found a sentence of `mobile.mdx` that had gone stale against `main`, fixed in the Spanish PR.
- `terms.mjs add` and `list`: inserted, updated, and restored a row.
- Viewer: the server's endpoints and the page ran in desktop Chrome, and Get prompt copied prompts with the section's terms. The quote filter was not run in Chrome.
- `terms-find` against Microsoft's Terminology Search for about 45 Spanish terms.

Known limits:

- Chrome's model is small. Most findings I checked were wrong or already correct, so treat them as leads.
- The viewer asks the model for English only. Only Spanish has been run; other languages read side by side but get a weaker or refused review.
- Microsoft Learn rate-limits the fallback script after a few hundred requests in a row.

## Checklist

- [x] No changeset: docs and repo skills only, nothing in a published package.
- [x] Docs: no `docs/**/*.mdx` page describes behavior that changed.

title: A one-time code typed one digit per box replays the previous run's code
body:
### What happened When an agent step types a one-time code into six one-digit boxes, the replay cache saves the digits as normal input. The next run types the old code into a page that issued a new one. `derivedReason` from 0.23.1, given what the step saw (`Your code is 482913`), per typed value: ```text whole code 482913 -> minted-token box 1 digit 4 -> undefined box 2 digit 8 -> undefined ... box 6 digit 3 -> undefined ``` The [cache docs](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/847a09e6dbd39e09c8941ddcc903003c61412d81/docs/cache.mdx#L282-L288) say a value the agent read off the screen is a gap. That holds for the whole code, but not for one digit at a time. The check runs per typed value, and a single digit is neither a whole node nor a word of "Your code is 482913": https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/847a09e6dbd39e09c8941ddcc903003c61412d81/packages/core/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts#L767-L774 What this does on the next run: - the replay sends the old code, the page answers "Incorrect code", and the step hands off (`agent-concluded`, `end-mismatch`) - the replay saves nothing, since the agent still has to do the step - a real app counts a failed code attempt on every run, which can lock the account The web benchmark already has this exact scenario (six one-digit boxes, [`otp-auto-advance`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/847a09e6dbd39e09c8941ddcc903003c61412d81/apps/web-benchmark/app/src/Examples/OtpAutoAdvance.tsx#L11)), but its code never changes, so the old code happens to be right. I hit this in my own app, on a delete confirmation that emails a code. It's not related to #1789, and it's still on nightly. Expected: a value typed into an `autocomplete="one-time-code"` box is a gap, so the replay hands off before it. ### Reproduction https://github.com/yehomak/e2e-otp-repro (npm run check is deterministic; the e2e test needs agent.act, since only agent steps are cached. Model: gemini-flash-lite-latest, or any via AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY) ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npm install` 2. `npm run check`: the output above, no model or browser. Exit 1 means the bug, 0 means fixed. 3. Optional, end to end: set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` (model `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast`, or `E2E_MODEL`) or a Google key (`gemini-flash-lite-latest`, the model I ran it with), then run `npx e2e run` twice. The second run types the first run's code. ### Versions e2e 0.23.1, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.0, node 24.22.3. Same on 0.23.2-nightly-20261118030221. ### Engine @e2e-dev/web ### Anything else
Run 2 report excerpt (0.23.1, gemini-flash-lite-latest) ```json "cache": { "mode": "agent-concluded", "reason": "end-mismatch", "replayedActions": 6, "totalActions": 6, "detail": "every recorded action ran, but the recorded end state did not show on /: missing status \"Code verified\" and textbox \"First digit\" (+5 more), still showing textbox \"First digit\" and textbox \"Second digit\" (+4 more)" } ```
I have a fix ready and will open a PR shortly: - The web engine already reads `autocomplete="one-time-code"` into the node's `inputPurpose`. A value typed into such a node becomes a `minted-token` gap, the existing rule applied to one more case. - The first box becomes the gap, so nothing stale is saved. - A single digit there never counts as written in the instruction, so "enter the 6-digit code" can't make a 6 replay. A whole code in the instruction or params still replays. - No public API, wire, or cache-format change, so it doesn't touch #1692. The benchmark's saved recording still replays as it is. - Not covered: boxes without the `autocomplete` attribute, and mobile. Those could be a follow-up.

title: fix(cache): record a code typed into a one-time-code field as a run-time gap
body:
## What and why - A one-time code typed one digit per box was saved as normal input, so the next replay typed the previous run's code. The read-off-the-screen check sees each digit alone, and a lone digit is neither a whole node nor a word of `Your code is 482913`. - A value typed into a node whose `inputPurpose` is `one-time-code` is now a `minted-token` gap: one check in `derived.ts`, and one line in `action-dispatcher.ts` that passes the node's purpose. The web engine already sets it from `autocomplete`. - A lone digit in such a field never counts as written in the instruction, so "enter the 6-digit code" can't make a 6 replay. A whole code the instruction or params spell out (a word of its own, or a param's exact value) still replays. - The rule errs toward a gap. A wrong gap costs a model call; a missed one types a stale code. So a fixed code passed in `params` and typed one digit per box now runs live instead of replaying. - The first box becomes the gap, so nothing stale is saved. A stale entry already on disk fails its next replay, gets evicted, and is recorded again with the gap. ## Issue Fixes #1933 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The new integration test (`trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts`, a `/one-time-code` fixture page with a new code per load, scripted executor, no model) fails on `main` and passes here. - Removing the new check fails it and the new unit tests. Removing the dispatcher line fails the integration test alone. Dropping the lone-digit rule fails the "6-digit" unit test. - The repro from the issue, run with `E2E_FORK` set and `gemini-flash-lite-latest`: | | main (0.23.1 and nightly) | this branch | |---|---|---| | `npm run check` (no model) | exit 1, each digit `undefined` | exit 0, each digit `minted-token` | | Run 1 saves | `type` ×6 with the code's digits | 6 gaps (`minted-token`) | | Run 2 | types run 1's code, "Incorrect code", `end-mismatch` | gap at action 1, no stale digit typed |
Run 2 step.cache ```jsonc // main (0.23.1) { "mode": "agent-concluded", "reason": "end-mismatch", "replayedActions": 6, "totalActions": 6, "detail": "every recorded action ran, but the recorded end state did not show on /: missing status \"Code verified\" …" } // this branch { "mode": "missed", "reason": "gap", "replayedActions": 0, "totalActions": 6, "detail": "at action 1 of 6, tool type (run-time value)" } ```
- `e2e` unit suite 4098 passed, the cache and act integration suites pass, `pnpm check` passes. - #1630 also edits `action-dispatcher.ts` (`armAfter`), not the lines here. Left alone: the web benchmark's `otp-auto-advance` entry still replays under `--strict-cache`, since a replayed fill skips the check. Boxes without `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `press` / `typeText`, and mobile are follow-ups. I used Claude Code to find the bug and draft the change, and checked the code, the tests, and the repro runs myself. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(core): report launch() sessions in the test that opens them
body: A test that opens a second session with `launch()` from `@e2e-dev/core` (a second user in another browser, a phone beside the browser) now gets that session in its report, and neither session prints the other's secrets. - Before, the session's steps, model usage and video were missing from the report, and a secret passed only to `launch()` reached `report.json`, `trace.md` and the terminal in plaintext. - Now the session is part of the test that opened it, with no new public API. ```ts test('a second user in a second browser', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open('/todos'); await using host = await launch(web(), { app: { url }, secrets: { INVITE: process.env.INVITE! } }); const second = await host.newSession(); await second.app.open('/todos'); await second.screen.getByRole('button', 'Publish').tap(); }); ``` ```text 8. ✓ `locator.fill` `getByLabel("New todo")` (11ms, video 0:00) 9. ✓ `locator.tap` `getByRole("button", name: "Add")` (41ms, video 0:00) 10. ✗ launch-1 › `locator.tap` `getByRole("button", name: "Publish")` (807ms, launch-1 0:00) - LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND ``` ## What changed - **Report.** Each step of the session is mirrored into the test's step recorder under `actor: "launch-1"`, in the order it started, with the test file's line. Model usage counts toward the test. `progress.identity`, steps and video artifacts carry `actor` (schema and fixtures updated). - **Video.** A session opened inside a test that keeps video records one, kept beside the test's as `video/launch-1.*` under the same keep rule. Hosted links are kept as links. - **Ownership.** A host or session the test opened is the test's. An un-awaited step or opening fails the test with `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`, a timeout cuts the session's step before teardown, and what is still open is closed at the end. A session opened outside every test (file scope, `beforeAll`, a worker fixture) only has its steps recorded. - **Secrets.** Every owner of values (the run's config, an open host, an open session) shares them through one refcounted map on `globalThis`. A ledger redacts what is shared beside it at redaction time and stores none of it, so a saved session state carries only its own values. A host launched in a test keeps its secrets shared until that test ends. - **Errors.** An error a session throws no longer carries a secret in `details`. - **Reporters.** List, trace page, Markdown, JUnit and the HTML report name the session. The HTML player plays each step in its own session's video. - **Two installed copies.** Everything crosses through `globalThis` slots, as `currentAttempt()` already does, so a project with `@e2e-dev/core` beside `e2e` still reports and redacts. ```mermaid flowchart LR T[test body] -->|launch / newSession| S[seat reserved in the attempt] S --> O[session opened] O -->|each step: progress + record| M[mirror in the test's StepRecorder] M --> R[report, trace, reporters] O -->|close| V[video copied into the attempt's artifacts] B[body over] -->|quiesce| C[cut running steps, cancel openings] E[attempt end] -->|settle| X[close hosts and sessions, keep or drop videos, release secrets] ``` Code: `packages/core/src/run/secrecy.ts`, `packages/core/src/run/guest-steps.ts`, `packages/core/src/core/internals.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/run/guests.ts`. ## For the reviewer to decide - **Field name `actor`**, chosen to match the multi-user proposal so the report schema changes once. Names are minted as `launch-`. - **Behavior change.** The test now closes hosts and sessions it opened and left open. - **`AGENTS.md`.** The `launch` contract line changed. It used to say nothing is published to `globalThis`. - **Not covered.** Hosted attempts (`openHost`, `e2e mcp`) do not attribute launch sessions yet. Failure evidence is still the test's own screen, now labeled as such. Values a launch session itself learned stop being shared when that session closes. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI, a test driving a second browser with one secret only `launch()` knew and one only the config knew. Both values searched in the terminal output, `report.json`, `junit.xml`, `report.html`, every `trace.md` and `screen-at-failure.txt`. - mobile benchmark app, built CLI: an iOS simulator test driving an Android emulator session and a browser session, and the reverse. Also two iOS simulators. - a live agent run through the gateway: an agent on either session refused to read a screen showing the other's secret ("the todo title is redacted"), and `ai-trace.json` had no plaintext. | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Launch session's steps in the report | 0 of 4 | all, under `launch-1` | | Its video | none | `video/launch-1.webm` | | `launch()`-only secret, web: `report.json` / trace pages / terminal | 10 / 3 pages / 6 lines | 0 / 0 / 0 | | `launch()`-only secret, iOS + Android: `report.json` / result files | 2 / 4 | 0 / 0 | | Un-awaited launch step | test passed, browser leaked | `STEP_NOT_AWAITED`, session closed | | Test timeout under a launch step | step ran on for its own 8s | cancelled at the timeout | ```text × |web| tests-probe/two-users.e2e.ts > a second user in a second browser 1.71s → locator matched no nodes within getByRole("button", name: "Publish") × |web| tests-probe/two-users.e2e.ts > forgets to await and to close 398ms → the test body returned before locator.waitFor "getByText("never shown") … × |web| tests-probe/two-users.e2e.ts > times out under the second browser (timed-out) 1.79s → test timed out after 1500 ms in phase body ❯ video .e2e/results/two-users-a-second-user-in-a-second-…/attempt-1/video/video.webm ❯ video .e2e/results/two-users-a-second-user-in-a-second-…/attempt-1/video/launch-1.webm ``` HTML report of that run: the `launch-1` tag on each step, and the video switcher. ![html report](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b887969-e364-4f39-b8aa-15e18e17508e) The attached video is the second browser's recording from the test's artifacts. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d13154e-74d8-45b2-a0d0-daf87502da56

title: feat(reporters): build the built-in reporters on the public Reporter API
body:
The built-in reporters (`list`, `dot`, `json`, `junit`, `markdown`) were wired into the runner by name. A reporter of your own could not see what user code prints, show the `--step` prompt, add rows to the summary, or write files the way the built-ins do. `--reporter list,json` was refused, because both wanted stdout.

## What changed

- Every built-in is now an ordinary `Reporter`, built only on the public contract (`packages/e2e/src/run-types.ts`). The runner has no special path for any of them.
- `e2e/reporters` exports the factories: `list()`, `dot()`, `json()`, `junit({ outputFile })`, `markdown({ outputFile })`. A string id in `reporters` still works and is that factory called with no options:

  ```ts
  import { junit } from 'e2e/reporters';

  export default defineConfig({
    targets,
    reporters: ['list', junit({ outputFile: 'reports/junit.xml' })],
  });
  ```

- New hooks for any reporter:
  - `onOutput`: what user code prints, redacted, with the test it came from.
  - `onStepPrompt`: the `--step` prompt to show.
  - `onSummary`: every reporter's summary rows.
  - `reportFiles`: files the runner writes atomically, even after a second Ctrl-C.
- `printsTo: 'stdout' | 'stderr'` names the terminal stream a reporter prints to, at most one reporter per stream. Beside `json`, `list` and `dot` move to stderr unless given a `stream`, so `--reporter list,json` now works like `dot,json`.
- `--reporter` keeps the options of a built-in the config configured.
- An id named twice runs once (`json,json` printed two concatenated documents before).
- If a terminal reporter's `onOutput` or `onStepPrompt` throws or rejects, the runner prints one warning. For the rest of the run it prints the output, run errors, and prompt itself.
- `@e2e-dev/html-reporter` writes `report.html` through `reportFiles`.
- Compatibility: configs that work on main behave the same. Only `list,json` and `json,json` change, as above.
- `screen.pause()` (#1904) prints its lines without a terminal through `onOutput`, as the runner's own output, so `list` shows them under a `stdout | runner` heading. Main printed them through a private hook on the terminal reporter, which this PR removes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[user code output] --> R[redaction]
  R --> O{terminal reporter with onOutput?}
  O -- yes --> L[its onOutput, e.g. list]
  O -- no, or it broke --> T[terminal, as written]
  R --> M[every other onOutput, e.g. a socket mirror]
```

Output a reporter prints from inside `onOutput`, or from work it starts there, goes straight to the terminal. It never comes back to `onOutput`, so a reporter that echoes output cannot feed itself.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Built CLI against the testbed: the default suite, the stress suite (failures, timeouts, skips, flaky tests, hostile titles), `--step`, and `--reporter dot`, `dot,json`, `list,json`, `list,junit,markdown`. The web benchmark suite passes too.
- A separate end-to-end pass (GPT-6.2 Sol) ran every reporter scenario on the built main and on this branch, in scratch projects:
  - each built-in by id and by factory, the combinations, and secrets in test output, split across writes too;
  - custom reporters using every hook, and custom reporters whose hooks throw;
  - config errors and missing files;
  - Ctrl-C once and twice, `--watch`, `report.html`, and the GitHub job summary with a faked Actions environment.
- Its three regressions, all in custom terminal reporters with a broken hook, are fixed here and covered by tests (`run-user-output.test.ts`, `step-hold.test.ts`). Each test fails with its fix reverted.

| Scenario | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--reporter list,json` | `INVALID_CONFIG` | list on stderr, one JSON document on stdout |
| `--reporter json,json` | two JSON documents concatenated on stdout | one document |
| config `[list(), junit(...)]`, `--reporter list,json` | n/a (no factories) | list on stderr, one JSON document on stdout |
| Ctrl-C twice while reporters finish | JSON on stdout and `report.html` lost | both written |
| `json`, `junit`, `markdown`, html, GitHub summary, `--watch`, `--step` | | same output as main |

```text
$ e2e run --reporter list,json        # config: reporters: [list(), junit({ outputFile: 'reports/junit.xml' })]
exit 1                                 # the fixture has a failing test on purpose
stdout parses as one JSON doc: yes
stderr:
 RUN  e2e v0.23.1 ~/tmp/pr-reporters/proj
      run 01a1ef8b-a713-7849-9d05-4d09d4ee59a0 · targets: scratch
```

Reviewed with sol-loop: 5 rounds with gpt-6.2-sol. Sol verdict: changes requested at round 5, on one watch-mode leak and one broken-terminal-reporter fallback. Both are fixed here, and Sol's end-to-end pass above checked the result. A fresh-context review afterwards raised 7 findings, and 6 are fixed. The one left: `reportFiles` survives a second Ctrl-C for every reporter, not only the built-ins. That is the documented contract, so a report file never sits stale beside a new `report.json`.

---

Made with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: `e2e login spacexai` and the SuperGrok token refresh send `User-Agent: node`
body:
### What happened

`e2e login spacexai` and the SuperGrok token refresh call `auth.x.ai` with Node's default `User-Agent: node`. Model requests and `e2e models spacexai` send `e2e/<version> (<platform>; <arch>)`, which [`client-identity.ts`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/9d240ac954f65804fece214bfbf112966364d644/packages/core/src/internal/client-identity.ts#L5-L6) describes as what every vendor request identifies as.

`postForm` sets only `content-type` and `accept`:

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/9d240ac954f65804fece214bfbf112966364d644/packages/e2e/src/oauth/token-endpoint.ts#L24-L31

Expected: the sign-in and token requests carry the same `User-Agent` as the model requests.

### Reproduction

No repository: the bug needs no app, config or test, only the one file the steps below create. I can push it to a repository if you prefer a link.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In any project with `e2e` installed, save this as `print-user-agent.mjs`:

   ```js
   const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;
   globalThis.fetch = (input, init) => {
     const request = new Request(input, init);
     console.log(request.method, request.url, '| user-agent:', request.headers.get('user-agent') ?? '(not set; Node sends "node")');
     return realFetch(input, init);
   };
   ```

2. Run `node --import ./print-user-agent.mjs node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js login spacexai`, and press Ctrl-C once the code is shown.
3. It prints the line below for the device-code request, and the same for each poll of `https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token`. Expected `e2e/0.23.0 (…)`.

   ```text
   POST https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/device/code | user-agent: (not set; Node sends "node")
   ```

### Versions

e2e 0.23.0, node 22.23.4. The code is the same on `main` at 9d240ac.

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

I have a small fix, limited to the SpaceXAI provider, and will open a PR.

title: fix(oauth): send the e2e User-Agent on sign-in and token requests
body: ## What and why - `e2e login spacexai` and the SuperGrok token refresh call auth.x.ai with Node's default `User-Agent: node`. Model requests already send `e2e/ (; )`. - `postForm`, the helper every provider's device-code, poll, code-exchange and refresh request goes through, now always sends `USER_AGENT`, and so does the ChatGPT device login. SpaceXSI, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode Console all sign in and refresh as e2e. ## Issue Fixes #1937 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, on the `e2e@0.23.0` source with this diff applied. Not on `main`: I could not install `main`'s current dependency versions. The changed files are the same on `main` and 0.23.0, apart from the import path of `USER_AGENT`. `e2e login spacexai`, then a refresh, against a local recording server. What the server received, with the User-Agent last: ```text # 0.23.0 POST /oauth2/device/code (device code) node POST /oauth2/token (poll) node POST /oauth2/token (poll) node POST /oauth2/token (refresh) node GET /v1/language-models (model list) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) # 0.23.0 with this change POST /oauth2/device/code (device code) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) POST /oauth2/token (poll) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) POST /oauth2/token (poll) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) POST /oauth2/token (refresh) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) GET /v1/language-models (model list) e2e/0.23.0 (linux; x64) ``` - The two new assertions in `tests/unit/oauth/xai.test.ts` fail without the fix (`expected [ 'node', … ]`) and pass with it. The rest of `tests/unit/oauth`, the build and the typecheck pass, also with #1808 applied on top of 0.23.0. - One device-code request and one poll against the real auth.x.ai with the fix were accepted. A real token refresh was not run; it needs a SuperGrok login. - Maintainer follow-up (9b993fec4): each provider's login test asserts the header. Dropping it from `postForm` fails 7 tests, dropping it from the ChatGPT device login fails 1. A device-code request with the header against the real auth.x.ai, opencode.ai, auth.openai.com and github.com each answered 200. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.

title: Name the SuperGrok provider spacexsi, keeping spacexai and grok as aliases
feat(oauth): name the SuperGrok provider spacexsi, with spacexai and grok as aliases
body: ## What and why - The SuperGrok provider id is now `spacexsi` (was `spacexai`) and its display name `SpaceXSI`, the name the vendor's pages use (sources in the linked request). `e2e login`, `logout` and `models` take it; messages, the docs and the skill show it. - `spacexai` and `grok` work as aliases on all three commands, through one `PROVIDER_ALIASES` map with `canonicalProviderId()`, the same shape as `ROLE_ALIASES` / `canonicalRole()`. - A login stored under `spacexai`, in the credentials file or in `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, is still read and stays under that key, so an older e2e on the same machine keeps working. New logins are stored under `spacexsi`. - Unchanged: `grok()` from `e2e/oauth/grok`, `e2e init --gateway grok`, the model ids. ## Issue Closes #1942 Opened alongside the feature request, not after an agreement; it can wait for a maintainer's decision there. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes, the `packages/` changes on the `e2e@0.23.0` source, and the tests, build and typecheck again with #1808 applied on top. Not on `main`: I could not install `main`'s current dependency versions. On `main` with this diff I ran only the checks that need no dependencies (docs translations, docs examples, error codes, plugin sync); they pass. A login stored under `spacexai`, vendor answered by a local recording server: ```text # 0.23.0 $ e2e models spacexai SpaceXAI (spacexai): 5 models $ e2e models spacexsi error: command-argument value 'spacexsi' is invalid for argument 'provider'. Allowed choices are openai, github-copilot, opencode-console, spacexai. $ e2e models grok error: command-argument value 'grok' is invalid for argument 'provider'. Allowed choices are openai, github-copilot, opencode-console, spacexai. # 0.23.0 with this change, the same stored login $ e2e models spacexsi SpaceXSI (spacexsi): 5 models $ e2e models spacexai SpaceXSI (spacexsi): 5 models $ e2e models grok SpaceXSI (spacexsi): 5 models ``` - New tests cover the aliases on the command line, in the `login`, `logout` and `models` functions, for a login stored under `spacexai` in the file and in `E2E_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, for the lock file such a login is refreshed under, and for a `grok()` model call with the login under either name. 21 tests fail without the source change. With it, the touched test files, the build and the typecheck pass. - With the built CLI against the recording server: a token refresh keeps the login under `spacexai`, `e2e logout spacexai` removes it, `e2e login grok` stores a new login under `spacexsi`. - Not run: a real SuperGrok sign-in. The Japanese and Chinese sentences about the aliases were not checked by a native speaker. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it.
