title: Mobile benchmark: the Photo Picker recording misses on every fresh iOS simulator
body:
### Problem

The committed iOS recording for Photo Picker taps `image "Photo, October 15, 10:27"`. The system picker names a photo by its capture date, and the seeded `icon.png` has none, so Photos names it by the time `simctl addmedia` ran. On any other simulator, CI's included, the name differs, the replay hands off, and the step calls the model. The iOS agentic job shows it on every run, for example [this one](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/44373490979/job/135070629887) (`act completes Photo Picker ... 2 model calls`). The README lists it as a CI-only hand-off, with yet another date (`October 03, 22:50`).

### Proposed API

No API change. In `apps/mobile-benchmark/tests-agent/scenarios.e2e.ts`, `seedReceiptPhoto` adds the same `icon.png` with an `eXIf` chunk whose `DateTimeOriginal` is October 15, 10:27 of the current year. The file name stays `icon.png`, which the recording's end state (`Receipt attached: icon.png`) reads back, so the existing recording replays as is. Drop the Photo Picker line from the README's hand-off list.

### Upsides

Photo Picker replays from the recording on CI: no model calls and no model variance for that step. On a simulator here, the picker labels the dated photo `Photo, October 15, 10:27`, the same name the recording has.

### Downsides

The year has to be the current one. For older photos the picker spells out the year in the host region's date order (`30 March 2018` on a Mac set to Poland), which would differ between a Mac and CI. A simulator reused across New Year gets a second copy under the new year's name, which the picker can tell apart.

### Alternatives

Re-record on the CI image, which only moves the problem to the next simulator. Or seed a JPEG with a fixed date, which changes the file name the end state checks and needs a new recording.

### Which surface

Mobile benchmark (tests only).

On a fresh iOS 26.5 simulator with `CI=1 --strict-cache` and no model key, main fails the step with `REPLAY_STALE (target-not-found)` and the change replays it (`Cache 1 replayed`). Happy to send the PR.

title: cache: a one-time code typed into the focused field still replays the last run's code
body:
## Summary

#1934 makes the replay cache record a value typed into an `autocomplete="one-time-code"` field as a `minted-token` gap, but only for the `type` action, which names its field. When the agent types into the focused field instead (`typeText`), the field's purpose is not passed on. A code typed one digit per box that way is still saved as replayable digits, and the next run types the last run's code. That is the failure #1933 reports: a wrong code attempt on the app every replay, and the test still passes.

Root cause: `ActionDispatcher.recordTrace` passes `inputPurpose` only when `action.name === 'type'`. A `typeText` action carries no node, so `derivedReason` falls back to the general rules, and a lone digit is neither a whole node nor a word of its own in "Your code is 482913".

This depends on #1934 (it adds `StepEvidence.inputPurpose`). Web only: the mobile engine never reports `one-time-code` (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts:607` sets `password` only).

## Evidence

- Investigated revision: 17db9661d7fbcf5ec62714444762e99da652333e (head of #1934, detached). No running app or logs are involved; the defect is in the recording rule.
- `packages/core/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts:769-774`: `typeText` values go through `derivedReason`, but `...(action.name === 'type' ? { inputPurpose: action.node.inputPurpose } : {})` leaves the purpose out for them.
- `packages/core/src/agent/actions.ts:70-71`, `packages/core/src/cache/trace.ts:354-357`: a `typeText` action is `{ name: 'typeText', value, replace }`, with no node.
- `packages/core/src/agent/replay.ts:242-243`: replay types a recorded `typeText` into whatever has focus.
- On the web engine, the agent reaches `typeText` three ways:
  - the `type` tool with `target` left out (`packages/core/src/agent/primitives.ts:443-458`; its description tells the model to do this after `tap_at`);
  - `type_at` on a point with no listed control (`primitives.ts:869-880`);
  - the `typeIntoNode` fallback, a tap and then `typeText` when the node cannot be filled (`primitives.ts:711-718`).
- Probe of `derivedReason` at this revision, instruction "type the code shown on the page into the code boxes", shown `['Your code is 482913']`:

  ```text
  '4', no inputPurpose (the typeText path)      -> undefined     (recorded, replays)
  '4', inputPurpose: 'one-time-code' (type path) -> minted-token  (gap)
  '482913' whole, no inputPurpose                -> minted-token  (shown-word rule)
  ```

- What a replayed digit does on the next run: on #1933's base 847a09e6, with a page that issues a new code per load, a `read-write` cache sent the old code every other run and a `read-only` cache sent it on every run, all with exit 0. The `typeText` path at this revision records the same replayable digits.
- No existing test combines `typeText` with derived gaps. `packages/e2e/tests/integration/trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts` drives only `context.actions.type`.
- Duplicate search: open issues for "one-time code", "replay code digit", "typeText cache", and "derived gap" found only #1933. #1934 closes #1933, and #1934 covers the `type` action only.

## Current Gap

After #1934, `docs/cache.mdx` says `minted-token` covers "any value typed into a field marked `autocomplete="one-time-code"`". That holds for `type` and not for `typeText`.

## Proposed Scope

- In `ObservationFeed` (`packages/core/src/agent/observation-feed.ts`), keep a step-level flag that is set when any node observed in the step has `inputPurpose === 'one-time-code'`. Set it in `noteShown` (line 429), which already walks every observed node, and expose it as a read-only getter.
- In `ActionDispatcher.recordTrace`, pass `inputPurpose: 'one-time-code'` for a `typeText` action when that flag is set. `type` keeps passing its own node's purpose.
- Accepted cost: in a step whose screens listed a one-time-code field, every `typeText` value that the step does not spell out whole runs live. Over-flagging costs a model turn, never a wrong replay, which is the trade the header of `derived.ts` already accepts.
- Rejected alternatives:
  - The focused node of the newest observation: it is stale when the model sends a tap and a type in one turn.
  - The node of the last node-targeted action: it misses `tap_at` on a field the tree does not list.
  - The engine reporting the focused field's purpose from `keyboard.type`: that changes the engine contract and the protocol wire, and older engines would fail open.
- No change to the report wire, the cache format, or `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION`. As with #1934, an entry recorded before the fix replays once more. That run ends in `end-mismatch`, the step passes after the executor acts, and the entry is evicted.
- Docs: extend the `minted-token` sentence in `docs/cache.mdx` to cover focused typing in a step that showed a one-time-code field. Translations are best effort. Add a `@e2e-dev/core` patch changeset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a step whose observations listed an `autocomplete="one-time-code"` field, a `typeText` value is recorded as `{ name: 'tool', summary: 'tool type (run-time value)', derived: 'minted-token' }`. The exception is a value of 2 or more characters that the instruction carries as a word of its own, or that a param equals; that value replays, the same as #1934's rule for `type`.
- The replay of such a recording hands off at the first gap and never types a digit from the previous run.
- In a step that listed no one-time-code field, `typeText` keeps today's rules. The existing `typeText` replay tests in `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-replay.test.ts` and `packages/e2e/tests/unit/step-cache.test.ts` still pass.

## Test Scenarios

- Integration, modeled on `packages/e2e/tests/integration/trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts` and its `/one-time-code` fixture page. The executor reads the code, then for each box calls `context.actions.tap({ id })` and `context.actions.typeText(digit, { replace: false })`.
  - Run 1 (`read-write`): exit 0, and every recorded `typeText` is the derived gap above.
  - Run 2: the step reports `{ mode: 'missed', reason: 'gap' }`, the executor runs once, and it never sees "Incorrect code".
- Counterfactual: a page variant with the same boxes but no `autocomplete` keeps recording `typeText` actions. This pins the scope; fields with no declared purpose are out of scope here.
- Unit: an `ObservationFeed` that observed a node with `inputPurpose: 'one-time-code'` reports the flag, and one that did not reports it unset.

## Out of Scope

- Fields with no declared purpose, and codes split across fields on mobile.
- Mobile one-time-code purpose: agent-device 0.21.38 snapshot nodes carry no `textContentType` or autofill hint.
- A separate `DerivedReason` for one-time-code fields, which would be a report wire change.

title: cache: a code typed across several fields with no one-time-code purpose replays the last run's code
body:
## Summary

When the agent types a code the page showed, split over several fields (one digit per box, or 3+3) that do not declare `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, the replay cache saves every piece as replayable. The next run types the last run's code into a page that issued a new one. This is #1933's failure for fields that declare no purpose. #1934 fixes only fields that do declare it.

Unmarked segmented inputs are common on the web. On mobile no field ever declares the purpose: agent-device 0.21.38 snapshot nodes carry no `textContentType` or autofill hint, and `packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts:607` sets only `inputPurpose: 'password'`. So on iOS and Android every split code is affected.

Root cause: `derivedReason` (`packages/core/src/agent/derived.ts`) judges each typed value on its own. A piece of a code is not a whole node, and it is not a word of its own inside "Your code is 482913". `hasWord` (`derived.ts:125`) needs a non-alphanumeric character on each side, so every piece is recorded as replayable.

## Evidence

- Investigated revision: 17db9661d7fbcf5ec62714444762e99da652333e (head of #1934, detached). No running app or logs are involved; the defect is in the recording rule.
- Probe of `derivedReason` at this revision, instruction "Enter the 6-digit code shown on the page", shown `['Your code is 482913']`, no `inputPurpose`:

  ```text
  '4' '8' '2' '9' '1' '3' each        -> undefined     (replays)
  '482', '913' (3+3)                  -> undefined     (replays)
  '48', '29', '13' (2+2+2)            -> undefined     (replays)
  '482913' whole                      -> minted-token
  '482' with shown 'Your code is 482 913' -> minted-token (only a split screen text matches)
  ```

- End to end, using #1934's fixture page (`/one-time-code` in `packages/e2e/tests/helpers/fixture-pages/forms.ts`, a new code per load). Base 847a09e6 ignores the field's purpose, so its runs show the behavior an unmarked field has today:

  | run | `read-write` | `read-only` after one recording |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 2 | old code sent, `end-mismatch`, entry evicted | old code sent |
  | 3 | 6 replayable `type` actions recorded again | old code sent |
  | 4 | old code sent | — |

  Every run exits 0, because the executor repairs the step after the replay. The app still counts a failed code attempt each time.
- Recording internals the fix uses:
  - `TraceRecorder` keeps `actions[]` in memory until `finalize` (`packages/core/src/cache/recorder.ts:57`, `:82`, `:102-105`, `:111-161`).
  - `StepCache.stage` calls `finalize` only after the step passes.
  - Replay stops at the first gap (`packages/core/src/agent/replay.ts:182-183`, `:301-302`).
  - `ObservationFeed.shownText()` holds the text of the whole step, up to 4,096 entries (`packages/core/src/agent/observation-feed.ts:55`, `:127`).
- Benchmarks: `apps/web-benchmark/app/src/Examples/OtpAutoAdvance.tsx` marks its boxes with `autoComplete="one-time-code"`. No benchmark has unmarked boxes, and `apps/mobile-benchmark` has no segmented code input.
- Duplicate search: open issues for "one-time code", "replay code digit", "typeText cache", and "derived gap" found only #1933. #1933 expects the fix for `autocomplete="one-time-code"` boxes and lists boxes without it, and mobile, as not covered.

## Current Gap

`docs/cache.mdx` says a value the agent read off the screen is a gap. That holds for a whole code, but not for a code the agent types across several fields, unless a field declares a one-time-code purpose.

## Proposed Scope

A sequence rule in core, which works for every engine:

- In `ActionDispatcher` (`packages/core/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts`), track the step's current typed run while recording outside a replay.
  - A run is a sequence of `type` and `typeText` actions. Only `tap`, `tapAt`, and a `pressKey`/`press` of `Tab` may sit between two of them, since those only move focus.
  - Any other action ends the run, and so do a gap, truncation, and a replayed action.
  - Keep each typed value with its index in the recorder.
  - Cap the run at the last 12 typed values.
- When a typed value is recorded as replayable, test every suffix of the run that ends at it and has 2 or more values, longest first. Join the values of a suffix with no separator.
  - If the instruction or params spell the joined value out (the existing `isLiteral` test), stop: it replays.
  - Else, if the joined value is the whole of a shown node, or is data-shaped and a shown node holds it as a word of its own, the run is derived from that suffix's first action.
  - Reuse the existing `whole-node` and `minted-token` reasons. Do not apply the `date`, `pixels`, or `inputPurpose` rules to joined values; the per-value check already covers them.
- Add a `derivedJoinReason(joined, instruction, params, shown)` export to `derived.ts` beside `derivedReason`. It reuses `isLiteral`, `isDataShaped`, `hasWord`, and `normalize`.
- Add `TraceRecorder.gapFrom(index, reason)`: drop the recorded actions from `index` on and push the derived gap, as `recordDerivedGap` does. If the recorder is truncated, or already holds a gap at or before `index`, do nothing. Recording goes on after the gap as it does today.
- No change to the report wire (`DerivedReason`, `report-v1.schema.json`), the cache format, or `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION`. An entry recorded before the fix replays once more, ends in `end-mismatch`, and is evicted when the executor repairs the step, as with #1934.
- Accepted cost: unrelated short values typed in a row whose join happens to equal a shown token make that part of the step run live.
- Docs: in `docs/cache.mdx`, after the rule list, say that values typed in a row into several fields are also judged joined, and that the recording becomes a gap from the first piece. Translations are best effort. Add a `@e2e-dev/core` patch changeset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six one-character `type` values that join into a code a node showed as a word are recorded as one derived gap at the first piece, and nothing from them replays. The same holds for a 3+3 split and for `typeText` pieces with taps between them.
- A joined value the instruction or params spell out (for example `params: { code: '482913' }`) still replays piece by piece.
- Values that do not join into shown text (for example `Jane`, then `Doe`, on a page showing "Welcome") keep today's recording.
- The existing `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-recorder.test.ts` and `packages/e2e/tests/integration/trace-cache*.test.ts` tests still pass.

## Test Scenarios

- Unit, `packages/e2e/tests/unit/agent-derived.test.ts`, with shown `['Your code is 482913']`:
  - `derivedJoinReason('482913', 'enter the code', undefined, shown)` is `minted-token`.
  - The same with params `{ code: '482913' }` is `undefined`.
  - `derivedJoinReason('JaneDoe', …)` with shown `['Welcome']` is `undefined`.
- Unit, `packages/e2e/tests/unit/trace-recorder.test.ts`:
  - Record `navigate` and then six `type` actions, and call `gapFrom(1, 'minted-token')`. `finalize` returns `[navigate, { name: 'tool', summary: 'tool type (run-time value)', derived: 'minted-token' }]`.
  - With a gap already at index 0, `gapFrom(1, …)` changes nothing.
- Integration: add an unmarked variant of the `/one-time-code` fixture page (for example `?unmarked=1`, with the same boxes and no `autocomplete`). Model the test on `packages/e2e/tests/integration/trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts`.
  - Run 1 records exactly one action, the derived gap.
  - Run 2 reports `{ mode: 'missed', reason: 'gap' }`, the executor runs once, and it never sees "Incorrect code".
  - A 3+3 variant of the executor gives the same result.
- Counterfactual: the same unmarked page, with an instruction that spells out the code the page shows, records six replayable `type` actions.

## Out of Scope

- A code the screen never shows, such as one sent by SMS or email to a device, in a field that declares no purpose. Nothing on the screen ties it to this run.
- Layout guesses such as `maxlength=1` or `inputmode=numeric` groups. The reader does not expose them, and they would flag PIN and single-character fields.
- Mobile one-time-code purpose from `textContentType` or autofill hints. agent-device 0.21.38 does not expose them; that needs agent-device first.
- A separate `DerivedReason` for joined values, which would be a report wire change.

title: docs: add a Next.js guide page
body:
A Next.js developer had to collect the setup from `web.mdx`, `cache.mdx`, the skill, and the example. [`docs/frameworks/nextjs.mdx`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/kdy1/nextjs-guide-page/docs/frameworks/nextjs.mdx) puts it on one page, from `e2e init` to CI.

- **One config for both modes** ([`docs/examples/nextjs/e2e.config.ts`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/kdy1/nextjs-guide-page/docs/examples/nextjs/e2e.config.ts), typechecked): `next dev` with `reuseExisting` locally, `next start` when `CI` is set, with `next build` before `e2e run`. The config reads `CI` the way e2e does (`packages/core/src/internal/env.ts:10`): `CI=0` and `CI=false` mean a local run.
- **Fix Next.js problems:** three accordions.
  - The `allowedDevOrigins` hydration fix moves here from `web.mdx`, which now links to it.
  - The App Router's empty `role="alert"` route announcer, which `getByRole('alert')` also matches.
  - A webpack `watchOptions.ignored` entry for `.e2e/`.
- **Start a new app:** `create-next-app --example …/examples/with-next` for npm, pnpm, and bun, and the [Next.js with e2e template](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e-vercel-previews) for Vercel.
- **Navigation and links:** the page goes under Platforms, after Web. `web.mdx`, `cache.mdx`, and `example-projects.mdx` link to it. `docs/ja/` and `docs/zh/` get the page and the same link edits.
- **Skill:** `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` carries the same guidance (plugin copy synced), with a `patch` changeset for `e2e`, since the skill ships in the package.

## Issue

Closes ENG-1378

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes. The steps on the page ran with the published `e2e@0.23.1`, `@e2e-dev/web@0.16.0`, and Next.js 16.4.6, in fresh `create-next-app` projects.

| Step on the page | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npx e2e init --yes`, then the page's config with `init`'s `agents` kept, `npx e2e run` | passes, `next dev` started (ready 1.98s) |
| dev server already running, `npx e2e run` | `reused` it, passes |
| `npm run build`, then `CI=1 npx e2e run` | `next start` started (ready 0.49s), passes |
| `CI=false` and `CI=0` | `next dev` started, as e2e reads them |
| port `0` (`127.0.0.1`), a client counter test, no `allowedDevOrigins` | fails: the click never updates the counter, HMR WebSocket errors |
| same, with `allowedDevOrigins: ['127.0.0.1']` | passes |
| `getByRole('alert')` on a page with no alert of its own | count 1: the route announcer |
| `next dev --webpack`, a module under `.e2e/` changes | rebuilds without the page's `watchOptions`, does not rebuild with them |
| `npx create-next-app --example https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/tree/main/examples/with-next`, `npm run test:e2e` | 3 passed, 2 agent tests skipped without a key |

```text
 ✓ target "web" command at http://localhost:3000/ ready 1.98s
   ✓ |web| tests/example.e2e.ts > app opens 460ms
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Not verified:

- **The `.e2e/` rebuild loop itself.** I could not reproduce it on Next.js 15.5 or 16.4, with or without Tailwind, on Turbopack or webpack, in a single run or against a reused dev server. So the accordion is a conditional fix ("when `next dev` recompiles while the tests run"). Turbopack has no ignore option for it, so the page gives the webpack fix only.
- **The rendered page.** `mint dev` rejects the custom `theme` in `docs/docs.json`, so I did not see it on the site. `pnpm docs:check` compiles every page as MDX and checks anchors, examples, package-manager tabs, and the ja and zh outlines.

Review (fresh context, gpt-6.2-sol): four findings, all fixed.

- The sample imported `ai`, which `init` does not install for **None**. It now keeps `init`'s model import and `agents` entry.
- The port must match in both `dev` and `start`.
- `process.env.CI` disagreed with e2e on `CI=0` and `CI=false`.
- The `watchOptions` list replaced existing rules without saying so.

Notes:

- ENG-1378 says "App Router route cache", but the fact in `cache.mdx` is the route announcer. The page covers the announcer.
- ENG-1379 (making `with-next` a proper starter) is still open. The command on the page already works. The generated `package.json` keeps the name `e2e-example-with-next`, which is ENG-1379's scope.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(desktop): add the @e2e-dev/desktop engine on agent-desktop
body: Adds `@e2e-dev/desktop`: an engine for native macOS apps, built on [agent-desktop](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop). It reads and drives the app through the accessibility tree: observation, the act verbs, test ids, and secrets. It runs on macOS only; `prepare` and `init` refuse any other OS. ```ts // e2e.config.ts targets: [{ name: 'mac', engine: desktop(), app: { appPath: 'build/MyApp.app' } }], // tests/sign-in.e2e.ts import { test } from '@e2e-dev/desktop'; test('signs in', async ({ app, screen }) => { await app.open(); await screen.getByRole('textbox', 'Password').fill(credentials.user('ada').password); await screen.getByRole('combobox', 'Plan').selectOption('Team'); await screen.getByRole('button', 'Sign in').tap(); await expect(screen.getByTestId('status')).toContainText('Signed in as ada'); }); ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR H[harness] -- engine contract --> S[DesktopSurface] S -- one process per command --> A[agent-desktop CLI] A -- macOS accessibility --> App[app under test] P[prepare] -- download v1.3.1, check SHA-256 --> A ``` ## What changed - `packages/desktop` (new): the engine, built with `defineEngine` and importing only `@e2e-dev/core/engine`. - `src/binary.ts`: `prepare` downloads the pinned agent-desktop release and checks its SHA-256. The npm package `agent-desktop` is not a dependency: its `postinstall` would fail `check:install-scripts`. `desktop({ binary })` uses an install of your own. Runs that install at the same time publish with no lock: a rename that collides with a checked entry keeps that entry, only one run's rename moves a damaged entry aside, and a whole copy a run moved aside by mistake goes back. - `src/cli.ts`: runs one agent-desktop process per command, with a private `AGENT_DESKTOP_HOME` per worker. It maps agent-desktop's `disposition.delivery` onto the engine errors: a failure that may have reached the app is `ACTION_MAY_HAVE_COMMITTED`, and only a refusal that sent nothing is retryable. - `src/nodes.ts`: maps agent-desktop roles to ARIA names (`textfield` to `textbox`, `statictext` to `text`). `native_id` (`AXIdentifier`) becomes `testId`, and `secure` marks a password field. Anonymous wrapper groups and the window's own title-bar buttons are left out. - `src/surface.ts`: `app.open()` launches the app fresh, in the background unless `headed`: an installed app through agent-desktop's `launch`, an `appPath` build by its path (`open -g -n`), so LaunchServices cannot pick another copy with the same bundle id. Each launch puts a one-time token in the app's environment, and the engine reads, drives, and quits only the process that carries it (`ps -E`), or, for a `bundleId` launch, the new process agent-desktop's `launch` reports. A process is never taken for being new. An `appPath` to a bundle whose environment macOS hides (an Apple app, a build signed with `restrict`) is refused by `init` and `doctor`, which name the `bundleId` to use. Running copies are matched by `list-apps --app`, so a localized name (`계산기` for Calculator) still counts. Every test ends with that process quit, and launches and quits of one worker run one at a time. `desktop.useWindow()` picks the window `screen` reads. - Background: an app in the background is never brought forward. One that opens no window there fails the open with a message that it needs `headed: true`. `press` needs `headed` too: agent-desktop sends a key only to the active window, and the engine never sends a key by the app's name, which could reach another copy. - Cleanup: the launch token is written to the worker's state directory before the launch, and the process id and start time once the process is shown to be the launch's. The next run's `init` quits every process that carries the token of a worker that is gone, and the recorded process while it is still the one that started then. The record goes only once a lookup that worked shows the process exited; until then it stays, without the field text agent-desktop keeps, for the next run. - Reads: no read failure looks like an empty screen, so `not.toBeVisible()` cannot pass on one. A window that cannot be read (a locked screen) or a read cut short is a retryable `NODE_STALE`, so a locator reads again until its timeout; an app that quit, or a `useWindow` window that closed, is `INVALID_STATE`. `desktop({ maxDepth })` (default 24) sets how deep a read goes. `getByPlaceholder` is refused: macOS reports no placeholder, and names an unlabeled field by it. - Security: agent-desktop and the app it launches get only `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, `LC_*`, and `__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING` of the run's environment; `open` and NSWorkspace otherwise hand the app the caller's whole environment, secrets included. Fill text goes to agent-desktop on stdin, never in its arguments. A screenshot reads the window whole before and after the capture, crops the capture to the window, and paints every secure field black. It is withheld when a secure field has no bounds or a box with no area, a read was partial, a field moved during the capture, or the cropped size does not match the window. - Node ids stay the same while a control exists, so after an action the agent gets a diff, not the whole screen. A control with a look-alike sibling gets a new id in every read, so an old ref cannot land on its twin. - `apps/desktop-testbed` (new, private): an AppKit sign-in form (`pnpm build:app`) with 4 deterministic tests and 1 agentic test. No CI job runs it yet: macOS runners need Accessibility permission first. - Docs: a new `docs/desktop.mdx` page, `AGENT_DESKTOP_INSTALL_FAILED` in `reference/errors.mdx`, and one-line mentions in `engines.mdx`, `core-concepts.mdx`, and `skills/e2e`. Not in this PR: Windows and Linux (refused until secure fields and headless actions work there), the menu bar, an `e2e init` preset, and a CI job. Web content (a browser window, Electron, a web view) is out of scope for this engine. ## Review Four independent reviewers (codex gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5), each on its own checkout, then a human review (5a9ed79f5), then three more rounds by the same four on 5636e64ab, then a second human review (7e0b7d224, carried to a550ec96b). Every finding was fixed with a unit test that fails without the fix, except the 500 ms minimum an input gets once sent, which follows the mobile engine (`packages/mobile/src/support.ts`). The second human review, applied in 589345b5d..6999c1da5 (589345b5d first kept the lock and accepted a verified copy at the repair's rename; 0349475f4 then removed the lock): - Ownership: the one new copy with an unreadable environment is no longer taken (the first review had asked for that fallback). Only the token, or the process agent-desktop's `launch` reports, counts. - Recovery: a failed process lookup no longer reads as "nothing running", a kill is confirmed, the record names the process by id and start time, and a failed dispose keeps only that record. - Activation: the second `open` that brought a windowless background app forward is gone. - Keys: the by-name fallback is gone, and `press` is offered with `headed` only. - Cache: the lock is gone; the CI failure (`ENOTEMPTY` on Node 22.22.3 and 26) is reproduced by a test that holds one install at that point. - Optional: a stale read after a press focused the control is no longer retried; the stamp test and the select delivery test now fail on the mutations that survived. From the first human review: number fields, HTML `

title: cache: a clock time written as 5:42pm is kept as an end anchor, so the replay goes stale a minute later
fix(cache): read a clock time written as 5:42pm as volatile
body: ## What and why - `CLOCK_TIME` ended in `\b` right after the minutes, so `5:42pm` (no space before am/pm) never matched. The text stayed an end anchor and the replay went stale when the minute changed. `5:42 PM` and `17:42` were already skipped. - The pattern now also matches when am/pm follows the minutes directly: `/\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?(?=\b|[ap]\.?m\b)/i` (`packages/core/src/internal/dates.ts`). The am/pm is a lookahead, so the matched span is still the digits and nothing changes for text that matched before. - `maskClocks` had its own copy of the old pattern. It now builds from `CLOCK_TIME`, so a ticking `5:42pm` clock no longer reads as a screen change. `5:42am` to `5:42pm` still does. - Side effect: `derivedReason` shares the pattern, so a typed `9:30am` is a `date` like `09:30` and `9:30 am` already were. - `5:42pmx` and `16:10amp` still do not match. ## Issue Fixes #1954 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The repro script from the issue (`describeDelta`, then `deltaMismatch` a minute later), against `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/core build` of each side: | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `5:42pm -> endAnchors [{"role":"status","text":"Profile saved"},{"text":"Last saved 5:42pm"}]`, replay: `{"missing":[{"text":"Last saved 5:42pm"}],"present":[],"unrecordedAlerts":[]}` | `5:42pm -> endAnchors [{"role":"status","text":"Profile saved"}]`, replay: `"holds"` | - The three touched unit test files with the source of main: `3 failed | 194 passed (197)`. With the fix: `197 passed (197)`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: web: screen.tree() lists row, cell and listitem under role="presentation" tables and lists, which getByRole cannot find
body:
### What happened On a page that uses a layout table (``) or a list with `role="none"`, `screen.tree()` still lists the rows, cells and list items with their roles, but `getByRole` finds none of them. The docs say to use the tree to write a locator, so I wrote `screen.getByRole('row', 'Billing address Edit')` from it and got zero matches. ```html
Billing address
  • Home
  • Docs
``` `screen.tree()`: ```text #root document "Repro" #n2 rowgroup #n3 row "Billing address Edit" #n4 cell "Billing address" #n5 cell "Edit" #n6 button "Edit" #n7 listitem "Home" #n8 listitem "Docs" #n9 link "Docs" href="/docs" ``` `screen.getByRole('row').count()`, `('cell')` and `('listitem')` all return 0. I expected the tree to show no `rowgroup`, `row`, `cell` or `listitem` there. ARIA makes the required children of a presentational table or list presentational too, and Chrome's accessibility tree and Playwright both read it that way. The web engine's `implicitRole` (`packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts`) applies the role to the table or list only. Seen on main at 9d240ac and in the current nightly. ### Reproduction https://gist.github.com/JaynouOliver/4c11f821b9a918f0f19aee6221da9a61 ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npm install` 2. `npx @e2e-dev/web install chromium` 3. `npx e2e run` 4. Expected `layout.e2e.ts` to pass. It fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED: row: the tree lists 1 ... expected 0 to be 1` ### Versions e2e 0.23.2-nightly-20261118030221, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.1-nightly-20261118030221, node 22.23.4 ### Engine @e2e-dev/web ### Anything else Chromium, Linux. Adding this kind of markup to the cross-check fixtures (`packages/web/tests/crosscheck/fixtures.ts`) reports 23 disagreements with Chrome and Playwright. I have a small fix ready and will open a PR.

title: fix(web): drop row, cell, and listitem roles under a presentational table or list
body:
## What and why - Under `` or `
    `, the tree kept `rowgroup`, `row`, `cell`, `rowheader` and `listitem`. `getByRole` (Playwright) and Chrome drop those roles, so `screen.tree()` listed nodes a role locator could not find. - `implicitRole` in `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts` now inherits the presentational role for `li`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `td` and `th`, with the same parent table and conflict rule Playwright uses: a focusable parent, or one with a global ARIA attribute, keeps its children's roles. - An explicit role on the child still stands, and a nested real list or table is untouched. - New cross-check fixture page `layout tables and lists`; `expected.txt` is unchanged. ## Issue Fixes #1956 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Surface: `e2e run` in an empty project on the nightly (`e2e@0.23.2-nightly-20261118030221`, `@e2e-dev/web@0.16.1-nightly-20261118030221`), Chromium, a test comparing `screen.tree()` with `getByRole(...).count()`. title: feat(expect): add toBeEditable locator matcher
body:
Adds `expect(locator).toBeEditable()`, Playwright's locator matcher: it waits for an enabled control that is not read-only. ```ts await expect(screen.getByLabel('Email')).toBeEditable(); await expect(screen.getByLabel('Order id')).toBeEditable({ editable: false }); // read-only or disabled ``` - Read-only is a node state the engine reports (`SemanticNode.states.readonly`), present only where a node has one. The matcher reads it; a disabled node is not editable either, read the same way as `toBeEnabled`. - Web: decided in-page as Playwright's `getReadonly` does. `input`, `textarea`, `select` by their `readonly` attribute alone; an element whose ARIA role takes `aria-readonly` by that attribute, case folded (an editing host by its ARIA role, so a plain `
` stays editable and a `td` in a grid reads it); any other editing host and what is inside it `false`. - Mobile: only on Android, where agent-device's `editable` comes from `TextView.isTextEditable()`: a text field or search field gets `readonly: !editable`, a combobox `readonly: false` only when the platform says it takes text. iOS gets no state, because agent-device fills in `editable: true` for every iOS text field from its type. - Any node with no read-only state, like a button, fails both ways and the message names its role, as Playwright does. - The web and mobile engines require `@e2e-dev/core` and `e2e` at `>=0.25.0 <1`, since they emit a new contract field; `toBeEditable` needs those engine releases. - Types in `packages/core/src/types.ts`, pinned in `tests/types/sdk-types.ts`; MCP code surface lists the matcher. - Docs: `reference/expect.mdx` and the `states` union in `reference/engine.mdx` (en/ja/zh), the Playwright migration table; skill reference updated. ## Issue Part of #1855 (Assertions row, assigned). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `packages/e2e/tests/unit/expect-async-editable.test.ts` (10 cases: the engine state read both ways, disabled, `editable: false`, a node with no state, a secure field). - `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-platform.test.ts` in Chromium, `/editable-matcher`: native `readonly`, `aria-readonly` with case folding, a fieldset-disabled input, an editing host and a line inside it, `aria-readonly` on an input (ignored), a role="textbox" editing host with `aria-readonly`, a plain `contenteditable` with `aria-readonly` (editable), a grid `td` editing host with `aria-readonly` (read-only), a button. 50 passed. - `packages/mobile/tests/unit/nodes.test.ts`: Android text fields both ways, Android combobox with `editable: true`, iOS `TextView`/`TextField` with the `editable: true` agent-device fills in (no state). Whole mobile unit suite 558 passed; `@e2e-dev/web` suite 856 passed, 1 skipped. - `pnpm check` clean. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: fix(test): read the test.skip and test.fail condition by truthiness
body:
Inside a test body, `test.skip(condition, reason)` and `test.fail(condition, reason)` treated every condition that was not a boolean as true. So `test.skip(process.env.CI, 'only on CI')` skipped on a machine where `CI` is unset, and `test.fail(undefined, 'x')` marked a passing test, which then failed with `UNEXPECTED_PASS`. Playwright reads the condition by truthiness. The maintainer asked for this fix in its own PR in [#1887](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1887#issuecomment-6971141478) ("Your separate PR for it is welcome").

- `parseModifierCall` (`packages/e2e/src/internal/skip.ts`) now gets the call's own arguments (`skip(...args)`), so it can tell `skip(undefined, reason)` from `skip(reason?)`. With a condition, it reads the first argument by truthiness and takes the reason from the second argument only, as Playwright does.
- The one-argument forms keep e2e's `skip(reason?: string)` overload: `test.skip()`, `test.skip('reason')`, and `test.skip(undefined)` still always skip.
- A Promise condition (a missing `await`) or a function condition used to skip or mark the test every time. Inside a body both now fail the test with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Playwright also throws on a function there. It goes through the `readCondition` that `test.skipIf` and `test.runIf` already used, moved to `internal/skip.ts` with the error it throws as a parameter, so `skipIf` and `runIf` keep `COLLECTION_ERROR`. Outside a body, `test.skip(promise, reason)` keeps main's error: the call belongs in a test body. `isPromiseLike` moved to `internal/promise-like.ts` with its own unit test, now counts a function with a callable `then` as a thenable, and the MCP schema check uses it instead of its own copy.
- Docs: `reference/test.mdx` and the `TestAPI` JSDoc say "truthy", name the one-argument difference from Playwright, and list the Promise case under `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The ja and zh Types blocks carry the same JSDoc. The Playwright migration guide names the one-argument difference: write `test.skip(!!process.env.CI)`.

```ts
test('sync', async () => {
  test.skip(process.env.CI, 'flaky on CI'); // CI unset: runs (main: skipped)
  test.fail(flags.beta, 'beta gap');        // flag missing: runs as normal (main: UNEXPECTED_PASS)
  test.skip(await isSingleTenant(), 'x');   // still skips when true
  test.skip(isSingleTenant(), 'x');         // missing await: INVALID_ARGUMENT (main: always skipped)
  test.skip(() => isBeta, 'x');             // a function: INVALID_ARGUMENT (main: always skipped)
});
```

The condition stays typed `boolean`, as in Playwright, so TypeScript users hit the falsy cases only through `any` or a cast. JavaScript suites hit them directly.

## Issue

Fixes #1966

## Overlap with open PRs

`git merge-tree` of this head against each open PR that touches the same files:

| PR | Conflicting files |
| --- | --- |
| [#1887](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1887) `test.fixme` (mine) | `internal/skip.ts`, `collect/registry.ts`, `reference/test.mdx`, `migrate/playwright.mdx`, `runner-lifecycle.test.ts`, `sdk-types.ts` |
| [#1914](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1914) `test.skip()` from teardown | `internal/skip.ts`, `reference/test.mdx` |
| [#1925](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1925) `test.describe.fail` | `collect/registry.ts`, `sdk-types.ts` |
| [#1858](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1858) `test.todo` | `collect/registry.ts`, `sdk-types.ts`, `reference/test.mdx` (en, ja, zh) |

- #1887 is the one with a semantic dependency. It adds a third caller with the old `parseModifierCall(first, second)` signature, which no longer compiles once this lands. Whichever lands second moves `test.fixme` to `fixme(...args)` with `parseModifierCall('test.fixme()', args)` and adds `test.fixme(undefined, 'x')` and Promise cases. Passing `[first, second]` would compile but break a bare `test.fixme()`. I'll do that on #1887 if this one lands first.
- The other three are text conflicts only: none calls `parseModifierCall` or `readCondition` in a new place.

## For the maintainer

- A lone `test.skip(undefined)` or `test.skip('')` still skips, because it matches e2e's `skip(reason?: string)` overload. Playwright does not skip on either. Following Playwright here means narrowing the overload to `skip(): void; skip(reason: string): void`, which breaks callers that pass `string | undefined`. I kept today's behavior and documented the difference. Say if you want parity instead.
- Widening the condition type to `SynchronousCondition<Condition>`, as `skipIf` has, would let `test.skip(process.env.CI, 'x')` type-check. That is a public API change, so it is not in this PR.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes
- testbed, built CLI (`node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-falsy-repro.e2e.ts --reporter list`), one scratch test file (not committed), `origin/main` build against this branch:

| Call in the test body | `origin/main` (`bc2193ac`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test.skip(process.env.UNSET, 'flaky on CI')` | skipped `[flaky on CI]` | passed |
| `test.skip(flags.beta, 'beta only')`, flag missing | skipped `[beta only]` | passed |
| `test.skip(0, 'no items')` | skipped `[no items]` | passed |
| `test.fail(process.env.UNSET, 'known CI gap')`, passing body | failed, `UNEXPECTED_PASS` | passed |
| `test.skip('yes', 'the real reason')` | skipped `[yes]` | skipped `[the real reason]` |
| `test.skip()` | skipped | skipped |
| `test.skip('waiting on the API')` | skipped `[waiting on the API]` | skipped `[waiting on the API]` |
| `test.skip(undefined)` | skipped | skipped |
| `test.skip(Promise.resolve(false), 'async check')` | skipped `[async check]` | failed, `test.skip() got a Promise as its condition; await it before the call` |
| `test.skip(() => false, 'fn condition')` | skipped (not run on main here; main's parser counts any non-boolean as true) | failed, `test.skip() got a function as its condition; call it and pass the result` |

- Outside a body, `test.skip(Promise.resolve(false), 'async check')` at module level stops the run with `COLLECTION_ERROR: test.skip(condition, reason) skips the running test and must be called inside a test body`, the same error as on main.
- With `FALSY_REPRO_CI=1` set, the same file still skips the CI-only test and marks the CI-only `test.fail` (its passing body then fails with `UNEXPECTED_PASS`), so a truthy condition still applies.

title: feat(mcp): attach to a test held at screen.pause() or --step
body:
Stacked on #2003, which moves the session tools out of `mcp/`.

A test held at `screen.pause()` or at an `e2e run --step` hold now prints an ID, and you can attach `e2e mcp` to it. A coding agent can then look at the app and act on it while the test waits.

- The pause header shows the ID: `Paused (k3f9) in pays with a card [web]:`. In a terminal, the ID is on the test's row. It's random, and it stays the same for every hold of that attempt.
- `open_session {attach: "k3f9"}` opens a session on the held test's app. It has the same tools as a normal session on that target, and they work the same way: the grammar verbs, `run_code`, `type_secret`, `screenshot`, the project's tools, and recording. A test compares the two catalogs.
- `close_session` detaches and leaves the test held. When you resume the test, the session ends right away and a call still in progress is cancelled.
- Attached calls aren't recorded as steps in the report or the trace.
- `start_recording` works when the run doesn't record the test. When it does (`--video`), it fails with the directory of the run's video, since an engine session holds one recording. A recording still running when the session ends is saved.
- An unknown ID is answered with the held tests and their IDs.
- A reporter's `onStepPrompt` gets the ID as `attachId` on each held step. That's the only new public field. The function that attaches to a held test isn't reachable from a reporter.
- `e2e run --step` in a terminal now listens on the directory's step socket like a pause does, so an agent can attach at its holds. `e2e run --step next` from another shell resumes it as well.
- Attached sessions are counted in usage telemetry through the existing session event, with an `attached` field.

```txt
open_session {attach: "k3f9"}
call {tool: "observe", session: "<id>"}
call {tool: "run_code", args: {code: "await screen.getByRole('link', 'Todos').tap();"}, session: "<id>"}
close_session {session: "<id>"}
```

## How it works

The tools run in the worker, on the engine session the held attempt already has. The MCP server only forwards requests.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Coding agent
  participant M as e2e mcp
  participant R as e2e run (runner)
  participant W as Worker (held attempt)
  W->>R: step-hold
  R-->>A: prints "Paused (k3f9) ..."
  A->>M: open_session {attach: "k3f9"}
  M->>R: hello, attach (step socket)
  R->>W: step-attachment-request
  W-->>M: catalog and first screen, redacted
  A->>M: call {tool: "tap"}
  M->>R: call
  R->>W: step-attachment-request
  W-->>M: result, redacted
  Note over R,W: Enter or "--step next" ends the attachment
```

- The runner gives each held attempt an ID and relays requests to its worker (`StepAttachmentRelay`, called from `packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts`).
- The worker builds the session catalog over the held attempt in `packages/e2e/src/run/worker/held-test-tools.ts`, with `createStepExecution` from #2003 and an empty step recorder, so the calls stay out of the test's steps. Every reply is redacted with the attempt's secret ledger before it's sent.
- An attachment uses one connection on the existing step socket (`packages/e2e/src/cli/step-control.ts`). The messages are in `packages/e2e/src/run/step-attachment-wire.ts`. The first message carries a protocol version, and a mismatch is answered with both e2e versions.
- With several workers paused, each prompt is now drawn from the hold it names (`packages/e2e/src/cli/step.ts`). Before, a prompt could show one test's title next to another test's screen.

## Limits

- App logs and screen updates aren't recorded on the test while an attached call runs. Late effects of a call can show up in the trace after it returns or is cancelled by a resume. Browser callbacks don't say which side caused them.
- If the agent changes the app, the test resumes on the screen the agent left. A step that fails because of that is expected.
- A directory has one step socket, owned by the first run that pauses there. A second run paused in the same directory can't be attached to. Its ID is answered with the held tests of the run that owns the socket.
- If you resume while the agent is recording, the test continues right away. The video is saved in the background, and its path is in the MCP server's log.
- `e2e mcp` and `e2e run` must start in the same directory.
- There's no idle timeout for an attached session. It ends when the agent closes it, the test resumes, or the MCP server exits.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed, the built CLI and a real `e2e mcp` over stdio. A stepped run holds the smoke test, and an MCP client attaches, runs a statement, saves a screenshot, records a video, and the test is resumed from a shell.
- The attached video shows a coding agent doing the same from a prompt, against a headed run paused at `screen.pause()`. It was recorded before the IDs became random, so it shows `p1`.

```text
$ e2e run tests/smoke.e2e.ts --grep "playground renders and navigates" --step   # no terminal
Paused (7s46) before step 2 of playground renders and navigates [web]:
  expect.toHaveTitle "Playground" (tests/smoke.e2e.ts:6)

> open_session {attach: "zzzz"}
NO_SESSION: no held test matches that attachment id
Held tests:
7s46  playground renders and navigates [web]

> open_session {attach: "7s46"}
Session <id> open on target "web". Attached to 7s46, "playground renders and navigates" on target "web".
Credentials: "admin" (username "admin", password secret "admin.password"). ...

> tools
Session <id> on target "web": 32 tools. Run one with call {tool, args}. Use tools {tool} to see a tool's arguments.

> call {tool: "run_code"}
The statement passed.
1. passed: await expect(screen.getByRole("heading", "Playground")).toBeVisible();

> call {tool: "screenshot", args: {path: "attach-shot.png"}}
Screenshot attached: 768 by 432 pixels (0.6 per CSS pixel).        # attach-shot.png is on disk

> call {tool: "start_recording"}
Recording 1 started. Act as usual; stop_recording saves the video, and close_session saves one still running.

> call {tool: "stop_recording"}
Recording 1 stopped after 2.2 s.
- apps/testbed/.e2e/videos/<id>/1.webm                              # the file is on disk

$ e2e run --step next
✓ expect.toHaveTitle "Playground" 1ms
Paused (7s46) before step 3 of playground renders and navigates [web]:

> call {tool: "observe"}   # after the resume
NO_SESSION: session "<id>" ended: the test resumed; call open_session for a new one

$ e2e run --step rest
      Tests  1 passed (1)
The stepped run has ended.
```

- After the run, `.e2e/report.json` holds the test's 9 steps and none from the attached session.

title: fix(web,mobile): name engine handle types for inferred configs
body: - A config that infers `web()` or `mobile()` with `satisfies E2EConfig` fails `tsc` with TS2883 in a pnpm project that sets `declaration: true`. It broke in e2e 0.24.0, when `EngineHandle` moved to `@e2e-dev/core` (#1737, #1734): pnpm links core only inside the engines' own folders, so TypeScript has no import path for it. - `web()` now returns `WebEngine` and `mobile()` returns `MobileEngine`, interfaces declared in each engine package and exported from the main and `/engine` entries. The inferred type names a package the config already imports. - `scripts/install-smoke.ts` emits the declaration of such a config in the packed pnpm project. - `docs/reference/engine.mdx` shows the same pattern for third-party engines, and the web and mobile references list the new types. ```ts export interface WebEngine extends EngineHandle {} export function web(options: WebOptions = {}): WebEngine ``` Not covered: a fixtures file that calls `test.extend` from an engine package with no `e2e` import hits the same error on `TestAPI`. title: fix(core): run actions sent in the same turn as complete_step
body:
An action the model sends in the same turn as `complete_step` now runs. On main it was skipped, and the step still passed. This is the first half of the fix ENG-928 suggests ("allow the action + `complete_step` in one turn"). The latency in that issue is not fixed yet: the models tested still read the last result before they conclude (see Verified).

## Issue

Refs ENG-928

## What changed

- The AI SDK runs a turn's tool calls concurrently. `complete_step` sits outside the action queue, so its verdict landed first and the queued tap was skipped as "already concluding".
- The loop now reads the turn's calls from the model's reply, in the order sent (`wrapGenerate` middleware, `packages/core/src/agent/tool-loop.ts`). `complete_step` waits for every call sent before it in the turn, and is refused, with their results for the model to read, when:
  - a call did not run (the SDK refused its input), or failed
  - the last call changed nothing (`reportsNoEffect`, `packages/core/src/agent/screen-update.ts`). An earlier call that changed nothing does not count, because typing into a password field lists no change.
- A call sent after `complete_step` in the turn does not run. Its place in the reply decides this, not timing.
- Project tools that return a plain value or an async iterable are tracked too: an iterable that throws, or whose last output is a failure, refuses the verdict.
- The chassis instructions and the `complete_step` description say a step that only lists actions may end in the turn of its last action. This is not in `BASE_RULES`, since `@e2e-dev/acp` shares `BASE_RULES` and has no such wait.
- Side effect: `explore`'s `report_finding` sent with `complete_step` now runs. Before, the finding was lost.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as model
  participant L as loop
  M->>L: tap(n8), complete_step(passed)
  L->>L: tap runs
  Note over L: complete_step waits for tap
  alt tap failed, did not run, or changed nothing
    L-->>M: Rejected: tap ... in this turn
  else
    L-->>M: Step concluded (no further turn)
  end
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/agent-act-same-turn-verdict.test.ts`, a scripted model against the fixture app:

| case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tap Increment + `complete_step` in one turn | tap skipped, step passes, counter stays 0, `expect` fails | tap runs, 1 model call |
| dead-end tap + `complete_step` | verdict taken | refused: "had no visible effect" |
| tap on a missing id + `complete_step` | verdict taken | refused: "failed" |
| tap with invalid input + `complete_step` | verdict taken | refused: "did not run" |
| earlier tap changes nothing, last tap works | tap skipped | verdict taken, 1 model call |
| project tool: sync failure, iterable that throws, iterable ending in a failure | verdict taken | refused |
| `complete_step` then tap | passes | passes, tap does not run |

  On main, 8 of these 10 fail. All 10 pass here.
- Live models, a sign-in page whose wrong-password error toast lasts 5 s, then `expect(screen.getByRole('alert'))` after `agent.act` (two phrasings, `--no-cache --repeat-each 4`, `--ai-trace`):

| model | build | runs passed | turns where tap and `complete_step` went together |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| openai/gpt-6-luna-fast | main | 10/10 | n/a |
| openai/gpt-6-luna-fast | this branch | 8/8 | 0/8 |
| anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 | main | 8/8 | n/a |
| anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 | this branch | 8/8 | 0/8 |

  Both models finish the turn after the tap in about 1.5 to 2 s, so the toast survived on main too, and the issue does not reproduce with them. Neither model sends the tap and `complete_step` together. The likely cause is that the shared rules pull the other way: "Conclude passed only when the latest result shows the outcome", "a submit should be the last action of its turn", and "you verified it" in the `complete_step` description. Changing those touches `@e2e-dev/acp` too, so this PR leaves them for a follow-up.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web-benchmark run test:agent --strict-cache` with `CI=1`: 34/34 passed.

## Review

- A fresh-context review (codex gpt-6.2-sol) found three issues, all fixed:
  - plain-value and async-iterable tool results were not tracked
  - the no-effect check matched app text anywhere in a result; it now matches only a paragraph that opens with the report
  - `skills/e2e` did not describe the ordering rule

title: Track stale docs translations after English changes
body:
## Problem

`pnpm docs:check` compares translated pages with the English outline and code blocks and checks navigation labels. It can pass when the translated instructions are out of date. The separate [DeepL workflow](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/160cbfe7a/.github/workflows/docs-translations.yml) gives advisory feedback for Japanese on pull requests. It does not open a tracking issue.

## Verified example

I ran `node scripts/check-docs-translations.ts` on `main` at [`160cbfe7a`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/commit/160cbfe7a06df443d531060fc0e7467cb9db8368). All 198 translated pages matched their English outline and code.

The matching pages in Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Czech, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Hindi still describe the plugin as including the server.

## Suggested follow-up

- [ ] Update `coding-agents.mdx` and `mcp-server.mdx` in the six locales above.
- [ ] When an English docs change lands on `main`, compare each changed page with its existing translations. Flag a locale for review if the English source changed and the translation did not. A translation update in the same merge can count as reviewed.
- [ ] Open or update one GitHub tracking issue for the outstanding pages. Include the English diff and each affected locale's file. Keep the check advisory and preserve the existing English fallback for pages that have never been translated.

An untouched translation is a review signal. A reviewer may decide the English edit needs no translation change.

Related to the translation umbrella [#1890](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/1890).

title: docs(visual-testing): stop promising secrets stay out of screenshots on the Security card
body: ## What and why The Security card at the end of `docs/visual-testing.mdx` said: "How secrets stay out of screenshots, reports, and model input." That promise is wrong. Screenshots mask secure fields only, so a secret typed into a plain input, or shown anywhere else on screen, is in the image. The model provider gets that image too. - Web masks only `input[type="password" i]` (`SECURE_FIELD_SELECTOR`, `packages/web/src/read-node.ts:22`). - Mobile masks only nodes with `states.secure` (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts`). - `docs/security.mdx:23-28` ("What can still leak") and `docs/reference/security.mdx:176-179` already say this. The card now reads: "How secrets stay out of reports and the model's text input, and what can still leak." "The model's text input" is the wording `docs/security.mdx:18-19` uses for what redaction covers. cubic flagged the same line in the Hindi translation on #1986. That PR keeps the Hindi matching the English page, so the fix starts here. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `pnpm docs:check`: 281 pages compile, 4119 anchor links resolve, and 198 of 198 translated pages match their English outline and code. - No other English page promises that secrets stay out of screenshots. I searched `docs/`, `skills/`, and `README.md`. ## For maintainers - `docs/ja/visual-testing.mdx:124` and `docs/zh/visual-testing.mdx:124` still have the old promise. The translation check compares outlines and code, not card text, so it does not flag them. - A separate inaccuracy, not changed here: `docs/visual-testing.mdx:138-139` and `docs/reference/security.mdx:85` say the matcher fails with `POLICY_DENIED` when masking can't be proven. That holds on web. On mobile, `observe` returns no pixels for an unmaskable secure node (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1886-1887`), so the matcher fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` ("the engine returned no screenshot") instead. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fold follow-up: deep sidebar never folds, and a folded parent drops its children's fold records
body:
Follow-up to #1797, which folds large unchanged subtrees in MCP sessions. Two limits found while reviewing it. Neither is caused by that PR: base gives the same output in both cases.

1. A sidebar at depth 10 or more does not fold when its parent also holds changing content. formatNode caps the indent at MAX_INDENT_DEPTH = 10 (packages/core/src/agent/observation.ts:464), so spanEnds reads the sidebar's children as its siblings and the sidebar's span ends at once. Base and head both return 2,532 bytes with all 15 links listed.

2. When a parent folds, noteListed (packages/core/src/agent/screen-update.ts:209) keeps only the parent's record and drops the records of the subtrees under it: fullyListedSubtrees excludes any subtree holding a folded line. If the parent's own line changes on the next full screen, its unchanged child list (15 links in the reviewer's run) is listed again in full on base and head, instead of folding against the earlier listing.

Possible directions: track depth from the node tree instead of the rendered indent for the fold check, and keep child records under a folded parent so the child can fold again once the parent is listed in full.

title: fix(agent): prevent duplicate form submissions
body:
## What and why

- In the reported run, `agent.act` clicked **Update Product** twice after the first click left the screen unchanged. The built-in agent now checks the current screen before repeating the same commit by any route, including Enter. It retries when the screen shows the first press did not commit or when the tap only dismissed the keyboard.
- While a save is in progress, consecutive `observe` and `screenshot` calls have their own limits. A change to the listing, location, or tabs resets the unchanged-look count. The step still needs visible evidence to pass.
- `e2e explore` keeps its charter to retry and revisit on purpose.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Press the commit control] --> B{What does the screen show?}
  B -->|Still saving| C[Observe again]
  C --> B
  B -->|Commit failed or tap only closed keyboard| D[Retry when ready]
  B -->|Saved or outcome unclear| E[Run the requested check and conclude]
```

title: docs: on mobile, toHaveScreenshot fails with ASSERTION_FAILED, not POLICY_DENIED, when a secure field can't be masked
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Drafted by Claude Opus 5.5. Reviewed by samanyudas and posted on their behalf.**

### Page

`docs/visual-testing.mdx:138`, `docs/reference/expect.mdx:287`, `docs/reference/security.mdx:85`

### What is wrong

These three pages say the screenshot matcher fails with `POLICY_DENIED` when the engine can't prove every secure field on screen is masked. That's true on web. On mobile, the matcher fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` and "the engine returned no screenshot".

The mobile code does this:

1. If `redactSecure` can't mask a secure node, `capturePixels` returns `undefined` (`packages/mobile/src/surface.ts:1886-1887`). So `observe` returns no pixels.
2. `packages/e2e/src/expect/screenshot-capture.ts:62` checks for missing pixels before the masking check on line 63. So the matcher never reaches the `POLICY_DENIED` throw.
3. The matcher treats the screenshot as missing and keeps polling until it times out with `ASSERTION_FAILED`.

AGENTS.md says withheld pixels are `POLICY_DENIED`, so the code may be what's wrong, not the docs. I found this by reading the code on `main`. I haven't run it on a device.

### Suggested wording

Maintainers can fix it either way:

1. Change the mobile engine so the matcher throws `POLICY_DENIED`, as on web. The docs stay as they are.
2. Add the mobile case to the three pages: "On mobile, the engine withholds the screenshot instead, so the matcher waits and fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED`."

title: fix(cache): record a focused-field value as a gap when the step showed a one-time-code field
body: ## What and why - #1934 records a value typed into an `autocomplete="one-time-code"` field as a `minted-token` gap, but only for `type`, which names its field. When the agent types into the focused field (`typeText`: `type` with no target after a `tap`, the `typeIntoNode` fallback, or a custom executor that types at the caret), no field is named, so a code typed one digit per focused box was still recorded as replayable digits, and the next run typed the last run's code. - `ObservationFeed` now keeps a step-level flag, set in `noteShown` when any observed node has `inputPurpose === 'one-time-code'` (checked before the editable-field skip there, since the box is itself an input), exposed as `oneTimeCodeShown`. `ActionDispatcher.recordTrace` passes `inputPurpose: 'one-time-code'` for `typeText` when it is set; `type` keeps passing its own node's purpose. - Typing after `tap_at` was already a `pixels` gap, since `tap_at` needs a screenshot in the step; it is now labeled `minted-token` in such a step. - No change to the report wire, the cache format, or `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION`. Docs: `docs/cache.mdx` names focused typing in such a step in the `minted-token` rule and in the exception to "composed values replay". - Not in this PR: a single-character `press` or `pressKey` in such a step is still recorded as typed. A widget that reads only keydown would replay those keys. ## Issue Fixes #1949 Builds on #1934 (merged), whose `StepEvidence.inputPurpose` and `/one-time-code` fixture page it uses. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Main against this branch, the same scratch test on each build (not committed): an executor that taps each box on `/one-time-code` and types its digit into the focused field with `typeText`, run twice with `cache: 'read-write'`: | | main (a5d17889) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Run 1 recording | 12 replayable actions: 6 taps and 6 `typeText` digits (`9 5 2 6 2 3`) | 6 taps, each followed by a `minted-token` gap | | Run 2 cache | `agent-concluded`, `reason: 'end-mismatch'`, replayed 12 of 12, entry evicted | `agent-concluded`, `reason: 'gap'`, `derived: 'minted-token'`, replayed 1 of 12 | | Run 2 executor | sees "Incorrect code" after the replay typed the old code; the run exits 1 | never sees "Incorrect code"; the run exits 0 | The issue expected `mode: 'missed'` on run 2. With a tap before the first digit, the tap replays and the step reports `agent-concluded` with the same gap, which is the hand-off the docs describe. - `tests/integration/trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts` pins the branch column, and a counterfactual on `/one-time-code-plain` (the same boxes, no `autocomplete`), where `typeText` digits are still recorded, as today. - A unit test in `agent-observation.test.ts`: a step that observed a one-time-code field keeps the flag after the field is gone; one that never did stays unflagged. - `pnpm check`, and every suite `pnpm test` runs, in two parts after a reboot cut the first run short: core and `e2e`, then every other package. 7468 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed. `docs/cache.mdx`: one paragraph changed, 166 to 175 words, no fact cut. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: feat(mcp): run JavaScript in run_code
body:
`e2e mcp`'s `run_code` now runs JavaScript, so an agent reads, computes, and acts in one call. Before, it took flat test statements only: no variables, loops, or return values.

- 59% of MCP sessions in the last 30 days call `run_code`, and 27% of those hit `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, mostly from writing loops, variables, or `page.*`.
- The code runs in the server's Node process, on the objects a test body gets: `screen`, `app`, `expect`, `credentials`, `secrets`, and the engine's fixture (`browser`, `device`). A call waits, matches, and fails as it does in a test.
- A recorder (`session-tools/code-recorder.ts`) wraps those objects and writes down the test line each call spells, for the result and `test_lines`.
- `open_session {path}` opens on one page of the app, and the opening text is smaller.
- A single action on a control nothing names now prints a test line by its role (`getByRole("spinbutton")`), alone or narrowed like twins. Closes #1825.
- `agent.act()` is untouched. Only the MCP server changes.

```js
const items = screen.getByTestId('feed-item');
let seen = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
  const count = await items.count();
  if (count === seen) break;
  seen = count;
  await items.last().scrollIntoView();
}
const texts = await items.allTextContents();
return { total: texts.length, title: await browser.evaluate(() => document.title) };
```

## Trust model change

`run_code` has the authority of a test file. An earlier revision of this PR ran the code in a QuickJS sandbox and kept the closed grammar; that is gone (maintainer decision).

- **Why:** a coding agent on `e2e mcp` can already write a test and run it with `npx e2e run`, which has full Node authority. The sandbox cost a 440-line guest prelude, a second `expect`, no callbacks, and a name list of refused members. Playwright MCP's equivalent tool also runs in the server process.
- **Removed checks:** the grammar (`code-parse.ts`, `code-surface.ts`), the `type_secret` checks on a secret `fill` in `run_code`, the refusal of a locator found by part of a text in a project with secrets, and the refusal of host paths. These were on main for `run_code` statements, so this is a behavior change there too.
- **Kept:** the result passes the secret ledger, so a configured secret's exact value shows as `<secret:name>`. A read of a secure field is still `POLICY_DENIED` in the engine. The single-action tools (`type_secret`, `upload`, `locate`) are unchanged.
- **On by default, by design:** every `e2e mcp` server offers `run_code`. There is no `--allow-code` flag or config switch, and a client that approves `call` approves `run_code` with it. The docs say so.
- **Docs:** `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the security reference name `run_code` as the one place agent code runs, as code-trust.

This answers the two P0 review findings (host files, secrets in changed form) by changing the model, not by enforcement. It needs a reviewer's agreement.

## Behavior

- A line that fails throws the error a test gets. Uncaught, it stops the code.
- **Breaking:** lines the code does not await start together, as in any JavaScript. A flat script from main that relied on statement order needs `await`. The result carries a note with the count of calls not awaited.
- A failure nothing awaited fails the call: the line's promise records whether anything called `then` on it. So does a promise the code left to reject, and an error a timer callback throws; that one ends the call at once. None of them reach the process.
- An error from code the call left running after it ended goes to stderr as a warning. The session, or the held test's worker, keeps running.
- An `expect.soft` failure lets the code go on and fails the call at the end.
- A function the code hands to the engine (a `browser.route` handler) runs in the call's context. Its line is drafted once, with a comment that the server called it.
- An explicit `timeout` sets how long a line waits. Without one, a line waits up to 5 s.
- An object a call resolves with, such as a new tab, gets a `const newTab1 = await browser.newTab();` line in the draft.
- `import()` takes a Node built-in or an absolute path. A relative one resolves from e2e's install, not the project.
- `open_session {path}` on an engine with no `navigate` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- The code compiles strict, so it leaves no name on the server's globals.
- Code that never yields (`while (true) {}`) blocks the server. There is no CPU limit.

## Verification

- `pnpm check` passes.
- Unit and MCP integration tests pass locally: 252 files, 4493 tests.
- Driven live through the built CLI over MCP stdio: the web benchmark app (reads, `expect`, `browser.evaluate`, a `browser.route` handler, a new tab, syntax and runtime errors with line numbers, unawaited failures), and the mobile benchmark app on an iOS 26.5 simulator and an Android API 36 emulator (`device.*` reads and actions, a credential fill, `await import('node:fs')`).
- Cost benchmark rerun after the rewrite: 8 QA tasks, 3 runs each, Claude Code on Sonnet. Totals for the 8 tasks, averaged over the runs:

| | Tool calls | Time | Cost | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| e2e MCP | 33 | 158 s | $0.50 | 2.0 |
| Playwright MCP 0.0.86 | 75 | 276 s | $0.48 | 6.7 |

title: ci: label PRs opened by the e2e team
body:
## What and why

- PRs opened or reopened by someone listed in `.github/team.txt` get the `e2e team` label, so team and community PRs can be filtered apart.
- The list is a file, one GitHub login per line, read from the default branch on each run. A PR cannot add its own author.
- Why a list and not `author_association`: a member with private org membership reads as `COLLABORATOR` to anyone outside the org (#1889: `COLLABORATOR` anonymously, `MEMBER` with a member's token), the same as an outside collaborator.
- The list holds the 8 current `e2e-inc` org members. The label already exists in the repo.
- Team PRs already open stay unlabeled until reopened; they need a one-off labeling pass after merge.

```bash
team=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/contents/.github/team.txt" -H 'accept: application/vnd.github.raw')
if grep -qixF -- "$AUTHOR" <<< "$team"; then
  gh api --method POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR/labels" -f 'labels[]=e2e team' --silent
fi
```

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, the step only. `pull_request_target` runs the workflow from main, so the workflow itself first fires after merge.

- Ran the step's script by hand against this PR, reading the list from this branch (`?ref=oskar/team-label`) with my own token instead of the workflow token.
