title: fix(core): count a locator's waitedMs from where its deadline starts
body: - `tests/integration/cli-run.test.ts` fails on CI now and then with `expected 399 to be greater than or equal to 400` ([run on #2000](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/actions/runs/44723609722/job/136245352975)). The test is right: a `tap` on a 400 ms timeout reported `waitedMs: 399`. - Cause: a step built its deadline from one `Date.now()` and timed its wait from a second one. When the clock ticks between the two, the deadline expires while the wait still reads 1 ms short. - Fix: `LocatorEngine.deadline()` returns a `StepDeadline` (`packages/core/src/internal/time.ts`) that keeps the clock read it counts from. `tap` and the other actions, `waitFor`, `scrollUntilVisible`, and pointer actions report `deadline.elapsed()`, so a deadline that expired cannot report less than its timeout. - `StepDeadline` is internal. The `Deadline` engine authors import is unchanged, and `dist/engine/index.d.ts` does not mention the new class. - A resolve on a deadline it did not create (the scroll into view of `toHaveScreenshot`) still times itself, as before. - Not covered: a wait the engine's own timer cuts off just before the deadline still reports the time that passed, which can be under the timeout. That number is true, so it stays. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes Surface: the locator engine on fake time (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/locator-engine.test.ts`), plus the two integration files that assert `waitedMs` through the real CLI and runner. The new unit test makes the 1 ms gap happen every time: a 101 ms deadline, one tick, then the resolve, whose poll at 100 ms lands on the deadline. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `waitedMs: 100` on a 101 ms timeout, test fails | `waitedMs: 101`, test passes | ``` $ pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/cli-run.test.ts tests/integration/failure-evidence.test.ts Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 20 passed (20) ``` The CI failure itself is too rare to reproduce by rerunning the integration test, so the main column is the unit test with the one-line measurement put back.

title: feat(cli): run the selected mobile target on another device with e2e run --device
body: ## What and why - `e2e run --device ` runs the selected mobile target on another simulator, emulator, or phone for one run. It takes a name, UDID, or serial and replaces the target's `device` option. No config edit or env var needed: `e2e run --target ios --device 'iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)'`. - It applies to the one selected target whose engine selects a device. - With several selected (iOS and Android), the run fails with `TARGET_REQUIRED` and asks for `--target`. One device name rarely fits two platforms. - With none (`web()` only), it fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - On a target whose devices a `DeviceProvider` leases, it also fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. - Every refusal happens before any engine is prepared or test runs. - Engine contract: `EnginePrepareInfo.device` carries the name to `prepare`. An engine opts in with `selectsDevice: true`, which needs `prepare` and is carried by the manifest and the schema. `mobile()` declares it and binds that one device in `prepare`. Workers get it through the bindings `prepare` already hands them. - `e2e login --device` (ChatGPT device code) is unchanged. - Docs: the CLI reference, the engine reference, `errors.mdx`, the Maestro guide (the row moves from "Planned" to the map) and the mobile guide, in en/ja/zh where the page exists. Also the skill's `running.md` and its plugin copy. ## Issue Part of #1855, "Reporters and CLI": `npx e2e run --device "iPhone 16"`. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - On devices, through the built CLI. The config pins `ios` to `device: 'iPhone 17 Pro'` and `android` to a device that doesn't exist. - `e2e run --target ios --device 'iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)'` booted and drove the iPad. The test opened Settings and passed, and the iPhone was never booted. - `e2e run --target android --device emulator-5554` drove the Pixel 9 emulator (Android 16) by serial and passed. - `--target web --device …` gave `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`, `--target ios,android --device …` gave `TARGET_REQUIRED`, and `--device ' '` gave a usage error. - Tests: - New `run-device.test.ts`: the device reaches only the selecting target's `prepare`, `--target` picks among several, and the refusals. - Mobile unit tests: `prepare` binds the named device over a configured pool and over booted discovery, and a provider refuses it. - Protocol and schema: `selectsDevice` without `prepare` is refused. - Each of these breaks fails a test: dropping the device in `prepare`, dropping `selectsDevice` from the manifest, taking the first of several targets, and the mobile engine ignoring the device. - `pnpm check` passes. Mobile unit 559/559, e2e unit 4198/4198, e2e integration 120/121 files. The one failure is `bun-runtime.test.ts`, which fails the same way locally without this change. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [x] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

body:
A refactor with no behavior change. It's the base for #1972, which runs the MCP session's tools in the runner's worker to attach to a held test.

title: Replay cache keeps CJK counts followed by a copula (42件です) as anchors
body:
### What happened

Since #1837 and #1917, the replay cache reads `42件` and `42件を表示` as counts. A count followed by a copula is still kept as an anchor: `42件です`, `42件でした`, `총 42건입니다`, `42건이에요`, `42건이었습니다`, `42개예요`.

The word-end lookahead in `COUNT_TEXT` (`cache/anchors`) leaves out `で` because of `3行で書く`, so `です` never matches, and the Hangul check after `이` also rejects `이에요` and `이었`. A tally like `42件です` that grows with every run is recorded as an end anchor. The next run reads `43件です`, so `deltaMismatch` reports it missing.

kdy1 noted this as a follow-up in the last review on #1917.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Toraastrta/e2e-cjk-copula-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run repro`
3. Expected `42件です` to be dropped like `42件`, recording only `追加しました`. Instead it is recorded too, and the next run (`43件です`) reports it missing. The README shows the full output.

The script calls `describeDelta` and `deltaMismatch` from `@e2e-dev/core` in `e2e@0.24.1-nightly-20261120030209`, which includes #1917.

### Versions

e2e 0.24.1-nightly-20261120030209, node 24.15.0

### Engine

not engine specific

### Anything else

I have a fix ready that adds `です` and `でした` at a word end, and `입니다`, `이에요`, `이었`, `예요` and `였`, to the lookahead. `で` alone stays out, and so does `3行ですべて書く`. I can open a PR.

title: fix(cache): read CJK counts followed by a copula as counts
body: ## What and why - A CJK count followed by a copula (`42件です`, `총 42건입니다`, `42건이에요`) was kept as an anchor, so a growing tally made the next replay stale. kdy1 noted it as a follow-up on #1917. - Adds `です` and `でした`, and `입니다`, `이에요`, `이었`, `예요` and `였`, to the word-end lookahead in `COUNT_TEXT`. - `です` and `でした` only count at a word end. `で` alone stays out (`3行で書く`), and so do `3行ですべて書く` and `3個ですぐ届く`, where `で` is followed by another word. - Not covered: plain and other polite forms such as `42件だ`, `42件ですが`, `42건이다` and `42건입니까`. ## Issue Fixes #2004 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The repro in the issue, run on the nightly and on this branch's built `@e2e-dev/core`: | | main (`0.24.1-nightly-20261120030209`) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `42件です` then `43件です` | recorded as an end anchor, next run reports it missing | not recorded, replay passes | | `총 42건입니다` then `총 43건입니다` | recorded, next run reports it missing | not recorded, replay passes | | `42건이에요` then `43건이에요` | recorded, next run reports it missing | not recorded, replay passes | | `42件を表示` then `43件を表示` | replay passes | replay passes | - Deleting any single part of the new lookahead fails at least one test, and so does loosening `です` to match before another word. With the pattern on `main`, the 8 copula cases fail. - Old and new pattern over 1,602 counter and suffix combinations: only the copula forms above become counts, and nothing stops being one. `でも`, `では`, `できる`, `입구`, `이동` and `예정` are unchanged. I used Claude Code to draft the change. A fresh-context review found the `3行ですべて書く` case, which is fixed here. I checked the cases and results myself. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(core): stop launch() hosts from driving one mobile device
body:
Without a `session` option, two `launch(mobile())` hosts, or a host and the test's own device, no longer drive one simulator. Each host draws a random token and hands it to its engine as `hostId` on `prepare`, `init`, and `finish`. The mobile engine adds it to the agent-device session name (`e2e-ios-<hostId>-0`), so each host gets a session of its own. The target keeps the name it was given.

## Why it happened

- An unnamed `launch()` target is named after its platform (`packages/core/src/config/targets.ts:160`), and every host starts as worker slot 0 (`packages/core/src/run/standalone.ts`, `openWorker`).
- So every host drove the agent-device session `e2e-ios-0` (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`, `DevicePool.session`), the same name a runner worker on an unnamed `ios` target uses.
- `prepare` keeps a device held by one of the target's own session names (`BootedDevices.bind`, `packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`). The host took the device another live host, or the test's worker, was driving, and the two resumed one session.
- #1935 made a `launch()` host inside a test part of that test, so a second phone beside the test's device is now a supported pattern.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W[worker: target ios, slot 0] -->|e2e-ios-0| D1[iPhone 17]
  H1[launch host] -->|main: e2e-ios-0| D1
  H1 -.->|this branch: e2e-ios-hostId-0| D2[iPhone 18 Pro]
```

## What changed

- **Contract.** `EnginePrepareInfo`, `EngineInitInfo`, and `EngineFinishInfo` extend a new `EngineHostIdentity` (`packages/core/src/engine/contract.ts`) with an optional `hostId`. It is set for a `launch()` host and absent for `e2e run`. The protocol client spreads the info, so the field crosses the wire with no protocol change. `docs/reference/engine.mdx` (and its ja and zh copies) mirror it.
- **Core.** `launch()` draws a 96-bit token per host (`packages/core/src/core/launch.ts`) and passes it to `openCoreHost`, which hands it to `PreparedEngines` (`prepare` and `finish`, `packages/core/src/run/provision.ts`) and to `EngineSessions.initEngineOnce` (`packages/core/src/run/engine-sessions.ts`). Hosts in other processes, worker threads, or a second copy of `@e2e-dev/core` draw tokens of their own.
- **Mobile.** `DevicePool.session` takes the info and returns `e2e-<target>-<hostId>-<slot>` when `hostId` is set (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`). Inventory, `bind`, `warm`, and `init` build the name the same way, so `init` resumes the session `prepare` warmed. The `session` option still wins.
- **Bindings variable.** The variable `prepare` hands a slot's device to the workers in now includes `hostId` in its digest (`bindingsVariable`, `packages/mobile/src/bindings.ts`). A host opened inside a test inherits the run's environment, where the run's own bindings for a target of the same name already sit; a host's worker without the bindings in memory (an engine served in another process) would otherwise read the run's and drive the test's device.
- **Artifact folders.** A host's folders are named `core/host-<hostId>-<attempt id>` (`packages/core/src/run/standalone.ts`), no longer after the target. A custom engine's platform can be a secret's value, and on main a host with `artifactsDir` wrote that value into a folder name, which redaction never reaches.
- **Finish.** The mobile engine's `finish` forgets the target's device bindings. Otherwise one `mobile()` engine reused by host after host kept every finished host's device and daemon address. For a `launch()` host, `finish` also fails when a session it warmed did not close (agent-device refused, or the close was still pending at the cleanup budget), so `host.close()` throws with the session's name. Nothing else would free that device, since no later host or worker uses the name. A session agent-device no longer has (`SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, what the fallback close meets after the worker closed it) counts as closed; a run's worker and a `session` option keep their names and stay quiet.
- The agent-device daemon refuses a second session on a held device (`DEVICE_IN_USE`), so a conflict now fails with an error that names the holder instead of two hosts tapping one screen.
- `docs/core.mdx` gets a "Several hosts on devices" section: one free device per host, opening hosts one after another, opening each host's app before launching the next when the target names only `appPath`, and how to free a leaked session.

## For the reviewer to decide

- **A host inside a test needs a device the run left free.** A local run drives as many booted devices as it has workers and files. With 2 workers and 2 simulators, each test's host now fails with "every booted ios device is held". On main it silently shared the worker's device. The docs say to leave one free with `--workers` or the target's `device`.
- **Hosts that open at the same moment.** Two hosts opened with `Promise.all` read the same free device in `prepare`. One opens and the other fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE ... is owned by session "e2e-ios-<hostId>-0"`.
- **A program that exits without closing its host**, or a worker the scheduler kills, leaves the agent-device claim. Later hosts and `e2e run` workers skip that device until the session is closed. On main the shared name let the next host or worker take it back.
- **With a `session` option** every host still uses `<session>-0`, as the option documents.
- **Visible name.** The token shows in two places only: the host's agent-device session name and its artifact folder. A fixture's `targetName`, a step executor's `target.name`, `onNotice` lines, runtime errors, the replay cache key, and hosted providers' session names and tags all keep the target's name (`ios`, or the engine's name).
- **The fix needs both packages.** A new `@e2e-dev/core` with an older `@e2e-dev/mobile` keeps the bug: the old pool ignores `hostId`. `@e2e-dev/mobile` now needs `@e2e-dev/core` `>=0.24.1 <1`, the first release that sends `hostId`.
- **Bump.** A host that silently shared a device now fails when no free device is booted, and a host that ends without `close()` leaves its device held. The changeset says both and bumps `@e2e-dev/core`, `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, and `@e2e-dev/web` as `patch`, not marked `**Breaking:**`.

## Follow-up work

- **Hosts opened at the same moment.** The pool should retry a discovered slot on the next free device when agent-device refuses with `DEVICE_IN_USE` (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`), and never retry a device the config names or a provider leased. In progress on a local branch.
- **MCP `open_session` and `openHost`.** Two MCP sessions on one target still drive one device, on main too. Both can now pass a `hostId` of their own the same way, leaving the target name that keys their test ids, artifacts, and replay cache alone.
- **Targets with only `appPath`.** A device is held only once an app opens. Holding it at launch needs a way to claim a device without opening an app. The docs cover it until then.
- **A program that exits without closing a host.** Stays documented: guessing that a session was abandoned could take a device from a live host. `agent-device close --session` frees it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Two booted iOS simulators (iPhone 17, iPhone 18 Pro), agent-device 0.21.40. main at the merge base `1b007d4d7` and this branch at `8e0695b29`, each built in its own worktree.

- Runner: a scratch project per build whose `node_modules/e2e` and `node_modules/@e2e-dev/{core,mobile}` link to that build's packages, with one unnamed `ios` target. Its test opens `launch(mobile({ platform: 'ios' }))` beside its own `device`, taps on both, and throws if both report one device id. From the project, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run --no-cache --workers 1`.
- Program: two hosts in one process, opened one after the other (`node two-hosts.mjs seq`) and with `Promise.all` (`node two-hosts.mjs par`). Each host taps its own screen once both open.
- Mutation: a mobile `init` that names its session without `hostId`, and a bindings variable without it, each fail a unit test.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runner test: worker device and `launch()` device | both `e2e-ios-0` on iPhone 17, test fails | `e2e-ios-0` on iPhone 17 and `e2e-ios-<hostId>-0` on iPhone 18 Pro, passes |
| Two hosts, one after the other | both `e2e-ios-0` on one simulator, one host's step fails (`LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND`), 2 of 2 | one per simulator, both steps pass, 3 of 3 |
| Two hosts with `Promise.all` | not rerun here; at `9d240ac95` (2026-11-18) both hosts drove one simulator and one step failed | one opens, the other fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE` naming the holder, 2 of 2 |

```text
main (1b007d4d7)
WORKER e2e-ios-0 on iPhone 17
LAUNCH e2e-ios-0 on iPhone 17
   × |ios| tests/two.e2e.ts > a second phone beside the worker device 24.99s

this branch (8e0695b29)
WORKER e2e-ios-0 on iPhone 17
LAUNCH e2e-ios-d10ee930539221bb21d8119f-0 on iPhone 18 Pro
```

title: feat(expect): expect(fn).toPass() and expect.poll intervals
body:
Closes the Playwright and Cypress parity gap from the 2026-11-10 framework audit: a block of assertions could not be retried as one unit, and `expect.poll` took one fixed pause.

- `expect(fn).toPass({ timeout, intervals })` retries a block until it stops throwing. `.not.toPass()` and `expect.soft(fn).toPass()` work too.
- `expect.poll` takes `intervals`, a list of pauses whose last entry repeats.
- A `test.skip()` or `test.fixme()` inside a block or a read ends the retry and reports `skipped`.
- A `test.setTimeout()` call during a retry moves the retry's deadline.
- A top-level `toPass` config key sets the default `timeout` and `intervals`.
- Both APIs run on one retry loop, `packages/e2e/src/expect/retry.ts`.

```ts
await expect(async () => {
  const response = await fetch(`${app.baseUrl}/api/orders/42`);
  expect(response.status).toBe(200);
  await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Ready', { timeout: 200 });
}, 'the order is ready').toPass({ timeout: 5_000 });

await expect.poll(() => readStatus(), { intervals: [100, 250, 500] }).toBe('done');
```

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
toPass: { timeout: 30_000, intervals: [100, 500, 2_000] },
```

## Deprecated

- `interval` on `expect.poll` is deprecated in favor of `intervals`. It still works as `intervals: [interval]` and prints a one-line warning the first time it is used in a process. Removal is no earlier than April 1, 2027, per the window in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- The default pauses for `expect.poll` are `[100, 250, 500, 1000]` ms, the same as Playwright and `toPass`. They were a flat 100 ms.

## Behavior changes to existing `expect.poll`

These are in the docs and not in the changeset, which only lists what was added and what is deprecated.

- Steps still running in a poll read are cancelled when the read fails or is cut at the deadline, and later step calls from that read are refused. On main they kept running. Without this, a cut `toPass` block keeps acting on the app while the test moves on.
- A poll that reaches the test deadline fails the test with `TEST_TIMEOUT`, and its last failed sample goes under `secondaryErrors`. On main the same test reported `TEST_TIMEOUT` or `ASSERTION_FAILED ... stopped at the attempt deadline` depending on which timer fired first.
- In `beforeAll`, `afterAll`, and worker fixture teardown, a poll uses `config.assertionTimeout` in place of a fixed 5000 ms and is capped by the hook deadline. A hook timeout message includes the last failure.
- A call `timeout` above 2147483647 ms is `INVALID_CONFIG`. On main Node clamped it to 1 ms.
- A read or block that overruns the time it had when it started no longer passes. On main a synchronous read that ran past the deadline could still pass.
- Call options must be a plain object with known keys, and `intervals` entries must be positive integers.
- With the backoff default, the last read can come up to 1 s before the deadline. A value that turns right in that window passed on main and fails now. Playwright behaves the same way.

## Differences from Playwright that remain

- A throwing `expect.poll` read is retried. Playwright fails the poll.
- `toPass` is not a report step. The steps inside each try are, so a passing test can show failed steps from its early tries.
- The config key is top-level `toPass`, where Playwright has `expect.toPass`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed, built CLI: `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/topass-manual.e2e.ts`, a scratch file of nine cases on the `/controls` page (not in this PR). Four pass, five fail on purpose with the error each title names:

```text
 ✓ |web| toPass manual: these pass > a block passes after a few tries 1.44s
 ✓ |web| toPass manual: these pass > not.toPass passes on the first throw 67ms
 ✓ |web| toPass manual: these pass > expect.poll takes a list of intervals 1.41s
 ✓ |web| toPass manual: these pass > parallel assertions in a block pass on a later try 2.11s
 × |web| these fail on purpose > fails with ASSERTION_FAILED, the message, and the last error 924ms
   → expect(...).toPass() timed out after 800 ms
 × |web| these fail on purpose > fails with one soft assertion after the last line ran 445ms
   → 1 soft assertion failed
 × |web| these fail on purpose > fails with STEP_NOT_AWAITED at the toPass line 116ms
   → the test body returned before expect(...).toPass() finished; put `await`…
 × |web| these fail on purpose > fails with TEST_TIMEOUT when the block has no timeout (timed-out) 1.59s
   → test timed out after 1500 ms in phase body
 × |web| these fail on purpose > fails with INVALID_CONFIG for interval and intervals together
   → expect.poll cannot take both interval and intervals
```

- The failure a user reads when a block never passes:

```text
ASSERTION_FAILED: expect(...).toPass() timed out after 800 ms
Publish never enabled
last: expect.toBeEnabled failed
locator: getByRole("button", name: "Publish")
expected: enabled
observed: states: disabled (match count 1)
```

- `toPass()` with no timeout in `beforeAll`, with a block that always throws and a 1000 ms hook timeout:

```text
 ERROR  test error HOOK_FAILED (beforeAll)
beforeAll failed: beforeAll hook timed out
expect(...).toPass() stopped at the attempt deadline after 1001 ms
last: db not ready
```

- The test that reports `TEST_TIMEOUT` used to alternate between two error codes. `tests/integration/expect-poll-scope.test.ts` passed 15 of 15 runs after the fix and failed about 1 run in 5 before it.
- The committed testbed case is `apps/testbed/tests/controls.e2e.ts`, "retries a block until Publish is enabled and matches the enabled query".

Not done: the shortening pass `ship-pr` asks for on the three guide pages this touches (`docs/debugging.mdx`, `docs/migrate/playwright.mdx`, `docs/migrate/cypress.mdx`). Each has a one-line or one-row edit, and the rest of each page is left word for word.

title: fix(mobile): fail toHaveScreenshot with POLICY_DENIED when a secure field can't be masked
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 opened this PR on behalf of samanyudas. samanyudas has reviewed it yet.**

## Issue

Fixes #1996

## What changed

On mobile, `toHaveScreenshot` waited out its timeout and failed with `ASSERTION_FAILED` ("the engine returned no screenshot") when a secure field on screen could not be masked.
On the web, the same case fails at once with `POLICY_DENIED`, which is what the docs promise.
This PR follows the design in the [triage comment](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/1996#issuecomment-7037063442) and the [review](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/2014#pullrequestreview-6000150983).
The three docs pages the issue names stay unchanged.

- The mobile engine checks the secure fields' bounds from the tree before it takes a device screenshot (`secureBounds` in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`).
  When a secure field has no bounds, no screenshot of that screen can be masked, so it takes none and reports `maskedRegionCount: 0` without `pixels`.
  A screenshot that failed, or an image it cannot read, on a screen whose secure fields all have bounds still reports no count, so the matcher takes another one as on main.
- The engine contract allows that shape: `maskedRegionCount` without `pixels`, in answer to a pixels request, means withheld (`EngineSnapshot.maskedRegionCount`, `docs/reference/engine.mdx`).
- The session is now the one place that decides withheld pixels (`packages/core/src/engine/session.ts`).
  It keeps `pixels` on an observation only when the masked regions cover every secure node (`pixelsProvenMasked`).
  When the engine answered a pixels request with pixels or a count short of that, the observation gets `pixelsWithheld: 'MASKING_UNPROVEN'` instead, the token the agent already uses for unproven pixels.
  Fallback pixels for an unavailable tree have no secure node to count, so they rest on the engine's own proof (the web engine sends them only when its masking is proven).
- `toHaveScreenshot` fails with `POLICY_DENIED` on a withheld observation, before it treats missing pixels as "not yet" (`packages/e2e/src/expect/screenshot-capture.ts`).
- The agent passes the token on, so a model reads `MASKING_UNPROVEN` and no longer reads "this engine captures no pixels" (`UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`) (`clearPixels` in `packages/core/src/agent/observation.ts`).
  The matcher and `clearPixels` read only that field and no longer check the masking themselves.
- `app.screenshot()` on the same screen fails with `POLICY_DENIED` (exit 2), not `ENGINE_FAILURE` (exit 3), as AGENTS.md asks for withheld pixels (`maskedScreenshot` in `packages/mobile/src/surface.ts`, listed in `docs/reference/app.mdx`).
  A failed capture, or an image it cannot read, on a screen whose secure fields all have bounds keeps `ENGINE_FAILURE`.
  Failure evidence and agent evidence screenshots catch every error, so they are unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T{mobile: every secure field has bounds?} -->|no| C[count 0, no screenshot taken]
  T -->|yes| S[device screenshot]
  S -->|masked| B[pixels + count]
  S -->|failed or unreadable| D[nothing]
  B --> E{session: count covers secure nodes?}
  C --> E
  E -->|yes| P[pixels kept]
  E -->|no| F[pixelsWithheld: MASKING_UNPROVEN]
  F --> G[toHaveScreenshot: POLICY_DENIED at once]
  F --> H[agent: MASKING_UNPROVEN]
  D --> I[toHaveScreenshot keeps polling]
```

A runner and engine on different versions stay safe.
A new runner with an old `@e2e-dev/mobile` gets no count and behaves as before.
An old runner ignores a count without pixels.
So no peer floor changes.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes.
No Android SDK or iOS simulator is available here, and a real secure field always reports bounds, so the masking failure has to be forced.
The surface is the built `e2e run` CLI driving the built `@e2e-dev/mobile` `AgentDeviceSurface` over a scripted agent-device client.
That client serves a sign-in screen whose secure PIN field reports no bounds, plus a real 390x844 PNG screenshot.

| | main (`1b007d4d7`) | this branch (`660339fdb`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PIN field without bounds, `toHaveScreenshot` | `ASSERTION_FAILED: the engine returned no screenshot`, after the full 3 s poll (exit 1) | `POLICY_DENIED: expect.toHaveScreenshot could not prove every secure field on screen was masked, so the screenshot is not kept`, in 65 ms (exit 2) |
| PIN field without bounds, device screenshot fails | `ASSERTION_FAILED` after polling | `POLICY_DENIED` in 42 ms: no screenshot is taken |
| PIN field without bounds, first screenshot a truncated PNG | `ASSERTION_FAILED` after polling (from reading the code, not run by me) | `POLICY_DENIED` in 45 ms |
| PIN field with bounds | screenshot written | baseline written, the next run passes (PIN row black, `[0,0,0]`, checked at an earlier head) |
| PIN field with bounds, device screenshot fails | `ASSERTION_FAILED` after polling | same: `ASSERTION_FAILED: the engine returned no screenshot` after 3.05 s |
| PIN field with bounds, first screenshot a truncated PNG, baseline stored | passes (from reading `capturePixels` on main, not run by me) | passes: an unreadable image is no screenshot, so the matcher takes another |
| `app.screenshot()`, PIN field without bounds | `ENGINE_FAILURE`, exit 3 (reviewer run, not mine) | `POLICY_DENIED: a secure field on screen has no bounds to mask, so the screenshot is withheld`, exit 2 |
| `app.screenshot()`, PIN field with bounds, device screenshot fails | `ENGINE_FAILURE`, exit 3 | same |

- The new tests fail on main's source and pass here.
- Each of these breaks fails a test:
  - The session keeps unproven pixels, marks only a count without pixels, or marks a count no pixels request asked for.
  - The agent drops the masked-region count from the pixels it passes on.
  - The matcher ignores the token, or `clearPixels` drops it.
  - Mobile takes the device screenshot before it checks the bounds, in `observe` or in `app.screenshot()`.
  - Mobile skips a secure field without bounds, counts fields that aren't secure, or reports an unreadable image as withheld.
  - `app.screenshot()` on a field without bounds throws `ENGINE_FAILURE` again, or `POLICY_DENIED` as an engine error instead of a configuration error (exit 2).
- `pnpm check` passes.
  `@e2e-dev/mobile` passes 563 of 563.
  The e2e unit and integration files that cover the session, the matcher, and the agent's observation pass 227 of 227.
- Testbed default suite at `4baf80328` (before the `app.screenshot()` hunk): 595 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed (`controls.e2e.ts:248`, listed below).

## Open decisions

- Open PR #1953 (the `@e2e-dev/desktop` engine) withholds pixels the same way and reports no count, so its `toHaveScreenshot` would still wait and fail with `ASSERTION_FAILED`.
  Once this lands, it can report `maskedRegionCount` when it withholds, as `docs/reference/engine.mdx` now describes.
- The triage comment scoped the issue to the matcher.
  This PR also moves `app.screenshot()` to `POLICY_DENIED`, because it fails on the same line for the same cause.
  If you want this PR limited to the matcher, the `maskedScreenshot` hunk, its test lines, and the `app.mdx` row revert cleanly.
- `docs/reference/errors.mdx` says the [Policy denials](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/main/docs/reference/security.mdx#policy-denials) table in `security.mdx` lists every case.
  It has a `toHaveScreenshot()` row and now lacks an `app.screenshot()` row.
  The triage asked to leave `security.mdx` unchanged, so this PR doesn't add it.

Not fixed here, and older than this PR:

- On a screen with no secure field, the mobile engine ships a screenshot without decoding it, so a truncated PNG with a readable header reaches `toHaveScreenshot` and fails it with a decode error instead of a retry.
  Main has the same path and the same `decodePng` call in the matcher.
  A follow-up could treat an undecodable capture as missing in the matcher.
- The `agent.assert({ vision: true })` judgment prompt doesn't say why pixels are missing when they are withheld.
  The web engine's unproven pixels already reach it this way on main, and `prompts.ts` is unchanged here.
  The acting agent's screen does name `MASKING_UNPROVEN`.

Not related to this diff, seen while running the full suites on a loaded machine (load average 11 to 25 on 8 cores):

- `secret-ledger.test.ts` "reads a large text with single spaces in about its own size" failed its 5 s wall-clock bound twice in full runs and passed 3/3 alone.
- `set-input-files.e2e.ts:181` (large file upload) failed once in a full testbed run and passed alone.
- `controls.e2e.ts:248` (a button that opens no file chooser) failed twice in full testbed runs and passed 20/20 alone.
  Its 500 ms budget runs out first and it reports "did not become actionable" instead of "opened no file chooser".

Reviewed with sol-loop: 5 rounds with GPT-6.2 Sol. Sol verdict: approved

title: feat(cli): show --step keys under the summary and view the screen and app log
body:
`e2e run --step` and `screen.pause()` now show their keys under the live summary, as `--watch` does, and you can look at the screen and the app log while a step is held.

## What changed

- The key hints moved from inside the running tree to the last rows of the live window. The held step stays under its test, with `⏸` in place of `▶`.
- `s` shows the screen's accessibility tree and `l` shows the attempt's app log, in a scrolling viewer on the terminal's alternate screen. `p` prints the shown text above the live window so it stays in scrollback.
- The app log is read from the worker during the hold, through a `logs-request` and `logs-reply` message pair beside `screen-request`.
- Held time is left out of the run's duration. The terminal's `Duration` row stops while a step is held, and the report has a new `run.durationMs`. With several workers, an interval counts as held only while every running worker is held.
- The prompt's step number is now the step's position in the trace, so the prompt, the app log view, and the trace page use one number.

```text
 ❯ |web| tests/checkout.e2e.ts 0/1
   └── pays with a card (k3f9)
       ✓ app.open "/checkout" 412ms
       ⏸ step 2  locator.fill "getByLabel("Email")"  tests/checkout.e2e.ts:9

 Test Files  0 passed (1)
      Tests  0 passed (1)

Paused (k3f9) at step 2
  press enter to run this step, press h to show help, press q to quit
```

## Viewer

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Up, Down, `k`, `j` | Scroll one line |
| Page Up, Page Down, `b`, Space | Scroll one page |
| `g`, `G` | Go to the top or bottom |
| `s`, `l` | Switch to the screen or the app log |
| `p` | Close the viewer and print its text |
| `q`, Esc | Return to the prompt |

- While the viewer is open, the live window stops repainting and other writes to a terminal stream are held. They are written in order when it closes (`packages/e2e/src/run/process-output.ts`, `packages/e2e/src/report/live-window.ts`).
- The main screen and the cursor are restored on `q`, on Ctrl-C, when the hold ends, when the worker exits, and at process exit.
- The viewer works beside an MCP session attached to the same held test.

## Wire change: `run.durationMs`

- `report-1` gains an optional `run.durationMs`: the run's duration in milliseconds without held time. `run.startedAt` and `run.finishedAt` still record wall time.
- Schema, both fixtures, the builder, and `sdk-types.ts` change together.
- Markdown, the GitHub fold, the HTML report, telemetry, and the nightly examples script read it. Markdown, HTML, and the fold fall back to the timestamp difference for a report an older runner wrote.
- A new `run-hold` run event carries the held time to reporters. It is documented in `docs/reference/reporters.mdx`.

## Decisions to check

- With the key list open, there is no `press h to hide help` row. `--watch` has none either, and `h` still toggles.
- When `@e2e-dev/github` folds a rerun into the run before it, the footer duration is now the sum of the two runs. It used to span from the first run's start to the rerun's end, including the gap between them.
- Trace positions count nested steps, so the prompt's number can skip. After a held step with two recorded child steps, the next held step reads `step 5`, not `step 3`. `e2e run --step` without a terminal shows the same numbers.
- `ship-pr` asks for a shortening pass on `docs/debugging.mdx`. It was skipped on purpose: the page changes only where this feature needs it.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Testbed, built CLI in Ghostty, `e2e run <test> --step`. The attached video shows the footer, `h`, `s` with scrolling, `l` with three log lines, `p`, two steps, and `a`. The blue badges mark each key.
- The `Duration` row held at one value for four seconds at a prompt and continued from it. The final row and the report agree, for a run whose timestamps are 8.1 seconds apart:

```text
   Duration  2.73s (startup 91ms)
```

```json
{"startedAt":"2026-11-20T16:27:59.538Z","finishedAt":"2026-11-20T16:28:07.624Z","durationMs":2725}
```

- Ctrl-C inside the viewer leaves the alternate screen, shows the cursor, and exits 130.
- Not checked: Windows, and the viewer under `--watch` by hand. The integration tests cover Ctrl-C in the viewer under `--watch` and a pause without `--step`.

title: e2e doctor: check that an iOS app.appPath is a simulator build of app.bundleId
body:
### Problem

`e2e doctor` passes `app-path` once the `.app` exists (`packages/mobile/src/doctor.ts:70` only calls `stat`). The two iOS build mistakes I see most then show up mid-run, with errors that point somewhere else:

- `appPath` is a device build (`Debug-iphoneos`, `CFBundleSupportedPlatforms = iPhoneOS`). `device.installApp()` goes through, and `app.open()` fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE: ... Simulator device failed to launch dev.e2e.examples.swiftui.`
- The `.app`'s `CFBundleIdentifier` differs from `app.bundleId`. `device.installApp()` goes through, and `app.open()` fails with `... Hint: The app bundle is not installed on this simulator. Run install before open.`, right after the install.

In both cases doctor printed `✓ app-path` and `e2e run can start here` a minute earlier.

Reproduced with the SwiftUI example (`examples/with-swiftui`), built with `xcodebuild -sdk iphoneos CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` and `-sdk iphonesimulator`, on an iPad (A16) simulator, iOS 26.5, Xcode 26.6, e2e 0.24.0, @e2e-dev/mobile 0.12.8, agent-device 0.21.39. The test was `await device.installApp(); await app.open();`.

### Proposed API

No new API. For an iOS target with `app.appPath` pointing at a `.app` directory, the mobile engine's `app-path` check reads `Info.plist` and reports under the same id:

```
✗ app-path  [ios] /…/Debug-iphoneos/HelloApp.app is a device build (iPhoneOS); build for the simulator (-sdk iphonesimulator) or point app.appPath at a Debug-iphonesimulator build
✗ app-path  [ios] /…/HelloApp.app has CFBundleIdentifier com.example.hello, but app.bundleId is dev.e2e.examples.swiftui
```

Android, `.ipa`/`.apk` paths, and provider targets stay as they are.

### Upsides

- Catches both mistakes in `e2e doctor`, before a run, with the fix in the message.
- Keeps the `app-path` id, so `doctor-1` doesn't change.

### Downsides

- One `plutil -convert json` call (or a small binary-plist read) per iOS target in doctor.
- A physical-device target would need the opposite check (`iPhoneOS` expected). I'd keep it to simulators, or skip the platform check when the target selects a physical device.

### Alternatives

- Have `app.open()` explain the failure. That runs after install and depends on agent-device's error text; doctor is where setup gets checked.
- Fix it in agent-device's install. Possible too, but doctor already owns `app-path`.

### Which surface

CLI flags (`e2e doctor` output; no new flag)

I can build this, with unit tests on fixture plists and the doctor output from the SwiftUI example, if you agree with the approach.

title: secret-ledger.test.ts fails its 5 s wall-time cap on a loaded CPU
body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Samanyu Das**

`packages/e2e/tests/unit/secret-ledger.test.ts` fails "reads a large text with line breaks and indentation in about its own size" when other processes share its CPU:

```
AssertionError: expected 6876.720274000001 to be less than 5000
```

The test caps one `redactFragments` scan of an 8 MB text at 5 s of wall time (`secret-ledger.test.ts:453`). On one Linux machine (i7-10510U):

- Alone, the scan takes 1.5 to 2 s.
- Pinned to one CPU with three busy loops (`taskset`), it takes 5.8 to 10.2 s of wall time, and main's file fails 4 of 5 runs.
- I hit it once in a full `pnpm --filter e2e run test:unit` at a load average of 12. It passes 3 of 3 runs alone.

The scan's own CPU time stays at 1.4 to 2.5 s under the same contention, so the cap measures the machine's load, not the code.

title: test(e2e): time the redactFragments cost checks in CPU time
body:
## Issue

Fixes #2017.

## Why

- `secret-ledger.test.ts` caps one `redactFragments` scan of an 8 MB text at 5 s of wall time.
- Wall time grows when other processes share the CPU, so the test fails on a loaded runner with no change to the code.
- The 5 s cap catches a quadratic break table only on a slow machine. On an M-series Mac, a table grown by 64 entries instead of doubled passes it (review below).
- `scans a long text in one linear pass` is a ratio, so it holds on any machine. It fed single spaces only, so it never grew the break table.

## What changes

- The 8 MB cap reads the scan's own CPU time through `process.cpuUsage()`, still at 5 s. The memory and fragment checks in the same test are unchanged.

```ts
const cpu = process.cpuUsage();
const redacted = ledger.redactFragments(text);
const { user, system } = process.cpuUsage(cpu);
expect((user + system) / 1_000).toBeLessThan(5_000);
```

- `scans a long text in one linear pass` runs on single spaces and on line breaks with indentation (`packages/e2e/tests/unit/secret-ledger.test.ts:460`).
  - It reads CPU time instead of `performance.now()`.
  - It compares 10,000 against 320,000 repeats with a bound of 96, where it compared 20,000 against 160,000 with a bound of 24. Linear cost reads about 32.
  - At the old sizes, a break table grown by 64 reads about 22, under the old bound. The wider spread lets the quadratic term show.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

One Linux machine (i7-10510U, 8 threads), `pnpm --filter e2e exec vitest run tests/unit/secret-ledger.test.ts`.

The 8 MB cap, pinned with `taskset` to one CPU shared with three busy loops:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unmutated, pinned with 3 busy loops | failed 4 of 5 runs (`expected ... to be less than 5000`) | passed 10 of 10 runs |
| `redact.ts` break table grown by `+64` instead of doubled, no pinning | | failed 3 of 3 runs, 16 to 28 s of CPU time |
| The same mutation, pinned with 3 busy loops | | failed 2 of 2 runs, 20.6 and 21.9 s of CPU time |

The line-break ratio case, at load average 4 to 12:

| | ratio (bound 96) | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unmutated, standalone script | 37 to 41 | |
| Unmutated, the test file | | passed 4 of 4 runs |
| Break table grown by `+64`, standalone script | 253 | |
| Break table grown by `+64`, the test file | 323 and 375 | failed 2 of 2 runs |

- The single-space case reads 31 unmutated and is not affected by the `+64` mutation, since that text builds no break table.
- `pnpm --filter e2e run test:unit`: 4229 passed, 2 skipped, the 8 MB and ratio tests included under full-suite load.
- The two ratio cases took 1.5 s and 2.0 s here. That adds a few seconds to each unit job.
- Vitest's 30 s `testTimeout` still limits wall time.

## Limits

- A break table grown by a larger constant, such as 256 or 1024 entries at a time, is still quadratic but does not show at 320,000 repeats. Catching it needs a text several times larger, and I kept the test at its current length.

title: docs(security): document pages that hide a password field from e2e
body:
## Issue

Refs #2010. This is option 3 from [the triage comment](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues/2010#issuecomment-7044597380). Option 1, saving `Element.prototype.matches` in the context init script, waits for #1503, so the issue stays open.

## Why

- On the web engine, e2e decides whether a field is secure inside the page's main world: `el.matches(options.secureFieldSelector)` at `packages/web/src/in-page/read-semantics.ts:598` and `:1618`.
- If a page script replaces `Element.prototype.matches`, e2e reads a password field as a plain textbox, and the docs said that can't happen.

## What changes

- `docs/reference/security.mdx`, "Where redaction stops": a new item covers the case:
  - the observed screen and `inputValue` show the value
  - a failed `toHaveValue` prints the value
  - `getAttribute` and `toHaveAttribute` do the same when the HTML `value` attribute holds the password
  - configured secrets stay `<secret:name>`
  - screenshots still mask the field, unless it is in a closed shadow root and the page also replaces `querySelectorAll`
- The places that said password fields are always masked now link to that item:
  - the "The screen" row of the security reference's model-input table
  - `docs/agent-steps.mdx`
  - `docs/decision-models.mdx`, which also says the text model then sees the value and `type` can fill the field
  - `skills/e2e/references/agent.md`
- Lines that said a read of a *password field* is `POLICY_DENIED` now say *secure field*, as `screen.mdx` already does: `docs/reference/mcp.mdx` and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`. The skill edits are synced to `plugins/e2e/`.
- Pages that describe what e2e does with a *secure* field, such as `expect.mdx` "Secure fields", `screen.mdx`, and the `POLICY_DENIED` row, stay as they are. They remain true, because the hidden field no longer counts as secure.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

The testbed ran with the CLI built from main (`3e7d19de1`). The branch changes no code, so main and the branch behave the same. Each case loaded `<label>Password <input type="password" value="gen-Pw-918273"></label>`, once as is and once with `<script>Element.prototype.matches = () => false;</script>`.

| Read | without the script | with the script |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inputValue()` | `POLICY_DENIED` | `"gen-Pw-918273"` |
| `getAttribute('value')` | `POLICY_DENIED` | `"gen-Pw-918273"` |
| `inputValue()` / `getAttribute('value')` after `fill('typed-pw-777')`, no `value` attribute | not run | `"typed-pw-777"` / `null` |
| `expect(field).toHaveValue('nope')` | `POLICY_DENIED` | `ASSERTION_FAILED`, `trace.md` holds `value "gen-Pw-918273"` |
| `expect(field).toHaveAttribute('value', 'nope')` | `POLICY_DENIED` | `ASSERTION_FAILED`, the message holds the value |
| `inputValue()` on a configured secret (`admin-pass`) | `POLICY_DENIED` | `<secret:admin.password>` |
| Share of the field's screenshot pixels that are black (masked) | 100% | 100% |
| Same, closed shadow root, `querySelectorAll` replaced too | | 1.3% (unmasked, shows the bullets) |

title: web(): a typo'd browser name quietly runs chromium, a bad viewport fails every test late
body:
### What happened

`web()` checks most of its options at config load (`locale`, `userAgent`, `screencast`, ...) but not `browser` or `viewport`, so a bad value gets through:

- `browser: 'Firefox'` (or `'firefx'`, `'chrome'`, `'edge'`) loads fine and the run is green on headless chromium. `browserType` falls through to chromium for any string it doesn't know. the only hint is `chromium 159` in the report environment.
- `viewport: { width: '390', height: '844' }` (strings from env vars, say) loads fine, then every test fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE: connection failed: browser.newContext: viewport.width: expected integer, got string`, exit 3. `{ width: 0, height: 0 }` loads too and the page ends up with no size.

expected `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load for both, like `screencast.size` already does for the same `{ width, height }` shape.

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/3e7d19de16ea916ddfd761be3909cc873dd08a73/packages/web/src/browser-connection.ts#L148-L153

### Reproduction

https://github.com/kunalgoesbyken/e2e-repros (folders `browser-name` and `viewport`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `cd browser-name && npx e2e run`: 1 passed, the test logs a `HeadlessChrome/159` user agent. expected `INVALID_CONFIG` for `'Firefox'`.
3. `cd ../viewport && npx e2e run`: 1 failed, `ENGINE_FAILURE ... viewport.width: expected integer, got string`, exit 3. expected `INVALID_CONFIG`.

### Versions

e2e 0.24.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.1, node 26.3.0

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

### Anything else

i have a fix ready, it shares the `screencast.size` check with `viewport` and checks `browser` against `BROWSER_NAMES`. happy to open it.

title: fix(web): refuse an unknown browser name or a malformed viewport in web()
body: ## What and why - `web()` now throws `INVALID_CONFIG` at config load for a `browser` that isn't `chromium`, `firefox`, `webkit` or a provider, and for a `viewport` that isn't `null` or `{ width, height }` in whole pixels, each at least 1. - before, `browserType` ran chromium for any name it didn't know, so `browser: 'Firefox'` gave a green run on the wrong browser. a string or zero viewport loaded fine and then failed every test with `ENGINE_FAILURE` (exit 3), or left the page with no size. - the viewport reuses the `screencast.size` check (moved into `validatePixelSize`), so both report the same message and an unknown key the same way. - `docs/reference/web.mdx` gets the two Throws rows, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` mentions them. ## Issue Fixes #2036 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. `node probe.mjs ` on builds of `origin/main` and this branch: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `browser: 'Firefox'` | accepted | `INVALID_CONFIG: web({ browser }) must be one of chromium, firefox, webkit, or a browser provider, got "Firefox"` | | `viewport: { width: '390', height: '844' }` | accepted | `INVALID_CONFIG: web({ viewport }) must be { width, height } in whole pixels, each at least 1` | | `viewport: { width: 0, height: 0 }` | accepted | `INVALID_CONFIG: web({ viewport }) must be { width, height } in whole pixels, each at least 1` | | `browser: 'firefox', viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }` | accepted | accepted | | `viewport: null` | accepted | accepted | on the published 0.16.1, the [`browser-name` repro](https://github.com/kunalgoesbyken/e2e-repros/tree/master/browser-name) passes with a `HeadlessChrome/159` user agent and the [`viewport` repro](https://github.com/kunalgoesbyken/e2e-repros/tree/master/viewport) fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE ... viewport.width: expected integer, got string`. `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/unit`: 385 of 390 pass, including the new `web({ browser })` and `web({ viewport })` cases. the 5 failures are `install.test.ts` on Windows, they fail the same way on main for me. ## Checklist - title: web: setInputFiles with a path that doesn't exist is ENGINE_FAILURE (exit 3)
body:
### What happened

`setInputFiles` with a path that doesn't exist (a typo'd fixture, say) fails as `ENGINE_FAILURE`, which is infrastructure and exits 3:

```
ENGINE_FAILURE: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '...\missing-upload\fixtures\avatar.png'
```

playwright's ENOENT falls through `classifyActionError` to the last `ENGINE_FAILURE` line. one test with a wrong fixture path makes the whole run look like the infra broke, and with a button that opens a file chooser the button gets clicked before it fails.

the agent's `upload` already treats this as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`no file at ... under the project root`, `upload-paths.ts`), so i'd expect the same from the locator: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, exit 1.

https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/3e7d19de16ea916ddfd761be3909cc873dd08a73/packages/web/src/actions.ts#L236-L260

### Reproduction

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `cd missing-upload && npx e2e run`
3. the test fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE: ENOENT ...` and the run exits 3. expected `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and exit 1.

### Versions

e2e 0.24.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.1, node 26.3.0

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

### Anything else

title: fix(web): fail setInputFiles on a missing path as INVALID_ARGUMENT before clicking
body: ## What and why - `setInputFiles` now fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` when a path doesn't exist, a test error, exit 1. same idea as the agent's `upload`. - before, playwright's `ENOENT` fell through `classifyActionError` to `ENGINE_FAILURE`, so a typo'd fixture path made the run exit 3 like an infra failure. - the check is a `statSync` at the top of `uploadFiles`, so it runs before the element lookup and before a chooser button is clicked. a directory still goes through to playwright as before. - Throws row in `docs/reference/screen.mdx` and the skill's `writing-tests.md` updated. ## Issue Fixes #2038 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. the [`missing-upload` repro](https://github.com/kunalgoesbyken/e2e-repros/tree/master/missing-upload) (`setInputFiles('fixtures/avatar.png')` with no such file), published 0.16.1 vs a build of this branch: | | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | error | `ENGINE_FAILURE: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '...\fixtures\avatar.png'` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT: setInputFiles path does not exist: ...\fixtures\avatar.png` | | exit code | 3 | 1 | `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec vitest run tests/integration/upload-actions.test.ts`: 16/16. the 4 new cases (a file input and a chooser button, each through a locator and an element, with a missing file and a path under a file) fail on main and check that nothing got set or clicked. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; title: ci: drop stale review labels and let fork authors ask with /ready
body: ## What and why - `Ready for Human Review` only came off on a push, so it stayed on PRs that were no longer ready. At the time of writing 5 of 13 labeled PRs had a merge conflict. - Contributors from forks cannot add labels, so their PRs could never carry it. What changes: - `review-label.yml` also drops the label on a move back to draft, and a new `sweep` job removes it from every labeled PR with a merge conflict or a maintainer's standing change request. It runs on a push to main and when a review requests changes. - `review-verdict.yml` is a marker workflow. A `pull_request_review` run on a fork PR has a read-only token, so the sweep follows it through `workflow_run` and reads only live state. - `review-ready.yml`: the PR's author comments exactly `/ready`. The job adds the label or replies, in one comment edited in place, with what is missing. - `CONTRIBUTING.md` gets a "Ready for Human Review" section, `AGENTS.md`, the PR template, and the babysit and ship-pr skills point agents at it. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[push / draft] --> D[drop label] M[push to main] --> S[sweep labeled PRs] R[review requests changes] --> V[review-verdict] -- workflow_run --> S S -- conflict, change request, draft --> D C["/ready from the author"] --> G{gates} G -- pass --> L[add label] G -- fail --> N[reply with what is missing] ``` `/ready` gates (`scripts/review-label/gates.ts`): - no conflict, not a draft, no `needs:compliance`, no change request from a reviewer with write access - checks reported on the head, none failing or running, and no workflow run still held for a maintainer's approval (a first-time contributor's CI never starts until approved, and shows up in no check) - every review thread resolved; one somebody else opened needs the author's reply before the author resolves it - every comment from someone else, and every review summary a person wrote, has the author's 👍 `issue_comment` runs with a write token for any commenter, so `review-ready.yml`: - references no repository secret; the job token is scoped to `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `checks: read`, `statuses: read`, `pull-requests: write` - checks out only `scripts/review-label` from the default branch, never PR code, and installs nothing - passes the comment and the PR to the script as data (event file, API), never through an expression in `run` - writes only fixed strings, counts, logins, GitHub-built links, and check names cut down by `safeName` to comments and the log ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - `node scripts/review-label/sweep.ts --dry-run` against this repo: ``` would remove the label from #1797: merge conflict would remove the label from #1918: merge conflict would remove the label from #2002: merge conflict would remove the label from #2031: merge conflict would remove the label from 4 PR(s) ``` - `node scripts/review-label/ready.ts --dry-run` with a synthetic `/ready` event from each PR's author. A fork PR whose CI waits for approval: ``` #2037 is not ready: - changes requested by okwasniewski - GitHub is still computing whether it merges cleanly; comment `/ready` again in a minute - 5 workflow run(s) waiting for a maintainer to approve them, so CI has not run on the latest commit - 1 comment(s) or review(s) without your 👍: [1](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/2037#pullrequestreview-6004619390) ``` - A comment from someone other than the author, and one on a merged PR, print `nothing to do`. - Not run: the workflows themselves. `workflow_run`, `issue_comment`, and the token scopes can only be exercised from the default branch, so the first real runs happen after merge. A scope that turns out too narrow fails the job without labeling. Known limits: a fork can still remove CI workflows in its own PR, and a PR that edits `review-verdict.yml` only delays the change-request sweep until the next push to main. The label stays advisory.

title: feat(reporters)!: one live hook, interactive flag, and pause events
body:
Follow-up to #1936, before any of it is released. Proposal: ENG-1395.

- **One live hook.** `onEvent` is the only live hook. `onOutput` and `onStepPrompt` are gone, and with them the exported `StepPrompt`, `NumberedStep`, and `HeldStep`.
- **`interactive` replaces `printsTo`.** It means one thing: this reporter shows the run in the terminal, so the runner prints nothing itself. One reporter at most.
- **`collected` replaces `plan`.** It lists every test before the first one starts, with `repeatEach`. `plan` is still emitted right before it, deprecated, until April 1, 2027 at the earliest.
- **Step `source`.** A step's `start` progress names the test file line that called it, the same value its record has in the report.
- **`paused` / `resumed`.** A reporter can show a test that waits at `--step` or `screen.pause()`. It only observes: the runner still reads the keys and the `--step` commands.
- **stdout is never the runner's.** During a run the runner prints user output, run errors, and pauses on stderr only. Stdout holds what a reporter prints there.
- **`reportFiles` after a second Ctrl-C** has 5 seconds, where it had the full minute.
- **`--step` with the json reporter** works in a terminal. Stepped by commands it is still refused, since the run's log would hold the document.

```ts
interface Reporter {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly interactive?: boolean;
  onEvent?(event: RunEvent): void;
  reportFiles?(run: FinishedRun, signal: AbortSignal): readonly ReportFile[] | Promise<readonly ReportFile[]>;
  onRunFinished?(run: FinishedRun, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<ReporterSummary | void>;
  onSummary?(rows: ReporterSummary, run: FinishedRun): void;
}
```

```ts
{ type: 'collected'; total; files; repeatEach; tests: CollectedTestInfo[] }
{ type: 'output'; target?; pair; stream; text }          // no target: the runner process
{ type: 'step'; ...; progress: { phase: 'start'; kind; api; label; source? } }
{ type: 'paused'; testId; agent; repeat; target; titlePath; reason: 'step' | 'pause'; attachId; steps: PausedStep[]; keys: PausedKey[] }
{ type: 'resumed'; testId; agent; repeat; target }
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[user code prints] --> E[output event]
  E --> S{interactive reporter healthy?}
  S -- yes --> L[it shows the output]
  S -- no --> R[runner prints on stderr]
```

## Decisions worth a look

- **Only an interactive reporter's hooks write past the capture.** What any other reporter prints in `onEvent` or `onRunFinished` is still redacted user output, as on main, so a `console.log` in a custom reporter does not tear `list`'s live window. In `onSummary(rows, run)` every reporter prints to the stream it writes to, stdout included, redacted. Beside `json`, only the JSON report reaches stdout: what any other reporter writes there, an interactive one's hooks included, prints on stderr.
- **What a reporter prints while it is handed output is now redacted.** On main it went to the terminal as written. The stress suite caught a secret printed that way.
- **Config-load output moved to stderr too.** Otherwise `--reporter list,json` put a config's top-level `console.log` in front of the JSON.
- **An embedded run (`e2e/runner`) keeps output on its own stream.** The host owns both streams. With `json`, stdout is reserved for the report there too.
- **One interactive reporter at most**, built-in or not. `list({ stream: 'stdout' })` beside `json` is still refused.
- **An event's own fields are frozen.** Every sink gets the same object, so a reporter that assigns to one is quarantined. The records an event carries are shared, as on main; the docs say so.
- **Every `paused` gets a `resumed`**, also when its test or the run ends first. `h` at a prompt re-emits `paused` with the longer `keys`; the key wording lives in the CLI, the event carries it as data.
- **`--step` beside json needs a terminal on stdin, stdout, and stderr.** With `--reporter json` the CLI refuses up front; for a json reporter the config sets, the runner refuses when commands answer the steps. The screen and log viewer never opens on a stdout reserved for the report.
- **Events a sink triggers while it is handed one are queued**, so every sink sees `seq` in order.
- **`CollectedTestInfo`** is the public type name: `CollectedTest` is taken by the collector.

Structure: the runner's side of reporters moved to `run/reporter-host.ts` (`runner.ts` went from 1801 to 1569 lines), and pause pairing to `pauseEvents` in `run/step-hold.ts`.

Breaking for users: where output lands without `list` or `dot`. `plan` is deprecated, not removed, with no runtime warning: the runner cannot tell whether a reporter reads an event type. The changeset says both.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- testbed, built CLI, with a scratch interactive reporter that prints each event (`interactive: true`, `onEvent` only), on a test with `screen.pause()` in a pty. `h` then Enter:

```text
   │ runner: demo file loaded
collected 1 to run, 0 skipped, 2 left out
▶ pauses on the form
   app.open /forms  tests-reporter-demos/tests/pause.e2e.ts:4
   locator.fill getByLabel("Full name")  tests-reporter-demos/tests/pause.e2e.ts:5
⏸ pause at  tests-reporter-demos/tests/pause.e2e.ts:6: enter = resume, h = show help, q = quit
⏸ pause at  tests-reporter-demos/tests/pause.e2e.ts:6: enter = resume, s = show the screen, l = show the app log, q = quit
⏵ resumed
   locator.tap getByRole("button", name: "Save profile")  tests-reporter-demos/tests/pause.e2e.ts:7
✓ pauses on the form (passed)
```

- `--reporter json` with a reporter that only records events: stdout parses as the report, the test's `console.log` lines are on stderr.
- An interactive reporter that throws on `test-started`: one warning, then the runner prints the rest of the output on stderr.

```text
e2e: reporter "broken" threw on test-started: demo crash; ignoring it for the rest of the run
filling the form
a warning from the test
```

- Without a terminal, `screen.pause()` then `e2e run --step next`: the events file has `paused` with `keys: []` and then `resumed`.
- A scratch live page reporter (source line on the left, output on the right, over SSE) runs on the public contract alone.
- `--reporter list,dot`: `reporters "list" and "dot" both show the run in the terminal, where they would print everything twice; run one of them`.
- `pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test` and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` pass.

- New `tests/integration/reporter-stress.test.ts` runs reporters of every kind through the built CLI together: 12 hostile ones (throwing, rejecting, returning junk, assigning to events) beside `list`, a class-based one, printers in every hook, an interactive one that breaks mid-run at line 100 of 400, and 50 at once. The outcome, the report, and what a healthy reporter sees do not change, and no output line is lost or doubled.

Reviewed in four fresh-context passes (one before opening, then three rounds of a structure review and a correctness review each). No critical finding was left open. Declined, with reasons: dropping `total` and `files` from `collected` (kept for people moving from `plan`), merging `CollectedTestInfo` with `ListedPair` (its `id` is a result id), and deep-freezing events (result records are shared with the report builder).

title: chore(docs): fail the translation check on a repeated line
body: ## What and why - On [#2035](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/2035), a review suggestion was anchored on lines 291-292 of `docs/hi/mobile.mdx` but written for 292-293. GitHub replaced the anchored lines: the `device.clearKeychain()` sentence was deleted, the old line 293 stayed below its replacement, and `pnpm docs:check` passed. - `scripts/check-docs-translations.ts` now fails on a translated line of 12 or more characters that equals or ends the line above it in the same paragraph. That is the trace such a suggestion leaves when its last line keeps the old ending. A line that is only a tag (a nested ``) is left alone. It cannot see a deleted line. - The prose reader and `FRONTMATTER` move to `scripts/docs-prose.ts` with tests. The prose keeps one entry per source line, a blank one per code line, so the message names the line. The reason the check fails is stated once, on `repeatedLines` there. `AGENTS.md` and the check's header point to it. - `.github/filters.yml` covers `scripts/docs-*.ts`. Before, a change to `docs-pages.ts` or `docs-languages.ts` alone did not run the docs gate. `docs-translations.yml` adds `scripts/docs-pages.ts`, which `check-docs-translations-deepl.ts` imports. - `authoring-docs` "Translations" gains one bullet: after applying a suggestion on wrapped prose, reread the paragraph against the English page, since `docs:check` only catches a leftover repeated tail. ```text docs/hi/mobile.mdx:293: "लॉन्च पर नहीं रहता। `clearKeychain()` सिर्फ़ iOS पर है।" repeats the end of the line above it; a review suggestion likely replaced the wrong lines, so compare the paragraph with the English page A translation sits at the same path as its English page, has a title, no line repeats the end of the line above it, and each language has a navigation.json. See authoring-docs, "Translations". ``` ## Issue Part of #1890. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes | Tree | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | Real docs tree, `node scripts/check-docs-translations.ts` | exit 0 | exit 0, output byte-identical to main | | `docs/hi/mobile.mdx` from `b37c02fa2` (the broken #2035 head) | exit 0 | exit 1, names `docs/hi/mobile.mdx:293` | - The detector flags 0 lines on main across `docs/` (every language and English), `skills/`, and `.dev/skills/`. Across 1352 historical blobs of translated pages, it flags only the #2035 line. - Every rule in `docs-prose.ts` and the script's new lines has a mutation that a test kills (33 of 33). `scripts/check-docs-translations.test.ts` runs a copy of the script on a fixture docs tree, so removing the call fails a test. - `pnpm run test:scripts` passes 226 of 226, and `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run docs:check` exit 0, on the branch merged with main at `5acb82235`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: core: isModelRefusal throws a TypeError on ai < 7.0.88, though the peer range allows ^7.0.0
feat(test): add test.describe.only and the only option on describe
body: ## What and why - Adds `test.describe.only(title, fn)` and the `only` option on `describe`, the `test.describe.only('checkout', fn)` item of #1855. - A test inside a focused group registers with the same `only` mode `test.only` sets (`packages/e2e/src/collect/registry.ts`), so the existing focus rules and the CI rejection (`ONLY_IN_CI`) apply unchanged. - The innermost `only` wins: `only: false` on an inner group or a test opts it out. A skipped test or group stays unfocused and `filtered`, as beside `test.only`. - A serial group can be focused whole; `only` inside one is a `COLLECTION_ERROR`. ```ts describe.only('checkout', () => { test('pays by card', async ({ screen }) => {}); // runs describe('refunds', () => { test('refunds a card', async ({ screen }) => {}); // runs }); }); test('signs in', async ({ app }) => {}); // filtered ``` ## Issue Part of #1855 (`test.describe.only('checkout', fn)`, assigned to me). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed, built CLI: a file with a test outside, a `describe.only('checkout')` group with a nested group, and another unfocused group. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `COLLECTION_ERROR`: `describe.only is not a function` | the 2 tests in `checkout` run, nested one included; the rest are filtered | | - | with `CI=1`: `ONLY_IN_CI` | - New tests: `tests/integration/describe-only.test.ts` (focused groups beside a `test.only`, and `ONLY_IN_CI`), plus unit tests in `registry.test.ts` and `select.test.ts`. - The ja and zh reference pages keep the new `describe.only` section in English, as they do for `describe.fail`; the surrounding sentences and the migrate rows are translated. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [x] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(core): translate provider failures on ai releases before 7.0.88
body: ## What and why - `isModelRefusal` read `ToolChoiceViolationError` from `ai`, which exists only from 7.0.88. Core's peer range is `ai: ^7.0.0`, so on 7.0.0 to 7.0.87 every non-abort provider failure (4xx, 5xx after retries, rate limit) crashed with a `TypeError` instead of `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`. - The check now matches the error by name (`AI_ToolChoiceViolationError`) through a shared `isToolChoiceViolation` in `packages/core/src/agent/model/tool-choice.ts`, the matcher the forced-tool-choice checks in the same file already used for the same reason. - `AiSdk` (`packages/core/src/agent/ai-sdk.ts`) now omits `ToolChoiceViolationError`, so reading it from the loaded SDK is a type error, not an `undefined` at runtime. - Every other runtime export core reads (`generateText`, `jsonSchema`, `Output`, `asSchema`, `wrapLanguageModel`, `APICallError`, `NoObjectGeneratedError`, `RetryError`, `ToolLoopAgent`, `registerTelemetry`) exists in `ai@7.0.0`. `ToolChoiceViolationError` was the only one added later. - Tradeoff: keeping `^7.0.0` with this guard means the name check, not the SDK's `Symbol.for` marker, decides a refusal. That is the same check the tool loop already uses for this error. The alternative was raising the floor to `^7.0.88`, which is stricter on every brownfield project already on an older 7.x for no other gain. CI still type-checks against one `ai` version only, so the next late export would only be caught by review or by `AiSdk`. ## Issue Fixes #2048 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes The issue's repro (a `MockLanguageModelV4` that throws `APICallError` 400) against packed `@e2e-dev/core` installed with real `ai@7.0.35`: | `@e2e-dev/core@0.24.0` | this branch | | --- | --- | | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isInstance')` | `AgentError MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED model provider failed: Bad request` | - Same packed build on `ai@7.0.0`: plain call, structured call, and content-filter refusal (`MODEL_REFUSED`) all behave as on the current `ai`. - New `packages/e2e/tests/unit/ai-sdk-before-tool-choice-violation.test.ts` mocks `ai` without the export. It fails with the issue's `TypeError` when the old check is restored in `dist`.

title: acp: Claude Code step-tool calls (right_click_at, tap) intermittently flagged as the agent's own tools (POLICY_DENIED)
body:
## Summary

With the Claude Code executor (`claudeCode()` from `@e2e-dev/acp`), some `agent.act` steps fail with `POLICY_DENIED` because the agent supposedly ran "a tool of its own without asking". The tool names in those errors are step tools: `mcp__e2e_step__right_click_at`, and once just `tap`.

## Versions

- `e2e` 0.24.0, `@e2e-dev/web` 0.16.1, `@e2e-dev/acp` 0.1.3, `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.109.0
- `claudeCode({ model: 'sonnet' })`, signed in with a Claude Code login
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Node 24.21, Chromium from `@e2e-dev/web`, headless, `workers` at the default

## What happens

Each of these steps, in a React SPA, sometimes fails before it completes:

- `agent.act('create a new document named {title}')`, where the path starts from a right-click context menu
- `agent.act('create a new board')`, same path
- `agent.act('create a client organization named {name}, then close its fiscal profile')`

The errors as the report shows them:

```
POLICY_DENIED: agent.act failed: The agent ran a tool of its own without asking (mcp__e2e_step__right_click_at); only the step tools may act, so the step was stopped.
```

```
agent.act failed: The agent ran a tool of its own without asking (tap); …
```

It is intermittent: the same step passes on other runs or on retry. Steps whose path needs a right click hit it most often. In our runs every right-click path failed at least once out of four. Steps without a right click hit it rarely; we saw it once with `tap`.

## Expected

Calls of the step tools the runner offers (`right_click_at`, `tap`) are recognised as ours and allowed. Or, if `right_click_at` is not offered to this engine or executor, the agent is never shown it.

## What we looked at

In `@e2e-dev/acp/dist/session.js`, `isOurs()` treats a call as ours when one of these holds:
- `_meta.claudeCode.toolName` carries the `mcp__e2e_step__` prefix and a name in the session's tool set
- `rawInput` has the MCP call shape

Otherwise `observe()` reports the call as one of the agent's own as soon as it starts. Two possible causes fit what we saw, but we have not confirmed either:
- a `tool_call` or `tool_call_update` arrives before Claude Code's `_meta` is attached
- `right_click_at` is missing from the session's `ours` set even though the agent is offered it

## Workaround

We moved the right-click paths to locator steps (`locator.secondaryTap()`, or the app's launcher), and set `retries: 1`.

## Repro shape

Any web target whose create action lives in a context menu (`contextmenu` on a list region), with `agent.act('create a new X')` and the Claude Code executor. Run it a few times. I can share a sanitized `report.json` fragment if useful.

title: cache: a replay presses the same-named button in the wrong row when the button is the first thing in its row
body:
### What happened

A recorded `agent.act` step replays on another row than the one it was recorded on, and the test passes.

It happens when the tapped control has the same name as the other rows' controls and is the first text in its row, list item or card, like an `Archive` button in a table's first column. The cache keys a repeated control by its row's first text (`tap button "Reserve now" in "Offer B"`). Here that text is the button's own name, so no row is recorded, only the place: `tap button "Suspend" (2 of 5)`. On the next run the page still has five rows, with one new record on top, and the replay presses the second button again. That button now belongs to another customer.

In the repro, "Suspend the Acme Corp account" suspends Globex, reports `1 replayed` and passes, with and without `--strict-cache`. "Archive the invoice for Acme Corp" archives the Globex invoice first. The end check then sees the Acme row is still there and hands off, so the agent archives Acme too. Under `--strict-cache` that test fails with `REPLAY_STALE`, after the wrong invoice is archived.

When the button comes after the row's label, the same flows record `in "Acme Corp"` and replay on the right row.

### Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/JaynouOliver/48dcc765bcd43c892c3e33686af5471d

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put the five files in an empty folder, then `npm i` and `sh run.sh`. It starts the page server, runs the suite, puts one new customer on top of the list, and runs the suite again. No model is needed: a scripted executor in `e2e.config.ts` stands in for it and presses the button of the Acme Corp row.
2. Read the last block, which is what the app received. `sh run.sh --strict-cache` shows the strict run.

Actual, on the second run:

```
   ✓ archives the Acme Corp invoice > agent.act "Archive the invoice for Acme Corp" 14.70s
   ✓ suspends the Acme Corp account > agent.act "Suspend the Acme Corp account" 252ms
      Tests  2 passed (2)
      Cache  1 replayed · 1 handed off
== what the app did ==
APP archived the invoice of: Acme Corp
APP suspended: Acme Corp
APP archived the invoice of: Globex
APP archived the invoice of: Acme Corp
APP suspended: Globex
```

Expected: the second run acts on Acme Corp only, or hands off before it acts.

### Versions

e2e 0.24.0, @e2e-dev/web 0.16.1, node 22.23.4, Linux. The same on e2e 0.25.0-nightly-20261121030204 with @e2e-dev/web 0.17.0-nightly-20261121030204.

### Engine

@e2e-dev/web

### Anything else

`containerKey` (`packages/core/src/agent/actions.ts`) returns nothing when the row's first leaf text is the control's own name. A glyph button (`<button aria-label="Archive">×</button>`) records `in "×" (2 of 5)`, the same key for every row, and replays the same way.

I have a small fix: when such a control has twins, key it by the row's first text outside the control, if that text tells it from them.
