title: fix(desktop): fix input, read, cleanup, and launch bugs found reviewing #1953
body:
Four rounds of independent review of the `@e2e-dev/desktop` code that #1953 merged (codex gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, each on its own checkout), then a fresh-context review by gpt-6.2-sol. Every finding here was checked against the code, and agent-desktop 1.3.1's source where it mattered, before it was fixed. Each fix has a unit test that fails without it.

## What changed

Input reaches only the control it was aimed at:
- `typeText` types only into a focused control that offers `TypeText`. A replace clears with Cmd+A and Backspace, as the keyboard contract asks, and sends the Backspace only if the field still holds focus. Text over agent-desktop's 10,000-byte `type` limit, or with a NUL, is refused before any key is sent.
- A locator `press` on a look-alike checks that no twin came or went while it was focused (`likeness` on each binding).
- `press` refuses a character agent-desktop's macOS key map cannot press (`!`, `é`) before the control gets focus.
- A point tap is refused when another window took focus as the target came forward.
- `pressKey` waits out `settle`, as the other agent actions do.

Reads never pass as an empty screen:
- When `list-windows` cannot find the app (`APP_NOT_FOUND`) while its process still runs, the read is a retryable `NODE_STALE`. The same applies when the app list leaves out a live process that is still the launch's, which macOS does for a prohibited activation policy.
- `getByDisplayValue('')` finds an empty text field.
- Observation fields are cut at `OBSERVED_NAME_LIMIT` and `OBSERVED_TEXT_LIMIT`, as `packages/core/src/engine/contract.ts:131` asks of engines; `locate` still matches the whole text.
- A small app button named Close is kept unless it sits in the window's own row of title-bar buttons.

Cleanup and launch:
- The leftover-state sweep skips an entry that is not a real directory owned by the current user, so another user's planted record in a shared `/tmp` cannot get a process killed.
- A quit, and the next host on a reused `desktop()` handle, no longer lose track of the app: a failed dispose marks its record abandoned, `init` clears the last host's launch state, and a live process the app list leaves out is checked by start time or token before it counts as gone.
- `list-windows` and `list-apps` get the operation's budget (`--timeout-ms`), not agent-desktop's 5 s default.
- An open that shows no readable window says why: the screen is locked (asked of macOS, `CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the app opened no window, or its window cannot be read.

Errors and contracts:
- A screenshot that cannot mask a password field is `POLICY_DENIED`, as on the mobile engine, and `observe({ pixels: true })` reports `maskedRegionCount: 0` so the harness reads `MASKING_UNPROVEN`.
- A failed select says whether the option was chosen is unknown, and whether its menu was closed, is still open, or cannot be told.
- `desktop()` returns `DesktopEngine`, so a config that infers its type declares under pnpm (TS2883, the same fix #1976 made for web and mobile). `scripts/install-smoke.ts` now covers desktop.
- An install names why its rename failed, refuses a directory as the executable, and removes leftovers of killed installs once they are a day old.
- Unit tests get a private temp directory per file and a stand-in `ioreg`, so another checkout's run or the state of the Mac no longer changes their result.

Decided with the maintainer during review:
- `e2e run --headed` launches the app in the foreground. Physical input still needs `desktop({ headed: true })`, since the engine declares those capabilities when it is created.
- `selectOption` on an editable combo box is refused: agent-desktop's `select` writes the label as text there, so a missing option looks chosen. Use `fill()`.
- An off-screen control stays `hidden`, as on the mobile engine (`packages/mobile/src/nodes.ts:541`).

Docs: `docs/desktop.mdx`, the reference pages that list web and mobile (config, test, MCP, core, CLI), the package README, and `skills/e2e` running reference.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, partly. The Mac's screen was locked (`CGSSessionScreenIsLocked = true`), so fills, selects, key presses, and masked screenshots were not run live; the scripted agent-desktop unit suite covers them (193 passed, 1 skipped).

- `apps/desktop-testbed`, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/sign-in.e2e.ts` against the built packages, main and this branch. On a locked screen every test fails at `app.open()`, and main gives the wrong cause:

| main | this branch |
| --- | --- |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE: SignInForm launched in the background and opened no window. Some apps, such as document-based ones, show a window only once they come forward; set desktop({ headed: true }) for them` | `ENGINE_FAILURE: SignInForm launched, but the Mac's screen is locked, so no window can be read through accessibility; unlock it and run again` |

  Both runs quit the app and left no `e2e-agent-desktop-*` directory.
- `e2e doctor` on the testbed: agent-desktop 1.3.1, Accessibility, and `app-path` pass; Screen Recording warns (denied on this Mac).
- `node scripts/install-smoke.ts 11`: the config declaration step passes with a `desktop()` target, and the core-only project loads `@e2e-dev/desktop` without `e2e`.

title: fix(mobile): move a launch() host that loses a device race to the next free device
body:
Two `launch(mobile())` hosts opened at the same moment no longer fail when a second device is free. Without a `device` option, both hosts read the same booted device as free; the first one's warm-up claims it, and agent-device refuses the second with `DEVICE_IN_USE`. The losing host now moves that slot to the next free booted device. It fails only when none is left. This was the first follow-up listed in #2008.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[host A prepare] -->|inventory: iPhone 17 free| W1[warm iPhone 17: claims it]
  B[host B prepare] -->|inventory: iPhone 17 free| W2[warm iPhone 17]
  W2 -->|DEVICE_IN_USE, held by host A| M{discovered device?}
  M -- "main: no retry" --> F[ENGINE_FAILURE]
  M -- this branch --> R[next free device: iPhone 18 Pro]
```

## What changed

- `DevicePool.prepare` warms one slot at a time. When the warm-up throws `TakenDevice`, it records the refused device and asks `BootedDevices.replace` for the next booted device. That device must not be held, refused, or already driven by another slot (`DevicePool.prepare` and `BootedDevices.replace` in `packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`). Each refusal adds a device that `replace` never returns again, so a slot runs out of devices instead of looping.
- Only a device the pool found itself can move. A device the target names in `device`, or one a provider leased, is what the config asked for, so its refusal fails as before.
- `deviceHolder` (`packages/mobile/src/errors.ts`) reads the holder from agent-device's `DEVICE_IN_USE` refusal. It counts only refusals that mean another live session holds the device: a verified claim, a workspace session, or a session of the same daemon. A dead owner, a claim agent-device cannot verify, human control, and provider release each come with their own advice, so they are not treated as a race.
- A refusal by a short-lived agent-device command moves the slot too. agent-device claims a device as `transient:<command>` for the length of one boot, prepare, install, or push, and refuses with the live-owner reason. When the losing host's runner start meets the winner's `transient:prepare`, the slot moves to the next free device. When none is free, a refusal at the runner start or the app open keeps the device: the claim ends with the command, so the warm-up logs it and the worker starts, as on main. A boot it refuses with none free counts as a lost device: a host or a run's last slot fails, as on main, and a run with other slots left drops that slot. Only a claim refusal's `owner.session` is read as a short-lived command (`isShortLivedClaim`, `packages/mobile/src/errors.ts`); a session of the same daemon named `transient:smoke-0` is a live holder.
- The device `e2e run --device` names (#2002) is never moved, like one the config names.
- A slot that moves keeps its session name. `warmed` is now keyed by session name, so `finish` closes the slot's last client once. #2008's check that a `launch()` host's session actually closed still applies to that name.
- A slot that takes a dropped slot's number keeps the session it was bound under, carried in its binding (`SlotBinding.session`, internal to the package's worker environment), so its worker resumes that session. This matters when a device still holds this target's own session from an earlier run, which agent-device lets only that session use. `finish` closes every session the warm-up opened. A provider's own `session` field on a lease is ignored, like `leaseId`.
- `docs/core.mdx`, `docs/reference/mobile.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` (with its plugin copy) say a discovered device moves, and that a run with several workers goes on with one worker fewer when none is free.

## For the reviewer to decide

- **The bump is a patch.** If another live session refuses the device at the runner start or the app open, and no other device is free, a one-slot run or host now fails in `prepare` with agent-device's refusal, and a multi-worker run drops that slot. On main the refusal was logged and the worker failed when it started. The changeset says so. It bumps `@e2e-dev/mobile` only, as `patch`.
- **A multi-worker run that loses one slot's device goes on with one worker fewer.** With no `device` option, if another live session takes one slot's device during the warm-up and no other device is free, `prepare` drops that slot and reports one worker fewer. The slots after it take the numbers below before they warm, so each worker resumes the session it warmed under (`packages/mobile/src/pool.ts`, `prepare`). The runner already accepts fewer workers than it asked for (`withPreparedWorkers`, `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`), as it does when a device is held at inventory time. A `launch()` host, or a run whose last slot loses its device, fails with agent-device's refusal, naming the holder.
- **Targets with `appPath` can still collide.** Such a target opens nothing during warm-up, so no claim exists yet for the second host to meet. `docs/core.mdx` keeps its advice to open each host's app before launching the next one. A real fix needs a way to claim a device without opening an app (ENG-1420 item 3).

## Issue

Linear ENG-1420, item 1.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

Two booted iOS simulators (iPhone 17, iPhone 18 Pro), agent-device 0.21.41. main is `6fdb1c278`, each build in its own worktree. Two of the five `par` runs were on `b8a5f265f`, and the other rows on `2639e7a56`; the commits between them shorten a docs bullet and remove a cast and an interface, with no behavior change. The table below is the first round. The commits after `2639e7a56` (the short-lived refusals, the answer to kdy1's review, and the slot drop) ran again on the simulators at the head, `3db141275`, against main `b6e65ae37`; see "On the simulators at `3db141275`" further down. A scratch project for each build links `@e2e-dev/core`, `@e2e-dev/mobile`, and `e2e` to that build's packages.

- Program: `node two-hosts.mjs par` opens two hosts on `com.apple.Preferences` with `Promise.all`, then taps a different row on each host. `seq` opens the two hosts one after the other.
- Runner: a project with one unnamed `ios` target. Its test opens a `launch()` host beside the worker's own device and throws if both report the same device. Run with `e2e run --no-cache --workers 1`.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two hosts opened at the same moment (`par`) | 3 of 3 fail: `ENGINE_FAILURE boot failed: ios device C5655009-… is owned by session "e2e-ios-<hostId>-0"` | 5 of 5 pass: one host on each simulator, both taps pass |
| Two hosts one after the other (`seq`) | passes, one per simulator | passes, one per simulator |
| Runner test: worker device and `launch()` device | passes: `e2e-ios-0` on iPhone 17, `e2e-ios-<hostId>-0` on iPhone 18 Pro | passes, same split |

- The new unit test (`moves a discovered slot to the next free device…` in `packages/mobile/tests/unit/engine.test.ts`) fails with main's `pool.ts` and passes on this branch. It also fails under each of six mutants:
  - a refused device that does not count as held;
  - another slot's device that is not excluded;
  - a named or leased device that moves;
  - `movable` that ignores whether the pool found the device;
  - a refusal at the runner start that is swallowed;
  - a refusal at the app open that is swallowed.
- After kdy1's review (`75bc466ed`, `2503ec746`, `7325bc0b9`, `6385d8b04`, `9ed304941`, `e56266a1b`, `b0d2898bb`, `b1c93eac1`, `3db141275`, rebased on main `b6e65ae37`): the unit tests now cover the winner's `transient:prepare` refusing the loser's runner start, and separately its open, on A with B free (ends on B and the worker boots B, red on `1562b4eda`); with only A booted the slot keeps A; a boot refused by `transient:prepare` with only A fails; a same-daemon session named `transient:smoke-0` moves to B; two slots on A and B with A taken at the open go on with one worker on B, whose worker boots B; with three slots, losing the first, middle or last device runs the other two as slots 0 and 1, each under the session it warmed with; losing both of two fails with the holder's name; a later slot keeps its session through the drop, also when its device still holds this target's `e2e-ios-1`, and through a later move; a failed inventory after a refusal is the error; the exhaustion message has no `.;`. 15 mutants of the slot drop and the kept sessions each fail a test. `pnpm check` passes and the mobile unit suite is 595 of 595.
- **On the simulators at `3db141275`.** Only iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro were booted, agent-device 0.21.41, one daemon shared by every run. main is `b6e65ae37` (the base this branch is rebased on), each build in its own worktree; the two builds ran one after the other, alternating.

  | | main `b6e65ae37` | this branch `3db141275` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `node two-hosts.mjs par`, 10 runs each | 10 of 10 fail: the second host gets `ENGINE_FAILURE boot failed: ios device C5655009-… is owned by session "e2e-ios-<hostId>-0"` | 10 of 10 pass, one host on each simulator, both taps pass. Each run logs `C5655009-… is held by agent-device session "e2e-ios-<hostId>-0"; trying the next free device` |
  | Drop: a `launch()` host takes iPhone 17 while `e2e run --workers 2` (two test files) warms, 5 runs each | 5 of 5 exit 3: one test fails with `ENGINE_FAILURE boot failed: … is owned by session "e2e-ios-<hostId>-0"` (3 refused at the runner start, 2 at the app open), the other passes on iPhone 18 Pro | 5 of 5 pass: `no other booted device is free for slot 0; the run goes on with 1 worker(s)`, and both tests run as `e2e-ios-1` on iPhone 18 Pro, the session that slot warmed under |

  In all 15 branch runs the refusal came from the other host's live session; no run met a short-lived `transient:` claim, so that path is covered by the unit tests only. In the drop runs the host always won iPhone 17 first, so the case where the runner's later slot is the one dropped did not occur live.
- The unit test `moves a device a short-lived agent-device command refused to the next free one, and keeps it when none is free` replaces the earlier `keeps a device…` test: a short-lived refusal at the runner start or the open with B free ends on B; with only A it keeps A; with two slots and nothing else free it keeps A, and a refused boot drops that slot. Mutants that read a short-lived claim as live, ignore the boot, read the prefix from `details.session`, or keep the trailing period each fail an assertion.

title: fix(cache): record a code typed across several fields as a gap from its first piece
body: ## What and why - `derivedReason` judges each typed value on its own. A piece of a code is neither a whole node nor a word of its own inside "Your code is 482913", so a code the agent typed one digit per box, or three and three, into fields that declare no `autocomplete="one-time-code"` was recorded as replayable pieces, and the next run typed the last run's code. On iOS and Android no field declares that purpose, so every split code was affected. - `ActionDispatcher` now keeps the step's typed run: its `type` and `typeText` values, with only a `tap`, a `tapAt`, or a `Tab` press between them, the last 12. Any other action, and a mutating project tool, ends the run. A piece recorded as a gap on its own stays in the run, so a code that shares a digit with "Enter the 6-digit code" still joins whole. After each value, every run of 2 or more values that ends at it, longest first, is joined with no separator and judged by the new `derivedJoinReason` (`derived.ts`). The join meets only the literal check and the screen rules (`whole-node`, `minted-token`); the date, pixel, and field-purpose rules already judged each piece. - A join the screen showed cuts the recording with the new `TraceRecorder.gapFrom(index, reason)`: the actions from the join's first piece are dropped and one derived gap takes their place. It does nothing on a truncated recording or on one that already hands off at or before that index, and recording goes on after the gap. - Accepted cost, as the issue says: unrelated short values typed in a row whose join equals a word on the screen run live. - No change to the report wire, the cache format, or `REPLAY_POLICY_VERSION`. Docs: a note in `docs/cache.mdx` after the gap rules. ## Issue Fixes #1950 Builds on #1997 (merged): its `/one-time-code-plain` fixture page, which this PR extends with `?parts=2` (two boxes of three), `?code=` (a fixed six-digit code), and `?label=1` (a "6-digit" line). It replaces #1997's test "keeps recording focused digits on boxes that declare no purpose", since that behavior is what this PR fixes. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Before against after, the same scratch test on each build (not committed): an executor reads the code off `/one-time-code-plain` and types it, run twice with `cache: 'read-write'`. Before is #1997's merged code (2deb8bdc) with this PR's fixture page. | Typed as | Before: run 1 saves | Before: run 2 | This branch: run 1 saves | This branch: run 2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | One digit per box (`type`) | 6 `type` digits | replays 6 of 6, sees "Incorrect code", `end-mismatch` | one `minted-token` gap | `missed`, `reason: 'gap'`; the executor runs once and never sees "Incorrect code" | | Three and three (`type`, `Tab`, `typeText`) | `type 992`, `pressKey`, `typeText 300` | replays 3 of 3, sees "Incorrect code", `end-mismatch` | one `minted-token` gap | `missed`, `reason: 'gap'`; never sees "Incorrect code" | | A tap, then `typeText`, per box | 6 taps and 6 digits | replays 12 of 12, sees "Incorrect code", the run exits 1 | the first tap, then one `minted-token` gap | `agent-concluded`, `reason: 'gap'`, replayed 1 of 2; exits 0 | - `tests/integration/trace-cache-one-time-code.test.ts` pins the branch columns, plus the counterfactual: on `/one-time-code-plain?code=482913` with an instruction that spells the code out, the six `type` actions are recorded and replay, and the step finishes without the executor. - Two more integration cases: a page that also says "Enter the 6-digit code" with code `482613` records one gap, not `[4, 8, 2, gap, 1, 3]`; and an Enter press between two halves keeps both pieces replayable, where the run ends. - Unit tests: `derivedJoinReason` in `agent-derived.test.ts` (a join shown as a word, a join the params or instruction spell out, `JaneDoe` under "Welcome", no date rule on a join) and `gapFrom` in `trace-recorder.test.ts` (the cut, recording after the gap, an earlier gap, a truncated recording). - 12 of the 13 new tests fail on the base source and pass with the change. The Enter case passes on both, since the base never joins; dropping the run-end check makes it fail. - `pnpm check`, and the full `pnpm test` on main (6fdb1c27): 8046 passed, 25 skipped, 0 failed. - Not run: the web benchmark's agent suite. It replays its recordings read-only, which never reaches this recording path. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: cache: a one-time code sent with press or pressKey replays the last run's code
body:
### What happened

In a step whose screen shows a one-time code, a code sent one key at a time with `press` or `pressKey` is recorded as replayable keys. The next run presses the last run's digits into a page that issued a new code. The replay ends in `end-mismatch`, and in both runs below the executor could not recover, so the test failed.

`recordTrace` in `packages/core/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts` judges only `type` and `typeText` values with `derivedReason`, so a single-character key is never judged. #1934 and #1997 cover those two verbs on marked fields, and #2059 covers them on unmarked fields. The reviews of #1997 asked for this case to be tracked separately.

### Reproduction

The `/one-time-code` fixture page in `packages/e2e/tests/helpers/fixture-pages/forms.ts` issues a new code on every load and marks its six boxes `autocomplete="one-time-code"`. A scripted executor reads the code off the page and sends it one key per box:

```ts
for (const [index, digit] of [...code].entries()) {
  const box = { id: nodeIdFor(observation.text, new RegExp(`textbox "Digit ${index + 1}"`)) };
  await context.actions.press(box, digit);
  // or: await context.actions.tap(box); await context.actions.pressKey(digit);
}
```

| Sent with | Run 1 records | Run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `press` | 6 `press` actions holding the digits | replays 6 of 6, sees "Incorrect code", `end-mismatch`, exit 1 |
| `tap` + `pressKey` | 6 taps and 6 `pressKey` actions holding the digits | replays 12 of 12, sees "Incorrect code", `end-mismatch`, exit 1 |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a test on `/one-time-code` with `cache: 'read-write'` and the executor above. It passes and saves a recording.
2. Run it again. The page issues a new code.
3. The replay presses the first run's digits, the page shows "Incorrect code", and the test fails.

Expected: the digits are recorded as a run-time gap, as they are for `type`, so the replay hands the step to the executor before the first digit.

### Versions

e2e 0.24.0 at 25b3c128 (#2059 on main 6fdb1c27), Node v22.23.4, Linux, Chromium from `@e2e-dev/web`.

### Engine

web

### Anything else

A possible fix is to judge a single-character `press` or `pressKey` as a typed value in `recordTrace`, so the one-time-code rule and #2059's joined-value rule apply to it. Named keys such as `Enter` and `Tab` would stay as they are. The recording code is shared, so mobile is likely affected too, but I only ran this on web.

title: fix(acp): sign Codex in with an API key and redact provider keys
body:
- Let `codex()` start with an environment API key when Codex has no saved login. Keep request-based sign-in off when adapter logging would record credentials.
- Redact provider keys in runner output, traces, and caught model errors. Scan eligible text downloads for whole provider keys and keep their `incomplete` label when only provider keys are known.
- Ship the authentication and redaction changes together. The adapter depends on the redaction helpers in the accompanying e2e release.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

| Case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex starts with an environment key and a fresh credential store | The adapter reports that the agent is not signed in | The adapter opens the session using the API key |
| The built CLI receives a provider error that echoes a synthetic key | The synthetic key appears in the terminal and report | The CLI and report show `<secret:OPENAI_API_KEY>` |
| A text download is scanned with only a provider key known | The download stays `incomplete` | The download stays `incomplete` and eligible files have whole keys redacted |

The built CLI regression in `packages/e2e/tests/integration/provider-key-echo.test.ts` checks the terminal, report, summary, trace, and judge label.

The Chromium testbed and deterministic web benchmark passed against isolated local servers. A live model turn using only an environment key was outside these local checks.

title: fix(cache): do not replay one-time codes entered via keypresses
body: ## Issue Fixes #2060. ## What and why A one-time code typed one character at a time via `actions.press(target, digit)` or `actions.tap(target)` followed by `actions.pressKey(digit)` is cached and replayed on the next run. The app issues a fresh code, so the stale digit sequence causes an incorrect-code failure. Treat a **single character** pressed into a one-time-code field as a run-time value (`minted-token` gap), just like `type`/`typeText`. This deliberately leaves ordinary keypresses, named keys (`Tab`, `Enter`), and non-OTP fields unchanged. ## Verified - Added two integration cases using the existing `/one-time-code` fixture and scripted executor: targeted `press` and focused `pressKey`; each checks six derived gaps, a second run, and no incorrect-code replay. - `bun build` of both changed TypeScript files with all imports externalized: **syntax/transpilation passed**. - Full `pnpm check` and integration tests **were not run**: the remote Mac has critically limited free disk space, and this was prepared from a source-only checkout. Maintainer-approved CI is needed for final validation. Changeset and `docs/cache.mdx` updated; no API or wire contract change. This is distinct from the existing `type` and `typeText` fixes #1997/#2059. ### Independent-review follow-up (2026-11-23) The latest patch also treats Shift-modified printable keys such as `Shift+a` as one character in OTP fields, while leaving `Control+a`/`Alt+a`, named keys and navigation shortcuts replayable. Added focused unit tests; source-backed Bun assertions pass. Full end-to-end integration remains subject to upstream CI.

This is outdated: the e2e web locator's `.blur()` shipped in [#1919](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/1919) on 20 November 2026. Migrators can use the supported operation directly. ## Changes - Map Cypress `.blur()` to the identically named e2e locator method in the command translation table. - Remove `.blur()` from the unsupported/planned event row without altering the still-planned `.trigger()` or scrolling APIs. ## Verified - Cross-checked against merged implementation PR #1919 and the current [Playwright migration guide](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/blob/main/docs/migrate/playwright.mdx) which already lists `.blur()` as implemented. - Documentation-only correction; no source/test/API changes.

title: CLI SemVer comparison loses prerelease ordering above 2^53
body:
### Bug

CLI release-version comparison uses `Number(a) - Number(b)` for two numeric SemVer prerelease identifiers in `packages/e2e/src/internal/semver.ts:compareIdentifiers`. That loses precision for valid identifiers larger than JavaScript's 53-bit safe integer. For example:

```text
0.25.0-rc.9007199254740992  <  0.25.0-rc.9007199254740993
```

`compareVersions` incorrectly returns **0** (equal), which can corrupt prerelease ordering and comparator checks when release identifiers are large.

### Reproduction (public repository)

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-semver-repro

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-repro-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-semver-repro.git /tmp/e2e-semver-repro
cd /tmp/e2e-semver-repro
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-repro-source bun reproduce.ts
```

Actual: `Expected older < newer (-1), actual: 0` and nonzero status.
Expected: comparison is negative and script succeeds.

This is pure CLI release parsing, so no browser, app, e2e.config.ts, paid model or network execution is needed after cloning the repositories.

### Proposed fix

Compare numeric identifier **strings** by length and then lexicographically (they contain only ASCII decimal digits). Retain SemVer's numeric-before-nonnumeric rule, with tests for numbers on both sides of `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and ordinary nightly IDs. No public API change.

title: fix(cli): compare large numeric prerelease identifiers exactly
body: ## Issue Fixes #2065. ## What and why `compareIdentifiers()` converts numeric prerelease strings to JavaScript Numbers. Valid SemVer identifiers exceeding `2^53` are rounded, making distinct versions compare as equal and potentially selecting the wrong prerelease. Compare digit-string lengths then their lexical order instead; leave other version semantics unchanged. Public reproduction: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-semver-repro ## Verified - **Red:** on main, the public Bun reproducer returned **0** for `9007199254740992` versus `9007199254740993` (should be negative). - **Green:** running the same reproducer against the patch returned **-1** (exit 0). Additional direct assertions passed for 20-digit prerelease identifiers and a `satisfies()` range containing a large numeric identifier. - Both changed TypeScript source/test modules passed Bun transpilation checks. The full pnpm/Vitest suite **was not run** because the remote Mac startup disk is critically full; CI/maintainer review is needed. `docs/reference/cli.mdx` and a patch changeset were updated. No public API or wire format change.

title: Canonical JSON skips sparse-array entries, causing invalid JSON and hash collisions
body:
### Problem

The `canonicalJson()` encoder in `packages/core/src/internal/ids.ts` uses `value.map(...)` for arrays. In JavaScript, `.map` **skips holes**, so it emits empty fields when the array is sparse: `canonicalJson(new Array(1)) === "[]"` instead of `[null]`.

The output no longer represents the input's JSON value, and `canonicalDigest([]) === canonicalDigest(new Array(1))`. For multiple holes, it can even produce **invalid JSON** such as `[,]`. The current tests already cover undefined array values becoming null, but not sparse holes.

### Public reproduction

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/canonical-sparse.ts

Run:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-core-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-core-source bun canonical-sparse.ts
```

Actual: `[]` and an assertion failure. Expected: `[null]`, a distinct digest, and script exit 0. This is a pure core canonicalization bug; no app, browser, or model is involved.

### Proposed fix

Visit array positions, including holes (e.g. `Array.from(array, mapper)`), preserving the existing conversion of missing/undefined elements to `null`. Add tests for one and two holes and pin the distinct hashes. No API change.

title: fix(core): canonicalize sparse JSON array holes as null
body: ## Issue Fixes #2067. ## What and why `canonicalJson()` used `array.map()`, which skips holes. A sparse array with one hole therefore encoded as `[]`, identical to an empty array, while two holes even produced invalid JSON `[,]`. Use `Array.from()` to visit every slot; an absent element becomes JSON `null`, as the encoder already does for explicit `undefined` elements. Public reproduction: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/canonical-sparse.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** canonical bytes and SHA-256 digests collided between `[]` and a single-hole array. - **Green on patch:** the same public script passes; verified `[null]`, `[null,null]` and `[null,1,null,null]` cases, plus distinct/equal digest assertions. - Both changed TypeScript modules passed Bun transpilation. Full pnpm/Vitest tests were not run because the Mac startup disk has insufficient space; CI must confirm. A patch changeset is included. No public API or wire schema changes.

title: Package manager detection stops at an unrelated nested workspace
body:
### Problem

`detectWorkspacePackageManager()` stops at the **first ancestor with any `workspaces` declaration**, even if the target package does *not* match that ancestor's workspace package globs. This contradicts the function contract: choose the **nearest ancestor workspace that actually includes the target**.

In a nested monorepo, an outer root can declare `packageManager: "pnpm@10.4.1"` and `workspaces: ["packages/**"]`, while a nested `packages/sdk` declares its own `workspaces: ["plugins/*"]` that exclude the target `packages/sdk/apps/client`. The code hits the `break` inside its upward loop, never checks the outer matching root, and wrongly chooses npm in the client directory. That gives the user the wrong e2e setup command and lockfile root.

### Public reproducible project

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/nested-workspace-manager.ts

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-source bun nested-workspace-manager.ts
```

The script uses Bun to compile the *actual* upstream `package-manager.ts` and `@e2e-dev/core` helpers with only source import aliases; no browser, app, model, or install needed. **Actual:** `{manager: "npm",root: nested client}`; **expected:** `{manager: "pnpm",root: outer workspace}`.

### Proposed fix

Continue walking ancestor directories when a workspace declaration does not include the target, rather than breaking. Preserve preference for the *nearest matching* workspace and direct child lockfile/packageManager fields. Add a nested-workspace unit regression plus the existing nonmember test.

title: fix(cli): look beyond unrelated nested workspaces for package manager
body: ## Issue Fixes #2071. ## Problem and fix Package-manager detection stopped at an ancestor `workspaces` declaration even when its package globs **did not include** the target. An outer pnpm workspace could include that target, but the CLI recommended npm and selected the nested package as install root. Keep traversing unrelated workspace ancestors until the *nearest matching* workspace is found; preserve local package manager/lockfile preference. Public reproduction: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/nested-workspace-manager.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** source-backed Bun reproducer returned `{ manager: 'npm', root: nestedClient }` instead of the outer pnpm workspace. - **Green on patch:** same reproducer returns the correct outer `{ manager: 'pnpm', root: rootProject }` and passes. - Added Vitest unit regression for an unrelated intermediate workspace and a nearer matching workspace that must still win. - Both changed TypeScript files passed Bun transpilation. Full pnpm/Vitest suite not executed due Mac disk constraints; upstream CI needed. Includes `e2e` patch changeset. No public API/schema changes.

title: Package manager detection treats directories as lockfiles
body:
### Bug

`detectPackageManager()` identifies a package manager by testing `existsSync(path.join(project, lockName))`. This returns true for directories as well as files. If an npm project has an actual `package-lock.json` and a directory named `pnpm-lock.yaml` (for example, a wrongly extracted artifact), the E2E CLI chooses **pnpm** and gives incorrect installation instructions even though npm is the only manager with a real lockfile.

### Source-backed public reproduction

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/lockfile-directories.ts

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-source bun lockfile-directories.ts
```

The script bundles the **real** `package-manager.ts` and core helpers directly from source (no app, model, browser or dependency installation). **Actual:** `pnpm`, assertion fails. **Expected:** `npm` (only genuine lockfile).

### Proposed fix

Identify real regular files via `statSync(...).isFile()` rather than bare existence. Follow symlinks to regular files, but ignore directories and broken symlinks. Preserve the field > lockfile > invoking user agent priority. Add a focused unit regression to the existing package-manager test suite.

title: fix(cli): ignore directories named as package-manager lockfiles
body: ## Issue Fixes #2073. ## Problem and fix `detectPackageManager()` used bare `existsSync()` on each known lockfile name, so it counted a **directory** called `pnpm-lock.yaml` as a pnpm lockfile and selected the wrong package manager despite an actual `package-lock.json`. Only treat paths as lockfiles if `statSync(...).isFile()`, continuing to recognize a symlink that points to a real lockfile. Public source-backed repro: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/lockfile-directories.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** runnable Bun repro detected `pnpm` instead of `npm` in a directory with one fake pnpm lockfile directory and a real npm lockfile. - **Green:** same reproducer now returns npm; added a unit regression that verifies valid symlinks to real files remain accepted. - Both changed TypeScript files passed Bun transpilation. Full pnpm/Vitest suite not run due connected Mac disk constraints; upstream CI/maintainer verification is needed. Patch changeset included. Does not overlap the separate nested workspace ancestry fix #2072.

title: Fully qualified localhost URLs with a terminal DNS dot are rejected as remote HTTP
body:
### Problem

The URL policy recognizes `localhost` and `*.localhost` as loopback for development HTTP, but rejects the equally valid **fully qualified DNS form ending with a root dot**: `localhost.` / `app.localhost.`. `normalizeBaseUrl('localhost.:3000')` incorrectly infers HTTPS, while `normalizeBaseUrl('http://localhost.:3000')` throws `INVALID_APP_URL` claiming the hostname is not loopback. On macOS, both `localhost.` and `app.localhost.` resolve to `::1`/`127.0.0.1`; this breaks local E2E targets that write fully qualified DNS names. The shared implicit-test check also rejects `.test.` reserved hostnames, although `.test` is supported.

### Public source-backed reproduction

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/trailing-dot-localhost.ts

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-source bun trailing-dot-localhost.ts
```

**Actual:** `isLoopbackHost('localhost.') === false`, error on explicit local HTTP, default HTTPS. **Expected:** treat a single DNS root dot on a reserved localhost domain as still loopback; `api.test.` should still be an implicit test host. Ordinary `example.org.` must remain non-loopback, so remote HTTP stays denied.

### Proposed fix

Normalize one terminal DNS root dot **for reserved-host recognition only**, preserving the original URL serialization and all existing safety checks. Add tests for `localhost.`, `app.localhost.`, `api.test.`, and a non-loopback trailing-dot host.

title: fix(urls): recognize root-terminated localhost hostnames as loopback
body: ## Issue Fixes #2075. ## What and why The URL policy accepts `localhost` and `*.localhost` as loopback but rejects their valid DNS-root-terminated forms (`localhost.`, `api.localhost.`). That turns a schemeless local app URL into HTTPS, or rejects explicitly declared HTTP as though the target were remote. Strip **one terminal DNS root dot for reserved-host classification only**, leaving the serialized URL and all non-loopback restrictions untouched. Reserved `.test.` hostnames get the same implicit test environment as `.test`. Public repro: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/trailing-dot-localhost.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** `isLoopbackHost('localhost.')` returned false and local HTTP was rejected. - **Green:** the public source-backed Bun reproduction passes for localhost., api.localhost., and api.test. - Unit regression asserts remote `http://example.org.:3000` still fails and a malformed `localhost..` is not loopback. - Changed TypeScript source/test transpilation passed. Full pnpm/Vitest suite not run because Mac disk is nearly full; CI/maintainer validation needed. Includes `@e2e-dev/core` patch changeset; no public API or schema changes.

title: CI provenance accepts 41–63-digit hexadecimal strings as full Git commits
body:
### Problem

`COMMIT_HASH` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/git.ts` uses `/^[a-f0-9]{40,64}$/`, accepting all hexadecimal lengths from 40 to 64. Full Git commit IDs are **40 digits for SHA-1** and **64 for SHA-256**; there are no valid 41–63-digit full commit IDs. `detectVcs()` therefore accepts a malformed `GITHUB_SHA` CI variable of these lengths and incorrectly reports it as the tested code's commit provenance, even when there is no Git checkout. This undermines linking e2e run verdicts to the actual PR commit.

### Public source-backed reproduction

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/git-sha-length.ts

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-source bun git-sha-length.ts
```

Actual: a 41-digit hexadecimal string is accepted; script fails. Expected: reject all lengths other than 40 and 64, and refuse malformed `GITHUB_SHA` as source provenance while retaining both actual hash formats.

### Proposed fix

Change validation to exactly 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits. Extend the existing `vcs.test.ts` to cover invalid 41/60/63 digits (especially CI fallback), plus valid SHA-1 and SHA-256. No public API change.

title: fix(cli): require exact SHA-1 or SHA-256 widths for CI commits
body: ## Issue Fixes #2077. ## Problem and fix The runner's CI provenance check accepted any lowercase hexadecimal token of length **40 through 64** as a full Git commit hash. Git's full SHA-1 and SHA-256 object IDs are **exactly 40 and 64 hex characters**; 41–63 digits cannot represent either format. This could incorrectly attach a test verdict to an invalid `GITHUB_SHA`. Restrict the shared `COMMIT_HASH` pattern to the two valid widths. Public source-backed reproducer: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/git-sha-length.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** 41-, 60- and 63-digit invalid hashes were incorrectly accepted. - **Green:** the same public Bun repro passes, rejecting all intermediate widths while retaining valid SHA-1 and SHA-256 hashes and the CI fallback contract. - Added Vitest unit coverage for exact widths and invalid intermediate lengths. - Both TypeScript modules passed Bun transpilation. The full pnpm/Vitest suite **has not run** in the source-only environment, so upstream CI/maintainer validation is still needed. Includes `e2e` patch changeset; no external API change.

title: Runtime gate accepts unsupported prerelease and malformed Node/Bun versions
body:
### Problem

The runner advertises stable Node support through the published `engines.node` range `^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0`, and Bun through `>=1.4.3`, but `unsupportedRuntimeMessage()` in `packages/e2e/src/internal/runtime.ts` parses version components using `parseInt(part, 10) || 0`. It therefore incorrectly accepts `24.8.0-rc.1`, `22.22.3-rc.1` and even malformed strings such as `24.8.0garbage` as the corresponding **final** releases; Bun `1.4.3-canary.1` is also treated as stable 1.4.3. The compatibility gate can silently run on runtimes outside its supported release ranges.

### Public source-backed reproducer

https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/runtime-version-validation.ts

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e.git /tmp/e2e-source
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros.git /tmp/e2e-core-repros
cd /tmp/e2e-core-repros
E2E_REPO=/tmp/e2e-source bun runtime-version-validation.ts
```

**Actual:** `unsupportedRuntimeMessage({node: '24.8.0-rc.1'})` returns `undefined` (supported), and the assertion fails. **Expected:** reject prerelease/malformed Node/Bun version strings, while preserving stable `24.8.0`, `v24.8.0`, `22.22.3`, and Bun `1.4.3`.

The script imports the actual source and requires no browser, test app, model or dependency installation.

### Proposed fix

Parse an exact three-component stable version with numeric safe-integer components instead of prefix-parsing each field; treat malformed/prerelease values as unsupported, preserving the existing floor messages and stable-release ranges. Add unit coverage alongside the existing `runtime.test.ts` cases and ensure the constants remain aligned with package engines.

title: fix(cli): reject malformed and prerelease runtime versions
body: ## Issue Fixes #2079. ## Problem and fix The runtime gate parses each Node/Bun version segment with `parseInt`. This incorrectly treats `24.8.0-rc.1` and `24.8.0garbage` as stable Node `24.8.0`, and accepts Bun `1.4.3-canary.1` as stable 1.4.3. Those inputs are not covered by the declared supported stable release ranges. Parse the **complete** three-component stable version and reject prerelease, malformed, leading-zero and unsafe-integer components. Keep the existing runtime-floor error messages and supported release ranges unchanged. Public red/green reproduction: https://github.com/DivyamTalwar/e2e-core-repros/blob/main/runtime-version-validation.ts ## Verified - **Red on main:** Node `24.8.0-rc.1` was accepted as supported. - **Green:** same source-backed Bun script passes all prerelease/malformed Node/Bun rejection cases and stable version acceptance cases. - Extra direct assertions confirm all existing accepted Node/Bun stable floors and rejection of earlier unsupported Node releases. - Both TypeScript source and unit-test files passed Bun transpilation. Full pnpm/Vitest tests **have not run** in the source-only environment; upstream CI/maintainer verification remains necessary. Added focused Vitest regressions and the `e2e` patch changeset. title: feat(init): detect a Next.js app and write a config that starts it
body:
In a Next.js app, `npx e2e init` wrote the same placeholder target as anywhere else: `APP_URL` with a `localhost:3000` default and `app.command` only in a comment. The user then had to work out how to start the app before the first run passed. - init detects Next.js when `package.json` has `next` in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. With the web engine selected and no existing config, the web target runs the app's own scripts with the detected package manager (`packages/e2e/src/cli/init/frameworks.ts`). - `app.url` is `http://localhost:`, never `127.0.0.1`: Next.js 16 dev blocks cross-origin dev resources, so a `127.0.0.1` page never hydrates. The port comes from the `--port`, `--port=`, `-p`, `-pN`, or `PORT=` of the `next` command in the `dev` script. The default is 3000. - Locally, `app.command` runs ` run dev` with `reuseExisting: true`. When `build` and `start` exist and `start` serves the same port, the config adds a `ci` constant (it reads `CI` the way the runner does) and runs `start` in CI. - `init --ci github-actions|gitlab` adds a "Build the app" step before `e2e run`. It also does this on a later `--ci` over an existing config that runs the `start` script, whatever port that script uses. - init prints one `Found Next.js: ...` line and stops telling the user to set `APP_URL`. If the `dev` script is missing, has no fixed port (`$PORT`, `0`), or a port set by another command in the script, init warns and writes today's target. A project without `next` gets the same files as before. - Docs: `docs/reference/cli.mdx` (new "Next.js apps" section, CI pipeline bullet), `docs/frameworks/nextjs.mdx`, `skills/e2e/references/setup.md` with its plugin copy. Patch changeset. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[package.json has next?] -- no --> P[APP_URL placeholder] A -- yes --> B{dev script with a fixed port?} B -- no --> W[warn + APP_URL placeholder] B -- yes --> C{build + start on the same port?} C -- no --> D[command: pm run dev, reuseExisting] C -- yes --> E[command: ci ? pm run start : pm run dev] E --> F[--ci adds Build the app before e2e run] ``` Docs shortening pass: `nextjs.mdx` was 248 lines and 753 words on main. The first commit made it 260 lines and 863 words; after the pass it is 258 lines and 835 words. The pass merged the two "init writes this target" paragraphs and cut the CI paragraph from six lines to five. On `cli.mdx`, the Next.js note in the wizard list now only links to the section, which owns the "prints the commands and URL" fact. "A project without `next` gets the same files as before" is cut from the reference page: it is changelog wording, the Files table already describes the default, and the changeset keeps the sentence. ## Review A fresh-context review (Codex, gpt-6.2-sol) reported three findings: - Fixed: the port scan read a flag from any command in the script, so `node scripts/preflight.js -p 8080 && next dev` wrote port 8080. init now reads only the `next` command. A port that another command sets falls back to the placeholder with a warning (b817fdf9). - Fixed: a later `--ci` over an existing config that runs `start` in CI added no build step when `start` and `dev` listen on different ports (2e4323fb). - Not fixed: `executable: 'npm'` fails on Windows because `managed-process.ts` spawns without a shell, so the runner never finds `npm.cmd`. The cause is in the runner, not in this change. Every documented config already uses this shape (`docs/examples/nextjs`, `examples/with-next`, the quickstart). The runner needs a separate fix. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes. `e2e init` ran from this branch's built CLI (`node packages/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js`) in fresh `create-next-app@16` projects (Next.js 16.4.6). **main vs this branch**, `init --yes --skills none --mcp none` on the same untouched `create-next-app` `package.json` (main built from 71a2b795): | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | No detection line | `● Found Next.js: the web target starts npm run dev on http://localhost:3000, and npm run start in CI after npm run build` | | `└ Next: npm install, then APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run test:e2e` | `└ Next: npm install, then npm run test:e2e` | | `url: process.env.APP_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',`
`// command: { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'] },` | `url: 'http://localhost:3000',`
`command: ci ? { …'run', 'start' } : { …'run', 'dev', reuseExisting: true },` | **(a) npm, default port:** `init --yes` wrote this `e2e.config.ts`: ```ts import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'; import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web'; import { gateway } from 'ai'; // e2e reads CI the same way: unset, '', '0', and 'false' mean a local run. const ci = !['', '0', 'false'].includes(process.env.CI?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? ''); export default { // The Vercel AI Gateway serves the model id and reads AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, or the OIDC token of a linked Vercel project. agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast'), system: 'You are a thorough QA agent. Verify every outcome.', }, }, targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000', // Next.js: the dev server here, or one you already started on that port. // CI serves the production build: run `npm run build` before `e2e run`. command: ci ? { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'start'] } : { executable: 'npm', args: ['run', 'dev'], reuseExisting: true }, }, }], } satisfies E2EConfig; ``` Then `npm install && npm run test:e2e` passed through `next dev` (`✓ target "web" command at http://localhost:3000/ ready 1.40s`, 1 passed). After `npm run build`, `CI=1 npm run test:e2e` passed through `next start` (ready 258ms, 1 passed). This scenario used the published runner (e2e 0.24.0 from npm), since only `init` changed and the config is plain. **(b) pnpm, port 3200, GitHub Actions:** `dev` and `start` set to `-p 3200`, then `git init`, then `init --yes --ci github-actions`: ```text ● Found Next.js: the web target starts pnpm dev on http://localhost:3200, and pnpm start in CI after pnpm build … ◆ Created .github/workflows/e2e.yml (GitHub Actions) └ Next: pnpm install, then pnpm test:e2e ``` The config has `url: 'http://localhost:3200'` and `executable: 'pnpm'`. The workflow has this step right before `Run e2e`: ```yaml # e2e.config.ts serves this build in CI. - name: Build the app run: pnpm build ``` For this scenario, this branch's packed `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/core`, and `@e2e-dev/web` tarballs replaced the npm versions through pnpm `overrides`. `pnpm test:e2e` passed through `next dev` on 3200. After `pnpm build`, `CI=1 pnpm test:e2e` passed through `next start` on 3200. **Review fixes through the CLI:** - `dev: "node scripts/preflight.js -p 8080 && next dev"`: `▲ Found Next.js, but init cannot read a fixed port from the dev script; set app.url and app.command …`, and the placeholder target. - Existing config running `npm run start` in CI with `dev: "next dev -p 3100"` and `start: "next start"`: `--ci github-actions` writes `Build the app` / `npm run build`. Closes ENG-1387 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cli): keep the --target selection in the run header when --device is refused, and say which ids --device takes
body: ## What and why Follow-ups @kdy1 left on #2002: - **Run header.** When `--device` is refused, `run-started` fell back to every configured target, so `e2e run --target web --device Pixel_9` printed `targets: android, web` before failing with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. `selectRunTargets` now returns the `--target` selection along with the `--device` error, so the header prints `targets: web` again (`packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts`). - **Which ids `--device` takes.** The CLI reference said "by name, UDID, or serial". `deviceSelection` only treats a simulator UDID or an `emulator-` serial as an id. Any other value, including a physical phone's serial or UDID, is passed as a device name. The docs now say so. The `device` option behaves the same way on main; resolving physical ids is a separate change. - **Several targets.** `TARGET_REQUIRED` only counts selected targets that can take a device. The docs now say "several selected targets that can take a device", and that the other selected targets still run as configured. The doc edits are in `docs/reference/cli.mdx` (en, ja, zh), `docs/mobile.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/running.md` plus its plugin copy. ## Issue Follow-up to #2002 ([kdy1's review](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/pull/2002#pullrequestreview-6015954802)). ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The `run-device` integration test now configures `android` and `web` and runs `--target web --device Pixel_9`. It checks that `run-started` carries `targets: ['web']` and that nothing is prepared. | main | this branch | | --- | --- | | `run-started.targets`: `['android', 'web']` | `run-started.targets`: `['web']` | - Dropping the targets from the error again makes that test fail. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.

title: perf(core): drop quadratic locator walks and end positioned taps at their timeout
body:
`resolveExpression` (the locator semantics the desktop engine and custom engines run over a semantic tree) walked up a parent map for every containment check and copied a candidate array per `filter` match. On a large screen that is quadratic: a `filter({ has })` over 1,000 list rows took ~350 ms per resolve, and resolves run on every poll.

- **Subtree intervals.** `indexTree` records each node's pre-order range once, so "is X inside Y" is an interval test and the candidates of any `filter` match or `scope` are one contiguous slice of the pre-order array (`packages/core/src/engine/resolve.ts`).
- **Linear `innermostOnly`.** In document order a match contains another match exactly when it contains the next one, so the innermost pass is one scan instead of all pairs.
- **Matchers compiled once per pass, not per node.** `compileTextMatcher` (`packages/core/src/internal/text.ts`) is now the one text rule; `compareText` delegates to it, so there is still a single implementation.
- **`performWithin` uses `pollReads`.** Its hand-rolled poll loop is replaced by the shared one (`packages/core/src/locator/engine.ts`). Same error and cut-off handling, with two visible differences: a positioned `tap({ position })` no longer sleeps past its timeout (the old loop overshot by up to one poll delay), and it skips the read at the deadline, since a box found then could never be tapped, so the wait ends as `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` instead of `ACTION_FAILED`.
- **Retried locates stop at the deadline.** `resolveOnce` caps its retry sleep (after a retryable error such as `FRAME_NOT_FOUND`) at the time left, so a locator waiting on a missing frame ends at its timeout instead of the next poll tick.

`resolveExpression`'s results, error codes, and which error it throws first are unchanged (see Verified). A `filter` whose source matches nest (groups inside groups) still scans each match's subtree, so `hasText` there costs nodes × depth.

## Benchmark

`resolveExpression` median per call, a list screen with echoed labels as iOS reports them, main vs this branch:

| case | nodes | main | this PR | speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `filter({ has: button "Delete" })` | 802 | 3.36 ms | 0.050 ms | 68× |
| `filter({ hasText })` | 802 | 3.43 ms | 0.081 ms | 42× |
| `getByText` innermost, 200 matches | 802 | 1.59 ms | 0.076 ms | 21× |
| `role` in a `listitem` scope | 802 | 1.20 ms | 0.048 ms | 25× |
| `filter({ has: button "Delete" })` | 8,002 | 354 ms | 0.73 ms | 488× |
| `filter({ hasText })` | 8,002 | 372 ms | 1.04 ms | 359× |
| `getByText` innermost, 2,000 matches | 8,002 | 211 ms | 0.97 ms | 217× |
| `role` in a `listitem` scope | 8,002 | 121 ms | 0.67 ms | 181× |
| `matchesText` × 10k | | 1.98 ms | 2.02 ms | same |

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes

- Differential fuzz: 50,000 random trees × random expressions (every kind, nested `has`/`hasNot`/`scope`/`union`, invalid regexps, non-string roles, `frame`, `selector` with and without the hook), main's built `resolve.js` against this branch's: 0 differences in result ids or thrown error code and message.
- New unit tests pin innermost matches across deep and distant echoes, nested `has` ranges, and a `selector` inside `has` seeing only that candidate's descendants; they pass on main's build too, so they pin existing behavior.
- `performWithin` deadline, on the fake clock:

  | 350 ms timeout | main | this branch |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | positioned tap, node never gets a box | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 400 ms | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 350 ms |
  | positioned tap, box appears during a read started at the deadline | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 410 ms | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 350 ms |
  | locator on a frame that stays missing | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 400 ms | `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` at 350 ms |

- `pnpm test:testbed`: 598 passed, 3 skipped. `pnpm test:web-benchmark`: 95 passed (43 files).

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.2-sol (before the review fixes in 8422ef8). Sol verdict: approved

---

Changes made by Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code, running in T3 Code.

title: perf(core): compile secret patterns about 30x faster, redact line output 1.7x faster
body: Building the pattern that redacts a run's secrets was slow for what it does: every compile worked out each character's spellings from scratch, six locale case mappings per character, and a ledger compiles again at every registration. `StreamRedactor` also ran the value pattern over each write twice, once to place the cut and once to redact. Now each character's pattern is built once per process, and a stream of finished lines is searched once. What is redacted does not change. - `character(ch)` results are kept in `characterPatterns`, capped at 4096 entries. A pattern depends on its character alone, never on a ledger, a name, or a value. - `SecretLedger.holdFrom` returns as soon as the cut sits at either end of the text or right after a line break, and otherwise searches only the cut's own line. Both rest on one invariant: no occurrence holds a `\n` unless a value spans lines (`spansLines`), which the existing cut at the last line break already relied on. A value with inner whitespace or a line break takes the old path. - `redact` and `redactCut` skip the split on known markers when the text has no ` prints the password in whole lines and across writes line one line two password= split done stderr | |web| tests/zz-redact-evidence.e2e.ts > prints the password in whole lines and across writes stderr � ✓ |web| tests/zz-redact-evidence.e2e.ts > prints the password in whole lines and across writes 442ms ``` - Differential fuzz, main's `redact.ts` and this branch's loaded in one process: 140,000 random texts over random ledgers (short secrets, leading, trailing, and inner whitespace, CRLF, markers, JSON, URL, HTML-entity, and base64 spellings, random string and byte chunking). 0 differences in `redact`, `redactCut`, `redactFragments`, `holdFrom`, and `StreamRedactor` output. - Compiled pattern source, `maxFormLength`, and `spansLines` for 169,526 single-character values, including every ASCII character once the cache was full: identical to main. - `pnpm bench:ab -- tests/login-form.e2e.ts` (web benchmark, 4 pairs): every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on both builds. Suite time 1.34 s on both, verdict `same`. A fresh-context review asked for a test of the `spansLines` side of the new `holdFrom` branches; it is in. One pre-existing `StreamRedactor` edge case turned up while fuzzing. It behaves the same on main and here, and is tracked separately. Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.2-sol. Sol verdict: approved Written by Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code (T3 Code).

title: fix(desktop): fix reads, ids, input, and screenshots found in a second review of the desktop engine
body:
A second review of the `@e2e-dev/desktop` engine as it is on main (#1953 and #2056). Eleven rounds of four independent reviewers (codex gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, each on its own checkout), then a fresh-context review by gpt-6.2-sol. Every finding was checked against the code, and agent-desktop 1.3.1's source where it mattered. Each fix has a unit test that fails without it.

## What changed

Reads never pass as an empty or wrong screen:
- A read while the Mac is locked, one cut short by time, or one agent-desktop says may be retried (`APP_UNRESPONSIVE` with `details.retryable`) reads again as a retryable `NODE_STALE`. A screen lock is asked of macOS (`ioreg`) within the operation's budget.
- `app.open()` reads again when the app replaces its window mid-read, and launches again after a failed launch that left no process.
- A minimized window, a control with no width or height, and everything under a hidden or off-screen node (a dropped wrapper included) read as hidden.
- Window titles come from the accessibility root: without Screen Recording, agent-desktop's window list gives the app's name.
- With `snapshot: 'interactive'`, locators read the whole window, as on the mobile engine (`-i` drops static text).

Ids and input reach only the control meant:
- Interactive and whole reads keep separate identities; a read cut short retires only identities a look-alike took, under the id their parent held before, and gives no id to a child of a node it cut off; a closed window's identities go.
- Before a key, a look-alike field must still match by name and developer id; a focus check cut short says so.
- `press` refuses the shortcuts agent-desktop will not press (`ControlOrMeta+q` and the like) before focus moves, reaches a window on another Space, and refuses a minimized one.
- A swipe on the window goes to the first visible, enabled node that offers `Scroll`.
- Every point action, the agent's and a test's, is measured in the newest observation's window, as core hit-tests it (`packages/core/src/agent/action-dispatcher.ts:274`).

Screenshots:
- A screenshot withheld for a password field fails with `POLICY_DENIED` (a window deeper than `maxDepth` too), and reports a masked count so the agent reads `MASKING_UNPROVEN`. A capture that failed for any other reason (no Screen Recording, a resize, a read out of time) reports no count, so `toHaveScreenshot` captures again.
- agent-desktop's raw capture goes to a temporary directory inside the worker's state directory, so a killed capture leaves no unmasked image in the system's temporary directory.
- Static text and a window locator count as in view, so `toHaveScreenshot` works on them.
- Core: a masked count sent without pixels always reads as withheld, even when the tree shows no secure node, since a tree read in part can leave one out (`packages/core/src/engine/session.ts`). Web and mobile never send that, so they are unaffected.

Config, cleanup, and docs:
- `toBeEditable` works: text fields and editable combo boxes report `readonly`. The peer floor is now `>=0.25.0`, as for web and mobile.
- `desktop({ maxDepth })` takes 1 to 50 (agent-desktop's limit), and `desktop(null)` is refused.
- The state sweep records a worker's start time, read in UTC, so a recycled process id or another time zone cannot make it kill a live worker's app.
- Docs: what still reads as visible, the limits of agent-desktop's reads, and that off macOS a run needs `--target` to skip the desktop target.

Decided with the maintainer during review:
- A masked count without pixels reads as withheld (reverses one line #2014 tested).
- agent-desktop 1.3.1 drops a node's whole state list when one attribute cannot be read, `secure` included, and leaves out both an empty value and one it could not read. Both are documented limits; the engine cannot tell.
- A headed point tap clicks the point on screen; a floating window over it gets the click (agent-desktop has no window-scoped click). Documented.
- Only a minimized window reads as hidden; one on another Space still reads as visible, so a user can switch Spaces during a background run.
- A read cut short by time with no secure field seen is a failed capture that `toHaveScreenshot` takes again.
- The focus check before a key keeps re-reading the window; a form replaced by an identical-looking one on focus is out of scope.

The fresh-context review (gpt-6.2-sol) found three things:
- Fixed: a read cut short gave a menu a fresh id, so its twin items were not retired and one passed its id to the other.
- Not taken: `press --headed` raises the window after the focus check, and an app could move focus then. This is the focus-check decision above.
- Not taken: a launch record a nightly build wrote in local time is read in UTC now. The package has only nightly prereleases on npm, which carry no promise for their state files.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on macOS (Apple Silicon) with Accessibility granted and Screen Recording denied, against the built packages: `apps/desktop-testbed`, `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run`, main and this branch.

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/sign-in.e2e.ts` | 2 of 4: the fresh-launch test fails with `expected ["SignInForm"] to equal ["Sign In"]`, and the location reads `SignInForm › SignInForm` | 3 of 4: the location reads `SignInForm › Sign In` |
| `expect(getByTestId('username')).toBeEditable()` | fails: no read-only state | passes |
| `getByText('Not signed in').scrollIntoView()` | `node n15 (text) is not a control agent-desktop can scroll-to` | passes |

- The screenshot test fails on both with `Screen Recording permission not granted`, so masked screenshots were not run live; the unit suite covers them with a scripted agent-desktop.
- Headed input (`press`, point taps, typing) was not run live, as it would drive this Mac's keyboard and pointer.
- No `SignInForm` process and no `e2e-agent-desktop-*` directory was left after any run.

title: perf(core): paint screenshot masks up to 20x faster, compare identical screenshots 5x faster
body: `toHaveScreenshot` did more work per capture than it needed. It painted a mask one pixel at a time, and it drew a diff image on every poll, then threw it away unless that poll was the last. - `fillBoxes` paints one row of a mask box and copies it down the box, on a fresh copy of the capture (`packages/core/src/internal/image.ts`). On main a capture held in a `Buffer` was painted in place, since `Buffer#slice` shares memory. - `compareImages` only counts differing pixels. The new `diffImage` draws the diff, and `toHaveScreenshot` calls it once, for the failure that attaches it (`packages/e2e/src/expect/screenshot.ts`). - `Connection` drops its read buffer when a message leaves nothing behind (`packages/core/src/engine/protocol/connection.ts`). On main a 0-byte view kept the whole last message alive until the next chunk, and that message is often a screenshot. - `truncateUtf8` returns a string that cannot exceed the limit without encoding it, and `compareCodePoints` compares without building two arrays. `validateTitle` and `uuidv7` each lose a copy. ## The slower path A failing `toHaveScreenshot` takes longer. The step always runs to its deadline, so cheaper polls do not shorten it, and the diff is now a second pass after the deadline. Six runs per build of one failing assertion, default 5 s timeout, a tenth of the page changed: | Capture | Polls, main | Polls, this PR | Failing step, main | Failing step, this PR | Time in pixelmatch, main | Time in pixelmatch, this PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1280x720 | 49 | 49 | 5,033.5 ms | 5,050 ms (+0.3%) | 668 ms | 414 ms | | 2560x1440 | 25 | 25 | 5,075 ms | 5,122.5 ms (+0.9%) | 1,193 ms | 786 ms | I think that is the right trade: 16 to 48 ms on a step that already failed after 5 s, for a cheaper compare on every passing one. ## Benchmarks Main's built `@e2e-dev/core` against this branch's, Node 24.18, medians of 9 alternating rounds. The script checks that the mask, the pixel count, and the diff image equal main's before it times anything. | Operation | main | this PR | speedup | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1280x720: paint one mask box, a third of the screen | 6.94 ms | 0.32 ms | 21.7x | | 1280x720: paint one 300x100 mask box | 0.85 ms | 0.25 ms | 3.3x | | 1280x720: paint twenty 40x20 mask boxes | 0.51 ms | 0.30 ms | 1.7x | | 1280x720: compare, capture identical to the stored screenshot | 3.00 ms | 0.58 ms | 5.2x | | 1280x720: compare, mismatch, each poll | 16.6 ms | 12.8 ms | 1.3x | | 1280x720: draw the diff, once per failure | in the row above | 16.3 ms | | | 2560x1440: paint one mask box, a third of the screen | 28.8 ms | 2.32 ms | 12.4x | | 2560x1440: paint one 300x100 mask box | 3.10 ms | 2.70 ms | 1.1x | | 2560x1440: compare, capture identical to the stored screenshot | 11.9 ms | 2.30 ms | 5.2x | | 2560x1440: compare, mismatch, each poll | 65.2 ms | 50.7 ms | 1.3x | | 2560x1440: draw the diff, once per failure | in the row above | 63.9 ms | | | `truncateUtf8`, short string, 100k calls | 88.9 ms | 0.27 ms | 330x | | `truncateUtf8`, over the limit, 100k calls | 360.6 ms | 360.3 ms | 1.0x | | Sort 1,500 test paths | 4.80 ms | 1.35 ms | 3.6x | A small mask gains little, because copying the capture costs more than painting it. On a 2560x1440 capture the small-mask rows moved between 0.7x and 1.4x across three runs, so read them as no change. `pnpm bench:ab --suite testbed -- tests/visual.e2e.ts tests/screenshot.e2e.ts`, merge base `b6e65ae3` against this branch, 8 pairs, load 1.3: - Every test ran the same steps with the same outcome on every run of both builds, and every counter matched. - The gain does not show end to end on the testbed's small pages, where capture and waiting dominate. | Metric | base median | head median | change (95% CI) | verdict | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | wall (process) | 11.92 s | 11.91 s | -0.3% (-2.0% to +0.6%) | same | | suite (sum of attempts) | 10.84 s | 10.85 s | -0.1% (-2.0% to +0.7%) | same | | step `expect.toHaveScreenshot` | 1.28 s | 1.25 s | -2.7% (-7.6% to -1.2%) | unresolved | | step `expect.not.toHaveScreenshot` | 1.04 s | 1.05 s | +0.1% (-0.2% to +0.6%) | same, under the floor | | step `app.screenshot` | 2.58 s | 2.60 s | +0.2% (-2.4% to +4.3%) | same, under the floor | ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - testbed and web benchmark, built CLI: `pnpm test:testbed` and `pnpm test:web-benchmark` pass, masked and unmasked `toHaveScreenshot` included. - The failure path, in a scratch project linked to each build: a page painted with a tenth of its blocks recolored against a stored screenshot. Both builds fail the same way and attach the diff, actual, and expected images. A module hook around `pixelmatch` counted the calls for the table above. ```text FAIL |web| tests/fail.e2e.ts > page at 1280x720 ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toHaveScreenshot failed 96000 pixels (10% of the image) differ from tests/fail.e2e.ts-snapshots/page-1280-web-linux.png; run with --update-snapshots to keep this run's diff: .e2e-try/results/fail-page-at-1280x720-6c006229becb7a6c/attempt-1/screenshots/page-1280-diff.png actual: .e2e-try/results/fail-page-at-1280x720-6c006229becb7a6c/attempt-1/screenshots/page-1280-actual.png expected: .e2e-try/results/fail-page-at-1280x720-6c006229becb7a6c/attempt-1/screenshots/page-1280-expected.png ``` Not verified: the memory the connection change frees. It is read from the code, with a framing test for the read path it touches. Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.2-sol on high. title: fix: round durations and sizes before picking the unit
body: ## What and why - `formatDuration` in `markdown-text.ts` picked the unit before rounding, so 999.6ms showed as `1000ms` and 59.96s as `60.0s` in the markdown report (and the GitHub PR comment built from it), trace pages, and failure details. - It now rounds first, as #1829 did for the HTML report. Anything that rounds to a minute or more still goes through `formatMinutes`, which already rounds first, so 119.6s stays `2m 0s`. - I checked the other unit formatters in the repo. Four more had the same bug and are fixed here too: `formatMs` (`--debug` timings), `formatBytes` (`e2e cache stats`), `formatSize` (the HTML reporter's embedded page note), and `duration` in `scripts/bench-ab/markdown.ts`. The two size helpers moved into their own small modules so their tests use the production code. - Apart from `formatTime` in `report/format.ts`, none are left. It prints `1000ms` for 999.6ms, but it copies vitest's format, which prints `1000ms` for exactly 1000 too, so I left it. ## Issue Fixes #2090 ## Verified Ran it locally: yes | formatter | input | main | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `formatDuration` | 999.6ms | `1000ms` | `1.0s` | | `formatDuration` | 59_949ms (unchanged) | `59.9s` | `59.9s` | | `formatDuration` | 59_960ms | `60.0s` | `1m 0s` | | `formatDuration` | 119_600ms (unchanged) | `2m 0s` | `2m 0s` | | `formatMs` | 9_999.6ms | `10000ms` | `10.0s` | | `formatBytes` | 1_048_575 B | `1024.0 KiB` | `1.0 MiB` | | `formatSize` | 1_047_553 B | `1024 KB` | `1.0 MB` | | bench-ab `duration` | 999.6ms | `1000 ms` | `1.00 s` | - Each fix has a test that fails on main and passes here. - The [repro](https://gist.github.com/Wali05/e1b62c9ec41dac5a96dbe56d57c3781f) from #2090, run against this branch's build, prints `1.0s` and `1m 0s`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`.
