title: ci: install Chromium's cached apt packages without apt-get update
body:
## What and why - #1569 caches the `.deb` files, but `playwright-core install --with-deps` still runs `apt-get update` first, and that fetch is not cached. - On 2026-11-23 the runner image had no package lists, so every job fetched 41.2 MB of indexes from archive.ubuntu.com. With the mirror at 50-120 kB/s, the install step took 5-14 minutes even though the cache was restored (`Need to get 0 B/38.2 MB of archives.`): ``` Cache restored from key: chromium-apt-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64-playwright-1.65.1-da39cb57af492eb2 Fetched 41.2 MB in 13min 16s (51.7 kB/s) Need to get 0 B/38.2 MB of archives. ``` - `Install browsers` step in `spec` jobs: | Day | Jobs | p50 | p75 | p90 | max | over 60 s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-11-20 | 862 | 13 s | 16 s | 19 s | 34 s | 0% | | 2026-11-23 | 439 | 28 s | 90 s | 725 s | 877 s | 29% | - When the cache restores an entry, `.github/actions/chromium/action.yml` now installs it without the mirror: ```bash sudo apt-get install -y --no-download --no-remove --no-install-recommends /var/cache/chromium-apt/*.deb playwright-core install-deps --dry-run chromium # fails if any dependency is missing playwright-core install chromium ``` apt resolves the files against the installed packages, so it needs no package lists. A downgrade, a removal, a missing dependency, or a failed dry run falls back to `install --with-deps`, as before. - The key prefix stays `chromium-apt-`, so jobs use main's existing entry from the first run. A cold cache on a slow mirror day cannot fill itself: `apt-get update` plus 38 MB of packages runs past the 15 minute `spec` job timeout, and the job ends before the save step. - After the restore, the action keeps only the newest version of each package, because older entries can hold two versions of one package. The save step keeps only the files of the installed versions. - Trade-off: while the cache installs, nothing is downloaded, so the package versions stay those of the saved entry. A new entry is saved only after a fallback, for example when a runner image moves past the cached versions. Before, every job installed the newest versions from the mirror. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[restore .debs] --> B{entry restored?} B -- yes --> C[apt-get install files
no download, no removal] C --> D{dry run: all deps?} D -- yes --> E[install chromium] B -- no --> F[install --with-deps] C -- fails --> F D -- no --> F E --> G[keep installed versions, save if changed] F --> G ``` ## Issue No matching issue. This is a CI time fix for slow Ubuntu mirror days. ## Verified Ran it locally: no - CI-only change; the restore, root apt install, and save run only on Actions runners. Results from this PR's CI runs are below. - actionlint 1.7.12 passed on `spec.yml`, `benchmark.yml`, and `agent.yml` (Blacksmith runner label warnings ignored). - CI verification: in progress. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: title carries `!`, the changeset body names what breaks and what replaces it, and the deprecation warning landed a window earlier (stability policy in CONTRIBUTING.md). - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: the `docs/**/*.mdx` page for the behavior, and `skills/e2e/` if the skill describes it. - [ ] Contract change: emitted `.d.ts` reviewed, `tests/types/sdk-types.ts` updated; wire change edits the schema and both fixtures. - [ ] Engine contract change (`e2e/engine`): changesets for `e2e`, `@e2e-dev/web`, and `@e2e-dev/mobile`. ## AI assistance and human review AI was used to prepare these changes. Human review by @kdy1 is pending. - Harness: Claude Code - Model: claude-opus-5-5 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: chore(dev): PR description as source of truth, pnpm record:terminal
body: ## What - The PR description becomes the source of truth for a change. The template now asks for `## What`, `## Why`, `## How it works` (numbered steps through the diff), and `## Verified`. - Agents update the description after every push to an open PR, and run `unslop` on what they edit. - `pnpm record:terminal` records a command in a real TTY as `.mp4`, `.webm`, or `.gif`, for PRs that change what the terminal shows. ```bash pnpm record:terminal --cwd apps/testbed --out /tmp/branch.gif -- node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/todos.e2e.ts ``` ## Why Reviewing a PR here meant reading the diff to find out what it does. The old body was "a few bullets on what and why", it went stale as soon as review fixes were pushed, and nothing told an agent to go back and edit it. Terminal changes (reporters, CLI output, prompts) shipped with pasted text at best, because there was no way to record a terminal from a script. ## How it works 1. The template splits `## What and why` into `## What`, `## Why`, and `## How it works`, and lists the evidence `## Verified` expects (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`). 2. `writing-pr` gets a "Source of truth" section (`.dev/skills/writing-pr/SKILL.md:15`): the body describes the head commit, covers everything the diff does, and its evidence comes from the head. 3. `writing-pr` gets "After every push to an open PR" (`.dev/skills/writing-pr/SKILL.md:31`): fetch the body, check each section against what the push changed, run `unslop`, then `gh pr edit`. Its skill description now triggers on a push, so an agent loads it outside `ship-pr` and `babysit` too. `AGENTS.md:460` states the same rule for agents that load no skill. 4. `## Verified` gets a table of which evidence each kind of change needs (`.dev/skills/writing-pr/SKILL.md:113`): main beside the PR for a fix, the `pnpm bench:ab` table for a perf claim or a runner, agent, or engine change, a terminal recording for terminal output, the run's video for on-screen behavior. 5. The other skills point at those rules: - `ship-pr` captures the benchmark and recording during verify and checks the body against `git diff --stat` before opening (`.dev/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md:64`). - `babysit` updates the body right after a push and re-reads it against the final diff at handoff (`.dev/skills/babysit/SKILL.md:87`). - The fresh-context review prompt reads the body as the claim under review (`.dev/skills/ship-pr/references/review-prompt.md:34`). 6. `scripts/record-terminal.ts` builds a [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) tape and runs `vhs` on it (`scripts/record-terminal.ts:110`). The tape fixes the shell, size, and font, types the command, and waits for the prompt to return, so a failing run records too (`scripts/record-terminal/tape.ts:61`). `--tape ` plays the caller's keystrokes for a UI that takes keys (`scripts/record-terminal/tape.ts:70`). 7. Arguments after `--` are quoted again before they are typed, so bash runs what the calling shell parsed (`scripts/record-terminal/tape.ts:42`). The video is written to a scratch directory and copied to `--out` only on success, so a failed run keeps the earlier recording (`scripts/record-terminal.ts:122`). 8. The community PR bot treats the template's new `1.` placeholder as empty (`scripts/pr-policy/rules.ts:37`). It still passes a body written with the old `## What and why` heading. Decisions a reviewer may ask about: - `## Verified` keeps its name. Renaming it to `## Evidence` would fail the bot on every open PR. - The bot does not require `## How it works`. Requiring it would flag open community PRs on their next edit. - `vhs` is a prerequisite on `PATH`, not a dependency. `.fallowrc.json` lists it under `ignoreBinaries`. ## Issue None. Maintainer change to the repo's own workflow. ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - The script, driven through `nix shell nixpkgs#vhs -c` (vhs 0.11.0) on macOS, against the built CLI in `apps/testbed`. Each cell below is the tool's own output. | Passing run | Failing run (`NO_TESTS`) | | --- | --- | | ![passing run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6a39464-3168-4cb2-aac0-2b7f8eb82586) | ![failing run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c604e16-1868-41dc-9ba5-82da11e040f3) | | Quoted argument: `-- node -e 'console.log("sum", 1 + 1)'` | Keystrokes from `--tape` (`cat`, typed text, Ctrl+C) | | --- | --- | | ![quoted argument](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ecfe0b3-6b8f-42ff-8da0-87cf8de73864) | ![keystrokes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d100f2d-156f-48d2-b1c6-0b9d6b40c7b6) | - Failure paths, each exits 2: ```text $ node scripts/record-terminal.ts --out /tmp/rt-pr/keep.mp4 -- echo hi # vhs not on PATH record-terminal: vhs is not on PATH. Install it with `brew install vhs`, or run this under `nix shell nixpkgs#vhs -c`. $ cat /tmp/rt-pr/keep.mp4 # earlier file untouched keep $ node scripts/record-terminal.ts --out x.txt -- echo hi record-terminal: --out must end in .mp4, .webm, .gif $ node scripts/record-terminal.ts record-terminal: pass one of: a command after --, or --tape ``` - `pnpm test:scripts`: 235 pass, including the tape builder and the bot rules for both the old and the new template. - No benchmark: nothing in the runner, the agent loop, or an engine changes. - Not verified: the skills are instructions, so nothing proves an agent follows them. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only. - [ ] Breaking change: not one. - [ ] Docs updated in the same PR: no `docs/**` behavior changes; `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` are updated. - [ ] Contract change: none. - [ ] Engine contract change: none.

title: feat(config): set the default visible option of screen queries with locators
body:
## What and why

Role queries never match a hidden node, but `getByText`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`, and `getByTestId` do. On native apps, screens kept mounted behind the current one stay in the tree, so suites pass `{ visible: true }` to almost every query. A new `locators` config option makes that the default.

```ts
export default {
  targets: [
    { engine: mobile({ platform: 'ios' }), app: { bundleId: 'com.example.app' } },
    { name: 'web', engine: web(), app: { url }, locators: { visible: false } }, // this target keeps hidden matches
  ],
  locators: { visible: true },
} satisfies E2EConfig;

await screen.getByText('Saved').tap();                       // skips hidden nodes
await screen.getByText('Saved', { visible: false }).count(); // a query's own option wins
```

- `locators: { visible }` sits at the top level and on each target. A target's `visible` wins over the config's, and a query's own `visible` wins over both. The default is `false`, so existing suites run as before.
- Core resolves it per target (`ResolvedTarget.locators`). The screen applies it in the four queries (`packages/core/src/locator/screen.ts`). `getByRole` and `getByDisplayValue` are unchanged.
- An `e2e mcp` session applies it too: `run_code`, `locate`, and the test lines build the same queries a test under that config builds. Without this, `locate` counted hidden twins a test would skip, and a test line's `.nth(i)` could point at the wrong node.
- The config digest reads the default only through the resolved targets, so `{}`, `{ visible: false }`, and no key all digest alike.
- Docs: `reference/config.mdx` (`locators`, `LocatorsConfig`), `reference/screen.mdx` (Hidden duplicates), `reference/mcp.mdx`, `reference/errors.mdx`, the Maestro migration guide, and the `e2e` and `migrate-to-e2e` skills.

Error codes the new option can raise:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | `locators`, at the top level or on a target, is not an object, has a key other than `visible`, or has a `visible` that is not a boolean |

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, Chromium only. Firefox could not run on this machine.

- testbed `/controls` page, which has a hidden `banner` twin. A scratch config with `locators: { visible: true }` ran a test that uses no `{ visible: true }`: `getByTestId('banner')` resolves to one node and taps, `getByText('Sale')` resolves, and `getByTestId('banner', { visible: false })` counts 2.

```text
      run 01a208e5-1a0a-7eda-aaa8-9c861d48857f · targets: chromium
 ✓ target "chromium" command at http://127.0.0.1:4371/ ready 92ms
   ✓ |chromium| tests-visible-verify/visible.e2e.ts > queries skip the hidden twin without { visible: true } 344ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- The same config with `locators: { visible: 'yes' }`:

```text
 ERROR  configuration error INVALID_CONFIG (config)
locators.visible must be a boolean, got "yes"
```

- Firefox: not verified. Playwright's Firefox build (`firefox-1572`) does not start on this Mac (macOS 27.2.1). It exits with `Could not find profile folder`, also when started directly outside e2e and after a forced reinstall. CI runs no Firefox either. The default is applied in core before a query reaches the engine, so the engine gets the same `visible: true` query that `{ visible: true }` on a query sends today.
- `tests/integration/locators-visible.test.ts` runs two web targets from a config file through worker processes: one inherits `visible: true`, one overrides it with `false`.

title: feat(web): emulate a touchscreen with web({ hasTouch: true })
body:
Web targets had no touch emulation, so the touch code paths of a web app went untested. `web({ hasTouch: true })` turns it on. The default stays off.

```ts
targets: [{ name: 'web', engine: web({ hasTouch: true }), app: { url } }]

await screen.getByRole('button', 'Go').tap();          // touchstart, touchend, then the browser's click
await screen.tapAt({ x: 40, y: 30 });                  // same, at a point
await screen.swipe({ from: { x: 100, y: 200 }, to: { x: 300, y: 200 } }); // touchstart, touchmove, touchend (Chromium)
```

- `hasTouch` is passed to every context the engine creates (`packages/web/src/surface.ts`), as Playwright's `hasTouch` context option.
- A `tap` on a node uses Playwright's `tap()` instead of `click()`, through the label stand-in too. A `tap` at a point uses `page.touchscreen.tap` (`packages/web/src/actions.ts`).
- A path swipe (`screen.swipe({ from, to })`, the `swipeTo` pointer kind) sends `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` over CDP on Chromium. `cdpTouchscreen` gives the CDP session the mouse's `move`/`down`/`up` shape, so the existing `performPointDrag` paces it (`packages/web/src/support.ts`).
- Firefox and WebKit cannot send touch moves, so a path swipe there throws `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before any input goes out. Taps work on every browser.
- Every other action stays mouse and keyboard input: `doubleTap`, `secondaryTap`, `longPress`, `hover`, `check`/`uncheck`, `dragTo` (including the agent's `dragAt`), and directional swipes.
- Like `userAgent`, the option needs a newly created context. `hasTouch: true` with `connect.reconnectEndpoint` or an attempt-scoped browser provider is `INVALID_CONFIG`.

Docs: `reference/web.mdx` (new `hasTouch` entry), `reference/screen.mdx`, `reference/errors.mdx`, `reference/engine.mdx`, `web.mdx` (the "doesn't emulate touch" limit), `browser.mdx`, `migrate/playwright.mdx`, and `skills/e2e/references/setup.md`. The `SwipePathOptions` and `PointerAction` JSDoc in `@e2e-dev/core` now say an emulated touchscreen swipes by touch (comment only, so no core changeset).

## Error codes

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | `hasTouch` is not a boolean, or `hasTouch: true` on a persistent context. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` | A swipe along a path with `hasTouch` in Firefox or WebKit. |

Everything a tap or a path swipe already threw is unchanged.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, partly. Firefox could not run on this machine.

- Built CLI on the testbed `/pointer` page, with a scratch config of `web({ hasTouch: true })` and `web()` targets and a test that records `touchstart`, `touchmove`, `touchend`, `mousedown`, and `click`:

```text
|chromium-touch| a locator tap and a point tap fire touch events
tap events: touchstart,touchend,mousedown,click,touchstart,touchend,mousedown,click
|chromium-touch| a path swipe fires touch moves
swipe events: touchstart,touchmove,touchmove,touchend

|chromium-default| (web(), no hasTouch)
tap events: mousedown,click,mousedown,click
swipe events: mousedown,click

|webkit-touch| a locator tap and a point tap fire touch events
tap events: touchstart,touchend,mousedown,click,touchstart,touchend,mousedown,click
|webkit-touch| a path swipe fires touch moves
UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY: a swipe along a path with web({ hasTouch: true }) needs chromium: webkit cannot send touch moves
```

- Firefox: not verified on a real browser. Playwright's Firefox 159 build exits at launch on this Mac (`Could not find profile folder`, and `sandbox_extension_issue_file_to_process ... Operation not permitted` on a fresh install), with bare Playwright too, so it is the environment, not this change. The Firefox error is covered by a unit test with a stubbed page, and the live WebKit run above takes the same code path (any browser other than Chromium).
- New tests: `packages/web/tests/integration/touch.test.ts` (node tap, label stand-in tap, point tap, path swipe on Chromium, default without touch) and unit tests in `packages/web/tests/unit/actions.test.ts` (touchscreen tap, the CDP touch sequence, a cancelled swipe sends nothing, Firefox and WebKit refuse a path swipe).

## Review

Two independent reviews ran. Fixed: a cancelled swipe could still send the gesture, a failed CDP detach could replace the drag's error, `hasTouch: false` was refused on a persistent context, the web guide still said the engine cannot emulate touch, and docs and JSDoc described every web path swipe as a pointer drag. Not changed:

- Dropping `swipeTo` from `pointerActions` for Firefox or WebKit with `hasTouch`: core's error for an undeclared kind names only `swipeTo` and the declared list, and the engine's error names `hasTouch` and the browser.
- Mapping a provider that lacks `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` to `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`: no current provider is known to lack it, and the error already names the method.
- Pacing an undated touch swipe or waiting for the page to stop scrolling: a fast swipe flings a page as a finger does, the mobile engine also returns while a list coasts, and Playwright's stability check makes the next locator action wait. The reference now says to pass `duration` for a slower swipe.

title: feat(web): add browser.consoleMessages() and browser.pageErrors()
body:
## What and why

- `browser.consoleMessages()` and `browser.pageErrors()` on `@e2e-dev/web` return the active tab's console messages, uncaught errors, and unhandled rejections since the tab opened. Before this, you had to add an init script that wrapped `console.error` and listened for `error` and `unhandledrejection`, then read the results back with `evaluate`.
- Both read Playwright's per-page lists with `{ filter: 'all' }` (`packages/web/src/browser.ts`). Playwright's default, `'since-navigation'`, would drop entries at each navigation. Playwright keeps up to 200 of the latest entries per list.
- After `app.restart()`, the lists only have the new page's entries, because a restart closes the tab and opens a new page.
- A persistent browser (`connect.reconnectEndpoint`, or a provider in `attempt` scope) reuses its own first tab. Chrome replays that tab's earlier console output and errors to a new CDP client, so the engine now clears both lists after it moves that tab to `about:blank` (`packages/web/src/attempt-session.ts`).
- The return values only go to the test. The steps are recorded as `browser.consoleMessages` and `browser.pageErrors` without a label, and this change doesn't write the text to any report or artifact. Console output still shows up in the app log, as before.

```ts
test('the checkout page logs no errors', async ({ app, browser }) => {
  await app.open('/checkout');
  const errors = (await browser.consoleMessages()).filter((message) => message.type === 'error');
  expect(errors).toEqual([]);
  expect(await browser.pageErrors()).toEqual([]);
});
```

```ts
export interface WebConsoleMessage {
  readonly type: ReturnType<ConsoleMessage['type']>; // Playwright's union: 'log', 'warning', 'error', ...
  readonly text: string;
}

export interface WebPageError {
  readonly message: string;
  readonly stack: string; // empty for a thrown value that is not an Error
}
```

Error codes the new methods can throw:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `APP_NOT_OPEN` | No page is open yet. |
| `ACTION_FAILED` | The call ran past `actionTimeout`. |
| `ENGINE_FAILURE` | The browser connection was lost. |

There are no new error codes. `docs/reference/errors.mdx` already lists all three.

Docs: `docs/reference/web.mdx` (two entries, the summary table, the `Browser` block, the type exports), the Playwright migration guide (a mapping row, and the workaround row now covers only `page.clock`), and `skills/e2e/references/writing-tests.md`.

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on Chromium.

Firefox wasn't verified. Playwright's Firefox 159 (revision 1572) exits at launch on this Mac with `Could not find profile folder`. It fails the same way when started directly (`firefox -headless -profile <dir> --screenshot`) and from a fresh install. No CI job runs Firefox.

- Testbed, the built CLI, `e2e run tests/browser.e2e.ts`. The new test logs with `console.error`, leaves a rejection unhandled, and throws from a timer. All three are read back, and the lists are empty after `app.restart()`:

```text

  "messages": [{ "type": "log", "text": "ready" }, { "type": "error", "text": "broken 42" }],
```

title: feat(expect): add toBeInViewport
body:
Adds `expect(locator).toBeInViewport({ ratio?, timeout? })`, the Playwright matcher for checking that a node is inside the viewport. `toBeVisible()` passes for an off-screen pager page or content scrolled out of view, so tests had to poll `boundingBox()` against the viewport size instead.

```ts
await expect(screen.getByText('Step 2 of 3')).toBeInViewport();
await expect(screen.getByTestId('banner')).toBeInViewport({ ratio: 0.5 }); // default: 0, any part
await expect(screen.getByText('Step 1 of 3')).not.toBeInViewport();       // hidden, absent, or off screen
```

- The node's `rect` is compared with the viewport size of a screen observation (`session.observe`), so web, iOS, and Android don't need an engine change. The screen is observed only when the node is shown and has a box (`sample()` in `packages/e2e/src/expect/async.ts`).
- The ratio is the share of the box inside the viewport (`boxShareInViewport` in `packages/core/src/internal/geometry.ts`). It passes when the share is above 0 and at least `ratio`, with Playwright's `1e-9` tolerance.
- Negated, it passes for a hidden node, zero matches (a missing frame counts as zero), a node with no box, or a box outside the viewport. A web node scrolled wholly out of its iframe has no box, so it counts as outside.
- One difference from Playwright, documented in `reference/expect.mdx` and the Playwright guide: Playwright uses an `IntersectionObserver`, so a part that a scrolling container clips off counts as outside. Here, only the viewport bounds the box, so a pager page inside a narrower `overflow` container can still read as in view. When an engine already cuts a box to its container (the web engine for iframes, Android for list rows), the cut-off part doesn't count.
- Docs: a `reference/expect.mdx` entry and types. The Playwright guide drops the `boundingBox()` workaround, and the Detox and Maestro guides map their visibility percentages to `ratio`. The matcher is listed in `skills/e2e` and accepted by `run_code`.

Error codes the new API can throw (none new, so `reference/errors.mdx` is unchanged):

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | `ratio` is not a number from 0 to 1 (`null`, `NaN`, a string), or an option it does not take, before any read |
| `ASSERTION_FAILED` | the timeout runs out; the message names the observed ratio, `hidden`, `no box`, or `no node` |
| `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` | the locator matches more than one node |
| Engine errors (`ENGINE_FAILURE`, `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`, ...) | the locate, read, or observe call fails, as for the other locator matchers |

## Verified

Ran it locally: yes, on Chromium. Firefox: no, see below.

- Testbed with the built CLI, a scratch test on `/scroll` (not committed): `node node_modules/e2e/dist/cli/bin.js run tests/zz-in-viewport.e2e.ts --video`. The heading reads `toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1 })` before a wheel scroll. After the scroll it stays `toBeVisible()` but passes `not.toBeInViewport()`, and the rows list is in the viewport. The deliberate failure prints:

  ```text
  ASSERTION_FAILED: expect.toBeInViewport failed
  locator: getByRole("heading", name: "Scroll")
  expected: in viewport
  observed: viewport ratio 0 (match count 1)
  ```

- `packages/e2e/tests/integration/web-in-viewport.test.ts` runs a suite on the web engine in Chromium. It covers a full-width pager whose second page is visible but not in the viewport until "Next page", content below the fold before and after `scrollIntoView`, a box half past the bottom edge (passes `ratio: 0.5`, fails `0.6` with `observed: viewport ratio 0.5`), and the negated form on a hidden and an absent node.
- `packages/e2e/tests/unit/expect-in-viewport.test.ts` covers full, partial, corner, below, and edge-touching boxes, hidden, absent, and boxless nodes, the float tolerance, and option validation.
- Firefox: not run. Playwright's Firefox (`firefox-1572`) does not start on this Mac, headless or headed, even from a bare `firefox.launch()` outside the runner: `Could not find profile folder`, and headed `sandbox_extension_issue_file_to_process ... Operation not permitted`. The matcher has no browser-specific code. The web engine's `rect` and viewport come from the same in-page reader on every browser.
- iOS and Android: not run on a device. The matcher needs no engine change. A reviewer pointed out that Android reports a list row's bounds already cut to the list, from the golden snapshots in `packages/mobile/tests/fixtures/snapshots/android/`. The docs state that limit, but no device run confirms it.

title: ci(pr-policy): add the maintainer takeover label
body: ## What A maintainer who decides to finish a community PR themselves adds the `maintainer takeover` label. The bot then: - comments once, tagging the author and naming the maintainer who took over - assigns the PR to that maintainer - drops `needs:compliance` and its comment, and neither the 72 hour close nor the stale sweep touches the PR Removing the label deletes the comment, and the policy check applies again. The comment the author gets: ```text @contributor, thanks for the work so far. @maintainer is taking over this PR and will finish it. - You do not need to do anything else. Review comments and failing checks are on the maintainer from here. - Please do not push more commits, so the work does not collide. If you have something to add, comment here. - You keep the credit for the change. - The automated checks will not close this PR. If you would rather finish it yourself, say so here. ``` Dependabot PRs get only the `dependencies` label. ## Why When a maintainer finishes a contributor's PR, nothing on the PR says so. The author keeps pushing or waits for a review, and the policy bot can still flag the PR and close it after 72 hours, or close it as stale. The `dependabot.yml` change belongs to a label cleanup done by hand in the repo settings. Dependabot's defaults add `javascript` and `github_actions`, which nothing reads, and would bring them back after they were deleted. ## How it works 1. `pr-policy.yml` also runs on `labeled` and `unlabeled` (`.github/workflows/pr-policy.yml:12`) and gets a second step, `takeover.ts` (`:38`). 2. `outstanding()` returns no problems for a PR carrying the label (`scripts/pr-policy/rules.ts:169`). `check.ts:51` and the sweep's `settleFlagged` (`sweep.ts:118`) both call it on the live PR, so their existing "nothing to fix" path clears the flag. A PR labeled between the sweep's listing and its turn is caught the same way. 3. `isStale` skips a labeled PR (`rules.ts:262`). 4. `takeover.ts` skips closed PRs and PRs from maintainers or bots, then reads the live labels, the bot's announcement, and who last added the label from the timeline (`labeledBy`, `scripts/pr-policy/github.ts:108`). 5. `takeoverChange()` (`rules.ts:203`) decides from that state: post the announcement, rewrite it when another maintainer took over, withdraw it when the label is gone, or do nothing. 6. `announceTakeover` posts or edits the comment and assigns the maintainer (`github.ts:127`). `withdrawTakeover` deletes the comment and leaves the assignee, because nothing records why someone was assigned (`github.ts:138`). 7. `CONTRIBUTING.md:62` documents the label for contributors. Decision: both steps read the PR as it is and ignore which event fired. The workflow's concurrency group drops a queued run when a newer event arrives, so a step keyed on the `labeled` event could lose the announcement for good. For the same reason the job has no filter on the label's name: a skipped run would still evict a queued one. ## Issue ## Verified Ran it locally: yes - Both scripts with `--dry-run` against a live fork PR (#2102), with its REST payload as the event. This exercises the live reads, including the new timeline query: ```text #2102: nothing to fix #2102: the takeover announcement matches the label labeledBy takeover: undefined labeledBy size: [ 'github-actions' ] ``` - Not run: the announce and withdraw writes on a real PR. Labeling a real community PR pings its author, and the workflow runs from `main`, so it cannot run before merge. `takeoverChange`, `announceTakeover`, and `withdrawTakeover` are covered by `scripts/pr-policy/*.test.ts`. ## Checklist - [x] Changeset added (`pnpm changeset`) for any change to a published package, or the change is testbed, docs, or CI only.

title: kernel: the live view URL is printed into the run log
body:
The Kernel provider prints the browser's live view URL into the run log:

```ts
request.log(browser.liveViewUrl === undefined ? `browser ${browser.sessionId}` : `browser ${browser.sessionId}, watch at ${browser.liveViewUrl}`);
```

(`packages/kernel/src/provider.ts`)

`@e2e-dev/notte` keeps its viewer URL out of the log on purpose, because the URL carries tokens that act on the session and a run's log is often public CI output (`packages/notte/src/provider.ts`). A Kernel live view URL is the same kind of URL: whoever reads the log can act on the browser.

Expected: the provider logs `browser <id>` alone. Kernel's dashboard still finds the browser by its `e2e_run`, `e2e_target`, and `e2e_slot` tags, which the provider already sets, and `docs/integrations/kernel.mdx` describes the tags instead of the URL.

title: chore(ci): bump actions/setup-java from 6.2.0 to 6.3.0
body:
Bumps [actions/setup-java](https://github.com/actions/setup-java) from 6.2.0 to 6.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).
